source.japanese: 『巻頭歌』
source.english: Opening Song

target.text: 『Prefatory Song』

source.japanese:
俺が生まれた邑に
　ひとりの船乗りが住んでいて
　阿呆の船で暮らしたときのことを
　おいらに話してくれたのさ
source.english:
In the village where I was born,
There lived a sailor,
And he told me of his days
Aboard a ship of fools.

source.japanese:
そこで　俺らは霧に向かって出航し
　やがて緑の海を見つけたよ
　そして　渦巻く波の上
　阿呆の船で暮らしたさ
source.english:
So we sailed into the mist
Till we found a sea of green,
And upon its swirling waves
We lived aboard a ship of fools.

source.japanese:
俺らはみんな阿呆の船で暮らしてる
　阿呆のお船が俺らの家よ
　俺らはみんな船暮らし
　阿呆の船が俺らの家さ
source.english:
We all live aboard a ship of fools,
The ship of fools is home.
We all live aboard a ship,
The ship of fools is home.

source.japanese:
みぃんな船が大好きで
　だから降りても降りても
　帰ってきちまう
　阿呆の船
　阿呆　阿呆
　阿呆鳥!!
source.english:
We all love that ship so much,
No matter how often we leave,
We always come back—
To the ship of fools,
Fool, fool—
Albatross!!

source.japanese:
ところで皆の衆
　俺は　うっかりしとってさ
　その先どうなったか知らんのだよ
source.english:
Now then, folks—
I clean forgot,
so I don't know what happened after that.

source.japanese:
ヒヒヒ
　ホホ　ホ！
source.english:
Hee hee hee!
Ho ho ho!

source.japanese: 阿呆鳥!!
source.english: Albatross!

source.japanese: ───阿呆鳥の歌（ホシリンゴ族）
source.english: —The Albatross Song (Starr-Ringo Tribe)

target.text: In the town where I was born Lived a man who sailed the seas And he told me of his life Living on a ship of fools
So we sailed on to the fog Till we found the sea of green And atop the swirling waves We lived on our ship of fools
We all live on a ship of fools The ship of fools we call home We all live on a ship The ship of fools we call home

And we all love that ship So no matter how many times we get off We always end up coming back Ship of fools Fools, fools Albatross!! (TN: In Japanese, the albatross is also known as the "ahoudori", written "阿呆鳥", lit. fool-bird, for being easy to catch. This is a play on words that resurfaces several times.)
By the by, all ye gathered I'm a bit absentminded, see So I don't know what happened next
Hi hi hi Hoho ho!
Albatross!!
───Song of the Albatross (By the Hoshiringo clan) (TN: Hoshiringo is a pun on Ringo Starr, with "hoshi" meaning "star", and the song modelled, in part, after Yellow Submarine.)

source.japanese: ───かつて、船があった。
source.english: —Once, there was a ship.

source.japanese: ───薄暗く、混沌とした時代の隙間を縫うようにして、航海を続けるその船は。
source.english: —A ship that sailed on through the cracks of a dark and chaotic age.

source.japanese: ───錆と腐朽の一大集積であり。
source.english: —A vast accumulation of rust and rot.

source.japanese: ───有り体に言えば浮かんでいるのが、船体力学と物理学への挑戦であるかのような船で。
source.english: —To put it plainly, a ship whose very ability to float appeared to defy naval architecture and the laws of physics.

source.japanese: ───船の名は───
source.english: —And the ship's name was—
—Albatross!—

target.text: ───Once upon a time, there was a ship.
───As if weaving through the cracks in a gloomy age of disorder, that ship sailed on.
───She was a great heap of rust and decay.
───She floated, strictly speaking, but it was as if the ship herself was taunting the very concept of the structural mechanics of shipbuilding and the laws of physics.
───And that ship's name was───
───|The Albatross!───

source.japanese:
しかし物語の始まりは。
　海から離れて、まずは。
　とある時代、とある国の、とある港街の。
　雑踏の中から。
source.english:
But our story begins—
away from the sea, for now;
amid the crowds of a certain port town,
in a certain country, in a certain age.

target.text: But as for the beginning of this story. First, we must leave the seas. In a certain age, in a certain country, in a certain port town. In the midst of the hustle and bustle.

source.japanese:
深い、そして透けるような濃緑が積層し色為した黒の翼だった。
　港町の目抜き通りの、街灯りと人並みにふやけた宵闇などより、もっと鮮烈な、ずっと艶[つや]やかな。
source.english:
They were black wings, their blackness made of layer upon layer of deep, translucent green.
More vivid, more lustrous than the dusk along the port's main street, diluted by lamplight and the throng of people.

source.japanese:
翼を優雅に展開させ、気流に乗る水鳥のように。
　あるいは水面を切り裂き、気圏に飛翔せる飛び魚のように。
source.english:
Like a waterbird spreading its wings gracefully and riding the air.
Or a flying fish breaking the surface of the water and soaring into the sky.

source.japanese:
宵を迎えて、海中の珊瑚が触糸を拡げる様で賑わい始める頃合いの、港街だ。
　一夜の歓楽を求めて繰り出す者達、一日の生計から解放されて家路を急ぐ人々。物売りは声を張り上げ、呼び込みは招き街角の娼妓達は慣れた身のこなしで客に擦り寄る。
source.english:
Evening had come. The port was stirring into life, like coral spreading its tentacles beneath the sea.
People ventured out in search of a night's pleasure; others, released from the day's work, hurried home. Vendors shouted their wares. Barkers beckoned. The streetwalkers on the corners sidled up to customers with practiced ease.

source.japanese:
およそ新鮮味に欠けて、ありふれた港街の営みだが、宵闇が幻灯画の趣を与えている。
　けれど、その中にあってなお異質で、孤高で、不思議な後ろ姿だった。
source.english:
It was all the ordinary business of a port town, quite wanting in novelty, though twilight lent the scene the charm of a magic-lantern slide.
Yet even amid it, the figure remained a thing apart: alien, aloof, strange.

source.japanese:
夕凪に凪いだ空気が、薄い粥のように港町の薄闇の幅を温く満たしている。
　なのに緩んで滞留した街の空気の中、そこだけ風をまとうように黒髪を翼とたなびかせ。
source.english:
In the evening lull, air as tepid as thin gruel filled the port town's dim streets.
Yet amid that slack, stagnant atmosphere, her black hair streamed like wings, as though she alone wore the wind.

source.japanese:
肩先が触れ合わんばかりにすれ違う人と人とがある。障害物のように往路にはみ出した屋台もある。
　直進するにはいささか混み合いすぎた喧噪を、なのに身を躱したとも見えないのに、向きも歩みの拍子も変えず雑踏の中を進み往く。
source.english:
People passed so close their shoulders nearly touched. Stalls jutted into the street, obstacles in the way. It was far too crowded to walk a straight line.
Yet the figure moved through the throng without changing course or pace, without even seeming to dodge.

source.japanese:
風のみを伴連れに港町を通り抜けていく、独りの後姿だった。
　巷間の営みなど意にも介さず。
　何者にも遮[さえぎ]られず、目もくれず。
source.english:
A lone figure passed through the port with only the wind for company.
She paid the life of the streets no mind.
Nothing hindered her. Nothing earned so much as a glance.

target.text: They were wings of black tinged with a laminate layer of a deep, almost transparent green. Far more vivid than the streetlights of the thoroughfare grown indolent in the twilight hours, glowing with a perpetual glossy sheen.
Like a seabird elegantly unfolding its wings and gliding on the air currents. Or perhaps like a flying fish splitting apart the surface of the water, soaring into the atmosphere.

Late evening was approaching, and the port town was starting to awaken, like the undersea coral reefs spreading out their delicate tentacle feelers. Those flocking to the city seeking a night of pleasure, as well as those released from their daily toils rushing home. Salesmen raising their voices, barkers soliciting people, and prostitutes snuggling up to customers with well-practiced mannerisms.

Utterly lacking in novelty, the commonplace activities of a port town, the twilight giving it the appearance of a movie projected through a lanterna magica. And yet, in the midst of it all, there stood a proudly independent, mysterious figure of an entirely different character with its back turned.

The dim port town was suffused with lukewarm, calm evening air, like thin rice gruel. Yet amidst this town's slack and stagnant air, only that black hair flowed like it were surrounded by a gentle breeze.

One could only barely squeeze by other people while rubbing shoulder against shoulder. There were stalls jutting into the street like obstacles. It was a tumult rather too congested to attempt to pass through, but even though it didn't look like it was avoiding any of it, it continued to advance through the hustle and bustle without changing direction or missing a step.
Passing through the port town, with the wind as its sole companion, was a retreating figure. Paying no heed to the activities of the streets around it. Obstructed by none, sparing it nary a glance.

source.japanese:
その後ろ姿が、その後ろ姿が。
　予めその瞬間を選んでいたかのように。
　ああ、振り返る。
　けれど片頬しか見せず。
　それさえ、磨墨の雲の切れ間に半月が覗いてはすぐにまた隠れるように、横顔は一時の幻と、また黒髪の後ろ姿に立ち戻る。
source.english:
That figure, that receding figure—
As though she had chosen the moment in advance—
Ah, she turned.
But showed only one cheek.
Even that profile was a momentary vision, a half-moon glimpsed through a break in ink-black clouds before they closed again. Then it was gone, and once more there was only her black hair and receding back.

source.japanese:
ただその時、風が流れた。
　風が、青年の前髪を揺らして鼻梁へ流れた。
　靡く黒髪が呼んだ空気の流れが、重なり合う人々という障壁があるにも関わらず、遮られる事なく青年目指して届けられたかのようだった。
source.english:
Just then, a current of air stirred.
It ruffled the young man's fringe and brushed the bridge of his nose.
It seemed as though the breeze summoned by that streaming black hair had passed unhindered through the barrier of all those bodies, delivered straight to him.

source.japanese:
その時青年は、一筋の香りを嗅ぎ分ける。
　様々な生活臭が混じり合ってアクの強い、街中の空気に泥んでいたというのに、鼻先を流し浄めるようにその香りだけを、聞き分ける。
source.english:
At that moment, the young man caught a single thread of fragrance.
Though the city air lay muddied by the pungent mingling of all the smells of daily life, he could distinguish that scent alone, flowing past the tip of his nose as though to wash it clean.

source.japanese:
潮の香りだ───
　
　それも、混じり気のない、新鮮な海の精髄。
　まるで、未だいかなる航海者も至った事もない人跡未到の、真っ新の海原から初めて運ばれて来たかの。
source.english:
The scent of the sea—
The fresh, unadulterated essence of it.
As though it had come for the first time from a pristine ocean no voyager had ever reached.

source.japanese: 鼻先をくすぐるそんな香とともに、届いた、声があった。
source.english: With that scent tickling his nose came a voice.

target.text: That back, oh, that retreating figure. As though it had prepared for this moment in advance. Aah, it turned around. But it only showed one cheek. And even that, like the half-moon peeking out from a gap between inky clouds, was quickly hidden once more, like its side profile were a temporary illusion, it returned to being but a back clad in raven locks.

But in that moment, the wind blew. The wind blew, rustling the young man's forelocks and flowing down the ridge of his nose. The flow of wind called forth by the billowing black hair, despite the people standing between them who would act as obstacles, reached the young man without obstructions as if it had been aiming right for him.

In that moment, the young man picked out a single scent. Despite being mired in the city air, that acrid, bitter mixture of lived-in smells, he could distinguish it, that fragrance alone, as if it flowed through his nose and purified his senses.

It was the scent of the sea─── Moreover, it was without any admixtures: the pure, fresh essence of the sea. Like the scent of a pristine ocean, untraversed by any navigators, brought to him for the very first time.
And in tandem with the scent tickling his nose, a voice reached him.

source.japanese: 『───ようやく見つけた』
source.english: “—At last. I've found you.”

source.japanese: 『さあ、海に出よう直正』
source.english: “Come, Naomasa. Let's go to sea.”

source.japanese: 『私が、あなたを』
『待っているから───』
source.english: “…am waiting for you—”

target.text: 『───I finally found you』
『Now, let us take to the seas, Naomasa』
『For I have been』
『Waiting for you───』

source.japanese:
その時青年は、人声や足踏み、種々雑多な人々の営みの息吹の中に、届く筈もないのに、確かに聞いたと思った。
　まるで彼の耳だけを選んで伝えられた、彼方からのメッセージのように。
source.english:
Amid the voices, the footsteps, the breathing life of all those people, he thought he had heard it clearly, though it could never have reached him.
Like a message from far away, meant for his ears alone.

source.japanese: 囁きはいかなる大音声や愛の言葉、懇願よりも速やかに、青年の体の奥底、いわば彼という個性の根幹、存在の核へと、乾ききった海綿を満たす水のようにたちまちに浸透して、そして駆りたてる。
source.english: Faster than any roar, any word of love, any plea, the whisper penetrated to the depths of the young man's body—to the root of his selfhood, the core of his being—as swiftly as water fills a bone-dry sponge. And it drove him on.

source.japanese: 俗世の垢と欲望に塗れ、堕落しきった日々にふやけきった青年をして、強く強くかきたてる。
source.english: It drove the young man—steeped in worldly grime and desire, gone soft with days of utter dissipation—fiercely, fiercely on.

target.text: In that moment, though it should not have reached him amidst the voices, the stomping, and the breathing of the many diverse ways people were occupying themselves, he believed that he doubtlessly heard it. As if it had been conveyed to his ears alone by deliberate choice, like a message from far, far away.

The whisper, quicker than any raucous voice or words of love and supplication, reached the depths of the young man, the foundation of what one could call his individuality, to the core of his existence, instantly permeating him, like filling a dry sponge with water, and spurred him on.
This young man, drenched in lust and the filth of the base world, spending his days absentmindedly in depravity: it aroused him vigorously.

source.japanese:
駆りたてる───きっとそれは、畏れと憧れ。
　あまりの隔たりに畏れを抱いてしまうくらいに、何処か遠くにある届かない場所への、いてもたってもいられないほどの渇望。
source.english:
Drove him on—surely this was awe and longing.
An unbearable hunger for a place somewhere far away, beyond his reach. A place so remote that its very distance filled him with dread.

source.japanese:
かきたてる───多分それは、季節の変わり目に、唐突な流行り熱のように訪れる焦燥の念。
　漠然とした不安と、居心地の悪さが醸成する、焦りの気持ちだ。
source.english:
Stirred him—perhaps it was a feverish restlessness that struck without warning at the turn of the seasons.
An urgency brewed from vague unease and a discomfort he could not place.

source.japanese:
ほとんど第二の肌と慣れきって、日頃は意識もしない周囲の世界が、ふとした弾みで茨の衣と変じ、肌に棘して傷つけ、堪らない痛みと痒みで締めつけてくる。
　逃れられない檻なのではないかと感じてしまう。
source.english:
The world around him had grown as familiar as a second skin, something he scarcely noticed. Then, at the slightest turn, it would become a garment of thorns, pricking and wounding his flesh, constricting him with unbearable pain and itch.
It would feel like a cage from which there could be no escape.

source.japanese:
そんな居心地の悪さが不意に訪れる瞬間が、青年にはある。
　耐えきれないまでの、世界からの排斥感が濁流の如く押し寄せてくる瞬間が。
source.english:
There were moments when such discomfort came upon the young man without warning.
Moments when an unbearable sense of being cast out by the world surged over him like a muddy torrent.

source.japanese: ───囁く声、青年が日頃は深く沈めている意識の底から、憧憬と畏怖と焦燥を過[あやま]たず掬[すく]い上げる。
source.english: —The whispering voice reached down into the consciousness he ordinarily kept sunk deep within himself and drew up, unerringly, longing, dread, and restless need.

source.japanese:
だから。
　囁き、誘う声に導かれて青年は。
　水鳥のような、飛び魚のような不思議の後ろ姿を追いかけて。
　それまでの場所から、踏み出して───
source.english:
And so—
led by that whisper, that beckoning voice, the young man—
pursuing that strange figure, like a waterbird, like a flying fish—
stepped beyond the life he had known until then—

source.japanese: 道は、港へと、海へと通じていた。
source.english: The road led to the harbor, and to the sea.

target.text: Spurred on───it must have been awe and yearning. A distance so great it could cause him to feel awe; a great craving and longing, one that would not permit him to remain still, for a place somewhere far away in the distance that he could not reach.

Aroused───it was likely akin to a feeling of restless frustration, hitting abruptly like a sudden fever striking at the turn of the seasons. That feeling of burning impatience, fermented from a vague unease and the discomfort of not belonging.

The world surrounding you, so familiar it is like a second skin that you do not even notice, can change into a garb of thorns by some sudden whim of fate, piercing and wounding your skin, tightening with unbearable pain and itchiness. It might well end up feeling like an inescapable cage.

The very moment that unpleasantness unexpectedly befalls you is something the young man had experienced before. Until it is no longer bearable, that instant when that feeling of rejection from the world surges forwards and overwhelms you like a stream of mud.
───That whispering voice scooped up all his longings, his fears, and his frustrations without err, from the lowest depths of the young man's consciousness, sunken deep during his regular routines.

That is why. The young man was guided by the whisper, that enticing voice. Chasing after the back of that mysterious figure, like a seabird, like a flying fish. From the place he'd hitherto occupied, he set forth───
The road led towards the port, towards the ocean.

source.japanese:
【青年】
「……なぁんつってよぉ、
　どんだけけったいに見えたつったかて、
　なんぼ気ぃ惹かれたてったって」
source.english:
“…Yeah, well.
However weird she looked,
however much she caught my eye…”

source.japanese:
【青年】
「背中見ただけの女の子にほいほいついていくってどうなんだ本当。
　いや、それ以前にホントに女の子だったのかあれ」
source.english:
“What kind of idiot follows a girl when all he's seen is her back?
Come to think of it, was that even a girl?”

source.japanese:
【青年】
「そりゃ確かに髪は綺麗で長かったが、ろくすっぽ顔も見えなかったしなあ……」
source.english: “Sure, the hair was long and pretty, but I barely saw her face…”

source.japanese:
【青年】
「見境無いのも大概にしとこうぜ、俺。
　なあ俺、いや本気で。
　そのうち女関係で破滅するぞ、俺」
source.english:
“You've got to stop chasing anything that moves.
I'm talking to you, me.
Seriously. Women are going to be the ruin of you.”

target.text: 【Young Man】 「……How do I even put this? No matter how queer she might've looked, or how enticing she might've been.」
【Young Man】 「Why did I so thoughtlessly follow a girl just from seeing her back and nothing more, seriously. Wait, was she even really a girl in the first place?」
【Young Man】 「Sure, her hair was certainly long and pretty, but I barely got a peek at her face……」
【Young Man】 「There are limits to how indiscriminate you can be. Yeah, me, I'm being serious here. Relations with women are really going to be the end of me, one of these days.」

source.japanese:
【青年】
「てか、もう破滅に踏みこんでるよなこれ。
　うひゃああああっ」
source.english:
“Actually, I'm already pretty well ruined,
aren't I? Aaaaaagh!”

target.text: 【Young Man】 「Wait, I've already jumped head first into said end, haven't I? UHYAAAH!」

source.japanese:
轟音、閃光、弾け飛ぶ木片。
　銃声は目と鼻先で撃ち放たれたかに青年を絶叫させ、頭押さえて甲板に身を投げ出させたが、命中弾だったら音が聞こえたその時にくたばっている訳で、伏せたところで何を今さら。実際吹き飛ばして破片散らかしたのは、青年とは明後日の向きの索具と船上構造物の窓枠である。
source.english:
A roar, a flash, splinters bursting in every direction.
The shot went off as though from under the young man’s very nose, making him shriek, clutch his head, and fling himself flat on the deck. Had it hit him, of course, he would have been dead by the time he heard it, so diving for cover afterward was rather beside the point. What the shot had actually blown apart and scattered everywhere was a section of rigging and the window frame of a deckhouse off in an entirely different direction.

source.japanese:
大体ぼやいて悔いて半泣きになっている暇など有ったら、立ちむかうなり物陰に駆けこむなりするべきなのだ。
　白刃が海上の陽差し受けて酷薄に煌めき、連発に焼きついた銃身が、潮風の中にきな臭い匂いを添えている今となっては、過去を振り向く暇など無いはずだろう。
source.english:
If he had time to whine, repent, and almost burst into tears, he had time to fight back or run for cover.
Bare steel glittered cruelly in the sunlight on the sea. Gun barrels, scorched by repeated firing, added the acrid smell of powder to the salt wind. This was hardly the moment to look back on his life.

source.japanese:
襤褸船の上甲板は、今や修羅の巷だった。
　喉を裂かんばかりの怒号は彼我いずれの声とも知れず、血走った目はヒトの蛮性そのもの、霊長の長様は知性も悟性もかなぐり捨てて、血の報復に酔いしれてある。
　青年の乗りこむ船と、洋上隔てて三〇米ほど近くにまで迫った距離感は、襲撃の船の血気をいよいよ激しく煽り立て、接舷を待たずに攻めの手を放たせていた。
source.english:
The upper deck of the decrepit ship had become a street of carnage.
The throat-rending bellows of friend and foe were impossible to tell apart. Bloodshot eyes laid bare the savagery of humankind; His Lordship, chief of the primates, had thrown intellect and reason to the winds and was drunk on bloody revenge.
Only thirty meters of sea now separated the young man's ship from the attacking vessel. The narrowing distance only inflamed the attackers' bloodlust, and they opened their assault without waiting to come alongside.

target.text: Thundering roars, flashing lights, wooden splinters flying everywhere. The sound of gunfire in front of his eyes and nose made the young man scream, and he threw himself to the deck with his head cradled in his arms, but given he'd already be dead by the time he heard said noises had the bullets actually hit their mark, it would be rather belated to throw oneself down to the deck at this point. In reality, the scattered fragments flying everywhere came from the ship's rigging and the window frames of the on-deck structures, which the young man had mistaken for bullets.

To begin with, had one the time to spend on being lost in thought, regretful, and half in tears, one would be better served defiantly resisting or running for shelter. With white blades glinting cruelly in the ocean sunbeams and gun barrels burning in rapid volleys, in this very moment, where the sea breeze carried with it the stench of gunpowder and conflict, there surely was no time to reflect on the past.

For in this moment, the deck of this shabby ship was a scene of carnage. It was not possible to tell from which or where the throat-ripping roars of anger came, and their bloodshot eyes spoke of the very essence of human barbarism, the greatest of the primates throwing their intelligence and wisdom to the winds, drunk on bloody retribution. They had drawn so close that they were only separated from the ship the young man was aboard by roughly thirty metres of water, and the intensity of the ardour coming from the raiding ship was stirred by the shrinking sense of distance; lacking the patience to wait for coming alongside, they unleashed their attacks.

source.japanese:
ライフル弾も、手投げナイフも、しばし前までは敵愾心空しく、二者の間の波間に落ちこんでは剣呑な供物と捧げられていたのに、今は着弾する弾も充分な威力残して飛来する刃物も増えてきた。
　襲撃の船の上甲板は航海要員まで総動員したのか、すし詰めの相を呈しており、そいつらが例外なく武装して血にいきりたっているとあっては、青年には船と言うよりその輪郭なりに切り取られた地獄が迫ってきているように思われてならず。
source.english:
A little earlier, rifle bullets and throwing knives had exhausted their futile hostility in the waves between the ships, grim offerings to the sea. Now more bullets found their mark, and more blades arrived with force enough to kill.
The attackers' upper deck was packed, as though they had mustered even the men needed to run the ship. Every last one was armed and thirsting for blood. To the young man, it looked less like a ship approaching than a slice of hell cut to a ship's outline.

source.japanese:
こう激しく飛び交う凶弾凶器のただ中にあって、いやただ中だからこそ、青年は心底後悔していたと言えよう。
　あの日あの宵あの港町で、あの黒髪の後ろ姿にさえ気を取られなんだら、今頃はこんな死地の中、失禁しそうな膀胱をそれは必死の努力でこらえる事もなく、もしかしたら手頃な娼妓のぬくい乳房を頬寄せて、安い酒の安い夢心地の中、惰眠を貪っていられたかもしれないものを。
source.english:
Amid that furious storm of bullets and blades—or rather, because he was in the thick of it—the young man regretted his choices from the bottom of his heart.
If only the black-haired figure had not caught his eye that day, that evening, in that port town. Instead of fighting desperately to keep his bladder from emptying in this death trap, he might now have been sleeping off cheap liquor with his cheek against the warm breast of a whore he could afford.

source.japanese:
と、空しく追想する青年、いたずらに怯えて上甲板を駆けずり回るより、いっそそのまま伏していればまだ飛び道具を避ける目があるものを、わざわざ立ち上がってしまったのは、緊張に耐えかねたからである。
　上甲板を埋めるバラック群（なぜそんなものが船上にあるのかはひとまず置こう）にでも逃げこもうとしたのかも知れないが、タイミングが悪すぎた。
source.english:
He brooded to no purpose. Staying flat on the deck would at least have given him a chance of avoiding the missiles; running about in terror would not. Yet he stood up, unable to bear the suspense.
Perhaps he meant to shelter in the shacks that crowded the upper deck. Why a ship should have shacks on it is a question we shall leave for now. Whatever his intention, his timing could not have been worse.

target.text: There were rifle bullets as well as throwing knives; until just a moment ago, they had but fallen into the waters separating them in a show of vain enmity, a dangerous votive offering, but now, the impacting bullets felt plenty powerful, and the knives flying at them only increased in number. Perhaps the raiding ship had mobilized even their key crew members, for they stood packed like sardines on the deck, all of them armed without exception, blood boiling, and from the young man's point of view, it seemed less a boat and rather, more befittingly of its features, like a slice of Hell itself approaching.

And so, standing in the midst of this fierce flutter of lethal bullets and weapons, or perhaps it was exactly because he stood right in the midst of it, it could well be said that the young man here regretted it all from the bottom of his heart. That day, that night in that port town, had he just not been captivated so by that black-haired figure facing away from him, he would not be in this grave situation, desperately trying to keep his bladder on the verge of incontinence from leaking; perhaps he might instead be snuggling his cheek against the breasts of a convenient prostitute, lost in the cheap ecstasy of cheap liquor, idling away his time in indolence.

And so on. The young man reminisced in vain thus, and rather than running around the deck in fruitless fear, he had instead thrown himself to the deck, but having grown unable to stomach the thought of having to dodge yet more projectile weapons while prone, he purposely stood up. Perhaps he could have taken refuge in the cluster of shacks occupying the deck (and we shall leave the reason why such would be on board a ship for later), but his timing was simply too poor.

source.japanese: 大気を斬り裂いて、飛来するモノそれはぎらぎら光り剃刀の鋭さにまで研ぎあげられた青竜刀。余程の剛力自慢が投じたのか、距離をものともせずにびゅんびゅん回転しながら迫るが青年の脳天へ！
source.english: Something slashed through the air: a Chinese saber, glittering, honed to a razor's edge. Whoever had thrown it must have been prodigiously strong. It spun across the intervening distance as though the distance were nothing—straight at the young man's skull!

source.japanese: 青竜刀が巻き起こす旋風、横顔を撫でるまで迫って青年は、覚悟の間もなく脳漿甲板にぶちまけてはいさようなら、の、まさに間髪だった。
source.english: The wind of its passage brushed his cheek. He had no time even to brace himself. One instant more and his brains would be all over the deck, and that would be good-bye.

target.text: A green dragon crescent blade, edge sharpened to a dazzling razor, came flying, rendering the air itself asunder. It must have been thrown with enormous, herculean strength, for it revolved through the air with a sharp whizzing, undaunted by the distance, drawing near the crown of the young man's head!

The whirlwind raised by the green dragon crescent blade had drawn so near to the young man he could feel it stroking the side of his face; it would splatter his cerebrospinal fluid all over the deck without even permitting him a moment of resignation, goodbye world, literally but a hair's breadth away.

source.japanese:
白炎とたばしって青竜刀を弾き落としたのは日本刀の刀身の、冴えて冷たい。
　軌道が逸れたのは脳天かち割られる寸前で、僅かにかすって青年の髪を二・三本切りとばして、すかーんと船上構造物の壁に突き立った、びぃんと残った震え恐ろしい。
source.english:
A Japanese blade flashed like white fire, cold and keen, and struck the saber aside.
It changed course an instant before it split his skull, clipped two or three hairs, and buried itself in a deckhouse wall with a ringing crack. The shudder that lingered in the steel was horrible to watch.

source.japanese: 間抜けとは、鋼の撃ち合う閃音の、音を通り越した威力に横面を叩かれて、自分に致命の一撃が迫っていたのにようやく気づいた青年の事である。
source.english: Here was an idiot for you: only when the clash of steel struck him in the face, its force greater than mere sound, did the young man realize he had very nearly been killed.

source.japanese: 青年と青竜刀の間に瞬時に割りこんで弾き飛ばした、白の着物に褪せた小豆の袴[はかま]の男の声音が呆れ加減だったのもむべなるかな、だったが、
source.english: The man in the white kimono and faded russet hakama had darted between the young man and the saber and knocked it aside. No wonder his voice carried a note of weary exasperation:

target.text: The green dragon crescent blade, soaring like a white flame, was deflected to the side by the blade of a Japanese sword, cold and serene. The trajectory deviated right before it could split his head apart, barely missed, and cut off two or three of his hairs before lodging itself into the wall of one of the ship's on-deck structures, quivering with a terrifying twang.

Foolishness, for only after being struck on the side of his face with an awesome power, one that far exceeded the ringing noises of exchanged gunfire and clashing swords around him, did the young man finally realize that a fatal blow was drawing close to him, the fool.

The voice belonging to a man wearing a white kimono with a faded, reddish-brown hakama on top, he who had cut between the young man and the green dragon crescent blade and deflected it, was perhaps quite right in its astonishment, however,

source.japanese:
【和服の男】
「なにヤッてんのお前。そんなおっ死にてぇンなら、俺に叩っ斬られた方がまだ功徳になるてぇもんだぜ」
source.english: “What the hell are you doing? If you're so damn eager to die, at least let me cut you down. That'd earn some merit.”

target.text: 【Man in Japanese clothes】 「What the hell are you doing, dude? If you wanna die that badly, there'd be far more merit in it for you if you were to be cut down by me instead, y'know?」

source.japanese:
鞘に刀身収めて嘯いた台詞は、青年に迫った青竜刀とどっちつかずに物騒だったけれども仕方がない。
　この時代であっても若い者には珍しい和装で、その上邦人の骨相ながらも目だけが蒼いこの男は、何の因果か青年の殺害するよう依頼を受けている殺し屋なのだとか。殺し屋に命を救われたという状況の諧謔味を賞味する余裕のない青年はげんなりと、
source.english:
He sheathed his sword. The remark he tossed out was scarcely less menacing than the saber had been, but that was only to be expected.
Japanese dress was unusual for a young man even in this age. His features, too, were Japanese, though his eyes were blue. And by some twist of fate, this particular man was apparently an assassin hired to kill the young man.
The young man had no leisure to savor the irony of an assassin saving his life. He could only say, dispiritedly:

source.japanese:
【青年】
「功徳って、なんのだよう……」
source.english: “Merit? What for…?”

target.text: It was unclear which of the sword sheathed in its scabbard accompanied by that boastful remark and the green dragon crescent blade that had drawn so near to the young man was the more dangerous party here. The man, wearing a Japanese outfit unusual for a young man, even in this day and age, and furthermore, with Japanese phrenology yet possessed of blue eyes, was a murderer who had come to accept a request to murder this young man through some manner of fate, supposedly. The young man didn't have the composure to relish in the inherent humour of having his life saved by a murderer, and getting rather fed up with the situation,
【Young man】 「What kind of merit is that supposed to be……」

source.japanese:
【和服の男】
「そりゃお前、俺らに斬られ死にゃあ、俺らの懐にお足が入る」
source.english: “Simple. You die by my blade, and the money lands in my pocket.”

source.japanese:
【和服の男】
「俺への功徳になるだろうよ？」
source.english: “That'd earn me some merit, wouldn't it?”

source.japanese:
【青年】
「そんななぁ功徳って言うか───ひぃぃっ」
source.english: “Can you even call that merit—Aieee!”

target.text: 【Man in Japanese clothes】 「Well, y'see, if you're cut by my blade and croak, I'll get some scratch in my pocket.」
【Man in Japanese clothes】 「And that'll be plenty merit for me, no?」
【Young man】 「You can't call that meri─── HIIIH!」

source.japanese:
殺し屋に言い返す青年の体をかすめたのは、今度は銃弾だ。慌てて舷側の裡にしゃがみこんで、船縁から怖々覗けば、相手は相当に軽敏な船らしく、波間を切り開いて、もう服の釦[ボタン]や襯衣の縞を数えられるほど近くまでの肉迫だ。
　甲板には凶人ども、いかにも凶暴で獰猛そうなごろつきが満載され、どいつもこいつも殺意満々に目をぎらつかせているとくる。口々に罵り、口々におめきたてている。有り体に言って、殺す気一杯だ。誰を？　もちろんこの船の面子を。
source.english:
This time a bullet grazed him as he tried to answer back. He hastily crouched behind the bulwark and peered over the edge. The enemy vessel was fast and nimble, cutting through the waves until he could almost count the buttons on the men's clothes and the stripes on their shirts.
Her deck was crammed with thugs: vicious-looking, savage-looking men, every eye glittering with murderous intent. They cursed, they bellowed. In plain terms, they meant to kill. Whom? Everyone aboard this ship, of course.

target.text: This time, it was a bullet that grazed the young man about to make his retort to the murderer. He squatted down behind the ship's bulwark in a panic, and as he timidly peeked over the gunwale, there, the other party was cutting their way through the waves separating the two in a way truly befitting their light boat, closing in to the extent he could count the buttons on their clothes and the stripes on their undershirts.

The deck was full of ruffians, packed to the gills with the very picture of savage, ferocious rogues, one and all with eyes glinting with murderous desire. All of them swearing, screaming, and making noise. Frankly speaking, all of them ready to murder. Who? Why, the crew of this ship, of course.

source.japanese: 衣装こそ青年達と似たり寄ったりだが、その殺意たるやかつてマスケット銃とカトラスで七つの海を震え上がらせていた海賊どもに勝るとも劣らず、というより直系の子孫なのかもしれないが、とにかくあんな凶悪そうな連中を怒らせるなど、いったいこの船の連中は何をしでかしたのだ。
source.english: Their clothes differed little from those of the young man and his companions. Their bloodlust, however, rivaled that of the pirates who had once terrorized the seven seas with musket and cutlass. Perhaps they were their direct descendants. In any case, what on earth had this crew done to enrage such murderous bastards?

source.japanese: 青年はこんな上部甲板で刃と銃弾に晒されているよりは、と下層甲板に引っ込もうとずりずり膝這いを始めるのだが、その前に鬼をもひしぎそうな魁偉なる面貌の、ぬうと現れてずいと迫る。思わず腰を抜かしそうになる。
source.english: Rather than remain on the upper deck with bullets and blades flying about him, he began crawling on his knees toward the way below. Then an enormous, ferocious face rose in his path and bore down on him—a face that would have cowed a demon. His legs nearly gave out altogether.

target.text: While their outfits looked similar to the young man and his companions, with their murderous intent, musket rifles, and cutlasses, they'd be a match for the pirates who set the Seven Seas ashiver, or perhaps they might even be their direct descendants, but regardless, what in the world did the fellows on board this ship even do to anger these scoundrels so?

Rather than being exposed to gunfire and blades on the upper deck, the young man was just about ready to crawl on his knees to seek refuge below decks, but before he could, it suddenly appeared and drew close: it was a massive, grim mug that could overwhelm even an ogre. Instinctively, his legs gave out under him.

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「おい新前、貴様この忙しいときにどこに行こうってつもりだ」
source.english: “Hey, new boy. Where d'you think you're going at a time like this?”

source.japanese: 青年を遮[さえぎ]ったのは禿頭で、顔半面に龍の刺青のある初老の、いかにも頑丈そうで荒っぽそうな男で、これがこの船の水夫長なのだった。
source.english: The man barring his way was bald, getting on in years, and had a dragon tattooed across half his face. He looked tough, rough, and very solid. This was the ship's boatswain.

source.japanese:
【青年】
「どこにってその、このままだと弾に当たって痛くて死にそうなんで、ちょっと遮蔽のあるところに」
source.english: “Well, if I stay here, a bullet's going to hit me, and it'll hurt, and I'll probably die. So I thought I'd find a bit of cover.”

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「こざかしいこと抜かしてんな新前。いいか、むこうは大砲も積んでない。そんな相手に怖じけついてどうするか。あんなションベン弾など当たったところで穴が空くくらいなもんよ。怯んでるくらいなら、ほらお前も撃ち返せ」
source.english: “Don't get clever with me, new boy. They haven't even got a cannon! What are you scared of? Those pissy little bullets'll only put a hole in you. Quit cowering. Here—shoot back.”

target.text: 【Man with a terrifying face】 「Oi, green hand, just where were you about to slink off to while things are this damn busy?」
Obstructing the young man's path was a rough and tough middle-aged man with a bald dome and half his face inked in the shape of a dragon: it was none other than the ship's bosun.
【Young man】 「Where? Well, uh, if I stay here, at this rate, I'll be hit by a bullet and suffer a painful death, so, just somewhere a bit more sheltered.」

【Man with a terrifying face】 「You've got some nerve, green hand. Listen, they don't have any cannons. What is there to fear from their like? As if that spray of piss they call bullets could open so much as a hole in you. If you're so scared, then go on, shoot right back at them.」

source.japanese:
そういって手渡されたのが、持ちごたえのする拳銃という剥き出しの凶器だったのには、この船に乗り合わせるまではそれなりに平和な日々を送っていた青年にはあまりに露骨に過ぎたし、その銃はその銃で、弾倉というのがなかった。銃身後部にはパーカッションが具わっていた。彫金はそれなりに美々しいと言えば言えたが、今時先ごめ式であった。
　こんな骨董撃ち方も知らないし、撃ったところで当たりもしないだろう、それ以前に引き金引いた途端に暴発しそう。この襤褸船にはいかにも相応しく、こういう時代遅れの品物がごろごろ転がっているけれど、こんな物をよこされてもと青年は暗澹とした心地になる。
source.english:
He handed over a weighty pistol. To a young man whose life had been reasonably peaceful until he boarded this ship, the naked violence of the thing was altogether too blatant. Nor did it have a magazine. There was a percussion lock behind the barrel. The engraved metalwork was handsome enough, but a muzzle-loader? In this day and age?
He did not know how to fire this antique. If he managed it, he would never hit anything; more likely it would blow up the moment he pulled the trigger. Outdated rubbish like this lay everywhere aboard the decrepit vessel, and suited her perfectly. Having it thrust upon him only deepened his gloom.

source.japanese:
【青年】
「こんな骨董渡されたって。それに大体俺は、ただの船員で海兵隊でも何でもないですよう。撃ち合いなんてできませんってーの……」
source.english: “What am I supposed to do with an antique like this? And anyway, I'm just a sailor. I'm not a marine or anything. I can't go getting into gunfights…”

target.text: After being told as much, he was given something to fight them off, that something being an overtly lethal weapon in the form of a handgun, all too undisguised in its danger for this young man who had spent his days in relative peace until he was made to share his lot with this ship, and the gun itself was not possessed of what you could call a magazine. The rear part of the gun was equipped with a percussion cap. If pushed, he would admit that the chasing and repousse was quite beautiful, but it was a muzzleloader, in this day and age.

He didn't know how to shoot this antique, and he probably wouldn't hit anything, even if he could fire it, and before any of that, just pulling the trigger looked like it might make the gun explode. Befitting this ramshackle ship, this kind of antiquated article grew on trees here, but being handed something like this only left the young man with dark thoughts.

【Young man】 「And then you give me an ancient antique like this. First of all, I'm just a regular sailor, not part of a marine corps or anything. I'm telling you, I can't handle myself in a gunfight……」

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「がたがた逆らうな。陸育ちの娑婆造が。海兵もくそもあるか。だいたい見ろほら、こっちは、一等航海士様だって戦ってらあ」
source.english: “Quit your whining, you landlubber little shit. Marine, my ass. Look there—even our first mates are fighting.”

target.text: 【Man with a terrifying face】 「Cut the whiny backtalk. You landlubber milksop. Does it look like we have any marines here? Just take a look around. See, over there, even our prodigious first mates are fighting.」

source.japanese: と水夫長が指さす先は、上甲板中央の物見櫓───さよう物見櫓だ、八百八町の防火防犯の要の一つだった背高の奴だ。そんな物まで乗せているこの船はなんなのだという問いはまた置くとして、櫓台ではリーファージャケット、ミニスカートを勇ましく翻[ひるがえ]し、金髪を結い上げた二人の女が、飛び交う弾丸ものともせず足踏みしめ拳銃かざし（こちらは使い込んではいるようだが、それでも普通の回転式拳銃だ）て、ぴたりと息の合った連携で迫り来る敵船に撃ち返している。
source.english:
He pointed to the watchtower at the center of the upper deck. Yes, a watchtower: one of those tall structures that had helped keep the peace and watch for fires in Edo's ‘eight hundred and eight neighborhoods.’ Once again, let us put aside the question of why this ship carried such a thing.
On its platform stood two women with their blond hair pinned up, reefer jackets and miniskirts flaring bravely. Undaunted by the flying bullets, they planted their feet and fired back at the approaching ship in perfect concert. Their pistols looked well used, but at least they were ordinary revolvers.

target.text: And following the Bosun's pointing finger, there, on the midship of the upper deck, stood the watchtower─── Indeed, the watchtower, the tall fellow that served as one of the keystones of preventing fires and crime from one side of Edo to the other.

Setting aside the question of why this ship would be furnished with such for now, there, on the observation deck, stood two women with hair of spun gold tied in buns, clad in reefer jackets with miniskirts gallantly fluttering about, utterly uncaring of the exchange of bullets around them, feet firmly planted and guns held aloft (these guns also seemed like they'd seen their share of use, but even so, they were regular revolvers), firing back at the enemy ship drawing ever closer with perfect coordination, even down to their breathing.

source.japanese: お互いがお互いの死角を巧みに補い、あるいは時に一方が肩を銃架代わりに使わせて撃ち手を安定させ、拳銃とは思えないくらいの精密射撃を可能にする妙手。伸びやかに翳[かざ]される腕、位置取り滑[なめ]らかな足使い、その動きの淀みないこと、まるで一つの生き物の如しで───実際一等航海士の二人は、右と左寸分違わぬ同じ顔をしている。それもそのはず、彼女達は双子なのだ。一人が撃つ、一人が片割れを狙っていた悪漢を狙撃する。一人が弾を切らす、一人がすぐさま換えの弾倉を手渡す。時にくるくると目まぐるしく、時にぴたりと、見得を切るように大胆な姿勢に静止して。
source.english:
Each deftly covered the other's blind spots; at times one even lent the other her shoulder for a gun rest, steadying her aim and making possible a precision scarcely credible from a handgun. The free sweep of their arms, the smooth play of their feet as they took position—nothing in their motion caught or faltered. They moved like a single living creature.
Indeed, the two first mates—one to the right, one to the left—had identical faces down to the last detail. Naturally enough: they were twins. One fired; the other picked off a thug who had been aiming at her sister. One ran dry; the other instantly passed her a fresh cylinder. One moment they spun and wheeled in a dizzying blur, the next they stopped dead in a bold, theatrical pose.

target.text: One would cover the blind spots of the other adroitly, then at times, one would use the other's shoulder in place of a rifle stand to stabilize the shooter's aim, a brilliant move allowing precision shooting unthinkable of a handgun. Arms held aloft comfortably, legs fluidly getting into position, the absence of hesitation in those actions almost like a singular living being───and in fact, the two first mates had faces so perfectly similar you could not tell them apart.

And of course that would be so, for the two women were twins. One took a shot, the other sniped the raider aiming at her other half. One ran out of bullets, the other promptly handed her a replacement cylinder. At times whirling around dizzyingly fast, at times suddenly stopping, ceasing movement in a bold position as though they were striking a pose.

source.japanese:
【双子の女】
「あっはっはっはーっ、ほーら鴨撃ちだ！」
source.english: “Ahahahaha! Come on—it's a duck shoot!”

target.text: 【Female twin】 「Ah-ha-ha-ha, it's like shooting ducks!」

source.japanese:
【双子の女】
「あっはっはっはーっ、銃は鼓動に合わせて撃つ、それだけで狙いも技もいらないねえ！」
source.english: “Ahahahaha! Just fire with your heartbeat! No aiming, no skill required!”

source.japanese: 舞踏のようなポーズで傍若無人に撃ちまくり、そのくせ向こうの弾は届かない。呆れてしまうくらい好き勝手だが、青年は二人の無茶振りより、ついついそのひらひら舞い踊るプリーツスカートから伸びる太腿とその奥に、目がいってしまうわけで。つい先刻に死にかけていたにもかかわらず盛んな助平心の青年を嗤うべきか、修羅場を忘れさせるほどの引力を放つとは、やはりスカートの奥の暗がりこそさすがと激賞するべきなのか、ともかく位置としては高い位置、窃視には絶好のアングルなのに、どうしてか深秘の布地は寸毫もその尊影を垣間見せる事はなかった。
source.english:
They fired with all the heedless abandon of dancers striking poses, and still the enemy's bullets never touched them. Their freedom was absurd; yet the young man's attention fixed less on their mad performance than on the thighs emerging from those fluttering pleated skirts—and on whatever lay beyond.
Should one laugh at a young man whose lechery remained so vigorous though he had nearly died only moments before? Or lavish praise on the darkness beneath a skirt for exerting a pull strong enough to make him forget the carnage? In any event, the women stood above him at a perfect angle for peeping; yet somehow the sacred cloth concealed within refused to show so much as a hair's breadth of its august countenance.

target.text: 【Female twin】 「Ah-ha-ha-ha, as long as we shoot our guns to the rhythm of our hearts, we don't need no aiming or technique!」

Audaciously unleashing a hail of bullets all around them in theatrical poses, yet no bullets reached them in return. It was astonishingly self-indulgent, but the young man was not so much focused on their reckless actions; instead, his eyes wandered to the depths of those thighs stretching out from below the pleat skirts dancing heedlessly in the wind.

Perhaps this young man, dirty mind firing on all cylinders despite his brush with death just moments before, should be sneered at, or perhaps the darkness in the depths of the skirts should receive lavish praise for holding a gravitational pull powerful enough to make him forget the scene of carnage; regardless, they were in a high position, yet despite it being the perfect angle for peeking, for some reason, that most deeply mysterious and profound of fabrics showed nary a glimpse of its esteemed visage.

source.japanese:
【男の子】
「航海士の二人、いっつもあんな派手に動いてミニスカひらひらだけどー」
source.english: “Those two navigators—they're always zipping around so flashily, their miniskirts fluttering and all—”

target.text: 【Boy】 「The two number ones always move around so flamboyantly, miniskirts fluttering about.」

source.japanese:
【男の子】
「あれ、どうやってもパンツ見えないんだ。
　ふっしぎだよねえ」
source.english:
“Huh. No matter how hard I try, I can never see their underwear.
Weird, isn’t it?”

target.text: 【Boy】 「But you just can't get a glimpse of their panties. Strange, isn't it?」

source.japanese: 上甲板を走り回って、あちこちに甲斐甲斐しきバリケードを築いて廻っていたセーラー襟[えり]の男の子達がひそひそと囁きかわす。この少年達は船の下級水夫なのだが、奇妙な事にどれこれも同じ体格で同じ顔をしている事。航海士の双子程度ならまだ納得がいくけれど、さすがにこの下級水夫達の何人も何人もいて皆そっくり同じ顔というのは、五つ子や六つ子などの言葉で片付く問題ではない。
source.english: The sailor-collared boys who had been scurrying all over the upper deck, busily throwing up barricades here and there, exchanged these remarks in whispers. They were the ship's junior sailors, and there was one peculiar thing about them: every last one had the same build and the same face. Twins among the first mates were one thing. But junior sailors by the dozen, every one with precisely the same face—quintuplets and sextuplets could not explain that away.

source.japanese: なんなんだろうなこいつらはと、見るたび怪訝に思う青年なのだが、そんな事を思う間にも敵方の船は肉迫し、とうとう接舷の為の鉤付きロープまでもが投げ込まれてくる。一等航海士は善戦しているものの、いかんせんこちらには火力が足りない。舷側に引っかかったフックロープを斧で叩き切りつつ、水夫長が怒鳴る。
source.english: Every time he saw them, the young man wondered just what they were. Even as he wondered now, the enemy drew closer, until grappling lines began landing aboard. The first mates fought well, but the ship simply lacked firepower. Hacking through a rope hooked over the rail, the boatswain roared:

target.text: Running to and fro on the upper deck, briskly and diligently building barricades here and there, were young boys in sailor suits exchanging hushed whispers with one another. These young lads were the low-ranking sailors, but queerly enough, all of them shared the exact same build and face. The mates, given their status as twins, were certainly understandable, but with so many sailors possessing the exact same face, this far exceeded the scope of what could be hand-waved away as quintuplets or sextuplets.

What are these guys even, the young man thought, finding it more and more suspicious every time he saw them, but while he was pondering this, the enemy vessel had closed in and at long last begun tossing over hooked ropes to come alongside. As fiercely as the first mates fought, they were, unfortunately, lacking in firepower. While cutting down the hooked ropes caught on the bulwark, the Bosun yelled furiously.

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「ええくそ、役にたたねえな新前。
　この期に及んでがたがた言ってるなら、そうさな、船長を隠してこい」
source.english:
“Fuck's sake, new boy, you're useless!
If you're still going to stand there whining, go put the captain away.”

target.text: 【Man with a terrifying face】 「Grrh, damn it all, you're useless, green hand. If you still have time to whine after all this, let's see, go hide the captain.」

source.japanese: 顎をしゃくる先に船長が居る。このでたらめな船の、この水夫長が船長と仰ぐなら、それさぞかし凄まじい怪人なのではないかと誰もが身構えるだろう───しかし水夫長が指したのは、ちびでがりがりにやせっぽちで、その上髪と肌は真っ白、目は真っ赤の白子で、栄養不良の兎を思わせる女の子。洋上に繰り広げられたる修羅場に完全に恐慌を来し、意味もなく甲板をかけずりまわっては索具や船具とぶつかってひっくり返り、その度に鼻血や打ち身を増やしていく始末の。
source.english:
He jerked his chin toward the captain. Anyone might have braced themselves: if this extraordinary ship's boatswain acknowledged someone as his captain, surely that someone must be a monster beyond imagining.
But the girl he indicated was tiny and painfully thin. Her hair and skin were snow white, her eyes bright red: an albino, like an underfed rabbit. The battle on the open sea had sent her into a complete panic. She ran aimlessly about the deck, collided with rigging and fittings, and fell over. Each fall added another bruise or nosebleed to her collection.

target.text: There, in the direction he was pointing at with his chin, stood the captain. The captain of this ramshackle ship, the man this Bosun would call captain: anyone would certainly be on guard, ready to meet some manner of awe-inspiring monster───but in the direction the Bosun signalled, there stood a tiny bag of skin and bones, an albino with hair and skin of pure white and eyes bright red, a young girl bringing to mind an emaciated rabbit. Thoroughly struck with terror at the battlefield unfolding on the ocean, running around fruitlessly in wild abandon on the deck, bumping into rigging and fittings, toppling over, the only thing to show for it more bruises and a bloodier nose.

source.japanese:
【アルビノの女の子】
「あーっ、あーっ、弾いやあ、ナイフ怖い、怖い、死んじゃう、あーーっっ」
source.english: “Aah! Aah! No bullets! Knives are scary! Scary! I'm going to die! Aaaaaah!”

source.japanese: しまいに腰を抜かして珍妙な格好ではいずり回る様は、滑稽というか哀れというか、とにかく目も当てられない有様であり、青年はやむなく彼女の元に駆け寄って、小脇に抱えあげる。笑ってしまうほど軽いし、じたばたと暴れさせる手足も微笑ましいくらい力ない。青年は船長を抱えて、このような場合どうするか、叩き込まれていたとおりに従う。すなわち、中層甲板に降りていって、『せんちょう用』と大書された『箱』の中に彼女を押し込めてくるのだ
source.english:
At last her legs gave way, and she began crawling in a grotesque posture. Comic, pitiable—whatever one called it, the sight was unbearable. The young man had no choice but to run over and scoop her under his arm. She was laughably light. Her flailing limbs were almost endearing in their feebleness.
With the captain under his arm, he set about doing as he had been drilled to do in such an emergency: take her down to the middle deck and stuff her into a box boldly labeled FOR THE CAPTAIN.

target.text: 【Albino girl】 「Aah, aah, don't like bullets, knives are scary, scary, gonna die, aaaaah!」

After her legs finally gave out, she crawled around in a bizarre manner; did it make a comedic or pitiful sight? Regardless, it was a state of affairs hard to watch, and the young man, perforce, ran to the girl's side and lifted her by the armpits. Laughably light, floundering, struggling limbs amusingly powerless. The young man carried the captain and did as had been beaten into him already. That is to say, he descended to the middle deck, and he stuffed the girl inside a『box』with 『Captain's』written on it in big letters.

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「ただし───
　船長めを『しまって』きたら、すぐに戻ってくるんだぞ。撃ち合いができないんなら、代わりに斬り合いやってもらうしかねえからな」
source.english:
“And listen—once you've put her away,
get straight back up here! If you can't shoot, you'll have to fight with a blade instead!”

source.japanese:
【青年】
「えー……」
source.english: “Oh, come on…”

source.japanese: 降りていく青年の背なに降りかかった水夫長の怒声は、彼を頼りにしていると言うより、敵の的の散らす員数合わせ程度にしか考えていない事が見え隠れしていて、ただでさえろくな持ち合わせのない青年の士気をいよいよ萎えさせた。
source.english: The boatswain's shout pursued him down the stairs. It hinted not so much at any confidence in him as a desire to give the enemy one more target to spread their fire over. What little morale he possessed dwindled further.

target.text: 【Man with a terrifying face】 「However─── Once that damn captain of ours has been "put away", you come back here immediately. If you can't handle a gunfight, you're gonna have to settle for sword-fighting instead.」
【Young man】 「Ehhー……」

The angry roar from the Bosun slamming into the descending young man's back made it seem that rather than relying upon him, he was instead to be used merely to split the attentions of the enemy raiders, and barely present as the young man's morale was to begin with, even that was finally starting to wither away.

source.japanese: 全長一〇〇米程度のこの船の、この規模の船の常として昇降段は狭苦しく、小柄で女の子とはいえ抱えて降りるのはそれなりに骨だが、青年はそれでも段を踏み外して尻打ちつけて降る事もなく中層甲板に抜ける。船長が藁細工のように軽い事も幸いしたし、海が凪なら揺れも足を取るまでには至らない。それでも解放された上甲板から狭苦しい船内通路に降ると、足下に波のうねりが確かに意識された。
source.english: The ship was roughly a hundred meters long, and, as was usual on a vessel of that size, her companionways were cramped. Carrying a girl down one was awkward, however small she might be. Still, he reached the middle deck without missing a step or landing on his backside. It helped that the captain was as light as a straw doll. The sea was calm, too; the rolling did not quite unsettle his feet. Yet once he left the open deck for the confined passage below, he felt the swell distinctly beneath him.

source.japanese: 通路の鋼板の継ぎ目やのたうつ配管を躱して走られる程度にはこの船での時間を過ごしていた青年は、やがて行き当たりの片隅の頑丈そうな鋲打ちの箱を見て、白子の娘を小脇から下ろした、彼女はぺたりと崩れたが、いや、いやとまだ抜けたままの腰で後退る。
source.english: He had spent long enough aboard to run down the passage without tripping on the seams in the steel plates or the twisting pipes. At the far end, a sturdy-looking riveted box stood in a corner. He lowered the albino girl from under his arm. She collapsed onto the floor, then began shuffling backward, her legs still useless, saying no, no.

target.text: As was typical of ships of this scale, around 100 metres in total length, the ladderwells of this ship were cramped, so even if the girl was small of stature, it was still quite laborious to descend them while carrying her; still, the young man made it to the middle deck without missing a step and hitting his bum on the way down. It was fortunate the girl was so light it seemed she was made of straw, and the ocean was calm, so the shaking didn't impact his balance. Despite this, having descended from the freeing upper deck to the cramped internal passageways, he could certainly sense the swelling of the waves below his feet.

The young man had spent enough time on this ship to dodge the piping squirming out from between the seams of the iron plates coating the passageway while running past, and as he finally spotted the sturdy-looking riveted box in the corner of a dead end, he lowered the albino girl by her armpits, and she flopped down, still repeating words of displeasure, backing away from him with legs still powerless.

source.japanese:
【アルビノの女の子】
「やああ、やだよう。暗くて狭くて臭いよう、怖いよう」
source.english: “Noooo! I don't want to! It's dark and cramped and smelly! It's scary!”

source.japanese:
【青年】
「臭いのはお前さんが中で小便漏らすからだし、甲板に出てるともっと怖い目に遭うと思うよ？」
source.english: “It smells because you keep peeing in it. And I think you'll find scarier things than that up on deck.”

target.text: 【Albino girl】 「Nooo, don't want it. It's dark and cramped and smelly, it's scary.」
【Young man】 「It's smelly because you pissed yourself in there, but I think you'll be in for a much scarier time up on the deck, okay?」

source.japanese:
【アルビノの女の子】
「うう、怖いのや。でもおしっこ漏りる。
　あ、あ、今、出そうだよぅ」
source.english:
“Uuuh, I don't want scary things. But I can't hold my pee.
Ah, ah, it's going to come out now…”

source.japanese:
とにかく言われたとおりに中層甲板の箱に船長、白子の少女を押し込めようとすると、やはりそんな暗くて狭くて汚いところに閉じこめられるのは厭なのだろう、実際蓋を開ければ鼻につんと刺さるアンモニアの臭気、船内暮らしでは様々な悪臭が付き物とはいえ、余り歓迎できたものではないのは青年にも共感できたし、か細い手足を懸命に突っ張って抗[あらが]う船長には、赤むけの肌に塩を擦りこまれた白兎のそぞろ哀れもあったが、心を鬼にして青年は箱に少女を押しこんだ。
　その際掴んだのは胸だったり尻だったりしたようにも思えたけれど、意地汚く楽しむほどの柔らかさもなく、細こい骨の感触ばかりが手に透けて、何やら青年は餓死寸前の仔猫を拾いあげた時の居たたまれ無さに見舞われたという。
source.english:
Anyway, when he tried to shove the captain—the albino girl—into the box on the middle deck as instructed, she naturally balked at being shut inside somewhere so dark, cramped, and filthy. When he raised the lid, a sharp reek of ammonia struck his nose. Bad smells were part of life aboard ship, but even he could sympathize with her reluctance to face this one. The captain braced her spindly limbs in desperate resistance, as pitiful as a white rabbit with salt rubbed into its raw skin, but the young man hardened his heart and forced her into the box.
 He seemed to remember grabbing her breasts or buttocks in the process, but there was no softness there to savor—only the feel of delicate bones beneath his hands, filling him with the same unbearable pity as picking up a kitten on the brink of starvation.

source.japanese:
【青年】
「ああもう埒があかない、ほら、閉めといてやるから、出すときにはこっちに、な？」
source.english: “Oh, this is getting us nowhere. Look, I'll shut the lid for you. If you need to go, use this, all right?”

target.text: 【Albino girl】 「Uuh, don't like scary. But can't hold it. Ah, ah, pee's about to come out, right nooow!」

Regardless, he pushed the captain, the albino girl, inside the box as he was told to, but surely it must have been unpleasant to be shut inside such a dark, cramped, and filthy place, and when he actually opened the lid, his nose was met with the stinging stench of ammonia; while you get used to many awful smells living on a ship, the young man empathized with the fact that this was hardly a welcome situation, and the captain struggled for dear life with her pencil-thin limbs stretched out, invoking the pitiful image of rubbing salt on the grazed skin of a little white bunny, but the young man turned his heart to stone and pushed the girl in the box.

He did consider taking the opportunity to grab at her chest or her behind, but they were not nearly soft enough to elicit such wolfish desires; all that his hands were met with was the hard touch of slender bones, and an unpleasant awkwardness akin to picking up a little kitten on the verge of starvation befell the young man.
【Young man】 「Aaah, come on, we're not getting anywhere here. Look, I'm closing the lid, and when you need to piss, do it in this, okay?」

source.japanese: 青年、指示されていたとおりに「おまる」を取り出し、一緒に箱の中に押し込め、ついでにポケットからあめ玉一つ取り出して船長の手に握らせる。
source.english: Following his instructions, he produced a chamber pot and pushed it into the box with her. Then he took a candy from his pocket and put it in her hand.

source.japanese:
【青年】
「これあげるから、大人しくしとき」
source.english: “You can have this. Now be good.”

target.text: Just as he'd been instructed, the young man took out a chamber pot, stuffed it into the box with her, and while he was at it, grabbed a piece of candy from his pocket and put it in the captain's hand.
【Young man】 「I'm giving you this, so behave.」

source.japanese:
【アルビノの女の子】
「あ、えへー……。あめちゃん。
　クロ、あめちゃん好き」
source.english:
“Oh, hehe… Candy.
Kuro likes candy.”

source.japanese:
【青年】
「うんうん」
source.english: “Yes, yes.”

target.text: 【Albino girl】 「Ah, ehe……. Candy. Kuro loves candy.」
【Young man】 「Uh-huh.」

source.japanese: 早速に包み紙を解して口に収めてころころころ、頬っぺた膨らませて船長は甘さに判りやすく気を取られる、もともと二つの事を一緒くたに扱える容量は彼女の頭にない、その隙に適当に押しこめて、蓋を閉じると、やはり暗いのは厭なのか、しばらく暴れる様子だったが、ようやく鎮まって、かと思うと、巌に清水を流すような気配が伝わった。岩に清流といえば聞こえはいい。がこの箱の中からとあっては、船長が早速用を足しているのであろう。何のかんのと限界だったと見える。
source.english:
She promptly unwrapped it and popped it into her mouth. Round and round it went, bulging her cheek. The sweetness distracted her at once; her head had never had room for two things at the same time. He took the opportunity to tuck her in any old how and close the lid. She struggled for a while, apparently still unhappy with the dark, then finally settled. A sound followed, like clear water running over rocks.
Clear water over rocks: a lovely image. Coming from this box, however, it probably meant the captain had already begun relieving herself. For all her protests, she must have been at her limit.

target.text: She immediately removed the wrapping, put it in her mouth, rolled it around, and with puffed-up cheeks, it was plain to tell the captain had been thoroughly distracted, not that the girl's head had enough capacity to handle two things at once in the first place; he took the chance, pushed her in haphazardly, then closed the lid, but perhaps the darkness really was too much for her, for she struggled for a little while, and just as he thought she finally quieted down, there came the sound of spring water trickling over boulders. That had a nice, poetic ring to it. But inside this box, it seemed the urge to do her business had already overcome the captain. It certainly seemed like she'd reached a limit of some sort.

source.japanese:
───暗い箱の中でおまるに跨[またが]り放尿する少女、というイメージを一瞬でも想起しそうになって、そのいかがわしさに慌てて振り払う。零さないでくれよと祈ったけれど、何やら暗澹とした心地は抑えきれない。
　……くどいようだが、この女の子がこの船の船長だ。紛れ込んでしまったどこかの可哀相な子などではなく、まぎれもなく船長なのだ。青年にしても未だに信じられないが。
source.english:
For one instant he found himself on the verge of picturing a girl astride a chamber pot, urinating in a darkened box, and hastily drove the indecent image from his mind. Please, don’t spill it, he prayed, though he could not suppress the gloom settling over him.
…Not to belabor the point, but this girl was the captain of the ship. She was not some unfortunate child who had wandered aboard by mistake. She was, beyond all question, the captain. The young man himself still found it difficult to believe.

target.text: ───For an instant, it called to mind the image of the girl inside the dark box straddling the chamber pot while urinating, but he excised such indecent thoughts in a hurry. He made a prayer that nothing would spill over, but he could not stop the sombre mood that overcame him. ……This might be getting repetitious by now, but this girl was the captain of this ship. She was not some hapless girl who had managed to stumble her way onto the ship, no, she was, without doubt, the captain. The young man himself still didn't quite believe it.

source.japanese: さて、と青年は、水夫長の言いつけなどてんで守る気がなく、事が済むまでどこかの隙間に隠れていようと辺りを見回すのだが、その時近くの伝声管から声が響いたのに、ひぃ、とすくみ上がる。
source.english: Now then. He had no intention whatever of obeying the boatswain. He looked around for some gap where he could hide until it was all over. Then a voice sounded from a nearby speaking tube, and he froze with a squeak.

source.japanese:
【伝声管からの声】
『おやおや。君、いったいそんなところで何をやっているんです』
source.english: “Well, well. What on earth are you doing there?”

source.japanese:
【伝声管からの声】
『ほら、上では水夫長殿がきっとかんかんになっていますよ……』
source.english: “You know, our boatswain must be absolutely furious up above…”

source.japanese: 物柔らかな低音は、水夫長の上から殴りつけるような胴間声と対照的に穏やかなのに恐ろしい、ベクトルが違えどどちらも青年には恐ろしい。
source.english: The soft, low voice was gentle—terrifyingly gentle—in perfect contrast to the boatswain’s bludgeoning bass from on high. Their vectors differed, but to the young man both were equally terrifying.

source.japanese:
【青年】
「き、機関長!?　なんで俺がここにいるって」
source.english: “Ch-Chief? How did you know I was here?”

source.japanese: 伝声管伝いでいくらか声は歪んで、それでも管の向こうは船の心臓、機関室の主である事には間違いなくって、青年には罐から漏れる赤い明かりの中囁く黒衣の姿が目に浮かぶよう。あの男は機関室から滅多に離れる事はないのに、何故だか船内の状況を蜘蛛の巣の中心に位置しているかに把握している節がある。
source.english: The speaking tube distorted the voice somewhat, but there was no mistaking the master of the engine room, the chamber that was the ship’s heart. The young man could almost see the black-clad figure whispering amid the red light leaking from the boilers. The man scarcely ever left his engine room, yet somehow he appeared to grasp the state of everything aboard as though he sat at the center of a spider’s web.

source.japanese: 大体青年が呼びかけた覚えもないのに、彼にいちばん近い伝声管から語りかけてきたでないか。その際先程までは確実に閉まっていた筈の、錆の浮いた伝声管の蓋がかたりと自然に開いたのを見たような気もするが、やはり気のせいきっと気のせい。
source.english: The young man had not called him, after all. He had simply spoken from whichever tube was nearest. At that moment, the young man thought he had seen its rusty lid click open by itself, though he was sure it had been closed a moment earlier. But that must have been his imagination. Surely his imagination.

source.japanese:
【伝声管からの声】
『さて、ねえ。ああ君、水夫長に伝えてくれたまえ。船の足をもっと上げたかったから、こっちにももっと水夫を回してくれ、と』
source.english: “Well, now. Ah, would you tell the boatswain? I was hoping to get more speed out of her, so he must send me more men down here.”

source.japanese:
【青年】
「イェ、イェッサー！」
source.english: “Y-Yes, sir!”

source.japanese: 上甲板から層を隔てた船内通路までは上の騒乱も届かず、忘れてしまった事にして戦闘が収まるまでやり過ごそうとすれば此れ式とくる。
source.english: Here in the ship's passageway, one deck below the upper deck, none of the uproar reached him. He had only to pretend he had forgotten all about it and lie low until the fighting ended—and then this had to happen.

source.japanese: 上甲板に舞い戻ろうと駆け出したものの、やはりどうあっても気が進まない、やがて足は鈍ってしまいに嘆息して立ち止まり、傍らの隔壁に額を押し当て寄り掛かった、壁は心地よくひんやりとしており、ただこうしげしげ仔細に眺めると、ひどく古びて荒れているのが感じられる。
source.english: He broke into a run toward the upper deck, but his heart simply was not in it. His steps slowed. At last he stopped with a sigh and leaned his forehead against a bulkhead. The metal was pleasantly cool, though at such close quarters he could see how terribly old and battered it was.

source.japanese:
この船の船式はどうにも奇妙で、青年にはその船齢だって見当がつかない。長く続いた大戦以前の就航で有ることは間違いなしの老朽艦だが、もっと得体の知れない歳月をあちこちに潜[ひそ]ませているのがこの船だ。
　一時の感慨に水夫長の怒声も機関長の督促も心からおいやられ、隔壁の冷たさにしばし慰め求めた青年は、しかし安らぐ暇など遠いようで、また呼びかける声があった。
source.english:
The ship's design was so strange that he could not even guess her age. She was certainly an old vessel, launched before the protracted Great War. But here and there she seemed to harbor years of a far less fathomable kind.
For a moment, the thought drove both the boatswain's shouts and the chief engineer's demands from his mind. He sought a little comfort in the cool bulkhead. Rest, however, was apparently still a distant prospect. Another voice called to him.

target.text: Well now, the young man thought; not feeling very inclined to follow the orders of the Bosun, he started looking around the area for a corner to hide in until the whole affair was over, but at that moment, a voice resounded from the nearby voice pipe, and he cowered in fright with a squeak.
【Voice from the voice pipe】 『Goodness me. You there, what in the heavens do you think you're doing in a place like this?』
【Voice from the voice pipe】 『Come now, I'm certain our dear Bosun must be positively outraged up above by now……』

A mild-mannered bass, marking a great contrast to the bellowing roars of the Bosun striking hard from above; mellow yet terrifying, entirely different ends of the spectrum, and yet both struck fear into the young man's heart.
【Young man】 「Chi-, Chief Engineer!? How do you even know I'm here?」

The voice transmitted through the voice pipe was distorted, but even so, there was no doubt that it was the master of the ship's beating heart, the engine room, standing on the other side, and the young man could see the image of the black-clad man whispering in the red glow leaking out from the boiler clearly in his mind. Even though that man almost never left the engine room, he somehow had a way of being informed of the exact situation inside the ship at all times, like he were sitting right in the middle of a giant spider web.

The young man did not even recall being summoned in the first place, and had he not spoken to him from the voice pipe closest to him? And it was most definitely closed just a moment ago; he almost felt like the lid of the rusty voice pipe had opened entirely on its own, but it must have been his imagination, yes, surely.
【Voice from the voice pipe】 『Well, who can say. Oh yes, you, please do convey the following to the Bosun. I want to increase our speed, so assign more hands to my station. That is all.』
【Young man】 「Ye-, Yessir!】

Separated as they were from the upper deck, the mayhem up above did not reach the passageways, and if he simply forgot about it all and waited until the fighting was over, it wouldn't amount to much anyway.

He began running to make his way back to the upper deck, but he just couldn't bring himself to do so, and in the end, he came to a halt, legs leaden, heaving a deep, lamenting sigh, pushing his brow against the nearby bulkhead, but comfortably cool as the wall was, merely staring this closely at the details of it, it felt horribly old and dilapidated.

This ship's design truly was strange, and the young man could not estimate just how old it was. The ship was decrepit enough to very possibly have entered service before the long-lasting great war, and this ship must have drifted about in hiding here and there for an even longer, indeterminate amount of time. This fleeting sentiment had dispelled the Bosun's bellows and the Chief Engineer's urging from his mind, and the young man sought relief in the coolness of the bulkhead for a little while, but the time for repose yet seemed distant, for once more, a voice called out to him.

source.japanese:
【？？？】
「ちょうど良いところにいらしたわね」
source.english: “You've come at just the right moment.”

source.japanese: 艶やかで、天鵞織を宛がわれたような、成熟した女の声。なのに青年は、先ほど伝声管で機関長に注意された時と同じくらい、いや下手をするとそれよりもすくみ上がる。怖々振り向くまでもなく、相手は誰だかわかっている。
source.english: A mature woman’s voice, lustrous and velvet-lined. Yet the young man shrank from it as badly as he had when the chief engineer addressed him through the speaking tube—perhaps worse. He did not need to turn fearfully around to know who it was.

source.japanese: ───あの女だ。
source.english: —That woman.

source.japanese: なにを血迷ったか、この地獄のような船に好きこのんで客として乗りこんで、どこかの港で降りる風もなく無為の日々を送っている彼女は、臈長けた年増の美女なのに、青年はなぜかこの女性が恐ろしくてたまらなく、そして彼女の言うことには逆らいがたい。諦めて踵を返せば、船室の扉が招くように開け放たれてある。
source.english:
Whatever possessed her, she had chosen to board this hellish ship as a passenger. She spent her days in idleness and showed no sign of getting off at any port. An older beauty, poised and accomplished—and for some reason the young man was utterly terrified of her. He found it just as hard to disobey her.
Resigned, he turned. Her cabin door stood open in invitation.

target.text: 【???】 「Why, you showed up at just the right time.」

A voice belonging to a mature woman, mellow and as if wrapped in velvet. And yet, the young man, just as badly as when he had been admonished by the Chief Engineer through the voice pipe a little earlier, no, perhaps even more so, cowered in terror. He was already well aware of who it was before he'd finished fearfully turning around,
───It was THAT woman.

She must have lost her mind, boarding this hellish ship as a passenger by choice; this woman, showing no signs of disembarking at some port somewhere, simply letting the days pass her by in idleness, was an elegantly mature, beautiful woman, and yet for some reason, this young man was so scared of her that he could barely stand it, and furthermore, he had a hard time defying her word. When he spun on his heel in resignation, the door to the stateroom had already been left open as if inviting him inside.

source.japanese:
誘う声招く扉、そして相手が熟れた美人とくればこの不格好な船の中、澱んだ空気に艶を撒いて潤して、風変わりな快楽の時間に変えてくれる機会なのに、青年の足取りは慎重に鈍く、そろそろと船室を覗きこむと、織物張られた壁に豪奢な寝台、花を飾れば抜かりなく葡萄酒の瓶も籠に収まって、空気さえ別ごしらえに秘めやかに甘い。
　そこだけ何の豪華客船の一室かという景色の一等船室であり、準備よろしい卓上のカードの配置さえ、何やら秘め事のニュアンス含ませた符号のようにさえ受け取れる、それほどまでに女の微笑は艶めいて、爛熟した美花から振り零される蜜となって、青年の目とそして、股ぐらを絡めとった。
source.english:
A beckoning voice, an open door, a ripe beauty within. Here was a chance to lend the stale air of this misshapen ship a little sensual warmth, to turn the hours to an uncommon sort of pleasure. Yet his steps were slow and wary. He peered into the cabin. Fabric covered the walls; the bed was sumptuous. There were flowers, a bottle of wine in a basket. Even the air seemed specially prepared, secretly sweet.
This first-class cabin might have belonged to a luxury liner. The cards laid ready on the table almost looked like a coded invitation to some private indulgence. Such was the sensuality of her smile: honey spilling from a flower in full bloom, ensnaring his eyes—and his groin.

source.japanese:
【青年】
「な、なんでしょーか」
source.english: “Wh-What is it?”

source.japanese:
【女客】
「貴方、ちょうど良いところに。退屈してたの。皆さんなんだかばたばたしてしまって」
source.english: “You couldn't have come at a better time. I was bored. Everyone seems to be running about.”

source.japanese:
【女客】
「貴方、せっかくなのだから、カードのお相手をなさい。一人で退屈だったのよ」
source.english: “Now that you're here, you can play cards with me. I've been so bored on my own.”

source.japanese:
事も無げに言い放つ女客は円卓を寄せた寝台に横臥して、半身をもたげる挙措の端々に滲ませる、優美な緩慢と淫靡な含みは無意識のものであろう。こうして彼女はあくまで自然に、生来の習性のように男を惑わせる。
　こういう女性と交わす遣り取りがカードの遊戯だけで済むとは到底思えず、既に内心穏やかならざる疼きを覚え始める青年は、これと向き合うといつだってそうだと臍を噛む。恐ろしさと隣り合わせの情欲の熾火、いつ盛ってしまうか知れたものではなく、そうなったら取り返しのつかない事になる。
　どれだけこの部屋が豪奢を誇ろうとも、葡萄酒が最上等の甘美であろうとも、深入りは避けたい。
source.english:
The woman passenger spoke as though it were nothing. Reclining on the bed beside the round table, she raised herself on one elbow; every small movement betrayed a graceful languor, an indecent suggestion of which she was presumably unaware. She bewitched men as naturally as breathing, as though seduction were an instinct she had been born with.
He could not imagine any exchange with such a woman ending at a mere game of cards. An unruly ache had already begun inside him, and he ground his teeth: this always happened when he faced her. Desire smoldered beside fear, liable at any moment to flare into heat—and once it did, there would be no taking it back.
However sumptuous the room, however exquisite the wine, he wanted no part of going in too deep.

source.japanese:
そもそも今船はどういう状況にあるのか。
　思い直した時、これまで中層甲板では遠かった怒号の響き、唐突に強まってここまで伝わってきて、上甲板では遂に敵方が乗りこんできたらしい、危急の際をつげる。なのに女は意に介した様子もなく、青年を差し招く。
source.english:
Besides—what situation was the ship in at this very moment?
The thought had scarcely returned to him when the shouting, distant until now on the middle deck, abruptly swelled and carried all the way to the cabin. The enemy had apparently boarded the upper deck at last; the uproar proclaimed a crisis. The woman, however, showed no sign of caring. She beckoned the young man nearer.

target.text: A seductive voice, an inviting door, and a beautiful, mature woman as a partner would sweep aside the stagnant air of this misshapen ship and wet it with charm and allure, but despite presenting an opportunity for an hour of peculiar pleasure, the young man's footsteps were slow and deliberate, and as he gingerly peeked into the room, he saw tapestry-draped walls and an opulent bed, thoughtfully adorned with flowers and a bottle of grape wine nestled in a basket; even the air itself was prepared in a particular manner harbouring a hidden sweetness.

That in itself could be the scene of any first-class stateroom on a luxury passenger ship, but even the cards placed in full readiness on top of the table could be taken as some sort of code carrying implications of some secret, that was how brilliantly the woman's smile gleamed with feminine charm; it became honey overflowing from a beautiful flower in full bloom, entangling itself with the young man's eyes, and his crotch.
【Young man】 「Wh-, what could you possibly need?」
【Female passenger】 「You came at just the right time, dear. I was bored. All the others simply scurried away in a hurry for some reason.」
【Female passenger】 「Since you're here, dear, you will join me for a spot of cards. I was bored playing all by my lonesome.」

The female passenger said so nonchalantly and laid down on her side on the bed near the table, the graceful slowness and lascivious undertones that permeated every slight mannerism in her posture likely a product of subconscious action. Thus, this woman would, like it were the most natural thing in the world, as if it were a congenital behaviour, lead men astray. It was utterly unthinkable that a back-and-forth exchange with this kind of woman would end at just a card game, and the young man had already started to feel a not-so-calm throbbing take root internally; he regretted it bitterly every time he was confronted with this.

Terror accompanied by the glowing red embers of sexual desire, never certain when he'd go into rut, and if that were to pass, he'd do something that could never be amended. No matter how much luxury this room might boast of, no matter how sweet and delicious those top-class wines promised to be, he wanted to avoid getting too deeply involved.

Actually, just what in the world was the situation on the ship right now? As he thought it over once more, the echoes of the angry yelling that, until now, had been distant from the middle deck, suddenly grew in force and reached even here, so it seemed like the upper deck had at last been boarded by the enemy, indicating a grave state of affairs. Yet the women seemed not to let it bother her in the slightest, beckoning the young man to approach.

source.japanese:
【女客】
「ね。勝負しましょうね。わたくしが勝ったら、貴方、わたくしに一晩つきあいなさい。貴方が勝ったのなら、そうねえ、わたくしが一晩つきあって差し上げるわ」
source.english: “Come, let's play for something. If I win, you must spend the night with me. If you win… Well, then I shall spend the night with you.”

source.japanese:
【青年】
「……なにか指摘するのも無粋とは思うんだけど、それってどっちでも同じじゃ……」
source.english: “…I hate to spoil the moment by pointing it out, but isn't that the same either way?”

target.text: 【Female passenger】 「Say. Let us play a game, shall we? Should I win, dear, you will spend the night with me. Should you win, let me see, yes, I will graciously offer to spend the night with you.」
【Young man】 「……It feels a bit tactless to be pointing this out, but isn't that just the same thi……」

source.japanese:
【女客】
「はいはい。いいからおいで。
　近頃だと、セブンブリッジが好みだわ、わたくし」
source.english:
“Yes, yes. Never mind that. Come here.
I've been rather fond of Seven Bridge lately.”

source.japanese:
【青年】
（頼むから人の話を聞いてくれ……）
source.english: (Couldn't you please listen to what I'm saying…?)

target.text: 【Female passenger】 「Yes, yes. It is fine, just come here. These days, I find myself quite fond of Seven Bridge.」
【Young man】 （I'm begging you here, listen to people when they talk to you……）

source.japanese: と青年が憮然となるも、女客に聞き入れた様子は無し、あくまで自分本位に青年を部屋に引き入れ、カードを切り直す、物慣れた指捌きは船の危急など無視して美しい、美しいがしかし。
source.english: His disgruntlement made no impression. Intent on having her way, she drew him into the cabin and shuffled the cards again. Her practiced fingers moved beautifully, heedless of the danger to the ship. Beautifully, yes, but—

source.japanese:
【青年】
「あの……今上は、割とえらいことになってて、その、俺も一応現場にいないと、水夫長から怒られる……」
source.english: “Um… Things are getting pretty bad up above, and, well, I'm supposed to be there. The boatswain'll yell at me…”

target.text: So thought the young man while he grew more disheartened, but the female passenger showed no signs of listening; having lured this young man into her room out of pure selfishness, she reshuffled the cards, and the experienced movements of her deft fingers were a beautiful sight to behold if one ignored the crisis on the ship, quite beautiful, but.
【Young man】 「Uhm……right now, things are relatively serious up above, and, uhm, if I'm not up where it's happening, the Bosun will be furious with me, so……」

source.japanese:
【女客】
「そんなのは、わたくし知りません。わたくしは退屈なの。そちらの方が大事なの」
source.english: “That is no concern of mine. I'm bored. That matters more.”

target.text: 【Female passenger】 「I care not one whit for such things. For I am bored. And that is far more important.」

source.japanese: この女性はいつでもこうなのだ。なにより大切なのは自分の愉[たの]しみ。それ以外のことは眼中に無し。まったくもってひどい女であるし、それが無くとも青年はとにかくこの女性が怖い。怖い、離れたい、のに───なのに、彼女が脚を組み直す度、ドレスのスリットから覗くふくらはぎは、部屋の抑え目の灯りに映えて麗しい、目を奪われる。カードを広げて卓に身を乗り出す度、はち切れんばかりにたわむ乳房、布地に寄る皺さえ柔肉の膨らみを際立たせるからこちらも目を離せない。
source.english: She was always like this. Her own pleasure came first; everything else was beneath her notice. An appalling woman, quite apart from his inexplicable fear of her. He was frightened. He wanted to get away. Yet—yet whenever she crossed her legs anew, a calf appeared through the slit in her dress, lovely in the room's subdued light. He could not look away. Whenever she spread out the cards and leaned over the table, her breasts strained and swelled against the fabric. Even the creases emphasized their soft fullness. He could not look away from those, either.

source.japanese: おまけに女客は、青年の視線に気づいてなおそれを咎めるどころか、許すように嫣然と微笑んでみせる有様で。このままだといつも通り彼女のペースに乗せられて、延々と相手することとなるだろう。まあ、それでも良いか、何しろその乳と脚と尻だ。
source.english:
Worse, she noticed his gaze and did not reproach him. Instead, she smiled sweetly, as though giving permission. At this rate she would draw him into her rhythm as usual, and he would spend hours attending to her.
Well, perhaps that wouldn't be so bad. Those tits. Those legs. That ass.

source.japanese: 怖いものは怖いとしても、それらの弾力、見応え、艶めかしさもまた確かなことでありと、ふらふらと卓につきかける青年の、どうにも意志が弱い駄目人間である───と、爆ぜた！　寝台の奥の窓硝子！
source.english: Frightening she might be, but the supple resilience of her flesh, its splendor to the eye, its sensual sheen—these were equally undeniable. The young man, feckless and weak-willed, had already begun drifting toward the table—when the window beyond the bed burst apart!

target.text: This woman was always like this. Her own enjoyment far more important than anything else. Anything beyond that was completely disregarded. A truly terrible woman, but even that aside, the young man was simply scared of this woman. Scared, he wanted to get away, and yet───

and yet, when the woman recrossed her legs, the calves one could sneak a glance at through the slit of her dress looked so attractive, so beautiful in the subdued light of the room, it was enough to captivate his gaze.
