source.english:
Ships rose and fell lazily on the harbor's gentle waves. Newcomers, old campaigners, disgracefully shabby specimens—all still in service, though their condition varied.
There were imposing passenger liners, models of naval architecture fit for the color plates of a book on ships. Somewhat less grand were freighters that had completed several voyages and would make many more, bearing the wear and old wounds of the sea like medals. Then there were small vessels one step from the scrapyard, so lamentably abused and neglected that one wondered how their owners had let them come to this.

source.japanese: 他に繋がれているのは、このあたりの貧民層、それも陸にはまともに住処さえ持てないほどの連中がねぐらにしているような、つぎはぎだらけの掘っ建て小屋を乗せた船とも浮きバラックともつかぬシロモノだがあれは論外として、朔屋は自分が引っ立てられていく先をざっと推量した。
source.english: Others were moored there, too: things halfway between boats and floating shacks, bearing patched-together hovels. The district's poor used them for shelter, people too destitute to secure even a proper home on land. Those were beneath consideration. Sakuya took a rough guess at which vessel he was being led toward.

source.japanese: 昨夜の二人組は今思えば始めから朔屋を嵌めるつもりだったのだろう。酒場で酒に分別無くした浮かれ者を引っぱっていくなど、帆船時代の英海軍でもあるまいにの時代遅れの所業だと思われがちだが、この時代だってその伝統は途切れていないのである。
source.english: Looking back, the two women had probably meant to trap him from the beginning. Dragging off a fool who had drunk away his judgment in a tavern might seem outdated. This was not the Royal Navy in the age of sail, after all. Yet the tradition had by no means died out in this era.

source.japanese: およそこういう強制徴募を仕掛けるような連中の乗りこむ船といって、就航したて、装備も整ってぴかぴかな船であるとは考えづらい。どうせあちこち傷ついた、中古の船だろうと当たりをつけた頭で、ふるいを掛けてみたところ、港内に停泊した船の中でも最悪なのを峻別した。
source.english: A crew that resorted to such forcible recruitment was unlikely to serve aboard a newly launched, fully equipped, gleaming ship. Some battered secondhand vessel, surely. With that assumption, he sifted through the ships moored in the harbor and picked out the worst.

source.japanese: 烏賊釣りの漁船クラスのが一隻、それはもう目を覆いたくなるほど衰えた船だ。しかしあれは、外洋に出ていけるような船ではない。となると残りは、二〇〇〇頓クラスの貨物船がある。こちらも相当にガタが来ているが、それでも先の漁船よりはまだましで、少なくとも当直の間に、他の船と衝突するのと、自然浸水による沈没の両方を警戒する必要は無さそうだった。ひどい。確かにひどいけれども、まだ許せないことはない。朔屋は船員学校時代に、今の自分と同じく騙されて引っぱっていかれた挙げ句、港から出る前に沈没した船に乗りこむ羽目になった先輩というのを聞いた事がある。
source.english:
There was a boat about the size of a squid-fishing vessel, so far gone one wanted to cover one's eyes. But that could never venture onto the open sea. The other candidate was a freighter of about two thousand tons. She, too, was badly worn, though better than the fishing boat. At least a man standing watch aboard her would not have to guard simultaneously against collision and spontaneous sinking.
Bad. Certainly bad. But not quite intolerable. At school, Sakuya had heard of a senior student who had been tricked and hauled aboard just as he had—only for the ship to sink before leaving port.

source.japanese: 朔屋がそれと睨[にら]んだ船は、見た目こそガタがきているものの、洋上を往くにはどうやら差し支えは無さそうだったので、内心少しばかり胸を撫で下ろした事である。
source.english: The ship he had picked looked rickety, but seemed capable of traveling across the sea. Inwardly, he felt a little relief.

target.text: The port housed those wet behind the ears, the seasoned veterans, as well as the indecently decrepit, each one in their respective condition, ships in active service leisurely rolling on the peaceful waves.

That ship there seemed like she was deserving of a coloured page in an illustrated encyclopedia of ships, a magnificent passenger ship one could well call a paragon of shipbuilding, and that slightly inferior model there, she had completed quite a few voyages in her time, and she was sure to go on several more in the future, a freighter carrying her wear and scars as an Order of Merit, and then there was that small boat on the verge of being scrapped, tragic enough to make a man lament her fate of being worked so hard with barely any maintenance to show for it.

Without even bothering to consider what was otherwise moored in the port, a makeshift patchwork of huts and shacks that could only be identified as something between a ship and a floating shanty town, the sort of thing where the destitute of this part of town or perhaps those unable to hold down a place to live on land might make their roost, certainly quite the "fine" specimen, Sakuya could make a rough guess as to where he was being dragged off to.

Thinking back on the duo from yesterday, they likely intended to set up Sakuya from the very start. Hauling a reveler who'd lost his good judgement in the alcohol or some such from the bar: while it certainly felt like a rather antiquated method, reminiscent of what was once employed by the British Navy in the Age of Sail, it was clearly a tradition that had yet to be cut short even in this day and age.

Generally speaking, it was hard to imagine that a ship run by a crew made up of the sort of people who would trick somebody into impressment would be spick and span and fully equipped as she was about to commence on a new voyage. She would, at best, be scratched up here and there, and he estimated that she would probably be an old, used ship, but as he tried to filter through his options, that rigorous distinction only brought him to the worst possible ships among those moored in the port.

There was one ship the size of a squid jigging fishing boat, so dilapidated it made him want to cover his eyes. However, that thing did not seem like a ship that could take to the seas. As such, all that remained was a 2000-ton class freighter. This one was also quite rickety, but even so, it was better than the aforementioned squid jigger; at the very least, there seemed to be no need to be on guard against colliding with other ships or foundering due to seepage while he was on watch.

Awful. Certainly an awful thing to say, but it could be forgiven. Back when Sakuya was in nautical school, he had heard tales of an upperclassman who had been tricked in a similar way to his current self and been hauled away, ultimately boarding a ship that had sunk before it even left port.
The ship Sakuya had his eyes on did look a little worse for the wear, but it didn't seem like it would become a hindrance as she made her way across the seas, so he felt a little relieved internally.

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「アレが俺らの船だ」
source.english: “There's our ship.”

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「どうだ立派な船だろう。
　ロイドの保険屋だって、一等を点けるぜえ」
source.english:
“Fine vessel, eh?
Even the insurance boys at Lloyd's would give her top marks.”

source.japanese:
……龍の刺青に半面を恐ろしく飾った、魁偉なる容貌の恐ろしい顔の男も、得意気に胸を逸らしてあご先で示す───が。
　その指した先が、朔屋が眺めている向きとは微妙に異なることに、まだ彼は気がついていない。朔屋は朔屋で、その貨物船の上部構造物から伸びるアンテナが、子供が弄[もてあそ]んだ針金細工のようにひん曲がっている事を指摘なぞしたり───
source.english:
The terrifying man, his formidable face made more terrible by the dragon tattoo across one half, proudly puffed out his chest and pointed with his chin. But—
Sakuya had not yet noticed that the direction was slightly different from the one in which he was looking. He was busy remarking on the antenna rising from the freighter's superstructure, bent like a wire toy a child had played with.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、そうですね。
　ただアンテナばかりはどうにかした方が。
　あんなじゃあ、感度が悪くなる……」
source.english:
“Oh, yes. Very nice.
Though you might want to do something about that antenna.
That won't do much for your reception…”

target.text: 【Man with a terrifying face】 「That there's our ship.」
【Man with a terrifying face】 「A fine vessel, isn't she? Even the insurers at Lloyd's would mark her down as A1.」

……With a tattoo of a dragon fearsomely etched across half his face, a formidable physique, and a terrifying face, the man puffed out his chest with pride in all its brawny glory and pointed with his chin───but. He still hadn't noticed that the place he was pointing to was in a slightly different direction from where Sakuya was looking. Meanwhile, Sakuya was looking at the antenna rising from the superstructure on the freighter, about to make a comment on how it was bent like a kid messing around with wirework or something───
【Naomasa】 「Yes, you're quite right. But I really think it would be best to do something about that antenna. When it's bent like that, the reception gets worse……」

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「あ？　アンテナだぁ？
　俺らの船にゃ、そんな結構なモノはついてねえよ？」
source.english:
“Huh? Antenna?
Our ship's got no fancy gear like that.”

target.text: 【Man with a terrifying face】 「Huh? What antenna? Our ship doesn't have anything that fancy on her, you know?」

source.japanese: ぎょっとしてもう一度見直して、恐ろしい顔の男の視線の先が、自分とは別であることにようやく気がついて、朔屋はとてつもなく不安な予感に囚われた。
source.english: Startled, he looked again. At last he realized that the terrifying man's gaze led elsewhere. A prodigious foreboding seized him.

source.japanese: ───水夫の視線の先を辿る。
source.english: —He followed the sailor's eyes.

source.japanese: そこにあったのは───
source.english: What stood there was—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい……嘘でしょ？
　嘘っていってよ、ねえ……っ」
source.english:
“Hey… You're joking, right?
Tell me you're joking. Please…!”

source.japanese: 恐ろしい顔の男が示していた先は───
source.english: The terrifying man was pointing to—

target.text: Startled, he took another look, and there, following the direction of that man with the terrifying face's gaze, he finally noticed what he had failed to see before, and Sakuya was seized by a monumentally alarming premonition.
───Following the sailor's gaze.
What awaited him there was───
【Naomasa】 「Oi……you're joking, right? Tell me you're joking, please……?」
What the man with the terrifying face was pointing to was───

source.japanese:
朔屋が、
『港の片隅を不法占拠した、貧民層の浮きバラック』
　として認識していた、到底船とは呼べないような構造体であり───
source.english:
The structure Sakuya had dismissed as a floating shantytown, illegally occupying a corner of the harbor.
Something one could scarcely call a ship—

target.text: Sakuya had perceived it to be 『A floating shanty town lived in by the poor unlawfully occupying a corner of the port』, a structure that could not be called a ship under any circumstances───

source.japanese: 貨物船というには、その船体はいくらか細身に過ぎた。かといって細身を利して速度を求める、軍属の船というにしてもいい加減に過ぎた。
source.english: The hull was a little too slender for a freighter. Yet it was far too haphazard for a naval vessel designed to turn that slenderness into speed.

source.japanese: 全長はおよそ一〇〇米、全幅は一三米、喫水は六米に足らずといったところか。しかしこれらの船の諸元を語る単位をあてはめるのも烏滸がましいような、冒涜であるかのようなそれ。
source.english: Perhaps a hundred meters long, thirteen meters wide, with a draft of under six meters. But applying the ordinary specifications of a ship to this thing felt presumptuous. Blasphemous, even.

source.japanese: かつては甲板として、各種の構造物を乗せていたであろう部分には、述べたとおりに立ち並ぶ、小屋、バラック、倉庫の数々、それもちゃんと図面を引いて建てましてございとは口が裂けても言えないような、有り合わせの木っ端角材を手当たり次第にかき集めて強引にまとめたような、規格も統制も取れていない寄せ集めのオンボロばかり。近くに寄ってみれば、どれもこれも虫食いだらけ、潮風に粗びているのが判ったろう。
source.english: The part that had presumably once been the deck, bearing the various structures proper to a ship, was now—as already noted—lined with huts, shacks, and sheds, not one of which anyone with a straight face could claim had been built from anything resembling a plan: ramshackle miscellanies seemingly bullied together from whatever scraps and lengths of timber could be gathered, with no common standard and no governing order; and had one gone nearer, one would doubtless have found them worm-eaten to the last and weathered raw by the salt wind.

source.japanese: 船体は一応鋼板のようではあるけれど、至るところに赤錆浮いて、損傷した箇所も多く、またその補修が余所の廃材を奪ってきて、ろくに大きさも合わせもせずに力任せに打ちつけたようなつぎはぎで。
source.english: The hull did seem to be steel plate, at least. But red rust bloomed everywhere, and there were many damaged places. The repairs looked as though someone had stolen scrap from elsewhere and hammered it on by brute force, without bothering to make it fit.

source.japanese: ありていに言ってしまえば、海面に魚礁用のスクラップを恐る恐る浮かべ、一応沈まないと見るや甲板上にこれでもかと好き放題に貧民窟の襤褸小屋を並べ立ててみました、といった様相の、一種異様な、鉄屑と老朽した木っ端の一大混沌。
source.english:
To put it plainly: someone appeared to have gingerly floated a heap of scrap intended for an artificial reef. Once it proved unwilling to sink, they had crammed the deck with every slum shack they fancied.
A vast, singularly grotesque chaos of scrap iron and decayed wood.

source.japanese: 浮かんでいるのが造船力学と物理学への挑戦であるかのような弩の上にも超がつく襤褸船だったからだ───まともな感性の持ち主ならば、船と口にするのにも、気恥ずかしさを覚えることであろう。
source.english: This was a superlatively, extravagantly decrepit vessel whose very ability to float appeared to challenge naval architecture and the laws of physics. Anyone with normal sensibilities would have felt embarrassed even calling her a ship.

source.japanese:
あるいはもう少し繊細な感性の持ち主ならば、見ているだけでも耐えかねると、『それ』をたちまちに沈めにかかるに違いなく、そしてそれは大した労苦でもなく成し遂げられるはずである。
　なにしろ、船腹に少し力の入った蹴りをくれた程度でも、爪先は朽ちかけた鋼板に穴を穿[うが]ち、そこから速やかに浸水してキングストン弁を引き抜いたよりあっけなく沈没すること間違いなし、だからだ。
source.english:
A person with slightly more delicate sensibilities would doubtless have found the sight unbearable and set about sinking the thing at once. It could hardly have taken much effort.
A moderately forceful kick at the hull would surely have driven a toe through the rotting plate. Water would rush in, and she would go down more readily than if someone had pulled out a Kingston valve.

source.japanese: 余りに余りの衝撃に、朔屋が脳天を甑で殴られたイボイノシシの態でよろめいた時、彼の動作に海がおどけて合わせたか、一つ大きな波がうねった。やや高めの波が『それ』の横にもたれかかり、後家の掛け布団の中に潜[もぐ]り込む若衆めいた滑らかさで『それ』の下をくぐる───と、ぎぃぃぃとの軋りが、耳をつんざいて大きい、『それ』の上部の構造物の、あちこちから鳴り響いてはけたたましい。いやこの、『それ』の上部に居並ぶ木造小屋の数々が鳴らし立てていた軋りは、実のところ朔屋が埠頭に踏み出した時よりひっきりなしであったのだが、先ほどまでは彼もさすがに『それ』が船だと端から考えだにしていなかった、為に聞き過ごしにしていた。
source.english:
The shock was too much. Sakuya staggered like a warthog struck on the head with a rice steamer. As though the sea were comically following his movements, a large wave rose. It leaned against the thing's side, then slipped beneath it as smoothly as a young fellow slipping under a widow's quilt.
Creeeeeeak.
The structures above gave a deafening, piercing chorus. In fact, all those wooden shacks had been creaking incessantly since Sakuya first stepped onto the wharf. Until now, however, he had never imagined that the thing was a ship. He had paid the noises no attention.

source.japanese: ───船だと思うと、せいぜい女の寝返り程度の波うねりで、これほどまでに盛大に軋りの悲鳴を上げているとあっては冗談事では済まない。カミキリムシが一万匹も集って啼いたところでこれほどではあるまい。
source.english: —Once one thought of her as a ship, there was nothing funny about such a tremendous shriek of protest at a swell no greater than a woman turning over in bed. Ten thousand longhorn beetles singing together could scarcely have matched it.

source.japanese:
朔屋の、途端に麻薬中毒者じみて淀んだ眼差しで、見ている間にもばらり、甲板上の襤褸小屋の、寄せ波程度のうねりの圧にさえ耐えかねて、緩んで、壁の板が解れて外れて落ちていく。
　かと思うと反動で角度が復元した際にも、置かれていた木樽が転がりだして舷側より水面に転がり落ちていくという───甲板上の固定さえ、まともではないのであった。
source.english:
His eyes glazed over at once, like an addict's. As he watched, the pressure of a mere passing wave loosened one of the deckside hovels. Boards came away from its wall and fell.
Then the ship righted herself on the rebound, and a wooden barrel rolled across the deck and over the side into the water. They had not even secured the things aboard properly.

target.text: Her hull was a little too slender to call her a freighter. However, even if she put her narrow frame to use in the pursuit of speed, she was far too slipshod to be a naval vessel.

An overall length of around 100 metres, overall width of 13 metres, and did the draught even reach 6 metres? However, applying these units that describe the specifications of ships to this thing seemed presumptuous, perhaps even blasphemous.

The area that was once the deck, the part that now supported a variety of structures, was, as mentioned previously, lined with buildings, a large number of huts, shacks, and storehouses, something one would not dare claim was built in accordance with properly drafted blueprints, even with a gun to one's head; they seemed forcibly cobbled together from whatever scraps of lumber that could be scraped together at the time, a dilapidated melange with neither standards nor control. Were one to move closer, one would probably see how they were all worm-eaten and weather-beaten from the briny air.

Technically, the hull was made of steel plates, but they were covered in red rust from top to bottom, damaged in many places, repaired with scrap material pillaged from somewhere else, cobbled together by forcibly hammering the sheets together without even bothering to match the sizes properly.

Were one to put it bluntly, it was like someone had cautiously set some scrap metal afloat on the surface of the sea to be used as an artificial fish reef, and since it looked like it wouldn't sink for the time being, they then began piling on all sorts of dilapidated, slum-like shacks on the deck as they pleased, such was its condition: utterly bizarre, a great chaos of decaying wood and scrap iron.

This ship, so exceptionally ragged and dilapidated that the very fact of its flotation seemed like a challenge issued to shipbuilding mechanics and the laws of physics themselves─── Were one possessed of upright sensibilities, then the act of calling this a ship itself would surely leave one's face burning with shame.

Or were one instead possessed of a more delicate soul, it would be hard to even look at it; no doubt they would try to sink 『that thing』 right away, and they would certainly succeed without any great strain on their part. For you see, from but a kick with faint force to the side of the ship, or holes dug into the decaying steel plates with fingernails, it would promptly flood, then undoubtedly founder even faster than had one removed its Kingston valves.

Overwhelmed, the shock was so great that Sakuya staggered like a warthog hit in the dome with a steaming basket, and it seemed as if the ocean responded to his movement with a playful gesture of its own, for a single large wave rolled in. The rather tall wave leaned against the side of『that thing』, passing under 『that thing』with the smoothness of a young man sneaking under the covers of a widow's bed───and with a drawn-out creaking, a blaring loud enough to split his eardrums, the structures all over『that thing』 resounded in shrill tones.

The piercing creaking of the wooden shacks lined up on top of 『that thing』had actually been sounding incessantly since Sakuya first stepped out on the wharf, but since he reasonably had never considered 『that thing』a ship until just earlier, he had consequently ignored it.

───To a ship, the swell of that wave was at most like a woman stirring in her sleep, but the way it screamed so strenuously through its creaking was really not a laughing matter. Even were ten thousand longhorn beetles to gather together and stridulate in unison it would not be this shrill.

Sakuya's eyes suddenly clouded over, dull and sluggish like those of a drug addict; he could see it all falling apart right before his very own eyes, the run-down huts on the deck failing to hold against even this gentle surge, coming apart, the boards serving as walls loosening and falling right off. Even when the ship righted itself on the rebound, the wooden barrels placed on the deck rolled around and fell over the bulwark and into the sea ───not even the lashings and fastenings on deck were properly secured.

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「あれが、俺らの船、
『信天翁号』だ」
source.english:
“That's our ship.
The Albatross.”

source.japanese: きっぱりと言い切った、ああその声音だけは傲岸であるが故に頼もしいのに、その目つきにしても、不敵であると同時に力強いのに。
source.english: He declared it with perfect assurance. Ah, if only the haughty confidence in his voice could be trusted; if only the bold strength of his gaze—

target.text: 【Man with a terrifying face】 「That right there, that's our ship, the『Albatross』」

He stated that so resolutely, oh, but though that tone of voice was so reassuring precisely by virtue of its arrogance, even with that look in his eyes, at once audacious yet heartening in its strength, still.

source.japanese: その船───
source.english: For the ship—

source.japanese:
『信天翁号』本体と来たら。
　船という構造物に要求される、堅牢性や整合性など毛の一筋ほどもみつけられず。
source.english:
The Albatross herself—
possessed not a hair's breadth of the solidity or structural coherence a vessel required.

source.japanese: 朔屋は滅多にない、普段からそのような動きができていれば、彼にはもっと違った評価が与えられていたに違いない俊敏な動作で廻れ右してその場をとっとと後にしようとしたのだが。
source.english: Sakuya turned on his heel and tried to leave with a rare burst of agility. Had he moved like that in daily life, people would surely have formed a different opinion of him.

target.text: That ship───
As for this『Albatross』herself. He could not find a single shred of the durability or integrity that was demanded from these structures we call ships.

With a movement rare of Sakuya, an agile maneuver that, were he able to make use of regularly, would have undoubtedly left him with a very different reputation, he turned on his heel and quickly made to take his leave, but.

source.japanese:
遅かりし由良の介。
　男の猿臂はするする伸びて、朔屋の襟首をがっしり捕まえて、それこそ万力はだしの剛力で。
source.english:
Too late, Yuranosuke.
The man's long arm slid out and clamped Sakuya by the collar with a strength that put a vise to shame.

source.japanese:
【恐ろしい顔の男】
「そして俺が、信天翁号の水夫長だ。
　身内は龍の親爺てぇ呼ぶな。
　まあ水夫長だからよ、
　てめえみたいなぼんくらの扱いは、
　掌さすみたいに心得てる」
source.english:
“And I'm the Albatross's boatswain.
The crew calls me Old Long.
Being boatswain,
I know how to handle a useless bastard like you as well
as I know the back of my hand.”

target.text: Too late, Yuranosuke. The man's arms reached out in a smooth, swift motion, grabbing Sakuya tightly by the scruff of his neck, squeezing down on him like a vise with his titanic strength. (TN:遅かりし由良の介 is a turn of phrase that signifies being a little too late to something. It originates from the joururi play (a form of puppet theater accompanied by a shamisen) called "Kanadehon Chuushingura", likely one of the first works of Japanese literature to be translated to English, where Yuranosuke arrives just as the lord he serves as chief retainer commits seppuku.)

【Man with a terrifying face】 「And I am the bosun of the Albatross. My boys call me old man Long. And since I'm the bosun, I know how to handle halfwits of your sort like the back of my hand.」 (TN: The reading used for "龍" here is the Chinese one, that being "Long", or "Ron" in Japanese. The kanji itself means "dragon".)

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「今さら逃げようなんざ、
　考えるだけ無駄だぜぇ……？」
source.english:
“It's a waste of time even
thinking about running now, eh…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや逃げるなんてそんなはははは。
　ただほら、色々と荷物を取ってこないと───」
source.english:
“Run? Oh, no, nothing like that, hahaha.
It's just, you know, I've got things to collect—”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「いらねえよ。
　着替えなら貸してやる。
　他のもんなんざ、てめえみたいな新前にゃ、
　全部余計な荷物だ」
source.english:
“You don't need them.
We'll lend you a change of clothes.
Anything else is extra baggage
for a new boy like you.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「If you're even thinking of trying to run away now, you're just wasting your time, got it……?」
【Naomasa】 「No no, running away? Perish the thought, hahahaha. It's just, look, I have a bunch of luggage I really have to go pick up and───」
【Bosun】 「You don't need that. If you need a change of clothes, then we'll lend some to you. But anything else, for a green hand like you? All nothing but dead weight.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ああ、ただ───」
source.english: “Ah. Except—”

source.japanese: と水夫長は、朔屋を改めて値踏みするようにじろじろと、今になって一体いかなる資質を青年に求めようとしているのか。一時眺め回しては、すぐに失望したように鼻を鳴らした。
source.english: The boatswain looked him up and down anew, appraising him. What quality could he be seeking in the young man at this late stage? After a brief inspection, he snorted in apparent disappointment.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……はん、まず望み薄だな。一応訊くが、本だったら、持ちこんでええぞ」
source.english: “…Hah. Not much hope there. But I'll ask anyway. Books, you can bring.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「本って……エロ本とかっすか？」
source.english: “Books…? Like porn?”

source.japanese: 意外な申し出に朔屋、虚をつかれてついそれを口にするあたり、日頃彼が慣れ親しんでいる書物の傾向が知れよう。
source.english: The unexpected offer caught Sakuya off guard. His immediate reply revealed the kind of books with which he was most familiar.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Aah, but───」

With that, the Bosun gave Sakuya a good once-over as though he was reassessing his worth, but at this point, what kind of quality could he possibly be searching for in this young man? He looked him over for a time, then quickly snorted as if disappointed.
【Bosun】 「……Haah, dim prospects here, that's for sure. Suppose I'll ask just in case, but if you got any books, feel free to take them with you.」
【Naomasa】 「Books……like, porn mags?」
Taken off guard by the unexpected offer, Sakuya blurted that out, betraying the exact type of literature he himself habitually partook in.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「馬鹿、そんなんじゃねえ。小説だ小説。詩集とか随筆でもいい。戯曲だってありだ。
　ほら、コールリッジとかチョーサーとか、幾らでもあんだろうが」
source.english:
“Idiot. Not those. Novels. Poetry or essays'll do. Plays, too.
You know, Coleridge, Chaucer—there's no shortage.”

source.japanese: ただでさえまともな人文教養に疎い朔屋であり、ましてこの水夫長の口から作家めいた名を聞かされても、なにやらの呪文のようにしか聞こえず、晒すのは間抜け顔、二人の間を白けた空気が漂い流れる。朔屋は水夫長の手を眺めた。ぼんやりと、あんな無骨な指ではまともに頁を捲れるのか知らんと。眺めていると、ハンマーのように拳が握られ、ぎしりと軋んだので慌てて目を逸らして口笛を吹く真似、白々しい。朔屋の無礼な想像など、いかにも世慣れた水夫長にはお見通しというところ、とはいえこの意外の念、朔屋ならずとも無理はない。
source.english: Sakuya was ignorant enough of respectable literary culture to begin with, and from the boatswain’s mouth the names of authors sounded to him like so many incantations; his face went blank, and a dead silence drifted between them. Sakuya studied the boatswain’s hands, idly wondering whether such blunt fingers could even turn a page properly. As he watched, they clenched into a hammer of a fist with a creak. He hurriedly looked away and pretended to whistle. Transparently. A boatswain so worldly-wise had plainly seen through Sakuya’s insolent fancy; still, the surprise was natural enough, and hardly Sakuya’s alone.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You moron, nothing like that, I'm talking novels here, novels. Poetry anthologies and essays are fine too. Even plays can work. Look, like Coleridge, or Chaucer or something, there's plenty to choose from.」

Sakuya was already ill-informed on the matter of finer culture at the best of times, and hearing names that sounded like those of great authors coming from the mouth of this bosun, it all sounded like some manner of magic incantation to his ears; with an inane look on his face, an awkward, subdued atmosphere now hung heavy between the two men.

Sakuya observed the Bosun's hand. Could he even turn a page properly with those coarse fingers, he idly wondered. As he was looking, that hand clenched into a hammer-like fist, bones creaking, and so he hurriedly averted his eyes and let out an innocent whistle, displaying obviously feigned ignorance. This sophisticated, worldly bosun saw right through Sakuya's uncouth imagination, but be that as it may, this feeling of surprise would be understandable, even were one not called Sakuya.

source.japanese: 乗りこむといってこの襤褸船では、舷側から手垢にまみれ、潮風に粗びた縄梯子でも垂らしてくるのではと危惧していたところ、手摺りにあちこち歪みがあって段にもいくつか穴が空いてはいても、舷梯が下ろされていたので、朔屋はやや安堵してしまったものの、すぐさま己の暢気を戒める。水夫長に尻蹴り立てられてここまで来てしまったけれど、この舷梯を上ってしまったら最後だ。
source.english: To board this wreck, he had expected a rope ladder dangling over the side, greasy with hands and roughened by salt. Instead, a gangway had been lowered. Its rails were bent in places and several steps had holes, but it gave him a little relief all the same. Then he rebuked his own easygoing nature. The boatswain had kicked him this far. Once he went up that gangway, it would be over.

target.text: This run-down ship he was told to board was covered in the filth of long years of use on her side, and just when he began to worry that they would toss down a rope ladder frayed by the salty wind, a gangway was lowered instead, and even though the hand railing was twisted and bent here and there, to say nothing of the gaping holes in the steps, he felt a little relieved at seeing it, then immediately admonished himself for his carelessness. 　それくらい素敵な眺めだった。
　廃物の如き襤褸船の船腹は、見るだけでも心が沈んでしまうのに、そんな憂さなど忘れてしまう。
source.english:
Should he force himself to try escaping, hangover and all? Or fall to his knees, forehead to the ground, and beg to be let go? As he hesitated, rhythmic footsteps descended the gangway. He looked up, and every plan for escape scattered from his mind.
The sight was that wonderful.
The hull of this scrapheap of a ship was enough to sink one's heart merely by looking at it. Now he forgot all that misery.

I suppose we did. But you said you'd come aboard,
too.

And look—here's your contract.

source.japanese: 昨夜は背中に流していた髪も、今朝はきりりと編んで結い上げ、昨夜よりもごく自然に感じられるのは恐らくこの活動的な髪型の方が彼女の普段のスタイルだからだろう。昨夜の色香とは異なる質の、活発で、巻き上げられた発条のような躍動感に満ち満ちて、これはこれで魅力がある。酒場の朧な灯りではただ濃い色の異国の眸と見えた緑青の双眸だって、陽差しの下では透明に明るく澄んで、しなやかな生命力が溢れんばかり。

Last night her hair had flowed down her back. This morning it was briskly braided and pinned up. She looked much more natural, probably because this active hairstyle was the one she normally wore. It gave her a different appeal from last night's sensuality: lively, full of the energy of a wound spring. Attractive in its own right.
In the tavern's hazy light, her eyes had seemed merely dark and foreign. Now, in the sun, their turquoise was bright and clear, almost transparent. Supple vitality seemed about to overflow from them.

source.japanese: この女はああやって酒とドレスの媚態もこなすが、本来はもっと動的な、たとえば大海原の波と風に挑んでいる姿こそ本領なのだろう。なるほど一等航海士───できればこちらの姿でも一緒に呑みたいベッドの御相手願いたい、と性懲りもなしに鼻の下を伸ばしかかる朔屋に唇吊り上げてみせた笑みがまた不敵で大胆で、見惚れてしまいそう。

source.english: He almost did. But the hangover still aching at the back of his head somehow pulled him together.

source.japanese:

source.japanese: したり顔で笑む女は美しいけれど、事のあらましが見えてきた朔屋には、その美をのんびり愛でているどころではない。騙された憤懣やるかたなく、一等航海士に怒鳴り返してやろうとするのだが、彼女が二つにすっと───分かれた。

Her knowing smile was beautiful. But now that he was beginning to understand what had happened, Sakuya had no leisure to admire it. His anger at being deceived demanded an outlet. He tried to shout back at the first mate—
And she slid apart into two.

target.text: 【Blonde lady】 「Anyway, good of you to finally come. I've been waiting for you.」

The hair that was flowing down her back last night had been tied up in tight buns this morning, and the reason it felt so thoroughly natural on her compared to how she wore it last night was likely because this more functional way of doing her hair was her regular style. This woman did have a good command of seduction while drinking and dressed up like before, but by nature, she was more dynamic, active; as an example, her fearless figure standing in defiance of the waves and wind of the great sea would likely be where she truly shone. Certainly, a first mate───if at all possible, he would love to share a drink with and bed her in this form as well, so Sakuya thought, utterly incorrigible as he leered, and the way she curled her lips into a smile at him, so dauntless and bold, left him on the verge of being entranced.
Although he almost lost himself in her, the lingering throbbing of the hangover in the back of Sakuya's head somehow managed to pull him back to reality.
【Naomasa】 「What kind of idiot would consider a contract valid after you drink them under the table and shanghai them…… idiot, moron, pair of tits!」

With a self-satisfied smile on her face, the woman was still beautiful, but having realized the general course of events that had led him here, Sakuya could not bring himself to just admire that beauty at leisure. Frustrated at having been unable to clear away his indignation at being duped until now, just as he was about to roar back at the first mate, the woman suddenly turned into two───she split.

source.japanese: どうやら背後に隠れていたらしいが、分身の術でも遣ったかとしか見えず、それくらい後からでてきた方も同じ髪型同じ姿の、並べて身長計を当ててもぴたりと同じ目盛りに止まるのではないか。リーファージャケットの胸元に寄った布地の皺だって、寸分違わず同じ具合によじれていないか。

They began moving, at times dizzyingly fast, at times making certain to vary their pace between fast and slow with clear distinction, deftly moving their limbs so in tune that it would put a traditional dancer to shame. A brief separation to the left and the right, then a quick crossing and substitution.

Side by side they struck poses, the one on the right facing forwards and blowing a seductive kiss, the one on the left facing backwards while bent over at the hips, looking back over her shoulder while throwing a thumbs up, ass thrust out in a provocative display. They then pressed their backs together, beating out a rhythm with one leg, both holding out their index finger and waving it in front of Sakuya's nose, then parted once more. Suddenly, they embraced, then performed many a pirouette, but even more outrageous than their incredibly skillful footwork were their breasts, pushing and shoving against each other.

There was not a single halting step in the sequence of their combined movements, they never tripped over their feet: fluid and refined, breathing as one, even exceeding that level, so astonishing it was enough to make a man wonder if there was but one soul inhabiting both bodies.

source.japanese:
最後にぴたりと大見得の形で止まってから、右左と分かれて、対称形に両手大きく開掌して、問いかけてきたのに朔屋は一瞬面食らって言葉に詰まった。
　途中からは風変わりなダンスとしか見えず、何の為に二人が入れ替わり立ち替わりに左右を替えていたのかすっかり失念していたのである。
source.english:
At last they stopped dead in a grand theatrical pose. Then they parted right and left, spreading their open hands in symmetrical gestures, and asked their question. Sakuya was taken aback and, for an instant, could not speak.
Partway through, it had become no more than an unusual dance to him. He had entirely forgotten why they were changing places.

target.text: At last, they suddenly stopped in a dramatic pose, then split left and right, opening both hands wide with palms showing in a perfectly mirrored position, then posed him a question, which left Sakuya both bewildered and speechless for a brief time. From a certain point onwards, it had just looked like a bizarre dance to him, and it had completely slipped his mind what possible reason there could be for why these two kept taking turns to switch places from left to right.

source.japanese:
【金髪の双子】
「さあ、どっちがどっちかわっかるかなぁ？」
source.english: “So! Can you tell which is which?”

target.text: 【Blonde twin】 「Now then, can you tell who is who, I wonder?」

source.japanese:
【金髪の双子】
「どっちがシサムでキサラか当ててみせて？
　当てたら一晩付き合うよ。
　外したら身ぐるみ剥ぐからね」
source.english:
“Tell us who's Sisam and who's Kisara. Get it right,
and we'll spend a night with you. Get it wrong,
and we'll strip you of everything you've got.”

source.japanese: 言うまでもなく、朔屋には当然区別がつかなくなっていて───
source.english: Needless to say, Sakuya could no longer tell them apart—

target.text: 【Blonde twin】 「Can you guess who is Shisamu and who is Kisara? If you get it right, we'll spend the night with you! If you get it wrong, we're stripping you of everything you're carrying.」
Needles to say, Sakuya could, of course, no longer distinguish between them, and so he───

source.japanese:
双子二人の、我が身をカードに見立てたシャッフルは完璧であり、たとえ見抜く注意怠らず流れを追っていたとしても捉え切れたかどうか怪しい。大体この二人、それがわかってやっているだろうになんと意地の悪い悪戯をしかける。
　そう思っても、朔屋にとって当たった場合の褒賞は魅力的だった。昨夜つかみ損ねた快楽を、事によったら取り戻せる。外れたとしてもせいぜい裸に剥かれるのが関の山。財布の中身など、ズボンを洗った際に確かめたところ、小銭一つ残さず空になっていたもの、惜しむものなどない。
source.english:
The twins had shuffled themselves like cards, perfectly. Even had he watched carefully all the way through, he might not have kept track. Surely they knew that. What a nasty little trick.
Even so, the reward tempted him. He might yet recover the pleasure he had failed to obtain last night. If he lost, the worst they could do was strip him naked. When he checked his purse while washing his trousers, he had found it empty down to the last coin. There was nothing left to regret losing.

source.japanese: 右の片割れを見つめて、左の片割れを凝視して、したところで区別などつきようもなかったけれど、確率ならば二分の一、分の悪い賭けではない。
source.english: He stared at the twin on the right, scrutinized the one on the left. It did no good. Still, the odds were one in two. Not a bad bet.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ええと……。
　左がシサムで、右がキサラ、かな……？」
source.english:
“…Um…
Sisam on the left, Kisara on the right…?”

source.japanese: 指差し答えて、暫しの間。水夫長はこの茶番を無視してはいたが、苦い顔でいらついている様子であり、朔屋にも焦れてきた頃合いで、右のかたわれがふうと肩を落として、
source.english: He pointed and answered. A moment passed. The boatswain ignored this farce, though his sour expression showed his impatience. Just as Sakuya began to grow anxious, the twin on the right let her shoulders fall with a sigh.

target.text: The twin's shuffling, treating their own bodies as cards, was perfect, and even had one diligently followed the process without one's attention wavering, it was still doubtful if one could truly grasp it in its entirety. In the first place, these two probably knew that all too well, and yet they still did it: what a cruel little trick to play.

Even while thinking this, the reward in store for Sakuya should he guess right was very appealing. That pleasure he failed to get his hands on last night, depending on how things went here, he could retake it. Even should he fail, being stripped naked was the worst that could happen. He'd already checked his wallet while washing his pants, and it was completely empty with not a coin in sight, so he had nothing to regret.

He looked at the right half, then stared intensely at her counterpart on the left; not that he could actually differentiate them by doing this, but in terms of probability, it was a 50-50, not a bad bet to take.
【Naomasa】 「……Uuuhm……. Left is Shisamu, right is Kisara, I think……?」

He answered with a pointing finger, and a little time passed. The Bosun was ignoring this whole farce, but the scowl on his face indicated that he was getting irritated, and when even Sakuya began to get impatient, the twin on the right let her shoulders drop with a huff,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「当たりぃ……」
source.english: “Right…”

source.japanese: への字に結んだ口に悔しさを滲ませ、
source.english: Her mouth turned down with frustration.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Correeect……」
With her mouth set in a pout that betrayed her frustration,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ちぇー、見抜かれちゃった。　まあ仕方ないから、非番の夜なら付き合わないでもないけどさ」
source.english: “Damn. He saw through us. Well, I suppose we could spend a night with you when we're off duty.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Bah, so you saw through us. Well, so be it, I guess I can keep you company on a night where I'm not on watch.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……ところで一応訊いておきたいんだけど、
　ちゃんと追えてたわけ、どっちがどっちか」
source.english:
“…One thing I want to ask, though.
Were you really keeping track of which was which?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はっはっは、そりゃもちろん。
　スタートは右がシサムで左がキサラだ。
　そっからクロスは三回だったからさ、
　なら一回目で入れ替わって二回目で戻って、
　三回目でまた入れ替わる」
source.english:
“Hahaha, of course.
You started with Sisam on the right and Kisara on the left.
Then you crossed three times.
First time, you switched. Second time, you switched back.
Third time, you switched again.”

source.japanese: 当たりを引いた満悦と、一夜を過ごす期待で朔屋の口は軽くなり、得意気に種明かししたものの、
source.english: Delighted at having guessed right, and looking forward to their night together, Sakuya grew talkative. He proudly revealed his method, but—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……By the way, just for the record, I want to ask you. Could you actually follow us, as in, who was who?」

【Naomasa】 「Ha-ha-ha, but of course. At first, Shisamu was on the right and Kisara was on the left. Then you crossed three times, which means you swapped the first time, went back to your original positions the second, and then the third time, you swapped once more.」
The immense satisfaction of having guessed right and the promise of spending a night together with them had loosened Sakuya's tongue, and so he proudly revealed the trick, however,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……なぁにが。当てずっぽじゃん」
source.english: “…Oh, come on. You just guessed.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……Yeah, riiight. You just took a shot in the dark.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「案外良く見てるっておもったけど、
　はっ、やっぱ期待はずれ」
source.english:
“I thought you might be more observant than you looked.
Hah. Disappointing, as usual.”

source.japanese: ちっと失望の舌打ちそれぞれ一つ、二人は見下げた目つきで、
source.english: Each clicked her tongue in disappointment. Their looks were contemptuous.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I thought you had some unexpectedly good eyes, but…… haah, knew it, what a letdown.」
Both clicked their respective tongues in disappointment, and with a look of contempt in their eyes,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「二回目はくっついただけで交差してない。
　三回目のスピンの時、一回だけ半回転で左右を変えたんだ」
source.english:
“We only came together the second time. We didn't cross.
And during the third set of spins, one of the turns was only halfway round. That's when we changed sides.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「The second time we stuck close, but we didn't swap. During the third spin, we swapped sides by doing a single half-rotation.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「運も一つの実力だからさ、
　ヤマカンならヤマカンって言えばいいのに、
　とってつけた説明って、どうよ？」
source.english:
“Luck's a skill, too.
If you guessed, you could've just said so.
Why tack on an explanation?”

source.japanese: ……どうやら朔屋のいい加減な受け答えが、二人の不興を買ってしまったらしかった。
source.english: …Apparently, Sakuya's careless answer had offended them.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Luck is a talent in its own right, but still, if its just a hunch, then just say that. What were you thinking with that tacked-on explanation?」
……It appeared that Sakuya's ill-conceived answer had managed to incur their displeasure.

source.japanese: 左見右見、何度も繰り返しても見当もつかず、そもそも双子が本気でトリックしかけてきたなら到底朔屋の手に負えたものではない。もっと長い時間を共に過ごしてみれば、何らかの差違を見分ける目も育つかも知れないが、生憎昨夜知り合ったばかりで間もない。
source.english: He looked left, looked right, again and again, without a clue. If the twins were serious about tricking him, they were well beyond his powers. With more time together, perhaps he could have learned to spot some difference. Unfortunately, he had only met them last night.

source.japanese: 考えるだけ迷うだけ無駄だと、根が続かず朔屋はさっさと諦めた。もともと注意力散漫な男なのである。
source.english: Thinking and wondering were a waste of time. He lacked the patience and soon gave up. He had never been a particularly attentive man.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやあわかんないわ。
　目で追いきれなくなったし」
source.english:
“Nope, I can't tell.
I lost track.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それにそんな勝負っ気、途中から忘れた。
　ま、見てるだけでも良かったよ」
source.english:
“Besides, I forgot it was a contest halfway through.
It was nice just watching.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ただ希望としては、こう、少しずつ脱いでくとか、スカートの裾[すそ]をちょっとばかり捲[めく]ってみてくれたりしたら、もっと嬉しかったんだが……」
source.english: “Though if I could make a suggestion, I'd have been happier if you'd gradually taken things off, or lifted your skirts a little…”

source.japanese: 二人の仕掛けた惑わしに挑む事あっさり放棄して、それどころかストリップ紛いの注文をつけてへらへらと悪びれもしない朔屋に、双子は揃って腕組みして呆れ果てた溜め息を漏らしたが、やがてどちらともなくくつくつ笑い出した。
source.english: He cheerfully abandoned any attempt to beat their trick. Worse, he grinned without shame as he asked for something resembling a striptease. The twins folded their arms and sighed together in utter disbelief. Then a chuckle started up between them.

target.text: He looked left and right, over and over again, but no matter how many times he did, he was still just as clueless as before, and if these twins truly wanted to trick him, then it was utterly beyond Sakuya's capabilities to figure out in the first place. If they had spent some more time together, perhaps his eyes might have come to find some way to differentiate between the two, but unfortunately, he had only just come to know them the night before.
Thinking merely left him stumped, so he judged that a waste of time, and with his patience running thin, Sakuya quickly gave up. He was a man who had always been easily distracted.
【Naomasa】 「Weeell, I have no clue. My eyes couldn't keep up.」
【Naomasa】 「And at some point, I forgot this was even a game. Well, just looking was nice in its own right.」

【Naomasa】 「But if you're open to requests, then I'd prefer something like, stripping little by little, or if you could try to roll the bottoms of your skirts up just a bit, that'd make me a lot happier……」

Sakuya readily gave up on the misleading challenge prepared by the twins, and he instead began trying to make requests for some pseudo-striptease, grinning foolishly with not a hint of shame; the twins crossed their arms at him with an exasperated sigh, until finally, no longer able to stifle it, they both began to chuckle.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「いじりがいがあるんだかないんだか、判らない奴だねあんたってば」
source.english: “I can't decide whether you're worth teasing or not.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「You're hard to read. Can't tell if you're worth teasing or not.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「おまけに脱げと、尻を振れときた。
　そういうのは無料じゃあ見せらんないなあ」
source.english:
“And now it's ‘Take your clothes off, shake your ass.’
We don't show you that sort of thing for free.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And what's more, he tells us to strip, to shake our asses. We don't show that kind of stuff to others as charity.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「まあ、身ぐるみ剥ぐのは勘弁してあげる。
　どうせ財布の中身だって空だろうし」
source.english:
“Well, we'll let you off without stripping you.
Your purse is empty anyway, isn't it?”

source.japanese: 賭けにも乗ってこないのは用心深いのではなく意気地無いだけ、その後に悪びれもせず肌の露出を要求してきたのは大胆というより考え無し、どう見ても朔屋はここでも駄目さ加減を披露しただけ、それでも彼に向けられた双子の視線には、どこか興を覚えた風が浮かんでいるのが、妙な塩梅ではあった。
source.english: His refusal to take the bet was not caution, merely a lack of nerve. His shameless request for more exposed flesh afterward was not boldness, merely thoughtlessness. By any measure, Sakuya had done nothing but display his inadequacy once again. Yet there was something strangely amused in the twins' eyes as they regarded him.

source.japanese: 金髪の双子、信天翁号の一等航海士は朔屋をひとしきりいじくり回した後に、ぱんと一つ大きく手を拍って区切りにし、
source.english: After thoroughly playing with Sakuya, the blond twins—the Albatross's first mates—brought things to a close with a loud clap.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Well, we'll drop the whole stripping you bare thing. I'm sure your wallet's empty anyway.」

That he didn't join in on the bet was a result of cowardice, not prudence, and asking to see some skin with not a hint of shame after the fact was thoughtlessness, not boldness, and by any standards, it was clear that all Sakuya had shown here was the extent of his hopelessness, but even so, there was a hint of amused interest somewhere in the gazes the twins sent his way, a rather strange state of affairs.
The blonde twins, the first mates of the Albatross, having monkeyed around with Sakuya for a while, now clapped their hands together to mark an end to the silliness,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「さてさてともかく───
　ようこそ、信天翁号へ！」
source.english:
“Now then,
anyway—welcome aboard the Albatross!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Well then, setting that aside─── Welcome aboard the Albatross!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「さてさてよろしく───
　良い船だよ、この信天翁号は、ほんとに！」
source.english:
“Here's to working together—she's a good ship,
the Albatross. Really!”

source.japanese: おもむろに左右から青年の腕を取り、にんまり微笑む。その位置取りは昨夜の酒場を思わせて、朔屋に昨夜の続きを期待させたが、そんな都合の良い展開など振ろう筈もない。双子が押しやっていくのは舷梯へ、沈没寸前の廃物の塊、信天翁号へと続く舷梯へ、なのだとやっと気づいて抗[あらが]おうにも双子の力は意外にも強く、地に突っ張る足は空しく外れてずるずると、抵抗甲斐なく青年は段を引きずりあげられる、しまいにとうとう船へと連れこまれてしまう様、二頭の雌獅子に仕留められた餌食と大差なかった。
source.english:
They took an arm each and smiled broadly. Their positions recalled the tavern the previous night, and Sakuya began to hope for a continuation. No such convenient turn awaited him.
They were pushing him toward the gangway. The gangway that led to the Albatross, that mass of discarded junk on the verge of sinking. He finally realized it and tried to resist, but the twins were surprisingly strong. The feet he planted against the ground slid uselessly. They dragged him up the steps despite his struggles and at last took him aboard. He looked much like prey brought down by a pair of lionesses.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Well then, glad to have you aboard─── She's a good ship, our Albatross, I promise!」

They grasped the young man's arms gently from both sides, lips curled into satisfied smiles. The position reminded him of the bar last night, and it did make Sakuya hopeful for a continuation of last night's excitement, but there was no way such a convenient turn of events would come about.

The twins shoved him towards the gangway, the path leading to this heap of scrap on the verge of sinking, to the gangway leading to the Albatross, but when he finally realized as much and made to resist, the twins turned out to be unexpectedly strong; the legs he had planted firmly on the ground in vain were swept out from under him, he was dragged along, the pointlessly struggling young man pulled upwards, and in the end, when he was finally hauled up onto the ship, it was in a manner hardly any different from prey caught in the claws of two lionesses.

source.japanese: <01>適当に答えてみる
source.english: Take a guess.

target.text: <01>Tried guessing randomly

source.japanese: <01>そんな事判るかと開き直る
source.english: Flatly say I can't tell them apart.

target.text: <01>Retorted in indignant ignorance

source.japanese:
───かくして、なし崩しも大崩し、一ノ谷の裏手から、鵯鳥の逆落とし式に安穏で怠惰な陸から洋上に浮かぶスラム紛いの信天翁号に叩きこまれる事になった朔屋の目は。
　上甲板、という名のバラックの一大集積地から段を下り、船内へと連れて行かれた青年の目は。
　これから火責めに遭おうかという城で抜け道を求めるすくたれ者の怯えにびくついていたとしても無理はない。事実朔屋は隙あらばこの信天翁なる呪われた船から、早々に逃げ出そうと固く決意していたのだからして。
source.english:
—And so, the piecemeal collapse became wholesale. Like the headlong charge down Hiyodori Pass behind Ichi-no-Tani, Sakuya was hurled from a peaceful, indolent life ashore into the Albatross, a floating slum at sea. And his eyes—
His eyes, as he was led down from the vast agglomeration of shacks known as the upper deck and into the ship—
Well, no one could have blamed them for twitching with the terror of a craven hunting a secret passage out of a castle about to be put to the torch. Sakuya had, after all, firmly resolved to flee this accursed vessel at the first opportunity.

source.japanese: けれども、その決意も努力も空しかった。階段の鋲にけつまずいた振りして蹌踉めいてみせ、隙に上甲板へ駆け逃れようとしたのだが背後には、水夫長の尊大なる体躯が通路を塞いでほぼ幅一杯。その上朔屋の内心など容易く見抜いて水夫長の目が獰猛に光り、唇の端がめくれ返って豚の大腿骨でも噛み砕けそうなほどの犬歯をちらつかせたは余裕の笑みか威嚇か。それでも朔屋は懲りずに幾度か解囲を試みて、その都度無言の圧力に阻まれて、始めは睨視で済んでいたのにやがて牛の頭蓋骨でも叩き割りそうな拳骨をこれ見よがし握りしめられるにいたって、やむなく諦めた。
source.english:
Both resolve and effort proved futile. He pretended to trip on a rivet in the stairs and staggered, hoping to make a dash for the upper deck. Behind him, however, the boatswain's imposing body blocked nearly the full width of the passage. The man saw through him with ease. His eyes gleamed savagely, and the corners of his lips peeled back to reveal canine teeth that looked capable of crushing a pig's thighbone. Was that a confident smile, or a threat?
Even so, Sakuya tried several times to break through. Each attempt met the same silent pressure. At first a glare sufficed. Eventually the boatswain ostentatiously clenched a fist that looked capable of splitting a cow's skull, and Sakuya had to give up.

source.japanese: といって、朔屋が逃走を断念したというのではけしてなく、ほら、ある種の小動物は捕食者にいよいよ追いつめられた際、悪あがきを中断する時がある。そして向こうが待ってましたと仕留めにかかった瞬間に最後の力爆発させて走り逃れる、その式で、しばし相手を油断させておこうとしたので。幸い船に機関部の脈動は未だ響かず、今しばらくは停泊していよう、さにあらばタラップから港へと駆け下りる隙もあろう。
source.english:
Not that he had abandoned escape. Some small animals, you know, stop struggling when a predator has them cornered. Then, at the instant the predator thinks its victory assured and moves in for the kill, they burst away with the last of their strength. He meant to follow that example and let his captor grow careless for a while.
Fortunately, no engine's pulse yet sounded through the ship. She would remain moored a little longer. There would still be a chance to dash down the gangway to the harbor.

source.japanese:
いかに老練なこの水夫長とて、百の目を持つという巨人でもあるまいし、かつまた顔覆う刺青の龍とて本体を離れて水夫達をいちいち監視するでもなかろうし、目が離れる瞬間だってあるだろう。
　朔屋はとりあえずそのように、彼の望むろくでもない自由への希求の念をなに食わぬ面の下に沈め、改めて船内通路の様子を目探ってみる───と。
　船内は、いくらかはましであった。
source.english:
Experienced as he was, the boatswain was not the hundred-eyed giant. Nor was the tattooed dragon on his face likely to leave its host and keep watch over every sailor. He must look away sometime.
For the moment, Sakuya buried his yearning for his own worthless sort of freedom beneath an innocent expression. He took another look at the passage—and—
The interior was somewhat better.

source.japanese:
ただし、ましとは言っても上甲板に比べれば、という意味で、まずこの級の船であればあって然るべきの光量というのに欠けている。それでいて通路や内壁には配管が、その手の技術知識には疎い朔屋をしてさえ、どうにも無理があるのではないかと疑念を抱かせるほどごちゃごちゃと無秩序に這っていて、うっかりするとけつまずく、ぼんやりしていると出張った管に体のあちこちを打ちつける。
　おまけに、ただでさえ余裕に乏しい船内通路であるのに、後から適当に配されたらしい道具箱や用途不明の張り出しなどもそこらここらに、ここを船内勤務に要求される速度で一直線に駆けるには、余程の反射神経とバランス感覚が要求されるだろう。
　そのくせ通路の端々には、隠れんぼには最適であろうが円滑なる業務には邪魔そのもののデッドスペースなどが見受けられるのだから恐れ入る。
source.english:
Better than the upper deck, that is. It lacked the amount of light one ought to find aboard a ship of this class. Pipes crawled in disorder over the passage and inner walls, so tangled that even Sakuya, ignorant of such technical matters, wondered whether the arrangement was feasible. A careless step meant a stumble. An inattentive movement meant banging some part of oneself against a projecting pipe.
The passage was cramped enough already. Tool chests and protrusions of unknown purpose, apparently added later wherever they would fit, cluttered it further. Running straight down it at the speed required of a working sailor would take remarkable reflexes and balance.
Yet here and there were dead spaces, ideal for hide-and-seek and nothing but an impediment to smooth work. Astonishing.

target.text: ───Thus, down the slippery slope turned sheer cliff, like the headlong plunge down Hiyodori-goe, Sakuya was taken from his comfortable life of indolence on land and tossed onto this slum-like Albatross floating on the sea, oh cruel fate. (TN: This is a reference to the Battle of Ichi-no-Tani in 1184, where Minamoto no Yoshitsune personally lead a detachment of cavalry down the near-vertical cliff of Hiyodori-goe, routing the unsuspecting Taira.)

Down the steps from this great cluster of shanties, also known as the upper deck, the young man was led further inside the ship, oh cruel fate. It was no wonder he twitched with the terror of some spineless wretch frantically searching for an escape out of a castle destined to be put to the torch. In fact, if Sakuya ever were to find an opportunity to escape this accursed ship they called the Albatross, he was firmly determined to grasp it as soon as possible.

But even so, that determination and effort proved in vain. When he pretended to stumble over the rivets in the steps and made a show of reeling, attempting to use that as a chance to escape to the upper deck, behind him, the Bosun's imposing physique was blocking almost the entire passageway from side to side. And that wasn't all; the eyes of this bosun, seeing right through Sakuya's intentions with ease, gleamed with ferocity, and the edge of his lips pulled back, flashing canines that looked capable of easily crushing even a pig's femur: a composed smirk, or perhaps a threat?

And yet Sakuya remained incorrigible: he tried to break through the enemy siege multiple times, and each time, he would be thwarted by that silent pressure; at first, he got off with just a glare, but when, in an ostentatious show of intimidation, the Bosun finally clenched his fists that looked like they could crack the skull of a bull in half, he reluctantly gave up.

Although, with that said, Sakuya had by no means given up on his plan to escape; look, when certain small animals are finally cornered by their predators, there are times when they cease their vain struggle. Then, when the predator goes in for the kill, having awaited that moment, they escape with a final outburst of power, and likewise, he was simply lulling his opponent into a false sense of security, for a time. Fortunately, the pulsations from the engine room were yet to reverberate throughout the ship, so it seemed they would remain moored for now, whence it followed that there would be an opportunity for him to dash down that gangway and escape to the port.

However experienced this bosun may be, he was not some all-seeing, hundred-eyed giant; furthermore, surely the dragon tattoo covering his face could not separate from his body to monitor each and every sailor, so there would surely be moments where his watchful gaze would wander. But as described, for now, Sakuya kept his aspirations for the worthless freedom he desired veiled beneath a mask of feigned ignorance, once more letting his eyes wander to ascertain the state of the internal ship passageway───well. The inside of the ship was better, to some extent.

However, this "better" was only in the context of being compared to the upper deck; first of all, it lacked the amount of light that was appropriate for a ship of this class. Despite that, the piping running through the passageways and interior walls were left in such a haphazard, disorderly mess that even Sakuya, a man ill-informed on such matters of technical knowledge, couldn't help but wonder if this was even feasible at all; if one was not careful, one would trip all over it, and if one was not paying attention, one was like to knock one's body against all these pipes sticking out of the walls.

And to top it off, even though these passageways were already lacking in spare room, there were toolboxes that seemed to have been put there in a desultory fashion later on, as well as overhangs of indiscernible purpose here and there, and being able to run through this in a straight line at the speed demanded by on-board duties would surely require exceptional reflexes and balance. And yet, in spite of that, here and there in the passageways, he caught sight of dead space that would probably be perfectly suited for hide and seek but otherwise only get in the way of streamlined work; he couldn't help but be impressed.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「どうでえ。中に降りてみるとますます快適ってなもんだろう。
　おめえ、こんな居心地良いのは、Ｐ＆Ｏの船にだってそうそうないぜえ」
source.english:
“Well? Even more comfortable down here, eh?
You won't find many ships this cozy even in P&O.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はぁ……きっとそうでしょうよ……」
source.english: “Oh… I'm sure you won't…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So how about it? She's even more comfortable once you go inside, right? Listen, it's hard to find something this comfortable elsewhere, even on a P&O ship.」
【Naomasa】 「Haah……I'm sure that's the case……」

source.japanese: 相槌も適当なり、水夫長のぶちあげるにも程があって、かの英国一流の港運会社の船に一隻でもこんな信天翁号の如き代物が混ざっていた事が判明したならば、保険担当の者はたちどころに急性にして極めて悪性の胃潰瘍を発症し血を吐いて悶絶した事だろう、と口にしないだけの分別は辛うじて持ち合わせていた朔屋、水夫長に押し出されるように、船内通路の配管に頭をぶつけたり、歩く者の足を取る為に意地悪く仕組まれたのではないかと疑わしいほどの段差に爪先を打ちつけたりしながら、船の奥へ深くへ。これ以上踏みこめば二度と逃れられぬ、蛇のねぐらの深くに潜[もぐ]りこんでいくかの不安が募る、船内のいい加減で乱雑な様相を見るにつれつれ後悔は深くなり勝る。
source.english:
His agreement was vague. There were limits even to the boatswain's boasting. Had anyone discovered a vessel like the Albatross among that first-class British shipping company's fleet, the man responsible for insurance would surely have developed an acute and exceptionally malignant stomach ulcer, vomited blood, and collapsed in agony. Sakuya just about retained enough sense not to say so.
Prodded onward by the boatswain, he went deeper into the ship, banging his head on pipes and stubbing his toes on changes in level so maliciously placed they might have been designed to trip a walker. He felt as though he were entering the depths of a snake's den, going too far to escape again. Every glimpse of the interior's careless disorder deepened his regret.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（やっぱり俺、どうなっても、
　とにかくこの船に乗りこむ前に、
　逃げておくべきだったんじゃあ……）
source.english:
(I really should have run before I came aboard,
shouldn't I?
Whatever happened afterward…)

source.japanese: いつしか区画は船員達の居住区に入ったと見えて、通路の両脇に扉が並ぶようになっていたけれど、扉の列から漂うのは船乗り達の憩う場に然るべきの、くつろげる頼もしさ安らげる心強さから隔たって、脳病院の隔離区域に垂れこめる、湿気っぽく重苦しい気配の、どうにも浮かない事この上ない。思えばそういうおつむの病院の療士達というのも、白衣の天使どころか筋骨逞[たくま]しい獄吏はだしの凶猛な男達が多く、その意味では朔屋を押し出していく水夫長などはいかにも相応しい。惑乱した患者達を「優しく」黙らせるためのブラックジャックを手に持たせたりすると、嵌りすぎていて笑いも取れない。
source.english:
They seemed to have reached the crew's quarters. Doors began to line both sides of the passage. But nothing about them offered the reassuring ease of a place where sailors might rest. A damp, oppressive atmosphere hung there, like the isolation ward of a mental hospital. Thoroughly depressing.
Come to think of it, the orderlies in such institutions were often less angels in white than fierce, muscular men who could put prison guards to shame. In that sense, the boatswain driving Sakuya along was entirely fitting. Put a blackjack in his hand to ‘gently’ quiet the disturbed patients, and the likeness would be too exact for laughter.

source.japanese:
そんな目で居住区画を眺めていたから朔屋は、努めてその扉を見過ごしにしたのである。
　なにやら掠れた茶色、乾いた血膿とか泥土などを思わせる色合いの、拙劣な線が一面にのたくったその扉、扉には。
source.english:
With that view of the living quarters, Sakuya did his best to ignore one particular door.
Clumsy lines sprawled over its surface in a faded brown, a color suggesting dried blood and pus, or mud. On that door—

target.text: His interjections had also grown half-hearted ; the Bosun's boastful exaggerations had gone too far, and were it to become known that even a single vessel belonging to a certain prestigious British shipping line had been associated with the likes of the Albatross, their insurance representative would likely immediately be overcome by an acute and extremely malignant stomach ulcer, coughing up blood as he fainted in agony.

While Sakuya was just barely possessed of the prudence demanded to not put that into words, it felt as though he was being shoved forwards by the Bosun; he hit his head on the pipes in the passageways, hit his toes against the steps that he almost suspected were placed maliciously to trip up people while they were walking, and he went deeper into the depths of the ship. He could never leave again if he tread any further: the anxiety of crawling into the bottom of a snake's nest only intensified, and as he beheld the careless and disordered state of the ship's interior, his regret grew all the more profound, outweighing all that otherwise weighed on his mind.
【Naomasa】 （I knew it. No matter what would have happened as a result, I really should have run away before getting on board this ship……)

Before long, he seemed to have crossed into the part of the ship that housed the crew accommodation, and while there were doors lined up along both sides of the passageway, what wafted from those rows of doors was far from what should be emanating from a place of rest for sailors, that relaxing dependability and soothing reassurance; instead, it was like the damp, oppressive air hanging low over the isolation ward of a madhouse, and one would be hard-pressed to find a more depressing place.

On that topic, speaking of those healers from mental hospitals, rather than angelic nurses, there tended to be a lot more burly men made entirely of muscle and bone with a ferocity that could put gaolers to shame, and in that sense, the Bosun pushing Sakuya forwards made a great fit for this place indeed. And if the Bosun were to hold in his hand a blackjack of the kind used to "gently" quiet down any bewildered patients, it would fit so perfectly that it couldn't even elicit a smile from him.

And it was precisely because Sakuya beheld the cabins with that perspective that he did his utmost to overlook that door. It was a faded brown, a hue that brought to mind mud, or dried, bloody pus; that door, covered in a mass of crudely drawn lines squirming across its surface, oh, that door.

source.japanese:
耽美派、なのだろうか。
　意匠化された薔薇と思しき紋様が描き出されていた。
　そしてやはり朔屋の印象通り、その船室の主は脳内の回路にどこかしら異常を来していたのだろうか。
　薔薇の棘の蔓には、様々なモノが吊り下げられた画も描き加えられていた。
source.english:
An aesthete, perhaps?
A design resembling stylized roses had been painted there.
And, just as Sakuya suspected, perhaps something had gone wrong with the occupant's mental circuitry.
For various things had been added to the picture, hanging from the thorny rose vines.

source.japanese: ほら、豚が吊り下げられている、そら、兎が吊り下げられている、他にも小鳥だの犬だの熊のぬいぐるみだの魚だの蜥蜴だの蛙だの様々な生き物が、全て首吊りの形で。陰鬱に弛緩した態で。薔薇と同じ拙劣な線なのに、妙に真に迫って、ちょっと目にしただけでも心がささくれる。
source.english: Look, a pig hung there. Look, a rabbit. Little birds, dogs, a teddy bear, fish, lizards, frogs—all sorts of creatures, every one hanging by the neck. Limp and dismal. The lines were as crude as those of the roses, yet oddly convincing. A glance was enough to leave the mind scraped raw.

source.japanese: ……こんな扉の裡側には、どんな乗り組みが棲息しているのか、眺めればどうしても想像が働いてしまうけれど、いずれ心楽しい仔細であるはずもなく、朔屋は見ないように見ないように行き過ぎようとして、首が絞まった。
source.english: …What sort of crew member lived behind a door like this? Looking at it inevitably set the imagination working. None of the particulars could be pleasant. Sakuya tried to pass without looking, without looking—and something tightened about his neck.

source.japanese: 扉に描かれたる縊死体達が新たな仲間を求めて蔓薔薇を伸ばしてきたか、首筋に棘の鋭さ痛さが確かに食いこんだと思って、悲鳴迸らせそうになって、
source.english: Had the hanged creatures on the door sent out a rose vine in search of a new companion? He felt sharp, painful thorns bite into his neck, and nearly let out a scream—

target.text: It must have been the product of some Aesthete, he supposed? There was a pattern that resembled a stylized rose depicted on the door. And then, just as Sakuya had initially assumed, there must have been something very abnormal running through the owner of this room's brain indeed. For suspended from the thorny vines of the rose were a great many things depicted, dangling below.

Look, there's a pig hanging, and there, a bunny hanging, and a small bird and a dog and a stuffed bear and a fish and a lizard and a frog and all kinds of living creatures, all hanged by the neck. In a dismally flaccid manner. Despite being drawn as clumsily as the rose, they were oddly realistic, with just a small glance enough to fray the mind.

……What kind of crew could possibly inhabit what lay beyond this door? He couldn't keep his imagination from running wild once he'd seen it; surely there were no pleasant circumstances to be discovered here, and just as Sakuya tried to pass by it while acting like he'd seen nothing, his neck was constricted by something.

Those strangulated corpses drawn on that door must have reached out with their climbing rose in search of a new friend, that is what he thought, confident he could feel the sharp pain of thorns biting into the back of his neck, a scream about to surge up from his throat,
【Naomasa】 「Kherrgh……!?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「どこまで行くんだよ。
　ここだ、この部屋だ、お前の寝床は」
source.english:
“Where're you going? Here.
This room. This is where you sleep.”

source.japanese: 朔屋を捕らえたのは、扉の怪奇画が具現化させた障気などではなく、水夫長が背後から襟首つまみ上げた剛力にして、悲鳴と一緒に薄暗い妄想も立ち消えになったというものの。妄想よりも現実の方が優しいなどと誰が決めた。朔屋は陰鬱な意匠描き出された扉と水夫長に目まぐるしく視線を交互させた。
source.english:
What held Sakuya was not some miasma made flesh by the door's uncanny pictures, but the boatswain's enormous strength, lifting him by the collar from behind. The dark fancy vanished along with his scream.
But who had decided that reality was kinder than imagination? His eyes darted between the boatswain and the door with its gloomy design.

source.japanese: 青年の陸での下宿というのは六畳一間の、畳は粗び、柱と漆喰壁の間は建て付け緩んで隙間風、大家は少しばかり惚けがきた老爺であったけれど、それでもこんな扉がついた船室に比べれば、まだ温い陽差しの中の世界だったと言いきれる。こんな部屋などに起き臥ししようものなら、美国の古都、かつて魔女狩りに遭って拷問の果てに横死を遂げた老婆が住んでいた屋根裏部屋で見るのと同じ類の悪夢に襲われ、消耗死すること間違いなしと朔屋は、半泣きで抗議しようとした、顔がぐんと横に振られた。
source.english:
His lodgings ashore were a single six-mat room. The tatami were worn; loose joints between pillars and plaster let in drafts. His landlord was an old man beginning to lose his wits. Yet compared with a cabin behind this door, that room belonged to a world of warm sunshine.
Sleep and wake in a room like this, and he would surely waste away under nightmares of the sort one might dream in an attic in an old American town, where an elderly woman had once lived before witch hunters tortured her to death.
Sakuya tried to protest, on the verge of tears. His face jerked sharply sideways.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Where do you think you're going? We're here, it's this cabin, this is your berth.」

What had caught Sakuya by the neck was not some miasma manifested by the grotesque picture on the door, it was the herculean strength of the Bosun as he plucked him off the ground by his collar, the scream taking its leave along with his creepy delusions. But who decided that reality would be kinder than delusions? Sakuya's gaze flitted between the door with the gloomy design and the Bosun at dizzying speeds.

The young man's lodgings on shore had been a six-tatami room, the mats old and well-used, the fit between posts and plaster walls loose and draughty, and the landlord a slightly senile old man, but even so, compared to a cabin fitted with this door, he could confidently declare it a world bathed in still-warm sunlight.

If he had to rise from and go to bed in a room like this, he'd be assaulted by nightmares of a similar kind to the ones experienced when staying in an attic room found in one of America's ancient, storied cities once inhabited by an old lady who died a pitiful death after prolonged torture during the witch trials of the olden days; Sakuya had no doubt he'd waste to death, and he tried to say as much in protest while half in tears, rapidly swinging his head side to side.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「お前はどう見たってどうしようもねえへなちょこだが。
　でもよかったなあお前、船員学校にいたっていうのは買ってやる」
source.english:
“You're a hopeless little weakling any way I look at you.
Still, you went to sailors' school. I'll give you that much.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「始めっから一人部屋もらえるなんて、どこのオフィサー様だかな。
　ま、ここが今日からお前の部屋だ」
source.english:
“A cabin of your own from the start. You'd think you were some high-and-mighty officer.
Well, this is your room from today.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「No matter how I look at you, all I see is a hopeless green hand. But aren't you a lucky guy? I'll put some stock in your claims of having gone to nautical school.」
【Bosun】 「Look at little mister officer here, getting a room all to himself, right from the outset. Well, from today onwards, this is your cabin.」

source.japanese: 告げ様、水夫長が巻揚機じみた怪力の、片手で朔屋を吊り上げ片手で扉を引き開けて、ぶんと放り投げたが船室の中へ、朔屋の視界が抗議の間もなく流れ、青年の体が床にどすんと響いて痛い、ばたんと扉がたてられてむごい。
source.english: So saying, the boatswain, with the strength of a winch, hoisted Sakuya one-handed, hauled the door open with the other, and swung him into the cabin. His view went streaming by before he could protest; his body struck the floor with a thud—painful—and the door slammed shut behind him—cruel.

target.text: No sooner than he proclaimed thus did he use his winch-like superhuman strength to hoist Sakuya in the air with one hand and pull open the door with the other, then tossed him into the cabin; Sakuya's vision blurred before he even had the chance to object, the young man's body hitting the floor with a painful thump, door slammed shut behind him, what cruelty.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「げあ！　あ痛たたたた。
　あっ、水夫長。そんなひどい。
　俺、どうせならもっと別の部屋が」
source.english:
“Gah! Ow, ow, ow!
Hey, Boatswain! That's cruel!
I'd rather have a different room…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、この部屋じゃなけりゃあ、
　すし詰めの大部屋だって良い。
　だからお願い、この部屋は勘弁して。
　ていうかこの部屋、何か扉が怖えようっ」
source.english:
“Anything but this room.
I'd take a packed dormitory.
Please, spare me this one.
I mean, there's something scary about the door!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だいたいここは空き部屋なのかそもそも」
source.english: “Is it even empty in the first place?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Gah! Ow ow ow, that hurts! Ah, Bosun. How could you? If at all possible, I'd really prefer another cabin, so-」
【Naomasa】 「No, as long as it's not this one, I'll even take a shared cabin packed like sardines. I'm begging you, anywhere but here. I mean, there's just something kind of creepy about that door.」
【Naomasa】 「Actually, first off, is this cabin even vacant?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう。空き部屋に『なったばかりだ』とも。
　この前の航海で、そこを使ってた奴ぁ───」
source.english:
“Oh, yes. It's only just become empty.
The one who had it on the last voyage—”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「『お祭りだぁい』とか盆踊りしながら、
　飛び出しちまってそれっきりだ」
source.english:
“Off they went doing a Bon festival dance, yelling ‘Festival time!’
And that was the last we saw of them.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Aye. It『just became』vacant. See, back on our last voyage, the guy who used this cabin───」
【Bosun】 「He yelled "THE FESTIVAL'S ON!" or something while dancing the Bon-Odori, then he jumped off, and that was the last of him.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「真っ暗な晩、甲板から海の上にな！」
source.english: “Straight off the deck into the sea, on a pitch-black night!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やっぱりそういう話ですかい。
　扉、この部屋の扉ッ。
　見たまんま、気が変になってたんじゃねーの」
source.english:
“I knew it was that kind of story.
The door! This room's door!
He'd lost his mind, just like it looks!”

source.japanese: 打ち身に顔情けなくしかめつ、のろのろ立ち上がろうとて朔屋は、ぎょっと身を強張らせた。たてきられた戸の向こうで、ずるずるとなにやら重たげな嵩[かさ]の引きずられる音、続いてゴトンと扉の前で収まる音、最後に水夫長の蛮声が被さって、ごつい跫音が寝覚めの夢のように遠ざかる。
source.english: Sakuya was slowly trying to stand, his face twisted miserably at his bruises, when he froze. Beyond the closed door, something heavy scraped across the floor. Then came a clunk as it settled in front of the door. The boatswain's rough voice followed. His heavy footsteps receded like a dream on waking.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まあ精々綺麗に使ってやんな。
　誰か手ぇ空いてたら、手伝いに寄越してやっからよ」
source.english:
“Keep it nice and clean.
If anyone's free, I'll send them along to help.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「On a pitch black night, he plunged right from the deck and into the sea!」
【Naomasa】 「I knew that's where this was going. The door, the door to this room. It's exactly what it looks like, he must have gone mad, right?」

Sakuya's face twisted into a scowling grimace as he began sluggishly lifting his battered body off the floor, but then he suddenly tensed up in shock. From beyond the door slammed shut came the sound of something like a heavy rock being dragged across the floor, followed by a heavy thud as whatever it was stopped in front of the door; finally, the Bosun's gruff voice drowned everything out, and the thumping of his heavy footfalls receded into the distance like a dream upon the cusp of waking.
【Bosun】 「Well, just try to keep it clean. If I find somebody empty-handed, I'll send them over to help you out.」

source.japanese: 船内において身の回りの始末は各々が自分で尻を拭くのがお定まりのところ、手伝いなんてあてに出来るか、否問題はそこではなく、と朔屋は焦って扉にむしゃぶりついて、ドアノブがちゃつかせ鏡板に拳を打ちつけて、出せえ開けろと懲罰房に叩きこまれた悪童さながら悪足掻き、したところで扉の反対側の何かは余程重たくがっちり据えられたと見え、無駄な足掻きと終わったわ。あのじじい、と朔屋は水夫長への報復の決意を育てたが、それとて機会を見つけて食事の中に硝子の欠片でも混ぜてくれるとの、小心にして卑劣な手段くらいというのがこの青年の格というモノを示していよう。だいたいそんな事をしたところであの水夫長の強靱そうな歯と顎の前にはさしたる痛痒も与えるとは思えず、かつそんな決意を弄[もてあそ]んだところで船室の扉は今や劫経た亀の甲羅より頑固に硬く朔屋を閉じこめる。
source.english:
Aboard ship, each man was expected to see to his own affairs. As if he could count on help! No, that was not the problem. Sakuya flung himself anxiously at the door, rattled the knob, beat his fist against the panel. Let me out! Open up! He struggled like a delinquent thrown into a punishment cell. Whatever stood on the other side was apparently very heavy and firmly placed. All his struggles came to nothing.
That old bastard. A determination to avenge himself grew in Sakuya. It amounted, however, to no more than slipping shards of glass into the man's food when he had a chance—a cowardly, contemptible plan, revealing the young man's caliber. Besides, such glass hardly seemed likely to trouble the boatswain's formidable teeth and jaws. And pondering revenge would not alter the cabin door, now harder and more stubborn than an ancient tortoise's shell, keeping Sakuya shut inside.

source.japanese: （後に朔屋はひょんな契機から水夫長の弱点、というか奇癖を知るのだがそれはまた別の挿話）
source.english: (Later, a chance occurrence would reveal the boatswain's weakness—or rather, his peculiar habit. But that is another story.)

source.japanese:
どうやら水夫長殿慧眼で、朔屋を放置しておけばたちどころに逃げ出すと見てとって閉じこめていったらしい、賢い。
　いつまでも強情に戸を叩き続けたところで埒など開きそうにもなく、しまいにはまさしく脳病院の病室の中で、己を正常だと思いこんで助けを求め続ける狂人の姿と自分が重なってげんなりして、朔屋は仕方なく船室へと目を向けた。
source.english:
The boatswain had apparently seen with admirable clarity that Sakuya would run the moment he was left alone, and had shut him in. Clever.
No amount of stubborn knocking would get him anywhere. Eventually, he became disgusted by his resemblance to a madman in a hospital room, convinced that he was sane and endlessly calling for help. He had no choice but to look at the cabin.

source.japanese:
惨憺たる有り様だった。
　とりたてて見やすく、先の住人の狂を示した徴はない。壁一面に落書きされて部屋のどこにいようと焦点を合わせてくる『目』の画などないし、爪楊枝をくまなく突き立てられた赤子の人形や、鼻くそ集めて捏ねあげられた聖母像の祭壇も幸い見えない。
source.english:
It was a wretched sight.
There was no obvious token of the former occupant's madness. No eyes scrawled over every wall to follow him wherever he stood. Fortunately, there was no baby doll bristling with toothpicks, nor an altar to a Virgin Mary kneaded out of collected snot.

source.japanese: それでも室内には荒廃の気配というのか、まともな人間なら残して然るべきの、生活の垢とも言うべき痕跡がまるで見当たらず、先頃まで使っていたというには埃が厚く積もりすぎ、どうにも陰惨な気分にさせられる。ただ、壁に作りつけの、頑丈なばかりで粗末な寝台の、乱れのない寝具の一箇所ばかりが擦り切れて凹んでいるのと、船窓の下に、これも作りつけの卓の上に、いまし漂白されたと言わんばかりに眩い上質紙の束が置かれて白いのが荒れた室内の中で一際異様の気を放つ。よせばいいのに朔屋がわざわざ上質紙の束を覗きこんでみたところ。
source.english:
Even so, the room had an air of desolation. None of the ordinary traces of life, the accumulated grime a normal person should have left, were present. The dust lay too thick for somewhere supposedly occupied until recently. It was profoundly depressing.
There were only two exceptions. One spot in the bedding on the crude but sturdy built-in berth was worn and hollowed, though the rest was perfectly neat. And on the built-in desk below the porthole lay a stack of fine paper, dazzlingly white, as though freshly bleached. Its whiteness gave it a singularly strange presence in the derelict room.
Sakuya should have left well alone. Instead, he leaned over the paper.

target.text: It was the norm for all aboard a ship to each be able to take care of their own daily necessities, including cleaning up their own messes, so would a helper actually come? No, that really wasn't a pertinent problem right now, so Sakuya thought in a panic, grappling with the door, rattling the door knob, and pounding on the panel with his fists; let me out, open up, he yelled, struggling in vain like a naughty child thrown in the brig, but try as he might, whatever was on the other side seemed to be very heavy and firmly secured in place, and so it amounted to naught but wasted effort.

Damn that old man, Sakuya thought, the determination to get his revenge growing; when he found his chance, maybe he should mix some glass shards into his dinner: such cowardly, base means were all he could think of, and it displayed well the calibre of this young man. Even had he done such a thing, it was hard to imagine that the Bosun's sturdy-looking teeth and jaw would even feel any pain from crushing the glass in the first place, and furthermore, for all he fantasized about such resolve, the door to his cabin was even more stubbornly solid than the shell of a tortoise that had lived for aeons, locking Sakuya inside.
(Later on, by unexpected chance, Sakuya would come to learn of the Bosun's weak point, or rather, peculiar habit, but that's an episode for another time.)

Apparently, the great Bosun's keen eyes had noticed that Sakuya would attempt to run away if he was left alone, and so he locked him up, clever. It didn't seem like banging on the sturdy door was going to get him anywhere, no matter how stubbornly he persisted, and so, eventually, as he came to the demoralizing realization that he was the spitting image of a madman in a psychiatric ward continuously begging for help, insistent that he was the only sane one there, Sakuya begrudgingly turned his gaze from the door to the cabin.

What a wretched state of affairs. There were no particularly obvious signs of the madness that had afflicted the prior resident to be found. The walls weren't plastered with scribbles, and there weren't any paintings of『EYES』that followed you everywhere, always focused on you, no baby dolls with toothpicks stuck in them from head to toe, and an altar to the Virgin Mary kneaded together from a collection of boogers was, fortunately, also nowhere to be seen.

There was but a crude bed affixed to the wall, notable only for its sturdiness, with only a single spot in the otherwise undisturbed bedding that was worn out and sunken, and below the porthole, as well as on top of the built-in table, were bundles of high-quality wood-free paper, dazzlingly white as if they had just been bleached, the colour emitting a conspicuously queer air amidst this dilapidated room. He could have just let it be, but Sakuya still went to the effort of peeking at those bundles of wood-free paper.

source.japanese: 『　　床の隙間から　　見つめている　　　』
source.english: Watching from the gap in the floor

target.text: 『 From the gap in the floor They stare 』

source.japanese: のただ一行のみが紙葉の中央に、まるで定規で測ったようにきっちりと。見る者の心を硬直させる、棘々しい字体で───
source.english: That single line, and no other, occupied the exact center of the page, as though its place had been measured with a ruler—written in a thorny hand that made the mind seize up—
