target.text: But a single line in the middle of the paper, perfectly centred like it had been measured with a ruler. Characters written in a sharp, biting font, as if to petrify the heart of the reader───

source.japanese: ……朔屋は次の紙葉に続きがないかと一枚めくった。一枚下の紙葉にも、一言一句同じの一行が、それこそ寸分違わぬ位置に、全く同様の筆致で書きつけられているのみ他は無し。その下も同じ、さらに下も同じ、また下も同じと、めくるにつれ青年の手つきが狂疾めいた痙攣を帯びていく。
source.english: …He turned a sheet to see whether there was more beneath. The next page bore precisely the same line, word for word, in precisely the same place and the same handwriting. Nothing else. The page below was the same. The next, the same. The next, the same. As he turned them, his hands began to twitch as though afflicted by madness.

target.text: ……Sakuya figured there might be a continuation, and so he flipped to the next page. The next page contained the exact same line, word for word. And in the exact same spot, like it had been written by the very same pen stroke. And below that, the same, even further below, the same, yet further below, the same; a feverish shivering ran through the young man's page-turning hands.

source.japanese: しまいに朔屋はこらえかねて紙束むんずと引っ掴み、撒き散らしたのが夥しい。蝦蟇の油売りの、半紙を二枚が四枚四枚が八枚と細かに切り分けて、吹雪と流す芸なら軽薄ながらも華やぎが咲くけれど、こちら強張った顔の朔屋では、まして撒いた紙切れの一枚一枚に、
source.english: At last he could bear it no longer. He seized the whole stack and flung the sheets in all directions. A toad-oil seller's trick of cutting paper from two pieces into four, from four into eight, then sending it flying in a snowstorm might be frivolous, but at least it had some splendor. With Sakuya's rigid face, and with every scattered sheet declaring—

source.japanese: 『　　床の隙間から　　見つめている　　　』
source.english: Watching from the gap in the floor

source.japanese: とこう断言されていては。
source.english: —There was none of that.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うええなんだこれえええ。
　なんだってこう言う、人の心を不安定にするような文句を一枚ずつ全部にご丁寧に───」
source.english:
“Ugh,
what is this? Why would you go to all the trouble of writing something this unsettling on every single sheet—?”

source.japanese: ばさばさ舞い散る紙片はどこかの島で棺桶に冥途の川の渡し賃として収める紙の金じみて、余計に朔屋の気分へ冷風当てたし、船室を無駄に散らかすことになる、とは知りつつも。拾い集めるのも間抜けで億劫な気がして青年は、糸が切れた態で寝台に座りこんだ、ら、尻の位置がぴたりとそこだけ擦り切れていた部分と嵌[はま]るのである。そうやって座りこんで項垂れてみると、下がった視線は自然と床へ、床の、床板の、そこだけ隙間が空いているところへぴたりと据わるのである。
source.english:
The papers fluttered down like the paper money placed in coffins on some island to pay for passage across the river of the dead. That chilled him further. He knew he was making a pointless mess of the cabin, but picking it all up felt foolish and tiresome. Like a puppet with cut strings, he dropped onto the berth.
His backside fitted precisely into the one worn spot. Sitting there, head bowed, he found his lowered gaze falling naturally to the floor. The floorboards. The one place where a gap opened between them.

target.text: Finally, Sakuya grabbed the paper bundle with all his might, and the amount of paper he scattered was vast. Like a seller of toad oil cutting Japanese calligraphy paper, one became two, two became four, four became eight; he ripped it into minute shreds. (TN: This is a reference to a type of street performance done by sellers of toad oil, an ointment used in the Edo period, which is still performed in Tsukuba city in Ibaraki prefecture. The performer dresses as a samurai and cuts paper into tiny pieces with his sword. He then pretends to injure his arm at the end, and then applies the ointment to great effect, supposedly.)

Were this some artistic performance mimicking a snowstorm, then, while rather trifling, it would still make a glamorous sight, but Sakuya's expression was stiff, to say nothing of how, on every scattered scrap of paper:
『 From the gap in the floor They stare 』
It asserted thus.
【Naomasa】 「Waah, what is this stuff?! Why would anyone bother to so meticulously fill out every single page with a line that could drive a man insane───」

With an audible rustling, the fluttering scraps of paper resembled the paper money placed in a coffin on some island somewhere as ferriage for crossing the river to the underworld, only serving to blow an even colder wind on Sakuya's icy mood, to unnecessarily clutter the cabin, and he was already well aware of that. The young man felt it both foolish and bothersome to pick it all up, so he slumped down on the bed like somebody had cut his strings, but his butt was positioned exactly where the hollow had been worn into the bedding. Thus, sitting like that, head hanging, his gaze naturally went to the floor, the floor, the floorboards, held perfectly steady in the one place there was a gap.

source.japanese:
───船室の沈黙は、心掻き乱す禍々しさを裡に孕んだという。船を揺らす波のうねりは、揺り籠のそれではなく貧血時の眩暈を思わせたという。
　床板と床板の隙間は指一本程度の間隔ではあったけれど、その間隙によって朔屋は、この船室の先の主がいかなる日々を送っていたものか感得されて薄ぼんやりと。
source.english:
—The silence of the cabin seemed to hold a sinister power to disturb the mind. The swell that rocked the ship suggested not a cradle but the dizziness of anemia.
The gap between the boards was only a finger wide. Yet through it Sakuya gained a dim sense of the former occupant's days.

source.japanese: きっとそいつは、来る日も来る日も寝具が磨り減るくらいになるまで、この寝台に座って床の隙間を凝視し続けていたのに違いない。凝視し続けていたから脳の一部が歪んだのか、歪んでいたから一点のみ睨[にら]み続けていたのかは定かではないにしろ、朔屋も同様に見つめて見つめて見つめ続けるのが止められず、まるで崖縁の深淵に魅入られたかのよう、するうちに、青年の頬がにんまりと緩んだ。他人が見ていたなら、今後の付き合い方を考えた方が良いだろうの笑みだった。
source.english:
Surely the person had sat on this berth day after day, staring into the gap until the bedding wore away. Whether the staring had warped some portion of the brain, or a warped brain had caused the unceasing stare, was uncertain. Sakuya, too, kept looking, looking, looking, unable to stop. Like someone mesmerized by an abyss at a cliff's edge.
Then his cheeks loosened into a grin. Had anyone seen it, they would have reconsidered their future dealings with him.

source.japanese:
西洋には、とある男が突如精神の均衡を欠いて家族を斧と猟銃で惨殺し、しまいに自らの頭を撃ち抜いて果てるに至った陰惨な、『バイファップ家事件』というのがあるのだが、これは壁や柱の建て付けが微妙に歪んだ屋敷に住まいし続けた挙げ句、精神が蝕[むしば]まれていったからであるとかなんだとか。朔屋もまた、不気味な扉荒廃した船室奇怪な紙葉に不穏な床の隙間という道具立ての中に放りこまれ、狂気に囚われたとでも───早すぎる？　脆すぎる？　それは隙間に溜まる暗がりを見つめ続けた者以外には決めつけていいことではあるまい。
　そら、隙間の向こうから、幾つものかぎろう瞳が覗き返してはきてないか、ほら、その隙間の幅ぴったりに、髪を振り乱して刃物を擬した『細い女』が嵌[はま]りこんではいないか。
source.english:
There was a grim affair in the West known as the Bifapp Family Incident. A man suddenly lost his mental balance, slaughtered his family with an axe and a hunting gun, then blew out his own brains. Some said his mind had been slowly eaten away by living in a house whose walls and pillars were just slightly out of true.
Sakuya, too, had been thrown among an uncanny door, a derelict cabin, strange sheets of paper, and an ominous gap in the floor. Had madness caught him? Too soon? Too fragile? Nobody who had not gazed into the darkness gathering in that gap had the right to decide.
Look—were there not several shimmering eyes peering back? Look—was a thin woman not wedged into that exact narrow space, hair disheveled, blade poised?

source.japanese: ところで、もちろん朔屋が脳裏に投影されていたのはそんな禍々しい幻覚などではなかったとも。そうだとも。彼はふと思い浮かべたのだ。
source.english: Now, of course, no such dreadful hallucination had been projected into Sakuya's mind. Of course not. He had simply had a thought.
—But—

source.japanese: ───この部屋を使っていたのが。
source.english: —The person who used this room—

source.japanese: ───男だとは、限らないんじゃないの？
source.english: —Wasn't necessarily a man, was it?

source.japanese: 先の住人が男だったとは水夫長も言い切っておらず、あるいはひょっとして、妙齢の女だったかも知れない。そればかりか腺病気質の女にありがちな、薄く青白い肌に、血が透けた赤い唇の、もしかしたら黒髪美しく伸ばした女であったかも知れない。そうでなかったとは誰に言いきれよう。否そればかりか、美女であった可能性すらある。
source.english: The boatswain had never explicitly said the former occupant was a man. Perhaps it had been a young woman. Perhaps one of those frail, sickly women, with thin pale skin and lips reddened by the blood showing through. Perhaps she had beautiful long black hair. Who could say she had not? Indeed, she might even have been a beauty.

source.japanese:
そういう女には、山麓の療養所という舞台立てがいかにも似合おう。白壁の瀟洒な洋館の、二階の窓縁で月光に濡れて髪を梳[くしけず]る、虚ろな眼差しは月影を映すなら神秘的とも言い換えられて、いやむしろ、もっと相応しいのは山間より海辺の、目の細かい砂浜に眠れぬ夜の徒然に彷徨いでた図というのが、きっとその女には似合う。狭霧がかかっていれば猶よい。海は凪いで、波はきっと官能的なまでに緩慢に寄せては返しているだろう。
　白く薄い羅衣の裡で乳房は華奢で、夢遊病者めいた足取りに、ほそい脹ら脛はちらちら、白々と覗くはず。薄暮に迷いこんでいる心はそれ故に、かえって彼女の面差しを儚げに飾り、そんなのが脆そうな貝殻を二枚ばかり拾い上げ、二つを併せてそっと息を吹きこむ───貝を笛に吹くという、流行りではないが雅な手すさびなどをされるともうたまらない。
source.english:
Such a woman would suit a sanatorium at the foot of a mountain. An elegant Western house with white walls; she might sit at a second-floor window, combing her hair in the moonlight. Her vacant eyes, reflecting the moon, could be called mysterious instead.
No, a seaside setting would suit her better than the mountains. On a sleepless night, she would wander out onto a beach of fine sand. A little mist would improve the scene. The sea would be calm, the waves advancing and withdrawing with almost sensual slowness.
Her breasts would be delicate within a thin white nightgown. Slender calves would appear in pale flashes as she walked like a sleepwalker. A mind lost in twilight would lend her face an even more fragile beauty. Let her pick up two brittle-looking shells, join them, and gently breathe into them—playing a shell like a flute, an elegant pastime though scarcely fashionable—and he could bear no more.

source.japanese:
そんな女を。
　押し倒してやりたい砂の上に、手向かいは、少しはあったくらいが情趣を添える、心が虚ろな女の、花を手折る快美はいかばかりのものか。
source.english:
A woman like that.
He wanted to push her down onto the sand. A little resistance would add flavor. How delicious it would be to pluck the flower of a woman whose mind was empty.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひ……ひひ……ひひひひひ。
　そーいう女はもしかしたらけたたましい悲鳴をあげるかなあ。でもそれだと萎えちゃうから、きっと弱々しくもがくだけにさせよう。うんそれが良いそうに決まったひひひひ」
source.english:
“Heh… hehe… hehehehe.
A woman like that might let out an awful shriek. But that would put me off, so I'd make sure she only struggled weakly. Yes, that's better. Definitely. Hehehehe.”

source.japanese: 彼一人の中だけに留めておくにしても不健全かつ身勝手極まりない妄想の、この青年というのはいかなる時でもこういうろくでなしらしい。よくよく匂いに注意を払えば、船室内には埃の臭気の後ろに男の体臭の名残がじったり沁みているのに気がつきそうなものだが、朔屋の精神活動はいかがわしい妄想にのみ傾注されて、周りを気遣う余地などどこにもどこにも、想像内で彼は女の衣をまくり上げ、脚の間に膝を割り入れたところであり、もっと深くに分け入っていこうとしていたまさにその時に。
source.english:
Even kept entirely to himself, the fantasy was unhealthy and supremely selfish. Apparently this young man could be a scoundrel at any time. Had he paid proper attention to the smell, he might have noticed the lingering male body odor soaked into the room beneath the dust. But all his mental efforts were devoted to his sordid imagining. He had no room, none at all, to notice his surroundings.
In his imagination he had lifted the woman's clothes and forced a knee between her legs. He was just about to venture farther—

target.text: ───The silence in the cabin was heavy, laden with a sinisterness that disturbed the mind. The rolling of the waves shaking the boat brought not to mind a crib but instead the dizziness of anemia. The gap between the floorboards was but the width of a finger, but it was precisely that gap that gave Sakuya a vague sense of how the prior resident of this cabin must have spent his days.
There was no doubt that, day in and day out, until the bedding was worn down, he must have sat here on this bed and continued to glare at that gap in the floor; it was all but certain.

Was part of his brain perverted because he continued to stare, or did he continue to stare only at the same point because his brain was already perverted? That much wasn't clear, but similarly, Sakuya found himself unable to cease watching and watching and continuing to watch, like he were standing at the edge of a precipice, enthralled by the abyss below, and as he did this, his cheeks started to slacken. If another person saw this, they would smile to themselves as they reconsidered whether to maintain any future relationship with him or not.

Over in the West, a certain man suddenly became mentally unwell and brutally massacred his entire family with an axe and a hunting rifle before ultimately shooting himself in the head and meeting his own miserable end in what was the tragedy known as 『The House Vaifap Incident』, where as a consequence of living in a mansion where the angles of the fittings between the walls and the pillars were just subtly twisted, his mind grew twisted in turn, or so it is said.

Sakuya, too, had been thrown into a setting of an eerie door, a decaying cabin, grotesque paper, and a disquieting gap in the floorboards, seized by the madness of it all, but───was it not too soon? Was he not a little too frail? It was only for those who continued to gaze into the abyss pooling in that crack to make such judgments. Look, from beyond the gap, are there not several ephemeral eyes gazing back at thee, look, is there not a 『Slender Woman』fitting snugly within that gap, with hair dishevelled and brandishing a jagged knife?
Incidentally, what was projected within Sakuya's mind was, of course, no such ominous illusions, nothing of the sort. Absolutely not. A stray thought had suddenly crossed his mind.
───But.
───Nobody had ever said that whoever had used this cabin.
───Was necessarily a man, right?
The Bosun never explicitly said the prior occupant was a man, and perhaps, could it be, that maybe, it had been a woman in the prime of her youth?

Not just that, but, as is commonly seen in girls with a delicate constitution, of those with a glandular, scrofulous temperament, she would have thin, pale skin, red lips the colour of blood, perhaps even be a girl with long, beautiful black hair; who could say? (TN: The term used here, "腺病気質", is a historical Japanese medical term that means a disposition to have glandular issues, swollen lymph nodes, allergies, and so on, characterized by being pale, thin, and sensitive. It doesn't have any direct English equivalents, aside from a generic description of having a sickly disposition.)
And was that not the case, then somebody should have asserted as much. Nay, not only that, there was even the possibility that she had been a beautiful woman.

A sanatorium at the foot of a mountain would make the perfect setting for a girl like that. In a white-walled Western mansion of refined design, bathed in moonlight by the windowsill on the second floor, combing her hair, and if the moonbeams reflected in her hollow gaze, then the scene could also be expressed as mystical, no, more fitting than the mountains would be the seashore: the scene would be of her aimlessly wandering down a fine-sanded beach on a sleepless night, caught in the throes of her ennui, that would surely suit such a woman. And were it shrouded in a thin mist, then all the better for it.

The ocean would be calm, and the waves would surely be lapping the beach with a languor almost sensual. With slender breasts beneath a thin, white negligee, with the gait of a somnambulist, glimpses of her slender calves, certain to be pale as well. For all that her heart is lost in the gloaming, her features are clothed in an ever more ethereal grace; she would pick up two frail seashells, sending her breath through both at the same time───whistling with seashells, hardly fashionable anymore, but that elegant gesture would be just irresistible.

A woman like that. He wanted to push her down on the sand; would she resist, well, just a little would add to the charm; a woman with an empty heart, what exquisite bliss would it bring him to pluck such a flower?

【Naomasa】 「Hi……hihi……hihihihihi. A woman like that might let out some real ear-piercing screams. But if she did, that would ruin the mood, so I think I'll have her just writhe around weakly instead. Yeah, that's the way, that's definitely it, hihihihi.」
Even though it was kept entirely to himself, with such unwholesome and extremely self-serving delusions, this young man appeared to be a scoundrel even at the best of times.

Had he paid closer attention to the smell, he would likely have noticed that, hidden beneath the smell of the dust, the lingering remnants of male body odour permeated the inside of the cabin, but Sakuya's mental faculties were exclusively devoted to his indecent fantasies, he had no extra room in his head to pay attention to his surroundings, and in his imagination, he was lifting up the woman's clothing, driving his knee into the gap between her legs, and in that very moment, just when he made to push his way in even deeper.

source.japanese: がたがたがた、と。喧しい、船室の扉を塞いでいた箱がずらされる騒音が響いて、
source.english: Clatter, clatter, clatter. The box blocking the cabin door was being shifted noisily aside.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『おーうここだ。
　おい、ちゃあんと助けてやるんだぜ、え？
　さぼったらお仕置きだかんな』
source.english:
“Right,
here we are. You help him properly, hear? Slack off,
and you'll get punished.”

source.japanese: 水夫長の蛮声と、
source.english: The boatswain's roar. And—

source.japanese:
【？？？】
『む……くふ……ぅ、
　くび、もげるぅ……』
source.english:
“Mm… gh…
My neck's coming off…”

target.text: Rattle rattle rattle. The noise of the box blocking the cabin door being moved aside resounded loudly,
【Bosun】 「Yeah, over here. Oi, make sure to actually help, yeah? I catch you slacking off, you're getting punished.」
The Bosun's coarse voice,
【???】 「Mhh……khh……uh, neck, gonna snaaap……」

source.japanese: 聞き覚えのない声だったが、通路から伝わってきたのに朔屋の心より先に体が大仰天、ぎくりと発作のように跳ねて寝台の低い天井に強かに頭を打ちつけ、目の中に星が火花散らす。罰当たりな妄想はあっさり破られて、ちらちらと痛みの星が瞬く中に朔屋が見たのは、戸口に立ちはだかる水夫長と、彼が分厚く巨大な掌の中に引っ掴んだ、なにか、ふわふわとした、白い、そして細い。
source.english:
It was an unfamiliar voice. As it reached him from the passage, Sakuya's body startled before his mind did. He jolted as though in a fit and struck his head hard against the low ceiling above the berth. Stars sparked across his vision. His wicked fantasy broke at once.
Through the flickering stars of pain, he saw the boatswain filling the doorway. In one great, thick palm he held something fluffy, white, and thin.

target.text: As well as a voice he didn't recognize, and although it came from the passageway, Sakuya's body reacted with great shock before his mind caught up; he leapt up like he were having a seizure and hit his head hard against the low ceiling over the bed, stars dancing in his vision like fireworks. His accursed delusion quickly broken, what Sakuya saw between the twinkling stars of pain was the Bosun obstructing the doorway, clutching something in his thick, enormous palm: something fluffy, white, and slender.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おらよ。手伝い連れてきてやったぜ。
　こいつにも言ったが、さぼったら物哀しい目に遭わせる……さっさと片づけな」
source.english:
“Here. Brought you a helper. Told this one too:
slack off, and you'll have something to be sorry about. Get it cleaned up.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Here you go. Brought you your helper. I already told her, but if she slacks off, she'll suffer a most terrible fate…… now get to cleaning.」

source.japanese:
で、ぽういと、室内に投げこまれたのは、先ほどの朔屋と同じような放物線を描いた。もう少し飛んだのは、朔屋より軽かったからだろう。床に落ちた時にもとすんと、響きが軽い。
　ぶわりと。床に放射状に広がったのは髪の波か。緩くうねって、そして白、乳白の、朔屋は始め牛乳でもぶちまけられたような印象を抱いたが、それよりもモップのようだと眺める、床に伸びたそれ。
source.english:
With a light, careless toss, the new arrival traced much the same parabola as Sakuya had a little earlier. She flew farther, presumably because she weighed less; when she struck the floor, the thump was lighter too.
With a soft billow, a wave of hair—could that be what it was?—spread across the floor. Loose-curled and white, milk-white: Sakuya's first impression was of milk dashed over the boards. Then, regarding the thing stretched there, he thought it looked more like a mop.

source.japanese: ただ、なるほどモップの柄のように細いが、毛並みから伸びている人間の四肢だろう。突っ伏したまま呻[うめ]きも垂れているし、その声質からして少女らしい。
source.english: Thin as a mop handle, certainly. But the limbs emerging from that hair were human. The figure was also groaning facedown. From the voice, it seemed to be a girl.

target.text: With that, it was unceremoniously tossed into the room, following a similar trajectory to Sakuya just earlier. It flew a bit further, probably because it was lighter than Sakuya. And when it landed on the ground with a thump, the noise, too, was lighter. With an airy whoosh, what seemed like a wave of hair spread out radially across the floor. It undulated softly, and it was white, milky white, so at first, Sakuya was of the impression that it looked like somebody had dumped milk on the floor, but then it began to look more like a mop to him, what with the way it spread out across the floor.

However, while they certainly were as thin as a mop handle, the limbs stretching out from beneath the coat of hair were probably human. It was even groaning while remaining prostrate, and from the sound of its voice, it appeared to be a young girl.

source.japanese:
【少女】
「うううぅ……顔とお鼻を打ったから、顔とお鼻が、痛いくて、クロは、だから痛い」
source.english: “Uuuu… I hit my face and my nose. My face and my nose hurt, so Kuro… so it hurts.”

source.japanese: ……どうにも言語の統制が取れていない、舌っ足らずの見本のような声に朔屋は、熱病をひどく患った挙げ句お頭が可哀相な事になった近所の子を目の当たりにした心地していささか引き気味になったけれど、それでも白い髪の合間から覗く、手首をとって引きずり起こす。その枯れ木のように細く脆そうなのにも不安になったし、引いた手応えあまりにも軽く、ずるりと後ろに仰け反りそうになったのはもっとたじろぐ。雑な人形細工にありがちで、手荒に扱えば腕が肩からすっぽ抜ける、そんな危惧さえ抱かせしめる体の軽さ加減だったさ。軽さに見合って身の丈もひどく小柄で、六尺にも足らない朔屋の胸のあたりにも少女の頭は来ない。掴んだ手首を引き上げれば、少女の爪先はいとも簡単に床を離れて、青年の顎の辺りに吊り上げられる。
source.english:
…The words would not line up properly. The voice was a model of childish, stumbling speech. Sakuya felt as though he had met a neighborhood child whose mind had been left sadly damaged by a terrible fever, and recoiled a little. Even so, he took the wrist showing between the white strands and pulled her up.
It was as thin and fragile as a dead twig. That worried him. The resistance was so slight that he nearly toppled backward, which worried him more. Her lightness suggested a crudely made doll whose arm might pull straight out of its shoulder if handled roughly.
Her stature matched her weight. Sakuya himself was under six feet, yet her head did not reach his chest. When he raised the wrist in his hand, her toes left the floor with ease, and she hung up near his chin.

source.japanese: 白く細く、生成りの糸のようにだらしなくうねった髪の合間から、覗いた色が白を地にして赤い、その赤は生き血と等しい色で、二つ並んで、朔屋は彼女が放りこまれた弾みに額でも割ったかと、もしゃもしゃと、毛の長い仔犬の顔を掻[か]き分けるようにしてその顔を改める。
source.english: White and thin. Through the slack curls, like unbleached thread, red showed against white: two spots of red, the color of fresh blood. Sakuya wondered whether she had split her forehead when thrown into the room. He parted the shaggy hair to inspect her face, as though clearing the fur from a long-haired puppy's eyes.

source.japanese:
赤かったのは、眸。その真紅。血がそのままに透けた。肌の色は髪よりやや青みを帯びた白。色白、ではなく色素を欠いた。
　少女は、白子であったという。
source.english:
The red was in her eyes. Scarlet, as though the blood showed straight through. Her skin was a slightly bluish white compared with her hair. Not fair skin, but skin without pigment.
The girl was an albino.

target.text: 【Girl】 「Uuuugh……hit face and nose, face and nose hurts, that's why, Kuro hurts.」

……It seemed like she didn't have a good grasp of the language, and upon hearing this voice, this very model of poor enunciation, Sakuya felt a little hesitant, like he'd just seen a girl from the neighbourhood who, after suffering from a terrible fever, had become a little soft in the head, but even so, he took hold of the wrist peeking out from the white hair and pulled her up. It was as slender and brittle as a withered branch, so he became rather nervous. The resistance he felt upon pulling on it was so overly light that he almost fell over backwards, which only left him even more shaken.

Just like what frequently happened with poorly made dolls, he worried that if he handled her too roughly, her arm would detach from her shoulder, so light was her body. As was to be expected of something so terribly light, she was equally small of stature, the girl's head not even reaching Sakuya's chest, who himself couldn't even boast of reaching six feet. When he pulled up on the wrist he was holding, the girl's toes easily left the floor, and she was left dangling by the young man's chin.

From between her twisted strands of hair, thin and white like undyed yarn, he glimpsed a red colour surfacing in the white; it was a red the colour of fresh blood, two pools side by side, and Sakuya worried that the girl might have cracked open her forehead from the impact of being thrown, so he parted the hair covering her face like she were a puppy with a shaggy coat, then took a closer look at her.

The red was her eyes. That bright, crimson red. Like her very blood showed through. The colour of her skin was a somewhat paler white than her hair. Not fair-skinned, but lacking in pigment. The girl was an albino.

source.japanese:
【少女】
「えへへぇ……。クロ。ぷらんぷらんだねえ。
　お兄ちゃん、おっきい人です」
source.english:
“Ehehe… Kuro's dangling.
Mister, you're big.”

source.japanese: 片手掴みに吊り下げられてなお目線は朔屋より低いから、自然上目遣いの、顔に浮いてきたのは多分笑みで、親しさより媚び、阿る為に造った表情にしか見えず、しかもそれが追従としては機能していない。どちらかといえば脚を鎖で繋がれ、小突き回され続けた結果野生の孤高を怯えに塗り潰されてしまったピグミーマーモセットが、見世物として引きずり出された時の振るまいにも似た、痛ましくもあり浅ましくもある、そこはかと哀れで卑屈な風情ばかりが浮き彫りになった、そんな表情だ。
source.english:
Even suspended by one hand, her eyes remained below Sakuya's, so she naturally looked up at him. The expression forming on her face was probably a smile. It looked less friendly than ingratiating, manufactured to please him. Yet it failed even as flattery.
It resembled the behavior of a pygmy marmoset dragged out for exhibition: chained by the leg, knocked about until fear had painted over the proud solitude of a wild creature. Painful and abject, faintly pitiable, thoroughly submissive. That was all the expression revealed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺がでかいんじゃなかろう。君がちっさい。
　それに黒かぁないだろう。白いよ」
source.english:
“I'm not big. You're small.
And you're not black, either. You're white.”

target.text: 【Girl】 「Ehehe……. Kuro. Is dangle-dangling, huh. Mister, you're a big guy.」

Because she was being lifted up with one hand, her gaze was lower than Sakuya's, and so naturally, she was glancing upwards at him, and what showed on her face was probably a smile, but rather than a display of friendliness, he could only see it as a forced expression constructed explicitly to play up to him, to fawn on him, and yet it didn't function as flattery at all.

If he had to express it somehow, it was similar to the behaviour shown by a pygmy marmoset, one whose wild independence had been thoroughly overshadowed by fear after being shoved around and bullied ceaselessly, while it was being dragged out as a sideshow attraction, heartbreaking and wretched in equal measure, and only a vague but unmistakable air of pathetic servility stood out; that was her expression.

【Naomasa】 「It's not that I'm big. You're just small. And there's nothing black about you. You're white.」 (TN: The girl's name, Kuro, is pronounced the same as the colour black in Japanese, written "黒", so Sakuya is a bit confused.)

source.japanese: 少女が浮かべた卑屈な笑みに、彼女がこの船で日頃どんな扱いを受けているのか察せられ、朔屋はついつい身勝手な同病相憐れむの情───彼もまた、この海の吹き溜まりのような船の中で、これから自分がどのような扱いを受けるのか、早々に、恐らくは正しい予想を立てていたからで───を催して、つりこまれるように苦笑した。
source.english: The girl's servile smile told Sakuya what sort of treatment she ordinarily received aboard this ship, and he felt the selfish fellowship of one sufferer for another. After all, he too had already made what was probably an accurate forecast of how he would be treated from now on, here in this catch basin for everything the sea had cast aside. Caught by her smile, he answered with a wry one of his own.

source.japanese: 少女は、衣装もみすぼらしかった。羽織っている、元は船員用達の襯衣らしいのもまるで丈が合わず肩が下がり、唯一娘らしい色合いのキャミソールも日に焼け褪せて、そしていずれも、レギンスも、あちこちほつれ裾[すそ]はぼろぼろ。蔵に放りこんだまま鼠に食い荒らされた古着もかくやで、それが少女の日々の生活の不如意を見やすく語り、朔屋にさえ惻隠の情催させる。
source.english: Her clothes were shabby, too. The shirt hanging about her, apparently made for a sailor, was far too large and drooped at the shoulders. The camisole beneath offered the only girlish color, but even that had faded in the sun. Everything, including her leggings, was frayed here and there, the hems ragged. Old clothes abandoned in a storehouse for rats to gnaw might look like this. They plainly told of her straitened daily life and stirred pity even in Sakuya.

source.japanese: とまれほろ苦く、味付けされていようとも笑みは笑み、万国共通の言語であり、朔屋の微苦笑に白子の少女の身体からふっと力が抜けて、こんなにも軽々としているのに、青年は少女がやはり、初対面の相手に緊張していたのだと気づく。と、少女が体を緩めたのに、それまでは個体をぶら下げていた感触が水入りの革袋に持ち替えたかの頼りなさに変わって、片手では不確かと朔屋は少女のもう片方の手も取った。単に降ろせば済む事だろうに、両手で少女をＹの字の形にぶら下げて、ぷらんぷらんと。
source.english:
However bitter its flavor, a smile was a smile: a universal language. At Sakuya's faintly rueful one, the tension slipped out of the albino girl's body. Light as she was, he realized she had nevertheless been nervous before a stranger.
As she relaxed, the sensation in his hand changed. He had been holding a solid object; now it was as uncertain as a leather bag of water. One hand no longer seemed secure, so he took her other hand as well. He could simply have put her down. Instead, he suspended her in a Y shape by both hands, letting her dangle.

target.text: From the servile expression on the girl's face, it was not hard to guess what sort of treatment she received on this ship on a daily basis, and as misery loves company, he couldn't help but feel a selfish pity for her───for he, too, had already made an early and, dare he say, correct prediction of just what sort of treatment that he himself would be met with on this ship, this cesspool of the outcasts of the seas, hereafter───and feeling it well up from inside, he matched her smile with a forced, wry one of his own.

The girl's clothes were also shabby. The thing she had slipped into seemed like a shirt formerly used by a sailor, but because it was the completely wrong length for her, it hung off her shoulders, and her camisole, the only article she was wearing with a feminine colouration, was discoloured by the sun, and every piece, leggings included, were frayed all over with tatterered hems. Old clothes tossed into a storage room and eaten away at by mice probably looked like this too, and it clearly illustrated the daily hardships this girl suffered, sending a surge of compassion through even Sakuya.

In any case, even if it had a bitter taste to it, a smile was still a smile, a universal language, and upon seeing Sakuya's faint smile, the strength suddenly left her body, this despite her already being so light, and the young man realized that the girl must have felt nervous at meeting somebody for the first time.

However, now that the girl's body had gone slack, what had hitherto felt like holding a solid object now changed to something precarious, like she had been switched out for a leather sack full of water, and feeling uncertain at holding her with one hand, Sakuya took hold of the girl's other hand too. Although it seemed like this all could have been resolved if he had just put her down, he held the girl aloft with both arms spread in the shape of a Y, dangling her around.

source.japanese:
【少女】
「クロはクロだもの。
　あんたは、朔屋……さんで、朔屋さんだよね？」
source.english:
“Kuro is Kuro.
You're Sakuya… Mr. Sakuya, right?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「たしかに俺は朔屋だが。
　ああ、なんだ、クロってのは君の名前か。
　白いのに、クロっていうのはまぎらわしい」
source.english:
“I am Sakuya, yes.
Oh, I see. Kuro's your name.
Calling someone white ‘Black’ is confusing.”

source.japanese: なにか黒い猫やら犬やらを呼びつけるようなその名前も、彼女には似つかわしいかも知れない。それにしてもこのクロの軽々とした事といったら、華奢を通り越して病的ですらある。白子で小さきモノと言ったら、理科実験室などで硝子槽に飼い殺しにされている白鼠を思い起こさせるが、あれらはあれらなりの生命に溢れて軽捷なのに、このクロと来たらどうだろう。白い毛色と紅い眼は同じでも、クロはあからさまに栄養不良のうらなりの生き物で、顔の道具立ても本来なら可憐といっても良いところ、目の下に濃くこずんだ隈が台無しにしてるでないか、あの心の窓という眼差しも、今ひとつ焦点が合わずぶれているではないか。
source.english:
A name like one used to summon a black cat or dog might suit her, in a way. But how extraordinarily light she was. Beyond delicate: positively sickly. Small albino creatures brought to mind the white mice kept confined in glass tanks in school laboratories. Those mice were lively and quick in their own fashion. What of Kuro?
The white coloring and red eyes were the same, but she was plainly a stunted, underfed creature. Her features might naturally have been called pretty, yet the dark pools beneath her eyes spoiled them. And those eyes, the windows of the soul, were not quite focused. They wandered.

source.japanese: そんな風に少女の風体を検分している間、朔屋はなんの気なしにぷらぷらと、両手で吊り下げたクロを軽く揺するようにしていたのだが、次第にその顔が曇っていった。目つきがじろじろあからさますぎたかと、今更なに食わぬ顔を装う朔屋の前で。
source.english: As he inspected her appearance, he absentmindedly swayed her from side to side, holding both her hands. Her face gradually clouded. Had he been staring too openly? Belatedly, he tried to look unconcerned. Before him—

target.text: 【Girl】 「But Kuro is Kuro. And you're, Sakuya……san, Sakuya-san, right?」
【Naomasa】 「I am certainly Sakuya, yes, but. Ah, I see, your name is Kuro, is it? Named Kuro even though you're so white, that's just misleading.」

It was a name that sounded like something one would use to call for a black dog or cat or somesuch, but perhaps even that was was fitting for the girl. Be that as it may, this lightness of Kuro's, it had long since crossed the line of being slender and turned to sickliness.

When you mention something being small and albino, it brings to mind white mice kept alive in glass vats in a science laboratory or somesuch, but for all that those were agile and full of life in their own right, he wasn't quite so sure when it came to Kuro here. They shared the same white hair and red eyes, but Kuro was a pallid creature who was manifestly suffering from malnutrition, and while her facial features could by all rights be described as delicate, even lovely, the dark, gloomy circles around her eyes put it all to waste. Even the look in her eyes, often said to be a window to the soul, was currently blurry, unfocused, wasn't it?

While he examined the girl's appearance in this manner, Sakuya was also nonchalantly shaking Kuro around; he gently dangled Kuro back and forth as he held her up with both his hands, but gradually, her face began to cloud over. Worried that the look in his eyes had been too blatantly scrutinizing, Sakuya tried to feign an air of innocence, and there, right in front of him.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「う、うぅ……ぷ。
　クロ、お船が揺れるのは、平気。でも。
　こんな風に、揺する、されると。
　ぐるぐる、お腹の中……ぅぅ」
source.english:
“Uu… urp.
Kuro's all right when the ship rocks.
But… when you shake Kuro, like this… Round and round,
inside my tummy… Uu…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uh, ugh……buh. Kuro is fine, when the ship shakes. But. Being shaken, like this, is. Round and round, in Kuro's tummy……uuh.」

source.japanese: 赤い目が淀んで、絞めやすそうに細い喉の辺りで妙な音がくぐもって、頬が軽く膨らみ唇こらえるように縛られる、このままだと胸元に盛大にぶちまけられると慌てた朔屋の、なんぼ焦ったとてそれはないだろうの、ひどい、クロをぶら下げていた手を離すがいきなり予告なし。当然少女の体は支えを失いふっと落ちた、腰のない髪がわっと舞い、強かに打ちつけて尻から、とすんと鳴った、音は気抜けするくらい軽かったとはいえ、クロにとっては理不尽な、まぎれもない痛打だったのだろう。尾てい骨から脳天まで衝[つ]き抜ける激痛に、唇から息の塊が吐き出される。
source.english:
Her red eyes dulled. A strange sound gurgled in her thin, easily strangled-looking throat. Her cheeks puffed a little; her lips pressed shut in an effort to hold something back. Sakuya panicked at the thought of a generous spill down his chest.
However alarmed he was, surely there were limits. This was dreadful: without warning, he let go of the hands from which she hung. Naturally, deprived of support, she dropped. Her limp hair flew up. She struck the floor hard on her backside with a thump. The sound was almost disappointingly light, but to Kuro it must have been an unmistakable and wholly unfair blow. Pain shot from her tailbone to the crown of her head, forcing a lump of breath from her lips.

target.text: Her red eyes turned leaden, and a strange, muffled noise came from somewhere around her throat, a thing so slender it seemed like child's play to wring; her cheeks puffed out slightly, her lips pressed together as if holding something in, and Sakuya panicked, realizing that if this went on, that "something" would be splattered all over his chest soon, but no matter how panicked he was, he shouldn't have done that: how cruel a deed, to suddenly let go with the hands holding Kuro up with nary a warning.

Naturally, with the loss of what was supporting her body, the girl abruptly fell, her wispy hair fluttering in the air; a thunk sounded from her butt slamming into the floor, and though the sound was almost disappointingly light, to Kuro, it must have been a blow both unreasonably and undeniably painful. A sharp spike of pain shot from her tailbone all the way to the crown of her head, causing a spurt of air to escape from her lips.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「か、ふぅぅぅっ!?」
source.english: “K-Kahhhh!?”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「お尻、お、しりぃ……。
　割れるた、割れちゃったぁ……ッ」
source.english:
“My bottom, b-bottom…
It split! It's split open…!”

source.japanese:
宙で朔屋に揺すられて、喉を衝[つ]いたのは空えづきだったと見え、中味は逆流しないで済んだが、といって喉から零れるのは身も世もない呻[うめ]き声では替わりにもならない。
　尻を押さえて白髪振り乱し、転がり回るクロを見下ろし、朔屋は気の毒だな、となんとも他人事のように、むしろ胸元を反吐で汚さずに済んだとの安堵の方が強い人でなし、とはいえそんな彼も、ころころのたうち回った挙げ句少女が、今度は船室の壁に頭を強く打ちつけて、びくんと一つ剣呑に跳ねたきり動かなくなったのには流石に取り乱す。泡食って抱き起こせば、くるんと白目を剥いていたのがなんとも言えずみっともなく。
source.english:
Apparently, being swung through the air had only made her dry-heave. Nothing came back up. But the wretched groans issuing from her throat were hardly an improvement.
She clutched her backside and rolled about, white hair flying. Sakuya looked down and thought, Poor thing, as though it had nothing to do with him. The heartless fellow was more relieved that his shirt had escaped a coating of vomit.
Even he became flustered, however, when her rolling brought her head hard against the cabin wall. She gave one alarming jerk and went still. He hurriedly lifted her into his arms. Her eyes had rolled back, an indescribably undignified sight.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kh, fffhhh!?」
【Kuro】 「Butt, butt……. It broke, it split in twooooo……」

It seemed that while being shaken in the air by Sakuya, it was only retching that had reached her lips, so while she never quite regurgitated the contents of her stomach, that made a poor compensation for the groan of unfathomable sorrow that escaped her throat.

As he looked down on Kuro, the girl holding her butt as she shook her hair about wildly while rolling around, Sakuya did feel pity for her, almost like it had nothing to do with him; if anything, the feeling of relief at not having his chest soiled with her vomit was stronger, the brute, but even this man was understandably shaken when the girl, after rolling around while writhing in pain, ended up violently slamming her head into the cabin wall, then jumped dangerously into the air with a jolt and ceased to move. Panicked, when he lifted her up in his arms, the way her eyes rolled back in her head was indescribably painful to watch.

source.japanese: ……回路が切れやすい代わりに復活も早いのか、クロは直に意識を取り戻し、朔屋に宛われた部屋の片づけを始めた。片づけといえば仰々しいが、先の住人はほとんど私物を残しておらず、痕跡らしきものはほぼ埃くらい。後は例の紙束があったが、それを床にぶちまいたのは朔屋自身の痙攣的衝動に由来しており、本来なら彼が率先して拾い上げるのが筋というもの。
source.english: …Perhaps her circuits recovered as readily as they cut out. Kuro soon came to and began tidying the room assigned to Sakuya. Tidying was a grand word for it. The previous occupant had left almost no personal possessions; dust was virtually the only trace. There was also the pile of paper, but Sakuya himself had scattered that in a convulsive impulse. By rights, he should have led the effort to pick it up.

source.japanese: しかし朔屋は、手伝いに寄越された少女に甘えきり、これは楽だと決めこむぐうたら、寝台の奥に引っこんでクロに掃除全部を預ける。彼にしてみれば、こんな狭い部屋で二人ががさごそうごめき合ったらそれこそ邪魔だという言い分があったが、そんなのは言うまでもなく怠け者の理由付け。よくよく始末に余る男だこの朔屋直正、クロはクロでそういう人あしらいに慣れてしまっているのか文句も言わない辺りがいじましい。いじましい、それは確かに、けれど心映えは必ずしも仕事ぶりには結びつかないようで、クロの働きというのは、有り体に延べてしまえば不様であった、みっともなかった、どうにも手際が悪かった。
source.english:
Instead, the lazy man gladly relied on the girl sent to help him. This is easy, he decided, retreating to the back of the berth and leaving all the cleaning to Kuro. His argument was that two people rustling about in such a small room would only get in each other's way. Needless to say, this was a lazy man's excuse. Naomasa Sakuya was truly a difficult man to deal with.
Kuro, for her part, made no complaint. Perhaps she had grown used to being treated this way. That was pitiful. Pitiful, certainly—but her temperament was no guarantee of skill. In plain terms, her efforts were a disgrace. An embarrassment. She was hopelessly inept.

target.text: Perhaps she was quick to recover in exchange for how easy it was to short her circuits, for Kuro regained consciousness immediately, then began cleaning the room that had been addressed to Sakuya. Calling it cleaning was making a mountain out of a molehill: the previous occupant had left barely any personal belongings behind, and the only traces left to speak of were dust. There was also that bundle of paper, but that being dumped all over the floor was a result of Sakuya's own spastic impulses, so by all rights, he should have taken the initiative and picked it up himself.

However, Sakuya took full advantage of the girl sent to help him; he was a lazybones who assumed that would make his life easier, and so he retreated to the back of the bed and left all the cleaning to Kuro. If you asked him, he'd make the excuse that, in a cabin as small as this, if two people were rustling and squirming around, they would only get in the way of each other and be a nuisance, but this was clearly just a rationalization to be lazy.

Here was a man who was extraordinarily hard to deal with, this Sakuya Naomasa, and Kuro must have already been used to this sort of treatment, for the lack of complaining about the situation was almost pitifully earnest of her. Pitifully earnest, certainly so, yet a good, diligent spirit does not necessarily reflect in one's workmanship, or so it would seem, for Kuro's work was, frankly speaking, inelegant, unsightly, and very clumsy.

source.japanese: 船室に積もった埃を払おうと、はたきと箒を持ちだしたまではいい。が埃払いを、床に紙切れ散らばるままで始めたのはいかがなものか。箒をかければ紙が舞う、はたきの使いようも順序がいけない、箒の後ではたこうとするものだから、掃いたところに埃が落ちる、散ったままの紙切れが埃を吸ってはまた散らばる。紙と埃と、船室内は彼女が手を入れる前よりも余計に荒れて、クロはもたついて、片そうとあれこれすればするほどに状況は悪化していく。
source.english:
Producing a duster and broom to clear away the accumulated dust was a good start. Beginning while scraps of paper still littered the floor was less wise. The broom sent paper flying. She used the duster in the wrong order, too: after sweeping, so dust fell onto the places she had just swept. The scattered papers gathered dust and scattered again.
Paper and dust. The cabin was more chaotic than before she began. Kuro floundered. The more she tried to put things right, the worse they became.

target.text: As she made to sweep up the dust that had accumulated in the cabin, she had, at least, taken out a broom. But this sweeping. He questioned her judgment when she began to sweep while the floor was still covered in paper scraps. As she swung the broom around, the paper whirled into the air, and the order she used the feather duster in was also wrong, for she only began to dust after she used the broom, and so the dust fell down where she had just swept; the still-scattered paper absorbed the dust, then scattered even further.

With all the paper and dust everywhere, the cabin interior was now in greater disarray than when she had first begun to help; Kuro made no progress with her fumbling, and the harder she tried to clean it up, the worse the situation became.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「けほ、けへ……っ、
　あれ……？　あれ、どうして。
　この部屋、こんなに。汚れてなかったみたいな。
　こふ……っ、っ、っっ、っ……！」
source.english:
“Cough, cough…
Huh…? Huh, why?
This room wasn't… this dirty, I think.
Cough… kh… kh…!”

source.japanese: 埃は埃を呼んで、年に一度の煤払いの伽藍堂も顔負けに濛々と、朔屋にしてから耐えきれず鼻と口を覆って目を細めたのだから、ただ中で巻かれるクロの気管には大被害に、急性喘息でも発症しそうな、咳が細い、ひっきりなしの、聞いているだけで息苦しい。混乱しきってクロは、しまいには目を回してふらふらと立ち尽くす───朔屋は。
source.english:
Dust called up more dust, billowing thick enough to put a temple's annual cleaning to shame. Even Sakuya could not bear it. He covered his nose and mouth and narrowed his eyes. In the middle of the cloud, Kuro's airways suffered terribly. Her cough was thin, incessant, as though she were about to have an asthma attack; hearing it alone made one short of breath.
Utterly confused, she finally stood swaying, dizzy. Sakuya—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Khh, kehh……, Huh……? Huh, but why? This room, it wasn't. Didn't seem this dirty. Koff……kh, kh, khh, kh……!」

The dust attracted more dust, creating a haze thick enough that it would put even the main hall of a Buddhist temple after its annual dust-sweeping to shame, and even Sakuya could barely endure it; he covered his mouth and nose and narrowed his eyes, so Kuro, standing right in the middle of it all, her windpipe must have suffered tremendously, she seemed like she was on the verge of developing acute asthma, her coughs thin, incessant, and just listening to it was suffocating. Utterly confused, Kuro finally swooned, reeling as she just stood there without moving───and Sakuya, he

source.japanese: <01>見かねて、手伝った。
source.english: Couldn't stand watching any longer, and helped.

target.text: <01>Helped, unable to just watch

source.japanese: <01>口を出すだけにした。
source.english: Confined himself to commenting.

target.text: <01>Just gave his two cents

source.japanese:
【直正】
「君の仕事に手を出すのは出しゃばりだと思うが。
　なあ、まずはその紙切れを全部拾おうぜ」
source.english:
“I don't mean to take over your work,
but… Let's pick up all those bits of paper first.”

source.japanese:
出来れば朔屋も、寝台を直すふりしてさぼりを決めこみたい。水夫長とていちいち監視に来るほど暇でもなかろう。だいたいこんな狭い部屋の掃除くらい一人で充分だ、それにこのクロというのは、信天翁号の雑用か何かだろうし、だったらこれも彼女の仕事、手を出してしまうのも領分違い───
　───に、割りきれず、寝台からのそのそ埃の中に這い出して、紙切れを拾い始めてしまうあたり、怠け者にも徹し切れぬこの青年の中途半端さがある。粉っぽくなってしまった室内の空気、なるたけ吸わないようにと身を屈める朔屋の脇でクロは、硬直していた。怪訝に見上げれば、
source.english:
Sakuya, for his part, would have preferred to pretend to straighten the berth and settle in for a good spell of shirking. Surely even the boatswain had better things to do than keep coming around to check on him. Cleaning a little room this cramped was a one-person job to begin with; besides, this Kuro girl must be some sort of odd-job hand aboard the Albatross, which made it her work, and his pitching in a trespass upon another’s province—
—except he could not quite bring himself to leave it at that. He lumbered out of the berth and into the dust and began gathering up scraps of paper: there, in a nutshell, was this young man’s half-measured nature, incapable even of making a thoroughgoing idler of himself. As he stooped, trying to inhale as little as possible of the air gone powdery with dust, Kuro stood rigid beside him. Puzzled, he looked up at her.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「I know I'm being a bit intrusive, sticking my oar in your work like this, but. Hey, why don't we start by picking up all the paper scraps?」

If at all possible, Sakuya really wanted to slack off while pretending to do the bed. The Bosun probably didn't have the spare time to keep an eye on every little thing. In the first place, one person would be plenty to clean a cabin as cramped as this one, and this Kuro girl, she probably did the chores on the Albatross or something, so with this being part of her job, were he to do anything, he'd actually be overstepping his bounds and───

───But, unable to fully convince himself of that, he slowly crawled out from the bed and into the dust, then began to pick up the paper scraps, the young man revealing a habit of so thoroughly doing things by halves that he couldn't even stick to being lazy. Next to Sakuya, who had hunched over to inhale as little of the dusty air as possible, Kuro was frozen in place. When he looked up at her in confusion,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「すいません、です。あの、ごめんなさい」
source.english: “I'm sorry. Um… sorry.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……？　なにが」
source.english: “…? What for?”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロはぐずで、ぶきっちょな、クロだから。
　朔屋さんに、やらせちゃう……」
source.english:
“Kuro's so slow, and clumsy…
You end up doing it, Mr. Sakuya…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Apologies. Uhm, very sorry.」
【Naomasa】 「……Hm? About what?」
【Kuro】 「Because Kuro is a dullard, a clumsy Kuro. Made Sakuya-san do it……」

source.japanese: ……肩を細く強張らせて、俯き加減なのが、今にも不器用を叱られ頭を殴られるのを待ち構えているよう。戦慄かせる目元に、逃げ出したいのを必死に抑えつける内心がありありと、これには朔屋もまずは暗澹となった。次に尾籠にも頭をもたげてきたのは加虐心だったというなんともはや、この少女をからかい混じりにこづき回したらどうなるのかと心がついつい動きそうになる。
source.english: Shoulders drawn tight, head slightly bowed, she looked as though she were bracing herself to be scolded for her clumsiness and struck on the head at any moment. Her trembling eyes showed how hard she was fighting not to bolt, and at that sight Sakuya's mood first turned gloomy. Then, disgracefully, cruelty began to stir in him. What a creature he was: he found himself wondering what would happen if he teased this girl and knocked her about.

source.japanese: 泣くのか、あのへつらうような笑みで誤魔化すのか、それとももっと別の表情を見せてくれるのか。そんな彼女の、埃まみれの白髪を、払ってやるふりして軽く引っぱったりなどしてやるのもいいかも知れない。荒廃した船室の中に白子の哀れな少女を置くと、それはそれで痛々しいなりの興趣があって、ついつい朔屋の妄想いかがわしくもそそられる。
source.english: Would she cry? Hide it behind that fawning smile? Or show him some other face altogether? Perhaps he might pretend to brush the dust from her white hair and give it a little tug. Put one pitiful albino girl in a ruined cabin and the picture acquired its own wretched fascination—quite enough to set Sakuya's disreputable imagination pleasantly astir.

source.japanese: なんだったら、クロのレギンスの埃を叩き落とす、モノのはずみで引きずり降ろしてやるのもいい。晒されたような白の、痩せた腿[もも]や脚には埃汚れも目立つだろうそれが面白い、履き直すこと許してやらなかったら、クロは逆らえず、下半身丸出しのまま埃と苦戦するのだろう。そこにあるのは性的好奇心などいう生々しい情欲などでなく、悪童が女児のスカートをまくって馬鹿笑いするのと同じ質の幼稚気だが、いずれにしても嘆かわしい。さあ髪を引っぱるかレギンスを降ろすかと、悪戯心のままに朔屋の手は立ち尽くしたクロへと伸びて、彼の目は人としてあるまじきのさもしい光に揺らぎ、揺らいで、ふっとまたもとの小心な朔屋に戻って、手を伸ばしたのは紙切れにと。
source.english: For that matter, he might brush the dust from Kuro's leggings and yank them down in the process. The dirt would show nicely on those thin, exposed legs, white as though bleached; that would be amusing. If he then refused to let her pull them back up, Kuro would be unable to defy him and would have to keep fighting the dust with her lower half bare. This was not sexual curiosity, nothing so raw as lust, but the same childish impulse that makes a brat flip up a girl's skirt and howl with laughter—deplorable all the same. Hair or leggings, then? Carried by the mischief, Sakuya reached toward the motionless Kuro, his eyes wavering with a mean little light unworthy of any human being. Then the light vanished. He was his usual timid self again, and his hand reached instead for a scrap of paper.

target.text: ……Her shoulders tensed subtly, and from the way she looked slightly downwards, it seemed as though she was waiting to be scolded for being clumsy and hit on the head any moment now. Her quivering eyes betrayed her desire to escape from here that she so desperately tried to suppress, and at first, Sakuya's mood grew sombre. Soon enough, however, an indecent desire reared its ugly head: it was a sadistic urge, goodness gracious, where to even begin with him; he couldn't fight the growing desire to figure out just what would happen if he were to treat this girl to some teasing with a dash of bullying.

Would she break into tears, or would she try to smooth things over with that servile smile, or would she instead show him an entirely different expression? Perhaps he should take that girl's white, dust-covered hair, then pull on it lightly while pretending to brush the dust off, that might work. Having a poor little albino girl in this dilapidated cabin, there was a certain wretched charm to that which stabbed at his heart, and Sakuya found his more unsavoury fantasies stirred by the idea in spite of himself.

If she didn't mind, he could offer to beat the dust out of Kuro's leggings, and in the heat of the moment, he could just tug them down, that would also be nice. Her skinny thighs and legs, white as though bleached, they would cut a striking sight even while covered in dust; that sounded amusing, and if he didn't allow her to put them back on, Kuro wouldn't defy him; she'd surely continue her fierce struggle with the dust while her lower body was bared to the world.

It was not the kind of raw lust that one could call sexual curiosity, but instead a childishness similar to that of a naughty boy flipping a little girl's skirt and laughing hysterically, but regardless, it was still deplorable. Now then, time to pull her hair and flip her skirt: when Sakuya reached out for the still-frozen Kuro with his hands, driven by a heart full of mischief, eyes wavering with a base shine unbecoming of a human being, shifting and swaying, he abruptly reverted to his usual timid self, hands instead reaching for the scraps of paper.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……いいから。二人でやるのが早いから。
　俺はこっちのほう拾うから、君ゃあっちな」
source.english:
“…Never mind. It'll be quicker with two of us.
I'll pick up this side. You do over there.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……It's fine. It'll be faster if we do it together. I'll pick it up from this side, you start from that side.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あい」
source.english: “'Kay.”

source.japanese: こっくり頷[うなず]いた、クロの顔には感謝の感激朔屋の気恥ずかしいほどにありありと、どうやら少女は青年の寸前の目の色を見ずに済んだらしい。あるいは見ていてなお気づかないくらいに鈍感だったのかもしれないが、ともかく二人は動き出して、片づけはようやくまともに進む。朔屋がもっと早くに、クロが働きだした辺りで声をかけていたなら、七割方は終わっていたであろう頃合いで。
source.english:
She nodded. Her gratitude shone so plainly on her face that he felt embarrassed. Apparently she had missed the look in his eyes a moment earlier. Or perhaps she had seen it and was too dull to recognize it. In any case, they began moving, and the cleaning finally made proper progress.
Had he spoken up sooner, when Kuro first started work, they would probably have been seventy percent finished by now.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Aye.」

She nodded in agreement, and a gratitude so deeply heartfelt it left Sakuya embarrassed visibly radiated from her face; it seemed like the girl was spared the fate of noticing just how close to the edge the look in the young man's eyes had been. Or perhaps she was simply so dull that she wouldn't notice even had she seen it, but regardless, the two of them set to work, and the cleaning finally saw some proper progress; had Sakuya only called out to Kuro when she first started working, they would probably be about seventy percent done by now.

source.japanese: ……と、言えば後はいかにもてきぱきと進んだように聞こえる。実体はさに非ずして、クロは何枚か紙を拾い上げたところで手から取り零し、またやり直しする事になり、それを二回ばかり繰り返した。ようやくしっかり握る事を覚えた辺りで、後方不注意で朔屋の脚にけつまずき、埃の床に頭からのめって思いきり綿ごみ吸いこみ、激しくむせかえっては掃除を中断させた。しまいには朔屋も苛立ち始め、今度不始末をしでかしたら部屋から叩き出そうと決意した早々に、小さな悲鳴がクロから。
source.english: …Put that way, it sounds as though matters proceeded with exemplary dispatch thereafter. The reality was otherwise. Kuro would pick up several sheets only to drop them from her hand and have to begin again, and this she repeated twice. Just as she finally learned to keep a firm grip on them, she neglected what lay behind her, tripped over Sakuya’s leg, pitched headfirst into the dusty floor, inhaled a great wad of lint, and brought the cleaning to a halt with a violent fit of coughing. By the end even Sakuya’s patience had begun to fray. He had only just resolved to throw her out of the room if she bungled one more thing when a little shriek came from Kuro.

target.text: ……But, putting it that way made it sound like everything proceeded smoothly from there. The reality was quite different, for whenever Kuro picked up several scraps at once, they'd spill out from her hands, forcing her to start over again, and she repeated this whole process a couple times or so. Once she'd finally figured out how to grab the paper properly, inattention to what was behind her made her trip over Sakuya's leg; she fell on the dusty floor head first and inhaled a lump of sluts' wool with reckless abandon, and the resulting violent coughing put the cleaning on hold.
Eventually, Sakuya began to grow irritated, and just as he resolved to toss her out of the cabin the next time she caused any more trouble, a small shriek came from Kuro.

source.japanese:
憤然と向き直れば、ぎゅっと、片手の人差し指をきつく握りしめておろおろと、指先から彼女の目の色と同じ赤い雫が膨らんで、張り詰めてから滴ってたらり、とうとうたらり、床の埃に落ちていく。
　紙切れの端で指先を切ったと思しく、クロにしてみれば血止めのつもりで指の根元を押さえているのだろうが、それでは絞り出しているだけ。薔薇を摘[つ]む令嬢が棘に傷して、薔薇園の地に少女の生命の雫を吸わせている情景なら、唯美主義者が喜んで画にも描く詩文にも語ろう。しかし痩せっぽちのクロが、適当に掃き寄せられた埃の上に赤いのを零してじくじく空しく吸わせていくとあっては痛さ間抜けさの方が先に立ち、朔屋は気勢を削がれて、ポケットから鼻紙を引っぱり出した。くしゃくしゃによれてはいたが幸い未使用で、クロの指先に宛う。
source.english:
He wheeled around indignantly. Kuro stood there in a panic, clutching one forefinger. At its tip a bead of red—the color of her eyes—swelled, drew taut, and fell; then another dropped into the dust.
She had apparently cut herself on the edge of a scrap of paper. She must have thought gripping the base of the finger would stop the bleeding, but she was only squeezing more out. A young lady pricked by a thorn as she plucked a rose, letting drops of her life soak into the rose garden: an aesthete might delight in painting such a scene or celebrating it in verse. But scrawny Kuro bleeding into a carelessly swept heap of dust looked painful and foolish before it looked beautiful. Sakuya's indignation deserted him. He pulled a tissue from his pocket. It was crumpled but, fortunately, unused, and he pressed it to her fingertip.

target.text: When he turned back to face her in indignation, she was tightly clenching one of her index fingers, looking flustered; a red drop the same colour as her eyes swelled from the tip of her finger until, pulled taut with tension, it finally snapped off, the heavy bead dripping down and landing on the dust-laden floor. Apparently, she had cut her fingertip on the paper scraps, and in Kuro's mind, she was probably trying to put pressure on the root of her finger to stop the bleeding, but all it accomplished was squeezing more out.

Had this been the scene of a young maiden who had plucked a rose only to be stung by its thorns, of the tears of a maiden's life-force absorbed by the soil in a rose garden, then an Aesthete would gladly have painted it or spoken of it in poetry. But scrawny Kuro, red drops absorbed in vain by a pile of dust haphazardly swept together, only brought pain and stupidity to the fore of his mind, and with his fervor now dampened, Sakuya pulled out a tissue paper from his pocket. Wrinkled and crinkled, but fortunately unused, he applied it to Kuro's fingertip.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なにやってんだかなぁ……。ほら、そうやって血が止まるまで押さえてな。紙の切り傷は、刃物より痛いが我慢しろよ？」
source.english: “What are you doing…? Here. Hold it like that until the blood stops. A paper cut hurts more than a knife cut, but you'll have to bear it.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「What do you think you're doing……. Look, keep pressing it down like that until the bleeding stops. Paper cuts hurt worse than knives, so you'll have to bear with it, got it?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あ、あい……。
　あの、ちり紙、
　あとで洗って返す……します」
source.english:
“O-Okay… Um, the tissue…
I'll wash it and give it…
give it back later.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「んなモン洗ったら溶けちまうわ。
　いいから、ちょっと座ってなよ。
　後は俺がやるから」
source.english:
“Wash it and it'll fall apart.
Just sit down a bit.
I'll do the rest.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「A-, aye……. Uhm, the tissue paper, Kuro will wash it and bring it back……later.」
【Naomasa】 「Wash something like that and it's just gonna dissolve. It's fine, just sit down for a bit. I'll finish the rest myself.」

source.japanese:
クロには手出しさせない方がまだましだとやっと気づくあたり、朔屋も相当に無能で、実際室内はクロが入る前より散らかっていた。が、黙々と進めてみれば、元は大して私物もなかった船室である。片づけも埃払いも本気で手を着けてみればあっけなく、それでもやはり、終わった頃には青年の額や首筋には汗。
　拭い拭いしながら背を伸ばし凝りをほぐしていると、寝台ではクロがえへえへと手を打っていた。
source.english:
Only now did he realize that keeping Kuro out of the work was better. That said little for his own competence. The room was, in fact, messier than before she entered.
Still, it had contained few possessions to begin with. Once he quietly set to work in earnest, the tidying and dusting were soon done. By the end, nonetheless, sweat stood on his forehead and neck.
He wiped it away, straightened his back, and stretched the stiffness out. On the berth, Kuro was giggling and clapping.

target.text: The fact it took Sakuya this long to finally realize that he was better off not letting Kuro lift a finger spoke plenty of his own incompetence, and the cabin had, in fact, only become more cluttered than when Kuro had first entered it. But, as he soldiered on in silence, it became clear that the cabin had never contained many personal belongings. Once he genuinely set his hand to cleaning and dusting, it was almost over too soon, but even so, by the time the young man was done, his brow and neck were slick with sweat. As he wiped off the sweat while stretching his back to relieve the stiffness, over on the bed, Kuro was clapping her hands for him with a giggle.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「凄い、凄い、朔屋さん。
　これだったら、クロがしなかった方が、
　早いかったみたい。
　最初から朔屋さん、してれば、よかったね」
source.english:
“Amazing! Amazing, Mr. Sakuya!
It looks like…
it would've been quicker if Kuro hadn't helped.
You should've done it right from the start.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Amazing, amazing, Sakuya-san. Seems like, would have been faster if Kuro didn't do anything. Should have had Sakuya-san do it from the start, huh?」

source.japanese: 真実そうかも知れないといえ、それを本人が言ってしまってはおしまいだろうと、朔屋の片頬が引きつる。無言で寝台の端に腰かけるクロの前に立ち、
source.english: It might be true, but surely she should not be the one to say it. His cheek twitched. Without a word, he stood before Kuro, seated on the edge of the berth.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「…………Now listen here, you.」

Even if that might actually have been the truth, admitting that about yourself is like driving the final nail in your own coffin, or so Sakuya thought, and one of his cheeks twitched. He stood wordlessly in front of Kuro, who was sitting on the edge of the bed,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「な、なにぃ……？
　なんか、怒って……る、ね？」
source.english:
“Wh-What…?
You're sort of… angry, aren't you?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Wh-, whaat……? You're mad about something…… right?」

source.english: “—Eeeeek!—”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「───Hiyaah───！」

source.japanese: 朔屋は遂に拳を固め、いややっぱり殴ってしまうのは一線を越えてしまう気がして踏み切れず、代わりに朔屋はクロをベッドに押し倒し、その脚をぐいと抱えこみ───蹠をくすぐり責めにしたという。
source.english: At last Sakuya clenched his fist. No—actually hitting her still seemed a line he could not cross. Instead, he pushed her back onto the bed, caught her legs, and subjected the soles of her feet to a merciless tickling.

target.text: At last, Sakuya clenched his fist, but no, he felt that punching her would be crossing a line, and so he couldn't quite bring himself to take that plunge; instead, he pushed Kuro down on the bed, firmly gathering her legs in his arms───then subjected the soles of her feet to an assault of torturously relentless tickling.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あ、は、あははははははっ、
　あは、かはっ、苦し……いひひひひひっ、
　止め……えへへへへっ、かはっ、もっ、
　か、かんにん……ひひひ、ひぃ～～っっ」
source.english:
“Ah, ha, ahahahahaha!
Aha, kah, can't brea—heeheeheehee!
Sto—ehehehehe!
Kh, no mo—m-mercy… heehee, heeeeee!”

source.japanese: クロは呼吸困難寸前になるまで笑い狂って、責めが止んだ頃には息も絶え絶え、青年を見つめる真っ赤な目には、怨みがましいような、殴りはしなかった事を不思議と思っているようなどっちつかずの色が浮いたのだった。
source.english: Kuro laughed until she was almost unable to breathe. When the torment stopped, she lay gasping. The look in the scarlet eyes turned on him was ambiguous: something like resentment, something like wonder that he had not hit her.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Ah-, ha-, ahahahahahaha, aha, kah, it hurts……ihihihihihi, stop……ehehehehe, kah, please, for-, forgive……hihihi, hii～～」

Kuro laughed like a madwoman until she could barely draw air; when the assault finally ceased, her breathing was faint, and in those eyes of crimson fixed upon the young man, an ambiguous light surfaced: a mixture of something almost reproachful and what seemed like bewilderment that she hadn't been struck.

source.japanese:
自分の為に宛われた部屋にしろ、掃除というのはやっぱり面倒。それを好み、進んで没頭する人種は少なく、朔屋などは言わずもがな。朔屋としては寝台を直すふりしてさぼりを決めこみたい。水夫長とていちいち監視に来るほど暇でもなかろう。だいたいこんな狭い部屋の掃除くらい一人で充分だ、それにこのクロというのは、信天翁号の雑用か何かだろうし、だったらこれも彼女の仕事、手を出してしまうのも領分違い───
　この不器用な少女に任せきりにするのもそこはかと気が退ける、良心の呵責というやつは、けれど朔屋を動かすまでは至らなかった。
source.english:
Even when the room was his own, cleaning was a nuisance. Few people enjoyed it; fewer still threw themselves into it willingly. Sakuya, needless to say, belonged to neither group. He would rather pretend to straighten the berth and settle in for a good spell of shirking. Surely even the boatswain had better things to do than keep checking on him. Besides, one person was enough to clean a room this small, and Kuro was presumably the Albatross's errand girl or something of the sort. This was her work. Helping would only mean meddling in someone else's duties—
Leaving everything to so clumsy a girl troubled him faintly: the pangs of conscience, as they were called. They did not, however, trouble him enough to move.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「君の仕事に口を出すのは出しゃばりだと思うが。
　なあ、まずはその紙切れを全部拾おうぜ」
source.english:
“I don't mean to tell you how to do your work,
but… Let's pick up all those bits of paper first.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうして、埃掃除ってのは上から下に、だ。
　まずはたきを使ってから、床に落ちた分を掃くんだよ」
source.english:
“And when you're dusting, work from top to bottom.
Use the duster first, then sweep up what falls on the floor.”

source.japanese: いかにも尤[もっと]もらしい諭しぶりながら軽薄そのもので、相手がまともなら手痛い反撃をくらうのが必至、なのにクロはこういう口だけ出して手を出さない、一番駄目な手合いにぽかんと、下顎を落としたのは呆れて、ではなかった。感嘆していた。
source.english:
His advice sounded perfectly reasonable and was perfectly shallow. Anyone with sense would have given him a sharp answer. Yet Kuro stared with her mouth hanging open at this worst of all types, the man who offers advice and never a hand.
Not in disbelief. In admiration.

target.text: Even if this room had been addressed to him specifically, cleaning was bothersome all the same. It was a rare sort of person who would enjoy and willingly devote themselves to a task like that, and it needn't be said how Sakuya felt on the matter. If at all possible, Sakuya really wanted to slack off while pretending to do the bed.

The Bosun probably didn't have the spare time to keep an eye on every little thing. In the first place, one person would be plenty to clean a cabin as cramped as this one, and this Kuro girl, she probably did the chores on the Albatross or something, so with this being part of her job, were he to do anything, he'd actually be overstepping his bounds and─── He did feel a bit ashamed leaving everything in the hands of this clumsy girl, he did feel the pangs of his conscience, but that still wasn't quite enough to make Sakuya act.
【Naomasa】 「I know I'm being a bit intrusive, sticking my oar in your work like this, but. Hey, why don't you start by picking up all the paper scraps?」
【Naomasa】 「Once that's done, you clean the dust from top to bottom, got it? First you use the duster, then sweep up what fell to the floor.」

Though his words of advice sounded perfectly reasonable on the surface, they were also insincerity itself; were he dealing with a regular person, being met with a severe counterblow was a foregone conclusion, but while Kuro's jaw did drop in response to this most worthless of men, the sort that only ever gave his two cents without lifting a finger himself, it was not in astonishment at his nerve. It was from pure admiration.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ああ、そっかー……。
　そうだよ。ほんとだ。
　そうすれば、ちゃんとお掃除できるね」
source.english:
“Oh, that's it… Yes.
That's right.
That way I can clean properly.”

source.japanese: ……これは、この船でクロに今まで掃除の仕方一つ教える者がいなかったのか、それとも彼女が聞いた端から忘れていただけかと、朔屋の呆れ果てたざまこそ身勝手そのもの。それでもクロは朔屋を咎めるどころか感謝して、言われた通りの手順に戻る、やっぱり一人で、生真面目に、懸命に、そしてどこまでも不器用に。
source.english:
…Had nobody aboard ever taught Kuro even how to clean? Or did she forget the moment she was told? Sakuya's exasperation was the very picture of selfishness.
But instead of reproaching him, she thanked him and returned to work in the order he had described. Alone, of course. Earnestly, desperately, and clumsily to the end.

source.japanese: 結局クロが掃除を終えた時、費やした時間というのは、朔屋が手伝ってやっていた場合の、あるいは彼一人で取りかかっていた場合の、恐らくは三倍にも及んでいたという。
source.english: By the time she finished, the task had probably taken three times as long as it would have if Sakuya had helped—or done it by himself.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「君な、いつもそんな調子なのか？
　そんなじゃあ、あのおっかねえ水夫長に毎回ドヤされてんじゃないの？」
source.english:
“Are you always like
this? That scary boatswain must yell at you every time.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Aah, that so……. It is so. It really is. If Kuro does that, Kuro can clean properly, huh.」

……Well now. Was it the case that, heretofore, no one aboard this ship had ever taught Kuro how to clean, or was it simply that it had gone in one ear and out the other? Sakuya's appalled state was the very essence of egotism. And yet, Kuro did not admonish Sakuya in the slightest; she instead thanked him, then went back to doing things in the order she had been instructed to, still all by herself, dead serious, with utmost effort, and clumsy in every respect.
In the end, when Kuro finished cleaning, the amount of time it had taken was most likely around three times longer than if Sakuya had helped her, or even if he had just done it all by himself.
【Naomasa】 「Hey, are you always like this? If you are, doesn't that mean that scary bosun flips his lid at you every time you do anything?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うん。いつも拳骨、もらうの。
　ふくれて、たんこぶ痛いよ。
　こんどできたら、触らしたげる」
source.english:
“Yes. I always get punched.
The lump swells up, and it hurts.
Next time I get one, I'll let you touch it.”

source.japanese: 人任せにしておいてしれっと訊ねた朔屋こそ殴られるべきであろうし、えへらえへらと受け答えするクロはクロにしても、やはりお頭の螺子が何本かまとめて抜け落ちているのだろう。ある意味似合いの組み合わせなのだった。
source.english:
Sakuya, who had left all the work to her and now asked so blithely, was surely the one who deserved a punch. As for Kuro, answering with that foolish grin, several screws must have fallen out of her head at once.
In a way, they were well matched.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Yep. Kuro always gets knock on the head. Swells up, the bumps hurt. Next time Kuro gets one, will let you touch it.」

To so nonchalantly ask that question after leaving all the work to someone else, Sakuya was definitely the one who deserved to be punched here, but for as strange as Kuro seemed, responding to that with such an asinine grin meant she must have had more than a few screws loose herself. In a sense, they were birds of a feather.

source.japanese:
こうしてたっぷり余分な時間をかけて船室内の片づけをし終え、やれやれと一息ついて朔屋は、そこでもう一つ思い出す。この部屋の扉だ。前の住人がどんな意図で遺したかは知らず、ともかく自分はあんな奇怪な扉絵などごめんこうむると朔屋は、通路で体の埃を払い落として立ち去ろうとしていたクロを呼びとめた。で、二人はもう一仕事、朔屋としては先の住人の事を聞きたくもあったが、知ったところでろくな事はないと思い直して口を噤み、黙々と薔薇と首吊りの生き物たちを擦り落としていく。
　奇怪で心乱す絵がようやくほとんど消えた頃合いで、通路の向こうからどすどす喧しい、分厚い靴音が伝わり、
source.english:
Thus, after spending far more time than necessary putting the cabin in order, Sakuya paused with a weary sigh—and remembered one more thing: the door. Whatever the previous occupant had intended by it, Sakuya wanted no part of that grotesque painting. He called Kuro back as she stood dusting herself off in the passage, about to leave.
So they set to one more job. Sakuya would have liked to ask about the former occupant while they were at it, but reconsidered—nothing good could come of knowing—and held his tongue. In silence, they scrubbed away the roses and the creatures dangling by their necks.
Just as the strange, disquieting picture had at last all but vanished, the noisy thud-thud of heavy boots came pounding from farther down the passage—

target.text: Thus, having spent far more time than necessary, the cleaning of the cabin came to a close, and as Sakuya heaved an exasperated sigh, one more thing surfaced in his mind. The door to this room. He hadn't the first idea with what designs the prior occupant had left that behind in this world, but at the very least, Sakuya himself wanted nothing to do with it, and so he went to call out for Kuro to stay, the girl busy brushing the dust off her body in the passageway as she made to leave.

Now, the two had already done a bit of work, and while Sakuya did want to ask about the prior occupant, he reconsidered after coming to the realization that nothing good would come of that knowledge, so he held his tongue, instead beginning to scrape the rose and the creatures hanged by the neck off the door in silence. By the time that grotesque, disturbing drawing was almost entirely faded, plodding footfalls could be heard making their way noisily down the passageway,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なんだ、まだもそもそやってたんか。
　……ま、クロが混じってりゃそんなもンか」
source.english:
“What, still pottering about? …Well,
with Kuro involved, I suppose that's about right.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんた、判っててこの子を寄越したんですかい」
source.english: “You knew that when you sent her to me?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What, you still fumbling around here? ……Well, with Kuro involved, guess that's to be expected.」
【Naosama】 「You knew that, and you still sent her my way?」

source.japanese: 憮然となった朔屋を一睨[にら]みで黙らせ、水夫長は白子のクロへ、
source.english: One glare silenced Sakuya's disgruntled reply. The boatswain turned to the albino girl.

target.text: Silencing the indignant Sakuya with a single glare, the Bosun turned to Kuro the albino,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おうクロ、いつものやつだ、しりとりだ。
　……『鉄砲』！」
source.english:
“Right, Kuro. Our usual word-chain game.
…‘Rifle’!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（なんでいきなりしりとりなんだよ……）
source.english: (Why a word game, all of a sudden…?)

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hey Kuro, time for some shiritori, the usual. ……『|Cannon(Teppou)』!」 (TN: Shiritori is a Japanese word-chain game in which the player must give a word starting with the last syllable of the word given by the previous player. The main rules are no repeats, only nouns, and no words ending in n (in Japanese).)
【Naosama】 （What's with the sudden shiritori……)

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「『てっぽう』？　『う』。だね。
　うー……。
　ぅー…………」
source.english:
“Rifle? E, right.
Eee…
Eee…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「『Cannon(Teppou)』? 『U』. Right. Uー……. Uー…………」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あ！
『うどん』！」
source.english:
“Oh!
‘Eleven’!”

source.japanese:
十秒はたっぷり考えこんだ結果がこれで、一回でけちがついてしまって後が続かない。
　クロの肌や髪と同じ色の空気は、しかし朔屋の頭の上にだけ漂っているようだった。「う」の付く言葉など他に幾らでもあろうに、この娘はやはり、頭の中に詰まっているのはおが屑とかその類の、と朔屋は無礼にも気の毒な顔を隠しきれない。ただ水夫長の方は平然と、むしろそれで良しと頷[うなず]いて、
source.english:
She had spent a full ten seconds thinking, and this was the result. A word ending in n meant losing: the game was over after a single reply.
The air had gone as white as Kuro's skin and hair—but apparently only above Sakuya's head. There were plenty of other words beginning with e. Was the girl's skull really filled with sawdust or something similar? Rudely, he could not hide his pitying expression.
The boatswain remained composed. Indeed, he nodded as though satisfied.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Ah! Udon!」

After brooding over it for a whole ten seconds, this was all she had to show: having gotten off on the wrong foot, she found herself stuck. It felt as though an air the same hue as Kuro's skin and hair hung above Sakuya's head alone. There were still countless other words that started with "u"; sure enough, the inside of this girl's head really was packed full of sawdust or something like it, so Sakuya rudely thought, unable to keep the pity from surfacing on his face. Only the Bosun remained composed, and in fact, he nodded as though it was just what he had been hoping to hear,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう、いつも通りだな。
　じゃあ次の仕事だ」
source.english:
“Good. Same as always.
Now, next job.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「よおしこんどは、機関室に行って蒸気一杯バケツに汲[く]んでもらってこいっ」
source.english: “Right! Go down to the engine room and ask them to fill a bucket with steam for you.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そしたら倉庫に行って、当直の洋燈に使う、緑色の油を取ってくるんだ」
source.english: “Then go to the store and fetch some green oil for the watch lamps.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right, same as usual. On to your next task then.」
【Bosun】 「Alright, this time, you go to the engine room and get yourself a bucketful of steam.」
【Bosun】 「Once you're done with that, head to the lamp room and grab the green oil, the stuff we use in the watch lanterns.」

source.japanese: こんな差し向かいで、しかも雑音も少ない通路でも水夫長殿は胴間声、地声がでかいのかこの種の職掌にある人間の特徴なのか、すぐ脇でがなりたてられた朔屋は一瞬耳を覆いそうになって、そして噴き出した。どるん、と信天翁号も一つ身震いしたのが、朔屋の噴き出したのに併せたよう。
source.english:
Even face-to-face in a relatively quiet passage, the boatswain boomed. Was his natural voice so loud, or was it a trait of his profession? With the man roaring beside him, Sakuya nearly covered his ears. Then he burst out laughing.
The Albatross gave a shuddering rumble, as though joining him.

source.japanese: 新米のこの無礼な態度に水夫長は熊でも怯ませそうな顔で睨[にら]みつけて拳を振り上げ、そして頬を緩めてにやり。その顔でも充分に恐ろしいけれども、朔屋の失笑の意味は、しっかり水夫長にも了解されているらしく。
source.english: At the new boy's disrespect, the boatswain glared with a face that could have cowed a bear and raised his fist. Then his cheek loosened into a grin. That face was frightening enough, too, but he clearly understood the reason for Sakuya's laughter.

source.japanese:
なにほどもない、なんのことはない。
　今時の、現実の船乗りならまず口にもしない、紙も黄ばんで活字も掠れた海洋小説中くらいでしかお目にかかれないような、『船乗り達の冗談』という奴だったから。
source.english:
Nothing much. Nothing at all.
These were sailors' jokes. The kind no real sailor nowadays would think to tell, found only in sea novels with yellowed paper and faded print.

source.japanese:
機関室に駆けこんだところで、蒸気などバケツに汲[く]める訳もない。
　当直には警戒信号として緑色の灯りが用いられるが、それは緑の燃料を使うから光も緑に染まるのではなく、風防の硝子が緑だからだ。
source.english:
She could run down to the engine room, but nobody could fill a bucket with steam.
Green lights were used as warning signals on watch. They did not shine green because the fuel was green. The glass around the flame was green.

target.text: Even while facing each other like this, not to mention how it was in a passageway with barely any other noise, the great Bosun's voice was still coarse and thick; perhaps he was just loud by nature, or maybe it was a characteristic shared by all those in his line of employment, and Sakuya, being yelled at from right by his side, almost covered his ears for a moment, then burst into laughter. With a heavy sound, the entire Albatross also shuddered but once, as if trying to match Sakuya's outburst.

In the face of this lubber's insolence, the Bosun fixed him with a scowl that could send even a bear running for the hills and raised his fist high, only to then relax his cheeks and grin. Even that expression was still terrifying enough, but it appeared that the Bosun understood perfectly well the meaning behind Sakuya's inability to hold back his laughter.

It was nothing, really, it was nothing at all. The sort of thing that any actual sailor would well-nigh never make these days, the sort of thing you would only lay your eyes on in nautical fiction written on foxed pages with faded lettering: what you would call a 『Sailor's jest』

Rush into the engine room all you like, you couldn't possibly hope to scoop up steam with a bucket. And while a green light is used as a warning signal by those standing watch, the light isn't green because it uses a green fuel, it's because the glass chimney is green.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ア、アイ、ぼーすん。行ってきま───！」
source.english: “A-Aye, Bosun. I'm goi—!”

source.japanese: いずれも、船に乗りこんだばかりの子供をからかう戯れ言で、今どき通用しそうにない、のに、クロが恐ろしい水夫長の御言いつけと走り出すさま、あわあわとなんとも見苦しくけつまずいたりよろめいたり、それでも彼女なりの全力疾走なのだと微妙な気分になる朔屋の横で、
source.english: Both were teasing errands for a child newly aboard. They ought not to have worked in this day and age. Yet Kuro set off at the terrifying boatswain's command, flustered, stumbling and staggering in a thoroughly sorry fashion. Realizing that this was nevertheless her very best sprint gave Sakuya a peculiar feeling. Beside him—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「A-, aye, Bosun. Kuro's off───!」

All of it the sort of jest used to tease a child who had only just boarded a ship for the first time, the sort that would never work these days, and yet Kuro ran off to follow the honourable orders of the Bosun, leaving in a fluster, tripping and staggering in an unsightly manner, and next to Sakuya, who was left in an uneasy mood upon realizing that this must still have been her way of running with all she had,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……冗談だよこのうすのろ。今時どんなデッキボーイだって真に受けやしねえのに、あんたと来たら。
　そっちじゃねぇ。厨房に行って来いよ。
　芋の皮むきが足んねぇんだ。
　そら急げ───船長！」
source.english:
“It's a joke, you halfwit. No deck boy these days would fall for it, but you… Not that way!
Go to the galley.
They're short of hands to peel the potatoes.
Hurry up—Captain!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……That was a joke, you simpleton. Not even the dullest deck boy would take that at face value these days, and yet here you are. Not that way. Head to the galley. There's not enough potato peelers. Hurry it up───Captain!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「はひっ」
source.english: “Y-Yep!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「YESH!」

source.japanese: 朔屋にしてもあれくらい見苦しい廻れ右はない、というくらい危うげな踵[かかと]のターンで方向を変え、走り去っていくクロに、朔屋はまた噴き出そうとして、その息が変な具合に鼻へと抜けて聞き苦しい、青年は今度こそ聞き捨てならないジョークを耳にしたと思ったので。
source.english:
Even Sakuya had never performed so ungainly an about-turn. Kuro pivoted precariously on her heels and ran away. He was about to laugh again, but his breath escaped oddly through his nose, making an unpleasant sound.
This time, he thought he had heard a joke that could not be allowed to pass.
