target.text: Even Sakuya had never made a right about-face that disgraceful, so perilous was the heel turn she changed direction with, and Sakuya was on the verge of erupting into laughter once more at the sight of Kuro dashing off, his breath escaping through his nose with an unseemly snort; it seemed like he'd finally heard a joke he couldn't possibly let slide.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あんた今、誰に、なんて言いました？」
source.english: “…What did you just say? And who did you say it to?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……What did you just say, and to who?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「船長に、芋の皮むき手伝ってこいと。
　そうだな、お前も行くか？
　船長がやると、芋に点々と血が付いてよう。
　あいつほら、不器用だから」
source.english:
“Told the captain to help peel potatoes.
Come to think of it, you could go too.
When she does it, the potatoes get blood spots all over.
Clumsy, you know.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、そうだろうな、判る気が───って。
　そうではなく！
　船長って、誰が！」
source.english:
“Oh, yes, I can imagine—Wait.
That's not what I mean!
Who's the captain!?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「I said go help peel the potatoes, to the captain. Right, you wanna go too? When the captain peels, there's always little specks of blood left on the potatoes. Because she's, you know, clumsy.」
【Naomasa】 「Aah, guess you're right, I get what───wait. That's not it! You said captain, who's that supposed to be!?」

source.japanese: ちなみに通路に居合わせたのは、朔屋と水夫長とそしてクロの三人ばかり。水夫長が有りもしない幻影に向かって話しかける癖の持ち主という可能性もあるにはあるが、それなら何故クロが律儀に返事した？
source.english: Incidentally, only three people had been in the passage: Sakuya, the boatswain, and Kuro. It was possible that the boatswain had a habit of speaking to imaginary figures. But if so, why had Kuro dutifully answered?

source.japanese: ───そう、そうなのだった。一度なら聞き間違いあろうが、二度三度と繰り返されるとそれは考えづらい。
source.english: —Yes. That was how it was. Once might have been a mishearing. Twice, three times made that difficult to believe.

source.japanese: それでも、余りに余りの事態に、足元の床が脳軟化症を起こした痴呆老人の脳髄に成り代わったような錯覚に襲われ、朔屋はずぶずぶと海まで落ちこんでいくかの失墜感によろめいて、耐えきれず、そばの配管にすがりつく有り様の。そこへ水夫長の台詞、止めとばかり鈍器とめりこむ。
source.english:
Even so, it was too much. Sakuya felt as though the floor beneath him had become the softened brain of a senile old man. He staggered, with a sinking sensation that threatened to swallow him all the way down to the sea. Unable to bear it, he clung to a nearby pipe.
Then the boatswain's words drove in like a blunt weapon, the finishing blow.

target.text: Incidentally, the only people that were present in the passageway were Sakuya, the Bosun, and Kuro, only those three. It was certainly a possibility that the Bosun had an odd habit of talking to imaginary phantoms, but if so, why had Kuro replied so dutifully?
───Verily, that was indeed so. While it could be dismissed as him simply mishearing once, when it was repeated twice, even thrice, that explanation became difficult to defend.

But even so, faced with this overly outrageous state of affairs, he was overcome by a hallucination like the floor beneath his feet had been replaced with the brains of a demented senior citizen suffering from encephalomalacia; Sakuya staggered, feeling like he were sinking deep into the ocean, and unable to handle it, he was reduced to clinging to the nearby piping. And then, the Bosun uttered that line, a blunt instrument lodging into his skull like it was delivering the finishing blow.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「誰って、ここにゃ他にいねえだろうが。
　判りきったこと訊くなよど阿呆め。
　クロだよ。あれがこの信天翁の船長だ。
　あいつこそ『嵐を呼ぶ船長』───
　船長クロだ───！
　覚えたか、サンピンがっ」
source.english:
“Who? There's nobody else here, is there?
Don't ask questions you know the answer to, you idiot.
Kuro.
She's the captain of the Albatross.
The captain who calls up storms—Captain Kuro!
Got that, small fry?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Who? Well, not like there's anybody else here. Stop asking things you already know, you damn idiot. It's Kuro. She's the captain of this Albatross. The one and only 『Stormcalling Captain』─── Captain Kuro───! Got that through your thick skull, you nobody?」

source.japanese: いつから世界は、雑用、小間使いの類を船長と呼ぶようになったのか。天を衝[つ]く塔の建設が天譴によって中断されて以来、かつて一つであった世界言語は崩壊し、それから人類が混乱から立ち返るまで永き時を要したと言うが、朔屋の知らない間にまたどこかで万長の塔が造られて、そして打ち砕かれていたというのか、それとも酒がまだ残っているのか。にわかに頭の血管のどこかがずきずきと鳴り出す、いや、脈打っているのはこの船全体か、自分の頭が狂い始めているのか、真実船が脈動しているのか、どちらにしても脈打つのに合わせて視界がぶれる悪い汗が滲む。
source.english: Since when had the world taken to calling errand runners and menials captains? They said that when divine wrath halted the building of the tower that would pierce the heavens, the world’s once-united language collapsed, and that long ages passed before mankind found its way out of the ensuing confusion; had another tower ten thousand fathoms high been raised and smashed to pieces somewhere while Sakuya wasn’t looking? Or was the liquor still in him? All at once, some blood vessel in his head began to throb—or no, was it the whole ship that was pulsing? Was his mind beginning to crack, or was the ship truly beating? Whichever it was, his vision lurched with every pulse, and a clammy sweat seeped from his skin.

source.japanese:
───朔屋も本当は、水夫長がクロをそう呼んだ時に、どこかで納得している部分があったのだろう。この船、信天翁は海の不条理の掃き溜めのような、いっそ地獄と言いきってしまっていいような船であり、部屋の片づけといった日常的な動作に没入するうちにその事実から目を逸らしがちになっていたけれど。どこまでもいっても、信天翁号はおかしかった。それを今さらに突きつけられただけだ。
　けれど、けれども。
source.english:
—In truth, some part of Sakuya must have accepted it the moment the boatswain called Kuro captain. This ship, the Albatross, was a midden for all the sea’s absurdities—a vessel one might as well simply call hell. Immersing himself in so ordinary an act as putting a room to rights had only let him turn his eyes from that fact for a while. Through and through, the Albatross was wrong. The fact had merely been thrust in his face anew.
And yet. And yet.

target.text: Since when exactly had the world at large begun to call the likes of handmaids or drudges "Captain"? Ever since construction of the heaven-piercing tower was stayed by Heaven's judgment, the universal language that once existed ages ago broke down, and it was said that aeons would pass before humanity once more emerged from the ashes of the resulting chaos, but perhaps, somewhere else, another tower of immeasurable heights had been built without Sakuya's knowledge only to be destroyed once more, or perhaps there was still some alcohol coursing through his veins?

A faint throbbing somewhere inside the blood vessels running through his head began to make its presence known, nay, was it the whole ship that was pulsating, had he himself begun to lose his mind, was the ship actually pulsating with movement? Regardless of which it was, his vision blurred with every pulse, and he broke into a cold sweat.

───In truth, there was a part of Sakuya that had been convinced ever since the Bosun had first called Kuro by that appellation. This ship, the Albatross, was like a cesspool of the absurdities of the sea, what one might as well call hell itself, but he genuinely tried very hard to avert his eyes from the truth while immersing himself in the mundane motions of cleaning up a cabin. In every possible respect, this Albatross was simply wrong. He had merely been confronted with that anew.

source.japanese:
朔屋は空気を求めて激しく喘[あえ]いで、踏み殺される寸前の蛙の喘鳴、配管にすがっただけでは足らずにずるずると崩れていく、口元に歪んだ笑みをへばりつかせたまま。
　判る、朔屋の船室の先の住人が狂を発したわけが今は判る。別段に、空が突然黄土色に発光し、二つに割れてそこから巨大な仏頭が逆さに突き出てきてにやにや笑ったとか、海から桃色と黒のマーブル模様の象たちの一個連隊が浮上してきてラインダンスを踊り始めたとか、そういう非常事態に遭遇したわけでもないのだろう。彼だか彼女だか判らないがそいつは、ただこの船に乗っていただけだ。
　そして、それで充分だ。
source.english:
He gasped fiercely for air, wheezing like a frog about to be trodden to death. Clinging to the pipe was not enough. He slid down it, a twisted smile stuck to his mouth.
He understood. Now he understood why the previous occupant of his cabin had gone mad. There need not have been some extraordinary event: the sky suddenly glowing ocher, splitting in two, and a gigantic Buddha's head protruding upside down with a smirk; a regiment of pink-and-black marbled elephants rising from the sea to dance in a line. Nothing like that.
Whoever the person was, man or woman, they had simply been aboard this ship.
And that was enough.

source.japanese: こんな、ただ浮いているだけでも世界に卑猥な挑戦を続けているような船であるのにくわえ、船長が、文字通り船の長が、あの不器用でおつむの中身も可哀相な少女、クロだって───？
source.english: A ship that seemed to offer the world an obscene challenge simply by staying afloat. And her captain—the very head of the ship—was that clumsy, pitifully dim-witted girl? Kuro?

target.text: Sakuya gasped violently in search of air with the stridor of a frog on the verge of being trampled to death; just clinging to the piping was no longer enough for him, and he crumbled to the floor, a twisted smile still plastered across his face.

He understood. In this moment, he understood perfectly well why the prior occupant of his cabin went mad. It wasn't that the air suddenly began to emit an ochre light, split in two, and from there, the gigantic head of a Buddha statue emerged, hanging upside down with a grin, or that from the ocean came elephants marbled in pink and black, a full regiment rising to the surface, that began to perform a line dance: they hadn't run afoul of any such states of emergency in particular. He or she, he couldn't claim to know the person, had merely boarded this ship. And that was more than plenty.

In addition to being a ship that seems to be persistently issuing an obscene challenge to the world merely by virtue of floating, the Captain, the Master of the Vessel in every sense of the word, is that girl, who is not just clumsy, but cursed with pitiful mental faculties besides: it's Kuro, he says───?

source.japanese: 蹌踉と立ち上がる。目が回る、目の中でどこんと脈打つ。船も合わせて脈動しているのが耐えられない。世界を覆っている現実が、薄い皮膜と化したかのようだ。皮膜の一枚向こうでは、冒涜的な真実とやらが朔屋をせせら笑うように脈動しているのだろう。だからこんなにまで船内も耐えがたく震動しているのだろう。
source.english: He rose unsteadily. His head spun; something thumped behind his eyes. The ship's answering pulse was unbearable. The reality that covered the world seemed to have become a thin membrane. On its far side, some blasphemous truth must be throbbing, sneering at Sakuya. That must be why the ship shook so intolerably.

source.japanese: 水夫長は、襟首を摘[つま]みあげることも忘れ、朔屋の恐慌を呆れたように見送っている、それがせめてもの希望という奴で、このまま甲板まで上がれたなら、港に下りる隙があるはず。もう厭だとにかく厭だなにがなんでも厭厭厭厭厭と念仏のように口の裡で誦しつ朔屋は階段を目指し、上甲板を目指して泳ぐように宙を掻[か]く。
source.english:
The boatswain had even forgotten to catch him by the collar, merely watching his panic in disbelief. That was one small hope. If he could reach the deck now, he might have a chance to get back to the harbor.
No. I can't stand it. No, whatever happens, no, no, no, no, no. Muttering it like a prayer, Sakuya made for the stairs, for the upper deck, his arms clawing the air as though he were swimming.

target.text: He stood up, tottering. His eyes spun, a heavy throbbing within them. He couldn't stand how the ship pulsated in unison. It was as if the reality that covered the whole world had turned into a thin membrane. On the other side of that membrane, the blasphemous truth or something like it must have been pulsating as if it were sneering at Sakuya. That was why even the interior of the ship was vibrating in this intolerable manner, it had to be.

The Bosun, forgetting even to lift him by the collar, just watched Sakuya leave with a look of exasperation at his display of panic, and with that as his only saving grace, if he were to just ascend to the deck, there should be a chance for him to disembark to the port. He'd had enough, simply enough, enough enough enough enough enough of it all, so Sakuya chanted to himself like he were reciting the Nembutsu as he aimed for the ladder, clawing his way through the air like he were swimming, heading for the upper deck.

source.japanese: 途中で、通路の壁に造り付けられた伝声管の蓋が勝手に開き、『機関……叩き起こしましたよ……』と静かな囁きな癖して奇妙に耳朶に徹る声が低く響いてきたけれど、今の朔屋には聞こえない、この船の中で交わされる言葉など、何一つ彼の耳から脳には伝わらない。
source.english: On the way, the lid of a speaking tube built into the passage wall opened of its own accord, and a low voice came through: ‘The engine… I’ve beaten it awake…’ Quiet though it was, the whisper somehow bored straight into the ear. But Sakuya, in his present state, heard none of it. Nothing said aboard this ship could travel from his ears to his brain.

target.text: On the way, the lid on one of the voice pipes fastened to the passageway walls opened by itself, and he heard a deeply resounding voice that said: 『I have coaxed the engine…… from its slumber……』 It rang loudly in his ears despite being delivered in a hushed whisper, but right now, Sakuya didn't listen; any words and the like exchanged aboard this ship, not a single one went through his ear and into his brain.

source.japanese:
そして朔屋は、誰にも咎められる事なく。
　上甲板まで比喩でなく、階段を事実手をついて這い上がり、あと少しだ、倒れるなとふらつく体に鞭打ってタラップへと歩き出した、時、だった。
source.english:
And so, with nobody stopping him, Sakuya reached the upper deck. Not figuratively: he had actually crawled up the stairs on his hands. Almost there. Don't fall. He drove his unsteady body toward the gangway.
That was when it happened.

target.text: Thus, Sakuya wasn't reprimanded by anyone. It was not metaphorically, he actually crawled up the ladder on all fours, and muttering "just a little more, don't collapse on me now", he whipped his wobbling body onwards, and just as he began to walk towards the gangway leading back to the port, in that moment, it happened.

source.japanese: ───『信天翁号』は、爆発した。
source.english: —The Albatross exploded.

source.japanese: 少なくとも朔屋にはそれくらいの衝撃だった。足は甲板から５センチは浮き上がり、近くのバラックの、虫食いが曼陀羅のように彩った板壁まで弾き飛ばされて倒れこんだし、あちこちでそれらバラックの屋根が弾けたり壁板が落ちたりするのも目にしていた。
source.english: At least, the shock felt that great to Sakuya. His feet lifted at least five centimeters off the deck. He was flung against the wall of a nearby shack, its wormholes forming a mandala, and fell. Here and there he saw roofs burst and wallboards drop from the shacks.

target.text: ───The『Albatross』exploded.

If nothing else, such was the intensity of the impact Sakuya felt. His feet were floating about five centimetres above the deck, and he was sent flying into a nearby shack whose walls were decorated in worm-eaten furrows shaped like mandalas, then collapsed on the deck, and he witnessed roofs popping into the air and wall panels falling down and out here and there.

source.japanese: しかしそれは爆発などではない。
source.english: But it was not an explosion.

source.japanese:
否。
　爆発という言語の意味においては正しいだろう。
source.english:
No.
Strictly speaking, ‘explosion’ was the right word.

source.japanese:
ただしそれは、信天翁号のどこかの、主機関の内燃室で起こったのだった。
　すなわち、船の動力部で。
　すなわち、それは船が動き出した事を告げており。
source.english:
Only it had occurred somewhere in the combustion chamber of the Albatross's main engine.
In other words, in the ship's power plant.
In other words, it announced that the ship had begun to move.

source.japanese: すなわち、朔屋が先程から体感していた震動は、彼の精神状態を世界が反映したなどいう文学的な事態に非ずして、機関の始動音だったという。
source.english:
In other words, the vibrations Sakuya had been feeling were not some literary phenomenon in which the world reflected his state of mind.
They were the rumble of the engine starting.

target.text: But that was no explosion.
Nay. Semantically speaking, in the linguistic sense of the word "explosion", that would qualify as one.

However, it was something that occurred in the internal combustion chamber of the main engine located somewhere on the Albatross. In other words, the place supplying motive power to the ship. In other words, this signaled that the ship had begun moving.

In other words, the vibrations Sakuya had experienced since a little while ago were not, in fact, some literary vehicle of expression that projected Sakuya's mental state unto the world, it was the sound of an engine starting.

source.japanese:
『信天翁号』は、喘息患者の最後の咳のような凄まじい鳴動を一つ、よくその震動だけで船体が分解せずに済んだもの、次いで甲板上のバラックの隙間から生えた、辛うじて煙突と判別できる（なにしろ妙な角度に傾いていた上に、中途に余計な穴が空いていた）円筒から、辺り一面汚染しそうな量の煤塵を吐き出した。港に垂れこめていた午後の陽差しが翳[かげ]るほどの。その汚らしいこと露骨に過ぎて、世の終わりに降り注ぐという煤の雨さえ思わせて、なれば上げる汽笛は御使いがかき鳴らすという終末の喇叭か。
　だが言えるのは、たとえ本当に終末が来たとして、煉獄だか地獄だかに落ちていく列の先頭には、この『信天翁号』こそが相応しい、という事───
source.english:
The Albatross gave one tremendous roar like the final cough of an asthma sufferer—by some miracle the vibration alone failed to shake her hull apart—and then belched, from a cylinder sprouting amid the gaps between the shacks on deck and just barely identifiable as a funnel (it leaned at a preposterous angle and had gratuitous holes halfway up it), enough soot to pollute the entire vicinity. Enough to dim the afternoon sunlight hanging over the harbor. Its filth was so brazen it called to mind the rain of soot said to fall at the end of the world; and if so, was the whistle she now raised the trumpet of doomsday, blared by an angel?
But this much could be said: even if the end truly came, none was fitter than the Albatross to head the procession down into purgatory, or hell—

source.japanese: 壁に叩きつけられた衝撃に眩む朔屋が見たものは、停泊していた埠頭よりゆっくりゆっくり離れていく信天翁号。ゆっくりと間を空けていく、船と埠頭との距離、隔てるものは、船の動きが生んだ波のうねる海面。
source.english: Dazed by the impact against the wall, Sakuya watched the Albatross slowly, slowly leave her berth. The distance between ship and wharf grew by degrees. Between them was the sea, rippling with the waves of her own movement.

source.japanese:
後から朔屋は思う。
　それが、最後のチャンスだったのだ、と。
source.english:
Later, he would think:
that had been his last chance.

source.japanese:
この時、船は離れ始めていたとはいえ、まだ飛びこんで埠頭まで泳ぎ渡ること十分可能な距離だったはずだ。
　なのになぜ自分は虚けたまま倒れ伏したままだったのか。失神はしていなかった。意識はあった。
　船の起こす引き波の手に船尾までさらわれ、スクリューに巻きこまれる事を恐れていたとでもいうのか。なんの、その時の朔屋の脳髄が、そんな論理学者はだしに明晰に活動などしていた訳もなく。
source.english:
Even though the ship had begun to leave, he must still have been close enough to jump in and swim back to the wharf.
Why, then, had he lain there stupefied? He had not fainted. He was conscious.
Had he feared being swept astern by the ship's wake and caught in the propeller? Hardly. His brain at the time wasn't putting any logicians to shame.

target.text: The『Albatross』let out an awesome rumbling, like the final cough of an asthmatic patient; it was impressive that the ship herself was not ripped apart by that tremor alone, and following that, the cylinders sprouting up from the gaps between the shacks on the upper deck, which could barely be discerned to be funnels (not only did they lean at odd angles, they had plenty of holes on the way up), spouted up enough soot to pollute the whole surrounding area. Enough to darken the afternoon sunbeams spilling into the port.

It was so indecently excessive in its filth, invoking the rain of soot said to fall at the end of the world, and if so, would the loud steam whistle be the trumpets of the apocalypse sounded by the angels after the breaking of the seventh seal? But all he could say was that, assuming the end of the world truly was upon them, this『Albatross』in particular was most suitable to lead the long line of those heading for Purgatory or Hell.

Dizzied by the impact of being slammed against a wall, all Sakuya saw was the Albatross slowly, slowly drifting away from the wharf she was once moored at. The gap between ship and wharf gradually grew in size, and separating the two was the surface of the sea, rolling with the waves created from the ship's movement.
Later, Sakuya would think. That right there, that was my final chance.

In this moment, the ship might have begun to take her leave, but it was still a distance where it should have been more than possible for him to jump off and swim to the wharf. So why, then, did he remain prostrate, completely deflated? He hadn't fainted. He was conscious. Was he afraid of being pulled into the stern by the ship's undertow, afraid of being entangled in the screw? Not at all, no, at the time, Sakuya's brain was certainly not engaged in anything so cogent that it could put a logician to shame.

source.japanese: 朔屋はその時───
source.english: At that moment, Sakuya—

target.text: That moment, Sakuya was───

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「やっべ、ちょっとトイレで頑張りすぎた。
　こりゃキサラにどやされる」
source.english:
“Shit, I spent a little too long straining on the toilet.
Kisara's going to give me hell.”

source.japanese: 倒れた彼の、すぐ傍を慌ただしく駆け抜けていく信天翁号一等航海士、彼女の───
source.english: The Albatross's first mate hurried past where he lay. She—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Damn, got stuck in the bathroom for a little too long. Kisara's gonna fly off the handle.」
Right next to where Sakuya lay collapsed, there was the first mate of the Albatross, running past in a hurry, her───

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「しかし今日は、エンジンかかるのがやけに早いね。
　機関長、なぁにそんな頑張ったんだか」
source.english:
“Still, the engine started awfully fast today.
What's got the chief working so hard?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But the engine started up awfully early today, huh. Wonder what's got you working so hard today, Chief Engineer.」

source.japanese:
操舵室を目指しているのであろうか、走る姿はきびきびと、しなやかで、リズム正しく美しく、甲板を蹴る脚、そしてその太腿がなんとも眩しい。なにより世の男どもの目を惹きつけるのはその短かなスカートだろう、ひらひらと翻[ひるがえ]り、今にも捲[めく]れ返りそうにして、それでいてけしてその奥の神秘の布地を覗かせる事なく、もはや不可思議の具現と言っていい過言でないスカートだろう。
　籠目模様は、妖しの心を吸いつけてそれらの動きを封じ、為に魔除けとして用いられるという。この時の朔屋にも、一等航海士のミニスカートは籠目同様の、いやもっと精妙に、限定的な効果を発揮した。
　青年の心の中の、この益体もない船を下りたいという希望だけを麻酔して、彼の精神の残りの部分全てを奪い取った。
source.english:
Perhaps she was heading for the wheelhouse. Her running was brisk, supple, beautifully rhythmic. The legs striking the deck, and the thighs above them, were dazzling. What would draw any man's eyes most, however, was that short skirt. It fluttered and flipped, always on the verge of turning up, yet never revealing the mysterious fabric beneath. To call it an embodiment of the uncanny was hardly an exaggeration.
The woven lattice of a basket was said to trap the attention of evil spirits and hold them motionless, which was why it served as a charm. At that moment, the first mate's miniskirt worked on Sakuya much the same way. No—its effect was subtler, more selective.
It anesthetized only his wish to leave this worthless ship, while seizing every other part of his mind.

source.japanese: 端的に言えば朔屋は、女の脚に見惚れ、下着を覗こうとしたお陰で船から逃れる機会を失ったと、まあそういう次第である。
source.english:
Put simply, Sakuya lost his chance to escape because he was admiring a woman's legs and trying to see her underwear.
That was the whole of it.

target.text: She was probably running in the direction of the wheelhouse, her form brisk, graceful, and beautifully in rhythm, legs kicking down on the deck, and those thighs, what a dazzling sight they made. But what drew the gaze of the menfolk of the world most of all was surely that short skirt, flapping and fluttering, on the verge of flipping over any second, and yet it would never permit even a glimpse of that mystical fabric in its depths; it would probably not be an exaggeration to call this skirt an incarnation of the unfathomable at this point.

The kagome pattern is said to draw in the hearts and wills of spirits and seal their movements. For this reason, it is also used to ward off demonic entities. In this very moment, the first mate's miniskirt demonstrated a power similar to that of the kagome pattern on Sakuya, no, it was a more intricate, limited effect. It narcotized only one desire within this young man's heart, that being his wish to disembark from this absurd ship, and robbed him of all his remaining mental faculties.

To get straight to the point, Sakuya had been captivated by a woman's legs, and because he was trying to peek at her underwear, he then missed his chance to escape from the ship. Well, that was the short of things.

source.japanese: 海は、朔屋の。頭上で。
source.english:
The sea was above Sakuya.
Above his head.

source.japanese: 空を映して濃縮した深い紺碧の水面には波の連なり、押し寄せては去りゆき後から後からきりもなく、これが逆巻く荒波ならば、朔屋の頭へ噛みついてきそうで危うい眺めだが、幸い頭上の海は穏やか、突如弾けてその超絶の質量を下へ叩きつけてくる、などは杞憂と言って良い。
source.english: Its deep blue surface seemed to concentrate the reflected sky. Wave followed wave, advancing, withdrawing, endlessly replaced. Had they been raging breakers, the sight would have been dangerous: they might have bitten at his head. Fortunately, the sea overhead was calm. Fears that it might suddenly burst and bring its tremendous weight crashing down were groundless.

source.japanese: いかなる作用によって天水が逆転したのかは定かではないにしろ、眺望はただひたすらに絶佳にして、だのに朔屋は頭上の海へ、重力から解き放たれて飛翔していくのではないかとの不安に責め苛まれていた……それは苛まれもするだろう。
source.english:
Whatever force had reversed sky and water, the view was simply magnificent. Yet Sakuya was tormented by the fear that he might break free of gravity and fly into the sea above him…
Hardly surprising, really.

source.japanese: 朔屋の視点を離れて遠目に見ればそら、天水の順はたちどころに正常に復し、青年が信天翁号の船腹から荒縄で縛り上げられ、逆さ吊りにされているのだという視点の手品の種明かし、なにほどのことはない。
source.english:
Leave his viewpoint and look from a distance. There: sky and sea resume their proper order. The trick of perspective reveals itself. The young man is trussed in rough rope, hanging upside down from the Albatross's side.
Nothing much to it.

source.japanese: だから、朔屋の鼻の奥につんと来ている生臭さも潮の香りではない。数日ほど身を晒していれば潮風は肌に馴染み、本来街中を満たした雑な臭気を人が忘れがちになるように、海の精華を伸ばしたような潮の香りも鼻には届かなくなる。だから朔屋の鼻に匂うきな臭いのは、彼の鼻血なのだった。
source.english:
Thus the raw smell stinging the back of his nose was not the sea. After a few days exposed to it, the salt wind grew familiar on the skin. Just as people ceased to notice the mixed odors of a town, the scent of salt, like the diluted essence of the sea, no longer reached the nose.
The smell Sakuya noticed, therefore, came from his own nosebleed.

target.text: The sea. Was above. Sakuya's head.

A series of waves rippled across the deep, concentrated azure of the surface of water projected on the sky, pushing forwards and then pulling back, one after another, ceaselessly, and were these surging, raging waves, then it would have made for a rather precarious sight, one like to snap at Sakuya's head, but fortunately, the sea above his dome was calm, and the idea that it would suddenly explode and slam its superlative mass down on him could well be called an unfounded worry.

Though it remained uncertain what manner of action had caused the reversal of sky and sea, it certainly made for a superb vista to behold, but Sakuya remained tortured by the anxiety that he might be liberated from gravity and fly away into the sea above……that would probably be quite the harrowing experience.

Were one to distance oneself from Sakuya's perspective and look from afar, then behold, the skies and the water return to their usual state at once, and the magic trick, the sleight of perspective, is revealed to be nothing more than the young man being tied up in coarse rope and hanging upside down from the hull of the Albatross, hardly anything noteworthy.

Therefore, that pungent, fishy smell stinging Sakuya deep in his nose was not the scent of the sea. Once exposed to it for a few days, the salty air starts to settle into your skin, and by the time you have mostly forgotten the various smells that permeate the city, the scent of the sea water, like the very essence of the ocean itself reaching out for you, will no longer reach your nose. So this strange smell that Sakuya's nose was sniffing out was the smell of his own nosebleed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おぅういィ……。
　あんたら、人のこと簡単に逆さ吊りにしてくれるけどさァ……」
source.english:
“Heeeey…
It's all very well for you to hang a man upside down so casually…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Ooooii……. Guys, you sure hang people upside down like it's no big deal, but……」

source.japanese: ふん、と息めば鼻腔から血の粒が洟[はなみず]と綯[な]い交[ま]ぜになって飛沫く、それで胸苦しさは飛ぶどころかいよいよ深刻になってきて、朔屋は呻[うめ]く、情けなく、慈悲を求めて。
source.english: He snorted. Blood and mucus tangled together and sprayed from his nostrils. Far from relieving the pressure in his chest, it made it worse. He groaned miserably, asking for mercy.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「これ、そのうち俺、血の管とか破裂して死んじゃうよう……？
　いっくらサボタージュの懲罰つったって、流石にちょっと、洒落になってませんよ？」
source.english:
“At this rate, won't a blood vessel burst and kill me…?
You can call it punishment for slacking off, but this is getting seriously unfunny.”

source.japanese: 大体にして、上甲板の痛んだ部分の修理といっても、この信天翁号、全体が無傷でまともな部分など無きに等しい。だから少しくらいさぼったところで大して差し支えもあるまいと、これは言いつけを怠けていた朔屋の言い分であり、水夫長からしてみればまた別の意見もあろう。どちらにせよ確かなのは、仕事もせずふらふらと、厨房の料理酒を盗み呑みしようとしていたところを捕縛されるという、朔屋の要領の悪さであり、どこの世界でもそういう要領の悪い人間は辛い憂き目を見るという、まさに今が見本なのだった。
source.english: Granted, one might speak of repairing the damaged parts of the upper deck—but aboard the Albatross there was scarcely a sound, undamaged part to be found anywhere. Slacking off a little could hardly matter much: such was Sakuya’s case for neglecting his orders, though the boatswain would doubtless have had another opinion. In any event, what could not be disputed was Sakuya’s singular ineptitude: instead of working, he had gone wandering off to steal a drink of cooking wine from the galley and got himself caught. In every world, men that bad at getting away with things come to grief; and here he hung, a perfect specimen.

source.japanese: こうして朔屋の働きぶりは、彼の船内での位置を決めていった。船員学校にいた事もある、ではなく、そこから滑落した駄目でぼんくらで役立たずの使えない男。信天翁号に乗りこまされた時には一応二等航海士扱いではあったが、いまや実質的には下級水夫以下にと落ち着いた。あの船長クロと、同じレヴェルなのである。位置が確定するにつれ、朔屋に与えられる懲罰の苛酷の度合いは増していき、鉄拳制裁など日常茶飯事、飯抜きも度々となり、繰り返されるお仕置きに悪慣れしていくとなると、逆さ吊りその他の熾烈な刑も加わった。
source.english:
His performance gradually determined his place aboard. Not a man who had once attended a school for sailors, but a man who had fallen out of one: a useless, incompetent, hopeless good-for-nothing. When pressed aboard the Albatross, he had nominally been treated as a second mate. Now, in practice, he ranked below the junior sailors. On the same level as Captain Kuro.
As his place became clear, his punishments grew harsher. Blows were everyday business; missed meals came often. When he began to grow unpleasantly accustomed to these repeated chastisements, upside-down suspension and other fiercer penalties were added.

target.text: When he sent a gust of air through his nose, droplets of blood and snot mixed together and sprayed out of his nasal cavity; that didn't make the tightness in his chest abate, on the contrary, it was only growing more and more severe, and Sakuya groaned, pitifully, pleading for mercy.

【Naomasa】 「Any more of this and soon enough, my blood vessels are gonna burst and I'll die, you know……? Call this punishment for slacking off all you want, this is a little…… this really isn't gonna be a laughing matter, okay?」

To begin with, he'd been told to repair the damaged parts of the upper deck, but on the whole, there were barely any parts of this Albatross that could be considered undamaged or in decent condition. Therefore, even if he slacked off a little, it wouldn't really make a big difference: that was Sakuya's excuse for neglecting the duties he'd been assigned, but if you were to ask the Bosun, he'd probably have a different view on things.

What was certain, however, was that he went without working, wandered whimsically down into the galley, then got caught as he tried to sneak some cooking sake down his throat, and this was Sakuya's inept bungling at work: in any world, those who lack the knack for navigating through life smoothly are said to be destined for a fate of bitter hardships, and right now, he was the perfect example of that.

Thus, Sakuya's manner of working was what determined his position aboard the ship. Here was a man who had even gone to a nautical school, only he'd never finished it, and it was all downhill from there: a useless, good-for-nothing, thickheaded, hopeless man.

When he first boarded the Albatross, he was provisionally treated as a second mate, but now, he was in substance lower than the deck boys. On the same level as that Captain Kuro. As his position was etched deeper into stone, so did the punishments Sakuya were given also escalate in severity; physical punishment was an everyday occurrence, he would occasionally go without meals, and as he grew desensitized to the repeated punishments, being strung up by his feet were added to the list along with other fierce forms of punishment.

source.japanese:
もちろん、それも自業自得、さ。
　朔屋は濁音混じりの呻[うめ]き声でもう一度助命を乞うたが、船上から答えはなく、代わりにと海面に現れたものは、代わりにもならない。
source.english:
Of course, he had brought it all on himself.
With another thickened groan, he begged for his life. No answer came from the ship. Something appeared on the water instead. It was no substitute.

source.japanese:
のんびりとした波を割って浮き上がった物は、背景の穏やかさをたちまちのうちにたまらない緊迫に染め上げた。なんとなれば、三角の鰭だった。
　物語、それも海賊小説あたりでお馴染み、鱶の鰭。言うまでもなく得意技は、海賊船の後からついてきて、慰みに海に投げこまれる船長に逆らったとんまや捕虜の脚やら胴体やらを噛みちぎっていく事だ。
　それも、浮かんできた鰭だけでも朔屋の肘から先よりも長く、水面下の巨体を推測するに容易い。どうやら朔屋が垂らした、鼻血に惹かれてきたものと見える。
source.english:
What broke the languid surface instantly steeped that tranquil scene in unbearable tension: a triangular fin.
A shark’s fin, familiar from stories—pirate novels in particular. Its signature trick, needless to say, is to trail a pirate ship and bite the legs and torsos off fools who defy the captain, or prisoners, when they are tossed overboard for sport.
And the fin alone was longer than Sakuya’s arm from elbow to fingertips, making the bulk below easy enough to imagine. It appeared to have been drawn by the blood dripping from his nose.

source.japanese: 朔屋は、当然のように恐慌を来した。
source.english: Naturally, Sakuya panicked.

target.text: Of course, that, too, was simply him reaping what he had sown, to be sure. Sakuya groaned once more, voice choked and husky, begging for his life, but no answer came from the ship, and what appeared on the surface of the sea could not remotely be considered an adequate substitute.

The thing so nonchalantly splitting the waves asunder transformed the tranquility of the scenery into an unbearable tension on the instant. Why? Well, it was a triangular fin. A classic in stories and pirate novels alike, a large shark fin. Needless to say, its signature move was trailing after a pirate ship, tearing apart the legs and torsos of any fools and captives who had defied the captain and been tossed overboard for his amusement.

Furthermore, even just the surfacing fin was longer than Sakuya's forearm by itself, making it easy to guess at the enormous size of the body lurking beneath the waves. It must have been lured here by the nosebleed dripping from Sakuya, or so it seemed.
Sakuya, as was only natural, was thrown into a complete panic.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「な、ちょ……このあたりの内海にゃ、
　こんな兇悪なのいねぇって話でないの！
　なんでよりにもよってこんな時に───」
source.english:
“H-Hang on… I thought there weren't
things this vicious in these inland waters!
Why now, of all times—?”

source.japanese: ざっと水面までの距離を目測すれば、三から四米といったところ、到底安全圏内とは言いきれず、朔屋は煮えたぎった油の上で、熱に悶える蓑虫と、必死で身を折り身を捻りして、しかし両腕もがっちり戒められているとあっては無駄な足掻きとしか。浮かび上がった鰭はぐるぐると周泳し出して、一周一周するにつれ螺旋に円を狭めていって、閉じたその時に、巨体を砲弾とぶつけてくるのだろう。後に残るのは、朔屋を吊っていた荒縄ばかり、端っこにぎざきざの噛み傷のみ残して。
source.english:
He judged the distance to the surface at three or four meters. It was by no means safe. Like a bagworm writhing in the heat above boiling oil, he desperately bent and twisted. With both arms firmly bound, his efforts were futile.
The fin began circling. With every circuit, its spiral drew tighter. When the circle closed, that huge body would surely strike like a cannonball. Only the rough rope that had held Sakuya would remain, with ragged tooth marks at the end.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Wha-, wait……there's not supposed to be anything this vicious in these inland waters! And of all the times to show up───」

At a rough estimate, he was between three or four metres above the surface of the sea, not something you could definitively claim to be within the safe zone, and Sakuya bent and wriggled his body like a bagworm writhing in boiling oil, but with both arms tightly secured, it amounted to nothing but futile struggling. The fin that surfaced began to swim in circles, the diameter of the spiral narrowing with each rotation, and by the time it closed, surely its giant body would slam into him like a cannonball. All that would remain was the straw rope that had once kept Sakuya suspended, nothing but jagged bite marks at the ends.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーーーーっっ………………」
source.english: “Aaaaaaaaah…………”

source.japanese: 絶叫は、流れて掠れて細くなる、水面から噴火の勢いで跳ね上がってきた鱶の顎に攫[さら]われたなら、声も一緒に海面下へ下っていったのだろうが、今の場合、上へと流れた。
source.english:
His scream streamed away, thinned, grew hoarse. Had the jaws of a shark erupting from the water seized him, the voice would have gone down beneath the surface with him.
In this case, it went up.

source.japanese: 朔屋のぐるぐる巻きの体は、船腹に二度・三度バウンドしつつ、上へと引き揚げられていって、後には鱶鰭だけが取り残されて、跳躍の機会を逸して空しい、何度か波を切って往復したけれど、しまいには諦めたか海面下に沈んで、背景に劇伴が流れていたなら重低音の緊迫調から晴れて爽やかなのに戻ったところ。
source.english:
His tightly wrapped body rose, bouncing two or three times against the hull. Only the shark fin remained behind, having missed its chance to leap. It cut back and forth through the waves several times, then apparently gave up and sank.
Had there been music in the background, this was where the ominous bass would have cleared into a bright, refreshing tune.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「AAAAーーーー………………」」

His scream faded away, became hoarse and thin, and had he been taken in the jaws of the great shark leaping up from the water with the explosive force of a volcanic eruption, his voice would surely sink down with him, submerged beneath the waves, but at present, it was drifting upwards.

Wrapped round and round, Sakuya's body was hoisted upwards, bouncing against the hull of the ship a couple times en route, the shark fin the only thing left behind, lifeless after missing its chance to leap for him, cutting through the waves and making several round trips before ultimately giving up and diving beneath the waters once more, and if there had been background music playing, it would probably have shifted from a tense, heavy bass, returning to something pleasantly refreshing.

source.japanese:
一方甲板上の朔屋───
　
　戒めは船員ナイフで断ち切られても、朔屋の腕や首やらあちこちに縄目を残して、特殊な性的遊戯の痕跡めかしていかがわしい。あちこち鬱血していた血の巡りが戻っていくにつれ、皮膚の下では痛痒感がたまらない、頭も血が上りきっていてふらついていたけれど、それでも朔屋は救い主に感謝を述べるくらいには気力を振り絞る。
source.english:
Meanwhile, Sakuya was on deck—
A sailor's knife cut his bonds, though rope marks remained on his arms, neck, and elsewhere, looking suspiciously like traces of some specialized sexual amusement. As blood returned to the congested places, unbearable aches and itching stirred beneath his skin. His head was still so full of blood that he reeled. Even so, he summoned enough strength to thank his rescuers.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「た、助かった。
　有難う有難う君たち───」
source.english:
“S-Saved. Thank you.
Thank you, all of you—”

source.japanese:
そしてそれが限界で、上甲板のあばら屋の影に駆けこんで、げえげえと吐き戻し始める胃の中身、幸い、なのかどうか、腹には大して残っておらず、胃液混じりの涎が口の端から筋を引く。朔屋の苦しみを見かねたのか、背後に寄り添って背中をさすってやるのが一人、口を尖らせ掃除用具を取りに行く厳しいのが一人、船縁から身を乗りだし、消えていった鱶の大きさをああだこうだと話の種にしている暢気なのが二人ほど。
　皆、半ズボンがよく似合っていた。袖に折り返しのある、セーラー襟[えり]のお仕着せが愛らしかった。みな同じお揃いの、少年の。
source.english:
That was his limit. He hurried into the shadow of an upper-deck hovel and began noisily emptying his stomach. Fortunately—or not—there was little in it. Saliva mixed with gastric juice trailed from the corners of his mouth.
One, perhaps unable to watch his suffering, came up behind him and rubbed his back. Another, sterner, went to fetch cleaning tools with lips pursed. Two carefree ones leaned over the rail, making conversation about the size of the vanished shark.
Their shorts suited them beautifully. Their matching sailor-collared uniforms, with turned-back cuffs, were charming. All alike. All boys.

source.japanese:
乗せるなら、美しくペンキが塗られニスで綺麗に輝き眩しくワックスに磨かれた、海に浮かべた高級玩具のような船舶にこその者達で、まかり間違ってもこの海上の廃物集積場の如き信天翁号ではあってはならない筈、なのに彼らこそが。
　信天翁号の、実質的作業要員、下級水夫達なのだった。
source.english:
Such boys belonged aboard a vessel beautifully painted, bright with polished varnish and wax: a fine toy afloat on the sea. They ought never, by any mistake, to have been aboard this floating dump, the Albatross. Yet these were—
Her actual working hands. Her junior sailors.

target.text: Meanwhile, Sakuya back on deck─── His bindings were sawed through with a sailor's knife, rope burn was visible on Sakuya's arms and neck and various other places, and the whole thing looked like the indecent evidence of a particular kind of sexual play. As his blood circulation returned to normal, now no longer congested in several places, there was an unbearably itchy pain beneath his skin, and the blood returning to his head left him dizzy, but even so, Sakuya mustered the willpower to express the gratitude he felt to his saviours.
【Naomasa】 「You-, you saved me. Thank you thank you so much guys───」

And that was where he reached his limit. He rushed behind one of the hovels on the deck, then began noisily vomiting up the contents of his stomach, but fortunately, if one could consider it that, there was barely anything left in his stomach, and a trail of drool mixed with gastric juices ran down the corner of his mouth.

Perhaps his suffering was too hard to stomach, for someone approached him from behind and began massaging his back; another was unsparing, pursing their lips as they left to grab a cleaning utensil, and a couple more carefree sorts were leaning over the gunwale, chatting about how the size of the fin of the vanishing shark must have been this big, or that big, or something of the sort. They all looked great in their shorts. Their uniform they'd been provided, the sailor-style collar with the folded cuffs, was lovely. All dressed up the same, in a boy's uniform.

Were you to take them aboard somewhere, it should be on a vessel that was beautifully painted, gleaming with varnish, and polished to a dazzling shine with wax, the highest class of luxury toy to ever float on the seas, and even if by mistake, they should under no circumstances ever be seen aboard this floating junkyard at sea of an Albatross, and yet here they were all the same. They were the actual workforce of the Albatross, the deck boys.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫その一】
「またひどい目に遭ったもんだねえ朔屋さん。
　ほらハンケチ。真水に濡らしてあるから、
　これで口拭うと気持ちいいよ」
source.english:
“They put you through it again, didn't they, Mr. Sakuya?
Here's a handkerchief. It's wet with fresh water.
Wipe your mouth; it'll feel nice.”

target.text: 【Deck boy the First】 「Found yourself in a real pickle again, haven't you, Sakuya-san. Here, a handkerchief. It's moistened with fresh water, so you'll feel better once you wipe your mouth with it.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫その二】
「なんだっていいけどさ、どーせさぼりのお仕置きだろうし。……その吐いたヤツ、ちゃんと後で掃除しといてよ。モップはこっち」
source.english: “Whatever. It was punishment for slacking off anyway, wasn't it? …Clean up that vomit afterward, all right? Here's the mop.”

target.text: 【Deck boy the Second】 「Not like I care about the why. I'm sure this is just punishment for skipping out on work anyways. ……That stuff you just puked up, make sure you clean it later. Mop's over here.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫その三】
「あのサメ、かなり大きかったよ。
　あれぐらいなら、食べでも相当あるんじゃない？」
source.english:
“That shark was pretty big.
One that size would give us plenty to eat, wouldn't it?”

target.text: 【Deck boy the Third】 「That shark was pretty big. A shark that size would make a pretty filling meal, right?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫その四】
「うんうん同感。ね、今だったら、お肉針にかけてさ、ここから垂らしておけば戻ってこないかな。釣れないかな？　厨房から、塩肉のはしっこ、もらってこない？」
source.english: “Yes, exactly. Hey, if we put some meat on a hook and let it down now, would it come back? Could we catch it? Shall we get a scrap of salt meat from the galley?”

target.text: 【Deck boy the Fourth】 「Yep yep, agreed. Hey, if we're quick about it, it might still come back if we put some meat on a hook and dangle it down from here. Wonder if we can fish it up? Can you go bring some scraps of salted meat from the galley?」

source.japanese: 朔屋を労るの、手厳しい小言を浴びせるの、青年には我ら関せずと私事に耽るのと、言葉は様々であったが、喋る口はどれこれも似通っていた。似通う、などといったレヴェルを超えて、この船の下級水夫達は、一つの鋳型から鋳造されたように寸分違わず同じ貌[かお]をしているのである。
source.english:
One offered comfort, another stern reproaches, others engrossed themselves in their own affairs as though the young man were none of their concern. Their words differed. The mouths speaking them all looked alike.
Alike was not sufficient. The Albatross's junior sailors had precisely the same face, as though cast from a single mold.

source.japanese:
初めて朔屋が彼らを目にしたのは、並んで索具の整理していた二人の下級水夫の、双子かと勘違い、航海士も双子なら下級水夫もそうなのか、さして珍しいものではといえ、二揃いというのは珍しい、とてデッキブラシで甲板掃除の午後の陽の下、鼻歌まじりに舷側まで流して折り返したところで鉢合わせしそうに、それがまた別の下級水夫、なのに。
　これもまったく同じ貌[かお]をしており、三つ子か、とまでは発想の飛躍でもなかろうが、後から一人また一人と出てきた水夫達、みんな判子で捺したように顔が同じなのには思考が停止した。
　五つ子六つ子というのも聞いた事はある、あっても───まだ出てくるとあっては。
source.english:
The first time Sakuya saw them, he found two junior sailors lined up sorting the rigging and took them for twins: so the mates were twins and the junior hands were too? Twins were nothing so very rare, granted, but two sets aboard one ship was unusual. Then one afternoon, humming as he scrubbed the deck and worked his way out to the side before turning back, he almost ran headlong into another junior sailor—and yet.
This one had exactly the same face.
Triplets? That was hardly so extravagant a leap; but when one sailor after another emerged behind him, every last face alike as impressions from the same seal, his thoughts came to a halt.
One heard of quintuplets, sextuplets, even. But—even then—there were more.

source.japanese: 朔屋とぶつかりそうになった下級水夫は、初めそんな彼を不審そうな顔で見上げたが、ああ、と得心して手を打った。
source.english: The sailor who had nearly collided with him first looked up suspiciously. Then he understood, said ah, and clapped his hands.

target.text: Whether it was nursing Sakuya with kindness, showering him in harsh reprimands, or indulging in personal matters as though entirely indifferent to the young man's plight, their way of speaking was greatly similar. They had long left the realm of close resemblance, the deck boys of this ship, for their faces looked so exactly alike, it was as if they had all been cast from the very same mold.

When Sakuya first laid eyes upon them, he had thought that the two deck boys standing next to each other while performing maintenance on some rigging had to be twins, there was no doubt in his mind, for if the mates could be twins, then why could two deck boys not be? It wasn't said to be that rare, although two pairs was a bit unusual, but then, when he was cleaning the deck with a deck brush under the afternoon sun, humming a tune, as he made to turn around after reaching the bulwark, he was just about to bump into somebody, and that somebody turned out to be another deck boy, and yet.

He, too, had the exact same facial features; triplets perhaps, that wouldn't be a leap in logic, not really, but one after the other, more deck boys came, all of them with the exact same faces like it had been pressed on them with a stamp, and his thoughts came to a screeching halt. He had heard of quintuplets or sixtuplets, he had───but yet more still came.

When the deck boy about to collide headfirst with Sakuya looked up at him, it was with eyes full of such distrust at first, but then, with a little "aah" of comprehension, he clapped his hands together.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「僕達のこと、気になる？」
source.english: “Curious about us?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それはどうしたって……兄弟かなんかか？
　いやでも、双子、三つ子くらいならあるだろうが、ここまでみんな同じ顔と背丈ってのは……」
source.english:
“How could I not be…? Are you brothers or something?
I mean, twins, triplets, that happens. But for all of you to have the same face and height…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Are you curious about what's going on with us?」

【Naomasa】 「Well, there's only really one option… …you're all siblings or something? No, but even then, twins, or triplets, that might be possible, but for this many of you to have the same face and height, that would mean……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「違うよ」
source.english: “No.”

source.japanese: あっさり否定されて朔屋はいよいよ困惑する。無理もあるまい。金太郎飴だって、切ったところで微妙に顔が違う。それがこうも同じ顔が次から次へでは、誰だって自分の目を疑いたくもなろう。赤の他人でここまでの相似は有り得ず、果たしてどう説明をつけてくれるものやら待ち受ける彼へ、下級水夫がこともなげに言い放ったというのが、
source.english:
That easy denial left Sakuya still more confused. Naturally. Even the little Kintaro faces in a stick of candy varied a little from slice to slice. With the same face appearing over and over like this, anyone would begin to doubt his eyes. Unrelated people could never resemble one another so perfectly.
He waited to hear how they would explain it. The junior sailor spoke as though it were nothing.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あまり深く考えこまないでよ。
　僕達、そういうモノなんだ、ってこと」
source.english:
“Don't think too hard about it.
We're just that sort of thing.”

source.japanese: これである、これだけである。とはいえ少々のもっともらしい言説では受け入れられたかどうかはあやふやで、謎は謎のままに朔屋はそういうモノなのかと頷[うなず]くしかなかった。物怪顔で。
source.english:
That was it. All of it. Yet a plausible little explanation might not have persuaded him, either. The mystery remained a mystery. He could only nod, looking bewildered.
That sort of thing, then.

source.japanese: 更に朔屋は思い当たる。今彼は『僕たち』と言うたが、それはきっと……この信天翁号の下級水夫達は、全員同じ外見を共有しているということなのではなかろうか。よくよく見れば船のあちこちで小鳥廻しに立働いている下級水夫達まで顔みな同じと悟ると、朔屋の物怪顔、余計に深くなる。
source.english:
Another thought occurred to him. The boy had said ‘we.’ Surely that meant… every junior sailor aboard the Albatross shared the same appearance?
Looking closely, he realized that the little sailors flitting busily about elsewhere on the ship all had the same face, too. His bewilderment deepened.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「We aren't.」

Having been so easily denied, Sakuya grew more and more perplexed. It was no great wonder. Even a long stick of Kintarou candy would have subtle differences between the faces where it was cut. So for the same face to keep showing up like this, one after the other, it would surely drive anybody to doubt their own eyes. It was impossible to resemble a stranger this closely, and so, as he waited, wondering how exactly they intended to explain this away, what the deck boy nonchalantly declared to him was:
【Deck boy】 「Don't think too hard about it. That's just the way we are.」

That was it, that was all it was. However, while it was uncertain if a slightly more plausible explanation would have been easier to swallow, with the mystery remaining a mystery, all Sakuya could do was nod in return and accept that it simply was what it was. A look of blank amazement on his face.

Another thing came to Sakuya's mind. He had just said "we", so that surely meant……perhaps it was possible that all the deck boys of the Albatross shared the same features? When, upon closer inspection, Sakuya came to the realization that even the other deck boys fluttering about like busy little birds all around the ship as they attended to their tasks also all shared the same face, the amazement on his face only deepened.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ま、これからよろしくね。
　あ、君、僕と交替だよね。
　後、よろしく」
source.english:
“Well, here's to working together.
Oh, you're relieving me, aren't you?
I'll leave the rest to you.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Well, it's a pleasure to have you aboard, yeah? Ah, you there, you're my relief, right? Take care of the rest.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「はーい。君、後は休憩？
　ゆっくり休んでて」
source.english:
“Right. Are you on a break now?
Have a good rest.”

source.japanese: 朔屋と話していた水夫の背後から、また一人下級水夫が現れる、仕事を交替する。交替といっても同じ顔なのだから替わった気がしない。どうやら不条理は不条理として呑みこむしかなさそうだが、
source.english: Another junior sailor appeared behind the one speaking to Sakuya and took over his work. Since the faces were identical, it did not feel as though anyone had changed. Apparently the absurdity had to be swallowed whole. But—

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Riiight. Are you on break after? Make sure you take your time to get some proper rest.」

From behind the sailor Sakuya was speaking with, yet another deck boy appeared, the new arrival relieving the old. A relief of duty, yes, but they shared the same face, so it didn't feel like anything had changed. It seemed he was left with no choice but to accept the absurdity as just that, but,
【Naomasa】 「……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「すぐに慣れるよ」
source.english: “You'll get used to it soon.”

source.japanese: 朔屋の憮然とした胸の裡を汲[く]み取ったか、容易そうに告げたが、そうだろうかと甲板を透かし見れば、手を止めこちらの様子をうかがっている水夫がやっぱり皆して、同じ顔とくる。
source.english: Perhaps the boy understood his discontent. He said it so easily. Would he, though? Sakuya looked across the deck. The sailors who had paused in their work to watch them all had the same face, of course.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「You'll get used to it soon enough.」

Perhaps sensing the astonishment swirling within Sakuya's heart, he said it like it was so simple; I don't know about that, Sakuya thought as he ran his eyes over the deck, and there, sure enough, the other sailors who had stopped what they were doing and were keeping an eye on what was going on with him shared the exact same face.

source.japanese: どうしたって超現実的な光景と言う他なく、信天翁号は下級水夫までも変物揃いなのだった。
source.english: There was no other word for the sight: surreal. Even the Albatross's junior hands were an assortment of oddities.

source.japanese:
……今だって完全に慣れきった訳ではなく、溢血死寸前、鱶に囓られるかどうかの境まで追いこまれた後では、下級水夫達の一揃えの顔には見当識が揺らいで足元が怪しくなりかかる。
　海に落ちる陽差しもぎらぎら、波間に乱反射して、目に油を垂らしたように灼いてきて朔屋の神経を逆撫でに、不快感募るばかりで、下甲板の薄暗がりが今は恋しい。手近な索具にすがって立ち上がり、朔屋は退散する事にした。
source.english:
…He had still not grown entirely used to it. After nearly bleeding to death and nearly being eaten by a shark, he found the matching faces unsettling his sense of where he was. His footing began to feel doubtful.
Sunlight glittered fiercely on the sea, scattered by the waves, burning his eyes as though someone had poured oil into them. It scraped at his nerves. His discomfort grew, and he longed for the dimness below. He pulled himself up by a convenient piece of rigging and decided to retreat.

target.text: This could, assuredly, only be described as a most surreal of sights, and even the deck boys of the Albatross were eccentric, one and all.

……Even now, he still hadn't grown completely used to it, and on the verge of dying from a hemorrhage, right after being pushed to the point of being genuinely worried that he would be gnawed on by a shark, the uniform faces of the deck boys left him disoriented, footing on the verge of becoming perilous. The sunlight falling on the sea was also glaring, reflecting diffusely on the waves, and it burned Sakuya's eyes like someone had dripped oil on them, irritating his nerves, discomfort only growing, so right now, he just yearned for the dim light below decks. Leaning on some nearby rigging, Sakuya stood up, then made his retreat.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫その二】
「ああもう朔屋さんてば、ゲロ掃除は？」
source.english: “Oh, come on, Mr. Sakuya. What about your vomit?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「悪いな、後でやるよ。ちょっと今は無理。
　立ってるだけで反吐を追加しそう」
source.english:
“Sorry. I'll do it later. I can't right now.
Just standing here makes me feel like adding more.”

target.text: 【Deck boy the Second】 「Aah, come on, Sakuya-san, what happened to cleaning up the vomit?」
【Naomasa】 「Sorry, I'll do it later. I just can't do it right now. Just standing up is enough to make me nauseous again.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫その一】
「大丈夫……？　もう、仕方ないな。
　僕、この人下まで送ってくから、
　ちょっと離れるよ」
source.english:
“Are you all right…? Oh, honestly.
I'll take him below, then.
I'll be away a moment.”

target.text: 【Deck boy the First】 「Are you okay……? Boy, you're hopeless. I'll escort this guy down below, so I'll be gone for a bit.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫その三】
「水夫長にめっからないようにねぇ～」
source.english: “Don't let the bosun catch you!”

source.japanese: 顔は同じでも、朔屋への対応は三者三様、下級水夫達はそれぞれに微妙な個性を有しているらしく、新米の青年へ親和的なのもいてくれるのが有りがたい、有り難さに甘えて、朔屋は差し延べられた少年の手に頼り下甲板、船内通路へと。善光寺には牛に曳かれて参り、信天翁号の腹の中には風変わりな水夫の手に助けられ降りていく、地獄の中にも優しい手というのはあるようだ。
source.english:
Their faces were the same, but their reactions to him differed. Apparently each sailor had his own slight individuality. He was grateful that some were friendly to the newcomer. Relying on that kindness, he took the offered hand and went below, into the passage.
A cow might lead one to Zenkoji Temple. A strange sailor's helping hand led him into the belly of the Albatross. Even in hell, it seemed, there were gentle hands.

target.text: 【Deck boy the Third】 「Make sure the Bosun doesn't catch you, 'kay～」

Their faces were the same, but their treatment of Sakuya differed entirely between the three of them, so it did seem like the deck boys each had their own subtle idiosyncrasies, and he was grateful that friendliness towards the newcomer also counted amongst said quirks; presuming upon his kindness, Sakuya relied on the boy's outstretched hand as he went below decks, into the passageways.

Led by an ox he went to Zenkouji: down the belly of the Albatross he descended, helped along by the hand of the peculiar sailor; it seemed kind hands could be found even in hell. (TN: 善光寺には牛に曳かれて参り, as it is written here, is a Japanese proverb originating from the tale of (abbreviated) an old, greedy woman chasing an ox to Zenkouji temple, where she then undergoes a spiritual awakening. It means being led into a good situation or in the right direction by chance, what is also known as serendipity in English.)

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「え、や、ちょっと、
　なにするの、朔屋さん───」
source.english:
“Huh—no, wait,
what are you doing, Sakuya—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、ちょっと、そのなんだ。
　立ちくらみが来て」
source.english:
“No, wait, um, you see.
I’m feeling a little lightheaded.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Eh, sto-, wait, what are you doing, Sakuya-san───」
【Naomasa】 「Well, you know, just got a little dizzy.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「それは大変だと思うけど、
　なんで僕のこと、抱っこするのさ。
　あ、そんなにぎゅっとしないでよぅ……」
source.english:
“I get that it’s rough,
but why’re you holding me like this? Hey,
don’t squeeze so tight…”

source.japanese: 出港時には船内の、埃や煤を隅々から叩き出すくらいにけたたましかった機関部からの震動は、海に出てしまえば唸りを緩めて、何枚もの布地を隔てたようにくぐもった。あれほど五月蝿かったのが、こうなってみると放課後の校庭から教室へ、カーテン越しに漏れ伝わる野球団の掛け声と同じく、遠くて穏当で、安心感さえもたらして、こんな襤褸船でも動いている機関というのはいいと、ちょっとだけ信天翁号に親しみさえ覚えてしまう。
source.english: At departure the engine room’s roar had been so deafening it seemed to shake every last speck of dust and soot from every corner of the ship, but once out at sea the vibration eased, muffled as if by layers of cloth. What had been such a racket now felt like the baseball team’s cheers leaking through the curtains from the schoolyard into the classroom after class—distant, gentle, even reassuring. It made him think that even on a ragged ship like this, an engine that keeps her moving is a good thing, and he found himself feeling a little fond of the Albatross.

source.japanese: ましてや、朔屋が今引っこんでいる、船内通路の奥まった、階段下の暗がりの具合良さといったら穴熊が土中の巣に集めた枯葉の上でとぐろを巻くのと似通って、こんな隙間を蔵しているのならと、なんと朔屋でさえも、信天翁号の事がちょっぴり好きになってしまいそうだった。
source.english: Better still was the snugness of the dark nook beneath the stairs, tucked away deep in the passage where Sakuya had now holed up: it was like curling into the dead leaves a badger had gathered in its burrow. If the ship held crannies like this, why, even Sakuya might find himself growing just a little fond of the Albatross.

source.japanese:
こういう場処には一人籠もって孤独の快味を噛み締めるのもよろしいが、朔屋にとってもっと好ましいのは抱き心地よく良い匂いする娘とひたり密着している事。
　朔屋が抱きすくめている体は、やや生硬なきらいはあったが、たまには味というものであり、匂いに関しては申し分ない。
source.english:
A place like this was well suited to shutting oneself away and savoring the pleasure of solitude. Sakuya, however, preferred to press himself close against a girl who smelled wonderful and felt good in his arms.

After looking all around, she finally recognized her surroundings. At once her eyes clouded, like polished obsidian rubbed with a file. Her lovely lips crumpled before him. Sakuya felt oddly, grievously betrayed, and lost the thread of what to say.

target.text: When she stopped talking and surveyed her surroundings, the black hair that spilt from her shoulders shimmered with a gloss even in this dim light, and whenever it flowed and rippled, it was as though it were accompanied by the sound of celestial nymphs ringing their heavenly bells, chiming from between the stars of a clear night sky, ephemeral and faint as it reached the surface, such was its beauty.

Her roving eyes, the same shade as her hair, held a keen intellect, with a sharp, clear gaze, suggesting a vast and profound soul. This girl was───a doll-like delicacy coexisting with a vivacious, vibrant vitality: she possessed an exquisite beauty. As for her age, she was like a flower on the cusp of blossoming, blessed with a beauty that can only be found at that stage of development, while at the same time, she offered a glimpse, the promise of a wonderful future to come; this, too, a most sublime season of life in its own right.

She could well be said to be the sort of rare beauty the likes of which Sakuya had never even laid eyes on before, and yet. After scanning her surroundings, the scene finally registered in her mind; her eyes clouded over, dulling like the surface of filed-down obsidian, and he saw how her beautiful lips were suddenly squashed together; Sakuya was seized by some immense feeling of profound betrayal, and he couldn't find the words to continue their conversation.

source.japanese:
【娘】
「え。やだ、まさか。
　また───だったりする？」
source.english:
“Huh? No.
Surely not. Not… again?”

source.japanese: そう問いかけられたところで、異次元の言語を聞かされたように意味不明で、首を傾げた朔屋に畳みかけた声までもが歪んで聞き苦しい。
source.english: That question meant no more to him than a language from another dimension. He tilted his head. The voice that pressed him further was distorted now, unpleasant to hear.

target.text: 【Girl】 「What. Oh no, there's no way. Again───is it happening again?」

When he was poised that question, her words sounded as incomprehensible as a language from another dimension to his ears; even the voice bearing down on Sakuya, his head tilted in confusion, sounded warped, was unpleasant to hear.

source.japanese:
【娘】
「ちょっと君、この船、
　船名はもしかしてもしかすると……？」
source.english:
“Hey. This ship.
Is its name, by any possible chance…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「信天翁号って言うんだが……。
　いやだから、君こそ───」
source.english:
“It's called the Albatross…
But, look, who are you—?”

source.japanese: 誰だ一体と、続けようとした声音は上から覆い被さってきた娘の悲鳴に圧殺された。
source.english: He meant to finish the question. Her scream fell over his voice and crushed it.

target.text: 【Girl】 「Hey, you, this ship. Would the name of this ship by any chance happen to be……?」
【Naomasa】 「She's called the Albatross, but……. No, listen, who in the───」
"hell are you?", but as it tried to continue his question, his voice was smothered beneath the scream from that girl crashing down onto him from above.

source.english: “…Hh… Hh…”

source.japanese:
【娘】
「いやあーーーーーーっ」
source.english: “Nooooooo!”

source.japanese:
【娘】
「なんでまたこの船!?
　こんな半腐れの、悪魔のゴミ溜めの、
　懲罰大隊水上駐屯基地の、
　乗りこむ者皆希望を捨てよの、
　地獄みたいな船になんでまた私」
source.english:
“Why this ship again!?
This half-rotten devil's garbage heap,
this floating base for a penal battalion,
this ‘abandon all hope, ye who board her’ hell of a ship!
Why am I here again?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「その喩えには凄え同意するんだが、
　乗りこんだ後になって何を今さら」
source.english:
“I agree with all those descriptions,
but isn't it a bit late to notice after you've come aboard?”

target.text: 【Girl】 「……Nh, …………nー」
【Girl】 「NOOOOOーーーーーー」

【Girl】 「Why this ship AGAIN!? Why this half-rotten, Devil's dunghill of a waterborne penal battalion garrison where all ye who board here, abandon all hope, why am I on this living hell of a ship again?」
【Naomasa】 「I am in complete agreement with your choice of comparison, but it's a bit late to only realize that AFTER boarding the ship.」

source.japanese:
【娘】
「だって私、乗りこむ時は、港の倉庫の、
　貨物の中に隠れるのが普通だもの。
　積み込み先なんて、
　予想どおりに行く方が少ない───」
source.english:
“But I usually hide in cargo
in a harbor warehouse when I board.
It hardly ever
gets loaded where I expect—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……おい。
　今なんつったあんた」
source.english:
“…Hey.
What did you just say?”

source.japanese: 正体不明だった、娘の素性はぼんやりと、彼女が迂闊にも漏らした言葉によっていくらか定まって、現れつつある輪郭に、朔屋は大いに戸惑い、彼女をどう処したものだか考えあぐねる。きっとこの娘は、多分。
source.english: The girl's identity had been obscure. Now her careless words gave it a little definition. As its outline emerged, Sakuya was thoroughly perplexed, unsure what to do with her. Surely she was. Probably.

target.text: 【Girl】 「Well, I mean, when I board a ship, I almost always hide in a port warehouse, somewhere inside the cargo. The destination though, let's just say it's rare for things to go according to plan there───」
【Naomasa】 「……Oi. What was that just now?」

The girl's identity was an unknown, but through the words the woman had so carelessly divulged, her background could be determined, if only vaguely, and Sakuya was left greatly confused at the outline taking shape bit by bit; he racked his brain trying to figure out how to deal with this woman. This girl had to be, probably.

source.japanese:
【娘】
「……え？　私なにか言ったかな。
　もし何か聞こえたとしても、それは君の、
　そ・ら・み・み」
source.english:
“…Huh? Did I say something?
If you thought you heard anything,
you were i-mag-in-ing it.”

source.japanese: あれだけはっきり口にしておいて、今更濁しようもあるまいに、白々しく目を逸らす娘に朔屋は、カマをかけてみる。
source.english: She had said it clearly enough. There was no blurring it now. As she pointedly looked away, Sakuya tried to draw her out.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ええと、なんだったかな。
　み……？　ええと、
　みっ───」
source.english:
“…Um, what was it?
St…? Let's see.
St—”

target.text: 【Girl】 「……Huh? I wonder, did I actually say anything? If you happened to hear anything, that was just your i-ma-gi-na-tion.」

After having stated it so clearly, there was really no possible way the waters could be muddied here, but the girl feigned ignorance while averting her eyes, and so Sakuya decided to ask her a leading question.
【Naomasa】 「……Uuuhm, what's it called again? Sto……? Hmm, stooo───」

source.japanese:
【娘】
「あはははやだ、
　誰が密航者だなんてそんな」
source.english:
“Ahahaha, no,
who said anything about a stowaway?”

source.japanese:
カマなど、かけるのも馬鹿馬鹿しいくらい、娘はいとも簡単にその言葉を口にして、あっと噤んだけれどもう遅い、酒の瓶はひっくり返って全部零れ、羊はみんな厩舎から逃げ出して、林檎は台風で全滅、二人の間の背景は、下手くそな劇画家が描いたようにぐしゃぐしゃとデッサンが崩壊した。
　朔屋は有りもしない煙草を盛大に吹かすふりして、すっぱーと、憮然と言葉を吐き出した。
source.english:
Trying to draw her out was almost silly. She gave him the word so easily. Then she gasped and shut her mouth, but too late. The bottle had overturned and all the liquor spilled; every sheep had fled the stable; the typhoon had wiped out the apples. The background between them collapsed into the botched drawing of an inept comics artist.
Sakuya made a grand show of smoking a nonexistent cigarette. He blew an imaginary cloud and spoke with displeasure.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───俺はただ、みっ……か前の晩飯はなんだったかと思い出そうとしていただけなんだが。
　そうかそうか。君が密航者という生き物か」
source.english:
“—Still trying to remember what I had for dinner three nights ago. That's all I was going to say.
But I see, I see. You're one of those creatures called stowaways.”

target.text: 【Girl】 「Ahahaha, come now, there are no stowaways here, no way.」

Even for a leading question, it was ridiculously blatant, but the girl still said the word so easily, and even should she try to keep silent, it was too late now: the bottle of booze had toppled over and everything was wet, all the sheep had escaped from the stable, the apple trees had been destroyed by the typhoon, and the backdrop between the two broke down into a sloppy dessin like something drawn by the clumsy hand of a lousy manga artist, then crumbled away. Sakuya pretended to take a deep drag from an imaginary cigar, then blew out his disappointed response.

【Naomasa】 「───Now, I was just trying to remember if it was a cup of sto……ne-ground matcha I had before dinner the other day. I see, I see. So you're one of these creatures we call stowaways, are you?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ちが……私はその、自由な旅人っていうか」
source.english: “No, I'm… More of a free traveler.”

source.japanese: 朔屋は今になって段差から這い出したのだが、娘は完全に逃れる機を見失い、進み出た青年に気圧されてとすんと腰を落としてじりじりと、下がったところで通路に置かれた雑物入れに背を阻まれる。なおも後退ろうとばたばた、足は床を蹴って空しい。
source.english: Sakuya only now climbed out of the lowered section. The girl had completely missed her chance to escape. Overawed by his advance, she dropped onto her backside and edged backward. A storage box in the passage blocked her retreat. She kept trying anyway, her feet scuffling uselessly against the floor.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺も自由気侭なモラトリアムのつもりだったんだけどな、この船に徴用されて来、自由なんて言葉は空の彼方に飛んでった」
source.english: “I thought I was taking a free and easy break from life, too. Ever since I got pressed into this ship, the word ‘free’ has flown clean over the horizon.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まあ君、こんなところで押し問答してたって仕方ないやな。ほら、しゃんと立ちなよ───」
source.english: “Well, there's no point arguing here. Come on, stand up properly—”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「That's not……I'm just, uhh, a free-spirited traveller?」

Sakuya had now crawled out of the indentation, the girl had completely let her chance to escape pass her by, and overwhelmed by the intensity coming from the looming young man, she fell back onto her butt with a thump, but when she tried to slowly scoot back, she found her retreat obstructed by one of the chests containing various junk placed in the passageways. For all that she tried to retreat further, her feet just kicked against the floor in vain.

【Naomasa】 「I also believed myself unfettered, free to drift through life for a while yet, but ever since being pressed into service on this ship, words like "freedom" became but a distant memory, flying off into the horizon.」
【Naomasa】 「Well, not much point arguing back and forth here. Come on, stand up straight───」

source.japanese: 朔屋にしてみたところでこの船の二等航海士、いな今ではそれ以下の扱い、密航者を勝手に処断する権利もなく、水夫長かシサムキサラの判断を仰ごうと、とにかく娘を連れて行こうとしただけ、なのに。娘の顔は音を立てて引きつった。大きく息を吸いこんで、たっぷり溜めを造ってのびのびと、娘の口から伸びあがった台詞が朔屋の頬を叩きつける。
source.english:
Sakuya was only the ship's second mate—no, by now he was treated as less than that. He had no authority to decide what to do with a stowaway on his own. He merely intended to take the girl to the boatswain, or to Sisam and Kisara, and let them decide.
Yet her face drew tight with an almost audible snap. She took a deep breath, paused at length, and let the words rise from her mouth to slap him across the cheeks.

target.text: From Sakuya's point of view, as a second mate of this ship, no, right now he was treated as something below that, he did not have the authority to autocratically hand down a sentence to this stowaway, and he was going to go ask the Bosun or Shisamu and Kisara for their judgment; at any rate, he was going to drag this girl with him, and yet. The girl's face convulsed audibly, she took a deep breath, let out a long, unrestrained sigh, and then the words leaping out from the girl's mouth slammed against Sakuya's cheek.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「許してやめてひどい事しないでーっ」
source.english: “Spare me! Stop! Don't do horrible things to me!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Forgive me please stop don't do anything horrible to meeeー」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「阿片漬けにされて娼館に売っ払われるっ。
　足の腱を切られて逃げ出せないようにしてから、悪者達に払い下げられるっ。
　ペヨーテでらりらりにされて、太陽の神様に心臓と生き血を生贄にされるーっ」
source.english:
“You'll drug me with opium and sell me to a brothel!
Cut the tendons in my legs so I can't run, then sell me to villains!
Get me high on peyote and sacrifice my heart and living blood to the sun god!”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「来ないで寄らないで鬼悪魔罰当たり、ついでに男色家、触られただけで何かがうつるぅぅ……」
source.english: “Don't come near me, you monster, you devil, you wicked—sodomite, too! I'll catch something if you so much as touch me…!”

source.japanese: この時朔屋が押し出した母音はくぐもって、正確に表記するなら濁点が必要だったろう、それくらい、地獄の底から響いたように暗く危険な声音だった。
source.english: The vowel Sakuya produced was thick and muffled. To write it accurately, one would have needed some special mark of harshness. It was that dark, that dangerous: a voice rising from the bottom of hell.

source.japanese: ……かつてとある港に、海難事故に遭い航行能力を失った一隻の船が曳航されてきた事がある。乗員乗客はほぼ全員無事だったけれど、曳航される間にただ一人、行方不明者が発生していた。船室には遺書の類はなかったものの、争った形跡もなく、運悪く海に落ちたのだろうと処理された。ただその行方不明者の男は、室内に一枚の洋画を残していて、これは紆余曲折を経て、首都の公立美術館に渡る事となる。一時は公開されていたのだが、その期間は短く打ち切られ、収蔵庫に収められたまま封印されるに至ったという、曰く付きの絵画がある。
source.english:
…Once, a ship disabled in an accident at sea was towed into a certain port. Nearly all her crew and passengers were safe; yet during the tow, one man disappeared. No suicide note was found in his cabin, nor was there any sign of a struggle, and the matter was put down to an unlucky fall overboard.
The missing man left behind one Western-style painting. After sundry vicissitudes, it came into the possession of a public museum in the capital. The museum exhibited it briefly, then closed the display; ever since, the picture had remained sealed in storage. It was a work with a sinister history.

source.japanese:
遺した画家というのは怪奇と幻想をカンバスに具象化することに心血を注いだ男であり、その厭人癖と癇の強さが災いし、人の血を使って絵を描いていると口さがない噂を立てられたものだが、調査の結果少なくとも現存している彼の絵画は、希少ではあるにせよ、まっとうな顔料が用いられていることが判明した。
　それでも、件の洋画の封印がこの先解かれる事はない。
source.english:
The painter had devoted himself to giving horror and fantasy concrete form on canvas. His misanthropy and violent temper did him no favors. Malicious rumors arose that he painted with human blood. Investigation showed, however, that at least his surviving works used legitimate pigments, rare though some might be.
Even so, the seal on that particular painting would never be broken.

source.japanese: 人の生き血云々は噂好きな市民の捏造としても、洋画が展示されている間、原因不明の行方不明事件が館内で頻発したのは、紛れもない事実だったから。
source.english: Even if the story of living human blood was only an invention of gossiping citizens, people had repeatedly vanished from the museum for no known reason while the painting was on display. That was indisputable.

source.japanese:
洋画の表題は、『影中の男』。
　表題に反して、白無地の背景に、俯き加減の黒衣の男が佇んでいるという画で、一説には洋画家の自画像だったともされるが、その人物像から漂う陰鬱で滅滅とした気配たるや、鑑賞する者を軽い鬱病に落としこんだ事すらあったとか。洋画家は一種の天才だったのだろう。
　この画から、黒衣の男が消えて白無地の背景だけとなる日があったという。それが、館内で行方不明者が出た日と重なったのは、偶然に過ぎないのかも知れない。館内を巡回する警備員達が、行方不明になる娘たちは皆、事件の日に黒衣の男と語らっているところを見たというのも、単なる偶然なのかも知れない。
　いずれにしても、件の洋画の封印がこの先解かれる事は、ない。
source.english:
The painting was titled The Man in the Shadows.
Contrary to the title, it showed a black-clad man standing against a plain white background, his head slightly bowed. Some thought it a self-portrait. The figure's bleak, oppressive gloom had supposedly driven some viewers into mild depression. The painter must have been a genius of a kind.
There were days, it was said, when the man disappeared from the canvas, leaving only the white background. Those days coincided with disappearances in the museum. Perhaps that was merely chance. The guards who patrolled the galleries reported seeing the girls who went missing talking to a man in black on the day they vanished. Perhaps that, too, was merely chance.
Whatever the case, the painting would never again be unsealed.

source.japanese:
そして密航者の前に立ち尽くす朔屋から今、件の洋画内の男が漂わせていたのと同質の気配が発せられていたのだった───
　人間には誰しも触れられたくない精神的外傷というのがあり、まして朔屋のそれは、抉られたばかりで傷痕も生々しい。そんなモノに触れられては、朔屋ならずとも『影中の男』と同じになったろうとも。
　陰の気は密航者の四肢に絡みつき、自由を奪ったそこへ飛びかかり、朔屋が己の影のうちに娘を呑みこんでいく様、まさしく『影中の男』が犠牲者を捕らえた瞬間と異ならず。
source.english:
And now Sakuya, standing over the stowaway, gave off the selfsame aura as the man in that painting—
Every human being has some wound of the spirit he cannot bear to have touched. Sakuya's had only just been gouged open; the scar was raw. Prodded there, anyone might have become another Man in the Shadows.
The dark force wound about the stowaway's limbs and robbed them of motion. Sakuya sprang. As his shadow swallowed the girl, the scene differed not at all from the moment the Man in the Shadows took one of his victims—

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I'm gonna be doped up and sold off to a brothel! The tendons in my feet will be cut so I can't escape, and then I'll be sold for pennies to scoundrels! They'll get me high on peyote, and then my guts and blood will be sacrificed to the Sun Gooodー」
【Stowaway】 「Don't come closer don't approach me you accursed demon devil fiend, and you're also a sodomite! If you touch me, I'm gonna be infected with somethiiiiing……」
【Naomasa】 「──────Ah?」

The vowel that Sakuya squeezed from his throat that moment was muffled, and were one to represent it accurately in writing, it would likely need a voiced consonant, so dark and dangerous was the sound of his voice, as though it sounded from the depths of Hell itself.

……Once upon a time, there was a ship that was towed into a certain port after being involved in a maritime accident and losing its navigational capabilities. Almost all the passengers and crew aboard the ship were uninjured and safe, but while the ship was being towed, a single person had gone missing.

There was no will or any such thing left behind in the cabin, no traces of a fight, and it was treated as the man having fallen into the ocean through a streak of misfortune. But this missing man had left behind a single Western painting in his cabin, and after many twists and turns, it was ultimately handed over to a public art gallery in the capital. For a time, it was put on display, but that exhibition was cut short, and it is said that it remained sealed away in a storage room, a painting with a dark history.

The painter who had left behind this painting as his legacy was a man who poured his heart and soul into embodying the macabre and the fantastic on the canvas; it was said that his misanthropic habits and strong temper had caused his downfall, and there were even malicious rumours of him painting his works of art with human blood, but the results of investigations showed that, as they currently existed, scarce as they were, his paintings were made from entirely respectable paints and pigments. Nevertheless, the seal placed on that particular Western painting will never be lifted hereafter.

Even if the talk of human blood and the like were the fabrications of the gossipy citizenry, the fact that incidents of missing persons with no clear explanation occurred frequently within the gallery while the painting was on display was the undeniable truth.

The title of the Western painting was: 『The Man in the Shadows』 Converse to its title, it was a painting of a man clad in black standing still on a plain white background with a slightly downcast gaze; one theory proposed that this was a self-portrait of the artist, but the air of melancholy and desolation wafting from this human figure even caused some of those who had come to appreciate the painting to fall into a minor depression, or so it was said. This painter of Western art must have been a kind of genius.

It is said that there were days when the man clad in black vanished from the painting, leaving only the blank background. And that this coincided with the days where a disappearance would take place in the gallery could have been nothing more than coincidence. That the security guards patrolling the gallery said that all the girls who had gone missing had mentioned speaking to a man clad in black that very same day, that might be simple happenstance. Regardless, the seal placed on that particular Western painting will, henceforth, never be lifted.

And from Sakuya, who stood stock-still before the stowaway, there emanated the same kind of aura that the man in the aforesaid painting had exuded─── People have mental traumas that they do not wish for any other to touch upon; all the more so in Sakuya's case, whose scars of emotional pain were still freshly gouged. Were one to touch upon such, even the likes of Sakuya would end up just like 『The Man in the Shadows』

The sinister Qi of Yin coiled around the stowaway's limbs, robbing her of her freedom, and as Sakuya pounced upon her, he seemed to be trying to swallow her into his own shadow; indeed, it was no different from the moment 『The Man in the Shadows』 captured his victims.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「誰が男色野郎だ馬鹿ーーっっ。
　よりにもよってそんなこと言い出すなんて、
　お前あれか、そんななりしてほんとは男の子かッ」
source.english:
“Who’s the faggot, you idiot—!!
Of all things, to say something like that— Are you…
what, with that appearance, are you actually a boy?!”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「どうしてそういう話になってるのこれ！
　見て判らない？　私ちゃんと女の子、
　……って、やめてぇぇっ」
source.english:
“How did this even happen?!
Can’t you tell just by looking? I’m definitely a girl,
…Wait, stop itttt!”

source.japanese:
確かに密航者は、タイトなラインのブラウスにベスト、膝丈までのズボン、装飾らしい装飾はリボンタイだけの、山歩きにでも出かけようかという軽快な衣装だったけれど、乳房の膨らみ腰から腿[もも]への魅惑的な曲線と、その性別を見誤る人間はなんらかの認識異常者くらいだろう。
　しかし朔屋は。
