　私この船大好き。
　自分の心臓みたいに愛してる。
　だから、ちょっと次の港まで乗せてって、
　そこで下ろしてくれると嬉しいかなー、
　なんて」
source.english:
“Huh…?
No, that's not true.
Figure of speech!
I love this ship. Love her like my own heart.
So, um,
take me to the next port and let me off there?
That would be nice…”

source.japanese: 今更取り繕[つくろ]っても、後の祭りだったという。
source.english: Any attempt to patch things up now was too late.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Eh……. Kidding. That was just a figure of speech! I really love this ship! I love it like it's my very own heart. So, if you'd just let me sail with you to the next port, then let me disembark there, I'd be real happy I guess, just kidding!」
Try to smooth things over as she might, that ship had long since sailed.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
『えーやさえーやさ、僕らは陽気な水夫さん。
　今日の獲物はいけない子。
　密航企む女の子ー』
source.english:
“Heave away, heave away, we're jolly sailor boys.
Today's catch is a naughty girl,
A girl who stowed away!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Heave-ho, heave-ho, jolly tars are we. Our prize today's a naughty girl, wicked as can be. A girl who schemes to stow away, skulking on the seaー」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「やーめーてー……っっ」
source.english: “Sto-o-op…!”

source.japanese: 抵抗及ばず哀願聞き入れられず、娘は抵抗するもたちまちのうちに簀巻きにされ、下級水夫たちによって甲板に運び出され───
source.english: Her resistance was useless; her pleas went unheard. Struggling, she was promptly trussed like a bundle and carried onto the deck by the junior sailors—

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Please stooooopー……」

Resistance futile, pleas unheeded: for all she struggled, she was quickly wrapped up in a bamboo mat, then carried to the deck by the deck boys─── (TN: This refers to sumaki, written "簀巻", a form of vigilantism practiced in the Edo period, usually for punishing adultery, which involved wrapping the victim in a bamboo mat before throwing them into a river and watching them drown. In modern use, it doesn't necessarily have to be with a bamboo mat, but the imagery is similar.)

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
『僕らは今日も今日とて荷運び仕事。ちなみに餌は蛆ちゃんの湧いたハードタックに、薄いお塩のおつゆだけー』
source.english:
“We're hauling loads again today.
And what do we get for feed?
Hardtack full of little maggots,
And thin salt soup—that's all!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Heave away today, boys, and haul the cargo 'round. Bargemen on our hardtack, skillygalee to wash it downー」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あーーーー…………っっっ」
source.english: “Aaaaaaah………!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Aaaaーーーー…………」

source.japanese: 歌声に合わせて、海に投げ込まれてしまうのがあっという間の、朔屋には割って入る隙もない。泡だった海面を眺め下ろしつ、慄然となる。幾ら海に出た船の上は半ば治外法権だとはいえ、この発見即処刑というのは苛烈に過ぎないかと水夫長に問いかけた。
source.english: In time with the song, she was tossed into the sea before Sakuya had a chance to intervene. He looked down at the foaming surface and shuddered. Even if a ship at sea did stand halfway outside ordinary law, wasn't discovery followed by instant execution excessively harsh? He put the question to the boatswain.

target.text: Following the cadence of the song, she was tossed into the sea in a flash; Sakuya wasn't even given the time to consider intervening. As he looked down on the foaming surface of the sea, a terror gripped him. Even if a ship at sea was said to practically be in a state of extraterritoriality, he still went to ask the Bosun if this immediate execution upon discovery wasn't a little too severe a reaction.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あのー……いいんですかい、あの子、尻とか丸出しのまんま落ちてっちゃったけど（俺が脱がしたからなんだけど）」
source.english: “Um… is that okay? That girl fell with her butt and all hanging out (though I’m the one who took her clothes off).”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Uhmmmー……is this really fine? That girl just fell down there with her butt completely exposed (well, I'm the one who stripped her).」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「かまうな。あのメス餓鬼はたちが悪くてな。俺らの船に密航しくさっては、そのたんびにこんな筈じゃなかった、話が違うと文句垂れる脳ぐされよ」
source.english: “Never mind her. That brat's a nasty piece of work. Stows away on our ship, then every time she whines that it wasn't meant to be like this, wasn't what she expected. Rotten in the head.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「今まで何回ああやって海に叩っこんだかしらねえが、何でか次の港に入るたんびに、船倉に紛れこんでやがるんだよなあ……」
source.english: “Don't know how often we've thrown her in like that. Somehow, every time we put into another port, she's back in the hold…”

source.japanese: どうやらあの密航者、このはぐれ者揃いの信天翁号の中でも厄介者扱いされているらしかった───
source.english: Apparently even aboard the Albatross, a ship full of misfits, this stowaway was considered a nuisance—

source.japanese: なお密航者だが、朔屋も見ている前で海に逆落としかまされたというのに、いつの間にか船内に舞い戻ってきて食料を漁っているという噂が、何時しか船内にまことしやかに囁かれることになる。
source.english: As for the stowaway, Sakuya had seen her pitched headfirst into the sea. Yet in time, a rumor began to circulate aboard: she had somehow returned and was rummaging for food. It had the ring of truth.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Don't bother with her. That cheeky bitch is a nasty piece of work. Whenever that moron stows away on our ship, all that leaks out of her rotten brain is "Oh, it wasn't supposed to be like this, this wasn't the deal".」
【Bosun】 「I don't know how many times I've tossed her into the sea by now, but for some reason, every time we enter the next port, she somehow manages to slip into the damn hold again……」
Apparently, that stowaway was considered a nuisance, even among this gathering of misfits on the Albatross───

Furthermore, regarding the stowaway: even though Sakuya had seen her be tossed into the sea head first right before his very own eyes, before long, rumours began to circulate throughout the ship of her return, and of how she was scavenging for food; soon enough, those came to be whispered as though credible fact.

source.japanese: 密航者騒動から数日後の事───
source.english: Several days after the affair with the stowaway—

target.text: A few days after the stowaway affair──

source.japanese:
船底の倉庫から機関室へ徹夜で石炭を運びこむ、過酷な労働からようやく解放されて朔屋は文字通りの一息をついていた。
　体全体どこもかしこも煤塗れ、風呂を遣うか、それが叶わないならせめて厨房からお湯と手拭いを借りて体を拭おうか。
　それはなんとも魅惑的な案ではあったが、一旦垢を落としてしまったなら、張り詰めていた糸がたちどころに緩み、水に放りこまれた石より速やかに眠りの中に落ちてしまうだろう。どちらにしてもあまり長くは起きていられない事明らかで、それならば朔屋が選んだのは、まず腹をくちくさせる事だった。
　確かに体中隅々が真綿にくるまれたような疲労にあるけれど、ひどい空きっ腹では夢見にも障ろう。
source.english:
At last released from a brutal night's work carrying coal from the storeroom at the bottom of the ship to the engine room, Sakuya was, quite literally, taking a breath.
Every part of him was coated in soot. A bath? Failing that, perhaps he could borrow hot water and a towel from the galley and wipe himself down.
An enticing idea. But once he washed the grime away, the taut thread within him would immediately slacken. He would sink into sleep faster than a stone dropped in water. He clearly could not stay awake much longer either way. So he chose to fill his belly first.
True, fatigue seemed to swaddle every inch of him in silk wadding. But an empty stomach this bad would trouble even his dreams.

source.japanese: だから朔屋は、水筒と食い物の包みを開いて、食べる前からその美味を思ってほくそ笑んだ。水筒に詰めてあるのは、まだ新しい真水。といって一昨日降った雨を詰めた樽から汲[く]んできたものだが、港を出る時に積み込んだ水はもう臭いがひどくて生では飲めたものでない。流石に酒は監視が厳しく、巧妙に立ち回らないとすぐ露見して制裁なので、今日はこちらで我慢する。
source.english:
He opened his water bottle and his parcel of food, smiling at the taste before he had even begun. The bottle held comparatively fresh water. He had drawn it from a barrel of rain that fell the day before yesterday. The water loaded when they left port already smelled too bad to drink unboiled.
Alcohol was closely watched. Unless he moved with real cunning, any theft was quickly discovered and punished. Today, he would settle for this.

source.japanese: そして食い物は、香草をふんだんに使った上等なサラミのまるごと一本。独特な匂いも食べつけてみると乙なもので、朔屋は早速、樹の根元のごつごつした中に座り心地の良いところを選び、木漏れ日を浴びながらサラミの表を覆う香草の粒を掻[か]き落としにかかった。
source.english: For food, he had a whole fine salami, lavishly seasoned with herbs. Once he grew used to its distinctive smell, it had a particular charm. He promptly chose a comfortable place among the knotted roots of the tree, sat in dappled sunlight, and began scraping herb fragments from the salami's surface.

source.japanese: いつもなら自分の船室に引っこんで秘やかな悦び噛み締めるところ、船底の、息が詰まるように狭苦しい倉庫から抜け出した後では、たとい自分が馴染んだ部屋だろうと、籠もる、というのは暫くは御免蒙りたい朔屋だ。なにしろ船底倉庫はそのどん詰まりともなると、実体は隔壁間の空隙に過ぎず、通り抜けるだけでも困難なのに、左右の壁には火のような蒸気の鉄管が一面にぬたくっているので、手でも足でも触れると最後、大火傷が待ち構えている。その濛々と渦巻く熱気と、舞い散る石炭の粉の中、臨時に吊した二〇〇燭光の赤電球だけを頼りに潜[くぐ]り抜けては詰め込んで運び出してを繰り返すのだから、呼吸困難になるわ目が廻るわ……朔屋と並んで立ち働いた下級水夫達が、これが船の中でも一番二番にきつくて厭な仕事と零したのもなるほどと頷[うなず]かれるところ。
source.english: Ordinarily, he would have withdrawn to his own cabin to savor this private pleasure. But after escaping the suffocating confines of the storeroom at the bottom of the ship, shutting himself away—even in a room he knew and loved—was the last thing Sakuya wanted for a while. For at its farthest reaches the storeroom was no more than a gap between bulkheads, hard enough merely to squeeze through, while both walls were plastered with iron pipes carrying steam hot as fire: brush one with hand or foot and a terrible burn lay waiting. Through that billowing, churning heat and the flying coal dust, with only a makeshift two-hundred-candlepower red bulb to guide him, he had been forced to burrow in, load up, and haul out, over and over, until he could hardly breathe and the world spun around him… Small wonder the lower-ranking sailors who labored beside him called it one of the hardest and most hateful jobs aboard.

source.japanese:
そこから解放された朔屋が、葉擦れの清かなざわめきと木陰の匂いを求めるのも当然と言えた。そう、樹だ。それもちゃんと生きて、青々とした葉を広げたやつだ。船に樹木と来てはいささか奇妙な取り合わせだが、信天翁号のバラックだらけの上甲板の船尾近くには一本の楢の木が生い茂っているのである。仔細を問うのは意味がない。信天翁号だから、としか言いようがなく、船に存在する一々の細かい点を気に病み始めたらきりがない。たとえばこの楢の木のすぐ傍には、朱塗りが禿げて色褪せかかっているが、鳥居さえ立てられているのである。
　樹と鳥居の取り合わせというと樹木信仰だのなんだのと、ほらやはり話がややこしい。
　朔屋もだから取り立てて深くは考えず、木陰の涼しげな空気に火照った肌を冷やしながら、さあ、サラミをがぶり大きく一口───
source.english:
Naturally, he sought the clear rustle of leaves and the smell of shade. Yes, a tree. A living one, spreading green leaves. A tree and a ship made a peculiar combination, but an oak grew near the stern of the Albatross's shack-covered upper deck. There was no point asking for particulars. It was the Albatross. Nothing more could be said. Once one began worrying about every detail aboard, there would be no end to it.
For instance, beside this oak stood even a torii gate, its vermilion paint peeling and faded. A tree and a shrine gate: that suggested tree worship and so forth. See? Complications already.
Sakuya, too, declined to think deeply. The cool air beneath the leaves soothed his overheated skin. Now for one great bite of salami—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いただきまぁ───っぐが!?」
source.english: “Time to ea—Ghh!?”

target.text: Having finally been freed from the grueling labour of carrying coal from the ship's hold to the engine room all night, Sakuya took a very literal breather. His entire body covered in soot, he considered taking a bath, or if that wasn't possible, perhaps he should at least borrow some hot water and a towel from the galley and wipe his body down with it?

Those were certainly very attractive proposals, but once he had gotten the grime off, the thread of tension running through him would slacken all at once, and he'd likely sink into a deep sleep faster than a rock tossed into water. Regardless of what he did, it was clear he wasn't staying up much longer, and if that was the case, Sakuya chose to drive off his hunger first. His body certainly was fatigued, it was like he'd been wrapped up in silk wadding, but a completely empty stomach would probably spoil even his dreams.

Therefore, Sakuya took out his canteen and unwrapped his meal, and even before he ate, he relished in the thought of how delicious it was going to be with a smile. The canteen was full of fresh, clean water. Though with that said, it was water he'd scooped up from a barrel full of rain water that fell the day before yesterday, for the water he'd brought aboard the ship from before they left port was already awfully smelly and could no longer be drunk as was. The alcohol was under tight watch, as one would expect, and if he didn't play his cards right there, it would quickly be discovered and followed by swift punishment, so for today, he would settle for this.

And then, for his food, he had a whole high-quality salami seasoned generously with herbs. Even its unique smell was actually quite appealing once you got used to it, and Sakuya quickly chose a comfortable spot to sit between the gnarled roots of a tree, scraping off the flecks of herbs covering the surface of the salami as he bathed in the sun leaking through the treetop.

Ordinarily, he would seclude himself in his room and take his time to thoroughly chew on this secret pleasure of his, but after escaping from the hold, the bunker so suffocatingly cramped he could scarcely breathe, Sakuya would rather not, for a while, confine himself to a room, even were it his own cabin that he'd grown quite familiar with.

After all, the deepest stretch of the storage in the bottom of the hold was nothing more than a narrow gap between bulkheads; even just squeezing through was difficult enough, but the walls were covered in a meandering mess of iron steam lines, hot like fire to the touch, and were he to brush against them with his arms or legs, he'd come away with large burns for it.

All he could rely on for light while shrouded in the densely curling steam and swirling particles of coal dust was a makeshift 200-candlepower red light bulb strung up to the ceiling as he repeatedly squeezed through, stuffed the coal, hauled it back out, he couldn't breathe, his eyes swam……when the deck boys diligently at work standing next to him grumbled that this was the most gruelling, nastiest work on the ship, or at least second-to-worst, he could only nod in agreement.

And having been freed from that, it could only be considered natural that Sakuya longed for the gentle rustling of the leaves and the scents of the treeshade. Indeed, a tree. There was a living, healthy tree, verdant leaves spread wide. Having a tree on a ship was certainly a slightly peculiar combination, but near the stern of the shack-covered upper deck of the Albatross, a single oak tree thrived.

There is no sense in questioning the particulars. This is the Albatross, that is all one can say, for once you begin to get bothered by every little thing on this ship, it will never end. For instance, right next to this oak tree, a torii stands, the red paint on the wooden archway peeling off and faded. And the combination of a tree and a torii often signifies dendrolatry and the like and───see, I knew it was going to get complicated.

So Sakuya also didn't think particularly deeply on the subject, and while cooling his flushed skin in the refreshing air of the treeshade, it was time, he decided: he sunk his teeth into the salami and took a large bite───
【Naomasa】 「And a thank you for the foo─── GWAH!?」

source.japanese: かぶりつく寸前で、ごん、と脳天に豪い衝撃が叩きつけられて、サラミも水筒も取り落とし、朔屋は甲板に打ちのめされ目の中に火花の弾けるを見る───
source.english: Just before his teeth met it, an enormous thump struck the crown of his head. He dropped both salami and bottle, was knocked flat on the deck, and saw sparks burst before his eyes—

source.japanese: 何事───樹に接した、鳥居の笠木の上から何かが落ちてきたのだ。
source.english: What had happened? Something had fallen from the top beam of the torii beside the tree.

source.japanese: 何物───それは黒い。大きい。そして重い。
source.english: What was it? Black. Large. Heavy.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ってぇ～……なんだよいったい！」
source.english: “Owwww… What the hell!?”

target.text: Just as he was about to chew down─── clonk, the top of his head was struck with a tremendous impact, he dropped both the salami and the canteen, and Sakuya was knocked down on the deck as fireworks exploded behind his eyes───
What could it───something had fallen down from atop the upper lintel of the torii next to the tree.
Who could it───it was black. Big. And heavy.
【Naomasa】 「Ow～……what the hell was that?!」

source.japanese: 幸せの瞬間を邪魔されたうえに脳天が痛いわ舌を噛み損なったわで激怒した朔屋が見出したもの。
source.english: His moment of happiness had been ruined. His head hurt, and he had nearly bitten his tongue. Furious, Sakuya found—

source.japanese: それ。黒く分厚い体躯の、四肢に筋肉満ち満ちて、漆黒の中に白い毛を僅かに、闇の中の雨のように幾筋か散らした毛並み艶々と、双眸は炯々と、宇宙開闢時の炎をそのまま閉じこめたかに、光強かった。
source.english: The thing. A great black bulk of a body, four limbs brimming with muscle; a lustrous, pitch-black coat scattered with a scant few streaks of white, like rain through darkness; and two eyes blazing so fiercely that they seemed to hold, undiminished, the fires from the birth of the universe.
“Huh, a cat…?”

target.text: Not only had it ruined his moment of joy, his head also hurt, he had almost bit his tongue, and while seething, Sakuya noticed it.

That thing. With its black, bulky torso, four limbs packed with rippling muscles, faint whispers of white hair scattered across the jet black fur like streaks of rain in the darkness, giving it a glossy sheen, eyes glowing with a piercing brilliance, as though they held fast the very flames of the universe's creation captured at the dawn of time.
【Naomasa】 「Oh, a cat……?」

Sakuya was glared down by the piercing stare of this black cat as it sat with regal stillness, paws tucked neatly beneath its body in the feline version of a formal sit, its magnificent physique approaching that of a medium-sized dog, and he found himself unable to advance or retreat, body tense and alert. What tremendous dignity and gravitas.

source.japanese:
朔屋はそれ、猫の正座の形に悠然と座る、中型犬に迫ろうかという偉大なる体格の黒猫の、眼光に射すくめられて退くもならず進むもならずの状態で、身を強張らせていた。凄まじいまでの威厳と圧力だ。
　目を逸らしては殺られそうに恐ろしくて、じりじり後退る朔屋の前で黒猫は、大きく伸びしてから彼が取り落とした水筒へと歩み寄り、紐をくわえて青年から遠ざける。次いで、今度はサラミをくわえあげてから水筒まで戻り、悠然と肉の端を噛み始めた、どこまでも落ち着いた物腰で、睥睨する王者の気風さえ漂う。
source.english:
It sat serenely in a cat's upright posture: an enormous black cat, approaching the size of a medium dog. Its gaze pinned Sakuya. Unable to advance or retreat, he stiffened. Such tremendous dignity and force.
He feared that looking away would be fatal and edged backward. The cat stretched at leisure, approached the fallen water bottle, took its strap in its mouth, and dragged it away from him. Then it picked up the salami, returned to the bottle, and began calmly biting at one end. Every movement was composed, with something of a monarch surveying all beneath him.

source.japanese: しかし水のみならず食い物まで奪われた朔屋にとってはどんなに偉そうであろうと猫は猫、人間様の沽券に関わる。基本的に朔屋は犬猫の類にはニュートラルで、好きも嫌いも特にないのだが、この時は喉がひどく渇いており、また疲れ切っていた。
source.english: But it had stolen not only his water but his food. However imposing it looked, a cat was a cat. A human being's pride was at stake. Sakuya was generally neutral toward cats and dogs, neither particularly fond of them nor hostile. At this moment, however, he was terribly thirsty and utterly exhausted.

target.text: Right in front of Sakuya, who was slowly backing away from the cat, afraid he'd be killed if he took his eyes off it, the cat arched its back in a deep stretch, then walked up to the canteen he had dropped, took the string attached to it in its mouth, and then carried it away from the young man. Following that, now it picked up the salami, carried it back to where it had put the canteen, and then began chewing down on one end of the meat leisurely, an utterly relaxed demeanour through and through, exuding the temperament of a contemptuously scowling monarch.

However, deprived of not just his water but even his food, Sakuya cared little for how high and mighty the cat might be, for it was still but a cat, and human dignity was on the line here. Fundamentally, Sakuya was neutral on the subject of cats and dogs. He had no particular preference, but right now, his throat was awfully parched, and furthermore, he was exhausted.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「シッ、猫の食うもんじゃねえぞそれはっ」
source.english: “Shoo! That's not cat food!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Sssst! That's not for cats to eat!」

source.japanese: 邪険に追い払い、取り戻そうとした、瞬間に猫が走った、跳ねた、朔屋と瞬時に交錯する。
source.english: He moved to drive it off and snatch back his property—and in that instant the cat ran, sprang, and flashed past him.

source.japanese:
───朔屋の頬に焼きつく痛み。
　一瞬の交錯で、朔屋の頬に四筋の疵が走っていた。
source.english:
—A burning pain across his cheek.
In that single crossing, four scratches had appeared.

target.text: As he cruelly chased it away and attempted to regain what was his, in but the blink of an eye, the cat ran, jumped, and then crossed paths with Sakuya in a flash.
───Sakuya's cheek burned with severe pain. During their fleeting clash, four bloody furrows had been drawn across Sakuya's cheek.

source.japanese: 瞬時に血が上って、大人げも理性もなくし黒猫を蹴り飛ばそうとした、のだが。
source.english: Blood rushed to his head. Abandoning dignity and reason alike, he tried to kick the black cat away. But—

target.text: Blood welled up immediately, and losing both his maturity and reason, he attempted to kick the cat away, but.

source.japanese:
───暫時後。
　ひっかき疵を片頬どころか全身至る所に増やし、猫の前に本気の土下座をしている朔屋があった。
source.english:
—A little later.
Scratches had multiplied from one cheek to nearly every part of his body. Sakuya was on his knees before the cat, forehead pressed to the deck, bowing in earnest.

target.text: ───A short while later. The scratches were no longer contained to just a single cheek; they had multiplied until they covered him from head to toe, and Sakuya was prostrating himself before the cat with utmost sincerity.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なにをやってんのさ、朔屋」
source.english: “What are you doing, Sakuya?”

source.japanese: たまさかシサム・キサラが通りかかったので、朔屋は人間の意地も尊厳もなく、双子に泣きつく。
source.english: Sisam and Kisara happened to pass. With neither human pride nor dignity, he appealed to them in tears.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ね、姐さん、ひどいんだひどいんですぜそのクソ猫っ。人間の飲み物食い物に手を出して来やがる。俺が注意しようとしたらこのザマだ。なんて凶暴な猫なんだろう。こいつは恐水病にでも罹っているのじゃなかろうか」
source.english: “Ladies, it's horrible! Just horrible! That fucking cat! It went for a human's food and drink. I tried to tell it off, and look what happened. What a vicious cat. Could it have rabies?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわああ俺ちゅーしゃ打たないと死んじまう」
source.english: “Aaaaah, I'll die if I don't get shots!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それはそれとして、この狂猫、
　姐さん自慢の回転式拳銃で、
　がつんとやっちまって下せえ！」
source.english:
“Anyway,
that mad cat—please let it have it
with that revolver you're so proud of!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ほらあの、普段はベッドの枕の下に隠してあるあのごついので！」
source.english: “You know, that big one you usually keep under your pillow!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「What are you up to, Sakuya?」
By coincidence, Shisamu and Kisara passed by, and so Sakuya clung to them in tears, not a shred of human pride or dignity to be found.

【Naomasa】 「N-, nee-san, it's horrible, that damned cat is just terrible! It dares to lay its paws on human food and drink. Just look what happened to me after I tried to warn it. What a ferocious cat, right? For all we know, this beast could even be afflicted with hydrophobia, couldn't it?」 (TN: He's calling her "姐さん" here, which is a respectful way of referring to an elder sister or a young lady. It's commonly used to refer to an older, caring woman with a big-sisterly disposition.)
【Naomasa】 「Waaaaah, if I don't get an injection, I'm gonna die!」
【Naomasa】 「But that aside, nee-san, blast this crazy cat, give it a taste of your prized revolver, please!」
【Naomasa】 「You know, the one you usually hide under the pillow in your bed. That big, bulky thing!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「誰が誰であんたの姐さんかっ」
source.english: “Who are you calling ‘ladies’?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Who the hell are you calling nee-san?!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ちょいとお待ち。
　……なんであんたが、あたしらのコルトの隠し場所、知ってるわけ？」
source.english:
“Just a moment.
…How do you know where we hide our Colt?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんでもなにも。
　そりゃあ……」
source.english:
“What do you mean,
how? Well…”

source.japanese: 双子がたまたま鍵を掛け忘れた晩、二人が当直に出た隙を狙って部屋に忍びこんだ覚えがあるとか、下着を漁りにだったとか、口が裂けても言えず、口ごもりながら、
source.english: He could hardly confess that one night, when the twins forgot to lock their door, he had slipped into their cabin while they were on watch. Still less that he had gone rummaging for underwear. He stumbled over his words.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「女性が拳銃を隠す場所なんてほら、たいがい定まったもんだし」
source.english: “A woman only has so many places to hide a gun, you know.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ふぅん……まあ、それはそれでいいけれど」
source.english: “Hmm… Well, we'll leave that for now.”

source.japanese: いかに黒猫が敵いそうにない相手とはいえ、女に仕返し頼んですがるとはまこと見苦しい限りだが、シサム・キサラは朔屋と黒猫を見比べると───おもむろに叩きつけた。朔屋の額を甲板に。もう一度土下座を強要されて身もだえする朔屋に、
source.english:
Unbeatable though the black cat might be, there could be no more disgraceful spectacle than a man clinging to women and begging them to avenge him. Sisam and Kisara compared Sakuya with the cat—and then, very deliberately, slammed Sakuya's forehead into the deck.
As he writhed, forced once more into full prostration, they told him—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Just a minute there. ……And how, exactly, would you happen to know where I hide my Colt?」
【Naomasa】 「Oh, it's nothing, really. That's just because……」

The twins would occasionally forget to lock their cabin at night, and that he had memories of waiting for a chance where both were out on watch duty at the same time to sneak in, or that he'd rummaged through their underwear and such, he wouldn't ever admit to that, even with a gun to his head, and so while hemming and hawing,
【Naomasa】 「You know, it's pretty much settled where women hide their guns.」
【Kisara】 「Hmmmm……well, I'll leave it at that.」

No matter how thoroughly outmatched he seemed to be by this black cat, clinging to a woman as he begged her to avenge him was as pathetic as could be, but as Shisamu and Kisara looked between Sakuya and the black cat, comparing the two───they suddenly struck. Sakuya's forehead against the deck, that is. They then said to Sakuya, who was forced to prostrate himself once more while writhing in pain,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それよりこの莫迦、
　宗右衛門さんに何アヤつけてんだろ」
source.english:
“More importantly, idiot,
why are you picking a fight with Mr. Soemon?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「All that aside, you idiot, what kind of nonsense are you trying to pin on Souemon-san?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ごめんねえ宗右衛門さん、こいつ、まだ新米で、船のことなんかなんにも判ってなくってさ」
source.english: “Sorry, Mr. Soemon. He's new. He still doesn't know a thing about the ship.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Sorry about this, Souemon-san. This guy's still new around here, and he doesn't know the first thing about this ship.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ここは見逃したって、ね？」
source.english: “Let him off this time, all right?”

source.japanese:
黒猫を叱るどころかむしろ敬う調子の、これがあの双子の物言いとは信じられない朔屋に、二人はよっくと言い聞かせたという。
　曰く、この雄の黒猫は「時雨宗右衛門」といい、この船の中で一等偉く、飲み水も食料も一番上等なところを採る権利を持つそうな。船の中であれこれ意見が割れた時、最終決定権を持つのがこの宗右衛門で、船内の何人たりとも彼を遮[さえぎ]ってはならないのだそうな。
source.english:
Far from scolding the cat, they spoke with respect. Sakuya could scarcely believe these were the twins' voices. They made sure he understood.
The black tomcat was named Soemon Shigure. He was the most important being aboard. He had the right to the best drinking water and food. Whenever opinions differed, Soemon had the final say. Nobody on the ship was permitted to stand in his way.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……え？　じゃあ、こいつはその、船長よりも偉いの？」
source.english: “…Huh? So he's, what, more important than the captain?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Can you turn a blind eye to this whole mess, please?」

The two weren't scolding the cat; no, they were, if anything, reverent in their tone, and Sakuya, unable to square such a worshipful way of talking with the twins he knew, was given an exhaustive explanation by the two. According to them, this tomcat went by the name「Shigure Souemon」, and he was the highest-ranking member of this ship's crew, granted the right to take for himself the best food and water. When opinions were divided on this ship, the one with the final say in the matter was also Souemon here, and not a soul on the ship dared stand in his way.
【Naomasa】 「……Huh? So then, you're saying this guy here's higher ranking than even the captain?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あのクロんぼと彼じゃ、
　どっちがまともに見える？」
source.english:
“Which looks more sensible to you?
Him, or that little brat Kuro?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そりゃあ確かにあの子と、比べればこっちの猫の方が、無駄なくらいに堂々としているけれど」
source.english: “Well, compared with her, this cat certainly does look unnecessarily dignified…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Between little Kuro and him, who looks more respectable to you?」
【Naomasa】 「Well, sure, compared to that girl, this cat does carry himself with more majesty than he has any right to, I'll give you that, but still.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そういうこと。それで充分。
　あんたが来るずっと前からそうだったんだから。
　文句があるなら、宗右衛門さんに勝ってから言うンだね」
source.english:
“Exactly. That's enough.
It was like this long before you came.
If you've got a complaint, beat Mr. Soemon first, then tell us.”

source.japanese:
そう断言されたところでにわかに納得はいき難いが、確かに一等航海士、信天翁号の中では上位に立つ彼女たちからして、宗右衛門の権利を絶対として認めている様子がありありとしており、朔屋には何も言えなくなる。
　全身ひっかき傷だらけとなり、最後に宗右衛門に尻尾で頬をはたかれて、朔屋、いよいよこの船の中では常識というものが何もかも通用しないことを思い知る。
source.english:
However flatly they asserted it, he could hardly accept such a thing on the spot. Yet the first mates—women who ranked high aboard the Albatross—plainly recognized Soemon's rights as absolute, leaving Sakuya nothing to say.
Scratched from head to foot and, for a final indignity, slapped across the cheek by Soemon's tail, Sakuya at last learned that aboard this ship, every last rule of common sense was null and void.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（でも、猫の方が人より偉い船ってどうなのよ……）
source.english: (But what kind of ship has a cat outranking humans…?)

source.japanese: 後に、クロが宗右衛門の食餌の給仕などを真剣に務める姿を目にする機会もあり、朔屋はより一層暗澹たる気分に襲われたという。
source.english: Later, he would have occasion to see Kuro earnestly serving Soemon his meals. It plunged him into still deeper gloom.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「That's how it is. And all it needs to be. It's been like this since long before you came here. If you have any complaints, you can make them after defeating Souemon-san in battle.」

For all that she asserted it so definitively, it was still a little hard to accept, but it was true that even the first mates, these women who held a high-ranking position on the Albatross, seemed to very obviously recognize Souemon's authority as absolute, and there was nothing more Sakuya could say in return to that. His entire body was covered in scratches, and with a final slap from Souemon's tail striking him across the cheek, Sakuya had come to keenly understand that there was no such thing as common sense operating aboard this ship.
【Naomasa】 （Still, what kind of ship puts a cat above the humans……）
Later, he happened to catch sight of Kuro waiting earnestly on Souemon's table as he ate his dinner, and Sakuya sunk into an even deeper pit of despair.

source.japanese: 漁港は裏ぶれて活気に乏しく、ましてや夜の帳が降りた後では人通りも寂しい。風に乗って吹き流されてくる、飢えた野良犬の遠吠えも物哀しい路地を、朔屋はほくほくと浮かれた足取りで通り抜ける。質屋の、もう店を閉じた扉を騒々しく叩いて店主をひっばりだして叩きこんだ質草で懐は潤って、朔屋の気持ちは信天翁号に乗りこんで来珍しく浮き立っていた。
source.english: The fishing port was shabby and dispirited. After nightfall, its streets were lonelier still. Through an alley where the wind carried the mournful howls of hungry stray dogs, Sakuya walked with a buoyant, satisfied step. He had noisily battered on the closed door of a pawnshop, dragged out its owner, and handed over his goods. His pockets were fuller. For once since joining the Albatross, his heart was light.

source.japanese:
こんな鄙[ひな]びた漁港にも、船員相手の質屋というのは存在していて、船の積み荷からかっぱらってきた革靴を二・三足質草に叩きこむと、どうにか今夜一晩女を購えるくらいの軍資金に変わってくれた。
　久しぶりの上陸。
　朔屋は安堵と感動のあまり半笑いと半泣きの弛みきった表情となっているのも、今夜くらいは飲んでも目が爆発しない酒と、ちゃんとした女体にありつけそうとあればやむを得まい。
source.english:
Even this remote fishing port had a pawnbroker catering to sailors. Two or three pairs of leather shoes stolen from the ship's cargo had somehow become enough money to buy a woman for the night.
Shore leave, at last.
Relief and emotion left him with a slack expression halfway between laughter and tears. With a prospect of liquor that would not make his eyes explode, and a proper woman's body, it could hardly be helped.

source.japanese:
信天翁号は真水を積む為にこの漁港に寄ったのだが、なんぼ鄙[ひな]びて裏ぶれた漁村といえど、朔屋にはまず先にやる事があるはずではなかったか。すなわち、呪われた船と罰当たりな船員どもに別れの罵詈雑言と手の甲を見せた二本指を送って脱走する事、それが青年の願いだったはず、が、そんな事など船にはお見通しの。
　上陸を許すに当たって水夫長は、何時になく優しげな顔で朔屋に告げたものだ。
source.english:
The Albatross had called here to take on fresh water. But however remote and run-down the fishing village, surely there was something Sakuya should have done first? Desert. Bid the accursed ship and her wicked crew farewell with a flood of abuse and two raised fingers with the back of his hand toward them. That had been his wish.
The crew, however, saw through it. When granting him shore leave, the boatswain had told him, with an unusually kindly face:

target.text: The fishing port was run-down and devoid of life, and it was still more desolate once the veil of night had fallen over it. Through these melancholy alleys, with the distant baying of starving wild dogs riding on the wind, came Sakuya, beaming happily with a spring in his step, passing through. He had noisily banged on the doors of the already closed pawnshop, dragged the shopkeeper out, then lined his pockets by pawning some articles, and so Sakuya was in high spirits, a rare sight indeed ever since he boarded the Albatross.

Even in a fishing port this rural and rustic, there existed a pawnshop that dealt with sailors, and by tossing two or three pairs of leather boots that he'd pilfered from the ship's cargo at the pawnbroker, he'd been able to exchange them for enough funds to buy a woman for the night. It had been a while since he'd last had shore leave. Overwhelmed by relief and excitement, Sakuya's facial expression softened into something slack, halfway between smiling and crying, but given that only tonight would he finally get his hands on some booze that wouldn't make his eyes explode, and an actual woman's body, it was little wonder.

The Albatross had stopped by this fishing port to stock up on fresh water, but no matter how rustic and dilapidated a fishing village this may be, was there not something that Sakuya was supposed to prioritize here? In other words, giving his parting insults to this cursed ship and her accursed crew, showing them the back of his hands with two raised fingers, and then making good his escape: that must have been the young man's dearest desire, but alas, the crew had seen right through that. The Bosun, who had come to grant him shore leave, told Sakuya the following with an uncharacteristically kind expression.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『ええか、新米。
　この港はなあ、入江以外は三方山に囲まれた、陸の孤島となっておる』
source.english:
“Listen, new boy.
This port's cut off from the rest of the land. Mountains on three sides, apart from the inlet.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『内地に抜ける道は、峠の一本だけ』
source.english: “There's only one road inland. Over the pass.”

source.japanese: と、ベストの裡側をごそごそと、引っぱり出した文庫本に栞代わりに挟んでいた紙切れを拡げたと見れば地図だ。どうやら漁港周辺の地図と思しい。象のような指先で示して、
source.english: He rummaged about inside his vest, pulled out a paperback, and unfolded the scrap tucked into it as a bookmark: a map, apparently, of the area around the fishing port. Jabbing at it with an elephantine fingertip, he said:

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Listen up, green hand. This harbour, inlet aside, is surrounded in all three directions by mountains, making it an isolated island on land, in practice.」
【Bosun】 「There's only one road that goes inland, and it's through the mountain pass.」

He then rummaged around his pocket, pulled out a scrap of paper he'd been using as a bookmark for his pocket paperback, then unfolded it to reveal a map. It appeared to be a map of the fishing port and its surroundings. He pointed with his elephantine fingers,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『な、この道しかねえんだ。
　乗り合いバスも、この峠の向こう側の入口までしかこんし、それだって今日はもう終わっちまっている』
source.english:
“See? Only this road.
The bus only comes to the foot of the pass on the far side. And the last one's gone for today.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『おめえがもしも、ちょっと内地に散歩に行きたいなあなんぞと、気の利いた思いつき持ったって、今から歩いて夜明けに停留所に辿り着くかどうか』
source.english: “If you had some clever idea about taking a little stroll inland, you could start now, and who knows whether you'd reach the bus stop by dawn.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『そんな夜中のお散歩なぞより、酒でも呑んでたほうがましってことくらい、賢い賢い朔屋にはお判りになろうぜ』
source.english: “Our clever, clever Sakuya must understand that having a drink's better than a walk like that in the middle of the night.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「See, only this road here. Even the public busses only go up to the other side of the entrance to this mountain pass, and they're also done running for the day by now.」

【Bosun】 「So should you happen to feel the desire to go on a little stroll towards the inland, or get any other clever ideas like that, then I do wonder if you'd make it to the bus stop before dawn, should you start walking now.」
【Bosun】 「It'd be a lot smarter to go drink some booze instead of going for any nighttime walks, as I'm certain our clever, well-behaved little Sakuya will come to realize.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『……まあちなみに、まず無い事だろうが、昼になってもおめえが戻った来なかった場合、俺はちっとばかり気が荒くなるかもしれんな』
source.english: “…Incidentally, it'll never happen, of course, but if you're not back by noon, I might get a little rough.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『こんなクソ峠など、一息で駆け抜けちまうくらいにな。そこでおめえと出くわさない事を祈るぜえ』
source.english: “Rough enough to run over that fucking pass in one breath. Pray I don't meet you there.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Well, figured I should mention this, not that I think it'll happen, but should we find ourselves in the unfortunate situation where you're not back by noon tomorrow, I might grow just the tiniest bit testy.」
【Bosun】 「Enough that I might clear this shitty excuse for a mountain pass in a single breath. And then, well, I can only pray that I won't run into you there.」

source.japanese: 上陸、と聞いてときめいた自由の世界への憧れは、これで空しく潰えた。朔屋はこの辺りの地理に疎いのに比べ、水夫長はろくに陸に揚がらない癖して信天翁号の寄港先の周辺事情に知悉しているようで、そういう相手に運頼みでやりあう勇気は彼にはない。
source.english: The words ‘shore leave’ had stirred his longing for a free world. That hope now collapsed to nothing. Sakuya knew little of the local geography. The boatswain, despite hardly ever going ashore, seemed intimately familiar with the surroundings of every port the Albatross visited. Sakuya lacked the courage to challenge such a man on luck alone.

source.japanese: 少なくとも一晩だけでも酒と女の自由が許されたことを喜ぶべきと、後ろ髪は引かれたが諦めて、朔屋はいそいそと船を離れたのだった。
source.english: He should be grateful for even one night of freedom with drink and women. Reluctant though he was, he gave up and eagerly left the ship.

target.text: All his yearning for the world of freedom that had set his heart aflutter as soon as he heard the words "shore leave" was left crushed, never to amount to anything. Though Sakuya was ignorant of the local geography, in comparison, the Bosun seemed to know everything about the surroundings of any ports of call the Albatross stopped by, and this despite rarely going ashore himself, so he had not the courage to rely on luck when dealing with such a foe.

At the very least, he should rejoice that he was permitted the freedom of booze and women even for but a single night, and though it was with painful reluctance, Sakuya gave up, then eagerly left the ship.

source.japanese:
こんな鄙[ひな]びた漁村でも、寄港する船乗り相手の酒場はそれなりに賑わい、ホールのあちこちには酒場の娘たちが妍を競ってあった。
　首飾り、宝石は綺羅綺羅しく光っているが、安い輝きの、いかにもな紛い物。
　ドレスは薄く軽やかで、肩掛けなどを腕に緩くまとった様は、一見して夜会にも相応しい装いであったけれど、その色合いはフォーマルな座に並べるにはあまりも扇情的に過ぎた。布地も縫製もよくよく見ればいい加減で、こういう薄暗い酒場の、曖昧な影の中でこそ艶[つや]やかだが、光の下に引きずり出されればたちまち下手な化粧のように色褪せよう。
　腰や胸やら無遠慮に触れてくる酔漢にも淑女として無礼と身を引いたり叱責するどころか、嬌声上げて身をくねらせる。
source.english:
Even in a fishing village this remote, the tavern for visiting sailors was reasonably lively. Around the hall, its women competed in beauty.
Necklaces glittered, their stones offering a cheap, unmistakably counterfeit brilliance.
Their dresses were thin and light; shawls lay loosely about their arms. At first glance, they might have been dressed for an evening party. But the colors were far too provocative for a formal gathering. On closer inspection, the fabric and sewing were careless. They looked alluring in the uncertain shadows of a dim tavern like this. Dragged into the light, they would fade as quickly as badly applied makeup.
When drunken hands touched waist or breast without permission, the women neither recoiled nor rebuked the men as ladies might. They squealed and wriggled.

source.japanese: つまるところ、美しく華美な姿は男達を誘う為の装い、彼女達は荒くれ達、船乗り相手の一夜限りの恋人、酒場の売笑婦達なのであった。
source.english: In short, their bright and lovely appearance was meant to tempt men. They were lovers for one night, serving rough sailors. The tavern's prostitutes.

source.japanese:
そして今の朔屋には、そういう酒場の娘たちこそが、求めて止まない女そのものだった。
　機知に溢れ、知性の渇きを満足させてくれるような会話の応酬なんぞ糞喰らえ。
　どれだけ綺麗に着飾っていようが、女の衣裳なぞ背中のファスナーを摘[つ]んで下ろしブラジャーのホックを外す歓びの為だけにある。
source.english:
At present, they were precisely the women Sakuya craved.
To hell with witty exchanges that quenched one's thirst for intellectual company.

source.japanese: 二世の愛を誓われたいと願うより、煌びやかな破滅へと誘ってもらいたくなる、そういう声音で、艶やかなのに足下には深淵を覗かせる、匂びやかなのに麻痺させるほどに強烈な退廃も伴連れにする、そんな声を出す女なんて、あの人以外にいるわけがない、とは思い知っているのに朔屋は、
source.english: A voice that made one wish not for a vow of love through this life and the next, but for an invitation to glittering ruin. Lovely, yet opening an abyss at one's feet. Fragrant, yet accompanied by a decadence so potent it paralyzed. Sakuya knew perfectly well that no woman but her could possess such a voice. Nevertheless—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「人違いですよ。あなたのお知り合いみたいな人が、こんな場末でくだ撒いてるはずがない───」
source.english: “You've mistaken me for someone else. No acquaintance of yours would be blathering drunkenly in a dive like this—”

source.japanese:
見苦しく人違いを期待しながら背後にそろり、自慰を見咎められた少年のように振り向いて、一気に脱力した。誰も、いなかったので。酔いどれどもは、朔屋の挙動不審など知った事かはで、己の愉[たの]しみに耽[ふけ]って目もくれやしない、その無関心を有り難く受け取り、朔屋はほっと卓へと向き直った。
　雅やかな面差しの、笑顔が月の華と艶[つや]やかに咲いていた。だから朔屋は、椅子の上で腰を抜かした。
source.english:
Pathetically hoping she had mistaken him for someone else, he turned gingerly to look behind him, like a boy caught masturbating—and went limp all at once. No one was there. The drunks, caring not a whit for Sakuya’s suspicious behavior, were too busy with their own pleasures to spare him a glance. Gratefully accepting their indifference, he turned back to the table in relief.
There, upon those elegant features, a smile bloomed, lustrous as a flower under the moon. And so Sakuya collapsed bonelessly in his chair.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「るる、泪さん!?
　おい嘘だろ、まさかそんなあなたが……」
source.english:
“R-R-Rui!?
No, come on. Surely you can't be…”

target.text: 【??】 「Whatever are you up to, chattering away with only a bottle of alcohol for company? Nao-san, you certainly have a peculiar way of drinking.」

Fortunately, her visage disappeared from his mind, but in exchange, a voice brimming over with an ironclad realism more solid than any of his memories gently traced his neck; that voice, far more softly seductive and kinder than any memory, with a graceful hebetude yet hiding a dangerous stinger lurking at its very bottom.

Rather than making him wish that they pledged their eternal love for one another in this world and the next, it left him desiring to be lured into dazzling ruin, such was her voice; lustrous and glossy, and yet it let you see a glimpse of the deep abyss opening below your feet; radiating outwards with its lush beauty, and yet it was accompanied by a paralyzingly intense decadence; there could be no other woman than her with a voice like that, Sakuya was painfully aware of that, and yet,
【Naomasa】 「You've got the wrong man. There's no way an acquaintance of someone like you would be rambling into his cups in a run-down bar like───」

While pathetically hoping that it was just a case of mistaken identity, he stealthily looked back over his shoulder like a young boy who had previously been caught masturbating, then felt all his strength leave him in an instant. There was, nobody there. The drunkards didn't have a care in the world for Sakuya's suspicious behaviour, utterly engrossed in their own enjoyments as they were, paying him no attention, and Sakuya accepted that lack of concern with gratitude, then turned back to his table and heaved a sigh of relief. On graceful features, a smile bloomed with the vibrant lustre of a silken moonbeam flower. Therefore, Sakuya collapsed in his chair from shock.
【Naomasa】 「Ru-ru-, Rui-san!? Oi, you're kidding, there's no way someone like YOU would be……」

source.japanese:
泪───彩久津泪。長い事封じ籠めていた名が、自ら呼んだ声に引きずられて蘇る。
　夜に咲いて艶麗な、蜜を豊潤に湛えた花のように目覚ましい、美しいひと。確かな年は知らねど、濃まやかな色香零れんばかりの年増の女。
source.english:
Rui. Rui Irokuzu. A name he had kept shut away for so long came back to life, dragged out by his own voice.
A beautiful woman, startling as a sumptuous night-blooming flower brimming with nectar. He did not know her exact age. She was a mature woman, almost overflowing with rich sensuality.

source.japanese: 相手が若かろうが年増だろうが、大概の女に見境のない朔屋には、皿に盛って差し出された熟れきった果実であるはず、久闊を叙して後は二階に取った部屋に誘い、休んでいる酒場女をも引きずりこんで三人で組んずほぐれつと口説きにかかるのが彼としてはまず頷[うなず]ける行動だろう。
source.english: Young or mature, Sakuya was indiscriminate about most women. She ought to have been ripe fruit offered to him on a plate. A few words to renew their acquaintance, an invitation to the room he had taken upstairs, and perhaps a suggestion that they draw the resting tavern woman into a three-way tangle: that would have been entirely understandable behavior for him.

source.japanese:
が、口説くどころか朔屋は、立ち上がる事もままならず、じたじた床を蹴って椅子ごと身を遠ざけようと、どうにも見苦しい。女性への慎みを無縁とする朔屋であるからして、これは異常行動としか言いようがないのだが、とにかく彼には、この女性について良い思い出がないのだった。
　見ての通り臈長けた美女ではある。ただその美貌と肢体は男を滅ぼす類の女で、朔屋が知る限り夫を二桁近くも替え、それ以外にも彼女と関わったために破滅した男は数知れず。
source.english:
Instead, he could scarcely stand, much less proposition her. He kicked feebly at the floor, trying to move himself away, chair and all. An ugly spectacle. For a man wholly unacquainted with modest restraint before women, this could only be called abnormal behavior. But he simply had no happy memories of her.
She was, as anyone could see, a lovely woman of exquisite grace. Only hers was the sort of beauty, the sort of body, that destroyed men. To Sakuya's knowledge, her tally of husbands approached double figures. Countless other men had come to ruin through their involvement with her.

source.japanese: 実際朔屋も、過去に奇縁で彼女と知り合った際、初対面なのにもかかわらず、姦通を疑った当時の夫に匕首で斬りつけられ流血騒ぎとなった（この男は後に鉄道に飛びこんで轢死を遂げた）。
source.english: Indeed, when an odd chance first brought them together, her husband at the time suspected adultery and slashed Sakuya with a dagger. They had only just met, yet there was bloodshed. The husband later threw himself beneath a train and was crushed to death.

source.japanese: 二度目の出会いは帝都のホテルのホールを借り切った壮麗なパーティ会場、そんな席に招待客として居合わせていたあたり朔屋の過去というのも少なからず興味深いがそれは余談として、この時朔屋は毒殺されかかった。ボーイが配るシャンパンの、朔屋の順に意地汚く割りこんだ独身男が結果的には彼の身代わりとなったのだが、朔屋にとっては血塊吐き散らし、純白のテーブルクロスに剥がれるまで爪食いこませて悶え死んだ独身男の形相は、今もって忌まわしい記憶である。どうやら泪と話しこんでいた（といっても社交辞令程度の）朔屋に妬心催したホテルのマネージャーが、燻蒸消毒用の劇物をシャンパングラスに放りこんだらしいと後から伝え聞いた時の戦慄と言ったら。
source.english: Their second meeting took place at a magnificent party occupying an entire hall in a hotel in the imperial capital. That Sakuya had been there as an invited guest suggested a past of some interest, but let that remain a digression. On this occasion, he was nearly poisoned. An unmarried man greedily pushed ahead of him for the champagne a waiter was distributing, and effectively died in his place. Even now, Sakuya could not rid himself of the man's dreadful face as he vomited clots of blood, dug his nails into the immaculate white tablecloth until they tore off, and died in agony. Later he heard that the hotel manager, jealous of Sakuya's conversation with Rui—no more than polite small talk—had apparently put a highly toxic fumigant into the champagne glass. How that news had chilled him.

source.japanese: 三度目が最後の出会いで、場所は真夏の三浦半島の避暑地の浜辺、風に飛ばされた日傘の持ち主が、届けた時に泪だと知ったくらいに偶然の出会いだったのに、朔屋はその時の泪の取り巻き達に闇討ちに遭い、巡邏が駆けつけなんだら岩を抱き枕に海に叩きこまれる憂き目を見ていただろう。この取り巻きというのは地元の若衆どもで、それまで関わりもないような泪の如き貴婦人の来臨に手もなく舞い上がって守護騎士を気取った。言うまでもなく一方通行の思慕であり、中にはのぼせあがった挙げ句三代続いた地所を売り払うまでに入れ揚げ、他愛なく破産し首を括った若旦那もあったらしい。
source.english: Their third and last meeting was on a resort beach on the Miura Peninsula in high summer. Pure chance: he retrieved a windblown parasol and only discovered its owner was Rui when he brought it back. Yet her admirers at the time ambushed him. Had a patrol not arrived, he would have been thrown into the sea with a rock for a bedmate. These admirers were local young men, swept helplessly away by the arrival of a lady such as they had never known. They fancied themselves her guardian knights. Their adoration was, needless to say, entirely one-sided. One young heir, it seemed, became so infatuated that he sold land held by his family for three generations, promptly went bankrupt, and hanged himself.

source.japanese: 要は、男という生き物に破滅を贈って歩くのがこの泪という女なのである。泪本人に邪気があろうが無かろうが、関わった男は愚かな不幸者としか言いようがなく、三度の出会いを経てぼんくらの朔屋をして強烈に学習せしめるくらいの、男にとっての劇薬なのである。
source.english: In short, this woman Rui went about bestowing ruin on the creatures known as men. Whether or not she herself meant any harm, the men caught up with her could only be called unfortunate fools. She was a poison so powerful that three encounters had taught even a dullard like Sakuya a lasting lesson.

source.japanese: そして、泪自身には悪気も邪気も無いようなのが、なおのこと始末に負えなかった。ころころと娘のような笑窪で、語りかける泪は全くもってどこまでも美しい、語りかける眼差しにはなんら底意や曇りも見えず、破滅はただ、泪を中心に渦巻いては獲物を捕らえるのみで、彼女自身にはなんら累を及ぼさないかの如くさ、な。
source.english: What made her still more impossible to deal with was that she seemed to harbor neither malice nor ill intent. Speaking to him with girlish dimples, Rui was beautiful through and through. No ulterior purpose, no cloud, showed in her eyes. Ruin merely swirled about her, catching its prey. It never seemed to touch her at all.

target.text: Rui───Irokudzu Rui. A name that had long been sealed away in the depths of his mind, dragged back out by his own voice that called it and now resurrected before him. A beautiful person, striking like the dazzling pulchritude of a flower ripe with honey in bloom beneath the night sky. He was not certain of her age, a mature woman overflowing with a rich, alluring charm.

Whether she was a young or mature woman, in the eyes of someone like Sakuya, who, in general, did not discriminate in terms of women, she should have been like a ripe fruit served to him on a silver platter, and after apologizing for neglecting their acquaintance for so long, he would grab a room on the second floor, then attempt to woo her by proposing that they invite the resting bar girl to join in and spend the night as a tangled mess of limbs: a course of action that he would almost certainly readily approve of.

But, Sakuya was far from making any advances; he couldn't even manage to stand up on his own two feet, he recoiled, kicking at the floor in an attempt to move his chair as far away from her as he could, an absolutely unsightly display. For Sakuya, a man so utterly divorced from the concept of restraint in the face of a woman, this could only be said to be abnormal behaviour, but at any rate, there were no good memories involving this woman anywhere in his mind.

As was plain to see, she was an elegant and mature beauty. But she was the sort of woman who would bring ruin upon men with that beautiful face and body of hers; as far as Sakuya knew, the amount of times she'd changed husbands numbered somewhere in the double digits, and there must have been countless other men beyond those who had also been brought to ruin by associating with this woman.

In fact, when Sakuya first made her acquaintance by strange coincidence, regardless of the fact it was their very first time meeting, her then-husband, who suspected her of committing adultery with Sakuya, slashed at him with a dagger, resulting in a bloody incident. (This man later met his end by throwing himself in front of an oncoming train.)

The second time they met was at a grand party venue in a chartered hall at a hotel in the imperial capital, and while whatever occurred in Sakuya's past that led to him being present as an invited guest on that occasion is by all means fascinating, that would be a digression, but at the time, Sakuya survived an attempted poisoning.

A bachelor who greedily cut in front of Sakuya's place while he waited in line for where the waiter served the champagne ended up taking his place, but to Sakuya, the expression on that bachelor's face as he vomited blood clots everywhere, dug his nails into the pure white tablecloth until he ripped it clean off, then writhed in agony until he perished, remained an abhorrent memory even now.

It seemed like the hotel manager had grown jealous while Sakuya was deep in conversation with Rui (though with that said, it was nothing more than polite, empty compliments), and he had then apparently dumped a highly deleterious fumigation agent into the champagne glass or something, and Sakuya had shivered in terror when he was told as much later.

For their third and final meeting, the location was on the beach of a summer retreat on the Miura peninsula in the height of summer, and even though he only happened to realize that the owner of the parasol that had blown away in the wind was Rui when he delivered it back to her, Sakuya was ambushed under the veil of night by Rui's coterie of admirers at the time; had a patrolman not come rushing to the scene, he would surely have suffered the miserable fate of being tossed into the ocean while being made to hold a rock for a pillow.

These admirers were the local young men, ecstatic that a noblewoman like Rui, someone they had never met the likes of hitherto, had made her visit, acting like her guardian knights in shining armour. It goes without saying that this was, of course, a deep affection of a one-sided nature; among their number was supposedly a young gentleman who went so beside himself, he ended up showering her with so much money that he even sold off his estate inherited through three generations, foolishly went bankrupt, and then tied a noose around his neck.

To summarize: this woman, Rui, walked through life bestowing the gift of ruin upon the creature known as man. Regardless of whether Rui herself held any malice or not, any man who involved himself with her could only be called foolish or misfortunate; it took but three separate encounters to finally sear that lesson into the mind of a dimwit like Sakuya, so lethal a medicine was she to men.

And so, while Rui herself did not seem to hold any malice or ill will, that only made it even harder to deal with. With rounded, girlish dimples, speaking to him, Rui truly was absolutely beautiful in everything she had and did; speaking to him, there was not a trace of underlying motives or veiled darkness to be seen in her gaze; a vortex of ruin simply swirled around Rui with her as its core, only capturing its targets within, as though it would not bring any harm to the woman herself, yes.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お久しぶりね、直さん。
　船員学校に進んだ、ってうかがったわ。
　燕尾服の貴方も素敵だったけれど、
　海兵さんの衣装も、きっと似合ってよ」
source.english:
“It's been so long, Nao.
I heard you went on to a sailors' school.
You were lovely in tails,
but I'm sure a marine's uniform will suit you, too.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや俺は、別に兵隊を目指した訳じゃなく、
　家の方が強引に。ああそんなのはどうでもいい。
　一体なんだってあなたみたいな女がこんな曖昧酒場に……？」
source.english:
“No, I wasn't trying to become a soldier.
My family forced the matter.
Oh, never mind any of that. Why on earth would someone like you be in a shady tavern like this…?”

source.japanese: 泪は弟を相手にするように朔屋を愛称で呼ぶ、そんな近しげな接し様を、嬉しい、好もしい胸騒ぎで受けとめていたのは過去の事、今ではどうしたって身構えてしまって、朔屋は乱暴に呑み下した酒が、あちこちの血管で気違いじみた沁みこみ方を示すを感じ取り、水を求めて立ち上がろうとして、でも出来なくて、泪の長手袋の衣擦ればかりを耳に聴いた、酒場の喧噪もぼんやりと遠い。
source.english: Rui used his pet name as though speaking to a younger brother. Once, he had received that familiarity with a happy flutter of excitement. Those days were past. Now he could not help bracing himself. The liquor he had gulped so roughly seemed to be seeping madly into blood vessels all over his body. He tried to rise and get water, but could not. He heard only the rustle of Rui's long gloves. Even the tavern's clamor was dim and distant.

source.japanese: しなやかに顎の下で指を組んで、油に滑るボロ椅子にもこだわらず、ゆったり女王の座として艶冶な臀を乗せる泪。まとう紫紺は高雅を知る者のみが色に着られずに着こなせる色合いの、酒場女たちの見やすい派手はないのに、泪がいるだけで彼女達の方が侘びしくくすむ。布地の襞[ひだ]の影の一つ一つさえも、彼女を彩る宝飾として紫紺の中に精妙に溜まり、留まり、移ろう。
source.english: She folded her supple fingers beneath her chin and settled her lovely hips upon the battered, greasy chair as comfortably as upon a queen's throne. Deep violet was a shade only someone who understood elegance could wear without being worn by it. Her clothes lacked the obvious brightness of the tavern women's dresses, yet her mere presence made them look drab and forlorn. Even the shadows in each fold of fabric pooled, lingered, and shifted with exquisite precision in that violet, like jewels adorning her.

source.japanese: だがどれだけ臈長けて美しくあろうと、朔屋はこの夜の出会いをなるたけ短い時間で終わらせたい気持ちで一杯だった。再会の衝撃は口一杯に含んだ米酢と同じにきつく強く、さっさと別れてしまいたい。
source.english: However graceful and beautiful she might be, Sakuya wanted tonight's encounter over as quickly as possible. The shock of reunion was as sharp and overpowering as a mouthful of rice vinegar. He wanted to get away.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まあ、あなただって事情とか気分とか、あるだろうな。俺もここにはたまさか寄っただけですよ。
　もしかしたら、またどこかで会うかも知れないけれど」
source.english:
“Well, you must have your reasons. Or your moods. I only happened to stop here myself.
Perhaps we'll meet somewhere else again.”

source.japanese: 言葉はここで出される麦酒という名の、気の抜けきった別の何かほどに誠意が籠もらず、再会など期待してもいないのが丸見えで、これならいっそ会いたくないとはっきり告げる方がまだ礼に適っているというくらい。この苦手意識は不公平な事に朔屋のみが負うているらしく、泪は青年の人あしらいを、やんわりと目で咎め、
source.english: His words held about as much sincerity as the flat substance served here under the name of beer. His lack of enthusiasm for another meeting was painfully apparent. An outright declaration that he never wanted to see her would have been more courteous. Unfairly, this discomfort seemed his alone. Rui gently reproached his manners with her eyes—

target.text: 【Rui】 「It has been a while, Nao-san. You went to nautical school, or so I have been told. You did look wonderful in a tailcoat, dear, but I'm certain that the uniform of a marine suits you well, too.」

【Naomasa】 「Oh no, it's not like I was aiming to join the navy in particular, I was forced to go by my family. Aah, who cares about any of that. Why in the world is a woman like you in a seedy bar like this……?」

Rui called Sakuya with a pet name as though she were keeping a younger brother company, but to receive such treatment with a happy, fond beating of the heart was a thing of the past; right now, he was on guard for everything and anything, and Sakuya could feel the alcohol he had slammed down his throat so violently seeping into his veins all over, permeating his blood in a frenzied cascade, and longing for water, he made to stand up, but he couldn't; all that passed through his ears was the rustling fabric of Rui's long gloves, and the tumult of the bar grew hazy and distant.

Linking her fingers in a refined manner under her chin, paying no mind to the shabby chair slick with grease, Rui placed her enticing buttocks on the chair like it were a queen's comfortable throne. The combination of purple and navy blue hues she was clad in was the sort of colour only those who understood noble elegance could hope to wear without being worn by the colour in turn; it was far from the eye-catching, gaudy colours worn by the bar girls, but by Rui's mere presence, the other women grew dreary and unassuming. Even the shadows cast by each and every individual fold of the fabric, like jewels adorning her person, subtly pooled, lingered, and shifted within the bright indigo.

But no matter how elegantly beautiful she was, Sakuya was filled with the desire to cut this night's encounter short as quickly as possible. The shock of their reunion was as sharply intense as holding a mouthful of rice vinegar against his tongue, and he wished to take his leave without delay.

【Naomasa】 「Well, I'm sure even you have your circumstances or your whims and all that, I'm sure you do. I also just happened to stop by here. Perhaps, if things align, we might meet again somewhere someday, but.」

His words were flat and lifeless, without a trace of sincerity, like the swill they served in this bar that they had the gall to call beer, and it was plain to hear that he held no expectations for any future reunions or the like; if anything, one could say that it would be more polite to be clear and bluntly state that he would rather not meet her at all. Apparently, and what injustice, it was only the young man who was burdened by the awareness of how hard a time he had dealing with her, for Rui gently rebuked the young man's treatment of others with a look,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「つれないこと。
　せっかくの再会なのに。
　わたくしは直さんに会えて嬉しいわ。
　なのに貴方は、わたくしの事がお嫌いのご様子」
source.english:
“How cold.
After we've finally met again.
I'm glad to see you, Nao.
Yet you seem to dislike me.”

source.japanese: 嫌いと言うより畏いので、関わるとたいがいが厄介ごとに巻きこまれる事となった過去がざっと脳裏を流れていく、朔屋は泪に───
source.english: Fear, rather than dislike. His past encounters with her, most of which had plunged him into trouble, passed swiftly through his mind. Sakuya—

target.text: 【Rui】 「What a cold thing to say. Especially in light of how long it has been. I, for one, am delighted that I got to meet you again, Nao-san. And yet, dear, you seem to find my presence disagreeable.」
He found her more scary than disagreeable, but as his experiences of the past flashed through his mind, of how getting involved with her usually lead to nothing but trouble for him, Sakuya───

source.japanese: ───こういう女は、幽かに拗[す]ねた様さえ蠱惑的で、恨み辛みをぶつける方こそ、聞き分けのない野暮の極み、そうと知りつつ朔屋は言わずにいられなかった。
source.english: —Even the faintest pout was seductive on a woman like this. To fling one's grievances at her was the very height of graceless, unreasonable behavior. He knew that. Still, he could not leave it unsaid.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやその……嫌いって事はないが、正直言うと畏いんです。泪さん、こんなコト言いたかないが、あなたに会うと大抵その後俺はひどい目に遭う、だから、その……」
source.english: “No, well… I don't dislike you. But frankly, I'm afraid of you. Rui, I hate to say this, but every time I meet you, something awful usually happens to me afterward. So, you know…”

target.text: ───This kind of woman was alluring even when subtly sulking, and it is he who vents his bitter resentments who is the epitome of an unreasonable boor, but even though he was well aware of this, Sakuya still couldn't stop himself from saying it.

【Naomasa】 「No, err……I don't dislike you, but being honest with you, I'm afraid. Rui-san, I don't really want to say this, but whenever I meet you, I usually end up in some terrible trouble later, so, uhmm……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あらそうだったの。
　それはとってもお気の毒。
　直さんは、きっと運が悪いのね。
　けれどそんなのは長続きしないもの」
source.english:
“Oh, is that so?
How very unfortunate.
You must have bad luck, Nao.
But that sort of thing doesn't last long.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Goodness, is that so? I'm terribly sorry to hear that. You must be a very unfortunate man, Nao-san, that much is clear. But such things never last long.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「良いことだってあるわ。そのうちにね。
　ところで───」
source.english:
“Good things happen, too.
Eventually. Now—”

source.japanese: 朔屋の恐れなどにはこだわった様子などかけらも見せずに話を流した、そもそも彼女には毛の先ほども底意がない。周囲に群がった男が何を血迷うとも、だからといって咲き誇った花を責めるのは明らかに筋違いの、その花は毒の蜜潜[ひそ]ませていようとも。
source.english: She passed over his fear without showing the slightest concern. Indeed, she had not a hair's breadth of ulterior intent. Whatever madness seized the men who crowded about her, it was plainly unjust to blame the blooming flower. Even if that flower held poisonous nectar.

source.japanese: とはいえそれで朔屋が古い畏れを払拭しえたかというと話は別で、それこそ頭上にぐるぐると信天翁が周遊し、小馬鹿と鳴かれたかの歯痒さを抱いてあったのだが。
source.english: Whether this dispelled Sakuya's old fear was another matter. He felt the impotent irritation of a man with an albatross circling overhead, crying Little fool! at him.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Good things will befall you as well. Sooner or later. Incidentally───」

Without showing even a hint of concern for something as trifling as Sakuya's fears, she moved the conversation along: this woman had absolutely no ulterior motives in the first place. No matter what maddened delusions took hold of the men swarming her, it would nevertheless clearly be illogical to misplace the blame on the flower blossoming in full glory, regardless of the poisoned nectar it hid within its petals.

Be that as it may, whether that was enough for Sakuya to rid himself of his old fears was a different story entirely; he harboured a bothersome frustration within himself, exactly as though an albatross were flying in circles above his head, screeching at him in mockery.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「まあ、細かいお話は適当にして。
　わたくし、貴方を捜していたの」
source.english:
“Never mind the little details.
I've been looking for you.”

source.japanese:
つまり泪の目当ては誰あろう。
　他ならぬこの自分───？
　頭上の幻想の信天翁は腐肉漁りの禿鷲と化し、朔屋は今度こそ駆け足で逃げ出したくなった。
source.english:
So the person Rui wanted was—who else?
Him?
The imaginary albatross overhead became a carrion-seeking vulture. Now he truly wanted to run.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Now then, I will be a bit cursory with the details. I have been looking for you, dear.」

In other words, Rui's objective was none other than. None other than he himself───? The illusory albatross above his head transformed into an Old World vulture scavenging for rotten flesh, and now, Sakuya really wanted to make his escape in double time.

source.japanese: 頤を粋な角度に引いて、幽かに拗[す]ねた気色に上目遣いの女から滲むは、男心をそそって止まない艶の、恨み辛みを保ち続けるには難しい。
source.english: She lowered her chin at an artful angle and looked up at him, faintly petulant. The allure she gave off stirred a man's heart without cease. It was hard to hold on to one's grievances.

source.japanese:
なにより泪が美しいことには嘘も掛け値も無し、乳房はあのシサム・キサラを凌駕する量感を誇っていたし、腰から尻にかけての曲線などは精通前の少年だろうが種の涸れ果てた老人だろうが、眺めているだけで逸物の先から逸る腺液を滲ませてしまいそうに生々しく淫猥だ。
　こういう相手に朔屋の如き、下半身に従属している男が強面に出られるはずがない。
source.english:
Above all, Rui's beauty admitted neither lie nor exaggeration. Her breasts boasted a fullness greater even than Sisam's and Kisara's; the curves from waist to buttocks were so vividly obscene that the mere sight might make the tip of any member bead with eager fluid, whether it belonged to a boy yet to spill his first seed or an old man whose seed had long run dry.
A man like Sakuya, ruled from the waist down, could hardly put on a stern face before such a woman.

source.japanese: 積年の畏れなど火の前のバターと溶けて流れて、代わりと浮き上がったのは朔屋お馴染みの笑みだった。鼻の下を伸ばしてだらしなく脂下がった例の。
source.english: Years of fear melted and ran away like butter before a flame. In their place surfaced Sakuya's familiar smile. That loose, smug, lecherous grin.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、俺があなたを嫌うなんて、そんなありえないって」
source.english: “Me, dislike you? No, that's impossible.”

target.text: She drew her lower jaw into a refined angle, then looked at him through her lashes, betraying a faint hint of petulance in her gaze, and her charm that never ceased to tempt the male heart made it hard to continue to bear a grudge.

And more than anything, there was no lie or exaggeration in calling Rui beautiful: her chest boasted of dimensions far surpassing those of Shisamu's and Kisara's, and the curves of her hips and butt were so graphically obscene that just laying one's gaze upon them would make glandular fluids ooze out excitedly from the tip of one's penis, be one a young boy yet to experience semenarche or an old man whose seed had dried out entirely. And when in the company of such a woman, the likes of Sakuya, a man subordinate to his lower half, could not possibly act so overbearing.
His long-standing fear melted and washed away like butter before a flame, and what arose to take its place was one of Sakuya's familiar smiles. Ogling, sloppy, and self-satisfied: the usual smirk.
【Naomasa】 「No no, me, dislike you? Perish the thought, impossible.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ほんとうに？」
source.english: “Really?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「本当だって。そんな昔のことをいつまでも引きずってたってしょうがない」
source.english: “Really. No point dragging the past around forever.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「刺し殺され損なったのも、毒盛られかかったのも、溺れ死にするところだったのも、なにも泪さんが悪いってわけじゃないし」
source.english: “Nearly getting stabbed to death, poisoned, and drowned—none of that was your fault, Rui.”

source.japanese:
己の蒙った被害すら、女に誇る武勇伝じみた響きを持たせ、この時朔屋が銀の煙管でも携えていたなら、『脂下がる』の語源通り、中の脂が吸い口まで降りてくるくらいに得意気に雁首上向きにおったてていたことだろう。
　実際、酒の酔いも手伝って、朔屋の別の雁首は頭をもたげつつあった。
source.english:
He even made the injuries he had suffered sound like martial exploits recounted to impress a woman. Had he carried a silver pipe just then, he would have tilted its head so proudly upward that the tar inside would run down to the mouthpiece: the very image of a tar-dripping leer.
In fact, aided by drink, another head of Sakuya's was beginning to rise.

source.japanese: 物騒な台詞を並べつつ朔屋は、瞼の裏のシサム・キサラの肢体と泪を臆面もなく比べていたりの、あの二人と盛るなら、それは野生の宴、精も根も燃やし尽くすような激しい交わりとなろう、一方泪が相手なら肉の快美にどこまでも溺れていくような蕩けていくような淫戯となろう、などと好き放題な妄想に耽[ふけ]っていたのだ、が。
source.english: As he recited these alarming incidents, he shamelessly compared Rui with the bodies of Sisam and Kisara behind his eyelids. To rut with those two would be a wild feast, a fierce coupling that burned through every last reserve of strength and seed. With Rui, by contrast, the pleasures would melt him, drown him without end in the sweetness of flesh. He indulged freely in such fantasies—but—

target.text: 【Rui】 「Truly?」
【Naomasa】 「It's true. There's no point in dredging up things from the past for all eternity.」

【Naomasa】 「When I was almost stabbed to death, when somebody tried to serve me poison, even when I was about to be drowned to death. It's not like you were to blame for anything in all that, Rui-san.」

Even the harm that had befallen him now rang of the tales of heroism and bravery one would vaunt of to a woman, and were Sakuya possessed of a silver kiseru, he would, like the etymological origins of the term 『脂下がる』suggests, probably tilt the bowl of his pipe upwards in pride until the resin within would roll all the way down to the mouthpiece. In reality, the intoxication from the booze also helped things along, and an entirely different part of Sakuya reared its pipehead. (TN: "脂下がる" is literally read as dripping resin. Functionally it means looking smug or self-satisfied.)

While Sakuya rattled off some disturbing lines, he shamelessly compared the bodies of Kisara and Shisamu with Rui's in his mind; were he to copulate with those two, it would be a wild feast, surely the sort of coupling that would exhaust all his energy, physically and mentally; on the other hand, were he to have Rui as his companion for the night, he would melt into licentious play like he were drowning in the delights of the flesh, and so on; he lost himself in his self-indulgent delusions, but.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そお？　ならよかった。
　過ぎた昔にくよくよしない方って素敵」
source.english:
“Is that so? I'm glad.
A man who doesn't brood over the past is wonderful.”

source.japanese: 素敵と褒められて心が動かないほど木石ではない朔屋ではあったが、次の言葉を聞いては身裡が木や石どころか金物より固く冷えていく。
source.english: Sakuya was not made of wood or stone: being called wonderful moved him. But at her next words, something inside him grew colder and harder than metal, never mind wood or stone.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Is that so? Then all is well. To not fret over what has already passed is a wonderful thing.」

Sakuya heart was not wrought of wood or stone to the point of not being affected at being praised for being wonderful, but as he heard the next words, his insides froze to something far harder than any wood, stone, or even metal.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「まあ、細かいお話は適当にして。
　わたくし、貴方を捜していたの」
source.english:
“Never mind the little details.
I've been looking for you.”

source.japanese:
つまり泪の目当ては誰あろう。
　他ならぬこの自分───？
　束の間抱いた欲情は寒気と共に音を立てて引いていき、悪魔に影でも踏まれた悪心地に総身包まれる。
　朔屋は今更ながら駆け足で逃げ出したくなった。
source.english:
So the person Rui wanted was—who else?
Him?
His momentary lust ebbed noisily away with a chill. A foul sensation enveloped him, as though a devil had stepped on his shadow.
Belatedly, he wanted to run.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なんだって？」
source.english: “…What did you say?”

source.japanese: 聞き直すのが恐ろしくてたまらなかったが、訊ねずにはいられない。聞き違いと言う事も有り得る。
source.english: He was terrified to ask again, but had to. He might have misheard.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Now then, I will be a bit cursory with the details. I have been looking for you, dear.」

In other words, Rui's objective was none other than. None other than he himself───? The fleeting surge of lust he had harboured drained from him audibly, retreating hand-in-hand with the advent of a sudden chill, his entire body embraced by an evil sensation like the Devil himself had stepped into his shadow. Belated as it was, Sakuya wanted to make his escape in double time.
【Naomasa】 「……What did you just say?」
The thought of hearing it once more was so terrifying that he almost couldn't bear to, but he had to inquire. It was possible he had simply misheard.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ようやく逢えたわね、貴方。
　貴方は今、信天翁号というお船に乗っているのでしょう」
source.english:
“At last I've found you.
You're aboard a ship called the Albatross now, aren't you?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「At long last I found you, dear. You're sailing with the ship known as the Albatross now, I believe?」

source.japanese:
聞き違いどころではなく───なぜそんなことまで知っているのだろうこの女。
　水面に垂らした一滴の墨はたちまち拡かるがその分すぐに薄れる。しかし朔屋の胃の底から湧き起こったそれは、一つまみの予兆から墨滴の速さで膨れあがる癖して、濃度薄れるどころかますます濃くなりまさっていくばかり。やがて胸郭に満ちあふれ、次の泪の言葉で、
source.english:
He had not misheard. Far from it. How did this woman know even that?
A drop of ink spreads swiftly over water, but thins as it does so. What welled from the bottom of Sakuya's stomach swelled from a pinch of foreboding with the speed of that ink, yet instead of growing pale, it became denser and denser. Soon it filled his chest. Then Rui spoke again—

target.text: It wasn't even an issue of whether he'd misheard her───how did this woman even know so much? As quickly as a single drop of ink dropped onto the surface of water spreads, it dilutes just as rapidly in turn. But that which welled up from the bottom of Sakuya's stomach, for all that it swelled up with the speed of that drop of ink from the tiniest omen of things to come, far from diluting, grew only thicker and thicker. Before long, it had filled his thorax, overflowing, and upon hearing Rui's next words,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくし、同じお船に乗る事になりました。
　貴方、案内してちょうだい。
　それからお船の皆様に、
　紹介、よろしくお願いよ」
source.english:
“I'm going to be on the same ship.
You'll show me around,
won't you?
And please introduce me to everyone aboard.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「And so, it has been decided that I will be boarding that very same ship. Dear, do show me around, please. And then, if you would also introduce me to all the members of the crew, I would be much obliged.」

source.japanese: 黒々とした予感は、遂に喉から脳内に溢れかえり、朔屋の視界まで真っ黒に染めたのだった。
source.english: The black foreboding finally overflowed through his throat and into his brain. Even his vision went pitch-black.

source.japanese: ───ああ、嗚呼！　朔屋には最早悲劇の台詞しか呟けない。
source.english: Ah! Alas! Sakuya could only murmur the words of tragedy now.

target.text: His jet-black premonition had finally flooded into his brain from his throat, and even Sakuya's vision was dyed pitch black.
───Aah, Alas! All Sakuya could do now was mutter the dramatic lines of a tragedy.

source.japanese: ああ、この俺、朔屋直正は、男の中でも一番辛い、哀れな境涯、なまじこのべらぼうに綺麗な女の快い言葉の蜜の香りに酔うただけに。気高く澄んだ理性の働きは、耳をくすぐる鐘の音[ね]、それも狂うて、いま、この耳に、ひび割れた音を聞かねばならぬ……ひび割れた音を……。
source.english: Oh, I, Naomasa Sakuya, of men most deject and wretched, who drank the honey of this outrageously beautiful woman's sweet words! Noble, clear reason, once bells to delight the ear, now jangles out of tune. And these ears must hear those cracked notes… those cracked notes…

source.japanese: ───よろよろと食い滓や吸い殻だらけの床に跪いては祈りの形に手を組んで朔屋は、衝撃に半ば盲いた目で天を見上げる───酒場の景気悪い灯りが、この時スポットライトの８の字交差で朔屋を照らし出したのは、なんの気配りか意地悪か。
source.english: He sank unsteadily to his knees on the floor strewn with scraps and cigarette ends. Folding his hands in prayer, he looked toward heaven through eyes half blinded by shock. At that moment the tavern's dismal lights picked him out like spotlights crossing in a figure eight. What solicitude—or what malice—was this?

target.text: Alas, and I, Sakuya Naomasa, of men most deject and wretched, mine is a piteous lot. All for that I have drunk too deep the honey of this fair maiden's musicked words. Now see that noble and most sovereign reason, like sweet bells jangled, out of time and harsh; now, within mine ears, all that remains is naught but a hollow toll……a hollow toll……

───Reeling, Sakuya fell to his knees, landing on the floor covered in tobacco ashes and food scraps, hands linked in prayer, then looked up at the ceiling with eyes half-blind from shock───was it a form of consideration or malice that, in this very moment, the dull lights of the bar swept around in a ballyhoo centered on Sakuya?

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あらオフェーリア。シェイクスピアなんて、今どき退屈だわ」
source.english: “Oh, Ophelia. Shakespeare's so boring these days.”

source.japanese: ずばりと斬り落とされて朔屋は、空しく舞台袖に退場を……空しいも何も、今が機会と、ぶんぶん頭を振って目の霞をなんとか払い、酒場のドアーを蹴り開けて尻に帆駆けてとんずらを決めこんだだけの事───
source.english: Cut down so neatly, Sakuya made a futile exit into the wings… Futile, nothing. He seized his chance, shook his head vigorously to clear his blurred sight, kicked the tavern door open, and fled with all sail set—

target.text: 【Rui】 「Oh, Ophelia. I do find Shakespeare dreadfully tedious these days.」

Decisively cut down, Sakuya fruitlessly made to exit stage left……fruitless, no, now was his chance; he violently shook his head to dispel the haze from his eyes, kicked open the door to the bar, took to his heels, he just decided to bolt, that was all───

source.japanese: ……ま、逃げ出したというたかて、酒場の姉さん相手に好き放題に盛りまくり、得体の知れない混ざり酒を流しこんだ腰や足では走るといってもたかが知れている。心臓は破れんばかりに乱打して、舌は口内に膨れあがり、もう走れない、もう限界、血を吐く思いの不如帰、これだけ走ったなら酒場も遠い、あの女だってまけただろう、でもこの覚えがある匂いは、なんだ？
source.english: …Well, fled. After rutting to his heart's content with the tavern woman and pouring unknown adulterated liquor down his throat, his hips and legs could only carry him so far. His heart beat fit to burst; his tongue swelled in his mouth. No more running. He had reached his limit. Like a cuckoo crying itself bloody. Surely he had run far enough to leave the tavern well behind. Surely he had shaken that woman off. But what was this familiar smell?

source.japanese: 温く微かに生臭く街中では聞かれない匂い、わりと最近に鼻にした───なんのことはない、潮の香だ。いつしか蹲っていたのは、波止場の縁、海の際だ。背後にはまだ酒場の灯りが滲んでいる。なにほどもない、百米程度しか距離が稼げていない。
source.english: Warm, faintly fishy, not a smell found in the streets. He had smelled it fairly recently. Nothing mysterious: the sea. He found himself crouching at the edge of the wharf, beside the water. The tavern lights still blurred behind him. He had gained barely a hundred meters.

source.japanese: なのにもう走れない。朔屋は脂汗だらだら、筑波山麓の蝦蟇もかくやに垂れ流して唇歪める、悪い、気持ちが悪い、ひどく気分が悪い。港の夜灯りが切な涙に滲んでぼやけてぐるぐる廻る、廻っているのは世界か頭の中か、どちらにしても酒を喰らった後でこんなに回すなんてひどい、これはきっと悪酔いしている……。
source.english: Yet he could run no farther. Greasy sweat streamed from him as prodigiously as from the legendary oil-sweating toad of Mount Tsukuba, and his lips twisted. Bad. He felt bad. Horribly sick. The harbor's night lights blurred through miserable tears and went round and round. Was the world spinning, or the inside of his head? Either way, it was cruel to set things spinning after he had been drinking. Surely he was drunk in the very worst way…

source.japanese:
悪酔いしているからこの体たらくなのだ、と気づくどころではない朔屋、喉に指つき入れて、不快の源を根限りにちらちら夜光虫瞬く入江にぶちまけ始めたりでどうにもこうにも、繋留索に足を乗せて遠く想うのが少年達の憧れの船乗りなら、防波堤の縁で頭を逆さに反吐ぶちまけるこの男は、典型的な屑の船乗りの見本であろう。自分の始末は自分でつけろが船乗りだろうとなんだろうと、いい大人の常識であり、船や宿に帰る通りすがりもいないでもなかったけれど、朔屋の事など皆礼儀正しく無視で過ぎていく。
　むしろ海に逆さに蹴り落とされなかっただけ幸運と言えようが、この夜は上空に居合わせたカミサマの一柱もあったらしい。朔屋の傍へわざわざ寄ってきた男があったのである。これをカミサマの善意と見るのは微妙なところ。
source.english:
Sakuya was in no condition to realize that drink itself accounted for his sorry state. He thrust his fingers into his throat and began emptying the source of his misery, with all his strength, into the inlet where luminous plankton flickered. Really, now. If the sailor of boys' dreams stood with one foot on a mooring line, gazing into the distance, this man hanging his head over a breakwater and spewing vomit was a model of the typical worthless sailor. Sailor or otherwise, a grown man was expected to clean up his own mess. A few people passed on their way back to ships or lodgings. They all politely ignored him.
He might have counted himself lucky not to be kicked headfirst into the sea. Yet one of the gods apparently happened to be overhead that night. A man deliberately came over to him. Whether this could be called divine benevolence was debatable.

target.text: ……Well, he did escape, in a sense, but he had been unrestrained in his relentless copulating with the lady from the bar, then knocked back some dubious rotgut, so though he ran using his hips and legs, it didn't amount to much.
