His heart battered away like it was on the verge of exploding, his tongue swelled up inside his mouth, he could not run any longer, he was at his limits, a cuckoo on the verge of coughing up blood, and having run this far, the bar must be distant now; surely that woman must have given up, but this familiar smell, what was it? (TN: The mention of a cuckoo here is a reference to the novel "不如帰", known in English as "The Cuckoo", written in 1899 by author Tokutomi Roka.)

A lukewarm, faintly fishy smell of the sort you wouldn't pick up in town, one he'd smelled quite recently─── why, it was nothing noteworthy at all, just the scent of the tide. Before realizing it, he found himself squatting down before the edge of a wharf, at the verge of the sea. The light from the bar still bled through from behind him. That, too, was not noteworthy in the least, for he had only gained around 100 metres in distance.

And yet he could no longer run. Sakuya was covered in greasy sweat, discharging oil like the toads at the base of mount Tsukuba, lips twisted; sick, he felt sick, he felt terribly sick. The night lights of the port grew hazy through his miserable tears and spun, round and round; was it the world spinning or the insides of his head, regardless of which, it was awful to be spun around like this after having knocked back some drinks, this had to be some form of drunken sickness……

Far beyond the point of realizing that his pathetic predicament stemmed from drinking himself sick, Sakuya shoved his fingers down his throat, then began to unleash the source of his discomfort into the inlet, surface glittering with Noctiluca scintillans, a lost cause; if the ideal sailor, the aspiration of boys the world over, stood with a foot on the hawser, gazing onto the sea and dreaming of distant shores, then this man, hanging his head upside down over the edge of the wharf and vomiting up the contents of his stomach, would surely be the very model of low-life sailor scum.

And given that sailors always cleaned up their own messes no matter what, which was really just common sense for any sensible adult, it wasn't that there was nobody passing by on their way back to their boats or lodgings, they simply all courteously ignored Sakuya as they walked past. If anything, one could say he should count himself lucky they didn't kick him into the sea head first, but it seemed like there was a god in the heavens watching over Sakuya on this night. There was a man who purposefully strode to Sakuya's side. It was a bit questionable if one could truly call this an act of goodwill by a god, however.

source.japanese: 酔うて吐いて苦しいのは所詮本人であり、他人がどれだけ気遣おうと紛れるものではないのだし、そもそも善意有る神ならば、泪と朔屋を引き合わせもしないだろう。大体寄ってきた男だって、興がっている風はあっても朔屋を親身に案じている様には見えなかった。
source.english: After all, the suffering of drunken vomiting belonged to the vomiter. No amount of concern from others could relieve it. And a benevolent god would never have brought Rui and Sakuya together in the first place. Besides, though the approaching man looked amused, he hardly seemed to feel any heartfelt concern.

source.japanese:
【？？？】
「なんだなあ兄さん。悪い酒のようだ」
source.english: “Well now, brother. Looks like bad liquor.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああいやちょっと。うべべべべべ」
source.english: “Oh, no, just a little—bleuuugh.”

source.japanese: 不快に酸い逆噴射の、弱まる谷間を選って首をどうにかねじ向ければ、白い着物に灰黒の地に細縞の袴[はかま]、年の頃なら朔屋と同年代、若いのに今どき珍しい和装の男だったりしたから、朔屋は一時吐き止めてその男をほとんど不躾なまでに見つめた。和装を着馴らして肌に馴染ませた様子は、前時代の書生かさもなくばお釜帽の探偵じみた扮装で、ただ両の眼の色のみが、風変わりに蒼かった、冴えた水晶のように、どこまでも透徹して蒼い。が、異国の血が混じっている骨相ではない。
source.english: In a lull between unpleasantly sour eruptions, he managed to twist his neck. White kimono; fine-striped hakama of dark gray. A young man about Sakuya's age, dressed in Japanese clothes, an uncommon sight these days. Sakuya stopped vomiting for a moment and stared almost rudely. The ease with which the clothes lay upon him suggested an old-fashioned student, or perhaps a detective in a bowler hat. Only his eyes were unusual: blue, clear and penetrating as flawless crystal. His features, however, showed no sign of foreign blood.

source.japanese:
待てよ、朔屋は疑念を抱く。港街の灯りを逆光に受けているのに、何故この男の目の色までが見てとれるのだ、と。
　一度疑ってみてようやく、朔屋は男の目が夜闇に自ずと蒼い燐光を放っている事に気づいたのである。
source.english:
Wait. Sakuya grew suspicious. With the lights of the port behind him, how could he make out even the color of the man's eyes?
Only once he asked himself this did he notice that the eyes themselves gave off a blue phosphorescence in the dark.

source.japanese:
海面にまばらに漂う夜光虫の、ぼんやりと頼りなく、どことなく不気味な火とも異なる、浄い光だ。それが和装の男の、端正ながらも油断ならない貌立ちに、独特な風合いを与えていた。飄々としているといえばいいのか、どこか得体が知れないというのか。口元に溜めた笑みは皮肉げと言えたが、不遜、と切り捨てるにはどこか枯れて落ち着いた佇まいで一種の風格をさえ漂わせ、なにやら達人の境涯を見たような心地にさえさせられて。
　懐手で朔屋をけしかけたのも、ただ軽口というにはどこか独特の気風が香る。
source.english:
A pure light, unlike the dim, uncertain, faintly uncanny glow of the luminous plankton scattered over the sea. It gave the man's handsome but dangerous features a peculiar character. Carefree—or somehow unfathomable? The smile about his mouth could be called sardonic. But to dismiss it as insolence would miss the seasoned calm of his bearing, the distinct air of mastery that almost made one feel one was looking at an adept.
Even the way he stood with his hands tucked inside his clothes and urged Sakuya on had a flavor beyond ordinary banter.

target.text: Getting drunk, throwing up, and suffering was, after all, entirely on the shoulders of the man who drank, and were somebody else to worry about him, could it not be some form of scam or trickery, and if there even was a well-meaning god, then Sakuya wouldn't have met with Rui at all. To begin with, this man who approached, while he seemed interested and somewhat amused, did not show any signs of kindly concern for Sakuya.
【???】 「What's going on with you, man? You look plastered.」
【Naomasa】 「Aah, no, just a little. Blaargrgh!」

Finding a moment where the foul outward surges of stomach acid abated, he turned his neck, and there, he saw a man dressed in a white kimono with a pinstriped, dark-grey hakama over it, his age placing him somewhere in the same generation as Sakuya, young, and yet wearing a Japanese style of clothing that made a rare sight these days, and for a time, Sakuya ceased his vomiting as he stared at the man until it was almost impolite.

He looked very at home in the Japanese clothes, as if it were a second skin to him, and while it looked like the sort of costume one might wear to dress up as a student of a bygone era, or if not that, perhaps a bowler-hatted detective, it was just that, the colour of both his eyes, they were an unusual blue, like frigid crystals, a perfectly clear and penetrating azure. Still, there was nothing phrenological or anything in his skeletal build that suggested he carried even a drop of foreign blood. (TN: The detective here is a reference to Kindaichi Kousuke, the main character of Yokomizo Seishi's long-running series of detective novels.)

Hold on, Sakuya thought, misgivings in his mind. The lights of the port town were behind this man, casting him in deep silhouette, so how, then, could he so clearly discern even the colour of this man's eyes, he wondered. Now that he had questioned it once, Sakuya finally realized that this man's eyes were naturally emitting an azure phosphorescence in the dark of the night.

Unlike the hazy, indefinite, somehow eerie flames of the Noctiluca scintillans floating in scattered clusters across the ocean surface, it was a pure light. It gave a unique feel to the handsome yet cunning countenance of this man clad in Japanese clothing. Perhaps one could describe it as an air of easygoing aloofness, or perhaps as strange and unfathomable in some way.

The smile playing on his lips carried a hint of cynical irony, and yet, to dismiss him merely as arrogant would be to undersell his weathered composure, a subdued maturity that lent him a distinct air of dignity, almost leaving one with the impression of having witnessed the inner state of mind of a true master. And even as he goaded Sakuya with his hands still in the space between his kimono's inner and outer layers, though it was nothing but lighthearted banter, it was still tinged with a characteristic flair.

source.japanese:
【和服の男】
「おお吐け吐いちまえ。
　なんもかんも出しちまった方が、いっそ楽だぞ」
source.english:
“Go on, puke it all up.
Better out than in.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おお全くだ。
　せっかく今夜はそこそこ上手い酒が飲めたのに。
　せっかく女も抱けたのに───うげえええええ」
source.english:
“Exactly.
Finally had some half-decent liquor tonight.
Finally got to sleep with a woman—bleuuuuugh!”

source.japanese: 酔いと快楽の名残は泪との思いもかけない再会に一気に醒め、まして彼女が同じ船に乗りこむとあっては。どんな上等の酒だって、たちまちに人を害する悪酒と化そう。ふらりと現れた見知らぬ男を警戒するより、まずは毒を出してしまう事が先決と、薄ぼんやりとした夜闇湛えた海に益体もない反吐の色をぶちまける朔屋の、中味がでんぐり返りそうなこの苦しみよ、せめて引き換えに彼を曖昧酒場から遠ざけてくれるくらいの知恵を与えてくれるのなら。望み薄な願いだろうが。
source.english: The last glow of drink and pleasure had been dispelled at a stroke by his unexpected reunion with Rui—and now she was coming aboard the same ship. Under such circumstances, the finest liquor would turn instantly poisonous. Before he worried about the stranger who had drifted out of nowhere, the first order of business was to get the poison out. Sakuya splashed the pointless colors of his vomit across the dim night pooled on the sea, suffering as though his insides were about to somersault. If only this misery would grant him, in exchange, wisdom enough to keep away from shady taverns. A faint hope, admittedly.

source.japanese: しかしたとい朔屋が、悪所を憚るだけの知恵をつけたにせよ、縁というのは良きにせよ悪しにせよ、一度結ばれてしまえば中々に断ち切りがたい。というのも。己の吐瀉物が逆流して、鼻からも戻していた朔屋にさえ、嗅ぎ取れる芳しい空気が、ふわりと訪れた。香水の加減を知らず、振りすぎた勘違い女のどぎつい匂いではない。品良く元からの肌の匂いと混淆された、床しい匂いであるのに、朔屋のつまった鼻の奥に届いたのである。或いは肌それ自体で感じ取ったのかも知れない。真に美しい女を傍にすれば、男なんぞは単純な構築物、五感はシンプルに女の全てを感じる為に、目や鼻の別など忘れるのである。
source.english: Yet even if Sakuya acquired enough sense to avoid such places, a bond once formed, good or bad, was difficult to sever. For now a fragrant air softly arrived, perceptible even to him as his own vomit came back through his nose. Not the overpowering stink of a foolish woman who did not know how much perfume to use. A discreet, lovely scent, gracefully mingled with the natural smell of skin. Yet it reached the depths of his clogged nose. Or perhaps his skin itself sensed it. Beside a truly beautiful woman, a man was a simple construction: all five senses existed merely to perceive her, forgetting any distinction between eye and nose.

source.japanese:
ただ寄ってきたのがいかに佳い女といっても、朔屋にとっては取り扱い細心の注意を要すの泪ときては、わざわざ追いかけてきてくれたといえども、手放しで喜ぶどころでない。
　えづきが、一層にひどくなったのを、さて単純に無礼と誹っていいものかどうか。
source.english:
But however beautiful the approaching woman, she was Rui, whom Sakuya had to handle with the utmost care. That she had taken the trouble to follow him was hardly cause for unqualified joy.
His retching grew worse. Whether one could condemn this as mere bad manners was another question.

target.text: 【Man in Japanese clothing】 「Oooh, puke away, puke it up. Getting it all outta your system will actually leave you feeling much better.」
【Naomasa】 「Ugh, damn right. And here I finally got to drink some pretty decent booze tonight. I finally got to lay with a woman, too, and then───bleeeeecch!」

He had been roused from his intoxication and remnants of pleasure all at once at his unexpected reunion with Rui, and all the more so when she claimed she was going to board the same ship as him. No matter how excellent the liquor, it would instantly be reduced to swill unfit for human consumption.

Rather than being guarded towards this unfamiliar man who suddenly showed up out of nowhere, he decided to prioritize ridding himself of the poison, and so Sakuya spewed the wretched hues of his bile into the sea full of the murky dark of night; oh, this anguish, it was like his insides were doing somersaults, if only it could bestow upon him the wisdom to keep at a distance from seedy bars in exchange. Probably a wish with dim prospects.

However, even supposing that Sakuya obtained the wisdom to at least have some scruples about entering houses of ill repute, ties are, for better or worse, quite difficult to cut once made. Because. Even after regurgitating his own vomit through his own nose, he picked up on a fragrant air softly floating his way.

It was not the cloying smell of a deluded woman who knew not the strength of her perfumes and applied far too much. It had intermixed with a scent of skin that was refined to begin with, an elegant fragrance, and so it managed to reach the depths of Sakuya's clogged nose. Or perhaps it was the very skin itself he sensed. Indeed, with but a beautiful woman placed at his side, man is a very simple creature: all his five senses exist but for to sense a woman's everything, any distinction between nose and ear forgotten.

But no matter how good a woman it was who drew closer, considering it was Rui, who, in Sakuya's eyes, required the utmost care when handling, down to every last detail of their interactions, even had she gone out of her way to chase him down, he could not truly be happy with the situation. His nauseous regorging grew even worse, but then again, was it really fair to dismiss it as pure rudeness on his part?

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そんなになるまで呑むなんて、案外お酒との付き合い方が不得意なのね、直さん」
source.english: “Drinking yourself into such a state. You're less adept with liquor than I'd thought, Nao.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あっはっは、あなたに言われるたぁ、
　もう笑いしかでてこないわ。
　……えーろろろろぉ～～」
source.english:
“Ha ha ha. Coming from you, that's… I can only laugh.
…Blerorororooo…”

source.japanese:
【和装の男】
「悪酔いすんのも気持ち良う呑むも、どっちだって酒の醍醐味さね、姐さん───って」
source.english: “A rotten drunk or a merry one—either way, that's the joy of booze, sister—”

source.japanese: 箴言なのか軽口なのか、いずれとも受け取れる言葉の尻がふと途切れ、二人の視線が行き交う朔屋の背中越し、二人ともこれでは青年を気遣っているのか野次馬なのか判別できない事である。
source.english: Was it aphorism or flippancy? It could pass for either—until the tail end of the remark suddenly broke off and the two exchanged looks over Sakuya’s back. As things stood, there was no telling whether either of them was concerned for the young man or merely there for the spectacle.

target.text: 【Rui】 「To think you'd let yourself end up in such a sorry state. Who knew you were so poor at carrying your drink, Nao-san?」
【Naomasa】 「Ah-hah-hah, hearing that from you, all I can do is laugh. ……Ech-grgrlgrlgrglooh～～」
【Man in Japanese clothing】 「Whether you drink yourself sick or have a nice, pleasant time with it, either one's part of the real pleasure of drinking, lady───woah.」

Was he quoting some proverb or just being flippant? Regardless of how one interpreted it, the end of his sentence was suddenly cut off, and both exchanged glances over Sakuya's back; it wasn't possible to discern if they were being considerate of the young man or just rubbernecking.

source.english: “Oh, you—”

source.japanese:
【和服の男】
「なんだ、あんたか」
source.english: “Oh. It's you.”

source.japanese: お互い面識があるらしい二人が、反吐に苦しむ自分の頭の上で遣り取りしているのが朔屋にはいささか鬱陶しくて、大人しく吐いていればいいのに割りこんで、
source.english: Apparently they knew each other. Their conversation over his head as he struggled with vomiting irritated Sakuya. He should have quietly got on with being sick. Instead, he interrupted—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うえええ気持ち悪い。あ、あんたこの女の知り合いか。悪いことぁ言わない、関わり合いにならない方がいい。この女はこう見た目は良いが、関わった男は軒並み破滅するんだ」
source.english: “Ugh, I feel awful. Oh, you know her? Take my advice: keep away. She looks good, but every man who gets involved with her comes to ruin.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あのね、直さん、わたくし、こちらとそんなに親しくはないの。ちょっと前にこちらに訊かれただけなのよ」
source.english: “Nao, we're not particularly close. He simply asked me something a little while ago.”
“…What?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「貴方のことを」
source.english: “About you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はん？　なんだ、あんた、もしかして俺の事を捜してたの？」
source.english: “Huh? What, were you looking for me?”

source.japanese: まだ吐ききったわけではないが、少しずつ間歇泉の感覚が間遠になって、口を挟みやすくなって、朔屋はようよう頭をもたげる。なんだとて、今夜はわざわざ自分を訪ねる者と二人も出くわす、しかも一方は悪縁の巡り合わせにある女であり、もう一方など見も知らぬ、これはまたいかさまなと朔屋は、この時はただ珍しい事と暢気に構えていたのだが、しっぺ返しは間近に迫っていた。
source.english: He had not emptied himself completely, but the geyser's eruptions were growing farther apart, leaving more room for conversation. At last he lifted his head. Two people had come looking expressly for him tonight. One was a woman bound to him by disastrous fortune; the other, someone he had never seen before. How odd. Just then Sakuya regarded it as no more than a curious occurrence. The consequences were close at hand.

source.japanese:
【和服の男】
「ああ、そんなとこだな」
source.english: “Yeah. More or less.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺になんか用か。っても俺いまご覧の案配。まともな受け答えはできかねるんでまた明日にでも」
source.english: “Want something from me? Well, you can see the state I'm in. Not fit for a proper conversation. Try again tomorrow.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あのね、貴方。こちらは智里さんといって、『殺し屋』よ。
　それもとっても腕が立つって評判の」
source.english:
“Listen, dear. This is Tomosato. He's an assassin.
Reputedly a very capable one.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そんな方が誰かを捜しているってなったら、なんのつもりなのかは言わずともわかるでしょうに」
source.english: “If a man like that is looking for someone, surely his intentions need no explanation.”

source.japanese: 事ここにいたって朔屋の喉は、奇妙なしゃっくりを大きく一つあげて、えづきさえも止まって、智里という、和装の男をまじまじ見つめる。痩せ形と見えたその男は、ただ肉付きが薄いのではなく、無駄な肉一切そぎ落とされた、強靱な武器のような筋骨をしており、そうと覚ると、身内が我知らず震えてくる程の威力を秘めているのだった。
source.english: At this, Sakuya's throat gave one enormous, peculiar hiccup; even the retching stopped. He stared at Tomosato, the man in Japanese dress. What he had taken for slenderness was not mere lack of flesh: every useless ounce had been pared away, leaving a frame of muscle and bone like a tempered weapon. Once Sakuya understood what lay concealed there, his body began to tremble of its own accord.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんた、まさか」
source.english: “You… surely not…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Goodness, you're───」
【Man in Japanese clothing】 「Oh, it's you?」

Sakuya felt a little depressed at having these two, who seemed mutually acquainted, start conversing over his own head as he suffered in his fits of vomiting, and even though he should just have stayed still and kept vomiting, he intruded on the conversation,

【Naomasa】 「Bleeeech, I feel sick. Y-, you know this woman? I'm telling you this for your own good, you really shouldn't involve yourself with her. This woman might look real good, but every single man who's gotten involved with her has been ruined.」
【Rui】 「Now listen here, Nao-san, I am not that close with this man. He merely asked something of me a short while ago.」
【Naomasa】 「……Hm? Asked what?」
【Rui】 「About you, dear.」
【Naomasa】 「Huh? Why? Were you maybe looking for me or something?」

He hadn't quite finished throwing everything up yet, but bit by bit, the geyser-like sensation ebbed away, and as it became easier to close his mouth, Sakuya finally raised his head fully. For whatever the cause, two people had intentionally sought him out tonight; moreover, one was a woman with whom he had shared ill-fated encounters of chance, the other a complete stranger, and Sakuya thought the latter had to be some sort of scam; right now, he was taking it lightly, believing it all to be nothing but an unusual occurrence, but the retaliation for that was drawing near.
【Man in Japanese clothing】 「Yeah, something like that.」
【Naomasa】 「Do you have some business with me? Or, well, it should be plain from looking. It's a little hard for me to give a proper answer right now, but perhaps tomorrow?」
【Rui】 「A moment, dear. This man goes by the name Tomosato, and he is a『hired killer』. He is also renowned for being very able at his work.」
【Rui】 「If a man such as him is looking for someone, I do not suppose it needs to be said what exactly it is that he intends.」

As the situation continued to spiral out of his control, Sakuya's throat let out a large, odd hiccup, his nausea ceased too, and he stared intently at this Tomosato, this man in Japanese clothing. The man looked to be of a slender build, but his physique was not sparse in musculature: every bit of wasteful flesh had been pruned, his body wrought of muscles and bone like a tough, powerful weapon, and as he realized as much, it hid within it a power so grave it made Sakuya's whole body instinctively tremble at his presence.
【Naomasa】 「You're-, you can't be.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おうとも。俺は人殺しだよ。あんたを殺すために雇われた、ね」
source.english: “Oh yes. I'm a killer. Hired to kill you, in fact.”

source.japanese: 全くもって飄然と、小石でも放るようにぬけぬけと言い放ったものだった。
source.english: He said it with perfect ease, as casually as tossing a pebble.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「誰が、なんだって俺なんかを、何の為に」
source.english: “Who? Why me? What for?”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そいつをうっかりばらすような殺し屋が有るもんかい。まあ人の怨みなんざ、どこで買うか知れたもんじゃないって事だなあ」
source.english: “What assassin carelessly gives that away? You never know where you might earn somebody's resentment.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どこかの奥様にでも、手をつけたんじゃなくって？　女遊びは殿方の甲斐性とはいうけれど、上手に立ち回れる方でないと、火傷はつきものよ」
source.english: “Have you been putting your hands on someone's wife? They say chasing women is a mark of a man's prowess. But unless you know how to go about it, you're bound to get burned.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「But of course I can. I am a murderer. I was hired to kill you, 'kay?」
As nonchalant as could be, he blurted out that statement so brazenly, as if he were merely tossing a pebble in his direction.
【Naomasa】 「Who did, and why in the world for someone like me, for what reason?」
【Tomosato】 「Good luck finding a hired killer who'll just let that slip. Well, you never know where you might have incurred someone's wrath, right? It's something like that.」

【Rui】 「Did you perchance have an affair with someone's wife somewhere? They say that a gentleman's worth is measured by his philandering, but be that as it may, if you are unable to conduct yourself tactfully, you will inevitably be burned for it.」

source.japanese:
───高い水音と、水飛沫が跳ね上がる。
　朔屋が海に転落したのは、ショックでバランスを崩したせいか、はたまた殺し屋への恐怖に恐慌来して海中に逃れようとしたからか。
　その彼を運良く近くに転がっていた漁師の鉤竿で海から引き上げたのが殺し屋、智里だとあっては、浮かない笑い話という他ない。
source.english:
A high splash, and water leapt into the air.
Had Sakuya toppled into the sea because the shock threw him off balance? Or had fear of the assassin sent him into such a panic that he tried to take refuge underwater?
And when the man who fished him out with a fisherman’s gaff that happened, conveniently, to be lying nearby was Tomosato the assassin himself—well, the whole affair could only be called a joke no one felt like laughing at.

target.text: ───A spray of water flew up from below, accompanied by the loud sound of splashing water. Was it because he lost his balance from the shock that Sakuya dove into the water, or was he gripped by panic from the terror he felt towards the hired killer and attempted to escape into the sea? That he was then pulled out of the sea by someone using a fisherman's gaff fortunately lying nearby, only for that someone to turn out to be none other than the hired killer, this Tomosato, now that could only be considered a sick jest at his expense.

source.japanese: ……翌日信天翁号に戻った朔屋は、半ば風邪を引いて、一人ではろくに立てない有様だった。ずるずる引きずられてきていた。殺し屋智里に。それにのんびり日傘姿で伴っていたのは、泪。
source.english: …The next day, Sakuya returned to the Albatross with the beginnings of a cold, scarcely able to stand alone. He was being dragged along. By Tomosato, the assassin. Accompanying them at an unhurried pace beneath her parasol was Rui.

source.japanese: この日より、信天翁号の面子に泪と智里が加わった。泪はどういう目的が有るのかはっきりとは告げず、ただ信天翁号に乗る必要があったと仄[ほの]めかすのみ。彼女のまとう優雅なる怠惰と気品の所為か、それとも陸から何らかの申し送りがあったのか、泪は信天翁号の中で賓客待遇で、船室も最上等の部屋に陣取り、しかもそれを好き勝手に模様替えして、この襤褸船の中にそこだけ上流階級の居間を作り出して憚らない。
source.english: From that day, Rui and Tomosato joined the company aboard the Albatross. Rui gave no clear account of her purpose, merely hinting that she needed to be on the ship. Whether because of her languid elegance and refinement or some instructions sent from shore, she was treated as an honored guest. She occupied the best cabin, rearranged it however she pleased, and quite unabashedly created an upper-class drawing room in that one corner of the wretched ship.

source.japanese: 智里は智里で、朔屋を殺すために雇われたと公言しつつ、いっかなその手の行動を見せず、それどころか。
source.english: Tomosato, for his part, openly declared that he had been hired to kill Sakuya, yet never made the slightest move to do so. Quite the contrary—

target.text: ……When Sakuya returned to the Albatross the following day, he had partially come down with a cold, and he was in a state where he could barely stand by himself. Being dragged along slowly. By Tomosato, the hired killer. And then, casually accompanying them with parasol in hand, was Rui.

From this day onwards, Rui and Tomosato joined the lineup of the Albatross. Rui did not clearly state what sort of objective she had in doing so, merely alluding to there being a necessity for her to board the Albatross. Perhaps it was a consequence of the elegant indolence and grace the woman was clad in, or perhaps a message of some sort had arrived from land, but Rui was treated as a guest of honour aboard the Albatross: she secured the finest cabin as her room, even changed the design of it however she pleased, and didn't hesitate in the slightest at creating such an upper-class Western living room on board this run-down ship.
Tomosato, in a manner very like him, while openly declaring that he had been hired to kill Sakuya, never actually took any action to that effect. Quite to the contrary.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しかしあんたが殺し屋とはなあ。
　なら獲物はなんなのよ。
　素手で絞め殺すとか？」
source.english:
“Still, you, an assassin. What's your weapon,
then?
Strangle people with your bare hands?”

source.japanese: 上甲板の物陰に二人仲良く隠れて、ずらり並べているのは酒瓶の、厨房その他からちょろまかす時の朔屋と智里ときたら、旧年来の友人のように息が合っており、
source.english: The two hid companionably in a sheltered spot on the upper deck, an array of liquor bottles before them. When it came to pilfering from the galley and elsewhere, Sakuya and Tomosato worked together as smoothly as old friends—

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「But I still can't believe you're a hired killer. What's your weapon of choice then? You strangle people to death with your bare hands or something?」

When the two were hiding in the shade on the upper deck, getting along swimmingly, rows of booze bottles filched from the galley and elsewhere lined up next to them, then Sakuya and Tomosato made a perfect pair, like they'd been friends for years,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「野暮なこと訊くない。
　っても好奇心満々だなお前、物好きな。
　埒もねえ、俺の獲物は、これだ」
source.english:
“Don't ask impertinent questions.
Though you're certainly curious, you oddball.
Oh, never mind. This is my weapon.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Don't ask something that tactless. But aren't you just dying to know, you oddball. Whatever, here, this is my weapon.」

source.japanese:
とどこに隠し持っていたのか、三尺近い太刀を取り出し、抜く手も見せず朔屋の前に居合い抜き、鼻先すれすれに擬された切っ先から、刀身の冴えた冷たさが伝わってくるかのようだった。
　だが酒を喰らい酔うた朔屋は、切っ先の鋭さにも麻痺した体で、上から覗きこみ下から窺っては、珍かな、蝮の腹のようにうねる刀の地肌に喝采打ったりする始末で。
source.english:
From wherever he had concealed it, he produced a sword nearly three feet long. Sakuya never saw the drawing hand move. The point stopped just short of his nose, close enough that he could almost feel the blade's keen chill.
But drink had numbed Sakuya even to the sharpness of the point. He peered at it from above, inspected it from below, and applauded the curious grain of the steel, rippling like a viper's belly.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おっ、おっ、すっげえなあ、真剣だぁ。
　さぞや銘の知れた刀なんだろうが、
　俺にはどうせわかんねえから、
　どうでもいいや」
source.english:
“Oh! Oh, that's amazing! A real sword!
Must be some famous blade.
But I wouldn't know anyway,
so never mind.”

target.text: Where did he even hide that on his person? He pulled out a tachi nearly three shaku in length, then unsheathed it right in front of Sakuya with a draw too fast for the eye to follow, and with the tip of that blade pressed right to his nose, it was as though he could feel the very coolness and clearness of the blade itself through it. But, intoxicated after drinking, Sakuya's body was numbed to the sharpness of the blade; he studied it from the top and examined it from the bottom, then finally let loose a great round of applause for the unusual undulating surface of the sword blade, which twisted and wound like the belly of a pit viper.
【Naomasa】 「Ooh, ooh, amazing, a real sword. I'm sure it's some famous katana and all, but it's not like I'd know, so who cares.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「てめえ、人に抜かせておいて蘊蓄語りはいやだってか。しょうがねえ野郎だなあ。まあ俺も小難しいことどうでもいいわ」
source.english: “You make me draw it, then don't want to hear the lore? You're hopeless. Well, I don't care about the complicated stuff either.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうそう、呑め呑め。
　こんな船から出てきたにしちゃあ、このラム上等だぜえ」
source.english:
“Exactly. Drink up!
This rum's pretty good for something out of a ship like this.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Buddy, you make a man unsheathe his blade for you, and then you don't want to hear his erudite lecture? You're a real hopeless bastard. Well, not that I really give a damn about that kind of bothersome shit myself.」
【Naomasa】 「Right, right, drink, drink. This is some top shelf rum, at least for something that came from this ship.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おうおう、呑もう呑もう。
　俺ゃあつまみもギッてきた。
　ああ、陽も高ぇうちから呑む酒はぁ」
source.english:
“Yes, let's drink.
I stole some snacks, too.
Ah, drinking while the sun's still high—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「最高だぁーーっ」
source.english: “Best there is!”

source.japanese: とこのざまで、刃紋が陸奥の霊山とされる月山の稜線をそのまま映しこんだものであるとか、その辺りの興味深い曰くは一切語られることなく、二人はただただ酒を注いでは飲み干して酔っ払うことに夢中の意気投合ぶり、智里の、殺し屋と言い条、蕩尽の果てに顕れる通人にも通ずる飄々とした物言いと風格も確かに手伝っていたけれど、自分の命を奪いにきた相手と仲良く酒を酌み交わすようでは朔屋、警戒心というものがまるで欠如した馬鹿としか言いようがないのであった。
source.english: Such was their state. None of the interesting lore was told: how the blade's temper pattern reproduced the ridgeline of Mount Gassan, regarded as a sacred mountain of Mutsu, for example. They devoted themselves entirely to pouring liquor, draining it, and getting drunk, in perfect accord. Tomosato's airy speech and bearing certainly helped. Assassin though he was, he had something of the connoisseur's ease, attained at the far end of dissipation. Even so, to exchange friendly drinks with the man who had come to take his life made Sakuya nothing but a fool without a trace of caution.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Yeah, yeah, let's drink, let's drink. I swiped some snacks too. Aah, drinking while the sun's still high in the skyyy!」
【Naomasa】 「IS THE BEEEーーST!」

Thus, reduced to this, the fact that the pattern on the blade itself was an exact projection of the ridgeline of Mount Gassan, hailed as a sacred mountain deep in the old province of Mutsu, or any other deeply fascinating stories of that sort were not spoken of whatsoever; no, the two had simply found a kindred spirit in forgetting themselves in pouring and emptying cups of booze while getting drunk.

And while calling himself a hired killer, Tomosato's style and manner of speaking was so aloof and easygoing that it shared much in common with the sort of worldly man who materializes at the terminus of dissipation; that certainly helped matters, but to share a drink in good spirits with a man who was there to take his life, Sakuya could only be called nothing short of a fool completely lacking any sense of caution.

source.japanese: <01>素直に白状した
source.english: Admit it honestly.

target.text: <01>Honestly confessed

source.japanese: <01>昔の事は水に流す事にした
source.english: Let bygones be bygones.

target.text: <01>Let bygones be bygones

source.japanese: その日も海は紺青の顔料を溶かしこんだかの、四方八方風の一二方位視界届く限りの凪、凪、一面の大凪。海原は潮というよりもっと密度の高い粘体で固めたが如きの穏やかさで、大気の有り様などは宗右衛門猫の髭一筋も揺らさぬ無風状態。時さえ運行を鈍くして、太陽の奴さん午睡を決めこんだか、昼下がりの中天に留まったまま歩みを止めたかのよう。　信天翁号だって、ただ、船体を鈍く軋ませるばかりで、進んでいるのやら休んでいるのやら、だ。
source.english: That day, too, the sea looked as though deep-blue pigment had been dissolved in it. In every direction, to all twelve points of the wind, as far as the eye could reach: calm, calm, one vast calm. The ocean was so still it seemed set in some viscous substance denser than seawater. Not a breath of air stirred so much as one of Mr. Soemon's whiskers. Even time moved sluggishly. The sun appeared to have decided on a nap, halting high in the afternoon sky. The Albatross herself merely creaked dully. Whether she was moving or resting was anyone's guess.

source.japanese: 厳しい規律で成り立つ軍艦であれば、こんな海でも誰かしらこまめに立ち働き、手を動かしていようが、こちらは無頼と無法でもって世に憚る信天翁号。辺りに追っ手の船影も見えず、航海に問題なく、むら気の大なる主機関さえさしたる不満も見せず暢気に燻っているとなると、船内はさてどうなるか。
source.english: On a warship governed by strict discipline, someone would have been busily working even on a sea like this. But this was the Albatross, brazenly making her way through the world on lawlessness and knavery. No pursuing ship in sight, no trouble with the voyage, even the exceedingly temperamental main engine smoldering away contentedly without any particular complaint. What, then, happened aboard?

source.japanese:
掌の皺を読むように見易い事である。
　やる事が無くなるのである。
　仕事を皆放り出すのである。
　皆しててんで好き放題に───
　これが機会と、さぼりまくるのである。
source.english:
As easy to read as the creases of one's palm.
Nothing left to do.
Everyone threw down their work.
Everyone did exactly as they pleased—
They seized the opportunity to shirk with all their might.

source.japanese: よって船には極めて懶惰なる気分が強粘性の脂のように横溢し、隅々まで無為に麻酔させ、たとえば船楼、にては船長がすっかり弛緩して、お大事の人形を掴む指も緩んで手から落としそう、締まり失せた口元からは涎も零れそう、或いは上甲板では水夫長が船員パイプ燻らすもどこか上の空、頭は水平線にもたげられたが、眼差しの焦点ぶれて、彼の心は昨夜読み耽[ふけ]った悪漢小説の世界を反芻するばかりで───頑陋にして口やかましい水夫長殿からしてこれだもの。
source.english: An extraordinary sloth spread through the ship like thick, sticky grease, anesthetizing every corner into idleness. In the deckhouse, for example, the captain had gone utterly limp. The fingers holding her precious doll slackened as though about to let it fall; saliva threatened to escape her loose mouth. On the upper deck, the boatswain smoked his sailor's pipe absentmindedly. His head faced the horizon, but his eyes were out of focus. His mind merely chewed over the world of the picaresque novel in which he had immersed himself last night. Even the stubborn, narrow-minded, perpetually scolding boatswain was like this.

source.japanese: 船内では勤勉の部類に属す下級水夫達でさえ、当番の無い者は寝網に揺られ揺られてゆうらゆら、揺れも寝息も船のうねりに同期したのが並ぶ様はまさに『毛布の入江』の喩えに相応しい、番のある者達だって、思い思いに仕事を手放し物陰に潜[ひそ]むは或いは半ば公然と甲板に座って欠伸を吐くはで、もう。共通するのはいずれも心も体も停滞させ、怠けているからとて余所事に興ずるわけでもないという、これでは船全体が麻痺している、に近い。船上空のアホウドリも、舞うと言うより宙に静止したような。
source.english: Even the junior sailors, counted among the ship's diligent hands, swayed and swayed in their hammocks when off duty. Their swinging and sleeping breaths kept time with the roll of the ship; the rows of them fully deserved the name ‘Blanket Bay.’ Those on duty, meanwhile, abandoned their tasks and hid away, or sat on deck yawning almost openly. Really. What they shared was a stagnation of mind and body. They were not neglecting work to enjoy something else. The whole ship was closer to paralysis. Even the albatross overhead seemed less to fly than to hang motionless in the air.

source.japanese: 中には「死体ごっこ」と称するいかがわしげな遊戯、というのかもっと直截に「死んだ真似」というのが早いのか、要は食中毒、餓死、気死、マラリア等々の死因を勝手に想定して索具や箱にもたれるなり、甲板に転がるなりして死んだまね、に耽[ふけ]る一団があって、常なら本当にくたばったと勘違いした同類に、たちどころに袋に縫った帆布に重しと共に詰め込まれて水葬なのだろうが、この時は誰もがちらりと一瞥で撫でるきり。
source.english: One group indulged in a dubious game called ‘Playing Corpses.’ Or ‘Pretending to Be Dead,’ to put it more directly. Each invented a cause of death—food poisoning, starvation, shock, malaria, and so on—then leaned against rigging or crates, or sprawled on deck, and played dead. Ordinarily, their fellows might mistake them for actual corpses and promptly stitch them into weighted canvas sacks for burial at sea. Today, everyone merely brushed them with a glance.

source.japanese:
動的なのは、船中ほとんど見えやしない。
　趣味であれ個人の愉[たの]しみであれなんであれ、およそ活動的な一切に勤しむことは、船内の不文律に触れる、とでも言うかのように放棄せられて、恐らくは誰も敢えて挑むまい、ああそうだとも、およそこのべた凪の続く限りは。
source.english:
Almost nothing aboard was in motion.
Hobbies, private amusements, anything requiring activity had been abandoned, as though it violated an unwritten rule of the ship. Probably no one would dare challenge that rule. Yes, indeed. Not while this flat calm lasted.

target.text: It was yet another day where navy blue pigment had dissolved into the sea and spread through its waters, and in all directions cardinal and zodiac, as far as the eye could see, the wind was calm, a lull, the whole surface calm. The open sea was so quiet and mild it was as though it had been solidified by a denser, more viscous substance, the air so windless that not even a strand of Souemon the cat's whiskers were rustled by it.

Even the motion of time itself seemed to have dulled, and our friend the sun had decided to take an afternoon nap, standing still at her zenith this early afternoon, stuck in the heavens. The Albatross was no different, simply slowly and clumsily creaking along, uncertain if she was moving forwards or taking a break; so it was.

Were this a naval ship ran under strict discipline, even on a sea this calm, there would be someone working diligently and briskly, hands on deck and in motion, but this was the Albatross, famed throughout the world for her villainy and lawlessness. There was not a shadow of any pursuing ships to be seen in the vicinity, the voyage was smooth sailing, and even the capricious great main engine showed no particular dissatisfaction, smouldering and sputtering away with not a care in the world, but what of within the ship?

It was as plain to see as the nose on your face. They all had nothing to do. They all abandoned their posts. All doing whatever they pleased─── Using this as an excuse, they all slacked off as best they could.

And so, an exceedingly indolent mood spread throughout, like the ship had been inundated with an incredibly viscous fat, every nook and cranny anesthetized in idleness; take, for example, the watchtower, where the captain had grown completely flaccid, the fingers clutching her precious dolly now so limp it was about to fall from her hand, drool about to spill out of her mouth that had lost any semblance of firmness.

Or elsewhere, on the main deck, where the Bosun smoking his sailor's pipe seemed to have his head in the clouds, raised to the horizon, but his eyes were blurry and unfocused, his mind musing on the world of the picaresque novel he had been immersed in reading all last night and nothing else───even our stubborn, mean, nagging Bosun had been reduced to this.

Within the ship itself, even the deck boys possessed of a diligent nature who weren't on watch were swaying back and forth in their hammocks, rocked in a rhythmic lull, the way they shook and breathed in their sleep synchronizing with the rolling of the ship in such a manner that describing it metaphorically as 『a cove of blankets』 was quite apt, and even those on watch, why, they had abandoned their work in whatever way they preferred, some seeking refuge in the shade, others simply overtly sitting on the deck and yawning, but enough about that.

The commonality they held was that their minds and bodies had come to a standstill, and because they were slacking off, there was no way they'd find any interest in matters that didn't concern them directly, and so the whole ship was in a state of paralysis, or close enough to. Even the albatrosses in the air above the ship seemed more like they were suspended in mid-air than soaring in circles through it.

Some among them had come to play a dubious game they had dubbed "playing dead", or perhaps it would be quicker to more directly call it "pretending to be dead": in essence, a group of deck boys had engrossed themselves in leaning against the rigging and boxes, even falling over on the deck, and acting dead after arbitrarily assuming causes of death such as food poisoning, starvation, apoplexy, malaria, and many others.

Under normal circumstances, their fellow kind would mistakenly think they had actually kicked the bucket and quickly stuff them into canvas bags sewn from a sail cloth and filled with weights, then given them a proper sailor's burial at sea, but right now, nobody could bother to do more than spare them a brief glance and pat them on their heads.

There was barely any dynamism to be found aboard this ship. As if to say that devoting oneself to any active pursuit, even be they hobbies or personal pleasures, that giving even the smallest of efforts would violate the unwritten rules of this ship, so fully had they abandoned everything, and it was likely none would dare to challenge that; yes indeed, so it certainly was, at least for as long as this calm at sea endured.

source.japanese:
さてそんな中、朔屋青年は、といえば。
　事ある毎に当直や雑務放り出し、備蓄のラム酒に手を出しては水夫長に首を絞められ宗右衛門猫には体当たりを喰らい、索具にけつまずいた振りでシサム・キサラの尻へ頬摺りしようとして、双子の息の合った平手により両の奥歯をぐらつかせ、けれど懲りずに今度は着替えを覗こうとて彼女達の船室の鍵穴覗けば穴越しに見えたのは回転式拳銃の銃口、危うく片目の風通しが良くなるところだったりしているのが常日頃の彼だ。
（いっそそうされたほうが、役にも立たない脳味噌の目方が整理され、多少はさっぱりしただろうという意見はさておくとして）
　さぞやこの降って湧いたような自由を満喫している事と思われた、のだが───
source.english:
And amid all this, what of young Sakuya?
Usually he abandoned watches and chores at every opportunity, raided the rum stores, and earned a throttling from the boatswain or a bodily charge from Mr. Soemon. He would pretend to trip over rigging and try to rub his cheek against Sisam's or Kisara's backside, whereupon their synchronized slaps loosened the molars on both sides of his mouth. Undeterred, he might next attempt to watch them changing through the cabin keyhole, only to find a revolver's muzzle looking back. He had narrowly escaped improved ventilation through one eye. That was his everyday life.
Let us set aside the view that such ventilation might have trimmed the weight of his useless brain and left him somewhat refreshed.
One might therefore expect him to be making the most of this unlooked-for freedom. But—

source.japanese:
───確かに朔屋は、上甲板の下級水夫達と同様、船内通路にぶち転がってはいた。だがその、跪いたなりに肩が前にずるずるのめって尻ばかりが中途半端に突きだされた、の格好は、あまりのんびりくつろいでいる風ではない。
　むしろ、重力に耐えかねその体を支える事さえも億劫だ、だと言いたげな。
source.english:
—He was certainly sprawled in a passageway, much like the junior sailors on the upper deck. Yet his posture hardly suggested leisurely relaxation. Still on his knees, his shoulders had slumped farther and farther forward, leaving his backside awkwardly protruding.
Rather, he seemed to be saying that even supporting his body against gravity was too much trouble.

source.japanese:
船床に頬を擦りつけては頭をのろのろ蠢かせているのも、木床の磨り減った涼感を愉[たの]しむというより、いやいやと愚図る赤子のような。これでもし、甲板に滑り止めの砂撒く式の古い軍船であろうものなら、顔の半分削れて紅葉おろし的な何かになり果てた事であろうさ。背中からたちこめる気配がなんとも鬱陶しい、がその鬱陶しさも、朔屋の常日頃の軽薄さといい加減さから由来するものではなく、なにかこう、もっと別の。
　もっと、陰鬱で侘びしげな、別の。
source.english:
He rubbed his cheek against the floor and slowly shifted his head. Not as though enjoying the coolness of the worn wood, but like a baby fretfully refusing something. Had this been an old warship with sand scattered on deck for traction, half his face would have been grated into something resembling a red mash of radish and chili. An oppressive air rose from his back. Yet this oppression did not come from his usual frivolity or irresponsibility. Something else.
Something darker, more desolate.

source.japanese: よくよく観察すれば、朔屋は呻吟の音を漏らしているではないか。おまけにその声、聞きつけた者を、耳から陰に引きずりこむような暗い響きで喉の奥で燻っているような、で、どうにも女々しい。更に目を凝らせば、青年は眦に涙滲ませて、後から後から頬濡らしているのが見てとれよう。
source.english: A closer look revealed that Sakuya was groaning. The sound smoldered deep in his throat, so dark it seemed to drag anyone who heard it into gloom through the ears. Miserably unmanly. Look closer still, and tears could be seen gathering at the corners of his eyes, wetting his cheeks one after another.

source.japanese: ……一体、零れた涙が珠と凝るのは、麗しく儚き女性の特権であり、であるからこそ嗜虐趣味者に籠の鳥にされ、四六時中心中物の映画を見せつけられたり耳のそばで黒板を爪で引っかかれたり丸めた銀紙を奥歯で噛み締めさせられたりのあの手この手で紅涙しぼられたりの憂き目に遭うて、なるほどそれは無惨絵の負の魅力同様の感興催す景色なれども、涙浮かべるのが朔屋とあっては。興もへったくれもありはしない。何度も擦りつけるあまりに船床の埃で顔が、砂地に投げこんだ蛙の蟇肌よろしく段だらになっているとくればそれは、最早見苦しい以外のなにものでもない。
source.english: …Tears turning to pearls as they fall are the privilege of lovely, fragile women. Which is precisely why a sadist might cage such a woman and wring tears from her by every imaginable means: making her watch lovers' double-suicide films all day, scraping nails on a blackboard beside her ear, or forcing her to bite rolled-up foil with her molars. Admittedly, such a sight might excite the same perverse fascination as a picture of atrocities. But when the weeper was Sakuya? Not a shred of fascination. His repeated rubbing had streaked his face with dust from the floor, like the warty skin of a frog thrown onto sand. By this point, he was merely unsightly.

target.text: Now then, amidst all this, speaking on the subject of Sakuya. Whenever the chance arose, he would abandon his station and any miscellaneous duties he had been tasked with, and when he then laid his grubby hands on the ship's reserves of rum, his neck would be wrung by the Bosun, and he'd be rammed into by Souemon the cat, he'd pretend to stumble over the rigging and try to rub his cheeks against Shisamu's and Kisara's butt cheeks, then proceed to have his molars rattled by the twins' perfectly synchronized open palm strikes, and yet he would never learn from his mistakes.

As he next attempted to peep through the keyhole of their cabin to catch a glimpse of the girls changing out of their uniforms, all he'd see was the muzzle of a revolver, narrowly avoiding getting better airflow through one of his eye sockets; such was his everyday. （Let us set aside the opinion that it might indeed have been better were that to have occurred so that the mass of his useless brain would have been rearranged and left him rather more clearheaded.） Surely he would be enjoying this windfall of freedom from out of the blue to the fullest, so one would think, however───

───Certainly, Sakuya had, just like the deck boys on the upper deck, fallen down to the floor in the passageways. But the way he looked, on his knees, shoulders slumped forwards, only his ass half-assedly stuck up in the air, he certainly didn't seem very relaxed or carefree at all. Rather, it seemed more as though he could barely resist gravity, finding it tiresome to even support his body, one might be tempted to say.

Rubbing his cheeks against the ship's floor and wriggling his head around sluggishly was less because he was enjoying the coolness of the worn wooden floor and instead more like a whiny baby throwing a tantrum. Were this the sort of old naval vessel where sand was scattered on the floors to prevent slipping, he'd have probably scraped half his face off and been reduced to looking like grated daikon and chili. The presence enshrouding his back was truly terribly depressing, but this depressiveness was not something stemming from Sakuya's usual shallow frivolity or carelessness, it was more, something entirely different. Something different that was more gloomy and wretched by far.

Upon closer inspection, was Sakuya not emitting some manner of groaning noises? And on top of that, there was the voice itself, smouldering and sputtering from the depths of his throat with a murky, sombre timbre that sounded as though it might seize any misfortunate enough to hear it and haul them straight into the gloomy dark: it was terribly effeminate. Furthermore, were one to keep one's eyes skinned, one might perceive how the young man had tears welling up in the corners of his eyes, trickling down his cheeks, one after another.

……In general, spilled tears freezing into pearls is a privilege belonging to beautiful, ephemeral maidens, that being exactly they would be kept as caged birds by men of sadistic persuasions and made to watch movies depicting lovers' suicides, hear blackboards placed by their ears gouged into with nails, chew down tightly on rolled up tinfoil with their molars, suffering one miserable fate after the next: whatever means available used to squeeze out their bitter, feminine tears.

To be certain, that is a scene that would stir in the soul the same dark, morbid allure as the Muzan-e, however, these tears were shed by Sakuya. There was not a shred of interest to be found in those. (TN: The Muzan-e, written "無残絵", known in English as "bloody prints" or "cruel prints", are Japanese woodcut prints of a violent, gory, grotesque nature from the Edo and Meiji periods, a pre-cursor of sorts to the modern erotic guro scene.)

His cheek had been ground so repeatedly into the dust covering the ship's floor that it had become a mottled mess, resembling the warty skin of a toad tossed into sandy soil; by now, he was nothing short of wretched to behold.

source.japanese:
そこへ偶然通りかかったのが、のんびりと、煙管横ぐわえの懐手しての、あの飄々とした智里だったから、さして気にかけた風もなく見過ごしにできたのだろう。
　この男の、普段から周囲の忙しなさなど歯牙にもかけない傍若無人な風格は、船内のこの静止状態の中にあっても変わらず。
source.english:
The man who happened past was Tomosato, pipe held sideways in his mouth, hands tucked inside his clothes, as unhurried and carefree as ever. Small wonder he could overlook the spectacle without apparent concern.
His brazen indifference to the bustle around him never changed. It remained the same even in the ship's present stillness.

source.japanese: ありとあらゆる動的活動を放棄しているかの周りの様子も智里には知った事ではないようで、釣りでも愉[たの]しむつもりか、あの太刀の代わりに竿など担いでいるのが船内の停滞した風の中では浮きあがり、釣りといえばのんびりなのに活きている行為に見えるのが皮肉めく。
source.english: He seemed equally unconcerned that everyone else had abandoned all activity. Perhaps he intended to fish: he carried a rod instead of that sword. It stood out against the ship's stagnant air. Fishing was a leisurely occupation, yet here, ironically, it looked positively alive.

source.japanese: 智里。どこまでも気侭な自由人。床面に這いつくばる人影などそもそも視界にも入らぬか、雪駄の蹠が踏みつけにしたのは、朔屋の頭であった。
source.english: Tomosato. An utterly self-willed free spirit. Perhaps the figure crawling on the floor never entered his sight at all. The sole of his sandal came down on Sakuya's head.

target.text: And passing by in this direction by chance, casual and carefree, pipe sticking horizontally out of his mouth and hands in his kimono, came Tomosato, that aloof, detached man, and surely he would overlook this whole mess without giving it much thought. This man, and his outrageously audacious demeanour that showed he cared not a whit for the busyness of his surroundings under normal circumstances, had not changed at all, even while the ship was in this state of repose.

It seemed that Tomosato was completely unconcerned with the surrounding circumstances, the complete abandonment of any and all active activities, and perhaps he intended to enjoy some fishing, for he certainly stood out amidst the stagnant winds on this ship with the way he was carrying a fishing pole over his shoulder instead of that tachi of his; it held a trace of irony that the act of fishing, a leisurely activity, would be seen as something enlivening.

Tomosato. A free spirit through and through. Did the likes of this shadowy figure crawling on all fours on the floor not even enter his field of vision, for what the heels of his geta sandals stepped on───was Sakuya's head.

source.english: “…Urgh…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Ugeh……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「なんでぇ、烏公に啄まれた田螺が、気を吐くような」
source.english: “What's that? Sounds like a pond snail putting up a brave fight after a crow's pecked it.”

source.japanese: ようやくそこで、眼差しが下がり、行き合う、埃まみれの三等航海士の横顔、雪駄の端からはみ出たそれ、蒼い眸[ひとみ]の澄明さとの対比でいよいよ見苦しい。
source.english: Only then did his gaze lower and meet the dusty profile of the third officer, protruding from beneath the edge of his sandal. Beside the lucid blue of his eyes, it looked uglier still.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「What the-, that sounded like the spirited bubbling of a river snail pecked by Mister Crow.」 (TN: While I'm not entirely sure, this is probably a reference to the Japanese folk tale "田螺長者", read "Tanishi-chouja", where an old couple that was never blessed with child pray to Kannon. The child born, however, is a river snail, not human. Skipping a bit, the snail is later attacked by a crow, only for the impact to crack open the shell and a man the size of a human to emerge from it.)

And with that, he finally lowered his gaze, happened upon him, the profile of a third mate covered in dust protruding from the side of his geta, and the contrast with the bright clarity in those azure eyes only made him seem all the more unsightly.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あにやってんの、お前直の字。
　そりゃアレか？　新手の暗黒舞踏の振り付けかなんかか。信天翁から大駱駝へ乗り換えか」
source.english:
“What're you doing, Nao?
Some new butoh choreography? Trading the Albatross for Dairakudakan?”

source.japanese: ……何というのかこの男の物言い、語彙というのは同時代の人間には意味が不明瞭なのであるが、今の朔屋には意味が通ろうが通るまいがさしたる差はない。後頭部を踏みつけにする殺し屋の足、よけようともせずの、これがかの禅門、趙州和尚なら、草履を頭に乗せただけでも公案の種にもなろうが、床と智里の蹠の間で圧されみっともなく歪んだ朔屋の面は、いいところ、持国天様に四股で踏まれた天の邪鬼あたりが関の山。声だって、口からひりだした屁のように、陰に景気悪くくぐもった。
source.english: …The man's expressions and vocabulary were, somehow, obscure to people of his own time. Just now, whether they made sense or not made little difference to Sakuya. He did not even try to avoid the assassin's foot on the back of his head. Had this been the Zen master Zhaozhou, simply placing a sandal on his head could have furnished a koan. But Sakuya's face, grotesquely squeezed between floor and sole, could aspire at best to the little demon stomped flat beneath the guardian king Dhritarashtra. His voice, too, came out gloomy and muffled, like a fart forced through his mouth.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「The hell are you doing there, big Nao? Or what, is it that kind of thing? Some new Butoh choreography? You gonna transfer from the Albatross to the Great Camel Battleship?」 (TN: The nickname he uses here, "直の字", or Nao-no-ji, is a type of Japanese nickname where you add "の字" after the first kanji in a person's name, historically used in the red light districts of Edo or by close friends. Butoh, or "暗黒舞踏" as it is known in Japan, is a type of contemporary Japanese dance invented in 1963. The Great Camel Battleship, or "大駱駝艦", is an influential group of butoh dancers.)

……How to put it? This man's manner of speaking, what you could call his vocabulary, was unclear in its meaning to people from the same generation as him, but whether the meaning of his words were understood by Sakuya or not made no perceptible difference. The foot of this hired killer who was treading on the back of his head showed no sign of removing itself, and were he the Zen master Zhaozhou, merely having a zouri sandal on his head alone would be enough material for a koan, but.

Given that it was the pathetically twisted visage of Sakuya that was pressed between the floor and the sole of Tomosato's foot, the best one could expect was, at most, something like an amanojaku being trampled by Jikokuten doing a shiko. Even his voice, like he were forcing a fart out of his mouth, was gloomy, muffled, and lacked spirit. (TN: An amanojaku is a wretched, evil little yokai, oft depicted as trampled underfoot by statues of the Four Heavenly Kings. Jikokuten is one of the Four Heavenly Kings. The shiko is a traditional exercise done by sumo wrestlers where they lift one leg high before stomping it down on the ground.)

source.english: “I am—”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「I have───」

source.english: “…Aren't we polite all of a sudden?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「僕には、存在価値というものが微塵もないんです……っ。
　僕という現象は仮定された有機交流電燈のひとつの青い照明にもなりえず、全身一切合切髪の毛爪の先、細胞の一つ一つに至るまで平等に価値がない───」
source.english:
“I haven't the slightest value as a living being…! The phenomenon that is me cannot even be a single blue light from a hypothetical organic alternating-current lamp.
My whole body, every bit of it, to the tips of my hair and nails, down to each individual cell, is equally worthless—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「正直、酸素を吸って二酸化炭素を吐いてるだけで、珪藻類より劣る存在なんだ」
source.english: “Honestly, all I do is breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide. I rank below a diatom.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……『You』, have?」 (TN: Sakuya has changed his pronoun to "僕", read "boku", a softer, less casual pronoun than the "俺", read "ore", that he usually uses.)

【Naomasa】 「I have-, no, my existence holds no value in the slightest…… The phenomenon that is me could not even become the blue light of a single hypothetical organic AC lamp. Every single part of my entire body, from the ends of my hair and the tips of my toenails down to each and every cell, they are all equally worthless───」 (TN: This is a reference to Kenji Miyazawa's "Haru to Shura" poetry collection.)
【Naomasa】 「To be honest, all I do is breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide; I am an existence inferior even to diatoms.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「わはははは、お前なにを受信してるんだ。今日びンな台詞ァ、三文詩人か鬱病患者くらいしか並べねぇ」
source.english: “Ha ha ha! What're you picking up? Nobody strings lines like that together these days except a third-rate poet or a depressive.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Wahahahaha, what kind of signals are you receiving, man? These days, the only ones who spout lines like that are hack poets or the clinically depressed.」

source.english:
“—Wait.
Depression…?”

source.japanese: 船内通路の床にぶつぶつ、底無し沼の泥より湧き上がる悪性の瓦斯の泡と弾ける譫言めいたのに、智里は感得したように小首を傾げたという。
source.english: The muttering on the passage floor burst like bubbles of poisonous gas rising from the mud of a bottomless swamp. At these delirious words, Tomosato tilted his head as though something had dawned on him.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「───Wait. Depressed……?」

Even though he was grumbling on the floor of the passageway, his delirious ramblings like bursting bobbles of malignant gas risen from the mud of a bottomless bog, Tomosato tilted his head as though he'd attained a profound revelation.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そうかお前、鬱になッてんのか」
source.english: “Ah. You're depressed.”

source.japanese:
左様、いかにも左様───鬱。
　この朔屋直正、普段から酒に溺れ女の乳房と尻を追いかけ、いい大人としての義務や仕事と見ると大火に遭った江戸町民のように諸手を挙げてそれは必死に逃げ出すという碌で無し。それだけでも穴掘って埋めてやるのが世の為彼自身の為なんぼか善行となろうに、そこへさしてこの男、前段にて触れた通りに、躁鬱の振幅が異様に激しい。躁の時の五月蝿い事、この『五月蝿し』という字面に見える蝿のように目障りなのだが、鬱の場合はもっと酷[むご]い。とても酷[むご]い。えらく酷[むご]い。有り体に言うとその蝿がたかる糞に等しい。
　鬱時の朔屋は、自ら立って歩くことすら困難事、呼吸する事さえ億劫の、視界に入る景色は色盲者の如く灰色と映じ、自らを地虫芋虫程度の劣悪な存在としか感じられなくなるのである。
source.english:
Yes. Precisely. Depression.
Naomasa Sakuya was ordinarily a good-for-nothing who drowned himself in drink and chased women's breasts and backsides. At the sight of duties or work befitting a grown man, he raised both hands and fled with all the desperation of an Edo townsman caught in a great fire. That alone would make digging a hole and burying him something of a good deed, for the world and for himself. On top of it, as previously mentioned, his swings between mania and depression were extraordinarily violent. At his highs he buzzed about as noisily and obtrusively as a swarm of flies. Depressed, he was worse. Much worse. Remarkably worse. To speak plainly, he was the shit those flies swarmed upon.
When depressed, Sakuya found even standing and walking difficult. Breathing was a bother. Everything in sight appeared gray, as though he were color-blind, and he felt himself no better than some wretched grub or caterpillar.

source.japanese: 否、そう比較しては石の裏葉末の陰に潜[ひそ]んで人目を避ける程度の本能なら持ち合わせている地虫芋虫の類に失礼という奴で、なにしろ朔屋と来たら、わざわざ人目につくところでこうしてのたうっていたりの、日頃へらへらといい加減で怠惰な彼の方がまだまし、とそう勘違いさせてしまうくらいなのだから始末に負えない。
source.english: No: that comparison insulted grubs and caterpillars, which at least possessed enough instinct to hide from view beneath stones and leaves. Sakuya took the trouble to writhe somewhere people could see him. He was so impossible that he could make one mistakenly believe his usual grinning, careless laziness was preferable.

source.japanese: もともと朔屋青年にはこういう神経の障りがつきまとうてあり、季節の変わり目や衝撃的な出来事などに時折躁鬱を誘発されていたはいた。信天翁号に強制徴用されて以来、打ち続く肉体的精神的打撃にいつ何時発症してもおかしくはなかったのだが、それさえも抑えこむくらい、船の仕事は辛かった。日々の終わり、寝床に潜[もぐ]る前に一口のラム酒の配給あれば幸運で、零れた涙が酒を塩辛くする。宿の毛布の南京虫つまみに焼酎啜[すす]る山谷のニコヨンと信天翁の船員どちらが悲哀か興味深い比較はさておいて、ともかく毎日疲弊しきっていたおかげで、かえって躁も鬱も頭をもたげる機会が無かっただけのこと。
source.english: This nervous affliction had always troubled the young man. A change of season or a shocking incident sometimes brought on an episode of mania or depression. Since his forced conscription aboard the Albatross, the continuous physical and mental battering could have triggered it at any moment. But the work was hard enough to suppress even that. At day's end, he was lucky to receive a mouthful of rum before crawling into bed; his tears made it salty. Let us set aside the interesting question of whether an Albatross sailor or a Sanya day laborer sipping ‘bomb’ shochu in a flophouse, with bedbugs from the blanket for a snack, made the sadder spectacle. Exhaustion had simply left neither mania nor depression an opening.

source.japanese: ところがこの日先触れなく船内が休止状態に陥ったため、朔屋の緊張も、ふっと緩んだ背後から鬱がのしかかってきたのだろう。
source.english: But today the ship fell without warning into inactivity. As Sakuya's tension slackened, depression had probably borne down upon him from behind.

source.japanese: ……船が、内海に閉じこめられ同じような景色の中行ったり来たりを繰り返すばかりの、単調さも手伝ったのかも知れない。
source.english: …Perhaps the monotony helped: the ship confined to inland waters, going back and forth through much the same scenery.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああもうなんだか世界はすっかり灰色だ。
　まるで僕以外の全てが僕に悪意を向けてきてるみたいだ」
source.english:
“Oh, the whole world has gone gray.
It's as though everything except me means me harm.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どこかで何かの陰謀が横行している。
　断じて、僕の妄想なんかじゃない」
source.english:
“There's some conspiracy at work somewhere.
It absolutely isn't a delusion of mine.”

source.japanese: 踏んづけられたままで呟き続ける繰り言たるや、智里も初めは一笑に付していたものの、雪駄越しに袴[はかま]の裡に忍びこみ、腿から這い上がって陰嚢を高確率で陰金田虫に感染させようという気色悪さ。納豆の糸より執拗く、船殻汚損の一大勢力、貽貝の足糸の様に性質悪くからみつく。陰金田虫だって馬鹿には出来ない、陰金田虫は痒すぎる。掻いても掻[か]いても止まらない。こんなに辛いの止めるには、そっと優しく舐めること、と民間療法歌にあるくらいに厄介で、常人ならこの難病に罹る前に朔屋を蹴り飛ばして船底に溜まった汚水に叩きこんでしまうべき。がこの智里、余程神経が太いのかそもそも感受性が欠落しているのか、得心顔で一つ小さく頷[うなず]いた事である。朔屋の後頭部に足を置いたまま。
source.english: Still underfoot, he went on muttering his grievances. Tomosato had laughed them off at first, but their unpleasantness seemed ready to creep through his sandal, into his hakama, and up his thigh, with a very good chance of infecting his scrotum with jock itch. More persistent than sticky natto threads; as viciously entangling as the mussels' anchoring threads that did so much to foul a ship's hull. Nor was jock itch to be taken lightly. It was unbearably itchy. Scratch and scratch, and it would not stop. To ease such suffering, gently, tenderly lick it—or so went a folk-remedy song. That was how troublesome it was. A normal person ought to have kicked Sakuya into the bilge before contracting this dreadful disease. But whether Tomosato had unusually tough nerves or lacked sensitivity altogether, he gave a small nod of understanding. His foot remained on the back of Sakuya's head.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「I see, so you've gotten all depressed?」

Verily, very verily so───depression. This Sakuya Naomasa, ordinarily busy with chasing skirts and breasts and wallowing in drink, a useless good-for-nothing who the moment any duties or work expected of him in his capacity as a responsible adult entered his peripheral vision would raise both hands in the air and frantically run away like a citizen of Edo caught in a conflagration. If only for that, what an act of benevolence it would be to dig a hole and bury a certain someone in it, to both the world and the man himself; yet to make matters worse, as touched upon in the preceding part, the amplitudes of his manic-depressive cycles are extraordinarily violent.

When he is being a loud nuisance during his manic periods, he is an eyesore, much like the character of fly that can be seen in the word 『五月蝿し』, but it is far more miserable during his depressive periods. Very miserable. Extremely miserable. To put it bluntly, he was like the shit those aforementioned flies swarmed around. (TN: The word used here, "五月蝿し", read "urusashi", traces its origins to the flies that spawn in great swarms during the 5th month of the Japanese lunar calendar, which would be around early June these days. "五月" being the fifth month, "蝿" meaning fly, and the pronunciation coming from the association with "煩い", read "urusai", meaning noisy or annoying.)

As for Sakuya in his depressive periods, even standing up and walking was a struggle, even breathing was troublesome, any scenery that entered his field of vision was painted in grey like he were colour-blind, and an inferior existence on the level of a white grub or a hairy caterpillar was all he could envision himself as.

Nay, were one to compare him to such, it would be an affront to the species of grub or caterpillar that at least had the instincts to hide from sight behind rocks or in the shade of the apex of the blade of a leaf, for when it came to Sakuya, he deliberately writhed and wriggled like this within the sight of others; comparatively, the habitually flippant, perfunctory, and lazy version of the man was better, so bad was it that one could mistakenly think that, so hopeless and impossible was he to deal with.

The young man Sakuya had always been haunted by this mental defect, and when the seasons changed or a shocking event befell him, it would occasionally induce a bout of manic depression. Since he'd been forcibly impressed aboard the Albatross, he'd suffered continuous beatings of blows both physical and mental, so it wouldn't be strange at all for that to induce another episode at any moment. It could suppress even that, so backbreaking was the work on this ship. As the day came to an end, he would be lucky if he'd been rationed a single mouthful of rum before he'd crawl into bed, and the tears he shed only made the rum taste saltier.

Setting aside the deeply fascinating comparison of whether the day labourers in the mountainous valleys picking out the bedbugs from their blankets in their dosshouse while sipping on some shouchuu rotgut or the crew of the Albatross lived in greater misery, generally speaking, he was completely spent every day, and as a consequence, neither his mania nor his depression had the chance to rear their ugly heads.

On the contrary, it was likely that, on this day, where the ship had fallen into a state of standstill without any prior warning, Sakuya's tension had eased in turn, and so the depression must have begun to weigh heavily on his suddenly relaxed back.
……It might well be that the monotony of the ship being shut inside the same inland sea, where all they did was repeatedly go to and fro amidst the same scenery, could have had a hand in it as well.
【Naomasa】 「Aah, I've had enough, it is as though the world has turned entirely ashen. As if everything but myself is directing their wicked malice right at me.」
【Naomasa】 「Somewhere, some sort of conspiracy is running rampant. Absolutely, positively, this is NOT me being delusional.」

As he continued to mutter his complaints while still being tread on, a smile reached Tomosato's lips for the first time, at this skin-crawling foulness that seemed to sneak across his geta and into his hakama, slithering up his thighs while attempting to, most likely, infect his scrotum with tinea cruris. Clinging to him more tenaciously than natto strings, with a malignancy like the byssus of Korean mussels, one of the great titans of hull fouling.

One couldn't just make light of tinea crusis, for groin ringworm is inordinately itchy. One scratches and scratches but it just doesn't stop. To stop an itch this bad, one must softly and tenderly lick it away, such a nuisance was it that there even existed folk remedy songs of that sort; any normal person would kick Sakuya away and toss him into the bilge before contracting such a serious disease. But this Tomosato here, was he simply excessively thick-skinned, or was he not susceptible in the first place, for he gave a small nod with a convinced look on his face. With his foot still planted on the back of Sakuya's head.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おうおう。そうだともそうだとも。
　ジョン・キールだって言っている。
『妄想患者は造られるものにて生まれるものに非ず』───」
source.english:
“Yes, yes. Exactly.
John Keel said it, too:
‘Paranoids are made, not born.’”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、やっぱり」
source.english: “Ah. I knew it.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ついでに言えば、世の中の犯罪ってもんの八割がたは、猶太の七人委員会ってのがその糸を引いててな」
source.english: “And while we're on the subject, something like eighty percent of the world's crimes have their strings pulled by a Jewish committee of seven.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「デロっつう地底人は地底から夜毎日毎に毒電波を放射し続けてやがるし、テンプル騎士団なんぞは、十字軍以来、市民の生活を監視してる」
source.english: “The underground people called Deros keep blasting poisonous radio waves out of the earth, day and night. And the Knights Templar have been watching people's lives since the Crusades.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そ、そんな」
source.english: “N-no…”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「それによ、覚えはないか？　お前に届く手紙はいっつも誰かが検閲してる。電話だって盗聴されてらあ。そればっかじゃねえ」
source.english: “And listen. Haven't you noticed? Someone always censors your letters. Your phone's tapped, too. That's not all.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「こんな海の上だって、『奴等』の手は伸びてんのさ───船についてくる海豚がお前さんを見張ってる。阿呆鳥がお前の上で羽ばたくたんびに、そっと羽根から毒を零してる。
　……近頃妙に体が怠いだろう……？」
source.english:
“Even out here at sea, ‘they’ can reach you. The dolphins following the ship are keeping watch on you. Every time the albatross flaps its wings overhead, it quietly sprinkles poison from its feathers.
…Been feeling strangely tired lately, haven't you…?”

source.japanese: ひい、と朔屋から絞り出された悲鳴が、耳にした者の眉をひそめさせるほどに情けなく、前のめりに突っ伏していた体を胎児のように丸めさせたのは鬱に伴う退行症の典型と窺えたところで見苦しいことに変わりない。わざわざ朔屋の妄念の輪郭に合わせた言葉で脅迫観念を煽り立ててみせる、これはもしや、より強いショックでもってねじくれた神経を叩き解そうとかいう、手荒な治療紛いのつもりなのか───
source.english: The squeak wrung from Sakuya was so pathetic that anyone hearing it would have frowned. His prone body curled like a fetus. One might identify this as typical regression accompanying depression; that did not make it less unsightly. Tomosato was deliberately shaping his words to the contours of Sakuya's delusions, inflaming his obsessions. Could he intend some rough imitation of treatment, battering those twisted nerves loose with a still greater shock—

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Yeah, yeah. That's it, you're so right. Even John Keel also said it. 『Victims of delusion are created, never born.』───」
【Naomasa】 「Aah, I knew it.」
【Tomosato】 「Figured I'd mention it in passing, but the Jewish committee of seven is pulling the strings of eighty percent of the crime in the world.」

【Tomosato】 「The subterranian humanoids known as the "Deros" continue to emit radio waves into people's minds day and night from the cave cities, and The Knights Templar, for example, have, ever since the crusades, been closely monitoring the lives of the citizenry.」
【Naomasa】 「No, that can't be.」
【Tomosato】 「And what's more, doesn't this ring any bells? Any letter you get is always inspected by somebody. Even your phone is being wiretapped. And that's not all.」

【Tomosato】 「Even out on the sea like we are, 『their』tendrils still reach us─── the dolphins following the ship are watching you. Every time the albatrosses over your head flap their wings, they secretly spread a poison from their feathers. ……Your body has been feeling oddly sluggish lately, right……?」

The squeaking scream he wrung out from Sakuya was pitiful enough to draw the brows of any who heard it into a furrow, and even if the way his slumped, prostrate body curled into a fetal position was inferred to be a typical regressive pathology associated with depression, it didn't change how wretched it was to behold. Deliberately fanning the flames of his conceptual menace by matching his words with the contour of Sakuya's delusions, could this perhaps be, did he wish to beat his twisted mind straight with an even stronger shock, did he intend for this to be some sort of violent pseudo-treatment───

source.japanese:
【泪】
（……なに、なさっているの？）
source.english: (…What are you doing?)

source.japanese: ひょこ、と唐突に、それでいて古代魚の鰭が舞うようにゆうらりと淑やかに、二人の傍らの船室から打ち見てきた、洋装の紫紺が水底を思わせて深い。水平器の形した瞳孔の、どこか人離れした眸[ひとみ]が智里の蒼いそれと刹那絡んで、下に降りて、ふっと細められる。幾許かの感興を湛えて。
source.english: Suddenly, yet as gracefully and gently as the fins of an ancient fish dancing through the water, a figure in a deep purple Western-style dress—a color as deep as the ocean floor—peered out from the cabin beside the two of them. Her eyes, with pupils shaped like spirit levels, had a somewhat otherworldly quality; they briefly met Tomosato’s blue ones, then drifted downward and narrowed slightly, brimming with a touch of fascination.

target.text: 【Rui】 （……What, pray tell, are you doing?)

Suddenly, yet with a swaying, lady-like grace, like the dancing fin of a prehistoric fish, she peeked out from the cabin next to them, the indigo blue of her dress so deep it brought to mind the bottom of the sea. Her rather atypical eyes with their horizontal pupils caught Tomosato's azure for an instant, travelled down, then abruptly narrowed. Filled with some sort of interest.

source.japanese:
【泪】
（あら。面白いこと）
source.english: (Oh. How amusing.)

source.japanese: 船の女客、泪が潜[ひそ]めて小声なのは、朔屋を眺めて彼の状態を見てとって、慮ったというより、胸に抱く小柄な人影に気遣ったものか。智里も声には出さず、口元に溜めた諧謔の色味で答えた。
source.english: Rui, the ship's lady passenger, kept her voice low—perhaps less from consideration for Sakuya, whose condition she had discerned, than for the slight figure clasped to her bosom. Tomosato answered without a word, only a glint of mischief at the corners of his mouth.

target.text: 【Rui】 （Oh my. This seems amusing.)

That Rui, the female passenger of this ship, hid herself and spoke in low tones was not because she was carefully thinking things over after looking at Sakuya and seeing his state, rather, it was perhaps out of consideration for the petite figure currently embraced within her bosom. Tomosato also did not speak aloud, answering with a hint of humour playing on his lips.

source.japanese:
【智里】
（だろう？　こいつ、いじってて飽きねえんだもの。ついつい構いつけたくもなるわさ）
source.english: (Right? I never get tired of teasing this guy. I just can’t help but want to mess with him.)

source.japanese:
口元にも眼差しにも諧謔、皮肉の気色、そう、諧謔で皮肉だ、朔屋の鬱を手荒いやり方で叩き出そうなどいう志は皆無の、所詮この殺し屋にそんな殊勝な心映えを求めるだけ無駄と思い知らせる。
　泪は泪で、小笑みして頬に宿した慈しみも、朔屋に傾けたというより、胸の中の小柄な体に向けているのだった。豊麗な乳房に埋めるように抱き留めた、下級水夫に。
source.english:
Mischief and irony showed in Tomosato's mouth and eyes. Yes: mischief, and irony. He had no noble intention of beating Sakuya's melancholy out of him by rough treatment. It was folly to expect anything so admirable of this assassin.
Rui, for her part, smiled faintly. The tenderness on her cheeks was directed less toward Sakuya than toward the slight figure in her arms: a junior sailor, held so close he seemed buried in her luxuriant breasts.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 （Right? I never get bored of making of fun of this guy. Just can't stop myself from wanting to hang with him, against my better judgment.)

Both eyes and lips coloured with a hint of humour and sarcasm, yes, sarcastically joking, there were no ambitions the like of violently beating the depression out of Sakuya, and we must come to realize that, in the end, expecting such laudable thoughtfulness from this hired killer is an exercise in futility. As for Rui, the compassion held within the small smile on her cheeks was not devoted to Sakuya, instead directed at the petite body held within her bosom. To the one caught and held tight as if to bury him within her splendid, ample chest, that deck boy.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ひぁ……ん……っ」
source.english: “Hii… ah…!”

source.japanese: ……この少年の、臈長けた年増に抱かれたる様、蕩けそうなくらい円熟した柔肉に包まれる役得に酔う、も度合いが過ぎれば強い酒と同じで身を損なうの見本で、食虫花の蜜に捕らえられた哀れな犠牲、の風情が勝る。乳房が造る沃地は水夫にとって余りに香りが高すぎて、呼吸するだけで鼓動が乱れる頬が火照る、まいて泪が少年の、小体に締まった尻に掌被せ、宝珠を仕上げる細工師の精妙な運指で、太腿の狭間に引き寄せるとあっては───
source.english: …Behold the young sailor in the arms of a ripe, accomplished woman, intoxicated by the privilege of being wrapped in soft flesh matured almost to melting. Yet privilege in excess ruins the body like strong drink, and by now he looked less its fortunate beneficiary than the pitiful prey of a carnivorous flower, caught fast in its nectar. The fertile country between those breasts was far too richly perfumed for him; merely breathing there sent his heart racing and his cheeks aflame. And when Rui laid a hand over his small, taut buttocks and, with the exquisite fingerwork of a jeweler perfecting a precious orb, drew him between her thighs—

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Hyaah……nhh……」

……This young boy, embraced by an experienced, mature woman, was so drunk in the privilege of being held within the ripe, mellow softness of her flesh that he was on the verge of melting, a prime example of how consumption in excess can be as harmful to the body as strong waters, a poor victim caught in the nectar of an insectivorous plant; those were the most apt descriptions of the air surrounding him.

The scent of her fertile tracts of land was simply too heady, merely breathing it in made his heart run wild and set his cheeks aflame, to speak nothing of how Rui had laid a palm on the young lad's petite, firm butt, and how with the delicate fingering of a craftsman putting the finishing touches on a precious pearl, she drew him further into the gap between her thighs───

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あ……あ……っ、僕───
　声、出ちゃ……ぁっ」
source.english:
“Ah… ah… I—
I’m going to… cry out… ah!”

source.japanese: 果たして漏れるのは声だけか、抵抗もままならず、身悶えするのが辛うじて、腕は力なく脇に垂らされ、水夫の少年の微かに震える背中と、筍の、皮を被った若いところとか土筆坊のつんつんしてるのへあざとくこれ見よがしに練乳をかけ回してこねくり回すイメエジが二重写しに浮かぶかのよう。
source.english: Was his voice the only thing about to spill? Resistance was beyond him; he could barely writhe, his arms hanging limp at his sides. Over the young sailor's faintly trembling back, another image seemed superimposed: condensed milk poured with brazen deliberation over the tender young flesh of a bamboo shoot still in its sheath, or the pert head of a horsetail—and fingers kneading it everywhere.

target.text: 【Deckboy】 「Ah……ah……, I─── can't keep……voice in……ah.」

Was it truly only his voice that he ultimately couldn't hold in, for unable to resist, barely able to wriggle his body around, his arms hung limply down his sides, and the sight of the subtly shivering back of the young sailor seemed to almost bleed together into a superimposition with the image of condensed milk being ostentatiously poured all over the young parts of a bamboo shoot yet covered in peel, or the fertile stalk of a field horsetail jutting energetically into the air, mixed and kneaded together in a calculated display.

source.japanese:
【智里】
（そんで、姐さんなにやってんの。
　てもまあ、見たまんまだろうが）
source.english:
(So, sis, whatcha doing? Well,
looks like exactly what it looks like.)

target.text: 【Tomosato】 （So, what are you up to, lady? Well, it's probably exactly what it looks like.)

source.japanese:
【泪】
（わたくしは、ちょっとこの子とお喋りしたくって。
　でもなんだかこの子、あまり元気がないみたい。
　これから愉[たの]しくなりそうなのに、すぐにくったりってなってしまうの）
source.english:
(I just wanted to chat with this kid for a bit.
But for some reason, he doesn’t seem very energetic.
Things are about to get fun, but he’s already getting all worn out.)

target.text: 【Rui】 （I simply desired to have a little chat with this boy. But for some reason, this boy doesn't seem very energetic. It seemed like it was just about to become fun, and yet he went soft and limp so quickly.)

source.japanese:
【智里】
（あんたにかかりゃ、大概の奴はそうなるわ。
　なに連れこんでんだか知らねえが、
　あんまり虐めてやるなよ若い衆を）

target.text: 【Tomosato】 （When it comes to you, most guys are gonna end up like that. I don't really care what or who you bring back there with you, but don't bully the young lads too much.）

source.japanese:
……泪の本来の船室はここから区画を隔てており、彼女は空いている部屋に、適当にそこらの下級水夫を捕まえて引きずりこんだと見えた。もちろん他人との親しい触れ合いには愛撫が当然のように添え物としてある彼女だからして、『お喋り』といって、なんの、『お茶にスコーン。サワークリームにスグリのジャム』を味わいながらの健全な時間で済むものか。
　唇が微笑みつくるのは肌を啄む合間合間であるだろうし、舌も言葉紡ぐより、相手の耳朶や粘膜を賞翫するのに忙しいのではないかの、柔媚に尾籠な気配がつきまとう。
source.english:
…Rui’s own cabin lay a section away; evidently she had seized whichever junior sailor came to hand and dragged him into an empty room. With her, of course, caresses attended any intimate human contact as naturally as a garnish, so what chance was there that this “chat” would remain a wholesome interval spent enjoying “tea and scones, with sour cream and currant jam”?
Her lips would form their smiles in the intervals between pecks at his skin, and her tongue, rather than spinning words, was doubtless busier savoring his earlobes and mucous membranes. Something softly seductive and indecent clung to the whole affair.

source.japanese:
その証拠にこの下級水夫君を見るがよい。もともと十把一絡げの面子達であるのに加え、著しく不活性化した船内の空気にもろに影響されてただでさえ元気なかった彼らだ。
　ぐったりと弛緩した様、水揚げされた水母に異ならず、泪に髪の匂いを吸われたりされようものなら、香りどころか精気までも根こそぎ持っていかれる心地ならんか。
source.english:
For proof, behold this junior sailor. He and his fellows were a job lot to begin with, and the ship's profoundly inert atmosphere had struck them with particular force; they had scarcely been energetic even before. Now he sagged as limply as a jellyfish hauled ashore.
If Rui so much as breathed in the scent of his hair, might he not feel that she had drawn out not merely its fragrance but every last drop of his vitality?

source.japanese:
きっと泪に捕まったこの水夫、解放されても数日は人事不省の境を彷徨うに違いなく、泪の移り香に魘されて寝汗まみれになりつつも、彼の雄の部分だけは健気に自己主張してはひくつくのだろう。
