　そんな不埒で尾籠な泪と水夫の有り様に、普段の朔屋ならもっと妄想逞[たくま]しくするのだろうが、今日はいけなかった。
source.english:
Surely the sailor Rui had caught would spend several days hovering on the border of consciousness even after she released him, tormented in sleep by the scent she left upon him and drenched in sweat, while his manhood alone gallantly continued to assert itself and twitch.
Ordinarily, the lewd and indecent spectacle of Rui and the sailor would have sent Sakuya's imagination into vigorous excess. Today, however, he was past even that.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「泪さんや水夫君の事なんて、
　どうでもいいですからぁ」
source.english:
“I don't care about Rui
or that sailor…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「僕のこと、一思いにヤッて下さいよう。
　どうせ僕なんか、
　この世に在る意味がないのです」
source.english:
“Please just finish me off.
I don't have any reason
to exist in this world anyway.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だから、君のその抜き身で、
　僕の心の臓なり脳天なり、
　綺麗に一気にさっくりと───！」
source.english:
“So take that bare blade of yours
and put it straight through my heart,
or my skull, in one clean stroke—!”

target.text: ……Rui's actual stateroom was separated by bulkheads from here, and it looked like Rui had simply chosen an empty cabin, then lazily caught one of the deck boys and dragged him along with her. Of course, when it came to this woman, who viewed caressing and fondling as a natural supplement to friendly contact with others, when she said "chat", could it ever possibly end with a mere 『We'll have tea and scones. And gooseberry jam with the sour cream.』 while spending some wholesome time together?

Her lips probably only held that small smile in between pecking at his skin, and was her tongue not too busy with appreciating her companion's earlobes and mucous membranes to form words? A hint of indecency shadowed her soft, alluring charm.

As proof, one only needed to cast a glance at this deck boy. Not only were they lumped together in one big group from the start, a dime a dozen of nondescript faces, they had also already been heavily influenced by the stiflingly lifeless air aboard this ship to the point of being left lethargic. He was limp and lax, no different from a jellyfish pulled out of the water, and were his hair to have its scent inhaled by Rui, would it not feel as though not only his scent but even his very life force was being drained to the last drop?

There was no doubt that any sailor caught by Rui would, even after being released, be wandering through the realm of unconsciousness for days to come; he would moan and writhe in his sleep at the lingering scent of Rui, slick with sweat, but even so, the male part of him alone would commendably assert itself as it twitched. In the face of the licentious, indecent state of Rui and this deck boy, Sakuya's delusions would normally run far wilder and bolder, but today, he just couldn't do it.
【Naomasa】 「Rui and the deck boy and what they do, it's whatever, I don't caaare.」
【Naomasa】 「Just try to bump me off quickly. Not like there's any meaning in me existing in this world.」
【Naomasa】 「So, draw that sword of yours, go for my heart or my brain, and cut me down in one clean stroke───!」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「なんだって鬱陶しいなあ。
　……一発こいつでどつけば、
　ちっとは目も醒めるかね？」
source.english:
“You're so tiresome.
…Would a whack with this wake him up a little?”

source.japanese: 智里が太刀の鐺を床の朔屋の後頭部に擬したところ、ころころと心地よい笑いが、泪から零れた。
source.english: As Tomosato aimed the end of his sword's scabbard at the back of Sakuya's head on the floor, a pleasant, rippling laugh escaped Rui.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Damn, you really are depressing. ……If I give this guy a quick chop, he'll wake up a little, right?」
When Tomosato pressed the chape of his scabbard against the back of Sakuya's head, who was still lying on the floor, a pleasant, melodic chuckle escaped Rui's lips.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あら刃傷沙汰？
　よくってよ、とっても。
　さ、派手にやってちょうだいな」
source.english:
“Oh, bloodshed?
How lovely.
Do make it spectacular.”

source.japanese: 泪にとっては知己の朔屋の流血沙汰も、暇潰しの添え物程度でしかないらしい。手を打って喜ぶ様子がこの女にしては妙にあどけなく無邪気だったが、智里はうんざりしたように刀を引いた。
source.english: Apparently, even the spilling of her acquaintance Sakuya's blood was no more than an accompaniment to Rui's amusement. She clapped delightedly, strangely childlike and innocent for her. Tomosato pulled the sword away with a weary look.

target.text: 【Rui】 「My, will there be bloody swordplay? Go ahead, by all means. Now, do make it a good show.」

Apparently, the imminent spilling of the blood of her acquaintance, Sakuya, amounted to nothing more than an additional way to kill some time in Rui's eyes. The way she clasped her hands together in joy made for an oddly childlike and innocent gesture for this woman, and Tomosato withdrew his blade as though fed up, disgusted.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ねえよ、刃傷沙汰なんか。
　今だって鞘でどついたろうとは思ったが、
　抜く気はなかった。
　それも今、気が失せたわ」
source.english:
“No bloodshed.
I was thinking of hitting him with the scabbard,
not drawing it.
And now I don't feel like doing even that.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Hell no, no bloodshed or anything. I thought of hitting him with the scabbard just now, but I never intended to draw my blade. And now I've lost interest.」

source.japanese: この男、朔屋を殺す殺すと宣言しておきながら、一向にその生命を狙う様子もなく、これで果たして本当に殺し屋が務まるのかどうかが怪しくなってくる。太刀をいつものように見えないどこだかに引っこめて、智里は朔屋の襟[えり]を引きずり起こした。
source.english: For a man who repeatedly announced he would kill Sakuya, he showed no sign of attempting it. One began to wonder whether he could really make a living as an assassin. He put the sword away somewhere out of sight, as usual, then hauled Sakuya up by the collar.

target.text: Even as this man continued to proclaim that he would kill and murder Sakuya, he showed not the slightest hint of actually aiming for his life, and it had begun to grow questionable whether this man even was a hired killer at all. Tomosato put away his tachi somewhere nobody could see, as usual, then pulled Sakuya up by his collar.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「やい直の字。
　てめえがあんまりに鬱陶しいもんで、
　ついうっかり忘れてたぜ」
source.english:
“Hey, Nao.
You're so damned tiresome
I nearly forgot.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「航海士の双子がな、お前を呼んでたぞ？」
source.english: “The navigator twins were asking for you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はぁ……？
　シサムとキサラが？
　なんの用事でしょうか」
source.english:
“Huh…?
Sisam and Kisara?
What do they want?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Listen up, big Nao. You've been acting so depressed, I completely forgot to tell you.」
【Tomosato】 「The twin first mates, they were calling for you, y'know?」
【Naomasa】 「Haah……? Shisamu and Kisara? What could they need me for?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「知るかそんな事。
　知りたきゃてめえで行ってこい」
source.english:
“How would I know?
Go find out yourself.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「How would I know that? You wanna know? Then get going.」

source.japanese:
背中をびたんと叩かれて、朔屋はつんのめりながら、それでもよろよろと双子の部屋を目指す。なんとも気が重いが、呼び出しを無視したなら後でどういう目に遭わされるか判らない。
　自分など殺されてもいいとまで思い詰めていた割りには、あの双子の怒りが怖いというのは、全く妙な話である。
source.english:
A slap on the back sent Sakuya stumbling forward. He tottered toward the twins' cabin, his heart heavy. But if he ignored their summons, there was no telling what they might do to him later.
After going so far as to wish himself killed, it was very strange that he should still fear the twins' anger.

target.text: With a hard slap on his back, Sakuya almost toppled over forwards; still, he slowly made his way towards the twins' cabin. He did so with a very heavy heart, but he had no idea what treatment he'd be in for if he dared to ignore their summons. For someone who had brooded so much, tormenting himself to the point he was fine with being killed, he still feared the twins' wrath: what an altogether peculiar contradiction.

source.japanese:
さて朔屋が、鬱々と鬱陶しい足取りで双子の船室の前に立つと。
　中から激しく言い争う気配が響いてきて、なんだってこの二人は人を呼びつけておいて口喧嘩、こっちはこんなに心が辛いのに、と朔屋は暗く愚痴りながら扉を開ける、と。
source.english:
When Sakuya reached the twins' cabin, advancing with a gloomy, oppressive tread—
a furious argument was raging inside. They had summoned him, only to start quarreling? When his heart was suffering so? Muttering darkly, he opened the door—

target.text: Now then. Sakuya had made his way to the front of the twins' cabin with melancholy, heavy steps. The sound of a fierce argument could be heard from within; why the hell would they start a fight after calling someone over, and while my heart is in such agonizing pain at that, Sakuya darkly grumbled to himself while opening the door, and then.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「シサムの男日照りーーっ」
source.english: “Sisam's desperate for a man!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「YOU MAN-STARVED SPINSTERーー!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「キサラの生理不順ーーっ」
source.english: “Kisara, your periods are all over the place!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「YOU IRREGULARLY MENSTRUATING STRUMPETーー!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なな何をぅッ。嘘つかないでよ、
　ちゃんと二八日周期で来てるってーの！」
source.english:
“Wh-what? Don't lie!
Mine comes every twenty-eight days, right on time!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Wh-what are you-! Don't lie, it came in exactly at the regular time following the twenty-eight day cycle!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そっちこそ！　あたしだって、
　別にそこまで飢えちゃーいないさっ」
source.english:
“And you!
I'm not that desperate either!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Well you're one to talk! It's not like I'm that starved for men or anything!」

source.japanese: 一方は、肘を曲げ緩く握った掌を顔まで掲げ、片手は脇に自然に垂らす、どこか南大門金剛力士像吽形にも通ずる天地陰陽の構え───
source.english: One stood with an elbow bent, a loosely closed fist raised to her face, the other arm hanging naturally at her side. A stance of heaven and earth, yin and yang, not unlike the closed-mouthed guardian statue at the Great South Gate—

source.japanese: 片や対手は、腰をどっしり落とし、開掌の、右手を高く上、左を腰の下へ伸ばして、巌のように揺るぎない形、天地の構え。
source.english: Her opponent had sunk her weight low. Right hand open and high, left extended below her waist, she held a posture as immovable as a rock. Another stance of heaven and earth.

source.japanese: 両者共にあらゆる局面に対応可能、気勢迸ったその瞬時に相手を呑みこまんとする力流全身くまなく内在させた、体の置き方であり、罵声だって裂帛の気合い孕んで衝突する。実際朔屋などは、扉を潜[くぐ]った途端に双子がた走らせる甲声で、鼻先を物理的に叩かれたかの衝撃受けて、わあとのけぞって足を滑らせ、みっともなくも尻餅の、腰から目まで衝[つ]き抜けて火花と散った痛みに涙滲んだ、しかし視界の中で航海士の太腿、目線が下がってお陰で鮮やかにしなやかに際立つ。
source.english: Both held their bodies ready for any development, a current of power inhabiting every part of them, poised to swallow the other the instant their fighting spirit burst forth. Even their insults collided with the tearing force of battle cries. As Sakuya passed through the doorway, their shrill voices struck him with a shock almost physical, right at the tip of his nose. He cried out, recoiled, slipped, and landed disgracefully on his backside. Pain shot from hips to eyes and scattered in sparks, bringing tears. His lowered viewpoint, however, showed the navigators' supple thighs with splendid clarity.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（ふふふ、もしかしたら今日こそ今度こそ、
　奥まで見える瞬間に恵まれるのかも知れませんが）
source.english:
(Heh heh. Perhaps today, at last,
I'll be blessed with a moment when I can see all the way up…)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（しかし今日の僕は、そんなものに惑わされる心の余裕なぞ、これっぽっちもないのです）
source.english: (But today I haven't the slightest room in my heart to be distracted by such things.)

source.japanese:
普段なら、仰向けに倒れたなり、膝曲げ尻で床漕ぐ尺取り虫、助平根性遺憾なく発揮して、不様も今はなんのその、気取りや道徳など蛸に食わせろとずりずりにじって、もっと良い位置へ、素敵な景色が見やすいところへと求めただろう。
　ああやっと、今度こそ、何もかもが同じのこの双子はスカートの中味まで一緒なのかどうか、朔屋の胸中に碩学苦悩させるヴォイニッチ写本の暗号のようにこびりついていた疑問が今まさになん氷解する、至上の歓びが彼の顔を嵐の後の金輪と輝かせるのだろう。
source.english:
Ordinarily he would have stayed on his back, bent his knees, and propelled himself across the floor on his backside like an inchworm. He would have exercised his lechery to the full, disgrace be damned. Feed pretensions and morals to the octopus! He would wriggle into a better position, seeking a clearer view of that lovely prospect.
Ah, finally. At last he would know whether these twins, identical in everything else, were identical beneath their skirts as well. That question clung to his mind like the cipher of the Voynich manuscript tormenting a great scholar. Now it would be solved. Supreme joy would light his face like the sun's golden disc after a storm.

source.japanese:
しかし今日の朔屋は、双子の下着にすら興味を持ち得ず、倒れたまま虚ろな笑みを浮かべたきりで。
　本人は如来の仏像の物憂げな笑みのつもりなのだろうが、はたから見れば慢性腸捻転に悩むジュゴンの顔にしか見えない。
source.english:
Today, however, he could not muster an interest even in the twins' underwear. He merely lay there with a hollow smile.
He probably thought he was wearing the melancholy smile of a Buddha statue. To anyone else, he looked like a dugong suffering from chronic intestinal torsion.

target.text: One had her elbow bent with her loosely clenched fist raised to her face, the other hand hanging by her flank with effortless ease: the Tenchi In-You no Kamae, the stance of Heaven and Earth, Yin and Yang, which might share some commonalities with the statue of the Kongou Rikishi in closed-mouthed form at some southern gate somewhere─── (TN: The gate referred to here is the Great South Gate of the Toudai-ji in Nara city where the statues of the two Deva kings sculpted by the ancient masters Unkei and Kaikei stand. The stance, "天地陰陽の構え", is a stance used in several traditional schools of Japanese martial arts, like the Yagyuu Shingan-ryuu.)

And her opponent on the other side was sinking imposingly, palms open, right hand raised high, left pushed below her hips, form as unwavering as a rock: the Tenchi no Kamae, the stance of Heaven and Earth. (TN: The stance "天地の構え" is a concept you will find in many different Japanese martial arts, be they old or new.)

Both parties were capable of responding to any manner of position taken, ready to engulf their opponent the instant their fighting spirit surged forth, such a flow of power dwelt within every nook and cranny of their bodies it could fill; it was in the way their bodies were positioned, and even their shouts of abuse were charged with a sharp, piercing kiai as they collided.

In fact, Sakuya had been hit by an impact as though physically struck right on the tip of his nose from the shrill voices of the twins flying through the room as he walked in through the doorway; he bent backwards with a "wah!", his feet slipped out from under him, and he fell disgracefully on his ass, the pain shooting from his hips to his eyes, scattering as fireworks and seeping out as tears, but then the first mates' thighs entered his field of vision as a result of his gaze moving downwards, striking in their vivid, supple forms.
【Naomasa】 （Huhuhu. Perhaps, luck willing, today, this time for sure, might be the day where I am blessed with a moment where I can see all the way into the deepest depths.)
【Naomasa】 （But as I am today, I don't have the mental capacity to be led astray by such things. Not in the least.)

Normally, he'd collapse on his back, facing upwards, bending his knees and scooting his ass across the floor like an inchworm, his perverted character unleashed in full force with no regrets: "Being disgraceful is really no big deal, you can take your affectations and your morals and throw them to the octopuses", he would think as he slid along the ground into a better position, looking for a place where he could more easily catch sight of that most wonderful of views.

Aah, finally, this time for sure, and since the twins were the same in just about everything, would the contents of their skirts also be the same? These questions, which had clung to Sakuya's mind the way the cipher of the Voynich manuscript had caused such mental anguish for many a great scholar, would be resolved this very moment, supreme rapture radiating off his face like the golden ring on the horizon glowing after a storm, surely.

But the Sakuya of today held no interest in even the underwear of these twins; he simply maintained a hollow smile as he remained crumpled on the ground. The man himself likely intended for it to be like the sombre smile of a Nyorai Buddha statue, but from the outside, it could only be interpreted as the face of a dugong suffering from chronic volvulus.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あ、朔屋。やっと来たね。
　って、なにそのうっすら気味の悪いにやにや顔は」
source.english:
“Oh, Sakuya. Finally.
What's with that faintly creepy grin?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ah, Sakuya. Finally showed up, huh? Wait, what's with that kinda creepy smirk on your face?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「どれどれ、ほんとだ。
　慢性胃潰瘍に悩むウェーカリ猿みたい」
source.english:
“Let's see.
Oh, it is. Like a uakari monkey with chronic stomach ulcers.”

source.japanese: 戸口に転がったままの朔屋を訝しみ、どれどれと歩み寄って覗きこんできた双子は、一様に眉を顰[ひそ]めた。自分の憂鬱を理解してくれない双子の鈍感さにいらついた朔屋は、言わずもいいことを口にする、してしまう。
source.english: Puzzled by Sakuya lying in the doorway, the twins came over to inspect him. Both frowned. Irritated by their insensitivity to his melancholy, he said something he need not have said. Said it anyway.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あのね、お二人とも。
　人の事見下ろしているのは結構なんですが、
　いいんですか、僕がちょっと頭をずらせば、
　スカートの奥、丸見えになりますよ？」
source.english:
“Listen, you two.
Looking down at me is all very well,
but are you sure about this? If I move my head a little,
I'll have a clear view up your skirts.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Lemme see, you're right. Looks like a Uakari monkey suffering from chronic stomach ulcers.」

Suspicious of Sakuya still lying in the doorway, the twins walked closer to get a better look, brows knitted uniformly. Fed up with how insensitive the twins were for not understanding his depression, Sakuya put something into words that he really was better off not having, that he did.

【Naomasa】 「Now listen here, you two. It's all well and good for you to look down on others, but is this really okay with you? If I were to move my head just a little, the depths of your skirts would be on full display, you know?」

source.japanese:
朔屋が言うか言わないかのうちに。
　どごんと。杭打ち機の轟音もて、叩きつけられるが長靴の踵[かかと]で、まともに受けたなら顔面は靴底の形に綺麗に撃ち抜かれていただろうとも。ぷしゅうと、焦臭い煙さえ上がったのが朔屋の顔のすぐ横である。靴と顔との隙間は紙一枚程度であった。かの金字塔の石組みを構築するのと同じ精度であった。そしてシサムだかキサラだかの顔は、その古代建造物の脇に侍るスフィンクスと同じく平板なものであった。
source.english:
Before he had even quite finished—
Wham. A boot heel slammed down with the roar of a pile driver. Had it hit squarely, his face would have been punched out in the neat shape of its sole. A little puff of scorched-smelling smoke even rose beside his cheek. The gap between boot and face was scarcely a sheet of paper: the precision of the stonework in a pyramid. And Sisam's face—or Kisara's—was as blank as the Sphinx beside that ancient monument.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわあ危ないッ。やめましょうよ。
　……しかしあなた達は足もでかいですね。
　こうして並べると俺の顔と同じくらい。
　───ひゃあ！」
source.english:
“Whoa, that was close! Let's not do that.
…You've got big feet, too, haven't you? Side by side like this, one's about as big as my face.
—Eek!”

target.text: While the words had barely left Sakuya's mouth. Ka-KLONK. With the thundering of a pile-driver, the heel of a boot violently slammed against the floor, and had he taken that straight to the face, there would now be a sole-sized hole punched clean through it. Burnt-smelling smoke even rose up with a hiss from right next to Sakuya's face. The gap between the boot and his face was about the thickness of a sheet of paper. A level of precision rivalling the masonry of the famous pyramids. And the expressions on Shisamu's and Kisara's faces were as flat as that of the Sphinx serving by that ancient structure's side.
【Naomasa】 「Waah, that was close! Let's not do that. ……But wow, your feet are also real big, aren't they? When they're next to me like this, they look almost as big as my face. ───HIAH!」

source.japanese: 今日はただただ自滅嗜好に取り付かれている青年にも、どうにか残っていた、最低限の生存本能に感謝するがいい、咄嗟に身を翻[ひるがえ]してかわした第二撃、それまで朔屋の顔のあった位置にめりこんで、かと思えば矢継ぎ早に三撃四撃がどこんどこんと降り注ぎ、彼は自分の体がいったいどうやって最後まで回避し得たものか後になっても判らず、当然、双子のスカートの奥など覗いている暇などあろう筈もない。
source.english: Let the young man give thanks for the bare minimum of survival instinct somehow remaining amid today's urge toward self-destruction. He twisted aside at once. The second blow sank into the place his face had just occupied; then a third and fourth followed in rapid, thundering succession. Even afterward, he could not explain how his body had evaded them all. Naturally, he had no time to look up the twins' skirts.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「見、見えない。見えてませんってば。
　あなた達のでかい足の裏以外はなんもっ」
source.english:
“I can't see! I'm not seeing anything, honest!
Nothing but the bottoms of your enormous feet!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だからもう、勘弁してくれろーーっ」
source.english: “So please give me a break!”

target.text: Though this young man was possessed by nothing but self-destructive tendencies today, the absolute minimum of survival instincts somehow yet remained with him, something he should be grateful for; the second assault that he dodged by instantly changing the orientation of his body lodged right into the place where Sakuya's face had been until just before, and no sooner than that, a third and a fourth attack came raining down upon him, one after the other; how in the world his own body managed to dodge every single one until the very end was something he remained uncertain of after, and of course, he wasn't given a moment to peek into the depths of the twins' skirts.
【Naomasa】 「Didn't-, I didn't see. I said I didn't see anything. I saw nothing other than the soles of your huge feet!」
【Naomasa】 「So please, have mercy on meーー!」

source.japanese:
荒野の風に翻弄される回転草よろしく横転を繰り返し、戸口から部屋の中まで追いこまれ、よしなら寝台の下の暗がりに逃げこもう、としたら朔屋の鼻面は何かにめりこんだ、悪く柔らかい、何か。
　柔らかいとて痛みはなかったけれど息が詰まる、思いきり吸いこんで、鼻腔から脳の深くまで浸透した感覚は、悪臭だと、それも催涙瓦斯級の臭いだと判別されたのは一瞬遅れてのこと。
　青年は、転がりこんだのと同じ、いやもっと凄い勢いで寝台の下から飛び出して、室内をのたうつわ転げ回るわで、油虫に殺虫剤を撒くと大概こうなる。
source.english:
Like tumbleweed at the mercy of a wilderness wind, he rolled and rolled, driven from the doorway clear into the cabin. Very well, then—he would take refuge in the darkness beneath the bed. At which point Sakuya’s nose buried itself in something. Something unpleasantly soft.
Soft, so it did not hurt; but it stopped his breath. He sucked in a mighty lungful, and the sensation drove up through his nostrils into the depths of his brain. Only a beat later did he identify it as a stench—and a stench of tear-gas caliber.
The young man came shooting out from under the bed with the same momentum that had carried him in—no, with considerably more—and went writhing and rolling about the cabin. This, broadly speaking, is what happens when one sprays a cockroach with insecticide.

target.text: He rolled around sideways, again and again, like a tumbleweed buffeted by the wind in the wastelands, driven from the doorway and into the middle of the room; right, in that case, he'd try to escape into the darkness under the bed, and once he did, something hit Sakuya on the nose, an awfully soft……something.

It was soft, so it didn't exactly hurt, but he had trouble breathing, and when he inhaled with all his might, he was a moment too late in discerning that the sensation that permeated every part of him, from his nasal cavities to the deepest recesses of his brain, that awful stench, was on the level of tear gas. Just like when he'd rolled around before, no, now with far greater vigour, the young man leapt out from underneath the bed, writhing in pain as he tumbled about the room; if you spray a cockroach with insecticide, this is usually what you'll see.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……あん？　キサラ、ベッドの下って、
　何突っ込んであったっけか？」
source.english:
“…Huh? Kisara,
what did we put under the bed again?”

source.japanese: 二人、顔を見合わせて首を捻り、
source.english: The two looked at one another and tilted their heads.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……Huh? Kisara, what exactly was it we stuffed under the bed again?」
The two looked each other in the face, then cocked their heads in puzzlement,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ええと確か、履きっぱだったソックス……とか？　普段はあんま脱がないけど」
source.english: “Um, socks we'd been wearing forever… I think? We don't usually take them off much.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Uuuhm, if I'm not mistaken, some socks we'd been wearing…… or something? Not like we take them off that often though, normally.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ああそうそう。雨続きで長靴の中が湿気っぽくなった時なんか、脱いでそのまま放りこんであった───っけ？」
source.english: “Oh, right. When it kept raining and things got damp inside our boots, we took them off and threw them in there… Didn't we?”

source.japanese: 海上生活に慣れた彼女達であり、普段は就寝する時であっても、変事あれば直ぐさま駆け出せるよう長靴を履いたままベッドに入る事が多い。その彼女達でさえ、酷く蒸した時、或いは長靴の裡まで浸水した場合には流石に耐えきれなくなって素足で眠る。その際無頓着にも脱ぎ散らされた靴下は、さて今まで一体どこへと消えていたやら、この大海原の何処にか存在するという、靴下が樹に実り川に流れる物も靴下という、靴下の靴下による靴下の為の楽園、おおよそこの世に送り出された靴下達全てが夢想するという未知なる靴下島へと飛翔していったかと、双子はたいして気にも留めなんだのだが。真実は、二人が無意識に寝台下に蹴りこんでいたと、そういうことらしい。
source.english: Accustomed to life at sea, they often went to bed in their boots, ready to spring out at the first emergency. Even they could not endure extreme stuffiness, or water getting into their boots, and would then sleep barefoot. Where had all the socks so carelessly discarded on those occasions disappeared to? Perhaps they had flown away to that unknown island somewhere in the ocean, where socks grew on trees and even the things floating down its rivers were socks. A paradise of socks, by socks, for socks, of which almost every sock sent into this world supposedly dreamed. The twins had given it little thought. The truth, apparently, was that they had unconsciously kicked them beneath the bed.

source.japanese:
しかも、二人が信天翁号に乗船してからこの現在に至るまで、延々と。およそ女の子であろうが男の子であろうが寝台の下というのは長ずるにつれ、様々な秘密が隠匿される隙間となるのが通例で、為に『寝台下の怪物』なる概念は、寝台の主の幼年期にしかいられない。しかし双子担当の『怪物』は、鼻に栓して逃げ出していったに相違なく、秘密も浪漫もへったくれもあったものかの。
　事実朔屋も、女性の靴下というフェティッシュな代物に文字通り顔から埋もれていったにもかかわらず、溢れ出る涙は感涙ではなく苦し涙の、鼻から喉を爛れさせる刺激に溢れ出した粘液と混ざり合ったそれ。
source.english:
And had continued doing so from the day they joined the Albatross to the present. Whether a child is a boy or girl, the space beneath the bed generally becomes a hiding place for all manner of secrets as the child grows. Thus the ‘monster under the bed’ can remain only through the owner's childhood. The monster assigned to the twins, however, must have fled holding its nose. Secrets? Romance? Not a chance.
Indeed, although Sakuya had literally buried himself face-first in that fetishist's delight, women's socks, his overflowing tears were not tears of rapture but agony. They mingled with the mucus pouring out under an irritation that seemed to sear him from nose to throat.

source.japanese: 官土と名づく、藁灰入りの劣悪な阿片などより、三年もの間洗わずにいた靴下をば貴び、袋に入れて深々吸いこみ陶酔するような通好みならおそらくこれを愉悦として堪能しうるだろうが、朔屋は生憎そんな深い領域までには至っていなかったのは、不幸なのか幸なのか。
source.english: A connoisseur who prized socks left unwashed for three years above even the wretched straw-ash adulterated opium called kando, who bagged them and inhaled deeply in bliss, might have relished this pleasure. Unfortunately, Sakuya had not attained such depths. Or was that fortunate?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだこれ。
　目が痛い鼻が沁みる、
　喉の奥からつんとくる。
　うえがはえほおええええっっ」
source.english:
“What is this? My eyes hurt,
my nose burns,
it's stinging all the way from the back of my throat.
Uehaghaehoeeeh!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやほんと、なにこれ。
　ジョセフィーヌ、今晩だけは勘弁してつかあさい」
source.english:
“No, really,
what is this? Josephine, spare me just for tonight!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Aaah, right, right. Back when it kept raining all the time and our boots got all damp inside, we just took them off and tossed them under there I───think?」

These were women used to life on the sea, so normally, even when going to sleep, they'd often wear their boots to bed so they could immediately rush out if any emergencies demanded it. But even these women, at times when it was awfully hot and humid, or perhaps in situations where their boots had been submerged in water, soaked even on the inside, as one might expect, even they couldn't endure that and instead slept with bare feet.

And the socks they had so nonchalantly taken off and tossed around, now, where had they disappeared to until now? Had they perhaps taken flight to that place which exists somewhere in these vast seas, where socks grow as fruits on trees and what flows downriver is socks as well, a paradise of socks for the socks, by the socks, had they left for this yet undiscovered island of socks, that which is said to be the dream that just about all the socks sent out into this world of ours yearn for? The twins didn't seem to have given that issue much thought, but. The truth is, it seemed the two had unconsciously kicked them under their bed, or something to that effect.

Furthermore, from ever since the two of them first boarded this Albatross and up until this present day, this had gone on endlessly. As a rule, whether one is a boy or a girl, as one grows up, the space beneath the bed usually becomes a crevice of sorts where a wide variety of secrets are concealed, for the concept of 『The Monster Beneath the Bed』 only exists during the early childhood of the owner of said bed. However, the 『Monster』in charge of the twins must doubtless have plugged its nose and made its escape, and there were no secrets, romance, or any other such worthless trivialities to be found beneath this bed.

Back in reality, despite Sakuya literally having his face buried in the fetishistic article that was a woman's used socks, it was not tears of gratitude that flooded from his eyes but rather tears of suffering, mixed with the tidal wave of mucus oozing out of his nose from his throat, inflamed by the stinging stimulus.

Were one the sort of connoisseur who would prize these socks that had gone unwashed for three whole years, put them in a bag, then deeply inhale to achieve a state of intoxication far greater than what could be obtained from the poor-quality opium intermixed with straw ash known as kando, then one could probably have one's fill of pleasure and delight from these socks, but was it a blessing or misfortune that Sakuya had yet to step into such deep, dark realms? (TN: Kando, or "官土", originates from the slang terms used in the opium trade in East Asia. Kando is opium that is government-sanctioned, provided through the opium monopoly system managed by the Japanese colonial powers pre-WW2.)
【Naomasa】 「What the hell is this. My eyes hurt, my nose stings, something acrid is coming from the back of my throat. UEEHGHEGHOOEEEERGH!」
【Naomasa】 「No, seriously, what is this? Not tonight, Josephine!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ああ、どっかのナポレオンたらいうおっさんが寝てるところ、鼻先にチーズ持ってったら、奥さんの名前叫んで飛び起きたっつう」
source.english: “Oh, that fellow Napoleon or whoever. They put cheese under his nose while he was asleep, and he jumped up shouting his wife's name.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Right, they say that when some old guy from somewhere called Napoleon went to bed, if you then put some cheese under his nose, he'd jump out of bed and scream his wife's name.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「えー、あんな青カビたかった、くっさいチーズ臭と一緒にしない。
　……ていうか、そこまでひどい？」
source.english:
“Hey, don't compare it to that stinking blue-mold cheese.
…Is it really that bad?”

source.japanese: 二人の憮然とした顔と声音も届いた様子なく、じたばたと転がり回ってはあちこちの角に頭をぶつけて苦鳴を上げる直正に、双子も興味をついつい催した、が世には『よせばいいのに』との言葉もあって、シサムが部屋に転がっていた銛の先で、寝台下から一切れ引っぱり出したのもまさにその言葉通り。
source.english: Neither their affronted faces nor their voices seemed to reach Naomasa. He thrashed about, struck his head against various corners, and groaned in pain. The twins could not help becoming curious. But there is an expression in this world: ‘Leave well enough alone.’ Sisam, using the tip of a harpoon lying in the cabin to pull a scrap from beneath the bed, furnished a perfect example of why.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Ehh, don't lump them in with some stinky cheese covered in blue mold. ……Wait, is it really that bad?」

Neither their dumbfounded faces nor the sound of their voices seemed to reach him, and as they watched Naomasa roll around for some time, bumping his head on corners here and there, letting out anguished screams, the twins couldn't help but become curious, but there is a saying in this world, 『Leave well enough alone』, and that scrap of fabric Shisamu dragged out from beneath the bed using the tip of a harpoon that was lying on the floor, now that was exactly what those words were meant for.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あれ、あたしらこんな色のソックス持ってたっけ？」
source.english: “Huh? Did we have socks this color?”

source.japanese:
銛の先にぶら下げられた布切れは、薄鮮やかな緑だの橙だののだんだらに彩られ、二人の記憶にある灰色から隔たった色合いに、首を傾げつつ鼻先まで近づけて、ところで読書氏よ、諸賢はこの手のたまらない緊張に満ちた瞬間に覚えはないか。舞台上の男女の役者が、森の木陰で平和な睦言を愉[たの]しんでいるその幹の後ろに、匕首翳[かざ]した殺人鬼役の潜[ひそ]んでいるのが判った時などの、観客であるにもかかわらず大声上げて舞台に駆け上がりたくなるような瞬間だ。
　この一瞬、二瞬がそんな緊張で、焦れったくなるまでに拡張された果てに、遂に、起こった。
source.english:
The scrap dangling from the harpoon was streaked in pale, vivid green and orange. These colors were a long way from the gray the two remembered. Puzzled, they drew it toward their noses. Dear reader, have you ever known a moment of such intolerable suspense? Onstage, a man and woman enjoy peaceful lovers' talk beneath a tree. Behind its trunk, you see a lurking murderer with a dagger raised. Though only a spectator, you want to shout and rush onto the stage. A moment like that.
These one or two instants stretched with just such tension, to the point of maddening impatience. Then, at last, it happened.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Huh. Did we ever have any socks in this colour?」

The scrap of cloth hanging from the tip of the harpoon was coloured in uneven stripes of pale and vibrant greens and oranges, and while they tilted their heads in confusion at this combination of colours, which was quite distant from the grey of their memories, they brought it closer to their noses.

Incidentally, dear readers, have any of you wise gentlemen and ladies ever experienced a moment so filled with an unbearable tension before? The moment when, on a stage, where a male and female actor are enjoying some whispered intimacies in the peaceful forest tree-shade, you notice that a homicidal maniac holding aloft a dagger is hiding right behind the tree trunk they're sitting by, and even though you're but a member of the audience, you want to yell out loud and jump onto the scene, a moment just like that? After those one or two blinks of the eye, filled with such tension, stretched to the point of agonizing impatience, then, finally, it happened.
【Kisara】 「…………Ulp……」

source.japanese:
異音伴い腹部から喉が見てとれるほどに蠕動する、次いで頬が蛙のように丸く大きく膨らむ、喇叭を宛ってもいないのに、きつくに窄められた唇に浮いた細かな皺は、口腔に内在する巨大な圧力を示してだ。
　双子は目玉を裏返らせながら、必死で口を押さえて、船室の内壁の一点をぶん殴ったが二人一つの動作。
source.english:
With a strange noise, their bodies convulsed so violently that the peristaltic surge from belly to throat was visible; then their cheeks ballooned, round and huge as frogs’. No trumpet had been put to either mouth, yet the fine creases in their tightly pursed lips betrayed the enormous pressure contained within.
Their eyes rolling back, each twin clamped one hand desperately over her mouth and drove the other fist into the same spot on the cabin wall—two bodies, one motion.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「──────Gwah.」

Accompanied by a bizarre noise, they visibly vermiculated from their stomach to their throats; then their cheeks swelled up, big and round like a frog's, and though they weren't even holding a trumpet to their mouths, the fine wrinkles still surfacing around their tightly puckered lips spoke of the colossal pressure contained within their oral cavities. While their eyes rolled back in their heads, the twins desperately held their mouths closed, and both slammed a fist into the same spot on the cabin wall, movements synchronized, two as one.

source.japanese: 拳叩きつけられた衝撃は震動を生み、壁を走って双子の船室から外まで走り───
source.english: The impact of their fists produced a vibration. It ran along the wall, out of the twins' cabin—

source.japanese: 震動は信天翁号の内壁隔壁を超えて通路を駆け抜け天井を伝い───
source.english: Through the Albatross's inner walls and bulkheads, down passages, along ceilings—

source.japanese: やや減衰しながらも、明確な意志と力でもって、船内のある一箇所に到達した───
source.english: Somewhat diminished, but still with clear purpose and force, it reached one particular spot aboard—

target.text: The impact of their striking fists brought a tremor into the world: it ran along the walls, all the way outside the twins' cabin───
The tremor crossed the internal bulkheads of the Albatross, sweeping through the passageways along the ceiling───
Though somewhat dampened, with a clear will and strength, it reached a certain point within the ship───

source.japanese: ある一箇所、その場所、船長クロが、お遊び『一人影踏み』───ちなみにこの、当然何時まで経っても終わらないお遊戯は、或る心優しい下級水夫が彼女に教えてやったものであるが、後からそいつは、かの文士が倫敦留学中に患ったのと同じ類の病に罹患していた事が判明した───に夢中になっていた、瀝青臭い船倉の一画まで震動は届き、積み上げられていた貨物の函の天辺に、不安定に乗せられていた大きな金盥を揺らして、落としたがちょうどクロの脳天へ。鳴った音が高かった。
source.english: That particular spot was a tar-scented corner of the hold where Captain Kuro was engrossed in ‘Solo Shadow Tag.’ A kindhearted junior sailor had taught her this game, which, naturally, could never end. He was later discovered to suffer from the same sort of illness that afflicted a certain man of letters during his studies in London. The vibration reached that corner, shook a large metal washbasin balanced precariously atop stacked cargo crates, and dropped it squarely onto Kuro's head. The resulting note was high.

target.text: A certain point, that place, right where Captain Kuro was playing 『Stepping on Shadows By Myself』 ───Incidentally, this game, which would naturally never end no matter how much time passed, was something taught to the girl by a certain kindhearted deck boy; later, it would come to light that said deck boy had contracted a disease of the same kind as the one a certain literary man had suffered from during his studies abroad in London─── (TN: A reference to Natsume Souseki, one of Japan's greatest writers, who suffered a nervous breakdown during his time spent studying literature in London between 1900-1902.)

While her mind was completely engrossed in her little game, the tremor reached all the way to this corner of the ship's tar-smelling hold, and there, at the top of the piled-up crates of cargo, it shook loose a large metal basin that been left there unsecured, and it fell right towards the crown of Kuro's head. The sound it made rang loud and clear.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ひきゃああっっ!?」
source.english: “Hikyaaa!?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「HIKYAAAH!?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「とっても痛いくて、頭が、だから痛い。
　これなに……クロの頭をぶったら痛いのよ」
source.english:
“It hurts so much. My head, it… it hurts.
What's this…? It hurts when you hit Kuro's head.”

source.japanese: 舌足らずに呻[うめ]いて座りこんだクロの前に、破鐘の響きで転がった金盥の内に貼りつけられていた一枚の紙切れ、頭をさすりつ拾い上げれば書きつけられた一連の指示。
source.english: She sat down, groaning in her stumbling way. The basin rolled before her with the clang of a cracked bell. A scrap of paper was pasted inside. Rubbing her head, she picked it up. On it was a set of instructions.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「It hurts so much, head, so it hurts. What is this……if you hit Kuro's head, it really hurts.」

There, before Kuro, who was plopped down on the floor and groaning with poor enunciation, was a single scrap of paper that had been stuck to the inside of the metal basin rolling over with the discordant peal of a cracked bell, and when she picked it up while massaging her head, there turned out to be a sequence of instructions written down on it.

source.japanese:
『このタライに古新聞しいて、
　全速力で
　一等航海士船室まで持ってこい
　もたもたしてたら
　───【逆さはりつけ股ざきの刑】』
source.english:
LINE THIS BASIN WITH OLD NEWSPAPER.
BRING IT TO THE FIRST OFFICER'S CABIN
AT FULL SPEED.
IF YOU DAWDLE—
UPSIDE-DOWN CRUCIFIXION AND LEG-SPLITTING.

target.text: 『Lay out some old newspapers in this washbasin Then bring it to the first mates' cabin at full speed Should you dawdle ───【Upside-down Stake-tied Crotch-splitting Punishment】』

source.japanese:
クロにとってこんなに難しい指示を、読み下すだけでも一五秒、そして『逆さ磔股裂きの刑』で恐怖の余り意識が飛んで再起動するまでまた一〇秒、走り出したその時に内股になっていたのは、想像しただけで膀胱がえらい事になりそうだったから。
　もうクロはそれは急いで焦って懸命だったのだとも。
source.english:
Instructions this difficult took Kuro fifteen seconds merely to read. ‘Upside-down crucifixion and leg-splitting’ then frightened her into unconsciousness; another ten seconds passed before she restarted. When she finally ran, her knees turned inward. The mere thought was doing dreadful things to her bladder.
Kuro was hurrying, panicking, trying with all her might.

target.text: It took Kuro fifteen seconds to just read instructions this complicated all the way to the end, and the tremendous terror she felt at the words 『Upside-down Stake-tied Crotch-splitting Punishment』 caused her to lose consciousness, and it took her another ten seconds for her mind to reboot; the reason she ran pigeon-toed as she took off was because just imagining it alone almost took her bladder past the breaking point. By now, Kuro was in such a frantic rush, hurrying along with all she had.

source.japanese:
だからシサムキサラの船室まで辿り着いた時、クロの上半身が隠れるくらい大きな盥のあちこちに凹みが出来ていたのも、当直を寝過ごして水夫長から折檻くらった時のように鼻血を垂らしていたのも、それまでの労苦と必死さを物語っていたけれど。
　クロを待ち受けていたのは、シサムキサラ、そしてこちらも臨界を迎えた朔屋の、口元押さえて口内に押し戻さんとする、珍妙にして異様な形相。三人が金盥に飛びついた勢いでクロは簡単に失神し、後は───
source.english:
By the time she reached Sisam and Kisara's cabin, the basin, large enough to hide her upper body, had acquired dents here and there. Blood ran from her nose as it did when the boatswain punished her for sleeping through a watch. Both spoke of her exertions and desperate haste.
But waiting for her were Sisam, Kisara, and Sakuya, who had reached his own critical point. All three pressed hands over their mouths, trying to force their contents back inside. Their faces were bizarre and grotesque. The force with which they lunged at the basin easily knocked Kuro unconscious. After that—

target.text: So by the time she reached Shisamu and Kisara's cabin, the metal basin big enough to hide Kuro's upper body from view was dented here and there, and blood dripped down from her nose like she'd received physical punishment from the Bosun for oversleeping while on watch: all of it attested to how hard she'd struggled, how desperate she was, but. What awaited Kuro there was Shisamu and Kisara, as well as Sakuya, who had all already reached criticality, holding their mouths closed and trying to push what was inside their mouths back down, a decidedly bizarre expression. As all three eagerly jumped at the washbasin, Kuro quickly fainted, and after that───

source.japanese:
見るも凄絶。
　
　───聞くも無惨。
　
　──────嗅ぐも、酸鼻。
source.english:
Dreadful to behold.
—Horrific to hear.
——And to smell: appalling.

target.text: To behold it was gruesome. ───To hear it, atrocious. ──────And smell it, harrowing.

source.japanese:
そして大三角江をば大海嘯が逆流し、賽の河原にては硫黄混じりの間歇泉が噴出し、ぱんぱんに詰まった水風船が炸裂した。
（以上暗喩的表現）
source.english:
A vast tidal bore surged upriver through a great delta. Sulfurous geysers erupted at Sai-no-Kawara, the riverbank of the dead. A water balloon filled to bursting exploded.
The foregoing expressions are metaphorical.

target.text: Thus, a grand tidal bore came surging back up through the vast estuary; a geyser intermixed with sulfur spouted into the skies on the bank of the River Sanzu; the water balloon, filled to the breaking point, burst open. （The above is metaphorical expression）

source.japanese: その夜、甲板上の雨水桶で、クロがただでさえ紅い眼を白目まで充血させて、どこか偏執的な趣さえ漂わせた泣き顔で、
source.english: That night, at a rainwater barrel on deck, Kuro was seen with even the whites of her already red eyes bloodshot. Her tearful face had an almost obsessive air—

target.text: That night, by the rainwater pail on the upper deck, Kuro, whose eyes were already red at the best of times, had even the whites of her eyes congested with blood, with a tear-streaked face that exuded a hint of obsessiveness,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
『落ちないの。
　こすっても洗っても、
　臭い、取れないよう……』
source.english:
“It won't come off.
I scrub and wash,
but the smell won't go away…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
『これ、髪の毛の中まで入りこんでるの、
　グリーンピースさん、ピーマンさん、ニンジンさん……』
source.english:
“It's got right into my hair.
Mr. Green Pea, Mr. Bell Pepper, Mr. Carrot…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
『今日のお昼ご飯にでてたっけ……。
　クロが苦手なものばっかで、よけい、気持ち、悪く、なってきて……』
source.english:
“Were they in today's lunch…?
They're all things Kuro doesn't like. It makes me feel even more, more sick…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Won't come off. No matter how Kuro scrubs and washes, the smell won't come off……」
【Kuro】 「They're all the way in Kuro's hair. Mister Green Pea, Mister Bell Pepper, Mister Carrot……」
【Kuro】 「All things from today's lunch……. All things Kuro doesn't like. Only makes, Kuro feel, even more ill……」

source.japanese:
とか髪やら体やら執拗に濯いでいる姿が目撃されており、不審を抱いた下級水夫が理由を問い質したところ、何事を思い出したのか引きつけの発作を起こした為、不憫と覚えて大部屋まで保護していったのだが、彼の優しい心根が仇となった。
　下級水夫達と共にいったんは眠りに落ちたクロが、真夜中過ぎに絶叫とともに跳ね起き、両腕振り回しながら駆けずり回った為、寝網から叩き落とされ腰を打った者多数、クロにすがりつかれて涙と涎と鼻水まみれにされた上にその半狂乱の有り様に当てられ軽く狂気が伝染した者数名、と二次被害が拡大してしまったのだが、さてこれは余談。
source.english:
She kept rinsing her hair and body, saying such things. A puzzled junior sailor asked why. Whatever she remembered sent her into a convulsive fit. Taking pity, he brought her to the communal quarters for safety. His kindness worked against him.
Kuro initially fell asleep among the junior sailors. After midnight, she sprang up screaming and ran about waving both arms. Many were knocked from their hammocks and hurt their backs. Several others, clung to by Kuro and covered in tears, saliva, and snot, were so affected by her half-crazed state that a mild madness spread to them. The secondary damage grew. But that is a digression.

target.text: So she went, and when she was spotted rinsing her hair and body by a deck boy who, harbouring some suspicions, went to inquire about the reason for all this, perhaps she remembered something, for she had a fit of febrile convulsions, and finding her pitiable as a result, he escorted her to their large room, his kind disposition ultimately becoming his downfall.

Kuro, who had fallen asleep together with the deck boys for a time, suddenly leapt out of bed with a loud scream past midnight, running around the room while flailing her arms about, causing several sailors to be knocked out of their hammocks and hit their lower backs, and there were also several who, after being clung to by Kuro covered in tears, drool, and snot, not to mention her half-crazed state, were infected with a light bout of madness in turn, and so the secondary damage compounded, but setting that aside, for it is a digression.

source.japanese:
ともかく航海士の船室では、というと。
　三人は揃って胃液臭い溜め息をか細く吐いて、壁にもたれかかったのさえ辛そうな。朔屋などは日頃から不健康そうな痩せた頬が、より陰濃くこずんでいる。寝台下の危険物の事など、処理はおろか思いめぐらすだけでもまた腑がひっくり返りそうになるので、努めて念頭から追いやって、朔屋がようやく言葉らしい音を口にした。
source.english:
Meanwhile, back in the navigators' cabin.
The three gave faint sighs smelling of gastric juice. Even leaning against the wall seemed painful. Sakuya's ordinarily thin, unhealthy cheeks had sunk into deeper shadow. Merely thinking about the hazardous material beneath the bed, much less disposing of it, threatened to turn their guts over again. He did his best to drive it from his mind. Finally he produced something resembling words.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああもう……なんだって一体こんな羽目になった……」
source.english: “Oh, enough already… How on earth did it come to this…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうだ俺は、あんた達の怒鳴り声が、
　部屋の外まで響いてきたのが気になって」
source.english:
“Right. I heard you two yelling all the way outside the room,
and I was wondering—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……一体なんだってあんな、
　剣呑にやりあってたんですよ？」
source.english:
“…What were you fighting
about so viciously?”

source.japanese:
朔屋の目の色は、普段通りのへらへらと軽薄で真剣味にかける彼に立ち返っており、鬱は腐敗極めたソックスと、それから内臓口から出そうになるまで盛大に吐いて吐いて吐きまくったことにより、脳髄の外へ蹴り出されたらしい。
　それが彼とその周囲にとってよかったのかどうかは別として。
source.english:
His eyes had regained their usual frivolity. He was once more his grinning, unserious self. The socks, rotted to perfection, and the prodigious vomiting that had almost brought his insides out through his mouth seemed to have kicked depression clear of his brain.
Whether this was good for him or those around him was another matter.

target.text: Anyhow, back to matters in the first mates' cabin. All three as one were letting out enervated sighs reeking of gastric juices, finding it exhausting to just lean against the wall. Sakuya's cheeks, already gaunt and sickly-looking on a good day, had sunk even further into deep, dark shadows. Just pondering on the hazardous articles beneath the bed, let alone how to deal with them, was enough to make his innards topple over, so he did his utmost to drive it from his mind, and Sakuya finally produced a sound that was reminiscent of words.
【Naomasa】 「Aah, come on……why in the world did this have to happen to me……」
【Naomasa】 「That's right. Your angry shouting could be heard all the way outside your room, so I got curious.」
【Naomasa】 「……Just what exactly could have made you two leap at each other's throats like that?」

The look in Sakuya's eyes had returned to his usual careless frivolity, lacking any trace of sobriety, and it seemed that his depression had been kicked out of his brain by those utterly putrescent socks and the resulting deluge of puking, puking, and more puking everywhere until his internal organs were about to exit him through his mouth. Whether that was a positive development for the man himself and his surroundings was another thing.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ああ、それ……。
　いやあたしらは、ただ、さあ……」
source.english:
“Oh, that… Well,
we were just, you know…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Aah, that……. No, we were just-, so, about that……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「うん、ただちょっとね、
　アクちゃん、採りに行けないかって相談してたんだけど」
source.english:
“Yes,
we were only talking about whether we could go get little Aku.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なにそのアクちゃんっていうのは」
source.english: “What's this little Aku?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Yeah, we were just, you know, having a little discussion about if we should go fish up Aku-chan or not.」
【Naomasa】 「And what is this Aku-chan?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そのことで、あんたを呼んだのよ」
source.english: “That's what we called you for.”

source.japanese:
双子の説明にいわく───
　魚、なのだそうだ。
　それも、今のところ信天翁号が燻っているこの内海の、船の現在位置から少しばかり離れた海域に位置する、とある岩礁付近にしかいない魚だとか。
　活け作りが最高で、頭はその後に兜焼きにするのだという。双子が揉めていたのは、兜焼きにしたその魚の、どっちが目玉周りのぷるぷるを取るかで喧嘩になったからだとか。
　朔屋は、鬱とは別の脱力感に、またへなへなと脱力したことである。
source.english:
According to the twins—
It was a fish.
A fish found only around a certain reef in these inland waters, a little way from where the Albatross presently lay idle.
It was finest sliced and served fresh while still alive; afterward, the head was grilled. The twins had fallen out over which of them would get the soft, quivering flesh around the eyes of that grilled head.
Sakuya wilted all over again, overcome by a lassitude that had nothing whatever to do with depression.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どんだけ旨い魚か知らないけどさ、
　目ン玉なんて二つあるでしょ、
　仲良く半分こすりゃあいいだろうに」
source.english:
“I don't know how good this fish tastes,
but it has two eyes, doesn't it?
Why not share nicely and take one each?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「That's actually why we called for you.」

According to their explanation─── It was a fish, or so it seemed. And furthermore, it was a fish that only lived near a certain reef, one located in waters just a little ways from the Albatross' present position in the inlet sea where the ship was currently languishing, or something. The best way to prepare it was as fresh sashimi, and the head could then be served broiled. The twins had been arguing over which of them would get to take the succulent, gelatinous flesh around the eyeballs of that fish's broiled head for herself, and so it turned into a fight, or something.
Sakuya was assaulted by a feeling of enervation entirely different from his depression, then grew weak from exhaustion once more.
【Naomasa】 「Now, I don't know exactly how delicious this fish is, but there's got to be two eyeballs, right? You could just be nice and do halfsies.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あ、言ったね。あんたあれの旨さを知らないからそんなこと言えるんだ」
source.english: “Ha, listen to you. You can only say that because you don't know how good it is.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ah, he really went there. You can only say that because you don't know how tasty that fish is.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そーそー。二つあったら、二つとも独り占めにしたくなるって絶対」
source.english: “Exactly. If there are two, you'll want both for yourself. Guaranteed.”

source.japanese: じゅるじゅると、肉食の獣がするような舌なめずりに、朔屋はいささか、いやかなりげんなりする。
source.english: They licked their lips with the wet relish of carnivorous beasts. Sakuya found it a little—no, considerably—dispiriting.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「で、俺を呼んだわけは？」
source.english: “So why call me?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Yeah, yeah. If there's two, you'll want to hog them both, for sure.」
With a loud slurping, they licked their lips like carnivorous beasts, and Sakuya was a little, no, quite fed up with the whole matter.
【Naomasa】 「So, the reason you called me was?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「いやあ、今日は二人揃って体が空く時間は短くってさ。あたし等ちょっと行けそうにないから、あんたにとってきて欲しくって」
source.english: “Well, we haven't got much time when we're both free today. Looks like we can't go. We wanted you to get it for us.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「二人揃って空く時間が長くとれないって。
　じゃ、どっちか片方が行けばいいだろうに」
source.english:
“Not much time when you're both free?
Then why doesn't one of you go?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Weeell, see, the two of us have little free time together. And it doesn't really seem like we'll get the chance to go, so we'd like for you to go catch one for us.」
【Naomasa】 「You don't have a lot of free time together, you say. Well then, surely one of you two could just go alone.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あ、それだめ」
source.english: “Oh, that won't work.”

source.japanese:
なんでも、双子は。
　シサム・キサラ。
　大胆不敵にして天衣無縫を地でいく二人、そして信天翁号の一等航海士を、二人で務める双子の姉妹。
　二人で、というのは彼女達は常に相手が視界のうちにいないと頭がおかしくなるという奇病に取り付かれており、余り遠くに離れる事ができないから。二人が一番落ち着く体勢は、背中合わせに密着した状態で、この体勢の彼女達は、ほとんど無敵だという。やむなく遠く離れる場合はお互いを命綱で結び合うが、これで持つのは三時間程度。
　───だそうで。
source.english:
It seemed that the twins—
Sisam and Kisara.
Those fearless, utterly uninhibited sisters who together served as the Albatross's first officer.
Together, because they suffered from a peculiar illness: unless each could always see the other, they went mad. They could not go very far apart. Their most comfortable position was pressed back-to-back; in that formation, they were apparently almost invincible. If obliged to separate by some distance, they tied themselves together with a lifeline. That kept them going for about three hours.
—or so they said.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんたらは無敵の女と思ってたんだが……。
　よくよく難儀な体質に祟られたもんだ。
　ともかく、だから俺に、
　そのなんとか言う魚をとってこいと」
source.english:
“I thought you two were invincible women…
That's a troublesome condition you've been cursed
with. Anyway,
that's why you want me to fetch this whatever-it-is fish.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Ah, that won't work.」

In any and every which way, twins. Shisamu・Kisara. These two, living embodiments of genuinely daredevil, free spirits, a law unto themselves, as well as the first mates of the Albatross, these twin sisters.

The reason they had to be together was because they were afflicted by a strange illness where if they did not always have their other half in sight, they would lose their minds, leaving them unable to go too far away from each other. Their most comfortable position was when they were stuck firmly against each other, back to back, and when they took this stance, they were said to be nearly unrivaled. Were they to be distantly separated out of necessity, they would tether themselves together with a lifeline, but even so, they could only hold out for about three hours.

【Naomasa】 「And here I thought you two were invincible women…… You really have been cursed with a very troublesome predisposition. Anyway, so that's the reason why you're telling me to go get that whatever-fish.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「まーそういうこと。
　頼むよ、朔屋くぅん」
source.english:
“More or less.
Please, Sakuuuya.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まあ魚を釣ってくるくらいは構わないけどさ。釣れるかどうかは別にして。
　でも俺、船を離れていいんですかね」
source.english:
“Well, I don't mind going fishing. Whether I'll catch anything is another question.
But am I allowed off the ship?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Well, that's the gist of it. Pleeease, Sakuya-kuuun.」
【Naomasa】 「It's not that I mind something as small as catching a fish. Well, whether I can actually catch it or not is another matter. Thing is, am I actually allowed to leave this ship?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そのあたりの事は水夫長に、話通しておくから」
source.english: “We'll clear that with the bosun.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「We'll talk with the Bosun about all that, so you'll be fine.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「いや、わりいが駄目だ」
source.english: “No. Sorry, but no.”

source.japanese:
ぬういと、話に割りこんできたのがその水夫長、朔屋の首根っこを捕まえて、双子から遠ざける。
　双子はぷりぷりと怒りも露わにして───
source.english:
The boatswain himself loomed into the conversation, caught Sakuya by the scruff of the neck, and drew him away from the twins.
They bristled, openly indignant—

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Nah. Sorry, but that won't do.」

Out of nowhere, who should interrupt their conversation but the Bosun, who then proceeded to grab Sakuya by the scruff of his neck, dragging him away from the twins. The twins made no attempt to hide how they huffed with anger───

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「えー、なんでよ、どうしてよ。
　二・三時間くらいいいじゃんさあ」
source.english:
“What? Why? How come?
Two or three hours won't hurt.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Huuh, why? How come? We can have him for a couple hours, come on.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そうも言ってられん。
　こいつ、どうやらこないだ智里の野郎と厨房つきの水夫とっておきの、ラム酒を根こそぎ盗み飲みにしたらしいのが、さっき発覚してな」
source.english:
“Not that simple.
Turns out this idiot and that bastard Tomosato stole and drank every drop of the galley sailor's special rum the other day. Only just found out.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「That won't fly either. The other day, it seems like this guy and that rat bastard Tomosato stole and emptied out every last drop of the hidden stash of rum belonging to the sailor on mess duty. And he only just found out.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「厨房の水夫はもうかんかんよ。
　頭から湯気吹く勢いだ。
　奴の今日の仕事、全部この馬鹿に肩代わりさせないと、収まるものもおさまらん」
source.english:
“The galley sailor's furious.
Steam practically coming out of his head.
Nothing's going to settle him unless this fool does all his work today.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょっと。なんで俺だけ？
　智里は？」
source.english:
“Hang on. Why just me?
What about Tomosato?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「He is furious. Got steam blowing out his ears. And if I don't have this idiot take over his entire workload for today, we'll never hear the end of it.」
【Naomasa】 「Wait. Why just me? What about Tomosato?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「奴ぁどう隠れたんだか、どこ捜してもめっからねぇ。となりゃあ、全部てめえが引っ被るしかねえだろが。
　ま、あんなヤツとつるんでたことを怨むんだな」
source.english:
“He's hidden himself somehow. Can't find him anywhere. That means you take the whole lot.
Blame yourself for running around with someone like that.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Guy is hiding somewhere, but I can't find him, no matter how hard I look. Which means, you're gonna have to shoulder all the blame, got that? Well, you've only got your choice in friends to blame for this.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋って───ほんと、間抜け。
　なんで見つかるようなへまするかなあ」
source.english:
“Sakuya… You're such an idiot.
Why'd you screw up and get caught?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Come on, Sakuya───you're such an idiot. Why do you have to bungle things up so they find you out?」

source.japanese:
けなすところはそこなのかと、朔屋はつっこもうとするより先に、彼の視界は暗くなった。水夫長が、青年の顔をその巨体な手ですっぽり掴んで、ずるずると航海士の双子の部屋から引っ立てていったから。後に残された二人は、顔を見合わせて、それから遠ざかる朔屋に向かって、ぴたりと一つの動作で、中指を突きたてた。
　この、間抜け野郎と。
source.english:
That was what deserved criticism? Before Sakuya could object, his sight went dark. The boatswain's enormous hand covered his entire face, and he was dragged out of the twins' cabin. Left behind, the two exchanged a look. Then, with one perfectly synchronized movement, they raised their middle fingers at the receding Sakuya.
You idiot.

target.text: Was that really the part you should criticize me for, Sakuya thought, but before he could vocalize his rebuttal, his vision darkened. The Bosun had taken Sakuya's entire face in his massive hand, dragging him away from the twin first mates' cabin. The two who were left behind first looked at each other, and then, in the direction of the receding Sakuya, with a perfectly synchronized movement, stuck their middle fingers up in the air. "You stupid asshole!" those fingers all but shouted at him.

source.japanese:
その晩の事───
　信天翁号の朔屋の船室にて。
source.english:
That evening—
In Sakuya's cabin aboard the Albatross.

source.japanese: あの後丸一日中、厨房の雑用仕事を押しつけられた朔屋は、智里に毒を盛ることを真剣に考え始めていた。それくらい仕事はきつかった。
source.english: After an entire day of galley drudgery, Sakuya had begun seriously considering poisoning Tomosato. The work had been that hard.

source.japanese: どうにかし終えた頃には、意識は朦朧足はふらふら、どうやって自室に辿り着いたのか、それさえ覚えていない有り様で。
source.english: By the time he somehow finished, his mind was clouded and his legs unsteady. He could not even remember how he reached his cabin.

source.japanese: ところがベッドに倒れこむという、今の彼にとっては最大限の贅沢も、伝声管から鳴り響いた水夫長の蛮声によって酷くも奪い去られた。
source.english: But collapsing onto his bed, the greatest luxury presently imaginable, was cruelly denied him by the boatswain's roar from the speaking tube.

target.text: That evening─── In Sakuya's cabin on the Albatross.

After all that, Sakuya had spent the rest of his day busy with the miscellaneous tasks around the galley foisted upon him, and he was beginning to seriously consider serving Tomosato some poison. That was how gruelling the work was.
And by the time he somehow managed to finish it, consciousness hazy and legs unsteady, he did not even remember how he made it back to his own room, such was his state.
And yet, though collapsing onto his bed would be the greatest of luxuries for him in this moment, it was cruelly stolen from him by the gruff voice of the Bosun resounding through the voice pipes.

source.japanese: なんでも、直ちに水夫達の大部屋まで来いとの命令で。一体朔屋は、どれだけその命令を無視したかったことだろう。
source.english: He was ordered to report at once to the sailors' communal quarters. How desperately he wanted to ignore that order.

source.japanese:
しかし。
　これを無視すると、よくても『どうしてそんなになっても生きてるの？』という目に水夫長に遭わされるだろう。
source.english:
But—
If he ignored it, the boatswain would, at best, do things to him that left people asking, “How are you still alive?”

source.japanese: 泣く泣く朔屋、部屋を出る。
source.english: In tears, Sakuya left his room.

target.text: And of all the things, he was then ordered to head directly to the large room where the deck boys slept. Oh, how Sakuya would have loved to ignore such an order.

However. Were he to ignore this, even in the best case scenario, he'd likely suffer such a fierce reprisal from the Bosun's hands that people would ask him 『How are you still alive after being reduced to that?』
With a heavy heart, Sakuya reluctantly left his room.

source.japanese:
それで───
　
　最下層に位置する下級水夫達の大部屋は、地獄の釜の底が開いたかマラリアと猩紅熱が蔓延する復員船の船底かという惨状で、裸電球に薄暗く照らし出された有様に朔屋はほとんど反射的に回れ右、病原菌に捕まるより先に遁走しようとしたへっぴり腰は、しかし水夫長に片手で襟首つまみ上げられ爪先空しく宙を掻[か]く。
source.english:
And so—
The junior sailors' communal quarters on the lowest level looked as if the bottom had fallen out of hell's cauldron—or as if they were the hold of a repatriation ship rife with malaria and scarlet fever. At the sight, dimly lit by naked bulbs, Sakuya made an almost reflexive about-face. Before the germs could catch him, he tried to scuttle away. But the boatswain lifted him by the collar with one hand, leaving his toes scratching vainly at the air.

target.text: And then─── The large room belonging to the deck boys was found in the very bottom of the ship, and it was such a ghastly scene, it looked as though someone had opened the bottom of the cauldron of Hell, or that he had stepped into the hold of a repatriated vessel swept through by scarlet fever; upon witnessing the state of what lay illuminated beneath the dim, naked light bulbs, Sakuya spun on his heel almost reflexively, weak in the knees as he tried to make his escape before he contracted the pathogen, but the Bosun grabbed him by the collar, hoisting him up with one hand, his feet flailing through the air in vain.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「見るなり逃げんなすくたれもんが。しかしこりゃあ一体どうした有様だ。
　今夜の飯時にゃ、こいつら普通にピンピンしてたはずだが……」
source.english:
“Don't run the moment you see it, you worthless bastard.
But what the hell's happened here? These lads were all perfectly lively at supper…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃあきっと、晩飯の後になにかあったんでしょうな」
source.english: “Then something must have happened after supper.”

source.japanese:
弱くかつ煮凝りのように濁った灯りの下では、むしろ影の方が景気悪く不健康そうに深まって、いかにも空気を通して伝染そう、朔屋はとりあえず手巾でフード代わりに鼻と口を覆ったが、その布きれだってポケットの中で少なくとも数週間は蒸されたきり。どれだけ青年の汗と脂で蒸されているやら知れず、気休め程度にもなりはしない。
　下級水夫達は澱[よど]んだ空気の底、船内の下層世界にてあちらに転がりこちらで苦悶し、呻きが輪唱と、なんとも気味が悪い。
source.english:
Under that weak light, cloudy as aspic, the shadows only pooled more deeply, dismal and diseased, as though infection itself might travel through the air. Sakuya covered his nose and mouth with a handkerchief by way of a hood, but that scrap of cloth had been steaming in his pocket for at least several weeks. Who could say how thoroughly it had steeped in the young man’s sweat and grease? It was not so much as a comfort.
At the bottom of the stagnant air, down in the ship’s underworld, junior sailors lay strewn here and writhed there, their groans rising in a round—and a singularly ghastly one at that.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Don't run away as soon as you lay eyes on it, you pathetic halfwit. But what the hell is going on here? They were still full of life during dinner tonight, I'm confident of that, but……」
【Naomasa】 「In that case, something must have happened after dinner, right?」

Beneath the weak glow, as murky as congealed broth, if anything, the shadows only deepened in an unhealthy, languid way; it certainly seemed to spread through the air, so the first thing Sakuya did was cover his nose and mouth using a handkerchief as a makeshift mask, but that cloth had been steaming in his pocket for at least a few weeks. There was no way to know how much of the young man's sweat and grease it had soaked in, so it didn't even serve as a consolation. Here in this realm of stagnant air at the bottom of the ship's lower levels, the deck boys were scattered about on the floor here and there, writhing in agony, a circular canon of groans, terribly unsettling to behold.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「見たところ、戻してるのはいるようだが、垂れ流しているのはいねえな。
　どうやらチブスや赤痢じゃなさそうだが。
　素人判断じゃどうにもならんか。
　おおい船医っ!!」
source.english:
“Some are throwing up, by the looks of it, but none are shitting themselves.
Doesn't seem like typhoid or dysentery.
Still, an amateur can't decide these things.
Hey, Doctor!”

source.japanese: 荒れ狂う潮風に鍛えられた胴間声は、大部屋の半ばスープ状に澱[よど]んだ空気を激しく攪拌して、刺激に弱い幾名かはそれだけで横隔膜を揺さぶられて悶絶したけれど、肝腎の、水夫長が呼ばわった『船医』とやらからは応答返らず、蛮声は大部屋の暗がりに吸われて尻すぼみに消えた。
source.english: The booming voice, hardened by savage sea winds, violently stirred the half-soupy air of the quarters. For several sensitive sufferers, that alone shook their diaphragms and left them writhing. But the ‘doctor’ he had called—the person who mattered—gave no answer. The roar was swallowed by the dark and dwindled away.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いない……みたいですねえ」
source.english: “Doesn't seem to be here…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「From what I can tell, some of them seem to be vomiting, but they aren't soiling themselves. Doesn't seem to be typhoid or dysentery at least. Not like an amateur's judgment will get us far, will it? OOOI, DOCTOR!!」

Trained in the raging ocean gales, his thick, booming voice furiously whipped around the almost soup-like stagnant air of the large room; several of those sensitive to such stimuli had their diaphragms shaken by that alone and fainted in agony, but the crucial person, the one whom the Bosun had called "doctor" or something, did not give a response, and the rough voice was absorbed by the darkness of the large room, tapering off into nothingness.
【Naomasa】 「Not here……or so it seems, right?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まいったな」
source.english: “Damn it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ところでこの船、船医なんていたの。
　俺ゃてっきりその辺りは有耶無耶に流してるのかと」
source.english:
“By the way, this ship has a doctor?
I thought that was one of the things you glossed over.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well I'm stumped.」
【Naomasa】 「On that note, this ship actually has a doctor then? I thought for sure that you were all just kind of hand-waving that issue away.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「いやまあ、船医っつったってこいつら水夫達の一人なんだが。
　どこで覚えたんだがこれが医者の真似事をする。
　まあ牡蠣に食中りしたり、スパイクで足に穴開けたりしちまった時には重宝してるんだ」
source.english:
“Well, when I say doctor, he's one of these sailors.
Don't know where he learned it, but he plays at medicine.
Comes in handy when somebody gets sick on oysters or puts a spike through his foot.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「No, y'see, the guy I call doctor is just one of these sailors here. Don't know where he learned it, but he sure knows how to act like one. Well, when somebody gets food poisoning from oysters, or has a spike driven through their foot, he comes in real handy.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「眼鏡かけさせてるから、すぐに見分けもつくのによ、どこぉ失せやがった……ん？」
source.english: “Make him wear glasses so we can tell him apart straightaway, too. Where's he disappeared to… Hm?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「We make him wear glasses, so we should be able to tell him apart from the others right away. Now where the hell did he disappear……nh?」

source.japanese: 苦り切ってドスンと腰降ろした、積み上げて高くした寝網に妙な座り心地を覚えて水夫長は首を傾げたけれど、そんな細かい事に拘泥するような尻の厚さではない。その際押し殺したような吐息とも呻[うめ]きともつかぬ音がどこからか漏れたが、それだって周囲の苦悶の声にすぐに紛れて水夫長の耳朶には響かない、と、この荒くれ者の腕をちょんちょん突く朔屋の、恐れ知らずにもほどがある。
source.english: The boatswain dropped heavily onto some piled-up hammocks. Finding the seat oddly uncomfortable, he tilted his head. But his backside was too thick to concern itself with such small matters. A stifled sound, somewhere between a sigh and a groan, escaped from somewhere. It immediately merged with the surrounding suffering and never reached his ears. Sakuya tapped the brute's arm. There was such a thing as too much nerve.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「水夫長、ちょっとあんた」
source.english: “Bosun. Hey, you.”

target.text: The Bosun sat down with a thump and a sour scowl, then tilted his head in puzzlement at the strange discomfort he felt from sitting down on the tall heap of hammocks, but his backside was far too thick to let such a trivial detail bother him. And when an exhale sounding like somebody was being crushed to death, as well as a noise that could not even be described as a groan, spilled out from somewhere, that also easily blended in with the chorus of the suffering in the vicinity and so did not even reach the Bosun's earlobes, but, for Sakuya to poke this violent ruffian's arm repeatedly, surely there had to be limits to how fearless a man could be.
【Naomasa】 「Hey, Bosun, can you, uhh.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「うるせえな。こっちゃ明日の仕事と、動けるこいつらの人数の勘定で、余計な事聞きたかねえんだ」
source.english: “Shut up. I'm counting tomorrow's jobs against how many of these lads can move. Don't want to hear anything else.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもあんた、あんたが尻の下に敷いてんのがそれなんじゃ？」
source.english: “But isn't that him you're sitting on?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Shut it. Between figuring out tomorrow's work and counting how many of these lads are actually fit to move, I don't wanna hear any more of your useless questions.」
【Naomasa】 「But, you're-, isn't he the one you're flattening under your ass right now?」

source.japanese: ん？　と水夫長が見下ろした、目が、腰かけた彼の巨大なる尻の下にと向かった。下敷きになっていた。一人の水夫の、その顔には水夫長の尻に圧されへしゃげた眼鏡。
source.english: Hm? The boatswain looked down, beneath his enormous backside. A sailor was pinned there, his glasses flattened against his face by that same backside.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こりゃあまさに『船医喪失』……、
　って状況ですな。
　結構やばい状況」
source.english:
“Well, we're… flat out of doctors.
That's a pretty
bad situation.”

target.text: With a "hn?", the Bosun looked down, eyes directed below his enormous behind. He was being crushed. A single sailor, glasses squashed against his face, flattened by the Bosun's buttocks.

【Naomasa】 【And now we've actually lost the ship's doctor……that's what we're operating with. That's a pretty bad situation.」 (TN: This is originally a pun on "船医喪失" and "戦意喪失", both read identically as Sen-I-Sou-Shitsu, the former meaning "losing the ship's doctor" and the latter meaning "losing the will to fight".)

source.japanese:
【直正】
「っで！」
source.english: “Ow!”

source.japanese: ……朔屋を迎えたのは水夫長のハンマーの一撃の如き拳であったが、あながち無法とも言い切れまい。軽口は全くもって余計であった。
source.english: …What greeted Sakuya was a hammer blow of the boatswain's fist. It could not entirely be called unjustified. The joke had been quite unnecessary.

source.japanese: ともあれ、朔屋は消えそうになる意識に鞭打って、夜を徹しての水夫達の看病を余儀なくされた。明け方くらいにはようやく水夫達の容態も快方に向かったのだけれど、その頃には朔屋の両手はなにやら血塗れ、これは水夫達が吐血したなどではなく、朔屋が眠気に船漕ぐたびに水夫長にシッぺを打たれ、皮膚が裂けてしまったからだ。
source.english: In any event, fighting his fading consciousness, Sakuya was obliged to nurse the sailors all night. Toward dawn their condition finally began to improve. By then both his hands were bloody. Not because the sailors had vomited blood, but because the boatswain slapped them with two fingers whenever Sakuya nodded off, until the skin split.

source.japanese:
この惨事は言うまでもなくクロが引き起こしたものなのだが、クロがそんな風になってしまったのも、もとはといえば朔屋が悪い。
　あんなところにシサム・キサラが貯蔵していた靴下の山なぞ見つけてしまった、朔屋が一番悪い。
source.english:
Needless to say, Kuro had caused this disaster. But the original cause of Kuro's condition was Sakuya.
Sakuya was most to blame. He had gone and found the mountain of socks Sisam and Kisara had stored in that place.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Tuhh!」
……What greeted Sakuya's head was the Bosun's fist swung down like a hammer, but that couldn't be called entirely unjust. His flippant remark most certainly was completely uncalled for.

Anyhow, Sakuya's flagging consciousness was beaten back into him, and he was then forced to spend the whole night nursing the deck boys. When dawn arrived, the deck boys' condition was finally taking a turn for the better, but by then, both of Sakuya's hands were covered in blood; not blood coughed up by the deck boys, rather, every time Sakuya was about to nod off, his wrist would be struck by the Bosun's index and middle finger, and his skin eventually split open.

It goes without saying that this tragic incident was brought about by Kuro, but that Kuro ended up in such a state was all Sakuya's fault to begin with. As he was the one who had discovered the mountain of socks that Shisamu and Kisara had been storing in that place, Sakuya was the most to blame of any.

source.japanese:
明け方朔屋が、一歩歩いては失神、を繰り返しつつ自分の部屋へと戻ると、そこで世にも珍しいものを目にしたのだった。
　───朔屋の部屋の前を行ったり来たりしながら、ぐすぐすと涙顔になっている航海士だ。
　これはなんの天変地異の前ぶれだ。
　眠気さえいっぺんに消し飛んで、朔屋は恐る恐る訊ねてみる。
source.english:
At dawn, Sakuya returned to his cabin, repeatedly taking a step and passing out. There he encountered something exceedingly rare.
A navigator pacing before his door, sniffling, her face wet with tears.
What natural catastrophe did this portend?
Even his sleepiness vanished at once. He ventured a timid question.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ええと……あれ、あんたはどっちだ？」
source.english: “Um… Wait, which one are you?”

target.text: Dawn arrived, Sakuya fainted with every step he took, and repeating this process as he walked back to his room, there, he caught sight of something extremely unusual. ───There was the first mate, sniffling with a tear-stained face while pacing back and forth in front of Sakuya's cabin. This must have been a portent for some sort of cataclysmic event. Even his drowsiness was wholly blown away, and Sakuya timidly tried to inquire as to what was going on.
【Naomasa】 「Uuuhm……wait, which one are you?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたし、キサラだよゥ……」
source.english: “I'm Kisara…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃあキサラ、あんた一体どうしたの。
　そんな半泣きで。財布でも落としたか、生理が止まったか？」
source.english:
“Then, Kisara, what's happened?
Why the tears? Lost your purse? Missed a period?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そんなんじゃない、
　そんなのたいした事ない。
　シサムが、シサムがぁ……」
source.english:
“Not that.
That wouldn't matter.
Sisam, Sisam…”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「シサムがいなくなっちゃった。
　もう何時間もたってる。
　船の中どこ捜してもいないんだ。
　あいつ、きっと───」
source.english:
“Sisam's gone. It's been hours.
I've looked everywhere aboard,
and she isn't here.
She must have—”

source.japanese: この段階となると、ぼんくらと馬鹿にされている朔屋でさえ、事の予想は付いていた。この航海士の双子、昨日からやけになんとかいう魚を採りに行く事に執着を見せていなかったか？
source.english: At this point even Sakuya, mocked as a dullard, could guess what had happened. Hadn't these navigator twins been strangely obsessed since yesterday with catching some fish or other?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もしかして、一人で魚釣りに!?」
source.english: “Gone fishing alone!?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それしか考えらんない。
　シサム、ずっと前からアクちゃん食べたい食べたいって。だから、あたしが寝た後、こっそり起き出して……」
source.english:
“What else could it be? She's been going on about wanting little Aku for ages.
So after I fell asleep, she must have sneaked out…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもたかが魚釣りだよな？
　なにもそんな心配することは」
source.english:
“But it's only fishing, right?
Nothing to get so worried about.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I'm Kisaraaa……」
【Naomasa】 「Alright then, Kisara, what in the world happened to you to make you stand here, about to cry? Did you drop your wallet, did your period stop coming?」
【Kisara】 「Nothing like that. None of that matters. Shisamu, it's Shisamu, she's……」
【Kisara】 「Shisamu is gone. It's already been several hours. I've searched everywhere on the ship, but she's nowhere to be found. I'm certain, she must have───」

At this stage, even Sakuya, frequently mocked for his stupidity, could make a conjecture as to what had happened. These twin first mates, had they not shown an inordinate fixation with heading off to fish up some whatever-it-was-called fish yesterday?
【Naomasa】 「Could it be she went fishing by herself!?」
【Kisara】 「That's all I can think of. Shisamu's been talking about how much she really, really wants to eat Aku-chan for a long time now. So, after I went to sleep, she sneaked out of bed……」
【Naomasa】 「But she's just gone fishing, right? That shouldn't be anything to get so worked up about.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でも、だって。
　戻ってこないんだもの。
　離れて何時間もたつんだもの」
source.english:
“But, but… She
hasn't come back.
We've been apart for hours.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「But, it's because. She hasn't come back. And we've been separated for several hours now.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ちなみにあたし、実はこうして喋っているだけでもかなり限界」
source.english: “Actually, I'm pretty much at my limit just standing here talking.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ちょっとでも気を抜くと───」
source.english: “If I let my guard down even a little—”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「───あひん」
source.english: “—Ahin.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「By the way, to tell the truth, just talking to you like this is pretty much my limit.」
【Kisara】 「If I lose focus for even just a second───」
【Kisara】 「───Ahin」

source.japanese:
白目を剥いた。
　ややあって戻った時には、ぐるぐる眼。
　それはもう既に、朔屋が知る放胆で磊落な双子ではなかった。
　ごきりといわく言い難い不気味な音が響いて、キサラの首が三六〇度回転した。
　そうなったキサラの眸[ひとみ]は、朔屋が失禁しそうなほど常軌を逸しており、ぐるぐると渦巻きながら左右がてんで互いに出鱈目な眼球運動を繰り返している。その不気味さと言ったら、蝸牛の寄生虫、触覚に寄生し、中枢系を支配して宿主の行動を操るというあの恐ろしい寄生虫の蠕動に匹敵する。
source.english:
Her eyes rolled white.
After a moment, they returned, spinning.
This was no longer the bold, openhearted twin Sakuya knew.
An indescribably uncanny crack sounded. Kisara's neck turned through three hundred and sixty degrees.
Her eyes were so wildly abnormal that he nearly wet himself. They swirled, each eyeball repeatedly moving at random, independently of the other. Their eeriness rivaled the writhing of that dreadful snail parasite which infests the feelers, takes over the central nervous system, and controls its host's behavior.

target.text: Her eyes rolled back in her head. When they returned after a bit of time, her eyes now swam. This was no longer one of the dauntless, uninhibited twins who Sakuya knew. There was an indescribably uncanny, grinding crunch, and then Kisara's neck rotated three hundred and sixty degrees.

After that, the look in Kisara's eyes was so abnormal that Sakuya almost pissed himself, and while swirling around, her left and right eyeballs both repeated a series of altogether haphazard movements. This eeriness rivalled the vermiculating movements of that one horrifying parasitic flatworm that would parasitize a snail's tentacles, then take domination of its central nervous system and control its host.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「死にたい───」
source.english: “I want to die—”
“—Huh?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたし、部屋出てくる時に鍵掛けたっけか。
　ちゃんとコルトの安全装置掛けてきたっけか」
source.english:
“Did I lock the cabin when I left?
Did I put the safety on the Colt?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「もし誰かあたし達の部屋に入ってきて、
　コルトめっけて暴発させたらどうしよう。
　当たり所が悪くて死んじゃったらどうしよう」
source.english:
“What if someone goes into our cabin,
finds the Colt, and it goes off?
What if it hits somewhere bad and they die?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I want to die───」
【Naomasa】 「───Huh?」
【Kisara】 「Did I lock the door when I left my room? Did I remember to engage the safety on my Colt?」
【Kisara】 「What am I going to do if somebody went inside our cabin, then found the Colt and accidentally discharged it? What should I do if it hits something vital and they die?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そんな事になっちゃうくらいなら、いっそあたし今死んじゃえばいい───」
source.english: “Rather than let that happen, I should just die now—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや姐さん、そいつはちょっと心配しすぎ」
source.english: “Look, you're worrying a little too much.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If something like that could happen, then I might as well just die right here and now───」
