【Naomasa】 「No, lady, you're worrying a little too much there.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こないだちょっと小腹が減ったから、水夫の男の子達が隠してたビスケット、シサムと盗み食いしちゃったけれど、もしもそれで───」
source.english: “The other day I was peckish, so Sisam and I stole some biscuits the sailor boys had hidden. But what if—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あー、あんたも盗み食い、やっぱやるんだ。
　あいつら、細々とモノ隠すの好きだよな」
source.english:
“Oh, so you steal food, too.
They do like hiding little things away, don't they?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「もしもあの子達の中に、きっとお前が盗んだんだろういや盗んでない、の疑心暗鬼が広がっちゃったらどうしよう」
source.english: “What if they start suspecting each other? ‘You must have stolen them!’ ‘No, I didn't!’”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「When I got a little peckish the other day, together with Shisamu, I filched some biscuits that the boy sailors had hidden away, but, what if that───」
【Naomasa】 「Aaah, so you steal food too? I knew you two also did that. Those guys sure love squirreling away a bunch of things, don't they?」
【Kisara】 「What if those boys started jumping at shadows and doubting each other, like, "I'm sure you stole it", "no, I didn't!" and so on, what should I do?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それがもとで、いつもは優しいあの子達が、血みどろの殺し合いを始めちゃったらどうしよう。
　そんな事になったなら、あたし、死ぬしかない」
source.english:
“What if those nice boys start killing one another in a bloodbath because of it?
If that happens, I'll have to die.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なんでそうなんのよ」
source.english: “…How do you get to that?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And if that was the cause for those boys, always so kind, to start killing each other, covered in blood and gore, then what should I do? If it came to that, I have to die.」
【Naomasa】 「……How'd you reach that conclusion?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それだけじゃない。もしもこの船の汽罐がいきなり大爆発したならもう大変。あっという間もなく沈んじゃう。溺れ死には苦しいって言うよ」
source.english: “That's not all. What if the ship's boiler suddenly explodes? It'll be terrible. We'll sink before we know it. They say drowning hurts.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And that's not all. What if the ship's steam engine suddenly exploded, then it would be a complete disaster. We'd sink in the blink of an eye. They say that drowning is really painful, you know.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そんな事になる前に、いっそ死んでしまったほうがいい───」
source.english: “Better to die before that happens—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「えー……。そうなる前に機関長がなんか言ってくると思うけどなぁ……」
source.english: “Uh… I think the chief engineer would say something first…”

source.japanese:
【伝声管からの機関長の声】
『……なにか用ですか？　呼びましたか？』
source.english: “…Do you need something? Did you call me?”
source.speakerEn: Chief Engineer's Voice from the Speaking Tube

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いえなんも」
source.english: “No, nothing.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「So before that can happen, it'd be better if I just died───」
【Naomasa】 「Uhh……. No, I think the Chief Engineer would say something before that happens, so……」
【Voice of the Chief Engineer coming from a voice tube】 「……Do you have some business? Did someone call for me?」
【Naomasa】 「Nah, it's nothing.」

source.japanese: その後もキサラは、眼につくもの手当たり次第に杞憂の材料となるらしく、もう大変。
source.english: After that, everything Kisara's eye fell upon became fodder for some new and groundless fear. It was a nightmare.

source.japanese: 今度は、両腕をがっと真横に翳[かざ]し、棒のように硬直して、奇声を発しながら前にのめる、危険なくらいにのめる、このままいったら床に倒れる、その寸前で、びよんと後ろに仰け反った。びよんびよんと、このまま続けていたらアキレス腱がやられること間違いなしの、恐ろしい挙動だった。
source.english: Now she thrust both arms straight out to her sides, stiffened like a stick, and leaned forward with a peculiar cry. Dangerously far forward. Just before she would have fallen to the floor, she sprang backward. Boing, boing. A terrifying performance guaranteed to ruin her Achilles tendons if she kept it up.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「判った。怖い。見てるだけ聞いてるだけでこっちも漠然とした不安に襲われてくる。
　シサラ、シサラッ」
source.english:
“All right. This is scary. Just watching and listening is making me vaguely anxious, too.
Sisara! Sisara!”

source.japanese: 動揺のあまり二人の名前がごっちゃになったが構わず、朔屋はキサラの胸を鷲掴みにした。
source.english: In his agitation, he had mixed their names together. Never mind. Sakuya seized Kisara's breasts.

target.text: After that, Kisara continued to use whatever random thing that caught her eye as material for her groundless fears. What an ordeal.

This time, she had lifted both her arms into a perfectly horizontal line, stiff like a pole, leaning forwards while making strange noises, leaning dangerously forwards at that; if she kept going, she'd fall down to the floor, and just on the verge of tipping over, she bent backwards with a boing. It was a terrifying movement, bouncing back and forth, and if it continued like that, it would undoubtedly injure her Achilles tendons soon.
【Naomasa】 「I get it. It's scary. Just watching and listening to you makes me feel a vague unease too. Shisara, Shisara!」
Not paying any mind to the fact he'd mixed their names together in his agitation, Sakuya grabbed hold of Kisara's chest.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ふあああ!?」
source.english: “Fwaaa!?”

source.japanese:
ひたすらにキサラの乳房を揉みしだく朔屋。
　そればかりか、抱きついて乳房の中に顔を埋め匂いを存分に楽しみ、頬摺りまでかます始末。
　朔屋がやりたい放題するうちに、キサラの眸[ひとみ]にだんだん、だんだん焦点が戻ってきて。
source.english:
He kneaded her breasts relentlessly. Nor did he stop there. He clung to her, buried his face between them, thoroughly enjoyed the smell, and even rubbed his cheek against her.
As he indulged himself, focus gradually, gradually returned to her eyes.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「FWHAA!?」

Sakuya devoted his entire mind to giving Kisara's breasts a thorough massaging. And if that wasn't enough, he also embraced her and buried his face within her bosom, enjoying her smell to his heart's content, and at the end, he even sneaked in some cheek rubbing. While Sakuya was doing whatever he wanted, gradually, little by little, Kisara's eyes regained their focus.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ぁ……ァ……。
　う……朔屋、もう、いい。
　多分、少しだけ、平気……」
source.english:
“Ah… Ah…
Sakuya, that's enough.
I think I'm a little better…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「キサラ、キサラ、戻ってこい、
　いつまでも向こうに飛んでたら、

source.english: Tomosato himself was nowhere to be seen, but a boat had been set out on deck. In keeping with the Albatross, it was coming apart in several places; all the pair could do was pray it would not flood and sink beneath them.

source.japanese: 海面に下ろす前、キサラは忘れ物とて部屋に引き返して取ってきた何やら、紙の小袋と見えたが中味は不明だ。それで二人が乗りこもうという段になって、小舟の船底からのっそり顔を出してきた黒いのに、朔屋、尻込みの、先だって勘気を蒙ったばかりの宗右衛門猫だ。

Then, just as they were about to climb aboard, something black slowly raised its head from the bottom of the boat. Sakuya shrank back. The cat Soemon, whose wrath he had only recently incurred.

target.text: Though it was difficult for Rui to comprehend, a single small boat was exactly what Kisara and Sakuya needed in this moment. Any grudges about fondling chests or chests being fondled had to be shelved for now, for the search for her twin half, Shisamu, was far more important, and with the proverbial ship about to set sail, Sakuya resolved himself to accompany Kisara there. While they were women he had no shortage of grievances about, being unable to turn down a woman's requests was also part of Sakuya's nature.

While they didn't catch sight of Tomosato himself, they found the boat on the deck; in a display fitting for the Albatross, it was both rickety and decrepit all over, but all the two could do was pray that it would somehow manage to not flood and sink.

Before they lowered it to the surface of the sea, Kisara went back to her room to grab something she had forgotten or some such, returning with something that looked like a pouch, but its contents were unclear to him. With that done, now that the two were about to board the dinghy, something black slowly poked its head out from the bottom of it, and so Sakuya recoiled, for it was Souemon the cat. The very same cat who Sakuya had just recently incurred the disfavour of.

source.japanese: 二人が漕ぎ出そうというのにこの黒猫は降りようともせず、どころか船頭のように舳先に陣取った。黒猫との同船は朔屋には避けたいところであったけれど、キサラはかえって喜んで、全幅の信頼を置いて、かくて二人と一匹は波間に揺られる事となる───
source.english: They were about to row away, yet the black cat would not disembark. Instead, he stationed himself in the bow like a boatman. Sakuya would rather have avoided sharing a boat with him. Kisara, however, was delighted and placed complete trust in him. Thus two people and one cat set out rocking over the waves—

target.text: Even when the two were about to row out to sea, the black cat showed no sign of trying to disembark; on the contrary, he took position at the bow like a boatman. While Sakuya certainly would have preferred to avoid sharing a vessel with this black cat, on the other hand, Kisara seemed pleased, wholeheartedly placing her faith in him; thus, two people and one cat found themselves tossed about on the rolling waves───

source.japanese: 幸い海の面は引き続き寒天を凝らせたかのべた凪であり、脅かすような高波も暴風もなく、信天翁号を離れるにつれ、船が浮かんでいるだけでも種々にかき鳴らす喧しい雑音も遠ざかり、手漕ぎの短艇が進むは粛々と、伴奏は櫂が波を切る響きと軸受けに軋む音くらい、と思いきや。
source.english: Fortunately, the sea remained flat as set jelly. No threatening waves, no gales. As they drew away from the Albatross, even the assortment of noises she made merely by floating grew distant. Their rowboat advanced quietly. Its only accompaniment was the oars cutting the water and creaking in their rowlocks. Or so one might think—

source.japanese: もうキサラが母猫にはぐれた仔猫でもここまでではあるまいの、惨めに哀しくそして鬱陶しく、一時たりとも黙っていなかったのだった。
source.english: Kisara, meanwhile, did not fall silent for so much as a moment. Miserable, mournful, and maddening: no kitten separated from its mother could have made such a spectacle of itself.

target.text: Fortunately, the continually cold weather had almost congealed the surface of the water into a lull: there were no tall waves or raging gales to threaten them, and the further they rowed from the Albatross, so did the various thrumming, loud noises sounding just from the ship floating also grow distant, and with the rowboat advancing in quietude, their only accompaniment was the sound of oars cutting through waves and the creaking of the rowlocks. Or so one would think.
Even a kitten separated from its mother wouldn't be this wretched, miserable, and gloomy: Kisara was unable to stay silent for even a single moment.

source.japanese:

source.english: The boat was certainly as battered as its mother ship. Gaps had opened here and there between the planks, but they had at least been caulked with bark fiber and made more or less seaworthy. It was unlikely to start flooding quite so easily.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Hey, Sakuya, are we really okay here? A hole won't just, like, open up in the bottom of the boat, right?」

Certainly, just like its mother ship, this boat was showing its age here and there, and there were loose gaps between some of the planking, but the boat was caulked and the like, so there was some semblance of decency to be found, at least superficially, and so it wouldn't flood that easily.

source.japanese:

source.english: “Sakuya, hey, these oars look pretty old, too. They won't suddenly break, will they? If they break, we won't be able to get anywhere.”

source.english: True, salt wind had roughened the oars and stained them the dark brown of soy-simmered preserves. But ash was sturdy wood, and from the feel of them beneath his hands they would last this round trip, at least.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ね、朔屋、ねえ。ちょっとコンパス見せて。もし方位がずれてたら、どこに流されるか判らないから。漂流して飢え死になんて厭、厭、厭。そうなる前に死んじゃいたい」
source.english: “Sakuya. Sakuya, let me see the compass. If the bearing's wrong, who knows where we'll drift? I don't want to drift away and starve. No, no, no. I'd rather die before that.”

source.japanese: 全くもって洋上で方位を見失うのは致命的であり、本来船員学校所属の学生とはいえ、座学も実技もまるで駄目夫だった朔屋には方位の確保は生命線と言える。かといって三分間隔で一々方位を改めていては、櫂を漕ぐ手の障りとしか言いようがない。
source.english: Losing one's bearings at sea was fatal, certainly. Sakuya might technically have been a student at a sailors' school, but he was hopeless at theory and practice alike. Keeping his bearings was his lifeline. Checking them again every three minutes, however, merely interfered with rowing.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Hey, hey, Sakuya, this oar also looks kind of old too, but it's not like it's gonna suddenly snap in two, right? If it did, then we'd no longer be able to make any real headway.」

Yes, indeed, the oars had been worn down by the briny air, and they were tinged with the colour of boiled-down tsukudani, but the ash wood was sturdy, and judging from how it felt to row with them right now, they should, at the very least, last for the return trip. (TN: Tsukudani, written "佃煮" is fish, shellfish, sea weed and the like boiled down in a mixture of soy, mirin, and sugar. It is generally a dark brown.)

【Kisara】 「Hey, Sakuya, heeey. Show me the compass for a bit. Should our heading be off, who knows where we'll be swept away to. I don't want to be set adrift and starve to death, no, no, no. I'd sooner die before that happens.」

As a matter of fact, it would absolutely be lethal to lose one's bearings on the sea, and even Sakuya, who, although he had once been a student at a proper nautical school, was practically useless at both classroom learning and practical skills, would still claim that maintaining one's bearings was a matter of life or death. With that said, having to check their heading every three minutes could only be described as an impediment to his rowing hands.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ね、朔屋、朔屋ってば。もしあんたがいきなり発情してあたしを強姦しにかかったら、ああどうしようどうしよう」
source.english: “Sakuya. Sakuya, listen. What if you suddenly get horny and try to rape me? Oh, what would I do? What would I do?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Hey, Sakuya, listen to me, Sakuya. What if you suddenly get sexually aroused and then try to rape me? Aah, what should I do, what should I do?」
【Naomasa】 「Oi.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「今のあたしじゃきっと抵抗できないから、前から後から横から股関節外れるくらい犯されちゃうんだ、きっと」
source.english: “I couldn't possibly fight you off like this. You'd take me from the front, from behind, sideways—keep at it till my hips came out of their sockets. I know you would.”

source.japanese:

source.english: “Hold on, damn it.”
