「あたしが泣いても漏らしても、死んだ魚みたいな目になっても、朔屋は離してくれなくて───やあああああっ、妊娠させられちゃう、孕まされちゃう、生まされちゃうううううっっ、異常出産で死んじゃうっ」
source.english: “Even if I cried or wet myself or my eyes went like a dead fish's, you wouldn't let go—Nooooo! You'll get me pregnant, put a baby in me, make me give birth! I'll die in some abnormal delivery!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あーうん、大丈夫だから。
　言われてそういうアクシデントもありかと、一瞬考えないでもなかったが、今はなんもしないから。
　するとしてもちゃんとサックつけるから」
source.english:
“…Right. Fine. Don't worry.
Now that you mention it, I won't say the possibility didn't cross my mind for a second, but I'm not doing anything now.
And if I did, I'd use a rubber.”

source.japanese:
───短艇漕ぎ出してから絶え間なくこの調子で、普段の航海士の双子の大胆不敵を知る者にはその落差たるや我が目の正気を疑いたくなるだろうが、情けなくもこれが現実である。
　このままでは同舟しているだけで、空気感染で女を妊娠させる怪人扱いされかねない勢いにほとほと物哀しくなって、朔屋は頭を抱えつもどうにかキサラを宥めにかかる。蒼い気圏とより濃い海の、天水の狭間にあって朔屋の苦悩の形は、ロダンの彫刻のように珍しく様になっていて、ある種の女心そそらん姿であったりするのが、本人がその気はない時だけに皮肉めく。
source.english:
She had been like this without pause since they set out. Anyone who knew the navigator twins' usual fearlessness would have wondered whether his eyes had gone mad at the contrast. Pitiful though it was, this was reality.
At this rate, merely sharing a boat with her threatened to make Sakuya out as some monster who could impregnate women by airborne contagion. The thought filled him with a profound melancholy. He clutched his head and tried somehow to soothe her. Between the blue vault of air and the darker sea, suspended between heaven and water, his troubled pose looked uncommonly fine—like a sculpture by Rodin. It might even have stirred certain women's hearts. Ironic that this should happen only when the man himself had no such intention.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I'm sure I couldn't resist the way I am right now. I'd be violated from the front and the back and the side so hard my hip joints would dislocate, no doubt about it.」
【Naomasa】 「Hold it right there!」

【Kisara】 「Even if I cry or soil myself, even if my eyes are as dead a fish's, Sakuya wouldn't let go of me─── NOOOOOOO, I'm gonna be pregnant, I'm gonna be impregnated, I'm gonna give biiiiirth, I'll die from abnormal labour!」

【Naomasa】 「……Uhh, yeah, no, you'll be fine. Now that you mention it, an accident like that could take place, and it's not like I didn't consider it for a brief second, but I won't do anything right now, okay? And if I did, I'd be sure to use a condom.」

───She had been like this, without pause, ever since they rowed out to sea, and any who knew how dauntless the twin mates normally were would surely doubt their own eyes at the difference, but pathetic as it was, this was still reality. At this rate, he'd end up being treated like some kind of monster who impregnates women through airborne infection just by staying on the same boat as them, which left him deeply disheartened, and though he was holding his head in his hands all the while, Sakuya somehow managed to calm Kisara.

Caught between the blue of the atmosphere and the yet deeper blue of the ocean, between welkin and mere, the form of Sakuya's anguish cut a figure as striking as a Rodin sculpture through its novelty, possessing a particular kind of allure that couldn't help but stir a woman's heart; there was a certain irony to the fact that the man only looked like this when he himself had no intention of doing so.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あああごめんなさいごめんなさい、朔屋を困らせちゃったあたし。きっとこれが原因で朔屋は厭世家になって、しまいに神経衰弱になって、カルモチンたらふく食らって自殺しちゃうよう……っっ」
source.english: “Oh, I'm sorry, I'm sorry! I've upset you! Now you'll turn against the world, then have a nervous breakdown, then swallow a heap of Calmotin and kill yourself…!”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ごめんなさい、そんなコトになったら、ごめんなさいだから、あたしもすぐに後を追うから。
　死ぬから。死にますから、ごめんなさい」
source.english:
“I'm sorry! If that happens, I'm sorry, I'll follow you right away.
I'll die. I'll die, I'm sorry.”

source.japanese: ひたすらごめんなさいを擦り切れ加減のレコードのように繰り返し、キサラは狭い短艇の中で三界に寄る辺を失った孤児のようにひっきりなしに立ったり座ったりするものだから、その都度小舟が傾いで揺れて危かしい。流石に転覆とまでは至らずとも、こう心の均衡欠いていてはいつ彼女の方が短艇から転げ落ちるか知れたものではなく、朔屋は困り果てて、そこでキサラが乗りこむ際に自室から何やら持ちだしてきたのを思い出した。紙の小袋で、これがあればちょっとは心が鎮まる物だとか言っていたような覚えがある。鎮静剤の類だろうか。
source.english: Repeating her apologies like a worn record, Kisara kept standing and sitting in the narrow boat, like an orphan without a refuge anywhere in the three worlds. Each time, the little craft tilted and rocked dangerously. It did not quite capsize, but with her mind so unbalanced, who knew when she herself might tumble overboard? Sakuya was at his wits' end. Then he remembered what she had brought from her cabin. A small paper bag. Hadn't she said that having it would settle her mind a little? Some sort of sedative?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あの、キサラ、あんた何か持ってきてただろう？
　鎮静薬かなんかか？　とにかく、それ使ってみちゃどうか？」
source.english:
“Um, Kisara, you brought something, didn't you?
A sedative or something? Whatever it is, why not try it?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あ……そういえば。そ、そうだね。
　ちょっとは落ち着かないとね」
source.english:
“Oh… Right. Y-yes.
I ought to calm down a little.”

source.japanese:
震える手、指先では袋の折り口開ける事さえ覚束ないのか、紙擦れうるさく四苦八苦してからやっと取り出したのは硝子の小瓶、瞥見したところなにやらの茶褐色の粉末がたっぷり詰まっているらしい。その蓋にこれまた苦労するのが見ている朔屋がいらつくほどの不器用さ、蓋を捻ってまた袋に戻し、それを口元に宛がってキサラは、深々と吸いこんでは吐いてを三度四度、紙袋がべこべこ膨らんで凹む。
　……トルエン吸引に耽溺する中毒者の病的な様と異ならず、朔屋は嘆かわしげに眉をひそめたが、薬効は速やかで、キサラの瞳にかぎろう、ぐるぐると渦巻く惑乱はやがて鎮まっていった、とはいえまだまだ不安と懸念に頼りなかったが。
source.english:
Even unfolding the bag defeated her trembling fingers. After a great deal of fumbling and a loud rustle of paper, she finally produced a small glass vial that seemed to be packed with reddish-brown powder. She made such a business of the cap that merely watching set Sakuya's teeth on edge. At last she twisted it off, returned the vial to the bag, pressed the mouth of the bag to her lips, and drew three or four deep breaths; the paper swelled and collapsed with each one.
…She looked for all the world like an addict huffing toluene. Sakuya knit his brows in dismay. Yet the medicine acted swiftly: the feverish glimmer and spiraling confusion in Kisara's eyes gradually subsided, though they remained anything but free of fear and misgiving.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Aaaaah, I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm really bothering you here, Sakuya. This will definitely be the reason that Sakuya becomes a pessimist, and in the end, he'll have a nervous breakdown and gobble down a huge helping of Calmotin and kill himself……」 (TN: This refers to Dazai Osamu, a very famous Japanese author who frequently took overdoses of Calmotin, a hypnotic and sedative also known as bromisoval, in his many suicide attempts. He finally succeeded in drowning himself in 1948 together with his lover.)
【Kisara】 「I'm sorry, if that happens, then I'm really sorry, so I'll be following you right away. I'll die. I'm going to die, so I'm sorry.」

Repeatedly apologizing with all her heart like a broken record, Kisara incessantly stood up only to sit down once more in the cramped boat, like an orphan who had lost any place of belonging in the three realms of existence, and the small boat lurched and rocked dangerously each and every time.

Even though it never went as far as the boat capsizing, with her mind this unbalanced, she could well fall off it; at his wits' end, Sakuya remembered that Kisara had brought something from her room as they were about to board the boat. That small paper bag, he recalled her saying that it was something that could calm her mind, even just a little, as long as she had it with her. It was probably some sort of sedative?
【Naomasa】 「Uhm, Kisara, you brought something with you, right? Some sort of medicine to calm you down? Either way, how about you try using that?」
【Kisara】 「Ah……now that you mention it. Ri-, right. I need to calm down a little, don't I?」

Her hands shook, leaving him uncertain if she could even unfold the opening of the bag with the tips of her fingers, but after some loud rustling of paper and a lot of trouble, she finally pulled out a little glass bottle, and from a glance, it looked to be filled to the brim with some sort of dark, reddish-brown powder. She struggled once more, this time with the lid of the bottle, clumsy enough to frustrate Sakuya watching from the sidelines, but she soon twisted off the lid and put the bottle back in the bag. Kisara then lifted the bag to her mouth, inhaled and exhaled deeply three or four times, the paper bag inflating and collapsing in response.

……It was no different from the pathological behaviour of addicts indulging in toluene inhalation, and Sakuya knitted his brows in lamentation, but the medicinal effect was quick to show results, for the spinning, swirling confusion in her eyes abated at last, though with that said, she remained anxious, worried, and forlorn.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「すっはぁーー…………っっ」
source.english: “Ssshhhaaaah…”
“Haaah… Ah…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Ffhhhhーー…………」
【Kisara】 「Haah…………ah……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……うん。ちょっとだけ、落ち着いた。
　これだったらしばらくは保ちそう。
　騒がせてゴメン、朔屋」
source.english:
“…Yes. A little calmer.
I think this'll keep me going for a while.
Sorry for the fuss, Sakuya.”

source.japanese: キサラから謝罪の言葉を得ようとはなんとも希有な事、これなら、後宮の性奴の如くに嬲[なぶ]っても恭順するかもしれないが、正気に戻った際の報復を思うと陰嚢が萎縮する。朔屋はやっぱり自粛して、小瓶の中味を問うた。
source.english: To hear an apology from Kisara was a rare thing indeed. In this state she might submit even if he abused her like a sex slave in some emperor's harem—but the thought of her reprisals once sanity returned shriveled his scrotum. Sakuya restrained himself after all and asked what was in the vial.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それにしても豪く効いたな、それ。
　薬かなんかか？」
source.english:
“That worked pretty impressively.
Some kind of medicine?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……Yeah. I've calmed down, though just a little. Looks like I can hold out for a while longer now. Sorry for causing a fuss, Sakuya.」

What a rare turn of events it was to receive words of apology from Kisara: with the way she was acting, perhaps she might remain submissive even were he to degrade and sport with her like one would a harem sex slave, but as soon as he thought of the reprisal doubtless awaiting him once she regained her senses, his testicles shrivelled up. In the end, Sakuya chose self-restraint, instead asking her about the contents of that small bottle.
【Naomasa】 「All things considered, that stuff was remarkably effective. Is it medicine of some kind?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ああこれね。
　これ、シサムの耳滓だよ」
source.english:
“Oh,
this? It's Sisam's earwax.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Aah, this here, right? This is Shisamu's earwax.」
【Naomasa】 「…………Huh?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ほら、あいつの匂いの、濃いところなわけだから。
　あれの事が身近に感じられて、ちょっとは不安も和らぐっていう───」
source.english:
“You know, her smell's concentrated in it.
Makes me feel she's close by, so the anxiety eases a bit…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Look, it's just because it's something that smells really intensely of her. When it feels like she's close by my side, it calms my anxiety a little and───」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ちょっとなにその顔、なんでそんなにボートのはしっこに離れてくかな？」
source.english: “What's that face for? Why are you moving all the way to the edge of the boat?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Wait, what's with that look? Why are you moving all the way to the edge of the boat like that?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ひ、引かないでよ、自分から訊いておいて」
source.english: “D-don't recoil! You're the one who asked.”

source.japanese: 双子にとっては自分達の宿痾への保険なのだろう、とは察せられても。あれだけの耳垢を一々取っておいて溜めこんでいるのには、なんの気なしに手に取った石の裏に、微細な虫がびっしりと埋めつくしているのを見た時と同等の怖気催すを抑えられず、朔屋は腰を浮かせ気味にキサラと距離を開けたという。
source.english: He could see that this was the twins' insurance against their chronic affliction. Even so, the thought of their painstakingly saving every scrap of earwax until they had amassed that much gave him the same crawling horror as turning over an idle stone and discovering its underside carpeted with minute insects. Unable to master the shudder, Sakuya half rose and edged away from Kisara.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「D-, don't act so grossed out, you're the one who asked!」

In the twins' mind, this was probably some sort of insurance for their chronic disease, or so he presumed at least. For her to have picked out so much earwax, piece by little piece, only to then have hoarded it like that; he couldn't suppress the dread he felt, one no different than what he'd felt the moment he saw that the underside of a rock he'd once unthinkingly picked up was completely covered in a swarm of tiny insects, and Sakuya had half-risen to his feet as he tried to create distance between himself and Kisara.

source.japanese:
……こんな事ばかりやっていたものだから、短艇は始めのうちは遅々たる進度であったが、キサラが平静を取り戻してからは捗り、洋上見当違いの方角に迷う事なく、やがて目的の位置に到達を見る。
　ちなみに宗右衛門猫はこれらの無駄騒ぎからは離れて関与せず、舳先の上下に合わせて髭を微かに震わせて進路を見守るが超然と、人間二人などより余程頼もしかった。
source.english:
…All this had made their initial progress slow. Once Kisara recovered her composure, however, they made headway. Without wandering off in the wrong direction, they eventually reached their destination.
Throughout the pointless commotion, the cat Soemon had kept his distance and refused to get involved. His whiskers quivered slightly with the rise and fall of the bow as he watched their course in lofty detachment. Far more dependable than either human.

target.text: ……At first, the boat had made little headway because they had been too busy with their nonsense, but as Kisara regained her cool, they began to make good progress; without veering off course on the open ocean, before long, their arrival at their intended destination came into view. Incidentally, Souemon the cat had distanced himself and been a non-participant in the pointless turmoil, detached and aloof as he kept watch over the course of the boat, whiskers minutely vibrating in tandem with the vertical movement of the bow, far more dependable than the two humans.

source.japanese:
視界に入った時は洋上遙かのマッチ棒程度のそれは、今や突兀と鋭い姿で短艇の舳先の先に聳え立ち、朔屋の目に宙に切っ先突きつけて挑む巨神族の剣のように映じた。
　なぜその岩礁に巨神だなんだを想起したのか、心象の由来がしばし判然としなかったが、岩礁にいよいよ接近するにつれ諒解された。
　諒解して朔屋は、どうにも座り心地の悪い感触に囚われる、というのも。
source.english:
What had looked no larger than a matchstick far out at sea now reared jagged and sharp beyond the boat's bow. To Sakuya it resembled a Titan's sword, its point thrust at the heavens in challenge.
For a time he could not have said why the reef had put giants and gods into his head. As they drew nearer, the source of the fancy became clear.
Clear—and it left Sakuya in the grip of a distinctly uncomfortable feeling. For—

target.text: When it first entered their vision, it had looked like a matchstick peeking out of the ocean far in the distance, but it was now a pointed shape jutting sharply upwards, towering over the bow of the boat, giving Sakuya the visual impression of a sword from a clan of giant gods, point thrust towards the heavens. Why did the reef call to mind giant gods? The origins of his mental image remained unclear for a time, but as they drew nearer to the reef, he came to understand. And having understood, Sakuya was gripped by a profound sense of discomfort where he sat, because:

source.japanese: 突き立つ岩礁の、尖った天辺のあたり、額環と冠されてあるのは、三束の藁縄を太蛇の腹の如く縒り合わせ、奇数目の縄目ごとに御幣を挟んだ、あれは、注連縄という神祭具ではないか？　この祭具、標縄とも表し、通常は境界を示し、出入りを禁止することを示すために張りまわす。特に、神事において神聖な場所を画するために用いる事が多い。
source.english: Near the reef's pointed summit it wore a kind of circlet: three bundles of straw rope twisted together like the belly of a great serpent, with sacred paper streamers tucked into every other coil. Was that not a shimenawa, the ritual rope used to mark a boundary and forbid passage? In sacred rites especially, such ropes enclosed ground reserved for the gods.

source.japanese: シサム・キサラは、ただ岩礁々々とこともなげに宣っていたけれど、もとより罰当たりな信天翁号の乗員である上、信心など鼻をかんだ懐紙ほどにも価値を置かない輩であるところの彼女達とは異なり、朔屋は民族的に神域という概念には近しい。注連縄かかった岩礁には漠然とした尻込みを禁じえず、
source.english: Sisam and Kisara had dismissed it as merely a rock, but they were sailors of the blasphemous Albatross and valued religion no more than a tissue after they had blown their noses in it. Unlike them, Sakuya had the native instinct for sacred ground of a man born to this country. The rope-hung reef made him hesitate despite himself—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あれで、間違いはないんだよなキサラ？」
source.english: “You're sure that's the place, Kisara?”

target.text: The area around the pointed peak of the jutting reef was crowned with a circlet of sorts formed of three lengths of rope entwined into a braid, like the belly of a fat snake, with a nusa inserted into every odd-numbered twist, but was this not the divine ritual implement known as a shimenawa? This ritual implement, also written as "標縄", normally signified a boundary, one put up around something to display that entering and exiting was forbidden. (TN: Nusa, written "御幣" here, is an archaic reading of "gohei". It is a little staff with plaited paper streamers, oft seen in Shinto rituals. "注連縄" is the modern way to write shimenawa at shrines while "標縄" is more archaic.)
In particular, it was often used in Shinto rituals to demarcate places considered sacred.

Shisamu and Kisara had deigned to prattle on about reefs, reefs, but unlike those women, who, on top of being part of the naturally profane crew of the Albatross, were a lot that placed less value in piety than a tissue they'd blown their noses into, Sakuya was ethnically closer to the concept of the holy shrine precincts of Shintoism. He could not suppress an ambiguous hesitation at the idea of approaching a reef clad in a shimenawa,
【Naomasa】 「And this is the place. No mistake about that, right, Kisara?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「うん、あの岩礁の周りがアクちゃんの住処」
source.english: “Yes. Little Aku lives around that rock.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやあんたらなぁ、こういうカミサマ関係の場所って殺生御法度……いや、いい……」
source.english: “You two, honestly. Places connected with gods like this, you're not supposed to kill living things… No, never mind…”

source.japanese: 口にのぼせかけて朔屋自身、自分とて社に参る機会といってはせいぜい正月くらいの、それも御神酒目当ての不心得者であると思い当たり、濁す。酔いしれた挙げ句に裏路地の塀に書かれた鳥居の印へ放尿してのけた覚えだってないでもない。
source.english: He got that far, then recalled that he himself seldom visited a shrine except at New Year, and then only for the sacred sake. Once or twice, drunk, he might even have pissed on one of those torii painted on alley walls precisely to prevent it. He let the subject drop.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（そういや信天翁の上甲板にゃ鳥居も立ってるが、古株連中、アレについちゃどう考えてるんだ）
source.english: (Come to think of it, there's a shrine gate on the Albatross's upper deck, too. What do the old hands think of that?)

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Yeah, the vicinity of that reef is Aku-chan's habitat.」
【Naomasa】 「Come on you twooo, killing is prohibited around these sorts of places connected to the gods…… nah, whatever……」

About to raise the issue himself, Sakuya suddenly recalled that the only occasions on which he himself would visit a shrine would be around New Year, and he was the sort of misguided man who only went there for the sacred sake, so he evaded the subject. He would neither confirm nor deny if he could recall brazenly pissing on the symbol of a torii drawn on a wall in a back alley after getting drunk. (TN: Impurity, known in Japan as "kegare", is a major concern in Shintoism. Urinating on a sacred object is considered very impure, and so property owners would put torii and other divine symbols on the walls to keep people from urinating there.)
【Naomasa】 （Speaking of, there is a torii on the upper deck of the Albatross, but I wonder. What do the ship's veterans think about that one?）

source.japanese: 朔屋はふと船にと気を逸らしたが、隣で腰を浮かせ目を細くして岩礁を窺うキサラが呟いた声の、雨の夜に迷うて濡れる幼子に似て心細さげな。
source.english: His thoughts wandered briefly back to the ship. Beside him, Kisara half rose and narrowed her eyes at the rock. Her muttered words were as forlorn as a little child lost and wet on a rainy night.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんか……シサム、いないみたい……」
source.english: “It looks like… Sisam isn't there…”

source.japanese: 天辺の注連縄の造作が見てとれるくらい接近しつつあるのに、岩礁の水際から頂上まで双子の片割れの形は見えず、どうにか保っていた平静のメッキはすぐさま剥げて、キサラの声がまた不安を帯びる。シサムが乗ってきたはずの短艇も見えない。
source.english: They were close enough to make out the sacred rope's construction at the summit. Yet from waterline to top, the other twin was nowhere to be seen. Kisara's precarious veneer of composure peeled off at once, and anxiety entered her voice again. Nor could they see the boat in which Sisam must have come.

target.text: Sakuya had accidentally been distracted by thinking of the ship, but Kisara, so restless she couldn't sit still and peering at the reef with narrowed eyes from next to him, let out a murmuring as forlorn as a drenched little child lost on a rainy night.
【Kisara】 「Kinda seems like…… Shisamu isn't here……」

They had approached to the point that the workmanship of the shimenawa on the peak was clearly visible, and yet there was no sign of the figure of the other twin half anywhere, from the waterside to the summit; whatever pretence of composure that she had somehow managed to hold on to was quickly peeled away, and Kisara's voice was once more tinged with anxiety. The boat that Shisamu must have sailed here on was also nowhere to be seen.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「もしかして、足踏み外して落ちちゃったのシサム……？」
source.english: “Did she lose her footing and fall…?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それとも、方角間違って、どっかよそに流されちゃったのかなぁ………っ」
source.english: “Or get the direction wrong and drift off somewhere else…?”

source.japanese: 声音が歪み、語尾の震えが尻上がりに高まり、
source.english: Her voice warped. The quaver at the ends of her words rose higher—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Did Shisamu maybe lose her footing and fall in……?」
【Kisara】 「Or else, maybe she lost her bearings, and then she drifted off to somewhere else………」
Her tone of voice strained, the quivering of the inflection at the end of her sentences rising in intensity,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まさか、突然翼が生えてくるとかいう奇病に罹って、どっかに飛んでッちゃった？　あたしを置き去りにして？　───うあああん、シサム～～っ」
source.english: “What if she caught some strange disease that suddenly made wings grow, and flew off somewhere? Leaving me behind? Waaaah! Sisaaam!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ないない、それはない。
　ここまで漕いできてなんだが、もしかして、信天翁号のどっかに残ってたりするんじゃねえの？」
source.english:
“No, no.
Not that. We've rowed all this way, but could she still be somewhere aboard the Albatross?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Could it be, maybe she fell ill with a strange disease that made her grow wings all of a sudden, and then she flew off somewhere? And abandoned me? ───Waaaaaah, Shisamu～～!」
【Naosama】 「No, no, definitely not. I know we've already rowed this far out and all, but maybe she could just still be somewhere on the Albatross, right?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ないない、それはない。
　船の中にいたならあたし、
　多少離れてたって判るし」
source.english:
“No, no.
Not that. If she were on the ship, I'd know,
even some distance away.”

source.japanese: といって、剣のように細い岩礁の表面には人一人を見落とすような物陰もなく、キサラの言う、滑落や漂流の可能性も事ここになって危惧されてくる。朔屋にもキサラの懸念が伝染しかかって、むず痒いような不安に襲われた時───
source.english: Yet the blade-thin reef offered nowhere an entire person could remain unseen. By now even Sakuya had begun to fear that Kisara might be right: Sisam had slipped into the sea, or drifted away. Her anxiety was infecting him. Just as a crawling unease took hold—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「No, no, definitely not. If she was somewhere on the ship, I could tell, even if she was a little ways apart from me.」

So she said, but there was no cover behind which a single person could hide from view on the surface of this slender, sword-like reef, and he was beginning to feel uneasy that what Kisara mentioned earlier, her slipping off or being adrift, was becoming a very real possibility. Sakuya had also been infected by Kisara's worries, and just as he was assailed by an itching anxiety───

source.english:
“Aaah…
…………Eeeeh…………”

source.japanese: 音声はまだ遠かったが、洋上はほぼ無風状態ゆえ出所を見誤る恐れはない、間違いなく岩礁から切れ切れに伝わってくる。朔屋とキサラは一瞬顔見合わせて、すぐさま猛然と漕ぎ足を速めた、声は悲鳴の、切迫した響きを帯びて、二人を急かし立てる。
source.english: The voice was still distant. But there was almost no wind at sea, so its source could not be mistaken. It came unmistakably from the rock, in broken snatches. Sakuya and Kisara exchanged a glance, then immediately rowed with furious speed. The voice had the desperate urgency of a scream. It drove them on.

target.text: The voice was still distant, but since the surface of the sea was mostly windless, there was no need to worry about misjudging its point of origin: it undoubtedly came in disconnected pieces from the reef. Sakuya and Kisara looked each other in the eyes for an instant, then at once furiously quickened the pace of their rowing; the voice was tinged with the urgent tones of screaming, spurring the two of them into action.

source.japanese: 航跡を円弧に、岩礁の背後に短艇を迂回させる、朔屋達からは死角となっていた位置に。
source.english: Curving their wake, they brought the boat around behind the rock, to the side that had been hidden from them.

target.text: The boat was maneuvered around the reef, its wake tracing a wide arc, arriving behind the rock by what had been a dead angle from where Sakuya and Kisara had been before.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『ひわあああ、岩肌が尖ってて、
　掌切れルゥゥっ』
source.english:
“Hyaaaa! The rock's so sharp,
it's cutting my palms!”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『もしももしも、切ったところから膿んじゃって、全身カラシみたいに真っ黄色に膨れあがったらどうしよう!?　うわああん、ウミはひどいな黄色いなぁ～っ』
source.english: “What if the cuts get infected and my whole body swells up yellow as mustard? Pus is nasty, pus is yellow—waaaah!”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『それにこう岩っ肌にへばりついてると腰が冷えるぅぅ、生理不順になったらどうしよう、ああ、たァすけてぇぇ……っ』
source.english: “And clinging to this rock is making my hips cold! What if my periods go wrong? Oh, heeeelp…”

source.japanese:
岩礁の高所に背を押しつけるように必死でへばりつくその姿。注連縄張った禁足地に、金髪の乙女の取り合わせは奇妙な和洋折衷、さしずめ蕃神に捧げられた生贄の有り様なれど、従容と項垂れて運命の時を待つどころか、可哀相なくらい取り乱し、今まで足を踏み外さず耐えていられたのが不思議なくらい。
　何らかの事情で岩礁に乗り移った後で、短艇を流してしまったものと見えた。
source.english:
She clung desperately high on the rock, her back pressed against it. A blond maiden on forbidden ground enclosed by a sacred rope: an odd mixture of East and West. She looked like a sacrifice to some foreign god. But far from bowing her head serenely to await her appointed fate, she was so pitifully distraught that it seemed a wonder she had kept her footing this long.
Apparently she had climbed from her boat onto the rock for some reason, then let the boat drift away.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、間違いなくシサムだ……双子だと、やっぱり発作の現れ方もそっくりなんだな」
source.english: “Yes, definitely Sisam… Twins even have identical attacks, I see.”

source.japanese: 周りの事象全てを杞憂の種にする錯乱ぶりは双子の片割れと判を捺したように似通って、朔屋はつい大きく頷[うなず]いて納得の、
source.english: Every chance occurrence became fuel for baseless dread in exactly the same way as with her twin—as if stamped from the same mold. Sakuya found himself nodding vigorously in recognition.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「シサム～、あたしだ、キサラだ、待ってて今すぐ行くから───」
source.english: “Sisam! It's me, Kisara! Wait, I'm coming right now—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 『Waaaaah, the rock face is sharp, my palms are splittiiiing!』
【Shisamu】 『What if-, what if the cuts start to fester, and then my whole body swells up all yellow like mustard, WHAT SHOULD I DO!? Waaah, pus is such an ugly yellooow～!』
【Shisamu】 『Also, sticking to the rock like this makes my butt so cooooold, what do I do if my menstruation becomes irregular? Aah, somebody save meee……!』

That figure, desperately clinging on like she was pressing her back against some place high up on the rocky outcrop. The combination of a maiden with golden hair in a forbidden area marked with shimenawa made for a curious blend of Japanese and Western aesthetics: for all the world, her condition was that of a live sacrifice offered up to some savage, foreign god, but rather than calmly hanging her head and awaiting her moment of fate, she was instead pitifully flustered, to the point it was almost miraculous that she had lasted this long without losing her footing. It looked like, by some circumstance, her boat had drifted away after she had gone up on the reef.
【Naomasa】 「Yeah, that's definitely Shisamu…… you are twins, so I guess it makes sense that your fits also manifest the same way.」

Their delusional tendency to turn everything around them into seeds of unfounded calamity was so perfectly identical to their twin's, it was as if they had been cast from the same mold, and Sakuya unconsciously nodded emphatically in understanding,
【Kisara】 「Shisamu～, it's me, Kisara! Hold on, I'm coming right away───!」

source.japanese:
……舷側乗り越えて、海に飛びこんでいこうとするキサラのジャケットの裾[すそ]をすんでで掴んで引きずり戻し、反動殺しきれずに船内床に横様に倒れこむ、短艇が大きくぐらぐらと。
　宗右衛門が種族特有の平衡感覚で小揺るぎもせず、二人に呆れたような欠伸を放った。
source.english:
…Just in time, he caught the hem of Kisara's jacket as she tried to vault the side and dive into the sea. He hauled her back, failed to kill their momentum, and the two of them fell sideways onto the floor as the boat rocked violently.
With a cat's unerring balance, Soemon did not so much as sway. He merely gave the pair what looked like an exasperated yawn.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「落ち着こうよ、ねえ頼むから。
　ここまで来てあんたまでそれじゃあ、二人して遭難しかねない」
source.english:
“Let's calm down. Please, I'm begging you.
We've come this far. If you do that, both of us could end up needing rescue.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「りょ、了解。でも急いであげて、シサム、アレじゃあもう幾らも保たない」
source.english: “R-right. But hurry. Sisam can't last much longer like that.”

target.text: ……Kisara was about to climb over the side of the boat and jump into the sea, so he grabbed her tightly by the jacket sleeve and pulled her back in; unable to withstand the recoil, he toppled sideways onto the deck, the boat shaking violently in turn. Using the sense of balance characteristic to his species, Souemon did not even so much as stir, and he yawned in exasperation at the two of them.
【Naomasa】 「Let's just calm down, please, I'm begging you here. If you lose your nerve after having come all this way, you might well both end up lost at sea.」
【Kisara】 「R-, roger. But please, hurry it up, Shisamu can barely hold on any longer like that.」

source.japanese: 漕ぎ寄せれば、頭上のシサムの引きつった口元も、キサラと同様に混乱に濁り曇った眸[ひとみ]も見てとれる。短艇の接近に気づいたシサムは、だがしかし───
source.english: As they rowed closer, they could make out the strain around Sisam's mouth and the same bewildered cloud in her eyes as in Kisara's. Sisam noticed the approaching boat. But—

target.text: As they rowed closer, he could tell how, above their heads, Shisamu's lips were stretched taut and her eyes were cloudy and muddled in confusion like Kisara's. Shisamu noticed the boat drawing near her, and yet, nevertheless───

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ちょ……だめ、こっち来ちゃ駄目」
source.english: “Wait… No. Don't come here.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Wai-……don't, you can't come over here!」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はあ!?　あんたナニ言ってるんだ。
　今にも転落しそうなくせに。
　待ってろ、今船をつける！」
source.english:
“What!? What are you talking about?
You're about to fall off!
Hold on, I'll bring the boat alongside!”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「とにかく駄目なんだってば、
　アクちゃんが、アクちゃんが！」
source.english:
“Just don't, I'm telling you!
Little Aku! Little Aku!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなざまで！　魚採りなんざしてる場合かい」
source.english: “Look at the state you're in! This is no time to catch fish!”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そうじゃなくて！」
source.english: “That's not what I mean!”

source.japanese: 上と下とで喚き合う声、救助を焦る者と助けを希う者と差し合いなのに、言葉は行き違って要領を得ず、朔屋は困惑してキサラを見やる。
source.english: Their shouts crossed between rock and boat: one frantic to save, the other desperate to be saved, yet somehow neither made herself understood. Sakuya looked to Kisara in bewilderment.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あの人、いったいなに言ってンのキサラ。
　構うなって事か？」
source.english:
“What on earth is she saying?
Does she mean leave her alone?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「違う……多分。
　ねえシサム、もしかしてアクちゃん、
　もう来てるの？」
source.english:
“No… Probably.
Sisam,
is little Aku already here?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そう、さっきからぐるぐる廻ってる。
　だから今はやばい───今はまだ」
source.english:
“Yes. It's been circling for a while.
That's why it's dangerous now. Not yet—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だから魚のコト気にしてる場合じゃないだろう。
　とにかくシサムを下ろしてやらないと！」
source.english:
“I told you, this is no time to worry about fish!
We have to get Sisam down!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「HUH!? What are you on about? And coming from someone who looks like they're about to tumble down any moment too. Just wait, we're bringing the boat alongside now!」
【Shisamu】 「I'm telling you, you really just can't come over here, Aku-chan is-, Aku-chan is!」
【Naomasa】 「Is this really the time for something stupid like fishing? While you're in such a state!?」
【Shisamu】 「That's NOT what I mean!」

Voices screaming at each other from above as below: though it was but a hindrance for both he impatient to offer aid and she who yearns for succor, their words clashed in misunderstanding, never got to the point, and so Sakuya looked to Kisara in bewilderment.
【Naomasa】 「What the hell is that woman talking about, Kisara? Does she want me to ignore her up there?」
【Kisara】 「That's not it……probably. Hey, Shisamu, could it be that Aku-chan is already here?」
【Shisamu】 「Yeah, he's been swimming round and round for a while now. So it's dangerous right now───he's still───!」
【Naomasa】 「Like I said, this really is not the time to care about a fish, surely. Anyway, we have to get Shisamu down from there first!」

source.japanese:
双子達がどう二の足踏もうと、頭上のシサムの恐怖は真に迫り、快晴だった空に何時しか雲が湧きだして、辺りに雲間の光と影が交互に刷いて通り過ぎて空気を不穏に煽る。
　足の竦んだ女を岩台から引き下ろす、といっては鉄火場を潜[くぐ]り抜けて無数の信天翁号にはさしたる冒険でもなかろうが、日頃怠惰な朔屋にはまごうかたなき大難事、なのに青年にしては気力煥発と勇ましく、行動の人となって両舷の櫂を一人で遣って短艇を岩礁の際まで漕ぎ寄せていく。
　双子が鈍いのなら自分が助けると言わんばかりの行動力で、先日鬱を発症した反動で幾らか躁期に入りかかっていたのかも知れない。
source.english:
Whatever made the twins hesitate, Sisam's terror overhead was painfully real. Clouds had begun gathering in the formerly clear sky. Alternating brushes of sunlight and shadow passed around them, stirring the air into unease.
Getting a frightened woman down from a rock might not be much of an adventure for the Albatross's crew, veterans of countless dangerous encounters. But for ordinarily lazy Sakuya it was an unmistakable ordeal. Yet he became a man of action, filled with quite uncharacteristic courage and energy. Working both oars himself, he brought the boat toward the rock.
His vigor seemed to declare that if the twins were too slow, he would do the rescuing. Perhaps the recent depression had sent him rebounding toward a manic phase.

target.text: Now matter how hesitant the twins were, the fear Shisamu felt up above was true to life, and before he realized it, clouds had welled up and covered the previously clear skies; alternating beams of light and shadow from between the rifts in the clouds swept across the surroundings, charging the air with a foreboding tension.

Pulling a woman whose legs were frozen with fear down from a rocky tower: that must hardly have counted as a noteworthy adventure for the crew of the Albatross, they who had plowed their way through countless hellscapes, but it was unmistakably a struggle for the habitual idler that was Sakuya, and yet, this young man displayed a valiant, brilliant force of will for one of his character: he became a man of action, and using the oars on both sides of the boat, he rowed all the way up to the reef by himself.

With a dynamism and drive that all but said that if the twins were going to be this obtuse, then he'd just have to rescue them himself, perhaps he had entered his manic phase as a rebound to the onset of depression he had suffered through the other day.

Therefore, the reason that Sakuya only fixedly stared upwards was because he'd been uplifted by an uncharacteristic sense of duty, and while he could, without a doubt, catch a peek of what lay beneath Shisamu's skirt from this angle, it was not born from any impatience smouldering within him, of how that skirt could put an iron curtain to shame in spite of all that pert fluttering; would it never allow itself to be seen, no matter the circumstances? It was certainly nothing of that sort.

source.japanese:
だから朔屋が上ばかり凝視していたのは、何時にない使命感に昂揚していたからで、このアングルからなら間違いなくシサムのスカートの中が覗けそうだとか、あんな小賢しくひらひらしているのになんで鋼鉄のカーテンも顔負け、どうあっても見せないのかとやきもきしていたからでは、けしてない。
　いずれにしても、視線は上ばかりに向かい、海面下までには注意が及ばなかったのだ。
　なにやら宗右衛門が警告するように唸っても、キサラが焦った様子で肩を引いてきても、構わず短艇を接舷させようしたのだ。
source.english:
That Sakuya kept staring upward was, of course, because he was aflame with a rare sense of duty. It was certainly not because this angle ought to offer a view straight up Sisam's skirt, nor because he was maddened by how the sly, fluttering thing somehow guarded its secrets more impenetrably than an iron curtain. Certainly not.
Whatever the cause, his gaze never left what was above him, and his attention never reached beneath the sea.
Soemon growled a warning. Kisara tugged urgently at his shoulder. Sakuya ignored them both and tried to bring the boat alongside.

target.text: In any case, his gaze was directed upwards, and only upwards, and his attention did not quite reach the surface of the sea below him. Even when Souemon growled as if to warn him for whatever reason, even when Kisara pulled on his shoulder as though panicked, he cared not, and he continued his efforts to make the boat come alongside.

source.japanese: 短艇右方、数間隔てた海面下に、黒影が浮上してきたのにも気づかずに───
source.english: He never noticed the black shadow rising a few yards away beneath the water to starboard—

target.text: By the right side of the boat, some distance beneath the surface, a black shadow was emerging, but this, too, went unnoticed───

source.japanese:
たちまちに、黒影の。
　　深淵より───
　　　　　　　　　悪鬼の威力で。
source.english:
All at once, from that black shadow—
From the abyss—
With the might of a demon—

target.text: In an instant, a black shadow. From the abyssal depths─── With the might of a demon.

source.japanese: 水柱が　爆ぜた
source.english: A pillar of water burst.

source.japanese:
奔騰する水のうねり、短艇の船腹を大槌と叩いて危険な角度に横揺れさせ、水飛沫が驟雨と降り注ぐ。
　短艇を激烈な波浪に翻弄したものそれは、魚の口吻。
　
　───規格外れの。
　
　人間をも容易に一呑みにするほどの。
source.english:
The surging swell struck the boat's side like a great mallet, rolling it to a dangerous angle. Spray fell in a sudden downpour.
What had tossed the boat in those violent waves was a fish's snout.
—Absurdly outsized.
Large enough to swallow a human whole with ease.

source.japanese: 急浮上の速度を利して海上に跳ね上がる姿が、瞬撃の事態に魂引き攫[さら]われ短艇の操作もならずしがみつくばかりの朔屋の目に、フィルムの遅回しのようにひどくゆっくりと映った。
source.english: The speed of its ascent carried the creature leaping clear of the sea. Sakuya's soul had been snatched away by the sudden onslaught; he could do no more than cling to the boat, for steering it was beyond him. Yet to his eyes the spectacle unfolded with terrible slowness, like film run at half speed.

source.japanese:
棘々しかった。
　鰓鰭や鱗[うろこ]の末端。
　そして幾重にも連なった歯列が棘針と尖り。
　古々しかった。
　色合いは歳月を閲し苔むした巌の。
　巨大であった。
　海上に伸びあがった部分だけでもトラックほども。
　なのに水面下にまだ後を残して。
source.english:
Spiny.
The edges of its gills, its fins, its scales.
Row upon row of teeth, each honed to thorn and needle.
Ancient.
The color of a crag weathered and moss-grown through the ages.
Enormous.
The portion rearing above the sea was the size of a truck by itself.
And still the rest of it trailed beneath the surface.

source.japanese:
顎が、岩礁のシサム目がけて打ちかけられて、長靴の爪先一尺程までに迫り、狙われた者見ている者、三人の心胆氷と冷やして、最後の間を詰められず、落ちていく。
　長大な身をうねらせながら海面を穿[うが]ち、また大うねりと水柱を残して没していくまでが、どれだけ延々と引き延ばされて感じられた事か。
source.english:
Its jaws lunged at Sisam on the rock, coming within a foot of her boot tips. Target and witnesses alike—all three—felt their hearts freeze. Unable to close that last gap, it fell.
How endlessly prolonged it seemed: the immense body twisting, piercing the sea, sinking, leaving a great swell and a pillar of water behind.

target.text: A pillar of water exploded.

The rising swell of water struck the side of the boat like a great hammer, rolling it over to a dangerous angle, the spray of brine raining down on them like a sudden downpour. That thing, which had tossed about their boat with such a furious surge, was the mouth of a fish. ───One well beyond the ordinary. Large enough to easily swallow even a grown man in but a single gulp.

To Sakuya, who had lost his ability to steer the boat after his soul was swept away by this sudden assault and instead merely clung on for dear life, that shape, utilizing the speed of its sudden ascent to leap out from the surface of the ocean, was moving awfully slowly through the air, as though it were being projected in slow motion on film.

It was thorny. The tips of its gills, fins, scales. And the rows upon rows of teeth standing sharp like needles. It was ancient. Its colouring was like that of a boulder grown aged and mossy through the passage of time. It was gigantic. Even just the part that had surfaced was as large as a truck. And yet, still more of it remained below.

The jaws leapt up towards Shisamu on the reef, attempting to slam into her, drawing so close it was only about a foot from the tip of her boots; the one attacked as well as the two watching, all three felt their blood run cold as ice, but it was unable to close the very last distance, then fell. It drilled through the surface of the sea as it twisted its giant body, and with one great, final swell, it left behind another towering spray of water as it sunk beneath the surface, but oh, how interminably long those moments felt, stretching time to its breaking point.

source.english: “—Aaah! Aaah!”

source.japanese: シサムはずっと叫んでいたのだろうが、彼女の絶叫が朔屋の耳に届いたのは、海水の雨が降り止んでからだった。実際の時間にしてみれば数秒の間だったのだろうが、突然の衝撃に耳が麻酔されていたのだ。
source.english: Sisam had probably been screaming all along, but her cries only reached Sakuya's ears after the rain of seawater stopped. In actual time, perhaps only a few seconds had passed. The sudden shock had anesthetized his hearing.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「───AH～～, AAH～～!!」

Shisamu had probably been screaming the whole time, but her screams only reached his ear now because the rain of brine had stopped. In real time, it had likely only lasted a few seconds, but his ears had been anaesthetized by the sudden impact.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「よし、逃げよう！」
source.english: “Right. Let's run!”

source.japanese: やはりこの時の朔屋は常より反応が早かった。速やかに状況見極め的確に取りうる方途を選び取り、そしてキサラに、肩をがくがく、脳震盪起こしそうなくらいに揺すぶりたてられたという。ふるふる首を振りながら、半泣きの顔で。
source.english: At times like this Sakuya's reflexes truly were quicker than usual. He took in the situation, chose the one sensible course available—and then Kisara, half in tears and shaking her head, seized him by the shoulders and rattled him hard enough to cause a concussion.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Alright, let's get out of here!」

Sakuya really did react faster than usual right now. He quickly assessed the situation, selected the most appropriate course of action, and then Kisara shook his shoulders so violently that he almost suffered a concussion. She shook her head back and forth, tears welling up in her eyes.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だめええええシサムを置いてかないでえ！」
source.english: “Nooooo! Don't leave Sisam!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやだって、あんな化け物が出るなんて聞いてないもん俺。なんなんだありゃあ!?」
source.english: “But nobody told me there'd be a monster like that! What the hell was it!?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「始めから言ってるよあたしら、
　あれがアクちゃん、
　あれがアクルじゃないか」
source.english:
“We've been telling you from the start.
That's little Aku.
That's Akuru.”

source.japanese: アクル───
source.english: Akuru—

source.japanese: この邦[くに]の、今はなかば失われた古い古い神話に、女装癖のある皇子がまつろわぬ民を討伐した道行きの帰り、遭遇した大怪魚の名が、一名悪褸である。その大きさは近づく船を一呑みにしたほどというから、朔屋達が遭遇したのは伝承よりはやや小振りだが、それでも恐ろしい脅威には違いない。
source.english: In this country's ancient, half-forgotten mythology, a prince with a taste for women's clothes encountered a gigantic monstrous fish on his return from subduing rebellious peoples. One of its names was Akuru. It was supposedly large enough to swallow an approaching ship whole. The specimen they had encountered was somewhat smaller than the legend, but a terrifying threat nonetheless.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あっはっは、あんな化け物をちゃん付けにして、活け作りがどうとか目の周りのぷるぷるが珍味とか、あんたらはどれだけ命知らずなんだ」
source.english: “Ha ha ha. You give that monster a cute little pet name, talk about slicing it up alive and the delicacy around its eyes—just how suicidal are you two?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「歴史以前の世界ならまだともかく、なんだってあんな化け物がまだ生き残っているんだよう！」
source.english: “Maybe in some prehistoric world, but why's a monster like that still alive now!?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「NOOOOOO, PLEASE DON'T LEAVE SHISAMU BEHIND!」
【Naomasa】 「No, but, nobody told me anything about a monster like that showing up! What the hell is that thing!?」
【Kisara】 「But we told you right from the start. That's Aku-chan. That's Akuru, isn't it?」
Akuru───

In an ancient myth of this land of Japan, one almost lost to time these days, a certain prince with a habit of cross-dressing had subjugated some disobedient subjects and was on his way home, and of the several names given to the enormous legendary fish he encountered there, one was Akuru. (TN: Akuru is an evil god from Japanese mythology, and the prince here is Yamato Takeru, who, after conquering the people of Kumaso (a fierce, non-Yamato indigenous people who lived on what is now the island of Kyuushuu) by dressing up as a woman at a banquet and stabbing their leader, Torishi-Kaya, encountered Akuru on his way home. He then bravely mounted the rampaging fish and vanquished it with his sword.)

Its size was said to be gargantuan enough to almost swallow an entire boat in a single gulp, so the one Sakuya and company had encountered here was a bit on the smaller side, but even so, it was doubtless still a terrifying threat.

【Naomasa】 「Ah-ha-ha. First you give a monster like that a cute nickname like "Aku-chan", then you mention something about fresh sashimi and how the jiggly bit around the eyes is a delicacy. Just how reckless can you two be?!」
【Naomasa】 「It'd be one thing if we still lived in prehistoric times, but how in the world is a monster like that still alive today!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「海の上じゃ、なにがあったって不思議はない」
source.english: “At sea, nothing's too strange to happen.”

source.japanese:
きっぱり言い切られて朔屋は、眼差しをどんより澱[よど]ませた。シサム・キサラには今さらなにをの自明の理であるようだが、朔屋にはあまりに荒々しい洗礼であった。
　なにしろ、疑う暇も無く眼前にその証拠を見せられては、実在を論じている段ではない。
source.english:
At this categorical pronouncement, Sakuya's eyes went dull and stagnant. To Sisam and Kisara it was a truth too obvious to need saying; to him, it was a baptism far too savage.
There had been no leisure for doubt. With the proof thrust before his eyes, this was hardly the moment to debate whether such things existed.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「とにかく、逃げるにしても、シサムを下ろしてからにして……」
source.english: “Anyway, if we're going to run, get Sisam down first…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「There's nothing so strange it can't happen out at sea.」

Being told that so flatly to his face, the look in Sakuya's eyes grew leaden. It seemed like such an axiomatic truth to Shisara and Kisamu, as thought they wondered why he even had to ask, but this was an excessively brutal baptism for Sakuya. At any rate, he wasn't exactly given the time to doubt, and he had also been made to witness proof of it with his very own eyes, so this really wasn't the right place to discuss if that thing really existed or not.
【Kisara】 「Anyway, if we're going to escape, that'll have to be after we get Shisamu down from there……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そ、そう、今なら平気、早く助けて、
　アクちゃん、一回飛び出したら、
　大抵は暫くは潜[もぐ]ったままだからぁ……」
source.english:
“Y-yes. It's safe now. Hurry, help me.
Once little Aku jumps out,
it usually stays down for a while…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ye-, yeah! Now should be fine, so hurry up and save me, because, after Aku-chan jumps up once, he generally stays underwater for a bit, so……!」

source.japanese: 顎にかけられるところを寸前で免れたシサムだったが、緊張は彼女の体力気力を大きく削ぎ取っていったようで、岩肌にしがみつくのももう限界、生まれたての草食動物の仔のように膝が笑って、辛うじて踵[かかと]をかける程度の余地しかないとっかかりから、今にも滑落しそう。
source.english: Sisam had escaped those jaws by the narrowest margin, but the strain seemed to have drained both strength and spirit from her. She could scarcely cling to the rock any longer. Her knees shook like a newborn fawn's. The ledge gave her barely enough purchase for her heels; she looked ready to slip at any moment.

source.japanese:
アクルが没していた後の海面は、今はうねりも収まり、不穏な気配をまだ残していたけれど、この機を逸して再度の襲撃浮上に遭ったら目も当てられない。
　この隙にと、うねりに押されて岩礁から流されてしまった短艇を寄せようとして。
　また宗右衛門の警告の唸り！
source.english:
The swell left by Akuru's plunge had subsided, though an ominous air still hung over the water. If they missed this chance and faced another attack from below, the result did not bear thinking about.
While they had the opening, they tried to bring the boat—swept from the rock by the swell—back alongside.
Again came Soemon's warning growl!

target.text: After being a hair's breadth from being locked in those jaws, the tension seemed to have shaved off a significant portion of Shisamu's mental and physical energy; she was already at her limit just from clinging to the rock face, knees buckling like a baby herbivore fresh out of the womb, left with only enough room to barely rest her heels on, about to tumble down any moment.

The swell of the sea from when Akuru had submerged had abated now, and while an unsettling presence still lingered in the waters, it would be disastrous to let this chance pass them by only to have to suffer another leaping assault for it. Taking the chance, they tried to bring their boat, which had been swept away by the swelling of the sea, closer to the reef. Once again, Souemon unleashed a warning growl!

source.japanese:
見よ、黒猫が身を低くして鼻筋に皺寄せ睨[にら]みつける先。
　再び海面が盛り上がり、浮かび上がった馬の背ほどもある瘤。
　此度は高く跳躍する事もなく、岩礁からも短艇からも離れる事一〇米ほどの波間で、さほどの危険は無さそうに、思われたのも束の間、大怪魚の背は洋上を走り始める。大きな弧、その裡側に短艇と岩礁を閉じ込めて輪を作り、ぐるぐると、相当の速度で。
　始めは大きかった輪が螺旋を描き、次第に狭まっていくと気づいた時、短艇と岩礁の三人の目が恐怖に見開かれる。
source.english:
Look where the black cat crouched low, wrinkling his muzzle as he glared.
The sea heaved again, raising a hump broad as a horse's back. This time the fish did not leap. It surfaced about ten meters from both reef and boat, and for an instant seemed harmless enough. Then its back began racing over the sea. It carved a vast circle, trapping boat and rock within, round and round at tremendous speed.
The circle was becoming a spiral. By the time all three realized it was tightening, their eyes had opened wide with terror.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あれもしかして、俺達の事、まだ諦めてない、てか、完全に狙ってる……？」
source.english: “Wait—has that thing still not given up on us? I mean… it's definitely hunting us, isn't it?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「アクちゃん、執念深いから……」
source.english: “Little Aku's persistent…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「てことは、追い払うかなんかしないと、シサムどころか俺達までやばいって訳か……おいマジかよう」
source.english: “So unless we drive it off or something, we're in trouble, never mind Sisam… Oh, come on. Seriously?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「多分、そう……」
source.english: “Probably…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもあんた、追い払うって言うたかて……」
source.english: “But when you say drive it off…”

source.japanese: あんな化け物を相手取るには銛撃ち砲の二・三門があっても頼りないのに、こんな短艇にはそんな装備など望めたものでなく、朔屋がざっと改めても艇内には鯨銛の一本だに見当たらず、またあったところでこれまでそんな得物など手に取ったこともない彼にまともに扱えようとも思われない。
source.english: Even two or three harpoon guns would have felt inadequate against such a monster, and there was no hope of equipment like that in this little boat. Sakuya's hurried search found not so much as one whaling harpoon. Even had he found one, he had never handled such a weapon and could hardly expect to use it properly.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「武器の一つもないときた」
source.english: “Not one weapon.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「うああん、もうこの世は闇だ絶望だぁ～っ」
source.english: “Waaaah! The whole world's darkness and despair!”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「シサム、諦めたらだめえ～～っ」
source.english: “Sisam! Don't give up!”

source.japanese: 岩礁では双子の片割れ恐怖に押しひしがれて、岩肌にすがる手から急速に力が抜けていく、踵の下では狭い張り出しひび割れて、欠片が落ちていって波間に小さな飛沫、その間も着実に包囲の輪を狭めていく大怪魚の背中、状況は悪化の度合い増していくばかり。
source.english: On the rock, the other twin was crumpling beneath her fear. Her fingers were rapidly losing their hold. The narrow shelf beneath her heels cracked; fragments dropped into the waves with tiny splashes. All the while, the great fish's back drew its encircling course steadily tighter. The situation could only worsen.

target.text: Behold, bear witness to what the black cat glared so hard at that his nose wrinkled while he lowered his body. Once more, the surface of the sea bulged upwards, with a swelling as tall as a horse. This time, it did not leap on high, and given it was some ten metres distant from reef and boat alike, cradled in the rolling waves, things didn't seem that dangerous, but that thought was short-lived, for the ridge of the fish began to shoot through the ocean.

Swimming in a large arc, forming a ring that locked both boat and reef within itself, round and round it went, and at a considerable speed. What began as a ring soon turned into a spiral, and by the time they noticed how it gradually narrowed, the eyes of the three in the boat and on the reef widened in terror.
【Naomasa】 「Could it possibly be that it hasn't given up on us yet? Actually, isn't this thing totally gunning for us……?」
【Kisara】 「Once Aku-chan has you in his sights, he doesn't let go, so……」
【Naomasa】 「So what you're saying is, if we don't drive it away somehow, it won't just be Shisamu, we'll be in real trouble too…… oi, are you serious?」
【Kisara】 「Probably, yeah……」
【Naomasa】 「But listen, tell me to drive it away all you want……」

He'd be uneasy picking a fight with a monster like that even with a couple of harpoon cannons at his disposal, but one couldn't possibly expect for there to be any such equipment on a boat like this, and though Sakuya cast a quick glance over the boat's interior, he couldn't even find a single whaling harpoon; even had he found one, it was hard to imagine that someone like him, a man who had never laid hands on such a weapon before now, would be able to put it to good use.
【Naomasa】 「We came here without a single weapon.」
【Shisamu】 「Waaah, this world now holds nothing but darkness and despaaair～!」
【Kisara】 「Shisamu, you can't give uuup～～!」

The half of the twins up on the reef was being crushed beneath the pressure of her terror; the strength was quickly leaving her hands clinging to the rock face, the narrow overhang under her heels cracked, fragments of stone fell, splashing in the waves, and as all this happened, the ridge of the legendary fish steadily tightened its encirclement: the situation was only worsening by the second.

source.japanese: 三人共に心脆くも絶望しかかった人間達を尻目に、宗右衛門は警戒しながらも何処か優美な足取りで船尾の横板の下に潜[もぐ]りこんでいった。自分だけ安全な隙間に隠れようというのだろう、所詮は畜生、大怪魚の質量ぶち当てられたら、こんな短艇などどこに潜[ひそ]んでいたところで関係なく海の藻屑と化すというのに。
source.english: Leaving the three frail-hearted humans to their approaching despair, Soemon slipped beneath the stern thwart with wary but somehow graceful steps. Perhaps he meant to hide alone in a safe little space. An animal, after all. Yet when that monstrous mass struck, no hiding place in such a boat would save it from becoming debris in the sea.

target.text: Sending a sidelong glance at the three humans, all brittle of heart and on the verge of sinking into despair, Souemon continued to sound his warnings while he crawled beneath the stern thwart with a graceful gait. He was probably just trying to find a safe little gap he could hide in, for in the end, he was but a beast, though were they to be rammed into by the mass of that monstrous fish, he would be fish food just like the rest of them, regardless of where he hid on a dinghy like this.

source.japanese: などて、宗右衛門はそのようなすくたれた猫などでは有り得なかった。すぐに顔を出し、口にくわえて留め紐引きずって、引っぱり出してきたのが、彼の体よりも大きい頭陀袋。二人の前まで苦もなく引いてくると、前足で袋の口押さえて、にゃあの一声は世界中の雌猫を惚れさせてしまいそうに低く渋かった。
source.english: Of course, Soemon was no such craven beast. He soon poked his head back out, drawstring in his teeth, dragging a duffel larger than himself. He hauled it effortlessly before the pair, pinned its mouth beneath one forepaw, and let out a single meow so deep and suave it might have set every she-cat in the world swooning.

target.text: But then, it was unthinkable for Souemon to be so gutless a cat. He showed up again soon enough, and pulling on the drawstrings with his mouth, he hauled forth a sack larger than his own body. He dragged it in front of them both with no effort, pushed his front paw against the opening of the sack, his meowing cry so deep and refined it might well leave female cats all around the world enamoured with him.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なにその袋？
　そんなの、積み込んだ覚えもないのに」
source.english:
“What's that bag?
I don't remember putting anything like that aboard.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああきっと、この中味を空にして空気を詰めて、浮き輪代わりにしろとかそういう」
source.english: “Oh, probably we're meant to empty it and fill it with air, use it as a life ring or something.”

source.japanese:
袋の口を解しながら朔屋が吐いたどうにも後ろ向きな台詞に、眺める黒猫の目が見下げ果てたように細められた理由というのはすぐに明らかになった。
　中に収められていたのは、鬢付け油のようにべとついた樹脂に包まれた、円筒形が何本か。
source.english:
Sakuya uttered this thoroughly defeatist suggestion while loosening the sack. Why the watching black cat narrowed his eyes in utter contempt soon became clear.
Inside lay several cylinders wrapped in a resin as sticky as hair pomade.

source.japanese:
これは───発破、マイトだ。
　内地の鉱山会社の刻印が入った高威力の。
source.english:
This was—dynamite.
High-yield stuff stamped with the mark of a mining company from the mainland.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そのマイト……こないだの取り引きン時にガメてきた奴……なんでここに？」
source.english: “That dynamite… The stuff we pinched during the last deal… Why's it here?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「What's that sack? I don't remember loading anything like that onto the boat.」
【Naomasa】 「Aah, I guess he's telling us to empty it out, fill it with air, and then use it as a lifebuoy or something to that effect.」

He let out a decidedly negative line while opening the mouth of the sack, and it quickly became clear why the eyes of the black cat staring at him were narrowed with condescension and contempt. Stuffed inside the bag, covered in some sort of pomade-like, sticky resin, were several cylindrical sticks.
This was───dynamite. For rock blasting. The powerful stuff, engraved with the seal of a mainland mining company.
【Kisara】 「That dynamite……that's the stuff we swiped during our dealings the other day……why is it here?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ううん、何でだって構わない、
　朔屋、これだったら───」
source.english:
“No, never mind why.
Sakuya, with this—”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「No, it doesn't matter why. Sakuya, with this, we can───」

source.japanese:
失意から息を吹き返して、爆薬を二本まとめて掴み上げ、一緒に入っていた導火線を雷管の口に差しこみ、ジャケットから鉄側のライターを取り出した、溌剌とした動作と目の色は、舳先に立って大怪魚の軌跡に構えた時、までしか。
　保たなかった。
source.english:
Revived from despair, she snatched up two sticks of dynamite together, inserted one of the fuses from the bag into the detonator, and drew a metal-cased lighter from her jacket. The vigor in her movements, the life in her eyes—it lasted only until she took her stand in the bow and faced the monstrous fish's circuit.
Then it gave out.

target.text: Rallying her spirit from despondency, she grabbed two sticks of explosive, inserted the fuse into the mouth of their blasting caps, pulled out an iron lighter from her jacket, and what an animated look in her eyes: there she stood at the bow, readying herself for the moment the legendary fish's trail would draw closer, but. It didn't last longer than that.

source.japanese: 蹠から生じた震えが脹ら脛、腿と伝って腰まで昇り、全身震わせてがたがたがた、金髪の烈女は肩を抱いて、気が抜けた風船としゃがみこむ。
source.english: A tremor began in her soles, traveled through calves and thighs, and rose to her hips. Her whole body rattled and shook. The fierce blond woman hugged her shoulders and crumpled like a deflated balloon.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あああ、つい勢いで構えたけど、
　もしかしてこのマイトが不発だったらどうしよう」
source.english:
“Oh, I got carried away and got ready,
but what if the dynamite's a dud?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「この横板が腐ってて、投げようとした瞬間に踏み抜いたらどうしよう。ボートの中に転がり落ちたマイトが、あたし達を吹っ飛ばすかもしれない」
source.english: “What if this plank's rotten and I put my foot through it just as I throw? The dynamite might fall into the boat and blow us up.”

source.japanese: 打ち続く緊張と衝撃で、片割れの耳垢の匂いで誤魔化していた脳の発作がこの局面で盛り返したらしい。
source.english: The unrelenting strain and repeated shocks had apparently brought back the attack she had held at bay with the smell of her sister's earwax—and at the worst possible moment.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ここにきてそれか。だ、大丈夫だキサラ。
　あんたならきっとやれる、うまくいく……」
source.english:
“Now, of all times? I-it's all right,
Kisara. You can do it. It'll work…”

target.text: The tremor originating from the soles of her feet travelled up through her calves, her thighs, rose to her hips, her entire body trembled uncontrollably, and the blonde heroine hugged her shoulders, squatting like a deflated balloon.
【Kisara】 「Aaaah, I got caught up in the moment and was all poised for it, but what if maybe this dynamite misfires, then what do I do?」
【Kisara】 「If this plank is rotten and the moment I try to throw I step through it, then what do I do? When the dynamite falls into the boat, it could blow us all to smithereens.」

Through the battering of stress and shock raining down on her, it seemed as though the fits of her brain, which had been deceived by the smell of her other half's earwax, had managed a stunning comeback at this stage.
【Naomasa】 「Of all the times, this again? I-it's gonna be okay, Kisara. I'm sure you can do it, you'll do great……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「これでも……？」
source.english: “Even with this…?”

source.japanese: と朔屋に翳[かざ]してみせた、マイト持つ手は中風患者よりも定まらずぶるぶると震え、まともな投擲の用には到底使えそうにない。
source.english: The hand she raised for Sakuya to see, still clutching the dynamite, shook with the helpless violence of a palsied limb. It was plainly incapable of a proper throw.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それじゃ、あの瓶が入った例の袋は」
source.english: “Then what about that bag with the bottle?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Even like this……?」

Saying so, she raised something up for Sakuya to see: her hand holding the dynamite was even more shaky and unstable than a patient with palsy, and it certainly didn't seem useful in the slightest for any sort of proper throwing.
【Naomasa】 「Alright then, so where did that bag with the bottle in it go?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なくなっちゃた……実は、さっきアクちゃんが飛び出してきた時、海に落としちゃって」
source.english: “It's gone… Actually, when little Aku jumped out, I dropped it into the sea.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたし、だめ……朔屋、頼むよ……」
source.english: “I can't… Sakuya, please…”

source.japanese:
涙に潤むキサラの瞳は希有な、こんな時でもなければ唇押し当てて吸いあげたくなるようなか弱さがあったけれど、振られた役が重すぎる。
　朔屋は自分を取り巻く空気が、重く、瀝青の圧力に変じて迫り来たるように感じられ、耐えきれずのけぞった。どちらにしてもアクルの周回は更に速度を増して狭まり、迷っていられる贅沢など、許されそうにない……。
　朔屋は───
source.english:
There was a rare fragility in Kisara's tear-bright eyes, one that at any other time might have made him press his lips to them and drink the tears away. But the task she had handed him was too great.
The air around him seemed to turn into a crushing weight of tar. Sakuya recoiled beneath it. Meanwhile Akuru's circuit grew faster and tighter; they would not be granted the luxury of indecision…
Sakuya—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It's gone……the truth is, when Aku-chan jumped out of the water earlier, I dropped it into the sea.」
【Kisara】 「I can't do it……Sakuya, I'm begging you……」

Kisara's eyes glistening with tears were a rare sight to behold, and she looked so weak that, were this a different time and place, he would have pressed his lips against her orbs and sucked them dry, but the role he was being made to shoulder here was too heavy a burden for him. The air surrounding Sakuya was also heavy; it felt like it was pressing down on him like tar, and he reeled backwards, unable to endure it. No matter what he chose, Akuru's encirclement was only speeding up and narrowing, and it certainly didn't seem like he'd be permitted the luxury of remaining hesitant……. Thus, Sakuya───

source.japanese:
ざああ、と怪魚の背が波を切る響きが右から左に抜けて、また戻ってきた時には音はより近くなり、追いつめられて朔屋はある計画を思いついた。
　シサム・キサラの事もあるし、彼とて我が身の命が惜しい。
source.english:
The rushing sound of the monster's back cutting water passed from right to left. When it returned, it was closer. Cornered, Sakuya thought of a plan.
There were Sisam and Kisara to consider. He valued his own life, too.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、キサラ、諦めないで落ち着いてくれ。
　あんたさえしっかりすればチャンスはある。
　まずは深呼吸だ」
source.english:
“No, Kisara. Don't give up. Calm down.
If you can pull yourself together, we've got a chance.
First, breathe deeply.”

target.text: The sharp hiss of the ridge of the monstrous fish slicing through the waves shot past them from right to left, and whenever it returned, the noise was closer than before; chased into a corner, Sakuya came up with a plan. Shisamu and Kisara were a part of his considerations too, of course, but his own life was very dear to him.
【Naomasa】 「No, Kisara, don't give up, calm down. If you can collect yourself, we still have a fighting chance. Let's start with some deep breaths.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「無理だってのに……。
　すぅぅ、はぁあ……」
source.english:
“I told you, I can't…
In… Out…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「胸がきつそうだな、ジャケットのボタンを緩めるんだ」
source.english: “Looks tight around your chest. Undo your jacket buttons.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「But it's impossible……. Fhhh, haah……」
【Naomasa】 「Your chest is looking tight, loosen your jacket by undoing the buttons.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「え……？　うん」
source.english: “Huh…? All right.”

source.japanese: 不審げな顔をしつつも、空いた片手で釦を外せば、弾けるように前身頃、乳房がぶるんと振れる。ジャケットの下には、肩を出して裁断されたカラーガード風の内着、服の裡側で温[ぬく]められた香が立った。
source.english: Suspicious though she looked, she undid the buttons with her free hand. The front of the jacket sprang apart and her breasts bounced free. Beneath it she wore a shoulder-baring top cut like a color-guard uniform, and a warm fragrance rose from inside her clothes.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「腰だってきついだろう。
　スカートのホックを外すといい」
source.english:
“Must be tight at the waist too.
You should unhook your skirt.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Huh……? Sure.」

With a doubtful expression, she unfastened the buttons using her empty hand, and when she did, it was as though the front of her clothing burst open, chest bouncing wildly with a sudden shake. Underneath the jacket, she wore a sleek inner layer in the style of a colour guard, cut away at the shoulders, and a fragrance that had been warmed beneath her clothing wafted out.
【Naomasa】 「You must be feeling constricted around the hips, too. You should really unfasten the hook on your skirt.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ええ……っ？　なんか……。
　ううん、わかった」
source.english:
“What…? That's a bit…
No, all right.”

source.japanese:
ホックに手をかけても、やはり指先が震えてうまくいかない、早く外さないといけないのに、と焦る心が余計に指の働きを阻害して、キサラは焦れったいやら哀しいやらが綯い交ぜになった気持ちに見上げる朔屋は。
　体を低くして、キサラの脚の奥に、注いでいた目つきには今か今かとの粘ついた期待で満ち満ちていた。
source.english:
Even when her hand found the hook, her trembling fingers would not obey. The more she panicked that she must undo it quickly, the less they worked. Caught between frustration and misery, Kisara looked up at Sakuya.
He was crouching low. His eyes were trained deep between her legs, slick with expectation of the moment to come.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Huuuh……? Something about this doesn't……. Alright, got it.」

As she touched the hook, her fingertips proved too shaky after all, and it didn't go well; even though she knew she had to unlatch it quickly, her panicked mind only further hindered the movements of her fingers, and when she looked up at Sakuya with a mix of frustration and misery, Sakuya was. Lowering himself down on the decking, his gaze fixed deep between Kisara's legs, brimming with a sticky, greasy expectation, all but asking "Is it now? Is it happening now?"

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……朔屋ぁ……？」
source.english: “…Sakuya…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ？　いや、外からじゃどうあっても見えないなら、そっちから外してもらえばいいとか、考えてないッスよ？」
source.english: “Huh? No, I'm not thinking that if I can't possibly see from outside, I could get you to take it off yourself…”

source.japanese:
錯乱中ではあっても耐えがたい怒り、握りしめて棍棒代わりにしようとしたマイトは、拳の中から朔屋にもぎとられた。導火線とライターも取りあげられて、怒りの遣りどころに困り、睨みつけるキサラは、青年が舷側に片足をかけて海へ立ち向かうを見る。
　朔屋はマイトを右手に、ライターを弓手に、怪魚の周回の速度を測っていた。
source.english:
Addled though she was, this was one outrage too many. She clenched the dynamite to wield it as a club, but Sakuya plucked it from her fist. He took the fuse and lighter too. With nowhere to put her anger, Kisara could only glare as he set one foot on the gunwale and faced the sea.
Dynamite in his right hand, lighter in his left, Sakuya measured the circling monster's speed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺、こんなマイトとか使ったこと無いんだよな。導火線につけるタイミングとか、そのあたりの事はあんたに言ってもらわないと」
source.english: “I've never used dynamite or anything. You'll have to tell me when to light the fuse, all that.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「タイミングが来たら、言ってくれ」
source.english: “Tell me when it's time.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……Sakuyaaa……?」

【Naomasa】 「Hah? No, I definitely wasn't thinking that, since I can't under any circumstances seem to catch a glimpse from the outside, maybe I should just have you take it off instead, or anything like that, okay?」

Even in her state of confusion, an unbearable anger surged through her; she clenched the dynamite tightly like she were about to use it as a makeshift cudgel, but then it was snatched from her hand by Sakuya. The fuse and lighter was taken from her too, and Kisara, no longer certain where to direct her anger, instead glared at Sakuya, watching the young man as he put one foot up on the gunwale and faced the sea. There Sakuya stood, dynamite in his right hand, lighter in his bow hand, measuring the speed at which the monstrous fish was circling the water.
【Naomasa】 「You know, I've never tried using anything like this dynamite before. The timing of when to light the fuse, that kind of stuff, you'll need to tell me all that.」
【Naomasa】 「When the timing is right, tell me.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋、あんた、今のはあたしをちょっとでも落ち着けようって？　点火のタイミングのために？」
source.english: “Sakuya, was that just now meant to calm me down a little? So I could tell you when to light it?”
“…Huh?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Sakuya, are you saying that was all you trying to calm me down the best you could? All so you could get the timing right on lighting the fuse?」
【Naomasa】 「……Eh?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「え？」
source.english: “Huh?”

source.japanese: 見交わした眼は、綺麗に行き違った思惑で、曰く言い難い間抜けな戸惑いに満ちていた。
source.english: Their eyes met over a perfect pair of crossed purposes, brimming with an indescribably idiotic confusion.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「い、いや、そうだその通り。
　ほらやっぱりあんたらの方が慣れてるわけだしこういう荒事には」
source.english:
“Y-yes. Exactly. That's right.
You're more used to this sort of rough business, after all.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Eh?」
Their eyes briefly met, but their intentions had misaligned so completely that their gazes were filled with such an inane confusion that it was difficult to describe in words.
【Naomasa】 「No, I mean, yeah, that's it, that's exactly right. Look, I just knew that you two were definitely more used to all this than me, all this rough stuff, so.」

source.japanese: 嘘だ───とは思ったものの、朔屋の助平根性を責めるのがなんだか馬鹿らしくなってキサラは考えるのを止めた。青年のある意味で軸がぶれない心には、少しばかり頭が下がる想いがしないでもないような……すぐに気のせいだと思い直す、今はそんなことを思い煩[わずら]うよりも。
source.english: A lie—she knew it was a lie. But taking him to task for his lechery suddenly felt too absurd to bother with, and Kisara let the thought go. In one sense, perhaps, there was something almost admirable in the unwavering axis of the young man's soul… No. She was imagining it. And now was hardly the time to fret over such things.

source.japanese:
心を蝕[むしば]み、手足の自由を奪う惑乱は消えたわけではないけれど、それでも手をつき、膝でにじって、キサラは朔屋の傍らに進み、共に大怪魚を見据える。
　風はない。怪魚の巡りも速度を増したところで安定している。左方に抜けて視界から消えて背後を巡り、右方から現れた位置は、キサラが予想したところとほぼ一致した。
source.english:
The confusion gnawing at her mind and depriving her limbs of freedom had not disappeared. Even so, palms down, she edged forward on her knees to Sakuya's side. Together they stared at the monster.
No wind. The creature's circuit had accelerated, but its speed was steady. It passed out of sight to the left, circled behind them, and reappeared on the right almost exactly where Kisara expected.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
（この速度と軌跡なら───）
source.english: (At this speed, on this course—)

source.japanese: 岩礁上の片割れに呼びかける。
source.english: She called to her other half above them on the rock.

target.text: Liar───although she thought as much, she was starting to feel the fool for bothering to rebuke Sakuya for his perverted nature, and so Kisara stopped thinking. The way this young man, in a certain sense, carried an unshakable core within his heart, it wasn't that she didn't admire it just a little bit……she immediately reconsidered, filing that away as a figment of her imagination, and there was also something far more important than worrying about such nonsense right now.

It was not the case that the confusion that ate away at her mind and kept her from using her limbs as she desired was gone now, but even so, she put her hands on the decking and crawled forwards on her knees; Kisara made it to Sakuya's side, and they stared intently at the great fish together. There was no wind. Having picked up speed, the motion of the fish's encircling was also stable. It exited to the left, vanished from sight, circled around behind them, and the place it emerged again on their right was almost exactly where Kisara had predicted it would.
【Kisara】 （Given this speed and path───）
She called out to her other half up on the reef.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「シサム、あんた上から見てて！
　あんたから見て、
　九時のところにアクちゃん来たら、
　合図して」
source.english:
“Sisam, watch from up there!
When little Aku reaches nine o'clock from where you are, give us the signal!”
“Huh—Understood…!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Shisamu, you watch from up above! When Aku-chan arrives at 9 o'clock from your perspective, give us a signal!」
【Shisamu】 「Uh───understood……!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋、シサムが合図したら、
　火ィ着けんのよ？
　そんで次にあたしが合図したら、
　二時の方に、投げる。
　見当は……このボート二つ分くらい先」
source.english:
“Sakuya, light it when Sisam gives the signal.
Then, when I signal, throw toward two o'clock—about two boat lengths out.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「外しても、恨みっこ無しでいこう。
　俺……玉投げとか苦手なんだよ」
source.english:
“No hard feelings if I miss.
I'm… not much good at throwing balls.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Sakuya, when Shisamu gives the sign, you light the fuse, got it? And once I give another signal, you throw it, towards 2 o'clock. You're aiming for……out there, about two lengths of this boat.」
【Naomasa】 「If I miss, no hard feelings, okay? I was……never very good at throwing balls and stuff.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんたに得意なもんなんて、なにがあんの。
　いいから構えて」
source.english:
“What are you good at?
Just get ready.”

source.japanese: お世辞にも達者とは言い難い屁っ放り腰に朔屋が構え、キサラは自分をがたがたに崩壊させんと手ぐすね引く不安を胸の底に押しこんで水切り音に耳を澄まし、岩礁のシサムは大怪魚の軌跡を、最後の力を振り絞ってしがみつきながら目で追いかけ、雲の緩やかな運行に合わせて日と影が入れ替わり、
source.english: Sakuya took up a cringing stance that no charity could call competent. Kisara forced the anxiety lying in wait to shake her apart down into the depths of her heart and strained her ears for the hiss of parted water. On the rock, Sisam clung with the last of her strength and tracked the great fish's course with her eyes, while sunlight and shadow traded places to the slow passage of the clouds—

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「今、通った───！」
source.english: “It just passed—!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Is there even anything that you're good at? It's fine, just get ready.」

Even an expert in flattery would find it hard to comment positively on Sakuya's weak-kneed stance, and to ensure she didn't crumble to the floor herself, Kisara was ready and waiting, pushing her anxiety deep into her bosom, listening carefully for the sound of breaking water; up on the reef, Shisamu was following the path of the legendary fish with her eyes as she squeezed out every last bit of her strength to cling on to the rock, sun and shade switching places in concert with the gentle motion of the clouds,
【Shisamu】 「Now, it just passed───!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋、火！」
source.english: “Sakuya! Fire!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Sakuya, fire!」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ、ああ……って！
　着かねえ!?　キサラ、ライター着かない！」
source.english:
“Y-yes… Wait!
It won't light!? Kisara, the lighter won't light!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Ah, aaah……tch! It won't ignite!? Kisara, the lighter isn't flicking on!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ちょ、なんで先から着けておかないの！
　着けてよはやく、タイミングがずれるっ」
source.english:
“What? Why didn't you have it lit already?
Hurry! You'll miss the timing!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「んなコト言ったって……っ」
source.english: “Easy for you to say…!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Wha-, why didn't you flick it on in advance?! Hurry up and light it, the timing's gonna be off!」
【Naomasa】 「Easy enough for you to say……」

source.japanese: 朔屋直正、力もなければ学もなく、おまけに運にもそっぽを向かれた、ライターのフリンジを弾けば、一発で着火せず、体の裡側で蟲が騒ぐようなむず痒さもどかしさ、唇戦慄かせ泣きそうになりながらもう一度、フリンジは擦過音で嘲笑う、まだ着かない。三度目の正直、二度ある事は三度ある、二つの諺がコインの裏表と目まぐるしく入れ替わる。
source.english: Naomasa Sakuya had neither strength nor learning, and now luck had turned its back on him too. He struck the lighter's wheel. It failed to catch. An itching frustration stirred inside him like a commotion of insects. Lips trembling, almost in tears, he tried again. The wheel mocked him with a scrape. Still no flame. Third time's the charm; bad things come in threes. The two proverbs flashed back and forth like the faces of a spinning coin.

target.text: Sakuya Naomasa, bereft of both brawl and brain, and on top of that, even luck had turned her back on him, so when he flicked the spark wheel, he couldn't get a single flash of fire; an itching frustration welled up within his body, and with lips trembling and tears threatening to spill forth, he tried once more, the flint mocking him with its scraping sound, still refusing to ignite. Third time's the charm, what happens twice will happen thrice, the two proverbs swapping place in his head at dizzying speed like the heads and tails of a spinning coin.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「今だよ、まだ着かない!?」
source.english: “Now! Still no flame!?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It's now! Is it still not lit?!」

source.english: “—Damn… you…!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「───Nh, this STUPID───！」

source.japanese: 運命のコインの裏表、現れた目は───小さな、しかし三人にとっては人類が初めて自力で点[とも]し得た瞬間と同じくらい感動的な火と共に。
source.english:
Which face of fate's coin appeared?
A tiny flame—but to the three of them it was as momentous as the first flame ever kindled by human hands.

source.japanese:
最後に掴んだ運の一欠片だが間に合うか、導火線に火を移すのと投ずるのをほぼ同時にこなさねばならず、力加減の調節どころか構えるもならず、下手に放り投げるしかなかった。
　だがそれがかえって効を奏したのだろう。朔屋に下手に時間的猶予が与えられたならば、すくたれ者の彼のこと、導火線の火花に臆した挙げ句手が萎縮して、狙った位置まで届かなかったに違いない。
source.english:

target.text: The next splash of water that rose was caused by Shisamu, who, having successfully escaped her impending doom, dove headfirst from the reef. Souemon was quietly licking off any of the moisture that would ruin his coat still clinging to him, cutting a truly dignified figure, and Sakuya alone, fidgeting as he pulled his pants back up, was a rising star leaving his mark in the registry of the most inept souls in recorded human history.

source.japanese:
───一番の美味だという、目玉は跡形もなく吹き飛んでしまったけれども、アクルは身はまだまだ残しており、尾柄をロープで結索して曳航の、戦利品は蟻が蟋蟀を運ぶように短艇よりも大きい、櫂を漕ぐ手に堪[こた]える。
　ただ朔屋は、ここまでの功をねぎらわれて、船尾で休む事を許されていた。どっと押し寄せた疲労に横板にぐったりもたれ、どう怪魚の肉を分け合うか、姦しく相談する声なぞを聞くともなしに耳に流し、
source.english:
—The eyes, supposedly its supreme delicacy, had been blown away without a trace. But plenty of Akuru remained. They roped it by the base of the tail and towed it behind them; like ants hauling a cricket, the little boat bore a prize larger than itself, and the drag told on every stroke.
As a reward for his efforts so far, Sakuya had been permitted to rest in the stern. Fatigue struck him all at once. He slumped against a thwart, letting the twins' clamorous discussion of how to divide the meat wash through his ears unheard.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（生命の危機だったっていうに、逞しいこった……）
source.english: (Their lives were in danger, and now this. Tough women…)

source.japanese: となかば呆れ、なかば微笑ましく聞くうちに、二人以外の声に混ざる音が合ったような気がして身を起こす。始めは二人の声と軸受けの軋みで聴き取れなかったけれど、直に後からだと振り向くと。
source.english: Half appalled, half fondly amused, he listened. Then he thought he heard something besides their two voices and sat up. At first their chatter and the creak of the rowlocks obscured it. Soon he realized it came from behind and turned.

source.japanese:
短艇の後方、目視にして三ケーブル辺りの海上、沈み始めた夕日を受けて浮かぶ、あれは船、漁船らしい。双子は相談に夢中でまだ気づいていない。
　漁船など珍しくもない海域なのだが、何やら朔屋は不穏な心地して、双子に呼びかければ、ちょっと振り向いて眺めたと思うや、向き直って櫂を漕ぐ手を猛然と速める、その切羽詰まった回転の速さは、馬泥棒が露見した盗人の手綱捌きの。
source.english:
Behind them, perhaps three cables away, a shape floated upon the sea in the light of the setting sun. A boat. Apparently a fishing boat. Absorbed in their consultation, the twins had not noticed it yet.
Fishing boats were hardly unusual in these waters, but Sakuya felt uneasy and called to them. They glanced back, then immediately faced forward and rowed with furious speed. Their desperate pace resembled the handling of reins by thieves caught stealing horses.

target.text: ───What they had claimed to be the most delicious part, the eyeballs, had been blown away without leaving any trace behind, but there was still plenty of Akuru's body left, and so they tied it to the stern handle with a rope, and like ants transporting a cricket, they towed away their spoils of war, larger than even the boat itself, the rowing arms having to bear the now-heavier burden.
