But Sakuya, as a show of appreciation for his efforts, was permitted to rest at the stern. He reclined limply on the planks as the fatigue surged through him, letting the voices loudly discussing how the meat should be divided between them go in one ear and right out the other,
【Naomasa】 （And to think they were just knocking on death's door. They're made of stern stuff……）

Thinking that, split between exasperation and amusement as he listened to them bicker, he felt like he heard a voice that didn't belong to either of them mixed in somewhere and got back on his feet. At first, he couldn't quite pick it out over their voices and the creaking of the dinghy's bearings, but he quickly realized it came from behind them and turned around.

Behind the boat───he visually estimated it to be about three cables away from them───on the sea, floating in the light of the evening sun, which had just begun to sink below the horizon, came a boat, what seemed like a fishing boat. The twins were so engrossed in their discussion that they hadn't noticed it.

Fishing boats weren't a rare sight in these waters, but for some reason, Sakuya felt ill at ease, and when he called out to the twins, they turned around and looked only for them to immediately turn back again, furiously quickening the pace of their rowing, and the desperation in the speed of their rotation of the oars was like the way a horse thief would handle his reins once he'd been discovered.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なんでそんな逃げるように……。
　おいまさか……」
source.english:
“…Why are you rowing like you're running away?
Wait. Don't tell me…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……What are you trying to escape like that for……? Oi, don't tell me……」

source.japanese:
だがどれだけ双子が躍起となろうとも、向こうは烏賊釣り船程度の小型の漁船ながら高速の機関を積んでいるようで、軽捷に距離を詰め、みるみるうちに一ケーブルまで迫り来る。
　この距離になると甲板に数名の人影あるも見分けがつき、そのどいつもこいつも拳振り上げ地団駄踏みながら、止まれ戻れといきりたっている様子。
　朔屋の悪寒は、漁船からの拡声器での呼びかけに確信にと変わった。
source.english:
However frantically the twins rowed, the other craft—a fishing boat no larger than a squid boat—appeared to carry a powerful engine. It closed the distance with ease and was within a single cable before they knew it.
At that range they could distinguish several figures on deck. Every man was shaking a fist or stamping his feet, plainly roaring at them to stop and come back.
The call over the fishing boat's loudspeaker turned Sakuya's chill suspicion into certainty.

target.text: But no matter how desperate the twins became, while it might only have been a small fishing boat used for jigging squid, it seemed to be equipped with a high-speed engine, for it nimbly closed the distance, reducing the gap to a single cable in a twinkling. At this distance, it was possible to distinguish several human figures standing on the deck, all of them shaking their fists in the air and stomping their feet while yelling "Stop, come back!", their demeanour agitated. Sakuya's chills turned into certainty when they were called out to with a megaphone from the fishing boat.

source.japanese:
【漁船からの声】
『……の、不届き者、罰当たり！
　入らずの岩さ、着けよって……！』
source.english:
“…You damned blasphemers!
You landed on the Forbidden Rock…!”

source.japanese:
【漁船からの声】
『御魚様、獲りよって……！』
source.english: “Took the sacred fish…!”

source.japanese:
【漁船からの声】
『金比羅様のぉ、
　ミサキ魚を、よくもぉ……っ』
source.english:
“Lord Konpira's messenger fish!
How dare you…!”

source.japanese:
【漁船からの声】
『……絞めてくれっぞ、腐れども……！』
source.english: “…We'll wring your necks, you rotten bastards…!”

source.japanese:
【漁船からの声】
『おめぇら、あのあるばとろすの───
　ど腐れどもォ!!』
source.english:
“You're from that Albatross—
you filthy bastards!”

source.japanese:
これは───地元の訛り丸出しの叫び声から聴き取るに、やはりあの岩礁付近は禁足地で、おまけに悪婁はカミサマの使いとして、絶対に手を出してはいけない魚だったらしい。
　そういう禁を冒した朔屋達に、怒りに燃える地元漁師達は容赦など、なんで望めよう。
source.english:
Judging by the cries, thick with local dialect, the area around that rock was indeed forbidden ground. Moreover, Akuru was apparently a messenger of the gods: a fish one must never touch.
How could they expect mercy from the local fishermen, burning with anger at those who had broken these taboos?

target.text: 【Voice from the fishing boat】 『……ye, scoundrels, accursed fiends! Ye dared to touch the forbidden rock……!』

【Voice from the fishing boat】 『Ye dared to catch Osakanasaa……!』 (TN: Osakanasaa is written "御魚様" here, which would be pronounced "Osakana-sama" in non-accented Japanese. It is a very humble, reverent way to speak of a fish.)

【Voice from the fishing boat】 『Konpira-sama's fish misaki, how dare ye……』 (TN: Konpira-sama, written "金比羅様", is a Japanese deity of seafaring who has his origins in the Buddhist deity of water, Kumbhira, who was in turn originally a Hindu crocodile deity of the Ganges River. He is enshrined in Kotohira shrine, found in Kagawa prefecture on Tokushima, where he is worshipped as the guardian deity of sailors and travellers by sea. You can find Konpira shrines all over Japan, usually overlooking large ports. A misaki is an animal dispatched by a god as their messenger, like a crow or a fox. Here it is a fish.)
【Voice from the fishing boat】 『……I'll strangle ye, ye rotten scum……!』
【Voice from the fishing boat】 『Ye bastards of that Albatross─── YE ROTTEN SCUM!!』

This was───from what he could make out of the screaming voice thick with the local accent, this reef and its surroundings were, just as he feared, forbidden land, and on top of that, Akuru was a divine messenger of a god, and as such, a fish you were not allowed to lay a finger on. Having profaned such a taboo, Sakuya and company could hardly expect mercy from these local fishermen burning up with rage.

source.japanese: 漁船の舳先に発煙の、風切り音、ロープの尾を曳いて、短艇の後方程近くで水面に跳ね、二度ほど水を切った後で沈んでいったのは鯨銛の類と見えた。
source.english: Smoke issued from the fishing boat's bow. Something whistled through the air, trailing a rope, struck the water not far behind them, skipped twice, and sank. It appeared to be a whaling harpoon.

target.text: The bow of the fishing boat emitted smoke, the cutting sound of wind rushed past, the tail of a rope trailing behind it, skipping across the surface near the stern of their boat; that which had sunk into the depths after cutting through the water a couple of times looked to be some sort of whaling harpoon.

source.japanese:
威嚇───？　否、ロープを巻き戻してまた撃ちこんできた時、狙いはより定まり短艇から逸れはしたが、着水の飛沫が朔屋を濡らすほど。
　夕暮れの海水は温かったが、朔屋はぞっと身裡を冷やして、櫂を躍起と漕ぎ続ける双子に縋[すが]りついた。
source.english:
A warning? No. When they wound the rope back and fired again, the aim was better. It missed the boat, but the splash soaked Sakuya.
The evening seawater was warm. He chilled to the core and clung to the twins, who kept rowing frantically.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「し、白旗を揚げよう！
　誠心誠意土下座して、殺らなきゃこっちが殺られたって説明すれば、きっとわかってくれる」
source.english:
“L-let's raise a white flag!
Prostrate ourselves and explain from the bottoms of our hearts that it was kill or be killed. Surely they'll understand!”

target.text: A threat───? Nay, when they had fired again after winding the rope back, though they still missed, their aim was truer than before, and it was close enough for the resulting spray to drench Sakuya. The evening ocean water was lukewarm, but Sakuya felt a chill run up his spine as his blood ran cold, and he clung on to the twins still rowing desperately.

【Naomasa】 「Le-, let's raise the white flag! If we prostrate ourselves and apologize sincerely, then explain to them that if we didn't kill the fish, we'd have been killed instead, I'm sure they'd understand!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「どこまでおめでたいかなあんた。
　漁師の荒っぽいのは、下手なマフィアよりひどいよ」
source.english:
“How naive can you be?
A pack of rough fishermen can be worse than the mafia.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「軽く済んで手足の二・三本だね」
source.english: “If we got off lightly, we'd lose two or three limbs.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「How naive can you be? Wild, violent fishermen are far worse than some bungling mafioso goons.」
【Shisamu】 「If we get off lightly, they'll only take two or three of our limbs.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ひどけりゃあ、まあ、あたしらは慰み者にされてから魚の餌。あんたはイチモツちょん切られて餌にされた後、残りもまるごと全部餌、ってトコかな」
source.english: “If it goes badly, well, they'll have their fun with us before feeding us to the fish. You get your cock chopped off for bait, then the rest of you follows it in.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「And if they're feeling cruel, well, we'll be made into their playthings and then fed to the fish. You'll have your penis chopped off, and then after that is fed to the fish, the rest of you will be fish food too, or something like that.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だいたい白旗なんざ、そう都合よく積んでるもんかい」
source.english: “Besides, it's not as though we conveniently carry a white flag.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃああんた達パンツを脱げ。
　櫂の先にくくりつけて振り回しゃ、向こうだってちょっとくらいはお目こぼしを……」
source.english:
“Then take off your panties.
Tie them to an oar and wave them around. Maybe the sight will persuade those men to let us off a little easier…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「In the first place, it's not like we just happened to conveniently bring something like a white flag on this boat.」
【Naomasa】 「Then you two take your panties off. If you tie them around the tip of the oars and swing 'em around, I'm sure they'd be at least a little more lenient and……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「やぁなこった！　そもそも今日は白いの履いてないしさ」
source.english: “No chance! Besides, I'm not wearing white today.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃあ何色だ」
source.english: “What color, then?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「No way in hell! I'm not even wearing white panties today.」
【Naomasa】 「Then what colour?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「キサラとお揃いの、く……」
source.english: “Matching Kisara's. Bl—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I'm matching with Kisara, bla-……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「シサム！」
source.english: “Sisam!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Shisamu!」

source.japanese:
慌てて鋭く制止してシサムの口を噤ませてから、どれどれとスカートの裾[すそ]指先で摘[つ]んで捲[めく]り、中味を確かめようとしていた朔屋の横面張り飛ばし、キサラは櫂から手を離す。
　その頃にはもう半ケーブルの彼我の差、どれだけ力尽くしたとて、人力では内燃機関には敵わない。
source.english:
Kisara silenced Sisam with a hurried, sharp cry, then slapped Sakuya across the face; he had already pinched the hem of her skirt between his fingers and begun lifting it to see what was underneath. Kisara let go of the oar.
By then the gap was down to half a cable. Strain as they might, human muscle could not defeat an internal-combustion engine.

target.text: Flustered. she pointedly put a stop to Shisamu, making her shut her mouth, then sent Sakuya flying with a slap across his face as he was about to lift up the hem of her skirt with his fingertips to check what hid inside while muttering "let's have a looksie" to himself; as a result, Kisara ended up letting go of the oar in her hands. By then, there was already only around half a cable left between both sides, but even should they use all their might, human strength could not hope to rival an internal combustion engine.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「こりゃ、仕方ないけど、
　アクちゃんは諦めるかぁ……」
source.english:
“Nothing for it.
We'll have to give up little Aku…”

source.japanese: さも悔しげに唇歪め、シサムとキサラは船尾から乗りだして、大怪魚を縛っていた引き綱を何やらごそごそと。してから解き───
source.english: Their mouths twisting in obvious regret, Sisam and Kisara leaned over the stern. They fiddled with the towrope securing the monster, then released it—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「今さら魚を離したって、
　許してくれそうな相手じゃないんだろ。
　ああ、あんたらについてきた俺が……」
source.english:
“You said letting the fish
go now won't make them forgive us.
Oh, why did I come along with you…?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Well, this is a real shame, but I guess we'll have to give up on Aku-chan……」

With lips twisted in genuine frustration, Shisamu and Kisara leaned over the stern, then rummaged around, doing something with the towrope tied around the legendary fish. As they did, it unravelled───
【Naomasa】 「I don't think these are the kinds of guys who will just forgive us because we let the fish go at this point. Aaah, I chose to come with you myself, I'm such a……」

source.japanese: 大怪魚の死骸はボートの造波に押されてゆらゆらと流されゆき追っ手の漁船の鼻先へ、神魚に衝突する事避けようと迂回する前に、朔屋が自分を呪う文句を吐き追える前に。
source.english: The monster's carcass drifted in their wake toward the pursuing boat's bow. Before the fishermen could turn aside to avoid colliding with the sacred fish—before Sakuya could finish cursing himself—

target.text: Pushed away by the boat's wash, the carcass of the great monster fish drifted unsteadily, ending up right under the nose of the pursuing fishing boat, but before they could circumvent it to avoid colliding with their divine fish, before Sakuya could finish cursing his own foolishness.

source.japanese: 大爆発した。
source.english: It exploded violently.

source.japanese:
轟く爆音、吹き荒れるのは血潮と混じった水飛沫に肉片の、短艇を煽っては降り注ぎ、縦揺れに転落しないよう慌てて舷側にしがみついて朔屋は、爆煙の向こうで追っ手の船の有り様に愕然としたのである。木の葉の如く爆発の荒波に翻弄され、甲板上の漁師達を叩き落としたばかりか、大きく傾いだと見る間に、石のように沈んでく。
　恐らくは迂回しようと船腹を見せたところに爆圧を受け、喫水下が破損したものか。
source.english:
A deafening blast. Blood-mingled spray and chunks of flesh whipped through the air, buffeting the little boat and raining down upon it. Sakuya flung himself against the gunwale to keep from being pitched overboard. What he saw beyond the smoke appalled him. The pursuing boat, tossed like a leaf upon the blast-driven waves, flung its fishermen from the deck, heeled sharply over, and before his eyes sank like a stone.
It had probably shown its broadside while trying to turn away, taken the blast full on, and been ruptured below the waterline.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひ、ひっでぇ……なんてことだ。
　これじゃ完全に俺らの方が悪者だ。
　全身魚肉まみれになるし───」
source.english:
“Th-that's awful… What a disaster.
Now we're definitely the villains.
And I'm covered head to toe in fish flesh—”

source.japanese: 振り返ると、双子は船底に蹲っていたが、身を守るというよりそれは、短艇内に飛び散った物を摘[つま]み上げては盛んに口に運んでいるその様子は、貪欲そのものの。
source.english: He looked back. The twins were crouched in the bottom of the boat, less to protect themselves than to snatch up whatever had scattered there and pop it greedily into their mouths.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ、あんた達。
　なにもぐもぐしてんの。
　まさか、飛び散った欠片、
　拾い食いしてるとか」
source.english:
“Y-you two.
What are you chewing?
Don't tell me you're picking up the splattered chunks and eating them.”

target.text: There was a massive explosion.

The thundering roar of an explosion, a swirling gale of blood-soaked spray and chunks of flesh, buffeting the boat and showering down in torrents of red: Sakuya clung to the side of the boat in a panic so he didn't tumble overboard as the boat pitched, aghast at the state of the boat that had been pursuing them on the other side of the fumes. Tossed about like leaves by the raging waves produced by the blast, not only were the fishermen on deck knocked into the sea, the boat tilted sharply in front of his very eyes, then sunk beneath the waves like a rock.
Most likely, just as she made to turn to bypass the carcass, that's when she took the blast overpressure to her exposed stomach, resulting in a breach below the waterline.
【Naomasa】 「How-, how horrible……what have you done? Now we're definitely the villains here. My whole body is covered in fish meat───」

When he turned back, the twins were down on their knees on the decking, but rather than attempting to protect themselves, they were instead busy grabbing all the things scattered all over the boat, heartily bringing it to their mouths, their behaviour the very essence of gluttonous rapacity.
【Naomasa】 「Y-, you two. What are you chewing on? There's no way that you're actually, picking those scattered bits off the floor to eat them, right?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「まさか、そんな真似するわけないさ。
　…………もぐもぐ」
source.english:
“As if we'd do something like that.
…Munch, munch.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Perish the thought, we'd never do something like that. …………*chompchomp*」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「勿体ないから、せめて欠片だけでもとか、考えてないよ？
　爆弾解体法とか、知らないよ？
　………………ぱくぱく」
source.english:
“We're not thinking it's a waste and we should at least get some scraps. And I certainly don't know how to butcher a fish with a bomb.
…Chomp, chomp.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It would be such a waste, so we should at least enjoy the scraps, no thought like that ever crossed our minds, you know? I don't know the first thing about how you dispose of explosives, got it? ………………*munchmunch*」 (TN: There is some wordplay here. The compound word used is "爆弾解体法", which can literally mean "a method to dispose of a bomb", but also "an explosive method of dissection", as in, for example, butchering a fish with a bomb.)

source.japanese: ───超然として孤高の宗右衛門さえ、双子と同じく肉片に舌鼓を打っており、信天翁号の面子の逞[たくま]しさ強かさとそして、人を人とも思わぬ傍若無人さに朔屋、総身脱力し、がっくり膝から崩れ、夕暮れの空に零した笑みが、へらへらと痴呆じみて、そこはかと哀調を漂わせてあった───
source.english: Even the aloof and solitary Soemon was feasting on scraps beside the twins. Faced with the Albatross crew's hardiness, cunning, and brazen contempt for all humanity, Sakuya went limp. His knees gave way. The smile he spilled into the evening sky was loose, vacant, and touched throughout by a nameless sorrow—

target.text: ───Even the aloof, proudly independent Souemon was smacking his lips over the scraps of meat just like the twins, and confronted with their ruggedness, their resilience, as well as the inhuman way the crew of the Albatross treated others in their brazen audacity, Sakuya felt the strength leave his entire body, and he collapsed from his knees, crestfallen and exhausted; the smile he flashed at the evening sky was silly, almost senile, and with a subtle tinge of mournfulness───

source.japanese: （なおこの件がきっかけとなり、信天翁号はこのあたりの地元漁師達からも、明確な仇として追われる事になったという）
source.english: (This, incidentally, was how the Albatross came to be hunted as a declared enemy by the local fishermen of these waters.)

target.text: （Furthermore, with this incident as the trigger, the Albatross henceforth came to be regarded as a target of vengeance by the local fishermen of this area as well, pursued by them as a manifest enemy.）

source.japanese: <01>自分が投擲する覚悟を決めた
source.english: Resolve to make the throw himself.

target.text: <01>Mustered the resolve to throw it himself

source.japanese: <01>どう考えても無理とつっぱねた
source.english: Insist it is utterly impossible.

target.text: <01>Flatly refused. It was just impossible

source.japanese:
とある一日。
　朔屋が遅い昼食を摂っていた時の事。
source.english:
One day.
Sakuya was eating a late lunch.

source.japanese: 双子たちが、ちょっと仕事がある、なに簡単な仕事だよ、と持ちかけてきたのだが。
source.english: The twins approached him with a little job. Nothing difficult, they said. A simple job.

source.japanese:
仕事というのは、この港の倉庫に行って、そこにいる人物と会って、これこれの書類を渡してくること。なるほど聞く限りでは、簡単である。
　簡単そうではある、あるけれどしかし───
source.english:
He was to go to a warehouse in this port, meet someone there, and hand over some documents. Simple enough, from the sound of it.
It sounded simple. Certainly. But—

source.japanese:
日頃から、脱走の機会を窺っているとばれている朔屋を、なんでその絶好の糸口である陸へ遣わそうというのか。
　朔屋にしては珍しい勘働きで厄介事の兆し感じ取り、慎重になったという。
source.english:
They knew he was always looking for a chance to desert. Why send him ashore, offering the perfect opening?
With intuition rare for him, Sakuya sensed trouble and grew cautious.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ええー……？
　水夫君達の誰か、遣いに出せば済む事なんじゃ？」
source.english:
“Uhh…
Couldn't you just send one of the sailors?”

source.japanese: 面倒事は朔屋の最も遠ざけたいところ。それもあってと否むも、
source.english: Trouble was the one thing Sakuya most wished to keep at a distance. That was reason enough to refuse—but—

target.text: A certain day. It all began while Sakuya was having a late lunch.
"We have a little job for you. Why, it's really very simple." the twins said, bringing him a proposal.

As for this job, it involved going to a warehouse in this port, meeting up with an individual there, then handing over some documents about this and that. Indeed, based on what he'd been told, that was simple. It seemed simple, it certainly did, however───

Why would they send Sakuya, who was already well-known to be constantly looking for an opportunity to escape, ashore, when that would be the perfect starting point for such a flight? With an intuition uncharacteristically hard at work, Sakuya picked up on signs of trouble in his future, and so he became wary.
【Naomasa】 「Eeeehー……? Couldn't this whole thing be handled by just sending one of the sailors?」
Trouble was what Sakuya sought most to avoid. Citing that, among other things, he refused, however,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なかなかそうもいかないのよねこれが。
　あの子達は根っからの船員暮らしで、
　船からそんなに離れたがらないの」
source.english:
“It's not that easy, actually.
They've lived as sailors all their lives.
They don't like getting far from the ship.”

source.japanese: と、なおも朔屋を口説こうとする。渋る朔屋に、双子たちは色仕掛けとしなだれかかった。
source.english: They continued trying to persuade him. When he resisted, they leaned against him and resorted to seduction.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Doesn't seem like that's really gonna work out here. Those boys live as sailors through and through, so they don't like straying from the ship much, if they can help it.」
So she said and attempted to persuade Sakuya once again. Sakuya was reluctant, and so the twins began to seduce him by leaning against him, fawning on him.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「だいたい朔屋さあ、こないだのアクちゃんの件では、あんたのせいでひどい目に遭ったわけ」
source.english: “Besides, Sakuya, we had an awful time with little Aku the other day because of you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんであれが俺のせい？」
source.english: “How was that my fault?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「So, Sakuya, to begin with, it was really all your fault that we had such an awful time during the whole Aku-chan incident the other day.」
【Naomasa】 「How could that be my fault?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「だって考えてみれば、あの日あんたが盗み呑みの罰で引っぱっていかれずにさ、始めからアクちゃん採りに行ってきてくれたなら」
source.english: “Think about it. If you hadn't been dragged away for stealing rum, and had just gone to get little Aku for us in the first place—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Well, when you think about it, if you hadn't been dragged away as punishment for stealing booze that day, and you'd instead gone to fish up Aku-chan from the start.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたし独りで行こうなんて気も起こさなかったわけ。だからあんたのせい」
source.english: “I wouldn't have thought of going alone. So it's your fault.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おおなんたる責任転嫁」
source.english: “What a magnificent way to shift the blame.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Then the idea of going by myself would never have crossed my mind. So it's all your fault.」
【Naomasa】 「Wow, what a way to pass the buck.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まあまあ、そう拗[す]ねないで。
　今回、お遣いちゃんとしてこられたらぁ」
source.english:
“Come on, don't sulk.
If you do this errand properly…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Come now, don't sulk like that. This time, once your little errand is over and done with.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ね、船室のさ、普段人が来ないとこ、
　一つとっておくから───」
source.english:
“We'll reserve a cabin.
Somewhere people don't usually come—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Look, we'll reserve a cabin, one others usually never come to, and then───」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「で、あとは……二人っきり……ね？」
source.english: “And then… just the two of us… right?”

source.japanese: 朔屋の両腕をそれぞれ取って胸の中にかき抱き、唇耳朶に寄せて囁きの、余りに判りやすすぎる飴と鞭だが、下半身直結男の朔屋君には抗[あらが]いがたい誘惑だし、久しぶりに陸に上がっての仕事であるのは確かだ。逃げ出す機会だって見えてくるのではないか？　そのあたりの諸々鑑みて結局朔屋は、お遣いを引き受ける事にする。
source.english: Each twin took one of Sakuya's arms and buried it against her breasts, bringing her lips to his ear to whisper. The carrot and stick could hardly have been more obvious, yet to Sakuya—a man wired directly to his lower half—the temptation was hard to resist. Besides, this really was his first work ashore in some time. Might it not present a chance to escape? With all these considerations in mind, he finally accepted the errand.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Then, once you're done…… with just the two of us……please?」

Taking one of Sakuya's arms each, they pulled them within their respective bosoms, lips drawn close to his earlobes as they whispered: an overly transparent use of the carrot and the stick, but it was a temptation hard to resist for a man who thought with his loins like our dear Sakuya, and it had certainly been some time since he'd last done a job on land. Did they simply not realize how this was a chance for him to make his escape? Taking various things of that nature into account, in the end, Sakuya accepted the errand.

source.japanese: 囲いの葦簀から濛とたなびいた湯気は、青年の胸元にかかって湿り、熱く、すぐに颯と流れて後は涼しい。はたまた龍の吐息か火の山の息吹か、なんの、もっと俗で、湯気は大蒜、韮だの五辛の香味たっぷり孕んで鼻に利いたし、ぎとつく屋台の竹籠に並んだのは、ふっくらとして、白く柔らかで、うねってちょんと角が立った皮の造作も胃の腑に雄弁に囁きかける、豚饅、中華饅頭の出来たてのところで。うっかり湯気と匂いの流れに踏みこもうものなら、いつ銭を払ったのかも判然としないままに経木剥がして噛みついて、熱い汁が舌を焼いたところで我に返るところ間違いなし、実に深層心理辺りに巧みに作用する湯気であることは屋台の店主自身よくよく心得て、承知で盛大に蒸籠を蒸かしていたわけだが。
source.english: Steam billowed from behind a reed screen and drifted against the young man's chest: damp, hot, then swiftly gone, leaving coolness. A dragon's exhalation? The breath of a volcano? Nothing so exalted. The steam carried the rich scents of the five pungent herbs—garlic, chives, and the like—straight to his nose. On the greasy stall, arranged in bamboo baskets, lay freshly steamed pork buns. Plump, soft, and white, their wrappers twisted to little points that spoke eloquently to the stomach. Step carelessly into that drifting steam and fragrance, and without even knowing when you had paid, you would be peeling away the thin wooden wrapper and biting. Only when hot juice burned your tongue would you come to yourself. Steam that worked skillfully upon the deeper mind. The stallholder knew this perfectly well and deliberately kept the baskets steaming lavishly. But—

source.japanese:
【露店店主】
「……なああんた、買わないんならさぁ、
　さっさとよそ行ってくれんかね？
　客でもねえのが突っ立ってられると、
　邪魔でしょうがねえんだが」
source.english:
“…Listen, if you're not buying, could you take yourself somewhere else?
A man who isn't even a customer standing there blocking the place is a damned nuisance.”

source.japanese: 先刻より街角の、二人も立ってしまえば一杯の露店の前を塞がれては、店主ならずとも苦りきるのが当然だ。
source.english: Sakuya had been blocking the street-corner stall for some time. Two people standing before it would fill its entire frontage. Anyone, not just the owner, would have been thoroughly annoyed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いいじゃあないかちょっとくらい。
　さっきから見てると客なんか来ないみたいだし」
source.english:
“A little while won't hurt. I've been watching,
and you don't seem to have any customers.”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「ああ？　なんか言ったか」
source.english: “What? You say something?”

source.japanese:
本人は街に擦れたいっぱしの露店商面で凄んだつもりでも、顔が海苔の佃煮の小瓶のラベルのポンチ絵とそっくりときては、渋面は威しの用には立たず、むしろ滑稽味さえ催させる次第で。
　とこうせっかく人格劇の役者としても充分通用しそうな、店主の声回しと顔芸なのに、朔屋ときたら馬耳東風介上の空、蒸籠からむらむら立ち籠める湯気に封筒を翳[かざ]すのに夢中で、亭主などろくに見ていやしない。
source.english:
The owner put on what he intended as the glare of a seasoned, streetwise vendor. Unfortunately, his face was the very image of the cartoon on a little jar of seaweed relish; no scowl upon it could threaten anyone, and might instead provoke laughter.
A pity, for his voice and facial work might otherwise have qualified him as a character actor. Sakuya, however, paid no attention at all. Deaf to the world, he was absorbed in holding an envelope over the billowing steam and scarcely looked at the man.

source.japanese: 言いつけられた仕事を大人しくこなすだけに留めればいいものを、朔屋は預けられた封書の中味に出歯亀根性抑えがたく、糊付けにされた封筒を開けてみようとしているのである。鋏を入れたり破ってしまったりでは盗み見が露呈してしまうので、封の糊[のり]は湯気で溶かす。人として足らないところばかりであるのに、こういう悪知恵ばかり心得ているのが小面憎い。
source.english: He should have simply done as instructed. Instead, unable to curb his snooping curiosity about the letter entrusted to him, he was trying to open its glued flap. Cutting or tearing it would expose the intrusion. Steam would dissolve the glue. Deficient in almost every human quality, yet versed in such petty cunning: irritating indeed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ん、ならこいつをもらうよ。お幾らだい」
source.english: “Hm. Then I'll have this. How much?”

source.japanese: 亭主の咎めだてに、数十年の脂が現世の柵のように頼もしく染みついてべとついた屋台の、売り物に手を伸ばしてみたのだって半ば無意識だし、籠に並んで福々しい中華饅頭を器用に避けて、小皿につけあわせの搾菜なのだから恐れ入る。よく漬かって香がきついのを噛みながらには、さしもの亭主も眉が下がって、情けない。
source.english: Even reaching for something on sale in response to the owner's scolding was half unconscious. Decades of grease clung reassuringly to the stall, sticky as worldly entanglements. Yet his hand deftly avoided the cheerfully plump buns in their baskets and went instead to the pickled mustard stem served as a garnish on a small plate. Astonishing. As he chewed the pungent, well-pickled stuff, even the owner looked crestfallen.

source.japanese:
【店主】
「なんだかなあこの若僧は。付け合わせ一抓み囓って『勘定』もなにもあるもんかね……」
source.english: “What's with this young fellow? ‘How much,’ for a pinch of garnish?”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「大体、吝嗇が鰻屋の香気聴いて菜にするてぇなら落語だが。蒸籠の湯気を借りるなんて聞いたことないよ」
source.english: “There's a rakugo story about the miser who eats his rice to the smell of grilled eel. But I've never heard of anyone borrowing steam from a steamer.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやあこうやって同期のにやけ野郎に届いたラブレター、中味よく覗いたもんよ」
source.english: “Oh, I used to open love letters sent to a smarmy classmate this way all the time.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ついでに中味エロ小説まがいに書き換えて、すり替えてやったりとかな」
source.english: “Sometimes I'd rewrite them like dirty novels and swap them in.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちなみにそいつは後で婦女暴行犯として捕まったわけだが。差出人の女の子と逢った時、ナニ血迷ってナニやらかしたもんだか」
source.english: “Incidentally, he got arrested for rape afterward. Met the girl who'd sent the letter and lost his head somehow. Who knows what he did.”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「兄さん、あんたひどいよ」
source.english: “Young man, you're awful.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いいんだよ、仲間内でやってた賭け麻雀に大負けしたからって、サツに密告るような卑怯者だったんだから」
source.english: “Served him right. He was the kind of coward who lost heavily at our gambling mahjong, then informed on us to the cops.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……おお開いたぜえ。
　どれどれ───」
source.english:
“…Oh, it's open.
Let's see—”

target.text: The thick curtain of steam wafting from the yoshizu clung to the young man's chest, damp and hot, before being carried away on a sudden gust of wind, leaving a coolness behind. Was it the breath of a dragon? Or perhaps a blazing mountain? Not at all, it was far more worldly: the steam was heady with garlic, chives, the fragrance of the five root spices tickling his nose, and lined up in the greasy bamboo baskets of the stalls, plump and full, white and soft, the wavy yet slightly angular shape of the skin eloquently whispering to the stomach, were steamed pork buns, Chinese dumplings fresh from the steamers. (TN: Yoshizu, written "葦簀", are screens of horizontal slats of reeds.)

Were you to carelessly be swept away by the smell and step forwards, it'd still remain unclear to you when exactly you'd even spent the money as you peeled off the kyougi wrapping and dug in, and you would undoubtedly only come to your senses once the hot juices had scalded your tongue; the owners of these stalls had truly come to understand well how to skillfully exploit the subconscious with this steam, and in accordance with that understanding, they'd come to steam their food in such grand, magnificent steaming baskets, however. (TN: Kyougi, written "経木", is a traditional Japanese wrapping material made from paper-thin shavings of wood.)

【Street stall owner】 「……Hey, you there, if you're not gonna buy anything, can you go somewhere else already? If somebody who isn't a customer just stands there taking up space, it's nothing but a damn nuisance to me.」

If a stall on the corner of a street, which could only accommodate two customers at a time, was blocked by some guy who had just been standing there for a good while now, it would only be natural for anyone, owner of the stall or not, to scowl in annoyance.
【Naomasa】 「Come on, there's no harm in me being here for a little bit, right? And far as I've been able to see, it doesn't look like any customers are stopping by here anyway.」
【Owner】 「Haaah? You say something?」

Even if the man himself seemed to be under the impression that he could threaten him with the grimace of an established stall owner, a tough guy familiar with the dealings of the town, his face was exceedingly similar to the cartoon man you'd see on the label of a small jar of nori tsukudani, hence his sour expression did not serve his intent to intimidate, but rather gave rise to a certain comicality. (TN: This is a reference to a jar of nori seaweed boiled down in soy from the brand Momoya, specifically the "ごはんですよ!" product, which features an old man called Norihei.)

Thus, despite the funny facial performance and intonations of the stall owner, the sort of personality that might be well suited for theatre, when it came to Sakuya, he was praying to deaf ears, for Sakuya's attention had already been taken by something else, the young man engrossed in holding up an envelope into the thick curtain of steam enveloping the steaming baskets, barely paying the owner's antics any attention.

He could and should have just obediently carried out the work in the way he'd been instructed to, but Sakuya could not suppress his natural desire to peek on the contents of the sealed letter he had been entrusted with, now attempting to open the envelope sealed shut with glue. If he used a pair of scissors or tore it apart, the damage would betray his prying, so he instead opted to dissolve the glue with steam. It is quite detestable that someone so fundamentally lacking in character should be so well-versed in only these sorts of devious tricks.
【Naomasa】 「Hm, then I'll have one of those. How much?」

The owner kept carping at him, so he unconsciously reached out for one of the products placed on the stall, the surface of which was stained in decades of reassuringly ingrained grease clinging to it like the inescapable fetters of the material world, with his hand and adroitly avoided the plump rows of Chinese dumplings in the basket, instead landing on a little plate garnished with Szechuan pickles, what truly impressive work. While he chewed down on something deeply fermented with a pungent, biting aroma, even the owner's face lost its edge, now crestfallen, pitiable.
【Owner】 「What is wrong with this youngster? What kind of bill am I supposed to give to somebody who barely had a nibble of the side dish……」

【Owner】 「To begin with, if some stingy cheapskate was lured in by the aroma coming from a dumpling stand only to ask for vegetables instead, that's something you might see in Rakugo, but this? I have never in my life heard of somebody wanting to borrow the steam from the steaming baskets.」
【Naomasa】 「Well, I'd often peek at the contents of the love letters delivered to some smug, smirking bastard I shared a class with this way.」
【Naomasa】 「And as I did, maybe I might have rewritten the contents to be like something out of a smut novel, and then maybe switched it out.」
【Naomasa】 「Incidentally, later, this man was arrested for rape. When he met the woman who sent the letters, it seems like he lost control of himself and committed some kind of horrible mistake.」
【Owner】 「Brother, you are a cruel man.」
【Naomasa】 「It's no big deal. He was the kind of rat who'd snitch to the police, and all because he lost big while doing some private mahjong gambling with friends.」
【Naomasa】 「……Ooh, it's open. Let's see───」

source.japanese: 入っていたのは、端で破られた政府の臨時発行印紙一枚。それのみ。貨幣としては最低の価値しかない。ただその破れ目に何事か赤印の割り印が。
source.english: Inside was a single stamp from a temporary government issue, torn along one edge. Nothing else. As currency it had only the lowest value. But along the tear was part of some red seal stamped across it.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（なんだぁこりゃ）
source.english: (What's this?)

source.japanese: 何らかの書類ならともかく、半切れの印紙のみでは当てずっぽうもならず、困惑する朔屋を横目にして、店主は街路の向こうへ視線を流した。
source.english: A document might have given him something to guess at. Half a stamp gave him nothing. As Sakuya puzzled over it, the owner glanced past him, across the street.

source.japanese:
【店主】
「まあなんだっていいんだけどさ。
　あんたいいのかい、あの白子の餓鬼、
　あんたの連れじゃないのかい？」
source.english:
“Whatever.
But are you sure about that albino kid?
Isn't she with you?”

source.japanese: 見れば朔屋について下船してきたクロが、通りかかったチンドン屋の賑々しいのにふらふらとついて行ってしまったところ。
source.english: He looked. Kuro, who had come ashore with him, was drifting off after a passing advertising band's noisy street procession.

target.text: Inside was a single provisional government-issued revenue stamp torn at the edge. That was all. As a form of currency, it held the lowest value possible. However, across that tear, some manner of red tally seal had been struck.
【Naomasa】 （What the hell is this?）

It'd be one thing if it was some sort of document, but all he had was shots in the dark with half a piece of a revenue stamp, and with a sidelong glance at the bewildered Sakuya, the stall owner then cast his gaze across the street.
【Owner】 「Well, not that it's any skin off my nose or anything. But are you fine with what's happening with her, that albino brat. Isn't she with you?」

When he looked, Sakuya noticed that Kuro, who'd disembarked together with him, had been captivated by the gaiety of a band of elaborately costumed Chindonya as they marched away, whimsically following them on unsteady feet. (TN: Chindonya, written "チンドン屋" here, also known as Japanese marching bands, are a type of elaborately costumed street musicians who advertise for shops and establishments through their performances. They have a somewhat untrustworthy image, having been used to advertise gambling and black markets in the past.)

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「わあ、なんか楽しそう、面白そう。
　どこ行くのかな、なんかのお祭りかな。
　クロに教えて」
source.english:
“Wow, that looks fun. Interesting.
Where are they going? Is it some festival?
Tell Kuro.”

source.japanese: 後先もなく、警戒もまるでなく、ハーメルンのネズミ取りに連れ去られていく子供のように遠ざかるクロを、朔屋、慌てて追いかけて襟首掴んで引き留めた。
source.english: Utterly heedless and without a scrap of caution, Kuro wandered farther and farther away like one of the children lured off by the Pied Piper of Hamelin. Sakuya dashed after her and caught her by the collar.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああもう、ちょっとでも目を離しゃすぐこれだ。
　なんだってお前さんをつけてよこしたかな」
source.english:
“Oh, for crying out loud. Look away for a moment and there you go.
Why'd they send you along?”

source.japanese:
せっかく久しぶりの陸に降りて、あわよくば尻に帆掛けてとんずらのつもりの朔屋だったのに───
　何故かクロも共に付けられているとあっては。
　なんだって彼女がついてくるのか。朔屋が逃げてしまわないようにお目付役なのか。だとしても到底まともにこなせるとは思えないのだが。
　あるいは朔屋に対しての厭がらせ、なのだろうか。
　クロを連れて歩けば、要らぬ気疲れを強いられるのは間違いない。だが、本気でクロを見失ってそれっきり、という事だって充分にあり得る。
　いなくなっても構わない、そういう扱いという事かと、朔屋は、そぞろ哀れを催して軽くクロの頭を掌でぽんぽんぽん、愛叩してやろうとしたのに。
source.english:
He had finally got ashore after so long, intending to flee at the slightest opportunity. Yet for some reason Kuro had been sent with him.
Why was she here? To watch him and prevent his escape? She hardly seemed capable of doing that properly.
Or was this harassment?
Walking around with her would undoubtedly exhaust him with unnecessary worry. But it was quite possible he might genuinely lose her and never see her again.
Did that mean they did not care if she disappeared? A little pity stirred him. He tried to give her head a few light, affectionate pats. But—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Waah, looks kinda fun, interesting. Wonder where they're going, maybe some kinda festival? Tell Kuro, tell Kuro!」

No thought spared for the consequences, with practically no caution in her heart, Kuro grew more and more distant, like a little child being abducted by the Rat-Catcher from Hameln, and Sakuya caught up to her in a fluster, then grabbed her by the collar to stop her.
【Naomasa】 「Oh come on, I take my eyes off you for a second and this is what happens. Of all the people they could have sent along, why did it have to be you?」

It had been a good while since Sakuya had gone ashore last, and if circumstances permitted it, he had hoped to turn tail and make good his escape, and yet─── For some reason, Kuro had to come with him. Why did she have to come? Was she meant to keep an eye on Sakuya so he didn't try to escape? If so, then it was impossible to believe that she was doing a very good job of that. Or maybe this could be harassment aimed at him. Wasn't that possible?

As he walked around with Kuro in tow, there was no mistaking that it imposed an unnecessary mental burden on him. But, it was also plenty possible that if he truly lost sight of Kuro here, she'd never be seen again. It seemed like they didn't care if she disappeared, that was how they treated her: for some reason, that made Sakuya feel some pity, and so he lightly patted Kuro on the head with the palm of his hand, just trying to give her a little love-tap, and yet.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ご、ごめっ、なぁさい……っ。
　もうしません、しないです、から。
　クロをぶたないで───」
source.english:
“S-sorry… I'm sorry…
I won't do it again, I won't,
so… Don't hit Kuro—”

source.japanese: 白子の少女はひっと身を竦めて上目遣いの、浮かべてみせた笑みに、阿るような遜るような卑屈が滲んで、扱いに困り果てる朔屋だった。
source.english: The albino girl gave a little gasp and shrank away, peering up at him. The smile she summoned was steeped in such cringing, fawning abasement that Sakuya was utterly at a loss as to what to do with her.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「S-, so-, rry……. Won't do it again, Kuro won't, so. Please don't hit Kuro───」

The albino girl flinched, shrinking back from him and looking up through her lashes, the smile pulled over her face oozing with flattery and self-abasing grovelling; Sakuya was at a complete loss for how to deal with her.

source.japanese: 夜闇が濃くなりまさるにつれ、港に通う風は足を緩めて滞留し、潮風に散らされる事なく、夜気に重油の匂いが蟠る。湾に突きだした堤防の先にて燈台がぐるぐると、回す一つ目の灯火は海上の残照の中ではまだ道化めいて白けているが、直に夜航の船の心強い導き手となろう。夜番を運良く免れた水夫は、ロッカーに隠しておいた上陸用の糊[のり]の利いた襯衣に袖[そで]を通し、筋や骨を軋ませる、一日の苦役の疲労を港湾労働者達は肩を回して散らしながら、それぞれのお定まりの飯屋や酒場目指して街方へと流れていく。
source.english: As darkness deepened, the wind crossing the port slowed and lingered. Without the sea breeze to disperse it, the smell of heavy oil coiled in the night air. At the end of a breakwater projecting into the bay, a lighthouse turned its single eye round and round. Against the last light on the sea, it still looked foolish and ineffectual. Soon it would become a reassuring guide to ships sailing at night. Sailors lucky enough to avoid the night watch slipped into starched shore-going shirts hidden in their lockers. Dockworkers rolled their shoulders to dispel a day's fatigue, muscles and bones creaking. Each drifted toward the streets and his usual eating house or tavern.

target.text: As the dark of night deepened, so did the wind blowing through the port also abate in turn, stagnating, and no longer dispersed by the salty gusts, the stench of heavy fuel oil coiled around the night air. A lighthouse revolved at the end of the breakwater jutting out into the bay, the light of the first rotation almost comically subdued in the afterglow of the sea, but soon enough, it would surely make a reassuring guide for any night-faring vessels.

A sailor fortunate enough to escape the night watch stuck his arms through the sleeves of a nicely starched shirt for use on land that he'd hidden away in his locker, and the muscles and bones of the stevedores creaked as they rotated their shoulders to relieve the fatigue of a day of hard labour, all streaming towards the main street as they made their way to the eating houses or bars they frequented.

source.japanese: 船から港へ、港から街路へ、移動していく喧噪に逆らって人気の失せつつある港湾倉庫群を目指す二人がある。流れに逆行して、というて木の間を躱す燕のように、とは軽敏にいかない。撞球台に放たれた持ち玉よろしくあちらの荒くれにぶつかっては手荒に弾き飛ばされ、こちらの無頼の前によろばいでては跳ね返されてと、撲ち身の一つ二つこさえながら、それでも二人は遅れを取り戻そうとの必死さ滲む。正確には、連れの一方ばかりが焦っていたのであるが。
source.english:
Against the tide of clamor flowing from ships to port and port to streets, two figures made for the warehouses as they emptied of people. They did not slip against that current with the lightness of swallows threading trees. No: like a cue ball loosed upon a billiard table, they struck one roughneck and went caroming away, staggered before another and were knocked back again. Bruised once or twice, they still struggled desperately to make up the lost time.
Strictly speaking, only one of them was desperate.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まずいなぁ……すっかり暗くなっちまった。
　クロぉ、お前がもたもたしてるからだぜ」
source.english:
“This is bad… It's completely dark.
Kuro, it's because you keep dawdling.”

target.text: From ships to the port, from the port to the streets. There were two who defied the tumult of this migrating flock, making their way to the cluster of increasingly deserted warehouses down by the port.

They went against the stream, but it was nothing like a swallow flitting between the trees, nothing so quick and nimble. Like a cue ball launched across a billiard table, they collided with the rowdies over there, were roughly knocked aside, stumbled in front of the scoundrels over here, only to be sent flying back whence they came, but even with a bruise or two to show for it, their desperation to recover lost time still shone through. To be more precise, only one half of this group was in any kind of hurry.
【Naomasa】 「This is baaad……it's pitch black already. Kuro, this is all because you're dawdling.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だって、サアカスだったもの。
　きょういの、ええと……千里、眼と、
　しじょう最高の、軽業って。
　いた、いたい、引っぱっちゃやぁ」
source.english:
“But it was a circus.
Amazing, um… clair… voyance,
and the greatest acrobatics ever.
Ow, ow, don't pull…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「何がサアカスなもんだかな。
　お前なんぞそんなとこのこのこ首突っこんだらたちまち攫[さら]われる」
source.english:
“What circus?
Poke your nose into a place like that and they'll carry you off straightaway.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「奥羽山中の『六尺のオオイタチ（大板血）』とか、ブルネイ渡りの『毛達磨男』に混じって、親の因果が子に報いの『白子娘』でござぁいと、たちまち丸盆前座にされちまうのがオチだぁ。
　……ああすいませんね、こいつ、ちっとばかりとろいもんで」
source.english:
“With the ‘Six-Foot Giant Weasel’ from the Ou mountains—a big board stained with blood—and the ‘Hairy Human Ball’ from Borneo, it'll be ‘Behold the albino girl, her parents' sins visited upon their child!’ They'll have you on a round sideshow stage as the opening act before you know it.
…Oh, excuse us. She's a bit slow.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But there was a circus. The miraculous, uhmm…… second sight, and history's greatest, most daring acrobatics, it said. Ow, oww, don't pull.」
【Naomasa】 「Can you really call that a circus? If someone like you brazenly poked your nose in there, you'd be kidnapped in the blink of an eye.】

【Naomasa】 「You'd be lumped in with the 『Six-Shaku Giant Weasel』from the Oou mountains, or the『Hairy Daruma Man』 hailing all the way from Borneo.」 (TN: The weasel originates from a rakugo story, 夜店風景, lit. "sights at a night fair", with the jokes revolving around scams. The setup of the final joke is that giant weasel is pronounced "Ooitachi" in Japanese, the same as "大板血", meaning a large board smeared in blood. "毛達磨男", lit. "hairy Daruma Man", is a daring synthesis of the Wild Men of Borneo and Daruma Man. Starting in 1765, Daruma Man was named so because he had no legs, performing acrobatic acts with his arms alone.)

【Naomasa】 「“And here comes the『Albino Girl』 suffering karmic retribution for her parents' misdeeds!". You'd immediately be put on a big, round tray as the opening act, that's the only fate awaiting you there. ……Aah, my apologies, this girl here's a bit slow in the head.」

source.japanese:
今もどんと肩ぶっつけ合った港男達に、いい加減な詫び文句で割って入ってクロを背に隠す。
　白子の娘の、乳白の髪、肌と血凝りのような目の色は夜目にも悪目立ちして、歩みを遮[さえぎ]られた港男達の奇異の眼差しが、クロの哀れな様子に嗜虐催し意地悪な悪戯を企んで歪みかねないその前に、と乱暴に手を引いて引き離しつ、朔屋のぼやきはいささか責任転嫁の。
source.english:
They had just collided shoulder-first with another knot of harbor men. Sakuya offered a perfunctory apology, stepped between them, and hid Kuro behind his back.
Her milk-white hair and skin and blood-clot eyes stood out even in the dark. Before the strange looks of the men whose way they had blocked could twist at her pitiful appearance into sadistic mischief, Sakuya seized her hand and dragged her away. His complaint was, to put it mildly, an exercise in shifting blame.

source.japanese:
チンドン屋についていった後で、町外れの曲馬団の呼びこみに、ふらふら引かれていって迷子になりかけたのはクロであるが、朔屋だって道中で見かけた豊満美女に、一時の火遊びを気取ってかき口説いたりで寄り道した。
　乳と尻ばかりに栄養がいったような女が地回りの情婦とかで、小指の欠けて刺青もんもんの腕で絞め殺そうになったところをほうほうの態で逃げ延びたという時間喰らいの顛末もあったり、まったくクロを笑えぬ穀潰しな。
source.english:
Kuro was the one who had followed the advertising band, then drifted after a circus barker on the outskirts and nearly got lost. But Sakuya too had dawdled along the way, stopping to sweet-talk a voluptuous beauty into what he fancied a casual fling.
The woman—built as if every scrap of nourishment had gone straight to her tits and ass—turned out to be a local tough’s mistress, and the local tough, one pinky missing and his arms dense with tattoos, very nearly strangled Sakuya. Escaping by the skin of his teeth had eaten up its share of time as well. The useless parasite was in no position to laugh at Kuro.

target.text: Even now, he still stepped in, offering a half-hearted apology to the longshoremen Kuro bumped shoulders with while hiding her behind his back. This albino girl's milky-white hair and skin, as well as her eyes a colour like congealed blood, were conspicuous, even in the dark of night, and it wasn't hard to imagine that the strange looks from the longshoremen whose walking had been obstructed could twist into conjuring up malicious tricks out of some form of sadism aroused in them by witnessing Kuro's pitiful state of being, so before that could happen, Sakuya violently pulled her away, but his grumbling was him shifting the blame a little bit.

While it was true that Kuro, after following the Chindonya, had been on the verge of becoming a lost child once more as she tottered after a barker from a circus on the outskirts of town, Sakuya also took a detour, for he caught sight of a voluptuous beauty on the way, then tried pretentiously flirting with her in his desire for a brief aventure.

This woman, for whom any nutrition seemed to have only gone to her ass and tits, was the mistress of a local gangster or something, so when he was moments away from being strangled to death by an arm covered in a full sleeve of tattoos and missing a little finger, he scrambled to make his escape, ultimately wasting a lot of time: a truly useless parasite in no position to make fun of Kuro.

source.japanese: こうして朔屋達が指定の倉庫に辿り着いた時は、かく益体のない寄り道回り道で時間を食いつぶし、刻限を時計一巡りほども遅れた頃であったとか。朔屋は倉庫に駆けずりこむ前に、小賢しくも髪を鳥の巣にかき回し服のあちこち乱し港の油混じりの土埃塗りたくって『さっき、通関の檻から逃げ出した大食蟻獣に襲われてしまい必死に逃げ出して来たのでまことに遺憾ながら遅れてしまいました』の風を装ったところ、取引相手から怒りを通り越した、犬の糞にたかる蝿でも見るような目線を送られ、小芝居も完膚無きまで無視されたという。
source.english: By the time they reached the designated warehouse, such pointless detours had wasted enough time to make them a whole turn of the clock behind schedule, or so the story goes. Before rushing inside, Sakuya cunningly tousled his hair into a bird's nest, disordered his clothes, and smeared himself with the port's oily dirt. His performance suggested: ‘A giant anteater escaped from its customs cage and attacked me. I fled desperately, so regrettably I am late.’ His counterpart's look, however, had gone beyond anger. It was the look one gives flies swarming on dog shit. The little performance was utterly ignored.

source.japanese:
大体朔屋も始めから、相手を見て冗談が通じるような相手かどうか悟るべき。がらんと積み荷も乏しいのに薄汚れて荒廃の気色濃い倉庫の中で、その男だけは塵一つ被っていなかった。それも自分で払うのではなく、奴隷の躾[しつけ]叩きこんだメイド任せに羽根箒で浄めさせる手合いで、白く眩しいマオカラーで上下隆と揃え、糸くず一つさえ見えないくらいにブラシのしっかりかかって、仕立てもよろしく袖[そで]から肩口を思いきり引っぱっても、すぐに皺一つなく戻るであろう。
　面差しはそれなりに整っていたけれど、搾取に慣れた者に特有の傲慢が目に溜まる。ただその支配相は代々の青い血に篆刻されたものではないとは見えて、人を不快にさせる、卑しくにやけ加減で口角が歪む。さして観相術の心得を持ち合わせない朔屋にも容易く察せられる、こいつは───成金だ。
source.english:
Sakuya ought to have known at a glance whether this was a man likely to appreciate a joke. The warehouse was filthy and desolate despite its emptiness and scant cargo; the man alone bore not a speck of dust. Nor was he the sort to brush it off himself. That work he left to a maid disciplined into slavery, who purified him with a feather duster. His dazzling white mandarin-collar suit matched perfectly from coat to trousers, had been brushed free of the smallest thread, and was so finely tailored that one could wrench sleeve or shoulder without leaving a wrinkle.
His features were handsome enough, but his eyes held the arrogance peculiar to men long accustomed to exploitation. This was not the authority engraved by generations of blue blood: a base, smirking twist at the corners of his mouth made the distinction unpleasantly clear. Even Sakuya, no student of physiognomy, could read the truth with ease. The man was—new money.

source.japanese: だからといって舐めて居丈高に掛かれる相手ではない事を言葉を交わす前に感じ取ったのは、朔屋にしてからが権勢に弱く強きにへつらう軟弱者であったから。たとい先代かそこらで歩がひっくり返ったような金満であろうと金の力の灼かなること言うまでもないし、何よりその成金……おほん、そのぽっと出のお大尽……もとい、富豪の両脇には、矜羯羅・制多迦の両童子の如く、屈強な男二人が固めていたからである。ダークスーツにボルサリーノ、灰色の襯衣に青のタイは見ようによっては粋と言えたが、コミニュケーションと言えば言語より暴力を重視すること間違いなしの粗暴で野卑な面相からして、下品なチンピラ、という枠からは外れない……なにが不動の脇侍どころか、地獄の獄卒、牛頭馬頭がいいところ。
source.english: Yet even before they exchanged words, he sensed this was no one to treat with contempt or bluster. Sakuya himself was a weakling before power, cringing toward the strong. Even if a pawn had been promoted into this wealth only in the previous generation, money's force was undeniable. Above all, on either side of the upstart—hem, the suddenly prosperous grandee—rather, the wealthy gentleman—stood two powerful men, guarding him like Kongara and Seitaka. Dark suits and Borsalino hats; gray shirts and blue ties. Seen one way, they might have been stylish. But their crude, brutal faces left no doubt that they preferred violence to language as a means of communication. They never escaped the category of vulgar hoodlum. Fudo's attendants? Hardly. Hell's Ox-Head and Horse-Face were closer.

source.japanese: どれだけ身なりよろしく整えたところで、やはりというか所詮というか、海の厄介者信天翁号の取引相手にはお差し合いの、これは、やくざ者かギャングの類だ、根本を、信天翁号の面々が日頃からシノギを見苦しく奪い合っている外道と同じところに置いている。
source.english: However fine their clothes, they were, after all, fitting partners for that maritime nuisance the Albatross. Yakuza, gangsters, or something of the kind: their roots lay in the same soil as the scoundrels with whom the Albatross crew fought so sordidly over its rackets.

source.japanese:
【白スーツの金持ち】
「遅いな。いい歳をして使いもまともに出来ないような役立たずを寄越すあたり、お前の船の面子も底が知れる」
source.english: “You're late. Sending a useless fellow who can't run an errand properly at his age tells me all I need to know about your ship's company.”
source.speakerEn: Rich Man in a White Suit

source.japanese:
【白スーツの金持ち】
「いや……あの信天翁号にまともな『商取引』を期待する方が酷、か。どれだけ粋がったところで、所詮は居場所もない愚連隊もどきだからな、信天翁の奴らは。噂通りだな───」
source.english: “No… Perhaps expecting a proper ‘business transaction’ from the Albatross is itself unfair. Whatever airs they put on, they're merely a gang of delinquents with nowhere to belong. Just as the rumors say—”
source.speakerEn: Rich Man in a White Suit

source.japanese: 駆け足の、荒い息を押さえようとする朔屋をさも見苦しげに一瞥し、居丈高に言い放ってから口元に宛がった飾り入りの手巾で語尾が曇った、罵倒の文句には苛立ちと怒りが見やすい。普段から、埃と悪臭の籠もるがままに放置された廃倉庫に尊大なる身を待たされた事に対しての不快の念だろうが、それだけではないと朔屋は不審を覚[おぼ]ゆる。怒りに尖る眼差しには滑るような油光りも入り交じり、それは恐らくは渇望の心。こういう手合いは相手を下と認識すれば、目を合わせるどころか洟[はな]も引っかけない傲慢さを示すものだが、この男、どうにも目の端でちらちらと朔屋達に欲色の視線をよこしてきているのだ。
source.english: He cast a disgusted glance at Sakuya, who was still trying to master his ragged breath, then delivered his abuse from on high. The last words blurred behind the embroidered handkerchief he raised to his mouth. His irritation was plain enough: he had been made to wait in an abandoned warehouse left thick with dust and stench. Yet Sakuya sensed that this was not all. An oily gleam slid beneath the anger in the man's eyes—the gleam of appetite. Men like him, once they had judged another person beneath them, ordinarily refused even to meet that person's gaze. This one kept stealing glances at Sakuya's party from the corners of his eyes. Glances colored unmistakably by lust.

source.japanese:
ははぁん奴さん、こう豪くお冠なのも、実のところこの取引とやらに余程ご執心だったからと見える───とそう、つけいる隙になりそうなと見るや目端が利いてくるあたり、朔屋も中途半端に狭っ辛い。
　もちろんそんな得心はおくびにも出さず、なにしろお大尽自体は朔屋と似たり寄ったりな線の細さではあるとはいえ、両脇に控えた手下が恐ろしい、差し出口は呑みこんだ。ただでさえ船の上では余計な一言多くして、吊されたり絞められたり畳まれたりしている彼である。
source.english:
Aha. Perhaps he was so furious because he badly wanted whatever this deal offered. The moment Sakuya saw a possible opening, his eyes grew sharp. He possessed a half-baked cunning of his own.
Of course, he betrayed none of that understanding. The grandee himself was thinly built, much like Sakuya, but the men attending him were frightening. He swallowed his unnecessary remarks. On the ship, too, one word too many was forever getting him strung up, throttled, or folded in half.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやその、ホントすんません。
　来る途中で色々ありまして。
　で、それで僕は、何をすればいいんでしょうか」
source.english:
“No, um, I'm really sorry.
Various things happened on the way.
So, what am I supposed to do?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんしろ僕は、ただここで貴方がたに会ってこいと、それしか言われてないもんでして」
source.english: “All I was told was to come here and meet you.”

source.japanese: 殊更阿呆を装うまでもなく、朔屋は本当にそれだけの指示しか受け取っておらず、こんな裏ぶれた事この上ない倉庫でなにをしようというのか、見当もつかないのだ。朔屋が預かった物は例の封書の一つのみ、向こうだって空手で、倉庫には取引に供するような荷らしい物は見当たらない。それどころか倉庫は床にかつての荷箱の痕と思しい線を寒々しく残して寂しく広く、往時は満載になった事もあろうし、立ち働く人足の出入りに忙しなかった有り様が忍ばれるだけに、現在の侘びしさと言ったらなかった。荒れているのは信天翁号も同じだが、あちらは開き直ったようなふてぶてしささえ漂わせているのに、この倉庫と来たら、巨大な髑髏の歯欠け落ちた口腔に立ったような嘘寒ささえ感じさせるでないか。
source.english: He need not especially pretend to be a fool. Those really were all the instructions he had received, and he could not imagine what they meant to do in this supremely run-down warehouse. He had only the one envelope. The other party was empty-handed, too. No cargo suitable for a transaction was in sight. Indeed, the floor retained only forlorn outlines where crates had once stood, leaving a cold, lonely expanse. One could imagine the old days, filled with goods and busy with laborers coming and going. That made the present desolation all the worse. The Albatross was equally decrepit, but she possessed a brazen air of having embraced it. This warehouse made him feel the eerie chill of standing in the toothless mouth of a gigantic skull.

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「本当に子供の使いと同じだなお前は。
　……まあいい。書類を預かってるだろう」
source.english:
“You really are no better than a child sent on an errand.
Never mind. You have some papers, don't you?”

target.text: Thus, by the time Sakuya and Kuro arrived at the designated warehouse, having wasted time with such pointless detours and diversions, they were about a full revolution of the minute hand past the appointed time.

Before Sakuya bolted into the warehouse, he cheekily ruffled his hair around so it looked like a bird's nest, rumpled his clothing here and there, and finally smeared some of the dust mixed with oil from the port on himself, dressing up as if to say 『Just earlier, I was assaulted by a giant anteater that had escaped from customs, and I was desperately trying to escape that thing all the way here, so while it is very regrettable, I am unfortunately late.』, but the other party must have been exceedingly angry, for he looked at him like he were a fly swarming around dog shit, his theatrics also completely and utterly ignored.

In the first place, as soon as Sakuya saw the other party, he ought to have discerned if he was the kind of man whom his jokes would land with. There he stood, in this deserted warehouse with barely any cargo to speak of, slightly dirty and thick in signs of decay and waste, and yet this man alone was covered not in a speck of dust.

And it was not the man himself who had wiped it off, it was like it had been cleaned with a feather brush by maids who had been beaten into slavish obedience; he was dressed smartly from top to bottom, with a dazzlingly white Mao collar shirt so painstakingly brushed that not a single piece of lint could be seen, the outfit well-tailored; no matter where you yanked on it, from the sleeves to the collar, it would surely immediately return to its original shape with not a single wrinkle to mar it.

His facial features were also quite well-proportioned, but the arrogance particular to those long accustomed to exploiting others was heavy in his eyes. Yet that air of dominance on his features did not look to be the sort carved into a man's visage through generations of blue blood, and the corners of his mouth were twisted into a smirk, one just vulgar enough to leave others ill at ease. Even Sakuya, who was not particularly well-versed in the science of physiognomy, could easily sense it: this man─── was nouveau riche.

But with all that said, that he had perceived this man to not be one he should underestimate, not be one he should act all high and mighty with, and all before exchanging any words with him, was because Sakuya was a craven toady who cowered before power and fawned over the strong.

Even if his wealth was of the pawn-turned-gold-general variety from a mere generation ago, the vivid brilliance of the manifest power of money is, of course, beyond dispute, but most of all, it was because, on either side of this nouveau riche……ahem, this inexperienced parvenu……er, rather, this wealthy millionaire, like the twin boys Kongara and Seitaka, stood two burly bodyguards. (TN: The term for new money in Japan, written "成金", originally meant a shogi piece promoted to gold general, hence the shogi talk. Kongara and Seitaka, written "矜羯羅" and "制多迦", are the two acolytes of Fudou Myou-ou, the Japanese name for Acala.)

Dark suits with borsalinos, blue ties over grey shirts: based on looks alone, they certainly cut a stylish figure, but in terms of what they were communicating with their rough, coarse countenances, which seemed the sort to prioritize violence over words, they couldn't quite escape being categorized as vulgar underlings…… but they were a far sight from the acolytes standing by the side of Fudou; more accurately, they were like the guardians of the underworld, Gozu and Mezu, the Ox-head and Horse-face.

No matter how well they dressed or groomed, as one might expect, when all was said and done, given they had dealings with the scourge of the seas, the Albatross, they could only be fittingly dubious in turn, so they must have been some sort of gangsters; at their core, they were cut from the same cloth as the rest of those degenerates that the crew of the Albatross would habitually contend with, making an unsightly spectacle as they scrambled for their piece of the racket.

【Rich guy in white suit】 「You're late. If they're sending someone so useless that, despite being a grown man, they're incapable of performing even a simple errand, then that says all I need to know about the crew of your ship.」

【Rich guy in white suit】 「No……expecting any proper "business dealings" out of the Albatross would be cruel, yes? No matter how you may put on airs, you are but a pack of pseudo-thugs with no place to call home, you riff-raff from the Albatross. Just as rumoured───」

He threw a contemptuous glance Sakuya's way as though genuinely disgusted at the sight of him trying to calm his heavy breathing from all the running, and after speaking haughtily, he then covered his mouth with a trimmed handkerchief, the end of his final sentence trailing off; the disparaging remarks easily betrayed his frustration and anger. Ordinarily, it would like stem from a sense of displeasure that his pompous, important self was made to wait in this abandoned warehouse pungent with dust and other foul smells, but Sakuya harboured a suspicion that this was not all it was.

The look in his eyes, sharp with anger, was also covered in a slippery, greasy sheen, and that most likely stemmed from a desperate craving for something. This sort, once they deemed another as below them, would not only refuse eye contact, but ignore them entirely in a display of arrogance, and yet this man was instead glancing repeatedly from the corner of his eye at Sakuya and Kuro, his eyes hazy with lust.

Aha, buddy, you're sure in a terribly bad mood, but it looks to me like that's all because you're actually very attached to our little deal here─── if he were quick-witted and sensible enough to say something along those lines, then it appeared there was a weakness ripe for the exploitation, but Sakuya's slyness was a half-baked thing.

Of course, he showed no outward signs of any such understanding, for you see, though the rich man himself, much like Sakuya, seemed slender and frail, the henchmen flanking him were terrifying, and so he refrained from making any impertinent remarks. And this was the man who was hung up, strangled, and folded up because he always made one clever remark too many on the ship.
【Naomasa】 「No, uhh, I really am sorry. A lot of stuff happened on the way here. So then, now that I'm here, what exactly should I be doing?」
【Naomasa】 「You see, all I was told is that I had to go and meet you here. Nothing else.」

He wasn't intentionally playing stupid, Sakuya truly had only been given that directive; what was he even supposed to be doing in this dilapidated warehouse? He couldn't come up with an answer to that. All Sakuya had been entrusted with was the aforementioned sealed letter, the other party was empty-handed too, and he couldn't spot any cargo in the warehouse that could be offered up for a deal of some sort.

On the contrary, there were lines that looked to be the trails left by the boxes that used to be on the floor of this warehouse, gloomily leaving nothing but a lonesome vastness behind; in bygone times, this place was probably packed, and while the business of all the workers running to and fro and in and out would likely be hard to put up with, the miserably wretched state in the present was beyond compare. The Albatross was also dilapidated, but while the Albatross exuded a defiant, almost brazen attitude, did this warehouse not instead give off a chilling, unsettling feeling, like he were standing in the mouth of a giant skull whose teeth had fallen out?
【Rich guy】 「You really are no different from an errand boy, are you? ……So be it. I should hope you were entrusted with a document.」

source.japanese: 手下の一人に顎で示して朔屋へと差し向ける、どすどすと本人は威圧のつもりか、下品なまでに磨き上げたエナメルの靴で汚れた足元わざわざ音高く、鳴らして寄ってきたで案の定埃が舞い上がって、煙幕じみた霞に裸電球の光線がサーチライトの光条じみる。もとよりその書類しか持ち合わせていない朔屋は、鼻腔を犯す埃の粒子に閉口し、内心で毒づきながら手渡す封書の、ただ預かってきただけ、中味に興味など鼻糞ほどもないとあっさりと（封は糊[のり]に唾して閉じ直してあった）。
source.english: A jerk of the chin sent one henchman toward him. Perhaps intending intimidation, the fellow loudly stamped through the dirt in patent-leather shoes polished to vulgar brilliance. Predictably, dust rose. In the smoke-screen haze, rays from the naked bulbs looked like searchlight beams. Sakuya had nothing but the document in any case. Irritated by the dust invading his nose, he cursed inwardly and casually handed over the envelope. Merely entrusted with it; not a speck of interest in its contents. He had spat on the glue and resealed it.

target.text: He gestured to one of his henchmen with his chin and sent him towards Sakuya, but while the noisy footfalls were likely intended to be an intimidating display by the man himself, he was stomping down so hard on the filthy floor, all to deliberately make his footsteps ring out louder, in his patent leather shoes, which were polished to such a shine that it bordered on vulgarity, that, as he noisily drew closer, just as one might expect, the dust whirled up in the air, and the beams of light from the naked bulb above almost looked like the rays of a searchlight through the dimness of the smokescreen.

Sakuya, who had nothing on his person but the document, closed his mouth as the particles of dust ravaged his nostrils, cursing them bitterly in his mind as he handed over the sealed letter; he didn't give a damn about the contents of that letter, so it was handed over without any fuss (he had resealed the letter by softening the glue with his spit).

source.japanese:
【手下】
「旦那、こちらです」
source.english: “Here it is, sir.”

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「ああ」
source.english: “Yes.”

target.text: 【Henchman】 「Here it is, boss.」
【Rich man】 「Good.」

source.japanese: 鷹揚に受け取って、葉巻の端切り用のナイフを内ポケットからぱちり、封を切る手は大人を気取っていかにもな勿体つけを、装って、微妙な焦りが浮いてやしないか。それのみならず、やはりこちらを覗き見しているようなが朔屋の気にかかる。というよりその目線が捕らえているのは───クロ？
source.english: He accepted the envelope with a magnanimous air, snapped a cigar cutter from his inner pocket, and slit the seal. Every motion affected the ponderous ceremony of a man playing at adulthood—yet was there not a trace of haste beneath it? More troubling still, he continued to steal glances at them. Or rather, what his eyes had fixed upon was—Kuro?

source.japanese:
先程からやけに大人しい。街中でもこうだったらなんの苦労もないのに、この小娘、あれは俺を困らせようと思ってか、嫌がらせかと逆捩じの朔屋、あのお大尽も一体こんな貧相な小娘に何を見ているのだと、倉庫に入ってからようやく初めてクロに目を向けたのだが。
　肩が細かく震えていた。
　顔が、藁半紙でも丸めたようにそれはそれはくしゃくしゃに崩れていた。
source.english:
She had been remarkably quiet. Had she behaved like this in town, there would have been no trouble. Had all that been deliberate, to annoy him? Sakuya twisted matters perversely. What did the grandee see in such a miserable little girl? For the first time since entering the warehouse, he turned his eyes to her.
Her shoulders trembled minutely.
Her face was crumpled, utterly crumpled, like balled-up pulp paper.

source.japanese: 胡椒を叩きつけられた狆だってこうはいかないとぎょっとして、思わず一歩下がった朔屋の前でクロは、遂に臨界を超えて、身が二つ折りになった、白髪が舞い踊る、弾けた音が───
source.english: Not even a Japanese chin pelted with pepper could have managed that. Startled, Sakuya stepped back. Before him, Kuro finally passed her critical point and doubled over. White hair flew. The sound burst out—

target.text: He accepted it with generous composure, then pulled out a cigar cutter from his breast pocket, flicked it open, his hands mimicking the poise of maturity, breaking the seal with a theatrical flourish, all of it affected, for was there not just the faintest hint of impatience wafting from him? But that was not all, for the way he seemed to be sneaking glances at them still niggled at Sakuya's mind. Rather, the one who had captivated his gaze so was─── Kuro?

She had been awfully quiet for a while now. He wouldn't have suffered such hardships back in town if she had just acted like this the whole time, so had this little girl done all that in an attempt to cause trouble for him? Having twisted her actions into harassment of himself, Sakuya, wondering what in the world that rich guy even saw in such a scrawny girl, turned his eyes to Kuro for the first time since entering the warehouse. Her shoulders were trembling faintly. And her face, goodness, it was all crumpled up like a piece of straw paper squeezed into a ball.

Not even a Japanese Chin hit in the snout with a fistful of pepper would look quite this bad, and in front of Sakuya, who recoiled, instinctively taking a step back, Kuro appeared to finally have crossed her limit: her body folded over in two at her midsection, white hair fluttering through the air, and with the sound of something bursting open───

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ひゃああっっっくしょーーんっっ！」
source.english: “Hyaaaa-CHOO!”

source.japanese:
手下が蹴立てた埃は背丈だけは人並みにある朔屋さえ煙たがらせたのだから、クロなど推して知るべしで、強かに吸いこんでいたのだろう、鼻腔をこれでもかとくすぐられていたのだろう、くしゃみは小柄な体が張り裂けそうなほど強烈にやかましく、同時に鼻痒さからの解放に爽快ですら、の、ただしこれははたで聞いている者にとってはで、クロとしては爽快どころではなかった、それどころでは。
　くしゃみは潔く抜けていくだけに留まらず、喉に絡まって彼女を咳きこませ、
source.english:
The dust kicked up by the henchman had bothered even Sakuya, who at least had an ordinary person's height. One could imagine what it did to Kuro. She must have inhaled a great deal. It must have tickled her nose beyond endurance. The sneeze was so fierce and loud that her little body seemed ready to split. The release from that itching was almost refreshing—to a listener, that is. For Kuro it was nothing of the kind. Far from it.
The sneeze did not simply pass cleanly out. It caught in her throat and made her cough—

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「っ!?　え、ふ、こほ……コふッ、
　コン……っ」
source.english:
“!? Eh, fuh, cohh… Cough…
Coh…”

source.japanese: 崩れてぺたりと手をついた床は、また埃まみれで咳をさらに激しくし、
source.english: She collapsed, palms flat on the floor. More dust. Her coughing grew worse.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「AaaaCHHHOOOーー!」

The dust kicked up by the henchman had whirled up high enough to be a nuisance to a man of average height like Sakuya, but as could easily be imagined, someone like Kuro must have inhaled a great deal, and her nostrils must have been tickled relentlessly until now; her sneeze was so intensely loud it seemed as if her tiny frame would burst wide open, but at the same time, being finally released from the itchiness in her nose must have felt refreshing; this, however, was from the perspective of someone who was only listening, for Kuro did not feel refreshed in the slightest. Far from it, in fact. The sneezing did not simply gracefully pass through her; it got stuck in her throat, and she coughed violently,
【Kuro】 「Phh!? Eh, fhh, khh……cough, khn……」
She collapsed, hands braced against the floor, but that, too, was covered in dust, and so her coughing only intensified,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……ふっ、こほ、ん、んっ、んぅ～……？」
source.english: “…Fuh, cough, mm, mm, mmm…?”

source.japanese: ……出口のない圧力が体内を暴れ回る苦痛は、便秘や胃酸過多に苦しむ持病持ちなら共感してくれるだろう。しかもそれらの苦痛は漸増的に高まっていくのに、今回のクロは突然のくしゃみによる、突発的で自家中毒的な内圧である。それも高圧の。見ているうちに、蹲ったクロのほつれ髪から覗くうなじや耳朶が赤くなるやら青くなるやら目まぐるしく、焦って朔屋は抱き起こして、少女の頬が向日葵の種を一杯に詰め込んだ天竺鼠よろしく膨れあがり、唇懸命に食いしばっているのに、起こさなければよかったと、返す手で反射的に突き飛ばしたのがなんともはや、酷いというか仕方ない反応というか、ともかくそれが止めとなり、堤防を崩す、最後の一突きとなり。
source.english: …Anyone afflicted with chronic constipation or excess stomach acid might sympathize with the agony of pressure raging inside the body with no outlet. Those pains, however, mount by degrees. Kuro's was a sudden, self-poisoning internal pressure born of the sneeze—and a high one. As Sakuya watched, the nape and ears visible through her fallen hair flickered alarmingly from red to blue. He hurried to lift her. Then he saw her cheeks bulging like a guinea pig's packed with sunflower seeds, her lips clenched with desperate force, and instantly regretted it. The same hands that raised her shoved her away by reflex. Cruel? Understandable? Either way, that was the finishing blow: the last thrust that broke the dam.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Fhh, cough, n, nh, ngh～……?」

……The pain of the pressure rampaging through her body with no outlet was something a patient suffering from chronic constipation or hyperacidity could surely sympathize with. Moreover, while their pain was one that gradually intensified over time, Kuro's current state was one of abrupt, autotoxemic internal pressure triggered by an unexpected sneeze. And a high internal pressure at that.

Before his very eyes, what he could glimpse of the nape of Kuro's neck and her earlobe as he peeked through her unkempt hair flicked between red and blue at dizzying speeds; panicked, Sakuya tried to help her sit up, lifting her up in his arms, but the girl's cheeks were bulging like a guinea pig's stuffed to the brim with sunflower seeds; she was trying so very hard to keep her lips sealed shut, so regretting ever lifting her up in the first place, he reflexively shoved her back down in the same breath, but call it cruel or the inevitable reaction, regardless, that became the final mercy blow, collapsed the levee, was the straw that broke the camel's back.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ぅぇぁぁぁああ～～～っっっ」
source.english: “Uweaaaaah…”

source.japanese: 体力に乏しいクロの身に、ここまで街中を無駄にふらついたり朔屋に無理矢理走らされたりで相当の負荷がかかっていたのが災いしたのだろうかとか、小賢しい分析などまさに反吐でも喰らえで、最初の一吹きで反吐は床の上に埃その他の堆積物と混ざり合った目出度い混淆の液溜まりを為し、続く第二波第三波が湿った音と共に版図を広げ、
source.english: Perhaps Kuro's meager strength had been overtaxed by the day's useless wandering and Sakuya's forced run. But to hell with clever analysis—the first eruption of vomit itself mingled with dust and the floor's other deposits into one auspicious puddle, and a second and third wave spread its dominion with wet sounds—

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うぇ、えぶっ、むーーーーっ」
source.english: “Ueh, ebuh, mmmm…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「UeeaaaaAAARGH～～～」

The considerable strain imposed upon Kuro's body, already lacking in stamina from having pointlessly wandered through town and having been forced to dash here by Sakuya, was probably her downfall, but all these clever, pretentious analyses could literally eat vomit; with the first spurt, the puke formed a delightfully auspicious puddle of liquid intermixed with the dust and any other debris on the floor, which was then followed by a second and third gushing, expanding its territory with moist noises,
【Kuro】 「Uegh, eufh, mmMMHHhhーーーー」

source.japanese:
衝き上がるえづきの苦しみに目がほとんど白目に裏返り、クロはぶるぶると悶えながら自ら広げた小間物屋（隠語的表現）に顔から倒れ伏していく、その襟首を引き留めた手は、頼もしい、誰あろう、朔屋───などであろうか、多くの殴る蹴るを経て拳胼胝などでごつごつしているから彼ではない、なんと取引相手の手下の一人。二重の意味で呆気にとられた朔屋には構いもせず、甲斐甲斐しく少女の口元を拭い、どういう気まぐれで慈悲を示すのか、またどういう心づもりでてきぱきと、どこからか取り出した六尺棒にクロの手足を縛りつけていくのか。両の手首を一つにくくりつけ、両脚を膝の裏で戒めて、出来上がった形は、仕留めた狸を棒に縛りつけて担いでいく時のそれ。
　そのままずるずる引きずって行くのがボスの下へ、部下の突然の暴走に金持ちは度を失う、でもなく、むしろ喜色で頷[うなず]いた。
source.english:
The surge of retching rolled Kuro's eyes nearly white. Shuddering, she toppled face-first toward the little shop of wares she had spread before her—to employ the euphemism—when a hand caught her by the collar. Reassuringly, it was Sakuya's—one might have thought. But this hand was knobbed with calluses from a great deal of punching and kicking, and therefore could not be his. It belonged, astonishingly, to one of their business partner's henchmen.
Ignoring Sakuya, who was dumbfounded in two distinct senses, the man solicitously wiped the girl's mouth. By what whim did he show such mercy? And to what end did he so briskly produce a six-foot staff from somewhere and bind Kuro's limbs to it? He lashed her wrists together, then tied both legs behind the knees. The finished article resembled a dead raccoon dog trussed to a pole for carrying.
He dragged her away toward the boss. The rich man did not lose his composure at his subordinate's sudden rampage. Quite the contrary: he nodded with delight.

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「よぅーしそうだ。それでいい。
　いきなり戻したのには面食らったが───」
source.english:
“All right, that’s it. That’s good enough.
I was taken aback when you suddenly threw up, though—”

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「それもまたそそるなぁ、クロくん」
source.english: “That only makes you more enticing, little Kuro.”

source.japanese: ……訳もわからないうちに、荒廃した倉庫という背景が、ボッシュなる幻視者がものした異端的な宗教画とも迷妄の一大産物ともつかぬ世界にすり替わったかの失墜感で眩暈しながら、朔屋は左右を見て、前後を見て、それでも受け入れきる事は出来ずに間抜けた笑み口元に張りつかせて呟いた。
source.english: …Before he knew it, he felt as though the backdrop of the dilapidated warehouse had been replaced by a world that might have been a heretical religious painting by the visionary Bosch or some vast product of delusion. Dizzy with the feeling that he was falling, Sakuya looked left and right, then front and back. Still unable to fully accept it, he muttered with a dazed smile frozen on his lips.

target.text: Kuro's eyes had almost rolled back in her head from the pain of the retching surging up her throat, and while shaking in agony, Kuro was just about to collapse face-first into the haberdashery (slang expression) that she herself had put on display, but she was grabbed by the collar, held in place; how reassuring that hand was, and whose could it be, Sakuya's─── (TN: This is referring to an old Japanese slang term from the Edo period, "小間物屋を広げる", literally meaning spreading out the haberdashery, with the vomit being likened to the display of assorted goods spread out on, say, a carpet. It is an expression mostly seen in Rakugo these days.)

While it very well could have been, it was rugged and covered in calluses formed through countless punches and kicks, so it could not be him, and of all the people, who should it be but one of their business partner's henchmen. Paying no mind to Sakuya, who was now left stunned in two ways at once, he was brisk and efficient as he wiped her mouth; what kind of whim had brought about this display of compassion, and furthermore, with what intent did he then promptly whip out a rokushakubo from somewhere only to tie Kuro's hands and feet to it? (TN: A rokushakubo, written "六尺棒", is a pole roughly 180 cm in length traditionally used for self-defence and capturing lawbreakers.)

He tied both her wrists together, fastened both her legs together at the back of her knees, and the finished result looked exactly like when a hunter tied a bagged tanuki to a pole and carried it away on his shoulders. And just like that, he dragged her over to his boss. Was he flustered at the reckless behaviour suddenly displayed by his henchman? No, far from it, and if anything, he nodded with delight.
【Rich guy】 「Niiice, that's it. That's good. Admittedly, I was taken aback when you suddenly threw up, but───」
【Rich guy】 「But that's arousing in its own way, isn't it, Kuro-kun?」

……While reeling from sudden vertigo, as if plunging into an abyss, as though the backdrop, the dilapidated warehouse, were replaced, dissolving into one of the worlds painted by the great visionary Bosch, masterworks that could be termed neither heretical altarpieces nor the grand product of a delusion, Sakuya looked left and right, forwards and backwards, but still finding himself unable to accept the situation, with a vacant smile frozen on his lips, he muttered.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ええと、これ、どういうこと？」
source.english: “Um, what does this mean?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Uhmm, what is happening here?」

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「どういう事もなにも」
source.english: “What do you mean, ‘what do you mean’?”
