【金持ち】
「それに、あんな海の破落戸ども、港に停泊するだけでどれだけの怨みと反感を買っているのやら。お前達、自分達がどれだけ忌み嫌われているか、もう少し自覚したらどうだ？」
source.english: “Besides, just by dropping anchor in the harbor, those sea ruffians must be stirring up a whole lot of resentment and hostility. Why don’t you guys try to be a little more aware of just how much you’re despised?”

source.japanese:
そんなのは今更言われずとも痛感している朔屋であり、あの不運の一夜を契機に船に連れこまれていなかったら、彼だって信天翁号に石を投げる側に位置していたのだ。
　正論は美しくそして時に残酷であるという。うっかり素直に頷[うなず]いてしまったはいいものの、ついに朔屋の全身各部位は、意識の統御を離れて出鱈目てんで勝手に活動開始した。左脚は伏せて射線を回避しようとし、口は泣き叫んで慈悲を乞う準備、腹は恐怖に膀胱を締めあげ、手は無意味に目を塞ごうとする、まとまりに欠けることこの上ない。その中で朔屋の心は───
source.english:
Sakuya knew it already, without anyone saying so; had he not been brought aboard after that unlucky night, he, too, would have been among those throwing stones at the Albatross.
Sound reasoning is beautiful—and sometimes cruel. He had nodded, carelessly, but now every part of his body broke free and started moving on its own. His left leg tried to get him down out of the line of fire, his mouth prepared to wail and beg for mercy, his stomach clenched his bladder in fear, and his hands tried pointlessly to shield his eyes—a scene of total disarray. And in the middle of it all, Sakuya’s mind—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……? Don't really get it, but Kuro……starting, to feel bad……」
【Kuro】 「Gonna puke again……, ueh, uegh……auhn」

However, after having thrown up everything within her just earlier, the contents of her stomach were as empty as the storehouses of a village pillaged by the Kwantung Army: all that came out of her was retching and a miniscule amount of gastric juice, but not even being permitted relief from the impulse to vomit, the needle of Kuro's mind easily swung past the maximum. Nay, if anything, perhaps we ought to say that she had done well to endure this long?

Even to a man like Sakuya, who had a tendency to get lost in his own overactive imagination, this man's plan just left him feeling sick from its inordinate cruelty; this was the asylum in Sugamo, or if not that, then the Kyuushuu Imperial University's Psychiatric Open Treatment Ward, or so he attempted to convince himself as he desperately tried to not think about anything involving Kuro. (TN: The madhouse in Sugamo was an infamous asylum in Japan that was reformed in 1901. Sugamo is shorthand for "the madhouse" in Japanese literature, much like Bedlam in English. The Open Treatment Ward is a reference to the novel Dogra Magra written by Yumeno Kyuusaku.)

Sakuya would much prefer not to have a lunatic like this so brazenly left at large in public, and that was exactly why he was chanting "this warehouse is an asylum" in an attempt to cast a magic charm on himself, but as he arrived at the realization that he truly was facing this madman head-on with no lattice door between them, he only felt all the more sick for it, knees no longer able to support his body. While both his legs trembled with an audible clatter, he still had to face up to this unhinged reality. In a move quite bold for him, he castigated the man───
【Naomasa】 「That's not just a thing for young girls, that's soft necrophilia, you deviant! Call this the lofty tastes of the rich all you want, this is just going too far.」

【Rich guy】 「Prattle on as you like. I don't believe this is something poor people could ever hope to understand. You are aware that this deal was proposed by the people from your ship to begin with, yes?」

───Suspecting that his words just then might have been a kind of religious auditory hallucination of the sort occasionally bestowed upon the righteous from the heavens, after looking right, looking left, looking behind himself, and looking in front himself, Sakuya finally turned to the heavens, sought its guidance, but all he found was a ceiling covered in spider webs; no signs of divine revelation awaited him, so with nothing else to do, all he had left was to ask the man to repeat his question.
【Naomasa】 「What did you just say?」
【Rich guy】 「Again, I said that your people are the ones who proposed this deal. Why, to tell you the truth, I'm glad you saved me the trouble.」

Apparently, while he was trying to devise a scheme that would let him lure Kuro here and capture her, to his amazement, it was the Albatross that offered to sell Kuro to him. Somebody from the Albatross (it seemed likely to have been the Bosun or the mates) had caught wind of this rich man's desire and made the proposal to him. That is to say, this time, Kuro was not Sakuya's companion, she was the commodity that had been passed from hand to hand with indifference; that appeared to be the particulars of this incident───

【Rich guy】 「But I must hand it to you. I'm impressed, in a sense, by your commitment. The Albatross will treat even comrades as commodities to be sold without batting an eyelid. ───You filthy low-lifes.」

Like being derided as an inferior species by a bipedal frog for, of all the things, still flaunting his navel in this day and age, being treated like a low-life by this man should not be enough to actually incense him, but in this case alone, what he said could only be described as a fair point, which left him feeling frustrated, miserable, and absolutely pathetic; overwhelmed by the shamefulness of it all, the nerves in Sakuya's face went slack, and just as he was about to collapse from the knees down, one of the white suit's henchmen reached out for him with a hand and caught him. My, how reassuring.

……And what was supposed to be so reassuring about that? No, this was a display of mercilessness, for clasped tightly in the hand held out was a hard, glossy lump of black iron, but upon spotting that threat, his instincts in charge of violently battering the alarm bells in his brain were the very height of imbecility, no different from their owner, for what good did it do to only warn him of the crisis he was in once the hard, cold, and lethal muzzle was already pointed at his forehead and chest? No, they really ought to have informed him to run away much earlier.
【Rich guy】 「Now then, with the merchandise safely in my possession, paying the price would be following proper procedures and all───」

Before Sakuya could snap at the man, demanding to know what kind of lunatic points a gun at someone when they're supposed to be paying, he realized that the man wasn't carrying a suitcase or anything of the sort to hold the fee, and that was not all; he also showed no indication of pulling out a wallet either, and so Sakuya felt a chill at the back of his neck. The sweat he hadn't realized he was shedding was terribly cold, and nothing good had ever happened to him once he felt a sweat like this one form.
The rich man had not forgotten to hand over the payment for Kuro to Sakuya. ───No. He was about to, but then it seemed as though he had changed his mind at the very last second,

【Rich guy】 「But in these times we live in, the powers that be keep an awfully unsparing eye on many things. Should it happen to become known that I've engaged in human trafficking, why, I'd be ruined in an instant.」
【Rich guy】 「So, the fact that I "liberated" this girl? I'll need to make sure none of that ever took place.」
【Rich guy】 「Fortunately for me, the only witness from your side of the deal appears to be you.」

The rest of it went without saying. A man who had been forcibly shanghaied into service on a ship as terrible as the Albatross was sent ashore on an errand, so anyone expecting him to obediently return would have to be as stupid as someone who'd trip over their own right foot. It wasn't the first or even second time that Sakuya himself had considered making his escape during this trip ashore. Therefore. At this point, if a green sailor or two were to never return, no veterans on the ship would spare it a second thought.
【Naomasa】 「No no no, wait, let's rethink all this, okay? Look, it's not like those guys would ever care if one or two people like me went missing.」

While he was professing his own lack of value, Sakuya did want to cry, just a little, but he somehow managed to hold in the tears as he continued to stall for time, not that he thought him dragging things out would somehow change this situation for the better.
【Naomasa】 「When it comes to coin, those guys are more dogged than the demonic hounds of hell. If you don't pay them the money, I'm certain they'll be coming to collect───」

【Rich guy】 「I took a little girl, who was illegally made to work on that ship, into my custody. I feel like I'll easily be able to solve the situation with something of that nature. A claim from that rotten ship, or from I, a man who has invested quite a lot of money into this port. Now, who could possibly hold the advantage there?」
【Naomasa】 「……An excellent point.」

【Rich guy】 「Furthermore, do you have any idea just how much resentment and antipathy you thugs of the sea incur from mooring in this port alone? Have you people considered being a little more self-aware of just how utterly despised you are?」

Sakuya was already painfully aware of that without being told it anew; if only he hadn't been dragged to that ship after that most misfortunate of nights, then he'd surely belong to the side throwing rocks at the Albatross.

It is said that while sound arguments can be beautiful, at times, they can also be brutally cruel. He had caught himself nodding along in agreement, but at long last, every part of Sakuya's entire body had separated from his conscious control and begun to arbitrarily take completely haphazard action. His left leg lowered to the floor as if to avoid the line of fire, his mouth was preparing to open wide to wail and scream and beg for mercy, his stomach tightened around his bladder with fear, and his hand vainly attempted to cover his eyes; nothing less coordinated could be found in this realm. And amidst it all, Sakuya's heart───

source.japanese:
好き勝手に自己主張する体のあちこちの中、右脚だけは辛うじて地に着いていたのは、どうにか土性骨残していた為でなく、主と同じくすくたれ者であるあまりに、泰然と腰を抜かしていたというにすぎないだろう。足が腰を抜かすとは奇怪な謂[い]いだが。ともかく、その右だけが心に沿わせられると感じた時に、朔屋は本当に、自分でも信じられない事に、一歩踏み出していたのである。かすかに呻[うめ]くクロを目指して。もしかしたらその時、朔屋のご先祖の一人が幽冥の通路を越えて合力してくれていたのかも知れない。朔屋の如き駄目男を排出した血筋でも、家系図総ざらえにすれば一人くらいは気骨備えた丈夫があったのかも。
　朔屋にしてから自分の行動が意外であったのなら、金持ちの方の驚きはいかばかりか。向かってくる彼に対して、やや鼻白んだように瞬きさえ。
source.english:
Of all the parts of his body asserting themselves as they pleased, only his right leg still barely touched the ground. This was not because it had preserved some scrap of backbone. No: being every bit as spineless as its owner, it had simply gone weak at the knees with magnificent composure. A leg going weak at the knees was a curious expression, but never mind. The instant Sakuya felt that one leg alone might obey his will, he did the genuinely unbelievable: he stepped forward. Toward Kuro, whose faint moan reached him.
Perhaps at that moment one of Sakuya's ancestors crossed the road from the dead to lend him strength. Even a bloodline capable of producing a good-for-nothing like Sakuya might, if one ransacked the family tree, contain a single sturdy man of spirit.
If Sakuya himself was astonished by his action, how much greater was the rich man's surprise? He even blinked at Sakuya's approach, faintly disconcerted.

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「なんだなぁ。なんのつもりだ。
　銃を怖がる程度の頭もないのか？
　それともとうとうおかしくなったわけ？」
source.english:
“What’s this? What the hell do you think you’re doing?
Don’t you have enough sense to be afraid of a gun?
Or have you finally lost your mind?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「や、その……すんません、
　自分でもなんか、その」
source.english:
“Uh, well… I’m sorry,
I guess even I, well…”

source.japanese: 踏み出しておきながらどこまでも強きにへりくだり式で、やはり朔屋の行動は蛮勇どころか、逃げ出す方向を間違っただけと見るべきか───
source.english: Even after stepping forward, he continued to abase himself before the strong. Perhaps this was not reckless courage at all. Perhaps Sakuya had merely chosen the wrong direction in which to flee—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもあの、品だけ渡して金持ってかなかったら、船に戻った時、俺絶対死ぬほどの折檻くらうんで」
source.english: “But, um, if I just hand over the goods and don’t take the money, I’ll definitely get beaten within an inch of my life when I get back to the ship.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「死ぬような目……、
　今か、後か、どっちがいいのか、
　ううう、どっちも厭だぁ……」
source.english:
“Going through something that could kill me…
Now or later—which is better?
Uuuu, I hate both of them…”

source.japanese: ぐずぐずと半泣き、鼻水まで垂らして、それでもまた一歩を踏んだところを見ると、いかな理不尽な罰であろうと、船での鉄拳制裁は眼前の銃と同じくらいの恐怖を朔屋の骨身に刻んでいると見える。迫ってくるといっても手に寸鉄さえなく、おまけにいい歳した男が泣きを入れながらでは迫力は微塵もなく、白スーツはすぐに気を取り直し、手下に唇の端吊り上げて、もう言わずもがな、さっさと始末をつけろの合図に、かちゃりと金属音が答えた。撃鉄を起こす音だった。いよいよもってもうお終い、こんなところで一巻の、否一巻にも充たない朔屋の人生に終止符が───
source.english:
Hesitant, half in tears, snot trailing from his nose—and yet he took another step. Evidently, however unreasonable the punishment, the ship's iron discipline had engraved in Sakuya's bones a terror equal to that inspired by the gun before him. Still, he advanced unarmed; and a grown man blubbering as he came possessed not a particle of menace. The man in white quickly recovered himself and crooked one corner of his mouth at his henchman. The signal needed no words: finish it. A metallic click replied.
The hammer cocked.
Now it was truly over. Here a full stop would be put to the single volume—no, the fraction of a volume—that was Sakuya's life—

target.text: Among the various parts of his body willfully self-asserting their egos, only his right foot barely remained tethered to the floor, but it was not because a semblance of grit yet remained within it, no, it was simply just as craven as its owner, and this was nothing more than his leg's spine turning to jelly, paralyzed from fear. A leg's spine turning to jelly was an unusual expression. Regardless, the moment he sensed that this right leg of his alone acted in accordance with his heart, Sakuya, and this really was something unbelievable even to the man himself, took a single step forwards. Heading for the faintly groaning Kuro.

Perhaps at that moment, one of Sakuya's ancestors crossed the passage from the underworld to lend him a helping hand. Even in a bloodline that had excreted a man as worthless as Sakuya, were one to do a comprehensive review of the entire extend family tree, then surely there had to be at least one manly warrior possessed of a strong moral backbone and mettle who counted amongst their ranks. If Sakuya himself thought his own actions surprising, then how shocked must the rich man have been. He even looked a little daunted at the prospect of Sakuya approaching, if but for a moment.
【Rich guy】 「What's the matter? What do you think you're doing? Do you not even have the faculties to fear a gun? Or have you just finally lost your marbles?」
【Naomasa】 「No, uhm……sorry, I myself don't really, uhm.」

With the way he so abased himself when faced with strength even as he stepped forwards, in the end, Sakuya's actions were not a product of reckless valour, far from it; perhaps they ought to be interpreted as the man simply mistaking which direction to escape───
【Naomasa】 「But, look, if I just hand over the goods without getting any money in return, I'll be beaten half to death when I get back to the ship.」
【Naomasa】 「A mortal ordeal……, Now, later, what's best here? Uugh, I don't want either……」

Grumbling about the unfairness of it all while on the verge of tears, he even had snot dribbling down his face, but considering the fact that he still took another step forwards, no matter how irrational and unjust those punishments may have been, it seemed that the beatings he'd received aboard the ship had etched just as great a terror into Sakuya's very bones as what he felt at the sight of a gun held right up to his face.

Though he was drawing closer, he did not carry even so much as a short blade in his hands, and on top of that, a man of his age looming closer while crying and begging for mercy did not carry a shred of impact; the white suit quickly regained his bearings, raised the corner of his lips to his henchmen, and while it surely went without saying, that was a sign to put an end to him immediately, one answered with the clinking of metal. It was the sound of a hammer clicking into place. At long last, with that, it was now over: in a squalid place like this, a full stop was placed at the end of the book of───nay, at the end of Sakuya's life, which could not even fill a book───

source.japanese:
銃口を向けられたまま暫時の緊張を強いられた時、なんで相手はまず撃たないのか訝しむのは、修羅場を踏んだ経験のあるものか余程の阿呆くらいである。中途半端にそのどちらでもない朔屋は、あっさりと銃の圧力に屈した。クロは可哀相は可哀相なれど、あの変態異常性欲者に飼われている限りは、少なくとも自分よりは長生きできるはず。そんな相手を助けようとするのは暴虎馮河の勇の愚行、朔屋が銃口からもクロからも逃れるように、手が勝手に目を覆うに任せたのは、あながち無意味とは言いきれまい。
　少なくとも自分に鉛玉がめりこむその銃光は見ずに済む……が、視覚を閉ざした事により拡大された聴覚が捉えた、かちゃりと金属音の、それ撃鉄を起こす響き、いよいよもってもうお終い、こんなところで一巻の、否一巻にも充たない朔屋の人生に終止符が───
source.english:
When one has been kept under a gun for some time, only a man seasoned by mortal scrapes—or an exceptional fool—wonders why the other fellow does not simply fire. Sakuya, half-baked in both capacities and complete in neither, promptly buckled beneath the gun’s menace. Pitiful Kuro might be, but so long as that depraved pervert kept her, she would at least live longer than Sakuya. Trying to rescue her would be the foolhardy courage of fighting a tiger barehanded or fording a river on foot. So when Sakuya let his hands cover his eyes of their own accord, shutting out both the muzzle and Kuro, the gesture was perhaps not entirely pointless.
At least he would be spared the flash when the lead slug buried itself in him... But with sight cut off, his hearing swelled to fill the gap and caught the metallic click—the hammer cocking. Now it truly was over. Here, of all places, came the end of the volume—no, the end of a life that would not even fill one—

target.text: When the stress of having a gun pointed at you for some time is foisted upon you, if the first thing that goes through your head is being suspicious of why they haven't just shot you already, then you are either a veteran of truly brutal battlefields or a complete idiot. And as a man always doing things by half measures, Sakuya was neither of the two: he readily succumbed before the pressure radiating from the gun. Kuro's situation was as pitiful as could be, but as long as she was kept by that degenerate with his sexual deviations, at the very least, she should live a life longer than himself.

Trying to save someone like that would be the folly of a foolhardy hero, and as though to escape both the gun and Kuro, Sakuya's hands instinctively covered his eyes, which could not be declared entirely meaningless.

At the very least, he wouldn't have to witness the muzzle flash as the shot of lead dug into him……but, with his sight now blocked, his sense of hearing was augmented in turn, and it caught the clinking of metal; that was the sound of the hammer lifting. At long last, with that, it was now over: in a squalid place like this, a full stop was placed at the end of the book of───nay, at the end of Sakuya's life, which could not even fill a book───

source.japanese: がぁぁぁぁん！
source.english: Boooooom!

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぎゃああああああ！
　撃たれたぁぁっ」
source.english:
“Aaaaaaargh!
I’ve been shot!”

source.japanese: 鳴った音は高く、朔屋はとうとう数滴パンツの中に失禁で、堤防が全決壊しなかっただけでも立派と言えて、その割りこんだ音は彼のみならず対峙していた連中にとっても意想外の事であり、全員の動きが瞬時に凝結する。
source.english: The sharp ring of it made Sakuya finally lose control, leaking a few drops of urine into his pants. It was a feat in itself that the dam hadn’t completely burst. That sudden sound took not only him but also the men facing him by surprise, and everyone’s movements froze instantly.

source.japanese:
そう───銃を構えた手下にとってもボスにとっても、思いも寄らない轟音だった。銃声だってここまで重いものか。実際拳銃は、銃把こそ手下の手の温度を帯びていたけれど銃身に炸裂熱無く硝煙の揺らめく筋も見えず、朔屋の体で痛むのは馬鹿声張り上げた喉くらい、どこにも焦げ穴一つ開いていない。
　では轟音はどこから、それは倉庫の外から、壁を隔てて遠いのに、その音源の凄まじさが窺えるほどに破壊力を蔵した音、遠大な。
source.english:
Yes—the roar had startled both the henchman holding the gun and his master. Could a pistol shot carry such weight? In fact, although the grip had taken on the warmth of the henchman's hand, the barrel held no blast heat and no thread of powder smoke wavered from it. The only part of Sakuya's body that hurt was his throat, abused by his own scream. Not one charred hole had opened anywhere.
Then where had the roar come from? Outside the warehouse. Far off, beyond the wall—yet the sound carried such destructive force that one could imagine the immensity of its source. A vast sound. A far-reaching one.

target.text: BAAAAANG!
【Naomasa】 「GYAAAAH! I'VE BEEN SHOOOOT!」

The rumbling boomed so loudly, Sakuya finally let a few drops leak out into his underwear, and one could even call it impressive that the entire wharf hadn't collapsed, but the noise that forced itself upon them was shocking not just for him, but also for the lot he was squaring off against, and everybody present froze entirely for a moment.

Indeed───to both the henchmen holding guns and their boss, this was also an entirely unforeseen thunderous roar. There was no way a gunshot could be this weighty. In actuality, while the grip of the handgun certainly held a trace of the temperature coming from the henchman's hand, the gun as a whole held not the heat of a violent explosion, nor was there a wavering trail of gunpowder smoke anywhere to be seen, and the only thing hurting on Sakuya's body was his throat after screaming like an idiot, with not a single scorched hole to be found anywhere on his person.

Then where had the thundering roar come from? It was from the outside of the warehouse, and though it was distant, separated from them by the walls, it was a sound containing such destructive power that it betrayed a glimpse of the sheer awesomeness of its source, truly grand and far-reaching in scale.

source.japanese: 次いで走りこんできたのが、ボスに侍っていたのと同様のダークスーツの男で、つんのめり、手を鶏の飛べない翼と泳がせて、扉を抜けて一声、
source.english: Next came another man in a dark suit like the ones attending the boss. He pitched through the doorway, arms flapping like the flightless wings of a chicken, and shouted—

target.text: Next, a man came running, clad in a dark suit identical to those worn by the men attending their boss here, and while pitching forwards, waving his arms about like the flightless wings of a chicken, he stepped through the door and shouted:

source.japanese:
【手下】
「だ、旦那ッ。旦那の三番倉庫で爆発が、火がッ、いきなり燃え広がってっ」
source.english: “M-Master! Your Warehouse Three—there’s been an explosion! Fire! All of a sudden, it’s spreading!”

source.japanese: 外で見張っていたらしい手下から叩きつけられた報せで、面々の石化していた体が肉に戻るより先に、このタイミングで意識取り戻したのはクロ、澱んでいた眸[ひとみ]に光が戻った、とは言っても普段が普段だからたかが知れており、
source.english: The news, delivered by the henchman who’d apparently been keeping watch outside, jolted Kuro awake—before the others’ stone-still bodies had even softened back to flesh. Light flickered in her clouded eyes—though, given her usual state, it wasn’t much to write home about, and

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「注射、やめてぇっ、
　豚さんとトモダチも、なんか怖いよぉ……」
source.english:
“No more needles!
And I don't want to be friends with the pig either. It sounds scary…”

source.japanese:
急転した事態を全くよそに、断線前の記憶を引きずって身悶えする、がそんなのは耳から吊り下げられた兎よりも甲斐ない抵抗に過ぎず、屈強な手下にかかっては難なく手をひねられてそこまでの、そこまでになったろうとも、爆発音に虚を衝[つ]かれてさえいなかったなら。身を捩り、ひねり、髪乱す白子の娘に一瞬だけ遅れた反応がその手下にとっての命運を分けた。金持ちの部下としても、男としても。
　人間の内心を悉く見透かして恐れられた山中の怪、サトリの魔物に傷を与え追い払ったのは、猟師が折ろうとした粗朶が手の裡から弾けて、偶然に怪にぶち当たった事に因るという。狙うという、心の働きの外で起こる偶発時には天眼通とて対処は困難の故事だが、この時同様の事が生じた。
source.english:
Completely oblivious to the sudden turn of events, she writhed, clinging to the memories from before the connection was severed—but such resistance was even more futile than that of a rabbit hung by its ears. The burly henchman would have twisted her wrist effortlessly, and that would have been the end of it—had he not been caught off guard by the explosion. That split-second lag in reacting to the albino girl—twisting, writhing, hair askew—sealed the henchman’s fate. Both as a man under a wealthy master and as a man in his own right.
It is said that the satori—a mountain apparition feared for its ability to see right through a person’s innermost thoughts—was wounded and driven off not by any deliberate action, but simply because a piece of brushwood the hunter had been trying to snap sprang from his hand and accidentally struck the monster. The old tale shows how even clairvoyance struggles with accidents that arise outside conscious intent. Something much the same happened right then.

target.text: 【Henchman】 「BO-, BOSS! In your third warehouse, boss, an explosion, a fire, it just lit up out of nowhere and the flames are spreading!」

Before the petrified bodies of all present could turn from stone back to flesh after having the news brought by the henchman, who appeared to have been keeping watch outside, slapped in their faces, it was Kuro who first returned to the waking world; the light came back to her dull eyes, though with that said, given how she normally was, that wasn't particularly noticeable,
【Kuro】 「Stop it with the injections, and being friends with a piggy, that sounds kinda scary too……」

Completely oblivious to the sudden change in circumstances, she dragged the memory from right before she disconnected back out and writhed in pain, but her struggling was even more pointless than that of a bunny strung up by the ears, and when dealing with a brawny henchman, it would only last until her wrists were easily twisted, but even if that was all it would amount to, that was only the case assuming he hadn't been caught entirely on the back foot by the explosion. Reacting just a moment too late to the albino girl with disheveled hair contorting and twisting her body around was what sealed his fate. Both as an underling of this rich man and as a man.

To wound and drive away the monster known as a Satori, a yokai hailing from the mountains feared for being able to peer into the entirety of man's mind, the twig that the huntsman made to snap had to burst out from within his hand, all so it happened to strike the yokai by unpredictable coincidence. It is a piece of folklore describing how even clairvoyance struggles to contend with the accidental, that born of no conscious aim, what occurs beyond the realm of human will, but in this moment, a similar situation arose.

source.japanese: クロの身悶えは、俎板に釘で頭を打ち留められた鰻と同じく痙攣的な反射であり、彼女自身意図していなかった力と角度で、六尺棒が両膝の間からすっぽ抜け、なまじ縛りつけて抑えられていたのが瞬発的に放たれただけに、反動で加速され、宙を奔った速度は目に追えないほど。クロの足から外れたと思った瞬間には───身の毛のよだつ音がした。爆発音や銃声とも異質で、くぐもって、なのに男にとっては聞くだけでも身の毛がよだつ。
source.english: Kuro's writhing was a convulsive reflex, like an eel with its head nailed to a chopping board. With a force and angle she had never intended, the six-foot pole slipped from between her knees. Precisely because she had been tied and held in check, its sudden release accelerated it with the recoil. It shot through the air faster than the eye could follow. The instant it came free of her legs—a hair-raising sound. Unlike a blast or a gunshot. Muffled, yet enough to make any man's hair stand merely to hear it.

target.text: Kuro's writhing was a convulsive reflex similar to that of an eel on a cutting board executed by having a nail hammered through its head: neither the angle nor the force were a product of the girl's own designs, but the rokushakubo slipped clean out from between her knees, and given that the bindings were undone in an instant, having only been fastened halfway, the recoil made it accelerate; it flashed through the air so fast his eyes couldn't keep up, and no sooner than it seemed to part from between Kuro's legs───did he hear a hair-raising sound. Of a different nature from either the explosion or the gunfire: muffled, but it was the sort of noise that would make the hairs of any man who heard it stand on end.

source.japanese:
六尺棒は。
　朔屋に銃を向けていた手下の。
　その股間に。
　残酷なまでに深々と。
source.english:
The six-foot pole.
The henchman aiming a gun at Sakuya.
His groin.
Cruelly deep—

source.japanese:
ああ───
　めりこんで。
source.english:
Ah—
It struck home.

target.text: The rokushakubo. Lodged into the crotch. Of the henchman aiming a gun at Sakuya. So very deeply it was brutal to behold.
Alas─── How deep it was buried within.

source.japanese:
たまらない間の中で、ぶくぶくと小泡が弾ける。
　かちかちがちがちと硬く細かい音伴って。
source.english:
In an unbearable interval, tiny bubbles broke and foamed.
Accompanied by a hard, fine clacking and chattering.

target.text: For an unbearable amount of time, little bubbles foamed and burst. Accompanied by the sound of hard, minute rattling.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あ……え……ごめん、なさい……？」
source.english: “Ah… Eh… I'm sorry…?”

source.japanese:
手下が、がちがちと歯を鳴らしながら悶絶していた。
　南方熊楠翁によれば、金的に深刻なる痛打を受けたる場合、股間の痛みもさりながら、余りの衝撃に神経回路の齟齬が発生し、歯の根が合わなくなるという。この記述が正しいことを確認した朔屋は、同性として身の裡が縮み上がる思いだったけれど、かといって手下に全く同情はできなかった。自分に銃を突きつけてくる相手にそこまで寛大になれるほど、朔屋は人間ができていない。
source.english:
The henchman writhed in agony, his teeth chattering.
According to the venerable Kumagusu Minakata, a grave blow to the testicles produced not only pain in the groin but such a shock to the nervous system that one's teeth would not stop chattering. Having confirmed this account, Sakuya felt himself shrink inside as a fellow man. But he could muster no sympathy for the henchman. He had not developed enough generosity to extend it to someone pointing a gun at him.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Ah……eh……so-, rry……?」

With chattering teeth, the henchman fainted in agony. According to the venerable gentleman Minakata Kumagusu, in situations where one receives a severely crushing blow to the family jewels, while there is a pain in the crotch, the excessive shock causes an outbreak of disruptive inconsistency in the neural network, leading one's teeth to chatter uncontrollably. (TN: Minakata Kumagusu, written "南方熊楠", was a Japanese biologist, ethnologist, and author who lived between 1867-1941)

Sakuya, who could now confirm that this description had proven correct, certainly did flinch internally as a member of the same sex, but with that said, he also felt no sympathy at all for this henchman. Sakuya was not the sort of man to be so magnanimous to another who had thrust a gun at him.

source.japanese: 耐久力を余程信頼していたのか、どずんと床に伏した手下に金持ち見る間に色を失ったし、外から駆けこんできた手下の報告もまた衝撃だったようで、金持ち殿、クロと戸口の外を代わる代わりに睨[にら]んで葛藤の内心ありありと、選んだのは外に駆け出すあたり、爆発したのは余程重要なものの倉庫だったよう。
source.english: Perhaps the rich man had placed considerable faith in his subordinate's endurance. As the fellow dropped heavily to the floor, he visibly paled. The report from the henchman who had rushed in was apparently another shock. The wealthy gentleman glared alternately at Kuro and the doorway, his inner conflict plain. He chose to run outside. Whatever had exploded must have been an important warehouse.

source.japanese:
【手下】
「あ、旦那、こいつ等はどうするんでっ？」
source.english: “Ah, sir, what about these two?”

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「バカ、いいから、どうせ逃げられない、
　今はそれより向こうを！
　なんて事だ、
　あそこには今度の商談用の……っ」
source.english:
“Idiot! Never mind. They can't escape anyway.
The other place comes first!
What a disaster.
In there, for the coming deal, I've got—”

target.text: Perhaps he had placed overmuch faith in his durability, for when the henchman collapsed on the floor with a heavy thud right before his eyes, the rich man's face face drained of colour, but it also seemed the report from the henchman who had come running in from the outside was quite shocking, and so, given that Mr. Rich Guy, clearly caught in an internal conflict as he glared back and forth between Kuro and the door, decided on running outside, the warehouse that exploded must have housed something extremely important to him.
【Henchman】 「Ah, boss, what are we gonna do about these two?」

【Rich man】 「Forget that, you idiot, they have nowhere to run, and more importantly, I gotta get over there, pronto! Damn it all, that's where I keep all the stuff for our upcoming business negotiations……」

source.japanese: 金持ちとしては手下に場を任せたつもりだったのかも知れないが、手下にしてみれば常にボスの傍にあるのが第一優先事項であったようで、朔屋とクロを憎さげに睨[にら]みつけてから、結局選んだのが外に飛びだしていったボスを追う事であったたという。自らの判断能力を放棄するような手下しか抱えていないあたり、このボスの底、やはり浅いのだろう。
source.english: Perhaps the rich man meant to leave his subordinates in charge here. For them, however, staying beside their boss evidently took priority. After glaring hatefully at Sakuya and Kuro, the man ultimately chose to follow his employer outside. A boss whose men had surrendered their own judgment must, after all, have been a shallow one.

target.text: Perhaps the rich man had intended to leave this place to his henchman, but from the henchman's perspective, his highest priority seemed to be always remaining by the boss' side, so after glaring hatefully at Kuro and Sakuya, he ultimately chose to leap outside and chase after his boss. To only employ henchmen who had abandoned their own ability to make judgments suggested that, in the end, this boss really did have a character as thin as a wafer.

source.japanese:
【手下】
「てめえら、どうせ逃げられねえからな、
　大人しくしてろや……っ」
source.english:
“You bastards can't escape anyway.
Stay put…!”

target.text: 【Henchman】 「You bastards have nowhere to run, so you'd better stay and behave……」

source.japanese: 捨て台詞までがボスの模倣で、報せに来たのもまた返す刀で走り出して、倉庫には朔屋とクロの二人だけ（意識不明の手下は数に入らぬとして）、いよいよ空しい広さが広がるばかり。朔屋はクロとしばし呆然と目を交わして、そして彼女を担ぎ上げて扉に駆けた。まだクロの手には縛りつけられたまま六尺棒が残っているが、解いている余裕はないし、外に見張りがあろうとも荏苒手をこまねいているだけに留まるほど、朔屋といえど脳味噌に鬆は入っていない。よし、たとい外に出た瞬間に敢え無く捕まる可能性もあるが、一筋の蜘蛛の糸はあるはず、ここに残っていてはやがて戻ってきた誰かに確実に捕まる。それだけの判断力は残していて、とにかく、悶絶した護衛には目もくれず、ここを先途と逃げ出す朔屋の、一応自分を助けてくれた事になるクロを肩に担ぎあげると、か細い声で囁かれた。
source.english:
Even the henchman's parting threat was an imitation of his boss. The messenger turned on his heel and ran out after them, leaving only Sakuya and Kuro in the warehouse—if one declined to count the unconscious guard. Its empty breadth seemed to expand around them.
For a moment they stared blankly at each other. Then Sakuya hoisted Kuro onto his shoulder and ran for the door. The six-foot pole was still bound to her hands, but there was no time to free it. Whatever guards might wait outside, even Sakuya's brain was not so riddled with holes that he would remain here wringing his hands. They might be caught the instant they emerged. Even so, some single spider's thread of hope must remain; if they stayed, whoever returned would certainly catch them. That much judgment was left to him.
Without another glance at the writhing guard, Sakuya seized the moment and fled. Kuro—who had, after all, saved him in a fashion—whispered faintly from his shoulder—

target.text: Even his parting threat imitated his boss, and the other man who'd come running in had also taken off right after giving his report, so only Sakuya and Kuro were left in the warehouse (the unconscious henchman didn't count), and all that remained was a vast, empty expanse growing bigger and bigger. For a time, Sakuya and Kuro just exchanged a dumbfounded look, and then he hoisted the girl over his shoulder and ran to the door.

The rokushakubo that Kuro's hands were tied to was still there, but he didn't have the time to untie her from it, and regardless of whether there were any lookouts posted outside, not even Sakuya was soft-headed enough to just remain idly standing here with his arms folded.

Right, so even if he assumed that it was a possibility that he'd be tragically captured the instant he went outside, there surely had to be a strand of spider silk to latch on to, a single straw to clutch at, for if he stayed here, they'd return before long, and then he'd definitely be caught by someone. He still had enough ability left in him to make that judgment, but regardless, turning a blind eye to the guard fainted in agony, knowing this was his last chance to escape, as soon as Sakuya began to flee, figuring that he should carry Kuro over his shoulder, for she had sort of saved him, he was whispered to in a soft voice.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……あんね、クロさっき、棒、振り回す？
　ぶんぶんして、あの人のお股に当たっちゃった時」
source.english:
“…You know, just now, when Kuro was swinging the pole?
Going whoosh-whoosh, and it hit that man's crotch…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いい、それ以上言うな」
source.english: “Enough. Don't say any more.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Hey. When Kuro swung around, the pole? When it went whoom, and hit that man in the crotch.」
【Naomasa】 「It's okay, don't say any more.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でもぉ……なんか……。
　くちゃっ
　って、そんな感じ、で、手にまだ……。
　くちゃっ　　　　───って」
source.english:
“But… Something… Squish. It felt like that. Still in my hands…
Squish—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「言うな、だから言うなぁぁぁっ」
source.english: “Don't say it! I said don't say it!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Buuut……it kinda……. Khrrk it said. Can still feel it, in Kuro's hand……. Khrrk ───it said.」
【Naomasa】 「Don't say it, I said don't say iiiiit!」

source.japanese: その感触がなにを物語っていたのか、想像するだけでおぞましく、ちょっと内股になりながら、倉庫を転び出る───
source.english: The mere thought of what that sensation meant was horrifying. Knees a little turned inward, he stumbled out of the warehouse—

target.text: Even imagining what that sensation signified was terrifying, and while slightly pigeon-toed, he stumbled outside the warehouse───

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あと、それから……」
source.english: “And, also…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「後にしてくれ、今はそれどころじゃない」
source.english: “Later. This isn't the time.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「And then, also, after that……」
【Naomasa】 「Leave it for later, please, now really isn't the time.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あい……でも、あんがと」
source.english: “Okay… But, thank you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ？」
source.english: “Huh?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Aye……but, thanks.」
【Naomasa】 「Aah?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さん、クロのこと、助けようってしてくれた。
　なんとなくわかったの……。
　だから、あんがと」
source.english:
“Mr. Sakuya, you tried to help Kuro.
I could sort of tell…
So, thank you.”

source.japanese: 踏み倒されそうになった代金を回収しようとしていただけだとは、この脳足りんの娘に説明したところで通ずるとは思えず、朔屋はそれ以上構わなかったけれども、なぜか彼の耳朶に思春期、世間知らずの少年じみた熱が通ったのに、朔屋自身訳がわからず狼狽えたとか。
source.english: Explaining to this dim girl that he had only been trying to collect a payment the other man meant to evade would hardly get through to her. Sakuya left it alone. Yet for some reason his ears grew hot, like those of an innocent adolescent boy. He himself did not understand why, and was disconcerted.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san tried to save Kuro. Kuro could tell, kind of……. So, thanks.」

He was just trying to collect the payment that they were going to bilk him out of, but he didn't believe this brainless girl would understand that, even should he try to explain it, and so he stopped paying it any further mind, but for reasons he himself couldn't grasp, a heat reminiscent of a naive, adolescent boy burned in his ears, leaving Sakuya flustered and lost in his own bewilderment.

source.japanese: <01>どうにかクロを助け出そうと願った
source.english: Try somehow to rescue Kuro.

target.text: <01>Prayed for any way to save Kuro

source.japanese: <01>何をしても無駄と諦めた
source.english: Give up. Nothing he did would make a difference.

target.text: <01>Abandoned hope, all would be futile

source.japanese: さて、ブラックジャックでぶん殴られるかそれとも鉛弾の洗礼喰らうか、まず間違いなく荒事に慣れた男達は倉庫の外にも待機している筈なので、さしずめ朔屋は煮えたぎった湯鍋から油弾けるフライパンに飛びこんだレンズ豆も同然、数歩は駆けたけれどすぐ失速して、クロを担いだままそろりそろりと目探る、周囲を取り囲むのはさて銃を構えた黒服か、道中差しを抜いた山賊か、もう朔屋はなにが来ても恐ろしさには変わりなしと、やけくそと悔しさと恐怖のまぜこぜの感情に荒い息をついたところ。
source.english: Now, whether he would be clubbed with a blackjack or baptized in lead, men well versed in violence were almost certainly waiting outside the warehouse, too. Sakuya was a lentil leaping from a boiling pot into a frying pan of spitting oil. He ran a few steps, then quickly lost speed and cautiously searched his surroundings, Kuro still on his shoulder. Would the encircling figures be black-suited gunmen, or bandits with swords drawn? Whatever came, it would be equally terrifying. He breathed hard, caught between desperation, resentment, and fear—

source.japanese: 後頭部にめりこんでくる棍棒もなく、腹腔に盲貫する銃弾もなく、痛いのと言ったら額から目に流れて沁みる汗くらいなもの、汗に薄汚れ脈動するようにぼやける夜灯りの中に、黒服や白スーツの金持ちは確かに立っていて、朔屋は身を強張らせたけれど。
source.english: No club struck the back of his head. No bullet penetrated his abdomen. The only pain was sweat running from his forehead and stinging his eyes. In the night lights, dirtied by sweat and blurred as though pulsing, stood the black suits and the rich man in white. Sakuya stiffened. But—

source.japanese: 彼らはみな一様に朔屋に背を向けてあり、男の尻など見て愉[たの]しむ趣味などない青年はこれ幸いと、とにかく倉庫から遠ざかろうとして、そこで男達があまりに浮き足立っているのにふと足が止まる。
source.english: They all had their backs to him. With no taste for admiring men's backsides, he took this fortunate opportunity to get away from the warehouse. Then their extreme agitation made him pause.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（なにしてんのこの人達？）
source.english: (What are these people doing?)

source.japanese: 彼らは皆して視線を一点集中波止場の果てへ、つい釣られて朔屋も伸びあがるようにして窺えば、向こうは何やら騒然と、ひどく騒然と、まず夜闇の果てを明るませてもくもくと、空に立ちのぼっているのは黒煙だ、輪郭を炎に縁取られて黒い、そちらの方から。
source.english: Every gaze was fixed upon a single point at the far end of the wharf. Drawn along with them, Sakuya craned up to see. Something was in an uproar over there, a terrible uproar: black smoke billowed skyward, brightening the farthest reaches of the night, black with its contours picked out in flame. And from that direction—

target.text: Now then. Would he be violently beaten with blackjacks or suffer a baptism by lead bullets? There'd surely be men practised in the art of violence on standby outside the warehouse too, and Sakuya, best likened to a lentil leaping out of the pot of boiling water and straight into the frying pan bursting with oil, immediately lost all propulsion after running a few steps, slowly and quietly running his eyes over the scene with Kuro still slung over his shoulder.

Well now, who had encircled the surrounding area? Was it men clad in black with guns at the ready, was it mountain bandits with knives brandished? Whatever it was that would come his way, the fear Sakuya felt wouldn't change, and the moment he took a heaving breath, heavy with a messy mixture of despair, frustration, and terror.
【Naomasa】 「…………Huh?」

There was no baton lodging itself into the back of his head, no lead bullets piercing through his appendix either: the only thing he could call painful was the sweat travelling down his brow and stinging his eyes, and there, beneath the night lights, blurry and pulsating as they were through the sweat blotting his sight, the men in black and the rich guy in the white suit certainly stood, and Sakuya's entire body tensed in response, however.

One as all had their backs turned to Sakuya, and to this young man, who did not find any particular enjoyment in staring at the likes of male butts, this was a stroke of fortune, so he made to distance himself from the warehouse first things first, but the men were so inordinately agitated and fidgety that he couldn't help but suddenly come to a halt.
【Naomasa】 （Just what are these people doing?）

They were all focusing their gazes on a singular point at the end of the wharf, and when Sakuya, reeled in against his better judgment, leaned forwards to get a better look, something over there was making a commotion, a terribly noisy one, but most importantly, there was something that set the very edges of the night aglow, a pillar of dark smoke rose towards the heavens, a black silhouette whose outline was fringed with flame, coming from that direction.

source.japanese:
カンカンとの、夜闇を劈くは半鐘の、遠くとも鋭い音色と、数は不明ながらも慌ただしい気配を伝えてくる人々の蠢き。これに白スーツの金持ちはもう頭を抱えるは地団駄を踏むはで、そこに朔屋とクロを脅かした傲慢な居佇まいなどは影も残ってない。
　気を持て余すあまり己の足さえ扱いかねて、ばたばたと右に左に前に後に慌てふためく様のなんとも見苦しく、声だって調子を外し割れていた。
source.english:
Clang, clang. A fire bell's sharp notes split the night, distant though they were. The movements of an unknown number of people conveyed frantic activity. At this, the rich man in white held his head and stamped his feet. No trace remained of the arrogant bearing that had threatened Sakuya and Kuro.
So agitated he could scarcely manage his own legs, he flapped right, left, forward, back. An ugly spectacle. His voice cracked out of tune.

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「あああなんてことだ、あああんなに燃えて、商談が、荷が、荷がァァァ!?」
source.english: “Aah, what a disaster! Look at it burn! The deal—the cargo! The cargo!”

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「お、お、お前達、なにぼけっとつっ立っているんだ、行ってどうにかしてこい、消してこいっ」
source.english: “Y-you! What are you standing there for? Go do something! Put it out!”

source.japanese:
【手下】
「わ、わかりやしたっ。
　……でもどうやって───」
source.english:
“Y-yes, sir!
…But how—”

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「それくらい自分で考えろよ馬鹿ッ。
　何の為に金もらってるんだお前達ッ」
source.english:
“Think for yourselves, idiots!
What do you think you're paid for!?”

source.japanese:
【手下】
「……へいっ！　とにかく火を消して、ヤクはできるだけ運び出して来まさぁ！」
source.english: “…Yes, sir! We'll put the fire out and bring away as much of the dope as we can!”

target.text: The veil of night was pierced by the clanging of a hanging fire bell, the peals sharp in timbre despite the distance, and while the exact number of men was unclear to him, the panicked presence of several people rustling about could be felt. The rich guy in the white suit was already cradling his head in his hands and stamping his feet in frustration, not even a ghost left of the arrogant air he had clad himself in while he threatened Sakuya and Kuro. Assaulted by emotion so powerful that he could barely control his own legs, he stomped right and left and backwards and forwards in a manner so noisily confused that it was hard to watch, and even his voice was cracking.
【Rich guy】 「Aaaaah, this can't be happening, look at it burn! My deal, my goods, my goooods!?」
【Rich guy】 「Y-, y-, you people, why are you just standing here gawping? Get over there and do something, go put it out!」
【Henchman】 「S-, sure thing, boss. ……But how are we meant to───」
【Rich guy】 「You can figure that part out on your own, moron! What the hell am I even paying you people for?!」
【Henchman】 「……Yessir! We'll put out the fire first, then carry out as much of the dope as possible!」

source.japanese:
【金持ち】
「馬鹿っ。もう、馬鹿っ！
　余計なこと言う前に、
　いいから行ってこいってば!!」
source.english:
“Idiot! Oh, you idiot!
Before you say anything else,
just get going!”

target.text: 【Rich guy】 「Idiot. Enough, you idiots! Instead of blabbering about things you really shouldn't say out loud, I told you to just get the hell over there!!」

source.japanese: ───今何やら、朔屋にしても聞き捨てならないような言葉が混ざって、唖然と立ち尽くすうちにも、黒服の手下達、親分格の罵倒にもめげず波止場の奥へと走り出していく健気、金の切れ目が縁の切れ目という輩にも金が続く限りは契約の忠義があるということか、夜灯りの奥、闇濃くなりまさる波止場の向こうへと黒服の色溶けこんでいく、かに見えて。
source.english: Somewhere in that exchange was a word even Sakuya could not ignore. As he stood dumbfounded, the black-suited henchmen set off toward the far end of the wharf, undaunted by their boss's abuse. Admirable. Men whose loyalties ended with the money apparently retained contractual fidelity while it lasted. Beyond the night lights, the black suits seemed to melt into the deepening darkness—

target.text: ───Right then. There were some words mixed in there that even Sakuya couldn't just pretend to not have heard, but even as he stood there in stunned silence, the henchmen clad in black still admirably ran towards the depths of the port without being put out in the slightest by their boss' disparaging words; as the money ends, so does the love, or more aptly put, it seemed like their loyalty would last for as long as the money kept flowing, and the black of their clothes melted into the deepening darkness on the other side of the wharf, or so it looked.

source.japanese:
【手下】
「───わぁ！　うわわわわっ!?」
source.english: “—Wah! Whoa, whoa, whoa!?”

source.japanese:
【手下】
「こりゃぁ……あああっ、ヤッベぇ！」
source.english: “This is—aaagh, this is bad!”

source.japanese: 駆け出した時よりも必死の態で黒服達、また倉庫の常夜灯の圏内に駆け戻ってきて、ただその顔は駆け出す前より悪い汗に滑って、サングラスもずれて、それ狼狽の形相の、強面の怖さ失せにけり、いったい何事が鉄火場に慣れた彼らをと、夜の波止場を凝視した朔屋の耳にこの時届いてきたのは、エンジンの咆哮とそして、闇に錐の先のような白閃穿[うが]つ、あれは銃声だ、撃発光だ！
source.english: More desperate than when they had left, they came running back into the warehouse's circle of light. Their faces were slicker with unpleasant sweat, their sunglasses askew. Panic had erased their intimidating looks. What could have frightened men accustomed to violence? As Sakuya stared toward the dark wharf, an engine's roar reached him. Then white flashes pierced the darkness like awl points. Gunshots. Muzzle flashes!

target.text: 【Henchman】 「───Wah! UWAWAWWAWAH!?」
【Henchman】 「That's……aaaah, oh SHIT!」

In an even more desperate manner than when they had first ran off, the men in black once more dashed back within range of the perpetual night lights of the warehouse, but their faces were slick with a much colder sweat than before they had left, their sunglasses askew, and their expressions of panic had wiped off any remaining trace of intimidation from their fierce mugs.

What in the world could have brought these goons, men so used to scenes of gunfire, to this, he wondered, but what reached Sakuya's ears that moment as he stared fixedly at the night-time wharf, that was the roar of an engine, as well as a flash of white light boring through the darkness like the tip of a drill, and that was the sound of gunfire, a muzzle flash!

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あははは、良い的がある！
　弾に当たるとー、
　痛くて死ぬので注意しな！」
source.english:
“Ha ha ha!
Nice targets!
Watch out—bullets hurt and kill!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ahahaha, we've got some nice targets! Better be carefulー, 'cause if a bullet gets you, you'll die a painful death!」

source.japanese: その野放図な、夜という時間を出鱈目に撹拌する声を聞いて朔屋がまず抱いたのは、安堵の類の感慨でなく、憮然といおうか反撥心といおうか。心に連動して唇が饐えた物でも食ったようにへしゃげる朔屋の見守るうち、波止場の向こうから爆走してくるそれ、四輪駆動の車体の頑丈そうなこと、この場にては頼もしいを通り越して暴威ですらあり、黒服の男達は追い立てられ惑う、銃声響く度に踊るわ踊る。
source.english: At that unbridled voice, stirring the night into chaos, Sakuya's first feeling was not relief. Resentment, perhaps. Resistance. His lips crumpled as though he had tasted something rancid. From beyond the wharf came a vehicle at furious speed. Its four-wheel-drive body looked sturdy; here it was more than reassuring. It was violent power. The men in black were driven into confusion, dancing every time a shot rang out.

source.japanese:
【手下】
「うわあよせやめろうっ！」
source.english: “Whoa! Stop! Cut it out!”

target.text: When he heard that free-spirited and unrestrained voice churning through the hours of the night with reckless abandon, the first thing he felt was not a deep feeling of relief of some sort, it was more akin to glum indignation, or perhaps rebelliousness?

As Sakuya's lips scrunched up, puckering in unison with his heart like he'd eaten something both spoiled and sour while he kept watch over the affair, it came roaring towards them from the other side of the wharf, that thing which looked like the robust frame of a four-wheel drive vehicle; in this case, it had transcended the dependable and transformed into tyrannical violence, leaving the men in black bewildered as they were driven away, dancing and twirling every time the gunfire echoed through the dark.
【Henchman】 「WAAAH, CEASE, STOP!」

source.japanese: 叫んでも無駄の無駄、ジープの蛇行と銃弾に追いつめられてまず黒服が、波止場の縁から叩き落とされるが暗い波の下に、これを朔屋はいい気味だと嘲笑うより、どこか哀れと思ってしまったのは単に彼が愚かなお人好しだからとは言いきれまい。それくらいジープの咆哮と拳銃の乱撃は破壊的で、圧倒的で、小型の嵐と化して波止場に吹き荒れて。
source.english: The cries were worse than useless. Cornered by the jeep's swerving course and bullets, first one black suit was knocked from the edge of the wharf into the dark waves below. That Sakuya felt something like pity rather than gloating at his deserts could not be put down merely to his being a foolish softhearted man. The jeep's roar and wild pistol fire were that destructive, that overwhelming: a small storm raging across the wharf.

source.japanese: 黒服達はそれでも最後まで雇用者を護ろうとしていた天晴れ、中には同じく銃を抜いて応戦しようとした者もあったし、彼らの銃弾はジープの車体に火花散らして運転手の禿頭や後部座席で乱射する女二人を闇の中明るみに出したけれど、射撃の精密さより物を言うのはこの場合我の強さなのか、ジープの驀進と銃撃は留まるところを知らない。
source.english: Even so, they tried to protect their employer to the end. Admirable again. Some drew guns and returned fire. Their bullets sparked against the jeep's body, lighting the driver's bald head and the two women firing wildly from the back seat. But perhaps strength of will spoke louder than accuracy in this case. The jeep's headlong charge and gunfire never faltered.

target.text: He could scream all he liked, it was the height of futility, and having been driven into a corner by the bullets and the zigzagging jeep, most of the men in black were knocked off the edge of the wharf and into the dark waves lurking below; rather than simply sneering in schadenfreude, a part of Sakuya did pity them, and this could not simply be said to be because he was a foolishly softhearted man. That was simply how destructive the thundering of the jeep and scattering curtain of bullets were, how overwhelming it all was, taking the shape of a minor storm and laying waste to the entire wharf.

It should be lauded how, in spite of it all, the men in black still tried to protect their employer until the very last, some among them also pulling out their own guns and attempting to return fire, their gunfire sending sparks flying across the chassis of the jeep and lighting up the cover of dark concealing the bald driver and the two women sitting in the back seats shooting with reckless abandon, but in this case, it seemed that sheer strength of self-will spoke louder than precision in shooting, for the concept of being stopped was entirely alien to both the jeep's unbridled charge and the hail of gunfire.

source.japanese: それは我が強いだろう、やりたい放題勝手気ままだったろうとも、車が迫るにつれはっきりしてくる、運転者の顔半面に躍る龍と後部座席で拳銃を無制限にぶっ放し続ける金髪碧眼の双子の姿、海の持て余し者、陸には居られぬ無法者、信天翁号の水夫長と航海士の双子とあっては。
source.english: Strong-willed, certainly. Self-willed, doing whatever they pleased, certainly. As the vehicle drew closer, the dragon dancing across half the driver's face became clear, along with the blond, blue-eyed twins firing pistols without restraint behind him. The Albatross's boatswain and navigator twins: the sea's unwanted, outlaws who could not remain ashore.

target.text: It certainly was a strong force of will, and they most certainly were also doing whatever they pleased, however they pleased; they grew clearer and clearer the closer the car approached, the dragon dancing on one half of the bald driver's face and the forms of the blonde-haired, blue-eyed twins ceaselessly blasting their revolvers from the back seat, the recalcitrants of the seas, outlaws incapable of existing on land: it was the Bosun and the twin first mates of the Albatross.

source.japanese: 人と言うより人食いの獣めかして逞[たくま]しい歯を向いて、水夫長がハンドルを手荒に取り回す、するとまた一人黒服が落ち、双子が傲慢でかつ心底愉快そうな哄笑を添えて代わる代わるあるいは同時に銃爪を引けば黒服達は踊りというには悲愴に過ぎる様で手足を振り回し跳ね回る。中には命中して倒れ伏す者もあるが、双子にとっては当たろうが外れようがお構いなしの、ただただ己の銃弾によって人が右往左往取り乱すのが面白くてたまらないと言わんばかりの、こちらも水夫長に負けず劣らずの獰猛な笑みであった。
source.english: Baring powerful teeth like a man-eating beast rather than a human, the boatswain wrenched the wheel about. Another black suit fell. Laughing arrogantly, delighted to their cores, the twins pulled their triggers by turns or together. The men flailed and leaped in motions too tragic to call dancing. Some were hit and dropped. The twins did not care whether they hit or missed. Their savage smiles matched the boatswain's, declaring that the sheer fun of making people panic and scatter under their bullets was irresistible.

target.text: The Bosun bared his powerful rows of teeth at them, more man-eating beast than man, wildly turning the steering wheel; another man in black fell; the heartfelt enjoyment of the twins' boisterous, haughty peals of laughter served as the accompaniment while they pulled the trigger in turns, or perhaps even simultaneously, and the men in black flailed their arms and legs and jumped around in a manner too heartrendingly pitiful to be described as dancing.

Some among them had been struck and collapsed to the ground, but the twins didn't care whether they hit or missed the mark, all but saying that they simply found it terribly amusing to see people in disarray, running all over the place from their bullets, both of them displaying a savage grin that could rival even the Bosun's.

source.japanese: 闇を兇悪な光が貫き足下のコンクリートを穿[うが]つ、白スーツの金持ちが引きつけた悲鳴で右に飛ぶ、とお次は飛んだ先でも銃光だ、整髪料と香水の利いた頭髪を何本か弾き飛ばして頭上すれすれをかすめたのに左へ跳ねる、今度待ち受けていたのはジープの猛進、金持ちは咄嗟に周囲の黒服達に助けを求めようとしたけれど、そこで彼は知った、手勢は既に全て撃ち倒されるか海に叩き落とされるかして、残っていたのは自分一人と。
source.english: A vicious light pierced the darkness and chipped the concrete at the rich man's feet. With a convulsive scream, he leaped right. Another muzzle flash met him there, shaving away several hairs stiff with dressing and perfume as a bullet skimmed his head. He sprang left. This time the jeep charged at him. He tried to seek help from his men—and discovered they had all been shot down or knocked into the sea. Only he remained.

target.text: When a vicious light pierced through the dark and bored into the concrete, the rich guy in the white suit screamed convulsively as he leapt to the right aaaand then there was a flash from a muzzle right where he jumped to as well, blowing off several strands of gelled, perfumed hair as he barely dodged the bullet whizzing over his head, and so he flew towards the left instead; this time, the jeep's ferocious charge was what greeted him, and the rich man immediately turned to the men in black surrounding him for aid, however, that is when he realized it: that all his forces had either been shot dead on the ground or knocked into the ocean, and he himself was the only man left standing.

source.japanese: 視界を圧して膨れあがるかのジープのフロントと銃撃に、金持ちは血走った目と上擦った悲鳴を挙げたが、エンジンの咆哮に呑みこまれる、寸前で彼は身を翻[ひるがえ]す先、手下と同じ海。まだ先に落ちた者達の白泡残した波間に高く水柱。
source.english: The jeep’s front end seemed to swell until it filled his vision. Faced with it and the gunfire, the rich man flung up bloodshot eyes and a shrill scream, only for the engine’s roar to swallow it. At the last instant he flung himself aside—into the same sea that had swallowed his men. A tall column of water rose among waves still white with the foam of those who had fallen before him.

target.text: With a storm of bullets and the front of the jeep almost ballooning until it dominated his entire field of vision, the rich man let out a shrill scream with bloodshot eyes, but it was swallowed in the roar of the engine, and on the verge of being blown away, just like his henchmen, he chose the sea. A tall splash of water rose from between the waves of white foam left by those who had fallen before him.

source.japanese: ───この僅かな時間に生じた殲滅劇に、朔屋が快哉よりも恐怖を抱いたとしてもあり得るところ、なにしろジープは勢い緩めず、魂引っ攫われたように佇立していた青年へと突進してきて、それでも止まった、止まったけれど排気熱が鼻先を焼くようなすれすれの、制動も音高くコンクリートにタイヤの焦げ痕まで残して、もしかしたら朔屋も物のついでと轢殺しかけて直前で気づいただけかもしれない。知らぬは気絶したままのクロばかり、きっとそれは幸運なことであったろう。
source.english: —If this annihilation, accomplished in so little time, inspired fear rather than triumph in Sakuya, that was understandable. The jeep did not slow. It charged straight at the young man standing as though his soul had been stolen. It stopped, yes, but so close that its exhaust heat seemed to burn his nose. The brakes shrieked, leaving scorched tire marks on the concrete. Perhaps they had nearly run him down in passing and noticed only at the last moment. Only the still-unconscious Kuro knew nothing. That was surely fortunate.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あっ！　あんなところに馬鹿がいる
　ついでにクロもいる。
　ちぇー……命冥加なことだね二人とも」
source.english:
“Oh! There's an idiot over there.
Kuro, too. Tch…
Lucky to be alive, both of you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひ、轢かれるかと思った……」
source.english: “I-I thought you were going to run me over…”

source.japanese: じゃきじゃきと慣れた手順にローダーで弾倉を詰め直すキサラを、朔屋は救いの女神を、というより黙示の終末に騎行する喇叭吹きでも目の当たりにしたように見つめ、つい後退ったところに浴びせかけられたのが水夫長の蛮声だ。
source.english: Kisara refilled her pistol with a speedloader, her hands brisk with practice. Sakuya stared at her less as a goddess of deliverance than as some mounted trumpeter heralding the end of days. He had just begun to edge backward when the boatswain's savage roar struck him—

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おら新米、さっさと乗りやがれィ！
　ここでぼさっとしてて、奴らに捕まりてぇなら好きにするがいい！」
source.english:
“New boy! Get in, now!
Want to stand there till they catch you? Suit yourself!”

source.japanese: してみると一応は朔屋とクロを救うつもりもあったようだがはてさてはてさて、何故青年が逃げ出さなかったというと場の流れも当然あったが、それより逃げたら逃げたで背後からジープに轢殺されるかさもなくば双子の銃弾にぶち抜かれるという恐怖の方が勝っていたのも、この場合は致し方無しというところ。ジープにクロをまず預けて、おたおたと乗りこむ朔屋を引きずりあげた双子の手は、助けると言うより焦れて痛いくらいであった。
source.english: So apparently they did mean to rescue Sakuya and Kuro, at least in part. Well, well. Why did he not run away? The momentum of events helped, certainly. But stronger still was the fear that flight would bring the jeep down upon him from behind—or, failing that, one of the twins' bullets. In the circumstances, one could hardly blame him. He put Kuro into the jeep first, then fumbled aboard himself. The twins hauled him up with hands more impatient than helpful, and rough enough to hurt.

target.text: ───When faced with this dramatic scene of carnage, which took place in but a scant few moments, there was nothing unusual about the fact that Sakuya was left more afraid than elated, for the jeep didn't lower its speed, charging right at the young man who stood stock-still as though his soul had been ripped from his corpus, and yet it stopped, it did come to a stop, but the hot exhaust was so close to touching him that it felt like his nose were on fire, and it braked noisily, leaving burnt tracks of rubber on the concrete; perhaps they had only noticed that it was Sakuya a second before they were about to run over and kill him while still caught in the heat of the moment?
The still-unconscious Kuro was the only one ignorant of what had happened, and surely that must have been a stroke of good fortune for her.
【Kisara】 「Ah! Of all the places to find an idiot. And Kuro's there too. Tchー……must be divine providence keeping the both of you alive.」
【Naomasa】 「Th-, thought I was about to be run over there for a second……」

While Kisara chambered a fresh set of bullets into the cylinder of her revolver using a speedloader with practised ease and a crisp click, Sakuya just stared at her, less as though he'd caught sight of a goddess of salvation and more like he'd witnessed one of the trumpet blowers riding on horseback at the end of Revelations, and when he at last began to step back from them, he was buffeted by the Bosun's coarse shouting.
【Bosun】 「Come on, green hand, get your ass in a seat already! If you wanna waste time just standing around here so you can get caught by these lubbers, then be my guest!」

Considering what he said, it did seem like they'd come here with the intent to save Sakuya and Kuro, but he'd be damned if he knew how he should respond to that. As for why the young man didn't make his escape now, there was, of course, him being swept along by the flow of events, but more pressing than that, the fear of being run over by the jeep or hit by a bullet fired by the twins as soon as he made to escape was a much bigger factor, so there was simply nothing else he could do in this situation.

He first leaned Kuro against the jeep, and while he fretted over whether to go in the jeep or not himself, the twins reached down to him with their hands and pulled him up, but that was less to help him and more because they were getting painfully impatient.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんであんた達がここに。
　というかあんたら、俺と、ついでにクロをなんて目に遭わせるンだっ。さっき『ちぇー』とかいったのはどっちだ」
source.english:
“Why are you here?
Or rather, what the hell have you put me through? Kuro, too, incidentally. Which one just said ‘Tch’?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「まあそう言うなイ。
　あんた達がこっちにこいつら引きつけてくれたお陰で、あたし等の仕事がやりやすくなった───でも畜生、ええもう畜生っ」
source.english:
“Oh, don't be like that.
You two drew them over here and made our job easier. But damn it—damn it all!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Why are you guys even here? Or rather, what the hell were you just about to do to me, and Kuro too, let's not forget. And which one of you two clicked your tongue just now?」
【Shisamu】 「Now now, don't put it like that. Thanks to you two luring those guys over here, our job got a whole lot easier───but damn, damn it all to hell!」

source.japanese: 踏みこむアクセルの響きよりまだ強く声張り上げ、歯噛みのシサムには朔屋とクロを危地に追いこんでおいて罪悪感の欠片もなく、あの金持ちの語っていたことはやはり真実と青年を落胆させたけれど、その度合いは薄く、どこかでこの暴戻な扱いを受け入れるしかないと諦めてある彼がいる。
source.english: Sisam shouted louder than the accelerating engine and ground her teeth. She showed not a trace of guilt at having put Sakuya and Kuro in danger. So what the rich man had said was true. It disheartened Sakuya, but only faintly. Some part of him had resigned itself to accepting such brutal treatment.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんなご大層にしまいこんでやがっから、
　もっとマシなもんだと思ってたのに！」
source.english:
“After all that fuss hiding it away,
we thought it'd be something better!”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「うはははは、ぜぇーんぶヤクでやがんの！」
source.english: “Bwahahaha! It was all dope!”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ちっくしょーーーーい！」
source.english: “Goddaaaamn it!”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「無駄足もいいところだってのホントに！
　ああもうこれも全部朔屋のせいだ。
　この役立たず、うんこ、うんこ！」
source.english:
“What a complete waste of a trip!
And it's all Sakuya's fault.
Useless! Turd! Turd!”

source.japanese:
水夫長達だけで悔しがり、地団駄を踏むようにアクセルを荒く吹かしているだけならまだしもの、怒りの矛先は朔屋にまで逸れてきて、このままだとせっかく乗りこんだのにまた叩き落とされかねない勢いで、慌てて言い返す。
　朔屋にとっては見知らぬ港であろうと陸に置き去りにされるのはむしろ望むところなのだが状況が状況の、なにしろ背後では、まだ距離はあったけれど追撃の車がちらほらと。ここでジープから弾き出されてはどうしようもない。
source.english:
It would have been one thing if the boatswain and twins had merely raged among themselves, revving the engine as though stamping their feet. But now their anger veered toward Sakuya, and at this rate he might be tossed straight back out after finally scrambling aboard. He hurried to answer.
Ordinarily, being left ashore even in an unfamiliar port would have suited him perfectly. Not in these circumstances. A few pursuing cars were already visible behind them, still some distance away. Thrown from the jeep here, he would be helpless.

source.japanese:
【直正】

　こうしてちゃんと迎えに来たじゃない」
source.english:
“Huh? Don't fuss over details.
We came all this way to pick you up, didn't we?”

source.japanese:

source.english: “If that was the plan, you could've told me from the start!”

source.english: “If we'd told someone as loose-lipped as you, they'd have found out before we were halfway there.”

source.japanese:
疾駆の風の中に金の前髪躍らせる航海士の双子は、流れる港の夜灯りを眸[ひとみ]に宿し、生命の躍動横溢させて美しい、それは夢のように美しかったけれど、朔屋が迷いこんだのは夢は夢でも悪夢といえた。
　信天翁号の面子の好き勝手やりたい放題なこと心得つつあるつもりの朔屋だったが、まだまだ認識が甘かったようで、まさか同じ船に乗りこむ者までその犯罪行為の餌に用いるとはと、青年は強い目眩を覚えてジープの手摺りにしがみつく。
source.english:
The navigator twins' blond bangs danced in the wind of their speed, the streaming harbor lights caught in their eyes. They brimmed with the pulse of life and were beautiful—beautiful as a dream. Yet the dream into which Sakuya had wandered was a nightmare.
He had thought he was beginning to understand how utterly the Albatross crew indulged their every whim. His understanding was still naive. To use even a shipmate as bait for their crimes? Dizzy, he clung to the jeep's handrail.

We're honest sailors.
Where's Providence when you need it?”

Drugs are the one thing we don't touch.”

source.japanese: 水夫長も航海士も何やら豪く激昂しており、話の端々から朔屋が聴き取ったところ、あの白スーツの金持ちがえらく値の張る品を港の奥の倉庫に隠していると聞き及び、朔屋とクロを囮に頂戴に上がったようなのだが───その品というのが麻薬だったらしく、手を出さずに、しかしちゃっかり荷に混じっていたダイナマイトで吹き飛ばして帰ってきたらしい───大人しく引き返すに留めていればいいものを、何故騒動を拡大させるのか朔屋には理解の及ばぬところである。それもさりながら、あらゆる違法行為に平気で手を染めていそうな信天翁号の面子なのに麻薬だけは扱わないというのも、妙なこと、不思議に感じられて仕方がない。
source.english: Boatswain and navigators alike were in a towering rage. From their scattered remarks, Sakuya gathered that they had heard of some extraordinarily valuable goods hidden by the rich man in a warehouse at the back of the port and had gone to help themselves, using Sakuya and Kuro as decoys. The goods had apparently proved to be narcotics, so they had left them untouched—but had obligingly used some dynamite mixed in with the cargo to blow the place up before returning. Why could they not simply have withdrawn quietly? Why compound the uproar? Sakuya could not understand. More puzzling still was that people who seemed ready to commit every imaginable crime refused to handle drugs, of all things.

target.text: With her raised voice louder than the sound produced by the pressed-down accelerator, Kisara showed not a shadow of guilt for putting Sakuya and Kuro in such a dangerous situation as she clenched her teeth; the young man felt his heart sink as he realized that rich man really had spoken the truth after all, but it did not sink far, for somewhere, a part of him had simply given up and accepted this unreasonably violent treatment as inevitable.

source.japanese:
機関長、ロックフォール・王は罐の前で計器を読みつつ、朔屋に訝しげな声を掛けた。この地獄のような船の、それもまさしく釜の番人である彼は、いついかなる時も隆として、ワイシャツには炭の汚れ一つ飛ばしたこともないと噂されており、今日も闇の中に白が炎に映える。だが同時に凄まじい健忘癖の持ち主であると朔屋にも近頃ようやく納得されてきており、根気よく伝令を繰り返した。
　すると紳士はまた穏やかに了解して、そしてまた機関室の徒然などを語り出すのだが、今度はその内容がだんだんと不穏な響きを帯びてくるのである。
source.english:
The chief engineer, Roquefort Wang, addressed him suspiciously while reading the gauges before the furnace. The guardian of the very cauldron of this hellish ship was always immaculate. Rumor held that not a fleck of coal had ever dirtied his shirt. Today, too, its white caught the flames in the dark. Yet Sakuya had at last come to accept that the man possessed an extraordinary tendency to forget. Patiently, he delivered the message again.
The gentleman acknowledged it with the same calm and resumed his discourse on life in the engine room. This time, however, the tale gradually acquired an ominous note.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Incidentally, who might you be? And what business brings you down to a place like this, hmm?」

The Chief Engineer, Roquefort Wang, called out to Sakuya in an inquisitive tone of voice while continuing to read the gauge in front of the steam boiler. He, the veritable keeper of the cauldron on this hellish ship, was always stylish and well-dressed no matter the occasion, and just as rumoured, his dress shirt was not stained by a single speck of coal dust, like a vivid white blaze in the darkness. But at the same time, he was also the unfortunate owner of an appalling form of amnesia, that much Sakuya had, at long last, recently come to accept, and with great patience, he repeated his orders.

When he did, the gentleman calmly accepted the order once more, and then he once again began to recount his idle musings about the engine room, but this time, the contents of his anecdotes began to take on an increasingly unsettling tone.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……君は知っていますか。この窯の中に放り込んだら、人間など一瞬で燃え尽きてしまうことを」
source.english: “…Did you know? Throw a person into this furnace, and they'll burn up in an instant.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……Are you aware of this? That if thrown inside this furnace, the likes of a man would be burnt to ashes in but an instant.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「その時は……あれは燐が燃えるんだろうね。
　美しい、そう、とても美しい蒼い炎を放つことを」
source.english:
“At that moment… The phosphorus must be burning, I suppose.
It gives off a beautiful blue flame. Yes, very beautiful.”

source.japanese: さすがにぞっとして言葉を失う朔屋に、機関長はまた問いかける。
source.english: Sakuya was chilled into silence. Again, the engineer asked—

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「And when that happens……it must be the phosphorus burning, no? A beautiful, yes, an absolutely gorgeous flame of greenish-blue is released.」
To Sakuya, who was naturally left both speechless and with a chill up his spine, the Chief Engineer posed a question once more.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ところで、君は誰ですか。
　そしてこんなところに何の用かね？」
source.english:
“By the way, who are you?
And what do you want down here?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Incidentally, who might you be? And what business brings you down to a place like this, hmm?」

source.japanese: ……どうやら朔屋をからかっているのでも意地悪しているわけでもけして無く、本気の本気で忘却しているらしい。これは用件は紙面にして伝えないといけないと、朔屋、慌ててとって返し、メモを用意して再度機関室へ、彼自身どうにも間が抜けたやりとりだとは思うのだが、機関長その人を前にするとつい畏まってしまう、この男には確かに水夫長とは別質の威が具わっている。
source.english: …Apparently the chief engineer was neither teasing Sakuya nor being malicious. He had genuinely, completely forgotten. The message would have to be put on paper. Sakuya hurried back, prepared a note, and returned to the engine room. He found the whole exchange desperately foolish, yet in the chief engineer's presence he could not help standing on ceremony. The man possessed an authority wholly different from the boatswain's.

source.japanese: ここまですれば用件も棄却されずに済むだろうと、朔屋は腰を据えて機関長の談話を拝聴にかかる。水夫長の把握力が届かないこの領域は、機関長の機嫌を損ねない限り格好のサボタージュの場でもある。
source.english: That ought to keep the message from slipping his mind. Sakuya settled in to listen respectfully to the engineer's conversation. Beyond the boatswain's reach, this domain was also an ideal place to shirk, provided he did not offend its master.

source.japanese: ところが───機関長の今度の話というのが、先ほどまでの話と同じようでいて細部がまるで違う。どうやら自分で話した事も覚えていられないらしい。朔屋、なにやら自分まで記憶の薄暮に迷いこみそうな感覚に囚われて、仕方なく上甲板に戻ろうとするのだが、去り際につい気になって訊ねてしまったところ───
source.english: But—the engineer's next account was the same in outline as the last and utterly different in every particular. Apparently he could not remember even what he himself had said. Feeling as though he might wander into the twilight of memory himself, Sakuya reluctantly decided to return to the upper deck. As he left, however, curiosity prompted one question—

target.text: ……Apparently, he wasn't trying to tease Sakuya or being malicious in the slightest, he truly and genuinely simply seemed to have forgotten. Realizing that he would have to convey his business here through a piece of paper, Sakuya hastily turned back, prepared a written note, then went back to the engine room once more; he himself believed it to be nothing more than a hopelessly inane exchange, but when he stood in front of the man, the Chief Engineer himself, he couldn't help but stand up straight; this man certainly was endowed with a gravitas of a different nature than the Bosun's.

Convinced that, having gone this far, surely the business he came to convey would not be forgotten again, Sakuya settled in and began to listen to the Chief Engineer's remarks once more with respectful attentiveness. For as long as it did not sour the mood of the Chief Engineer, this territory, where the long arm of the Bosun could not reach, made an excellent place to slack off.

However───though what the Chief Engineer spoke of now was similar to what he had just earlier, the particulars were completely different. Apparently, he couldn't even remember what he had said himself. Sakuya, seized by a sensation as though even he might stray into the twilight of his own memory, reluctantly made to return to the upper deck, but just as he was about to take his leave, when he couldn't help but ask about something that had been niggling at him───

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ところでさっきの話は本当ですか」
source.english: “By the way, was that story you just told me true?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「By the way, is that thing you brought up earlier true?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「何の話だね？」
source.english: “What story?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ほら、その窯に人間を放り込むと、一瞬で燃え尽きてしまって蒼く燐が燃えるとか言う」
source.english: “About throwing a person into the furnace. How they'd burn up in an instant, with the phosphorus burning blue.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「What do you speak of?」
【Naomasa】 「You know, about how if you toss a person inside that furnace, they'd burn to ash in an instant and emit a blue flame of phosphorus. You said something like that.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……君は物騒なことを言いますね。
　そんな話、いったい誰から聞いたんだ？」
source.english:
“…What a gruesome thing to say.
Who on earth told you such a story?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……You certainly say some rather unnerving things. Whoever did you hear such a thing from?」

source.japanese: もうなにか、てんでお話にならない。それ以上は聞かずに機関室を出た朔屋の背後で、なにやら室内からとんでもない爆発音と、扉の隙間からもうもうとあふれ出す黒煙と。やっぱりこの船にはまともな人間は居ないらしいと言う、暗澹たる一件となった。
source.english: Really, now—there was no making head or tail of any of it. Sakuya asked no more and left the engine room; behind him came some preposterous explosion from within, then black smoke boiling through the gap in the door—and so the whole sorry business became one more dismal indication that, apparently, there was not a normal human being aboard this ship after all.

target.text: He'd had enough, it was all just a big waste of time. And when Sakuya left the engine room without asking any more questions, some manner of enormous explosion sounded from behind him, and a thick, black smoke billowed out through the gaps of the door. It turned into a dismal affair, one all but saying that there truly were no reasonable people to be found aboard this ship after all.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どうなさったの、直さん。
　またずいぶんと涼しそうな恰好で」
source.english:
“Whatever's the matter, Nao?
Dressed to keep cool again, I see.”

source.japanese:
とある港に寄港中の信天翁号の機関室は、ひっそりと静まり返っていた。
　これが出港間近なら、機関室周りは下級水夫が絶えず出入りして、蜂の巣を突いたようにひどくひどく慌ただしい。出航前の機関室周りは、石炭の積み込みその他で目まぐるしいくらいだが、現在はまだ日数に余裕を残しており、眠りに憩うような穏やかささえ漂わせてある。
source.english:
The Albatross lay in port, her engine room hushed.
Had departure been near, junior sailors would have been coming and going incessantly, as frantic as bees in a disturbed hive. Loading coal and making every other preparation would have kept the place dizzyingly busy. Several days remained, however, and a calm like repose in sleep lay over it.

source.japanese: そんな静謐の機関室の暗がりの中で朔屋は───
source.english: In the darkness of that tranquil engine room, Sakuya—

source.japanese: 猿股一丁の姿を晒してあった。
source.english: stood exposed in nothing but his undershorts.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Whatever is the matter, Nao-san? How remarkably light of dress you are today.」

The engine room of the Albatross, currently moored in a certain port, had reverted to deserted quietude. Were the ship close to leaving port, an endless stream of deck boys would be coming and going all around the engine room, terribly hectic and hurried like someone had stirred up a bee nest. The area around the engine room during the time just before departure was almost dizzying with its bustle, what with the loading of the coal and everything else going on, but right now, there were still plenty of days left of their current stay, and a serenity hung over the place, reminiscent of the repose of deep sleep.
And in the darkness of that tranquil engine room, Sakuya was───

Exposed, clad in but a single pair of sarumata. (TN: Sarumata, written "猿股", literally "monkey-crotch", is a term originating from the Edo period that came to describe Western-style underwear worn by men, in contrast with the traditional fundoshi loincloths, when such underwear was imported in the early Meiji period. They are long, baggy underpants, reaching halfway down the thigh and sitting above the knee.)

source.japanese: その大胆ななりとは裏腹に、しょげ返って身も世もないほど情けない表情を浮かべてある。
source.english: For all the daring of his attire, he looked utterly crushed.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それでこちらは、どなた？」
source.english: “And who is this gentleman?”

source.japanese: 泪の誰何に、半袖のポロシャツ姿の小太りな、両手首に汗止めのサポーターを巻いたその男は、いかにも人好きのしそうな柔和な笑みを浮かべて見せたものだった。
source.english: At Rui's question, the plump man in a short-sleeved polo shirt, sweatbands about both wrists, put on a mild smile of immediate, universal appeal.

source.japanese:
【小太りの男】
「ああ、こりゃどうも。あたしは鬼島と申しましてね。そちらの朔屋さんとは、この午後にお知己にならしてもらいました」
source.english: “Oh, pleased to meet you. Name's Onijima. Had the pleasure of getting acquainted with Mr. Sakuya here this afternoon.”

source.japanese:
【鬼島】
「ちょっとしたゲームの席でね……」
source.english: “Over a little game…”

source.japanese: なにが人好きがしそうなものか。鬼島と名乗った男の笑みは、たちどころにメッキが剥げて底意地の悪さを露呈しつつあった。
source.english: Like him? Hardly. The plating rapidly peeled from Onijima's smile, exposing the spite beneath.

source.japanese:
【鬼島】
「そこで朔屋さんは少しばかり負債をしょいまして。このあたしに。お手持ちの物で払える分はいただいたんですが」
source.english: “Mr. Sakuya incurred a small debt. To me. I've taken what he could pay from what he had on him.”

source.japanese:
【鬼島】
「まあさすがに素っ裸で往来に出てもらうのも可哀相だったんでね、最後の一枚だけは残して差し上げたんですが」
source.english: “But I felt sorry for him, sending him into the street stark naked. So I let him keep that last scrap of clothing.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……でもなぁ。あんなの、どう考えてもイカサマなんだよなぁ」
source.english: “…Still. However you look at it, that was cheating.”

source.japanese:
【鬼島】
「心外な。人をペテン師のように言うのは失礼ですぜ、旦那。……ま、多少『勝負の駆け引き』って奴を使わせてはもらいましたがね」
source.english: “I'm offended. Calling a man a swindler is rude, sir. Though I did employ a little ‘gamesmanship.’”

target.text: And in stark contrast to that bold appearance, he wore a crestfallen expression that made it look as though the world were full of nothing but miserable sorrows.
【Rui】 「And who would you be?」
Rui spoke to somebody, a plump man in a short-sleeve polo shirt with sweat-absorbing wristbands on both his wrists showing her a gentle smile that made him seem the very picture of affable charm.
【Plump man】 「Aah, a pleasure to meet you. The name is Kijima. Earlier this afternoon, I had the privilege of making the acquaintance of Sakuya-san over there.」
【Kijima】 「When he joined me for a little game, you see……」
