To the old hands, all this was no more than a child's errand, something to do on the side. Their seafaring instincts would grow dull at this rate, they said. Why, then, was the Albatross content to remain in such tepid waters?
A junior sailor whispered the explanation to Sakuya later, nearly rekindling his determination to desert.

source.japanese:
───海上封鎖されていたからだそうで。
　───この内海の、北西と南東の両海峡。
　───紀伊と関門と各々呼ばれた両水路。
source.english:
There was a naval blockade.
Both straits leading out of the inland sea, northwest and southeast.
The two waterways called Kii and Kanmon.

source.japanese: この二つの、外海へ出る為の要所を、チューブの両端をがっしり噛み締める留め金のように、官憲に抑えられていたからだそうで。それもこの信天翁号をわざわざ名指しで的に掛けてだというから恐れ入る。事実上どん詰まりに追いこまれたも同然の、しかもそこには海賊崩れという豺狼どもが目をぎらつかせていたとくる。
source.english: The authorities had clamped down on those two outlets to the open sea like fasteners biting into both ends of a tube. And the Albatross herself had been singled out by name. Quite an honor. They were effectively trapped in a dead end, where jackals in the shape of pirates gone to seed waited with glittering eyes.

source.japanese: ここで、物語の時間軸は車輪の輻[や]のようにからから廻[めぐ]って、始まりの海戦その直後に立ち戻る───
source.english: Here the story's timeline rattles around like the spokes of a wheel, bringing us back to the moments immediately after the naval battle with which we began—

target.text: ───Now then. Starting from the circumstances that led to Sakuya being forced to board the Albatross, it all gave off the distinct impression that he had been dragged down into the depths of Naraka by an Ido-Nyuudou, but. (TN: Ido-Nyuudou, written "井戸入道", is not the name of an actual yokai, but many yokai are said to live at the bottom of deep, dark wells. Are you to look into a well at night, perhaps he might scare you with his big, bald head, or pull you down into its depths. Naraka, written "奈落", is Buddhist hell.)

Were we to roughly trace the following days and arrange them into a pointillistic image, spectacles and scenes as narrated hitherto would emerge. Gunfire and life-threatening danger at the drop of a hat, a series of extreme, picaresque situations involving monsters and villains, goodness me, how stimulating, but the stimulation was nothing like the pleasant sensation of finding a pressure point, and the only things stabbing him were needle-tips laced with a lethal, hidden poison; when Sakuya reflected on the events he had experienced thus far, he couldn't help but see clowns from hell cavorting and laughing raucously from the shadows of his memories.

Even amidst such unprecedented days as these, in terms of distance, he'd only sailed what would amount to a stroll through the neighbourhood for a fully fledged sailor, for you see, the ship had yet to leave for the open seas.

The crew of the Albatross was a motley gathering of people, of whites and yellows of unclear racial ancestry, though the only black fellow aboard was a cat, so perhaps their numbers were a little lacking, but in that sense, she was a truly cosmopolitan vessel, and in fact, she would come to make her appearance in every corner of the world; despite being the sort of ship that left one having to worry if her engine would throw a tantrum after merely five nautical miles only to spontaneously founder, she would still travel all across the whole wide world, and given that, what a most splendid of romantic tales it made for.

One could understand why the albatrosses circling the sky above the ship would follow her to the end of the world. Surely they must have fallen head over webbed feet from just how exceedingly wonderful it all was.

That vessel, so widely engaged in the business of trade, was currently smouldering along, laying low in the picturesque coastal waters of the Seto Inland Sea, but naturally, for all that it was overflowing with a beautiful array of nature's colours, Sakuya was surely not possessed of the luxury to take in the view.

It is said that the sea breeze has a healthy effect on the human body, that the idyllic, pastoral view of the inland sea is a pleasant treat for the eyes, and were he to continue working as a sailor on something like an ordinary freighter in these waters, even an outcast from society the likes of Sakuya would have his limbs conditioned reasonably well, and a seed of honest energy would surely have taken root in his spirit, to a certain extent.

But to Sakuya, this had been a series of life-threatening crises far more harmful to his body and mind than the days he had spent intoxicated and chasing skirts had ever been, and when he looked into the mirror with the mercury peeling off as he was about to shave off his scraggly beard, he couldn't help but feel that the circles around his eyes were only getting darker and darker.

According to the old guard, this was nothing more than a collection of odd jobs that amounted to nothing more than 『child's play』, the kind that would just dull their instincts as sailors. So then why was the Albatross content to remain in such a tepid, complacent state of being? When he later had an explanation of the circumstances whispered into his ear by a deck boy, the embers of Sakuya's desire to escape from this ship blazed into glorious flame once more, however.
───It was apparently because there was a naval blockade being enacted. ───In this inland sea, at both the northwestern and southeastern straits. ───In both the channels of Kii and Kanmon.

It was because, apparently, these two nexi used to exit into the open sea, like two clamps biting tightly onto both ends of a tube, had been placed under the control of the authorities. And that this had been done specifically because this Albatross was in their sights was really quite amazing. They had effectively been chased into a dead end, and to make matters worse, a pack of jackals in the form of pirate has-beens were already there, eyes gleaming with hungry malice.

And with that, the axis of time belonging to this story finally starts to clank and clatter as it spins like the spokes of a wheel as we return to the immediate aftermath of the opening naval battle───

source.japanese: 何が哀しうて、戦争も終わって久しいこの世の中で、甲板上で白兵戦と繰り広げなければならないのかと、朔屋は頭を抱えて長嘆息の、手が滑[ぬめ]った。頬に粘ついているのは汗だけではない。脂と血潮のどろどろの、殺し屋智里が斬り伏せた凶漢どもからのとばっちりであった。
source.english: What had he done to deserve hand-to-hand fighting on a ship's deck, in a world where the war had long since ended? Sakuya held his head and let out a long sigh. His hands slipped. It was not only sweat making his cheeks sticky. There was a sludge of fat and blood too, spattered from the thugs Tomosato had cut down.

source.japanese: 目前に兇剣、後頭部に銃口が迫っていた時の絶望と恐怖がほぼ同じ強度で再来して、一歩間違えればこの赤黒いぬるぬるを撒き散らしていたのは自分なのだと、朔屋は座りこんで背を預けていた上甲板のバラックの壁でごしごしと、掌擦りつける目つきは悲愴で、唇も絶叫の形に開きゆく。波飛沫と風に荒れたその板壁だって真新しい弾痕やら刀傷があちこちに、それに今さら気づいて朔屋ははっと周囲を恐る恐る見回した。まだ上甲板には敵の凶手が残っているのではないかと思考が働いたのがようやく今になってで、ただそれくらい朔屋は、泪の船室で敵の返り血を浴びてからというもの混乱と後悔の渦に揉み苦茶にされていたのである。
source.english: The despair and terror of a sword before his eyes, a gun muzzle at the back of his head, returned almost undiminished. One false step, and he would have been the one spraying this dark-red slime. Sitting against a shack on the upper deck, he scrubbed his palms on the wall with a look of anguish, his mouth opening into the shape of a scream. The boards, already weathered by wind and spray, bore fresh bullet holes and sword cuts everywhere. He noticed them at last and glanced fearfully around. Only now did it occur to him that armed enemies might still be on the upper deck. Ever since he had been drenched in their blood in Rui's cabin, confusion and regret had been tossing him about in their vortex.

target.text: What a miserable joke it is: that in this world of ours, where war is a relic of times past, we must engage in hand-to-hand combat on this deck, so Sakuya thought, cradling his head in his hands while he let out a long sigh, but his hands slid across his skin. What stuck to his cheeks was not merely sweat. He was slick with a thick mixture of fat and blood, sprayed all over him when Tomosato the murderer had cut down those scoundrels.

The terror and despair reared their ugly heads again with almost the same intensity as back when he had a dagger brandished before his eyes and a muzzle pushed against the back of his head, for had he made one wrong move, this slimy reddish-black scattered all over could well have been his own; Sakuya planted his rear on the deck, then scrubbed himself clean against the wall of the shack on the upper deck he'd leaned his back against, the look in his eyes as he rubbed his palms together painfully tragic, his lips still parted in the shape of a stillborn scream.

The wooden wall, marked by the wear and tear of ocean spray and wind, was riddled all over with fresh bullet holes and scrapes, and having only just now noticed that, Sakuya timidly surveyed his surroundings. Perhaps there might still be some antagonistic evildoers roaming about the deck; his belated thoughts had only now finally begun to operate in that direction, that was simply how thoroughly Sakuya had been tossed about in the crushing whirlpool of confusion and regrets that was being showered by the spatter of blood exploding outwards from the enemies in Rui's cabin.

source.japanese:
上甲板では───
　下級水夫達が破壊された船上構造物の破片の回収や、敵方の負傷者や死体をまとめて海に叩き落としの後始末で、戦闘後も細々と忙しそうではあったけれど。少なくともそこに動いて朔屋を害するような凶漢どもの姿は一人も見えなくって。
source.english:
On the upper deck,
the junior sailors were still busily occupied with the aftermath: gathering pieces of wrecked superstructure and hurling the enemy wounded and dead alike into the sea. At least no thug remained on his feet to do Sakuya harm.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……退いてくれたか……。
　───助かったああああ～～～」
source.english:
“…They've pulled back…
We made it!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……よく生きてられたな、俺達……」
source.english: “…It's a wonder we survived…”

source.japanese:
深々と吸いこむ空気は潮の匂いとそして生々しい血臭の、それでも吐き気より安堵の方が勝って朔屋は肩から力を抜いた。お気楽一代男の彼でもさすがに死の修羅場では全身緊張で強張って痛いくらいだったのがやっと一息つく余裕が戻ったという。
　頭上から降りてくるのも真新しい死体に歓喜する禿鷲どもの耳障りな音でなく、アホウドリたちの暢気に間延びした鳴き声であるのも手伝った。
source.english:
His deep breath brought salt and the raw smell of blood into his lungs. Relief still outweighed nausea, and the tension left his shoulders. Even this lifelong loafer had been rigid to the point of pain during the mortal struggle. At last he could draw breath.
It helped that the cries overhead were the lazy, drawn-out calls of albatrosses, not the grating voices of vultures rejoicing over fresh corpses.

source.japanese: この安心感をより確かな物とする為に、朔屋は敵手の船が海上をしかと遠ざかっていってくれている事を改める為、ズボンの後に手を回す。例の泪とのゲームで身ぐるみ剥がれた三下チンピラからの戦利品、あの古めかしい望遠鏡は立ち回りの最中に失われたり壊れたりする事もなくお手製のホルダーに収まって、引き出して熟[な]れた金属の質感の折り畳み式を伸ばして覗いて海上を右左、と、拡大された視界の中、三時の方角に敵影の、確かに信天翁号に船尾を向けてあって、朔屋はまた嘆息、今度は生きのびた事への喜びも籠もっていた。
source.english: To put his relief on firmer ground, Sakuya reached behind his trousers. He wanted to make certain the enemy ship was actually sailing away. The old telescope, spoils from the petty thug stripped bare in that game with Rui, had survived the fighting intact in its homemade holder. He drew it out, extended the telescoping sections of well-worn metal, and swept the sea from side to side. There, at three o'clock in his magnified view, was the enemy ship, her stern unmistakably turned toward the Albatross. He sighed again, this time with something of the joy of survival.

source.japanese: 望遠鏡の視界の中の敵船の連中は人数を減らし、船体も朔屋の知らぬうち信天翁号がいかなる反撃を与えていた物か、穴あきチーズのように随分ぼろぼろになっている、けれど、こちらも船にかなりの被害を受けている。今後数日はこの修理に追われるだろうとの厭気も生きのびたからこその、戦闘よりはまだましだと朔屋が珍しく感心物、下級水夫達の手伝いに自ら進んで回ろうとして忙しそうなところに当たりをつけて、きょろきょろしているところに金の髪がぬいと出て、陽光を弾いた。聞こえてきたのは猫撫で声。
source.english: The enemy crew had dwindled, and their ship looked like a hole-riddled cheese. Sakuya had no idea what sort of counterattack the Albatross had managed while he wasn't looking. Their own ship had taken considerable damage too. He would spend the next several days on repairs, no doubt—a dreary prospect, but one available only to the living. It was better than fighting. In a rare, praiseworthy impulse, Sakuya decided to help the junior sailors without being told. As he looked around for somewhere busy enough to need him, golden hair slid into view and flashed in the sunlight. A wheedling voice followed.

target.text: On the upper deck─── The deck boys were gathering together the fragments of the structures on the upper deck that had been broken and dealing with the remaining wounded and deceased from the enemy side by tossing them overboard, and so they also seemed to be scraping along, busying themselves after the end of battle. At the very least, Sakuya could not spot even a single villain who might try to cause him harm stirring over there.
【Naomasa】 「……Did they retreat……? ───I'm saaaaaved～～～」
【Naomasa】 「……I'm shocked we lived through that, all of us……」

The air he breathed in deeply was rank with the scent of the tide and freshly-shed blood, but even so, the feeling of relief triumphed over his desire to vomit, and Sakuya finally let his shoulders hang. Even he, the most easy-going man of his generation, had tensed throughout his whole body to the point it hurt while amidst all this bloodshed and death, but now, he had finally regained enough composure to take a little breather. It also helped that it was not the ear-piercing racket of Old World vultures screeching in joy at the discovery of fresh corpses raining down on his head, but rather the leisurely, drawn-out calls of the albatrosses.
To solidify this feeling of relief, Sakuya decided to reconfirm that the enemy vessel was definitely distancing herself from them, and so he moved his hand to the back of his trousers.

The spoils of victory that had been stripped from that third-rate gangster during the aforementioned game with Rui, that antique telescope, had not been lost or broken in the midst of the fighting, but was instead firmly secured in its holder, one of his own make, and he pulled it out, extended the two-draw contraption with its masterful metal texture, then peered into it and swung his gaze left and right over the sea, and there, in his expanded field of vision, he spotted the enemy vessel at 3 o'clock, and they certainly were heading in the direction of the Albatross' stern; Sakuya released another pained sigh, but this time, it also contained the joy of living to see another day.

Through the telescope, he could see that there were less people on board the enemy ship than before, and had the hull been on the receiving end of some counter-attacks from the Albatross without him realizing, for it looked quite tattered, like a Swiss cheese full of eyes, but their own ship had received a substantial amount of damage as well.

He certainly was disinclined to spend the next few days catching up on the repairs, but that was only an issue to him because he was still alive, so he much preferred it to the fighting, an abnormally admirable perspective for Sakuya; he was making his way over to the deck boys, getting ready to volunteer to help them, figuring out where they seemed most busy, but while he was looking all around, strands of golden hair slipped into view, shimmering in the sunlight. He heard a soft, wheedling voice.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……ねえさあ、朔屋くぅん……」
source.english: “Say, Sakuya…”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「君にしちゃあ、またずいぶん上等な望遠鏡だけどさ、それ」
source.english: “That's an awfully nice telescope for someone like you.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「それ、ギャンブルのカタに巻き上げたヤツだって……？」
source.english: “I hear you took it off someone to cover a gambling debt…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやその……よくご存じで」
source.english: “Well, uh… You know about that?”

source.japanese: 航海士の猫撫で声に覚えた予感は、朔屋が信天翁号に乗船してから得た唯一無二くらいの金目の物を巻き上げられそうな危機、よりはいくらか別の気配を含んで、慎重に出方を待つ、と。
source.english: Her coaxing voice gave him a bad feeling. Not simply the fear that she might confiscate practically the only valuable thing he had acquired since boarding the Albatross. There was something else in it. He waited cautiously for her next move.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……Hey, so, Sakuya-kuuun……」
【Shisamu】 「That's a real fancy telescope you got there, for somebody like you.」
【Shisamu】 「Would that be the thing you swindled from that gambler guy……?」
【Naomasa】 「No, well……I'm surprised you know.」

The premonition he felt from the first mate's ingratiating tone of voice was that of the danger that the one and only valuable item Sakuya had gotten his hands on ever since boarding the Albatross was about to be pilfered from him, but there was a hint of something else contained within, so he prudently decided to wait for her to make the first move, and then.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「うんうん、教えてくれたからねえ。
　……乗りこんできた奴がね。
　質問にこころよくお答えしてくれましたとも」
source.english:
“Oh, yes. Someone told us.
One of the men who boarded.
Very obliging about answering our questions, he was.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「一体なんで喧嘩ふっかけてきたのか、まあうちらも色々と心当たりはないでもない。
　……てか、ありすぎるんだけどー」
source.english:
“Why were they picking a fight with us? Well, it's not as if we couldn't think of a few reasons.
Actually, we could think of far too many.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I sure do, 'cause somebody told me all about it, you see. ……Those guys who boarded the ship, yeah? They were even so kind as to answer my questions.」
【Shisamu】 「Why the hell were they picking a fight with us, I asked, and, well, it's not that we don't have a bunch of guesses as to why. ……If anything, we have far too many, buuut……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「今回のは、あんたが泪さんのトコに引っぱってきたチンピラの、そのボスの差し金だとさ。
　手下がいいように毟られた、腹いせっぽい」
source.english:
“This time it was on orders from the boss of that little hoodlum you dragged to Rui's place.
Seems he didn't like his man getting fleeced quite so thoroughly.”

source.japanese: 話の向きが帯びてきた不穏、強請りたかりとは別なようだがより厄介そうな色合いで、朔屋、たどたどしく誤魔化しにかかる。
source.english: The conversation was taking an ominous turn. Not extortion, apparently, but something more troublesome. Sakuya stumbled into an attempt to change the subject.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ええとその、あ。あんたはどっちだ？　キサラ？　シサム？」
source.english: “Uh, well, oh. Which one are you? Kisara? Sisam?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「This time around, it seems like the guy who instigated all this is the boss of that lowlife you dragged before Rui. Heard his underling got ripped off like that, left him hankering for revenge.」

The conversation had taken an unsettling turn; he was starting to pick up on an undertone far more troublesome than any worry he'd had earlier about being extorted, and so Sakuya tried to awkwardly evade the issue.
【Naomasa】 「Uhmm, errr, right. Which one are you? Kisara? Or Shisamu?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「シサムだよ」
source.english: “Sisam.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃあシサム、
　キサラと離れてて平気なん？」
source.english:
“So, Sisam.
Are you all right being away from Kisara?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I'm Shisamu.」
【Naomasa】 「Alright then. Shisamu, you fine being apart from Kisara?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「命綱繋いであるから大丈夫。
　それよりも───」
source.english:
“We're connected by a lifeline. It's fine.
More importantly—”

source.japanese: 見ればなるほど、腰のあたりから細縄が伸びて船のどこやらへと繋がっていたけれど、こんなのはただの気休めでは、朔屋が疑っていられたほど気楽な話の流れではない。
source.english: Sure enough, a thin rope ran from her waist to somewhere else aboard the ship. Sakuya might have wondered whether it did any good beyond making her feel safer, had the conversation allowed him that much leisure.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「We're connected with a lifeline, so we're fine. More importantly───」

Upon closer inspection, indeed, there was a thin rope extending out from around her waist, connected to somewhere else on the ship, but this was nothing more than a temporary reprieve; the flow of this conversation was not headed anywhere as lighthearted as Sakuya had previously suspected.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「つまり今度のは、あんたのせいじゃないか。
　いらん厄介事持ちこみくさって、
　この馬鹿、このこのこの！」
source.english:
“So this one's your fault!
Bringing us trouble we didn't need, you idiot!
Take that, and that, and that!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「In other words, this whole mess is all your fault, isn't it? Sure dragged a bunch of unnecessary trouble back with you, you moron, stupid, idiot!」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぐええええ、それはどっちかってぇと、泪さんのせい……ぐええええ」
source.english: “Gaaah! If anything, that was Rui's faul—gaaah!”

source.japanese: シサムの手足が打撃の速さで朔屋に絡みつき、片腕が首をもう片腕が腕を、脚は腰の辺りに蛸のように巻きついて、相当に複雑な形に青年を拘束、弾力に満ちた肉を嬉しく味わうどころか全身の筋骨が軋んでばらばらにされていくかのよう。男女の肉体的特性を無視した力に朔屋の肺腑は息を絞り出されて視界も充血していく、なにやらちらちらちらつく幻覚も───洋上に───
source.english: Sisam's limbs clamped around Sakuya with the speed of a blow: one arm about his neck, the other pinning his arm, her legs wound octopus-wise around his waist, binding the young man into a decidedly intricate shape. Far from delighting in so much springy flesh, he felt every muscle and bone creak as though she were pulling him limb from limb. Her strength made nonsense of the physical differences between man and woman; it wrung the breath from his lungs, red seeped into his vision—and now some sort of hallucination was flickering there—out at sea—

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Gweeeh, if I had to blame somebody, I'd say this is actually Rui's fault……gweeehh!」

Shisamu's limbs wrapped around Sakuya with the speed of a strike, one arm around his neck, the other around his flank, and her legs coiled around his waist like an octopus, restraining the young man in a rather complex form, but rather than happily enjoying the bountiful, bouncy flesh rubbing against him, it was like the muscles and bones all over his body groaned as they were ripped apart. With a strength that completely disregarded the difference in physical characteristics inherent to man and woman, the air was wrung out of Sakuya's lungs, his vision was tinged with blood, and there was some sort of flickering, twinkling hallucination too ───on the surface of the sea───
【Naomasa】 「──────Nh?」

source.japanese:
ぐいぐい締めあげられて、溶暗しつつある視界の中だったが、朔屋は懸命に首を捻って一つ呼吸を肺に入れ、気を入れて睨[にら]み据えても幻と消える風もなく、洋上のそれは、また船だった。更に別の入り方で極め技を仕掛けてくるシサムの腕の中、どうにか望遠鏡を目に宛がって焦点を合わせれば、先ほど去っていた敵の船が体勢を整え直して再選挑んできた、のではないようだったけれど。
　向こうがどうやらこの辺りの漁船らしいのが、朔屋の記憶から不安感を引き出した。
　二・三隻、信天翁号に向かってきている。
source.english:
Even as the pressure tightened and his vision began to fade, Sakuya forced his neck around, drew a breath, and stared. The thing did not vanish like an illusion. It was another ship. As Sisam shifted into yet another submission hold, he somehow got the telescope to his eye and focused it. Not the enemy ship they had just driven off, regrouped for a rematch, it seemed.
They looked like local fishing boats. That stirred an uneasy memory.
Two or three of them were heading toward the Albatross.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょっと待って。
　なんか別の船が……？」
source.english:
“Wait a second.
There are some other boats…?”

source.japanese: そして、船に届いた拡声器からの怒鳴り声が、朔屋の不安を現実のものと変えた。
source.english: A bellow from a loudspeaker carried across to the ship, turning his unease into fact.

target.text: He was being squeezed tight with immense force, and his vision was also starting to fade, but Sakuya still twisted his neck with great effort and heaved a single breath of air down into his lungs, but though he concentrated, fixing it with a glare, the hallucination showed no signs of disappearing; that thing on the surface of the sea, it was another ship.

Though he was still held in Shisamu's arms as she shifted into yet another submission hold, this one assaulting him from a different angle, he somehow managed to raise the telescope to his eye, but when he adjusted the focus, was it the enemy ship that had just retreated now coming back to challenge them once more after managing to rally her spirits? No, that did not appear to be the case. It looked to be just a local fishing boat, but its shape elicited a malaise from Sakuya's memory.
【Naomasa】 「Hold on a second. Looks like another ship is……?」
And then, the angry yell that carried all they way to the ship through the megaphone transformed Sakuya's malaise into concrete reality.

source.japanese:
【漁船からの声】
『止まれえ、こんド腐れ船ぇ！』
source.english: “Stop, you goddamn rotten ship!”

source.japanese:
【漁船からの声】
『御魚様殺っておいて、
　逃げられっと思うなよお！』
source.english:
“You killed our sacred fish!
Don't think you're getting away!”

source.japanese:
【漁船からの声】
『今度こそ海ン底さ、叩っこんでくれらぁ！』
source.english: “This time we're sending you straight to the bottom!”

source.japanese: ……シサム・キサラとしてはたかが魚如きに小五月蝿しと煩[わずら]わしい程度のものかも知れない。しかし『板子一枚下は地獄』という箴言は、漁師にとってこの時代にあっても古い言い伝えではなく実感伴う現実の、故に彼らは信心深い、その信心の先をぶち壊されては、怒髪天を衝[つ]くのも頷[うなず]かれよう。この手の怒りは輩[ともがら]に同心に伝播する、漁船の数は二艘[そう]・三艘、後にはまだ幾艘[そう]か追随しているのかも知れない。
source.english: Sisam and Kisara might find all this clamor over a mere fish no more than a tiresome nuisance. Yet for fishermen, even in this age, the maxim that hell lay one plank below was no hoary saying but palpable fact. Hence their piety; and when the object of that faith was smashed, small wonder their rage touched heaven. Anger of this kind spread from one comrade to another. Two fishing boats, three—and who knew how many more might yet be following?

source.japanese: 舳先、波に上下させるのは漁船は質朴な造りではあったけれど、その怒りは船の形を宝珠奪われた龍の顎[あぎと]にも見せて、切り裂く波の白さは牙の間から湧き立つ炎の吐息、戦意においては先ほどの海賊崩れとなんら劣るところなく、純粋さに関しては上だったろう。
source.english: Their bows rose and fell on the waves. Plainly built boats, yet their wrath made them look like the jaws of dragons robbed of their sacred pearls. The white water they cleaved was a fiery breath welling between their teeth. Their fighting spirit was no less than that of the ragged pirates before them, and considerably purer.

target.text: 【Voice from the fishing boat】 『CEEEEEASE, YE ROTTEN SHIP!』
【Voice from the fishing boat】 『Don't think we'll let ye escape! Not after murdering Osakanasaa!』
【Voice from the fishing boat】 『Mark me words, we'll slam ye 'neath the waves to meet Davy Jones!』

……In the minds of Shisamu and Kisara, perhaps they might have seemed nothing more than annoyingly persistent about the likes of a mere fish. However, to fishermen, the proverb of 『There is only a plank between one and perdition』 was, even in this day and age, not merely some old saying, but a truth that felt very real to them, especially to the deeply superstitious sort like this lot, and for the two to have destroyed the head of their faith like that, one could understand why they were left absolutely infuriated.
This particular kind of anger spreads widely among those like-minded, and there were two, maybe three fishing boats in total, and there might well have been several more right on their heels.

The bows of their fishing boats would bob up and down with the waves, but though of a simple construction, that anger made the shape of their boats look like the jaws of a dragon whose wish-fulfilling Cintamani jewel had been stolen, the whites of the splitting waves like the flaming breath gushing forth from the gaps between its teeth; in terms of fighting spirit, they rivalled those pirate has-beens from before, but when it came to the purity of their emotion, they surely surpassed them.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……とかなんとか言ってますが。一等航海士様？
　いやあ人の恨みを買うことにかけちゃ、
　そちらも負けていませんなぁ」
source.english:
“Well, Chief Mate? You heard them.
I must say, you're no slouch at making enemies yourself.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……So, were you saying something? O first mate? Goodness me, when it comes to incurring grudges from others, you know how to put up a good fight, huh?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なに勝ち誇ったツラしてるのよ。
　……あいつらもしつこいなあ、たかが魚一匹で」
source.english:
“What are you looking so smug about?
…They're persistent. All this over one lousy fish.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Why are you acting like you got one over on me here? ……Those guys are damn stubborn. And all for a single stupid fish.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……へっ。やったろうじゃん二連戦！
　あたしのコルトはまだ血に飢えてるぜぇ」
source.english:
“Hah! Two fights in a row? Bring it on!
My Colt's still thirsty for blood!”

source.japanese: と航海士は太腿の銃帯からまだ熱籠もっていそうな回転式拳銃をスカートの裾[すそ]翻[ひるがえ]して抜きはなって、殺られる前に撃ての殺気満々、逸る気勢に銃把に絡めたしなやかな指は凶器としっくりよく馴染で、荒々しいのに奇妙に色っぽく、紺碧の空と海の中で滴るような精気に輝いた。
source.english: She flicked up her skirt and drew the revolver from the gun belt at her thigh. It looked as though it might still be warm. Shoot them before they kill you: she radiated murderous eagerness. Her supple fingers curled around the grip as if they and the weapon belonged together. Rough as she was, there was something oddly sensual about her, her vitality almost dripping from her as she shone against the blue sea and sky.

source.japanese: が、航海士の銃撃姿勢がどれだけ鮮烈だろうと、地元漁師は返り討ちにするにはどう考えてもこちらに一方的に非があり、あまり乱暴な事をしていては寝覚めが悪い。
source.english: But however striking she looked with her gun, there was no getting around it: in this business with the local fishermen, the Albatross was entirely to blame. Violence taken too far would not make for easy sleep.

source.japanese:
朔屋もならず者達の死体には衝撃を受けたが、それでも奴らは逆恨みであり、その結末は受けいれられた、が、地元漁師達に関しては。朔屋は弾の補充に余念ないシサムにいささかやりきれない思いを感じて、信天翁号の進路に目を逸らして、彼女が替えの弾を取り出すべく上着の襟[えり]ぐいと引いたのに内着の薄いので乳房の膨らみがよりくっきりさせているとまた視線を戻して、すぐさま顔をさっき逸[そ]らしていた向きへと振り向けて、なんとも落ち着きのない。一度は好物へと向けていた朔屋の視線を引きつけたのは、海の彼方、迫り来る漁船とは別の方に見えた黒影の一瞬だけではあったが、その一瞬だけで愕[がく]とさせるに足る。
　望遠鏡を助けに目を凝らせば船ではない、船ではないけれど。
source.english:
The thugs' corpses had shocked Sakuya too, but their grievance was misdirected. He could accept their fate. The local fishermen were another matter. Watching Sisam busily replenish her ammunition, he felt a little sick at heart and looked away, ahead along the Albatross's course. Then she tugged her jacket open to fetch more cartridges, and the thin shirt beneath showed the swell of her breasts more clearly. His eyes returned, only for his head to swing back at once in the direction he had just been looking. A restless fellow. What had snatched his gaze from something he liked so much was a momentary glimpse of darkness far out at sea, away from the approaching fishing boats. A moment was enough to startle him.
Through the telescope, he saw it was not a ship. Not a ship, but—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……盛り上がってるところ済まないけどさ。
　なんか、こっちの進路……」
source.english:
“Sorry to interrupt while you're having fun,
but there's something ahead of us…”

source.japanese:
立ち籠めていた。
　暗雲だった。
　まだ相当距離を隔てていたが、相当に大。
　各部で濃淡の度合いはあっても色は黒。
　予感させるものは───嵐。
source.english:
It was gathering.
Dark cloud.
Still a considerable distance away, but immense.
Darker in some places than others, yet black throughout.
What it promised—a storm.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あれ、嵐の先触れっぽくないか？」
source.english: “Doesn't that look like a storm coming?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……Heh. Let's do it then, round two! My Colt still thirsts for blood.」

And so the first mate pulled out her revolver, still hot to the touch, from the gun belt around her thigh, the motion flipping up her skirt in the process, filled to the brim with a determination to shoot to kill before they could get her first; driven by an impatient spirit, her lithe fingers coiled around the grip with a well-accustomed touch, a sight at once brutal yet strangely erotic, radiant with a dripping vitality shimmering amidst the deep azure of the sky and sea.

Still, no matter how striking a figure the first mate cut in her shooting stance, there was no escaping the fact that they were entirely in the wrong; doing something too ruthless to the local fishermen, like striking down their would-be avengers, would weigh too heavily on his conscience for him to get a good night's sleep.

Sakuya had been shocked by the corpses of those scoundrels, but their anger had been completely baseless, so he had come to terms with their fate, but the local fishermen were a different story. Sakuya found it hard to tolerate how the only thing on Shisamu's mind was replenishing her supply of bullets, so he diverted his eyes to the course of the Albatross; when the woman tugged hard at the collar of her jacket to reach some spare bullets, the thinness of her inner layer only made the swell of her breasts all the more pronounced, and so his gaze drifted back towards her form for a moment before he whipped his head back to where he'd averted his gaze once before. How incredibly restless a man.

What had pulled on Sakuya's gaze so, even after he'd already caught sight of his favourite treat, was a black shadow on the distant horizon, one coming from a different direction than the approaching fishing boats, spotted for but an instant, but that instant alone was enough to alarm him. When, with the help of his telescope, he strained his eyes to get a better look, he realized that was no ship. It was no ship, yes, but.
【Naomasa】 「……Sorry for interrupting you while you're all fired up. But there's something, dead ahead……」

They hung low and heavy. They were dark clouds. Though they were still far away, they were substantial in size. Though the depth varied across their different parts, their colour was all black. It foreshadowed───a tempest.
【Naomasa】 「Wait, doesn't that look like the precursor to a storm?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「どれどれ……？
　───確かに。こりゃあマジっぽいね。
　面白いことになってきた」
source.english:
“Let's see…
Yeah. That looks serious.
Things are getting interesting.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なにが面白いんだようっ。
　追っ払ったと思ったらまたすぐ別口の追っ手、しかもかんかんになってるとくる」
source.english:
“What's interesting about it?
We chase one lot off and another comes after us straight away, mad as hell!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「その上嵐まで来そうだってのに。
　ああどうしようどうしよう。
　今度こそ駄目だぁぁぁぁぁ……」
source.english:
“And now a storm on top of everything!
What do we do? What do we do?
This time we're finished…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Let me see……? ───It sure does. And it's looking pretty serious too, huh. Now things are getting interesting.」
【Naomasa】 「What do you mean "interesting"? As soon as I thought we'd chased them off for good, another group of pursuers show up, and these guys are steaming mad.」
【Naomasa】 「And on top of that, there's a storm coming. Aaah, what do we do, what do we do? This time it's all oveeeeer……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「はっ！　なにさ狼狽えンじゃないよ、こんな成り行きくらいで。こんなの屁みたいなもんじゃない。
　むしろこっからが信天翁号の本領さぁ！」
source.english:
“Hah! Don't lose your head over a little thing like this. It's nothing but a fart.
This is where the Albatross really comes into her own!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「本領て……」
source.english: “Comes into her own…?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Hah! This isn't worth losing your head over, not with the way things are going here. This isn't even a fart in the wind. If anything, this is where the Albatross really shines!」
【Naomasa】 「Really shines, you say……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「クロんとこに行っておいで朔屋。
　それとも私とくる？　キサラんところに戻るけど」
source.english:
“Go see Kuro, Sakuya.
Or come with me? I'm going back to Kisara.”

source.japanese: ───連戦と嵐の先触れにシサムはたじろぐどころか伸びやかな手足を勝負に挑む競技者のように屈伸させたで、朔屋の鼻に届いたのは香りだ。ただ盛りの娘ではあっても長い船員暮らし、まして一戦闘の後では甘いとは言えず、リーファージャケットに染み着いた油と硝煙と、そして汗との匂いでややもすれば悪く臭う、のに、彼女の体臭は奇妙に、男、雄に響くもので。汗を含んで濡れ光る金の髪も項[うなじ]の産毛も、それが躍動する有り様を彼女の匂いを嗅ぎ取れるくらいの近くで眺めていたいと思わせる、たとえそれが悪事だろうとも、容認しかねる暴力行為であろうとも。きっと彼女の片割れも同じような姿であろう。
source.english: Far from flinching at another fight and the approaching storm, Sisam flexed her long limbs like an athlete preparing to compete. Sakuya caught her scent. A young woman in her prime, yes, but a longtime sailor, and fresh from a battle. It was hardly a sweet fragrance: oil and gunsmoke ingrained in her reefer jacket, mingled with sweat, could easily have stunk. Yet her body's smell spoke strangely to the male in him, the animal. Her golden hair glistened with sweat, as did the fine hairs at her nape. He wanted to watch her in motion from close enough to smell her, even if she was doing something wicked, committing violence he could not condone. Surely her other half would present much the same sight.

source.japanese: ───だから朔屋は、このままシサムと共にあって、双子の片割れの許に赴くか、それとも───
source.english: So would Sakuya stay with Sisam and go to her twin, or—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「You should go pay Kuro a visit, Sakuya. Or do you want to come with me? I'm heading back to Kisara.」

───Shisamu flinched not in the face of a series of battles nor the presage of a storm; on the contrary, she was bending and stretching her supple limbs like an athlete contending in a competition, and a fragrance reached Sakuya's nose. For all that she was a girl in the prime of her youth, she had lived on a ship for a long time, not to mention just finished a battle, so it could hardly be called sweet; with the gunpowder smoke and oil that stained her reefer jacket, as well as the stink of her sweat, it was more apt to be called a foul stench, and yet, the woman's body odour resonated strangely within him, as a man, as a male.

Her golden hair, shimmering wet with sweat, and the fine down at the nape of her neck throbbed with such vibrant motion it made him long to watch her from close enough to breathe in her scent, even if that might have been a wrongdoing on his part, the sort of violent act considered intolerable. Surely her other half was in a similar state.
───Therefore, did Sakuya remain with Shisamu, heading towards her twin half, or did he instead───

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだかよく判らないが、クロのトコに行けばいいんだな？　じゃあ俺はそっちに！」
source.english: “I'm not quite following, but I should go to Kuro, right? Off I go, then!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「I don't really understand why, but I just gotta head to where Kuro is, right? Alright, I'll go there!」

source.japanese: 迷ったけれど朔屋は、結局クロのところへ走る事にした。双子の姿は確かに奇妙な吸引力を放っていたが、それでも白子の少女の事を言われると、あの哀れでか弱い姿は朔屋の憐憫に訴えかける。
source.english: After some hesitation, Sakuya decided to run to Kuro. The twins certainly exerted a peculiar attraction, but mention of the albino girl brought that pitiful, frail figure to mind and appealed to his compassion.

source.japanese: クロは船内の船長の『箱』の中にまだいるはずと、船員服の上着を脱いで袖[そで]を腰に巻き、朔屋はバラックの合間駆け抜けて中層甲板に続く昇降段へ、疲れきっている脚なのに、青年が危惧していたよりは不思議に軽く言う事を聞いてくれた。
source.english: Kuro should still be in the captain's ‘box’ inside the ship. Sakuya took off his uniform jacket, tied its sleeves around his waist, and ran between the shacks toward the companionway to the middle deck. Exhausted though his legs were, they obeyed with an unexpected lightness.

target.text: Though he hesitated, in the end, Sakuya ran to Kuro's side. The figures of the twins certainly emanated a strange power of attraction, sucking him in, but still, whenever the albino girl was brought up, that miserable, frail figure of hers appealed to Sakuya's compassion.

Kuro should still be in the Captain's 『box』inside the ship, so he stripped off his sailor jacket, tied the sleeves around his waist, then ran through the gaps between the shacks towards the ladder leading to the middle deck; in spite of how fatigued his legs were, they obeyed his commands far more readily than the young man had feared.

source.japanese: クロのところへ走る朔屋の、この嵐と新たな敵襲にあの白子の少女がなんの役に立つのかとんと判らぬ介ではあったけれど、あの双子は何やら確信めいたものさえ抱いている様子で、ならば従ってみるのも面白いだろうと。　で『箱』のところに戻ると、水夫長が一足先に蓋を開けようとしているところであったが、その顔はこの腕力派の老水夫にしては珍しく懸念に揺らいでいた。
source.english:
Running to Kuro, he had no idea what the albino girl could possibly do about a storm and a fresh attack. But the twins seemed almost certain of something. It might be interesting to take their advice.
When he reached the box, the boatswain was already there, about to open the lid. For once, concern troubled the old bruiser's face.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「水夫長、まだ別口の追っ手が。
　それから……っ」
source.english:
“Bosun! We've got another lot after us.
And—”

target.text: Sakuya was running to where Kuro was, not that he really had the first idea what kind of help that albino girl could be in the face of a storm and a new enemy assault, but that twin seemed to carry some kind of conviction about it, so it might also be interesting to just do as she told him. So, when he returned to where the 『box』was, the Bosun had arrived one step ahead of him, already about to open the lid, but his face, quite unlike this old sailor with a proclivity for using brute strength, was wavering with concern.
【Naomasa】 「Bosun, we've got more pursuers coming, from a different group. And then……」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう新前。わかっとるわい。
　そんな顔でクロんとこに駆けてきたところをみると───」
source.english:
“Aye, new boy. I know.
And if you've come running to Kuro with that look on your face—”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Ho there, green hand. I know that. And if you're running to get Kuro with a look like that on your mug, then that means───」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「やっと出してくれた……ああ臭かった。
　今度ちゃんとお掃除しておかないと」
source.english:
“Finally, you've let me out… Oh, it stank in there.
I'll have to clean it properly next time.”

source.japanese:
───子猫の首根っこでも摘[つま]むように引きずり出されたものと、思いきやクロは自ら飛び出してきて、その挙動が俊敏、そう俊敏だったのだ。あの何時もおどおどと縺[もつ]れるような足取りの彼女が。その時点で朔屋は違和感を抱いていたし、船内通路にしゃんと、そうしゃんとだ、立ったクロに青年は目を緩く見開き下顎を落としての間抜け面、裏切られたような衝撃さえ襲ってきて、そう、裏切られていた。
　朔屋が船内の役立たず仲間と勝手に見なして、後ろ向きな共感を向けていたクロが、この今のクロは。
source.english:
He expected her to be hauled out by the scruff like a kitten. Instead, Kuro sprang out herself, and her movements were brisk. Yes, brisk. The girl whose frightened feet were always stumbling over one another. Already, something felt wrong. When she stood straight in the passage—yes, straight—Sakuya stared with slack eyes and a hanging jaw. He felt almost betrayed. And he had been betrayed.
Kuro, whom he had arbitrarily classed as a fellow useless person aboard, whom he had approached with the sympathy of shared inadequacy—this Kuro before him now—

source.japanese:
同じ素材なのに、日陰の裏なりの花を造る担当の神様から、強風に真っ向から羽ばたく強い翼の鳥達担当の神様が解体して造り直したように、その挙措、雰囲気からして全く別のクロだった。何しろ背筋に芯が通っている、そればかりが双眸に宿るは透徹した意志の光、朔屋があれは別の世界の生き物だとさっさと自分を仲間外れにした、己の生を己の力で踏破していく者達特有の。
　水夫長さえ唇を強く引き結んだけれど、彼にはまだ見覚えた貌[かお]であったのか、頼もしげに頷[うなず]いて、
source.english:
It was as if the god responsible for stunted flowers in the shade had handed his work to the god of birds whose powerful wings beat straight into the gale, and the latter had dismantled her and remade her from the same materials. Her bearing, her entire presence, belonged to another Kuro. There was firmness in her spine, and a light of lucid purpose in her eyes. The look particular to people who made their way through life by their own strength: creatures of another world, Sakuya had long ago decided, excluding himself at once.
Even the boatswain pressed his lips together. But this was a face he recognized, apparently. He nodded with renewed confidence.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「You finally let Kuro out……aaah, that reeked. Need to give it a good cleaning later.」

───She was pulled up like a kitten grabbed by the scruff of the neck, or so he thought, but Kuro had jumped out herself, and the action was quick and nimble, yes, quick and nimble. That girl, always shuffling around with a gait that made it seem she'd trip over her own feet any second. That very moment, Sakuya began to harbour a profound sense of wrongness within himself, and she stood up neatly and properly in the passageway, yes, properly; Sakuya looked like an idiot as he slowly opened his eyes wide and dropped his jaw when Kuro stood up, and he was assaulted by a shock as though he'd been betrayed, yes, been betrayed.
Sakuya had selfishly considered her a fellow comrade-in-uselessness aboard this ship, and Kuro, whom he'd come to feel a retrogressive sort of sympathy for, right now, that Kuro, she was.

Though forged from the same material, it was like she had been taken from the hands of the goddess in charge of creating frail, shade-growing blossoms only for the god in charge of the birds that fly headlong into the gales on their powerful, storm-defying wings to dismantle and rebuild her anew; from her bearing, the air she was clad in, this was a completely different Kuro. Above all, a steel core ran through her spine, and not just that, her twin orbs held a lucid light of clear resolve, the sort that made Sakuya quickly distance himself from her, labeling her a creature from another realm; it was a gaze uniquely present in those who forge a path through existence by virtue of their own inner strength.
Even the Bosun pursed his lips tightly, but perhaps it was a face he recognized, for he nodded reassuringly,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「あんたがその顔になってるってことは……。
　おいクロ、しりとりだ。
『鯨』！」
source.english:
“If you've got that look…
Kuro, word chain.
Whale!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「If you've got a look like that in your eyes, that means……. Oi, Kuro, time for shiritori. 『Whale(Kujira)』!」

source.english: “…Elephant.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……『Trumpet(Rappa)』」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……『パイナップル』」
source.english: “…Trumpet.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……『Pineapple(Painappuru)』!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「『坩堝』」
source.english: “Telescope.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「『Crucible(Rutsubo)』」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「『ボイラー』」
source.english: “Engine.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「『Boiler(Boiraー)』」

source.english: “Eel!”

source.japanese: 驚くまいてや、しりとりとなると掛けあい最初の一回目で『ん』を出して負けるクロが、流暢に続けているではないか。
source.english: Wonder of wonders: Kuro, who invariably lost the word-chain game on her very first answer, was keeping it going as fluently as you please.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「『Chili oil(Raーyu)』!」
Believe it or not, Kuro, who would usually lose at shiritori on the very first exchange by saying a word ending in 『n』, is actually continuing the chain fluently!

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……よし。
　どうやら本気で来るようだな」
source.english:
“…Right.
Looks like it's really coming.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だからそう言ってるじゃないッスか。
　シサム・キサラの時の漁師どもみたいだけど、漁師ってのは気が荒いし、
　喧嘩となると容赦しませんぜ！」
source.english:
“That's what I've been telling you!
They're those fishermen from the Sisam-and-Kisara business. Fishermen are a rough lot,
and they don't hold back in a fight!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Alright. Looks like it's actually coming.」

【Naomasa】 「No, didn't I already tell you that? It looks like it's the fishermen from back during that time with Shisamu and Kisara, but these fishermen are real bad-tempered, and if this turns into a fight, they won't show us any mercy!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そっちのことじゃないよ、朔屋さん。
　嵐が来る。クロには感じられる。
　澄んだ水みたいに───全部がはっきりしてる」
source.english:
“Not that, Mr. Sakuya. A storm is coming. Kuro can feel it.
Like clear water—everything is so distinct.”

source.japanese: 声だって変わっているのだ。湿気と錆に緩んだ弦を、磨き直して調律したように耳を凛と叩き、滑舌も呂律も整って、一枚の無垢の白金の板だ。
source.english: Her voice had changed too. Strings loosened by damp and rust had been polished and tuned again, striking his ear with a clear note. Her tongue no longer stumbled over her words. A sheet of pure platinum.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「行こう、操舵室へ！
　嵐が来るよ！」
source.english:
“Come on, to the wheelhouse!
The storm's coming!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え。なにこれなにこのクロ。
　お前、閉じ込められすぎて、頭がやられたか？　それとも、悪いクスリにでも手を出したか？」
source.english:
“Huh? What is this? What the hell kind of Kuro are you?
Did being shut in there too long scramble your brain? Or have you started taking some nasty drug?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「He's not talking about them, Sakuya-san. A storm is coming. Kuro can sense it. Everything is sharp now─── Like looking through clear water.」

Even her voice had changed. As though strings, loosened by moisture and rust, had been polished and tuned once more, it struck his ears with a cold dignity, and both her articulation and speech were also free of flaws, like a solid plate of pure platinum.
【Kuro】 「Let us be off, to the wheelhouse! The storm is approaching!」
【Naomasa】 「What? What is happening, and who is this Kuro? Were you locked in the box for too long and hit your head? Or did you maybe try some bad drugs?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……そうか。お前初めてだったな。
　こいつはよ、こうなんだよ。
　嵐が来るとこうなるんだよ。
　だから『嵐を呼ぶ船長』なんだ」
source.english:
“…Right. Your first time seeing this.
This is how she gets. When a storm's coming.
That's why she's the ‘storm-calling captain.’”

source.japanese: どうやら水夫長は、しりとりが続くがどうかでクロの覚醒の度合いを測っていたようだ。一回で終わってしまうようならクロのおつむは平常運転、難しい事は考えられず舌っ足らず、それが今のように続くとなると、彼女の頭が活性化し始めたという事、すなわち嵐の到来を告げている。言うなれば気圧計のようなもので、だから水夫長は事あるごとにクロにしりとりをふっかけていたのだろう。
source.english: Apparently, the boatswain had been using the word chain to gauge how far Kuro had awakened. If the game ended after one exchange, her mind was functioning normally: unable to handle complicated thoughts, her speech clumsy. If she could keep it going, as she did now, her brain had begun to stir. A storm was on its way. A sort of barometer. That must have been why the boatswain kept challenging her to word chains at every opportunity.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Right. This would be your first time. This is what this girl here's like. When a storm comes, she changes into this. That's why she's the 『Stormcalling Captain』」

It seemed like the Bosun had been measuring the extent of Kuro's awakening by seeing if she could continue the shiritori chain. If it ended in one round, then Kuro's brain was operating at regular capacity, unable to think of anything too difficult and tied of tongue, but if it continued on like it did just now, it meant the girl's head had started to activate; that is to say, it was a harbinger of the arrival of a storm. In other words, she was like a barometer, and that was surely why the Bosun kept challenging Kuro to play shiritori whenever the chance arose.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「朔屋、てめえもついてこい。てめえにもなにかやることくらいあんだろうからな」
source.english: “You come too, Sakuya. There ought to be something even you can do.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Sakuya, you come with us too. There's gotta be something there even you can manage.」

source.japanese:
操舵室へ向かう三人、朔屋にはクロのしゃっきりした姿が信じられないけれど───
　なにやら一抹の淋しさも味わっていたけれど、それでもこのクロならば嵐にも揺るがないだろう。何をしでかしてくれるかは未知数ではあったが。
source.english:
The three headed for the wheelhouse. Sakuya could scarcely believe Kuro's new vigor.
It left him with a faint loneliness too. But surely this Kuro could stand firm against a storm. What she might actually do remained to be seen.

target.text: The three headed for the wheelhouse, and though the straightness of Kuro's posture still beggared belief to Sakuya─── For some reason, he even felt a touch of loneliness; still, as long as Kuro was like this, she would surely not waver before this storm. It still remained an unknown just what exactly she'd be doing, however.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こんな時にクロのところに行ったって仕方ないだろう。あんた達と一緒の方がましだ。また白兵戦となったら、あんた達の後に隠れさせてもらうわ」
source.english: “What's the point of going to Kuro at a time like this? Better to stick with you two. If there's more hand-to-hand fighting, I'll hide behind you.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Surely there'd be no point in heading to Kuro at a time like this. Going with you two would be better. If we get into close combat again, I'll be hiding behind your skirts.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんだってそうヘタレかなあんたは。
　まあいいけどさ、今ならクロのトコに行けば、面白いもんが見られるけど」
source.english:
“Why are you such a coward? Fine, whatever.
Though you'd see something interesting if you went to Kuro now.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Why do you have to be such a sissy? Well, whatever, but if you were to go to Kuro right now, you'd get to see something interesting.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「じゃ、とりあえずキサラんとこに戻ろう」
source.english: “Let's go back to Kisara, then.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Alright, let's go back to Kisara for now.」

source.japanese: 命綱を辿ってキサラの元に戻ると、舷側で、片づけた敵の死体を海に叩き落として、面倒なのは何時だって後始末、やれやれと肩を叩いて伸びをした、貌が朔屋とシサムをみてぱっと綻[ほころ]んだ。
source.english: They followed the lifeline back to Kisara. At the rail, she flung an enemy corpse into the sea, patted her shoulders, and stretched. Cleaning up was always the nuisance. Then she saw Sakuya and Sisam, and her face brightened.

target.text: As they followed the lifeline and returned to where Kisara was, there she stood by the bulwark, throwing the corpses of the enemies she'd bumped off into the ocean, the sort of cleanup that was troublesome but always had to be done, and with a "good grief", she tapped her shoulders to relieve the tension, stretched, and her face instantly broke into a broad smile upon spotting Sakuya and Shisamu.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あ、いいところに来た。この死体、海に叩っこむの手伝え……って、シサム？　朔屋もだけど、なに真面目な顔になってんの？」
source.english: “Oh, good timing. Help me chuck this stiff overboar—Sisam? Sakuya too. What's with the serious faces?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Aah, you came at just the right time. Help me toss these stiffs overboard……wait, Shisamu? Well, you too, Sakuya, but what's got you looking so serious?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんか敵のお代わりが来てるけど、あんな漁師風情、どうにでもなるじゃん」
source.english: “Looks like another helping of enemies is coming, but a few fishermen? We can handle them however we like.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Seems like another group of enemies are joining the fray, but we can easily handle those lousy fishermen.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「違うよキサラ。嵐が来るみたい。
　そうとなりゃ、話は別でしょ？」
source.english:
“That's not it, Kisara. A storm's coming, apparently.
That's a different matter, isn't it?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「That's not it, Kisara. Looks like a storm's brewing. And if that's the case, it's a whole different kettle of fish, right?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……それホント？」
source.english: “…Really?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……Is that true?」

source.japanese: 疑わしげに眼を細めたそこへ、駆けてきた一人の下級水夫は息を弾ませての前傾姿勢、三人の前を勢いに行き過ぎて近くの索具を掴んで慣性を殺して、焦る仕草が朔屋達の報せが真実であることを示す。
source.english: As she narrowed her eyes in doubt, a junior sailor came running, bent forward and panting. His momentum carried him past all three of them; he grabbed the nearby rigging to stop himself. His urgent gestures confirmed their news.

target.text: From where she narrowed her eyes in doubt, a single deck boy came running, panting and leaning forwards, his momentum carrying him past the three of them as he grabbed a piece of rigging to dampen his inertia, his anxious demeanour pointing to Sakuya and Shisamu's tidings being true.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あ、こんなところにいた。
　一等航海士、船長が呼んでます。
　操舵室に来てって」
source.english:
“Oh, there you are. Chief Mate,
the captain's calling for you.
Come to the wheelhouse, she says.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Ah, so this is where you were. Chief mates, the captain has summoned you. Come to the wheelhouse, she said.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「クロ、じゃなくて『船長』になってる？」
source.english: “She's not Kuro anymore? She's the ‘captain’?”

source.japanese: はい、と頷[うなず]く下級水夫の頭をキサラはご褒美に撫でてやる、と、帽子がずれて、栗色の髪がふわふわさらさらと、くすぐったげではあったがこの下級水夫は素直な質[たち]であったと見えてまんざらでもなさそうな、得意気に微笑んで次の相手に伝える為にまた駆けていく。
source.english: He nodded yes, and Kisara rewarded him with a pat on the head. His cap shifted, releasing a soft flutter of chestnut hair. It seemed to tickle, but this junior sailor was apparently an agreeable sort and rather pleased. He smiled proudly and ran off to deliver his next message.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「So it's "the captain" now, not just Kuro?」

Yes, he nodded in return, and Kisara patted him on the head as a reward; when she did, his hat slid off, chestnut-brown hair fluffy and silky, and while he looked a little embarrassed, this deck boy was possessed of an honest nature, so he didn't look all that displeased, instead proudly smiling and taking off once more to convey the message to the next person.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「本気だなこりゃ。クロより先に勘づくたぁ、朔屋にしてはよくやった。偉い偉い」
source.english: “This is serious, then. You noticed before Kuro? Good work, for you, Sakuya. Well done, well done.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなん褒められたかてさぁ……。
　どうなんのよこの船。
　敵は追加でやってくる、おまけに嵐だ」
source.english:
“What good's praise going to do me…?
What's going to happen to the ship?
More enemies coming, and a storm on top of that!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「船は浮いてられるのが不思議なくらいのオンボロ、……うわあああ……今度こそダメだこりゃあ！」
source.english: “This rotten tub's a miracle just to stay afloat… Aaaah… This time we're really done for!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「This is getting serious. And you even noticed before Kuro, that's a job well done for someone like you, Sakuya. Good boy, good boy.」
【Naomasa】 「What good's praise gonna do me……. What's gonna happen to the ship? There are more enemies coming, and as if that's not enough, there's also a storm.」
【Naomasa】 「And the ship's so decrepit that it's a miracle she can remain afloat, ……waaaah……this time it's over for sure!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こんなコトくらいでオタつくんじゃないの。
　喧嘩ふっかけられるンなんて慣れッコだし、
　嵐なんて───見せてあげるよ朔屋」
source.english:
“Don't panic over a little thing like this.
We're used to people picking fights.
As for storms—I'll show you, Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Don't get all flustered over something this minor. We're used to people trying to pick a fight with us, and a little storm─── we'll show you, Sakuya.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そう、見せてあげる。
　信天翁号の」
source.english:
“Yes, we'll show you.
What the Albatross—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Yeah, we'll show you. What the Albatross─」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「本領発揮、ってヤツをね」
source.english: “—can really do.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Is really made of, all that stuff.」

source.japanese: 自信満々に断言され、とにかく、操舵室へ向かう。操舵室とてこの船では船内電話の代わりに伝声管が用いられているような部屋であり、さてそこではいったいどんな見物が待っている事やら、だ。
source.english: After these supremely confident assurances, they headed for the wheelhouse. On this ship, even that room used speaking tubes instead of an internal telephone. What spectacle could be waiting there?

target.text: Full of confidence, that much was asserted, but regardless, to the wheelhouse they headed. Even the wheelhouse seemed to be a room where voice pipes were used in place of an internal telephone system on this ship; now then, just what manner of spectacle awaits us there?

source.japanese:
クロのところに行くか、シサムと共に行くか、迷った挙げ句朔屋が選んだのは、そのどちらでもない、泪のところに報せに行くことだった。
　なぜそのつもりになったのか、朔屋自身よく判らなかったけれど。
source.english:
After wavering between Kuro and following Sisam, Sakuya chose neither. He would go and warn Rui.
Why he had decided on that, he could not quite say himself.

target.text: Should he head to Kuro, or should he go with Shisamu? After hesitating for a while, Sakuya ultimately chose neither, for he instead decided to visit Rui to bring her the bad news. As for why he decided to do so, not even Sakuya himself could say.

source.japanese:
この船室の扉を潜[くぐ]ると何時も、信天翁号なのにこんな部屋が隠されていたのかと、朔屋は眺める度、格差というものに唖然となる。
　自分のあのむさ苦しい部屋と比べてどうだろう。みっしりと柔らかな詰め物に張り詰めた洋椅子、葡萄酒の瓶やカードが散らばった卓にはそこだけで豪奢と退廃の気韻を漂わせ、部屋に満ちた女の匂いと合わせ、船の中と言うより貴族の城館のサロンを思わせた。
　先ほど盛大に血水ぶちまけられたばかりだというのに、下級水夫あたりがよほどがんばったものか、汚れを叩き出したお湯の濡れが残ってはいたが、絨毯の血痕はうっすら。
source.english:
Every time he passed through her cabin door, the disparity left him dumbfounded. A room like this, hidden aboard the Albatross?
Compare it with his own squalid quarters. Chairs padded thickly with soft stuffing; wine bottles and cards scattered over a table that alone exuded luxury and decadence. Combined with the woman's scent filling the room, it suggested a salon in an aristocratic mansion rather than a ship.
Someone, probably the junior sailors, must have worked terribly hard. A great quantity of blood had been spilled here only moments ago, yet the carpet showed little more than faint stains. Dampness remained from the hot water used to scrub out the filth.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そう……また別の、この船に恨みを持っている方達がいらして。そしてそれだけじゃなくって」
source.english: “I see… Another group with a grudge against this ship has arrived. And that's not all.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「嵐もやってきているのね。
　確かにこうなると───ちょっとした事態ねえ」
source.english:
“A storm is coming too.
Yes, that does make this—something of an occasion.”

source.japanese:
敵の新手も嵐の報せも柳に風と流して泪は、血統書付きの猫さながらの柔媚さに身を起こした、寝台だってうっかり迂闊に寝そべろうものなら体が半分がた沈んでしまいそうに柔らかで、豪勢で。昼間の電燈だと、思い出したようにぱちりと切ったベッドサイドのランプの傘も、朔屋には様式も知れない意匠の粋が凝らされている。
　……灯りを落とした部屋には、隠微な静けさが垂れこめた。窓硝子だけはさすがに破れたままだが、角度のせいか泪の部屋自体が入れる事を厭[いと]うたか、漁師達のおめきも高まり始めた波の音[ね]も、横溢する贅沢の前に吸われてしまってどこか遠い。
source.english:
Neither new enemies nor the approaching storm seemed to trouble Rui. She sat up with the languid grace of a pedigreed cat, on a bed so soft and sumptuous that an incautious visitor might sink halfway into it. Remembering that an electric light was burning in daytime, she clicked off the bedside lamp. Even its shade embodied a refinement of design whose style Sakuya could not name.
An intimate hush settled over the darkened room. The window glass was still broken, but whether because of the angle or because the cabin itself refused them entry, the fishermen's shouts and the growing sound of waves seemed absorbed by this abundant luxury, far away.

source.japanese: 泪がこの凶報を聞いても平然としていたし、朔屋もそれくらいは予想が付いていたのだけれど。ぽん、と軽く手を打ち合わせ、ころころと、童女のようにあどけなく笑いながら、
source.english: Rui was unperturbed by the dreadful news. Sakuya had expected as much. But she lightly clapped her hands and laughed, a bright, innocent ripple like a little girl's.

target.text: Every time he walked through the door to this cabin, he always found himself wondering how a stateroom like this one could be hidden aboard the Albatross of all ships, and every time he beheld it, he was always astonished at the sheer disparity on display. He wasn't really sure how to feel when comparing it to his own squalid cabin. A Western chair stretched taut with soft stuffing, scattered bottles of wine and cards on the table, enough to fill the room with an air of extravagance, decadence, and refinement by itself, and when combined with the scent of woman that pervaded the room, it brought to mind the image of a salon in a noble's fortified manor rather than the inside of a ship.

Though it had just been drenched in vast amounts of blood and other fluids, perhaps the deck boys had put in some extra effort, for while there were still some wet spots from the hot water used to clean off the filth, the bloodstains on the carpet were faint.
【Rui】 「I see……there are yet more persons who bear a grudge against this ship. And that is not all, you say.」
【Rui】 「For a storm, too, is coming. Certainly, if that is the case─── we do have a little situation on our hands, do we not?」

She let the tidings of both new enemies and a storm pass her by in stride like a willow bending in the wind, raising herself from the bed with the captivating mannerisms of a pedigreed cat, and even that bed was so soft that were he to thoughtlessly sprawl out on it, half his body might well sink into the mattress: a grand, lavish article. Even the lampshade of the bedside lamp, which she'd left turned on in the middle of the day, now turning it off with a click as though she had only just remembered, was richly decorated in an aesthetically tasteful style that Sakuya did not even recognize.

……A mysterious veil of quietude hung low over the darkened room. The glass alone was, as was only to be expected, still broken, but maybe it was a consequence of the angle, or perhaps because the act of entering Rui's stateroom itself was something they were loath to, for even the yells of the fishermen and the sounds of the waves that had begun to rise tall were, when faced with the inundating luxury, absorbed by it, distant from them.

That Rui would remain composed even after hearing these terrible news was something Sakuya had already predicted. She clapped her hands softly together, and while laughing with the rippling innocence of a young girl,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それは───とっても愉[たの]しみ。
　ふふ、よくってよ直さん」
source.english:
“How very delightful.
Heehee. Excellent, Nao.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「なんだか素敵なお話になってきたじゃない」
source.english: “Isn't this turning into a lovely story?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「素敵な……って。あなた、本気で言ってるんですかそれ。どう考えても絶体絶命、はやくどこかに隠れたほうがよかないか」
source.english: “Lovely… Are you serious? Any way you look at it, we're in mortal danger. Shouldn't you hide somewhere, quickly?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I am looking forward to that ───very much so. Huhu, very well, Nao-san.」
【Rui】 「This is all turning into a rather lovely tale, is it not?」
【Naomasa】 「A lovely……wait. Are you seriously saying that? No matter how you look at this, we're driven into a corner here, so wouldn't it be best if you hurried up and found somewhere to hide?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どうして？」
source.english: “Why?”

source.japanese: こうも不思議そうに訊き返されては、朔屋の方も戸惑うしかないわけで。
source.english: She asked with such genuine puzzlement that Sakuya could only be bewildered in turn.

target.text: 【Rui】 「But why?」
When asked a question in return in such a puzzled tone of voice, all Sakuya could do was also be bewildered in turn.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「次のお客さまは、カードを嗜むといいのだけれど。
　好みの方だったら、ベッドで愉[たの]しむのも素敵」
source.english:
“I do hope our next guests enjoy cards.
And if one takes my fancy, it would be lovely to enjoy ourselves in bed.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それに、誰もいらっしゃらなくっても、嵐。
　退屈だったのよ、わたくしとっても」
source.english:
“Even if no one comes, there's still the storm.
I've been so very bored.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「少しくらい心がまぎれるわ」
source.english: “It should take my mind off things a little.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「心が紛れるときたよこの女……。
　俺、なにを心配してここに来たんだろうなあ……」
source.english:
“Take her mind off things, she says…
What did I come here worrying about…?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Though it would be nice if our next guests had an interest in cards. If they are to my liking, it would also be wonderful to enjoy ourselves in bed.」
【Rui】 「Furthermore, even if no one should come, the storm will. I was bored. So very, very bored.」
【Rui】 「It will distract me a little.」
【Naomasa】 「"A distraction", she calls it. This woman is just……. Why did I even bother getting worried enough to come down here……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「心配？　わたくしを？　直さんは面白いことをおっしゃる」
source.english: “Worrying? About me? What funny things you say, Nao.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Worried? About me? What amusing things you say, Nao-san.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でも殿方に気にかけていただけるのなら、それは幸せな女よ。有難うね、貴方」
source.english: “Still, a woman fortunate enough to receive a gentleman's concern is a happy woman. Thank you, my dear.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「But if a gentleman cares about me, then I am a fortunate woman indeed. Thank you, dear.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「じゃあ、早速上の甲板に出てみましょうか」
source.english: “Well, let's go up on deck at once.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……は？　今なんとおっしゃいましたね」
source.english: “…Sorry? What did you just say?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Well then, let us head to the deck without delay, shall we?」
【Naomasa】 「……Hah? What did you say just now?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくし、嵐の時にお船の方々がどんな様子なのか、見てみたいって思っていたの」
source.english: “I've been wanting to see what everyone aboard does during a storm.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でも泪さん、敵が、それに嵐も───」
source.english: “But, Rui, the enemy—and the storm—”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I have often thought that I should very much like to witness how those on a ship fare in the midst of a storm.」
【Naomasa】 「But, Rui-san, the enemy, and the storm───」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「血のにおいを嗅いだ時から、なんだか体が熱いわ。
　雨に打たれるのなら、それもいい。
　疼きを少しは流してくれるでしょう」
source.english:
“I've felt rather hot ever since I smelled the blood.
A drenching in the rain might be pleasant.
Perhaps it will wash away a little of this ache.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Ever since I sensed the smell of blood, my body has been strangely hot. If I am to be struck by the rain, then let it be so. It will surely wash away some of this throbbing.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それとも直さん、
　貴方が御相手してくれて？」
source.english:
“Unless you would care
to attend to me, Nao?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「上甲板に行きましょう泪さん。
　水夫長あたりの傍にいたほうが安全かも知れませんし」
source.english:
“Let's go to the upper deck, Rui.
We might be safer near the boatswain.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Or perhaps, Nao-san, you will keep me company here?」
【Naomasa】 「Let's go up on deck, Rui-san. Sticking close to the Bosun might be safer, you never know.」

source.japanese:
朔屋の即答は、嵐よりも敵よりも、このままだと本当に泪にベッドに引きずりこまれかねないことを恐れての。
　ベッドの上では敵うどころかひどい目に遭わされそうな、そんな危機感を泪に抱いたし、励んでいるところに敵が襲ってきたなら、嫉妬したそやつになにをされるか知れたものではない。
　諦めて上甲板に向かう。
source.english:
Sakuya's immediate answer came from the fear that, if they stayed here, she might really drag him into bed. It frightened him more than the storm or the enemy.
He doubted he could match her there. She was more likely to put him through hell. And if an enemy arrived while they were at it, who knew what some jealous fellow might do to him?
Resigned, he headed for the upper deck.

target.text: Sakuya's immediate answer was because, while he was scared of the storm and the enemy, he was far more terrified that, at this rate, he might very well actually be dragged into bed with Rui. He wasn't just worried about holding his own against her in bed, he felt something more like an impending sense of doom, like he was in for a horrible fate; were he to make love to Rui, should the enemy attack while he was hard at work, who knows what they might do to him in a fit of jealousy. He resigned himself, then headed for the upper deck.

source.japanese:
───信天翁号の上甲板は、報復に燃える漁師達の船団が追いつくより先に、嵐に見舞われていた。
　ぽつぽつと雨粒の降り出したと見るや、後は一気に、強風と横殴りの雨と波の大揺れと。もとより崩壊寸前のバラック群は、雨風と荒波とでもうぎしぎしぎいぎいといつばらばらに分解しさってもおかしくない。
source.english:
The storm reached the Albatross's upper deck before the fleet of vengeful fishermen could catch up.
A few scattered drops of rain, and then everything at once: strong winds, rain driving sideways, waves pitching the ship. The shacks had been on the verge of collapse to begin with. Now, under the rain, wind, and heavy seas, they creaked and groaned as if they might disintegrate at any moment.

source.japanese: そんな中で操舵室内は、緊張感と騒々しさに満ち満ちていた。その中に紛れているある感触を嗅ぎとって、朔屋は首を捻っていた。これ以上ない切迫の状況下にあるのに、どこか頼もしい空気が入り交じっていたのである。この信天翁号に入船して以来、ついぞ感じた事のない、安心感とさえ言って良かった。朔屋はそのわけを嵐の中の操舵室で目撃する事になる。
source.english: The wheelhouse was filled with tension and noise, yet Sakuya felt another current mingled with them and wondered at it. The situation could hardly have been more desperate, but there was something reassuring in the air. He might even have called it a sense of security—something he had never felt since boarding the Albatross. In the storm-tossed wheelhouse, he was about to see why.

target.text: ───Before the fleet of fishermen ablaze with the passionate flames of vengeance could catch up to them, the storm struck the upper deck of the Albatross. It looked like scattered drops of rain at first, and then, all at once, came powerful gales of wind, slanting downpour, and great rolling waves. The cluster of shanties, already on the verge of collapse, creaked and jarred and grated in the rain, wind, and raging waves to the point they might well have broken apart and scattered all across the deck at any moment.

And amidst all that, the wheelhouse was packed to the brim with tension and tumult. Sniffing out a certain feeling intermingling with that, Sakuya tilted his head. Though the situation could not be more acute, there was some manner of air of dependability mixed within. It was a feeling he had not felt even once since boarding this Albatross, and it could even be called a sense of security. Sakuya now witnessed the reason for that within this wheelhouse in the midst of the storm.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「状況了解。
　これより信天翁号、
　嵐を横断する───！」
source.english:
“Situation understood.
The Albatross will now cross the storm!”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ロックフォール、もっと船足を！　あと五ノットは上げて！」
source.english: “Roquefort, more speed! Another five knots!”

source.japanese: 伝声管に向かい、機関室に指示を出しているのは、クロだ。張りのある声で、小柄でか細い体躯に気力を充溢させているのが、あのクロだ。
source.english: It was Kuro giving orders to the engine room through the speaking tube. Kuro, her voice ringing, her small, frail body brimming with spirit.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Situation understood. Henceforth, the Albatross will cut through the storm───!」
【Kuro】 「Roquefort, more speed! Five more knots!」
Facing the voice pipe, the one who was giving instructions to the engine room was───none other than Kuro. With a firm voice, tiny and delicate body brimming with spirit, that Kuro.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「無理じゃない。知ってるんだから。汽罐の安全弁のバネの間、鉄の切れっ端を差しこんで圧力上げて」
source.english: “It isn't impossible. I know what you can do. Wedge a piece of iron between the coils of the boiler safety-valve spring and raise the pressure.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「時々こっそり試してるんでしょう。
　いい機会じゃない今なら！」
source.english:
“You try it in secret now and then, don't you?
Well, this is your chance!”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「航海士、船の現在位置は」
source.english: “Mates, our present position?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「カシマとヌワジマの間───」
source.english: “Between Kashima and Nuwajima—”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「正確にはカシマ北東の突端から、ヌワジマ、カザキリバナに向かってちょうど三マイル！」
source.english: “Exactly three miles from Kashima's northeastern tip toward Kazakiribana on Nuwajima!”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「なら津和地島と怒和島の間を通って豊後水道に抜ける」
source.english: “Then we'll pass between Tsuwajishima and Nuwajima and get out through the Bungo Channel.”

source.japanese:
海図に一瞥をくれただけで、定点観測をしたわけでもないのに、双子の声音も自信に満ちていて、ただ感覚のみで算出した現在値に微塵の迷いも疑いも抱いていない。確かめたわけではないが、恐らく誤差は殆ど無いのではないかと、朔屋にもそう感じられた。
　このようにしてクロもさりながら、航海士の双子も異能の力を見せつける。信天翁号はまこと不可思議な船であった。
source.english:
The twins had only glanced at the chart. They had taken no bearings, yet their voices were full of confidence, without the slightest doubt about a position calculated entirely by instinct. Sakuya had not checked, but he felt they were probably all but exact.
Kuro was not the only one displaying uncanny powers. The twin mates had their own. The Albatross was a truly inexplicable ship.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「新針路は南西半点南───ちょっと待って」
source.english: “New course, southwest, half a point south—wait.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「It's not impossible. Kuro knows how. Shove a scrap of iron between the springs of the boiler's safety valve and crank up the pressure.」
【Kuro】 「You already secretly try it yourself every now and then, right? Isn't this the perfect chance to give it a shot!」
【Kuro】 「First mates, the ship's current position.」
【Shisamu】 「Between Kashima and Nuwajima───」
【Kisara】 「More precisely, from the northeastern tip of Kashima, we're exactly three miles in the direction of Kazakiribana on Nuwajima!」
【Kuro】 「Then we'll pass through the gap between Tsuwajishima and Nuwajima, then make our way out the Bungo Channel.」

They spared the sea chart but a cursory glance, they weren't even keeping watch on a fixed observation point, and yet the voices of the twins were also full of confidence, calculating the current position of the ship entirely on intuition, carrying not a shadow of hesitation or doubt. Not that he had any way to confirm it, but there was probably almost no error to be found in that measurement. Even Sakuya also felt that way. Thus, not only was Kuro showing off some kind of abnormal ability, but the twin first mates were also displaying one of their own. The Albatross truly was an enigma of a ship.
【Kuro】 「New course, Southwest-half-south─── belay that.」

source.japanese: 帽子を片手押さえに操舵室から飛び出して、船縁にしがみついて波濤渦巻く嵐の海を覗きこもうとして、いかんせんどうにも背丈が足りない。
source.english: Holding her cap with one hand, she ran out of the wheelhouse and clung to the rail, trying to peer into the storm's swirling seas. Unfortunately, she was simply too short.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さん、クロを抱え上げて！」
source.english: “Mr. Sakuya, lift Kuro up!”

source.japanese:
強く命じる言葉に、反感などは生まれる余地は不思議と皆無、朔屋は言われるままに、手近な繋環を片手で掴んで、もう片手でクロの腰に腕を回して抱き上げる。船縁から危険なくらいに身を大きく乗り出し、前方を窺う。
　軽いのは相変わらずなのに、芯でも通ったように体がしっかりしている。
　朔屋には暗雲と横殴りの雨、ひっきりなしに甲板を洗う波飛沫で海の様子などろくに見えなかったのに、クロは何事か見抜いたらしい。はっとした顔つきで操舵室まで駆け戻る。立っていることも困難な揺れなのに、クロの足取りは過[あやま]たず、固い一本道のように走り抜ける。
source.english:
Strangely, her commanding tone left him no room for resentment. He did as he was told, gripping a nearby shackle with one hand and lifting Kuro with his other arm around her waist. She leaned dangerously far over the rail to look ahead.
She was as light as ever, but her body felt firm now, as though something held it straight from within.
Dark clouds, driving rain, spray constantly washing over the deck—Sakuya could scarcely make out the sea. Kuro, however, seemed to discern something. Her face sharpened, and she ran back to the wheelhouse. The ship's motion made it difficult even to stand, yet her feet never faltered. She ran as if along a solid, straight path.

target.text: With one hand keeping her hat pressed down on her head, she leapt out of the wheelhouse, clinging to the ship's bulwark as she tried to peer into the surging sea swirling in the storm, but unfortunately, she was simply not tall enough.
【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san, lift Kuro up!」

Strangely enough, despite being ordered so strongly, the words left no room for any antipathy to form, and so Sakuya did as he was asked; he grabbed onto a nearby shackle with one hand, wrapped his other arm around Kuro's waist, then lifted her up. She leaned dangerously far out over the gunwale, examining what lay ahead. She was as light as she ever had been, yet her body was now firm, as though a strong core ran through her.

Sakuya could barely notice anything about the state of the sea through the dark clouds, the slanting downpour, and the incessant sprays of sea water washing over the deck, but apparently, Kuro had perceived something. She ran back into the wheelhouse with an expression as though she had made a sudden realization. Though the ship rolled enough to make just standing up difficult, there was no err to be found in Kuro's step as she ran back in a stable, straight line.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「一等航海士、取り舵一杯！　急いでっ」
source.english: “Chief Mate, hard a-port! Quickly!”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「でもそんなコトしたら、横波まともに食らうコトに───いいやわかった！」
source.english: “But that'll put us broadside to the waves—never mind, understood!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Chief mate, hard-a-port! Hurry!」 (TN: A note on terminology for commands. Unlike, say, the British Navy, which used indirect orders based on how the tiller would move until 1933, in Japan, commands were always given directly. That is to say, in the British Navy, if you said "hard-a-starboard", the ship would actually turn to port, because to go left on an old sailing ship, you had to put the tiller to the right. The Japanese skipped this confusion when they modernized their navy during the Meiji Restoration.)
【Shisamu】 「But if we do that, we'll be taking a beam sea head on─── no, understood!」

source.japanese:
シサムは躊躇ったものの、即座に指示に従う。クロがこの状態である限り無条件に信用する事に決めているらしい。
　信天翁号、針路急速転換。横波をまともに受けて船が大きく揺れる、上甲板を高波が洗う、固定されていないものが派手に甲板上を転がり、いくつかは船縁を越えて波に獲物として攫[さら]われていく。
source.english:
Sisam hesitated, then obeyed immediately. Apparently she had decided to trust Kuro without question while she was in this state.
The Albatross changed course sharply. A wave struck her broadside and rolled her heavily. High water swept the upper deck. Everything not secured went tumbling across it; several objects passed over the rail and were snatched away as the waves' prey.

target.text: Though Shisamu hesitated, she immediately obeyed the order. It seemed like it had been decided that as long as Kuro was in this state, her orders were to be unconditionally trusted. The Albatross rapidly changed course. The ship rolled violently as she took the beam sea directly against her broadside, tall waves washing over the upper deck, everything not tightly secured loudly rolling around, several things carried over the edge of the bulwark, swept away as prey for the waves.

source.japanese: 朔屋も手近な索具とロープにしっかり腕を絡めたものの、危うく攫[さら]われそうになる。辛うじて波の攻撃をやり過ごし、荒い息をつく朔屋の傍へ、悠然と歩み寄ってきたのが泪だ。この嵐の中を、なにを好きこのんでかわざわざ上甲板まで上がってきていた泪は、髪を強風になぶらせ濡れたドレスで肢体の線を浮き彫りにさせ、なのに凄艶な色香をまとっていた。
source.english: Sakuya locked his arms around the nearest rigging and ropes, yet nearly found himself swept away. He barely weathered the wave's assault and stood panting when Rui came strolling serenely up beside him. What possessed her to come all the way up to the upper deck in this storm was beyond him. The gale worried at her hair, and her soaked dress threw the lines of her body into relief; even so, she carried an almost fearsome sensual glamour.

target.text: Though Sakuya had linked his arms securely around the nearby rigging and rope, he was still close to being swept away himself. Having only barely made it through the assault of the waves with ragged breath, who should then come casually strolling to Sakuya's side but Rui. Rui, who, for reasons only heaven knows, had gone out of her way to venture all the way up to the upper deck in the middle of this tempest, had her hair tossed about in the strong winds, wet dress clinging tightly to and accentuating the lines of her body; despite everything around her, she was still clad in a beautiful sensuality intense enough to leave him shivering.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「今ちょっと、船縁から海を覗いてみたのだけれど」
source.english: “I just looked over the side into the sea.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「この横揺れの中、海を!?　よく転がり落ちずに済んだもんだ……危ないって泪さん」
source.english: “Into the sea, with us rolling like this!? You're lucky you didn't fall over… That's dangerous, Rui!”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そんなの平気よ。それよりも危なかったのは、このお船のほう」
source.english: “I'm quite all right. It was the ship that was in more danger.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I just peered over the gunwale to have a look at the sea.」
【Naomasa】 「At the sea, while the ship's rolling like this!? I'm amazed you haven't tumbled overboard yet…… that's really dangerous, Rui-san.」
【Rui】 「I will be fine. More pressingly, this ship is what is in danger.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「今見たの。波が下がった時、岩礁というのかしら？　そういうものの頭が覗いていたわ」
