source.english: “I saw it just now, when the wave fell away. A reef, is that what you call it? The top of something like that was showing.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I just caught sight of it. When the waves receded, a reef, I suppose you would call it? I could see their heads peeking out from below the surface.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「船の、船腹すれすれのところを通り過ぎていったのよ。知っていらして？　あのまま進んでいたら、どうなったのかしら」
source.english: “It went past almost touching the ship's side. Did you know it was there? I wonder what would have happened if we'd gone straight on.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「か、隠れ岩礁かよ……じゃあクロはさっき針路を確かめた時に───でもどうやって気づいたんだ？
　この雨風の中で……」
source.english:
“A—a submerged reef…? So when Kuro went to check the course just now—but how did she notice it?
In this wind and rain…?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「The ship just barely passed by without scraping its belly against it. Were you aware of that? If we stayed the course, I do wonder what would have happened.」
【Naomasa】 「S-, seriously, a hidden reef……? Then when Kuro went to confirm the course just now───but how did she even notice? And in a rainstorm this heavy……」

source.japanese: 操舵室に振り返れば、クロはまた伝声管に声を張り上げて、その様は普段の彼女からは考えられないほど荒々しくて、そして凛々しい。
source.english: Looking back at the wheelhouse, he saw Kuro shouting into the speaking tube again, fierce and gallant beyond anything her usual self suggested.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そこにいるのは誰？　水夫長？
　ちょうど良かった、船のお尻が重い。
　今の波のせいで、右舷の方、
　船尾から三つ目の倉庫が浸水してる。
　水夫達を向かわせて！」
source.english:
“Who's there? Boatswain?
Good timing. The stern is sitting heavy. That last wave has flooded the third storeroom forward from the stern on the starboard side. Send the sailors there!”

target.text: When he looked over his shoulder into the wheelhouse, Kuro was raising her voice into the voice pipe again, in a manner so full of intense energy that would normally be unthinkable for the girl, and with dignity to boot.

【Kuro】 「Who is that over there? Bosun? Excellent timing. The ship's heavy at the stern. Because of the waves just now, the third starboard hold counting from the stern is flooding. Send the sailors there!」

source.japanese: このようにしてクロは、神の眼でも持っているのか操舵室にあって船内全てを把握し、的確な指示を矢次ざまに繰り出し続け───
source.english: And so Kuro, as though she had the eyes of a god, grasped everything inside the ship from the wheelhouse and fired off one precise order after another—

source.japanese: 物理学と船舶工学への卑猥な挑戦であり───
source.english: A ship that was an obscene challenge to physics and naval engineering—

source.japanese: 到底航海には耐えうる代物とは思われない、洋上に浮かぶ襤褸と屑鉄の一大混沌であり───
source.english: A vast chaos of rags and scrap iron floating on the sea, impossible to conceive as fit for a voyage—

source.japanese: 嵐など、最初の一風だけで分解しさって、抗しようもない筈の信天翁号なのに───
source.english: The Albatross, which ought to have fallen apart at the first breath of a storm, incapable of resistance—

target.text: Like so, as though she were possessed of the Eye of Providence, Kuro grasped the situation on the entire ship from the wheelhouse by herself, continuing to send out precise orders in rapid succession───
It was a vulgar taunt issued to the science of physics and naval architecture───
It seemed utterly unthinkable for it to be seaworthy, a great, chaotic mess of scrap iron and shabby junk floating on the seas───
And were there a storm, it would splinter into tiny pieces at the very first gust of wind; it should have been impossible for the Albatross to defy it, and yet───

source.japanese: ───どれくらいの時間がたったのか。数十分？　数時間？　いずれにしても朔屋には一秒が数倍にも拡大されたように錯覚されるほどの、驚愕と動転とに埋めつくされた濃密な時間であった。操舵室周りで伝令役のような事をやらされていた朔屋も、途中からは船底部の浸水の対処に駆り出され、船内を絶え間なく見舞っていた船殻の軋みと揺れが少しずつ収まりだした事で、船が嵐を抜けつつあるのを覚ったのである。
source.english: How much time had passed? Tens of minutes? Hours? Whatever the answer, it had been time packed with astonishment and agitation, so dense that every second seemed to expand severalfold. Sakuya had first been made to serve as a messenger around the wheelhouse, then drafted into fighting the flooding below decks. As the hull's incessant groaning and shaking began to subside, he realized they were coming out of the storm.

source.japanese: しかも信じられない事に、嵐の前にはひとたまりもあるまいと思われていたこの船は、損害も軽微に暴風域を脱し去りつつあるようだ。
source.english: Incredibly, the ship he had thought would be helpless before the storm was leaving its fiercest winds with only minor damage.

source.japanese: 信天翁号に敵意燃やして迫っていた漁船など、嵐の中で一隻二隻と脱落していって、攻撃はおろか追いついた船の一隻だになく、その船影を消していた。
source.english: The fishing boats, pursuing the Albatross in their fury, had dropped away one by one. Not a single one had caught up, let alone attacked. Their silhouettes were gone.

source.japanese: 狐惑わしにでも遭ったような心地で上甲板に上がり、操舵室に向かう。あの神業的な指揮能力を発揮していたのが本当にクロなのか、今さらながら信じられず、もう一度自身の眼で確かめるつもりであったのだが───と。
source.english: Feeling as though a fox had bewitched him, Sakuya climbed to the upper deck and headed for the wheelhouse. Even now, he could scarcely believe it had really been Kuro directing them with such miraculous skill. He meant to see for himself once more—when—

source.japanese: 徐々に雲間に光を覗かせていく空と、波のうねりに嵐の名残をまだ残す海の向こう、暴風域を脱しつつある信天翁号の進路上に浮かんでいるあの影は───船影？
source.english:
Light was beginning to show between the clouds. The sea still carried the storm's aftermath in its swells. Ahead, along the course of the Albatross as she emerged from the violent winds, floated a shadow.
A ship?

source.japanese: にわかに凄まじい悪寒に囚われて、朔屋、腰に差してあった例の望遠鏡を抜き、また覗いてみたところ、たちまち膝から力が抜けていった。
source.english: A terrible chill seized him. Sakuya drew the telescope from his waist and looked again. At once, the strength went out of his knees.

target.text: ───How much time had passed? Tens of minutes? Several hours? Regardless of which, it had been so dense a time packed with countless shocking twists and turns that it was enough for Sakuya to hallucinate a single second into a thousandfold its length. Sakuya, who had been assigned the role of something akin to a messenger in the area around the wheelhouse, had also been sent running to deal with flooding in the bilge partway through, and when the creaking and shaking of the hull that had ceaselessly assaulted the inside of the ship finally began to abate, he came to realize that the ship was starting to make its way out through the storm.

And in an unbelievable turn of events, it seemed this ship, which could scarcely be imagined to withstand a storm for more than a brief moment, was escaping the storm zone with only insignificant damage.

The fishing boats, which had been pursuing the Albatross with burning hostility, had fallen by the wayside in the storm one after another, and not even a single ship managed to catch up to them, let alone attack, before they had all vanished from sight.

While gripped by an addling uncertainty as though beguiled to his doom by a fox, he still went to the upper deck, then headed for the wheelhouse. Was it truly Kuro who had displayed such a miraculous ability of command? Even now, he still could not believe it. He had intended to confirm it once more with his own eyes, however───just then.

Beneath the sky gradually letting the light peek through the veil of clouds, and beyond the sea, where the swell of the waves yet carried the remnants of the storm, there, floating on the course the Albatross was taking as she escaped from the storm zone, was a distant figure of───a ship?
Suddenly seized by a dreadful chill, Sakuya pulled out that telescope holstered at his hip, and when he looked through it once more, his knees immediately buckled beneath him.

source.japanese: それは───一隻の巡視船だった。
source.english: It was a patrol vessel.

source.japanese: 大戦から生き残った老朽艦が警備任務に回されたと思しい艦だが、その手の官憲の艦は信天翁号には言うまでもなく鬼門。叩けば物理的にも比喩的にも埃が雲霞のように沸き立つ信天翁号としては、遭遇したくない相手の上位を常に占める。停船させられたが最後、乗り組み達は監獄送りとなる事間違いなしで───まあ突きつめればこの信天翁号自体が洋上の監獄のようなものではあるが。
source.english: Apparently it was an aging warship that had survived the Great War and been reassigned to patrol duty. Needless to say, vessels of the law were the Albatross's bane. Give this ship a shake and clouds of incriminating dust would billow out, literally and figuratively; a patrol vessel therefore ranked high among the things her crew least wished to encounter. Once made to heave to, they would undoubtedly be sent to prison—though, when one got down to it, the Albatross herself was already something of a prison at sea.

source.japanese: 望遠鏡を眼に構えたまま反射的に走り出そうとして、拡大された視界が輪転するのに眩暈しそうになる。それくらい動揺していた。
source.english: He instinctively started to run with the telescope still at his eye. The magnified view reeled, almost making him dizzy. That was how badly shaken he was.

target.text: It was───a single patrol boat.

She appeared to be a veteran of the Great War, now a decrepit relic relegated to patrol duty, but needless to say, this sort of warship helmed by the authorities was anathema to the Albatross, the sort she needed to avoid like the plague. For a ship like the Albatross, which would both literally and metaphorically release a towering cloud of dust were she to be beaten, that kind of ship always occupied the highest position among a ranking of things she wished not to encounter. Were they to be detained, the entire crew would doubtless be sent to prison ───well, upon closer inspection, the Albatross itself could well be said to be like a prison on the seas already, but still.
He reflexively set off in a run with the telescope still held up to his eye, and the rotation of his enlarged field of view almost made him dizzy. So profoundly shaken was he.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「じきに───完全に、嵐を抜ける───」
source.english: “Soon—we'll be completely—out of the storm—”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「みんな、お疲れ様───」
source.english: “Everyone—well done—”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Any moment now───we will be entirely clear of the storm───」
【Kuro】 「All of you, excellent work───」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あひぇぇ……」
source.english: “Ahhehh…”

source.japanese:
伝声管にすがって座りこむクロは、さながら骨と肉が溶け流れて空気のみが詰まった革袋のよう。先刻までの魔力めいた船への把握力が、完全に失われた事を物語っていた。
　それどころか先程までの緊張と疲労が一気に来たのか、むしろ普段にまして呆けきり、眼などは表面に紙ヤスリでも掛けたかにざらついて濁りきっている。これでは信天翁号に迫る巡視船に対してものの役に立たないであろう。
source.english:
Kuro sank down, clinging to the speaking tube, like a leather bag whose flesh and bones had melted away, leaving only air inside. Her almost magical grasp of the ship had vanished completely.
More than that, perhaps all the tension and exhaustion had struck at once. She was dazed beyond her usual state, her eyes dull and rough, as though someone had taken sandpaper to their surface. She would be no use against the patrol vessel approaching the Albatross.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Ahieeeh……」

Clinging to the voice pipe as she plopped down, it was like Kuro's bones and flesh had melted and washed away, and all that remained was a leather bag filled with air. That was a testament to how the supernatural power to grasp all on the ship, which she held until just moments ago, had now completely vanished. Not just that, it was like all the tension and fatigue she'd accumulated struck her all at once; in fact, she looked even more sluggish than usual, like the way her eyes were so gritty and muddy that it looked like somebody had rubbed them down with sandpaper. In this state, she would probably be completely useless against the patrol boat approaching the Albatross.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「おう朔屋。どうやら波に攫[さら]われもせず生き残ったみたいね。どうよ、この信天翁号」
source.english: “Hey, Sakuya. Looks like you survived without getting swept overboard. What do you think of our Albatross?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Hey there, Sakuya. Looks like you made it through without getting swept away by the waves. So what do you think of our Albatross?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ちょっとしたもんでしょ？　そんじょそこらの船じゃ、こうはいかないよ、って、どうしたの、えらい焦った顔で」
source.english: “Not bad, is she? Your average ship couldn't do that. What's wrong? You look awfully worried.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どうしたもこうしたも……悪魔かなんかに呪われてるだろうこの船」
source.english: “What's wrong? This ship's cursed by a demon or something, isn't it?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「今度は巡視船だ……型落ちの艦みたいだけど、それでもこっちとは装備なんもかも比べものにならない」
source.english: “Now it's a patrol vessel… She may be obsolete, but her weapons—everything about her—is beyond comparison with us.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「She's not all bad, is she? Any old ship, like all those other ones, they couldn't pull this off. Wait, what's wrong, you're looking real panicked.」
【Naomasa】 「What isn't wrong here…… this ship must be cursed by some demon or devil or something.」
【Naomasa】 「Now it's a patrol boat…… looks like some outdated warship, but still, our equipment can't even begin to compare to theirs.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どうするんだ今度は───うおう!?」
source.english: “What do we do this time—whoa!?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「What the hell do we do, this time we're───WOAH!?」

source.japanese: やにわ操舵室から駆け出した双子の勢いに錐揉みになる朔屋、回転が収まってから双子をよろよろ追いかける。
source.english: The twins suddenly charged out of the wheelhouse, sending Sakuya spinning. Once he stopped, he staggered after them.

target.text: Sakuya was left spinning like a drill from the sheer momentum of the twins when they suddenly leapt out the wheelhouse, and once he regained his balance, he wobbled outside in pursuit of them.

source.japanese: 舳先にぞろぞろ集まって針路を見守る信天翁号の面子の顔は、まだ不敵な笑顔、に見せかけて流石にみな一様に頬がひくついていた。
source.english: The Albatross's crew gathered at the bow to watch their course. Their faces still wore fearless smiles—or pretended to. Every cheek was twitching now.

target.text: Gathered in a crowd on the bow of the ship to observe their course, the faces of the crew of the Albatross were still plastered with defiant smiles, or at least they feigned as much, for it was surely not surprising that all of them had twitching cheeks.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「うわははは。ありゃあ海上封鎖の一隻だな。
　こっち方面にゃ廻ってきてない筈だったんだが、気まぐれか、どっかの指示か、どちらにしてもろくでもねえ」
source.english:
“Wahahaha! One of the blockade ships.
She wasn't supposed to be in these parts. A whim, orders from somewhere—either way, no damned good.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Uwahahahah. That there's one of the ships from the blockade. Weren't supposed to be any of them swinging round this way, but whether it's a fluke or someone's orders, it's bad news either way.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あはははは、さすがに三連戦は滅多にないね」
source.english: “Ahahaha! Three fights in a row. Even we don't get that very often.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ahahaha. Even for us, three battles in a row is a rarity, isn't it?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「うふふふふ、嵐が終わっちゃうと、クロも役立たずだし」
source.english: “Heeheehee! And once the storm's over, Kuro's useless again.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Uhuhuhuhu. And with the storm over, Kuro won't be any help either.」

source.japanese:
どうやら放胆をもって鳴る信天翁号の一同にとっても危機的な事態らしく、朔屋はこっそり皆から離れ、船上のバラックの壁に向かい、意を決して目をつぶって───がんがん打ちつけ始める、額はたちどころに切れて血の筋が眼にへと伝う。
　シサムはこの突然の奇行に振り返ったものの、動じた風もなく切り捨てた。
source.english:
Apparently even the famously reckless crew of the Albatross considered this a crisis. Sakuya slipped away from them, faced the wall of a shack, made up his mind, closed his eyes—and began banging his forehead against it. The skin split at once, and blood ran down toward his eyes.
Sisam turned at this sudden eccentricity, but dismissed it without a trace of alarm.

target.text: It seemed like, even to all concerned on the Albatross roaring in their boldness, this was also a very critical situation, and Sakuya quietly took his leave from the rest of them, faced the wall of one of the shacks on the deck, hardened his resolve, closed his eyes───then began to vigorously hammer his head against it, his forehead quickly splitting, a trail of blood reaching his eyes. Shisamu turned her head towards him at this sudden display of bizarre behavior, but without a shadow of agitation to be seen in her, she instead verbally cut him down where he stood.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「朔屋くぅん。君、そんな風に自分を痛めつけて、
『自分はこの船に捕らえられた無関係の市民で、今までも散々に暴力を受けていました』」
source.english:
“Sakuya, dear. You're not hurting yourself like that so you can say,
‘I'm an innocent civilian held prisoner aboard this ship. They've been subjecting me to terrible violence all along.’”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「『この額の怪我もその証拠です。なんで自分は保護を要求します』とかって、自分だけは助かって、あたしらの事を売り渡そうとか考えて、ないよねええ……？」
source.english: “‘This injury on my forehead proves it. I demand protection.’ Save yourself and sell the rest of us out? You wouldn't be thinking anything like that, would you…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやあはっはっは。まさか。単に俺は、官憲を見ると手近なものに頭を打ちつけたくなるって奇病に罹っているだけだとも」
source.english: “Oh, hahahaha. Of course not. I merely suffer from a rare disease that makes me want to bang my head against the nearest object whenever I see the authorities.”

source.japanese: 言い訳は見苦しく、朔屋の額には血と一緒に冷や汗も流れる。
source.english: A wretched excuse. Cold sweat mingled with the blood on his forehead.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Sakuya-kuuun. Are you hurting yourself like that just so you can go: 『I am but an unrelated citizen held captive aboard this ship, and I have been the victim of all sorts of unspeakable violence until now.』」

【Shisamu】 「『This wound on my head also serves as proof of what I claim. Why, I demand that I be taken into protective custody.』 or something, all to save yourself while you throw the rest of us to the wolves───surely you're not thinking anything like that, riiiiight……?」

【Naomasa】 「Nooo-ho-ho-ho. Perish the thought. It's just, I happen to suffer from a very queer disease that gives me this uncontrollable urge to hit my head against anything close at hand when I catch sight of the authorities, that's all.」
His excuse was painfully bad, and a cold sweat now ran alongside the blood down Sakuya's brow.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まあ泪女史はたいして波風もなく解放されるだろうが……」
source.english: “Well, they'd probably release Madam Rui without too much fuss…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well, I'm sure the esteemed Madam Rui will be released without much issue, but……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくし、お巡りさんは嫌いなの。
　あの方たちって、いつも不粋で退屈だわ。
　そんな方たちとご一緒するくらいなら、
　まだこちらにいた方がましというもの」
source.english:
“I dislike policemen.
They're always so tiresome and ill-mannered.
I'd rather stay here than keep company
with people like that.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I do so despise patrolmen. Those men are always boorish and boring both. If the alternative is going with such people, then I would much prefer to remain here with all of you.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「有り難いお言葉、痛みいるね。
　……ま、どうにかやってみようか。
　おい朔屋、機関室にまだ汽罐は保つか、
　聞いてこい」
source.english:
“Much obliged. Kind words indeed.
Well, let's see what we can do. Sakuya, go down to the engine room. Ask if the boiler can still hold out.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Your kind words are much appreciated. ……Well, why don't we try making it through this mess? Oi, Sakuya, go down to the engine room, ask if the boilers are still holding.」

source.japanese:
水夫長達はまだ逃走の意志力失っていないようだが、朔屋がざっと目測したところ、巡視船との彼我の隔たりは一ケーブルほど。
　通常あの手の艦の船足はさして高速ではないとはいえ、こちらはそれを下回る鈍足のオンボロ船である。今から回頭して最大船速を出したところで、いずれ追いつかれてしまうだろう。
source.english:
The boatswain and the others had not yet lost the will to escape. But Sakuya's quick estimate put the patrol vessel about a cable away.
Ships of that sort were not usually particularly fast, but their own lumbering wreck was slower still. Even if they turned around now and made their best speed, they would eventually be caught.

target.text: It seemed like the Bosun and the rest still had yet to lose the willpower to make their escape, and when Sakuya made a rough visual estimate, the distance between the patrol vessel and them was about one cable. Normally, that kind of warship wasn't particularly speedy, but they were sailing an even slower, worn-out ship. If they were to turn the ship around and set off at maximum speed now, they'd surely be caught sooner rather than later.

source.japanese: 信天翁号も遂に捕らえられるかと思われた、その時に───
source.english: Just when the Albatross seemed finally about to be captured—

source.japanese:
二つの船の間の海が突如として盛り上がり、浮上し来たったものがある。
　朔屋はそれが何か、初めは判らなかった。
source.english:
The sea between the two ships suddenly swelled. Something rose from it.
At first, Sakuya could not tell what it was.

source.japanese: 海水が流れ落ちていって、輪郭が露わになっても、判らなかった。
source.english: Even when the water streamed away and its outline emerged, he could not tell.

source.japanese: 何故ならそんなものなど、彼の生涯で見た覚えも聞いた覚えもなかったから。
source.english: For he had never seen or heard of anything like it in his life.

target.text: And no sooner than when it seemed that, this time, the Albatross would finally be captured, that very moment───
The sea between the two ships suddenly surged upwards: something had begun to surface. At first, Sakuya had no idea what that thing was.
But even as the seawater flowed away, as its contour emerged from beneath, he still didn't comprehend it.
For the likes of that thing was something he had never seen or heard of even once before in his entire life.

source.japanese: それは、白く、巨大な、目も鼻もない、のっぺりとした顔と肌で───総体としては人間型に見えなくもなかったけれど。
source.english: White and immense, with smooth skin and a blank face, neither eyes nor nose—taken as a whole, it might have been called human in shape.

source.japanese: 浮上したそいつから押し寄せてくる気配は、まるで禁断の奥津城が忌まわしくも万古の昔から抱き続けてきた黯い闇の死臭めいた呪わしさに満ち満ち、底知れぬ坑道の入口じみた双眸には、人類以前の生物が崇拝したと伝えられる蕃神の、不定形の、軟質の、両生類の卵束と黒山羊とそして丘の影に潜[ひそ]む這いずる粘菌との背徳的な結合を仄[ほの]めかす虚無が揺曳してああ、ああ、この姿を目の当たりにしてしまった者よ、お前の魂に安らぎのあらんことをなぜならお前たちは現実というのものがいかに不安定な、大海に点在する孤島よりも頼りなく儚いものと覚ってしまって最早安らかに眠れる夜とてなく窓を何度も何度も見返して這い寄る混沌と邪悪の脅威に怯え続けることになるだろうからそしてどんな癒しも薬も役には立たぬ狂気の薄暮に囚われてとかなんとかかの北米の顔の長ぇ恐怖小説作家じみた難読の修辞が延々続くくらい大変な……。
source.english: The presence rolling off the thing was steeped in a malediction like the stench of death from blackest darkness, hoarded since time immemorial within a forbidden tomb. In its eyes, like the mouths of bottomless mine shafts, there flickered the void of an alien god said to have been worshiped by creatures older than humanity: formless, soft, hinting at an unholy union of amphibian egg clusters, a black goat, and crawling slime mold concealed behind a hill. Ah, ah, you who have witnessed this shape, may your souls find peace! For you have learned how unstable a thing reality is, frailer and more fleeting than islands scattered in the great ocean. No longer shall you know a peaceful night's sleep, but turn again and again to your windows, shuddering at the threat of crawling chaos and evil, trapped in a twilight of madness beyond the reach of any remedy or medicine—or some such impenetrable rhetoric, continuing at length in the manner of that long-faced North American horror writer. It was that sort of serious business…

target.text: It was white, enormous, with neither eyes nor nose, face and skin both flat and featureless───as a whole, it was possible to see it as a humanoid shape, but.

The miasma surging from that rising monstrosity was steeped in the maledictions of some putrid, sepulchral effluvium, a corruption held entombed within the depths of forbidden ancestral crypts since the dawn of untold aeons; in those twin orbs, pits like shafts of unknowable depths, there shimmered a void hinting at the blasphemous union of those Outer Gods worshipped by pre-human entities in days of yore: an amorphous, gelatinous fusion of batrachian spawn, the Black Goat, and the crawling myxomycetes that lurk in the shadows of those hills.

O, woe to him who gazes upon this form, may your soul find repose, for you have perceived the fragility of reality, come to understand it is a thing more precarious and ephemeral than a lone isle scattered in a vast, indifferent sea; no longer shall your nights grant you the sanctuary of sleep; you shall turn to the window again and again, trembling before the crawling chaos and the heralds of ancient, heretical evil, and neither balm nor opiate shall deliver you from this twilight of madness, and so on and so forth: a seemingly endless stream of those turgid, unreadable rhetorical flourishes favoured by a certain long-faced North American horror writer shall continue to haunt you forevermore, a most terrible fate which…….

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あれは───」
source.english: “That's—”

source.japanese: キサラがうっそりと呟いた。
source.english: Kisara murmured hollowly.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「アレはウミヒト───」
source.english: “That's one of the Sea People—”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「That's───」
Kisara muttered absentmindedly.
【Kisara】 「That's an Umihito───」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「はん、ウミヒトだぁ？」
source.english: “Hah. Sea People?”

source.japanese: 嵐の間中どこに潜[ひそ]んでいたものだか、姿を見せなかった殺し屋が、水の飛沫一つも受けていない姿でいつの間にか場に混じっていて、鼻を鳴らした。
source.english: The assassin, who had been nowhere to be seen throughout the storm, was suddenly among them without a single drop of spray on him. He snorted.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ありゃあヒトガタ、南極のニンゲンじゃねえか。
　そうか、こっちの世界にも似たようなのがいるんだな。しかし───
　こいつは、なにかが妙な───」
source.english:
“That's a Hitogata. The Antarctic Ningen, isn't it?
I see. There's something similar in this world too.
But—something's strange about this one—”

source.japanese:
妙な、とはそちらの物言いだと船の乗り組み達は懐手の殺し屋へ、海の巨怪に向けるのと同質の眼差しを向ける。
　白く巨大なヒトガタは、今は天を圧して佇立するのみで挙動を見せていないが、それだけでも途方もない霊的質量ともいうべき気配を湛えて、これには信天翁号の面子も苦笑いより素直に愕然とする事を選んでいたけれど、智里の言葉はある種ヒトガタの存在と同じくらいに意味不明に響いたらしかった。
source.english:
‘Strange,’ indeed—coming from a man who talked like that. The crew gave the assassin, standing there with his hands tucked into his sleeves, much the same look they gave the colossal apparition in the sea.
The huge white human shape merely stood there now, pressing against the sky and making no move. That alone lent it a presence of what could only be called immeasurable spiritual mass. Even the Albatross crew chose naked stupefaction over wry smiles; yet Tomosato's words seemed, in their fashion, every bit as incomprehensible as the creature's existence.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Hah, an Umihito?」

He must have been hiding away somewhere during the storm, but the murderer for hire, who hadn't shown himself before, joined the gathering at some point without getting a single splash of water on himself, then snorted.

【Tomosato】 「Isn't that thing the Hitogata, the Ningen from the Antarctic? I see, so there's something similar in this world as well. However───something about this guy is strange───」 (TN: Tomosato is referring to cryptids known as "Hitogata" and "Ningen", respectively meaning "human figure" and "human". They originate from the occult board on the imageboard 2chan. They have human-shaped bodies, are enormous, white, live underwater, and have flat, featureless faces and skin. They are fundamentally similar, but the Hitogata live on the North Pole, the Ningen in the Antarctic.)

Your way of talking is what's strange here, the crew of the Albatross all but said as they sent a look towards the murderer standing with his hands in the breast of his kimono, one very similar to what they were giving the giant sea monster.

For now, the large white humanoid merely stood imposingly, motionless as it dominated the skies, but even so, it projected an extraordinary amount of spiritual mass, or what should perhaps be rephrased as presence, and here, the crew of the Albatross chose to be honest with themselves, expressing stunned amazement rather than wry, strained smiles, but in a sense, Tomosato's words rang as incomprehensibly cryptic to them as the existence of this humanoid.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「『南極』ってなによこの優男。
　あんたがナニ言ってるのかよくわかんないけど、
　あたしら船乗りはアレをウミヒトって呼んでる」
source.english:
“‘Antarctic’? What's that supposed to mean,
pretty boy? I don't know what you're talking about.
We sailors call those things Sea People.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「What the hell is "the Antarctic" supposed to be, you sissy. I haven't the first clue what you're talking about, but we sailors call that thing an Umihito.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「外洋を航海する船が時おり出くわすシロモノでね。
　ってもあたしも話に聞いたくらい。
　まさかホントにあんなのがいるなんて。
　しかもこんな陸地近くで」
source.english:
“Ships crossing the open sea run into them now and then.
I've only heard stories myself.
I never thought they really existed.
And this close to land, too.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「It's a creature that ships travelling the open seas will sometimes come across. But with that said, I've also only heard the rumors. Never though I'd actually see one of those things. And this close to land at that.」

source.japanese:
そして毒気を抜かれたように呟く双子の隣で朔屋は。額にこびりついて乾き始めた返り血を爪の先でほじりながら朔屋は。
　独創的な作劇能力というのに欠ける喜劇作家が仕組んだかのような、この次から次への非常識事態の到来に朔屋は───朔屋の中で、ころりと、落ちた、音、それまでは怠惰でいい加減ではあるが彼の人となりを、一応は人間向きに繋いでまとめていた大事な部品が外れて落ちた音。
　色々と堰[せ]きとめていた諸部品が外れて緩んで落ちていった後に衝[つ]き上げてきたものがある。
source.english:
And Sakuya, beside the twins as they murmured in bewilderment—Sakuya, picking with a fingernail at the spattered blood beginning to dry on his forehead—
Sakuya, faced with this succession of absurd events, as if contrived by a comic playwright utterly lacking in inventive powers—something inside him dropped with a little clunk. An important part had come loose and fallen out. Lazy and irresponsible though he was, it had held his character together in a shape more or less suited to human society.
The various parts that had kept things in check loosened, detached themselves, fell away. And after them, something surged up.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ぷっ」
source.english: “…Pff.”

source.japanese: こらえきれず噴き出して。
source.english: He could not hold it back. It burst out.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あはは、あはははは、
　あーっはっはっはっはっはっはっはっは！」
source.english:
“Ahaha, ahahahaha—
Aaaahahahahahahahaha!”

source.japanese:
遂に笑い出した。あまりにもあまりの事態に。ここしばらく覚えなかったほどの、突き抜けた呵々大笑───
　周りの乗り組み達、信天翁号の怪人物達でさえぎょっとするほどの、まるで笑いの擬音文字が朔屋から湧きだして螺旋を描いて天に舞い上がり、嵐雲の晴れ初めの、鮭の肉色、黄薔薇の花弁の彩[いろどり]、瑠璃の紺青、光に染め抜かれてたとりどりの色合いの雲に、文字の形を穿[うが]って突き抜けていくような笑い声だった。
source.english:
At last he laughed. At the sheer excess of it all. A great, unrestrained roar, the sort of laughter he hadn't known in quite some time.
Even the strange inhabitants of the Albatross around him were startled. It was as though the letters spelling his laughter poured out of him, spiraled into the sky, and pierced the clouds beginning to clear after the storm. Salmon flesh, yellow rose petals, the deep blue of lapis lazuli—clouds dyed in a multitude of colors by the light, punched through with holes in the shapes of letters. Such was his laughter.

target.text: And then there was Sakuya, standing next to the twins and coughing like he were trying to rid himself of toxic vapours. While picking at the spurt of blood that had begun to dry and solidify on his brow with the tip of his fingernail, Sakuya was.

At the advent of what seemed like something put together by a comedy writer utterly lacking in anything resembling creative or original playwriting abilities, just one absurd situation after the other, Sakuya was───inside Sakuya, there was the sound of something rolling, then falling: it was the sound of that all-important component that had, until then, held together his lazy, irresponsible character in a somewhat human fashion, coming loose and falling down. And after the various parts that had been damming up all manner of things within him disconnected, loosened, and fell apart, something was welling up.
【Naomasa】 「……Pff.」
Unable to hold it in, he erupted.
【Naomasa】 「Ahaha, ahahaha, AAーHA HA HA HA HA HA HA HA!」
And at long last, he laughed. Laughed at this situation so utterly over the top. Roaring heartily with a piercing laughter, a sort he hadn't experienced in a good while now───

So loud was it that the crew surrounding him, even the monsters of the Albatross, were taken aback; it was as if the very onomatopoeia of laughter itself were gushing out of Sakuya, forming a spiral and soaring into the heavens, into those storm clouds just beginning to clear, into the colour of salmon flesh, the brilliance of yellow rose petals, and the deep blue of Lapis Lazuli, with a laugh so loud as though to gouge the shape of those letters into these clouds dyed in pale streaks of light and pierce through them.

source.english: —A New Chapter—

target.text: ───Interlude───

source.japanese: 罐の火の一部が零れ落ちたかに一対の赤い光は床に溜まった影の中で灯る。しばし連星のように留まっていたが、ふっと消え失せた、としか思えないほどの速き起こりで、闇中を走ったのである。光の緒も引かない程の瞬速の、動きも小さな跫音も人間の感覚では追い切れない域にあったが、生き物を追う生き物として有史以前から完成された存在が船にはある。
source.english: A pair of red lights burned in the shadows pooled on the floor, as if a little of the furnace fire had spilled there. For a while they remained like binary stars, then moved so abruptly that they seemed simply to go out. They were racing through the dark. Too swift even to trail a thread of light, their movements and tiny footfalls exceeded human senses. But aboard this ship lived another creature, perfected since before recorded history for the pursuit of living prey.

source.japanese: 物陰から新たな影が生じて、しかしこちらは質量血肉を備えた影の、その身のこなしのしなやかな事流体の如く、疾き事弾丸の如く、先に消えた一対の光を追って影から出でて影にと沈む。一瞬、罐から漏れる明かりを弾いて、一対の光が爛[らん]と輝く。刹那の光輝───
source.english: A new shadow emerged from concealment. This one possessed mass, flesh, and blood. Fluid in its supple movements, swift as a bullet, it pursued the vanished pair of lights, emerging from shadow and sinking into shadow again. For an instant, another pair flared, reflecting the light escaping from the furnace. A moment's brilliance—

target.text: As if a part of the furnace fire had spilled over, a pair of red lights lit up the shadows that pooled on the floor. For a time, they held still like binary stars, and then they vanished: they ran through the dark so quickly that it could only seem that way, at least. With such blindingly quick speed that they did not even leave behind a trail of light, both their movements and tiny footsteps were now in the realm where human senses could no longer follow them, but there was an existence aboard this ship that had perfected the art of hunting its fellow life since prehistoric times.

A new shadow was born from the shade, however, this was a shadow endowed with mass, with flesh and blood; its carriage elegant as flowing liquid, speed like that of a bullet, it chased after the just-vanished twin lights, emerging from the shadow before sinking into it once more. For an instant, the light leaking from the furnace flared up, twin lights glittering brilliantly. A split second of radiance───

source.japanese: 影の溜まりの中ではどのような攻防が繰り広げられているのか定かではなかったけれど、長くは続かず、暗がりの奥で、「ヂッ！」と短く詰まった、生き物の断末魔が悲痛で、同時に生命が生命を奪う事の原初的な悦びを、耳にした者に思い出させた。
source.english: What attack and counterattack unfolded in those pools of darkness no one could tell, but it was soon over. From deep within came a short, strangled “Jit!”—a creature’s anguished death cry, recalling at once to all who heard it the primal delight of life taking life.

target.text: It was unclear what manner of offence and defence was unfolding within the pooling shadows, but it did not last long, and in the depths of the dark, there sounded a clipped, gasping chirp, what invoked for all who heard it the heartbreaking death throes of a living creature, and at the same time, the primeval joy of one life stealing the life of another.

source.japanese: やがて影からぬう、と出でても影がそのまま凝[こご]ったかに黒い、所々真夜中の流星のように白い毛筋を混ぜた毛並みの、信天翁号の番猫宗右衛門が、その逞[たくま]しき顎[あぎと]に丸々太って大なる鼠をぶら下げて。
source.english: Presently the Albatross's watch-cat Soemon emerged, still black as congealed shadow, a few white hairs streaking his coat like meteors in a midnight sky. From his powerful jaws hung an enormous, fat rat.

target.text: At long last, it smoothly emerged from the shadows, though it was black as if the shadows themselves had congealed, a coat of fur streaked in places with fine lines of white like comets soaring across the midnight sky: it was the watchcat of the Albatross, Souemon, with a great mouse so fat it was completely round dangling from his muscular jaws.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……お疲れ様、宗右衛門殿。
　申し訳ないのですが、食事は奥の方でお願いします」
source.english:
“…Well done, Mr. Soemon.
My apologies, but would you please take your meal farther back?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……Excellent work, Lord Souemon. My sincerest apologies, but I must request that you partake in your meal in the back.」

source.japanese: 機関長でさえ口調に敬意を表すこの黒猫は、ただ船の害獣をしかと仕留めた事を告げたかっただけと見え、大人しく影の中に戻って、貪り喰らう様こそ見せなかったものの、肉を割き骨を噛み砕く音が機関室の重低音の中で異様なまでに生々しかった。朔屋はこの咀嚼音に機関長振る舞いのウイスキイ垂らした紅茶に血の味さえ混じるような悪心地に見舞われたが、宗右衛門が相手では抗議も申し立てられない。彼以外の、機関室の卓に着いた男達には猫の食事の音など屁とも感じぬ豪毅の者ばかりで、水夫長はむしろ賞賛の頷[うなず]きを何度か繰り返してから、
source.english: Even the chief engineer addressed the black cat with respect. Apparently Soemon had only wanted to announce his successful disposal of a shipboard pest. He returned obediently to the shadows. They were spared the sight of him devouring it, but the tearing flesh and crunching bones sounded unnaturally vivid amid the engine room's deep rumble. Sakuya felt sick, as if the tea the engineer had served him, laced with whiskey, had acquired a taste of blood. But one could hardly lodge a complaint against Soemon. The other men at the engine-room table were all stalwarts who did not give a damn about a cat eating. The boatswain, in fact, nodded several times in approval before speaking.

target.text: This black cat, whom even the Chief Engineer spoke to with the utmost respect, appeared to just have wanted to report that he had dealt the killing blow to one of the pests aboard the ship without leaving room for doubt, for he quietly returned to the shadows once more, and though he did not show any outward signs of devouring his kill, the sounds of parting flesh and crushing bone were abnormally vivid even in the deep thrumming of the engine room. This sound of mastication left Sakuya with an uncomfortable feeling in his chest, like the black tea with whisky he had been treated to by the Chief Engineer was even beginning to taste a little of blood, but when it came to Souemon, he had no room to raise any objections.

Sakuya aside, all the men seated at this table in the engine room were of a hardy breed, men who cared less for the sound of a cat's meal than they would a fart in the wind; in fact, the Bosun nodded repeatedly in approval, and then,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「じゃあ、クソ鬱陶しいネズ公を宗右衛門が片づけてくれたところで、さっきの話の続きといこう」
source.english: “Now that Soemon's dealt with that damned nuisance of a rat, let's get back to what we were discussing.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Alright, now that Souemon has dealt with that obnoxious little shit of a mister mousey, let's get back to the talking.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ええと、どこまで話したっけか、王よ？」
source.english: “Where had we got to, Wang?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Uhm, where were we again, Wang?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「いや、私達はそもそも何故こんな会合を開いているのでしたか？」
source.english: “Well, why were we holding this meeting in the first place?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「No, why were we even holding this assembly here to begin with?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……。いや、すまん。
　あんたに聞いて悪かった。
　おい朔屋、なんだったか？」
source.english:
“…Sorry. My mistake, asking you.
Sakuya, what was it?”

source.japanese:
近々の事を記憶していられないという機関長の持病は水夫長も知るところであったし、折り合いは悪いとはいえ水夫の長と機関室の長、お互いを立てるところは心得ていて、軽く詫びてから朔屋に続きを促した。
　これでいつもの朔屋なら、他の男がする真面目な話なぞ聞き流していてまた水夫長の鉄拳を喰らうところであったが、この時に限っては話の再開を待ち侘びだったので、遅滞なく答えられた。
source.english:
The boatswain knew of the engineer's chronic inability to remember recent events. They might not get along, but the head of the sailors and the head of the engine room understood when to show each other respect. He apologized briefly, then prompted Sakuya.
Ordinarily Sakuya would have let other men's serious conversation flow past him, earning another blow from the boatswain's fist. This time, however, he had been eager for them to resume. He answered without delay.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺らがなんで集まってるのかは、正直俺もよく判りませんがね、話してたのはほらあの、ウミヒトの事だった」
source.english: “Honestly, I don't really know why we're all here either. But we were talking about that thing, you know. One of the Sea People.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……. No, my bad. Shouldn't have asked you. Oi, Sakuya, where were we again?」

It seemed like the Bosun was also aware of the Chief Engineer's chronic disease that left him unable to remember recent events, and for all that they got along like oil and water, the chief of the sailors and the chief of the engine room each had an understanding of where the other stood, so while offering a minor apology, he instead urged Sakuya to continue. Were this the usual Sakuya, he would once again suffer the iron fist of the Bosun for never paying attention to anything serious when spoken by another man, but this time alone, he was the one impatiently waiting for their conversation to continue, and he answered with no delay.
【Naomasa】 「Honestly, the reason why we're gathered here is not really something I understand myself, but we were talking about, you know, that Umihito thing.」

source.japanese:
───ウミヒト───
　
　深淵から浮上し来[きた]る、巨大な白いヒトガタ。嵐と追っ手から逃れ仰せたものの、今度は官憲に進路を阻まれた信天翁号の前に現れたる異形の存在。
　こうして朔屋達が機関室に集って話をしていられるという事は、官憲の巡視艦から逃れられたという事実を物語っており、あの異常事態からいかな流れを辿って今に至るのか、実に興味深く───
source.english:
The Sea People.
An enormous white human shape rising from the abyss. Having escaped the storm and their pursuers, the Albatross had found her course blocked by the authorities, and this strange being had appeared before her.
The fact that they could sit here talking in the engine room meant they had escaped the patrol vessel. How had that extraordinary situation developed into this one? A most fascinating question—

target.text: ───Umihito─── Surfacing from the deepest abyss, a giant, white humanoid. Though they had just managed to make good their escape from their pursuers and the storm, their course forwards was now blocked by the authorities; it was then that it had suddenly emerged before the Albatross, a grotesque existence.

And so the fact that Sakuya and the rest were gathered here in the engine room and speaking thus was a testament to the fact that they had also managed to escape from the patrol boat helmed by the authorities, but just what course of events had brought them from that absurd situation to the present? In truth, it was an incredibly fascinating───

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう、そうだったそうだった。
　マアしかしあんなこたァどうでもいいんだ。
　それより下級水夫達が最近バラックで作ってるあれの事だが」
source.english:
“Right, right. That was it.
Well, none of that matters. What's more important is what the junior sailors have been making in their shack lately.”

source.japanese: 実に興味深く、深く───思っていたのは朔屋だけだったようで、水夫長には釣った魚がミノカサゴ、見た目は派手だが毒がある、喰って喰えない事はないが面倒くさいと実にあっさり投げ出して、さっさと次の話に入る、ウミヒトへの興味はまるで無し。
source.english: Most fascinating—fascinating—but apparently only to Sakuya. To the boatswain, it was like catching a lionfish. Showy, but venomous. You could eat it, perhaps, but too much trouble. He tossed it aside with perfect ease and went straight on to the next topic, utterly uninterested in the Sea People.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right, that's it, that's it. But come on, what does that thing even matter? More importantly, about that stuff the deck boys recently made in one of the shacks.」

It truly was fascinating, very much so ───and the only one who seemed to think so here was Sakuya, for to the Bosun, it was like the fish he'd caught had turned out to be a luna lionfish, and while it looked real flashy, it was also venomous, and so finding it too bothersome to weigh if he should eat it or not, he instead just nonchalantly tossed it back in the ocean, promptly moving on the next topic: he held basically no interest in the Umihito.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「あいつら、バラックの中に土盛って、野菜なんぞを育てているようだが……。
　うまくいくと思うか？」
source.english:
“They've piled up soil in the shack and seem to be growing vegetables…
Think they'll make it work?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Those guys have made a pile of dirt inside a shack, and it looks like they're growing vegetables or something in there, but……. You think it's gonna work out?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「支那では、古代より船の道中、大豆を育ててモヤシにしていたという例もある。お陰で壊血病の害も抑えられたという。その辺りは西洋の船乗りより知恵深かったというところでしょう」
source.english: “There are accounts of soybeans being grown into sprouts aboard ships in China since ancient times. This is said to have reduced the harm done by scurvy. In that respect, they were wiser than Western sailors.”

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「だから、例がない事ではない。
　ただし、水夫君達が成功させられるかどうかはまた別だね」
source.english:
“So it is not without precedent.
Whether our sailors can succeed is another question.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「In China, there are examples from the ancient past of men growing soybeans on ships and eating the beansprouts as they sailed. As a result, they were able to limit the harmful effects of scurvy. It is said that, in this respect, they actually held a greater wealth of knowledge than Western sailors at the time.」 (TN: The Chief Engineer uses the old Japanese term for China here, "Shina", written "支那". After World War II, the Chinese claimed it was discriminatory, used derogatorily in the Sino-Japanese Wars, and so it is generally avoided now, replaced with "Chuukoku", written "中国", the same kanji as in Chinese.)
【Chief Engineer】 「As such, it is not unprecedented. However, whether the sailors will find success in their endeavours or not is a different story altogether.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だよなあ。しかもあいつらが植えてんのはモヤシなんぞよりむつかしい。トマトやニガウリあたりだ」
source.english: “Exactly. And what they've planted is harder to grow than sprouts. Tomatoes and bitter melons.”

source.japanese:
下級水夫達は細心の注意を払って育成に励んでいるようだが、なにしろ陸とは勝手が違う海の上、屋内とはいえバラックの造りはいい加減で、潮風が入れば時には大波に激しく揺すられる、先ほど宗右衛門が仕留めたとはいえ、鼠は後を絶たず、奴らは苗も囓る。なにより水夫君達は水夫であって農夫ではない。
　見込みはあまり高くはなかろうというのが座のおおよその意見だった。
source.english:
The junior sailors seemed to be tending their plants with the greatest care. But life at sea was not life on land. Indoors or not, the shack was poorly built. Salt wind found its way in; heavy waves sometimes shook it violently. Soemon had just dispatched a rat, but there were always more, and they gnawed seedlings too. Above all, these sailors were sailors, not farmers.
The general opinion around the table was that their chances were not particularly good.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right you are. Moreover, they've planted something a lot more complicated than some beansprouts. Stuff like tomatoes, bitter melons.」

The sailors seemed to have paid close attention to the finer details, making great efforts to nurture the plants, but they were out on the ocean, a place very different from land, and even if it was inside a building, the construction of the shacks was quite perfunctory; when the salty sea breeze came blowing, they would at times be made to violently shake and jolt by the surging waves, and even if Souemon had just put one down, there was also no end to the mice, and they would nibble on the saplings. And most pressing of all, the sailors were sailors, not farmers. It didn't seem like they should expect too much from it: that was the general opinion of those gathered here.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まあ、うまくいったらめっけもの、ってところだろ。飯にも幅が増える」
source.english: “Well, if it works, that'll be a bonus. Give us more variety at meals.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well, if things go well, it'll be a nice bonus, something like that. It'll add some variety to our meals.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「て訳で朔屋、手伝ってやれとは言わんが、邪魔したり生りかけの実をかっぱらったりするんじゃねえぞ。水夫共の機嫌を損ねるといろいろ面倒だからな」
source.english: “So, Sakuya. I'm not telling you to help, but don't get in their way or steal the fruit before it's ripe. Annoying those sailors makes all sorts of trouble.”

source.japanese: がっちり釘を刺されて朔屋、自分が信用されていない事はもちろん面白くなかったけれど、それよりウミヒトの話題が流されてしまったのが納得いかない。
source.english: A firm warning. Naturally, Sakuya disliked being so distrusted, but what bothered him more was having the subject of the Sea People brushed aside.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しませんてそんな事ぁ。
　てか、ウミヒトの方が気になるよ俺は。
　ありゃ一体なんだったのか───」
source.english:
“I wouldn't do anything like that.
Anyway, I'm more interested in that Sea Person.
What the hell was it—?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So with that said, Sakuya, while I won't tell you to help them out, don't get in their way or pilfer whatever fruits they manage to grow. It's always a heap of trouble when the sailors get in a bad mood.」

Given an astute warning, it wasn't that Sakuya found it amusing to not be trusted in the slightest, of course, but the thing he was most displeased with was that the topic of the Umihito had been completely glossed over.
【Naomasa】 「I wouldn't do something like that. But hey, I'm more concerned about the Umihito. What in the world was that thing───」

source.japanese: あの時浮上したウミヒトは───
source.english: The being that had risen from the sea that day—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺達だけ行かせたけれど、巡視船だけ通せんぼして───」
source.english: “It let us through, but blocked the patrol vessel—”

source.japanese: まるで、信天翁号を助けるように───
source.english: As though it were helping the Albatross—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「この船が得体の知れないなぁもともとだが、
あんな化け物とも縁があるとはさすがにびっくりだ。どういう事なんですよ、水夫長」
source.english:
“This ship's always been mysterious,
but I never expected it to have ties to a monster like that. What was all that about, Bosun?”

source.japanese: ───水夫達の菜園だ何だより、よほどそちらの方が重大事ではないかと食い下がるも水夫長ははんと鼻を鳴らして取りあわず、
source.english: Surely that was far more important than the sailors' vegetable garden? He persisted, but the boatswain merely snorted and refused to engage.

target.text: The Umihito that surfaced back then was───
【Naomasa】 「It only allowed us to leave, and it only denied the patrol boat passage───」
Almost as though it was…… coming to the Albatross' aid───
【Naomasa】 「I already knew this ship was one big enigma, but I'm certainly shocked to find she shares some kind of connection with a monster like that. What is all that about, Bosun?」
───But though he kept pressing that this was a matter far more important than the sailors' vegetable garden or whatever, the Bosun simply snorted with a "hmpf", not concerning himself with it at all,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「俺だってあれがなんなのかは知らねえし、
　べつにどうでもいいじゃねえか、
　だいたい二週間も前のコトだろうが」
source.english:
“I don't know what it was either.
And who cares?
It was two weeks ago, anyway.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「It's not like I know what that thing is either, and does it really even matter? It's already been two weeks since it happened.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おい殺し屋、
　てめえはなんぞ意見はあるか？」
source.english:
“Hey, assassin.
Got anything to say?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Oi, murderer, you have any opinion on this?」

source.japanese: 何故か彼までこの場に呼ばれていた、智里は、先程から懐手に腕組みで、黙然と卓に顔をうつむけ考えこんでいる様子、と見えたが、かくりと頭がのめった、船を漕いでいる。呼びかけに目を覚まして大欠伸、悪びれるところがない、実に悠然としたものである。
source.english: For some reason, Tomosato had been invited too. All this time he had sat with his arms folded inside his clothes, his head bowed toward the table, silently considering—or so it seemed, until his head dipped. He was nodding off. The question woke him, and he gave a great yawn without the slightest embarrassment. Perfectly at ease.

target.text: One could wonder why he'd even been called to this place, for Tomosato had been crossing his arms inside his kimono for some time now, looking down at the table in silence as if deep in thought, or so it seemed, but his head lurched forward: he was nodding off. He awoke as he was called upon with a great yawn, not a hint of shame to be seen; in fact, he was entirely composed.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……おお。この部屋ぁ陽気がよくって眠っちまったい。で、なんだって？」
source.english: “…Oh. Nice and warm in here. Fell asleep. What was that?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ウミヒトの事だよ。あんた、あれ見てなんか言ってたじゃないか。なんぞ心当たりとかは……」
source.english: “The Sea People. You said something when you saw that thing. Any idea what it was…?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Ooh. The climate down in this room makes me real sleepy. So, you were saying?」
【Naomasa】 「We're talking about the Umihito. Hey, didn't you say something when you saw it? Like you had some kind of idea about what it……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「『小学館入門百科シリーズ三二：妖怪なんでも入門』一四六ページ参照、だ」
source.english: “See page 146 of Everything You Need to Know About Monsters, volume thirty-two of Shogakukan's Beginner's Encyclopedia series.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はあ？」
source.english: “Huh?”

source.japanese: すらすらと諳んじた時、蒼い眸[ひとみ]が凛とした光を流して、機関室の赤い薄明かりの中で怜悧とあったが、台詞がなんとも手前勝手に垂れ流し、後は説明もない。本読みの水夫長や博学多識の機関長にも心当たりのない出版社と書名で、朔屋のみならず二人にも首を傾げさせる。この男の物言いと来たら何時でも此[こ]れ式[しき]の、彼自身にしか意味が判らない事ばかり。
source.english: As he smoothly recited the reference, his blue eyes gave off a clear light, keen in the engine room's red gloom. But he had spilled the words for his own convenience and offered no explanation. Even the book-loving boatswain and the widely learned engineer had never heard of the publisher or title. They tilted their heads along with Sakuya. The man was always saying things like this, intelligible only to himself.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Consult page 146 of 『The Shougakukan Encyclopediac Primer Series 32: Yokai for Dummies』」 (TN: Shougakukan is a real publisher of encyclopedias among much else in Japan. The "妖怪なんでも入門" is a real book, lit. "Introduction to all things yokai", published in 1974, written and illustrated by Mizuki Shigeru, who was a leading figure on the topic of yokai. He is also known, among many other things, for creating the manga "GeGeGe no Kitarou".)
【Naomasa】 「Haah?」

As he smoothly recited that from memory, a piercing, dignified light flowed from those azure eyes, a sagacious gleam within the dim red light of the engine room, but the line itself was a stream of awfully self-serving drivel with no explanation following it. Upon hearing a book title from a publishing company that neither the bibliophilic Bosun nor the extensively erudite Chief Engineer knew of, it was not just Sakuya who was left tilting his head quizzically, but the other two as well. The man's diction was ever thus: riddled with cryptic turns of phrase that only he himself could hope to fathom.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ともかく、海坊主かなんかの類だろ。
　俺が聞いたモノとはちと様子が違うようだが、まあ世界は広い。何があったっておかしかねえやな」
source.english:
“Anyway, some sort of sea monk, I suppose.
A little different from what I've heard of, but it's a big world. Nothing would surprise me.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Anyway, it's probably like some kind of Umibouzu. It's a bit different from the ones I've heard of, but the world's a big place. Anything can happen, really.」 (TN: An Umibouzu, written "海坊主", is a Japanese yokai. It takes the form of a giant, black, humanoid being, often encountered by ships at night, where a calm sea suddenly surges, only for a bald head to surface and destroy or damage the ship.)

source.japanese:
【智里】
「だいたい餅は餅屋で、海の事なら船乗りのあんた達だろうが」
source.english: “And you leave things to the experts. You're the sailors. The sea's your business.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「To begin with, every man knows his business best, so matters of the sea are best left to sailors like you, right?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「抜かせよ、てめえだって殺し屋てぇ言いながら、標的のこれと仲良く酒呑んでんじゃねえか。殺るンならさっさと殺りやがれよ、俺はとめねえから」
source.english: “Talk all you like. You call yourself an assassin, yet here you are drinking sociably with your target. If you're going to kill him, get on with it. I won't stop you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ろくでもない事思い出させないでくれよ水夫長。ていうか、あんたも水夫の長なら止めてくれよな……」
source.english: “…Don't remind him of things like that, Bosun. And if you're the head of the sailors, you ought to stop him…”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「うるせえ、かえって良い厄介払いになるくれえだ。とにかく、こいつも知らねえようだし、ウミヒトの事はこれきりだ」
source.english: “Shut up. Be a good way to get rid of a nuisance. Anyway, he doesn't know either. That's the end of the Sea People.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Cut the crap. You keep calling yourself a murderer, but there you are, knocking 'em back like old chums with your mark. If you're gonna kill him, then get it over with already, I ain't stopping you.」
【Naomasa】 「……Please don't make me remember things best left forgotten, Bosun. Actually, you're the boss of us sailors, so you should stop him……」
【Bosun】 「Shaddup. If anything, he'd be ridding me of a lot of trouble. Anyway, he doesn't seem to know anything either, so that's it for the Umihito.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それで、次の話だが───」
source.english: “Now, next item—”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So then, onto the next topic───」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ところで、私達はそもそも何故こんな会合を開いているのでしたか？」
source.english: “By the way, why were we holding this meeting in the first place?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Incidentally, why are we even holding this assembly here to begin with?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……朔屋。説明してやれ」
source.english: “…Sakuya. Explain it to him.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺だってよくわかんないってば。
　なんで呼ばれたの、俺も智里も」
source.english:
“I told you, I don't know either.
Why did you call me and Tomosato here?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……言ってなかったか？　まあたまには、女子供ぬきでな、船のあれこれの事を確認しておきてえわけだ」
source.english: “…Didn't I say? Well, sometimes I want to go over the ship's affairs without the women and children around.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それでこんな、色気もへったくれもない、むさ苦しい男所帯の寄り合いか……」
source.english: “So that's why it's a gathering of grubby men without a trace of charm…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Sakuya. Explain it to him.」
【Naomasa】 「I told you, it's not like I know that either. Why did you even call for us, Tomosato and me?」
【Bosun】 「……I never told you? Well, every now and then, I like to check in on what's happening around the ship. Without the women and kids around.」
【Naomasa】 「So that's why we're holding this sordid sausage fest with not a hint of sexiness to be found……?」

source.japanese:
朔屋としては、こんな薄暗い機関室で男だらけが額突き合わせてもそもそやっているくらいなら、シサムやキサラ、泪あたりも呼んだ方が見た目的に心が和らぐのにとつい不満を、口の端に上せた途端に水夫長の兇悪な一睨[にら]み。
　男尊女卑云々を賢しく言い出す以前の問題として、水夫長の単純な気分の問題なのだろう。それに付き合わされる朔屋としては色々言いたいところもないでもないが、ここで水夫長の機嫌損ねては後々厄介な事になろうと、卑屈に笑って口を噤んだ。
source.english:
If they were going to huddle together muttering in this gloomy engine room, Sakuya would have preferred to invite Sisam, Kisara, or Rui. The sight of them alone would have soothed his spirits. He let a little of this discontent reach his lips, and received a savage glare from the boatswain.
Before anyone clever started talking about male supremacy, this was probably just the boatswain's mood. Sakuya, obliged to accommodate it, had a thing or two he might have said. But annoying the boatswain now would make trouble later. He smiled cravenly and shut his mouth.

source.japanese: こうして信天翁号が、とにもかくにもあの窮地から逃れ出でてから数週間が経つ。そして過ぎてしまえば喉元の熱いのもなんとやらで、船の主だった面子はもう、あの巨大な白いヒトガタの事など思い煩[わずら]う事をやめていたのだった───
source.english: And so several weeks had passed since the Albatross somehow escaped that desperate situation. Once the scalding mouthful has passed the throat, its heat is forgotten, as the proverb has it; and the leading inhabitants of the ship had already ceased to trouble themselves over the enormous white human shape—

target.text: In Sakuya's head, if he had to spend his time squirming in this gloomy engine room while huddled together with a bunch of men, his mind would be visually comforted if they had called Shisamu, Kisara, or maybe Rui for him to look at, but just as that complaint was about to escape his lips, he was met with a vicious glare from the Bosun.

Setting aside any clever talk of male chauvinism and so on, the issue here was likely more fundamental: a matter of the Bosun's temperament. As someone forced to keep him company here, Sakuya had plenty he wanted to say, but he also figured that it would just spell a bunch of trouble later if he upset the Bosun, so with a servile smile, he kept his mouth shut.

Thus, several weeks passed since the Albatross somehow or other managed to escape from its predicament. Just as it is oft said how vows made in storms are forgotten in calms or some such, the leading figures of the Albatross had already ceased to worry about anything regarding that giant, white, humanoid form───

source.japanese:
およそこの世界の成り立ちというものは。
　虚空のただ中にとぐろを巻いた近無限の巨蛇の上に乗った、これも超大な神亀の更に乗っかった、やはり規格外の三匹の巨象が海と大地を支えている、という構造図に描かれる───
　などと端から叙述していけば、これは麻薬常用者あたりが、脳髄の荒廃と引き換えの酩酊作用のうちに空に飛翔せる精神体で獲得した胡乱げな認識とも聞こえよう。だかこれは古の天竺の学識共が遺した大真面目な宗論中の著述であったりするから恐れ入る。
　あるいは古代の沙門どもは大麻や鴉片に溺れていたという可能性も捨てきれまい。それくらい彼らの世界観や教義というのは複雑怪奇を極めているし、もしかしたら蘇摩なる伝説の霊薬にさえ手を染めていた可能性さえ。
source.english:
The world, broadly speaking, is arranged thus: an almost infinite serpent coiled in the void; upon it, an equally enormous divine tortoise; and upon that, three elephants of similarly extravagant dimensions, supporting the sea and land. Such is the diagram.
Presented in this fashion, it might sound like the dubious revelation of some habitual drug user, obtained by a spirit soaring through the heavens in an intoxication purchased at the cost of a ruined brain. Yet it appears in the perfectly serious religious writings left by the learned men of ancient India. Remarkable.
Or perhaps we should not dismiss the possibility that those ancient ascetics were steeped in hashish and opium. Their cosmologies and doctrines are strange and intricate enough. They might even have dabbled in that legendary elixir, soma.

target.text: The general opinion on the origin of this world is as follows. Atop a near-infinite serpent, coiled around himself in the middle of the void, rests a truly gargantuan sacred Jinki turtle, and atop that turtle, sure enough, rests three or four abnormally colossal elephants supporting the weight of the oceans and the land: that is how it is portrayed in the structural diagram of the cosmolo─── (TN: This is all based around Hindu cosmology. Here, the world-turtle is specifically referred to as a "Jinki", written "神亀", a turtle that was historically treated as an auspicious omen when sighted in Japan.)

If you were to describe it as such right from the outset, then it must surely sound like the questionable cognition of some sort of drug addict, one acquired as a spiritual body liberated from the fetters of flesh soaring through the skies, a feat achieved through the effect of some intoxication in exchange for laying ravage to the contents of your brains. But this is, in fact, recorded in the writings describing serious doctrinal disputes left behind by the scholars of ancient India. How awe-inspiring, truly.

Or perhaps we can not discount the possibility that the Shramana of antiquity spent their days addicted to hashish or opium. That is simply how complicated and mysterious their world view and doctrine was, and perhaps there is even the possibility that they had a taste of that legendary elixir known as Soma.

source.japanese: そういえば蘇摩の守護神というのは確か、と朔屋は帆差針を剛い布地に突き刺しながら幻想する。蘇摩の神というのはお月様を擬人（神格）化した、すげえイカす半裸の女神様ではなかったか───仏の経典とヴェーダの聖典が都合良く混じっているところからして、もう幻想を通り越して妄想の域だが、朔屋は良いなあ羨ましいなあ坊主の野郎、きっと女神のおっぱいから霊薬を直吸いにしてたんだろうなあと溜息を漏らした。婆羅門と沙門あたりに知られようものなら、印度古武術カラリパヤットと少林拳修めた僧兵集団を送りこまれてガンジス川あたりに叩きこまれそうな妄想の、ただ朔屋にとっては素直で切実な羨望で、それ故にいよいよ始末に負えない、そもそもまともな男であればそこまで発想も飛躍しない。
source.english: Come to think of it, wasn't soma's guardian deity…? Sakuya let his imagination wander as he pushed a sail needle through stiff cloth. The god of soma was the moon personified—or deified—as an exceedingly attractive, half-naked goddess, wasn't it? Mixing Buddhist scripture and the Vedas to suit himself already carried him past imagination into delusion, but he sighed. Lucky bastards, those monks. They must have drunk the elixir straight from the goddess's breasts. If the Brahmins or ascetics ever learned of such fantasies, they might send a band of warrior monks trained in the ancient Indian art of kalaripayattu and Shaolin boxing to throw Sakuya into the Ganges. To Sakuya, however, it was simply a sincere and urgent envy, which made him all the more hopeless. A sensible man would not have let his thoughts leap so far in the first place.

source.japanese:
おそらくは、朔屋が尻を据えているこの高所、信天翁号の上甲板から生えだした物見櫓からの眺めに影響されているのだろうの、潮の加減で船体が左にゆらり、右へとゆらりする水平線から、一体波という奴はなんで生まれるのかと思いを馳せた事から始まっている。それで、もし世界が蛇と亀と象とに支えられているというなら、そいつらが身じろぎする度に海と大地は揺らぐのだろうと、例の世界構造図を連想したのであるが。
　言うまでもなく、現実逃避である。
source.english:
It was probably the view from his high perch that had inspired him. He sat in the lookout tower sprouting from the Albatross's upper deck, watching the horizon as the tide rocked the hull gently left, then right, and wondering what made waves at all. If the world rested on a snake, a tortoise, and elephants, then whenever they moved, surely land and sea would shake. Thus he had recalled that diagram of the world's structure.
Needless to say, this was escapism.

target.text: "And on that note, if I remember right, the guardian deity of Soma was..."; so Sakuya fantasized as he pierced the sturdy fabric with his sail needle. He was pretty sure that the deity of Soma was a (divine) anthropomorphism of the Moon, and wasn't she also a really hot, half-naked goddess─── He mixed together parts of Buddhist sutras and the Veda in whatever way was convenient to him, and by this point, it had transcended the realm of fantasy and reached that of delusion, but all Sakuya thought was "Good for you, man. I wish that were me, you damn Buddhist priests, I'm sure you get to suck the sacred elixir directly from the goddess' tits!" while heaving a great sigh.

If the Brahmana or the Shramana came to know of this, they would send in a group of warrior monks who had mastered the ancient Indian martial art of Kalaripayattu and Shaolin Kung Fu, who would then toss him into the Ganges River, so blasphemous was his delusion, but in Sakuya's mind, this was nothing but honest, genuine envy, and consequently, he was truly beyond redemption: a reasonable man's conception would never have made such great leaps in the first place.

More than likely, he'd been influenced by the view from this tall place he had planted his buttocks upon, the watchtower that shot into the sky from the upper deck of the Albatross, and it had all begun when he witnessed how, depending on the tide, the ship would sway left or right, which set his mind to work wondering how exactly these waves were formed as they travelled here from the distant horizon. And then, what if perhaps the world was balanced on top of elephants on top of a turtle on top of a snake, and whenever they rustled their bodies, the oceans and the earth would shake with them, surely, and so he conjured up the associations leading to the aforementioned structural diagram of the world, but.
Needless to say, this was an escape from reality.

source.japanese: 朔屋の手に握られているのは帆差針、膝の上にのたくるのは数十丈に及ぶ帆布、命じられたは繕[つくろ]い仕事、布地は狭苦しい物見櫓の台を半ば埋めて梯子の口から零れている始末、それもぱりっと皓く陽の匂い孕んでいる新品ならいくらか気分も軽くしてくれる。
source.english: In his hand was a sail needle; across his knees sprawled hundreds of feet of canvas. He had been ordered to mend it. The stuff half-filled the lookout's cramped platform and spilled through the ladder opening. Had it been new, crisp white cloth bearing the scent of sunshine, it might have lightened his mood a little.

source.japanese: だが信天翁号においては、なんであれ新品などいう代物は、乞食が汚れ無き処女童貞を嘲罵するが如く軽侮せられ、またなかば目の仇にもされるのが習いで、船に引き攫[さら]われてきたばかりの朔屋などは、その『清潔』ぶりを散々に嘲笑われからかわれたものだ。実際には新品とは言い難い彼の襯衣も早速水夫長の、新人教育に名を借りた粛清の憂き目に遭い、不潔な船内の中でもその度合い更に勝る汚水槽に叩きこまれて、船の匂いが馴染むまでと二日ほど軟禁もされたり、ようやく解放された頃には鼻がほとんど馬鹿になっていたりで。この清潔蔑視、新品憎悪の精神から例外とされているのは機関長のワイシャツだがあくまで例外は例外。
source.english: But aboard the Albatross, new things of any kind were habitually scorned, rather as beggars might revile an unblemished virgin. They were treated almost as enemies. When Sakuya was first dragged aboard, his ‘cleanliness’ had earned endless mockery and teasing. His shirt was hardly new, but the boatswain had soon subjected it to a purge under the name of training a recruit. Sakuya had been thrown into the bilge tank, filthy beyond even the rest of the ship, and confined there for two days to acquire the ship's smell. By the time he was released, his nose had practically stopped working. The engineer's dress shirts were exempt from this contempt for cleanliness, this hatred of newness. But an exception was an exception.

source.japanese: ともかく、朔屋が前にして悪戦苦闘している帆布も、饐えた魚油の臭気が繊維の隙間まで染みつき、どこぞのしけた運河の泥ですすぎ洗いしたのではと嘆かわしくなるくらいの汚れようであり、朔屋が手つき拙く差し通す帆差針もまた、そう呼ぶのが烏滸がましい代物であった。適当な車輪からもぎとってきたと思しき輻の、端を金槌で叩き丸めて針穴にしているような物であった。
source.english: The canvas Sakuya was wrestling with, at any rate, had stale fish oil soaked into every gap between its fibers. It was so dirty he wondered dismally whether someone had rinsed it in the mud of a wretched canal. Nor did the object he clumsily pushed through it deserve the name of sail needle. Apparently torn from some convenient wheel, it was a spoke with one end hammered around into an eye.

source.japanese:
そもそもこの、帆布の繕[つくろ]いという仕事からして、で、なるほど船で帆布と言えば腑に落ちるように聞こえる、がそれは、と朔屋は上甲板を眺め回した。物見櫓の高みからだと、半ばからぶち折れ半壊の惨めを晒す煙突がいやでも目につく。左様煙突、信天翁号はこれでも一応、あくまで分類的にはレシプロ機関を搭載した船で、帆船ではない。檣柱など、ミズンもメインもフォアも見えはしない。
　辛うじて、舳先から魔女の鼻のように突き出す棒きれが斜檣とも見えなくもないが、繋がれる綱索など無く、下級水夫達のパンツの物干し竿と化している。
source.english:
Then there was the very job of mending canvas. Canvas aboard a ship: yes, that sounded reasonable. But only if—Sakuya looked across the upper deck. From the lookout's height, the miserable funnel, snapped midway and half-ruined, was impossible to miss. Yes, a funnel. For all her faults, the Albatross was, strictly by classification, a vessel powered by a reciprocating engine, not a sailing ship. There was no mizzenmast, mainmast, or foremast to be seen.
The stick projecting from the bow like a witch's nose might just pass for a bowsprit, but it carried no rigging. It had become a clothesline for the junior sailors' underpants.

target.text: Clasped tight in Sakuya's hand was a sail needle, and tucked atop his knees was what felt like dozens of jou worth of sailcloth, which he'd been ordered to mend, but the cloth took up most of the cramped space on the watchtower platform, even spilling out and down from the ladder entrance; had it at least been a brand new article, one crisply starched, pure white, and filled with the scent of sunshine, then he would have been in slightly higher spirits. (TN: One jou, written "丈", is an old Japanese unit of length, equivalent to approximately 3.03 metres.)

But aboard the Albatross, as long as it was new, whatever the article might be, it would be scorned the way a filthy beggar would sneer at an unsullied, virgin nun, and it was even habit for some to view such things with active hostility; for instance, Sakuya, after only just having been abducted onto the ship, was thoroughly ridiculed for his "unsoiled" air.

In fact, his shirt, which could hardly be called new, was promptly met with the tragic fate of being purged under the pretense of what the Bosun called "educating the green hand"; after it was dunked into the bilge tank, which was even dirtier than the rest of this already unsanitary ship's interior, he was then confined for two whole days until he had grown accustomed to the smell of the ship, and by the time he'd finally been released again, his nose was practically dysfunctional. The only thing that was an exception to this disdain for cleanliness and loathing of the new was the Chief Engineer's dress shirt, but in the end, an exception to the rule is just that.

Regardless, even this sail, which Sakuya was struggling so valiantly with, was ingrained with the sour stench of rotten fish oil, all the way into the cracks in the fibres, so deplorably filthy it made him wonder if it had not been rinsed and washed in the mud of some murky waterway somewhere, and the sail needle that Sakuya handled clumsily as he pierced the fabric? To call it such would be ridiculously presumptuous. It looked like a spoke that had been plucked off from some random wheel somewhere only to have the end beaten with a hammer into something that was probably supposed to be an eye.

And to begin with, this task of mending the sailcloth? Certainly, it sounded quite convincing when you spoke of sailcloth on a ship, but then Sakuya took a good view of the upper deck. From his vantage point atop the watchtower, he could not help but catch sight of the miserable state of the funnels, terribly bent and partially ruined from the midpoint, even if he wished he hadn't. Verily, funnels, for the Albatross was, of a sort, if only in terms of classification, a ship equipped with a reciprocating engine: she was not a sailing ship. There were no masts anywhere to be seen: no mizzen, no main, and no fore.

With some difficulty, one might barely be able to justify interpreting the rod that stuck out from the bow like the crooked nose of a witch as the bowsprit, but there were no ropes or anything tied to it, and it had turned into a laundry pole for the deck boys to dry their underwear on.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（……なんだってこう、意味もない仕事を押しつけてくるかなぁ……）
source.english: (Why do they keep saddling me with pointless work…?)

source.japanese: 既に幾度目か数えるのも阿呆らしいほどの溜め息は、欠伸とともに噛み殺された。単調でやり甲斐ない作業は青年の集中力を著しく割き、くわえて海は凪いで、物見櫓の高所ではいくらか拡大される横揺れも、こう退屈だと揺り椅子の揺れのように朔屋の体に物憂く緩い、眠気を催そうというもの。
source.english: Another sigh—counting them would have been idiotic—was swallowed along with a yawn. The monotonous, unrewarding work badly eroded his concentration. The sea was calm, and though the ship's rolling was amplified somewhat at the lookout's height, in his boredom it rocked his body as languidly as a rocking chair. Enough to make anyone sleepy.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （……This kind of feels like I'm having some compleeeetely pointless work foisted on me……）

He stifled a sigh, the likes of which he had already let out so many of that bothering to keep count felt ridiculous, together with a yawn. This monotonous, pointless task had already spent a remarkable portion of the young man's concentration, and in addition, the ocean was at a lull, so for all that the rolling of the ship was magnified in a place this high, it only shook Sakuya's body back and forth languidly with the tedious motion of a rocking chair, as though trying to make him drowsy.

source.japanese: これで朔屋がうたた寝せずに済んでいるのは、彼の監督という名目で寄越された船長クロの方が先に、さっさと船を漕ぎ出したのを眺めるうち、睡魔とすれ違ってしまっただけ、変に目が冴えてしまったという。
source.english: Sakuya had escaped dozing off only because Captain Kuro, sent along ostensibly to supervise him, had promptly begun nodding off herself. Watching her, he had somehow missed his own rendezvous with sleep. His eyes were oddly wide awake now.

source.japanese: 見ているうちにも、クロの頭が前に折れてこくり、やや持ち上がってはまたかくりと、船に在って櫂も持たずに船を漕ぐ。白子の娘の手は当然止まっていて、輻の帆差針の、針穴に麻糸を通そうとしていた名残を残すのみ。
source.english: Even as he watched, Kuro's head dipped, rose a little, and dipped again. Here aboard a ship, she rowed through sleep without an oar. Naturally, the albino girl's hands had stopped. She still held the makeshift needle and hemp thread, just as she had when trying to thread it.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（監督もお目付もあったものかい、これでさ）
source.english: (Some supervisor. Some watchdog.)

source.japanese:
内心毒づいたのもむべなるかな、針の穴に駱駝を通す様な、とは富める者が己の財貨を棄て去る事の困難を喩えた箴言だが、この輻の帆差針はそれはいい加減に作られ、鰹の眼窩ほども広く、通せないのは盲者か中風持ちくらいしかおるまいを、クロは何度も何度も通し損ねて、失敗を繰り返すうちに眠気に負けてしまって、つまりがろくに裁縫の経験のない朔屋より手は遅く役に立っていない。
　朔屋はいい加減この年になって己の無能を自覚しつつあり（それは怠惰で開き直りに近い認識ではあったけれども）、他人から能無し役立たずと後ろ指指さされても、酒に溺れてみるとか酒がない時は仕方なく猥本を開いていかがわしい世界に没頭するとかの、劣等感を紛らわす身の処し方を覚えるようになってある。
source.english:
His inward curse was understandable. Passing a camel through a needle's eye: a maxim likening that feat to the difficulty a rich man faced in abandoning his wealth. But this spoke-needle was so crudely made that its eye was as large as a bonito's socket. Only a blind person or someone with palsy ought to have failed to thread it. Kuro, however, had missed it again and again, until repeated failure gave way to sleep. In short, she was slower and less useful than Sakuya, who had scarcely any experience of sewing.
At his age, Sakuya had begun to recognize his own incompetence—though that recognition approached lazy defiance. When people called him a useless fool behind his back, he knew how to dull the sting: drown himself in drink, or, when there was no drink, open a dirty book and disappear into its disreputable world.

source.japanese:
ただ───
　
　陸からこの海の吹き溜まりのような信天翁号に移っても朔屋の立ち位置は変わらず、新米である事も手伝ってより一層の不遇をかこつてある彼でさえ、この船長、クロにはしばしば目を覆いたくなるのだった。
　あまりにも、自分よりも役立たずで。
　あまりにも、おつむが可哀相で。
source.english:
But—
Moving from land to this maritime refuse heap called the Albatross had not improved his standing. Being the new boy only made his lot worse. Even so, Captain Kuro often made him want to cover his eyes.
She was so much more useless than he was.
Her poor brain was so pitiable.

source.japanese:
いざ嵐、大時化ともなればクロの指揮能力というのは、朔屋を一グロス取り揃えても敵わないほど神かがったものとなり、それは青年も既に目にしてはいるのだが、普段の様子がお話にならない事夥[おびただ]しい。嵐過ぎ去り空晴れ渡っていくとともに栓を抜いた風船のように萎えてしまえば、それまでの神通力宿した勇姿など、深酔い時の幻覚のようなものではないかと信じがたい。ましてここしばらく海は穏やかで、クロが賦活される機会は絶えて、となれば彼女の無能が強調されるばかり。今だって朔屋としては辛抱強く手を動かしているのに、クロときたら佳い心持ちでおねむでござる。見かねて揺り起こそうとして。
　頭を睡魔に揺らしつづけるクロの、顔の下から何やらすぅと伸びてきた糸のある。
　鈍く光って、先に雫の玉をつけた糸はどうやら、唇から垂れてきた涎らしい。
source.english:
When a storm or heavy seas came, Kuro's command became so godlike that a whole gross of Sakuyas could not match her. He had already seen it. But her ordinary state was hopeless beyond words. As the storm passed and the sky cleared, she deflated like a balloon with the air let out. Her former valor, charged with supernatural power, became as hard to believe in as a drunken hallucination. The sea had been calm for some time now. There had been no opportunity for Kuro to come alive, and her incompetence only stood out more. Even now, while Sakuya patiently worked, Kuro was enjoying a lovely little nap. Unable to bear the sight, he was about to shake her awake.
Then, beneath the face bobbing in sleep, a thread began to extend.
Dully shining, with a droplet at its tip, it appeared to be saliva trailing from her lips.

source.japanese: ……朔屋の胸中に、むらむらと悪戯心が頭をもたげた。そら、眠り呆ける愛玩動物の、無警戒な腹をついまさぐってやりたくなるのと同じ情動だ、さしたる害意というのはない。
source.english: A mischievous impulse stirred in Sakuya's breast: the same impulse that makes one want to prod a sleeping pet's unguarded belly. No particular malice.

source.japanese:
害意はなかったけれど。
　かくり、かくりと頷[うなず]くような仕草続けるクロの顔の下、額のあたりに帆差針を突きだしてみたのも深く考えた行為ではなかったし、針先ではなく針の穴の方を向けてやるあたりも、まだ朔屋の優しさではあったろうけれど。
　クロの首が前に、船の揺れに合わせてより深くのめって、弾みに額を針穴の先が突いたのは朔屋の思いつき通りだったが、その反応は。
　朔屋の予想を超えていた。
source.english:
There was no malice in it, but—
He had not thought deeply before holding the sail needle beneath Kuro's nodding forehead; that he turned the eye toward her rather than the point might still count as kindness.
Her head dipped farther with the roll of the ship. Just as he intended, the eye of the needle prodded her forehead. Her reaction, however, exceeded his expectations.

target.text: The reason that Sakuya had managed to not doze off was because while he had been observing Captain Kuro, who had been made to accompany him here under the pretext of being his supervisor, as she promptly begun to nod off, he had just missed his own run-in with the Sandman, and he was left strangely wakeful.

Right before his eyes, Kuro's head would repeatedly lurch forwards, and a short while after she lifted it up, it would fall once more, the girl rowing her merry way down the ocean of sleep with no oars at hand. The albino girl's hands had, of course, come to a halt, with the only trace left of her having worked at all being the remnants of an attempt to pass the hemp thread through the eye of the sail needle made from a spoke.
【Naomasa】 （Fat lot of good this supervision and oversight does.）

Perhaps it was only quite right of him to harbour such venomous thoughts within, for though a proverb involving threading a camel through the eye of a needle did exist, a metaphor for the hardships of a rich man forsaking his own worldly fortune, this sail needle wrought of a spoke was pretty carelessly made, and the hole was as wide as the eye socket of a skipjack tuna; only those suffering from blindness or palsy would be unable to thread this needle, and yet Kuro had failed at doing so again and again, and while repeating her failure, she lost to the temptation of sleep, which is to say, her hands were even slower and less effective than Sakuya's, who himself barely had any experience with sewing.

At his age, Sakuya was finally starting to come to terms with his own incompetence (although it was a realization closely rooted in a defiance born of indolence); when he was criticized behind his back by others for being incompetent and useless, he would try to drown himself in alcohol, and in times where the bottle had run dry, he would resign himself to, say, opening a pornographic book and immersing himself in its sleazy world, so he had come to learn what actions he needed to take to distract himself from his own inferiority complex.

It was just that─── Though he had transferred from the land to this dreg heap of the ocean that was the Albatross, Sakuya's standing remained unchanged, yet even as he bemoaned his misfortunate lot in life compounded by his status as a newcomer, the mere sight of this captain, of Kuro, was often tragic enough to make him want to shield his eyes. Because she was simply so, so much more incompetent than Sakuya himself. Because her poor excuse for a brain was simply so, so pitifully dim-witted.
