But come a great storm at sea, Kuro's ability to command was so godlike that even were one to assemble a whole gross of Sakuyas, they would be unable to rival it, and the young man had already witnessed it with his very own eyes, but it was so tremendous a thing that her normal state of being was not even worth mentioning in the same breath. And as the storm passed and gave way to clear skies, when she would deflate like the air was being let out of a balloon, that heroic figure containing such divine powers seemed so fanciful, it left him wondering if it had not merely been a hallucination from when he had been deep in his cups.

And that was to say nothing of when the ocean was calm, where any opportunities for Kuro to be invigorated were cut off at the root, which only emphasized her incompetence. Even now, while Sakuya was patiently setting his hands to work, Kuro had already fallen into a comfortable nap. And when he could no longer just watch and went to shake her awake. From the bottom of Kuro's face, the girl still rocking back and forth in the embrace of sleep, was a string slowly drooping downwards. With a dull glow, and a small bead forming at the end of the string, it seemed to be drool dangling down from her lips.

……Within Sakuya's bosom, the irresistible urge to make mischief suddenly reared its ugly head. Look, it is the same affect that makes you want to grope around the defenceless stomach of a beloved pet lost in deep sleep, and it is done with no particularly malicious intent.

There was no malice to be found, but. Kuro's face still continued to nod forwards with jerking motions, and below her face, around her brow, he held out the sail needle; this, too, was not an action given any deeper thought, and the fact that he placed it with the needle eye pointing at her instead of the tip was likely an expression of Sakuya's kindness, however. Kuro's head bent forwards, lurching even deeper in tandem with the rolling of the ship; with that momentum, her forehead caught the top of the needle, exactly as Sakuya had envisioned, but her reaction, on the other hand. Now that exceeded Sakuya's wildest expectations.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……けひぃあっ!?」
source.english: “…Kehyaa!?”

source.japanese: 潮風の中のうたた寝で、すがれかけていた喉から漏れた音は、寝覚めの可愛さの欠片もなく、烏の喘鳴じみて、跳ね上がった肩は電極押し当てられた蛙のそれ、腰などは一寸は浮いていただろう。とすんと落ちて、その痛みに寝起きの顔をしかめたのも束の間、眠りの霞が晴れていくにつれ、白子の赤い眸[ひとみ]が、血走って、毛細血管張り裂けて血潮の涙零すのでは危ぶまれるまでに、見開かれ、
source.english: The cry that escaped her throat, already dried by a nap in the sea breeze, possessed not a trace of the charm of waking. It was more like a crow's wheeze. Her shoulders jumped like a frog with electrodes pressed to it; her backside must have risen an inch. She dropped with a thump and briefly winced at the pain. As the mist of sleep cleared, Kuro's red eyes opened so wide and bloodshot that he feared their capillaries might burst and spill tears of blood.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Kehyah!?」

Snoozing in the sea breeze, the noise that escaped her throat on the verge of withering was not a cute little yawn of awakening, it was more akin to the wheezing of a bird, shoulders jerking up like those of a frog with electrodes pressed against it, and even her behind seemed to float an inch up in the air. She fell down again with a thud, and though her sleepy face scrunched up as she winced at the pain, that only lasted a brief moment; as the haze of sleep cleared, her crimson albino eyes flew wide open, so bloodshot that he feared the capillaries within might burst and weep tears of hot blood,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「えあ、う。
　クロ───眠っちゃって、いた？」
source.english:
“Ah, uh.
Kuro—was asleep?”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……ごっ。
　ごげっ、ご、め……っ」
source.english: “…S-s—sor—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「よう。起きたか、クロ」
source.english: “Hey. Awake now, Kuro?”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「めっ……めん、ど、うぁっ」
source.english: “Sor… rry—ah!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんぞね、蛙でも呑んだか、
　腹ン中で鳴いてるような声で」
source.english:
“What's that? Swallowed a frog?
Sounds like it's croaking in your stomach.”

source.japanese:
度を逸した声音に朔屋の方もたじろいで、腰を浮かせる彼の前で、クロがべたん、身を二つ折りの、帆布に散った髪が目覚ましく白く、為した布地の汚らしさとの好対照を鑑賞、などしていられない。
　べたん、べたんとクロが夜店の安い玩具じみた運動を繰り返しているのは、彼女式の土下座と朔屋が覚った時には、白子は触覚をつつかれたザリガニのようにじたじたと後退っていて。後退っていく後ろは、また間の悪い事に櫓に造り付けられた梯子の方、台にぐるり巡らされた柵が途切れている箇所であり。
source.english:
Her extraordinary voice unnerved Sakuya too. As he rose slightly, she flopped forward, folding herself in half. The hair scattered across the canvas was strikingly white, but this was no time to appreciate its contrast with the filthy cloth.
Flop, flop: she repeated the movement like a cheap toy from a night stall. By the time he realized she was attempting her version of a prostration, the albino girl was scrabbling backward like a crayfish with its antennae prodded. Unfortunately, behind her lay the lookout's ladder—the gap in the railing around the platform.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ご、ごぇっ、
　ごめん、なさいっ。なさいでしたっ」
source.english:
“S-sorr—
I'm sorry! I was—I'm sorry!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、ごめんなさいって言いたかったのか。
　いやそんな、そこまでせんでも。
　ってクロ、そっちは、あ、駄目。
　まずいよ」
source.english:
“Oh, you were trying to say sorry.
No, really, you don't have to go that far.
Wait, Kuro, that way—ah, no.
That's bad.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ごめんなざい、ゆるして。
　もうしないよ、起きるよクロ。
　だから」
source.english:
“S-sorry, forgive me.
Won't do it again. Kuro'll stay awake.
So—”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「『箱のおしおき』もっ。
『おしりにトウガラシのおしおき』も……っ。
　しないで、やあああ……」
source.english:
“No box punishment!
No pepper-on-the-bottom punishment…
Don't, nooo…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだそりゃ、いったいどんな刑罰だ。
　いや、具体的には聞きたくないような。
　いやそうじゃなくクロ、
　俺は別にそんな怒っちゃ───」
source.english:
“What the hell kind of punishment is that?
Actually, I'm not sure I want the details.
No, that's not the point, Kuro.
I'm not even angry—”

source.japanese: 日頃クロがその不始末にどのような扱いを受けているものやら、なにやら拷問道具ばかり集めた博物室に迷いこんだような暗澹たる気持ちに囚われて、それどころではないと振り払って、このままクロがエビよろしく後ろに下がっては、と留めようと、つい手が走ったのは当たり前の反応で、しかしクロにはその手も打擲の拳と映ったか。
source.english: What treatment did Kuro receive for her daily blunders? A bleak feeling took hold of him, as if he had wandered into a museum devoted to instruments of torture. He shook it off. There was no time for that. If she kept retreating like a shrimp—he reached out to stop her, naturally enough. But perhaps Kuro saw even that hand as a fist raised to strike.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Eah, uh. Kuro───was fallen asleep?」
【Kuro】 「……So─. Sow─, so─, rr-……」
【Naomasa】 「Hey, you. Finally awake, Kuro?」
【Kuro】 「Rr─……rry, doh, uah.」
【Naomasa】 「What's wrong, you swallow a frog? You sure sound like one's croaking from your stomach.」

Even Sakuya shrunk back from her unhinged tone of voice, half-risen to his feet, and right before him, Kuro flopped down, her body doubled fully over, her hair scattered across the sailcloth a strikingly vivid white; the marked contrast it made with the filthiness of the cloth was worth appreciating, but that was not a luxury he could afford right now.

Again and again she repeated the motion of folding in half like a cheap toy at a night fair stall, and by the time Sakuya finally realized that this must have been her own unique way of prostrating herself, the albino was frantically retreating, like a crayfish whose antennae had been poked at. In an exceedingly unfortunate turn of events, right behind where she was backing away to was where the ladder was built into the watchtower, the one place where the boarded railing enclosing the platform was interrupted.
【Kuro】 「So─, sowe─, very, sorry. Rry.」
【Naomasa】 「Ohh, you were trying to say that you're sorry? No, no, you don't have to go that far. Wait, Kuro, not there, ah, don't. Oh no.」
【Kuro】 「Very sorry, forgive Kuro. Won't do it again, Kuro is awake. So.」
【Kuro】 「Not the『Box Punishment』 Or the『Chili in the Butt Punishment』 Please don't, noooooo……」
【Naomasa】 「What the-, what kind of punishment is that supposed to be? Never mind, I don't think I want to know the specifics. No, that's not what I mean, Kuro, I'm not even that mad at───」

Just what kind of treatment did Kuro usually suffer for her misdeeds, Sakuya wondered, consumed by a sense of gloom as though he had stumbled into a museum full of nothing but some manner of torture implements, but he shook it off, this really wasn't the time, for if Kuro kept this up, cowering backwards like a shrimp, then───with those thoughts running through his head, when he made to stop her retreat, it was but a natural reflex for him to stick his hands forwards towards her without even thinking about it, but perhaps, in Kuro's eyes, those hands also looked like fists poised to beat her?

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ごめんなさ───ぁぁぁーーっ!?」
source.english: “I'm sorr—aaaaah!?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「VERY SORR───aaaaーー!?」

source.japanese:
逃れようと大きく下がった、体が下に流れた、ざっと白い流れが宙に翻[ひるがえ]った、声音の端も頼りなく音階を下げてクロは、物見櫓の台から消えた。
　あっと身を乗りだして、朔屋は辛うじて掴み留めたとも。クロの靴の片方だけを。残りの脚やら身やらは、見事に逃したさ。
　信天翁号の物見櫓は造りも適当で、高さだって中途半端ではあるが、天辺から叩きつければただでは済むまい。うちどころが悪ければそれなりけり、だって充分あり得る。
　赤い血潮に白の髪と肌を染め抜いて、甲板上に横たわっているクロ、頭の鉢はぱっくり割れて、枯れ枝の手足は脆く折れてでたらめに投げ出される、体温もたちまちに冷えていく。
source.english:
She drew sharply back to escape—and slipped downward. A white streak flicked through the air; the end of her cry descended feebly through the scale. Kuro vanished from the lookout platform.
Sakuya lunged forward and just managed to catch her. One of her shoes, that is. The rest of her leg and body escaped him beautifully.
The Albatross's lookout tower was carelessly built, and of no impressive height. But a fall from its top would still do damage. Land badly, and it might be the end.
Kuro lying on the deck, her white hair and skin dyed red with blood. Her skull split open, her twig limbs snapped and flung at random. Her warmth rapidly leaving her.

source.japanese:
この時物見櫓に、小啄木鳥の飛んできて、鳥というより大柄な蝉の態で物見櫓の柱に留まりつ、朽ちかけた木材の中から木喰い虫を突きだした嘴の旋律が、場に奇妙な、そして物凄まじい間を添えた事である。
　この小啄木鳥、本来の生息域から遠く離れて信天翁号のバラックに住まいしている鳥であるのだがそれはさておき、予想外の事態に朔屋は、手の中に残ったズック靴を眺めてわなわなと口を悲鳴の形に開けて、ふと首を傾げた。
source.english:
At that moment, a Japanese pygmy woodpecker flew to the lookout. Looking more like an oversized cicada than a bird, it clung to a post and tapped out a melody as it pecked wood-boring insects from the rotting timber. The sound lent the scene a strange and dreadful pause.
This little woodpecker lived among the Albatross's shacks, far from its natural habitat, but let that pass. Faced with the unexpected, Sakuya stared at the canvas shoe left in his hand. Trembling, he opened his mouth to scream—then tilted his head.

source.japanese: 口を間抜けな形に開けたまま、クロのズック靴へと鼻先を近寄せて、すんすんと嗅いで。瞼をぎゅっと閉ざしたのは、クロの末期から目を閉ざしたいとかそんな臆病心ではなく、もっと判りやすい拒絶反応の。
source.english: His mouth still hanging stupidly open, he brought Kuro's shoe to his nose and sniffed. He squeezed his eyes shut—not in cowardice before Kuro's death, but in a much simpler reflex of disgust.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわあ。こりゃ臭えや。
　あいつ、なりはああでも足の臭いは一人前だぁ。なんか鳥の巣みたいな臭いがすっぞこれ……」
source.english:
“Ugh. That stinks.
Whatever she looks like, her feet smell as much as anyone's. This thing smells like a bird's nest…”

source.japanese: 顔を遠ざけてはまた怖々と近づけてはご丁寧にのけぞって、三ヶ月ばかりも忘れ去って放置した弁当箱の蓋をついつい開けたくなる人間心理と共通しているとはいえ、やはりどうにも頭が湧いている。
source.english: He drew his face away, brought it cautiously back, and each time dutifully recoiled. Perhaps it was the same human impulse that makes one want to open a lunchbox forgotten for three months. Still, there was plainly something wrong with his head.

source.japanese: それでも、まだこんこんと小啄木鳥が柱を打つ、リズムの中に朔屋にじわじわと恐怖が再来しつつあった。というより小啄木鳥も靴の臭気もあったものかは、とにかくクロの末期を見届けないと、そしてもし本当にくたばっていたなら、皆になんと申し開きを立てよう、いや、在らぬ嫌疑ひっ被さられるくらいなら、いっそ死骸をどこかに隠してしまうかどこがいい？　船倉の奥深くか、それとも簡単に海か？　朔屋の脳髄が彼にしては珍しく目まぐるしく回転するうちに。
source.english: Even so, amid the woodpecker's continuing knock-knock at the post, fear began to return. Never mind birds or the shoe's smell: he had to establish Kuro's fate. And if she really had died, what could he say to the others? No, rather than have some false accusation pinned on him, perhaps he should hide the body. Where? Deep in a hold? Or simply in the sea? His brain whirled with an energy uncommon in him, when—

target.text: She recoiled sharply to escape him, and then her body slid downwards, a stream of white briefly fluttered through the air, her faltering voice finishing its precarious descent into silence as Kuro disappeared from the watchtower platform. With a cry of surprise, he leaned forwards, and Sakuya just barely managed to grab hold of her. Of one of Kuro's shoes, that is. The rest of her leg and her body had all entirely escaped his grasp.

The construction of the watchtower on the Albatross was also done by halves, why, even its height was rather underwhelming, but were you to fall from the top, it would not end without injury. And were you to land on the wrong thing, there was a distinct possibility that it could spell the end for you. With white hair and skin stained red in a tide of warm blood, Kuro was flat on the deck, the top of her head split wide open, her limbs, brittle as withered branches, broken, splayed out at haphazard angles, and her body temperature also rapidly falling.

Right then, a pygmy woodpecker flew over to the watchtower, though it clung to the post of the tower in a manner more closely resembling a giant locust than a bird, and the drumming of its beak, which pecked at decaying wood to dig out the bark beetles within, punctuated the silence with a rhythm at once bizarre and ghastly. This pygmy woodpecker was a bird that resided in the shacks on the Albatross, a place far from its natural habitat, but setting that aside, faced with this unexpected turn of events, Sakuya stared at the canvas shoe still in his hand, his lips trembled as they fell open in a wordless scream, and then he suddenly tilted his head.

With his mouth still wide open, he lifted Kuro's canvas shoe to the tip of nose, then gave it a good, long sniff. The reason he wrenched his eyes shut was not from a desire to avert his eyes from Kuro's grisly fate, nothing so gutless: it was a more transparent act of visceral rejection.
【Naomasa】 「Yuck. This reeks. That girl might not look like much, but her feet stink with the best of them. Phew, this thing smells like a damn bird's nest or something……」

Pulling his face away from it, then timidly approaching it again, only to bend backwards with utmost caution: his actions held much in common with the human psychological desire of wanting to open the lid of a lunchbox that you had forgotten about and left to fester for three months, but all the same, this man had completely lost his mind.

Even so, as the pygmy woodpecker continued its rhythmic knocking against the pillar, a slow, creeping dread resurfaced within Sakuya. Never mind any pygmy woodpeckers or smelly shoes, he had to ascertain Kuro's final moments with his own eyes, and then, if she truly had croaked, he had to figure out how he would even begin to explain it to the others, no, if he would just end up being falsely accused of something, then would it not be better if he just hid her corpse away somewhere? Maybe down in the depths of the hold, or perhaps simply in the sea? And while the cylinders in Sakuya's brain spun at what was an unusually rapid velocity for him.

source.japanese:
【声】
『……お前、ナニを揉めたんだ。
　女が自分で身投げすンなあ、
　覚悟の風情ちうもんがあるが』
source.english:
“What did you two fight about?
A woman jumping to her death ought to have a certain air of resolve.”

source.japanese:
【声】
『突き落としてやるんなら、
　もっと場所選んでやりなよ。
　こんなみっともねえ櫓なんかじゃなくさ』
source.english:
“And if you're pushing her off,
choose a better spot.
Not some shabby tower like this.”

source.japanese:
【声】
『せめて時計台の天辺とか、
　白糸の滝の崖っぷちとかよう』
source.english:
“At least the top of a clock tower,
or a cliff at Shiraito Falls.”

target.text: 【Voice】 『……Dude, what were you two fighting about? You know, when a woman goes and throws herself off a ledge, she's got this certain air of resolve about her.』
【Voice】 『So if you're gonna push her off, then pick your location better. Not a watchtower this unsightly.』
【Voice】 『You could at least choose the top of a clock tower, or the cliff edge by the Shiraito Falls or something.』

source.japanese:
およそ良識派からは眉を顰[ひそ]められそうな不穏な言は、だがその喉から吐かれると飄々と、戯作本のような風情さえ漂わせて、身ごなし軽く梯子から頭を覗かせた、目が蒼い。
　智里だった。殺し屋の。
　袴の裾[すそ]を颯と捌[さば]いて台に身を滑りこませる、彼が片手には細い、白い足首の握られて、どれだけ肉付き薄くとも、ちゃんとまだ血の通ったクロの足、逆さ吊りに、朔屋に突きだして、
source.english:
Words likely to make any decent person frown, yet from that throat they emerged with a breezy air almost worthy of an old comic tale. A head appeared lightly above the ladder. Blue eyes.
Tomosato. The assassin.
He swept aside the hem of his hakama and slipped onto the platform. In one hand he held a thin white ankle: Kuro's, still living however scant its flesh. He presented her to Sakuya upside down.

target.text: Unsettling words that would surely raise eyebrows among the more respectable members of society, but when expelled from that throat, they sounded so effortlessly aloof that they even carried the droll air of the satirical pulp fiction of yore, and a head nimbly poked up from the top of the ladder, with azure eyes. It was Tomosato, the murderer. He swiftly adjusted the hem of his hakama, then slid himself up on the platform, a slender, white ankle held in one of his hands; regardless of how bony it was, that was Kuro's leg with lifeblood still running through its veins, suspended upside down, and he thrust it at Sakuya,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「お前、梯子段に昇ろうとすりゃあ上からこの白子が降ってきてけつかる。それともなにか、俺の天骨にこいつを叩きつけて、亡き者にしてくれようてぇ腹か」
source.english: “I start up the ladder, and this albino girl comes raining down on me. What, were you planning to smash her onto my head and finish me off?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Buddy, just as I was making my way up the rungs of this ladder, this damn albino came crashing down on me from above. Or what, were you trying to crack my skull open with this girl and put me six feet under? That your play here?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おお、おッかねえ。直の字、お前もしかしたら、いい人殺しになれるかもしれんぞ」
source.english: “Oh, terrifying. Nao, you might make a fine murderer yet.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こ、殺し屋はあんただろうがッ。
　でも、正直助かったぁ……」
source.english:
“Y-you're the assassin!
But honestly, you saved me…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Oooh, how scary. Big Nao, maybe, just maybe, you could make for a good murderer.」
【Naomasa】 「You're the only m-, murderer here. But, seriously, you really saved my bacon……」

source.japanese:
無造作に投げ出されたクロの体は笑えてしまうくらい軽い音を、いや笑い事になったのは朔屋にとってなんとも僥倖だったろう。落ちてくるクロを抱きとめたのが他ならぬこの男だったのも。他の乗り組みなら、どんな仕置きが朔屋に下されていたか知れない。
　落下に気[ショック]死していたクロも乱暴な扱いに目を覚まして、きょろきょろとして、はっと飛びつく帆布と帆差針に、慌ててて仕事を続けようとしているあたり、最前の事故の事など都合良く頭から飛んでいるらしい、ここまでくるとこの娘の脳の造りはある意味羨ましい。
source.english:
Kuro's body made an almost comically light sound as he casually tossed her down. That it could now be a laughing matter was a tremendous stroke of luck for Sakuya. So was the fact that this particular man had caught her. Had it been another member of the crew, who knew what punishment Sakuya might have received?
Kuro, who had fainted from the shock of falling, woke at this rough treatment. She looked around, then hastily seized the canvas and needle and tried to resume her work. Apparently the accident had conveniently fallen out of her head. At this point, the structure of her brain was almost enviable.

target.text: Carelessly thrown aside, Kuro's body made a laughably light sound; well, the fact this ended up being a laughing matter at all was surely a stroke of incredibly good fortune for Sakuya. The one who had caught the falling Kuro in his arms was none other than this man. Had it been any other member of the crew, Sakuya could not even begin to guess at the punishment that would have been inflicted on him.

Kuro, who had fainted from the shock of falling, now awoke due to the rough treatment, then looked around goggle-eyed, but given that, as though having a sudden realization, she then pounced at the sailcloth and sail needle, frantically attempting to continue her work, it seemed that the accident from just moments ago had conveniently vanished from her mind; at this point, the wiring of this girl's brain was, in a certain sense, enviable.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ま、今度はもっと巧い事やるんだな。
　もっともお前にそういう肝があンなら、
　そもそもこんな船にゃ捕まってねえだろうが」
source.english:
“Well, do a better job next time.
Though if you had the guts for that, you wouldn't
have been caught by a ship like this in the first place.”

source.japanese: どこまでも人聞きの悪い口を垂れる智里ながら、朔屋にとってもクロにとっても恩人で、人殺しが気まぐれに人を救う諧謔などこの際脇に置いて朔屋は問いかける。
source.english: Tomosato could make anything sound incriminating. Nevertheless, at this point he was a benefactor to Sakuya and Kuro alike. Setting aside for the moment the irony of a killer saving someone on a whim, Sakuya asked—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だから事故なんだよこれは。
　ともかくありがとうな……で、あんたは？
　なんでここに？」
source.english:
“I'm telling you, it was an accident.
Anyway, thanks… And you?
Why are you here?”

source.japanese: それには答えず智里は、手を目庇しに額に当てて、櫓の柵から身を乗りだして見やるが海原の一方へ。
source.english: Instead of answering, Tomosato shaded his eyes with a hand, leaned over the lookout railing, and gazed in one direction across the sea.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Well, just be more clever about it next time, alright? Though, guess if you had the guts to pull something like that, you wouldn't be stuck on a ship like this in the first place.」

Despite Tomosato's endless stream of scandalous remarks, he was still the man both Sakuya and Kuro owed their lives; Sakuya set aside the inherent humor in a murderer saving someone's life on a whim and posed him a question.
【Naomasa】 「I'm telling you, it was an accident. Anyway, thanks……so, what about you? Why are you here?」
Leaving that unanswered, Tomosato instead put his hand to his brow as a visor, leaned over the watchtower parapet, then cast his gaze in a particular direction out across the open sea.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おお、やっぱり山が立ってやがら。
　龍の親爺はまだ気づいちゃねえようだが。
　直正、あすこが見えるか？」
source.english:
“Aye, a bird mountain's forming out there.
Old Long doesn't seem to have noticed yet.
Naomasa, can you see it?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Damn, would you look at that, there really is a mountain rising. Though it doesn't seem like old man Long has noticed yet. Naomasa, you see it over yonder?」
【Naomasa】 「Err……?」

source.japanese:
この男の蒼い眸[ひとみ]というのは、朔屋と同じ民族に属しているはずなのに希有であり、この海と同じく測りがたい深さとそして透徹な光を湛える時がある。そんな智里と同じものが見えるかどうか危ぶみながら、朔屋が隣で眼を細めると、信天翁号を離れる事二浬[マイル]ばかりの、舳先と同じ方角の洋上に、水鳥が集い、翼広げて旋回しつ、降りたり舞い上がったりを繰り返しているでないか。
　これは鰹[カツオ]や鰯[イワシ]の類が群をなして海面近くまで揚がってきた時などに見られる現象で、水鳥が狙いやすい魚に集まるのである。漁師言葉で『山が立つ』と言い習わして、大漁を約束する先触れとして有り難がられる。
source.english:
Though Tomosato belonged to the same people as Sakuya, blue eyes like his were rare. At times they held an unfathomable depth and lucid light, like the sea itself. Doubting whether he could see what Tomosato saw, Sakuya narrowed his eyes beside him. About two nautical miles away, in the direction of the Albatross's bow, seabirds had gathered. They wheeled with spread wings, descending and rising again.
This happened when schools of bonito, sardines, or the like came close to the surface. The birds gathered for fish easy to catch. Fishermen called it a ‘mountain rising,’ and welcomed it as the promise of a large haul.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ……確かに。鴎か海猫か。
　なんか魚群が来てんのかな。
　水夫達に教えてやれば、早速釣りが始まるよ」
source.english:
“Oh… Yes. Gulls, or black-tailed gulls.
A school of fish coming, maybe.
Tell the sailors, and they'll start fishing straight away.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺もこんな退屈仕事より、まだそっちの方が面白そうだ」
source.english: “I'd rather do that than this boring job.”

target.text: The azure eyes of this man were quite the rarity, especially given that he should belong to the same ethnicity as Sakuya, and there were times when they harboured both a depth as immeasurable as this very ocean and a light as clear as crystal. While he found it doubtful that he would be able to see the same things as these eyes belonging to Tomosato could, when Sakuya narrowed his eyes by his side, there, about two miles away from the Albatross, on the surface of the sea in the same direction as the bow, was there not a gathering of seabirds, their wings spread wide and circling, locked in an endless dance of diving and soaring?

This is a phenomenon seen when the likes of bonito or sardines form schools that rise all the way up to near the surface of the sea, with the seabirds then congregating around the easy prey. In the language of Japanese fishermen, it is known as the idiom 『A mountain rises』 and it is greatly appreciated as a herald of a bountiful catch.
【Naomasa】 「Yeah……sure is. Seagulls, or black-tailed gulls maybe? Wonder if there's a school of fish. If we tell the deck boys, they'll get to fishing them up right away.」
【Naomasa】 「Sound a lot more interesting to me than this drudgery.」

source.japanese: 信天翁号は基本的に（一応）交易船であり、漁船ではないのだが、漁の当てあればむざむざ見逃しはしない。航海の中で鮮魚は、乗り組み達の食事として、あるいは臨時の収穫物としていつだって歓迎されるのである。智里より早く水夫長に伝えれば、少しは彼の覚え目出度くもなろうとさもしく櫓を滑り降りようとして、朔屋は智里から襟首を摘[つま]まれた。
source.english: The Albatross was basically—nominally—a trading vessel, not a fishing boat. But she never passed up a chance of a catch. Fresh fish on a voyage were always welcome, whether as food for the crew or an incidental haul. If he told the boatswain before Tomosato did, he might gain a little favor. With this mean calculation, Sakuya was about to slide down from the lookout when the assassin caught him by the collar.

target.text: The Albatross was, at her core, (nominally) a merchant ship, not a fishing boat, but if there was a catch to be had, they wouldn't just let it pass them by. On a voyage at sea, fresh fish are always a welcome sight, be it as a meal for the crew or an incidental bounty to sell. If he told the Bosun about it before Tomosato could, he might get back in his good books, Sakuya thought, but as he greedily made to slip down from the watchtower, Tomosato pinched Sakuya by the scruff of his neck.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「残念だが魚と遊ぶつもりなら気がはええ。
　お前望遠鏡持ってたろ？
　そいつで確かめてみ？」
source.english:
“Sorry, but it's too early to go playing with fish.
You've got a telescope,
haven't you? Check with that.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Unfortunately, if you're planning on playing with fish, you're being hasty. You have a telescope with you, right? Why don't you take another look through that?」

source.japanese:
殺し屋の蒼い眸[ひとみ]は、この時既に水鳥たちが何に群れているのか勘づいていたのかも知れない。
　とにかく朔屋はいわれるままに、ズボンの後ろに差していたあの望遠鏡、泪から押し頂いた戦利品、折り畳みの奴を早速繰り出して、宛がった、片目の視界の焦点を合わせるのにしばらく手間取っていたが。
　青年の指が、望遠鏡の、実用というより工芸品めいた精緻な浮かし彫りを強く握りしめて節だった。
source.english:
Perhaps the assassin's blue eyes had already discerned what the birds were gathering around.
Sakuya did as instructed. He drew the collapsible telescope tucked behind his waistband, the spoils graciously bestowed by Rui, and put it to his eye. It took him a while to focus.
His fingers tightened, knuckles prominent, around its delicate relief work, more like a crafted ornament than a practical tool.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんか……浮かんでる……ありゃあ───」
source.english: “Something's… floating… That's—”

target.text: Perhaps the azure eyes of this murderer had, in this moment, already noticed what it was the seabirds were circling. Regardless, doing as he was told, Sakuya quickly whipped out the telescope, the spoils of victory so graciously bestowed upon him by Rui, from its holder at the back of his trousers, extended it, then set it to his eye, but he struggled for a little while with aligning the focus of his one-eyed view. The young man's fingers gripped the intricate relief carvings of the telescope, more reminiscent of a work of art than a practical tool, so tightly his knuckles protruded.
【Naomasa】 「There's something…… floating……that's───」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい、人じゃあないか！」
source.english: “Hey! That's a person!”

source.japanese:
何やらの木っ端にあれは、しがみついているのか身を縛りつけているのか。
　小柄で、細身で、亜麻色の髪が長い───
　女の子か!?　と推し量った、途端に、朔屋の心が逸った。それも相当に軌道からこっ外れた勢いと角度で。
source.english:
Was that figure clinging to some splinter of wood, or lashed to it?
Small, slender, with long flaxen hair—
A girl!? The instant the thought occurred to him, Sakuya’s heart took off—at considerable speed, and on a course considerably removed from reason.

source.japanese: 頬は青ざめて、弱々しい、けれどまだ息を通わせているのはきっと豪華客船あたりから放り出された令嬢だ。それもこんな航路から外れた洋上に漂うあたり、何か格別の曰くがあるのに違いない。内乱から落ち逃れて異国の地に身を隠そうとしている貴族の姫さまという事も充分有り得るいやそうに決まった。しかもあんな風に水鳥を集って彼女の位置を報せているのは、その純真で気高い心根を、禽類ながらも感得したものだろう。
source.english: Pale cheeks, a frail body, yet still breathing: surely a young lady cast overboard from some luxury liner. And to be adrift so far off the shipping lanes—there must be some singular history behind it. A princess of the blood, perhaps, escaped from a civil war and bound for hiding in a foreign land. Entirely possible. No, unquestionably so. Why, the waterbirds themselves had gathered to proclaim her whereabouts, brute fowl though they were, having perceived the purity and nobility of her heart.

source.japanese:
気高く美しい、異国の姫君───！
　
　深窓の身の上は、今まで男など知るよしもない処女の肌、傷ついた身も心も、掬いあげた朔屋の前には開かれて、初めての男の抱擁を受け入れる。
　後は亡命下に身を落ち着けてから、あらかじめ分散させておいた財産を結集させて、それを元手にひっそりと、けれど贅沢な暮らしを送るのもいい。なんだったら、追われた国に戻って王制を取り戻す手伝いをしたっていい。ただし前線に出るという暴挙は論外、常に姫の傍らに侍って守り、やがては救国の英雄として歴史に名を残そう……。
source.english:
A noble and beautiful princess of foreign parts—!

Sheltered from the world, her virgin flesh had never known a man; now wounded body and wounded heart alike would open before Sakuya, her rescuer, and receive a man’s embrace for the first time.
Once safely settled in exile, she could gather the fortune she had prudently dispersed beforehand; with that as their capital, they might live quietly but luxuriously. Or he might even help her return to the country that had cast her out and restore the monarchy. Going to the front was, of course, out of the question. He would remain always at the princess’s side, attending and protecting her, until at last his name went down in history as the hero who saved a nation…

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Oi, isn't that a person!」

There, upon that scrap of wood. Was he clinging for dear life, or had he lashed himself to it? Slender of build, small of stature, with long, flaxen hair─── WAS THAT A GIRL!? He conjectured thus, and in that instant, Sakuya's mind wandered. And it was with considerable force, at quite the angle, veering significantly from its prior trajectory.

Frail, pale-faced, and yet she still drew breath: this all suggested she must have been a high-born lady, cast into the sea from some luxury ocean liner. And for her to be adrift on the ocean this far from any sea lanes, there undoubtedly had to be some extraordinary circumstances at play. And it was more than possible that she was a young lady of noble birth hiding herself in a foreign land, on the run from a rebellion, no, it had to be so. Moreover, that the seafowl should flock together thus to herald her presence must surely have been because, birds though they are, they had keenly sensed the purity of her noble soul.

A noble beauty, the princess of a foreign land───! Raised in a secluded inner room in a vast mansion, her virgin skin yet to know the touch of a man; her broken body and heart both would be laid bare before Sakuya, he who picked up their scattered pieces, as she surrendered to a man's embrace for the very first time.

Later, after settling down in exile, they would gather her assets that had been dispersed beforehand, and with that capital, they would live modestly, but living a life of luxury wouldn't be bad either. And if she were so inclined, why, they could also return to the country from which she was exiled, and there, he could help her restore the monarchy. However, partaking in violence on the front lines would be out of the question, for he would always serve and protect his princess right by her side, and eventually, he would go down in history as the hero who brought salvation to her country…….

source.japanese: づん、と片目に衝撃めりこんで、望遠鏡の視界の中に繰り広げられていた、思春期の自意識過剰気味の妄想はたちどころにちらちら明滅する光に覆いつくされ、朔屋は痛みのあまり物見櫓の上をごろごろ転がり回り、危うく先ほどのクロの二の舞を演ずるところであったという。
source.english: Something slammed into one eye. The adolescent fantasy unfolding in the telescope's field—already swollen with self-importance—vanished beneath a burst of flickering light. Sakuya rolled around the lookout in agony, narrowly avoiding the same fate Kuro had suffered moments before.

target.text: Something impacted with his eye, sinking into it with a thunk, and the delusions reeking of overly self-conscious adolescence, which had been unfolding within the view through the telescope, were immediately obscured by flickering lights; Sakuya was in such immense pain that he rolled around on top of the watchtower, barely avoiding giving a repeat performance of Kuro's misfortune from earlier.

source.japanese: 愚かにも妄想を言葉にしていたのか、それとも都合の良い事ばかり考える頭の中を見透かされたか、智里は朔屋の眼窩にめりこませた望遠鏡を引き剥がすと、何が洋上に起こっているのか、先程から知りたくてたまらない様子で柵にぴょんぴょん飛びついていたクロに手渡してやりながら、来た時と同じく平然と、櫓から降りていったのだった。はやばやと興味を失ったといわんばかりに、気まぐれに。
source.english: Had Sakuya foolishly spoken his fantasy aloud, or had Tomosato simply seen through a head occupied entirely with thoughts convenient to its owner? Tomosato wrenched from Sakuya’s eye socket the telescope he had just driven into it and handed it to Kuro, who had been hopping at the railing for some time, beside herself to know what was happening out at sea. Then, with the same composure with which he had arrived, he climbed down from the lookout—as capriciously as if he had already lost interest.

target.text: Had he foolishly put his delusions into words, or perhaps his brain full of nothing but wishful thoughts had been read like a book, for Tomosato ripped away the telescope currently digging into Sakuya's orbital cavity, and while handing it over to Kuro, who had skipped over to the railing a little earlier, seemingly unable to endure her burning curiosity about what was happening at sea any longer, he then crawled down from the watchtower with the same calm as when he had arrived. All but saying that he had quickly lost any interest on a sudden caprice.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「直正よう。もちっと良く見てみろや。
　ありゃあ、男だぜ───」
source.english:
“Naomasa. Take a better look.
That's a man—”

source.japanese: もちろん、朔屋は目の痛みでそれどころではなく、クロはクロで望遠鏡のレンズにこびりついた朔屋の涙を布で拭ううち、そちらに夢中になって他愛なく他の事など目に入らなくなっていた為、智里の呟きは空しく潮風に持っていかれて洋上にほぐれた。
source.english: Sakuya, of course, was too occupied with the pain in his eye. Kuro, meanwhile, had begun wiping his tears off the telescope lens with a cloth. Absorbed in that, she innocently lost sight of everything else. Tomosato's murmur was carried away by the salt wind and unraveled over the sea.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Hey, Naomasa. Look a little closer. That there? That's a man───」

Naturally, the pain in his eye left Sakuya in no condition to listen, and Kuro, being Kuro, while busying herself with wiping Sakuya's tears smeared on the telescope lens off with a cloth, had grown too engrossed in the act for any other trifling matters to warrant her attention, and so Tomosato's muttering was futilely carried away on the salty breeze, coming apart on the open sea.

source.japanese:
そうして朔屋は。
　せっかく繕[つくろ]っていた帆布を、今度は一部裁ち切って袋に縫い直す事を、水夫長の、ぎりぎりと耳を捻りながらの蛮声で命令されており、溜息つきつきざくざく適当に針を使っていた。そう厳命されて、そんな適当で良いのかと問わば、良いのだ、と答える。
　何しろ死骸を水葬にする為の袋である。そんな物に必要以上に気を遣うのは、雑巾に薔薇の刺繍を縫い上げるのと同じ酔狂だからして。
source.english:
And so Sakuya was now cutting up part of the canvas he had so carefully mended and sewing it into a bag. The boatswain had bellowed the order while twisting his ear hard. Sakuya sighed and jabbed the needle carelessly through the cloth. Given such strict orders, was that slapdash work acceptable? Yes, it was.
This was a bag for burying a corpse at sea. Taking more care than necessary would have been as eccentric as embroidering roses on a cleaning rag.

target.text: Thus, Sakuya. Had cut off a section of the sailcloth he had so painstakingly been mending, and this time, was resewing that part into a sack, just as he'd been ordered to by the Bosun's coarse voice while the man violently twisted his ear, and with sigh after sigh, he haphazardly stabbed away with his needle in crude, jagged stitches. After being given such strict orders, when he asked if it really was fine for him to do such a sloppy job, "it's fine" was the only answer given in return. For you see, this was a sack made to bury a corpse at sea. To fuss over such a thing any more than strictly necessary would be as eccentric as embroidering a rose on a cleaning rag.

source.japanese:
そう、引き揚げられた漂流者は。
　上甲板に揚げられた時既に、自ら仰向けになる気力さえ遺しておらず、水夫長の爪先でひっくり返されたその顔には。
　素人目にも明らかな死相を浮かべて、息など航海士シサムの懐中コンパスの硝子面を幽かに曇らす程度にしか通わせていない有り様で。
　なにより、猛魚にでも囓られたか、頬肉がごっそり抉[えぐ]られ骨が露出し、鼻梁も削れて顔半分ほとんどしゃれこうべ、鼻の孔からモズクガニ君が可愛らしい鋏を出して挨拶してきたとあっては。
source.english:
Yes, the castaway they had hauled aboard—
By the time he reached the upper deck, he lacked even the strength to turn onto his back. The boatswain flipped him over with the toe of a shoe, revealing a face—
A face marked by death, obvious even to an amateur. His breath barely misted the glass of Sisam's pocket compass.
Above all, perhaps some predatory fish had bitten him. A great chunk of cheek was gone, exposing bone. The bridge of his nose had been scraped away. Half his face was practically a skull, and a little mitten crab poked its charming claws from a nostril to say hello.

target.text: Indeed, the castaway who had been pulled up from the sea. By the time he had been dragged up on the deck, he no longer had even the energy to turn over and lie on his back by himself, and that face, rolled over by the toe of the Bosun's boot. Even for an amateur, it was plain to see that the shadow of death hung low over his pallid face, for he was in so grave a state that the breath he drew was only strong enough to faintly fog over the glass surface of First Mate Shisamu's pocket compass.

And more than anything, had he been gnawed on by ferocious fish or something, for the flesh had been almost entirely gouged from his cheek, leaving the bone exposed, the ridge of his nose had been worn down, almost half his face reduced to a skull, and from out his nasal cavities came Japanese mitten crabs sticking out their little pincers in an adorable greeting.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ああこれは駄目だね。もういけない。
　前にこういうのを引き揚げた事があるよ」
source.english:
“Oh, no good. He's beyond saving.
We've pulled up one like this before.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Ah, yeah, this is no good. It's too late for him. We've fished out a guy like this before.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あれは刑部島……あたりだっけ？　あの時も、すぐに死んじまったもの」
source.english: “Near Osakabejima… wasn't it? That one died straight away too.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「That was by Osakabejima…… or somewhere around there, I think? Back then, he also died right after.」 (TN: This entire part references the supernatural detective novel "悪霊島", read "Akuryoutou", known in English by its movie adaptation "The Island of Evil Spirits". It is the last full-length novel in the famous series of detective novels featuring Kindaichi Kousuke written by Yokomizo Seishi. Osakabejima is a fictional island that serves as the setting for Akuryoutou.)

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「いやいやシサム、すぐに、じゃない。
　少なくとも───
『あの島には恐ろしい悪霊が取り憑いている…腰と腰がくっついた双子…鵺の鳴く夜は気をつけろ…』
　って言い残すくらいの間はあった」
source.english:
“No, no, Sisam. Not straight away.
At least he had time to say,
‘That island is haunted by a terrible evil spirit… Twins joined at the waist…
Beware the nights when the nue cries…’”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「No no, Shisamu, he didn't die immediately. At the very least─── He had enough time left to leave us these dying words: 『That island is possessed by dreadful evil spirits…twins conjoined hip to hip…beware on nights where the Nue cries…』」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ふぅん。ま、あなた達も似たようなものでしょう。
　しょっちゅう背中ぴったりくっつけて離れないんだから」
source.english:
“Huh. You're much the same yourselves, aren't you?
Always stuck together back to back.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Hmph. Well, you two are similar enough, I suppose. 'Cause you're always glued back to back and joined at the hips.」

source.japanese: ……甲板上の騒ぎを聞きつけたか、のこのこ出てきた上に、雰囲気に無頓着な台詞を並べた密航者が、またたちまちのうちに捕らえられて簀巻きにされ、悲鳴と抵抗空しく舷側から逆さ吊りにされたという一幕は余談ながらも、場はお陰で完全に白けきって、なけなしの緊迫感も霧消し果ててかえってこなくなって、乗り組み達は散っていって三々五々。
source.english: An aside: the stowaway had apparently heard the commotion on deck and wandered out. Her remarks, utterly indifferent to the mood, earned her another swift capture. Wrapped in a mat, she was hung upside down over the side, her screams and resistance useless. The incident killed the atmosphere completely. What little tension remained evaporated, never to return, and the crew drifted away in twos and threes.

target.text: ……There was a scene where the stowaway, having apparently heard the commotion on the deck, not only shamelessly sauntered out but also spouted off some lines completely oblivious to the atmosphere only to immediately be captured once more, wrapped in a bamboo mat, then hung upside down from the side of the ship, her screaming and struggling ending in vain; while that entire scene was an aside, it was enough to completely ruin the excitement of all present; what little urgency they felt vanished like mist and never returned, and so the crew all split into smaller groups.

source.japanese: もとより信天翁号はお堅い救助船ではない。漂流者を引き揚げたのだって、船としての最低限の義務を果たしたというより、単に針路が漂流者と重なっていただけ、物のついでである。なので一通り体を改め、金目の物も見当たらずと見るや、水夫長は息を引き取り次第水葬にしてやれと、たちまち興味を失った。
source.english: The Albatross was no earnest rescue ship. Hauling in the castaway had not been the fulfillment of a vessel's most basic duty. He simply happened to lie along her course. An incidental pickup. After a cursory search of his body revealed nothing valuable, the boatswain lost interest at once. Bury him at sea as soon as he died, he ordered.

source.japanese: 朔屋とクロに看病を一応命じはしたものの、初めから助かるとは考えてもいないのがありありと。もっともいかな名医が乗り合わせていたとて、首を横に振る事間違いなしで、漂流者はそこまで生きてただけでもほとんど奇跡に近い状態だったのである。
source.english: He did nominally tell Sakuya and Kuro to nurse him, but plainly expected no recovery. In any case, even a great physician aboard would undoubtedly have shaken his head. That the castaway had lived this long was almost a miracle.

target.text: Of course, the Albatross was no square rescue ship. Even hauling up the castaway was not so much a fulfillment of a ship's most basic of duties as it was a simple coincidence of course: they just happened to cross paths and made an incidental rescue. Therefore, they briefly examined the man's body, and when it didn't seem like there was anything valuable to be found, the Bosun then said that they'd give him a burial at sea once he'd breathed his last, his interest quickly gone.

He did order Sakuya and Kuro to nurse him just in case, but it was plainly obvious that the thought of the man surviving never even crossed his mind. For even if they had some manner of distinguished physician sailing along with them, he would undoubtedly simply shake his head, for the man was in such a sorry state that it was almost a miracle he'd lived this long already.

source.japanese: そういうわけで朔屋は、聞こえよがしの溜め息を挽歌代わりに死体袋縫い合わせていたのだが、それより災難なのはクロ、直に絶命する人間相手におろおろと尽くしようもない手を尽くそうとする姿こそ哀れ。
source.english: Thus Sakuya sewed the body bag, offering conspicuously audible sighs in place of an elegy. Kuro had it worse. Her bewildered attempts to do everything she could for a man beyond help, soon to die, were pitiable.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なあクロ、可哀相だが、その人には、
　もう何かしてやろうとするだけ、
　かえって辛いよ」
source.english:
“Listen, Kuro. It's sad,
but anything more you try to do for him
will only make it harder on him.”

target.text: That was why Sakuya was stitching together a sack for the corpse, offering up heavy, pointed sighs in place of a funeral dirge, but far more misfortunate was Kuro, bewildered and shaken at dealing with a man on the verge of death, trying everything she could though there was nothing she could hope to do for him: a truly pitiful sight.
【Naomasa】 「Look, Kuro, I know it's sad, but trying to do anything for that poor guy now will only make it harder on him.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もうそっとしておいてやんな。
　静かに、逝かせてやろう……」
source.english:
“Let him be now.
Let him go quietly…”

source.japanese:
あながち朔屋を無神経とも誹られまい。
　漂流者の彼、見れば身なりは暗黒大陸の奥地にでも乗りこもうかという探検家の装いで、ただ手足は細く生白く、察するに探検隊に同行する記録者か学者とおぼゆるが、その生涯を語る物を持ち合わせていたにせよもう失われ、何処から来たのか、どういう経緯だったのかは知りようもない。
　これ以上深く関わりようもなく、ならばこれより先は無駄に延命を試みるのはかえって酷だろうと、それは水夫長ならぬ朔屋にも首肯される道理であった。
source.english:
One could not simply condemn Sakuya as insensitive.
The castaway was dressed like an explorer setting out for the interior of the Dark Continent. His limbs, however, were thin and pale. Perhaps he had been a scholar or a chronicler accompanying an expedition. If he had possessed anything that told his story, it was lost now. There was no knowing where he had come from or what had happened.
They could involve themselves no further. Trying to prolong his life pointlessly would only be cruel. Not merely the boatswain but Sakuya too could accept that reasoning.

source.japanese:
……まあ朔屋にしてみれば本音は、惨たらしく破壊された顔相に向かい合っているだけでも気味悪く、お前もまた海にいる間にこういう死に目を迎える可能性だってなきにしもあらずだ、と囁かれているようで、逝くならさっさと逝ってくれと口には出さずとも考えていたのではあるが。
　落ちつかなげに手を上げたり下げたりしているクロに一瞥をくれてから、死体袋を仕上げようとした時、漂流者の喉から泥を跳ねかすような音の鳴って、いよいよお陀仏かと身を強張らせた耳に、
source.english:
Though Sakuya's real feeling was that merely facing those hideously ruined features gave him the creeps. They seemed to whisper that he too might meet such an end while at sea. If you're going to die, get it over with, he thought, though he did not say it.
He glanced at Kuro, whose hands rose and fell restlessly, and was about to finish the bag when a sound like splashing mud came from the castaway's throat. He stiffened, thinking this must be the end, and heard—

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Just leave him alone already. Let him pass away, peacefully……」

One could not entirely dismiss this as Sakuya being insensitive. The castaway was, as far as he could tell, clad in an outfit worn by explorers embarking on expeditions into the depths of the Dark Continent, but his limbs were slender and pallid, so one could infer that he was likely a chronicler or scholar of the sort that would accompany said explorers, but even if he were possessed of anything that could tell the tale of such a life, it had already been lost, and thus, there was no way of knowing where he came from or by what means he ended up here.

As no deeper involvement with the man was possible, any further effort to prolong his life would, on the contrary, only be a misguided cruelty, a line of reasoning that not just the Bosun but even Sakuya also found himself nodding in agreement with.

……Well, when it came to Sakuya's true feelings on the matter, he simply felt uncomfortable just looking at the horrifically brutalized facial features; they seemed to whisper to him, "For as long as you are out at sea, there will always be the possibility that you will meet a similar end", and though he never said it out loud, he was thinking to himself: "If you're going to die, can you just get it over with?"

After sending a glance in Kuro's direction, who was restlessly raising and lowering her hands, he was just about to finish with the body bag when he heard a sound like splashing mud coming from the castaway's throat, and as he tensed his body, wondering if this was when the castaway was finally going to kick the bucket, it reached his ears,

source.japanese: 末期の息というには、余分な音が多く、肺が押し出した無意味な声か、それとも言葉の切れ端かとつい膝を進めたところ、
source.english: Too many extra sounds for a final breath. Was it a meaningless noise forced out by the lungs, or fragments of words? He found himself moving closer on his knees.

source.japanese:
【漂流者】
「終わらない嵐が───」
source.english: “A storm that never ends—”

source.japanese:
【漂流者】
「既に滅びた生き物たちの、残された───」
source.english: “What was left of creatures already extinct—”

source.japanese:
【漂流者】
「僕はそこで、みつけた……」
source.english: “There… I found…”

source.japanese:
これだけの言葉を、無論流暢に繋げたはずもなく、辛うじて見開いた瞼[まぶた]の裡の眸[ひとみ]はもう死人の濁り、なのに余程心残りだったのか、絶命しかけては踏みとどまって、なおも何事か遺そうとして、ごとりと。
　遂に半壊した顔を横ざまに、それきり。
　今度こそ本当に動かなくなった。
source.english:
Naturally, he had not strung even those few words together fluently. His eyes, barely visible beneath the lids he forced apart, already had a dead man's cloudiness. Yet something must have remained desperately important to him. Again and again he halted on the edge of death, still trying to leave something behind—then his head dropped.
The half-ruined face fell to one side. That was all.
This time, he truly moved no more.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「聞いた、クロ？」
source.english: “Did you hear that, Kuro?”

target.text: 【Castaway】 「……. ……hgh. ……」

For a rasping final breath, there really was an excess of noise; perhaps it was some nonsensical sounds pushed out from his lungs, but as the thought struck him that it could be fragments of words, and he couldn't help but crawl closer on his knees,
【Castaway】 「The Ceaseless Storm is───」
【Castaway】 「The remnants left…… of creatures long extinct───」
【Castaway】 「It was there……I found……」

Even these few words were, of course, not strung together fluently, and the eyes behind the eyelids he had wrenched open with great difficulty were already leaden with the haze of death, but he must have felt a great regret, for even as the final breath of life escaped him, he held out, still desperate to leave some dying message or other behind, and then, a thump. His already half-destroyed face fell sideways, and that was the end. Now, he truly had stopped moving.
【Naomasa】 「You hear that, Kuro?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「う、うん……でもクロには、
　ぜんぜんわかんない……」
source.english:
“Y-yes…
But Kuro doesn't understand any of it…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺にだってわかんないわな。
　死に際の譫言だろうな」
source.english:
“Neither do I.
A dying man's delirium, I suppose.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でも……嵐……。
　おわんないって」
source.english:
“But… a storm…
He said it doesn't end.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だから譫言だよ譫言。
　さ、詰めちまおうやこの人、袋に。
　ああ、重しがいるな。
　なんか見繕ってこないと……」
source.english:
“I said delirium. Delirium.
Come on, let's get him in the bag.
Oh, we need a weight.
I'll have to find something…”

source.japanese: 朔屋はやはり気味悪そうにしていても、死体を間においてこんなやりとりを交わせるくらいには擦れてきていたのだろう。死体袋に詰める重しを求めて立ち上がったが、クロは嵐という言葉に反応して、なおも未練げに、漂流者の剥き出しの歯列の口元に屈みこんで耳寄せたところ、ぴちゃりと。
source.english: Unsettled though he remained, Sakuya had apparently become hardened enough to hold a conversation like this across a corpse. He stood to find a weight for the body bag. Kuro, still caught by the word ‘storm,’ lingered, bending close until her ear almost touched the castaway's mouth—the lips gone, the teeth naked. Then came a little wet flick.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Y-, yeah……but Kuro doesn't get it at all……」
【Naomasa】 「Not like I did either. Probably just the delirium of a man in his death throes.」
【Kuro】 「But he said……a storm……. That doesn't stop.」
【Naomasa】 「He was delirious, I'm telling you, it was just nonsense. Alright, let's stuff this guy in the sack. Right, gonna need something to weigh this down with. Gotta find something fitting……」

Sakuya might still have been repulsed, but given that he was able carry on a conversation like this right over a corpse, he must have grown somewhat desensitized by now. He rose to his feet to go search for a weight that could be packed into the sack, but Kuro had reacted to the word "storm", and as if still having some lingering attachment to it, she bent down and brought her ear close to the bared rows of teeth in the castaway's mouth, and just then came a wet smack.

source.japanese:
死骸の口腔から跳ねた、小さな、でもよく肥えた、蝦だった。跳ねて、蝦にとってもそしてクロにとっても好ましからざる所へ飛びこんだ。
　すなわち、聴き取ろうと集中したあまりに半開きにしていたクロの口の中へ。
source.english:
A shrimp sprang from the dead man's mouth. Small, but well-fed. It leaped somewhere neither it nor Kuro would have wished it to go.
Into Kuro's mouth, left half-open as she concentrated on listening.

target.text: It leapt out from the oral cavity of the corpse: a small, but very plump leech. It leapt, but it plunged into a place that was a far cry from preferable for either the leech or Kuro. That is to say, it jumped right into her mouth, left half-open in intense concentration as she tried to pick up anything resembling a word.

source.japanese:
反射的に閉じてしまったのが、またいけなかった。
　かしゃりと、くぐもっていても朔屋にも聞こえたくらいな、砕ける音。それまで漂流者の肉をたらふく食ってぬくぬくと、死肉で太った蝦[えび]を、噛んでしまった音。
　……棒でも背筋に通されたように即座にぴょこんと突っ立って、ぶるるるると輪郭ぶれんばかりの勢いで震え出したは、日頃のクロには滅多にない躍動的な見物であった、とはいえ。
source.english:
She reflexively closed it. Another mistake.
A muffled crunch, loud enough for Sakuya to hear. She had bitten the shrimp, plump and content from feasting on the castaway's flesh. Fattened on carrion.
She popped upright at once, as though a rod had been driven through her spine, and began shuddering so violently that her outline almost blurred. A display of animation seldom seen in the everyday Kuro. Still—

target.text: She snapped it shut reflexively, but that was yet another mistake. There was a click, and muffled as it might have been, it was still loud enough for Sakuya to hear the sound of something being crushed. It was the sound of this leech, which had cozily eaten its fill of the castaway's corpse until now, growing fat on carrion, being bitten into. ……As though a rod had been driven down her spine, she immediately leapt to her feet, then began shaking with such vigour that her very contour grew blurry; it was an usually lively spectacle considering Kuro's habitual behaviour, but with that said.

source.japanese:
白子の喉が物凄い蠕動音を立て、胃から何事か迫り上がってくるのが外から見ても判るとあっては、見物と看過するわけにはいかなかった。跳び退るより、慌ててクロの口を塞ぐ事を選んだのは、もしクロが決壊させてしまえば、位置的に死骸が吐瀉物まみれとなり、ただでさえ薄気味悪い物に余計な飾りをつけたくなかっただけの事、袋に詰めるのがいよいよ厭[いや]になる。
　こみあげる内圧に頬、蛙のように膨らませ、目をきろきろ回すクロに怒鳴りつけ、目で船縁を指し示した。
source.english:
Her throat churned horribly; Sakuya could see something surging up from her stomach. This was no longer a spectacle he could merely watch. Rather than leap clear, he clapped a hand over Kuro's mouth—not out of concern for her, but because in their present positions an eruption would cover the corpse in vomit. The thing was hideous enough already; he wanted no extra decoration, and the thought of bagging it afterward was worse still.
Her cheeks bulged like a frog's under the pressure and her eyes rolled wildly. Sakuya shouted at her and jerked his gaze toward the rail.

target.text: A ghastly noise of vermiculation rose from the albino's throat; he could tell that something was pressing upwards from her stomach even from the outside, and he couldn't afford to simply treat this as a spectacle to watch. The reason why he chose to block Kuro's mouth in a panic rather than jumping backwards in retreat was because, if Kuro's floodgates were to open, then the corpse would be covered in vomit by virtue of its position; he simply did not wish to add any unnecessary decorations to something that was already unsettling enough as it was, and then he would really come to dread having to stuff it in the sack later.
Her cheeks inflated like frog's from the surging internal pressure, and as Kuro's eyes started looking around restlessly, he shouted at her, pointing to the gunwale with his eyes.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こらえろほんの少しだけ！
　あっちだ、いいな？
　さん・にぃ・いち……行けッ」
source.english:
“Hold it! Just a little longer!
Over there,
got it? Three, two, one… Go!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Hold it in, just a little while! Over there, got it? Three, two, one……GO!」

source.japanese:
見交わす眼と目で拍子を取って、塞いだ手も外され、背中をどやしつけられ、舷側へと走るクロはその時だけ嵐の彼女が舞い降りたように早く、多少尾籠な固形物混じりの雫を後ろに巻いたけれど許容範囲に収まって、舷側に取り付いて鼻で大きく吸ってからのびのびと───あの小さな体からよくも、と呆れるくらいの濁音が弾けた。たまさか先ほど密航者が吊されたままの所であり、嘔吐に混じって彼女の盛大な悲鳴も響いた。
　末期的な情況に吊られ、朔屋もえずきを催した。
source.english:
Taking their timing from each other's eyes, Sakuya whipped his hand away and thumped her on the back. Kuro flew toward the rail with the speed of her storm-self descending into her for that one moment. A few droplets mingled with indelicate solids sprayed behind her, but remained within acceptable limits. She seized the rail, drew a great breath through her nose, and let it all out—an astonishingly guttural eruption from so small a body. As chance would have it, the stowaway was still hanging directly below, and her magnificent scream joined Kuro's retching.
The whole appalling spectacle set Sakuya gagging too.

target.text: Keeping time with the meeting of their eyes, he removed the hand blocking her mouth, then gave her a good slap on the back, and Kuro raced towards the ship's side, possessed of the same speed as the girl who would only swoop down upon the ship during a storm, and though a few disgusting droplets containing solid matter trailed behind her, it was still within the permissible range; she clung to the bulwark, and after heaving a deep breath through her nose, with a liberating feeling───a burst of guttural noises exploded from her, gravelly enough to leave him stunned that such a tiny frame could even produce them.

By sheer coincidence, it was also right above the place where the stowaway had been suspended upside down from just a little while earlier, and mixed in with the sound of vomiting, her vigorous screams carried far and wide. Dragged along by the terminal state of affairs, Sakuya felt a sympathetic heave crawl up his own throat.

source.japanese:
……彼だけではなかった。恐るべき事に死者さえも耐えられなかったようだ。
　それまで完全に死んでいたはずの漂流者の喉が、もう一度、最後に今一度音高くなって、吐き出したのである。
　実際には死後の内臓の収縮とかその類の蠕動だったのだろうが、朔屋にとってはなんにせよたまったものではなく、抜かしかけた腰を、踏み留まらせた物がある。
source.english:
He was not alone. Horrifyingly, even the dead seemed unable to bear it.
The castaway, who ought to have been well and truly dead, gave one last loud rattle in his throat—and threw up.
It was probably a postmortem contraction of the organs, or something of that sort. Whatever the cause, Sakuya could not bear it. His knees almost gave way, but something stopped him.

target.text: ……And it was not just him, for in a dreadful turn of events, even the deceased seemed unable to endure it. The throat of the castaway, who by all rights had been stone-dead until then, once again, one last time, made a loud noise and vomited something up. In reality, it was probably just vermiculations stemming from his internal organs contracting and shrivelling up after death or something of the kind, but regardless of what the cause was, it remained an unbearable situation to Sakuya, and yet, there was something that made his knees on the verge of buckling stand their ground.

source.japanese:
胃の内容物などほとんど残っておらず、死者が吐き出したものは海水とそして、革袋。
　裡側に何かを蔵した、革袋。死人が吐いた物など到底手をつける気になれない筈を朔屋をして拾い上げさせたのは、鈍感な彼にしても予感が働いたに違いない。
source.english:
There was scarcely anything left in the stomach. What the dead man expelled was seawater—and a leather pouch.
A leather pouch with something inside. Nothing vomited by a corpse should have tempted Sakuya to touch it. Yet he picked it up. Some premonition must have stirred even in that dull fellow.

target.text: With almost nothing left inside its stomach, the corpse vomited up sea water, as well as a small leather bag. A leather bag, and one containing something within it at that. The reason Sakuya picked it up, even though he certainly had not the ghost of any inclination to touch something vomited up by a corpse, was undoubtedly because his intuition, dull though it may be, was hard at work.

source.japanese:
もどかしく、袋の口緩めて振り出してみれば、この日は高曇りという、空の高所に薄く濁った蓋されて陽差しがどこかか弱い、浮かない空もやいであったにもかかわらず。
　掌で燃えていた。
　弱い陽差しを存分に取りこんで、内部で増殖させまるで自らが一つの恒星であるかのように、輝いて、燃えて、さんざめいて目を射る。鶉卵大の。宝玉。否、大地の精髄と表すべきか。
source.english:
Impatiently, he loosened the pouch's mouth and shook out its contents. The day was high overcast, a thin, murky lid drawn across the heavens. The sunlight was feeble; the sky, dispiriting. Yet—
It burned in his palm.
Taking in every bit of the weak sunlight and multiplying it within, it shone as though it were itself a star. Shone, burned, glittered, pierced his eyes. A jewel the size of a quail's egg. No, the very essence of the earth.

source.japanese:
漂流者が見出した物は、これだったのだろう。
　女たちが身を飾る、真珠やダイヤが人工なのか硝子製なのか、ろくろく見分けのつかぬ朔屋ではあるが、この太古の光輝を固形にしたような宝玉を、人類が造り出す事など到底及びうるまいと思われた。
　吐く息は吸いこまれ、吸う息も密度が薄くなるような息苦しいほどの凝視の間に周囲の事物は意味を喪い、クロのえずきも密航者の絶叫も排斥されて、世界は結晶化されたこの輝きのみ。
　純粋で硬質な時間はしかし、ぬう、と現れた手によって奪い去られた。無骨で、爪の先で板に根元まで撃ちこまれた五寸釘さえ掘り出しそうな指先が、朔屋の手からひょいと宝玉を摘[つま]みあげ、その不躾なる事神聖冒涜に匹敵しよう。
source.english:
This was surely what the castaway had found.
Sakuya could scarcely tell a genuine pearl or diamond from an imitation, or even from glass. But he felt that humanity could never have made this gem, like the brilliance of primeval ages given solid form.
As he stared, breathless, each exhalation seemed drawn into it and the air he inhaled lost substance. Everything around him was stripped of meaning. Kuro's retching and the stowaway's screams were shut out. The world was nothing but this crystallized radiance.
Then a hand stole that pure, hard moment away. Coarse fingers—whose nails looked capable of prying from a board a six-inch spike driven all the way to its head—plucked the gem from Sakuya's palm. The sheer rudeness bordered on sacrilege.

source.japanese: が、糾弾は敵わなかった。取りあげたのは、朔屋が夢中になっているうちに、傍らに現れた水夫長で、哀しいかな朔屋の身には、既にこの老水夫への絶対服従が刻みこまれている。
source.english: But he could not protest. The boatswain had appeared beside him while he was lost in contemplation. Sadly, absolute obedience to this old sailor was already engraved in Sakuya's being.

target.text: When he impatiently loosened the opening of the bag and then shook the contents out, though this was a day of high, thin clouds, as though a hazy lid had been placed over the heavens, leaving the sunlight faint and the sky smeared a brooding grey, despite all that. It burned atop the palm of his hand. It fully absorbed the weak sunlight, amplifying it internally until it glowed like a sun, brilliant, burning, dazzling as it pierced his eyes with its radiance. The size of a quail egg. A jewel. Nay, perhaps it was better expressed as the very pith of the land itself.

The thing the castaway had discovered was surely this. Though Sakuya could barely tell the difference between the numerous stones women would adorn themselves with, were they pearl, diamond, or simply wrought from glass, one would think it forever beyond the reach of mankind to craft such a gem, a jewel that seemed as though primordial splendour itself had been frozen into solid form.

He was lost in a fixation so suffocating that his exhaled breath was drawn back in, the very air he inhaled seemed to thin, and the world around him began to lose all meaning; Kuro's vomiting and the stowaway's screams of terror were expunged, the entire world crystallized into this radiance alone. Though the purity of it seemed to solidify the flow of time, it was stolen from him by a hand that suddenly slid into view. Those rough fingertips, which looked as though they could with their nails alone pry out even a spike fifteen centimetres of length driven into a board, suddenly plucked the jewel out of Sakuya's hands, an insolent action that was tantamount to sacrilege.

However, to denounce this would be impossible. For the one who had confiscated it was none other than the Bosun, who had arrived by Sakuya's side while he stood in a daze, and lamentable though it may be, absolute obedience to this old mariner had already been carved deeply into Sakuya's being by now.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まさかこいつぁ……」
source.english: “Could this be…?”

source.japanese: 人差し指と親指の間に摘[つま]みあげ、片目、刺青に覆われた方に近づけて覗きこむ、宝玉の光に照らされその龍の刺青が、一時真の生を得たかに揺らめき、ある意味では龍に宝玉というのは相応しいとも言えたろう。
source.english: Pinching it between thumb and forefinger, he brought it close to the eye on the tattooed side of his face. Lit by the jewel, the dragon tattoo flickered as though it had briefly acquired true life. In a sense, a dragon and a precious jewel were well matched.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「朔屋、てめえの見つけたなぁ、
　事によっちゃとんでもねえぞ……」
source.english:
“Sakuya,
what you've found—this could be something incredible…”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「こりゃあ、『ザウエル』じゃねえのか」
source.english: “Isn't this a ‘Zauer’?”

source.japanese: 水夫長にしても放心の態で呟いたその名、朔屋には当然聞き覚えなど無かったけれど、その態[ざま]と差し合いに、エキゾティックな音韻で響いたのだった。
source.english: Even the boatswain seemed dazed as he murmured the name. Sakuya, naturally, had never heard it; but set against the old man's stunned expression, its exotic syllables rang with strange significance.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Could this possibly be……」

Holding it between his index finger and thumb, he brought it close to one eye, the side covered by his tattoo, and peered into it; lit up by the light of the jewel, the dragon tattoo writhed as if it truly had been granted life for but a fleeting moment, and it could well be said that, in a certain sense, jewels and dragons go well together.
【Bosun】 「So this is your find, Sakuya, hmm? Depending on how it shakes out, this could be incredible……」
【Bosun】 「This thing's a『Sauer』, isn't it?」

That name, muttered in a manner uncharacteristically absentminded for the Bosun, was, of course, not one that Sakuya had any recollection of hearing before, but combined with its appearance, the name resonated with an exotic timbre.

source.japanese:
───洋上をあてどなく漂う、一隻の船がある。
　機関を養う腕もなく、舵輪を回す手とてなく、死の翳[かげ]り洋上に漂わせ、晴天にあってなお暗冥の気をまとう船だ。
　この漂流船を見出して乗りこんだ者は、船内を見舞った災禍と暴力の後をまざまざと見るだろう。上甲板、船上構造物、船内、船倉と至るところに散乱する人骨に、目を背[そむ]けたくなるだろう。
　人骨は乾ききって長い事たつというのに、船内の空気には血臭がいまだ濃く澱[よど]んでいるかのよう。
source.english:
A ship drifts aimlessly at sea.
No arms to tend her engine, no hands to turn her wheel. She casts the shadow of death upon the water and wears an air of darkness even beneath a clear sky.
Anyone who discovers this drifting vessel and boards her will see, all too clearly, the traces of disaster and violence within. Human bones scattered everywhere—upper deck, superstructure, interior, holds—will make them want to turn away.
The bones have long been dry, yet the ship's air seems still thick with a lingering smell of blood.

target.text: ───Aimlessly drifting across the ocean was a single ship. With no hands to feed the engine, no hands to turn the wheel, casting a shade of death over the sea, there was a ship, which, even beneath a clear sky, was still clad in the darkness of the underworld.

Any who found this adrift ship and boarded it would surely bear witness to the aftermath of the violence and calamity that had befallen it. They would surely wish to avert their eyes from the human bones scattered everywhere───from the upper deck, the structures upon it, the interior, and all the way down to the hold. Though the human bones were left desiccated by the passage of time, it was as though the very air of the ship itself was still heavy and stagnant with the metallic smell of blood.

source.japanese:
そう、かつて『それ』は起こったのだ。
　そう、かつては『信天翁号』と呼ばれていたこの船で。
　その時の情景を、頁を捲[めく]り返すように巻き戻せば───船内の通路を踝[くるぶし]まで浸したのは潮で、潮は潮でも人の生命の雫であるそれ、血潮の。
　酸鼻にして凄惨、凄惨にして阿鼻叫喚の渦は、先ほどで最高潮に達して後は引いていくばかり。しかしそれは船内を見舞った暴力の嵐が鎮静化した事を示さず、なんの、ただ悲鳴と怒号を迸[ほとばし]らせる喉、喉、喉が息絶えていっただけ。
source.english:
Yes, it happened once.
Here, on the vessel once called the Albatross.
Turn back to that scene as one turns back the pages: a tide floods the passages ankle-deep. A tide, but of the drops of human life. Blood.
The hideous, ghastly vortex of shrieks and agony has just reached its height and begun to ebb. Not that the storm of violence aboard has calmed. Far from it. Only the throats pouring out screams and roars—throat after throat after throat—have fallen silent in death.

source.japanese: 通路には累々と、あちらの隅に転がった死体は頭を叩き割られ、こちらに倒れ伏した死骸は切り裂かれた腹腔からぶわぶわと腸を零し、命絶えた体はそらそこらここらどこにでも、絞め殺され眼球飛びだした顔があり、毒盛られて黒ずんだ舌を吐いたも有り、生命を奪う手段の見本市と化し、信天翁号はかくして完全な死の船と成り果て、海上に人の浅ましさと欲望の象徴として漂う事になった。
source.english: Bodies lie heaped along the passage. In that corner, a corpse with its skull smashed open. Here, one lies fallen, entrails bulging from a slit abdomen. Dead bodies there, here, everywhere. A strangled face with bulging eyes; a poisoned mouth with a blackened tongue protruding. A trade fair of ways to take a life. Thus the Albatross became a ship of death in every sense, drifting at sea as an emblem of human greed and baseness.

target.text: Indeed, long ago,『that』occured. Indeed, on this ship once known as 『The Albatross』 If we return to the scene of back then, rewinding time as though turning over the pages in a book───the tide had flooded the passageways to the ankle, but it was one formed of drops of human lifeforce, a tide of blood.

Appalling and gruesome, gruesome indeed, a maelstrom of the agonizing cries of pandemonium, one which had already reached its climax just earlier, and now, all it could do was recede. But that was not a sign that the storm of violence that had befallen this ship was calming, far from it, it was simply that those throats whence the screams and angry roars had gushed forth, those throats, those throats had all breathed their last.

They lay in heaps around the passageway; the corpse lying in that corner over there had its head split wide open, and over here, a corpse was collapsed face down, spilling spongy viscera from an abdominal cavity ripped apart, bodies bereft of life scattered here and there and everywhere, those strangled to death with eyeballs bulging out of their sockets, those fed poison vomiting out their blackened tongues; it had become a trade fair of ways to kill, and thus, the Albatross had been reduced to a ship of total death, drifting on the seas as a representation of the depravity and greed of humanity.

source.japanese:
一体何が、乗組員達をかくも凄惨に狂わせた？
　答えを得たくば、勇を鼓して足を進めてみよ。
　骸骨と成り果てても、暴虐の証をまざまざ遺す死の影の中を進んでみよ。
　やがて火も落ち果て、炭くべる手とてなく冷えきった釜の前で、ある骨を見出す事になるだろう。
source.english:
What drove the crew to such a ghastly madness?
If you would know, summon your courage and go forward.
Pass through death's shadows, where even the skeletons bear vivid evidence of violence.
At last, before a furnace gone cold, its fire extinguished for want of hands to feed it coal, you will find one skeleton.

source.japanese: それは、元は青年だったと思しき船員服の骸骨かも知れず。
source.english: Perhaps a skeleton in a sailor's uniform, once a young man.

source.japanese: それは、元は有閑の女だったと思しき、紫紺のドレスを張りつかせた遺骨かも知れず───
source.english: Perhaps remains with a deep violet dress clinging to them, once a woman of leisure—

source.japanese: また頁を捲[めく]り返すように時を巻き戻せば───
source.english: Turn back the pages of time once more—

source.japanese: それは、今この場面、この時に起こった。
source.english: It happened here, in this scene, at this very moment.

target.text: Whatever could have possibly driven the crew into so ghastly a frenzy? Should you wish to know the answer, you must first muster up your courage and take a step forwards. You must advance onwards, into the shadows of death that yet vividly attest to the atrocities committed, reduced to skeletons though they may be. And there, before the cauldron whose flames ultimately died out with no hands to feed it coal, now cold to the touch, you shall surely find a certain bone.
And there, perhaps you will find a skeleton clad in a sailor's uniform that seemingly used to be a young man.
And there, perhaps you will find the remains of what seemingly used to be a leisured woman, curves still clung to by a dress of indigo───
And if we once more wind back time, as though turning over the pages of a book───
It happened now, here in this place, at this very moment.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「さて───もうこのお船で生きているのは、
　わたくしと貴方だけのご様子。
　一体どうなさるおつもり？
　決めるのは貴方。直さんよ」
source.english:
“Well then—it seems the only ones still alive
aboard this ship are you and me.
What exactly do you intend to do?
The choice is yours, Nao.”

source.japanese:
信天翁号の女客、彩久津泪は、ドレスを裡側から張り詰めさせる、豊麗な乳房の狭間に光の精髄を押し当てて、朔屋へと胸を逸らして昂然と。光は、掌の裡[うち]に握りこまれ、指の隙間から幽かに漏れ出して、青年の欲望を煽り立てる、兇悪に、黒々と炎を呼ぶ。
　奪ってしまえ───黒い炎は、燃え盛り、かつ獣の如く凝集して青年の腸を焦がすのだ。
　奪ってしまえという。宝玉を。
　いっそ邪魔立てする女も、一緒に奪ってしまえ。
source.english:
Rui Irokuzu, the Albatross's female passenger, pressed that essence of light into the cleft of the magnificent breasts stretching her dress taut from within, and thrust her chest proudly toward Sakuya. Clenched in her palm, the light leaked faintly between her fingers and fanned the young man's desire into a vicious, pitch-black flame.
Take it—the black fire blazed and gathered like a beast, scorching his entrails.
Take it, the fire said. The jewel.
And while you are about it, take the woman obstructing you as well.

source.japanese:
ほら、その生意気な首なんて、ちょっと力を入れれば容易く折れそうな。そのみしりと膨らんだ乳房など、爪を立てればあっけなく裂けそうで。乳房も、尻も、裂いてしまえよかし。たばしる血潮で宝玉を洗えば輝きは増すだろう、なんだったら殺人後の渇きを潤す為に呑み干したっていい。
　獣性のままに殺した女の血潮は、甘いに違いない。
　渇望に身を灼いて殺したおんなの肉は、ぷち、ぷちと歯の間で甘美に弾けるだろう。
source.english:
Look at that insolent neck: the least little pressure would snap it. And those breasts, swollen fit to creak—a fingernail would split them as easily as anything. Rip them open. Her ass too. Wash the jewel in the blood that spurts from her and it will shine the brighter; for that matter, drink it down and slake the thirst that comes after murder.

source.japanese:

Gouge me, tear me apart, devour me?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やめて下さいよ泪姐さん。
　有りもしない波風、わざわざ立てなくたっていいよ。ほら、おふざけは程ほどにして、早くその石を返してくれ。……水夫長にまた殴られる」
source.english:
“Please stop, Rui.
You don’t have to go out of your way to stir up trouble where there isn’t any. Come on, enough fooling around—give me that stone back already. …Boatswain’s gonna beat me up again.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Rui-neesan, please, stop that. You don't have to go out of your way to stir up some imaginary strife. Look, keep the jokes in moderation, and just hurry up and give me back that stone. ……The Bosun is gonna hit me again.」

source.japanese: 乗ってこないと見てとるや、泪は退屈そうな鼻息を一つ、開掌した指捌[さば]きも滑らかな、その仕草だけである種のイソギンチャクじみた淫靡を匂わせ、隣の機関長へあっさり宝玉を手渡して、なんら執着も未練も見せず。
source.english: Seeing he wouldn’t take the bait, she gave a bored snort and smoothly unfurled her fingers. The gesture alone exuded a certain sensuality, like a sea anemone. She readily handed the gem to the chief engineer beside her, showing no attachment or reluctance whatsoever.

source.japanese: ───と、いうわけで。
source.english: —And there you have it.

source.japanese:
泪はそれは楽しげに、宝玉が原因で船内に血みどろの争奪戦が発生し、最後の一人となるまで殺し合う様などを、言霊の力豊かに、眼に浮かぶように語ってみせたものだけれど。
　信天翁号は相変わらず欲と人の業を満載して、今日も沈没寸前ながらも図太く海上にその醜い姿を晒しているのであった。
source.english:
With evident delight, Rui had described a bloody struggle over the jewel, everyone killing everyone else until only one remained. Such was the power of her words that the scene seemed to stand before their eyes.
The Albatross, meanwhile, remained laden with desire and human sin. As close to sinking as ever, she still brazenly flaunted her ugliness on the open sea.

source.japanese:
あれだけ生々しく宝玉を原因にした、船内の血みどろの奪い合いを語りながらも、この女自体はさして惹かれた様子を見せていないのが、得体の知れぬ恐ろしさを感じさせる。
　朔屋についてきたクロなどは、泪の忍び声の、予言めいた争奪戦の情景を耳にしただけで震え上がり、膀胱が大変な危機なのか、内腿をもぞもぞ摺[す]り合わせている始末で、適当に切り上げて引き揚げないと失禁の後始末などを押しつけられかねない。
source.english:
For all the vividness of her tale of bloody competition over the jewel, the woman herself seemed scarcely drawn to it. That gave her an unfathomable, frightening quality.
Kuro, who had followed Sakuya here, shuddered merely at hearing Rui's low voice describe the struggle like a prophecy. Her bladder seemed to be in dire peril; she rubbed her inner thighs together restlessly. If they did not cut the visit short, Sakuya might find himself saddled with cleaning up an accident.

source.japanese: 水夫長は、宝玉を『ザウエル』と呼んだものの確信が持てない様子で、朔屋とクロを機関室に遣わしたのである。曰く、機関長はこういった宝石には詳しい、と。なんでも機関長は元は富裕な華僑の出である故らしいが、朔屋はこういった地獄の船に集まる面子の出自など、どれも怪しいものだと話半分に聞いていた。大体この機関長も、なるほど衣装や身のこなしからどこか典雅な風が漂わせているけれど、それだって時と場合によりにけり、こんな、半日も立ち働いただけで隅々の毛穴、鼻腔の奥まで煤まみれになりそうな機関室にあって、フロッグコートには毛羽の一つ無く、ワイシャツは常時真っ新な、目が痛くなるくらいの白であるというのは納得しかねる。拡大鏡用いて宝玉を鑑定する今も、黒眼鏡は着けたままというのも見た目にどうしたって怪しい。
source.english: The boatswain had called the jewel a ‘Zauer,’ but seemed uncertain. He had sent Sakuya and Kuro to the engine room, saying the chief engineer knew about gems of this sort. Apparently the man came from a wealthy overseas Chinese family. Sakuya took such accounts with a grain of salt; everyone gathered aboard this hellish ship had a dubious background. True, the engineer's clothes and bearing possessed a certain refinement, but place and circumstance mattered. In an engine room where half a day's work should have filled every pore and the depths of one's nostrils with soot, the absence of a single stray fiber on his frock coat—and the perpetual, eye-hurting white of his shirt—were difficult to accept. Even now, appraising the jewel through a loupe, he kept his dark glasses on. The sight was unmistakably suspicious.

source.japanese: 水夫長の命がなければ、持ちこむ事すら思いもしなかったであろう朔屋は、それでもただ彼が速やかに鑑定を終えるのを見守るしかなかったという。
source.english: Without the boatswain's orders, Sakuya would never have thought to bring it here. Now he could only watch and hope the appraisal was soon done.

target.text: Realizing he would not play along, Rui let a single bored breath escape her nose; even the way she moved her fingers as she spread her palms was smooth, that gesture alone suggestive of the obscenity of a particular type of sea anemone, and she nonchalantly handed the jewel back to the Chief Engineer standing next to her, showing not a hint of neither lingering attachment nor reluctance.
───So, to summarize.

Rui had cheerfully amused herself with the idea that this jewel was the reason behind the outbreak of a gory struggle within the ship, one where they had killed each other until only one man remained standing at the very end, and she spoke with such power and eloquence that he could see it being brought to life before his eyes, however. The Albatross was, as ever, loaded to capacity with greed and human sin, and while she was on the verge of sinking yet again today, she still continued to shamelessly expose her unsightly form on the surface of the sea.

Though she had spoken in such lurid detail of the gory struggle for the jewel unfolding on this ship, the woman herself did not show any particular attraction to it, but that itself only gave off a sense of unknowable dread. And Kuro, who had accompanied Sakuya here, had begun to shiver just from hearing Rui's whispering voice describing the scenes of a future yet to come in prophetic tones, and her bladder must have been going through a severe crisis, for she had ended up rubbing her thighs together as she fidgeted, and had he not cut the whole thing short at a suitable time, it was not hard to imagine that he'd be the one forced to deal with the aftermath of her incontinence.

The Bosun had called the jewel a 『Sauer』, but he didn't seem too confident about it, and so he had dispatched Sakuya and Kuro to the engine room. Apparently, the Chief Engineer was knowledgeable about these kinds of jewels, at least according to the Bosun. As far as he had heard, the reason for this was that the Chief Engineer originated from an affluent Chinese family living overseas, but since the ancestry of any of the people gathered aboard this hellish ship was bound to be questionable, Sakuya took the whole thing with a grain of salt.

Admittedly, his attire and carriage exuded a certain refined elegance, but surely that should be considered subject to time and place; in this engine room, where a mere half day's worth of hard labour would leave the pores on every nook and cranny of your skin, all the way to the depths of your nostrils, clogged with soot, it defied reason that there was not a single stray fiber on his frock coat, and that his shirt stayed a white so blindingly pristine it actually stung the eyes. Even now, what with the way he still wore sunglasses while he appraised the jewel with a loupe, everything about the way he looked was somehow very suspicious.

Had the Bosun not ordered him to, Sakuya probably would never have even considered bringing the jewel to him, but regardless, all Sakuya could do was watch as he swiftly brought the appraisal to an end.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……なるほど。
　このカラットの石で、罅割れや内包物の一つもないのは、それだけで驚嘆すべきではあるでしょう。それで女史、貴女はどう見立てます？」
source.english:
“…I see.
For a stone of this carat weight to have neither a crack nor a single inclusion is remarkable in itself. And you, madam? Your assessment?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……I see. That a stone of this carat would not have a single crack or inclusion is in itself something shocking enough it ought to demand admiration. So, milady, what is your assessment?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どう、もなにも。
　貴方が思っているとおりではなくって？」
source.english:
“What is there to assess?
Isn't it precisely what you think it is?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「What of it? It is exactly as you imagine, is it not?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「まあ、ね。
　朔屋君。水夫長の勘働きは、正しかったようですよ。彼はあれであれで鋭い目をお持ちだ」
source.english:
“Well, yes.
Mr. Sakuya, it appears the bosun's instinct was correct. Whatever else one may say of him, he has a keen eye.”

source.japanese:
