いささか微妙なニュアンスの籠もった賛辞に、朔屋は機関と水夫のそれぞれの長の間にわだかまる、微妙な確執を感じ取ったが敢えてそれには関知せず、機関長が押し返してきた宝玉『ザウエル』を、より丁寧に布切れの中に包みこんで、クロに預けた。
　こいつもか、と朔屋は内心でほろ苦い感慨を噛み締めながら、泪と同じくさしたる執着も匂わせることなく返して寄越した機関長を、横目で伺う。
source.english:
The praise had a certain equivocal ring. Sakuya caught the hint of bad blood between chief engineer and boatswain, but deliberately kept out of it. He wrapped the Zauer the engineer pushed back to him still more carefully in a scrap of cloth and entrusted it to Kuro.
Another one, he thought, chewing on the faintly bitter realization as he glanced sideways at the chief engineer. Like Rui, the man had returned the jewel without betraying so much as a trace of attachment.

source.japanese: 宝石には疎[うと]い朔屋をして、ザウエルには独占欲を抱かざるを得ず、水夫長に見咎められていなかったなら、クロを言いくるめて取りあげてしまった事だってあり得る、のに、機関長はこだわりも見せず二人へ戻した。実に自然な余裕が感じられる物腰で、前向性健忘症という宿痾を抱えてなお、朔屋との格の違いをまあ見せつけてくれたもの。朔屋が抱いた感情には、劣等感と妬心の混淆された色合いであった事を認めざるを得まい。
source.english: Ignorant though Sakuya was about gems, he could not help wanting the Zauer for himself. Had the boatswain not caught him with it, he might have talked Kuro around and taken it. Yet the engineer handed it back without concern. Such a naturally easy manner. Even burdened with chronic anterograde amnesia, the man had thoroughly demonstrated the difference in stature between them. One must admit that Sakuya's response was tinged with both inferiority and envy.

source.japanese:
機関長も泪も、実に平然としたものだった。
　泪は宝玉を種に不穏な話を弄[もてあそ]びこそすれ、むしろ朔屋達の来訪で中断せられた、機関長とのカードゲームの方が気になる顔で、手札を徒然に爪先で弾いたりして、話の掛け合いにも乗らずゲームにも付き合わない朔屋に大いにご不興の様子だ。おおよその女というのは、宝石貴石の類を前にすると目の色が変わるもの、なのにこの女と来たら。
　泪自身、その身に朔屋の飲み代にしたなら年単位で保ちそうな石を着けてはいるが、どれだけ輝き揺らめき冷たく澄んでいようとも所詮は無機の美質、彼女の血と肌と肉の前には、添え物でしかないのが判る。いかな高価な宝石であろうとも、所詮身にまとう物に過ぎず、振り回される物ではないという事。
source.english:
Both the engineer and Rui were perfectly calm.
Rui might toy with ominous stories inspired by the jewel, but what truly concerned her was the card game with the engineer, interrupted by their arrival. She idly flicked her cards with a fingernail and seemed thoroughly displeased with Sakuya, who would neither join her conversational play nor sit down to a game. Most women's eyes lit up at the sight of jewels and precious stones. This one, however—
She wore stones that would have kept Sakuya in drink for years. Yet however they shone and shimmered, however cool and clear, their beauty was ultimately inorganic. Beside her blood, skin, and flesh, they were mere accessories. However expensive a jewel, it was something to wear, not something to be ruled by.

source.japanese:
宝石類の真贋篩う目も、属する階層に付随してきただけで、泪にとっては農夫が野菜の出来如何を見分けるのと同じ、殊更に得意がる技能でもないのだろうが。朔屋には、その自然な余裕が小癪に思えてならなかった。
　とはいえ朔屋だって、実家はそこそこの旧家なのではあるが。
source.english:
Her eye for real gems and false probably came with her social class. For Rui, it was no more remarkable than a farmer's ability to judge vegetables—no accomplishment worth boasting of. Sakuya nevertheless found that natural assurance insufferable.
Though his own family, for that matter, was a respectable old one.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Well, I suppose. Sakuya-kun. It would appear that the Bosun's instincts were telling him the truth. For a man of his sort, he is possessed of a keen eye.」

A compliment with a somewhat questionable nuance to it, but regardless of whatever subtle antagonism that lurked between the respective chiefs of the engine and the sailors he had picked up on, he was ultimately unrelated to the whole matter, and so he took the『Sauer』jewel that the Chief Engineer had returned to him, wrapped it very gingerly in a rag, then entrusted it to Kuro. "This guy too?", Sakuya thought to himself as he chewed on a slightly bitter emotion, sending a sidelong glance at the Chief Engineer, who, just like Rui, had handed it back to him without offering a glimpse of any particular attachment.

For a man as unversed in the matter of jewels as Sakuya, it was impossible for him not to feel a possessiveness towards the Sauer, and had he not been grilled about it by the Bosun, it was quite possible he would have ended up deceiving Kuro and taking it for himself, and yet, the Chief Engineer had returned it to them both without betraying any fixation. In fact, with such natural self-possession in his mannerisms, and all the more so with him suffering from a chronic case of anterograde amnesia, he certainly made a convincing demonstration of the vast difference in class between himself and Sakuya.
This feeling Sakuya harboured within himself was one he begrudgingly had to admit was an intermixture coloured in hues of inferiority and envy.

Both the Chief Engineer and Rui truly were calm and composed. Rui had used the jewel as material to amuse herself with by concocting a disturbing tale, but if anything, her expression suggested that she was far more engaged with the card game between her and the Chief Engineer, which had been interrupted by Sakuya and Kuro's visit, flicking the cards with her fingertip in tedium, seeming greatly dissatisfied with Sakuya for being unwilling to join in on either her tale or her game. Most women get a certain glint in their eyes at the sight of jewels and other precious stones, but this woman was a different story.

Rui herself was already adorned with stones that were worth enough to fund several years worth of Sakuya's drinking habits, but for all the glimmer and the shimmer, their cool, serene clarity, it was ultimately an inorganic beauty, and when placed before her blood, skin, and flesh, he could tell it was nothing more than a complement. Even the costliest stone was, in the end, merely an ornament: a thing to be possessed, not something to be possessed by.

Being possessed of eyes able to distinguish between the genuine and the spurious in matters of gemstones is simply incident to the social class you belong to, and so to Rui, it was like a farmer discerning if a vegetable was ripe, surely not the sort of skill one would intentionally flaunt with pride. Sakuya couldn't help but find that effortless composure of hers galling. Though with that said, Sakuya was also from a rather old, established family himself.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「で、それは間違いなく『ザウエル』なわけですが。
　君たちは、そんな代物をどこで手に入れてきたんだね？」
source.english:
“So, it is certainly a Zauer.
But where did you acquire such a thing?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それは来た時に話しましたって……。
　後で泪さんにでも聞いて下さいな。
　それより、全体、この『ザウエル』ってなぁ何物なんです。俺は今までこんな石、聞いた事もなかった」
source.english:
“We told you when we got here…
Ask Rui later.
What I want to know is, what exactly is a Zauer? I've never heard of a stone like this.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Now, this is undoubtedly a『Sauer』. But wherever did the two of you get your hands on such an article?」

【Naomasa】 「We told you when we got here……. Just ask Rui about it later, please. More importantly, what in the world is this『Sauer』thing even in the first place? I've never heard of a stone like this before now.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ああ、まあ当然だろうね。
　これは当たり前の市場に出回る石じゃない。
　希少性においては、パライバトルマリンを上回る」
source.english:
“Ah, naturally enough.
It isn't a stone found on ordinary markets.
Rarer than Paraíba tourmaline.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……俺はそもそも、そのパライバなんちゃらというヤツからして知らんのですが」
source.english: “…I don't even know what that Paraíba-whatever is.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Aah, well, that is to be expected. This is not the sort of stone you will find on the open market. In terms of rarity, it actually surpasses a Paraiba tourmaline.」
【Naomasa】 「……Not like I even know what this Paraiba-something-or-other is in the first place.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ではこう言い換えよう。『ザウエル』は、そもそも鉱床からして未発見なんだ」
source.english: “Then let me put it another way. No mineral deposit containing Zauer has ever been discovered.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はん……？　そうなりゃ確かに市場には出てこないだろうが、そしたらどうやって見つけるんで」
source.english: “Huh…? Well, that'd certainly keep it off the market. But how do you find it, then?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Allow me to rephrase. As it stands, an ore deposit containing a『Sauer』 still has yet to be discovered.」
【Naomasa】 「Huh……? Yeah, then it's no wonder it wouldn't show up on the market, but in that case, how would you even go about finding one?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ある種の肺魚の砂嚢の中から、極々稀に発見される、と口伝えにされている」
source.english: “The story goes that it is found, very rarely, in the gizzard of a certain species of lungfish.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「肺魚って、あの、蛙だか井守だか魚だかの合いの子みたいな……？　ならその肺魚を根気よく捕ってきゃ、そのうち見つかるような気がするなぁ……」
source.english: “Lungfish? Those things like a cross between a frog, a newt, and a fish…? Keep catching those patiently, and you'd find one sooner or later, I'd think…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「On exceedingly rare occasions, it is found within the gizzard of a certain species of lungfish, or so it has been passed down orally.」

【Naomasa】 「A lungfish? You mean that thing that looks like a crossbreed of a frog, a newt, and a fish……? Then if you were really persistent and caught a lot of those lungfish, I feel like you'd have to find one sooner or later……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そのお魚が、まだ見つかれば、のお話よ」
source.english: “If that fish could still be found.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「That would be the case, assuming you could still find that fish.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「学者先生のお話を聞きますとね、なんでもそのお魚は、とっくの大昔、有史以前に絶滅して、今では化石くらいしか見つからないのですって」
source.english: “From what the scholars say, it became extinct a very long time ago, before recorded history. Now they find only fossils.”

source.japanese:
これには絶句するしかなく、朔屋にも事のあらましが了解されてきた。有史以前に絶滅した肺魚の化石など、確かに下手な鉱床より発見が困難だろう。そんな物朔屋の如き無学者が知らなくても当然ではあるが、人は己の無知と直面した場合に取りうる態度がいくつかある。
　一つは無知を恥とせず、それを看過する知的怠惰をこそ恥として、より深く知り理解しようと努める。
　あるいは、知らずにいた事をふて腐れるばかりで、無知の殻に引きこもろうとする。
source.english:
He could only fall silent. Even Sakuya was beginning to grasp the situation. Fossils of a lungfish extinct since prehistoric times would certainly be harder to find than many a mineral deposit. No wonder an uneducated fellow like him had never heard of it. But people have several possible responses when faced with their own ignorance.
One is to feel no shame in not knowing, but to feel shame in the intellectual laziness of letting it pass, and strive for deeper knowledge and understanding.
Another is merely to sulk at having been ignorant and retreat into one's shell.

source.japanese: 後者は言うまでもなく人類が積み重ねてきた思索と好奇心の営々たる資産に唾吐きかける行為だが、誰しも聖人君子でいられるならば、そもそも修身の授業は必要ない。小人閑居して不善を為すの見本の如き朔屋も、無知である事にふて腐れたが、彼などは相応の教育の機会を与えられながらも、遊び呆けて酒と女に現を抜かして自ら放り出したのだからして、拗ねる資格すらもない。
source.english: The latter, needless to say, amounts to spitting on the accumulated wealth of humanity's thought and curiosity. But if everyone could be a sage, there would be no need for moral instruction in the first place. Sakuya was a perfect example of the petty man who gets up to no good when left idle. He sulked over his ignorance too. Yet he had been given a fair opportunity for education and thrown it away himself, fooling around, absorbed in drink and women. He did not even have the right to sulk.

target.text: 【Rui】 「I heard of it from a scholar. As he told it, this particular fish went extinct long, long ago, in prehistoric times, and these days, they are only found as fossils.」
【Naomasa】 「…………」

At this, he could only be rendered speechless, for even Sakuya had come to understand the gist of the situation. Finding fossils of lungfish that went extinct in prehistoric times was certainly a more challenging endeavour than locating your average ore deposit. That someone as unlearned as Sakuya would not know this was only natural, but there were several ways in which one could respond when confronted with one's own ignorance.

One was to not view ignorance itself as a disgrace, but rather the intellectual sloth responsible for having turned a blind eye to something, striving instead to seek a deeper knowledge and comprehension. Alternatively, one could fester in disgruntled frustration over what they did not know, then retreat further into a shell of their own ignorance.

It goes without saying that the latter sort were acting in a manner that spat on the great wealth accumulated by humanity as a whole, earned through profound logical reasoning and hardworking curiosity, but if we could all be saints, then we would not need to give lessons in morality in the first place. Sakuya, a man who was the very exemplar of the saying "an idle brain is the devil's shop", also grew disgruntled whenever he felt ignorant, but while he had been given the opportunity to receive a proper education, he had instead neglected himself and abandoned reality to waste his time on idle amusements, drink, and women, and so he was not even qualified to sulk.

source.japanese: その益体もなく拗[す]ねた気持ちを顔に出している朔屋に、泪は叱りつけるのも面倒と言いたげに、カードの端に微妙なひねりをくわえて放れば手裏剣の回転して宙をよぎり、青年の額にすかんと角が刺さる。
source.english: As Sakuya let this pointless resentment show on his face, Rui gave a playing card a subtle twist and threw it, as if even scolding him would be too much bother. It spun through the air like a throwing star. One corner stuck neatly in his forehead.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……痛ぇなあ。何しますか泪さん。
　まあ出自なんてどうでもいいよ俺には。
　とにかく高値で売れるには違いない、と」
source.english:
“…That hurt. What are you doing, Rui?
I don't care where it comes from. The point is, it'll sell for a lot of money.”

target.text: With his fruitless sulking plain to see on his face, in an act all but saying that she found it too troublesome to even bother scolding him for it, Rui added a slight twist to the edge of a card, and when she threw it, it spun like a shuriken, flashed through the air, and the corner of the card lodged itself into the young man's brow with a thunk.
【Naomasa】 「……That hurts. What are you doing, Rui-san? Well, not like I really care about its origins. The important thing is, you're saying it's sure to fetch a high price.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「さあ、ね。
　なにお拗[す]ねになっているのか存じませんけれど。
　教えて差し上げる」
source.english:
“Perhaps.
I don't know what you're sulking about,
but let me explain something.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Who can say, really. I am not certain what you are sulking about, but I shall explain for you.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「このクラスの石になるとね、お値段なんてあってないも同然なの。ブローカーが勝手にお値段をつけて、お客は言い値で買えるかどうかがステイタスになるの」
source.english: “With a stone of this class, a price scarcely means anything. A broker sets whatever price he pleases, and the customer's status depends on being able to pay it.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「When it comes to stones of this calibre, they may as well not have a value. The brokers make an arbitrary valuation, and it becomes a matter of status whether the customer can afford it at the asking price or not.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ま。そこらのブローカーに持ちこんだって、そこそこのお値段で買い叩かれるのが関の山って言うところ」
source.english: “Take it to an ordinary broker, and the best you can expect is to be beaten down to some middling sum.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Well. Bringing the stone to those brokers and being forced to sell it at a bargain for a mediocre price is about the best you can expect.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それでも、少しはお財布、重たくなるかしら」
source.english: “Still, it might make your purse a little heavier.”

source.japanese: その少しというのだって、実家から勘当状態にある貧乏学生にはでかいのだと、額に刺さったカード引き抜いて、机に投げ返しつ、なおもしつこく悋気の尻尾に噛みつき続ける朔屋の袖[そで]をくいくいと、引くものがある。先程から会話の流れに乗る事も出来ず、ぽかんと立ち尽くしていたクロだった。なんだか所在なげ、どころか泣きそうに眉を歪めていた。
source.english: Even that ‘little’ was a great deal to a poor student all but disowned by his family. Sakuya pulled the card from his forehead and tossed it back onto the table, still stubbornly gnawing at the tail of his envy. Something tugged his sleeve. Kuro. Unable to follow the conversation, she had stood gaping all this time. Now she looked more than ill at ease. Her brows were crooked as though she might cry.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Still, I suppose it might make your purse feel a little heavier.」

To a penniless student disowned by his family, what she called "a little" carried significant weight, he thought as he pulled the card from his brow, then threw it back on the table, and while Sakuya continued to stubbornly cling to the remnants of his envy, something pulled at his sleeve, giving a few tugs. It was Kuro, who had been standing there dazed for some time, unable to find her way into the flow of the conversation. She looked not just bored, her brows were even furrowed as though she was about to cry.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あの、朔屋さん……ご用事、終わった、
　みたいですか」
source.english:
“Um, Mr. Sakuya… Are we…
finished here now?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ。聞く事は聞いたと思う……」
source.english: “Yes. I think we've asked what we needed to…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uhm, Sakuya-san……looks like, we're done with our errand?」
【Naomasa】 「Yeah. I think we've heard all we needed to hear……」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そんなら、もどっていい、かなぁ。
　あんね、クロね、さっき怖いお話聞かされてから、
　ずっと我慢で、我慢して、しました。おしっこ。
　でももう……あ、あぁ……うぅー……」
source.english:
“Then can we go back?
You know, Kuro's been holding it… holding it…
since that scary story. Kuro has to pee.
But now… ah, ahh… oooh…”

source.japanese: 最前よりこらえていた尿意が、限界に達したのであろう。朔屋もこれ以上は機関長達から聞く事なしと、部屋から退散する事にした───
source.english: The need she had been resisting had apparently reached its limit. Sakuya had nothing more to ask the engineer and Rui, so they retreated from the room—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Then, is it okay, if we go back? Uhm, so, Kuro was, listening to that scary story earlier, and held, this whole time, held it in. Kuro did. The pee. But now it's……ah, aah……uuuー……」

Endured for a while now, her urge to urinate seemed to have finally reached the breaking point. Sakuya also no longer had anything to ask from the Chief Engineer and company, and so they decided to take their leave───

source.japanese:
船内通路の暗がりに、細い水流れの音響くとあっては、すわ隔壁に孔が開いての浸水か、配管が腐食しての漏水かと、いずれ船には好ましからざる事態と慌てて駆けつけた者があったとしても馬鹿を見る。
　水音は、通路からやや引っこんだ奥にある、便所の扉の向こうから。閉まりきっておらず白くうねる髪と同じく白く細い脚が覗いているところと遭遇しても、恐縮せずともよい、開けっ放しにしたのクロだから。旧式の船の便所に相応しく、薄汚れて狭苦しい、暗い、臭いと三拍子も四拍子も揃っていて、機関室での話の後では扉たてきって籠もるのに、少女にとって恐怖の場所でありすぎた。
source.english:
A faint sound of running water echoed in the dark passage. A hole in the bulkhead? Flooding? Corroded pipes leaking? All undesirable things aboard a ship, but anyone who rushed over in alarm would only look a fool.
The sound came from behind the lavatory door, set a little back from the passage. Even if one encountered the white, curling hair and equally white, thin legs visible through the half-open door, there was no need for embarrassment. Kuro had left it open. It had all the charms of an old ship's lavatory: filthy, cramped, dark, and foul-smelling. After the story in the engine room, it was far too frightening a place for the girl to shut herself inside.

source.japanese:
かつまた、水音は便所の外でも。一人で用を足すのを恐れたクロに、側で待っててと哀願されて、ついてやっていたのはいいのだが、便所からの水音聞くともなしに耳にしているうちに、つられて催して、近くにあったクロの『箱』からおまるを引っぱり出して放尿していたのである。だから二条の水流は、少なくとも船を沈める類のものではない。
　痩せッぽちの白子の少女といい年晒した男二人が連れションの、なんとも尾籠な光景を見て、気分の方はずんと沈むかもしれないが。
source.english:
There was running water outside the lavatory too. Kuro, afraid to relieve herself alone, had begged Sakuya to wait nearby. That was all very well, but as he absently heard the water from within, he began to feel the need himself. He pulled a chamber pot from Kuro's box nearby and was urinating into it. Neither of these two streams, then, was likely to sink the ship.
The sight of a scrawny albino girl and a man old enough to know better taking a piss together might, however, sink one's spirits considerably.

target.text: Within the darkness of the passageway came the faint tinkling of a delicate stream of water; goodness me, was it water flooding in from a hole opened in a bulkhead, was it water leaking from rusted pipes? Had there been any who thought the ship was in some sort of undesirable state only to come running in a hurry, then they would have looked quite the fool.

The sound of water came from beyond a washroom door, recessed slightly in the depths of the passageway. Even should you encounter a glimpse of undulating white hair and equally pale, slender legs through the half-closed door, you needn't feel awkward; it was Kuro herself who had left it open. Appropriately for a washroom on an old-fashioned ship, it was dingy, cramped, dark, and smelly; it satisfied all three or even four of those characteristics, and though she had slammed the door shut and cooped herself up in there after hearing that story in the engine room, in the end, the place was simply too scary for the girl.

Moreover, there was even a sound of water coming from outside the washroom. As she was scared to finish her business by her lonesome, Kuro had pleaded with him to wait nearby, and though he had no particular issue with that, while he pretended not to hear the sound of running water coming from the washroom, he, too, was enticed into a similar need, and so he had pulled out the bedpan from Kuro's『Box』nearby and was urinating in that himself. That is why these two streams of water were, if nothing else, not the sort of thing that would sink a ship.
An albino girl thin as a rail and a man old enough to know better taking a leak together: a thoroughly indecent sight, and one that might well make your spirits plummet like a stone, but.

source.japanese:
……なお宝珠を発見したのは、漂流者を看取った朔屋とクロではあるものの、当然のように没収が決定されてある。船で拾い上げた漂流者の遺物は船の共有財産、修理代その他に充てるとか、お題目はもっともらしく二人に逆らう余地はない。
　朔屋などは当然不満顔で、
source.english:
Now, although Sakuya and Kuro had discovered the jewel while attending the castaway's death, its confiscation had naturally been decided. The possessions of a castaway picked up by the ship were common property, to be used for repairs and other expenses. Plausible enough principles. Neither could object.
Sakuya, of course, looked displeased.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーあ。勿体なかったなあクロ。さっさと取りあげられちまったい」
source.english: “Ah, what a waste, Kuro. They took it straight off us.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「見つけたところ見られてなけりゃあ、ネコババできたかもな」
source.english: “If they hadn't seen us find it, we might've pocketed it.”

source.japanese: とかロクでもないことを抜かすのだが、クロはあまり拘ってはいない様子。
source.english: Disreputable remarks of that sort. Kuro, however, seemed not particularly concerned.

target.text: ……Although it had been Sakuya and Kuro who discovered the jewel as they nursed the castaway in his final moments, it was decided that it would be confiscated from them as if it were the most natural thing in the world. Any relics from castaways picked up by the ship was the ship's communal property, and it would be set aside for the cost of repairs and so on; the arguments they made were plausible enough to leave the two with no room to oppose them. Of course, a man like Sakuya was still displeased,
【Naomasa】 「Aaah. What a damn waste, Kuro. They nabbed it from us in no time.」
【Naomasa】 「If only we hadn't been seen the moment we found it, maybe we could have pocketed it or something.」
Despite him blathering on about such nonsense, Kuro didn't seem to pay it much mind.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だって、クロはもっといいの、持ってるもん」
source.english: “But Kuro has better things.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But, Kuro has even better stuff.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だから、取られてもあんまり悔しくないもん」
source.english: “So Kuro doesn't mind much that they took it.”

source.japanese:
そうと豪毅な事を言われたところでなんで信じられたものか。
　実はクロという少女のお遊びというか趣味というかだが、彼女は光り物を集める癖[ヘキ]がある。もちろん光るというて、ビー玉だの波に洗われたガラス瓶の欠片だの、微笑ましいが無価値なガラクタばかりで、彼女は船室に、それこそ烏[カラス]の巣のように、そういう光るガラクタ詰めこんだ『宝箱』を隠し持っているのが公然の秘密。
source.english:
A bold statement, but how could he believe it?
The girl did, in fact, have a pastime or hobby: a habit of collecting shiny things. Shiny meant marbles, of course, or pieces of glass bottle washed smooth by the waves. Endearing, but worthless junk. It was an open secret that she hid a ‘treasure chest’ in her cabin—a crow's nest crammed with such glittering rubbish.

source.japanese: さしもの貪欲な信天翁号の面子もそれには手を着けたりもせず看過してあり、それは朔屋も同様で、クロの気前いい台詞も聞き流した。
source.english: Even the greedy inhabitants of the Albatross left it alone. Sakuya was no different, and he let her generous-sounding words pass.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「That's why, when they took it, Kuro wasn't that upset.」

She could assert that with all the firm strength of character she wanted, but how could he possibly believe her? Call it a little game or pastime, but the truth was, this girl named Kuro had a habit of collecting shiny things. Of course, the shiny here refers to bric-a-brac like little marbles and fragments of glass bottles washed clean by the waves───heartwarming, but ultimately all worthless─── and it was an open secret on the ship that, in her cabin, she had a hidden 『Treasure Chest』full of that kind of sparkling rubbish, almost like a crow's nest.
As greedy as the crew of the Albatross was, even they turned a blind eye to it, and Sakuya felt much the same way, letting Kuro's generous words go in one ear and out the other.

source.japanese: さて、まさしく降って湧いたようなザウエルの、それ一つで当分は遊んで暮らせるくらいの財を得た信天翁号だったが、それでも満足しない、飽く事のない貪婪、が、水夫長の遠い記憶を呼び覚ました。
source.english: So the Albatross had acquired a Zauer as though it had fallen from the sky, a fortune sufficient to keep them idle for some time. But still they were not satisfied. Their insatiable greed stirred an old memory in the boatswain.

target.text: Now then. The sudden windfall of the Sauer, which had practically landed in their laps from out of thin air, where even a single stone alone would provide the Albatross with enough wealth to live a life of leisure for the foreseeable future, but that avarice of his, unappeasable, insatiable even by that much, awakened a distant memory in the Bosun.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「あの学者はさっさとおっ死んじまったが、そういや、おなじような『いつまでも止まない嵐』から生きて帰ってきた水夫の噂、聞いたことある」
source.english: “That scholar died soon enough. But come to think of it, I've heard rumors of a sailor who came back alive from a similar ‘storm that never ends.’”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「That scholar has already kicked the bucket, of course, but, I do remember hearing a rumour. Of a sailor who lived to tell the tale of a similar "storm that never ceases".」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ってえ事は。
　そいつから話を聞ければ、もしかしたらもっとザウエルが───」
source.english:
“Which means,
if we could hear his story, maybe there'd be more Zauer—”

source.japanese:
かくして信天翁号の次の行き先は定まった。
　突っ張らかった欲の皮の、求めるままに信天翁号、その水夫がいるという港へ───
source.english:
Thus the Albatross's next destination was decided.
With the skin of her greed stretched taut, the Albatross followed her appetite toward the port where that sailor was said to be—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Which means. If we hear his tale, maybe we can get our hands on even more Sauers───」

Thus, the next destination of the Albatross was settled. Noses led by their immense greed, at the mercy of their rapacious souls, the Albatross set sail for the port where this sailor could be found───

source.japanese: 信天翁号が洋上であの漂流死体を拾ってから二十日ばかり後の事───緬甸の片隅の港にて。
source.english: Some twenty days after the Albatross picked up that drifting corpse—at a port in a corner of Burma.

source.japanese:
港の酒場は造りも喧噪もどこもかしこ似たり寄ったり、たとい初めて足を踏み入れた船乗りであろうと、故国に戻ったかの安心感が、慣れたタオルの気やすさでもって包みこむ。あくどい煙草の煙も、級数も付かないような安酒の臭気も、船乗り達のきつい汗の臭いも酒場娘たちの香水も、常人なら眼を回しかねない魔女の鍋の中のごった煮なのに、陸では寛げない熟練の船乗りをして、胸襟開かしせしめるのだから、慣れというのは恐ろしい。
　朔屋も、普段ならこの渦を巻いて押し寄せる猛烈な人いきれと、古いジュークボックスからのひっきりなしに雨音混じる歌謡曲に、安らぐとまでは至らずとも、閉口しないで済むくらいには面の皮、船員暮らしの垢に鍛えられつつあったが。
source.english:
Harbor taverns were much alike in their construction and their noise. Even a sailor entering one for the first time felt the security of home wrap around him with the easy familiarity of an old towel. Acrid tobacco smoke, liquor too cheap to merit a grade, sailors' rank sweat, barmaids' perfume: a stew in a witch's cauldron that might make an ordinary person's head spin. Yet it let a seasoned sailor, unable to relax on land, open his heart. Habit was a terrible thing.
Normally, Sakuya might not have found comfort in that fierce, swirling press of humanity, or the popular songs issuing from an old jukebox amid a rainlike crackle. But his hide was being toughened by the grime of life at sea. He had at least learned not to be overwhelmed.

target.text: It happened twenty days after the Albatross had picked up the corpse of the castaway out at sea───in a port found in a remote corner of Burma.

Be it the layout or the boisterous noise, taverns in ports are much the same wherever you go; supposing that you were a sailor stepping foot into one for the very first time, that comfortable feeling of returning home would envelop you, like wrapping yourself in the comfort of a familiar towel.

Even the nasty tobacco smoke, the stench of alcohol so cheap it hasn't even been graded, the harsh reek of the sailors' sweat, and the perfume of the bar girls: like a mulligan stew in a witch's cauldron, it is enough to leave any ordinary person's eyes swimming, but for experienced sailors, those unable to feel at home on land, it would be enough to coax their hearts open; habits truly are a terrifying thing. (TN: In Japan, sake is graded based on the rice polishing ratio. That is to say, how much of the outer layer of the rice grain has been milled away.)

Sakuya was no different; ordinarily, the air thick with the sultry heat emanating from the crowd of people, swirling around and bearing down on him, as well as the noise of Kayoukyoku mixed with the sound of rain played incessantly by an ancient jukebox, would not quite bring him comfort, but that he had now grown to tolerate it was a sign that his skin had grown thicker, tempered in the grime of a sailor's life. (TN: Kayoukyoku, written "歌謡曲", is a style of Japanese pop music that peaked in the 1950s, heavily inspired by Western popular music of the time, contrasting with the classical Japanese popular music, Enka.)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（いや、わかる、わかるよ皆の衆。
　信天翁号が憎まれ船だってのは俺だって）
source.english:
(I know, I know, everyone.
Even I know the Albatross is a hated ship.)

source.japanese: 朔屋とそしてクロが、酒場のスウィングドアを押し揺らした途端に、場のざわめきは鳴りやんで、皆一斉に、恋人がおっ死んだとの虫の報せでも届いたか悪魔に背中にでも撫でられたか。すぐに粗布から水が沁み出す塩梅で人声は戻ってきたけれど、囁き交わす声は『あれがアルバトロスの』『胸糞わりい』だの『今度ぁどんな悪さをしに来やがった』『だれか波止場に行って、あの船の土手っ腹に銛撃ち銃でも叩っこんでこいよ』だの、剥きつけな敵意と底意が満ち満ちた。
source.english: The moment Sakuya and Kuro pushed through the swinging doors, the noise stopped. Everyone reacted at once, as if a premonition had told them their lover was dead, or the devil had stroked their back. Voices soon returned, seeping like water through coarse cloth. But the murmurs were ‘That's one of the Albatross lot,’ ‘Makes me sick,’ ‘What are they here to do this time?’ and ‘Someone go down to the quay and shoot a harpoon into that ship's belly.’ Naked hostility and ill intent filled the room.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（それにしたってもこれは……。
　いきすぎじゃないか？）
source.english:
(Even so,
isn't this… a little much?)

source.japanese:
それまで上機嫌にストリップダンサーのパンツに札びらねじ込んでいた奴がこれ見よがしに唾を吐く、ショットグラス積み上げラムの一気飲み競争に興じていた奴が真っ赤な額を青ざめさせ十字を切って席を立つ、カード賭博に耽[ふけ]っていた卓では親も子も揃ってリボルバーの弾倉に弾を籠め始める始末の、どいつもこいつも横目に、肩越しに、或いはあからさまに視線をよこしてちらちらちら、剣山を内張りにした袋にでも詰められたような、朔屋の居心地の悪さと言ったらない。
　浮かんでいるのが悪魔の奇跡である信天翁号の船型は一目見たら忘れられない代物で、入港したところを見咎めたどこぞの差し出者が、早速酒場に駆けこんでご注進と及んだものらしい。
source.english:
The fellow who until then had been merrily stuffing banknotes into a stripper’s panties now spat with ostentatious contempt; another, engaged in a rum-chugging contest over towers of shot glasses, went from scarlet-faced to bloodless, crossed himself, and left his seat; at the card table, dealer and players alike began thumbing cartridges into their revolvers. Every man jack of them was looking his way—sidelong, over a shoulder, or with no pretense at all, a fusillade of glances—and Sakuya might as well have been sewn into a sack lined with flower frogs, every spike turned inward, for all the comfort he felt.
The lines of the Albatross—whose very floating was a devil’s miracle—were not to be forgotten once seen. Some officious informer must have spotted her making port and run straight to the tavern to spread the alarm.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （No, no, I get it, I understand you, all of you. The Albatross is a detestable ship, even I feel that way.）

The instant the saloon doors leading into the bar were swung open by Sakuya and then Kuro, the commotion of the place died down, quieting all at once; had they felt a premonition that their lover had died, or did they feel the Devil stroking their backs? Like water being wrung out of a washcloth, the sound of voices quickly returned, but the whispers exchanged were 『Those two are from the Albatross!』 『Revolting!』and 『What sort of villainy are they here to commit this time?』 『Somebody, go to the wharf and shoot a harpoon right into her guts, or blast her with a handgun!』 and so on, brimming with naked animosity and dark designs.
【Naomasa】 （But even so, isn't this……. Going a little too far?）

Some fellows who, until then, had been in a great mood while cramming paper money down the panties of an exotic dancer now made a deliberate show of spitting; the beet-red faces of guys who had been engaged in a contest of knocking back shot glasses full of rum now paled, making the sign of the cross as they rose from their seats; at a card table engrossing in gambling, it had come to the point where both the dealer and the players all simultaneously began loading their revolvers with bullets.

Each and every one of them gave the two sidelong glances, looked over their shoulders, or perhaps very blatantly stared, repeatedly glancing at them, and Sakuya had never felt such excruciating discomfort; it felt as though he'd been stuffed into a bag lined with pin frogs. (TN: A pin frog, written "剣山", lit. "mountain of swords", is a form of needle holder used in ikebana, Japanese flower arrangement. It has a heavy base of metal covered in thick needles that hold the flowers in place.)

The design of the Albatross, floating only through the graces of a miracle performed by the Devil himself, was the sort you'd never forget once you had laid eyes on it, and it seemed some nosy people who found fault with them staying in this port had run straight to the bar to report the unfortunate news.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ひやあ!?」
source.english: “Hyaa!?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Hyaaah!?」

source.japanese: こう敵意悪意に晒されればさしもの朔屋にも多少は用心するもので、歩く先から先に突き出されてくる客どもの足を、それでも芋虫が棘をよける程度にのろのろ躱[かわ]していたのだが、その背後で床を体が撃つ響き、ほとんど骨皮ばかりの軽さはクロが倒れたが音だ。のろまなこと朔屋を上回るこの白子の少女は、場内の敵意にも疎[うと]かったが同時に注意力にも乏しく、客の悪意の足を避けきれなかったようだ。
source.english: Surrounded by such hostility, even Sakuya took a little care. He evaded the feet customers stuck into his path, though as slowly as a caterpillar avoiding thorns. Behind him came the sound of a body striking the floor. The lightness of it, almost all skin and bone: Kuro had fallen. Slower even than Sakuya, the albino girl was oblivious to the room's hostility and short on attention besides. She had failed to avoid someone's malicious foot.

target.text: Being exposed to animosity and ill intent like so, even Sakuya was somewhat guarded, and though the other patrons stuck their legs out in front of where he was walking, he still managed to sluggishly dodge them like a caterpillar avoiding thorns, but then he heard the sound of a body impacting the floor behind him with the lightness of nothing but skin and bones, which could only be the sound of Kuro falling over. This albino girl, who surpassed Sakuya in matters of dimwittery, was oblivious to the enmity within the premises, but at the same time, she was also lacking in attentiveness, and so it seemed she had been unable to avoid the malicious leg of a patron.

source.japanese: 舌打ち、を漏らしそうになるがここは言わば虎の穴、どう逆捩じにとられてもおかしくないので憚って、それでもクロを助け起こせば、顔はおが屑やら食い滓でざらざらの、きょとんとしたのが痛みに歪む。どうやら一拍遅れで神経が痛みを伝えたらしい。ぐずりかかる唇に慌てて人差し指押し当てて黙らせて、朔屋はカウンターの一画に身を縮め気味に浅く掛けた、遠慮がちにしたつもりが余計にバーテンダーの癇に障[さわ]った。
source.english: He nearly clicked his tongue. But this was a tiger's den, so to speak, where anything might be taken the wrong way. He refrained and helped Kuro up. Her face, rough with sawdust and food scraps, passed from bewilderment into pain. Apparently her nerves had taken a moment to deliver the news. As her lips began to pout, he hastily pressed a forefinger against them to silence her. He perched shallowly on a stool at one end of the counter, drawing himself in. An attempt at diffidence that only annoyed the bartender more.

target.text: He was on the verge of clicking his tongue at the man, but he was inside the lion's den; any slight could be twisted against him here, so he held it in, but he still helped Kuro stand, her face gritty with sawdust and crumbs, the bewildered look on her face twisting with pain. It seemed that her nerves had, somehow or other, transmitted the pain a beat too late. In a fluster, he pushed his index finger to her lips to silence them before they could begin to grumble, and Sakuya then perched himself on a stool at a corner of the counter, shoulders hunched to make himself seem smaller, but his attempt to be considerate only served to provoke the bartender further.

source.japanese: どん、とカウンターに叩きつけられたのは、小皿を使ってやるのも惜しいと言わんばかりの灰皿に、山と漏られた塩の、白さもなんとも尖々しい。
source.english: An ashtray slammed onto the counter, as if even a small dish would have been too much courtesy. Salt was heaped in it. Even its whiteness looked prickly.

target.text: With a clonk, something was slammed down on the counter; atop a little ashtray, all but saying that even a small dish would be wasted on their ilk, was a heap of salt piled high, even its whiteness terribly prickly to look at.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なんです、こりゃあ」
source.english: “…What's this?”

source.japanese:
【バーテンダー】
「見ての通り、塩だぁね」
source.english: “Salt, as you can see.”

source.japanese: 傷の走った頬髭といういかにもな古強者、酸いも甘いも噛み分けた筈の酒場の賢者からして喧嘩腰、半身を向けての横目の睨[にら]みで。
source.english: Scarred cheeks, side-whiskers: every inch the old campaigner. Even this tavern sage, who ought to have known life's bitter and sweet alike, was spoiling for a fight. Half-turned away, he glared sideways.

source.japanese:
【バーテンダー】
「先に言っておくが、酒もビールもミルクも水もないからな、売り切れだ。塩でも舐めてろい」
source.english: “I'll tell you now. No liquor, beer, milk, or water. Sold out. Lick some salt.”

source.japanese:
【酒場の客】
「マスター、テキーラをダブルで」
source.english: “A double tequila, barkeep.”

source.japanese:
【バーテンダー】
「おう、少々お待ちを」
source.english: “Right. Coming up.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……What the hell is this?」

【Bartender】 「As you can see, salt, right?」 (TN: While just serving salt also has obvious implications in English, it is also a play on two Japanese traditions, as well as a pun. Salt is used in Shinto tradition to purify, and many Japanese bars and eateries place small, conical piles of salt at their entrance to ward off evil energy. There is also the tradition of throwing a handful of salt through the doorway behind an unpleasant customer as they leave. And salt, just as it can mean bitter or upset over something petty in English, also has the colloquial meaning of cold, unwelcoming treatment in Japanese.)

With a scar running through his sideburns, he was the very picture of a veteran, but he was also awfully belligerent for a tavern sage experienced in the bittersweet ways of the world, his body half-turned while fixing them with a sideways glare.
【Bartender】 「Before you ask, we don't have any liquor, beer, milk, or water. We're sold out. Go lick salt.」
【Patron of the bar】 「Barkeep! A tequila, make it double!」
【Bartender】 「Coming right up.」

source.japanese: 一呼吸の間に売り切れだった筈の酒が補給された手回しの良さだが、多分朔屋達が頼んだとたんにまた品切れになるのだろう。お追従の注文さえ許されない厳戒態勢、食人族の部落に踏みこんだ宣教師でもこうはあるまいと肩を落とした朔屋の脇で、どこまで読めないのか、クロは出された塩を舐めては顔をしかめていた。
source.english: Remarkably efficient restocking: the liquor supposedly sold out had been replenished within a breath. No doubt it would be out of stock again the moment Sakuya or Kuro asked. Security was so tight that even a placatory order was forbidden. A missionary entering a village of cannibals might have had an easier time. Sakuya's shoulders sagged. Beside him, Kuro showed the extraordinary extent of her inability to read a room by licking the salt they had been given, then making a face.

target.text: What incredibly efficient arrangements he must have had in place to resupply liquor that was sold out in the span of a single breath, but the moment Sakuya or Kuro were to order something, he'd probably just claim they were out again. The bar was on such high alert that, even with some added lip service, they were not allowed to make an order, and when Sakuya's shoulders slumped at the realization that not even a missionary venturing into the settlement of a cannibalistic tribe would be treated so coldly, just how incapable of reading this situation could she be? There, by his side, Kuro was licking the salt they'd been served and scrunching up her face.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あの……」
source.english: “Um…”

source.japanese: なにか言いかけたところでぴしゃりと遮[さえぎ]られる。相変わらず朔屋をまともに見向きしないまま。
source.english: He was cut off sharply before he could begin. The bartender still would not look properly at him.

source.japanese:
【バーテンダー】
「……二年前だったか。この港を仕切る顔役のな。情婦が若い手下と手に手をとって逃げ出した事があった───」
source.english: “…Two years ago, was it? The mistress of the man who runs this port ran off hand in hand with one of his young underlings.”

source.japanese:
【バーテンダー】
「そいつらな、どう血迷ったんだか、逃げる足に選んだのがお前らアルバトロスよ。まあそこまではいい。それだけなら密通野郎と顔役と、そしてお前らだけの問題だからな」
source.english: “Don't know what got into them, but they picked your Albatross as their getaway. Fine, so far. That alone was between the lovers, the boss, and you lot.”

source.japanese: ぼそぼそと、渋く錆びた語りはジャズでも唸らせれば股を濡らす女もありそうなところ、朔屋の背にのしかかったのは背後からのいや増しの敵意、膨れあがっていく巨大な風船と共に密室に閉じ込められる危機感を招く。酒場の内は、当時の事情を知る客ばかり。
source.english: His low, rusted voice might have made women wet had he used it to sing jazz. What settled upon Sakuya's back, however, was the growing hostility behind him. The sensation of being locked in a room with an enormous balloon steadily inflating. Everyone here knew what had happened.

source.japanese:
【バーテンダー】
「だが逃げるって段で、港の海に重油ぶちまけて一杯にして、火ぃ放っていったとありゃあ話は別だ。
　なんぼ追っ手の船が邪魔だったたぁいえ……関係無ぇ船までたくさん焼けたんだ」
source.english:
“But when you left, you filled the harbor with heavy oil and set it on fire. That's another matter.
I don't care if the pursuing ships were in your way… Plenty of ships with nothing to do with it burned too.”

source.japanese: あの連中ならやりかねない、いやきっとやると頭を抱えた朔屋に追い討ちの槍が更に。
source.english: That crew might do it. No—they certainly would. Sakuya clutched his head at the thought, and then came another spear-thrust.

source.japanese:
【バーテンダー】
「ちなみにその後で、間男は身ぐるみ剥がれた死体になって浜に流れ着き、女は女で澳門の売春宿で客を取らされているのがめっかった。
　すっかり気が狂っていたらしいがな」
source.english:
“And afterward, the lover's stripped corpse washed up on the beach. The woman turned up being made to take customers in a Macau brothel.
Gone completely mad, apparently.”

source.japanese:
【バーテンダー】
「で、そんなアルバトロスのお前らが、今さらなんの御用でございますかね？」
source.english: “So what might you fine people from the Albatross want here now?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Uhhmm……」
Just as he made to say something to her, he was abruptly cut off. All while, as ever, refusing to face Sakuya directly.
【Bartender】 「……Was it two years ago now? The big guy in charge of this port. When his mistress ran away, hand in hand with one of his young subordinates───」

【Bartender】 「I do wonder what had possessed those two, for the method of escape they chose was you people on the Albatross. Well, that was all well and good. If that was all, then it would only be a problem between that cheating rat bastard, the boss, and all of you lot.」

If the gravelly, subdued muttering of his narration was instead sung with a growl to some jazz, there'd likely be some women left soaked between their legs, but what weighed down on Sakuya's back was an ever-increasing hostility, stirring within him a sense of impending danger like he was trapped in a sealed room with a giant inflating balloon. The bar was full of customers who were all familiar with the circumstances of that time.

【Bartender】 「But if, when they escaped, they poured bunker oil into the waters around the port, and then lit this oil on fire, then its a whole different story. No matter how much the ships on their tail would've gotten in their way……plenty of innocent ships went up in flames too.」
It wasn't hard to imagine those guys doing that; no, they definitely would, Sakuya thought as he cradled his head in his hands, and as though to rub the proverbial salt even deeper into the wound.

【Bartender】 「By the way, after all that, the corpse of her paramour was found dead, washed ashore and stripped of all his belongings, and the woman herself, well, she was discovered being forced to entertain clients at a brothel in Macao. Seems she'd gone stark raving mad.」
【Bartender】 「So, what manner of business could you fine folks from the Albatross possibly have with us this time?」

source.japanese: 朔屋は───他に見えないよう抱えこんだ頭の下でうっすら笑い、ひっそりと震えだした。かたかたと、カウンターの反対端の客のタンブラーまで揺らすくらいの怯えぶりで。信天翁号と関わって以来、顔を出す先鼻先で覗く先が、悉く、それまでは無縁だった死地と地続きになっている。信天翁号の悪名を侮りすぎていた自分に、朔屋は臍を食いちぎるほどに噛んだところで遅し。卓上の塩を頭から全部被ったとて、この厄は容易には払えまい。
source.english: Hidden beneath the head he had buried in his arms, Sakuya smiled faintly and began, very quietly, to shake—rattling hard enough to set even a tumbler at the far end of the counter trembling. Ever since he had fallen in with the Albatross, every place he showed his face, every place he poked his nose, had opened straight onto some killing ground hitherto foreign to his life. Too late now to gnaw his navel bloody with regret over having underestimated the ship's infamy. He could pour every grain of salt on the table over his head and still not exorcise this curse.

target.text: Sakuya was───smiling thinly beneath the arms covering his face so nobody could see him, then quietly began to tremble. So frightened was he that it was enough to make another customer's tumbler on the opposite side of the counter rattle. Ever since he'd become involved with the Albatross, everywhere he showed his face or poked his nose into, each and every time, without exception, had seen him thrust into a seamless chain of lethal predicaments that were once so foreign to him.

But by the time he was forced to swallow the pill that he'd taken the infamy of the Albatross much too lightly, one so bitter he could taste the acid on his tongue, it was already too late. Even if he poured all the salt on the table over his head, this misfortune would not so easily be driven away.

source.japanese:
水夫長、龍の親爺に、あの漂死体が告げていた『止まない嵐』、すなわちザウエルへの手がかりを知る水夫がこの港の酒場にいるらしい、聞き出してこいと命じられ、その時せっかくの上陸なのにひどく気が進まなかったわけを今さら覚った。あれは悪い予感の虫報せだったのだ。
　こんな敵地の真っ直中では、話を訊くは愚か、まず生きて帰る事を諦めた方がよさそうな。
source.english:
Old Long, the boatswain, had ordered him to come here. A sailor at this port's tavern apparently knew something about the ‘storm that never ends’ mentioned by the drifting corpse—a clue to Zauer. Go and ask him. Only now did Sakuya understand why he had been so reluctant, despite a chance to go ashore. A bad premonition.
Forget gathering information in the middle of enemy territory. He might as well give up on getting back alive.

source.japanese:
朔屋は、深く怨んで呪った。
　彼に命じつけた水夫長がこの場にあれば、朔屋とて食ってかかったろうが、あのザウエルを金に換える為、泪を伴って宝石商に渡りをつけに赴いている。朔屋にクロを付けてよこしたのは、半人前と半人前でようやく一人前の手と口になるだろうの心づもりか知らんが、マイナスにマイナスを足したところで負の数は増えるのみである。まだどちらか一人の方がましだったろう。
source.english:
He bitterly resented and cursed the man.
Had the boatswain who sent him been here, even Sakuya would have confronted him. But Old Long had gone with Rui to make contact with a jeweler and turn the Zauer into cash. Perhaps he had sent Kuro along thinking two half-baked sailors might add up to one who knew what to do and what to say. Add a negative to a negative, however, and all one gets is a larger negative. Either of them alone would have been better.

target.text: A sailor who knew of this 『Ceaseless Storm』 that drifting corpse had told them of, in other words, a clue to the whereabouts of the Sauers, could supposedly be found in the bar of this port, and he'd been ordered to find him and ask him about it by the Bosun, old man Long; it was only just now that Sakuya finally realized why he had felt so unmotivated despite being given a long-awaited opportunity for some shore leave. That gut feeling had been a dark foreboding. Trapped in the middle of enemy territory like this, it would probably be best to give up on hearing the tale, to say nothing of returning to tell it.

With deep resentment in his heart, Sakuya bitterly cursed them all. If the man who had ordered him here, the Bosun, was with him right now, even Sakuya would probably have lashed out at him, then left to go accompany Rui while she got in touch with a jeweler to exchange the Sauer they had for money. Sakuya didn't know if they made Kuro accompany him because they secretly expected that two half-assed people would finally combine into a whole ass and all it was attached to, but were you to add two negative numbers together, you would only get more negative numbers for your trouble. It would probably have gone better if only one of them had come.

source.japanese: クロはクロで、塩の灰皿を鼻先に持っていってくんくんと、しきりに匂いを確かめるのが自分の垂れた小便を嗅ぐ白鼠のような、
source.english: Kuro, meanwhile, kept bringing the ashtray of salt to her nose and sniffing it, like a white rat smelling its own urine.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（……なにやってんだよクロ）
source.english: (…What are you doing, Kuro?)

target.text: And Kuro, being herself, had brought the ashtray to the tip of her nose and was sniffing at the salt, repeatedly verifying the scent like a white mouse smelling its own urine,
【Naomasa】 （……Just what are you doing, Kuro?）

source.japanese:
【クロ】
（これ、お塩？　でもせっかく、くれた。
　くれたから、特別なのかな、
　塩じゃないのかなって）
source.english:
(Is it salt? But they gave it to us.
So maybe it's special.
Maybe it's not salt.)

source.japanese: と、全くもって死んだ魚並みに賢い限りだが、吸いこみすぎて塩粒鼻に詰まらせ、酢を舐めた狆[チン]ころの顔になって、今にも張り裂けそうなのには朔屋、肝を潰した。この一触即発状態の酒場ではくしゃみ一つでも命取りになりかねない。朔屋は慌てて手を走らせたが、メロスは間に合わず一高生は天城峠で伊豆の踊子と出会う前に崖から転がり落ちた。
source.english: Wise as a dead fish. But she sniffed too hard, got salt grains up her nose, and made the face of a little Japanese Chin that had licked vinegar. She looked about to burst. Sakuya was horrified. In this tavern, poised to explode, a single sneeze might be fatal. He hastily reached out, but Melos did not arrive in time. The First Higher School student tumbled off a cliff at Amagi Pass before meeting the Izu dancer.

target.text: 【Kuro】 （Is this salt? But he gave it to us. If he gave it, maybe it's special, maybe not salt, Kuro wondered.）

So she said. Truly, this girl was as clever as a dead fish, but then she inhaled too hard, got grains of salt lodged up her nose, her face remarkably similar to that of a Chin lapping up vinegar, about to erupt at any second; Sakuya was horrified. A single sneeze in this powder keg of a bar could well cost them their lives.

Sakuya quickly threw his hand forwards in a panic, but Melos did not make it in time, a student of the First Higher School tumbled down the cliff before he could meet the dancing girl of Izu at the Mount Amagi tunnel. (TN: Melos is a reference to "走れメロス", known in English as "Run, Melos!", a Japanese short story written by Osamu Dazai. The dancing girl is a reference to "伊豆の踊子", most commonly known as "The Dancing Girl of Izu" in English, a short story written by Kawabata Yasunari. The First Higher School was a university preparatory boy's boarding school in Tokyo that was incorporated into the University of Tokyo in 1950.)

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「───ひゃくしゅん───っ！」
source.english: “Hyaa-choo!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「───aaAACHOO───!」

source.japanese:
あの港湾倉庫で売り払われ損なった時もこの今も、どうにも要所要所でやらかしてくれるのがこのクロで、どうしてこうも上も下も緩いのか、酒場に響き渡ったくしゃみに硬直した朔屋の背なに突つくもの、それは不気味な沈黙の裡[うち]に拳鍔を嵌[は]める気配であり、飛び出しナイフの鞘走りであり、回転弾倉の撃鉄を起こす金属音であり、どれもこれも切っ先のようにちくちくと。
　相も変わらず不健康そうな隈が濃く浮いた目元をしょぼつかせ、手の甲をぬるつかせ洟[はな]を拭うクロの首を締め上げたくなった朔屋だが、僅かな身じろぎ一つが場を激発させそうで動けなくなる。
source.english:
At the harbor warehouse, when she nearly got sold, and now here: Kuro always managed to blunder at the crucial moment. Why was she so loose at both ends? The sneeze rang through the tavern. Sakuya froze. At his back, the uncanny silence prickled with the fitting of brass knuckles, the snap of switchblades, the metallic cocking of revolvers. Every sound a needle point.
Kuro blinked beneath her ever-present unhealthy shadows and wiped her nose, slicking the back of her hand. He wanted to strangle her. But the slightest movement seemed liable to detonate the room, and he could not move.

target.text: Back when she was almost sold off in that port warehouse, and right now as well, this Kuro girl always seemed to bungle things up at the most critical moments; why oh why did she have to be this slack both above as below─── something poked at Sakuya's back as he stiffened after the sneeze echoed through the bar; from within the ominous silence came the signs of someone fitting on a pair of knuckle dusters, a switchblade sliding out of its sheath, and the sound of a revolver's hammer being cocked, each and every one of them pricking at him like the point of a sword.

Sakuya wanted to strangle Kuro, who was smearing the back of her hands in slimy snot as she wiped off those ever-present, unhealthily dark, heavy bags that surrounded her eyes, but with the situation ready to explode at the slightest provocation, he found himself unable to move even a muscle.

source.japanese:
クロを盾にと抱え上げて攻撃を耐えるなり、その場に放置して自分だけ逃げるなりやり様はいくつかあろうが、そのいずれも選び取れないあたり、朔屋というのは、困っている子供を置き去りにする事も出来ないお人好し、というより要衝での果敢な決断力に欠けているだけである。
　じわりじわりと満ちてくる殺気の潮は血の臭い混じり、バーテンダーはカウンターの中に退避体勢、用意よろしく鉄鍋を被り、朔屋は緊張に耐えかね止まり木を蹴ろうとした。阿波踊りを一差し舞いながら、スウィングドアまで突撃する所存の、気が振れた者の舞い踊りなら、狂気の感染恐れて手加減してくれる者もある筈との、小賢しい猿知恵と評する他ない。
source.english:
He might pick Kuro up as a shield, or leave her there and run alone. Several courses were available. His inability to choose one did not mean Sakuya was too kindhearted to abandon a child in trouble. He simply lacked decisive courage when it mattered.
The murderous tide rising around him carried a smell of blood. Behind the counter, the bartender prepared to take cover, prudently putting an iron pot on his head. Sakuya could no longer bear the tension and was about to kick away from the stool. He intended to dance an Awa dance while charging for the swinging doors. Surely someone would hold back from a madman's dance for fear the madness was contagious. Cleverness worthy of a monkey, and nothing more.

target.text: There were several methods by which he could deal with this situation, like picking Kuro up in his arms and using her as a shield to fend off attacks, or just leaving her behind and running away by himself just to name a few, but given that he chose none of those, Sakuya must have been the sort of goodhearted man who could not simply abandon a child in trouble; it was not so much that, and more that he simply lacked the decisiveness to make bold decisions when it mattered most.

The gathering tide of bloodlust permeating the air was interspersed with the metallic smell of actual blood, and the bartender had taken a stance ready to evacuate below the counter any moment, a prudently prepared iron pot over his head; unable to handle the pressure anymore, Sakuya was about to kick over his bar stool.

His belief that, by charging toward the swing doors while performing a round of the Awa Odori Bon, dancing like someone touched in the head, some would surely stay their hand for fear of being infected by that madness themselves, could only be dismissed as the height of laughably shallow cunning. (TN: The Awa Odori, written "阿波踊り", is a festival with a history spanning centuries originating from Tokushima. It was often referred to as the "狂気踊り" or "狂踊", lit. "madness dance", in the Edo and Meiji periods. The most famous chant goes "The dancers are fools, the watchers are fools; since both are fools, might as well dance!")

source.japanese: もちろん実行しようものなら遠慮どころか良い的と、全身傷だらけにされて踊る踊りは断末魔の舞いと成り果てたところさ、タイミング良くか悪くか、ジュークボックスが次の曲をがなりたて始めた、その曲というのが、どこの馬鹿が選曲したのか、そもそもそんな曲をレコードに吹きこんだ馬鹿があったのか、とにもかくにも『樽を転がせ』であり、その馬鹿陽気な声がまず衆目の気勢を削いで著しい。次いで酒場の片隅で、それまで酔い潰れていた禿頭の老船乗りが歌に誘われ息吹き返し、
source.english: Had he tried it, naturally, they would not have hesitated. They would have found him an excellent target, covered him in wounds, and turned his dance into a death agony. But with good timing or bad, the jukebox began blaring its next tune. What idiot had selected it? For that matter, had some idiot actually recorded it? In any case, it was ‘Roll the Barrel,’ and its foolishly cheerful voice first took a considerable amount of fight out of the crowd. Then, in a corner of the tavern, a bald old sailor who had been passed out revived at the song's invitation.

target.text: Of course, were he to actually attempt to carry this out, then he would not be met with hesitation; on the contrary, he'd be considered the perfect target, his body covered in wounds all over, his dancing degenerating into a shuffle of agonizing death throes. In what could be either good or terrible timing, the jukebox began belting out the next song, and it must have been some idiot who had chosen it───in fact, was there even someone out there stupid enough to record a song like this on a gramophone record───but at any rate, the song playing was 『Roll Out the Barrel』, and that inanely cheerful voice dampened the spirits of more or less all ears present tremendously.
Next, over in a nook of the bar, a bald sailor, who'd been knock-out drunk until then, was lured back to life by the song,

source.japanese:
【禿頭の船乗り】
「亡者の箱まで　もがき上るは一五匹
　いっちょうグイッと　ヨー　ホホー！
　他の連中は酒と悪魔が片付けた
　ヨー　ホホー！　もいっちょグイッと！」
source.english:
“Fifteen men claw up to the dead man's chest—
Yo-ho-ho, and a great big swig!
Drink and the devil have done for the rest—
Yo-ho-ho, and another swig!”

target.text: 【Bald sailor】 「Fifteen men on a dead man's chestー …Yo-ho-ho, and a bottle of rum! Drink and the devil had done for the restー …Yo-ho-ho, and a bottle of rum!」 (TN: While this is the original text to Dead Man's Chest, the sea shanty featured in Treasure Island by Robert Louis Stevenson, the original Japanese here features a liberal translation. It goes as follows: "Fifteen scrambling up a dead man's chest Gulp it all down with a yo-ho-ho! Drink and the devil had done for the rest Yo-ho-ho! And another big gulp!")

source.japanese: と寝覚めと酒焼けの濁声上げてトディーのカップを一煽り、酒場の中には老水夫と壊れ加減のスピーカーの、音の歪んだ合唱が首を斬り落とされた鵞鳥の勢いで縦横無尽に飛び回ったてひとくさり、血気に逸[はや]る者さえ虚を突かれて塑像と化した。
source.english: His sleep-thick, drink-scorched rasp rose, and he tossed back his cup of toddy. For a while, the distorted duet of old sailor and failing speaker hurtled everywhere through the tavern with the energy of a goose whose head had been cut off. Even those eager for blood were caught off guard and turned to statues.

target.text: That was how he awoke, raising his guttural voice left hoarse from the drink, then knocked back the rest of his cup of toddy, and the distorted chorus of sound from the old sailor and broken speaker flew around the bar in any and all directions with the vigour of a decapitated goose; even those full of hot-headed recklessness were caught off guard and turned into plaster statues.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の船乗り】
「ぷっはぁ、あー喉渇いた。
　おう、なんでぇお前ら。黙りこくって。
　そんなに俺様の話が待ち遠しかったんか」
source.english:
“Phaaah! Ah, thirsty.
What's with you lot? All gone quiet.
Couldn't wait to hear my story, eh?”

source.japanese: どうやら潰れる前の話の続きの様子だが、老水夫の場の流れを無視した自意識過剰に酒場の中にたれこめた白けた空気の、ものともせずに話し始めたあたりこの禿頭、相当に神経が太い。
source.english: Apparently he was resuming something from before he passed out. His self-importance, oblivious to the room's mood, spread a flatness through the tavern. He began talking regardless. The bald fellow possessed remarkably thick nerves.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の船乗り】
「あー、どこまで話したっけか？
　そうだ、霧の辺りまでか」
source.english:
“Ah, where was I? Right.
Got as far as the fog.”

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「……しかしよう、
　そんなのありえねえだろう」
source.english:
“…Still,
that's impossible, isn't it?”

source.japanese:
酒場に居合わせた者には、流血沙汰を歓迎しない者もあったのか、他が制止しないうちに入れた半畳で、武器やら殺気やらは収まりつかないながらも勢い失っていったのに、朔屋はくたくたとカウンターに突っ伏しながら安堵の息をついた事である。
　とはいえ睨[にら]みつけてくる眼は変わらず、聞きこみどころではないと、朔屋はクロを一つ小突いてからそっと忍び出ようとしたのだが───
source.english:
Perhaps some customers did not welcome bloodshed. One threw in a heckle before anyone could stop him. The weapons and murderous intent did not quite settle, but their momentum faded. Sakuya slumped against the counter and breathed in relief.
The hostile eyes remained, however. This was no place to ask questions. He gave Kuro a little poke and was about to slip away quietly—

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「一つところでずっと吹き荒れてる嵐なんざ、
　聞いた事もねえぜえ」
source.english:
“Never heard of a storm raging forever
in one spot.”

target.text: 【Bald sailor】 「Pwwaaaahh, aaah, me throat's dry. Hey, what's wrong lads? Quiet as the grave. That eager to hear me tale?」

He seemed about to continue a story he'd been telling before drinking himself into a stupor, but the old mariner's excessive ego made him completely oblivious to the flow in the room, and unfazed by the stifling, spoiled air hanging low in the bar, the bald man began to regale them with his tale once more; he must have had very thick skin.
【Bald sailor】 「Aaahー, how far did I get? Right, to the fog, was it?」
【Bald sailor】 「……Still, ye'd think it impossible.」

Perhaps there were some among those present in the bar who did not welcome bloodshed with open arms; before anyone else could act to stop them, someone threw in a well-timed jeer, and though their weapons remained drawn and the air still thick with bloodlust, the wind had been taken out of their sails, and so Sakuya slumped wearily against the counter while heaving a sigh in relief. With that said, however, the baleful glares sent their way remained, and accepting that this really was not the time to try to gather information, Sakuya poked Kuro, then made to sneak his way outside, but───
【Bald sailor】 「Can't say I'd ever heard the likes of it before, a storm that forever rages on in a single place.」

source.japanese: 朔屋ははっとクロの顔を覗きこんだ。日頃から曇り加減の紅い眸[ひとみ]が、どんより澱[よど]んで覗き返してきただけだった。反応はたっぷり三拍は遅れて、クロがはっと服の裾[すそ]をつかんだ朔屋は、既に脱力感にうなだれていた。
source.english: Sakuya abruptly peered into Kuro's face. Her usually clouded red eyes looked back with a stagnant dullness. Her response came a full three beats late. By the time she caught his hem in sudden realization, his head was already bowed in exhaustion.

target.text: Sakuya peered into Kuro's face with a sudden realization. Her crimson eyes, foggy on a good day, just peered back into his, leaden and gloomy. Her reaction was delayed by at least three beats, and when Kuro abruptly grabbed his sleeve, Sakuya was already hanging his head in deep exhaustion.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「さ、朔屋さん。今、言った。
　嵐のことを言った。
　あの赤毛の人が、嵐。って。
　だから訊きにいかないと」
source.english:
“M-Mr. Sakuya. He just said…
a storm.
The red-haired man said… a storm.
We have to ask him.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「遅いんだよ反応が……それにあっちの愛蘭じゃねえ。
　言ったのはあのハゲ爺さんの方だ」
source.english:
“You're slow to catch on… And not that Irishman.
It was the bald old fellow who said it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だいたい、行ったって俺ら相手じゃまともに口をきいてくれるかどうか。でも幸い、勝手に話してくれるみたいだし、黙って聞いとこうぜ、クロ」
source.english: “Besides, even if we went over, who knows if he'd talk to us? Luckily, he seems ready to talk on his own. Let's just listen quietly, Kuro.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Sa-, Sakuya-san. He just said it. He talked about the storm. That ginger man, the storm. He said. So we have to go ask him.」
【Naomasa】 「That reaction is way too slow…… and it wasn't that Irishman over there. It was that old baldy there who said it.」

【Naomasa】 「And I'm not sure if he's gonna be able to hold a proper conversation with us, even if we go there. But fortunately for us, Kuro, it looks like he'll tell us all on his own, so let's stay quiet and just listen instead.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あ……あい」
source.english: “Ah… y-yes.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「A-……Aye.」

source.japanese: 蝸牛なら引っこむ殻もあろうがカウンターの朔屋とクロは剥き出しの、蛞蝓ばり先ほどよりも更に小さく卑屈に身を縮め、傍にあった英字新聞を目隠しの衝立にして、禿頭の水夫の濁声に聞き入る……。
source.english: A snail would have had a shell to retreat into. Sakuya and Kuro at the counter were exposed like slugs. They shrank smaller and more cravenly than before, using a nearby English-language newspaper as a screen, and listened to the bald sailor's rasp…

target.text: A snail would have a shell it could retract into, but like slugs, Sakuya and Kuro at the counter were completely bare, shrinking in on themselves in a manner much smaller and more grovelling than earlier, using a nearby newspaper in English as a partition to hide from sight, listening attentively to the bald sailor's gravelly voice…….

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「南米の西海岸辺りだと、潮向きと季節風がかち合う海域があって、そこにはまると確かに抜け出せねえ」
source.english: “Off South America's west coast, there are waters where the currents and seasonal winds collide. Get caught there, and you really can't get out.”

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「そういう海域なら、風が吹きやまないように感じられるだろうが……えんえん嵐が止まない海なんて、あるものかね」
source.english: “In a place like that, the wind might seem never to stop… But a sea where a storm keeps going forever? Is there such a thing?”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「……おい若造。てめえみてえな若造なんぞが、このおれに偉そうな口を叩くんじゃねえ。こちとらてめえのちんぽに毛が生える前からの筋金入りよ」
source.english: “…Listen, boy. A youngster like you doesn't get to talk big to me. I was a hardened sailor before you had hair on your cock.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「てめえは銛一つ腕一本でフカとやりあった事があるか？　え？　マゼランの海峡を、何度行き来した事があるんだよ？　ええ？」
source.english: “Ever fought a shark with one harpoon and one arm? Eh? How many times have you crossed the Strait of Magellan? Eh?”

target.text: 【Bald sailor】 「It was somewhere around the western coast of South America, waters where the tidal currents and seasonal winds clash together. If ye get stuck in there, it is a certainty ye will never be getting out again.」
【Sailor in the bar】 「In waters like that, it might feel like the winds never stop blowing, but……there's simply no way there exists anything like a sea where the storm never ends, yeah?」
【Bald sailor】 「……Oi, kiddo. Don't think a brat the likes of ye can start talking a big game to a man like meself. I've been old salt since before the first hairs grew on yer cock.」
【Bald sailor】 「Ye ever wrestled a shark with one arm and a harpoon before, ye little shite? Hm? How many times have ye crossed the Strait of Magellan? Hmm?」

source.japanese: 赤毛の相方の胸板を指先で突つきながらやりこめる、どこまで真実の武勇伝か定かならないが、船乗りはこの手の法螺話の遣り取りには慣れたもので、赤毛の方もまあまあと要領よく宥[なだ]め、トディーのカップを握らせる。ぐいとまた呑み下して、口元の跳ねを拭って、
source.english: He jabbed a finger at the red-haired man's chest as he put him in his place. How much of his prowess was true remained uncertain. Sailors were accustomed to exchanges of tall tales like this, and the redhead placated him efficiently, putting the toddy cup in his hand. Another gulp. He wiped the splashes from his mouth.

target.text: He stabbed his ginger companion in the chest with a fingertip while pressing him verbally, and though it wasn't clear how true to life his tales of heroism at sea were, sailors were used to these kinds of cock-and-bull stories, so with practiced hand, the ginger fellow soothed him with a soft "now now", sliding a cup of toddy into his hand. He knocked it all down once more, wiping the splashes from around his mouth,

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「答えらんなきゃ黙ってな。
　黙って聞いてな、このシャッド様の話をよう」
source.english:
“Can't answer? Shut up,
then. Shut up and listen to the great Shad.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「ありゃあ晩香坡で鮭と蟹を買い付けて、桑港から布哇へ廻って帰るルートだったさ……ぼろい商売、しこたま儲けた後だった」
source.english: “We'd bought salmon and crab in Vancouver. Going back by way of Frisco and Hawaii… Easy business. We'd made a bundle.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「だがその後がいけねえや。『クーガー・キング』はいい船だったが、船長は業晒しでよ。出航前に盲目の乞食をふざけて海に叩き落としやがった、あの罰当たりが」
source.english: “Then it all went wrong. The Cougar King was a fine ship, but the captain was a disgrace. Before we sailed, the damned bastard knocked a blind beggar into the sea for a joke.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「しばらくはなんともなかったが、十日目あたりから霧に祟られた。思えばその霧だって妙だ、季節外れの霧のくせして、妙に粘っこくて濃い、粥みてえだったな」
source.english: “Nothing happened for a while. Around the tenth day, fog began plaguing us. Looking back, that fog was strange in itself. Out of season, and thick and sticky as porridge.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「霧に撒かれてがくんと船足が落ちた───もちろん難船を警戒して速度を落としたんだが、そんだけじゃねえ」
source.english: “Lost in that fog, our speed dropped sharply. Of course we'd slowed down to avoid wrecking, but that wasn't all.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「機関長と一等航海士が言うにゃ、波の様子がおかしいと。
　罐にゃ三割り増しで石炭食わせてるってのに、全然進まねえと。
　こんな海流、聞いた事もねえと」
source.english:
“The chief engineer and chief mate said the waves were wrong.
Feeding the boiler thirty percent more coal, and we weren't getting anywhere.
Never heard of a current like it, they said.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「船長はカンカンになったともよ。海路を決めんなあ船長だ。てめえの仕事にケチつけられた気分だったんだろうさ」
source.english: “The captain was furious, naturally. The captain picks the course. Must've felt they were finding fault with his work.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「進まねえんなら、石炭を五割り増しで罐[かま]にぶちこむんだ、速度をあげろの一点張り、まあ後は豪い騒ぎになったが、そんでもどうにか霧の切れ間が見えた時ゃあ、みんなやんやの喝采だったね」
source.english: “If we weren't moving, put fifty percent more coal in the furnace. Go faster. That's all he'd say. Well, there was one hell of a fuss after that. But when we finally saw a break in the fog, everyone cheered.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「ても、喜んだのも続かねえ。霧の隧道抜けたと思ったら───ありゃあ、二海里もなかった。眼と鼻の先だった───」
source.english: “Didn't stay happy long. Thought we'd come through the fog tunnel—and there it was. Less than two nautical miles away. Right under our noses—”

target.text: 【Bald sailor】 「Answer or shut yer trap. Pipe down and listen to the tale of I, Shad.」
【Bald sailor】 「We'd gone to buy crab and salmon in Vancouver, then went round from 'Cisco to Hawaii, then back home again……was a cushy business, and we'd made a lot of money.」

【Bald sailor】 「But the problems began after. The『Cougar King』was a good ship, that she was, but her captain was a sinner paying his dues to fate. All because he had to go and knock that poor blind beggar into the waters as a little joke before setting out to sea, that accursed fool.」

【Bald sailor】 「Nothing much happened for a while, but around the tenth day, we were haunted by a deep fog. But thinking back on it, that fog was queer, oddly clinging and soupy for an unseasonable fog, like a thick rice gruel.」
【Bald sailor】 「Enveloped in fog, the ship's speed suddenly dropped───of course, wary of running into a shipwreck, we'd slowed down ourselves, but that wasn't all.」

【Bald sailor】 「The chief engineer and the chief mate said that something was off about the waves. Though the boiler had been fed three-tenths more coal, we weren't making any headway, they said. Never afore had they heard of a current like this, they said.」
【Bald sailor】 「Oh, but the captain was furious. He was the one deciding the route. Must have felt like his hard work was being carped at.」

【Bald sailor】 「If we weren't making any headway, then we'd up the amount of coal by five-tenths and toss it all in the firebox, focused on nothing but upping the speed, that man, and, well, all hell broke loose after that, but still, by the time we somehow managed to reach a break in the fog, we all clapped and cheered.」
【Bald sailor】 「But that joy didn't last, for no sooner than it seemed we'd left that tunnel of fog───there it was, not even two nautical miles away. Right in front of our eyes and noses───」

source.japanese: 一息に、ここまで語って息が切れたかぜいぜいごろごろと、老水夫は喉を鳴らして喘[あえ]ぎながら、唇を一湿し、しようとしたトディーのカップは空でお代わりを言いつけようとしたところを、隣の席の水夫が舫の綱でも投げ渡すようにサトウキビのアラックの瓶をば回す。
source.english: Perhaps speaking so long without a pause had exhausted him. The old sailor wheezed and rattled in his throat. He tried to moisten his lips, but the toddy cup was empty. Before he could order more, the sailor beside him passed over a bottle of sugarcane arrack as though tossing him a mooring line.

target.text: Having told the whole story until now in a single breath, he must have run out, for he was wheezing for more, and while clearing his throat, he wet his lips, or tried to, but his cup of toddy was empty, and as he made to order a replacement, the sailor seated next to him passed him a bottle of sugarcane arrack like he was tossing him a mooring rope.

source.japanese: 気づけば耳欹ている他の衆も多く、今も昔も海の怪異譚は船乗り達の良い慰めと言うところ、信天翁号の馬鹿者どもと、制裁にいきりたってくれるよりは遙かに増しだし、朔屋にとっても自分達が求めていた話だ、話の継ぎを待つ。
source.english: By now, plenty of others were listening too. Now as ever, uncanny tales of the sea were a fine comfort to sailors. Far better than their working themselves up to punish the fools from the Albatross. This was also the story Sakuya had come for. He waited for it to continue.

target.text: Before he'd noticed it, a large crowd of others were also pricking up their ears, and it seemed even these days, it remained the case that curious tales of things at sea made a good diversion for sailors; it was, at least, far preferable to them losing their tempers and punishing the fools from the Albatross, and to Sakuya, this was also the very tale they'd come here in search for, and so he waited for the story to continue.

source.japanese: きつい酒精を生のままラッパ飲みに飲み下し、焼けた息を吐き、続きまで誰も茶々を入れなかったのは、酒焼けした声ながら老水夫の声の上げ下げ話の緩急が堂に入ったもので、語りの谷間が実に気を持たせる効果を発揮したからである。
source.english: The old man drank the strong liquor neat from the bottle and exhaled a scorched breath. No one interrupted before he resumed. Drink-burned though his voice was, its rises and falls and the pacing of his tale were masterly; the pauses in his recital held the listeners beautifully in suspense.

target.text: He drank the strong spirits neat, chugging it down straight from the bottle, then let out a burning breath, and the reason nobody interrupted with any silly remarks until he resumed his tale was because, while his voice was hoarse from the drinking, the old sailor was a master of inflections and pacing, the gap in his narration remarkably effective at building suspense.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「船の舳先の向こうに、嵐の壁が広がってたんだ。
　ナニ言ってるかわからねえ？　馬鹿、俺だってわかるか。とにかくそうとしか言い様がねえんだから」
source.english:
“A wall of storm stretched out beyond the bow.
Don't understand what I'm saying? Fool, neither do I. There's just no other way to put it.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「海の他ンとこぁ晴れてんのに、そこだけな膠みてぇな雲がはりついて、煤みてぇに真っ黒なんだよ、それが水平線を隠して端から端まで広がってやがる……おい、嘘じゃねえんだ」
source.english: “Rest of the sea was clear, but clouds were stuck over that one place like glue. Black as soot. Hid the horizon from end to end… I'm not lying.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「笑っちゃったね。それまではなんともなかった、気圧計の水銀が……いや、ちっとばかりは下がっていたかな。でもよそれだって、雨にもならねえような具合だったてぇのに」
source.english: “Had to laugh. The mercury in the barometer had been fine till then… Well, maybe it'd dropped a little. But not enough even for rain.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「それが出てきたとたんにだ、がたんと目盛り振りきって下がったんだから、笑っちゃう」
source.english: “Then the thing appeared, and down it went. Right off the scale. Had to laugh.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「慌てて進路を変えように、今度は舵が利かねえ。霧からは抜けたんだが、クソ海流には嵌ったままだったんだな」
source.english: “We tried to change course in a hurry, but now the helm wouldn't answer. Out of the fog, yes, but still stuck in that damned current.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「後は一直線。
　……ああ、嵐のこたァ、てめぇがなんぼヒヨッコっていったかてわかるな？」
source.english:
“Straight on after that.
Ah, you may be a chick fresh out of the egg, but you know what a storm's like?”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「腹ン中がでんぐり返るみてえな三角波だ。そいつの、エベレストみてえに馬鹿高い天辺まで、押し上げられたかと思えば逆落としよ。キールが阿女っこみてえな悲鳴を上げる、船ン中の螺子止めされてねえもんは、全部転がり落ちる」
source.english: “Steep, peaked waves that feel like your guts are turning somersaults. Up you go to the top, ridiculously high as Everest, then headlong down. The keel screams like a wench. Everything aboard that isn't screwed down tumbles away.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「こんな波が腹からぶち当たれば最後だ、航海士は舵輪にワイヤーで拳固をくくりつける、汽罐焚きは火傷でただれだらけよ」
source.english: “One of those hits you broadside, and it's over. The mate wires his fists to the wheel. The stokers are covered in burns and blisters.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「どこもかしこも水浸し、上甲板は礫[つぶて]みてえな雨、船内は浸水で腰まであっぷあっぷ、鉄管なんざスチーム漏れてねえ奴のが少ねえ。ちょっと気ィ抜きゃ隔壁に叩きつけられあばらが砕ける」
source.english: “Water everywhere. Rain like stones on the upper deck. Flooding waist-deep inside. More pipes leaking steam than not. Let your guard down for a second, and you're smashed against a bulkhead with your ribs broken.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「そんでも中ならまだましで、上甲板なんぞから指令所まで走るだけで、五・六っぺんは最期の覚悟を決めにゃあなんねえ。舷側を越えてくる波に足を取られりゃ、あっという間もなく海にどぼんだからな」
source.english: “Still better inside, though. Just running from the upper deck to the control room, you make your peace with death five or six times. A wave comes over the rail and takes your feet, and you're in the sea before you know it.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「ああ、いっぱしの船乗りなら、こんくらいは誰でも知ってる。だが俺らがぶち当たったなぁ、おめえらが知ってる嵐の……倍はひどかった」
source.english: “Aye, any proper sailor knows that much. But what we hit was twice as bad as any storm you lot know.”

target.text: 【Bald sailor】 「Beyond the bow of the ship, a stormwall stretched out. Ye haven't got a clue what I'm on about? Idiot, like I know meself. Anyways, that's the only way I know to describe it.」

【Bald sailor】 「The rest of the sea was clear as could be, only there did the clouds stick to each other like glue, pitch black as soot, and the damn thing covered the horizon from edge to edge……oi, I'm not fibbing.」

【Bald sailor】 「I laughed. Until then, there'd been no signs of anything of the sort, even the mercury in the barometer was……well, maybe it had dropped a smidgen. But still, it wasn't a big enough fall to promise even a drop of rain.」
【Bald sailor】 「But the moment that showed itself, the mercury crashed all the way to the bottom of the scale, and so I laughed.」
【Bald sailor】 「Panicked, we tried to change course, but this time, the rudder didn't work. We'd gotten free from the fog, but we were still stuck in that godforsaken ocean current.」
【Bald sailor】 「And the rest was a straight shot. ……Aah, do ye have the faintest idea how green ye all are, when it comes to storms?」

【Bald sailor】 「Waves so jagged they would turn yer stomachs inside out. No sooner than those things push ye up their crests, as ridiculously tall as Mount Everest itself, do they send ye hurtling down again. The keel shrieks like a whore, and anything on the ship not secured with screws rolls right off into the sea.」
【Bald sailor】 「If a wave like that slams into yer stomach, it's the end for ye, and the mate ties his clenched fists to the helm with wire, and the stoker is covered in burns.」

【Bald sailor】 「The whole ship's awash, the rain's pelting the top deck like stones, and inside, the flooding's got ye floundering waist-deep, only a scant few iron pipes not leaking steam. Let yer guard down for a moment and ye'll be hurled against the wall, yer ribs cracking.」

【Bald sailor】 「But it's still better being inside, for just running from the deck to the bridge, ye'll have to prepare yerself to meet the Reaper a good five or six times. 'Cause if the waves washing over the broadside sweep ye off yer feet, ye'll plop into the ocean in the blink of an eye.」
【Bald sailor】 「Aah, any sailor worth his salt would know this much. But the one we ran into, she was nothing like the storms ye know of……worse, many times over.」

source.japanese: ごとんと瓶を卓に下ろし、悄然と項垂れた老水夫に、居合わせた者達はそれぞれに経験した嵐を思い出しているのか、沈黙の味が濃く酒場を満たした。気の利いた者がジュークボックスの電源を落とし、今や酒場はこの禿頭の水夫の独壇場となる。
source.english: He set the bottle on the table with a clunk and bowed his head dejectedly. Perhaps each listener was remembering storms of his own. A thick taste of silence filled the tavern. Someone with sense switched off the jukebox. The room now belonged entirely to the bald sailor.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「仲間も何人も死んだし、
　居なくなったよ……。
　どうやって抜けられたんだか、
　ありゃ船魂様の御利益だな。
　それが、六年前の事だ」
source.english:
“Plenty of our mates died.
Others just disappeared…
How we got out, I don't know.
Blessing of the ship's spirit,
that was. Six years ago.”

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「……ああ、あんたが遭った嵐がどんだけひどかったは判った。そいつは疑わねぇよ」
source.english: “…All right. I understand how bad your storm was. I don't doubt that.”

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「でもだからって、その嵐がいつでも同じ地点にあるてぇのは、まだ信じらんねぇ」
source.english: “But I still can't believe it stays in the same spot all the time.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「っけ、おきゃあがれ。言うと思ったぜ。
　一回だけならそうだろうさ。
　だが俺はな、次に行った時も、寸分狂わぬ位置で、同じ嵐に遭遇したんだ」
source.english:
“Bah, shut up. Knew you'd say that. Fair enough if I'd only gone once.
But the next time I went, I met the same storm in exactly the same position.”

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「んな魔物みてえな海に、また行ったってのかあんたは！」
source.english: “You went back to a sea like that? Like some damned monster?”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「おうとも。二ヶ月前だ。俺らの事を聞きつけたんだろうが、頼みこまれたんだ。その嵐ン中になんとしてでも行かにゃなんねえて。ひょろひょろした若いので、調査がどうとか行ってたさ。ありゃどっかの学者先生だな」
