source.english: “Sure did. Two months ago. Someone must've heard about me. Begged me to take him. Had to get into that storm, whatever it took. Skinny young fellow, talking about research. Some sort of scholar.”

target.text: He lowered the bottle to the table with a heavy clonk, and upon witnessing how despondently the old sailor hung his head, perhaps the people present were recalling the storms they'd each experienced, for a heavy silence filled the bar. A considerate fellow turned off the jukebox, for at this point, the bar was this bald mariner's stage alone.

【Bald sailor】 「Several of me comrades died that day, just disappeared……. I know not how I made it through, but it must have been by the divine grace of our ship's guardian deity. All of that happened six years ago.」
【Sailor in the bar】 「……Aye, I understand how terrible the storm you encountered must have been. That much I don't doubt.」
【Sailor in the bar】 「But that doesn't mean that I believe it yet, that this storm always rages in the same place.」

【Bald sailor】 「Keh, that's enough out of ye. I thought ye'd say as much. Maybe ye'd be right, if it only happened once. But see, the next time I went on that route, I encountered the very same storm in the very same place.」
【Sailor in the bar】 「So you actually went back to that monstrous a sea again!?」

【Bald sailor】 「I sure did. Two months ago. He must have heard about us from somewhere, for we were requested specifically by him. Said he had to get inside that storm, no matter the cost. A lanky young lad, talking about some kind of investigation. Must have been some fancy scholar from somewhere.」

source.japanese: クロを抱きかかえた手の動揺が、衝立にと翳[かざ]した新聞紙に伝わって、ざら紙をがさりと鳴らしたけれど、幸い聞きつけた者はおらず、朔屋はクロに目配せを、の、クロはやっぱり口を半開きにしてぽかぁんと、涎まで細い糸に垂らして、切れる寸前まで間がかかってからじゅるりと口内に吸い戻される、ようやく意味が通った。
source.english: The tremor in Sakuya's arms around Kuro reached the newspaper he held up as a screen. The rough paper rustled, but fortunately no one noticed. He glanced meaningfully at her. Kuro, as usual, had her mouth half-open and a blank look on her face. A fine thread of saliva dangled from it. Just before it could break, she slurped it back; at last, the meaning reached her.

target.text: The trembling of his arms embracing Kuro travelled to the newspaper he was holding up as a screen, and the rough paper made a rustling sound, but fortunately, none had their ears directed their way; Sakuya sent a signal to Kuro with his eyes, but, sure enough, Kuro just stood there, staring blankly with her mouth left half open; there was even a slender thread of drool dribbling down, and just when it was on the verge of snapping, she slurped it back into her mouth; at long last, there was comprehension.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
（その学者のひとって。
　あの学者のひと？　死んじゃったひと）
source.english:
(That scholar.
Is he that scholar? The one who died?)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（みたいだな……ほんとに繋がるのかよ、
　止まない嵐とやらと『ザウエル』と）
source.english:
(Looks like it…
So there really is a link between this endless storm and Zauer?)

target.text: 【Kuro】 （This scholar person. Was it that scholar person? The man who died?）
【Naomasa】 （Seems like it……maybe they really are connected, this ceaseless storm or whatever and the『Sauer』)

source.japanese: いよいよ的中引き当てたらしく、朔屋の身の裡[うち]いつになく締まったが、同時に突き当たるのが大難題の、老水夫から肝腎の緯度経度を引き出す算段というのが思いつかない。握らせる金子も交換条件も、船の連中は授けてくれなかった吝嗇の。
source.english: Apparently they had hit the mark at last. Sakuya grew uncommonly alert. But now came the great obstacle: he could think of no way to get the crucial latitude and longitude out of the old sailor. The stingy crew had given him neither money to press into the man's hand nor anything to offer in exchange.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「頭ぁ何度も下げられたし、金もたぁんと積まれた。そして俺にゃ、なにより勇気てぇ奴があった。そんで水先案内をやってやったのよ───そしたら、また同じ海域で同じ嵐に遭遇したのよ」
source.english: “He bowed his head again and again, and piled up plenty of money. Above all, I had courage. So I piloted him there—and hit the same storm in the same waters again.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「ただ、とてもじゃねえが奥までは進めたもんじゃなかった。触りの辺りで引き返してきたが、それだっておめえ、船はがたがたになったぜぇ。言い出しっぺの学者先生だって、いなくなっちまった……波に攫われたか」
source.english: “Couldn't possibly get far inside it, though. Turned back after barely touching the edge, and even that battered the ship to pieces. The scholar who started it all disappeared too… Swept away, maybe.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「驚ぇたのは、波にまぎれて船ン中に投げこまれた真鍮盤でな。
　聞いて驚け、その木っ端ァ、六年前の船の、操舵室の扉に付いてたやつだ。波に扉ごともぎとられたんだ」
source.english:
“What surprised me was a brass plate thrown aboard with the waves.
Get this: that bit of wreckage had been on the wheelhouse door of my ship six years before. A wave tore it off, door and all.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「わかるかおい。六年も嵐に閉じ込められて、同じ海ん中をぐるぐる周りしてたのさ」
source.english: “Understand? Six years trapped in the storm, going round and round in the same sea.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「……嵐から抜け出す前に、雨雲の奥に島みてえな影が見えた気もするが、そいつは見間違いかもしらん。なにしろあんなところに島なんぞねえからな……」
source.english: “…Before we got out, I thought I saw something like an island through the rain clouds. Might've been mistaken. There's no island in a place like that…”

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「やまねえ嵐に、有る筈のない島か……。
　爺さん、あんた話が巧いな。
　すっかりその気にさせられちまったぜ」
source.english:
“An endless storm and an island that shouldn't exist…
You're a fine storyteller,
old man. Had me believing every word.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「まだ言うか若造、てめえみてえなヒヨッコに、海のなにが───」
source.english: “Still at it, boy? What does a chick like you know about the sea—?”

source.japanese:
ここまで話を聞くだけ聞いて、肝腎の位置情報を得ずに戻ったならば、待ち受けるはいったいどんな仕置きか、舳先吊りの極刑、竜骨潜りの懲罰、シサム・キサラが素手にて去勢仕ると待ち受けている事だって有り得ると、集団リンチの難から逃れたところで船の連中が同じくらい恐ろしい。
　陸の酒場と波間の船の上、くたばるなら女の腹の上が良いと願う朔屋には、どちらも避けたい青山の、かといってここにきて聞き出す算段を閃くような、恰好良い男では有り得ない。
　天を仰いだところで目につくのは乗ったり回る扇風機、あれの軸に首つりの縄を掛けたなら、縊死に漏らした糞便を客達の頭上に撒き散らす事になる、せめてそれが意趣返しかと、どこまでも後ろ向きに意識を逸らしていたのが仇となった。
source.english:
If he returned after hearing all this without the vital position, what punishment awaited him? Hanging from the bow? Keelhauling? Sisam and Kisara might even be waiting to castrate him with their bare hands. Escape a mob beating here, and the crew would be just as terrifying.
A tavern ashore or a ship among the waves: neither was the resting place Sakuya wanted. If he had to die, he wanted it to be atop a woman's belly. But he was not the sort of fine fellow who suddenly thought of a clever way to extract the information.
Looking heavenward, he saw only a languid ceiling fan. Hang a noose from its axle, and the filth he released in death would be scattered over the customers' heads. A little revenge, at least? His thoughts fled ever backward. That was his undoing.

target.text: It seemed like they'd finally drawn the winning ticket here, and an usual tenseness spread within Sakuya's body, but at the same time, they'd also run head-first into their greatest challenge, for he couldn't think of a way to draw out the all-important latitude and longitude from this old sailor. The lot from the ship had been too miserly to give him any coin to bribe him with or anything else to exchange for the information.

【Bald sailor】 「How he grovelled, bowing deep again and again, and greased me palms with plenty of cash. But above all, I had the courage to see it through. And so I piloted his ship, I did───and then, I ran into the very same storm in the very same waters once more.」

【Bald sailor】 「Thing is, wasn't any way in hell we could've made it all the way inside. We pulled back just as we made contact, but even that alone, ye hear me, the whole ship was breaking apart. Even the scholar who proposed the whole thing in the first place vanished……swept away by the waves?」

【Bald sailor】 「But what really shocked me, now that was the brass plate tossed up on the ship by the waves. Listen and be amazed, for that sorry thing, it was the very same plate attached to the wheelhouse door on that ship from six years before. The waves had ripped it off, along with the whole damn door.」
【Bald sailor】 「Oi, ye get what I'm saying? It had been trapped inside that storm for six whole years, circling round and round in the same waters.」

【Bald sailor】 「……Before making it out of the storm, I feel like I saw the shadow of something like an island deep within those clouds, but maybe I was seeing things. After all, there are no islands to be found in a place like that……」
【Sailor in the bar】 「An island that shouldn't exist, within a storm that never ceases……. Gramps, you've got a real knack for storytelling. You had me hook, line, and sinker.」
【Bald sailor】 「This again, ye brat, what the hell does a green hand like ye even know about the seas───」

If he'd heard this much of the tale and still returned without managing to obtain the essential information that was the location, just what manner of capital punishment would await him? Maybe being hung from the bow, perhaps a keelhauling, it was even possible that Kisara and Shisamu castrating him with their bare hands was all he had in store, so though he might have escaped a public lynching here at the bar, the crew back at the ship were just as terrifying.

In a bar on land or on a ship floating atop the waves? If he was to perish, Sakuya only hoped it would be on top of a woman's stomach, and so he'd prefer to be spared having either as his final resting place, though with that said, he was certainly not the sort of man cool enough to come up with a plan to extract that information at this point.

A revolving electric fan caught his eye as he looked to the heavens; if they tied a noose to the axle of that thing, all the feces that would leak out of him after being hung from there would scatter and spray all over the heads of the clientele, and at least that would make for some form of revenge; those were the thoughts running through his head, and his relentless refusal to confront reality proved his undoing.

source.japanese:
はっと気づいた時には、腕の中に囲いこんでいた白がいない───
　クロが、とことこと、鰐の口に飛びこむ白兎、とことこと、荒くれ達の間を不器用なジグザグ線で縫って、ちょんと膝をついたのが老水夫の脇で。
　で、もらした台詞というのが───
source.english:
When he noticed, the white figure enclosed in his arms was gone.
Kuro was toddling away, a white rabbit entering a crocodile's mouth, threading a clumsy zigzag through the rough men. She dropped to her knees beside the old sailor.
And what she said was—

target.text: By the time he suddenly realized something was off, the white that had been encircled within his arms was nowhere to be seen─── Kuro, with brisk little steps, like a white rabbit leaping into the mouth of a shark, tap tap, weaved her way past the rough, rowdy crowd with a clumsy zig-zagging, then knelt lightly by the old sailor's side. And the line she uttered was───

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いいなぁ」
source.english: “How nice.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「……あん？　今誰が、なんつった？」
source.english: “…Eh? Who said what?”

source.japanese:
吹けば酒場の梁まで舞い飛び、突けば壁のヌードポスターまで押されていって、どぎつい媚態の金髪裸女の尻の横で叩き潰された蝿と並んでへばりつきそうな、そんなどうしようもないほどちっぽけなクロの、舌っ足らずの一言なのに、空気が軋んで、重力もこの時二倍ほども増したのよう。
　朔屋などは失禁寸前、膀胱を見舞った発作が去らない事には動けそうもないのに、クロはへらへらと続ける、続けてしまう。
source.english:
A breath might have sent her flying to the tavern's beams. A poke might have pushed her all the way to the nude poster on the wall, where she would stick beside a crushed fly by the buttocks of a garishly seductive blonde. Such a hopelessly tiny Kuro, and only one clumsy phrase. Yet the air creaked, and gravity seemed to double.
Sakuya was on the verge of wetting himself. Until the spasm in his bladder passed, he could scarcely move. Kuro, however, continued with her foolish smile. Went right on.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「That's nice.」
【Bald sailor】 「……Hnh? Who just said what?」

Were she blown at, she'd whirl up to the beams under the ceiling; if prodded, she'd be pushed all the way to the nude poster hanging on the wall, sticking to it like the fly squashed right next to the garishly seductive naked blonde lady's buttocks; that was how hopelessly and trivially tiny Kuro was, and at but a single poorly expressed sentence from her lips, the air creaked and grated as though gravity itself had doubled in force this very moment. Sakuya was on the verge of pissing himself, but though he seemed unable to move even a muscle until the spasm seizing his bladder passed, she continued with a foolish smile on her face, Kuro just kept going.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いいなぁ、って思って、言った、です。
　ずっと嵐。すごい、いいなぁ」
source.english:
“Kuro thought it was nice. So… said so.
A storm all the time. So, so nice.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「That's nice, Kuro thought, and said. Always stormy. Amazing, that's nice.」

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「このガキ……白子の、やせっぽちのションベン小娘……知ってるぞ、こいつぁアルバトロスの船長さまだ！」
source.english: “This brat… Scrawny albino piss-girl… I know her. She's the great captain of the Albatross!”

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「おう、噂ァ聞いた事があるぜ。なんでも『嵐を呼ぶ船長』たらいう、えれえ勇ましい通り名の。だがそれがこんな、ションベン臭ぇような小娘か？」
source.english: “Aye, I've heard the rumor. ‘Storm-calling captain,’ some mighty brave name like that. But she's this little piss-smelling girl?”

source.japanese:
【酒場の船乗り】
「流石はあの、船乗りのゴミためだ。こんなのが船長ときた。
　おい船長、さっそく嵐を呼んでみてくれよ、小せえところでいいからさ」
source.english:
“What else from that garbage heap of sailors? This thing's their captain.
Go on, Captain. Call up a storm for us. A little one'll do.”

source.japanese:
やはり朔屋はまだまだ信天翁号では新米で、クロでさえこんな場末に噂として伝わっているのはある意味凄い。赤毛のおどけに空気が割れて、皆どっと笑う、しかし。
　老水夫だけが笑わない、浮かべたのは笑いの代わりにもならない、こめかみ辺りの血の筋で、みりみりとたちまちに。クロの頭蓋骨など一口で半分も噛み割りそうな歯を食いしばり、身を二つ折りに屈める、腕にぶるぶる震えるのは怒り、朔屋はまたしても睾丸が攣[つ]れるほど萎縮するのを感じた。
source.english:
Sakuya was still very much a newcomer to the Albatross. That even Kuro was known by rumor in a backwater like this was impressive in its way. The redhead's joke split the tension, and everyone laughed. But—
The old sailor alone did not laugh. Instead, veins sprang up at his temples, a poor substitute for amusement. He clenched teeth that looked capable of biting away half Kuro's skull and folded himself forward, his arms trembling with rage. Sakuya felt himself shrink again, enough to pull painfully at his testicles.

target.text: 【Sailor in the bar】 「You little shit……an albino chit, and skinny like a bag of bones…… I know her, she's the eminent captain of the Albatross!」

【Sailor in the bar】 「Yeah, heard the rumors about her. I'm told they call her the 『Stormcalling Captain』, a nickname fit for a hero. And you're saying that belongs to a piss-stained little chit like her?」

【Sailor in the bar】 「What else would you expect from a dreg heap of sailors like that? This is all their vaunted captain amounts to. Oi, Captain, call forth a storm for us already, we'll even take a small one.」

Sakuya really was a newcomer on the Albatross after all, for it was, in a certain sense, amazing that rumours of even Kuro had reached a seedy bar this far away. The redhead's witty antics eased up the tense mood, and everybody laughed, but. Only the old sailor did not join in on the laughter, and what surfaced on his face also made a poor substitute; instantly, veins around his temples creaked from the surging pressure. He clenched his teeth, maw so large that he could crush half of Kuro's skull in a single bite, his body was bent over, almost folded in half, his arms trembling with rage, and once again, Sakuya felt his testicles crawl so deep inside his body they cramped.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「おい……嬢ちゃん。まだ俺が優しいうちにもいちど訊いといてやる。いってえ、なにが『いい』んだよ……？」
source.english: “Listen… little girl. I'll ask you one more time while I'm still being kind. What exactly is ‘nice’…?”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「船長はクソだったが、『クーガー・キング』はいい船だった。それがあの後は、スクリュウはぶち折れ、キールだって幾つもひびが入って、廃船にするしかなかった」
source.english: “The captain was shit, but the Cougar King was a fine ship. Afterward, her screw was broken, her keel cracked in several places. Had to scrap her.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「いなくなっちまった奴ン中にゃ、俺の朋輩だってあったんだ……いい奴だったよ。船もトモダチも台無しにした嵐の、なにがいいんだって……？」
source.english: “One of those who disappeared was my friend… A good man. What's nice about a storm that ruined my ship and my friends…?”

target.text: 【Bald sailor】 「Oi……little missy. I'll ask one more time while I'm still feeling kind. What. The hell. Is so "nice" about any of that……?」

【Bald sailor】 「The captain was a piece of shit, but the『Cougar King』was a fine ship. And after all that, the screw was bent and broken, there were several cracks in the keel, and she had to be scrapped.」

【Bald sailor】 「And some of the people who disappeared that day, I called them comrade……they were good men. So what are ye trying to say is so nice about this storm that ruined the ship and me comrades both……?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だって───」
source.english: “Because—”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Because───」

source.japanese: 漏らしそうでも垂らしそうでもとにかくと、朔屋は止まり木から降りざま身を床に投げ出して、出来うる限りの低い体勢の匍匐前進、机の隧道を潜[くぐ]り半ズボンの毛ずねや筋骨逞[たくま]しいデニムの足の林をこいで、肘や膝が擦れて汚れだらけになるのも厭[いと]わずクロの元まで辿り着き、小声で叱咤したのだけれども。
source.english: Whether he leaked or not, something had to be done. Sakuya came off his stool and threw himself to the floor, crawling as low as he could. Through tunnels under tables, through a forest of hairy shins in shorts and powerful legs in denim. He did not care that his elbows and knees were scraped and filthy. He reached Kuro and rebuked her in a whisper.

target.text: Regardless of if he would drip or leak, just as Sakuya got off the bar stool, he threw himself on the ground, crawled forwards on his stomach as low to the floor as possible, slithered under the table tunnels and pushed through the thicket of hairy shins in shorts and burly legs clad in denim, and while he loathed the unpleasant sensation of his elbows and knees being scraped and covered in filth, he still made it to Kuro's side; for all that he tried to scold her with a whisper, however.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（おい、クロ、やめとけって……！）
source.english: (Hey, Kuro. Stop it…!)

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （Oi, Kuro, stop that……!）

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロ、嵐になると、ちゃんとなる。
　なるから、嵐、ずっとあるのがいい。
　あるのがいいから、
　ずっとの嵐は、いいなぁ」
source.english:
“When there's a storm, Kuro can do things right.
So… a storm all the time would be good.
It would be good, so…
a storm that never ends would be nice.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「こんクソ餓鬼ゃあ……船がクソなら、乗ってる奴も餓鬼までクソにたかる蛆か」
source.english: “You little shit… Ship's shit, and everyone aboard, even the brats, are maggots on it.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro, when it storms, becomes right. Since Kuro becomes right, it's nice, if it always storms. Because Kuro wants it to always storm, an always storm is nice.」
【Bald sailor】 「Ye shithead of a brat……if the ship's a piece of shit, then all the people on board, brats and all, must be the maggots swarming that shit.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ね、おじいさん、聞かせてもっと。
　どこに行けばあるのか、クロに教えてな。
　あ。お礼もいいます。
　クロ、ありがとうのクロです」
source.english:
“Please, Grandpa, tell Kuro more.
Tell Kuro where to go. Oh.
Kuro'll say thank you, too.
Kuro's a thank-you Kuro.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だからおじいさん、
　ずっとの嵐はどこ───」
source.english:
“So, Grandpa,
where's that never-ending storm—?”

source.japanese:
ああクロよ、老水夫に敵意のない事示す為に、微笑み造ったつもりが例によってぎこちなく媚びる上目遣いとなっているクロよ、一つ事を前にするとその一つ以外は見えなくなるクロよ、もう少しだけでいい、お前の頭の容量が広かったなら！
　朔屋の制止を容れる余地なく、クロはただただ止まない嵐の事を知りたくって、哀願の、それしか考えられていない。
source.english:
Ah, Kuro. Trying to smile to show the old sailor you meant no harm, and producing, as usual, an awkward, ingratiating upward glance. Kuro, who could see nothing else once a single thing occupied her. If only your head had a little more room!
No space remained for Sakuya's warning. Kuro wanted only to know about the storm that never stopped. She pleaded, incapable of thinking of anything else.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「うるせえ───
　うるせえうるせえ、黙れ白っ子が！
　嵐に遭いたいなんざ、なにが船乗りだぁ！」
source.english:
“Shut up—shut up,
shut up, you white little brat!
What sort of sailor wants to meet a storm!?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Hey, old man, tell Kuro, more. Where to go to find it, tell Kuro. Ah. Will say thanks, too. Kuro, is a thanking Kuro.」
【Kuro】 「So please, old man, where is the always storm───」

Alas, O Kuro, you tried to put on a forced smile to show the old sailor that you meant no harm, but as ever, it came out as an awkward, fawning look from beneath your lashes; O Kuro, faced with one thing, all else becomes invisible to you; O Kuro, if only your brain was blessed with more capacity, even just a little more would be enough! Left with no room to spare to heed Sakuya's attempt to stop her, Kuro simply wanted to know about the ceaseless storm, and all she could think of was pleading him for it.
【Bald sailor】 「Shut up─── Shut up, shut up, SHUT IT YE ALBINO! What in the fuck kind of sailor WANTS to run into a storm!?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「え……だってクロ。ちゃんとしてないと、いつもみんなが馬鹿、言うの。だからちゃんとしたいから、クロ、嵐が来ないと」
source.english: “But… when Kuro can't do things right, everyone calls Kuro stupid. Kuro wants to do things right. So Kuro needs a storm…”

source.japanese: 老水夫の罵声が弾けても、彼女としては珍しく懸命に食い下がる。
source.english: Even when the old sailor's abuse burst out, she persisted with an earnestness rare in her.

source.japanese:
それは日頃何かというと軽んじられ、皆から愚鈍に扱われているクロの、切なる願いではあったろう。
　しかしそういうお祈りは、お星さまの下で一人天に訴えればいいのであって、もちろん聞き入れられる事など星辰が変わるまで待っても有り得ないだろうが、星空は願いを容れてくれずとも綺麗だし、流れ星の一つくらいは見せてくれるかも知れない。
source.english:
It was surely Kuro's desperate wish, born of being constantly belittled and treated as a dullard by everyone.
But a prayer like that ought to be made alone beneath the stars, appealing to heaven. It would never be granted, of course, even if she waited until the constellations changed. Yet the starry sky was beautiful, whether it accepted wishes or not. It might show her a shooting star or two.

source.japanese:
ところがここはさあどこだ。信天翁号に大して敵意を燃やす者達が集う場末の船員酒場で、訴える相手は天のカミサマと言うより地獄の獄卒めいた老水夫、お祈りの作法からして完全に間違っている。
　嵐から命からがら生還してきた相手に、嵐を願う言を吐くなど、火薬庫で尻の穴に煙草を差した鼠を放つに等しい。可哀相なのは尻を痛めつけられる鼠である。ろくでもない言を吐いたクロではない。
　その証拠に、禿頭の水夫がにゅういと猿臂を伸ばし、起重機はだしの膂力で締めあげながらクロを小脇に抱えこんだ時、誰もこの白子の少女を哀れと想う者など一人だになきぞ哀しき。
source.english:
But where, pray tell, were they? In a seedy dockside tavern packed with people burning hatred for the Albatross; and the god to whom Kuro offered her prayer was an old sailor more infernal gaoler than heavenly deity. She had mistaken the entire rite.
To tell a man who had barely survived a storm that storms were desirable was like releasing into a powder magazine a mouse with a lit cigarette stuck up its ass. The pitiable party here was the mouse whose backside had been abused, not Kuro, who had said the unforgivable thing.
Proof: when the bald sailor shot out his long ape arm and clamped Kuro under it with strength that put a crane to shame, not one soul present pitied the albino girl. A tragedy indeed.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uh……because, if Kuro isn't right, then everybody else always calls Kuro stupid. So because Kuro wants to become right, then Kuro, has to have a storm.」
Even as the loud insults erupted out from the old sailor, she, quite uncharacteristically, eagerly persisted.

This must have been a heartfelt desire deep within Kuro, she who was always looked down upon at any opportunity, treated like an imbecile by everyone around her. But those sorts of prayers were better offered to the heavens as one stood by their lonesome beneath the stars, and though should you wait for even the celestial bodies themselves to change, it would likely still be impossible for the prayer to be granted, even if the starry skies would not grant us our wishes, they still made a beautiful sight, and perhaps they might even present to you a shooting star for your viewing pleasure.

However, let's see, where exactly was she again? A seedy bar where men burning with the flames of animosity towards the Albatross gather, the person she pleaded with was an old mariner who looked more like one of Hell's gaolers than our Father who art in Heaven, and even her prayer etiquette was completely incorrect. To utter words expressing desire for a storm to a man who just barely scraped through one with his life intact was no different than releasing a rat with a cigarette shoved up its bum into a warehouse full of explosives. The one to be pitied here is the rat whose rear end is being abused. Not Kuro spewing her worthless nonsense.

As a testament to that, when this bald mariner smoothly extended his long, monkey-like arms, then lifted Kuro by her armpits while squeezing with a strength that could put a crane to shame, not even a single person felt so much as a hint of pity for this albino. Ah, what cruel tragedy.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「まだ言うかッ！　クソ餓鬼、船乗りにゃ言って良い事悪い事あるも知らねえか。餓鬼だろうがなんだろうが、ちょっとでも船に乗ったなら───クソがぁ!!」
source.english: “Still at it! You little shit—don't you know there are things one says to a sailor and things one does not? Brat or no brat, once you've set foot aboard a ship—damn you!”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「大人をな、なめんじゃねえぞ餓鬼───こうだぁ！」
source.english: “Don't take a grown man lightly, brat—take this!”

target.text: 【Bald sailor】 「And ye still yap on about that! Ye little shithead, it don't seem like ye know what kinda things are right and wrong for a sailor to say. I don't care if ye're a little chit or not, if ye've ever stepped foot on a ship in yer life───damn it all!!」
【Bald sailor】 「Don't take the piss with us grownups, ye stupid brat───take THIS!」

source.japanese:
レギンスを引きずり下ろされ露わにされた、笑えてしまうくらいに肉の薄いクロの、白い、粘土の切れ端のような尻。
　たかだかと振り翳[かざ]された掌は、捕手のグローブのように分厚く大きく、怒りの熱が輪郭に沿って空気を歪め、目を背[そむ]けたくなるほど残酷で。
　残酷な力は、そのまま、振り下ろされた。
　クロの小さな尻の上で、爆発した。
source.english:
Her leggings were dragged down, exposing Kuro's white backside—so meager as to be almost laughable, like a scrap of clay.
The palm raised high above her was thick and broad as a catcher's mitt; the heat of its anger warped the air along its outline, so cruel a sight that one wanted to look away.
That cruel force fell.
It exploded against Kuro's little backside.

target.text: As her leggings were pulled down, Kuro's laughably bony butt, pasty white like a piece of clay, was exposed to the world. Swung high and held aloft was a palm, thick and large as a catcher's mitt, and the heat of his anger distorted the air around its contour, making so brutally cruel a sight it left you wanting to avert your eyes. That cruel power, just like that, was swung downwards without hesitation. Atop Kuro's little butt, it exploded.

source.japanese:
尻打ち据え、ばあんと爆ぜた音は、酒場の脂に曇った窓硝子を空気伝いに細く震動させたほど。床に身を投げ出したままの朔屋の鼓膜にさえ痛いくらいに響いたのに、直撃を受けたクロは。
　着弾の衝撃で、白くうねる髪がふわりと浮き上がり、羽根が地に落ちるように収まる。クロの鼻から短く詰まった息が押し出され、唇は小さく窄[すぼ]められ、見る間に頬が膨らんだのは体内の空気が衝撃に噴き出してきたせいか。
source.english:
The blow burst against her backside with a crack loud enough to send a fine tremor through the tavern’s grease-clouded windowpanes. It rang painfully even in Sakuya’s eardrums where he lay sprawled on the floor. And Kuro had taken it point-blank.
The impact lifted her billowing white hair; it floated down again like a feather settling to earth. A short, choked breath burst from her nose. Her lips pursed, and before their eyes her cheeks began to swell—had the blow driven the very air from her body up into them?

source.japanese:
ただその顔も眼差しもきょとんとして、自分の身に何が生じたのかまだ把握しきれない様子の、そこで小さな破裂音で唇から頬の空気が抜ける。
　見ているだけでたまらない一拍を置いて、紅い眼が見開かれていく、眼球零れんばかりに見開かれていく。
source.english:
Her face and eyes remained blank, as if she still couldn’t grasp what had happened; then, with a small pop, the air in her cheeks escaped through her lips.
After a heart-stopping pause—unbearable to watch—her red eyes widened, opening so wide that her eyeballs seemed ready to pop out.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Nffhh……!?」

She was struck so hard on her butt, the sound of the explosive clap travelled through the air and made the bar's windows cloudy with grease tremble minutely. It rung out so loudly it even hurt Sakuya's eardrums, the man still flat on the floor, but what, then, of Kuro, who had received the hit directly? The impact from the strike sent her billowing white hair floating gently into the air, and then it settled like feathers falling to the ground. A small, choked breath was pushed out of Kuro's nose, her lips puckered, and the way her cheeks puffed up before his eyes was perhaps a result of the air within her gushing out from the impact?

But the look in her eyes was dazed, her expression stupefied; she didn't seem to yet have grasped what had actually happened to her own person, and with a small, plosive sound, the air in her cheeks left her mouth. After a moment where even looking at her was unbearable, her crimson eyes opened wide, so wide it looked like her eyeballs might well fall out of their sockets.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「え。あ。クロ、いけないこと。
　言ってな……ぃひぃぃんんんっ!?」
source.english:
“Huh? Oh.
Kuro didn’t say anything bad… eeeehhhhhh!?”

source.japanese: 体幹貫いたのが激痛だとようやく認識したように、語尾も遅れて悲鳴に上擦る。
source.english: Only now did she seem to recognize the agony that had driven through her core; a beat late, the end of her sentence climbed into a scream.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「こうだ！」
source.english: “Like this!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uh. Ah. Kuro, bad thing. Didn't say……anythIINNGGH!?」
As though she'd finally grown aware of the intense pain piercing her core, the end of her sentence grew shrill with a belated scream.
【Bald sailor】 「AND THIS!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いたぁいいいっ！」
source.english: “Ow, that hurts!”

source.japanese:
禿頭の水夫の容赦ない事、大の男でさえ一発で音を上げそうな打擲を、続ける事になんら躊躇いなく、また平手が炸裂する。
　白く腰のない猫毛の髪が舞う、ついでにキャミソールの繊維に潜[もぐ]りこんだ埃まで叩き出されてこちらも白く薄い小さな煙を上げる、その衝撃たるやいかばかりか───
source.english:
The bald sailor showed no mercy. Without the slightest hesitation he continued a beating that would have made even a grown man cry surrender after one blow. Another open hand exploded.
Kuro's fine white hair, limp as a cat's, flew up; even the dust buried in the fibers of her camisole was beaten free, raising a little pale cloud. Such was the force of the impact—

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「口の聞き方ぁ、叩きこんでくれらぁ！」
source.english: “I’ll beat some manners into you!”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「っあ、あ～～～っっ！」
source.english: “Ah, aaahhh!!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あー……ちょっとちょっとおっさん、
　このコ、おつむがちょっとその、可哀相なヤツなんだ。あまり目くじら立てんでやってくれないか」
source.english:
“Ah… Hey, hey, old man,
this kid’s a little, um, slow on the uptake. Could you go easy on her?”

source.japanese:
喉が裂けて血が滴るような悲鳴が惨めで哀れだ。
　朔屋も遂にこらえかねて起き上がり、老水夫の腕を留めようと、卓越しに手を伸ばしたところで取り巻きどもに押さえつけられた、ばかりか。
source.english:
Her scream was wretched and pitiful, as though her throat had split and blood were dripping from it.

Her white hair, wispy like the fur of a cat, fluttered through the air, and even the dust lurking within the fibres of her camisole was beaten out in passing, it, too, forming a thin, small cloud of white smoke; how violent an impact it must have been───

target.text: She had no idea what she'd done wrong; he wouldn't tell her, and so she continued to apologize without knowing why, but not even this was she permitted, simply beaten over and over───Kuro. The albino girl of the Albatross.

Why were the smiles she made so servile, why did she always look through her lashes as though fawning on others? Because no matter how warmly she believed herself to be smiling, she had never once been met with kindness in turn. Why were her eyes covered in circles of such pronounced darkness, rings of black that never disappeared? Because so many tears had been squeezed out of them, day in and day out, as though wringing a sponge.

Why did the girl always hide or play by her lonesome in the shadows? Because any time she would carelessly show herself in front of others or make a thoughtless comment, even if the girl had no ill intentions, it would be interpreted uncharitably and she would be harshly berated for it.
Even Sakuya had at last reached comprehension. After being constantly subjected to such horrible treatment, anyone would end up like this.

source.japanese: 彼自身、普段クロを軽んじているところがないとは言えないにしても、外部から言われるとなるとむかっ腹。ただそれは必ずしもクロへの同情というのではなく、憎んでいようが呪っていようがひとまずは朔屋の陣地である信天翁号という領域を踏みにじられた思いした為であったが、青年の矮小な怒りなど、背後から浴びせかけられた拳骨に敢え無く封じこまれる。しかも酒場の船乗り達の拳骨は、朔屋を伸す為でなく痛みに苦しめる為のもので、一発一発は軽かったが指の節を尖らせ急所外して痛み長びかせる嗜虐的な、そんなのが小刻みに矢継ぎ早に後頭部背中肩口二の腕一面に降り注いでは、まともに言い返す事も難しい。

The young man's paltry anger was quickly stifled by fists from behind. The tavern sailors did not mean to knock him senseless; they meant to hurt him. Each blow was light, but sadistically placed: knuckles thrust out, vital points avoided, the pain deliberately prolonged. In quick succession they rained over the back of his head, his back, shoulders, and upper arms, making any coherent reply impossible.

Though he couldn't claim that he himself didn't usually look down on Kuro, when some outsider did it, his temper flared. Even the hand Sakuya extended, unable to bear the sight any longer, was pulled back, accompanied by mockery, unable to reach her.
【Naomasa】 「Wait, please, I said wait. No matter what, this is definitely going way too far. She's gonna die───nh!」
【Sailor in the bar】 「Shut up, you're just as guilty. So? Should we wrap you in a bamboo mat and see if you sink, hmm?」

At some point, the old sailor, Kuro, and Sakuya had been surrounded by the clientele of the bar, a large group forming a ring around them; the bar had become a crowd of faces, faces, more faces, sneering, painted over in jeering voices, voices, more voices, as though space-time itself had begun to warp. And amidst that, the silhouettes of the old sailor continuing the spanking with his arm swung high and the bar patrons goading him on deformed in a queer manner, like the frenzied dancing of the legendary circus troupe of madmen said to perform at midnight, into a squishy, wobbling smear.
The scene flowed away───
Sakuya's consciousness grew hazy───

source.japanese:
【声】
「───なにをそんなに、いきりたっていらっしゃるの？」
source.english: “What has you all so terribly worked up?”

source.japanese: 男達の濁って歪んだ罵声の中で声は、たっぷり蜜を含んで甘い───たとえそれが毒の蜜であったとしても。狂騒に浮かされた熱気の中でドレスが飾り石の軌跡を残光と曳いて、艶麗に流れて留まるが老水夫の半身へ。紫紺の色合いは夕に花弁を拡げる花のように涼やかに、かつ底知れぬ深みを湛えて女の豊麗な肢体を際立たせていた。
source.english: Amid the men's murky, distorted abuse, the voice was sweet with honey—even if it was poisoned honey. Through the feverish tumult a dress flowed exquisitely, its ornamental stones trailing afterimages, and came to rest beside the old sailor. Deep violet, cool as a flower opening its petals at evening, yet fathomlessly rich, it accentuated the woman's sumptuous figure.

target.text: 【Voice】 「───Whatever could have brought you to lose your temper so?」

From within the indistinct, warped voices of the men came a voice filled with sweetest nectar───poisonous though that nectar may be. The semi-precious stones of her dress trailed with a glittering afterglow through the air hot with their frenzied excitement, flowing with a dazzling beauty before coming to a stop by the old mariner's side. The hue of indigo was clear as a flower unfolding its petals in the evening glow, filled with an unfathomable depth that only served to highlight the voluptuous shape of this woman's body.

source.japanese:
水夫長と共に別口で動いているはずの、泪だった。
　ただの一言で場の流れを完全に横攫[さら]いにし、男達の眼など釘付けの、この女には造作もないことの。
source.english:
Rui. She was supposed to be attending to other business with the boatswain.
One phrase had snatched away the entire current of the room and nailed every man's eyes to her. For this woman, nothing could have been easier.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「……なんだあんた、
　どこの奥様───うむ!?」
source.english:
“…Who the hell are you?
Some fine lady—mmph!?”

target.text: It was the woman who was supposed to be working on a separate matter with the Bosun, Rui. With just a few words, she had completely captured the attention of the entire place; keeping the eyes of men glued to her was child's play for this woman.
【Bald sailor】 「……And who are ye, somebody's wife or───hmmff!?」

source.japanese: 毒気を抜かれ、威嚇も忘れ、虚けた声で誰何の老水夫の口に泪はおもむろに、緩慢なくせして逃れようのない身のこなしで、唇、を、重ねる。
source.english: The old sailor’s venom drained away, his threats forgotten, his voice hollow as he asked who she was. Rui—slowly yet inescapably—pressed her lips against his.

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「んん!?　んむっ？　む、む……」
source.english: “Hmm!? Mmm? Mm, mm…”

source.japanese:
熟しきった肢体の曲線を、巧みに老水夫の筋骨の輪郭にぴたりと密着させ、口づけは深く、情熱的な蛇、誘い、貪り、反応に喜ばしげに答え、深く、かつ深く舌と舌とを絡ませ合う様と粘質な音は、眺めているだけで股ぐらをまさぐられるかのよう。
　実際、酒場の客のうち、お堅そうなの助平そうなの、若いの年取ったの取り混ぜて、何人かがオーノゥオーノゥと声を上擦らせながら、股間を押さえて転がり回った。傍にいるだけで当てられたものと見える。
　初めは眼を白黒させていた老水夫も、すぐに目を欲情に曇らせ、押しのけようとしていた腕は抱擁に代わり、泪にぐいぐい股間を押しつけるまでとなり、長く、肺活量の限界に挑戦すると言わんばかりに唇と舌との淫戯は果てしなく長く続くかに思われたが、それでもしまいに泪は顔を離した。
source.english:
She fitted every ripe curve of her body expertly to the old sailor’s muscular frame. The kiss went deep—a passionate serpent, coaxing and devouring, answering his response with evident delight; deeper, still deeper, their tongues entwined, and the sight of it, together with those wet, viscous sounds, was like being fondled between the legs.
Indeed, several patrons—the straitlaced and the lecherous, young and old alike—clutched their groins and rolled about the floor, their voices breaking into cries of “Oh no, oh no!” Mere proximity appeared to have overcome them.
The old sailor’s eyes, rolling white at first, soon filmed with lust. The arms that had tried to push her away became an embrace; presently he was grinding his crotch hard against Rui. The obscene sport of lips and tongues seemed likely to go on forever, as though the pair meant to test the limits of their lungs. At long last, however, Rui drew her face away.

target.text: The wind taken from his sails, even his blustering threats forgotten, with movements at once measured and yet not allowing him any escape, Rui took the old sailor's lips, which had inquired into her identity with a hollow voice, and covered them. With her own lips.
【Bald sailor】 「NNH!? Nmm? Mh, mh……」

Pressing the rich curves of her body at the peak of ripeness against him, she masterfully melded into the outline of the old sailor's muscle and bone, and with deep kisses, like a passionate snake, she seduced, devoured, answered his reactions joyfully, and as their tongues entwined deeper, yet deeper, the sticky noises their union produced seemed to almost physically grope around the crotches of those witnessing it. At first, the old man's eyes had been darting about in confusion, but now they, too, were clouded in a haze of desire, the arms trying to push her away now pulling her into an embrace instead, even going so far as to vigorously rub his crotch against Rui, and for a long time, this continued, the sexual foreplay of their lips and tongues seemed to never end, dragging on as though they were putting the limits of their lung capacity to the test, but eventually, Rui pulled her face away from his.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───ふぅ───
　素敵よ、あなた」
source.english:
“Phew…
You're wonderful.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「な……なんだ……あんたいきなり……。
　どっかで……会った……か？」
source.english:
“Wh… what… you… all of a sudden…
Have we… met… somewhere before?”

source.japanese:
つい先程までは怒りに鉄の芯が通ったような老水夫の肉体も、今やなりだけ立派な革袋、くなくなと張りを失い、クロを腕から取りこぼす、とさりと。
　落ちた音は乾いた笑いが漏れてしまうくらいに軽々として、床に散り敷かれた白髪も丸めて捨てた花紙の山のように寒々しい。顔から落ちたにもかかわらず、クロはぴくりともしなかった。
source.english:
Moments before, the old sailor's body had seemed to contain an iron core of rage. Now it was merely an impressive-looking leather sack, all tension gone. Kuro slipped from his arm and landed with a soft thump.
The sound was light enough to draw a dry laugh; her white hair lay scattered over the floor, bleak as a heap of crumpled tissues. Though she had fallen face-first, Kuro did not twitch.

target.text: 【Rui】 「───Fuh─── You are magnificent, dear.」
【Bald sailor】 「Wh-……what's with ye…… all of a sudden……. Have we……met……somewhere before?」

Even the old sailor's body, which until a moment ago seemed to have an iron core of anger, was now nothing but an imposing leather sack; it went limp, lost all tension, and Kuro tumbled out from his arms with a thump. With a sound of falling to the floor so light and dry that it might well coax a snort from any who heard it, even her hair strewn about on the floor was as bleak as a pile of crumbled-up tissue paper. Despite falling face-first, Kuro did not so much as twitch.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それにとっても逞[たくま]しいのね。
　けれども、少しお疲れみたい。
　息でわかります」
source.english:
“And so powerfully built.
But you seem a little tired.
I can tell by your breathing.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「And you're so strong and manly. However, you seem a little tired. I can tell from your breathing.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「なにかお飲み物でも入れて、少し休憩なさらないと。ご一緒いたしますわ」
source.english: “Why don’t you pour yourself a drink and take a little break? I’ll join you.”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「つったってあんた……」
source.english: “Even so, you…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I simply must insist you have something to drink and take a small break. I shall accompany you.」
【Bald sailor】 「Ye can't just……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしが一緒では、お厭[いや]……？」
source.english: “Do you mind… if I come along?”

source.japanese:
【禿頭の水夫】
「いやそうは言わねえが」
source.english: “Well, I wouldn’t exactly put it that way…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Would my company displease you……?」
【Bald sailor】 「No, I didn't say that, but-」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そう───あなた、嬉しい。
　それならゆっくり、ね。
　お二階の方がよろしいかしら？」
source.english:
“I see—I’m glad to hear that. In that case,
let’s take our time.
Would you prefer to go upstairs?”

source.japanese: 朔屋は唐突な泪の登場と、彼女の相手を選ばぬ淫蕩振りに魂引き攫[さら]われ虚脱して、クロの安否もぼんやりと遠い。
source.english: Rui's sudden appearance and indiscriminate lust had snatched away Sakuya's soul and left him limp; even concern for Kuro receded into a vague distance.

source.japanese:
泪は老水夫の胸板に、乳房でもってしなだれながら誘ったその言葉、何を意味しているのか判らないものはこの場におらず、なにより彼女の媚態は木石であろうと奔走させそうに淫らがましい。
　だから、泪が背後に腕を回した時も、誰も彼女のしなの一つとして見逃したし、それくらい床に伸びたクロへとすいと振ってみせた指の先にまで女の色香が満ちていた。朔屋だけが、その直前の秘やかな目配せを辛うじて掬[すく]いとっていたから、泪の意図に勘づいて、戒めの腕から身を捩って逃れ出る。
source.english:
Not a soul present could mistake the meaning of Rui's invitation as she pressed her breasts against the old sailor's chest; her manner was lewd enough to set wood and stone themselves running after her.
Thus, when Rui slipped an arm behind her back, everyone dismissed it as one more coquettish gesture. Even the fingertip she flicked lightly toward Kuro on the floor seemed steeped in feminine allure. Sakuya alone caught the swift secret glance that preceded it. Understanding her intent, he twisted free of the arms restraining him.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Is that so───very glad to hear it, dear. Then let us take our time, yes? Would the second floor suit you better?」

After Rui's sudden entrance, Sakuya was left completely despondent, his soul snatched from his body by her utterly indiscriminate, licentious behaviour, and the well-being of Kuro seemed a vague, distant concern.

While leaning languidly against the old sailor's chest, her breasts pressing into him, Rui whispered those sweet words of seduction; not a single soul in this place was unaware of the meaning behind them, and more than anything, this woman's coquetry was so obscene, it was enough to make even the most unfeeling man of stone run wild with passion.

So when Rui slung her arm around his back, everyone dismissed it as just another of her many small gestures; so possessed of a feminine sensuality was this woman that even the tip of her finger, pointing towards Kuro stretched out on the floor, was brimming with it. Sakuya alone barely managed to catch the secretive glance she had sent him just before that, and picking up on Rui's intention, with a twist of his body, he escaped the arms confining him.

source.japanese: クロをいじましいほど軽い体を抱き上げて肩に担ぎ、逃げるが一目散、扉へと、泪が通ったなりに男達は道を開けたままだったから、その隙間を縫うて店の外へと転び出る。
source.english: He hoisted Kuro's pitifully light body onto his shoulder and fled headlong for the door. The men still stood parted where Rui had passed; he wove through the gap and tumbled out of the tavern.

target.text: He picked up Kuro's pitifully light body from the ground and slung her over his shoulder, running away as fast as his legs would take him, towards the door; the path Rui had trod between the men was still left wide open, and so he weaved his way down that gap and stumbled out of the establishment.

source.japanese: 疾走にクロを肩にぽんぽん跳ね上げつ、追っ手を恐れて振り向けば、窓硝子越しに窺えたのが老水夫と腕を絡めて二階に上がっていく泪の姿の、なんともはや話が早い、段取りに慣れている。酒場男達はみな一様に立ち竦み、中には覗くつもりか二階へ上がっていく者もあったが、朔屋達を追いかけてくる者はいなかった。そういえば押さえつけられているところから逃れた時だって男達の腕に力なく、泪は彼女にしかできないやり方で、男達をいっぺんに無力化してみせたのであった。
source.english:
He ran flat out, Kuro bouncing on his shoulder. Fearing pursuit, he glanced back through the window and saw Rui going upstairs arm in arm with the old sailor. Admirably quick; thoroughly practiced.
The men in the tavern stood rooted. Some even started upstairs, perhaps intending to peep, but no one pursued Sakuya and Kuro. Come to think of it, their arms had already gone slack when he tore free. In a fashion possible to her alone, Rui had rendered every man there powerless at once.

target.text: Kuro bounced up and down on his shoulder while he sprinted away, and when he looked back in fear of pursuers, he caught a glimpse of Rui's figure ascending to the second floor through a windowpane, her arms linked with the old sailor's, awfully quick to move things along, experienced with the process. The other men in the bar stood motionless one as all, and though some among them made to move up the stairs, perhaps intending to sneak a peek, there were none who came in pursuit of Sakuya and Kuro. Come to think of it, there had been no real strength left in the men's arms when he had escaped from their grasp, so Rui, in a way only she could, had managed to instantly render all the men powerless at once.

source.japanese: ───船内食堂には豚脂の匂い芳しく漂い、厨房係の下級水夫が調理器具を使う音が夕食を告げる心地よい騒がしさだったが、朔屋は長机に上半身預け、食欲も忘れてぐったりと───食い気どころではない。波止場の片隅に信天翁号の出鱈目な船影が見えてきた時、うっかり安堵で啜[すす]り泣いてしまったのが朔屋にとっては大いなる不覚、ただそうさせてしまうくらいクロを担いでの全力疾走は彼を疲労困憊させていた。……といっても、意識を失い重心が掴みにくかったとはいえ、クロの軽さを考えれば、朔屋の体力の無さは嘆かわしいのに変わりないのであるが。
source.english: The ship's mess hall smelled pleasantly of lard. From the galley came the junior cook's utensils, a comfortable clatter announcing dinner. Sakuya lay with his upper body across the long table, limp, his appetite forgotten. Eating was the last thing on his mind. When the Albatross's preposterous silhouette had appeared in a corner of the quay, he had inadvertently sobbed in relief. A humiliating lapse. Running flat out with Kuro on his shoulder had exhausted him enough for that. Though, unconscious and difficult to balance as she had been, given her lightness, his lack of stamina remained lamentable.

source.japanese: そして草臥れきっていようがいまいが、水夫長は安定して朔屋に容赦がなかった。
source.english: Exhausted or not, Sakuya could count on the boatswain's lack of mercy.

target.text: ───The savoury scent of lard wafted through the ship's messroom, and the sound of the deck boy in charge of the galley using the cookware made for a comfortable commotion that marked the advent of dinner, but Sakuya was leaning his upper body against the long table, hunger forgotten and completely languid───he was in no mood to eat. That he, the moment he caught sight of the Albatross' disorganized mess of a silhouette in a corner of the wharf, had inadvertently burst into tears of relief, was a great defeat in Sakuya's eyes, but that was simply how utterly spent he'd been after sprinting with all his might while carrying Kuro over his shoulder.

……With that said, though she was unconscious, which had made it harder to locate her center of gravity, when taking Kuro's lightness into consideration, Sakuya's lack of stamina remained as lamentable as ever.
And then, regardless of how exhausted he seemed or not, the Bosun still remained consistently merciless when it came to Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……じゃあ結局、聞き出してきたなぁ泪女史の方か。こいつ等はやっぱり役立たずか。
　っけ！　とことん使えねぇ……」
source.english:
“…So in the end, Madam Rui got the information. These two were useless after all.
Bah! Utterly good for nothing…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そりゃあないでしょうよ水夫長。
　ほんとに聞き込みしたいんなら、クロなんかつけてよこす方がおかしい───ぎゃあ！」
source.english:
“That's not fair, Bosun.
If you really wanted someone to ask questions, sending Kuro along was the mistake—ow!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……So, in the end, it was Miss Rui who got the info out of him? So you two really were no help after all? Keh! Useless to the last……」
【Naomasa】 「Now that's not quite fair, Bosun. If you really wanted to get that info out of him, then what were you thinking sending Kuro of all people with me to───GYAH!」

source.japanese:
結局、老水夫から問題の海域の位置情報を探り出してきたのは泪であり、痛めつけられたクロの他は空手で戻ってきた朔屋が無能である事、これは替えようのない事実である。
　それでもひどすぎると、のっそりともたげ、水夫長に抗議の頭はすぐさま拳叩きつけられ、また机に突っ伏す事になる。
source.english:
In the end, Rui had extracted the location of the waters in question from the old sailor. Sakuya had returned empty-handed, apart from the injured Kuro. His incompetence was an unalterable fact.
Still, it was too much. He slowly raised his head to protest, only to have the boatswain's fist strike it and send him face-down onto the table again.

target.text: Ultimately, Rui was the one who had managed to extract the location of the waters they sought from the old mariner, and Sakuya, who, the tormented Kuro aside, had returned empty-handed, was incompetent; these were the immutable facts. Still, it was just too cruel of him, and he slowly raised his head to say as much, but any ideas of protest were quickly beaten down by the Bosun's fist, and he was once again left splayed out across the table.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そんで、クロは」
source.english: “And Kuro?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「部屋で寝込んでますよう……尻ぃ腫[は]れ上がってるし、熱まで出てきて」
source.english: “In bed in her room… Her backside's swollen, and she's got a fever now too.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So, what about Kuro?」
【Naomasa】 「Laid up in her cabin, fast asleep…… her butt's all swollen, and she's even got a fever.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ほんとうに口は災いのもと。おっかない事」
source.english: “A loose tongue really is asking for trouble. How frightening.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しかし泪さん、あなた、あの後なにをしてきた。
　どうやって聞き出してきた。
　あのハゲ親爺、えれえ依怙地になってたのに」
source.english:
“But, Rui. What did you do afterward?
How did you get it out of him?
That bald old fellow was being awfully stubborn.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Silence truly is golden, lest your mouth be the source of disaster. What a frightful thing.」
【Naomasa】 「But Rui-san, what did you even do after that? How did you get the info out of him? That bald coot had really dug his heels in.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そお？　とっても話のわかる殿方だったわ。
　少し訊ねただけで、すぐに教えて下さったもの」
source.english:
“Was he? I found him a most reasonable gentleman.
I asked a little, and he told me at once.”

source.japanese: 泪は昨夜に遅れること数時間後、彼が水夫長にがみがみと罵りつけられているところに悠然と戻ってきて、疲れきった朔屋とは裏腹に至極快調で、肌などはなにやら生命の精髄でも浴びたかに艶[つや]やかさを増して、ただ様子だけを見るならば朔屋の方がよっぽどの難事業に揉まれてきたようだが、成果を掴んできたのは女客の方。青年のやった事など空騒ぎでしかないという。
source.english: Rui had returned several hours later, strolling in while the boatswain was berating him. In contrast to the exhausted young man, she was in excellent spirits. Her skin had acquired a fresh luster, as though she had bathed in the essence of life. Judging by their appearances, Sakuya seemed to have endured the more difficult undertaking. But it was the female passenger who had brought back results. His efforts amounted to nothing but a pointless fuss.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……話のわかる、って。
　少し訊ねただけ、って」
source.english:
“…Reasonable.
You asked a little.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Really now? He was a very reasonable gentleman with me. I only had to inquire about a few things before he promptly told me all.」

Yesterday, while the Bosun was berating and scolding him, Rui had leisurely returned several hours after his arrival, and in stark contrast to the exhausted Sakuya, she was in an exceedingly good mood, her lustrous skin even glossier than before, as though she had been showered in the essence of life itself; judging from their condition alone, it was Sakuya who appeared to have faced a much more strenuous undertaking, but the female passenger was the one who had achieved the results. As if to say that all the young man had done was make a big fuss about nothing.
【Naomasa】 「……Reasonable, you say. A few inquiries, you say.」

source.japanese: 色々と追求したいところではあったが、爪の様子などをのんびり確かめている彼女にそれ以上聞けば薮蛇をつつき出しそうだったので、やっぱり朔屋はだらしなく長机に伸びるしかなかった───
source.english: There were any number of questions he wanted to press. But Rui was leisurely inspecting her nails, and asking more seemed likely to stir up something better left alone. Sakuya could only sprawl feebly across the long table again—

target.text: There were several parts of her explanation that he'd love to pursue a little further, but posing any more questions to this woman, who was inspecting the state of her nails in a carefree manner, seemed like it would just be stirring up a hornet's nest, so in the end, all Sakuya did was stretch his body limply out across the long table───

source.japanese:
なお例の禿頭の老水夫は、泪との一時を過ごした後、妙に腰に力が入らない様子でふらふらヤサまで戻った姿を目撃されたのを最後に、変死を遂げているところを発見された。
　その死に様は、内側から鍵のかかった密室で、喉を鋭利な爪のようなもので斬り裂かれての失血死、室内には陸の上なのにもかかわらず異様なまでの魚臭さが充満し、死骸やベッドには正体不明の鱗[うろこ]が散らばっていたという、顔の長い神経症の作家がものした怪奇小説紛いの死であったとかなんだとか。
source.english:
As for the bald old sailor, after spending that time with Rui, he was last seen tottering home, his hips oddly unsteady. Later he was found dead under mysterious circumstances.
In a room locked from inside, his throat had been slit by something like sharp claws, and he had bled to death. Though on land, the room was filled with an extraordinary fishy smell. Unidentified scales lay scattered over the corpse and bed. A death straight out of a horror tale by that long-faced, neurotic writer, or so they said.

target.text: Furthermore, after spending some time with Rui, the aforementioned old sailor was last seen alive staggering back home with a queer lack of strength in his lower back, and he was later discovered having died in a most unnatural of ways. The manner in which he died was, supposedly, as follows: Within a closed room locked from the inside, he died from loss of blood after his throat had been cut to shreds by something like sharp nails, and despite being on land, the room was so pungent with the stench of fish it reached the bizarre, the corpse and the bed both littered with unidentifiable scales: it was a death reminiscent of a supernatural horror novel penned by some long-faced, neurotic writer.

source.japanese:
機関室の闇はただ暗がりという以上に、濃厚な漆が蟠っているかの稠密な粘度を有しており、扉を開けても外から光差しこまず、むしろ通路へ向かってとろとろと床を伝って流れ出すのではとさえ。
　闇の密度は距離感を奪う。暗がりの奥の曲軸の駆動音は遙か彼方から空間を渡ってくるとも感じられたし、機関室の奥行きは船体の半ば以上を占めている事も有り得た。
　主罐から漏れる火明かりや室内各部の赤色灯が闇の中に点々々、アクセントの様に配されてあるが、それらは明るく照らし出すというより、闇の向こうから覗きこむ獣の眸[まなこ]めいている。
source.english:
The engine room's darkness was more than an absence of light. It had a dense viscosity, as if thick lacquer lay coiled within. Opening the door did not seem to let light in. Rather, the darkness might flow slowly out along the floor into the passage.
Its density robbed one of any sense of distance. The sound of the crankshaft working deep within seemed to travel across space from somewhere far away. The engine room might have occupied more than half the hull's length.
Firelight escaping the main boiler and the red lamps about the room dotted the dark like accents. But they did not so much illuminate it as resemble the eyes of beasts peering out from beyond.

source.japanese: と、こうどうにも陰に籠もった連想を催させるのは、室内に籠もった温気が思考を鈍くさせるからだろう。無造作に下履きのゴムに手を掛け、尻を丸出しに剥いてやりつつ、朔屋も機関室の温気に頭の中に重苦しさを覚えていた。
source.english: That the mind should run to such persistently gloomy fancies was likely the doing of the heat pent up in the room, dulling thought. Casually catching hold of the waistband and stripping the buttocks bare, Sakuya too felt the engine room’s heat settling like lead inside his skull.

source.japanese: といって朔屋が暑苦しさのあまりにトチ狂って下半身をさらけ出し、尻踊りを披露したわけではない生憎ながら。朔屋がずり下ろしたのはクロのレギンスであり、もしも青年が独り機関室の中で尻を出して喜ぶ癖があるのなら、彼が幼児期になにか深刻な心的外傷を負った可能性を危惧してやるべきだが、信天翁号の白子の少女の尻をぷりんと剥いてやるのならば孤独な一人遊びではないので全く安心なのである。
source.english: That did not mean Sakuya had gone mad from the oppressive heat, bared his own lower half, and begun performing a dance of the buttocks—unfortunately. The leggings he had pulled down belonged to Kuro. Had the young man possessed a habit of baring his backside for solitary pleasure in the engine room, one might reasonably fear some grave childhood trauma. target.text: The Stygian dark of the engine room was not mere darkness; endowed with a thick viscosity as though coated in a rich East-Asian lacquer, were one to open the door, no light would shine in from the outside; on the contrary, it even seemed to instead slither across the floor towards the passageway like a thick syrup, flowing back outside. The intensity of the dark robbed man of his sense of distance. It felt like the sound of the crankshafts working away in the depths of the darkness had only arrived here after crossing the heavens from somewhere far in the beyond, and it was quite possible that the depth of the engine room occupied more than half the length of the ship's hull.

The embers spilling out from the main boiler and the red lamps within the room lit up the dark like tiny, scattered pinpricks of light, arranged like accent pieces, but rather than illuminating the room, they seemed more akin to the eyes of savage beasts peering out from within the dark.

But what incited such suggestive associations of things lurking unseen in shadowy realms was probably a consequence of the humid air that filled the room and dulled the faculties of all present. While casually hooking his fingers into the elastic waistband of a pair of underwear and stripping an ass bare for the world to see, Sakuya also felt the stifling sultriness of the engine room filling his head.

What Sakuya was sliding off was Kuro's leggings; supposing the young man did have a peculiar habit of finding joy in sticking out his ass by himself in the engine room, then we ought to have been worried about the possibility that he had suffered some manner of grave psychological trauma in his formative years, but given that he was instead stripping bare the ass of the albino girl from the Albatross, freed from its coverings with a little wobble, this was no solitary activity to entertain himself, and so we can remain completely at ease.

source.japanese:

　クロと向かい合うと、どうしても小動物を構いつけるように接してしまい、彼女が一応とはいえ女の子である事を忘れてしまいがちになるのである。
source.english:
Taking grateful advantage of the darkness to hide where he was looking, Sakuya turned his face away from Kuro. Only afterward, red to the ears, did he realize that he had very nearly failed to stop at a fingertip: like a man bending his mouth to the rim of a teacup brimful of shochu, he had been on the point of putting his lips to the corner of Kuro’s eye and sucking the tears away. What in heaven’s name had he almost done to this scrawny little girl? Had he set about it from the first with the oily gusto of a man bent on fooling around with a woman, he might at least have been spared quite this much embarrassment.
Face-to-face with Kuro, he could not help treating her as one fusses over some small animal, and was forever forgetting that, technically speaking, she was a girl.

source.japanese:
さて湿布を剥がしてやると、じわじわ立ちのぼって朔屋の鼻面を覆うのが機関室の温気に増した熱の、これは真っ赤に腫[は]れ上がったクロの尻から発せられる体熱である。
　先だって緬甸の安酒場で惨たらしい折檻を喰らってから数日がたったが、腫れは一向に収まらずその間クロは座る事はおろか歩行もへっぴり腰のよちよち歩きを強いられた。折檻を受けたその晩などはひどい熱を発して譫妄状態に陥り、船内通路を這いずり回っているところを下級水夫の一人に発見され、彼に絶叫上げさせるに至った。その下級水夫を怯懦と誹[そし]るなかれ。船内通路は陽が落ちると、亡霊徘徊しそうな廃工場めいた相を呈するその中を、正体をなくしたクロが、襤褸けたキャミソール一つで（下半身はなにも履いていられないほど熱を持ち腫[は]れ上がっていた）這いずっている様は、想像するだに不気味と言おうか慄然と迫る異様があったろう。
source.english:
Once Sakuya peeled away the compress, another wave of heat rose through the engine room's swelter and washed over his face. It came from Kuro's buttocks, swollen a furious red.
Several days had passed since the savage punishment at that Burmese dive, yet the swelling showed no sign of subsiding. In all that time Kuro had been unable to sit, or even to walk except in a tottering waddle with her backside thrust out. On the night of the beating she had run a high fever and fallen delirious. A junior sailor found her crawling through the ship's passageways, and the sight made him scream.
Do not call that junior sailor a coward. After sunset, those passageways resembled an abandoned factory where ghosts might roam. Kuro, senseless, crawling through them in a single tattered camisole—nothing below the waist because the swelling burned too fiercely to bear clothing—must have made a ghastly, chilling sight.

source.japanese: 下級水夫が語るらく、巨大な尺取り虫、それも繭になり損ねた芋虫が出現したかと思ったと。なるほど、クロの白髪はまとまり損なった繭の糸にも見えたろうし、キャミソールの色褪せた桃色などは繭の中で蕩けかかった肉色にも映ったろう。江戸川乱歩も驚愕すべし、である。
source.english: According to the junior sailor, it looked as if a giant inchworm—one that had failed to form a cocoon—had appeared. Kuro’s white hair looked like the threads of a cocoon that had failed to take shape, and the faded peach of her camisole like the color of flesh beginning to melt inside one. Even Edogawa Ranpo would be astonished.

target.text: With the darkness thankfully concealing his gaze, Sakuya turned his face away from Kuro. In truth, he had actually not intended to settle for just using his fingers; he had been moving his mouth towards her as though he was greeting the rim of a teacup filled to the brim with cheap, potent shochu, as if about to place his lips by Kuro's eye and slurp up her tears, and Sakuya's face grew hot with shame when he realized as much after the fact, and he wondered just what the hell kind of mistake he was about to be guilty of making with a girl this scrawny. If his intent from the start was simply to have some sleazy fun with a woman, then he would not have been nearly this embarrassed.

Whenever he was face to face with Kuro, he couldn't help but end up treating her like he was looking after a small animal, and he found it all too easy to forget that she was, technically, a young woman.

Now then, having peeled off the patches, what was it that slowly rose up to cover Sakuya's nose, adding heat to the already sultry air of the engine room? It was the body heat emitted from Kuro's bright-red, swollen buttocks. It had been several days since she had been on the receiving end of that atrocious spanking in that cheap bar in Burma, but during those days, the swelling showed no signs of abating, so while sitting was naturally out of the question, she had even been forced to walk with a toddling, hesitant gait.

That night when she'd received the spanking, she broke into a dreadful fever and fell into a delirious state, and while creeping about through the passageways, she was discovered by a lone deck boy, and the sight made him howl in terror. But slander not that deck boy as a spineless coward.

Once the sun sets, the passageways of the ship assume an appearance reminiscent of an abandoned factory where spectres seem like to prowl, and therein was Kuro, bereft of her senses, wearing but a single tattered camisole (the swollen skin was so hot that she could not stand to wear anything on the lower half of her body); simply imagining it was so bizarre it could well be called eerie, perhaps even horrifying.

As the deck boy told it, he though that a giant inchworm had emerged, or perhaps a caterpillar unable to fully form a cocoon. Indeed, Kuro's white hair could be seen as resembling the threads of a cocoon that had not managed to form correctly, and the faded peach pink of her camisole must have taken on the appearance of the hues of the dissolving flesh within the cocoon. Even Edogawa Ranpo would be astonished, certainly. (TN: Edogawa Ranpo was the father of the modern crime novel in Japan. This is a reference to one of his short stories by the name "芋虫", lit. "The Caterpillar", both reviled and renowned for its dark, ero guro subject matter.)

source.japanese: 主罐の灼熱光に目をやられた後ではかえって湿布の交換に手間取ったが、機関長には文句も言えず黙々と貼り替える。真実親切心から出た行為なのかも知れないし、直接的な暴力を行使する水夫長とは異なって、洗練された紳士然としていながらもどこかしら畏いところがある機関長に賢しらな文句が叩けるほど、朔屋は覚悟が定まっていない。加えて仕事の途中だったという引け目も手伝った。
source.english: After the main boiler's glare blinded him, replacing the plaster took longer than before. Still, Sakuya could not complain to the chief engineer and worked in silence. Perhaps the man had acted from genuine kindness. Unlike the boatswain, with his direct violence, the engineer remained a polished gentleman—yet there was something fearsome in him all the same, and Sakuya lacked the nerve for clever objections. Besides, he was conscious of having interrupted his assigned work.

source.japanese: そもそも朔屋とクロはただ尻の手当の為だけにこんな暗がりでもぞもぞやりに来たのではない。先日の『止まない嵐』の情報を探り損ねた、命じられた仕事を満足にこなせなかった罰として、機関室での雑用を言いつけられたのだった。
source.english: Sakuya and Kuro had not come to fumble about in this darkness merely to tend her backside. As punishment for failing to learn about the ‘storm that never ends,’ for failing to carry out their assigned job satisfactorily, they had been set to odd jobs in the engine room.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しかし水夫長もひでぇよな……。
　クロがどうにか動き回れるようになったと思ったら、すぐに罰当番ときた」
source.english:
“The boatswain's a bastard, though…
Kuro can barely get about again, and straight away he puts her on punishment duty.”

source.japanese: ぼやきを吐けば、吸う息で機関室の温気が腹に溜まっていく、この温度も朔屋を温く倦怠に誘い、拭き掃除の、ウエスと布巾を使う手を鈍らせる。
source.english: He grumbled, then breathed in the engine room's warmth until it seemed to fill his belly. The heat drew him into a tepid lassitude, slowing his hands as he wiped things down with rags and cleaning cloths.

target.text: And so he concisely described the incident that took place in the cheap bar in Burma. Clad in black, the Chief Engineer still wore his dark glasses even in this gloom, and though one might worry that his vision would be far darker, it seemed that Sakuya fumbling with his hands in the shadows was perfectly visible to him, but it appeared less like something inexplicable and more like something distinctive to this man.

It actually ended up taking even longer to change out the patches after having his retinas scorched by the burning light from the main boiler, but he did not issue any complaints to the Chief Engineer and instead settled for applying the patches in silence. The action could have been taken with genuine kindness in mind, and unlike the Bosun, who would resort to direct violence, while this Chief Engineer acted like a refined gentlemen, there was still something intimidating about him, and so Sakuya had yet to muster the resolve to make any cheeky complains to him. Moreover, the bit of guilt he felt because he was in the middle of working only made matters worse.

It was not the case that Sakuya and Kuro were squirming about in this dark a place just to treat her sore buttocks. They had failed to obtain information on『The Ceaseless Storm』 the other day, and as punishment for failing to adequately complete their assigned task, they had been ordered to do chores in the engine room.
【Naomasa】 「But the Bosun is just awful……. As soon as it looked like Kuro was finally able to move around again, she was immediately given a punishment watch.」

As he let out his grumbling complaints, the sultriness of the engine room accumulated within him, and the temperature lulled Sakuya into a lukewarm fatigue, dulling the motions of his hands wiping things clean with a rag and dishcloth.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ふむ……つまり君は、この部屋での仕事は避けたいと。それなら石炭室に紹介しようか。
　あすこは常に人手不足だからね」
source.english:
“Hm… So you would prefer not to work in this room? Shall I recommend you to the coal room, then?
They're always short-handed there.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いい!?　機関長、そいつぁご勘弁を」
source.english: “What!? Chief, please—not that!”

source.japanese:
石炭室や、石炭で満タンの倉庫方面での作業は船内の誰もが嫌う重労働の、朔屋も幾度か駆り出されたけれど、積み込みや運び出しの無限とも思える繰り返しの果てに得たものと言えば、折れそうなくらいに軋む背骨や手足の骨、時折悪夢となって寝床に忍びこむ煤粉の記憶である。
　マスクは着けていたものの、それでも解放されてしばらくは爆発的な咳が収まらず、喉からも鼻からも、痰を通り越して糊状に凝[こご]った煤の塊で手巾が台無しになった。
　今のクロにそんな苦役を負わせたならば、なにかの弾みでよろめいただけでそれが命取り、石炭の山に生き埋めとなって船霊様の仲間入りをした事だろう。陸の屋敷神にはオシラサマというのがあるが、船霊オクロサマでは語呂の悪さいかんともし難い。
source.english:
Work in the coal room and the holds packed with coal was backbreaking labor hated by everyone aboard. Sakuya had been pressed into it more than once. After the seemingly endless loading and hauling, all he had to show for it were bones that creaked as though ready to snap and memories of coal dust that sometimes crept into his berth as nightmares.
He had worn a mask, but even after they released him, the explosive coughing would not stop. What came from his throat and nose went beyond phlegm: clots of soot congealed into paste and ruined his handkerchief.
Put Kuro through such labor in her present condition, and the slightest stumble might kill her. Buried alive beneath a mountain of coal, she would join the company of the ship spirits. Ashore there was a household god called Oshira-sama. But a ship spirit called O-Kuro-sama? There was no saving the sound of it.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Humm……In other words, you are saying that you wish to avoid working in this room. In that case, how about I introduce you to the coal bunkers? They always suffer from a shortage of hands down there, you see.」
【Naomasa】 「EEK!? Chief Engineer, please, have mercy on me!」

Working in the coal bunker, down at the storage compartments filled with coal, was heavy labour despised by all hands on the ship; Sakuya had been forced to participate in the work down there several times already, but all he could be said to have obtained at the end of what felt like an infinitely repeating cycle of loading and transporting was a creaking in his spine and limbs that felt as if they were about to snap, not to mention memories of crawling around on a floor covered in soot that would occasionally revisit him in his nightmares.

He had been wearing a mask, but after being released from his duties, the violent coughing would still not cease, and the paste-like, congealed lumps of soot coming from his throat and nose, which far surpassed the likes of ordinary phlegm, also ruined his handkerchief. If Kuro were to bear the burden of such toils in her current state, then, if, by some chance, she were to stumble over, that would be the fatal blow, and she'd surely end up buried beneath a mountain of coal, joining the ranks of the ship's guardian spirits.

While the yashikigami on land count Oshira-sama among their ranks, for a kami enshrined on a ship, the name Okuro-sama is unfortunate-sounding in a way that is hard to reconcile with. (TN: Some layers of wordplay, with Oshira, written "御白", meaning white, and Okuro, written "御黒", meaning black, the "O" of "御" being an honorific prefix, and the "黒" being both the black of the coal and read identically to Kuro's name. Oshira-sama is a real yashikigami, a type of god enshrined near human dwellings, worshipped as a kami of farms and silkworms. Okuro, however, has a name that is a little gloomy for a guardian spirit.)

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「そうですか……それでは、差し渡し一フィートくらいの大皿に、こう緑豆を山盛りにしてだね、それを箸で一つ一つ摘んで別の皿に移すんです。空になった元の皿に戻す。それを一日繰り返す」
source.english: “I see… Then take a large plate, about a foot across, and pile it high with mung beans. Pick them up with chopsticks, one at a time, and move them to another plate. Then return them to the first, now empty. Repeat that all day.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……参考に窺うんですが、それはなんのどういう仕事で？」
source.english: “…Just so I know, what sort of job is that, exactly?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「If you insist……in that case, you will pile up mung beans like so on a large plate roughly one foot in diameter, and then you will pick them up, one by one, with chopsticks and move them to a different plate. Then you shall return them to the plate you just emptied. You will repeat this for the entire day.」
【Naomasa】 「……I'm asking for future reference here, but what kind of work is that even supposed to be?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「いいやそれは仕事ではなく、単なるレクリエーションだ。これを一日続けた後部屋から出ると、世界の全てが輝いて見えるようになる」
source.english: “No, it isn't a job. Simply recreation. After doing it for a day, leave the room, and the entire world will appear to shine.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Oh no, it's not work at all, just simple recreation. Having repeated this for a full day, once you leave the room, the whole world will seem radiant in your eyes.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ま、しばらくは豆料理を見るだけでも、顔面チックの発作に襲われてしまうようになるが」
source.english: “Though for a while, the mere sight of a bean dish will bring on a fit of facial twitching.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……機関長、この朔屋、誠心誠意機関室の清掃に努めさせていただきます！」
source.english: “…Chief, I, Sakuya, shall devote myself heart and soul to cleaning your engine room!”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Well, for a time, just the mere sight of a bean dish will be enough to trigger a facial tic.」
【Naomasa】 「……Chief Engineer. I, Sakuya, will pour my heart and soul into cleaning this engine room!」

source.japanese:
朔屋はああぼやいてみたけれど、水夫長の言いつけはもしや彼なりの温情ではなかったと考え直す事にした。水夫長が本気で罰をくれるつもりなら、機関長の言ったように、二人を機関室と続きの石炭室に送りこんだ事だろうの、そちらは船底の煉獄に等しい空間なのだ。
　引き換え機関室は、機関長が己の領分として日頃から弛まず知行しており、実のところ、朔屋やクロなどの不器用者が手を出せるような雑仕事など大して残されていない。
source.english:
For all his grumbling, Sakuya decided that perhaps the boatswain's orders had been a kindness of sorts. Had he truly meant to punish them, he would have sent them, as the engineer suggested, into the coal room adjoining the engine room—the purgatory at the ship's bottom.
The engine room, by contrast, was the chief engineer's own domain, governed by him with unremitting care. In truth, few odd jobs remained for bunglers like Sakuya and Kuro to lay hands on.

source.japanese:
この今だって、仕事と言っても配管各所の計測器の油汚れを拭って落とす程度の、船の中では軽作業の部類。
　なのに。クロにやらせると拭いても拭いてもメーターの硝子盤に油汚れが伸びるばかりで、いっかな綺麗になりやしない。
　だからクロは大いに狼狽えた。狼狽えて余計に必死になった。必死になればなるほど汚れはひどくなって、しまいにクロは困り果ててぺたんと腰を落とし、途端にひんと悲鳴を詰まらせ目を剥いた。
　尻はどれだけ分厚く膨れていようとも、腫れているかぎりは尻当てになるどころか痛みの素でしかない訳で、そんな尻で迂闊に座るからそうなる。
source.english:
Even now, their work amounted to wiping oily grime from the gauges along the pipes. Light work, by shipboard standards.
Yet when Kuro did it, every wipe merely spread the grease over the glass. It never got cleaner.
Kuro panicked. Panic made her more desperate. The harder she tried, the worse the dirt became. At last, utterly at a loss, she dropped onto her backside—and choked off a squeal, eyes wide.
However thickly swollen it was, swelling made her backside a source of pain, not a cushion. That was what came of sitting down carelessly on it.

target.text: Sakuya might have grumbled like that, but then he reassessed the Bosun's orders, wondering if they couldn't have been his way of being considerate. Had the Bosun truly intended to punish them, then just like the Chief Engineer had mentioned earlier, he'd surely have dispatched them to the coal bunker adjoining the engine room, a space equivalent to the purgatory of the bottom of this ship. In contrast, the engine room was ruled by the Chief Engineer as his own domain, and he always carried out his duties without slack, and in fact, there were hardly any chores left of the sort that clumsy bunglers like Sakuya and Kuro could be trusted to handle.

Even right now, though it was work, it was as simple as wiping off oil stains from the measuring instruments found around the piping, the sort classed as light-duty work on a ship. And yet. When Kuro did it, no matter how she wiped and wiped, the oily grime was just smeared across the glass panels of the meters, never becoming clean.

So Kuro was greatly flustered. And being flustered only made her all the more frantic. And the more frantic she became, the worse the stains became, and finally, at her wits' end, Kuro fell flat on her butt, stifling a shriek as soon as she hit the floor, her eyes shooting wide open. It mattered not how thickly engorged her buttocks were: for as long as they were swollen, they wouldn't function as a cushion, no, on the contrary, they would only bring her pain; that's what happens when you carelessly sit down with your buttocks in such a state.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああクロクロ。
　お前ね、ウエスを後に使ったって、汚れが広がるばかりだろ」
source.english:
“Ah, Kuro, Kuro.
If you use the rag afterward, all you'll do is spread the dirt.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Aah, Kuro, Kuro. Listen, if you use the rag last, then you'll just end up getting the grime everywhere.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まず先にウエスを使って、そのあとで布巾で拭き取る。段取り守んなきゃあ」
source.english: “Rag first, then wipe it off with the cloth. You've got to do it in the right order.”

source.japanese: クロの両手を取って教えこんでやる朔屋は、はて自分はこんなに面倒見の良い奴だったか知らんと顎に拳を当て思案顔の、微妙な渋さ。
source.english: Sakuya took both her hands and showed her how. Had he always been so attentive to others? He rested a fist against his chin and considered the question with faintly dubious solemnity.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「First, start with the rag, then wipe it off with the dishcloth after. Gotta do it in the right order.」

Taking both of Kuro's hands in one of his and teaching her how to do it right, Sakuya wondered, unsure if he truly was this kind and helpful a man at the end of the day, resting his other fist on his chin, a subtle tinge of refinement in his pondering expression.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……すごいなあ。
　朔屋さん、なんでもできる、ます。
　これからもクロに教えてね？」
source.english:
“…Amazing.
You can do everything, Mr. Sakuya. You…
can. Keep teaching Kuro, please?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はっはっは、役立たず扱いに関しちゃ、俺だってお前に負けず劣らずだぞ」
source.english: “Hahaha. As far as being considered useless goes, I'm every bit your match.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まあ、こういう余裕のある時ならな。
　でもお前さん、見てると、
　売っ払われそこなったり、
　引っ叩たかれりで、
　落ち着いて教えるどころじゃねえんだよなあ」
source.english:
“Well,
when we have a quiet moment like this. But every time I see you,
you're either about to be sold off
or getting beaten.
It's hard to teach you anything in peace.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……That's amazing. Sakuya-san, can do anything. Please keep teaching Kuro from now on, okay?」
【Naomasa】 「Ha-ha-ha. When it comes to being treated as useless, the two of us are neck and neck.」

【Naomasa】 「Well, as long as it's times like this, with some breathing room. But whenever I see you, you're almost sold off, or beaten black and blue, and it's not really the best time to sit down and calmly teach you anything.」

source.japanese:
計器の硝子盤に息を吹きかければ白く霞む、拭き取りながらしみじみと思い返すだに、全くもってクロはろくな目に遭っていない。
　右のウエスで油落として左の布巾で拭って、息を吹きかけてまた拭う、と朔屋のやったことをそのまま繰り返すクロを、後に立って見守るに、なにやら胸にやるせない想いさわさわと迫った。
　朔屋自身も自分が銀の匙くわえて生まれてきたとは見なせないにしろ、クロを見ていると、まだいくらか幸運であるかの幻想を抱いてしまう。朔屋にしても己が穀潰しであり役立たずである事、臆面もなく承知の助ではあるにしても、嵐が来ていない時のクロの度合いは青年を遙かに勝る。
source.english:
His breath clouded the gauge glass white. Wiping it, he reflected: Kuro really did suffer one wretched thing after another.
She copied him exactly. Grease off with the rag in her right hand, wipe with the cloth in her left, breathe on it, wipe again. Watching from behind, he felt a helpless sadness stirring in his chest.
Sakuya did not consider himself born with a silver spoon in his mouth, but watching Kuro almost let him imagine he had been fortunate. He freely admitted that he was a wastrel and good for nothing; yet when no storm was blowing, Kuro outdid him by far in sheer uselessness.

source.japanese:
役立たずが役立たずとで同病相憐れむの、どこか心に痛い接しようだと朔屋は、溜め息で腕組みした事である。そしたら彼を振り返ったクロは、それも仕事の手順かと、真似して腕組みした事である。
　朔屋はそれは別にやらぬでよいと止めようとしたのだが、ふと茶目っ気催し足を組み替えところ、またクロは同じように繰り返す。
　ついつい魔が差して───
source.english:
Two useless creatures, fellow sufferers in the same affliction, pitying one another—the intimacy pricked somewhere in Sakuya's heart. He sighed and folded his arms. Kuro turned, took this for another step in the work, and folded hers.
He was about to tell her that part was unnecessary. Then mischief stirred: he crossed his legs differently, and Kuro copied him again.
A little devil took hold of him—

target.text: When he breathed onto the glass panel covering a meter, it fogged up with white; as he quietly reflected upon things while wiping it off, he realized it really had been nothing but one rotten disaster after another for Kuro. Removing the oil with the rag in her right hand, then wiping it off with the dishcloth in her left, breathing on it, then wiping again; as Sakuya stood behind Kuro, watching over her while she repeated the exact motions he had just gone through, some manner of inconsolable sorrow welled up in his bosom.

Though Sakuya did not at all consider himself to have been born with a silver spoon lodged in his mouth, when looking at Kuro, he came to entertain the fantasy that, perhaps, he had still been somewhat fortunate. Being a useless sponger was something Sakuya shamelessly embraced, but when there was no storm in sight, Kuro far surpassed the young man in matters of worthlessness.

The misery of fellow good-for-nothings also loves company, but being treated like that made Sakuya feel a sharp pain stabbing at his heart, and he crossed his arms while heaving a deep sigh.
