And having turned her head to look at him, believing it was part of the work process, Kuro also crossed her arms in imitation of him. Sakuya made to stop her, to tell her she really didn't need to do that, but feeling a sudden playfulness well up, he crossed his legs, and once more, Kuro repeated the same action. He couldn't help but fall for the temptation───

source.japanese:
朔屋は右足でホップした。クロも後れて、やや後に同じく繰り返す。
　次に左足踵[かかと]を左斜め前にだして、戻し、もう一度右足でホップしながら同様に。なにかと言えばこれ、ジェンカのステップである。
　単純なステップではあるがクロは覚えきれずにあわあわと、身に染みこませるには何度か見せてやらなければならず、朔屋は途中ではて自分は一体なんでこんな煉獄の舞台裏のような機関室で白子の娘にジェンカを教えてやっているのか知らんと、帰りかかった我を引き攫[さら]って、音楽だった。
source.english:
Sakuya hopped on his right foot. Kuro did the same, after a delay.
Next, his left heel forward at an angle to the left, back, another hop on the right foot, and repeat. The steps of a jenkka dance.
Simple steps, but Kuro could not remember them and floundered. He had to show her several times before they settled into her body. Partway through, Sakuya began to wonder why he was teaching an albino girl the jenkka in an engine room like purgatory's backstage. As his senses threatened to return, something carried them away again.
Music.

target.text: Sakuya hopped with his right foot. Kuro was daunted, but a little later, she repeated the motion. Next, he extended the heel of his left foot diagonally forwards to the left, pulled it back, then repeated the same movement while hopping with his right foot again. These were none other than the steps to the jenkka.

The steps were simple, but Kuro couldn't remember them and became flustered, so he had to show her several times until she'd grown familiar enough with them; partway through, Sakuya did wonder why the hell he was teaching an albino girl how to dance the jenkka in this backstage of purgatory that was the engine room, but what reeled him back in, just as he was finally beginning to return to his senses, that was the music.

source.japanese:
レッツキス　頬寄せて
　
　レッツキス　目を閉じて
source.english:
Let's kiss, cheek to cheek.
Let's kiss, close your eyes.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あレッツ　キッス　頬寄せてっ、
　あレッツ　キッス　目を閉じてぇ」
source.english:
“Ah, let's kiss, cheek to cheek!
Ah, let's kiss, close your eyes!”

source.japanese:
レッツキス　小鳥のように
　
　唇を　重ねよう（た）
source.english:
Let's kiss, like little birds.
Let our lips meet (our lips met).

target.text: Let's kiss cheek to cheek Let's kiss close your eyes (TN: This is a song by Sakamoto Kyuu called "Letkis (Jenka)", a Japanese cover of "Letkis" by Finnish composer Rauno Lehtinen written for a type of Finnish line dance, letkajenkka, also known as letkis. Interestingly, the "letkis" became various versions of "let's kiss" in foreign versions despite kissing having nothing to do with the original title.)
【Naomasa】 「Oh let's kiss cheek to cheek, Oh let's kiss close your eyesss!」
Let's kiss like little birds Let's press our lips together

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「れっつ　きす　ことりのように
　唇を　かさねた」
source.english:
“Let's kiss, like little birds.
Our lips met.”

source.japanese: レッツキスとクロがたとたと、辿々しいなれども違えずステップを踏み、
source.english: Let's kiss: Kuro toddled through the steps, faltering but correct.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「レッツキス　照れないで
　レッツキス　慎ましく～」
source.english:
“Let's kiss, don't be shy.
Let's kiss, modestly…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Let's kiss like little birds Press our lips together.」
With a titter-tatter, Kuro danced to Letkis, and though it was haltingly, she did not miss a single step,
【Naomasa】 「Let's kiss don't be shy Let's kiss modest and mild～」

source.japanese: 朔屋もクロの後から肩に手を乗せ同じステップ繰り返し、蓄音機からは擦れたノイズも味なジェンカが賑々しく、クロと朔屋の二人だけのジェンカトレイン、機関室を右に左に行ったり来たり、するうち最後のフレーズ響いてぴたりとポーズ、レコードが尽きた後でようやく朔屋は猛烈に恥ずかしくなったとか。
source.english: Coming up behind Kuro, Sakuya laid his hands on her shoulders and repeated the steps, while the gramophone struck up a boisterous jenkka, its worn crackle a charm in itself; and off went the jenkka train of Kuro and Sakuya, those two alone, back and forth across the engine room, now right, now left, until the final phrase rang out and brought them to a dead halt in their pose—and it was only after the record had run out that Sakuya was seized, so the tale goes, by a truly ferocious embarrassment.

target.text: Sakuya placed his hand on the back of Kuro's shoulder and repeated the same steps, the lively jenkka coming from the gramophone garnished with a scratchy noise; Sakuya and Kuro formed a jenkka train of just the two of them, going back and forth through the engine room, left and right, striking a pose just as the last phrase sounded, and it was only after the record ended that Sakuya finally felt intensely embarrassed, among other things.

source.english:
“…Hmm?
Hmm? I don't understand…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Hmm～～～mh? Hmm～～～mh? I don't understand……」

source.japanese: ぱんぱんと、白手袋で拍手を拍つ機関長の脇に、蓄音機。
source.english: The gramophone stood beside the engineer, who applauded with his white-gloved hands.

target.text: Next to the Chief Engineer, who was giving them a loud applause with hands clad in white gloves, there was a gramophone.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「───世にはクックロビン音頭というものがあってね。これの最後のポーズが、ヨガで言う『不易のアサナ』と酷似しており」
source.english: “There is a dance in this world called the Cock Robin Dance. Its final pose closely resembles what yoga calls the ‘unchanging asana.’”

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「おどっているうちに心気が昂進され、晴れやかな心地となり、つい夢中になってしまうのだとかなんだとか」
source.english: “As one dances, the spirits rise, the mind becomes cheerful, and one grows quite absorbed—or some such thing.”

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「そのジェンカのステップも、能で言うところの『西江水』の歩法と共通しているという。止められなくもなろう。幽玄の神意やどるという能と同じだとすれば」
source.english: “The steps of that jenkka are also said to resemble the ‘West River Water’ footwork of Noh. If it shares that profound, mysterious divine intent said to dwell in Noh, no wonder you couldn't stop.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はぁ～世の中のあれこれには、どんな不思議が隠れているか知れたもんじゃないんですな」
source.english: “Ah… You never know what mysteries might be hidden in all the things of this world.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「───Now, there exists in this world of ours a folk dance known as "Cock Robin". And the final pose one strikes in that bears a striking resemblance to what is known in Yoga as the 『Asana of Immutability』」 (TN: This is a reference to a Japanese gag manga by Maya Mineo, "パタリロ!", known as "Patalliro!" or "Patariro!" overseas. One gag is a lively festival dance set to the lyrics of the nursery rhyme "Who Killed Cock Robin", forming an absurd contrast with its grim lyrics, and it even served as an ending song for its anime adaptation. The Asana of Immutability is also from Patalliro.)
【Chief Engineer】 「And as you dance, your spirit is roused, you become so cheerful, you cannot help but lose yourself in the moment, or something of the sort.」

【Chief Engineer】 「And those jenkka steps, they also share several commonalities with the manner of walking displayed in Noh during the『Saikou-no-mizu』part. It would surely be unstoppable. If it is the same as Noh theatre, which is said to contain the divine will of the ethereal aesthetics of the profound and subtle, that is.」 (TN: Without getting too sidetracked, this is some very obscure Japanese cultural theory which posits that Japan took to jenkka so quickly because the basics of its steps share commonalities with a particular type of movement of a Kuse in a Noh play.)
【Naomasa】 「Haah～, you never know what mysteries lie hidden beneath all sorts of things in this world.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「なおクックロビン音頭の『不易のポーズ』云々に関しては、後年言いだした人間がきっぱり嘘だと明かした」
source.english: “Incidentally, that business about the Cock Robin Dance's ‘unchanging pose’—the person who came up with it later admitted outright that it was a lie.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「へ。じゃあジェンカで能がと言うのは」
source.english: “Huh? Then what about jenkka and Noh?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「In addition, regarding the 『Asana of Immutability』of the Cock Robin folk dance and all that. The man who had first claimed that would, in his later years, come to flatly reveal it to be a lie.」
【Naomasa】 「Huh. Then what about that thing with the jenkka and the Noh?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「何を言っているのだね君、『西江水』は柳生の奥義の一手だ。なんでフィンランド民謡のジェンカがそこで出てくるのだ、というか……」
source.english: “What are you talking about? ‘West River Water’ is one of the Yagyu school's secret techniques. What does a Finnish folk tune like the jenkka have to do with that? And anyway…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Whatever are you talking about, good sir? The『Saikou-no-mizu』 is a top secret technique of the Yagyuu. Rather, I should ask why you would even mention the Finnish folk dance of jenkka here……」 (TN: More esoteric Japanese culture. The Saikou-no-mizu, or "西江水", is, in fact, mentioned in the secret teachings of the Yagyuu clan, and is a concept originating from a Zen koan in the Entangling Vines, "宗門葛藤集", featuring Zen master Mazu Daoyi and Layman Pang. The Yagyuu clan headed one of Japan's greatest schools of swordsmanship and taught the blade to the Tokugawa shogun.)

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……たった二人でそんな事やって、
　楽しいのかね君達」
source.english:
“…Is that truly enjoyable
with only the two of you?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんたがやらせたんでしょうがぁぁ。
　蓄音機まで掛けてノリノリで」
source.english:
“You made us do it!
You even put on the gramophone and got completely carried away!”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……But to do something like that, just the two of you, means you must have rather enjoyed yourselves, yes?」
【Naomasa】 「Come oooon, you're the one who put us up to it. You got so into it that you even put a record on the gramophone.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「そういえばそんな事もあったか。
　ところで君達、なんでたった二人でジェンカなどを踊っているのかね」
source.english:
“Come to think of it, perhaps I did.
By the way, why are the two of you dancing the jenkka alone?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああもう鬱陶しいなあ……」
source.english: “Oh, this is getting on my nerves…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Now that you mention it, I suppose I did do that, didn't I? Incidentally, why exactly did you decide to dance the jenkka of all things with just the two of you?」
【Naomasa】 「Argh, this is just irritating……」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ううう。おどったりすると、
　やぱりお尻が痛いかった。
　これ、いつまで痛いンかな……」
source.english:
“Ooh. Dancing…
it still hurt Kuro's bottom.
How long will it keep hurting…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「かなり酷く腫[は]れてるし熱もあるからな……。
　でもまあ、あと三、四日くらいで痛みは退くだろ」
source.english:
“It's terribly swollen and still hot to the touch…
But the pain should ease in another three or four days.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uuuh. When Kuro dances, Kuro's butt still hurts. How long will it hurt……」
【Naomasa】 「You've got some pretty bad swelling, and it's still feverish……. But, well, in another three, maybe four days, I'm sure the pain will be gone.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「まだそんなに……。
　…………どうして、かなあ」
source.english:
“That long still…?
…Why, I wonder.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なにがってお前。あんなごついおっちゃんにあんだけ本気で叩かれたんだもの、ケツが柘榴みてえになんないですんだだけ、まだましだろ」
source.english: “What do you mean, why? A great big fellow hit you that hard. You're lucky your ass didn't end up like a pomegranate.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Still that long……. …………Wonder why.」
【Naomasa】 「What are you talking about, girl? After getting a serious spanking by an old man that burly, you should count yourself lucky that your ass doesn't look like a pomegranate right now.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うん、それ。
　……あの小父さん、
　なんであんなに怒ったんだろ」
source.english:
“Yes, that.
…Why did that man get so angry?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え……そりゃ当たり前だろう。
　だってそりゃ……ええと」
source.english:
“Huh…? Well, obviously.
Because… uh…”

source.japanese: クロが今さらそんな事も理解していないことに戸惑いを覚えたものの、朔屋もいざ言葉にしようとすると、舌からするりと漏れてうまく言えない。言葉に迷ううちに、蓄音機など影も形も無く隠し終えた機関長が、
source.english: He was baffled that Kuro still failed to understand even that. But when he tried to put it into words, it slipped off his tongue without forming properly. While he struggled, the engineer, who had finished concealing the gramophone without a trace, spoke.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Yeah, that. ……That old man. Wonder why he got so mad.」
【Naomasa】 「Huh……well, surely that's obvious. It's because, you know……uhmm.」

Although Sakuya was bewildered that Kuro still could not understood such a thing, when he now tried to put it into words, they just slid off his tongue, and he was unable to express it properly. While he was hesitating with his words, the Chief Engineer, who had just finished putting the gramophone back into its hiding spot without betraying a hint of doing so,

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「矜持の問題というものだ、
　クロ、お前はその水夫とやらに対し、
『自分は嵐なんて平気、むしろその方が良い』
　……およそそんなような事を言ったんじゃないのかね？」
source.english:
“A question of pride, Kuro.
You told this sailor something like,
‘Storms don't trouble me.
In fact, I prefer them.’ Didn't you?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……だいたいそんなところです」
source.english: “…More or less.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「It is an issue of pride. Kuro, to this sailor, or whomever it was, you said: 『I'm fine with a storm, and if anything, I prefer it that way.』 ……That was, at least, the gist of what you said, was it not?」
【Naomasa】 「……It was pretty much something along those lines.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「だろうね。それが、嵐から命からがら生還した彼の矜持、プライドといったものを傷つけた。だから激怒した。実に単純でわかりやすい」
source.english: “I thought so. That wounded the pride of a man who had barely escaped a storm alive. So he became furious. Quite simple and easy to understand.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「I figured as much. And that hurt the pride he feels for barely making it back with his life intact from that storm. That is why he was so furious. It is actually quite easy to understand in its simplicity.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「わかり、ないです……どうして？
　クロは嵐がよい、言います。
　でも……ええとそれでも」
source.english:
“Kuro doesn't… understand. Why?
Kuro says storms are good.
But… um, even so—”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……ア。それ。
　あの小父さんは嵐で怖い目にあったこと。
　なくならない。べつの、ことなのに」
source.english:
“Oh. That's it.
What happened to that man in the storm… the scary things.
That doesn't change. It's… a different thing.”

source.japanese:
どうしても理解できない様子のクロ。
　クロが嵐を好むと言ったところで、あの老水夫が嵐から生還したという事実は変わらないのに、何故それで激昂したのか、クロにはやはり、わからない。
source.english:
Kuro truly could not understand.
Her saying she liked storms did not change the fact that the old sailor had survived one. Why, then, had it enraged him? She still did not know.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うーんとな、こういうことだ。
　あのおっさんには、自慢なんだよ。
　命も危険なような嵐から生きて帰ったことが」
source.english:
“Well, look,
it's like this. He's proud of coming back alive
from a storm that might have killed him.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ところがそんなおっかない嵐を、クロみたいな弱っちい女の子が、良い、素敵だわー、って言っちまうと……」
source.english: “But when a weak little girl like you says that terrifying storm is good, it's lovely—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そこから生きて戻ってきたって、別に大変でもないみたいになっちゃうんだな。そうすると自慢できないだろ？」
source.english: “It makes surviving it seem like nothing much. Then he can't boast about it, can he?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Don't……get it……why? Kuro said a storm is nice. But……uhmm, but even so.」
【Kuro】 「……Ah. That. That old man had a scary time in the storm. That won't go away. That's something else, but he still.」

Kuro just didn't seem able to wrap her head around it. Just because Kuro said she liked storms, that didn't change the fact that the old sailor had returned home with his life intact from a storm, so why did that make him so furious? In the end, Kuro just could not understand that.
【Naomasa】 「Right, so, it's something like this. That old man has his pride. He's proud of the fact that he managed to live to tell the tale of a life-threateningly dangerous storm.」
【Naomasa】 「But when a weak little girl like you, Kuro, then tells him "nice, that's sooo wonderful", in spite of that storm being so scary……」
【Naomasa】 「Then it won't really seem like that big of a deal that he made it back alive from that storm. And in that case, he wouldn't be able to be proud of it, right?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「なかなか説明が巧いな、朔屋君。
　それで合っているだろう。船乗りに限らず、男は危険を、冒険を、美徳とする傾向にある」
source.english:
“Very well explained, Mr. Sakuya.
I believe that is correct. Sailors are hardly alone: men tend to regard danger and adventure as virtues.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「You have quite the gift for explaining things, Sakuya-kun. I'm certain that is correct. And it is not limited to just sailors, for all men have a tendency to glorify danger, adventure, as a virtue.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「その冒険を否定されたようなものなのだろうね。
　その水夫にとっては」
source.english:
“To that sailor,
it probably felt as though you had denied the worth of his adventure.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「I suppose it was as if his adventure had been invalidated. In that sailor's mind, at least.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でもお……冒険なんてえらいことは、なんもかもちゃんとできる人だから、言えるんだよ」
source.english: “But… you can only talk about big things like adventure if you can do everything right.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Buuut……it's only because he can do everything right, that he can even talk about something as great as adventure.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロは、冒険よりも、おそうじとか、やらないと。でもできない。いろんなこと、できない」
source.english: “Kuro has to do things like… cleaning. Not adventures. But Kuro can't. Lots of things Kuro can't do.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いっぱいがんばっても、でもわらわれる」
source.english: “Kuro tries so hard. But… they still laugh.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「お前もしんどいよなあ……」
source.english: “It's hard for you too, isn't it…”

source.japanese:
クロの根深い劣等感を、なんで朔屋が嗤[わら]えたろう。
　クロには、まず人としてやっていけるという自信さえない。
source.english:
How could Sakuya laugh at Kuro's deep-rooted sense of inferiority?
She had no confidence that she could even get by as a human being.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro has to do cleaning and stuff, before adventure. But Kuro can't. So many things Kuro can't do.」
【Kuro】 「Kuro tries so, so hard, but just gets laughed at.」
【Naomasa】 「You've got it rough too, huh……」
How could Sakuya possibly laugh at Kuro's deep-rooted inferiority complex? Kuro lacked even the confidence to exist as a human being.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でもクロは、嵐が来れば。
　ちゃんとしてられる。から。
　だからいつも嵐のところがいい。
　そうであれば、
　クロだってちゃんとしてられる」
source.english:
“But Kuro…
when a storm comes, Kuro can do things right.
That's why…
a place where there's always a storm would be good.
Then Kuro could do things right, too.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「みんなから、撲たれたり、
　どんって押されたりしなくってすむ」
source.english:
“Then people wouldn't hit Kuro.
Or shove Kuro.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……きっと。嵐だから、嵐の時みたいに。
　たよりにしてもらえる」
source.english:
“…They would. Because there'd be a storm. Like when a storm comes…
they'd rely on Kuro.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……そりゃようお前、確かに今回の話が上手くいけば、止まない嵐の中に突入することになるわけなんだけどよ」
source.english: “…Well, yes. If this business works out, we will be heading into a storm that never ends.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「みんなもお宝、ザウエルの期待に目が血走ってござる。……なんかこう、浮かない気分なのは俺だけなんかなあ……」
source.english: “Everyone's eyes are bloodshot with dreams of treasure—of Zauer… Am I the only one who can't seem to feel happy about it?”

source.japanese: クロの言葉を聞いた後でも、やはり嵐を目指して進んでいくなどどうにも気が重くて、朔屋はもう、今からうんざりと。
source.english: Even after hearing Kuro, sailing toward a storm still weighed on his spirits. Sakuya was sick of it already.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But when the storm comes, Kuro can be right. So. That's why an always storm is nice. If Kuro has that, even Kuro can be right.」
【Kuro】 「Won't have, to be hit, or shoved around by everybody.」
【Kuro】 「……Kuro is sure. It's a storm, so they'll all rely on Kuro, just like when it storms.」
【Naomasa】 「……Well, you know, if this whole thing goes well, we'll end up charging straight into a ceaseless storm and all that.」

【Naomasa】 「And the rest have eyes burning with anticipation for the treasure, for those Sauers. ……It kind of feels like I'm the only person here who's not feeling too excited about this whole thing……」
Even after hearing Kuro's words, the thought of heading towards a storm still left him with a heavy heart, and Sakuya was already sick of it all.

source.japanese: ───その黒鯛は、兄弟朋輩が皆当たり前の黒い鱗[うろこ]である中で一匹だけ、造化の神の色配合の手誤りで赤い鱗[うろこ]に全身包み、酷い排斥や虐めこそなかったけれど、どうにも群れに馴染めぬ毎日の。それでも繕いを当てるように仲間とは折り合い着けて海暮らし、波は荒いが微虫に満ちて滋養豊かにて、岩肌で波拍子に合わせて揺れる海苔を前菜に喰む、砂底にぬたうつ磯蚯蚓をつつけばよく肥えて鱗[うろこ]と身を豊かに養う。こう安閑とした日々を送っていたところにひょこと出たのが大なる魚、九絵だ。育れば大助と出世する黒鯛も、チヌのうちでは九絵の格好の餌、砂渦巻き立てる猛進に群れ蹴散らされ岩窪に追いこまれ、食い荒らされてひとたまりもない。
source.english: There was a black sea bream whose kin and companions all wore the usual black scales, but who was himself clothed entirely in red: a slip of the hand as the god of creation mixed the colors. He suffered no cruel rejection or bullying, yet never quite fit into the school; still, he patched together an accommodation with the others and lived his life at sea. The waves were rough, but rich with nourishing plankton; he nibbled as an appetizer at seaweed swaying on the rocks to their rhythm, then pecked at ragworms writhing over the sandy bottom, growing plump and well nourished in scales and flesh. His days passed peacefully—until a great longtooth grouper appeared. A black sea bream might earn the grander name of Oosuke as it grew, but a small one was ideal prey for a grouper. The grouper's charge threw up whirling sand and scattered the school, driving it into hollows in the rocks to be devoured without a chance.

source.japanese: 群れは呂布将軍に飛びこまれた農兵よろしく総崩れの全滅に、ところで件の赤い黒鯛は鰭[ひれ]が強く生まれついており、彼だけは逃れて、みても今までの群れは既に無し。潮の流れに雄々しく逆らってみても括れ蔦の群生を発見しても苦楽を共にする仲間がないでは、生を生きる感慨にも乏しく小魚の漏らした小さな吐息はしかししみじみ深い寂寥籠もった泡となって水面まで運ばれる。
source.english: The school collapsed and was annihilated like peasant soldiers with General Lü Bu charging into their midst. The red-scaled black sea bream, however, had been born with strong fins. He alone escaped. But his old school was gone. He might bravely fight the current, or discover a thriving patch of sea grapes—but without companions to share hardship and joy, there was little savor in being alive. The little fish's tiny sigh, though, formed a bubble laden with profound loneliness and rose to the surface.

source.japanese: こうして餌場と塒の独りの往還空しく繰り返す赤い黒鯛が、新たな群れと出会ったのは、より膨れようとする群れの習性か、それとも孤独な魂の引力の方が呼び寄せたか、いずれにしてもまずは喜ばしい邂逅ではあった。
source.english: Alone, the red-scaled black sea bream repeated his empty journeys between feeding grounds and refuge. Then he met a new school. Whether it was a school's instinct to grow larger, or the pull of a lonely soul that had brought them together, the meeting was a happy one—at first.

source.japanese:
ただし、岩場一帯にいまだ九絵が陣取って、黒鯛の群れが肥えるのを待ち構えてあり、そして新たな家族となった群れが九絵の襲撃に怯えきったみじめな日々を送っているとあっては、その喜ばしきも半減の話。
　迫る死刑執行にも従容と、萎縮しきった同胞を憂う赤い鱗[うろこ]の黒鯛に、彼をしてこのはみ出し物の我が身を受け入れてくれた群れに酬いたいという願いが彼をして一計を案じせしめた。
source.english:
But the grouper still held the rocky ground, waiting for the sea bream to fatten. His new family lived in wretched fear of its attacks. That halved the joy.
The red-scaled bream worried for his fellows, so cowed that they quietly awaited their approaching execution. He wanted to repay the school that had accepted an outsider like himself. That wish led him to devise a plan.

source.japanese:
すなわち、それまでは大魚に襲われても算を乱して無秩序に逃げ惑うしか知らなかった群れに、統制を与える───群れを一つの、九絵を超えて巨大な魚の陣形に組み、赤い鱗[うろこ]の黒鯛が司令塔かつ赤い眼として陣の頭部に収まるという物。半信半疑であった群れを説き伏せたところからして、赤い鱗[うろこ]の黒鯛には率いる才というのが眠っていたのだろう。
　……果実も熟して肉も程良く太ったとみて襲いかかった九絵は、予想外の反撃に手もなく退散だ、よもや自分より大なる魚が目を赤く攻撃色に光らせて挑んでこようとは思ってもいまいて。
source.english:
He would bring order to a school that had previously known only to scatter in panic when a large fish attacked. They would form a single fish larger than the grouper, with the red-scaled bream at its head, both commander and red eye. That he persuaded his doubtful fellows suggested a dormant gift for leadership.
When the grouper decided the fruit was ripe, the flesh suitably fat, and attacked, the unexpected counterstroke easily sent it fleeing. Who could have imagined a fish larger than itself charging with a red eye blazing for battle?

source.japanese:
ようやく黒鯛の群れは強敵への武器も入れて万々歳、赤い鱗[うろこ]の黒鯛も自分の存在意義を確かめられ、悠然と群れは磯に大魚の形為して、これからも共に潮に生きようと達成感を噛み締めていた、ところを、横から万々歳も赤い黒鯛の意気揚々もまとめて網に攫われた。まさに一網打尽である。
　この時代の保存食はとにかく保たせる事優先、味は二の次の三の次の瓶詰め缶詰め、これら信天翁号の航海中の主食に飽いた、航海士の双子が命じたによって短艇を出した下級水夫達には網内に満つる黒鯛の無念の断末魔もぴちぴちの活きの良さ。
source.english:
At last the school had a weapon against its mighty enemy. Hurrah! The red-scaled bream had found a reason for his existence too. Leisurely forming their great fish shape by the shore, they savored their achievement: together they would go on living in the tide. Then a net swept in from the side and carried off hurrahs, triumph, and red bream alike. A clean sweep, literally.
Preserved food in this age put keeping quality first. Taste came second or third. Jars and cans were the Albatross's staple fare at sea, and the twin mates had tired of it. The junior sailors sent out in a boat at their orders saw the sea bream's bitter death throes inside the net as nothing more than fine, lively freshness.

source.japanese:
大量大量とほくほくもので漕いで返して、小魚たちは鱗[うろこ]を落とされ臓物を抜かれて開かれて、バラックの屋根にずらり延べられ、今はもう生気も水気も、快晴下に乾されてゆらゆら、乾いていくしかない末路の緩い蒸気、ゆらゆら。
　信天翁号に採って採り過ぎる、という事はなく、近々に消費しきれなかった分は日乾として乗り組み達の舌を楽しませるのである。
source.english:
A great catch, a great catch. They rowed back delighted. The little fish were scaled, gutted, split open, and laid in rows on a shack roof. Now their life and moisture alike could only dry away beneath a clear sky. Faint vapor wavered over their inevitable end.
There was no such thing as catching too much aboard the Albatross. Whatever they could not eat soon would delight the crew's tongues as dried fish.

source.japanese: それでも赤い黒鯛の戦術は死後も継承され、信天翁号舳先近くの荒れ小屋の一つの屋根の上、トッケイの肌ばりにざらついた屋根板の上で、今も黒い鱗[うろこ]の仲間達は、大魚の形に並べられ、紅い魚はその目の位置に収まるように置かれてあり───
source.english: Even after death, however, the red bream's tactics lived on. On the rough roof boards of a shack near the Albatross's bow, coarse as a tokay gecko's skin, his black-scaled companions still lay in the shape of a great fish. The red one occupied the eye—

target.text: ───He was a black bream living amongst his fellow brethren, who were clad in scales of black as though it were the most natural thing in the world, yet only his body, the result of a slip of the hand by the Creator God while mixing His colours, was clad entirely in scales of red, and though he suffered no cruel ostracism or bullying in particular, he still spent his every day unable to fit in with the rest of the school.

Even so, like mending a worn set of clothes by sewing on a patch, he had made peace with his brethren and lived his life in the ocean; when the seas were rough, it was full of plankton and rich in nourishment, they would snack on the nori swaying on the surface of the rocks in tandem with the passage of the waves as an hors d'ouevre, and as he continued to peck at the eunicids rolling around on the sandy bottom, he grew plump, rich of the scales that enveloped his body.

While he spent his days in such relaxation and comfort, what should suddenly emerge but a great fish, a longtooth grouper. Even this sea bream who, were he to continue to grow larger, could one day make it big and be promoted to Oosuke, was, for as long as he remained but a juvenile bream, only fit to be fish food, and the ferocious charge whirling up the sand around them scattered the school, driving them into hollows in the rocks; none of them stood a chance as they were devoured. (TN: Oosuke, written "大助", is a very big salmon from the folk legend Sake no Oosuke, which takes place in the Touhoku region. It also means a very big king salmon in general.)

The school was routed and annihilated like a unit of conscripted farmers jumped by General Lu Bu, but it bears mention that the aforementioned red black bream had been born with strong fins, and so he alone escaped; when he looked back, his school was already gone. Even as he heroically tried to defy the tidal current, even as he discovered a rich clump of sea grapes, he had none to share life's joys and sorrows with anymore, and the small sigh that escaped this little fish, who did not have a strong concept of life and living to begin with, was still filled with a heartfelt, deep desolation, and it turned into little bubbles that were carried all the way up to the surface of the sea.

Thus, vainly repeating the solitary commute between feeding ground and lair, one day, the red black bream encountered a new school; was it because the school had an ingrained tendency to attempt to expand, or was it the gravitational pull of his lonely soul that had drawn them in? Regardless of which, it was a joyous chance encounter.

However, the longtooth grouper was still encamped in the area surrounding the rocky bed; it was biding its time for the school of black sea bream to fatten up, and thus, the fact that the school, which had now become his new family, was spending its days in abject misery, terrified of the longtooth grouper's assault, cast a dark shadow over his joy Calm and composed even as the moment of execution loomed ever closer, this red-scaled black bream, grieving for his cowering brethren, desired to repay the school, which had accepted one such as him, an outcast, and this led him to devise a plan.

That is to say, he would give unity and control to this school, which hitherto only knew to scatter and chaotically flee when attacked by a large fish─── all as one, the entire school would together assume a formation in the shape of a giant fish that exceeded the size of the longtooth grouper, and the red-scaled black bream would be positioned in the head of this formation, functioning as both the commander and the red eye. That he managed to convince the skeptical school suggested this red-scaled black bream must have had a latent talent for commanding.

……When the longtooth grouper went on the attack, judging that the fruit must have ripened and the meat grown succulent with fat, it retreated helplessly after being caught off guard by the unexpected counterattack, never imagining that a fish even greater than itself would challenge it with eyes glowing red with aggression.

At long last, the school of black bream had acquired a weapon to counter even their most powerful enemies, praise be; the red-scaled black bream had also found his raison d'etre, and the school leisurely held the shape of a great fish by the rocky seashore; henceforth, they would together live on in these waters, and as he savoured that feeling of pride and accomplishment, that very moment, came a net, swinging in from the side, scooping up both those celebrating with cheer and the triumphant red black bream himself, all in one go. Quite literally catching them all in one fell swoop.

In this day and age, where the priority of any preserved foods was the act of preservation itself, stuck in cans or bottles where taste was a distant second or third consideration, the twin first mates had grown tired of the staple foods of the Albatross as she sailed along, and the deck boys, who had been ordered by them to launch the small boat, found the nets to be full of the tragic death throes of black bream still throbbing with vitality.

Beaming happily at the great catch as they rowed back, they then descaled the small fish, opened them to remove their insides, and lined them up on the roof of a shack; by now, their vitality and moisture alike had been dried out by the clear sky, the only fate they had in store becoming dried husks, and the vapours spelling their end rose gently upwards. It was not that the Albatross had caught too many fish, simply that sun-drying the portion they wouldn't consume in the immediate future delighted the palates of the crew.

Nevertheless, the stratagem of the red black bream had been inherited even beyond his final moments, for on the rooftop of one of those dilapidated huts near the bow of the Albatross, on a shingle coarse and rough as a gecko's skin, even now, he lay together with his black-scaled brethren in the shape of a giant fish, the red fish placed so that he would fit right in the position of its eye───

source.japanese:
【直正】
（……何やってんのよあの子達は……）
source.english: (…What are those kids doing…?)

source.japanese: 丸い視界、端がやや歪んだ望遠鏡の筒先では、バラックの屋根で下級水夫達が先日揚げたという黒鯛の小魚達を日乾しにしている最中で、まだそれだけなら水夫達のこまめな雑仕事、何故わざわざ大魚の形に並べて、黒い中に一尾だけ赤いのを目の辺りに据えてみるのか。深意は無い、水夫君達の遊び半分だったとしても、群れを率いた赤い鱗[うろこ]の黒鯛の物語、老蛤が吐いた蜃気楼のように頭の中に描き出されようというもので。
source.english: At the end of the telescope, in a round view slightly distorted at the edges, the junior sailors were drying the small sea bream caught a few days before. That alone would have been their usual diligent work. But why arrange them as a large fish, with the one red specimen among the black at its eye? There was no deeper meaning to it. The sailors might only have been mixing play with work, but it was enough to conjure the story of the red-scaled bream leading his school—like a mirage breathed out by an ancient clam—in Sakuya's head.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （……What are those boys up to……）

Through the circular field of vision of the telescope's lens, with its slightly distorted edges, there, on the roof of a shack, lay the small black bream, which had been caught by the deck boys the other day, in the process of being sun-dried, and if that was all they were doing, then it would just be one of many examples of the deck boys earnestly at work, but why did they have to go out of their way to line them up in the shape of a giant fish, placing but a single red one as an eye in the midst of all the black?

Even if it held no greater meaning, even if it was only done in good fun by the deck boys, why was the tale of the red-scaled black bream commanding the school being told through such vivid imagery in his head, like the mirages exhaled by ancient hamaguri clams? (TN: A reference to "蜃", read "Shin", a bivalve clam of ancient Chinese legend that would breathe out mirages. It is also sometimes a dragon.)

source.japanese: こうして朔屋が眺めるうちに、屋根の上の下級水夫君二人、何やら帽子を脱いで蝿追いの篠竹細いの構えてじゃん拳だ、水夫式に何回か前振りに構えてから本手を出しての勝ったと負けた、負けた方はさっと帽子を被って、勝ちは相手に被られる前に篠竹で脳天をやりこめんとす、いわゆる『叩いて被って』であり、離れたところから望見しているとはいえ朔屋にも二人の攻守は目まぐるしい。穏やかな波に揺られて矢継ぎ早の水夫二人の手、剣舞のように翻[ひるがえ]り、加速していって、ただの遊びと言うにも真剣味がまして細竹はしなる鞭のよう。一体なにをそんな本気勝負なのかと言わば、水夫二人の目がちらちらと例の赤い鱗[うろこ]の黒鯛へと、どうやらどちらが他より目立つ小魚を取るかで意見が割れたと覚[おぼ]ゆる……。
source.english: As Sakuya watched, the two junior sailors on the roof took off their caps, armed themselves with slender bamboo switches used to chase flies, and began rock-paper-scissors. Sailor fashion: a few preliminary feints before the real hand. Winner and loser. The loser quickly put on his cap; the winner tried to strike his head with the bamboo before he could cover it. The game of hit-or-cover. Even at this distance, their attack and defense were dizzyingly fast. Rocked by gentle waves, their hands flashed like a sword dance, faster and faster. What had been play acquired an earnest edge, the bamboo flexing like whips. Why such a serious contest? Both kept glancing at the red-scaled sea bream. Apparently they disagreed about who should get the little fish that stood out from the rest.

target.text: And while Sakuya was observing thus, two deck boys on top of the roof had removed their hats, holding some sort of thin, fly-repelling bamboo grass in one hand while they played rock-paper-scissors with the other, and after doing the lead-in over and over again in the sailor way, they then made their real move; one won, and one lost. The loser quickly put his hat on, the winner tried to jab the bamboo grass into the loser's head before he could cover it with his hat, the so-called『Tataite Kabutte』version of the game, and though he observed the proceedings from afar, their offence and defence unfolded at dizzying speeds.

Swaying gently on the waves, the hands of the two sailors flashed through the air in rapid succession like a sword dance, accelerating; even if it was just a game, they were dead serious, and the bamboo grass bent like a whip. As for what had brought them to such a serious battle, the eyes of both sailors would flicker towards the aforementioned red-scaled black bream, so it seemed like they were of split opinions on who would get to claim the fish that stood out so from all the others……

source.japanese: そんな物、黒の中にたまさか赤いのが紛れたから目立つだけ、なにもそう角立てて取りあうこともなかろうにと、これは遠眼鏡に醒めた朔屋だから言える視点で、水夫二人は至って真剣、を過ぎてとうとう篠竹捨てて拳を固めてぽかぽかやり合い始める始末。二人が幾ら船に慣れているといって乗っているのは柵もないあばら屋の屋根、それも干し魚が埋めて足の踏み場もない板屋根で、暴れれば軋む、たわむ、じゃれ合う仔犬は微笑ましいが周りが見えていない。二人は一つに縺[もつ]れあった挙げ句、屋根の縁を踏み外した、朔屋があっと言う間もなく落ちて、帽子だけが紙風船と一時宙に留まったけれどそれもふわふわ揺れながら主の後を追う。
source.english: It only stood out because one red fish happened to lie among black ones. Surely there was no need to quarrel over it. But that was the detached view available to Sakuya through his telescope. The two sailors were entirely serious. Too serious: at last they threw down the bamboo, clenched their fists, and began punching each other. However accustomed to shipboard life they were, they stood on an unrailed shack roof, its boards so covered in drying fish that there was scarcely room for a foot. Their struggling made it creak and bend. Wrestling puppies were charming, but unaware of their surroundings. Tangled together, they stepped off the roof's edge and fell before Sakuya could even cry out. Only their caps remained briefly aloft like paper balloons, then drifted after their owners.

target.text: Something as trifling as that, only remarkable because it was a bit of red that happened to be mixed in amongst the black, surely wasn't something worth struggling so wildly for, but this was a perspective that Sakuya could only hold through the cool calm of a telescope, for the sailors were extremely serious; too serious, even, and they finally threw away the bamboo grass, clenched their fists, and then began to fistfight.

No matter how used the two were to being on a ship, they were standing on the roof of a miserable shack with no parapet, and on shingles covered in dried fish no less, so they barely had any footing to work with, and as they scrambled, it creaked and bent; their little puppy-dog scuffle was heartwarming to watch, but they couldn't see what was happening around them. After but one entanglement, they'd stepped off the edge of the roof, fallen before Sakuya even had the time to exclaim "ah!", and only their hats were left suspended in the air for a brief time like paper balloons before they, too, gently swayed downwards in pursuit of their owners.

source.japanese:
で、帽子がふわりと落ちて被さった主達は腰を打ちつけて甲板上で呻[うめ]いてあったが、彼らをからかうように上空から阿呆鳥、ルート記号の下降線で屋根をかすめ、まんまと取っていったのが例の赤い鱗[うろこ]の黒鯛だったという。
　しばしの呆然、そして落胆しきってもそもそ屋根へと上がり直す下級水夫が哀れやら滑稽やら、微苦笑の朔屋の天骨をごん、と叩いた衝撃で視界がぶれる。
source.english:
The caps floated down over their owners, who had struck their backsides and were groaning on deck. As if to mock them, an albatross swooped from overhead, skimmed the roof in the descending stroke of a square-root sign, and made off with the red-scaled bream.
A stunned pause. Then the utterly dejected junior sailors clambered back up. Pitiful and comical. Sakuya gave a faint, wry smile—until a blow landed on his crown and shook his view.

target.text: And so, the hats fell gently down and covered the heads of their owners, who had struck their butts and were groaning on the upper deck, but as if to make fun of their misery, an albatross descended from the skies, and following the downward line of the radical symbol, pilfered something from the roof; what it had artfully snatched was none other than that aforementioned red-scaled black bream. After being dumbfounded for a brief time, uncertain if the despondent deck boys sluggishly climbing back up to the roof once more were pitiful or laughable to behold, the bittersweet smile on Sakuya's face wavered in unison with his vision as the impact of a fist ran through his skeleton with a loud clonk.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「しゃんと見張りせんか、朔屋。
　よそ見しとったろうおまえ今」
source.english:
“Keep a proper watch, Sakuya.
You were looking somewhere else just now.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……痛ぇっすよ水夫長。
　ちゃんと見てましたって。
　まだどこにも雲なんかは見えない……」
source.english:
“…That hurt, Bosun.
I was watching.
Still no clouds anywhere…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You keeping a proper watch, Sakuya? Looks to me like your eyes were wandering just now.」
【Naomasa】 「……That really hurts, Bosun. I'm looking properly, alright. I still don't see any clouds anywhere……」

source.japanese: 打ち据えた水夫長に向き直れば、拡大された視界もぐるりと廻って、レンズの円内に一杯充たしたのは黒々と繁茂し蔦絡まり合う密林だ。それもじくじくと露に塗れた。胸悪くなるくらいむっといきれ立つ眺めが水夫長の密生したる胸毛と気づいて朔屋は、えづき催す前に片目をぎゅっと縛る。そうなっても望遠鏡を離さないのは第二一連隊の喇叭吹きの忠勇にも比せられる、わけもなく朔屋はまた下らない悪さをした罰で、あの望遠鏡を片目に押し当てる形で手ごとぐるぐると頭に縛りつけられて、哨戒に立たされていただけの事。
source.english: He turned toward the boatswain, taking his magnified view with him. The circle filled with a dense black jungle, vines tangled and slick with dew. He realized this stifling, nauseating landscape was the boatswain's thick chest hair and squeezed his eye shut before he could gag. That he never lowered the telescope might suggest loyalty and bravery worthy of the Twenty-first Regiment's bugler. Of course, it was nothing of the kind. As punishment for yet another petty misdeed, the telescope and his hand had been bound tightly around his head, holding it against one eye. He had merely been put on lookout duty that way.

source.japanese: 件の望遠鏡は新米水夫には奢った品と召し上げられることこそなかったものの、爾来朔屋は事あるごとに観測として物見櫓に押し上げられる羽目になっていた。今日だって泪が酒場の船乗りから聞き出してきた『止まない嵐』の発見を命じられている。海域としてはこの辺りの筈で、日数も経ってクロの尻の腫[は]れも癒えてきたが、しかしどうにも目当ての嵐は、先触れも気配も浮かばせず、四海を円盤状に取り巻く水平線は気圏の晴れた青と水界の穏やかな碧を区切り雲もまばら、それとて綿のように白く優しいのばかり。暗雲は望んだ時に訪れてくれない。ま、船にあって望む者の方が常軌を逸しているのだが。
source.english: The telescope had escaped confiscation as too fine a possession for a novice. Since acquiring it, however, Sakuya had been sent up to the lookout at every opportunity to make observations. Today, too, he was ordered to find the ‘storm that never ends,’ whose position Rui had learned from the tavern sailor. These should have been the right waters. Days had passed, and even Kuro's swelling was healing. Yet the desired storm showed not a hint of its approach. The horizon, a disc surrounding them, divided the air's clear blue from the sea's peaceful green-blue. Clouds were few, and those few soft and white as cotton. Dark clouds did not arrive when wanted. Though wanting them aboard a ship was itself madness.

target.text: When he turned to face the Bosun, the origin of the strike, his magnified vision spun round and round, and a jet-black, luxuriantly dense thicket of intertwining vines filled up the circular lens. And it was oozing, smeared with dew. By the time Sakuya realized that this view, so muggy it left him ill at ease, was the Bosun's thickly-grown chest hair, he squeezed his one eye tightly shut before nausea could overtake him.

That he still refused to remove the telescope from his eye, even in this situation, was comparable to the loyalty and bravery of the bugler of the 21st Regiment, but the reason was simply that, for no particular cause other than punishment for some trivial mischief he had committed, Sakuya had been forced into sentry duty, and the telescope had been lashed round and round his head, hand and all, pressed firmly to his eye. (TN: The bugler is Kiguchi Kohei, a Japanese soldier hailed as a hero who died in battle in the First Sino-Japanese War in 1894. He is said to have never let go of his bugle, even in death.)

While the telescope in question was never actually confiscated as a luxury ill-suited for a mere green sailor, ever since that day, Sakuya had been forced up the watchtower for observation duties at every turn. Today was no exception, and he'd been ordered to discover the『Ceaseless Storm』that Rui had extracted information about from that sailor in the bar.

It should be somewhere around these waters, and as the days passed, while Kuro's butt had recovered from its swelling, no matter how hard he looked, neither portent nor hint of the storm he was looking for would surface; though the horizon that encircled the Seven Seas in the shape of a disk was sparsely decorated with straggling clouds that broke up the blues of the clear atmosphere and the azures of the gentle hydrosphere, they were all meek and white as cotton. Dark skies never come calling when desired. Well, any who desired such while sailing on a ship had gone off the rails.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「泪女史が訊きだしてきたってぇ言ったなら、その事じてぇにゃ嘘はねえんだろうが、その爺とやらが間違ったことを信じてたって可能性はある」
source.english: “If Madam Rui says she got it out of him, that part's no lie. But the old man might've believed something wrong.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Since Miss Rui is the one who obtained the info, I reckon there's no lie in it, but there's still the possibility that old guy or whoever was mistaken about what he believed happened.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おいクロ、『カンパチ』」
source.english: “Kuro. ‘Amberjack.’”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Oi, Kuro.『Amberjack(Kanpachi)』」

source.english: “Um… ‘Kitchen’…”

source.japanese: 朔屋が観測員ならクロは気圧計、ただし水銀の代わりに詰まっているのはどうにも頼りない脳味噌、目盛りを告げる舌も相変わらずたどたどしい。ようやく座れるようにはなったが、ややもするとまだ痛みがぶり返してくるようで、落ち着かぬげに立てたり落としたりする腰は釣瓶井戸の桶。度に白髪が舞ったり流れたり。
source.english: Sakuya was the observer; Kuro, the barometer. Instead of mercury, however, she contained a most unreliable brain, and the tongue reporting her reading stumbled as usual. She could finally sit again, but the pain still sometimes returned. Her restless rising and sinking resembled a well bucket, her white hair lifting and falling with it.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Mn……lessee,『Chicken』……」

If Sakuya was the observer, then Kuro was the barometer, but instead of being filled with mercury, it was packed with utterly unreliable brain tissue, and her tongue announcing its gradations was as hesitant as ever. She was finally able to sit down once more, but the pain was still liable to return when she did, and so she would stand up, then sit once more, unable to settle down, her hips moving like the bucket in a well. And every time, her white hair would whirl and drift about.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……続かねえな。
　だいたい一つところにじっとしているような嵐があんなら、他にも噂くらいは入ってくるだろうし……クロ、『粘土』」
source.english:
“…Still can't keep it going.
If there was a storm staying in one place, surely we'd have heard other rumors… Kuro. ‘Clay.’”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Can't keep it going, huh. Anyways, if there did exist a storm that just stayed still in a single place, then there'd have to be several other rumours about it…… Kuro,『Clay(Nendo)』」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロ……もう言葉、思いつかなくなってきて。ンン……と、あ。『ドカン』」
source.english: “Kuro… can't think of words anymore. Umm… Ah. ‘Yen.’”

source.japanese:
反響で暗い孔の深みを測る小石のように水夫長が掛け句を放るも、まだクロの頭の中にはあの透徹した容量は広がっておらず、長続きしないやりとり、嵐の兆しはまだ遠い。
　中途半端な自尊心持ち合わせた船乗りなら、この観測器具代わりの扱いに臍曲げるところだろうが、クロでは依怙地になる以前にただただ言いつけを処理するだけで必死、両の人差し指をこめかみに当ててうんうんと、回らぬ頭で言葉を求める様は健気と言えたが。これが頓知の利く小坊主なら大いに期待の持てようところ、このクロでは。
source.english:
The boatswain tossed out words like pebbles measuring a dark hole's depth by their echoes. But the lucid space had not yet opened in Kuro's head. The exchange never lasted. A storm was still far off.
A sailor with even a middling amount of pride might have resented being treated as an instrument. Kuro, however, was too busy coping with orders even to reach stubbornness. With both forefingers at her temples, she strained her sluggish mind for words. Brave effort. Had she been a witty little novice monk, one might have expected great things. But this was Kuro.

source.japanese: ただ、信天翁の面子と付き合うようになってから日が浅い朔屋には、クロがしりとりに弱いのもこう頻繁では、白々しさが先に立つ。
source.english: Sakuya had not been among the Albatross's company for long, and after seeing Kuro fail at word chains this often, he was beginning to find the whole performance a little too convenient.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro……has already run out of words. Leeeet's……see, ah. 『Bang(Dokan)』」

Though the Bosun continued to chuck the opening link of a word-chain at Kuro like he was measuring the depths of a dark hole by throwing down a pebble and listening for the echo, Kuro's brain had yet to expand its capacity with that clarity of mind, and their short-lived exchange meant any signs of a storm were still a distant hope.

If she was a sailor possessed of even a half-baked sense of self-respect, then she'd surely be cross at being treated like a substitute for some measuring instrument, but before she could grow headstrong, Kuro was frantic enough just trying to process the instructions she'd been given; she pushed both her index fingers against her temples as she hemmed and hawwed, and it could even be called admirable how strenuously she searched for the words despite her lack of comprehension. Were she a quick-witted young monk in training, then there would be much to be hopeful about in the future, but this was Kuro.
However, to Sakuya, who had still not spent that many days with the crew of the Albatross, with Kuro's losses at shiritori being this incessant, it was starting to feel more contrived than anything.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ねえ水夫長、
　ほんとにクロこれ、わざとでないの？」
source.english:
“…Bosun.
Are you sure Kuro isn't doing this on purpose?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Hey, Bosun, are you sure that Kuro isn't losing on purpose?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「こいつがンな器用なことができるタマか。
　ええ事を教えてやろう朔屋。
　この船では海のど真ん中で真水が尽きても、
　手に入れる術ッてヤツがある」
source.english:
“Does she look capable of a trick like that? I'll tell you something,
Sakuya.
This ship has a way to get fresh water even
when we run out in the middle of the sea.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ。やだ、なんか見当がつくような」
source.english: “Oh, no. I think I can guess where this is going.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You really think she'd be clever enough to pull that? Let me tell you a little something, Sakuya. When this ship runs out of fresh water right in the middle of the ocean, we have a little trick up our sleeve for getting some more.」
【Naomasa】 「Ah. Oh no, I feel like I know where this is going.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そうよ。まずな、クロを立たせるわけだ。
　そんでクロをぐるぐると回しながらしりとりをしていく」
source.english:
“Right. First, stand Kuro up.
Then turn her round and round while playing word chain.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「他と反応が違う方角を見つけてだな、そっちの方に進みながら、少しずつ範囲を狭めていく訳よ」
source.english: “Find a direction where she reacts differently. Head that way and narrow it down little by little.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「That's right. First, you make Kuro stand somewhere. Then you spin her round and round while playing shiritori with her.」
【Bosun】 「When you find a direction where her reaction's different, then you head that way, gradually narrowing down the area all the while.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それでしりとりが二回三回続くようになった、もうしめたもんだ。そっちの方に進めば嵐が来る、少なくとも雨水は手に入る」
source.english: “When she keeps going for two or three answers, you've got it. Go that way, and a storm comes. At least you'll get rainwater.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あんた達、もしかしなくても馬鹿だろう……」
source.english: “…You really are idiots, aren't you…”

source.japanese: 真水が乏しくなるというからには、きっと空は銅[あかがね]融[と]かしたような油照りで、火の箭[や]の陽差しに白い肌を赤膨れさせたクロの夜店の回転籤[くじ]とくるくるくる、に、取り巻く船員達はやいのとしりとり言葉を浴びせかける情景は何の厭勝の儀かさもなくば、絞める鶏の肉質を高める為の虐待か。思い浮かべただけで舌の根に苦酸っぱい汁が湧いて、朔屋は慣れたはずの潮風の生臭さが急に喉に堪[こた]えて唾を呑み下す。
source.english: If fresh water was running short, the sky must be gleaming with a greasy heat like molten copper. Beneath sunlight's fiery arrows, Kuro's white skin blistering red, she would spin like a raffle drum at a night stall, crew around her clamoring word-chain prompts. What sort of ritual was that? Or abuse to improve the meat of a chicken before slaughter? Imagining it brought bitter, sour liquid to the back of Sakuya's tongue. The salt wind's fishy smell, which he ought to have grown used to, suddenly caught in his throat. He swallowed.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「And once she can continue the chain two or three times, that's when you stop. You keep going that direction, a storm will come, so if nothing else, you'll get a bit of rain water.」
【Naomasa】 「……There's no doubt about it, you all have to be idiots……」

Since they would have to be lacking fresh water, it would be a muggy, airless day where the sky was painted in hues of molten copper, and the rays of the sun would pierce Kuro's white skin like flaming arrows, turning it red and swollen as they spun her like a lottery machine at a night fair, round and round and round, the sailors encircling her aggressively hurling more shiritori words at her; if this scene was not some manner of ritual to ward off evil spirits, then perhaps it was some form of sadistic cruelty meant to enhance the quality of the meat of the chicken they were strangling?

Just imagining it was enough to cause some bitter juices to rise to the back of his tongue, and the fishy smell of the sea breeze, which he should already have grown accustomed to by now, suddenly filled his throat, making him swallow his saliva.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「あん、なんぞ言うたか娑婆造が」
source.english: “Eh? You say something, landlubber?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いいえなんにも」
source.english: “Nothing at all.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hmm, you say something, milksop?」
【Naomasa】 「Oh no, not a word.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ただ、それやるとクロは、何度もぐるぐるされる上に、なけなしのおつむから絞り出すようにして『言葉さがし』するから、後はしばらく使いもんにならなくなっちまう」
source.english: “Trouble is, Kuro gets spun over and over, then has to wring ‘words’ out of what little brain she's got. Leaves her useless for a while afterward.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひでぇ……」
source.english: “That's awful…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Though, if you do that, not only is Kuro spun around, again and again, she also has to wring out what little brainpower she has for the "word search", so she's completely useless for a good while after.」
【Naomasa】 「That's terrible……」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「良いじゃねえか。ひでぇてのは、てめえみたいな完全な役立たずの事よ。クロは少なくともそういう使い道があるし、なによりは嵐の時はすげえしな。クロ、『金貨』」
source.english: “What's wrong with it? Awful means someone completely useless, like you. At least Kuro can be used that way. Above all, she's amazing in a storm. Kuro. ‘Gold.’”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What's so wrong with that? What's terrible is somebody completely useless like you. At least Kuro has that much going for her, and more importantly, she's damn amazing to have when a storm comes around. Kuro, 『Gold Coin(Kinka)』」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「えーと、えーと、えーと、えーとぅ……。
　うう、うう、なんか、頭、熱く……あっ。
『カタツムリ』……！」
source.english:
“Um, um, um, umm… Ooh, ooh.
Kuro's head… it's getting hot…
Ah. ‘Doll’…!”

source.japanese:
水夫長に嘲罵されるのにも慣れつつある朔屋を哀しと嘆くべきなのか、それとも嘆くというのはもう少し高級な人間にのみ許された精神活動なのだと、真実役立たずである朔屋には侮蔑の追突きくらわしてやるところか。
　ともかく、クロの頭上にもわもわと、真夏の岩床に立ちのぼるような空気の揺らぎが髪の間から、無理矢理回転させ続けたお陰で白子の頭に異常な発熱が籠もるのに、朔屋は慌てて足下の水張ったバケツに海綿を浸して片手でしぼり、クロの額に押し当てれば知恵熱に水気が蒸れて物見櫓に温室めいた温気が満つる。
source.english:
Should one grieve that Sakuya was growing accustomed to the boatswain's abuse? Or was grief a spiritual exercise reserved for finer men, leaving a genuine good-for-nothing like him fit only for one more jab of contempt?
In any event, the air above Kuro's head shimmered through her hair like heat rising from rock in midsummer. Forced to keep her brain turning, the albino girl had built up an extraordinary fever in her skull. Sakuya hurriedly dipped a sponge into the bucket at his feet, wrung it out one-handed, and pressed it to her forehead. The heat of thought steamed the moisture away, filling the lookout with the warmth of a greenhouse.
“…Hm? Just now…?”

source.japanese:
このバケツに張った水とて船暮らしには貴重品で、残った分は後で洗濯物に回される手筈だ。
　水夫長としては望遠鏡で片手が塞がった朔屋でも搾[しぼ]りやすいようにと海綿の塊を持ちだしてきたつもりが、クロの額に押し当てたなり手を止めた彼に、こんな簡単仕事でも手間取ると焦れた様子で、
source.english:
Even the water in this bucket was precious aboard a ship. What remained would be used for laundry later.
The boatswain had brought a lump of sponge to make squeezing easier for Sakuya, whose other hand was occupied by the telescope. Seeing him stop with it pressed to Kuro's forehead, he grew impatient at incompetence in so simple a task.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uuhm, uuhm, uuhm, uuhmmm……. Uuh, unh, head, kind of…… getting hot……ah. 『Snail(Katatsumuri)』……!」

Should we lament it as pitiful that Sakuya was growing used to being verbally abused by the Bosun, or should the act of lamenting itself be a mental activity reserved only for a slightly higher class of human being, leaving us to instead deliver a parting blow of derision to the genuinely shiftless Sakuya?

Regardless, something rose thickly from the top of Kuro's head: from the gaps between her hair came air swaying as though it were rising from igneous bedrock in midsummer; as a result of her brain being forced to keep working, the albino's head was now generating an abnormal amount of heat, so Sakuya quickly soaked a sponge in the bucket full of water by his feet, squeezing it with one hand, and when he pushed it against Kuro's brow, the moisture turned to steam from her developmental fever, shrouding the watchtower in a sultry heat like they were standing in a greenhouse.
【Naomasa】 「……Hmm? Did she just……?」

Even the water that filled this bucket was a precious commodity for those living on a ship, and what remained of it was planned to be used for the laundry later. The Bosun had brought along a lump of sponge so that even Sakuya, whose one hand was occupied with the telescope, could easily wring it out, but upon witnessing the way he stopped moving as soon as he pressed it against Kuro's forehead, he seemed to have grown impatient, irritated that even such a simple task was taking Sakuya this long,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なのにてめえと来たら、油断すりゃあ酒はちょろまかすわ仕事はさぼるわ下級水夫にいらねえちょっかいをかけるわ。
　……『リネン』。
　ったく、てめえって奴あよう」
source.english:
“You, meanwhile, steal liquor the moment I look away, shirk work, meddle with the junior sailors for no reason…
‘Linen.’
Honestly, you…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「水夫長、水夫長、今、クロが」
source.english: “Bosun, Bosun. Kuro just—”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「But when it comes to you, the second I relax my guard, there you go, off pilfering booze and slacking off on watch, then messing with and causing more trouble for the sailors. ……『Linen』. I swear, you are such a─」
【Naomasa】 「Bosun, Bosun, just now, Kuro just─」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「うるせえ、余計な口きくな。
　雲の一つでも、しっかりめっけねえことには、そいつは解いてやらんぜ」
source.english:
“Shut up. Cut the chatter.
Find me at least one cloud, or that thing stays tied on.”

source.japanese: 宝島を求めて海原遙かを望見し続けたあまりに望遠鏡と一体化してしまった御伽話の水夫はだしに、朔屋が望遠鏡と頭を一つに戒められているのは、確かに彼が自分の枕の破れ目を繕[つくろ]う為に、乾してあった下級水夫のパンツを切り裂いたことが露見したからなのだが、だとしてもあんまりに過ぎると抗議しようとして、そこで先ほど気づいた事をまた思い出した。
source.english: Like the fairy-tale sailor who searched so long for a treasure island that he became one with his telescope, Sakuya was bound to his. Admittedly, he had been caught cutting up a junior sailor's drying underpants to patch his own torn pillow. But even so, this was too much. As he prepared to protest, he remembered what he had just noticed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いい加減に解いて下さいよう。うっかり転んだりぶつけたりしたら、目に刺さっちまいますってこんなの。いえそうじゃなく、今、負けたの水夫長のほ……」
source.english: “Untie it, please. If I fall or hit something, it'll stick into my eye. No, that's not it. Just now, you're the one who lost—”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Shut up, I didn't ask. Until you manage to find me just one measly cloud, I won't be taking that off your mug.」

As though to upstage a sailor from a fairy tale who had continued to look out across the distant sea in search of a treasure island for so long that he ended up fusing with his telescope, the telescope had been fastened to Sakuya's head, and while it was certainly true that this was a consequence of him being caught ripping apart the underwear of a deck boy, which had been hung out to dry, in order to repair a tear in his pillow, he was still about to protest that this was going too far, but that was only until he remembered something that he had noticed just earlier.
【Naomasa】 「Just take this off my face already. If I trip on accident or bump into something, it's gonna stab me right in the eye. No, that's not it, Bosun, you just-, you're the one who lo……」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「俺がなんだと、リネンのなにが間違って……うん？　クロ『竹馬』」
source.english: “I what? What's wrong with linen—hm? Kuro. ‘Trapeze.’”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What are you talking about, what's the problem with linen……hm? Kuro,『Stilts(Takeuma)』」

source.japanese:
反射的に怒鳴り返してから水夫長も、ようやく心に引っかかったと見えた。クロのしりとりが『ん』音で終わっていなかったことを。
　またクロもおずおずと続けた、続けられた。
source.english:
Only after shouting back did the boatswain seem to notice what had snagged in his mind: Kuro's word had not ended in n.
Timidly, she tried again—and this time, continued.

target.text: Though he roared back reflexively, it seemed the Bosun had finally noticed something niggling at his mind. That Kuro's choice of shiritori word did not end with an『n』sound. Once more, Kuro continued haltingly; she was able to continue.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あの……『まつげ』……」
source.english: “Um… ‘Eyelash’…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uhmm…… 『Eyelashes(Matsuge)』……」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「！　朔屋、どうだ、まだ何も見えンか」
source.english: “! Sakuya! Anything yet?”

source.japanese: ───クロの眸[ひとみ]と顔つきに僅かながらも、張りが。
source.english: A little firmness had entered Kuro's eyes and face.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Ah! Sakuya, how about it, you see anything yet?」
───While faint, there was a hint of firmness in Kuro's gaze and countenance.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はいはい、なんにも……いや。
　水夫長、前方、
　相当離れてるが雲が見える！
　こっからの距離だと細かくは見えない。
　ただかなり黒いような」
source.english:
“Yes, yes, noth—no. Bosun, ahead.
A long way off,
but I can see clouds!
Too far to make out details.
They look pretty black, though.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Yeah, yeah, there's nothi……no, wait. Bosun, straight ahead, it's still quite distant, but I can see clouds! Can't make out the details from this far away. But they seem pretty dark.」

source.japanese: ───かつ、朔屋が片目閉じに見据えた望遠鏡の向こう、信天翁号の針路に、青と碧と白の透明な色合いの中に一点、濁った染みが。
source.english: There, beyond the telescope through which Sakuya stared with one eye squeezed shut, a single murky stain stood along the Albatross's course amid transparent blue, green-blue, and white.

source.japanese: 風雨を孕んで濁る、乱雲の色合いが。
source.english: The murk of storm clouds heavy with wind and rain.

target.text: ───And there, in the direction that the telescope, which Sakuya gazed fixedly through with one eye held closed, was pointing, on the course of the Albatross, was a single spot of murkiness seeping into the midst of the clear hues of white, turquoise, and azure.
A murkiness heavy with wind and rain, the shade of turbulent rain clouds.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「よーし……ええぞ。
　向かう先が見えたな」
source.english:
“Right… Good.
Now we can see where we're going.”

source.japanese:
広大な海空の中でまだ微細な濁点ではあったけれど、やがて直面すれば船には吹き荒ぶ風雨と荒ぶる波濤が世界の全てとなる、そんな質量を内在させて針路に佇立する暗雲に、水夫長はむしろ待望の獰猛な微笑。色々と常識外れの信天翁号乗り組み達の心性の中でも特に、嵐を前にしてのこの昂ぶりは、朔屋には何時までも理解及ばぬ領域であろう。
　まともで、どれだけ堅牢に造られた船であろうとも時化に突入することは否むところ、ましてこの信天翁号、ただ航行しているだけでも船体のあちこちでガタがきた索具外れるわ浸水するわ、ひどい時には主罐が気絶してまる一日は目を覚まさぬ時さえあるのに。嵐など兆しの雨一粒がおりただけで皆それぞれの宗派の神仏に祈りを捧げるべきなのに（もっとも信天翁号には信仰心持ち合わせた輩など皆無に等しかったが）。
source.english:
Still a tiny dark point in the vast sea and sky. Yet those clouds held a mass that, once encountered, would make raging wind, rain, and waves the ship's entire world. The boatswain gave them a savage smile of welcome. Of all the Albatross crew's departures from common sense, this excitement before a storm would probably forever remain beyond Sakuya's understanding.
Even a proper, stoutly built ship would refuse to enter heavy weather. This was the Albatross, whose loose rigging fell away and whose hull leaked during ordinary sailing. Sometimes the main boiler even fainted and failed to wake for a whole day. At the first heralding raindrop, everyone ought to pray to the gods of their respective faiths—though virtually no one aboard possessed religious feeling.

source.japanese:
なのに信天翁号は、嵐を前にして細胞に賦活液を注射されたかに活力を漲[みなぎ]らせつつの、ただそのやけくそな活気は覚醒剤を入れた兵士と同質のもので、朔屋にしても初めてというわけではないがどうにも馴染めない。
　おまけにはこの時は、クロの反応も些[いささ]か異様であった。朔屋が乱雲に望遠鏡の筒先向けた際、置き台代わりと頭の天辺に載せられた海綿の、絞りが甘くて雫がたらたら垂れるのも構わず、また振り落としもせず載せたままなのが、地蔵なら苔むした頭に雲雀が巣掛けても微動だにせぬだろうがこれはクロ、普段なら立っているだけでも体の芯がぶれぶれの彼女にしてはどうにも奇妙だった。
source.english:
Yet faced with a storm the Albatross surged with life, as though every cell had been injected with some activating serum. It was the desperate vitality of a soldier on stimulants, and although Sakuya had seen it before, he could never grow used to it.
More disturbing was Kuro's reaction. When Sakuya trained the telescope on the storm clouds, he rested the sponge on the crown of her head as a makeshift stand. He had wrung it badly, and water trickled down, yet she neither objected nor shook it off. A stone Jizo might remain still while a lark nested on its mossy head—but this was Kuro, whose very center usually wavered even when she was only standing. It was most peculiar.

source.japanese: おまけに口からは、たまさか波長を捕らえた鉱石ラジオのアンプのように、ひっきりなしにしりとり文句を吐き出し続けてあるのだ。
source.english: And her mouth kept pouring out word-chain answers like the amplifier of a crystal radio that had happened to catch a wavelength.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Alright then……that's good. Our destination's in sight.」

It was still just a minute dot amidst the vast sea and sky, but when time came for them to confront it, the raging rainstorm and surging waves would be all-encompassing on this ship, becoming her entire world, so immense a mass was compressed within these dark clouds that yet stood motionless on their course, but far from being daunted, the Bosun was cracking a savage smile in eager anticipation. Even amongst all the other various eccentric dispositions of the crew members of the Albatross, this one in particular, this arousal before the storm, belonged to a realm so removed from the one Sakuya inhabited that he could never hope to understand it.

If sensible, no matter how sturdy one's ship was built, one would refuse to brave the stormy seas, but all the more so if the ship was this Albatross; by merely sailing along her course, the creaking heard from all around the hull would betray its age, the rigging would fall off, compartments would flood, and when it was really bad, there were even times when the main boiler would faint and go a whole day before waking up once more.

Really, the moment the first raindrops serving as the harbinger of a storm began to fall, everyone aboard this ship ought to offer up prayers to whatever gods and buddhas their respective denominations worshipped (there was virtually not a single person aboard this Albatross possessed of a pious heart, however).

And yet, the Albatross, now that she was before a tempest, surged with life as if her very cells has been injected with a revitalizing fluid, however, that desperate vigour was of the same nature as that of a soldier given a stimulant, and though this was not the first time Sakuya witnessed it, he simply could not get used to the sight.

Additionally, in times like this, Kuro's reactions were also a little queer. When Sakuya turned his telescope towards the turbulent clouds, the sponge that he'd left on top of her head, using it as a substitute for a stand, simply remained there, and uncaring of the fact that he was still gently squeezing it and dripping water down on her head, she did not shake it off; were she a Jizou, then a skylark would build a nest on her moss-covered head, so motionless was Kuro; for a girl whose body normally wobbled just from standing still alone, there was something undeniably strange about this.
And to top it off, like a crystal radio's amplifier that happened to catch a wavelength, her mouth incessantly rattled off a chain of words for shiritori, one after the other.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「『げんこつ』…『つばめ』…『メンコ』…『コマ』…『マント』…『とけい』…」
source.english: “‘Hand’… ‘Doll’… ‘Leaf’… ‘Fist’… ‘Top’… ‘Pocket watch’…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「『Fist(Genkotsu)』… 『Swallow(Tsubame)』… 『Menko(Menko)』… 『Piece(Koma)』… 『Mantle(Manto)』… 『Clock(Tokei)』…」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おお？　なんだか今回は過敏だな。
　ま、いざ突入となったら頼むわ、
『船長』！」
source.english:
“Oh? Extra sensitive this time.
Well, once we go in, we're counting on you,
Captain!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Oh? A little oversensitive this time around. Well, we'll be relying on you when it comes time to break through,『Captain』!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あい！　クロがんばるよ。
　がんばって、がんばるから、だから、
　クロは……いらない子、違うよね……？」
source.english:
“Yes! Kuro'll try hard.
Try hard, try very hard, so…
Kuro isn't an unwanted child, right…?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Aye! Kuro will work hard. Work real hard, will do Kuro's best, so, Kuro isn't……an unwanted child, right……?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おうおう、違うとも」
source.english: “Aye, aye. Of course not.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hey now, nothing of the sort.」

source.japanese:
下級水夫達をかき集める為に、水夫長は熟練した者にありがちな鷹揚なぞんざいさで櫓の梯子を下っていくところであったが、相好を崩したのがいかにも勝手で、朔屋にはどうにもクロが不憫に思えて。
　けれど同時に、朔屋の腹の、底から圧してきたのは、情交の輪の中から取り残されてしまったかのような息苦しさ、それは多分きっと、妬ましさという感情の、日頃は自分と同じくらいに無能と軽んぜられているクロでさえ、時と場合を得れば泥中から洗われた金の指輪の輝きを見せる、なに自分はなんなのだろうと。
source.english:
The boatswain descended the lookout ladder to gather the junior sailors, with the careless ease common to veterans. His beaming face seemed awfully self-serving. Sakuya felt sorry for Kuro.
But at the same time, something pressed up from the bottom of his belly, a suffocation like being left outside a circle of affection. Probably, surely, envy. Even Kuro, normally despised as every bit as useless as he was, could shine like a gold ring washed out of mud when her moment came. What, then, was he?

target.text: With a composed carelessness common to experienced men, the Bosun climbed down the ladder to gather up the deck boys, but the way he grinned so broadly seemed awfully self-centered to Sakuya, and he couldn't help but find Kuro pitiable.

At the same time, however, there was a weight pressing up from the pit of Sakuya's stomach, a breathlessness, as if he'd been cast out from a circle of sexual intimacy, and this was probably───surely───the emotion of envy; he was envious that even Kuro, who was normally belittled as being incompetent just as much as he himself, would, given the right time and place, shine with the brilliance of a gold ring washed clean from the mud; who, or what, did he amount to then?

source.japanese: ───風を受けて千切れんばかりに唸りをあげているのはロビンソン式風力計、などいう上等の品などもしあったとしても早晩質草に叩きこまれてしまうこの船では、雨風に打たれ翻[ひるがえ]っているのも物干し綱から取りこみ忘れられた下級水夫の半ズボン、これでは風力計添え物のあの多色の吹き流しの替わりにもなりはしないが、今、ぱんと銃声のような響きで風に持って行かれてしまってみると、喪失感は奇妙に大きい。願わくば持ち主の下級水夫君に半ズボンの替えがあらんことを。もしないのなら、補充が着くまで彼は下半身を涼しく過ごすことになろう、この暴風雨の中で。
source.english: Roaring in the wind, almost tearing itself apart, was a Robinson cup anemometer—or would have been, had so fine an instrument existed aboard this ship. It would soon have found its way to a pawnbroker anyway. What actually whipped in the wind and rain was a pair of shorts some junior sailor had forgotten on the clothesline. They could not even pass for the colored streamers sometimes mounted with the instrument. Yet when the wind snatched them away with a crack like a gunshot, the sense of loss was curiously profound. May their owner possess a second pair. If not, his lower half would remain well ventilated until replacements arrived—in the midst of this very storm.

source.japanese:
ただ風雨の強さは干し綱に忘れられた衣装をもぎとってはいっても、甲板上のバラックの屋根や羽目板を剥いだり駆け回る下級水夫達を押し倒すまでには至らない。
　以前嵐に突入した際は、手近な索具に腕絡みつけていないとたちどころに舷側越えて波濤に叩き落とされそうになった朔屋でも、この度はなんとか船の縦揺れ横揺れに足下滑らせてバラックの壁に叩きつけられる程度で済んであり、肩を打ちつけた骨が挫ける程ではない。
　頬歪めて索環に掴まり立ちした、朔屋の頭上で景気悪くくぐもった音が爆ぜて、ぶちまけたのが夥[おびただ]しい煤煙だ、運悪く煙突の下で足を止めてしまっている。
source.english:
Strong enough to tear forgotten clothes from a line, the wind and rain had not yet stripped roofs or boards from the shacks, or knocked down the junior sailors running about.
In the previous storm, Sakuya would have been swept over the rail and into the sea at once without an arm wrapped around nearby rigging. This time, the ship's pitching and rolling merely made him slip and slam into a shack wall—not hard enough to break his shoulder.
Grimacing, he hauled himself upright by a ringbolt. A muffled, dispiriting blast sounded overhead and dumped an enormous quantity of soot on him. Unluckily, he had stopped beneath a funnel.

source.japanese:
凸凹と船上構造物上に突き出た煙突の一つは呆れたことに中程から折れてしまって煤煙を宙に逃すどころか甲板上に蛸の墨と吐きかけて、何故誰も修理しないのかと嘆かわしくなった後で何故何時まで中折れのままでいられるのかと怪訝の念がこみあげる。幾度の時化、荒れ海を越えてもそれ以上ひどく壊れたり千切れ飛んだりしないその中折れ煙突は、ある種崖の縁ぎりぎりで太古から留まり続ける球形の奇岩といった自然界の奇観に似通う不思議さを纏[まと]うてすら。
　何にせよ雨と波飛沫でぐずぐずのところに煤粉ぶちまけられた朔屋は炭鉱内の浸水で溺死した哀れな鉱夫の相を呈し、つい彼は機関長へ毒づきたくなって、ぐっとこらえて、何しろあの奇怪な紳士の耳は機関室にあってなお全船に届いていることもあり得ると。
source.english:
One of the funnels jutting unevenly above the superstructure had, unbelievably, broken off halfway up. Instead of releasing its smoke into the air, it spat it across the deck like an octopus squirting ink. First came the lament: why had no one repaired it? Then the bewilderment: how could it remain half-broken forever? Storm after storm, rough sea after rough sea, it neither broke any further nor tore free. It had taken on the mystery of some natural wonder, a round boulder balanced since antiquity on the very lip of a cliff.
At any rate, already sodden with rain and spray, Sakuya now looked like some pitiable miner drowned in a flooded pit. He nearly cursed the chief engineer, then restrained himself. That uncanny gentleman's ears might well reach every corner of the ship, even from the engine room.

source.japanese:
船員服の袖[そで]で顔を拭ったところで煤黒を伸ばすだけであり、これならばいっそもう少し拓けたところで雨風を浴びた方が洗い流されようと、駆け出そうとして朔屋は陰から現れた黒い塊、その大なる質量と鉢合わせしそうになって足を滑らせた。
　今度は背中をこれでもかと打って声も無くのたうつ青年の顔上にぬうと出たその黒いの、目鼻立ちも彼の記号である刺青も煤煙に塗りこめられて一見では何の妖怪黒入道かの有り様ではあったが、野太い声は水夫長のものであった。どうやら彼も先の煤煙の噴射に巻きこまれたらしい。
source.english:
Wiping his face with his uniform sleeve only spread the blackness. Better to stand somewhere open and let wind and rain wash it off. He started to run, nearly collided with a great black mass emerging from the shadows, and slipped.
This time he struck his back hard and writhed without a sound. The black thing loomed over his face. Soot obscured its features and its identifying tattoo, making it look like some monstrous black monk. But the deep voice belonged to the boatswain. Apparently he too had been caught in that blast of smoke.

target.text: ───A Robinson cup anemometer groaning on the verge of being ripped apart as the wind struck it: had this ship been possessed of such a fine article, it would have been pawned off sooner or later; no, what was buffeted by the rainstorm and fluttering about were instead a deck boy's pair of shorts that the owner had forgotten to retrieve from the clothesline, and this certainly made a poor substitute for the multi-coloured wind sock that usually supplemented an anemometer, but just now, when they were taken by the gales with the echoing clap of a gunshot, the sense of loss was strangely profound.

If at all possible, let us pray that the deck boy whose shorts were lost may have a spare pair somewhere. For if he does not, then he will have to pass the time with a refreshing breeze around his nethers until he can procure a replacement, and in this violent rainstorm at that.

However, though the force of the rain and wind was strong enough to snatch away clothes forgotten on the clothesline, it was not enough to knock down the deck boys running about while stripping off the roofs and cladding of the shacks on the upper deck. Even Sakuya, who during the prior storm would have been thrown overboard by the surging waves in an instant had he not wrapped his arms around the nearby rigging, managed this time to only loose his footing and crash into the wall of a shack as the ship pitched and rolled, and while he did hit his shoulder, the impact wasn't severe enough to fracture a bone.

Cheeks contorting, he grabbed a shackle and pulled himself back on his feet, but then a muffled, ominous sound erupted above Sakuya's head, and an immense amount of soot and smoke spewed forth; unfortunately, Sakuya had come to a halt right beneath a funnel.

One of the funnels protruding from the uneven heights of the ship's superstructure had, quite absurdly, broken off in the middle, and rather than releasing its dark fumes skyward, it spewed soot onto the upper deck like octopus ink; after lamenting why in the world nobody had bothered to repair it, a sense of puzzlement filled his heart; how had it managed to remain standing all this time while broken in the middle? How many times must it have crossed the stormy seas, and yet it had not been torn to pieces or simply broken off.

This snapped funnel even possessed a certain mystique, calling to mind one of the wondrous sights of nature, similar to an unusually globular rock perched on the very brink of a cliff, held fast in its impossible position since time immemorial. At any rate, Sakuya, already a drenched mess from the rain and sea spray, had now been covered in a heap of sooty dust, and he resembled a pitiful miner who had drowned in a flooded coal mine; he couldn't help but want to curse the Chief Engineer's name, but he held his tongue, for it was quite possible that the ears of that mysterious gentleman still reached all around the ship even as the man himself remained in the engine room.

When he wiped his face with the sleeve of his sailor clothes, all he accomplished was smearing the black soot around, so with that being the case, he thought, then the rainstorm would hopefully wash it away if he stood somewhere more open, but just as he was about to take off, a black lump emerged from the shadows; he almost collided with that great mass, and then he slipped.

Was my shoulder not enough, the young man tried to say as he hit his back against the deck, writhing soundlessly, and the black thing suddenly slid into view above Sakuya's face, both its features and distinctive tattoo plastered in soot and smoke, so at first glance, it might have been mistaken for some kind of Kuronyuudou yokai, but that deep voice definitely belonged to the Bosun. It seemed that he, too, had been caught up in the eruption of soot and smoke just earlier. (TN: Kuronyuudou is a big, black, and bald man. While it is another name for the Umibouzu, he can also show himself by tree roots.)

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なぁにをンなところでぐだぐだと寝っ転がってけつかるか。寝てるくれぇなら、石炭室で釜焚きでも手伝ってこいやぁ」
source.english: “What are you lying around here for? If you've time for a nap, go help stoke in the coal room!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「げ、げほっ、うう俺ゃ、下層甲板倉庫の水漏れに砂嚢積んできたんですよう。ほんで次の指示をもらいに来たッつぅのに……」
source.english: “C-cough… I just piled sandbags against a leak in the lower-deck storeroom. Came up for my next orders…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ま、いいや。釜焚きの手伝いしてくりゃいいんスね？　行って来まぁす……」
source.english: “Fine, whatever. Help stoke, right? Off I go…”

source.japanese: 黒く汚れた中にぽかりと空いた水夫長の口腔の肉色は凶暴な狒狒めいていたが、猛る風雨を打ち消すほどの蛮声は途切れて、為に吹き荒れる風が一際激しさ増したかの、この時彼は少なからず唖然と言葉を失っていたのである。
source.english: The fleshy color of the boatswain's open mouth, gaping amid all that black grime, made him resemble a savage baboon. But the bellow that could drown out wind and rain had ceased, and the storm seemed suddenly louder. For once, astonishment had struck him speechless.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What the hell do you think you're up to, napping in a place like this. If you've got time to sleep, then get your ass down to the stokehole and help fire the boilers!」
【Naomasa】 「Kh, cough, ugh, I have been down on the lower deck, piling up sand bags to plug the leak in the hold. I promise, I only came here to get my next set of orders……」
【Naomasa】 「No, whatever. I just have to help with stoking the fire, yeah? Off I gooo……」

Amidst the black grime, the fleshy colour of the bosun's wide-open oral cavity resembled that of a savage baboon, and his voice, so rough and wild it seemed to drown out the fierce rainstorm, was suddenly cut short, which made the raging gales seem to intensify as a result; in this moment, the man was more than a little stunned, to the point of speechlessness.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「朔屋おめぇ、何か風に飛ばされた木っ端でも頭にぶち喰らったか？　てめえが文句もいわず釜焚きに走るてな、いってえどういう風の吹き回しだ」
source.english: “Sakuya, did some flying timber hit you in the head? Running off to stoke without a complaint? What's got into you?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなひどい。俺はただ、こう船がぎしぎし軋んでちゃあ、さぼったところで落ち着かないだけで」
source.english: “That's cruel. With the ship creaking like this, I just can't relax even if I shirk.”

source.japanese: 風に負けじと張り上げた声で気後れを隠す、朔屋の言葉は真が半分残りは偽り、じっとしていられない気持ちは本当ではあったし、船が軋んで呻[うめ]いで大揺れするのには船内のどこに隠れたって同じで、それで働く発心起こす辺りは盆だけは忙しがる村の怠け者と変わらない。ただ朔屋の中で少しばかり鬱屈していたのがクロへの心象である。
source.english: He raised his voice against the wind to hide his unease. Half true, half false. He really could not keep still. The ship would creak, groan, and pitch wherever he hid. Letting that inspire him to work made him no different from a village idler who became busy only at the Bon festival. But something else had been brooding within him: his feelings about Kuro.

source.japanese:
日頃は邪魔者余計者扱いされるあの白子の少女が、嵐の時には船の長にと奉られる。嵐の時には、嵐の時だけ、日照りの時のみ社の奥から式次第と共に雨師さまと変わりないご都合者、しかし朔屋にはその『時だけ』さえない。
　役立たず扱いに悪慣れした朔屋にして他人の能力を嫉[そね]む心が残っていたのは、全く余計としか言う他なく、青年を今だけ忙しく駆りたてたところで人が彼を評する目は変わらないというのに。
source.english:
