Normally the albino girl was treated as an encumbrance, an unwanted extra. In a storm, they exalted her as master of the ship. In a storm—in a storm alone. She was a convenient little divinity, like a rain god brought from the shrine with all due ceremony only in time of drought. But Sakuya had no such moment. Not even one.
That a man so accustomed to being called useless still had enough spirit to envy another's talents was entirely more than he needed. It might spur him busily onward for now, but it would not change how anyone saw him.

source.japanese: ちらちらとバラックの向こうの操舵室を窺う朔屋に、懸念と勘違いして水夫長は、
source.english: Sakuya kept glancing past the shacks toward the wheelhouse. The boatswain mistook it for concern.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Sakuya, were you hit in the head by a piece of wood blown around in the storm or something? I never dreamed you'd run down to stoke the boilers with not a single complaint, where is this coming from?」
【Naomasa】 「That's not very nice. It's just, with the ship creaking and grating like this, even if I tried to slack off, I wouldn't be able to relax.」

Straining his voice against the wind to mask his nerves, Sakuya offered words that were half truth but also half lie, for while it certainly was true that he felt unable to just sit still, and no matter where he hid inside the ship, the creaking, groaning, and violent rolling would be the same, for this to be what brought about this spiritual awakening to productivity made him no different from the village idler who only bestirs himself during the Bon festival. The only thing that left Sakuya feeling ever-so-slightly frustrated, however, was the impression he held of Kuro.

That albino girl was usually treated as nothing but a superfluous nuisance, but when it stormed, she was revered as the ship's captain. In times of storm, and only then, a convenient soul to keep on hand, no different from the rain god being pulled out from the depths of the shrine as part of a ceremony held only in times of drought; but Sakuya did not have even just that "only then".

For a man like Sakuya, who'd already grown desensitized to being treated as useless, to still harbour feelings of envy towards other people's talents deep in his heart could only be described as utterly unnecessary; for all that he was spurred into a temporary flurry of activity right now, it would not alter the way the world perceives him.
Sakuya kept glancing towards the wheelhouse on the other side of the shack, and the Bosun, misinterpreting that as concern,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……そんなに船長が不安かよ。
　何を今さら、お前だって嵐ン時のクロは見てるだろうにな」
source.english:
“…That worried about the captain?
Why now? You've seen Kuro in a storm yourself.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……You really that worried about the captain? No need for that now, you've already seen what Kuro's like during a storm yourself.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まあ確かに日頃が日頃だ。
　俺だって慣れてなけりゃあ、
　鼻で笑ったことだろうぜ」
source.english:
“Well, knowing what she's usually like…
I'd have snorted too,
if I wasn't used to it.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「アレが嵐の時だきゃあ、
　カミサマみたいになるなんてな」
source.english:
“That thing becoming like
a god only when there's a storm.”

source.japanese: と水夫長も朔屋に倣[なら]って操舵室へと顎先向けた、そこへ波が巻き上げたホンダワラの束が一塊、頭にべしゃりと被さって、田舎芝居の出来の悪い鬘のよう、沈み加減の朔屋にもはなはだ滑稽で失笑の、幸い水夫長の視界は海草に塞がれ気づかれずに済んだのだが、口の端に残った笑いは次の言葉で疑問符に消しやられた。
source.english: Following Sakuya's gaze, the boatswain tipped his chin toward the wheelhouse. Just then a wave-tossed clump of sargassum flopped onto his head like a bad wig in a country play. Even in his gloom Sakuya found it comical enough to let out a laugh. Fortunately, the seaweed covered the boatswain's eyes, and he escaped notice. But the smile still clinging to Sakuya's lips vanished into a puzzled frown at what came next.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well, given how she normally acts. If I weren't used to it myself, I'd have scoffed at the idea.」
【Bosun】 「Only when it storms does that girl become godlike, of all the things.」

After saying so, the Bosun followed Sakuya's example and also swung his chin towards the wheelhouse, and just as he did, a clump of Sargassum seaweed whirled up by the waves landed right on his head with a wet slap, like a poorly made wig from a play at a provincial theatre, and even the sombre Sakuya couldn't suppress a smirk at how comical a sight it made, but fortunately, the Bosun's vision was blocked by the seaweed, and he never noticed; any trace of a smile yet lingering by the corners of his mouth was quickly wiped off by question marks when he heard the words that followed.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……そういや思い出したぞ。
　この海域の位置、聞いた時から奥歯に引っかかってたんだ」
source.english:
“…Now I remember.
The location of these waters has been nagging at me ever since I heard it.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「昔、クロを拾ったのがこの辺りだったらしいぜ───」
source.english: “Apparently this is around where they picked Kuro up long ago—”

source.japanese:
───股ぐらの底から空気の塊に押し上げられる浮遊感は、朔屋の驚愕の形容ではなく、波が信天翁号を高く押し上げた為のもの、船体が分解し去ることこそ無かったものの、次の瞬間には舳先を下にしての橇下り、危険な滑走感に開けたままの歯が舌を噛みそうになって、青年は天地が返る恐怖にささくれが刺さるのも厭[いと]わずバラックの窓枠を必死に掴む。
　足下が急角度の壁になるような船の揺れにも水夫長殿、長靴の蹠に氷壁用のアイゼンでも生やしているのか仁王立ちの姿勢崩さず、むっつりと腕組みしたまま、解れた記憶の端を解くのに集中、している限りは波の揺れなど届かぬかのくそ落ち着き振りで。
source.english:
The sensation of being pushed upward by a mass of air beneath his crotch was not a description of Sakuya's astonishment. A wave had lifted the Albatross high. Her hull did not disintegrate, but the next instant she went sledding down bow-first. The dangerous slide nearly made him bite his tongue before he could close his mouth. Terrified of earth and sky overturning, he clutched a shack's window frame, heedless of splinters.
The boatswain, meanwhile, stood planted as the deck became a steep wall underfoot. Did the soles of his boots have ice-climbing crampons? His arms remained grimly folded while he concentrated on unraveling the loose end of memory. As long as that occupied him, the waves seemed unable to reach his damned composure.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「俺がそれを聞いたのは先代の水夫長からだ。その先代の水夫長も、更に前の代からの水夫長に聞いた、といっていたな」
source.english: “Heard it from the bosun before me. And he said he'd heard it from the bosun before him.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「いや、正確にはこの嵐からは、いくらか離れた辺りだったらしいが───」
source.english: “Well, strictly speaking, somewhere a little way from this storm, apparently—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うべっ、べっ、べっべっべっ、
　待てよ、それが本当なら、クロは一体いくつなんですよ。とてもそういう年には見えないでしょうがっ」
source.english:
“Bleh, bleh, bleh—wait.
If that's true, how old is Kuro? She doesn't look anything like that age!”

source.japanese: 甲板上で迂闊にも固定されていない物は全て海底に流す勢いで洗っていく被せ波をさんざんに鼻や口内に流しこまれて朔屋は咳きこんだが、塩水がつんと沁みるのも構わず吐き出して、水夫長に喚き返した。
source.english: A wave swept the deck as if determined to send everything not secured to the bottom. It poured freely into Sakuya's nose and mouth. He coughed, spat despite the stinging salt water, and shouted back at the boatswain.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Right, that reminds me. The location of these waters has been bothering me ever since I first heard about it, like something stuck in one of my molars.」
【Bosun】 「Supposedly, a long time ago, this is around where Kuro was first picked up───」

───The sensation of weightlessness, as though being hoisted by a mass of air from deep in his groin, was no mere metaphor for Sakuya's shock, but rather because a wave had flung the Albatross high in the air; although the hull was not completely torn apart, the next moment, the bow dove sharply, and she went sledding down, the perilous sensation of sliding on the verge of causing his still-open mouth to bite down on his tongue, and the terror of the world itself turning upside down made the young man desperately clutch the window frame of the shack, uncaring of the splinters stabbing into his skin.

Though the ship pitched so deep that the deck beneath their feet turned into a steep wall, perhaps the Bosun had crampons for climbing ice walls growing out from beneath the soles of his boots, for he remained in an imposing stance, posture unbroken, taciturn with his arms crossed, concentrating on unravelling the yarn of memory he had grasped but a single thread of, and for as long as he did, he looked infuriatingly calm, as though the puny heaving of the waves was beneath his notice.
【Bosun】 「I heard that from the previous bosun. And that previous bosun, he heard it from the bosun before him, or so he said.」
【Bosun】 「No, strictly speaking, it was somewhere a little ways away from this storm, supposedly, but───」
【Naomasa】 「Bhleh, peh, pehpehpeh, wait a minute, if that's true, then just how old is Kuro? Nothing about her looks that old.」

The waves washed over the deck with such force that anything carelessly left unfastened on the upper deck might well have been swept away to the bottom of the sea, and Sakuya coughed as it flooded his nose and mouth, but with not a care for how the salty water stung him, he spat it out, yelling back at the Bosun.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「知るかよ。俺だって聞いた話なんだから。
　それでも確かにクロは、俺が初めてこれに乗りこんだ時からいたな。今と同じ、変わらない姿で」
source.english:
“How should I know? It's only what I heard.
But Kuro was certainly here when I first came aboard. Looked the same as she does now. No change.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「How should I know? Even I've only heard all this from others. Still, it's certainly true that Kuro was there when I first boarded this ship. And looking no different from how she does right now.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おまけに、拾ったっつうたが、
　ほんとは空から落ちてきたらしい。
　……なにもないところからな」
source.english:
“And I said picked up, but apparently she actually fell out of the sky.
Out of nothing.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「嵐を呼ぶ云々より、そっちの方が不気味じゃねえかどう考えても」
source.english: “That's creepier than any business about calling storms, however you look at it.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「On top of that, while I said they picked her up, it seems she actually fell from the sky. ……And from right out of thin air at that.」
【Naomasa】 「Isn't that way more ominous than that whole stormcalling thing, no matter how you look at it?」

source.japanese:
───水場を遠く離れた陸上に、突如空から魚や蛙の類その他が降り注ぐという奇現象は確かにある。その落下物の目録は多岐に渡るが、人が振ってきたという事例は存在しない。だというのに。
　
　───空から落ちてきた、クロ。
　
　当時から変わらぬ姿でいるという、クロ。
source.english:
There were indeed strange occurrences in which fish, frogs, and other things suddenly rained from the sky onto land far from water. The catalogue of fallen objects was extensive. But no recorded case had ever included a human being. And yet—
Kuro, fallen from the sky.
Kuro, said to have remained unchanged since that day.

target.text: ───There are certainly strange phenomena where, on land far from water, fish and frogs and the like will suddenly rain down from the skies. The list of these fallen objects is extensive, but there exist no prior cases of people falling. And yet. ───From the skies she fell, Kuro. Said to be unchanged from that time to this, Kuro.

source.japanese:
何の値打ちもないと高を括って砂浜に拾い上げた、下らない、磨り減って濁った硝子瓶の緑の欠片に思いもかけず鋭い縁が残っていて、指を切ってしまったような驚きだった。
　傾いだ信天翁号の角度なりにバラックの壁に背中を有無言わせず押しつけていた力が緩み、やがて足も甲板にどうにか降りて、船が復したのを伝えてきたことにも気づかないほど、朔屋は困惑していたという。
source.english:
It was like picking up a worthless, worn, clouded-green shard of bottle glass from the beach, only to discover the edge still sharp when it cut one's finger.
The force pinning his back to the shack wall slackened as the Albatross righted herself. His feet at last found the deck again, but Sakuya was too bewildered even to notice.

source.japanese:
長い時代と深い含みを潜[ひそ]ませた水夫長との会話は、しかし実際には風雨と波の間にスタッカートを爪弾き出すように怒鳴り交わされて、時間にすれば二・三分に足らず、水夫長もそれ以上は嵐の中でお喋りに労を費やすを好まず、打ち切ってぶつ切りに。
　朔屋には気にかかることなのだが、水夫長はそれ以上とりあわず、青年を出会い頭の胴間声通りに機関室方面へと追いやった。
source.english:
Freighted with long ages and deep implications, the conversation had in fact been shouted back and forth through wind, rain, and waves, the voices plucking out a staccato, and had lasted less than two or three minutes. The boatswain had no wish to spend any more effort on talk in the midst of a storm, and cut it abruptly short.
Sakuya was dying to know more, but the boatswain would not indulge him. True to the booming order with which they had met, he drove the young man off toward the engine room.

target.text: It was a surprise like thoughtlessly picking up what one had assumed to be a worthless, worn-down, cloudy fragment of a green glass bottle on a beach only to find it still had a sharp edge, cutting one's finger on it. The force that had been pinning him against the shack wall, dictated by the angle of the Albatross as she lurched, slackened its hold on him, and he finally managed to lower his feet back down to the deck; he did not even notice how that conveyed to him that the ship had returned to a normal angle, so bewildered was he.

His conversation with the Bosun spanned a long period of time and held deep implications, but in reality, it had been an exchange of shouts like they were plucking staccato notes in the gaps between the wind, rain, and waves, and in terms of time, it hadn't even occupied two or three minutes; the Bosun didn't seem keen on wasting any more effort to continue their chat in the middle of the storm, and so he abruptly cut it short. It still weighed heavily on Sakuya's mind, but the Bosun didn't concern himself with it any longer; he drove the young man down towards the engine room with the same guttural shouting as when they'd first collided.

source.japanese: ───もちろん朔屋は、水夫長からああも謎めいた言葉を聞かされては、御簾の向こうの貴婦人の影が狐の耳と尾を生やしていたのを覗いてしまった匹夫の勘ぐり、クロの事が頭から離れなくなって、下甲板への昇降段を下るはずの足は操舵室の窓硝子の陰で忍び足する。この嵐では大概の音など吹き散らされようものを跫音を憚るあたりはいかにも彼らしい小心だったが、この抜き足差し足に助けられて後家への夜這いを成功させた事もあり、朔屋にしてはまずまずの芸、まあ螻蛄の水練並みではある。
source.english: Of course, after hearing such mysterious words from the boatswain, Sakuya could no more get Kuro out of his head than could some common bumpkin, once he had spied fox ears and a tail on the shadow of a noblewoman behind her screen, cease his speculations. The feet meant for the companionway to the lower deck went tiptoeing instead beneath the wheelhouse windows. In this storm almost any sound would be blown away, yet he still took pains over his footfalls: cowardice entirely in character. Then again, this same soft-footed stealth had once won him a nighttime visit to a widow, so it was a tolerable art by Sakuya’s standards—though roughly on a par with a mole cricket’s swimming.

source.japanese: だが朔屋がわざわざ跫音を殺すまでもなく、慎重に覗きこんだ鼻面を叩いて窓硝子がびりびり震動した。それくらい操舵室の中は指示に張り詰め怒声で一杯、朔屋の気配など気にも留めていなかったろう。
source.english: There was no need to muffle his footsteps. As he cautiously peered in, the window glass vibrated against his nose. The wheelhouse was so taut with orders and full of angry voices that no one would have noticed him.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「───現在の進行方向、七二度……いや七九度、いや───」
source.english: “Current heading, seventy-two degrees… No, seventy-nine. No—”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんなのこの、地獄の気違い犬みたいな波と風はっ。針路が全っ然定まんない！」
source.english: “What are these winds and waves, some mad dog out of hell? We can't hold a course at all!”

source.japanese: 室内にては、シサムが何時になく真剣に位置を弾き出し、キサラはジャケットの縫い目引きちぎる勢いで舵輪を振り回し、
source.english: Inside, Sisam calculated their position with uncommon seriousness. Kisara worked the wheel so fiercely that she might tear her jacket's seams.

target.text: ───Of course, having been told something so enigmatic by the Bosun, with the suspicions held by a man of low status after witnessing the silhouette of a noblewoman through a bamboo blind grow the tails and ears of a fox, he could no longer get thoughts of Kuro out of his head, and his legs, which were supposed to descend the ladder to below decks, had instead carried him into the shadows by the wheelhouse window with sneaky steps.

It was a sort of prudence very like him that, even as nearly all sound would be blown away in this storm, he was still hesitant to make any noise with his footfalls, but it was also thanks to this tiptoeing of his that his night crawling into that widow's room at night that one time had been a success, so for the likes of Sakuya, this was a passable technique; well, it was on par with a mole cricket practicing swimming.

But there was no need for Sakuya to go out of his way to silence his footsteps, for the windowpane rattled so violently, it physically struck the tip of the nose Sakuya was discreetly pressing against it as he peered inside. That was how thick with the tension of barked commands and angry yells the inside of the wheelhouse was; no one there would have spared even a single thought for Sakuya's presence.
【Shisamu】 「───Current heading, zero-seven-two……no, zero-seven-nine, no───」
【Kisara】 「What is going on with the wind and waves, they're like mad dogs from hell! Our heading refuses to be held, it's all over the place!」
Inside the room, Shisamu was uncharacteristically serious about calculating their location, and Kisara was swinging the helm around with such force that the seams of her jacket were about to tear,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「浸水処置急いで、二〇三号船室、誰かが窓開けっ放しにしてる」
source.english: “Deal with the flooding, quickly. Cabin two-zero-three. Someone's left the window open.”

source.japanese:
そして、クロだ。
　
　白い髪、紅い眸[ひとみ]は変わらずとも、日陰に末生りの幽霊茸の娘はそこにいない。今や彼女は白狐白蛇と同種の、神がかった威と力を宿した半肉半霊の存在めいて、一挙一動腕の一振り声の一音、身口意───体と言語意識と心性と───が統合制御された、ここにおわす者こそ覚者か。
　
　これがクロなら、あれは誰だ。朔屋の撫でる手に怯えて、打たれずに済むと知ってだらしなく口を緩めた少女は誰なのか。朔屋の頼りない腕でも抱え上げられそうなひ弱い少女は今のクロの中に果たして在るのか。
source.english:
And Kuro.
White hair, red eyes—unchanged. Yet the girl who had resembled a sickly ghost mushroom grown in shade was nowhere to be seen. Now she seemed a being half flesh and half spirit, imbued with the numinous power of a white fox or serpent. Every gesture, every sweep of her arm, every note of her voice—body, speech, and mind; flesh, language, consciousness, and character—was unified and under command. Was this the awakened one who stood before them?
If this was Kuro, then who had the other been? Who was the girl who flinched from Sakuya's caress, then let her mouth sag when she realized he would not strike her? Did that frail girl, light enough for even Sakuya's unreliable arms to lift, truly exist inside this Kuro?

source.japanese:
頼もしい。勇ましい。委ねられる。
　
　嵐が狂おうが船が悲鳴に軋もうが、この白子の少女在る限りは無条件に信天翁号の航路の先を信じられる。それほどの心力が、操舵室の薄い壁一枚の向こうに今やある。
　なのに朔屋は、深井戸の底の井守と虚空の星間の琅干殿に座す飛天ほどの隔たりが意識されてならず───
source.english:
Dependable. Gallant. One could place oneself in her hands.
However wildly the storm raged, however the ship screamed and creaked, so long as this albino girl remained, one could believe without condition in whatever course lay ahead of the Albatross. Such strength of spirit now stood beyond the wheelhouse's one thin wall.
And yet Sakuya could think only of the distance between them: the distance between a newt at the bottom of a deep well and a celestial dancer enthroned in a jade palace among the stars—

source.japanese: 硝子窓の縁すれすれに見上げる青年は、硝子の面にひどく陰に凝[こご]ったかぎろいが浮いているのにたじろぎ、それがガラスに映った己の眸[ひとみ]の色だと気づいて慄然とした。
source.english: Looking up just below the window's edge, he recoiled from a darkly congealed glimmer on the glass. Realizing it was the color of his own reflected eyes chilled him.

source.japanese:
海はこの時朔屋の心を嗅ぎとったでもあるまいに、波がひどく意地悪にして、乗りきったかと思うと船の舳先を強引に向きを変えたりと弄[もてあそ]び、航海士の双子の歯をきりきり噛ませ、目を血走らせる。
　なにかが妙な嵐だった。洋上で嵐に揉まれた事は一度きりの朔屋にすらそうと感じさせる、風雨自体は並み程度なのに、波浪には何か人為的な底意が潜[ひそ]んで、船を高く押し上げては海底まで引きこみ、また三方から一挙に襲いかかる。となれば空いた一方に逃れるしかないけれど、それには得体の知れぬ心が仕掛けた罠に嵌[はま]りこむかの不安が残る。
source.english:
Surely the sea had not scented his heart. Yet its waves were spiteful, wrenching the bow aside just when the ship seemed to have ridden them out. They toyed with her, making the twin mates grind their teeth and redden their eyes.
Something was strange about this storm. Even Sakuya, who had been through only one at sea, could feel it. The wind and rain were ordinary enough, but the waves seemed to conceal a deliberate ill intent. They pushed the ship high, dragged her toward the bottom, then attacked from three sides at once. That left only the fourth direction to escape—but one feared falling into a trap laid by some inscrutable mind.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Contain the flooding, double time. Cabin two-zero-three, someone has left the porthole wide open.」

And then there was Kuro. Though her white hair and crimson eyes were unchanged, that wan ghost mushroom in the shade was nowhere to be found. Now, like a being kin to the Byakko or the Shirohebi, she was an existence seemingly half-flesh and half-spirit possessed of divine majesty and power, her every movement, every sound that left her lips, her action, speech, and thought───body and words, consciousness and nature───was unified and controlled; perhaps the girl present here was truly enlightened? (TN: The Byakko here is not the more famous tiger, but instead a white-furred fox with supernatural powers.)

If this was Kuro, then who was that? Who was the girl frightened by Sakuya's caressing hand, who only let her mouth hang slack with relief upon realizing she would not be struck? Did that girl, so frail and delicate that she could be carried even in Sakuya's feeble arms, truly exist somewhere inside this Kuro of the present?

Dependable. Valiant. Trustworthy. No matter how the storm raged or how the ship howled and creaked, as long as this albino girl was here, he could have unconditional faith in the course of the Albatross. That was how dominant a force of will existed on the other side of the thin wall of the wheelhouse right now.

And yet, Sakuya did not feel that the gap between them was as vast as that of a newt at the bottom of a deep well and the Hiten sitting in the Roukan Palace in the void between the stars─── (TN: The Hiten, written "飛天" are celestial beings in Buddhism, and you'll often see them depicted as flying nymphs or heavenly musicians. They frequently feature on murals in Buddhist temples. Roukan, written "琅干" here (the real character for 干 can't be displayed due to the encoding), refers to a type of beautiful, high-quality green jade. A jade palace is a classic poetic trope in East-Asian literature as the dwelling of higher beings.)

Looking up from below the pane, eyes just barely peering over the edge, a glint congealed in intense shadow shimmered across the surface of the glass, and he recoiled; when he realized it was the colour of his own eyes reflected in the glass, he was left horrified.

Though it was unlikely the sea had sensed what ran through Sakuya's heart in this moment, the waves were terribly mean-spirited, for no sooner than it seemed they had weathered them would the waves toy with the ship's bow, forcibly changing her direction, making the twin mates grind their teeth together, their eyes bloodshot.

Something was strange about this storm. Even Sakuya, who had only experienced a single storm on the open seas, could feel it; the wind and rain itself was nothing unusual, but it was as if some manner of artificial intent lurked within the surging waves, lifting the ship high on their crest all to drag her down to the bottom of the sea, and they would assault the ship from three directions all at once. And with that, all they could do was make their escape through the one direction yet left open to them, but an unease remained, as if they were being led into a trap set by some mysterious, unknowable mind.

source.japanese:
だがそれでもクロなら。
　
　
　嵐に覚醒したクロなら。
　
　
　クロがある限りいかなる嵐もと、それだけは日頃は鈍愚な少女に全船員が認めるクロ。
　
　
　彼女なら。
　
　
　だから、もちろんクロは凛然と───
source.english:
But even so, Kuro—
Kuro awakened by the storm—
Kuro, whom every sailor credited with the power to face any storm, however dull she was ordinarily—
She could.
So, naturally, Kuro would answer with a clear, commanding voice—

target.text: Even so, as long as they had Kuro. As long as they had Kuro, awakened by the storm. As long as Kuro was here, they could weather any storm, that much was acknowledged by all the crew members, though Kuro was usually such a dull-witted girl. As long as she was here. Therefore, naturally, Kuro was dignified and commanding as she───

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「次は……次は……あれ……次、は？」
source.english: “Next… next… Huh… What's next?”

source.japanese: 調律が緩んだ琴絃は、それまで冴えていた分だけ聞き苦しい。覗き見る朔屋はそこに見慣れたクロ、いつもの愚かでのろまなクロの片鱗を見て、ようやく操舵室内の少女に安心感を覚えたけれどもそんなのは同病相哀れむの退行的な安堵であって、この危急の時には肥溜めに捨ててしまうがいい。
source.english: A string loosened from its tuning sounded all the worse for having been clear before. Peering in, Sakuya caught a glimpse of the familiar Kuro, the usual stupid, sluggish Kuro. At last he felt reassured by the girl in the wheelhouse. But that was a regressive comfort, the sympathy of shared affliction. In this emergency, it belonged in a cesspit.

source.japanese:
クロの様子はどうにもおかしく、普段のような完全な明晰が薄れる瞬間があるようだった。よもやこの奇妙な嵐、そしてこの海域に彼女の把握力を狂わせるなにかがあるとでも言うのか。
　クロの弛緩に気づいた、操舵室の隅にちんまり控えて用命を待つ下級水夫が激励の、
source.english:
Something was wrong with Kuro. There seemed to be moments when her usual storm-born clarity faded. Could something in this strange storm, these waters, be disturbing her grasp?
A junior sailor waiting for orders in a corner of the wheelhouse noticed her lapse and offered encouragement.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「しっかり！　船長！　こんな時くらいしか活躍できないんだから！」
source.english: “Steady, Captain! This is about the only time you get to shine!”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「うわ辛辣。
　でも事実、もしここで船長が駄目になったら、この船、色々とまずいよね……」
source.english:
“Wow, that's harsh.
But true. If the captain fails us now, this ship's in all kinds of trouble…”

source.japanese: 激励した口は少々口さがない、そういう個性の下級水夫だったのだろうが、二人の無遠慮な言葉は室内をいたたまれない沈黙で充たしシサムもキサラも舵輪からは手こそ離しはしなかったけれど、振り返っての無言の問いかけ、嵐の響きは部屋の外に蹲[うずくま]る朔屋より室内の者達に巨大に響いたのではないだろうか。
source.english: The encouragement had a cutting edge; perhaps that was simply this particular junior sailor's way. The two boys' tactless words filled the wheelhouse with an unbearable silence. Neither Sisam nor Kisara took a hand from the wheel, but both turned with a question in their eyes. Perhaps the storm sounded louder still to those inside than it did to Sakuya crouching beyond the wall.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Next we……next we…… huh……next we?」

The dissonance of a koto string out of tune was all the more unpleasant to hear for how clear its sound had been before. Peeking inside, Sakuya caught a glimpse of the Kuro he knew, the usual stupid, dim-witted Kuro, and though he finally felt a sense of security upon seeing the girl within the wheelhouse, it was the sort of regressive relief born from misery loving company; in a time of emergency like this, such things were best discarded in a cesspool.

Kuro's behaviour was terribly odd, and there seemed to be moments when her usual perfect clarity of mind would dim. Could it be that that within this strange storm, within these waters, there existed something that made her powers of command falter? Having noticed Kuro growing slack, a deck boy, tucked away in a corner of the wheelhouse and waiting for orders, offered her encouragement:
【Deck boy】 「Captain! Keep it together! These are the only times you get to shine!」
【Deck boy】 「Ouch, that's harsh. But the truth is, if our captain goes limp here, this ship is in for a whole lot of trouble……」

They way they encouraged her was a little backhanded, they must have been deck boys possessed of a sharper tongue than average, but their rudely blunt words filled the room with an unbearable silence; though neither Shisamu nor Kisama could take their hands off the helm, as they looked over their shoulders, the wordless question in their eyes and the thrum of the storm likely reverberated with a weight far more crushing for those within the room than it did for Sakuya crouching just outside.

source.japanese:
注視を受けてクロ、場を誤魔化すように髪を掻[か]きあげて、そこで嵐の時だけ被る船長帽、今日は忘れていた事に気づいてより寄る辺なき眼差しの、一度・二度頭を打ち振って、舞い上がった髪が落ち着いた時には、目に力を取り戻していた。
　嵐の時だけの矜持が力を与えたか、それとも単に一時的な不調だったのか、ともかく、迸らせた声には力。言い聞かせる力。
source.english:
Under their scrutiny, Kuro raked back her hair as if to cover the moment. Then she realized she had forgotten the captain's cap she wore only in storms. Her eyes grew still more defenseless. She shook her head once, twice. When the flying hair settled, strength had returned to her gaze.
Had her storm-only pride given her power, or had it merely been a passing lapse? Whatever the cause, the voice that burst out had force. The force to persuade.

target.text: Now receiving their full attention, Kuro ran a hand through her hair as if to cover up her stumble, but then she noticed that she'd forgotten to put on her captain's hat today, the one she only wore during storms, leaving her with a forlorn, abandoned look in her eyes; she shook her head once, then twice, and by the time her fluttering hair settled once more, she had regained that strength in her gaze. Perhaps that pride she held only during a storm had given her strength, or perhaps it had simply been a brief slump; regardless of which, her voice brimmed with strength once more. A strength that persuaded others.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だ、大丈夫。
　次はあの三角波をとにかく抜ける。
　そうしたらしばらく波はやり過ごせる！」
source.english:
“I-it's all right.
Next, we just have to get past that steep, peaked wave.
Then we can ride out the waves for a while!”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「信じてクロを！　大丈夫だからクロは。
　波を読んで、風を聞いて、
　船の鼓動に耳澄ませて。
　うん、いつもと同じで、
　クロはやれる───」
source.english:
“Trust Kuro! Kuro's all right.
Read the waves, listen to the wind,
listen closely to the ship's heartbeat.
Yes. Just like always.
Kuro can do it—”

source.japanese:
それは、船員達だけにではなく、彼女自身にも言い聞かせる力。
　だが、アクシデントはまだまだ続いて。
source.english:
The force of persuasion was directed not only at the sailors, but at herself.
Yet the mishaps continued.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Ku-, Kuro's fine. Next, we just need to get through that pyramidal wave. Once we do that, we can weather the waves for a time!」
【Kuro】 「Have faith in Kuro! Because Kuro is fine. Kuro will read the waves, listen to the wind, keep Kuro's ears peeled for the throbbing of the ship. Yes, same as always, Kuro will do it───」
It was a strength that persuaded not just the sailors, but even the girl herself. And yet, the accidents kept happening.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「え？　石炭が足りなくなりそう？　なんで、この前積みこんだばかりで……」
source.english: “What? We're going to run short of coal? Why? We only just loaded—”

source.japanese: 伝声管から鳴った報せに耳傾けてクロは、自分に問いかけの、その問いかけると言う事からして、嵐の時の完全に確信のある彼女なら排されるところだったのだ。その後に素早く補いをつけたとしても、いよいよクロの不調は隠しきれなくなりつつあった。
source.english: At the report ringing from the speaking tube, Kuro asked herself why. That she asked at all was already something her storm-self, perfect in its certainties, would never have done. Whatever quick expedient she supplied afterward, Kuro’s faltering could no longer be hidden.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Eh? It doesn't look like we have enough coal? But how, we just loaded up the other day……」

Listening intently to the report sounding through the voice pipes, Kuro asked a question to herself, and the very act of asking that question was a course of action she would have dismissed were she the girl possessed of perfect confidence during a storm. Though she quickly made up for it afterwards, Kuro's poor condition was becoming harder and harder for her to conceal.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……バラックを一つ急いで解体！　そいつを罐にぶちこんで！」
source.english: “…Dismantle a shack, quickly! Put it in the furnace!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（もしかして今回はこれ、
　どうにもまずいんじゃあないのか……）
source.english:
(Maybe this time
we're… really in trouble…)

source.japanese:
朔屋が濡れた船員服によるところではない寒気を肌えに覚えてぞくぞくと鳥肌立てかけた時、バラックの角を折れてこちらに駆けてくる下級水夫のあり、盗み聞きの後ろめたさに窓の下から離れて身を隠す。
　そんな朔屋が見えていたのかいなかったのか、ともかく少年は操舵室に、不安定な足場ものともしない軽業めいた足取りで一直線、よほど急ぎの伝令と見えて、その通りで、開け放った扉、風雨中に吹きこむ構わずもどかしげに放った言葉は、ロープを詰めた箱の影に這いずりこんだ朔屋の耳にも鮮やかに。
source.english:
A chill owing nothing to his wet sailor's clothes prickled gooseflesh over Sakuya's skin. Just then a junior sailor came running around the corner of a shack. Guilty about eavesdropping, Sakuya slipped from beneath the window and hid.
Whether or not the boy saw him, he made straight for the wheelhouse with an acrobat's disregard for the treacherous footing. An urgent messenger if ever there was one—and so he proved. He flung the door open, heedless of the wind and rain blowing in, and blurted words sharp enough to reach Sakuya even where he had crawled into the shadow of a rope-filled crate.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「船長、陸影が見えたって！　西北西の方」
source.english: “Captain! They've sighted land! West-northwest!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Dismantle one of the shacks, quick! Then toss it into the boiler!」
【Naomasa】 （Could it be that, this time, we're in some serious trouble……）

When Sakuya felt a chill wash over his skin that wasn't just caused by his drenched clothes, shivering as gooseflesh rose, a deck boy came running in his direction after turning the corner of a shack, and feeling guilty about eavesdropping, he made his exit from beneath the window and hid himself.

Perhaps he saw Sakuya, perhaps he didn't, but regardless of which, the boy headed straight for the wheelhouse with acrobatic steps as though entirely unfazed by the slippery footing; he looked like he was delivering an exceedingly important message, and he certainly was; those words, uttered impatiently through a door left wide open with no heed paid to the wind or the rain, reached even Sakuya's ears with vivid clarity as he crawled into the shadows of a box filled with rope.
【Deck boy】 「Captain, land ahoy! To the west-northwest!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ああやっと……見えてくれないと嘘だって思ってた。感覚は告げているのに、嵐が行かせてくれないなんて───」
source.english: “Ah, finally… I thought it had to be a lie if it didn't come into view. My senses tell me it's there, but the storm won't let us reach it—”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Aah, at last……when you said you saw nothing, Kuro thought it a lie. Kuro's senses are telling her it's right there, but the storm refuses passage and───」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「みんな、もう少しだけ奮起して！」
source.english: “Everyone, just a little more effort!”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ア、アイ、マム……！」
source.english: “A-aye, ma'am…!”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「でも今回は……なんだかヤバ気？」
source.english: “But this time… Looks a bit bad?”

source.japanese: 先ほどのクロの逡巡を目の当たりにしていた下級水夫は、まだ心細さげに同輩と船長クロを交互に眺めたが、そうやって批判めいて賢しら口を叩いているよりはと、解体したバラックの材木運びを手伝いに駆け出していく。
source.english: The junior sailor who had witnessed Kuro's hesitation still looked anxiously between his fellow and Captain Kuro. But rather than stand there offering clever criticism, he ran to help carry timber from the dismantled shack.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「All of you, we must rouse ourselves for just a little longer!」
【Deck boy】 「A-, aye, ma'am……!」
【Deck boy】 「But don't things seem…… a little sketchy this time around?」

The deck boy who had witnessed Kuro's hesitation earlier still seemed disheartened while glancing alternately at his fellow and Captain Kuro, but rather than indulging in critical, pretentious remarks, he instead rushed off to help carry the timber from the dismantled shack.

source.japanese: かくして下級水夫達は走り回り各所で奮戦し、航海士は舵を取り続け、水夫長も機関長もそれぞれの職掌に尽力し、朔屋でさえもまた下層甲板に舞い戻って水の汲[く]み出しに不健康な体力搾[しぼ]りだし───
source.english: Thus the junior sailors ran and struggled at every station, the mates held the wheel, and the boatswain and chief engineer labored at their respective duties. Even Sakuya returned to the lower deck and wrung from his unhealthy body enough strength to bail water—

target.text: Thus, the deck boys ran around, fighting valiantly all throughout the ship, the first mates continued to take the helm, the Bosun and the Chief Engineer devoted their all to their respective functions, and even Sakuya returned to the lower deck to bale out water, squeezing out every drop of his meagre physical strength───

source.japanese: 船は、ようやく───
source.english: At last, the ship—

target.text: And at long last, the ship───

source.japanese:
───或いは、信天翁号の面子の、ザウエルなる希少な珠に滾[たぎ]った欲の前には、奇怪な嵐の威力も一歩譲ったと言うところか。
　暴風は鳴りを潜[ひそ]め、海面は風浪階級で言えばＲｏｕｇｈｔ、やや波高しの域にまで収まって、荒れ狂う波の衝角は今では馬の背が行き来する程度の高さ。
　
　───それとも、信天翁号の乗り組み達の欲かきをよろしく心得て、嵐を勢子にそこまで追いこんだのか。
　暴風は静まったとはいえ未だ雨は降り止まず、海流はその環礁の奥へ奥へと引きこむ流れで船の竜骨を捉え、もう離そうとしない。
source.english:
Perhaps even the uncanny storm's power had yielded before the Albatross crew's burning greed for the rare jewel called Zauer.
The gale fell quiet. On the scale of sea conditions, the surface had subsided to ‘rough’: the waves were still somewhat high, but the battering rams of raging water were now merely horses' backs passing to and fro.
Or perhaps, understanding the crew's greed perfectly, something had used the storm as a beater to drive them here.
The gale had calmed, but the rain did not stop. A current leading deeper and deeper into the atoll caught the ship's keel and would not let go.

source.japanese: そう、環礁、なのだった。
source.english: Yes, an atoll.

target.text: ───Perhaps, faced with the avaricious desire of the crew of the Albatross, their roiling, seething longing for the rare pearl they called a Sauer, even the might of this mysterious storm had ceded ground. The howling of the gales had subsided, the state of the sea was a "rough" on the Douglass Sea scale, remaining within the realm of moderately tall wave crests, and the naval rams of the raging waves, once so fierce, now reached no higher than the spine of a horse passing by.

───Or perhaps, well aware of the rapaciousness of the crew of the Albatross, the storm had driven them this far into its clutches like it was a beater on a hunt? Though the gales had quieted down, the rain continued to fall incessantly, and the ocean current pulled the ship's keel deeper and deeper into the atoll, refusing to release its grip ever again.
Indeed, an atoll.

source.japanese:
船縁に凭[もた]れようとして、差し延べた手はぷるぷるとさんざんこづき回された仔山羊のように震えて、朔屋は体を持ち上げきれずずるずるなりに舷側に額押し当て頽[くずお]れる。
　たまに働きぶりを見せたところで普段が普段のさぼり癖と不摂生、体がついていかずに嵐から解放された弛緩も手伝い、立ち上がって場景を改める気力もない、ところの背中にどすんと捺された雪駄の足。
source.english:
Sakuya tried to brace himself against the rail, but his outstretched hand trembled like a young goat that had been prodded mercilessly. Unable to lift himself, he slithered down and collapsed with his forehead against the ship's side.
One rare burst of labor could not make up for his habitual idleness and dissipation. His body had failed him, and the release that followed the storm drained away what little remained. He lacked even the strength to stand and take in the scene—until a sandaled foot planted itself heavily between his shoulders.

target.text: He attempted to prop himself against the gunwale, his outstretched hand shaking like a baby goat that had been mercilessly bullied and shoved around, but Sakuya was ultimately unable to raise his body, and with his brow pressed against the bulwark, he slowly slid down, collapsing.

Though he would occasionally show off a work ethic, as a consequence of his usual habit of slacking off combined with an unhealthy lifestyle, his body was unable to keep up with his will, and the relaxation he felt after being liberated from the storm didn't help matters; as he lay there, unable to muster the willpower to even stand up and take in the scenery, a setta-clad foot stepped down on his back with a thump.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「なに骨ぇ抜かれた猿みてえなザマ晒してんだかよ」
source.english: “What are you doing, looking like a boneless monkey?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あんたか。みんな総出で大忙しだったってのに、一段落着いた頃になってのこのこと……いやあんたに切った張った以外を当てにする俺が莫迦だった」
source.english: “…You. Everyone was flat out working, and you stroll up once it's settled… No, I'm the idiot for expecting anything from you besides cutting and fighting.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「The hell are you doing out here, lying down like a boneless monkey.」

【Naomasa】 「……Oh, it's you? We've been so damn busy, all hands on deck, and as soon as things settle down, you shamelessly saunter in……no, I was an idiot for counting on you for anything that doesn't involve cutting things down.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おーおー、ヤサぐれてやがんなあ。
　こいつでも入れて、
　ちっとはしゃんとしろい」
source.english:
“Oh, oh. Bitter, aren't we?
Put some of this in you
and straighten up a little.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Ooh, ooh, look at you being all sulky today, huh? Get some of this down your throat, then pull yourself together.」

source.japanese: 疲れきった背中に足を擦[なす]る無礼さえ詰[なじ]る気力もないのが、耳元でちゃぷんと鳴ったのに、神経に電撃走る、それまでは振り向きもせなんだ癖して朔屋の手、枯れ節の香気嗅いだ猫の敏捷さで走って耳元の水音に、掴んだのは扁平な形、酒のポケットボトルの形は手が覚えていて、ろくろく確かめもせず蓋を捻って、鼻先に香るのがブランデーの精華と知った時にはもう、瓶を逆さに中味を喉に流しこむ。
source.english: He lacked even the strength to rebuke the foot rubbing rudely at his exhausted back. Then a little slosh beside his ear sent lightning through his nerves. Until that instant he had not so much as turned; now his hand darted out with the speed of a cat catching the scent of dried bonito. It closed around something flat. His hand knew the shape of a pocket flask. Without troubling to check, he twisted off the cap. By the time the fine aroma of brandy reached his nose, he had already upended the bottle and was pouring its contents down his throat.

target.text: Sakuya was so exhausted, he did not even have the willpower to tell him off for the rudeness of rubbing his foot into his back, but the second he heard a splashing by his ears, it was like lightning flashed through his nerves, and though he had yet to even look over his shoulder, Sakuya's hand moved with the agility of a cat that had picked up the fragrance of karebushi. (TN: Karebushi, written “枯れ節”, is a traditional form of katsuobushi, also known as bonito flakes, repeatedly inoculated with mold and sun-dried. Cats love it, apparently.)

What he grabbed was flat, and his hand recognized it as a hip flask; without really bothering with checking to make sure, he twisted the lid off, and by the time he realized that the aroma wafting to his nose was tickling it with the essence of brandy, he'd already turned the flask on its head and sent the contents flowing down his throat.

source.japanese: 二口、三口、位しか中には残っていなかったけれど、酒精の芳香と刺激は霊験というのが相応しく、速やかに朔屋の全身から倦怠を払った。立ち上がった時には智里に心友への朗らかな笑顔くっきりと、現金な男もあったもの。
source.english: Only two or three mouthfuls remained, but the fragrance and sting of alcohol deserved to be called miraculous: they swept the weariness from Sakuya's whole body. When he stood, a bright smile for his dearest friend beamed upon Tomosato. A transparently self-serving fellow if ever there was one.

target.text: Only two or three sips remained in the flask, but the aroma and bite of the spirits were nothing short of a miracle cure, swiftly purging any exhaustion from Sakuya's body. By the time he was getting back on his feet, a clear, beaming smile for his bosom buddy Tomosato was already etched on his face; what a fair-weather friend.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もっと。今度はバーボンの粗いキックが欲しいぜ」
source.english: “More. This time I want bourbon's rough kick.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「More. I want that sharp bourbon kick this time.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「何がもっとで、何だその馴れ馴れしい面ぁよ。判りやすい奴だな相変わらず」
source.english: “What's this ‘more’? And why are you grinning like we're best friends? Easy to read as ever.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Whaddya mean more, and what's up with that overly friendly smile? You're as transparent as you've ever been.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「まあいくらかは元気も出たろ。
　そんでどうなのよ、
　お前としてはこの眺めはさ」
source.english:
“Well, you've got a little life back.
So what
do you think of this view?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どう、と振られてもなぁ……」
source.english: “What do I think…?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Well, that must have cheered you up a little. So then, how about it, what do you make of this view?」
【Naomasa】 「Ask me that all you like, but……」

source.japanese: 唇に残った酒精を意地汚く嘗めながら朔屋は、眼前に展開される景色を形容する言葉を探しあぐねて、酒もいくらか脳を解きほぐしていたけれど、それでも見つからず、肩を竦めて両掌を上に広げて見せるジェスチュアで感嘆詞に替えた。
source.english: Greedily licking the liquor from his lips, Sakuya searched in vain for words to describe the scene before him. The drink had loosened his brain a little, but still nothing came. He shrugged and spread his hands, palms upward, substituting the gesture for an exclamation.

source.japanese:
確かに朔屋の乏しい語彙に落としこむよりは、肉体言語に委ねた方が彼の感慨は伝わりりやすいだろう。
　嵐の圏内を抜けてもそこは晴れやかな青空も雲間からの光もなく、ひたすら陰鬱な、薄汚れたウエスの灰色に百年は積もった綿埃の分厚さの暗雲に閉ざされた天蓋より銀線は絶え間なく降り注ぎ、風は背景遠くに下がったものの止まず音の帷[とばり]と化して世界を閉ざす。
　信天翁号を取り囲んでいるのは円弧に伸びた環礁の、大仰に腕を広げてかき抱いた、体幹の位置にその島はあった。
source.english:
Indeed, his impressions were better entrusted to the language of the body than forced into his scant vocabulary.
Beyond the storm's fiercest reach lay no cheerful blue sky, no light breaking between clouds. Silver threads fell without cease from a wholly sullen canopy, gray as filthy rags and thick as a hundred years of settled lint. The wind had receded far into the background but had not stopped; it became a curtain of sound closing off the world.
The atoll curved around the Albatross like a pair of arms flung wide to embrace her. The island stood where the torso should have been.

source.japanese:
それを島と表していいものかどうか。
　死んだ羊の群れのように重苦しく低く垂れこめる暗雲と、暴れ出したいところをこらえるように不穏にうねる暗色の海との間に、無秩序に積み重ねられた木材の連なり。世界中の木造文化圏の貧民窟を中途半端に爆破して、形状保った家屋をかき集めて積み上げた、といえばその輪郭にはやや近い。
　視線を廻らせる限り、あちらの小屋とこちらの建物の隙間にはまた木造の家屋、幾重にも重層してその密度は、隙間を開けて並べればたちまち倒壊してしまうと恐れたかのよう。
　印象としては信天翁号上甲板のバラック群に似通うところがあるが、その総量はグノーシス派が内観するところの小宇宙の域まで達して、まだ船はその集積地まで四ケーブルは間を置いているのに、のしかかってくる気配の質量で船の喫水が下がってしまいそう。
source.english:
Could it even be called an island?
Between dark clouds hanging low and heavy as a flock of dead sheep and a dark sea heaving ominously as if restraining an urge to riot sprawled a chaos of piled timber. Imagine setting charges beneath every wooden slum in the world, half demolishing them, then gathering up whatever houses held their shape and heaping them together: that came somewhere near its outline.
Wherever the eye turned, another wooden house was wedged between this hut and that building, layer upon layer, packed as though leaving any gap would bring the whole mass down.
It somewhat resembled the warren of shacks on the Albatross's upper deck, but here their totality approached the microcosm contemplated by the Gnostics. The ship still lay four cables from the mass, yet the sheer weight of its looming presence seemed enough to lower her waterline.

source.japanese: 幸い環礁の内部は信天翁号の竜骨の下にまだ余裕を残しており、嵐を逃れたはいいが座礁、という平みっともない憂き目を見ずには済みそうではあったが。
source.english: Fortunately, the atoll's interior still left room beneath the Albatross's keel. They seemed likely to avoid the abject embarrassment of escaping the storm only to run aground.

target.text: While greedily licking his lips clean of any remaining alcohol, Sakuya struggled to find the words that could accurately express the scenery unfolding before his eyes, and though his brain had been somewhat unwound by the drink, he still couldn't find them; with a shrug of his shoulders and both palms spread upwards, he replaced his exclamation with a gesture.

Certainly, compared to attempting to reduce it into something that could be expressed through Sakuya's meagre vocabulary, it was probably easier to convey his heartfelt impression on the matter by entrusting it entirely to body language.

Though they had broken through the area veiled by the storm, it was neither clear blue skies nor light shining through the gaps in the clouds that awaited them; from the canopy shrouded in entirely gloomy, dark clouds, like a filthy, ash-grey rag thick with lint accumulated through centuries, did silver streaks rain down incessantly, and though the wind had receded into the distant background, it still continued unabated, forming a curtain of sound that closed off the world. Encircling the Albatross was an atoll in the shape of an arc, and embraced within its exaggeratedly outstretched arms, located at the core of its body, was that island.

Was it even appropriate to call that thing an island? Between the brooding, dark clouds, oppressive like a flock of dead sheep, and the dark sea unnervingly undulating as if attempting to restrain its desire to rage and riot, lay a haphazard stretch of heaps of timber. If one imagined that someone had partly blown up the slums of the cultural spheres where people yet lived in wooden constructions found around the world, then scraped together any buildings that still retained their shape and piled them up, that would be a fairly close description of what it looked like.

As far as the eye could see, between the shed over there and the building over here were yet more wooden buildings, stacked on top of each other, layer upon layer, with such density it seemed as if whoever had built this was afraid that had they lined them up with any space between, the buildings would all collapse immediately.

The impression it gave bore some resemblance to the cluster of shacks littering the upper deck of the Albatross, but its aggregate volume had reached the level of the microcosm as envisioned by the Gnostics through introspection, and though the ship was still four cables out from the great heap, the looming presence of its mass still felt heavy enough it might well sink her draught.

Fortunately, the interior of the atoll yet provided sufficient clearance beneath the Albatross' keel, and so they had been spared the humiliating fate of escaping the storm only to run aground against a hidden reef, but.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「シサムとキサラのご託宣を信じりゃ、この辺りの海で、こんなボロ屋寄せ集めた島なぞ、船乗りの噂にも上った事がないとかでよ」
source.english: “Believe the pronouncements of Sisam and Kisara, and no sailor's ever so much as heard a rumor of an island cobbled together from ramshackle houses like this in these waters.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「If we buy into the divine revelations of Shisamu and Kisara, there is not so much as a single rumour whispered between sailors that anything like this island, a collection of dilapidated shacks, can be found in these waters.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「嵐の事を知った奴はあっても、それを抜けた無茶野郎はいねえって事だろうな」
source.english: “Some know about the storm. No mad bastard's got through it, then.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だろうなぁ……。なんだよこれ。
　そりゃあ人が住む島に建物があったって、
　なんもおかしくはないが……」
source.english:
“Probably…
What is this? Buildings on an inhabited island aren't
strange in themselves…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それでもこいつはおかしいよ。
　土地がない漁港辺りは、こんな風に海っ縁まで家を建てる事はある」
source.english:
“But this is wrong.
A fishing port short of land might build houses right to the water's edge like this.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あるけれども……これは違うだろう。
　この島は、全部建物で、
　埋めつくされてやがら」
source.english:
“Might, but… this is different.
The whole island's filled
with buildings.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Probably just means that, while there are guys who know about the storm, none of them were reckless enough to make it through.」
【Naomasa】 「Guess so……. But what is that thing? Sure, having buildings on islands where people live, nothing strange about that, but……」
【Naomasa】 「But even so, that thing is weird. Near fishing harbours where land is scarce, there are cases where you'll find houses built right against the edge of the sea like this.」
【Naomasa】 「There are cases, but…… I think this is different. This island, all of it, the whole damn thing is completely covered with buildings.」

source.japanese:
朔屋のざっと目測した通り、島には高台も内陸部もあろうに、ここの住人達には波浪と潮風から建物を守ろうという思想は欠片もなかったらしく、ただ島の地面という地面を木造建築で埋めつくそうとの執念めいた気配が雨霞と化して靄っているかのような。
　朔屋の気持ちも陸地を見てもいっかな奮わず、信天翁号は嵐を逃れ得たのではなく奸智で環礁内に追いこむこの潮流に乗せられたのではと疑い始める始末の、いかなるものの邪念かは知らねど。
source.english:
Just as Sakuya's rough survey suggested, there ought to have been heights and an interior. Yet the inhabitants appeared to have no notion of protecting their buildings from waves and salt wind. An obsession with filling every scrap of ground with wooden structures seemed to hang there as rainy mist.
Even the sight of land did nothing for his spirits. He began to suspect they had not escaped the storm at all. Some cunning current had carried them into the atoll. Whose malicious design, he did not know.

target.text: Based on Sakuya's cursory measurement, there must have been both elevated and inland areas, but it was as though the inhabitants of this island had not spared a single thought for protecting their buildings from the surging waves and the salty sea breeze; it seemed as if something akin to an obsession with simply covering every inch of this island in wooden buildings had transformed into a hazy drizzle and was shrouding the island in mist.

Even when seeing land, Sakuya's spirits weren't roused in the least; he began to suspect that the Albatross had not secured escape from the storm, but had instead been cunningly driven into this atoll by the tidal current, all through some manner of wicked design, though he knew not yet what sort.

source.japanese: 潮に流されて木造家屋の集積体が迫ってくるにつれ、流れ出す鬼気のいよいよ濃くなったような想いして、絡めとられるようで、己をかき抱いて身震いの、雨はいよいよ不吉に冷たい。食堂に降りてホットバタードラムでもねだろうかと踵[きびす]を返しかけると、いまし昇降段から上がってきたのが紫紺の色も目に艶[つや]やかな、泪だった。
source.english: Carried by the tide, they drew nearer the heap of wooden houses. Its uncanny presence seemed to grow denser, entangling him. He hugged himself and shuddered. The rain was colder, more ominous. He was about to turn and go down to the mess hall to beg for a hot buttered rum when Rui came up the companionway, her deep violet dress lovely to the eye.

target.text: As they were carried along by the tide and the heap of wooden buildings drew nearer, it felt to him as if the ghastly aura pouring out from it grew thicker and thicker in turn, like he was being entangled in it, and he hugged himself tightly, body shuddering, for the rain was also growing more and more ominously cold. He was about to turn on his heel and head down to the galley to pester them for a hot buttered rum, and who should come up the ladder in that very moment, even the indigo of her dress imbued with a fetching lustre, but Rui.

source.japanese: 嵐の間は彼女の船室で大人しくしていたようだが、雨風が弱まったとなって辺りの様子を窺いに上がってきたのだろう。
source.english: Apparently she had stayed quietly in her cabin during the storm. She had probably come up to inspect their surroundings now that the wind and rain had weakened.

target.text: It seemed like the woman had behaved and stayed in her cabin during the storm, but with the rain and wind having subsided, she had likely come up on the deck to examine the state of their surroundings.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ふぅ───今回の嵐は、前の時よりは大人しうございましたのに、ずいぶんとひどく揺れたのね」
source.english: “Ah… This storm was milder than the previous one, yet we rolled quite terribly.”

source.japanese: 嵐を抜けたといっても雨は替わらずびしゃびしゃと悪く冷たいのに、泪は傘の一つも持たず、たちまち髪の先や頤[おとがい]に雫を帯びたが、朔屋の濡れ鼠のみじめさとは異なり、肌の雫は澄んだ珠、水気に貼りつくドレスは肢体の艶[なま]めかしさを際立てて、この女は陽差しに乾くのを厭[いと]うて日傘は差しても、雨に濡れるのは苦にしないらしい。
source.english: Though they had passed beyond the gale, rain still fell with an ugly chill. Rui carried no umbrella, and droplets soon jewelled the ends of her hair and her chin. Yet unlike Sakuya in his drowned-rat misery, she wore clear pearls upon her skin, while the wet dress clinging to her made the sensual curves of her body still more pronounced. She might raise a parasol rather than let sunlight dry her, but apparently rain troubled her not at all.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あなたもそんな風に感じたか……。
　こんな嵐に好きこのんで突入してくのは、
　この船くらいなものだろうな」
source.english:
“You felt it too…
This ship's probably the only one that'd go
into a storm like that by choice.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まあ、といって本来の目的は、こうして嵐を越えた、この島にあるみたいだけどさ」
source.english: “Though the real purpose seems to lie here, on the island beyond it.”

source.japanese:
ザウエル、ザウエル、大地の精髄、劫初の太陽の炎と月の影を裡[うち]に封じこめて自ら輝く稀なる宝珠。島はなるほど異様ではあったけれど、そんな至宝を隠すには異様の質がどうにも異なっているように朔屋には思えてならない。どちらかといえばこの木造家屋に埋めつくされた島は、人間の怨念と妄執に織り上げられた亡霊奇譚の奥津城というのが相応しい。
　雨と予感とで体を外から内から冷やして身震いの朔屋とは裏腹に、泪は涼やかに目を瞠[みは]って、
source.english:
Zauer, Zauer. Essence of the earth, the rare jewel that held within it the sun's flame and moon's shadow from the beginning of time, and shone of itself. The island was certainly strange. Yet to Sakuya, its strangeness seemed of entirely the wrong kind to hide such a treasure. This island buried in wooden houses was more suited to be the tomb of a ghost story woven from human grudges and obsession.
Rain chilled him from outside, foreboding from within. He shuddered. Rui, by contrast, opened her eyes wide with a cool interest.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Phew───though this storm was milder than the last one, the ship still lurched quite dreadfully, no?」

Though they had made it through the storm, the rain remained, continuing to pelt them with a wet, miserable chill, and yet Rui did not even carry an umbrella; while drops of water formed on the ends of her hair and her chin, in stark contrast to the pitiable state of Sakuya, who looked like a drowned rat, the drops on her skin were like clear pearls, and the dress now clinging to her with moisture served only to accentuate the seductiveness of her body; though this woman abhorred drying up in the sun, and therefore would carry a parasol, it seemed she was not worried about getting drenched in the rain.
【Naomasa】 「So you felt that way too……? This ship is probably the only one that would willingly charge into a storm like this.」
【Naomasa】 「Well, having said that, seems our real objective here is on this island, which we braved the storm to reach.」

Sauer, Sauer, pith of the vast land, the flames of the primordial sun and the beams of the shadowy moon sealed within, rare jewel of innate brilliance. Indeed, the island was certainly abnormal, but Sakuya couldn't help but feel that it was an abnormality of a nature entirely different from the sort that would hide the greatest of treasures. If he had to put it into words, he could best describe this island covered in wooden buildings as the sepulcher where a ghostly tale woven from the lingering malice and obsessive delusions of humanity had been interred.
But in contrast to the shivering Sakuya, chilled from the inside and out by the rain and his premonition both, Rui was wide-eyed, her gaze carrying a refreshing clarity,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それで、こちらの島にしばらく留まるの？
　ちょっと面白そうだこと。
　島内には、何やら建物も見えるご様子」
source.english:
“So we're stopping at this island for a while?
It looks rather interesting.
There seem to be buildings on it.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「So then, will we be staying on this island for a spell? That does seem a little interesting. I do believe I can even see some manner of buildings on the island.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どなたか、
　お住まいでいらっしゃるのかしら」
source.english:
“Might someone
live there?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……え。あ、そ、そうか。
　確かに建物があるんなら、
　誰かがいたって不思議はないよな。
　……じゃあなんで俺、
　そんな風には全然考えなかったんだろ」
source.english:
“…Huh? Oh, y-yes.
If there are buildings,
it wouldn't be strange for someone
to be there…
Why hadn't I thought of it that way at all?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Could it be, then, that someone resides there, I wonder.」
【Naomasa】 「……Uh. Ah, I-, I guess? It's true that, if there's buildings, it wouldn't be at all surprising for someone to live there. ……But then I wonder, why did I never think of it that way at all?」

source.japanese:
泪に問われて朔屋はようやく、島の住人というのに思いが向いたくらいで、それまで彼は、人の手になる被造物の形を目の当たりにしながらも、島の建築群を風雨と歳月が刻みあげて塔の形に仕上げた岩塊のようにしか見なしていなかった自分に気づき鼻白んだ。
　だが朔屋の先入観も至って当たり前の、こう薄気味悪く雨の帷[とばり]に暗く覆われているというのに、島の各所どこにも灯りの一つだに見えず、厨や暖炉から立ちのぼる煙一筋もなく、島はただただ深閑と嵐の中心に横たわるばかりで───
source.english:
Only Rui's question turned his thoughts to inhabitants. Despite seeing shapes made by human hands, he realized he had regarded the buildings as nothing more than rocks carved into towers by wind, rain, and time. He felt foolish.
But his preconception was entirely natural. Uncanny and dark beneath a curtain of rain, the island showed not a single light anywhere. No thread of smoke from a kitchen or hearth. It simply lay in profound silence at the storm's center—

target.text: Only when asked by Rui did Sakuya's thoughts finally turn towards the island's inhabitants; until that moment, despite seeing these creations wrought by human hands with his very own eyes, he had seen the architectural clusters of the island as nothing more than rocky masses carved into the shape of towers by the wind, the rain, and the passage of time, and when he realized as much, he looked abashed.

But Sakuya's preconceived notions were exceedingly natural, for though it was shrouded in so dark and uncanny a curtain of rain, there was not a single light to be seen anywhere on the island, no lines of smoke rising from any kitchens or hearths; the island did nothing but lie still, profoundly silent within the core of the storm───

source.japanese: ……島は嵐の目に位置しているのだろう。それも永遠の。嵐は移動する様子を見せず島を取り巻いて、巨大な天然の結界を為していた。信天翁号の面々は欲の皮突っ張り、島から掠奪の一つでもやらかさない事にはそもそも抜錨する気もないだろうが、それ以前の問題として嵐を踏み越える際に船体に受けた消耗を処置しない事にはどうしようもない。
source.english: The island must lie in the storm's eye—an eternal eye. The storm showed no sign of moving, but surrounded the island as an immense natural barrier. Greed had stretched the Albatross crew's skins taut; they would hardly weigh anchor before contriving to loot something ashore. But first things first: the damage taken in crossing the storm had to be seen to.

source.japanese:
環礁内という事で海面の状態は多少穏やかだし、それどころか船を停泊しておけるような港のような構造物さえ有る。ただ航海士も水夫長も、朔屋ほどではないにしろ島の不気味な様子を警戒してか、直接接舷はせずに湾内に錨を降ろした。
　ともかく船を泊めて嵐からのダメージに応急処置を施すうちに夜となり、そこで信天翁号の乗り組み達はついに限界がきて、さしもの好奇心の主達も上陸することもなくばたばたと丸太のように寝台に伏して眠りを貪りにかかった。
source.english:
Within the atoll, the sea was somewhat calmer. There was even a structure like a harbor where they could berth. Yet the mates and boatswain seemed wary of the island's eerie appearance, if less so than Sakuya. They did not come alongside, but dropped anchor in the bay.
They stopped the ship and made emergency repairs to the storm damage. Night came. At last the crew reached their limit. For all their curiosity, even they did not go ashore. They fell onto their bunks like logs and began devouring sleep.

source.japanese: だが朔屋は、嵐の際の（彼にしては珍しい）奔走と、その後の復旧作業で疲労は極みの向こう側まで突き抜けてしまって心気は無駄な亢進状態、眠りこもうと努力しても目は煮凝りのようにぎょろついて、瞼は降りてくれず、諦めて彼はもそもそと寝台から這い出した。人が働くべき時に怠け、眠る時に動きまわる、どこまでいってもまともな営みというのに相容れない男である。
source.english: Sakuya, however, had run about during the storm—a rarity in itself—and worked on the repairs afterward. His exhaustion had gone past sleep into a useless nervous excitement. However hard he tried to drift off, his eyes bulged like aspic and his lids refused to descend. At last he gave up and crawled awkwardly from his bunk. Idle when men ought to work and on the move when they ought to sleep: to the bitter end, a man incompatible with ordinary life.

source.japanese:
それどころか一旦眠りを諦めてしまえば、こういう船内が疲弊しきっている時こそ酒をちょろまかす格好の機会とほくそ笑んで、貯蔵室まで一人夜行、ついには鼻歌に唸るは盗人賛歌、後先などは考えもしない。
　だから朔屋の忍び足をぎくりと止めたのは、今さら見つかる可能性を恐れる理性ではなく、通路の奥に佇む白い影を見たからで、すわ早々と島内の亡霊が乗りこんできたかと怯んだからで───朔屋は既にして島を悪霊の住処と決めてかかっている節がある。
source.english:
Worse, once he abandoned sleep, he grinned at the excellent opportunity to steal liquor while everyone aboard was exhausted. Alone, he made his nocturnal journey toward the storeroom, finally humming a hymn to thieves, never considering what came next.
What stopped his stealthy feet was not a belated, rational fear of discovery. He had seen a white shadow standing deep in the passage. Had an island ghost already boarded? He recoiled. Sakuya seemed already to have decided that the island was a dwelling place of evil spirits.

target.text: ……The island must have been located within the eye of the storm. And eternally so at that. Showing no signs of moving, the storm encircled the island, forming a gigantic natural barrier. The insatiably avaricious crew of the Albatross surely wouldn't even think to weigh anchor before pillaging at least something from this island, but before even considering that issue, they would not get far if they didn't deal with the wear and tear the hull had sustained while weathering the storm.

Since they were within an atoll, the surface of the sea was relatively calm, and in fact, there was even a port-like structure where it seemed one could leave a ship moored. But the first mates and the Bosun, though it was not to the same extent as Sakuya, were perhaps still wary of the creepy air of the island, for they decided instead to lower the anchor inside the atoll without coming right alongside the island.

Regardless, as they anchored the ship and began stop-gap repairs on the damage wrought by the storm, night fell, and by then, the crew of the Albatross had finally reached their limit; even the most curious among them did not bother to go ashore, but had instead collapsed on their beds like logs, greedily indulging in the sweet embrace of sleep.

But Sakuya, between his (uncharacteristically) frantic efforts during the storm and the subsequent intense labour of the repair work, ended up with his fatigue pushed far beyond any limit, leaving his mind in a state of futile hyper-arousal, and no matter how he endeavoured to fall asleep, his eyes bulged out of their sockets like they were made of jelly, he was unable to even close his eyelids, and giving up, he slithered out of his bed. Lazing when he ought to work, active when he ought to sleep: truly, this was a man incompatible with any manner of decent living.

On the contrary, now that he had given up on sleep for the time being, this was the perfect chance to pilfer some booze while the whole ship was this exhausted, he thought to himself with a grin; he left on a night trip by himself to the spirit room, eventually humming the anthem of a thief, not sparing a single thought for the consequences in store.

So what brought Sakuya's tiptoeing to a halt with a startled jerk was not his reason, nor was it a belated fear of the possibility of being discovered; it was because he saw a white shadow standing motionless in the depths of the passageway, he flinched at seeing that, oh my goodness, a ghost from that island had already boarded their ship───it seemed that Sakuya had already made up his mind that the island was a haunt for evil spirits.

source.japanese:
血走る眼を細めて怖々透かし見れば、なんの事はない枯れ尾花、白いのは腰のないうねり髪、クロがうっそりと通路の船窓の下に立ち尽くしていただけの事───だけの事、というには開け放しの船窓から吹きこむ雨風が白髪を乱して、さながら窓の外から白くか細い女の手が幾筋も入りこんで力なくかい招くかの薄気味悪さ、下手な亡者よりも凄まじく、朔屋は思わず廻れ右して逃げ出したくなったくらいだった。
　が、また足が止まる。歩いてきて止まって逃げ出しかけてはまた止まる、なんとも歯切れ悪い足取りだが、これは朔屋を誹[そし]れまい。
source.english:
Narrowing his bloodshot eyes, he peered fearfully into the gloom. The ghost resolved itself into withered silver grass—or rather, into limp waves of white hair. It was only Kuro, standing listlessly beneath a porthole in the passage. Only Kuro—except that wind and rain poured through the open port and tossed her hair into the likeness of pale, slender women's hands reaching in from outside, weakly beckoning. The sight was more ghastly than any common specter. Sakuya nearly wheeled around and fled.
But once again his feet stopped. He had walked, stopped, almost fled, then stopped again: hopelessly irresolute progress, though one could hardly blame him for it.

target.text: When he fearfully narrowed his bloodshot eyes to get a better view of it in the dark, it turned out to be nothing at all, for the white of the withered silver grass was hair wispily undulating; it was just Kuro, vacantly standing stock-still below a porthole in the passageway───that was all, but as the wind blew in through the wide-open porthole and sent her white hair whirling, it was like several slender, white arms of women reached in through the window, and their feeble beckoning was far eerier than any old ghoul or ghost, enough so to make Sakuya unconsciously want to make a right about-face and run away.
But his legs stopped once more. He walked, stopped, began to run away before stopping once again; what an incredibly noncommittal manner of walking, but Sakuya should not be spoken ill of for this.

source.japanese:
風に散らされて聴き取りづらい、クロの呟きにはそれでもまぎれもない哀感と苦渋が滲み出していたから。日頃はどこか感情の芯がはっきりしない少女にしては、痛々しさ胸に迫るほどに浮き彫りになっていたから。
　接触の悪い常夜灯の下でも、クロの顎から滴り落ちているのは雨の雫ばかりでなく、少女の涙も混じっていただろうし、どころかその色合いが眸[ひとみ]の血の赤を搾[しぼ]って薄紅帯びているのでは、と思われたほど。
source.english:
The wind scattered Kuro's murmurs and made them difficult to catch, yet unmistakable sorrow and anguish bled through. In a girl whose emotions usually seemed to have no fixed center, the pain now stood out sharply enough to catch at his heart.
Even beneath the flickering night lamp, the drops falling from her chin could not all have been rain. Her tears must have mingled with them—indeed, they seemed almost tinged with pink, as though wrung from the blood-red of her eyes.

target.text: For though it was hard to hear, scattered by the wind as it was, Kuro's murmuring voice still oozed with an unmistakable melancholy and bitterness. It was because, for a girl whose emotional core usually seemed so vague, this threw her anguish into such sharp relief that it tore at his heart. Even under the flickering of the faulty night light, he could tell it was not just raindrops dripping down from Kuro's chin, but likely also the girl's tears; in fact, their hue seemed a pale pink, as though being tinged with the blood-red of the eyes they had been wrung from.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……どうして？　クロ、今回は、いつもの嵐のときと、なんか違った」
source.english: “…Why? This time, Kuro was different. Not like in other storms.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Why? Kuro, this time was kind of different, from the usual storms.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロは、もしかして、嵐でも、もう変わらない？　クロのまま、変われない？
　誰!?　朔屋さん───」
source.english:
“Maybe Kuro won't change anymore, even in a storm? Kuro will just stay Kuro… never change?
Who's there!? Mr. Sakuya—”

source.japanese: 眺めているばかりでは耐えきれなくなって、朔屋はわざと踵[かかと]を鳴らした。クロの夜想を乱さぬようにとさり気なさを務めたつもりではあったが、びくりと身じろぎして、向き直れば白髪が雨によじれて重く舞い、雫を散らして、少女はそれをさも雨の雫のよう拭ってみせたが、白目まで赤く充血させた、潤んだ眼差しを隠すまでには思い至らない辺り彼女の取り繕[つくろ]いはまだまだ幼い。涙はちらつく灯りの下でも判然と。
source.english: He could no longer bear merely to watch, and deliberately clicked his heel. He had meant to approach casually, without disturbing Kuro's nocturne, but she flinched and turned. Her rain-twisted hair swung heavily and scattered drops. She wiped them away as though they were nothing but rain, yet never thought to hide her streaming eyes, bloodshot even to the whites. Her attempt at concealment was still hopelessly artless. The tears were plain even beneath the flickering lamp.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、覗くつもりはなかった。
　まあ調子悪い時だってあるさ。
　あんま気にしなさんなって」
source.english:
“No, I wasn't trying to spy.
Everyone has bad days.
Don't worry about it too much.”

source.japanese:
自尊心を鎧にし、他人に弱味を見せたがらぬ相手には有効の、泣き言聞かぬ振りのあしらいより朔屋は直截な言葉を選んだ。今のクロには言外に意味を含ませるよりはっきりと伝えた方が判りやすかろうと。
　今のクロは、意識が体の輪郭を越えて拡大して全船を掌握するクロではなく、それどころかか細い肩をがくりと落として、ただでさえ小さい体が一回りも萎縮して見えた。
　有り体に言ってしまえば、船長の時のクロではなく、朔屋の無能な腕であっても中にすっぽり収めてやれる少女であったから。
source.english:
Pretending not to have heard her complaint might have worked with someone armored in pride, someone unwilling to show weakness. Sakuya chose plain words instead. This Kuro would understand a direct statement more easily than a meaning left between the lines.
This was not the Kuro whose consciousness expanded beyond her body's outline to encompass the ship. Her frail shoulders sagged, making her already small body seem smaller still.
Plainly, she was not Captain Kuro. She was a girl even Sakuya's incompetent arms could enclose completely.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ほら、雨と潮でずぶ濡れじゃないか。
　このタオルはまだ乾いてる。
　拭いてやるよ、顔」
source.english:
“Look, you're soaked in rain and salt water.
This towel's still dry.
I'll wipe your face.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Maybe, Kuro won't change anymore, even when it storms? Kuro will remain Kuro, can't be changed? Who!? Sakuya-san───」

Having grown unable to bear just looking at this, Sakuya deliberately made a loud noise with his heel. He was trying to act nonchalant so as not to disturb Kuro's nocturnal brooding, but she stirred with a start, and when she turned around, her white hair, tangled and heavy with rain, danced through the air, shedding drops of water everywhere; though the girl tried to wipe them off like they were nothing but raindrops, that she did not even think of trying to hide her tear-choked gaze, how even the whites of her eyes were congested and red, was a testament to the girl's inexperience when it came to putting up a brave front. Her tears were plain to see, even beneath the flickering lights.
【Naomasa】 「Sorry, wasn't trying to eavesdrop. Well, we all have times when we're not feeling well. Don't let it bother you too much.」

Rather than pretending that he had not heard her cry, the sort of treatment that would be effective on those who clad themselves in a suit of armour composed of pride, unwilling to show weakness to others, Sakuya instead chose direct words. As Kuro was now, it was probably much easier for her to understand if he put it plainly rather than layering some implicit meaning between his words, or so he thought.

As Kuro was now, she was not the Kuro whose consciousness transcended the contours of her body, expanding to cover and grasp the entire ship, quite the opposite; her narrow shoulders were slumped, as though her already tiny body had shrunken down another size. Were he to put it frankly, it was because she was not Captain Kuro, but instead the little girl who could snugly be held even within Sakuya's incompetent arms.
【Naomasa】 「Look at you, all soaked from the rain and the spray. This towel here is still dry. I'll wipe your face down for you.」

source.japanese:
腰から下げたタオルを引き出して、歩み寄る朔屋に、クロはまたひくりとたじろいで、心細げに見回す通路の前後ろ、青年を夜更かし厳しく咎める寮監とでも見たか、口は言い訳を探して戦慄いて、逃げられる間合いではないと覚って、またあの卑屈な笑みを造ろうとして───ぽかんと軽く緩む。
　クロには朔屋ほどの背丈であっても正面に立たれるとのしかかられるよう、クロにとって上から降ってくるものは叱り飛ばす声とか張り倒す手などがほとんどで、反射的に身が竦む、けれど朔屋は腰を屈めて少女と目線を合わせたのである。
source.english:
Sakuya drew the towel from his waist and approached. Kuro flinched again, glancing anxiously up and down the passage. Had she mistaken him for a dormitory warden come to punish her for being up late? Her mouth trembled in search of an excuse. Realizing she was too close to escape, she tried once more to form that cringing smile—only for it to slacken in blank surprise.
Even a man no taller than Sakuya seemed to loom when he stood before her. Most things that came down upon Kuro from above were shouted rebukes or hands that struck her. Her body shrank by reflex. But Sakuya bent at the waist and brought his eyes level with hers.

target.text: When Sakuya pulled out the towel hanging down from his waist, then walked towards her, Kuro recoiled with a start once more, anxiously looking around the passageway, swinging her gaze back and forth; perhaps the young man looked in her eyes as a housemaster coming to harshly rebuke her for staying up late, for her mouth trembled as it searched for excuses, and when she realized that the narrowing distance between them no longer allowed her any escape, she once more tried to manufacture that servile smile─── but her lips gently relaxed, parting vacantly.

Even had Sakuya only been as tall as Kuro, if he stood right before her, it would still seem as though she was being pinned down by him; in Kuro's mind, anything descending upon her from above was mostly an angry, scolding voice or the open palm of a striking hand, hence she reflexively shrunk into herself, but Sakuya stooped over to meet the girl's gaze at her level.

source.japanese: 盆暗の朔屋にしては利け者の気転も、クロがいつも通りの哀れなクロに戻っていたから利いた事で、相手より優位と知ると人には自ずと余裕が生まれるからだが、それでもクロにはよく効いて、彼女の緊張は青年の狙い通りに解れる。船窓を閉めて、雨風を閉めだして。
source.english: For a dullard, Sakuya had shown remarkable tact—made possible only because Kuro had reverted to her usual pitiable self. Knowing one has the upper hand naturally lends a certain composure. Whatever its unflattering source, the gesture worked: her tension loosened exactly as he had intended. He closed the porthole and shut out the wind and rain.

target.text: This tact inherent to the shrewd, quite uncharacteristic for a blockhead like Sakuya, also only functioned because Kuro had returned to the usual, pathetic Kuro, for when people realize they have the upper hand on others, that awareness of their superiority naturally births a sense of composure; with that said, it truly was very effective on Kuro, and the tension running through the girl dissolved exactly as the young man had intended. He closed the porthole, shutting out the rain and wind.

source.japanese: しばらくは朔屋に頬や瞼[まぶた]を拭われるままに任せていたクロだったが、やがて、ぽつりと。
source.english: For a while Kuro let him wipe her cheeks and eyelids. At last she spoke, quietly.

target.text: For a time, Kuro remained still while she let Sakuya dry off her cheeks and eyelids, but eventually, muttered words began to spill.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……クロは。やっぱり……。
　駄目、なのかなあ……」
source.english:
“…Is Kuro… no good,
after all…?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Maybe. Kuro is……. Useless after all……」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「せっかくの、ずっと吹いてる嵐のところに来たのに……」
source.english: “Even after coming all this way, to a place where there's always a storm…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あれで駄目なら、他の奴だって駄目だろ。
　ま今回は、多少は手こずったみたいだが」
source.english:
“If that counts as no good, everyone else is no good too.
Well, you seemed to have a bit more trouble this time.”

source.japanese:
駄目。だめ。ダメな奴。
　
　朔屋が何度耳にした評価だったろう。
　ただ朔屋の方は自分がそうと言われても当然の人間だと早々に開き直り、むしろ軽んじられる事に逆説的な気楽さを見出したものだ。常人には当然の努力も勤勉も、自分には続けられる甲斐性もないと、とある女の情夫になってはや一週間目に覚った自堕落男。
　だが朔屋はそうと開き直れてもクロには？　待望していた『止まない嵐』に我が身を置いてみたのに、願っていたような明晰な感覚が曇ってしまったクロには？
source.english:
No good. Useless. A good-for-nothing.
How many times had Sakuya heard that verdict? He had long since accepted that he deserved it and even found a paradoxical ease in being despised. A mere week into life as some woman's kept lover, the wastrel had already realized he lacked the stuff to sustain even the effort and diligence ordinary men took for granted.
Sakuya could brazen it out. But Kuro? Kuro, who had finally placed herself in the longed-for ‘storm that never ends,’ only to find the clarity she had hoped for clouding over?

source.japanese: クロの呟きは、怠惰の粘液に塗れた朔屋の心の芯にさえ、ずしりと重く響いたという。
source.english: Her murmur struck with dull weight even at the core of Sakuya's heart, slimed over though it was with idleness.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Came all this way, to where a storm always blows, and still……」
【Naomasa】 「If you call that useless, then the rest of us are even worse. Well, you did seem to have a bit of trouble this time, but.」

No good. Hopeless. A useless guy. An assessment Sakuya must have heard countless times. Sakuya, however, had quickly adopted a defiant stance, embracing that he was indeed the kind of person who deserved such a label, and if anything, he even discovered a paradoxical comfort in being looked down upon. He really didn't have the ability to keep up with any of that hard work and diligence that regular people took for granted; that was the realization this dissolute, slovenly man had come to after but a week spent as the gigolo of a certain woman.

However, while Sakuya had defiantly embraced it, what of Kuro? Though she had finally cast herself into the 『Ceaseless Storm』that she had so long awaited, she found that the clarity of mind she had so eagerly desired had instead dimmed───what of Kuro?
Kuro's muttered words resonated deeply within the core of even Sakuya's heart, smeared in the phlegm of indolence though it was.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さん、クロは怖いよ」
source.english: “Mr. Sakuya, Kuro's scared.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「おかしいの。クロがちゃんと船長になれないのが怖い。でも今は、ちょっと違う、
　それだけじゃない」
source.english:
“It's strange. Kuro's scared of not being able to do the captain's job right. But now it's a little different.
That's not all.”

source.japanese: 台風の目の中という事で、クロのスイッチは中途半端に入ったままであり、いつもよりはやや言も明瞭だが、船を指揮する状態には程遠い。
source.english: In the storm's eye, Kuro's switch remained halfway on. Her words were a little clearer than usual, but far from the state in which she commanded the ship.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san, Kuro is scared.」
【Kuro】 「It's strange. Kuro is scared Kuro can't properly become captain. But right now, it's a bit different. That's not all.」

They were in what could be called the eye of a typhoon, so Kuro's switch remained halfway flicked, and her speech was somewhat more lucid than usual, although it was still a far cry from the state she was in when commanding the ship.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロはなんだか……この島が怖い」
source.english: “Somehow… Kuro's scared of this island.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おいおい……」
source.english: “Hey, now…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「せっかくの、ずっと探してた、
『止まない嵐』、なのに……」
source.english:
“Even though it's the ‘storm that never ends,’
the one Kuro's been searching for all this time…”

source.japanese: もう慰めの言葉も見当たらず、ただ機械的にクロの濡れ髪の水気をタオルに吸わせ続けるしかない朔屋、こんなやせっぽちの肢体に動く男心はないけれど、それでも一つ奮発して抱きしめてやるのはどうだろうと、クロの前に膝でにじった時───
source.english: No words of comfort remained. Sakuya could only go on mechanically blotting the wet from Kuro's hair with the towel. Her scrawny frame stirred no desire in him; even so, perhaps he could manage one grand gesture and embrace her. He shuffled toward her on his knees—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro is somehow……scared of this island.」
【Naomasa】 「Hey now……」
【Kuro】 「Came all this way, to what Kuro searched for all this time, the 『Ceaseless Storm』 and still……」
