No longer able to find any words of comfort, all Sakuya could do was mechanically continue to absorb the moisture from Kuro's drenched hair with the towel; while no part of his male instincts were moved by desire for this scrawny bag of bones, he still wondered if it wouldn't be the right thing for him to go the extra mile here and pluck up the courage to embrace her, and when he knelt down in front of Kuro───

source.japanese:
ぎい、と閉じていたはずの船窓が開いたのには二人とも仰天した。それで雨風激しく吹きこんできたならまだ納得いったものの、窓の開きは緩慢で、外でも風雨は籠もったように低い。ならば何故開いた。夜更けの駄目男と哀れな少女の愁嘆場に、雨と風の精がからかい混じりに水を差そうとしたとでも。
　二人はしばし凝結していたが、やがて朔屋は留め金の下ろし方が甘かったのだろうと自分に言い聞かせてまた窓を閉めようとして、
source.english:
The porthole that should have been shut opened with a creak. Both were startled. Had wind and rain rushed in fiercely, they might have understood. But it opened slowly, and outside the weather sounded low and muffled. Why, then, had it opened? Had spirits of rain and wind come to tease this late-night scene of a useless man and a pitiful girl's sorrow?
For a while they froze. Then Sakuya told himself he must not have lowered the catch properly and reached to close it again.

target.text: A creaking sounded. When the porthole, which was supposed to be closed shut, suddenly opened, they were both taken aback. Had the rain and wind violently blown inside, then he could have understood, but the window opened sluggishly, and even outside, the rainstorm seemed subdued as though it had been muffled. If so, then whyever had it opened? Perhaps the spirits of rain and wind wished to pour cold water on this pathetic scene of a useless man and a pitiful girl together late at night with a sprinkling of mischief. The two were frozen solid for a time, but eventually, Sakuya convinced himself that he hadn't been thorough enough when he latched it shut, and he once more went to close the porthole,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……今のなに！　今の声、なに！」
source.english: “…What was that! What was that voice!”

source.japanese:
朔屋には何も聞こえなかったが、後退るクロの、あまりに真に迫った恐怖の相に偽りとも思えず、そもそもこの娘にそんな小芝居を打つような知性は乏しい。
　だからクロに倣[なら]って耳を澄まして───
source.english:
Sakuya had heard nothing. But Kuro's retreating terror was too convincing to seem false. In any case, the girl possessed little of the intelligence needed for such a performance.
So, following her example, he listened closely—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え……？　なんか聞こえたか？
　俺には雨風の音しか───」
source.english:
“Huh…? Did you hear something?
All I hear is wind and rain—”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……What was that just now?! That voice, what was that?!」

Sakuya could not hear anything, but the fear on Kuro's face as she backed away seemed so natural that it was impossible to imagine it being a put-on, and the girl was probably too lacking in the intelligence necessary to stage a little performance like that in the first place. Therefore, following Kuro's example, he pricked up his ears───
【Naomasa】 「Huh……? Did you hear something? All I hear is the sound of wind and rain───」

source.japanese:
聞こえる───？　否。
　
　
　では聞こえない───？
　
　
　それも、否だった。
source.english:
Could he hear it? No.
Then he could not hear it?
That, too, was no.

source.japanese:
船窓に寄り来るは、島から吹き寄せる風。
　雨と波の囁きの中に切れ切れに、幽かに、それなのに言葉と判る音節、入り交じって。
source.english:
Wind came from the island to the porthole.
Faint and broken among the whispers of rain and waves, sounds mingled with it—yet unmistakably syllables, unmistakably words.

target.text: Could he hear it───? Nay. So then, could he not hear it───? That, too, was a nay.
Coming through the porthole was the wind blowing in from the island. Fragmented amidst the whispers of the rain and waves came syllables. Faint, and yet recognizable as words, mixed together.

source.japanese:
『我が造りし人を
　　　　　　　拭い去らん
　　　　　　　　人より獣　　　　　　　』
source.english:
‘Man whom I have made
             I will blot out
                 from man to beast             ’

source.japanese:
『　　　天空の鳥に至る
　　　　　　滅ぼさん
　　我　　　造りし　　　悔ゆれば　なり』
source.english:
‘       unto the birds of heaven
               I will destroy
     for I      repent      having made      ’

source.japanese:
『かくて　　　の後
　　　　　　洪水　　　臨めり
　　大淵の源皆破れ
　　　　　雨　　　注げり
　　　　　　　は　面に漂えり　　　　　』
source.english:
‘And after       
               the flood       came
     all the fountains of the great deep were broken open
            rain       poured
                 floated upon the surface       ’

target.text: 『 destroy mankind I have created from the face of the earth man to beast 』
『 even the fowls of the air shall destroy them For I regret act of creating this』
『Thus after cause it to rain upon all fountains great deep broken up rain fell upon went upon the face of 』

source.japanese:
───夜の雨風の中に言葉が漂うてあった。
　聞かせようとしているのか、ただ語りたいだけか、いずれにしても、怒り、哀しみ、悔やみ、そして───呪う言葉。
source.english:
Words drifted in the night's wind and rain.
Did they mean to be heard, or merely wish to speak? Either way, words of anger, sorrow, regret—and a curse.

source.japanese:
風の中に訴えのかのような声は。
　或いはこの世界の記憶であり───
　
　もしかしたら鎮魂の歌なのかも知れないが。
　だとしてもあまりに禍言めいて、朔屋の顔色死人のように青ざめさせ、
source.english:
That voice in the wind, almost pleading—
Perhaps it was a memory of this world.
Perhaps a song for the repose of the dead.
Even so, it sounded far too much like an ill-omened utterance, and Sakuya's face blanched to the color of a corpse.

target.text: ───There were words drifting within the nocturnal rainstorm. Were they trying to be heard, did they simply wish to speak? Regardless of which, they were words of anger, misery, regret, and───a malediction.

A voice, like a plea carried on the wind. Or perhaps it was a memory of this world─── Mayhap it could even be a requiem. But were it to be so, it was simply too ill-omened, and it made Sakuya's complexion turn pallid as a corpse,

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……いや、確かに何か、島から。
　こりゃあ、なんだ───うっ？」
source.english:
“…No, there's definitely something,
from the island. What is this—ugh?”

source.japanese:
腕に食いこんだ痛みに顔しかめ、振り返ればクロが、震える恐怖の塊だった。かくりと膝を突き、今にも倒れそうな体、支えていたのは朔屋の腕を掴んだ手。彼女自身は意識していなかったろうが、強く強く握りしめた手。クロにしては信じられないほど強い力が、恐怖の程を示していた。
　吹きこむ風から身を避けようと、朔屋の半身に縋[すが]って額を押し当てる、まるで見なければ聞かなければ、世界には自分を脅かす恐怖など存在しないとでも言うかのように。
source.english:
Pain bit into his arm. Grimacing, he turned to find Kuro reduced to a trembling knot of terror. Her knees had buckled, and only the hand locked around his arm kept her from falling. Without realizing it, she must have been gripping harder and harder. Such strength was unthinkable in Kuro, and showed the measure of her fear.
Seeking shelter from the incoming wind, she clung to his side and pressed her forehead against him, as though if she neither looked nor listened, the world could contain nothing capable of frightening her.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Wait, there is definitely something coming from the island. What is this───ough?」

He grimaced at the pain digging into his arm, and when he turned his head, there was Kuro, a bundle of shivering terror. She had fallen to her knees, and the only thing still supporting her body on the verge of collapse was her hand gripping on to Sakuya's arm. The girl herself did not seem to be aware of it, but her hand was grasping him tightly. It was with a strength that beggared belief coming from Kuro, and it displayed well the extent of her fear.

In an effort to escape the wind blowing in, she clung to one side of Sakuya's body and pressed her brow against him, as if to say that, for as long as she could not see or hear them, there existed no horrors in this world that could threaten her.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さん、クロは怖い。
　ほんとは……来たら、いけなかった？
　朔屋さん、クロを、クロを、助けて」
source.english:
“Mr. Sakuya, Kuro's scared.
Maybe Kuro… shouldn't have come after all?
Mr. Sakuya, help Kuro. Help Kuro.”

source.japanese: 夜の船、船員達は寝静まっているけれどもそこかしこに寝息や寝言が密かに響いて、生命の気配はあちこちに聞こえていたのにクロと朔屋はそれらから隔絶されて、ただ二人だけで夜の声の脅威に晒されて、お互いをただ一つの人肌のよすがとして抱き合っていたけれど、風の中から声が完全に消えた頃合いに、クロがようやく漏らした。
source.english: Night aboard the ship. The sailors slept, but breaths and muttered dreams sounded quietly here and there. Signs of life could be heard everywhere. Yet Kuro and Sakuya were cut off from them, exposed alone to the menace of the night's voice. They held each other as their sole refuge of human warmth. When the voice had completely vanished from the wind, Kuro finally spoke.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san, Kuro is scared. Maybe Kuro……really shouldn't ever have come here? Sakuya-san, Kuro-, help, save Kuro.」

A ship at night: though all the crew members were quietly at sleep, the whispers of their breathing and sleep-talking sounded secretively from here and there, signs of life could be heard from all over, and yet Kuro and Sakuya were completely isolated from all that; they were just the two of them, exposed to the menace of this nocturnal voice, each embracing the other tightly as the only source of human warmth they could rely on. By the time the voice had completely vanished from within the wind, Kuro finally let something out.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あれ……クロ、変。
　まだなんにもなってないのに、
　助けて、なんて」
source.english:
“Huh… Kuro's strange.
Nothing's happened yet,
and Kuro's asking for help…”

source.japanese: いったい何にあれほど怯えていたのか、彼女自身理解が及ばぬ、もどかしげな、けれど知ってしまうのも恐ろしいような、そんな微妙な表情で、朔屋の目を見上げ、ころりと小石のように軽く哀しく独りごちたのだった。
source.english: She could not herself understand what had frightened her so badly. Frustrated at not knowing, yet seemingly afraid to know, she looked up into Sakuya's eyes with an expression balanced delicately between the two. Then, speaking only to herself, she let the words fall with the light, sad finality of a pebble.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Huh……Kuro is weird. Nothing has happened yet, so why save?」

Whatever it was that could have scared her so, it seemed beyond the girl's own comprehension; frustrated, yet also terrified of coming to know the truth, that was what the complicated subtleties of the expression on the girl's face hinted at as she looked up into Sakuya's eyes, light and mournful words muttered only to the self tumbling out like tiny pebbles.

source.japanese:
翌朝明けて───といっても雨は引き続き重苦しく垂れこめて、目覚ましの明るい陽光は雲の帷[とばり]に敗退して船の四囲は寒色の色合いしか見えない、波も、島の遠景も、全てが灰緑色に沈んで気分を萎えさせる事甚だしい。
　昨日島に辿り着いた信天翁号の乗員達にはまだ二日目の雨だが、それでもこの島を取り巻く嵐は風説通りに永遠に止まないのではないかと誰彼となく思わしせしめる。
source.english:
Next morning dawned—though rain still hung heavy, and the bright sunlight that should have awakened them had lost its battle with the curtain of clouds. Only cold colors surrounded the ship. Waves and distant island alike sank into gray-green, thoroughly dispiriting.
For the Albatross's crew, who had reached the island yesterday, this was only the second day of rain. Yet it was enough to make anyone wonder whether the surrounding storm really would never end, as rumor claimed.

source.japanese:
それでも、なんの、船の修理もとりあえず一段落ついたし、雨くらいで怯むものか、こんな撃たれても冷たく濡れるだけで済むような雨、これまで潜[くぐ]ってきた銃弾と凶刃の雨に比べれば優しい子守歌のようなもの、という事で、短艇を早速下ろしにかかる信天翁号の航海士の双子や水夫長の目は明るかった、というより欲にぎらついていた。
　何しろザウエル、たとえそれがなくともこれだけの建築物擁した島、島内にはなにがしか金目の物が転がっていよう。となれば探索だと、篠つく雨音を圧して波間に鳴り渡る船乗りの歌は、昨日の疲労などは嘘のようにひたすら喧[やかま]しい。
　悪評を轟かす信天翁号、悪辣であり貪欲である為には、根本的に逞[たくま]しさが要求されるのである。
source.english:
But what of it? The repairs were done for the moment; why let a little rain frighten them? Rain that only left you cold and wet when it struck was a gentle lullaby beside the showers of bullets and murderous blades they'd passed through. The twin mates and boatswain hurried to lower a boat, their eyes bright—or rather, glittering with greed.
Zauer, after all. And even without it, an island boasting so many buildings must have something valuable lying about. Exploration, then! Sailors' songs rang over the waves above the driving rain, noisily enough to make yesterday's exhaustion seem a lie.
To be as vicious and greedy as the notorious Albatross, one needed a fundamental toughness.

source.japanese:
朝番から外れており、昨夜の夜更かしも尾を曳いて朔屋は朝食の時間を過ごしており、見苦しくも口一杯に馬鈴薯の潰した飯を詰めこんで上甲板に飛び出してきた時には、第一陣の短艇はもう島へと漕ぎ出したところ。
　第二陣の短艇に駆けこもうとした、足は空しく宙を蹴ったし首が絞まって口中のじゃがの滓を撒き散らして汚らしい。
　水夫長がその巻揚機はだしの膂力で朔屋の襟首摘[つま]んで持ち上げて、猫の仔にやるよりぞんざいに青年を揺すりたて、言い切ったのが一言、鉈で枝葉の余分なところを切り払うような一言。
source.english:
Exempt from morning watch and still feeling the effects of the night before, Sakuya had dawdled over breakfast; by the time he burst onto the upper deck, disgracefully cramming his mouth with mashed potatoes, the first launch was already pulling for the island.
He made a dash for the second, only for his feet to kick uselessly at the air, his collar to choke him, and scraps of potato to spray filthily from his mouth.
The boatswain had plucked him up by the collar with the raw strength of a windlass. Shaking the young man with less ceremony than he might a kitten, he delivered a single sentence—a hatchet-stroke stripping a branch of all its excess foliage.

target.text: Dawn broke on the following morn─── but with that said, the rain continued to fall, brooding and heavy, and the bright sunbeams of the early morning suffered defeat, withdrawing from their battle against the veil of clouds, leaving the surroundings of the ship dyed in nothing but cold colours─── the waves too, the distant scenery of the island too, all of it sinking into hues of greyish-green; what a tremendously demotivating sight. Having arrived at the island only yesterday, this was but the second day of rain for the crew members of the Albatross, and yet it was enough to leave them all wondering if, just as rumoured, the storm encircling this island truly was perpetual, ceaseless.

Still, this is nothing, the ship repairs have reached a good stopping point for now, who would cower before a bit of rain; at worst, we'll end up a little cold and wet, and compared to the rain of bullets and deadly blades we've overcome already, this is like a gentle lullaby; so it went, and the eyes of the twin first mates of the Albatross and her bosun, who had promptly begun to lower the boat, were bright, or rather, gleaming with greed.

In any case, even assuming there were none of these Sauers around, on an island with this many structures, they'd surely get their grubby hands on some sort of valuables. And with that being the case, they would go exploring; the song of the sailors resounding across the waves, drowning out the noise of the heavy drizzle, was so immensely loud it made the exhaustion of yesterday seem but a lie. The Albatross, name and reputation known far and wide, infamous for her viciousness and greed, fundamentally demanded indomitability from her crew.

Having been relieved of morning watch, and still feeling the aftermath of his late-night escapades of the prior night, Sakuya had been spending his time eating breakfast, and by the time he leapt out on the upper deck, his mouth disgracefully stuffed to the brim with his meal of mashed potatoes, the first group had already rowed out to the island. He tried to rush into the second group's boat, but his legs kicked through the air in vain, his neck was strangled, and the remnants of potato still in his mouth scattered everywhere in a filthy mess.

The Bosun had grabbed Sakuya by the collar and lifted him into the air using his immense, winch-like strength, shook the young man more roughly than a cat would her kitten, then made a single, decisive statement, a declaration that sounded like he was cutting off any excess branches with a Nata machete. (TN: The Nata machete, written "鉈", is as much a hatchet as it is a machete, adept at chopping and splitting branches with its short, heavy blade.)

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「新入りは、留守番だ」
source.english: “New hands stay aboard.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ええー……？　でもみんな行っちゃうじゃないの。特に女性陣なんかも……。
　泪さんだって」
source.english:
“Whaaat…? But everyone's going. Especially the women…
Even Rui.”

source.japanese: シサム・キサラは当然のように第一陣で出発し、日頃は船内の莫迦騒ぎからは一歩引いたところにたゆたう泪でさえ、第二陣の短艇の列に並んである。頭にはボンネット、ドレスにはケープを重ねたその輪郭、日頃の艶麗な肢体を隠して和らげつつも、若い娘のように華やいで、名指しされたのに振り返り、
source.english: Sisam and Kisara had naturally left with the first party. Even Rui, who normally floated a step apart from the ship's foolish commotions, stood in line for the second boat. Her bonnet and the cape over her dress concealed and softened her usual voluptuous figure, yet she looked as bright and festive as a young girl. Hearing herself named, she turned.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Rookies are on anchor watch.」
【Naomasa】 「Huuh……? But everybody's going, right? Especially the ladies……. Even Rui-san is going.」

Shisamu and Kisara departed with the first group as a matter of course, and even Rui, who usually drifted about a step removed from the ridiculous commotion on board the ship, stood in line by the second group's boat. With a bonnet on her head and a cape drawn over her dress, her usual charmingly elegant figure was concealed and softened, yet she still radiated beauty like a young girl, and when her name was called, she turned around,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あんまりぐらぐら揺れたので、たまにはしっかりした地面が踏みたいの」
source.english: “We've been tossed about so much. I'd like to stand on firm ground for a change.”

source.japanese: 退屈しのぎを隠そうともせず。陸続と下級水夫も続いて短艇の席は埋まっていったが、引き換え朔屋の胸中には置いてけぼりの空しさが広がって。島に感じた陰鬱な印象は印象として、仲間外れはそれより切ない。船には下級水夫達の大半が残ろうが、彼らは基本的に生真面目であり、雨に閉ざされた船内ではきっと自分は一人浮く、気鬱になると水夫長に抗議はしてみたけれども。
source.english: She made no effort to conceal that she was merely escaping boredom. Junior sailors streamed into line behind her until every seat in the launch was taken; meanwhile the hollow ache of being left behind spread through Sakuya. The island's gloom was one thing. Exclusion hurt worse. Most of the junior sailors would remain aboard, true, but they were an earnest lot, and shut up with them aboard a rainbound ship, he was sure to stand out alone and sink into melancholy. He tried that complaint on the boatswain, but—

target.text: 【Rui】 「It shook so terribly, and so I wish to stand on some solid ground for a change.」

She was not even trying to hide that she was just staving off her boredom. The seats in the boat were filled one after another with an endless stream of deck boys, but in return, the emptiness of being left behind spread through Sakuya's heart. The gloomy impression he got from the island was just that, an impression; being ostracized was far more miserable. The majority of the deck boys would probably be remaining on the ship, but they were fundamentally very earnest people, and thinking that he'd be the one man left out on this rain-covered ship, that he'd end up becoming depressed, he tried to protest to the Bosun, however.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それにな、クロがどうにも具合悪いみてえだ。朝食にも出てこなんだ。
　お前は残って看病してやんな。
　クロだって……ま、女は女だろう」
source.english:
“Besides, Kuro’s under the weather. Didn’t even show for breakfast.
You stay behind and tend to her. Kuro, too…
well, a woman’s a woman, after all.”

source.japanese: 朔屋が探索組に混ざる事熱望したのも、できれば女の子と一緒に過ごしたい、もしかしたら島にも女の子とお酒呑めるところくらいあるかもしれないと邪念抱いていたからに過ぎず、もしも航海士の双子かさもなくてもちょっと怖いが泪でもいい、差し向かいで飲めば気塞ぎな雨も肴になるだろうとの不料簡、こんなのは当然水夫長にどつかれて留守番組に回されても仕方ない。
source.english: Sakuya had begged to join the search party only because he wanted, if possible, to spend time with a girl—and because perhaps the island might even have somewhere he could drink with one. The twin mates would be ideal; failing them, Rui would do, intimidating though she was. Drinking face-to-face, even the gloomy rain might make a decent accompaniment. With motives so misguided, of course the boatswain could hardly be blamed for knocking him about and assigning him to the party staying aboard.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやさすがに俺も、あれに手を出そうとは……だいたい普段アンタ達だって、クロの事女の子扱い全然してないでないの」
source.english: “No, even I wouldn’t go so far as to make a move on that… Besides, you guys don’t normally treat Kuro like a girl at all, do you?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Besides, Kuro doesn't seem to be doing too good. Didn't even show up for breakfast. You stay behind and nurse her. And even Kuro is……well, a woman's a woman, right?」

Sakuya's burning desire to join the exploration team stemmed from a want that, if possible, he'd love to spend some time with a girl, and perhaps, there might even be a place on this island where one could share a drink with one; it was no more than these wicked thoughts he harboured; maybe with the twin first mates, and if not them, then, though she was a bit scary, he could settle for Rui, but as long as he could drink face to face with someone, even this unpleasant rain could make a good conversation starter, such were the indiscreet thoughts that filled his head; it was only natural that a man like this would be punched by the Bosun, and being assigned to anchor watch was also inevitable.
【Naomasa】 「Oh come on, even I wouldn't try to go there with her……besides, it's not like you guys ever treat Kuro like a girl, do you?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「うるせえ」
source.english: “Shut up.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Shut it.」

source.japanese: 一喝され、手荒に下ろされ押し出されてたたらを踏んだ、前にのめって鼻先から甲板に倒れかかるところを踏み留まって向き直れば、水夫長はあの肥腹に不釣り合いの意外に軽敏な動きで縄梯子から下っていくところ。追いすがってしつこく覗きこめば、鼻面にぱんと叩きつけられたのが、送り幽霊を封じるお札のような、一冊のペーパーバック。
source.english: After that roar, Sakuya was set down roughly and shoved away. He stumbled forward, almost fell nose-first onto the deck, and recovered. Turning back, he found the boatswain descending the rope ladder with an unexpected nimbleness for such a fat belly. Sakuya followed and persistently peered down. A paperback slapped into his face, like a talisman sealing away a ghost that would not stop following.

target.text: Rebuked, he stumbled after being roughly lowered to the ground and pushed away, and as he tumbled forwards, on the verge of falling nose-first on the deck, he managed to stand firm; by the time he turned around, the Bosun was already descending the rope ladder with surprisingly agile steps, disproportionate to his large belly. Hot on his heels, when Sakuya stubbornly went to take a look, with a thump, he was hit on the nose by something; it was a paperback book, like a talisman to seal away the spirits of the deceased as they passed on to the afterlife.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ええから留守番しておれっちゅうに。
　退屈ならそいつを読んでろ。
　ただし汚したり破ったりしたなら、
　一頁につき鞭一〇回だからな」
source.english:
“I'm telling you, stay aboard.
If you're bored, read that.
But if you dirty it or tear it,
it's ten lashes for every page.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「That's enough out of you, just stay here and watch the ship. If you get bored, read this. But if anything's stained or torn, you're getting ten lashes for every page.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うああん、ここまで頼んでも駄目、
　あんた達ひどい、俺仲間外れ。
　俺哀しい、仕方ない、本読む……」
source.english:
“Waaah… All that begging. Still no.
You're cruel. Left out. I'm sad.
Nothing for it. I'll read the book…”

source.japanese: 不満で片言になるも、表紙を改める、水夫長が気を利かしてせめてポルノ小説でも置いていってくれたならまだ我慢もできよう、と、文字を追う目が引っかかる、漢字仮名でない、アルファベットで意味が飲みこみづらかった。
source.english: Discontent reduced him to fragments. Still, he inspected the cover. Had the boatswain thoughtfully left him a pornographic novel, he might have borne it. His eyes caught on the lettering. Not kanji and kana, but letters of the alphabet. The meaning was harder to grasp.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Waaah, even after begging this much, I'm still getting nowhere. You guys are terrible, leaving me out. What misery, but what can I do, I'll read the book……」

Though he prattled on like a child in dissatisfaction, he still inspected the cover of the book; had the Bosun been considerate enough to leave a porn novel for him, then he might just be able to make do, but, as they trailed down the letters, something caught his eyes; this wasn't written in kanji or kana, it was written in the English alphabet, and that made it difficult for him to grasp the meaning.

source.japanese:
『Ｔｈｅ　Ｎａｒｒａｔｉｖｅ　ｏｆ　
　Ａｒｔｈｕｒ　Ｇｏｒｄｏｎ　Ｐｙｍ
　ｏｆ　Ｎａｎｔｕｃｋｅｔ』
source.english:
The Narrative of
Arthur Gordon Pym
of Nantucket

source.japanese:
とまたずらずら長い、邦訳版でない原書の、読んで読めない事はないけれど、何が哀しくて慣れない言語で疲れる読書と叩き返そうとしたが、手が逸れて海に放りこんだりしては大人しく留守居していた方が百倍は増しという目にあわされる。それでも未練がましく舷側から短艇見下ろせば、下級水夫の中でも剽軽者が朔屋に向かって帽子とってのご挨拶、零れた髪が暗鬱な波の中にあって目覚ましく黒く艶[なま]めいた。
　そいつは、下級水夫などではなかった。
source.english:
Another interminable title. The original English, not a Japanese translation. He could read it, but why should he tire himself with a book in an unfamiliar language? He nearly threw it back. Yet if his hand slipped and sent it into the sea, he would suffer something a hundred times worse than quietly staying aboard. Still wistful, he looked down over the side at the boat. One of the more mischievous junior sailors took off his cap in greeting. The hair that spilled out was strikingly black and lovely against the gloomy waves.
Not a junior sailor at all.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あっ。あいつ！
　あいつまでちゃっかり！」
source.english:
“Ah!
Her! Even she managed it!”

target.text: 『 THE NARRATIVE OF ARTHUR GORDON PYM OF NANTUCKET 』

So it continued in a long, drawn-out string of letters, the original book, not a Japanese translation, and though it was not as if he couldn't read it, he would be so miserable and exhausted trying to read in a language he was unaccustomed to that he almost tried to throw the book back at the Bosun in retaliation, but if his aim was off and he ended up tossing it into the ocean, then his suffering would be a hundred-fold that of just quietly staying on the ship. When he nevertheless looked down at the boat, still not knowing when to give up, a jovial fellow of a deck boy faced Sakuya and tipped his hat in greeting, his wet hair a strikingly glossy dark even when framed by the gloomy sea.
That right there, that was no deck boy.
【Naomasa】 「Ah. It's her! Even she's sneaking on!」

source.japanese: 下級水夫の外見の記号としてセーラー帽というのがあるけれど、それ一つ被るだけでよくばれない、周りの目は節穴かと憤るが、よくよく考えれば周りの下級水夫達の目は前髪の奥であるのか無いのか判らない、ともかくそいつはあの密航者、常習的密航犯の、これまでどこに潜[ひそ]んでいたものか、そしてなんの意図があるのか知らず、ともかく彼女までがちゃっかり短艇に乗りこんでいたのには朔屋、心底悔しいやら情けないやら。
source.english: A sailor cap was one of the junior sailors' identifying marks. But to go unnoticed merely by putting one on—were everyone's eyes no better than knotholes? Then again, the other junior sailors' eyes were hidden beneath their bangs; one could scarcely tell whether they had eyes at all. Anyway, it was the stowaway. The habitual stowaway. Where she had been hiding, or what she intended, he did not know. But even she had neatly slipped into the boat. Sakuya was bitterly vexed and miserable.

target.text: A sailor hat is the classic visual shorthand for a deck boy, but it was still quite shocking that just wearing one of those let her get away with it; he seethed that every person around her must be blind, but thinking about it more carefully, he couldn't actually tell if the deck boys around her even had eyes hidden deep beneath those forelocks; regardless, it was that stowaway, she who habitually committed the crime of stowing away,; where had she even been hiding until now, and he also had no clue what her intentions were, but regardless, given that even she had shrewdly managed to sneak her way on board that boat, Sakuya felt both bitterly disappointed and pathetic from the bottom of his heart.

source.japanese:
渋々居残る事受け入れるしか無く、朔屋、
船内通路に降りるも、こうむかっ腹では足取りも荒くなろうし目につく一々が癇に触って仕方ない。そもそも船内通路からして変に暗くて長くて邪魔物ばかりで裏ぶれた工場の地下道じみて意気を削ぐ、色合いだって婆の造る煮染めみたい地味、こうなればと朔屋は倉庫からペンキ缶を持ち出す事を考えた。
　この地味な通路を、水夫長を嘲る絵やら航海士の双子の、より卑猥にディフォルメした裸体やらで埋めつくす事に費やせば、退屈な一日もそれなりに過ごせるだろう。
　だが、としかつめらしく腕組みに黙考の、衝動に流されるのはそれはそれで愉[たの]しいだろうが、通路を落書きだらけにしてしまえばこれから先青年自身一時の勢いの痕跡に悩まされる事にもなりかねない。
source.english:
With no choice but to accept being left behind, Sakuya descended into the ship's passageways. In such a temper his tread naturally grew heavy, and every last thing in sight grated on him. The passage itself was perversely dark, long, and choked with obstacles, dispiriting as a tunnel beneath a derelict factory; even its palette was as drab as an old woman's pot of simmered vegetables. Thereupon Sakuya conceived of fetching a paint can from the storeroom.
A day spent covering these dreary corridors with pictures mocking the boatswain and grotesquely lewder caricatures of the twin mates' naked bodies might prove tolerable after all.
Then he folded his arms and considered the matter gravely. Surrendering to impulse would certainly be enjoyable, but if he filled the passageways with graffiti, he himself might be condemned to live among the traces of that momentary enthusiasm ever after.

source.japanese:
どうやら目論見は目論見のままに留めておくのが良さそうだと、唇へしゃげさせて諦めて、朔屋はクロの船室へ向かった。彼自身昨夜の様子からクロの事が少なからず気にかかっていたのである。
　昨夜はあの後どうにか宥[なだ]めてクロを船室まで送り、寝台に押しこんだがやはりすぐには寝つけない様子。枕元に侍って寝物語の柄でなし、すがる眼差しを振りきって船室を後にしたのだけれど、白子の娘がその後悶々と輾転反側したのは想像に易く、事実今朝も朝食の席に居合わせなかったとか。
source.english:
Best let the scheme remain a scheme. He twisted his lips, abandoned it, and headed for Kuro's cabin. Her condition last night had worried him too.
Afterward, he had somehow soothed her, taken her to the cabin, and bundled her into bed. She still did not seem able to sleep. He was not the sort to sit at her bedside telling stories. He had shaken off her clinging gaze and left. It was easy to imagine the albino girl tossing and turning afterward. In fact, she apparently hadn't been at breakfast that morning, either.

source.japanese: それでも水夫長の言いつけに大人しく従うようなが業腹で、更にどすどすと、床に長靴叩きつける勢いでクロの部屋まで来たところ、中から伝わったのは跫音にあからさまに大慌ての気配、具合悪しと聞いたが騒げる元気はあるようで、叩扉もいい加減に引き開ければドアノブが引っかかる、を強引に引いて室内に踏みこむと───
source.english: Still, the thought of meekly obeying the boatswain’s orders stuck in his craw. He stomped all the harder, as though meaning to drive his boots through the floor, and when he reached Kuro’s room, the sound of his approach set off a transparently frantic commotion within. Sick, was she? She seemed lively enough to make a racket. Giving the door no more than a perfunctory knock, he pulled; the knob caught. He wrenched it past the resistance and stepped inside—

target.text: All he could do was reluctantly accept that he was to stay behind, and Sakuya, though he descended into the passageway, was so angry that it was no wonder his footfalls were so heavy, that every little thing that caught his eye grated on his nerves.

And to begin with, for a passageway in a ship, it was weirdly dark and long and full of things that just got in the way; it was more like the subterranean tunnels of some run-down factory, really, simply discouraging, and even its colouring was as plain as the nishime his granny made, and if this is how it's going to be, Sakuya thought as he considered retrieving a paint can from the hold. (TN: Nishime, written "煮染め", is a Japanese dish of vegetables and things like konnyaku simmered in soy until the liquid is almost gone.)

If he spent his time painting over this drab passageway with, say, pictures ridiculing the Bosun, or covering it in the naked bodies of the twin first mates, deformed in ever more obscene ways, that would make for a bearable way to make a boring day pass him by. However, Sakuya thought, crossing his arms, now silent in deep thought; while it would be quite fun to just let go and have his impulses take the wheel, once he'd ended up filling the passageway with graffiti, it was not hard to imagine that afterwards, the young man himself would end up being tormented by the evidence left in the wake of his fleeting passions.

It was probably for the best that he left his scheming as just that, Sakuya thought as he pursed his lips flat, gave up on the idea, and then headed for Kuro's cabin. He himself was not a little worried about Kuro after how she had acted last night.

Last night, he'd somehow managed to calm Kuro down after that incident, then escorted her back to her cabin, but though he crammed her into her bed, she didn't seem like she'd be falling asleep any time soon. He was not the type to wait on someone by their bedside and tell them a bedtime story, and he had brushed off her pleading looks and left her cabin; still, it was easy to imagine how the albino girl would continue to toss and turn in agony afterwards, and in fact, she had not shown up for breakfast this morning either, apparently.

Nevertheless, he resented the idea of just meekly obeying the Bosun's orders, so when he arrived at Kuro's cabin, it was with heavier and heavier stomps, almost slamming his boots against the floor, and from within the cabin came the sound of footsteps, ones clearly hinting at a state of great panic; he'd been told she wasn't feeling well, but based on the tumult within, she certainly seemed energetic enough; giving the door a perfunctory knock, he pulled it open only for the doorknob to snag, but he wrenched it open regardless and stepped inside the room───

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「っあばっ……わ、うあ、
　だめ……っ！　いまクロいない、
　ないない！」
source.english:
“Ah—buh… W-wah! No…
Kuro's not here. Not here,
not here!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Abuh……wah, uwaah, no, don't……! Kuro isn't here right now, not here not here!」

source.japanese:
眼前に乱れ散ったぶわぶわ白いの、養蚕の繭棚をひっくり返したのではない、ドアノブを抑えたのが朔屋が力任せに引ききった反動で尻餅ついたクロの髪。
　目に被さって隠したけれど、口元が判りやすく焦って声も上擦って、じたじたと部屋の隅へと四つ這いににじる。
source.english:
The fluffy whiteness scattered before him was not an overturned rack of silkworm cocoons. It was Kuro's hair. She had been holding the knob, and his forcible pull had sent her onto her backside.
Her hair covered her eyes, but her mouth clearly showed panic. Her voice rose, and she scrabbled on all fours toward a corner.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや普通にいるじゃないの」
source.english: “You're right here.”

target.text: A billowing, white mass scattered before his eyes; it wasn't that he had upended a sericulture rack full of cocoons, it was Kuro's hair, who had been holding the doorknob, then fallen onto her backside from the recoil of Sakuya pulling it with all his might. Though her eyes were covered and hidden from him, her mouth easily betrayed her panic; her voice was also shrill, and cowering, she scrambled on all fours into a corner of the room.
【Naomasa】 「No, you're actually just right there, aren't you.」

source.japanese: ばかりか、彼女にしては俊敏な挙動で、これで元気がないというなら世のあらかたの人間は半病人と言う事になる。部屋の隅まで這いずって、捏ねてあったのに覆い被さったのは隠すつもりか、だがクロの体躯ではそれこそ白鼠が砕く前の鏡餅を腹の下にかいこもうとするようなもので、脇腹や股の間からはみ出してしまって丸わかり、どうやら寝台の敷布と見えた、が。
source.english: And remarkably quick, for her. If this was a lack of energy, most of humanity must be half-sick. In the corner, she covered a crumpled heap, apparently trying to hide it. But her little body could no more conceal it than a white rat could tuck an unbroken stack of New Year's rice cakes beneath its belly. It protruded at her sides and between her legs, perfectly visible. Apparently a bedsheet, but—

target.text: Not only that, her movements were surprisingly agile for her, so if this was considered not feeling well, then most people in the world would have to be considered semi-invalids. She crawled all the way into the corner, and perhaps her nonsensical argument was an attempt to hide whatever it was she was covering, but with Kuro's small frame, it was like a white mouse trying to tuck a still-intact kagami mochi beneath its belly; it bulged out from the sides of her torso and between her legs, plain to see, and it looked like the sheets from her bed, but. (TN: Kagami mochi, written "鏡餅", is a New Year offering consisting of two pieces of mochi stacked on each other.)

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いないの、ないの。
　これもない、ないです、
　入っちゃ……だめ」
source.english:
“Not here. Not here.
This isn't here either.
It's not. Don't… come in.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……お前さん、なにを必死に隠そうしてるのかと思ったら」
source.english: “…I was wondering what you were so desperate to hide.”

source.japanese: 敷き布の上に被さり、朔屋に肩越しに上擦った目線を寄越してはまた俯[うつむ]く、こういう風に狼狽著しいのは、さて自分だったらどんな場合だろうとざっと脳裏に思い浮かべても、自涜の場面を手伝い女に目撃された際、自慰の具の猥本を布団の下に押しこもうとしたあの時の状況くらいしか思い当たらぬ、どこまでも下[シモ]に思考が結びついてしまう朔屋だったが、この時は尾籠と詰[なじ]るどころか正解に近かった。
source.english: She lay on the bedspread, glancing sidelong over her shoulder at Sakuya, then back down—so visibly flustered that he briefly wondered what could put him in such a state. The only situation that came to mind was the time he’d tried to shove his porn magazine under the futon after being caught by a maid while jerking off. Sakuya’s thoughts were inevitably tied to his lower regions, but on this occasion, far from deserving a rebuke for vulgarity, he was actually quite close to the correct answer.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Not in here, not here. This isn't here either, it's not, you can't……come in.」
【Naomasa】 「……Oh you. And here I was, wondering what you were so desperately trying to hide.」

Covering the sheets by lying on top of them, sending a flustered look over her shoulder at Sakuya, then once more casting her eyes downward; what could have left her so remarkably panicked? Well now, if this was me in her place, what could have brought me to this, but though he briefly tried to imagine it, all it reminded him of was the scene back when he was caught masturbating by the help, then desperately tried to shove the pornographic book he'd used for masturbatory aid beneath his futon; Sakuya's mind always headed right for the gutter, but this time, it should not be harped on as mere vulgarity, and in fact, it was quite close to the truth of the matter.

source.japanese:
そう、下の事だ。
　初めは何事かと戸惑った朔屋だが、室内の空気に残る臭いには覚えがある、これは『船長の箱』の中に立ち籠めていたあの臭い、つんと鼻を衝[つ]く、零れた尿の。
　尿の臭い、クロが隠そうとしていたのは彼女の煎餅布団。臭いは小便の臭い。となれば導き出される帰結は一つの、どうにもこの小娘、寝小便を垂れてしまっていたらしい……。
　それと気づいてそっと無言で部屋を出てやるような気遣い、武士の情け乙女の含羞いといった類の心配りを、この鈍感な朔屋ができるはずもなく、そればかりか極めて簡潔に要点を衝[つ]いた一言で結んだのだった。
　一言で、クロの急所を抉[えぐ]ったのだった。
source.english:
Yes: something below the waist.
At first Sakuya had been puzzled. Then he recognized the smell lingering in the room—the same stink that had filled the ‘Captain's Box,’ the sharp nose-sting of spilled urine.
Urine. Kuro was trying to hide her pancake-thin futon. The room smelled of piss. Only one conclusion remained: the wretched girl had wet the bed…
Sakuya, dense as ever, possessed none of the grace to withdraw in silence once he understood—none of that courtesy one might call a samurai's compassion or consideration for a maiden's modesty. Quite the opposite. He summed up the situation in a single blunt remark that struck straight to the point.
One sentence, driven into Kuro's most vulnerable spot.

target.text: Indeed, matters relating to the gutter. At first, Sakuya was perplexed as to what this could possibly be, but he recognized that smell lingering in the room from somewhere; it was that very same smell that also lingered inside the 『Captain's Box』, the pungent, stinging smell of spilt urine. The smell of urine, and what Kuro was trying to hide was her thin bedding. The smell was the smell of pee. And with that being the case, there was only one conclusion that could be derived from this: it seemed this little girl had accidentally wet the bed…….

Upon noticing this, he was considerate enough to sneak out of the room wordlessly, showing a tact akin to a samurai's compassion or the delicate bashfulness of a maiden───there was no way this insensitive dullard Sakuya could do such a thing; on the contrary, he concluded things with an exceedingly succinct, to-the-point remark. And with that single remark, he cut Kuro to the quick.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ、寝小便」
source.english: “Oh, bedwetting.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Oh, you wet the bed.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「う～～～……。
　見ないでって。クロ言ったのに。
　ふぇ、えぅ……うう……ぐしゅっ」
source.english:
“Uuuuugh…
I told you not to look. Kuro told you.
Fuh… euh… uu… sniffle.”

source.japanese: たちまち火が点いたように泣き出すクロに困り果てる朔屋の、その時になってようやく、彼女がレギンスも着けていない、下半身剥き出しだったのに気づく始末で───
source.english: Kuro burst into tears as though someone had touched a match to her, leaving Sakuya utterly at a loss. Only then did he finally notice that she wore no leggings at all—that she was bare from the waist down—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uuh～～～……. Don't look. Kuro even said it. Fweh, euh……uu……snff.」

Like a fire erupting, Kuro suddenly burst into tears, leaving Sakuya utterly at his wits' end, but it was only then that he finally noticed it: that the girl was not even wearing her leggings, her lower body completely bare───

source.japanese:
雨は時に強まり、弱まりしながらも延々と留まる時を知らず。今は小糠雨という、霧吹きで散らしたように粒が微細な雨で、傘を持ち出しても風に流されて縁から内に入りこんで吹くや肌にまとわりつき、さりとて防水衣を持ち出す程には大振りというのではない憎たらしい匙加減、そもそも信天翁号にはその手の小洒落た装備は乏しく、第一陣、二陣併せて一〇人余の探索隊全員に行き渡る数すら揃わない。
　木造の家並みの合間を縫う通路は、両脇に庇[ひさし]が大きく張り出しその下を歩む限りは雨も防がれそうな造りだが、こう、降るというより舞い飛ぶような細かい粒が相手では。
source.english:
The rain went on without cease, waxing and waning. At present it was a powder-fine drizzle, more like spray from an atomizer than falling rain. An umbrella did little: the wind drove moisture under its rim to cling to the skin. Yet the rain was not heavy enough to warrant waterproofs—an infuriatingly exact degree of nuisance. In any case, the Albatross possessed few such refined conveniences, nowhere near enough for the dozen or so explorers in the two parties.
The lanes threading between the wooden houses had deep eaves projecting from both sides, enough to shelter anyone walking below—against ordinary rain. But droplets this fine flew more than they fell—

source.japanese: なので皆、毛先や肌に一面薄白い粉を塗[まぶ]したかに露がしとど、鼻腔にまで侵入してくる水気は閉口ものと見えて、意気揚々と乗りこんできたわりには一行の歩度は息が詰まったようにもたついて、樹上しか知らない猿が水中に放りこまれた不様と異ならず、ただ泪ばかりがケープの端やドレスの裳裾を軽やかに捌[さば]く、水魚の鰭[ひれ]の優雅が一同の中に華やかな。軽やかな布地にも関わらず水気を弾くのは、よほど高級で目の詰んだ生地なのか。
source.english: Everyone's hair and skin were thickly beaded with moisture, as if dusted all over with fine white powder. It insinuated itself even into their nostrils, to general disgust. For all the party's triumphant arrival, their pace now dragged as though breath had grown short; they looked no better than tree-dwelling monkeys thrown into water. Only Rui moved gracefully among them, lightly managing the edges of her cape and the hem of her dress like the fins of a fish. Despite its lightness, the fabric shed water. Very costly, perhaps, and woven exceedingly close.

source.japanese:
短艇を乗り付けた桟橋が木組みだったのはまだしもとして、踏みいっていく先までが桟橋と同様の材、組み方の板敷きの通路とあっては、この島の住人の木造嗜好も相当に徹底している。まるでそれ以外の建材を見た事がないとでも言いたげな。
　元は木造の文化圏の生まれである泪にしてから外地での生活が長く、ここまで木造建築で埋めつくした屋並みは珍しいようで、初めはあれこれと目線を振り向けていたけれど、建物の、高さに差はあってもどれも似たような造りが続くのにすぐに飽きて、今では小さな欠伸で上品に退屈の意を表明している。
source.english:
A wooden pier for the boat was one thing. But the passages ahead were plank walks made of the same material and construction. The inhabitants' preference for wood was remarkably thorough, as if they had never seen another building material.
Rui had been born into a culture of wooden buildings, but she had spent many years abroad; a townscape so completely filled with them seemed unusual even to her. At first she looked this way and that. But despite differences in height, they all continued in much the same style. She soon tired of them and now expressed her boredom with small, polite yawns.

source.japanese:
気鬱ぎの細雨とただ連なるばかりで見映えのしない木造の家屋達の、この単調かつ暗く侘びしい景色にも一同は、島の住人と出会えて言葉を交わせるなら、状況も変わるだろう、とて耐えた。
　このろくに訪れる船乗りとていないような島では信天翁号の悪評も伝わっていないだろう、先入観を弾いた『取り引き』も可能やも知れぬ。周囲の家屋に押し入って、海賊が山賊に商売替えしたかの乱行を避けたのは住人達の目を憚ってこそで。
source.english:
The party endured the monotonous, dark, desolate scene: disheartening drizzle and one undistinguished wooden house after another. If they could only meet the islanders and exchange a few words, matters might improve.
On an island scarcely visited by sailors, the Albatross's infamy had probably never reached anyone. ‘Trade’ unburdened by prejudice might therefore be possible. Only the thought of being watched by the inhabitants kept them from breaking into the houses and behaving like pirates who had changed trades and taken up banditry.

source.japanese:
だが水夫長が潮で鍛えた胴間声響かせ、家並みに垂れこめる霧雨を渦に乱しても。
　シサムとキサラが外向けの、特に男の耳朶に訴えるような作り声で四つ辻から四方に声を投げてみても。
　下級水夫達が変声期前の声でくすぐったく、かつ健気に居並ぶ家屋の戸を叩いてみても。
　全て声は、静けさに迎えられて呑みこまれて、木造の壁や辻を伝って遠ざかってそれっきり。
　答える喉はなく、かといって排斥の沈黙で一行を見舞っている気配さえもなく、動くものといっては通路歩む彼らだけ。
source.english:
But even when the boatswain's salt-hardened bellow set the mist over the houses swirling—
Even when Sisam and Kisara called in all four directions from a crossroads, putting on voices meant especially to appeal to men's ears—
Even when the junior sailors knocked at the doors, calling earnestly in voices not yet broken, voices that almost tickled the ear—
Every voice was received by silence and swallowed. It traveled along wooden walls and intersections, dwindled, and was gone.
No throat answered. Nor was there even a sense of silence meant to exclude them. The only movement was their own along the passages.

target.text: Though the rain would intensify at times, subside at others, it still kept falling as though unfamiliar with even the concept of cessation. It was now a light drizzle, composed of droplets so fine it was like they had been sprayed out by a vaporiser, and were one to bring an umbrella, the wind would blow the rain around the edges; it would cling to the skin, yet for all that, it was an odious dosage of moisture, not heavy to the extent one would feel the need to bring waterproof clothing, not that the Albatross had much in the way of such fancy equipment.

She was not even loaded with enough supplies to cover the combined numbers of the first and second expedition team, which counted only a little over ten people between the two. The passages winding between the rows of wooden houses were built with eaves that served as large overhangs on both sides, seemingly to protect one from the rain as long as one walked underneath them, but against a rain like this, which seemed to whirl around in the wind rather than fall from above, they were wanting.

Therefore, the tips of the hair and the surface of the skin of everyone present dripped with dew as though sprinkled in a faint white dust, they all appeared to be fed up with the moisture that even invaded their nostrils, and though their spirits had been so high when they boarded the boat, the walking pace of the party was now sluggish as though they struggled to breathe, their clumsiness no different from a monkey that had only known life in the treetops being tossed into water.

Only Rui, as she nimbly swept the edges of her cape and the hem of her dress, possessed the fluid grace of a fish fin, an elegance that stood out among the entire party. The fabric still repelled the water despite its lightness, so it must have been some exceptionally high-grade, densely woven fabric

It was one thing for the pier where they had rowed the boat alongside to be made of timber, but when even the very paths stretching inland were planked in the exact same materials as the pier, it became clear that the residents of this island were remarkably thorough in their penchant for woodwork. It almost seemed to say that they had never even seen any other building materials.

Though Rui did hail from a cultural sphere of wooden construction, she had spent long years living in foreign lands, and rows of houses so entirely filled with wooden buildings seemed a rare sight for her, too; at first, her eyes fluttered from here to there, but though there was some difference in the height of the buildings, each and every one of them all seemed of a very similar make, and so she quickly lost interest in them, now elegantly expressing her boredom through small yawns.

Even in this monotonous, dark, and desolate scenery composed of a depressing drizzle and endless rows of drab wooden houses, the group endured, believing that if they could just meet the residents of this island and exchange some words with them, surely the situation would change.

On this island, which certainly didn't seem like it got much in the way of visiting sailors, the Albatross' infamous reputation had surely not preceded them, so it might even be possible for them to make some "deals" without any preconceived notions getting in the way. That they did not forcibly break into the surrounding houses, avoiding the sorts of violent conduct that would make them look like pirates who had changed occupation to brigands, was precisely because they were concerned how that would reflect in the eyes of the residents.

However, though the Bosun let his vulgarly thick voice tempered on the seas resound far and wide, disrupting the drizzle shrouding the rows of houses into a swirling vortex. Even as Shisamu and Kisara tried shouting in every which direction down the intersections with unnaturally put-on voices, the sort that appealed to the male ear in particular, still. The deck boys were embarrassed by their prepubescent voices, and they also knocked politely on the doors of every house down the row, but for all that.

All these voices were met with and swallowed up by silence, drifting away into the distance along the wooden walls and intersections, and that was the end of that. No voices answered their calls, nor were there even any signs of the silence of shunning befalling the group; the only things in motion here were them, walking down the paths.

source.japanese: この島全体を覆った木造の建築群は、どうやら生命の鼓動なくした廃址なのだった。
source.english: The mass of wooden buildings covering the island was, it seemed, a ruin bereft of every pulse of life.

source.japanese:
そうと察せられた後でも一行が、早速屋内に侵入を試みて掠奪と企てなかったのは、今は亡き島の住人達の怒りを殊勝に恐れたなどではなく、ただ契機を失ってしまっただけの事。それに、かの珍[めずら]かな貴石がこう見た目に十把一絡げの屋並みの中に収められているなど、軒先の干し柿の紐の先に金塊を風鎮とぶら下げているようなもの、有り得ないと一行の中に暗黙の了解が生じていたからもある。
　ともかく、そういう次第で一行は、初めは呼び交わしていた声も尻すぼまりに、辺りの家並みの中に押し入る事もせず、とりあえずは家並みの様子が変わる辺りまで、宝物を収めていそうな倉の類が見えるまでと細雨の中を黙々進んでいた訳なのだが。
source.english:
Even after realizing this, the party did not immediately break in and begin looting. Not because they admirably feared the anger of the dead islanders; their cue had simply vanished. Besides, an unspoken consensus had formed that the rare gem could not possibly lie among rows of houses so indistinguishable from the outside. One might as well hang a gold ingot as the weight on a string of persimmons drying beneath the eaves.
So their calls gradually died away. Without entering any of the houses around them, they trudged silently through the drizzle, intending at least to continue until the neighborhood changed—until they saw some storehouse that looked fit to hold treasure.

source.japanese:
聞こえるものはそれぞれの雨に咽[むせ]ぶような息遣い、濡れた板壁や板敷きの通路は風情といえばいえたが沈鬱で、街並みを行くというより、果てしない深みに沈潜していくような、信天翁号の上甲板に出るより閉塞感をもたらして、空気は湿気っぽいのに一同の心をざらつかせる。
　遂にこらえかねたか、双子の一方立ち止まり、しげしげと庇[ひさし]を支える柱を見つめて、睨んで、このままでは鬱憤に囓りつくのでは、と周りに緊張及ぼしたが、
source.english:
They heard only one another's breathing, as though each were choking on the rain. Wet board walls and plank walkways possessed atmosphere, certainly, but it was a melancholy one. This felt less like walking through a town than sinking into some bottomless depth—more claustrophobic even than the Albatross's crowded upper deck. The air was damp, yet somehow rasped their spirits raw.
At last one of the twins stopped, perhaps unable to bear it any longer, and studied a post supporting the eaves. Studied it, then glared. Those around her tensed, half expecting her to bite into it out of sheer frustration. But—

target.text: The clusters of wooden construction covering this entire island appeared to be nothing but ruins bereft of the throbbing heartbeat of life.

Though they had surmised as much, that the party still did not immediately attempt to break into the buildings and pillage what remained was not because they were afraid of incurring the resentment of the villagers of this dead island, nothing so laudable as that, the impetus to do so had simply passed them by. Furthermore, did it really look like that certain rare, precious stone would be contained within these rows of similar houses? It would be like tying a gold ingot to the end of a string of dried persimmons hanging down from the front of a house to keep it still in the wind; a tacit understanding had formed between the whole party that it was simply not feasible.

Regardless, therefore, the voices initially calling out soon began to fizzle out, and they also did not break into any of the houses around them; for the time being, until something about the rows of houses changed, until they caught sight of some kind of storehouse that looked like it might contain treasure, they just silently advanced through the drizzle.

All they could hear was their respective breathing smothered in the rain, and while the wet, wooden walls and boardwalks could be said to have their own charm, it was melancholy; it was less like walking along streets of houses and more as if they were sinking into an endless deep, bringing about an even more stifling sense of claustrophobic entrapment than stepping out on the upper deck of the Albatross; the air was humid, yet it left the hearts of all present gritty.

Perhaps she could endure it no longer, for one of the twins stopped in her tracks, stared fixedly at a post supporting the eaves of a building, glared at it; it even made those around her concerned she might sink her teeth into it out of frustration, but,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんだか……妙だよ、この島の廃屋は。
　木材一つ取ってみてもさ。
　古さがみんな……同じみたいだ」
source.english:
“Something's… strange about these empty houses.
Even the timber.
It all looks… the same age.”

source.japanese:
航海士はただ荒れ狂うばかりでなく、見るべきところは見る、観察眼を示して見せたのである。確かに彼女の言う通り、これら廃屋群は、どこかしら奇妙であった。
　完全に無人なら、こういう木造家屋はさっさと傷む。なのにどれもこれも、ある程度以上は古びておらず、完全に倒壊した家屋というのが見当たらない。こういう廃屋というのは進行の度合いに程度はあっても劣化は進み、櫛の歯を折るようにあちらで崩れ、こちらで倒れしているものなのに───
　まるで完全に同時期に一気に建造されたか、さもなくばある時を境に古びる事を止めてしまったかの、いずれにしても考えづらい事である。
source.english:
The mate did more than rampage. She knew where to look, and demonstrated a keen eye. As she said, something about these deserted houses was odd.
Entirely uninhabited, wooden buildings deteriorated quickly. Yet none had aged beyond a certain point. Not a single completely collapsed house was to be seen. Ruins decayed at different rates, certainly, but one ought to fall here, another there, like teeth broken from a comb.
As though everything had been built at once, in precisely the same period. Or else had stopped aging at a certain moment. Neither was easy to imagine.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Something is……odd about all the abandoned houses on this island. Look, take just the timber here. It all looks……equally old.」

The first mate was not simply going berserk, she had seen what ought to be seen, making a clear demonstration of her keen powers of observation. Certainly, it was as she said, something about this heap of deserted houses was strange.

Were they completely deserted, then wooden buildings like these would quickly rot. Nevertheless, none of them had aged past a certain extent, and they could not find a single house that had completely collapsed. While the degree to which it had progressed could vary from place to place, the deterioration would continue to advance in abandoned houses like these, and like the bent teeth of a comb, they should be crumbling here, collapsing there, and yet─── Had they all been erected in one go at practically the exact same time, or if not that, after a certain turning point, had they all ceased ageing? In either case, the idea was difficult to entertain.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そうね。まるである時を境に、古びることをやめてしまったとでも言うみたい」
source.english: “Yes. As though they ceased to age at a certain moment.”

source.japanese:
キサラの指摘にそっと板壁を指で撫でた、密航者の、露細かに帯びた黒髪の艶[つや]の中には、廃址の往時の姿が幻像と投影されそうな、深く物想わしげな風情を孕んで、彼女の端麗な美貌と合わさり戦慄しかねないほどの調和を見せて。
　さすがのシサムも嘆賞の吐息漏らした、りなどするものか。むきつけに放りつけたのである。咎め文句を。軟弱な男ならば一発でころりと参りかねない密航者の秀貌だろうと黒髪の艶[つや]だろうと、常習的に船に侵入されている彼女達にとっては油虫のてかりと大差なく、
source.english:
At Kisara's observation, the stowaway gently stroked the board wall with a finger. Her black hair glistened with fine beads of dew. Its sheen held a deep air of reverie, as though a phantom image of the ruins in their former days might be projected there; together with her exquisite beauty, it made a harmony that could make one shudder.
Even Sisam let out an admiring sigh—or like hell she did. She flung a rebuke straight at her. That fine face and glossy black hair might knock a weak man flat. To women whose ship she habitually invaded, they differed little from a cockroach's sheen.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「That's right. One could even say it seems that, after a certain turning point, they all ceased ageing.」

There the stowaway stood, softly running a finger across the wooden wall Kisara had pointed out earlier, and within her lustrous black hair, finely coated in dew, it was as though the shape these ruins had held in antiquity was being projected as an illusory vision, so deeply contemplative an air was it pregnant with, creating so breathtaking a harmony with her stunning beauty that it was hard not to shudder at the sight.

Even Shisamu let out of a long sigh of admiration; did you really think so? She did let something out at her presence. Words of rebuke. The stowaway's sublime visage and glossy black hair would easily bring a weak man to his knees from a single glance, but to them, whose ship had been habitually infiltrated by this recidivist, it was hardly different from the glistening of a plant louse.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんか格好つけた口ぶりだが、いや、なんであんたがついてきているのかな？」
source.english: “That's a grand way of putting it, but—why exactly are you with us?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「That's a pretty pretentious way to put it but, wait, why exactly is it that you're following us?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まあ、気にしないで。ほらこういうのは、旅は道連れ世は情け……」
source.english: “Oh, don't worry about it. You know how it goes: a journey needs companions, and life needs kindness…”

source.japanese:
白昼夢から醒めた令嬢の、儚げで可憐な笑み、と本人は取り繕[つくろ]ったつもりかも知れないが、シサムには目鼻口を適当に並べた福笑いより噴飯ものの、密航者の脇にひたりと寄り添い片腕をがっと掴む、片割れに顎で合図して反対側も同様に。
　大柄な野生の美女二人に挟まれた密航者は谷間の白百合、剣呑な空気を察して身悶えしても双子の握力鉄の爪、右に見ればキサラはあえかな笑み、ただし唇をちろりと嘗めて肉に飢えたよう、左と見やればシサムは眉根を下げて優しく切なげな、ただしこめかみが幽かにひくついて、感情の所在地を物語る。
source.english:
Perhaps the stowaway meant to compose the fragile, charming smile of a young lady waking from a daydream. To Sisam it was more ridiculous than a round of Fukuwarai with the features strewn at random. She pressed close to the stowaway, seized one arm, then jerked her chin at her twin, who did the same on the other side.
Between the two tall, feral beauties, the stowaway was a white lily in a gorge. She sensed danger and writhed, but the twins' grips were iron claws. On her right, Kisara wore a delicate smile—while the little lick she gave her lips spoke of hunger for flesh. On her left, Sisam's lowered brows made her look gentle and wistful—while the faint twitch at her temple disclosed where her feelings truly resided.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Now, let's not worry about that. Look, this is like that saying: "In traveling, a companion; in life, compassion"……」

The beautifully ephemeral smile of a young lady of good breeding waking from her daydream, perhaps that's what the woman herself intended it to be, but in Shisamu's eyes, it looked more ridiculous than a fukuwarai whose facial features had been haphazardly slapped together, and so she snuggled right against the stowaway's side as she tightly grasped one of her arms, signaling her other half with a jerk of the chin to restrain the opposite arm in the same manner. (TN: Fukuwarai, written "福笑い", is a game played during New Year celebrations in Japan where you decorate faces with paper cutouts of facial features while blindfolded.)

Trapped between two wild beauties of Amazonian stature, the stowaway was The Lily in the Valley, and sensing the danger in the air, she tried to writhe and struggle, but the grip strength of the twins was like iron claws; when she turned right, Kisara had a faint, feminine smile on her face, but she was licking her lips like she was starving for meat; when she turned left, Shisamu had lowered her eyebrows, expression tender and wistful, but her temples twitched slightly, a testament to exactly where her true feelings lay.

source.japanese:
密航者は思った。
　───裸に剥かれるなら、せめて釦は引きちぎらないで欲しい、だってこれ一張羅だし。
source.english:
The stowaway thought.
───If I’m going to be stripped naked, I wish they’d at least leave the buttons intact—after all, this is my only outfit.

target.text: The stowaway thought. ───If I am to be stripped naked, at the very least, I'd prefer that you please do not tear off the buttons, for this is my only good set of clothes.

source.japanese:
密航者は念じた。
　───亀甲に縛られるのはもう仕方ない、なかば慣れてしまったけれど、せめてそこら辺に転がすだけにして。高いところから吊されると縄目が二週間は消えず、鏡で見る度笑えてくるの、涙混じりに。
source.english:
The stowaway prayed.
—Being tied in turtle-shell bonds is inevitable now, and I’m half used to them, but at least just leave me lying around somewhere. When they hang me high, the rope marks won’t fade for two weeks, and every time I catch my reflection I burst into laughter—tears running.

source.japanese: 密航者は恐れた。
source.english: The stowaway was terrified.

target.text: The stowaway offered a silent prayer. ───I've already resigned myself to being tied in a tortoiseshell pattern, I'm even half used to it by now, but could you at least just leave me on the floor somewhere over there? When I'm hung from a high place the rope marks are still there two weeks later, and every time I look in the mirror, I can't help but laugh, with tears streaming down my face.
The stowaway dreaded.

source.japanese: ───それとも今度こそ強姦されるのかしら。誰が相手なのかしらあの朔屋とかいうのなら女好きだろうけどまず普通のセックスで済むだろうでも龍[ロン]の爺なら見た目からして脂ぎって精力過多だから七日七晩挿入したままの連続性交お腹が蛙みたいに膨れあがるまで流しこまれて最後は衰弱心不全それともロックフォール機関長あの人が紳士に見えるのはきっとインポテンツだからでその代わりにありとあらゆる張り型拷問器具を駆使するタイプに違いなく最後には『洋梨』で膣を内から裂かれて股ぐらから大量出血失血死あるいはこの双子達だって有り得るこの女達は全頭マスクを被って空気チューブくわえて私の膣に頭蓋を貫入させてくるくらいの事さえやりかねない骨盤を砕いてからだって白人て基本的に相手の人体を破壊するような行為にも躊躇いがないしああそれとももしかしてこれらの事を全部やられてしまうのかも───
source.english:
—Or are they finally going to rape me this time? Who will it be? If it's that Sakuya fellow, he's a womanizer, but at least it would probably end with ordinary sex. But Old Long looks greasy and oversexed enough to stay inside me for seven days and seven nights, pumping me full until my belly swells like a frog's and I die of exhaustion or heart failure.
Or Chief Engineer Roquefort. He only looks like a gentleman because he's impotent; to make up for it, he must be the kind who uses every dildo and torture instrument imaginable, until at last he tears my vagina open from within with the Pear and I hemorrhage between the legs and bleed to death.
Or it could be the twins themselves. Those women might put on full-head masks, bite down on breathing tubes, and ram their skulls into my vagina—even after smashing my pelvis. White people never hesitate over an act merely because it destroys the other person's body.
Oh. Or perhaps they're going to do all of it to me—

target.text: ───Or maybe this is the time I'll finally be raped? Who would be the one to fuck me if it's that Sakuya guy or whatever his name is he's a bit of a womanizer but it'd probably just end with some regular sex but that old man Long based on his looks alone he'd be real greasy and overly energetic so he'd have continuous intercourse with me for seven whole days and nights where he'd remain inside me the whole time and pump me full until my stomach is bloated like a frog's and then I'd croak after my heart fails from the exhaustion or maybe that Roquefort guy he looks like a gentleman and that's definitely because he's impotent and so instead he'd be the type to make full use of every conceivable type of dildo

and torture implement no mistaking it and then at the end he'd use the 『Pear of Anguish』to rip my vagina apart from within and rivers of blood would flow from my crotch and I'd die of hemorrhaging or maybe those twins it's possible they'd fully cover their heads with masks and hold an air tube in their mouths and then pierce my vagina with their craniums it wouldn't be hard to imagine they'd go that far and crush my pelvis because white people generally show no hesitation even when doing something that would destroy the body of another or maybe they'll end up doing all of these things to me or───

source.japanese: 鼻の奥がじんと疼いて、流すまい弱味を気取らせまいと眉間に力を入れて抑えたつもりでも、涙は哀しく滲んで目尻に溜まる、その煌めきは一時の儚きものである分だけ、ザウエルの輝きにも勝っていた、が、ぐい黒髪後ろから引かれて、弾みで零れて脆くも散った。
source.english: A dull ache gathered behind her nose. She knitted her brow, meaning to hold the tears back and betray no weakness, but they welled sadly all the same and pooled at the corners of her eyes. Their glimmer, precisely because it was so fleeting, outshone even Zauer. Then someone jerked her black hair from behind. The tears spilled at the jolt and their fragile brilliance scattered.

target.text: The depths of her nose throbbed with a numbing pain, but though she tried to hold them in, furrowing her brow to not let her weakness show, tears welled up miserably and pooled in the corners of her eyes, and their momentary shimmer, all the more precious for their fleeting nature, surpassed the brilliance of even the Sauer, however, her black hair was pulled from behind, and the jolt made them spill, the fragile sparkle easily scattering.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「このメス餓鬼なあ、ぶつぶつ言ってんの、
　所々聞こえてんだぜおい。
　判った、もう情けなんてかけるか」
source.english:
“This little bitch is muttering to herself,
and I can hear bits of it,
you know. Fine, no more mercy.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Oi, you cheeky little bitch, I could hear bits and pieces of all that muttering. Fine, I'm through being merciful.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あ。痛い痛い。やめておくれ、髪引っ張らないで、しっぽ掴まないで……」
source.english: “Ah. It hurts, it hurts. Please stop—don’t pull my hair, don’t grab my tail…”

source.japanese: 黒髪手荒に指に絡ませ無惨にぐいぐい後ろに引いて、逸らされた喉はまさに斬首の白刃待つ形、ついでに密航者の腰の鞄から垂れる革帯びもぎちぎち引っぱって、両脇からシサム・キサラが抑えていなかったら彼女は牛蒡抜きに辻へと投げ出されていたろう。といって別にシサム・キサラの情けでない。
source.english: He wound her black hair brutally around his fingers and hauled backward. Her throat arched bare as though awaiting the executioner's white blade. For good measure he seized the leather strap hanging from her waist bag and pulled that taut as well. Had Sisam and Kisara not pinned her between them, she would have been uprooted and flung into the street like a burdock. Not that the twins were restraining her out of mercy.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Ah. It hurts it hurts. Please stop, don't pull on my hair, don't grab it by the tail end……」

Her black hair was roughly tangled in his fingers and mercilessly pulled back, her bared throat the very image of one awaiting decapitation by the headsman's naked blade; while this was happening, the leather strap dangling from the bag around the stowaway's hips was also being tugged on with a creak, and if Shisamu and Kisara had not been holding her in place from both sides, she would probably have been yanked away like he was uprooting a burdock and flung towards the intersection. With that said, this was no mercy on the parts of Shisamu and Kisara.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そうか、離せというなら離してやろう」
source.english: “I see. If you want me to let go, I’ll let go.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Alright. If you tell me to let go, then I'll let go.」

source.japanese: たとえクロや朔屋相手でなくても、密航者とあれば容赦しない信天翁号一同、ぎりぎりまで後ろに引いてから水夫長、ぱっと髪と革帯から手を離したから密航者の体は反動で前に泳いだ、完全に体幹が崩れたところを、両脇の航海士が勢いつけて前に放りつけたものだからひとたまりもあるまいてや。
source.english: Kuro or Sakuya might occasionally receive mercy; a stowaway never did. The boatswain hauled her as far back as she would go, then abruptly released both hair and strap. The recoil sent her flailing forward. At the instant her balance failed completely, the twin mates on either side put their weight behind her and hurled her ahead. She never stood a chance.

target.text: Even if they weren't dealing with Sakuya or Kuro here, the crew of the Albatross would still show no mercy to anyone found to be a stowaway; after pulling her back as far as he could, the Bosun suddenly let go of her hair and the leather strap, the stowaway's body lunged forwards from the jolt of the release, and just as her balance completely gave way, the first mates on both sides threw her forwards with great force, and so she could surely not offer even a ghost of resistance.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「え……あ、わ、わわわっ、止ま……っ」
source.english: “Eh… Ah, w-w-w-wait, stop…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Eh……ah, wa-, wawawah, sto……」

With the momentum of a marble flung by a sling, no, shot out by a mechanical launcher, it ought to be more accurately restated, the stowaway flew through the air like a cannonball, and while the long trail of flowing black hair left in her wake was beautiful, the woman in question was not in a position to be pleased at having her admirable qualities praised, and she was set to ram right into the windowpane of an abandoned house; moments before impact, like an action star on the silver screen, she curled up her body and crossed both arms to shield her head, a reflex deserving of lavish praise, but──

source.japanese: スリングで放たれたビー玉もかくや、いや射出装置で打ち出された、と言い直すべき勢いで密航者、緒と曳いた黒髪の流れは麗しかったけれど本人としてはそんな美質を云々されても嬉しいどころではなく、砲弾のように宙を飛んで突っこんでいった先が廃屋の窓硝子、衝突の寸前で銀幕の活劇俳優よろしく体を丸め両腕を交差させ頭部を庇[かば]ったのは激賞ものの反射神経といえたが───まず、彼女の形なりに窓硝子は丸く穿[うが]たれた。次の瞬間派手な破砕音を伴って硝子全体が飛散した。後は屋内を人体転がる響きとがしゃりと何かにめりこむ衝撃音と。
source.english:
The stowaway flew like a marble loosed from a sling—no, at such speed one must say fired from a launcher. Her black hair streamed behind her in a beautiful train, though she was in no position to appreciate the distinction. Cannonball-like, she hurtled toward the window of a derelict house. An instant before impact she curled herself up like the hero of a screen adventure and crossed both arms over her head: reflexes worthy of the highest praise.
First, a round hole in the stowaway's shape appeared in the pane. A heartbeat later the whole sheet of glass burst apart with a magnificent crash. Then came the sounds of a human body rolling through the room, followed by a splintering crunch as she embedded herself in something.

target.text: First, the window was pierced, leaving behind a round hole the shape of the girl. The next instant, a loud sound of something being smashed was accompanied by the entire glass pane scattering in all directions. After that came the sound of a human body rolling around inside the building and the sound of something crashing into something else, lodging itself deep inside.

source.japanese: シサム・キサラは高く掲げたそれぞれの掌打ち合わせ、水夫長は厳めしく腕組みし、お互いの息の合った連携に悪い微笑みを交わしあってから、扉を蹴破って屋内に踏みこむ、と───
source.english: Sisam and Kisara slapped their palms together high in the air, the boatswain sternly folded his arms, and after exchanging wicked smiles at their smooth timing, they kicked in the door and charged in—

target.text: Shisamu and Kisara raised their hands high and struck their palms together, the Bosun crossed his arms sternly, and after exchanging a wicked smirk at their perfectly coordinated teamwork, they kicked down the door and stepped inside the house, and there───

source.japanese:
屋内は、三方に区切られた窓からの外光で仄明るく、うち一つがいまし乱暴に破壊されていなければ水槽の中に漂うかの静寂に充たされていたろう。埃も静かに堆積するばかりであったろう。
　けれども今となっては信天翁号一行の闖入に乱されて、埃は粒子と舞い窓からの雨粒と混じりあった。
source.english:
Inside, daylight filtering through windows in three walls left the room dimly luminous; had one of those panes not just been violently destroyed, it would have been steeped in a stillness like drifting inside an aquarium. Dust, too, would merely have gone on settling in silence.
But now the Albatross party’s intrusion had disturbed it: dust rose in motes and mingled with the raindrops coming through the window.

source.japanese: 室内はがらんと空虚で調度といったものが乏しく、ただ密航者が着弾した先で堆く積み上げられた生白いのがあるばかり、仄明かりの中でもそれは殊更に浮き上がり、痛みに顔をしかめる彼女よりも、後から踏みこんだ面々の方がその輪郭を先に見分ける、見分けて皆微かに眉間に皺寄せる。
source.english: The room was cavernously bare, almost without furnishings. Its only feature was a high mound of sickly white material where the stowaway had landed. Even in the half-light it stood out with peculiar clarity. Those entering behind her made out its contours before the stowaway herself could, occupied as she was with grimacing in pain. Recognition drew a faint furrow between every pair of brows.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「痛いなあもう……。
　死者には平和を、生者には優しく。
　こんな墓穴みたいな島だもの、
　もっと静かに───」
source.english:
“Ouch, that really hurts…
Peace to the dead, kindness to the living.
It’s an island like a grave, after all,
so be a little quieter—”

target.text: The interior was dimly lit by the natural light filtering in from windows on three sides; had one of them not just been violently shattered, the room would have been filled with a stillness as though one was drifting within an aquarium. The dust, too, would have been content to simply quietly continue to accumulate. But now, the dust had been disrupted by the forcible entry of the group from the Albatross, and it whirled about as little particles, mixing together with the raindrops coming through the window.

The interior was spacious and empty, sparse in things that could be called furniture, and all there was to speak of was something pale stacked in a towering pile where the stowaway had landed; even in the faint light, it stood out especially clearly, and those who had entered after her discerned the general contour of what they were looking at before the girl grimacing in pain could, and it made all who did recognize it slightly furrow their brows.
【Stowaway】 「Come on, that really hurt……. Peace to the dead, kindness to the living. This island is already like a grave, so if you could be a bit more quiet when───」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ねえ君もそう思うよね、
　目がまん丸で、鼻筋とがって、
　歯を剥きだしている君。
　あら素敵にすべすべね。硬くて───？」
source.english:
“Hey, you think so too,
don’t you—you with those round eyes,
that pointed ridge of a nose,
and those bared teeth. Oh, how wonderfully smooth. And hard—?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Hey, you think so too, right, you with your eyes wide open, nasal bridge so pointed, teeth so bared. My, how wonderfully smooth you are. And hard───?」

source.japanese:
着弾の衝撃で頭に被さったそれ、ちょうど珍奇なヘルメットのよう、密航者はそれをかぱりと脱いで、虚ろな二つ孔を覗きこんで、痛みを分け合った者同士特有の親しげな微笑を注いでは、硬質の表面をさらさらと白魚の指先で刷く、薄明かりの中に浮かぶ可憐な娘とそれは、お互いの特質を更に高め合い、凄まじいまでの対比を見せた。
　
　それ───黄色味を帯びた白の。

(For the record, when the stowaway finally fainted, they simply left her there. No binding, no punishment, no stripping her naked and fitting antelope bones over her entire body. To abandon her and nothing more was surely a measure overflowing with mercy.)

source.japanese: その想像力に富んだ悪戯は、時には船内を和ませて、道化師代わりに可愛がられる事もあったが、それも程度を弁えていればの話。
source.english: His imaginative pranks sometimes cheered the ship, earning him an affectionate place as its resident clown. But that depended on his knowing when to stop.

target.text: Tears mixing with the raindrops on his cheeks, a gently sobbing deck boy took off his sailor cap like he was removing the cupule of an acorn, and as he timidly ran a hand across the top of his head, something resonated deeply within him, and like sap weeping from carved bark, he added yet another layer of tears.

Amongst his fellow deck boys, he was, to put it mildly, full of playfulness, and seen in a less charitable light, he went much too far with his jokes; amongst his kin, who, though they had their differences, were mostly very earnest people, he was a singular character, and the one who had pressed those skulls against the stowaway's chest while she sat confused in a mountain of antelope bones, only driving her all the more crazy in the process, was also none other than he.

(Incidentally, when the stowaway finally lost consciousness, they had simply abandoned her there. Given they did not tie her up, punish her, strip her naked, or dress her entire body up in an outfit of antelope bones, but had simply left her behind, their treatment of her could actually well be described as brimming with warm-hearted kindliness.)

This imaginative mischief of his would occasionally lighten the mood on board, and he was also doted upon as the ship's resident jester; however, this was with the assumption that he kept it within the realm of the reasonable.

source.japanese: 島内各所から拾い集めた各種の骨、頭蓋骨や脊髄、尺骨や骨盤など巧妙に組み合わせて一つのオブジェと為した手先の器用、それも賞賛するべきなのかも知れない。
source.english: There might even have been something to admire in the dexterity with which he had assembled the bones collected about the island—skulls, spines, ulnae, pelvises—into a single ingenious object.

source.japanese: しかし───そのオブジェというのが、暗黒大陸の邪宗の本尊はだしの、大きな杖というかトーテムポールかという代物で、尖端には雄羊の頭蓋骨を主格に霊長類の頭蓋骨を両面に配し、雄牛の脊髄を柱に狐の脊髄を二重螺旋に巻きつけて、後は各部にじゃらじゃら各種動物の指の骨やら牙やらをぶら下げて出来上がったるも禍々しき。
source.english: Except that the object in question was an enormous staff, or perhaps a totem pole, that would have put the idols of the Dark Continent's sinister cults to shame. A ram's skull crowned it, with a primate skull on either side. Fox spines wound in a double helix around the central spine of a bull, while finger bones and fangs from assorted animals dangled and clattered all over it. A thoroughly baleful creation.

source.japanese: いかなる天恵が、いや悪魔の恩寵が降[くだ]ったのか、その組み合わせの妙は急拵えのオブジェであるにも関わらず、遙かな歳月を閲[けみ]した人類以前の種族の邪神像の、人知を超えた邪悪さと奸智と恐怖を宿して、気の弱い御婦人ならば目にしただけで気絶しそう、いやいっそ、新大陸の奥地で土着信仰と悪魔崇拝が混淆された邪教の本尊として祭り上げられ森の奥で石柱高くに据えられて、夜な夜な影と邪妖が一つに混じりあう乱舞と血の供儀と乱舞を捧げられるに相応しい、それくらいのマガモノと化していた。
source.english: What heavenly gift—or rather, what diabolical grace—had inspired such an arrangement? For all its hasty construction, the thing possessed the inhuman evil, cunning and terror of an idol worshipped through immemorial ages by a race older than mankind. A timid lady might faint at the mere sight of it. Indeed, it deserved to be enshrined high upon a stone pillar deep in the New World's forests, the central idol of a cult blending native belief with devil worship, attended night after night by blood sacrifices and wild dances in which shadows and malignant spirits became one. That was the measure of the abomination he had made.

source.japanese:
こんなのが、島内の廃屋の各所を探検する下級水夫の前にぬうと現れ出でたと思ってみたまえ。人跡絶えた廃屋であったとしても、見知らぬ暗がりに忍びこむには下級水夫君達、肝がやや細い。
　おっかなびっくりで潜[くぐ]った戸口の脇の影溜まりが、予想だにせぬ深淵で、異界まで通じているなどと考えだけでも竦[すく]む少年達の、そんな彼らの鼻先に、影からぬうと突き出されたる地獄よりの骨の使者！
source.english:
Now imagine such a thing looming before a junior sailor exploring one of the island's abandoned houses. Deserted they might be, but the young sailors were not especially brave about creeping into unfamiliar darkness.
They shivered at the mere thought that the pool of shadow beside a doorway they had timidly entered might conceal an unimaginable abyss, opening into another world. And out of that shadow, right beneath their noses, thrust this bony emissary from hell!

source.japanese: 悲鳴をあげて泣き出すくらいではまだ強気な方で、棒のように硬直して失神したもの多数、その際あちこちぶつけて打ち身をこしらえた者が四人、恐怖の針が振りきれて、ケタケタ馬鹿笑いしながらジルバのダンスで通りに飛び出していった者一名、狂気の乱舞は遭遇した者の精神を病ませるという妖怪ひょうすべの跛行にも似て、そんなのが暗い雨に濡れる木造建築群の廂間をひょこひょこ手足上下させ腰を打ち振る情景を目撃したなら、記憶に癒しがたい傷が刻まれよう。
source.english: Those who merely screamed and burst into tears were the stouthearted ones. Many went rigid and fainted; four acquired bruises by striking various objects on the way down. One, with terror's needle driven clean off the dial, burst into idiotic cackles and jitterbugged out into the street. His insane dance resembled the limping capers of the hyōsube, whose wild gyrations were said to unhinge anyone who saw them. The sight of such a creature bobbing its limbs and shaking its hips through the narrow gaps between wooden buildings, all drenched in dark rain, would surely leave an incurable scar upon the memory.

source.japanese:
こういう規範破りの不埒者は、往々にして天罰といった概念も笑い飛ばしがちにするものだが、そんな形而上的な罰ならずとも信天翁号には地獄の羅卒より凶猛な龍がいる。
　看過せらるる悪巫山戯の域を越えているのは明白だったその下級水夫、水夫長のお叱りの拳骨を脳天に喰らう事になった───
source.english:
Such impious breakers of rules often laugh at the very notion of divine punishment. But no metaphysical chastisement was needed aboard the Albatross: it had Long, fiercer than any jailer of hell.
The sailor's prank had plainly exceeded all permissible bounds. A reprimand descended upon the crown of his head in the form of the boatswain's fist.

source.japanese:
まあこの下級水夫君の呪物製作は間違いなく暴走ではあるとはいえ、彼にそんな天啓与えてしまうくらい、廃屋の街の至るところ、廃屋内には動物類の骨が散乱していたのである。
　大小様々、種別は無数、中には水夫長でさえ見分けられない、否、識別に躊躇う代物さえ混じって、それ既に太古に絶滅したる生き物達の骨格としか考えられなかったから。
source.english:
The junior sailor's excursion into fetish-making had certainly got out of hand. Yet the very fact that he had received such inspiration testified to the bones scattered throughout the abandoned town, in every house.
Large and small, of innumerable species, they included things even the boatswain could not identify—or, rather, hesitated to identify, since they could only belong to creatures extinct since remote antiquity.

target.text: He was adroit enough to combine all the various kinds of bones they'd gathered from all over the island─── the skulls and the spines, the ulnae and the pelves, and so on───into a single object, so perhaps those dextrous fingers of his also deserved commendation.
