However───the object in question was a giant staff, or perhaps it should be called a totem pole, which put the principal object of worship of a heretical sect based in the Dark Continent to shame; with the skull of a ram adorning the tip as the main subject, flanked by the skulls of primates on either side, the spine of a bull serving as the pillar, the spines of foxes coiling around it in a double helix, and finally, various finger bones and fangs and such from all manner of different species of animal clicking as they swung around, suspended from various parts, even in its completion, this creation was baleful.

What manner of divine grace, or rather, demonic boon had been bestowed upon him? Such was the exquisite quality of its assembly that, despite being a hastily fashioned object, it harboured within it the superhuman malevolence, insidious cunning, and terror of the idol of a wicked god worshipped by antehuman species through long aeons; a lady faint of heart would like as not swoon at the mere sight of it.

Nay, if anything, deep in the remotest reaches of the New World, it would be enshrined as the principal object of worship of a sinister, heretical religion born from a syncretism of native beliefs and diabolism, set high upon a stone column, a fitting vessel for the offerings made night after night; a chaotic swirl of shadows and evil spectres coalescing into one, rites of blood sacrifice, and mad, frenzied revelry; so malignant an object had it become.

Please try to envision an object like this suddenly appearing before a deck boy exploring the various abandoned buildings of this island. While they might have been houses with no signs of human habitation, sneaking into unfamiliar darkness still left the deck boys with little nerve to spare. The shadows pooling by the doorway they gingerly stepped through was an abyss impossible to predict, it could even lead to another world, so the boys thought, some of them freezing in terror from that mere thought alone, and then, suddenly, emerging from the shadows, right in front of their noses, was an envoy of bone hailing from Hell!

Screaming and crying was a privilege reserved for those possessed of fortitude; there were plenty who went stiff like a rod, and in so doing, four people suffered bruising after bumping against things here and there.

The needle of terror was swinging wildly; one person burst out into the street, cackling like a lunatic while dancing the jitterbug, his maddened dancing similar to the halting steps of the yokai Hyousube, said to afflict the minds of all who encounter him, and were you to witness such a sight, of unsteady limbs flailing up and down, of hips swinging wildly in so dark an alley between a cluster of wooden buildings wet with rain, an immedicable wound would be etched into your memory. (TN: Hyousube, written "ひょうすべ", are bald, hairy fellows with a silly gait who like eggplants and are said to spread disease to people who witness them, fevers in particular.)

These sorts of norm-violating scoundrels oft have a habit of laughing off the concept of genuine divine punishment, but even without any such metaphysical retribution, the Albatross had a dragon more ferocious than the gaolers of Hell. This deck boy, whose mischief had clearly long since exceeded the line of what could be turned a blind eye to, came to suffer the scolding fist of the Bosun on the crown of his head───

Now, though the deck boy's creation of this fetish was undoubtedly reckless behavior, there were simply so many animal bones scattered throughout the abandoned buildings of this town that he was blessed with such divine inspiration. Varying in size, innumerable in kind, some among them could not even be recognized by the Bosun, nay, there were even bones that he hesitated to identify, for in his mind, they could only be the skeletons of creatures that had become extinct in prehistoric times.

source.japanese: ……拾い上げた趾骨は、水夫長の咬力ならばドアの握りほどもあるそれを、犬歯に当てて卵を割るように噛み砕く事はできたろうが、ただ噛み割るのではなく正体を判別するのは博物学に些[いささ]かの造詣ある彼にとっても困難時で、手にとったまま、卵の中の孵[かえ]る前の雛の雌雄の判定を命じられた農夫のように考えあぐねる。
source.english: The toe bone he had picked up was as big as a doorknob. With his powerful jaws, Long could probably have set it against a canine tooth and cracked it like an egg. Identifying it, rather than simply breaking it, proved difficult even for a man with some knowledge of natural history. He stood pondering it in his hand, like a farmer commanded to determine the sex of a chick still inside its egg.

source.japanese: 尋常の牛でもなければ馬でもない、趾骨のサイズからして全体は体高三米[メートル]に及ぼうかという巨獣としか考えられず、陸上をそんな巨大な生き物が闊歩していた時代は太古の帷[とばり]の向こうへとうに過ぎ去った。化石化しているのならまだしもの、骨はまだ人肌めいた感触を残してあり───
source.english: No ordinary cow or horse. Judging by the size of the toe bone, it could only have belonged to a colossal beast some three meters tall. The age when such giants strode the earth had long since vanished behind the curtain of antiquity. Had it been fossilized, that would have been one thing. But the bone still had something of the feel of human skin…

target.text: ……With his biting force, the Bosun could have crushed the phalanx held in his hand, a bone roughly the size of a door knob, like an egg were he to put it between his canines and bite down; however, even for him, a man possessed of some scholarly knowledge of natural history, cracking the case of its true nature was proving far more difficult than simply doing so with his teeth, and so it remained in his hand while he racked his brains in vain like a farmer who'd been told to determine the sex of a chick before it hatched from its egg.

This belonged to no ordinary cattle, nor any horse, and from the sheer size of this phalanx, he could only imagine it to be a giant beast reaching at least three metres in height when measured at the withers, but the days when such gigantic creatures brazenly swaggered around on land had long since retreated beneath the veil of antiquity. Had it been fossilized, it would be one thing; instead, the bone still retained a warmth reminiscent of living skin───

source.japanese:
このように水夫長が困惑している一方、探索の部隊を二つに割いたもう一方、航海士の双子率いる方は、板切れを前に悪戦苦闘していた。
　いい加減に歩き疲れた、休憩がてらの昼食に、温かい汁か珈琲でも添えようとて、薪代わりに乱暴に廃屋の床板を剥がしたのはいいのだが。
source.english:
While the boatswain puzzled over this, the other half of the divided search party, led by the twin navigators, was fighting a losing battle with a piece of wood.
Tired of walking, they had stopped for lunch and thought to accompany it with hot soup or coffee. Ripping up the floorboards of an abandoned house for firewood had been easy enough.

source.japanese:
こちらはこちらで娑婆塞ぎの因業爺の如き
難物の、たかが木っ端一つが。
　廃屋の造りは目立って堅牢、とまでは至らぬが、外の雨気を遮[さえぎ]るくらいには普請の狂いなく、内は埃を舞わせ積もらせるくらいには乾いた。
　双子が剥がした床板なども、信天翁号のバラックの材に比べてよっぽど素性が良く、湿気に蚕食された様子も木喰い虫が彫った跡もない。
source.english:
But a mere scrap of wood proved as intractable as some vicious old man who refused to die and make room for the living.
The abandoned houses were not conspicuously sturdy,
but their construction remained true enough to keep out the rain; inside, it was dry enough for dust to gather and drift.
The floorboards the twins had pried up were far better timber than the stuff used in the Albatross's shacks. Neither damp nor woodworm had eaten into them.

source.japanese:
むしろ一攫千金を狙うより、この廃址の廃屋を適当に解体し掠奪して船体の修繕に充てるなり古材として売っ払うなりしたほうが、地味に船の財となるのではないか、などと、堅実に殖財企てられるようなら、そもそもザウエル探索などはしていない信天翁一行、剥ぎ取った床板を薪にしようとしたが。これがいっこうに点火できない。
　細木に割いても、ナイフで表面削って毛羽ただせても、行糧包んでいた古い英字新聞を焚き付けにしても、広告のドラッグストアの髭親父や清涼飲料水の瓶がぶすぶす火刑に焦げて灰になっていくばかりで、いっかな火の移る気配がない。材木と偽った陶器の店頭見本だと言わんばかりに。
source.english:
Rather than chase a fortune, perhaps they might profit quietly by dismantling a few houses, looting the timber and using it to repair the hull or selling it secondhand. But if the Albatross party had been capable of such sensible schemes for increasing their wealth, they would never have gone hunting Zauer in the first place. They tried to burn the floorboards. Nothing would make them catch.
Splitting them into thin sticks, raising a fuzz on the surface with a knife, using the old English-language newspaper that had wrapped their provisions as kindling—nothing worked. The bearded man in the drugstore advertisement and the soft-drink bottle merely smoldered at the stake and fell to ash. Not a spark would pass to the wood. It might have been a ceramic showroom sample masquerading as timber.

source.japanese:
シサム・キサラなどは途中で飽きてどっかと胡座かき、棒きれに細く割ったので床を叩いて拍子とり、まーだ？　まーだ？　と下級水夫達に飯の準備を急かしつける我侭の大姐御、どちらがメアリ・リードでアン・ボニーやら、だ。
　結局火は最後まで点けられなくって、昼食は船から持ち出しの、薄めたワインと冷菜でこしらえるしかなくて、冷菜と生パンの火の気も暖もない、外の雨垂れも寒々しく浸[し]みてくるよう。
source.english:
Sisam and Kisara soon lost interest. They plumped themselves down cross-legged and beat time on the floor with slivers of wood, demanding, ‘Ready yet? Ready yet?’ of the junior sailors preparing lunch. A pair of imperious pirate queens—which one was Mary Read and which Anne Bonny was anybody's guess.
In the end, no fire could be coaxed from the wood. Lunch had to consist of the cold provisions and watered wine brought from the ship. Cold food and plain bread, without a flame or a trace of warmth; even the rain outside seemed to soak its chill into them.

source.japanese: 脇に膾斬りにされた死体が積まれようと、大嵐のただ中であろうと船首像のように昂然と物に動ぜず、大酒を食らうような双子ではあるが、小糠雨と骨の山では活劇の昂ぶりもなく辛気くさいばかりで、気分が沈んでいくを免れない。
source.english: The twins could drink prodigiously beside a heap of chopped-up corpses or in the heart of a raging storm, proud and unshaken as a figurehead. But drizzle and piles of bones offered none of the exhilaration of an adventure. They were simply depressing. Even the twins could not keep their spirits from sinking.

source.japanese: ちらちらと屋内の片隅の、骨の山へ放る眼差しの色は鈍い、鈍いのだが、一方顔の下方では、というと。
source.english: Their glances toward the bones piled in a corner were dull. Dull, yes—but a little lower down their faces, things were rather different.

target.text: While the Bosun was baffled thus, the other half of the landing party, the group lead by the twin first mates, were locked in a fierce struggle, contending with some pieces of wood. They'd grown fed up with walking by now, figured that maybe having some warm soup or coffee during their lunch break could do wonders, and so they had the great idea of violently removing the floorboards from an abandoned house to serve as firewood, but.

Here, however, their hard nut to crack, which was as tough as a stubborn old geezer whose existence amounted to nothing but a waste of space in this earthly realm, was a measly scrap of wood. The structure of the abandoned building wasn't quite visibly sturdy, but its construction was functional enough to ward off the rain from outside, leaving the interior so dry that enough dust could accumulate to whirl around.

The floorboard that the twins had torn off was, compared to the timber of the shacks on the Albatross, in far better condition; there were no signs of encroaching spoilage from humidity, nor any tracks carved by wood-boring insects.

If anything, rather than aiming to strike it rich, would dismantling these ruins and scavenging what materials they could get their hands on, whether it be to patch up the hull with or selling it off as reclaimed timber, not bolster the coffers of their ship by a respectable amount; had they been able to apply themselves to any such stable moneymaking schemes, then this party from the Albatross would never have set forth on their quest for the Sauers to begin with; thus, they instead attempted to use the stripped floorboard as firewood. But it simply refused to ignite.

Though they broke it into splinters, though they used their knives to scrape off wood shavings, even as they tried using as kindling the old English newspapers that had served as the wrapping of their supplies, all it amounted to was the moustached man in the drugstore advert and the bottles of soft drink being executed by burning in smouldering flames, reduced to ashes with not a single sign of the fire spreading to the board. It seemed for all the world like a ceramic shopfront model masquerading as timber.

Shisamu and Kisara had already lost interest halfway through and sat down cross-legged with a heavy thump, snapping a scrap of wood into little pieces, tapping the floor rhythmically, hurrying on the deck boys preparing their lunch with drawn-out cries of "Are you dooone? Are you dooone?", a selfish set of mistresses; which one was Mary Read and which one was Anne Bonny?

In the end, the fire never took, and their lunch consisted only of thin wine and some cold vegetable appetizers they'd brought with them from the ship; as they sat there with neither warmth from their cold vegetables and untoasted bread nor any heat from a fire, it felt as if the chill of the raindrops falling outside was seeping into their bones.

Whether corpses cut to ribbons were piled at their side or they were caught in the midst of a great tempest, these twins stood unflinching and proud as a ship's figurehead, knocking back drink without batting an eye, but there was no dramatic excitement to be found in this drizzle and the mountains of bones; it was but dreary and tedious, and so it was inevitable that their spirits would sink.
As their gazes flickered around the room, sending glances towards the heap of bones, the look in their eyes was leaden; it was leaden indeed, but what of the lower half of their faces?

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「気持ち悪いね。……ここ、動物園かなんかだったのかな」
source.english: “Creepy, isn't it? …Think this place was a zoo or something?”

source.japanese: 染みなく皓い硬玉の歯並びが、薄切りの玉葱と肉と胡瓜の香漬けを噛み砕いて間断なく、
source.english: Kisara's spotless jade-white teeth worked without pause, crushing thin slices of onion, meat and pickled cucumber.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Creepy place, isn't it? ……Wonder if this place used to be a zoo or something.」
The spotless white jadeite of her rows of teeth crunched through thinly sliced onions, meat, and pickled cucumbers without interruption,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「こんな島で？　しかも誰もいないし」
source.english: “On an island like this? And there's nobody here.”

source.japanese: 片割れもザワークラウトとマッシュポテトを頬に詰めこむのに余念なく、呑み下す合間を縫っての受け答えだ。
source.english: Her other half was equally occupied stuffing her cheeks with sauerkraut and mashed potatoes, fitting her answers into the intervals between swallows.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「On an island like this? There's not even anybody here.」
Though her other half also had her cheeks stuffed, this one with sauerkraut and mashed potatoes, she still answered earnestly by making good use of the gaps between her swallowing.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「にしてもほんと、見事に骨ばっかり」
source.english: “Still, it really is nothing but bones.”

source.japanese: でごくんと、巣籠もり前の栗鼠もかくやに膨らませた頬一杯の膨らみ、奥に吸いこまれていくのが二人拍子を同じくして、喉の外まで響いた盛んな嚥下の音と喉の上下の動きがあからさまなあまり、性行為を露出させるような露悪趣味的で卑猥な様相まで呈した。
source.english: Gulp. Cheeks swollen like squirrels preparing to nest emptied into their throats in perfect time. Their swallowing rang out and their throats rose and fell, the whole display so blatant that it became positively obscene, as if they were exposing a sexual act.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Seriously though, there really is just nothing but bones.」

With a loud gulp, the two of them both swallowed the contents of their cheeks, which were puffed out like those of a squirrel readying itself for hibernation, in perfect unison; the sound of their swallowing, so vigorous it resounded beyond the walls of their throats, together with the explicit, rhythmical motion was so excessively blatant, it assumed an exhibitionistic quality, the deliberate, wanton vulgarity of flaunting a sexual act.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「これ、みんななんで、
　死んじゃったのかなあ……」
source.english:
“What do you think
killed them all…?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But, I do wonder, how did they all die……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「寿命……飢え死に……病気に、事故、後はなにかにやられて」
source.english: “Old age… starvation… sickness, accidents. Or something got them.”

source.japanese: そして下級水夫達は大わらわ、言問いと疑問は黒不浄にまつわる言葉なれども、彼らは横一列に並んで雀の学校、端からライ麦の粗パンを手渡しに流して順々に、コンビーフの、玉葱の、胡瓜の香漬けの、それぞれ薄切りを乗せて挟んでサンドイッチに仕上げる工程弛[たゆ]みなく、空き缶や瓶が後ろに積まれたのが首狩り族の獲ってきた首級めく、などと表しては薮蛇か。
source.english: The junior sailors, meanwhile, were busy indeed. Their questions concerned the pollution of death, yet they lined up in a neat row like a school of sparrows, passing coarse rye bread down the line. Thin slices of corned beef, onion and pickled cucumber were laid on in turn, then enclosed in bread: an uninterrupted sandwich assembly line. The empty cans and bottles piled behind them resembled a headhunter's trophies—though perhaps that comparison was asking for trouble.

source.japanese: 仲間の一人が並べ上げた、島内の骨達の死因がふと気にかかったように、下級水夫の一人が、
source.english: Something in his companion's list of possible causes of death among the island's bones caught one junior sailor's attention.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Old age……starvation……illness, accidents, or they might have been done in by something.」

And then there were the deck boys, working feverishly at their task; though their questions and doubts revolved around the dark impurities of death, they were all lined up in a row like the sparrow school, passing rustic rye bread from one end to the other, then corned beef, onion, and finally pickled cucumber, making sandwiches filled with thin slices of said ingredients without any slack, the empty bottles and cans piled up behind them like the decapitated heads taken by a headhunting tribe, but perhaps such similes only serve to stir up a hornet's nest? (TN: The sparrow school, written "雀の学校", is a Japanese nursery rhyme composed in the year 1922)
As though he had suddenly grown curious about the possible causes of death of all these bones on the island that one of his fellows had recited, one of the deck boys opened his mouth,

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「なにかって、なにさ」
source.english: “What kind of something?”

source.japanese: と余所事考えで、出来上がったサンドイッチをキサラに渡そうとしたものだから、手がらみ引かれて指まで囓られそうな勢い、仰天して引っこめれば大振りのサンドイッチが航海士の歯列の間でばっさり両断されて、よくうっかり者の指を落とす紙の裁断機はだしの切断力に水夫君はひっそり肝を冷やした。
source.english: Distracted by the question, he offered Kisara a finished sandwich. She dragged his hand toward her mouth and all but bit his fingers with it. He pulled back in alarm as the enormous sandwich was severed between the navigator's teeth. Such cutting power would shame one of those paper guillotines forever depriving the careless of fingers. The sailor felt a private chill of terror.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「What do you mean, "something"?」

With his mind busy elsewhere, as he made to hand over the finished sandwich to Kisara, she grabbed it, hand and all, then pulled with enough force that it seemed she was about to chew down on his fingers, too; astonished, just as he hastily retracted his hand, the sandwich was cleanly bisected between the first mate's rows of teeth, and upon witnessing a cutting force that could put a paper guillotine to shame, which so frequently lops off the fingers of the careless, the deck boy was chilled to the bone.

source.japanese:
流れ作業で次から次へと生産されていく端からサンドイッチは双子の口の中に消えゆき、余るという事がない。
　コンビーフもザワークラウトもピクルスも、皆この時代にありふれた保存食糧であり、味もおおよそは想像がつく。火が使えないのではそれらを切って刻んで合わせるくらいの、料理ともいえない料理ではあったが、そこは下級水夫の心映えか、或いはシサム・キサラの味への拘[こだわ]りが大雑把なだけか、見ているだけで胸焼けしそうなほど二人はがつがつと。溜め食いする狼のような健啖で航海士は、きっかり五回の咀嚼で靴底のようにでかいサンドイッチを平らげて、
source.english:
Sandwich after sandwich emerged from the assembly line and vanished into the twins' mouths. There was never a surplus.
Corned beef, sauerkraut and pickles were all common preserved foods of the period; their flavors need little imagining. With no fire, the sailors could do little more than slice, chop and combine them—hardly cooking at all. Whether it was the junior sailors' thoughtfulness or merely Sisam and Kisara's undiscriminating palates, the two ate with such ferocity that watching them was enough to give one heartburn. Voracious as wolves laying in provisions, the navigators disposed of sandwiches the size of shoe soles in precisely five chews.

target.text: The sandwiches that were produced one after another through their assembly-line system disappeared into the twins' mouths as soon as they were made, with no leftovers to spare. Corned beef, sauerkraut, and pickles were all commonplace preserved foodstuffs in this age, and you could roughly imagine how it would taste. They had no fire to use, and so all they could do was slice and chop, a form of cooking that could hardly be called as such; whether it was this deck boy's disposition or that Shisamu and Kisara just weren't very particular about taste, just looking at the way they greedily scoffed down the food was enough to give him heartburn.
The first mates were as voracious as wolves stuffing themselves with days worth of food in a single meal, and in exactly five chews, they devoured a sandwich the size of a shoe sole,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そりゃあまあ、ライオンだのトラだのヒョウだの、肉食の連中さ」
source.english: “Well, lions, tigers, leopards. Carnivores.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Well, it obviously has to be, you know, a lion or a tiger or a leopard, some kind of carnivore.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「つまり一等航海士みたいな？」
source.english: “You mean, like the first mates?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「In other words, something like one of the mates?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「……そんなのがもしうろついてたら、確かにおっかないなあ」
source.english: “…If anything like that was prowling around, it really would be scary.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「……If something like that was prowling around, that sure would be scary.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……言うよねえ、このコたちも」
source.english: “…Listen to these little brats.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……These kids don't mince words either, do they?」

source.japanese: 胡座のミニスカートの端から健やかに伸びる太腿を、はしたなくばたばた漕ぎながら苦笑するシサムから、その下級水夫はふて腐れたように顔を逸らす。指までサンドイッチの具にされ損なっては、温厚な下級水夫君とはいえ少しはむくれよう。やや皮肉めかしたけれども、今一度骨の山を眺めて彼は、外の雨気が忍びこんだかに肌に寒さを覚えた。
source.english: Sisam gave a wry smile. Sitting cross-legged, she flapped her legs indecorously, healthy thighs extending below the hem of her miniskirt. The sailor turned away in a sulk. Even the mildest junior sailor was entitled to some resentment after nearly having his fingers added to the sandwich filling. The remark had been edged with sarcasm; another look at the bones, however, sent a chill over his skin, as though the damp outside had crept indoors.

target.text: While she immodestly swung around her firm thighs emerging healthily from beneath the hem of her miniskirt in her cross-legged position, Shisamu gave a wry smile, causing the deck boy to turn away from her with a sulky expression. Mild-mannered though this deck boy was, even he must have grown a little upset that his fingers were almost turned into sandwich fillings. With a lingering air of irony, as he looked once more upon the mountain of bones, he felt a chill settle against his skin, as if the dampness of the rain outside had stolen in.

source.japanese:
これまで見てきた廃屋内の骨の山に共通する特徴は、皆同数の番[つが]いであった事。
　中には航海士の言った通りに牙や爪の傷痕残していたものもある。そういった骨達は損傷し、屋内で散乱していたし、家屋も窓が破られたり扉がこぼたれたりで、外部から何らかの肉食獣が侵入して抗[あらが]う術持たぬ獲物達を食い荒らしたのだろうと窺える。
source.english:
The bone-heaps in the houses they had explored all shared one feature: the animals were invariably present in matched pairs.
Some bore just such traces of fang and claw as the navigator had suggested. These bones lay damaged and strewn indoors, while windows had been broken and doors smashed in; one could readily suppose that some carnivore had forced its way inside and ravaged prey with no means of resistance.

target.text: The distinctive trait shared amongst all these piles of bones within the abandoned buildings he'd seen hitherto was that they all consisted of an even number of paired mates. Just as the first mate had said, some amongst them still bore scars from fang and claw. Those bones were damaged, scattered all over the interior, the furnishings and the windows also broken, the door likewise destroyed; some manner of carnivore must have raided the place and wolfed down all these defenseless prey animals, that much could be surmised.

source.japanese:
だかそういった、弱肉強食の摂理の下に骨を晒した者達は、まだ納得がいく。不気味だったのはそれ以外の骨の山だ。
　彼らは如何にして死を迎えた？
　疫病に斃[たお]れたにしても餓えと渇きに命尽きたのだとしても、屋内が綺麗に過ぎるのである。
source.english:
But those who had left their bones under the law of tooth and claw were at least explicable. It was the other piles that troubled them.
How had those animals met their deaths?
Whether disease had felled them or hunger and thirst had finished them, the houses were too clean.

source.japanese:
かつては動物たちを囲うていたと思しき柵の内側には、それぞれの秣[まぐさ]、飼料の桶などが据えられて、中には藁束や穀物の名残などが風化してあった。一方で禽獣達の飼育に付き物の糞便は跡形もない。
　折り重なっていた骨の山だって、理を詰めていけば動物たちがそのように一つところに固まって絶命するとは考えがたいのである。
source.english:
Inside the enclosures that seemed once to have held the animals stood mangers and feed tubs. Some retained the weathered remnants of bundles of straw or grain. Yet there was no trace of the dung that inevitably accompanied the keeping of birds and beasts.
Nor, when one thought it through, was it easy to imagine the animals dying all huddled together in the heaps their bones now formed.

source.japanese:
そもそも病や餓えに見舞われた生き物達が、何故屋外に逃げ出しもせず廃屋の中に留まり続けたのか。
　始めは島内の至る処これ木造という景色と、捜索する廃屋内のどれもこれも骨が残されているという状況の異様さに気を逸らされて、皆深くは穿[うが]って推量はしなかったものの、やがて状況が差し示す、惻々と迫る不気味さが潜[ひそ]んでいる。
source.english:
And why had creatures suffering from illness or starvation stayed in their houses instead of escaping outside?
At first, the strange spectacle of an island built entirely of wood, with bones in every house they searched, had distracted them from looking deeper. Gradually, though, a disquieting implication began to press upon them.

target.text: But such bones, the bleached remains of those who had perished under the natural order of the survival of the fittest, of the strong preying on the weak, those he could still come to terms with. What was truly uncanny were the piles of bones not like that. How had they met their end? Even supposing they had succumbed to some epidemic or perished from hunger and thirst, the interior was simply far too clean for that.

Inside the fences that once seemingly corralled these animals, mangers and feed troughs remained fixed in place, still containing the weathered remains of straw bundles and grain. On the other hand, there were no traces of the faeces that was an inevitable byproduct of rearing birds and beasts. Even these stacked heaps of bones were inconsistent; when he tried to logically fill in the gaps, it was difficult to entertain the idea that these animals had all huddled together in a single, concentrated space like this to breathe their last.

To begin with, if these creatures had suffered from illness or starvation, why would they choose to simply stay inside the building instead of even trying to escape outside? At first, they had been distracted by the bizarre nature of this island, the scenery of every inch covered in wooden construction, how there were bones in each and every building they explored, and so no one had made any conjectures delving too deeply into the heart of the matter, but eventually, the eeriness lurking beneath it all, what the circumstances pointed to, began to loom ever closer, felt keenly by all.

source.japanese: ───骨の山は、まるで何者かが獣群が死したる後に積み上げたようでないか。
source.english: Didn't the heaps of bones look as if someone had piled them up after the animals died?

source.japanese: ───これだけの生き物達に、如何様にして飼料を供給していたのか。
source.english: How had enough fodder been supplied for so many creatures?

source.japanese: ───またこれらの生き物達の排泄物は、糞便の処理はどのように行っていたのか。
source.english: How had their waste, all their dung, been disposed of?

source.japanese: ───そして生き物達は、なぜ大半が屋内に留まったまま従容と死を受け入れたのか。
source.english: And why had most of the creatures remained indoors, meekly accepting death?

target.text: ───Did it not almost seem as if someone had piled together these heaps of bones after the herds of beasts had perished?
───By what means had they managed to supply feed to this many animals?
───Moreover, by what means was the excrement, the faeces of these animals, disposed of?
───And finally, how come the majority of these animals remained within the building as they calmly accepted their death?

source.japanese: 数え始めれば切りがないが、最大の謎は。
source.english: Once one started counting, the questions were endless. But the greatest mystery was this:

source.japanese: ───そもそも───
source.english: What, in the first place…

source.japanese:
一体如何なる意図、目的があってこんな海図にも乗っていないような島に生き物達をかき集めたのだ？
　本来の環境を離れたモノ達まで。
source.english:
For what design, to what purpose, had all these creatures been gathered upon an island that seemed not even to appear on the charts?
Even creatures taken far from their native habitats.

target.text: Once they began, there was no end to the questions, but the greatest mystery of them all, that was:
───To begin with───

With what intent, what possible purpose, had someone gathered all these creatures on an island that doesn't even seem to exist on any nautical chart? Even those so distant from their original environments.

source.japanese: ……霧雨に煙[けぶ]る廃址は寂寞として、一種の静寂美が垂れこめてはいる。古びた木造の家屋の谷間を板敷きの通廊で廻れば、森閑とした気韻に包まれて、浄化された哀惜さえ催される。
source.english: The ruins, hazed with fine rain, lay desolate beneath a peculiar beauty of stillness. Walking the boarded passages between the old wooden houses, one was enveloped in profound quiet, moved even to a kind of sorrow washed clean.

source.japanese: しかし。
source.english: And yet.

source.japanese: 一つの島が、街が、滅びて、物音といえば雨垂れと廂[ひさし]や樋[とい]から落ちた雫が幾つかの流れとなって低きへと降っていく索莫とした響きばかりとなるには、相応の理由が必要なのだろう。もし廃屋の裡[うち]や通りの辻の影に佇む亡霊あったとしても、彼らは必ずしも滅亡を受け入れて死の憩いを許諾した、哀しくも穏やかな相を湛えているとは限るまい。
source.english: For an island, a town, to perish until its only sounds were the desolate patter of rain and the dripping from eaves and gutters, gathering into little streams that ran downward—surely there had to be a reason. If ghosts stood in the shadows within the houses or at the street corners, there was no assurance that their faces bore the sad serenity of those who had accepted destruction and consented to the repose of death.

source.japanese: 免れ得なかった滅びの無念に、面貌引き歪めているかも知れず、生者を仲間の列に引き入れんと怨念の形相張りつけている事だって有り得る。或いは島内のどこかに、散乱する骨に痕跡を刻んだ肉食獣が生き残り、潜んでいないと誰が保証できる？
source.english: Their features might be twisted with rage at the ruin they had been unable to escape, their faces fixed in hatred as they sought to draw the living into their company. Or who could guarantee that the carnivores whose marks scarred the scattered bones had not survived somewhere on the island, lurking still?

source.japanese:
片割れと共にある限りは生者だろうと死者だろうと臆するものでないシサム・キサラであったが、死の静寂の中でふっと後れ毛を生命無き温度の手で撫でられた心地して、思わず周囲を見回した事である。生き物なくとも大気は自ずと流動する、実際には廃屋内の人数で気流が生じただけなのだろう、怪しい影も見えず、キサラはサンドイッチの追加をねだってまたかぶりつこうとして、もう一度訝しげに屋内を見回した。
　動物達を養う為の柵、飼い葉桶の他には調度も乏しい室内、自分達の他に誰かが隠れていられる隙間も陰もなく、不審なものはない。
source.english:
So long as they had each other, Sisam and Kisara feared neither living nor dead. Yet in that deathly silence they felt something stroke the loose hair at their napes, like fingers emptied of life's warmth, and despite themselves looked around. Air moved of its own accord even where nothing lived; in truth, the people within the house had probably stirred a draft. No suspicious shadow appeared. Kisara asked for another sandwich and was about to bite into it when she looked around once more, puzzled.
Apart from the animal pens and feeding troughs, the room held little furniture. There was no space, no patch of shadow, in which another person might hide. Nothing suspicious.

source.japanese:
ないけれど、足りないものがある事に思い当たった。色合い。紺青の。淑やかで高貴な色が見えない。泪が纏[まと]うあの。
　無駄口を叩かずとも不思議な磁場めいた気配を放つ女である。その一方で、下らない会話を聞けば跫音を気取らせずに離れる事もする女である。人間の心理の間隙を読む術に長けているのであろうが、キサラには一体何時から泪の声が聞こえなくなっていたのか、即座には数えられなくなってあり。
source.english:
Nothing—and yet something was missing. A color. That deep blue. A dignified, noble shade. The one Rui wore.
Even without joining in the chatter, the woman gave off a presence like a strange magnetic field. But she was also capable of slipping away, unheard, when the conversation grew tedious. She was probably adept at reading the gaps in human attention. Kisara could not immediately reckon how long it had been since she last heard Rui's voice.

target.text: ……Hazy in the misty rain, the ruins rested in forlorn silence, draped in a singular beauty of stillness. Were one to roam around the boardwalk passages running between the aged wooden houses, one would be enveloped in dignified serenity, and it would even evoke a sense of purified grief.
However.

A whole island, a town, dead and ruined, the only sounds it produced that of the rain dripping down from the eaves and the gutters, forming several streams that run to lower ground; there was nothing but the sound of bleak desolation, and that surely demanded an adequate reason. Even assuming the souls of the dead stood in the shadows of the intersections or the interiors of the buildings, there was no guarantee that they would have accepted their downfall and been permitted the peaceful repose of death, nor that they possessed a sorrowful yet serene countenance.

Perhaps their features would be contorted with the bitter regret of their inescapable demise, and it was also entirely plausible they'd have a look of rancour etched into their faces as they tried to drag the living into their ranks. Or maybe, somewhere on this island, the carnivorous beast that had carved those scars into the scattered bones yet lived on; could anyone guarantee it was not lurking in the shadows?

And while Shisamu and Kisara were here, they who feared no creature, living or dead, as long as they were with their other half, amidst this silence of the grave, he suddenly felt as if a cold, lifeless hand stroked one of his straggling hairs, causing him to unconsciously survey his surroundings. Even without any living creatures, the air would flow on its own, in fact, it was probably just some airflow created by this many people being inside a room; he couldn't spot any suspicious shadows either, and when Kisara, having pestered the other deck boys for another sandwich, was just about to bite down on it, he cast another suspicious glance around the interior.

Aside from the fence and mangers used to rear animals, it was a room scarce of furnishings; there were no nooks or shadows for anyone not of their number to hide in, there was nothing suspicious at all.

There was nothing there, but he suddenly realized there was something missing instead. A hue. Of indigo. He couldn't see that graceful, noble colour anywhere. The one Rui was clad in. Though she never wasted her breath on pointless chatter, she was a woman possessed of a mysterious magnetism. By the same token, she was also the kind of woman who, if she heard a conversation she thought tedious, would take her leave without making a sound. While Rui may have excelled at reading the hidden cracks in the human psyche, Kisara could no longer immediately pinpoint exactly how long it had been since Rui's voice had last reached her ears.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんか、泪さんが───
　ついてきてないような……。
　誰か知らない？」
source.english:
“Rui doesn't seem to be… with us anymore.
Anyone know
where she went?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It kind of feels like Rui─── isn't with us anymore……. Does anyone know where she is?」

source.japanese:
問いかけに皆一様に顔を見交わした、仕草からして誰にも心当たりはない様子、一同に困惑の波紋広がって、板敷きの床がひどくささくれだったかに尻の据わりが悪くなる。信天翁号が乗客を乗せる事はないでもなかったのだけれど、ほとんどが密入国者か国外逃亡を図る手合いで、乗り組み達が扱ういかがわしげな荷と扱いを同じにするのが相応しい者達ばかり。中には船の荷に手をつける護摩の灰や、乗りこんだ後で船賃を値切りにかかる不心得者まであるくらいで。
　ところが泪はどうにもそれら怪しからん客とは勝手が異なる。姿、立ち居振る舞いからして、防波堤の吹き溜まりの波間に寄せられた、半腐れの海草の束やら錆の浮いた浮き缶の合間に透かし模様の絹織物が降りたようなもので、何より金払いが良い。
source.english:
Everyone exchanged looks. From their gestures, none had any idea. Bewilderment rippled through the company; sitting still grew uncomfortable, as though the floorboards had become horribly splintered. The Albatross did sometimes carry passengers, but most were illegal immigrants or people fleeing the country, fit to be handled like the dubious cargo her crew dealt in. Some even stole from the ship's stores or tried to bargain down their fares after coming aboard.
Rui was quite unlike these disreputable customers. Her appearance and bearing made her seem a piece of openwork silk fallen among the half-rotten seaweed and rusty cans washed into a breakwater's stagnant corners. Above all, she paid handsomely.

source.japanese: ただどちらかというと信天翁号には本来無縁の筈の賓客であり、彼女一流の気侭も手伝って、乗り組み達には些[いささ]か扱いづらい相手だった。が、だからといって捨ておいてもいられぬ。下級水夫の一人が戸口に駆け寄って通りの来し方過ぐる方を窺ってみても、張り出した庇の下に人影はなし、細かな雨粒が渦を巻いて帷[とばり]と視界を隠す。
source.english: She was, if anything, the sort of distinguished guest the Albatross would ordinarily never have carried. Her own particular brand of caprice made her somewhat difficult for the crew to handle. That did not mean they could simply abandon her. One junior sailor hurried to the doorway and looked up and down the street. No figure stood beneath the projecting eaves. Fine raindrops whirled into a curtain, hiding the view.

target.text: In response to the question, they all exchanged glances as one, and based on that gesture, it seemed nobody knew; all at once, ripples of bewilderment spread, and as though suddenly rough and splintered, the wooden floorboards grew uncomfortable to sit on. It was not exactly unprecedented for the Albatross to carry passengers, but they were mostly the sort scheming to illegally immigrate or flee the country, nothing but people who deserved the exact same treatment as the dubious cargo the crew otherwise handled. Among their numbers were even thieves posing as travellers trying to get their grubby hands on the ship's cargo, as well as injudicious fellows who would try to haggle down the fare after boarding.

Nevertheless, Rui was of an entirely different character than such disgraceful passengers. From her appearance and her mannerisms alone, it was as if an article of openwork silk had washed in with the waves to a breakwater where half-rotten lumps of seaweed and rusted cans had gathered, and more than anything, she paid really good money.

But if truth be told, she was the sort of privileged guest of honour who should have been utterly divorced from anything involving the Albatross in the first place; compounded by her characteristic caprice, the crew found her rather difficult to manage. But that did not mean they could simply abandon her here. Even as one of the deck boys rushed over to the doorway and carefully surveyed the street, both the way they had come as well as the way they were going, there was not a shadow of a woman to be seen beneath the overhanging eaves, and the fine raindrops swirled together, forming a veil and obscuring visibility.

source.japanese: 今にも一人で泪の行方を求めて駆け出しそうに、あわわと浮き足だった忠義の小姓は、以前に泪にねっとりと玩具にされた下級水夫であったが、彼にはその際の手さばきの甘やかさ、舌先から口移しに零された甘露が、麻薬のように忘れがたく染み着いてしまっているのらしい。
source.english: The loyal page, who looked ready to bolt off alone in search of Rui, was flustered and on edge. He was a low-ranking sailor who had once been thoroughly toyed with by Rui, and it seemed that the indulgent way she had handled him then—and the sweet syrup dripped from the tip of her tongue into his mouth—had become ingrained in him like a drug, impossible to forget.

target.text: This loyal page, looking as though he might dash out by himself in search of Rui's whereabouts any moment now, muttering restlessly and tapping his feet, was the deck boy who had previously been toyed with in a slow, lascivious manner by Rui, but it seemed the tenderness of her deft manipulations at that time, the syrup that dripped down from the tip of her tongue into his mouth, had indelibly stained his body like a narcotic, leaving an unforgettable impression on him.

source.japanese:
後先見失いかかった下級水夫を仲間があれこれ宥[なだ]め、捜索するにしても皆でと言い聞かせて、廃屋に満ちた時ならぬ騒動をよそにして、先ほど薪にせんと刻まれた板切れを拾い上げた手があった。
　枯れた手つきであり、いかにも当たり前に一行の中に混じっており、板切れにあれこれ尽くされた着火の努力の跡を検分する様子もごく自然だったから、始めは誰も咎めなかったのだけれど。
source.english:
His companions soothed the junior sailor, who was on the verge of losing all sense, explaining that if they were to search, they must go together. Amid the sudden commotion filling the abandoned house, a hand picked up one of the pieces of wood they had chopped for fuel.
It was a withered hand. Its owner mingled so naturally with the party, and examined the evidence of their efforts to light the wood so matter-of-factly, that at first nobody challenged him.

target.text: His fellow crewmen did all they could to calm this deck boy, who was moments from being entirely blind to the consequences, and they tried to persuade him that, if they were to go on a search, they should all go together; entirely indifferent to the sudden commotion filling the abandoned house, a hand reached down to pick up a piece of the wood that had been chopped for firewood just earlier. It was a withered hand, but it had blended in with the party as though its presence was nothing out of the ordinary, and the way it examined the traces of the various efforts they'd gone to in trying to ignite the scrap of wood also seemed quite natural, so at first, nobody challenged it, but.

source.japanese:
【？？？】
「こんな真似したって、
　火なんぞ点かんわな」
source.english:
“You won't get a fire
going like that.”

source.japanese:
【？？？】
「これらの材木には、
　分子レベルで耐火、耐腐食の処理が、
　施されておる」
source.english:
“This timber has been treated
at the molecular level to resist fire
and decay.”

source.japanese:
【？？？】
「燃焼させるつもりなら、
　高炉にでも放りこまんと」
source.english:
“If you want to burn it,
you'll have to throw it into a blast furnace or something.”

target.text: 【???】 「With the way you're going about it, you'll never get so much as a spark to take.」
【???】 「For this timber here, see, it's been treated at a molecular level, to make it fire- and corrosion-proof.」
【???】 「If you intend to burn this, you'll have to toss it into a blast furnace, or something like it.」

source.japanese: 呟かれた言葉の意味が針先ほども理解できず、訊ね直そうと振り返った一人を始めとして、皆がぎょくりと硬直する。
source.english: One sailor, unable to comprehend so much as a needlepoint of what the stranger muttered, turned to ask him to repeat it. He froze. The others froze with him.

target.text: Unable to make neither heads nor tails of the words muttered to them, starting from the first person who turned around to ask him to repeat himself, they all froze solid.

source.japanese: 一同の中に混じっていた、長衣姿の、フードを目深に下ろしていたから貌立ちまではしかとは判別できない、ただ声や長衣の裾[すそ]から覗く手には湯にふやけた和紙を無理矢理乾かしたような皺が一面の、老爺と思われた。
source.english: A robed figure stood among them, his hood pulled too low for them to make out his features. His voice, and his hands where they showed from under the robe, suggested an old man. Those hands were covered in wrinkles like Japanese paper soaked in hot water and forcibly dried.

target.text: Standing there amongst the group was a figure clad in a long robe, with a hood pulled so deep over his eyes that one couldn't even clearly discern his facial features; still, both his voice and the hand peeking out from the sleeve of his robe, like washi soaked in hot water and then aggressively dried, were completely covered in wrinkles, so he appeared to be an old man. (TN: Washi, written "和紙", is traditional Japanese paper, usually made from paper mulberry fibers. It is still used today for sliding doors, hanging scrolls, traditional painting, calligraphy, among many other things. )

source.japanese:
いつの間にか。どこから。
　
　
　誰もが等し並に同じ驚きで言葉を失う。
　
　
　一座にまぎれこんでいたのは老人。
　
　
　何時の間に。一体どこから───
source.english:
When? From where?

The same astonishment struck them all speechless.

An old man had joined their company.

When? Where on earth had he come from?

target.text: Before anyone realized it. From out of nowhere. Everyone, without exception, was struck speechless by the exact same astonishment. An old man had slipped into their company. Since when had he been there? And from where in the───

source.japanese:
板敷きを、踏んだ沓[くつ]は踵[かかと]が高く、年季の入った放蕩者ならシャンパンを注いで風変わりなグラスにしようというほど、爪先からかけての曲線が艶[なま]めかしい。靴底は滑らかで硬く、女の足を飾るための宝飾にはなっても、蹠を保護し、歩行の実用に供するにはどうにも頼りない。が、女は足を滑らせる不様は晒さず、踝まで埋まるような絨毯を踏むのと同じ足取りで、右にとふらり、ゆらりと左へ、それこそ足の向くまま気の向くままに。
　泪は信天翁号の面々から離れて一人、島内の廃屋の合間を往く。
source.english:
The shoes treading the boards were high-heeled, their curves from the toes onward so enticing that an experienced debauchee might have filled them with champagne and used them as unconventional glasses. Their soles were smooth and hard: jewels to adorn a woman's feet, perhaps, but decidedly unreliable as protection for those feet or practical aids to walking. Yet the woman never suffered the indignity of slipping. She walked as if upon a carpet deep enough to swallow her ankles, drifting right, swaying left,
wherever her feet and fancy took her. Rui had left the Albatross party and was wandering alone among the island's abandoned houses.

source.japanese:
別段島内を探索して回る一行の騒々しさが
生え初めの双葉のように柔らかな神経に障[さわ]って癇癖発したわけではない。かといって傷つきやすい貴重品の様に扱われる事に厭気が差したわけでもない。泪を動かすのは癇性、厭気といった内部から衝[つ]き上げてくる衝動ではなく、ただ倦怠の。
　泪にとって耐えがたいのは、彼女を取り巻く空気それ自体が変質し、世界に横溢し、肌を包みこんでくるかの倦怠感。それはまるで四肢の関節や首筋、乳房や腰に見えない蜘蛛の糸を懸けられたかのよう。
source.english:
It was not that the explorers' uproar had irritated nerves as tender as newly sprouted leaves and provoked a fit of temper.
Nor had she tired of being treated like a fragile and precious object. Rui was not moved by impulses welling up within her—irritation, disgust—but simply by ennui.
What she could not bear was a weariness that seemed to alter the very air around her, overflow the world and envelop her skin. As though invisible spider threads had been fastened to the joints of her limbs, her nape, her breasts, her waist.

source.japanese: 懸糸から逃れられない糸繰り人形の定めなのか、それとも懸糸を断ち切って自儘に生きようとする意志なのか、いずれにしても泪は絡みつく倦怠感の糸によって探索の一行から歩度を緩めて遠ざかったのだが、緩急の呼吸がごくさり気なかったために誰も彼女には気づかなかった。
source.english: Was it the fate of a marionette unable to escape its strings, or the will to sever them and live as she pleased? Either way, those clinging threads of ennui had drawn Rui away from the explorers as she slowed her pace. The change of rhythm was so imperceptible that nobody noticed.

source.japanese:
ただそうやって離れたところで───
　
　板敷きの通路に張り出した庇[ひさし]の下の暗がりに廃屋の裡[うち]を確かめれば、窓硝子に映し出された容貌の、唇を蓮っ葉に尖らせた、見やすく御不満げな。
　すいと流れて硝子の面から消えると、窓の奥にはやはり骨の堆積、硝子越しで角も和らげられて、匙で突いて崩したプディング菓子と見えなくもない。が、実際に舌に甘い菓子なら泪の不興を幾らかは慰めようものを、そこは骨は骨。まして彼女が覗きこんできた廃屋は、種類に差はあっても同じようにごろごろごろ、二度・三度覗いただけで飽きてくる。
source.english:
But even once she had slipped away…
In the darkness beneath an eave projecting over the boarded passage, she examined a house's interior. Her face reflected in the window wore a brazen pout, plainly displeased. As it slid away from the glass, another heap of bones appeared beyond. The glass softened their edges until they might almost have been a pudding broken up with a spoon. An actual sweet upon her tongue might have soothed Rui's displeasure somewhat. Bones were bones. And every house she peered into held the same jumbled heaps, whatever the differences in species. Two or three looks were enough to bore her.

target.text: The heel of the shoe clacking on the floorboards was tall, the curve running from the toes so captivating that a seasoned libertine might well pour champagne into it and use it as an eccentric drinking glass. The sole was smooth and hard, and though it served its purpose as an ornament accentuating a woman, as well as supported her heel, it simply seemed an impractical companion for a walk. But the woman did not disgrace herself by slipping; with a gait as though she was stepping into a carpet that swallowed her feet to the ankles, she slowly swayed to the right, then swung relaxedly to the left, simply going wherever her feet took her and her heart led her.
Rui, having drifted away from the crew of the Albatross, was wandering through the abandoned ruins on this island all by herself.

It wasn't because the noise of the group roaming around and exploring the island had gotten on her nerves, tender as newly sprouted leaves, in particular, and caused her to lose her temper. Having said that, it was also not because she had grown fed up with being treated like some fragile, precious commodity. What had urged Rui into motion was not her temper or frustration, no such impulses welling up from within; it was simply ennui. What Rui found unbearable was the languor; as if the very air surrounding her had transformed, saturating the world and enveloping her skin. It was as though an invisible spider's thread was woven around the joints of her limbs, around her neck, chest, and hips.

Was she fated to be a marionette unable to escape its strings, or did she have the will to sever the ties that bound her and live on through her own selfish desires? Regardless, Rui's pace had been slowed by the threads of ennui clinging to her, drifting apart from the exploration party, but the rhythm of her shifting pace was so subtle that none had noticed her disappearance.

But after having parted ways thus─── Standing in the darkness beneath one of the eaves protruding over the passage covered in floorboards, as she checked the interior of a building, the lips of the countenance reflected in the glass were stuck out in a cheeky, petulant pout, its dissatisfaction plain for any to see.

After it smoothly slid off the glass surface and vanished, as expected, there was a pile of bones beyond the windowpane, and with the corners softened through the glass, it could even be mistaken for a pudding that had been prodded at with a spoon and collapsed. But had it actually been a sweet-tasting treat, then it might have soothed some of Rui's displeasure; the bones were but bones. To say nothing of how, while there was some variety in species, there were similar bones everywhere, and after peeking inside the room but two or three times, she grew bored.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どちらを向いても、みぃんな、骨、骨。
　からんと渇いていて、かつんと硬くて、
　そして───退屈で」
source.english:
“Whichever way I look, it's bones, bones, bones.
Dry and hollow, hard and clattering,
and… dull.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「No matter where I turn, it is nothing but bones, bones, and more bones. Bone dry, stiff, hard, and worst of all───boring.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「見るのなら、生きている動物のほうが、
　まだ面白そうなのに」
source.english:
“Living animals would at least be more
interesting to look at.”

source.japanese: 廃屋に堆[うずたか]い骨の山は、最初こそ森閑とした荒廃の中にあってグランギニョル劇場の見世物めいたが、打ち続けば新鮮味も薄れる、グロテスクを売りにした化け物舞台の、押し出しは扇情的であっても他に芸がなければ凡百の演[だ]し物の中に埋もれていくのと同じ倣[なら]いだ。
source.english: At first, the bones heaped in the houses had lent the silent desolation something of a Grand Guignol spectacle. Repeated often enough, they lost their novelty. A monster show trading on the grotesque might make a sensational entrance, but without another trick it would sink among the countless ordinary acts.

source.japanese: 今さらこうやって何度も重ねて見せつけられずとも、つまるところ温血の生き物は全て肉と皮を除けば同じ構造を有している事など、泪ならずとも自明の理[ことわり]である。
source.english: One hardly needed to be Rui to know that all warm-blooded creatures possessed much the same structure once stripped of flesh and skin. There was no need to demonstrate it over and over now.

target.text: 【Rui】 「If I must look at animals, then I believe seeing them alive would have made a more interesting sight.」

These heaps of bone, piled up in the abandoned houses and set in the quiet desolation, initially gave an impression reminiscent of the spectacles of the Theatre du Grand-Guignol, but as the sight repeated itself, the novelty wore off in turn, like a performance of ghastly ghouls selling itself on its grotesqueness; even if it gave a sensational impression to the audience, if it held no other artistic merit, then it was doomed to be buried in obscurity amidst all the other performances imitating the very same concept.

Even without being shown it thus again and again, ultimately, the fact that all warm-blooded creatures, once stripped of flesh and skin, share the same underlying structure was a truth so self-evident that anyone could have realized as much on their own.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そして、止まない雨。
　雨は窓の内から眺める分には、
　それなりに風情ではあるけれど」
source.english:
“And the rain never stops.
Rain has a certain charm when one is indoors,
watching it through a window…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「And then, this ceaseless rain. Rain does have a certain charm of its own, as long as you're looking at it from inside a window, but.」

source.japanese:
軽く舞う雨粒を怨[えん]じたところで仕方ないけれど、ボンネットの裡より曇天見あげる、目庇の形は、雨に飛翔を邪魔されて不満の白鳥のくちばしの風にも見える。
　
　───と。
　廃址の街並みの、小箱を乱雑に重ねたように積層して高さも統一されず段々の中、分けて小高い建物上に塔屋が見えるのだが、その窓、その周りに。
source.english:
There was little point in resenting the lightly dancing drops. As she looked up at the overcast sky from within her bonnet, its brim resembled the beak of a swan vexed at having its flight hindered by rain.
Then—
Among the ruined town's irregular tiers, stacked like carelessly piled little boxes, she noticed a rooftop chamber crowning a particularly tall building. Its window, and the space around it…

source.japanese:
窓には白い影と、窓の周りに黒い何かが飛び回っている、と泪に見えたのはほんの一刹那の事で、気を惹かれて、目を凝らすとやはり雨、小糠雨、霧雨、細雨、そればかり。
　気のせいかとしばし佇んで、気のせいでもいいと思い直して歩み始める泪、その塔屋へ。
　退屈にも退屈を重ねる彼女にとっては、些細な幻でも足を運ぶ契機になるのであった。
source.english:
For an instant, Rui thought she saw a white shape in the window and something black flitting about it. Her interest caught, she peered harder. Nothing but rain: fine drizzle, misting rain, a thin rain.
She stood a moment, wondering if she had imagined it, then decided she didn't care if she had and set off toward the rooftop chamber.
With boredom piled on boredom, even a trivial illusion was reason enough for her to go.

target.text: It was a waste of effort to begrudge the lightly whirling raindrops, but she still looked up at the cloudy sky from inside her bonnet, the shape of its brim looking like the bill of a dissatisfied swan frustrated that its flight was being hindered by the rain. ───Just then. Amidst the tiered townscape of the ruins, like small boxes had been piled up messily at uneven heights, atop one building that was slightly taller than all the rest, there was something that looked like a tower, but its window, and the vicinity.

Within the window was a white shadow, and some manner of dark shape fluttering around the frame, or so it looked like to Rui, only for a fleeting instant; it fascinated her, but as she strained her eyes to get a better look, in the end, all she saw was rain, drizzle, mist, sprinkle, and nothing more. For a time, she just stood there, wondering if she had been imagining things, but then reconsidered; even if it was but her mind playing tricks, that would be fine too, Rui thought, and she set forth once more, towards that rooftop tower. For this woman, drowning in layers of boredom upon boredom, even the most trivial of illusions would be reason enough to head there.

source.japanese:
足の生えた鰻用か、と怪しいくらい細く長く暗い木の段を三度ほど折り返して上がった建物の屋上、そこもまた板張りの広場で、細雨に侘びしく濡れている、その向こうに小屋掛けされた塔屋が一つ。なにかに引かれるように歩み寄る泪だっだが、彼女がその小さな小屋から、建物の屋上に設けられる塔屋というより、古い時代の船に設けられた船尾楼のように想ったのは何故だったろう。
　洋上の長雨に延々降り籠められて、陽差しの色も忘れて倦み疲れた船楼。そんな風に感じた自分に首を傾げつ歩み寄ったところ、塔屋の扉が生憎だ、鍵が掛かっている。
source.english:
Three turns of a wooden stairway so narrow, long and dark that one might suspect it had been made for eels with legs brought her to the roof. Here, too, was a boarded open space, forlornly wet with fine rain, and beyond it a little rooftop hut. Rui approached as if something drew her. Why did the little structure suggest not a rooftop chamber, but the sterncastle of a ship from an earlier age?
A sterncastle confined for ages beneath the endless rains at sea, weary beyond remembering the color of sunlight. Puzzled at her own impression, she drew closer. Unfortunately, the door was locked.

target.text: So narrow and long were the dark wooden steps of the stairs leading up to the roof of the building she ascended, doubling back on themselves no less than three times, that she half suspected it was made with an eel that had sprouted legs in mind; at the top, she was greeted by yet another open space covered in floorboards, drearily wet in the misty rain, and on the opposite side stood a single, jury-rigged tower. Rui walked towards it as if being pulled by something, yet she wondered: what was it about that tiny structure that made her think of an aftercastle on an old sailing ship rather than a tower built atop a roof?

An aftercastle grown weary of the monotony of being trapped endlessly in a long spell of rain at sea, so long it had even forgotten the colour of sunlight. She tilted her head in puzzlement at herself for feeling thus and approached the tower, but unfortunately, the door to the tower was locked.

source.japanese: ただ扉には硝子窓が嵌めこまれ、屋内の様子が見てとれる。好奇心は抱いても、鍵を破るのは面倒、と覗きこんで泪は、白い影の正体を知る。
source.english: A pane of glass set into the door allowed a view inside. Curious though she was, breaking a lock would be tiresome. Rui peered through and discovered what the white shape was.

source.japanese:
───人の白骨だった。
　簡素な麻の長衣まとい、小さな椅子に腰かけ、外へと向かう窓へ手を差しのばして。
source.english:
A human skeleton.
Clad in a simple linen robe, seated on a little chair, reaching a hand toward the window that looked outside.

source.japanese: ───泪が先ほど仰望した街角からは、けして見えないくらいに当屋内の奥まった影で。
source.english: Deep in the chamber's shadows, where it could never have been visible from the street corner at which Rui had stood looking up.

source.japanese: 虚ろな眼窩で、なにを求めているのか、何に手を差し延べているのか、死して肉の重みから解放されてなお、渇望が、生々しく切実に骨格内に残留している。
source.english: What did it seek with those empty sockets? What was that hand reaching for? Dead, freed even of the weight of flesh, it retained a yearning within its bones so urgent that it seemed alive.

target.text: However, a glass window was fitted into the door, allowing the state of its interior to be grasped. Though her curiosity was piqued, breaking the lock would be bothersome; with those thoughts in her head, Rui peered inside, and she came to know the true nature of that white shadow.
───It was the bleached bones of a human. Clad in a simple linen robe, sitting on a small chair, reaching a hand out toward the window looking outside.
───In the shadows deep within the room, so far inside that it would have been impossible for Rui to have seen it from that street corner she had looked up from just earlier.
With those empty eye sockets, what did it seek, what did it reach out for; even in death, released from the burdens of the flesh, with vivid sincerity, a craving yet lingered in its skeletal frame.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「動物ばかりではなく、人間もちゃあんと揃えました───と、でもこちらも骨でいらっしゃる」
source.english: “Not just animals, then. Humans have been duly included… But you, too, are all bones.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It is not just animals, they also made sure to include a human to complete the set───though, this, too, is naught but bones.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「根本の思想からして、
　わたくしの好みとはあわないご様子」
source.english:
“It seems the underlying
philosophy is quite at odds with my tastes.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It does appear that their fundamental philosophy does not quite align with my personal tastes.」

source.japanese: いかに渇望の形、身に浸むほどであろうと、泪は自分の好みから外れた事にはかかずらわない。他にと扉の窓越しに目を凝らしたところで、塔屋内には調度の少なく、書き物机が一脚とそれから───床に点々散っているのはあれは、鳩の羽根だろうか、そして一枚だけ黒いのは、烏の風切り羽根。鳩と烏と、塔屋内の住人は、ここで鳥たちを養い、空に想いを放っていたのだろうか。差し延べられた手は鳥を迎える為か、放つ為か。
source.english: However deeply that shape of longing might pierce her, Rui did not concern herself with anything outside her tastes. She searched instead through the glass for something else. The chamber held little furniture: one writing desk, and then… were those dove feathers scattered over the floor? A single black feather among them was a crow's flight feather. Doves and crows. Had the inhabitant kept birds here, sending thoughts aloft with them? Was the outstretched hand meant to receive a bird, or to release one?

source.japanese:
ボンネットの目庇の先で軽く硝子をつつく泪こそ、鳥が訪れて嘴で叩くような、と覗きこむうちに、机の上に一葉の紙が乗せられているのに気がついた。
　多少黄ばんではいるものの、室内に剥き出しに放置されてきた割りには状態が良い。表にのたくった紋様と見えるのは、地図の線とも見えたし、そうでもないようにも───
source.english:
Rui herself, lightly tapping the glass with her bonnet's brim, resembled a visiting bird pecking at the window. As she peered inside, she noticed a single sheet of paper on the desk.
Somewhat yellowed, it was nevertheless well preserved for something left exposed in the room. The wandering patterns upon it might have been the lines of a map—or perhaps not…

target.text: No matter the form the craving took, even if it was intense enough to seep into her very being, Rui refused to get involved in matters that didn't suit her tastes. When she strained her eyes to take a closer look through the glass in the door, she saw the interior was sparse with furnishing, there was just a single writing desk, and beyond that───scattered across the floor was what must have been dove feathers, as well as a single black flight pinion. Doves and crows: perhaps the resident of this tower had raised birds here and released their longings into the sky? Was the hand stretched out to welcome the birds in, or was it to release them?

While Rui continued to lightly tap at the glass with the edge of her bonnet's brim, exactly like a visiting bird announcing its arrival by pecking with its beak, as she peered inside, she noticed a sheet of paper on top of the desk. Although slightly yellowed, considering it had been left exposed in this room, it was still in relatively good condition. The patterns scrawled on the surface looked like the lines of a map, or perhaps not───

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───あれは、海図？」
source.english: “…A nautical chart?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「───Is that a chart?」

source.japanese:
泪がもっとよく近く覗きこもうと、ボンネットを外そうとした刹那───轟、と風が唸った。
　建物を揺るがさんばかりの強風で、ケープの端やボンネットを紐から引きちぎらんばかりに吹き荒れて、泪の身体が押し遣られてしまいそうなくらい、凄まじい。
　建物もぎしぎし軋んで今にも倒壊しそう、泪にとっては建物が倒壊しようが塔屋が吹き飛ばされようが別に関わりのない事だが、巻きこまれて潰されるのは面白くない。死ぬにも最後の息が埃というのは冴えない事と、泪は屋上を渡って建物の中に戻る、狭苦しい階段をヒールの踵[かかと]で上手に踏んでたんたんたん、駆けたりはしないけれど、足早に降りて木造の通りへ退散だ、が、出て、振り返ってみると───
source.english:
Rui was about to remove her bonnet for a better, closer look when the wind roared.
A violent gust threatened to shake the building, to rip away the edges of her cape and tear her bonnet from its strings. It was strong enough almost to sweep her bodily away. The building creaked as though about to collapse.
Rui had no particular objection to the building collapsing or its rooftop chamber blowing away, but being caught beneath them and crushed would be no pleasure. Even in dying, a final breath of dust seemed a dreary prospect. She crossed the roof and went inside, deftly placing her heels upon the cramped stairs: tap, tap, tap. She did not run, but descended briskly and retreated into the wooden street. Then she stepped out and looked back…

target.text: As soon as Rui made to take off her bonnet so she could get a better, closer look, that very instant─── the wind howled, roared. A powerful gale, strong enough to shake the very building itself, swept over her, so tremendous it threatened to tear off her cape and rip the bonnet from its strings, and Rui's body was almost shoved away.

The building also creaked and jarred as if about to collapse; not that it particularly mattered to Rui if it did, or if the tower was taken by the winds, but it would not be very amusing to be crushed in the process. Believing it to be rather dull for her final breath to be a mouthful of dust, Rui crossed the rooftop and returned back inside the building, deftly descending the cramped steps with clicking heels; she was not exactly running, but she did retreat to the wooden passages with a quick gait, however, after exiting, when she turned back───

source.japanese:
あれほどひどい風だったのが、今は微風も残さずぴたりと止んで、建物からは埃が零れた様子もない。
　こうなるとそもそも吹き荒れた事からして怪しくなってくる。どうにも理に落ちない奇妙な現象も、泪には少しばかり気慰みにはなったようで、仄かな笑みで服の乱れを直して、来た道を引き返す足取りは、先よりは幾分浮かれ加減だった。
source.english:
That dreadful wind had stopped utterly. Not the faintest breeze remained; not even dust seemed to have fallen from the building.
Now it was questionable whether it had ever blown at all. The inexplicable phenomenon appeared to have given Rui a little diversion. With a faint smile, she straightened her clothes and retraced her steps, rather more buoyantly than before.

target.text: The wind had been so terribly fierce just moments ago, but now, not even the gentlest of breezes remained; the wind had entirely ceased to blow, and there was no sign of dust spilling out from the building either. At this point, that there had even been so violent a gale at all was beginning to seem suspicious. It seemed as though this illogical, bizarre phenomenon had served as at least a small diversion for Rui, for with a faint smile on her lips, she put her clothing in order, and while she walked back the way she came, her step seemed to carry more of a lighthearted bounce than earlier.

source.japanese: ……泪にとってはほんの一歩二歩足を伸ばしてみた程度の心算で、帰り道も、似たような家並みが続く通りを迷いもしない上手の散歩者、間を置かずに他の面子と再合流を果たしたのだが。
source.english: To Rui, it had been no more than a step or two out of her way. An accomplished stroller, she returned without getting lost among the streets of similar houses, and soon rejoined the others.

target.text: ……In Rui's mind, she had only planned to stretch her legs a little, and as a proficient stroller, the sort who would not get lost while retracing their steps through streets lined with endless rows of similar houses, she managed to reunite with the rest without delay, but.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……何事もなかったようにお戻りだね、あんたも」
source.english: “…Back as if nothing happened, are you?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……So you also just reappear as if nothing happened, huh?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ええ、なにも、ございませんでしたもの」
source.english: “Yes. Nothing did happen.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Why yes I do, for you see, nothing happened.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……こんなところだろうと思ったよ。
　つい心配なんぞしちまったけど、
　なぁんかこっちが馬鹿みたい」
source.english:
“…Thought it'd be something like
that. We actually went and worried about you.
Now I feel like an idiot.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……I figured it would be something like that. I couldn't help but get a little worried, but now I kinda feel stupid for even bothering.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「まあまあ。
　無事で戻ってきて、なによりなんだからさ」
source.english:
“Come
on. The important thing is she's back safe.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Now, now. She's back safe and sound, and that's all that matters」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……お二人とも、
　なにかございましたの？」
source.english:
“…Has something
happened to you two?”

source.japanese:
塔屋で鳥の羽や人骨を眺めたくらいでは、特に告げるまでもないと泪は思うた、けれど海図の方はあるいは重要な情報源ともなろうに、泪にとって興味の埒外にある事で、これも告げずに過ごした。後は心躍らせる珍事も事故もない、つまらないと、彼女には退屈であっても、不意に消えられては一行にとっては有り難くない、面白くない。
　ただ、一行の気色は、ただ泪の勝手を咎めるせいだけでなく、もう一つ別の、戸惑すの色合いが入り混じっていて、下級水夫が微妙に歯切れ悪く説明する。
source.english:
Rui considered the bird feathers and human bones in the rooftop chamber scarcely worth mentioning. The chart might conceivably prove an important source of information; but that, too, fell outside the bounds of her interest, and she let it pass unmentioned. After that, there had been no strange occurrence or accident to set the heart dancing. How dull. Yet if it had been dull for her, her sudden disappearance had been neither welcome nor amusing to the others.
There was more in the company’s looks, however, than reproach for Rui’s willfulness: another shade was mixed in, one of bewilderment. A junior sailor explained, with an awkward hesitation.

target.text: 【Rui】 「……You two, is something the matter?」

That she had looked at some bird feathers and a human skeleton in a rooftop turret was not something Rui believed to be worth informing them of in particular, and although the nautical chart could be a vital source of information, it was something completely outside of Rui's interests, and so she never told them of that either. Beyond that, there had been no heart-throbbing incidents or accidents, it was quite boring, as she put it; even if the woman herself had been bored, her sudden disappearance was something the rest of the party found neither welcome nor amusing.

However, the group's mood was not formed just of reproach for Rui's selfishness; there was another hue intermixed, one of bewilderment, and a deck boy explained it to her in an oddly hesitant, stilted manner.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「うん、この島、人、いたんだ。
　あのね、あのお爺ちゃんがね」
source.english:
“Yeah. There is someone on this island.
You see, that old man…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Yes, so there is a man on this island. Look, that grandpa, he, well.」

source.japanese: 島に住人が？　と小首を傾げる泪の背後、影の中から伸ばされる手の、皺を無理矢理伸ばして貼り直したような肌、慎重にそして大胆に、獲物を狙う手つきで、泪の艶麗な臀へと、届く寸前で。
source.english: An inhabitant on the island? Rui tilted her head. Behind her, from the shadows, a hand reached out: its skin looked like a mass of wrinkles forcibly stretched smooth and pasted down anew. Cautiously and yet boldly, with the motions of a hand closing on its prey, it came within a hair of Rui’s voluptuous buttocks—

target.text: There is a resident on this island? When Rui asked so while tilting her head slightly in puzzlement, a hand stretched out from within the shadows behind her, covered in skin that looked as though somebody had forcibly smoothed out the wrinkles and re-affixed it to the bone, cautious yet bold, with the movement of a predator hunting down its prey, reaching for Rui's bewitching buttocks, and just before it could.

source.japanese:
背中に目でも生えていた事か、泪は片足を残してひょいと身体を前に押し出したので、背後からの手は敢えなく肩透かし、ばかりか泪が置き残した踵に爪先を引っかけ、前にのめった、支える者も掴むような物もなく、派手に床に身を打ちつけてごろごろごろ。
　長衣の姿はあの老人の。
source.english:
As though she had eyes in her back, Rui planted one foot and slipped her body neatly forward. The hand grasping from behind met empty air. Worse for its owner, his toe caught upon the heel she had left behind. He pitched forward; with no one to support him and nothing to seize, he struck the floor spectacularly and went rolling.
The long robe belonged to the old man.

target.text: Did she have eyes growing on her back or something, for while keeping one leg planted, Rui suddenly pushed her body forwards, and so the hand coming from behind her tragically missed its mark; that was not all, for the tip of his toes caught on the heel Rui had left in place, so he stumbled forwards, and with nobody to support him or anything to grab on to, he loudly slammed his body against the floor, tumbling forwards. The figure clad in the long robe belonged to that old man.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……だぁれ、この方」
source.english: “…Who… might this gentleman be?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……And who, exactly, would this be?」

source.japanese: 床に身を投げ出して老人の呻く、痛々しいが誰も手を貸そうとする者はなく、むしろ老人の破廉恥な手を平然と流した泪への賞賛と、そしてどこか当てが外れた悔しさに唇を尖らせる双子と下級水夫達だ。
source.english: The old man lay sprawled on the floor and groaned—a pitiful sight—yet no one made a move to help him. Instead, the twins and the junior sailors pursed their lips in a mix of admiration for Rui, who had calmly evaded the old man’s shameless hand, and frustration at their expectations having been somehow dashed.

target.text: The old man groaned after having thrown himself onto the floor, but though it made for a painful sight, there was nobody who tried to lend him a hand; if anything, the twins and the deck boys commended Rui for so nonchalantly evading the old man's shameless hands, pursing their lips with a certain frustration of having had their expectations betrayed.

source.japanese: 老人が一行に割りこんだ時、年寄りだからと油断したのか、まずシサムとキサラがそれぞれ右と左の乳を掴まれ、更には下級水夫君の一人が、ついているのかいないか確認せんとてか、股ぐらを揉みしだかれたのである。しかも裾[すそ]から手を滑りこまされ、半ズボンの内側でこれでもか、と。
source.english: When the old man first insinuated himself among the party, perhaps his advanced age put them off their guard. Sisam and Kisara each found one breast seized—right and left, respectively—and then one junior sailor had his crotch kneaded, as though the old man meant to ascertain whether anything was attached there at all. Worse, he slipped a hand up through the leg of the sailor's shorts and worked him over from inside with a vengeance.

source.japanese:
枯れて細い指なのに、破廉恥な事と言ったら、ここにはいないが朔屋より手が速いかも知れない。
　大事なところ、可愛らしい筍[たけのこ]の先をさんざんな目に遭わされた下級水夫君は、廃屋の隅で胎児の形で蹲[うずくま]り、親指の爪をかみ続けている。身体をゆらゆらと揺らして、時折危険に痙攣しつつ。
source.english:
Withered and thin though his fingers were, in shamelessness he might have been quicker even than Sakuya—who was, admittedly, absent.
After his most precious place—the tip of his charming little bamboo shoot—had been thoroughly abused, the junior sailor crouched in a fetal curl in one corner of the house and gnawed ceaselessly at his thumbnail. He rocked to and fro, punctuated by the occasional alarming convulsion.

target.text: They must have let their guard down when he forced himself into their company because he was old; first, he grabbed Shisamu and Kisara by their left and right breast respectively, and on top of that, he then groped around the crotch of one of the deck boys, perhaps to check if they had any extra equipment down there. Moreover, he had even slipped a hand in through the leg opening, groping around inside the shorts as if to say he wasn't quite convinced yet.

Though his fingers were slender and withered, as soon as it came to indecent matters, his hands might well have moved even faster than Sakuya's, though he wasn't present. The deck boy, whose private parts, whose precious, adorable little bamboo shoot had suffered a most terrible experience, was curled up in the fetal position in a corner of the room, continuously biting his thumbnail. He rocked his body back and forth, occasionally convulsing dangerously.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「知らないわよゥ。いつの間にか混ざってたんだから。ていうか、お爺さん、あんた誰よ、ほんとに」
source.english: “I don’t know. He just snuck in without me noticing. And anyway, old man, who are you, really?”

source.japanese:
信天翁号の面子にそうまで傍若無人な手出しして、点かない薪の替わりに焚き付けにされてもおかしくないところを無傷なのは、ただ寛容が許したからでない。
　キサラの問いは、ただ老人の誰何という以上に、島の情報を欲していた。火炙りにするにも（もとから薫製のようななりをしているが）聞き出す事は聞きだしてから、というわけだ。
source.english:
That he remained unhurt after laying hands so brazenly on the Albatross crew—when they might easily have used him for kindling in place of the firewood that refused to catch—was not owed to tolerance alone.
Kisara wanted more than the old man's name; she wanted information about the island. If they were going to roast him over a fire—though he already looked smoked—they meant to extract what he knew first.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「How the hell would I know? He just joined us without anybody noticing. Actually, who are you, you old goat, seriously.」

That he remained unharmed after having so audaciously put his hands on the crew of the Albatross, despite how easy it was to imagine him being used as kindling in place of the firewood that refused to ignite, was not because their generosity had forgiven his transgressions. Kisara's question went beyond just asking for the old man's identity; it was born from a want for more information about the island. Even if they were going to burn him at the stake (although he already looked as if he'd been smoked beforehand), then it would be after they'd gotten all the information they could get out of him, or so the reasoning went.

source.japanese:
【老人】
「儂は……この島の、最後の生き残りじゃ……いたた、年寄りは骨折しやすいんだぞ……」
source.english: “I’m… the last survivor on this island… Ouch, old bones break easy, you know…”

source.japanese: もそもそと起き出して老人は、それくらいは見れば判って言わずもがなを、わざとらしい呻[うめ]き混じりに、しかしシサム・キサラは取りあわず、
source.english: The old man stirred and sat up, stating the obvious between deliberately exaggerated groans—anyone could see that much, so it hardly needed saying—but Sisam and Kisara paid him no mind.

target.text: 【Old man】 「I……am the last survivor of this island……ow ow, us old folk have brittle bones……」

As he slowly rose to his feet, the old man said something that went without saying, obvious to all just from looking at him, and all while sprinkling in some forced groans, but Shisamu and Kisara paid that no heed,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「じゃあ教えて、この島がなんなのか。どうにも妙じゃない、この島」
source.english: “Then tell me—what is this island? There’s just something strange about it.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Alright, tell us then, what's going on with this island? It's awfully strange, isn't it?」

source.japanese:
【老人】
「失敬な。人の島を妙ちきりん扱いするとは。
　本来なら入島料を取っても良いくらいのところ、好きにさせておくとは儂なんて寛大」
source.english:
“How rude. Calling my island bizarre.
I’d have every right to levy an entrance fee, but I let you roam free—how generous of me.”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「ま、こんなところで金なんぞあっても仕方ない。替わりに金髪ちゃん、あんたの乳とか、そっちのお姉ちゃんの尻とかで。
　儂はまだまだ……この通りホレ！」
source.english:
“Well, money don’t mean jack in a joint like this. Instead, Blonde Girl, you can pay with those tits, or that lady over there’s ass…
I’m still going strong… Just look at me!”

source.japanese:
顔貌は長衣の頭巾の深く引き下ろされた奥でしかとは見てとれぬ、老人の、乾ききった手足とは裏腹に舌ばかりはまだ水気、というか卑猥な湿り気をたっぷり残していや回る事回る事。枯れた老人が胸が膨らみ始めた孫娘をからかうような、実感乏しい猥語などでは収まらない。
　老人の、転倒の痛みであちこち身体をさすっているかに思われた手は、何時しか長衣のうちの、股の辺りでもぞもぞ、ばかりか腰を前後させているでないか、干涸れた身体にしては妙に軽敏に。
source.english:
The old man's features lay hidden deep beneath the hood of his robe. His limbs might have been parched dry, but his tongue alone retained abundant moisture—an obscene wetness, rather—and how it wagged. This went far beyond the hollow smut of some withered grandfather teasing a granddaughter just beginning to fill out.
The hands that had seemed to be rubbing his bruises from the fall had somehow found their way beneath his robe and begun to fidget about the crotch. Worse, his hips were pumping to and fro with a nimbleness bizarre in so desiccated a frame.

target.text: 【Old man】 「What disrespect. Treating another man's island like some bizarre curiosity. By all rights, I should charge an entrance fee for this island, and here I am, letting you rummage around as you please, what profound generosity.」
【Old man】 「Well, not that money would do me any good in a place like this. In exchange, blondie, I'll have you pay with your tits, or maybe that fine lady's ass. I've still got it……BEHOLD!」

His features could not clearly be discerned, hidden as they were deep within the shadows of the robe's low-drawn hood, permitting only a scant glance, but in contrast to his dried-out limbs, his tongue alone was yet moist, or rather, it left copious amounts of obscene moisture in its wake as it spun round and round. And he did not limit himself to the insincere vulgarity of a withered old man teasing his granddaughter whose breasts had just begun to swell.

The old man's hands had seemed to just be massaging his body here and there in response to the pain from his tumble, but at some point, they had moved inside his robe, wriggling around near his crotch; as if that wasn't enough, was he not also thrusting his hips back and forth, and in a manner oddly agile for so desiccated a body at that.

source.japanese:
【老人】
「現役だからして、子種もそこらの若造よりずっと元気にぴっちぴちしておるわ。
　……はっ!?
　今神から啓示が降った───」
source.english:
“I’m still at it, and my seed’s far livelier than any young punk’s around here.
…Huh!?
Just got a revelation from God—”

target.text: 【Old man】 「I'm still in active service, and my seed is also far more virile and spunky than what any of those youngsters there can boast of. ……HUH!? A revelation from God just descended upon me───」

source.japanese: がっと天を仰いだ、その間にも腰は単純拍子と複合拍子で自在に律動させながらで、双子の額には澱[よど]んだ感情を示して青ずんだ縦線が何本も走った。
source.english: He flung his head back; even as he did so his hips rolled in both simple and compound rhythms, and several vertical lines, blue with pent-up emotion, ran across the twins’ foreheads.

target.text: He flung his head back to gaze into the heavens; all the while, his hips continued to thrust, freely moving between simple and compound metre; multiple pale-blue vertical lines ran down the twins' foreheads, betraying the stagnant emotions pooling within them.

source.japanese:
【老人】
「はい……はい……おお……。
　産めよ増やせよ……地に満ちよ？
　この島を再び生命溢れる、
　儂と女達の約束の地にせよ、と───」
source.english:
“Yes… yes… oh… Be fruitful and multiply…
fill the earth?
Make this island once again a land teeming with life,
the promised land for me and the women—”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「おお……神の啓示とあらば。
　さすればこの儂、老骨に鞭打ってでも、
『繁殖』に励まねばなりますまい……。
　あー、ところで君達。セーラー君達」
source.english:
“Oh… If this is a divine revelation,
then I must devote myself to ‘breeding,’ even
if I have to drive these old bones beyond their limits…
Ah, by the way, you lot. You sailors.”

target.text: 【Old man】 「Yes……yes……ooh……. Be fruitful, and multiply…… and replenish the earth? Bring forth abundantly on this island, let this be the Promised Land of me and these women, He says───」

【Old man】 「Ooh……if this is a divine revelation from God, then. If it is so, then even my humble self must rouse these old bones, I must be zealous in my efforts to 『Breed』……. Aah, on that note, you there. Young sailors.」

source.japanese: 老人がまるで轆轤の回転のような妙に滑らかな動きで頭を彼らに巡らせた、下級水夫はこの動作に、頬のなよやかな産毛毛羽立たせ引き攣[つ]らせて、総員後退り、中にはカタカタ震えが止まらなくなる子もあるほど。
