source.english: The old man swiveled his head toward them in a strangely smooth arc, like a potter’s wheel. The sight made the junior sailors’ fine cheek fuzz bristle; their faces twitched, they all recoiled, and some began to shake uncontrollably.

target.text: The old man spun his head towards them with a movement as queerly smooth as the turning of a potter's wheel; the motion was so uncanny, it caused the delicate peach fuzz on the deck boys' cheeks to fluff up and twitch, all of them retreating from the sight, some among them even trembling uncontrollably.

source.japanese:
【老人】
「物の本には、
『男の子でも妊娠した事例』というのが報告されてあってだね」
source.english:
“In the books,
there are reports of ‘cases where even boys became pregnant,’ you see.”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「中でも、
『前髪で目が隠れていて、
　一見女の子と見紛うような可愛い子で、
　半ズボン着用者』
　というのが特にその可能性が高いという」
source.english:
“Among them,
‘a cute kid whose eyes are hidden by his bangs,
who at first glance could be mistaken for a girl,
and who wears
shorts’ is said to be especially likely to become pregnant.”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「……誰ぞ『科学的可能性の被験者』に、
　志願してくれる良い子は───
　いないかのぉぉぉ～……？」
source.english:
“……Is there any good kid out there who’d like to volunteer
as a ‘test subject to explore this scientific possibility’—
anyone at allllll……?”

target.text: 【Old man】 「You see, according to the literature, there are reports of 『Cases where even boys have become pregnant』」

【Old man】 「And among them, 『Those who hide their eyes behind their forelocks、 who are such cuties they might be mistaken for girls at first glance, and wear shorts』 are said to have a particularly high chance of conceiving.」
【Old man】 「……Is there any good boy here who'd like to volunteer as a 『Test Subject of Scientific Potentiality』 ───Hmmmmmmmm～……?」

source.japanese: 妙に限定的な被検体の条件を並べ上げ、それで、一際強く、何事かを抉り貫くように強く、こぉーんと腰を強く突き出したままの姿勢で静止した、長衣の股間がありありと隆起して、照準を定めるように微動していたのに下級水夫君達───ぱたぱたと、花が散るように気絶して倒れていったという。
source.english: After rattling off a strangely specific list of criteria for test subjects, he thrust his hips forcefully forward—especially forcefully, as if to gouge straight through something—and froze in that pose. The crotch of his robe bulged visibly and twitched as if taking aim. At the sight, the junior sailors fainted one after another, fluttering down like scattered petals.

target.text: He offered some strangely restrictive prerequisites for his test subjects, and then, with remarkable force, as if he was drilling into something, piercing it with immense strength, he came to a halt, his hips remaining deeply thrust forwards, a protuberance clearly visible in the crotch of his robes, the bulge slightly quivering as if aligning its aim, and the deck boys───like scattering flower petals, fainted and collapsed in rapid succession.

source.japanese:
【老人】
「それくらいやってくれるのなら、
　島の事も少しは教えてやってもよい……。
　あ。痛い。痛い痛い痛い痛い」
source.english:
“If you’re willing to do that much for me,
I might be willing to tell you a little about the island… Ah. It hurts.
It hurts, it hurts, it hurts, it hurts.”

target.text: 【Old man】 「If you're willing to do that for me, then I suppose I don't mind telling you a little about the island……. Ah. Ow. Owowowow!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「爺ィ……」
source.english: “You old geezer…”

source.japanese: 横合いからキサラの手が伸びて、老人の頬を摘[つま]んだ、そのままぐいと引かれた。涸れて貼りついているように見えて、妙なくらいに長く伸びたのは、何重にも折りこまれた皺のせいだろうか。
source.english: Kisara’s hand darted out from the side, pinched the old man’s cheek, and gave it a hard tug. His skin looked parched and tight, yet stretched oddly far—perhaps because of the layers upon layers of wrinkles.

source.japanese:
【老人】
「痛い痛い、皮が剥がれるだろうか金髪ちゃん。剥くのは包茎のちんぽこだけで沢山だ。
　だから痛いってば」
source.english:
“It hurts, it hurts—is my skin gonna peel off, blondie? Pulling back a dick’s foreskin is quite enough for me.
I said it hurts!”

source.japanese:
この際キサラの手が、相手はただ年寄りだから容赦しなかったのは当然だし、それに彼女には一つの疑いがあったのである。そう、本気で剥ぐつもりだった。老人の化けの皮を。
　キサラは朔屋青年が老人の変装して、島にこっそり乗りこんできていたのではと勘繰ったのである。
source.english:
Naturally Kisara had no thought of sparing him merely because he was old. More than that, she had a suspicion. She truly did mean to strip away the old man's borrowed skin.
Kisara suspected that Sakuya had disguised himself as an old man and secretly made his way onto the island.

source.japanese: しかし、老人は、ここぞとばかりに年寄りの湿っぽい哀れっぽさで呻[うめ]くばかりで、マスクが剥がれる音も偽皺の樹脂が千切れる感触もなく、正真正銘見た通りの年寄りと言う事、それはそれで始末に負えないという、ろくでもない事実しか判明しなかった。
source.english: The old man merely groaned, seizing the moment with an old man’s maudlin self-pity. There was no sound of a mask peeling off, nor any sensation of resin tearing in fake wrinkles—it became clear that he was, in fact, exactly what he appeared to be: a genuine old man. And that, in itself, made him no easier to deal with—a wretched discovery.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Graaamps……」

Kisara's hand reached in from the side, then pinched the old man's cheek and tugged hard on it. The skin looked dry and plastered on, but then also stretched weirdly far; it must have been a result of the several layers of wrinkles folded over each other?
【Old man】 「That hurts, that hurts, are you trying to peel my skin off, blondie? The only skin you need to peel off is what's covering my phimotic cock. I said that hurts!」

In these circumstances, it was only natural that Kisara's hand held no mercy, even if she was just dealing with an elderly man, for a suspicion lingered in her mind. Indeed, she had truly intended peel it off. The mask this old man wore, that is. For Kisara suspected that the young man Sakuya had disguised himself as an old man, then secretly sneaked onto the island.

However, while the old man did nothing but groan with the damp, miserable pathos of the elderly, seizing the moment to play the part, there was no sound of a mask peeling away, nor any sensation of artificial wrinkles made of resin being torn to shreds; that is to say, he was genuinely an old man, exactly as he looked, and that in itself was hard to cope with; such was the only worthless truth that came to light.

source.japanese:
───結局、老人を船まで連れていく事になった。もちろん下級水夫達は大反対したけれど、知っている限りの事は聞き出す必要もあり、かつまた船のどこかにでも閉じこめて、しっかり監視を付けておいた方が、島内をふらふら徘徊されるよりずっと安心だと、双子にそう主張されては一理あり、皆渋々と受け入れたけれど。
　船へと連行していく間、誰も老人の手が届くところには近づこうとせず、頭巾の頭が向けられる度皆悲鳴で逃げ回った為、戻りはそれは賑やかな道行きとなったが、歓迎する者は誰一人としていなかった。
source.english:
In the end, they decided to take the old man back to the ship. The junior sailors vehemently objected, of course, but they needed to extract everything he knew. And as the twins argued, shutting him up somewhere aboard under close watch would be much safer than allowing him to wander the island. There was sense in that. Everyone reluctantly agreed.
During the journey, nobody would come within reach of his hands. Whenever his hooded head turned their way, they scattered screaming. It made for a lively procession back to the ship, but not a single person welcomed it.

target.text: ───In the end, they decided to bring the old man back with them to the ship. Naturally, the deck boys were strongly opposed to the idea, but they did need to figure out everything he knew, and besides, locking him up somewhere on the ship and keeping a close eye on him would bring much greater peace of mind than just letting him wander around the island; certainly, there was some logic to what the twins asserted, and so they all reluctantly accepted it.

While marching him to the ship, no one dared step within the old man's reach, and every time his hooded head turned their way, they would scatter with screams, making for a remarkably boisterous procession on the journey back, though not a single soul welcomed him there.

source.japanese: その推進力は機関車の如く、その体躯はビヤ樽の如く、どかどかと踏みしだく足は岩塊の如く、水夫長は船内通路を往く、綽名の由来の龍が半面にのたくる。
source.english: With the drive of a locomotive, the bulk of a beer barrel and feet that trampled like lumps of rock, the boatswain thundered through the ship's passageways. The dragon that gave him his nickname writhed across half his face.

target.text: The propulsive power was like a locomotive, the body built like a beer barrel, and the noisily stomping feet like lumps of rock; the Bosun was moving through the ship passageway, the dragon that gave him his ekename slithering across half his face.

source.japanese: そこへクロの船室からひょこと頭を出[いだ]した朔屋こそぼんやりもの、印度の山車の猛進と相対したようなもので、慌てて身を引っこめたものの、水夫長に服の端を引っかけられて、竜巻に巻きこまれる勢いで戸口に叩きつけられた。
source.english: Sakuya chose that moment to poke his vacant head out of Kuro's cabin, placing himself squarely in the path of an Indian juggernaut. He hastily withdrew, but the boatswain caught the edge of his clothes and slammed him into the doorway with the force of a passing tornado.

target.text: And just then, Sakuya, ever hopelessly oblivious, poked his head out of Kuro's cabin; it was as though he was facing the onslaught of the Juggernaut of India head on, and so he hastily pulled back into the room, but the edge of his clothes caught on the Bosun, and he was slammed against the doorway with all the force of being swept away by a tornado.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いってぇ……。
　水夫長、なにそんな急いでんの」
source.english:
“Ow…
What's the hurry, Bosun?”

source.japanese: 肩口に撲ち身こしらえて呻[うめ]く朔屋を尻目に駆け去っていく、かに思われて配管を掴んで急制動、ぬうと顔を突き出してきたので青年は、龍に鼻先を噛みつかれる思いしたという。
source.english: He seemed about to charge away, leaving Sakuya moaning over his bruised shoulder, but grabbed a pipe and braked abruptly. Then he thrust his face forward. The young man felt as though the dragon had snapped at the tip of his nose.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Ouch……. Bosun, what's got you in such a rush?」

He gave Sakuya, who was groaning from the bruise he'd received on the top of his shoulder, a sidelong glance as he continued to gallop past him, or so it seemed, but he grabbed hold of some piping and slammed on the brakes, then suddenly thrust his face forwards, so quickly it even convinced the young man that the dragon was snapping at his nose.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう朔屋か。てめえ、爺を見なかったか」
source.english: “Oh, Sakuya. You seen the old bastard?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだいきなり。爺てのはなんですよ」
source.english: “What's this all of a sudden? What old bastard?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「爺たぁ爺だぁね。こうボロボロのマントみたいなの羽織った奴だ……どうだ？」
source.english: “The old bastard's the old bastard. Wears a ragged sort of cape… Well?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どうだもなにも……誰なのその爺てのは」
source.english: “Well what? Who is this old man?”

source.japanese: どうにも要領を得ないやりとりは、水夫長の気が急いてるせいか朔屋の飲み込みが悪いせいか、ともかく焦れったげに水夫長がざっと説明したので、朔屋もようやく一行が島内で出会って信天翁へと共に戻ってきた怪老人の事を知った次第なのだった。
source.english: Whether the boatswain was too impatient or Sakuya too slow on the uptake, their exchange got nowhere. At last Long gave an irritated outline of events, and the young man learned of the strange old fellow the others had met on the island and brought back to the Albatross.

source.japanese:
というかそれ以前の問題として、昨日クロと共に船に留守居を命じられた朔屋には、そもそも島の内がどういう様子なのか、ここで聞くまで全く伝わっていなかった仲間外れ。
　この日は昨夜から強まった雨を押して探索を続行するかどうか、意見が水夫長と航海士の間で割れていたし、連れ戻った老人の姿が船内に見えなくなってしまった事も手伝って、でなければ乗り組み達はさっさと島に出かけ、朔屋とクロはまた置いてけぼりを喰らっていただろう。
source.english:
For that matter, having been ordered yesterday to stay aboard with Kuro, Sakuya had heard nothing whatsoever of what the island was like until this moment. Left out entirely.
Today the boatswain and navigators disagreed over whether to continue exploring in the rain, which had intensified overnight. That, and the disappearance of the old man they had brought back, had kept the crew aboard. Otherwise they would have gone straight ashore, leaving Sakuya and Kuro behind again.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「とにかく、俺はそんな爺なんて見ちゃいないよ。……あ」
source.english: “Anyway, I haven't seen any old man… Oh.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hey, if it isn't Sakuya. You seen an old man around here?」
【Naomasa】 「What's this all of a sudden? What do you mean old man?」
【Bosun】 「An old man is an old man, yeah? Guy is wearing this tattered, cloak-like thing……so how about it?」
【Naomasa】 「How about what……who is this old man even?」

The exchange was rather confusing, and whether it was the Bosun to blame for being in such a hurry, or it was Sakuya to blame for being too slow to understand, regardless, the Bosun ended up impatiently giving a rough outline of the events that had transpired, and only then did Sakuya also finally learn of the mysterious old man that the party had encountered on the island and brought back with them to the Albatross.

Rather, there was a much bigger, fundamental problem here: Sakuya, who had been ordered to watch the ship together with Kuro the day before, had, until this moment, not been told the first thing about what the island was like; he had been left out yet again.

On this day, the question was whether or not to continue the exploration despite the heavy rain that had only intensified since last night; opinions were split between the Bosun and the first mates, and the disappearance of the old man they'd brought back to the ship also helped make their decision for them; otherwise, the crew would have left for the island once more without delay, and Sakuya and Kuro would most likely have been left behind again.
【Naomasa】 「Anyway, I haven't seen any old man like that around. ……Ah.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なんでぇ。ちっとでも心当たりがあるんならさっさと吐け。こっちゃ見ての通り忙しいんだからな」
source.english: “What? If you've got the slightest idea, spit it out. Can't you see I'm busy?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「別に見たとか心当たりがあるって訳じゃないんだが、その爺さん、あんたらが見てないうちに島に戻ってったんじゃないの？」
source.english: “I haven't seen him or anything. But couldn't he have gone back to the island while you weren't looking?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こんなボロ船より……ああいや、慣れない船が落ち着かなくってさ」
source.english: “Maybe this wreck—I mean, an unfamiliar ship—made him feel uneasy.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「きっとそうだぜ水夫長、
　捜すつもりなら島に行った方が速いって。
　なんだったら俺も捜すの手伝うから。
　だから、俺らも島に上陸させてくれよう」
source.english:
“Bet that's it, Bosun.
If you want to find him, you'll do it quicker ashore.
I'll even help you look, if you like.
Come on, let us go to the island too.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What is it? If you've got the slightest idea, then spit it out already. As you can see, I'm real busy.」
【Naomasa】 「It's not like I've seen him or have any particular guess as to where he is, but couldn't this old guy just have returned to the island while you weren't keeping an eye on him?」
【Naomasa】 「Maybe he'd rather be there than on a ship this run-down……uhh, I mean, settle down, he couldn't really settle down on an unfamiliar ship.」

【Naomasa】 「That has to be it, Bosun, so if you're looking for him, it'd be faster if you went to the island. And if you want, I'll even help you look for him too. So please, let us set foot on the island too!」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「島に戻ってるかも、だぁ？　短艇を動かした様子もないのにか？」
source.english: “Gone back to the island, has he? When there's no sign the boat's been moved?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「He might have returned to the island, you say? Despite there being no sign that the boat's been used?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だいたいお前が出てきたかて、なんの役に立つと言うンだ。だから残ってろい、大人しく、な。船を見てる奴だって入り用だし」
source.english: “And what good would you do ashore? Stay here and behave yourself. Someone's got to mind the ship.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんないけず言わないでさあ」
source.english: “Don't be so mean…”

source.japanese:
雨に濡れて狭霧渦巻く静かな気色を風情と取るより、辛気臭いと鼻つまむ気風の方が強い信天翁号の面々には、島内の、静謐湛えた廃址など、一日歩いただけで見飽きて、屋内の動物達の骨の山も不気味は不気味だが、どうせ大した金にもならない、ああまで乾ききっていては出汁も取れない、では一行の気を惹きつけるにはどうにも押しが足らない。
　が、それは上陸した者達だから言える事。
source.english:
The Albatross company were more inclined to wrinkle their noses at the gloom of a quiet, rain-soaked landscape with mist swirling through it than to appreciate its charm. One day's walk had exhausted the appeal of the island's tranquil ruins. The animal bones inside the houses were certainly eerie, but they wouldn't fetch much money, and were too dry even to make stock. They lacked the force to hold the party's interest.
But that was easy to say when one had been ashore.

source.japanese:
酒と女があればいい、血湧き肉躍るような冒険など、どうせ巻きこまれたところで出だしで躓[つまず]いて中途退場が落ちだと、平穏でだらけた日々を望みとする朔屋にも好奇心というものはある。
　嵐を超えて辿り着いた無人島の中を、ちらとでも覗いてみたいと願うのは、当たり前な心の流れと言えた。
source.english:
All Sakuya wanted was drink and women. As for stirring adventures, if he got dragged into one he would merely stumble at the outset and retire halfway through. He wished for peaceful, idle days—but even he possessed curiosity.
Wanting so much as a glimpse of the deserted island they had reached beyond the storm was a perfectly natural impulse.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「And should you come with us, what good are you gonna do? That's why you stay put and behave, got it? Even the people just minding the ship are essential.」
【Naomasa】 「Come ooon, don't be so mean.」

Rather than appreciating the quiet atmosphere of the swirling mists and drenching rain, the desire to pinch their noses in frustration was a far stronger sentiment amongst the crew of the Albatross, for they had grown fed up of seeing these ruins brimming with tranquility in but a single day of walking through them, and while the piles of animal bones within the buildings certainly were unsettling in their own right, unsettling wouldn't earn them much money at all, and dry as they were, they couldn't even be used for broth; it simply lacked any sort of impact that could attract the crew's interest.
But this was only something they could say because they had actually set foot on the island.

All he needed was booze and women; even if he did get dragged into some blood-pumping adventure full of thrills, all that awaited him was just stumbling right at the starting line and dropping out halfway through anyway, but though he wished for nothing but peaceful days, Sakuya still held that spark of curiosity within himself. The desire to catch a glimpse of what lay hidden on this deserted island they had reached after weathering the storm, why, one could say it was a perfectly natural flow of the heart.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ……起きてきたか、クロ」
source.english: “Oh… You're up, Kuro.”

source.japanese: 昨夜の情事の後、島から遠く届いた怪しの声に気絶したクロは、朝までそのまま喪神していたのだが、戸口での騒がしげなやりとりに目を覚ましたと見えて、乾いた涙の目脂を擦り擦りもぞもぞと、起き出してきたがまだ目は虚ろ、無理もないが前後の状況が呑みこめていない。
source.english: After last night's tryst, Kuro had fainted at a strange voice carrying all the way from the island and lain insensible until morning. The commotion at the doorway appeared to have roused her. She stirred, rubbing the dried crust of tears from her eyes, and rose at last—her gaze still vacant, her mind, understandably, nowhere near catching up with events.

source.japanese:
顧みれば朝っぱらからクロの部屋から出てきた事を訝しく見られても無理からぬところ、水夫長は行方不明の老人に気を取られて、そこまで詮索する余裕はないらしい。
　朔屋は失神したクロの、息遣いはまず確かなのに安堵して、敢えて起こすのも忍びなく、彼女をベッドに押しこんだはいいが、自室まで戻るのが億劫になって、その脇に潜[もぐ]りこんで眠ってしまっていた。一通りざっと情事の後始末して、衣服を着け直してやっていた事に胸を撫で下ろしつつ、クロが余計な口を叩き出す前に畳みかけた。
source.english:
In retrospect, anyone might have wondered why he was emerging from Kuro's room at this hour. The bosun, preoccupied with the missing old man, seemed to have no attention to spare for such inquiries.
Sakuya had first reassured himself that Kuro was breathing steadily. He could not bring himself to wake her, so he had tucked her into bed; then, too lazy to return to his own cabin, he had crawled in beside her and fallen asleep. Thank heaven he had at least cleaned up the worst of last night's business and dressed her again. Before Kuro could volunteer anything inconvenient, he hurried on.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なあクロだって島に行ってみたいよな？」
source.english: “You'd like to see the island too, wouldn't you, Kuro?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Ah……so you're awake, Kuro?」

After their liaison last night, upon hearing that eerie voice reaching them from the distant island, Kuro had fainted, and she had remained unconscious until morning, but it seemed as though she had been roused from slumber by the tumult and conversation by the doorway; she rubbed the rheum of her dried tears off while squirming, but even after dragging herself out of bed, her eyes were still vacant; small wonder, for she had yet to grasp the context of what was happening.

When he reflected on it, it would only be reasonable for it to be viewed with suspicion that he came out of Kuro's room this early in the morning, but the Bosun's thoughts were occupied with the missing old man, so it seemed he lacked the mental allowance to pry that deeply into the matter.

Upon realizing that the unconscious Kuro was still breathing steadily, Sakuya had felt relieved, but he couldn't bring himself to purposely wake her up, and so he had just tucked her into her bed; that much was fine, but he had also found it too bothersome to head all the way back to his own room, and so he had crawled into her bed and fallen asleep by her side. While breathing a sigh of relief that he had more or less taken care of the aftermath already, as well as thought to put her clothes back on, he quickly pressed on, throwing a question in Kuro's face before she could say anything indiscreet.
【Naomasa】 「Come on, even Kuro wants to go to the island, right?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「え……？　クロは……ええと。
　島には、そんな、行かなくても」
source.english:
“Huh…? Kuro… um. The island…
Kuro doesn't really need to go.”

source.japanese: クロはどうやらこの島を目の当たりにした時から本能的な恐怖を抱いているようで、朔屋の誘い水にも気乗り薄、答えはどうにもはかばかしくない。
source.english: Kuro seemed to have felt an instinctive fear of the island ever since first seeing it. Sakuya's prompting failed to tempt her. Her answer was dispiritingly vague.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ええー……」
source.english: “Aww…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uh……? Kuro is……uhmm. Doesn't really……need to go to the island.」

It appeared that, ever since first laying eyes on this island, Kuro had been harbouring an instinctual dread, and so she was unenthusiastic in response to Sakuya's attempt at creating a pretext, her answer not being what he hoped for at all.
【Naomasa】 「Eeehhー……」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「それにクロ、他の港とかでも、おるす番だから。あ、いやだって事なくて、あんま、降りると」
source.english: “Kuro stays aboard at other ports too. Oh, Kuro doesn't mind. If Kuro goes ashore too much…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「And also, even in other ports, Kuro watches the ship. Ah, not because Kuro doesn't want to, that Kuro doesn't……get much off the ship.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「港の人とか、他の船の人とかに、
　……怒らいたりするから。
　なんで怒るか、わからないけど、
　ごめんってしても、許してもらえない」
source.english:
“People at the port, people from other ships…
get angry with Kuro.
I don't know why.
Even when Kuro says sorry, they won't forgive her.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Because the people from the port, or other ships, ……they get angry. Don't know why they get angry, but even when Kuro says sorry, they don't forgive Kuro.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だからいつもおるす番ね、クロ。
　だからるす番、
　そんなにいやじゃないもの」
source.english:
“So Kuro always stays to mind the ship.
That's why…
Kuro doesn't mind it so much.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひでえ。港に入ったら入ったで、船から出してもやらないのか……ちょっとくらい遊びに行かせるとかしてやればいいのに……」
source.english: “That's awful. You reach a port and they still won't let you off the ship… They could at least let you go and have a little fun…”

source.japanese: そんな時でも蔑[ないがし]ろにされている、どこまでも哀れなクロに、朔屋の声の調子が低くなったが、水夫長はこれっぽっちも気に掛けた風もなく、
source.english: Even then she was neglected. Poor Kuro, in every possible way. Sakuya's voice sank, but the boatswain seemed not to care in the slightest.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「That's why Kuro always watches the ship. So watching the ship is not so bad.」
【Naomasa】 「That's terrible. So even as it enters port, you still don't get off the ship……you should at least go out and have a little fun or something……」

Upon witnessing the utterly pathetic Kuro, treated with disdainful neglect even at such times, Sakuya's voice lowered in pitch, but the Bosun showed not the slightest sign of it weighing on his heart,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「つぅこった。クロもなんでかお前にゃ懐いとるようだし、ちょうどええわ」
source.english: “There you go. She's taken to you for some reason. Works out nicely.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「And that's that. Kuro's also taken a liking to you, for whatever reason, so it works out fine.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「役立たず同士、大人しくしてるこったな」
source.english: “Useless, both of you. Stay put and keep quiet.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You two be on your best behaviour, as fellow incompetents.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわあああん、さすがだぞ俺。
　なんも言い返せねえぜえ」
source.english:
“Waaah! That's me all right.
Can't even argue…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Waaaaah, what else could I expect from myself? I have no retorts.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さんはでも、クロと違って水夫長に、言えるよ。口、きいてるよ」
source.english: “But you can talk to the bosun, Mr. Sakuya. Kuro can't. You talk to him.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……凄いなあ」
source.english: “…Amazing.”

source.japanese: とそのように驚嘆されても。朔屋には全く褒められているようには受け取られず、
source.english: Such admiration hardly felt like a compliment to Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……お部屋に戻って、床板の木目でも数えてよっか……」
source.english: “…Shall we go back to your room and count the grain in the floorboards…?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But Sakuya-san, unlike Kuro, can talk with the Bosun. Can actually talk.」
【Kuro】 「……That's amazing.」
She could be however struck with admiration she liked. Sakuya did not take it as a compliment at all,
【Naomasa】 「……We might as well go back inside your cabin, maybe count the grains in the floorboards……」

source.japanese: 朔屋としては皮肉めかした冗談のつもりだったが、クロはそれでも構わないと見えて、あい、と素直に頷[うなず]いた。
source.english: He had meant it as a sarcastic joke. Kuro apparently saw no objection, and meekly nodded. ‘Yes.’

target.text: Sakuya had intended it to be a sardonic joke, yet Kuro didn't seem to mind at all; with an "aye", she nodded her head obediently.

source.japanese: 巧言令色鮮少、とはよく言ったものだが、弁舌もまた一つの才なのであって、根深い巌[いわお]は語りかけているだけではなるほど動かせないとしても、それを動かし得る機械や人数を遣う人物の心へ言葉を響かせ得るならまた話は別の。まあ朔屋にそもそもそんな滑らかな口舌あらば、もう少し異なった人生を歩んでいたはずで、自身に生産的な能力は皆無としても金満家の後家などに取り入り……ではなく、騙くらかし……もとへ、ご機嫌を取って……いやその、ああ、相談役だ、その辺りに落ち着いて、日々の酒代には不自由しないくらいのご身分を得ていた事だって有り得る。
source.english: ‘Smooth words and flattering looks seldom go with a good heart’: well said, perhaps, but eloquence is itself a talent. Words alone cannot move a deeply rooted boulder, certainly. Yet if they can reach the heart of the person who commands the machinery or the men capable of moving it, that is another matter. Had Sakuya possessed such a glib tongue, he would have led a somewhat different life. Even without any productive ability of his own, he might have ingratiated himself with some wealthy widow… no, swindled her… rather, catered to her wishes… well, ah, become her adviser, that's it. Settled into such a position, he might at least have had no difficulty finding his daily drinking money.

target.text: Fine words and an insinuating appearance are seldom associated with true virtue, or so it is often said, but eloquence is a talent in itself, for even if a great rock deeply entrenched in the ground will not be moved from words alone, it is a different tale entirely if one's words manage to reach a mind that can dispatch the machines or people necessary to do so instead.

Well, if Sakuya had such a smooth tongue to begin with, then he would surely be walking down a slightly different path in life, for even if he himself was not possessed of any constructive abilities, he could have found a rich widow and charmed…… not quite, deceived……scratch that, buttered up……no, well, ah, an advisor, he would settle for something in that wheelhouse, and it is very possible that he could have secured for himself a position that would allow him to spend his days without ever being in want of coin for drink.

source.japanese: まあそんな小器用さで立ち回れていなかったからこそ、水夫長の調伏も叶わず、結局はクロと共に船に蟄居閉門を申しつけられているわけだが───水夫長は老人の捜索によほど気を取られていたのか、朔屋とクロに特に仕事を言いつけてもいかなかった。考えようによっては、まる一日休暇を得た、とも言える。
source.english: Precisely because he lacked that dexterity, he had failed to tame the boatswain and ended up confined aboard with Kuro. Long had apparently been so absorbed in searching for the old man that he had gone off without assigning them any work. Viewed another way, they had been given a whole day off.

source.japanese:
が朔屋は、その休みの時間を、結局半日がたもうつらうつらと、眠って休息を身体に与えるでもなく、起きて何か活動するでもない、
　中途半端で、どうしようもなく無駄にして過ごした。
source.english:
Sakuya squandered nearly half of it dozing: neither sleeping properly to rest his body, nor waking to do anything.
A hopeless, halfhearted waste.

source.japanese: ……人の真の教養というのは、時間をいかに上手に食い潰す術をどれだけ心得ているかにも表れるという。
source.english: A person's true refinement, they say, also shows in how many ways he knows to eat up time gracefully.

target.text: Well, it was precisely because he was incapable of navigating so shrewdly through life that, with the deadly curse he put upon the Bosun not working out either, in the end, he and Kuro were ordered to stay confined on the ship, but───the Bosun really must have been very occupied with searching for that old man, for he had not ordered Sakuya or Kuro to do any work in particular. And depending on how you thought about it, it was like they had been given a whole day off, one could even say.

But Sakuya, given this time of repose, ultimately spent half the day drowsily: not granting his body the relief of sleep, but also without getting up and doing anything productive. Wasted it in a manner hopeless in its half-heartedness.
……It is said that the true measure of a man's cultivation is revealed by the degree to which he has mastered the art of killing time.

source.japanese: かつ、小人閑居して不善を為す、ともいう。監視する目が無くとも、悪さする事もなく大人しくしていたのは立派は立派だが、朔屋の場合は悪さを企む甲斐性もなかっただけの事。小人にもなれやしない半端者。
source.english: And they also say that the petty man does evil when no one is watching. Behaving himself without a watchful eye upon him was commendable, certainly, but Sakuya simply lacked the initiative to devise any mischief. A half-made creature who could not even manage to be petty.

target.text: Furthermore, it is also said that an idle mind is the devil's workshop. That he was behaving himself instead of causing trouble, and without any watchful eyes on him to boot, was both impressive and praiseworthy, but in Sakuya's case, it was simply because he lacked the resourcefulness to plan any mischief. The sort of mind so idle that even the devil himself did not want to set up shop.

source.japanese: クロが寝台に腰かけて、船の洋燈の火屋を掃除している様子を見守るうち、単調な動きに眠気催し、椅子に座ったまま意識が曖昧になって、がくんと頭が大きく前にのめって椅子から転がり落ちそうになってさすがに意識がはっと身体に戻った。時にはあろうまいことか、船室は蚊帳でも釣ったかに薄ぼんやりと小暗くなっており。
source.english: Watching Kuro clean the ship's lamp chimneys as she sat on the bed, he grew sleepy from the repetitive motion. His awareness blurred in his chair until his head lurched forward and he nearly tumbled off it. That, at last, brought his mind snapping back into his body. Somehow, the cabin had grown dim and hazy, as if a mosquito net had been hung across it.

target.text: Kuro was sitting on her bed, cleaning the glass chimney of one of the ship's lamps, and while he observed her, the monotonous movements made him sleepy, and still sitting in a chair, his consciousness grew hazy; when his head suddenly dropped sharply, his body on the verge of tumbling out of the chair, his consciousness finally returned to his body. At times, unthinkable though it might seem, the cabin grew dimly dark, as though a mosquito net had been strung up, hanging over the room.

source.japanese: クロも洋燈の硝子を持って貌[かお]を俯[うつむ]け加減の、下からつぅ、と涎が垂れ落ちかかっていた。朔屋の寝汚さが感染したか、彼女も眠気に捕まってある。ただ白子の少女の、朔屋よりよほど偉い、寝台には綺麗になった火屋がクロを取り巻いて蓮の台[うてな]のようにずらずらと、青年が半睡半覚の間で時を無駄にしているうちに、それだけの仕事はこなしていた。
source.english: Kuro, too, was nodding over a glass chimney, a thread of saliva about to drip from beneath her lowered face. Had Sakuya's sloth proved contagious? Drowsiness had caught her as well. But the albino girl deserved far more credit than he. Clean chimneys lined the bed around her like a lotus throne. While the young man had wasted his time between sleep and waking, she had done that much work.

target.text: Kuro, holding a glass chimney in her hand, had also slightly inclined her head, and a thread of drool dangled from below, on the verge of dripping down. Perhaps she'd been infected by Sakuya's somnolence, for she, too, had been caught in the claws of Somnus. But this albino girl was more admirable than Sakuya by far, for placed on the bed, now-clean chimneys surrounded Kuro like a lotus throne; that was how much work she'd managed to do while the young man had been idling away his time in the limbo between sleep and the waking world.

source.japanese:
洋燈の火屋磨き、といって大した面倒事でもない。
　何事につけ旧式というか、新しい装備をとにかく吝嗇する信天翁号ではいまだあちこちの灯りに洋燈を吊しているのだけれど、風防の硝子はやがて煤に内側から曇って、定期的に汚れを拭い取ってやらないといけない。この時火屋の中にウエスを差しこんで拭うには、子供かあるいはそれくらい細い手首が望ましい。大人では手が入らない。
source.english:
Cleaning lamp chimneys was hardly a complicated business.
Old-fashioned in every respect—or simply too stingy to buy new equipment—the Albatross still hung oil lamps here and there for light. Soot gradually clouded the insides of their glass windguards, which had to be wiped clean periodically. A child's wrist, or one equally slender, was best for reaching inside with a rag. An adult's hand would not fit.

source.japanese:
というか子供にもできる単純な手仕事で、クロなどはやらせておくのにうってつけなのである。
　もちろん落としたりなどして割ったりせぬよう注意は必要だが、クロは賢い、そのあたりはちゃあんと考えてある。作業の場に寝台を選んであり、下は布団だもの、もし落としても特に差し支えはない。
source.english:
In other words, it was simple manual work even a child could do: ideal for keeping Kuro occupied.
Naturally, care was needed not to drop and break them, but Kuro was clever. She had thought of that. She had chosen the bed as her workplace. With bedding underneath, a dropped chimney would do no particular harm.

target.text: Polishing the chimney of a lamp was, all things considered, not a particularly bothersome task. Always doing everything the old way no matter what, or more aptly put, the Albatross was too stingy to procure new equipment, and so there were still these old oil lamps hanging all over the place, but sooner or later, the glass shielding the flame from wind would be blackened with soot, and it had to be wiped clean periodically. And when one then had to stick a rag inside the chimney and polish it, a child or someone with similarly thin wrists was desirable. The hands of an adult could not fit in there.

And since this was also a manual task so simple that even a child could handle it, Kuro was the ideal girl for the job. Of course, one needed to be attentive enough to not, say, drop the chimney and crack the glass, but Kuro was a clever girl, for she had already thought of that. She had chosen her bed as her workstation, for below was her bedding, so even should she drop the glass, it would not cause any problems in particular.

source.japanese: それで硝子の火屋を、見ているだけで背中がむずむず焦れったくなってくるほど一つ一つ手間暇かけて、龍の掌中の珠でも磨き上げるかに丁寧に丁寧に、煤汚れを拭き取っていたクロだったが、うたた寝の朔屋は邪魔にはならない替わりに話し相手にもならない、雨は小やみなく続いて心を鈍磨させる、眠気を催さない方がおかしい。
source.english: She had been wiping the soot from the glass chimneys, lavishing so much time on each that merely watching made one's back itch with impatience. Carefully, carefully—as though polishing the jewel in a dragon's palm. But a dozing Sakuya, though no impediment, was no company either. The unbroken rain dulled the mind. Not growing sleepy would have been stranger.

target.text: So there Kuro sat, spending so much time and effort on every little smudge on the chimney that just watching it was enough to make itchy impatience crawl across one's back, as attentive and thorough as if she were polishing a jewel cradled in the claws of a dragon; while the dozing Sakuya wasn't being a nuisance to Kuro as she wiped off the soot stains, in return, he also made a poor companion for conversation, and with the incessant rain dulling her mind, it would, if anything, be stranger if she wasn't being lulled to sleep.

source.japanese: 睡魔に船を漕いだ弾みに、片手を差しこんだままの火屋にこつんと、額を当てて、はっと心づいた、切れ落ちる寸前だった涎の筋をずるり吸いこんでは目を瞠[みは]ってきょろきょろきょろ。
source.english: A nod of sleep brought her forehead against the glass, with one hand still inside it. Tap. She woke with a start, sucked back the strand of drool just about to fall, and looked around wide-eyed.

target.text: And when she nodded off in sleep's embrace, with a clunk, the jerk of her head made her hit her brow against the chimney still held in her hand; she came back to life with a start, inhaled the line of drool about to fall down with a slurp, then goggled all around the room.

source.japanese: 顔見合わせる朔屋とクロ、二人して蕩[とろ]けかかって胡乱な目つきの、船窓の外の雨垂れを枕に、だらだらと退屈に引き延ばされたような時間は、のろのろと鈍足に留まるかに見えて、気がつけば思ったより過ぎていたという。こうもいい加減で実にならない時間の使い方もあるまい。ま、クロの方はなんぼか仕事の成果残しているが。
source.english: Sakuya and Kuro looked at one another, both almost melting with drowsiness, their eyes bleary. With the rain at the porthole for a pillow, time had stretched out in languid boredom, seeming to creep so slowly it scarcely moved. Then they found more of it had passed than they thought. There could hardly be a more aimless, unproductive use of time. Well, Kuro had at least left some work to show for hers.

target.text: Kuro and Sakuya exchanged glances, both pairs of eyes filled with a dazed, hazy look on the verge of melting away; with the raindrops outside the porthole serving as a pillow, it might have seemed as if this time, dragged on by its endless monotony, moved with a slow-footed plodding, but before they knew it, the time had passed them by much faster than he had imagined it. There was surely no other way to idle away time more irresponsibly fruitless than this. Well, Kuro had managed to produce some fruit through her labour.

source.japanese: なんにしても退屈に時間を持て余したはずが、船室ははや、ぼやけて薄暗い。二人の漫然と弛緩した気分が身体から漏出したのではなく、止まない雨に覆われたこの島の、足早な夕闇の訪れである。朔屋とクロは、自分達の心がどれだけ眠りに漂うてあったのか、それさえ暗迷としていたから、軽く瞬いて目を開けた時には夕闇がやってきていたようなもの、狐に化かされ顔になるのも詮なき事とはいえ、端から眺める者あったら、その鬱陶しい、歯切れの悪い塩梅に、後ろ頭をどやしつけたくなったであろう。
source.english: However they had idled away the hours, the cabin was already blurred with dusk. This was not their vague lassitude leaking out of their bodies, but the early fall of evening upon the island beneath its ceaseless rain. Neither Sakuya nor Kuro knew how far their minds had drifted into sleep. It was almost as if dusk had arrived between one blink and the next. Their bewildered looks, as though a fox had bewitched them, were understandable. Any observer, however, would have wanted to cuff the backs of their heads for being so irritatingly slow and muddled.

target.text: At any rate, while they should have been bored and had more time on their hands than they'd know what to do with, the cabin was already blurry and dim. It was not that their aimless, flaccid mood had leaked out from their bodies, but rather because night had fallen quickly on this island covered in a veil of incessant rain.

How long had their minds been adrift on the sea of slumber, even that was beyond Kuro and Sakuya's comprehension; it was as if twilight had arrived after but a brief blink of the eyes, but though it could be called inevitable for them to wear the face of a man who had been deceived by a fox, any who saw them from the sidelines, who witnessed this obnoxiously unfocused, indecisive state of being, would more like than not be gripped by a desire to smack them in the back of the head. (TN: The proverb in use here is "狐に化かされ顔", literally "face of having been deceived by a fox". It means a dumbfounded expression.)

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「雨、止まないね」
source.english: “The rain won't stop.”

source.japanese: 他愛なく寝こけていたのがお互いなんとのう気恥ずかしく、ぼやけた笑みに見やれば船窓の、雨垂れを連ね重ねて、硝子の面それ自体が溶け出したように、流れては垂れゆく、島の雨は絶えて止む事を知らず。
source.english: Both were vaguely embarrassed at having dozed off so readily. With hazy smiles they looked toward the porthole, where raindrops joined and overlapped, flowing down as though the glass itself were melting. The island's rain knew no pause.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ。嵐も、だな」
source.english: “Yeah. The storm, too.”

source.japanese: 環礁の中は沈んだ雨なれど、入り江から外海に出ればそこは渦巻く嵐の、こちらも信天翁号が島に辿り着いてから一向に収まる事なく、それを想えば島を出る際の労苦が予想されてうんざりとなる。クロがどれだけ神がかった操船能力を発揮しようとも、船が波浪に揉みくちゃにされる事には変わりがない。
source.english: Within the atoll lay this subdued rain. Out beyond the inlet, the storm still swirled, unabated since the Albatross reached the island. Thinking of it made the prospect of leaving exhausting. Whatever godlike seamanship Kuro displayed, the ship would still be battered and tossed by the waves.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「The rain won't stop, huh.」

They both felt a little embarrassed at falling asleep so easily, and when they gazed at the porthole with faint smiles, they saw raindrops run down, trail after trail, as if the glass surface itself was beginning to dissolve, flowing away and dripping down; the rain of this island was ignorant of even the concept of cessation.
【Naomasa】 「Yeah. The storm, too.」

While the rain in the center of the atoll was more subdued, were one to leave the inlet and set for the open sea, a swirling storm still raged, and that had not subsided in the slightest since the Albatross had arrived at the island either; just thinking about that made him dread the prospect of all the hardships that awaited him when they would depart from the island. No matter how godlike the seamanship Kuro may demonstrate, it didn't change the fact that the ship would still be tossed about by the surging waves.

source.japanese: 加えてクロは、ここ数日の間何時にも増して不安定だ。島それ自体に怯え、あの怪しい、島からの声など聞こうものならころりと気絶する。何らかの因縁があるのか───
source.english: And Kuro had been more unstable than ever these past few days. The island itself frightened her; one hearing of that strange voice from it was enough to make her faint. Was there some connection…?

target.text: In addition, for these past few days, Kuro had been more unstable than she usually was. She feared the island itself, and upon hearing that eerie voice coming from the island, she would faint in a heartbeat. Was there some sort of connection───

source.japanese: 物想う、朔屋は横合いからのしんねりとした気配に横目に窺えば、クロが随分と気遣わしげに見つめてきているところ。紅い眸[ひとみ]で生真面目に真っ直ぐに。少しばかり気詰まりになって朔屋は、まだそんな頃合いではあるまいとは思いつつも、沈黙の谷間を繋ぐように、磨いたばかりの洋燈に火を点[とも]す、と、洋燈の明かりは意外に頼もしく暗がりを部屋の隅に追いやった。目が泥[なず]んでいたけれど、部屋は二人が思うよりずっと暗くなっていたらしい。
source.english: As Sakuya pondered, a persistent presence at his side made him glance over. Kuro was watching him with great concern, her red eyes earnest and direct. A little ill at ease, he lit the freshly polished lamp to bridge the silence, though he doubted it was late enough to need it. Its light drove the darkness to the cabin's corners with unexpected strength. Their eyes had grown dull. The room must have been much darker than either realized.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「結局水夫長は俺達の事、島に連れてってくれる気はないようだし、あーあ、どうにも退屈だ……」
source.english: “Looks like the bosun's got no intention of taking us ashore after all. Ahh, this is so boring…”

source.japanese: 舌打ち混じりに愚痴ったものだが、別にそこまで真からの恨み言ではない、のにクロがやにわ身を乗りだす。
source.english: He complained with a click of his tongue, without any particularly heartfelt resentment. Yet Kuro suddenly leaned forward.

target.text: Lost deep in his musings, when Sakuya peeked at the persistent presence by his flank with a sidelong glance, it turned out to be Kuro, who was watching him intently in an awfully anxious manner. Her crimson orbs stared directly at him with deep sincerity. And even having him inside her, though it was a greatly discomforting feeling she'd never felt before, if they did it again and again, then surely the shape within herself would grow familiar with Sakuya-san's─── And doing that, again and again, was bad? All the others would get angry? And maybe, just maybe, it was all her fault?

source.japanese: 白子の少女の中に、吐き戻す時の胃液のような苦く酸い不安がむらむら立ち籠めて、いてもたってもいられなくなる、みんなに、みんなに許してもらわないと───！
source.english: A bitter, sour anxiety—like stomach acid rising when one vomits—welled up inside the albino girl, making her unable to sit still. She had to be forgiven by everyone, by everyone—!

target.text: An anxiety as bitter and acidic as the gastric juices from when she would vomit suddenly shrouded the albino girl's insides; she could no longer just sit here, she had to find all the others, find them and beg their forgiveness───!

source.japanese: クロの眸[ひとみ]の赤が、不安、懼れ、そして焦燥と判りやすくくるくると変調して、朔屋が言葉を失ううちに、少女は寝台から滑り降り、踵を衝[つ]いた途端ずきんと下腹部に走った鈍痛に顔一層悲壮にして、飛びついたのが部屋の隅、少女自身は襤褸布やら空箱やらを積み上げて隠しているつもりだろうが全然隠し切れていない、鋲打ちの木箱、他の乗り組み達が『クロのお宝箱』と半笑いで尊称送るそれに、だ。
source.english: The red of Kuro's eyes wheeled visibly through anxiety, fear and desperation. While Sakuya stood speechless, she slid from the bed. The moment her heels struck the floor, pain stabbed through her lower belly; her face grew more tragic still. She flung herself toward a riveted wooden box in the corner, supposedly concealed beneath a pile of rags and empty cartons that concealed it not at all: the object the rest of the crew, with half a smile, dignified as ‘Kuro's Treasure Chest.’

target.text: The red of Kuro's eyes swung restlessly between obvious anxiety, fear, and agitation, and while Sakuya remained at a loss for words, the girl slid off her bed, but the moment her heel struck the floor, a dull pain throbbed in her lower abdomen, and her expression grew all the more tragic in its bravery; she leapt into a corner of the cabin, to the riveted wooden box, that which the girl herself had heaped tattered rags and empty boxes on top of in what was probably a doomed attempt at concealment, that which the other crew members reverently referred to as 『Kuro's Treasure Chest』, albeit with a faint smile on their faces.

source.japanese: お大事なのに、南京錠は壊れて鍵輪を引っかけているだけなのをもどかしく外して開けば中にはごたごたと、お弾きだの、摩耗した瓶の欠片だの、真鍮製の釦[ボタン]と思しき物、すべすべした滑石や少しばかり値打ち物そうなトンボ玉、夜店でよく売っている紛い物の指輪、鼈甲と見えてそうでない樹脂製の歯の欠けた櫛、砕けかかった桜貝の入った小瓶、等々、安っぽい光り物の見本としてあげられるような小物ばかりを襤褸布の上にぶちまけたのが呆れるほど沢山。
source.english: Precious though the box was to her, its padlock was broken and merely hooked in place. She fumbled it open. Inside lay a jumble of glass game counters, worn shards of bottle glass, something that might have been a brass button, pieces of smooth soapstone, a glass bead that looked to have a little value, a false ring of the sort sold at night markets, a resin comb masquerading as tortoiseshell with teeth missing, a tiny bottle containing a crumbling pink shell, and more besides. All these cheap glittering trifles had been spilled in astonishing profusion over a rag.

target.text: Despite her treating it as something so very precious, the padlock was broken, its shackle merely hooked in place, and after impatiently unhooking it and lifting the lid, inside was a cluttered jumble of contents: flat ohajiki glass pieces, abraded shards of glass bottles, something that looked like a brass button, and some smooth talc. (TN: Ohajiki, written "お弾き", is a traditional Japanese children's game similar to marbles, with the main difference being that the pieces are flatter, coin-shaped discs made of coloured glass or plastic.)

The only things that looked to be of any value, regardless of how insignificant that value was, were a glass bead, a counterfeit ring of the sort frequently sold at night fairs, a comb that looked like tortoiseshell but was actually made of resin and missing some teeth, a small bottle containing the partially-broken shell of a sakuragai, and so on, nothing but small items one would offer as examples of cheap, shiny things, dumped all over the tattered cloth in a heap of staggering size. (TN: A sakuragai, written "桜貝", is a Japanese tellin clam. It's informally known as a sakura shell, named after the vivid pink colour of its shell.)

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「お、お願いしてくる。みんなに、クロの宝物あげるるから、怒らないでて、いってくるよう……」
source.english: “I-I’ll go ask them. I’ll give everyone Kuro’s treasure and ask them not to get mad…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「落ち着けて、黙っとけばいいから、騒ぎを広めるなって。だいたいクロの宝物、みんな見向きもしないでないの」
source.english: “Calm down. Just keep quiet—don’t get everyone else stirred up over this. Besides, nobody even gives Kuro’s treasure a second glance, do they?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「W-, will go ask them nicely. Will give them all, all of Kuro's treasures, then will tell them to please not be angry……」
【Naomasa】 「Calm down, you just have to keep quiet about it, so don't make things worse by making a scene. It's not like anybody's interested in your treasures to begin with, Kuro.」

source.japanese: 転がりだした種々につい目が奪われて、見開いたものの、いずれも手に取るまでもなくガラクタと知れて、なんの烏の貯め込み屋だと苦笑に細められた、目はまたすぐに丸く、いや零れ落ちんばかりに瞠[みは]られる事になった。
source.english: The miscellany rolling across the floor caught Sakuya's eye. He stared, then recognized every piece as rubbish without needing to pick up a single one, and narrowed his eyes in a wry smile. What sort of magpie had amassed all this? A moment later his eyes rounded again—wider still, until they seemed ready to fall from his head.

target.text: He couldn't help but have his eyes drawn to the various thing scattered about, but though his eyes were wide open, he could tell all of it was junk without even bothering to pick any of it up; was she some kind of hoarding crow, he thought, narrowing his eyes with a wry smile, but soon enough, he was left saucer-eyed yet again, nay, his eyes opened so wide that they were on the verge of falling out of their sockets.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でもみんなが、島探してるのは、
　これだよ？」
source.english:
“But this is what everyone's looking for on the island,
isn't it?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But they're all searching the island for this, right?」

source.japanese: ガラクタの中で、それだけ別格なのか繻子の小巾着に収められていた。口緩めて掌に落とせば───
source.english: Unlike the other junk, this one had been kept in a little satin pouch, as if it belonged to a class apart. She loosened its mouth and let the contents fall into her palm.

source.japanese:
洋燈の大人しやかな明かりなど、たちまち霞んで色褪せた。室内に空の星が降りてきたかのようだった。太陽の光輝と月の幻想を混ぜ合わせてより貴[たっと]き光と為したかのようだった。
　太古の星と陽と月を封じこめて、自ら燃えていた。
　クロの掌の中で燃えていた。
source.english:
The oil lamp's modest glow dimmed and faded at once. A star from the sky seemed to have descended into the room. As though the sun's radiance and the moon's enchantment had been mingled into a nobler light.
It held the stars, sun and moon of antiquity sealed within itself, burning.
Burning in Kuro's palm.

target.text: Amidst the junk, as though it was special alone, was something kept within a drawstring pouch of satin. And when she loosened the string and dropped the contents into her palm───

The likes of the meek light from the lamp instantly grew dim and stale, dulled in colour. It was as if a star from the heavens had descended into the cabin. As if the radiant splendour of the sun and the illusory glow of the moon had been united, forming an even more precious, august light. It had sealed away the stars, sun, and moon of antiquity, burning entirely of its own accord. Burning in the palm of Kuro's hand.

source.japanese: ザウエル───
source.english: Zauer…

source.japanese: いと貴[たっと]き至宝よ───
source.english: O treasure beyond price…

source.japanese: もっとも軽んじられ、嘲笑される少女の掌の中で燃えて在れ───
source.english: Burn there, in the palm of the girl most despised and mocked…

target.text: Sauer───
O most priceless of treasures───
Blaze into existence within the palm of the girl most ridiculed and scorned by all───

source.japanese:
朔屋が椅子から派手に転がり落ちたのも無理はあるまい。あの漂流者が遺したモノは、そうそうに船の財産として換金されて、朔屋はあれほどの宝玉、もう二度とは見られまいと思っていたところにこれだ。
　
　しかも先のザウエルは同種の中でもまだ小物でぼんやりモノだったと言わんばかりに、クロが手にしているザウエルの方が一回りも大きく、光も強かった。
　
　輝きは瞼を閉じてなお暗闇の中に残る。
source.english:
No wonder Sakuya fell spectacularly out of his chair. The castaway's stone had promptly been sold for the ship's funds. He had thought he would never see such a jewel again.
And now this. The Zauer in Kuro's hand was a good deal larger, its light stronger, as if the first had been a dull and puny specimen of its kind.
Its brilliance remained in the dark even after he closed his eyes.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょっおとまてぇっ！　ななななんだってお前がこんなとこに。ああ、だからこないだ、あんなのたいしたことないって」
source.english: “W-wait a minute! W-what the hell are you doing with this here? Oh, so that's why you said the other one was nothing special…”

target.text: It was no wonder that Sakuya tumbled out of his chair with a loud crash. What that man cast adrift had left behind had quickly been exchanged for money to fill up the ship's coffers, and Sakuya was certain that he would never lay his eyes on a jewel like that ever again, and yet, here it was. Moreover, as though all but saying that the previous Sauer had been small and dim amongst its kind, the Sauer Kuro was holding in her hand was noticeably larger, and its shine was stronger to boot. Even after he closed his eyes, the brilliant glow lingered in the dark.
【Naomasa】 「Now hoooold on a second! W-w-w-why the hell do you have something like that in there?! Aah, so that's why, when you said it wasn't that special the other day!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロがいちばん初めに持ってたきらきら。
　他のよりずっときらきら。
　これならみんな、怒らない……」
source.english:
“Kuro's very first sparkly thing.
Much sparklier than the others.
With this, nobody'll be angry…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「い、いいからっ。これはお前が持っておき。
　さもなきャ俺が盗んで売り払いたい。
　───あ」
source.english:
“J-just keep it yourself.
Otherwise I'll want to steal it and sell it.
…Oh.”

source.japanese:
白子の少女は、自分が手の中に収まるくらいの珠一つで、この信天翁号など一〇隻……いや、何隻あっても足らないほどの至宝だとちゃんと認識しているのかどうか。
　ちょっとだけ惜しそうに見つめたけれど、その程度で手放せてしまうくらいの、他のガラクタよりはやや上等といわん程度の執着で、あっさりと、空恐ろしいほどあっさりと。
source.english:
Did the albino girl truly understand that this single stone, small enough to sit in her palm, was worth ten Albatrosses… no, however many one counted, it would not be enough?
She gazed at it with a trace of regret, but no more than that. Just enough attachment to suggest it was a little better than her other junk. And then she relinquished it with terrifying ease.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「This is Kuro's number one first ever sparkly. Much more sparkly than the rest. With this, the others won't be upset……」
【Naomasa】 「N-no, it's fine! You keep that for yourself. If you don't, I'll want to steal it and sell it off. ───Ah.」

The albino girl, with just that one pearl small enough to fit in her hand, could buy the likes of this Albatross ten times over……no, did she truly understand that this was a treasure so priceless that no amount of ships could ever hope to be enough? She stared at it with a tinge of regret, and after only that minor hesitation, nothing more than an attachment stemming from it being slightly superior to her other junk, she let go of it, readily, with such ease it scared him.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あげる、朔屋さんに」
source.english: “Here. For you, Mr. Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょ、きゃああ～～ああっっ!?」
source.english: “Wait—aaaaaah!?”

source.japanese:
あっさりと朔屋に差し出してきたものだから、青年は反射的に手を出して受け取ったものの、赤熱した金属片でも押しこまれたように絶叫し、握りこんでぶんぶん振り回してから、クロに押し戻した、それはもう焦りに焦り、必死を重ねた形相で。
　クロの手に戻してからも動揺の息収まらず、掌の方は灼[や]け爛[ただ]れ、はしていない、冷たい珠だったけれど、感触がしつこく残ったのにむしろ閉口した朔屋である。
　クロは受け取ったけれど、また朔屋にしつこくて渡そうとしたが、そんなものそうひょいひょい手にしていられたものではない、何より心臓に悪い。
source.english:
She held it out so readily that he accepted it by reflex, then screamed as though she had thrust red-hot metal into his hand. Clenching it, he waved his fist wildly before pressing it back upon her, his face frantic with desperation.
Even after returning it, he could not settle his breathing. His palm was not scorched or blistered. The stone had been cold, but its touch lingered so stubbornly that he found that worse.
Kuro took it, then persisted in trying to give it back. One could not casually handle such a thing. Above all, it was bad for the heart.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Will give it to Sakuya-san.」
【Naomasa】 「Wai-, KYAAA～～AH!?」

Because she held it out for Sakuya so casually, the young man reflexively took it, but he screamed as if he'd been handed a red-hot scrap of metal, and after gripping it tightly and swinging his fist about wildly, he pushed it back to Kuro, his face contorted into layers upon layers of sheer, frantic desperation.

Even after returning it to Kuro's hand, his agitated breathing would not calm, and his palm was burning and sore; no, it was but a pearl cold to the touch, but the sensation still stubbornly clung to his palm, which, if anything, only left Sakuya at his wits' end instead. While Kuro had accepted it back, she still stubbornly tried handing it back to Sakuya, but something like that shouldn't be handed over so lightly, and above all, it was bad for his heart.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「これで、朔屋さんがクロに入れても、怒られないなら。クロいらない」
source.english: “If that means no one will get angry even if Mr. Sakuya puts it in Kuro, then I don’t need it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだか話がずれてきてるだろうがそれは。
　いいよ、いいからお前が持っておけって。
　何時かは役に立つかも知れないし、それに、
　みんなが血眼で探してるのを、
　お前が持ってるのはなかなか愉快だ」
source.english:
“We're getting off the point here. It's fine.
Just keep it, will you? It might be useful someday.
Besides,
there's something pretty funny about you having the thing everyone's
tearing their hair out looking for.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はは……っ。それで笑えちまうんだから、俺も大概だ。しかしお前、それ、どこで手に入れたのよ」
source.english: “Ha… I'm a real piece of work myself, finding that funny. But where did you get it?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「If with this, even if Sakuya-san puts it inside Kuro, they won't get angry. Then Kuro doesn't need it.」

【Naomasa】 「I feel like we're getting off track here. It's okay, that's enough, you just keep it. You never know when it might come in handy, and besides, that the thing they're all desperately searching for, their eyes bloodshot, is actually in your possession, now that is a very amusing thought.」
【Naomasa】 「Haha……. And I guess I'm a nasty piece of work myself, laughing at this. But seriously, where did you get your hands on that?」

source.japanese:
朔屋、クロの手を取って、握りこませて、大地の精髄を押し戻しながら、この青年にしては珍しく快活な笑いを零していた。
　財宝の価値は限度を越えており、かえって朔屋に所有欲を与えず、船内でも立場のない少女がそれを所有していた事に、たまらない可笑しみのみをもたらしたのである。
　他人に優るところ何一つ持たず、阿呆よ馬鹿よと嘲罵されるのが習い性になっている朔屋が、超越して貴い、一つの勝利を得た瞬間でもあった。宝玉を廻って、その誘惑を幻惑され、幾多の血さえ流された事だって在ったのだから。
source.english:
Sakuya took Kuro's hand and closed her fingers around it, pressing back the essence of the earth with a cheerful laugh rare for him.
The treasure's value exceeded all bounds and, perversely, aroused no wish to possess it. All it brought him was irresistible amusement that the girl with no standing aboard should own it.
Sakuya, who excelled at nothing and had grown accustomed to being jeered at as an idiot and a fool, had won a single victory of transcendent worth. Much blood had been shed over precious stones, after all, under their tempting, bewildering spell.

target.text: While taking Kuro's hand in his, making it squeeze tight, pushing the pith of the earth back to her, Sakuya let out a cheerful laugh, one quite unusual for this young man. The value of this treasure exceeded any and all bounds, but that did not give Sakuya any desire to possess it; on the contrary, that a girl, and one with no standing aboard even this ship at that, had ownership of it, now that brought him an irresistible joy.

To Sakuya, a man possessed not of a single thing in which he excelled over others, to whom it was second nature to be mocked as a simpleton, a fool, this was transcendental, priceless; it was even a moment in which he had finally achieved a single victory. For many had been fascinated by the allure of this gem, and much blood had been shed over it.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うう、わかんない……。
　クロがたぶん、始めから持ってたんだとおもう。他のきらきらもたくさん集めたけど、こんなきらきら、無かったから」
source.english:
“I don't know…
Kuro probably had it from the start, I think. Kuro collected lots of other sparkly things, but nothing sparkled like this.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「よくわからんが、ちょっとだけ胸がすっとしたな。でも焦ったら、なんか喉が渇いちまった。飲み物でも盗りに、いや、取りに行ってくるか」
source.english: “Don't quite get it, but I feel a little better. All that excitement's made me thirsty, though. I'll go and steal—I mean, get—something to drink.”

source.japanese:
ザウエルを、剥き出しにされているとなにやらいたたまれない気持ちになってくるのでしまわせて、朔屋がようやっとついた吐息の、どれだけ安堵に満ちていた事か。
　昂奮したら喉が渇いたし、酒の酔いで洗わない事には、舌が他の船員達のいる前でザウエルという単語をばらしかねない。
　何より強い光を見続けて、気分が不安定になった。無尽蔵の富もたらす宝玉より、一杯の強い酒が欲しい。
source.english:
He made her put the Zauer away. Having it out in the open made him oddly uncomfortable. What relief filled the breath he finally released. His excitement had left him thirsty.
Unless he washed it away in a drunken haze, his tongue might let slip the word Zauer in front of the other sailors.
More than anything, looking at that strong light for so long had unsettled him. He wanted a glass of strong liquor more than a jewel promising limitless wealth.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uuh, don't know……. Kuro thinks, probably had it to begin with. Gathered many other sparklies, but nothing as sparkly as this one.」
【Naomasa】 「Can't say I'm following, but I am feeling pretty satisfied right now. But after getting so worked up, my throat's gotten dry. Guess I'll go stea-, no, grab something to drink.」

Whenever the Sauer was on open display, he felt like he was being seized by some kind of desire to be anywhere else, unable to just sit there, so he made her put it away, and Sakuya was finally able to breathe a sigh of relief; and what relief it must have been filled with.

After getting so agitated, his throat had grown dry, and if he didn't wash that thirst away with the intoxication of drink, it wasn't hard to imagine that the word "Sauer" would slip off his tongue while he was with the other sailors. And most of all, after having stared at that bright glare for so long, his mood had grown unstable. He would much rather have a glass of strong liquor than some jewel that would bring him inexhaustible wealth.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロが行く！　朔屋さんはお酒がいいよね。
　食べるのもいっしょに、もてくるよ」
source.english:
“Kuro'll go! You want liquor, don't you, Mr.
Sakuya? Kuro'll bring food too.”

source.japanese:
クロ、朔屋の痰が絡んだような荒れた声にはっと顔を上げ、にっこり綻ばせた。
　朔屋は「入れる」のを躊躇ったし、クロが一番大事にしている石も受け取ってもらえなくって、もう何も思いつかなくて途方に暮れていたところ。
　自分でもできそうな事があるのは嬉しい、それが青年の望んでいる事なら、尚更。
source.english:
At the scrape of Sakuya's phlegmy voice, Kuro looked up sharply and blossomed into a smile.
He had hesitated to ‘put it in,’ and he had refused even the stone she treasured above everything else. With no other idea left to her, she had been quite at a loss. The discovery of something she might actually do delighted her—more so if it was what he wanted.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro will go! Sakuya-san wants alcohol, right? Will bring some food back, too.」

Upon hearing Sakuya's rough voice, which sounded as though it was covered in phlegm, Kuro raised her head with a start, breaking into a broad grin. Sakuya had been hesitant to "put it inside" her, and he wouldn't take the stone Kuro cherished most; just as she could no longer think of anything, at a complete loss at what to do. She was glad that there was something that even she herself could probably do, and if it was something the young man desired, then all the more so.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「火は使わせてもらえないけど、切ったり、ちぎったりはできるから」
source.english: “They won't let Kuro use the fire, but Kuro can cut things and tear things up.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「They won't let Kuro use fire, but can cut, and tear things up.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だから、待っててね。いないくなってたり、しないでね」
source.english: “So wait here, okay? Don't… don't go away.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「So, please wait for Kuro. Don't disappear, or anything like that, please?」

source.japanese: 止める間もなく厨房にと駆け出す、クロの背中に舞う白の髪も、主の心境あらわしてか勢いよくたなびいて。
source.english: Before he could stop her, she dashed off toward the galley. The white hair dancing down her back streamed with vigor, as if expressing its owner's feelings.

target.text: Without even giving him a chance to stop her, Kuro broke into a run towards the galley, and the white hair fluttering around Kuro's back, as if to express its master's state of mind, billowed with great spirit.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あいつ……俺がザウエルかっぱらうとか、考えてないのかね。
　おまけにやけに世話焼きたがる」
source.english:
“That girl… doesn’t she think I might steal the Zauer or something?
On top of that, she’s awfully eager to look after me.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おいまさかこれ……有り得るのか、俺みたいなんになびくなんてのは」
source.english: “Hey, wait—could this really be… Is it even possible that she could fall for someone like me?”

source.japanese: クロが自分に好意を、しかも少女が年上の青年に甘え懐くような、他愛ない『好き』ではなく、もっとしっかりと女としての芯が通った好意を寄せているのでは───まさか。一度抱いたくらいで───？　けれど当然のようにクロは初体験であったし、娘にとってそれは大きな意味をもつ行為であるとは聞いている、けれど、と何やらいたたまれなくなる朔屋のいさぎわるいことこの上ない。
source.english: Could Kuro feel something for him—not the harmless affection with which a younger woman might cling to an older man, but desire with a woman's firm center to it? Surely not. Not merely because he had slept with her once—? Yet it had been her first time, and he had heard that such an act could mean a great deal to a woman. Yet, yet—Sakuya squirmed away from the thought with consummate cowardice.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「That girl……I guess the thought never even crossed her mind, that I might swipe the Sauer. And on top of that, she's being awfully eager about taking care of my needs.」
【Naomasa】 「Oi, there's no way that this…… is it possible? What is there even to be swayed by in a guy like me?」

That Kuro held an affection for him, and moreover, not the sort of trivial, innocent『like』of a young girl acting spoiled and growing attached to a young man her senior; rather, she harboured a much more steadfast affection, firmly rooted in her womanhood───she couldn't possibly. From making love to her just once───? But he had shared Kuro's first experience with her as if it was a matter of course, and he had heard that, for a girl, it was an act that carried a great significance, but; such were the thoughts running through Sakuya's head while he was growing immensely uncomfortable: a man peerless in his lack of gallantry.

source.japanese:
ところがその後、待てど暮らせど、クロはいっかな戻ってくる気配がない。
　ザウエルの一件があるだけに、朔屋は厭な予感を抱いた、こんな悪い予感なぞ杞憂であってくれと祈りながら、様子を見に行くことにする。
source.english:
But she did not return. He waited and waited, with no sign of Kuro.
The affair of the Zauer gave him a nasty foreboding. Praying it would prove groundless, he went to see what had happened.

target.text: Nevertheless, after this, no matter how long he waited, Kuro showed no signs of returning. Sakuya had a bad feeling about this, all the more so because there had just been that incident with the Sauer, and while praying that his premonition would turn out to be but an unfounded worry, he set off to check on her.

source.japanese:
───顔の骨が。
　金属板でも嵌めこまれたように、硬く引き攣[つ]って、骨自体からずくんずくんと響いてくるようなこれは、痛みだ。
　あまりの恐怖がもたらす、幻のように実態がない癖に、心にも体にも抉[えぐ]りこんでるような痛みで───
source.english:
The bones of her face.
They had tightened as though metal plates had been fitted inside them. Deep within the bones something throbbed and throbbed: pain.
Pain born of overwhelming terror, insubstantial as a phantom, yet gouging into both mind and body.

source.japanese:
強張っているのは顔だけでない。四肢が、関節が、内臓さえも。ぎちぎちと軋みきりきりと締まり、ねじくれる。
　今や彼女の身体は彼女の思い通りに動かせず、それどころか拘束する檻となり───
　
　髪だって、雨に濡れて重たくよじれ、目を打ちつける陰険な鞭だ。服も、足にまとわりつき腕に絡みつき、死にもの狂いの手足掻きを嘲笑っては邪魔しにかかる。
source.english:
Not only her face had seized up. Limbs, joints, even her organs cramped and creaked, tightened and twisted.
Her body no longer obeyed her; it had become a cage that bound her. Even her hair,
heavy and tangled with rain, was a malicious whip striking her eyes. Her clothes clung to her legs and wound about her arms, obstructing her frantic struggle as though mocking it.

source.japanese: 彼女の身体や、身に着けているものだけではない。不器用なりに歩き慣れて、何時もだったら駆けっこだってできる上甲板は今や凝固した溶岩地帯、見知った筈の道具箱やバラックの角が、高低の段差がばらばらと組み変わり、角も角度か鋭角から鈍角に突如変じたように、曲がろうとして曲がりきれず、あちこち転がった綱[ロープ]などは死してなお動き止めない亡者の蛇、足首に巻きついては締めつけ───
source.english: It was not merely her body and her clothes. The upper deck, which she knew well enough to run across despite her clumsiness, had become a field of hardened lava. Familiar toolboxes, the corners of shacks, changes in level all seemed to rearrange themselves at random. Angles shifted suddenly from sharp to obtuse; she tried to turn and failed. Ropes lying about were dead serpents that had not ceased moving, coiling about her ankles and tightening…

source.japanese: 恐怖の根源は、彼女の内部に発生する内在的なものではものではなく、島から滅々と運ばれてくるこの雨や、あるいはあの奇怪な誦唱によってもたらされるものですらなく、クロの背後に厳然と存在する人影にあり───
source.english: The source of her terror was not something rising within herself. Nor was it the rain borne mournfully from the island, or even that uncanny chanting. It was the figure that stood unmistakably behind Kuro.

source.japanese:
恐怖に千々に引き裂かれた心の破片の一つ一つに、背後の影が存在し、いやましに膨れあがり、クロの息さえも圧迫していく、視界が揺れる、舞い踊る、もうなにが見えているのかも判らない、目に映るぐちゃぐちゃのどろどろは船の上甲板の気色なのか、目に流れこんできた脂汗と冷や汗と、そして涙の混淆物なのか。
　
　心は発狂せんばかりに焦り乱れているのに、もう足が、身体が動かない、もうほとんど四つ這いに、犬のように舌を出して喘[あえ]ぎ喘[あえ]ぎ、それでも辛うじて前に進んでいた身体に、強い衝撃の、足先から。
source.english:
Every fragment of her terror-shattered mind contained that shadow behind her. It swelled ever larger, constricting even her breath. Her vision shook and danced. She no longer knew what she was seeing. Was that murky, muddled mess the upper deck, or the mixture of greasy sweat, cold sweat and tears running into her eyes?
Her mind raced in a frenzy bordering on madness, but her legs, her body would scarcely move. Almost on all fours, she panted with her tongue out like a dog. Still she barely managed to creep forward—until a violent shock struck her from the tips of her feet.

target.text: ───Her facial bones. As though a metal plate had been wedged inside, were stiff and seizing up, and a deep throb reverberated from within the bone itself; this was pain. Produced by terror beyond her means to handle, and despite being like an illusion, lacking any real substance, it brought with it a pain that felt like it was gouging into both mind and body───

It was not just her face that had stiffened. Her limbs, her joints, even her viscera. Creaking and groaning and tightening, twisting. The girl's body would no longer obey her commands; on the contrary, it had become a cage that constrained her─── Even her hair, wet in the rain, heavy and tangled, was a wily whip lashing at her eyes. And her clothes, too, clung to her legs and coiled around her arms, mocking the desperate struggle of her limbs, sabotaging her efforts.

It was not just her body, or the things she was wearing on it either. She had grown experienced with walking in her own clumsy way, but the upper deck, which she could usually even sprint across, was now a region of solidified lava; the toolboxes and corners of the shacks that she ought to recognize by sight were rearranged in a chaotic mix of elevations, and the corners, too, felt as if they abruptly changed angles from acute to obtuse; even when she tried to turn a corner, she was unable to, and the ropes scattered all over the deck, like deceased snakes that continued to slither on even in death, wrapped around her ankles, squeezing───

The source of her fear was not something internal that arose from within the girl, nor was it this bleak rain drifting dismally from the island, and neither was it even something brought about by that ominous recitation; it was the shadowy figure looming gravely behind Kuro's back───

Within each and every one of the thousands of splinters that her heart had been torn into by the terror, the shadow behind her was present, swelling ever more; even Kuro's breath was being suppressed, her vision swayed, it danced, she couldn't even tell what she was looking at anymore; was the chaotic, muddy slush that met her eyes the state of the ship's upper deck, or was it a mixture of the greasy and cold sweat that had flowed into her eyes, as well as tears she had yet to shed?

Her heart was beating in such disarrayed panic that her last thread of sanity was about to snap, she could no longer move her legs, her body, she was now crawling on her hands and feet, tongue sticking out like a dog, panting and groaning; still, her body just barely inched forward, and then, she felt a powerful impact, starting from the tips of her toes.

source.japanese: 恐慌に混乱を来[きた]した身体が、普段の四肢感覚を失い、いつもは跨[また]いでいるはずの段差に躓いたらしかった。だがクロには、背後の人影が底意地悪く背中を押してきたようにしか考えられず、爪先だけではなく背中にも衝撃を受けたとしか思えなかった。
source.english: Her panic-stricken body had lost its ordinary sense of its own limbs; she had apparently tripped on a step she would usually have stepped over. But Kuro could only believe that the figure behind her had spitefully shoved her in the back. She was certain the blow had struck her back as well as her toes.

target.text: Her body, brought to a state of chaos from the terror, had lost normal sensation in its limbs, and it seemed she had stumbled over a bump that she would always step over. But to Kuro, all that ran through her mind was that the figure looming over her back must have maliciously pushed her from behind, she could only feel it as an impact coming not just from her toes, but her back as well.

source.japanese: 身体がふっと軽くなったと思ったのも刹那、宙を泳いで支えを求める手は空しくひらひら、死ぬ寸前の蝶のよう、末期の蝶と同じで地に落ちた、じくじくと濡れた上甲板にばたばたと哀しく羽ばたいて、舞い上がる事叶わないのも同じ。
source.english: For an instant her body felt light. Her hands fluttered vainly in the air, seeking support, like a butterfly about to die. Like that dying butterfly, she fell to the ground. Fluttered miserably upon the sodden upper deck. And could not rise.

source.japanese:
クロは恐怖にがっちりと掌握されてしまっていた。
　見張りの下級水夫の交替の隙を突き、彼女にしては手際よく酒と食い物を手に入れていたのに、何故雨の様子を見に上甲板に出てみようなどと考えてしまったのだろう。
　せっかく手に入れた麻袋の中の酒の瓶は、身が投げ出された弾みで離れたところに落ちて、砕ける音を立てたのが哀しい、悔しい、だがそんな事よりも、今はただひたすらに───
source.english:
Terror held Kuro firmly in its grasp.
She had seized the moment when the junior sailors on watch changed shifts, obtaining drink and food with unusual efficiency. Why had she then thought to go up on deck to see how the rain was doing?
The bottle in the sack she had secured fell some distance away as her body was flung down. The sound of it breaking was sad, frustrating. But more than any of that, now, simply…

target.text: The feeling that her body had suddenly grown lighter also lasted but a fleeting moment; she sailed through the air, her hands futilely flapping about in search of support, like a butterfly on the verge of death, and just like a butterfly meeting its end, she also fell to the ground; flapping her wings miserably atop the slick upper deck, her wish to soar into the skies also to be granted nevermore.

Kuro was clenching her fists tightly in fear. She'd taken advantage of the short gap that formed when the deck boys on watch duty were changing shifts, and had managed to, for someone like her, adroitly obtain some drink and food, so how come she still ended up having the bright idea to head out on the upper deck to check on the rain? As her body was thrown on the floor, the impact made the hemp bag containing the bottle of alcohol she'd gone to such lengths to get fall to the floor some distance away; the sound of the bottle breaking was miserable, frustrating, but more importantly, right now, all she had on her mind was───

source.japanese: ───恐ろしい───
source.english: Terrifying.

target.text: ───Terrifying───

source.japanese:
転んだ際に打ちつけたのは、顎の先か肘か掌か、それとも全部か、ずきずきとてんでばらばらに痛んでどこからどこまでが痛みの核なのか判らない、それに痛みより恐怖の方がクロを衝[つ]き動かして、甲板の上に体をどうにか直したのだがもう遅い。
　人影はもうクロが逃げようのない間境を踏み越えていた。
source.english:
What had she struck when she fell? The tip of her chin, an elbow, a palm—all of them? Separate aches throbbed here and there, until she could not tell where the pain began or ended. But fear drove her harder than pain. She somehow righted herself upon the deck. Too late.
The figure had already come too close for Kuro to escape.

source.japanese:
【影】
『───まさか───おまえなのか───』
source.english: ‘Impossible… Is it you…?’

target.text: Was it the tip of her chin, her elbow, or her palms she banged against the deck when she fell; perhaps it was all of them, the throbbing pain was fragmented and diffuse, leaving her unable to tell where the source of the pain began and ended, but what roused Kuro was the terror, not the pain, and she somehow managed to pull herself to her feet on the deck, however; it was already too late. The shadowy figure had stepped across the boundary from which Kuro was no longer permitted escape.
【Shadow】 『───Can it truly be───you───』

source.japanese: 人影は、裾や袖[そで]なとあちこちがぼろぼろにほつれた長衣を纏[まと]っていたのだが、そのほつれ解けた輪郭の端々が、上甲板を閉ざし始めた雨の夕闇と溶け合い、得体の知れない影を引きずって歩むかのよう。
source.english: The figure wore a robe whose hem and sleeves were ragged and frayed. Its unraveling edges merged with the rainy dusk beginning to close over the upper deck, as though he walked dragging an unfathomable shadow.

target.text: The figure was clad in a long robe, its hems and sleeves and every which part tattered and frayed all over, but the edges of that frayed silhouette melted into the twilight rain that had begun to cover the upper deck, and it almost seemed to be walking forwards as though dragging with it an inscrutable shadow.

source.japanese:
【影】
『よもや───ここに戻ってきておったとは』
source.english: ‘To think… you had returned here.’

source.japanese:
人影は、長衣の頭巾を目深に引き被り、よじれた髪の端や顎の先くらいしか見えず、衣の裡[うち]から暗く虚ろに、なのに澱[よど]んだ声を響かせる。
　その、声だ───
　その声こそ、信天翁号が島に着いた日、そしてクロが朔屋と肌を重ねた直後に腐ったような風に運ばれ来たった、途切れ途切れの声そのものであり。
source.english:
The figure had pulled the hood of his robe low over his face, revealing only the tips of his tangled hair and the tip of his chin, and a dark, hollow, yet murky voice echoed from within the robe.
 That voice—it was the very same broken, intermittent voice carried on a putrid breeze the day the Albatross reached the island, and again immediately after Kuro and Sakuya had made love.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あ～～～っっ！　やーーーーっ、
　ごな、ごないでぇぇっっ！」
source.english:
“Aaaah! Noooo! Don't,
don't come neeeear!”

source.japanese:
【影】
『何故、儂の元に戻らぬ───』
source.english: ‘Why do you not return to me…?’

source.japanese:
クロはおよそ知らざる相手だというのに、あちらは彼女を知っている口ぶりなのが、忌まわしい、恐ろしい、心が千切れてしまいそう。
　けれど───クロは本当に知らないのだろうか。
　人影が少女をここまで強烈に恐れさせ狂乱させるのは、クロの記憶のどこかにこの姿が遺されていたからではないだろうか。
source.english:
Though Kuro had no knowledge of the man, he spoke as if he knew her. It was hateful, terrifying; her heart felt ready to tear itself apart.
But—did Kuro truly not know him?
Could this shadow have driven her into such terror and frenzy unless some trace of him remained in her memory?

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「し、しんな、しんないいいい、
　クロ、あんたなんか───
　いいいいっ、来ないでええーーーっ」
source.english:
“I don't, don't knooow!
Kuro doesn't know you!
Eeeee! Don't come neeeear!”

source.japanese:
人影が、足取りとも思えない、奇妙に粘ついた動きで、なのに滑らかな、不気味な動きで前に出る。
　あたりは一面宵闇に覆われてきているというのに、長衣の輪郭から伸びる影はより濃さを増し、長さを伸ばしてクロへと迫る、卑猥で汚怪な触腕のように。
source.english:
The figure advanced with a strangely clinging motion that scarcely seemed a gait at all, yet smooth and uncanny.
Dusk was covering everything around them, but the shadow stretching from his robe grew darker and longer as it reached toward Kuro, like an obscene, foul tentacle.

target.text: 【Shadow】 『Never did I dream───that you would return to this place.』

The shadowy figure had the hood of its robe pulled low over its eyes, only showing the tips of its tangled hair and the point of its chin, and from within the robes, a dark, hollow, and yet hoarse voice echoed forth. It was that voice─── That very voice, that was what had arrived as if carried on putrid winds on the day the Albatross had arrived at the island, as well as right after Kuro had made love to Sakuya; it was that very same fragmented voice.
【Kuro】 「AA～～～! NOOーーーー, DON'T, DON'T COME CLOSEEER!」
【Shadow】 『Why have you not returned to my side───』

He was an entirely unknown man to Kuro, and yet he spoke as if he knew her; it was abominable, terrifying, her heart felt as if it would be torn to shreds. But───did Kuro truly not know? That this shadowy figure would induce in her so intense a fear and frenzy, could it not be because this form was left behind somewhere within Kuro's memories, lingering?
【Kuro】 「D-, DON-, DON'T KNOOOOW, KURO, SOMEONE LIKE YOU─── HIIIH, DON'T COME ANY CLOSEEERーーー」

The shadowy figure, in what didn't even resemble steps, with an oddly glutinous motion yet smooth all the same, advanced with uncanny movements. Though the surroundings were entirely shrouded in the dark of twilight, the shadow stretching out from the robe's silhouette grew even darker; it extended in length, and like obscene and vile tentacles, drew nearer to Kuro.

source.english: ‘Have you forgotten…?’

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「しんない、しんない、
　クロ、なにも、なんにも、だぅ、あっ」
source.english:
“Don't know, don't know.
Kuro doesn't know… anything, nothing… ah, ah!”

source.japanese:
【影】
『───見つけたのか───』
source.english: ‘Have you found it…?’

source.japanese:
【影】
『儂が命じたもの───
　渇望して止まぬもの───
　見つけたのか───』
source.english:
‘What I demanded…
What I ceaselessly crave…
Have you found it…?’

source.japanese:
影を濃く纏い、なのにその輪郭はクロの恐怖が増すにつれてはっきりと、人影は信天翁号の面々が木造の島にて出会い、連れ来たったあの老人の。
　宛がった部屋からいつの間にか姿を消していたあの老人の。
　何処へ潜[ひそ]んでいたのか、それが明らかになったところでクロの恐怖が減ずるとは思われず、ただ老人は白子の少女の異常なまでの恐怖の象徴として、影を引きずり、迫る。
source.english:
Though steeped in shadow, the figure grew clearer as Kuro's terror mounted. It was the old man the Albatross company had met on the wooden island and brought aboard.
The old man who had disappeared, unseen,
