from the room assigned him. Knowing where he had been hiding would scarcely have lessened Kuro's terror. He merely approached, dragging his shadow as the embodiment of the albino girl's abnormal fear.

target.text: 【Shadow】 『───Did you forget?───』
【Kuro】 「DONKNOW, DONKNOW, Kuro knows nothing at all, ah!」
【Shadow】 『───Did you find it?───』
【Shadow】 『What I ordered you to─── What I never cease to crave─── Did you find it?───』

Shadow clung to him deeply, and yet as Kuro's terror intensified, his outline grew clearer in turn; the shadowy figure was none other than the man the crew of the Albatross had met on that island of wooden make, that old man they'd brought back with them. He who had suddenly disappeared from the room they had assigned him, that old man. Just where had he been lurking? It was difficult to imagine that Kuro's terror would subside once she knew, and acting as the symbol of the albino girl's paralyzing fear, dragging his shadow behind him, this old man simply loomed closer and closer.

source.japanese: 地に伸びる影が膨れあがり、クロを覆っていくそれだけで少女は、心が砕けんばかりの恐ろしさに見舞われ、今や発狂死寸前の。
source.english: The shadow upon the deck swelled and covered Kuro. That alone brought a terror that threatened to shatter her mind. She was all but at the point of dying mad.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あー、あーー、あー……っ、
　クロは、知らない、ばかだから、
　なんも、みつからない……、
　うあーーーっっ」
source.english:
“Aaah, aaah…
Kuro doesn't know. Kuro's stupid,
so… can't find anything…
Aaaaah!”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「んぎっ!?　い、げっ、おぶぇぇっっ」
source.english: “Nggh!? G-gah… urgh!”

source.japanese:
老人がなにを求めているのか、なにをそこまで渇望しているのか、見当もつかないクロは、ただ逃げ場を求めて、手足をばたつかせるも、神経の接続が切れてしまったようにまともに動いてなどくれやしない。
　大体既に腰が抜けており、立ち上がる事もならず尻で地を不様に掻[か]くだけ、しかももう背後にはバラックの壁。
source.english:
Kuro had no idea what the old man sought, what he craved so fiercely. She flailed her limbs, looking only for escape, but they refused to move properly, as though their nerve connections had been severed. Her legs had already given way.
Unable to stand, she could only scrape backward awkwardly on her bottom. Behind her now stood the wall of a shack.

target.text: The shadow extending across the deck swelled in size, and just being covered by it was enough for the girl's mind to be on the brink of shattering, such terror was she struck by, on the verge of going mad and dying any moment now.
【Kuro】 「Aー, Aーー, aー……, Kuro is stupid, so doesn't know, didn't find anything……, uaahーーー!」
【Kuro】 「NGH!? Iih, grh, bleeegh!」

What was it the old man wanted, what was it he craved so desperately? Having not the first idea, Kuro simply sought escape, but for all that she tried to flail her limbs around, as though the synapses in her nerves had been cut, they refused to properly move. Her knees had already given out under her, and unable to even rise to her feet, she could only clumsily scoot backwards along the deck on her butt, and yet she already had her back against the wall of a shack.

source.japanese:
がつごつと、肉の薄い背中に青痣こしらえかねない執拗さで背後の壁と後ずさり続けるのだが、老人は意にも介せず進み出て、ついにはクロをその影の中に呑みこんでいく。
　ただ老人の影を受けたそれだけで、クロの恐怖はまた更なる段階を迎えたようで、口の中で引きつけていた舌が勝手に暴れ回り、顎もがたがたと痙攣する、その合間に舌が噛みこまれてしまって、ぞぶりと歯が食いこんでしまって、くぐもる悲鳴、零れる血涎れ、クロは、クロは、口元を抑えていやいやと首を振るのだけれど、老人の歩みは止まらない、止めてくれない。
source.english:
Thump, thump. She kept backing into it with a persistence that threatened to bruise her thinly padded back. The old man advanced without a care, finally engulfing her in his shadow.
That mere contact seemed to carry Kuro's terror to another stage. Her tongue, already convulsing in her mouth, thrashed of its own accord. Her jaw shook. Between its spasms, her tongue was caught. Teeth sank wetly into it. A muffled scream, bloody saliva spilling out. Kuro, Kuro pressed a hand to her mouth and shook her head, no, no. But the old man did not stop. Would not stop.

target.text: She continued to retreat into the wall, banging against it with a persistence that was like to leave bruising on her skinny back, but the old man cared not in the slightest for her plight as he moved forwards, and at last, he began to swallow Kuro within that shadow of his.

Just receiving the touch of the old man's shadow alone was enough for Kuro's terror to reach new heights; her convulsing tongue began to thrash around inside her mouth of its own accord, her jaw rattled as spasms ran through it, and between the two, she bit her tongue, her teeth digging deeply into it with a wet sound, a stifled scream, dripping blood-tinged saliva, Kuro, Kuro was───clenching her mouth shut and swinging her neck back and forth in rejection, yet the old man's advance did not stop, it would not be stopped.

source.japanese:
【老人】
『情け、なや……』
source.english: ‘Pathetic…’

source.japanese:
無情に吐き捨て、迫る。
　老人の身体が、クロに覆い被さっていく。
　クロの両目が、瞳だけでなく白い部分までもが血走って、今にも毛細血管が裂けてしまいそう。
source.english:
He spat the word mercilessly and drew closer.
His body loomed over Kuro.
Her eyes were bloodshot, not merely the irises but the whites as well, as if the tiny vessels would burst at any moment.

target.text: 【Shadow】 『How pathetic……』

He spat at her heartlessly, drawing closer. The old man's body began to loom over and cover Kuro's own. It wasn't just her pupils, even the whites of Kuro's eyes were the colour of blood, capillaries on the verge of bursting at any moment.

source.japanese:
【老人】
『───告げよ───我に』
source.english: ‘Tell me…’

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うーっ、う～～～っっ！　
　ぶぇぇ……」
source.english:
“Uuh! Uuuuh!
Ugh…”

source.japanese:
酷薄に強要し、更に迫る。腰を二つ折りにして、クロの顔を覗きこむ。
　クロは唇の端から血涎、拭う事もできず、純然たる恐怖で舌を強ばらせ、せめて視線だけでも逸らそうとするのだけれど、どうしてか目は老人に釘付けされて離れない、その上、身体の中でぴしぴしとなにかが引き剥がされるような音までが、眼球にも響くような。恐怖の余り硬直した身体の、細かな靱帯が引きちぎれる音だろうか。
source.english:
He insisted cruelly, coming closer still. Bent double, he peered into her face.
Bloody saliva ran from her lips; she could not wipe it away. Pure terror had stiffened her tongue. She tried at least to avert her gaze, but somehow her eyes remained pinned to him. And inside her body, sharp little tearing sounds seemed to echo even in her eyeballs. Was that the sound of fine ligaments snapping in a body rigid with fear?

source.japanese:
【老人】
『使命───果たさぬ限り───』
source.english: ‘Until you fulfill your mission…’

source.japanese:
【老人】
『お前は───どこにも───降りられぬ』
source.english: ‘You can land… nowhere.’

source.japanese:
今や老人は、クロと頭巾の縁を擦り合わせんばかりに肉迫し、彼女の鼻先で、怪鳥の鉤爪を思わせる、汚れて尖った爪の先を陰険に蠢かせる。
　それだけでクロは、心臓どころか自分の存在の一番の核、魂まで爪で削られたような激痛が、全身に走り、ついに。
source.english:
The old man was so close now that the edge of his hood nearly brushed her. Before her nose he maliciously stirred the dirty, pointed tips of his nails, like a monstrous bird's talons.
That alone sent agony through Kuro's entire body. Not merely her heart, but the very core of her existence, her soul, seemed to have been scraped by those nails. At last…

source.japanese:
【老人】
『お前は───永久に───』
source.english: ‘You shall remain… forever…’

source.japanese:
【老人】
『かつての翼失い───
　その不様な姿のままで───』
source.english:
‘Your former wings lost…
In that wretched shape…’

source.japanese:
そしてクロは、老人の呪詛の言葉を最後に、なにもかも判らなくなった。紅い眸[ひとみ]が、かくんと虚脱して焦点を失った。あまりの衝撃、押し寄せる恐怖に神経の接続が狂い、認識から外界が遮断されたのだ。
　目は開いているものの───なにも見ていない。
　口は緩く開いて、何事か微かに呟いているものの、声は言葉を為さず、舌の縺[もつ]れる。ただ見苦しく涎を垂れ流させる───
source.english:
With the old man's curse, Kuro ceased to understand anything at all. Her red eyes went slack and lost their focus. The shock, the flood of terror had disordered her nerve connections, cutting the outer world off from her awareness.
Her eyes remained open, but saw nothing.
Her mouth hung loosely open, faintly muttering something, but the sounds formed no words. Her tongue tangled. Only drool ran foully from her lips.

source.japanese: クロに覆い被さる、まさに寸前で、上甲板の向こうから跫音が伝わって来て、老人は頭巾の裡[うち]で聞き苦しい舌打ちの音を立てると、また影の中に溶けこむように消えていった。
source.english: Just as he was about to lean over Kuro, footsteps came from the far side of the upper deck. An ugly click of the tongue sounded within his hood. Then the old man vanished again, as though dissolving into the shadows.

target.text: 【Shadow】 『───Speak───unto me.』
【Kuro】 「Uーkh, uh～～～! Bweeeh……」

Cruelly coercive, drawing ever nearer. Bent in half at the hips, peering into Kuro's face. Kuro could not even wipe off the blood-tinged saliva hanging from the corner of her mouth, for the pure terror had stiffened her tongue; at the very least she could avert her gaze from his, but for some reason, her eyes were riveted to the old man, incapable of separating from him, and on top of that, there was even the sound of something breaking within her body, as though something was being ripped apart, resonating all the way up to her eyeballs. Perhaps it was the sound of the tiny ligaments of a body stiffened from sheer horror being torn off?
【Shadow】 『For as long as your mission─── is yet to be carried out───』
【Shadow】 『You shall never───wherever you go───find rest for the sole of your foot.』

By now, the old man had drawn so close to Kuro that the edge of his hood was on the verge of rubbing against her, and held right before the tip of her nose, filthy, tapered fingernails that brought to mind the talons of a monstrous bird wriggled sinisterly. That alone made intense agony shoot through her entire body, as if not just her heart, but even the very deepest core of her existence, her soul, was being scraped off by those nails, and at last.
【Shadow】 『You───who lost the wings you once possessed───』
【Shadow】 『Will for all eternity─── remain in that unsightly form───』
【Kuro】 「……Khkeh. …………」

Thus, until the very end, Kuro remained oblivious to any significance the old man's maledictions may have held. Her crimson orbs suddenly went slack, glazing over as they lost focus. Together with the overwhelming shock, the encroaching terror descending upon her disrupted the neural connections, shutting out the outside world from her consciousness. Her eyes remained open─── but they saw nothing. Jaw slack, her mouth hung open, faintly muttering something, but her voice did not form words, her tongue tangled. She was reduced to merely drooling in an unsightly manner───

Falling upon Kuro, right on the very verge of doing so, footfalls sounded from across the upper deck; the old man made an unpleasant clicking noise with his tongue from within the hood, and as if dissolving into the shadows once more, he vanished.

source.japanese: 戻りが遅いのに焦れてクロを捜しに船室を出た朔屋は、よもや彼女が雨足強まった上甲板に出ていようとは考えず、後回しにしたものだから、少女を発見した時にはひどく濡れてしまっていた。
source.english: Exasperated at how long Kuro was taking, Sakuya had left the cabin to find her. It never occurred to him that she might be on the upper deck in the intensifying rain, so he put off searching there. By the time he found her, she was terribly soaked.

source.japanese: 辺りははやばやと宵闇に隠れ、船室から持ち出してきた洋燈の光の輪の中に照らし出されたクロ、倒れ伏したクロを見て、朔屋がまずしたのは、愕然と天を仰ぐ事だった。といってほんの僅か離れただけで、クロの身に生じた悲劇を天が黙認した事を責めようというのではない。青年は倒れ伏したクロの手足があまりに力なくばらばらと乱れているのに、彼女の荷物らしき麻袋が離れたところに投げ出されているのに、少女がどこか高い処から墜落死したのではと仰天したのである。
source.english: Dusk had already hidden their surroundings. The lamp he had brought from the cabin cast a circle of light upon Kuro's fallen body. His first act was to look up in horror. Not to reproach heaven for permitting such a tragedy in the brief interval he had left her alone. Rather, her limbs lay so helplessly disordered, and the sack that seemed to be hers had been thrown so far away, that he feared she had fallen to her death from some high place.

source.japanese: もちろん見あげてところで見えるものは暗雲と雨の銀筋ばかり、朔屋はとにかくクロを抱き起こして、首筋に掌を当てた。そしてほっと漏らした安堵の吐息、雨に冷えていたが脈は通うてある。
source.english: Of course, looking up revealed only dark clouds and silver cords of rain. Sakuya lifted Kuro and pressed a palm to her neck. A breath of relief escaped him. Her skin was cold with rain, but a pulse beat beneath it.

target.text: After growing impatient with Kuro's late return, Sakuya had left the cabin to go look for her, but with the rain having intensified, he never so much as imagined that the girl would have wandered out onto the upper deck, so because he put off looking for her there, by the time he found the girl, she was soaking wet.

The surroundings had quickly been hidden beneath the cover of twilight, and when he saw Kuro collapsed on the deck, illuminated by the circle of light emitted from the lamp he'd brought with him from the cabin, the first thing Sakuya did was stare into the heavens in blank amazement.

With that said, it was not that he was trying to blame God for tacitly permitting the tragedy that had befallen Kuro to unfold while he was but a short distance away. When the young man saw how limply and haphazardly Kuro's limbs lay sprawled out on the deck, how the jute bag that seemed like something she'd been carrying had been flung some distance away, thinking that the girl might have fallen from somewhere high up and died, he cast his gaze to the sky in horror. (TN: This contains wordplay on the word "仰天", which means to be incredibly shocked to the point that you actually look into the sky in amazement)

Of course, when he looked up, all he saw was dark clouds and silver streaks of rain, so setting that theory aside for now, Sakuya lifted Kuro up in his arms, then placed his palm on her neck. And then he let out a sigh of relief, for while she was cold from the rain, a pulse yet beat within.

source.japanese:
できるなら船室まで抱えていってやるべきだったのだろうが、朔屋が冷静さを残していたのは、クロの脈を確かめるまで。彼もまたクロの惨状に、狂乱の女神の髪で編んだ投網に絡めとられた漁師のように大いに惑乱していたのである。
　信天翁号は確かに津々浦々行く先々に混乱と諍[いさか]いと騒動を撒き散らして歩く疫病媒体の如き船ではあるが、だからといっていがみ合う三悪人がお互いの首を刎ねて死したる後も、その首海上に舞い上がり、三つ巴になって噛みつき合うという『舞首』のように、船内までもが相争っているわけではない。
source.english:
He should, if he could, have carried her back to the cabin. But Sakuya's composure lasted only long enough to check her pulse. The sight of Kuro had thoroughly bewildered him too, like a fisherman caught in a casting net woven from the hair of the goddess of frenzy.
Certainly the Albatross was a ship like a carrier of disease, spreading confusion, quarrels and uproar through every harbor it visited. That did not mean its occupants were forever at one another's throats, like the maikubi—three feuding villains whose severed heads were said to rise over the sea and continue biting each other in a three-way struggle even after death.

source.japanese:
もちろん乗り合わせている面子が面子だからして多分に下っ端には容赦なく、朔屋などは日頃さんざんに虐げられてはいるがそれは彼の無能と怯懦に負うところが大きく、青年がどんな共同体に潜[もぐ]りこんだところで見る憂き目は大差ないだろう。クロもまた常から人扱いというより覚えの悪い犬猫の仔を躾[しつけ]ける如く遇ぜられているが、それでも朔屋よりはよほど重要視されている。
　なにか粗相をしでかした仕置きだとしても、ああも無造作に雨の中に打ち棄てていくというのはちと考えづらく、朔屋にはクロをいかなる事態が見舞ったものか見当もつかない。
source.english:
Given the company aboard, they were naturally merciless toward those at the bottom. Sakuya was habitually abused, but much of that was due to his incompetence and cowardice. Whatever community he wormed his way into, his lot would probably differ little. Kuro, too, was usually treated less like a person than a slow-learning puppy or kitten to be trained. Yet she was valued far more highly than he.
Even as punishment for some mishap, it was difficult to imagine her being thrown out so carelessly into the rain. Sakuya could not guess what had happened to her.

source.japanese:
とにかくまずは身体を悪く冷やす雨垂れから遠ざけねばと、クロを抱えて転がりこんだ甲板上のバラックの中は、確かに剥き出しに雨ざらしになる事だけは免れたものの。
　中は殺風景が身に浸むような、天井も見えないいい加減な造りに屋根板が見えて、これも隙間だらけで、あの裏ぶれて侘びしい、雨漏りというのがあちこちから、ぽたん、ぽたん、ぽたん。
　雨に降り籠められて、廃寺の山門の二階に上ったところ、死人の衣剥いでいる老女と鉢合わせた、逃散の農民の物哀しさというのはこんな心持ちであろうかと、朔屋は中に入った事を一瞬悔いたが、今はクロの方が気懸かりである。
source.english:
First he had to get her out of the rain before the cold did further harm. He carried Kuro into one of the shacks on deck, which at least spared her from lying wholly exposed.
Its bare interior, however, struck desolation into the heart. There was no ceiling, only carelessly fitted roof boards full of gaps. Dreary leaks fell here and there. Plop, plop, plop.
Was this how a fugitive peasant felt, driven by rain into the upper story of an abandoned temple gate, only to find an old woman stripping clothes from corpses? For one moment Sakuya regretted entering. Kuro mattered more just then.

source.japanese: なにがあったのかは知らず、人事不省になっているクロを、こういう場合揺り起こしていいものか、自発的に目を醒ますまで手出ししない方が適当なのか、素人考えでは判別しかねて朔屋、とりあえず雨漏りのないところにそろそろと降ろしたはいいがさて、と手を拱[こまね]いた。
source.english: He did not know what had happened. Was it right to shake someone awake when she was unconscious like this, or better to leave her alone until she woke naturally? His amateur judgment could not decide. For now he cautiously lowered her where the roof did not leak, then stood helpless. What next?

source.japanese: これでたとえば相手が酒場のお姉さんや航海士の双子辺りなら、締めつけは身体に障りだと早速に上半身を裸にしかかる朔屋でも、さすがにクロが相手では。底意もなにもなく、脱がして腹などを拭ってやったとしてもそれだけで、布切れを洗濯板に擦りつけている情景とさほど異ならず、手を出しかねて、いるうちに少女の瞼[まぶた]がひくついた。
source.english: If the other person were a bar hostess or one of the twin navigators, Sakuya would immediately start stripping her to the waist on the grounds that tight clothing was bad for the body. But when it came to Kuro, even he hesitated. There would be no ulterior motive at all; even if he undressed her and wiped her belly and such, that would be all there was to it, scarcely different from rubbing a rag against a washboard. While he hesitated to lay a hand on her, her eyelids twitched.

source.japanese:
やれ嬉や、青年の抱えて上げ下ろし、短い間ではあるが腕の中で歩度に揺られたのが、人事不省に断線した神経を繋ぎ直してくれたらしい。
　雨水を拭ってやるにも、意識のないぐにゃぐにゃした身体では柔い蒟蒻を掴むようなもので手に余る、少しは気の芯が入った方がやりやすい、と待ち構える朔屋の前でクロは、クロときたら。
source.english:
Oh, thank goodness. Lifting and lowering her, swaying her briefly in his arms as he walked, appeared to have reconnected the nerves severed by unconsciousness.
Wiping the rain from an insensible, limp body was like handling soft konjac jelly: more than he could manage. It would be easier once she was a little more alert. Sakuya waited eagerly. But Kuro—Kuro…

target.text: If at all possible, he probably ought to have carried her back to her room, but Sakuya's presence of mind only stayed with him until he had confirmed the existence of Kuro's pulse. For upon witnessing Kuro's disastrous plight, like a fisherman tangled in a casting net knotted from the hair of a mad goddess, he, too, was left profoundly distraught. While it may have been true that the Albatross was a ship that, indeed, like a wandering plague carrier, spread chaos, conflict, and turmoil in each and every port of call, that did not mean that they would continue to fight amongst themselves aboard the ship as well.

It was not like the tale of the 『Maikubi』, wherein three scoundrels quarreled, and even after beheading each other and breathing their last, their heads would still fly high above the sea, forming a mitsudomoe as they continued to snap at each other. (TN: Maikubi, lit. "dancing heads", is a classic Japanese ghost story set in the sea near Manazuru, Kanagawa. A mitsudomoe, written "三つ巴" is three tomoe, a comma-like swirl, arranged in a circle)

Of course, given who the crew he shared a ship with consisted of, they would assuredly show no mercy to those below them, and Sakuya himself was harshly persecuted on a daily basis, but that was in large part due to his own fecklessness and cowardice, and no matter what sort of community he would sneak into, the fate awaiting him was unlikely to be any less miserable. Kuro was also habitually treated less like a human and more like she was a slow-learning puppy or kitten being disciplined, but even so, she was still regarded much more highly than Sakuya.

Even assuming this to be a punishment for making some kind of careless blunder, it was still a little hard to imagine they would just abandon her in the rain so callously, and Sakuya had not the first idea what manner of situation had befallen Kuro.

Regardless, first things first, he had to get her away from these raindrops that only chilled her body and worsened her condition, so he lifted Kuro up in his arms and barged into one of the shacks on the upper deck; it certainly kept them from being left completely exposed to the rain, however. The interior was so dreary it almost seeped into his body, and the construction was so slapdash that there was no ceiling to see, leaving only the bare roof boards visible, and they, too, were full of gaps: bleak and shabby, rain leaking through here and there, drip, drip, drip.

A peasant driven to abandon his fields from onerous taxation, spurred to seek shelter from the downpour, went up to the second floor of an abandoned temple gate, only to come face to face with an old woman divesting a corpse of its clothes; perhaps the melancholy desolation he felt must have been something like this, Sakuya thought, regretting going inside for but an instant, but right now, he was more worried about Kuro.

He didn't know what had happened, but was it right to shake the unconscious Kuro awake in this situation, or was it instead more appropriate to not interfere until she had awoken voluntarily? With only his amateur thoughts to guide him, Sakuya found it difficult to discern what was right to do, but for the time being, just putting her down gently in a spot where the rain didn't leak inside would be fine, and so he did, then watched her with folded arms.

If, for instance, he was dealing with someone like one of the bar girls or the twin first mates, then Sakuya would immediately have stripped their upper half naked as the pressure on their chest would be physically harmful to them, but with Kuro, he couldn't quite bring himself to do that. There were no untoward motives underlying his actions at all, why, he had only bared her stomach so he could wipe it dry, the sight was really not much different from rubbing a scrap of cloth against a washboard, and while he struggled thus with making a move on her, the girl's eyelids twitched.

Ah, joy of joys, lifted and lowered in the young man's embrace: it was for but a brief time, but while in his arms, she had been rocked with each step, and that seemed to have reconnected the synapses that had been severed while she was unconscious. Even trying to wipe off the rainwater was beyond his ability to manage; handling her limp, unconscious body was like trying to grasp soft konjac jelly, and so Sakuya waited, thinking it would be a lot easier when there was a little spark of life tensing her up, and right in front of him, Kuro, oh Kuro, of all the things.

source.japanese: 瞬きを二度・三度、バラックの屋根板剥き出しなのを不思議そうに見上げていたが、目線が横に、朔屋へと流れてそして───ひ、と短かな息で爪弾き出された。寸の詰まった悲鳴だった。クロから見あげると、朔屋は洋燈の光源に近すぎて、影に沈んで、その黒々とした輪郭が、クロの中の絃にひどく響いた。
source.english: She blinked two or three times, looking wonderingly at the shack's exposed roof boards. Then her gaze shifted sideways to Sakuya. A short breath plucked out a sound: ‘Hih.’ A compressed scream. Seen from below, he was too close to the lamp's light, sunk in shadow. That black outline struck violently at a string within Kuro.

target.text: She blinked twice, thrice, looked up at the exposed roof boards of the shack as if puzzled by them, but her gaze drifted sideways, towards Sakuya, and then───a short breath was plucked from her throat. It was a choked-back scream. From Kuro's perspective, Sakuya was standing much too close to the lamp providing the light, and so he sunk deep into the shadows, and that jet-black silhouette resonated harshly with the strings within Kuro.

source.japanese:
たちまち顔がひきつり歪む、
クロの神経の繋がりは回復したように見えて、中途半端に短絡してしまっていたようで、朔屋を見て影と断じさせた、自分を恐怖の底に叩きこんだあの老人だと───半狂乱となるのが、たちまちのうち。
source.english:
Her face contracted and twisted at once.
Her nerves seemed to have reconnected, but only in a partial short circuit. Looking at Sakuya, she identified him as the shadow—the old man who had plunged her into the depths of terror. She went half-mad in an instant.

target.text: Her face immediately contorted and twitched, and though it appeared as if Kuro's synapses had recovered, they also seemed to have partially short-circuited, for looking at Sakuya, they made her conclude that he was the shadow, that he was the one who had dragged her into the depths of terror, that old man───she went half-mad, all in the blink of an eye.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「やぁ～～～、やあよぅぅ……、
　黒いの、怖いの、近くに来たら」
source.english:
“Nooo, nooo… The black thing,
the scary thing… If it comes close…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Noo～～～, nooouuh……, black, scary, if it gets close!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あーっっっ、いぅぅぅーーーっっ」
source.english: “Aaaah! Eeeee!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Aahー, iiuuuhーーー」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「お、おい落ち着けって、俺だ、朔屋さんだ。
　クロ、わからないのかクロよう！」
source.english:
“H-hey, calm down! It's me, Mr. Sakuya.
Kuro, don't you know me?”

source.japanese: 釣り糸にかかった烏賊、あるいは霞網に捕らえられた鶫[ツグミ]、色気が失せて白いのが暴れたる様だ、洋燈の光の中で残像を引いて、手が跳ねる足が躍る白い髪が乱れ咲く。クロは必死なのだろうが、哀れで、笑えてしまうくらい力に乏しく、腕相撲でも下級水夫君に辛うじて勝てる程度の不甲斐ない朔屋でさえ抑えるのにたやすい。
source.english: A squid on a fishing line, a thrush caught in a mist net: a pale thing struggling, all its color gone. In the lamplight, her limbs trailed afterimages, hands springing up, feet dancing, white hair flowering wildly. She must have been desperate, but she was so pitifully weak it was almost laughable. Even feeble Sakuya, who could scarcely beat a junior sailor at arm-wrestling, could easily hold her down.

source.japanese: けれどその抑えるだけで、かえってクロの身を損なってしまいそうだから、朔屋は少女の狂態を扱いかねた。
source.english: But simply restraining her seemed likely to injure her further. Sakuya did not know how to handle her frenzy.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「O-, oi, calm down, it's me, it's Sakuya-san. Kuro, hey, can't you tell it's me, Kuro!」

Like a squid hooked on a fishing line, or perhaps a thrush caught in a mist net, something pale and drained of colour was violently struggling, afterimages trailing after it in the light of the lamp, hands springing, feet bouncing, and white hair bursting into a wild bloom. Kuro must have been frantic, but she was so weak that it was pitiful, laughable, for even Sakuya, a man so pathetic that he could only barely snatch a narrow victory from one of the deck boys in a bout of arm wrestling, could easily hold her down.
However, trying to restrain her only seemed like it would harm Kuro instead, so Sakuya was left at a loss as to how to handle the girl's frenzied behaviour.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ううぅ、ううぅ、クロもう飛べない。
　全部いろおちた。クロもう。
　たくさん見た。あった」
source.english:
“Uuh, uuh… Kuro can't fly anymore.
All the color fell away. Kuro…
Saw lots. There were lots.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でもクロが降りられるとこ、
　なかったもの」
source.english:
“But there was nowhere Kuro
could land.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロのせいなの……？
　クロ、だから、シロになった……ぅ、ぅ、
　ああああ～、うぇぇん、あぁーん……」
source.english:
“Kuro's fault…?
Kuro… that's why Kuro turned White…
uuh, uuh… Aaaah, waaah…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「クロ、お前何を言ってるんだ、おい、落ち着け、じってしてなって、この……うあ!?」
source.english: “Kuro, what are you talking about? Hey, calm down! Hold still, you… Uwah!?”

source.japanese: 歯を剥き出し、指は鉤にして寄らば裂くぞの構えで振り回す、クロがこれまで見せた事のない向敵相の、しかしその危うさ孕んだ攻撃的な顔は、相手を害そうというのではなく、ただ迫る脅威を追い払わんとした小鼠の足掻きで、狂乱して走り回った挙げ句柱や壁に激突して全身の骨挫[くじ]きかねない、かえって我が身を傷つけそうで、朔屋も躍起と、加減して力の限り抑えつけるという難事に挑む。非力な男と月足らずの白子の手が交差するのは、はたから見ればとんと猫の戯れ合いめくが、本人達はあくまで懸命の、手と手が舞って翻[ひるがえ]って、白く折れそうなのがとんと船員服の胸を押す、雄鶏が蹴る方がよほど堪[こた]えるのではないかという軽々した力だったが、タイミングが変に合って、朔屋の体が後ろに流れた、支えようと手をついて、ついた手が。
source.english:
She bared her teeth and crooked her fingers into hooks, lashing out as though she would tear apart anyone who came near. Kuro had never worn such a hostile face. Yet for all its dangerous aggression, she meant no harm; this was merely a little mouse's desperate attempt to drive away a threat. Left to race about in her frenzy, she might smash into a post or wall and break every bone in her body. She was likelier to injure herself. Sakuya therefore undertook the difficult feat of restraining her with all his strength while somehow moderating it.
From outside, the hands of the feeble man and the undersized albino might have looked like cats at play, though both were in deadly earnest. Their hands danced and wheeled. One pale, breakable-looking palm struck his sailor's jacket with a force so slight that a rooster's kick would surely have hurt more. Yet the timing was uncannily exact. Sakuya toppled backward, put out a hand to catch himself, and that hand—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uuh, uuh, Kuro can't fly anymore. Has lost all colour. Kuro already. Saw so much. Found it.」
【Kuro】 「But there was just no place for Kuro to alight.」
【Kuro】 「Is that Kuro's fault……? Is that……why Kuro became white……uh, uh, aaaaah～, waaah, aaaーnh……」
【Naomasa】 「Kuro, what are you talking about? Oi, calm down, just stay still you little……wah!?」

Baring her teeth, she brandished her fingers in a stance like they were talons promising to tear him apart if he dared approach; Kuro wore a bellicose expression of a sort he'd never seen on her face hitherto, however, that aggressive visage, laden with such danger, was not worn for the purpose of harming an enemy, it was merely the struggling of a tiny mouse trying to drive away the imminent threat, so if he let her run about in a frenzy, she might end up crashing into a post or a wall, and she could very well shatter every bone in her body, only hurting herself all the more, and so Sakuya, also desperate, took on the daunting challenge of restraining her with as little force as possible.

As the arms of a feeble man and an albino the product of a premature birth clashed, it must have seemed nothing more than the rough-and-tumble play of frolicking cats from the sidelines, but the two in question were earnest as could be, hands dancing and twisting; a pale hand, so feeble it could snap any moment, pushed against the chest of the sailor uniform, with force so feather-light that being kicked by a rooster would have been far harder to bear, but through a strange stroke of apt timing, Sakuya's body swayed backwards, and he braced a hand against the floor to find support, and that hand.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「てぇぇぇっ!?　な、なんだ、これっ」
source.english: “Owwww!? W-what's this?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「OOOOW!? Wh-, what the hell is this?」

source.japanese: 後ろについた手にちくりと来たのが、白刃素手で握ってしまったほどにも痛んで、つい張り上げた声、朔屋自身も驚くほど甲声で、本人がそれなのだから、クロなどはびしりと瞬時に硬直していたのだが。
source.english: A prick in the hand he had planted behind him hurt as though he had seized a naked blade. He cried out in a voice so shrill it startled even himself. Small wonder Kuro went instantly rigid.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あいて……っ、なんだこれ、酒瓶の欠片？
　あー、転んで割っちまったのか。
　クロ、お前は怪我ないか？　あそこには毛がないのは知ってるがそうではなく」
source.english:
“Ow… what’s this? A shard of a liquor bottle?
Ah, I guess you fell and broke it.
Kuro, are you hurt? I know you don’t have any hair there, but that’s not what I mean.”

target.text: The stinging in the hand he'd thrust behind him was so painful, it was as if he'd grabbed a naked blade with his bare hand, and the yell that burst out from his throat was so shrill, it surprised even Sakuya himself; given that the man in question felt that way, the likes of Kuro froze in place in the blink of an eye.

【Naomasa】 「Ouch……, what is this, a shard of glass from a bottle of liquor? Aah, is this the one you dropped and broke? Kuro, are you hurt anywhere? I know how you're feeling down there, but that's not what I'm talking about.」 (TN: Sakuya, ever the tactful gentleman, makes a little jest here with "怪我ない" and "毛がない", respectively meaning "uninjured" and "hairless", both pronounced "ke ga nai".)

source.japanese:
見ればクロが提げていた袋に手を衝[つ]いて、その中味でちょっと手に傷をつけてしまったらしい。
　袋の布を破ってつきだしていた、酒瓶らしい、割れた硝子の角だった。と正体が判れば大した切り傷でもない。
　ただ、朔屋の甲声が警策となって、学僧の座禅中の倦怠を払うが如し、クロの鼻先を叩[はた]いて正気を取り戻させた。
source.english:
He had put his hand on the sack Kuro had carried and slightly cut it on the contents.
A corner of broken glass, apparently from the liquor bottle, protruded through the fabric. Knowing what it was, he saw the cut was nothing serious.
But his shrill cry acted like the stick that rouses a drowsy trainee monk in seated meditation: it struck at Kuro's nose and restored her senses.

target.text: Taking a look, he had apparently propped himself up against the bag Kuro had brought with her, accidentally cutting his hand a little on its contents. Jutting out after having torn a hole in the fabric of the bag containing it was what seemed part of a bottle of liquor, a sharp edge of broken glass. And now that he realized what it was, it wasn't really that much of a cut.

However, Sakuya's shrill voice had become a kyousaku, and exactly like driving away the torpor of a novice monk during zazen, it had struck Kuro right on the tip of her nose, making her come back to her senses. (TN: A kyousaku, written "警策", also known as a keizaku depending on the school of Zen Buddhism, is a little stick used by a Zen priest to strike an inattentive monk sitting in Zen meditation. Zazen, written "坐禅", is a catch-all term for seated Zen meditation.)

source.japanese: 見つめ返す眸[ひとみ]がきょとんと、暗がりの中で洋燈の明かり宿して、聖者のように澄んで、落ち着き払って見えたけれど───混じり気のないものは危うい、と朔屋はすぐ思い知る事になる。
source.english: Her eyes returned his gaze in bewilderment. Holding the lamplight in the dark, they looked clear as a saint's, perfectly composed. But purity was dangerous—as Sakuya would soon learn.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あ……朔屋さんだ」
source.english: “Oh… Mr. Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうそう。俺だよ。少しは落ち着いたか。
　一体お前、なにがあった───」
source.english:
“That's right. It's me. Calmed down a little?
What on earth happened to you…?”

target.text: The eyes gazing back at him were wide-open and blank, catching the lamplight in the dark, as clear as a saint's; they seemed perfectly serene, and yet───very soon, Sakuya would come to understand the precarity of purity.
【Kuro】 「Ah……it's Sakuya-san.」
【Naomasa】 「Right, right. It's me. So have you calmed down a little? What in the world happened to you───」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さん、血……怪我？」
source.english: “Mr. Sakuya, blood… Are you hurt?”

source.japanese:
クロは、朔屋の問いに答えなかった。
　青年の掌を汚す血潮から目が離せない様子で、その眸[ひとみ]が、血の色を透かして、『鳩の血』とも称される最上等の紅玉めいた色合いが、徐々に───
source.english:
Kuro did not answer his question.
She seemed unable to take her eyes off the blood staining his palm. Her eyes shone with a translucent, blood-red hue, like the finest ‘pigeon's blood’ ruby. Gradually…

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ん。まあ俺はちょっと切っただけで。
　お前は……」
source.english:
“Mm. Just a little cut.
Are you…?”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロのせいなの……？　あ……っ。
　おさけも……割れて……。
　……割れて……だめに……くろが？」
source.english:
“Kuro's fault…? Oh…
The liquor bottle too… broken…
Broken… ruined… Kuro did it?”

source.japanese: 眸が、透明度を失い、熱を通した卵のように濁っていって───
source.english: Her eyes lost their transparency, clouding like an egg as it cooks.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「気にすんな、別に一日呑まないくらいで死には……クロ？」
source.english: “Don't worry. I'm not going to die if I go one day without a drink… Kuro?”

source.japanese: 朔屋は本当に、クロを責めるつもりなど毛頭なかったのである。ここまで捜しに来たのも少女の身を案ずるならばこそで、暴れた彼女を強く抑えたからといってなにも暴力に物を言わせてどうこうするつもりもない、それ以前にクロになにがあってあんな所に倒れていたのか、それさえ判っていない。
source.english: Sakuya truly had no intention whatsoever of blaming her. He had come to look for her out of concern. Holding her firmly when she struggled did not mean he wished to impose anything upon her by violence. Before any of that, he did not even know what had happened to leave her lying there.

source.japanese:
判ったのは、その何事かが少女の精神をひどく蝕[むしば]んだのだ、という事。
　朔屋は今のクロを見て、真に心抉[えぐ]られた人間の目は、正視に耐えないものだと初めて思い知った。濁りきった色合いは傷口に溜まった膿と同じ、双眸自体が顔の中央に空いた虚ろな孔と化して、漏出するのは鉄錆びたの血潮と爛[ただ]れた肉の臭い、心の傷痕がそこにはそのまま現れている。その傷痕をまざまざと見せつける故に、朔屋はクロの貌[かお]に、双眸に、耐えきれないほど痛ましさを覚えるのだ───
source.english:
What he did know was that something had grievously eaten into her mind.
Looking at Kuro now, Sakuya understood for the first time that the eyes of someone truly torn apart within were unbearable to look at. Their clouded color was like pus collected in a wound. The eyes themselves had become hollow holes in the middle of her face, leaking the smell of rusty blood and putrefying flesh. The scars upon her mind showed there unchanged. And because they showed so plainly, the sight of Kuro's face, her eyes, brought him an intolerable anguish.

source.japanese:
ましてそんな貌[かお]が、虚孔の様な眼差しが、無理矢理に表情を造ろうとしているとあっては、痛々しいを通り越しておぞましくさえ、ある。
　……能の面[おもて]は、そこにただ一つの表情しか刻まれていないにもかかわらず、太夫の所作、舞台上の陰翳によって千変万化の貌[かお]を見せる。無表情故の多彩な、幽玄の中に佇む貌[かお]なき貌[かお]だ。
source.english:
Worse still, that face, that gaze like empty holes, was forcibly trying to make an expression. Beyond pitiful, it was horrifying.
A Noh mask has only one expression carved upon it, yet the actor's movements and the shadows upon the stage give it a thousand changing faces. Its very expressionlessness gives it that range: a faceless face poised in profound mystery.

source.japanese: ところがこの今のクロの貌[かお]はそれら能面達の表情とは全く逆の、なるほど、貌の造作を操って、筋肉を動かせばとりあえずは表情らしいものは出来上がろう、そら、クロが双眸を三日月を寝かせて横に並べたものにする、ほら、頬を緩めて唇の端を吊り上げる、と、それは笑みと分類される貌[かお]の形にはなるけれど───けして、そこに現れているのは、幸いや喜悦の徴[しるし]などではない、などであってたまるか、クロが心から幸に喜んでいるのなら、今の彼女の貌[かお]は何故そんなにも。
source.english: Kuro's face was precisely the opposite of those masks. Certainly, manipulate the features, move the muscles, and something resembling an expression will result. There: she makes her two eyes into crescents laid sideways. There: she relaxes her cheeks, lifts the corners of her lips. The shape can be classified as a smile. But what appears there is by no means a sign of happiness or delight. It could not possibly be. If Kuro were genuinely happy, why was her face now so…

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san, blood……hurt?」

Kuro did not answer Sakuya's question. She seemed unable to tear her eyes from the warm blood staining the young man's palm, and those eyes, translucent with the colour of blood, began to gradually assume a hue reminiscent of the finest of rubies, a shade known as 『Pigeon's Blood』───
【Naomasa】 「Mh. Well, I just cut myself a little. You're……」
【Kuro】 「Was that Kuro's fault……? Ah……. Also broke……the alcohol……. ……broke……useless……Kuro is?」
Her eyes lost their transparency, instead becoming turbid like a cooked egg───
【Naomasa】 「Don't worry about it, it's not like spending a single day sober is going to kill me or any……Kuro?」

Sakuya had not the slightest intention of finding any fault with Kuro whatsoever, he truly didn't. He had expressly gone this far in searching for the girl precisely because he was worried about the girl's safety, so just because he had needed to be firm in restraining the rampaging girl, that did not mean he had ever intended to resort to violence, and before any of that, he didn't even know what had happened to Kuro to make her collapse in a place like that.
What he did know, however, was that whatever this something had been, it had disturbed the girl's psyche severely.

Looking at Kuro as she was now, this was the very first time Sakuya realized how unbearable it could be to look square into the eyes of someone whose mind had been truly shattered. The cloudy hue was like the pus accumulating in the mouth of a wound, the twin orbs themselves had been reduced to hollow, gaping cavities in the center of her face, rusted blood and the stench of festering flesh oozed out from within; the scars of her heart were manifested there, exactly as they were. And because those scars were so starkly on display, Sakuya felt an unbearable agony from looking at Kuro's face, peering into her eyes───
Not to mention how, when such a face, such a hollow pit of a gaze, forcibly attempted to manufacture an expression, it transcended the painful and became downright repulsive.

……Despite a Noh mask having only a single expression carved into it, it is transformed into a visage of innumerable variety through a tayuu's performance and the subtle interplay of shadows on the stage. Diverse through a lack of expression, a faceless face standing in the realm of yuugen. (TN: A tayuu, written "太夫" is another name for a high-ranking Noh actor, usually the principal chanter or the head of the school. Yuugen, written "幽玄" is an aesthetic idea formed in the Japanese Middle Ages that places value in the mysterious, quiet beauty of the subtle and profound.)

However, Kuro's current face was the exact opposite of the expressions of those Noh masks; indeed, by manipulating the features of your face, setting your muscles into motion and so on, you will surely form something resembling an expression, at least at first; behold, Kuro turned her eyes into the shape of crescent moons lying flat side by side; look, she relaxed her cheeks and lifted up the corners of her lips, and with that, the shape of her face did become something that would be categorized as a smile, however───

What emerged there was, under no circumstances, a symbol of happiness or joy, indeed, how could it be anything of the sort; if Kuro was genuinely happy from the bottom of her heart, then why was her current expression so─

source.japanese: 気持ちが───悪い。
source.english: Repulsive.

target.text: So utterly───revolting.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あはははうふふ。えへっ。
　ごめんあさい。えへ？　ごめん、します。
　クロ。だめです、やぱり」
source.english:
“Ahahaha, heehee. Heh.
I'm sorry. Heh? Kuro says sorry. Kuro's…
no good, after all.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「おつかい、できない。
　おじいさんにいわれたこともできない。
　なんにも。えへ、うふ。
　朔屋さんのおさけも、わりました」
source.english:
“Can't run errands.
Can't do what the old man said either. Nothing.
Heh, heehee.
Broke your liquor bottle too, Mr. Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロなんか。いないほうがいい。
　だからおじいさんもクロを飛ばしたの。
　戻ってくるなて。見つけるまで」
source.english:
“It'd be better if Kuro wasn't here.
That's why the old man sent Kuro flying.
Don't come back, he said. Not till you find it.”

source.japanese:
クロは、笑っているのに泣いていた。笑っているのに恐れていた。笑っているのに怯えていた。苦しんでいた。悔やんでいた、絶望していた、哀しんでいた、嘆いていた───
　
　貌ではそれはもう力の限りに笑みの形、造らんとしていたけれど、懸命さが滲めば滲む分だけ、健気が透ける分だけ、それは笑顔から遠ざかっていく、たとえば髑髏の肉腐り落ちた剥き出しの歯列とか、黒後家蜘蛛の背中の異様な貌[かお]の紋様とか、そういったものにしか見えず。
source.english:
Kuro was smiling, yet she wept. Smiling, yet afraid. Smiling, yet frightened. Suffering. Regretting, despairing, grieving, lamenting… She tried with all her might to make her face into a smile.
But the more her effort showed, the more her brave persistence shone through, the farther it moved from a smile. It resembled only such things as the exposed teeth of a skull whose flesh had rotted away, or the uncanny face-pattern upon a black widow spider's back.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい……落ち着けよクロッ。
　その爺さんてな何の話だ───あ。
　水夫長が言ってた、
　この島のただ独りの生き残りだって言う」
source.english:
“Hey… Calm down, Kuro!
What's this about an old man…? Oh.
The one the bosun mentioned.
They say he's this island's only survivor…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「けど全体、なんだって、そんなのがお前に絡んでくるんだよ!?」
source.english: “But why the hell would he be bothering you!?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「その爺が、一体なにをやって、お前をそんなにしちまったんだようっ」
source.english: “What did that old bastard do to leave you like this?”

source.japanese:
クロが船室から出て行って僅かな時間。その間に少女は船内に潜[ひそ]んでいた老人と遭遇し、何事かを蒙[こうむ]ったのに違いない。
　暴力ではない、犯された風もない、肉体的には見た限りではなにも害を受けた様子はない。
　けれど老人は、クロの心を穿[うが]ち、貫き、がたがたに壊していったのだ。人をここまで壊してしまうものとはなんだ？　恐怖か？　絶望か？　ならばならば、クロの恐怖とは、絶望とは一体───
source.english:
In the brief time since leaving the cabin, Kuro must have encountered the old man hiding aboard and suffered something at his hands.
Not physical violence. She showed no sign of having been raped, nor, as far as he could see, of any bodily harm.
Yet the old man had bored through her mind, pierced it and smashed it to pieces. What could break a person so completely? Fear? Despair? Then, then—what was Kuro's fear? What was her despair?

source.japanese: こんな事になるのなら、あの時なんとしてでも止めておくべきだったと悔やんでも悔やみきれない朔屋、哀れ、もうそれは既に起こってしまい、変更は利かないのだ。
source.english: Had he known it would end like this, he would have stopped her at any cost. Regret could not punish Sakuya enough. But the thing had already happened, poor man, and no hand could alter it now.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でもクロはできない。
　もう、クロはもどれない。
　みんなといっしょに、だめ」
source.english:
“But Kuro can't.
Can't go back anymore.
Can't… be with everyone.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Ahahahauhuhu. Eheh. Sorry. Ehe? Kuro is sorry. Kuro. Is no good, after all.」
【Kuro】 「Can't run errands. Can't even do what grandpa told Kuro to either. Nothing at all. Ehe, uhu. Also broke Sakuya-san's alcohol.」
【Kuro】 「Would be best if someone like Kuro just. Wasn't here. That's also why grandpa sent Kuro flying off. Don't come back, he said. Until you find it.」

Though Kuro laughed, she was crying. Though Kuro laughed, she was afraid. Though Kuro laughed, she was scared. Suffering. She regretted, despaired, grieved, lamented─── Her face was trying with all its might to form a smile, to manufacture its shape, but the more intensely her earnestness showed through, the more transparent her commendable bravery, it only drifted further from a smile in turn; take her bared rows of teeth, like those of a skull whose flesh had peeled and rotted off, or like the strange facial pattern on the back of a black widow spider; that was all he could see it as.
【Naomasa】 「Oi……calm down, Kuro. Who is this grandpa you're talking───ah. The old man the Bosun mentioned, the one he called the only survivor left on this island.」
【Naomasa】 「But why in the world, for what possible reason, would someone like that have anything to do with you!?」
【Naomasa】 「That old man, what in the hell did he do to leave you all like this?」

And as the downpour continued, all sorts of issues arose on board the ragged Albatross that demanded their attention as well. Therefore, the crew had been nailed to the ship while this torrential downpour continued, and they, too, were in need of a breather.

source.japanese: やがてある朝───とはいえ降り続く雨に景色には常に曖昧な昏さが垂れこめ、朝陽赫耀と到来とはいかないわけだが───驟雨が手を弱めるを見た。数日ぶりの好機と信天翁号の乗り組み達は島へと財宝求めて繰り出す、この根気強さを堅気の商売に用いれば、と思うのは素人衆、世には楽をする為に全身全力を費やす手合いもある。
source.english: At last, one morning—though the ceaseless rain kept the world sunk in a vague darkness, with no radiant sunrise to announce the hour—the downpour loosened its grip. Seizing their first opportunity in days, the Albatross crew went ashore in search of treasure. Only amateurs would wonder why they could not apply such perseverance to honest trade. Some people devote their entire strength to the pursuit of an easy life.

source.japanese: ただ本日は、探索隊の人数は幾らか減じた。水夫長が船に残ったからである。長丁場になりそうと看てとり、腰を据えるならそれなりに船内でも準備を整えないといけないと。船の位置も、環礁の中から島の桟橋へと寄せ直した。島に渡るのに一々短艇を出す手間を省く為である。
source.english: Today's search party was somewhat smaller. The boatswain had stayed aboard. Seeing that this might be a lengthy business, he had decided that settling in called for preparations on the ship as well. They had moved her from within the atoll to the island's pier, sparing themselves the trouble of launching a boat every time they went ashore.

target.text: Finally, on a certain morning─── though with that said, the incessantly pouring rain left a vague murkiness hanging low over the scenery, so it was not as if the brilliant red of the morning sun ever visited them─── the heavy shower suddenly seemed to loosen its grip. With this being the first good opportunity in several days, the crew of the Albatross set forth for the island once more in search of treasure; had they but used this tenacity in the pursuit of an honest trade, but only the amateur masses would think such thoughts, for in this world, there are those who must spend their entire soul and body on their endeavours before they can be at ease.

However, today, the number of people in the exploration team had been reduced by several heads. This was because the Bosun had stayed behind on the ship. Judging that it seemed like they were in this for the long haul, if they were to settle in, there were some arrangements that needed to be made on board the ship first. There was also the ship's position to consider, and he had moved her from the middle of the atoll towards the island's pier. It would save them the trouble of having to prepare the boat every single time they wanted to cross over to the island.

source.japanese:
さて島内の、廃屋の一つの中では。
　低く澱[よど]んだ床の影になかば同化し、かつ異なる色合いを人型の輪郭が二つ。その床にべったりと溶け崩れたかの異様な姿勢は、瑜伽の行法極めんとするサドゥーの体位かはたまた夏眠に陥った肺魚の『繭』か、なんの、三昧境に浸るどころか仮死の眠りに彷徨うどころか、二つの輪郭から放たれているのは、獲物の跫音を逃すまいとする雌豹の集中力、航海士の双子が頭を向かい合わせの対称形に、床から何事かを感じ取ろうと穿心の気力、細く鋭い。
source.english:
Now, inside one of the island's abandoned houses…
Two human outlines lay half-merged with the low shadows upon the floor, yet differing from them in color. Their peculiar poses, as though their bodies had melted flat into the boards, might have been the asanas of sadhus seeking mastery of yoga, or the cocoons of estivating lungfish. Nothing of the sort. Neither absorbed in meditation nor lost in a deathlike sleep, the two shapes radiated the concentration of she-leopards determined not to miss a footfall from their prey. The twin navigators lay symmetrically, heads facing one another, striving with fine, piercing attention to sense something through the floor.

source.japanese:
取り囲む下級水夫達も二人の集中を乱す事を憚[はばか]り、ただ息を殺して立ち尽くし見守る。朔屋が居合わせたなら、双子と同様に床へ身を投げ出したろうが、傾注する先はスカートの奥である事は述べるまでなく、激昂した双子に長靴の靴底で顔面打ちつけられ、軽く済んで鼻骨陥没、床に無駄な血を吸わせた事だろう。
　行儀よろしい水夫君達はその手の破廉恥行為とは無縁だったが、ただ緊張に耐えかねた水夫の一人が、朝礼の校長の長口舌にぶっ倒れる生徒よろしく膝から崩落しかかったが、左右から朋輩が慌てて手を走らせ支える。
source.english:
The junior sailors surrounding them stood motionless, scarcely daring to breathe lest they break the twins' concentration. Had Sakuya been present, he too would have flung himself upon the floor, though naturally his attention would have lain beneath their skirts. The enraged twins would have planted their boot soles in his face, crushing his nose at the very least and making the floor drink useless blood.
The well-behaved junior sailors entertained no such indecency. One, however, could no longer bear the tension and began to fold at the knees like a pupil fainting through the principal's interminable morning address. His companions caught him hastily from either side.

source.japanese: きりきりと弓を引き絞る弦鳴りさえ聞こえそうな沈黙の、どれだけ続いたのか、やがてとうとうシサムが顔をあげた。
source.english: How long had that silence lasted, so taut one could almost hear a bowstring being drawn? At last Sisam raised her face.

target.text: Now then. On the island, within one of the deserted buildings. Half-assimilated into the low, stagnant shadows on the floor were two contours of human shapes that once held a different hue. This queer posture, sticking to the floor as though their shape had dissolved: was this the asana of a Sadhu striving to perfect the art of yoga, or perhaps the cocoon of a lungfish fallen into a state of aestivation? Why, nothing of the sort.

Far from being immersed in samadhi or strolling through the sleep of suspended animation, what emanated from these two silhouettes was the intense concentration of two leopardesses trying not to lose the footfalls of their prey; it was the symmetrical forms of the twin first mates facing each other, their piercing force of will sharp as they attempted to feel something from the floor.

The deck boys encircling the two were also hesitant to disturb the duo's concentration, simply holding their breath as they watched on. Had Sakuya been present with them, he would surely have tossed himself on the floor just like the twins, but as went without saying, he would be devoting his attention to the depths of their skirts; he would be stomped in the face by the sole of a boot worn by a furious twin, and if he was lucky, he would escape with only a depressed nasal fracture, but the floor would surely be made to soak up blood needlessly spilt.

Such shameless acts were foreign to these well-mannered sailors, but there was a single sailor unable to bear the tension, and like a student falling flat on his face from listening to the long-winded yammering of a principal at a morning assembly, his knees were about to give way, his comrades from both sides rushing over in a panic to keep him upright.
It was a silence stretched so taut you could almost hear the creaking of the bowstring drawn to its limits; how long could this go on, they wondered, but eventually, Shisamu finally raised her head.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ねえキサラ、気づいたか？」
source.english: “Kisara. Did you notice?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Hey, Kisara, you notice?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんたが感じることならあたしもわかる。
　それがウチらの道理だ。
　こう言いたいんだよね」
source.english:
“If you feel it, so do I.
That's how we work.
This is what you mean, isn't it?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If you're feeling it, I get it too. That's the logic we live by. This is what you want to say, right?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「この島───動いてる───って」
source.english: “This island… is moving.”

source.japanese:
ジャケットから埃を払いつ立ち上がったキサラの、シサムと目配せ交わし合う、何時になく真剣な眼差しが廃屋の仄明かりの中に美しく冴える、ただそれは研ぎ上げられた刃の、鋼の鋭さと匂いに通じて、居合わせた者達の背筋にもたらしたのも、硬く冷たい予感で。
　今にも足下が大鳴動して、島が濁流の中の木の葉のように舞い出すのではとの危惧もありありと、下級水夫が訊ねる、声音にすがる色が見え隠れして。
source.english:
Kisara stood, brushing dust from her jacket, and exchanged a look with Sisam. Their unusually serious eyes gleamed beautifully in the house's dim light. But that beauty carried the sharpness and scent of freshly honed steel, bringing a hard, cold premonition down the spines of those around them.
A junior sailor asked, a pleading note slipping into his voice. He plainly feared the ground might begin to roar at any moment and the island spin away like a leaf in a torrent.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「This island───is moving───」

After brushing the dust off her jacket and standing up, Kisara exchanged glances with Shisamu, the unusually serious look in her eyes beautifully clear within the dim light of the deserted house, but that clarity exuded the sharpness of the steel of a honed blade, and it made a hard, icy premonition run through the spines of all present who beheld it. A great rumbling could thunder forth from beneath their feet at any moment, and with his unease at the idea that this island might well be floating around like a leaf in a muddy stream palpable, a deck boy enquired, his tone of voice betraying glimpses of an imploring timbre.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「それ……ほんとに？　じゃあこの島、浮島って事？　どっかに流されちゃうって事？」
source.english: “Really…? Then it's a floating island? We're going to drift off somewhere?”

source.japanese:
総毛だった下級水夫の肩を掌で、落ち着かせてやるように軽く叩いてやったりすると、上背があり均整の取れた肢体の彼女であるだけに、いかにも頼もしい姐御肌の、だが台詞の後半が何やら不穏な響きを孕んだ。
　見上げる下級水夫の頤[おとがい]の線に滲むは健気色、彼は航海士の言葉を、せっかく頼りにしていたのに。
source.english:
Sisam gave the terrified junior sailor's shoulder a light, reassuring pat. Tall and beautifully proportioned, she looked every inch the dependable elder sister; yet the latter half of her answer carried an ominous note.
A touching faith showed in the line of his uplifted chin. He had wanted so badly to rely upon the navigator's words.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Is that……really true? Then, is this a floating island? Are we being swept away to somewhere?」

Using her palm, she gently patted the shoulder of the deck boy whose hair stood on end as if to calm him down, the sort of dependable, big-sisterly disposition only found in women tall of stature and with the proportions to match, but the latter part of the conversation had a disquieting ring to it. Earnest bravery bled through the jawline of the deck boy as he looked up; he had placed such faith in the mate's words, and yet.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そうすぐに、ではないだろうけど。
　でも、浮島と言うにしてもこれは……」
source.english:
“Not immediately, probably.
But even for a floating island, this…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Not right away, or so I'd hope. Still, even for a floating island, this is……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「うん……たぶん、造られたものだよ、
　恐らくは全部木材で───」
source.english:
“Yeah… I think someone built it.
Probably entirely out of wood…”

source.japanese: 五蘊、と、鐘楼台の大鐘衝[つ]いたが如き擬音が肩に重圧伴ってのしかかる、それほどまでに野放図な意味的質量を蔵した推測だった。
source.english: Gong. A syllable freighted with the whole burden of body and mind, tolling like a great bell in its tower, bore down upon their shoulders. Such was the unbounded mass of meaning contained in that conjecture.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Yeah……this thing is probably artificial, and most likely made entirely of wood───」

Gooong. It was like the onomatopoeia of something striking the great bell of a belfry felt with all five skandhas, bearing down on his shoulders together with a heavy pressure; it was a conjecture carrying so unbridled a weight of significance. (TN: This line is a pun on the word "Goun", written "五蘊", meaning the five skandhas, playing on the pronunciation being very similar to the gong of a bell.)

source.japanese:
いやしくも島一つを組み上げるのに、どれだけの量の木材が要求されるのか。
　いかなる輸送手段を用いるのか。島を取り巻く嵐を越えて。
　そしてどれだけの歳月がかかるのか。
　それぞれの条件を並べ上げただけでも気が遠くなる。
source.english:
How much timber would it take to build an entire island?
What means of transporting it could there have been—through the storm surrounding it?
And how many years would the work require?
Simply setting out those conditions was dizzying.

source.japanese: ましてこの島に残された廃屋群は、少なく見積もっても世紀の歳月を経ているように思われる。この時代の最新の技術を駆使しても島一つまるごと建造するというのは非常の難事業であるのに、そんな過去に可能とする技術があったとも思われない。
source.english: The abandoned houses seemed, at the lowest estimate, to have stood for a century. Building a whole island would be a stupendous undertaking even with the latest technology of this age. It was hard to imagine that techniques capable of it had existed so far in the past.

source.japanese: だとすれば───
source.english: If so…

source.japanese:
ここで用いられたのは技術は。
　既存の概念を超えた───
source.english:
The technology used here…
lay beyond the concepts they knew…

target.text: Even assuming one was bold enough to build an entire island, just how vast a quantity of timber would it require? What manner of transportation methods did they use? To brave the storm surrounding the island. And how much time must it have taken? Just listing the respective conditions was enough to overwhelm the mind.

And that was to say nothing of how, even at a conservative estimate, the buildings abandoned on this island appeared to have stood for at least a century. Even were one to make full use of the latest technology of this era, building an entire island from top to bottom would be an extraordinarily herculean task, so it was impossible to imagine that there was any technology that made this feasible in so distant a past.
And if that was the case───
Then the technology in use here. Transcended existing conception───

source.japanese: あの老人に訊ねれば、もう少し仔細が判明したのだろうが、老人は長雨の間に姿を消していた。
source.english: They might have learned more by asking the old man. But he had vanished during the long rains.

target.text: If they could just ask that old man, the details would have been a little clearer, but the old man had vanished into the long spell of rain.

source.english: “Ah!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「───Ah!」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「どうしたの、航海士……」
source.english: “What is it, Mate…?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「What's the matter, mate……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「今なんか、そこの隙間からさ、なにかが動いて見えたような」
source.english: “Just now, through that gap. Thought I saw something moving.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Just now, I think I saw something moving, through that gap there.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「え、やだ……もしかして、ここらの骨を、
　全部骨にした奴かな……？」
source.english:
“Oh, no… Could it be whatever reduced all the creatures around here…
to bones?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Eh, no way……maybe it's the thing, that turned all these bones here into bones……?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「いや……さすがにそれは……大型の肉食獣を養っていけるくらいの獲物は、もうこの島には、いないと、思うんだけど……」
source.english: “No… Surely not… I don't think there's enough prey left on this island to support a large carnivore…”

source.japanese: なにかが奥歯に挟まったような物言いのキサラだった。
source.english: Kisara spoke as though something were caught between her back teeth.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「No……that's a little much…… there's no creature big enough to subsist on large predators left on this island, not anymore, I don't think, but……」
Kisara spoke as if something was stuck between her teeth.

source.japanese:
シサム・キサラが廃屋の床に身を低く伏して、島の根の音聴きとらんと聴覚へ全神経傾注していたのと同じ頃───
　朔屋も同じ島内にあり、奇しくも彼は彼で板目の上に倒れてあったのだが、こちらは仰向け大の字の、両手両足おっ広[ぴろ]げて、切れた足を生やし損ねててんで不格好な、陸に打ち揚げられた海星の態である。
source.english:
At about the same time that Sisam and Kisara were lying low upon a deserted house's floor, straining all their attention to hear the island's roots,
Sakuya was on that same island. By curious coincidence, he too lay upon its boards. But he was flat on his back, arms and legs spread wide: a starfish washed ashore, grotesquely shaped from failing to regrow a severed limb.

source.japanese:
降り続く雨は島内に上がると不思議に目が細かく、視界の中で漂い微風に舞ったりする様は面白い眺めではある。
　ただ海星なら水気と親しみもしようが、一音足らぬヒトにあっては、こうじくじくと水まみれとなると色々障[さわ]りにもなろう。過ぎたる湿気は諸病の元だ。
　だのに朔屋は、背に水が浸みるのも構わず、大の字なりにぐん伸びたまま。
source.english:
Once ashore, one found the unremitting rain strangely fine-grained; the way it drifted through one’s field of vision and danced upon the faint breeze made an entertaining spectacle.
A starfish might make a friend of wetness, but a mere man—one syllable the poorer and no fish at all—was liable to suffer all manner of inconvenience from such a clammy soaking. Excess moisture is the mother of maladies.
Yet Sakuya lay stretched to his utmost, arms and legs flung wide, indifferent to the water seeping into his back.

source.japanese: 見上ぐる天に蓋するは灰色雲の、幾重にも折り重なった雲塊の、濃淡様々に異なれど、人の時間を奪い取っては貯蓄するという謎の銀行員達が纏[まと]う衣と同じ色、眺めるうちに朔屋も時間の観念を奪われたか、彼の脳裏で一瞬裡に、長雨に船に閉ざされた数日間の幾つもの時間、出来事が輻輳した。
source.english: Gray clouds covered the sky he stared into. Layer upon layer, in varying shades, all the same color as the clothes worn by those mysterious bankers who stole people's time and stored it away. Perhaps the sight had robbed Sakuya of his own sense of time. In an instant, assorted hours and events from the rain-bound days aboard crowded into his head.

source.japanese: たとえば───
source.english: For example…

target.text: While Shisamu and Kisara lowered their bodies to the floor, devoting their entire nervous systems to their auditory perceptions in an effort to pick up the sound coming from the root of the island, around that same time─── Sakuya, too, was similarly on the island, and strangely enough, he, too, had collapsed onto the seams of the joined floorboards, but he was facing upwards, spread-eagle, arms and legs alike sprawled wide with all the grace of a starfish that had washed ashore and failed to regrow its severed arms.

The ever-falling drops of rain grew oddly fine upon arriving on the island, and watching how they danced and whirled in the gentle breeze within his vision did make for an amusing spectacle to behold. Were he but a starfish, then he would have had an affection for moisture, but as a mere human lacking that final syllable, it must have been rather harmful for him to be this sodden. Excessive moisture is the root of all manners of illness. (TN: This is a Japanese pun. Starfish, written "海星", is pronounced "hitode", while human is pronounced "hito".)
And yet Sakuya cared not, even as his back soaked in the water, and simply continued to lie on the floor with his limbs outstretched.

What covered the sky he gazed upon was a dome of gray, lumps of cloud intersecting and overlapping in countless layers, their depth and shade different one and all, yet each the same colour as the clothes worn by the enigmatic bankers who snatch people's time and stash it away, and as he beheld this, perhaps even Sakuya had his sense of time stolen, for in a brief instant, all the little happenings that had taken place while he was trapped on the ship veiled in endless rain these past few days converged within his mind.
For instance───

source.japanese:
船の食堂続きの厨房で、下級水夫達が白米を精[しら]げていた時の事。米は保存の観点から見ても優秀な穀物だが、ただし炊き上げるまでに他より余分に水が要求される。信天翁号ではよほど真水の貯蔵に余裕がない限りは食事に供される事少ないが、この度に限っては無尽蔵に降ってくる雨から水を取ればいいし、環礁内の波は比較的穏やかで、火を使っても火災の恐れは少ない。
　飯を炊くにはうってつけの好機であった。
　銀シャリの気配に釣られて厨房を覗いてみた朔屋は、そこで手伝いに駆り出されていたクロを見かけるも、声が掛けられない。
source.english:
There had been the time the junior sailors were polishing rice in the galley beside the mess. Rice kept admirably, but required more water than other grains before it could be cooked. The Albatross rarely served it unless fresh water was abundant. This time, though, they could draw from the limitless rain. The waves within the atoll were comparatively gentle, making a cooking fire less likely to cause a blaze.
An ideal opportunity for rice.
Lured by the prospect of gleaming white grains, Sakuya had peered into the galley. There he saw Kuro, pressed into helping, but could not speak to her.

target.text: It happened in the galley connected to the mess hall, back when the deck boys were polishing the rice. Rice is an outstanding grain from the perspective of conservation, however, boiling the rice will demand an excess of water compared to other grains. On the Albatross, as long as they did not have ample amounts of fresh water stored, rice was rarely served with their meals, but in this situation in particular, they could simply collect some of the inexhaustible supply of falling rain water, and the waves within the atoll were relatively gentle, so even should they use an open flame, there was little fear of a fire breaking out.

It was the perfect chance to boil some rice. Lured by the hints of freshly cooked rice in the air, Sakuya was peeking into the galley, but even as he spotted Kuro, who had been ordered to help out in there, he could not bring himself to call out to her.

source.japanese: あるいは───
source.english: Or…

target.text: Or perhaps───

source.japanese:
物見櫓に佇み、ぼんやり島の方を眺めるクロを見かけた事もあったが、朔屋はやはり呼びかけずにその場を立ち去った。
　あの後、老人はどこに消えたものだか姿を見せることはなかったし、島の方から怪しの声が聞こえてくることもなかった。クロを怯えさせる物事も特になく、取り立てて慰めてやる必要もない。
　だからクロにつきっきりでいることもない。
　……とは建前の、有り体に言って朔屋は、クロにいったいどんな面ぶらぶらぶら下げて接していいものやら、見当がつかなくなっていたのである。
source.english:
He had also seen Kuro standing in the lookout tower, gazing vaguely toward the island, and had gone away without calling to her. The old man had not appeared again after that night; where he had vanished, no one knew. Nor had the strange voice sounded from the island. Nothing in particular was frightening Kuro, so she required no special comforting. There was no need to remain forever at her side.
Such was his pretext. The truth was that Sakuya no longer knew what face he could possibly show her.

target.text: He had also spotted Kuro standing atop the watchtower, staring vacantly in the direction of the island, but ultimately, Sakuya took his leave without calling out to her. After all that, the old man had vanished to somewhere, but he hadn't shown himself since, and that suspicious voice coming from the island could no longer be heard either. There was nothing in particular that terrified Kuro, and so there was also no particular need for him to comfort her. Therefore, he didn't have to stick close to Kuro all the time. ……Such was his official stance, but putting it bluntly, Sakuya simply had not the first idea of how in the world he should act around Kuro.

source.japanese: 桟橋へ着けた信天翁号から、朔屋がこっそり島へ降りてみたのだって、船の中にいては遅かれ速かれクロと鉢合わせしてしまうだろうと、それを気に病んだ意気地無し。
source.english: Even his slipping ashore from the Albatross at the pier had been an act of cowardice. Remaining aboard, he would sooner or later run into Kuro. The prospect worried him.

target.text: Crossing the jetty the Albatross was anchored at, Sakuya had stealthily disembarked to the island, and even this was all because he knew that, should he stay on the ship, he would surely run into Kuro sooner or later; this left him anxious, spineless sissy that he was.

source.japanese: が、島に降りたところで心が落ち着く筈もなく、気もそぞろに木造の死街を歩む内に、疎かな足下を水気に取られた、派手に転んで背中を打ちつけて、のたうち回る内に立ち上がるのがなにか馬鹿馬鹿しくなって大の字なりに伸びたと、そういう次第である。
source.english: Going ashore could hardly settle his mind. Walking distractedly through the wooden dead town, he neglected his footing and slipped on the wet boards. He fell spectacularly, striking his back. While writhing about, he somehow began to find the idea of standing again ridiculous. Thus he had ended up lying spread-eagled.

source.japanese: どうにも億劫で立つ気力も湧かないが、このままだと、あの底知れぬ鬱の虚孔に落ちこんでしまいそうで、のろのろと身を起こした朔屋の、眉が怪訝にひそめられた。
source.english: He felt too weary to muster the will to stand. But staying like this seemed likely to send him down that bottomless hole of depression. He slowly sat up. Then frowned in puzzlement.

source.japanese: 建ち並ぶ廃屋の隙間を往く、白い影を見たからである。すわ廃址の亡霊と縮み上がってそこで、もしやと心づいて後を追う。
source.english: A white shadow moved through a gap between the deserted houses. He shrank in alarm—a ghost of the ruins! Then a thought struck him, and he followed.

target.text: But having disembarked to the island was itself not enough to set his heart at ease, and while he restlessly wandered about this dead town of timber, his careless feet were swept out from under him by the slick ground; he made a spectacular fall, struck his back, and as he writhed on the ground in pain, something about bothering to stand back up began to feel ridiculous, and so he remained on his back, spread-eagle; thus was this state of affairs brought about.

The act of standing up was so hopelessly bothersome to him that he simply could not muster the willpower to see it through, but if he remained like this, it seemed as if he might fall into that bottomless chasm of depression once more, and so Sakuya slowly raised his body off the ground, eyebrows knit together in puzzlement.

For he glimpsed a white shadow flitting through the gaps between the rows of abandoned houses. Goodness me───he flinched at the though of it being a ghost haunting these ruins, but perhaps, could it be, he realized, deciding to pursue it.

source.japanese: やがて朔屋は、島の一角で、廃屋の一つに入っていくクロを見かけた。彼女が一人であったのが不安で後を追ってみると───
source.english: Eventually, in a corner of the island, he saw Kuro entering one of the houses. Uneasy at her being alone, he went after her…

target.text: Before long, Sakuya saw Kuro enter a single building in a nook of the island. Concerned that she was by herself, when he then chased after her───

source.japanese: 窓の際に立ち、雨を眺めて佇むクロは戸口に背中を向けて、朔屋の気配に気づいた様子もない。
source.english: Kuro stood beside a window, watching the rain with her back to the doorway. She gave no sign of noticing Sakuya.

target.text: Standing by the window, Kuro had her back towards the door as she looked out at the rain, showing no sign of having noticed Sakuya's presence.

source.japanese: その背中にも、雫滴らせる白の髪にも、声で呼びかけるのが躊躇われる危うさ、儚さが垂れこめて、だから朔屋は、ぎしり、との木床の軋みを朔屋は敢えて鳴らした。が、鶯張りの、鳥が囀るように軽やかな、とはいかず、神経痛の老婆の呻吟のような音で軋んで、朔屋にも予想外に不気味であった。
source.english: Her back, and the white hair dripping upon it, carried a fragility that made him hesitate to call out. Instead, he deliberately made the floorboards creak. They did not sing lightly like birds upon a nightingale floor. They groaned like an old woman with neuralgia. Even Sakuya found the sound unexpectedly sinister.

source.japanese: ───音立てた本人してからたじろいだのだから、クロの反応もあながち過敏とは言えまい。
source.english: Even the man who had made the noise recoiled from it, so Kuro's reaction could hardly be called oversensitive.

target.text: That back, as well as the white hair dripping with moisture, all exuded a frailness, an ephemeral quality that made him hesitate in calling out to her, and so Sakuya, with a loud creak, deliberately stepped noisily down on the floorboards. But the light chirping of the Japanese bush warbler it was not; it creaked like the groaning of an old lady in the throes of neuralgia, a sound that was unexpectedly eerie even to Sakuya.
───And since even the man who made the noise himself flinched, Kuro's reaction could not necessarily be deemed overly sensitive.

source.english: “Eep!”

source.japanese: 蹠を真下から衝[つ]き上げられたかに、棒の姿勢で跳び上がって、踵がとすんと落ちて、ぐにゃぐにゃと崩れた、立ち上がろうとしたが、手足がばたばた床を叩いても、濡れ髪に埃を吸わせても、足下定まらず、どうやら、腰を抜かしてしまったようだった。
source.english: She sprang rigidly into the air as though struck from beneath the soles of her feet. Her heels landed with a thud; her body crumpled. She tried to stand, but however her hands and feet battered the floor, however much dust her wet hair gathered, she could not steady her legs. They seemed to have given way altogether.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……いや悪かった。
　驚かなくっていい。俺だよ」
source.english:
“…Sorry.
No need to be scared. It's me.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……それとも俺だから、
　びっくりしたのかな……」
source.english:
“…Or were you startled
because it's me…?”

source.japanese:
独りごちて、ともかく手を差し延べてクロを引き起こせば、朔屋と覚って幾らか安心したのか、がくがくともとらぬ膝ながらどうにか立ち上がる。
　埃を払ってやろうとしたのだが、重く濡れた上着はびたびたと景気の悪い音を立てるばかり。
source.english:
Muttering that to himself, he reached down and helped her up. Recognizing Sakuya appeared to reassure her somewhat. Her knees shook unsteadily, but she managed to stand.
He tried brushing off the dust, only for her sodden jacket to make dispiriting slapping sounds.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「───Pyuh!」

As if she had been pushed up from directly beneath the soles of her feet, she jumped into the air while stiff as a rod, then fell down heavily on her heels, limply teetering as she lost her balance and collapsed, and though she tried to rise once more, for all that her limbs flopped about and struck the floor, for all that her wet locks absorbed all the dust around her, she was unable to steady her footing; it seemed her knees had entirely given out on her.
【Naomasa】 「……Uhh, sorry about that. No need to be so shocked. It's just me.」
【Naomasa】 「……Or maybe you were shocked precisely because it is me……」

He mumbled thus to himself, but setting that aside, when he extended a hand to Kuro and pulled her back to her feet, perhaps she felt some form of relief upon realizing it was Sakuya, for though her knees continued to rattle, she still managed to stand once more. She tried to brush the dust off, but the heavy, sodden jacket only made a dreary, squelching sound.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そんなこと、ないよ。ちょっとびっくり。
　それだけ」
source.english:
“Not that. Just got a little fright.
That's all.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ま、警戒するのもわかるけどさ
　なんもしないよ、少なくとも今はさ」
source.english:
“Well, I can see why you'd be on your guard.
I'm not going to do anything. Not now, at least.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもクロ、そんなにびくびくするんなら、
　なにも島ン中に上がってこない方が良いんじゃないんか？」
source.english:
“But if it scares you so much, Kuro,
wouldn't you be better off not coming ashore?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───それとも、俺と同じ船ン中にゃ、いたくない、とかか」
source.english: “Or don't you want to be on the same ship as me…?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「That's not it at all. Just a bit surprised. That's all.」
【Naomasa】 「Well, I get why you're wary, but I'm not gonna do anything, at least not right now.」
【Naomasa】 「But, Kuro, if you're just gonna be shaking in fear like this, wouldn't it be better if you just didn't go on the island at all?」
【Naomasa】 「───Or maybe, you just don't want to be on the same ship as me, or something?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……その。クロは。
　クロは……あ、ぅ……」
source.english:
“…Well. Kuro…
Kuro… ah, uuh…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……いいよ。無理に喋ろうとしなくても。
　まあ、独りになりたい時もあるか……」
source.english:
“…It's all right. Don't force yourself to talk.
I suppose everyone wants to be alone sometimes…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「邪魔したな。俺は行くから。
　ただ、やっぱり独りじゃ危ないって思うぜ。
　水夫君達でも良い。
　一緒にいたほうが、さ。
　じゃあ、な……」
source.english:
“Sorry to bother you. I'll go.
But I still think being alone here is dangerous.
Even one of the sailors
would do. Better to have someone with you.
See you…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Uhm. Kuro is. Kuro is……ah, uh……」
【Naomasa】 「……It's fine. No need to force yourself to talk. Well, I suppose there's times when you want to be alone……」

【Naomasa】 「Sorry for the interruption. I'll be going now. It's just, I really do think it's dangerous for you to be alone. Even one of the sailors would be fine. To be together with here, that is. Alright, see you……」

source.japanese: 背を向けて、想いを殺して立ち去ろうとして、引いてきた力は柳の枝が絡んだかにか弱いものではあったけれど、朔屋が押し殺そうとした想いも一緒に掴んできたから、足はぴたりと止まった。
source.english: He turned away, suppressing his feelings, and began to leave. The pull that caught him was as weak as a willow twig winding about him. But it caught the feelings he was trying to suppress as well, and his feet stopped dead.

target.text: He turned his back to her, suppressed his emotions, and made to leave, but though the force that pulled on him was so feeble it might as well have been a willow branch that had tangled around him, it had also clutched the feelings Sakuya was attempting to stifle, and so his feet came to a halt.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……なんで。朔屋さん、たくさんしゃべる。
　でもなんで。クロ、見てくれない」
source.english:
“…Why? You say so much, Mr. Sakuya.
But why… won't you look at Kuro?”
“Huh?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Why? Sakuya-san says a lot. But why? Won't look at Kuro.」
【Naomasa】 「Huh?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「前は、クロの顔、見てくれてた。
　でも今は違ったよ。ずっとクロの頭の上ばっか」
source.english:
“Before, you looked at Kuro's face.
But not now. Just over Kuro's head, all the time.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロ、朔屋さんに怒られる、したのかな」
source.english: “Did Kuro do something to make you angry?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Before, looked at Kuro's face. But now was different. Always above Kuro's head.」
【Kuro】 「Did Kuro maybe do something to upset Sakuya-san?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「なら……ならクロごめんなさいするよ。
　クロがごめんなさいってしても。
　みんな。あんまり聞いてくれないけど」
source.english:
“Then… then Kuro'll say sorry.
Even when Kuro says sorry,
everyone… doesn't really listen.”

source.japanese:
向き直ればクロは、朔屋を見あげて真っ直ぐ視線を置いて、問いかけるのにも、詫びるにも、朔屋ただ独りを見つめて。
　あの夜、クロが老人と遭遇した夜、恐怖からの錯乱のあまり、前にいる朔屋をまるで見ずに、見えない誰かに詫びて回っていた時とは全く別、ただ朔屋だけに言葉を届かせようとしていた。
source.english:
When he turned, she looked straight up at him. Asking, apologizing, looking only at Sakuya. Quite unlike the night she had met the old man,
when her fear-stricken frenzy had left her blind to Sakuya in front of her, apologizing to invisible people. Now she was trying to make her words reach him alone.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Then……then Kuro will say sorry. But even if Kuro says sorry. Nobody. Really listens to it.」

When he turned back to face her, Kuro was looking up, her eyes directly on him; whether she was asking him something or apologizing to him, she fixed her gaze on nothing but Sakuya. Compared to that night, the night where Kuro had run into that old man, where the overwhelming derangement brought about from fear had left her all but incapable of seeing Sakuya as he stood before her, apologizing to some unseen someone instead, this was entirely different; she simply wanted her words to reach Sakuya and Sakuya alone.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「それでも……するから。
　だから朔屋さん。クロを怒らないで。
　クロを……いやって、しないでよう……」
source.english:
“Still… Kuro'll say it anyway.
So don't be angry, Mr.
Sakuya. Don't… don't hate Kuro…”

source.japanese:
自分の謝罪の言葉など、真面目に相手してくれる者はないと知りつつもクロは朔屋に謝って、何度も詫びて、謝られる謂[い]われも詫びられる理由もない青年を大いに戸惑わせたが、なにより朔屋の度を失わせたのは。
　くしゃりと、紙を握り潰したように歪んだクロの顔、その眸[ひとみ]に盛り上がっては溢れ出した涙。
source.english:
Knowing nobody took her apologies seriously, Kuro nevertheless apologized to Sakuya again and again, greatly bewildering him: she had nothing to apologize to him for. But what most unnerved him was her face.
It crumpled like paper crushed in a fist. Tears swelled in her eyes and overflowed.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Even so……Kuro will do it. So, Sakuya-san. Don't be upset with Kuro. Don't……hate Kuro, please……」

Though she was well aware that no one would earnestly listen to her words of apology, Kuro still offered them, apologized again and again, and since he had neither reason to receive an apology nor any cause that demanded someone beg him for forgiveness, the young man was left greatly bewildered at what to do, but there was one thing that made Sakuya lose his composure more than any other. Kuro's face was distorted, crumpled like a piece of paper being crushed in his hands, and within those eyes, tears welled up and spilled out.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ぅ、ふ……っ、ふぇ、ふぇぇぇぇぇ……」
source.english: “Uuh… uh… weh, weeeh…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ごべん、あざい……、
　もっ、泣かない、でも」
source.english:
“S-sorry…
Won't cry… but…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uh, fuh……, waah, waaaaah……」
【Kuro】 「So, wwy……, won't cry anymore, but.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「なんで……いつもとまってくれない、だろ、
　う……っ、ひぐ……っ、ぅぅぅぅ……っ」
source.english:
“Why… won't they ever stop…?
Uuh… hic… uuuuh…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「クロ、よう……っ」
source.english: “Kuro…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Why……can't make it stop, uh……hh, hic……, uuuuuh……」
【Naomasa】 「Kuro, hey……」

source.japanese: クロは、耐えきれず抱きしめたクロは。
source.english: Kuro—Kuro, whom he had been unable to keep from gathering into his arms—

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「んぅぅ～っ、だめぇ……だよう」
source.english: “Nnnh… Nooo… don't…”

source.japanese: 朔屋の腕の輪の中で身悶えして、胸板から顔を遠ざけようとして懸命に、抱擁を拒[こば]むまでに少女を哀しませてしまった自分に果てしなく慚愧して、だからこそ朔屋はクロを離そうとしなかったのだけれど。
source.english: She struggled within the circle of his arms, desperately trying to draw her face from his chest. The thought that he had saddened her enough to reject even his embrace filled him with endless shame. Precisely for that reason, he would not let her go.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「今日は、ほんっとに、なんもしないから。
　お前がいやがるような、裸にして、
　お前のあそこいじったりとか、
　そういうことはしないから」
source.english:
“I swear I won’t do a thing today.
I won’t do anything you’d hate—stripping you naked,
messing with you down there,
none of that.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ちが……の、クロのはなで……、
　おふく、汚れる……」
source.english:
“It's not… Kuro's nose…
it'll get your clothes dirty…”

source.japanese:
朔屋を拒絶するどころか。
　クロはどこまでも朔屋を案じて、けれどそれはどうにも自分を卑屈に貶める言葉で、
source.english:
Far from rejecting him,
