she was concerned for Sakuya throughout. But even that concern came in words that abased her.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなん誰が気にするか」
source.english: “Who cares about that?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だから、じっとしていてくれ。
　なんかその、俺まで泣きそうになる」
source.english:
“So hold still.
I'm… starting to feel like crying myself.”

target.text: Embraced by him after he could no longer bear it, Kuro───
【Kuro】 「Nnnuhh～, noo……you can't.」

Writhed and squirmed within Sakuya's arms, tried to pull her face away from his chest with utmost effort, and he felt endlessly ashamed for having made this girl so miserable that she would deny even an embrace from him; that was exactly why Sakuya did not let go of her, however.
【Naomasa】 「Today I really, truly will not do anything. Nothing you don't want. I won't strip you naked, won't grope around your crotch, nothing of the sort.」
【Kuro】 「That's not……it, Kuro's nose……, clothes will get dirty……」
Rejecting Sakuya? Nothing of the sort. Kuro was concerned for Sakuya to the last, but it was ever with denigrating words of self-abasement,
【Naomasa】 「Who would care about something like that?」
【Naomasa】 「So, just sit still for me. I, uh, I'm about to start crying too here.」

source.japanese: 鼻の根に力を入れてこみあげてくる涙を押し戻し、さっと屋内を見回せば、壁際にごたごたと押し遣られた調度類のひとまとめの中に椅子の一つ。引き出してくるのも性急だったのは、もたもたと間を開けていてはクロが逃げ出してしまうのではと恐れた為に。
source.english: He set his face, forcing back the tears that rose, and glanced around. A chair stood among the furniture shoved haphazardly against a wall. He hurried to pull it out, fearing that if he wasted time, Kuro might run away.

target.text: He clenched his radix to push back the tears that had begun to well up, and after throwing a quick glance around the room, he found a single chair amidst a collection of furniture shoved messily against the wall. He was impatient even in pulling out the chair, a consequence of his fear that Kuro might end up running away if he dawdled.

source.japanese: 肩を軽く押して座らせれば少女はことんと大人しく収まってくれたのに、ほっと胸を撫で下ろしつ、いったん前に回ってしゃがみこむ。
source.english: A light pressure upon her shoulders seated her. She settled meekly into the chair, and he breathed a sigh of relief before coming around and crouching in front of her.

source.japanese: ん、と頷[うなず]いてみせるのも、別段委細があるわけではなく、ただクロを安心させる為。背後に回る時も、怯えさせないように彼女の肩に手を置いたまま。とにかく朔屋は、クロの視界から外れる時は彼女の身体に軽く、触れた手を離さないようにと意識した。クロの不安、懸念を和らげてやるのに、それくらいしか思いつかなかったから。
source.english: He nodded: no special meaning, just reassurance. When he moved behind her, he kept a hand on her shoulder so as not to frighten her. Whenever he moved out of her sight, he made sure to keep a hand resting lightly on her. That was all he could think of to ease her anxiety.

target.text: When he gave a gentle push on her shoulders to sit her down on the chair, she settled right in without a fuss, so he heaved a deep sigh of relief, then made his way to the front of the chair and briefly squatted down.

He gave a visible nod of affirmation, not because he had any particular reason to, but simply to reassure Kuro. And when he walked back around her again, he also left a hand on her shoulder to keep her from getting scared. For now, whenever he was out of Kuro's field of vision, Sakuya was being very mindful of keeping his hand in gentle contact with the girl's body. He wanted to relieve Kuro's anxiety, her worries, and this was all he could think of to help.

source.japanese:
死街にかかる、風に巻かれてさらさらとたなびいて軽い雨粒に、朔屋は良く晴れた海上でのクロの髪をなんとなしに連想した。そうやってよく乾いている時は、少女の髪は僅かな気流や仕草にふわりふわりと腰がなく、舞う。普段目にしていた時は、クロの頼りなげな内面が髪の一筋にまで現れているようで、どうにも儚い、心細いもののように眺めていたのに、この島に来てから空気は何時でも水気を含んで重く、クロの髪も湿気を吸ってやや重苦しくうねった。
　そうなってみたらみたで、普段よりよほど消沈したような、と朔屋は、そこでふと腑に落ちた。
source.english:
The fine rain upon the dead town, winding in the breeze and streaming softly, reminded Sakuya of Kuro's hair on a clear day at sea. When dry, her hair floated and danced at the slightest movement or breath of air, with no body to it at all. He had usually seen it as frail and forlorn, her uncertain nature expressed in every strand. Since reaching the island, however, the air had always been heavy with moisture. Her hair absorbed it and hung in oppressive waves.
That made her look still more dispirited than usual. Suddenly he understood.

source.japanese:
この島に着いて以来、どうにもクロが何時にも増して所在なげに見えるのは、そういう見た目のせいもあるのか、と。
　彼女の髪を手拭いで扱き、水気を切ってやりながら。
source.english:
Perhaps her appearance was part of the reason Kuro had seemed even more lost since they reached the island.
He drew a cloth along her hair, squeezing out the water.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「違う、違うとお前は言う。
　そうだな、なんだかお前の言う事は、
　どうにもみんなにゃ届かない」
source.english:
“You keep saying, ‘No, that's not it.
That's not it.’ You're right.
Somehow nothing you say seems to get through to anyone.”

source.japanese:
物想う、朔屋はこの青年にしてはしんみりと、相手の胸に優しく浸みるような声音で語りかけながら、クロが先程から繰り返していた、否む言葉を自らの口に上[のぼ]せてみる。
　違う、違う、違う───自ら舌にしてみると、相手を否定して手で払いのけるというよりも、縋って詫びて、離れていこうとする衣の裾[すそ]を掴んで引き留めるような、そんな響きがあると朔屋は想った。
　先ほど繰り返したクロも、朔屋に縋[すが]るような心地だったのだろうか。
source.english:
Lost in thought, Sakuya spoke with an unusual tenderness, his voice seeming gently to seep into her heart. He tried the words of denial she had been repeating upon his own tongue. No, that's not it.
No, that's not it. No, that's not it… On his own lips, they sounded less like rejecting someone and waving them away than clinging and apologizing, catching at the hem of a departing garment to hold its wearer back.
Was that how Kuro had felt when she repeated them to him?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でも、今は俺も同じだ。
　違う、ていうよ」
source.english:
“But now it's the same for me. I'm saying,
‘No, that's not it,’ too.”

source.japanese: 手拭いで水気を切るといったって、朔屋の腰にぶら下げられていたそれは、先ほど木造の街の辻にぶち倒れていた折りに濡れてしまっていて、乾いた海綿に吸いこませるように、とはいかない。それでもクロの濡れてよじれる髪はぽたぽた毛先から滴らんばかりであったから、濡れ加減の手拭いでも扱いて髪をまとめてやる用には立つ。
source.english: The cloth hanging at his waist had been soaked when he fell in the wooden street. It could hardly absorb water like a dry sponge. Still, Kuro's tangled wet hair was all but dripping from its tips. Even a damp cloth could squeeze it out and gather it together.

source.japanese:
髪を時折軽く、くん、と引かれる感触にクロは、反射的に首筋を硬くする。そのせいもあってか、背後から見つめるクロの背中は、まだまだ硬く、打ち解けないように朔屋には思えた。その硬さを解[と]き解[ほぐ]すように、指先を白い髪の中に潜[くぐ]らせると、少なくと厭[いや]がる素振りは見せない。
　引っかけて痛みを与えないように、注意深く髪を指で梳[す]いていく。
　朔屋としては、なまじな性の愛撫より気を遣っていたのだった。
source.english:
Each faint tug at her hair made Kuro stiffen at the nape. Perhaps for that reason, her back still looked hard and unyielding to Sakuya. He slipped his fingers into the white hair as though to loosen that rigidity; at least she showed no dislike.
He combed carefully with his fingers, taking pains not to catch and hurt her. Sakuya was exercising more care than he ever brought to an ordinary sexual caress.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……なにが、ですか」
source.english: “…What's not?”

source.japanese:
問い返す、クロの声はまだ硬い。
　自分はまた余計な事を口にして、青年を閉口させたのではないかと懸念する風がある。
source.english:
Kuro's answering voice remained stiff.
She seemed afraid she had said one unnecessary thing too many and exasperated him again.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺は怒っちゃなんかないっての。
　むしろ俺は、クロのほうが怒ったり厭[いや]がったりしてるのかってさ」
source.english:
“I'm not angry.
If anything, I thought you were angry with me, or couldn't stand me.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「な、ないっ。クロ、ない。クロにはないですそんな。朔屋さんに厭[いや]がる、怒るはない、ないよ、ないからっ」
source.english: “N-no! Kuro doesn't! Nothing like that. Kuro's not angry with you, Mr. Sakuya. Kuro doesn't hate you. No, no, no!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「お……あ……落ち着けてって。
　いやだって、さぁ、あの時ほら」
source.english:
“C… c… calm down. I mean,
come on, you know, back then—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「二回目の時、お前を抱いちゃった時の」
source.english: “The second time—when I ended up sleeping with you—”

target.text: For some reason or another, the delicate drops of rain whirled around in the wind as they fell upon this town of death reminded him of Kuro's hair beneath the clear skies out at sea. During such times when it was dry, the girl's hair would flutter about wispily at the slightest breeze or movement, dancing through the air.

Usually, whenever he caught sight of it, it was as if Kuro's helpless inner self expressed itself through even the singular strands of her hair, and he would look upon Kuro as a thoroughly ephemeral, forlorn being, yet ever since they had first arrived at this island, the air had been heavy with moisture, and Kuro's hair, too, had absorbed the humidity, curling and twisting in a rather stifling manner. And now that her hair was soaked, she seemed in far lower spirits than usual; so Sakuya thought, and with that, it suddenly dawned on him.

Ever since arriving at this island, Kuro had seemed far more lost and unsure what to do with herself than usual, and perhaps that was also in part because of the way she looked, he mused. And while he ran a towel down her hair, gently squeezing out the moisture.
【Naomasa】 「That's not it, that's wrong, you say. You're right, it does kind of seem like whatever you say just doesn't really reach anyone.」

Lost deep in his own thoughts, while speaking in a tone of voice unusually intimate for this young man, the sort that softly sinks into the listener's heart, Sakuya tried vocalizing the words of denial that Kuro had been repeating for a time now with his own tongue.

That's not it, wrong, you're wrong─── when he tried putting it into words himself, it was not so much an attempt at denying the other and brushing them away, but instead clinging and apologetic, like clutching the hem of a garment about to slip away and trying to hold it in place; that was the emotion it resonated with, Sakuya felt. Then perhaps Kuro, who had repeatedly uttered these words just before, must also have felt like she was clinging to Sakuya?
【Naomasa】 「But right now, I'm no different. That's wrong, is what I'm saying.」

Though he was attempting to dry the water off with the towel, while hanging down from Sakuya's waist, that towel had already gotten wet when he had fallen onto the floorboards of an intersection in this wooden town earlier, so it could hardly be described as sucking up the moisture like a dry sponge. Even so, water still dripped down from the ends of Kuro's sodden, tangled hair, so even a damp towel was was fit for purpose to wring out and bundle up her hair.

In response to the occasional light tug of her hair, Kuro stiffened her neck reflexively. Perhaps that, too, was at fault, for as he looked down on Kuro from behind, her back was still rigid, as if she was not opening up to him, or so it seemed to Sakuya. In an effort to loosen that stiffness, he ran his fingertips through her white hair, and if nothing else, she didn't show any signs of disliking it. He attentively combed his fingers through her hair, careful not to catch on it and cause her pain. Sakuya, for his part, was actually exercising far more care here than during any of his half-hearted sexual petting.
【Kuro】 「……What is wrong?」
Asking the question back, Kuro's voice was still stiff. It carried a hint of worry that she would once more say something she shouldn't have, something that might make the young man tire of her.
【Naomasa】 「I told you, I'm not upset with you or anything like that. If anything, I'm the one worried that you might be upset with me, or even dislike me, Kuro.」
【Kuro】 「N-, no! Kuro isn't. Not Kuro, isn't nothing like that. Doesn't dislike Sakuya-san, isn't upset, at all, isn't, so!」
【Naomasa】 「Oh……ah……just calm down, please. Well, it's just, you know, back then, look.」
【Naomasa】 「Back when I made love to you, the second time.」

source.japanese:
口にしてしまえば沈黙の間の、朔屋が予想していた通りに案の定、重苦しい。静かな虚ろの癖に圧迫感を伴った無音が二人の間に垂れかかる。
　その間も、ゆっくりとだが休みなく動いてクロの髪を整えていく朔屋の指。こいつは悪くないぞ、と青年は想う。
source.english:
The silence that followed, as Sakuya had expected, was oppressively heavy. A quiet, hollow yet suffocating silence hung between them.
Even then, Sakuya’s fingers moved slowly but steadily, smoothing out Kuro’s hair. “This isn’t so bad,” the young man thought.

source.japanese: 異性に触れるというと、どうしても性交の手引きか前段階といった意識がつきまとう朔屋だったが、こうしてクロの髪を梳[す]いてやっていると、沈黙のきつさを和らげる効能のある。触れていたいのだ、黙っているのも会話を拒[こば]む為でなく、お互いの言葉を慎重に待っているだけなのだと、手つきで告げてやる事ができる。
source.english: To Sakuya, touching a woman almost inevitably meant either an invitation to bed or a step along the way. Yet running his fingers through Kuro's hair eased the strain of their silence. Through his hands he could tell her that he simply wanted to go on touching her—that their silence was no refusal to speak, only the two of them waiting carefully for each other's words.

target.text: Once he put it into words, sure enough, the silence between them was, just as Sakuya had expected it to be, oppressive. A long silence, accompanied by an intense pressure despite the void of sound, descended upon them both. Even during this, Sakuya's fingers continued to gently yet tirelessly work at fixing Kuro's hair. She's blameless in this, the young man felt.

Sakuya was the sort of man who, whenever he touched someone of the opposite sex, would have his every thought haunted by the idea that it was but the preliminary step leading into sexual intercourse, but as he combed through Kuro's hair like this, it had the effect of softening the harshness of the silence. I want to touch you, and this silence is not a refusal to speak, but instead us patiently waiting for the other to choose their words with care; he could communicate that through his hands.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……やっぱり、それなんだ……」
source.english: “……So that’s what it is, after all……”

source.japanese:
そうしてクロに触れていたから、彼女が落胆を滲ませ口にした時も、狼狽えず、自分の言葉を過[あやま]たず伝えてやれるだけの心の準備も整っていた。
　そればかりか、台詞を区切る合間に、外の小糠雨の静かな響きを、心を沈静させるようにクロに聞かせてやる事さえできた。二人の会話の中にも、ただ雨の静かに降り続く。
source.english:
Because he remained in contact with Kuro, the disappointment in her voice did not throw him into panic. He had time enough within himself to answer without mangling the truth.
More than that, in each pause he could let the fine rain outside speak softly to her and settle her heart. Even within their conversation, the rain went on falling.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうじゃなくって。
　あん時は、最後は泪さんと二人がかりだっただろ？」
source.english:
“That’s not what I meant.
Back then, in the end, it was me and Rui working together, wasn’t it?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やり過ぎちまって、申し訳ない気持ちで」
source.english: “I went too far, and I feel really sorry about it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そういう目で見るとさ、クロがなんか俺の事、怖がっているように見えたんだな」
source.english: “When I looked at it that way, it seemed like Kuro was kind of scared of me.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Figures it would be that……」

And because he touched her thus, even when despondency bled through her words, she kept her presence of mind, for she had mentally prepared herself to at least convey her own words without any mistakes. Moreover, in the pause between their lines, he was even able to let Kuro listen to the gentle drumming of the light drizzle outside in an effort to calm her mind. Even within their conversation, there was only the quiet, perpetual falling of the rain.
【Naomasa】 「Like I said, that's not it. Back then, in the end, I had to join forces with Rui-san, right?」
【Naomasa】 「I felt guilty, like I went too far.」
【Naomasa】 「And when I looked at things that way, it kind of seemed like you were, scared of me or something, Kuro.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロも、勘違い？　朔屋さんも？」
source.english: “So Kuro misunderstood too? And you did too, Mr. Sakuya?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そういうこと。馬鹿だな、俺達二人そろってな」
source.english: “That's right. Pair of idiots, aren't we?”

source.japanese: こくり、とクロの顎が前に軽く降りたのは、朔屋が後ろ髪を柔く引いた反動のせいだけではあるまい。二人の間に広がっていた溝を、言葉足らずの会話で、それでも雨の静けさと、髪という魂の端を架け渡して、梳いて、梳かれる事をよすがとして、埋め終えた事を了承する、頷きようだった。
source.english: Her chin dipped lightly. That could not merely have been the response to his gentle tug upon the hair at the back of her head. Their conversation had been poor in words, yet the stillness of the rain and her hair—the outermost reach of her soul—had spanned the gulf between them. Combing and being combed had given them a way across. Her nod seemed to acknowledge that the gulf had closed.

source.japanese: この時に朔屋は、この今だけでなく、これから先もこうやって少女の白い毛を梳[す]いてやるのもいい、むしろ自分からそれを望んでいると気づいたのは、一つの愛の、本人にもそれと告げない始まりであった。
source.english: Sakuya realized then that he would like to comb her white hair this way not only now, but in the days to come. Indeed, he wanted to. It was the beginning of a love that did not yet announce itself even to him.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro also……misunderstood? Sakuya-san too?」
【Naomasa】 「That's how it is. We're real idiots, the both of us.」

When Kuro's chin dropped slightly forwards, it was not just a reaction to Sakuya gently pulling on the hair on the back of her head. By way of their conversation that, while tongue-tied, still held the serenity of the rain, as well as by forming a bridge with the strands of her soul that was her hair through the act of combing and being combed, the chasm that had been widening between them had now been filled once more; it was akin to a nod acknowledging that.

In this moment, it dawned on Sakuya that he would be glad to comb through the girl's white hair like this, and not just in the now, but in the future as well, or rather, he realized that he himself was the one who wanted to; that was when a love began to bloom, one that went unheralded even to the man himself.

source.japanese:
クロはといえば、椅子の上で膝を抱きかかえ、ちょんと小さく収まって、少しずつ緊張を解かして、軽く椅子を揺すったりなぞの、どうにもその辺りは稚気な悪戯。ことん、ことんと小さく鳴る椅子の脚に、ふと朔屋はかつてのこの廃屋の、木造の島の住人達を想像した。
　今日初めて島に揚がった青年だが、それでも船の他の乗り組み達と同じく奇妙な点を感じ取っている。まずこの島の経てきた歳月だ。それが全く見当がつかない。ただ朔屋が盆暗であるから、というだけでもなかろう。
source.english:
Kuro, meanwhile, sat tucked small into the chair with her knees clasped. Her tension loosened little by little; she even began to rock the chair, a childish bit of mischief. The soft knocking of its legs made Sakuya imagine the former inhabitants of this house, of this wooden island.
He had come ashore for the first time today, but, like the other crew members, already sensed its oddities. First, how many years had the island seen? He had no idea. Surely that was not merely because he was dim-witted.

source.japanese: それに、建築様式のあたりが着かない。西洋風にも東洋風にも見える。それは、朔屋達が知る、東洋も西洋も関係のない文化洋式にあった事を語っていないか。そして、島のあちこち至るところに遍在している生き物達の骨だ。水夫長の言葉を信じるなら、太古に絶滅した生き物達の骨も混ざっていたそうで、しかもそれが他のものと、見たところ古さの段階が変わらなかったという。
source.english: Nor could he place its architecture. It looked both Western and Eastern. Didn't that suggest a culture unrelated to the East and West they knew? Then there were the bones of creatures everywhere upon the island. If the boatswain was to be believed, some belonged to animals extinct since remote antiquity. Yet they had apparently looked no older than the rest.

target.text: As for Kuro, she was sitting on the chair, hugging her knees, making herself smaller, gradually easing her tense body, amusing herself with what could only be a spot of childish mischief by gently rocking the chair back and forth. As he heard the legs of the chair clack against the floor, Sakuya's thoughts suddenly jumped to imagining the inhabitants who once lived on this island of timber, within these abandoned houses.

Today was the very first time this young man had stepped foot on the island, but even so, he still picked up on the same points of peculiarity as the rest of the crew. First, there was the issue of how many years this island had seen. He had not the first clue. And this could not merely be blamed on Sakuya being a thickheaded simpleton.

Furthermore, he also couldn't place the architectural style. It looked both Western and Eastern. Or perhaps, could that not instead suggest the existence of some other foreign culture, one entirely unrelated to either the Western or Eastern ones Sakuya and the rest knew of? And then, there was the bones of creatures ubiquitously present all over the island. If the words of the Bosun were to be believed, there were apparently even bones of creatures that went extinct in ancient times mixed in, and what's more, as far as he could tell, they looked to be at the very same stage of aging.

source.japanese: ───これらの事から朔屋が思い浮かべたのは、この島は朔屋達の未だ知らざる、地図に未記載の世界の果てから島ごと、嵐を共に漂流してきて、この位置に落ち着いたのではないかという、日頃脳天気な朔屋にしても、荒唐無稽に過ぎる推測、いやさ妄想なのだった。朔屋の脳内で妄想は活発に膨らみ、たとえばクロが座っているこの椅子一つ取っても、かつてこれに座していた住人は、果たして朔屋達と同じ姿形を有していたのかそれさえ怪しい、否、それどころか朔屋がその形状から勝手に椅子と思いなしているだけで、全く別の用途に充てられていた事だってあり得るではないか。
source.english: From these things, Sakuya imagined that the entire island, together with its storm, had drifted from some unknown edge of the world absent from their maps and settled here. Even for his usually carefree mind, this was too extravagant a conjecture—no, a delusion. It swelled busily in his head. Take the chair Kuro sat in: had its former occupant even possessed the same shape as they did? That was doubtful. Indeed, perhaps it was not a chair at all. He had simply assumed so from its shape, when its purpose might have been quite different.

source.japanese: そしてこの島自体も、かつてあった場処で、既に世紀どころか万の単位でもって歳月を数えており、外気に当てればたちまちのうちに崩壊するところを島の周囲に滞留する嵐が、外界から島を隔絶させ護っているのではないか。
source.english: And perhaps, in its former location, the island had counted its years not in centuries but tens of thousands. Exposure to the outside air might make it collapse at once. Could the storm lingering about it be protecting it, keeping it isolated from the outer world?

source.japanese:
嵐、嵐か───元が注意力散漫な朔屋だけに、思考は横道に出会う度にそれまでの道筋から逸れていく。嵐───クロが待望して止まないもの。嵐の中にあればクロは、人並み以上の知力心力を発揮して、彼女一人だけでも世界に屹然と対峙して生きていけよう。自分などよりよほど立派に、賢明に。
　嵐の時の、船長であるクロを思い浮かべると、心がどうにも落ち着きを無くす。ああなったクロは、このように自分がべたべた触れる事など、嫌悪、忌避するのではないか───
source.english:
A storm. The storm… With his scattered attention, Sakuya's thoughts wandered off whenever they met a side path. The storm: what Kuro longed for without cease. In a storm she displayed more than ordinary intelligence and strength of mind. Alone, she could stand firmly against the world and live.
Far better, far more wisely than he. Imagining Kuro as the captain she became in a storm unsettled him. Would that Kuro recoil from him touching her so familiarly?

target.text: ───Based upon these circumstances, Sakuya imagined thus: was it not possible that this island had drifted here together with the storm, hailing from somewhere at the ends of the world, from a place yet unknown to Sakuya and company, unmarked on any map, before settling in this place? Even for someone as habitually carefree as Sakuya, this was an excessively absurd conjecture, no, it was outright delusional.

Within Sakuya's brain, these delusions expanded vigorously: for example, consider just the chair that Kuro was sitting on; it was questionable whether the residents who had once sat on this chair actually even held the same form as Sakuya and the rest, nay, if anything, Sakuya might well just have assumed it to be a chair from its shape, but was it not entirely plausible that it had once served a completely different purpose?

And then there was this island itself: could it not be the case that, in the location it had once occupied, its age would already be counted not in centuries but millennia, and were it to be exposed to the open air, it would crumble in the blink of an eye, and so the storm lingering in its surroundings was actually isolating the island from the outside world, protecting it?

Storm, the storm───given that Sakuya was a man whose mind was prone to wander by nature, his thoughts would stray from their prior path each and every time he came across a detour. The storm───the unceasing one that Kuro so eagerly desired. Were she within a storm, Kuro would demonstrate an intelligence and force of will far above the average; the girl seemed able to live on in a solitary showdown against the very world itself, towering over all. Far more admirable, sagacious, than the likes of himself.
When he thought of Kuro during a storm, as the Captain, his heart would always grow unsteady. Once she became like that, would Kuro not feel disgusted, repulsed at him touching her so intimately───?

source.japanese: ……朔屋の懸念が感応したのか、クロが思い立ったように問いかけてきたのも、覚醒したる自分自身の話題だった。
source.english: Perhaps his anxiety reached her. Kuro's sudden question, too, concerned her awakened self.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さんは───クロがもしずっと頭良いままだったら、クロのこといや？」
source.english: “Mr. Sakuya… if Kuro stayed clever all the time, would you hate Kuro?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「たぶん……そうなんじゃないかな。あの時のお前さんは、滅茶苦茶すごいからさ。俺なんか足下にも寄れない、カミサマみてえな船長だ」
source.english: “Probably… I suppose so. You're incredible then. I couldn't come anywhere near you. A captain like a god.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうまで凄い相手にゃ、
　俺はちょっと近寄れないなあ」
source.english:
“I can't really get close
to somebody that amazing.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だって、俺もどうしようもない役立たずだしさあ。だから、お前さんは俺の事を優しいなぞと言い寄るが、そいつもどうやら違うだろう」
source.english: “I'm useless myself, after all. So you keep calling me kind, but I don't think that's right either.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺より可哀相なお前さんだから、俺は優しくできるんだよ……ああ、言っちゃった」
source.english: “I can be kind to you because you're more pitiful than me… Ah. Said it.”

source.japanese:
朔屋がそれをぶちまけてしまったのは、クロが彼に寄せる信頼、厚意の前に、飾りたくないと想ったからか、それとも、偽善であるより偽悪を気取った方が、この場の気分にそぐったためか。どちらにしても、正直に打ち明けていい事と悪い事もあろうに。
　ただ朔屋は、生のままの自分を体ごとぶつけてくるクロに、下手なお為ごかしで相手する事はできなくなっていたのだ。
source.english:
Had Sakuya blurted that out because he did not want to dress himself up before her trust and affection? Or did playing the villain simply suit the mood better than playing the hypocrite? Either way, there were things one should and should not honestly confess.
But with Kuro offering him her whole unvarnished self, he could no longer answer with clumsy, self-serving platitudes.

target.text: ……Perhaps she was sensitive to Sakuya's worries, for Kuro posed a question as if it had suddenly sprung to mind, and it was on the subject of her own awakened self.
【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san, would─── if Kuro always stayed smart, would Sakuya-san not like Kuro?」
【Naomasa】 「Probably……wouldn't, I don't think. When you're like that, you're just so incredibly amazing. Someone that the likes of me could never hold a candle to, a godlike Captain.」
【Naomasa】 「And I think I'd find it difficult to approach someone that amazing.」
【Naomasa】 「Because I'm also just a hopeless good-for-nothing, you know? So, you keep telling me I'm kind and all that, but I don't think that's quite right.」
【Naomasa】 「You're more pathetic than I am, and that's why I can be kind to you…… aah, there, I said it.」

Did Sakuya end up blurting it all out because he did not want to put on airs in the face of the trust and affection Kuro felt for him, or was it instead because he felt that acting the villain suited the mood here better than being a hypocrite? Regardless of which, he did honestly lay bare his heart for her, be it for good or bad. It was simply that, with Kuro having thrown the full weight of her raw, unadorned self at him, Sakuya could no longer bring himself to meet her with transparent attempts at insincere, self-serving kindness.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……あんね、朔屋さん。ほんとはね。優しい人は、時々いてたよ」
source.english: “…You know, Mr. Sakuya. There were kind people sometimes. Really.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でもそういう人たちは、クロとお話は、してくれなかった。朔屋さんみたいに、厭な、本当のことまで、話してなんかくれなかった」
source.english: “But they didn't talk with Kuro. Not like you. They didn't tell Kuro true things—even the unpleasant ones—the way you do.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「それにね、何よりね。
　クロを、女の子だって。
　言ってくれたのも、時々いてた。
　でも───ああいうふうに、抱いてくれたのは───朔屋さんだけで」
source.english:
“And you know,
more than anything…
Sometimes there were people who’d say Kuro was a girl.
But—the only one who ever slept with me like that was… Mr. Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Uhmm, Sakuya-san. The truth is. There were kind people, now and then.」
【Kuro】 「But those kinds of people wouldn't really talk to Kuro. Wouldn't talk to Kuro, about the unpleasant truths, like Sakuya-san does.」
【Kuro】 「And then, most of all. Even Kuro is a girl too. Would tell Kuro that, sometimes. But───being made love to like that───only Sakuya-san did that.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でも。なのに。朔屋さん、あれから。
　クロを困った目で見るよう、なったよ。
　クロは朔屋さんに抱かれて、
　いけないかったのかな」
source.english:
“But… even so… Mr. Sakuya, ever since then…
you’ve started looking at Kuro with that troubled look.
Was it wrong
for Kuro to sleep with you?”

source.japanese:
ぽつぽつと、かつて出会った人達の事を語りながら、瞼の裏に蘇らせるように面を伏せる、クロの後ろ髪が朔屋の指に分けられて、項を覗かせる。何処をどう贔屓目に見ても華奢に過ぎて、壊れ物のようであるのは出会った時から変わらない。
　なのに窓からの雨にくすんだ光の中に浮かぶその背、項、呟く言葉は、青年の心にしみじみと染みいるような風情を湛えてあり、随分と様変わりをしたようにもみえる。
　そうさせたのは、もしや自分なのかと、鈍感な朔屋は今にして実感し、何やら鼓動の速まる想い、持て余す。
source.english:
She spoke in fragments of people she had known, lowering her face as though to summon them behind her eyelids. Sakuya's fingers parted Kuro's hair and bared her nape. Even viewed in the kindest light, she was as frail, as much like some breakable object, as on the day they met.
And yet her back, her nape, the words she murmured in the rain-muted light—all seeped into the young man's heart, and she seemed greatly changed. Only now did the oblivious Sakuya wonder if he might be the cause. He did not know what to do with the thought. His heart beat faster.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「それ、考えてたら。ううん、ほかにもいろいろ。でも、なんか、怒られるよりぶたれるより哀しくなって。一人でいたかった。でも一人だともっと、哀しかった」
source.english: “I was thinking about that. No, there were other things, too. But somehow it made me sadder than getting scolded or beaten. I wanted to be alone. But being alone made me feel even sadder.”

source.japanese:
クロ、船内にあっても、いや、何処にあっても、大勢の中で独りぼっちのクロ。
　それは多分、きっととても、哀しい事なのに、彼女自身が一人である事の孤独を知ったのも、朔屋のせいではないか。
　朔屋がそのようにしてしまったのではないか、この少女を一人の女のように抱いてしまって。
source.english:
Kuro: alone among the crowd aboard ship, alone wherever she went.
Surely that was terribly sad. Yet had Sakuya also taught her to recognize the loneliness of being alone?
Had he done this to her by embracing her as a woman in her own right?

source.japanese:
───朔屋は、この期に及んで往生際の悪い事甚だしい。廃屋内の右を見た。左を見た。後ろにも目をやった。
　けれど今日は、泪はいなかった。だが泪がいたとして、どうするつもりだったのかと自答する。
　また彼女に縋[すが]るのか？　この子をどうあやしてやればいいのかと教えを請うのか？
source.english:
—Even now Sakuya clung disgracefully to escape. He looked right across the abandoned room, then left, then behind him.
Rui was not there today. But what, he asked himself, would he have done if she were? Clung to her again? Begged her to teach him how to comfort Kuro?

source.japanese:
幾らなんでもそれは違うだろう、と朔屋は自嘲する。違うとは思う、でもどう応えてやればいいのか、女の肌は幾つか知っていても、その心深くにまで踏み入った経験の薄い朔屋は、今にしてこの手の事柄に関しては、自分もクロと大差ないのだと認めるしかなかった。クロと同じで、考えれば考えるほど思考の袋小路に嵌[はま]って抜け出せなくなる。
　なら、どうしたいのだろうと自答する。
source.english:
Even he could see that would be wrong. Yet knowing it was wrong did not tell him how to answer. Sakuya knew the skin of several women but had seldom ventured into the depths beneath it; in matters of the heart, he now had to admit, he was scarcely better equipped than Kuro. Like her, the more he thought, the farther he wandered into a blind alley.
Then what did he want? He asked himself again.

source.japanese:
クロと一緒にいて、厭なのか？
　───もう一度部屋を見回す。森閑とした廃屋は、雨の中で多少ひんやりとしていたけれど、その隔絶された雰囲気が、朔屋に居心地の良さをもたらしている、中でクロの存在はけして邪魔ではなく、どころか、二人で安穏と隠れているかの安らぎさえ感じさせている。
　それでは、この細く痩せた身体は、嫌いか？　好みの問題で言えば確かにこれまでの朔屋の嗜好にはない身体だったけれど云々云々、とまた自分が、慣れない事をしているのに気がついた。
　女と見れば自分はどうしていたのかと、朔屋は思い出す。
　クロの華奢な肩を見ても、自然にやり方を思い出していた。
source.english:
Did he dislike being with Kuro?
—He looked around the room once more. The deserted house, hushed beneath the rain, was a little chilly, yet its seclusion put Sakuya strangely at ease. Kuro’s presence was no intrusion; on the contrary, it lent him the peace of imagining the two of them hidden away here together.
Then did he dislike this slender, wasted body? Granted, as a matter of taste it bore little resemblance to the bodies Sakuya had favored before, et cetera, et cetera—and there he was again, doing something that did not come naturally to him.
What had he always done when he saw a woman? Sakuya remembered.
One look at Kuro’s delicate shoulders, and the way of it came naturally back to him.

source.japanese: それに、次の台詞が、朔屋の心の天秤にことんと載って、皿を一方に落としたのだった。
source.english: Then Kuro's next words dropped with a small, decisive weight upon the scales in Sakuya's heart, sending one pan down.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But. Even so. Sakuya-san, since then. Began looking at Kuro, with troubled eyes. Kuro wonders if it was a bad thing, that Kuro was made love to by Sakuya-san.」

While she spoke haltingly of the people she had met in the past, she lowered her face as if the memories were brought back to life behind her closed eyelids, and the hair on the back of her head was parted by Sakuya's fingers, the nape of her neck peeking through. No matter how favourable a light he tried to view it in, it was simply too delicate, its fragility unchanged since the day they first met.

And yet, silhouetted against the rain-dimmed light shining through the windows, her back, the nape of her neck, as well as her murmured words carried an air that seeped deeply into the young man's heart, making her seem utterly transformed in his eyes. And the one responsible for this change was, perhaps, none other than himself; in this instant, it sank in for the otherwise insensitive Sakuya, an emotion that made his heart race, growing beyond his control.
【Kuro】 「And then, when Kuro thought that. No, many other things too. But, somehow, it made Kuro sadder than being scolded, or being hit. Wanted to be alone. But being alone only made Kuro sadder.」

Kuro───even when aboard the ship, no, anywhere she went, Kuro was alone in a crowd. That might have, no, it surely must have been a terribly sad affair, but could it not also have been Sakuya's fault that the girl herself had come to know the loneliness of being alone? Was it not Sakuya who had caused this, after making love to this girl as if she were a grown woman?

───Even now, Sakuya was still being unreasonably stubborn in his unwillingness to give up. He looked to the right inside the abandoned building. Looked to the left. He even looked behind himself. But today, Rui was not present. However, even supposing Rui had been here, what did he even intend to do with that, he asked himself. Would he once more cling to the woman? Would he beg her to tell him how he should go about comforting this girl?

No matter how you look at it, that is surely not right, Sakuya thought in self-deprecation. He did think it wrong, but how was he meant to respond to this? Though he had sampled the fruits of many a woman, Sakuya had precious little experience with delving into the depths of the heart, and right now, he had to admit that when it came to matters of this sort, he was hardly any better than Kuro. And just like Kuro, the harder he thought about it, the deeper he got stuck in mental dead ends, unable to break out. So then, what do I want to do, he asked himself.

Was being with Kuro something he found disagreeable? ───Sakuya surveyed the room once more. The silent house was somewhat chilly in the rain, but this secluded atmosphere actually brought a feeling of comfort to Sakuya, and Kuro's presence within it certainly did not spoil it by any means, anything but; it even left him with a peace of mind, as if the two of them were hiding away together in complete tranquility.

So then, did he dislike this thin, skinny body? If it came down to personal preference, then certainly, her body did not match Sakuya's preferences hitherto, and so on, but then, he realized that he was doing something out of character yet again. When he laid eyes on a woman, what was it he used to do, Sakuya recalled. Even when looking at Kuro's slender shoulders, he naturally remembered how to do it.
Furthermore, her next line landed on the scales of Sakuya's heart with a thunk, causing one of the plates to drop all the way down.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さん、いた。いてくれた。
　クロ、ほんとは嬉しかったの」
source.english:
“Mr. Sakuya, you were there. You were there for me.
I was actually really happy.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でも朔屋さんは、やっぱりクロ、
　見てくれなくて。
　それでなんか……涙出ちゃって」
source.english:
“But Mr. Sakuya…
he still wouldn’t look at me.
So I just… started crying.”

source.japanese:
朔屋は───クロを背後から抱きしめていた。細い肩、折れそうな首、砕けてしまいそうな薄い胸、すっぽりと自分の中に。抱きたい。こうして。それとももしかしたら、もっと生の、おとことおんなで繋がるように抱きたいのかも知れない。
　けれどこの今はこれでいい。こうして、そっと胸の中に収めるだけでいいと朔屋は、腕に優しい力を籠める。
　こわれものを扱うようにではなく、大事なものを慈しむように、優しく力を籠めた。
source.english:
Sakuya was holding Kuro from behind. Her slender shoulders, the neck that seemed ready to snap, the shallow chest that might shatter—he gathered all of her within himself. He wanted to hold her. Like this. Or perhaps he wanted the rawer embrace in which man and woman joined their bodies.
For now, this was enough. It was enough to contain her softly against his chest. Sakuya tightened his arms—not as one handles a breakable object, but as one cherishes something precious.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なんかさ。クロの事、こうやってきゅって抱きしめたくなった」
source.english: “…Somehow, I just felt like holding you tight like this.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こうしてても、まだ、
　涙、出てきそうか？」
source.english:
“Do you still feel like crying,
even now?”

source.japanese: ───クロは、首を横に振ってから、肩口に乗った朔屋の顎に頬を寄せる、その目尻にはまだ涙が残っていたけれど、もう滲んでは来ない、あとは乾くだけだろう。
source.english: Kuro shook her head, then nestled her cheek against the chin Sakuya had rested upon her shoulder. Tears remained at the corners of her eyes, but no more welled up. They would dry now; that was all.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san was there. Was there for Kuro. Kuro was actually really happy.」
【Kuro】 「But in the end, Sakuya-san still wouldn't look at Kuro. And then, for some reason…… the tears just came.」

Sakuya───embraced Kuro from behind. Her narrow shoulders, her fragile neck about to snap, her chest so flat he might end up crushing it, it all fit snugly within his arms. I want to hold you. Like this. Or maybe, just maybe, I want to hold you in a more raw way, one that connects us as man and woman. But for now, in this present, this was fine. It was enough to simply stay like this, softly holding her close to his chest, Sakuya thought, a tender strength coursing through his arms. Not the sort that treated her as something that could break apart at the slightest touch, but to cherish what he cared deeply for: a tender strength.
【Naomasa】 「……You know, for some reason. I just really felt like giving you a big hug like this, Kuro.」
【Naomasa】 「And when we're like this, do you still feel like you're about to cry?」

───After shaking her head back and forth, Kuro drew her cheek closer to Sakuya's chin resting on her shoulder, and while tears yet remained in the corners of her eyes, they no longer welled up; all that was left was for them to dry.

source.japanese: 一方。何時忍び寄ったのか、窓からこっそり覗き見していたのがこの二人、航海士の双子にて。
source.english: Meanwhile, two people had crept up unnoticed and were peeking through the window: the twin navigators.

source.japanese: 屋内の朔屋は、先ほど中をしげしげと見回したはずなのに、何故だか窓にだけは目を向けていなかったという粗忽者なので、二人の存在を針の先程も感知していない。クロに於いてはなにをかいわんやだ。
source.english: Careless Sakuya had looked all about the room earlier, but somehow not at the window. He had not the faintest inkling of their presence. Kuro, needless to say, knew still less.

source.japanese: そして双子はと言えば───大層、ご立腹のご様子で御座る。
source.english: As for the twins… they were most displeased indeed.

target.text: Meanwhile. It wasn't clear when exactly they'd stolen up on the window, but the two of them were furtively peeking inside through it; it was the twin first mates.

Though Sakuya within the building must have looked through the entire room several times just now, he was the sort of careless man who, for whatever reason, neglected to pay any attention to the window alone, and so he did not pick up on even a hint of the duo's presence. Kuro didn't even bear mentioning.
And as for the twins───they appeared to be tremendously wroth.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「っけ！　舌っ足らずと馬鹿がつるんで、傷のちゅっぱちゅぱしゃぶり合い、ときゃーがった」
source.english: “Tch! The tongue-tied one and the idiot, pairing off to suck each other's wounds. Slurp, slurp.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Feh! A tongue-tied brat and a retard clinging to each other, slobbering all over each other's wounds, disgusting!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「うっわ。そこまで言わなくってもさ。
　しっかし朔屋もまあ……。
　アレに、手を出すふつー？
　なんか怪しいとは思ってたけど」
source.english:
“Whoa. You didn't have to go that far.
But still, Sakuya…
Who normally makes a move on that? I knew there was something fishy going on,
though.”

source.japanese:
……廃址の中を歩むクロに気づいたのは朔屋だけではない。シサムかキサラかどちらが先かは知らねど、双子も廃屋の狭間にクロの白を目にしていて、この島になにをしに来たかと怪しんで後をつけてみればこれである。クロはクロで、自分が悪目立ちする事をいい加減自覚するべきだと思われる。
　ともあれ双子は、廃屋の窓の木枠の下に、熱帯の派手な色合いの蜥蜴のようにへばりつき、耳聡い兎のように中に耳澄まし、そして、燃やしていたのは、どこぞの多神教の主神、その奥様のお得意であられるところの───
source.english:
Sakuya was not the only one who had noticed Kuro walking through the ruins. Whether Sisam or Kisara saw her first was unknown, but the twins, too, had caught a glimpse of her white figure between the houses. Wondering what she was doing ashore, they followed. And found this. Kuro really ought to have realized by now how conspicuously she stood out.
In any event, the twins clung beneath the wooden window frame like brilliantly colored tropical lizards, listening with the sharp ears of rabbits. And what burned within them was the particular specialty of the wife of the chief god in a certain polytheistic religion…

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Woah. No need to go that far. But damn, Sakuya……. You actually made a move on that? I did have a feeling something was fishy here, but still.」

……Sakuya was not the only one to notice Kuro wandering around the ruins by herself. While it wasn't clear which of Shisamu or Kisara had noticed her first, the twins had also spotted the white of Kuro in the gaps between the buildings; suspicious of what she'd come to the island for, when they then proceeded to tail her, this is what they arrived to. One should think it high time that Kuro ought to finally grow aware of the fact she stuck out like a sore thumb.

In any case, below the wooden frame of the window of the abandoned house, the twins stuck to the wall like a pair of brightly coloured tropical lizards, their ears peeled for any sound within like sharp-eared rabbits, and last but not least, were burning up with that which happens to be the forte of the wife of the king of the gods of a certain polytheistic religion───

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「見てらんないったらない。
　腹まで立ってきたわっ、
　行くよ、行くったらキサラっ」
source.english:
“I can't watch this. It's starting
to piss me off.
Come on, Kisara. We're going.”

source.japanese:
かの女神の得意技だ、嫉妬心という。
　双子は側にあるのが片割れだけだったから、それぞれの心境隠しもせなんだが、これでもし他人に見られていたなら、そ奴は恐らく……二度と日の目を見られないだろう。
source.english:
That goddess's favorite art: jealousy.
With only her other half beside her, neither twin concealed her feelings. Had anyone else witnessed them, however, that person would probably… never see daylight again.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I can't stand watching this. My blood's beyond boiling, I'm out! I said we're going, Kisara!」

The speciality of a certain goddess, a heart ablaze with the green flames of envy and jealousy. With only their other half there beside them, the twins made no efforts to conceal their inner feelings, but supposing this were to be witnessed by another, that poor soul would, in all likelihood……never see the light of day again.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんでそこまで怒ってんのさ。
　朔屋があっこまで節操なかったから？」
source.english:
“Why're you so mad?
Because Sakuya had so little self-control?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Why are you getting so angry? Because Sakuya's been making a move on everything with a pulse so far?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「違うよ、羨ましいの、クロが。
　ありゃ、連れ合い見つける勢いだよ、
　あたしらより先に───」
source.english:
“No. I'm jealous of Kuro.
At this rate she'll find herself
a partner before we do…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Not that, I'm just envious. Of Kuro. Just look at that, she's well on her way to snag a husband, and ahead of us at that───」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あ。なんか言われてみると腹立ってきた」
source.english: “Oh. Now that you mention it, I'm starting to get pissed off too.”

source.japanese: 双子は腹立ちのあまりどすどす長靴を板敷きの通り叩きつけていこうとして、すぐに中の二人に気づかれると思い直してそろそろと、そんな風に二人からこそこそと隠れていると思い知ってしまってはまた苛立ちのめらめらと。
source.english: So angry were they that they almost stomped their boots down the boarded street. Then they remembered the two inside would hear them, and crept away softly. Realizing they were sneaking about, hiding from those two, only made their irritation blaze harder.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Ah. Now that you mention it, my blood's also beginning to boil.」

Fuming with rage, the twins were moments away from slamming their boots against the boards covering the street before catching themselves, realizing that the two inside would notice them immediately; they tiptoed away, but the bitter realization that they were sneaking around and hiding from those two like that only fueled their seething, making their anger flare up all over again.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……それから。まだ、あるです」
source.english: “…And… there's something else.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なんがだ？　もうこの際全部話しちまえ」
source.english: “…What is it? You might as well tell me everything now.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ん……あい。それはなにか。少し、思い出してきた感じ、するです」
source.english: “Mm… yes. It's… Kuro's starting to remember a little, I think.”

source.japanese:
クロの肌艶がほんのり血が通ってきていたのは、屋内の温度に馴染んできただけでなく、朔屋の抱擁もあったのだろう。
　先ほどより、声音も程良く落ち着きを得ていた。
source.english:
A little color had returned to Kuro's skin, perhaps not only from growing accustomed to the room's temperature, but from Sakuya's embrace.
Her voice, too, had settled into an easier calm.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロ、この島のこと、知ってるみたいな、わからないみたいな。よくわからないよ。
　でもここの嵐とか。木の板とか。いろんなの」
source.english:
“It's like Kuro knows this island… and like Kuro doesn't. Kuro's not sure.
But the storm here. The wooden boards. Lots of things…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「見てるとクロは、なにかを───」
source.english: “Looking at them, Kuro… something…”

source.japanese:
───信天翁号の船員達は、過去の事を語らない。過去の事情によって船に乗りこんできても、それを引きずりはしない。
　クロもまた過去を語った事ないけれど、それは自ら口を閉ざしていたのではなく、失われていたからで、クロは自分がどういう生まれでどこから来たのか、そもそも語りうる記憶を持っていなかったのだが、それがこの島にやってきて以来、解れつつある記憶の糸口があるようで、この時も、ぽつぽつと、抜け落ちてまばらな数珠の珠を数えるように。
source.english:
The Albatross crew did not speak of the past. Whatever circumstances had brought them aboard, they did not drag them along.
Kuro, too, had never spoken of hers, but not because she chose to keep silent. It was lost. She had no memories to recount of how she had been born or where she had come from. Since arriving on the island, however, the end of a loosening thread seemed to be emerging. Now, too, she spoke haltingly, like someone counting a string of prayer beads from which many beads had fallen away.

source.japanese: 朔屋はまたクロの髪を梳[す]いてやりながら、クロの語りに聞きいるうち、ぽつんと少女の髪の中に来たのに、始めは自分がどこか怪我か何かを知らぬ間に負っていて、そこから滴ったのではないか思ったのだ。
source.english: Sakuya began combing her hair again as he listened. When a tiny spot appeared amid the white, his first thought was that he had somehow hurt himself without noticing and that blood from the wound had dripped into her hair.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……And then. There's……still more.」
【Naomasa】 「……What about it? Might as well spill everything at this point.」
【Kuro】 「Mh……aye. It kind of. Feels like Kuro is starting to remember, a little.」

A faint, healthy glow had returned to Kuro's complexion, not just because she had grown accustomed to the temperature within the house, but surely also because of Sakuya's embrace. And compared to earlier, her voice had settled into a comfortable, steady tone.
【Kuro】 「It feels like, this island, Kuro knows it, but also doesn't. Can't really tell. But the storm. Or the wooden boards. All kinds of things.」
【Kuro】 「When Kuro sees them, something───」

───The crew members of the Albatross speak not of their past. Even had they boarded the ship because of their past circumstances, they never dragged it aboard with them. Kuro also had yet to speak of her past, but that was not because she herself had chosen to keep her mouth shut, but rather because it was lost to her; where was she born and from whence did she hail? To begin with, Kuro did not even possess the memories that would enable her to speak of such things, but ever since coming to this island, it seemed there was a thread of memory beginning to unravel, and this time too, bit by bit, as if counting the scattered prayer beads of a rosary now sparse after so many had fallen away.

As Sakuya listened to Kuro's narration while he combed through her hair once more, a solitary speck emerged within the girl's hair, so at first, he wondered if he had sustained an injury somewhere without noticing, believing it to have dripped down onto her from himself.

source.japanese:
それくらい、白の中で鮮烈だった。
　暗い暗い色。深い色。光を閉じこめる色。
　鮮血の色合いと似通うが、それは血などではなく、シンプルに黒なのだった。
source.english:
So vivid was it against the white.
A dark, dark color. Deep. A color that imprisoned light.
It resembled fresh blood, but was not blood at all. Simply black.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（なんだ……!?　こいつ、髪の色が……）
source.english: (What…!? Her hair's changing color…)

source.japanese:
目を閉じ、物想いするクロの、白い髪の中に浮いた黒の斑[ふ]は始めは燐寸の先程度、一つだけ、だったのが、朔屋の見やる間に小指の先から短冊や小皿くらいの大きさに拡大し、数も二つ・三つ・四つとどんどん増えて後はもう数え果たさず。どんどん浮いて、だんだらに染まっていく。
　自分の傷の血などではない、雨漏りが天井を抜けるうちに塗料の類に染まったかと見あげても、一筋も垂れてきているのはない。
　白の中の黒は、少女の髪の中に自ら浮かび上がってきているようだった。
source.english:
Kuro closed her eyes in thought. At first, the black marking upon her white hair had been a single patch the size of a match head. As Sakuya watched, it grew to the size of the tip of a little finger, then a strip of paper, then a small plate. Two, three, four patches appeared, then too many to count.
More kept surfacing, staining her hair in irregular bands. Not blood from his own wound. Had a leak picked up paint as it passed through the roof? He looked up, but not a single drop was falling.
The black seemed to rise of itself within the girl's white hair.

source.japanese: 朔屋がそれを、クロから隠したのは何故だったろう。髪を拭いてやっていたタオルを目にやって、雫を拭き取るように、目隠しを。
source.english: Why did Sakuya hide it from her? He drew the cloth he had been using to dry her hair across her eyes, covering them as though wiping away drops of water.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まあ、無理に思い出そうとすんな。
　思い出そうとすると、頭痛くなるぞ、そういうもやもやしたのは」
source.english:
“Well, don't force yourself to remember.
Trying to recall fuzzy things like that will give you a headache.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そお……あ、目ぇ、少しくすぐったい」
source.english: “Really…? Oh, that tickles my eyes a little.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「前髪も濡れてっからさ。ちゃんと拭いとかないと」
source.english: “Your bangs are wet too. Got to wipe them properly.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あい…………ん。目ン玉揉み揉みされると、気持ちいいみたいな、こあいみたいな」
source.english: “Yes… Mm. Having my eyeballs rubbed feels… sort of nice. Sort of scary.”

source.japanese:
初めてだったのか、クロは絞った手拭いで瞼[まぶた]を揉まれる心地好さを、しばらくは恐縮そうに味わっていたけれど、やがて身体も和らいで、朔屋に笑みかけようとして、そこで。
　手拭いが瞼[まぶた]からずれた時に見て、クロもまた慌てたのである。
source.english:
Perhaps it was new to her. For a while, Kuro seemed almost apologetic as she enjoyed the feel of the wrung-out cloth rubbing her eyelids. Gradually her body relaxed, and she tried to smile at Sakuya.
Then, as the cloth slipped from her eyes, she saw. She, too, was startled.

source.japanese: 自分の髪の中にこんな異状が生じる事を、クロ自身もこれまで知らなかった、こんな現象は彼女にしても初めてだったのである。
source.english: Kuro had never known such a change to occur in her hair. This was a first for her as well.

target.text: So striking was it against the white. A dark, dark colour. A deep colour. A colour that trapped all light within. Though it bore a close resemblance to the shade of fresh blood, that was not blood at all; it was simply black.
【Naomasa】 （What the……!? The colour of her hair, it's……）

With her eyes closed, Kuro was deep in thought, and the blotch of black surfacing within the white hair was, at first, but the size of a matchhead, and one was all there was, but before his very eyes, from the tip of his little finger to a tanzaku or a small plate, it expanded in size; there were two now, three, no, four, continuing to grow in size and number until he gave up counting. Emerging in rapid succession, gradually dying it in uneven blotches.

This was not blood from a wound of his own, and even as he looked up to the ceiling to see if it was being stained by some manner of pigment leaking through with the rain, there was not a single streak of colour dripping down from above. The black amidst the white seemed to be emerging on its own from within the girl's hair.

Whyever was it that Sakuya decided to hide that from Kuro? He took the towel that he'd been using to dry her hair and put it over her eyes, as if wiping off the drops of water, using it as a blindfold.
【Naomasa】 「Well, don't try too hard to remember. You'll end up with a headache, trying to remember vague things like that.」
【Kuro】 「That so……ah, eyes, a bit ticklish.」
【Naomasa】 「Your fringe is dripping wet too. Gotta make sure it's all dry.」
【Kuro】 「Aye…………nnh. When Kuro's eyeballs get rubbed, it kind of feels good, but also kind of scary.」

Perhaps it was her first time, for Kuro bashfully savoured the pleasantness of having her eyelids rubbed with a wrung-out towel for a time, but eventually, with her body relaxed as well, as she made to smile at Sakuya, right then. The moment the towel left her eyelids and she saw it, Kuro also panicked once more.
Kuro herself had never known that such an abnormality could arise in her own hair until now, and it was the first time that even she experienced this phenomenon.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「え……っ？　黒いのが、まざって……クロの髪に……？」
source.english: “Huh…? Black's mixed… into Kuro's hair…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「い、いやきっと、これはなんかで汚れただけだろ？　あんま気にすんな」
source.english: “N-no, it's probably just dirt or something. Don't worry about it.”

source.japanese: 一掬い手にとってしげしげ確かめているのを、朔屋は逸らして、手拭いを広げてクロの頭にふわり、隠した理由を口には出せず、言葉を濁す。
source.english: She gathered a handful to examine closely. Sakuya diverted her, spreading the cloth and laying it lightly over her head. Unable to say why he was hiding it, he mumbled evasively.

source.japanese:
その黒い色合い自体は、最上の漆や黒蜜を思わせてとても綺麗ではあったけれども。
　それが斑[まだら]に白の中に散らかって、出鱈目な模様に染め抜いている様子は、お世辞にも綺麗とは言えず、それどころか奇病の症例のように見えた、などとなんでクロに告げられるものか、残酷な。クロだって大いに戸惑っている様子なのに。
source.english:
The black itself was beautiful, suggesting the finest lacquer or dark syrup.
But the way it lay scattered through the white, staining it in random patterns, could not be called beautiful by any stretch. It looked more like the symptoms of some strange disease. How could he tell Kuro that? It would be cruel. She was bewildered enough already.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「どっかでころんで、汚しちゃったっけ？
　それとも何か、かかったりしたっけ……？
　ううん、違う、これ、きっと」
source.english:
“Did Kuro fall somewhere and get it dirty?
Or did something… splash on it…? No.
That's not it. This must be…”

source.japanese: す、と瞼[まぶた]を下ろして、心の中で何事を測って、クロは白い鳥のするように背後へ首を捻って、
source.english: She gently lowered her eyelids, gauging something within herself, then turned like a white bird to look back over her shoulder.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ねえ朔屋さん───」
source.english: “Mr. Sakuya…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「お、おう。なんだ……？」
source.english: “Y-yeah. What is it…?”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロね、ほんとはね……多分。
　今のクロ、違うんだよ。
　ずっと前。もっともっと前」
source.english:
“Kuro… really… probably.
Kuro's different now. A long time ago.
Much, much longer ago…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「前のクロと、今のクロは……違う」
source.english: “Kuro back then and Kuro now… aren't the same.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Eh……? Something black is…… mixed into……Kuro's hair……?」
【Naomasa】 「N-, no, this has to be some kind of filth or dirt, right? Don't worry about it too much.」

As she took a small handful of hair in her hand and examined it closely, Sakuya diverted her attention from it, unfolded the towel, then placed it gently over Kuro's head, not speaking of the reason why he had hidden it from her, his words evasive.

That shade of black itself was beautiful, the sort that brought to mind the deepest of jet blacks or dark brown sugar syrup, however. When it was scattered in blotches amidst a sea of white, and in such a haphazard pattern at that, even as flattery, it could not be called beautiful; on the contrary, it looked like a case of a rare disease, but how could he possibly tell Kuro something so heartless? Kuro was already confused enough as it was.
【Kuro】 「Tripped somewhere and got it dirty? Or it got covered in something……? No, that's not it, this has to be.」
She lowered her eyelids smoothly, weighed something within her mind, and then, like a white bird, Kuro twisted her neck all the way around to her back,
【Kuro】 「Hey, Sakuya-san───」
【Naomasa】 「Y-, yeah. What is it……?」
【Kuro】 「See, Kuro, actually……probably. The Kuro here now is different. From long ago. Much, much longer.」
【Kuro】 「The Kuro from before, and the Kuro from now, are……different.」

source.japanese:
斑に染まった髪をまた一掬[すく]い、手に取るのを今度は朔屋も妨げなかった。
　クロが混乱したり怯えるようであれば、見せるまいとしたのだろうが、彼女は不思議と落ち着いていた。
source.english:
Again she took a handful of her mottled hair.
This time Sakuya did not stop her. Had she been confused or frightened, he would have tried to keep her from seeing it. But she was strangely calm.

source.japanese: ───どこかしら憂愁を滲ませていたけれど、その想いが少女を徒らに損ねるものではない限り、取りあげてしまうのもまた罪と。朔屋はだからそれ以上はしなかった。
source.english: There was a trace of sorrow in her. Yet so long as the feeling did not needlessly harm her, taking it away would be a wrong of its own. Sakuya did nothing more.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「お前、昔の事って
　なんか覚えてるのか……？」
source.english:
“Do you remember anything…
about long ago?”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ううん、あんまりは。
　あんまり前のコトは、よく覚えてらりない。
　クロ、なんかずっと信天翁号に、
　いてるけど───」
source.english:
“No, not much.
Kuro can't really remember things from that far back.
Kuro's been on the Albatross
all this time…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「その前のことは、あんまり。
　でも……あれは嵐。
　ずっと、嵐、やっぱり、嵐」
source.english:
“Before that, not much.
But… there was a storm.
Always a storm. Yes, a storm.”

source.japanese: やはりクロの記憶には、どうしても嵐がまつわるのだろうか。ただ、自然の最大級の脅威であるはずの嵐を語るクロの声は、遠い故郷に想いを馳せる漂泊者のように郷愁を帯びて、椅子の中で少し丸めた背も、優しい、柔和しい、しおらしい。
source.english: Were storms inevitably entwined with Kuro's memories? Yet when she spoke of what should have been nature's greatest threat, her voice held the homesickness of a wanderer thinking of a distant homeland. Her back, slightly rounded in the chair, looked gentle, mild, demure.

target.text: She grabbed another handful of hair dyed in patches, and this time, Sakuya did not prevent her from taking it within her hands. Had Kuro seemed confused or scared, then he would surely have tried to not let her see, but the girl was strangely composed.

───Though she exuded a subtle hint of melancholy, as long as those feelings did not needlessly harm the girl, depriving her of them would also be a sin in itself, he thought. Sakuya therefore did nothing more.
【Naomasa】 「Are you remembering something? From your past……?」
【Kuro】 「No, not much. Can't remember things from the past too clearly. Kuro has kind of always been on the Albatross, but───」
【Kuro】 「Things from before that, not much. But……that was a storm. Always, a storm, after all, a storm.」

As one would expect, it seemed storms would inevitably come up in Kuro's memories. It was just that, when she spoke of what must be one of nature's greatest threats, a storm, the timbre of her voice was tinged with nostalgia, like a deracine whose thoughts drifted to his distant homeland, and the way she slightly hunched her back in the chair was also gentle, soft, meek.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「それで、それで……どうなったんだろ。
　クロ、なんか大切なこと、あった。
　でも、どうしても、できなかった？」
source.english:
“And then, and then… what happened?
There was something important. For Kuro.
But… Kuro couldn't do it, no matter what?”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「───なにを？　しないと？
　だめ。もうおもいだせない」
source.english:
“What…? Had to do what…?
No. Can't remember anymore.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あは。クロはどうして、こうなんだろ。
　大切なことも。しないといけないことも」
source.english:
“Ahaha. Why is Kuro like this? Important things.
Things that have to be done.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そんなことも、忘れて。
　思い出せない。なのに」
source.english:
“Kuro forgot even those. Can't remember.
And yet…”

source.japanese:
少女の呟きが、ぽつりぽつりと魂の欠片のように廃屋の中に零されては静寂に拡散していく、白の髪の中で黒が、墨を滲ませたように広がり、流れ、また形を替える。
　ふと朔屋は、こうして中途半端に黒が混じるから不格好に見えるのであって、これがもし全て一色黒に染まったなら美しいのではないか、とそのように想像して、何故か微妙に気持ちが不安定にぶれた。
source.english:
Her murmurs fell like fragments of a soul into the abandoned house, one by one, dispersing into silence. Black spread through her white hair like bleeding ink, flowed, changed shape again.
Suddenly Sakuya thought it looked awkward only because the black was mixed in so incompletely. Mightn't it be beautiful if all of it became a single black? Imagining that, he felt inexplicably unsettled.

source.japanese:
クロが、その名前の響きの通り黒髪の少女であったなら───どうにも朔屋の中ではしっくりと収まらない。
　ただどうしても、クロが自分の外見をどのように思っているかは知らぬ、それを敢えて考えずに朔屋が思うのは、この廃屋の中で二人で寄り添って、さわさわと肌撫でる秘密めいた歓びを感じられているのは、全てが今の条件が整っていてこそ、というおよそ朔屋らしからぬ審美的な観念の。
　木造の廃屋。雨の仄明かりに滲む窓。森閑とした雨垂れ。そして白い髪に肌、紅い眸[ひとみ]の不思議な少女。それでないとこんなにも玄妙な雰囲気は味わえまい。
source.english:
If Kuro were a black-haired girl, as the sound of her name suggested… Somehow that did not sit right within him.
He did not know what she thought of her own appearance. Deliberately setting that aside, he thought the secret joy that brushed softly over his skin as they sat close together in this deserted house existed only because every condition was just as it was. An aesthetic notion quite unlike Sakuya. The wooden house. The window blurred by rain-dimmed light. The profound quiet of falling rain.
And the strange girl with white hair and skin, red eyes. Without them, the atmosphere could never have held this subtle mystery.

source.japanese: もちろん朔屋はクロが訥々と語る言葉にちゃんと耳を傾けていたし、その審美的な観点も、心の隅でちらと感じていただけの事。それらの感興は、クロがほろりと零した涙の哀しさに、いたわしさに洗い流された。
source.english: Of course he was listening properly to her halting words. That aesthetic feeling had only flickered in a corner of his mind. The sadness of Kuro's sudden tear—and the tenderness it stirred in him—washed all such reveries away.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さんに見てもらえなくって、
　哀しいとか」
source.english:
“Feeling sad…
because you won't look at Kuro…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そっちのことの方が、気になる、なんて。
　クロはやっぱり……だめな子なんだねえ」
source.english:
“That matters more…
Kuro really is a no-good girl, isn't she?”

source.japanese:
泣き笑い。哀しい泣き笑い。
　クロがついぞ見せたことのない表情に、朔屋は胸つかれる思いしたという。
source.english:
A smile through tears.
A sad smile through tears. Kuro had never shown him such an expression. It struck Sakuya to the heart.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「And then, and then……what was it then? There was something very important to Kuro. But, just couldn't do it?」
【Kuro】 「───Something? Had to be done? No good. Can't remember anymore.」
【Kuro】 「Ahah. Wonder why Kuro is like this. That important thing, too. Even what had to be done.」
【Kuro】 「Forgotten even that. Can't remember. And still.」

The girl's murmurs, like fragments of her soul, spilled out one by one into the room, diffusing into the silence, and like bleeding ink, the black amidst the white of her hair spread, flowed, and changed shape yet again. Suddenly, the thought struck Sakuya that, though it made an unpleasant sight while the black was mixed this haphazardly, were it all dyed a single shade of black, would it not be beautiful; as he imagined it thus, for some reason, his emotions grew subtly unstable, wavering.

If Kuro, as the sound of her name would suggest, were a black-haired girl, then───it just did not sit right within Sakuya. It was just that, though Sakuya knew not what Kuro thought of her own appearance, and so deliberately tried to keep that out of his considerations, when they were snuggled up together in this abandoned house, just the two of them, the reason he could feel this secretive delight gently brushing against his skin was only because all of the exact conditions were in place: an aesthetic notion utterly uncharacteristic of Sakuya.

An abandoned wooden house. A window blurred in the faint glow of the rain. The hushed raindrops. And finally, a mysterious girl of white hair and skin, with eyes of crimson. Without all this present, he would be unable to savour an atmosphere this subtly profound.

Of course, Sakuya still made sure to lend an ear to Kuro's halting narration, and that aesthetic perspective was but something he barely glimpsed somewhere in the back of his mind. All those fancies were swept away by the heartrending misery of the tears Kuro softly shed.
【Kuro】 「When Sakuya-san wouldn't look at Kuro, was so miserable.」
【Kuro】 「And to think, that's what Kuro is more worried about. Kuro really is……a useless girl, right?」
A tear-stained smile. A sad, tear-stained smile. Seeing an expression that Kuro had never once shown before, Sakuya felt a sharp pang in his chest.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だからさ、そんな前のコトなんか、気にするなって。信天翁号の船員なんて、みんな過去になにかあったりするようなのばっかだ」
source.english: “I'm telling you, don't worry about all that stuff from long ago. Everyone on the Albatross has something in their past.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもみんな、そんなの気にしないで生きてるし、さ」
source.english: “But they all get on with living without worrying about it.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Like I said, don't let things from so far in the past bother you. Everyone on the Albatross, each and every one of them, have had something happen in the past, it seems.」
【Naomasa】 「But they're all living life without letting it get to them, right?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うん……でもね。
　たぶんこの島とクロは、
　きっとなんかがあった」
source.english:
“Mm… but… this island and Kuro…
probably…
something must have happened.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「それ、全部おもいだせたら。
　クロは、どうなっちゃうか。
　わかんない───」
source.english:
“If Kuro remembers all of it…
what'll happen to Kuro?
I don't know…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「こわいのか、そうなりたいのか。
　それも、わかんないよ」
source.english:
“Kuro doesn't know if it's scary, or if Kuro wants it to happen.
Kuro doesn't know that either.”

source.japanese: 臆病なクロ、本当は人一倍感じやすいクロ、なのにこの時のクロは、自分の髪に生じた不思議より、自ら御しかねる心の動きの方に戸惑っていた。
source.english: Kuro was timid, and in truth more sensitive than most; yet at that moment she was more bewildered by the movements of her own ungovernable heart than by the strange thing happening to her hair.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Yeah……but still. Something must have happened, between this island and Kuro, probably.」
【Kuro】 「And if Kuro remembers it all. Then what will happen to Kuro? Don't know───」
【Kuro】 「Is it scary, does Kuro want to become like that? Don't know that either.」

Timid Kuro, who in truth was twice as sensitive as any other. Yet in this moment, Kuro was less bewildered by the strange phenomenon occurring in her hair than she was by the uncontrollable stirrings of her own heart.

source.japanese: ───幸い、髪の異変はやがて鎮まって、クロの髪は白一色を取り戻していったが、それは少女の注意が過去の記憶から逸れていくのと同調しているかのようだった。
source.english: Fortunately, the change soon subsided, and her hair returned to pure white. It seemed to coincide with her attention drifting away from memories of the past.

target.text: ───Fortunately, the abnormality of her hair eventually subsided, and Kuro's hair was regaining its pure white, but it was as if that change was mirroring the way the girl's attention was drifting away from her memories of the past.

source.japanese:
……どこから、どのようにして話がそのように転んだものか。
　信天翁号から離れて二人きり、静まり返った廃屋に二人きりで引き籠もっている、という秘密の冒険めかした状況がそうさせたのかも知れない。
　あるいは朔屋がクロという一人の少女の内面に触れて抱いた、もっと切実な願いだったのかも知れない。
　嵐の時以外は皆に、犬コロや猫助のようになおざりにされているクロだけれども、ちゃんとこのように鋭敏な感性を具[そな]え、切々とした願いを抱いて、葛藤し、無くしてしまった記憶に思い悩む、立派な一人の女の子、人間なのだと、どうにかして皆に認めさせてやりたいという。
source.english:
How had the conversation taken such a turn?
Perhaps it was the air of a secret adventure: away from the Albatross, just the two of them, shut inside a silent abandoned house.
Or perhaps Sakuya had felt a more urgent wish upon touching the inner life of this one woman, Kuro.
Outside a storm, everyone neglected her like a puppy or a kitten. Yet here she was, possessed of keen feeling, earnest wishes, conflicts, troubled by the memories she had lost. A woman in her own right. A person. Somehow he wanted to make the others acknowledge that.

source.japanese:
朔屋だって、クロと少しずつお互いの距離を縮め、そうしてようやく理解し始めた事柄だ。このクロはどうしてもその不健康そうで異様な外見と、言葉足らずな物言いが先に立ち、まともに耳を傾けてくれる者がいないせいで、人扱いされていない。けれどもその実は至って真っ当な感覚と考え方を持ち合わせているではないか。……言葉にして伝えられないだけで。
　であるのなら、と朔屋が思い立ったのは、何故だろう。
source.english:
Sakuya himself had only begun to understand it as the distance between them gradually narrowed. Kuro's unhealthy, strange appearance and halting speech always came first. Nobody listened properly, so nobody treated her as a person. But her feelings and her way of thinking were perfectly sound. She simply could not put them into words.
If that was so… Why had the thought occurred to him?

source.japanese: なんにしてもクロをそうと皆に知らしめるには、彼女の頼りなげな舌や、馬鹿で無能扱いされている朔屋の言説ではいかにも心許ない。とあれば、言の葉で伝えられないなら、行動で示してやるまで───と柄にもない、願いを抱くに至ったのは、何故なのだろう。
source.english: In any event, making the others recognize her would be difficult through her uncertain tongue, or the pronouncements of Sakuya, dismissed as an incompetent fool. If words could not convey it, they would have to show it through action. Why had he come to harbor such an uncharacteristic wish?

source.japanese:
彼自身が一人の人間としては大いに足らないところがある、というよりあり過ぎるというのに、クロに対して『どうにかして認めさせてやりたい』などという願いを持つに至ったのは。
　もしかするとそれは───
　
　クロに己の願いを仮託していたのかも知れない。朔屋自身気づいていない願い。彼もまた、皆に誇れるようなモノを、なにか一つでも持ちたいという。
source.english:
He himself had many shortcomings as a human being—far too many. Why should he wish to make the others recognize Kuro? Perhaps…
he was entrusting her with a desire of his own,
one he had not recognized. He, too, wanted something, just one thing, he could proudly show them.

source.japanese: それとも、もしかするとクロへの仲間意識だったのかも知れない。ただし同じく軽んじられている者同士の共感とは微妙に異なる。
source.english: Or perhaps he felt a fellowship with her. Not quite the sympathy of two people equally despised.

target.text: ……Whence, and in what way, did the conversation end up landing on this topic? Away from the Albatross, just the two of them, cooped up in an abandoned house fallen still as death once more: perhaps it was this situation, with its air of secret adventure, that had brought it about. Or perhaps it was a more earnest wish that Sakuya conceived after touching upon the inmost self of the young girl who went by Kuro.

When it wasn't storming, Kuro was treated by the rest with the sort of disregard reserved for a puppy or a kitty-cat, and yet she was endowed with acute sensitivities, cherished a fervent desire, was conflicted, troubled by the memories she had lost, an admirable young woman, a human being; by hook or by crook, he wanted to make them all recognize her for who she was.

Even Sakuya, as he and Kuro gradually grew closer, had thus finally begun to understand this. Because Kuro's sickly, strange appearance and tongue-tied manner of speech inevitably took centre stage, no one was truly willing to lend an ear to her words, and so she was not treated as a human being. However, in reality, was she not possessed of entirely sound sensibilities and ways of thinking? ……She just couldn't convey it through words. And if that was the case, Sakuya thought, making up his mind; but why did he suddenly strike on this thought?

At any rate, if he wished to make it known what Kuro was really like, then the idea of doing it by way of the girl's unreliable tongue or the statements of Sakuya, who was treated as an idiot incompetent, utterly failed at engendering confidence in him. And with that being the case, if it could not be conveyed through words, then it would have to be done through action───but why was it, then, that he had come to harbour a wish so out of character for him?

He himself had a great many shortcomings as a human being; rather, he was excessively insufficient, and yet he had still come to hold this desire for Kuro: 『I want to make them acknowledge her by whatever means necessary.』 Perhaps it was because─── Perhaps he was using Kuro as a pretext for his own desire. A desire that Sakuya himself had yet to notice. That he himself wished to have something, anything, that he could show off with pride to everyone else.
Or instead, perhaps it was a sense of camaraderie he felt for Kuro. However, it subtly differed from the sense of empathy shared by comrades being similarly disdained.

source.japanese: 朔屋はこれまで怠慢な放蕩の人生を送ってきたけれど、それで完全に堕落しきる事もできない中途半端な人間だ。信天翁号に引きずりこまれ、鉄火と悪辣に塗[まみ]れた日々をそれなりに過ごしてきたけれど、朔屋はどうしても航海士や水夫長、あるいは機関長のように、大胆不敵、豪毅怪力、隠然孤高といった独自のスタイル、哲学を有する無頼の自由人にはなりきれない。恐らくはこれからもそうだろう。
source.english: Sakuya had led a lazy, dissolute life, yet remained too irresolute even to sink into complete depravity. Dragged aboard the Albatross, he had endured its days of gunfire and villainy after a fashion. But he could never become a lawless free spirit with a style and philosophy of his own, like the navigators, the boatswain or the chief engineer: fearless audacity, mighty strength, aloof independence. Probably he never would.

source.japanese: 陸の社会を形成する善き人間性とか秩序と勤勉を尊ぶ倫理の中で暮らしていくには怠惰に過ぎ、かといって無頼の自由の海に飛びこんで、荒れ狂う嵐のような日々に生きていかれる自信もない。
source.english: Too lazy to live among the good character and the ethics of order and industry that formed society ashore. Yet without the confidence to plunge into the lawless sea of freedom and live through days like raging storms.

source.japanese: どこまでも中途半端な男ではあるが、本質としては気弱な善人と言っていいだろう。
source.english: A man who could never wholly be one thing or another; at heart, however, he might fairly be called a timid good man.

source.japanese: そんな朔屋が、無頼の異人達の中で、実は真っ当な感覚と善性を持ち合わせていたクロに共感を寄せるようになっても不思議ではない。なればこそ、彼女の為に尽力もしたいという───
source.english: It was hardly strange that such a man would feel kinship with Kuro, who among these lawless eccentrics possessed sound instincts and an essential goodness. Hence his wish to do what he could for her—

source.japanese: そんな己の潜在願望に気づいているのかいないのか、廃屋の一角で、朔屋はしみじみとクロに語りかけた事だった。
source.english: Aware or unaware of that hidden desire, he spoke earnestly to Kuro in a corner of the abandoned house.

target.text: Sakuya had lived a life of lazy debauchery hitherto, but he was also the sort of half-baked man unable to descend fully into wanton degeneracy. He had been dragged onto the Albatross, and ever since then, had spent his fair share of days smeared in gunfire and villainy, but unlike the first mates or the Bosun, or perhaps even the Chief Engineer, being dauntless and daredevil, a man of herculean strength and fortitude, a rebellious free spirit with his own unique style and philosophy of latent, proud aloofness: these were all things that, no matter how he tried, Sakuya could not entirely become. And in all likelihood never would.

He was much too indolent to live amidst the elements that made up society on land, what with their good human nature, their order, and their ethics that prize diligence, but with that said, he also lacked the confidence to plunge into the seas of reckless freedom and spend his days in that raging storm.
He was a man incomplete by every measure, but his true character could best be described as a timid, pessimistic man of virtue.

And for such a man as Sakuya, living amongst villainous foreigners, the question of why his empathy had come to be drawn towards Kuro, a girl who was actually possessed of sound sensibilities and an innate goodness, was no great mystery at all. For this reason in particular, he wished to devote himself to this, for her sake───
Perhaps he was aware of such a latent desire within himself, perhaps not; in a corner of the abandoned house, Sakuya spoke to Kuro from the heart.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なあクロ。別に船長状態にならなくってもさ、なんかできるって、みんなを驚かせてやれるようなこと」
source.english: “Kuro. Even without turning into the captain, there's something you can do. Something that'll surprise everyone.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Hey, Kuro. You don't necessarily have to be the captain, you know? There's still something you can do, something that'll shock them all.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そんなコト、クロにできるって、
　朔屋さんは本当にそう思う？」
source.english:
“You really think Kuro
can do something like that?”

source.japanese:
それまで胸中に寄り来たっていた寂寥を、朔屋に髪をいじらせる心地好さで慰めていたクロは、それまでは望むべくもなし、と無意識理に諦めていた果実を差し出されたように、他人任せの快さから、ふっと顔を上げた。
　けれどそれを果たして望んで良いのか、ためらいがちな臆病さは、これまでの彼女の処遇を鑑みればもっともなところ。
source.english:
Until then she had soothed the loneliness gathering within her by letting Sakuya play with her hair. Now she lifted her face from that passive pleasure, as if offered a fruit she had unconsciously given up hoping for. Whether she was allowed to want it still made her hesitate.
After the way she had been treated, that timid caution was understandable.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……正直、難しいだろうなあ。
　でも、だからって船に引き籠もってばっかじゃあ気が滅入る」
source.english:
“…Honestly, it'll probably be difficult.
But staying shut aboard all the time gets you down.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「酒呑んでダラダラしようとか思っても、
　なんでかこう言う時に限って、
　ほとんどなくなってて、
　ロクなのないんだよ」
source.english:
“Even if I wanted to drink and laze around,
somehow it's precisely at times like this
that the booze is nearly gone.
Nothing decent left.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺もいい加減、
　気分がくさくさしてきたから。
　なあ、ちょっと奥の方に行ってみないか」
source.english:
“I'm getting
fed up myself.
How about we go a little farther in?”

source.japanese: 退屈しのぎに少し大がかりな散歩、あるいはちょっとした冒険に誘うような、軽い口ぶりだったのは、朔屋自身望み薄だと判っていたからだが、それでもまずは動いてみないと始まらないと信ずる、意外な真摯もまた、剽げた声音の中に混ざっていたのだった。
source.english: He spoke lightly, inviting her on a rather extensive walk to kill boredom, perhaps a little adventure. He knew the prospects were poor. Yet his playful voice also held an unexpected sincerity: nothing would begin unless they first made a move.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それにな。俺思ったんだが。
　クロ、別に嵐がなくっても、お前、そのままで、みんなから馬鹿にされなくて済むってやりかた、きっとあるぜ」
source.english:
“And I was thinking.
Even without a storm, Kuro, there must be some way for you to stay just as you are and stop everyone making fun of you.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san, do you really think Kuro can do such a thing?」

Kuro, who hitherto had been soothing the desolation pressing against her heart with the pleasant comfort of letting Sakuya play with her hair, as though offered a fruit that she had unconsciously given up on, one she ought not even dream of, abruptly looked up from the sweet bliss of surrendering to the care of another. However, her wonder if it was truly right to desire that, her hesitant cowardice, was entirely understandable in light of the treatment she had suffered up until now.
【Naomasa】 「……Honestly, I think it'll be hard. But, if we make that an excuse to just stay holed up on the ship all the time, we'll get depressed.」
【Naomasa】 「Whenever I'm in the mood to just idle away the time with drink, for some reason, that's exactly when I realize I'm pretty much out, and there's nothing decent left.」
【Naomasa】 「I'm also starting to feel down in the dumps about this whole thing, so. Hey, what say you to venturing a little deeper inside?」

He spoke flippantly, as though inviting her on a slightly large-scale walk to kill some time, or perhaps on a little adventure, because Sakuya himself knew that the prospects were dim, but even so, the belief that nothing would begin unless one took action, an unexpected sincerity, was also woven into that facetious tone of voice.
【Naomasa】 「And also. I was thinking. Kuro, even without a storm, there has to be a way for you to stay just the way you are, without having to be belittled by everybody else. I'm sure of it.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そんなの……クロ思いつかないよ……。
　あう。やっぱり、クロ、ばかだから」
source.english:
“Kuro can't think of anything… Ah.
Because Kuro's stupid, after all.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だから、その馬鹿なクロ……ごめんな、話の流れだから。馬鹿なクロが、なにか凄いことをやったとするだろ？」
source.english: “So suppose stupid Kuro—sorry, just following the argument—suppose stupid Kuro does something amazing?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そしたら、嵐じゃない時のクロでも、きっと大丈夫さあ」
source.english: “Then even the Kuro outside a storm will be all right.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「嵐の時みたいに、尊敬はされなくっても、
　馬鹿にされない。それで充分じゃないか」
source.english:
“Maybe they won't respect you like they do in a storm.
But they won't laugh at you. Isn't that enough?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺らみたいな能無しでも、あんまりたくさんをねだらなきゃ、それなりに世の中と折り合いをつけていけるって」
source.english: “Even useless people like us can come to terms with the world, more or less, if we don't ask for too much.”

source.japanese:
朔屋なりの、どうにも後ろ向きな人生訓だが、足りるを知る、と言い替えられなくもなく、クロは暫[しばら]く、真剣に、廃屋のくすんだ窓硝子に心中の像を投影させるかに凝視して、あれこれ想い悩んで、それでも最後には宜[うべ]のうた。
　青年からの提案でよし、と小さく頷[うなず]いて、小さく微笑んで。
source.english:
A decidedly backward-looking lesson in life, in Sakuya's fashion. One could, however, call it knowing when one had enough. Kuro stared earnestly at the house's dull window, as though projecting the images within her upon it. She thought and worried for a while,
but finally agreed. A little nod at his suggestion. A little smile.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro can't……think up anything like that……. Augh. Because, in the end, Kuro really is stupid.」
【Naomasa】 「Like I said, that stupid Kuro…… sorry, just going with the flow here. Let's say that stupid Kuro pulled off something absolutely incredible?」
