【Naomasa】 「If she did that, then even if she was the Kuro when it isn't storming, I'm sure she'd be just fine, right?」
【Naomasa】 「Even if you're not revered like when it storms, you won't be looked down on. Isn't that good enough?」
【Naomasa】 「Even incompetents like us, as long as we don't beg for too much, can reach a decent enough compromise with the world we live in.」

Befitting of Sakuya, it was a terribly pessimistic life lesson, but perhaps it could be rephrased as "find satisfaction in your lot in life", and for a time, with sincerity, Kuro stared intently at the hazy window of the abandoned house as though an image of her inmost feelings were projected upon it; after agonizing over this and that, she ultimately gave her consent. She met the young man's proposal with a small nod of approval, smiling faintly.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「う……うん？　そう、かな。……そうかも。
　じゃあ、そうなるには、どうすればいいかな……」
source.english:
“Mm… is that right? …Maybe.
Then how can Kuro make that happen…?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Y……yeah? Is that so? ……Maybe so. Then, what should Kuro do to make that happen……」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロがなにかすごいこと……信天翁号を、空飛ばせてみる……」
source.english: “Something amazing… Make the Albatross fly…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、そいつは……凄いは凄いが、方法が全く思いつかない……」
source.english: “Well, that… would be amazing, yes, but I can't think of any way to do it…”

source.japanese: もちろん突拍子もない答えで、朔屋はクロの、正解へのご褒美を期待するような眼差しには無下に否定も出来かねて、歯切れ悪く濁して、
source.english: Naturally, it was a preposterous answer. But with Kuro looking at him as though expecting a reward for getting it right, he could not reject it outright. He equivocated.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Something incredible Kuro can do…… try to make the Albatross fly through the sky……」
【Naomasa】 「No, that's……that is incredible, but I can't think of a single way to make it happen……」

Naturally, when met with a look from Kuro that seemed expectant of a reward for getting the question right after giving him such an outlandish answer, he found it difficult to just flatly deny her, his response an evasive mumbling,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「じゃあ、みんなに……一生分の、あめちゃんをあげるぅ……」
source.english: “Then give everyone… enough candy for a whole lifetime…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……そうか。クロはもともと物欲ってやつが慎ましいんだな。でもまあそのあたりだ。クロ、飴玉じゃあ、みんなが喜ぶには、
ちっと足んねえ」
source.english:
“…I see. You don't want much in the way of possessions, do you? Still, that's the right direction.
Candy wouldn't quite be enough to make everyone happy.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もっと喜ぶもの……みんなはいつもなにを欲しがってる？」
source.english: “Something they'd like more… What does everyone always want?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Then, giving everybody…… a lifetime's worth of candies……」
【Naomasa】 「……Right. Your worldly wants have always been modest by nature. But yeah, something along those lines. Kuro, hard candy is not quite enough to make them all happy.」
【Naomasa】 「Something that would make them even happier……what is it that they all always want again?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ええと、ええと、美味しいリンゴでもなくて、人形ちゃんは……そんなに欲しいくないみたい」
source.english: “Um, um… Not nice apples. Dolls… they don't seem to want dolls very much.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uuhm, uhmmm, isn't delicious apples either, and dollies……don't seem like something they'd want that much.」

source.japanese: 沈思黙考、いや完黙とはいかず、んー、とモーターの旋音の如き唸[うな]りを食いしばった唇から、身体も揺らして椅子が軋んで、クロは全身の細胞で根限りに考えて、彼女の真剣なあまり、待ち受ける朔屋にも四方の板壁が重苦しく迫り来るかの圧迫感さえ覚え始めたところで、クロが出した答えは金色に光り輝いていた。
source.english: Deep, silent thought—though not entirely silent. An ‘mmm’ hummed through her clenched lips like the whirr of a motor. Her body rocked and the chair creaked. Kuro thought with every cell, straining to her limit. So earnest was she that Sakuya, waiting, began to feel the wooden walls pressing heavily toward him. Then her answer shone golden.

target.text: She racked her brains in silence; well, she wasn't entirely silent, for a groaning "hmm" like the whirring of a spinning motor came from her tightly pressed lips, and her body rocking back and forth made the chair creak; Kuro strained every cell in her entire body to think with all her might, and just as the waiting Sakuya began to feel even a sense of oppression from her overwhelming earnestness, as if the surrounding wooden walls were closing in on him, the answer she gave glittered with a golden gleam.

source.english: “Oh… money…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そう。正解、よー考えついたじゃねえか」
source.english: “That's it. Right answer. Good thinking.”

source.japanese:
いかにもありきたりで、考えるに及ばないと嗤[わら]うなかれ、真理は普遍的で手品の種明かしよりも単純な形を取るものだからして。
　しかし、この難問への答えを得る為にクロは、機関長が船の主罐の安全弁を細工して規格外れの出力を得る術数よりも、全神経に無理を強いたと見えて───
　
　ご名答を褒め称えようと、朔屋がぽんぽんと手を置いたクロの頭が、熱かった。
source.english:
Do not laugh at so obvious an answer, one scarcely worth thinking about. Truth is universal, and takes forms simpler than the secret of a conjuring trick.
Yet solving this difficult problem seemed to have strained Kuro's every nerve more than the chief engineer strained the main boiler by tampering with its safety valve to obtain power beyond its rating.
Sakuya reached to pat her head in praise. It was hot.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Ah……money……?」
【Naomasa】 「That's right. Correct answer, you did really well coming up with that.」

Do not scoff at it as utterly banal and unworthy of thought, for truth is universal, taking a form far simpler than the magician revealing his trick. However, to arrive at the answer to this gruelling riddle, it seemed as though she, in an act that exceeded even the artifice of the Chief Engineer who had tampered with the safety valve of the ship's main boiler to wring out an output well beyond the conventional, had forced her entire nervous system beyond its limits─── As though praising an excellent answer, Sakuya put his hand on Kuro's head and patted it, but it was hot.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロ、考えすぎて、頭……熱……」
source.english: “Kuro thought too much. Head's… hot…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわあ知恵熱!?　冷やせ冷やせ……」
source.english: “Whoa, a fever from thinking!? Cool it, cool it…”

source.japanese: 絞った手拭いを額に押し当て冷却の時間数分、クロはぜえはあと荒い息をついてどうにも危なっかしく見えたが、それでもやがて収まって、朔屋に戻した手拭いが、湯に浸したような。
source.english: Several minutes of cooling with a wrung-out cloth against her forehead. Kuro panted, looking precarious indeed. Eventually she settled, but the cloth she returned to Sakuya felt as though it had been dipped in hot water.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro thought too hard, head……hot……」

【Naomasa】 「Woah, your brain overheated!? Gotta cool it down, cool it down……」 (TN: The term used here is "知恵熱", which literally means "intelligence fever". Like teething fever in the West, it's a term for the inexplicable fevers experienced by infants, but in Japan, it's also frequently misused to mean a fever after thinking too hard, also known as a psychogenic fever.)

She pressed the wrung towel against her forehead to let it cool for several minutes, and though things were looking awfully precarious as Kuro continued to heave ragged breaths, it eventually subsided; when it was returned to Sakuya, the towel felt as if it had been soaked in hot water.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でも、クロはお金、持たないです。
　お仕事のわけまえ、クロの分、
　航海士と水夫長があずかってくれてるから、
　今持たない」
source.english:
“But Kuro doesn't have any money.
The mates and the boatswain keep
Kuro's share of the pay,
so Kuro doesn't have it now.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But, Kuro doesn't have any money. The share from work, Kuro's portion, the mates and the Bosun said they're looking after it for Kuro, so Kuro doesn't have it right now.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロはあんま、お金欲しくないから。
　その分みんなに……あげるぅ」
source.english:
“Kuro doesn't really want money.
So Kuro'll give that share… to everyone.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぅ……うっ、うっ、うっ」
source.english: “Uh… uh… uh…”

source.japanese: ……声を忍ばせ咽[むせ]び泣く、朔屋は、これでも涙を抑えようとしたのである。彼の男泣き、人間らしい心の欠片もあれば理解もされよう。つまり、クロは。どれだけ信天翁号で過ごしてきたか知れないが、少なくとも水夫長や一等航海士の双子が乗り合わせるようになってからは、一度も、一度もたりとも───これに匹敵する悪行は、親類からのお年玉を親がピンハネする事ぐらいか。
source.english: Sakuya sobbed quietly. He was trying to hold back his tears, even so. Anyone with a scrap of human feeling could understand a man's weeping here. In other words, Kuro… Who knew how long she had spent aboard the Albatross? But at least since the boatswain and the twin first mates had joined, not once, not even once… Perhaps the only comparable wickedness was parents skimming their children's New Year's money from relatives.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro doesn't really want money very much. So will give that portion……to all the others.」
【Naomasa】 「Uh……uhh, uhh, uuuhh.」

……Stifling his voice and sobbing quietly; though it may not have seemed it, this was Sakuya trying to hold back his tears. Were one possessed of but a shred of a heart becoming of a human, then surely these rare male tears of his could be understood. In other words, Kuro had. He wasn't sure exactly how much time she'd spent aboard the Albatross, but it was, at the very least, since the Bosun or the twin first mates joined the crew, and not once, not even a single, measly time ───it was like parents skimming off the New Year's money a child was gifted by their relatives; perhaps only a misdeed so wicked could compare?

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さん泣くと、なにかクロも涙。
　ふぇ……ふぇぇぇ……」
source.english:
“When you cry, Mr. Sakuya, somehow Kuro…
starts crying too. Wuh… wuuh…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うっうっ、クロ、たぶんお前が預けているお金はな、戻ってこない……いや、そんな事はないよなっ」
source.english: “Uuh… uuh… Kuro, that money you've left with them is probably never coming back… No, that can't be right!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもそれだけじゃ、きっと足らない。
　そこでこの島のことだよ。
　あの学者がここから流れきたんなら、
　どっかにザウエルが……あるかもしれない」
source.english:
“But that alone probably wouldn't be enough.
Which brings us to this island.
If that scholar drifted over from here,
there might be Zauer… somewhere.”

source.japanese:
朔屋はあくまでクロが自前で答えを導き出す事を待ったけれど、この調子ではそこに至るまでに何度少女が知恵熱を発するか、何度青年が男泣きに啼[な]くか知れたものではなく、下手するとそれまでに二人ともここで乾き死にして、島内の他の動物達よろしく仲良く番[つがい]の骨を晒す事にもなりかねない。
　後の世で誰かに発見された時に、二つの頭蓋骨の容積からして、まだ脳が未発達な人類以前の霊長類とか取り沙汰もされかねず、そんな屈辱に甘んじる前に、クロの答えに上げ底履かせて正解とした。
source.english:
He had intended to wait until she found the answer herself. At this rate, though, who knew how many thinking fevers she would have, how often he would break into manly sobs before they got there? They might both dry up and die first, leaving their paired bones like the island's other animals.
Someone discovering them in a later age might judge from the volume of their two skulls that they were prehuman primates with still-undeveloped brains. Rather than accept that humiliation, he propped up Kuro's answer and called it correct.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「クロが持ってるあの一個は、最後の手段にしよう」
source.english: “Let's keep the one you already have as our last resort.”

source.japanese:
───そういう欲をかくから。
　その後二人は───
　
　　　　───あんな運命を───
　招き寄せる事になってしまうのだけれど。
source.english:
—It was precisely because they grew greedy.
Afterward, the two of them would…

        …draw that fate down upon themselves.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もっとザウエルを見つけ出して、みんなにあげたら……どうだ？」
source.english: “What if we find more Zauer and give it to everyone?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「When Sakuya-san cries, Kuro also tears up for some reason. Uwa……uwaaah……」
【Naomasa】 「Unh, uuuh, Kuro, I don't think the money you left with them is ever coming back to you…… no, of course it will, yeah!」
【Naomasa】 「But that alone won't be enough, I'm certain. And that's where this island comes in. If that scholar came drifting from here, then maybe those Sauers…… could be around here somewhere.」

Sakuya was doing his utmost to wait for Kuro to deduce the answer on her own, but with how things were going, he could only guess at how many times her brain would have to overheat before arriving at the right one, and it was also impossible to say how many times the young man would break down in manly tears, so if they were not careful, they might even wither up and die, and it was quite possible they would even end up like the other animals on the island, the bones of yet another happily-mated pair on display.

It was also quite possible that, when discovered by later generations, it would be speculated that, based on the volume of their craniums, they belonged to something like a species of pre-hominid primate whose brains were still underdeveloped; before he would have to resign himself to such disgrace, he gave Kuro's answer a push in the right direction before marking it as correct.
【Naomasa】 「Let's save the one you have, Kuro, as a last resort.」
───It all stemmed from that greed. That later, the two of them─── ───invited upon themselves─── so terrible a fate.
【Naomasa】 「What if we found even more Sauers, then gave them to everybody else ……how does that sound?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「みんな……喜んでくれるかな。
　みんな……嬉しいかな。
　みんな嬉しいと、
　クロは叱られたり、叩かれたり……ない？」
source.english:
“Will everyone… be glad?
Happy?
If they're happy,
Kuro won't get scolded or hit…?”

source.japanese: 朔屋へ身を乗りだして、船員服の裾[すそ]を掴んで真摯に問いかける、その掴む力の意外な強さ。クロの願う心が健気に現れている。
source.english: She leaned toward him, caught the hem of his sailor shirt and asked in earnest. Her grip was unexpectedly strong. Her wish showed there, touchingly plain.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、きっとだ」
source.english: “Yeah. I'm sure of it.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Wonder……if they'll all be pleased. Would they……all be happy? If they're all happy, then Kuro won't be scolded, or hit……anymore?」

Leaning towards Sakuya, she clutched the hem of his sailor uniform and earnestly asked him thus, and the surprising strength within that grip. Kuro's heartfelt yearning shone through it with touching bravery.
【Naomasa】 「Yeah, I'm sure of it.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「なら探すよ。クロ、いっしょけんめ、さがす。そして見つけて、シサムとキサラに上げる、水夫長にも。機関長、水夫のみんな」
source.english: “Then Kuro'll look. Look really hard. Find it and give it to Sisam and Kisara. The boatswain too. The chief engineer. All the sailors.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Then will search. Kuro will give all Kuro has to look. And when we find them, give them to Shisamu and Kisara, and also the Bosun. The Chief Engineer, and all the sailors!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そん時足りなかったら、クロのザウエル、足してもいいよね……？」
source.english: “And if that's not enough, Kuro can add Kuro's Zauer…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ああ」
source.english: “…Yeah.”

source.japanese: ろくな価値もない光り物、ガラクタに関してはあれこれ集めておきながら、真に価値あるものに対しては執着を見せないクロにどこかしら不安覚えないでもない朔屋だったけれど、とにかくそれで、探しに行こうという事になった。
source.english: She collected all manner of worthless glittering junk, yet showed no attachment to something truly valuable. That gave Sakuya a certain uneasiness. In any event, they decided to go looking.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「And if not enough, then Kuro can also give them Kuro's Sauer, right……?」
【Naomasa】 「……Yeah.」

While she collected all sorts of shiny, worthless junk, Kuro displayed no attachment to the one thing that held true value; though something about that made Sakuya feel a little uneasy, regardless, with that, they decided to go searching.

source.japanese:
ばさり、がらんと、鋳鉄製机の上に投げ出されたそれは、機関室備え付けの堅牢だが無骨な設備に被せるより、どこかの金満家の応接間の床を飾るか、さもなくば博物館で防虫剤の匂いの中、ひっそりと展示の機会を待っているほうが相応しいといえた。
　ただ、どれだけの歳月がその上を過ぎ去っていったのか、全体的に萎縮して、粗び、今しがたされたような雑な扱いへの不満を、その虚ろな眼窩から訴えるような。
source.english:
Flap, clatter. The thing thrown upon the cast-iron table belonged less upon the engine room's sturdy, graceless fittings than on the drawing-room floor of some wealthy man, or perhaps in a museum, quietly awaiting display amid the smell of mothballs.
How many years had passed over it? It had shrunk and roughened all over; its hollow sockets seemed to protest the careless treatment it had received only moments ago.

target.text: With a thud and a clang, it was tossed on top of the cast-iron table; it was the sort of thing that seemed far more at home serving as a decoration on the floor of some millionaire's drawing room than covering the sturdy yet crudely utilitarian fixtures installed in the engine room, or if not that, in some museum heavy with the smell of insect repellent, quietly awaiting its chance to be put on display. Yet, as though a testament to the countless years that had washed over it, it was entirely shrunken, coat coarse and weathered; from somewhere within its hollow eye sockets, it seemed to cry out with discontent at the rough treatment it had just been on the receiving end of.

source.japanese:
それでも、歳月による劣化を差し引いても、美事な皮であった。獅子のものだ。全身の。全身美麗な黒褐色を呈し、鬣と尾の房毛は比類なく壮大、そしてその体躯ときたら、萎びて皮だけになっていても、世界中で最大とされる、暗黒大陸の同類に倍する勢い。
　ただし、皮だけではない。その裡[うち]には骨格が残されてあり、しかも肉や腱の残骸一片も残さず、骨は薬品処理でも受けたかに、滑らかな表面を晒しているのが、口腔から覗かれた。
source.english:
Even allowing for the damage of time, it was a magnificent skin. A lion's. The whole animal. Beautifully blackish-brown throughout, with an incomparably grand mane and tufted tail. And its size—even shriveled down to a skin, it all but doubled the largest lions in the world, those of the Dark Continent.
But it was not merely skin. Its skeleton remained within. Through the mouth one could see smooth bones, as if chemically treated, with not a scrap of flesh or tendon left upon them.

source.japanese:
機関長は、入室するなり物も言わずの水夫長のこの振る舞いに、目に見えるような驚愕や不興は表さず、ただ黒眼鏡の視線を机上の獅子の皮へと注ぐのみ。
　水夫長がじりじりと焦[じ]れ始めた段を見計らったかのように、
source.english:
The boatswain had done all this upon entering, without a word. The chief engineer displayed neither visible astonishment nor displeasure, merely directing his dark-glassed gaze toward the lion skin upon the table.
Almost as if waiting for Long to begin growing impatient, he said:

target.text: Nevertheless, even accounting for the deterioration it had suffered at the hands of time, it was still a magnificent skin. The skin of a lion. The whole body. Fully clad in a beautiful, dark brown, its mane and tassel of peerless majesty, and as for its physique, even withered and reduced to nothing but skin, it still boasted twice the size of its kin from the Dark Continent, considered to be the largest in the whole world.

However, it was not just skin. The skeleton still remained within, and yet there was not a single piece of meat or tendon left; it almost seemed to have undergone some sort of chemical treatment, so smooth a surface could be glimpsed on the bones through its mouth.

The Chief Engineer did not betray a hint of neither astonishment nor displeasure at the behaviour of the Bosun, who had yet to utter a word since entering the room, and instead simply kept his gaze veiled by dark glasses fixed on the lion skin atop the table. And as though he had timed it to the exact moment the Bosun began to grow impatient,

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……それで？」
source.english: “…And?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……So?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……それで、じゃねえだろう。なにか意見を言えよ、何時も通り博識百般なところを見せてみろい、ロックフォール・王！」
source.english: “Not ‘and.’ Say something. Show us your usual encyclopedic knowledge, Roquefort Wang!”

source.japanese: 水夫と機関のそれぞれの長は、それぞれ船内の独立した王国の主でもあり、それが為に相会う時には微妙な緊張が生ずるという。実際水夫長も口を開くなり挑発的な言質を吐いたが、機関長の方はというと、どこまでも泰然自若とした佇まいで、己の律を崩さず、整った顔だちに考え深げな色を湛えて押し黙る事、またしばし。水夫長のこめかみに血の筋が浮き出る頃合いで、
source.english: The head of the sailors and the head of the engines each ruled an independent kingdom aboard. Their meetings were said to produce a delicate tension. Certainly the boatswain had begun provocatively. The chief engineer, meanwhile, remained composed to the last, preserving his own rhythm, his fine features thoughtful. He stayed silent a little longer. When a vein stood out at Long's temple…

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……None of your "so?" business. Give me your damn opinion. It's time to show off that erudite brain of yours like always, Roquefort Wan!」

The respective chiefs of the sailors and the engine were akin to the lords of their own independent kingdoms aboard the ship, and as a consequence, a delicate tension would arise whenever they were to meet. Indeed, the Bosun had spat out provocative remarks no sooner than he opened his mouth, but when it came to the Chief Engineer, his air was that of total imperturbation, his self-possession unshaken, his handsome face wearing a deeply thoughtful expression, keeping silent, for a short time. And just as the veins on the Bosun's temple grew pronounced,

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「『印度の獅子』でしょうかね。
　インド亜大陸のライオンと言えば、本来は阿弗利加産のそれに比べて、体格は小柄で色合いも薄いという」
source.english:
“Felis leo indicus, perhaps.
The lions of the Indian subcontinent are ordinarily said to be smaller and paler than their African counterparts.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「This would be the Indian lion, 『Felis Leo Indicus』, would it not? It is said that, by nature, the lions of the Indian subcontinent are smaller in size and have lighter colouration than those native to Africa.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ただ伝説や、博物学に該博な作家がものした小説中に、時折散見せらるる記述がある」
source.english: “But one occasionally finds accounts in legend, or novels by writers deeply versed in natural history.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「But in legend, as well as novels penned by authors with extensive knowledge of natural history, there are the occasional descriptions found here and there.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「曰く、『本来の印度の獅子は、暗黒大陸の同類に比して、より偉大な種族であった』『その体格は阿弗利加の獅子に比べて倍ほどもあり、ただ独りで狩りを行う』とか───」
source.english: “To the effect that the original Indian lions were a mightier race than those of the Dark Continent. Twice the size of African lions, hunting alone, and so forth…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「According to those: 『The original Indian lions were, compared to their counterparts from the Dark Continent, a grander species by far.』 『Compared to the African lion, its physique is roughly twice the size, and it only hunts alone.』 And so on───」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「まあ私も、標本とはいえ現物を見るのは初めてですが」
source.english: “This is my first sight of an actual example, though admittedly a specimen.”

source.japanese:
机上の、過去の栄光を留める偉大なる皮に、しばし祈りでも捧げるように顔の前で指を組んで、それから機関長は水夫長の言葉の継ぎを待つ。ごんごんとシャフトが重低音奏でる機関室の王はあくまで彼であり、たとえ水夫長であろうとこの部屋に入った限りに於いては謁見者、王は謁見の者の意見に応じて知識を開陳はしても、度を越して多弁になると言う事はない。
　ここしばらく機関室まで降りてくる機会がなかったせいか、その辺りの呼吸を失念しかかって焦れていた水夫長だったが、やがて思い出したと見えて、語を継いだ。
source.english:
He clasped his fingers before his face for a moment, almost as if praying to the magnificent skin that preserved its former glory. Then he waited for Long to continue. Amid the shafts' deep, pounding music, he remained the engine room's king. Even the boatswain entered as a petitioner. The king might unfold his knowledge in response to a petitioner's remarks, but never grew excessively talkative.
Perhaps because he had not visited the engine room for a while, Long had nearly forgotten that rhythm and grown impatient. At last he seemed to remember, and continued.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Well, this is also my first time seeing the real thing, specimen though it may be.」

For a brief time, as though offering a prayer to the magnificent hide retaining its past glory atop the table, the Chief Engineer clasped his hands together before his face, then waited for the Bosun to continue. Within this engine room, where the shafts clang together in a concert of deep, rumbling bass, it must not be forgotten that he was king, and even should it be the Bosun himself, the moment any entered this room, they were a mere petitioner, and even should the king elect to share of his knowledge in response to the opinions of those whom he grants audience, he would not become garrulous.

Perhaps it was because he had not had the opportunity to come down to the engine room for a while now, for having just about forgotten the tacit dynamics of this place, the Bosun was growing frustrated, but eventually, he seemed to remember, then took over speaking.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……ああ、あんたの言う通りこいつは、今どきどこのインドにもいねえ、印度の獅子だろうぜ」
source.english: “…Yeah. Like you say, probably an Indian lion you won't find anywhere in India these days.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Yeah, just as you say, this big guy is probably an Indian lion of the sort you won't find anywhere today, not even in India.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だが問題はそこんとこじゃねえ。標本なんかじゃねえんだ、それは。よっくと改めろ、切った縫ったの傷は一個もねえ。つまりそいつぁ、外身にゃなんも手を着けず、肉だけ溶かして骨と皮だけ残したんだろうぜ」
source.english: “But that's not the point. It isn't a specimen. Look closely. Not one cut or stitch. Looks like the flesh was dissolved away without touching the outside, leaving only bones and skin.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「But that's not the issue here. This thing, it ain't no specimen. Take another reeeal close look, there's not a single scar from being cut or stitched. Which means, whatever did this, without so much as touching the exterior, melted only the flesh and left nothing but skin and bones.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ふむ……これも、島のどこかで？」
source.english: “Hm… This, too, came from somewhere on the island?”

source.japanese: 機関長は信天翁号がこの木造の島に到着してからも、ほとんどこの機関室から出てくる事はなく、船の機関の調整に抜かりない様子だが、それでもおおよその事情は把握しているようだった。
source.english: Since the Albatross reached the wooden island, the chief engineer had scarcely emerged from his engine room. He seemed meticulous in tending the machinery, yet still knew the general situation.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Humm……and this, too, was found somewhere on the island?」

Even since the Albatross had arrived at this island made of timber, the Chief Engineer had barely left this engine room, seemingly occupied with meticulously adjusting the ship's engines; nevertheless, he still seemed to generally grasp the situation.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そうだ。平水夫がめっけたんだが。廃屋ン中の一番奥まったところでな、どうやら巣を作ってたようだ。餌に取ってきたんだろう、他のケダモノの骨もごろごろよ。だが───他の、こいつらに喰われるような生き物はいいとして、だ」
source.english: “Yeah. A sailor found it, right at the back of a deserted house. Looks like they'd made a den. Bones of other beasts all over, probably brought back for food. Now, the creatures these things ate are one matter…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「That's right. A sailor found it. It was in the very back of an abandoned building, looked like it was denning there. Must have caught some prey, for the bones of other beasts were all over the place. But───while we can set aside what happened to the other animals, the ones that look like they were eaten by these.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「こいつは、一体、どんなナニが、こんな塩梅にしやがったんだ？」
source.english: “But what the hell did this to the lions?”

source.japanese: それが水夫長の貌[かお]に、懸念の色を張りつけている原因なのだった。
source.english: That was what had fixed the look of concern upon the boatswain's face.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What in the hell kind of something is behind what happened to this one?」
That was the cause of the look of worry etched on the Bosun's face.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「餓死や病死の可能性もあるでしょうに」
source.english: “Starvation or disease would also be possible.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Surely there is also the possibility it died of starvation or disease.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おいおい王[ワン]よ、お前さんともあろう者が寝言は困る。巣を作ってた、と言ったろう？　他にもこのライオン様のな、同族がな。みんな同じなりでくたばってやがったぜ」
source.english: “Come on, Wang. A man like you shouldn't talk in his sleep. I said they'd made a den. Other lions like this one. All dead the same way.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「飢え死にするったって、一つところで固まってるこたあねえ。病気で死ぬにも、なんてぇか、この皮の具合、弱った感じがねえ」
source.english: “Even starving animals wouldn't all huddle in one place. And if they'd died of sickness… something about the skins doesn't look weakened.”

source.japanese: かつては島で生きていた骨達のうち、草食動物はあるいは餓え、あるいは病死、そして水夫長が持ちきたった皮と骨の元の姿、捕食者の顎[あぎと]にかかって喰われた者もあるであろう。しかしその捕食者を、痕跡らしい痕跡もなく───というよりこの骨と皮のみの異物があるいはなによりの痕跡か───斃し去ったモノがあるとしたならそ奴の正体や如何。
source.english: Among the bones of the island's former inhabitants, herbivores might have died of starvation or illness, or been eaten by the predators whose former shape the boatswain's bones and skin preserved. But if something had killed those predators without leaving a trace—or rather, if this uncanny remnant of bones and skin was itself the greatest trace—what was it?

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Come now, Wan, can't have you of all people start talking nonsense. Didn't I just tell you it made a den? There are more like our mighty lion here, of his kind. And all of them kicked the damn bucket in the exact same way.」

【Bosun】 「Had they starved to death, then they wouldn't all be huddled together in the same place. And for an animal that died of disease, how should I put it, looking at the condition of this pelt, it doesn't look sickly at all.」

Amongst the many bones of those who once lived upon this island, the herbivores had perhaps starved, or else succumbed to disease, and surely some of them must have been caught in the jaws of a predator, devoured by the form that the skin and bones the Bosun had brought with him originally took. But as for what bested this predator, there was no evidence of anything whatsoever ───or rather, this corpse consisting of nothing but skin and bones could be the greatest evidence of all─── but even assuming there was something that had killed it, what of its true identity then?

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ふむ……」
source.english: “Hm…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Humm……」

source.japanese:
と、またやや俯[うつ]いて長考に入る構えだったが機関長、何事か心づいたように顔を上げると、機関室の暗がりの奥に下がっていって、何かを探しているらしい気配で、しばし。
　しかし戻ってきた時にも空手で、機関長自身不審そうに眉間に微かな皺を寄せてあった。
source.english:
The chief engineer lowered his face again as if preparing for long thought. Then, seeming to recall something, he looked up and withdrew into the engine room's darkness.
For a while he appeared to be searching. He returned empty-handed, a faint puzzled crease between his brows.

target.text: With a hum, the Chief Engineer once more cast his eyes downwards and prepared for a lengthy session of contemplation, but as though struck by a sudden realization, he lifted his head, then retreated deep into the darkness of the engine room, and with the air of a man searching for something, stayed there a time. However, even when he returned, he was just as empty-handed as before, and the Chief Engineer himself had faintly furrowed brows as though finding something suspicious.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「妙だな……。ああ失礼、こっちの話です」
source.english: “Odd… Ah, excuse me. I was talking to myself.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「How curious……. Ah, do pardon me, just muttering to myself.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なんだよ、気になるじゃねえか。言えよ」
source.english: “Now you've got me wondering. Out with it.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What's all this about, now I'm getting curious. Spit it out.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「いや、あなたほどではないが、私にも蔵書はある。とある博物学者の手沢本なんだが、それが今探した限りでは見つからない。その中に、ちょっと気になる記述があってね。
　……まあまあ、落ち着いて。内容はほとんど覚えているから」
source.english:
“Well, I have a library too, though not on your scale. One volume is a copy once owned and handled by a certain naturalist, but I can't find it just now. There was a passage in it that came to mind…
There, there, calm down. I remember most of the contents.”

source.japanese: 蔵書の紛失、と聞いて水夫長が見せた激甚の相は、機関室に入って以来もっとも恐ろしいものだった。他人のものであろうが人の書物に手を着けるようなろくでなしは、この龍の刺青に誓って盗んだ本の一頁につき一本ずつ骨をへし折ってくれるとの怪気炎を宥[なだ]めて、機関長は諳[そら]んじる……。
source.english: At the news of a missing book, Long assumed the most terrifying expression he had shown since entering the engine room. By the dragon tattoo, he swore, any scoundrel who laid hands upon another person's book would have one bone broken for every page stolen. The chief engineer soothed that monstrous blaze of indignation, then recited from memory…

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Why, while it doesn't hold a candle to yours, I, too, have a personal collection of books. I have an annotated personal copy that belonged to a certain natural historian, but when searching for it just now, I was unable to find it. You see, there is an account within the book that I find myself a little curious about. ……Now, now, do calm yourself. I remember almost everything written within it.」

Upon hearing of a book going missing, the look of violent fury on the Bosun's face was the most terrifying one he had shown since stepping foot in the engine room. It might have belonged to another, but any worthless bum who would dare lay so much as a finger on a man's books would have a bone broken for each and every page in that stolen book, so he swore on this dragon tattoo of his; calming that flame of exaggerated passions, the Chief Engineer recited from memory…….

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「Ｄｅ　Ｈｉｓｔｏｒｉａｅ　Ｎａｔｕｒａｌｉｓ　ｉｎ　Ｊａｐａｎ───これの初版、それも私家版で、他の版にはないような書きこみがいくつかある」
source.english: “De Historiae Naturalis in Japan. A first edition, privately printed, with several annotations absent from other editions.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「De Historiae Naturalis in Japan─── the first edition, and a privately printed one at that, with several annotations that you will not find in any other editions.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「その一六頁上段、爬虫類目録のうち、Ｗｕｍｉ─ｈｅｂｉという文字を朱線で抹消して、？マークを附してあったのですが」
source.english: “At the top of page sixteen, in the reptile catalog, Wumi-hebi had been struck through in red, with a question mark added.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「In the upper section of page sixteen, within the Catalogus Reptilia, the letters "Wumi-hebi" have been struck off with red, appended with a question mark.」 (TN: A reference to the works of Philipp Franz von Ziebold, a German botanist and physician famous for his studies of Japanese flora and fauna. He published the dissertation "De Historiae Naturalis in Japonia Statu" in 1824 wherein the "wumi-hebi", as he romanized it, does, in fact, feature.)

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「と、次頁の魚類目録の始めの方、円口類の項に、Ｖの表示がしてありましてね。つまり───」
source.english: “Near the beginning of the fish catalog on the following page, there was a V marked by the entry for cyclostomes. In other words…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「And then, where the Catalogus Pisces on the following page begins, in the section on cyclostomes, there is a "V" mark. That is to say───」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「その博物学者は、始めは爬虫類に分類するつもりだったＷｕｍｉ─ｈｅｂｉを円口類に挿入されるべき何かを発見して、それは当時まだ研究中だったと、まあそう言う事だと思われるのです」
source.english: “The naturalist seems to have discovered something that made Wumi-hebi, originally intended for classification among reptiles, belong among the cyclostomes instead. The matter was presumably still under investigation then.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「This natural historian discovered something signifying that this Wumi-hebi, which he had originally intended to classify as a reptile, instead ought to be placed in the Cyclostomi superclass, and at the time of writing, he was still in the midst of researching that, or, well, it certainly seems to be something along those lines.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「つまり、そいつが……？」
source.english: “So that thing did this…?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So what you're saying is, that thing is……?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「さて───ただふと、思い出したんでね。
　そもそも私は学者でも探検家でもない。こういう件に関して、はっきりした意見を求められても、その、困る」
source.english:
“Who knows? It merely occurred to me.
I am neither a scholar nor an explorer. Being asked for a definite opinion on such matters is, well, difficult.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Well now───it simply sprung to mind, unbidden. To begin with, I am neither a scholar nor an explorer. Being asked for a definitive opinion on matters such as these, well, it puts me in a difficult position.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ちっ、相変わらずぬらくらした口ぶりだな。
　たあ言え、参考になったぜ。ま、どんな生きもんだろうと、餌もないところで生きながらえているとは思えんな」
source.english:
“Tch. Slippery as ever. Still, that's useful.
Whatever it is, I can't see any creature surviving where there's nothing to eat.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Tch, always slippery as a damn eel. That said, it was worth a listen. Well, no matter what kind of creature we're dealing with here, it's hard to imagine it lasting long in a place without any food.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「このライオンをやった奴だって、今頃は島のどっかで骨になっているだろうよ」
source.english: “Whatever did this to the lions will be bones somewhere on the island by now.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Whatever it was that killed this lion, by now, it's got to be just another pile of bones lying around somewhere on this island.」

source.japanese:
それだけを言い置くと、邪魔したなの一言であとは無駄話、世間話の一つもなく、水夫長は機関室を辞そうとして、そこで呼びとめられた。
　何やら更に秘め隠された曰くの一つでも吐きそうなタイミングに水夫長、神妙に振り返ると。
source.english:
Leaving it at that, with a brief farewell and no idle conversation, Long was about to quit the engine room when he was called back.
The timing seemed to promise another hidden story. He turned solemnly.

target.text: After leaving that alone as his parting remarks, as well as giving a curt apology for the interruption, the Bosun made no further idle chatter or small talk, but just as he was about to take his leave from the engine room, he was called back. With the timing being perfect for him to spill yet another deeply hidden secret of some sort, when the Bosun solemnly turned around.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「久しぶりですね、水夫長。
　今日は一体どういうご用向きで」
source.english:
“It's been a long time, Boatswain.
What brings you here today?”

source.japanese: 機関長がこれである。今日初めて水夫長を迎えたような口ぶりの。それどころか机上に置かれた獅子の骨と皮を、たった今見つけたように、意外そうな表情で、
source.english: There was the chief engineer. Speaking as though greeting Long for the first time that day. Indeed, he seemed to notice the lion's bones and skin upon the table only now, with surprise.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「It has been a while, hasn't it, Bosun. Whatever is the nature of your business here today?」

This was how the Chief Engineer was. He spoke as if he had only just greeted the Bosun for the very first time today. In fact, as though he had only just now noticed the presence of the bones and skin of a lion that had been left lying on the table, his expression seemed one of surprise.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ところで、この皮とその中に綺麗に骨だけ残ったのはなんなんです？　観た雰囲気では、獅子のそれのように思えるが───」
source.english: “Incidentally, what is this skin with nothing but neatly preserved bones inside? By the look of it, I would say a lion…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Incidentally, what exactly is this skin with nothing but spotless bones remaining inside? From what I can tell, I believe it to be a lion of some sort, but───」

source.japanese: とかなんとか、始めからもう一度繰り返さえなければならない流れには水夫長、付き合いきれずに適当に受け流して、今度こそ機関室を後にしたけれど、扉が閉じる寸前に、暗がりの奥から微かに響いてきたのは、含み笑い。本当は、何もかも心得ていると言わんばかりの───時折機関長はこうした含み笑いを見せるから、豪放かつ直情型の水夫長とは、職掌柄だけでなく性格的にも折り合いが悪いのであった。
source.english: Long could not face going through the whole conversation again. He answered vaguely and left the engine room for good. Just before the door closed, however, a faint chuckle came from the darkness. As though its owner had known everything all along. The chief engineer occasionally indulged in such knowing chuckles. Hence his poor relations with the expansive, straightforward boatswain were a matter not merely of their offices, but their temperaments.

target.text: And so on and so forth: thus, the Bosun was stuck having to explain the entire thing from the beginning once more, but not having the patience for it, he eventually just brushed him off, and this time, he made certain to depart the engine room, but just as the door was on the verge of closing, what should sound from the depths of the darkness but a faint, suppressed chuckling. All but saying that, in truth, he had grasped everything─── the Chief Engineer would occasionally make a deliberate show of suppressed laughter like so, hence why he and the broad-minded, straight-shooting Bosun were at odds not just with respect to their official duties, but also their personalities.

source.japanese: 朔屋達の歩みゆく先は木造建築群の重ね重、過ぎ来し方にも積層し、両脇で折り重なって広がって。囲繞する壁と柱と屋根の、軒と軒を連ね隣り合わせてほとんど隙間なく密集したその様、かつての住人の残した妄執と形容するに相応しい。
source.english: Before Sakuya and Kuro, wooden buildings rose layer upon layer; behind them, too, they lay piled, overlapping and spreading to either side. Walls and pillars and roofs encircled them, eave joined to neighboring eave in a crush with scarcely a gap: a sight fit to be called the obsession left behind by the people who once lived here.

source.japanese: だがこんな畸形の幻想じみた風景に埋没しながらも朔屋が味わっていたのは郷愁めいた感慨の。信天翁号の他の面子には馴染みが薄い木造建築の連なりは、朔屋が幼かった頃、家族と共に訪れた、鄙びた温泉の宿場町の古い屋並みとどこか似通うと言えない事もない。通りを行く度辻を曲がる度入れ替わり立ち替わり現れる虫籠格子や櫺子窓などの床しい造りはまだ幼い朔屋にも、古き時代の名残りを懐かしく感じさせたものである。
source.english: Yet immersed in this grotesque, fantastical scene, Sakuya felt something like nostalgia. The wooden houses, unfamiliar to the other Albatross crew, somewhat resembled the old streets of a rustic hot-spring town he had visited with his family as a child. At every turn, another pleasing insect-cage lattice or barred window appeared. Even young Sakuya had felt a nostalgic fondness for those survivals of an older age.

source.japanese: そうと思えばこの木造の廃址も、雨に濡れた匂いの中でどこやら胸中の懐かしき原風景と似通うようにも。が、独り歩きではこうは思うまい。
source.english: Seen that way, these wooden ruins, amid the smell of rain-soaked timber, resembled some cherished first landscape within him. He would not have thought so walking alone.

source.japanese: 森閑として細雨に霞み靄がかる街を歩く影二つ。一つが歩けばもう一つも歩き出し、一つが止まればまた一つも止まる。一つは猫背気味の青年の姿、朔屋。今ひとつは白い髪を頼りなくうねらせた小柄で痩せた手足、クロ。
source.english: Two shadows moved through the silent streets hazed with fine rain and mist. When one walked, the other began walking. When one stopped, the other stopped. One was the slightly stooped young man, Sakuya. The other, small with thin limbs and white hair waving without strength, was Kuro.

target.text: Ahead of Sakuya and Kuro lay layers upon layers of wooden buildings, piling up over the path they had left behind, sprawling out into overlapping heaps on either side. The surrounding walls, posts, and roofs densely packed together, eaves adjoined so closely in succession there were hardly any gaps, a state of affairs so claustrophobic it made a worthy metaphor of the lingering obsessions of those who once lived here, of Ichabod.

However, even while immersed within this fantastical scenery of bizarre shapes, what Sakuya experienced was reminiscent of a deep nostalgia. While the rows of wooden houses were hardly a familiar sight to the other crew members of the Albatross, it wouldn't be entirely inaccurate to say that something about them resembled an old row of houses in a rural stage station town with a hot spring that Sakuya had visited with his family back when he was a young boy.

The charming make of the insect-cage latticework or the latticed windows that would constantly shift places whenever he went down the street or turned a corner made even the still-young Sakuya feel a sense of nostalgia for these relics of days of yore.

And when he thought about it that way, even these wooden ruins, with their rain-soaked scent, resembled a nostalgic, indelible scene of his childhood stashed away somewhere in his heart. But, were he walking by himself, he wouldn't think this way.

There were two shades who walked apace through this quiet town shrouded in a haze of misty rain. When one began to walk, the other likewise set forth. When one came to a halt, the other likewise stopped in its tracks. One was the figure of a young man with a slightly hunched back, Sakuya. The other had white hair wispily billowing behind it, small of stature and skinny of limbs, Kuro.

source.japanese: 小糠雨にしとどに濡れた街並みの色合いは沈んで侘びしく、一つの絵の具の濃淡だけで描き出したかのようだ。ただクロの白の髪だけが。先んじて朔屋の姿を見失ってしまうことを恐れて、そして遅れて後ろに置いていかれてしまうことを厭[いと]うて、青年の隣をつかず離れず白子の少女の、色の抜け落ちた白、色ならぬ白だけが視界の端に浮き上がる。先ほど廃屋の中で幾許か休んでいたし、朔屋ができる限り丁寧に水気を拭ったお陰で少女の濡れ髪はあらかた乾いて、挙措の度にふわふわ揺れて流れる軽やかさを取り戻してある。
source.english: The rain-drenched town lay in subdued, forlorn colors, as though painted in different shades of a single pigment. Only Kuro's white hair… Afraid to go ahead and lose sight of Sakuya, unwilling to fall behind and be left, the albino woman stayed close beside him. Her colorless white, that white which was not a color, floated at the edge of his vision. They had rested awhile in the house, and his careful wiping had left her hair mostly dry. It had recovered its lightness, softly floating with each movement.

source.japanese: 軽やか、というより頼りない、というべきか。弾力に乏しい、猫の腹毛や鳥の胸毛を長くしたような髪質で、僅かな気流にも流されて、クロは自分の呼吸でこの毛先を鼻に吸いこみよくくしゃみなどをしていたりと、どちらかといえば質の悪い髪の毛である。無重力下にあるように漂うクロの髪は、現実の力強さを著しく欠いて、この少女が四肢と言わず毛先まで出来損ないである事を示していたけれど、クロが感じさせる現実感の乏しさが、今の朔屋には奇妙に心地好かった。
source.english: Lightness—or rather, frailty. With little spring in it, her hair resembled a cat's belly fur or a bird's breast feathers grown long. The slightest current carried it away. She often drew the ends into her nose with her own breath and sneezed. Poor-quality hair, on the whole. Floating as if weightless, it had so little of the strength of real things: the woman was a botched creature, not merely in her limbs but to the very tips of her hair. Yet that sense of unreality felt strangely pleasant to Sakuya now.

source.japanese: ザウエルを探すという事になって島内を探索し始めたわけだけれど、朔屋に確たる見込みなどあろう筈もない。それでも歩き出したのは、長の雨で気が鬱[ふさ]がれたせいもあったが、それだけではない。クロに皆を見返してやる為にと持ちかけては見たけれど、そんなのはどうにも期待薄だと、青年自身心得てもいる。
source.english: They had begun exploring in search of Zauer. Naturally, he had no definite prospect of finding any. Part of what made him start walking was the gloom of the long rain, but not only that. He had proposed showing everyone what Kuro could do, though he knew himself how little hope there was.

source.japanese: それなのにクロをどうして連れ出してみたのか、朔屋自身今一つ理解されていなかったのだけれど、こうしてクロを隣にして歩いていると、少しだけ判るような気がしたし、それと認めてしまうのが猛烈に気恥ずかしかった。
source.english: He did not quite understand why he had brought her out. Walking with her beside him, he felt he understood a little. Admitting it was fiercely embarrassing.

source.japanese:
青年はただ、単に───
　クロを、この白子の不出来な少女を───
source.english:
The young man simply…
Kuro, this botched albino woman…

source.japanese:
連れ出してみたかっただけ。
　そぞろ歩き、共歩きしてみたかっただけ。
source.english:
He had merely wanted to take her out.
To stroll. To walk together.

source.japanese: こんな小便臭い、月のモノの訪れがあるかどうかもわからないような小娘に、朔屋が抱くようになった想いを、もし言葉にして並べてしまおうものなら、青年はたちどころに失語症に陥り、羞恥のあまりに布団被って籠もりきって一週間は出てこなくなるだろう。
source.english: If he tried to set down in words the feelings he had begun to harbor for this piss-smelling little slip of a woman, whose slight body gave no sign it had ever known a period, the young man would instantly fall mute; then, overcome with shame, he would burrow beneath his futon for a week and refuse to come out.

target.text: The colour of the townscape left dripping wet by the fine rain was sombre and dreary, as though it had been rendered on a canvas in but a single shade of paint. Only Kuro's white hair made for an exception. She feared walking too far ahead and losing sight of Sakuya, and she also found the idea of lagging behind and being left by her lonesome unpleasant, so she stayed beside the young man, neither too close nor too far, and the albino girl's white was all that could be seen in the periphery of his vision; a white drained of colour, a white that was no colour at all.

They had rested for some time within that abandoned house, and Sakuya had done his utmost to thoroughly dry off any moisture, so the girl's wet hair was nearly dry now, and it had regained the lightness that let it sway and flow with every little movement she made.

Rather than being light, perhaps it was better called airy. With a texture lacking in resilience, like it was formed of elongated strands of a cat's belly fur or the down of a bird's breast, it was easily swept away by the faintest breeze, and Kuro would even suck the ends of her hair into her nose through her own breathing, often causing her to sneeze; if he had to pick, her hair was of poor quality.

Kuro's hair, fluttering as though weightless, was strikingly devoid of actual substance, a testament to how not only this girl's limbs were a failure, but also how she was even defect all the way to the tips of her hair, but the lack of tangibility Kuro exuded was strangely comforting to Sakuya in this moment.

Though they began their exploration of the island in search of Sauers, Sakuya could surely not have any kind of concrete expectations of success. And yet he still set out, perhaps in part because the long spell of rain had left him in low spirits, but it was not that alone. He had tried suggesting it to Kuro as a way for her to get one over on the others and prove herself, but it was an awfully long shot, and the young man himself was well aware of this.

Despite all this, why had he still decided to bring Kuro with him; Sakuya was not entirely sure himself, but as he walked with Kuro by his side thus, he felt like he was beginning to understand it a little, although having to admit to what it was left him immensely embarrassed.
The young man just, he simply─── Wanted to take Kuro, this bungling albino girl───
He just wanted to take her with him. He just wanted to go on a relaxed stroll with her, to walk together.

If Sakuya were to put into words the feelings he had come to harbour for this little girl, so small and childish that he couldn't tell if she had even had her monthly visitor yet, then the young man would likely instantly suffer a bout of aphasia, so overwhelmed by embarrassment that he would hide away under his covers and not come out for a whole week.

source.japanese:
これまで何度も女を抱いて、浮かれ騒いで、からかわれたり遊ばれたり、それでも懲りずに尻を追いかけてきた朔屋だが、今クロに振れている心には馴染みが薄い。
　それは多分。

よしんばあの泥中に手がかりの埋もれていたとしても、探るのは最後の最後としたいと、二人はドーム状の建物を後にしたのだが。
　しかし朔屋達は知らなかった。この水槽内に封じられていたモノが、先ほどの水の流出と共に、秘やかに島内に放たれてしまったことを。
source.english:
Even if a clue lay buried in the mud, searching it could wait until the very last resort. They left the dome.
But they did not know that the thing confined within the tank had slipped out with the escaping water, silently released upon the island.

target.text: There might well be a clue buried somewhere in that mud for aught that he knew, but he would leave dredging through it as the very final of his final options, and so the two left the dome-shaped building behind. However, Sakuya and Kuro were unaware. That what had been sealed away within this water tank had been released onto the island along with the outflow of water a moment ago.

source.japanese: 封じられていたモノ。
source.english: The thing that had been confined.

target.text: That which had been sealed within.

source.japanese: それは───古代の恐怖。
source.english: An ancient terror.

target.text: It was───a primeval horror.

source.japanese: 巡る、巡る、蕩児としては二流、船員としても三流の青年と、嵐の時だけ心力目醒めて神がかった船長になり得る白子の少女という、どうにも変梃な二人道中、生き物の絶えた、雨に煙[けぶ]る木造の街並みの中を、巡る足取りはとぼとぼと力ない。
source.english: On they wandered, on they wandered: a second-rate rake and third-rate sailor, and an albino young woman whose mind awakened only in storms, when she could become a godlike captain. A decidedly odd traveling pair. Their footsteps dragged weakly through the rain-hazed wooden town, emptied of life.

source.japanese: たとえ朔屋には、そこが世界有数の景勝地で、風光明媚な景色がパノラマのように広がっていたとしても、風景に目を遊ばせるより女の乳房を弄[もてあそ]びながら酒でも舐めていた方がまし、という嗜好の持ち主であるからして、周囲の状況がどうあれ大差は無かろうと思われるのだけれど、そんな無神経な彼でさえ、長く歩くにはこの廃址、静けさが深く沈みすぎていた。それは死者の沈黙と言っていい。廃屋の中に堆[うずたか]い生き物達の、けして再び語り出す事のない深い沈黙だ。
source.english: Even amid one of the world's celebrated beauty spots, a panorama of exquisite scenery, Sakuya would rather toy with a woman's breasts over a drink than let his eyes roam the view. His surroundings ought to make little difference. Yet even for such an insensitive man, the silence of these ruins sank too deep for a long walk. The silence of the dead. The profound silence of creatures heaped within the houses, never to speak again.

target.text: Round and round they went; a young man who was second-rate as a libertine and third-rate as a sailor together with an albino girl who only during a storm could awaken her force of will and become a godlike captain, and as these two continued their strange journey through these wooden streets devoid of life and shrouded in a haze of rain, the gait of their wandering legs was trudging and feeble.

Even should Sakuya find himself in one of the world's most picturesque places, blessed with the most beautiful scenery unfolding itself before him in a panoramic view, he'd sooner lap on a bottle of booze while fondling a woman's tits than let his eyes roam nature's beauty; he was the sort of man who held such preferences, and so one would also think him the sort of man for whom the state of his surroundings would not make any real difference, but even to a callous man such as he, these ruins were steeped in a silence far too deep for a long stroll.
It could well be called the silence of the dead. A profound silence from which the creatures piled up within the abandoned buildings were never to speak again.

source.japanese: 世の中には墓所を巡って死者の憩いを共感する事を満足を覚える者もあるにはあっても、彼らの愉悦は、外界とそれら聖域を出入りし、その差異を認識出来てこそ。島一つ、全体が墓跡とあっては墓地逍遥者とて消化不良を起こしかねない。
source.english: Some people enjoy wandering graveyards, sharing in the repose of the dead. But their pleasure depends upon passing between those sanctuaries and the outside world, recognizing the difference. An entire island of graves might give even a cemetery stroller indigestion.

source.japanese: 朔屋は始めこそ水夫長に島の探索に加えてくれと懇願してははねつけられて憤ったものだが、今ならば水夫長の、すぐに飽きる、長居して面白いものではないとの由が、全くその通りと了解される。
source.english: At first, Sakuya had begged Long to include him in the exploration and resented being refused. Now he understood perfectly the boatswain's point: one soon tired of the island, and lingering here was no fun.

source.japanese: もちろん積み重なった骨達は、歳月に乾ききって、不浄や汚穢といった死の負の側面は浄化され、今ではただただ淡々と廃屋内の暗がりに沈んでいるが、それでもこう島全体に積み重なっていると思えばどうしても鼻につく。
source.english: Of course, time had dried the piled bones thoroughly, stripping death of its filth and pollution. They merely rested quietly in the houses' dark. Still, knowing they lay heaped throughout the island made their presence impossible to ignore.

target.text: While this world did count within it those who could find satisfaction in visiting cemeteries and sharing in the repose of the dead, their delight arose precisely because, free to come and go between the outside world and these sacred spaces, they could perceive that difference. But on an entire island covered in monuments to the dead, even a saunterer of cemeteries would be liable to find himself suffering a bout of indigestion.

In the very beginning, Sakuya had been indignant that his pleas to join the expedition had been so flatly rejected by the Bosun, but now, he could fully comprehend what the Bosun had meant when he said he'd soon grow tired of it, and that it wasn't the kind of place that would be interesting to linger in, and the Bosun had been all too right.

The piled-up bones had, of course, dried out over the years, all the negative associations with death such as impurity and filth purified away, and now they merely sunk into the darkness of the abandoned houses with indifference, and yet when he thought of how they were lying in heaps all over the island like this, he couldn't help but feel sick and tired of them.

source.japanese: それに、クロだ。そのひ弱い打ち見と、普段の生活の場が船上である事を思えば、意外なほどによく歩く少女だったけれど、それでも限度がある。不平を一言も漏らさずに、青年の隣を短かな歩度でついてくるのは健気でいじらしうあったが、鈍感な朔屋にも、次第次第にクロが足を引きずりがちになっているのは見てとれて、
source.english: And then there was Kuro. Given her frail appearance and a life ordinarily spent aboard ship, the young woman walked surprisingly well. But there were limits. Without a single complaint, she kept beside him in short steps, brave and touching. Even dull Sakuya could see she was gradually beginning to drag her feet.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（やっぱり、思いつき程度で始めても、
　どうにかなるもんじゃないか……）
source.english:
(An idea off the top of my head…
I suppose that isn't enough to make things work…)

target.text: Besides, there was Kuro. Considering how sickly she looked at a glance, as well as how the environment of her day-to-day life was aboard a ship, the girl made for a surprisingly good walker, but even that had its limits. Without uttering a single word of complaint, it was commendable and endearing both how she walked by the young man's side and kept pace with her short stride, but even the insensitive Sakuya had noticed how, step by step, Kuro's feet grew more inclined to drag.
【Naomasa】 （Turns out starting something on a total whim doesn't just magically make it work out after all……）

source.japanese: と当初の意気込みもどこへやら、弱気の渦巻き胸中にぐるぐる回り、表情も次第次第に気難しくなっていっては、クロに不安そうに見あげられて慌てて愁眉を開いてみせる、この区画間に入ってはその繰り返し。
source.english: His initial enthusiasm had vanished. Discouragement swirled within him; his face grew increasingly ill-tempered. Kuro looked up anxiously and he hastily smoothed his brow. Since entering this stretch between districts, it had been the same thing over and over.

source.japanese: 廃址の中の、ある一画とある一画の境目辺り、密航者に教えられた区画、魚類と両生類の遺骨が眠るそれぞれの区画の中間の辺り。
source.english: A boundary between two sections of the ruins. The sections the stowaway had described, where fish bones and amphibian bones respectively slept. Somewhere between them.

source.japanese: 朔屋の推理が的を射ているなら、かつて肺魚達が飼育されていたのはこの辺りであるはずだ───が、灰色ならぬ酒色の青年の脳髄からひり出された推理なぞになんの信憑性があるものか。おまけにここ何日かはその燃料である酒精もろくろく入っていないと来ては。
source.english: If his deduction was right, this should be where the lungfish had once been kept. But what faith could anyone put in a deduction squeezed out of this young man's brain matter—not gray but booze-colored? Especially when, these past few days, it had scarcely received any of its fuel, alcohol.

target.text: So he thought, his initial enthusiasm having left for greener pastures, a maelstrom of negativity swirling round and round within his bosom, his expression gradually growing more and more sullen too; whenever Kuro looked up at him anxiously, he would hurriedly wipe the tension from his face to reassure her, a routine they'd repeated over and over since entering this section.

In the section within the ruins that the stowaway had told them of, on the boundary between one particular area and another, somewhere between the respective sections where the remains of fish and amphibians rested.

If Sakuya's reasoning was on target, then this should be around the place where the lungfish were once kept─── but, what credibility could there possibly be in deductions excreted from the liquor-sodden brain of a young man whose grey matter had been dyed the colour of wine? Not to mention how, for the past several days now, he'd not ingested nearly enough of the spirits that served to fuel it.

source.japanese: それでも朔屋は、なかば意地になりながら、廃屋の中をまた暴きにかかった。扉を封じている錠は、単純な閂[かんぬき]であるのがほとんどなのがまだしもの救いで、船員ナイフを扉の隙間にねじこんでこじればどうにか片はつく。ただ不審というか、そうやって侵入してみる廃屋内は骨は残されていても動くモノは無く、扉も一つかせいぜい二つ、そのいずれも内側から閂[かんぬき]がかかっているあれば、かつて生き物達を世話した誰かがあったとしても、彼らは最後に如何にして外から閂[かんぬき]を下ろして去っていったのだろうか。
source.english: Half out of stubbornness, he set about breaking into another house. Most doors were secured by simple bars, at least. Working his sailor's knife into a gap and prying would do the job. Yet there was something odd. Inside were bones, but nothing moving. One door, two at most, every one barred from within. If someone had once tended the creatures, how had that person finally left and lowered the bars from outside?

target.text: Nevertheless, half out of stubbornness, Sakuya once more set about rummaging around the interior of yet another abandoned house. The one saving grace was that almost all of the locks holding the doors shut were simple bolts, and so he could manage to pry them open by wedging his sailor's knife through the gap of the door.

However, one thing was uncanny; within the abandoned houses he broke into like that, though bones were left behind, there was nothing within that had moved them there, and while there were only one or two doors at most, every single one would always be bolted shut from the inside, so even had there been someone who once cared for these creatures, by whatever means had they managed to slide the bolt into place from the outside when they finally left?

source.japanese:
だが朔屋は余計な事は考えないようにして、廃屋内を手早く観察して外に戻る。
　戸口にクロを見張りに立たせているのは、船の面子か他の誰か（こちらは考えづらいが）が通りかかった時の用心で、一通り見終えてからクロに無言で首を振る。この廃屋も、外れ。
source.english:
Sakuya tried not to think of unnecessary matters. He inspected the interior quickly and came out.
Kuro stood watch at the doorway in case another crew member—or someone else, though that was unlikely—passed. After looking, he silently shook his head. Another wrong house.

target.text: But trying not to ponder overmuch on things he didn't strictly have to, Sakuya quickly surveyed the interior before returning outside. He had made Kuro stand watch by the entrance, a precaution taken in case some other member of the ship's crew (though this was hard to imagine) would happen to pass by, and after throwing around a brief glance, he silently shook his head at Kuro. This abandoned house was yet another miss.

source.japanese:
暫時とはいえ外で待つクロは退屈かも知れないが、中を観てここも空振りだったと告げる朔屋も中々に辛い。もうなんどこのやりとりを重ねた事か。クロが対して文句も言わずに、じゃあ次ねと落胆も見せずとりなすのが、かえって辛い。
　それに二人とも、大した考えもなく船を飛び出してきた為、遠出の準備がない。孤島とはいえそれなりに面積はあり、徒歩で縦断するには相当の重労働、先に密航者から聞いてあたりをつけておらなんだら、朔屋もクロもそうそうに音を上げていた筈。……今でさえ朔屋の腹はぐうぐう卑しく鳴っている、クロも似たり寄ったりで、先程などは空腹の空えづきなどを漏らしていたりで。霧雨に唇が常に湿っているお陰で渇きはそれほど深刻ではないが、それとて限度はあろう。
source.english:
Waiting outside might bore Kuro, brief though it was. Reporting another failure was hard for Sakuya too. How often had they repeated this? Her lack of complaint, her undiscouraged ‘Next one, then,’ made it harder.
They had left the ship without much thought or preparation for a long trip. Isolated though it was, the island had a fair area; crossing it on foot was considerable labor. Without the stowaway's directions, both would long since have given up. Even now his stomach growled greedily. Kuro's was much the same; she had recently retched from hunger. Mist kept their lips wet, so thirst was less urgent. Even that would have a limit.

target.text: He couldn't say if Kuro was bored waiting outside for him, even if it only was for a short while, but Sakuya, who had to scope out the inside only to have to report back that it was yet another swing and a miss, certainly found it rather bitter. How many times must they have repeated this exchange already? And when Kuro would not utter a single complaint, not betray a ghost of despondency as she said "okay, next one then", it only made it all the more painful to him.

In addition, because the two of them had both rushed off the ship without giving it much thought, they hadn't prepared for a long outing. Isolated island it might be, it still boasted a significant size, so crossing it on foot was rather hard work, and if they hadn't been able to make an informed guess from the information they heard from the stowaway earlier, both Sakuya and Kuro would surely have thrown in the towel sooner rather than later.

……Even now, Sakuya's stomach was grumbling greedily, and Kuro was in much the same boat; just moments ago, the sheer emptiness of her stomach had left her dry-heaving. Thanks to their lips being perpetually moistened by the drizzle, the threat of thirst was not quite so grave, but even that surely had its limits.

source.japanese:
唇の雫を嘗め嘗め、クロを覗きこめば、彼女も丁度青年を見あげる間合いで、見交わした目は互いに「そろそろ休憩はいかが」と問いかけてあった。
　ただそのこと自体には二人とも異存はないものの、休みを取るなら腰を下ろしたいというのが、二人の間のまず暗黙の了解。そしてクロの希望としては、できれば建物の中の方が良い、との言で、通りの両側には確かに建物から庇[ひさし]が張り出しては来ているけれど、こう風に流される軽い雨では、彼女の腰のない髪に雨粒がまとわりついて重くする。それを厭[いと]うたのもあるし、道端に雨ばかりを眺めて座りこんでいると、なんだか地面に根を下ろして茸になってしまいそうだ、とも。
source.english:
Licking drops from his lips, he glanced at Kuro just as she looked up. Their meeting eyes asked the same thing: time for a rest?
Both agreed, and both tacitly understood that resting meant sitting down. Kuro hoped to do it indoors. Eaves projected over either side of the street, certainly, but rain this light drifted with the wind, clinging to her limp hair and weighing it down. She disliked that. Besides, sitting at the roadside watching nothing but rain made her feel she might put down roots and turn into a mushroom.

target.text: Licking the drops of his lips, when he peered down at Kuro, it just so happened to be when she, too, looked up at the young man, and their exchanged glances asked each other the same question: 「How about taking a break soon?」 But while neither of them objected to that idea in itself, there was a tacit understanding between them: if they were to rest, they wanted it to be somewhere they could sit down.

And then there was Kuro's desire, with her saying that she preferred to take a break indoors if possible, for while it was true that eaves extended out from the buildings on both sides of the street, with the rain being so light that it was carried on the wind, the raindrops would cling to her limp hair and make it heavy. While there was the fact she disliked that, it was also in part because, if she sat by the wayside just staring at the rain as it fell, she felt as though she would somehow take root in the ground and turn into a mushroom, or so she said.

source.japanese:
……他愛のない妄想ではある（茸にあるのは石突きで根ではないという些末事はさておき）。あるけれど、南方の密林には迷いこんだ人間を樹に変えてしまう魔処があると朔屋は聞いた事がある。その密林とこの廃址一つの共通点があって、あちらも年中細かな雨に覆われているとかで。……魔力が姿を変えるとて、密林なら聳立する樹にもしてくれようが、この鬱々とした死街には青々とした樹木はそぐわない。ならば建物の陰にひっそり寄り添う大小の茸、というのが朔屋とクロの成れの果て、というのはあっても可笑しくはない話で、朔屋もクロの意見を受け入れた。
　一方朔屋からの注文というのは、これが中々に難しい。
source.english:
A harmless fantasy, certainly—setting aside the trivial fact that mushrooms had stem bases, not roots. Yet Sakuya had heard of enchanted places in southern jungles that turned lost humans into trees. Those jungles shared one thing with these ruins: they too were reportedly covered in fine rain all year. Magic might transform a person, but a jungle would at least make him a towering tree. Green trees would not suit this gloomy dead town. A pair of mushrooms, large and small, nestling in the shadows of a building: that might reasonably be their fate. He accepted Kuro's suggestion.
His own condition was rather more difficult.

source.japanese: 朔屋は、骨がない屋内を望んだのである。もう何軒観てきたのかしかと数えてはいないが、魚の、蛙や井守の、鰭があるの四肢があるの、とにかく骨はもう胸焼けするくらいに見飽きて、しばらくは視界に入らないところで過ごしたいという、単純にしてこの島の状況を思えば贅沢な希望、どちらかというクロより朔屋の方が厳しい条件、を充たす為に二人は今しばらく痛む足を引きずり歩かないとならなかった。
source.english: Sakuya wanted an interior without bones. He had lost count of the houses he had seen. Fish, frogs, newts; fins, limbs—he was sick of bones to the point of heartburn, and wished to spend a little time where none were visible. Simple, yet luxurious given the island's circumstances. His condition was stricter than hers. To satisfy it, they had to drag their aching feet a little farther.

target.text: ……It was but a silly delusion (setting aside the trivial matter that mushrooms have a stem base and not roots). That was all it was, but Sakuya had heard tales of places within the jungles of the south inhabited by magical beings that would transform any humans who had strayed within into trees. And those jungles and this ruin had a point of commonality, for those were also shrouded in a light rain all year round.

……While magic might change one's shape, and might perhaps be able to turn people into grand, towering trees in a dense jungle, a verdant tree would not at all suit this gloomy town of the dead. Therefore, perhaps turning into a pair of mushrooms, one large and one small, quietly snuggling up to each other in the shadow of a building would be the ultimate fate awaiting Sakuya and Kuro; that really didn't seem so ridiculously outlandish a possibility after all, and so Sakuya concurred with Kuro's opinion. On the other hand, when it came to Sakuya's request, this was rather more difficult to grant.

Sakuya wished for a room with no bones. He could no longer count how many he had seen, but there were those of fish, of frogs, and of newts, with fins and limbs alike; regardless, he was simply so utterly sick and tired of seeing bones that it gave him heartburn, so for a little while, he'd like to spend some time without any being in his sight, but simple wish that this was, considering the state of this island, it made for a rather excessive demand; in order to satisfy these conditions, wherein Sakuya's, if anything, was harder to meet than Kuro's, the two of them had to drag their aching feet forwards for a while longer.

source.japanese: 建物を片端から覗きこみ、この辺りは魚類と両生類の区画だからどこもかしこも木製の生[い]け簀[す]や桶[おけ]、中の水は乾ききって、かつては泳いでいた物達の骨骨骨、しまいには朔屋、クロの肌の色さえ剥き出しの骨に見えてくるような始末の、二人して所期の目的が肺魚の骨群を探し当てる事だと言うのをすっかり忘れて、目的がすり替わって、骨骨骨、がない建物、ない建物と、二人で口の中に念じつつ死街をうろつき回る様、気が触れた亡霊とさほど異ならず。
source.english: They peered into building after building. This was the fish and amphibian district: wooden pools and tubs everywhere, their water dried away, and the bones, bones, bones of former swimmers. Eventually even Kuro's skin began to look like exposed bone to Sakuya. Both forgot that their original purpose was to find lungfish remains. Their goal changed. Bones, bones, bones—a building without them, without them. Muttering that to themselves as they wandered the dead town, they differed little from demented ghosts.

source.japanese: 見つかったか、見つからなかったか、の点で言えば、見つかった。ただ、二重の意味で。
source.english: As to whether they found what they sought: they did. In two senses.

target.text: They systematically peered into every single building, and given that this area was the section of fish and amphibians, there were wooden fish tanks and tubs all over the place, the water within dried up, all full of nothing but bones, bones and more bones of the creatures that once swam within them, and by the end of it, even the colour of Sakuya and Kuro's skin had begun to resemble naked bone.

They had both completely forgotten their original objective of finding skeletons belonging to lungfish; their objective had subtly shifted, bones bones bones, a building without bones, just one building; the way the two of them wandered through this town of death, all while quietly chanting such thoughts to themselves, was hardly any different to a pair of deranged ghosts.
In terms of whether they found one or not, they did. However, it was in two senses.

source.japanese: その建物は、一見すると公会堂のように見えなくもない、他よりは大きめな建築物で、玄関口の扉は頑丈そうな、山門じみて背が高く、とてもではないが朔屋の船員ナイフ程度では歯が立ちそうにない。そもそもそのナイフも、先程からの無理な使用が祟って刀身がねじれてきてしまっている。
source.english: The building was larger than the others and looked rather like a public hall. Its entrance doors were sturdy, tall as a temple gate; Sakuya's sailor's knife could never manage them. The blade was already twisting from the strain of its recent use.

target.text: At a first glance, that building looked somewhat like a public hall; it was a structure on the larger side compared to the rest, and the front door was a sturdy-looking sort, tall like a main temple gate, and though he wouldn't outright call it impossible, it really didn't seem like prising it open was within the capabilities of the likes of Sakuya's sailor's knife. And that was to say nothing of how the blade of the knife had already ended up thoroughly warped from the rough treatment it had been put through earlier.

source.japanese:
仕方なく二人は、手拭いにクロのズック靴の片方を包んで、建物の窓を叩き割るという些[いささ]か乱暴な手段を執らざるをえなかった。手拭いに包もうにもこの島には大きめの石ころなど言うものは見当たらなかったから。窓硝子の鍵をこじ開け、ようよう入りこんだ屋内は、これも公会堂のホールのようにがらんと広く、やはり板壁板張りの床、そして骨は───なかった。観たところ小骨の類もひとっつも。
　喜び勇んで駆けこんだ朔屋だったが。
source.english:
With no alternative, they wrapped one of Kuro's canvas shoes in the cloth and used it to smash a window—a somewhat violent measure. The island offered no sizable stone to wrap instead. They forced the window latch and finally entered. Inside was a broad, empty space like a public auditorium, again with wooden walls and floor. And bones… none. Not even a little one, as far as they could see.
Sakuya rushed in delighted.

target.text: Left with little other choice, the two wrapped the towel around one of Kuro's canvas shoes, forced to resort to the slightly violent means of smashing one of the windows of the building to pieces. They had to make do with wrapping a towel around her shoe, for there were no largish stones or anything of the sort to be found on this island.

After prising open the window lock, they slipped inside at long last; the interior was also vast and empty, much like the main chamber of a public hall, with wooden walls and a floor made up of wooden boards as expected, and the bones were───nowhere to be found. From what he could see, there was not even a single tiny bone anywhere. Overjoyed, Sakuya rushed inside, but.

source.japanese:
広間の中に駆けこんで、踏みしめた床の板敷きの途端に。クロは観た、聞いた。朔屋には衝[つ]き抜けた、絶叫した。
　クロがまず観たもの、駆けこんでいった朔屋の身体が、夕暮れに翔ぶ蝙蝠が、方向転換の際その自在で急速度のあまりに視界からふっとかき消えて見えるように、青年の身体が見えなくなる瞬間の。次に聞いたものは、魂消えるような絶叫に、もし広間に何らかの亡霊潜[ひそ]んでいたとしてもたちどころに退散しただろう、それくらいに痛切だった。
　朔屋は床板を踏み抜いて、両脚の間に一枚の板、挟まる形になって。
source.english:
The instant he ran into the hall and trod upon its boards, Kuro saw and heard.
Sakuya felt something pierce him, and screamed. First she saw his body vanish, like a bat in dusk making such a quick, effortless turn that it suddenly disappears from sight. Then came a scream so agonized that any ghost lurking in the hall would surely have fled at once.
Sakuya had gone through the floor, leaving a board between his legs.

source.japanese:
だから朔屋が受けた衝撃とは、股間から脳天を、まるで地に潜[ひそ]みし蛟竜が時機を得て垂直に昇天しさったかに貫き抜けた痛打によるものであり、迸った絶叫は言わずもがな、男性として深刻な危機に直面したためである。
　両目の中ではぱちぱちと弾ける星屑を観た。
source.english:
The shock was a crushing blow that shot from his crotch through the crown of his head, like a dragon hidden in the earth seizing its moment to ascend vertically into heaven. The scream hardly needs explaining. He faced a grave crisis as a man.
Stars crackled inside both eyes.

target.text: He rushed inside the hall, and the second he stepped firmly down on the wooden floorboards. Kuro saw it, then heard it. That Sakuya stepped right through it, then screamed. First, Kuro saw Sakuya's body rushing inside, and much like a bat flying through the twilight that, due to its free and rapid movement, seems to suddenly vanish into thin air when changing directions, the instant the young man's body then disappeared from view. Next, she heard a scream so soul-shattering that any ghosts lurking within the hall would have fled the very instant they heard it; it was that heartbreaking.
Sakuya had stepped through the floorboards, leaving a plank lodged right between his legs.

Accordingly, the shock that Sakuya experienced was like a crushing blow that pierced him all the way from his groin to the crown of his head, as if a kouryuu that had been lurking on the ground had seized its opportunity and ascended vertically to the heavens in one swift motion; the scream that burst forth from him was, needless to say, because he, as a man, was facing a grave crisis. Sakuya saw countless tiny stars crackling and popping in both his eyes. (TN: A kouryuu, written "蛟竜", is a form of Chinese dragon that dwells in water and transforms into a flying dragon when the conditions are just right.)

source.japanese: しばらくはクロがどれだけおろおろと慰めようとしても、朔屋は股間を押さえて転がり回るしかなく、どうにか落ち着いた頃にはげっそり頬がこけていた。
source.english: For a while, however anxiously Kuro tried to comfort him, he could only roll about clutching his crotch. By the time he settled, his cheeks had hollowed.

target.text: For a while, no matter how the flustered Kuro helplessly tried to console him, Sakuya could only roll around on the floor while clutching his crotch, and by the time he had managed to somehow calm himself, he looked haggard, his cheeks gaunt.

source.japanese: ともかく、どういう底意地の悪い落とし穴だと踏み抜いた辺りを調べれば、床板が朽ちていて足が突き抜けた、というのではない。この島の木材には不思議と朽ちたモノは無いと言う事はまだ朔屋達は知らなかったが、ともかく、青年は床に架け渡されてた長板の、緩んでいた隙間に足を踏み入れてしまったと、そう言う事らしい。
source.english: What malicious pitfall was this? Examining the place he had fallen through, they found it was not rotten flooring. They did not yet know the island's timber was strangely free of decay. In any event, he seemed to have stepped into a loosened gap among the long boards laid across the floor.

source.japanese: 一体どういう意図で床にそんな長板を架け渡してあるのかと覗きこめば、どうやらこの広間の床全体というのが、長板を組み合わせた蓋のように造り。
source.english: Why had such boards been laid there? Peering inside, they found that the hall's entire floor seemed to be a lid assembled from long planks.

target.text: In any case, when he went to investigate the area where he had stepped into what had to be some manner of malicious pitfall, he realized that it was not simply that the floorboards were rotten and his foot had gone right though them. Sakuya and Kuro were still unaware of the fact that, strangely enough, none of the wood on this island had actually decayed, but regardless, the young man had stepped into a loose gap in the long boards spanning the floor, or so it seemed.

When he peered into the gap to figure out what in the world the intention was behind placing such long boards across the floor, it seemed as if the entire floor of this hall was constructed like a lid of long planks joined together.

source.japanese:
端から外して開けていくと───
　かつては生[い]け簀[す]だったと思しき、屋外より一段下がった板敷きの床となっていて、床の上は、既に水は流出してしまったようで乾いて粗[あら]びて、そして、至るところに骨の塊。肺魚の。
source.english:
They removed them one by one from the edge.
Beneath lay what seemed a former fish tank, its boarded bottom below the outside level. The water had apparently drained away long ago, leaving a dry, rough floor. All over it lay clumps of bones. Lungfish bones.

target.text: When he then loosened the planks from the edge and opened up the floor─── It seemed to have once served as a fish tank; there was a wooden floor built one level lower than the outside, and the surface of that floor, as though the water had already drained away, was dry and rough, and finally, there were clumps of bone, here and there and everywhere. Bones of lungfish.

source.japanese: そして至るところの骨の中、星が下ったように煌めいていた。
source.english: Among the bones scattered everywhere, points of light glittered as though stars had fallen.

target.text: And within those bones scattered all over the place, it glittered as if the stars themselves had fallen.

source.japanese: ザウエル、だった。
source.english: Zauer.

target.text: They were Sauers.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いっぱい、きらきら……」
source.english: “So many sparkly things…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい、みんな、みんな呼んでこないとっ」
source.english: “Everyone. We've got to get everyone!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「So many sparklies……」
【Naomasa】 「Oi, the others, we have to go and get all the others!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「てめえ朔屋、そしてクロ、どういう冗談これは。いやだって冗談とか仕込みでしょ？　そうでもないとあたしが見てるもの、全部現実って……」
source.english: “Sakuya, you bastard—and Kuro—what kind of joke is this? It is a joke, right? Something you've rigged up? Otherwise everything I'm seeing is real…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやだから、真贋の鑑定は後で、
　あんたらがっ、て……ちょ、
　首……極ま……っ。
　あん……でも、おっぱぃ……」
source.english:
“I told you, you can check if they're genuine later…
you…
Wait… my neck…
choking… Ahh… but your boobs…”

source.japanese: キサラは激怒とにやけ笑いと驚愕の、いずれの顔を造ればいいのか判じかねたかの奇怪な表情を頬桁に張りつけていたし、どういう顔をすればいいのか困っていたのは朔屋もまた。背後からぐいぐい締めあげてくる彼女の乳房と朔屋の背中は密着し、意識混濁と至福の弾力が混淆された感覚を朔屋にもたらしていたから。
source.english: Kisara wore a grotesque expression, unable to decide whether it should be fury, a grin or astonishment. Nor did Sakuya know what expression to wear. Her breasts pressed against his back as she tightened her hold from behind, giving him a sensation compounded of fading consciousness and blissful elasticity.

source.japanese: やがて朔屋の腕が糸の切れた人形の如くかくんと落ちて反応がなくなったと見るや、焦れきったキサラは朔屋を突き飛ばし、生け簀[す]の床へ突進していく。
source.english: When his arms dropped limply like a puppet's with cut strings and he ceased responding, the exasperated Kisara shoved him away and charged onto the tank floor.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Damn it, Sakuya, and you, Kuro, what kind of joke is this? I mean, this has to be a joke or some kind of setup, right? If it isn't, that means everything that I'm seeing right now is actually real……」
【Naomasa】 「No, again, leave the appraisal of their authenticity for later, you guys can, wait……hol-, neck……can't brea……. Agh……but, titties……」

Kisara had a strange expression plastered across her cheekbones, as if she found it hard to decide if she should show rage, a smirk, or astonishment, but when it came to struggling over which expression to make, Sakuya was in the same boat. For the woman's breasts were pressed firmly against Sakuya's back as she squeezed him tightly from behind, bringing to Sakuya a sensation formed from a mixture of blissful bounciness and a muddled mind.

Finally, noticing how Sakuya had ceased responding, his arms fallen limply down by his sides like a marionette with its strings cut, Kisara, having completely lost her patience, thrust Sakuya away, then charged down towards the bottom of the fish tank.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「い!?　全部これ、なの、嘘じゃない、
　───ザウエルなの!?」
source.english:
“Huh!?
All of this—seriously—it's Zauer!?”

source.japanese: 朽たれた藁のようにふらふらと崩れかかった朔屋を助け起こしたのはシサムだ、助け起こしたというには妙だ、朔屋の後ろ襟首を片手掴みにして、足許力入らぬ態を構わず力任せに引いて、骨格内に抱かれて燃ゆる宝珠まで、青年の足は引きずられてずるずるなり。ぐい、と宝珠へ青年の顔押し遣って、
source.english: It was Sisam who helped Sakuya up as he collapsed like withered straw. ‘Helped up’ was an odd description. She seized his collar from behind with one hand and dragged him bodily toward a jewel burning within a skeleton, indifferent to his powerless feet scraping along. Then she thrust his face toward it.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うーんんぅ……、
　俺には多分そうだってしか……言えないってのに……」
source.english:
“Nnnh…
I can only say… I think so…”
