source.japanese: その辺で疑念を昂奮が押しのけたのか、やにわ、感極まったあまりにがっと両腕を天に挑戦する反逆児のように高々と突き上げ、喉も垂直に反らして、口から噴き上がったのは長三和音の雄叫び、音が螺旋状の膨らみを持ってするする伸び上がり、声の尾を曳いてシサムも宝珠へと猛進していく。
source.english: Perhaps excitement finally shoved doubt aside. Overcome, she flung both arms high, like a rebel defying heaven, tipped her head far back and let a roar in a major triad burst forth. The sound swelled in a spiral, stretching upward. Trailing that long cry, Sisam charged toward the jewels too.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「IIH!? Are these, all of these, and you're not lying, ───SAUERS!?」

Wobbling back and forth on the verge of crumbling to the floor like a piece of rotten straw, it was Shisamu who helped Sakuya back to his feet, but calling what she did helping him up was questionable, for she had grabbed the back of Sakuya's collar with one hand, pulling him with all her might without the slightest regard for his inability to stand by himself, and the young man's feet were dragged along the floor, all the way to the burning jewel embraced by a skeleton. She shoved the young man's face towards the jewel.
【Naomasa】 「Hmmmm……, All I can really say is that…… they're probably real, so……」

The excitement must have swept aside any lingering doubts, for suddenly, overcome with emotion, she thrust both arms high into the air like a traitor challenging the heavens, head bent back with her throat exposed, and erupting from her mouth came a triumphant cry resounding like a major triad, the sound stretching outwards in a swelling helix pattern; with her voice trailing behind her, Shisamu also charged towards the jewels.

source.japanese: いきなり手を離されたものだから、朔屋は前のめりに肺魚の骨格中に倒れこむ、しばらくじたばたと骨片と格闘した後ようやく立ち上がったが、今度は立ちくらみが来て、後ろによろめいてまた体を崩しかける、危うし、と手を、飛ぼうとする鶏の羽ばたきのように振り回せば、どん、と壁が支えてくれた。
source.english: Released abruptly, Sakuya fell forward among the lungfish skeletons. He fought the fragments awhile before standing. Then dizziness struck; he staggered backward, nearly falling again. He waved his hands like a chicken trying to fly. Thump. A wall supported him.

source.japanese:
随分と男臭い壁で、変にごつごつとしていた。
　じょりと、背中に擦れたのは剛[こわ]い毛の感触の、怖々と振り返れば今度は水夫長だ、腕組みの仁王立ち、足をずんと踏んばって、広間に散乱した骨と宝珠を睨[にら]みつけている。
source.english:
A wall that smelled strongly of a man, and was oddly knobbly.
Coarse hair rasped against his back. He fearfully turned. The boatswain this time, arms folded, feet planted like a temple guardian, glaring at the bones and jewels scattered through the hall.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……お前、なんか企んでじゃないか？」
source.english: “…You plotting something?”

source.japanese: 憮然と吐いた言葉がどこまでも疑り深い。
source.english: The sullen words were steeped in suspicion.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだって、みんなそう疑り深いんだ。
　たとえ偽物だとしても、俺にはこんなの用意している暇はないっての」
source.english:
“Why does everyone have to be so suspicious?
Even if they were fakes, when would I have had time to set all this up?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それに、こんな、内側から燃えているような石、どんな贋物用意するのだって大変だってーの」
source.english: “And making fake stones that look like they're burning inside would be a hell of a job!”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「───ま、それもそうか。
　───それにしても、てめえとクロがなぁ。
　見つけてくるとはなぁ……」
source.english:
“…Well, that's true.
Still… you and Kuro.
Finding this…”

target.text: With her hand having suddenly released its grip on him, Sakuya tilted forwards and collapsed into the lungfish skeletons, and after floundering about while wrestling with the bone fragments for a time, he finally rose to his feet once more, but this time, a dizzy spell overcame him, his body staggering backwards; about to lose his balance once more, just on the verge of collapsing, when he swung his arms up and down like a chicken flapping its wings to take flight, with a thud, a wall supported his body.

The wall had an awful reek of male body odour, and it was strangely rugged to boot. Realizing that what scraped against his back was the texture of coarse hair, when he timidly turned around, this time, it was the Bosun, his arms crossed in an imposing stance, legs planted firmly on the ground, glaring at the bones and jewels scattered all over the hall.
【Bosun】 「……You're up to something, aren't you?」
The words he spat out sourly were dripping with unwavering distrust.
【Naomasa】 「Why are you all so suspicious of me? Even assuming these are fakes, I'm telling you, I didn't have the time to set this up even if I wanted to.」
【Naomasa】 「Besides, just preparing fakes that could seem to burn from within like these ones do would be incredibly difficult.」
【Bosun】 「───Well, suppose that's true. ───Even so, you and Kuro, huh. Unbelievable that you'd the ones to find them……」

source.japanese: 長々と嘆息すると、腹の肉が凹んで、背を預ける形となっていた朔屋はついよろめいた、と次の呼吸で水夫長はぼんとズボンの釦[ボタン]千切らんかの勢いで腹を膨張させた為、青年はパチンコの弾よろしく弾き飛ばされ、また床にぶち転がされる羽目となった。水夫長も宝珠に驀進していく。
source.english: Long sighed at length, his belly sinking inward. Leaning against it, Sakuya wobbled. On the next breath, the belly swelled with a boom as if to tear the buttons off Long's trousers. Sakuya was shot away like a pachinko ball and sprawled upon the floor again. The boatswain charged toward the jewels too.

target.text: As he heaved a long, deep sigh, the flesh of his stomach collapsed inwards, and Sakuya, who had come to lean back against it, suddenly stumbled; with his next breath, the Bosun's stomach swelled up with such force that it looked like it might tear the buttons off his trousers, and so the young man was sent flying like a pachinko ball, thrown down on the floor once more. The Bosun, too, charged headlong at the jewels.

source.japanese: せっかく皆のために見つけてきたというのに、誰も彼も目前の情景を容易に受け入れようとはせず、疑念の相をそれぞれしつこいまでに開陳したけれど、自ら燃える宝珠の炎に疑団たちまち溶かされて、飛びついていく。
source.english: They had found them for everyone, yet nobody readily accepted the sight. Each stubbornly displayed suspicion. Then the flames of the self-burning jewels melted all doubt, and everyone pounced.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「拾え拾えーーっ!!」
source.english: “Grab them! Grab them!”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こんだけありゃあ、みんなで分けたってどんだけの数になるか……」
source.english: “With this many, even split between all of us, how much would we each get…?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんだってできる、なんだって買える……。
　酒、船、豪邸……もっと凄いのも、なんだって」
source.english:
“Anything we want. Anything we want to buy…
booze, ships, mansions… bigger things, anything…”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「やっべぇ、顔が変な笑いで固まっちゃう」
source.english: “Oh, shit. My face is stuck in this weird grin.”

source.japanese:
───皆が笑っていた。
　シサムとキサラも、水夫長も、下級水夫達も、白炎撒き散らす、星雲の開闢の時に立ち合わせたように、宝珠の炎に魅せられて。
　その笑顔はなるほど、いかにもな現世的な欲望に裏打ちされた、欲の脂滴るような大笑だったろう。けれどそれだけに偽りない笑顔であり、人間的とも言い換えられて、朔屋もまたいつしか笑いの渦に加わっていた。
source.english:
Everyone smiled.
Sisam and Kisara, the boatswain, the junior sailors—all enchanted by the jewels' flames, as though present at the birth of a nebula scattering white fire.
Their broad grins were certainly founded upon worldly desire, dripping the grease of greed. But that made them honest smiles, human ones. Sakuya found himself joining the whirl of laughter.

source.japanese: 増援に駆けつけてきた下級水夫の流れに呑みこまれて、右回転左回転にくるくる舞うクロを引っぱり出して、抱きかかえる。
source.english: More junior sailors came rushing in and swept Kuro along, spinning her this way and that. Sakuya pulled her free and gathered her into his arms.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はははっ、はっはっはっ、
　どうだクロ、やったな俺達！
　こりゃあ間違いなく一財産だ」
source.english:
“Hahaha! We did it,
Kuro!
That's a fortune, no question!”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「きらきら、一杯で、みんな、嬉しい？
　クロと朔屋さん、ほめてもらえる？」
source.english:
“Lots of sparkly things… Everyone happy?
Will they praise Kuro and Mr. Sakuya?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もちろんそうだろうさ！
　こんないっぱいあるなら、
　俺らにも分け前がさ！
　一つくらい、貰ったって良いだろうぜっ」
source.english:
“Of course!
With so many,
we'll get a share too.
Surely we could have at least one!”

source.japanese:
分け前と言ったって、たくさんは要らないと朔屋は、クロに頬をすり寄せながら胸の裡[うち]で数える。二個・三個、その程度で良い、否そんなに沢山も要らない、一つで良い。
　一つくらい拝借させてもらう程度で良い、一つくらいなら、こんなにも沢山転がっているのだもの、水夫長達もお目こぼししてくれるだろう。
source.english:
He did not need much of a share, he counted inwardly as he pressed his cheek to hers. Two or three would do. No, that was too many. One.
Merely borrowing one would be enough. There were so many lying about; Long and the others would surely overlook a single one.

source.japanese: そう考えて朔屋は、一つを、選んでいると目移りしてしまいそうだから、一番近くに転がっていたものを一つだけ、クロを抱きかかえたまま身を屈め、摘み上げて、指の間で拈[ひね]り回して、そうして見つめてみれば確かにこの宝珠、希有にして美しい。
source.english: So he picked one up. Choosing might tempt his eye to wander, so he took the nearest. Still holding Kuro, he bent, lifted it and rolled it between his fingers. Looking closely, he saw the jewel truly was rare and beautiful.

source.japanese:
───この稀代の宝珠の発見を、皆には告げず、クロと山分け、或いは朔屋であっても彼女を欺く事など容易だろうの、独り占め。
　そういった悪想念が朔屋に産まれなかったのは何故だろう。
source.english:
Why had he not conceived of keeping this extraordinary discovery from everyone, splitting it with Kuro—or even taking it all himself?
Deceiving her would be easy even for Sakuya.

source.japanese:
幾つか理由はあったろう。このランクの宝石となると、値段などあってないも同然、幾らまで金を支払えるかがステータスとなる、と。他にも、たとえ朔屋自身が所有し得ずとも、信天翁号の皆が富めば、回り回って朔屋の利にもなるだろう、と、等々、尤もらしい理由は幾つか挙げられるだろうが、結局のところ朔屋は面倒だったのである。
　値が付かないほど高価、という事は、換金するにも煩雑な手間がかかると言う事。質草と叩きこもうとしたところで、質屋の主人に怪訝な顔で門前払い、というのが結句だろう。
source.english:
There were several possible reasons. At this level, gemstones had effectively no price: how much one could pay became a mark of status. Even if he could not own them himself, wealth for the Albatross crew would eventually benefit him. And so forth. Plausible reasons, several of them.
In the end, though, Sakuya could not be bothered. Pricelessly expensive meant troublesome to turn into money. Try dropping one into a pawnshop, and the proprietor would look askance and turn him away.

source.japanese: 換金できない株券と同じ様なもので、朔屋が所有していたところで、戸棚の中に仕舞い込んで、時折引っぱり出してはその驚異、幻惑の美を鑑賞するのがせいぜいがところ関の山。自分にとっては過ぎたる財だと、朔屋はそのように考えた。
source.english: Like shares one could not cash in. Owning it would mean keeping it in a cupboard, taking it out now and then to admire its wondrous, bewildering beauty. That was about the limit. A treasure beyond his station, he thought.

source.japanese: 金にこだわらない、といえば美質であり、金の価値を知らない、といえば欠点にもなろう、どちらにしても朔屋にとって金というのは、札入れに入った紙幣数枚、今日明日の酒代に足りるかどうかの単位で測られ、それ以上ともなると、店を借り切るとか女を買いにいくとかで、財を元手に利殖と言った経済感覚はこの青年に、ない。
source.english: Indifference to money could be called a virtue; ignorance of its value, a fault. Either way, Sakuya measured money in the few notes in his wallet, enough or not enough for today's and tomorrow's drinks. Beyond that, he might book a whole tavern for himself or pay for women. He had no notion of using wealth to generate more.

source.japanese: ただただ、皆が大歓声に夢中で漁っているのを眺めるのが楽しかった。摘み上げた指先で、天地開闢の炎を封じこめて、千変万化に転変する色合いと光を見つめるのも面白かった、何より、頬摺りにクロが滑[すべ]らかな肌で応えてくれたのが嬉しかった。
source.english: He simply enjoyed watching everyone scrabble about with great cheers. Enjoyed the changing colors and light of the fire of creation enclosed between his fingertips. Above all, he was glad Kuro answered his nuzzling with her smooth cheek.

source.japanese: 始めのうちクロは、船の皆が怒号張り上げ目を血走らせ、宝珠に飛びかかっていく様子に戸惑っていたけれど、朔屋の嬉しげな声にすぐに頬を柔らかくして、柔らかな、そうとても柔らかな笑みを解いてみせたのだった。
source.english: At first she had been bewildered by the crew's shouts, their bloodshot eyes, their lunges at the jewels. Sakuya's delighted voice soon softened her cheeks. She unfolded a soft, very soft smile.

source.japanese: 多分この時、歓びは歓びでも、朔屋とクロだけは他の乗り組み達とは異なる想いを共有していたのだろう。
source.english: Perhaps just then, joyful though everyone was, Sakuya and Kuro alone shared a different feeling from the rest.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そっかぁ……そんなら、よかったねぇ。
　朔屋さんとクロとでも、できたねぇ。
　クロ達にも、できることあったんだ……」
source.english:
“Oh… then that's good. Mr.
Sakuya and Kuro could do it too.
There was something we could do…”

source.japanese:
堅牢な船の中の奥まった船室に抱かれてあるかに安心しきって、朔屋の抱擁に身を委ね、足先を跳ね上げている様などは、日頃少女を蝕[むしば]む屈託など溶けさったようにあどけなく、朗らかな魅力さえクロに与えていた。
　三白眼の眸[ひとみ]でさえも、風変わりな可愛げに輝いて、嵐の中で硬質の貴石と結晶する、あの神懸かった心力が噴出する窓みたいな目より、ずっとこっちの方が好きになれると、朔屋はクロと犬の子同士のように体を強く合わせる。
source.english:
She trusted his embrace as completely as if nestled in a sheltered cabin deep within a sturdy ship. Her feet kicked up; her usual cares seemed dissolved, leaving an innocence that gave her a bright charm. Even her eyes,
with whites showing beneath the irises, shone with an unusual sweetness. Sakuya thought he could love these eyes far more easily than the hard gems they crystallized into during storms, windows through which that godlike mental power burst forth. He pressed close to her like one puppy to another.

target.text: For all that he'd gone out of his way to find this for their sake, none were willing to so easily accept the sight before their eyes, each and every one of them expressing their respective doubts to the point of stubbornness, but even the persistent lump of distrust lodged deep within them quickly melted away before the flames of these naturally blazing jewels, and they all jumped at the alluring sight.
【Shisamu】 「PICK 'EM UP! PICK 'EM UUUP!!」
【Kisara】 「With this many, even if we split them up between all of us, who knows how many we'll each get……」
【Shisamu】 「I could do anything, I could buy anything……. Drink, ships, mansions…… and even more amazing things, anything!」
【Kisara】 「Oh shit, my face is freezing into this freaky smile.」

───They were all smiling. Shisamu and Kisara, the Bosun, and the deck boys too, as though witnessing the scattering white flames born at the genesis of a nebula, were all captivated by the flames of the jewels. The smiles on those faces were surely underpinned by terribly worldly desires, indeed, their raucous laughter dripped with the grease of greed. But precisely because of that, they were genuine smiles; put another way, they could also be described as human, and before he knew it, Sakuya had also joined the vortex of laughter.

He found Kuro being swept away by the current of deck boys who were rushing in as reinforcement, spinning clockwise and counterclockwise, round and round, and he pulled her out, then lifted her into an embrace.
【Naomasa】 「Hahaha, ha-ha-ha, how about that, Kuro, we did it! Now this is a fortune, no two ways about it!」
【Kuro】 「Is everyone happy, with all these sparklies? Will Kuro and Sakuya-san be praised?」
【Naomasa】 「But of course! There's so many of them, we'll get a cut too! We can grab at least one, right?!」

When it came to his share, he didn't really need that much, Sakuya thought, counting within his head while pulling Kuro's cheek into his chest. Two, three, that many should be enough, no, he didn't really need that many, one would be plenty. Borrowing just one would be fine; if it was just the one, then with this many rolling around on the floor, the Bosun and the rest would overlook it, surely.

With those thoughts in his head, afraid that he would be unable to choose if he tried to pick out just one, Sakuya therefore stooped over, all while still holding Kuro in his arms, to pluck up just the one that was lying the closest to him, spinning it round between his fingers, and when he looked at it closely like so, this jewel was indeed a rare sort of beauty.

───Without informing the others of the discovery of these matchless jewels, he could split them equally with Kuro; or else, for surely even a man like Sakuya would easily be able to pull the wool over this girl's eyes, he could take them all for himself. Whyever was it that such wicked ideas had not been born within Sakuya?

There must have been several reasons. Once a jewel was of this rank, it might as well as not have a price, and the amount one could spend to obtain it would itself become a status symbol, or so he had heard. Furthermore, even if Sakuya could not obtain one for himself, if everyone on the Albatross grew richer, some of that would eventually make its way back into Sakuya's hands, and so on; he could offer many a plausible reason, but at the end of the day, Sakuya simply found it far too bothersome.

Being so expensive it was priceless meant that converting it into cash would be an awful hassle. Even should he try to pawn it off somewhere, the pawnbroker would simply turn him away at the door with a dubious look on his face, and that would likely be the end of that.

It was like having a stock certificate that could not be exchanged for cash, and should one find itself in Sakuya's possession, it would, at best, be kept tucked away in some cupboard, occasionally pulled out to appreciate that miraculous, bewitching beauty. It was a fortune too great for one such as himself; that was how Sakuya thought of it.

To not be attached to money is a virtue; to be ignorant of the value of money is a flaw; regardless of which it was, in Sakuya's eyes, money was just some sheets of paper stuffed in his billfold, measured only in units indicating their capacity to cover the drinking expenses of today and tomorrow, and should he end up with anything beyond that, he'd charter the bar or go buy a woman, for the good economic sense to use his fortune as capital to make more money with was nowhere to be found in this young man.

He simply enjoyed watching the others excitedly cheering as they lost themselves in their scavenging. While it was also amusing to hold between his fingertips the flames of creation and gaze upon the infinite variety of ever-changing colours and light, more than anything, he was happy that Kuro responded to his cheek nuzzle with her own smooth skin.

At first, Kuro had been confused at the way the others from the ship had all roared, how they had seemed to leap at the jewels with bloodshot eyes, but at Sakuya's joyful voice, her cheeks quickly softened, breaking into a gentle, yes, a very gentle smile.
In this moment, though it, too, was a form of joy, Sakuya and Kuro alone must have shared in a feeling quite different from rest of the crew.
【Kuro】 「That so……then, that's great. Even Sakuya-san and Kuro could do it. There was something, something even we could do……」

Feeling completely at ease as if held in a cabin deep within a sturdy ship, she surrendered herself to Sakuya's embrace, and the way she lifted her toes up gave Kuro an innocent, even cheerful charm, as if all the worries that usually ate away at the girl had melted away. Even with their scleral show, her sanpaku eyes sparkled with a peculiar loveliness, and compared to those eyes that crystallized into hard gemstones when it stormed, those eyes that seemed like windows from which that divine force of will erupted, these were easier to fall for by far; so Sakuya thought as he and Kuro pressed their bodies tightly against each other like puppies.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ねえ朔屋さん、クロね、
　朔屋さんに教えてもらえれば、
　きっと他のことだって───」

source.english: “Yeah!”

source.japanese: なんだってできる、とまでは朔屋だって思い上がっていない。それでも、仲間を驚かせてやれるくらいの事は出来る。悪意で出し抜くのではなく、偉い奴だと笑顔で迎えてもらえるくらいの事は、たとえ少しばかり困難であろうとも、このクロとなら、自分だって少しは無理と背伸びで、やれる事がある、と。
source.english: Even he was not conceited enough to think they could do anything whatsoever. But they could surprise their companions. Not maliciously outwit them, but do something to be welcomed with smiling praise. Difficult it might be, yet with Kuro he could strain a little, reach a little farther, and accomplish something.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Hey, Sakuya-san, if Kuro could be taught by Sakuya-san, then there has to be even more things that───」
【Naomasa】 「Yeah───!」

Even Sakuya wasn't so conceited as to think they could achieve anything they set their minds to. Even so, they could at least do something that would surprise their comrades. Not by outwitting them through spite, but by doing something that made them thought of as great people and greeted with a smile, and even should it prove just a little challenging here and there, as long as he was with this Kuro here, even he could accomplish something, if he just pushed past his limits and reached a little higher.

source.japanese:
それは。
　それこそが。
　朔屋の。そしてクロの。
source.english:
That.
That very thing.
Was Sakuya's. And Kuro's.

source.japanese: ───思い上がり───
source.english: Presumption.

source.japanese:
───容易に過ぎる───
　とは考えなかったか、朔屋よ？
source.english:
Didn't you think it
all too easy, Sakuya?

target.text: And that. That very thought. Was Sakuya's. And Kuro's.
───Hubris───
───This is too easy─── Did that thought never strike you, O Sakuya?

source.japanese:
島が進化の系統樹になぞらえられている事を考察したくらいで、天地の精髄ばかりか、これまで自分達を軽んじていた仲間の信頼までも得られるなどと、それは都合の良い考えだと、疑いもしなかったのか？
　確かに世の中には幸運に恵まれた人間というのはある。けれど朔屋よ、クロよ、お前達は光の帯を腰に巻きもせず、銀の匙[スプーン]だってくわえて産まれてこなかった。
source.english:
Merely recognizing the island's arrangement as an evolutionary tree, and obtaining not only the essence of heaven and earth but the trust of those who had despised you—didn't you suspect how convenient that was? Certainly some people are blessed with luck.
But Sakuya, Kuro, neither of you wore a girdle of light or was born with a silver spoon in your mouth.

source.japanese:
だから朔屋、そしてクロ。
　二人は、これより知る事になる。
　自分達が手に入れようとしていた物、希求していた物が砕けていく音を、聴く事になる。

　まず手始めは。
source.english:
And so,
Sakuya and Kuro would learn.
They would hear the things they had tried to obtain, the things they longed for, shatter.
To begin with…

target.text: Simply by considering the idea that the island was modelled after the phylogenetic tree, not only did you obtain the soul of the Universe, you even earned the trust of your comrades, they who had looked down on you hitherto; did you never suspect that to be an awfully convenient notion? Certainly, there are men in this world of ours who are blessed with great fortune. But, O Sakuya, O Kuro, you were not born with a sash of radiance tied around your waists, nor with a silver spoon in your mouths.

Therefore, Sakuya, and Kuro. Henceforth, you will come to know. You will come to hear the sound of that which you had tried to obtain, that which you desired so fervently, shattering to pieces. To start with.

source.japanese:
皆が、財宝の発見に酔いしれていたその瞬間。
　建物の窓が破砕された。
　外から。
　撒き散らされる破片の中から、黒い粘塊が流入する。
　室内に雪崩れこんできた、その粘塊じみたものはなんぞ。
source.english:
At the very instant everyone was intoxicated by the treasure's discovery,
a window broke.
From outside.
Amid the scattered fragments flowed a black, sticky mass.
What was this thing, this mass tumbling into the room?

target.text: The very instant they had all grown intoxicated with the discovery of this fortune. One of the building's windows was shattered. From the outside. From amidst the scattered debris, a black, viscous mass flowed in. Whatever could this slimy mass that crashed into the room like an avalanche be?

source.japanese:
始め朔屋は、広間の窓に背を向けて、外に通じる扉からの外光にザウエルを透かし見ていたから、硝子が割れる音を聞いても、はしゃぎすぎた誰かが物の弾みで拳なり持ち物なりをぶつけたのだろう、程度にしか考えていなかった。
　すぐに水夫長辺りの叱り飛ばす声が響いて、少しばかり落ち着きを取り戻して、それでもザウエルを根こそぎかき集めるまで、騒ぎは続くのだろうと、さして気にも留めていなかったのだ。
source.english:
Sakuya had his back to the hall's windows, holding the Zauer against the daylight from the open door. On hearing glass break, he assumed someone had got overexcited and accidentally struck a window with a fist or some object.
The boatswain would shout, things would settle a little, and the commotion would nevertheless continue until every Zauer was gathered. He paid it no particular attention.

target.text: At first, Sakuya was facing away from the window in the hall, looking through the Sauer at the natural light pouring in from the door leading outside, so though he heard the sound of glass breaking, he assumed it was probably nothing more than somebody getting a little too heated in the excitement of it all and smashing it with their fists or a personal effect. Immediately after, a fiercely scolding voice rang out, probably from the Bosun, and while he regained a bit of his calm, the commotion would surely continue until they had gathered up every last Sauer, so he still didn't pay it much heed.

source.japanese:
けれど、朔屋とクロがその背に聞いたのは、人間の沈黙と、人間以外のなにかが立てる、粘く湿った、そして大きな何かを引きずるような音。
　粘ついて湿って、大きななにかと問われても、粘ついて湿った何か大きい物だろうとしか鸚鵡返しの答えしかできない朔屋は、だから背後で何事か生じているのか判別しかねて振り返ったのだが。
source.english:
But what he and Kuro heard behind them was human silence, and a sound made by something other than human: sticky, wet, as though dragging something large.
Asked what was sticky, wet and large, Sakuya could only parrot back that it must be some large, wet, sticky thing. Unable to judge what was happening, he turned.

target.text: However, what Sakuya and Kuro heard behind their backs was human silence, as well as a sound made by something non-human: damp and sticky, and like something large being dragged around. Should he be asked what was large, damp, and sticky, all Sakuya could do was parrot the question back, answering "something large, damp, and sticky", so finding it difficult to discern just what was going on behind his back, when he then turned around.

source.japanese:
朔屋もクロも、振り返ったところで何が何だかとんと判じかねた。広間の奥の窓が確かに壊れている。けれど誰かが弾みで壊したと言うにはあまりに派手な、外から解体工事の鉄球でも叩きつけられたという破壊の跡。それはどうやら鉄球などではなく、広間の中央に溜まっている粘つく塊によるらしい。
　青黒い、瀝青の塊のような何か。ひどい悪臭を伴っており、ヘドロの腐ったような臭気が広間一面に広がっていく。
source.english:
Turning gave neither of them any understanding. The far window was certainly broken. But far too spectacularly for an accidental blow: it looked as though a demolition ball had struck from outside. Apparently the cause was not a ball, but the sticky mass pooled in the hall's center.
Something blue-black, like a lump of tar. It stank. A smell like rotten sludge spread throughout the room.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（あれ……この臭い、どっかで……？）
source.english: (That… haven't I smelled that somewhere…?)

source.japanese:
臭いというのは映像的記憶より、印象、感興といった直感的な記憶に結びつきやすいものだが、この時朔屋が臭気に思い出しかけたのは、嘔吐しそうなクロという、悪臭に対して余りに当然の反応であり、どうにもあてにならない。
　いずれにせよこの粘塊がどういう成分に由来するのか、かつまた、無人であるはずの（いたとしてもせいぜい老人ひとりの）島において、どのような作用がその粘塊を、よりにもよって皆が歓喜の最中にあるところに投げつけてきたのか。
source.english:
Smell tends to connect with intuitive memories—impressions, feelings—rather than pictures. What this stench nearly brought back to Sakuya was Kuro on the verge of vomiting.
Such a natural response to a foul smell was scarcely useful. Whatever the substance of this mass, what force had thrown it at them, precisely in the midst of their rejoicing, on an island supposedly empty save, at most, for one old man?

source.japanese: 朔屋だけでなく、航海士も水夫長も、下級水夫達もみな同じ思いだったと見えて、床に延びた粘塊を呆然と凝視の、それぞれに虚を衝かれた姿勢のまま。幸い、それの下敷きになった者はいないようだが……。
source.english: The navigators, the boatswain and the junior sailors appeared to wonder the same. All stared blankly at the mass spread upon the floor, frozen in the poses in which it had caught them unawares. Fortunately, nobody seemed to have been crushed beneath it…

target.text: Having turned around, both Sakuya and Kuro still struggled with making heads or tails of the situation. The window deeper inside the hall had been broken, that much was certain. However, the destruction was far too spectacular to be attributed to someone simply breaking it on a whim; it looked more as if a wrecking ball had been slammed into it from the outside. But then it seemed not to have been caused by an iron ball, but rather that sticky mass pooling in the center of the hall. It was like a bluish-black lump of tar. It was accompanied by a terrible stench, and a stink akin to putrid sludge was rapidly spreading through the entire hall.
【Naomasa】 （Wait……this stench, where have I……?）

Smells are more easily associated with intuitive memories such as impressions or something that aroused interest than visual memories, but what the smell dredged out from Sakuya's mind in this moment was the image of Kuro on the verge of vomiting, an entirely natural reaction to a foul stench, so that couldn't be counted upon at all. At any rate, what manner of components was this viscous mass derived from, and moreover, on an island that was supposedly deserted (or at most inhabited by a single old man), what manner of action was responsible for throwing this lump of slime here, and of all the times, right while everyone was in the midst of jubilation?

It wasn't just Sakuya, for the first mates, the Bosun, and all the deck boys also seemed to share his thoughts, staring blankly at the sticky lump spread out across the floor, each remaining in their respective stances of being caught off guard. Fortunately, it seemed no one had been flattened beneath it, but…….

source.japanese:
航海士の双子が閃いたのは、何者かが自分達の財宝獲得を阻止せんと妨害を図ってきた、という現実的な発想だったようで、シサムが銃帯から回転弾倉式抜き放ち、油断なき構えで窓の孔へと索敵に寄っていく。
　床のねばねばについては、こちらも用心に拳銃構えて、キサラが様子を見るという、二方面警戒を怠らない。双子故に実に堂に入って息の合った連携だったが、これが結果的には一同の犠牲者を最低限に留める事に繋がった。
source.english:
The twins' practical thought seemed to be that someone was trying to obstruct their acquisition of the treasure. Sisam drew her revolver from her gun belt and cautiously moved toward the broken window to look for an enemy.
Kisara covered the sticky thing on the floor with her own pistol. They neglected neither direction. Natural, perfectly coordinated teamwork for twins—and, in the end, it would keep the company's losses to a minimum.

target.text: The first thing that flashed through the minds of the twin first mates was that someone was trying to sabotage their efforts to obtain the treasure, or at least they seemed to be taking that sort of realistic approach to the situation, for Shisamu pulled her revolver free from her gun belt, and maintaining an alert stance, she approached the broken window to scout for enemies.

In regards to the sticky thing on the floor, here Kisara also adopted a cautious stance with revolver in hand, keeping an eye on it, ensuring vigilance in both directions. Being twins, their teamwork truly was remarkably polished and perfectly coordinated, and this ultimately lead to keeping casualties among all present to a minimum.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「え……ちょ、なに？　あれ？」
source.english: “Huh… Wait. What? What's that?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Eh……wai-, what? Huh?」

source.japanese:
念のためにと、拳銃を擬[ぎ]したシサムがまずその粘塊の中になにかの形があるのを認めた。煮凝りの中に小魚の身が寄せられているような塩梅だが、シサムがその形をより詳細に見分けようと注意を集中させた刹那───
　粘塊が、弾けるように解けた。くるくると捩[よじ]った輪ゴムが解けるような挙動でぶるるんと広がった時も、一行は始めの『粘塊』の印象が強く、無生物的な動きとしか思えなかったのだ。
source.english:
Sisam, pistol aimed as a precaution, first recognized a shape within the mass. Like the flesh of a little fish set in aspic. The instant she focused to make it out more clearly, the mass sprang apart.
It spread with a quivering motion like a twisted rubber band unwinding. The first impression of a ‘mass’ was so strong that they still took the movement for something inanimate.

source.japanese: 解けて、長く伸びて、一方の端をもたげた時になってようやく、一行はそれが生き物だと気づいた。
source.english: Only when it uncoiled, stretched long and raised one end did they realize it was alive.

source.japanese: だがそれでも、一行はそんな生き物となど、見た事も聞いた事もなかったのだ。
source.english: Yet none had ever seen or heard of such a creature.

target.text: Pressing her gun against it just in case, Shisamu noticed there was some kind of shape inside the lump of slime. It looked as though the meat of small fish had been collected within a jelly-like broth, but the instant Shisamu focused her attention in an effort to make out that shape in finer detail─── The sticky substance dissolved as though it had burst open. Even when it spread out in a wobbly motion like a twisted rubber band unravelling, the initial impression the group had of it as a viscous lump remained strong, and they could still only think of it as an inorganic movement.
When it unravelled, stretched out long, and one end of it reared up from the ground, at long last the group realized that it was a living creature.
But even so, the group had neither seen nor heard of anything like such a creature ever before.

source.japanese:
それは巨大な海蛇とも何ともつかぬ怪生物。否、形こそ海蛇に似通うものの、おそらくは原始的な円口類の一種だったろう。
　体長はおよそ五～六米、頭が鋭三角形、その形状は鈍い鏃[やじり]のよう。三角形の頂点に相当する部分はほとんど円錐形で、わずかに吸盤状の襞[ひだ]が覗いている。青黒い全身は粘液に滑[ぬめ]光り───
　だが一行を恐怖に包んだのは、そのおぞましい外見よりも、そいつが放射する気配だった。
source.english:
A monstrous thing like a giant sea serpent—or something else. No, though its shape resembled a sea snake's, it was probably a kind of primitive cyclostome.
Some five or six meters long, with a sharply triangular head like a blunt arrowhead. The triangle's tip was almost conical, showing a faint sucker-like fold. Slime gleamed over its blue-black body.
Yet what wrapped the company in terror was less its hideous appearance than the presence it radiated.

source.japanese:
己以外の生きて動く物は、それにとっては全て餌食。食欲の権化、というより食欲の欠如を感じさせる。欲というのなら充たされる事もあろうが、始めから欠如しているのなら永久に足るをしらない。あるのはただ喰らい尽くせとの本能。
　いたって単純な原理に則った生き物であり、その余りに単純であるが故に、純粋であるだけに恐ろしい。
source.english:
Everything living and moving besides itself was prey. Rather than an incarnation of appetite, it suggested an absence of appetite. A desire might be satisfied; an absence from the beginning could never know enough. Only the instinct to devour everything.
A creature following an exceedingly simple principle. Terrifying precisely because that principle was so simple, so pure.

source.japanese:
全身を収縮させるように動き出したそれ、大海蛇は、明確な意志でもって、巨体でありながら俊敏な速度で信天翁号の船員達に襲いかかっていった。
　それまで一行にとっては歓喜の泉だった、宝珠の広間がたちまちのうちに地獄の溜め池と化す。
　巨体をうねらせ、下級水夫の一人に向かっていく。標的となった下級水夫は、それこそ蛇に狙われた蛙の如く呆然と佇んでいた、ところへ水夫長からの蛮声。
source.english:
The great sea serpent began moving as though contracting its whole body, then attacked the Albatross crew with clear intent and speed astonishing for its size.
The jewel-filled hall, their wellspring of joy, became a pool of hell.
Its enormous body undulated toward one junior sailor, who stood stunned like a frog marked by a snake. Then the boatswain bellowed.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「何を固まってんだっ。逃げろ、いいから逃げろ、みんなこの腐れ広間から、さっさと逃げろいっ!!」
source.english: “What are you freezing for? Run! Just run! Everyone get out of this rotten hall, now!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもみんな、ザウエルは……っ？」
source.english: “But the Zauer…!”

target.text: It was a monstrous creature, defying classification as either a giant sea serpent or any other known beast. Nay, while its shape in particular resembled a sea snake, it was likely a kind of primeval species of cyclostome. The length of its body spanned about five to six metres, its head was an acute triangle, and its form resembled a blunt arrowhead. The parts corresponding to the vertexes of that triangle were almost conical in shape, offering a small glimpse at the suction cup-like folds within. The entirety of its bluish-black body was slick and shiny with sticky mucus─── But what had enveloped the entire group in terror was not its repulsive appearance, but the aura it emitted.

All living, moving creatures but itself were prey to this creature. It was an embodiment of appetite, or rather, it gave the impression of an absence of appetite. For had this thing a desire, then surely that could be sated, but if it lacked said desire in the first place, then it would never know contentment. An instinct to devour all was all that was. It was a creature that operated on an exceedingly simply principle, but it was the excessive simplicity of it, that sheer purity of it, that made it so terrifying.

That thing, the giant sea serpent, began moving as though its entire body was contracting, and with clear intent, it pounced on the crew of the Albatross with a nimble speed that belied its massive body. This hall of jewels, which had been a wellspring of joy for the whole group hitherto, transformed into a pond from the depths of hell in the blink of an eye.

Giant body slithering, it bore down on one of the deck boys. The targeted deck boy was rooted to the spot in a daze, exactly like the proverbial frog stared down by a snake; just then, a gruff yell came his way from the Bosun. (TN: This refers to the Japanese idiom "蛇に睨まれた蛙", which literally means a frog watched by a snake. It means being so overwhelmed by fear before a powerful foe that you freeze up, unable to move.)
【Bosun】 「What are you freezing up for!? RUN AWAY, JUST RUN AWAY, EVERYBODY, GET THE HELL OUT OF THIS DAMN HALL RIGHT NOW!!」
【Naomasa】 「But, guys, the Sauers……?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「バカッ、悔しいけど、鼻血出るほどだけど、今はそんなのに構ってないで逃げろおっ」
source.english: “Idiot! I hate leaving it—hate it enough to give me a nosebleed—but forget that and run!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Moron, it sucks, it's so frustrating that I'm almost bleeding out my nose, but stop worrying about that right now and RUUUN!」

source.japanese: 阿鼻叫喚劇、しかして無言劇。恐怖と狂騒が皆の聴覚を奪った。皆してとにかく広間から逃れなければと、殺到していくが外への扉へ、そこで詰まる事態は避けられて、木造の街路へ飛び出しては逃れでていく船員達。
source.english: A drama of screams and anguish, yet a silent one. Terror and frenzy robbed them of hearing. They all rushed toward the door, intent only upon escaping the hall. A crush there was averted; sailors burst into the wooden street and fled.

target.text: First it was pandemonium, now it was pantomime. Fear and frenzy robbed them all of their hearing. All as one felt they had to escape this hall at all costs, and so they rushed for the door leading outside; they managed to avoid forming a blockade there, and the sailors leapt out into the wooden streets to escape.

source.japanese:
と、幸運はそこまで、板敷きの通りに出た途端、下級水夫の一人が雨に濡れた木板に足滑らせて転倒───そこへ、ザウエルの広間より抜け出してきた大海蛇が迫る。
　魁偉な頭をのたくらせ、全身を大きく波うたせ、空気を嗅ぎ回るような挙動は芋虫や子蛇がやるなら可愛げも見えたかも知れないが、五米級の長物がやると凄まじく不気味な迫力が宿る。
source.english:
Their luck ended there. No sooner was he outside than a junior sailor slipped on the rain-wet boards and fell. The giant sea serpent emerged from the Zauer hall and approached.
It swung its grotesque head and rippled its whole body, seeming to sniff the air. A caterpillar or little snake doing that might have looked cute. A five-meter creature made it tremendously sinister.

source.japanese:
ただ迫り来る異形の迫力に転倒したまま竦んでいた少年水夫へ、巨体を利して雪崩かかって囓りついた、わけではなかった。
　彼の前で鎌首をもたげ、どこかご機嫌を窺うようにそろそろと下ろして吻[ふん]の先を触れさせただけ、鼻先を押しつけただけ、と見えたのに。
source.english:
It did not descend bodily and bite the junior sailor, who lay frozen before the approaching monstrosity. It raised its head in front of him,
then lowered it cautiously, almost solicitously. Merely touched him with its snout. Merely pressed its nose against him, it seemed.

target.text: But that was when their luck ran out, for the moment they stepped out onto the boarded street, one of the deck boys slipped on a wooden board slick with rain and fell down───and the great sea serpent, which had slipped out from the hall of the Sauers, was closing in on him. Gigantic head swaying, entire body undulating in great waves: its behaviours like sniffing around the air might have looked adorable had it been a caterpillar or a snakeling, but when a long object measuring at least five metres did it, it took on a tremendously uncanny intensity.

Though the young sailor, faced with the monstrous presence of the grotesque shape looming over him, simply lay rooted to the spot where he fell, exploiting its enormous body to fall upon him like an avalanche and sink its teeth into him was not what the creature did. It reared up its head before him, and then, as if testing the waters, slowly lowered itself and merely touched him with its proboscis, just pressed the tip of its nose against him, or so it looked.

source.japanese:
瞬間。下級水夫は海老ぞりに、背骨が折れるのではと言う恐ろしい勢いと角度で。指先まで逆に反り反っているのに、悲鳴の一つもない、のは、口を限界まで開けて硬直しているからだった。
　び、びんっ、と短く詰まった痙攣で、どんと倒れて動かなくなった。
source.english:
In an instant, his back arched with a violence and at an angle that threatened to break his spine. Even his fingertips bent backward. No scream: his mouth was fixed open to its limit.
A brief, tight convulsion. Then he fell heavily and stopped moving.

target.text: In an instant. The deck boy arched his body backwards like a shrimp with such a terrifying force and angle that it seemed his spine would snap. Even his fingertips curled back and forth, and yet there was not a single scream, for his mouth was stretched open as wide as it could go and locked in place. With a few short, tight convulsions, he collapsed with a thump and ceased to move.

source.japanese: 下級水夫が顔面を打ちつけた鈍い衝撃音で、音が戻ってくる。
source.english: The dull impact of the junior sailor's face striking the boards brought sound back.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なんだ!?　ありゃあ、電気喰らった時みてえな……野郎っ！　ありゃあ電気鰻かっ!?」
source.english: “What!? That looked like he'd been shocked… Bastard! Is it an electric eel!?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「こいつはまさか、ロックフォールの言ってた……？」
source.english: “Could this be what Roquefort was talking about…?”

target.text: And with the dull impact of the deck boy's face hitting the floor, sound returned.
【Bosun】 「WHAT!? That was like someone getting shocked by electricity ……son of a bitch! Is that thing an electric eel!?」
【Bosun】 「Could it be, is this the creature Roquefort was talking about……?」

source.japanese: 巨大な海蛇は、倒れ伏した下級水夫の前で鎌首をもたげると、ああ見よやその異様な頭、逆三角形の頭部は、いかなる奇怪な筋肉と靱帯を骨格構造を有しているのか、鋭角の円錐状に収縮したのだ。
source.english: The giant sea serpent raised its head before the fallen junior sailor—oh, behold that bizarre head! By means of some unimaginable arrangement of muscle, ligament and bone, its inverted triangle contracted into a sharp cone.

source.japanese: 騎乗槍の切っ先の鋭さと、ゴム質の弾力を兼ね備えた頭の先で、撃ち斃した下級水夫の体表を嗅ぎ回り、彼が身に着けた水兵服に暫時戸惑っていた様子であったが、すぐさま嗅ぎ分ける魔性の感覚、半ズボンの裾[すそ]から細く尖らせた口吻の先を潜[もぐ]りこませて、小さな尻のあわいへと押し進めていく───
source.english: Its head combined the keen point of a lance with the give of rubber. It nosed over the junior sailor it had felled, seeming briefly perplexed by his uniform; then its demonic sense found what it sought. The slender point slipped beneath the hem of his shorts and pressed into the cleft of his small buttocks—

target.text: The enormous sea serpent reared its head before the collapsed deck boy; oh, behold that bizarre head, that inverted triangular head, what manner of weird muscles and ligaments must its skeletal structure possess, for it contracted into the shape of an acute cone.

With the tip of its head possessed of both the sharpness of the point of a lance as well as the elasticity of rubber, it sniffed around the surface of the body of the deck boy it had shocked into unconsciousness, and while it seemed a bit perplexed for a moment at the sailor uniform that he was wearing, its devilish senses let it promptly scent out the difference, and slipping the tip of its sharply tapering proboscis under the hem of his shorts, it pressed forwards towards the crack between his small buttocks───

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「だめえええっ、誰かぁ……！　誰かぁ！
　誰でもいいよ、あの子を助けて、
　優しくって、仲間想いの良い子なんだ」
source.english:
“Nooooo! Somebody…! Anybody!
Please, save him—he's kind,
he always looks after his shipmates!”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「この前みんなが食中毒で死にかけた時も、
　あの子はみんなの汚れ物の世話、
　全部してくれた───」
source.english:
“Even the other day, when everyone nearly died from food poisoning,
he took care of all our filthy things—
every last one—”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「食べられちゃうよう、
　なんだかすっごい卑猥なやり方で、
　あの子が食べられちゃうようっ」
source.english:
“He's being eaten,
in this incredibly obscene way—
he's being eaten!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「NOOOOOOO, SOMEBODYYY……! SOMEBODYYY! It doesn't matter who, just somebody save him! He's so kind, a good boy who cares deeply for his friends!」
【Deck boy】 「And the other day, when we were all just about to die from food poisoning, he's the one who took care of everybody's dirty clothes, he did all of it───」
【Deck boy】 「He's going to be eaten, and in some really obscene way, he's going to be eateeen!」

source.japanese: 大切な仲間の危機に何も出来ない非力に歯噛みしおろおろ救いを求める下級水夫の手を、優しく取って、力強く頷[うなず]いた頤[おとがい]がある。端正な手であったし、繊細な線の横顔だった。大海蛇を指差して、語り出すは。
source.english: The junior sailor gnashed his teeth, powerless to help a dear comrade and frantically seeking aid. Then a fine-boned hand gently took his, and a delicate profile gave him a firm nod. Its owner pointed toward the giant sea serpent and began to speak.

target.text: Gritting his teeth in frustration at his powerlessness to do anything to save his precious friend from danger, the deck boy tearfully begged for help; a vigorously nodding chin took his hand tenderly in its own. It was a shapely, graceful hand, and a profile drawn in delicate lines. It pointed at the great sea serpent, then began its narration.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あれは円口類、それも始原の一種でしょうね。あの類の生き物は、獲物の皮膚を擂[す]り鉢[ばち]状の歯で食い破り、あるいは体腔から頭部を侵入させて」
source.english: “That’s a cyclostome—probably a primitive species. Creatures of that type tear through their prey’s skin with mortar-shaped teeth, or they invade through the body cavity with their heads…”

source.japanese: いつの間にか、そう、いつの間にか、なのだ、この娘の登場というのは。いる時には、気がつくとそこにいる。この時も、黒髪のしなやかな姿が、逃げ出しかねて留まる一行の中にいつの間にか入り交じってあり、
source.english: Before anyone noticed—yes, that was always how this woman appeared. Whenever she was present, one became aware that she was simply there. So it was now: her slender, black-haired figure had slipped unnoticed among the company, who still lingered because they could not bring themselves to flee.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「That right there is a cyclostome, and likely a primeval species at that. Creatures belonging to this taxon either tear apart the skin of their prey using their mortar-like teeth, or else penetrate their prey's body by inserting their head through a body cavity.」

Just when had she, right, when exactly had this girl made her appearance? Whenever she was present, you would just happen to notice her already there. And this time was no exception; her slender, black-haired figure had somehow blended in with the group, which had found itself unable to escape and come to a halt, and all without anyone noticing it,

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「つまりは口とか肛門とか性器とか。体の穴から何らかの消化酵素でもって、体内の肉や内臓を溶解させて啜[すす]り取る───後に残るのは、骨と皮ばかり」
source.english: “In other words, the mouth, the anus, the genitals—through the body’s orifices, using some kind of digestive enzyme to dissolve the flesh and internal organs inside the body and slurp them up—leaving nothing but skin and bones behind.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「In other words, the mouth or the anus or the genitals and so on. And through these holes in the body, it uses some manner of digestive enzyme to liquefy the flesh and organs within the body, then slurps it all up───and all that's left is skin and bones.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ああ、つまりは。この島に残っていた、奇妙なくらいに綺麗に骨だけ残った死骸達、あれらは恐らくあの生き物に捕食されたのね」
source.english: “Ah, so that’s it. Those oddly pristine skeletal remains left on this island—they were probably preyed upon by that creature.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Aah, so that means. All those skeletons left on this island that consist of nothing but bones picked so clean it seems bizarre, they were, in all likelihood, preyed upon by this creature.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ってことはあの子、お尻から、中味、全部吸い取られて───ぅ、うぷっ！」
source.english: “Then he's having everything inside him sucked out through his rear—u-urp!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「So what you're saying is, this guy-, he'll have everything inside him sucked out from his butt───ulp!」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「うぶ、うえええええええ！」
source.english: “Urp, bleeeeeeeurgh!”

source.japanese:
密航者の大海蛇の生態を語る口ぶりは、乾いて散文的な言葉で構成されていたけれど、この場合誇張がないのはかえって空恐ろしい。
　伝えられた事実の無慈悲で容赦なく、また直接にその情景を目の当たりにしつつあるだけに水夫君達のおぞましさいかばかりなものか、堪えきれず吐き戻す者まで出たのも無理はあるまい。
source.english:
The stowaway described the giant sea serpent's habits in dry, prosaic terms, but here the very absence of exaggeration made them more terrifying.
The facts were merciless, and the sailors were watching them become reality before their eyes. Small wonder their horror overwhelmed them; some could bear no more and vomited.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Uhglh, bhleeeeegh!」

As the stowaway spoke of the ecology of this great sea serpent, it was in a manner composed of dry, prosaic words, but in this case, the lack of exaggeration only made it all the more terrifying. With the unsparing manner in which the ruthless reality was conveyed to them, as well as the fact that they were currently witnessing said reality with their very own eyes, how horrifying it must have been to the deck boys, and it was no wonder that some among them couldn't bear it and began to vomit.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……長々とようもまあ、有り難いご講釈、有り難すぎて涙が出るぜ、おう、お前なんでいる」
source.english: “…What a long and edifying lecture. I'm so grateful I could cry. Hey—what the hell are you doing here?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……A bit long-winded, but thank you kindly for the lecture. Why, I'm so grateful I've got tears in my eyes and-, hey, why are you here?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それに、ようもウチの水夫に上等な口叩いてくれたの、このメス餓鬼がぁ！」
source.english: “And on top of that, you had the nerve to mouth off to my crew, you bratty little bitch!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Besides, you've got a lot of nerve talking so high and mighty to my sailors, you bratty little bitch!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あれ？　私の言った事、どこかに間違いがあったとか……？」
source.english: “Huh? Was there a mistake somewhere in what I said…?”

source.japanese: 博物学の考査ならば問題なく点をもらえただろうが、憂えるべきはそこではない。それとも単純に積極的な被虐嗜好者という度し難い人種で、故意にやっている事を隠しているだけなのか、懸念に瞼[まぶた]に映した翳[かげ]りは青磁を思わせて薄蒼く、すこぶる付きの美を宿したが、美しい娘を女衒に叩き売りにする事だって平気の平左でやってのけそうなのが信天翁号の船員であり、水夫長もこの時朔屋へ唇の端を吊り上げながら、
source.english: Had this been an examination in natural history, she would have earned full marks. But that was not the point. Or was she simply one of those incorrigible creatures, an enthusiastic masochist concealing that she acted deliberately? The troubled shadow over her eyelids was pale blue as celadon and surpassingly beautiful. But the Albatross was crewed by men who could sell a beautiful woman to a procurer without turning a hair, and now the boatswain crooked one corner of his mouth at Sakuya—

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Huh? Was there a mistake in any of what I just said……?」

If this were a natural history test, then she would doubtless get points for her answer, but that was not what she ought to be worried about. Or perhaps she was simply a proactive masochist, an incorrigible sort of person, just trying to hide what she had deliberately done, for the shadow born of concern cast upon her eyelids was a pale green reminiscent of celadon porcelain, possessed of a beauty that could only be called extraordinary, but he was a member of the crew of the Albatross, who seemed like the sorts of people who would have no qualms about selling of a beautiful girl to a pimp at a bargain, and the Bosun also looked towards Sakuya at this moment, the corner of his mouth curling upwards,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……おう、朔屋。良いこと思いついたぜ。
　このメス餓鬼をな、こうやって」
source.english:
“…Hey, Sakuya. I’ve got a great idea.
Take this bratty little bitch, and do this to her…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Hey, Sakuya. I just though of a great idea. Watch, we take this cheeky brat, and then we do this!」

source.japanese: 言うやいなや、密航者の首根っ子と腰の革鞄をがっと掴み、軽々と、高々と頭上に持ち上げた水夫長の膂力、攻城弩の弦を引き絞る巻揚機の様に筋肉の束を浮き彫りにして、
source.english: No sooner had he spoken than the boatswain seized the stowaway by the scruff of her neck and by the leather bag at her waist, hoisting her effortlessly high above his head. Bundles of muscle stood out across him like the winch drawing back the string of a siege crossbow—

target.text: No sooner than the words left his mouth did the Bosun grab the stowaway tightly by the scruff of the neck and the leather bag around her hips, his herculean strength effortlessly lifting her high above his head, and like a winch drawing the bowstring of a ballista taut, his bundles of muscles bulging visibly,

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あ、痛い痛い痛い、
　首がお腹が締まって息が───
　なに？　私をなにする───あ───」
source.english:
“Ow, ow, ow,
my neck and stomach are being squeezed—I can’t breathe—
What? What are you doing to me—ah—”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Ah, ow ow ow, you're squeezing my neck and my stomach and I can't breathe─── What? What are you doing to me───ah───」

source.japanese: 水夫長にぶん投げられ、大海蛇に着弾する密航者。滑る肌の上で電撃の迸[ほとばし]り、弾き飛ばされたものの、何故だか平気だった。むしろぴんぴんとしていた。派手な悲鳴で粘液まみれ、なにかしら卑猥な眺めだった。
source.english: The stowaway was hurled by the boatswain and struck the giant sea serpent. A bolt of electricity surged across its slimy skin, knocking her back—yet for some reason, she was fine. In fact, she was as lively as ever. Covered in slime and letting out a loud scream, she presented a rather obscene sight.

target.text: Tossed violently by the Bosun, the stowaway hit the great sea serpent. Zapped by electric shocks atop its slippery skin, she was blasted away, and yet, for some reason, she was fine. If anything, she seemed full of vigour. Covered in slimy mucus and screaming loudly, she actually made for a lewd sight to behold, somehow.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ぬるぬるっ、ぬるぅっ、あああ服が髪が体中が、粘液で、悪臭放つ粘液で、ぬっるぬっるぅ……」
source.english: “Slippery, so slippery… Ahhh, my clothes, my hair, my whole body—it’s covered in slime, stinking slime… sooo slippery…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So slimy and sticky, aaah, my clothes, my hair, my whole body, all sticky with this foul-smelling slime, it's so slimyyy……」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……なんで生きとるんじゃあいつは。
　しかもあの海蛇、あれにゃ興味を示さんとくる。海蛇ですらあいつは好まんか」
source.english:
“…How the hell is that woman still alive?
And the sea snake doesn't even show any interest in her. Even a sea snake can't stand her?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……How is that girl still alive? And what's more, that sea snake shows no interest in her. So even sea snakes don't like her?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「水夫長、水夫長、今の投擲で、
　敵は一瞬怯んだようでありますが、
　しかし敵は極めて損耗軽微、
　戦友をどうか助けて下さいでありますっ」
source.english:
“Boatswain, Boatswain!
That throw seems to have made the enemy flinch for a moment,
but it has suffered almost no damage.
Please rescue our comrade!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Bosun, Bosun, that throw just now looks like it made the enemy flinch for a moment, but their losses are extremely insignificant, so please, save our comrade in arms!」

source.japanese: 密航者を投げつけられた衝撃で大海蛇は一度は下級水夫から身を引いたものの、黒髪の娘の方にはそれきり興味を失ったか、獲物と見なさず、中断された食事に戻ろうと、再び下級水夫へ這いずり寄っていた。
source.english: The impact of the stowaway had driven the giant sea serpent back from the junior sailor for a moment. It now seemed to have lost interest in the black-haired woman, however, or never to have regarded her as prey. It crawled toward the fallen sailor again, intent upon resuming its interrupted meal.

target.text: The impact of having the stowaway thrown at it did initially make the great sea serpent pull away from the deck boy, but it must have lost interest in the black-haired girl entirely, for having deemed her as not being prey, intending to resume its interrupted meal, it instead slithered towards the deck boy once more.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「つったってもおめえ、見ての通りのでかさに加え、電気まで撃ってきやがる」
source.english: “Easy to say. Look how damn big it is. And it shoots electricity too.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Easy enough for you to say, 'cause on top of being as big as it looks, this damn thing can even shoot out electricity.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「皮も分厚い上に、豪いぬるぬるしてるもんだから、こんなピストルじゃ弾も徹らない」
source.english: “Its hide's thick and slippery as hell. Bullets from a pistol like this won't get through.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「And not only is its skin thick, it's also extremely slippery, so with a pistol like mine, not even a bullet will be penetrating that.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ああいうのに、どこまで保つかわからないけど。……やるしかないか……？」
source.english: “Don't know how long it'll hold against something like that… But do we have a choice…?”

source.japanese:
双子がなにか意を決しかけたところで、近くの廃屋からふらりと出てきた人影、着馴らして形の崩れた着物に袴[はかま]の姿は、飄々とした気風さえ漂わせていたけれど。
　げふうと漏らしたおくびには品も慎みもあったものかで、おまけに熟柿を潰したようにぷんと臭った。したたかな酒を流しこんだ後に特有の。
source.english:
Just as the twins seemed about to resolve upon something, a figure sauntered from a nearby house. His kimono and hakama, worn shapeless, gave off an air of carefree detachment.
But the belch he released had neither refinement nor restraint. It stank like a crushed overripe persimmon: the unmistakable smell of strong liquor drunk in quantity.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「With that said, it's not like we know how much it can handle, so. ……Guess we have to give it a shot……?」

Right when the twins had made up their minds about something or other, a figure staggered out of a nearby building, dressed in a hakama and a well-worn kimono now rumpled from long use, exuding even an air of easygoing aloofness. There was certainly no elegance or modesty to be found in the burp he let out, and to make matters worse, it also reeked as if someone had smashed open a ripe persimmon. That distinctive smell that comes after downing a strong drink.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「騒がしいなあもう。
　てめえら、人が気持ちよう、
　酒喰らってりゃあ、ばたばたと」
source.english:
“What a goddamn racket.
Here I am enjoying a drink,
and you lot start running about…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あっ。近頃姿が見えず、酒もなくなっているかと思ったら、あんたかぁ！」
source.english: “Oh! So that's where you've been! I was wondering where all the booze had gone—you drank it!”

source.japanese:
大海蛇の恐怖とか下級水夫の悲劇とか、そういう深刻な事態へ、酔っぱらいが道端の雑草に小便をぶちまけるような、どうにも場にそぐわぬ詰問をここで浴びせる、朔屋も朔屋。
　それを無視して生欠伸で胸元をばりばり掻いていた智里だったが、皆がなにやらあまりにも進退窮まった感に包まれている、睨み据えている奴がいる、と大海蛇の方へ振り向いて、びくりと肩を震わせた。
　さしもの智里でさえも───
　　　　　　　　　　　　と思いきや。
source.english:
Sakuya was Sakuya: throwing so misplaced an accusation into the terror of the sea serpent and the junior sailor's tragedy, like a drunk pissing over roadside weeds.
Tomosato ignored him, half-yawned and scratched his chest vigorously. Then, noticing that everyone was hopelessly cornered and some were glaring at something, he turned toward the serpent. His shoulders jerked.
Even Tomosato…
Or so one might have thought.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Keep it down, will you? You lot, can't even have a good time knocking back some drink in peace without you making all this racket.」
【Naomasa】 「Oh. I hadn't seen you around lately, and I was thinking the booze had gone missing too. So that was all you!」

As though he'd completely forgotten about the grave state of affairs, like the horror of the great sea serpent or the tragic fate of the deck boy, by showering him with stern demands for an explanation for something entirely out place, like a drunkard pissing all over the weeds by the roadside, Sakuya was also being himself.

And ignoring that, Tomosato was vigorously scratching his chest while letting out a yawn, but sensing that everyone was enveloped in an air of utter desperation, and that there was even someone glaring intently at him, he turned towards the great sea serpent, and with a sudden start, his shoulders trembled. Even Tomosato, of all people─── Or so it seemed.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「アあん、なんだぁあのコウガイビルのでっかいなぁ……っぶ、ぶひゃひゃひゃひゃひゃ、
　あっはっはっは。おい見ろあの頭」
source.english:
“Aaah, what the hell is that? That giant hammerhead worm… b-buhahaha, ahahaha.
Hey, look at that head!”

source.japanese: また皆に振り向くなり、しゃがみこんで片膝ばんばん叩きながら、指さして大哄笑の、指さされるまでもないし、そもそも笑えるような段でもない、のに殺し屋の笑いは遠慮がなさ過ぎた。
source.english: He whirled back to the crew, crouched, and began slapping one knee while pointing and cackling. There was no need to point it out, and the moment was hardly funny, yet the hitman’s laughter was far too unrestrained.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Haaah, what's with this huge hammerhead worm-looking thing……pff, pfwahahahaha, ahahaha! Oi, look at its head!」

He turned back to the rest once more, squatted down, and while slapping one of his knees, pointed at it and roared with laughter; there was really no need to point, it wasn't even funny to begin with, and yet the killer's laughter was far too lacking in tact.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「へのこだへのこ、ちんぽこだ、魔羅だ。
　あっはっはっはっは、
　なにこの淫獣、腹いてぇ」
source.english:
“Penis, penis, dick, cock. Ahahaha,
what the hell is this lecherous beast?
My stomach hurts.”

source.japanese: 殺し屋の笑声は爽快とか痛快とかそういうものではなく、破壊的ですらあった。ただの馬鹿笑いだった。この男、場の空気をたたき壊す事に関しては、朔屋に並ぶものがある。
source.english: The hitman’s laughter wasn’t refreshing or exhilarating—it was downright destructive. Just a mindless cackle. When it came to shattering the atmosphere, this man was on par with Sakuya.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「It's a penis, a penis, that's a dick, a huge cock! Ahahahaha, what is with this lewd beast, ah, my stomach hurts!」

The killer's laughter wasn't anything invigorating or exhilarating; it was downright destructive. It was just guffawing. When it came to completely spoiling the mood, this man stood shoulder to shoulder with Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「……あーあ。
　誰もが思ってたけど口には出してなかったこと、言っちゃったよあの人」
source.english:
“…Oh, man.
He went and said what everyone was thinking but nobody would say out loud.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「……Aaaww. He really went and did it, he actually said what we were all thinking but never said out loud.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「馬鹿やめろおい、せっかく腹に入れた酒が、
　全部逆流するだろうがあっはっはっは」
source.english:
“Cut the crap, man!
All that booze I just drank is gonna come right back up, ha ha ha ha!”

source.japanese: さらには、下級水夫をも辟易とさせる言動のみならずこの男、自身が物理的な破壊力まで縦横に駆使するので手に負えない、立ち上がったその時には、例によって例の如く、現れた時には居合わせた全員が様々な角度で無手である事を見ていたはずなのに、あの定寸を越えて長い刀をいつの間にか手にしていた。
source.english: Nor was his manner, which disgusted even the junior sailors, the only problem. He wielded physical destruction freely too. When he stood, the usual thing had happened: everyone must have seen his empty hands from various angles upon his arrival, yet now he held that sword of unusual length.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Oi, stop that, you idiots, all that perfectly good booze I just drank is gonna come right back upfhahaha!」

Furthermore, not only did this man's behavior make even the deck boys fed up, he even freely made use of physically destructive force whenever it so pleased him, so he was entirely unmanageable; the moment he stood back up, as ever was his habit, despite how everyone present must have seen from all manner of angles that he was empty-handed when he appeared, before anyone knew it, he nevertheless held that long blade exceeding the regular length of a katana in his hands.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……ンの野郎。
　たたっ斬っちゃる」
source.english:
“…Bastard.
I'll cut you down.”

source.japanese:
眼差しを七分眼にすれば眸[ひとみ]の蒼の揺らぎが凝縮されて、すぅ、と動き出せば燐光の軌跡さえ置き残す、智里は、大海蛇へと歩を進めている。
　居合わせた者全員の、意識の虚ろを衝いた動きの起こりで、あ、と気づいた時には、無造作としか言い様のない足取りで大海蛇の眼前に、その知覚でさえ、蒼い眼の男が動き出したと思った次の瞬間には目前にあったようにしか感じられなかったろう。
source.english:
His eyes narrowed; the wavering blue condensed, seeming to leave a phosphorescent trail as he moved. Tomosato advanced upon the serpent.
The beginning of his movement slipped through a blind spot in everyone's awareness. By the time they noticed, he was already before it, his steps utterly casual. Even to the serpent, it could only have seemed that the blue-eyed man began moving in one instant and stood before it in the next.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……You big bastard. I'm cutting you down.」

When he narrowed his gaze to seven-tenths its usual size, the shimmering of his azure eyes condensed; when he began to move with a hiss, it even left behind a phosphorescent trail, and Tomosato stepped towards the great sea serpent.

With a movement that began at the exact moment the attention of all present lapsed, by the time a gasp of realization could escape anyone's lips, with a stride that could only be described as utterly effortless, he already stood right before the great sea serpent's eyes, and even with its mighty senses, just as it seemed the blue-eyed man was about to move, in the next instant, it must have felt as if he was already right under its nose.

source.japanese:
剣尖が描く円弧は大きく滑らかで、けれど誰にも智里がいかなる剣の入りで斬撃を放ったのか見えたものはおらず、見たのは智里が振り抜いた刀を脇に、自然にこちらへ戻ってくる姿と、大海蛇の頭部の根元辺りに深々と刻まれた斬撃の線ばかり。なにやら去勢されたかの。
　智里の剣は人間のみならず、劫初の恐怖を、その身に纏[まと]う電撃ごと斬り伏せる、ように見えて。
source.english:
The sword tip described a great, smooth arc. Yet nobody saw how Tomosato entered the cut. All they saw was him returning naturally, his swung blade at his side, and a slash deeply scored near the base of the serpent's head. As though it had been castrated.
His sword seemed able to fell not merely humans but a terror from the dawn of time, electricity and all.

source.japanese: 大海蛇に浮いた斬撃の線はあっさりと薄れて消えた。
source.english: The cut upon the great sea serpent simply faded and disappeared.

target.text: The arc traced by the point of his sword was grand and smooth, but none could perceive from what angle Tomosato had initiated the slash; all they saw was Tomosato, the sword he had swung through now held by his side, returning to them in a natural manner, as well as lines of slashes etched deeply into the base of the great sea serpent's head. It sort of looked like it had been castrated. Not only did Tomosato's sword slay men, it even cut down a horror of ancient aeons together with the very lightning enveloping its body, or so it seemed.
The slashing marks carved into the great sea serpent quickly faded, then vanished.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あ、あれ？
　今、斬れてたよね、間違いなく」
source.english:
“H-huh?
It was cut just now. Definitely.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Wh-, huh? It was cut just now, right, no mistaking that.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おうとも。剣閃、しっかり抜けてたぜ、
　だが……」
source.english:
“Damn right. The blade went clean through.
But…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Sure was. The flash of his sword went straight through it, but……」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「───なにあの人。斬れ味よすぎて、斬れたのにまたくっついてるじゃない。
　凄すぎて逆に駄目の好例だ」
source.english:
“What is that man? That cut was too clean—the sides joined back up after he'd cut them apart.
A perfect example of being so good it's bad.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「───What is wrong with that guy? His blade is so sharp that even though he cut through it, it just stuck right back together again. A perfect example of how you can be so amazing at something you actually become useless.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だが、今のでちっとは怯んだようだ。
　───今だ、あの水夫、
　拾って逃げるぞ！」
source.english:
“Still, that made it flinch a bit.
Now!
Grab the sailor and run!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「But, it looks like that made it falter a bit. ───Now's our chance, pick up that sailor and then get out of here!」

source.japanese:
たとえばそこが海の上ならば。あの道化た悪魔が真剣に造りだしたかのおン襤褸船信天翁号にあるならば。どのような死地を迎えようともせせら笑って切り抜けて、あるいはついにその褒められた物ではない人生の最期を迎えようとも、死神に唾吐きかけて、冥界の河の渡し賃さえ、酒に替えて海にぶちまけてくれと願う無頼の徒であっても。
　陸の上では本来の剛胆も半減すると見えて、逃げるわ逃げるわ、木造の通り、雨に濡れた板敷きに足を取られ、泡を食って這いずって、逃げる。海の無法者共と言うより、戦国の世の塗炭に苦しんだ百姓の逃散めく。
source.english:
At sea—aboard that accursed wreck, the Albatross, which looked as if a clownish devil had earnestly designed it—these outlaws would have sneered their way through any deadly predicament. Even at the end of their less-than-admirable lives, they would spit at Death and ask that their fare across the underworld's river be exchanged for booze and poured into the sea.
On land, their native boldness seemed halved. Run, run, run. They slipped on the rain-wet boards, panicked, crawled and fled. Less seaborne outlaws than peasants fleeing the miseries of the Warring States age.

target.text: Assume that they were out to sea. That they were on that run-down ship that only a jesting devil could earnestly have dreamt up, the Albatross. Then no matter the life-and-death situation, they would cut their way through it with a sneering smirk on their faces, or even should they finally be about to face the end of their not-so-praiseworthy lives, they would spit on the Grim Reaper, and even wish to exchange their fare to cross the river Styx for booze before dumping it all into the ocean. Even a gang of outlaws like them.

On land, it seemed as if their inherent dauntlessness had been cut in half: run away, run away, slipping on the floorboards of the wooden streets slick with rain, losing their heads while crawling along the ground, run away. Rather than outlaws of the sea, they resembled peasants fleeing the wretched miseries of the Warring States period.

source.japanese:
背後に迫るは、信天翁号の船員達の誰も聴いた事がないような───いや、機関長は知っていたか、ともかくも造化の神のいかなる悪意か、この時代まで生き残っていた太古の捕食者。
　一行の前に姿を現した時は、まだ寝惚け眼だったと言わんばかりに速度を増して追随する、下級水夫の中に絶望の細波波及する、水夫長や航海士でさえある種の覚悟を決めて振り返れば、どういう気まぐれか、大海蛇、通りの向こうで動き止んで、鎌首をもたげて周囲の空気に何事か聞き入っているような。
source.english:
Behind them came a predator from antiquity, preserved into this era by some malice of the god of creation. None of the Albatross crew had heard of its like—no, the chief engineer knew it, come to think of it.
As if it had still been sleepy on first appearing, it now gained speed in pursuit. Ripples of despair spread among the junior sailors. Even Long and the navigators turned, prepared for something final. But through some whim, the serpent had stopped down the street, head raised as though listening to the air.

target.text: Looming nearer from behind was something not a soul from the crew of the Albatross had ever heard of─── no, perhaps the Chief Engineer knew of it, but regardless, by what malice of the god of creation had this ancient predator survived into this age?

When it appeared before the group, as if all but saying that it was still half-asleep, it increased its speed and began gaining on them; ripples of despair spread amongst the deck boys, and when the Bosun and even the first mates turned around with some sort of grim resolve in their hearts, by way of what must have been some inexplicable whim, the great sea serpent had come to a halt down the street, rearing its head as though listening intently to something in the surrounding air.

source.japanese:
なんにせよ好機には違いなし、と、再び駆け出す皆だったが、誰もが気づいていた。
　自分達は、信天翁号が停泊する桟橋とは真逆の方向に走っている、と。
source.english:
Whatever the reason, it was an opportunity. They ran again. Yet everyone knew:
they were running in precisely the opposite direction from the pier where the Albatross lay.

target.text: At any rate, this was undoubtedly a golden opportunity, and so they all broke into a run once more, but everyone realized it. That they were running in the exact opposite direction of the jetty where the Albatross was anchored.

source.japanese:
やがて誰かが一つの建物を指差す、と船の上では珍しいくらいの一つ流れになってその扉に殺到していく。蹴り開けて、屋内の骨や有り合わせの防御壁を扉の内に築くが、あの劫初の恐怖相手ではどれほど保つものやら。
　この廃址ではどれも建物は似たり寄ったり、大海蛇への砦となるような堅固な建物はないだろうに、ここへ皆が逃げこんだのは、階を三階と重ね、周囲に比べて見晴らしが利いたからである。
source.english:
At last someone pointed to a building. With a unity rare aboard, they rushed its door, kicked it open and built a barricade inside from bones and whatever came to hand. How long that would hold against a terror from time's beginning was another matter.
Buildings here were much alike. None could serve as a strong fortress against the serpent. They had chosen this one because its three stories offered a better view than its neighbors.

target.text: Eventually, someone pointed at a building, and in a single stream of the sort so unified that it made a rare sight aboard a ship, they rushed towards the door. They kicked the door open, then constructed a defensive barrier by the inwards-facing side of the door using the bones they found inside and anything else they had on hand, but how long could that truly withstand that primeval horror?

Each and every building in this ruin was pretty much alike, and it seemed unlikely any would be sturdy enough to serve as a fortress against the great sea serpent, but the reason they had all taken refuge within this one was because it had three floors, and so compared to its surroundings, it offered a better outlook.

source.japanese: 我先にと最上階に駆け上がって、皆窓へと飛びついた。
source.english: Scrambling ahead of one another, they ran to the top floor and crowded the windows.

target.text: After scrambling to be first to the top floor, they all leapt at the window.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……どうだよ、朔屋」
source.english: “…Well, Sakuya?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……How's it looking, Sakuya?」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぁー……、桟橋までの路に、がっちり居座っちまってますわ……」
source.english: “Ahh… It's planted itself right on the way to the pier…”

source.japanese: 運良くあの折り畳み式の望遠鏡を船から持ち出していた朔屋に観察役が命じられ、青年は観ているだけでなにやら不快な気分になる怪物を、いやいや望遠鏡で眺めるうちに、明らかになった事実は、あまり楽しいものではなかった。
source.english: Fortunately, Sakuya had brought the folding telescope from the ship, and was assigned to observe. Reluctantly studying a monster whose mere appearance made him uncomfortable, he discovered something unpleasant.

source.japanese:
大海蛇は、廃址から桟橋を結ぶ、ただ一本の路に通ずる、木造の通りの合流点、ちょっとした広場様になっている地点にその長大な身体を留め、くねらせてあるという事。
　朔屋がそれを告げたところ。
source.english:
The serpent had settled its long, writhing body upon a little square where the wooden streets converged, leading to the single road between the ruins and the pier.
Sakuya reported it.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Aah……, it has firmly planted itself right on the path to the jetty……」

Sakuya, who had luckily decided to bring that folding telescope with him from the ship, was ordered to act as the lookout, and as the young man reluctantly gazed through the telescope at the monster, which for whatever reason made him feel ill at ease just looking at it, the truth that became apparent was not a particularly pleasant one.

The truth that the place leading to the one and only path connecting the ruins to the jetty, a junction of wooden streets that came together to form a small, plaza-like spot, was where the great sea serpent had chosen to rest its massive form, wriggling back and forth. When Sakuya told them as much.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「つったってお前、何も馬鹿正直に路を通んなくちゃいけねえって法はねえわな。なんだったら屋根伝いに行ったっていいし、やりようは幾らでもあんだろ……」
source.english: “Doesn't mean we have to be stupid enough to use the road. We could go over the roofs. Any number of ways…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You say that, but it's not like there's a law demanding we have to be honest to a fault and stick to the road like idiots. If need be, we could just go along the rooftops, there's gotta be plenty of ways to go about this……」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう殺し屋。もう一回たたっ切ってこい」
source.english: “Hey, assassin. Go cut it again.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hey, murderer. Go and cut that thing down one more time.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「やんだおら。おめえ、ああやって用心棒の先生よろしく出て行ってよ、しくじった時のあのみっともなさったらねェぞ」
source.english: “Not me. You go out playing the great hired swordsman like that, then fail? There's nothing more embarrassing.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「もう二度とやりたくね」
source.english: “Never doing that again.”

source.japanese: 斬れるか斬れないか、他人にどう思われたところでてんで構わぬ体の蒼眼居士、ただこっ恥ずかしかったのは本当のようで、吹かす煙管がせわしない。と、智里の視線がふいと流れた、先に。
source.english: The blue-eyed fellow acted as though he cared nothing whether he could cut it, or what anyone thought. His embarrassment nevertheless appeared genuine: he puffed his pipe busily. Then his gaze drifted aside.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Oh give me a break, man. I already ran out there playing the hotshot bodyguard once, and the shame of screwing that up was unbearable.」
【Tomosato】 「I never want to do that again.」

Could he cut it down or not; there was not a bone in the body of this blue-eyed koji that cared a whit for what others thought of his ability, however, from how restlessly he was puffing on his kiseru, he did seem to be genuinely embarrassed. Then, Tomosato's gaze suddenly shifted, and in the place it landed. (TN: A koji, written "居士", is a devout male lay Buddhist, but over time, it drifted from being strictly religious to more of a cultural archetype describing a refined gentleman of leisure or a hermit, the sort who is highly educated and uncaring of the opinions of broader society.)

source.japanese:
【声】
「無駄、だろうなあ」
source.english: “Wouldn't do any good.”

target.text: 【Voice】 「Wasted effort, I should think.」

source.japanese:
こちらからせせら笑う事はあっても、嘲笑される事には血でもって酬[むく]いる信天翁号の水夫長と航海士が、殺気を漲[みなぎ]らせて投げつけた視線の先、部屋の隅の丸椅子に座していたのは、あの老人だった。
　航海士二人にふざけた悪戯吹っかけ、下級水夫達を怯えさせ、そして、クロを錯乱するほどの恐怖に叩きこんだあの。
source.english:
The boatswain and navigators were quite willing to sneer at others, but answered ridicule with blood. Their murderous gazes fell upon the old man seated on a stool in the room's corner.
The one who had played outrageous tricks on the twins, frightened the junior sailors, and plunged Kuro into a terror bordering on madness.

source.japanese: けくっ、と朔屋が聞いた奇妙な音は、クロが喉を引き攣[つ]らせた音。クロは朔屋の背後にしゃがみこみ、頭を抱えてがたがたと震えていた。老人は朔屋とクロには気づいた風もなく進み出て、窓から大海蛇を望見して、ひとしきり肩を震わせていたのは、声も無く笑っていたのだった───
source.english: The peculiar ‘ghk’ Sakuya heard came from Kuro's throat contracting. She crouched behind him, clutching her head and shaking. The old man advanced as though he had not noticed them. He looked through the window at the serpent and shook his shoulders awhile. Laughing without a sound.

source.japanese:
【老人】
「ありゃあな、あんな卑猥な頭をしておるが、この島に最後まで生き残って、そしてこれからも生き残り続けるだろうの、最悪の捕食動物だよ……」
source.english: “For all that obscene head, it's the worst predator on this island. The last survivor, and likely to keep surviving…”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「ああいうなりをしとるが、その性、恐ろしく狡猾でなあ。あのあたりはほれ、この島の路の合流点であるし、雨が強く降れば水が溢れよる」
source.english: “It looks like that, but it's fearfully cunning. That spot, you see, is where the island's roads join. Heavy rain will make the water overflow.”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「すれば、電気も通りやすくなるし、あいつはそんな事をせんでも鋭敏な感覚の持ち主でな」
source.english: “Then electricity travels more easily. Not that it needs such help. Its senses are keen.”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「周囲三〇〇米くらいなら、生き物の生命電流を感じ取るよ。それで、どこまでも追いかけてきよるわ」
source.english: “It can detect the vital electrical currents of creatures within about three hundred meters. And follow them wherever they go.”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「一度狙われたら、まあ助からんな」
source.english: “Once it's marked you, there's little chance.”

target.text: Though they may laugh mockingly at others, the Bosun and first mates of the Albatross would be sure to repay any ridicule with blood, and in the place they cast their gazes dripping with a palpable thirst for blood, sitting on a stool in the corner of the room, was that old man. He who had played naughty tricks on the two first mates, scared the deck boys, and finally, struck such terror into the heart of Kuro that she was driven to derangement, that very one.

The strange choking sound that Sakuya heard was that of Kuro's throat constricting. Kuro had crouched down behind Sakuya, holding her head in her hands while she trembled. Without betraying any sign of having noticed Sakuya's or Kuro's presence, the old man stepped forwards, observing the great sea serpent from afar through the window; the reason his shoulders shook for a time was because he was laughing without making a sound───
【Old man】 「That thing there might have an absolutely indecent head, but it is the last surviving creature on this island, and one that'll likely live on longer yet: the most horrible of predators……」
【Old man】 「It might not look the part, but its nature is terrifyingly cunning. See, around that area is where the roads of this island meet, and when it rains heavily, it floods with water.」
【Old man】 「Once that happens, it also makes it easier for electricity to flow, but this thing is possessed of such keen senses that it does not even need to bother with that.」
【Old man】 「Within a radius of about three hundred metres or so, it can sense the bioelectric current of any living being. And so, it will stubbornly chase you down wherever you may go.」
【Old man】 「Once you're targeted, well, you're pretty much doomed.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「よく喋る爺だなあこいつあ！
　爺、やけにあの化け物に詳しいようじゃねえか。あんた、アレの飼い主かなんかか。
　だったらたたじゃおかねえ───」
source.english:
“Chatty old bastard, aren't you!
Know a hell of a lot about that monster. You its owner or something?
If you are, you're not getting away with…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「This old goat sure yaps a lot! Old man, you seem awfully well-informed about that monster, don't you? You its owner or something? If so, don't think we're letting you off the hook───」

source.japanese:
【老人】
「そうとも、いう。
　儂がこの島に、全ての生き物を持ちこんだんだからな。当然、あれもだ」
source.english:
“You could say
that. I brought every creature to this island. That one included, naturally.”

target.text: 【Old man】 「Why, I certainly am. For I am the one who brought all the living creatures to this island. Naturally, that thing included.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「爺ぃ……」
source.english: “Old bastard…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Old maaan……」

source.japanese:
【老人】
「爺ではない。儂の名は、ノアという」
source.english: “Not ‘old bastard.’ My name is Noah.”

target.text: 【Old man】 「I am not "old man". My name is Noah.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ホ！　ノアと来やがったか！　爺、てめえにゃ随分過ぎた名だなぁ！
　それともご先祖様かなんかかあんたの」
source.english:
“Ha! Noah, is it! Rather too grand a name for you!
Or was he an ancestor of yours?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「聖人にかぶれて、てめぇの餓鬼に同じ名をつける奴があるが、あんたの親もその口か」
source.english: “Some people get carried away with saints and name their brats after them. Your parents like that too?”

source.japanese: 水夫長の揶揄は一同の意気を鼓舞する為で、言わば老人は槍玉に挙げられたわけだが、返ってきたのは意想外の反撃の、水夫長は老練な眼を困惑に白黒させたという。
source.english: Long's mockery was intended to encourage the company. The old man had become his target. But the unexpected counterattack made even that old hand's eyes dart in bewilderment.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hoh! Noah, of all the things! Old man, that's a name way too grand for the likes of you! Or what, is he supposed to be one of your ancestors or something?」
【Bosun】 「Some bastards get so infatuated with a saint that they name their little shit after one, guess your folks were cut from the same cloth?」

The Bosun's banter was intended to rally the spirits of the crew, the old man made the sacrificial lamb so to speak, but the unexpected counterblow he received in return left the Bosun's seasoned eyes wide as saucers in bafflement.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「だから、儂がそのノアだ、と言うておるのよ。本人様じゃい、その人じゃい、ｅｃｃｅ　ｈｏｍｏじゃい」
