source.english: “I'm telling you, I am that Noah. The man himself. The very one. Ecce homo.”

source.japanese:
───たとえ聖書の名を知らない人間であっても、『ノアの方舟』の名は知っていようと言うくらい有名な、伝説中の伝説だ。
　旧約聖書の巻頭を飾る「創世記」において、ノアの方舟伝説が登場するのは第六章。
　……ちなみにアダムとイヴが楽園を追放されたのが第三章。この楽園追放をもって人類の繁栄は始まる訳だから、間二章しか保たずに人類は破滅の時を迎える事になる。まあ信天翁号の面子を見ていると、大概の神ならそれを考えるようになるだろうが。
source.english:
Even someone who had never heard of the Bible would know ‘Noah's Ark’: a legend among legends.
The story appeared in chapter six of Genesis, the book opening the Old Testament.
Incidentally, Adam and Eve were driven from Paradise in chapter three. Humanity's prosperity began with that expulsion, so it lasted only two intervening chapters before the hour of destruction. Looking at the Albatross company, most gods would probably begin considering it.

source.japanese:
さて、アダムとイヴの子孫たる人類が、産めよ殖やせと地に満ちて大いなる繁栄を享受するも、まあその素行の悪さにいたくお怒りになった神が手による、四〇日間にわたる暴風雨と大洪水に襲われ、地上の万物は悉[ことごと]く水に没し去った。
　ただ一つの生き残り、生命の最後の希望は、神が『善きひと』と認定したノアとその家族、彼らが造った方舟と、それに集められた雄雌一番[つが]いずつの動物たちだけ、なんとも心細い限りである。
source.english:
Adam and Eve's descendants had been fruitful and multiplied, filling the earth and enjoying great prosperity. God, however, became exceedingly angry at their bad behavior. Forty days of storms and a vast flood submerged all things upon the earth.
The sole survivors, life's last hope, were Noah, whom God had certified as a ‘good man,’ his family, the ark they had built, and the animals gathered aboard, one male and one female of each. A decidedly tenuous hope.

source.japanese: 結局大水は一五〇日もの間地の面を没させ、減じていくまでが更に一五〇日の期間を要したという。七月の一七日にアララテ山の頂上に漂着した方舟の中から、ノアは鳩を放ち水の引き具合を確かめようとするが、水はなお大地を満たして、鳩の留まれるような物や場所はなにもなく、鳩はノアの元へ空しく帰還した。七日後、再び放った鳩は橄欖の若葉を加えて戻り、水が引きつつある事を告げ、更に七日後に放つともう再び船には戻らなかった……落ち着くべき陸地を発見していたからである。
source.english: The flood covered the face of the earth for a hundred and fifty days. Another hundred and fifty were said to have passed before it diminished. The ark came to rest upon Mount Ararat on the seventeenth day of the seventh month. Noah released a dove to see how far the waters had receded. They still filled the land; finding nowhere to perch, it returned in vain. Released seven days later, it brought back a young olive leaf, announcing the retreat of the waters. Seven days after that, he sent it out again. It never returned: it had found land upon which to settle.

source.japanese: かくして『西暦』なら六〇〇と一年の二月二七日に、神の啓示によってノアと家族は船を出[い]で、地上には再び生き物による真の繁栄が築かれた、つまり現在の世界に存在する生き物というのは皆このノアと方舟に乗り合わせていた物達の子孫と言う事になる……。
source.english: Thus, on the twenty-seventh day of the second month in the year six hundred and one—if reckoned in ‘AD’ terms—Noah and his family left the vessel at God's command. True prosperity of living things was established again upon the earth. All the creatures in the present world, in other words, descended from Noah and those aboard his ark…

source.japanese:
これが世に伝わる『ノアの方舟と大洪水』伝説のあらましではあるが。
　皆、居合わせた者一同、ノアを名乗った老人を源に生じ濃さと暗さを増しながら、じわりじわりと迫る、言わば古よりの影に肩や胸元を押されるような圧迫感に押し黙った、訳ではない。
　自分が伝説中の登場人物その人である、と告げられたところで、別に信天翁号の面子ならずとて、はいそうですかと納得できるようなものでもあるまい。なるほど、この島は明らかに異様で、島内には確かに、多種多様の生物たちの番[つがい]の骨が散乱している。
　島内全体の木造建築物にも、どれもこれも古さが画一化されている、得体の知れ無さが立ち籠めている。
source.english:
Such was the outline of the story of Noah's Ark and the Great Flood.
The company had not fallen silent because some ancient shadow, emanating from the self-proclaimed Noah and growing darker and denser, pressed upon their shoulders and chests.
Being told that someone was a legendary figure in person would hardly make anyone—not merely this crew—accept it at once. Certainly the island was strange. Bones of paired animals of many species lay scattered throughout it.
Its wooden buildings all possessed the same uniform age, steeped in an air of something no one could fathom.

source.japanese:
けれど、だからといって、ここでたとえ老人がノアを名乗ったとしても『方舟伝説』を思わせる程の太古からの、怖るべき、遙けき時間の堆積までは感じられない、というのが船員達の正直な印象であり、加えてそもそもの矛盾が生じている。
　水夫長が、老人を自前の鷲のような目と、刺青の龍で睨[にら]み据えながら、ばん、と室内の壁にプレス機の如き勢いで掌叩きつければ、彼の内心の苛立ち示すようにもうもうと埃舞い上がり、下級水夫君達を咳きこませる。
source.english:
Yet even with the old man calling himself Noah, they honestly felt none of the dreadful, distant accumulation of time that would suggest the ark legend. Besides, there was a contradiction.
Long fixed him with his own eagle eyes and the tattooed dragon, then slapped a wall with the force of a press. Dust billowed in expression of his irritation, making the junior sailors cough.

target.text: 【Noah】 「Like I said, I am that Noah, that's what I'm telling you. The man himself, one and the same, ecce homo.」

───Even those who had not heard of the Bible before knew of it, knew of the name『Noah's Ark』, so famous was it, a legend amongst legends. In the 「Book of Genesis」that marks the beginning of the Old Testament, the legend of Noah's Ark appears in the sixth chapter. ……Incidentally, the expulsion of Adam and Eve from the Garden of Eden is the third chapter. The flourishing of humanity was brought about by this expulsion from paradise, so humanity only lasted but two chapters before being faced with utter destruction. Well, looking at the crew of the Albatross, most gods would probably come to think the same.

Now then, humanity, progeny of Adam and Eve, be fruitful, and multiply, and you shall fill the face of the earth and enjoy great prosperity, but, well, having grown exceedingly mad at the wickedness of man's actions, by His hand were they struck by a great rainstorm that lasted forty days and nights and a great flood, and all of creation that moved upon the earth was entirely submerged beneath the great flood, vanishing under the water. The lone survivors, the final hope for life, was Noah and his family, deemed『righteous』by God, upon the ark they had built, along with the animals gathered there in pairs of one male and female; what a terribly fragile thread of hope that made for.

In the end, it is said that the waters prevailed upon the earth an hundred and fifty days, and that another hundred and fifty days passed before the flood had fully receded. On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark had come to rest on the summit of Mount Ararat, and from there, Noah sent forth a dove, to see if the waters were abated, but the waters were still on the face of the ground, there was nowhere or nothing upon which a dove could find rest for the sole of her foot, and so the dove returned unto Noah with nothing to show for it.

Seven days later, he again sent forth the dove, and lo, this time, she returned with a fresh olive leaf pluckt off, a testament to the waters having abated from off the earth, and when he again sent forth the dove seven days later, it returned not again unto him any more……for it had found the land in which it ought to settle.

Thus, using the Gregorian calender, on the 27th day of February of his 601st year, Noah and his family left the ark in accordance with a divine revelation from God, and true prosperity was once more established by those living things who went forth out of the ark; in other words, all living things that exist in the present world would have to be the progeny of those who were on board Noah's ark…….

This is the outline of the legend of 『Noah's Ark and the Great Flood』 as it is passed down around the world. It was not that all of them, every single person present, had fallen silent beneath a crushing pressure that seemed to weigh heavily on their shoulders and chest, that emanated from this old man calling himself Noah, growing denser and darker while it slowly crept ever closer; a shadow of antiquity, so to speak.

I am that very character from the legend: the moment you are told as much, you need not count yourself a member of the crew of the Albatross, it is still not the sort of claim you can just simply accept with an "Oh, is that so?". Indeed, this island was evidently bizarre, and certainly, the bones of mated pairs of a great variety of animals were scattered about the island. And even the wooden buildings throughout the island, with the way that each and every one was uniformly timeworn, were shrouded in an air of unsettling incomprehensibility.

However, even with all that, and even if the old man here claimed to be Noah, he did not evoke the sort of vast accumulation of distant aeons that ought to be feared, that gave one the impression of the『Legend of the Ark』, such was the honest impression of the crew, and it also created a fundamental contradiction. While fixing the old man with a glare from both his own eagle-like eyes and the dragon tattoo on his face, the Bosun slammed his palm against the wall with all the force of a machine press, and as though to reflect his inner frustration, a thick cloud of dust billowed out, causing the deck boys to cough.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「百歩譲っててめえが本物のノアで、くたばり損なってここにいるとしよう。
　なら、なんで俺達はここにいるんだよっ」
source.english:
“Let's give you every benefit of the doubt. You're the real Noah and somehow haven't died yet.
Then how the hell are we here?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「For the sake of argument, let's say that you are the real Noah and that you missed your chance to kick the bucket and ended up here. Then how the hell are we here?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それに世界の生き物も、あんたの方舟の生き物たちの子孫なんだろみんな！
　それがここで骨になってちゃあ、子孫もクソもねえやあ！」
source.english:
“And all the world's creatures are supposed to descend from the animals on your ark!
If they're lying here as bones, there couldn't be any goddamn descendants!”

source.japanese: ……わざわざ相手の言葉に乗った上で、それを論理で打ち負かそうとするとはこの強面の男も案外律儀者だが、一方老人はまた窓から大海蛇の様子を眺め、頭巾の裡[うち]でほくそ笑んで肩を震わせる様は、出来のいい兵器を愛でる死の商人のようですらあり、とうてい全ての生き物を後世に伝える事許された『善き人』とは思えなかったが、
source.english: For such a forbidding man, taking the other's premise and trying to defeat it logically was unexpectedly conscientious. The old man looked out at the serpent again, grinning within his hood, shoulders shaking like an arms dealer admiring a well-made weapon. Hardly the ‘good man’ entrusted with preserving all creatures for posterity. Yet…

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Besides, all the creatures of the world are all supposed to be the descendants of the creatures on YOUR ark, right!? If they all ended up as bones here, they'd have shit for posterity!」

……This fierce-looking man was unexpectedly conscientious, for not only did he go out of his way to go along with the premise of his opponent, he even went so far as to attempt to defeat it through logical argument, but on the other hand, the old man still beheld the state of the great sea serpent from the window, chuckling to himself within his hood while his shoulders shook in a way that even brought to mind a merchant of death stroking a well-made ordnance, and he did not remotely appear the sort of "righteous man" entrusted with passing all living creatures down to posterity, but,

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「ノアが一人だけだなどと誰が決めたんじゃ。
　一文明の崩壊にあたって、当時現存しておる生物相の保存管理役に当てられた者は、皆ノアじゃ」
source.english:
“Who decided there could only be one Noah?
At the collapse of a civilization, anyone assigned to preserve and manage the fauna then in existence is a Noah.”

target.text: 【Noah】 「Whoever decided that there could only be a single Noah? In the event of the collapse of a civilization, those appointed to the duty of preserving and managing the extant biota are Noah, all of us.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「は……はぁん？
　てめえ、なに言って……」
source.english:
“H… huh?
What are you saying…?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Wh-……huuuh? What the hell are you saying……」

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「だいたい、生物相を保存しようという大難事、一つの計画、一つの作戦だけに頼る訳なかろ。お前達だとて、重要な計画にはフォローちうのをつけるだろうが」
source.english: “Such a tremendous task as preserving living species could hardly depend upon a single plan, a single mission. Even you arrange backup for an important undertaking.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「儂はな、第三次『方舟計画』プランβ、ウリエルタイプのプロジェクトマスター、コードネーム『ノア』、認識番号００００四－二三甲、本名……は、この際どうでもええわ」
source.english: “I am project master of the Third Ark Project, Plan Beta, Uriel type. Codename Noah. Identification number 00004-23A. Real name… doesn't matter just now.”

source.japanese: とうとうと、立て板に水、というより油でも流すかの流暢さで捲[まく]し立てられても、一同には異次元の言語でも駆使されているようにとんと理解が及ばず───だが、老人はそこまで語ったものの。肩を落とした、ようにしか見えなかった。
source.english: He rattled it off, smooth as water—or oil—running down a plank. To the listeners it might have been a language from another dimension; they understood nothing. But having said that much, the old man seemed to let his shoulders fall.

target.text: 【Noah】 「In the first place, there was simply no way that a task as arduous as preserving the biota would be entrusted to a single plan, a single mission. Even you people must have something like a backup for any important plans.」
【Noah】 「I am the project master of the third 『Ark Project』plan β, Type Uriel, code name『Noah』, identification number 00004-23A, and my real name is……well, that doesn't matter at this point.」

Though he spoke to them in an endless stream of eloquent words as fluid as water, or rather, oil running down a board, it was as if he was speaking fluently in a language from another dimension, and it was beyond the comprehension of any of them─── and yet, though the old man had spoken so much. He only seemed despondent, his shoulders slumped.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「しかし儂は……果たせンかった。
　他のノア達は……どうなったか知らん。
　なんにせよ、儂の方舟はいつまで経っても」
source.english:
“But I… could not accomplish it.
What happened to the other Noahs…
I don't know. Whatever the case, my ark never…”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「───嵐から、抜けられんかったよ」
source.english: “…We never escaped the storm.”

target.text: 【Noah】 「But I……could not accomplish my mission. The other Noahs……I know not what happened to. At any rate, no matter how much time passed, my ark.」
【Noah】 「───Could not escape the storm.」

source.japanese:
窓辺から離れ、室内を歩み、また丸椅子に戻って座すまで、数歩の間、その僅かな間に老人から、長衣の肩やその内側から、救いようのないほど倦[う]み疲れた者の悲哀と、生涯を捧げた計画の頓挫を迎えた者の、凄惨な絶望とが溢れだし、部屋を濃い翳[かげ]りに塗り替えてくいかのよう。
　椅子に腰を下ろしたすがたにも、重荷に耐えかねた人の拭い去りがたい疲労が澱[よど]んでひたすらに沈鬱だった。
source.english:
He left the window, crossed the room and returned to the stool. In those few steps, the grief of someone hopelessly exhausted and the appalling despair of a life's work defeated poured from his shoulders, from within his robe, seeming to repaint the room in dense shadow.
Even seated, he seemed sunk in the ineradicable fatigue of someone unable to bear his burden. Unrelieved gloom settled there.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「なにが原因なのか、いまだもって不明だ。
　気象制御システムがこのような誤動作を起こす事など、セキュリテイ上ありえん。時空閉鎖系も方舟計画の船には干渉権限を保持しない」
source.english:
“The cause remains unknown.
For security reasons, such a malfunction in the weather-control system is impossible. Nor does the closed spacetime system hold authority to interfere with Ark Project vessels.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「だが事実として嵐は儂の方舟を襲い続けた……いや、襲い続けている。今もだ。お前たちも知るとおりだ。船は、いまだ嵐に囚われたままだよ」
source.english: “Yet the storm continued to assault my ark… No, continues. Even now. As you know. The vessel is still trapped within it.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「物語の復元能力が働いたのではないか。
　儂はそう睨[にら]んでおる。なにしろ、生物相を保存する、という題目の下、当時は現存しておらなんだモノまで収集したからな」
source.english:
“Perhaps the narrative's power to restore itself intervened.
That is my suspicion. In the name of preserving the fauna, we even collected things no longer existing at the time.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「どこかに無理をかければ、どこかにその歪みが来る。……ま、当然の道理だわ」
source.english: “Strain something in one place, and the distortion appears elsewhere… A natural principle, really.”

source.japanese: 次第に老人の声が低く成りゆき、廃屋に積もった埃の中に吸われていったが、その物哀しさは哀しさとして、どうにもおかしな点がちらほらと。そもそも老人が使う語句からして意味不明ではあったが、そればかりではない。石鹸の、虹色に色合いを転変させる泡の中に、幾つか濁った物が混ざるのを見て、老人に問いかける。
source.english: His voice gradually lowered and was absorbed into the dust of the house. Sadness aside, there were odd points here and there. His very vocabulary was incomprehensible, but that was not all. A few cloudy flecks showed in that soap bubble's shifting rainbow colors. Sakuya questioned him.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「爺さんの言ってる事はさっぱりわかんないけどさ。じゃあまあそっちはそっちとして、爺さんのその方舟とやらはどこよ？　まだこの嵐ン中から出られてないんだろ？」
source.english: “I don't understand a word of it, old man. Fine, leave that aside. Where's this ark of yours? It still hasn't got out of the storm, right?”

source.japanese: 朔屋の問いに航海士が何事か口にしかけたが、結局はなにも言わずに押し黙る、言うのが面倒になっただけかも知れぬ。
source.english: A navigator began to answer Sakuya, then said nothing. Perhaps explaining had merely become too much bother.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「どこ、もなにも。こういう時にも、察しの悪い奴というのはどうしても一人は混じるもんだな……若造、この島がそうだ」
source.english: “Where? There always has to be one slow fellow, even at a time like this… Young man, this island is it.”

target.text: He stepped back from the window, walked into the room, returned to the stool once more, then sat down; in the time those steps took, in that brief moment, from the old man, and the shoulders of his robe and within it, the sorrow of a man irremediably world-weary, together with the ghastly despair of a man who had witnessed the ruin of his life's work, poured forth as though smearing the room in deep, gloomy shadow. Even when sitting down did the ineffaceable fatigue of a man unable to bear so heavy a burden linger within his form, exuding a deep, earnest melancholy.

【Noah】 「Whatever the cause of it was, it still remains unclear to this day. It is inconceivable for the weather control system to malfunction like this, from a security standpoint. The space-time closure system also doesn't retain the authority to interfere with the ships of the Ark Project.」
【Noah】 「But the reality of things is that this storm continued to assail my ark ……nay, it continues to. Even now. It is just as you all know. This ship remains trapped in this storm, to this day.」

【Noah】 「Perhaps the narrative's ability to reconstruct itself was at work. I surmise as much. At any rate, operating under the heading of preserving the biota, we even gathered things that were not extant at the time.」
【Noah】 「If you push too hard somewhere, something has to give elsewhere. ……Well, that's only logical.」

The old man's voice gradually grew lower and lower, absorbed by the dust that had accumulated within the abandoned building, but melancholy as it all was, there was a sprinkling of odd details. The vocabulary the old man used was incomprehensible to begin with, but that was not all. Seeing several impurities mixed into the soap bubbles shimmering and shifting in prismatic hues, he posed the old man a question.
【Naomasa】 「I don't understand a word of what you're saying, old man. Alright, so, setting all that aside for now, where did this ark-thing of yours go? It still can't get out of this storm, right?」
One of the first mates was about to say something in response to Sakuya's question, but in the end, she remained silent without a word; perhaps she just found it too bothersome to say.
【Noah】 「What do you mean, "where"? Even in times like these, there just always has to be that one guy who is slow on the uptake…… Boy, it's this island.」

source.japanese: 丸椅子に身を起こし、片腕をさ、横に伸ばして凪ぐ仕草、島全体示すように。
source.english: He straightened on the stool, extended an arm and swept it sideways, as though indicating the whole island.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「この島は、儂の方舟を解体して造ったんだ、と、ここまで聞けば大概判りそうなもんだがな」
source.english: “I dismantled my ark to build this island. One would think most people could work that out after hearing so much.”

source.japanese:
───現在彼らが隠れるこの三階建ての廃屋、そしてその他全ての廃屋、島内を走る通路、各構造物、ばかりか恐らくこの島全てが、『ノアの方舟』を解体して、その構造材で組み上げた───と言われても、一同にはやはり実感に乏しい話としか。
　この島が一つの木造建築物である。ここまではいい。シサム・キサラもそれは感じ取っている。それ自体は大いなる驚異だ。
　が、しかし、それが元は一つの船だった、と告げられても、まるで実感が生じない、と言うのが一同の正直な印象であった。
　そもそも信天翁号の一向は、老人がノアその人だと名乗った時点で、ボケが高じたあげく妄言を吐くようになった徘徊老人、程度にしか考えていない。
source.english:
This three-story house where they sheltered, all the other houses, the paths and structures—probably the entire island—had been assembled from the materials of a dismantled Noah's Ark. Even told that, the company could scarcely make it feel real.
The island was a single wooden structure. Very well. Sisam and Kisara had sensed that too. A great wonder in itself.
But that it had formerly been one ship—none of them could really take that in. From the instant the old man claimed to be Noah,
the Albatross company had taken him for a wandering old dotard whose senility had begun producing delusions.

target.text: Straightening up on the stool, he extended one arm to the side in a calm, sweeping motion, as if pointing out the entire island.
【Noah】 「This island was built from my dismantled Ark, but, having heard this much, you'd think you would have put two and two together by now.」

───The three-storied house they were currently taking refuge in, as well as all the other ruined buildings, the pathways running across the island, all the various structures, and not just that, but in all likelihood even the entire island itself was put together from the structural materials obtained from dismantling『Noah's Ark』 ───but to all present, even when told as much, it sounded only as a tale with a tenuous connection to reality.

This island was a single wooden construct. So far so good. Shisamu and Kisara had already perceived as much. That in itself was already a great wonder. But, however, he could inform them that this used to be a single ship all he liked, it just didn't feel real to them; that was their honest impression. To begin with, the moment the old man introduced himself as Noah, the man himself, the entire crew of the Albatross considered him to be nothing more than some old man roaming about whose senility had worsened to the point of spouting off delusions.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え……じゃあ、方舟ばらしちゃったの？　
　はー。そらまあさぞやご苦労な。
　……ん？　ああ、判った判ったクロ、
　もうこの爺さんとは口、聞かねえから」
source.english:
“Huh… You took the ark apart? Well.
Must've been a lot of work…
Mm? All right, Kuro.
I get it. Won't talk to him anymore.”

source.japanese:
老人の登場時より怯えきっているクロは、朔屋が彼に話しかけただけでもいよいよ狂乱の度合い深め、青年の背で縮み上がってはぐいぐいと、とにかく老人から隠れたい離れたい一心で、朔屋を引っ張る朔屋の背に顔を押しつける。
　少しばかり扱いあぐね、背後に手を回して軽く頭を撫でてやるのがせいぜいの、皆でこうして逃れてきたところを自分達だけ離れる訳にもいくまい。そうやって離れてしまうのも危険なような気もするし。
source.english:
Terrified since the old man's arrival, Kuro grew more frantic merely at Sakuya addressing him. She shrank behind the young man, tugging him insistently, pressing her face to his back, intent only upon hiding and getting away.
He scarcely knew how to handle her. Reaching back to pat her head was about all he could do. Everyone had escaped here together; they could not simply leave on their own. Separating also felt dangerous.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Uh……so then, you took apart the whole Ark? Haaah. Well, that sure must have been hard work, yeah. ……Hm? Yeah, I get it, Kuro, I get it. I won't talk to this old man anymore, it's fine.」

Kuro had been utterly seized with terror ever since the old man made his entrance, and the mere act of Sakuya speaking with him only deepened her frenzy; she cowered behind his back, shrinking up, all that ran through her mind was the desire to simply hide from that old man, to get away from him, and she tugged forcefully on Sakuya while pressing her face into his back. Finding himself just a little unsure how to handle her, the most he could do was reach around his back with a hand and lightly pat her on the head, for with everyone having escaped here together, it wasn't as if the two of them could just up and leave. He also felt it would be rather dangerous to just separate like that.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「もちろん儂とて『方舟』を解体などしたくはなかった……どれだけ台風が続こうとも……理論的には、大型級で風速七〇ノット級の台風に常時晒され続けても、五世紀は無補給無整備で持ちこたえられる……そのように設計、建造されておったしな……」
source.english: “Naturally, I had no wish to dismantle the ark… However long the typhoon lasted… In theory, it was designed and built to endure continuous exposure to a major typhoon with seventy-knot winds for five centuries, without resupply or maintenance…”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「航海当初は全てが順調にいっておった。食料、水、薬品の備蓄は十二分にあり、給餌装置も、排泄物の処理装置も、捕食生物、攻撃性の強い生物の情動抑制装置も。皆問題なく稼働しておったよ……しかし」
source.english: “At first, all went well. Stores of food, water and medicines were more than sufficient. The feeding devices, the waste-processing equipment, the emotional suppression systems for predators and highly aggressive creatures. All operated without trouble… But…”

target.text: 【Noah】 「Of course, I also did not wish to disassemble the『Ark』or anything of the sort……no matter how long the typhoon would have continued to rage……theoretically, even should it be constantly exposed to a typhoon with sustained winds of seventy knots, a large class would be able to withstand it for five centuries without resupplying or maintenance ……that was what it was designed for, how it was constructed……」

【Noah】 「At the outset of our voyage, everything went swimmingly. Our stocks of victuals, water, and medicine were more than plentiful, and our feeding devices, as well as our excrement processors, and also our emotional suppression devices for use on predators or highly aggressive animals. All of them operating without a single issue. ……However.」

source.japanese:
───ある日。
　───悲劇が起こったのだ、という。
　──動力供給機構の異常動作、そして停止だったと老人は語った。
source.english:
One day.
Tragedy came, he said.
The power-supply mechanism malfunctioned, then stopped.

source.japanese: 凶暴な攻撃本能を持つ生物たちを抑制していた機構も、動力の供給が止まってしまえば廃物と変わりない。水夫長が発見したような太古の生物中の覇者、暴君、それに航海士も語ったように猫科の捕食者達。他にも見当もつかないような生物もあったかも知れない───そう、今一行の死神となっているあの大海蛇といった───
source.english: The systems restraining creatures of ferocious aggression were no better than scrap without power. The ancient tyrants, rulers among beasts, such as the boatswain had found; the feline predators the navigators had mentioned. Perhaps other unimaginable creatures as well. Yes, like the sea serpent now serving as the company's Death…

source.japanese:
……動力供給機構の復旧まで三日三晩の連続作業が要求されたというし、結局完全なる修復は不可能だったのだという。
　その間に事態は悪化の一途を迎え、穏和な生き物たちは次々と捕食者達の牙にかかり、清掃、空調の両装置の作動不能が遺体の腐敗とそれに端を発する疫病の蔓延を招いた。
　そして、嵐───予定されていた四〇日を過ぎても全く収まる兆しもなく吹き荒れ続ける嵐。船内の人間、管理者達は絶望した。
source.english:
Restoring the power supply had required three days and nights of uninterrupted work, and complete repair ultimately proved impossible.
Meanwhile, matters worsened without cease. Gentle creatures fell one after another to predators' teeth. Failed cleaning and ventilation systems allowed corpses to rot, spreading disease.
And the storm—blowing on without any sign of abating beyond the planned forty days. The people aboard, the administrators, despaired.

source.japanese: ……朔屋は想像してみる。むっとする閉じきった世界。広さは、とりあえずタンカーくらいだろうか。その内部は暗闇に閉ざされ、船内の機械は全てまともに動かない。そんな暗闇の中を徘徊し、手当たり次第に他の生物に襲いかかる猛獣たち。蔓延する死の気配に疫病───間違いなく自分であれば精神が保たない。一晩目でたやすく発狂するだろう。
source.english: Sakuya tried imagining it. A stifling, sealed world. Perhaps about the size of a tanker. Inside, darkness. None of the machinery working properly. Fierce beasts prowling that darkness, attacking any creature they found. Death everywhere, disease… His mind would certainly not last. He would easily go mad on the first night.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「全体の機構はある程度復興したが、それでも十全とはとうてい言えず、うち続く嵐……。
　船は堅牢であったが、人間の精神の方が保たなんだな。儂や他の管理者達はまだ耐えられた事態でも、家族達は別だった」
source.english:
“The mechanisms were restored to a degree, but nowhere near fully. And the continuing storm…
The ship was strong; the human mind did not endure. The others and I, the administrators, could still bear it. Our families were another matter.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「……同僚、というよりあれは、儂にとっては弟のような男がおってな……そいつも死んだよ。船内を哨戒中、オオアリクイに背後から襲いかかられ、ふりほどく事もできずその舌を鼻孔から差し入れられ、脳髄を全て啜[すす]らりとられてな……」
source.english: “…There was a colleague. More like a younger brother to me… He died too. A giant anteater attacked him from behind while he was patrolling the ship. He couldn't shake it off. It thrust its tongue through his nostril and sucked out all his brains…”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「彼の妻はその時臨月だった……彼の死が伝わってしもうてな。ショックで異常出産を起こし、子供も母胎も保たんかった。
　今際のきわに哀願されたよ。
　───どうか、生き物たちに陸地を───
　と。自分や夫、そして子供が死ぬ事よりも、最期まで生き物達の末を憂いておったわい」
source.english:
“His wife was at term… She learned of his death, and the shock brought on a disastrous labor; neither mother nor child survived.
As she lay dying, she begged me:
please, give the creatures land.
To the last, she worried for their future more than for the deaths of herself, her husband and her child.”

source.japanese: ……辛気くさい話だ、と水夫長以下欠伸を垂れたのが信天翁号面子である。ちなみに朔屋はついうっかりもらい泣きをしていたりで。
source.english: What a depressing story. Long and the others yawned: that was the Albatross company. Sakuya, incidentally, had carelessly begun crying in sympathy.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「それで儂も、心が決まった。
　とにかく、仮初めでいい、こんな密閉された船内でない、島を造ろうと」
source.english:
“That settled my mind too.
Temporary or not, I would make an island. Something other than this sealed ship.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「まあ困難は当然あった訳だが、結果としてはお前たちが乗っかっているこの島だ。
　島を築き、島内に生き物たちを養う為の家屋を築き───それでも雨は、やはり降りやまんかった」
source.english:
“There were difficulties, naturally. But the result is the island beneath your feet.
I built it, then houses upon it to keep the creatures… Still, the rain would not stop.”

source.japanese: 老人の声が、熱望と絶望、そして渇望とが渦巻いて、どろどろと滾[たぎる]るような内圧を秘めゆき、室内の床を這うように広がっては満ちて、一行は老人を核として部屋が暗く翳[かげ]りゆくかの心地に囚われた。
source.english: His voice held an inner pressure, boiling thickly with mingled hope, despair and craving. It crept across the floor, spreading and filling the room. The listeners felt darkness gathering with the old man at its core.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「儂は必死で鳥を放ち続けたよ。
　陸地の証を持ち帰る事をひたすら念じてな。
　何度も───何度も。
　ひたすらの祈りと共に───」
source.english:
“I kept releasing birds, desperately.
Praying they would bring back proof of land. Again…
and again.
With nothing but prayer…”

target.text: ───A certain day. ───A tragedy occurred, he said. ───The old man recounted the malfunction, and subsequent shutdown, of the power supply mechanism.

The machinery that restrained the creatures with instincts of ferocious aggression was no better than scrap once the supply of power was cut off. The supreme rulers, the tyrants of ancient times like those the Bosun had discovered, as well as the feline predators the first mates had spoken of. Perhaps there were also other creatures that they could scarce imagine─── indeed, like the great sea serpent that currently acted the part of the group's very own Grim Reaper───

……He said that it took them three whole days and nights of ceaseless work to restore the power supply mechanism, but ultimately, it was not possible to fully repair it. Meanwhile, the situation only worsened; one after another, the mild, peaceful animals were beset upon by the fangs of predators, and the inoperability of both the cleaning and air conditioning systems resulted in the decomposition of the corpses, as well as the subsequent spread of pestilence that wrought.

And then, there was the storm─── the storm that, despite the scheduled forty days having passed, still continued to rage without showing the first sign of abating. The humans on board the ship, the administrators, despaired.

……Sakuya tried to imagine it. A stifling, closed-off world. The size, well, it was probably about that of a tanker? Its interior covered in a blanket of darkness, and none of the machinery on board working properly. And prowling in that darkness were savage beasts indiscriminately attacking the other animals. An air of death and pestilence running rampant───there was no doubt he would be unable to maintain his sanity in that situation. He would easily go insane on the very first night, most like.

【Noah】 「The mechanisms had, to a certain degree, been restored to functionality, but it was far from perfect, and the storm raged on……. The ship was sturdy, but the human psyche was not. While I and the other administrators could still endure the situation, it was a different story for our families.」

【Noah】 「……A colleague, though that man was more like a younger brother to me……he also died. While patrolling the ship, he was pounced on from behind by a giant anteater, and before he could shake it off, its tongue had been thrust up his nostril, and his entire brain was sucked out……」

【Noah】 「His wife was in her final month of pregnancy at the time……and then news of his death spread. The shock caused an abnormal childbirth, and neither the child nor the mother's body survived the ordeal. She pleaded with me on her deathbed. ──Pray, lead the animals to land── So she begged. Until the very end, she remained more worried about the fate of the animals than the deaths of herself or her husband, or even her child.」
……What a dark, depressing tale, yawned the Bosun and the rest, for such were the crew of the Albatross. Incidentally, Sakuya couldn't help but be moved to tears by it all.
【Noah】 「With that, my resolve was steeled. For the time being, even a makeshift one would do; I would build an island, somewhere not within the confines of this sealed vessel.」

【Noah】 「Well, there were some difficulties, naturally, but the result is this very island you now stand upon. I built an island, and on the island, I built the buildings necessary to provide for the animals─── and yet, the rain still never ceased to fall.」

The old man's voice was a swirling jumble of burning desire, despair, and craving, harbouring within it an internal pressure that seemed to roil and seethe, spreading and filling the room as though it were crawling along the floor; the group was seized by a feeling as if the room were being swallowed by a deepening darkness with the old man as its center.
【Noah】 「I desperately continued to send forth a bird. Devotedly praying for it to bring home proof of land. Over and over───again and again. With my earnest prayers───」

source.japanese: ゆっくり立ち上がる老人は、人と言うより、長衣の中に執念と妄執をガス状に詰め込んで、過去が伸ばしてきた手のように思え、歩む動きもどこか関節や靱帯の構造が勝手の異なるように、くにゃくにゃと、そう見えるほど、緩慢で音のない動きだったのに。
source.english: He rose slowly. Less a man than a robe packed with the gaseous stuff of obsession, a hand stretched out by the past. His movement seemed to follow unfamiliar arrangements of joints and ligaments, bending loosely. Slow and silent though it was…

target.text: As he slowly rose from the chair, the old man seemed less human and more a robe stuffed full with a gaseous mixture of obsession and deep-seated delusions; like a hand stretching out from the past, even the way he moved while walking was wobbly and mushy, as though the structure of his ligaments and joints was somehow different; though it was a motion so languid and soundless as to look that way.

source.japanese: どすん、と音は朔屋の背後から。ばたばたともがく音も続いて、見ればクロは、声さえ出せないくらいに必死で引きつった形相で、老人から逃げだそうとあがいており、なのに恐慌のあまり手足に意味のある動き、全く宿らず。
source.english: Thud. The sound came from behind Sakuya, followed by frantic struggling. He looked: Kuro's face was drawn into so desperate a rictus that she could not even cry out. She tried to flee the old man, but panic robbed every motion of her limbs of meaning.

source.japanese:
老人が進む───
　クロが引きつる。
　
　老人が歩む───
　
　クロが隠れる場所を求めて頭を振り回す。
　老人が手を伸ばす───
source.english:
The old man advanced.
Kuro convulsed.
The old man walked.
Kuro swung her head about, seeking somewhere to hide.
The old man stretched out a hand.

source.japanese: クロの喉が過呼吸を起こし、冬枯れの風の音を鳴らす。朔屋が飛びついて背後に庇[かば]う。
source.english: Kuro began hyperventilating, her throat sounding like wind over a winter-bare waste. Sakuya sprang to shelter her behind him.

target.text: A thump sounded from behind Sakuya. The sounds of struggling continued, and when he looked, Kuro's expression was so contorted with desperation that she couldn't even make a sound, flailing about in an effort to escape from the old man, and yet, she was so overwhelmed by panic that the ability to make any meaningful movements no longer resided in her limbs.
The old man advanced─── Kuro twitched. The old man walked─── Kuro swung her head around, searching for a place to hide. The old man reached out his hand───
Kuro's throat started to hyperventilate, producing the sound of a desolate winter wind. Sakuya jumped in and shielded her behind his back.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい爺さん、なにちっちゃい女の子を脅かしてんだ。ほら見ろ、こんなになって。まだ漏らしてないのが不思議なくらいで───」
source.english: “Hey, old man. Why are you terrorizing a woman half your size? Look at her. It's a wonder she hasn't wet herself…”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「なにが……女の子だ……。
　儂が放ったのは、鴉よ。
　艶やかで黒き、そして強い羽根。
　嵐にも負けぬ……な」
source.english:
“What… woman…?
What I released was a crow.
With glossy, strong black feathers.
Not even a storm could defeat it…”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「鳥の中の鳥、その叡智は神話中の常連となるほどの、な。
　これ以上に使命を託すに相応しい鳥が、他にあろうか」
source.english:
“A bird among birds. Its wisdom makes it a constant presence in myth.
What bird could be more suited to such a mission?”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「だから儂は、全ての船員、生き物の為に願いを込めて、鴉を放ち続けた。
　陸地を発見させる為になぁ……」
source.english:
“So, with my hopes for every sailor and creature, I kept sending out the crow.
To find land…”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「だがその鴉[カラス]は何度放っても戻ってきよる。陸を見つけもせんでな。
　儂は呪った。その艶[つや]やかな黒。
　大いなる叡智の色、黒」
source.english:
“But however often I sent it, that crow returned. Without finding land.
I cursed its glossy black.
Black, the color of great wisdom.”

source.japanese: 老人が、朔屋の前に立つ。朔屋の鼻先に漂う、黴臭さ、幽かな腐臭、薬品臭さ、オイルの匂い、それらが青年に、目の前に立つものを人と言うよりも、長衣の形をした何かの機械とか、研究室とかそんなものを連想させ、たじろいだ瞬間に肩に掛かった手、さしたる剛力にもあらず、なのに手首の一返しで青年は部屋の隅まで放り出されるが薄汚れて片方しかない靴下のよう、無用、邪魔、それ以外の何ものでもないと。
source.english: He stood before Sakuya. Mold, faint rot, chemicals, oil: the smells reaching the young man's nose suggested not a person, but a machine or laboratory shaped like a robe. As Sakuya flinched, a hand rested on his shoulder. No great strength, yet one turn of the wrist flung him into the room's corner like a dirty lone sock. Useless. In the way. Nothing else.

source.japanese:
そして青年がのけられれば白、この時の白は、溶け崩れた乳酪のように床に頽[くずお]れ、びくり、びくりと身を震わせるばかりで、手足は完全に萎えていた。
　そもそもクロが、四肢の使いようからして頼りないのも当然だったのだ。本来あるべき形ではなかったのだから。
source.english:
Once the young man was removed, there was white. White collapsed upon the floor like melted butter, doing nothing but twitch and shudder, its limbs utterly weak.
Naturally Kuro had never known how to use them properly. This was not the shape she ought to have had.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「……全く役に立たなかったではないか！
　だから。儂は！　呪ってやったわい。
　役立たずの鴉[カラス]を」
source.english:
“…Utterly useless!
So I cursed it.
That useless crow!”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「陸地を見つけるその時まで、休む事ならじ、戻ってくる事ならじ、と。
　そうそう、ついでにな、他の鴉[カラス]と区別がつくように───」
source.english:
“Until it found land, it must not rest. Must not return.
And, while I was at it, to distinguish it from the other crows…”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「呪って、みぃんな、白くしてヤッたわい」
source.english: “I cursed it all white.”

source.japanese: ノアが、身を二つ折りにする、その挙動は圧搾空気で動かす人形のよう、しかもクロを脅かす為にわざとやっているような節すら見受けられ、老人の本性の歪みを物語る。
source.english: Noah bent double like a compressed-air puppet. He even seemed to do it deliberately to frighten Kuro, revealing the distortion of his nature.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「おうおう、そこにいるわ。かつての力全てを失った、哀れで、みじめで、誰からも望まれぬ、そんな情けない生き物が」
source.english: “There it is. All its former powers lost. A poor, miserable creature nobody wants. Pathetic.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「かつての面影など無いくせに、名前だけは未だ名乗っているのが滑稽でならんわ！」
source.english: “Not a trace of what it was, yet still calling itself by the same name. Hilarious!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Oi, gramps, what are you scaring a little girl for? Come on, just look at how poorly she's holding up. It's a miracle she hasn't pissed herself by now───」
【Noah】 「A little girl……what nonsense……. What I sent forth was a crow. Lustrous, dark, and powerful wings. Wings that would not yield before even a storm……yes.」
【Noah】 「A bird amongst birds, with wisdom so sage that it is a constant companion in myth and legend, yes. Is there any other bird more worthy of being entrusted with a mission?」
【Noah】 「And that is why I kept sending forth the crow, carrying my prayers on behalf of the entire crew, of all living creatures. So it may one day discover land……」

【Noah】 「But no matter how many times I sent forth that damned crow, it had the nerve to keep coming back. Without ever finding any land at that. I cursed it. That lustruous black. The colour of great wisdom, black.」

The old man stood before Sakuya. It drifted to Sakuya's nose, the musty stench of mold, of a faint rot, of chemicals, a smell of oil, and that made the young man associate what stood before him not with a man, but rather some manner of machine assuming the shape of a robe, with laboratories and the like; the moment he shrunk back, a hand landed on his shoulder, and though it held no strength of particular note, with a mere flick of the wrist, the young man was tossed all the way into a corner of the room like a dirty sock, as if to say he was useless, a hindrance, and that was all he amounted to.

Thus, with Sakuya now unceremoniously pushed out of the way, the white now collapsed to the floor like melting butter, its body merely trembling, its limbs gone entirely limp. It was only natural that Kuro seemed so clumsy and feeble from the way she used her limbs. For they were not in the shape they ought to hold by nature.
【Noah】 「……You are just UTTERLY useless, aren't you! And that is why. THAT I! Cursed you. Put a curse on this useless crow.」
【Noah】 「Until the day you find land, you shall not rest, nor shall you return, I said. Right, right, and while I was at it, to help distinguish you from any other crow───」
【Noah】 「I cursed you, turned aaaall of you white, I did.」

Noah folded himself in half, the movement like that of a doll powered by pneumatics; moreover, it even seemed as if he deliberately did it just to scare Kuro, a testament to the distorted nature of the old man's true character.
【Noah】 「Yes, yes, there you are. Having lost all your former strength, pitiable, wretched, unwanted by all, so pathetic a creature right before my eyes!」
【Noah】 「You retain not a shadow of your former self, and yet you still cling to your name alone! How utterly farcical!」

source.japanese: クロは……まず視線が上にくるりとぶれた。喪神の霧の中に逃げ込もうとしたようだがそんな都合のいい逃避を老人は許さず、むしろこちらの方が意地悪鳥の鉤爪のような指の先を伸ばし、少女のあばらをたっぷりとくすぐっては、恐怖に笑い声も出ない、痙攣的な笑いでこちらに引き戻し、赤い眸[ひとみ]、今は血が滲んだような濁りきった眸[ひとみ]を覗きこんで、たっぷりと怯えの味を賞味してから。
source.english: Kuro's eyes first rolled upward, as though seeking refuge in the fog of unconsciousness. He allowed no such convenient escape. Extending fingers like the talons of a spiteful bird, he thoroughly tickled her ribs. Though terror robbed her laughter of all voice, its convulsions dragged her back. He peered into her red eyes, clouded now as though blood had seeped into them, and savored their fear.

target.text: First……Kuro's gaze flickered upwards and lost focus. It was as if she was trying to escape into the fog of unconsciousness, but the old man did not permit such a convenient flight from reality; rather, he stretched the tips of his fingers towards her like the talons of a malicious bird, then thoroughly tickled the girl's ribs, and unable to voice it out of sheer terror, it was with a convulsive laugh that he brought her back to wakefulness; peering into those red eyes, now completely clouded as if blood had seeped into them, he fully savoured every last drop of fear within them, and then.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「クロ……烏などと───っ」
source.english: “Kuro… Still calling yourself Crow…!”

target.text: 【Noah】 「Kuro……to call yourself crow───!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……ｋｅっ……、
　ｋｅっ、ｋａ───
　ｋａａａａａｈｈｈｈｈっ！」
source.english:
“…Keh…
keh, ka…
kaaaaaah!”

source.japanese: 皆思わず耳を塞いだ。それくらい聞き苦しく不快で惨めな悲鳴だった。人間の声ですらなかった。思えばクロが舌足らずだったのも当然で、元々が人の言葉を喋るような生き物ではない。かといって今更本来の音で啼こうにも、その喉は人のもの、鳥の声艶[つや]やかに長く伸ばすようには造られておらず、クロはどちらの声、言葉であろうと不自由でしかないのだろう。クロ、ミュルメコレオンの悲哀を宿すもの。
source.english: Everyone involuntarily covered their ears. The scream was that unpleasant, wretched, unbearable. Not even a human voice. Naturally Kuro's speech had faltered: she had never been a creature that spoke human language. Yet trying to cry in her original voice now was impossible too. Hers was a human throat, not made to draw out a bird's rich, long cry. Neither voice, neither language could give her freedom. Kuro bore the sorrow of the myrmecoleon.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……keh……, keh, caa─── CAAAAAWWWWW!」

All instinctively covered their ears. So unbearably unpleasant and miserable a cry was it. It was not even a human voice. Thinking about it, Kuro being tongue-tied was also only natural; she was not the sort of creature that spoke the human tongue by nature. With that said, even as she now tried to caw in the manner intrinsic to her being, that throat was human, never built to sustain the long, lustrous notes of birdsong, and no matter which voice or tongue Kuro were to use, she would surely never be fluent. Kuro, bearer of the Myrmecoleon's sorrow.

source.japanese:
啼いて、いやいやをして、涙を撒き散らして、息もできなくて、咳きこんで、悶えて、逃げようとして体をぶつけて、ここまで哀れな姿を、誰も手を貸そうというものはいなくて、というより呆気にとられていた。
　老人の話など与太半分に聞いていた上に、信天翁号の嵐を呼ぶ船長、といえば勇ましいが、嵐の時以外はてんで役に立たない少女を捕まえて、強い羽根だの偉大な知恵だの鴉[カラス]だの。老人の頭がいよいよトチ狂ったのではないかとやや引き気味に見たのも、仕方ない事だろう。
source.english:
Crying, shaking her head, scattering tears, unable to breathe, coughing, writhing, banging into things as she tried to flee—so pitiful, yet nobody helped. They were stunned. They had half-dismissed the old man's account as nonsense.
Now he spoke of strong wings, great wisdom and crows while tormenting the Albatross's storm-calling captain—an impressive title, but an utterly useless woman outside a storm. It was understandable that they watched with a little recoil, wondering if his mind had finally gone altogether.

source.japanese: ようやくショックから立ち上がった朔屋が、クロを老人から引き離してやれば、その手に縋[すが]りつく、非力な手のいとおしさ。頭を胸にかき抱いて、
source.english: At last Sakuya recovered from the shock and stood. He pulled Kuro away from the old man. How dear the powerless hands that clung to his. He pressed her head to his chest.

target.text: She cawed, shook her head, scattered tears all around her, couldn't even breathe, coughed fitfully, writhed in pain, slammed her body against things as she tried to escape, but it was not that there was nobody willing to lend a hand to her in such a piteous state; rather, they were simply all dumbfounded.

Not only had half the old man's story sounded like nonsensical ramblings to them, he had also grabbed the Storm-calling Captain of the Albatross, she whose nickname sounded so valiant yet when it didn't storm was a completely useless little girl, claiming she was a crow with mighty wings and great wisdom. It was perhaps also inevitable, then, that they seemed to recoil a bit, wondering if the old man's mind had finally snapped.

When Sakuya, who had at long last recovered from the shock and risen to his feet, pulled Kuro away from the old man, what pathos of that helpless hand, clinging to his. He pulled her head into a tight embrace against his chest,

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひでぇ……それ、全然クロのせいじゃないだろうが……」
source.english: “That's awful… None of that was Kuro's fault…”

source.japanese: 朔屋でさえ指摘できる論理の綻[ほころ]びを、しかし老人は平然と受けて流した、別のパラダイムで、それは神話、伝承の拠って立つところのもので。
source.english: Even Sakuya could point out the flaw in his logic. The old man brushed it aside without concern, invoking another paradigm: the one upon which myths and legends stood.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「You're awful……that's clearly not Kuro's fault at all……」

There were open seams in his logic that even Sakuya could point out, but the old man calmly shrugged it off, for he operated in a different paradigm entirely, the very foundation upon which myth and legend stand.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「いいや。その鴉[カラス]のせいだな。神話・伝説の再構築には、遵守しなければならない事柄、順序といったものが存在する」
source.english: “No. It was the crow's fault. Reconstructing myths and legends requires certain matters, certain sequences, to be observed.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「そういった手順を踏まねば、記録は物語に、そして伝説には昇華し得ないのでな。
　儂の物語では、鳥が陸の証を持ち帰ることがなにより重要だった……」
source.english:
“Without following those procedures, a record cannot be raised into a story, and then a legend.
In my story, it was paramount that a bird bring back proof of land…”

source.japanese: ノアが放ち続けた鳥───鴉。
source.english: The bird Noah had kept releasing. A crow.

source.japanese:
その鴉[カラス]こそが、クロの正体。
　クロのクロウは、鴉のクロウ。
source.english:
That crow was Kuro. Her name,
Kuro, echoed ‘crow.’

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「お前は───陸地にたどり着けたのか？　儂らの至るべき、陸を───」
source.english: “Did you reach land? The land we were meant to arrive at…?”
“Crow…”

target.text: 【Noah】 「Oh no. That crow is entirely to blame. When reconstructing myth and legend, there exist matters and procedures that absolutely must be adhered to.」

【Noah】 「And without following those procedures, accounts cannot sublimate into stories, and subsequently into legends. In my story, a bird bringing home proof of land was the most important thing of all……」
The bird Noah continued to send forth───the crow.

That very crow was Kuro's true identity. The Kuro of Kuro's name came from crow. (TN: This might sound a bit redundant in English, but crow is "karasu" in Japanese, so the English word for crow is used here instead in the original text, where it is pronounced as "クロウ/Kurou", phonetically very close to "クロ/Kuro".)
【Noah】 「Did you───finally find land? The land we are meant to reach───」
【Noah】 「O crow───」

source.japanese: 真剣に、黒々とした渇望一色で塗りつぶし、語りかける老人を見ても、他の面子はやはり、信じられないでいたのだけれど、この時、クロの髪に変容が、朔屋が一度目にしたあの変容が、また生じていた。
source.english: The old man spoke in deadly earnest, his whole bearing steeped in dark craving. The others still could not believe him. But Kuro's hair was changing again, undergoing the transformation Sakuya had already seen.

source.japanese:
白い髪の中に浮いたのは小さな黒の斑[まだら]。
　見やる間に小指の先から短冊や小皿くらいの大きさに拡大し、数も二つ・三つ・四つとどんどん増えて後はもう数え果たさず。どんどん浮いて、だんだらに染まっていく。白の中に黒が、浮かび上がって。
source.english:
A little black patch appeared within the white.
Before their eyes it grew from the tip of a little finger to a strip of paper, a small plate. Two, three, four patches, then too many to count. More surfaced, staining it in irregular bands. Black rose within the white.

target.text: Even when they saw the old man address her with a voice so earnest, painted over in a single, jet-black shade of thirst, in the end, the rest of the crew still just couldn't believe it, but in that moment, a transformation in Kuro's hair, the very same transformation that Sakuya had already witnessed once before, was occurring again.

What surfaced within the white hair was a tiny black blotch. Before their very eyes, from the tip of a little finger to a tanzaku or a small plate, it expanded in size; there were two now, three, no, four, continuing to grow in size and number until they could no longer be counted. Emerging in rapid succession, gradually dying it in uneven blotches. Black emerged from within the white.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ク、クロ……っ。
　見つけた。知ってる。たくさん。
　だから、だからもう許して」
source.english:
“K-Kuro… found it.
Kuro knows. Lots.
So, so please forgive Kuro…”

source.japanese:
その黒い色合い自体は、最上の漆や黒蜜を思わせてとても綺麗ではあったけれども。
　それが斑[まだら]に白の中に散らかって、出鱈目な模様に染め抜いている様子は、お世辞にも綺麗とは言えず、それどころか奇病の症例のように見えた。
　信天翁号の船員達は、それまでクロがそのような変容を見せるなど知らず、この一時で老人の言葉が必ずしも絵空事ばかりではないのではないかと考え始めたのである。
source.english:
The black itself was beautiful, suggesting the finest lacquer or dark syrup.
But the way it lay scattered through the white, staining it in random patterns, could not be called beautiful by any stretch. It looked more like the symptoms of some strange disease.
The Albatross sailors had never known Kuro could change like this. In that moment they began wondering if the old man's words were not wholly fanciful.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Ku-, Kuro……. Found. Learned of. A lot. So-, so please just forgive Kuro.」

That shade of black itself was beautiful, the sort that brought to mind the deepest of jet blacks or dark brown sugar syrup, however. When it was scattered in blotches amidst a sea of white, and in such a haphazard pattern at that, even as flattery, it could not be called beautiful; on the contrary, it looked like a case of a rare disease. Hitherto, the crew of the Albatross had never known that Kuro could undergo such a change in appearance, and this moment was what made them begin to think that perhaps the old man's tale might not necessarily be a pipe dream in its entirety.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロの呪い、といて───！」
source.english: “Lift Kuro's curse…!”

source.japanese: 老人に縋[すが]りつこうとするも、触れられるのも厭だと言わんばかりにノアは、クロの額を手で押し返すものだから、白子の少女の脚ばかりが空しく床を掻[か]く、それでも少女は何度でも縋[すが]ろうとする、今の自分をこうしてしまったのが老人なら、哀願するしかないではないか、と。
source.english: She tried to cling to him. Noah pressed her forehead back with one hand, as though loath even to be touched. The albino woman's feet merely scraped the floor in vain. Still she tried again and again. If he had made her this way, what could she do but beg him?

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Lift Kuro's curse───!」

Even when she tried clinging to him, Noah simply pushed Kuro back by the forehead with his hand as if he couldn't stand even being touched by her, leaving the albino girl's legs to merely scrabble against the floor in vain, and yet she still tried to cling to him, over and over again, for if it was this old man who had turned her current self into what it now was, then what else could she do but plead with him.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「是非もない。儂も、お前を呪い続けるより、今はただ陸に臨みたいのみ───」
source.english: “Nothing for it. Rather than keep cursing you, I now wish only to stand upon land…”

target.text: 【Noah】 「Needs must. Rather than upholding this curse upon you, right now, I desire only to look upon the land───」

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「その為には、儂の海図が必要でな。海図に陸の位置と針路を書き込んでようやく───嵐も終わりを告げるだろう」
source.english: “For that, I need my chart. Only once the land's position and the course are written upon it… will the storm end.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「そして、儂らの長きにわたる漂流も、終わりを迎えるだろう」
source.english: “Then our long drifting, too, will end.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「で、まあついでを言うなら、
　そうしてくれたなら、儂、あの大海蛇、どうにかしてやってもよろしいかなぁ、などと愚考いたす次第」
source.english:
“And, incidentally,
should you do that, I might see my way to doing something about that great sea serpent. Such is my humble thought.”

source.japanese:
茶目っ気の、付け足しのように漏らした言葉だったが、当然一行は、一面針と溶岩で塞がれた荒野の中に、一筋の脱出航路を見いだしたように色めき立つ訳で。
　朔屋は、だが、この老人のぐるぐると変わる雰囲気に胡散臭さを禁じ得ず、なにしろ遙かな世界の悲哀を語るかと思えばクロのような小さな相手に憎悪と怨念を滾[たぎ]らせ、そして今はむずがゆいような茶目っ気の、こういう情緒が安定しない者をまともにするとろくな事がないというのを、皆どうして判らないだろう。普段から自分の事を見ているくせに、とどうにも乗り切れないのであったが。
source.english:
He added it almost playfully, as an afterthought. Naturally the company brightened, as if discovering a single escape route through a wilderness covered in needles and lava.
Sakuya, however, could not shake his suspicion at the old man's changing manner. One moment he spoke the grief of a distant world, the next boiled with hatred and resentment toward someone as small as Kuro; now came this irritating playfulness. Why did nobody understand that taking such emotionally unstable people seriously led to trouble? They looked at him every day, after all. He could not quite join their enthusiasm.

target.text: 【Noah】 「And for that purpose, my nautical chart is necessary. When the position of the land and a course is marked on that chart, at long last─── the storm, too, will herald its end.」
【Noah】 「Thus, our long journey adrift shall finally reach its end.」

【Noah】 「And, while we're on the subject, if you would get that for me, perhaps it might please you if I were to go and sort out that whole giant sea serpent problem for you; such is the humble conclusion my foolish mind has arrived at.」

They were playful remarks, uttered as if he was attaching a little bonus, but naturally, as if a lone path of escape had just been discovered in a wasteland entirely covered in needles and lava, the entire group was suddenly buzzing with excitement.

Sakuya, on the other hand, could not help but feel suspicious of this old man's ever-shifting demeanour; after all, just as it seemed he was going to regale them with tales of the sorrow of a distant world, he was then seething with bitter resentment and deep-seated loathing towards a little girl like Kuro, and then there was this unsettling playfulness now; why was it that none of the others could understand that nothing good would ever come from seriously engaging with someone so emotionally unstable? And that was despite them seeing what he was like every single day; that thought left him utterly unable to go along with it.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「爺、そりゃ本当だろうな。
　今更嘘で俺らを釣ったなら───」
source.english:
“Old man, that had better be true.
If you're luring us with lies now…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Must be the truth you're telling there, old man. Because if it turns out you reeled us in with a lie───」

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「どうとってもらっても構わないのだがね。
　ただ、あの生き物を今まで封じておったのは儂だ。なにしろ、お前らが島に来てもすぐには出てこなかっただろ、アレ」
source.english:
“Believe whatever you like.
But I kept that creature confined until now. It didn't appear the moment you reached the island, did it?”

target.text: 【Noah】 「Interpret it however you like, it matters not to me. However, it was I who kept that creature sealed away until now. As you know, even when you people came to the island, that thing didn't show itself right away, did it?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「確かに……」
source.english: “True…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Certainly……」

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「それで、だ。そのためには」
source.english: “And so, for that…”

source.japanese: その為には、海図で針路を示してやることが必要なのだと、老人はクロを突き返しながら。そうすれば元は方舟である島は陸地に辿り着けて、安らかに眠れるのだ、と。
source.english: They had to mark the course upon the chart, he said, pushing Kuro away. Then the island, formerly an ark, could reach land and sleep peacefully.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「海図だぁ……？
　気に入りの枕とかでなくってか」
source.english:
“A chart…?
Not a favorite pillow or something?”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「ああ、そうだ。だが、その海図をどこにやってしまったのかが、わからないのだよ」
source.english: “Yes. But I don't know where I've put the chart.”

target.text: 【Noah】 「So then. For that purpose.」

For that purpose, they would need to mark a course on the nautical chart, the old man said while shoving Kuro back at Sakuya. Once that was done, the island, which was originally an ark, could finally reach land, then rest in peace, he said.
【Naomasa】 「A chart……? Sure you don't also want your favorite pillow while we're at it?」
【Noah】 「Yes, a chart. However, I know not where I put that nautical chart.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ふぅん。海図。
　それでしたら、見覚えがあってよ」
source.english:
“Hmm. A nautical chart.
I believe I've seen one.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え、あれ、泪さん、
　あなた、いたのかここに」
source.english:
“Huh? Ms. Rui?
You were here?”

source.japanese:
朔屋のみならず、他の面子も同様に、失礼ながら仰天の、泪はそれまで一言も口を挟まず下級水夫達の中に混じっていたのだ。
　まるで、ノアの話になど興味もない、と言いたげに。
source.english:
Not merely Sakuya but the others were, impolitely, astonished. Rui had been among the junior sailors without interjecting a single word.
As if to declare no interest in Noah's tale.

source.japanese:
それで泪が語るらく。
　例の、彼女が散策中に出くわした、塔屋とその中に置かれていた海図の事。
　たいして興味もない事なのか、言葉短かに語ったのが、却って装飾もなく、簡素な織物の筋を辿るように、簡潔に要領を伝えたが、その塔屋の話を聞いて、噴き出したノアもノアであろう。
source.english:
She described the rooftop chamber she had found on her walk,
and the chart inside it. Perhaps from lack of interest, she spoke briefly.
That left the account unadorned, like following the threads of plain cloth: concise and clear. Noah being Noah, however, he burst into laughter at the mention of the chamber.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Hmm. A chart. In that case, I recall seeing one.」
【Naomasa】 「Uh, wait, Rui-san, were you here with us?」

It wasn't Sakuya alone. The rest of the crew were, if you will pardon my rudeness, just as utterly dumbstruck as he, for until then, Rui had been blending in with the deck boys, refraining from interjecting even a single time. It was as though she was all but saying that she held no interest in the likes of Noah's tale.

And then Rui told her own tale. Of the tower she had come across during her stroll, as well as the aforementioned nautical chart placed within it. She must not have found it very interesting, for the words she spoke were brief, but that very brevity only stripped it of any ornamentation in turn, and like tracing the threads of a plain weave, she succinctly conveyed the essentials, but it was also very like Noah to suddenly burst into laughter upon hearing that tale of a tower.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「鳩の羽根が散らばった、部屋なあ。
　そうかあいつめ、あいつが持って籠もっていたか。じゃあ見つからんわけだ」
source.english:
“A room scattered with dove feathers…
Ah, so that's who had it, shut away in there. No wonder I couldn't find it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだよ、誰がどうやって、だよ。
　この島、あんたが造ったんだろ。
　それで見つからないってのは、
　うさん臭くないか」
source.english:
“Who did what?
You built this island, didn't you?
Isn't it suspicious that you
can't find it?”

source.japanese: 先ほどノアに抱いた印象をどうしても引きずっているし、お大事のクロを虐めてくれた事もあるしで、朔屋はどうしてもこの老人に心を許す気になれず、クロは背後に隠す、自分の心も猜疑心に鎧[よろ]うで、老人を指摘したのだが。
source.english: Sakuya could not discard his earlier impression of Noah. Besides, the man had tormented his precious Kuro. He could not bring himself to trust him. Keeping Kuro behind him, armoring his own heart with suspicion, he challenged the old man.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「その骨はな、儂の妻のものだよ。
　晩年、哀しい事に折り合いがあまり良くなくてな。あれはあれで、一人で引き籠もってしまいおった」
source.english:
“Those bones belong to my wife.
Sadly, toward the end we did not get along very well. She shut herself away alone.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「儂が近づけないような、そういうセキュリテイでも拵[こしら]えたんだろう。船のセキュリティの設計担当だったからな、あれは」
source.english: “She must have devised security to keep me from approaching. The ship's security design was her responsibility.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ちなみに不仲の原因は」
source.english: “…Incidentally, why didn't you get along?”

source.japanese: そういう余計な事に突っ込む朔屋も朔屋だが、けろりと堪える老人も、どこかがやはり突き抜けていた。
source.english: Sakuya was Sakuya, prying into unnecessary matters. The old man, answering blithely, was somehow beyond ordinary bounds as well.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「好みの不一致だ。儂は鴉[カラス]を好み、妻は鳩[ハト]を好んだ。夫婦であっても、お互い譲れんことはあるわいな」
source.english: “Different tastes. I favored crows; my wife, doves. Even married people have things they won't yield upon.”

source.japanese: と、そこまではまだ、笑い飛ばせ無くもない、微妙な間合いにあったのだが───
source.english: Up to that point, the matter still hovered at the delicate threshold of something one might laugh off. But—

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「ああ、それなら判る。
　ここからのルートは───おや」
source.english:
“Ah, I know the place,
then. The route from here… Oh.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おやってなんだよおやって。
　なんか良い予感しないよ、
　さっさと言ってくれ」
source.english:
“What do you mean, ‘oh’?
I've got a bad feeling.
Just tell us.”

target.text: 【Noah】 「A room littered with dove feathers, was it? Of course, so it was her, that sly woman was the one who took it and hid herself away, huh? So that's why I couldn't find it.」
【Naomasa】 「What are you talking about, who did what and how? You're the one who built this island, right? So isn't it a little fishy that you couldn't find it?」

Unable to rid himself of the impression Noah had given him earlier, and also because he had tormented his precious Kuro, Sakuya simply could not bring himself to relax his guard around this old man; hiding Kuro behind his back, his own heart clad in the armour of suspicion, he made pointed comments at the old man.
【Noah】 「Those bones, they belong to my wife. Much to my sorrow, we didn't really see eye to eye in her final years. Her being who she was, she ended up confining herself away, all alone.」
【Noah】 「She must have set up some kind of security measures that would keep me away. She was the woman responsible for designing the ship's security system, you see.」
【Naomasa】 「……By the way, what was the cause for the discord?」
Sakuya was one thing for poking his nose into such unnecessary business as he was wont to, but the old man, who took it entirely in stride, was himself, in some respects, out of this world.
【Noah】 「A clash of tastes. I preferred crows, my wife preferred doves. Even between husband and wife, there are some things you just can't compromise on.」
Up to this point, things remained in that delicate territory where it was not impossible to simply laugh it off, but───
【Noah】 「Aah, I know where to head then. The route from here is───oh dear.」
【Naomasa】 「And what's "oh dear" supposed to mean? I don't have a good feeling about this, just spit it out already.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「朔屋、なにてめえが仕切ってんだ。
　で、なんなんだよ爺」
source.english:
“Sakuya, who put you in charge?
Well, old man? What is it?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Sakuya, why the hell do you think you're in charge here? So, what is it, old man?」

source.japanese:
そして老人は、泪の説明のように、簡潔に告げた。
　泪が示した、海図の塔屋がある建物には、どうしても大海蛇が陣取る合流点を通っていかなければならない、と。
source.english:
The old man explained as briefly as Rui had. To reach the building with the chart's rooftop chamber,
they would have to pass the junction occupied by the serpent.

target.text: Thus, in the same manner as Rui's explanation, the old man informed them succinctly. That to make it to the building with the tower containing that chart Rui had spoken of, they absolutely had to pass through the intersection that the great sea serpent was occupying.

source.japanese: 一同に降りかかった沈黙の意味を計りかねたか、クロが迷路に突っ込まれてそもそもそこでなにをすればいいのかが判らない鼠のように、まだ恐怖の涙に潤む眼差しをしょぼつかせる。朔屋はとりあえず、鍵の掛かった箱があって、でもその錠を開ける鍵は、箱の中に入ってるんだと喩えを借りて説明してやると、納得したのかしないのか、ただ朔屋に身をすり寄せて、うん、と頷[うなず]く、青年しか今は心を許せる相手がいないかのように。
source.english: Unable to judge the meaning of the silence descending upon them, Kuro blinked her terror-wet eyes like a mouse put into a maze without even knowing what it was meant to do. Sakuya explained by analogy: there was a locked box, but the key to its lock was inside the box. Whether she understood or not, she merely nestled against him and nodded. As though he alone could now be trusted.

source.japanese:
そして、そこに、ノアだった。
　今偶さか想い出したかのように、しかし機を狙ったように、ノアだった。
source.english:
And there was Noah.
As though he had happened to remember just now. Yet as if he had been waiting for his moment. Noah.

target.text: Perhaps she was struggling to work out the significance of the silence that had fallen upon them all, for like a mouse shoved into a labyrinth without the first clue of what to do in the first place, Kuro's eyes grew bleary with tears of fear once more. For now, Sakuya tried explaining it to her using an analogy: imagine there being a locked box, but the key to open that lock is within the box itself; whether she understood it or not, she just snuggled up to Sakuya, nodding with a soft "yeah", as if the young man was the only person she could trust right now.
And then, right there, was Noah. As if he had just happened to remember it now by chance, yet also as if he had waited for the perfect moment, Noah said:

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「なにを鴉[カラス]といちゃついているんだこの変態。
　お前、暢気に比喩的表現なんぞを用いておるが、あれを放ったのは自分とその鴉[カラス]だと言う事、判っていないだろう？」
source.english:
“What are you doing, flirting with a crow, you pervert?
Leisurely using analogies like that—you don't realize it was you and that crow who released the creature, do you?”

target.text: 【Noah】 「What are you doing flirting with a crow, you degenerate. You sit there casually playing around with little figures of speech, but you don't seem to realize that the ones who released that thing are none other than you yourself and that crow, do you?」

source.japanese: ───場の沈黙の重さが、朔屋とそしてクロにのみ集中した。
source.english: The weight of the room's silence concentrated upon Sakuya and Kuro alone.

target.text: ───The oppressive weight of the silence in the room was concentrated solely on Sakuya and Kuro.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……てめえかよ、朔屋」
source.english: “…You, Sakuya?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え、ちょっと待って、俺にはなんの事やら、
　心当たりも……」
source.english:
“Wait. I don't know what you're talking about.
Nothing comes to mind…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……So it was you, Sakuya.」
【Naomasa】 「Huh, wait a second, whatever it is I've done, I've got no clue what……」

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「ほほー……あの汚水溜まったドーム。
　あすこの水門を開けた覚えもないと」
source.english:
“Ohh… You don't remember opening the sluice
in that dome full of foul water?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、覚えてるよ。だってあれ豪[えら]い硬くて、
　手の皮が剥けそうに───いたいっ」
source.english:
“Well, I remember.
It was so stiff I nearly tore the skin off my hands… Ow!”

target.text: 【Noah】 「Oh-hoh……that dome filled with unclean water. Are you saying you don't recall opening the slide gate there?」
【Naomasa】 「Oh no, I remember that. I mean, that thing was so stupidly stiff, it felt like the skin on my hands was about to peel right───ow!」

source.japanese:
肩を掴んだ万力は、シサムの手。
　睨みつける眸[ひとみ]に出会って、朔屋は悲鳴を上げ損ねた。瞋恚でザウエルより燃えていた。乳や臀に性的な悪戯を仕掛けた時の怒声や拳足は、優しく親しい微笑みのようなものなのだと知った、今知って知らなければ良かったと後悔した。
source.english:
The vise clamped upon his shoulder was Sisam's hand.
Meeting her glare, he failed even to scream. It burned with wrath fiercer than Zauer. Her shouts and blows when he played sexual tricks upon her breasts and backside had been gentle, friendly smiles by comparison. He knew that now, and wished he had not.

target.text: The vise gripping his shoulder was Shisamu's hand. When he met the eyes glaring at him, Sakuya failed to even scream. They blazed with a wrothful flame even brighter than the Sauers. Sakuya understood that the angry shouts, fists, and kicks sent flying his way whenever he made some playful sexual advances on their breasts and buttocks were like gentle, intimate smiles, and now that he knew, he deeply regretted obtaining this knowledge.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「使えない、使えないと思っていられるうちは、まだましだった、っていうことか」
source.english: “So it was better while we could still just think you useless.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Guess things were still better back when all I could think was how useless you were, huh?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「早く船に戻って手当てしてあげないと、この子、死んじゃうかもしれないのに……朔屋さんの、せいだ」
source.english: “We've got to get back to the ship and treat him, or he might die… It's your fault, Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「We need to get back to the ship quickly and treat his injuries, or this guy might actually die…… and that's all Sakuya-san's fault.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……この人は、単に巡り合わせが悪いだけ。
　そのお陰で、刺されたり海に放りこまれたりしたけれど」
source.english:
“…He merely has unfortunate luck.
Which got him stabbed and thrown into the sea…”

source.japanese: 航海士ばかりではない。日頃は朔屋に厚意的な者達までも、見下げたような眼差しで、
source.english: Not only the navigators. Even those usually well disposed toward him looked down upon him.

target.text: 【Rui】 「……This man was simply dealt nothing but poor hands by fate. Owing to that, he was stabbed and thrown into the sea.」
It was not just the first mate. Even all those who usually treated Sakuya with kindness looked at him with contempt in their eyes,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「きっちりそん時にくたばってりゃよかったんだ」
source.english: “Should've damn well died then.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Would have been better if you'd dropped dead right then and there.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんだって余計なことをすんだよ、あんたらはさぁ……」
source.english: “Why do you two have to do things you shouldn't…?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Why the hell do you two always have to go and make things worse……」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「違うの。クロは、みんなにほめてもらいたかっただけ」
source.english: “No. Kuro only wanted everyone to praise Kuro.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「That's not right. Kuro just wanted to be praised by everybody,」

source.japanese:
言葉を失い立ち尽くす朔屋を庇[かば]うように。
　そもそも一連の結果を招く行動の端を解いたのは、朔屋であるのに。クロが、前に出る、のも滅多にない事。たとえば航海士はそんなにひどくは当たらないし、時々は笑ってくれる人だけれど、やはりクロにとっては厳しく恐いお姉さん。
　けれども、とクロは食い下がった。
　いつもは良く判らなくって失敗する。
　今回もそうかも知れない。
　でも今回は、誰かに言いつけられた仕事を失敗したんじゃない。
　今回は───
source.english:
As though shielding the speechless Sakuya.
He had begun the actions that brought these consequences. Kuro stepping forward was rare. The navigators did not treat her terribly; sometimes they even smiled.
Still, they were stern, frightening older sisters to her. Yet she persisted.
Usually she failed because she did not understand.
Perhaps this time too.
But this time she had not failed
at a task someone assigned her. This time…

target.text: As if to protect Sakuya, who had been rendered both speechless and motionless. Even though the one who had originally set the wheels in motion on the chain of events that had led to this outcome was Sakuya. Kuro stepped forward, a rare thing. Even if, for example, the first mate had never treated her that harshly, and was someone who would occasionally smile at her, in the end, she was still a strict, scary lady to Kuro.

But even so, Kuro thought, refusing to back down. Usually, she wouldn't understand things too well and make mistakes. And that might be the case this time too. But this time, she hadn't failed at a task somebody else had ordered her to do. This time───

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロは、馬鹿にされたり、怒られたりするの、やだっただけ」
source.english: “Kuro just didn't want to be laughed at or scolded.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro was just fed up with being made fun of or getting yelled at.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「それが、いけない、かったの？
　クロは、どうすれば、よかったのかなぁ」
source.english:
“Was that… wrong?
What should Kuro have done?”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロは、みんなみたいになりたいって、
　思っちゃ、だめだったのかな」
source.english:
“Wasn't Kuro allowed to want
to be like everyone?”

source.japanese:
クロがいつになく必死だったのは、それが少女のせめてもの、願いとか夢だとか。
　そういった、彼女のお大事の『きらきら』と同じくらい、いやそれ以上に大切にしたいもので、朔屋に教えもらったものだからで、それがあれば、みんなの中で哀しい気持ちにならなくってすむ、惨めな思いで物陰で蹲[うずくま]っていなくってすむ、と。
　それは、大それた願いだったのかどうか、クロにはよく判らない。
　クロは、なにを願った事など、なかったから。あるとすれば、嵐の中の自分でいたいと言う事だけれど、それだって結局はこの願いの別の現れでしかない。
　願わない、夢も抱かないクロが、ずっと心の底に秘めていた思い。
source.english:
She was unusually desperate because this was her modest wish, her dream.
Something to cherish as much as her treasured sparkly things—more than them. Sakuya had taught it to her. With it she would not have to feel sad among the others, or crouch miserably in a corner.
Whether it was an extravagant wish, she did not know.
Kuro had never wished for anything. Except to remain her storm-time self, but that was merely another form of the same desire.
The thought she had hidden deep within, she who never wished, never dreamed.

source.japanese:
拳に爪を食いこませている朔屋がいる。彼にもう少し握力があって、剛毅な心を持っていたなら、血を滲ませた掌で、クロを抱いて庇[かば]っていたかも知れない。あるいは皆に殴りかかっていったかも知れない。
　しかしこの時、朔屋にはそういった強い心もなかったし、なにしろ事の張本人なので、クロの哀しいくらい真摯な訴えを、そしてそれが現実と衝突して瓦解していく様を、半笑いで見守っているしかなかった訳で。
source.english:
Sakuya dug his nails into his fists. Had his grip and his spirit been a little stronger, he might have held Kuro protectively, blood seeping from his palms.
Or attacked the others. Just then he possessed no such strength. Besides, he had caused the trouble himself. So he could only watch with a half-smile as her painfully earnest appeal collided with reality and crumbled.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Was that bad? What should Kuro have done then?」
【Kuro】 「Maybe Kuro thinking that Kuro wanted to be like the rest was wrong?」

Kuro was so unwontedly desperate because this was the girl's sole wish, her sole dream. And that was something she wanted to cherish just as much as, no, even more than her precious "sparklies", for it was something she had been taught by Sakuya, and as long as she had that, she would be spared from feeling miserable while with the others, would no longer have to cower in the shadows with a head full of wretched thoughts.

Whether that was too grand a wish for her, Kuro didn't really know. For Kuro had never wished for anything. If there was one thing, it was only that she wanted to be the self she was during a storm, but even that, in the end, was merely a different manifestation of this very same wish. A desire that Kuro, who never wished for or dreamt of anything, had always harboured down in the deepest reaches of her heart.

There Sakuya was, digging his fingernails into his clenched fists. Had he but a slightly stronger grip, were he but possessed of a resolute heart, then perhaps he might have held Kuro in his blood-stained palms and protected her. Or perhaps he might have begun swinging his fists at them all. But in this moment, Sakuya was not possessed of such a stout heart, and since he was the man responsible for this, all he could do was watch how Kuro's heartrendingly sincere pleas clashed with reality and crumbled away, a faint smile on his face.

source.japanese:
───半笑い？
　
　クロの哀訴を、砕かれる様を、半笑い？
　
　そうとも朔屋はへらへら笑っていた。
　きっと次は誰かが、こう言うぞ。
　自分のやる事に責任持て。
　とかそういう事だ。
source.english:
A half-smile?
At Kuro's pleading, at the way she was being broken?
Yes. Sakuya smiled foolishly.
Someone would surely say it next:
take responsibility for what you
do. Something like that.

target.text: ───A faint smile? Kuro's pleas were being crushed before him, and he smiled at that? Damn right Sakuya had a foolish grin on his lips. For he was certain someone would say this next: Take responsibility for your actions. Or something like that.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「お前は知らなければならなかった。
　願う、祈るだけならいい。
　ただし、行動したならば。
　それがどういう意図であろうとも」
source.english:
“You should have known.
Wishing, praying—fine.
But once you've acted,
whatever your intention…”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「その行動の責任を取らなくてはならないことを、クロ、お前は知るべきだった」
source.english: “You have to answer for that action. Kuro, you should have known.”

source.japanese:
ほら、ござった。
　あまりに予想通りで、朔屋はもう大笑いしたくなったが、こらえる術は知っていた。彼自身が何度となく通過した道だったから、身の御し様は知っていた。
　挫折、躓き、青春の蹉跌とかなんだとか。さんざん経験してきて、落ち着いた結論は、ここらへんの足許に転がった石っころで転んで、立ち上がれる人間ばかりでは……ああ、もういいや。
source.english:
There it was. So utterly predictable that Sakuya wanted to laugh aloud.
But he knew how to contain it. He had passed along this road often enough to know how to govern himself.
Setbacks, stumbles, the failures of youth or whatever. Plenty of experience, and the conclusion he had reached was that not everyone who tripped upon a stone lying around their feet could get back up… Ah, forget it.

source.japanese:
俯いて、肩をそばだてボロボロと、ついに声もなく涙ばかりを零し始めたクロの肩を抱き寄せる。もう、皆の目を憚[はばか]るつもりもなかった。なにしろ、クロにこうしていいのは、こうしてやれるのは、そう自分だけ。信天翁号の中では新前の自分だが、他の皆にはこんな事、させてやらない。
　そもそもできまい。
source.english:
He drew Kuro's shoulders to him. Her head lowered, shoulders hunched, tears finally falling without a sound. He no longer intended to be wary of the others' eyes. He alone was allowed to do this for her. He alone could. A newcomer to the Albatross, but he would not let the others do such a thing.
They could not, anyway.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（何故ってあんた達は、やってやれる人間だからな……俺やクロとは違うもんな……）
source.english: (Because you're people who can make things happen… Not like me and Kuro…)

source.japanese:
凄まじいまでの弱者としての自覚。
　朔屋のある意味強靱な点は、これを抱いていて、酒だ女だと笑っていられる点にあるが、だからといって彼の弱さが克服される訳でも無能が改善される訳でもない。朔屋の無能は巡り合わせが引き寄せるところも大きいけれど、それだけに改善しきれないところもある。
source.english:
An overwhelming awareness of his own weakness.
In one sense, Sakuya's strength was his ability to know that and still laugh over drink and women. It did not conquer his weakness or cure his incompetence. Much of that incompetence arose from sheer ill luck, which made it all the harder to correct.

source.japanese:
朔屋はクロの中に、自分と同じものを見いだしていた。水夫長や航海士、泪には最後まで理解しきる事のできない、弱きものの卑屈なまでのいじましさ、これとこの先どう付き合っていくのか、教示してやれるのはこの船に於いては自分だけだろうと朔屋は、しゃくり上げるクロの肩を抱いて、とりあえずは皆から少し離してやる事にする。
　こういう時には、大勢の体熱や息づかいだけで、自分が死んでしまいたいほど惨めな生き物に思えてくるから。
　隣の部屋に移ろうとする朔屋とクロに、何か言いかけた水夫長へ、
source.english:
He had found in Kuro what he knew in himself: the cringing, almost servile desperation of the weak, something Long, the navigators and Rui could never fully understand. Probably he alone aboard could teach her how to live with it. Holding her sobbing shoulders, he decided first to take her a little way from the others.
At such times, the heat and breath of a crowd alone could make one feel a creature so miserable one wished to die.
As they moved toward the next room, the boatswain began to say something.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……すんませんです。俺ら、ちょっと考え無しでした。あの、後で何やればいいか、聞きますんで」
source.english: “…Sorry. We didn't think it through. I'll ask what we should do afterward…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんで、今はクロだけでも、ちょっと落ち着かせてくるんで」
source.english: “For now, I'll just go and settle Kuro down a little.”

source.japanese:
正直、なにをやらされるかは大体見当が付いている。それを思うと怖ろしくて仕方ない。怖い事はさっさと聞いてしまった方が良いけれど、今はとにかくクロを慰めておかないと。
　朔屋はひたすら卑屈に阿[おもね]って、続きの部屋にとクロと自分を皆の目から隔離する。
source.english:
Honestly, he had a fairly good idea what they would be made to do. Thinking of it terrified him. Better to hear frightening things promptly, but first he must comfort Kuro.
He fawned abjectly, withdrawing himself and her from everyone's gaze into the adjoining room.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You should have known. Just wishes or prayers are fine. However, once you act. No matter what your intentions may be.」
【Bosun】 「Kuro, you should have known that you have to take responsibility for your actions.」

See, right on cue. It was all so utterly predictable that Sakuya already wanted to burst out laughing, but he knew how to keep it inside. This was a road he himself had traveled down many a time, so he had learned to control himself. Failures, missteps, the setbacks of youth and whatnot. Having been through it all, the sober conclusion he'd come to was this: when people stumble over a stray pebble at their feet, not everyone can just pick themselves right back up……aah, enough of that.

He threw an arm around Kuro, who was hanging her head, hunching her shoulders, and had at last begun to shed nothing but silent tears, then pulled her close.
