Yet another timber dropped with a thud exactly where Sakuya and Kuro had just risen; then the fall became a cascade. Had something pierced a weakness in the structures' core? Or had the incoming blow carried such extraordinary force? Whatever the answer, it had not struck the serpent directly—and yet it proved fatal.

source.japanese:
朔屋達を外して降った材木は、大海蛇に対しては破砕され、ぎざぎざと出来損ないの、しかし却ってひどい傷を残す槍のように降り注ぎ、その粘膜に覆われた肌に、垂直に突き立ったのだ。大概の打撃や斬撃なら、肌を覆う粘膜が逸らすか絡め取るかでこの生き物に大きな傷を与えるまでには至らない。
　しかしこの時、刀の用法で言えば『刃筋が立った』状態で、角材、柱材、梁材が次々と大海蛇に降り注いで、これには天然の防御膜も抗しようがなかった。
　偶然、といえばもちろん偶然。しかしそう言い切れないほどの執拗さがあった。
　まるで、木造の建築物群が、鬱憤を晴らしているかのように。
source.english:
The timbers that missed Sakuya and Kuro shattered into ragged, ill-made spears, all the more vicious for their irregularity, and plunged straight into the serpent's slime-covered skin. Ordinarily that film would deflect a blow or entangle a cutting edge before it could do the creature serious harm.
This time, however, beams, posts and squared timbers fell one after another with what a swordsman would call true edge alignment. Against that, the natural defense was powerless. Coincidence?
Of course. Yet the assault possessed a persistence that made coincidence difficult to believe.
It was as though the wooden buildings were venting a long-held grievance.

source.japanese: 人間の生などとは時間感覚からして異なる時間を生き延びてきた大海蛇にしても、感じた事のない苦痛、苦痛など知らなかった生き物に、これは生命に関わる危険との警告を乱打する。筋肉が締まる、躍動する、しかしもはや獲物を追い詰めるより、苦痛に反射しての狂乱の踊り、蛇体が呪術に用いる文字のように妖しい曲線を様々に描いて、悶える、仰け反る、丸まる、収縮する、訳も分からず逃げ出す朔屋達の背後で。
source.english: The sea serpent had survived across ages utterly unlike a human lifespan. Now it felt a pain it had never known. A creature ignorant of pain was battered with warnings that its life was in danger. Muscles tightened and leaped, no longer to corner prey, but in a frenzied dance of reflex. The serpentine body traced uncanny curves like the characters of a sorcerer's script: writhing, arching, coiling, contracting, behind Sakuya and Kuro as they fled without understanding anything.

target.text: Starting with that beam, the collapse of the wooden houses began. If Noah's words were to believed, these wooden buildings should have had no issues withstanding any paltry corrosion or impacts. And there, right where Sakuya and Kuro had just been getting up, another piece of square timber fell with a crash, and by now, it was raining down on them in a chain reaction; perhaps there was a structurally weak core that had been pierced through, or maybe the impact that had come flying in just harboured so immense a force? In any case, though it never struck the beast directly, it still sealed the great sea serpent's fate.

The falling timber that had missed Kuro and Sakuya instead shattered against the great sea serpent, raining down on it like jagged, defective spears, but their splintered nature only made them leave wounds all the more terrible in their wake, thrust vertically through its skin covered in a mucous membrane. Most blunt strikes or slashes would either be diverted from or caught in the mucous membrane covering its skin, leaving them unable to cause any grave injury to this creature.

However, right now, in a state where, if described through terms of sword technique, 『the Hasuji was perfectly aligned』, the square timber, the posts, and the beams hailed down upon the great sea serpent one after another, and this was something its natural defensive membrane could never hope to defy. A coincidence? Yes, of course it was a coincidence. But it fell with such persistence that it was difficult to state so with confidence. It was almost as if the cluster of wooden buildings were venting their pent-up anger. (TN: Hasuji is a term in Japanese sword technique that refers to the alignment of the cutting edge.)

Even in this great sea serpent, which had survived through a span of time utterly alien to the perception of time shared by puny man, faced with an agony the likes it had never felt, a suffering the likes it never knew existed, the warning bells were battered with reckless abandon, informing the creature that this was a life-threatening danger.

Its muscles tightened, throbbed powerfully, but this was no longer to chase down its prey, it was a frenzied dance of reflexive responses to pain; its serpentine body traced a wide array of bewitchingly mysterious curves reminiscent of symbols used in magical incantations, writhed in agony, bent backwards, curled up, contracted, all behind the backs of Sakuya and Kuro who were fleeing without the first clue as to what was going on.

source.japanese:
電撃が走る、幾度も走る、紫煙が立ち籠める。だがもはや、撃たれて喪神する獲物もなく、断末魔の足掻きとして。大海蛇の苦悶にあがく体は、次々に周囲の建物を倒壊させ、より深くそして建材の破砕の尖りでもって悠久を生き抜いた生命を埋めていく。
　最後に、瓦礫の隙間から閃光さえ迸[ほとばし]るほどの強烈な放電を放ったが、それこそ最期の吐息、最期の放電に、オゾン臭帯びた煙が立ちのぼる。
source.english:
Electricity flashed, again and again. Purple fumes gathered. But there was no prey left to strike senseless. These were its death throes. Its agonized body brought the surrounding buildings down one after another, burying deeper in their jagged timbers the life that had endured through eons.
At last it released a discharge so fierce that light burst through the gaps in the rubble. A final breath. A final discharge. Ozone-scented smoke rose.

target.text: Electricity surged, ran across its body time after time, enshrouding it in a purple smoke. However, this was also no longer to strike and stun any prey, but instead the desperate struggle of the creature in its final death throes. The body of the great sea serpent, flailing about in anguish, caused the surrounding buildings to collapse one after another; the life that had endured through eternal aeons was thus buried deeper and deeper beneath the sharp edges of shattered timber.

At the very end, it emitted so powerful a discharge that even flashes of light seemed to surge out from the gaps in the rubble, but that truly was its dying breath, its dying discharge, and smoke carrying the smell of ozone rose into the air.

source.japanese: 何故生き延びられたのか、喜びよりも不可解さが優るほどの突発的活あり得ない事態に、何とも間の抜けた顔で振り返る二人には、倒壊が大海蛇を狙って殺到しているようにしか見えなかった。安全圏まで離れてみると、排球の試合の様子を見るようにその様がよく判る。流れてきたオゾンの煙に顔をしかめ、見交わす二人の目には、放心の色すら合った。
source.english: The sudden, impossible turn left them more bewildered by survival than glad of it. They looked back with foolish faces. It could only seem that the falling buildings were converging on the serpent. From a safe distance they saw the pattern clearly, as one might see the play at a volleyball match. They grimaced at the drifting ozone smoke and exchanged dazed looks.

target.text: Faced with a situation so sudden and absurdly impossible that the incomprehensibility of it entirely eclipsed any joy at how they'd managed to somehow make it out alive, the two turned around with utterly dumbfounded expressions; to them, it looked like nothing less than the collapse converging en masse to target the great sea serpent. Once they stepped back to a safe distance, just like watching a volleyball match unfold, the entire scene became perfectly clear. Within the eyes of these two, wincing at the ozone smoke blowing their way, exchanging glances, was even a look of dazed absentmindedness.

source.japanese: 劫初の恐怖はかくして絶える───
source.english: And so the terror from the world's beginning came to an end—

target.text: Thus, the antediluvian terror became extinct───

source.japanese: 一方、朔屋とクロの、大海蛇との邂逅点から廃屋の家並みを幾重にも隔[へだ]たった、環礁内の桟橋に停泊した信天翁号の上甲板の上では。
source.english: Meanwhile, several ranks of abandoned houses away from the place where Sakuya and Kuro had met the serpent, on the upper deck of the Albatross, moored at the pier within the atoll—

target.text: Meanwhile, separated by row upon row of ruined houses from the point where Sakuya, Kuro, and the great sea serpent had their fated confrontation, on the upper deck of the Albatross anchored by the wooden jetty within the atoll.

source.japanese:
バラックの一つの横壁に、大穴が穿[うが]たれていた。羆が怒りに任せて突進したのではないかと疑わしい程の穴だが、しかしただの剛力では、穴を穿[うが]つ前にこんな組みが荒いバラックなど全体を崩落させるだろう。
　つまりよほどの瞬発的で指向性を有した力が板壁をぶち抜いたと見るべきだが、穴の縁の痕跡を鑑[かんが]みるに、どうやらその威力は内側から放たれたとしか考えられず。
source.english:
A great hole had been punched in the side of one shack. It looked as though an enraged brown bear had charged through. But mere brute force would have brought the entire loosely built shack down before making such a hole.
A force both sudden and tightly directed must have blasted through the boards. And judging by the marks around the edges, that force could only have come from inside.

target.text: A large hole had been gouged into the side wall of one of the shacks. A hole so suspiciously large it was likely to leave one wondering if perhaps a brown bear had barged through it in a fit of rage, however, sheer strength alone would surely cause the entire shack, poorly constructed as it was, to collapse before any holes could be made. In other words, it should be assumed that an immense, explosive force with clear directionality punched through the wooden wall, but taking into account the marks by the edge of the hole, it would be unthinkable for it be anything other than a force that had been unleashed from within.

source.japanese: と───ひょいと穴の内側から突き出されて、きょろきょろと辺りの人気を忍ぶように見回したは、とんと巣籠もりの黒貂が時季外れの餌探しに出る風情であったが、大小無数の木屑と埃を浴びて、それでもなお黒耀の艶[つや]失わぬ髪の、頭の一揺すりで汚れを振るい落とす、密航者の。
source.english: A head popped out of the hole and looked furtively around for signs of anyone nearby, much like a sable emerging from its den to seek food out of season. Countless wood chips and dust had settled in the hair, yet it retained its black, obsidian luster. A single shake dislodged the dirt. The stowaway.

source.japanese: 大海蛇に礫[つぶて]代わりに投げつけられて、いかがわしいレビューの、潤滑液塗されて桃色の光の下でぬらぬら肢体をくねらす踊り子嬢よろしくのたうっていた筈だが一体いつの間にここに、そして衣服にも肌にも粘液の名残もない、その謎の解明は後世に委ねずばなるまい。
source.english: She must have been hurled like a pebble at the sea serpent and left writhing like a dancer in a seedy revue, coated in lubricant, her glistening body twisting under pink light—but when had she ended up here? And how was there no trace of mucus on her clothing or skin? That mystery would have to be left to future generations to solve.

source.japanese:
それより問題なのは、バラックの穴の縁を跨[また]ぎ越した彼女の身のこなしが、周囲に人目のない事を確認してから、悠然としているのに無駄な力みの一切無い自然体となっていたこと。そして、けほ、と小さく優雅に漏らした咳や、髪の間に火薬の匂いを残していたこと。
　つまりはバラックに大穴穿[うが]った事態に、彼女の関与があったのは国語事典で『暗躍』の項を引くように明らかであり───
source.english:
The more pressing question was how she stepped over the edge of the hole. Having made sure nobody was watching, she moved at ease, unhurried and without a trace of wasted tension. And there was the little, elegant cough she gave, the smell of gunpowder lingering in her hair.
Her involvement in the shack's perforation was as plain as looking up 'covert action' in a dictionary.

target.text: And then───the way it suddenly popped out from within the hole, glancing around restlessly as if trying to conceal itself from any human presence in the vicinity, had the air of a sable, normally completely holed up in its den, venturing out to forage out of season, and though it was covered in dust and wood chips of all shapes and sizes, with a single shake of its head, that hair, which yet retained its lustre of gleaming obsidian, rid itself of the dust and grime; it was none other than the stowaway.

There was no mistaking that she had been hurled at the great sea serpent in place of a pebble, writhing and squirming like a dancer from some sleazy revue wriggling around her slippery limbs smeared in some manner of lubricant beneath the pink lights, so when in the world had she managed to make it here, not to mention there being no traces of any slimy mucus on her skin or her clothes either; the unravelling of that mystery, however, must be left to posterity.

The more pressing issue at hand was the fact that though the woman carried herself thus as she strode over the edge of the hole in the shack, after ensuring there were no watchful eyes around, she settled into a natural stance: completely composed, yet still entirely devoid of unnecessary tension. And then there was the fact that she was letting out small, dainty coughs, and that the smell of gunpowder lingered in her hair. In short, her involvement in whatever lead to this massive hole blasted through the shack was about as glaringly obvious as looking up the definition of 『behind-the-scenes』in the English dictionary and finding her name───

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……一発、つい撃っちゃった。
　ばれないよう、さてなんて誤魔化そう。
　やれやれ……」
source.english:
“…Went and fired a shot. Now,
how do I cover that up without anyone finding out?
Good grief…”

source.japanese:
どうやら彼女には好ましくない成り行きと見えたが、僅かに吊り上げた唇の形は弦月の秀麗、困じいってるくせに興がる機嫌が揺曳し、あるいは彼女の冴えた眸[ひとみ]には。
　朔屋の窮地が映っていたのかも知れない。
source.english:
She did not seem pleased by this turn of events. Yet her slightly upturned lips formed a lovely crescent moon; though plainly in trouble, she could not quite suppress her amusement.
Perhaps those keen eyes of hers had caught Sakuya's predicament.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「……Couldn't help but fire a shot. Now then, how to cover this up so nobody notices? Good grief……」

It didn't seem like this was a particularly favourable course of events to this woman, but the shape of her faintly raised lips held the exquisite beauty of the crescent moon, and despite her deeply troubled demeanor, an amused disposition flickered in and out of view, or perhaps it owed to what was depicted within her clear eyes. It might well have been a reflection of Sakuya's predicament.

source.japanese:
が、余裕はそこまで。
　ぱたり、と、背後に鳴った軽く乾いた響きに怪訝に振り返れば、バラックの壁板の一枚が倒れたところ。
　その一枚が引き金となって残りの壁も四方順繰りにぱたぱたぱたり、支えを失った癖して澄ましかえってボロ屋根が宙に留まっていたが、密航者の注視に今さら気づいたように慌てて落ちる間抜けもの。
source.english:
Her composure lasted no longer.
A light, dry patter sounded behind her. She turned in puzzlement: one plank of the shack's wall had fallen.
That triggered the remaining walls, which toppled in turn on all four sides, pat, pat, pat. With nothing holding it up, the decrepit roof remained serenely in midair. Then, as if belatedly noticing the stowaway's stare, the foolish thing hurriedly fell.

target.text: But, that was as long as her composure lasted. Puzzled at the soft, dry clattering coming from behind her, when she turned around, the entire wall of the shack had collapsed. And that single wall triggered the remaining walls to collapse in turns, and the rickety roof, in spite of losing its supports, seemed entirely unconcerned; it actually remained hanging in mid-air for a while before hurriedly crashing down as if only just noticing the stowaway's fixed gaze, the silly thing.

source.japanese: だが密航者の眉が引き攣[つ]ったのは、壁板と屋根が披露したお座敷芸を不興じたのではなく、バラックという覆いが取り払われて、内部に鎮座していたものが露わになってしまったからである。
source.english: But the little parlor trick with the walls and roof wasn't what made her eyebrow twitch. The shack's covering was gone, exposing what had sat inside.

target.text: But the reason the stowaway's eyebrow twitched was not because she was left unimpressed by the little performance put on by the walls and the roof, but rather because now that the shack that served as its cover had been demolished, that which had been enshrined within had been exposed.

source.japanese: ごつごつとして、無闇矢鱈と目方があって、角張った鉄塊を積み重ねて、そして筒先をいまだ撃発の余熱でちりちりと空気焦がしている。旧式の。発射に耐えたのが不思議なくらい古めかしい。あわあわと隠しにかかろうにも、偽装していたバラックは屑拾いでも敬遠しそうな廃材に成り果てた。
source.english: Bulky, enormously heavy, angular masses of iron piled upon one another. Its muzzle still scorched the air with the lingering heat of a shot. Old-fashioned. So antiquated it was a wonder it had survived firing at all. She might frantically try to hide it, but the shack that had disguised it was now scrap even a scavenger would pass over.

source.japanese: ───バラックの中に収められていたもの。
source.english: What had been housed inside the shack—

target.text: It was a rugged, absurdly heavy stack of angular iron blocks, the tip of its barrel still scorching the air with the sizzling residual heat of the blast. An older type. So time-worn it was a miracle that it even withstood the discharge. For all that she frantically tried to hide it, the shack that had served as its camouflage had been reduced to scrap that even a ragpicker would give a wide berth.
───That which had been stored within the shack.

source.japanese: 単装の、艦上砲だった。
source.english: Was a naval gun in a single-gun mount.

target.text: Was a single-mount deck gun.

source.japanese: ……そして朔屋とクロは。最期、という瞬間に廃屋群を破壊し、大海蛇を瓦礫の中に埋めつくして、二人の生命を救ったあの大轟音は何がもたらしたものか、さっぱり訳がわからなかったけれど、今はそれを詮索するよりもやるべき事がある。
source.english: As for Sakuya and Kuro: they had no idea what had produced the immense roar which, at the final instant, destroyed the abandoned buildings, buried the serpent in rubble and saved their lives. For now, however, something else had to be done before they investigated.

source.japanese:
泪に教えられた通りの道を辿る───
　
　───と。
　廃址の街並みの、小箱を乱雑に重ねたように積層して高さも統一されず段々の中、分けて小高い建物上に塔屋が見える、あれだ。
　もう大海蛇はいない。絶縁のためと着こんだスーツは動きづらく、そして蒸し暑い。二人は建物に入りこんでスーツを脱いでから、塔屋へと続く階段を登り始める。
source.english:
They followed the route Rui had described—and there it was. Amid the uneven tiers of abandoned buildings, piled like little boxes carelessly stacked and left at different heights, a tower room rose from the roof of one of the taller structures.
The serpent was gone. Their insulating suits were awkward to move in, hot and damp. They entered the building, stripped them off and began climbing the stairs to the tower room.

target.text: ……And then, there were Sakuya and Kuro. Whatever that thundering roar that, in the moment that could only be described as their last, had demolished the abandoned buildings, buried the great sea serpent in the rubble, and saved their lives was, they really had not the slightest of clues, but right now, they had something else they ought to be doing before prying into that matter.

They followed the path as they had been instructed by Rui─── ───And there. Amidst the tiered townscape of the ruins, like small boxes had been piled up messily at uneven heights, atop one building that was slightly taller than all the rest, there was something that looked like a tower, and that had to be it. The great sea serpent was no more. The suits they had put on for their insulating properties were hard to move in, not to mention hot and stuffy. The two of them went inside the building, and after discarding the suits, they began climbing the stairs leading to the tower.

source.japanese: 足の生えた鰻用か、と怪しいくらい細く長く暗い木の段を三度ほど折り返して上がった建物の屋上、そこもまた板張りの広場で、細雨に侘びしく濡れている、その向こうに小屋掛けされた塔屋が一つ。
source.english: The wooden steps were so narrow, long and dark you might suspect them of being designed for an eel with legs. Three turns brought them to the roof: another expanse of planking, forlornly wet with fine rain. Across it stood the little rooftop room.

source.japanese: その小さな塔屋に、朔屋とクロもまた、泪が感じたのと同じように、古い時代の船に設けられた船尾楼のような、と言う印象を受けた。
source.english: To Sakuya and Kuro, as to Rui before them, the little tower room suggested the sterncastle of a ship from another age.

target.text: So narrow and long were the dark wooden steps of the stairs leading up to the roof of the building they ascended, doubling back on themselves no less than three times, that they half suspected it was made with an eel that had sprouted legs in mind; at the top, they were greeted by yet another open space covered in floorboards, drearily wet in the misty rain, and on the opposite side stood a single, jury-rigged tower.
And as they saw that small tower, Sakuya and Kuro, just like Rui had felt before them, were also given the impression of something akin to an aftercastle on an old sailing ship.

source.japanese:
『我造りし人を我地の面より拭い去らん
　人より獣　天空の鳥に至るまで滅ぼさん
　そは我これを創りしことを悔ゆればなり
　今七日ありて我四〇日四〇夜
　地に雨を降らしめ
　我創りたるあらゆるものを
　地の面より拭い去らん
　かくて七日の後洪水地に臨めり
　その日大淵の源皆潰れ
　雨四〇日四〇夜地に注ぎ
　方舟は水の面に漂えり　　　　　　　　』
source.english:
“I will wipe the people I have made from the face of the earth.
From man to beast, to the birds of the sky, I will destroy them,
For I repent that I have made them.
Yet seven days, and for forty days and forty nights
I will send rain upon the earth,
And all that I have made
I will wipe from the face of the earth.
And after seven days the flood came upon the earth.
That day all the fountains of the great deep broke open.
Rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty nights,
And the ark floated upon the waters.”

source.japanese:
『地に動く肉なるものの鳥　家畜　獣
　地に這う全てのもの　および　人皆死ねり
　その鼻に生命の息の通うもの皆死ねり
　ただ彼と共に
　方舟にありしもののみ残れり
　彼地の面より水の引きしかを見んとて
　鳥を放ちいだしけるが
　再び彼のところへ還らざりき……　　　』
source.english:
“All flesh that moved upon the earth died:
Birds, livestock, beasts,
Everything that crept upon the earth, and all mankind.
All whose nostrils held the breath of life died.
Only those with him
In the ark remained.
To see whether the waters had withdrawn from the face of the earth,
He sent out a bird,
But it did not return to him again…”

source.japanese:
屋上を塔屋へと渡る中、小糠雨を渦巻かせて聞こえてきた声、夜毎に島から響いてクロを怯えさせた声。今、その塔屋の中か。
　クロはもうその声を聞いても、ただただ哀しげに唇を噛むばかりで、取り乱したりはしなかったけれど。
　朔屋にはクロが声も涙も見せず、慟哭しているようにしか思われなかったのである。
source.english:
As they crossed the roof, the voice came through the swirling drizzle. The voice that had sounded from the island night after night and frightened Kuro.
Was it inside the rooftop room now? Kuro merely bit her lip sadly. She no longer lost her composure at the sound.
Yet to Sakuya she seemed to be weeping bitterly, without a sound or a tear.

target.text: 『I shall destroy the man whom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, even the fowls of the air, I shall destroy them. For it repenteth me that I have made them. For yet seven days, and I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights; and every living substance that I have made will I destroy from off the face of the earth. Thus, it came to pass after seven days, that the waters of the flood were upon the earth. On this day, all the fountains of the great deep were broken up. Rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights. And the Ark went upon the face of the waters. 』

『And all flesh died that moved upon the earth, both of fowl, and of cattle, and of beast, and of every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth, and every man: All in whose nostrils was the breath of life, died; and he only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark. To see if the waters were abated from off the face of the ground; he released and sent forth a bird; yet she returned not again unto him any more…… 』

While they crossed the rooftop towards the tower, a voice reached them, sending the veil of fine drizzle into a swirl; it was the voice that had terrified Kuro so as it echoed from the island every night. Had it just come from within the tower? Even when Kuro heard this voice now, all she did was bite her lip sadly, no longer breaking into pieces, but. To Sakuya, though she neither made a sound nor showed any tears, it seemed Kuro must have been wailing in anguish.

source.japanese: 塔屋の扉を開けようとしたのだが、生憎鍵が掛かっていて、朔屋をげんなりさせたけれど、クロが試すと、彼女ならばよし、と許可するようにすんなり開く───この一事を取っても、少女とこの島の繋がりを朔屋に感じさせた。
source.english: Sakuya tried the door. Locked. His spirits sagged. But when Kuro tried, it opened readily, as though granting her permission. That alone impressed upon him the bond between the woman and the island.

target.text: He tried opening the door to the tower, but it was locked, unfortunately, and while that left Sakuya dispirited, when Kuro tried, it opened easily, as though granting her permission to step inside───even this single incident alone made Sakuya feel the connection between the girl and this island.

source.japanese: 塔屋内には調度の少なく、書き物机が一脚とそれから───床に点々散っている、これは、鳩の羽根だろうか、そして中に一枚だけ黒いのは、烏の風切り羽根。
source.english: The room was sparsely furnished: a writing desk, and—scattered over the floor, feathers. Dove feathers, perhaps. One among them was black. A crow's flight feather.

source.japanese: クロは───その羽根を拾い上げて、胸にかき抱き、涙を一粒、二粒、けれど零したのはそれだけ。後はきっと振りきって、窓の側に座る、一体の人の白骨に向けた。室内に踏みこんだ時から目についてはいた、その白骨。
source.english: Kuro picked up the feather and clasped it to her chest. One tear, then two. No more. Then she pulled herself together and turned to the human skeleton seated by the window. They had noticed it from the instant they stepped inside.

source.japanese:
簡素な麻の長衣まとい、小さな椅子に腰かけ、片手を窓枠に差し掛ける形に硬化していた。渇望の形に。
　ノアの妻であったという、この白骨の事、気にならないでもない。
source.english:
Dressed in a simple linen robe, it sat on a small chair, one hand reaching toward the window frame. Fixed in an attitude of longing.
Sakuya could not help being curious about this skeleton, said to have been Noah's wife.

target.text: The room was sparsely furnished; there was a single writing desk, and beyond that───what must have been dove feathers scattered here and there on the floor, and right in the middle of them, but a single black flight feather from a crow.

Kuro───picked up that feather, clasped it to her breast, then shed a tear or two, but that was all she shed. After that, she abruptly turned around, facing the solitary white skeleton sitting by the window. It had caught his eye from the moment he stepped inside the room, that white skeleton.

Clad in a simple linen robe, sitting on a small chair, with one hand frozen, reaching for the window frame. Frozen in a shape of deep longing. How could he not be curious about this skeleton, said to supposedly be that of Noah's wife.

source.japanese: 朔屋は書き物机に歩み寄り、机の上に乗せられていた一枚の紙葉に手を伸ばして、そこでクロに振り返る。少女が頷[うなず]いて促したのに取りあげる、多少黄ばんではいるものの、室内に剥き出しに放置されてきた割りには状態が良い、それがノアの海図だった───どれだけ古いのか定かならぬが、その描線は朔屋が知る現代の海図と遜色ないくらいに精緻を極めていた。
source.english: Sakuya approached the writing desk and reached for the single sheet lying upon it. Then he looked back at Kuro. She nodded for him to go ahead. He picked it up. A little yellowed, but well preserved considering how long it had lain exposed in the room. Noah's chart. Its age was uncertain, yet the lines were as exquisitely precise as those of the modern charts Sakuya knew.

source.japanese: ───かくして二人はノアの海図を手に入れて、塔屋を後にする。
source.english: Thus the two obtained Noah's chart and left the rooftop room.

target.text: Sakuya walked up to the writing desk, reached out for the single piece of paper that had been left on it, then looked back at Kuro. The girl nodded encouragingly, so he picked it up, and though it was slightly yellowed, considering how it had been left exposed within the room, it was in relatively good condition; that was Noah's chart ───while it was unclear exactly how old it was, the lines drawn upon it were so exceedingly detailed and precise that they were comparable to any modern nautical chart that Sakuya was familiar with.
───Thus, the two obtained Noah's chart, then left the tower.

source.japanese: ───室内には、蔓植物が幾列にも垂れさがり、樹液を滴らせ熱帯性の帷[とばり]となし、荒原の稲[イネ]科の草々が風紋にうねり、清いせせらぎが山林の羊歯植物の合間を流れて、砂丘が砂粒の面を陽光に灼かれ星の雫に凍える。ありとあらゆる自然の相が混在し、重なり合い、幾重も幾重も、薄さと立体を兼ね備えた不思議な幕がうねり、波うつ。ありとあらゆる生き物達があった。馴染み深きもの、珍かなもの、異様なもの、強きもの、弱きもの、喰らうもの、喰らわれるもの、古きもの、新しきもの───
source.english: Inside the room, rows of vines hung dripping sap, forming a tropical curtain; grasses of the wild plains undulated in patterns drawn by wind; clear streams ran among the ferns of mountain forests; the sun scorched the faces of dunes, and drops of starlight froze them. Every aspect of nature mingled and overlapped, layer upon layer—strange curtains at once diaphanous and deep, rippling and billowing. Every sort of creature was there: familiar, rare, uncanny, strong, weak, eater and eaten, old and new—

source.japanese: 兎が耳を欹[そばだ]てて森のざわめきに聞き入り、獅子が風に向かい鬣[たてがみ]をそよがせ、篦鹿の扁平に尖った角が沼沢地から水草をまとわりつかせ浮き上がり、群れを為した狼[おおかみ]達が雪煙を巻き上げて駆け抜ける、鼻行類がその粘ついた鼻先に蝿を吸いつけ、翼広げた鷹[たか]の影が荒原の低木の上をよぎり、泥沢地の泥の上で蟒蛇が陽差しに血を温[ぬく]める、熊が仔供たちのじゃれ合いを見守りながらのんびりと杉の樹皮に背の毛皮を擦りつけ、畢方がくわえ持ち来たった火によって一つの山林が焼かれ、川獺は河原に獲ってきた魚たちを祭の供物のように並べ、岩塩を求めて象たちは列をなして荒野を渡っていく、原生林の雨に毛並みに雫を宿して雲豹は縄張りを巡回中、角兎の老いた一体が遠く離れた故郷を思う……。
source.english: A rabbit pricked its ears to the forest's rustling; a lion faced the wind, its mane stirring; a moose's broad, pointed antlers rose from marsh water trailing weeds; wolves raced in a pack through a cloud of snow. A snouter caught flies on its sticky nose; the shadow of a hawk, wings spread, crossed the scrub of a wild plain; a great snake warmed its blood in the sun upon the mud of a swamp; a bear leisurely rubbed its back against cedar bark, watching its cubs play; a Bifang burned a mountain forest with the fire it had carried in its beak. An otter laid its catch along the riverbank like offerings for a festival; elephants crossed a wilderness in line, seeking rock salt; a clouded leopard patrolled its territory, drops clinging to its fur in the virgin forest's rain; an old jackalope thought of its far-off home…

source.japanese: これらの獣類の中を経巡る老人は、その時代から老人ではあったけれど、当時の慈愛に満ちたその顔相と言ったら、乾いた地に降り注ぐ雨であり、餓えた腹を癒す白く柔らかな麺麭であり、誰もが疲れた足を休める大樹の木陰であり。
source.english: The old man wandering among these beasts had been old even then. But the tenderness in his face in those days was rain upon dry ground, soft white bread to a hungry belly, the shade of a great tree where anyone might rest weary feet.

source.japanese: 獣類たちは老人を当然のように共同体の中に客人として受け入れ、仔達を眺める事を許したし、牙や爪持つ者たちも風変わりな隣人として日光浴を供にした。全てが調和の中にあり、獣草合い唱和し、神天にしろしめし蝸牛枝に這いなべてこの世は事もなし───けれど、永遠かに見えた自然の平穏は朔屋とクロの眺めるうちにも、失われていったのだった。
source.english: The beasts naturally accepted him into their community as a guest. They let him watch their young. Those with fangs and claws shared their sunbathing with this curious neighbor. All was harmony. Beasts and grasses sang together. God was in his heaven, the snail upon the branch, and all was right with the world. Yet even as Sakuya and Kuro watched, that seemingly eternal peace was lost.

source.japanese: 滅びの相もまた様々な形態を取っていた。それは戦争（朔屋が知るような、またあるいは全く知らざる戦争もあったし）、疫病が爆発的に蔓延したせいもあった。原因不明の出生率低下が全ての生命体を見舞った事さえある。垂れ流される廃液と煤煙によって地と水が毒され、獣類が生きられなくなった世もあった。そしてもちろん神話・聖典通りに巨大洪水によって地が覆われた事も。
source.english: Destruction, too, took many forms. There were wars—wars Sakuya knew, and others utterly unknown to him. Epidemics spread explosively. Once, even the birth rate of every living thing had fallen for no known reason. In other ages, discharged waste and smoke poisoned earth and water until beasts could no longer live. And of course there had been times when a mighty flood covered the earth, as told in myth and scripture.

target.text: ───Inside the room, several rows of vines were hanging down, forming a tropical curtain dripping with sap; true grasses from the wilderness billowed in wind-wrought cascades; a pure stream trickled between the ferns of the mountain forests; the grainy faces of the sand dunes were scorched by the sunlight, then frozen beneath the celestial tears of night. Every conceivable facet of nature intermingling, overlapping, layer upon layer, a mysterious veil, both delicate and dimensional, undulating and rippling like a wave. Every conceivable living being was here. The deeply familiar, the rare, the bizarre, the powerful, the weak, those who eat, those who are eaten, the ancient, the new───

The bunny pricked up its ears to listen attentively to the murmuring of the forest; the lion faced the wind as it rustled its mane; the flat, pointed antlers of the moose rose from the marsh, draped in tangled water weeds; the wolves, forming a pack, whirled up smoke-like sprays of snow as they dashed past; the rhinogrades used the sticky tips of those distinctive noses of theirs to attract flies; the shadow of a hawk with wings unfurled flashed past the shrubs of the wilderness; the great snake warmed its blood in the sunlight atop the mire of the muddy marshland.

The bear leisurely rubbed the fur of its back against the bark of a cedar tree while keeping an eye on the frolicking of its cubs; the mountain forest was burned to cinders by the flame held in the beak of the bifang; the river otter lined up the fish it had caught on the riverbank as if they were an offering at a festival; the elephants formed an orderly line and traversed the wilderness in search of rock salt; the clouded leopard patrolled its territory in the primeval forest, beads of rain rolling atop its fur; a lone, timeworn jackalope gazed inwards as it thought of the faraway place it once called home…….

The elder who journeyed through the realm of these beasts was an old man even back in that age, but the compassion that radiated from his expression in those days was rain falling on dry land, soft, white bread filling a starving stomach, the shade of a great tree where any could rest their weary legs.

The beasts welcomed the elder into the midst of their community, as if it were the most natural thing in the world; they permitted him to gaze fondly upon their children, those equipped with fang and claw shared with him in their sunbathing as if he were simply an eccentric neighbour. All was in harmony, the fauna and the flora joined in chorus, God reigned in Heaven, a snail crawled along a branch, and all was right with the world───however, what once appeared an everlasting tranquility in nature was lost, slipping away before Sakuya and Kuro's very eyes.

The faces of ruin likewise assumed many different forms. It was through war (some of the kind Sakuya knew, as well other wars that he knew absolutely nothing of), and it was also due in part to the explosive spread of pestilence. There was even a case where inexplicable declines in birth rates affected every life-form. Through discharged waste and soot and smoke were the lands and the waters poisoned, and the world also became unlivable for the beasts. And of course, as written in myths and scripture, the land was also covered in the waters of a great flood.

source.japanese: 老人が経験したのはいかなる滅びだったのだろうか。それは語られず、ただ獣達が。倒れ、落ち、地に伏し、水に沈み、燃えて、老人がどれだけ苦闘しようとも救いきれず、差し延べた手が届く前に死したる屍となり、肉が腐り皮が破け腸が流れ出し───
source.english: Which destruction had the old man experienced? That was not told. Only the beasts. Falling, dropping, sinking to the earth, drowning, burning. However he struggled, he could not save them all. Before his outstretched hands reached them they were corpses: flesh rotting, skin splitting, guts spilling out—

source.japanese:
そして、骨だけを遺した。
　それでも多くの獣達がその船に集められた。実際に野に跳ねていた生き物達を乗船させた事もあったし、大山椒魚だって今回は乗せてもらえて洪水以前の人扱いされずにすんだし、あるいは遺伝子情報のみが集積せられた物もあった。
source.english:
Leaving only bones.
Even so, many beasts had been gathered aboard that ship. Sometimes they were living creatures taken from the wild. This time even the giant salamander had been allowed aboard, spared being mistaken for antediluvian man. Sometimes only their genetic information was collected.

source.japanese: ───滅びゆく動物達の幻影。老人を取り巻いて。老人は縋[すが]ろうとするのだが、幻影達は遠ざかり、薄れぼやけ、消えていくばかり。
source.english: Phantoms of dying animals surrounded the old man. He tried to cling to them, but they only drew away, faded, blurred and vanished.

target.text: What immeasurable destruction must the old man have witnessed? It was left untold; there were only the beasts. Collapsing, falling, prostrating themselves upon the earth, sinking into the waters, burning; no matter how hard the elder struggled, they could not be saved; they would die and become corpses before his outstretched hands could reach them; their flesh would rot, their skin would tear, their viscera would gush forth───

And finally, only bones remained. Nevertheless, many beasts were gathered on that ship. In fact, he let some of the creatures that had been hopping around in the wild board his ship too, even the giant salamander was spared from being treated as an antediluvian and allowed on board this time, and there were also some creatures who only had their genetic information collected.
───The phantoms of perishing beasts. Surrounded the elder. The old man tried to cling to them, but the phantoms only grew distant, faded, dimmed, disappeared.

source.japanese: 扉を開けた途端に眼前に展開された数々の情景に、朔屋とクロは瞬きどころか息をするのも躊躇われ、見入っていたのは暫時の事だったけれども、その僅かな間に歴史を廻り灯籠の画のように何周も繰り返し見たような錯覚に囚われた。
source.english: The scenes had unfolded before Sakuya and Kuro the instant they opened the door. They had watched only a little while, scarcely daring to blink or breathe. Yet in that brief time they seemed to have seen history repeat itself through many revolutions, like pictures turning in a revolving lantern.

source.japanese: 幻影、幻覚の類かそれとも老人の記憶が外界に投影せられたものなのか、いずれ朔屋達は知れず、情景の重ね幕が薄れていけば消え残ったものは、やはりがらんと室内と老人───ノアと、そして島内に遍在する骨の山。
source.english: Phantoms, hallucinations, or the old man's memories projected into the world outside him? They did not know. As the layered curtains of scenes faded, what remained was again the empty room, the old man—Noah—and the heaps of bones found everywhere on the island.

source.japanese:
あの情景が何を意味するものか朔屋には判然としなかったけれど、消え果ててみると屋内の淋しさはひたひたと満ち潮のように迫る。
　……別の意味で。
source.english:
Sakuya had not clearly understood what the scenes meant. But once they vanished, the room's loneliness came creeping in like a rising tide.
In another sense.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あの、他のみんなは？」
source.english: “…Uh. Where's everyone else?”

source.japanese: 朔屋達を送り出すだけ送り出しておいて、信天翁号の船員達、室内に一人も見えず。ノアだけが空間に投影された情景の中に佇んでいたのだった。
source.english: Having sent Sakuya and Kuro off, the Albatross's crew had disappeared. Not one remained in the room. Noah alone had stood amid those projected scenes.

target.text: As they witnessed the numerous scenes unfolding before their eyes the moment they opened the door, both Sakuya and Kuro didn't just forget to blink, they hesitated to even breathe, and while they were captivated by it for but a short time, in that brief instant, they were seized by the illusion of having traversed history, of seeing it repeat over and over again, like the paintings of a revolving lantern.

Was it some manner of illusion or hallucination, or was it perhaps the memories of the old man projected out onto the outer world? Sakuya and Kuro knew not which it was, but as the veil of overlapping scenes grew fainter, all that remained upon its disappearance was the empty interior and the old man───Noah, as well as a mountain of the bones omnipresent on this island.
Sakuya couldn't quite grasp what those sights meant, but once they fully vanished, the desolation within the room began to slowly draw nearer like a creeping tide. ……In a different sense.
【Naomasa】 「……Uhm, where are all the others?」

Despite having merely sent Sakuya and Kuro off on their merry way and nothing else, not a single crew member of the Albatross was anywhere to be seen in the room. Noah alone was standing within the scene projected into space.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「……あ。あいつらか？　えーとな、あいつらなら、そのあれだ。船の出港準備をせにゃならんので、先に行くと……」
source.english: “…Oh. Them? Well, they, uh. They said they had to get the ship ready to sail, so they'd go on ahead…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……いや、いいよ爺さん、
　そういういらん気遣いはさ。
　みんな、あの淫獣がくたばったところ見て、
　さっさと出てったんだろ……？」
source.english:
“No, it's all right, old man.
Spare me the pointless consideration.
Everyone saw that lustful beast drop dead and cleared out at once,
didn't they…?”

source.japanese: 朔屋は、問いかけたものの、どうせ答えは判りきっていた事だから、しまいには語尾からして湿気らせ項垂れた。
source.english: Sakuya asked the question, but he already knew the answer, so his voice trailed off and he hung his head.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「ああと……そうとも言う。
　って知るか儂がそんな事、
　大体なんのＱシップかあの砲撃は。
　もうちっとヤツと組[く]んず解[ほぐ]れつ、
　粘液と電撃の宴
　見せてくれるかと思うたによ」
source.english:
“Ah… you could put it that way.
But how the hell should I know?
More to the point,
what kind of Q-ship stunt was that barrage?
I thought you might wrestle with the thing a little longer
and give us a proper feast of slime and lightning.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はへ……？　やっぱあれ、砲撃だったんか。
　しかしどっから……。
　でもまあ、いいやそんな事は───」
source.english:
“Huh…? So that was gunfire.
But where from…? Oh,
whatever. Doesn't matter—”

source.japanese: 実際朔屋の悄気た様と言ったら、クロなどもがらんとした室内におおよその状況を見てとったようだが、放置されたのは同じ彼女にしても、青年に何をどう言ってやればいいのか言葉につまったほど。
source.english: Sakuya looked so thoroughly crestfallen that Kuro was at a loss for words. The empty room had apparently told her enough of what had happened. She had been abandoned too, but even she could not think what to say to him.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「ああ確かにどうでもええわ。お前があんまりしょっぱい顔しとるんでほだされた儂が馬鹿だったわ。お前ら二人とも要らん子扱いだったと言う事だ。あー情けない情けない」
source.english: “Aye, it doesn't matter. Fool that I was, letting that miserable face of yours soften me. They wanted neither of you around, that's all. Pathetic. Pathetic.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわあ……爺が人の弱味見るとこれだ。なんだよ爺さんあんただって。さっきは部屋ン中にあんな動物ドキュメンタリーおっぴろげて。ついしんみりしそうになったのはこっちだっつーの」
source.english: “Oh, great… Show the old man a sore spot and this is what you get. What about you? All that animal documentary you had playing in here. I was the one nearly getting sentimental.”

source.japanese: 少しばかり共感めいた物を覗かせたところで、所詮怪老人は怪老人にしか過ぎず、朔屋の気弱と見ればたちまち居丈高、鶏冠逆立てて猛る老鶏より始末が悪くて、つい同じ土俵で剣突返してしまい、睨み合う、頭巾の奥で陰険に燃える炎と、酒に白目黄ばんだ不摂生の眼差しと。
source.english: A glimpse of something like fellow feeling changed nothing. The strange old man remained a strange old man. The moment he saw Sakuya weaken, he grew imperious, worse than an old rooster raging with its comb erect. Sakuya found himself descending to Noah's level and snapping back. They glared at each other: sinister fire beneath the hood against an unhealthy stare, its whites yellowed by drink.

target.text: 【Noah】 「……Ah. Those people? Uhm, well, if you mean THOSE people, it was, uhh, right, that. They said they needed to get the ship ready for departure, and so they would go on ahead and……」
【Naomasa】 「……No, that's enough, old man. No need to sugarcoat it. After seeing that obscene monster drop dead, they all just immediately left, didn't they……?」
Although Sakuya had been the one to ask, he already knew what the answer would be, so by the time he was done talking, his voice was damp and his head hung low.

【Noah】 「Uhm, well……you could say that. Wait, like I care about any of that, what the hell kind of Q-ship are you sailing on with cannon fire like that? I was hoping you'd wrestle with that thing a bit more, give me a veritable feast for the eyes of slime and blasts of lightning.」
【Naomasa】 「Awhuh……? So that really was cannon fire? But where did it come from……? But, well, no, that doesn't matter───」

On the subject of just how utterly dejected Sakuya truly looked: Even though Kuro seemed to have already deduced the general state of affairs from the empty room, and even though she herself had been left behind just the same, she found herself at a complete loss for words when trying to think of what to say to the young man; that was how bad it was.

【Noah】 「Oh yes, that certainly doesn't matter. I'm the fool for letting myself be swayed into feeling sorry for you just because you made a face that miserable. Yes, it means the both of you were treated like unwanted children. Alas, how pathetic, how pitiful.」

【Naomasa】 「Wow……typical of this geezer to act like this the second he finds a weakness. What's wrong with you, old man, take a look at yourself. You were just playing this whole animal documentary right in the middle of the room. And I even almost got a little misty-eyed over it.」

Just when he thought he'd caught a glimpse of something he could empathize with, in the end, this creepy old weirdo was just that and nothing more; the moment he spotted Sakuya's timidity, he immediately became overbearing, even worse to deal with than a raging old rooster with his cockscomb erect, and unable to keep himself from stooping to the same level, he threw a sharp rebuke back at him; they glared at each other, the flames burning treacherously from deep within the hood pitted against a gaze of intemperance, the whites of his eyes yellowed by drink.

source.japanese: その下から、おろおろと二者を見上げるのが不健康そうな白子の赤の眸[ひとみ]で、視殺戦というにしても、なんとも垢抜けない取り合わせではある。
source.english: Below them, the unhealthy red eyes of an albino looked anxiously from one to the other. For a battle of murderous stares, it was a decidedly unglamorous lineup.

source.japanese: 先に付き合いきれなくなったのは、ノアだった。
source.english: Noah was the first to tire of the business.

target.text: And from below, the red eyes of a sickly albino looking up at the two of them in a fluster; for a dramatic stare-down, what a hopelessly unsophisticated combination they made.
The first to give in was Noah.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「うるさいなこちゃこちゃと。最早どうでもええんだそんな事は！
　そんな事より持ってきたんだろうな、海図を」
source.english:
“Oh, stop your endless fussing! None of that matters anymore!
More to the point, you brought it, didn't you? The chart.”

source.japanese: 乗りだして、迫る老人の、長衣がばさばさ不穏な雲のよう、クロややたじろいで後退り、朔屋の服の裾[すそ]掴んで、片手の海図を胸にかいこむ。物言いたげな顔で見あげてくる彼女を、力づけてやるように頷[うなず]き返した。
source.english: The old man leaned forward, pressing them, his robe flapping like an ominous cloud. Kuro faltered and stepped back. She caught the hem of Sakuya's clothes and hugged the chart to her chest with the other hand. She looked up at him as though asking something. He nodded back to give her courage.

target.text: 【Noah】 「Can you just shut it with all your yammering. I'm already done caring about any of that! More importantly, you brought it with you, right? The chart!」

The old man leaned forwards, drew nearer, his long robe rustling like an ominous cloud; recoiling slightly, Kuro took a step back and grabbed on to the hem of Sakuya's clothes, clutching the nautical chart in her other hand against her chest. The girl looked up at him with an expression as if she was searching for the words to say something, and he nodded back, trying to encourage her.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「おう、それだ、それよ……。
　儂の大事な大事な、海図だ」
source.english:
“Yes, that. That's it…
My precious, precious chart.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「さあ、の、鴉よ。
　お前が陸地を見つけたというのなら、
　今こそ儂に告げるがよい」
source.english:
“Come, crow.
If you have found land,
tell me now.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「その位置、その針路。
　海図に書き入れた時、
　ようやく我が長きにわたる航海も。
　───成就、しようぞ」
source.english:
“Its position.
The course to reach it.
When you mark them upon the chart,
my long voyage will at last… be fulfilled.”

source.japanese:
そこまでの生々しい執着を見せているのに、猫撫で声、なんとかしてクロを懐柔しようとしているのが浅ましい、力ずくで奪ったところで海図だけでは無意味なのだろう。
　自分のなりが怯えさせる事を承知はしているのか、触れ得るような間合い以上までは踏みこんでは来ないけれどそれでも、クロの恐れること限りなく、この老人に呪われた夜の事、記憶自体は既に定かではないにしても、よほど忌まわしい感触が骨身に染み着いてしまっているのだろう。
source.english:
Such naked obsession, yet such a coaxing voice. His attempt to win Kuro over was contemptible.
Taking the chart by force would presumably be useless without her. Perhaps he knew how frightening he looked: he stopped short of coming within reach. Still, Kuro's fear was boundless. Her memory of the night he cursed her was no longer clear, but its loathsomeness must have soaked deep into her bones.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「なあ、鴉よ。
　早う、な？　何時までもその呪われた姿でいるのは、辛かろう？」
source.english:
“Come, crow.
Quickly, hm? It must hurt, remaining in that cursed form all this time.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「告げるだけでよいのだ。
　さすればお前は、
　あの賢く、力強き羽根の、
　黒く艶[つや]やかな姿に戻れる───」
source.english:
“You need only tell me.
Then you may return to your clever,
strong-winged self.
Black and glossy—”

source.japanese:
滴る脂のように妄執をぎらつかせ、迫るノアの猫撫で声は、大洪水から生命の種を守り、次代へと伝えんとした長命人の誇りも気高さも毛ほども感じられず───
　朔屋にはただただ厭[いと]うしく、呪わしかった。
　これでは呪われているのは一体どちらなのか、判ったものではない。
source.english:
Noah pressed her in that coaxing voice, obsession glistening from it like dripping fat. Not a trace remained of the pride or nobility of a long-lived man who had sought to preserve the seeds of life through the great flood and hand them down to another age.
Sakuya found him only hateful, accursed.
At this point, which of them was cursed? There was no telling.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「戻りたくないか？　本当の姿に。
　戻りたくないか？　空を舞う鴉[カラス]に」
source.english:
“Don't you want to return? To your true form?
Don't you want to return to the crow that soars through the sky?”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「飛翔するお前は、それは美事なもんだったぞ……風切り羽根を一杯に広げ、鷹にも負けぬ威風であった……」
source.english: “You were a magnificent sight in flight… your flight feathers spread to their fullest, with a majesty no hawk could surpass…”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「……今でこそ、そんななりになっておるがな、くく……」
source.english: “…Though look at you now. Heh, heh…”

source.japanese: ノアの語る声音には憎悪と尊崇の入り交じって、老人の、かつてのクロに抱きたる複雑な心を覗かせる。
source.english: Hatred mingled with reverence in Noah's voice. It gave a glimpse of the old man's complicated feelings toward the Kuro of long ago.

target.text: 【Noah】 「Yes, that's it, that's the one……. My most precious of precious, my chart.」
【Noah】 「Now then, O crow. If you claim to have found land, speak of it to me this instant.」
【Noah】 「That position, that course. Once marked upon the chart, finally, this long voyage of mine. ───Shall be fulfilled.」

Though he had shown so vivid an obsession hitherto, the way he now desperately tried to win over Kuro with a fawning voice was abject, so simply stealing the chart by force was likely meaningless. Perhaps he was aware that his own appearance scared her, for he never stepped any closer than just within reach of her, but even so, Kuro's fear knew no bounds; even though the memory of that night when she had been cursed by this old man was itself already unclear to her, the repugnant sensation of it must have deeply ingrained itself into the very marrow of her bones.
【Noah】 「Come, O crow. Swiftly now, yes? It must pain you to forever remain in that cursed form.」
【Noah】 「You but have to speak it. Once you have done so, you will regain that wisdom, those powerful feathers, recover that form clad in lustrous black───」

Within the wheedling whine of Noah's voice as he pressed her, gleaming with obsession as though it were dripping with grease, was not a shadow of neither the pride nor nobility of Methuselah's legacy, the sacred duty of protecting the seeds of life from the Great Flood, to be felt─── To Sakuya, it was utterly repulsive, accursed. It made it impossible to tell which of them was truly cursed.
【Noah】 「Do you not wish to return? To your true form. Do you not wish to return? To a crow soaring through the skies.」
【Noah】 「When you were in flight, how magnificent a sight you made…… all your flight feathers unfurled, with a majestic dignity that rivalled even the hawk……」
【Noah】 「……A far cry from your sorry state now, keheh……」
Loathing and reverence mixed together in Noah's voice as he spoke, offering a glimpse into the complex emotions the elder harboured for the Kuro that once was.

source.japanese:
クロは、ノアの妄念に、悪臭を嗅いだように海図を抱いたまま後じさったけれど、ノアの黒々とした妄執に記憶の扉こじ開けられたか、ふっと遠くに焦点を置く目になった、それは恐らく空高く飛翔せるものの、高みを往く眼差しなのであったろう。
　───在りし日の、クロの。
source.english:
Clutching the chart, Kuro backed away from Noah's obsession as though from a foul smell. Yet perhaps that black fixation had forced open a door in her memory, for her eyes suddenly focused far away: the gaze, perhaps, of a creature flying high through the upper reaches of the sky.
The gaze Kuro had possessed long ago.

target.text: As though Noah's obsession were a foul odour, Kuro was still retreating while tightly clasping the chart, but perhaps Noah's jet-black delusions had wrenched open the door to her memories, for suddenly, her eyes focused on something distant, and that was, in all likelihood, the gaze of someone soaring high in the sky, a gaze heading for great heights. ───Kuro's gaze, of bygone days.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「───そうだ。
　クロはほんとは、カラスだったんだ」
source.english:
“That's right.
Kuro was really… a crow.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「嵐の中、どこまでも飛んでける。
　どこが陸地なのか、探して、どこまでも」
source.english:
“Could fly anywhere through the storm.
Looking for land. On and on.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ずっと昔は、クロは。
　なによりも知恵のある、カラスで。
　他のどの鳥よりも、
　飛ぶのが上手なカラスで」
source.english:
“Long ago,
Kuro was… a crow wiser than anything else.
A crow that flew
better than any other bird.”

source.japanese: 低く呟くクロは、過去に僅かなりとも触れたせいか、常よりも舌が座って、思慮とさえ言える深い心を感じさせ、なるほど鴉[クロウ]、と朔屋に思わせた。
source.english: Kuro murmured softly. Perhaps that slight brush with her past had steadied her tongue. Her voice now held a depth that might almost be called wisdom. A crow indeed, Sakuya thought.

source.japanese: と言ってクロは、そのひ弱い両手で羽ばたきの真似事などしてみせたのではない。人の姿形で鳥を飛翔を真似ても不様なだけ、クロはただ、一瞬だけ嵐の時の彼女の眸[ひとみ]を取り戻しただけ。すぐに曇ってしまったけれど、その鋭き眼力は、あの思慮深き黒き鳥なのだと、なるほどと朔屋を。
source.english: Not that Kuro flapped her weak hands to imitate wings. Aping a bird's flight in human form would only look foolish. For a single instant she had merely regained the eyes she had in a storm. They soon clouded again, but that sharp gaze convinced Sakuya: yes, the wise black bird.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「───That's right. Kuro really was a crow.」
【Kuro】 「Through the storm, can keep flying, endlessly. Where is land, searching, endlessly.」
【Kuro】 「Long, long ago, Kuro was. A crow, wiser than any other. A crow, better at flying than any other bird.」

Whispered in low tones, perhaps it was because she had come into touch, however faintly, with her past, for Kuro's tongue was steadier than usual, conveying a depth of mind that could even be called wisdom; "Indeed, a crow", it left Sakuya thinking.

With that said, it was not as if Kuro was attempting to imitate flapping her wings with those feeble arms of hers. Trying to imitate a bird in flight with a human form would only be unsightly, no, for but a brief moment, Kuro merely regained the eyes of the girl herself as she was during a storm. They clouded over quickly once more, but that piercing gaze, indeed, it belonged to that profoundly thoughtful black bird, it made Sakuya think.

source.japanese:
鴉、鴉、思慮ある鳥よ、いと黒き鳥よ。あらゆる鳥の中でも群を抜いての知恵者よ。神話、伝説中の常連よ。お前達は後代その賢しきが故に時に人から忌み嫌われる事もあったけれど、その出自は輝かしい。その羽根の黒さの由来は、時に太陽とも結びつく。天空の黄金の炎に近づきすぎたために、その羽根黒く焦がされたのだ、とも。
　太陽の隠語として『金烏』と言う語すらあるではないか。
source.english:
Crow, crow, bird of wisdom, blackest of birds. Wisest by far among all winged creatures. A familiar presence in myth and legend. In later ages mankind sometimes hated and shunned you for that very cleverness, yet your beginnings were glorious. Even the black of your feathers has sometimes been bound to the sun: you flew too near heaven's golden fire, and your plumage was charred.
Is not even the sun itself called the Golden Crow?

source.japanese:
鴉、知恵のある鴉、であるならば、たとえかつての主であったとしても、お前を呪うような相手には、否むがよい。
　───またとあらじ！　と啼[な]いてみせるがよい。
source.english:
Crow, wise crow. Then refuse the one who curses you, even if once he was your master.
Cry out—Nevermore!

target.text: Crow, crow, O thoughtful bird, O bird of deepest black. O sage amongst your winged kind, unrivaled in your wisdom. O constant companion of myth, of legend. In posterity, that sage wisdom would at times draw upon you ire and loathing from man, but your origin yet glitters gloriously.

The source of the blackness of your plumage is, at times, intertwined even with the sun. You flew too close to the golden flame in the heavens, and so those feathers were scorched a deep black, it is said. Indeed, does not the term『Kinu』 exist as a poetic metaphor for the sun herself? (TN: The connection between crow and sun is referring to Yatagarasu, written "八咫烏", a three-legged crow in Japanese mythology that lives in the sun. This is believed to be a localization of the similar Chinese crow of myth, the Jinwu, or Kinu in Japanese, written "金烏".)

Crow, sage crow, if that is truly you, then even should he be your master from days of yore, you should deny him, a man who would curse you so. ───You should cry out "Nevermore!" (TN: Crow and raven are both "karasu" in Japanese.)

source.japanese:
けれど、クロは。
　否みもせず、眼力で射貫きもせず。
　ただ、哀れな声を───
source.english:
But Kuro neither refused
nor pierced him with her gaze.
She merely spoke in a pitiable voice.

target.text: However, Kuro. Neither denied him, nor pierced through him with her sharp gaze. With a pitiful voice, she merely───

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「それなのにクロは、降りられる陸地を見つけられなかったから」
source.english: “But Kuro couldn't find land to come down on.”

source.japanese: ノアが方舟から放ったという鴉は、風雨の中に飛び立っては幾度となく戻ってきたという───陸地を見つけられなかったら、戻ってきたのだという。
source.english: The crow Noah released from the ark, they say, flew out into the wind and rain and returned many times. Returned when it could not find land.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「And yet, Kuro could find no solid ground to alight on.」
The crow that Noah had sent forth from his ark was said to have flown out into the storm and returned countless times───because it was unable to find land, it returned.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「おじいに教えてあげられなかったから。
　でも、そのせいなの？
　クロが今、こんなになっちゃったのは」
source.english:
“Couldn't tell Grandpa.
But is that why?
Is that why Kuro's… like this now?”

source.japanese:
クロは、かつて嵐を衝[つ]いて舞い上がっていた時代がもしあったとしても、声にも、そのか細い肩にも、手足にも、鳥の中の鳥としての矜持や気概は全く見えず、呪われてあった年月が、彼女に何をもたらしたのか、どう変えてしまったのかを物語っていた。
　震えて舌足らずの言葉、か弱き手足にひ弱な白い肌。何もかもが、かつての彼女が偉大であればあったほど、今の彼女の哀れを酷薄に告げる。
source.english:
Even if she had once risen into the teeth of storms, Kuro now showed none of the pride or spirit of that bird among birds. Not in her voice, her narrow shoulders, her arms or legs. They spoke instead of what the cursed years had brought her, how they had changed her. Trembling, halting speech.
Weak limbs, frail white skin. The greater she had once been, the more cruelly everything proclaimed her present misery.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「So couldn't tell grandpa of any. But, is that the reason? That Kuro has become the way Kuro is now.」

Even had there once been a time when Kuro had soared through the storm, neither her voice, nor her slender shoulders, not even her limbs showed even a shadow of the pride or spirit befitting a bird among birds, a testament to what all those years spent cursed had done to her, how they had changed her. Her trembling, tongue-tied words, her feeble limbs and frail white skin. Anything and everything about her: for all the magnificence she had held in the past, it only spoke more cruelly of how pitiful a state she was in now.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「……待たされすぎたよ、儂らは。
　刻一刻と失われていく生命。
　守るべき物達が失われていく絶望」
source.english:
“…We waited too long.
Life slipping away with every moment.
The despair of losing what we ought to protect.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「鴉、お前が飛び呆けている間になあ……。
　お前は幾度か船に戻ってきたが。
　お前は何も持ち来たらんかった。
　儂らの希望、約束の地の証を、なにも」
source.english:
“While you flew about, crow…
You came back to the ship several times.
But you brought us nothing. No hope.
No sign of the promised land. Nothing.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「その度に深まる我らの絶望───
　お前には判るまいなあ」
source.english:
“Our despair deepened each time.
You wouldn't understand.”

source.japanese:
憂愁に深く沈んだ吐息でクロを責めるノアの、恨みの深さは伝わっても、だからと朔屋を納得させるものではない。
　二者の間に進み出たのは、老人の非難がましい視線からクロを遮[さえぎ]るために。
source.english:
Noah blamed Kuro with a sigh sunk deep in melancholy. Sakuya could feel the depth of the grudge, but it did not persuade him.
He stepped between them to shield Kuro from the old man's accusing eyes.

target.text: 【Noah】 「……Too long were we made to wait. Life ebbing away second by second. The despair of seeing that which we must protect vanish before us.」

【Noah】 「Crow, see, while you flew around in some befuddled daze……. You returned to the ship several times, but. You brought back nothing with you. Our hope, proof of the promised land, not a single thing.」
【Noah】 「Our despair, which deepened each and every time─── You could never hope to understand, could you?」

Though the depth of Noah's resentment was conveyed as he blamed Kuro with a sigh deeply steeped in melancholy, that in itself was not enough to leave Sakuya convinced. He stepped between the two to shield Kuro from the elder's reproachful gaze.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「爺さん、そりゃあひどいだろう。
　どう考えてもあんたの逆恨みじゃないか」
source.english:
“That's cruel, old man. However you look at it,
you're taking it out on the wrong person.”

source.japanese: ───鴉の騎士を気取ったつもりであったとしたならば、朔屋は一言の元に斬って捨てられた。
source.english: If he had meant to play the crow's knight, Sakuya was cut down with a single remark.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「黙れこの少女性愛者。お前な、子供は慈しみ育てる者であって、セックスの対象にするもんじゃないだろうが。その上お前は鳥姦嗜好者じゃ。重度の変態だ」
source.english: “Shut up, you pedophile. Listen, kids are meant to be cherished and raised—they’re not objects of sexual desire. On top of that, you’ve got a fetish for sex with birds. You’re a severe pervert.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「お前な、何を気取っているつもりか知らんが、そこのところ、少し顧みたらどうだ？」
source.english: “I don't know what role you imagine you're playing, but why don't you stop and take a look at yourself?”

source.japanese: ……朔屋は、言葉の針に、しかも返しがついた針に心を深々と抉[えぐ]られて、廃屋の床の上を耳を押さえて転がり廻っていて、クロの盾すら満足にこなせないのだった。
source.english: The needle of those words—barbed, no less—gouged deep into Sakuya's heart. He rolled over the floor of the abandoned house clutching his ears, no longer capable even of serving as Kuro's shield.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「だいたいな、逆恨みかどうかなぞ、誰が決めるんだ。怨む本人には、怨めしい怨めしいという思いがあっても、それを不当な恨みとは思うまい」
source.english: “Anyway, who decides whether a grudge is unjust? The one holding it may feel bitter, bitter indeed. But he won't think his bitterness unjustified.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「That's just cruel, old man. No matter how you look at it, isn't your resentment here misplaced?」
───If Sakuya had intended to act the part of the crow's knight in shining armor, then he was swiftly cut down in but a few words.

【Noah】 「Shut up, you pedophile. Listen here you, children are supposed to be raised with tender affection, not used as sex objects, you got that? And you have a fetish for fucking birds on top of that. You are a serious degenerate.」
【Noah】 「Look, I don't know what you're trying to act all high and mighty about, but maybe you should take a moment to reflect on that first?」

……Sakuya's heart was deeply gouged by a needle of words───a barbed needle at that───and so he rolled around on the floor of the abandoned house, hands over his ears, unfit to serve even as Kuro's shield.

【Noah】 「Besides, who's to say what qualifies as a misplaced grudge? Even if the person holding it is filled with nothing but pure, bitter resentment, they certainly wouldn't view their own feelings as unjustified.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そんな……」
source.english: “But…”

source.japanese:
悲痛な声、今もしクロが涙を零したならば、眸の血の赤が混じって薄赤く滴りそうなくらい、痛切な声。
　ノアの言葉は、人の業の深さを思い知らせ、クロを打ちのめす。
source.english:
A voice so anguished that, had Kuro shed tears, the blood-red of her eyes seemed likely to mingle with them and drip pale red.
Noah's words taught her the depth of human perversity and crushed her.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「That's……」

A voice of heartbreak: was Kuro to shed tears in this moment, they would likely trickle down in trails of light red as if mixed with the blood-red of her eyes, so acute was it. Noah's words laid bare the sinful nature of man, devastating Kuro.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ひどい、なんでクロだけ……。
　クロばっか、なんで……」
source.english:
“Cruel. Why only Kuro…?
Always Kuro. Why…?”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「じゃから、それもここまでだと言うておるのに。さ、早う、な？　……な？
　何を躊躇う？　望んでその哀れな姿に留まろうというのか？」
source.english:
“And I'm telling you, that ends here. Come, quickly, hm? Hm…?
Why hesitate? Do you want to stay in that pitiful form?”

source.japanese: かき口説く老人の、いやらしい声の他に、クロに問いかける声があった。
source.english: Another voice was questioning Kuro, besides the old man's oily entreaties.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Awful, why only Kuro……. Why always Kuro……」
【Noah】 「As I said, that, too, all ends here. Now, swiftly, yes? ……Yes? What are you hesitating for? Are you saying you desire to remain in that pitiful state?」
Besides the disgusting, wheedling voice of the old man, there was another voice questioning Kuro.

source.japanese:
───じゃあクロよ、お前は。
　
　───どうするつもりなんだ？
source.english:
Well then, Kuro—
what are you going to do?

source.japanese: ───行ってしまうのか？　元の姿を取り戻して、どこかに飛んで行ってしまうのか？
source.english: Will you leave? Get your old form back, then fly off somewhere?

source.japanese: ───それに、この爺に陸地を教えたところで、本当にお前の呪いは解かれるのか？
source.english: And if you tell this old man where the land is, will he really lift your curse?

source.japanese: ───もし爺さんが約束を守ってくれなけりゃ、お前は今のクロのままだぜ？
source.english: If he doesn't keep his promise, you'll still be the Kuro you are now.

source.japanese: ───今のままでも、嵐が来ればお前はすごい奴じゃないかよう。それで、足りないのか、なあ、クロ。
source.english: Even as you are, you're amazing when a storm comes. Isn't that enough? Hey, Kuro?

target.text: ───Alright then, Kuro. ───What are you going to do?
───Are you leaving? Will you regain your true form, then fly away somewhere?
───What's more, when you tell this old man of the land you found, will your curse truly be broken?
───Should this old man not keep his promise, you'll stay the Kuro you are right now, you know?
───Even as you are now, when a storm arrives, are you not amazing? Is that not enough for you, Kuro?

source.japanese:
誰あろう、誰でもない、朔屋の声だった。ノアの糾弾から、ようやく我を取り戻した朔屋だった。いまだノアからの非難の傷は深く、身を起こすのも大儀で、ゆっくり立ち上がり、足許を確かめるように踏みしめて、クロの背後に立つ。
　けれど。後ろから支えてやるような位置に立ちながら、朔屋の言葉はよりクロを迷わせるものでしかない。
　何が青年をして、そのような惑わす言葉を吐かせたものか。
source.english:
The voice belonged to none other than Sakuya, who had at last recovered from Noah's denunciation. The wound remained deep; even rising was an effort. Slowly he stood, planted his feet as though testing the ground, and took his place behind Kuro.
Yet although he stood as if to support her, his words only deepened her confusion.
What had moved the young man to bewilder her so?

target.text: Whoever could it be? Why, it was the voice of none other than Sakuya. Sakuya, who had at last returned to his senses after crumpling before Noah's denunciation. The wounds wrought by Noah's criticism yet remained deep, even getting up was laborious, but he slowly got to his feet, stepped firmly on the floor as if ascertaining his footing, then positioned himself behind Kuro. However. While he stood in a position as if it to support her from behind, Sakuya's words only left Kuro all the more confused. Whatever could have lead the young man to speak such perplexing words?

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いいよ。もう。朔屋さんの好きにして。
　クロはね。もう考えられない」
source.english:
“It's all right. Mr. Sakuya… do whatever you want with Kuro.
Kuro can't think anymore.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……いいんだな、ほんとに、それで」
source.english: “…You're sure? You really want that?”

source.japanese: 朔屋にことりと背中を預けて、あいと頷[うなず]いた、クロの横顔の線には、他者に全てを委ねきって後悔の翳[かげ]り一つ無く、ただ白々と、白々と。
source.english: Kuro rested her back lightly against him and nodded yes. Having entrusted everything to another, she showed not the slightest shadow of regret. Her profile was only pale—blankly, utterly white.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Fine. Whatever. Will do as Sakuya-san wants. Kuro. Can't think about it anymore.」
【Naomasa】 「……Are you really, truly fine with that?」

She leaned her back into Sakuya, and with an "aye", she nodded; there was not the slightest shadow of regret from surrendering her everything into the hands of another to be seen in the lines that made up Kuro's profile; it was but a pure, clear white.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「どのくらい、飛び続けて、こうなったんだろう」
source.english: “How long did Kuro keep flying… before becoming this?”

source.japanese:
首筋から胸元に流れる髪を一筋、指の中に掬[すく]いとる。白くて汚れを吸ったらすぐに目立ち、腰もなく、もつれやすい髪。伸ばしっぱなしの髪。
　何時から───こうなのだろう。
source.english:
She gathered between her fingers a strand of hair flowing from neck to chest. White hair, quick to show any dirt, limp and easily tangled. Hair left to grow unchecked.
Since when had it been like this?

target.text: 【Kuro】 「No matter how far Kuro kept flying, it would still end up like this.」

She scooped up a single strand of hair that flowed from the nape of her neck to her chest and held it between her fingers. White, any grime it absorbed would instantly stand out, limp, quick to tangle. Unkempt hair simply left to grow. Since when───had it been like this?

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「こうなったその時に、クロはもう、終わってたんだ、きっと。もう、後はつけたしみたいなもの」
source.english: “When Kuro became this… Kuro was already finished, probably. Everything after was… just added on.”

source.japanese:
髪を掬[すく]った、手首も眺める。
　枯れた木の枝のように細くて、やはり白い、肌の薄い手だ。非力で、他の人なら軽々運べるものでも、ちょっと持ち上げただけで疲れてしまう腕。足だってそう。歩くだけなら随分と遠出も出来るけれど、駆け足は下手くそ、すぐに縺[もつ]れて転んでしまう。
　一体いつから、こうだったのだろう。
source.english:
She looked at the wrist of the hand that held her hair.
Thin as a dead branch. White too, with thin skin. Powerless. Arms that tired from merely lifting something anyone else could carry easily. Her legs were the same. She could go quite far if she only walked, but she was no good at running. Soon they tangled and she fell.
Since when had she been like this?

target.text: 【Kuro】 「And when Kuro became like this, Kuro was already over and done with, without a doubt. By then, the rest was just an afterthought.」

She looked at the wrist that had scooped up the hair. Slender as a withered tree branch, a hand clad in thin skin that, sure enough, was white. Feeble arms: left exhausted after but a single lift of something easily carried by any other. Even her legs were like that. Were she just walking, she could manage a surprisingly distant trip, but her running was clumsy, and her feet would quickly tangle and make her fall over. Just how long had it been since she became like this?

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でも、朔屋さんがクロをおんなのこに、
　そしておんなにしてくれた時は、
　うれしかったよ」
source.english:
“But when Mr. Sakuya turned Kuro into a girl,
and made me a woman,
I was really happy.”

source.japanese: 語りながら、身体を眺め下ろす。痩せこけて、どんなに食べても大きくなれない身体だ。そもそもそんなに沢山は食べられない。何時か誰かに、きっとそのうちに背も伸びるし、そうしたら胸だってふっくらしてくると言われたような気もするけれど、あれは誰だったろう。
source.english: As she spoke, she looked down at her wasted body, a body that would not grow however much she ate. She could not eat very much in the first place. Someone, once, had told her that one day she would surely grow taller, and then her breasts would fill out too. Or so she vaguely remembered. Who had that been?

source.japanese:
結局、いつまで経っても自分はこのままだ。
　けれど、こんな髪でも、手足でも、身体でも。
source.english:
In the end, no matter how much time passed, she would remain as she was.
And yet—even with hair like this, limbs like this, a body like this.

source.japanese:
馬鹿で、物覚えが悪くて、他の人からはまともに見てもらえない自分でも。
　この人は、自分を抱いてくれた。他の人が近寄らないところまで踏みこんで、他の人がしてくれない事をしてくれて、そして自分に教えてくれた。
source.english:
Foolish, slow to learn, never taken seriously by anyone else—even so,
this man had embraced her. He had ventured where no one else would approach, done what no one else would do for her, and taught her.

source.japanese:
クロには判らなかった事を、教えてくれた朔屋。
　他の誰でもない、クロの側にいてくれた朔屋。
　そんな朔屋なら───もう、なにもかも。
source.english:
Sakuya, who had taught Kuro what she had never understood.
Sakuya, no one else, who had remained at her side.
If it was Sakuya, then—everything. She could give him all of it.

source.japanese:
委ねてしまっていいのではないかと、クロは。多分、あの大海蛇の前で、この青年となら最期を共にするのも幸せなのだと知ってしまった時から、クロは。
　青年に、自分に遺された、最後の大事な芯を預けてしまっていたのだろう。
source.english:
Perhaps she could entrust it all to him. Perhaps, from the moment she realized before the great sea serpent that sharing this young man's end would itself be happiness,
Kuro had already entrusted him with the last precious core that remained to her.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But, when Sakuya-san treated Kuro like a girl, and made a Kuro a woman, Kuro was so happy.」

As she spoke, she looked down her body. Much too skinny, a body that would never grow larger no matter how much she ate. Not that she could eat that much to begin with. She felt like, at some point, she had been told by somebody that, one of these days, she would definitely grow taller, and once that happened, even her chest would swell in size, but who had that been again?
In the end, no matter how much time passed, she would remain as she was. But, even with this hair, these limbs, this body.

Even as her stupid, obtuse self that none other would take seriously. This man, he had embraced her. He had stepped into places others wouldn't approach, he had done things for her what others would not, and he had taught her things.
Sakuya had taught Kuro that which she did not know. It was Sakuya who had been by Kuro's side, and none other. If it was Sakuya, then─── anything and everything she was.

Would it not be fine to entrust it all to him, Kuro thought. It was probably ever since that time, in front of the great sea serpent, when she realized that even sharing her final moments together with this young man was bliss. Perhaps Kuro had already come to entrust the young man with the final, most precious core that remained within her.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「何を言うているのだ、お前は……。
　ここまで来て、全てを棄てるつもりか」
source.english:
“What are you saying…?
After coming this far, are you going to throw it all away?”

target.text: 【Noah】 「Whatever are you talking about, you……. Do you intend to cast it all away, and after having come this far?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だまれ───だまれ、おじい。
　この人は、おじいが取っていって全部。
　クロから全部取っていったクロを」
source.english:
“Shut up—shut up, Grandpa.
This man held the Kuro you took everything from. Everything, Grandpa.
You took it all from Kuro, and he—”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「抱いてくれた。おじいなんか、呪っただけ。
　おじいなんか、おじいなんか───」
source.english:
“He held me. You just cursed me,
Grandpa. You, Grandpa, you───”

source.japanese:
これまでノアに怯え続けていたクロが、初めて老人に反抗してみせた、顔は歯を剥き出しにして睨[にら]みつける、追いつめられた挙げ句の悲壮感ばかりが滲む相ではあったけれど。
　それでも確かに少女はノアに逆らってみせたのだ。屹と目を剥き、拳を握りしめて、きっぱりと告げた。訣別しようとしていた。
source.english:
Kuro, who until now had done nothing but cower before Noah, defied the old man for the first time. Her teeth were bared and her eyes glared, though her face showed only the desperate pathos of someone driven to the edge.
Even so, she had defied him. Eyes wide, fists clenched, she spoke without wavering. She was severing herself from him.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ここにきて、
　なんにもできなかったくせに。
　朔屋さんみたいな人とも、
　会えなかったくせに」
source.english:
“You came all this way and couldn't do anything.
Couldn't even meet someone like Mr. Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロの方が、かってるよ」
source.english: “Kuro's the one who won.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Shut up───shut up, grandpa. This man, he, everything you took. He, with Kuro, who had everything taken from her.」
【Kuro】 「Embraced Kuro. Grandpa just cursed. Grandpa just, grandpa just───」

Kuro, who had always feared Noah, defied the old man for the very first time, glaring at him with her teeth bared, her face exuding nothing but that grim, tragic resolve that manifests in those who have been cornered. Even so, the girl certainly defied Noah. Widening her eyes fiercely, her fists clenched, she declared it with absolute finality. That she intended to part ways with him for good.
【Kuro】 「After everything, coming all this way, you couldn't accomplish anything. You could not even find, someone like Sakuya-san.」
【Kuro】 「Kuro wins this one.」

source.japanese:
クロは心を決めつつある今だったが、朔屋はまだ迷いを残していた。
　クロを老人の願いから解放してやるべきなのか、どうか。迷うまでもない事なのだ、とは思う。けれどそれを選んでしまうのは、自分の生をも決定づけてしまうのではないか───
　そんな躊躇いにも囚われたけれど。
　それでも朔屋は───
source.english:
Kuro was coming to her decision, but Sakuya still hesitated.
Should he free her from the old man's designs? Surely there should be no question. Yet making that choice might determine the course of his own life as well.
That thought held him back.
Even so, Sakuya—

target.text: While Kuro's heart was settling on a decision, hesitation yet remained in Sakuya's. Should he release Kuro from the fetters of the old man's wish, or not? This wasn't even something to be hesitant about, or so he thought. But if he were to choose that, would it not determine the course of his own life as well─── He was still seized by such hesitation, but. Even so, Sakuya───

source.japanese: <01>解放してやらない
source.english: Do not set her free

target.text: <01>Don't set her free

source.japanese: <01>解放してやる
source.english: Set her free

target.text: <01>Set her free

source.japanese:
海図を取り戻し、最も近い陸地の位置をクロから示される事で、老人はかつての箱船である島の行き先をようやく定める。
　長年の宿業から解放され、クロ、元の黒さを取り戻していくかに見える。けれども完全には戻らない。やはり呪われた歳月が長すぎたのだ。艶やか等とはとても言えない、所々色褪せて薄汚れたような黒色。
　朔屋は、それに耐えられない。このままでは、自分と同じ愚かで始末に負えない生き物であったクロが、自分よりも聡明な知性の幾許を取り戻すかも知れない。
　それ故に、彼女を縛ろうとする。
　同時に、クロを「自分の女」として愛するようになっていたことも自覚していた。
source.english:
With his chart restored to him and Kuro pointing out the nearest land, the old man at last set a destination for the island that had once been an ark.
Freed from her long karmic burden, Kuro seemed to regain her former blackness—but never completely. The accursed years had simply gone on too long. Her black was anything but lustrous: faded here and there, dingy and worn.
Sakuya could not bear it. At this rate, Kuro—the stupid, unmanageable creature who had once been as witless as he was—might regain even a little of her old intelligence and become cleverer than him.
And so he sought to bind her.
At the same time, he understood that he had come to love Kuro as ‘his woman.’

target.text: Having regained his nautical chart, and with the position of the nearest landmass marked on it by Kuro, the old man finally decided the destination of his island, formerly his ark. Released at long last from the karmic burden of long years, Kuro seemed to be regaining her former blackness. It did not, however, return completely. In the end, she must have been cursed for too many years. It was far from being lustrous; it was but a grimy, faded black scattered here and there.

Sakuya could not stand it. At this rate, Kuro, a creature as incorrigibly foolish as himself, might well regain some of her intellect, which was sharper by far than his own. Therefore, he attempted to fetter her. At the same time, he also became self-aware of the fact that he had come to love Kuro as「his woman」.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なあクロ、お前それでいいのか？」
source.english: “Hey, Kuro. Is that really what you want?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺は前の白の方が好きだったよ」
source.english: “I liked you better when you were white.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんな溝泥みたいな色より、あっちの方がずっと可愛かった」
source.english: “You were much cuter that way than in this gutter-mud black.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なあ、良いじゃないか、馬鹿のまんまでも。
　みんなだって、賢いまんまのお前より、時々すごくて普段は間抜けなお前の事が、きっと好きだと思うぜ」
source.english:
“Come on. There's nothing wrong with staying stupid.
I bet everyone likes you better when you're amazing sometimes and a fool the rest of the time, instead of clever all the time.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Hey, Kuro, are you really fine with this?」
【Naomasa】 「I really liked your earlier white.」
【Naomasa】 「It was much, much cuter than this colour that looks like something scraped off the bottom of a drain.」

【Naomasa】 「Hey, isn't it fine, to just remain an idiot. I'm sure everyone else likes you more when you're sometimes amazing and usually stupid, rather than when you're always smart, that's what I think.」

source.japanese:
稚拙な口説き文句だったが、男性経験に疎[うと]いクロにとっては老人の呪詛より甘い誘惑の言葉。
　迷って、迷ったあげくに、クロは───
source.english:
A clumsy attempt to win her over. But to Kuro, who knew little of men, these tempting words were sweeter than the old man's curse.
She hesitated, hesitated, and at last—

source.japanese: 海図を───
source.english: The chart—

target.text: It was an absolutely artless attempt at convincing her with loving words, but to Kuro, who had precious little experience with men, they were words of far sweeter temptation than the old man's maledictions. She wavered, and after much hesitation, Kuro───
Took the chart───

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロは、クロは、なんかもう、どうでもいいや。がんばってみても駄目。願ってみても、むだ」
source.english: “Kuro, Kuro… doesn't really care anymore. Trying doesn't work. Wishing doesn't help.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro……Kuro……kind of doesn't even care anymore. Trying Kuro's best was a waste. Trying to wish, all in vain.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロがなにをやったって、ね。
　でも、この人はちがう」
source.english:
“Whatever Kuro does…
But this person is different.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Didn't matter what Kuro did, right? But, this man is different.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さんは、クロがなにかしようとしなくっても、そばにいてくれるよ」
source.english: “Mr. Sakuya stays with Kuro… even when Kuro doesn't try to do anything.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san, he stays by Kuro's side, even if Kuro doesn't try to do anything.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「もうあとは、めんどくさい。
　つかれちゃった。
　みとめちゃうと、なんか、すごい簡単だ」
source.english:
“Everything else is too much trouble now.
Kuro's tired.
Once you admit it, it all becomes… so simple.”

source.japanese: ぽつんぽつんと、哀しいくらい静かな声音で呟きながら、クロは。
source.english: Murmuring brokenly, in a voice so quiet it was heartbreaking, Kuro—

source.japanese:
海図を───
　
　　　　　　　　白い指の先に摘[つま]んで。
source.english:
The chart—

                   pinched between her white fingertips.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「な……よせ、馬鹿者、止めンかッ」
source.english: “Wha—don't, you fool! Stop!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Doing any more is just too much trouble. Kuro is tired. When Kuro accepts that, it's somehow so very simple.」
While whispering a few stilted words, in a voice so quiet it was almost heartbreaking, Kuro.
Took the chart─── between her white fingertips.
【Noah】 「Wh-……cease, you fool, stop that!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ばいばい、じいちゃん」
source.english: “Bye-bye, Grandpa.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Bye bye, grandpa.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ばいばい。ずっと前の、クロ。
　クロねえ、ほんとは前みたいに、どんなとこまでも飛んでける、クロがよかったな」
source.english:
“Bye-bye. Kuro from long ago.
Kuro really wanted… to be the Kuro that could fly anywhere, like before.”
