target.text: 【Kuro】 「Bye bye, Kuro, from long, long ago. You know, Kuro, to tell the truth, wished Kuro was like the old Kuro, the girl who could fly anywhere.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……でも、もういいや。
　クロ、飛んでいきたいとこなんて、
　思いつかないし」
source.english:
“…But never mind.
Kuro can't think of anywhere
to fly to.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロは、信天翁号でいいや。みんなから馬鹿にされたっても……いじめられても」
source.english: “The Albatross is enough for Kuro. Even if everyone makes fun of Kuro… even if they bully Kuro.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「どうせ、クロにはやりたいことも、いきたいとこもめっからない」
source.english: “Kuro won't find anything she wants to do or anywhere she wants to go anyway.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……But, don't care anymore. Kuro can't think of a single place Kuro wants to fly to.」
【Kuro】 「Kuro is fine with the Albatross. Even if Kuro is made fun of by them all……or even bullied.」
【Kuro】 「Not like Kuro can find anything Kuro wants do, or anywhere Kuro wants to go anyway.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「もう、考えるの、しなくっていい。
　しないほうがいい。
　クロは───やめよう、うん」
source.english:
“Don't have to think anymore.
Better not to. Kuro will—stop.
Yes.”

source.japanese: クロは、それは静かな声で、穏やかな顔で。
source.english: In such a quiet voice, with such a calm face—

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いろいろと、やめちゃおう──」
source.english: “Let's stop… all sorts of things.”

source.japanese: 全てを諦めきった、穏やかで、哀しい顔で。
source.english: A calm, sad face that had given up everything.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「No longer have to think, at all. It's best not to. Kuro───will give up, yeah.」
In a quiet voice, with a serene look, Kuro.
【Kuro】 「Will just give up, on a whole lot of things──」
Gave up on everything, with a calm, sorrowful expression.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ばいばい、ノア───
　クロを放ったこと。
　クロを呪ったこと。
　昔のことに、なりすぎちゃったねえ」
source.english:
“Bye-bye, Noah.
Sending Kuro out.
Cursing Kuro.
It's all… too far in the past now.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ばいばい、ノア。
　どうでもよくなっちゃったよ───」
source.english:
“Bye-bye, Noah.
It doesn't matter anymore—”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「よせ、止めてくれ───!!
　頼む、それだけは───！」
source.english:
“Don't! Stop—! Please,
anything but that!”

source.japanese: ノアの制止も、最早届かず。
source.english: Noah's protests could no longer reach her.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Bye bye, Noah─── Sending Kuro out. Cursing Kuro. Has become something too far in the past, right?」
【Kuro】 「Bye bye, Noah. It stopped mattering to Kuro───」
【Noah】 「Cease, please, stop───!! I am begging you, that alone───!」
Noah's pleas to stop now fell on deaf ears.

source.japanese: クロは海図を───引き裂いて、打ち棄てたのだった。
source.english: Kuro tore the chart apart—and cast it away.

target.text: Kuro took the chart and─── tore it to pieces, then threw it away.

source.japanese:
……かくしてノアの最後の望みも潰え、島は崩壊していくのだった。
　崩れ、散り去っていく太古の木片の間から、信天翁号はかろうじて脱出を遂げる。
source.english:
Thus Noah's last hope was destroyed, and the island began to fall apart.
Amid the ancient fragments of wood collapsing and scattering, the Albatross barely made its escape.

target.text: ……Thus, as Noah's final wish, too, was crushed, the island began to collapse. And from amidst the crumbling, scattering splinters of ancient wood, the Albatross barely managed to escape.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なにが起こったんだか知らないが、この島、こりゃもうだめだ、崩れるっ」
source.english: “No idea what's happened, but this island's finished. It's falling apart!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I don't know what happened, but this island is done for, it's crumbling apart!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あ！　朔屋、クロ、どこ行ってたんだ。
　いや、くたばってなかったのか……とか思ってないよ？」
source.english:
“Oh! Sakuya, Kuro! Where've you been? No,
I wasn't thinking you were dead or anything, all right?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ah! Sakuya, Kuro, where have you been? I mean, not that I was thinking "Oh, guess they didn't kick the bucket after all" or anything!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「とにかく急いで乗船だっ。
　……それから、クロは下に引っこめておき。
　それが今は使い物になりそうにないのは、みりゃ判るからね……」
source.english:
“Anyway, get aboard, quick!
And take Kuro below.
One look tells you she'll be no use now…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Anyway, hurry up and board the ship. ……And once you're up, make sure to bring Kuro downstairs. Because I can tell she's not gonna be of any use right now just from one look at her……」

source.japanese:
クロはわあわあ泣いて泣いて泣き通しだ。
　だが朔屋は罪悪感に駆られると同時に、どこかしら安堵を抱いていたのだった。
　彼女がそのままである事に、自分が守ってやれる存在である事に。とことん駄目な男なのだ、この青年は。
　ノアの妄執が消えるとともに、晴れていく嵐雲を後にして、信天翁号はまた海へと戻っていく。
source.english:
Kuro wailed and wailed and would not stop.
But alongside Sakuya's guilt was a certain relief.
She was still as she had been. Still someone he could protect. The young man was hopeless to the core.
Leaving behind the storm clouds that cleared as Noah's obsession vanished, the Albatross returned to sea.

target.text: Kuro wailed loudly as she cried, cried, and then cried some more. But while Sakuya's body was being wracked by a feeling of guilt, at the same time, some part of him also harboured a feeling of relief. From the fact the girl would remain as she was, that she would be someone that he could protect. Utterly hopeless to the last, this young man was. Leaving behind the storm clouds that were clearing up in tandem with the disappearance of Noah's obsession, the Albatross returned to the seas once more.

source.japanese: 信天翁号は相変わらずも怪しげな連中を乗せ、怪しからぬ商売を続けている。
source.english: The Albatross still carried its dubious company and pursued its disreputable trade.

source.japanese: 乗り組みは変わらず、朔屋も相変わらず船に留まり続けてあり───
source.english: The crew remained unchanged. Sakuya, as ever, remained aboard.

source.japanese:
ただしクロは───
　完全に朔屋のみに依存する存在になり果てていた。
source.english:
Kuro, however,
had become a creature wholly dependent upon Sakuya alone.

source.japanese: 駄目である時の鈍さ加減は更に極まり、もう自分の身の回りの事すらも朔屋がいないとままならない始末。まあクロにしてみれば、自分を守って何から何までやってくれる男がそばにいるのだから、これはこれで悪くないと思っている。そんな風に感じてしまうあたり、この娘も相当に根が腐っている。
source.english: At her most useless she had grown duller than ever; without Sakuya she could no longer manage even the simplest business of looking after herself. As Kuro saw it, however, a man now stood beside her who protected her and did absolutely everything for her, so perhaps the arrangement was not so bad. That she could think this way only showed how thoroughly rotten the woman was at heart.

source.japanese: 朔屋は朔屋で、自分がいなければ満足に生きていく事もままならない哀れな生き物がいるという事に、奇妙な充足感を覚えつつ、クロにべったりついて信天翁号での日々を送っていく。
source.english: For his part, Sakuya drew a peculiar satisfaction from knowing that someone as pitiful as Kuro could scarcely live without him. Glued fast to her in return, he passed his days aboard the Albatross.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「えへえ。ノアじいちゃんは、クロみたいな役立たずには、何も与えられるものなんてないっていってたけど、あれ、嘘だったねえ」
source.english: “Heh, heh. Grandpa Noah said there was nothing to give someone useless like Kuro. But that was a lie.”

source.japanese:
クロを膝の上に横たえ、さらさらと髪を梳[と]いていく朔屋の、手つき、随分と慣れた様子だった。
　それは慣れて巧みにもなろう。二人は四六時中離れず、寄り添っているのだから。
source.english:
With Kuro lying across his lap, Sakuya drew the comb smoothly through her hair. His hands were practiced.
And no wonder they had grown deft: the two spent every hour together, pressed close and never apart.

source.japanese: 船の他の面子が呆れようとも嘲罵しようとも、二人が離れる時は、無い。
source.english: Let the rest of the crew gape or jeer as they pleased: there was never a moment when the two came apart.

target.text: As ever, the Albatross sailed on, carrying with her a shady crew and continuing her illicit trade.
The crew remained unchanged, and Sakuya, too, remained aboard the ship, unchanged───
However, Kuro was─── Degenerating into an existence that was completely dependent on Sakuya and Sakuya alone.

The degree of her dullness when she was hopeless had grown even more extreme, and it had reached the point where, without Sakuya, she could no longer even take care of her own personal needs. Well, from Kuro's perspective, having a man by her side who would protect her and take care of anything and everything for her was not so bad in its own right, or so she thought. And the fact that she felt this way was a testament to how this girl, too, was rather rotten at her core.

And Sakuya, for his part, felt a peculiar sense of satisfaction in knowing that there was a pitiful creature out there unable to live a satisfying life without him, and he spent his days aboard the Albatross sticking close to Kuro.
【Kuro】 「Ehehe. Grandpa Noah said that there was nothing that could be given to someone as useless as Kuro, but that was a big lie, wasn't it?」

As Sakuya laid Kuro on his lap and began to smoothly brush her hair, the movement of his hands seemed considerably practiced. But of course he would grow practiced and even skilled at this. For the two of them were inseparable, glued to each other day and night.
No matter how exasperated the rest of the ship's crew became, or how they tried to mock and ridicule, times where the two were apart simply didn't exist.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロには朔屋さんがいてくれるもんねえ」
source.english: “Because Kuro has Mr. Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロ、もうだめでいいや。
　朔屋さんがいてくれるんなら……」
source.english:
“Kuro doesn't mind being useless now.
If Mr. Sakuya stays…”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ううん。逆だよね。
　朔屋さんは、クロがあうあうあーだから、
　一緒にいてなんでもしてくれるの。
　だからクロは、
　ずっとあうあうあーでいるよ」
source.english:
“No. It's the other way around, isn't it?
Mr. Sakuya stays with Kuro and does everything for Kuro because Kuro's all ‘uh, uh, aaah.’
So Kuro will stay all ‘uh, uh, aaah’ forever.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「もうクロは、憧れない。
　嵐の海になんて、憧れない。
　クロは、あたまが悪くて、
　舌っ足らずのクロで、ずっといるよ」
source.english:
“Kuro won't long for it anymore.
Won't long for the stormy sea.
Kuro will stay stupid—Kuro who can't get her words out right. Forever.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さんが、クロの髪、櫛かけてくれて。
　こうして抱っこしてくれて。
　それでいい」
source.english:
“Mr. Sakuya combs Kuro's hair.
Holds Kuro like this.
That's enough.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ねえ朔屋さん、
　クロの髪、白いほうがいい？
　それとも黒いほうがいい？」
source.english:
“Mr. Sakuya?
Do you like Kuro's hair better white?
Or black?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「お前は、白いままでいいよ───」
source.english: “You can stay white—”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うん。
　あんがと。
　えへへ……嬉しいなあ」
source.english:
“Yes.
Thank you.
Heh, heh… So happy.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「なぁんだ。朔屋さんに会えたことで、
　クロには、他になんにも───
　なくって、よくなってたんだね」
source.english:
“Oh. Meeting Mr. Sakuya meant Kuro didn't need—
didn't need anything else after all.”

source.japanese: こうして駄目な二人を、駄目の二乗を重ねた二人を乗せて信天翁号は波の間に間に消えていく。
source.english: And so, with these two hopeless people aboard, their hopelessness squared, the Albatross disappeared between the waves.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Because Kuro has Sakuya-san by Kuro's side, right?」
【Kuro】 「Kuro is fine with being useless now. If Sakuya-san is there for Kuro, then……」

【Kuro】 「No. It's the opposite, right? It's because Kuro is so durrrr that Sakuya-san stays with and will do anything for Kuro. So Kuro just stays durrrr forever.」 (TN: The term Kuro uses is "あうあうあー", which is essentially the Japanese net slang version of going "hurr durr" or "derp derp" in English, signifying someone with profound mental retardation.)
【Kuro】 「Kuro won't yearn anymore. Won't yearn for some dumb stormy sea. Kuro just stays stupid, tongue-tied Kuro, forever and ever.」
【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san brushes Kuro's hair. And holds Kuro like this. That's all Kuro needs.」
【Kuro】 「Hey, Sakuya-san. Is Kuro's hair best white? Or is it best black?」
【Naomasa】 「You're best just staying white───」
【Kuro】 「Yeah. Thanks. Ehehe……so happy.」
【Kuro】 「Oh, so that's it. Just by meeting Sakuya-san, Kuro didn't need─── anything else anymore, huh.」
Thus, bearing these two hopeless souls ───hopelessness squared─── the Albatross vanished into the rolling waves.

source.japanese:
このままノアとクロの望みを成就させてやったなら───爺の事など知った事ではないが、クロはどうなってしまうのだろう。
　本来の姿と聡明さ、適応力を取り戻したクロは、信天翁号など捨ててどこかに去ってしまうのではないだろうか。
source.english:
If he let Noah and Kuro have what they wished—never mind the old man, but what would become of Kuro?
With her true form, intelligence and adaptability restored, might she abandon the Albatross and go elsewhere?

target.text: If he allowed Kuro's and Noah's wishes to be realized in this way, then─── he didn't give a dead rat about that old man, but what would happen to Kuro? Once Kuro regained her rightful form, wisdom, and adaptability, would she not abandon the likes of the Albatross and leave for somewhere distant?

source.japanese:
朔屋は深く悩んだ。深く深く懊悩した。
　それでも───それでもクロの思うとおりにさせてやろうと決意したのである。駄目な奴駄目な奴人に面罵され、後ろ指指される辛さ悲しさを知り抜いている朔屋は、それを受け入れたつもりでも、心のどこかで願っていたのではないか。
source.english:
Sakuya agonized over it. Agonized long and hard.
Even so—even so, he resolved to let Kuro do as she wished. He knew all too well the pain and sorrow of people calling him a good-for-nothing, a good-for-nothing, to his face, then pointing at him behind his back. He thought he had accepted it. Yet somewhere in his heart, had he not still hoped?

source.japanese:
自分が人並みとなり、まともな働きの一つもこなして、他人の中に受け入れてもらえる日が来る事を。
　たとえ自分ではそれが叶わずとも、クロにそういう日が来るとしたなら。それが叶うのなら。
　
　朔屋は、望んだ。
　クロが痴愚の呪縛から解き放たれる事を。
source.english:
For a day when he would be as good as anyone else, do one decent piece of work, be accepted among other people.
Even if it could not come true for him, what if such a day could come for Kuro? If her wish could be granted?
Sakuya wished for it.
For Kuro to be freed from the curse of stupidity.

target.text: Sakuya was deeply troubled. Deeply, profoundly anguished. But even so───even so, he decided to let Kuro have her way. Sakuya knew all there was to know of the bitter sorrow that was being denigrated as useless both to one's face and behind one's back, and even though he was certain he had accepted it by now, was there not somewhere within his heart that wished otherwise?

That the day would come where he could be like most people, where he could hold a steady, honest job, where he would be accepted into the midst of others. Even if that may never come true for himself, if that day could come for Kuro, then. If that could be granted, then. Sakuya wished. That Kuro would be set free from the cursed fetters of imbecility.

source.japanese: 海図を抱きかかえたクロの背を、軽くノアへと押し出してやったのだった。
source.english: He gave Kuro, still clutching the chart in her arms, a gentle push toward Noah.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いいの、朔屋さん……クロの為に？」
source.english: “You're sure, Mr. Sakuya…? For Kuro?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……まあね。
　羨ましくないといえば嘘になる。
　でも凛々しいお前はお前で、
　格好良いもんな」
source.english:
“…Well.
I'd be lying if I said I wasn't jealous.
But when you're gallant and capable like that,
you're awfully impressive too.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「誰だって、ああなりたいさ。
　俺にはそれを止めるなんてひどい事、
　ちょっとできそうにないや」
source.english:
“Anyone would want to be like
that. I don't think I could do something
as cruel as stopping you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ほら、ノアの爺に海図渡して、
　陸地の位置を教えてやるがいいぜ」
source.english:
“Go on. Give old Noah the chart
and tell him where the land is.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……間抜けな話だよな。
　一体どんだけ嵐につかまって彷徨い続けてたんだよ、この爺さんは」
source.english:
“…Ridiculous, isn't it?
Just how long has the old man been wandering around trapped in storms?”

target.text: He gave Kuro, who was clutching the chart tightly, a gentle push forwards towards Noah.
【Kuro】 「Is this okay, Sakuya-san…… for Kuro's sake?」
【Naomasa】 「……Well, yeah. I would be lying if I said I wasn't envious. But when you're dignified like that, you're cool in your own right.」
【Naomasa】 「Everybody wants to be like that. And doing something as cruel as keeping you from that, it's just not something I can really bring myself to do.」
【Naomasa】 「Come on, give old Noah the chart, tell him where land is.」
【Naomasa】 「……What a sorry tale, huh. Just how long has this old guy been drifting around, caught in this storm.」

source.japanese:
───一方その頃。
　この木造の島の中の人知れぬ一角。
　物の綾目も判らぬ暗闇の中、ぼう、と丸い火が灯る。
　洋燈を翳[かざ]した密航者だ。
source.english:
Meanwhile,
in an unseen corner of the wooden island,
a round flame glowed in darkness too deep to distinguish one thing from another.
The stowaway, holding up a lantern.

target.text: ───Elsewhere, around that time. In a hidden corner of this wooden island. In a darkness so profound that even the shape of things couldn't be discerned, a round flame flared softly into life. It was the stowaway holding aloft an oil lamp.

source.japanese:
洋燈の光が照らし出した景色を見るに、そこはどうやら島内の地下であるらしい。
　密航者が向かい合っているのは、様々な船の破片や、壊れた船具が堆く積み重なっている巨大な山だ。
source.english:
What the lantern revealed suggested she was somewhere beneath the island's surface.
She faced a great mound of fragments from all sorts of ships, broken gear piled high.

target.text: Judging from the scenery illuminated by the light of the lamp, it appeared to be somewhere underground on the island. And what the stowaway was facing was a great mountain of fragments of various shipwrecks and broken ship equipment piled high.

source.japanese:
彼女はその中から、一本の木柱を見出して、手を差し延べる───と、柱はその長さを縮めながら手の中に収まる。
　鉛筆大になった柱を、腰の革鞄の中にしまいこみながら、囁いた。
source.english:
Among the wreckage she found a wooden post and reached toward it. As the post came into her hand, its great length contracted.
Now no bigger than a pencil, it slipped into the leather bag at her waist. She whispered—

target.text: And from within that, the girl picked out a single wooden post, reached for it───and just like that, the post shrunk in length until it fit within her hand. While stuffing the post now the size of a pencil into the leather bag around her waist, she whispered.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「これで、取り返せた、ミズンの」
source.english: “There. Got it back. The mizzen's…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And that's the mizzen recovered.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「さてこれからの……話だけど」
source.english: “Now, as for what happens next…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So……about what to do from here on.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まあしばらくは、また『密航』だ」
source.english: “Well, back to ‘stowing away’ for a while.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Well, for the time being, it's back to『stowing away』.」

source.japanese:
海図を取り戻し、最も近い陸地の位置をノアに教えてやる事で、老人は行き先をようやく定める。
　長年の宿業から解放され、クロ、元の黒さを取り戻していくかに見える───が。
source.english:
With his chart returned and Kuro telling him where the nearest land lay, the old man finally determined his destination.
Freed from the karmic burden of long years, Kuro seemed to be regaining her original blackness. But—

source.japanese:
ノアは笑みを浮かべた。
　長年の宿願が成就した、晴れやかな笑み、などではなく、人間の陰惨で陰険で底意地の悪い、依怙地で悪辣で狡猾な、諸々の負の部分を煮詰めたかの、暗く呪わしい笑みだった。
source.english:
Noah smiled.
Not a bright smile at the fulfillment of a long-held wish. A dark, accursed smile, as though all humanity's grimness, spite, mean spirit, obstinacy, malice and cunning had been boiled down into it.

target.text: Having regained his nautical chart, and with the position of the nearest landmass shown to Noah, the old man finally determined his destination. Released at long last from the karmic burden of long years, Kuro seemed to be regaining her former blackness ───but.

Noah smiled His longstanding desire finally realized, a bright, sunny smile now on his face it was not, no, it was made up of the most cruel and treacherous feelings lurking deep within man; it was obstinate, vicious, and cunning, as if all manner of negative aspects had been distilled, a darkly accursed smile.

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「よくやってくれた、鴉よ」
source.english: “Well done, crow.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「しかしお前は───儂をあまりにも長く待たせすぎた」
source.english: “But you—kept me waiting far too long.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「見てみい、この島を。
　かつての方舟のざまを。
　もうみぃんな、無うなってしまったわっ」
source.english:
“Look at this island.
Look what's become of the ark.
Everything, everything is gone!”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「ここまで儂を待たせたお前、儂から望みの全てを奪い去ったお前を許す事など、やはりできた相談ではないわ」
source.english: “You made me wait all this time. You robbed me of everything I hoped for. Forgive you? No, it cannot be done.”

source.japanese:
【ノア】
「お前は一生そうやって呪われておれ」
source.english: “Stay cursed for the rest of your life.”

target.text: 【Noah】 「You have done well, O crow.」
【Noah】 「However, you have───simply kept me waiting for far too long.」
【Noah】 「Behold this island. The sorry state of my former ark. Aaaaall on it now lost and gone.」
【Noah】 「To forgive you, you who made me wait this long, who took from me all my hope, is simply not an option that I can even entertain.」
【Noah】 「May you remain cursed like that for the rest of your life.」

source.japanese:
呵々大笑して部屋を飛び出していくのノアの、老人とは思われないほど凄まじい勢いはクロはおろか、朔屋に止められないほど。
　そして窓の外から轟いたのは、聞いた事もあり、けして珍しい音ではなかったけれど、こんな細雨に沈潜している島にはおよそ似つかわしくない轟音だった。
source.english:
Laughing uproariously, Noah bolted from the room with a speed astonishing in an old man—too swift for Kuro or even Sakuya to stop.
Then a roar came from beyond the window: familiar enough, by no means rare, yet utterly alien to this island submerged in fine rain.

target.text: Laughing heartily, Noah flew out of the room with such fierce energy belying his age that neither Kuro nor even Sakuya could stop him. And what rumbled from outside the window was a sound he had heard before; it was not an unusual sound by any means, but it was a roaring that seemed utterly out of place on an island so deeply immersed in misty rain.

source.japanese:
エンジンの轟音。
　窓に飛びつくと、ノアは巨大なバイクに跨[またが]り、長衣をたなびかせ走り去っていくまさにその瞬間の、呼びかけはアクセルを拭かす音に掻[か]き消される。
source.english:
The roar of an engine.
They rushed to the window just as Noah raced away astride an enormous motorcycle, his long robe streaming behind him. Their cries were swallowed by the engine's revs.

target.text: It was the roar of an engine. Leaping to the window, they saw Noah straddling a massive motorcycle, his long robe billowing behind him as he sped away, and just in that moment, her call was drowned out by the revving of the engine.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そんな、ひどい……っ！
　ひどいよう、おじい、約束、違うッ」
source.english:
“No, that's cruel…! Cruel, Grandpa!
You promised! That's not what you promised!”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「待って、待ってぇぇ！」
source.english: “Wait! Waaaait!”

source.japanese:
窓から突き出され、差し伸ばされた手、それこそ逃した鳥を求めるようなだが、伸ばしたその彼女が鳥なのだ。ただそれを知る朔屋は諧謔覚えるどころか、おぞましささえ催して、その感覚の隆起はクロに対して非道かも知れないけれど、人はあまりに痛ましい絶望を目の当たりにした時、共感もできず酸で爛[ただ]れるような苦痛さえ心に覚える。自分がそうなったら、との恐れとおぞましさが先に立つ。真の絶望とはそうしたものだ。
　朔屋には、クロの追いすがろうとする手が、死者の沼地から生える白い茸の、夜の舞踏のようにさえ思えて、目を逸らしてしまうほど、おぞましく哀しい。
source.english:
Her hand thrust through the window and reached as though for an escaped bird—yet she herself was the bird. Sakuya knew it, but the irony brought no laughter; it sickened him. Such revulsion might have been cruel to Kuro. Yet confronted with despair too painful to witness, a person may lose even the power of sympathy and feel the heart burn as though eaten by acid. First comes the fear and horror of imagining oneself in that place. Such is true despair.
To Sakuya, Kuro's hand clutching after Noah seemed like a white mushroom sprung from a marsh of the dead, dancing in the night—so horrible and so sorrowful that he had to look away.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「That's awful……! That's so cruel, grandpa, this isn't what you promised!」
【Kuro】 「Wait, WAAAAIT!」

With her hand thrust through the window, outstretched, she was the very picture of someone reaching for a bird, but the girl who reached out was the bird herself. Yet Sakuya could not find the slightest humour in that knowledge, on the contrary, he even felt repulsed, and while this surge of emotion might seem unjustly cruel to Kuro, when people are faced with such heartrending despair, incapable of even empathy, they feel a pain in the heart that sears like acid. All else is overshadowed by the sickening dread of the question: "What if that were me?". That is the essence of true despair.

To Sakuya, Kuro's desperately clinging hands looked even like the nocturnal dancing of white mushrooms sprouting from the swamp of the dead, so repulsive and miserable that he could not help but avert his eyes.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「なんで？　クロ、ちゃんと言われた通りにしたよ？　一生懸命、がんばったよ？」
source.english: “Why? Kuro did everything you said, didn't she? Kuro tried so hard…”

source.japanese: 呼びかけたところで戻る声も老人もあろう筈のなく、とす、と腰を落とした、クロは、体の芯を壊されて、立つ事もままならないよう。まだ綺麗に、とまではいかないけれど、往事の艶を思わせるくらいには戻ってきていた黒の色が、へたり込んだ黒の背中で、腰で。
source.english: No voice answered her, nor would the old man return however she called. Kuro dropped onto her backside with a small thud, as though the core of her body had broken and left her unable to stand. The black returning to her hair was not yet beautiful, but it had recovered enough to recall its former luster. Now it lay across her slumped back and waist—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Why? Kuro did just as was told? Really tried as hard as Kuro could?」

She could call out to him all she wanted, there was surely no way that either the old man himself or his voice would return because of it, and Kuro sunk to the floor with a thunk, the core within her utterly broken, leaving her unable to stay standing. While it could still not be called pretty, enough of the black colour had returned to evoke the lustre of its past glory, visible on her slumped back and at her waist.

source.japanese:
頭頂から流れて、毛先へと。毛先から床にまで伝うと見えたが、そのまま消えて、もう戻らない。
　さながらクロの小さな体に充満した絶望の質量、容積が甚大に過ぎて、体内に戻ってきていた当時の彼女を追い出してしまったかのように。
source.english:
It flowed from the crown of her head down to the ends of her hair. It seemed about to run from those tips onto the floor—but instead it vanished and did not return.
It was as though the mass and volume of despair filling Kuro's slight body had grown too great and driven out the self of long ago that had only begun to return.

source.japanese:
戻らない。
　クロが望んでいた、健やかに、力強く天空を飛翔していたクロ。
　もう、戻らない。
　大いなる叡智を秘めて鎮まる夜の様に、黒かった羽の色。
　もう二度と、戻らない。
　彼女を鳥の中の鳥たらしめていた、誇り、矜持、知恵、全て。
　全て、抜け落ちてしまって、クロに残されたのは、朔屋が知っているクロの色。
　なにも持たない、空っぽの白。
　持ち合わせているのは、血肉だけである事を物語る、眸の赤。
source.english:
It would not return.
The Kuro she had longed for, healthy and strong, flying through the heavens.
That Kuro would not return.
The black of her feathers, like a still night holding great wisdom.
Never, ever to return.
Pride, dignity, intelligence, all that had made her a bird among birds. All had fallen away.
What remained was the color of the Kuro Sakuya knew.
Empty white, possessing nothing.
The red of her eyes: nothing but flesh and blood to call her own.

target.text: It flowed from the top of her head to the tips of her hair. It looked as if it trickled from those tips all the way to the floor, but then it vanished, never to return. It was as if the sheer mass and volume of the despair that permeated Kuro's small body was so immense that it had accidentally driven out the girl of those days who had returned to her place within Kuro's body.

She would not return. She who Kuro had wished for: the healthy, strong Kuro who soared through the heavens. It would return no more. The colour of her plumage: dark as the quiet night that hid within itself sage wisdom. It would never return to her again. What made her a bird among birds: her pride, her dignity, her wisdom, all of it. All of it had come out of her, and all that remained within Kuro was the colour of Kuro that he knew so well. That which had nothing: empty white. And what was testament to the fact that all she had left was her flesh and blood: the red of her eyes.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「なのにどうして───」
source.english: “Then why—”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「So why then───」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……もういや」
source.english: “…Can't stand it anymore.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい、クロ……」
source.english: “Hey, Kuro…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Enough.」
【Naomasa】 「Oi, Kuro……」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「もういや、なんもかも、いや。
　いや、いや、いや」
source.english:
“Can't stand it anymore.
Any of it. No, no, no.”

source.japanese:
打ち振る首さえ、力なく。
　嘆く力も乏しいクロ。
source.english:
Even the shake of her head was weak.
Kuro had scarcely the strength to grieve.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「もうクロ、なにもしたくない。
　なんにも願わない。
　そんなコトするから、こんなに哀しい」
source.english:
“Kuro doesn't want to do anything now.
Won't wish for anything.
Doing that… makes it hurt so much.”

source.japanese:
彼女が願っていたのは、そんなに大それた事だったのだろうか。
　それとも彼女には、願う事さえ、大それていたのだろうか。
source.english:
Had she wished for something so extravagant?
Or was the very act of wishing too extravagant for her?

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Had enough of everything, enough. Enough, enough, enough!」
Even her shaking head was feeble. Kuro lacked in even the strength to grieve.
【Kuro】 「Kuro doesn't want…… to do anything anymore. Doesn't wish for anything. It's all because Kuro did, that Kuro is this sad.」
Was what the girl wished for truly that audacious? Or perhaps, even merely the act of wishing for something itself was the girl asking too much?

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロ、もういい。
　もうどこにも行かない」
source.english:
“Kuro's had enough.
Won't go anywhere anymore.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro……has had enough. Will not go anywhere anymore.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「朔屋さん───ごめんなさい。
　クロに、せっかく、
　クロにたくさんしてくれた」
source.english:
“Mr. Sakuya—Kuro's sorry.
You did so much…
went to so much trouble… for Kuro.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Sakuya-san───sorry. Went to such trouble for Kuro, did so much for Kuro.」

source.japanese:
全てを諦めきって、悲観しきって、クロは。
　朔屋に。謝ったのは、どういう意味なのか。
　判る、けれども。
　朔屋は慟哭した。
source.english:
Kuro had given up on everything and sunk into utter despair.
Now she apologized to Sakuya. What did that apology mean?
He understood.
And Sakuya sobbed in anguish.

source.japanese: もうクロを、己の元に繋ぎとめておく事はできないと、理解してしまったから。
source.english: Because he had understood that he could no longer keep Kuro beside him.

source.japanese: そして結局、願う事、かく在りたいと望む事すら、弱い者には許されていないのだと、また再びここでも学んでしまったから。
source.english: Because here, once again, he had learned that in the end the weak were not allowed even to wish, even to hope to be what they wanted to be.

target.text: Having given up on everything, entirely despondent, Kuro. Apologized. To Sakuya. But what did that even mean? He understood, but even so. Sakuya lamented.
For he had come to realize that he could no longer keep Kuro by his side.
And in the end, he once more had to learn the bitter lesson that the act of wishing, and even the desire to be who you want to be, was not something permitted for the weak.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でも、最後はこんな。
　きっとクロは、
　これから、どこに行っても、
　なにをやってもこんなだ」
source.english:
“But this is how it ends.
Probably wherever Kuro goes from now on, whatever Kuro does, it'll always end like this.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ならクロは、もうどこにも行かない、
　行きたくない」
source.english:
“So Kuro won't go anywhere now.
Doesn't want to.”

source.japanese:
そんな事はない、と言えなかった。
　否定しきれなかったのではなく、そういう言葉を吐こうとした、朔屋の口から漏れたのは嗚咽だったから。
　クロと似たり寄ったりな、嗚咽。
source.english:
He could not say, That's not true.
Not because he couldn't deny it outright, but because when he tried to speak, what escaped his mouth was a sob.
A sob much like Kuro's.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But, it always ends like this. Kuro is sure that, no matter where Kuro goes from here, no matter what Kuro does, it'll end like this.」
【Kuro】 「Then Kuro won't go anywhere anymore, doesn't want to go.」
That's not true at all, he couldn't say. It was not that he was unable to deny it, but when he tried to utter those words, all that came from Sakuya's mouth was sobbing. A sobbing similar to Kuro's.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「誰かとあうから、哀しいことになるから。
　だったらもう、誰とも会いたくない」
source.english:
“Meeting someone… makes sad things happen.
So Kuro doesn't want to meet anyone anymore.”

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロは、ここにいるよ。
　もうここでいいよ。
　ここ、もともと、
　クロがいたところだったんだし」
source.english:
“Kuro will stay here.
Here will do now.
It's… where
Kuro was in the first place.”

source.japanese:
あれほど、共感と同情と、そして愛情を抱いた少女なのに、朔屋はクロを───ここから連れ出す事も、まして残って二人で共にいる事も、できそうになかった。
　恐かった。
source.english:
For all his fellow feeling, his sympathy, his love for the girl, Sakuya seemed unable even to take her away from here,
let alone remain here with her. He was afraid.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「It's because you meet someone that something sad will happen. Then Kuro doesn't want to meet anyone anymore.」
【Kuro】 「Kuro……will be right here. Will be fine staying here now. Besides, this place is where Kuro came from in the first place.」
He had so much sympathy, compassion, and love for this girl, and yet, Sakuya could───not bring himself to take Kuro with him away from here, to say nothing of staying here with her. He was terrified.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「───さいなら、朔屋さん」
source.english: “───Goodbye, Mr. Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「───Goodbye, Sakuya-san.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「さいなら。
　クロのこと、抱いてくれた人」
source.english:
“Goodbye.
Goodbye to the man who held Kuro.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Goodbye. The man who would embrace Kuro.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「───さいなら。
　クロの好きな、朔屋さん」
source.english:
“Goodbye—
Mr. Sakuya, whom Kuro loves.”

source.japanese:
朔屋は。
　情けなくて最低の朔屋は。
　このまま彼女と一緒にいたら、いずれ彼女の中に自分の弱さを見いだして憎むようになるだろうとか、依存し合って離れられない奇形の生き物のようになるだろうとか。
　クロに吸いついて、彼女を食いつぶしてしまうだろうとか。そうなる事が容易に予想できる自分が恐かった。
　だから朔屋もまた、クロに負けず劣らず、弱虫なのだった。そういった弱者同士の愛憎すらからも、逃げてしまうくらいに。
source.english:
Sakuya.
Pitiful, worthless Sakuya.
If he stayed with her, he might one day see his own weakness in her and come to hate her; or they might depend upon each other until they became a malformed creature that could not be separated;
or he might cling to Kuro and feed upon her until she was spent. He was afraid of himself, of how readily he could foresee these things.
And so Sakuya, too, was every bit as much a coward as Kuro. Coward enough to flee even the love and hatred between two weak people.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「───Goodbye. Kuro's beloved Sakuya-san.」

Sakuya. Pathetic, despicable Sakuya. If he stayed with the girl like this, perhaps he would eventually discover his own weaknesses somewhere within the girl and come to loathe her, or perhaps they would become like malformed creatures dependent on each other, unable to let go. He would probably come to latch on to Kuro, and devour the girl. He was terrified of himself for being able to so easily imagine such a thing. Therefore, Sakuya was also a coward, and no less one than Kuro. To the point where he would even run away from the love and hatred born between these mutual weaklings.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「───さいなら。みんな。
　信天翁号───」
source.english:
“Goodbye. Everyone.
Albatross—”

source.japanese: これが朔屋の、せめぎ合う諸々の気持ちで啜[すす]り泣き、涙と鼻水で咽頭を一杯にしていたから、クロに惜別も、慰留も、共にいたいとも告げる事もできないままで、それまで一つに寄り添うていたものが二つに離れた、どうしようもなく歯切れ悪くみっともなく思い切りも悪い、これが朔屋の、クロとの別れなのだった。
source.english: This was Sakuya's farewell to Kuro: sobbing as all those feelings fought within him, throat clogged with tears and snot, he could neither offer a word of parting, beg her to stay, nor say he wished to remain with her. What had nestled together as one until then drew apart into two. Halting, shameful, irresolute—this was how Sakuya left Kuro.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「───Goodbye. Everybody. The Albatross───」

Because Sakuya was sobbing with all his many conflicting feelings struggling against each other, his pharynx choked with tears and snot, he remained unable to tell Kuro of his sorrow at their parting, to persuade her to stay, to convey to her how dearly he wished to be with her; what had hitherto nestled together as one now split into two───it was hopelessly awkward, pathetic, and entirely lacking in closure: that was Sakuya's parting from Kuro.

source.japanese:
───かくしてノアの妄執は忌まわしい形で晴らされ、島を取り巻く嵐も晴れた。
　しかし、蹌踉と港へと戻る朔屋は一人。
　乗りこむ時には伴っていた小柄でやせっぽちで白い少女のいない、一人きり。
source.english:
And so Noah's obsession was satisfied in a loathsome way. The storm around the island cleared.
But Sakuya stumbled back to the harbor alone.
Alone, without the little, thin, white girl who had accompanied him ashore.

target.text: ───Thus, Noah's obsession was dispelled in a most abominable manner, and the storm enclosing the island also cleared. However, as he stumbled back to the jetty, Sakuya was alone. And when he boarded the ship, it was without the petite, scrawny, white girl who had been accompanying him; he was all by his lonesome.

source.japanese:
朔屋が港に駆け戻るまでは信天翁号は待機しており、青年を迎え入れる。
　航海士や水夫長は、朔屋の傍らにクロがいない事に何事か言いかけたが、虚脱しきった朔屋を見て、そのあまりに物哀しく呆けた顔に結局は何も言わず、船の抜錨作業に追い立てた。
source.english:
The Albatross waited until Sakuya came running back to the harbor, then took him aboard.
The navigators and boatswain began to ask why Kuro was not beside him. But they saw his total exhaustion, the desolate vacancy of his face, and in the end said nothing. They merely hurried him into the work of weighing anchor.

source.japanese: そうして信天翁号は、また日常に、やくざな航海家業に立ち戻っていったのだけど。
source.english: Thus the Albatross returned to its ordinary life, its disreputable business of voyaging. But—

target.text: The Albatross stood by until Sakuya had rushed all the way back to the jetty, welcoming the young man aboard. The first mates and the Bosun were about to say something or other to Sakuya when they saw Kuro not being by his side, but upon seeing how despondent Sakuya was, the utterly dejected and vacant look on his face, they ultimately said nothing and instead sent him off to help with weighing anchor.
Thus, the Albatross went back to her daily routine, returning to her disreputable seafaring trade.

source.japanese: ───とある船乗りが港の酒場で酔った仲間相手に、こちらも酔った口調で何事か語っている。
source.english: In a harbor tavern, a sailor spoke drunkenly to his drunken companions.

source.japanese:
───だからよう。本当なんだって。
　───その島は、みんな木で出来てやがんのよ。家も道路もなんもかも。
source.english:
“I'm telling you, it's true.
The whole island's made of wood. Houses, roads, everything.”

source.japanese:
───商船航路からは外れてるし、普通だったら誰もいかねえ海域だ。
　───でも俺らの船、嵐に流されてさ。
source.english:
“It's off the merchant routes. Nobody'd normally go into that stretch of sea.
But our ship got blown there in a storm.”

source.japanese:
───修理と、補給でもできりゃあと島に乗りこんでみたんだが、誰もいやしねえ。
　───島には街もあったが、まるごと一つゴーストタウンだ、ありゃあ。
　───しかも家ン中には獣の骨ばっかでさ、薄気味悪いったらなかったぜ。
source.english:
“Went ashore, thought maybe we could get repairs and supplies. Not a soul there.
There's a town on the island, but the whole thing's a ghost town.
And inside the houses, nothing but animal bones. Creepy as hell.”

source.japanese:
───めぼしいものもなんにもなくって、さっさと修理だけ済ませるかって戻ろうとした時だ。
　───そいつが、影から覗いてたんだよ。
source.english:
“There wasn't a damned thing worth taking, so we figured we'd finish the repairs and clear out.
We were heading back when we saw it peering from the shadows.”

source.japanese:
───骨も気味悪かったが、そいつも気味悪かったな。
　───まっ白な髪に、真っ赤な目の、白子ってやつだ。
　───貧相な小娘でよ。びくびくと怯えてやがったな。
source.english:
“Bones were creepy enough, but so was she.
Snow-white hair, bright red eyes. An albino, they call it.
A scrawny little girl. Scared and jumpy.”

source.japanese:
───俺らが何か言う前に逃げていっちまった。だから後は知らねえよ。
　───まあ、好きでそこにいるんだろ。
source.english:
“Ran off before we could say a word. Don't know what happened after that. Well,
I suppose it's where she wants to be.”

source.japanese:
───お似合いだったぜ、あの辛気臭い島とはさ。
　───ああ、幽霊だったのかも知れねえな。
source.english:
“She suited that dreary island, all right.
Ah, maybe she was a ghost.”

source.japanese:
───だが生きていようと死んでいようと、同じこったろうよ。
　───あんな島で一人でさ。
source.english:
“But alive or dead, what's the difference?
All alone on an island like that.”

source.japanese: ───人間、ああいう暮らしはしたくねえなあ───
source.english: “No one would want to live like that—”

target.text: ───In a port bar, a certain sailor spoke of something to his drunken companion, telling his tale with a drunken lilt of his own.
───I'm telling you. It's true, man. ───That island, the whole thing's made of wood. The houses, the streets, all of it.
───It's off the main merchant routes, in an area of the sea that nobody would normally visit. ───But our ship, she was taken by the storm.

───We went on the island hoping to get some repairs done, restock on supplies, but there was nobody there. ───There was a town on the island, but that whole place was like one big ghost town. ───And there was nothing but the bones of beasts within the houses. It was incredibly unsettling.
───There was nothing all that interesting, so right as we were about to head back to just get the repairs over and done with. ───That thing was peeking at us from the shadows.
───The bones were creepy, but so was that thing. ───Pure white hair, blood-red eyes. It was one of those albinos. ───It was a scrawny little girl. She was even trembling with fear.
───She ran away before we could say anything. So I don't know what happened to her after that. ───Well, I guess she's only there because she wants to be.
───She made a great match with that gloomy island. ───Ah, maybe she was a ghost.
───But whether she's dead or alive, it's all the same, aye? ───On an island like that, all by herself.
───No man would want to live that kind of life───

source.english: —A New Chapter—

target.text: ───Interlude───

source.japanese: 罐の火の一部が零れ落ちたかに一対の赤い光は床に溜まった影の中で灯る。しばし連星のように留まっていたが、ふっと消え失せた、としか思えないほどの速き起こりで、闇中を走ったのである。光の緒も引かない程の瞬速の、動きも小さな跫音も人間の感覚では追い切れない域にあったが、生き物を追う生き物として有史以前から完成された存在が船にはある。
source.english: A pair of red lights burned in the shadows pooled on the floor, as if a little of the furnace fire had spilled there. For a while they remained like binary stars, then moved so abruptly that they seemed simply to go out. They were racing through the dark. Too swift even to trail a thread of light, their movements and tiny footfalls exceeded human senses. But aboard this ship lived another creature, perfected since before recorded history for the pursuit of living prey.

source.japanese: 物陰から新たな影が生じて、しかしこちらは質量血肉を備えた影の、その身のこなしのしなやかな事流体の如く、疾き事弾丸の如く、先に消えた一対の光を追って影から出でて影にと沈む。一瞬、罐から漏れる明かりを弾いて、一対の光が爛[らん]と輝く。刹那の光輝───
source.english: A new shadow emerged from concealment. This one possessed mass, flesh, and blood. Fluid in its supple movements, swift as a bullet, it pursued the vanished pair of lights, emerging from shadow and sinking into shadow again. For an instant, another pair flared, reflecting the light escaping from the furnace. A moment's brilliance—

target.text: As if a part of the furnace fire had spilled over, a pair of red lights lit up the shadows that pooled on the floor. For a time, they held still like binary stars, and then they vanished: they ran through the dark so quickly that it could only seem that way, at least. With such blindingly quick speed that they did not even leave behind a trail of light, both their movements and tiny footsteps were now in the realm where human senses could no longer follow them, but there was an existence aboard this ship that had perfected the art of hunting its fellow life since prehistoric times.

A new shadow was born from the shade, however, this was a shadow endowed with mass, with flesh and blood; its carriage elegant as flowing liquid, speed like that of a bullet, it chased after the just-vanished twin lights, emerging from the shadow before sinking into it once more. For an instant, the light leaking from the furnace flared up, twin lights glittering brilliantly. A split second of radiance───

source.japanese: 影の溜まりの中ではどのような攻防が繰り広げられているのか定かではなかったけれど、長くは続かず、暗がりの奥で、「ヂッ！」と短く詰まった、生き物の断末魔が悲痛で、同時に生命が生命を奪う事の原初的な悦びを、耳にした者に思い出させた。
source.english: No one could tell what struggle was playing out in those pools of shadow, but it did not last long. From deep in the dark came a short, strangled squeak—a creature’s agonized death cry, which at the same time reminded all who heard it of the primordial pleasure of one life taking another.

target.text: It was unclear what manner of offence and defence was unfolding within the pooling shadows, but it did not last long, and in the depths of the dark, there sounded a clipped, gasping chirp, what invoked for all who heard it the heartbreaking death throes of a living creature, and at the same time, the primeval joy of one life stealing the life of another.

source.japanese: やがて影からぬう、と出でても影がそのまま凝[こご]ったかに黒い、所々真夜中の流星のように白い毛筋を混ぜた毛並みの、信天翁号の番猫宗右衛門が、その逞[たくま]しき顎[あぎと]に丸々太って大なる鼠をぶら下げて。
source.english: Presently the Albatross's watch-cat Soemon emerged, still black as congealed shadow, a few white hairs streaking his coat like meteors in a midnight sky. From his powerful jaws hung an enormous, fat rat.

target.text: At long last, it smoothly emerged from the shadows, though it was black as if the shadows themselves had congealed, a coat of fur streaked in places with fine lines of white like comets soaring across the midnight sky: it was the watchcat of the Albatross, Souemon, with a great mouse so fat it was completely round dangling from his muscular jaws.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……お疲れ様、宗右衛門殿。
　申し訳ないのですが、食事は奥の方でお願いします」
source.english:
“…Well done, Mr. Soemon.
My apologies, but would you please take your meal farther back?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……Excellent work, Lord Souemon. My sincerest apologies, but I must request that you partake in your meal in the back.」

source.japanese: 機関長でさえ口調に敬意を表すこの黒猫は、ただ船の害獣をしかと仕留めた事を告げたかっただけと見え、大人しく影の中に戻って、貪り喰らう様こそ見せなかったものの、肉を割き骨を噛み砕く音が機関室の重低音の中で異様なまでに生々しかった。朔屋はこの咀嚼音に機関長振る舞いのウイスキイ垂らした紅茶に血の味さえ混じるような悪心地に見舞われたが、宗右衛門が相手では抗議も申し立てられない。彼以外の、機関室の卓に着いた男達には猫の食事の音など屁とも感じぬ豪毅の者ばかりで、水夫長はむしろ賞賛の頷[うなず]きを何度か繰り返してから、
source.english: Even the chief engineer addressed the black cat with respect. Apparently Soemon had only wanted to announce his successful disposal of a shipboard pest. He returned obediently to the shadows. They were spared the sight of him devouring it, but the tearing flesh and crunching bones sounded unnaturally vivid amid the engine room's deep rumble. Sakuya felt sick, as if the tea the engineer had served him, laced with whiskey, had acquired a taste of blood. But one could hardly lodge a complaint against Soemon. The other men at the engine-room table were all stalwarts who did not give a damn about a cat eating. The boatswain, in fact, nodded several times in approval before speaking.

target.text: This black cat, whom even the Chief Engineer spoke to with the utmost respect, appeared to just have wanted to report that he had dealt the killing blow to one of the pests aboard the ship without leaving room for doubt, for he quietly returned to the shadows once more, and though he did not show any outward signs of devouring his kill, the sounds of parting flesh and crushing bone were abnormally vivid even in the deep thrumming of the engine room. This sound of mastication left Sakuya with an uncomfortable feeling in his chest, like the black tea with whisky he had been treated to by the Chief Engineer was even beginning to taste a little of blood, but when it came to Souemon, he had no room to raise any objections.

Sakuya aside, all the men seated at this table in the engine room were of a hardy breed, men who cared less for the sound of a cat's meal than they would a fart in the wind; in fact, the Bosun nodded repeatedly in approval, and then,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「じゃあ、クソ鬱陶しいネズ公を宗右衛門が片づけてくれたところで、さっきの話の続きといこう」
source.english: “Now that Soemon's dealt with that damned nuisance of a rat, let's get back to what we were discussing.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Alright, now that Souemon has dealt with that obnoxious little shit of a mister mousey, let's get back to the talking.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ええと、どこまで話したっけか、王よ？」
source.english: “Where had we got to, Wang?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Uhm, where were we again, Wang?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「いや、私達はそもそも何故こんな会合を開いているのでしたか？」
source.english: “Well, why were we holding this meeting in the first place?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「No, why were we even holding this assembly here to begin with?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……。いや、すまん。
　あんたに聞いて悪かった。
　おい朔屋、なんだったか？」
source.english:
“…Sorry. My mistake, asking you.
Sakuya, what was it?”

source.japanese:
近々の事を記憶していられないという機関長の持病は水夫長も知るところであったし、折り合いは悪いとはいえ水夫の長と機関室の長、お互いを立てるところは心得ていて、軽く詫びてから朔屋に続きを促した。
　これでいつもの朔屋なら、他の男がする真面目な話なぞ聞き流していてまた水夫長の鉄拳を喰らうところであったが、この時に限っては話の再開を待ち侘びだったので、遅滞なく答えられた。
source.english:
The boatswain knew of the engineer's chronic inability to remember recent events. They might not get along, but the head of the sailors and the head of the engine room understood when to show each other respect. He apologized briefly, then prompted Sakuya.
Ordinarily Sakuya would have let other men's serious conversation flow past him, earning another blow from the boatswain's fist. This time, however, he had been eager for them to resume. He answered without delay.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺らがなんで集まってるのかは、正直俺もよく判りませんがね、話してたのはほらあの、ウミヒトの事だった」
source.english: “Honestly, I don't really know why we're all here either. But we were talking about that thing, you know. One of the Sea People.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……. No, my bad. Shouldn't have asked you. Oi, Sakuya, where were we again?」

It seemed like the Bosun was also aware of the Chief Engineer's chronic disease that left him unable to remember recent events, and for all that they got along like oil and water, the chief of the sailors and the chief of the engine room each had an understanding of where the other stood, so while offering a minor apology, he instead urged Sakuya to continue. Were this the usual Sakuya, he would once again suffer the iron fist of the Bosun for never paying attention to anything serious when spoken by another man, but this time alone, he was the one impatiently waiting for their conversation to continue, and he answered with no delay.
【Naomasa】 「Honestly, the reason why we're gathered here is not really something I understand myself, but we were talking about, you know, that Umihito thing.」

source.japanese:
───ウミヒト───
　
　深淵から浮上し来[きた]る、巨大な白いヒトガタ。嵐と追っ手から逃れ仰せたものの、今度は官憲に進路を阻まれた信天翁号の前に現れたる異形の存在。
　こうして朔屋達が機関室に集って話をしていられるという事は、官憲の巡視艦から逃れられたという事実を物語っており、あの異常事態からいかな流れを辿って今に至るのか、実に興味深く───
source.english:
The Sea People.
An enormous white human shape rising from the abyss: the strange being that appeared before the Albatross after she escaped storm and pursuit only to have an official patrol vessel bar her way.
Sakuya and the others were now sitting peacefully in the engine room, so plainly the Albatross had escaped the patrol. By what course had that extraordinary crisis led them here? A deeply fascinating question—

target.text: ───Umihito─── Surfacing from the deepest abyss, a giant, white humanoid. Though they had just managed to make good their escape from their pursuers and the storm, their course forwards was now blocked by the authorities; it was then that it had suddenly emerged before the Albatross, a grotesque existence.

And so the fact that Sakuya and the rest were gathered here in the engine room and speaking thus was a testament to the fact that they had also managed to escape from the patrol boat helmed by the authorities, but just what course of events had brought them from that absurd situation to the present? In truth, it was an incredibly fascinating───

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう、そうだったそうだった。
　マアしかしあんなこたァどうでもいいんだ。
　それより下級水夫達が最近バラックで作ってるあれの事だが」
source.english:
“Right, right. That was it.
Well, none of that matters. What's more important is what the junior sailors have been making in their shack lately.”

source.japanese: 実に興味深く、深く───思っていたのは朔屋だけだったようで、水夫長には釣った魚がミノカサゴ、見た目は派手だが毒がある、喰って喰えない事はないが面倒くさいと実にあっさり投げ出して、さっさと次の話に入る、ウミヒトへの興味はまるで無し。
source.english: Deeply fascinating—or so Sakuya alone appeared to think. To the boatswain, the Sea Person was a lionfish hauled up on a line: showy, venomous, technically edible, and far too much trouble. He tossed the subject aside just as readily and moved on, displaying not the least interest in the being.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right, that's it, that's it. But come on, what does that thing even matter? More importantly, about that stuff the deck boys recently made in one of the shacks.」

It truly was fascinating, very much so ───and the only one who seemed to think so here was Sakuya, for to the Bosun, it was like the fish he'd caught had turned out to be a luna lionfish, and while it looked real flashy, it was also venomous, and so finding it too bothersome to weigh if he should eat it or not, he instead just nonchalantly tossed it back in the ocean, promptly moving on the next topic: he held basically no interest in the Umihito.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「あいつら、バラックの中に土盛って、野菜なんぞを育てているようだが……。
　うまくいくと思うか？」
source.english:
“They've piled up soil in the shack and seem to be growing vegetables…
Think they'll make it work?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Those guys have made a pile of dirt inside a shack, and it looks like they're growing vegetables or something in there, but……. You think it's gonna work out?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「支那では、古代より船の道中、大豆を育ててモヤシにしていたという例もある。お陰で壊血病の害も抑えられたという。その辺りは西洋の船乗りより知恵深かったというところでしょう」
source.english: “There are accounts of soybeans being grown into sprouts aboard ships in China since ancient times. This is said to have reduced the harm done by scurvy. In that respect, they were wiser than Western sailors.”

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「だから、例がない事ではない。
　ただし、水夫君達が成功させられるかどうかはまた別だね」
source.english:
“So it is not without precedent.
Whether our sailors can succeed is another question.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「In China, there are examples from the ancient past of men growing soybeans on ships and eating the beansprouts as they sailed. As a result, they were able to limit the harmful effects of scurvy. It is said that, in this respect, they actually held a greater wealth of knowledge than Western sailors at the time.」 (TN: The Chief Engineer uses the old Japanese term for China here, "Shina", written "支那". After World War II, the Chinese claimed it was discriminatory, used derogatorily in the Sino-Japanese Wars, and so it is generally avoided now, replaced with "Chuukoku", written "中国", the same kanji as in Chinese.)
【Chief Engineer】 「As such, it is not unprecedented. However, whether the sailors will find success in their endeavours or not is a different story altogether.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だよなあ。しかもあいつらが植えてんのはモヤシなんぞよりむつかしい。トマトやニガウリあたりだ」
source.english: “Exactly. And what they've planted is harder to grow than sprouts. Tomatoes and bitter melons.”

source.japanese:
下級水夫達は細心の注意を払って育成に励んでいるようだが、なにしろ陸とは勝手が違う海の上、屋内とはいえバラックの造りはいい加減で、潮風が入れば時には大波に激しく揺すられる、先ほど宗右衛門が仕留めたとはいえ、鼠は後を絶たず、奴らは苗も囓る。なにより水夫君達は水夫であって農夫ではない。
　見込みはあまり高くはなかろうというのが座のおおよその意見だった。
source.english:
The junior sailors seemed to be tending their plants with the greatest care. But life at sea was not life on land. Indoors or not, the shack was poorly built. Salt wind found its way in; heavy waves sometimes shook it violently. Soemon had just dispatched a rat, but there were always more, and they gnawed seedlings too. Above all, these sailors were sailors, not farmers.
The general opinion around the table was that their chances were not particularly good.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right you are. Moreover, they've planted something a lot more complicated than some beansprouts. Stuff like tomatoes, bitter melons.」

The sailors seemed to have paid close attention to the finer details, making great efforts to nurture the plants, but they were out on the ocean, a place very different from land, and even if it was inside a building, the construction of the shacks was quite perfunctory; when the salty sea breeze came blowing, they would at times be made to violently shake and jolt by the surging waves, and even if Souemon had just put one down, there was also no end to the mice, and they would nibble on the saplings. And most pressing of all, the sailors were sailors, not farmers. It didn't seem like they should expect too much from it: that was the general opinion of those gathered here.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まあ、うまくいったらめっけもの、ってところだろ。飯にも幅が増える」
source.english: “Well, if it works, that'll be a bonus. Give us more variety at meals.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well, if things go well, it'll be a nice bonus, something like that. It'll add some variety to our meals.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「て訳で朔屋、手伝ってやれとは言わんが、邪魔したり生りかけの実をかっぱらったりするんじゃねえぞ。水夫共の機嫌を損ねるといろいろ面倒だからな」
source.english: “So, Sakuya. I'm not telling you to help, but don't get in their way or steal the fruit before it's ripe. Annoying those sailors makes all sorts of trouble.”

source.japanese: がっちり釘を刺されて朔屋、自分が信用されていない事はもちろん面白くなかったけれど、それよりウミヒトの話題が流されてしまったのが納得いかない。
source.english: A firm warning. Naturally, Sakuya disliked being so distrusted, but what bothered him more was having the subject of the Sea People brushed aside.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しませんてそんな事ぁ。
　てか、ウミヒトの方が気になるよ俺は。
　ありゃ一体なんだったのか───」
source.english:
“I wouldn't do anything like that. Anyway,
I'm more interested in the Sea Person.
What in the world was that thing—?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So with that said, Sakuya, while I won't tell you to help them out, don't get in their way or pilfer whatever fruits they manage to grow. It's always a heap of trouble when the sailors get in a bad mood.」

Given an astute warning, it wasn't that Sakuya found it amusing to not be trusted in the slightest, of course, but the thing he was most displeased with was that the topic of the Umihito had been completely glossed over.
【Naomasa】 「I wouldn't do something like that. But hey, I'm more concerned about the Umihito. What in the world was that thing───」

source.japanese: あの時浮上したウミヒトは───
source.english: The being that had risen from the sea that day—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺達だけ行かせたけれど、巡視船だけ通せんぼして───」
source.english: “It let us through, but blocked the patrol vessel—”

source.japanese: まるで、信天翁号を助けるように───
source.english: As though it were helping the Albatross—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「この船が得体の知れないなぁもともとだが、
あんな化け物とも縁があるとはさすがにびっくりだ。どういう事なんですよ、水夫長」
source.english:
“This ship's always been mysterious,
but I never expected it to have ties to a monster like that. What was all that about, Bosun?”

source.japanese: ───水夫達の菜園だ何だより、よほどそちらの方が重大事ではないかと食い下がるも水夫長ははんと鼻を鳴らして取りあわず、
source.english: Surely that was far more important than the sailors' vegetable garden? He persisted, but the boatswain merely snorted and refused to engage.

target.text: The Umihito that surfaced back then was───
【Naomasa】 「It only allowed us to leave, and it only denied the patrol boat passage───」
Almost as though it was…… coming to the Albatross' aid───
【Naomasa】 「I already knew this ship was one big enigma, but I'm certainly shocked to find she shares some kind of connection with a monster like that. What is all that about, Bosun?」
───But though he kept pressing that this was a matter far more important than the sailors' vegetable garden or whatever, the Bosun simply snorted with a "hmpf", not concerning himself with it at all,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「俺だってあれがなんなのかは知らねえし、
　べつにどうでもいいじゃねえか、
　だいたい二週間も前のコトだろうが」
source.english:
“I don't know what it was either.
And who cares?
It was two weeks ago, anyway.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「It's not like I know what that thing is either, and does it really even matter? It's already been two weeks since it happened.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おい殺し屋、
　てめえはなんぞ意見はあるか？」
source.english:
“Hey, assassin.
Got anything to say?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Oi, murderer, you have any opinion on this?」

source.japanese: 何故か彼までこの場に呼ばれていた、智里は、先程から懐手に腕組みで、黙然と卓に顔をうつむけ考えこんでいる様子、と見えたが、かくりと頭がのめった、船を漕いでいる。呼びかけに目を覚まして大欠伸、悪びれるところがない、実に悠然としたものである。
source.english: For some reason, Tomosato had been invited too. All this time he had sat with his arms folded inside his clothes, his head bowed toward the table, silently considering—or so it seemed, until his head dipped. He was nodding off. The question woke him, and he gave a great yawn without the slightest embarrassment. Perfectly at ease.

target.text: One could wonder why he'd even been called to this place, for Tomosato had been crossing his arms inside his kimono for some time now, looking down at the table in silence as if deep in thought, or so it seemed, but his head lurched forward: he was nodding off. He awoke as he was called upon with a great yawn, not a hint of shame to be seen; in fact, he was entirely composed.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……おお。この部屋ぁ陽気がよくって眠っちまったい。で、なんだって？」
source.english: “…Oh. Nice and warm in here. Fell asleep. What was that?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ウミヒトの事だよ。あんた、あれ見てなんか言ってたじゃないか。なんぞ心当たりとかは……」
source.english: “The Sea People. You said something when you saw that thing. Any idea what it was…?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Ooh. The climate down in this room makes me real sleepy. So, you were saying?」
【Naomasa】 「We're talking about the Umihito. Hey, didn't you say something when you saw it? Like you had some kind of idea about what it……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「『小学館入門百科シリーズ三二：妖怪なんでも入門』一四六ページ参照、だ」
source.english: “See page 146 of Everything You Need to Know About Monsters, volume thirty-two of Shogakukan's Beginner's Encyclopedia series.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はあ？」
source.english: “Huh?”

source.japanese: すらすらと諳んじた時、蒼い眸[ひとみ]が凛とした光を流して、機関室の赤い薄明かりの中で怜悧とあったが、台詞がなんとも手前勝手に垂れ流し、後は説明もない。本読みの水夫長や博学多識の機関長にも心当たりのない出版社と書名で、朔屋のみならず二人にも首を傾げさせる。この男の物言いと来たら何時でも此[こ]れ式[しき]の、彼自身にしか意味が判らない事ばかり。
source.english: As he reeled off the citation from memory, his blue eyes shed a stern, lucid light, keen amid the engine room’s dim red glow. Yet he had tossed out the words solely for his own satisfaction and offered no explanation afterward. Neither the bookish boatswain nor the erudite engineer recognized the publisher or the title; both cocked their heads along with Sakuya. The man always talked this way: nothing but remarks that made sense to himself alone.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Consult page 146 of 『The Shougakukan Encyclopediac Primer Series 32: Yokai for Dummies』」 (TN: Shougakukan is a real publisher of encyclopedias among much else in Japan. The "妖怪なんでも入門" is a real book, lit. "Introduction to all things yokai", published in 1974, written and illustrated by Mizuki Shigeru, who was a leading figure on the topic of yokai. He is also known, among many other things, for creating the manga "GeGeGe no Kitarou".)
【Naomasa】 「Haah?」

As he smoothly recited that from memory, a piercing, dignified light flowed from those azure eyes, a sagacious gleam within the dim red light of the engine room, but the line itself was a stream of awfully self-serving drivel with no explanation following it. Upon hearing a book title from a publishing company that neither the bibliophilic Bosun nor the extensively erudite Chief Engineer knew of, it was not just Sakuya who was left tilting his head quizzically, but the other two as well. The man's diction was ever thus: riddled with cryptic turns of phrase that only he himself could hope to fathom.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ともかく、海坊主かなんかの類だろ。
　俺が聞いたモノとはちと様子が違うようだが、まあ世界は広い。何があったっておかしかねえやな」
source.english:
“Anyway, some sort of sea monk, I suppose.
A little different from what I've heard of, but it's a big world. Nothing would surprise me.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Anyway, it's probably like some kind of Umibouzu. It's a bit different from the ones I've heard of, but the world's a big place. Anything can happen, really.」 (TN: An Umibouzu, written "海坊主", is a Japanese yokai. It takes the form of a giant, black, humanoid being, often encountered by ships at night, where a calm sea suddenly surges, only for a bald head to surface and destroy or damage the ship.)

source.japanese:
【智里】
「だいたい餅は餅屋で、海の事なら船乗りのあんた達だろうが」
source.english: “And you leave things to the experts. You're the sailors. The sea's your business.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「To begin with, every man knows his business best, so matters of the sea are best left to sailors like you, right?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「抜かせよ、てめえだって殺し屋てぇ言いながら、標的のこれと仲良く酒呑んでんじゃねえか。殺るンならさっさと殺りやがれよ、俺はとめねえから」
source.english: “Spare me. You call yourself an assassin, but here you are having a friendly drink with your target. If you're going to kill him, get on with it. I won't stop you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ろくでもない事思い出させないでくれよ水夫長。ていうか、あんたも水夫の長なら止めてくれよな……」
source.english: “…Don't remind him of things like that, Bosun. And if you're the head of the sailors, you ought to stop him…”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「うるせえ、かえって良い厄介払いになるくれえだ。とにかく、こいつも知らねえようだし、ウミヒトの事はこれきりだ」
source.english: “Shut up. Be a good way to get rid of a nuisance. Anyway, he doesn't know either. That's the end of the Sea People.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Cut the crap. You keep calling yourself a murderer, but there you are, knocking 'em back like old chums with your mark. If you're gonna kill him, then get it over with already, I ain't stopping you.」
【Naomasa】 「……Please don't make me remember things best left forgotten, Bosun. Actually, you're the boss of us sailors, so you should stop him……」
【Bosun】 「Shaddup. If anything, he'd be ridding me of a lot of trouble. Anyway, he doesn't seem to know anything either, so that's it for the Umihito.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それで、次の話だが───」
source.english: “Now, next item—”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So then, onto the next topic───」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ところで、私達はそもそも何故こんな会合を開いているのでしたか？」
source.english: “By the way, why were we holding this meeting in the first place?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Incidentally, why are we even holding this assembly here to begin with?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……朔屋。説明してやれ」
source.english: “…Sakuya. Explain it to him.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺だってよくわかんないってば。
　なんで呼ばれたの、俺も智里も」
source.english:
“I told you, I don't know either.
Why did you call me and Tomosato here?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……言ってなかったか？　まあたまには、女子供ぬきでな、船のあれこれの事を確認しておきてえわけだ」
source.english: “…Didn't I say? Well, sometimes I want to go over the ship's affairs without the women and children around.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それでこんな、色気もへったくれもない、むさ苦しい男所帯の寄り合いか……」
source.english: “So that's why it's a gathering of grubby men without a trace of charm…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Sakuya. Explain it to him.」
【Naomasa】 「I told you, it's not like I know that either. Why did you even call for us, Tomosato and me?」
【Bosun】 「……I never told you? Well, every now and then, I like to check in on what's happening around the ship. Without the women and kids around.」
【Naomasa】 「So that's why we're holding this sordid sausage fest with not a hint of sexiness to be found……?」

source.japanese:
朔屋としては、こんな薄暗い機関室で男だらけが額突き合わせてもそもそやっているくらいなら、シサムやキサラ、泪あたりも呼んだ方が見た目的に心が和らぐのにとつい不満を、口の端に上せた途端に水夫長の兇悪な一睨[にら]み。
　男尊女卑云々を賢しく言い出す以前の問題として、水夫長の単純な気分の問題なのだろう。それに付き合わされる朔屋としては色々言いたいところもないでもないが、ここで水夫長の機嫌損ねては後々厄介な事になろうと、卑屈に笑って口を噤んだ。
source.english:
If they were going to huddle together muttering in this gloomy engine room, Sakuya would have preferred to invite Sisam, Kisara, or Rui. The sight of them alone would have soothed his spirits. He let a little of this discontent reach his lips, and received a savage glare from the boatswain.
Before anyone clever started talking about male supremacy, this was probably just the boatswain's mood. Sakuya, obliged to accommodate it, had a thing or two he might have said. But annoying the boatswain now would make trouble later. He smiled cravenly and shut his mouth.

source.japanese: こうして信天翁号が、とにもかくにもあの窮地から逃れ出でてから数週間が経つ。そして過ぎてしまえば喉元の熱いのもなんとやらで、船の主だった面子はもう、あの巨大な白いヒトガタの事など思い煩[わずら]う事をやめていたのだった───
source.english: Several weeks had passed since the Albatross somehow escaped that desperate situation. Danger past, danger forgotten: the ship's principal figures had already ceased to trouble themselves about the enormous white human shape—

target.text: In Sakuya's head, if he had to spend his time squirming in this gloomy engine room while huddled together with a bunch of men, his mind would be visually comforted if they had called Shisamu, Kisara, or maybe Rui for him to look at, but just as that complaint was about to escape his lips, he was met with a vicious glare from the Bosun.

Setting aside any clever talk of male chauvinism and so on, the issue here was likely more fundamental: a matter of the Bosun's temperament. As someone forced to keep him company here, Sakuya had plenty he wanted to say, but he also figured that it would just spell a bunch of trouble later if he upset the Bosun, so with a servile smile, he kept his mouth shut.

Thus, several weeks passed since the Albatross somehow or other managed to escape from its predicament. Just as it is oft said how vows made in storms are forgotten in calms or some such, the leading figures of the Albatross had already ceased to worry about anything regarding that giant, white, humanoid form───

source.japanese:
信天翁号船内食堂の、頭上に乱雲さえ呼びかねないほどの熱気、それも極めて世俗的な欲望で蒸しに蒸された熱気の中にあって、混じり気のない玻璃の鈴弾いたほどに、あまりにも澄明で硬質な響きなのであった。
　
　チン、チロリンと。
　
　───岩手花巻生まれの夭逝した詩人あたりなら、『仮定された有機交流電燈の瞬き』だの『あらゆる透明な幽霊の複合体』とかなんだとか、得意とした言霊の錬金術で幻想的に修辞したであろう澄んだ音色なのだが、鳴らしているのはどこぞの支那そば屋の出前を下げ忘れたままと思しき、双つ喜と雷文がぐるりと縁に廻ったラーメン丼の中で跳ね回る賽子とあっては。なんの、詩的も霊質も蜂の頭もあったものかは。
source.english:
In the Albatross's mess, worldly desire had steamed the air to a fever pitch, enough to summon storm clouds overhead. Yet the sound that rang through it was astonishingly clear and hard, like a bell of pure crystal struck. Tink, tinkle-tink.
A certain poet born in Hanamaki, Iwate,
who died young, might have adorned that lucid sound with ‘the flickering of a hypothetical organic alternating-current lamp’ or ‘a composite of all transparent ghosts,’ working his favorite alchemy of words. But what rang was dice bouncing in a ramen bowl, double-happiness characters and a thunder-pattern border circling the rim, apparently left over from some noodle shop's delivery and never returned. Poetry? Spirit? A bee's head, for that matter? Nothing of the sort.

target.text: Amidst the stifling heat inside the mess hall of the Albatross, a temperature so intense it threatened to conjure even storm clouds overhead, steamed to a boil by exceedingly worldly desires, a sound so remarkably clear and hard, as if a bell of purest glass had been struck, rang out. With a chin-chiro-rin.

───A poet born in Hanamaki, Iwate, who suffered an untimely death would perhaps describe it as 『The flickering of a hypothetical organic alternating-current lamp』or 『A composite of all transparent ghosts』or something of that sort; it was a sound so clear that it would be described in fantastically romantic rhetorical flourishes by specialists in kotodama alchemy. (TN: This is a reference to Miyazawa Kenji, famous Japanese poet, and his collection of poems, Haru to Shura. Kotodama, written "言霊", is a word describing the Japanese belief in the power of words to alter reality. Here it's meant as a wordsmith.)

What produced the sound, however, was a set of dice, bouncing around what someone seemed to have forgotten to clear away after ordering home delivery from some Chinese soba shop; it was a ramen bowl decorated with the Chinese ornamental symbol for double happiness surrounded by an enclosing edge drawn in a raimon pattern. Why, there was nothing poetic, spiritual, or anything worth even a tinker's damn to be found. (TN: Chinese soba, written "支那そば", is one of the earliest names for what we know today as ramen, originating from the first ramen shop in Japan founded in 1910. The raimon pattern, written "雷文", is an ancient Japanese motif that consists of interlocked square spirals, often seen on ramen bowls.)

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「さあさあ、張って悪いは親父の頭、張らなきゃ喰えねえ提灯屋、とくらぁっ」
source.english: “Come on, lay your bets! Don't lay one on your old man's head—but a lantern-maker who won't lay paper can't earn his bread!”

source.japanese: 古典的な掛け声に、龍の刺青も心なしか躍動して、
source.english: At that classic gambling cry, even the dragon tattoo seemed to stir.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Come on, come on, you can slap your money down anywhere but your old man's head, and if he doesn't spread his paper, the lantern seller can't eat, that's how it goes!」 (TN: This is all wordplay and slang that is somewhat challenging to translate, so I will also explain. These are puns on the verb "張る", which can certainly mean to slap or strike, as well as stretching and pasting paper, but it also means to bet. These particular lines are associated with traditional Japanese gambling jargon used to keep the momentum going, and they are classics in Edo-period Japanese entertainment like rakugo.)
With a classic shout of encouragement, his dragon tattoo also seeming to throb with life,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「一ぃ二三ぃ～～っっ」
source.english: “One, two, three!”

source.japanese: 水夫長の灰の眸[ひとみ]も。
source.english: The boatswain's gray eyes, too.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「HIIFUMII～～」 (TN: The game of dice they are playing is called "chinchirorin" in Japanese, known as cee-lo in English. This is what the earlier chin-chiro-rin referred to, with the game having received its name after the sound the dice make when they strike the bowl or the other dice. The Bosun's chant here is referencing the outcome that makes you instantly lose and pass the turn, which is rolling a combination of 1-2-3, read Hi-Fu-Mi. Incidentally, a combination of 4-5-6 is an instant win.)
The bosun's grey eyes.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「一ぃ二三ぃ～～っっ」
source.english: “One, two, three!”

source.japanese: 航海士の双子の青の眸[ひとみ]も───
source.english: And the navigator twins' blue eyes—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「HIIFUMII～～」
As well as the twin first mates' green eyes───

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「さもなきゃ一か、
　いっそションベン……っ」
source.english:
“Or a one!
Better yet, a piss-out…!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If it's not gonna be a one, at least piss away her turn……」 (TN: The term Kisara uses here, "ションベン", literally means piss, but in chinchirorin, it's a term for when the dice fly out of the bowl and the result is invalid.)

source.japanese: 親役は船の黒猫宗右衛門を傍らに伴った、女客彩久津泪の、しかし彼女は賽は振らず、やや下がって優雅に茶などを啜[すす]っている。中盆（振り役）は適当な下級水夫を捕まえて、どんなに負けようともお咎めなしと押しつけたどうやら女客は賽子賭博にはあまり興味がないご様子。
source.english: The banker was their passenger, Rui Irokuzu, with the black cat Soemon beside her. But she did not roll. She sat a little back, sipping tea gracefully. For the actual throwing, she had seized a convenient junior sailor and delegated the job, promising no punishment however much he lost. Apparently the lady had little interest in dice.

target.text: The role of the banker was filled by the female passenger, Irokudzu Rui, who was accompanied by the ship's black cat, Souemon, sitting next to her, but the woman did not throw any dice, instead sitting a short distance away, elegantly sipping on some tea. The nakabon (and shooter) was a random deck boy she had grabbed, pushing the role on him while promising that he would not be penalised no matter how much he lost; it seemed this female passenger did not hold very much interest in gambling with dice. (TN: The nakabon, written "中盆", is an impartial third party who judges in disputes between banker and players, and he serves as the dealer of sorts.)

source.japanese: さて泪に任された下級水夫が振り出した、目まぐるしく転変する三つの賽子の出目を、なんとしても操ってくれようという気合いで睨[にら]みつける目玉は、血走って、ひン剥かれて、後頭部を軽く叩いただけで眼窩から零れ落ちかねない。三者が視線に結集させたこの意念力たるや、精進潔斎に身を削り、修法究めた密の大阿闍梨が儀式執り行う時に、或るいは匹敵するほどであった。
source.english: Now the junior sailor Rui had appointed cast the dice. The boatswain and the twins glared at the three tumbling cubes and their bewildering succession of faces with the fixed resolve to bend them somehow to their will. Their eyes were bloodshot, peeled so wide that the lightest tap to the backs of their heads might have spilled them from their sockets. The psychic force the three concentrated into those gazes was perhaps equal to that of a great adept of esoteric Buddhism, his flesh pared away by fasting and purification, performing a rite at the summit of his discipline.

target.text: Now then, the eyeballs glaring with such intensity at the rapidly shifting eyes of the trio of dice shot by the deck boy that it was as though they were trying to control the outcome, by hook or by crook, were bloodshot, peeled wide open, indeed, it was quite possible they would fall out from their sockets from just a light tap to the back of the head.

The sheer force of will concentrated within the stares of this trio was that of a Daiajari of an esoteric Buddhist sect, one who had undergone great hardships by purifying his body through abstinence of meat, a master of prayer and incantation, when he performed ceremony and rite, or else something that could rival one such as him. (TN: A Daiajari, written "大阿闍梨", is the Japanese word for a Buddhist monk in an esoteric sect who has received the qualification to be an Acharya, and who can also preside over the consecration rituals that confer this status to others.)

source.japanese:
実際、賽子の面に、もう一つくらい穴を増やしそうな勢いで睨[にら]みつけている目線を、食堂の一画に築かれた護摩壇に向けさえすれば、炉の中の奉書を念力で発火させる事も可能であったろう。
　左様護摩壇だ。作法正しく方位もよろしく築かれて、白木の香も真新しい。檀炉に積み上げられた護摩札などは、水夫長、シサム・キサラ、飢えもしるけき野獣の眼光の前には容易く発火点を迎えて燃え上がろう。
source.english:
Indeed, if they turned those stares, fierce enough to bore another pip into a die, toward the fire altar erected in a corner of the mess, they could probably have set the ceremonial papers in its hearth ablaze by will alone.
Yes, a fire altar. Properly built, properly oriented, the scent of its unfinished wood still fresh. The votive slips stacked upon it would readily have reached their ignition point beneath the hungry beast-eyes of the boatswain, Sisam and Kisara.

target.text: In fact, were they to direct this intensely glaring gaze of theirs, so forceful it might well bore another hole into the faces of the dice, towards the gomadan that had been erected by one of the walls of the mess hall, it might even be possible they could set ablaze the housho paper within the fire pit through spiritual force alone. (TN: A gomadan, written "護摩壇", is a ritual altar used in Esoteric Buddhism where offerings are burnt in sacred fire. Housho paper, written "奉書", is a type of Japanese mulberry paper. These days, it is, among other things, used in Shinto rituals or to write down hand-copied sutras.)

Yes, indeed, a gomadan. Constructed not only with proper ritual etiquette, but aligned in the correct orientation too, and the fragrance of the untreated wood was also brand new. (TN: In Estoric Japanese Buddhism, like Shingon or Tendai, the orientation the practitioner faces when praying at a gomadan is highly deliberate. When facing eastwards, for instance, it can symbolize growth and wealth, known as "増益法", read "Zouyaku-hou". Using untreated wood for altars symbolizes purity in Japanese sacred traditions like Shinto and Buddhism.)

The gomafuda piled up within the ritual hearth would, faced with that gaze of a beast well-acquainted with hunger that lingered in the glinting eyes of the Bosun, Shisamu, and Kisara, easily reach their ignition point and burst into flames. (TN: Gomafuda, written "護摩札", are paper talismans with prayers inscribed on them that are burnt within the gomadan.)

source.japanese: その通り、護摩壇だ。檀の前に侍っているのは僧形ならず、信天翁号の下級水夫であったが、朗々と誦している最中の真言には、それこそ阿闍梨はだしの、大なる巌を穿[うが]つ水流のような、極限までに細く鋭く練りこまれた念が張り詰めていた。彼の背後には、同様に結跏趺坐して結印する同僚達が並ぶ。
source.english: Yes, a fire altar. Before it sat not a monk but a junior sailor of the Albatross. Yet the mantra he chanted rang with an intent drawn so fine and keen that it put an adept to shame, like a stream piercing solid rock. Behind him sat his fellows, legs crossed in full lotus, hands forming sacred signs.

source.japanese: 阿闍梨役の下級水夫に導かれた幾重もの詠唱が、水夫長と航海士達の唸り声に絡まり、満ち潮と高まり引き潮と鎮まってはまた満ちて、食堂内の空気を殷々とどよもして。
source.english: Led by the junior sailor playing the adept, their layered chanting twined with the growls of the boatswain and the navigators. Rising like the flood tide, sinking like the ebb, rising again, it made the air of the mess reverberate.

target.text: That's right, a gomadan. The one officiating before the altar wore not the guise of a priest, it was one of the deck boys of the Albatross, but within the mantra currently being sonorously chanted was a spiritual intent honed to the utmost limit until it was as thin and sharp as a stream of water piercing a great boulder, one that could put an Ajari to shame, vibrating with taut intensity. Behind him, his colleagues were lined up, similarly seated in the full lotus position and forming the same mudras.

The multiple layers of chanting conducted by the deck boy assuming the role of Ajari entwined with the roars of the Bosun and the mates, swelling like the rising tide, subsiding like the ebbing tide, then swelling once more, a great rumbling resounding through the air in the mess hall.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「きぇぇぇええ、
　ノウマク サラバタタギャテイビャク、
　一ぃ二三ぃ～～っっ」
source.english:
“Kyeeeee!
Nomaku sarabatatagyateibyaku!
One, two, three!”

source.japanese:
印を結んで。
　首座格の下級水夫が復誦する───「光明真言五光印！」
（参集したその他の下級水夫、次々と指を組む）
source.english:
Hands formed the seals.
The leading junior sailor repeated: ‘The Fivefold Light Seal of the Mantra of Light!’
(The assembled sailors interlaced their fingers, one after another.)

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「KIEEEEEH, NOUMAKUSARABATATAGIYATEIBYAKU, HIIFUMII～～」 (TN: This is part of the Great Mantra of Fudou Myouou (Acala), written "不動明王火界咒". This is primarily used during highly sacred rituals, such as the goma, so the flames may get rid of negative karma and spiritual blockages.)

Form the mudra. The deck boy assuming the role of shuza chanted in response─── 「KOUMYOUSHINGONGOKOUIN!」 (The other deck boys who had gathered joined their fingers one after another.)
