(TN: A shuza, written "首座", is the head of the trainee monks. Koumyou shingon, written "光明真言", is the Mantra of Light. Gokou-in, written "五光印", is probably a stylized reference to an actual mudra in Esoteric Buddhism called the Goshiko-in, written "五色光印", where the right hand is held up with all five fingers spread open.)

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「サラバボッケイビャク───
　一ぃ二三ぃ～～っっ」
source.english:
“Sarababokkeibyaku—One,
two, three!”

source.japanese:
腕を振り。
　復誦───「九字を切り！」
（下級水夫達、ざくざくと虚空に手刀を刻む）
source.english:
Arms swung.
The refrain: ‘Trace the Nine Syllables!’
(The sailors' knife-hands slashed patterns into empty air.)

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「SARABABOKKEIBYAKU─── HIIFUMII～～」

Swing your arms. Chant in response─── 「CUT THE NINE SYMBOLS!」 (The deck boys carved large slices through the air with their hands as the blades.) (TN: "九字を切り", also known as Kuji-Kiri, involves performing a sequence of nine mudras while reciting nine sacred syllables/characters followed by the Sword Mudra, popular among superstitious warriors as a form of battle preparation.)

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「サラバタタラタ───
　一二三か、さもなきゃションベン、
　ＯＢでろぉぉ～～っ」
source.english:
“Sarabatatarata—One-two-three,
or a piss-out!
Out of bounds!”

source.japanese:
髪乱す！
　復誦───「剛力招来～！」
（下級水夫一同、原住民の火踊りのように頭を前に後ろに打ち振り廻る）
source.english:
Hair flew!
The refrain: ‘Summon Mighty Power!’
(All the junior sailors swung their heads back and forth, like an indigenous fire dance.)

source.japanese: 森羅万象、物事の基を極限まで突き詰めていくと「波動」に帰すという、この時食堂に充満したのは、そんな天地開闢をも思わせる音の波、声の震動であり、この域にまで凝縮された祈りなら、賽子の出目など容易く操る筈、きっとそう、そうに決まった、皆が望む一・二・三の目、ラーメン丼の中にそら、降り出されろ。
source.english: Probe the first principles of all creation deeply enough, it is said, and everything resolves at last into “vibration.” What filled the mess at that moment was just such a wave of sound, a vibration of voices suggestive of the very creation of heaven and earth. Prayer concentrated to such a pitch could surely command so trifling a thing as the fall of dice. Surely. It must. The one-two-three they all desired—come, tumble out into the ramen bowl.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「SARABATATARATA─── HI-FU-MI OR PISS IT AWAY, FLY OUT OF BOOOOOUNDS～～!」

Hair in disarray! Chant in response─── 「SUMMON MIGHTY STRENGTH～!」 (All in unison, the deck boys swung and shook their heads back and forth vigorously like tribal fire dancers.) (TN: This is a reference to the 1973 Tokusatsu series "Inazuman", where the protagonist, Watari Gorou, yells "剛力招来" (剛力 meaning mighty strength, 招来 meaning summon or invoke) when he transforms into Sanagiman, one of his transformations.)

It is said that when pursued to its absolute limits, the foundation of all things in creation is reduced to wave motion; such a wave of sound, vocal vibrations that invoked the very creation of the heavens and earth, was what filled the mess hall in this moment, and with prayer so concentrated within this space, they should easily be able to control the likes of some measly pips on a die, they must, of course it was so; behold, let the eyes of one, two, and three that they all desired so rain down upon this ramen bowl.

source.japanese: かくして。
source.english: And so.

target.text: Thus.

source.japanese:
【親役の下級水夫】
「はい───
　四五六！」
source.english:
“Here we are—Four,
five, six!”

target.text: 【Banker deck boy】 「Alright─── four, five, six!」

source.japanese:
沈黙が、場を完膚無きまでに打ちのめしたので。
　シサムとキサラと水夫長の目から、それまでの炎が失せてたちどころにどろどろと濁り、三者共にごんごんごんと食堂の長机に額を打ちつけた音の、くぐもって痛いの重いのなんの。
　なにしろ親の総取りおまけに二倍付けである。
　張っていた子の落胆の程が窺えよう。
　憤懣やるかたなくして、水夫長と航海士は護摩壇で祈っていた下級水夫達に躍りかかっていった。言うまでもなく八つ当たりである。
source.english:
Silence crushed the room utterly.
The fire vanished from the eyes of Sisam, Kisara and the boatswain; in an instant their gazes turned dull and muddy. Thud, thud, thud went three foreheads against the mess hall's long table—and how muffled the blows, how painful, how ponderous.
The banker had swept the table, after all, and at double stakes.
One may imagine the bettors' despair.
With their fury nowhere else to go, the boatswain and the navigators sprang upon the junior sailors praying at the fire altar. Needless to say, it was sheer displaced rage.

target.text: A profound silence completely shattered the atmosphere beyond repair. The flames that had burned so bright hitherto now faded from the eyes of Shisamu, Kisara, and the Bosun as they instantly clouded over, and the trio of thuds from all three slamming their foreheads down on the long table in the mess hall in unison, alas, how muffled, painful, and heavy they were. After all, not only was this a total sweep for the banker, she'd also won double.

One can well imagine how devastated the players who had placed their wagers were. Overcome with uncontrollable fury, the Bosun and the first mates leapt upon the deck boys who had been praying at the gomadan. Needless to say, this was just them venting.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「こーのぉ～～っ、小僧どもめぇっ。
　君らが脇でうんうん唸ってっからっ」
source.english:
“Heyyyy~~, you little brats.
It’s because you’re all groaning away over here…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「YOOOUUUU～～, damn little brats! This is all because you guys were groaning and moaning next to me!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「変な念力集中させてるからっ。出目がめったくったになったじゃないか～っ」
source.english: “It’s ’cause you’re focusing your psychic power all weirdly. Now the dice roll’s all messed up, isn’t it~!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And because you were concentrating some weird spiritual energy. That's why the dice roll was all messed up, riight～? 」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「どどどどうしてくれるっ。
　これで先月の稼ぎが皆溶けたワッ。
　償え、償えようっ」
source.english:
“W-w-what are you going to do about this? All
my earnings from last month are gone.
Make it up to me, make it up to me!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Wh-wh-wh-what are you going to do about this? With this, all our earnings from last month are up in smoke! Atone, atooone!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「君ら一人当たり、幾らで売れるかなぁ～？
　なぁに簡単なお仕事だよ？」
source.english:
“I wonder how much each of you would sell
for~? Don't worry—it's easy work.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I wonder, how much would you guys sell for per head, hmm～? Why, it'll be simple work for you, you know?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そうだとも、心配いらないから。
　白豚みたいにぶよぶよ太った、
　有閑マダムのあそこを舐めたりするだけの、
　簡単なお仕事」
source.english:
“That’s right. Don’t worry.
It’s an easy job—just licking the private
parts of some idle rich lady who’s as flabby
as a white pig.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Oh, to be sure, there is no need to worry at all. It'll only be stuff like licking clean the downstairs of a madame from the leisure class, plump and flabby like a white pig, simple work.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「船のことは心配しなくっていいよ、ほら君達ってば、いつの間にか増えたり減ったりしてるじゃない」
source.english: “Don’t fret about the ship. Come on, you guys—your numbers go up and down before anyone even notices, don’t they?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And no need to worry about the ship, I mean, look, you guys always come and go without any of us noticing, right?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おいおいそいつぁやり過ぎだぜぇ。
　だが小僧ども、貴様等のせいで、
　賽の目がおかしくなったなあ、
　こりゃ事実だ」
source.english:
“Hey, hey, that’s going too far.
But you kids, because of you,
the dice have gone haywire,
that’s for sure.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Oi oi, that's going too far. But you little brats, it is all thanks to you lot that the dice have gone completely sideways, that's the truth.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「でなけりゃあ……六回連続でぇ……」
source.english: “Otherwise… six times in a row…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「If it isn't……then the bank couldn't possibly……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「親の総取りなんかぁ……」
source.english: “The banker taking everything…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Have swept everything……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「出るもんかーーーっっ！」
source.english: “Like hell that would happen!!!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「SIX TIMES IN A ROOOWーーー!」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ようし貴様らっ、今から無意味に上甲板を五〇往復してこい駆け足でッ」
source.english: “All right, you lot! Now go run back and forth across the upper deck fifty times—for no good reason!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Alright you little bastards, go run fifty pointless laps around the upper deck, on the double!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「水夫長がそう言うなら、売っ払うのだけは負かってあげる。
　その代わりに、物見櫓の梯子を意味なく一〇〇回昇り降りだぁ全速で！」
source.english:
“If the boatswain says so, I'll let you off being sold.
In return, you'll climb the lookout-tower ladder up and down a hundred times for no reason—at full speed!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If the Bosun insists, then I'll at least spare you from being sold off. Instead, go climb up and down the ladder to the watchtower one hundred pointless times, at full speed!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「キサラが負けるならあたしだって勘弁してあげよう、そうね、今から海に飛びこんで、竜骨潜り五往復ってとこでどうよ？」
source.english: “If Kisara’s gonna cut you some slack, I’ll cut you some slack too. How about this: you’ll jump in the ocean right now and swim under the keel and back five times—what do you say?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「If Kisara is willing to spare you, then I'll also let you off the hook, but, right, how about you go jump into the ocean right now, then dive five round trips under the keel?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ああん、航海士、水夫長、いじめないでいじめないで」
source.english: “Aaah, Mate, Boatswain, please don’t pick on me, please don’t pick on me.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Aaahn, mates, Bosun, don't bully us, don't bully us.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「僕らただ、航海の安全、
　お祈りしてただけなの」
source.english:
“We were just…
praying for a safe voyage.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「We were just praying for a safe voyage.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「よそでやってよ、そういうことは」
source.english: “Go do that somewhere else.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Then go do that kind of thing somewhere else!」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「でも後から来たのは航海士達の方……、
　あっ。なんでもない、
　僕なんにも言ってない」
source.english:
“But the ones who showed up later were the mates…
Oh. Never mind,
I didn’t say anything.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But you're the ones who came after we already……ah. Nothing, I said absolutely nothing.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ほうほうそうかそうか。
　つまり君達ゃ……往復の数を二倍に増やして欲しいんだねぇ……？」
source.english:
“I see, I see.
So what you’re saying is… you want us to double the number of round trips, right…?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Oh, I see, is that so? So what you're saying is…… you want us to double the number of trips, yeah……?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「きゃ～あああ～～……っ」
source.english: “Eek~ Aaaah~~……!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「KYA～AAA～～……」

source.japanese: このあまりに理不尽な暴虐に、手持ちの金などさっさと溶かしてしまった一抜けの朔屋や、そもそも混ぜてもらえなかったクロなどは、片隅に引っこんでお互い恐怖に固く抱きしめ合ってぶるぶる震えるのみ。
source.english: At such utterly unreasonable tyranny, Sakuya, first to bow out after quickly losing all his money, and Kuro, who had never been allowed to join at all, could only huddle in a corner. They clung tightly to each other and shook with fear.

target.text: Upon witnessing this outrageously absurd tyranny, Sakuya, the first to drop out after immediately blowing whatever paltry sum of money he had on hand, and Kuro, who was never allowed to participate to begin with, could only cower in a corner, embracing each other tightly in mutual horror while they shook and shivered.

source.japanese: それでもこのままではいかなとばっちりが降ってくるものだか知れたものではなく、朔屋はクロと共に足取り揃えて忍び足、始めたところで。
source.english: But who knew what might spill over onto them if they stayed? Sakuya and Kuro matched their steps and began to tiptoe away. Just then—

target.text: Still, it was impossible to say what manner of stray blows they might catch with the way things were going, so Sakuya and Kuro both tiptoed off apace, and right as they began to move.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……はぷしゅっ」
source.english: “…Hapshoo!”

source.japanese: 自分の白髪が鼻先をくすぐって、くしゃみをかましたクロの口元を押さえたところでもう遅い。朔屋は、場の視線が自分達に集まってとてもとても痛くて仕方が無く、急性の顔面チックを発症しかかった。
source.english: Kuro's white hair tickled her nose and she sneezed. Sakuya clapped a hand over her mouth, but too late. Every eye in the room converged upon them, painfully, excruciatingly, and his face nearly began to twitch beyond control.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Achoo!」

By the time he tried to cover Kuro's mouth, who had let out a sneeze after her own white hair tickled the tip of her nose, it was already too late. The stares from everyone present boring into them felt so immensely painful, Sakuya was on the verge of developing acute facial tics.

source.japanese: にゅういと右からシサムの、左からキサラの猿臂が伸びて朔屋の肩を掴み首筋に巻きついたのが、長机を越えて間合いを無視し、ゴムのように関節の可動域を無視したのが怪奇現象、しかし賭博に狂うた人間はそれくらいのことはやってのけるのである、まして悪名高い信天翁号の船員と来ては。
source.english: From the right came Sisam's long arm, from the left Kisara's; they seized Sakuya's shoulders and wound about his neck, stretching across the long table without regard for distance, rubberlike without regard for their joints' range of motion. A supernatural phenomenon—but people mad with gambling could manage that much. Especially members of the notorious Albatross crew.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「クロよぅ……お前さん見てると、俺は、こんな自分でも要領の良い奴に見えてくるから不思議なんだよ……」
source.english: “Kuro… Funny thing. Watching you makes even me look like someone who knows how to get by…”

target.text: Sliding in from the right came Shisamu's, from the left Kisara's, their long, outstretched arms gripping on to Sakuya's shoulders and coiling around his neck, but they had completely disregarded the distance needed to cross the long table, and as if made of rubber, also ignored the possible range of motion inherent to their joints; it was a bizarrely unnatural phenomenon, however, a woman driven mad by gambling could pull off at least that much, and all the more so when it came to the crew of the infamous Albatross.
【Naomasa】 「Hey, Kuro……when I look at you, even somebody like me suddenly starts to look pretty competent, isn't that strange……?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ごめん、あさいっ、すいませっ、クククロ、
　謝る、しますから。だからっ。
　お腹、くすぐらないでぇ───
　けひゃひゃひゃひゃぁぁぁぁっ」
source.english:
“S-sorry! P-pardon! K-K-Kuro…
Kuro will say sorry!
So…
don't tickle Kuro's tummy—Kehahahahahaaa!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Very sorry, apologi-, Ku-Ku-Kuro, will apologize, so. Don't tickle Kuro's stomach─── KHYAHYAHYAHYAaaaah!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……やあ朔屋君。ウチの船長を虐待するとはいい度胸だね……」
source.english: “…Well, Sakuya. Some nerve, abusing our captain…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺が!?　このコを虐待？　これで虐待なら、縛りつけて水滴を一粒一粒五分間隔で垂らしたり、釣り餌のゴカイでみっちりの樽ン中に三〇分ばかり漬けこんだりしたアレはなんて言うんだ」
source.english: “Me!? Abusing this girl? If this is abuse, what do you call tying her up and dripping water on her, one drop every five minutes? Or leaving her for half an hour in a barrel packed with ragworms for fishing bait?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちなみにどっちもあんたらがやったことだと記憶してるが」
source.english: “As I recall, both were your doing.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……Hey there, Sakuya-kun. You've got some balls, what with how you're abusing our captain……」

【Naomasa】 「ME?! Abuse this girl? If this is abuse, then what do you call tying her down to something and dripping water on her every five minutes, one drop after another, and then tossing her into a barrel chock-full of those lugworms we use as bait for a good thirty minutes?」
【Naomasa】 「By the way, I remember that both those things were done by YOU TWO!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……お水……ピチョン……ピチョン……。
　長くて……細くて……。
　足がたくさん生えたむいむい……。
　体……中で……ぞよぞよ……ざわざわ」
source.english:
“…Water… Drip… Drip… Long…
thin…
Little bugs with lots of legs…
All over… wriggling… crawling…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Water……splish……splash……. Long……thin……. Little buggies with lots of legs……. Inside……body…… creeping……crawling.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「いやあああっっ、やあああっっ、
　あーーーっ、あー……、あ、あ、あ……。
　クロ、クロ……ひぎぃ……っ」
source.english:
“Nooooo! Noooo!
Ahhhh, ah… ah, ah, ah…
Kuro, Kuro… eeeh…!”

source.japanese: クロはその時の記憶を蘇らせたか、しばし尻に焼け火箸押し当てられたように泣いて喚いて垂らして、仰天した朔屋の手の中でタバスコをかけられた両生動物よろしく痙攣していたが、最後に細い息でかくんと失神の、綺麗に白目を剥いていたので赤いところが無くなって全身白くなったとさ。
source.english: Perhaps the memory had returned. For a while Kuro wept, screamed and dribbled as though a hot poker had been pressed to her backside. She convulsed in Sakuya's astonished hands like an amphibian doused with Tabasco. At last, with a thin breath, her head dropped and she fainted. Her eyes rolled back so neatly that all the red vanished. White from head to toe, the story goes.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーあ……。可哀相になあ、よしよしクロや、ベッドまで運んでったげるからな」
source.english: “Oh, dear… Poor thing. There, there, Kuro. I'll take you to bed.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Noooo, NOOOO, Aーーーah, aー……, ah, ah, ah……. Kuro, Kuro……ngh……」

Kuro's memory of that time must have flashed through her head, and for a while, as if a pair of red-hot fire tongs had been pressed against her backside, she cried and screamed and spilled liquids all over herself, and held in the arms of the utterly astonished Sakuya, she convulsed like an amphibian doused in Tabasco sauce, but finally, with a wheezing breath, she limply fainted, and with her eyes now completely rolled back into her skull, her red parts were gone, leaving her entire body white.
【Naomasa】 「Oh dear……. You poor little thing. There, there, Kuro, I'll carry you back to your bed.」

source.japanese: 朔屋はしみじみ哀れの顔で、クロを運びだそうとしたものの、それでもシサムとキサラの拘束は解かれていなかった。
source.english: With a look of heartfelt pity, Sakuya tried to carry her away. But Sisam and Kisara still had him firmly held.

target.text: With an expression of heartfelt pity, Sakuya made to carry Kuro away, however, Shisamu and Kisara's restraining hold on him had yet to be released.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「いけないわ、なにを善人面して、
　クロをダシに逃げようとしているのかしら。
　朔屋くぅん」
source.english:
“Oh, come on. What are you trying to pull,
acting all virtuous and using Kuro as an excuse to get away,
our dear Sakuya?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「This won't do. Now why would you play the saint and use Kuro as an excuse to try and run away, I wonder? Sakuya-kuuun.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ダメよぉ朔屋君。クロをベッドに運んだついでに性的な悪戯をしようだなんて。幾らなんでも人の倫に外れ過ぎた行いですよぅ」
source.english: “No way, Sakuya. So you’re thinking of carrying Kuro to bed and fooling around with her while you’re at it? That’s way outside the bounds of decency, no matter how you look at it.”

source.japanese: とても甘い声であった。しかし言っていることは反吐をぶちまけたが如く身も蓋もなくて、朔屋はさすがに奮いたった。
source.english: The voice was sweet, but the words were as crude as vomit, and Sakuya bristled.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こ、抗議する。断固として抗議するっ。
　いくら俺でもこんな、お赤飯もまだ来てないような小娘相手にちょめちょめちょめ、あ、有り得ん」
source.english:
“I—I protest. I protest vehemently.
Even for someone like me, to be fiddling around with some little girl who hasn’t even had her red rice yet—ah, that’s unthinkable.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「That's just not right, Sakuya-kun. Carrying Kuro to bed only to take the opportunity to sexually molest her while you're at it, of all the things. Honestly, no matter how you look at it, that's so depraved it strays into the inhuman.」

Their voices were dripping with honey. But the words they were saying were so blunt and tactless they might as well have been vomiting them all over him, and Sakuya was understandably roused into reaction.

【Naomasa】 「O-objection. I firmly object to that. Even for someone the likes of me, doing this and that and who-knows-what with a little girl who doesn't even seem to have come of age yet, that's just-, it's inconceivable.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「しかしクロは本当は、支那娼館『燈猫館』で、その道の英才教育を受けた、プロフェッショナルだとしたならどうかな」
source.english: “But what if Kuro’s actually a pro, trained in that line of work at the Chinese brothel ‘Tōbyōkan’?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「But if Kuro had actually received a special education for the gifted at the Chinese brothel『Toubyoukan』 in the sensual arts they specialize in, if she were a professional, then I do wonder what you'd do?」 (TN: The 燈猫館, literally The Lantern Cat House, is a fictional brothel (probably), but the kanji chosen are deliberate. The first, 燈, evokes the glowing lanterns of red-light districts. The second, 猫, references popular slang for lower-class geisha or prostitutes in the Edo period, neko, which stems from their playing of the shamisen, which was traditionally made with cat skin.)

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「その舌戯（絶技）、すでに種尽き涸れ果てた、齢九〇のお爺ちゃんの愚息も三〇秒で昇天させ」
source.english: “Her tongue-play—a consummate art—can send even the useless member of a ninety-year-old grandfather, his seed long since spent and dried, to heaven in thirty seconds.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Her special tongue technique could bring even the withered wand of some grandpa in his nineties whose seed had long since dried up to the heavens in thirty seconds.」 (TN: This is a pun on 舌戯, literally "tongue play", and 絶技, "special move" (like martial arts), both pronounced "zetsugi".)

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「その名器は肉襞粒々極楽三段真空締め、指を入れただけでも思わずオットセイ君三連発、
　───だとしたら？」
source.english:
“And that legendary instrument of hers—granular folds of flesh, triple-stage paradise vacuum grip—insert a single finger and even Mister Fur Seal will fire three salvos.
What then?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「馬鹿娘どもっ。人命が懸かっているのだぞ。経験上こうなったクランケは、舌で気道を塞いで窒息死の恐れがあるのだぞ。君らがどう言おうとクロ君は隔離して安静にしなくてはならない───ところで、クロの部屋って鍵かかったっけ？　いや単なる興味で訊くんだけどさ」
source.english: “You idiots. A human life is at stake here. From my experience, patients in this condition can choke to death—their own tongues block their airways. No matter what you say, Kuro has to be isolated and kept at rest—by the way, can Kuro’s room be locked? I’m just asking out of curiosity, though.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Every little bump inside her divine sheath could lock you in a threefold nirvana vacuum embrace, and even just sticking a finger inside would be enough to involuntarily make your little trouser snake explode three times in a row, ───what would you do then?」

【Naomasa】 「You foolish little girls. A human life is on the line here, you know? In my experience, patients like her are in danger of blocking their airway with their tongue and suffocating as a consequence. No matter what you two may say, Kuro-kun must be isolated and allowed to rest and recuperate───by the way, does the door to Kuro's room have a lock? No, no, just asking out of idle curiosity, that's all.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「鍵をかけてナニをするつもりよナニを」
source.english: “What the hell are you planning to do once you lock the door? What?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「And what exactly do you intend to do once you've locked the door, huh?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「やっぱりあんた……最低だ」
source.english: “Just as I thought… you’re the worst.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I knew it…… you really are beneath contempt.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ちなみに直さん、『燈猫館』だったら三〇年も前に閉館しているはず。
　当局の手が入ってね」
source.english:
“Oh, and Nao, Tōbyōkan should have shut its doors thirty years back.
The authorities stepped in.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「──────えっ。
　…………ってことは。
　だ、騙したなキサラ、シサム。
　ひどい。なんて悪質極まりない詐欺だ。
　あんたらそれでも人間か」
source.english:
“Huh?
…………So that means…
Y-you tricked me, Kisara and Sisam. That’s awful.
What a despicable scam.
Are you two even human?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Incidentally, Nao-san, if you're speaking of the『Toubyoukan』, it should already have closed down some thirty years ago. The authorities were involved.」
【Naomasa】 「──────Eh. …………So then, that would mean. Y-, you tricked me, Kisara, Shisamu. You're awful. What a heinous con. Can you two even still call yourselves human?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「五月蝿い、下衆はどっちだ下衆は。最近クロはちょっとあんたに懐いているようだけど」
source.english: “Shut up. Which of us is the scumbag? Which one? Kuro seems to have taken a bit of a liking to you lately, though.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Shut up, who do you think you are to call other people scum, huh? While it does seem like Kuro has grown quite attached to you lately.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「今度からあんたがいる時ゃ、このコにゃ貞操帯を履かせないといかんね」
source.english: “From now on, whenever you’re around, I’ll have to make this kid wear a chastity belt.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「From now on, we'll have to make this girl wear a chastity belt whenever you're around.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「さて、そんな最低な少女性愛趣味の朔屋に物の相談なんだけど」
source.english: “So, Sakuya—you with your despicable pedophilic tendencies—I’ve got a favor to ask.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「な、なんだようっ。人をこんなひどい嘘に引っかけておいて、これ以上何を言おうっていうんだ」
source.english: “W-what the hell? You tricked me with such a terrible lie—what else are you going to say now?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Now, despite your despicable sexual penchant for little girls, we actually have a little favour to ask from you, Sakuya.」
【Naomasa】 「Wh-, what is it then? Not only did you trick a man with such a cruel lie, you claim to have even more you wish to say?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なぁに、簡単な事さぁ」
source.english: “It’s nothing—it’s easy.”

source.japanese: 先ほど『簡単な仕事』と称して、この双子が下級水夫に何を命じようとしたのか舌の根も乾かぬうちだったから、朔屋は大いに警戒したという。
source.english: The twins had only just described the fate they meant to inflict upon the junior sailors as ‘easy work.’ Naturally Sakuya received the same phrase with extreme caution.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Why, it's a simple thing, see.」

The words regarding whatever it was they had been trying to order the deck boys to do under the guise of a "simple job" mere moments ago had scarce left the twins' mouths, and so Sakuya was on high alert.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「おう朔屋。ちと金貸せや」
source.english: “Hey, Sakuya. Lend us some money.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あっはっは、莫迦言っちゃいけない。
　俺なんてさっき早々に持ち金全部毟[むし]られた。
　あんたらだって見てただろうが」
source.english:
“Ha, ha, ha. Don't be ridiculous.
I was fleeced of every penny right at the start.
You saw it yourselves.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Yo, Sakuya. Spot me some cash.」
【Naomasa】 「Ah-ha-ha, stop with the nonsense. Why, I was already stripped of all my money right after we began. Surely you two must also have seen it yourselves, right?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「へえ。そう。なら朔屋、あんたちょっと右の長靴脱いでみ？」
source.english: “Oh. Did you? Then take off your right boot, Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「えっ」
source.english: “Huh?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Really. That so. In that case, Sakuya, why don't you try taking off that right boot of yours for a bit?」
【Naomasa】 「Huh?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ついでに左の長靴も脱いでみ？」
source.english: “And while you're at it, the left one.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And while you're at it, do your left boot too?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そんでその中敷きを、
　ちょっと剥がしてみなよ」
source.english:
“Then just peel
up the insoles.”

source.japanese:
朔屋の額に冷たい汗が流れたのは、言うまでもなくそこが青年のへそくりの隠し場所だったからである。
　立ち往生する朔屋の肩を首を、巻きついたままの双子の腕が締め上げてぎぃりぎぃり、だから青年の冷や汗もたーらりたらり。
　この追求に水を入れたのは水夫長、さすがに水夫の長と言うだけはあったもの。
source.english:
Cold sweat ran down Sakuya's forehead. Naturally: that was where he hid his secret savings.
He stood helpless while the twins' arms tightened around his shoulders and neck. Creak, creak. Drip, drip went the sweat.
The boatswain interrupted the interrogation. As one might expect of the head of the sailors.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「And once you've done that, try peeling off that insole a bit.」

Needless to say, the reason a cold sweat was running down Sakuya's brow was because that was, in fact, the hiding place of the young man's secret savings. Still wrapped around the frozen Sakuya, the twins' arms constricted his shoulders and neck with an agonizingly creaking squeeze, squeeze, sending beads of cold sweat running down the young man's face with a trickle, trickle. The one who called a timeout on this shakedown was the Bosun; certainly, he showed himself well worthy of the title of chief of the sailors.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「待て、シサム、キサラ。
　お前達、そいつはちょっとな……」
source.english:
“Wait, Sisam, Kisara.
That's a little…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そ、そうッスよね龍の親爺。
　水夫長殿ももっと言ってやって下さいよ」
source.english:
“R-right, Old Long?
Please, Boatswain, sir—tell them!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hold it, Shisamu, Kisara. You two, that's a little too……」
【Naomasa】 「Th-that's exactly right, old man Long. Bosun, sir, please keep giving them what's for!」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なあ一等航海士よ。
　お前達、そいつはちょっと───
　甘いってもんだぜ？」
source.english:
“Listen, Chief Mate.
You two are being a little—too soft,
aren't you?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんですとっ」
source.english: “What did you say!?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Now listen here, first mates. You two, that's a little too─── lenient of you, you know?」
【Naomasa】 「Wait what did you just say?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なあ朔屋。てめえちょっと、ベルトを外してみろや」
source.english: “Now, Sakuya. Take off your belt.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あの僕ちょっと男色の方面は、
　そのちょっとぅ」
source.english:
“Uh, I'm not really…
into men, that is…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hey, Sakuya. Why don't you try taking off your belt for a bit?」
【Naomasa】 「Listen, I, this homosexuality thing, it's not really my thing and─」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「誤魔化さなくていいからよ。ベルト外して、その裡側の縫い目を解いてみろやおらぁっ」
source.english: “No need to play dumb. Take off the belt and unpick the seam on the inside. Come on!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Don't bother trying to wriggle your way out of this one. Take off your damn belt and then try undoing the stitching on the inside!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「長靴もだぁっ」
source.english: “The boots too!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Your boots too!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「とりゃああっっ」
source.english: “Hyaaaa!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーっ、あーーっっ！
　堪忍してぇ、その銭まで巻き上げられたら、
　明日のお酒も呑めなくなっちゃうううっ」
source.english:
“Ah! Aaaah! Mercy!
Take that money too and I won't
even be able to drink tomorrow!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Hyaaahh!」
【Naomasa】 「Ahー, aahーー! Please, have mercy, if you strip me of even this paltry coin, I won't have any booze to drink tomorroooow!」

source.japanese:
三方向から怪鳥の如く飛びかかられ、たちまち脱がされ解かれて、長靴からベルトの中から、朔屋がせこせこ必死で貯めた小金はたちまち白日の下に、ああ流れよ我が涙、と三等航海士は言った。
　そして食堂の片隅に容赦なく蹴り転がされ、しくしく鬱陶しく泣き崩れる朔屋には水夫長と航海士はもう一瞥だにくれず、賽子賭博が再開されようとした時───
source.english:
They swooped on him from three sides like monstrous birds. Boots off, belt unpicked—in an instant, the paltry savings Sakuya had so desperately scraped together were brought to light. Ah, flow my tears, the third mate said.
Then he was kicked mercilessly into a corner of the mess, where he collapsed in tedious little sobs. The boatswain and navigators did not spare him another glance. Just as the dice game was about to resume—

target.text: They leapt upon him from three directions like monstrous birds; he was quickly stripped, the seams undone, and from his belt and his boots, all the paltry coin Sakuya had so painstakingly saved was soon exposed to the light of day; O flow, my tears, the third-rate sailor exclaimed. And then he was mercilessly kicked to the floor in a corner of the mess hall; the Bosun and the mates spared not Sakuya even a single fleeting glance as he broke down into depressing fits of weeping, and just as they were about to resume their game of dice───

source.japanese:
【泪】
「賭け事は、それくらいになさらない？
　皆のコマが尽きたなら、
　先程のお話を考える───
　そういう約束じゃなかったかしら」
source.english:
“Shall we leave the gambling there?
When everyone ran out of money,
we were to consider the proposal.
Wasn't that our agreement?”

source.japanese: 負けがかさみ、眼を血走らせていた子側はこの水を差す言葉に睨[にら]みつけたが、親を張っていた泪が言い出しては無視するわけにもいかず、皆渋い顔で落ち着け直す尻の下、長椅子軋む。
source.english: The losing players, their eyes bloodshot, glared at the interruption. But it came from Rui, who held the bank. They could hardly ignore her. Sour-faced, they settled back down, the long bench creaking beneath them.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Why don't we leave the gambling at this? Once you had all exhausted your funds, you would consider what I spoke of earlier─── was that not the agreement we had?」

The bettors, whose eyes were bloodshot from the string of losses, glared back at her words that threw cold water all over their heated excitement, but since it was Rui, who was playing the role of the banker, who had said it, they also could not simply ignore it, and the bench creaked beneath their buttocks as they all settled down once more with glum looks on their faces.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なぁ……。
　あんたそれ本気で言ってンのか？
　そんなん俺らの柄じゃねえやな、
　どう考えても」
source.english:
“Look…
You mean it?
Whatever way you look at it,
that isn't our sort of thing.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Look……. Are you serious about this? That kind of thing just ain't our style, no matter how you look at it.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どう受け取られても、
　それはあなた方のご自由ですけれども」
source.english:
“How you choose
to take it is entirely up to you.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「いずれにしてもわたくしはお話をお伝えしただけ。それ以上の事は、存じません」
source.english: “In any event, I have merely passed on the proposal. Beyond that, I know nothing.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Interpret it however you want, that is something entirely up to you.」
【Rui】 「Regardless of what you believe, I am merely relaying what I have been told. Anything beyond that, I know nothing of.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そうは言うけどね。そういうのって、役人とかどっかの学校の先生とかさ、そこらへんがやる事なんじゃないの、普通」
source.english: “You say that, but isn't that normally a job for officials, or some school's teachers, people like that?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「You say that, but. Isn't that kind of thing something done by a government official, some academic from some school, or someone of that sort, usually?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だよね───北限氷土を探ってこい、だなんて」
source.english: “Right. Go explore the Northern Ice Wastes, indeed.”

source.japanese:
───泪は、その依頼を旧知の実業家から受けたと伝えた。
　それは、この世界の果て、北限氷土のどこかにあるという、地図上の新たな指標となる地点を調査、発見してほしいという依頼で。
　この、海の裏街道の吹きだまりの中でも澱[よど]みも澱[よど]んだ奇怪な連中が揃う船、信天翁号に寄せられる依頼としては、全くもってそぐわないアカデミックなものであった事は言うまでもあるまい。
source.english:
Rui said the request had come from an entrepreneur she had known for years.
They were to investigate and find a place, said to lie somewhere in the Northern Ice Wastes at the end of this world,
that would serve as a new reference point on the map. Needless to say, such an academic request was utterly unsuited to the Albatross, with its bizarre company, the very dregs of the stagnant backwaters of the sea's crooked byways.

source.japanese: これまでは最底辺の密貿易がほとんどで、そうした探検行的な仕事はろくにこなした事もないので、船内は紛糾していたのである。
source.english: Until now their work had consisted almost entirely of bottom-rung smuggling. They had scarcely attempted anything resembling an expedition, and so the ship was in an uproar.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Right───asking us to go investigate the northernmost permafrost, of all things.」

───Rui told them that she had received the request from a businessman, an old acquaintance of hers. And the request was to investigate and discover a location said to lie somewhere in the northernmost permafrost, at the very edge of this world, that would serve as a new landmark on the map. Needless to say, for a request received by the Albatross, a ship manned by a motley crew of the foulest, most stagnant of sediment, even by the standards of a shady dreg heap of the seas, this was of an entirely academic nature, utterly and completely unsuited for them.
Until now, they had almost exclusively engaged in the lowest rung of smuggling, and they had hardly ever done any expeditionary work of that sort, so there was a lot of turmoil on board the ship.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お引き受けなさるかどうか。
　それだけを決めて下さいましな」
source.english:
“Please simply decide
whether you will accept.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Will you accept the request or not? Could you kindly at least decide on that much.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「あんたは払いの良い客だ。
　あんたが持ってきた依頼なら、二つ返事で引き受けたいところだが……だがなあ」
source.english:
“You're a customer who pays well.
I'd like to say yes to any job you bring us. But… well…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You are a generously paying passenger. And if it's a request brought by you, then I'd love to give my ready agreement, but……but, you see.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたしは正直なんとも言えない。
　ただ北限氷土ともなると、
　この船の装備じゃちょっと……」
source.english:
“Honestly, I can't say either way.
But the Northern Ice Wastes…
With the equipment aboard this ship…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Honestly, I don't know what to make of it. It's just, if we're heading to the northernmost permafrost, then I think the equipment on this ship is a bit, well……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……でも、正直言うと、あたしはちょっと興味ある。だってこれまでやったことない仕事だし、報酬は幾らって言ったっけ、泪さん」
source.english: “…Honestly, though, I'm a little interested. It's work we've never done before. How much did you say it paid, Rui?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……But, to tell the truth, I am a little interested. I mean, it's work we've never done before, and how much did you say the payment was again, Rui-san?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「英ポンドで三五万とうかがっています」
source.english: “Three hundred and fifty thousand pounds sterling, I am told.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I was told it would be 350,000 in British pounds.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「豪毅な話だぜ、それだけ聞くとよ。
　しかも前金で半額だろ？
　美味しすぎてどう考えても、
　やばい臭いしかしてこねえ」
source.english:
“Sounds mighty generous when you put it that way.
And half in advance, right?
Too sweet a deal.
Whichever way you look at it, it stinks of trouble.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「A daring proposition, just from hearing that alone. And we're getting paid half in advance on top of that, yeah? No matter how you slice it, that's too sweet a deal. All I'm getting is the stink of something shady.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そのあたりのご判断は、そちらでどうぞ」
source.english: “I shall leave that judgment to you.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Feel free to draw whatever conclusions regarding such as it pleases you.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ロックフォールの奴はなんて言ってた？」
source.english: “What did Roquefort say?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What did Roquefort have to say about it?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
『私は皆様の判断にお任せしますよ……。
　ただしこの船の主罐では、
　北限氷土探索とあっては、
　些かの無理がある事は伝えておきたい』
source.english:
‘I shall leave it to everyone's judgment…
But I must point out that, with this ship's
main boiler,
exploring the Northern Ice Wastes would be rather difficult.’

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 『I shall defer to your collective judgment……. That said, I should like to point out that, with this ship's main boiler, exploring the northernmost permafrost will be pushing it a little.』

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「となると、条件付き保留が二で、反対と賛成がそれぞれ一か……クロと朔屋はそもそも数に入いんないし」
source.english: “So that's two conditional abstentions, one vote against and one in favor… Kuro and Sakuya don't count in the first place.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（はいはい、どうせそういうこったろうよ。
　いいから俺の銭返せよう）
source.english:
(Yes, yes, of course we don't.
Just give me my money back.)

source.japanese: このようにして船内の意見は二つに割れて、挙げ句に解決策は、やはり博打なのだった。
source.english: Thus opinion aboard was split in two. In the end, the solution was gambling once again.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「So with that, we've got two conditional deferments, as well as one vote against and one for…… Kuro and Sakuya were never considered part of the tally to begin with.」
【Naomasa】 （Yes, yes, I figured that's how it was going to turn out anyway. Whatever, just give me my money back!）
Thus, opinions on board were divided cleanly in two, and in the end, the solution came down to gambling.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……よし。賽の目に任せようぜ。
　丁の目だったらこの件は無しだ。
　半だったら引き受けるだけは引き受ける」
source.english:
“…Right. Let's leave it to the dice.
Even, we drop it.
Odd, we'll at least accept.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Alright. Let's leave it all to the dice. If it's evens, we drop the matter. If it's odds, we'll at least try to take it on.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それでええな？」
source.english: “Agreed?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「That fine with you?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「いいよー」
source.english: “Fine by me.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Sounds good.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「キサラに同じだよ」
source.english: “Same as Kisara.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Same as Kisara.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「じゃあ振るぜ……おい小僧、
　これもお前振れ」
source.english:
“Then here goes… Hey, boy.
You throw this one too.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Then let the dice be cast……oi, kid, you're throwing these too.」

source.japanese: 先程まで壺役務めていた下級水夫にまた任される。そして皆の注視の元、振り出された目は。
source.english: The junior sailor who had thrown for them before was given the job again. Under everyone's gaze, the dice rolled—

target.text: The deck boy who had previously served as the roller of the dice cup was once more assigned that role. Finally, the focus of everyone's attention, the eyes that had been rolled were……

source.japanese: 六
source.english: Six.

source.japanese: 三
source.english: Three.

source.japanese: 一
source.english: One.

source.japanese: 溜息がどこからともなく漏れて、
source.english: A sigh escaped from somewhere.

target.text: Six
Three
One
A sigh escaped from somewhere,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……てな訳だ。悪いな泪さんよ。
　今回は縁がなかったと思って───」
source.english:
“…There it is. Sorry, Rui.
Call it a job that wasn't meant for us—”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……And that's how it goes. Sorry about this, Rui-san. Just consider it something that wasn't meant to be this time around and───」

source.japanese:
とこれでこの話は波の間に間に消えゆこうとした時だった。
　宗右衛門が机に跳び上がり、前足の爪の先で三の目の賽をちょんとつついて。
source.english:
The proposal was about to disappear between the waves when Soemon sprang onto the table.
With the tip of a front claw, he nudged the die showing three.

target.text: And with that, when the matter was just about to sink beneath the waves and vanish for good, right then. Souemon jumped up on the table, then tapped the die that had come up three with the tip of the claw of his front paw.

source.japanese: 四の目に変えて。
source.english: And changed it to four.

target.text: Changing it to a four.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……宗右衛門さん……。あんたこの仕事、
　受けろって言ってるの……」
source.english:
“…Mr. Soemon…
Are you telling us to take this job…?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……Souemon-san……. Are you telling us we should take on this job……」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「本気かよ……」
source.english: “You serious…?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Are you serious……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「でも信天翁号のしきたりだと、意見が割れた時、最後に決めるのは───」
source.english: “But by our custom aboard the Albatross, when opinions are split, the final decision belongs to—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But that's our custom here on the Albatross. When opinions are divided, the final decision is made by───」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そうか……そうだったよな。
　よし、決まった。泪さん、伝えてやってくれ。受けるぜ、この仕事！」
source.english:
“Right… It does, doesn't it?
All right, settled. Rui, pass the word along. We'll take this job!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right……that's how it was, yeah. Alright, it's decided. Rui-san, you can tell him this. We're taking the job!」

source.japanese:
【直正】
（おいおい……本気かよ……。
　まあこの船らしいと言えばそうなんだが）
source.english:
(Hey, hey… Seriously…?
Well, I suppose that's just like this ship.)

source.japanese:
受けるかどうか。話は縺[もつ]れた挙げ句に、決定したのは猫の宗右衛門。朔屋は、この船は猫が一番えらいのかと愕然とするも、結局は納得してしまう。
　とりあえず現在は運ばなくてはならない積み荷があるので、依頼を果たすのは港に荷を下ろしたその後で、という事になる。信天翁号、まずは次の港へ。
source.english:
Accept or refuse? After all the tangled argument, Soemon the cat made the decision. Sakuya was appalled. Was the cat truly the highest authority aboard? Yet in the end even he found himself accepting it.
For the moment they still had cargo to deliver, so the commission would wait until it had been unloaded. First, the Albatross would make for the next harbor.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （Come on now……are you being real with me here……? Well, come to think of it, I guess that's very like this ship.）

Should they take it or leave it? After the discussion turned into a convoluted tangle, in the end, the final decision fell to Souemon the cat. Though Sakuya was astonished to learn that a cat was the highest-ranking presence aboard this ship, in the end, he came to accept it. Regardless, they currently carried some cargo that needed to be delivered, so it was decided that fulfilling the request would have to wait until after said cargo was unloaded at a port. First things first, the Albatross set sail for the next port.

source.japanese: ───時に朔屋は、項の辺りに摺[す]れる潮風の温[ぬる]さの中に、玉葱とバターを炒める芳しい香気が混ざるのを嗅ぎ、朝な夕な以外は暢気な阿呆鳥達の声が活気を得て、喧しく飛び交いだしたを聴いて、厨房の司厨長係を務める下級水夫達が昼食の仕込みに手をつける頃合いだと測った。
source.english: —From the warm sea breeze brushing the nape of his neck, Sakuya caught the savory fragrance of onions frying in butter. The normally indolent albatrosses, lively only morning and evening, had begun to cry and wheel noisily overhead. He judged that the junior sailors assigned to the galley must be starting lunch.

target.text: ───At times, Sakuya, smelling the fragrant aroma of onions and butter sauteing within the lukewarm sea breeze brushing against the nape of his neck, and hearing the albatrosses, usually so laid-back outside of dawn and dusk, grow animated in their cries and fly about noisily, inferred that it was about the time the deck boys working underneath the chief cook in the galley were starting to prep for lunch.

source.japanese:
玉葱を刻んだのと塩蔵肉のスープは昼食の定番の菜の一つだし、おおよその余り物を、別の献立の一部にと美事に用立てる魔法を心得たる、司厨長係の下級水夫の技前を持ってしても、箸にも棒にもかからない屑野菜、腐った肉類の切れっ端などが艫[とも]からぶちまけられるのも、決まって昼食の仕込み前だ。
　光栄にも同じ名前をいただいた、信天翁号の翼有るお仲間達は、船からの残飯を支給される時間をちゃんと心得て、毎日同じ頃合いに騒ぎ始めるのである。
source.english:
Soup of chopped onions and salted meat was a lunchtime staple. And just before preparations began, scraps of vegetables and rotten meat were tossed over the stern: leftovers beyond even the cooks' magic for making splendid use of nearly anything in another dish.
The Albatross's winged companions, honored with the same name, knew perfectly well when the ship handed out scraps. Every day they began their commotion at the same time.

source.japanese: （ちなみに信天翁号でもっとも献立の種類が多いのは朝食、嵩が豊富なのは昼食であり、夕食は比較的あっさりしたものとなる）
source.english: (Incidentally, breakfast aboard the Albatross offered the greatest variety, lunch the greatest quantity, while supper was comparatively light.)

target.text: Chopped onion and salt-cured meat soup was one of the staple side dishes served at lunch, but when scraps of vegetable and rotted meats were dumped overboard from the stern, the sort of refuse that, even had one the skills of the deck boy serving as chief cook, who had learned some kind of magic that allowed him to take most leftovers and use them superbly as part of another dish, was truly beyond salvation, then it was sure to be just before lunch prep began.

The winged comrades of the Albatross, they who were honoured at having the privilege of sharing the same name, had diligently learned the time they would be supplied with food scraps from the ship, and so they always began making a ruckus at the same time every day.
(Incidentally, the meal most diverse in its offering of dishes was breakfast, most substantial in volume was lunch, and dinner was comparatively light and plain.)

source.japanese:
このように信天翁号では時計の几帳面な針目盛りとは別の、まこと泰然とした、大陸の道士の気風にも相通じる時間の観念の中に生きてあり、朔屋も馴染みつつある……などと悠長なものか。
　朔屋が腕時計や懐中時計の類を見に帯びないのは、よしそんなご大層な物[ブツ]を持ち合わせていたとしても、自分から質屋に叩きこむか、さもなくばいつの間にか消えているのがオチだからで。
source.english:
Thus the Albatross lived by a serenely unhurried conception of time, apart from the precise markings of a clock, something akin to the spirit of a mainland Taoist sage. Sakuya, too, was growing accustomed to it…
Or so one might leisurely suppose. The reason he wore neither wristwatch nor pocket watch was that, even if he possessed so grand an article, he would either pawn it himself or find it had disappeared before he knew it.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（……にしても、大して動きもせんでも、腹だけは減るのはある意味不自由だよなあ）
source.english: (Still, getting hungry when you've hardly moved is a nuisance, in a way.)

source.japanese:
と朔屋は、飛び交う阿呆鳥たちが甲板上に落とす、間延びしたＭ字型の影を目で追いながら、両手首に力を籠めた。
　───が、びくともせぬ。
source.english:
Watching the stretched-out M-shaped shadows cast upon the deck by the wheeling albatrosses, Sakuya put all his strength into his wrists.
—Nothing budged.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（このままだと、昼飯の時間、過ぎちまうかなあ……）
source.english: (At this rate… am I going to miss lunch?)

source.japanese: 大して動きも働きもせぬでも、極端な話、布団に籠城して手の皺の数を数えていたって空腹は訪れる。それに朔屋とて一応はこの午前中、仕事らしきものに就いてはいた。
source.english: Even without doing much work or moving about—even, to take an extreme example, barricaded in bed counting the creases of one's hands—hunger came. Besides, Sakuya had spent the morning on something that could pass for work.

source.japanese:
下級水夫達が用いる漁網の繕いという、眼精疲労と肩凝りは別としても、上甲板で日向ぼっこしながらでも片づけられる軽作業で、そんな楽な仕事を回してもらえたのは、偶然入手した単行本を、抜かりなく水夫長に心づけしていた事による。
　なおこの単行本は『スカラムーシュ』の原書であったのだが、船の積み荷にである安煙草の中に何故か一冊だけまぎれていたのを発見したのだ。
source.english:
Mending the fishing nets used by the junior sailors. It was easy work, eyestrain and stiff shoulders aside, and could be done while basking in the sun on the upper deck. Sakuya had landed so cushy an assignment because he had taken care to slip the boatswain a book that had come into his hands by chance.
An original-language copy of Scaramouche, as it happened. He had found the single volume inexplicably mixed into their cargo of cheap tobacco.

source.japanese: ただし、この数日後、水夫長がさて読書と繰り広げてみると、中のページがくり抜かれて、一ダースばかりのコンドームが収められているのを目の当たりにした憤慨に、朔屋の船室まで成敗しにいく事となるのが、それは余談として。
source.english: A few days later, however, the boatswain would settle down to read, discover the pages hollowed out around a dozen or so condoms, and march to Sakuya's cabin in fury to administer justice. But that is a digression.

target.text: Thus, the Albatross operated within a conception of time entirely distinct from that of the mechanically punctual graduations on the surface of a clock, a truly serene temporal flow that resonated with the tranquil spirit of continental Taoist sages, and Sakuya was also gradually becoming accustomed to it……as if it was anything that easygoing. The reason Sakuya did not carry a wristwatch or pocket watch or anything of the sort on his person was because even if he were to happen to have such an impressive article on hand, the only outcomes would be himself dumping it in some pawnshop, or if not that, it suddenly disappearing without a trace.
【Naomasa】 （……Even so, the fact that I still get hungry despite barely moving is pretty inconvenient, in a sense.)

So Sakuya thought, and while chasing the lazy, M-shaped shadows cast on the deck by the albatrosses wheeling overhead with his eyes, he channeled strength into his wrists. ───But they didn't budge an inch.
【Naomasa】 （At this rate, I might actually miss lunchtime……)

Though he hardly moved nor worked, to offer an extreme example, even were you to hole up beneath your futon and count the wrinkles on your hands, hunger would still call upon you. In addition, Sakuya had technically been engaged in something that resembled work this morning.

It was mending the fishing nets that the deck boys used, and aside from the stiff shoulders and eyestrain, it was light work that could be taken care of while sunbathing on the upper deck; as for the reason he had been blessed with so easy a job, it was because he had shrewdly made sure to gift the Bosun a book he had happened to get his hands on. Furthermore, this book was 『Scaramouche』in its original language; he had discovered that, for some reason, a lone book had gotten mixed in amongst the cheap tobacco in the ship's cargo.

However, a few days later, when the Bosun opened the book all ready and raring to read, he was positively enraged to find that the pages within had been hollowed out, with about a dozen or so condoms stored within; he even went all the way to Sakuya's cabin to mete out just punishment, but I digress.

source.japanese:
ともかく、朔屋が就いていたのは針糸仕事だった筈なのだが、青年は上甲板の片隅でそれこそ網に絡まったオットセイの態で、全身に荒縄巻きつけて、動くもならず解くもならずの窮状に陥っていた。
　それで腹が減ったとか抜かしているときては、莫迦もいいところなのか突き抜けてお大尽の風格か、多分いずれでもなく、一人だけではない、お仲間がいる心強さからである。
source.english:
Anyway, Sakuya ought to have been plying needle and thread. Instead he lay in a corner of the upper deck like a fur seal tangled in a net, his whole body wrapped in coarse rope. He could neither move nor free himself.
And there he was complaining of hunger. Was this idiocy at its purest, or had he transcended folly and attained the lordly ease of a millionaire? Probably neither. He was simply fortified by the knowledge that he had company in his plight.

source.japanese: 朔屋からやや離れたところで、同様に荒縄にぐるぐる巻きになって、こちらは出来の悪いモップのように転がっていたのはクロだった。ただ朔屋ほど気楽にぶち転がっていられないようで、何しろ白子の少女の方は口にがっつり縄の結び目が轡[くつわ]と嵌[はま]ってあり、口封じどころか息まで封じてぷつぷつぷつ、唇の隙間から蟹の如き泡で、白目を剥いて痙攣の、朔屋にもこれは危険な段階と危機感募らせるのだが、文字通り手も足も出ない。
source.english: A little way off, Kuro lay equally swaddled in coarse rope, looking like a badly made mop. Unlike Sakuya, however, she was in no condition to lie there unconcerned. A great knot was jammed into the albino woman's mouth as a gag, choking off not merely her words but her breath. Bubbles frothed crablike between her lips; her eyes rolled back and her body convulsed. Sakuya's alarm mounted as he realized how dangerous her condition had become, but quite literally he could move neither hand nor foot.

source.japanese: これで智里が釣りと洒落こんで上甲板に上がらず、二人の惨状を見かけなんだら朔屋はともかくとしてクロの方は今頃、全身に巻きつけていた網を晒しに替えてのお弔い巻き、キャンバス地の袋に詰められて海に水葬された可能性も充分有り得たわけで、殺し屋がすらり抜き放った切っ先の、アレクサンドロス大王の故事もある、ややこしい結び目は解くより斬ったが早いと両断した時にはもう、クロはほとんど死に体だった。
source.english: If Tomosato had not come up to the deck for a spot of fishing and discovered their predicament, Sakuya might have survived, but Kuro could well by then have traded the net around her for a funeral shroud, been sewn into a canvas sack, and been buried at sea. The assassin drew his blade with a practiced sweep. Better to cut a Gordian knot than untie it, as Alexander the Great had shown. By the time Tomosato severed this one, Kuro was already nearly dead.

target.text: Regardless, while Sakuya should have been engaged in work with thread and needle, the young man was in a nook of the upper deck, the spitting image of a fur seal ensnared in a net, his entire body wrapped up in straw rope, and the distressing predicament of being both unable to move and unable to untangle himself had befallen him. And even then, he was still able to start whining about being hungry; was he a complete idiot, or had he broken through into the realm of the fabulously rich? It was probably neither, for he was not alone, no, he had the reassurance of a companion's presence.

A little apart from Sakuya, wrapped round and round in straw rope in much the same way, was Kuro, rolling around like a poorly made mop. But she had not fallen over in as comfortable a position as Sakuya had, for you see, a large knot in the rope had lodged itself right inside the albino girl's mouth like a bit, not just gagging her, but even preventing her from breathing; she was foaming at the mouth like a crab, her eyes rolled into the back of her head while she convulsed, and even Sakuya also felt a growing sense of impending crisis, realizing that this was heading in a dangerous direction, but he was literally unable to lift a finger.

Had Tomosato not made his way up to the upper deck to indulge in a spot of fishing, then caught sight of their tragic state, then, setting aside Sakuya, right about now, it was all too possible that the net that had been wrapped around Kuro's entire body would have been replaced with sarashi as a funeral wrap, and then she would have been stuffed into a canvas bag and given a funeral at sea, so when the murderer, echoing the legend of Alexander the Great, realized that a tangled knot was quicker cut than untied, then used the tip of his smoothly unsheathed blade to bisect it, by that time, Kuro was already on the brink of death.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───それで、だ。
　どうやら次の仕事は北限氷土の───
　ごほごほごほ」
source.english:
“Anyway.
Apparently the next job's in the Northern Ice—cough,
cough, cough!”

source.japanese:
言い差した口は、智里が吹きかけた煙管の煙に巻かれて中断の、だが煙に巻こうとしたのは実のところ殺し屋の方ではない。
　智里は、さも呆れ果てた風に眉じりを下げて、
source.english:
Tomosato's pipe smoke swallowed Sakuya's unfinished words. Yet it was not the assassin who had been trying to throw up a smokescreen.
Tomosato lowered his brows in utter exasperation.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「───And so, with that. Seems like our next job is exploring the northernmost─── *cough cough cough*」

The words leaving his lips were swallowed within the pipe smoke that Tomosato exhaled into his face, interrupted before he could finish, but in truth, the one actually blowing smoke here wasn't the murderer. Tomosato lowered the tail of his eyebrows as if truly astonished,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「なーにが『それで、だ』でぇ。
　なんだって白子と莫迦が仲良く荒巻でぶちころがってんだよ」
source.english:
“What d'you mean, ‘anyway’?
Why were an albino and an idiot lying there all neatly trussed together?”

source.japanese: しん、と冴えた眼差しで朔屋とクロを見据えた、眸には殺しを生計とする者とは思えぬほど透き通った蒼が際立ったが、次の言葉は何が透き通ったものやらの、
source.english: His gaze was still and keen upon Sakuya and Kuro. The clear blue of his eyes hardly suited a man who killed for a living. But what followed was not clear and pure at all.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「What's "and so, with that" supposed to mean? I want to know why an albino and an idiot were rolling around on the floor like happy little aramaki.」 (TN: Aramaki, written "荒巻" here, is dried, salted salmon. In the past, the salmon was wrapped up in straw rope or bamboo leaves for better preservation.)

Suddenly falling still, he fixed his clear gaze on Sakuya and Kuro, his eyes so striking a crystalline blue that it was almost unthinkable that this man made his living killing others, but what clear purity there was to be found in the next words he uttered was anyone's guess,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ああそうか。てめえら、手仕事の徒[いたづ]らに、縄の結び方でも練習してたんだろう」
source.english: “Ah, got it. You were fiddling about with your handiwork, practicing knots.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Ahh, I see. Passing the hours with a bit of handiwork, you must have been practicing knot-tying.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ほんで二人揃って不器用に、ああでもないこうでもないしてるうちに、手やら足やら縄が絡まって、しまいにはあのざまに成り果てた、と」
source.english: “Then the pair of you fumbled about, this way, that way, got rope tangled around arms and legs, and ended up like that.”

source.japanese: ……なんぼなんだとてその推理には無理がありすぎると、朔屋は笑い飛ばしただろうか。クロは話についていけず、きょとんと胡乱な目をして見せただろうか。
source.english: Did Sakuya laugh the deduction off as altogether too far-fetched? Did Kuro, unable to follow, give him a blank, doubtful look?

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「And so, with both of you being as clumsy as the other, while you were going "not like this, but not like that either", your arms and legs and whatnot got tangled up in the rope, and in the end, you were left in that sorry state.」

……Surely Sakuya would think that, even if it sounded convincing, his deductions were too far-fetched and laugh it off? Surely Kuro would be unable to follow the conversation, only giving a vacant, confused look in return?

source.japanese:
なんの。
　二人共に浮かべた感嘆の目の色は、智里の推測が一言一句間違っていなかった事を示しており、二人はぱちぱちと拍手を送ったりしたものだから、　今度は智里に拳固で軽いお仕置きをもらった事である。
source.english:
Not in the least.
Both stared at Tomosato in admiration, proving that his deduction had been correct in every particular. They even applauded, whereupon he rewarded them with a mild knock on the head.

target.text: Perish the thought. The look of astonished admiration that surfaced in the eyes of both made it apparent that there was not a single incorrect line of thought in Tomosato's deductions, and both of them gave him a round of applause in return; therefore, this time, they received a light punishment by way of Tomosato's fists.

source.japanese: とはいえ、クロも朔屋も小突かれ慣れしており、多少の拳骨では堪[こた]えない。朔屋も特にいじける事もなく、先ほどの話の続きを持ち出した。
source.english: Both were accustomed to being knocked about. A few knocks made little impression. Sakuya did not particularly sulk, but resumed his earlier subject.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ってなわけで、次の港で積み荷を揚げたら、今度は北限氷土だとよ。しかも最後は猫が決めたときやがる」
source.english: “…So there you are. Unload the cargo at the next port, and then it's the Northern Ice Wastes. And a cat made the final decision, would you believe.”

source.japanese: と無理矢理話をねじ曲げて、ただ辺りを憚[はばか]るように結んだのは、口では強気に言いつつもかの黒猫を懼[おそ]れていたからで、その辺りの物陰でもし聞かれでもしたなら後が怖い。
source.english: He forced the subject around, ending warily, mindful of his surroundings. For all his bold talk, he was afraid of that black cat. If the cat happened to be listening from some nearby shadow, there would be trouble afterward.

target.text: With that said, both Kuro and Sakuya were used to a few light jabs here and there, and a couple knocks to the head weren't enough to faze them. Sakuya also didn't seem to have lost his nerve in particular, bringing up the subject of conversation from just earlier once more.

【Naomasa】 「……And so, with that, once we've unloaded the cargo at the next port, we'll be heading to the northernmost permafrost next, apparently. And of all the things, it was a damn cat that made the final decision.」

The reason he forcibly twisted the topic around and brought it to a hasty, hushed close as if nervous of his surroundings was that, though his words were full of bravado, he was secretly terrified of that black cat, and he dreaded what might be in store for him if it were listening in from somewhere in the shadows nearby.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「まあそう言うナイ。あの猫はなかなかの偉物だぜ。しかし北限氷土、ねえ……。
　慣れねえな、その響きにも、その果てを越えた船乗りは無いちゅう話にも」
source.english:
“Don't talk like that. That's quite a cat. But the Northern Ice Wastes, eh… Can't get used to the name.
Or that business about no sailor ever getting past the far edge.”

source.japanese: 妙に遠い目をする智里こそが朔屋にはかえってなぜ太陽は東から昇るのかと問われたような心地で。
source.english: To Sakuya, Tomosato's oddly distant gaze was as baffling as if he had been asked why the sun rose in the east.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……そんなもんか？　誰だって知ってる話だろうが。北限氷土は世界の果て。その先がどうなってるのか知ってる奴はいないってのは。な、クロ？」
source.english: “…Really? Everyone knows that. The Northern Ice Wastes are the end of the world. Nobody knows what's beyond them. Right, Kuro?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Come now, don't say that. That cat is quite the remarkable character. But the northernmost permafrost, you say……. Sits a little wrong with me, both the sound of it, and the fact there's not a single sailor who has managed to cross beyond that edge.」
It was the oddly distant look in Tomosato's eyes that only made Sakuya feel all the more as if he had been asked why the sun rises in the east.
【Naomasa】 「……Is that really all? Everybody has to know that. The northernmost permafrost is the end of the world. And they say that nobody knows what lies beyond it. Isn't that right, Kuro?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あい。クロは思う。
　きっと、氷の果ては、おっきな崖になっていて、そこを越えたら、なんもかも、落っこちる、おしまいだってクロは思う」
source.english:
“Yes. Kuro thinks…
there must be a great big cliff at the end of the ice. Go past it, and everything falls. That's the end, Kuro thinks.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Aye. Kuro thinks. Has to be, the edge of the ice becomes a huge cliff, and if they cross it, anything and everything falls off, and then it's all over, Kuro thinks.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おうおう、クロは賢いな。
　まあそういうもんか、こっちだと……。
　ところでクロよ、なんかおめえ、
　やけに歩きづらそうだが」
source.english:
“Aye, aye. Clever Kuro.
Well, I suppose that's how things are over here…
By the way, Kuro,
you seem to be having a hell of a time walking.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Wow, you're such a clever girl, Kuro. Well, guess that's just how it works around here……. By the way, Kuro, you kind of, look like you're having a real hard time walking.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うう、こないだから、わからない。
　航海士に、はかされた。
　鉄のパンツはかされて、朔屋さんには気ぃつけろて、クロ言われても、わからない」
source.english:
“Ugh… Kuro still does not understand.
The mate made Kuro wear them. Iron pants. She told Kuro to watch out for Mr. Sakuya, but Kuro does not understand.”

source.japanese: さも困[こう]じいって眼差しをたゆたわせるクロは、朔屋も気づいていたのだが今日はどうにも内股気味、というにも奇妙な歩き方をしてあり、キャミソールの裾[すそ]をちょいとまくり上げて改めれば、確かにレギンスの腰の辺りがお襁褓でも下に履いたかにだぶついた、指の節で叩けばこれがこつこつ硬い。
source.english: Kuro's gaze wandered in obvious bewilderment. Sakuya, too, had noticed her peculiar gait today—merely calling her pigeon-toed hardly covered it. When he lifted the hem of her camisole to investigate, he found her leggings bulging about the waist as though she wore a diaper underneath. A tap of his knuckle produced a hard little knock.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uuh, since the other day, don't get it. Made to wear, by the mates. Made to wear iron panties, and be careful around Sakuya-san, Kuro was told, but still don't get it.」

Kuro gaze wavered as if she were in great distress, and Sakuya had also noticed that she was walking in a very pigeon-toed manner today, but even that didn't quite capture how strange her gait was, and as he rolled up the hem of her camisole a little bit to get a better look, the part of her leggings around her waist certainly were too large, bulging out as if she was wearing a diaper beneath, and a tap with his knuckle gave a hard, solid knock in return.

source.japanese: ───途端、昨日の、食堂の航海士の言葉が朔屋の脳裏をかすめて過ぎる。
source.english: At once, the navigator's words in the mess hall the day before flashed through Sakuya's mind.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ……っの女ども。
　本気でやりやがった……」
source.english:
“Th—those women.
They really went through with it…”

target.text: ───The moment he did so, the words of the first mates in the mess hall yesterday flashed through Sakuya's mind.
【Naomasa】 「Th……ose nasty women. They actually went and did it……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「げひゃひゃひゃひゃ、なんだそれ。
　ははぁ、さしづめおめえ、
　この白子が支那辺りの娼館仕込みで」
source.english:
“Gehyah-hah-hah! What the hell is that? Oh,
I see.
Somebody fed you a line about this albino being trained in a Chinese brothel—”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Gyahyahyahya, what the hell is that? Ah-haah, so in the end, after that whole spiel about how this albino had been trained in some brothel found somewhere in China.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「口もまんこも絶品だとか吹きこまれた嘘八百を、まんま信じて部屋に連れこもうとしたとかだろうぜ。
　───本気にする莫迦があるかよ」
source.english:
“—said her mouth and cunt were both exquisite—and you swallowed it whole and tried to drag her into your room.
What kind of idiot takes that seriously?”

source.japanese:
───元はそれなりに歴史在る旧家の、次男坊だったと言う事を物語るような、小首をかしげて、穏和にきょとんとした顔だった。智里の言葉に朔屋がまず浮かべてみせたのは。
　次に下顎を軽く落として、目をやや見開いて、こめかみや頬のあたりに疑問符を漂わせて、こちらもまた育ちの良い者が品良く戸惑う顔だった。
　そして朔屋は、次の瞬間それまでの平和で上品な相を一気に崩してぶーと噴き出した。
source.english:
He tilted his head in a gentle, puzzled way—the sort of look that whispered of being the second son of an old, established family. That was the first expression Sakuya gave in reply to Tomosato’s words. Next, his jaw dropped a fraction, his eyes widened a hair, and a question mark hung around his temples and cheeks—another bit of refined bewilderment from someone raised right.
Then, in the very next instant, he utterly shattered his previously peaceful and refined expression and burst out laughing.

source.japanese: 先ほどの縄結びの一件といいこれといい、慧眼にも程がある、あり過ぎる、こうずばずば言い当てられたのではやりづらい事この上ない。
source.english: That and the business with the knots: Tomosato was far too perceptive. When he hit the mark this mercilessly, he was impossible to deal with.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……智里、あんたあの日は部屋で寝てたと言ったが、ホントは隠れて見てたんじゃないのか？」
source.english: “…Tomosato, you said you were asleep in your room that day. Were you actually hiding somewhere and watching?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「You completely fell for that pack of lies you were fed about both her mouth and pussy being exquisite, then actually tried to bring her to your room or something, didn't you? ───Is there even an idiot out there dumb enough to take that seriously?」

───His expression was mildly puzzled, his head tilted slightly to the side; it was the sort of demeanour that served as a testament to the fact that he was, formerly, the second son of a fairly traditional, historically established family. Next, his lower jaw gently fell, his eyes opened a little wider, and question marks floated in the air around his temples and cheeks, and this, too, was a seemly and sophisticated expression of perplexity of a man of good upbringing. Then, the very next moment, the harmoniously refined manner Sakuya had maintained until then suddenly crumbled apart as an undignified snort burst out his nose.

Not just the rope tying incident from before, but now this, too; there had to be limits to how discerning one's eye could be, it was too keen; there was nothing harder to deal with than someone who just kept on so bluntly hitting the nail square on the head.
【Naomasa】 「……Tomosato, you said you were sleeping in your room that day, but you were actually just hiding and watching the whole thing, weren't you?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「知らねえっての。
　それより直の字よ、
　何やら針路に霧がかかってきたようだが」
source.english:
“I don't know anything about it.
More to the point,
Nao, looks like there's fog coming up ahead.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「霧になるなんて話は、
　聞いてないんだが……」
source.english:
“Nobody said
anything about fog…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Like I care about that. More importantly, big Nao, looks like some kind of fog is gathering on our course.」
【Naomasa】 「But I never heard anything about it becoming foggy today……」

source.japanese:
四囲は波に乱れなく、空も穏やかに蒼い中、行く手から湿り気でも嗅いだか、智里が手を庇[ひさし]がわりに蒼い目を細める。
　朔屋にはまだ何も見えなかったし、朝焼けの色や雲の具合で一日の天気を予測する術に長けた下級水夫からも霧の話は聞いていない。
source.english:
The sea was calm all around and the sky serenely blue. Had Tomosato smelled moisture ahead? He shaded his blue eyes with one hand and narrowed them.
Sakuya could see nothing yet. Nor had any of the junior sailors skilled at predicting the day's weather from the dawn colors and the state of the clouds said anything about fog.

target.text: In their surroundings, there was no unrest to be seen in the waves, and the skies were also a peaceful blue, but perhaps he had sensed some humidity ahead, for using his hand in place of a visor, Tomosato narrowed his azure eyes. Sakuya still couldn't see anything, and he also hadn't heard anything about fog from the deck boy who excelled in the art of predicting the day's weather from the colour of the sunrise and the condition of the clouds.

source.japanese: だが例の望遠鏡を取り出して針路を眺めたところ───確かに水平線にむらむらと、墨でも滲ませたような薄濁りの立ち籠めつつあるようだった。
source.english: But he took out the telescope and looked ahead. There, sure enough, a faint murk seemed to be gathering along the horizon, like ink beginning to bleed.

target.text: But when he pulled out that telescope of his and gazed upon their course─── certainly, it seemed as though a hazy murkiness was beginning to gather and shroud the horizon like ink bleeding onto paper.

source.japanese:
普段なら比較的安全で、どうという事もない航路の筈だという話だった。この時季では霧も珍しいという話だった。
　だが現実に、信天翁号が遭遇しているのは、その濁った白味の中に得体の知れぬ不吉さを潜[ひそ]ませ船を分厚く取り囲み、外界から切り離すような濃く密な霧の。洋上どれだけ広がっているのかそれさえ見当もつかぬ。
　たかだか水の細かい粒、薬罐が噴き出す湯気の親類、と強気に出たところで、伸ばした手の先が霞むほどの濃霧には強がりも空しく、信天翁号は船足を緩める事を余儀なくされた。
source.english:
It should have been a relatively safe, unremarkable route, they said. Fog was rare at this time of year, they said.
Yet here it was, thick and dense around the Albatross, an unknown menace lurking in its muddy whiteness, cutting the ship off from the world outside. They could not even guess how far it spread over the sea.
Mere particles of water. A cousin of steam from a kettle. Bold words availed nothing against fog that blurred the end of an outstretched hand. The Albatross had to slow.

target.text: Ordinarily, this was supposed to be a relatively safe and routine passage. Fog was also supposed to be a rare sight at this time of year. But in reality, what the Albatross had encountered was a thick layer of cloudy white wherein an unfathomable ominousness lurked, the sort of deep, dense fog that shrouded ships and cut them off from the outside world. It was not even possible to estimate how far it extended out across the sea.

It was nothing more than fine water droplets, kindred of the steam spouting out from kettles, but for all the bravado one could muster while saying as much, any displays of courage rang hollow when faced with a fog so thick it even obscured what lay right before one's outstretched hand, and the Albatross was forced to slow her pace.

source.japanese: 下級水夫の伝令で、朔屋はクロを操舵室まで引っぱっていったのだが、霧に巻かれた上甲板は初めて通る道、しかも山中の獣道のようにまるで勝手が違って見えて、何度かつまずきバラックの角にあちこち身体をぶつける始末の、船の上にあってこれである。羅針盤くらいしかまともな観測機器を持ち合わせぬ信天翁号など、この霧に巻かれてたやすく針路を見失うのではないか、危ぶむ朔屋の眼前に現れ出でたる、丈高い二つの赤鬼！　とつんのめりそうになったところで、霧を透かして航海士の双子を見る。
source.english: A junior sailor brought the summons, and Sakuya dragged Kuro toward the wheelhouse. Shrouded in fog, the upper deck felt like an unknown road—worse, some unfamiliar game trail in the mountains. He stumbled repeatedly and bruised himself on the corners of the shacks, and this aboard his own ship. With no reliable instrument but a compass, would the Albatross not lose her course at once? While he fretted, two tall red demons materialized before him. He nearly pitched forward before recognizing the navigator twins through the mist.

source.japanese:
精気に溢れ気配が強い双子の存在を、衝突寸前になるまで気づかせないほどに濃く覆う霧の、これでは目隠しされて歩くのとほとんど変わりない。
　双子も同様に、朔屋達が突如出現したようなやや面食らった顔をしていたがすぐさま気を取り直し、二人を操舵室へ引っぱりこむ。
　……甲板上をどれだけ小走りに急いだのか、距離感が失われていたのだが、操舵室は双子のすぐ後ろにあった。
source.english:
The fog lay so thick that even the twins—vivid, forceful presences both—went unnoticed until the instant before collision. Walking through it was scarcely different from walking blindfolded.
The twins, too, looked momentarily taken aback, as though Sakuya and Kuro had appeared from nowhere. They recovered at once and pulled them into the wheelhouse.
…How far had he scurried across the deck? The fog had robbed him of all sense of distance, yet the wheelhouse stood directly behind the twins.

target.text: Following the order delivered his way by a deck boy, Sakuya was dragging Kuro all the way to the wheelhouse, but he had never walked across the upper deck shrouded in fog before; it was like treading a path he had never been on, so different did it look that it seemed almost like an animal trail winding through the mountains, and so he stumbled several times, bumping every part of his body against the corners of the shacks, and all while on a ship at that.

This was the Albatross, a ship that lacked any proper navigational instruments beyond a simple compass, so would they not easily lose their course once enshrouded in this fog; just as Sakuya worried so, they emerged right before his eyes, two towering red oni! Regaining his balance after stumbling and nearly pitching forwards, he peered through the mist to see it was none other than the twin first mates.

The fog covering them was so thick that he didn't even notice the existence of these twins so brimming with vitality and a powerful presence until he was on the verge of crashing into them; this was barely any different from walking around blindfolded. As if Sakuya and Kuro had similarly also suddenly appeared right before them, the twins also looked a little bewildered, but they quickly collected themselves, then pulled both of them into the wheelhouse. ……He had scurried across the upper deck so fast that he'd lost all sense of distance, but the wheelhouse turned out to be right behind the twins.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「クロ、しりとりだ。いくよ。
『ねずみ』」
source.english:
“Kuro, word chain. Here we go.
‘Gerbil.’”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Kuro, it's shiritori time. Here we go. 『|Mouse(Nezumi)』

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あ、あい！　ねずみ……み……み……ああ！『ミカン』！」
source.english: “Y-yes! Gerbil… l… l… Ah! ‘Lemon’!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「A-, aye! Nezumi……mi……mi……aah! 『Mandarin(Mikan)!』

source.japanese: 自信満々に言い放ったものの、たちまちクロのしょぼくれて、俯いてしまって、ただでさえ不健康で景気の悪い白子の、鬱陶しい事この上ない。
source.english: She had delivered the answer with perfect confidence, only to wilt at once and hang her head. The albino was unhealthy-looking and cheerless to begin with; now she made an unbearably dismal sight.

target.text: Though she brimmed with confidence as she blurted it out, Kuro quickly lost heart, then hung her head, and with her already being a sickly and dispirited albino at the best of times, there was no sight in this world more depressing to behold.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「てことは、霧だけで嵐は来ないか。
　幸いなんだかどうなんだか。
　でもこの辺りの海の様子は、
　だいたい覚えてるから……」
source.english:
“So it's only fog. No storm coming.
Whether that's good news is another matter.
But we more
or less remember the sea around here…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「So that means it's just fog, and there's no storm coming? Not sure if that counts as a silver lining or not. But I do mostly remember what the waters around here are like, so……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたしらだけでも、どうにかなんでしょ」
source.english: “We should manage between us.”

source.japanese:
二人は操舵室の窓硝子を透して外の霧を睨[にら]みつけて、その眼差しの鋭き事、横顔の厳しくも美しき事、一対の神像のようであったが、かといってこの霧を透視できるとはさすがに思われぬ。
　舷側を超えて上甲板上に溢れた濃霧は、信天翁号が知らない間に雲の中に突入していたかの眺めをもたらして、海の、周囲の様子を暗い濃白の中に覆い隠した。
source.english:
The twins glared out through the wheelhouse windows. Such keen eyes, such stern and beautiful profiles: a pair of divine statues. But surely even they could not see through this fog.
Spilling over the sides and onto the upper deck, it made the Albatross seem to have entered a cloud without noticing. The sea and everything around it vanished into a dark, dense white.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「We should be able to make it work somehow, even if it's just us.」

The two were staring fixedly at the fog through the glass window of the wheelhouse, and how piercing those gazes, how stern yet beautiful those profiles, they were like a pair of divine statues, but with that said, it was still hard to imagine that they could actually see through this fog. As the dense fog spilled over the gunwale and rolled across the upper deck, it produced a view as if the Albatross had, unnoticed, plunged right into a cloud, and the state of the ocean and their surroundings were obscured within a murky, thick white.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あの……シサム、さん。
　あのう」
source.english:
“Um… Ms. Sisam.
Um…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uhm……Shisamu-san. Uhmm.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なに？　嵐が来ないんならあんたにゃ出番はないよ。怖いんだったら朔屋に『箱』にしまってもらいな」
source.english: “What? If no storm's coming, we don't need you. If you're scared, have Sakuya put you away in ‘the Box.’”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「What? If a storm isn't coming, then you have no role to play. If you're scared, then go ask Sakuya to put you inside the『Box』.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロ、怖いかな。うん、怖いかも。
　でもそれではなくして。
　あのぅ……おまた、すれて、痛いくて」
source.english:
“Is Kuro scared? Mm. Maybe Kuro is. But that is not it.
Um… Kuro is chafed between her legs. It hurts…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああそうだ。外してやれよ可哀相に。
　ほんの冗談だったんだ、真に受けないでくれよ、クロの為にも俺の為にも」
source.english:
“Oh, right. Take it off her, poor thing.
I was just joking—don’t take it seriously, for Kuro’s sake and mine.”

source.japanese: 股間に両手を挟んで摺[す]り合わせ、いかにも具合落ち着かなさげな様子のクロの哀れな事、袋を頭にかぶせられた痩せ犬と似通うて、朔屋も合わせて懇願したのだが。
source.english: Kuro held both hands between her thighs and rubbed them restlessly together. She looked utterly miserable and ill at ease, like a skinny dog with a sack over its head, and Sakuya joined her in pleading.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Wonder if Kuro is scared. Yeah, maybe scared. But that's not it. Uhmm……crotch chafing, it hurts.」
【Naomasa】 「Ahh, right. Take that off her, the poor thing. It really was just a joke, please don't take it seriously. For Kuro's sake, and mine, too.」

Rubbing her hands together between her legs, looking distinctly ill at ease, how pitiful Kuro was, closely resembling a skinny dog with a bag over its head, and so Sakuya also joined in and pleaded her case.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あーそういえば着けっぱだったっけ……。
　シサム、あんた鍵は？」
source.english:
“Oh, come to think of it, I left it on… Sisam,
you got the key?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Aah, now that you mention it, we did just leave it on her……. Shisamu, you have the key?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あれ、キサラが持ってたんじゃなかった？」
source.english: “Wait, didn’t Kisara have that?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Huh, didn't you have it, Kisara?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ううん、知らないよあたしは」
source.english: “Nope, don’t know a thing.”

source.japanese: 舵輪を握り、身を乗りだして霧に対峙する双子の背中は、船の命運一身に背負っているかの凛々しさ、対してクロの苦しみは股擦れとか用を足す時に困るとか、下の事柄に終始して些末事に見えなくもないが、本人にとっては切実で、朔屋も少女が鉄の戒めから疾[と]く解放されん事を願って見守っていたのだが。どうにもこの双子。当然なのかも知れないが、船の針路の事以外には真剣味に欠けるというか。
source.english: The twins, braced at the wheel and leaning forward to confront the fog, carried themselves with the gallantry of two people bearing the ship's whole fate upon their backs. Beside that, Kuro's troubles—chafing between the legs, difficulty relieving herself, one ignoble concern after another—might have seemed trivial. To Kuro herself they were urgent, and Sakuya watched in hope that she would soon be freed from the iron restraint. Yet these twins—perhaps naturally enough—seemed incapable of taking anything seriously except the ship's course.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「No, I don't know where it is.」

The figures of the twins as seen from behind, gripping onto the helm while leaning forwards and facing the fog, held an imposing dignity, as if they alone carried the fate of the ship upon their backs; in contrast, Kuro's anguish all seemed to revolve around matters like her thighs chafing or trouble when relieving herself, mostly bodily matters that may seem trivial at first glance, but for the person in question, were very pressing, and Sakuya watched over the girl, praying that she may swiftly be released from her iron bindings, but. These twins. It was, perhaps, to be expected, but they were hopelessly lacking in seriousness when it came to anything other than the course of the ship, one could say.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「え……じゃあクロは、鉄のパンツ。
　ずっと、はいたまんまの、ままですか」
source.english:
“Huh…
So, the iron pants—am I supposed to keep ’em on… forever?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あのなああんたら……」
source.english: “Listen, you lot…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Eh……Then Kuro will, forever. Have to keep wearing iron panties like this?」
【Naomasa】 「Now listen here you two……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ちょっと黙っとき。今思い出すから。
