　確か……今朝、枕の下に隠そうとして、でも朔屋に見つかるとそりゃもうやばいから」
source.english:
“Keep quiet a sec. Let me think…
I’m pretty sure I was going to hide it under my pillow this morning, but if Sakuya found it, I’d be in deep shit, so…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Shut up for a second. I'm remembering right now. I believe it was……this morning, I was going to hide it under my pillow, but then I thought, it'd be really bad if Sakuya found it, so then……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「シサム、その後ポッケにしまってなかったっけか？」
source.english: “Sisam, didn’t you stash it in your pocket after that?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Shisamu, didn't you put it in your pocket after that?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そうだったそうだった」
source.english: “That’s right, that’s right.”

source.japanese: リーファージャケットのポケットをあざこうとして、そこで内張が破けていたことが発覚する、してしまう。
source.english: She went to rummage through the pocket of her reefer jacket and discovered—or rather, couldn’t help but discover—that the lining was torn.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Right, I did, I did.」
She tried rummaging around the pocket of her reefer jacket only to discover, much to his dismay, that the lining was torn.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……あれ。なんかポッケの内側が……」
source.english: “…Huh. Something's wrong inside my pocket…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「莫迦ーーっっ。
　あんた……まさか落としたとかか？
　船内全部探せってか？　おい頼むぜ……」
source.english:
“You idiot—!! You…
don’t tell me you dropped it?
You want me to search the entire ship? Come on, give me a break…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……Huh. It kind of feels like the lining of my pocket is……」
【Naomasa】 「You idioooot. Don't tell me……that you dropped it or something? Are you gonna tell me to search the whole ship? Come on, I'm begging you here……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「うるさいっての。そうだ思い出した、破れてたから、持ち歩くのはやめて、鍵付きの引き出しにしまったんだね」
source.english: “Quiet, will ya. Come to think of it, the lining was torn, so I quit carrying it and stuck it in a locked drawer.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I said shut up. Right, I just remembered. Because it was torn, I decided not to walk around with it, then put it away in a locked drawer.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そういやそんなコトしてたっけね。
　で、その引き出しの鍵は？」
source.english:
“Now that you mention it,
you did. So where's the key to that drawer?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Now that you mention it, you did do that, didn't you? So, the key for the drawer?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あれ、キサラに預けたと思ったけど」
source.english: “Huh? I thought I’d left it with Kisara.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Huh, but I thought I left that key with you, Kisara.」

source.japanese: 舵を取る事に神経を集中しているのだろう、双子のやりとりはどこか焦点をぼやかして核心から遠回り、骨が欲しいのに芋やら人参やらを放られる犬のもどかしさに朔屋を焦らしていたのだが、そんな彼の服の裾[すそ]をちょんと、と頼りなげに引っぱる手がある。
source.english: Perhaps the helm demanded too much of their attention: the twins kept drifting past the point and circling farther from it, until Sakuya felt like a dog offered potatoes and carrots when it wanted a bone. Then a hand gave an uncertain little tug at his shirt hem.

target.text: It was probably because their minds were fully concentrated on taking the helm, but something about the exchange between these twins had taken a detour away from the actual point, the focus blurring, and feeling the frustration of a dog that wanted a bone but had only been thrown spuds or carrots instead, Sakuya was growing impatient, but there was a hand worriedly tugging on the hem of his clothes.

source.japanese: さっさと双子から貞操帯の鍵の在処を聞き出したくて、その手を邪険に振り払っていたけれどまたくいくい、引かれるのが五月蝿く、きっと睨[にら]めばクロだ、当の被害者より朔屋の方がむきになっている。
source.english: He wanted the twins to tell him where the chastity-belt key was, and quickly, so he brushed the hand aside. It tugged again and again until, irritated, he wheeled to glare at its owner. Kuro. Sakuya was more worked up than the victim herself.

source.japanese: 何事だと、口まで出かかった厳しい声音は立ち消えた。クロが怯えた目つきで霧の向こうのとある一点をしきりに指差して、そこには───
source.english: The stern “What the hell?” on the tip of his tongue died away. Kuro kept pointing at a certain spot beyond the fog, fear in her eyes, and there—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え、あ……っ」
source.english: “Eh, uh…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい……おい……」
source.english: “Hey… hey…”

target.text: He needed to get the hiding place of the key to the chastity belt from these twins as quickly as possible, so he coldly brushed the hand away, but it once again tugged on him; the pulling grated on his nerves, and were he to glare back, he was certain it would be Kuro; Sakuya had become more worked up than the actual victim.

With the words "What is it then?" still on the tip of his tongue, his harsh tone of voice fizzled out before it could be unleashed. Kuro was repeatedly pointing at a certain spot beyond the fog with a terrified look in her eyes, and what he saw there───
【Naomasa】 「Uh, ah……」
【Naomasa】 「Oi……oi……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「黙れ朔屋。あんたのような少女性愛者にゃ発言権なんぞないっての。
　待ってよ、今思い出すから」
source.english:
“Shut up, Sakuya. A pedophile like you has no right to speak. Wait a sec,
I’ll remember it in a moment.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いい加減その鬱陶しいやりとりはやめてくれ、そっちは一旦置いといてだ。
　さっきから……霧の奥で、
　なんか光ってるんだが」
source.english:
“Enough with that annoying back-and-forth already—let’s put that aside for now.
For a while now… deep within the fog,
something’s been glowing.”

source.japanese: クロに続いて朔屋も気づいた、薄蒼い、人魂じみた色合いながら、濃霧の奥にあって輝滅を伝えてくる、霧に降った天狼星のような、光の一点、信天翁号の右手側に。
source.english: Kuro had noticed it, then Sakuya: a point of light to starboard. Pale blue, the shade of a wandering ghost-fire, yet its flickering reached them through the dense mist. Like Sirius fallen into the fog.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Zip it, Sakuya. A creep into little girls like you doesn't even have the right to speak. I'm telling you to wait, I'm just about to remember.」
【Naomasa】 「Can you just drop that aggravating conversation already, shelve it for a minute. For a while now……deep in the fog, there's been something glowing.」

Following Kuro, Sakuya also noticed it; while shining an ethereal blue, its hue akin to that of a hitodama, it was deep within the thick fog, a single point of light conveying a fading brilliance, as though Sirius himself had fallen into the mist, on the starboard side of the Albatross. (TN: Hitodama, written "人魂", are balls of fire that mainly float in the air during the night. They are said to be the souls of the dead that have separated from their bodies, which is also their namesake. They usually glow a sorrowful, pale blue, and they share some visual similarities with the will-o'-the-wisp of Western folklore.)

source.japanese:
そして───浮かび上がった影は、霧を越えて接近してきたというより、信天翁号を取り巻く濃霧が蝟集して、船の形を為してみたかの、古色蒼然とした、帆船だった。まるで霧が、これまでに襲ってきた船の中からお気に入りの一隻を選び出して、その形容を真似たかのような。それも古い時代に属していた船から。
　至るところ霧を絡みつかせて信天翁号の至近に出現した船は四本檣[マスト]のバーク型、それぞれ最前、中央、後部の各檣[マスト]の横帆も最後尾檣の縦帆も、あちこち破れ、ほつれ、船上構造物や船首船尾の各楼もまた、延々と荒海の中を漂流し続けたかに老朽し、信天翁号の傍に帆走するというのに、霧の作用でか今にも衝突せんばかりに膨れあがったと思えば消え去る程に遠ざかるように見える。
source.english:
And then—the shape that emerged was an ancient sailing ship, less a vessel approaching through the fog than the dense mist around the Albatross swarming together and assuming the form of one. As though the fog had selected a favorite from among all the ships it had preyed upon and imitated its likeness—and chosen one from an elder age.
Fog clinging to her everywhere, the vessel that appeared close beside the Albatross was a four-masted barque. The square sails of the foremost, middle, and after masts, and the fore-and-aft sail of the sternmost mast, were torn and frayed here and there; the deck structures, forecastle, and sterncastle were likewise decrepit, as though she had drifted endlessly through savage seas. Yet even as she sailed beside the Albatross, perhaps through some trick of the fog, she seemed first to swell until collision was imminent, then to recede almost beyond sight.

source.japanese:
そちらから押し寄せる霧も、他よりずっと温度が低いような、呼ばわる声の一つだになく、静まり返って随走する、こういう船を幽霊船と言わずしてなんという。
　こうやって随走してくる幽霊船で名高いのは、此方の船を鏡に映したような瓜二つで、そういう二重存在に遭遇した船は漏れなく沈没の悲劇を見るという。
source.english:
The fog streaming from her seemed colder than the rest. No one hailed them; not a voice sounded. She accompanied the Albatross in silence. If this was not a ghost ship,
what was? Famous among such accompanying apparitions was the exact double of one's own vessel, as though reflected in a mirror. Every ship that encountered such a doppelgänger, so the story went, met the same tragic end: it sank.

source.japanese: が、もし霧が寄越したとして、その四本檣[マスト]の船を選んだのは正解だったろう。信天翁号の姿を写した船を召喚しようものなら、その洋上をよたよた漂う不様な姿を傍目に見て、怯えるどころか笑ってしまってお話しにならない。
source.english: If the fog had sent the apparition, though, it had been right to choose a four-master. Had it conjured a likeness of the Albatross, one glimpse of that ungainly shape wallowing along from the outside would have made them laugh rather than tremble. No story worth telling there.

target.text: Thus───the shadow that emerged did not simply pass through the fog and approach them, rather, it was as if the thick fog enshrouding the Albatross had consolidated and taken the shape of a ship. An antique and weathered sailing ship. As though the fog had picked out its favourite vessel from amongst the many ships it had assailed hitherto, then imitated her form. And it had taken its pick from ships that belonged to an era in the distant past at that.

Covered in fog from stern to bow, the ship that manifested very near the Albatross was a four-masted barque; the respective square sails of the main-, mizzen- and fore-mast, as well as the fore-and-aft sail of the jigger-mast, were torn and frayed all over, and the ship's superstructure, from the forecastle to the aftcastle, was heavily weathered, as though she had been drifting endlessly through rough seas, and although she was sailing alongside the Albatross, in what must have been some effect of the fog, just when she seemed to swell in size as though about to collide with them, the next moment she seemed to draw so far away that she nearly vanished from sight.

Even the fog rolling in from that direction felt colder than any other; there was nary a single call or cry to be heard as she glided alongside them, still as the grave, and if this was not a ghost ship, then what else could it possibly be? Amongst the phantom ships known to shadow vessels thus, the most infamous is an exact mirror, the spitting image of one's own ship, and it is said that any vessel unfortunate enough to encounter such a doppelganger invariably meets her tragic end at the bottom of the sea.

However, assuming it was sent by the fog, then choosing that four-masted ship was surely the right decision. Had it instead attempted to summon a ship that mirrored the appearance of the Albatross, then once somebody saw that ungainly form drifting unsteadily across the surface of the sea from an outsider's perspective, they'd be far more like to break into laughter than screams of terror, and that wouldn't make for a tale worth telling.

source.japanese: 朔屋が声も無く、古形の帆船を見つめていると、船尾楼の辺りで光る青がある。鬼火なのか洋燈の灯なのかは知れず、先程から霧の向こうで瞬いていたのがその光だった。灯り、覆い隠されて、長く灯ったり、かつ短く灯ったり。灯りを用いたモールス信号だ。
source.english: Sakuya stared speechlessly at the old-fashioned sailing ship. A blue light shone near its sterncastle. Whether ghost-fire or a lamp he could not tell; it was the light that had been flickering beyond the mist. It flared, vanished beneath a cover, burned long, then short: Morse code sent by lamp.

target.text: As Sakuya wordlessly stared at the antiquated sailing ship, there was a blue light shining near the aftcastle. He knew not if it was an onibi or the light of a lamp, but for a while now, that light had been flickering from beyond the fog. It lit up, was covered, then lit up for a long time, as well as a short time. It was Morse code utilizing the light. (TN: An onibi, written "鬼火", is similar to the hitodama from earlier, and is a ball of fire that floats in the air. It is generally described as blue and like the flame of a torch. They are believed to be spirits born from the corpses of humans or animals, or human resentment turned to flame.)

source.japanese:
【直正】
「灯り信号ときた……また気取ってやがるぜ。
　誰が読めるかっての……」
source.english:
“Light signals… Putting on airs again.
Who the hell can read those?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Oh great, light signals…… real nice and pretentious of them. Who can even read that crap……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「読めない方がおかしいっての。
　えーと、短く三回、長いの一回、長いの三回、そんで短く長く長く短く───
　で、その繰り返し、と」
source.english:
“Not being able to read them's the strange part.
Let's see. Three short, one long, three long, then short-long-long-short.
And repeat.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It'd be stranger if you couldn't. Uh, three short, one long, three long, then short, long, long, short─── and then it repeats.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「こんなん簡単じゃない。
　Ｓ・Ｔ・Ｏ・Ｐ、ストップ、
　テイセンセヨ、だ」
source.english:
“Easy.
S-T-O-P. Stop.
Heave to.”

source.japanese: すらすらと読み解く双子が柄になく物知りというより、一応船員学校に身を置いた事もありながら、モールス信号の初歩も知らない朔屋の方が情けないと言う事なのだろう。
source.english: Rather than the twins being unusually learned, perhaps Sakuya was unusually pathetic: he had once attended a nautical school, yet did not know even elementary Morse code.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Well, that's simple, isn't it? Ｓ・Ｔ・Ｏ・Ｐ, STOP, stop the ship, it says.」

It was not that the twins interpreting it so fluently were uncharacteristically knowledgeable, but rather that Sakuya was pathetic for lacking even a basic grasp on Morse code despite nominally having attended a nautical school.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……おい。そりゃ本当か」
source.english: “…Hey. Is that true?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Oi. Is that true?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「わっ、水夫長、なんでそんな怖い顔。
　普通にしてても怖いんだから、
　ちょっとは気ぃ遣ってよ」
source.english:
“Ah! Bosun, what's with that terrifying look?
You're scary enough as it is. Show a little consideration,
would you?”

source.japanese: もともと建て付けの悪い操舵室の扉、この時の軋みはあまりに不気味に場にそぐいすぎて朔屋を縮み上がらせたし、全身に霧をまとわりつかせた様は、その樽の如くずんぐりした体躯と相俟って、霧の沼地から蘇ってきた水死体と変わらない。
source.english: The wheelhouse door never fit properly. Now its creak suited the scene so eerily that Sakuya shrank. Fog clung all over the boatswain's barrel-shaped body. He might have been a drowned corpse risen from a marsh of mist.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Waah, Bosun, what's with the scary face? You're scary enough at the best of times, so be a little considerate, would you.」

The door to the wheelhouse was poorly fitted to begin with, and the creaking it made just then was so inordinately creepy that it almost suited the atmosphere too well, making Sakuya flinch, and with the way the mist clung to his entire body, as well as his stout, barrel-like physique, he was no different from a waterlogged corpse risen from some foggy swampland that walked amongst the living once more.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「よけいなお世話だ、こう言う時だけカマトトぶりやがって。いいから聞け」
source.english: “Mind your own business. Playing innocent only at times like this. Just listen.”

source.japanese: 古めかしい帆船と灯り信号に、普段は剛胆な掌帆長が、慄然とした顔だった。船乗り仲間に伝わる伝説を語りだす。
source.english: The ancient sailing ship and its light signal had left the ordinarily bold boatswain appalled. He began to tell a legend passed among sailors.

source.japanese: ───いわく、この世には涜神の罪で神に呪われた船というのがあって、その船は未来永劫七つの海をあてどもなく漂流し続ける定めなのだ、と。
source.english: —Legend had it that somewhere in this world sailed a ship cursed by God for the sin of blasphemy, condemned to wander the seven seas without destination for all eternity.

source.japanese:
そして時にその幽霊船は、自分達の呪いに現世の船を巻きこもうとするのだ、と。
　呪われた幽霊船と常に共にある霧に惑わされ、船は為す術もなく航路を見失い、難破するのだ───と。
source.english:
Sometimes the ghost ship tried to draw vessels of the living world into its curse.
Bewildered by the fog that always accompanied the damned ship, they helplessly lost their course and were wrecked.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Didn't ask for your damn opinion. You only ever act the innocent maiden in times like these. Just listen up.」
Met with the time-worn sailing ship and the light signals, the face of the usually intrepid sailmaster was one of horror. He began to narrate a legend once told to him by a sailor comrade.
───According to said legend, there is supposedly a ship cursed by God for committing the sin of sacrilege, and that ship is destined to drift aimlessly across the Seven Seas forevermore, he said.

And at times, that ghost ship attempts to drag vessels from the world of the living into its own curse. Lead astray by the cursed ghost ship and the fog that serves as its eternal companion, the vessel drifts helplessly off its course before it meets its end and founders───he told.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんかどこかで聞いたような……。
　でもそれ、喜望峰辺りの話でしょ」
source.english:
“Sounds familiar…
But isn't that a story from around the Cape of Good Hope?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Kind of feels like I've heard that somewhere before……. But isn't that a tale from around the Cape of Good Hope?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「海は世界中で繋がってんだろが」
source.english: “The sea joins up all around the world, doesn't it?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Come on, the seas connect around the whole damn world.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「でもこいつらって───」
source.english: “But these people—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But these guys are───」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そうよ、お前の考えてる通り、この世のモノじゃない……」
source.english: “That's right. Just as you think. Not of this world…”

source.japanese: ……そこで水夫長は前に進み出て双子に何やら目配せを送ったけれど、朔屋には水夫長の背に隠れて見えなかった。
source.english: The boatswain stepped forward and gave the twins some sort of meaningful look. His back hid it from Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まさか……この信天翁号、いくら腐れ船だってそんな行く先々で化け物の類と出会ってたまるかよ」
source.english: “No way… However rotten the Albatross is, we can't run into monsters everywhere we go.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「That's right, it's just as you think. They're not of this world……」
……And then the Bosun stepped forwards and signaled something or other to the twins with his eyes, but that was all hidden behind the Bosun's back, and so Sakuya didn't see it.
【Naomasa】 「No way……no matter how rotten a ship this Albatross may be, there is just no damn way we keep running into monsters everywhere we go.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ほほう、よう吼えた朔屋。
　そこまで言うなら、羅針盤見てみろ。シサム、見せてやれ」
source.english:
“Oh, well roared, Sakuya.
If you're so sure, look at the compass. Sisam, show him.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well, well, you've got some bark to you, Sakuya. If you're that sure of it, look at the compass. Shisamu, show him.」

source.japanese: シサムの懐中羅針盤を引っぱり出してみるとなんとあろうことか、針がふらふら、触覚をもがれた蟻の歩みのように右に左に揺れて、一向に定まらず、その意味が浸透するにつれ朔屋の身裡をますます冷やしていく。
source.english: Out came Sisam's pocket compass. Impossible—the needle wandered right and left like an ant stripped of its feelers, never settling. As the meaning sank in, Sakuya grew colder and colder.

target.text: And lo and behold, when Shisamu pulled out her pocket compass, how the needle flickered, shaking left and right like the gait of an ant whose antennae had been plucked off, entirely unstable, and as the implication of that gradually seeped into him, so did an even more biting chill creep through Sakuya's bones in turn.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え、これって……嘘じゃないよな？」
source.english: “Huh? This… You aren't joking, are you?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Wha-, this……isn't a trick, right?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そんな都合よく磁石に嘘つかれてたまるかい。ね、朔屋、見ての通りだ」
source.english: “How's a magnet supposed to tell such a convenient lie? There you are, Sakuya. See for yourself.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「磁石も利かない、天測しようにも辺りはご覧の有り様、じゃあ無線は!?」
source.english: “The compass doesn't work. Look around—no chance of taking a celestial sight. Then the radio!?”

source.japanese:
実際、方位磁石は利かなくなり、空も陸影も霧に遮[さえぎ]られ、更に信天翁号にはまともに動く無線など無く、このままでは為す術もなく漂流するばかりだろう。その上謎の帆船まで出来しては。
　よくもここまで、行く先々で非常事態に巻きこまれる、これでは信天翁号だって呪われている事伝説の船に負けず劣らずというところで。
source.english:
Indeed, the compass had ceased to work, fog hid sky and land, and the Albatross possessed no properly functioning radio. If things went on like this, they would likely be left to drift helplessly.
And now this mysterious sailing ship. To be caught in such emergencies wherever they went: at this rate the Albatross herself was no less cursed than the ship of legend.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Like hell a compass would just lie that conveniently. See, Sakuya, it's exactly what it looks like.」
【Naomasa】 「The compass isn't working, and even should we try celestial navigation, you can see what it's like out there, but then what about the radio!?」

Indeed, the compass had ceased to function, both sky and distant land alike were obscured behind fog, and moreover, the Albatross did not have any properly functioning radio or anything of the sort, so at this rate, they'd likely just drift along helplessly. In addition to all this, an enigmatic sailing ship had even emerged. How in the world did they manage to get caught up in a crisis everywhere they went; with a track record like this, one could well say that the Albatross was every bit as cursed as that ship from the legend.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「もう、やだなあ朔屋さん。
　そんな良いもの、もし積んでたところで」
source.english:
“Oh, come on, Mr. Sakuya.
Even if we had something that nice aboard…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Oh, stop it, Sakuya-san. Even should we by any chance happen to get our hands on something that valuable.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「一等航海士か水夫長が売っ払うちゃうに決まってるじゃないか」
source.english: “The chief mate or the bosun would've sold it, of course.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「くそう可愛いなあ君らは何時でもニコニコとっ。とにかく、まずいんじゃないのこれ」
source.english: “Damn, you lot are adorable, always grinning like that! Anyway, this is bad, isn't it?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「It'd obviously be sold off by the first mates or the Bosun, right?」
【Naomasa】 「Goddamn it, you guys are just frustratingly adorable, always with a smile on your lips. But anyway, this is pretty bad, isn't it?」

source.japanese: とはいえ下級水夫達とて必ずしも泰然と構えているのではなく、みな固唾を呑んで成り行きに身を硬くしている者がほとんど、それでも一番落ち着きをなくして、それはもう意気地無く狼狽えているのが朔屋であり、あわあわと手をばたつかせるわ足下ひっきりなしに踏み換えるわ、その見苦しさは目にした者に反面教師的な効果を与えるほど。シサムは朔屋の肩越しに視線をやって、これ見よがしに、わざと聞こえるように、
source.english: Not that the junior sailors were all perfectly composed. Most stood rigid, swallowing hard as events unfolded. Yet the one who had lost all composure—the one floundering about most abjectly of all—was Sakuya: hands fluttering in panic, feet forever shifting beneath him, so unsightly a spectacle that merely witnessing it taught a man precisely how not to behave. Sisam cast a glance over Sakuya's shoulder and, ostentatiously making certain he could hear, said—

target.text: With that said, it was not as if the deck boys were necessarily maintaining a composed facade either; they were all holding their breath, with most of them tensed up as they anxiously waited to see how things would unfold, and yet the one most visibly shaken, helplessly flustered without a shred of resolve, was still Sakuya, who was waving his hands around in panic, incessantly shuffling his feet, and the sheer disgrace of it made him serve as a stellar example of how not to act for any who witnessed it. Shisamu threw a glance over Sakuya's shoulder, then said the following in an ostentatious manner that was clearly meant for him to hear,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「でも、今さら焦ったって仕方ないよね」
source.english: “Still, no point getting worked up now.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But there's nothing to gain from getting all worked up at this point.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そうね。あたしらはただ舵を取るだけさ」
source.english: “Right. We'll just take the helm.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「豪い男前だなあんたら。
　舵を取るったってこの霧で、おまけに磁石もダメ、クロは……」
source.english:
“Very dashing, both of you.
But how do you steer in this fog, with the compass no good and Kuro…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「That's right. We're just taking the helm.」
【Naomasa】 「Look at you two, so gallant you'd put any man to shame. Taking the helm in this fog, without any compass to boot, and Kuro is……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「今日は船長、出番ないみたいだから、
　下に連れてっておいたよ」
source.english:
“No work for the captain today, apparently,
so we took her below.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だとさ。それで何をどうするって───」
source.english: “There you are. Then what are we supposed to—”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「It doesn't seem like our captain has a part to play today, so we took her down below.」
【Naomasa】 「So he says. So then, what and how are you going to───」

source.japanese: だが朔屋の危惧をよそに、シサム・キサラは悠然としたもの、こんな襤褸船でも一等航海士の職掌は伊達ではないと、濃霧の中舵を取り続けたのだった。見知った海域であるとはいえ、数米先も定かならぬ不明の霧の中を、掌を指してみせるように。
source.english: But despite Sakuya's fears, Sisam and Kisara remained perfectly unhurried. Even aboard this ramshackle ship, the office of chief mate was no empty title. Familiar waters or not, one could scarcely see a few meters ahead in that impenetrable fog, yet they steered through it as though the route lay mapped across their own palms.

target.text: However, completely ignoring Sakuya's concerns, Shisamu and Kisara remained calm and composed, and as if to say that, even on a run-down ship like this, they didn't hold the position of first mate for show, they continued to helm the ship through the thick fog. Familiar waters these may be, it was still through a fog so blinding you could barely make out a few metres ahead, and yet they nevertheless steered the ship as if the sea was clear as day.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「舵、細かく切ろう。
　二九八度、速度は───」
source.english:
“Small helm adjustments.
Two-nine-eight degrees. Speed—”

source.japanese: ───波に揺らぐ船にあろうと、正中線正しく通し、床に根を生やしたように動じず。
source.english: Even aboard a ship swaying with the waves, they held themselves perfectly centered, unmoving as though rooted in the floor.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Fine adjustments on the helm. Two-nine-eight degrees, speed───」
───Even on a ship rolling on the waves, her centerline remained perfectly aligned, and she stood immovable as though rooted to the deck.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「今のとこ、微速でいいでしょ。
　操舵室より機関室へ。
　速度は微速に落として」
source.english:
“Dead slow will do for now.
Wheelhouse to engine room.
Reduce to dead slow.”

source.japanese: 前方を見据える眸[ひとみ]を充たす輝きは、航海者を導く星の光か───
source.english: The brilliance in their eyes as they stared ahead—was it the light of stars that guide a voyager?

source.japanese:
【機関長】
『了解』
source.english: ‘Understood.’

source.japanese: 壁に這う伝声管で答える渋く低い声音は機関室からの、常と変わらず沈着で、この操舵室に航海士あれば、そして機関室に彼の人あれば、船の目と心臓は鋭く強靱で、なまじの海難など寄せつけぬ頼もしさを聞く者に及ぼす───この信天翁号は艱難辛苦にあって映えるというのがなんとも皮肉だ。
source.english: The speaking tube running along the wall brought back a low, mellow voice from the engine room, as composed as ever. With these navigators in the wheelhouse, with that man in the engine room, the ship had keen eyes and a strong heart: those who heard him felt an assurance that no ordinary peril of the sea could touch her. How ironic that the Albatross should shine amid hardship.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「For now, dead slow should be fine. Wheelhouse to engine room. Reduce speed to dead slow.」
The radiance filling those eyes firmly locked ahead was like the very starlight that guided navigators───
【Chief Engineer】 『Affirmative.』

The reply through the voicepipe crawling across the walls came from the engine room, its ever-present composure delivered in a husky baritone; as long as the first mates were here in this wheelhouse, and that man was in the engine room, the eyes and heart of the ship would remain sharp and tenacious, filling any listeners with a quiet assurance that no ordinary peril at sea would get the better of them───it really was bitter irony that the Albatross only seemed to shine the brightest in times of trial and tribulation.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「このまま七分……いや、八分進んで」
source.english: “Seven minutes on this course… No, eight.”

source.japanese:
全身を感覚器官となし、肌や髪の毛先一本一本に触れる気流で周囲の状況を読み取っているような、二人がその身に宿す知覚力には、朔屋は見覚えがあった。
　嵐の時のクロ、船長クロの把握力と似通っているのだ。ただクロの方は、船全体に己の全感覚を拡大、浸透させ、船を自分の手足のように統御する様相だが、シサム・キサラの知覚力は、どこであろうと己の立つ位置を知り、いかなる状況であろうと見失わずに進む事を可能とする力なのではないか。
source.english:
Sakuya had seen something like the twins' preternatural perception before. They seemed to turn their whole bodies into organs of sense, reading their surroundings from the air currents brushing their skin and the tips of every hair.
It resembled Kuro's command in a storm—Captain Kuro's. But Kuro extended every sense throughout the ship and controlled the vessel like her own limbs. Perhaps the twins' gift instead allowed them to know precisely where they stood, wherever they were, and to advance without losing their way in any circumstances.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Hold this for seven……no, make it eight minutes.」

Their entire body as a sensory organ, it was as if they perceived the state of their surroundings through the air currents touching their skin and every little tip of every strand of their hair, and that acuity they harboured within them was something Sakuya recalled seeing before.

Like Kuro during a storm: it resembled closely the ability of total command that Captain Kuro displayed. But in Kuro's case, it was as if all the senses of her body expanded to the entire ship and permeated it, she had the bearing of someone controlling the ship like it were her own limbs, but the perceptual acuity of Shisamu and Kisara, was it not instead the power to, no matter where they may find themselves, always know the exact location they were standing in, and no matter the situation they were placed in, be able to move forwards without losing sight of their destination?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ、あら……？
　なんか今、岩陰が……」
source.english:
“Uh… what?
Was that the shadow of a rock just now…?”

source.japanese: 霧を割き、舷側をすり抜けていった岩礁は、海から突きだした鎌のように尖って、針路がほんの少しでもぶれていたなら船腹を切り裂いていたのに違いない。朔屋はそのぎりぎりの際に胃の腑の締めつけられる心地だが、シサムはとうに気づいていたと言わんばかりに、いや、事実気づいていたのだろう、声音はどこまでも平然と。
source.english: The reef split the fog and slid past the hull, sharp as a sickle thrust from the sea. The slightest deviation would surely have slit the ship open. Sakuya's stomach clenched at the narrow escape. Sisam spoke as calmly as though she had noticed the danger long before. No—she probably had.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「O-, oh dear……? I kind of think I saw the shadow of a rock just now……」

Splitting the fog, the reef on the side of the ship that barely streaked past them was sharp as a sickle jutting out from the ocean, and had their course wavered in the slightest, then there was no doubt that it would have torn open the belly of the ship. After being that hair's breadth from disaster, Sakuya felt as thought his stomach was being wrenched tight, but as if to all but say that she had noticed long ago, no, in reality, she probably had, Shisamu's tone of voice was entirely self-possessed.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「この辺りは岩礁が多くてね。
　知らないで通るとかなり難渋するはずよ」
source.english:
“Lots of reefs around here.
Anyone coming through without knowing them would have a rough time.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、知ってたにしても、この霧じゃ……」
source.english: “Even if you know them, in this fog…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Lots of reefs around this area, yeah? Would give you a real hard time if you tried passing through here without knowing.」
【Naomasa】 「No, even if you knew about it, with this fog……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ここで、針路は二八一度へ。
　あっちの船が追いついてきそうだから、
　速度は半速に上げて」
source.english:
“Here, change course to two-eight-one degrees.
That ship looks like it's catching up.
Increase to half speed.”

source.japanese: 細かく舵輪を繰るうちに、今度は両側からアーチ様に繋がった岩壁の、掴みかからんばかりに狭い隙間を信天翁、するりと通り抜けて、船腹の軋みは獲物逃した岩の罠に嘲笑を浴びせかけるかのよう。
source.english: With minute turns of the wheel, the Albatross slipped cleanly through a gap so narrow that the rock walls arching in from either side seemed ready to seize her. The groan of her hull sounded like laughter flung back at a stone trap whose prey had escaped.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「今度は両舷に岩壁かよ。
　なんだってあんたら、こんな的確に……」
source.english:
“Rock walls on both sides now.
How do you know so exactly…?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Here, steer course two-eight-one. That ship seems to be gaining on us, so bring us up to half ahead.」

With precise adjustments at the helm, this time, the Albatross glided smoothly through an arching rock formation, squeezing past a gap so dangerously tight the stone seemed about to reach out and grab her from both sides, and the creaking of the hull almost sounded like the ship herself was hurling mockery at the rocky trap that had let its prey escape.
【Naomasa】 「And now it's rock walls on both sides? How the hell can you two be this precise……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「五分間、針路宣候。
　それから船首反対に、二九五度───」
source.english:
“Steady on this course for five minutes.
Then bring the bow around to two-nine-five degrees—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Steady as she goes for five minutes. Then bring her head around to two-nine-five───」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……どういう仕組みか知らんがな、
　この二人、現在位置が判るんだよ、観測器具とかそんなものなくってもな」
source.english:
“…Don't know how it works,
but these two know their position. Without instruments or anything.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……I don't know what kind of trick is at work here, but these two always know their current position, even without any navigational instruments.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だから一旦地形さえ記憶しちまえば、
　こんな芸当だってお手の物ってわけだ」
source.english:
“Once they've memorized the lay of the land,
this sort of trick's easy for them.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So as long as they know the waters, pulling off a trick like this is second nature to them.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ただまあ、二人揃ってないとダメ、だがな」
source.english: “Though they have to be together.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ……そりゃあ俺も知ってるわ」
source.english: “Ah… That much I know.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「It's just, well, it won't work without both of them together」
【Naomasa】 「Oh yeah……even I know that part.」

source.japanese:
水夫長が結んだ通り、ろくな海図も、観測器具もないのにもかかわらず、双子の指示は的確そのものだった。
　二人の操船に従い、信天翁号が進路を変えていくと、霧の中を岩礁が船の脇を通り過ぎていく。
　二人の操船がなかったら、この霧の中で岩礁と激突、この襤褸船などひとたまりもなく沈没していたに違いない。
source.english:
As the boatswain had said, the twins' directions were exact despite the lack of decent charts or instruments.
Under their hands, the Albatross changed course again and again while reefs slid past through the fog.
Without the twins at the helm, she would surely have struck one, and this ramshackle vessel would have gone down at once.

target.text: Just as the Bosun had concluded, despite not having any proper chart or navigational instruments to work with, the instructions from the twins were precision itself. Following their steering, the Albatross changed course, and within the fog, reefs passed by the side of the ship. Without their deft steering, there was no doubt they would have crashed into a reef in this fog, and the likes of this derelict ship would have foundered without the least resistance.

source.japanese:
───しかし天然の海難は免れても、あの帆船から逃れられたわけではない。
　朔屋は信天翁号がすれすれで天然の罠を躱[かわ]していく見事、そればかりに気を取られて一時失念していたが、不気味に古びた帆船も岩礁を避けてまさしく幽霊のように、は依然として信天翁号に追随してきてるのだった……。
source.english:
But escape from the sea's natural perils did not mean escape from that sailing ship.
For a time Sakuya had forgotten it, transfixed by the skill with which the Albatross skimmed past one natural trap after another. Yet the eerily ancient vessel, too, threaded the reefs like a ghost and still followed the Albatross…

target.text: ───But while they might have escaped a shipwreck by natural causes, they had not managed to escape that sailing ship. Sakuya had been so preoccupied with the spectacle of the Albatross barely shaving past disaster after disaster as she dodged those traps set by nature herself that he had momentarily forgotten all about it, but that uncannily timeworn sailing ship, as though were it a ghost, also slipped past the reefs, and it was still catching up to the Albatross…….

source.japanese:
信天翁号が霧の中を往く間、時に右に時に左に位置を変えながらしつこく追随してきた幽霊船の、何処までも食い下がってくるかの
執念深さ、流石、と言えたが。
　自ら動いて信天翁号を久遠の薄明に封じこめるかに見えた濃霧も、遂にその密度減じて晴れていき、幽霊船の輪郭も徐々に判然と。
　霧から引きずり出された帆船の姿は、輪郭が曖昧だった時に比べて不気味さを減じ、恐ろしいというよりみずぼらしさが目についた。
　死体は屍衣を引き剥がされても不吉な事には変わりないが、その帆船はこうしてみると単なる老朽船の、先程からモールス信号もひっきりなしに繁くしているのが、なにやら老人の繰り言めいて迫力というのに欠ける。
source.english:
As the Albatross sailed through the fog, the ghost ship dogged her with remarkable tenacity, shifting now to starboard, now to port, but never relinquishing the chase. Yet even the dense mist, which had seemed to move of its own accord and seal the ship in eternal twilight, at last began to thin; the ghost ship's outline gradually sharpened.
Dragged out of the fog, the vessel lost some of the menace it had possessed while indistinct. Shabbiness caught the eye more readily than terror. A corpse remains sinister even when stripped of its shroud, but seen clearly, this was merely a decrepit old ship. Its incessant Morse signals had begun to resemble an old man's grumbling and carried about as much force.

source.japanese:
そもそもなんの目的で現れたのか、ただ恐怖を植え付けるためだけにか、なるほど度を越した恐怖は人を殺すとはいえ、それには相応の舞台立てが必要で、霧の帷[とばり]を失った今となっては。速度も減じ、船足のろまな信天翁にも置いていかれる始末の。
　濃霧も次第に薄れ、このままなら無事に脱出なるか、一体何のために出てきたのかと首を捻り、朔屋の見やる先で───
source.english:
Why had it appeared in the first place? Only to instill terror? True, fear beyond a certain degree could kill, but that required a suitable stage, and now it had lost its curtain of mist; it was slowing too, even falling behind the sluggish Albatross.
The fog continued thinning. Perhaps they would escape safely after all? Wondering what it had appeared for, Sakuya looked toward it—

target.text: While the Albatross travelled through the fog, at times it would be on their left, at other times on their right, but that ghost ship was still doggedly pursuing them; would it continue to hound them to the end of the world? It was an impressive display of tenacity, one could say, but. Even the dense fog, which had seemed to move of its own will to seal the Albatross within a timeless gloam, at long last thinned and cleared, and the outline of the ghost ship also gradually grew clearer.

After being dragged out of the fog, the shape of the ship was less ominous compared to when its silhouette was hazy, and rather than being afraid, its shabbiness was what caught his eye. Even if a corpse is stripped of its burial shroud, it remains no less unsettling than before, but looking at the sailing ship like this, it was nothing more than some old, decrepit ship, and while the Morse code they'd been sending for a while now was still being frequently flashed without interruption, it felt lacking in impact, like the ramblings of an old man.

To begin with, for what purpose did they even show themselves? Was it simply to plant the seeds of fear in them? Indeed, while excessive fear certainly can kill a man, that still demands a fitting stage, and that had been lost together with the veil of fog. They had also lowered their speed, and all that awaited them was being left behind by even the slow-moving Albatross. The thick fog continued to gradually thin, and as he tilted his head while wondering if they'd manage to make good their escape with the way things stood, and why that ship had bothered showing up at all, there, in the direction of Sakuya's gaze───

source.japanese:
帆船はぶるんと鳴動した。
　朔屋の疑念を嘲罵と受け取ったでもあるまいに、なにやら燻っていた怒りを爆発させた塩梅で、ぐんぐんと船速を増した。
　それ、勢いはあったとしても、亡霊の怨念というよりもっと現世的な欲望に根差した速度であったのだが、帆船の接近に泡を食った朔屋にはそんな細かい点まで観察していられる余裕なく、すがるように振り向けば、航海士は眼を細め、ほくそ笑んでいるでないか。
source.english:
The sailing ship shuddered with a low rumble.
Surely it had not mistaken Sakuya's doubt for an insult, yet it seemed to erupt with some long-smoldering anger and rapidly gathered speed. Its vigor, however, sprang less from the resentment of the dead than from some altogether worldly appetite. Panicking at its approach, Sakuya had no leisure to observe such niceties; he turned pleadingly, only to find the navigators narrowing their eyes and smirking.

target.text: The sailing ship shook and rumbled. While it surely hadn't taken Sakuya's doubts as pointed mockery, with what seemed an explosion of some long-smouldering anger, the ship surged ahead with swiftly increasing speed. Granted, it was moving with undeniable momentum, yet its speed was rooted in more worldly desires than ghostly grudges, but Sakuya, panicking at the approach of the sailing ship, hardly had the leeway to observe such fine details, and as he turned around with a look of desperate pleading in his eyes, the first mates narrowed their eyes and───were smirking at him, were they not?

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「おー、頑張る頑張る、木っ端かいぞ……いや、幽霊どもが」
source.english: “Oh, look at them go. Those two-bit pira—ghosts, I mean.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「相手も頑張るって、何を悠長な。
　このまんまじゃ接触しちまう！」
source.english:
“Look at them go? How can you be so calm?
We're going to collide!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Wow, they're trying really hard, these pathetic nobodies…… uh, I mean, ghosts.」
【Naomasa】 「What do you mean they're trying hard, what's with the nonchalant attitude? They'll be coming right alongside us at this rate!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あー、どうにかぶつかんないよう、それはあたしらでなんとかしとくから」
source.english: “Ah, we'll manage not to hit them somehow. Leave that to us.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そっちはなんとかしておくって、あ。あ。あ。奴ら、鉤綱とか掛梯子とか持ち出してきてる！」
source.english: “Leave it to you—ah. Ah. Ah! They're bringing out grappling ropes and ladders!”

source.japanese: 鎧袖一触の間合いに迫った帆船の、甲板に集まったるは船から湧きだした亡者共か、帆船の全長と全幅は似たり寄ったり、ただ檣[マスト]の分だけ上背があって、ぴたりと横付けされると上からのしかかられるかの重苦しさ。
source.english: The sailing ship drew within range of a single decisive clash. Figures crowded its deck—dead souls welling up from the vessel itself? She was about the same length and beam as the Albatross, but her masts towered higher, and when she drew tight alongside, she seemed to loom down upon them with crushing weight.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Aah, don't worry, we'll do something to make sure they don't hit us.」
【Naomasa】 「You just said you'd do something about it, ah. Ah. Ah. Those guys, they're pulling out grappling hooks and ladders!」

The sailing ship had drawn close enough for a swift, decisive victory, and gathering on the deck, was that not the restless dead that had surged out from the ship? While the overall length and beam of the sailing ship was roughly the same as the Albatross, their masts alone were taller, and when it was brought right alongside them, it felt as though an oppressive weight was looming down on them from above.

source.japanese: 威圧的ではあるし、濃霧が消音していたのか、霧の帷[とばり]を抜けてみると檣[マスト]や船体の軋みは信天翁号に劣らず耳を劈[つんざ]く、我が船の騒音には慣れても他のそれは神経に障[さわ]り、朔屋の怯えを呼び戻す。
source.english: It was imposing enough. Perhaps the dense fog had muffled it: now that they had passed beyond the curtain of mist, its hull and masts shrieked as deafeningly as the Albatross's. Sakuya had grown accustomed to his own ship's din, but another vessel's grated upon his nerves and revived his fear.

target.text: It was overbearing, and perhaps the dense fog must have muffled it, but now that the veil of mist had lifted, the creaking of its masts and hull pierced his ears in a manner not to be outdone by the Albatross, but while he had grown used to the din of his own ship, this new noise really grated on his nerves, and it brought back Sakuya's panic.

source.japanese:
───が。
　幽霊船、亡霊を乗せた船としては、どうにも直接的な脅迫の手口ではないか？
source.english:
But for a ghost ship,
a vessel of the dead, was this not a rather direct method of intimidation?

source.japanese: かんかんと舷側の縁に掛かる鉤も梯子も、壁を抜け虚空を滑るのが常套の、亡霊達の移乗手段としては、いささか物理的に過ぎやしないか？
source.english: Hooks and ladders clanged against their rail. For ghosts accustomed to passing through walls and gliding through empty air, was that not an excessively physical way to board?

target.text: ───However. For a ghost ship, a vessel carrying the souls of the damned, was this not an awfully direct method of intimidation?

And the hooks and ladders clanging against the gunwale, too: as a means of transfer used by ghosts, who would conventionally simply slip through walls and glide through the air, was it not just the slightest bit too physical?

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「いやはや、殺る気満々だねありゃ」
source.english: “Well, well. They're certainly eager to kill.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Goodness me, they are just dripping with bloodlust.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「朔屋よ、白兵戦だぜ、こりゃあ」
source.english: “Sakuya, this'll be hand-to-hand.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ま、またか!?　勘弁してくれ、なんだって今どきそんな海賊時代みたいな……ん？」
source.english: “A-again!? Spare me! Why, in this day and age, are we fighting like it's the age of pirates… Hm?”

source.japanese: 自分が言い出した言葉に何事か引っかかるものを覚えたけれど、それを確かめる間もなく朔屋は水夫長に手渡された棒状の物を見て目を剥いた。
source.english: Something in his own words caught at his mind. Before he could examine it, the boatswain handed him a long object. His eyes bulged.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Sakuya, we've got some hand-to-hand combat coming up.」
【Naomasa】 「A-, again!? Spare me, please, why the hell does it feel like we're suddenly back in the age of pirates or somethi……nghh?」

Though he felt something niggling at him in the words that he himself had said, he wasn't given the time to confirm what it was, for when Sakuya saw the stick-shaped object he was handed by the Bosun, his eyes opened wide.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ええからええから。ほら武器をやろう。
　俺は水夫どもを指揮してくるから、
　まずはてめえが防戦しておくんだぜ」
source.english:
“Never mind, never mind. Here, take a weapon.
I'm off to command the sailors.
You hold the enemy back until then.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Yeah, yeah, never mind that. Here, I'm giving you a weapon. I'll be taking command of the sailors, so you go hold the line first.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「武器ってこれ、デッキブラシでないの」
source.english: “A weapon? Isn't this a deck brush?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「You call it a weapon, but isn't this just a deck brush?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「それこそホーリーブラシ！　ウィンチェスター教会でえっらい坊さんが、聖別の儀式をかけた、幽霊にゃ滅法利く得物さね」
source.english: “Why, that's the Holy Brush! Some exalted priest at Winchester Church performed a rite of consecration over it. Murder on ghosts.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「That there is none other than the Holy Brush! An eminent priest blessed it with a rite of consecration in the Winchester Cathedral, and it is a weapon extraordinarily effective against any ghastly ghosts, y'know?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「すっげぇぜ。そいつさえありゃ、朔屋は無敵だぁー」
source.english: “It's amazing. With that in your hands, Sakuya, you're invincible!”

source.japanese: 宿命の英雄が、伝説の武器を手にした時に現れて祝福授ける妖精……の可憐さ儚さとは二人は縁遠い、露わな太腿や自己主張激しい乳房は、むしろ積極的に男に色仕掛けで惑わす妖霊と近縁だったろうし、囃したてるのだってなんとも無責任で、朔屋をこれっぽっちも安心させやしない。
source.english: Fairies appear to bless a destined hero when he acquires a legendary weapon—but the twins had little of a fairy's delicate, fleeting loveliness. Those bare thighs, those aggressively assertive breasts, brought them closer to female djinn who actively bewitched men with their charms, while their altogether irresponsible cheers gave Sakuya not the slightest comfort.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「胡散臭ぇよっ。そんな都合の良いモノがこの船にあってたまるか……いや待てよ、こういうのに限って積んでそうだな……でも待て、こういうのって宗派とかが大事……」
source.english: “Sounds fishy! No way this ship's got something that convenient… No, wait. Just the sort of thing it would carry… But hold on, doesn't the denomination matter with this stuff…?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It's amazing. As long as you have it by your side, Sakuya, you're invincibleー!」

Like the fairy who appeared to bestow her blessing upon the destined hero as he took the weapon of legend in hand ……but these two were far removed from any of that delicate beauty or ephemeral charm; their exposed thighs and fiercely self-asserting chests were, if anything, probably more closely related to the jinniyah that aggressively seduce and beguile men, and all that mindless cheering to egg him on was utterly irresponsible, and it did nothing to reassure him in the least.

【Naomasa】 「Sounds reaaaal fishy. There's no way something that convenient would be on this ship……wait, actually, this is exactly the kind of thing we would have on board……but wait, in these cases, denominations and such are very important and……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「いいから一発、
　派手にかましてきぃやーっ」
source.english:
“Just go give
them one great big whack!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Enough already, just get out there and give 'em a big old smack!」

source.japanese: デッキブラシを握ってぶつぶつと、呟いていた隙にどんと背中を蹴り出され、操舵室から転[まろ]び出るが甲板上へ、前にのめった朔屋の頭上をかすめて薙いだサアベルの、バランスを崩していなかったら頭半分輪切りに飛ばされていたタイミング、初手から死地を跨[また]ぎ越す、いやはや暢気に怖がっていられる余裕などない、どこにも。
source.english: While he stood muttering with the deck brush, a kick in the back sent him tumbling from the wheelhouse onto the deck, and a saber swept just over his pitching head. Had he not been off balance, it would have sliced away half his skull: his very first move had carried him across the edge of death. No time to be afraid at his leisure now. None at all.

target.text: While distracted with muttering complaints to himself with the deck brush clenched tightly in hand, he was suddenly kicked hard in the back, and just as he stumbled out of the wheelhouse to the upper deck, a sweeping sabre skimmed right over the top of Sakuya's head, and had he not lost his balance, the timing of the swing would have sliced half his face off; he was walking a tightrope atop the jaws of death from the outset, and he no longer had the luxury of being scared in peace, not even a shred it.

source.japanese: このように朔屋は、幽霊どもと真正面切って鉢合わせすること余儀なくされたわけだが。
source.english: And so Sakuya was obliged to meet the ghosts face-to-face.

target.text: Thus, Sakuya found himself forced into a direct, face-to-face encounter with those spectres.

source.japanese: 襞をたっぷり取った洋袴、サッシュベルトを巻いて派手なコートを引っかけた奴。縞のバンダナ被って油引きの襯衣を滑[ぬめ]らせ毛脛の半ズボン姿の奴、古式正しい海賊姿の、面はあちらもこちらも髑髏の虚ろな眼窩と禍[まが]き笑みを貼り付けにした剥き出しの歯列で、それら古典的な幽霊達が、鉤綱、やら掛梯子やらを伝って次から次へと乗りこんでくるのは、地獄の釜が開いたか死者が蘇るという終末の裁きの日か。
source.english: One wore generously pleated trousers, a sash belt and a showy coat thrown over his shoulders. Another had a striped bandanna, a slippery oilskin shirt and shorts exposing hairy shins. Proper old-fashioned pirates, but every face was a skull: hollow sockets, exposed teeth fixed in a baleful grin. These classic ghosts came aboard one after another by grappling rope and ladder. Had the cauldron of hell opened? Was this the final Judgment Day, when the dead arose?

target.text: A fellow clad in wide, deeply pleated slops and a flamboyant coat cinched with a sash belt. A lad wearing a striped bandanna, draped in a grease-slicked shirt, and wearing shorts showing off his hairy legs; they were all wearing authentic, traditional pirate outfits, faces everywhere, each one a skull with hollow eye sockets and a sinister grin plastered over bared rows of teeth, and these classic ghosts boarded the ship one after another by means of rope or ladders; had the gates to Hell opened, was this the day of The Last Judgment where it is said all the dead will be resurrected?

source.japanese: 冥府の軍勢のように凄まじく、間違いなく脅威ではあるのだが、それは霧の中を追随してきた際の、ぞくぞくと肌を凍えさせる恐怖ではなく、判りやすい暴力であり、呪い、取り殺すのではなく挑んできたのは白兵戦、怪奇小説の文体が剣戟小説のそれに突如変調したかのちぐはぐさ加減が、ある。
source.english: They were dreadful, like an army of the underworld, and certainly a threat, but not the shivering, skin-freezing terror of their pursuit through the fog. This was plain violence: not a curse, not a haunting that killed, but close combat. A strange mismatch, as though the prose of a supernatural tale had abruptly changed into a swashbuckler's.

source.japanese: とはいえ朔屋にとっては食い違いを咎め立てしていられる状況ではなく、そんな悠長に違和感をあげつらっていては、彼の方が手足を刻まれて右と左にちぐはぐにされてしまいかねない危機の、朔屋はこれに対して即座に対処した。
source.english: Sakuya, however, was in no position to lodge a complaint about the mismatch. If he took his time dissecting the incongruity, he might be the one carved limb from limb, his own right and left reduced to a mismatched set. Faced with that danger, he acted at once.

target.text: Though as fearsome as the legions of the underworld, and doubtless a threat, it was not the sort of dread that chilled the skin and bones like when they had been shadowed through the fog, no, this was an easily understood violence, he would not be cursed or haunted to death, for what they challenged him to was hand-to-hand combat; it had a certain degree of incoherence to it, as if the literary style of a Gothic horror novel had suddenly transformed into that of period swordplay fiction.

With that said, as far as Sakuya was concerned, this really was not the right time or place to start fault-finding any inconsistencies; if he were to so leisurely carp on about things that felt out of place to him, it was not hard to imagine that he might end up having his limbs hacked apart and swapped left-to-right, so dire a peril was it, and so Sakuya immediately dealt with it.

source.japanese: 背中を向けて、全速で、逃げ出したのだ。
source.english: Turned his back and ran at full speed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーーーっ、だから俺、荒事なんかできないっつーの……げっ！」
source.english: “Aaaah! I told you, I'm no good in a fight… Gah!”

target.text: He turned his back to them, and at full tilt, ran away.
【Naomasa】 「AAーーーHH, I TOLD YOU, I DON'T DO FIGHTING ……GEH!」

source.japanese: ───当然、背後にも迫っていた敵に阻まれた。
source.english: Naturally, an enemy approaching from behind blocked him.

target.text: ───Naturally, his retreat was cut off by the enemies closing in from behind.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
『ってなコト言ってますが、シサムさん？』
source.english: ‘So he says. Your thoughts, Ms. Sisam?’

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『そんな悠長なこと抜かしてると、たちまちケツからざっくりやられますねキサラさん』
source.english: ‘If he persists in such leisurely talk, he'll get his ass sliced open in no time, Ms. Kisara.’

source.japanese: 朔屋の窮地をしごく的確に、そして全く他人事に実況する双子は操舵室の中、白兵戦を隔てているのが叩けば破れる安硝子一枚なのにも関わらず、二人は別次元に身を置いているかに実に闊達に観戦の、笑顔がなんと素敵に朗らかで。
source.english: Inside the wheelhouse, the twins offered an extremely accurate account of Sakuya's predicament as though it were wholly someone else's problem. Only a cheap pane of glass, breakable with a tap, separated them from the fighting, yet they watched as freely as though in another dimension, their smiles so wonderfully sunny.

target.text: 【Kisara】 『And that's what he's going with, Shisamu-san. A comment?』
【Shisamu】 『If he keeps mouthing off like that, they'll actually tear him a new asshole in a heartbeat, Kisara-san.』

The twins were inside the wheelhouse, and as if it didn't concern them in the slightest, were reporting live on Sakuya's predicament with the utmost accuracy, and despite the fact they were only separated from combat by a single cheap pane of glass that was easily breakable, the two were watching the spectacle with remarkably cheerful enthusiasm, as if they were doing it from a different dimension, and with wonderfully sunny smiles at that.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やめてやめてやめて、ほらホールダップ、降参、あーゆーおーけー？」
source.english: “Stop, stop, stop! Look, hands up! I surrender! Are you okay?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「STOP STOP STOP, come on, hold up, I surrender, AA-YOO-OH-KAY?」

source.japanese: だが如何に朗らかな笑顔で見守られていようと朔屋にはなんの救いにもならず、青年は両手を挙げて、突きつけられた切っ先から後退るも、背後でじゃかじゃかと鍔鳴りの剣呑な響き、何時か船に攻めこまれた時といい、たやすく挟み撃ちを許してしまう迂闊さは、全く改善せられていない。
source.english: However sunny the smiles watching over him, they did Sakuya no good. Hands raised, he backed away from a leveled blade, only to hear the sinister clatter of sword guards behind him. Just as when the ship had been attacked before, his carelessness let the enemy catch him from both sides. No improvement whatsoever.

target.text: But no matter how warm and radiant their smiles may have been as they watched over him, it amounted to no salvation for Sakuya, and though the young man lifted both hands high in the air as he retreated from the tip of the sword pointed his way, behind him came the menacing rattling of sword guards, and just like that other time the ship had been boarded, his careless tendency to allow himself to easily be caught in a pincer attack had not been rectified in the slightest.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
『それで見逃してくれる相手なら、そもそも信天翁号に喧嘩売ってくるはずもないですよね、シサムさん』
source.english: ‘Anyone who'd let him go at that would never have picked a fight with the Albatross in the first place, would they, Ms. Sisam?’

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『ですねーキサラさん。朔屋君はいい加減自分のいる船のことを、学ぶべきでしょーねー』
source.english: ‘Quite so, Ms. Kisara. Mr. Sakuya really ought to learn what sort of ship he's aboard.’

target.text: 【Kisara】 『If they were the sort willing to let him go that easily, they wouldn't have picked a fight with the Albatross in the first place, right, Shisamu-san?』
【Shisamu】 『Riiight, Kisara-san. It really is about time Sakuya-kun starts learning a little about the ship he's on, riiight?』

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょ、待っ、なんだってこっちゃデッキブラシ一本なのに、そっちはピストルまで持ってんの。ずるいじゃないのそんな、あ、あ、待ってよして撃たないでーっ」
source.english: “W-wait! I've got one deck brush and you've even got pistols? That's cheating! Ah, ah, wait, stop, don't shoot!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Hol-, wait, how come you guys get to have pistols when all I have is this lousy deck brush? Don't you think that's unfair, ah, ah, wait, cease, don't shootー!」

source.japanese: 頬を灼き腕と脇腹の隙間を抜けていく弾丸の、どちらの向きから発射されているのか判らないほど周章狼狽、悲鳴で逃げ惑うばかりでは、躱そうにも身を隠そうにも安全な退路など見つけられるはずもなく───
source.english: A bullet seared his cheek and passed through the gap between arm and flank. His panic was so complete that he could not even tell which direction it had come from. Merely shrieking and running, he had no hope of dodging, finding cover, or discovering any safe avenue of retreat—

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『……ねえキサラさん、朔屋君は腕っ節だけでなく、頭も弱いみたいですねー』
source.english: ‘…Ms. Kisara, it seems Mr. Sakuya is as feeble in the head as he is with his fists.’

target.text: He couldn't even tell which side the bullet that singed his cheek as it slipped through the gap between his arm and his side was fired from, so panicked and dismayed was he, but simply fleeing blindly while screaming would leave him no hope of spotting a safe line of retreat, whether he tried to physically dodge or take cover somewhere───
【Shisamu】 『……Hey, Kisara-san. Looks like Sakuya's not just soft in the arms, he's soft in the head too, riiight?』

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
『おやシサムさんもそう思いますか。全く同感です。なんで幽霊が、ヤッパや拳銃なんぞで武装してるの、不思議に思わないんですかねえ』
source.english: ‘You think so too, Ms. Sisam? I entirely agree. Doesn't he find it strange that ghosts are armed with knives and pistols?’

target.text: 【Kisara】 『My, you think so too, Shisamu-san? Couldn't agree with you more. Really makes you wonder why ghosts would be armed with blades and handguns, doesn't it?』

source.japanese:
【直正】
「がっ、だっ、痛い、痛いよ本気で！
　あがが、これ、奥歯とか、
　イっちゃってるって！」
source.english:
“Gah! Ow! That really hurts!
Agh, my molars—I think my molars are gone!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Gah, ow, ow, that really hurts! Arghh, stop that, my molars are totally busted now!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
『朔屋君、ばかすかヤられてます。……さすがにそろそろ気づいてもいいんじゃないでしょうか、シサムさん？』
source.english: ‘Mr. Sakuya is taking quite a beating. Surely he might begin to notice by now, Ms. Sisam?’

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『あー本泣き入ってる入ってる……うーんどうでしょうか。キサラさん、ここまで来て判ってないってコトは、最後までそのまんま、って事もありうるかもしれません』
source.english: ‘Ah, now he's really crying. Really crying… Hm, I wonder. Ms. Kisara, if he still hasn't understood after all this, perhaps he won't understand to the very end.’

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やめてぇぇ、もうやめてあげてぇぇっ、
　落ちる、そんなされたら落ちる、
　海に落ちちゃうーーっ」
source.english:
“Stoooop! Stop it, please!
I'll fall!
Keep that up and I'll fall into the sea!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 『Sakuya-kun is getting pummeled left and right. ……It really is high time he noticed, don't you think so, Shisamu-san?』

【Shisamu】 『Ahh, he's actually started full-on crying now……hmm, I wonder. Kisara-san, given that he still hasn't realized, it might well be possible that he actually doesn't realize until the very end.』
【Naomasa】 「Stooop, please, just stooop, I'll fall, if you do that I'll fall, I'll fall into the oceanーー!」

source.japanese: 硝子越しでは声はしかとは聴き取れないが、とにかくシサム・キサラは加勢にも来てくれないばかりか何やら自分を小馬鹿にしている気配のあり、船の幅一杯を使って右に左に、長さを頼んで前に後ろに、バラックを当てにしてあちらにこちらに逃げたり隠れたり、朔屋はそれはそれは一生懸命に、ちょっと可愛い小町娘の家に夜這いに入ったのが露見してしまったばかりか、娘の兄が男色家で、仕置きにと朔屋の尻を狙って襲いかかってきたのから逃げ出した時と同じくらい、それはもう必死に逃げ惑う───
source.english: Though the glass kept him from making out their words, it was plain that Sisam and Kisara, far from coming to his aid, were somehow making a fool of him. Using the whole breadth of the ship to flee left and right, its length to flee fore and aft, and the shacks to dodge and hide hither and yon, Sakuya ran for all he was worth—as desperately, indeed, as on the night when he had slipped into a pretty girl's bedchamber, only to be discovered and pursued by her brother, a lover of men, who came after him with punitive designs upon his backside. With just that degree of desperation did he flee every which way—

target.text: He couldn't clearly make out their voices through the glass, but at any rate, not only did it feel like Shisamu and Kisara were not coming to assist him, they even seemed to be mocking him in some way, and using the full beam of the ship to weave left and right, relying on her full length to dash back and forth, and ducking behind the shacks to flee and hide at every turn, my goodness, Sakuya was running for his life just as frantically as that one time when he not only was caught red-handed sneaking into the local belle's house for a night-time visit, her older brother also turned out to be a homosexual, and as punishment, he leapt at Sakuya's rear end, and so he had fled from there in a panic.
By now he was just desperately scrambling to escape───

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『うーん、彼はこのまま叩き落とされちゃった方が、いいような気もしてきましたよ、キサラさん。そうすれば撃たれたり刺されたりからは、逃げられるでしょうし』
source.english: ‘Hm. Ms. Kisara, I'm beginning to think he might be better off knocked overboard. That ought to save him from the shooting and stabbing.’

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
『しかしですねシサムさん、多分朔屋君は、そんなコトも考えつかんでしょうし、彼のことだから墜ちたら墜ちたで、スクリュウに巻きこまれてズタボロになるのがオチかと』
source.english: ‘But, Ms. Sisam, that probably wouldn't occur to Mr. Sakuya. And knowing him, if he did fall, I suspect he'd only get caught in the propeller and torn to shreds.’

target.text: 【Shisamu】 『Hmm, you know, I'm starting to feel like it might have been for the best if he just got knocked off the ship there, Kisara-san. That way, he might avoid getting shot or stabbed.』

【Kisara】 『But you see, Shisamu-san, Sakuya probably wouldn't even think so far ahead, and knowing him, if he does end up falling, the only fate that awaits him is being sucked into the propeller and ripped to shreds, probably.』

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あのなああんたら……なんの未練があるのか知りませんが、こっちゃこんだけ頭下げてるじゃないですか。なのにボコボコパンパンと。ずるいでしょうがそんなの」
source.english: “…Listen, you lot… I don't know what lingering regrets you've got, but I'm bowing and scraping as hard as I can. And you just keep thumping and firing. That's not fair.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「生身の人間は、幽霊様には触ることもできんのですよ？　なのにあんたらと来たら、遠慮も容赦もなく殴るわ蹴るわ刺すわ撃ってくるわ……。
　…………ん？　んんん？」
source.english:
“A living person can't even touch a ghost, you know? Yet you keep punching, kicking, stabbing, shooting without a shred of mercy…
Hm? Hmmm?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Just listen to me, you guys…… I don't know what kind of lingering regrets you still hold, but, look, I've been bowing my head and apologizing this much already, right? And yet you're still beating me black and blue. That's not fair, is it?」

【Naomasa】 「Us humble men of flesh and blood can't even touch noble ghosts such as yourselves, you know? But then when it comes to you guys, you show neither restraint nor mercy and just punch and kick and stab and shoot and……. …………Hm? Hmmm?」

source.japanese: 亡霊達は朔屋のあまりに懸命に逃げ回る様に嗜虐的な喜び見出したのか、一思いに仕留める事はせず、カトラスの柄やら拳銃の銃把やらでゴンゴンこんこんと四方からいたぶり始める始末、朔屋君は反撃もままならず、亀の姿勢に丸まって降り注ぐ殴打に不平たらたら耐えていたのだが───
source.english: Perhaps the ghosts had found a sadistic pleasure in his frantic flight: rather than finish him in one stroke, they began tormenting him from all sides with cutlass hilts and pistol butts. Thump, thump, tap, tap. Unable even to strike back, Sakuya curled like a turtle and endured the blows raining down, complaining all the while. But—

target.text: Perhaps these spectres had discovered some sadistic delight in the way Sakuya so strenuously ran for his life, for they did not instantly shoot him dead; instead, they had begun to torment him from all sides with repeated thuds and knocks using the hilts of their cutlasses and grips of their pistols, a sorry state of affairs, and Sakuya was unable to launch any counteroffensive, merely curling up like a turtle, complaining and whining incessantly as he endured the rain of blows, but───

source.japanese: ようやく彼も、亡霊達の異常な点に気づいたらしい。
source.english: At last he seemed to notice something strange about these ghosts.

target.text: At long last, it seemed that he, too, had noticed what was so unusual about these ghosts.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『おや？　朔屋君の様子が……？』
source.english: ‘Oh? A change in Mr. Sakuya's demeanor…?’

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
『あれ？　これはどうやらさすがに……？』
source.english: ‘Hm? Could he at last…?’

target.text: 【Shisamu】 『Oh my? Sakuya's looking a little……?』
【Kisara】 『Oh? Surely by now he has to……?』

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そういや、幽霊に取り殺されたって話は聞いても、殴り殺されたり、まして撃ち殺されたりって聞かないよなあ……」
source.english: “Come to think of it, you hear of ghosts haunting people to death. Never beating them to death. Let alone shooting…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あのー……あんたらもしかして、
　生身の……？
　おい。おい、そこの右端から三人目。
　あんた今、ヅラがずれたの……。
　直さなかったか？」
source.english:
“Uh… Are you perhaps… flesh and blood?
Hey.
You, third from the right.
Didn't you just…
straighten your wig after it slipped?”

source.japanese:
朔屋、始めは失禁せんばかりに震え上がって甲板を右往左往して海に転落しかけたりもするのだが、本当に幽霊なら、恐怖以外の脅威はない、筈。
　なのに相手は平気で物理的攻撃を仕掛けてくるでないか。そして今の朔屋の指摘に慌てた振るまい。
source.english:
Sakuya had begun so frightened he nearly wet himself, scrambling about the deck and almost falling into the sea—but real ghosts ought to pose no threat beyond fear.
Yet these ghosts attacked him physically without hesitation. And now his remark had made them flustered.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Thinking about it, while I've heard of people haunted to death by ghosts, I've never really heard of anybody punched to death, to say nothing of being shot to death by one……」
【Naomasa】 「Uhmm, soo……could you fellows possibly actually be made of flesh and blood……? Oi. Oi, you there, third from the right. Hey, your mask just slipped……. You gonna leave it like that?」

At first, Sakuya had been shaking while on the verge of pissing himself, running every which way on the deck, even about to fall into the ocean, but if these truly were ghosts, they could not pose any threat to him outside of terror, or so it should be. Yet despite that, were these enemies not launching physical attacks against him without any scruples? And then there was their flustered reaction to Sakuya's pointed comments just now.

source.japanese:
……偽装だったのだ。
　海賊たちの。
　亡霊に扮した。
source.english:
…A disguise.
Pirates.
Dressed as ghosts.

source.japanese: ようやくにして、そして偶然にそれに気づき、日頃虐げられていたいじめられっ子が、逆上するようにそら、朔屋の反撃が開始される───！
source.english: At last, by chance, he understood. Like a bullied child who had suffered daily and finally snapped, Sakuya began to fight back!

target.text: ……It was a disguise. Worn by pirates. Who dressed up as ghosts.
At long last he realized, and by sheer coincidence at that, but now, like a bullied child who had been pushed too far snapping and flying into a rage, behold, Sakuya's counterattack commenced───!

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おのれら……。
　よくも人のことを脅かしてくれた。
　海賊なら海賊らしく襲ってこいよぉっ。
　相手が人間だって判りゃ、
　話は別だぁーーっ」
source.english:
“You bastards…
How dare you scare me!
If you're pirates, attack like pirates!
If you're human,
that's another matter!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「You sons of……. How dare you scare others like that? If you're pirates, then attack me like you're damn pirates. Now that I know I'm dealing with humans, it's a whole different storyーー!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「お。やっと反撃、
　始まりましたねキサラさん」
source.english:
“Oh. At last,
a counterattack, Ms. Kisara.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんかもう、既にぼろぼろですけどねシサムさん……ってシサム、そろそろこの話し方、やめない？」
source.english: “Though he's already rather battered, Ms. Sisam… Hey, Sisam. Can we stop talking like this now?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「んー、わりと楽しかったけど、ここらへんにしとくか。
　それ朔屋、こっから反撃の狼煙だぁ！」
source.english:
“Mm. It was pretty fun, but let's leave it there.
Go on, Sakuya! That's the signal—counterattack!”

source.japanese: 朔屋は今まで担がれていた悔しさから、普段にはない勇猛さで相手に飛びかかっていったものの。
source.english: Bitter at having been fooled all this time, Sakuya leaped at them with unusual bravery. But—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ooh. At last, his counterattack has begun, Kisara-san.」
【Kisara】 「It kind of feels like it's already in shambles though, Shisamu-san…… hey, Shisamu, can we stop talking like this already?」
【Shisamu】 「Hmm, it's been relatively fun, but let's wrap it up here then. Here we go, Sakuya, that's the signal for our counterattack to begin!」
The bitter frustration that Sakuya had been carrying on his shoulders until now made him leap at his opponents with a valiance usually unthinkable of him, but.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「っで！　なんだよ、やっぱり痛いんだよ！
　くそう、あんたら非道いだろよってたかって」
source.english:
“Ow! What the hell? It still hurts!
Damn it, you're cruel, all ganging up like that!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「OW! What the hell, that actually really hurts! Shit, ganging up on me like this is just cruel!」

source.japanese: 大上段にデッキブラシを振りかぶって掛かっても、構えも何もない子供の拳と同じでたやすく弾かれる。
source.english: He raised the deck brush high and charged, but his attack had neither stance nor form. It was knocked aside as easily as a child's punch.

target.text: For all that he held his deck brush high above his head like a kendo sword and swung down, it was repelled as easily as the fists of a child thrown with neither stance nor skill.

source.japanese: いとも簡単にカウンターを喰らい───
source.english: A counterblow caught him with perfect ease.

target.text: And he was countered with the greatest of ease───

source.japanese: 基本的戦闘能力という物が皆無の朔屋はあっさり迎撃され───それでも今日は怒りの方が勝るのか、めげずに撃ちかかっていっては───
source.english: Lacking the most basic fighting ability, Sakuya was beaten back at once. Yet perhaps today his anger was stronger. Undaunted, he charged and swung again—

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「さっくやはセイラー、のろまなセイラ～、
　さっくやが怒れば、ブラシが飛ぶぜ～」
source.english:
“Sakuya's a sailor, a slowpoke sailor!
When Sakuya gets mad, watch his brush go sailing!”

target.text: Completely lacking in anything that could be called basic combat ability, Sakuya was readily intercepted and repelled───but even so, perhaps fury prevailed today, for he kept on attacking without letting it discourage him───
【Shisamu】 「Sakuya's a sailor, a numskull of a sailor～, if he gets his blood in a boil, his brush it goes a-flying～」

source.japanese:
シサム───
　
　キサラ───
source.english:
Sisam—
Kisara—

source.japanese: 無頼船信天翁号の一等航海士。
source.english: Chief mates of the outlaw ship Albatross.

source.japanese:
北方の出だとはいうが、その血の起源は那辺にあるかは定かではなく。
　それでも沿岸を荒らし回った金髪碧眼の蛮族達の豪毅と放埒と快楽を愛する心を受け継いでいるのは間違いなく。
source.english:
They were said to come from the north, though the ultimate origin of their blood was uncertain.
Even so, they had undoubtedly inherited the boldness, wild abandon, and love of pleasure of the blond, blue-eyed barbarians who once ravaged the coasts.

source.japanese: その感覚のときめきは、文明社会の小賢しい倫理や規範とは無関係、血の輝きと酒の酔いと性の喜びとをただ愛して。
source.english: Their senses thrilled beyond the petty ethics and rules of civilized society. They loved simply the glitter of blood, the intoxication of liquor, and the pleasures of the flesh.

source.japanese: 今はセックスに耽[ふけ]っているわけではないが、肌の火照りは根を同じくし、鉄火場の騒乱に血は滾[たぎ]り、となれば後は、歌だ、躍りだ！
source.english: They were not indulging in sex now, but the heat of their skin sprang from the same root; the riot of combat set their blood boiling. And then—song! Dancing!

target.text: Shisamu─── Kisara───
First mates of the rogue ship, the Albatross.

Thought they were said to hail from the north, the roots of their lineage were yet veiled in mystery. Nevertheless, there was no mistaking that they had inherited the fortitude, willfulness, and love for life's pleasures of the blonde, blue-eyed barbarians who once raided the coasts.

That heart-stirring thrill of sensation shared no relation with the sanctimonious ethics and norms of civilized society; it simply loved to revel in the brilliance of blood, the intoxication of drink, and the pleasures of the flesh.

And while they weren't indulging in sex right now, the flush of their skin shared the same root; the chaos of the battlefield made their blood seethe with excitement, and so what had to come next was song, dance!

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こん棒代わりに、ブラシで叩きゃ～、
　なぜだか朔屋がぁ、吹っ飛ぶぜぇ～」
source.english:
“Swing that brush like a club, let it fly—
And it's Sakuya who goes sailing sky-high!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「In place of a cudgel, he beats 'em with a brush～ but why then is it that Sakuya, himself is sent a-flying～」

source.japanese: 腕を振り上げればぶるんと乳房が跳ねる、足踏み鳴らせばスカートの裾[すそ]がチアガールはだしに舞い翻[ひるがえ]る、双子が踏むステップは軽やかにリズミカルに、時に騒がしく、縦横無尽に空間を広げ広大な原野と見せ、あるいは丸盆の用に縮めては見る者の目を釘付けにする。
source.english: Their breasts bounced with every raised arm, their skirt hems whirled with every stamping foot, putting a cheerleader to shame. Lightly, rhythmically, sometimes noisily, the twins' steps ranged freely, seeming to expand the space into a vast plain, then shrink it to the size of a round tray; every watching eye was held fast.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そこだ！　ジャブだ！　ほら右パンチ！」
source.english: “There! Jab! Come on, right punch!”

target.text: When they lifted their arms, their breasts bounced up and down, and with every stomp, the hem of their skirts fluttered and twirled with energy that could put cheerleaders to shame; the steps the twins tread were light, rhythmic, and at times boisterous, bending space at will, stretching it into a vast, sweeping wilderness one moment, then folding it down to the size of a small tray the next, riveting the eyes of all who saw them.
【Kisara】 「Right there! Jab! Come on, throw a right hook!」

source.japanese: そら、キサラが拳固めて抉[えぐ]るように振り抜く、見事な突きはただ宙を打っただけなのに、拍子を合わせて朔屋が吹っ飛ぶ。
source.english: Kisara clenched her fist and drove it in a fine, gouging punch. She hit only empty air. In perfect time, Sakuya went flying.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「おっと左アッパー、ちっくしょう～、
　やりやがったな！」
source.english:
“Whoa, left uppercut!
Damn it—you bastard!”

target.text: There! Kisara clenched her fist and drove it through like she was carving through the air, and though her magnificent thrust only struck emptiness, with perfect timing, Sakuya was sent flying back.
【Shisamu】 「Watch out, a left uppercut, darn～, that bastard got you good!」

source.japanese: そら、シサムが体軸を右に左に揺らして牽制しながら、天にまで届かん勢いで拳を衝[つ]き上げる、これも虚空に風を巻いただけなのに、機を同じくして朔屋が弾け飛ぶ。
source.english: Sisam swayed from side to side, feinting, then drove her fist upward as though to reach the heavens. Again, it merely stirred the empty air, yet at that very instant Sakuya went flying.

target.text: Behold! While swaying her core right to left in a feint, Shisamu launched her fist skyward as if to reach the very heavens, and though this, too, was merely a gust spun into the void, at the very same moment, Sakuya was hurled away.

source.japanese: ───やられているのは、朔屋ばかりなり。
source.english: Only Sakuya was getting hit.

target.text: ───It was Sakuya, and Sakuya alone, who took the blows.

source.japanese:
さんざんに殴られ打ち倒されて、足もふらついてくるけれど、もう背後は舷側、逃げ場もなくて、やけくそでデッキブラシを振り上げては撃ちかかろうとして、足下を滑らせる。
　ところがそれが奏効した。
source.english:
Beaten and knocked down so often his legs began to wobble, he found the rail at his back, with no escape; desperately he raised the deck brush to strike again—and slipped.
But this worked.

target.text: Having been miserably beaten and knocked down, his legs were shaking and unsteady, but his back was already against the bulwark; he had nowhere left to run, and just as he swung his deck brush high and made one last desperate assault, he slipped. That, however, was what did the trick.

source.japanese: 予想外の打撃が偶然相手の顎を直撃し、急所を撃ち抜かれた海賊あっさり昏倒の、意外に脆い。
source.english: The unexpected blow struck his opponent's jaw by chance. Hit squarely in that vulnerable spot, the pirate collapsed unconscious. Surprisingly fragile.

target.text: The unexpected blow happened to hit his opponent directly on the chin by pure chance, and the pirate, struck right in a vital spot, quickly fainted, proving surprisingly frail.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「倍にして返すぜ、フックだボディだ、
　ボディだチンだ！」
source.english:
“Pay 'em back double! Hook!
Body! Body! Chin!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Repay him double what you got, hook, body, body, chin!」

source.japanese: キサラの声もすぐ後ろに聞こえた気がして、当てにならない仲間でも、加勢とあればやはり心強い。朔屋は一瞬勢いづいたけれど、やっぱり喧嘩慣れしていない、後が続かない。仲間が一人やられたことに激昂した海賊は、二人三人と一斉に朔屋に拳銃を向けて───
source.english: Kisara's voice seemed to come from just behind him; unreliable comrades or not, the prospect of help was heartening, and for a moment Sakuya rallied. But he was no experienced fighter, and he could not follow through. Enraged at their fellow's defeat, two or three pirates leveled pistols at him together.

target.text: He felt like he could hear Kisara's voice coming from right behind him, and even though they were not comrades to be counted upon, just having any reinforcements really was reassuring after all. Sakuya was invigorated for an instant, but in the end, he really wasn't used to fighting, and he couldn't keep it up. Enraged that one of their comrades had fallen, a few more pirates pointed their guns at Sakuya all at once───

source.japanese: 引き金が落ちる寸前で、海賊たちはまとめて棒のようにぶっ倒れる。背後からの一撃で。
source.english: Just before the triggers could be pulled, the pirates all toppled like sticks. A blow from behind.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「えーい面倒だ、
　この辺でノックアウトだいっ」
source.english:
“Ah,
enough of this! Time for a knockout!”

target.text: And just before they could pull the trigger, the pirates dropped like logs one and all. Felled by a blow from behind.
【Shisamu】 「Ugh, to hell with this hassle, I'm knocking you out cold here!」

source.japanese: シサム・キサラ以下下級水夫達、それに水夫長、智里も、それぞれの得物を振り抜いた形で、海賊たちを叩きのめしていたのだった。
source.english: Sisam and Kisara, the junior sailors, the boatswain, and Tomosato all stood with their chosen weapons at the end of a swing. Together they had knocked the pirates flat.

target.text: Shisamu and Kisara, followed by the deck boys, as well as the Bosun, and Tomosato too, were all left standing in the follow-through of a clean swing of their respective weapons, having soundly knocked the pirates flat on the deck.

source.japanese: ようやく切り抜けたと、安心したらもう後が続かない、がくついてしまった膝を支えきれず、がくりと腰を落とした甲板が、滑っているのはただの潮の垢か血脂か、見るのも厭[いと]わしく、双子に吐いたが恨み言、真っ平御免の鉄火場を、まがりなりにも戦い抜いた今日くらいは、これくらいは許されよう。
source.english: Once he knew they had escaped, relief took him and there was nothing left in him. Unable to support his buckling knees, he sank heavily onto the deck—which was slick with what, mere salt scum, or blood and grease? The very sight was loathsome. As for the litany of grievances he poured upon the twins: on this day, at least, when he had somehow fought his way through a pitched battle he wanted no part of, surely he might be allowed that much.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「シサム～、キサラ～、なぁ、あんたら、操舵室にいたんじゃないのかよう」
source.english: “Sisam… Kisara… Weren't you two in the wheelhouse?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだって出てきてドンパチやってるんだ。
　出てくるんなら、最初からやってくれ……。
　見れ、俺もうこんなにぼろぼろよ……？」
source.english:
“Why'd you come out and start fighting?
If you were coming, you could've done it from the start…
Look. I'm already a wreck…”

target.text: Now that he felt the relief of finally having overcome it, he was completely spent, and with trembling knees that could no longer support his weight, he fell to the deck with a thud; was this slippery smear on the deck merely ocean scum or was it blood and fat? Just the thought of looking was repugnant enough to him, and the only words he could find for the twins were resentful complaints, but having somehow or other managed to fight his way through this scene of carnage, something that he had already had more than enough of for a lifetime, he could surely be allowed that much for today.
【Naomasa】 「Shisamu～, Kisara～, hey, you two, weren't you supposed to be in the wheelhouse?」
【Naomasa】 「Why the hell did you just show up and start blasting? If you're going to show up, could you please just do so from the start……. Just look at me, I'm beaten all black and blue, alright……?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「いやー、まあ、うん、朔屋の奮闘があったからこそ、だね」
source.english: “Ah, well, yes. Only thanks to your valiant efforts, Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そうそう。あんたが頑張ってくれたから、反撃の糸口が掴めたんだ、うんそうだ、そういうことに違いない」
source.english: “Exactly. You worked so hard we found an opening to strike back. Yes, that's it. Must be.”

source.japanese: 海賊たちの一隊が朔屋に構っていた間に、他の連中はもう撃退されており、幽霊船、に偽装した船も、さっさと敗走していくところ。
source.english: While one group of pirates had been occupied with Sakuya, the rest had already been driven off. The vessel disguised as a ghost ship was itself making a hasty retreat.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あいつら、この辺りで最近幅きかせだした連中らしいんだよね」
source.english: “Apparently they've been throwing their weight around here lately.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でも所詮はヘッポコピーよ。霧に迷った船しか襲わないんじゃさ」
source.english: “But they're two-bit nobodies. Only attack ships lost in the fog.”
