target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Weeeell, look, uhmm, it was all thanks to the fierce fight that you put up, Sakuya, right?」
【Kisara】 「Yeah, yeah. It's all thanks to your great efforts that we could find an opening to strike back, right, definitely, no doubt about it.」

While that gang of pirates were busy entertaining themselves with Sakuya, the rest of their crew had already been repelled, and the ghost ship, or the ship that had disguised itself as one, was also beating a hasty retreat.
【Shisamu】 「Seems like these are the guys who have been throwing their weight around here lately.」
【Kisara】 「But at the end of the day, they turned out to be nothing more than bumbling clowns. Only attacking ships that stray into the fog.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「しかもあんな愉快な仮装で脅しかけてからじゃないと、まともな出入りもできないってんだから」
source.english: “And can't even manage a proper fight without scaring people in those delightful costumes first.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもよ、磁石が狂ったのは本当じゃないか」
source.english: “But the compass really went wrong.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そりゃ狂うわな。この辺りの岩は磁性が強い溶岩質でな。まあここを航路に使う船乗りには、よく知られたことなんだが」
source.english: “Course it did. The rocks around here are strongly magnetic lava. Well known to any sailor who uses this route.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「朔屋には、
　ちょーっと判りづらかったかなぁ」
source.english:
“Maybe a little
hard for you to understand, Sakuya?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「判るか、そんなもの。
　……て事は始めっから……」
source.english:
“How was I supposed to know?
…So right from the start…”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あの偽幽霊どもが仕掛けてくるかどうかはしらなかったけど、ちょっと乗っからせてもらったってわけ」
source.english: “Didn't know whether those fake ghosts would attack. But we thought we'd play along a bit.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「いやー、朔屋がどんだけ頑張ってくれるか、
　見てみたかったんだよね」
source.english:
“We wanted to see how hard you'd try,
Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And what's more, unless they first give people a scare with those delightful costumes, they can't even put up a proper fight.」
【Naomasa】 「But still, you can't deny the compass went haywire, right?」
【Bosun】 「But of course it would. The rocks around here are volcanic and strongly magnetic, see. Well, that's no secret to the sailors who ply these waters.」
【Shisamu】 「Guess it might have been a teeensy bit difficult to comprehend for Sakuya.」
【Naomasa】 「And how would I even know something like that? ……So then, right from the start, you already……」
【Kisara】 「Didn't know for sure if those phony ghosts were actually going to pick a fight with us or not, but I figured I'd play along with it for a bit.」
【Shisamu】 「Weeell, honestly, I just wanted to see how hard you'd push yourself, Sakuya.」

source.japanese: 朔屋は脱力して、こらえきれず甲板に大の字に伸びてしまったという。もう双子のスカートの中を覗く気力すら残っていなかったと言うから、朔屋にしては本当に滅多にない奮戦だったには違いない。
source.english: All strength went out of Sakuya, and he could no longer help himself: he sprawled spread-eagled upon the deck, or so the story goes. And since the story further has it that he lacked even the strength to peer up the twins' skirts, there can be no doubt that, for Sakuya, this had been a truly exceptional feat of arms.

source.japanese: そんな朔屋の元にしゃがみこんで、双子は。
source.english: The twins crouched beside him.

target.text: Whatever strength remained drained from Sakuya's limbs, and unable to contain himself any longer, he splayed out on the deck, spread-eagle. He lacked even the energy to peek under the twins' skirts by now, so this had undoubtedly been a rare sort of valiant struggle on Sakuya's part.
And crouching down in front of him was the twins.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんにしたっても、やっつけたじゃない。
　……一人だけだけど」
source.english:
“Whatever else, you did beat them.
…Only one, but…”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「どうだった、ぶちのめしてやった感触は。
　……一人だけだけど」
source.english:
“How'd it feel, knocking a pirate flat?
…Only one, but…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーそうだとも。こんだけ叩きのめされても、俺にはたった一人相手にするのが関の山ですよ」
source.english: “Oh, yes. After getting beaten to a pulp myself, one of them's all I can handle.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でもゼロじゃない分だけ、
　遙かにましってものさ」
source.english:
“Still,
that's a hell of a lot better than zero.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「これからもその調子で頼むよ、朔屋」
source.english: “Keep it up, Sakuya.”

source.japanese: 双子は、朔屋になんとも晴れ晴れとした笑顔を向けたことである。
source.english: They gave him the most radiantly cheerful smiles.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Whatever the case, you beat them, didn't you? ……Though it was just one guy.」
【Shisamu】 「So how did it feel, giving them a real drubbing? ……Though it was just one guy.」
【Naomasa】 「Yeah, got me there. Even after getting beaten up this badly, the best I can hope to manage is taking down just a single guy.」
【Kisara】 「Still, just the fact it's not zero makes it way better in my book.」
【Shisamu】 「We're counting on you to keep that up, Sakuya」
The twins beamed at Sakuya with wonderfully radiant smiles.

source.japanese:
その日朔屋は、目覚めと共に誓っていた。正確には昨夜眠りに就く前の誓いを船窓から差しこむ朝日に向かって繰り返した。
　
　───もう当分、あの双子には近づくまい。
　どれだけ金髪が豪奢であろうと、どれだけ乳房が魅惑的であろうと、どれだけ臀が美事であろうと、どれだけ太腿がむっちむちのぱつんぱつんであろうと、あの双子に関わるとろくな事がない。
source.english:
That day, Sakuya swore an oath upon waking. More precisely, he repeated to the morning sun coming through the porthole the oath he had sworn before going to sleep.
For a while, he would keep away from those twins.
However luxurious their blond hair, however enticing their breasts, however magnificent their backsides, however plump and taut those thighs, nothing good came of getting involved with them.

source.japanese: その証拠に見よ、この体中全身至るところの青痣、かさ蓋、切り傷、火傷、先日の偽幽霊どもから負わされた傷だが、これだけ喰らっておいてよく致命傷には至らず済んだもの。切り傷などは相手の刃物の手入れが悪かったのが幸いしただけし、火傷は銃弾が掠めていった跡である。ほんの少しでもずれていたなら銃創になっていた筈だ。
source.english: For proof, behold his body. Bruises, scabs, cuts and burns everywhere. Wounds from the recent encounter with those counterfeit ghosts. Amazing that he had taken so much punishment without a fatal injury. The cuts had spared him only because the enemy's blades were poorly kept. The burns marked where bullets had grazed him. A little farther either way and they would have been bullet wounds.

source.japanese: だから朔屋は今後、少なくともこの怒りが収まるまではあの双子に近づくまいと誓った。誰に誓った？　自分に誓った！　迂闊に近づいたならば、きっと激情に任せて後先考えずに双子を強姦しようと襲いかかり、そしてまず間違いなく返り討ちされるだろう可哀相な自分に誓った。
source.english: And so he swore to keep away from the twins, at least until his anger subsided. Swore to whom? Himself! His poor self, who, should he venture too close, would surely attack the twins in a fit of rage and try to rape them, heedless of the consequences—and almost certainly get beaten down in return.

source.japanese:
だから今日は、上甲板のバラック群の一つにも引っこんで、なるべく双子と会わないようにして過ごすのだ。そのバラックというのは朔屋が先頃からこっそり築き上げた、この船の中でも彼だけの隠れ家である。酒をちょろまかし、食糧もかっぱらってきて、さらには先頃寄港した港で積み荷とこっそり交換したエロ本までも持ちこんである。男の隠れ家としては完璧である。
　サボりがばれて後で懲罰喰らおうとも、今日一日はその天国でのんびり過ごすのだ。
　朔屋がかく決意して、気分はうきうきと、足取りは下っ手くそなスキップで船室を出てみると、
source.english:
Today, then, he would hole up in one of the shacks on the upper deck and avoid them as much as possible. This particular shack was the private refuge he had lately, secretly established aboard. Stolen liquor, pilfered food, even dirty magazines secretly exchanged for cargo at their last port. A perfect man's hideaway.
Even if he was caught shirking and punished afterward, he would spend today at leisure in that paradise.
With this resolve, a buoyant heart and a thoroughly inept skip, Sakuya left his cabin.

target.text: That day, upon waking, Sakuya made a vow. To be precise, he faced the rays of the rising sun streaming through the porthole, then repeated the vow that he had sworn last night before falling asleep. ───For the foreseeable future, he would keep his distance from those twins. No matter how magnificent their golden locks, no matter how alluring their chests, no matter how spectacular their butts, no matter how plump and taut their thighs, nothing good would come from being involved with those twins.

And as proof, behold: look upon the bruises, scabs, cuts, burns, all the wounds he had suffered at the hands of those fake ghosts the other day now covering his body from head to toe; in fact, having received this many wounds, it was a miracle that he had avoided suffering anything fatal. The only reason the cuts weren't worse was because he was fortunate enough that his opponents had maintained their blades poorly, but the burns were the marks left by bullets grazing his skin. Had they been just ever so slightly shifted to the side, then they would surely have become gunshot wounds instead.

Therefore, Sakuya made a vow that, henceforth, at least until his anger had cooled off, he would keep his distance from those twins. Who did he make it to? Himself! Were he to carelessly approach them, he would surely be overcome by violent impulses and assault the twins in an ill-fated attempt to rape them without regard for the consequences, and then he would assuredly be struck down in retaliation; thus, he vowed to his pitiful self.

And that was why he would retire to one of the shacks on the upper deck today, spending the hours in a way that would give him the best chances of not having to meet the twins. This shack was one that Sakuya had built in secret recently, the one place on this entire ship that he could call a hideaway for him and him alone. He'd pilfered some booze, swiped some food as well, and on top of that, he'd even brought with him the porn magazine he'd secretly exchanged some of their cargo for at their latest port of call the other day. As a man's hideaway, it was perfection.

Though he would certainly be on the receiving end of some punishment if his slacking were to be discovered, he would spend the whole of today at leisure in this little paradise. Having made up his mind thus, just as he left his cabin with a buoyant mood and a clumsy skip in his step,

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……これ、なんぞね？」
source.english: “…What's this, then?”

source.japanese:
部屋の扉の前に落ちたる、一枚の布切れ。
　拾い上げてみればソックスの、多少くたびれてはいたが綺麗に洗ってあり、同じ色だがアルファベットが一文字縫い取りしてある。
　Ｓの字だった。この船の中でこの頭文字を抱く者と言えば───朔屋はきっぱりと、決然と、即座に、ポケットにしまいこんだ。
　辺りを警戒してしまったのは、なにか誤解されないかと恐れたからであるが、そうやって見回していると、通路の先にまた一枚の布切れが。
source.english:
A scrap of cloth lay before his door.
He picked it up. A sock, somewhat worn but freshly washed. A single letter was embroidered in thread of the same color. S.
And aboard this ship, a person with that initial—firmly, decisively, instantly, Sakuya put it in his pocket.
He looked cautiously around, afraid someone might misunderstand. In doing so he spotted another scrap farther down the passage.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……What, exactly, is this?」

A piece of cloth lay in front of the cabin door. When he tried picking it up, it turned out to be a pair of socks; while a little worse for the wear, they had been washed clean, and they were entirely monochrome except for a single letter of the alphabet embroidered on them. It was the letter S. And as for who on this ship that this initial could belong to───Sakuya resolutely, decisively, and immediately stuffed it in his pocket. Fearing that his actions here could invite some form of misunderstanding, he became wary of his surroundings, but as he looked around, there, at the end of the passage, was yet another piece of cloth.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……今度も、なんですよ？」
source.english: “…And what's this one, then?”

source.japanese: またソックスであったが、今度はＫの字の縫い取りがあった。この船の中でこの頭文字を抱く者と言えば。
source.english: Another sock. This one embroidered with a K. And aboard this ship, a person with that initial—

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Same thing again, right?」
It was yet another pair of socks, but this time, they were embroidered with the letter K. And as for who on this ship that this initial could belong to……

source.japanese: こんな風にして、船内通路から昇降段、上甲板までＳとＫが代わる代わるに、手袋、腕章、次はああ、ブラジャー、そしてなんとパンツと続き───
source.english: Thus, along the passages, up the stairs and onto the upper deck, S and K alternated. Gloves. Armbands. Next, ah, a bra. And then, would you believe, panties.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「な、なんで俺の隠れ家の前に、
　最後の一枚が」
source.english:
“W-why is the last one…
outside my hideaway?”

source.japanese:
朔屋の、誰も知らないはずの秘密の隠れ家の前に、最後となるはずのパンツの一枚が落ちていたのだった。
　蒐集家の性というものは恐ろしく、そして哀れなものである。罠と判っていても完遂の為には飛びこまずにはいられない。けれど、と朔屋は逡巡する。最後のパンツはＫのイニシァルが縫い取りされているはずだが、そこでもしやＲとかＴとか記されてあったら、朔屋はその忌まわしい事実の発覚に発狂するだろう。とＲ氏やＴ氏に対して大層失礼な葛藤を繰り返していると───
source.english:
The final pair of panties lay before the secret refuge that nobody should have known about.
A collector's nature is dreadful, and pitiful. Even knowing it for a trap, he cannot help plunging in to complete the set. Yet Sakuya hesitated. The last pair should have K embroidered upon it. What if it bore an R or a T? That loathsome discovery would drive him mad. While he struggled with thoughts most insulting to Mr. R and Mr. T—

target.text: Thus, in this manner, from the passageway to the ladder, all the way up to the upper deck, alternating between S and K, were gloves, armbands, and next, ahh, brassieres, and then, goodness, even panties, and then───
【Naomasa】 「Wh-, why is the final piece here, right in front of my hideaway?」

What should make for the final pair of panties was lying in front of Sakuya's secret hideaway, the place none other should know of. The soul of a collector is a thing to be feared and pitied both. Even though he knew it was a trap, he had to charge into it for the sake of completion. However, Sakuya thought, hesitating. This final pair of panties should be embroidered with the initial of K, but were they instead marked with something like an R or a T by any chance, then Sakuya would surely go mad with the discovery of so loathsome a truth. And while he continued to agonize over this internal conflict that really was extremely rude towards Mr. R and Mr. T───

source.japanese:
【声】
『さ、さ、さ～くや来い。
　こっちのアンヨはあぁまいよ～』
source.english:
‘Sa, sa, Sakuya, come!
Sweet feet over here!’

source.japanese: どこかで聞いた歌声と共に、バラックの戸口から、さて伸び出しましたのは一本の脚でございます。素足で、爪先まで綺麗に磨かれ、朝日に輝いて美しく、そしてむしゃぶりつきたくなるほど艶[なま]めかしく宙を掻[か]いていた。
source.english: With a somehow familiar song, a leg now extended from the shack's doorway, ladies and gentlemen. Bare, polished beautifully down to the toes, shining in the morning sun. It swept through the air with a sensuality that made him want to fasten his mouth upon it.

source.japanese:
【声】
『さ、さ、さ～くや来い。
　こっちのお尻もあぁまいよ～』
source.english:
‘Sa, sa, Sakuya, come!
The bottom here's sweet too!’

source.japanese:
脚が引っこんでいって次は、臀であった。どこかで見たようなスカートを履いてはいたが、相変わらず見えるか見えないかの絶妙な瀬戸際で裾[すそ]がひらひら揺れている。
　朔屋は葛藤し、迷い、懊悩し、それでも辛うじて踏みとどまり、鼻血を噴きかねない我慢でじりじりと下がろうとして、
source.english:
The leg withdrew. Next came a backside. It wore a skirt he seemed to recognize, the hem fluttering, as ever, at the exquisite boundary of seeing and not quite seeing.
Sakuya struggled, wavered, agonized. Somehow he held his ground. With a restraint that nearly gave him a nosebleed, he began inching backward.

source.japanese:
【声】
『なんか、なかなかノッてこないね？』
source.english: ‘He's not really taking the bait, is he?’

source.japanese:
【声】
『ちょっとパンチが足りないかな。
　シサム、おっぱいいっちゃえ』
source.english:
‘Maybe it needs a little more punch.
Sisam, go with the boobs.’

source.japanese:
【声】
『ええ？　でも……まあいいか。
　どうせやるんならさ……、
　脱いじゃうよあたしは』
source.english:
‘Huh? But… Well, all right.
If we're doing
this… I'm taking it off.’

source.japanese:
【声】
『お～、やる気だねシサム。
　そんならあたしも一緒にやるよ。
　二人なら効果も倍に───』
source.english:
‘Oh, keen, are you, Sisam?
Then I'll join you.
Two of us, twice the effect—’

source.japanese:
【声】
『よく言ったキサラ。
　じゃあ、せぇの、で───』
source.english:
‘Well said, Kisara.
On my count, then—’

source.japanese:
【声】
『せーの……』
source.english: ‘Ready, and…’

source.japanese:
朔屋はこの朝誓ったのだ。
　もう当分、あの双子には近づくまいと。
source.english:
That morning, Sakuya made a vow.
He wouldn’t go near those twins for quite some time.

source.japanese:
誓いなぞに縛られるかちんこちんの莫迦貝は、修身の教科書と結婚して床入りしてその
お年寄りを助けたり父母を敬ったりしている良い子の挿絵に腰を擦りつけていればいいのである。
　朔屋は猛然と甲板を蹴って、砲弾のようにバラック中に飛翔していった。しかも、空中で体勢を制御するという離れ業で手を伸ばし、途中落ちていたパンツを漏れなく回収して。
source.english:
Let himself be bound by some oath? Any hidebound, clam-brained fool who would do that could marry a moral-education textbook, take it to bed, and grind his hips against its illustrations of good little children helping old people and honoring their parents.
Sakuya launched himself savagely from the deck and flew into the shack like a cannonball. Better yet, with the acrobatic feat of controlling his posture in midair, he reached out and gathered up every last pair of panties lying along his path.

target.text: All it took to wash away all of Sakuya's animosity, resentment, and any other dregs from within his heart that had congealed somewhere in his throat was the burn of neat whisky sliding down it, and that long sigh of pure satisfaction felt less as though it escaped his lips and more as if the top of his head had popped open, his contentment bursting out like a whale's spout.

To someone like Sakuya, who, in his time spent here on the Albatross, had once experienced so desperate a thirst for alcohol that he had even resorted to getting drunk by downing a mixture of hair tonic and caramel, this was a truly exquisite drink, no different from the divine waters of a heaven-sent sacred spring, though why would these two be treating him to such fine drink?

This pure, unadulterated whisky, free of any cheap additives, actually tasted remarkably similar to the one Sakuya had kept carefully stashed away and saved as his special treat for today, the one he was looking forward to perhaps sparingly sipping neat, or perhaps lightly stirring with some plain soda and swigging, but this was no mere resemblance. source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「えっへっへ、あたしはこっちのシェリー開けちゃおう。アモンティリャードの二〇年モノ。あたしは冷えてなくってもいいや」
source.english: “Heh, heh. I'll open this sherry. Twenty-year-old amontillado. Don't mind if it isn't chilled.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「んお？　また気取った酒を……あれ？
　俺そんなの持ちこんでないよ？」
source.english:
“Hm? Another fancy drink… Wait.
I didn't bring that in.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「だってこれ、あたしらが持ってきたやつだもの。
　あんたもしかして、ここにある酒と食い物全部、自分が貯めたモノだって思ってた？」
source.english:
“Because we brought it.
Did you think every drink and every scrap of food here was from your hoard?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そーいや見覚えのないモノも……。
　なんで？」
source.english:
“Come to think of it, I don't recognize some
of this… Why?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Mmm-mm-mm-mm……gulpgulp. Haaah～, nothing hits the spot like a drink in the morning.」

He chugged straight from the bottle. Sakuya chugged a lot. Of alcohol. He drank like there was no tomorrow. If there were ever a Sakuya who could refrain from drinking when presented with beauties, booze, and a bite to go with it, it could only be a dead Sakuya.

Nay, even had he kicked the bucket, gone stiff as a board, once a drop of alcohol spilled unto his lips, he would doubtless grow soft and limp once more, like a corpse with its nostrils stuffed full with Kouya mercury. (TN: Kouya mercury, written "高野水銀", refers to the cinnabar and liquid mercury used as traditional embalming substances in ancient Japanese and Chinese burial practices to soften and preserve the corpse. Mount Kouya is the sacred headquarters of Shingon Esoteric Buddhism, and it was Japan's premier mining hub for cinnabar and liquid mercury.)

Anyway, Sakuya being who he was, though he may have been compelled to so graciously share all of his treasured hoard, he no longer held much of a grudge over it; that had all been washed away by the liquor.
【Kisara】 「Eh-heh-heh, guess I'll open up this sherry. A 20-year-old Amontillado. I don't mind that it isn't chilled.」
【Naomasa】 「Nwha? Another fancy-sounding drink……huh? Wait, but I didn't bring anything like that with me?」
【Shisamu】 「Well that's because this here is something we brought with us. Wait, did you maybe think that all the booze and food here was stuff you'd stashed away?」
【Naomasa】 「Now that you mention it, there's stuff I don't remember seeing……. But why?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんでもなにも。朔屋にたかるばっかが芸じゃないってね」
source.english: “Why not? Sponging off Sakuya isn't our only talent.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「だからこのシェリーもそこらのも全部、好きに食べちゃってよ。ほらこんなのどう、キプロス島の海胆の塩漬け」
source.english: “So help yourself to the sherry and everything else. How about this? Salted sea urchin from Cyprus.”

source.japanese:
揃って両腕を大きく開いて、惜しげもなく振る舞う笑顔と酒と肴と、その快活な振るまい、親しげな笑顔のなんとも素敵で、山頂にてかの聖者に世界を与えようとした悪魔の誘惑なんぞは、丁重にＮｏＴｈａｎｋｙｏｕで追い返しただろうが、これには抗[あらが]いがたい。
　時にどうしようもなく悪辣で、また阿婆擦れもいいところの双子だが、姐御肌の気っ風の良さも確かにあって、一度酒を共にすると決めて胸襟を開いた双子の背から、さっと清涼な風が吹き抜けるよう、身を任せるその心地好さ、恐らく朔屋が信天翁号に乗りこんでから、もっとも幸福な瞬間であったろう。
source.english:
They spread their arms wide: smiles, liquor, delicacies, all offered without stint. Their cheerful ease and affectionate smiles were irresistible. Sakuya might have dismissed with a polite No Thank You the devil who offered the saint the whole world from a mountaintop, but not this temptation.
The twins could be incorrigibly vicious, brazen hussies to the last, yet they also possessed the openhanded generosity of elder sisters. Once they had decided to drink with a man and opened their hearts to him, it felt as though a cool, clean wind swept out from behind them. To surrender himself to it was bliss. This was probably Sakuya's happiest moment since boarding the Albatross.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「What do you mean why? Just mooching off you wouldn't be very classy, Sakuya.」
【Shisamu】 「So this sherry, and all that stuff over there, feel free to eat and drink whatever your heart desires. Look, how about this, some salt-cured sea urchin from Cyprus.」

Both of them held their arms wide open, generously treating him to smiles, drink, and food, and how wonderful their cheerful demeanour and friendly grins were; he would have politely turned away the Devil himself, offering the very world to that saint upon the mountaintop, with a "no thank you", but this was beyond his ability to resist.

Though at times, these twins were irredeemably wicked, and at other times, the very image of shameless hussies, there was no denying they had a big-sisterly spirit and warmth to them, and once he had decided to share a drink with them and open his heart, it was as though a cool, refreshing breeze swept in past the twins' backs, leaving behind that sweet, easy comfort of simply surrendering himself to the present; it was, in all likelihood, the most blissful moment Sakuya had experienced since joining the crew of the Albatross.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「海胆とはまたオツな。下手な生より、塩利かせたやつのほうが甘いんだよな」
source.english: “Sea urchin. A fine choice. Properly salted, it's sweeter than mediocre fresh stuff.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなら俺は、お返しにポルフディオ・アネホと台湾産天然のカラスミだぁ」
source.english: “Then I'll answer with Porfidio Añejo and Taiwanese bottarga from wild-caught fish!”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「テキーラとカラスミときたか……こっちゃイイ感じに塩が抜けるね」
source.english: “Tequila and bottarga, eh… That'll wash the salt down nicely.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「じゃあ魚揃いで、蒸しホウボウにライムを搾[しぼ]ろう。日本酒もあるよ、貴醸酒だからちょっと甘いか」
source.english: “Keeping it fishy, let's squeeze lime over steamed gurnard. There's sake too. It's kijoshu, so maybe a little sweet.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いい、いい、ポン酒は辛口に尽きるとか抜かす了見の狭い奴は塩でも舐めてろ、甘いのだって大好きだごくごくごく」
source.english: “Fine, fine. Narrow-minded fools who say sake has to be dry can lick salt. Love the sweet stuff too, glug, glug, glug.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でもシェリーと味醂は似てるよね。
　よく言われることだけど」
source.english:
“Still, sherry and mirin taste alike.
People often say so.”

source.japanese:
この日朔屋達が持ち寄った肴は、船暮らしのせいでかほとんどが瓶詰め缶詰めのモノばかり、それでもその種類の豊富なこと、保存食なりの利点を生かして風味にしたもの、料亭やビストロの出来たてとは異なる質ながら美味佳肴ばかりで。
　朔屋もシサムもキサラもよく大いに喰らいかつ呑んだ。
source.english:
Perhaps because of life at sea, nearly everything they had brought that day was bottled or canned. Yet what variety! Foods that turned the very fact of preservation into flavor: a different pleasure from dishes fresh out of a fine Japanese kitchen or a bistro, but every one a delicacy.
Sakuya, Sisam and Kisara ate heartily and drank mightily.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しかし───俺は絶対またなんかの罠かと思ったんだよな、正直なところ。
　だってあんた達、いつも色仕掛けで俺を釣るし」
source.english:
“Still… Honestly, I was sure it was another trap.
You're always using your charms to reel me in.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Sea urchin, now that is a tasteful choice. You know, salt-cured sea urchin actually ends up tasting sweeter than mediocre fresh stuff.」

【Naomasa】 「In that case, I'll return the favor with Porfidio Anejo and some wild-caught karasumi from Taiwan!」 (TN: Karasumi is salted, sun-dried mullet roe, traditionally made in Nagasaki in Japan. It's also made in Taiwan, and it is very similar to bottarga from Italy.)
【Kisara】 「Tequila and karasumi, huh…… that'll mellow out the saltiness just right.」

【Shisamu】 「Then to round out our ensemble of fish, let's squeeze some lime on this steamed gurnard. There's Japanese sake too, but it's kijoushu, so maybe it'll be a bit too sweet?」 (TN: Kijoushu, written "貴醸酒", is a sweet, full-bodied sake that is made by replacing some or all of the brewing water with already finished sake. It's also sometimes known as luxury sake in the West.)
【Naomasa】 「It's fine, it's fine, anybody narrow-minded enough to say something like "sake's only good when it's dry" can go lick salt, 'cause I love it sweet too *glugglugglug*」
【Kisara】 「Still, sherry and mirin taste pretty similar, right? People say that all the time, at least.」

The drinking snacks that Sakuya and company had brought with them today were, as a consequence of living on a ship, almost exclusively canned or bottled, but even so, with the abundant variety and flavours that capitalized on the qualities of preserved food, though the inherent quality was different compared to what would be served freshly prepared in a high-end, traditional Japanese restaurant or a bistro, they were all epicurean dishes. Sakuya, Shisamu, and Kisara all feasted and drank with hearty abandon.
【Naomasa】 「But really───I thought for sure this was going to be some kind of trap again, to tell the truth. I mean, you two are always luring me in with your feminine wiles.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あっはっは、なら色仕掛けもない不意打ち闇討ちの方がいい？」
source.english: “Ha, ha, ha. Would you prefer an ambush in the dark with no charms involved?”

source.japanese: とかなんとか、ちらちら太腿を見せながら。
source.english: She said it with little flashes of thigh.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやそんなの御免蒙[こうむ]る。見れるだけでもいい。見るだけでなくって、触れたり舐めたりできればもっと幸せだ。ヤれたりできたら愚息も昇天」
source.english: “No, thank you. Looking's enough. Better still if I could touch and lick instead of just looking. And if we did it, my little lad would ascend to heaven.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そのネタはもういいっての。
　でもホント、判りやすいよね朔屋って。
　下半身に正直すぎる」
source.english:
“Enough of that joke.
But you really are easy to read, Sakuya. Far too honest about everything below the waist.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おうとも、硬派とクールを気取って、そんで女の方からあんよ開いてくれる様な美形じゃないってことなんて、俺判ってるもんちゃんと」
source.english: “Of course. I know perfectly well I'm not handsome enough to play tough and cool and have women open their legs for me.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それにだって、楽しいもん、女の子と遊んでると。それを考えると、罠だ仕掛けだって見えても、つい行っちゃうもん。アハハははは、信じた俺が莫迦でしたーぁぁ、ああん」
source.english: “And it's fun, playing with women. Thinking of that, even if I can see a trap, a setup, I go anyway. Ahahahahaha! I was a fool to believe yooou… Ahhh.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ah-hah-hah, then would you prefer if we skipped the seduction and just went for surprise attacks and ambushes?」
She said something or other to that effect, all while flashing her thighs.

【Naomasa】 「No, I'll have to respectfully decline. Just being able to see it is enough. But if instead of just watching, if I could touch or lick you instead, I'd be much happier. And if I could pull off fucking you, my junior would ascend to the heavens.」
【Kisara】 「I told you, enough talking about that kind of stuff. But seriously, you're such an open book, Sakuya. Way too driven by your dick.」

【Naomasa】 「Damn right I am. Say I pretended to be all strait-laced and cool, then my face is nowhere near handsome enough to get the women to want to spread their legs for me, I know that painfully well.」

【Naomasa】 「And also, it's just fun, fooling around with women. And when I think of that, even when I know it's a trap, I just can't help walking right into it. Ahahahaha, I was just a damn idiot for falling for it, aah, aaaargh.」

source.japanese:
卵黄で練り合わせた小海老の擂り身をクラッカーで挟んだ奴をばりばり咬みながら、朔屋は右の眉と目を笑いの三日月にして、左に泣きの涙を滲ませる、一人福笑いという、無駄に小器用な真似をこなして、食って笑って泣いてと忙しい。
　その上言っている事も、こうあけすけに過ぎては気取らず飾らずの粋[いき]に通ずるどころか、莫迦を晒す恥を知らないというだけだこれでは。こらえかねたか、胡座から股割りの前にのめって、すまん寝の様[ざま]、俯けた顔の下から漏れ出すのは嘆きか笑いか、声がくぐもり混ざって聞き苦しい。
source.english:
Crunching crackers filled with shrimp paste kneaded with egg yolk, Sakuya shaped his right eye and eyebrow into crescents of laughter while tears welled on the left—a one-man funny-face puzzle, a pointless little feat of dexterity, busy eating, laughing, crying.
With candor this naked, there was no question of unpretentious charm: only a fool too shameless to know he was making a spectacle of himself. Unable to bear it, perhaps, he pitched forward from his cross-legged seat, legs splayed wide, like a cat sleeping with its face pressed down; laughter or lament escaped from beneath that lowered face, muffled together into an unpleasant sound.

target.text: While crunching down on some shrimp surimi kneaded in egg yolk stuffed between two crackers, Sakuya's right brow and eye curved into a smiling crescent, his left shimmered with tears, the man performing the needlessly deft feat of playing a game of solo fukuwarai, busying himself with eating, laughing, and crying.

And on top of that, there was what this man was actually saying; far from his excessive honesty having an unvarnished and authentic sense of tasteful flair, it was simply that he knew no shame from exposing his idiocy to the world, wasn't it? He must have been unable to control himself any longer, for he changed his cross-legged sitting position to a split while leaning forwards, like he had fallen asleep while prostrating himself; it wasn't clear if the voice spilling out from beneath his downcast face was meant to be lament or laughter, and his muffled, garbled voice was unpleasant to listen to.

source.japanese:
いい大人の本音というのはさっきシサムがするりと啜[すす]った、酢漬けのチベル川鰈の切り身といった珍味の類と同じで、小出しにするから有り難みがあるのであり、遠慮もなく垂れ流しにされては胸焼けがする。
　がシサムにはあまりに哀れの度合いが過ぎて胸に迫ったと見えて、乳房の中に抱き寄せ聖母のように甘えさせてやりたげに、物優しい眼差しで、朔屋に差し延べようとした手は、キサラに横から叩[はた]き落とされた。
source.english:
An adult's true feelings are like the delicacy Sisam had just smoothly swallowed—a piece of pickled flounder from the Tiber. Valued because served in little portions. Pour them out without restraint and they give you heartburn.
Yet his excessive pitifulness seemed to move Sisam. With gentle eyes, as though she wished to gather him into her breasts like the Virgin and let him be indulged, she reached a hand toward him. Kisara knocked it down from the side.

target.text: The honest feelings of a respectable adult were akin to the sort of rare delicacy that Shisamu had just slurped down, those pickled slices of flounder from the Tiber: while there was worth and virtue to be found when served sparingly, if one indulged without restraint, all that awaited was heartburn. But the immense pity it inspired seemed to have been too much for Shisamu, appeared to strike a chord deep within her heart, for with a tender look in her eyes, like she wished to fawn on him and embrace him within her bosom as though were she the Holy Mother herself, she reached a hand out towards Sakuya, but it was struck down from the side by Kisara.

source.japanese: 駄目、駄目と無言で首を振って片割れの軽挙を戒める。そんな仏心を見せたら、抱擁だけで済むはずがないと、大怪魚悪婁の一件での経験からの忠告に、シサムも憑きモノが落ちたかの目覚め顔、厄落としと杯の薬草リキュール酒を呑み干した。
source.english: No, no. Kisara silently shook her head, warning her other half against such rashness. Show him that mercy and he would never stop at an embrace: advice born of the affair with the monstrous fish Akuru. Sisam came to her senses as though a possessing spirit had left her, then drained her cup of herbal liqueur to dispel the ill luck.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「泣いてんだか笑ってるんだか、どっちかにしようよ。まあ、今日だって確かに胸とお尻で釣ったけど、後でなんかを吹っかけるつもりはないって」
source.english: “Laughing or crying, pick one. Well, yes, today we did lure you with boobs and bottoms. But we're not setting you up for something afterward.”

target.text: Wordlessly shaking her head in a way that all but said "no, don't do it", she admonished her counterpart's rash action. If she showed such merciful compassion, it wouldn't just end with holding him in her arms; faced with that warning sourced from their experience during the incident with Akuru, the great legendary fish, the look on Shisamu's face was that of a woman who had awoken from a possession, like some manner of spectre had left her, and she gulped down a cup filled with liquor infused with medicinal herbs to finish the exorcism.

【Kisara】 「Are you crying or laughing, can you just pick one. Well, we certainly did lure you in here with our breasts and buttocks today, but we really aren't planning on demanding anything unreasonable in return.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「単に朔屋と酒呑みたかっただけ。
　あんたが来てからこういう機会、考えてみればなかったし」
source.english:
“Just wanted to drink with you.
Come to think of it, we haven't had a chance like this since you came aboard.”

source.japanese: それに、こないだの偽幽霊の時は、あんたも一応頑張ったしね、の労[ねぎら]いが小声だったのは、この二人にして照れがあったのかも知れない。信じられないことだが。
source.english: “Besides, you did your bit when those fake ghosts came around,” they added under their breath. Perhaps even these two were capable of embarrassment when it came to offering praise. Incredible though that was.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あの智里とは、ちょくちょく隠れ酒してるみたいだけどね───あ、もしかしてあいつも呼んだ方がよかった？」
source.english: “You seem to sneak drinks with that Tomosato fairly often. Ah, should we have invited him too?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「らろーーーっ、らめええええ、智里きたら女の子とか、きっとあんたらも、あいつの方に行っちゃうの……だってあいつのほうが絶対もてるし」
source.english: “Nooooo! Don't! If Tomosato came, all the girls—you two as well—you'd go to him… He always gets more women than me.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こ、ここだけの話ですが姐さん、智里って、女の子と来たら女衒に売り飛ばしたり岡場所に追いやったりちょっと素敵なお風呂に沈めたりするヤツですぜ？」
source.english: “J-just between us, ladies, Tomosato's the sort who sells women to procurers, packs them off to unlicensed brothels, or sinks them in one of those rather nice bathhouses, you know?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「食い物にされた女は数知れず、みんなが泣いてその涙がこの海にどんだけ流れこんでいる事やら知れたもんじゃないのホントに」
source.english: “No counting the women he's preyed on. All weeping. No telling how many of their tears have run into this sea. Honestly.”

source.japanese: 岡っ引きに告げ口する町奴か、片手を屏風と立てて耳打ちしようとて、ついでに耳たぶの匂いでも嗅ごうとしてきた朔屋のこめかみを鉄の爪で掴んで押し遣りながら、シサム、
source.english: Like a townsman tattling to a constable, he raised a hand as a screen to whisper—and tried to sniff her earlobe while he was at it. Sisam caught his temple in an iron claw and pushed him away.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「We just wanted to share some drinks with you Sakuya, that's all. Thinking about it, we haven't really had a chance to do so since you joined us.」

Besides, this is also a thank-you for sort of making an effort with those fake ghosts the other day, she said under her breath, so perhaps these two might even have felt a little bashful. That beggared belief, however.
【Kisara】 「Though it does seem like you've been secretly drinking with that Tomosato guy every now and then, right───oh, would it have been better if we also invited him?」
【Naomasa】 「SHTOOーーー, DOOOON'T, if Tomosato shows up, then all the girls, and you ladies too I bet, are just gonna flock to him instead ……cause that guy's definitely way more popular with the ladies!」

【Naomasa】 「Th-, this is just between you and me, young lady, but this Tomosato guy, when it comes to girls, he's the type who sells them off to a brothel or forces them to work in the red-light district while he's off submerged in a rather lovely bath somewhere else, you got that?」
【Naomasa】 「There's no telling how many women have been preyed upon, and lord knows how many of their salty tears have bled into this ocean, it's the truth, I swear!」

Did he think himself a machi-yakko snitching to an okappiki or something? (TN: Machi-yakko, written "町奴", lit. "town fellows", were members of street gangs formed by townspeople of all stripes and colours in the early Edo period, and they emerged as a sort of counter-force to the hatamotoyakko, written "旗本奴", groups of young, privileged samurai retainers, in particular bannermen serving the shogun directly, who abused their status to villainous ends. The okappiki, written "岡っ引き", were unofficial police assistants or informants. Think private thief catchers not formally employed by the government, usually former criminals themselves.)

He held one hand up like a folding screen and made to whisper into her ear, even tried to get a sniff of her earlobe while he was at it, and so while grabbing Sakuya's temples in her iron claws and shoving him aside, Shisamu then said:

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……呑み友達つかまえて、ようも臆面なくあることないこと」
source.english: “…Some drinking buddy you are. Mixing truth and lies without a blush.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「もしかして朔屋、本当はあれのこと、嫌ってるとか？」
source.english: “Sakuya, do you actually hate him?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ばーははははっはは、嫌うも何もあーた、あいつぁ殺し屋ですよこ・ろ・ち・や。しかもターゲットは俺だっていう。酒でも呑まにゃあ正気で話せませんわい」
source.english: “Bahahahaha! Hate him? He's an assassin, my dear. An ash-shash-in. And says I'm his target. Can't talk to him sober without losing my mind.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……それ、言ってること完全に破綻してるけど、確かにすっかり忘れてたわ……あれが殺し屋だってこと」
source.english: “…That's completely incoherent. But I really had forgotten… that he's an assassin.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そういやそうだっけ……。やっぱおかしいわ、あいつもあんたも」
source.english: “Oh, right, he is… You and he are both strange.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーもう、あーもう、ほらあいつの名前が出た途端にあいつの話ばっかになった。ダメでしょうそれじゃあ君達！」
source.english: “Oh, honestly! Oh, honestly! The instant his name comes up, it's all about him. That won't do, ladies!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「何よりあいつにゃあ、おっぱいもお尻もついでに女のあそこもないの！
　色々と論外なの！」

【Naomasa】 「Oh no no, the second time, I was nearly slipped a deadly toxin, so that was a life-or-death situation. No scars or anything, but.」

The only one who failed to grasp the acrid, choking taste of the silence that had rendered the twin first mates mute was none other than the very person who had uttered the words that summoned it. Oblivious to the two whose lips were pursed into tight frowns as if they were the ones who had been forced to sip from the cup of poison vinegar, Sakuya grumbled on,

【Naomasa】 「And every single time, it was at the hands of some man who I'd had nothing to do with at all. Back then, I───actually, this still holds true even now───but I really, truly did not attempt to make a single move on Rui-san.」

【Naomasa】 「And, well, you know, we were acquaintances, and so I spoke to her a little, but it was really nothing more than a polite greeting. And yet, those guys, that was enough to make them completely explode with jealousy.」

【Naomasa】 「They say jealousy is something women should keep in moderation, but that is bull. Male jealousy is much, much worse. Like hell I'd just let myself get killed over some stupid misunderstanding.」
【Naomasa】 「In short, that's the kind of woman Rui-san is. She's the type who drags men into ruin. And the worst part is, she doesn't even realize it herself.」
【Naomasa】 「Even someone like me would be wary, alright?」
Once more, a moment of silence However, after a bit of time passed, Shisamu and Kisara burst into a roaring laughter, and with such force they had to hold their stomachs.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え？　あれ？　今の話、なんか笑いどころあったか？」
source.english: “Huh? What? Was there anything funny in that?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あっは、あはははっ、いやごめん、あんた、おんなに手ぇ出して痛い目に遭うのはまあ仕方がないとして」
source.english: “Ahaha, hahaha! Sorry, but… Get hurt for making a move on a woman, fair enough…”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あはははっ、あははっ、別に手ぇ出さなくても死にかけるっていう。それでも女好きって───」
source.english: “Ahahahaha! Ahaha! Nearly die without even making a move, though. And still you love women—”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ば、莫迦だ。見てよキサラ、ここに莫迦の一人見本市がいる」
source.english: “I-idiot. Look, Kisara. A one-man trade fair of idiocy.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「見てる見てる、聳え立つシヴァリンガ級の莫迦だもの、見る気なくっても勝手に目に入ってくるよ」
source.english: “Looking, looking. An idiot on the scale of a towering Shiva lingam. Can't help seeing him even if I don't try.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「えー……そこまで言うかー……」
source.english: “Uh… You have to go that far…?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Eh? Huh? Was there anything funny to laugh about in what I just said?」
【Shisamu】 「A-hah, ahahaha, nono, I'm sorry, it's just, if you get your fingers burned when trying to play around with women, that's all on you.」
【Kisara】 「Ahahaha, ahaha, but even though you weren't even trying anything like that, you were still almost killed. And you're still a womanizer───!」
【Shisamu】 「Idi-, you're such an idiot. Behold, Kisara, before you stands a one-man exhibition of idiocy.」
【Kisara】 「Oh, I see him alright, he's such a towering, Shivalinga-grade idiot that even if I tried not to look, he'd just force his way into my vision.」
【Naomasa】 「Eeh……do you really have to go that far……?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「もうしょんぼりしたってほだされない。
　だって───ほら！」
source.english:
“I'm not softening just because you look sad.
Because—look!”

source.japanese: シサムが、くいっと己の乳房を腕組みに、下から掬[すく]い上げてみせる。と。
source.english: Sisam crossed her arms and lifted her breasts from beneath. And—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おっ！」
source.english: “Oh!”

source.japanese: 朔屋は眸[ひとみ]をおっぱいの形にする勢いで目に一杯に映して身を乗りだす。
source.english: Sakuya leaned forward, filling his eyes with the sight until they nearly took the shape of breasts themselves.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I won't be swayed just because you're looking all downcast anymore. Because───look!」
Shisamu crossed her arms, then made a show of scooping up her breasts from below with a brisk lift. And then.
【Naomasa】 「WHOA!」
His eyes practically bulging out in the shape of breasts, Sakuya leaned forwards as if trying to fill his entire field of vision with them.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こっちだって───どう？」
source.english: “And over here—how's this?”

source.japanese: キサラがちらりとスカートの端を、繊細かつ大胆な調節でまくり上げてみせる。
source.english: With a delicate, daring adjustment, Kisara lifted the edge of her skirt for a glimpse.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───うおっ」
source.english: “Whoa!”

source.japanese: ひゅんっと目覚ましい反応速度で朔屋の視線が移動する。右と左に目まぐるしく視線を飛ばして朔屋は、しまいに目を回し、ふらふらと立ち竦み、それでも立派だった。
source.english: His gaze shifted with astounding speed. Back and forth, right and left. At last he grew dizzy and stood swaying. Still, he was magnificent.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And how about me─── what do you think?」
Kisara briefly teased up the hem of her skirt with a motion equal parts dainty and audacious.
【Naomasa】 「───UOH!」

With a remarkable reaction speed, Sakuya's eyes whipped around. His eyes darted left to right in a dizzying blur, and before long, his vision spun, he staggered to a halt, swayed on his feet, and yet, Sakuya remained dignified to the end.

source.japanese: 酒瓶に残っていた二割方残っていた酒を、きちんと飲み干してから───ぶっ倒れたのだから。
source.english: Because he had made sure to drain the last fifth or so of the bottle—before collapsing.

target.text: After all, he had made sure to dutifully drain every last drop of the roughly two-tenths of liquor that remained in the bottle───before keeling over.

source.japanese:
双子から、やんややんやの喝采が降り注ぐ。
　朔屋はことほど左様に、ぶっ潰れるにしても女体を目に焼きつけ、酒を浴びるだけ浴びたわけで、それは幸せな喪神だったろう。
source.english:
The twins showered him with cheers.
Even in going under, Sakuya had burned the female body into his eyes and drenched himself in as much liquor as he could drink. A happy oblivion, surely.

source.japanese:
幸せだったのは朔屋だけではない、双子もまた。この、楽しさはなんだろう。酒精がもたらした、一時の幻惑であるとは知りつつも、いや知っているからこそかえって、酒を愛する者は酔いを愛する。心楽しく酔う事のできる呑み仲間を得難く想う。
　二人にとって青年は、日頃は欺いたりからかったりの相手だが、この時は同じ酒酌み交わすと相手として申し分なく、口にこそせなんだが誘って面白しと認めていたのは、朔屋にとっては金の勲章にも勝る誉れとなったろう……ま、結局指一本触らせてもらえなかったと悔しがるだけかも知れないが。
source.english:
Sakuya was not alone in his happiness; the twins were happy too. What was this pleasure? They knew it for a passing illusion born of alcohol—yet perhaps precisely because they knew, they embraced it. Those who loved drink loved drunkenness, and prized the rare companions with whom they could get happily drunk.
Ordinarily this young man was someone to trick and tease. Tonight, however, he was all one could wish for in a drinking companion. Though neither said it aloud, both acknowledged that inviting him had been a pleasure. To Sakuya, that would have been an honor surpassing a gold medal. Well—perhaps he would merely have resented not being allowed to touch either woman with so much as one finger.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あー……面白かった。いやあ、始めは朔屋のこと、ちょっとねぎらってやるつもりだった筈だよね、あたしら」
source.english: “Ah… That was fun. At first we meant to show Sakuya a little appreciation, didn't we?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そのつもりだったけどさ。でもあたしらの方が笑わせてもらってない、これ？」
source.english: “That was the idea. But he's been the one making us laugh, hasn't he?”

source.japanese: 本当に可笑しい奴だと、二人は酔い果てた朔屋に向けて、改めて乾杯して、向き合って腕絡めて、互いの酒を互いの口に流しこんで、さも愉快そうな、そして満悦の吐息をついた事である。
source.english: The twins declared him a truly ridiculous man and toasted the thoroughly sodden Sakuya once more. Then they faced one another, linked arms, and poured their drinks into each other's mouths before breathing out sighs of complete and evident contentment.

target.text: A thundering ovation and shouts of hooray from the twins rained down upon him. Thus, having come to this, even as he collapsed in his drunkenness, Sakuya had made sure to burn the image of the female form into his eyes, made sure to drown himself in drink, and it must have been a blissful kind of stupor, if ever there was one.

But it was not just Sakuya who felt bliss, for so, too, did the twins. What was this joy, really? Even knowing it to be a mere fleeting illusion wrought by the spirits they had ingested, nay, perhaps because they know as much do those who love drink cherish being drunk all the more. And they lament how rare and precious it is to find a drinking companion in whose company one can get pleasantly, joyfully drunk.

To these two, this young man was normally but a target of their teasing and tricks, but in this moment, as someone sharing and pouring the same drink as them, they had no complaints, and though it never passed their lips, they had still invited him and acknowledged him as fun to be around; to Sakuya, that would likely be an honour worth more than any golden medal……well, then again, he might just end up kicking himself for not even getting to touch them.
【Kisara】 「Aahー……that was some great fun. No really, at first, we did just come here to show a little bit of our appreciation for Sakuya, didn't we?」
【Shisamu】 「That was the intent, yeah. But like, aren't we the ones who ended up being entertained here?」

They looked at the dead-drunk Sakuya, and thinking to themselves what a truly ridiculous guy he was, raised their glasses in a formal toast to him, then turned to face each other, linked their arms together, and each poured their own drink into the other's mouth; finally, they let out a sigh filled with pure, satisfied delight.

source.japanese:
信天翁号、寄港せり。
　この度の商取引───有り体に言えば密貿易───の荷を下ろす為と、泪を通じて北限氷土調査の前払い金を受け取る為である。
　荷の積み降ろしでは言うまでもなく朔屋以下下級水夫達は酷使されたけれど、それが終わってしまえば上陸する隙を見つけるのはそれほど難しいことではなかった。
source.english:
The Albatross made port.
This visit had two purposes: to unload the cargo from the latest commercial venture—smuggling, to speak plainly—and to receive through Rui the advance payment for the Northern Ice Wastes survey. Naturally, Sakuya and the other junior sailors were worked mercilessly during the unloading. Once it was done, however, finding an opportunity to go ashore was not especially difficult.

target.text: The Albatross made port. It was to unload the cargo from this business transaction───or to speak frankly, smuggling───and to receive the advance payment for their expedition to the northernmost permafrost through Rui's connection. Needless to say, loading and unloading cargo involved Sakuya as well as the deck boys being mercilessly worked to the bone, but once that was over, finding an opportunity to go ashore wasn't all that difficult.

source.japanese: しばらくぶりの揺れない足下を踏みつつ、朔屋が港町を流していた時の事。
source.english: For the first time in a while, the ground did not sway beneath Sakuya's feet as he drifted through the port town.

source.japanese:
【声】
『───申し訳ないが、お求めの版は品切れでね！』
source.english: ‘I'm sorry, but we're out of the edition you want!’

target.text: While Sakuya was drifting through the port town, taking his first steps in a good while on steady ground, it happened.
【Voice】 『───Sincerest apologies, but the edition you have requested is out of stock!』

source.japanese: 辺りに轟くというのではないが、通りにまでは聞こえる程度に、抑えられてはいても響く声、敵意と忌避感が籠もった。こういう台詞というのは、品があるのに売りたくない場合の商売人の常套文句である。
source.english: Not a roar, yet loud enough to reach the street. A restrained voice that still carried, full of hostility and aversion. The standard line of a tradesman who has the goods but does not wish to sell.

target.text: It was not as if it thundered throughout the neighbourhood, but it could be heard all the way out on the street, so loudly did that voice carry despite its owner's attempt at restraint, laden with animosity and aversion. Now, a line like that one, that was the sort of trite line brought out when a merchant did, in fact, have the article, but simply didn't want to sell it.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（どこの港でも、嫌われ者ってな、いるもんだな）
source.english: (Every port's got someone nobody likes.)

source.japanese:
とか他人事ゆえの観戦気分で朔屋が覗いた半開きの扉は、港沿いの街には付き物の、地図や海図を商う商会の、金筋の飾り線も賢しげな硝子戸、さして深入りする気もなく通り過ぎようとして、青年の足を止めた硝子越しの色合い、それは赤茶のリーファージャケットの。
　は、と胸を劈[つんざ]くような予感に更に深く覗けば───
source.english:
With the idle excitement of a spectator to whom it was all somebody else’s affair, Sakuya peered through a half-open door—the gold-ruled glass door, putting on its knowing air, of one of those map-and-chart concerns no waterfront town is complete without. He meant to pass on without involving himself any further, when a color beyond the glass stopped the young man in his tracks: the reddish brown of a reefer jacket.
Ah. A premonition lanced through his breast, and he peered deeper inside—

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （Looks like every port's got its black sheep, huh?）

And with that detached curiosity of a spectator with no skin in the game, Sakuya peeked through the half-open door, and it turned out to belong to one of those companies dealing in maps and charts that were a fixture of any port town, with the glass panels of said door adorned with smart-looking, gold-trimmed lines, but just as he was about to pass by the shop, not feeling much desire to get too deeply involved, there was something about the colour beyond the glass that stopped the young man in his tracks, for it was the hue of a reddish-brown reefer jacket. He let out a sharp gasp, and driven by an almost heart-rending premonition, when he sneaked a yet closer peek───

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「じゃあ、ちょっとくらい版が古い奴でもいいんだ。そいつだったら残ってないかな？」
source.english: “Then an edition that's a little older will do. Have you got any of those left?”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「探してはみるが、期待しなさんなよ……」
source.english: “I'll look. Don't get your hopes up…”

source.japanese: ……通りから垣の目覗きの朔屋にさえ、あからさまな気乗り薄、丸々と肥えた頬の壮年の店主は、探す手つきも単なる外面繕[つくろ]うだけと見抜けるほどにぞんざいで。案の定───
source.english: Even to Sakuya peeking in from the street, the man's reluctance was blatant. The middle-aged shopkeeper had plump cheeks, and his search was so perfunctory that anyone could see he was only keeping up appearances. And sure enough—

source.japanese:
【店主】
「ああやっぱりそれも品切れだな」
source.english: “Ah, no. Out of those too.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Alright, then a slightly older edition of it would be fine too. Maybe you still have one of those in stock?」
【Shopkeeper】 「I'll try looking around, but don't expect anything……」

……Even Sakuya, peeking through the glass from the outside as he was, could see that the way this blatantly unenthusiastic, middle-aged shopkeeper with his rounded, fat cheeks was searching around was nothing more than an attempt to keep up outward appearances, so sloppy and careless an effort was it. And as expected───
【Shopkeeper】 「Aah, I knew it, we're sold out of those too.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「それだったら……参謀本部編纂の奴じゃなくってもいいよ。
　どこか他の版元の奴でも───」
source.english:
“Then… it doesn't have to be compiled by the General Staff.
Another publisher's will do—”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「……あのな、言われなきゃわからないほど、初心ってわけでもあるまいが……」
source.english: “…Look. You're not so innocent you need it spelled out…”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「あんたらに売る地図はないって事だよ。
『信天翁号』の船員だろう、あんたら二人。聞いたことあるんだぜ、北方系の双子の女の話はさ」
source.english:
“I've got no maps to sell you.
You're crew on the Albatross, aren't you? Heard about you two. The twin women from the north.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「In that case……it doesn't have to be the General Staff version. Even one from some other publisher would───」
【Shopkeeper】 「……Now listen here, I'm not so green that I don't get it without having to be told first……」
【Shopkeeper】 「I don't have any charts to sell to you lot. You two are part of the crew of the Albatross, aren't you? I've heard about you before, tales of these northern twin girls.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まあ確かにあたしらは信天翁号の船員だけど、だからって海図を売ってはいけないって事もないじゃない」
source.english: “Yes, we're crew on the Albatross. Doesn't mean you're not allowed to sell us charts.”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「よく言うぜ。あんたらがなにをしてきたか、自分達が一番よく判ってるだろうが。こっちはな、そりゃ多少は足下を見る事はあるかもしれんが」
source.english: “Listen to you. You know better than anyone what you've done. Me, I might take a little advantage of a customer now and then…”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「それでもご法と、商売人の道義に外れることはやっちゃいない。だがあんたらと来たら、どうだ」
source.english: “But I don't break the law or the ethics of a tradesman. What about you?”

source.japanese: ああまでやる気の欠片も見えずとも、あれでそれなり商売人の辛抱強さを猫被りしていたと見え、かなぐり捨てれば頬肉も太々しい、頬杖で鷹揚に構えたつもりだろうが、道義とやらを笠に着る娑婆塞ぎ、洋風のカウンターよりいっそ因業両替の番台に座らせた方が似つかわしい。
source.english: For all his visible lack of enthusiasm, he had apparently still been wearing a mask of a tradesman's patience. Once he threw it off, even the flesh of his cheeks seemed brazen. Chin propped on his hand, he probably imagined he looked magnanimous: a waste of space sheltering behind his precious morality, better suited to an extortionate money changer's desk than that Western counter.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Well, sure, we're crew members of the Albatross, but that doesn't mean you can't sell us any charts, does it?」
【Shopkeeper】 「You've got some nerve. You should know damn well yourselves what you've done. Sure, maybe I'll size people up a little and take advantage of them every now and them.」
【Shopkeeper】 「But even so, I've never once crossed the law or betrayed the code of an honest merchant. But when it comes to you lot, I really do wonder.」

Despite showing not an ounce of enthusiasm, it seemed that he was, in his own way, feigning the patient perseverance befitting a merchant, but once he tossed that aside, even his meaty cheeks grew smug and brazen, and though he no doubt fancied himself magnanimous as he rested his chin on his hand, he only looked the part of a sanctimonious nuisance who clad himself in the cloak of righteousness; rather than a Western-style counter like this, he would look far more at home perched behind a booth as a callous skinflint of a moneylender.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「いやいや、こっちの店に迷惑かける気はないんだ。だから頼むってば」
source.english: “No, no, we're not looking to cause your shop any trouble. Come on, please.”

source.japanese:
───朔屋は反射的に目を背[そむ]けたくなったという。どれだけ餓えたとしても、獲物に哀願して肉を請う虎はいない。日頃さんざか痛い目に遭わされている女であろうと、否、だからこそそんな女の諂[へつら]う姿など見たくなかったのだ。
　先だって酌み交わした酒と、馬鹿話で浮かれ騒いだ時間への裏切りのようにさえ思えた。
source.english:
Sakuya, it is said, wanted instinctively to look away. However hungry it may grow, no tiger begs its prey to give it meat. She might be a woman who had dealt him no end of pain; no—precisely for that reason, he did not want to see such a woman abase herself so.
It seemed almost a betrayal of the drinks they had shared the other day, of the hours they had spent carousing over foolish talk.

source.japanese:
【店主】
「……しつこい女だな。まあ……そうだな。
　なんだったら考えてやらんこともない」
source.english:
“…Persistent woman. Well…
Yes. I might consider it.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Now, now, we have no intention of causing any trouble for your business. So please, I'm begging you here.」

───Sakuya reflexively felt a desire to avert his eyes. No tiger, no matter how starving it may be, would entreat its prey and beg for its flesh. Even if they were woman who habitually caused him hardship and suffering, nay, precisely because of that, he did not wish to see them debase themselves by fawning on someone. It even felt like a betrayal of that joyous time they'd spent together just a little while ago, sharing drink and making merry over idle talk.
【Shopkeeper】 「……You're real stubborn women. Well then……right. If you're so inclined, then I might have a proposal.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんだ、親父さん、ほんとは話がわかる人じゃない。いいよ、少しくらいは割高でも」
source.english: “Oh, so you do understand, old man. Fine. We don't mind paying a little extra.”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「なに勘違いしてるんだ。正値で売ってやるよ。多少は割り引いてやったっていい」
source.english: “You've got it wrong. I'll sell at the normal price. Might even give you a discount.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Would you look at that, the gentleman is reasonable after all. Sure thing, we can even pay a little extra, if needed.」
【Shopkeeper】 「You seem to be misunderstanding something. I'm selling it to you at the standard price. Why, I might even throw in a bit of a discount.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「え、それはちょっと気が退けるかな」
source.english: “Huh? We'd feel a little bad about that.”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「気にするな。ただし。
　店が引けた後だ。それまで待てるな？」
source.english:
“Don't worry.
But after closing. You can wait till then?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Uh, I don't know, I'd feel kind of guilty taking that.」
【Shopkeeper】 「Don't let it bother you. However. It will be after the shop closes. Can you wait until then?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まあ、真夜中とかにならなければ……」
source.english: “Well, so long as it isn't midnight or something…”

source.japanese:
キサラには、シサムには、ふんぞり返った店主の、精力過多にじくじく滲んだ脂で照り光った頬が見えていないのか。
　たるんだ頬をカウンターに叩きつければ、そこにはべっとり脂の跡が、それこそ壮年の性欲の案内地図として転写されよう。
　持ちかけているのは、いやしくも通りに面して構えた店内で許されるような取引でない事を見抜けないような、そんな女ではないはずなのに。事実、予想するまでもなく、
source.english:
Could Kisara and Sisam not see the swaggering shopkeeper’s cheeks, glossy with the grease that oozed from his surfeit of virility?
Slap those sagging jowls down on the counter and they would leave a thick slick behind—a perfect guide map to middle-aged lust.
Surely they were not the kind of women who could fail to see that what he was proposing was no transaction permissible inside a shop open to the public street. Indeed, there was no need to guess—

source.japanese:
【店主】
「いいや。今晩は外泊許可を取ってもらう。
　ヌビク・シキ通りのクラレンスビルの地下。
　ルーレットって名のバーがある」
source.english:
“No. You'll get permission to spend the night ashore.
Basement of the Clarence Building, Nubik-Shiki Street.
There's a bar called Roulette.”

source.japanese:
【店主】
「そこの個室を取っておく。
　二人で来いよ？　一人だけじゃ駄目だぜ」
source.english:
“I'll book a private room.
Both of you, understand? One won't do.”

source.japanese:
とこう突きつけてくるのは、狐が兎を誑[たぶら]かすのと同じでいかにも有り勝ち、見え透いた流れではあったが、信天翁号の航海士は柔な兎などではないけして、朔屋にはこのやりとり、たまりかねた。
　どうせなら、華燭の席から花嫁攫[さら]う無鉄砲無計画な若造の作法で、バイクで硝子戸たたき割って乗りこんでやれば箔もついたろうが、徒手空拳の朔屋は、破壊力よりただ迅速のみを尊んだ。
source.english:
His pressing it on them like this was a turn as trite and transparent as a fox beguiling a rabbit; but the Albatross’s navigators were by no means soft little rabbits, and for Sakuya the exchange had become unendurable.
He might have lent the business some grandeur by smashing through the glass door on a motorcycle, in the approved style of a reckless, planless young fool carrying a bride off from her wedding feast. With no weapon but his naked fists, however, Sakuya paid homage not to destructive force, but to speed alone.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Well, as long as we don't have to wait until midnight or something……」

Could Kisara and Shisamu not see how his cheeks, slick with oils oozing out of his pores from excess sexual vigour, glistened as the shopkeeper reclined? If he were to slap his sagging cheeks down on the counter, the sticky smear of grease left behind would be imprinted onto the surface like a veritable guide map to middle-aged lust. They were hardly the sort of women who would fail to see through the fact that the deal being proposed wasn't the sort permitted inside a shop facing the streets. In fact, he didn't even need to predict what came next,
【Shopkeeper】 「No. You'll need to get permission to spend the night ashore for tonight. In the basement of the Clarence building on Nubik-Shiki street. There's a bar called Roulette.」
【Shopkeeper】 「I'll reserve a private room there. Both of you come, alright? Just one of you won't cut it.」

Thrusting a demand upon them like this was no different from the fox deceiving the rabbit with honeyed words, an all-too-common and transparent ploy, but while the first mates of the Albatross were certainly not soft rabbits by any means, Sakuya still found this exchange of words unbearable to listen to. If possible, he would have liked to add some prestige and flair to the whole affair by riding a motorcycle through the glass door and smashing it to pieces in the manner of a brash young man without a plan storming the candlelit altar to steal away the bride, but as Sakuya was currently empty-handed, he prized swiftness of action alone over destructive power.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、ここにいましたか、一等航海士。航海予定立てたいって言うンで、機関長、甲板長が待ってますよ。さ、行きましょうか」
source.english: “Ah, there you are, Chief Mates. The chief engineer and the boatswain want to plan the voyage. They're waiting for you. Shall we go?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Oh, so this is where you were, chief mates. The Chief Engineer and the Bosun are waiting for you, said they want to draw up a plan for the voyage. Now then, shall we be off?」

source.japanese:
朔屋は双子のそれぞれ手をとって引きずり出す。
　呆気にとられていたのか、双子はしばらくは朔屋に引かれるままだったけれど、やがて邪険に手を振り解いた、けれど。顔に浮かんでいたのは苦笑の、責めるような棘はない。
source.english:
Sakuya took a hand from each twin and dragged them out.
Perhaps dumbfounded, they let him pull them along for a while. Eventually they shook him off roughly. Yet their wry smiles held no accusing sting.

target.text: Sakuya took a hand from each twin in his own and dragged them out. They must have been completely taken on the back foot, because for a while, they simply allowed themselves to be pulled away by Sakuya, but eventually, they harshly shook their hands free of his, however. While the smiles on their faces were wry and strained, they showed no sharp thorns of condemnation.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なにを白々しい芝居をやってんだか。
　あんたがあたしらを一等航海士だって。
　初めて聞いた」
source.english:
“What a shameless little performance.
Calling us Chief Mates.
First time I've heard that from you.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「What was up with that shamelessly transparent acting? You even called us chief mates. First time I've heard that one.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「航海予定立案だぁ？　そんなん港にいるうちからやった例しなんて、今まであったかシサム」
source.english: “Planning a voyage? When have we ever done that while still in port, Sisam?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Drawing up a plan for the voyage, are we? Has there ever been a case in the past where we've done that while still in port, Shisamu?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「覚えてないねえ……ああ、一回だけやったっけか」
source.english: “Don't recall… Ah, once, wasn't it?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Can't say I remember any…… aah, maybe we did it just once?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ああ、あったあった。でもその後、真夏だったのにドでかい雹が降ってきて、物見櫓の屋根に穴が空いたんだよね」
source.english: “Oh, right. Then huge hailstones fell, in midsummer, and punched holes in the lookout tower's roof.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Right, there was that one time, yeah. But just after that, despite being midsummer, massive chunks of hail began to fall from the sky, blowing holes straight through the roof of the watchtower, right?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「───朔屋、あんた細かい事気にしすぎ」
source.english: “Sakuya. You worry too much about little things.”

source.japanese: すっと細めた瞼[まぶた]のあわいで碧眼が、先ほど振り払った手よりも強く、朔屋を突き放すように、光って冷たい。
source.english: Between lids drawn suddenly narrow, blue eyes flashed cold, thrusting Sakuya away more forcefully than she had flung off his hand a moment before.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもなあ。同じ船の仲間がああもあからさまに、体売れ、って言われてるの見ちゃさ」
source.english: “Still. When I see my own shipmates being told so plainly to sell their bodies…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「───Sakuya, you worry too much about the little things.」
Through her suddenly narrowed eyelids, her turquoise eyes gleamed coldly, seeming to push Sakuya away with even greater force than the hand she had just brushed his away with before.
【Naomasa】 「But, it's just. When I see fellow shipmates being told to, sell their bodies, in such an obvious way, you know.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「同じ船の仲間と来た。あんた、忘れてんじゃない？　自分がなんで信天翁号に乗る羽目になったのか」
source.english: “Your own shipmates, eh? Have you forgotten why you ended up on the Albatross?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And now he calls us fellow shipmates. Have you forgotten or something? How exactly it was you ended up on the Albatross to begin with?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そういや今日は、脱走は考えてないの？
　絶好の機会だと思うんだけどな」
source.english:
“Come to think of it, no escape attempt today?
Perfect chance, I'd say.”

source.japanese:
仲間、という言葉を面と向かってせせら笑う双子に、強い反感を抱けなかったのはどうしてか。朔屋自身不思議ではあったが、これまで莫迦だ役立たずだ無能だ下半身男だ穀潰し脳天パーだと罵りつけても、それでも彼を、帰る術もないような外国の港に置き去りにしたり寝ている間に海に厄介払いしたりしなかったのも、また確かな事実なのである。
（ただそれでも朔屋は、自分に浴びせかけられてきた嘲罵の単語の列を俯瞰して、ちょっとだけ、そうちょっとだけ物哀しくなった）
source.english:
Why couldn't he bring himself to resent the twins more for sneering in his face at the word 'shipmates'? Sakuya himself found it strange. They had called him idiot, useless, incompetent, all crotch, freeloader, empty head. Yet it was also true that they had never abandoned him in a foreign port with no way home, nor tossed him into the sea in his sleep to be rid of him.
(Still, surveying the procession of insults he had received, Sakuya felt just a little—yes, a little—sad.)

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……茶化すなよ。あんたらみたいな無敵の女が、ああも軽く扱われてるの見るのは、俺だって良い気分じゃないんだ」
source.english: “…Don't make fun of it. Even I don't like seeing invincible women like you treated so cheaply.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Which reminds me, haven't you considered fleeing today? I think this is a perfect opportunity, really.」

Why was it that he did not feel any powerful antipathy towards these twins who simply sneered with contempt when met with the word "shipmate" from him? It was a mystery to Sakuya himself, but even though they had hitherto abused and insulted him by calling him idiot, useless, incompetent, thinking with the wrong head, parasite, numskull, and on and on, they also had yet to abandon him to fend for himself in some port of a foreign country with no means to return home, nor had they simply gotten rid of the nuisance by tossing him into the ocean while he slept; that was also established fact.
(Nevertheless, as Sakuya examined from a distance the string of insults that had been hurled his way, he felt a little, yea, a tiny bit melancholy.)
【Naomasa】 「……Stop making light of this. When I see women as peerless as you two get treated so cheaply, it doesn't sit right with me either.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こんなの気にしてたら、港になんか下りられなくなるよ、朔屋」
source.english: “Let things like that bother you and you won't be able to go ashore at all, Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんたはまだ顔が知られてないからね、実感薄いみたいだけど」
source.english: “Nobody knows your face yet. Doesn't seem real to you.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If a little thing like that gets to you, soon enough, you won't even be able to set foot in port, Sakuya.」
【Kisara】 「Your face isn't widely known out there yet, so it probably doesn't feel that real to you.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あのおっさんが言ってたことは、嘘なんかじゃないし。あたしらがあちこちでしたいようにやってるのは、本当じゃないか」
source.english: “The old man wasn't lying. It's true we do whatever we please wherever we go.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だからって───」
source.english: “Even so—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But what that old goat said wasn't exactly a lie or anything. We really are doing whatever the hell we want wherever the hell we go, aren't we?」
【Naomasa】 「That doesn't justify───」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ほんとにいやなら、あの船を降りてるさ。
　なんのかんのと好きでやってること。
　後ろ指さされようが、
　それは自業自得ってね」
source.english:
“If we really hated it, we'd leave the ship.
Whatever else, we do it because we like it.
People point fingers?
Brought it on ourselves.”

source.japanese:
……この時実際に、擦れ違った船員が、忌まわしいモノでも見た目でシサムとキサラに後ろ指を向けていたのだが。
　次の瞬間、その指先は真反対に向けられた。
　すなわち、三人が後にしてきた地図商会に。
source.english:
At that very moment, a passing sailor had been pointing at Sisam and Kisara with a look of disgust.
The next instant, his finger pointed the opposite way.
Toward the map dealer the three had just left.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If I really found it unbearable, I would just get off that ship. Despite everything, I do it because I love it. If people point fingers at me behind my back, that's just me reaping what I sow, right?」

……In this very moment, a sailor who passed by them was looking at Shisamu and Kisara like he had just witnessed something abominable, and he was, in fact, pointing a finger at them. The next moment, that fingertip was pointed in the exact opposite direction. To wit, at the map company the three had just left behind.

source.japanese: 轟音と共に爆発した、地図商会に。
source.english: Which exploded with a roar.

target.text: There was an explosion followed by a deafening roar. Inside the map company.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「な……な、なんで!?
　危なかった、あそこに残ってたら、
　俺達みんな巻きこまれて……」
source.english:
“W-why!? That was close!
If we'd stayed,
we'd all have been caught in it…”

source.japanese:
朔屋は耳を疑った。命の危機を辛くも逃れたというのに、シサムとキサラが零していた
のは忍び笑いの、こらえきれない笑いを辛うじて抑えたといった態の。それで、この鈍感な朔屋にもようやく事の次第が了解された来たわけである。
source.english:
Sakuya could not believe his ears. They had barely escaped mortal danger,
yet Sisam and Kisara were snickering, scarcely holding back their laughter. Even slow Sakuya finally began to understand.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい、シサム、キサラッ。
　あんたらまさか───っ」
source.english:
“Hey, Sisam, Kisara.
You two aren’t—”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「WH-……WH-, WHY!? Damn that was close, if we had stayed in there, we would all have been caught up in……」

Sakuya couldn't believe his ears. Even though they had only narrowly escaped life-threatening danger, what spilled out from both Shisamu's and Kisara's lips were stifled chuckles, and it seemed as if they could only barely keep unrestrained guffawing at bay. And with that, even our dull Sakuya finally arrived at an understanding of the circumstances that had led to this.
【Naomasa】 「Oi, Shisamu, Kisara. Don't tell me you two───!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「さあ、ねえ。
　そういえばキサラ、あれ、どこいったっけ。
　ほら、クロを売っ払うがどうのの時、
　あの腐れ金持ちからくすねてきたマイト」
source.english:
“Well, I wonder.
Come to think of it, Kisara, where did that go again?
You know,
the dynamite we swiped from that filthy rich guy back when we were talking about selling Kuro.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Well, who can say? That reminds me, Kisara, wherever did it end up again? You know, that dynamite we swiped from that degenerate rich guy, back during the whole selling off Kuro thing and all that stuff.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「どこだったかなあ。さっきまでたまさか持っていたような気もするけど、でももう持ってないんだよな～」
source.english: “Where was it again? I feel like I had it a second ago, but now it’s gone~”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「訂正する。あんたら、無敵の女って言うよりも。女悪魔っていうんだ、そうに違いないそうに決まった」
source.english: “Correction. Not invincible women. She-devils. That's what you are, no question.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I sure wonder where it went. I feel like I might have had it with me by pure coincidence until just a little while ago, but it seems like I don't have it anymore～」
【Naomasa】 「I am amending my prior statement. You two, you're not peerless women. You're she-devils, there's no doubt about it, it's been decided.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「人聞きの悪い。悪魔だったらそもそもあんなに舐められたりするもんかい」
source.english: “Don't slander us. If we were devils, nobody would've treated us with that much contempt.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「How slanderous. If we were devils, we never would have allowed him to treat us so contemptuously in the first place.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「とはいえ、これ以上舐められたりしちゃ、ウチらの商売的に、いろいろと差し支えあるしね」
source.english: “Still, letting anyone treat us with more contempt than that would cause all sorts of problems for our business.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「That said, if we keep letting people walk all over us, it'll be bad for business, and in more ways than one, you know.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「北限氷土方面の、既知領域分の地図と海図が欲しかったんだけど。ま、他にも店はあるさ」
source.english: “We wanted maps and charts of the known territory toward the Northern Ice Wastes. Well, there are other shops.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「We were just hoping to get land maps and nautical charts covering the already-charted regions of the northernmost permafrost. Well, plenty of other shops out there.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ってなわけで、あたしらはまだちょっと回ってみるから。でもあんたはあんまりふらふらしてないほうが身の為だと思うよ」
source.english: “So we'll look around a little more. But you'd better not wander too much. For your own good.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And so on that note, we'll still be looking around for a bit longer. But I don't think you should wander around aimlessly for too long. For your own sake.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんかまた、信天翁号に関しての、ろくでもない、根も葉もない噂が一つ、できそうだから」
source.english: “Looks like another nasty, utterly unfounded rumor about the Albatross is about to be born.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Because it looks like, for whatever reason, yet another ridiculous, completely unfounded rumour about the Albatross is about to start spreading.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「根も葉もないって事はないだろうよ……」
source.english: “Can't exactly call it unfounded…”

source.japanese: 呆然と二人を見送るしかない朔屋だった。
source.english: Sakuya could only watch them go in a daze.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「I don't think it's really all that unfounded……」
All Sakuya could do was watch the two of them walk away in a daze.

source.japanese:
先日双子とさんざか呑んだので、酒にはそれほど飢えていないけれど、二人はちらちら見せるばかりで体には全然触れさせてもくれなかった。
　性欲を持て余し、とにかく酒場のお姉さんに一発気持ちよくしてもらおうと店に入ったはいいのだが。
source.english:
After all that drinking with the twins the other day, he was not especially starved for liquor. But they had only flashed glimpses of their bodies, never let him touch at all.
Frustrated with desire, he went into a tavern to have one of its women give him a good time.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（で、出直そう）
source.english: (Better come back later.)

source.japanese: 酒場の中には先客が。あのおとろちい泪が現地の金持ちとなにやら商談の最中で、彼女の事が怖くてたまらない朔屋はこれはいかんと引き返そうとするのだが、別の誰かに酒場の中に押しこまれる。背中を押し立ててくるのは、金の結い髪に赤のリーファージャケット、先ほど別れたはずのシサムとキサラで。
source.english: Someone was already there. That scawy Rui, conducting some business with a wealthy local. Sakuya, terrified of her, was about to retreat when someone else pushed him into the tavern. Blond hair tied up, red reefer jackets. Sisam and Kisara, whom he had supposedly just left.

target.text: He'd had plenty to drink with the twins the other day, and so he wasn't that thirsty for liquor, but the two had only been showing him teasing glimpses, not allowing him to touch their bodies at all. He was feeling too lustful to handle it by himself, and so he went out, hoping to score a good time with some lady from some bar, though he really should have just gone to a house of ill repute instead.
【Naomasa】 （Well, think I'll come back later.）

The bar already had patrons. That scawwy lady, Rui, was in the middle of some kind of business negotiations with a local wealthy man about something or other, and Sakuya, hopelessly terrified of her, decided this wouldn't do, already on his way back out the door, but he was shoved back inside the bar by someone else. Pushing against his back were a pair of elaborate golden coiffures and red reefer jackets; it was the duo he'd parted ways with just earlier, Shisamu and Kisara.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「おー、朔屋もやっぱりここに来てたかあ。
　ていってもウチらに呑ませてくれるのは、
　こういう酒場くらいしかないしね」
source.english:
“Oh, Sakuya—you came here after all.
Not that many places in town
will serve the likes of us.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ooh, had a feeling you'd end up here too, Sakuya. That said, the only places that'll serve people like us, that'd be crummy bars like this one.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それとも酒目当てじゃなくって、今夜は女の気分だった？　でも一杯くらいはあたしらに付き合いな。したらおっぱいくらいは揉んでもいいからさ。ねーシサム」
source.english: “Or wasn't it the drink? In the mood for a woman tonight? Still, have a glass with us. Then you can at least squeeze our boobs. Right, Sisam?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやそのあの、俺はちょっと急用を思い出して───って、キサラ、今なんつった。やらせてくれるってぇ!?」
source.english: “No, uh, I just remembered some urgent business—Kisara, what did you say? You'll let me do it!?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Or are you in the mood for a woman tonight instead of a drink? Still, you gotta have at least one drink with us. If you do, I'll let you fondle my tits or something. Riiight, Shisamu?」
【Naomasa】 「No, well, it's, uhmm, I just remembered I have some very urgent business and───wait, Kisara, what was that? You'll let me do you!?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ないない、そこまでは許してない。
　とにかく、入口で立ちんぼも迷惑だ。
　座ろうよ」
source.english:
“No, no. Didn't give permission for that much.
Anyway, standing in the entrance is a nuisance.
Let's sit.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「No, no, didn't consent to that much. Anyways, we're being a nuisance just standing here at the entrance. Let's go take a seat.」

source.japanese:
二人も朔屋同様、休暇をもらったらしい。
　一等航海士がそうひょいひょい船を離れていいのかどうかというところだが、その辺りの規律は実に緩い信天翁号、朔屋はなし崩しに双子と同席になる。ただし一応泪とは離れた席にとったのは、双子は向こうの商談に憚[はばか]ったのか、泪恐怖症の朔屋を慮った為かは定かならず
　朔屋としては、今日は酒より女を抱きたい気分なのだが、一応上司に当たる一等航海士には逆らえない。
source.english:
The twins appeared to have shore leave too.
Whether chief mates should so casually abandon ship was another question, but discipline aboard the Albatross was decidedly loose, and thus Sakuya found himself at a table with them. They did at least choose one some distance from Rui—whether to avoid disturbing her negotiation or out of consideration for Sakuya's Rui phobia, it was impossible to say.

source.japanese:

source.english: The killer had climbed to the lookout, blue eyes peering over the platform's edge. (TN: Fujidzuru-maki, written "藤蔓巻", refers to the wrapping on the handle of a Japanese sword. It looks a bit like wisteria vines wrapped around something. target.text: Tilting his head while wondering if that could be true, Sakuya, still lying on his side with one cheek resting in his hand, yawned again, eyes stinging a little as they watered from waking up; he closed them, opened them again, and then, a sharp chill settled into the tip of his nose. And so, while the sudden incident gradually caused an atmosphere of unease to settle over the ship, had Sakuya ignored it, and had Tomosato not forcibly drawn his attention to it, then the Albatross would undoubtedly simply have continued on her merry way, passing it by.

source.japanese:
何かというと四六時中厄介事に巻きこまれている、或いは招き寄せている感の強い信天翁号だが、さすがにそれは過言というもので、一日二四時間を四時間事に分けた六単位のうち、実際にトラブルに遭遇しているのは、航海を平均すれば大体四単位程度に収まる。
　これとても平均化しての数字であり、なんだかんだと朔屋がへまをやらかして斜檣から吊されたり、密航者が発見されて舷側から両脚を大きく開脚せられ縛り上げられた屈辱固めの姿勢で吊されたり、クロが食堂で食べきれず、自室に持ちこんで食べ物をついうっかり黴[カビ]の温床にして、寝台から部屋一面に大繁殖させては下級水夫滅菌部隊の出動となり、厳重な清浄作業の後で、夜具ごと上甲板の洗濯紐に吊されたりする程度の、実に微笑ましい出来事ばかりが続く穏やかな日々も多い。
source.english:
The Albatross may seem forever embroiled in trouble—or actively summoning it—but that would be an exaggeration. Divide the day into six four-hour watches and, averaged across a voyage, trouble occupies only about four.
Even that is merely an average. There are plenty of tranquil days filled with nothing but heartwarming little incidents: Sakuya bungles something and is hung from the bowsprit; a stowaway is discovered and strung over the side in a humiliating hold, legs spread wide and bound; or Kuro fails to finish a meal, carries it back to her cabin, and inadvertently breeds a mold colony that spreads from her bunk across the entire room, prompting deployment of the junior-sailor sterilization squad—after whose rigorous cleansing, Kuro is hung from the upper-deck laundry line along with her bedding.

source.japanese: ただ、船内では平穏とは退屈と同義語であり、打ち続けば皆自然と飽きが来る、だらけてくる、ただでさえ風紀の緩み著しい信天翁号にては目も当てられない状況となり、朔屋あたりは吊されるだけでは満足できなくなってくるのか、より深刻かつ救いのない悪行をやらかすようになってくる（たとえば水夫長の書物の頁を巻紙に使って、巻き煙草を密売しようとしたり）。こういった無為の内に過ぎる日々に刺激を与え、賦活する為には、難破船発見といったニュースは実に格好な出来事と思われたのに───
source.english: Aboard, however, peace meant boredom. Let it continue and everyone naturally grew weary and slack. On the Albatross, where discipline was lax enough already, the result became unbearable.
