Sakuya, perhaps no longer satisfied with merely being hung up, would commit more serious, more hopeless offenses—trying, for example, to use pages from the boatswain's books as cigarette papers and sell the cigarettes illicitly. To enliven such idle days, the discovery of a wreck seemed ideal. Yet—

source.japanese: 朔屋、このお手柄に仕事の免除か酒の一瓶でもねだろうと早速水夫長に注進に参じたところ、これが奇妙な事に反応がはかばしくないのである。
source.english: Sakuya hurried to report his achievement to the boatswain, hoping to ask for time off or a bottle of liquor. Strangely, the response was unenthusiastic.

target.text: The Albatross got involved in trouble at every opportunity, night and day, or perhaps she just had a strong knack for inviting such upon herself, but that was an exaggeration, naturally, for when dividing the twenty-four hours of a day into six even periods of four hours, averaging across their voyages, they actually only ran into trouble in four of those periods per day.

This number was painted with a very broad brush; through all manner of mishaps, Sakuya would end up making some big blunder and be hung from the bowsprit as a result; the stowaway would be discovered and tied up with her legs spread wide open, then hung down from the broadside while stuck in a very humiliating pose.

Kuro would be unable to finish her meal in the mess, bringing it back to her personal cabin where the food turned into a breeding ground for mold after it slipped her mind, leading to the mold covering the entire surface of her bed and the room as it multiplied in great numbers, which would lead to the mobilization of a sterilization squad composed of deck boys, and after a very rigorous cleaning job, she would be hung up together with her bedding from a clothesline on the upper deck; there were many peaceful days where nothing but little heartwarming episodes like these happened in succession.

However, on board the ship, peace and quiet were synonymous with boredom, and if it persisted long enough, everyone would naturally grow bored, become languid and lazy, and even the Albatross, which ordinarily was strikingly lax with discipline, would fall into an unsightly state; take Sakuya, who, perhaps no longer able to find satisfaction in just being hung up, became liable to commit even more grave and irredeemable misdeeds (like trying to deal black-market cigarettes he hand-rolled using pages he'd snatched from the Bosun's books, for example).
To inject some much-needed stimulation into these days spent in idleness, to reinvigorate them, news like the discovery of a shipwreck seemed like just the right kind of event, and yet───

Sakuya, convinced he could use this commendable feat of his as an excuse to be granted an exemption from work, or maybe even pester him for a bottle of booze, had immediately rushed to the Bosun to report to him, but in a strange turn of events, the response he received in turn wasn't very promising.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……難破船だぁ？
　また厄介なブツを見つけてくれたな、朔屋よ」
source.english:
“…A wreck?
Found us another damn nuisance, have you, Sakuya?”

source.japanese:
……朔屋が持ってさえ、御婦人物のように瀟洒な望遠鏡は、水夫長の手の中では妖精の玩具のように壊れやすく見えたが、彼の扱い自体はさすがに堂に入った物で、青年より手早く焦点を合わせて件の難破船の状況を検分して、どうにも微妙な目の色を浮かべた。
　水夫長から望遠鏡を受け取ったが、クロがしきりに貸して欲しい様子なので、少女に渡してから、水夫長に問いかける。
source.english:
Elegant as a lady's accessory even in Sakuya's hand, the telescope looked fragile as a fairy's toy in the boatswain's. But his handling was assured. He focused faster than the young man, examined the wreck, and looked distinctly uncertain what to make of it.
Sakuya took it back, then passed it to Kuro, who plainly wanted a turn, before questioning him.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……A shipwreck you say? So you've found yourself another round of trouble for us, Sakuya.」

……The telescope, which already looked like the sort of elegant and refined article befitting a lady when in Sakuya's hands, looked as fragile as a fairy's toy in the Bosun's meaty paws, but his manner of handling it was just as expert as one would expect; he brought the telescope into focus quicker than the young man, then inspected the state of the aforementioned shipwreck, an unmistakably conflicted look in his eyes. The Bosun returned his telescope to him, but Kuro seemed awfully eager to borrow it, so after handing it over to the young girl, he then asked the Bosun a question.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「厄介て……」
source.english: “A nuisance…?”

source.japanese: 難破船は、信天翁号の右の舷側、四時半ほどの方角、距離は三ケーブルばかり。海流か風向きか、ゆらゆらとゆっくりとだが遠ざかりあり、このまま見過ごしにするか調査してみるかの判断も早めにつけずばなるまいが、水夫長は観たところ気乗り薄なのが朔屋にはどうにも信じがたい。こういう場合、唐草模様の風呂敷かついで手拭いほっかむり、一番名乗りで喜び勇んで乗りこんで、根こそぎかっぱいできそうな手合いではないか。
source.english: The wreck lay about three cables off the Albatross’s starboard side, at roughly the four-thirty bearing. Current or wind was carrying it slowly farther away, so they would have to decide soon whether to let it pass or investigate. Yet the boatswain’s evident reluctance was simply beyond Sakuya. Wasn’t he precisely the sort to knot a towel over his head, sling an arabesque-patterned burglar’s bundle over his shoulder, rush aboard ahead of everyone, and gleefully strip the place bare?

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「When you say trouble……」

The shipwreck floated off the starboard side of the Albatross at a bearing just shy of four-thirty o'clock, roughly three cables away. Maybe it was the ocean currents or the wind at work, for while it was slow and swaying, it was still drifting away from them, and they would need to decide soon whether to turn a blind eye to it or investigate it further, but the Bosun was, as far as he could tell, not very enthusiastic about the whole thing, something Sakuya struggled to believe.

In a situation like this, he'd be slinging a furoshiki adorned with a traditional karakusa pattern over his shoulder, covering his head by tying a hand towel around it, and be the first to volunteer to rush over and board the ship in high spirits, snatching everything he could find; was that not the sort of man he was? (TN: A furoshiki, written "風呂敷", is a Japanese wrapping cloth used for many things, and ones with an arabesque vine pattern, known as the karakusa pattern in Japan, are used all the time in stereotypical depictions of thieves, where they use it as a sack to carry away their stolen goods in.)

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「もし生きとるもんがあったら、助けてやらんとあかんからな。ところがこちらは北上中と来る」
source.english: “If anyone's alive, we've got to rescue them. Trouble is, we're heading north.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「If there's anybody still alive on there, we'll have to save them, that's what. And wouldn't you know it, we're right in the middle of heading north.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「こっから先は大きな港にゃ寄らねぇ。色々と面倒なんだよ」
source.english: “No big ports from here on. Makes things a pain.”

source.japanese: さすがの信天翁号も、漂流者は無条件で助けるという、最低限の海の倫理だけには従っているらしい。
source.english: Apparently even the Albatross observed that bare minimum of maritime ethics: rescue castaways without conditions.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「望遠鏡でざっと見た限りだと、生存者は見えなかったようですぜ」
source.english: “Didn't see any survivors in a quick look through the telescope.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「From here on out, we're not putting in at any major ports. It's trouble in a lot of ways.」
Even a ship like the Albatross seemed to adhere to the bare minimum of seafaring ethics: rescuing castaways unconditionally.
【Naomasa】 「Far as I could tell from a brief look through the telescope, there didn't seem to be any survivors.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「むぅ……生きてるもんがないなら、それは逆に歓迎なんだが……船内で動けなくなっとるのかも知れんし……」
source.english: “Mmm… If nobody's alive, that's good news, actually… But some might be trapped inside, unable to move…”

source.japanese: 水夫長の目が、金目のモノを漁る喜びへの期待と、生存者救助の手間との間で揺れ動いているところに口を挟んできたのが航海士達だった。先ほど物見櫓から転がり落ちたダメージから回復したようだが、朔屋は二人が何気なく臀を庇っているのを見てとった。
source.english: His eyes wavered between the prospect of valuables to plunder and the bother of survivors to rescue. The navigators interrupted. They seemed recovered from their fall beneath the lookout, though Sakuya noticed how discreetly each protected her backside.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Mmh……if there's nobody alive, then that'd actually be welcome news, but……there might be somebody trapped somewhere inside the ship, unable to move……」

As the Bosun's eyes flickered, torn between the thrill of hunting for valuables and the hassle of rescuing survivors, it was the mates who interjected. It seemed like they'd recovered from whatever damage they'd sustained after tumbling down from the watchtower earlier, but Sakuya did notice how the two of them were innocently shielding their butts.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ま、乗りこむだけ乗りこんでみようよ。
　あたしらは今、手ぇ空いてるし」
source.english:
“Well, let's at least go aboard.
We've got nothing to do right now.”

source.japanese: と、こちらは乗り気のご様子。舷側から背伸びで難破船の様子を、一生懸命に眺めているクロの、襟首を摘[つま]んで軽々持ち上げ、自分へと向かせれば、白子の少女は猫の、それもあんまり鼠をとらない奴のようにだらんと手足を伸ばした、その片手には朔屋の望遠鏡。水夫長の次に借りていたクロだが、望遠鏡、朔屋本人より大活躍である。
source.english: They, at least, seemed willing. Kuro stood on tiptoe at the side, straining to see the wreck. Sisam pinched her collar, lifted her easily, turned her around. The albino girl dangled like a cat, and not a particularly good mouser at that, Sakuya's telescope in one hand. She had borrowed it after the boatswain. The telescope was getting far more use than its owner.

source.japanese: ただシサムは別段クロから望遠鏡を取りあげようというのではなく、仕掛けたのが例のしりとりだ。
source.english: But Sisam was not after the telescope. Instead, she began the usual word chain.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Come on, let's at least board her and see what comes of it. We've got plenty of time on our hands right now.」

So she said, and they certainly seemed enthusiastic about it. When she grabbed Kuro, who was standing on tiptoes and leaning out over the gunwale, giving her all to get a good look at the state of the shipwreck, by the collar and easily lifted her into the air, then turned her around so they faced each other, the albino girl splayed her limbs out languidly like a cat, and one that didn't seem to catch too many mice at that, and in one of her hands was Sakuya's telescope. It had been borrowed by Kuro after the Bosun had his turn, but the telescope was proving far more useful than Sakuya himself.
But without seeming particularly inclined to confiscate the telescope from Kuro, Shisamu instead challenged her to the usual game of shiritori.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「クロ、しりとり。
『板切れ』」
source.english:
“Kuro, word chain.
‘Board.’”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Kuro, shiritori. 『Scrap wood(Itakire)』

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「しりとり……板切れ……。わかった。
『れんこん』！」
source.english:
“Word chain… Board… Got it.
‘Daikon’!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Shiritori……scrap wood……. Got it. 『Lotus root(Renkon)』!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「はい、嵐とかもないようだし。
　あたしらがいってくるよ。
　あとは……朔屋とクロもおいで」
source.english:
“Right. No storms or anything,
apparently. We'll go over.
Sakuya, Kuro, you come too.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Alright, doesn't seem like we're hitting a storm or anything. We're going over and taking a look. And……Sakuya and Kuro, you two come with us.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え、俺も？　……まあ、なんか運び出さなきゃなんなくなった時の荷物運びかなんかだろうが、クロはまたどうして」
source.english: “Huh, me too? Well… Probably to carry things if we find anything worth taking out. But why Kuro?”

source.japanese: こういう状況だと、どうしても事の枠外に置かれがちな新前朔屋、声がかかったのには少しく意外で、だが自分はまだそう、労働要因として数えられる事もあろうが、クロまで、ともなると少女には失礼だが一体なんの用に使うつもりか見当もつかない。
source.english: Being a newcomer, Sakuya tended to be left out of affairs like this, so the summons surprised him. He could understand counting himself as an extra pair of hands. But Kuro? No offense to the girl, yet he could not imagine what use they meant to make of her.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Huh, me too? ……Well, I guess if we end up needing to carry stuff out, I can do that or whatever, but then what are you bringing Kuro for?」

In situations like these, the greenhorn Sakuya ever found himself sidelined, so it was a bit surprising that he'd be called out to, but, well, he could probably be counted as a pair of hands for manual labour or other errands, but even Kuro was included, and while it was very rude to the girl, he just couldn't think of whatever it was they wanted her for.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「難船とかだとさ、くたばったあとでもお宝惜しんで、狭苦しいところに隠す奴もあんのよ」
source.english: “On a wreck, some people can't bear to part with their treasure even after they're dead. They'll hide it in the tightest little places.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「With shipwrecks, you get these guys who love their precious treasure so much, they'll stuff it into some cramped little hole, clinging to it even after they croak.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そういう隙間に潜[もぐ]らせるにゃ、クロが一番だ」
source.english: “Kuro's best for crawling into those gaps.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「引っかかって出てこらんなくなったら、
　どうすんだよ」
source.english:
“And if she gets stuck and can't
get out?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And when it comes to crawling into little cracks like those, Kuro's our best bet.」
【Naomasa】 「But what if she gets stuck and can't get out again, what will you do then?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「大丈夫、腰に綱つけとくから、引っぱればいい」
source.english: “No problem. Tie a rope round her waist and pull.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（腰からちぎれんじゃないのかそれ……）
source.english: (Won't that tear her in half…?)

source.japanese: 言いながら、早速にシサムが引っぱり出した麻の綱の輪に、クロの痩せた裸体が菱の目、亀甲と色々に愉快に縛られている姿を想像しては振り払う朔屋で、ともかく、やはりクロがそういうぞんざいな扱いなのが、むしろ納得されてしまうあたり、気の毒に思われてくるが、クロ自身は一つのお仕事として了解しているようで、さっさと短艇の方で待機だ。
source.english: As Sisam spoke, she promptly produced a loop of hemp rope. Sakuya pictured Kuro's thin, naked body merrily bound in diamond-lattice and turtle-shell patterns, then banished the image. That such rough treatment seemed so natural for Kuro only made him pity her more. Kuro herself apparently accepted it as just another job; she had already gone to wait by the boat.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「It's fine, we're tying a rope around her waist, so we just have to pull on that.」
【Naomasa】 （Won't you just rip her in half if you do that……）

When he saw Shisamu promptly pull out a loop of hemp rope while speaking, Sakuya found himself imagining Kuro's skinny body naked and tied up in a variety of amusing patterns, like the diamond lattice, the tortoiseshell, and so on, but he shook off the stream of images; in any case, the fact that Kuro was being treated so offhandedly conversely only made it easier for him to accept it in the end, and while he did feel pity for her, it seemed that Kuro herself had acknowledged it as just another job, the girl already waiting by the boat.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……妙だぞ、あの船。
　人の臭いがしてこねえ」
source.english:
“…Something's odd about that ship.
No human smell coming from it.”

source.japanese: ……下級水夫達がえっちらおっちら短艇を降ろし始めた段になって、智里がこれである。難破船を眺めて智里は、不審げに眼を細めたが、そう言う事はもう少し早めに告げればよかろうと、朔屋の答えはつい適当になった。
source.english: Only once the junior sailors had begun laboriously lowering the boat did Tomosato say this. He narrowed his eyes suspiciously at the wreck. Sakuya thought he might have mentioned it a little sooner, and answered with careless flippancy.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ってことは、乗員全滅か。
　水夫長等が喜ぶだろうぜ。
　金目のモノでもありゃなおさらな」
source.english:
“So the whole crew's dead.
That'll make the boatswain and company happy.
Even more if there's something valuable.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Something's off about that ship. It doesn't smell of human.」

……Just as the deck boys began heaving and hauling to lower the boat, Tomosato appeared. Staring at the shipwreck, Tomosato narrowed his eyes suspiciously, but thinking to himself that this sort of thing ought to have been mentioned a little earlier, Sakuya's response ended up being rather half-hearted.
【Naomasa】 「So you're saying that the crew's been wiped out? That'll make the Bosun and the rest happy, I imagine. All the more so if there's anything valuable on board.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そういうんじゃねえよ。お宝はどうだか知らんが、人の臭いが感じられんのだという。
　生きてるのも死んでるのも」
source.english:
“Not what I mean. Don't know about treasure. I'm saying there's no human smell.
Living or dead.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「全滅にしたって、死骸の一つや二つは転がっていそうなものだぜ。そういう臭いもないんだよ」
source.english: “Even if everyone died, you'd expect a corpse or two lying around. No smell of that either.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんたは犬かなんかかい」
source.english: “What are you, a dog?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「That's not what I'm saying. I don't know anything about treasure, but I can't pick up any human smell. Neither from the living nor the dead.」
【Tomosato】 「If they were all "wiped out", there should be a corpse or two lying around somewhere. There's not even the smell of that.」
【Naomasa】 「Are you a dog or something?」

source.japanese:
つい軽く言い返したものの───
　智里が感じ取っているのものは、現実の、いわゆる腐臭や血臭などではなく、人間の死の気配の、人を幾多斬り殺してきたであろう殺し屋ならではの感覚なのではないかと覚って朔屋はにわかに嘘寒い心地に見舞われる。
source.english:
The flippant answer slipped out.
But then it struck Sakuya: what Tomosato sensed might not be any actual odor of blood or decay, but the presence of human death—a sense particular to a killer who had presumably cut down any number of people. Abruptly he felt a hollow chill.

source.japanese: 日頃酒を酌み交わす相手の手が、血に濡れたものである事を、今更ながらに思い知る形ではあるが、見れば見るほどこの智里という男、「殺し屋」という言葉がもたらす実感が遠くなるのが不思議なところ。人を惨殺するところも刀身に殺気を満たすところも見たはずなのに、難破船を眺めて、海と同じ色の眸[ひとみ]を細めているところは、殺し屋、というよりは───見当もつかない。どういう事をやって生きてきたのかさっぱり見当もつかない。
source.english: It brought home to him, belatedly, that his usual drinking companion's hands were stained with blood. Yet oddly, the more he looked at Tomosato, the less palpable the word ‘killer’ became. He had seen the man slaughter people, seen his blade fill with killing intent. But now, narrowing sea-colored eyes at the wreck, he looked less like a killer than—Sakuya could not guess. Could not begin to guess what he had done, how he had lived.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……なんだよ、人の顔をじろじろと。
　直公、先に言っておくが、お前はあまり、
　難しいこたぁこちゃこちゃ考えんなよ」
source.english:
“…What? Staring at my face.
I'll tell you now, Nao:
don't go getting yourself tangled up in complicated thoughts.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……よかった。男色がどうのとか、
　そういうありきたりな台詞が、
　あんたから出てこなくてさ」
source.english:
“…Thank God.
Thought you'd give me some stock line about
wanting men or something.”

target.text: He had blurted out that flippant retort, but─── Was it not possible that what Tomosato was sensing was not real smells, that is to say, not the stench of decay or blood, but the very presence of human death, a sense he could have come to possess as a murderer who had likely cut down myriad people; as that dawned on him, a sudden, uncanny chill washed over Sakuya.

It was perhaps a belated realization, that the hands of this man he would regularly share drinks with were stained in rivers of blood, but it was a strange thing; the more he observed this man, Tomosato, the further he seemed to drift from the reality the word「Murderer」carried. In spite of how he had personally witnessed him massacre people, and how his blade itself was saturated with a lust for blood, as the man gazed at the shipwreck, his eyes that shared their colour with the ocean itself narrowing, he was less murderer and more─── he couldn't think of anything. He hadn't the faintest idea what kind of life he'd lived.

【Tomosato】 「……What's with you staring at my face like that? Nao-kou, I'm warning you right now, don't go overthinking all the complicated stuff.」 (TN: The nickname he uses here is "直公", read Nao-kou, It is an honorific that, in classical Japanese, evokes a sense of formality and deferential reverence based on its historical use for feudal lords, equivalent to "lord" in English. During late Edo, the urban men began adopting the language previously used by the upper class, and it became a mix of affectionate and slightly patronizing. Think something like "Good sir Nao".)
【Naomasa】 「……Thank god. I'm so glad I didn't have to suffer some stale line like "are you gay?" or something coming out of your mouth.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「なんだっていいが、どうにも辛気くせえな。
　こりゃああれか───メアリ・セレ……」
source.english:
“Whatever. Something's depressing about
this. Maybe it's that—the Mary Cele…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Whatever it is, this thing's real gloomy, huh. Could it be that─── The Mary Cele……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋ぁ！　さっさと来いってばぁ。
　あんたも櫂[オール]を漕ぐんだよ」
source.english:
“Sakuya! Get over here already!
You're rowing too!”

source.japanese: 智里の台詞、キサラの焦れったげに急かす声に途中で遮[さえぎ]られて、朔屋も慌てて短艇の降ろし方へ駆け足で手伝いに廻る───
source.english: Kisara's impatient call cut Tomosato short. Sakuya hurried over to help lower the boat—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Sakuyaaa! Get your butt over here already! You're also grabbing an oar!」
Tomosato's line was interrupted partway by Kisara's impatient, rushing voice and so Sakuya also hurried to the boat in a fluster, helping to lower it───

source.japanese: 洋上漂うその船、船長三〇米[メートル]程度の貨物船だったが、乗りこむにあたって、巧妙に隠れ潜[ひそ]んでいた賊からの伏撃といった障害もなく、鉤付きの縄梯子を投げかけるのに少々手間取ったくらい、それとて双子が面倒くさがって朔屋にやらせたせいなのだが、ともかく捜索メンバーは容易に船内に入りこんだ訳だが、朔屋、何処やら拍子抜けの感を味わっていた。が、戦闘に巻きこまれるよりは平穏が一番とすぐに思い直す。
source.english: The drifting vessel was a freighter about thirty meters long. No bandits cleverly concealed aboard lay in ambush. The only difficulty was throwing up the hooked rope ladder, and that only because the twins were too lazy and made Sakuya do it. Thus the search party boarded easily. Sakuya felt a little let down, but promptly reconsidered: peace was better than getting caught in a fight.

source.japanese: 漕いできた短艇を舷側の索具に舫綱でしっかり繋いで、見回す上甲板の様相も中層甲板の通路の見た目も、いくらかは荒涼としていたが、実に穏やかなもので、朔屋はかえって居心地の悪さを覚えたほどだった。漂流している船、と見なしてからは、内部はさぞ荒れているだろう、浸水もあって潮に腐った臭いや腐朽した積み荷が漂っているだろうと、無意識に独り決めしていた節がある。
source.english: They made the boat fast to the rigging along the ship’s side with the painter. The upper deck and the passages of the middle deck looked somewhat desolate, but perfectly tranquil—so tranquil that Sakuya found it unsettling. Once he had decided to think of her as a ship adrift, he seemed to have taken it for granted that she would be a ruin within: taking on water, the reek of salt-rotted things in the air, decaying cargo floating about.

source.japanese:
それなのにこの船、貨物と少数の客を運ぶ商船と思しきこの船と来たら、状態だけ見れば信天翁号よりよほど立派だった。否、雲泥の差があった。
　そもそも信天翁号に匹敵するような襤褸船が浮いて漂流していられるはずがないと想像も及ばないあたり、朔屋も随分とあの愉快な船に染まりつつある。
source.english:
Yet this ship, apparently a merchant vessel carrying freight and a few passengers, was in far better condition than the Albatross. No, there was a world of difference.
It never occurred to him that a ship as decrepit as the Albatross could scarcely remain afloat and drifting in the first place. Sakuya was becoming thoroughly accustomed to that merry vessel.

source.japanese:
だが、立派な見た目に驚いたのも移乗した始めのうちだけ、朔屋は、そして一行は、次第に胡散臭げな眼差しを四囲に放るようになった。
　船室の扉を確かめれば、鍵も掛かっておらず、ドアノブも錆にやや軋んだ程度で素直に開く、が、その奥に人影はない。
　一つの船室だけでなく、覗いてみた船室全てが同じ塩梅で、遂にシサムが口にした言葉は、言葉にこそ差違有れど、皆に共通した思いだったろう。
source.english:
Their surprise at its fine appearance lasted only through the first moments aboard. Gradually Sakuya, and the rest, began looking about with suspicion.
Cabin doors were unlocked. Knobs squeaked a little with rust but turned readily. No one waited behind them.
Every cabin they tried was the same. At last Sisam spoke a thought they all must have shared, however differently they might have phrased it.

target.text: The ship floating on the sea was a cargo vessel approximately thirty metres in length, but when they boarded it, there were no hindrances like bandits who had cleverly hid themselves to lie in wait for them; at worst, it took a little longer than expected to toss up the rope ladder with the hook attached, but that might have been because the twins found it too bothersome and made Sakuya do it; regardless, the members of the search team thus easily made it inside the ship, although Sakuya, for some reason, felt oddly let down. He quickly thought better of it, however, reminding himself that peace and calm was far better than being dragged into battle.

They made the rowboat fast to the ship's side-rigging with a sturdy mooring line, and looking around, while both the state of the upper deck and the appearance of the 'tween-deck passageway were rather dreary, it was actually quite tranquil, to the point it even left Sakuya feeling uncomfortable. Having deemed it a ship adrift, the inside would surely be dilapidated, there would also be flooding, and the smell of cargo rotting in the seawater would hang in the air; he seemed to unconsciously have taken that for granted.

And yet when it came to this vessel, which seemed to be a merchant ship that would transport cargo and a small number of passengers, based on what he could see of its condition alone, it was more impressive than the Albatross by far. Yea, it was like comparing the heavens to the earth. The fact that it didn't once cross his mind that it should never even have been possible for a ship dilapidated enough to rival the Albatross to remain floating while adrift was evidence of how Sakuya was quickly taking on the colours of that whimsical ship.

However, his surprise at its impressive appearance lasted only during the initial moments after boarding, for Sakuya, as well as the rest of the party, gradually began to look at their surroundings with suspicion in their eyes.

When they checked the doors to the cabins, they were unlocked, opening easily with only a bit of creaking from the hinges and some rust on the doorknobs, but there were no signs of people inside. And it wasn't just one cabin; every single cabin they looked within were in the same state, and the words that Shisamu finally uttered, though there might have been differences in their exact choice of them, was surely a feeling they all shared.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんか、変だよこの船……」
source.english: “Something's wrong with this ship…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「There's something strange about this ship……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「全滅なら全滅でいいよ。病気とか、餓死とか、原因は色々あるだろうし」
source.english: “Everyone dead, that's one thing. Disease, starvation—plenty of possible reasons.”

source.japanese:
何度目かの船室の確認を行ってから、航海士の双子はとうとう足を止めて通路の壁により掛かる。
　船室も、通路の来し方、そして伸びている先に目を凝らしても、人影や動くものの気配はなく、なのに船内には今までのところ、智里の言った通り遺骸や、何か争ったような跡もない。
　これらの状況を、奇妙と受け取る程度の頭もないクロは別として、他の三人はこの船がどこかおかしいと決めつけるに至っていた。
source.english:
After inspecting another cabin, the twin navigators finally stopped and leaned against the passage wall.
In the cabins, behind them and farther down the passage, there was no one, no hint of movement. Yet, as Tomosato had said, so far they had found neither bodies nor evidence of a struggle.
Apart from Kuro, who lacked even the sense to find this strange, all three had concluded that something was wrong with the ship.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If they were wiped out, so be it. Could be disease, starvation, there are plenty of possible causes.」

After checking many a cabin, the twin mates finally came to a halt and leaned against the wall of the passageway. Be it the cabins or the part of the passageway they'd already passed through, even should they strain their eyes in the direction that still lay ahead of them, there were no signs of any human presence or movement, and yet, in all the places they'd looked through so far, just as Tomosato had said, there were neither bodies nor traces of any sort of conflict. With this being the situation, setting aside Kuro, who didn't even have the brains needed to interpret this as being weird, the remaining three had arrived at the conclusion that something about this ship was wrong.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「朔屋知ってる？　乗員全滅の原因ね、変わり種のだと、船員同士がラリってトチ狂って、最後の一人になるまで殺し合って、そして残ったのは自殺したっていう」
source.english: “Ever hear one of the stranger stories of how a whole crew died, Sakuya? They all got high and went mad, killed each other till there was only one left. Then he killed himself.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだその壮絶な顛末は」
source.english: “What the hell kind of ending is that?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Did you know, Sakuya? Out of the many reasons why a whole crew would die, one of the more bizarre cases is that the whole crew got high out of their minds, went raving mad, started slaughtering each other down to the last man, and then that final survivor took his own life.」
【Naomasa】 「Damn, what a grisly way for things to end.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「小麦粉がばい菌に汚染されてたんだけど、その菌ってのがさ、幻覚剤に使われるのと同じ成分を含んでてね」
source.english: “Their flour was contaminated with germs. And those germs contained the same stuff they use in hallucinogens.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「The flour had been contaminated with a fungus, but this particular fungus, see, turns out it contains the same compound found in hallucinogens.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「それで焼いたパン、乗員のほとんどが食べちゃったんでもう最後よ」
source.english: “Most of the crew ate bread baked with it. That was the end of them.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「By the time most of the crew had eaten the bread baked with that flour, it was already over.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「毒のパン、おっかないよ……クロなんだか、パンが食べれなくなる、そうな感じ……」
source.english: “Poison bread, scary… Kuro feels like… maybe she can't eat bread anymore…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「んー、クロがラリラリになったところで大して怖くもないような」
source.english: “Hmm. Kuro off her head wouldn't be all that scary.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Poison bread, that's scary…… feels like Kuro, kind of, might not be able to eat bread anymore……」
【Naomasa】 「Hmm, I don't think it'd be that scary if Kuro started tripping out.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんただって人の事言えるかい。四六時中ラリってるみたいな面してさ」
source.english: “You're one to talk. You look off your head twenty-four hours a day.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひ、ひどい」
source.english: “C-cruel.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Look who's talking! You look like you're stoned around the clock.」
【Naomasa】 「Wh-, that's mean!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「とにかく、幻覚パンの話は話としても、それだって血の跡とか死体とか残るでしょうよ。
　でもこの船はそれさえない」
source.english:
“Anyway, hallucinogenic bread is one thing. Even that would leave bloodstains and bodies.
This ship doesn't have those either.”

source.japanese: 今まで見てきた限り、ではあり、もしや船内のどこか他には、惨劇の跡、とまではいかずとも船員失踪の秘密を物語るような痕跡あるかもよ、と双子は内壁から身を起こし、また歩き出したが、その足取りは長靴なのにもかかわらず、妙なくらい跫音が殺されて、二人が警戒態勢にある事を示している。
source.english: So far, at least. Perhaps elsewhere aboard there might be traces—not necessarily of a massacre, but traces that could explain the crew's disappearance. The twins pushed away from the wall and set off again. Despite their boots, their footsteps were strangely quiet: they were on guard.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Anyway, hallucinogenic bread or not, there'd still be bloodstains or bodies left behind, right? But this ship doesn't even have that.」

Based on what they'd seen so far, yes, but perhaps somewhere else on board, there might be traces that, while not necessarily evidence of a bloody tragedy, could still shed light on the mystery behind the crew's disappearance; with that belief in their hearts, the twins pushed off the wall and started to walk again, but despite wearing boots, their footfalls were strangely muffled, suggesting that the two were in a state of high alert.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なにがあったってわけ？
　皆してお魚と恋仲にでもなって、
　仲良く海にでも飛びこんだ？」
source.english:
“So what happened?
Everybody fell in love with fish
and jumped into the sea together?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「So what the hell happened? Did they all fall head over heels for the fish, then went diving into the ocean hand-in-hand?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「それとも翼が生えてくるとかいう奇病にでも罹って、みんなでお空に飛んでった？」
source.english: “Or caught some weird disease that grows wings, and all flew off into the sky?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Or perhaps they were afflicted with an odd disease that made them grow wings, and then they all flew off into the heavens?」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やあ、シサムはロマンティストだなあ。
　……っがっ、痛ぇ、痛いってばよっ」
source.english:
“Well, Sisam. What a romantic you are… Gah!
Ow, ow, I said!”

source.japanese: 人の尻穴に指を突っこんで、上になって好き放題に精汁を搾[しぼ]りとりにかかる女にしては可愛らしい幻想でないかと、つい口にしてしまった軽口は、シサムが無造作に差し延べてそしてぞんざいに、ただ孔が開きそうなほどの剛力でこめかみを締めあげてきたのに封じられた。
source.english: Rather charming fantasies for a woman who stuck her finger in a man's asshole, got on top and milked him dry, weren't they? The quip had escaped before he knew it. Sisam silenced it by reaching out casually and squeezing his temples with enough careless force to bore holes.

source.japanese: 二度・三度朔屋を片手で振り回しつつ見回す周囲の、シサムは通路中に他より大きめの出入り口を見かけ、朔屋を引きずったまま中を窺えば、船内食堂の、油や香辛料の匂いがまだ微かに染みついてある。
source.english: Swinging Sakuya about one-handed two or three times as she looked around, Sisam noticed a larger doorway in the passage. She peered inside, still dragging him. It was the ship's dining room; faint smells of grease and spices lingered.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Wow, you're such a romantic, Shisamu. ……Gah, that hurts, I said that hurts!」

He just though that, for women who'd stick their fingers up another person's asshole, then crawl on top of them and milk them dry of their semen until they were satisfied, that was a rather adorable little fantasy, but his careless quip was quickly cut short when Shisamu casually reached out and roughly clamped down on his temples, squeezing with brute force so intense it felt as if she might bore a hole right through his head.

As Shisamu scanned her surroundings, swinging Sakuya around with one hand a couple of times as she turned, she caught sight of a doorway in the passageway larger than the rest, and when she peeked inside, dragging Sakuya with her all the while, it turned out to be the ship's mess, the air still filled with a faint, ingrained smell of oil and spices.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でもそうとでも言わなきゃ説明もつかない。
　……いや、そんな突拍子もない話でも、
　説明しきれない……見てよ、これ」
source.english:
“But without something like that, there's no explaining it…
No,
even a wild story like that wouldn't explain all this. Look.”

source.japanese: 難破船の食堂の、卓上には配膳されたまま皿の、埃を被っているのが、船内の無人の気配と合わさりより荒廃した感を強める。漂流して以来時化にも遭わなかったのか、卓上で皿は大して乱れた様子もなく、元は料理だったと思しき残滓がそのまま乾涸らびて、どうやら配膳直後の様子を残しているようだった。
source.english: In the wreck's dining room, plates sat where they had been served. Their dust, together with the deserted air of the ship, deepened the sense of abandonment. Perhaps no storm had struck since it began drifting; the plates were scarcely disturbed. Remains of what had once been food had simply dried up, as though preserving the moment just after the meal was served.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「これ、食べてる途中だったみたい。
　ってことは、乗員が一斉に示し合わせてなにかやった、とかじゃなくって───」
source.english:
“Looks as if they were halfway through eating.
Which means the crew didn't all plan something together—”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「いつものようになにかしてた時に、なにかがいきなり起こって、それで皆がいなくなった……。そんな状況だったんじゃないかな」
source.english: “They were doing something ordinary when something suddenly happened, and then they all disappeared… Something like that, maybe.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「But there's no way to explain it otherwise. ……No, even with something that absurd, this still can't be explained……just look at this.」

The plates still set on the table in the mess of the shipwreck were covered with dust, but when combined with the pervasive emptiness of the ship, it only heightened the feeling of desolation. Had she just never encountered any stormy seas since she became adrift, for the plates on the table showed little sign of disarray, and the dried-up remnants of what was presumably once part of a meal looked as though they had been left just as they were the moment the meal was laid out.
【Kisara】 「This looks like they were in the middle of eating. Which means, it wasn't like the crew all planned something beforehand and left together───」
【Kisara】 「While they were going about their usual routines, something suddenly happened, and then they all disappeared……. It must have been something like that, I guess?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「その何かってな、何よ」
source.english: “What's the something?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But this "something", what is it?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それが判りゃあ苦労はしないっての」
source.english: “If I knew, we wouldn't have a problem.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If I knew that much, I wouldn't be racking my brains over it.」

source.japanese: 能無しのくせしてこういう時には皆が評定している時には一家言挟みたがる朔屋がこれまで大人しくなにも言わずにいたのは、いまだシサムに顔面を掴まれたまま引きずられてきていたからだが、いい加減持ち疲れたと見えて、ぽいと無造作に投げ捨てられては床にバウンド、机の脚に側頭部を撲[う]ちつけて頭を押さえて転がり回った。
source.english: Useless though he was, Sakuya ordinarily liked to contribute an opinion whenever everyone deliberated. He had been quiet only because Sisam still had him by the face and was dragging him along. Apparently tired of carrying him at last, she casually tossed him aside. He bounced on the floor, struck the side of his head against a table leg, and rolled about clutching it.

target.text: The fact that Sakuya, a man who usually loves to chime in with his two pennies' worth whenever everyone else is deliberating despite being an incompetent dimwit, had stayed quiet as a lamb and refrained from interjecting was because, even now, he was still held in Shisamu's tight grip while she dragged him along, but she looked to have grown tired of carrying him around, for she carelessly tossed him aside, sending him bouncing off the floor; he slammed the temporal region of his head against a table leg, then proceeded to roll around on the floor while cradling his head in his hands.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うーっ、うーっ、ようやく離してくれたかと思えばこれかようっ、シサム、もそっとこう、その、優しく……」
source.english: “Uhh, uhh… You finally let go, and that's what I get? Sisam, couldn't you be a little, you know… gentler…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Uuh, uugh, just when I thought you were finally letting me go, now this happens. Shisamu, can't you be a little more, you know, gentle……」

source.japanese: ひとしきり呻[うめ]いて、後はけろりと立ち上がる辺り、随分と打たれ強さが鍛えられてきて、シサムの指の跡が残るこめかみを揉み散らしながら、先ほどの双子の会話の後を引き続けた、あんな風に顔面鷲掴みにされても話を聞いてはいたらしい。
source.english: He groaned for a while, then stood up as though nothing had happened. His capacity for taking a beating had improved considerably. Rubbing the finger marks on his temples, he returned to the twins' conversation. Apparently he had been listening even with his face gripped like that.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なにか、突発事が起こったとかじゃなくってさ、もう一つあるぞ」
source.english: “There's another possibility—something besides a sudden accident.”

source.japanese: 朔屋のくせになにか理論でもあるのかと大して期待した様子もなく、食堂内をあれこれ窺いながらの聞き流しにする双子に、青年が開陳した推測というのは、さて───
source.english: A theory, from Sakuya? Without much expectation, the twins listened idly while looking about the dining room. The young man offered the following conjecture—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「つまり、だ。誰かを……この場合は俺達だが、こうやって悩ませる為に、この状況を仕組んで、みんなで失踪した、
　ってのはどうだ？」
source.english:
“See, what if they set all this up to puzzle somebody—in this case us—and then everyone
disappeared?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「別の船に乗り移るとか、あるいは短艇に分乗してとか」
source.english: “Transferred to another ship. Or split up among the boats.”

source.japanese: ……双子は何時しか捜索の手を止めて、食堂の長机のそれぞれ左右の端に腰かけて、背中合わせに身を捻って朔屋の話に聞きいった左右対称の体勢は、どこかの騎士家の紋章じみていたが、聞くだけ聞いて、二人とも感心すればいいのかどうなのか、苦悩に額まで押さえて見せた事である。
source.english: At some point the twins had stopped searching and sat at opposite ends of a long dining table, twisting back to back to hear him. Their symmetrical posture resembled the coat of arms of some knightly house. They heard him out, then both pressed hands to their foreheads in anguish, uncertain whether to be impressed.

target.text: After groaning in agony for a while, he sprang back up like nothing happened, proof that he had grown remarkably resilient to being hit, and while rubbing his temples where Shisamu's fingers had left their mark, he continued on from the twins' earlier conversation; it seemed that, even with his face being clutched that tightly, he had somehow managed to not miss a word of it.
【Naomasa】 「It's not that something had to suddenly happen, or anything like that. There's still another possibility.」

The twins, not having any particularly great expectations from someone like Sakuya presenting something resembling a theory, let his words go in one ear and out the other while continuing to look around the messroom; as for this hypothesis unveiled by the young man, well now───
【Naomasa】 「So, basically. Someone…… well, in this case, us, was meant to be baffled by all this. That's why they staged all this, then vanished. How about that?」
【Naomasa】 「They could have transferred to another ship, or perhaps they split up and sailed off in several smaller boats, something like that.」

……At some point, the twins had ceased their searching, sitting their respective butts on the left and right side of the end of the long table in the messroom, back to back, twisting their bodies as they listened intently to Sakuya, their symmetrical posture resembling the heraldic supporters of a coat of arms belonging to some knightly house, but while they were certainly listening, unsure of whether or not they should be impressed by what they heard, they both clutched their foreheads in an apparent display of anguish.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まずい……朔屋のいつもの馬鹿なのに、ついうっかりそれもありかも、とか思っちゃったよあたし」
source.english: “Oh, hell… It's Sakuya's usual stupidity, and for a second I thought it might actually be possible.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Oh no……this is just Sakuya being his usual idiot self, but against my better judgment, I've actually ended up thinking it might be possible.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたしも……いやいや待て待て、落ち着こうあたし」
source.english: “Me too… No, no, wait. Calm down. Get a grip.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「さすがにいつ発見されるかも判らないような海のただ中に、いつ来るかも判らない誰かをおちょくる為に、船まるごと捨ててく馬鹿がいたら、そいつは朔屋以上の超級馬鹿だ」
source.english: “A fool who'd abandon a whole ship in the middle of the sea just to mess with someone who might or might not come along, God knows when, is a higher order of fool than Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひどい……」
source.english: “Cruel…”

source.japanese:
やがて、誰ともなく口にした。
　船内の状況が、ある海難事件と酷似していたのである。
　海難事件史上最大の謎と称されている、それは───
source.english:
Eventually someone gave it voice.
The state of the ship closely resembled a certain maritime incident,
called the greatest mystery in the history of disasters at sea. It was—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Me too……no no no, wait, wait, get a grip, girl!」

【Shisamu】 「If there was an idiot who actually ditched an entire ship right in the middle of the ocean, where nobody could know when or if it would ever be found, just to mess with some random person who might show up at some unknowable point in time, then that person is a top-tier idiot who'd make even Sakuya look smart.」
【Naomasa】 「That's mean……」

Eventually, someone brought it up. How the situation on this ship bore an uncanny resemblance to a certain incident at sea. What is said to be the greatest enigma in the history of shipwrecks, namely───

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ねえ、これってやっぱり……」
source.english: “Hey. Isn't this, after all…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Hey, this has to be……」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんたが何考えてるのか、俺にも判るよ。
　こりゃあ、あれだ……あれとそっくりだ」
source.english:
“I know what you're thinking.
It's that… Just like that.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「I can also tell what you're thinking. This has to be that…… it's the spitting image of it.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「『メアリ・セレステ号』事件───」
source.english: “The Mary Celeste incident—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「The mystery of the Mary Celeste───」

source.japanese: 『メアリ・セレステ号』事件。船は手つかずなのに、乗員だけ消えていた謎の事件。
source.english: The Mary Celeste incident: the mystery of a ship found untouched, its crew simply vanished.

source.japanese: この船も『メアリ・セレステ号』同様、全長三〇米[メートル]余り、三〇〇頓級のこぢんまりとした商船であったが、これまで一行が探ってみた限りでは、船内の状況が『メアリ・セレステ号』と酷似しているとしか言いようがなかった。
source.english: Like the Mary Celeste, this was a small merchant ship a little over thirty meters long and of the three-hundred-ton class. Everything they had seen so far looked uncannily like the famous case.

target.text: The mystery of the Mary Celeste. An enigmatic incident, the ship left entirely untouched with only the crew missing.

Just like the Mary Celeste, this ship's length overall was a little above thirty metres, and it was also a modest merchant ship of the compact 300-ton class; from what the group had investigated so far, the situation on board this ship could only be described as eerily similar to that of the Mary Celeste.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そんなけったいな事件が二度も起こってたまるか、って言いたいところだけど」
source.english: “I'd like to say there's no way a freakish thing like that could happen twice.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「There's no way in hell an incident that bizarre could happen twice, is what I'd love to say.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「これだけ状況が同じだとね……」
source.english: “But when everything's this much alike…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やっぱり、俺の説が有力なんじゃないの？
　有名な事件の真似して、発見者をびっくりさせたかったとか」
source.english:
“Doesn't that make my theory more likely?
They copied a famous case to surprise whoever found them.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But with the circumstances being this similar……」
【Naomasa】 「See, don't you think my theory is plausible after all? Imitating a famous mystery, trying to spook whoever discovers it, something like that?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「だーかーら。船一隻。無駄にして。しかも別に壊れてるわけじゃない。この不景気な世の中で、そんな阿呆がいたら、あたしが全財産身ぐるみはいでくれるわい」
source.english: “Like. I. Said. Wasting a whole ship. One that isn't even broken. In this lousy economy. If there's a fool like that, I'll strip him of everything he owns.”

source.japanese: 三人額突き合わせての雁首評定どうにも歯切れの悪し、弾を撃ってきたり光り物で刺してきたりの相手ならそれこそ鼻歌まじりで撃破する双子でも、なにもない、と言うのが奇怪な事象に関しては手を拱[こまね]く、朔屋はそもそも数に入らない、の三人の頭上に景気悪く立ち籠めた迷妄の暗雲を分けて差しこんできた光とは。白かった。赤かった。クロだった。
source.english:
The three put their heads together, but their council went nowhere. The twins could dispatch gunmen or blade-wielding attackers with a tune on their lips; confronted with a mystery whose whole substance was that nothing was there, even they stood helpless. Sakuya did not count to begin with.
Then a ray of light broke through the cheerless cloud of perplexity above them. It was white. It was red. It was Kuro.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Like I said. Wasting. A. Whole. Ship. And it's not like it's even wrecked or anything. In this lousy economy? If there really is an idiot like that out there, I will personally strip them of every last coin they own.」

Three heads huddled in council, forehead against forehead, and yet no progress was made; even the twins, who'd fiercely crush any who stood in their path with gunfire or gleaming blades of steel while humming a tune, could, when the strangeness of this phenomenon arose from the very absence of anything at all, do nothing but fold their arms helplessly, completely stumped, and Sakuya never counted for anything to begin with; what beam of light could possibly break through the gloomy clouds of folly looming over the trio's heads? It was white. It was red. It was Kuro.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……じゃあ。ここ、何か残っている？　かも。アメちゃんとかないかなぁ」
source.english: “…Then. Is there anything left here? Maybe. Wonder if there's candy.”

source.japanese: 食堂に残ったあれこれの、そんなところをひっくり返してもさすがになにも出てこないだろうに、目につくような灰皿などをひっくり返しながらのクロだった。大人達が考えこむ余りに放置されて、退屈だったと見える。
source.english: She rummaged among the dining room's leftovers. Surely nothing would emerge from places like that, yet Kuro turned over whatever caught her eye, even ashtrays. Abandoned while the adults thought too hard, she had apparently grown bored.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Then. Something left behind here? Maybe. Wonder if there's candies.」

Even though it was obvious that nothing would come of turning over and rummaging through the odds and ends left in the messroom, Kuro still went ahead and did it anyway, flipping over whatever seemed to catch her eye, like ashtrays. She'd been neglected for too long while the adults brooded and pondered, and she seemed to have grown bored as a result.

source.japanese: 本人は全く気づいていないだろう、無知の知が輝くようなクロの一言で、シサムとキサラはあ、と顔を見合わせ、そして朔屋もおお、と得心して膝を叩いたあたり、彼もやはり信天翁号の流儀に染まりつつあるという事か。
source.english: Kuro herself likely never realized it, but at her remark, shining with the wisdom of knowing nothing, Sisam and Kisara looked at one another: ah. Sakuya, too, slapped his knee in understanding. Perhaps he really was absorbing the Albatross's ways.

source.japanese:
そもそも彼らは、難破船の謎に鳩首並べて実にもならない評議を開く為に波乗り越えて短艇漕いできたわけではない。
　無人の難破船に遭遇した、無頼の船乗りとしての当然の権利を行使する為にやってきたのであり、いかなる理由で船が漂流するに至ったか、また船内の人気が失せたのかなど、明らかになろうがなるまいが目的には一向に関係無いではないか。
source.english:
They had not rowed over the waves to put their heads together in fruitless debate about a wreck's mysteries.
They had come to exercise the natural right of outlaw sailors encountering an abandoned ship. Whether anyone learned why it had drifted here or why the people aboard had vanished made no difference whatever to their purpose.

target.text: The girl herself probably didn't notice, but upon hearing the words Kuro uttered, almost dazzlingly bright with the wisdom of the ignorant, Shisamu and Kisara looked each other in the eyes with a short "ah"; given that Sakuya also let out an "ooh" and slapped his knee in realization, it really did seem he was starting to become influenced by the ways of the Albatross.

To begin with, they hadn't braved the waves in a rowboat just to huddle together and hold a fruitless discussion on the enigma of this shipwreck. They had come here to exercise their rightful claim as rogue sailors who'd come across a derelict wreck adrift with not a soul aboard, and whatever course of events this ship may have been set adrift through, as well as whatever was to blame for the sudden disappearance of the crew, whether any of it ever came to light or not, that really had no bearing whatsoever on their purpose at hand, did it?

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まさか、クロに教えられる日が来るたぁ、
　考えてもなかったのことよ」
source.english:
“Never thought I'd live to be taught
a lesson by Kuro.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「クロは賢いなぁ……」
source.english: “Kuro's so clever…”

source.japanese: 朔屋がご褒美に頭を撫でてやろうとした横合いから、かっさらってクロを胸に抱き入れたキサラは、馬鹿がうつるからと青年が触れようとした辺りを大仰に払って見せている辺り、扱いがどこまでもひどい。
source.english: Sakuya reached to pat her head in reward. Kisara snatched Kuro sideways into her arms, then ostentatiously brushed off the spot his hand had nearly touched, saying stupidity was contagious. They really did treat Sakuya abominably at every turn.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「To think the day would come when I'd be taught something by Kuro, the thought never so much as crossed my mind.」
【Naomasa】 「You're so smart, Kuro……」

Just as Sakuya made to pat Kuro on the head as a reward, Kisara snatched her away and cradled Kuro against her chest, and she made a big show of exaggeratedly brushing aside the young man when he tried touching her, as if to say he would infect Kuro with his idiocy; truly, their treatment of him was cruel in every respect.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「朔屋なんかよりよっぽどね……そうだよ。
　別に乗り組みがどうなったかなんざ、
　あたしらには便所紙よりどうでもいい事だった」
source.english:
“A lot cleverer than Sakuya…
That's right.
What happened to the crew mattered less to us than toilet paper.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Much more intelligent than someone like Sakuya……that's right. It doesn't really matter what happened to the crew, that's worth less to us than toilet paper.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……え？　……え？
　クロは先生、違うよ。船長。
　だから教えるとか、違うもの」
source.english:
“…Huh? …Huh?
Kuro's not a teacher. Captain.
Teaching's different, so…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Eh? ……Eh? Kuro isn't teacher. Is captain. So teaching and stuff isn't right.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「いいや。クロってば言ったろ？
　何か残ってないか、
　アメちゃんとかないかって」
source.english:
“No, you said it, Kuro.
Anything left?
Any candy?”

source.japanese: いつだって縺[もつ]れ加減のクロの白い髪を、撫でつけてやったりなぞしているシサムとキサラの指先は、茶の革手袋をつけてはいてもやはり女の手つきで、そういうしおらしい事をさせても中々に映える。娘同士の割り込めない親しさが漂って、朔屋君はちょっとばかりつまらない心持ちを覚える。
source.english: Sisam and Kisara stroked down Kuro's perpetually tangled white hair. Even in brown leather gloves, their fingers had a woman's touch, and such gentleness suited them surprisingly well. An intimacy among girls, with no place for him to intrude, hung about them. Mr. Sakuya felt a little left out.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Nope. Kuro, you just said it, right? That something might be left behind here, wondering if there's any candies around.」

Though the fingertips that Shisamu and Kisara were using to stroke and comb through Kuro's ever-tangled white hair were clad in brown leather gloves, they still worked with a woman's touch, and even when doing something so sweet and demure, it actually suited them surprisingly well. An intimacy between fellow girls that could not be intruded upon hung in the air, and poor Sakuya-kun began to feel just a little bit left out.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そうそう。あたしらそもそも、船員が全滅してたら、金目のモノかっぱごうって、それで乗りこんだったんだ」
source.english: “Right. We came aboard to steal anything valuable if the whole crew was dead.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「いなくなりてぇ奴は勝手に消えてりゃいい。
　何があったにしても、
　あたしらには関係無い」
source.english:
“If they want to disappear, let 'em.
Whatever happened,
it's nothing to do with us.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Right, right. We figured that if the crew had been wiped out, we'd swipe anything shiny we could find, that's why we even bothered boarding this ship at all.」
【Kisara】 「Anybody who wants to disappear can go ahead and vanish for all I care. Whatever might have happened, it's got nothing to do with us.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「よし、残りの区画も、
　手分けして探してみよう。
　あたしとシサム、クロと朔屋ね」
source.english:
“All right,
split up and search the rest.
Me and Sisam. Kuro and Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ええ、どうしてえ？
　そっちのどっちか、
　俺と一緒でもいいじゃないの。
　せっかく二人きりになれるってのに……」
source.english:
“Whaaat,
why?
One of you could go with me.
A chance to be alone together…”

source.japanese: 双子が揃っていないと、あの酒場の二階での凄まじいほどの快楽には届かないかも知れないが、それでもどちらかとだけでもイイ事ができたなら、それはとってもイイ事ではないか、と朔屋は弄[もてあそ]んでいた匙を放り投げて、食い下がっては見たけれど。
source.english: Without both twins, perhaps he would not reach the staggering pleasure of that room above the bar. Still, even something nice with one alone would be very nice indeed. Sakuya tossed aside the spoon he had been fiddling with and tried to insist.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Alright, let's split up and search the remaining compartments. Me with Shisamu, Kuro with Sakuya, okay?」
【Naomasa】 「Aww, but why? Can't we just have one of you two come with me? We'd finally get a chance to be alone, just the two of us……」

While he might never be able to reach a pleasure as tremendous as what he experienced back on the second floor of that bar without doing both twins at once, if he could still have a good time with even just one of them, then wouldn't that also make for an absolutely wonderful adventure; so Sakuya thought, tossing aside the spoon he'd been fiddling with, looking as though he'd dug his heels in, but.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「下心まるみえだっつーの。
　それに忘れたか、あたしら二人、
　下手に引き離して置くとどうなるか」
source.english:
“Your motives couldn't be more obvious.
And have you forgotten
what happens when you leave us two separated?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ごもっとも。そういやそうだった。
　そういう事なら従うさ。
　ほら、行こうクロ」
source.english:
“…Fair point. Right, I'd forgotten.
If that's how it is, I'll do as I'm told.
Come on, Kuro.”

source.japanese: 拳足で打撃と共に叩きこむのではなく、珍しく理詰めで言い聞かせるシサムの、その理は朔屋にも納得せられ、なるほどそうなると双子は双子で、朔屋はクロと組む他無い。
source.english: For once Sisam persuaded him with reason instead of driving her point home with fists or feet. Even Sakuya could accept that logic. The twins must stay together, and he must pair with Kuro.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「You're not even trying to hide what you're really after. Besides, have you forgotten? What happens if the two of us are carelessly kept apart?」
【Naomasa】 「……Point taken. Now that you mention it, that is true. In that case, I'll yield. Come on, let's go, Kuro.」

Rather than hammering it into him with a bit of help from her fists and feet, in a rare turn of events, Shisamu had instead persuaded him through reasoning, and that logic was sound enough to convince even Sakuya; indeed, with that being the case, there was no other choice for their groupings than the twins going together and Sakuya going with Kuro.

source.japanese:
かくしてクロと朔屋、そしてシサムとキサラで船内の残りの区画の探索に赴いた訳だが。
　───ひとしきり探し回ってみても、大して金目のモノはない。財布がいくつかあったが、その程度の、ただ朔屋は始めからとくに期待もしていなかったので、あまり落胆はせず、それはクロも同様らしく、「なんにもないね」と虚ろ笑いが二人どちらからともなく無人の船室の虚ろな宙に流した。まあ、幸運というのは自分達以外の誰かにしか降らないもの、との諦観を共通させた事が収穫といえたか。
source.english:
Thus Kuro and Sakuya, Sisam and Kisara, set off to search the remaining sections.
After a thorough search, they found little worth stealing. A few purses, no more. Sakuya had expected little from the outset, so was hardly disappointed; Kuro appeared to feel the same. “Nothing here,” one of them said with a hollow laugh, the words drifting through the hollow air of an empty cabin. Perhaps the one thing they had gained was a shared resignation: luck only ever fell upon somebody else.

source.japanese:
ただ、船倉に降りていってみたところ、四角い出入り口の奥には、何やらごたごたと嵩張り積まれた荷があって、ほとんど飽きていた心を浮き立たせた。
　のだが、やはり二人はどこまでも幸運に恵まれていない事がすぐに明らかになる。
source.english:
Down in the hold, however, a bulky jumble of cargo lay piled beyond the square doorway.
Their interest, nearly spent, stirred at the sight—only for it to become clear once again just how completely fortune had forsaken them.

target.text: Thus, Kuro and Sakuya, along with Shisamu and Kisara, embarked on their search of the ship's remaining compartments, but. ───Though they searched high and low for a good while, they didn't find anything all that valuable. There were several wallets, but that was about it; Sakuya, however, was not really expecting anything special to begin with, so he wasn't that crestfallen, and Kuro seemed to have a similar mindset as well; "there's nothing here at all, huh", one of them muttered with a hollow smile, the words drifting through the empty air of the deserted cabin, not seeming to originate from either of them in particular.
Well, perhaps the one thing they'd found was a shared resignation: Good fortune only ever smiles on others.

However, when they tried descending into the hold, the sight of a jumble of bulky cargo piled beyond the square entrance stirred their thoroughly weary hearts back to life. That it did, but it quickly became clear that, in the end, the two of them were ever forsaken by Lady Luck.

source.japanese:
船倉の奥は暗く、恐らくはここも他の船室、区画と同様無人だろうとは予想されても、暗がりは人の足を本能的に押し留めさせる。
　クロも船倉内にはすぐに踏みこもうとはせず、出入り口の戸柱にすがりつき、鼻先だけを暗がりへと向けて、ひくひくと空気を嗅ぐ仕草に、閉じこめられていた籠の蓋をいきなり開け放たれた白鼠と同じ、入るか逃げるかの差はあれ、戸惑いの色浮かばせる。
source.english:
The back of the hold was dark. It was probably deserted like every other cabin and compartment, but darkness checks the feet by instinct.
Kuro, too, made no move to step inside. She clung to the doorpost and poked only the tip of her nose into the gloom, twitching as she sniffed the air, with the same bewildered look as a white mouse whose cage lid has suddenly been thrown open—save that Kuro was wondering whether to enter, and the mouse whether to flee.

target.text: The back of the hold was dark, and though he expected it to most likely be deserted like any of the other cabins or compartments, darkness instinctively makes man stop in his tracks. Kuro also didn't immediately try to venture inside the hold, instead clinging to the jamb of the entrance, only the tip of her nose facing the darkness, twitching as if sniffing the air, just like a white mouse whose cage lid is abruptly flung open; whether it chooses to step beyond its bounds or retreat back inside, there is still that same look of bewilderment on its face.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……なんか、によいがする」
source.english: “…Something smewls.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「におい、な。こりゃアルコールの臭いか。
　積んでるものまで『メアリ・セレステ号』と同じかい」
source.english:
“Smells. Alcohol, is it?
Even the cargo's the same as the Mary Celeste's?”

source.japanese: アルコールの臭いを嗅ぎ分ける事に関しては、朔屋、人並み以上の嗅覚を示して、倉庫内に積まれた荷の輪郭をアルコールの樽だと見てとった。混じり気のない、ただ酒精だけの匂いからして、恐らくは工業用のアルコールだろう。
source.english: When it came to detecting alcohol, Sakuya displayed a better-than-average nose. He recognized the piled shapes within as barrels of alcohol. From the unmixed smell of pure spirit, it was probably industrial alcohol.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Kind of smells of something.」
【Naomasa】 「Smell, you say. Isn't this the smell of alcohol? So it's even loaded with the same cargo as the Mary Celeste, huh?」

When it came to distinguishing between the different smells of alcohol, Sakuya demonstrated an olfactory sense well above the average, and he'd also noticed that the contour of the cargo stashed within the hold was that of barrels of alcohol. Judging by the pure, undiluted scent of nothing but ethanol, this was, in all likelihood, industrial alcohol.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「おく、暗いくて、よく見える、ないね。
　ええと───あ。ランプ」
source.english:
“Dark in the back, can't…
see well. Um—ah. Lamp.”

source.japanese: 船倉は入り口から奥は余りよく見えなかったけれど、戸口の傍に角燈と燐寸が置いてあって、
source.english: They could see little of the hold from the entrance, but a lantern and matches stood beside the door.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Back is so dark, can't really, see too well, right? Uuhhm───ah. A lamp.」
One couldn't see too far into the hold from the entrance, but there was an oil lantern and some matches that had been left by the door,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「点けると、中、もっとよく見えるから、点けるといいよ。クロが点けたげる───」
source.english: “Light it, then we can see inside better. Should light it. Kuro'll do it—”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「If lit, should be able to see inside better, so should light. Kuro will light it───」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょぉーっと待ったぁぁぁ！」
source.english: “Waaaaait a minute!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「HOOOOOLD IT RIGHT THERE!」

source.japanese: アルコールの揮発した空気の中で火を点けるなど自殺行為の、そもそもアルコールを積んだ船倉に火の気を置いていくなど、この船に乗りこんでいたのは紛れもなく馬鹿。
source.english: Lighting a flame in air full of alcohol vapor was suicide. In the first place, anyone who left a source of fire in a hold full of alcohol was an unmistakable idiot.

target.text: Doing something like lighting a flame in air filled with alcohol vapour was nothing short of an act of suicide, and the fact that they'd even left a source of fire in a hold loaded with alcohol meant that the crew on board this ship were genuine idiots.

source.japanese: 朔屋にはしては珍しく俊敏にクロに飛びかかり、突き飛ばしてしまったところ、
source.english: With rare speed for Sakuya, he lunged at Kuro and shoved her aside—

source.japanese: 腰の横を支点にくの字なり、軽きに過ぎる体重が仇となり、横様に吹っ飛んで、戸口に脇腹を打ちつけては弾き返される、とすんとまた軽い音でぶっ倒れて床に白い髪をうねらせて、数秒悶えていたものの、かくん、と、力が失せた。
source.english: She folded at the waist. Her all-too-light weight betrayed her: she flew sideways, struck her flank against the doorway, bounced back. With another light thud she fell, white hair spilling over the floor. She writhed a few seconds, then went abruptly limp.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あっ。クロ、まずい、力の加減を間違った。
　いいところに入っちまった。
　おいクロ、しっかりしろ」
source.english:
“Ah. Kuro, shit, I pushed too hard.
Got you right in the wrong spot.
Hey, Kuro. Stay with me.”

source.japanese:
罪悪感にかられ抱き起こしたクロはあっけなく失神していた。
　なお、樽のアルコールは保管が悪かったのか大半が揮発し、金にはならなさそうだった。
source.english:
Guiltily, he lifted Kuro in his arms. She had fainted with alarming ease.
Incidentally, perhaps because of poor storage, most of the alcohol in the barrels had evaporated. They were unlikely to fetch much.

target.text: With uncharacteristic agility, Sakuya threw himself at Kuro and sent her flying, and that moment,
【Kuro】 「GWEH───!?」

With the side of her waist as the fulcrum, she bent over in the shape of a chevron; being too light in weight became her downfall, and she was sent flying sideways, slammed her flank into the door, bounced off it, then collapsed to the floor with a light thud, the waves of her white hair undulating; she writhed in agony for some seconds, but then, with a sudden jerk, went limp.
【Naomasa】 「Ah. Kuro, oh no, I misjudged my strength. Must have hit a vital spot by mistake. Oi, Kuro, stay with me!」

Driven by guilt, he lifted Kuro up in his arms, only to find she had already fainted all too easily. Furthermore, the barrels of alcohol must have been stored improperly, for the majority of the alcohol had volatilized, and it didn't really seem like what was left would be worth any money.

source.japanese: 船倉にも大したものは見つからず、手分けした区画を一通り探し終えて中層甲板に上がってきた朔屋とクロは、シサムとキサラの様子はどうかと見て回るうちに二人を見出した船室は、他よりはやや広く、執務机やキャビネットなども整えられた、どうやら船長室らしい。
source.english: Having found little in the hold and finished their assigned search, Sakuya and Kuro returned to the middle deck to see how Sisam and Kisara had fared. They found the twins in a cabin slightly larger than the others, furnished with a desk and cabinets. It appeared to be the captain's cabin.

source.japanese: さすが船の中で一番金目の物がありそうな部屋を探し当てる、と朔屋は双子の嗅覚を賞賛しつつ部屋に入ったが、二人の様子が妙だ。つかず離れずくっついているのはいつものことだが、なのにどこか心ここにあらずといったような。
source.english: Of course they had sniffed out the room most likely to contain valuables, Sakuya thought admiringly as he entered. But something was odd about the twins. Their close proximity was usual enough. Yet somehow their minds seemed elsewhere.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……シサム？　キサラ？
　どうしたんだ、なんだかぼうっとしているようだが。こっちは一通り見てきたぜ」
source.english:
“…Sisam? Kisara?
What's up? You look kind of dazed. We've looked through our bit.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「財布がいくつかあったけど、大して中味は入っちゃいない。拾わないよりはましだけど」
source.english: “Found a few purses, but not much in them. Better than nothing.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あとは船倉にアルコールの樽が積んであったが、そっちは駄目だ。あらかた揮発してやがる。あんなものはわざわざ持ち出す事もないと思うが」
source.english: “And there are barrels of alcohol in the hold, but they're no good. Most of it's evaporated. Don't think it's worth carrying that stuff out.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───あの、聞いててくれました？」
source.english: “—Um, were you listening?”

source.japanese: このような小振りの貨物船でも船長室ともあればそれなりに美々しく整えられた調度も、無人の空気が侘びしい景色に変えてしまっている中で、双子は本来ならその零れんばかりの精気で室内に荒っぽいながらも華やぎと言っていい空気を与えるはずなのに、この時二人は、船窓から海の様子を眺めてぼんやり、執務机に目をくれるともなく視線を落としてぼんやり、とどうにも精彩を欠き、朔屋の話も聞いていたのかいないのか。
source.english: Even aboard a small freighter, the captain's cabin boasted fine furnishings; the deserted air had turned them into a forlorn sight. Ordinarily the twins' overflowing vitality would have lent the room a rough-edged brilliance. Now one gazed vaguely out at the sea, the other vaguely down toward the desk, both strangely subdued. Had they heard Sakuya or not?

target.text: They had not found anything of significance in the hold either, and having finished searching the sections they'd been assigned, Sakuya and Kuro went back up to the 'tween deck; while looking around to see how things were going for Shisamu and Kisara, the cabin they eventually found them in was a bit more spacious than the others, furnished with things like a writing bureau and a cabinet, and it seemed to be the captain's cabin.

Trust the twins to track down the room that seemed most like to contain anything of value on this ship, Sakuya thought, admiring the twins' nose for treasure while entering the room, but the two were acting strange. The way they stood near each other, neither too close nor too far, was nothing out of the ordinary, and yet something about them made it feel to him as if they were there in body but not in spirit.
【Naomasa】 「……Shisamu? Kisara? What's wrong, you two look a little out of it. We're done looking through our portion.」
【Naomasa】 「We found several wallets, but the contents were nothing worth mentioning. Not great, but better than just leaving them to rot.」

【Naomasa】 「Aside from those, there are barrels of alcohol stacked down in the hold, but those are no good. Almost entirely evaporated. I don't think there's any point going out of our way to carry something like that back to the ship.」
【Naomasa】 「───Uhm, are you listening to me?」

Even on a modest cargo ship like this, the captain's quarters were still well-appointed with tasteful splendour, but the deserted atmosphere had transformed even that to a desolate scene, and though the twins should normally fill the room with an atmosphere wild yet undeniably bright just by virtue of their inherent vitality that seemed to burst out from them, in this moment, the two were in a daze, looking out at the ocean through the porthole, absentmindedly lowering their gazes without sparing the writing bureau so much as a glance, sullen and lacking their usual lustre, and one could wonder whether they'd even been listening to Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あ、ふぇ……っ。
　聞いてた。うん、聞いてた」
source.english:
“Ah, huh… I heard you.
Yeah. I was listening.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Ah, bwuh……. I was listening. Yeah, I heard you.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「財布と、樽コールでしょ？」
source.english: “Purses and barrelcohol, right?”

source.japanese: 答えも、どうにも一拍遅れていたし、目を上げて初めてそこに朔屋とクロが戻ってきていたのに気づいたように瞬きなぞしている有り様で。
source.english: The answers came a beat late. They raised their eyes and blinked as though only now noticing Sakuya and Kuro had returned.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それは冗談なのか言い間違えなのか……。
　で、そっちは？」
source.english:
“Was that a joke or a slip of the tongue…?
Anyway, how'd you do?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Wallets and, uh, barrelcohol, right?」
Their replies were also a beat too slow, and they even blinked away as if only just realizing upon looking up that Sakuya and Kuro had returned.
【Naomasa】 「Was that supposed to be some kind of joke or was it just a slip of the tongue……. So, how did things go on your end?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ああ、あたしたちのほうも、
　めぼしいもんはなんもなかった。
　どうにも無駄足だったね」
source.english:
“Oh,
nothing worth taking on our side either.
Wasted trip, really.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Right, we didn't really, find anything notable either. Seems like we went on a fool's errand here, huh?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そうそう。
　あとはこの船の船長の日記くらいかな」
source.english:
“Right.
Just this captain's diary, I guess.”

source.japanese:
……執務机に乗せられた大判の、船に置くのに相応しい、簡素ながらも質の佳い丈夫そうな紙を用いた帳面には朔屋も入った時から気づいていたのだけれど、双子に断りもなく触れるとどやされそうな気がして、敢えて手を出さずにいたのだけれど。
　聞けばどう考えても重要な物品証拠、なのにシサムの口ぶりはどうにも投げ遣りな、それが朔屋にもどうにも不審な。
source.english:
Sakuya had noticed the large notebook on the desk when he entered: plain but made of fine, sturdy paper suitable for a ship. He had deliberately refrained from touching it, suspecting a scolding if he did so without the twins' leave.
But surely it was an important piece of evidence. Sisam's strangely indifferent tone struck even Sakuya as suspicious.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「くらいかなって……。
　それ、わりと重要でないの」
source.english:
“Just, I guess…?
Isn't that pretty important?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「何が起こったのかの、手がかりになるかも知れないだろ？」
source.english: “Might give us a clue what happened.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Yeah, yeah. Beyond that, there's just the captain's logbook, I guess.」

……Sakuya had been aware of its presence from the moment he stepped foot in the cabin; there was a large foolscap logbook resting on the bureau, made with simply yet fine, sturdy paper well-suited for use on a ship, but he felt like he'd be yelled at by the twins if he touched it without getting their permission first, so he had purposely refrained from laying a hand on it. Upon hearing it described, this was a crucial piece of physical evidence by any measure, and yet Shisamu's tone of voice was strangely dismissive, and that made Sakuya very suspicious in turn.
【Naomasa】 「Just that, you guess……. Isn't that relatively important?」
【Naomasa】 「I mean, it could hold a very important clue for figuring out what happened here, right?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「どうかなぁ～。
　ほら、これじゃあねえ……」
source.english:
“Who knoows?
Look. Like this…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Who can say～. Look, not like this it won't……」

source.japanese: シサムがひらひら見せると、ノートは後半部が破り去られており、なるほど、これでは事件を解く鍵にはなりそうにない。
source.english: Sisam fluttered the notebook before him. Its latter half had been torn away. In that state, it was hardly likely to furnish the key to the mystery.

target.text: When Shisamu fluttered the pages open to show him, it turned out the latter half of the logbook had been torn out; indeed, in this state, it wasn't likely to hold the key to solving this case.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「残ってる部分も、
　大した事は書いてなかった。
　読めるんなら読んでもいいけど、
　退屈だよ？」
source.english:
“Nothing much
in the part that's left,
either.
Read it if you can, but it's boring.”

source.japanese: 英文の記述は、ざっと目を通したところ確かに淡々とした退屈な内容で、朔屋はすぐに興味を失ったけれど、破り去られる直前の頁に、走り書きされていたのがこの一文である。
source.english: The entries were in English. A quick glance confirmed their dry, dull content, and Sakuya soon lost interest. But on the page just before the torn section, this sentence had been scrawled:

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And there's nothing that interesting written in the remaining half. If you want to, you can go ahead and read it, but it's pretty boring, you know?」

As he quickly glanced over the accounts written in English, certainly, the contents were tediously dry, and Sakuya quickly lost any interest in them, but on the final page just before the rest had been torn out, there was a hastily scribbled sentence.

source.japanese:
『我妻マリアが───
　セント・エルモの火が───』
source.english:
‘My wife Maria—
St. Elmo's fire—’

target.text: 『My wife Maria is─── St. Elmo's fire is───』

source.japanese: 読み下して、朔屋の片眉が呆れ加減に撓[しな]い、口元も歪んで、顔を上げればシサムもキサラも似たり寄ったりの貌[かお]、三人共にここでも思いを同じくしていた。
source.english: Reading it, Sakuya raised an eyebrow in exasperation, twisted his mouth, then looked up. Sisam and Kisara wore much the same expressions. Once again all three shared a thought.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あのさあ、くどくて申し訳ないんだが、
　やっぱりこれ、模倣犯の仕業じゃないか？
　この日記まで『メアリ・セレステ号』のパクリだろこれ」
source.english:
“…Look, sorry to keep saying it,
but isn't this a copycat's work?
Even the diary's ripped off from the Mary Celeste incident.”

target.text: When he was done reading, one of Sakuya's eyebrows was arched in mild exasperation, a wry twist pulling at his lips; when he looked up, Shisamu and Kisara wore similar expressions, and all three of them shared the same thought here as well.
【Naomasa】 「……Now look, I'm sorry for sounding like a broken record, but seriously, this has to be the work of some copycat, right? Even this log is cribbed from the Mary Celeste!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……かもね。馬鹿な金持ちってのが、本当にいただけ……。
　否定できなくなってきたかな」
source.english:
“…Maybe. Just means there really was an idiot with money…
Getting harder to rule out.”

source.japanese: 双子はいかにも胡散臭そうに肩を竦め、朔屋の言葉に一応の賛意まで示して見せたけれど、心から信じこんでいるのではないのは明白の、どうせ俺[おい]らの言葉なぞ、たとえ当たってたってまともにゃ聞いちゃもらえんだろ、と少しばかり拗[す]ね加減の朔屋、船長の日誌をなんとのう手悪戯しているうちに、ふと気づいた。
source.english: The twins shrugged dubiously and even made a show of agreeing. Clearly they did not truly believe him. Nobody ever takes what I say seriously, even if I'm right, Sakuya thought, a little sulkily. Idly fiddling with the captain's journal, he suddenly noticed something.

source.japanese: 朔屋にしては目聡い、と言うべきの、帳面の後半、破り去られたその辺り。双子は発見した時には既にこうだったと言わんばかりの口ぶりだったが、そこには悔しげな色が感じられなかった。それにこうして眺めてみるとその破れ目が、妙に新しい、紙の他の部分に比べても埃に褪せた様子もなく白い。
source.english: It was a sharp observation, by Sakuya's standards. The back half of the notebook had been torn away. The twins spoke as though it had already been like that when they found it, yet showed none of the frustration one might expect. And now that he looked closely, the torn edge was suspiciously fresh: white, unlike the dusty, faded rest of the paper.

source.japanese:
不審に、帳面から双子に目線をあげても、二人は朔屋の凝視に気づいた風もなく……なのだろうか、気づいてなお意に介した風もない様子を取ったのではないだろうか。
　ただ朔屋がそれを言い出した物かどうか迷っているうちにクロが、口元に手を開けて大欠伸の、三人が余り構ってくれないのに退屈と眠気を催したらしい。
source.english:
Suspicious now, he raised his eyes from the notebook to the twins. Neither seemed aware of his stare… Or were they? Had they noticed and simply chosen to look indifferent?
While Sakuya wondered whether to raise the matter, Kuro yawned hugely behind her open hand. Ignored by all three, she had evidently grown bored and sleepy.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……Could be. That somewhere out there, there really is some fool with the money to burn……. I don't think I can outright deny the possibility anymore.」

Shrugging their shoulders in an awfully suspicious manner, the twins did offer some sort of tentative agreement with Sakuya's words, but it was glaringly obvious that they didn't believe it from the heart; besides, if it was coming from him, then even should he be right, they were probably not going to seriously listen to him, Sakuya thought with a small pout, and while he was idly fiddling with the captain's logbook, he happened to notice it.

It was remarkably perceptive for Sakuya, one might say, noticing that spot in the latter half of the logbook where the paper had been torn out. The twins had certainly spoken in a manner heavily implying that it had already been torn off by the time they discovered it, but they did not betray even a hint of disappointment when saying it. Furthermore, now that he observed it closer, the tear itself seemed strangely fresh; even compared to the rest of the paper, it was white, showing no signs of being dulled beneath a layer of dust.

Though he looked up from the logbook to the twins, a gleam of suspicion in his eyes, the two showed no sign of having noticed how he stared at them…… or perhaps they did, but even after noticing, they still deliberately maintained an air of indifference? But while Sakuya vacillated between broaching the topic or not, Kuro covered her mouth with her hand while letting out a big yawn; she had apparently grown both bored and sleepy because the other three didn't pay her enough attention.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まあ、他にはめぼしいモノはないようだし、諦めてウチらの船に戻ろっか」
source.english: “Well, doesn't seem there's anything else worth taking. Let's give up and go back to our ship.”

source.japanese:
クロの退屈を潮にと、キサラはぱん、と一つ手を鳴らして探索のお終いを提案したが、朔屋にはやはりどうにも割りきれないものを遺した。
　日記に残された言葉のうち、その言葉だけが原典の事件には無く、差違を示してはいないか。
source.english:
Taking Kuro's boredom as her cue, Kisara clapped once and proposed an end to the search. But Sakuya was left with something he could not dismiss.
Of the words remaining in the diary, wasn't “St. Elmo's fire” the one phrase absent from the original incident? Might it not mark a difference?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しかしこの『セント・エルモの灯』ってのはなんなんだろうな。いやもちろん聞き覚えくらいはあるよ」
source.english: “But what do you make of this ‘St. Elmo's fire’? I mean, sure, I've heard of it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「雨とか嵐の夜に、マストに灯るって言う人魂みたいな奴だ……でも、たったその一言だけじゃなあ、意味不明だよ」
source.english: “Those ghostly lights they say appear on masts on rainy or stormy nights… But just those words? Can't tell what it means.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Well, there doesn't seem to be anything worth grabbing here, so why don't we just give up and go back to our ship?」

Using Kuro's boredom as a convenient excuse, with a sharp, decisive clap of her hands, Kisara suggested ending their exploration here, but in the end, it left something with Sakuya that he simply could not make his peace with. Of the words recorded in that logbook, only those particular words were never present anywhere in the log from the original mystery, and didn't that indicate a discrepancy?
【Naomasa】 「But still, I wonder what this 『St. Elmo's fire』thing is about. I mean, I've heard about it before, of course.」
【Naomasa】 「They say it's like a hitodama, a floating ball of fire that lights up on the mast on rainy or stormy nights……but, that one sentence alone just doesn't make any sense.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そう。結局何があったのかは……よく判らない。
　もしも続きが残ってたなら、話は違ったかもしれないけど」
source.english:
“Right. In the end, we don't really know what happened.
If the rest were still there, maybe it'd be different.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Right. In the end, whatever it is that happened here……we still don't really know. If the rest of the logbook was still here, maybe it would have been a different story.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なくなってんだから、
　どうしようもないよ」
source.english:
“It's gone.
Nothing we can do.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But it's gone, so there's nothing we can do.」

source.japanese:
それで船長室を出て、船をそのままに捨ておき、信天翁号へ戻る事になったのだが、朔屋の胸にふと疑念が残る。
　もしや日記は……双子が朔屋達が部屋に入る寸前に、破ったのではなかろうか、と。
source.english:
So they left the captain's cabin, abandoned the ship as it was, and headed back to the Albatross.
Still, one suspicion lingered with Sakuya: had the twins themselves torn those pages out just before he and Kuro entered?

target.text: And with that, they left the captain's quarters, abandoned the ship to its fate, and returned to the Albatross, but a sudden flicker of doubt lingered in Sakuya's bosom. Had the twins……perhaps torn up that logbook right before Sakuya and Kuro stepped into the cabin?

source.english: —The dead of night.

source.japanese: ……酒の肴を狙っての、朔屋の食料庫暴きが常習化するにつれ、発覚した時の懲罰が厳しくなるのは当然ではあるが、毎回毎回三途の河原まで観世音菩薩さま達の踊るラインダンスを見物に行かされたのでは、いつ帰ってこられなくなるか知れたものでない。
source.english: …As Sakuya's raids upon the stores for drinking snacks became habitual, the punishment when caught naturally grew harsher. But if every single time he was sent to the banks of the Sanzu River to watch the venerable bodhisattva Kannon and company doing a line dance, who knew when he might fail to return?

source.japanese: 流石の朔屋も学習して、多少の肴なら自給自足する術を覚えた。釣り糸を長くして、舷側から垂らせば、天然自然のお恵みがある。朔屋などをこの世に生み落としてここまで生かしてきた事からして、世界というのは非常なる温情家であり、その上肴まで寄越すとなれば、もう大抵の人間は阿呆みたいに口半開きに笑いながらでも人生を謳歌していかれそうなものだが、まあそれは閑却。
source.english: Even Sakuya learned. He acquired a means of supplying a few snacks himself: lengthen a fishing line, drop it over the side, and nature bestowed her gifts.
