A world that had brought such a creature as Sakuya into being and kept him alive this long was merciful indeed. Add free snacks, and most people ought to be able to enjoy life smiling foolishly with their mouths half-open. But let that pass.

source.japanese: 今夜は烏賊がいい、ゴンズイやオコゼの類辺りだと美味は美味なのだが口に入れるまでが大変で、いつぞやは毒魚に関してろくな知識をもたなかった朔屋は、右腕紫に膨れあがり二晩ほど悶絶する羽目にもなって、それで懲りないあたりがこの青年らしいし、そればかりか釣果の選り好みまでするようになっては言語道断級だが、まあ、夜釣りの楽しみは朔屋にしてみればまだ健全な方。
source.english: Tonight, squid would do nicely. Striped catfish and stingfish were delicious enough, but getting them into his mouth was another matter. Once, knowing next to nothing about venomous fish, Sakuya had suffered two nights of agony with his right arm swollen purple. That he learned no caution was characteristic; that he now presumed to pick and choose his catch was outrageous. Still, night fishing was relatively wholesome for this young man.

source.japanese: 性欲に悶えて悶々として、手淫に耽[ふけ]るか次の寄港地で酒場のお姉さん相手にたっぷり吐き出すまで溜めておくかに迷うて夜を徒[いたづ]らに空費するよりかは幾らかましと言えた。
source.english: It was at least somewhat better than wasting the night in a fever of lust, agonizing over whether to masturbate or save the whole load for some barroom woman at the next port.

target.text: ───Late at night.

……As Sakuya's raids on the larder in search of snacks to go with his drinks became more routine, it was only natural that the punishment he was served upon being discovered would grow harsher in turn, but if he was dragged all the way to the banks of the Sanzu River every single time to watch a line dance performed by Kannon Bodhisattvas, there was no telling when he'd be unable to make it back home again.

(TN: Sanzu River is the Japanese Buddhist equivalent of the River Styx. It is a common trope in Japanese culture for a near-death experience to involve waking up on a misty riverbank surrounded by flowers, welcoming figures, or other tempting sights. To simplify things, in Pure Land Buddhism, you'll often see Amida Buddha accompanied by a retinue of heavenly beings, Kannon included, descending in an ethereal procession atop purple clouds to escort the soul to paradise. Kannon is known for mercy and compassion, but she is also a woman, so this also plays on the sight across the river being so captivating that Sakuya would be lured across.)

Even Sakuya eventually learned the art of self-sufficiency, and he had figured out how to procure a few drinking snacks on his own. Cast a long line over the gunwale, and nature will bless you with her bounty. Given that this world had brought the likes of Sakuya into herself and sustained him to this point, she truly was a caretaker exceedingly warm of heart, and were she to even go so far as to offer him snacks to go with his drinks, then by now, the majority of people would be like to go on to revel in the joys of life, smiling with their mouths left half-open like idiots all the while, but, well, that's beside the point.

Squid would be good tonight, and while fish like the striped eel catfish or devil scorpionfish certainly were delicious, it was a huge hassle just to get to the point where you could actually eat them, and some time ago, back when Sakuya didn't know the first thing about venomous fish, he'd even suffered through his arm swelling up and turning purple, reduced to writhing in agony for two whole nights, and while it was very like this young man to learn nothing from that experience, now he'd even become so outrageous that he was picky about his catch, but, well, considering this was Sakuya, enjoying a bout of night fishing still counted as one of his more wholesome pleasures.

Compared to wasting away the night restlessly agonizing over his pent-up desires, torn between indulging in onanism or holding it in until the next port of call where he could release it all together with some bar girl, it certainly was a somewhat better use of his time.

source.japanese: そんなこんなで、以前に船内の倉庫から見つけ出して半日ばかり手入れして、ようやく使用可能にまでかこつけた釣り具を担いで上甲板まで上がってきた朔屋は、まだ見ぬ今夜の釣果に、どうせなら人魚、それも西洋式のが掛かってくれないか、若狭の辺りのは御免蒙[こうむ]るなどと、酒欲が性欲に浸食されつつあったのだが───
source.english: At any rate, Sakuya shouldered the fishing tackle he had found in a shipboard storeroom and spent half a day coaxing back into working order, then climbed to the upper deck dreaming of the night's still-unseen catch. Why not hook a mermaid while he was at it? A Western one, mind; he wanted none of those from around Wakasa. Lust was steadily encroaching upon his thirst for drink—

target.text: After this and that, having spent about half a day fixing up the fishing gear he'd found earlier in the ship's hold, now finally able to pass it off as being in usable condition, Sakuya had climbed up to the upper deck with said gear slung over his shoulder.

As for the yet-unseen catch of tonight, if he was allowed a choice in the matter, wouldn't a mermaid be nice, and a Western mermaid while he was at it; he'd certainly rather be spared any from around Wakasa, and as his desire for drink was gradually being encroached upon by his desire for sex─── (TN: Traditional Japanese ningyo, written "人魚", are far from the beautiful, seductive singers of the West. They are grotesque freaks, actual fish with human heads and sharp claws. One of the most famous folk tales involving a ningyo is that of Yao Bikuni from Wakasa.)

source.japanese:
酒も肴も、人魚のおっぱいも、心愉しき妄想は、舷側、右舷に展開せられた背景音楽付きの一大見物に横殴りに駆逐された。
　それは、舷側に立った途端に艫[とも]の方から巨大な街の夜景一つが追随してきては、追いついて、目を左右上下どちらに向けても綺羅綺羅しい夜灯りで占領して行き過ぎるともなれば、朔屋ならずとも誰でもそうなる。
　完全に通り過ぎるまで、たっぷり二分はかかったのではないかと思われたその街の夜景色というのは、要は、なんの事はない豪華客船だ。
source.english:
Liquor, snacks, mermaids' breasts: all these happy visions were swept aside by a grand spectacle, complete with music, off the starboard side.
No sooner had he reached the rail than an entire city's nightscape caught up from astern, overtook him, filled every direction with glittering lights and passed. Anyone, not merely Sakuya, would have been overwhelmed.
The city seemed to take a full two minutes to pass him. In short, it was nothing more mysterious than a luxury liner.

source.japanese: ただ、全長、全幅、全高、どれをとっても信天翁号のたっぷり三倍以上はあったし、なによりぴかぴかと惜しげもなく電照振り撒いていたし、中層甲板の舷側辺りに設けられたコンサート会場では楽団の演奏がいまし酣[たけなわ]で、流麗に奏でられる『ラ・クンパルシータ』の旋律は朔屋の耳にも届くほどであったし、船室の窓に身体押し当て後背立位でせっせと励んでいた、白人のカップルのお姉さんの艶[つや]やかな口紅の色まではっきり見えて朔屋を半勃起させたし、なにより船腹は上から下までペンキ塗料がぴっかぴかで錆や腐朽など兆しの欠片も見られず、朔屋を今更ながらにお月様を肥溜めの底から覗いたような惨めな気分にさせた。
source.english: Only, in length, beam, and height alike, the thing was a good three times the size of the Albatross, if not more. It flung electric light about without stint. At a concert stage by the middle deck's rail an orchestra played at full tilt, and even Sakuya could hear the flowing strains of ‘La Cumparsita.’ A white couple labored energetically against one cabin window, the woman pressed to the glass and the man taking her from behind; he could distinguish the glossy color of her lipstick, and that alone gave him half an erection. Above all, the hull shone with fresh paint from top to bottom, without the least hint of rust or rot. Once again Sakuya felt as wretched as a man looking up at the moon from the bottom of a cesspit.

source.japanese: なにしろペンキやそれを塗布したりといった贅沢品は、お奇麗なお金持ちの道楽よとせせら笑い、目の仇にするような僻[ひが]み根性もの揃いの信天翁号は、船腹の色は赤錆の色なのだからお話にならない。とにかく、そんな豪華客船が追い越していったのが風も感じられるくらいの目と鼻の先。距離にして五米[メートル]も隔てていなかったのではないだろうか。あの級数の船なら汽笛、号鐘、銅鑼の、警戒・連絡用音響設備全て具[そな]えているだろうに、どれ一つ鳴らされた様子もなかったのは何故だろうと首を捻って朔屋はすぐに合点した。夜といって、まともな光量に乏しい信天翁号など、向こうからすれば洋上の浮き草の塊に夜光虫がこちゃこちゃと固まったようにしか見えなかったのに違いない。
source.english: On the Albatross, a crew of resentful souls jeered at such luxuries as paint and putting it on as diversions for those oh-so-refined rich people. The hull was the color of red rust: no comparison was possible. In any case, the liner passed close enough for him to feel its wind. Perhaps there had not been five meters between them. A ship of that class surely carried whistles, bells, gongs, every sound device for warning and communication. Why had not one sounded? Sakuya wondered, then understood. At night, with scarcely a decent light aboard, the Albatross must have looked to them like a clump of floating weed dotted with a few sea sparkles.

target.text: All the pleasant fantasies in his mind, visions of drink, snacks, and even mermaid titties, were all violently swept aside by the grand spectacle unfolding off to the side of the ship, to starboard, complete with accompanying background music. The moment he stepped up to the bulwark at the ship's side, the nightscape of a massive city in its entirety came trailing in from the stern, steadily catching up to them, and when every which direction he turned his eyes───left, right, up, down───was dominated by dazzlingly brilliant night lights streaming past him, it wasn't just Sakuya; anyone would end up overwhelmed.
It felt as if it might well have taken a full two minutes before it had completely passed him by; that glittering night skyline was, in a word, nothing more than an ordinary luxury cruise ship.

It was just that, its length overall, beam, air draught, regardless of which, it was at least three times that of the Albatross with extra to spare, and more than any of that, it was scattering electric light everywhere in an unsparingly lavish display, the performance by the orchestra playing in the concert venue set up near the ship's mid-deck rail was in full swing, the beautifully played melody of 『La Cumparsita』so loud it even reached Sakuya's ears, and he could even clearly see the glossy shade of a woman's lipstick as her body was pressed against a cabin window, the white couple vigorously going at it from behind while standing, leaving him half-erect.

Most of all, however, the ship's hull gleamed from top to bottom with a fresh coat of paint, not showing even the slightest hint of rust or decay, and belated as it was, Sakuya was struck anew with the wretchedly miserable feeling of staring up at the moon from the depths of a pit of night soil.

At any rate, both paint and the act of applying it was nothing but luxury, sneered at as a vain amusement of the prim and pampered rich, and the Albatross, crewed by such bitter souls and jaundiced minds who saw elegance as an affront that was to be treated as no less than a sworn enemy, had a hull the colour of rust red, so she was already beyond salvation.

Regardless, that luxury cruiser passed them by, but it was so close he could practically feel the air displaced by it blowing right under his nose. In terms of distance, it couldn't have been more than five metres away, if that. A ship of that class must have been equipped with steam whistles, a ship's bell, a gong, all kinds of audio equipment for communications and warnings, and as Sakuya tilted his head, wondering how it could be they didn't seem to have set off a single one, the reason quickly dawned on him. It was night, so given there was hardly a decent light aboard the Albatross, she must have looked to the other vessel like nothing more than a patch of floating seaweed teeming with a cluster of sea sparkles.

source.japanese: そうと気づいた時に朔屋の腹に来たったのはむかっ腹と言うより物哀しさだったが、しみじみと哀愁を噛み締めているどころか、豪華客船の造波で船が大揺れ小揺れ、弾みで危うく釣り具を舷側から放り出すところで、哀愁も白人のお姉さんの口紅の色も叩き出され、朔屋は笑うしかなかったという。
source.english: That realization brought sadness rather than anger. But there was no time to savor melancholy. The liner's wake rocked the ship wildly, nearly tossing his tackle over the rail. Melancholy and the white woman's lipstick alike were driven from his mind. They say Sakuya could only laugh.

target.text: Upon coming to that realization, what Sakuya felt was less anger and more melancholy, but instead of being allowed the time to digest his grief, the wake of the luxury cruise ship sent the Albatross rocking, both wildly and gently, and when he almost flung his fishing gear overboard from the jolting, both his sorrows and the shade of that white lady's lipstick were knocked clean out of his head, and all Sakuya could do was laugh.

【直正】
「じゃああんたの目はなんか調子がおかしい、確実におかしい、だって今、すれすれだったぞ、ぶわーって、向こうの金持ちのタイの色まで見えたぞ、ラ・クンパルシータだったんだぞ！」
source.english: “Then there's definitely something wrong with your eyes. It came past this close—whoosh! I could see the color of some rich passenger's tie. We were close enough to hear ‘La Cumparsita’!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Huh? Well, if you have to ask, the ocean. I mean, we're on watch.」

【Naomasa】 「Then something's wrong with your eyes, they're definitely messed up, because a minute ago, it just barely missed us, going BWOOOOOOOH, hell, I could even see the colour of the ties of the rich guys over there, they were playing La Cumparsita!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「朔屋、あんたの言ってる事がわかんない」
source.english: “Sakuya, I have no idea what you're talking about.”

source.japanese: そらっ惚けているのでもなんでもなく、本気で豪華客船との接触寸前であったのを知らない様子で、朔屋に向けた顔には当惑が満ちて、青年の見当識を怪しくさせたほど。
source.english: Not playing innocent or anything of the sort. They genuinely seemed unaware of how nearly they had collided with the liner. Such bewilderment filled the faces turned toward him that Sakuya began to doubt his own bearings.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺の方がわかんないよっ。
　衝突寸前だったの！　右舷から！　どっかのお金持ちの客船と！　向こうが流してたダンスミュージックが聞こえるくらい接近してたんだって！」
source.english:
“I'm the one who doesn't understand!
We almost collided! Off starboard! With some liner full of rich people! It came close enough for us to hear the dance music aboard!”

source.japanese: 自分の方が夢か幻覚でも見ていたのではないかという危惧を振り払うような、朔屋の身振り手振りの熱演だが、二人とも今ひとつ真に迫らないようで、きょとんと首を傾げるのが、こんな時でなければ、あまり見られない可愛げの表情と言えば言えたが、流石にこの今はそう気楽に愛でてもいられない。
source.english: He gestured fervently, as though driving away the fear that he himself had dreamed or hallucinated it. Neither woman seemed convinced. They tilted their heads blankly. Under other circumstances he might have found this a rare, charming expression, but now was no time to admire it idly.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Sakuya, I have no clue what you're on about.」

They weren't just playing dumb, no, they seemed to genuinely not know that they had been on the verge of colliding with a luxury cruise ship, and the sheer bewilderment on the faces turned towards Sakuya was enough to make the young man doubt his own grasp on reality.

【Naomasa】 「I'm the one who doesn't understand any of this! We were inches from colliding! At starboard! With some cruise ship for rich people! It came so close, I could hear the dance music coming from their ship!」

The impassioned theatricality of Sakuya's gesticulation seemed almost like an attempt to shake off the unsettling thought that he might have been the one dreaming or hallucinating the whole thing, but the performance didn't seem to land, for they just tilted their heads with looks of blank confusion, and were it not for the current situation, one might have deemed it a rare and endearing expression; the present moment did not offer him the leeway for lighthearted admiration, however.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「え。シサム、見てた？」
source.english: “Huh. Sisam, did you see?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Huh. Shisamu, you see anything?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ううん、あたし、左舷見てたから」
source.english: “No. I was watching to port.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Nope, I was looking at port, so.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ああ、あたしもだ。そういやなんか、ちょっとライトがさしたような気が、しないでもないような……」
source.english: “Oh, me too. Come to think of it, maybe there was a little light shining over us… Maybe…”

source.japanese: いつもなら、打てば響くような、というより打とうとかしようものなら、機先を制されてコルトで撃ちこんできかねない二人にして、この螺子が二・三本もまとめて抜けたかの反応の鈍さと鬱陶しさ、朔屋は二人の肩口にクロの生き霊でも憑いているのではないかとしげしげ見つめたが、月影が濡らしているばかりで、つまりは今の二人、これが素であるらしかった。
source.english: Ordinarily, they responded as smartly as struck bells. Or rather, try to strike them and they might beat you to it with a Colt bullet. Now they were sluggish and tiresome, as though two or three screws had fallen out at once. Sakuya peered at their shoulders, wondering whether Kuro's living spirit had possessed them. There was nothing there but moonlight. Apparently this was simply the twins themselves.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんたらが、二人揃って……。
　なにやってんだかなあ……」
source.english:
“Both of you, together…
What are you doing…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「これ、たとえ俺が黙ってったって、誰かが気づくぞ……水夫長に話がいったら、あんたらだってただじゃすむまいに……」
source.english: “Even if I keep quiet, someone'll notice… If it gets to the boatswain, you two won't get off lightly…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Yeah, me too. Now that you mention it, I kind of feel like there might have been a flicker of light in the corner of my eyes, or maybe not……」

Under normal circumstances, these two wouldn't just respond instantly, they'd beat you to the punch before you even tried making a move, likely already firing their Colts your way, but the maddening sluggishness of their reactions, as if they had two or even three screws come loose all at once, made Sakuya stare intently at them, wondering if that wasn't Kuro's ikiryou clinging to their shoulders and possessing them, but all they were bathed in was damp moonbeams; in other words, right now, the twins were their natural selves. (TN: An ikiryou, written "生き霊", is a "living spirit" that leaves a living person's body out of intense feelings to linger or possess someone else.)
【Naomasa】 「You girls, both of you……. Seriously, what are you doing……」
【Naomasa】 「Even assuming I hold my tongue about this, somebody is going to notice it……and if the Bosun hears about this, even you two aren't just gonna get off scot-free……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「えー……それは、やだなあ……」
source.english: “Ugh… Wouldn't like that…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Ehhー……I don't really like the sound of that……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたしらも、クロみたいに折檻されんのかしら……」
source.english: “I wonder if we’ll get punished like Kuro…”

source.japanese: なにを連想したのか知らないが、頬にうっすら朱を置いて、ミニスカートの裾[すそ]微妙に揺らしてもじもじと、櫓台の床を蹴っているあたり、妙を通り越して奇怪ですらあり、朔屋は本気で二人を案じたほど。
source.english: What had come into their minds he could not say. But there they stood faintly blushing, fidgeting and scuffing the lookout platform while the hems of their miniskirts trembled. It went beyond merely strange and became downright uncanny; Sakuya began genuinely to worry about the pair.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なんかおかしいな、あんたら。
　酒でも呑んでるのか？」
source.english:
“…Something's wrong with you two.
Have you been drinking?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Maybe we're also going to get punished like Kuro……」

He wasn't sure what exactly they were imagining in association with that, but a faint blush had bloomed on their cheeks, they fidgeted in a way that made the hems of their skirts sway ever so slightly, and when they began to kick at the floor of the tower platform, it went beyond the strange and plunged into the realm of the bizarre, to the point it made Sakuya genuinely concerned for them.
【Naomasa】 「……Something is a little off here with you two. Have you been drinking or something?」

source.japanese: 報告するかしまいか、朔屋はあれこれ悩んだのだ。ヤらせてくれた女には無条件で甘くなる判りやすい男である。二人と肌を重ねたあの夜の後だもの、鬼の首でも取った様にご注進に及んだら、なんと情の薄い男だと軽蔑されて、もうヤらせてもらえないかも知れない。それはとてもとても困る。
source.english: Sakuya agonized over whether to report them. He was a simple creature, unconditionally indulgent toward any woman who let him sleep with her. After the night he had shared with the twins, if he rushed off to report them in triumph, they might despise him as a cold-hearted man and never let him do it again. That would be very, very troublesome.

source.japanese: かといって見なかった事にして済ませるには事が大きすぎる。何事もなかった、というのは結果論であり、今頃、洋上陸影も見えない夜の海で、皆して仲良く輪になって耐久立ち泳ぎ競争という愉快な事態になっていた事だって充分に有り得る。向こうの船は、信天翁号を轢破してもかすり傷程度で済んだだろうという推測は、この際たいして慰めにもならない。
source.english: Yet this was too grave simply to pretend he had seen nothing. Nothing happened: easy to say afterward. They might perfectly well have been out there now, in the night sea with no land in sight, all in a friendly circle competing to see who could tread water longest. The conjecture that the other ship could have run the Albatross down and escaped with a scratch brought little comfort.

target.text: Should he report them or not? Sakuya anguished over it in this way and that. He was the sort of straightforward man who became unconditionally indulgent with any woman who had let him fuck her. This was after they'd spent a night of intimacy in the same bed, and if he triumphantly rushed to report them as if he had slain an oni, how heartless and cold a man would he be scorned as, maybe they wouldn't even let him fuck them anymore. And that would be deeply, deeply troubling.

Even if, hypothetically, he pretended to not have seen anything, this was too grave an incident. To claim that nothing actually happened was merely a conclusion drawn through the lenses of hindsight, because it was entirely plausible that, by now, they could be floating out in the middle of the moonlit ocean with no land in sight, all forming a happy little circle, competing in a cheerful contest of who could tread water the longest. His guess that the other ship would've gotten away with nothing more than a few scratches after wrecking the Albatross didn't offer much consolation at this point.

source.japanese: 結局朔屋が余り葛藤せずに済んだのは、青年が物見櫓で暢気していた双子を見てから程なくして、水夫長その人が上がってきたからで───
source.english: In the end Sakuya was spared much conflict. Shortly after he found the twins lounging in the lookout, the boatswain himself climbed up—

target.text: In the end, Sakuya was spared having to wrestle overly much with his conflicted heart, the reason being that, not long after the young man had found the twins lounging on top of the watchtower, the Bosun himself came climbing up the ladder───

source.japanese:
始め朔屋は、怪人藁頭辺りでも出現したのか見誤ったのは、水夫長が本来なら禿頭のところ、妙に粗い、そしてよじれによじれた頭髪を生やして登場したからで、それはよくよく見ればモップのブラシなのだった。
　就寝前に本の修理に用いたボンドを誤ってぶちまけてしまい、それを拭いたモップをベッド側に怠惰にも放置していたところ、豪華客船とのニアミスの大揺れでベッドから転がり落ちた水夫長、その程度では起きない豪毅が仇になった。転がり落ちて水夫長、ボンド乾きかけのモップに頭からつっこみ───
source.english:
At first Sakuya took him for some straw-headed monster. Coarse, fantastically twisted hair had sprouted where the boatswain ought to have been bald; upon closer inspection, it proved to be the head of a mop.
Before bed he had spilled the glue he used to repair books, wiped it up with the mop, and lazily left the mop beside his bunk. The violent lurch caused by their near miss with the liner rolled him out of bed. His heroic ability to sleep through anything betrayed him: out he rolled, headfirst into the mop and its half-dried glue—

source.japanese: 物見櫓にて、双子の過失を認めた水夫長の、怒りの余り声も出さずに全身の筋肉をぴくんぴくんと振るわせている姿は、今回に限っては全く非のない朔屋でさえ観念して物見櫓から身投げしかけたほどだった。
source.english: Once the boatswain had established the twins' guilt, he stood upon the lookout platform speechless with rage, every muscle twitching. The sight nearly drove even Sakuya—entirely innocent for once—to accept his fate and throw himself off the platform.

target.text: What Sakuya at first mistakenly thought to be the arrival of some kind of dubious, straw-headed creature turned out to be the Bosun, who was usually quite bald, sporting a strangely coarse mop of hair twisted and tangled into a mess, and upon closer inspection, it turned out to be the head of an actual mop.

He had accidentally spilt some glue he was using to repair a book before retiring for the night, and he had lazily left the mop he had used to wipe it up with by his bedside, so when the great rolling of the ship caused by the near miss with the luxury cruise ship made the Bosun tumble out of his bed, it was his formidable toughness, that which kept him asleep through something as trifling as that, which became his downfall on this occasion. Tumbling down, the Bosun had crashed headfirst into the mop caked in tacky, half-dried glue───

Up in the watchtower, the Bosun, having deemed it to be a blunder of the twins' making, was so beside himself with fury that he could not even speak, the muscles covering his entire body twitching, and he made for a sight so terrifying that even Sakuya, who in this particular instance was entirely blameless, nearly resigned himself to his fate and threw himself off the tower.

source.japanese:
かくして、航海士の双子、朔屋言うところの『愉快で哀しい折檻』を受ける事になった。それはもう存分に、お腹一杯に。
　まずは、船の舳先と船尾、両極端に隔てられて───
source.english:
Thus the twin navigators received what Sakuya called the ‘merry, miserable punishment’: a full helping, enough to fill their bellies.
First they were separated to opposite ends of the ship, bow and stern—

source.japanese: 信天翁号の舳先には、一体何時から、そして誰が、そこに置いたのか判然としない犬小屋がある。現在そこを根城にしている犬はおらず、無住の小屋となっているが、この日は久方ぶりの住人を迎えてあった。
source.english: At the Albatross's bow stood a kennel. Who had put it there, or when, no one could say. No dog currently made its home there; the little house stood empty. That day it welcomed its first resident in some time.

target.text: Thus, the twin mates ended up on the receiving end of what Sakuya had previously described as "delightfully miserable punishment". And they were getting more than enough───their fill of it and then some. To start, they were separated at opposite extremes───one at the bow, the other at the stern───

At the bow of the Albatross, though it was entirely unclear exactly when, or by whom, it had been built, there stood a doghouse. At present, no dog claimed the shed as its stronghold, and it had become uninhabited, but on this day, it welcomed a resident for the first time in ages.

source.japanese:
シサムだ。
　彼女は舳先の犬小屋の中に監禁され、ひたすら土下座の姿勢で反省の刑を科せられた。
source.english:
Sisam.
Confined in the kennel at the bow, she was sentenced to reflect upon her deeds, prostrate with her forehead to the floor throughout.

target.text: It was Shisamu. The woman had been confined within the doghouse at the bow, subjected to a punishment of endless repentance while kneeling and prostrating herself in an earnest dogeza.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ううう、ごめんなさいごめんなさい、
　あたしはわんわんにも劣る間抜けなメス畜生でございますごめんなさい」
source.english:
“Uhh, I'm sorry, I'm sorry.
I'm a stupid female beast, worse than a doggy, I'm sorry.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「こうしてるだけでもこの犬小屋ごと高波に攫[さら]われて死んじゃうかと思うと、怖くて失禁しそうですごめんなさい」
source.english: “Just being here, thinking a big wave could take the whole kennel and kill me, I'm so scared I'll wet myself, I'm sorry.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Uuh, I'm sorry I'm sorry, I'm a retarded animal bitch inferior even to a doggy I'm so sorry!」
【Shisamu】 「Just kneeling here is enough to make me feel like a giant wave could sweep me away along with this whole doghouse and kill me and it's so scary I'm about to piss myself I'm so sorry!」

source.japanese: 一方、船尾、艫の方に隔てられたキサラは。
source.english: Meanwhile, Kisara, isolated at the stern—

target.text: Meanwhile, Kisara, who'd been isolated at the stern of the ship.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あああ、ごめんなさいごめんなさい、
　あたしはパンツを履く値打ちもないみじめなビッチでございますごめんなさい」
source.english:
“Aaaah, I’m sorry, I’m sorry,
I’m a pathetic bitch who isn’t even worthy of wearing panties—I’m so sorry.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「普段はどんな角度でも鉄壁の守備を誇るこのスカートも、反射の作用には勝てませんごめんなさい」
source.english: “Even this skirt, which ordinarily boasts an impregnable defense from every angle, is powerless against a reflection. I'm sorry.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「恥ずかしくてそして今まさにおしっこが失禁の危機であり、そんな瞬間を見られたら恥辱死しそうですごめんなさい」
source.english: “I’m so embarrassed, and right now I’m on the verge of wetting myself—if anyone saw that happen, I’d die of shame. I’m so sorry.”

source.japanese: キサラは船尾で、適当な柱に縛りつけられ、水張った金盥の上を跨[また]がされ、しかもパンツを履く事を許されていなかった。見届け役の下級水夫達が見守る中、水の面に映ってスカートの奥、脚の間が丸見えである。
source.english: At the stern Kisara was lashed to a convenient post and forced to straddle a metal basin filled with water; worse, she wasn't allowed to wear panties. The junior sailors detailed to supervise watched as the surface reflected the view up her skirt, laying everything between her legs bare.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Aaaah, I'm sorry I'm sorry, I'm just a wretched slut who doesn't even deserve the dignity of wearing underwear I'm so sorry!」
【Kisara】 「Even this skirt that usually boasts the ironclad defense of a fortress from every angle is no match for the laws of reflection I'm so sorry!」
【Kisara】 「It's embarrassing and also I'm seconds away from pissing myself and if anybody saw me do that then I'd surely perish from the sheer disgrace I'm so sorry!」

Kisara had been tied to some pole at the stern, made to straddle a metal basin filled with water, and on top of that, hadn't been allowed to wear panties. Under the gazes of the deck boys gathered to bear witness, the depths hidden beneath her skirt were reflected on the surface of the water, and everything between her legs was clearly visible there.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「僕らだって別にそんなの、見たい訳じゃないけどさー……」
source.english: “It’s not like we really want to see that kind of thing, though…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「It's not like we really want to see it that badly, you know……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「水夫長の言いつけだもん仕方ないよね。
　あ、今なんかちょろってきた」
source.english:
“It's the boatswain's orders,
so what can we do? Oh—something just trickled out.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But it's the Bosun's orders, so what can you do, right? Ah, something just leaked out!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「アーーっ、見ないで、見ないでぇぇぇ……」
source.english: “Aaaah, don’t look, don’t lookkkk……”

source.japanese: なおキサラはこの懲罰に処される前に、機関長の特別の計らいで、ウイスキイをたっぷり利かせた紅茶を量にして半ガロンは振る舞われており、その後トイレに行く事は許されていないと言うから、今彼女の膀胱を襲っているのが如何なる試練なのかは、まあ想像するまでもなかろう。
source.english: Before the punishment began, the chief engineer had thoughtfully seen to it that Kisara was served a good half gallon of tea generously laced with whiskey. She had not been allowed to visit the lavatory since. No great imagination is required to appreciate the ordeal then assailing her bladder.

source.japanese:
結論から言うと、キサラはあっさり陥落した。悪名高い信天翁号の航海士とはいえ、双子の片割れと引き離されると日頃の大胆不敵な覇気も消失する。反射刑の恥辱と襲いかかる尿意だけでも、今のキサラには悶死級の辛苦であるのに、そこへさして水夫長に言いくるめられた下級水夫が持ちだしてきたブツがある。鼻を洗濯バサミでつまみながらだ。
　それ、双子の船室のベッドの下に押しこめられていた例の腐れソックスの残り。あの汚穢極めた汚物は全て焼却処分にした筈が、何故残っていたのか。その子細はこの際問題ではあるまい。
source.english:
To give the ending away, Kisara capitulated almost at once. Even a navigator of the notorious Albatross lost her usual dauntless spirit when parted from her twin. The humiliation of the reflection punishment and the assault upon her bladder were already mortal torments to Kisara in her present condition. Then one of the junior sailors, talked around by the boatswain, appeared carrying something, his nostrils pinched shut with a clothespin.
It was what remained of the notorious rotten socks once stuffed beneath the twins' bed. The entire obscene abomination was supposed to have been burned; how any of it survived need not detain us here.

source.japanese:
問題は、その腐臭、糸を引きそうなブツを、下級水夫君が棒っ切れの先に刺してキサラの鼻先に押しつけてきた事で───
　もちろん、息を止めて耐えようとした。無駄だった。息など止めたところで臭撃は目の粘膜に刺さった。
　そしてキサラの中で、水風船が弾けて、あひん、と鳴いて、それでおしまいの。
source.english:
The problem was that the junior sailor had skewered the reeking, almost stringy object on a stick and thrust it under Kisara's nose—
Naturally she held her breath and endured. Useless. Breath or no breath, the stench stabbed through the mucous membranes of her eyes.
Then a water balloon burst inside Kisara. She squeaked ahin, and that was the end of it.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「AAAーーH, don't look, don't look at meeeee……」

Furthermore, before Kisara was subjected to this punishment, as a special treat from the Chief Engineer, she had been served a good half gallon of black tea spiked with a generous helping of whisky, and as the story went, she had also not been allowed to go to the toilet after, so exactly what manner of trial her bladder was undergoing at the moment, well, one hardly needs to imagine.

To make a long story short, Kisara yielded all too easily. Mate of the infamous Albatross though she may be, when separated from her twin counterpart, her usual daring and dauntless spirit also vanished. Just the humiliation of this reflective punishment and the need for relief assailing her desperate bladder were enough torture to make Kisara die of agony as she was, and yet, just then, a deck boy, having been talked into it by the Bosun, produced a certain article. All while pinching his nose shut with a clothespin.

That thing, it was a remnant of those rotten socks that had been stuffed under the bed in the twins' cabin. That foul, utterly defiled filth was supposed to have been incinerated in its entirety, so whyever did it yet linger in this world? Those particulars were of little consequence at this juncture.

What was of consequence was that fetid stench of rot, and how a deck boy took that oozing, putrid thing that looked as if it was about to form sticky threads, impaled it on the end of a stick, then pressed it right against the tip of Kisara's nose─── Of course, she held her breath and tried to endure it. It was a vain effort. By the time she'd ceased to breathe, the assault of foul stenches had long pierced the mucous membranes of her eyes. Thus, inside Kisara, the water balloon burst, she let out a whimpering "ahhn", and that was the end of her.

source.japanese: キサラが上からも下からも垂れ流しながら、思うた未来予想図がある。
source.english: While leaking from both ends, Kisara conceived the following vision of her future.

source.japanese:
───もう、いいよね。あそこで。
　
　───うん、いいよ。あそこで。
　
　───あたしの部屋、これから先は。
　
　───『船長の箱』で。
　
　───あたしとシサム、クロに頭に下げて。
　
　───あの箱に間借りさせてもらおう。
source.english:
—That place will do now, won't it?
—Yes. That place will do.
—From now on, my room will be—
—the ‘Captain's Box.’
—Sisam and I will bow our heads to Kuro—
—and ask her to let us lodge in that box.

source.japanese:
───名前、変えないとね。
　
　───『船長と航海士の箱』に。
　
　───叶うならね、もう少し大きな箱に。
　
　───そんで、三人でおまる使い回して。
　───うん、それで生きていこう。
　
　───嵐の時だけは、出してくれるかなあ。
source.english:
—We'll have to change the name.
—To ‘The Captain and the Navigators' Box.’
—If we can, a slightly larger box.
—Then the three of us can share a single chamber pot.
—Yes. We'll live like that.
—At least during storms, they'll let us out… won't they?

target.text: While leaking from both above and below, there was a vision of the future that Kisara imagined.

───I've done enough now, right? I'll go there. ───Yeah, it's okay. I'll go there. ───My room, from now on. ───Will be the『Captain's Box』 ───Shisamu and I, we'll lower our heads to Kuro. ───And humbly ask if she will allow us to rent a room in that box.

───We'll have to change the name, won't we? ───To the『Captain and Mates' Box』 ───If but one wish of mine could be granted, it would be for a slighter larger box. ───And then, the three of us will have to share the bedpan. ───Yeah, that's how we'll live. ───I wonder if they'll only let us out when it storms.

source.japanese: 船尾でキサラが中々に愉快な未来設計を立てている一方、船首のシサムはといえば。
source.english: While Kisara was constructing this highly diverting vision of her future at the stern, Sisam at the bow—

target.text: While Kisara was formulating a rather pleasant plan for the future at the stern, when it came to Shisamu at the bow.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ここ予想以上に揺れるごめんなさい、
　それに犬臭いごめんなさい」
source.english:
“It rocks more than I expected, I'm sorry.
And it smells like dog, I'm sorry.”

source.japanese: 普段なら、船が揺れようが逆立ちしようが平気の平左で固茹で卵を水無しで食べて、字の細かい新聞でも読もうかという彼女だけれど、今は片割れと舳[へさき]と艫[とも]に隔てられてある。片割れが隣にいないというそれだけでも、たちどころにありとあらゆる不安のダイナマイトを満載した暴走機関車に乗って、破滅の火薬庫目座して驀進していくような彼女であるが、そこにくわえてこんな狭苦しく揺れの激しい空間に放置されてはたまったものではなかろう。
source.english: Ordinarily she would think nothing of the ship rocking or even turning upside down, cheerfully eating a hard-boiled egg without water and reading a newspaper's fine print. Now she and her other half were separated, bow to stern. The simple absence of her sister already put her on a runaway locomotive packed with the dynamite of every imaginable anxiety, hurtling toward the powder magazine of ruin. Add abandonment in this cramped, violently rocking space, and how could she bear it?

source.japanese:
その上、何代前にここで起居していたのだか知らぬが小屋には犬の臭い潮風にも褪せず染みつき、そんな中で土下座の姿勢を続けていると、背中から自分ほどもある大なる雄犬にのしかかられているかの不安に取り憑かれる。
　視界の限られてひどく揺れる狭い空間の中で「メス畜生」「メス畜生」と連呼していたせいで、シサムは何時しか自己催眠的な精神状態に陥って、自分がその大なる雄犬に、後ろから、猛り勃[た]った雄根を、おんなの孔に、根元まで、貫かれているかの、妄想が。
source.english:
To make matters worse, the smell left by whatever dog had occupied the kennel generations ago remained soaked into it, unfaded by the sea wind. Forced to remain prostrate amid it, Sisam became possessed by the fear that a great male dog as large as herself was mounting her from behind.
In the cramped, violently pitching space with its narrow view, her endless repetition of ‘female beast, female beast’ gradually induced a sort of self-hypnosis: a fantasy of the great dog behind her, driving its raging cock into her woman's hole, all the way to the root.

source.japanese:
人間などとは比べものにならないくらい獰猛な雄根にそれこそ内臓がめくれ返るくらいに犯される情景が、暗がりの中でなかば実体化してシサムを遅い、吐き気を催させる。
　そのえづきさえ、彼女自身はまだ経験した事はないが、妊婦のあのえづきを連想させて、連想は更に妄想を呼んで、シサムは遂に仔犬をぽろぽろ産み落としている自分の未来を思った。犬と違って複乳ではないからお乳をあげる時はキサラにも手伝ってもらわないと、などと想いながら。
　もう横揺れ縦揺れからさえも雄犬の抽送運動あたりが連想されてしまい、それだけで想像妊娠しかねない勢いのシサムなのだった。　思わず「わん」とか「きゃん」とか鳴き真似をしたところ、なんとなく今の気分にぴったりな気がして、懲罰が終わるまで鳴き続けたという───
source.english:
The scene—an organ incomparably more savage than any man's violating her until it seemed her very entrails must turn inside out—half materialized in the darkness and came upon Sisam with nauseating force.
Even her retching called up the sickness of pregnancy, though she had never experienced it herself. Association begot further fantasy, until she imagined her future self dropping puppies one after another. Unlike a bitch, she had no row of teats; Kisara would have to help nurse them.
By then the ship's every roll and pitch suggested the dog's thrusting. Her imagination had such momentum that the motion alone seemed capable of inducing a phantom pregnancy. When an involuntary woof or yelp escaped her, it felt oddly perfect for her mood. They say she continued barking until her punishment ended—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「It's shaking a lot more here than I expected I'm sorry and it reeks of dog I'm sorry!」

Normally, whether the ship was rolling or she was doing a headstand, this woman would stay cool as a cucumber, able to choke down a bone-dry, hard-boiled egg without a single drop of water, or even read a newspaper with small print, but right now, she and her other half were separated, one at the bow and the other at the stern.

The mere fact that her other half was no longer beside her was enough to instantly place her on a runaway locomotive jam-packed with dynamite made from every conceivable anxiety barreling straight towards a massive powder keg of ruin, that was the sort of woman she was, and what's more, she had been abandoned in this cramped, violently shaking space; it must have been unbearable.

On top of that, while it wasn't clear how many generations it had been since anything lived here, the smell of dog still permeated the shed, yet to fade even in the salty sea breeze, and when made to remain in a dogeza position in such circumstances, she became possessed by the fear that a massive male dog the size of herself might be about press down on her from behind.

In a horribly shaking cramped space with limited visibility, she had been called "animal bitch", "animal bitch" repeatedly, and as a result, at some point, Shisamu had fallen into a self-induced hypnotic state of mind, experiencing wild delusions, as if she were being penetrated, from behind, by that massive dog, and its fierce erection, stabbing right into her bitch hole, was penetrating her all the way to the knot.

The scene of a penis so ferociously savage that it defied comparison to the likes of a human's violating her to the point of it turning her insides inside out semi-materialized in the dark and assaulted Shisamu, inducing nausea in her. And even that nausea, though the woman herself had yet to actually experience it, was something she associated with the nausea of pregnancy, and that association summoned yet more delusions, and finally, Shisamu envisioned her own future, one where she was squirting out a litter of puppies, one after another. All while thinking things like, since she didn't have multiple pairs of breasts like a dog, she'd need Kisara's help when nursing them.

At this point, Shisamu was even associating the shaking up and down and side to side with the thrusting motions of that male dog, and she was doing it with such fervor that it was almost enough to induce a false pregnancy in her. After impulsively letting out a few woofs and yips, it somehow felt so perfectly fitting for the mood that she barked incessantly until the punishment was over, or so the story went───

source.japanese:
朔屋には、何やら痛ましくて、二人の有り様を見ているのも辛かったけれど、見届ける義務があると（勝手に）信じて、船尾と舳先を駆け巡ってはしっかりと鑑賞していた。一〇往復以上はしただろうか。普段の面倒くさがりの彼としては信じがたい運動量である。
　こうして朔屋にまでじっくりと恥辱の極みを鑑賞されたせいでもあるまいが、これ以降、シサム・キサラの振る舞いにおかしな点が目立ち始めるようになった。
source.english:
Sakuya found their plight somehow painful, almost too painful to watch. Yet having arbitrarily decided that he was duty-bound to witness it, he raced between bow and stern and studied both spectacles thoroughly. He must have made more than ten round trips—an incredible quantity of exercise for so inveterate an idler.
Whether or not it was because even Sakuya had been allowed to contemplate their ultimate humiliation at leisure, oddities thereafter became increasingly conspicuous in Sisam and Kisara's behavior.

target.text: For Sakuya, it was somehow heartbreaking, and even just watching the pathetic state the two of them were in was painfully bitter, and yet, convinced that he had a (self-appointed) duty to see things through with his own two eyes, he darted back and forth between the bow and the stern, making sure to fully drink in the sight. He must have ran more than ten round trips. For someone as habitually lazy as he, it was an amount of exercise that beggared belief. Though it probably wasn't entirely because even Sakuya had been given a front-row seat to fully savour the peak of their disgrace, henceforth, noticeable oddities began to surface in Shisamu's and Kisara's behaviour.

source.japanese:
……別に立ち聞きしようとしたわけではないのだ。双子はバラックの戸をたてもせず、中で話しこんでいたのだから。
　それも、朔屋が見慣れた、あの手足の先端まで気の漲[みなぎ]った姿ではなく、一方がバラックの壁にもたれてだらりと足を伸ばし、一方がその足に頭を乗せて横たわって、の、掴まる枝もないのでこうして御座いのナマケモノの姉妹の如きの有り様を晒しての。
source.english:
…He had not meant to eavesdrop. The twins had left the shack's door open and were talking inside.
Nor did they present the familiar figures whose vigor reached even the tips of their fingers and toes. One slumped against the wall, legs out; the other lay with her head upon those legs. Sister sloths without a branch to hang from, obliged to arrange themselves like this instead.

source.japanese: 朔屋が顔を突っこんできたのに、のろのろと身を起こしはしたものの、かくも弛緩しきった姿を見られた事になにも感ずるところもないようで、再開した話というのがまた、二つの瓢箪で鯰[なまず]を挟もうとするような、ぬらりくらりと捉えどころのない話で、その上漠然とした不安というか、聞いている朔屋に不安定な居心地の悪さをもたらしたのである。
source.english: When Sakuya poked his head in, they raised themselves slowly, but seemed utterly unconcerned that he had seen them so limp. The conversation they resumed was as slippery and elusive as trying to catch a catfish between two gourds. Worse, beneath it ran a vague anxiety that left Sakuya himself feeling somehow unmoored.

target.text: ……It was not that he was trying to eavesdrop in particular. It was just that the twins were deep in conversation inside a shack they hadn't even bothered to close the door to. What's more, they were a far cry from the sight Sakuya was familiar with, radiating with vitality down to their very fingertips and toes; instead, one was slumped limply against the wall of the shack with her legs stretched out, the other lying down with her head pillowed on those legs, sprawled out like a pair of helpless sloth sisters who, having no branches to hang from, had resigned themselves to just sitting around.

Even though Sakuya had stuck his head into the room, while they did sluggishly lift themselves off the floor, they didn't seem the least bit bothered about being caught in so unguarded a state, and the conversation they resumed was like trying to trap a catfish between two gourds, elusive and hazy, impossible to pin down, and on top of that, it stirred a vague sense of anxiety in Sakuya as he listened, or rather, an unsettling discomfort. (TN: The phrase about catfish and gourds here is a play on a famous saying in Japanese, "瓢箪で鯰を押さえる", lit. catching a catfish with a gourd. The closest English equivalent is something like "slippery as an eel".)

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんかさ、近頃なんか、ひどく居心地が悪くって。だから落ち着かない。注意とかも疎[おろそ]かになる」
source.english: “It's just… Lately I've felt terribly out of place. I can't settle down. I keep letting my attention wander.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「居心地が悪いって、この船の事か？」
source.english: “Uncomfortable? On this ship?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Lately, I've kind of felt terribly ill at ease. That's why I just can't settle down. I've even started to neglect paying attention to things.」
【Naomasa】 「When you say ill at ease, do you mean what happened with the ship?」

source.japanese: ……念のため申し添えておくが、三人が座っているのは、安い煙草と珈琲の匂いが充満する、活動家のモットーや決起集会のビラが壁紙代わりにごてごて貼られた、アプレゲールやモラトリアムの学生諸君のたむろする地下喫茶などではない。
source.english: …To clarify: the three were not sitting in a basement café thick with the smell of cheap cigarettes and coffee, walls papered with activists' slogans and rally leaflets, a haunt of postwar rebels and students with adult life on hold.

source.japanese: 潮と煤と油の臭い染みついた、どこの廃材の寄せ集めかという信天翁号のバラックであり、交わす会話も次はどこの港の船乗りをカモにしてやろうと穏やかではないのがよく似合う、そんな無頼者達の小屋なのに、シサム・キサラの言葉はどうにもとりとめがなく、先日のニアミス事件についても朔屋が訊ねてみればこれである。
source.english: This was the Albatross's shack, assembled from who knew what scraps, steeped in the smells of salt, soot and oil—a hut for outlaws, just the place for unsavory talk of which port's sailors they would fleece next. Yet Sisam and Kisara spoke without any clear point. When Sakuya asked about the recent near collision, this was what he got.

target.text: ……Allow me to add, just in case, but the place that the three were sitting in wasn't one of those underground cafes filled with the scent of coffee and cheap tobacco, walls plastered over with activist slogans and rally handbills in place of wallpaper, where the disillusioned apres-guerre youth and moratorium students hung out. (TN: The "moratorium" here is a reference to Japanese postwar culture, from the 1960s and onwards in particular, describing students who would linger in university life without direction, often politically engaged and exploring identity and ideology while avoiding societal responsibilities.)

It was one of the shacks on the Albatross, odds and ends of scrap wood from god-knows-where indelibly stained with the smells of brine, soot, and oil, well suited for holding sinister discussions on which port they should swindle some sailors in next; despite it being a den for such rogues, Shisamu's and Kisara's words were awfully rambling, and even when Sakuya asked them about the near-miss incident the other day, this was how they responded:

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そういうんじゃない」
source.english: “Not that.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「That's not what this is.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんて言ったらいいんだろう、このいてもたってもいられないような感覚は」
source.english: “How do I put it? This feeling that I can't stay still, can't bear being here…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「How should I even begin to describe this urge to crawl out of my skin?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「この世界全部が、あたしらを閉じこめてくるような……たまらない、気持ちの悪さ」
source.english: “Like the whole world's shutting us in… An unbearable, sickening feeling.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「As if this entire world itself is imprisoning us……an unbearable, sickening dread.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「このまんまじゃおかしくなっちゃいそう。それっくらい、ひどくやな予感？　前兆？　そんなものさえ、感じてるんだ。だから───」
source.english: “If this keeps up, I feel like I'll go mad. It's that bad. Like I've got some horrible premonition—an omen, maybe. I can feel even that. So—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「If things keep going like this, I feel like I'm going to go crazy. That's how bad it is, this terrible gut feeling? Omen? It's gotten to the point where I'm even feeling things like that. That's why───」

source.japanese:
それは───
　
　朔屋には心当たりが全くない、といえば嘘になる心境の。
　たとえば季節の変わり目に、唐突な流行り熱のように訪れる、あの焦燥の念。漠然とした不安と、居心地の悪さが醸成する、焦りの気持ちだ。
source.english:
That feeling—
Sakuya could not truthfully claim to know nothing of it. It was the restlessness that descended at the turn of a season, sudden as a fever going round: an urgency brewed of vague anxiety and discomfort.

source.japanese:
ほとんど第二の肌と慣れきって、日頃は意識もしない周囲の世界が、ふとした弾みで茨[いばら]の衣[ころも]と変じ、肌に棘して傷つけ、溜まらない痛みと痒[かゆ]みで締めつけてくるかの。感ずる度、世界が逃れられない檻なのではないかと感じてしまう。
　それを強く意識してしまうと鬱になるから、朔屋は日頃あまり考え無いようにしているのだけれど。
source.english:
The world around him, worn so familiarly as to be almost a second skin, normally beneath notice, would suddenly become a garment of briars, pricking and wounding his skin, tightening around him with intolerable pain and itching. Each time he felt it, the world seemed an inescapable cage.
Thinking too hard about it depressed him, so ordinarily Sakuya tried not to think.

target.text: That was─── If Sakuya claimed to be totally clueless to what that was like, it would be a lie; that was his mental state. For example, that feeling of restless frustration, hitting abruptly like a sudden fever striking at the turn of the seasons. That feeling of burning impatience, fermented from a vague unease and the discomfort of not belonging.

The feeling of how the world surrounding you, so familiar it is like a second skin that you do not even notice, can change into a garb of thorns by some sudden whim of fate, piercing and wounding your skin, tightening with unbearable pain and itchiness. And each time you feel it, you can't help but feel as if the world itself has become an inescapable cage. If he became overly conscious of that, he would fall into depression, and so Sakuya tried not to think too much about it on a daily basis.

source.japanese:
にわかに、ぼろくていい加減な造りのバラックの壁が、重圧を伴って迫り来る岩の壁になったかの居心地悪ささえ覚える。
　けれどこの心持ち、伝えていいものか、どうか。朔屋は自分が周りにどう思われているかよくよく知り抜いている。
source.english:
Abruptly even the shack's shabby, slapdash walls seemed to become walls of rock bearing down upon him.
But should he tell them how he felt? Sakuya knew very well what those around him thought of him.

source.japanese: 怠惰で無能で阿呆で隙あらば女の臀を追いかけている駄目男───そんな自分が世界の居心地の悪さがどうのといきなり宣[のたま]いだしてしまえば、下手をすると聴診器を額に当てられた挙げ句脳病院の詰め物のある病室にぶちこまれる羽目にもなりかねない。
source.english: Lazy, useless, stupid: a hopeless man forever chasing a woman's ass whenever he saw the chance. If a creature like that suddenly began holding forth on how ill at ease the world made him, he might end up with a stethoscope pressed to his forehead and be bundled into a padded room at the madhouse.

target.text: He was even feeling an oppressive discomfort, as if the ramshackle walls of the shack had suddenly turned into looming faces of rock bearing down on him with all their weight. But this feeling, was it even one he ought to share? Sakuya was only all too aware of exactly what his surroundings thought of him.

A lazy, incompetent, idiotic, hopeless man who chased skirts at any opportunity ───if someone like himself were to start proclaiming how discomforting the world felt and other such existential dread, in the worst case scenario, it was all too likely he would end up being tossed inside a padded cell in some madhouse after having a stethoscope pressed against his forehead.

source.japanese:
けれどもそれはこの双子も同じ事。
　朔屋が知る限り、二人は遠く引き離されない限り、世界の中で自分の居場所を完全に心得る者達である。
　その双子がこんな事を言い出すとは。
source.english:
Yet that went for the twins too.
As far as Sakuya knew, unless they were separated far from one another, these two knew precisely where they belonged in the world.
And now those twins were saying this.

source.japanese: 一体───と朔屋が近頃なにか双子に妙な事でも降ったかと考えこむに、彼の心当たりとしては、あの難破船と出会うた事くらいしか思い浮かばぬ。
source.english: What on earth could have happened to the twins lately? Sakuya pondered the question, but the only thing that came to mind was their encounter with that wreck.

target.text: However, these twins felt the same. As far as Sakuya knew, as long as these two were not pulled far apart from each other, they were people with a complete grasp of where they belonged in this world. And that twins like them would be saying something like this, it was.
What could possibly───as Sakuya pondered whether anything strange might have befallen these twins lately, the only thing that came to his mind was their encounter with that shipwreck.

source.japanese: 朔屋には、どうにも、あの難破船から戻ってきて以来、二人の歯車が狂ってしまったかに感じられてならなかった。
source.english: Sakuya could not shake the feeling that ever since their return from that ship, something in the twins' workings had gone awry.

source.japanese: 考えこむ朔屋に、シサムがかけた言葉は、優しげではあったけれど、どうにも投げ遣りな、声音からして緩み加減の、そして中味も、
source.english: To the brooding Sakuya, Sisam spoke in a voice that sounded gentle enough yet somehow careless, almost slack. And the substance of what she said was no better—

target.text: Ever since returning from that shipwreck, Sakuya couldn't shake the feeling that something in the gears that kept them running had fallen hopelessly out of alignment.
The words Shisamu offered the brooding Sakuya sounded gentle on the surface, yet they were undeniably offhand, lax in both tone and substance alike,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「───妙な話をしちまったね。ほらほら朔屋、あんたもそんな変な顔してないで。男前が台無しだよ？」
source.english: “—Guess we got onto a strange subject. Come on, Sakuya, don't pull that face. You'll ruin those handsome looks of yours.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（やっぱりおかしいよこの二人……）
source.english: (Something really is wrong with these two…)

source.japanese:
───これである。
　褒められると手もなくにやける朔屋であるが、これには二人が精神を病んでいる事を危惧せざるを得なかった。
　これは検証する必要がある、と、怪訝そうな顔をする二人をバラックに待たせて、金盥を引っぱり出してキサラの前に置いて、シサムの前で土下座の姿勢を取って「わん」との鳴き真似を試みたところ。
source.english:
There it was.
Ordinarily, a word of praise made Sakuya grin helplessly. This time he could only fear that the twins were suffering some disorder of the mind. A test was required.
He left the puzzled pair waiting in the shack, fetched a metal basin and set it before Kisara, then prostrated himself before Sisam and attempted a single ‘woof.’

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「───That was a bit of a strange thing to say, huh? Come now, Sakuya, you wipe that weird look off your face too. You're wasting your dashing good looks, you know?」
【Naomasa】 （There really is something wrong with these two……）

───And that brought him to this. Sakuya would always beam at the first hint of praise, but when they acted like this, he couldn't help but worry that there was something deeply mentally wrong with the two. This would require some verification, he thought, and so, leaving them with puzzled expressions, he made the two wait in the shack, then came back dragging a metal basin with him, placed it before Kisara, after which he prostrated himself in a dogeza in front of Shisamu and tried to imitate a bark, and when he did.

source.japanese: ぴー、とかいう音が響いた。それも二重だった。何事かと顔を上げれば、二人の顔、老酒で茹でた上海蟹の如く真っ赤に染まり、あら美味しそうとか見守るうちにもまたぴー、二人の脳天から湯気が噴出する音である。
source.english: A shrill piiiii rang out. In stereo. He raised his head. Both faces were scarlet as Shanghai crabs boiled in rice wine—my, how appetizing. As he watched, another piiiii sounded: steam jetting from both crowns.

target.text: A sharp whistle pierced the air. And in two overlapping tones at that. Wondering just what it could be, when he looked up, he saw their faces had turned scarlet, brightly flushed like Chinese mitten crabs boiled in aged Shaoxing wine, and while he looked on as if enjoying this feast for the eyes, another whistle rang out; it was the sound of steam erupting from the tops of their heads.

source.japanese: この後朔屋は当然のように袋叩きを喰らったわけだが、その拳足は何時も通りの二人だったので、少しだけ安心できた次第。
source.english: After that, Sakuya naturally got a thorough beating, but since their punches and kicks were as familiar as ever, he felt just a little relieved.

target.text: After this, as though it were only natural, Sakuya received a pummeling, but since those fists and feet belonged to their usual selves, he actually felt a little relieved.

source.japanese: 人は誰しも余人の知らざる一面を持つ、というのはよく言われた箴言であり、人文的教養といったものにおよそ無縁な朔屋であっても、文言でも経験則からも実感として心得る人生訓である。
source.english: Everyone has a side unknown to others: a much-repeated maxim. Even Sakuya, scarcely acquainted with anything resembling the humanities, understood it as a lesson in life, both in words and from experience.

source.japanese: 朔屋はそれを、船員学校の教師から教えられた。厳格で寡黙で、長身で鶴のような痩躯の、への字に結んだ口を滅多に崩す事のない初老の男であったが、公正で求める者には別け隔てなく熱心に教授する人であった為、隠れて学生人気は高いという、教師の一つの完成型であった。
source.english: He had learned it from an instructor at maritime school. The man was stern and taciturn, already entering old age, tall and crane-thin, and seldom unbent the downturned line of his mouth. Yet he was fair and taught any student who sought him out with equal zeal, which made him secretly popular: one of the forms in which the ideal teacher might be perfected.

source.japanese:
そう、朔屋はこの人から勿体なくも教えられたのだ。
　この狭苦しい小屋に焚かれた香の匂いはどこかしらその記憶を呼び起こす。
source.english:
Yes, Sakuya had been privileged to learn it from this man.
The incense burning in this cramped hut somehow revived that memory.

target.text: It is a well-worn maxim that every man harbours a side unknown to others, and even Sakuya, a man who stood wholly detached from the refinement of arts and letters, had come to take the reality of this life lesson to heart, proven true both by written wisdom and personal experience.

Sakuya had been taught this lesson by his classroom teacher at the maritime school. Stern and taciturn, tall and lean as a crane, he was a man nearing old age whose mouth was set in a perpetual frown only rarely broken, but because he was a man dedicated to fairness, who imparted knowledge passionately to all who sought it without displaying any favouritism, he was said to secretly be very popular with the students, and he embodied one fully realized ideal of a teacher.

Indeed, Sakuya had been granted the undeserved privilege of being taught by this man. Something about the aroma of the incense burning within this cramped hut had stirred that memory back to life within him.

source.japanese: あれは───その初老の教師が教場に置き忘れていった万年筆をたまさか見つけた朔屋が、彼の人の寓居まで届けに行ったときの事。何も教師の人品骨柄に感じ入って発心起こしたとか、そんな殊勝ッ気である筈もなく、そうして心証良くしておけば、査定に多少は手心加えてくれるかも知らん、の見やすい下心で。
source.english: It had happened when Sakuya found a fountain pen the instructor had left in the classroom and took it to his lodgings. Not from admiration of the man's character, nor any such virtuous impulse. His motive was transparent: make a good impression, perhaps receive a little leniency in his assessment.

source.japanese:
ともかく家並みまばらな町外れ、野原や雑木林の合間合間に小体な家屋がぽつぽつと、この時代の郊外の住宅地など大抵がこんなものだが、中でも他の屋から隔たったのがその教師の侘び住まい。訪ね当てた頃にはもうとっぷりと夜も更けていたので、教師の家の灯りのほんのり温かさに救われた心地で玄関戸を叩いたのだが応答がない───灯りは見えているに。
　今更空しく引き返す事にも疲れ果て、裏庭の方に回ってみた、その時からある種の予感が働いていたのだが。
source.english:
At the thinly settled edge of town, small houses dotted the fields and copses. Most suburban districts of that age were much the same, but the teacher's humble dwelling stood apart even from those. Night had fallen completely by the time Sakuya found it. The faint warmth of its light came as a relief, and he knocked at the front door. No answer—though the light was plainly visible.
Too tired now to turn back empty-handed, he went around to the rear garden. Some premonition had already begun to work upon him.

source.japanese: なんとのう跫音忍ばせて、身を低くして植え込みにの影を渡って、濡れ縁の寝間を覗けば猫間障子が開いていて、中が窺える。と見えたのは振袖の袂[たもと]と白足袋の足だ。それも艶[あで]やかな染め模様と清潔にくすみもない足袋で、すわと朔屋の目が見開かれて、天女を仰ぐように濡れ縁の縁から見上ぐる、秘蔵の箱入り娘か、いや独身と聞いた、ならば妾か通いの情婦か、全く人は見かけによらぬもの。寝間からは、沈香の佳いところでも焚いているのか、やや癖のある、生薬のような匂いも漂いだしていた。
source.english: Without quite knowing why, he softened his tread, crouched low, and passed through the shadows of the shrubbery. Peering from the veranda into the bedroom, he found one panel of the shoji open and could see inside. What first met his eyes was the long sleeve of a kimono and feet in white tabi: the silk brilliantly patterned, the socks unstained and immaculate. Sakuya's eyes flew wide. Gazing up from the edge of the veranda as though at a celestial maiden, he wondered: some treasured daughter kept under lock and key? No—the man was unmarried. Then a mistress, a lover who visited by night? Truly, one could never judge by appearances. From the bedroom drifted another smell, peculiar and medicinal. Fine aloeswood burning, perhaps.

source.japanese: こんな佳いのを隠していようとは、謹厳実直居士と謳われた先生も隅に置けない、と朔屋はにやついたが、これをかたに教師を脅す気などはない。馬鹿で手のつけられない怠け者ではあるが、そういう悪辣さは持ち合わせていないのである。
source.english: To think he had hidden away such a lovely thing! The celebrated paragon of sober integrity had unsuspected depths. Sakuya grinned. But he had no intention of blackmailing his teacher with the discovery. Stupid and incurably lazy though he was, he lacked that sort of viciousness.

target.text: It was───it happened when Sakuya had, by chance, noticed that this almost-elderly teacher of his had forgotten his fountain pen in their place of learning, then set off to pay a visit to that man's humble abode to return it to him. Had the teacher's noble character inspired a spiritual awakening of virtue in Sakuya, no, there was no way it was anything that admirable; he figured that, if he were to make a good impression, maybe his teacher would show some leniency when it came time to evaluate his grades; that was his transparent ulterior motive.

At any rate, it was on the outskirts of town, where houses were few and far between, small, modest homes dotted between fields and patches of woodland; suburban residential areas in this era were mostly like this, but farther removed than any of the others houses stood his teacher's humble, secluded dwelling. By the time he had arrived to pay his visit, the night was already growing late, and with the gentle glow of the light within his teacher's home giving him a fleeting sense of salvation, he knocked, but there was no answer ───even though he could clearly see that the lights were on.

By now, he was so worn out that just the thought of returning home in vain at this point left him drained, so he tried circling around to the back yard, and in that moment, a certain kind of premonition had begun to take hold within him.

Without quite knowing why, he softened his step, kept low to the ground, and slipped through the shadows of the shrubbery, and when he peeked towards the bedroom from the open-air veranda, he saw that the nekoma-shouji screen was open, allowing him a look inside. (TN: A feature of shouji panels mentioned here, the nekoma-shouji, written "猫間障子", refers to a little opening at the bottom found on some sliding panels that is usually used as a cat door.)

And what caught his eye therein were the long sleeves of a furisode and feet clad in white tabi. And what's more, the fabric was adorned with such alluringly vibrant dyed patterns and the tabi so impeccably pristine that they betrayed not a trace of dullness. (TN: A furisode, written "振袖", is a type of kimono with long, wide sleeves, historically worn by young, unmarried women. Tabi, written "足袋", are the Japanese socks with a toe split down the middle.)

With a surprised "oh my!", Sakuya's eyes opened wide as saucers, and as he looked up from the edge of the veranda like he was reverently gazing up at a heavenly nymph for guidance, his mind raced: who could that be, was this his cherished little princess sheltered away from the world, no, he'd heard he was single, so in that case, was it a mistress or a prostitute, you really could not judge a book by its cover. From the bedroom wafted a faint fragrance; perhaps he was even burning fine agarwood incense, laced with a slightly unusual tang reminiscent of medicinal herbs.

To think he was hiding away such a beauty; even a teacher lauded as a gentleman scholar of solemn and upright character had more to him than met the eyes, Sakuya thought with a broad smirk, but he had no intention of using this as leverage to blackmail his teacher. He was a fool and a layabout utterly beyond help, but he wasn't possessed of such ruthlessness.

source.japanese: ただ、教師の愛人のご尊顔というのを一目なり拝んでおきたくて、より深く出歯亀の視線を寝間に潜[もぐ]りこませれば、振袖姿の佇みたるは姿見の前。貌が───玄人筋なのか、夜更けの愛人宅に忍ぶにきちんと化粧を刷いた貌[かお]が。
source.english: He merely wanted one glimpse of the face of the teacher's mistress. His peeping gaze crept farther into the bedroom. The figure in the long-sleeved kimono stood before a full-length mirror. Her face—perhaps she was a professional, to come secretly to her lover's house so late with her makeup properly applied—her face…

source.japanese: 朔屋が気づいた違和感は、白粉の香を厭[いや]なものと混ぜて悪くしたような臭気芬々と放ちて、なんとなればその振袖姿、柳腰は佳品としても背が妙に高い。人手足らないチンドン行列の先頭で、親爺が開き直って芸者姿してるよりもまだ高い。
source.english: Then Sakuya grasped what had disturbed him: the figure gave off a powerful stench, like face powder gone rancid with something vile mixed into it. And though the willow waist beneath that long-sleeved kimono was a fine specimen, she was strangely tall. Taller even than some old fellow brazenly got up as a geisha to lead an understaffed street-advertising band.

target.text: He simply desired the honour of catching a glimpse of the esteemed countenance of his teacher's mistress, and as the peeping tom's gaze slipped deeper into the bedroom, there she stood in her furisode, poised before a full-length mirror. Her visage─── was she a professional, for her visage had been meticulously painted in makeup all to slip into a lover's home late at night.

The sense of wrongness Sakuya had picked up on gave off a pungent stench, like the scent of white face powder tainted by something foul, and if he were to put a reason to it, it had to be that figure clad in a furisode, for even supposing that her willowy figure was a masterful work of art, her stature was oddly tall. She was even taller than a gruff old man unabashedly dressing up as a geisha to lead an understaffed procession of street performers.

source.japanese: ……厭な予感はもうそこで捨て置いて、見猿決めこんで引き返せば良かったものを朔屋は、なんで鏡に映る顔を凝然確かめてしまったのか、いまだに後悔している。白粉厚く塗りたくり、べっとり紅を引いた化粧顔に、かの教師を見出してしまった事を今でも悔やんでいる。
source.english: …If only he had left that bad feeling alone, played see-no-evil and turned back. Why had he insisted upon examining the face in the mirror? He regretted it still. Still regretted recognizing his teacher beneath the thickly plastered white powder and smeared red lips.

source.japanese: 毒々しく女装した教師は、いやらしく身をくねらせ不気味にしなを作り、鏡に映じる変身にいたくご満悦の体、振袖の袂[たもと]で鏡の面を叩いたりしたのは、本人は侠[きゃん]な媚態のつもりなのかも知れないが、朔屋には蛇体になかば変じかかった清姫が、安珍の隠れた鐘を鱗[うろこ]の長胴巻きつけて締めあげているより、もっとずっと凄まじい光景に見えて仕方なく、その後どのようにして気づかれず退散したのか、どういう道筋で下宿まで戻ったのか、ろくろく覚えていない始末さ。
source.english: The teacher, luridly dressed as a woman, twisted lewdly and struck eerie, coy poses, plainly delighted with the transformation reflected in the mirror. He even slapped the glass with a long sleeve. Perhaps he thought it a saucy, seductive gesture. To Sakuya it was far more appalling than Kiyohime, half changed into a serpent, winding her long scaly body tight around the bell that hid Anchin. He scarcely remembered how he had escaped unseen, or which roads had brought him back to his boardinghouse.

source.japanese:
全くもって。
　人は誰しも余人の知らざる一面を持つ。
　とは繰り返される箴言であり───
source.english:
Indeed.
Everyone has a side unknown to others.
So went the oft-repeated maxim—

source.japanese: だから、シサムとキサラ、信天翁号の一等航海士の二人にも、朔屋の知らざる側面があったとしてもそれは当然の事であるが、にしてもこれは、青年は何度目になるのか、小屋の中を見回した。
source.english: Naturally, then, Sisam and Kisara, the Albatross's two chief mates, should have sides unknown to Sakuya. Even so, this was something else. For what must have been the umpteenth time, the young man looked around the hut.

target.text: ……By now, Sakuya really should have cast off his bad feeling and decided to act the part of the wise monkey, see-no-evil, so why was it, exactly, that he ended up frozen in place as he fixed his gaze on the face reflected in that mirror, something he still regretted even to this day? Even now, he lamented having seen that face, slathered in thick, white face powder, caked with sticky rouge, and recognizing his teacher beneath the mask.

His teacher, dressed in that loathsomely garish drag, twisted his body with obscenely suggestive affectations, struck uncanny, flirtatiously feminine poses, utterly delighted with the transformation reflected in the mirror; perhaps the man himself believed it to be pert, tomboyish coquetry, but in Sakuya's eyes, the sight could only seem even more ghastly than that of Kiyohime, halfway transformed into a serpentine body, coiling her long, scaly trunk around the bell Anchin was hiding under, and in what way exactly he managed to slip away unnoticed, or what route it was he took back to his lodgings, that he could scarce remember.
Verily. Every man harbours a side unknown to others. A well-worn maxim───

Therefore, even should Shisamu and Kisara, first mates of the Albatross, harbour a side unknown to Sakuya, that was only natural, but even so, this felt a little different, and the young man scanned the hut, wondering how many times he must have done so by now.

source.japanese: 土間に切られた炉には低く小さな炎が蜥蜴の舌の閃きのようにちろちろと、しかし絶やされることなく燃え続け、時折得体の知れない香草の、乾された束が放りこまれる度にぱっと火が炎となって、朔屋があの夜嗅いだ沈香とどこか似通う、そしてより異教的な刺激香を解き放つ。
source.english: In the hearth cut into the earthen floor, small flames flickered low as lizards' tongues, never quite going out. Now and then a bundle of unknown dried herbs was thrown in. The fire flared, releasing a pungent, more pagan scent somehow akin to the aloeswood of that remembered night.

source.japanese: 柱や屋根から細紐で束ねられ、小屋のそこらここらにぶら下げられているのは同様の乾した生薬達、ばかりではなく明らかに小動物の丸干しやらもっと大きな獣の内臓を煮干しにしたのやら。壁や床には、その手の博物館や専攻の教授先生なら垂涎モノの、あれは呪具の類だろう、異様な紋様施した仮面や盾、飾り杖、名前の判別もつかぬ奇品がずらずらずら、一つだけでも薄気味悪いのに、数が揃うと人間よりも強い意識力を蔵し、監視してくるような圧迫感さえ。屋根や内壁に張られた革は、さしずめ海豹辺りの革か。
source.english: From pillars and roof hung bundles of the same dried medicinals—and not only herbs, but small animals dried whole and the boiled-dry entrails of larger beasts. Walls and floor were crowded with objects to make a curator or professor in the relevant field salivate: ritual implements, surely—masks and shields worked with uncanny designs, ceremonial staffs, curiosities he could not begin to name, rank upon rank. Any one would have been eerie enough. Massed together, they seemed to harbor a consciousness stronger than man's, oppressive in its scrutiny. The hides stretched over roof and inner walls were sealskin, perhaps.

target.text: Down in the hearth dug into the earthen floor, a low flame flickered like the darting of a lizard's tongue, yet the fire never died out, it kept on burning, and every so often, a bundle of dried, unfamiliar herbs was thrown in, making it flare up into blazing flames, releasing a scent somehow reminiscent of the agarwood incense Sakuya had smelled that night, only sharper, more exotic in its paganistic intensity.

Similar bundles of dried medicinal herbs tied together with thin string could be seen hung here and there throughout the hut from the posts and the roof, and not only that, for beyond the herbs were what was also clearly whole dried small creatures, and even the innards of bigger beasts that had been boiled and dried.

On the walls and the floor were the sorts of things that museums or scholars specializing in the subject would drool over, likely tools used in magic incantations, masks and shields adorned with strange patterns, an ornate ceremonial staff, an endless stream of bizarre objects he couldn't discern by name, and merely one of these would be slightly unsettling, but when gathered in such numbers, they seemed to possess a power of consciousness stronger than that of man, even leaving him with the oppressive feeling that they were looming over him like silent watchers. The leather covering the roof and inner walls was presumably seal skin, or something similar.

source.japanese: ───もう、この時代でさえ廃[すた]れ始めた秘教冒険小説でしかお目に掛かれないような、記号を限度知らずに一つところに集めて臆面もなく叩きこんだような、典型的中の典型的な、『呪術師の住まい』だった。
source.english: —It was the archetypal ‘sorcerer's dwelling,’ as though every imaginable token from the occult adventure novels already falling out of fashion in that age had been gathered in one place without restraint and hammered in without shame.

source.japanese: もちろん炉の前にはちゃあんとご本尊、呪術師殿の御座る。それも、人をいったん木乃伊にして、それをば湯に漬けてもう一度戻しましてございの、一面余すところなく皺塗れでありながら妙に血色が良いという、呪力が高いという相はさだめしこんなのであろうと門外漢の朔屋にすら感じ入らせるほどのが、だ。
source.english: And before the hearth sat, of course, the presiding sorcerer himself. A man who looked as though he had first been mummified, then restored with a soak in hot water: not a patch of him unwrinkled, yet oddly healthy in complexion. Even the uninitiated Sakuya felt that such a face must surely signify mighty magical powers.

source.japanese:
シサム・キサラもまた余人の知らざる一面を有する、といって流石にこの舞台立ての中で、軍服に男装して、軍事革命の計画を練っていたりはない。香の匂いに誘われ、かの教師の女装を思い出して例の箴言を実感したのは朔屋の勝手、航海士の双子は青年には理解不能の言語を操っていただけだ。
　だが、それだけだが───
source.english:
Sisam and Kisara, too, had sides unknown to others. Not that, amid these trappings, they were dressed as men in military uniforms and planning an armed revolution. The incense had stirred Sakuya's memory of his cross-dressing teacher and made him ponder the maxim of his own accord. The navigators were merely speaking a language he could not understand.
Merely that—yet—

target.text: ───It was the sort you'd only see in those occult adventure novels that, even in this era, had already begun to fall out of favour, an overloaded collage of mystical symbols with no concept of restraint, hammered in with absolute shamelessness, most archetypal of archetypes, the quintessential 『Shaman's dwelling』.

And of course, right in front of the hearth sat the central figure, the shaman, in all his solemn glory. In addition, it was as if someone had first turned a person into a mummy, then soaked them in hot water to bring them back to life, leaving the skin entirely covered in wrinkles yet oddly flushed with colour all the same; so potent a sight was it that even Sakuya, a layman in such matters, felt it keenly: this was undoubtedly what great magical power looked like.

Shisamu and Kisara also harboured a side unknown to others, though that wasn't to say that, given this scenario they were in, they had cross-dressed in military uniform and were hatching plans for an armed revolution, nothing quite so dramatic. That the incense had stirred a memory of that teacher in drag, and that Sakuya had felt the truth of that aforementioned maxim anew, was entirely on his shoulders, for the twin mates simply repeated a bunch of words that were incomprehensible to the young man. But, that was all there was to it, yes, and yet───

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「───老師。聖双生児の伝承に関しては、ある程度知っているつもりなの」
source.english: “—Master. We believe we know something of the traditions of the Sacred Twins.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「───Elder. We consider ourselves to have a fair understanding of the legend of the Sacred Twins.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたし達が教えてほしいのは、
　三位一体者について」
source.english:
“What we would like you to teach us about is—
the Triune One.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「What we would like for you to tell us about is the Triune Being.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そして、これら二つに、なにかの関連性があるのか、という事」
source.english: “And whether there's any connection between the two.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「And finally, if there is some kind of relation between the two.」

source.japanese:
炉の埋もれ火に、鼻梁の陰翳濃く沈んでいたけれど、眸の光は知識に深い、考古学の研究室辺りに置けば、教授は色気を抜きにして双子を後継者にと教育するだろう。
　双子は呪術師と語らうにあたって、小屋にずかずか踏みこみどっかと胡座を降ろして開口一番不躾に問うた───のではない。
source.english:
The banked embers deepened the shadows along the bridges of their noses, yet their eyes shone with profound learning. Set them down in an archaeology department and a professor would have trained them as successors without one lustful thought.
The twins had not barged into the sorcerer's hut, plunked themselves down cross-legged, and rudely blurted out their questions.

source.japanese: 小屋を訪のう際にも、扉幕を潜[くぐ]る前にまず問答の、朔屋には暗号としか思えない奇妙な文句を長々とやりとりし、しかもそれを三度繰り返した。それで入[い]るを許されたが、双子は話よりまず貢ぎ物、名前も知れない野の鳥と草々（それさえ適当に選んだのではなく、然るべき基準によって選ばれたものらしい）を差し出して、それでようやく対話かと思えばまだあって、朔屋は恐らくそこで初めて双子の歌というのを聞いた。
source.english: Before passing through the curtained entrance, they had exchanged at length a series of strange phrases that sounded to Sakuya like a code—and repeated the exchange three times. That won them entry, but before any conversation came offerings: wild birds and herbs he could not name, apparently chosen not at random but according to proper criteria. Surely now they would talk? Not yet. It was then, probably for the first time, that Sakuya heard the twins sing.

source.japanese:
が、二人の唇に似合うような、当世風の歌謡曲などではなく、経でも詠ずるような、単調な、ワンフレーズを掛けてようやく一つ音階が上がるような歌だった。聞いているだけで居眠りしかけて、双子に脇腹ひどく抓[つね]りあげられてまだ痛い。
　その朗唱がどうやら正しい作法を踏んでいたようで、ようやく老呪術師は、棍棒ほどにも馬鹿でかくて重い煙管を、二人に回したのが、朔屋にはとんと意味不明だったが、それが訪問承諾の符号だったらしい。
source.english:
It was no fashionable popular song suited to their lips, but a monotonous chant like the recitation of scripture, one full phrase required to climb a single note. Merely listening nearly put Sakuya to sleep; the twins pinched his flank so hard that it still hurt. Their chanting had apparently observed the proper forms.
At last the old sorcerer passed them a pipe absurdly large and heavy as a club. Sakuya had no idea what it meant, but this, apparently, signaled acceptance of their visit.

source.japanese: かくも七面倒なやりとりなぞ、朔屋がかつて映画館で観た股旅物の渡世人達の旅の作法や仁義の切り方くらいしか心当たりはないが、部外者の理解を拒[こば]む、煩雑な儀式を要求される共同体は世の中に幾らでもあるのだろう。
source.english: The only comparable exchange Sakuya knew was the formal greetings and traveling etiquette of wandering outlaws in films he had seen. But there must be any number of communities in the world that demand elaborate rituals opaque to outsiders.

source.japanese: それ自体には別段異見はないけれど、そんな世界を双子達が知っており、その中での礼法を心得ていたのは、朔屋には全くもって、二人の余人には知られざる一面、なのだった。
source.english: He had no particular objection to that. What was wholly new, wholly a side unknown to others, was that the twins knew such a world, and knew how to conduct themselves within it.

source.japanese:
【老呪術師】
「聖双生児と───三位一体者とな。
　それは北限の秘奥にまつわる言い伝え。
　お主達、心得ておるのか。
　語られざる話を───」
source.english:
“The Sacred Twins—and the Triune One.
Traditions touching the deepest secrets of the northern limit.
Are you acquainted with them?
The tales not told—”

source.japanese: 双子の問いを受けて、開いた口元は重々しい、普段なら不心得者相手には彫像の如く沈黙で相対するのが窺える口元の皺の深さ、なのに老呪術師は、双子の礼法よほどよろしきを心得ていたと見え、訥々と、それでも糸を繰り出すように途切れなく、問いを受けては答え、語り続ける。
source.english: His mouth opened gravely to their questions. Its deep wrinkles suggested a man who ordinarily met the unworthy with a statue's silence. But the twins evidently knew the proper forms very well. Slowly, haltingly, yet without interruption, like drawing out a thread, the old sorcerer received their questions, answered, went on speaking.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（そして、俺は……。
　なんだってここにいるんだ……？）
source.english:
(And me…
Why the hell am I here…?)

source.japanese:
───信天翁号は、いまもって北上中。
　この度の航海は、ご禁制だったりどこからか横流ししてきたりの、どんな難癖つけられても文句は言えない荷を扱っているわけではなく、前払い金を貰えている、という希有な状況にあるせいで、普段なら行く先々の港で着手する、水夫長辺りが『真っ当な商取引』と唱える阿漕なお駄賃稼ぎというか詐欺行為の必要もなく、従って追っ手もかからず恨みを買った同業者の報復も官憲の手を患わせる事もなく、今のところは航海は順調と言えた───信じがたい事ではあるが。
　……ま、朔屋と双子が一夜を過ごしたあの港ではそのなんだ、一悶着がなかったわけではないが、反撃されるような禍根は、鉄火もて断ってきてある。
source.english:
The Albatross was still heading north.
This voyage carried none of the prohibited or diverted cargo that would leave them unable to complain, whatever charge was laid against them. Rarer still, they had been paid in advance. Thus there was no need for the crooked sidelines and petty frauds the boatswain called ‘honest commerce,’ ordinarily practiced in every port; no pursuers, no reprisals by aggrieved colleagues, no trouble with the authorities. So far the voyage could be called smooth—incredible though that was.
Well. At the port where Sakuya and the twins had spent the night, there had been a certain disturbance. But gunfire had severed any roots from which retaliation might grow.

source.japanese: 今のところの信天翁号は、世界地図を繰り開いてみて、そうさな、横に四分割の線を引き、一番上と二番目の区画を区切る分割線に差しかかるかどうかの辺り。針路の予定としては北亜米利加大陸とユーラシア大陸が内緒話を交わそうと突き出した耳の隙間の様な海峡を抜けて北限氷土に挑もうか、というところ。北亜米利加大陸の沿岸を鳶[とんび]伝いに北上中で、時折補給の為に寄港する港も、次第次第に小規模に、鄙びて裏ぶれて、船員達も陸に揚がる楽しみが少なくなってきている。
source.english: Unfold a world map, divide it into four horizontal strips, and the Albatross was somewhere approaching the line between the top and the second. The plan was to pass through the strait between North America and Eurasia, their ears thrust out as if to whisper secrets to one another, then challenge the Northern Ice Wastes. They were hopping north from port to port along North America's coast. Occasional provisioning stops grew gradually smaller, remoter, shabbier. The sailors found less and less pleasure ashore.
