source.japanese: これは信天翁号が悶着を避ける為、彼らを知る者が少ない港＝船の行き来の頻繁でない港を選んでいるせいだが、朔屋にとってはお姉さんと遊べるような酒場も少なくなってきているわ、気候も寒冷になってきているわで、以前までは寄港というと、いそいそと普段は仕舞い込んである私服の日乾しと酒代花代の調達に積み荷の私的流用にかかる彼にして、港に着いても船室でうつらうつらしているか、機関室の手伝いをするかが多くなってきていた───これも、信じがたい事ではあるが。
source.english: To avoid trouble, the Albatross chose ports where fewer people knew them: ports with little ship traffic. For Sakuya, there were fewer bars where he could play with women, and the weather was turning cold. Once, a port call had sent him eagerly airing the civilian clothes normally kept packed away, pilfering cargo to raise money for drink and women. Now he often dozed in his cabin even in port, or helped in the engine room. This, too, was incredible.

source.japanese: 今日久方ぶりに陸の地面を踏んだのも、シサム・キサラが船から下りるのをたまさか目撃して慌ててついてきただけの事であり、朔屋自身に確たる目的などあろう筈もない。
source.english: Today he had set foot on land for the first time in a while only because he happened to see Sisam and Kisara going ashore and hurried after them. No definite purpose of his own, of course.

source.japanese: せいぜいがところ、あわよくば双子が酔った勢いとか、地方の怪しげな精力剤に手を出したとかで淫心催す機会あらば逃さず捕まえて、また愉[たの]しい一夜を過ごしたい、などと虫の良い考えを抱いていた程度であるが、しかしその目論見も、船から下りて三時間ばかりも歩き、閑散とした漁港を出て更に閑散とした、自然が豊かな、といえば聞こえがいいが、羆に出くわす危険も考慮しなければいけないような原野にまで出てきた辺りで、「あー、そういえばあたし達、昨日から生理期間に入ってるから」との一言で粉砕された。さしもの朔屋もその周期にある女性に行為をせがむほどの見境無しでもないのである。血塗れになるし。
source.english: At most he hoped, conveniently enough, to seize any chance for another happy night if the twins grew amorous from drink or some dubious local aphrodisiac. But after three hours' walking, leaving a quiet fishing port for quieter wilderness—rich in nature, if one wanted a pleasant phrase, but also a place where meeting a brown bear must be reckoned with—that ambition shattered when one of them remarked, ‘Oh, by the way, our periods started yesterday.’ Even Sakuya was not so indiscriminate as to beg a woman for sex at that time. He would get blood all over him.

source.japanese: （ただ朔屋にもう少しの洞察力と知識の有れば、月経中にある女を呪術師が、小屋への訪問を許可するはずがないと言う事に思い当たったはずではあるが）
source.english: (Had Sakuya possessed a little more insight and knowledge, he would have realized that the sorcerer would never admit a menstruating woman to his hut.)

source.japanese: もうその段になると、一人で引き返すのもつまらない、というか道に迷った挙げ句助けを求める人家もないような山林の中で夜を迎える可能性濃厚になってきたので、双子から離れられなくなっていたわけで、『なんだってここにいるんだ』と問うなら、自分の胸に手を当ててみよとしか言いようがない。
source.english: By then turning back alone seemed dull. More importantly, he was increasingly likely to get lost and spend the night in woods where there would be no house at which to seek help. He could no longer leave the twins. If he asked why he was here, there was nothing to say but: put a hand to your heart and ask yourself.

source.japanese: かく往生際悪く、後悔の尻尾を噛み続けていた朔屋だが、そんな彼の疑問の種々の中でも、何故に航海士の双子が、このような前近代的湿潤に満ち満ちた世界へ今さら踏みこんでいくのか、という問いはそこまで異なものでもないだろう。
source.english: So Sakuya clung to regret, worrying at its tail, unwilling to accept his lot. Among his many questions, though, one was not altogether strange: why would the twin navigators now venture into a world so drenched in premodern murk?

source.japanese: なるほど青年の邦[くに]でも、町では陰陽師崩れの拝み屋が一つの文化装置として機能し、山間ではまだまだ迷信厭勝の類が幅を利かせている事は朔屋も心得ている。
source.english: In his own country, admittedly, the towns had prayer-healers, washed-up diviners of the old yin-yang school, who served a cultural function. In the hills, superstition and charms still held sway. Sakuya knew as much.

source.japanese: ……時代としてはまだまだそういう時代である。しかしそれでも朔屋には、どう考えてもシサムとキサラがこの手の前科学的科学に関する事柄に進んで踏みこんでいくような、そういう女達ではなかろうという思いこみが先に立っていた為、違和感を禁じえずにはいられなかった。
source.english: Such were still the times. Yet Sakuya had always assumed that Sisam and Kisara were simply not women who would eagerly enter into this sort of prescientific science. He could not help finding it incongruous.

source.japanese:
もちろん船乗りというのは基本的に迷信深いものである。一度海に出れば、『板子一枚下は地獄』という言葉はいまだ確かな実感を伴って意識され、人間が科学という力を手にした現在でも、どうにも制御できない自然力、あるいは超自然力諸々が存在している事は厭[いや]でも思い知らされる。鈍感な朔屋でさえもだ。
　色々と験を担ぎ、迷信を信じたくなる気持ちは理解できる。
source.english:
Sailors, of course, were fundamentally superstitious. Once at sea, ‘one plank between you and hell’ remained a saying felt in the flesh. Even now, with the power of science in human hands, forces of nature—and perhaps forces beyond nature—remained altogether uncontrollable. The sea impressed that truth upon a man whether he liked it or not, even upon a dull soul like Sakuya.
He understood the impulse to observe auspicious customs and put one's faith in omens.

target.text: Though the low glow of the embers buried in the hearth cast deep shadows across the bridges of their noses, the gleam in their eyes was profoundly intellectual, and if they were appointed to an archaeology lab, a professor would likely groom the twins as his successors with no amorous motivations. Barging into the hut, flopping down cross-legged, and the second they opened their mouths to speak to the shaman, they fired off a rude question───that, they did not.

Even when approaching the hut, before slipping under the curtain hanging over the entrance, there was a lengthy exchange of questions and answers consisting of strange phrases that Sakuya could only interpret as being some kind of cryptic code, and they repeated it three whole times.

Once that was done, they were finally given permission to enter, but before speaking, the twins first paid tribute, offering to the shaman a wild bird and grasses he knew not the names of (and not even those were randomly chosen, instead seeming to be selected based on proper criteria), and just when he finally thought they would start their conversation, that was, in all likelihood, the first time Sakuya had ever heard the twins singing.

But it was not some contemporary pop tune of the sort that seemed to better suit their lips, it was like a sutra or a chant, a monotonous song, the kind where an entire phrase would unfold before the pitch of their voices moved up a single scale degree. He was about to doze off just listening to it, and the twins pinched him in the side so hard that it still throbbed with pain even now.

It seemed that the chanting was performed in accordance with the proper rites, for at long last, the old shaman passed the twins his pipe, a thing so absurdly massive and heavy it could be mistaken for a club, and though it went completely over Sakuya's head, that was apparently a signal that he consented to their visit.

It was such an absurdly complicated exchange, and Sakuya's only real frame of reference was the travel etiquette and ritualized greetings of the wandering gamblers from matatabi-mono he once saw at the cinema, but surely the world was filled with communities that demanded elaborate, opaque rituals to reject any attempts at comprehension by outsiders. (TN: Matatabi-mono, written "股旅物", is a Japanese film gerne about wandering gamblers, ronin, or yakuza who are bound by the code of the underworld and travel around as they gamble. Films like Hitori Ookami or Matatabi are examples of this genre.)

He didn't have any particular objections to that in itself, but that the twins knew of this world, and that they had also mastered its etiquette, now that was, without a question, a side the two harboured deep within, one wholly unknown to Sakuya.

【Old Shaman】 「The Sacred Twins─── and the Triune Being, is it. Those are legends tied to the hidden secrets of the northernmost reaches. Do you truly understand? That you ask to hear the tales that are left unspoken───」

In response to the twins' questions, his mouth opened with solemn dignity, lined with creases deep enough to suggest that it would normally face the unworthy and impudent with the silence of a stone statue, and yet the elder shaman seemed to judge that the twins had a very firm grasp on the correct etiquette, for haltingly, yet without pause, like reeling out a thread, he answered each question, continuing his narration.
【Naomasa】 （And then there's me……. Why exactly am I here again……?）
───The Albatross was still northbound.

Their voyage on this occasion did not involve handling any contraband or goods diverted through some manner of illegal channel, the sort that would leave them with no room to object in the face of scrutiny or fault-finding, no, they had received an advance payment, and as a result of these rare circumstances they found themselves in, gone was the need for what usually began at every port they visited, where someone like the Bosun would engage in his unscrupulous, petty profiteering, or rather, frauds and scams, that he swore up and down were "honest business dealings", and for the time being, you could even say it was smooth sailing ───as much as that beggared belief.

……Well, it wasn't as if there hadn't been, let's say, a bit of a scuffle back in that port where Sakuya had spent a night together with the twins, but the roots of any seeds of retaliation had already been cleanly severed with fire and steel.

As for the Albatross right now, were you to spread out a map of the world and, let's see here, draw lines dividing it horizontally into four equal quarters, she'd be somewhere near the line separating the topmost quarter from the second. As for their planned course, they were set to pass through that narrow strait nestled between the continents of North America and Eurasia, the one that looked as if the two continents were leaning their ears close to whisper a secret to each other, and from there, they would brave the northernmost permafrost.

They were in the midst of making their way northward by hopping along the shores of North America like a black kite; the ports they occasionally made calls at for resupplying gradually grew smaller and smaller in scale, more shabby and neglected, and the crew's excitement to go ashore also grew smaller in turn.

This was so the Albatross could avoid running into any trouble; they deliberately chose ports where few knew of them, which equaled ports with infrequent ship traffic; consequently, there were also less bars of the sort where Sakuya could find a nice lady to have some fun with, and the climate had also grown colder, so even he, a man who would happily spring into action whenever they made port in the past, airing out his shore clothes that were usually stowed away and quietly skimming some cargo to fund his drink and women, upon arriving at port, was mostly dozing off in his cabin or helping out in the engine room ───though this, too, beggared belief.

Today was the first time he was stepping on solid ground in a good while, but it was only because he'd happened to witness Shisamu and Kisaru disembarking, then chased after them in a hurry, so it wasn't as if Sakuya himself had any clear goal in mind.

At absolute best, he was only indulging in some self-serving wishful thinking, hoping that, if luck was on his side and the twins happened to get in the mood, be it from getting drunk or dabbling in some suspicious local aphrodisiac, he would be able to seize that moment before it could slip away and spend another pleasant night together, but.

When the twins had walked for a good three hours after getting off the ship, leaving the deserted fishing harbour for somewhere even more quiet, somewhere rich in nature, and perhaps it sounded nice when put that way, but as they reached the sort of wilderness where one would need to seriously consider the danger of encountering a brown bear, even those hare-brained schemes of his were crushed into pieces by the words "ah, come to think of it, we did just start our period yesterday"; even someone like Sakuya wasn't so indiscriminate that he would pester a woman on her period for sex. He'd end up a bloody mess.
(However, had Sakuya possessed even just a little more insight and knowledge, he would have realized that no shaman would permit a menstruating woman to enter his hut.)

Having already come this far, it also felt like a waste to just turn back by his lonesome, or rather, there was a very high probability that, after taking a wrong turn, he'd have to spend the night in a montane forest that seemed bereft of any dwellings where he might seek aid, meaning he was left with no choice but to stick to the twins; therefore, were he to ask "why exactly am I here again?", then all one could tell him in return was to try putting his hand to his own heart.

Unwilling to let it go thus, Sakuya kept gnawing at the tail of his own regret, but amongst the many doubts swirling in his mind, it was hardly so strange a question to ask why these twin mates would, now of all times, choose to venture into a world so drenched with archaic clamminess.

Certainly, even in the young man's home country, there were also washed-up onmyouji turned spiritual hustlers who functioned as part of the cultural fixtures in towns, and the likes of superstitions and warding charms still enjoyed great influence in the mountains; that much the young man was well aware of. (TN: Onmyouji, written "陰陽師", were official court functionaries from the Nara to the Heian period, essentially holding the role of state-sanctioned diviners, exorcists, ritualists, and advisors.)

……It was still an age steeped in those ways. But even so, no matter how he looked at it, Kisara and Shisamu surely weren't the sort of women who'd willingly engage with this kind of proto-scientific science; that assumption took precedence within Sakuya, and so he was unable to suppress his discomfort.

Of course, sailors are fundamentally a deeply superstitious lot. After having been to sea but once, the reality of the old saying 『There is but a plank between a sailor and eternity』 is felt with conscious conviction, and you become painfully aware that, even in this present day where man has harnessed the power of science with his own hands, there exist many forces of nature, or perhaps even supernatural ones, that defy any attempts at control. Even the thickheaded Sakuya was no different. He could understand why one would come to want to believe in all kinds of superstitions, and to act on them.

source.japanese:
ただし、だとしてもそれらは畏怖、ないしは敬意によって、『よくない事』の累が我が身に降りかからないでくれよと祈る、いわゆる禁忌を避けたり遠ざけたりせんとする精神性だ。
　宗教学のセンセイ辺りに言わせれば『消極的呪術』にまつわる事柄で、自然力超自然力、それらの諸力を自ら操ろうとする積極的呪術者とは異なる筈で云々云々───要するに朔屋は、心の平静の為に寺社の御護り、教会のロザリオなど持つ事辺りまでは許容できても、日照りだからと雨乞いしたり、誰ぞに呪いをかけたり、といった事柄には忌避感を抱かざるをえず、双子がその手の事柄に積極的に噛みこんでいくことに関しても、正直なところ胡散臭さを感じてしまってならなかったのである。
source.english:
Even so, those superstitions arose from fear or reverence: a prayer that the consequences of some ‘bad thing’ might not descend upon oneself. It was the mentality that shunned taboos and kept them at a distance.
A professor of religion might have called this ‘negative magic,’ as distinct from the positive magician who sought to command the powers of nature and supernature himself, et cetera, et cetera. Put simply, Sakuya could tolerate a shrine amulet or church rosary carried for peace of mind; rainmaking in a drought or laying curses on people aroused an instinctive revulsion. And truth be told, the twins' active involvement in that sort of thing smelled suspicious to him.

source.japanese:
……そして老呪術師の話はまだ続いている。
　炉から流れ出る薫香とともに、不思議の言葉が綴られる。それらの言葉の中には、青年にもちらほらと聞き覚えのある語が混じっていなくもなく、かといって全体が理解できるわけでもない。織物のうちの、一本の糸だけを辿っていって全体の模様が見えないような、そんなもどかしさがある。
source.english:
…The old sorcerer was still talking.
Strange words came strung together with the incense drifting from the hearth. Here and there the young man recognized a term, but that did not make the whole comprehensible. It was like tracing one thread through a fabric and being unable to see the pattern of the whole. Maddening.

target.text: However, that was something driven by fear, or maybe even reverence, offered up as a prayer that any misfortune stemming from『Bad Things』 may pass one by, a psychological tendency to keep clear of or ward off any so-called taboos. Were one to ask a professor of religious studies, this would fall under the category of matters related to『Apotropaic Magic』, which is, of course, quite different from the arts of the active sorcerers who attempt to manipulate the various natural or supernatural forces themselves, and so on and so forth───

In essence, Sakuya could tolerate things like keeping around amulets and charms from shrines or temples for the sake of maintaining inner peace, or carrying a church rosary, but when it came to things like praying for rain because there was a drought, or casting curses on others, he couldn't help but feel a strong aversion, and truth be told, he found it hard not to harbour some suspicion towards the twins' eagerness to get involved in such matters.

……And the old shaman's tale was still going. Together with the incense drifting from the hearth, mysterious words were woven together. It wasn't as though there weren't a few words mixed in that rang a bell for the young man, but with that said, he could still not possibly hope to understand it as a whole. He felt somewhat frustrated, like he was tracing a single thread through a tapestry, unable to see the full pattern.

source.japanese: 北上していくにつれ、気候が寒くなっていく。寒い島々、沿岸を巡って、なぜかシサム・キサラはそこに住む現地の人々、呪術師と会話を重ねるようになる。
source.english: As they sailed north, the climate grew colder. Among the frigid islands and coasts, for some reason Sisam and Kisara began holding repeated conversations with the local inhabitants and their sorcerers.

source.japanese:
彼女たちが求めて聞き出そうとしているのは、双子に関する伝承と、三位一体を表象するモノを奉ずる人々がどこかにいなかったかという事。
　呪術師は、かつて北海のとある集落に、畏怖と同時に禁忌でもって扱われていた双子がいた事を語る。セントエルモの火の伝承も絡めて。
source.english:
They sought traditions concerning twins, and whether anywhere there had been people worshipping something that embodied a trinity.
The sorcerer spoke of twins once regarded with both awe and taboo in a certain settlement of the northern seas, weaving in traditions of St. Elmo's fire.

target.text: The further north they headed, the colder the climate grew. As they made their way around the shores of these frigid islands, Shisamu and Kisara had, for whatever reason, repeatedly engaged in conversation with the locals and their shamans.

What they were trying to uncover through their inquires was whether there were people somewhere who yet worshipped twin-related legends and symbols representing the Triune Being. The shaman told the tale of a pair of twins who once lived in a certain North Sea settlement, who were treated with equal parts awe and taboo. It was intertwined with the legend of St. Elmo's fire as well.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「三位一体者は、一体いかなる観念の象徴なのか。あるいは、神話においてなんの役割を果たすのか」
source.english: “What idea does the Triune One symbolize? Or what role does it play in myth?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「What concept, exactly, does the Triune Being symbolize? Or alternatively, what role does it serve within the realm of myth?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それに……なにか基準があるの？
　人が三位一体者足りうるには……」
source.english:
“And… Are there criteria?
For a person to be a Triune One…?”

source.japanese: 身を乗り出して訊ねる、キサラの横顔に炉の燠火が照って変に黄色く、青年にはその肌の色や輪郭の線が、どうにも見慣れない。完全に見知らぬ女ならともかく、今まで知っていた者が忽然と別人物に化してしまったような、そんな違和感さえある。
source.english: As Kisara leaned forward to ask, the embers cast a queer yellow light over her profile, and to the young man the hue of her skin, the very lines of her face, looked somehow unfamiliar. Were she a perfect stranger, that would be one thing; this was the disquiet of seeing someone he had known abruptly transformed into someone else.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And also……is there some kind of criterion? For what qualifies one to become a Triune Being……」

Leaning forwards as she asked, the glow from the embers in the hearth lit the skin of her profile in a queer yellow, and to the young man, her skin tone and the lines of her face looked wholly unfamiliar. It would be one thing if she were a complete stranger, but it was as if someone he'd known well until now had abruptly transformed into a completely different person; it left him with such a discomfort.

source.japanese:
【老呪術師】
「全ては───世界の果てより来たりしものなれば───」
source.english: “All things—having come from the ends of the world—”

target.text: 【Old Shaman】 「Since all that exists───has come from beyond the world's edge───」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「では何故、セントエルモの灯が一対で現れる時は、それが安全な旅を約束するの？
　セントエルモの灯は、三つで現れる事はなかった？」
source.english:
“Then why, when St. Elmo's fire appears as a pair, does it promise a safe voyage?
Has it never appeared in threes?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「So then why is it that whenever St. Elmo's fire appears as a pair, it promises safe passage? Has St. Elmo's fire never appeared as three?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「老師───北方の聖双生児を祀る邑[ムラ]の言い伝えでは、もう少しあらましが異なっていたわ。何故なの？」
source.english: “Master—the traditions of the village that worships the northern Sacred Twins gave a somewhat different account. Why?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Elder───the oral traditions of the northern villages that worship the sacred twins take a slightly different form. Why is that?」

source.japanese:
ああ、まただ、と朔屋は二人の語る言葉から耳を滑らせ、努めて深くは聞かないようにして。
　……炉の上で展開される異界の情景めいた会話の中に、朔屋の記憶と連想を刺激する言葉が時折混じるのも、青年を落ち着かない心地にさせて、眉をひっそりとひそめさせて。
　例えば、セントエルモの灯。その言葉、近頃何処かで聞いた、その何処か……それは確か、あの奇妙な難破船にて。
source.english:
Ah, there it was again. Sakuya let their words slide past his ears, deliberately refusing to listen too closely.
…Yet now and then, amid that conversation like a scene from another world unfolding over the hearth, came a word that pricked the young man's memory and set his thoughts running. That too made him uneasy and quietly drew his brows together.
St. Elmo's fire, for example. He had heard those words somewhere lately. Where had it been…? Yes: aboard that strange wreck.

source.japanese:
例えばその聖双生児がなんとやら。北方でどうのと聞こえるけれど、シサムとキサラもまた、どこかは知らねど北の方の生まれだと言っていなかったか。その上双子だというのも重なる。
　このように朔屋にも聞き覚えがある言葉が混ざるのに、それでは、と聞き入ると肝腎な話の中身がてんで理解しきれない。
source.english:
Then these Sacred Twins, whatever they were. Something about the north. Had not Sisam and Kisara said they, too, came from somewhere in the north? And they were twins.
Familiar words mingled like this, but whenever Sakuya tried to attend, he could not comprehend the essential substance at all.

source.japanese: 谿の向こうに咲いた花の、反対側より眺める間は判然と見えているのに、それではとその嶺[みね]に移って探しに登ると林中に迷ってたどり着けやしないのもどかしさ、だから朔屋は聞き覚えのある言葉であったとしても、あえて逸らす注意、これはこれで集中して聞き入るよりも疲れさせる。
source.english: A flower blooming across a valley: plainly visible from the other side, yet go to that ridge and climb to find it, and you lose yourself in the trees, never reaching it. That frustration. Sakuya deliberately turned his attention aside even from words he knew. The effort tired him more than attentive listening would have.

source.japanese:
双子に誘われたでもなく、ついてきたのは朔屋の勝手、なのだけれど、このような前時代がそのまま切り取られて現存しているかの呪術師の小屋の中、日頃慣れ親しんだ、と思ったはずの女達が理解の及ばないようなそうでないような会話を、かぎ慣れない燻煙と火の小さくふすべる響きを枕に延々と。
　……ちくちくと疎外感が刺して来ない方が不思議の、朔屋はひたすらに双子が話を切り上げてくれるその時を念じ続ける……。
source.english:
The twins had not invited him. He had followed of his own accord. Yet in this sorcerer's hut, a piece of a former age preserved intact, women he had thought he knew so well talked endlessly about things almost comprehensible, or not, with unfamiliar smoke and the soft mutter of flame as their accompaniment.
How could he fail to feel those little pricks of exclusion? Sakuya wished only, endlessly, for the moment they would finish…

target.text: Aah, they're still going, Sakuya thought as he let their words wash over him, doing his utmost to not listen too closely to them. ……As the conversation above the hearth unfolded like a scene one might witness in the realm of spirits, at times came words that stimulated Sakuya's memories and drew out the associations woven into them, words that brought to Sakuya a feeling of restless unease, made his brows gently furrow. For instance, St. Elmo's fire. Those words, he'd heard them somewhere recently, and that somewhere…… right, it was on that strange shipwreck.

And take for example those sacred twins or whatever. He'd heard something or other about those and the north, but Shisamu and Kisara, again, while he knew not from where, had they not said something about being born in the north? Furthermore, the fact they are twins also overlapped. In this manner, certain words that sounded familiar to Sakuya surfaced within the conversation, and yet when Sakuya truly tried to listen, the actual essence of the discussion was altogether impossible for him to fully grasp.

What maddening frustration it was to so clearly see a flower blooming across the ravine from afar, then try to cross to that ridge in search of it only to lose your way in the woods, never to reach it; that was why, even though there were certain words that had a familiar ring, he deliberately averted his attention, and this in itself demanded quite a bit of concentration, tiring him out faster than had he just tried to intently listen.

It wasn't as though the twins had invited him; Sakuya had simply followed them of his own free will, however, inside this shaman's hut, which seemed as if a slice of a bygone era had been carved out of the past and preserved in the present, these women, who he thought he had come to know and grown closer to through their days spent together, were having the sort of conversation that seemed at once to be beyond his understanding yet not entirely, cushioned on a pillow of the strange, unfamiliar scent of this smoke and the soft crackling of the fire, dragging on and on.
……It would have been a miracle not to feel the sharp prickle of alienation; Sakuya did nothing but endlessly pray for the moment the twins would finally wrap up their conversation…….

source.japanese: 糸杉の列を横目にし、白樺の林を越えて、月に照らされる低木の中の小径を辿って、といえば壮大なる景色の中に乗り出した風情だが、老呪術師の小屋を出て、帰りの路の長さに身構えた朔屋だったのに、想像していた時間の三分の二も過ぎないうちに港に戻ってきていて拍子抜け。
source.english: Past rows of cypress, through birch woods, along a path among moonlit shrubs: it sounded like a venture into grand scenery. Leaving the old sorcerer's hut, Sakuya braced himself for a long return. Yet before even two-thirds of the time he expected had elapsed, he was back at the port. The easy return left him oddly deflated.

source.japanese: 行きは全く知らぬ世界ときょろきょろしていたから長く感じられただけで、実際にはそこまでの距離ではなかったのだろう。子供が近所に意外なほど暗く密な林を発見し、その中を胸ときめく想いで漕いで、かつて使われていた古道などに行き会い、いよいよこれは油断ならない、隠された世界に通じる抜け道、と身構えて抜けると出たのは家の裏手だった、という時の肩すかしの感、といっては言い過ぎか。
source.english: Perhaps the outward trip had felt long only because he kept looking about an unfamiliar world. The distance might not really have been so great. Like a child finding an unexpectedly dark, dense wood nearby, pushing excitedly through it, discovering an old disused road, deciding this must be a passage to some hidden world—and emerging behind his own house. Or was that too much of an anticlimax?

source.japanese: いかに呪術師、シャーマンと言えども、人界から完全に隔絶した未踏の地に生きているわけではなく、どちらかと言えば人里と野の境に居を構えている事が普通という事を、朔屋が知らなかっただけで。
source.english: Sorcerers and shamans did not, after all, live in unexplored lands wholly cut off from mankind. More commonly they made their homes on the border between village and wild. Sakuya had merely not known it.

source.japanese: 下手を打てばどこかの窪地で野宿か、季節は夏の終わりにさしかかった頃合いだが、陽が落ちれば釣瓶落としに冷え込む地方で、えらい事になったと半ば覚悟の朔屋としては有り難い、ほっと気が抜けてみれば、共に歩む双子達はやっぱりいつもの彼女達で、老呪術師の小屋で受けた別人の印象は、仮面を脱いだように失せていた、これにもほっとした。ようやく話しかけてみる余裕も生まれてくる。
source.english: If things went badly he might have to camp in some hollow. Summer was nearing its end, but this was a region where the temperature dropped like a well bucket the moment the sun went down; Sakuya had half resigned himself to disaster. The easy return was therefore a blessing. Once relief had taken the tension out of him, the twins walking beside him looked like their usual selves again. The impression of strangers he had received in the sorcerer's hut had fallen from them like a mask. That too was a relief. At last he felt at ease enough to speak.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なあシサムさ、さっきの話は、ありゃいったいなんだ？　ああいう呪[まじな]い師の言葉がわけわからないのは当然としても、あんた達だって同じような言葉で」
source.english: “Hey, Sisam. What was all that talk about? I'd expect a sorcerer to be incomprehensible, but you two were using the same kind of words.”

target.text: They spared the row of cypresses but a glance as they passed them by, crossed through the birch forest, then followed a path cutting through shrubbery bathed in moonlight, and if he had to say, it really did give him the impression of setting out on a journey through magnificent scenery, but for all that Sakuya had braced himself for the long road back home after leaving the old shaman's hut, they managed to make it back to the port in no more than two-thirds of the time he had imagined it would take, leaving him a bit deflated.

On the way there, it had only felt so long because he had been restlessly looking around everywhere as he travelled through a completely unfamiliar world, but in reality, it probably hadn't been that far at all. A child discovered an unexpectedly dark and dense forest in the neighbourhood, and heart throbbing with anticipation, pushed through it, encountering something like an ancient trail; no dropping my guard now, this is a secret path leading into a hidden realm, the child would steel himself, only to emerge in his own backyard; it was the anticlimax of that moment he was feeling, though perhaps saying that was an exaggeration.

No matter how mystical their titles of sorcerer, of shaman, they did not live in some uncharted land entirely cut off from the world of man; if anything, it was normal for them to take up residence on the border between human habitation and the wilderness; Sakuya was simply ignorant of this fact.

Had he made a mistake on the way back, perhaps he would have had to spend the night outside in some hollow in the ground; the season had reached the cusp of summer's end, but this was a region where the cold dropped in as swiftly as the sun set, rushing in like a bucket falling down a well, so as someone who'd halfway resigned himself for a real disaster, Sakuya was grateful.

Feeling spent, once the tension left, the twins he was walking with were still the same women he'd known for a while now after all, and the impression he'd gotten of them as entirely different people in the old shaman's hut had vanished like a discarded mask, and this, too, made him sigh in quiet relief. He had finally found the composure needed to try talking to them.

【Naomasa】 「Hey, Shisamu, your conversation earlier, what the hell was that all about? Sure, it's only to be expected that some sorcerer like that guy would speak in incomprehensible riddles, but you two weren't being any less cryptic.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんだって言われてもさ……一から話すとエライ長話になるんで……それもまたエライ退屈な……それでも聞きたい？」
source.english: “What was it about…? If I start from the beginning, it'll be one hell of a long story. One hell of a boring story too. You still want to hear it?”

source.japanese:
───格別にシサムに厭[いと]うた様子はなかったけれど。聞き返してきたのだって、彼女が真に退屈と思っている風であり、朔屋を脅かすつもりもないようだったけれど。
　なのに朔屋は、ふと彼女の言葉、それを口にした時の佇まいに見たのは翳[かげ]り、疲れと憂さを秘めた。踏み込むには覚悟のいる間合いと見てあっさり引いたのは、賢明だったのか、単に臆病なのか。
source.english:
—Not that Sisam had seemed particularly reluctant. Even her question sounded as if she truly found the subject tedious, not as if she meant to frighten him off.
And yet, all at once, Sakuya had glimpsed in her words—in the way she held herself as she spoke them—a shadow harboring weariness and dejection. He took it for a distance that required some resolve to cross, and promptly withdrew. Was that wisdom, or mere cowardice?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……かいつまんでお願いします」
source.english: “…The short version, please.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Look, say what you will, but…… if I start from the beginning, it's going to be a ridiculously long story……and a stupidly boring one, too……you sure you still want to hear it?」

───Shisamu didn't seem particularly loath to do it. That she asked him in return really did make it seem to be because she genuinely thought it would be boring, and not because she intended to scare off the young man. And yet, what Sakuya saw, suddenly, and just for a moment, in her words, or more accurately, her demeanour as she spoke them, was a shadow of gloom, one hiding beneath it weariness and melancholy. He readily pulled back as soon as he judged that this was a threshold that demanded a certain resolve to cross; was this wisdom, or was it just cowardice?
【Naomasa】 「……Can you give me the short version, please?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「都合の良いヤツだなぁ……なんて言うのか、世の中にはある種の双子をあがめ奉る、ゴクローサンな連中がいるってコトと」
source.english: “You do like things easy… How to put it? There are people in the world who put themselves to the trouble of worshipping a certain kind of twins. And—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そのある種の双子って言うのは……」
source.english: “That certain kind of twins…”

source.japanese: 先ほどの呪術師の語りといい、これはどうにも彼女たちにまつわる事のようにしか思えなかったけれど、シサム、涼気に磨かれ澄んだ翡翠を溶かしたような緑の波に、防波堤に捨てられた、釣り具の錘[おもり]をぽしゃんと蹴り入れたきりでそれには答えず、
source.english: From the sorcerer's account, this could hardly be anything but a matter concerning the twins themselves. Sisam offered no answer. She merely kicked a discarded fishing sinker from the breakwater into the green waves, clear jade polished by the cool air and melted down. Plop—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Easy for you to say, isn't it…… how do I put it, there are some people out there with nothing better to do than revere and worship a certain kind of twins.」
【Naomasa】 「And that certain kind of twin would be……?」

Considering the shaman's narration from not too long ago as well, he just couldn't see this as anything other than something relating to these girls, but Shisamu simply kicked a discarded fishing sinker off the breakwater with a splash, sending it down beneath the green waves, polished and clear as liquefied jade in the cool air, leaving his question unanswered,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「三つ揃いのものを重要視する考えがあってね。二つと三つと。あたし等は、今それが気にかかってるんだ」
source.english: “There's a way of thinking that places importance on things in threes. Twos and threes. That's what's bothering us now.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だからあんな呪い師の小屋でお話か……でもこれ、船の連中は知ってて？」
source.english: “So that was what the visit to the sorcerer's hut was about… But do the others aboard know?”

source.japanese: この双子達が追いかけるなら、酒と儲けとそして快楽が相応しいと思い込む朔屋には、やはりそう簡単には納得のいく話ではなかったけれど、面と向かっては口にしづらいその想い、信天翁号の面子に仮託して問えば、
source.english: Sakuya had always assumed that drink, profit, and pleasure were the proper pursuits for these twins. Their turn toward the occult did not fit that picture. Unable to say as much to their faces, he framed his question instead as a concern about the rest of the Albatross's crew.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「There is a belief that places special importance on things that come in threes, okay. Twos and threes. That is what's weighing on our minds right now.」
【Naomasa】 「And that's why you went for a talk in some cursemonger's hut…… but, do the guys on the ship know about all this?」

Sakuya had always been convinced that if these twins were to chase after anything, it would be drink, profit, and pleasure, so this whole topic was something he found difficult to swallow, and when he asked about the crew of the Albatross, using them as a pretext for this feeling he found so hard to put into words when standing face-to-face with the twins,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「まーそのあたりの事は細かく気にしない。
　でも朔屋がそれをわざわざ告げ口しちゃったりするとぉ……」
source.english:
“Well, don't worry about the little details.
But if you go out of your way to tell on us…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Well, no need to obsess over the details on that end. But Sakuya, should you go out of your way to rat us out, well……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「朔屋君はある朝眼が醒めてみると、大事な大事な逸物が去勢されてました───なんて事になっちゃったりするかもよ」
source.english: “Mr. Sakuya may wake up one morning to find his precious, precious pride and joy gelded. Something like that.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やだなにそれおっかない」
source.english: “No thanks, that's scary.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「When little Sakuya-kun opens his eyes one morning, he might find that his most precious, most prized of possessions has been snipped off─── you never know if something like that might happen.」
【Naomasa】 「No way what the hell that's scary!」

source.japanese: 穏やかならざる言葉を、けれど冗談めかしてくれる辺りは、双子の朔屋に対しての親しみを語っていて、それが判れば今は充分と、青年もその時はおどけた口ぶりで笑ったのだけれど。
source.english: The words were anything but peaceful, yet the twins made a joke of them, and that spoke of their easy familiarity with Sakuya. For now, that reassurance was enough. He answered in the same playful tone and laughed.

target.text: Thought her words were far from soft and gentle, the fact they were dressed up as a joke still spoke of the affection the twins held for Sakuya, and once he realized that, for now, that was plenty for him, and at the time, the young man even laughed along with it, responding humorously in turn, but.

source.japanese: 後から思えばその時朔屋と口を聞いていたのはシサムだけ。キサラは黙りこくって夜の海の彼方を遠く眺めるばかり、遠く。考える事と口を聞く事、双子ならではの分担で、朔屋と語ってはいても彼女たちの心はこの時既に、遠く彼方を見つめていたのかも知れない。
source.english: Thinking back, only Sisam had spoken to him then. Kisara remained silent, gazing far out over the night sea. Far away. Thought and speech divided as only twins could divide them: though talking to Sakuya, perhaps their hearts were already fixed far beyond.

target.text: When he thought back on it later, it was only Shisamu whom Sakuya spoke with at the time. Kisara kept completely silent, simply staring into the distant beyond across the night sea, somewhere far, far away. Perhaps this was their way of allocating the burden of thinking and speaking as twins, and though they were in conversation with Sakura, by then, their hearts may well already have been gazing far beyond the horizon.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……見なかった事にしよう」
source.english: “…Let's pretend I didn't see.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……I'll just pretend I didn't see anything.」

source.japanese:
朔屋は、操舵室の扉を憚[はばか]る思いでそっと締めた。
　室内の作業台で見たものを見なかった事にしたけれど、それでも記憶というのはそうやって意識すればするほど深く刻まれる。
　普段は聞いたもの見たものを端から忘れて行くうつけ者なのに、要らぬ時に限って要らぬ事を覚えている典型だが、このときは朔屋を嘲る訳にもいくまい。その海図をわざわざしまい忘れた誰かがいけない。
source.english:
Sakuya closed the wheelhouse door softly, with some misgiving.
He pretended not to have seen what lay on the worktable, but memory cut deeper the more deliberately one tried to ignore it.
Ordinarily he was a fool who forgot each sight and sound as it came, the very type who remembered needless things only when they were unwanted. Yet here one could hardly mock him. Whoever had failed to put away that chart was at fault.

source.japanese:
その、誰かが───
　
　
　信天翁号の針路を歪めていたのだ。
source.english:
That someone—

had been bending the Albatross off her course.

target.text: Sakuya quietly closed the door to the wheelhouse, hesitation in his heart. He was pretending to not have seen what he had, in fact, just seen on the work table inside the room, but even so, memory is something that is only etched deeper into the mind the more conscious one becomes of it. Normally, he was the sort of blockhead who forgot everything no sooner than he had heard or seen it, he was a textbook case of only remembering something useless right when it was least needed, but this time, there was no excuse to scoff at Sakuya. The blame fell squarely on whoever had made a point of forgetting to put away that chart.
And that somebody─── Was tampering with the course of the Albatross.

source.japanese: 沿岸を港伝いに北上するという、所期の目的それ自体に変更は無いけれど、問題は港と港の間の航路。ごく単純な航路で進める筈が、海図に書き込まれた予定針路を見るに、一体何の鋸の歯か、というくらいのまさしくジグザグ航法で、ただでさえ鈍い信天翁号の船足なのにこれでは、『予定されていた本来の航海期間』よりずいぶんと時間をかける事になってしまう。
source.english: The original purpose remained unchanged: to work northward along the coast from port to port. The trouble lay in the routes between them. What ought to have been a simple course had been plotted into a zigzag worthy of a saw blade. The Albatross was slow enough already; this would lengthen the voyage far beyond the original schedule.

source.japanese:
本来の予定なら、北限氷土の探索に当たって、季節が夏の間になるように航路を設定していたはずだがこれでは───
　なぜわざわざ寒冷な時期を選ぼうとするのかと海図を睨[にら]んだところで答えが得られるはずもなく。
source.english:
The route should have been set to explore the Northern Ice Wastes while it was still summer.
But this—why deliberately choose a cold season? No amount of glaring at the chart would answer that.

source.japanese:
朔屋がこれを見なかった事にしたのは、こういう細工ができる者は船の中でごくごく限られると判じたからである。
　ただ、朔屋が口を噤[つぐ]んだところで、このように針路変更を物語る海図を迂闊に放置していては、いずれ───そしてそのいずれは、遠からず訪れるのだった。
source.english:
Sakuya chose to pretend he had seen nothing because only a very few people aboard were capable of tampering with the course this way.
Yet however tightly he kept his mouth shut, a chart advertising the change had been left lying carelessly in the open. Sooner or later—
and later would not be long in coming.

target.text: While their original goal of heading north along the coastline from port to port remained unchanged, the problem was the sea route between those ports. It should have been an extremely simple route, but when he looked at the planned course drawn on the chart, it was a zigzag so sharp it could've been mistaken for the teeth of a saw, and given the sluggish pace of the Albatross at the best of times, this would end up taking far more time than the voyage was originally scheduled for.

According to their initial schedule, their course had been planned so that their exploration of the northernmost permafrost would take place during the summer, but at this rate─── Not that he would get an answer to his question of why exactly someone would deliberately choose the cold season just from glaring at the chart.

As for the reason Sakuya had chosen to turn a blind eye to this, it was because he knew that there were only a very select few people who could even do this sort of tampering aboard the ship. However, even if Sakuya held his tongue, the fact that a chart speaking so clearly of alterations to their course had been carelessly left out in the open like this meant that, sooner or later───and that "sooner or later" came sooner rather than later.

source.japanese: 廃棄されるところだったオイルの缶の、その蓋にぼつぼつと千枚通しで孔を穿[うが]っていた朔屋である。これがもう少しまともな手であれば、孔も蜂の巣のように、までとはいかずともそこそこ整然と連なったであろうが、あいにくこの青年がやるとなると、大小てんでばらばらのアリジゴクのアパートのようになるのがオチで、不格好な事この上ない。
source.english: Sakuya was punching holes with an awl in the lid of an oil can destined for the trash. A more capable hand might have arranged them neatly, if not quite like a honeycomb. With this young man, inevitably, they became an apartment block of antlion pits, haphazardly large and small. The result could hardly have been uglier.

source.japanese:
……寒さが柔らかな厚みをもってくるんでくるような夜である。船は北海に入って久しく、船内の寒さいよいよ耐え難く、重ね着だけでは凌[しの]ぎきれない塩梅だがこれで実はまだ秋にさしかかったくらい。気の忙しい冬めが一つフライングをやらかしてくれた感がある。
　船内の朔屋の船室でさえそうなのだから、外などは今年初の雪がちらついてもおかしくはない。
source.english:
…A night when cold wrapped one in soft, thick layers. The ship had been in the northern seas for some time. The chill aboard was becoming unbearable; layers of clothing no longer sufficed. Yet autumn had only just begun. Impatient winter seemed to have jumped the gun.
If even Sakuya's cabin was like this, the year's first snow might well be fluttering outside.

source.japanese: 南の海では汗だくの煉獄だった機関室も、こうなると有り難いと入り浸ろうにも、そこは機関長の王国の、なかなかに出入国が厳しいというかなんというか、機関長が普段はやらない、紅茶にラム酒を垂らしたものを勧めてきたら退出の合図だという。これを飲み干してなお居座ろうとする者は、彼の人の勘気を蒙[こうむ]ってろくな目に遭わないとされ、その辺の機微に疎[うと]い朔屋などは、二杯目のラム入り紅茶を飲み干すか干さないかで異常な眠気に襲われて、目が覚めたら霙[みぞれ]混じりの雨の上甲板で大の字になって、低体温症に罹り損なった事があり、それ以来は油を売るにも節度を心がけるようになったのだから、ある意味機関長は教育者にも向いている。
source.english:
The engine room, a sweating purgatory in southern waters, now seemed so inviting that one might have moved in. Unfortunately, it was the chief engineer's kingdom, with strict immigration controls to match. If he offered tea with a dash of rum—a courtesy he never ordinarily extended—that was one's signal to leave. Anyone who drained the cup and lingered was said to incur his wrath and come to no good.
Sakuya, insensitive to such nuances, had once been overcome by unnatural drowsiness as he finished his second cup. He woke spread-eagled on the upper deck in sleet-laced rain, having narrowly escaped hypothermia. Ever since, he had practiced a certain moderation even in loafing. In that sense, perhaps the chief engineer did have a vocation as an educator.

source.japanese: ともかく、まともな暖房設備という福利厚生にもやはり乏しい信天翁号、暖を取るにも各人知恵を凝らす必要があり、朔屋も不器用な手で簡易焜炉を作成する必要に迫られた。言うまでもなく彼にとって最高の暖房とは裸の佳い女と一緒に布団にくるまる事であるが、その維持費支払い続けるだけの甲斐性有すなら、既に陸にて所帯でも構えていよう。
source.english: Proper heating was another employee benefit the Albatross conspicuously lacked. Everyone had to devise his own means of keeping warm, and Sakuya was reduced to fashioning a makeshift stove with his clumsy hands. Needless to say, the finest heating he could imagine was a beautiful naked woman beneath the same blankets. If he had possessed the means to pay that arrangement's upkeep, he would already have set up house ashore.

source.japanese: 一応双子のところに一冬の暖房を請うてお伺いをたてには参じてみたのだが、このところ彼女たちは何かの準備に忙しいらしく、しつこく食い下がったらいきなりドラム缶を抱かされ縛りつけられた。ぎゃあちべたいと悲鳴を上げる朔屋を尻目に双子達が一つ二つと数えながらドラム缶に放り込んでいく練炭の、ほどよく温まったのも最初の幾つかだけ。
source.english: He had duly called upon the twins to petition for their services as his heating for the winter. Lately, however, they seemed busy preparing something. When he persisted, they abruptly made him embrace an oil drum and tied him to it. Ignoring Sakuya's shrieks of ‘Cold!’ the twins counted one, two, as they tossed charcoal briquettes inside. Only the first few brought a pleasant warmth.

target.text: Puncturing the lid of an oil drum that was about to be discarded with an awl, digging little holes here and there, was Sakuya. And had he a slightly better technique, the holes could have been like a beehive, or even if not to that level, at least spread out in an orderly manner, but unfortunately, when this young man was responsible for the work, the only upshot would be something like an apartment building for antlions, uncoordinated and in all manner of sizes, the epitome of unsightly ungainliness.

……It was a night where the cold seemed to envelop you in a thick layer of velvet. The ship had been sailing through the northern seas for a good while now, and the cold aboard the ship had at long last grown unbearable, culminating in a situation where just layering your clothes would not be enough to stave off the cold, but it was actually only on the cusp of autumn. It felt like winter, ever restless, had made its visit ahead of schedule. That was how freezing it was, even in Sakuya's cabin inside the ship, so it would not be out of place should the year's first snow begin fluttering down outside.

Now that it had come to this, though he would love to hang around the engine room, which turned into sweaty perdition down in the southern seas, it was still the Chief Engineer's kingdom, and that was a place with rather strict immigration policies, or rather, how to put it, it was said that if the Chief Engineer ever were to offer you black tea with a splash of rum, something he usually would never do, it was a sign to leave.

Any who were to drain their cup and remain seated were said to curry his disfavour, and nothing good was considered to come of that; Sakuya, who was ignorant of any subtleties of that sort, had once been overcome by an abnormally strong drowsiness while wondering if he should finish his second cup of black tea with rum, and when he awoke, it was to find himself lying spread-eagle on the upper deck drenched in sleet-laced rain, and he ended up suffering from hypothermia, so ever since then, he had always been mindful to exercise restraint, even when loafing around; in a sense, the Chief Engineer was also well suited to be an educator.

At any rate, this was the Albatross, scarce in employee benefits like proper heating facilities as she ever was, so each man needed to apply his own wits to heat himself, and Sakuya had also been driven to craft a simple furnace with his own two clumsy hands. Needless to say, in his mind, the perfect method of heating was to be cooped up beneath his duvet together with a fine, naked woman, but were he possessed of both the financial means and gumption to keep covering the upkeep for something like that, then he would probably already have settled down on land and established a household of his own.

Just in case he could get away with it, he had already formally paid a visit to the twins' cabin to beg them most humbly for heat through the winter, but they seemed busy with making preparations for something or other, and when he stubbornly dug his heels in, he was suddenly made to hold a metal drum, then tied to it. While Sakuya shrieked "Gyaah, ish freeshing!", which was promptly ignored after a brief sidelong glance, the twins counted "and a one and a two" as they tossed charcoal briquettes into the drum, though only the first few of them were properly warmed.

source.japanese: ……実は今でも腕と腿[もも]にその時の痕がちょっと残っていて、妖怪アマメハギの到来をちょっとだけ望んでいる朔屋がある。
source.english: …Even now a few marks from that occasion remained on his arms and thighs. Sakuya rather hoped the Amamehagi—the masked winter spirit said to peel the fire calluses from idlers—might pay him a visit.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（うーむぅ、寒い朝でも一発着火、朔屋印のぽかぽか棒は、こするとすぐに温かいミルクも出ますって宣伝文句の何がいけなかったんだろう……）
source.english: (Hmm. ‘Lights first time, even on cold mornings! Sakuya-brand warming rod! Rub it and warm milk comes out right away!’ What was wrong with that advertising line…?)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（『すぐに』、じゃなくて『辛抱強く』って言わなくちゃいけなかったんだろうかもしかして）
source.english: (Maybe I should've said ‘with patience’ instead of ‘right away’.)

target.text: ……In fact, the marks from then yet remained on his arms and thighs even now, and there was a part of Sakuya that prayed for the arrival of the yokai Amamehagi. (TN: Amamehagi, written "アマメハギ" is a yokai hailing from the city of Wajima and the town of Noto, both in Ishikawa Prefecture. He is an eerie fellow sporting a classic oni mask, and he shows up to peel off the red rash one gets from sitting in front of a fire too long, which goes by a rather formal Latin name, "erythema ab igne", here referred to as "amame". This is considered the symbol of a lazybones who sat before the fire for too long. The "hagi" means to peel off.)

【Naomasa】 （Hmmm, I still don't get what was so wrong with my advertisement for the Sakuya-brand warming stick. It turns on instantly, even on cold mornings, and if you rub it, it'll quickly release a thick stream of warm milk……）
【Naomasa】 （I probably had to say something like "if you rub it really patiently" instead of "quickly", that might have been it.）

source.japanese: そもそもそれ以前の問題という事が本気で判っていない朔屋だったが、双子達の部屋に一冬の間借りを断られては自ら焜炉の一つも作るよりなく、不調法な手でオイルの缶の蓋に空気孔、缶の方には豆炭か炭団でもぶちこもう、と殊勝に寒への備え進めていると───
source.english: He sincerely failed to understand the more fundamental problem. Having been refused a winter's lodging in the twins' room, he had no choice but to make his own stove. Clumsily punching air holes in the oil-can lid, intending to fill the can with little coal briquettes or charcoal balls, he dutifully prepared against the cold—when—

target.text: Sakuya genuinely didn't grasp that there was a more fundamental issue with his behaviour, but having had his request to rent space in the twins' cabin for the winter denied, he was left no choice but to make an improvised heater by himself; with clumsy hands, he made air holes in the lid of the oil drum, and then, thinking he would throw in some coal or charcoal briquettes or something, right as he was in the middle of preparing for the cold with admirable diligence───

source.english: —A tremor—

target.text: ───A shudder───

source.japanese: 腹の底、否船の底から響いてくる震動の、異様な、信天翁号の気むずかしくストライキ起こしがちな主罐ががなりたてる文句や咳とは全く異なる。それらは喘息患者の咳のように、常に内在する不快な圧力が、蓋を弾けさせ吹き飛ばすように偶発的突発的に噴き上がるのだが、今朔屋が聴いたものは削れる音、硬質の何かがより硬度の劣る物質を削って食いこむような音。
source.english: It resounded from the bottom of his belly—no, the bottom of the ship. A strange vibration, wholly unlike the complaints and coughs of the Albatross's touchy, strike-prone main boiler. Those came like an asthmatic's cough, a constant unpleasant pressure suddenly bursting forth, blowing its lid. What Sakuya heard now was a grinding sound. Something hard cutting and biting into something less hard.

target.text: A violent shudder ran from the pit of his stomach, nay, from the very bilge of the ship, an abnormal one, completely different from the coughs and complaints that the foul-tempered and frequently striking main boiler of the Albatross would utter. Like the coughing of an asthmatic patient, an immanent, unpleasant pressure would unpredictably and suddenly boil over, almost blowing the lid off, but what Sakuya heard now was the sound of something scraping, the sound of something hard scraping and digging into something softer.

source.japanese: 寒気の中にさらに寒いような、そんな感触が青年の胸の内側でざらついた。足下に踏んだのが砂地で、さらさらと深淵へと流れ落ちて、やがて青年が踏んだ部分だけを柱と残し、後は虚空ばかりが広がっていくような。
source.english: A colder feeling within the cold rasped inside his chest. As though he stood on sand draining grain by grain into an abyss, until only the patch beneath his feet remained a pillar, all else empty space.

source.japanese:
ただ船体が軋む震動を聞いた、だけだ。その響きだけで船に何事が生じたのか判別できるほどの経験や技能があるわけでなし、朔屋が案ずるほどの事ではないのかも知れない。
　まだ工作の途中でもあるし、もし人手が要りようなら伝声管なり下級水夫の伝令なりで招集がかかろう。慌てて駆けつけていったのに結局は何事もなく、それどころかいいところに来たと要らない用事を言いつけられてしまうかも知れない。
source.english:
Merely a creaking vibration through the hull. He had neither the experience nor the skill to judge from that sound alone what had happened. Perhaps no need to worry.
His handiwork was unfinished. If hands were needed, a speaking tube or a junior sailor would summon him. He might rush there for nothing, or worse, arrive just in time to be given an unnecessary job.

target.text: A chill even colder than the air around him rasped against the young man's chest. It was like the floor beneath his feet had turned to sand, trickling down into the abyss until only the very patch he stood upon remained like a solitary pillar, naught but a void unfolding before him.

However, while he had heard the ship's hull creak along with an impact, that was all. It wasn't like he had the skill or experience needed to determine what exactly had occurred on this ship just from that noise alone, so perhaps it wasn't anything as bad as what Sakuya feared. He was still in the middle of his handicraft, and if they needed hands, then surely he'd be summoned through the voice pipe or an order delivered by a deck boy. Even if he were to rush there in a panic, it might turn out to be nothing, and worse still, he might be told "you came at just the right time" and be saddled with some undesirable chores.

source.japanese: 立ち上がる理由より座って構えるべきだと告げる声の方が多い。そちらの方がどれも尤[もっと]もらしく思われる。
source.english: More voices urged him to remain seated than to rise. Every one seemed reasonable.

source.japanese: ───という事は、そうやって自分を説き伏せようとしている、という事で───
source.english: Which meant—he was trying to persuade himself—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああんもう！　俺、そんな真面目クンなんかじゃなかったはずだろう!?」
source.english: “Oh, for fuck's sake! I wasn't supposed to be this conscientious!”

source.japanese: 朔屋はしまいに根負けして、千枚通しと金槌を放り投げ頭をかきむしって駆け出すが船室を飛び出して、やけっぱちになった小ネズミの如く、杞憂であれよと祈りながら。
source.english: At last Sakuya yielded to the nagging voice. He flung down awl and hammer, tore at his hair, and dashed from the cabin like a desperate little mouse, praying all the while that his fear was groundless.

target.text: There were a lot more voices telling him he ought to remain seated and prepare than ones giving him reasons to stand up. And those sounded to him more reasonable by far.
───In other words, you're trying to talk yourself into it, aren't you───
【Naomasa】 「Argh, come on! Since when was I supposed to be this much of a goody-two-shoes!?」

Ultimately, Sakuya gave in, hurled away the awl and hammer, pulled and tore at his head, rushed out of his cabin, and broke into a sprint, like a tiny mouse fallen into utter desperation, praying all the while that his fears may prove groundless.

source.japanese:
結果として、正しかったのは朔屋の───
　悪い予感の方の───
　この青年、そういう籤[くじ]ばかり引き当てる。
source.english:
As it turned out, Sakuya's intuition was right.
The bad one.
Those were the lots this young man kept drawing.

source.japanese:
もちろん、朔屋の所為というわけではない。
　青年としては珍しく勘働きが的中したというだけで、彼がそれを引き寄せたというわけではない。
　そんな大それたものを引き寄せるような魔力などあろう筈もない。
source.english:
Not his fault, of course.
For once his instincts had proved accurate; he had not drawn the thing to them.
He could hardly possess magic capable of attracting anything so tremendous.

source.japanese: 信天翁号船底部には、朔屋だけでなく、こちらは、長年の確かな勘によってだが水夫長も駆けつけてきてあり、しかしこの不敵な老水夫をして、予想を超えた事態に度を失わせるほどの、それ。
source.english: The boatswain, guided by the reliable instincts of long years, had likewise hurried to the bottom of the Albatross. But even that fearless old sailor was thrown into confusion by a situation beyond anything he had expected. That thing—

target.text: Ultimately, what turned out to be correct was Sakuya's─── Bad premonition─── These were the only lots this young man ever drew.

Of course, none of this was Sakuya's doing. It was simply that this young man's instincts were uncharacteristically on the mark, not that he had been the one to invite it upon them. By no means did he possess the magical powers to attract something so grand.

It wasn't just Sakuya there in the hold of the Albatross, for the Bosun had also come running, guided by intuition honed over many long years, yet that thing, it was a sight to shatter the nerves of even this intrepid old mariner, thrusting them into a situation far beyond all expectation.

source.japanese:
大洋の底から何とも劇的に伸び上がり、水面下僅か数十糎[センチ]では上から見たところ、やや扁平な線状に見えたであろうそれ。朔屋がもしそれを海面上から見つめる機会あれば、擬された経験から『智里の刀の眸子、真正面から見たような』と表したであろう、それ。
　剣の如き、孤岩、暗礁、だったのだ。
source.english:
Rising dramatically from the ocean floor, it stopped a mere few dozen centimeters below the surface and from above would have looked like a narrow, flattened line. Had Sakuya seen it from there, his experience of having blades aimed at him might have made him describe it as Tomosato's sword point viewed head-on.
It was a solitary rock—a submerged reef shaped like a sword.

source.japanese: その縁の鋭さ、ほとんど剃刀並みに船の赤錆だらけの船腹を田楽刺しにし、食いこんで、深々と、どこかしら現状に洋菓子めいた印象さえ与えるほどやすやすと。
source.english: Its edge, almost razor-sharp, skewered the red-rusted hull and bit deep. So easily that the whole affair took on something of the look of a Western confection.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おいなんだこりゃあ!?
　こんな剣みたいな！」
source.english:
“What the hell is this!?
It's like some kind of sword—!”

source.japanese:
朔屋と水夫長、それぞれ反対方面から駆けつけてきたようで、食いこんだ剣状の孤岩を間境に、対面に、似たようなやり方で頭を抱えた様子は、一つの舞台を壁仕切りで二つに割った二場面同時進行式の喜劇を思わせた。
　深刻な現実というのを俯瞰してみると凄味帯びた滑稽感が漂うの好例ではあるが。
source.english:
Sakuya and the boatswain had arrived from opposite directions. Facing one another across the embedded blade of rock, both clutching their heads much the same way, they resembled a comedy playing two scenes at once on a stage divided by a wall.
A fine instance of the terrible absurdity a serious reality can acquire when viewed from above.

source.japanese: そして、なんぼ水夫長の胴間声、薄い壁なら共鳴させるほどだからというて、それが引き金になったわけでもないのだが、彼が喚いた瞬間、孤岩と船腹の隙間から噴き上がった浸水の、余計な演出めいて物凄い。
source.english: The boatswain's booming voice could make thin walls resonate, but it had not caused this. At the instant he shouted, water erupted through the gap between rock and hull. A tremendous, gratuitous bit of stage business.

target.text: It rose upwards from the bottom of the ocean in an immensely dramatic manner, reaching up to only a few dozen centimetres below the surface, and when viewed from above, it would probably have looked like a somewhat flattened, linear shape. Had Sakuya been given the opportunity to view it from above the sea, based on his comparative experiences, he'd be like to describe that thing as follows: 『Like seeing the tip of Tomosato's blade staring you right in the eyes.』 Like a sword, there stood a solitary rock, a hidden reef.

With an edge almost razor-sharp, it pierced the rust-encrusted hull of the ship like a skewer through tofu, biting deep with such effortless ease that it somehow lent the entire scene the impression of slicing into a delicate piece of confectionery.
【Bosun】 「Oi, what the hell is this!? This sword-like thing!」

Having seemingly rushed in from opposite directions, Sakuya and the Bosun stood facing each other, and with the deeply embedded, sword-shaped rock serving as the boundary dividing them, the way they both clutched their heads evoked a farce performed on a single stage split in two by a wall partition with two scenes unfolding simultaneously. It did serve as a prime example of how harsh reality, when viewed from afar, can take on a grimly comedic quality.

And finally, even granted that the Bosun's booming voice was loud enough to make thin walls vibrate in response, there was still no way it could have been the trigger, but in spite of that, the instant he yelled, like an unnecessary theatrical flourish staged only for dramatic effect, the surge of floodwater erupted from the gap between the lone rock and the ship's hull with a terrifyingly tremendous force.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こ、こりゃまずいッスよ水夫長！
　浸水の勢いがただ事じゃないっ」
source.english:
“Th-this is bad, Boatswain!
The water's pouring in way too fast!”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「見りゃあわかるんだそんな事は。
　クソクソクソクソッッ、
　こんな深く、ざっくりイッちまっちゃあ、
　こりゃあ……」
source.english:
“I can see that!
Shit, shit, shit, shit!
Cut this deep—sliced wide open—
this is…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Th-, this is real bad, Bosun! The water's rushing in way too fast!」
【Bosun】 「I've got eyes too. Shit shit shit SHIT, It went in this deep, and tore open a gash this wide, this is real bad……」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どうやって脱出するんですこれ！」
source.english: “How do we get out of this?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それはあとで考える。
　今は浸水を止める事のほうが先だ！」
source.english:
“Think about that later.
Stop the flooding first!”

source.japanese: そう全ては後の事、このまま浸水を許せば信天翁号下層部は遠からず塩水渦巻く、北海領域の一部となる事確実で、これで夏場なら風変わりな水遊びの場、などと一瞬でも考える暢気者さえありそうな信天翁号、しかし噴き上がる水、飛沫が二・三滴かかるくらいでぞっとするほどの冷たさ、信天翁号の面子の表情をも冷たさを呼ぶほど。
source.english: Yes, everything else later. Let this continue and the Albatross's lower decks would soon become a swirling saltwater portion of the northern seas. In summer, some carefree soul aboard might briefly have considered it an unusual swimming spot. But two or three drops from this spray were enough to chill one to the core, to chill the crew's very expressions.

source.japanese:
……まだ水夫長も朔屋も駆けつけてきて程無かったが、この頃になると下級水夫の中でも敏捷なのが到着してあり、矢継ぎ早に繰り出される指示、水夫長から、怠慢な朔屋でさえ逆らったりさぼったりしようなど言う愚行致さず、下級水夫達に入り交じって必死働きの、青年にして余計な事を考えていられる暇もない。
　朔屋でもこれがいかなる事態なのか理解されてあった。
source.english:
Little time had passed since Sakuya and the boatswain arrived, but the quickest junior sailors were already there. Orders came in rapid succession. Even lazy Sakuya knew better than to disobey or shirk. Among the juniors he worked desperately, with no time for stray thoughts.
Even he understood what this was.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「How the hell are we supposed to get away from this thing!」
【Bosun】 「We'll think about that later. For now, stopping the flooding takes priority!」

Right, all that came later; if they allowed the flooding to continue like this, the hold of the Albatross would be nothing but swirling saltwater before long, fated to become a part of the northern seas; a carefree soul aboard the Albatross might, even for just a split second, have thought it a quirky water park were it summertime, but that spouting water was so chillingly cold, just being sprayed with two or three droplets was enough to send shudders through your body, draining the warmth right off the faces of even the crew of the Albatross.

……It had still barely been any time since both the Bosun and Sakuya had rushed over, but by this point, the particularly quick deck boys were arriving, and as orders were sent flying through the hold in rapid succession by the Bosun, not even lazy and negligent Sakuya committed any acts of folly like disobeying or trying to slack off; he joined in with the deck boys and frantically set to work, the young man not having the luxury to think of anything irrelevant. For even Sakuya had realized exactly what kind of situation they were in.

source.japanese: ───沈没の危機だ。
source.english: —They were in danger of sinking.

target.text: ───They were in danger of foundering.

source.japanese:
この船を沈めるつもりなら、イッカクあたりに体当たりさせるくらいで事足りたろうに、よりにもよって北の海は、こんな珍しき陥穽を用意してのけたのである。
『鶏を割[さ]くに焉[いずく]んぞ牛刀を用[もち]いん』とはよく言ったものだが、裂かれる鶏にとってはなんにしたところでたまったものではない。
　裂かれるは鶏ならぬ信天翁、名の通り翔んでいたならこのような海の剣などに捕まらず済んでいたものを、と嘆いたところで何も意味はない、何も。
source.english:
A narwhal's charge would probably have sufficed to sink this vessel. Yet the northern sea had contrived this rare trap instead.
‘Why use an ox-cleaver to kill a chicken?’ A fine saying, but the chicken being cut could hardly welcome either choice. This was no chicken,
but an albatross. Had it flown as its name suggested, no sword of the sea would have caught it. Lamenting that availed nothing. Nothing.

target.text: If one intended to sink this ship, then having something like a narwhal bump into it would probably suffice, and of all the places, it was the northern waters that had gone and prepared such a rare, treacherous trap for them.

『Why use an ox-cleaver to carve a chicken?』 A well-worn proverb, but for the chicken being carved up, no matter the method chosen, its fate remained unbearable. The bird carved up here was an albatross rather than a chicken, and had it been soaring through the skies as its name would suggest, then it would have escaped any such blades of the sea, but lamenting that now would amount to nothing, nothing at all.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「水夫長、槇皮、ボロ布、おが屑、後々えーと、とにかく詰め物に使えそうなモノ全部、穴塞げそうなモノ全部！　持ってきました！」
source.english: “Boatswain! Caulking bark, rags, sawdust, and, um—anything we could stuff in, anything to plug a hole! We brought it all!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Bosun, we have caulking, old rags, sawdust, and then, and then, uhh, anyways, anything we can use to stuff inside it, everything we can use to plug the hole! We brought it all!」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「よし良い子だ！　あとはポンプとバケツ。
　手ぇ空いてる奴は全部こっちに寄越せ。
　石炭室からも引っぱってこい！」
source.english:
“Good man! Pumps and buckets next.
Send every free hand here.
Pull them out of the coal room too!”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「どのみち今は汽罐なんぞ、
　下手には動かせねえ」
source.english:
“We can't risk running the boiler—
not now.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「冷てぇ、冷てぇぇぇ……っ。
　手、手が千切れそうだ水夫長！」
source.english:
“Cold, so c-cold…
My hands feel like they'll fall off, Boatswain!”

source.japanese:
下級水夫の一人の持ち来たった有り合わせの充填材を、浸水孔に押しこんで、押しこんでは押しこんでぎゅうぎゅうと、根太は敵[かたき]に押させよという、さながら朔屋は親の敵の息の根でも止める力で木っ端を詰め込んで、まずは目につく塩水を止める、と、先ほど詰めたばかりの襤褸布が弾けて水柱噴き上げて、青年の目頭を撃っては視界を遮[さえぎ]る。
　なんのコントかという有様だが、朔屋にしてみれば至って真剣の、集中力さえ千切るような水の冷たさ。
source.english:
He rammed the makeshift packing a junior sailor had brought into the breach, shoved and shoved, cramming it tight. ‘Let your enemy press the boil,’ as the saying went; Sakuya drove in splinters of wood with the strength of a man choking his parents' murderer. First the visible flow stopped. Then the rag he had just stuffed into place burst free, and a jet struck the corner of his eye and blinded him.
It looked like some comedy routine. To Sakuya it was deadly serious, the water cold enough to snap even concentration itself.

source.japanese: この時期にしては異常だとか、訴えたところで聞き入れる先などあろう筈もなく、朔屋ばかりでなく共働きの下級水夫達もまた、その可憐な唇を紫色に染めてある。中には冷たさの余り俯[うつぶ]せにぶっ倒れた気の毒なのもあって、慌てて運び出されたあの子はどうなったろう───と朔屋が憂う間もがちがちがち、動いているのに歯の根が合わぬ。
source.english: There was no one to hear a complaint that the cold was abnormal for the season. The junior sailors beside Sakuya had their tender lips dyed purple too. One poor sailor collapsed face-first from the cold and was hurried away. What had become of him? Even as Sakuya worried, his teeth clattered; though his body kept moving, he could not make them meet.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「我慢しろっ、あと少しで交替がくるっ。
　あ、おい貴様、湯を持ってこい、
　急いでだっ」
source.english:
“Hold on! Relief's coming soon!
Hey, you, bring hot water!
Quick!”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「作業に着く奴ぁ、低体温症に注意させろ。
　動けなくなっちまったら、
　それでお終いだからな！」
source.english:
“Warn everyone working about hypothermia.
Once they can't move,
that's the end!”

source.japanese: 水に浸からずば破砕孔に近づけず、一度でもこの夜の海水の冷たさ知った者は飛沫が飛ぶだけでも怖気を催したが、それでも、それでもと取り縋[すが]り、骨を喰[は]む冷たさに押し返されて、またそれでも、と、なにかしら生命の本質といった壮大な観念さえ思わせる奮闘が続き───永遠に、と思われるほどに続き───
source.english: No reaching the breach without entering the water. Anyone who had felt this night's seawater shuddered even at a flying drop. Yet they struggled on, clung on, were driven back by cold that gnawed their bones, tried again. Their struggle suggested something as grand as the essence of life itself. It continued—seemingly forever—

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Alright, that's a good boy! Next we need pumps and buckets. Send all the free hands we have over here. Go drag them out of the coal bunker as well!」
【Bosun】 「Besides, we can't afford to carelessly fire up the boiler right now.」
【Naomasa】 「F-freezing, it's so damn coooold……. My h-hands, my hands feel like they're gonna snap right off, Bosun!」

One of the deck boys had brought whatever material could be used as makeshift filler, and Sakuya was busy pushing that into the aperture of ingress, stuffing and cramming it all in until packed tight; it is said that when pressing the boil, you must treat it as if it were the enemy, and sure enough, Sakuya stuffed in the wood chips with all the force of a man squeezing the life from the murderer of his parents; first thing first, he had to plug any noticeable leaks of saltwater, but suddenly, the tattered rag he'd just packed in was sent flying, and a spout of water erupted, hitting the young man square in his eyes and obstructing his vision.
It looked like a scene right out of a comedy sketch, but to Sakuya, it was deadly serious, and the water was so cold, it felt like it even tore his ability to concentrate to shreds.

He could complain all he liked about it being abnormally cold for the season, there would surely be none to lend him an ear, and it wasn't just Sakuya, for the deck boys fared no better, their sweet, lovely lips dyed purple. There were even some unfortunate souls among them who'd collapsed face first from the overwhelming cold, and he could only guess at what that one boy who was hastily carried out had looked like───but even while Sakuya fretted, clatter-clatter-clatter, his teeth chattered uncontrollably, refusing to hold still despite him being in motion.
【Bosun】 「Tough it out, relief is on the way! Ah, oi, you there, bring some hot water, and make it double time!」
【Bosun】 「Warn anyone starting their shift to watch out for hypothermia. If we all freeze up, that's the end of us!」

You couldn't get close to the breach without getting submerged in water, and any who had come to know the frigid chill of this night-time saltwater would shiver in fear at just the first hint of a spray flying in their direction; nevertheless, they still held fast, pushed back against a chill that gnawed at their very bones; in spite of it all, the struggle raged on, evoking grand notions of even the very essence of life itself─── it continued for so long, it seemed like an eternity had passed───

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「材木の追加だよ！　上甲板のバラックの丈夫なとこばらしてきたよ！　よく乾いてるから！」
source.english: “More timber! Took apart the strong bits of the shack on the upper deck! It's good and dry!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Brought some additional wood! We took apart the sturdy parts of the shacks on deck! It's nice and dry!」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ええぞ……詰めこめ……とにかくまずは、水を止めろ……ええくそ、揺れるな……。
　仕方ねえ」
source.english:
“Good… Cram it in… Stop the water first, whatever it takes… Ah, shit, stop rocking…
Can't be helped.”

source.japanese: 単調な、悲惨ながらも果てしなく単調な、それ故に人の意志力体力を根こぎにする苦闘の時間、陥落するのは船の方かと絶望的な気運漂い始めた頃になって、ようやく、そうようやく、浸水の度合い、減じ始め、それまでは汲[く]み出すのが空しくなるほど後から後から増してきた水嵩の、追いつかなかったのが少しずつ追いついて、人力と自然力、いつしか拮抗し、ついには船底部の壁に船の残り時間を示して揺れていた水の線、徐々に、じりじりとだが下がりゆく。
source.english: A monotonous struggle. Miserable, endlessly monotonous, and therefore stripping will and strength to the roots. Just as despair began to suggest the ship would be the one to fall, at last—yes, at last—the flooding diminished. Before, water had risen faster than they could bail, making their efforts seem futile. Little by little they caught up. Human effort and natural force approached a balance. Finally the wavering line on the lower hull's wall, that measure of the ship's remaining time, began slowly, painfully to fall.

source.japanese: 気づいた下級水夫がそれを告げた時、皆始めはそれまでのあまりの辛さに半信半疑で、本当だと知った時にも、喜んだ瞬間にまた意地悪水が孤岩の隙間から責めてくるのではないかと憚[はばか]った、下級水夫の遠慮を破った馬鹿一人、信天翁号の馬鹿といえば彼である。
source.english: When a junior sailor noticed and announced it, at first everyone doubted him, worn down by their ordeal. Even on learning it was true, they hesitated to rejoice, lest the spiteful water attack again through the gap beside the rock. One fool broke their restraint. The Albatross's fool: who else?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おおう……、
　どうにかなりそうでないのこれ！」
source.english:
“Ohhh…
Looks like we might manage this!”

source.japanese: 朔屋が示した喜色に居合わせていた下級水夫君達は一瞬きっと青年を睨[にら]みつけ、はしたものの、そこまでだった。
source.english: At Sakuya's display of delight, the junior sailors present glared at him for one sharp instant. But only for an instant.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「馬鹿、気が早ええ……て言いてぇところだが、とにかくやれる事はやった……。
　後は変に船を動かさなければ、とりあえず傷が拡がる事はあんめぇ……」
source.english:
“I'd like to say you're jumping the gun, idiot…
But we've done what we can. As long as we don't move the ship carelessly, the damage shouldn't spread for now…”

source.japanese: この水夫長の一言に誰か一人が漏らした溜息安堵の吐息、が、次々に波及していって、中にはへたり込む者もあったほど、で尻に凍みる冷たさに慌てて立ち上がるわけだが。
source.english: At those words, someone breathed relief. The sigh spread from one to another. Some even slumped down—then hurriedly stood when cold bit into their backsides.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「航海士に言ってこい、主碇使うぞ、下ろして一時この位置に固定だっ」
source.english: “Tell the mates! We're using the main anchor. Drop it and hold us here for now!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……え……あの錨、使えたんか……」
source.english: “…Huh… That anchor actually works…?”

source.japanese: 信天翁号の左舷船首側にぶら下がったるそれを、朔屋も確かに日頃目にしていたし、あの辺りの舷側から吊るし刑にあった時なぞは、それに足で捕まって難を凌[しの]いだものだが、印象としてはこの襤褸の集積物をせいぜい船らしく見せるためのオブジェに留まって、実用の物だとは考えていなかったので。
source.english: Sakuya saw it daily, hanging at the port bow. Once, suspended in punishment from that part of the side, he had caught it with his feet and eased his plight. But he had taken it for an ornament, something that lent this heap of junk at least the appearance of a ship; he had never imagined it was functional.

source.japanese: とにかく、水夫長の命を受けて走っていった下級水夫だが───
source.english: The junior sailor ran off at the boatswain's order. But—

target.text: 【Bosun】 「That's good……cram it in…… first things, we at least have to stop the flooding…… damn it all, don't falter……. Won't do us any good.」

It was monotonous; yes, for all its misery, it was still interminably monotonous, and thus began a time of bitter struggle that tore from them any shred of willpower and strength they yet possessed, and just as the air grew heavy with despair, when it seemed as if the ship might be first to sink, finally, yes, at long last, the flooding began to recede.

Until now, the water had surged in endlessly, to the point their efforts at bailing it out felt futile, and though they hadn't quite caught up it with it yet, little by little, the tide was turning; unnoticed, the balance of the power of man and the forces of nature had shifted, they were now competing on even footing, and finally, the waterline that had been swaying against the bottom of the hull, marking the ship's remaining time, began its slow, agonizing descent.

When the first deck boy to notice it made the announcement, the immense hardship they'd been through left them dubious to begin with, and even when they realized it was true, in that moment of joy, they were still hesitant, wondering if that malevolent water wouldn't spout up from that gap between the hull and the rock to torment them once more, but there was a single idiot who shattered any tactful discretion shown by the deck boys; speaking of idiots on the Albatross, there was only one man it could be.
【Naomasa】 「Oooh……, looks like we might actually pull this off!」
All deck boys present who were witness to the joy Sakuya showed gave him a brief, piercing glare; that they certainly did, but nothing more.
【Bosun】 「Idiot, you're being too hasty…… is what I'd like to say, but we've done what we can……. As long as we don't suddenly move the ship around carelessly, the damage should be contained for now……」

Somebody let out a long sigh of relief after hearing the Bosun's words, and then it gradually rippled out through them; there were even some who sunk down to the floor, so great was the relief, but upon feeling the cold water freezing their asses, they hurriedly got up again.
【Bosun】 「Go tell the mates, we're using the bower anchor, lower it and secure the ship's position for a time.」
【Naomasa】 「……Huh……that anchor can actually be used……?」

Sakuya had certainly had his eyes drawn to that thing on a daily basis, dangling down from the port side of the bow, and when he'd been given the punishment of being hung down from the side of the ship around there, he had staved off some of the hardship by grabbing onto it with his legs, but it had only given him the impression that it was there to make this heap of scrap look as ship-like as possible, and he'd never thought of it as something with actual utility.
In any case, the deck boy ran off on the orders of the Bosun, but───

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「駄目です水夫長、一等航海士、二人ともいないよ、操舵室にも船室にも」
source.english: “No good, Boatswain! Both chief mates are gone. Not in the wheelhouse, not in their cabin.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「It's no good, Bosun, neither of the chief mates are anywhere to be found. They're not in the wheelhouse or their cabin!」

source.japanese: 持って帰ってきた報せは水夫長を激高させた。そういえばと朔屋も船底内を見回す。作業中からどうにも何かが足らないように感じていたその何か。その正体にここになってようやく思い当たった。
source.english: The news he brought back enraged the boatswain. Come to think of it—Sakuya looked around the lower hull. All through the work he had felt something missing. Only now did he identify it.

source.japanese: そう、信天翁号の一等航海士だ。航海中の航海士の職務というのは確かに操船や当直が主ではあるが、その辺りの職掌区分は緩い信天翁号、まして船の沈没の危機である。浸水現場に立ち会えない事もあるかも知れないが、さすがにその持ち場にいないというのは。
source.english: Yes, the Albatross's chief mates. Under way, a navigator's principal duties were handling the ship and keeping watch. But distinctions of duty were loose aboard the Albatross, and the ship was in danger of sinking. Perhaps they could not attend the flooding itself. But absent even from their posts—

source.japanese:
朔屋は、ここしばらくの双子の様子のおかしい事、他の乗り組み達からも隠れてやっているあのフィールドワーク、諸々含めてまた厭[いや]な予感を覚えた。

　予感などいうものは、吉兆に関しては当てにもならないが、不穏を孕むものに関しては的中する傾向にあり───
source.english:
Sakuya felt another bad presentiment, recalling the twins' recent strangeness and that fieldwork hidden from the rest of the crew.
Presentiments were worthless as promises of good fortune. The ominous sort tended to come true—

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……んだとぉ……あの雌猫ども……。
　このクソやばい、くそ忙しい時になにしてケツかる……っ。あいつら最近一体───」
source.english:
“…What… Those damn she-cats…
What the hell are they doing at a time like this, when we're in deep shit and up to our necks in work? What have those two been—”

target.text: The report brought back to him made the Bosun fly into a rage. Speaking of, Sakuya also took a look around the hold. All throughout the work he'd done, there had been this feeling that something was missing. Only now did its true nature finally dawn on him.

Right, the first mates of the Albatross. The professional duties of a mate during a voyage was mainly navigating the ship and watchstanding, to be certain, but the Albatross was lax when it came to the exact division of those sorts of duties, to say nothing of the fact the ship was on the brink of sinking. It wasn't impossible that there were circumstances that made them unable to be present at the actual breach itself, but for them to not even be at their station?

The strangeness of the twins' behavior lately, that fieldwork they'd been hiding even from the other crew members: all kinds of things combined to give Sakuya yet another terrible premonition. So-called premonitions are rarely useful for predicting good fortune, but when they carry with them foreboding unease, they tend to be right.

【Bosun】 「……What was that…… those goddamn hussies……. What the fuck do they think they're doing while we're neck-deep in a disaster this damned dangerous……. What in the hell has been up with those two lately───」

source.japanese:
───始め朔屋はその娘に、一体どこの病人がいつの間に船に迷いこんだと、見知らぬ誰かを見たような印象さえ受けたのだ。
　それくらい、弱々しく、精彩を欠いていた。
