　普段の、生命力が弾けんばかりの眸[ひとみ]を知っているだけに、なおさら。足取りだって霧中を歩む人のように頼りなく、実際船底部に散らばった諸々の材につまずいてよろけたほど。
source.english:
At first Sakuya took the girl for a stranger—a sick passenger who had somehow wandered aboard.
So weak was she, so utterly without animation; all the more shocking to a man who knew those eyes as ordinarily ready to burst with life.
Her steps were as uncertain as those of someone walking through fog. Indeed, she caught her foot on the materials scattered across the lower deck and staggered.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あ、みんなここにいたの……！」
source.english: “Oh, everyone was here…!”

target.text: ───When Sakuya first saw the girl, he wondered just who this sick person who must have lost their way and wandered onto the ship without anybody noticing was; it even left him with the impression of looking at a complete stranger. That was how feeble she looked, how stripped of the lustre of life she was. And it struck him all the more, knowing how those eyes of hers usually brimmed with vitality. Her gait was also hesitant and helpless, like someone stumbling through the fog, to the point that she did, in fact, stumble and trip over the pieces of wood scattered across the hold.
【Kisara】 「Ah, so this is where you all were……!」

source.japanese: これは───誰だ───？
source.english: Who—was this—?

source.japanese:
朔屋が知っている彼女達なら、髪は黄金を融[と]かしたような豪奢な艶[つや]を帯びているのに、ここに現れた者の髪ときたら、紅茶の出がらしのように褪せているでないか。
　何よりその眸[ひとみ]だ。相対した者に、果てしない挑戦とか大海原にこぎ出した人類の父祖の勇敢を想起せしめる碧の眸[ひとみ]は、今や───
source.english:
The twins Sakuya knew had hair with the luxuriant sheen of molten gold. The girl before him wore hair faded as spent tea leaves. Above all, there were her eyes:
green eyes that called up endless defiance and the courage of mankind's ancestors venturing upon the great ocean. Now—

source.japanese: 無理矢理叩き起こした死人のようにかき曇って。人の手足を萎えさせる、ありとあらゆる不安と恐れと怯えを詰め込んでかき回したようにぐるぐると渦巻いて。
source.english: Clouded as a corpse forcibly awakened. Swirling with every anxiety, fear and terror that could sap the strength of human limbs, all packed in and stirred together.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ね、ねえ、シサム知らないっ？
　どこにもいないの！
　さっき船が揺れた時もしかして───！」
source.english:
“H-hey, have you seen Sisam?
She's nowhere!
When the ship shook just now, maybe—!”

source.japanese:
シサム、を訊ねたからにはこちらはキサラなのだろう。なのだろうがしかし。
　これは───と愕然として、朔屋はそして思い出す。今ではもう随分遠い日の事のように思われるが、あの大怪魚の一件の際の彼女だこれは。ついでに言えば先日当直のしくじりから、船員皆の前で晒し者された時もなのだが、あちらは可哀相だから忘れる事にして。
　あの時の、片割れと引き離された時の、彼女達ではないか。
source.english:
Since she was asking after Sisam, this must be Kisara. Must be; and yet.
Sakuya stared, appalled—and remembered. It seemed an age ago now, but this was Kisara as she had been during the affair of the great monster fish. For that matter, she had been much the same the other day, when a botched watch got her pilloried before the entire crew—but that had been too pitiful, and he had elected to forget it.
Yes: this was what became of either twin when she was torn from her other half.

source.japanese: という事はつまり、と朔屋はキサラの後ろにもう一人を捜したが、彼女が引きずっているのは影だけの。人の弱々しさを指して影が薄い、などと言うが、双子に関しては影より片割れが側にない方が著しく釣り合いを失って見える。
source.english: Which meant—Sakuya looked behind Kisara for the other woman. She dragged only her shadow. People spoke of the weak as casting faint shadows. But with the twins, the absence of the other half unbalanced the picture far more than a missing shadow could.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「キサラ、てめぇ、
　なんで持ち場についてねぇ……？
　なんだって操舵室についてねえんだ」
source.english:
“Kisara.
Why aren't you at your post?
Why aren't you in the wheelhouse?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「え……っ？　でもあたし、
　今晩は非番で……」
source.english:
“Huh…?
But I'm off duty tonight…”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おお非番だとも、非番ですよ。
　だがな、こんな、今まで来たコトもない海で、非番だからと……水夫に操舵室任せる航海士がどこにいるんだクソが！」
source.english:
“Oh, you're off duty, are you? Of course.
But in waters we've never sailed before, what kind of goddamned chief mate leaves the wheelhouse to an ordinary sailor merely because she's off duty?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「シサムだぁ……？　知らねえよんな奴ぁ。
　だいたいどこで何してんだてめえはよ、
　え？」
source.english:
“Sisam…? How should I know?
What the hell have you been doing, anyway?
Where? Huh?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あ、その……あたし達、救命ボートの修理してて……この前積みこんだ奴の。
　ちょっと工具取りに戻って、離れて。
　ちょっとだから平気って思った！」
source.english:
“Ah, um… We were fixing a lifeboat. The one we loaded recently.
I went back for some tools, left her a little while.
Thought it'd be okay, just a little while!”

source.japanese: ……水夫長の剣幕に、今のキサラが言葉もなくさず答えていられるのは、それだけ彼女も必死、という事なのだろうが、言えば言うだけ、己の過失を吐く事になるのに気づいていない様子の、もうそんな事など顧みている余裕など蚊の目玉ほどもないのであろう、手当たり次第に問いかける。
source.english: That Kisara could answer the boatswain's fury at all in her present state showed her desperation. She did not seem to realize that each word confessed another fault. She had not a mosquito's-eye speck of attention to spare for such things. She questioned anyone she could.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そしたらシサム、戻ったらいなかった！
　誰か見なかった？
　あいつ、どこかにいなかった!?」
source.english:
“Then when I came back, Sisam was gone!
Did anyone see her?
Was she anywhere—anywhere at all?!”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「僕……見てない」
source.english: “I… didn't see her.”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「……知らない」
source.english: “…Don't know.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「じゃあ、なら、朔屋は……っ？」
source.english: “Then—then Sakuya…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、俺は、これがめりこんでから、すぐにここに駆けこんできて、それからずっと、離れてないから……」
source.english: “No, I ran straight here when this thing went into us. Haven't left since…”

target.text: Who───was that───?

Were she one of the women Sakuya knew, then her hair would have a luxurious sheen like molten gold, but was the hair of the person who appeared here not faded and discoloured like insipid black tea? But worst of all was those eyes. Those eyes of green jasper, which would evoke in any who met them a sense of endless defiance or recollections of the gallant heroicism of mankind's forefathers who once rowed out across the vast open seas, were now───

Overcast like those of a corpse risen from the dead against its will. Packed full of every conceivable anxiety and fear and panic, of what would make the strength in a man's limbs wither away into weakness, swirling and churning as they spun round and round in a jumbled mess.
【Bosun】 「───! You little……」
【Kisara】 「He-, hey, have you seen Shisamu? I can't find her anywhere! When the ship rocked earlier, maybe she───!」

Given that she asked about Shisamu, this was probably Kisara. It probably was, but still. This was just───so Sakuya thought, dumbstruck, then remembered. By now, it felt like something from a far-off day in the distant past, but she was acting just like she had been back during the incident with that big monster fish. And while he was at it, there was also that time the other day when they were publicly humiliated in front of the entire crew after that blunder they made while standing watch, but he felt bad for them, and so he had decided to forget about that. Back then, when they had both been separated from their other half; wasn't she acting just like them of that time?

So in others words, this meant, Sakuya thought, looking for one more person behind Kisara, but the only thing she'd dragged with her was her own shadow. Pointing out the frailness of a shadow can sometimes speak of human frailty instead, or so it is said, but when it comes to twins, it is not the absence of a shadow but rather the absence of their other half by their side that leaves them looking profoundly unbalanced.
【Bosun】 「Kisara, you moron, why aren't you at your station……? For what possible reason are you not in the wheelhouse?」
【Kisara】 「Huh……? But I'm not standing watch tonight……」

【Bosun】 「Yeah, you're certainly not, you're off watch. But see, we're sailing through a sea we've never been in before…… so what the hell kind of chief mate would leave the wheelhouse to a sailor just because they're off watch, goddamn it!」
【Bosun】 「Shisamu……? To hell with her! Where the fuck were you and what have you been up to, huh?」

【Kisara】 「Oh, uhm……we, uhh, were repairing the lifeboat……the one we loaded the other day. I was just heading back inside to grab some tools, so I left her. It was just for a little bit, so I thought it would be fine!」

……That Kisara was able to muster an answer without being at a complete loss for words while met with the Bosun's menacing glare was probably because the girl was just that desperate, but seemingly unaware that every word she spoke only dug her own grave deeper, and presumably lacking even a mosquito's eyeball worth of composure to care about such things, she blindly hurled questions at anyone and everyone within reach.
【Kisara】 「And then Shisamu, she was gone when I came back! Has anybody seen her? Isn't she around here somewhere!?」
【Deck boy】 「I……haven't seen her.」
【Deck boy】 「……No clue.」
【Kisara】 「Well then, what about, Sakuya, have you……?」
【Naomasa】 「No, I-, the moment this thing got lodged in the ship, I rushed straight here, and I haven't left ever since, so……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「これがめりこんで……って……え、あ？
　これって……岩礁……隠れてた……？」
source.english:
“This thing went in…? Huh, ah?
This… A reef… Hidden…?”

source.japanese: 下級水夫達と変わり映えのない、そしてキサラを哀しませる答えしか吐けないのが心苦しいが、今の朔屋は彼にしては珍しい精勤ぶりに疲れきって、シサムの行方がどこにあるのか、推測する事さえ困難だった。
source.english: It hurt to have only the same answer as the junior sailors, an answer that saddened Kisara. But Sakuya was exhausted by his unusually diligent work. Even guessing where Sisam might be was beyond him.

source.japanese:
そんな朔屋でさえ、キサラが今初めてこの剣のように無駄に派手な孤岩に気づいた有様に、苦い味が口内に湧いたものである。おそらくそれは、朔屋だけでなくこの場に居合わせた者全員に共通する心証だったろう。
　水夫長がその想いの代弁を、彼は水夫の長である、詰り咎[とが]める時、人は人の罪を明らかにしてもけして爽快なだけでない、苦しさ、空しさも共に胸中にこみ上げるのだけれど、それら水夫達の苦い思いも一人に引き受けて、糾弾もするから水夫の長なのだった。
source.english:
Even Sakuya tasted bitterness when he saw Kisara notice the extravagantly swordlike rock for the first time. Everyone present must have felt much the same. The boatswain gave voice to it.
He was, after all, the sailors' leader. To expose and condemn another's fault brings not only satisfaction but pain and futility; he took the crew's bitter feelings upon himself and made the accusation in their stead. That burden too was part of leading them.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……そういう、ことだよ。この朔屋でさえ、ずっとここに貼りつきっぱなしだ。がたがたと、病気の犬みてえに震えっぱなし凍えっぱなしでな」
source.english: “…That's right. Even Sakuya here's been stuck here the whole time. Freezing, shivering like a sick dog.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なのに、てめえと来たら、なんだ……ア？
　今初めて見たな？　この剣みてえな暗礁をよ。それで『シサムはどこ』だ？
　───知るもんかよっ！」
source.english:
“And you—what? Huh?
You've only just noticed this swordlike reef, haven't you?
And now you ask where Sisam is? How the hell should I know!”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おおかた、これが船の腹ぁ食い破った時のショックで、海に転がり落ちてったんだろうぜ！」
source.english: “Probably went overboard from the shock when this bit through the ship's belly!”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「この骨まで凍るような海だ。
　今頃はとっくにお陀仏だぁ！」
source.english:
“Sea cold enough to freeze your bones.
She'll be long dead by now!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「This thing got lodged…… you say……huh, ah? Is this……a hidden……reef……?」

He had nothing more to offer than the deck boys, and while only being able to give an answer he knew would sadden Kisara pained his heart, right now, Sakuya was completely exhausted after being so abnormally diligent, and he found even guessing at Shisamu's whereabouts to be difficult.

And yet even Sakuya felt a bitter taste welling up inside his mouth at the sad sight that was Kisara's state, who had only just now noticed that needlessly showy, sword-shaped lone rock. In all likelihood, this impression belonged not just to Sakuya, but was one shared by all members present.

The Bosun acted as the representative of that emotion; he was the leader of the sailors, and when admonishing or scolding, even when one man exposes another's wrongdoing, it is never just refreshing or cathartic alone; a distress and an emptiness also surges through your chest, but to assume responsibility for even the bitter feelings of these sailors, and then censuring the ones responsible, that is what it meant to be the leader of the sailors.
【Bosun】 「……That's exactly what it is. Even Sakuya here's been glued to this spot. Freezing and shivering like a sick dog the whole damn time.」
【Bosun】 「And yet, look at you, what the hell's your problem……huh? Now's the first time you see it, yeah? This sword-like hidden reef. And then you go "where's Shisamu?" ───Like I give a fuck!」
【Bosun】 「I'd bet, when this thing ripped right through the hull, the impact flung her straight into the sea!」
【Bosun】 「Into a sea this bone-chilling. She's long gone by now!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そんな───い、生きてる、
　シサム生きてるよ！　キサラには判る。
　だってあの子が死んじゃったら、
　キサラだって生きていられない」
source.english:
“No—alive, she's alive!
Kisara knows.
If she died,
Kisara couldn't be alive either.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だから、落ちたんなら、
　まだきっと海で……。
　ねえ、手伝って、捜すの手伝って。
　あの子を───助けて。お願い。頼むの。
　なんでもするから、だから、助け───」
source.english:
“So if she fell,
she must still be out there,
in the sea… Please, help me look.
Help her. Please. I'm asking.
I'll do anything, just help—”

source.japanese:
───二人であれば。
　片割れと二人、揃ってあれば。
　たとえ数倍する銃口に包囲されていようと嘲笑混じりに切り抜けて、例え最悪の強姦魔に自由を奪われようとも棒を涸らして返り討ちにするだろう、そんな双子も一人では。
　剣を落とした剣者、いや、杖を奪われた跛者、より力なき生き物、それが今のキサラだ。
source.english:
Together, both halves united,
the twins could laugh their way past gun barrels outnumbering them many times.
Even if the vilest rapist deprived them of freedom, they would drain him dry and turn the tables.
Yet alone—Kisara now was weaker than a swordsman who had dropped his blade. No, weaker than a cripple deprived of a stick.

source.japanese:
船底に持ち込んだ幾つもの非常灯の明かりの数だけ、彼女の影は足下に複数伸びているけれど、その影が主の弱さを数倍に、そして厭[いや]らしく戯画して踊らせる。
　伸ばしたその手、助けを請い願う手、求められた者に哀れみと憐憫を誘うより、目を背[そむ]けたくなるほどの醜さと疎[うと]ましさを感じさせるほどに、弱々しい。
source.english:
Every emergency lamp brought below cast another shadow from her feet. Those shadows multiplied their mistress's weakness, dancing it in vile caricature.
Her outstretched hand, begging help, was so weak it provoked less pity than a wish to turn away from its ugly, unwelcome frailty.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「てめえで、やんな。
　生きてるっていうんなら、一人でやんな」
source.english:
“Do it yourself.
If she's alive, go on your own.”

source.japanese: けれど、水夫長がこれ以上はないと言うほどの拒絶ではねのけたのは、キサラの弱さを憎み、疎んだためだけではない───
source.english: But the boatswain's utter rejection did not arise only from hatred and aversion toward Kisara's weakness—

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そんな……どうして……ずっとみんなと一緒だったよ、キサラなんだよ……？」
source.english: “No… Why…? I've been with you all this time. It's Kisara…?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なあキサラ。お前さんな、ここしばらく航路を勝手に変えてたろう。どう言うつもりか知らんが、最初の針路だったら、そもそもこんなところは通っちゃいない筈だ」
source.english: “Listen, Kisara. You've been changing the route on your own lately. Don't know what you're after, but on the original course we'd never have come through here.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それ……なんでっ」
source.english: “That—how…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（いや、なんでって……なあ？
　俺でさえ気づくものを、
　水夫長が判んないはずないじゃんかよう、
　キサラぁ……）
source.english:
(How…?
Come on. If even I noticed,
how could the Boatswain not know,
Kisara…?)

source.japanese:
やはり、朔屋などが黙認していても、露見して当然の事、それどころか水夫長は、あるいは機関長も、朔屋よりずっと前から気づいていたのではないだろうか。
　それをどうしてか、ただしもしなかった彼らにも罪はあるのかも知れない。もしかしたらキサラが言い出すのを待っていたのかも知れない。いずれにしても馬の鐙[あぶみ]は既に切れ、その訳を問うても詮無き事なのが今。
source.english:
Naturally the alteration was bound to be discovered, even if the likes of Sakuya looked the other way. The boatswain—perhaps the chief engineer too—might have known long before he did.
Perhaps they bore some blame for never questioning Kisara. Perhaps they had been waiting for her to confess. Either way, the stirrup leather had already snapped; asking why now would accomplish nothing.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そもそも、こんなくそったれな岩の刃に、噛みこまれる事もなかったんだよ、なあ……。
　こんなボロ船だって、みんなが乗ってるんだ。お前さん達だけじゃねえんだ」
source.english:
“Wouldn't have been caught by this fucking blade of rock in the first place.
Everyone's aboard this rotten ship. Not just you two.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そして、今はこの浸水をどうにかするんで手一杯だ。ようやく食いとめたが、このあとどうなるか、知れたもんじゃねえ」
source.english: “And right now we've got our hands full with the flooding. Finally held it back, but who knows what happens next.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だから、シサムを捜すのには、手を貸してやれねえんだよ」
source.english: “That's why we can't help you look for Sisam.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こんなに、お願いしても」
source.english: “Even if I beg you like this?”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「…………ごめんなさい」
source.english: “…I'm sorry.”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「船が沈んじゃったら、僕達……」
source.english: “If the ship sinks, we…”

source.japanese:
信天翁号の下級水夫達は、あらゆる意味でこの船に拠って立っている存在である。他の船乗りなら、あるいは別の船を見つけたりさもなくば最後の手段として陸に揚がったりもできようが、この下級水夫にとっては信天翁号は蝸牛の殻のようなものだ。降りる時は、生命形態が別の様相を迎える時だけである。
　その彼らにしてみれば、船の不沈はまさに自分たちの存在に関わって、それを危うくするような者、願いに対しては、意に添えないのも当然であろう。
source.english:
The Albatross's junior sailors were creatures whose entire existence, in every sense, rested upon this ship. Other sailors might find another vessel or, at the final extremity, settle ashore; but for these junior sailors the Albatross was a snail's shell. They would leave it only when their very form of life changed.
For them, keeping the ship afloat was nothing less than a question of their own existence. That they could not oblige someone whose wish endangered it was only natural.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「助けて」
source.english: “Help.”

source.japanese:
痛ましい、余りに痛ましい声だった。
　顔だった。
　
　───その癖、肉体だけは元のまま、いや、かつての光輝なくした今では、肉の人形の如き惨めなものだった、けれど。
source.english:
A pitiful voice. Too pitiful.
A pitiful face.
Yet her body alone remained unchanged. No, stripped of its former radiance, it was now a miserable doll of flesh. Still—

source.japanese:
世の中には、そういう肉を、好むものも。
　あるという事を。朔屋は───
source.english:
There were those in the world who liked such flesh.
Sakuya—

source.japanese: ───水夫長のしんみりした声で、我に返ったけれど。
source.english: The boatswain's grave voice brought him back to himself—

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「──────許せ、キサラ」
source.english: “—Forgive me, Kisara.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんでもするよ。どうなってもいいよ。
　キサラのこと、好きにしていいから」
source.english:
“I'll do anything. Don't care what happens to me.
You can do what you like with Kisara.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だから」
source.english: “So—”

source.japanese:
キサラは、キサラの、両腕を開いて見せたのは、もはや助けを求めるためではなく、差し出すための意思表示で。いや、意志ですらなかったのかも知れない。
　それしかないから、それだけしか代価にできるものがなかったから、体がそう動いただけなのだろう。
source.english:
When Kisara spread her arms, it was no longer to ask for help but to offer herself. Or perhaps there was not even intention in it.
There was nothing else—nothing else with which she could pay. Perhaps her body merely moved because that was all she had.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「No way───sh-, she's alive, Shisamu is alive! I, Kisara can tell. Because if she were to die, Kisara couldn't bear living!」

【Kisara】 「So, if she fell off, then she has to still be down in the ocean……. Come on, help, help me look for her. Find her───help me. Please. I'm begging you. I'll do anything for you, so please, help───」

───If they were two. If the two halves were together. Even if they were being surrounded by gun muzzles outnumbering them multiple times over, they would fight their way through it with mocking grins; even if they were stripped of their freedom by the most despicable of rapist maniacs, they would wring out every last drop in his rod and then turn the tables on him; she was one half of those twins. A creature even more powerless than a swordsman who had dropped his sword, yea, a cripple whose cane had been stolen from him: that was Kisara right now.

Beneath her feet stretched as many shadows as there were emergency lights brought down into the hold, yet those shadows danced grotesquely, serving only to mock and multiply their owner's weakness into a sickening caricature. That outstretched hand, that hand of hers imploring them for help, rather than inducing pity or compassion in those it called upon, it only left them feeling repulsed and unsympathetic to the point they wanted to avert their eyes, so feeble was it.
【Bosun】 「You go do it. By yourself. If you insist she's alive, then go save her on your own.」
However, the reason the Bosun had brushed her aside with a rejection so complete it couldn't be more absolute was not just because he loathed Kisara's weakness, or shunned it out of disgust───
【Kisara】 「How could you……why…… I've always stuck with all of you, it's me, Kisara, right……?」

【Bosun】 「Listen, Kisara. You've been changing the course however it damn well suited you for a while now, haven't you? I don't know what kind of excuse you plan on making, but if we followed the original course, then we wouldn't even have passed through this part of the sea to begin with.」
【Kisara】 「That……how!?」
【Naomasa】 （No, "how", I mean……really? Come on, if even I noticed it, then there's no way the Bosun didn't also realize it, Kisaraaa……）

Sure enough, even if the likes of Sakuya held his tongue, it was a matter of course that it would be discovered; in fact, the Bosun, and perhaps even the Chief Engineer too, might well have noticed it long before Sakuya ever did. For some reason, they simply didn't act on it, and perhaps that meant they also shared in the blame for this. Perhaps they might have been waiting for Kisara to be the one to broach the subject. Regardless of all that, the horse's stirrups had already been cut, and even should they ask the reason, it would be naught but an exercise in futility now.
【Bosun】 「And we never would have crashed into this piece of shit blade of a rock either, you hear me……. This wreck of a ship, she carries all of us. It's not just you two.」
【Bosun】 「And finally, there's the fact we have our hands full dealing with this flooding here right now. We finally managed to stop it, but whatever comes after now, we've got no way of knowing.」
【Bosun】 「That's why I can't lend you a hand in looking for Shisamu.」
【Kisara】 「Even after begging you this much?」
【Deck boy】 「…………I'm sorry.」
【Deck boy】 「If the ship goes down, then we……」

The deck boys of the Albatross are existences that are, in every sense of the word, dependent on this ship. Any other sailor could perhaps find another ship, or otherwise go ashore as a last resort, but for these deck boys, the Albatross is like the shell of a snail. They will only disembark when the time comes for their mode of existence to assume a different phase. As far as they were concerned, the sinking of this ship truly was something that their very existence hinged upon, and when begged by someone who had come dangerously close to causing that, it only stands to reason that they would not comply with that request.
【Kisara】 「Help.」

It was heartbreaking─── unbearably heartbreaking, that voice. That face. ───And yet, her body alone remained the same as it ever was; no, now without its former splendour, it was like a puppet of flesh, a most wretched thing, however.
In this world, there are those who have a fondness for such flesh. That is the reality of things. And Sakuya───
───Came to his senses upon hearing the Bosun's solemn tone of voice.
【Bosun】 「──────Forgive me, Kisara.」
【Kisara】 「I'll do anything. I don't care what happens to me. You can do whatever you want with Kisara, anything, so.」
【Kisara】 「So please.」

Kisara, she───what she presented as she spread her arms wide was no longer just her pleading for help, it was a declaration of her willingness to offer herself to them. Nay, perhaps it wasn't even a matter of will. It was because it was all she could do, because that was the only thing she could offer in return, so her body must have moved on its own.

source.japanese: 踏み出した時、足下がやはり怪しくて、つまずいて、よろめいた弾みに乳房までが揺れたのに、朔屋はついに怒鳴りつけた。
source.english: She stepped forward, her footing uncertain again, tripped, staggered. Even her breasts swayed. Sakuya finally shouted.

target.text: When she took a step forwards, her feet were still unsteady; she stumbled, staggered, and the jolt of it even made her breasts sway, but despite that, Sakuya finally shouted heatedly at her.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───やめろぉっ!!」
source.english: “—Stop it!!”

source.japanese: ───その、力失せても量と嵩[かさ]だけはそのままのキサラの体にどうしても奪われてしまった目線を取り戻すには、怒鳴りつけるしかなかったのだという───
source.english: They say he had to shout to tear his eyes away from Kisara's body, which, for all its vanished strength, had lost none of its bulk or fullness—

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ひっ」
source.english: “Ah!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんた、そんな女じゃないだろキサラ。
　ずるくて自分勝手で傲慢で！
　なにかって言えば壊すわ撃つわかっぱらうわ。色仕掛けだってやり放題で」
source.english:
“You're not that kind of woman, Kisara.
Sneaky, selfish, arrogant!
Always smashing, shooting, stealing. Using sex whenever you like.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもそうじゃないだろうあんたは。
　そんな、自分の体で男を買っても、男の為に売るようなのは、違うだろうよ、
　なあキサラ」
source.english:
“But that's not who you are. You'd buy a man with your body,
sure—but sell it for a man? That's not you.
Is it, Kisara?”

source.japanese:
なぜも朔屋がこれほどまでに苛立っているのか。
　それは多分、今のキサラの姿が人の矜持や誇りといったものに、唾を吐きかけて穢[けが]すくらい、弱すぎるから、一人で立って歩く事さえ放棄したような情けなさを見るから。
source.english:
Why was Sakuya so incensed?
Probably because Kisara's present weakness all but spat upon human dignity and pride. He saw a pitiful creature who seemed to have renounced even standing and walking alone.

source.japanese:
朔屋には、それがどういう事か、良く理解できた。こと人の弱さ情けなさ意気地無さだらしなさにかけてはプロフェッショナルの彼である。今のキサラは───弱さを武器にする事もできないくらいに、ひ弱いのだ。
　元々が偉大なる猫族の孤高と自己充足と、それを可能にする不羈を持ち合わせていながら、それを失ってみるとこうだ。
source.english:
Sakuya understood perfectly. When it came to weakness, helplessness, cowardice, and slovenliness, he was a professional. Kisara was now too frail even to make a weapon of weakness.
By nature she possessed the great feline race's proud aloofness, self-sufficiency, and the freedom that made both possible. Deprived of them, this was what she became.

source.japanese:
───そんなのって、ありか。
　弱さを武器にしていいのは、自分のような者だけだ。
　片割れがいなくなった、そんな事でお株を奪われてはたまらない。
source.english:
Was that fair?
Only the likes of him were entitled to make a weapon of weakness.
He would not have her steal his specialty merely because she had lost her other half.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんでもするって言うなら、そんな泣き落としにかかってるより、コルトあたりで脅して連れてけばいいじゃないか。そのほうがよっぽど速いだろ、ぐずぐずしてる暇なんかないんだろ」
source.english: “If you'll do anything, don't stand there trying to win people over with tears. Pull a Colt and force them to come. That'd be a hell of a lot quicker. You don't have time to stand around, do you?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……あ、く……っ、だって……」
source.english: “…Ah, uh… But…”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だって、キサラは一人だとなんにもできないから、だから、だから───」
source.english: “Kisara can't do anything alone. That's why, that's why—”

source.japanese: 怒鳴りつける朔屋の、何ともはやの浅ましさは、さしもの今のキサラにも堪[こた]えたのだろう。
source.english: The sheer, appalling baseness of Sakuya's shouting must have hurt even Kisara in her present state.

source.japanese:
打たれたようによろめいた。
　打ったのは、朔屋の、腐れた柳の枝が風に流されたようなひどい一撃。
　もうどれだけ痛烈に情けなかったのか、知れたものでない。
source.english:
She reeled as though struck.
The blow was Sakuya's—a wretched stroke, like a rotten willow branch tossed by the wind. There was no measuring how keenly that pitiful blow had cut.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……っ、……っ、……アーーーっっ、
　アーーーーーーっっっ！」
source.english:
“…Ah… Ah… Aaaah!
Aaaaaah!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「───STOP THAT!!」
───To reclaim his stolen gaze that had been helplessly drawn to Kisara's body, whose volume and mass alone was untouched despite how her strength had faded away, all he could do was shout at her───
【Kisara】 「Hih!」

【Naomasa】 「You're not that kind of woman, are you, Kisara? You're sly and selfish and arrogant! If I had to sum you up, it would be smashing, shooting, and stealing. You even wield seduction to manipulate however you damn well please!」
【Naomasa】 「But that's not who you are, is it? Using your body to buy a man like that, or selling yourself for the sake of one, that's just not right, is it, Kisara?」

Whyever was Sakuya so deeply frustrated? It was likely because Kisara's current state of being was far too feeble, so weak that she was spitting upon the very concept of human pride and dignity, displaying a wretchedness as if she had abandoned the ability even to stand on her own two feet and walk.

Sakuya understood full well what that meant. When it came to human weakness, patheticness, spinelessness, and gutlessness, he was a professional. And Kisara right now───could not even weaponize her frailty, so weakly was she. By nature, she possessed the solitary pride and self-containment of the mighty Felis genus, as well as the untamed spirit that made exercising it possible, but once she lost that, this is what she became.

───Was something like that even fair? The only ones allowed to weaponize weakness were people like himself. He couldn't stand it, to let her beat him at his own game like this, and all because her other half had vanished.

【Naomasa】 「If you say you're really willing to do anything, then instead of trying to use tears to get your way, why don't you just threaten us with your Colt or something and take us with you? That would go much faster, wouldn't it? I'm pretty sure you don't have time to waste hesitating here, am I right?」
【Kisara】 「……Ah, khh……, but……」
【Kisara】 「But, when Kisara's alone, Kisara can't do anything, so, so───」
The utter wretchedness of Sakuya's shouting, and goodness, how deplorable it was, must have taken a heavy toll on Kisara, even as she was now.

She staggered as though she had been struck And what struck her was Sakuya's cruel blow, like a rotten willow branch swept away in the wind. How bitterly miserable she must have felt was already beyond comprehension.
【Kisara】 「……, ……, ……AーーーH, AーーーーーーHHH!」

source.japanese: キサラ、船底部から飛び出していく、泣き叫びながら、涙をぼろぼろみっともなくまきちらしながら。
source.english: Kisara fled the lower hull, crying and screaming, scattering tears in ugly torrents.

target.text: Kisara leapt out of the hold, crying and screaming all the while, shedding a pathetic torrent of tears everywhere.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あっ、待てよキサラ、人の話は最後まで───」
source.english: “Ah, wait, Kisara! Hear me out—”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Ah, hold up, Kisara, listen until people are done talking to───」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「聞かせなくていいわ、んなクソ説教は。
　てめえなあ。偉そうな口叩くんなら、相手の目を睨[にら]みつけてしろや。キサラの乳ばっかみてやがってよ」
source.english:
“No need to hear the rest of that shit sermon.
And you—if you're going to talk big, look her in the eye while you do it. You've been staring at Kisara's tits the whole time.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「えっ。そうだった？」
source.english: “Huh. Was I?”

source.japanese:
じらり睨[にら]み据えてきた水夫長の目は、先ほどのキサラに置いたよりも、情けないものを見る目だったというからもの凄い。
　それで照れくさそうに笑う朔屋も、ある意味でなかなかの者ではあった。
source.english:
The look the boatswain leveled at him was, they say, even more the look one gives a pitiable specimen than the one he had bestowed on Kisara moments before—which was saying something.
That Sakuya could answer it with a sheepish smile made him, in his own fashion, quite a specimen himself.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「No need for her to listen to some shitty lecture like that. Listen here. If you're gonna talk a big, pretentious game, then do it while staring people straight in the eyes. All you did was look at Kisara's tits, you little shit.」
【Naomasa】 「Huh. Did I really?」

The Bosun fixed him with a sharp, lingering glare, a look reserved for something even more pathetic than what he'd given Kisara earlier, which only made it more frightful. And Sakuya, able to smile bashfully in return at that, was, in a certain sense, quite the man himself.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「うん。あと航海士の泣き顔見て、なんか手を握ったり開いたりしてた。あれ、なぁに？」
source.english: “Yeah. And you saw the mate looking all teary-eyed, and you were clenching and unclenching your fist. What was that all about?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Yeah. And then when you saw the mate's tearful face, you were kind of clenching and unclenching your hands. Now what could that mean?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「昂奮したりどきどきしたりするのを誤魔化す仕草だよね、大抵は」
source.english: “Usually it’s just a way to hide how worked up or nervous you are, right?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「えっ。君ら、なんでそんなに見る目が細かいの」
source.english: “Huh? Why’re you guys so observant?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「That's usually a gesture used to hide arousal or excitement, right?」
【Naomasa】 「Wha-. You guys, why do you have such a sharp eye for detail?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「朔屋なあ。お前死ね。死んじまえ。
　いっぺん死んでやり直せ、な？
　それもできなきゃ目障りだ───
　とっとと、失せやがれえええっっ！」
source.english:
“Sakuya. Die. Just die.
Die once and start over, will you?
If you can't even manage that, you're an eyesore—
get the hell out!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわあとばっちりぃ！
　しし、失礼するッス」
source.english:
“Whoa, caught in the crossfire!
E-excuse me, sir!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Look, Sakuya. Die. Just go ahead and die. Die once, and then do that over again, would you? And if you can't do that, you're an eyesore─── So hurry up AND GET THE HELL OUT OF HERE ALREADYYYY!」
【Naomasa】 「WAAH, I'm catching strays! E-e-excuse me, I'm outta here!」

source.japanese:
朔屋は即座に退散しながら、実はしめしめとほくそ笑む、何しろああも啖呵を切って見せたが、キサラを追いかけたくてたまらなく、かといってそれを許してくれるような場の雰囲気でもなかったから、どうしようかと手を拱[こまね]いていた、だから青年にとってはこれ幸い───
　火事に焼け出された町民のように走ってその場を逃れさる───が。
source.english:
As he made his hasty retreat, Sakuya was secretly gloating. Despite that bold speech, he was desperate to follow Kisara. The mood here would hardly permit it; he had been at a loss what to do. This suited him perfectly.
He fled like a townsman driven out by fire. But—

target.text: While Sakuya beat a hasty retreat, he was actually secretly smirking to himself in satisfaction; after all, while he might have made a show of speaking that scathingly, the urge to chase after Kisara was unbearable; having said that, however, the mood didn't exactly feel like he'd be allowed to do so, and he'd been looking on, at a loss of what to do, so for the young man, this was actually a blessing in disguise─── He ran away from that place like townspeople burned out of their homes by a conflagration───but.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「わー速い速い。あんなに速く走れたっけあの人」
source.english: “Wow, fast, fast. Could he always run that fast?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Wow, he's so fast. Could that guy always run that fast?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そりゃあな、女のケツ追っかけてるわけだからな。……さ、続きだ。
　いらねえ邪魔が入っちまった。
　下手すりゃここで長期戦だ」
source.english:
“Of course—he's chasing a woman's ass. …Right. Back to work.
That was one interruption we didn't need.
If this goes badly, we'll be here a long time.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well yeah, that's because he's chasing after a woman's ass. ……Alright, back to work. An unwelcome nuisance got in our way. Worst case, we're in for a drawn-out battle here.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「アイアイ、水夫長！」
source.english: “Aye aye, Boatswain!”

source.japanese:
朔屋のもくろみなど、水夫長はおろか下級水夫君達でさえもお見通し、やれやれと皆がついた溜息は、厄介払いの、ただでさえ状況はひどいのである。厄介な女は厄介な男に任せるのが割れ鍋に綴じ蓋のなんとやら、皆はこの愁嘆場を休憩の一時に変えて、腕捲り、鉢巻きの締め直しして、力を呼び戻した。
　さあ、まだまだこれからだ、と。
source.english:
Not only the boatswain but even the junior sailors saw straight through Sakuya's intentions. Their weary sighs marked a nuisance disposed of; the situation was bad enough already. Leave the troublesome woman to the troublesome man—a patched lid for a cracked pot, as the saying went. They turned the lamentable scene into a brief rest, rolled up their sleeves, retied their headbands, and summoned back their strength.
Now, then. There was plenty yet to do.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Aye aye, Bosun!」

Sakuya's little scheme was so transparent, even the deck boys saw right through it, to say nothing of the Bosun, and their collective sigh of exasperation was from the relief of getting rid of a nuisance, for the situation was bad enough already. Troublesome women are best left to troublesome men, a case of every Jack has his Jill, or however that went, and they all turned this melodramatic scene into a temporary break, then rolled up their sleeves, retightened their bandannas, and mustered up their strength. Thinking "alright then, this is where the real battle begins".

source.japanese:
北海の夜は黒硝子の様に硬化した凍気で研ぎ澄まされて、信天翁号上甲板の人を小馬鹿にしたようなシルエットさえも鋭角にしてみせた。昇降段の灯りの中から上甲板に浮き上がった朔屋の輪郭も、寒さに引き締まっていたが、彼の目は意気に満ち、吐息は若き魂の漏出のように白くなびき、人の熱を感じさせる。
　凍気をむしろ望んでいたと、身の裡焦がす焦りを鎮めんというのか、一つ白い息を汽笛の様に吐いた後、大きく吸いこんで、肺を硝子の小針に自ら晒すように大きく吸いこんで、そして青年の眸[ひとみ]は、くるんと白く裏返った。
source.english:
The night over the northern sea was whetted by cold hardened like black glass, sharpening even the vaguely mocking silhouette of the Albatross's upper deck. Sakuya emerged from the stairwell's glow, his outline drawn taut by the cold, but vigor filled his eyes. His breath streamed white like the leakage of a young soul—a visible sign of human warmth.
Perhaps he welcomed the freezing air, hoping it would cool the impatience burning inside him. He blew out one white breath like a ship's whistle, then drew a great breath in, exposing his lungs to a thousand tiny glass needles. And the young man's eyes rolled neatly back into his head.

source.japanese:
頬を食いだめた天竺鼠のようにぷっくらさせ、口元を押し戻すように必死に押さえて、舷側に走る、も間に合わない、バラックの陰までしか保たない、で、冴えた凍夜にびちゃびちゃびちゃ、聞き苦しい事この上ない。
　ほとんど胃液のえづきをひとしきり、立ち上がれば戻した後の肌には寒さは丹毒だ、寒いというより痛いので、がたがた震えながら。
source.english:
His cheeks bulging like a guinea pig's with food, he clamped a desperate hand over his mouth and ran for the rail. Too late: he made it only behind the shack. Splatter, splatter, splatter across the crystalline frozen night—an insufferable sound.
Once the dry heaving—mostly stomach acid—had passed, he stood. The cold against his skin now felt like erysipelas: not so much chill as pain. He shook violently.

target.text: Honed to a fine edge by a frigid chill that had hardened like black glass, the night over the northern seas rendered even the mockingly silly silhouette of the upper deck of the Albatross in sharp angles. Sakuya surfaced onto the upper deck from the light of the ladder, his silhouette also pulled taut by the cold, but his eyes were full of spirit, his breath white and fluttering like his young soul itself were being exhaled, conveying the passionate heat of man.

If anything, he desired the freezing air; perhaps it could calm the anxious impatience burning within him, and after exhaling a single white breath like a steam whistle, he inhaled, breathing in so deeply, it was as if he was baring his lungs to tiny glass needles, and then the young man's eyes rolled back into his head and turned completely white.

His cheeks puffed up like he were a guinea pig stuffing itself with food, he desperately pressed his hands to his mouth in an attempt to push it back in, ran to the side of the ship, but it was too late, he only made it behind a shack, and there, on this crispy freezing night, a loud brlbrlbrlrlrlr resounded; a less pleasant sound you would be hard-pressed to find. After a spell of violent retching that expelled little more than gastric acid, he got back on his feet, and the cold against his skin, freshly flushed from throwing up, attacked him like ignis sacer; it was painful rather than just cold, leaving him shivering.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ～～……。考えてみれば俺、
　今さっき必死で浸水せき止める仕事、
　やってたばっかじゃないかよ。
　その上で走ればそりゃー戻すわ」
source.english:
“Ahh… Come to think of it,
I've only just been working like hell
to stop us flooding.
Run on top of that and of course I'll puke.”

source.japanese: ……海に出てそれなりに経つのに、いっかな錬りという骨[コツ]が芯に入らない朔屋で、先ほどまでの少しは精悍な目つきも、吐き戻した後では普段に増した隈が戻って、既に凍傷にやられたが如きの様[ざま]な。
source.english: …Sakuya had been at sea a respectable while, yet had never developed anything resembling a seasoned man's backbone. The fleeting vigor in his eyes was gone; after vomiting, the shadows returned beneath them darker than ever, and he looked already ravaged by frostbite.

source.japanese: そのくすんだ目で四方を目探ったところで何も見えまいが、きょろらきょろらと遣りながら、
source.english: Those dull eyes could hardly discern much, but he cast them here and there—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぅおーい……キサラよぅ……。
　ここにもいないのか……キサラよぅ……」
source.english:
“Heeey… Kisara…
Not here either… Kisara…”

source.japanese: 呼べど呼びかけど応[いら]えのなく、
source.english: He called and called. No answer.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どっかに隠れてないかぁ……。
　俺、別に怒っちゃないからさぁ……。
　出てこいよう……。
　出てこないと言っちゃうぞぉ……」
source.english:
“Aren’t you hiding somewhere…?
I’m not really mad or anything…
Come on out…
If you don’t come out, I’m gonna say it…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「キサラの初体験は満で一五の時で、
　相手は年上の使用人で、
　向こうはあんまりに興奮しすぎて、
　入れただけでお腹の上に出しちゃってー」
source.english:
“Kisara’s first time was when she was exactly fifteen,
and her partner was an older servant.
He got way too excited,
and as soon as he entered her, he came right on her stomach—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「その後勢いがついちゃって、
　五回も立て続けに嵌[は]めちゃった、
　って言うのがあんたの初体験だって事ー、
　出てこないとばらしちゃうぞー。
　……ってあら言っちゃった」
source.english:
“You got carried away after
that, and ended up doing it five times in a row—that’s what you call your first time,
right?
If you don’t come out, I’m going to spill the beans.
…Oops, I said it.”

source.japanese: ……たとえ冷気に冴えて雪精が闇森の上空で今年の雪の塩梅を談合しているような夜だろうが、あるいは真夏の、丘の陰に役者に扮した妖精達が舞台でも開いていそうな夢のような夜だろうが、この青年にかかればたちまちに酔いどれのがなりたてる猥歌となり果てるという事がよく判る。朔屋にとって夜の寒気は、酔っ払ってあげく道端にぶち潰れた時に凍え死ぬか死なないかの目盛り程度でしかないのだろう。
source.english: …Whether the night was so sharp with cold that snow spirits conferred above a dark forest on the year's snowfall, or a dreamlike midsummer night on which fairies dressed as players seemed ready to stage a drama behind the hills, in this young man's hands it would instantly degenerate into a lewd song bawled by a drunk. To Sakuya, the night's cold was probably no more than a gauge of whether, after drinking himself insensible by the roadside, he would freeze to death.

source.japanese: ……要するに朔屋は船底部を飛び出した後、キサラを乱暴だが男らしくその背中を羽交い締めにする事も、手を掴み止めて落ち着けと軽い張り手を喰らわすといった気働きも見せる事もなく、見失ったのである。あんな芯の抜けた膝でへにゃへにゃと出ていったキサラを、である。この青年の巡りの悪さ、推して知るべき、か。
source.english: …In short, after rushing from the bottom of the ship, Sakuya had neither seized Kisara from behind in some rough but manly restraint nor shown the presence of mind to catch her by the hand, slap her lightly, and tell her to calm down. He had lost her—Kisara, who had staggered away on knees with no strength left in them. One can imagine how poorly the gears turned in this young man's head.

source.japanese: 船内の一々を捜していてはさすがに切りがない、シサムを見失ったという上甲板に戻ってきているのでは、とそこは考えて上がってきたものの、ここにもキサラは見えず、朔屋はバラックを開け閉めし、果ては縄がみっしりしまってあってクロでさえしまえないような道具箱を開けたりの、どうにも気の利かない捜しようで上甲板を行くうちに、行き当たった背中の、あら嬉しや、にならず、着崩した白の着物だった。
source.english: Searching every corner of the ship would never end. He had reasoned that she might have returned to the upper deck, where she had lost sight of Sisam, but Kisara was nowhere there either. He opened and shut the shack, even searched a toolbox packed so tight with rope that Kuro herself could not have been stuffed inside. As he worked his witless way around the upper deck, his eyes at last alighted on a back. Alas, no joy: it wore a loosely draped white kimono.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Ah～～……. Now that I think about it, I was working so frantically to stop the flooding, and I only just finished doing that, didn't I? If I sprint on top of that, of course I'd empty my stomach.」

……It had been quite a while since he first set out to sea, but Sakuya had not had even a shadow of a disciplined disposition truly settle in his core, and that slightly sharp, masculine look that had been in his eyes until just a moment ago was also nowhere to be seen; after throwing up, the dark circles around his eyes returned to him deeper than ever, and he was in so sorry a state, it looked as if he was already suffering from frostbite.
Though searching all around with those dim, clouded eyes would yield him nothing, his gaze still kept darting restlessly to and fro,
【Naomasa】 「OOOーI……Kisara……. You not here either……Kisara……?」
Though he called out again and again, no answer came,
【Naomasa】 「Are you hiding somewhere……? I'm not angry or anything, okay……? Please come out……. If you don't come out, I'll say it……」

【Naomasa】 「Kisara's first experience was when she was fifteen in full years, her partner was an older servant, and he was way too excited, so he ended up cumming all over her stomach right after putting it in!」

【Naomasa】 「After that, things picked up steam, and they ended up fucking five times in a row, and that was your first experieeence、 and if you don't come out, then I'll reveal it aaaall. ……Wait, oops, I just did.」

……Even if this were the sort of night where snow sprites, crisp and cheerful in the freezing air, would hold conference on the state of this year's snowfall in the skies above a dark forest, or perhaps the sort of night akin to a midsummer night's dream where the fairies dressed up as actors in the shadows of a hill and staged a performance of dance and theatre, as soon as it was put in this young man's hands, it would instantly degenerate into the hoarsely bellowed bawdy songs of a drunkard, that much was glaringly obvious to see.

From Sakuya's perspective, the chill of night probably seemed nothing more than a scale for measuring whether or not he would perish from the cold if he collapsed by the roadside after drinking himself senseless.

……To summarize, after Sakuya rushed out of the ship's hold, he did not pin Kisara's arms behind her back in a violent yet manly way, nor did he display tact by grabbing her by the hand and stopping her, then giving her a gentle slap on the cheek while telling her to calm down; he had simply lost sight of her. She who had walked off on knees wobbly and limp, that Kisara. The poor circulation of this young man's dim-witted brain almost spoke for itself, did it not?

Even should he search through every little nook and cranny on the whole ship, there would be no end to it, and she might have returned to the upper deck, the place she claimed to have lost sight of Shisamu, and thinking as much, he himself had gone up there, but he still couldn't find Kisara here either; Sakuya opened and closed the doors to every single shack, and in the end, it got to the point where he even flung open toolboxes so packed with rope that it seemed not even Kuro could fit inside; as he wandered across the upper deck in his clumsy search, he came upon someone's back, and what a joyful surprise; alas, it was no such thing, for it was but a sloppily-worn, white kimono.

source.japanese: 殺し屋が、一段高く箱の上に胡座組みして、つくねんと暗い夜を見上げて、こちらの自ずから光零すような蒼い眸[ひとみ]は、朔屋の濁った目よりよほど北海に相応しかった。が、その辺りの風趣を解す朔屋ではない。智里をまず見て口にしたのは、
source.english: The killer sat cross-legged on a raised box, alone, looking up into the dark night. Blue eyes seemed to spill their own light, far better suited to the northern sea than Sakuya's murky ones. But Sakuya could not appreciate such atmosphere. His first words on seeing Tomosato were—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うっわぁ寒[さっむ]っぇぇー……」
source.english: “Ugh, it's coooold…”

source.japanese:
で、重ね着してあるにもかかわらずもさもさと船員服の襟[えり]をかき合わせた。まあこれは智里も智里で、彼はいつものなり、白の着物に灰黒の袴[はかま]はいいとしても、その前身頃も、着崩したなりにはだけたままだったからで。
　こう、来るなり出会うなりやかましい朔屋へ、殺し屋はじらり視線を落として、自分の風采を小馬鹿にされた事に一言あったなら、彼も朔屋と同じ土俵に落ちてしまうのだが、
source.english:
He fussily drew his sailor's collar together despite his layers. To be fair, Tomosato wore his usual white kimono and charcoal-gray hakama, and the front hung open as ever.
The killer cast a sidelong glance down at Sakuya, noisy from the instant he arrived. Answering the slight against his style would have brought him down to Sakuya's level. Instead—

target.text: Cross-legged atop a box a step high, the murderer sat motionlessly, gazing vacantly up at the dark night by his lonesome, and those azure eyes, overflowing with a light all their own, were far better suited to the northern seas than Sakuya's murky gaze. However, Sakuya was never one to appreciate the refined charm of such things. The first thing he let out of his mouth when he saw Tomosato was:
【Naomasa】 「Aah, that looksh sho cooooldー……」

And with that, despite being bundled up in several layers, he still clumsily pulled the collar of his sailor uniform close. Mind you, Tomosato was hardly helping matters; setting aside his usual dark grey hakama over his white kimono, he had still left the front hanging open in his typical disheveled fashion. The murderer lowered his gaze slowly and deliberately, fixing it on Sakuya, a man ever noisy whenever he showed up or you ran into him, and had he uttered a single objection to having his style mocked, he would end up sinking to Sakuya's level, but,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「嘘つくなイ直の字。さっきのキサラの初めて云々、あれ、お前の時のじゃねえか」
source.english: “Don’t lie, Nao. That business earlier about Kisara’s ‘first time’—that was about you, wasn’t it?”

source.japanese: 風花の、ひとひら舞い来たりて二人の間を過ぎゆきにけり、黒々とした夜の中で鮮烈に白く、かつ朔屋の顔は赤黒く。
source.english: A single snowflake drifted by, passing between the two of them; it was strikingly white against the pitch-black night, while Sakuya’s face was dark red.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Lying is bad, big Nao. That stuff you just yelled about Kisara's first time or whatever, that was all you, wasn't it?」
A single flake of stray snow fluttered down to pass between the two: dazzlingly white against the jet-black of the night, while Sakuya's face burned a deep, dusky red.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「しかもおめえ朔屋、ホントは入れてすぐじゃなく、入れる前に漏らしたくせに、女の前だからって見栄張ることもねえだろ、童貞だったんだから」
source.english: “And you, Sakuya—you actually came before you even got it in, not right after. You didn’t have to put on a front just because there were girls around, did you? You were a virgin, after all.”

source.japanese:
今一度風花の来たったが、今度は朔屋の顔色見えず、なんとなれば青年は智里の前に深々と土下座していたから。オイルスキンのように夜に黒く、氷のように冷たい上甲板だったが、構ったものではなかった。これ以上智里様に要らぬ御無礼を働いては、初めて自涜を覚えた日の詳細までも暴露されかねないと。
　なんで智里がそんな事まで知っているのか、この際その子細などは問題ではない。その辺りの事情、掌を指すよろしく殺し屋が知っている事自体が大問題なのだ。
source.english:
Another flurry of snow came, but this time Sakuya's complexion was hidden: he lay prostrate before Tomosato. The upper deck was black as oilskin in the night and cold as ice, but he did not care. One more act of insolence toward Lord Tomosato and the man might expose even the details of the day Sakuya first learned to masturbate.
How Tomosato knew such things was beside the point. The great problem was that a killer knew them as plainly as the lines on his own palm.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「すんませんっしたぁ！　あっしの事は朔屋なんて呼ばずに犬屋とでも呼んで下せえ、旦那の卑しい犬めでございやすけえ。
　あ、お雪駄に埃が……」
source.english:
“I'm sooo sorry! Please don't call me Sakuya—call me Inuya instead. I'm just my master's lowly dog, after all.
Oh, there's dust on your sandals…”

source.japanese: と有りもしない埃を取る風情に低い体勢から手を伸ばしたのに、またじろりと睨[にら]んで、
source.english: Sakuya reached up from his cringing crouch and made a show of brushing away nonexistent dust. Tomosato only glared at him again.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Not to mention, Sakuya, you didn't actually cum right after sticking it in, you came before that. No need to put on airs just because you're in front a girl, you were a virgin, it's no big deal.」

Yet another flake of snow arrived on the winds, but this time, the colour of Sakuya's face was nowhere to be seen, the reason being that the young man was deeply prostrating himself in a dogeza before Tomosato. The night was black as oilskin, the deck cold as ice, but he paid it no heed. For if he committed any more needless insolence before Lord Tomosato, it was quite possible he would expose even the sordid details of that day he first learned of onanism. How did Tomosato even know such things; the particulars of that were not relevant in these circumstances. The fact that a murderer knew all those details like the back of his hand, however, was a great problem.

【Naomasa】 「I am so terribly sorry, sir! Pray, do not call my humble self Sakuya, but Inuya instead, for I am but the master's lowborn mutt. Ah, I see there is some dust on your setta……」 (TN: Inuya, written "犬屋", is just Sakuya's name with the first kanji replaced with the kanji for dog. Setta, written "雪駄", is a type of traditional Japanese sandal.)
With that, Sakuya reached out a hand from his low stance in a manner that made it seem he was brushing off some imaginary dust, and yet he was fixed with another sharp glare,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ねえぞ。三つとも」
source.english: “Gone. All three.”
“…Huh?”

source.japanese: この男とも船に乗りこんでから程なくの付き合いだが、この脈絡のない物言いに関しては何時まで経っても慣れる事できぬ。これは大概の人間なら皆そうで、朔屋の巡りの悪さばかりを責めるのも気の毒だ。
source.english: He had known this man almost since boarding, but could never grow accustomed to these remarks that came out of nowhere. Most people would be the same. It would be unfair to blame only Sakuya's slowness.

source.japanese:
ともかく、智里が顎をしゃくった方を見やれば、見やっても、舷側が広がっているばかりで、他には何も見えやしない。
　が、よくよく見ればそこには支柱の二本海へと伸びていて、今は空なのがいくらか不自然で、元は何かが索留されてあったと思しかった。
source.english:
He looked where Tomosato jerked his chin. The ship's side, nothing else.
But closer inspection showed two arms stretching out over the sea. Their emptiness looked somewhat unnatural. Something must once have been lashed there.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「They're gone. All three.」
【Naomasa】 「……Uh?」

Though he'd made the acquaintance of this man only shortly after boarding this ship, he could never get used to this way he sometimes spoke with neither context nor coherence, no matter how much time passed. Most people would feel the same way, so it was unfair to put all the blame on Sakuya's simple mind.

Regardless, when he looked in the direction that Tomosato had jerked his chin, for all that he did, all that filled his vision was the ship's side, and he could spot nothing else. Looking closely, however, a pair of davit arms extended out over the sea; that they were empty now felt somewhat unnatural, suggesting something had originally been lashed there with gripes.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「間抜け面さらしてんなよ、直公。
　シサムとキサラと救命ボートだよ。
　三つともここにゃあないないぷう、だ」
source.english:
“Don't stand there looking dumb, Nao.
Sisam, Kisara and the lifeboat.
All three gone bye-bye.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、つまり───？」
source.english: “Ah, meaning—?”

source.japanese: つまりも何も、智里はそこに双子が具合を見ていた救命ボートが吊してあったと、そう言っているのである。
source.english: No ‘meaning’ about it. Tomosato was saying that the lifeboat the twins had been working on had hung there.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Wipe that dumb look off your face, Nao-kou. I meant Shisamu, Kisara, and the lifeboat. All three are gone-gone-poof.」
【Naomasa】 「Aah, so in other words───?」
Forget about other words, this was where the life boat that the twins had been checking the condition of had been suspended from; that was what Tomosato was saying.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「どこまでも巡りの鈍い脳味噌だな、豆腐みたいにつるっつるかね。つまりもくそも、シサムと救命ボートは一緒に落っこったんだろ。
　それからキサラはこっちに来てねえぞ」
source.english:
“How slow can that brain be? Smooth as tofu? Sisam fell with the lifeboat, probably.
And Kisara hasn't been this way.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「How hopelessly sluggish your brain is. What, is it smooth as tofu in there? To hell with your other words, Shisamu and that lifeboat must have fallen down together. And Kisara hasn't returned here since.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「だから、三つともここにはないぞと、そう言うているのさ」
source.english: “That's why I'm saying none of the three are here.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんたの話し方がおかしいんだよう。
　とにかく、なら、もしかしてシサムは救命ボートの中に落ちてるかも……」
source.english:
“It's your way of talking that's weird.
Anyway, then Sisam might've fallen into the lifeboat…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「So, all three are nowhere to be found here, that's what I'm telling you.」
【Naomasa】 「You've got a weird way of talking. Anyways, in that case, maybe it's possible that Shisamu fell into the lifeboat……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そこまでは知らんがな。そうかも知れんし、そうでねえかも知れねえな」
source.english: “Don't know that much. Maybe. Maybe not.”

source.japanese:
……舷側から危なっかしく身を乗り出して、暗く冷たく畝[うね]る夜の海を、今更眺めたところで。
　身を引き戻し、船のうねりにしばし足下ふらつかせた風であった、朔屋が智里に訊ねた事というのも、殺し屋の物言いのように脈絡がなかったけれど。
source.english:
…He leaned precariously over the side. What use now to stare at the dark, cold swells?
Pulling back, he wavered on his feet awhile with the ship's movement. His question to Tomosato was no less disconnected than the killer's remarks.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───なああんた、一体いつ俺を殺すつもりなの？」
source.english: “—Hey. When exactly are you going to kill me?”

source.japanese: けれども、まだ青年の心の流れの方が見やすいだろう。殺す殺し屋だと言い張っておきながら、智里の言う事する事為す事、これまで朔屋の前に道を付ける事の方が多いので。判りづらいが。
source.english: Yet the young man's train of thought was easier to follow. Tomosato insisted he was a killer come to kill, but his words and deeds had more often opened a path before Sakuya. Difficult though it was to see.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「I don't know that much. Maybe that's what happened, maybe it isn't.」

……Sakuya leaned precariously far over the gunwale to gaze at the dark, cold, swelling night sea, as if that would do him any good now. He pulled himself back, seemed a bit unsteady on his feet for a while as the ship rolled, but what Sakuya then asked Tomosato about was as sudden and lacking in context as the way the murderer spoke.
【Naomasa】 「───Hey, so when in the world are you planning on killing me?」

However, the workings of this young man's mind were still easier to grasp. While he obstinately insisted that he was a murdering murderer, in terms of what Tomosato said, did, and had made happen hitherto? Much of it had served to pave the road before Sakuya and help him along it. Though it was difficult to understand.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「お前が海底洞窟に、
　大冒険に出る時あたりかな」
source.english:
“When you set off on a great
adventure into an undersea cave, maybe.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「智里ってさ……友達ろくにいないだろ」
source.english: “Tomosato… You don't have many friends, do you?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Somewhere around the time you set forth on a grand adventure, diving into a cave at the bottom of the ocean, I guess?」
【Naomasa】 「Tomosato, man……you don't really have any friends, do you?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おうとも」
source.english: “Sure don't.”

source.japanese:
するりと、水でも飲むように応えた智里の、では自分はなんなのだろうと、朔屋はようやく凍夜の冴えた風情が頭に染みいったか、感傷的に思った。この飄々とした蒼い眸[ひとみ]の男が、もし自分を友達だと呼んでくれるのなら、それは持つ物少ない自分にとって、大事のものの一つとなるのではないかと、朔屋にしては感傷的に想った。
　感傷的に暫[しばら]くそこに佇んで、二人とも同時に首を傾げた。
source.english:
The answer slipped from him as easily as drinking water. Then what was Sakuya to him? Perhaps the clear beauty of the frozen night had at last entered his head. He grew sentimental. If this blithe, blue-eyed man would call him a friend, might that not become one precious possession for someone with so few? Sentimental thoughts, for Sakuya.
He stood there sentimentally awhile. Both tilted their heads together.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あのさ、俺……、
　何しようとしてたんだっけ？」
source.english:
“…Hey, I…
What was I going to do?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Damn right I don't.」

Tomosato answered fluidly, as naturally as taking a swig of water, but then what about himself, Sakuya wondered, and perhaps the sharp clarity of the frigid night had finally begun to seep into his mind, for he felt sentimental. If this aloof, easygoing man with azure eyes were to call him friend, then for someone like himself, a man who had so little, that could become one of the few things he truly valued; so Sakuya felt, in an unusual display of sentiment. He just stood there for a while, lost in that sentiment, and then the two of them tilted their heads in unison.
【Naomasa】 「……Listen, I……, remind me again, what I was about to do?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「いや俺が訊きてぇや。
　お前、キサラを捜しに来てたのに、
　何いつまでそこにつっ立ってンの？」
source.english:
“I'd like to know.
You came looking for Kisara.
Why're you still standing there?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「No, that's what I wanna ask. You came here looking for Kisara, so how long are you just gonna stand there?」

source.japanese: おお、と拳で掌を打って、こいつはもしかして天眼通でもあるまい事か、と心から感心した顔で踵[きびす]を返して駆け戻っていく朔屋の背中を、智里は───こちらも心底感心の顔して送ったというから、もしかしたらこの二人、根底では似た者同士なのかも知れない。
source.english: He cried ‘Oh!’ and struck his fist into his palm, then turned and ran back with a look of heartfelt admiration: could the man possess divine sight? Tomosato, they say, watched him go with an equally sincere expression of wonder. Perhaps at bottom these two were much alike.

target.text: With an "oh!", he struck his palm with a fist, his face lighting up with genuine admiration as he wondered if this guy had clairvoyance or something, then did a pivot on his heel; looking at Sakuya's retreating figure dashing back inside, Tomosato───also saw Sakuya off with an expression of wholehearted admiration, so perhaps, deep down, they were cut from the same cloth.

source.japanese:
男前の　　殺し屋は
　
　寒そうに　　震えてた
　
『女を抱いてきたのか』
　
『あたりきよう』
　
『湯たんぽを抱きな』
　
　熱い鉛を　　抱いて　　死んだ
source.english:
The handsome killer
Shivered in the cold.

‘Had a woman in your arms?’
‘You bet I have.’

‘Hold a hot-water bottle.’

He held hot lead
And died.

target.text: The handsome murderer Shivered as if freezing 『Were you out embracing a woman?』 『Course I was.』 『Then go embrace a hot water bottle.』 Embracing hot lead he died (TN: This is a slightly modified version of the opening song to a movie from 1967, Koroshi no Rakuin, also known in English as Branded to Kill.)

source.japanese: ───智里と別れた後、再び船内に戻った朔屋は、彼の印象醒めやらず、遠い遠い昔に流行ったという古い古い銀幕の挿入歌なぞを微妙に間違えて歌いながら昇降段を駆け下りて、似合わない事をしでかした相応の報い天よりたちまち降って、最後の段を二段ほど踏み外して足を捻って痛い痛い、蹲って呻吟をしばし、立ち上がって走り去ってまた戻ってきて忙しい。
source.english: After parting from Tomosato, Sakuya went back inside with the man's impression still vivid in his mind. He raced down the stairs singing—slightly wrong—an ancient song from an ancient film said to have been popular long, long ago. Heaven promptly punished him for doing something so ill-suited to his character: he missed the last two steps, twisted his ankle—ow, ow—crouched and groaned awhile, got up and ran away, then came running back. A busy fellow.

source.japanese: 何しろキサラがそこに、昇降段の陰に昏倒していたのを一瞬は見ておきながら、なんでこんなところで寝てるんだ人騒がせな、自分の部屋で眠りやがれいこの唐変木、と智の字の伝法な調子にかぶれたか、見過ごしに行ってしまったのに気がついて慌てて戻ってきたのだった。
source.english: For Kisara lay unconscious there, in the stairway's shadow. He had seen her for an instant and, infected perhaps by Tomosato's swagger, thought: why sleep here, you nuisance, go to your room, you blockhead. He had passed her by. Realizing it, he hurried back.

source.japanese:
寒夜の階段下の、力なく倒れ伏している女の金髪は暗がりに赤味を帯びて、濃く塗り重ねた油絵の暗鬱な美調を描いたが、悠長に鑑賞するような美意識などは我が子を喰らっているサトゥルヌスあたりについでに喰わせちまえと朔屋は泡を食って抱き上げた、ら、航海士の肉体のみしりと詰まって重い。先だって上に跨[またが]られた時はまだ彼女に意識があったから重心を加減してもらえたけれど、気絶している時ではそうもいくまい。なにもキサラが太り肉[じし]というわけではなく、筋肉質で均整取れた肢体である事だが、ともかく朔屋は非力な腕に気合いで持ち上げる。
　掛け声は、先ほどの挿入歌の調子がまだ頭に残っていたのでそれだ。ところが。
source.english:
Beneath the stairs in the freezing night, the fallen woman’s blond hair took on a ruddy cast in the darkness, completing a somber oil painting laid on in heavy impasto. But any aesthetic sensibility inclined to pause and admire it could be fed as an afterthought to Saturn, busy devouring his son: Sakuya snatched her up in a panic—and found the navigator’s body packed solid and heavy. When she had straddled him earlier, she had still been conscious and could shift her weight to spare him; unconscious, she could hardly oblige. Not that Kisara was fat: hers was a muscular, well-proportioned figure. At any rate, Sakuya heaved her aloft by sheer force of spirit in his feeble arms.
The cry he gave as he lifted her came from that film song, whose tune still lingered in his head. Whereupon—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「『湯たんぽを抱き……なぁ！』
　……って。熱っ。熱い、キサラあんた肉たんぽ!?」
source.english:
“‘Hold a hot-water—bottle!’
…Hot! You're hot, Kisara. A hot-meat bottle!?”

source.japanese:
呼びかけても答えはあろう筈もなく、キサラは朔屋の腕の中でぐたりと頭を垂らした、その首筋が肌の肌理粗くしているくせに、こうも熱い、煮立ち湯を入れた直後の湯たんぽもかくやに熱いのには朔屋、いよいよ慌てた。
　片割れを失くした不安、精神的疲労で意識を失ったばかりか高熱まで発している。とにかく部屋までと、運んでいく朔屋は汗だくでよろめいて、これではどちらが熱病者なのか知れたものではなかった。
source.english:
No answer could possibly come. Kisara's head lolled in his arms; the skin at her neck had gone coarse with fever, yet it was hot—hot as a hot-water bottle freshly filled with boiling water. Sakuya's alarm mounted.
The anxiety of losing her other half and the exhaustion of spirit had not merely made her faint: she had developed a high fever. Sakuya staggered toward her room under his burden, pouring sweat, until it was impossible to tell which of them had the fever.

target.text: ───After parting ways with Tomosato, Sakuya had returned inside the ship once more, but unable to shake off the impression he left him with, he rushed down the ladder while singing an old, even ancient opening theme from the silver screen, one that had supposedly been popular in distant days of yore, with some subtle mistakes, and the punishment for doing something so out of character quickly came crashing down on him from the heavens; he missed the last couple steps, twisted his ankle, ouch ouch, crouched down and groaned for a while, then got back up, ran off, only to come running back again: what a busy man.

For you see, Kisara was right there, and though he saw her for a brief moment, "Why are you sleeping out here, causing a big fuss for nothing. Go sleep in your own damn room, you dumb oaf." were the thoughts running through his head; perhaps he had been infected by big Tomo's preachy tone, and though he overlooked her and kept going, he realized his mistake and hurried back in a fluster.

Beneath the ladder on this freezing night, the golden locks of this woman helplessly fallen flat on her face took on a reddish tinge in the dark, evoking the gloomy aesthetic harmony of a heavily layered oil painting, but any sort of aesthetic sensibilities that would permit one to leisurely savour such beauteous art might as well be fed to Saturn busy devouring his own son, Sakuya thought, almost losing his head as he picked her up in his arms, only to find the mate's body still full and heavy.

Last time she'd been straddling him, she was still conscious and adjusting her center of gravity, but when unconscious, it didn't go nearly as well. It was not like any part of Kisara was stout or corpulent, no, her body was muscular and well-proportioned, but regardless, Sakuya managed to force his scrawny arms to hoist her up through sheer willpower. As for his shout of exertion, the tune of that old opening theme from before was still stuck in his head, so that's what he ended up going with. And then.
【Naomasa】 「『Then go embrace a hot water…… bottle!』 ……Wait. Hot. That's really hot, Kisara, are you a hot flesh bottle or something!?」

He could call out to her all he liked, he surely wouldn't get an answer, for Kisara was slumped in Sakuya's arms, her head hanging limply, and the nape of her neck, despite how coarse the texture of the skin was, still radiated so much heat; it was a heat that could rival a hot water bottle freshly filled with boiling water, and Sakuya finally began to truly panic.

She hadn't just lost consciousness from the worry of losing her other half and the mental fatigue that brought with it, she was even running a high fever. First things first, he had to get her to her cabin, and as Sakuya carried her, he stumbled and staggered, drenched in sweat, and by the end, it was no longer possible to tell which of the two suffered from the fever.

source.japanese:
かくして離ればなれになってしまったシサム・キサラだ。いなくなってしまったのはシサム、残っているのはキサラ、と自分に言い聞かせて、人事不省となった双子の片割れを船室に寝かせ、朔屋も暗い心で見守る。どうして寝台に押しこむ時でさえ、この女のスカートはある以上は捲[まく]れ上がらないのかの大難問に頭を悩ませつつ。
　シサムの行方も気になるが、キサラを置いていく事にも不安が大きい。
source.english:
Thus Sisam and Kisara had been separated. Sisam gone, Kisara here: Sakuya repeated it to himself. He laid the unconscious twin in her cabin and watched her, heavy-hearted, puzzling over the great mystery of why her skirt would not rise beyond a certain point even when he pushed her into bed.
He worried about Sisam's whereabouts, but was deeply uneasy at leaving Kisara.

source.japanese:
浸水はかろうじて食い止めたようで、船内に退避を匂わせるような喧噪は聞こえてこない。だが、と朔屋は思い出す。船底部を芋刺しにしたあの暗礁の剣、相当に深く食いこんで、よほど巧い偶然が働かないと、無事に脱出できそうもないと朔屋が素人目の判断だが、実際そこまで見誤ってもいなかった。
　現在船底部では、水夫長がこれをどう切り抜けたものかの算段に、半面の龍も熱にやられて白い気を吐き出している───湯気が立っている。
source.english:
The flooding seemed barely contained. No clamor suggesting evacuation reached him. But he remembered that sword of reef skewering the hull. It had bitten so deeply that only a very fortunate chance seemed likely to free them safely. An amateur's judgment, yet not far wrong. Down below, the boatswain was devising an escape.
Even the dragon on one half of his face suffered from the heat of thought, breathing white vapor. Steam rose from it.

target.text: Thus, Shisamu and Kisara were torn apart. Shisamu was the one who had disappeared, Kisara the one who remained; so Sakuya told himself as he laid the unconscious half of the pair of twins to bed in her cabin, watching over her with a heavy heart. How come that, even when he pushed her into bed, this woman's skirt simply refused to roll up beyond a certain point? He continued to rack his brains over this great enigma. He was concerned about Shisamu's whereabouts, but just leaving Kisara behind also brought him great unease.

They seemed to have narrowly managed to stem the flooding, for he couldn't hear any tumult on the ship that suggested they were evacuating. However, Sakuya recalled. The blade of that hidden reef, which had skewered the bottom of the ship like a potato on a stick, had embedded itself rather deeply, and unless some very fortuitous coincidence intervened, safe escape from it seemed unlikely, at least in Sakuya's amateur opinion, and in truth, he wasn't that far off the mark. Down in the hold, the Bosun was currently straining his brains so feverishly for a way out that even the dragon covering half his face was overcome with heat, spewing white vapour ───steam rising off him.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……うん？　どうぞ」
source.english: “…Hm? Come in.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Hmm? Come in.」

source.japanese: 招き入れれば髑髏も白く晒したる死神、にしては随分ちんまりとまとまったと、いささかならず相当に失礼な印象で迎えた朔屋の心、幸い知らずにクロは、寝台に伏したキサラを認めて気遣わしげに睫翳濃くして、覗きこんで、
source.english: When he admitted her, Sakuya's first impression was of Death displaying a bleached-white skull—though a remarkably small and compact Death, to be sure. It was a thoroughly rude thought. Fortunately unaware of it, Kuro saw Kisara lying in bed, concern darkening the shadows of her lashes as she bent close.

target.text: "For a Grim Reaper with a stark, bleached-white skull, she's awfully tiny and unassuming"; thus was the more than just a little impolite impression in Sakuya's mind as he welcomed her inside, but fortunately, Kuro remained oblivious to that, and when she noticed Kisara lying in bed, she leaned in with a worried look, peering down with her lashes casting deep shadows over her eyes.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「キサラさん、死んじゃうの？」
source.english: “Is Kisara going to die?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……泣いちゃうよ、
　そんなこと言われたら俺」
source.english:
“…You'll make me cry
if you say things like that.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まあ、死にはしないとだろうとは思うんだけどさ……なんか、シサムがどっかに行っちゃったみたいなんだ。それでほら、キサラ、寝込んじまったんだな」
source.english: “Well, I don't think she'll die… Sisam seems to have gone somewhere. So, well, Kisara's taken to bed.”

source.japanese: と朔屋が説明するまでもなく、おおかたの事情は誰かより聞いていたのだろう、それにそもそもクロの方が朔屋より双子達と付き合いは長い。
source.english: He hardly needed to explain. Someone had probably told Kuro the general story. In the first place, she had known the twins longer than Sakuya.

source.japanese: 伏したキサラの寝息苦しげなのへ覗きこんで、聴くうちに、クロはたちまちその赤い眸[ひとみ]を涙に潤[うる]ませて、人魚の赤い蝋燭が溶けて流れるように航海士にと滴りかかったのは、しかしこれが涙ではない。洟の、筋引いて伸びてキサラの鼻梁に付きそうになるのを朔屋、慌てて布切れを突き出して受ける。
source.english: As Kuro bent close and listened to Kisara's labored sleep, her red eyes promptly brimmed with tears. Something dripped toward the navigator like the mermaid's red candle melting and running—but it was not tears. A string of snot stretched almost to the bridge of Kisara's nose. Sakuya hastily thrust out a scrap of cloth and caught it.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Is Kisara-san……going to die?」
【Naomasa】 「……Don't say that, you're gonna make me cry.」
【Naomasa】 「Well, I don't think she's going to die, but……it seems like Shisamu's went off somewhere. And then, look, Kisara fell into a deep sleep.」
It was hardly necessary for Sakuya to explain, she'd probably heard most of the circumstances from someone else, and moreover, Kuro had known the twins for a lot longer than Sakuya had.

Leaning in close to look at Kisara lying there, as she listened to her laboured breathing, Kuro's red eyes quickly grew wet with a sheen of tears, dripping down on the mate like a mermaid's red candle melting and flowing away, but it wasn't actually tears falling. A thin strand of snot stretched long and thin, nearly sticking to the bridge of Kisara's nose when Sakuya hurriedly thrust a rag under it to catch it. (TN: The mermaid candle is a reference to "赤い蝋燭と人魚", known as "The Red Candles and the Mermaid" in English, written by Ogawa Mimei, a famous writer of fairy tales, in 1921.)

source.japanese: ついでにクロにちーんと洟[はな]をかませて拭いてやったけれど、白子はそれでもぐすぐすと愁眉のまま、何事かを懸命に考え込んでいるようだった。
source.english: He had Kuro blow her nose and wiped it for her. Still sniffling, the albino kept her troubled look, seemingly thinking very hard about something.

source.japanese: 息苦しい程の間に、クロの洟[はなみず]また垂れて長く伸びてきた、のをずるんと一息に、錨を一気に巻き上げるようなと朔屋が感心するくらいに啜[すす]り込んで、
source.english: During that almost suffocating pause, her nose ran again, a long strand. One great sniff drew it back, so like hauling up an anchor at once that Sakuya admired it.

target.text: While he was at it, he made Kuro blow her nose into the rag, then wiped it clean, but the albino continued to sniffle with her brows knit in worry, and she seemed to be intently brooding over something.

In a breathlessly tense moment, Kuro's snot dangled down and stretched long once again, and then she sucked it up in a single breath, like weighing the anchor in one hard heave, with a slurp so loud that Sakuya was left impressed.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そ、そんならあの、クロ手伝う。
　捜すから、手伝う。
　シサムさんどこ───捜すよ」
source.english:
“Th-then, um, Kuro'll help.
Look for her, help.
Where Sisam is—I'll look.”

source.japanese:
あくまで優しいので。
　日頃シサムとキサラからは相当にいい加減、というかぞんざい、という雑というか、手荒、というか、とにかく優しくは扱われていないクロであるのに優しい。朔屋に胸にしみじみと、情けという心根はこれかと迫った。
　不器用な回れ右で、早速通路に飛び出していこうとするクロの襟首を摘[つま]んで留めると、白子の駆け足宙を掻[か]いて、降ろしてやれば進んでないのがいかにも不思議と足下を覗きこむ、彼女の頭を撫でてやりながら、
source.english:
Kind, always.
Though Sisam and Kisara habitually treated her carelessly—roughly, crudely, harshly, anything but kindly—Kuro was kind. Sakuya felt it deeply. Was this the heart called compassion?
Turning awkwardly, she was already about to rush into the passage. He pinched her collar to stop her, and her running feet pawed the air. Set down, she looked at them, plainly puzzled that she had made no progress. Stroking her head, he said—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「有難うな。そん時にはお願いするよ。
　でも今はどうすりゃいいのか、考え中なんだ」
source.english:
“Thanks. I'll ask when it's time.
Right now I'm thinking what we should do.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Th-, then if that's how it is, Kuro will help. Will help, looking. Look for where───Shisamu is.」

Unfailingly kind. Normally, Shisamu and Kisara would treat Kuro pretty carelessly, or rather, off-handedly, or perhaps roughly, or maybe run roughshod over her, or else, regardless, Kuro wasn't treated kindly, and yet kind she was in turn. It struck Sakuya deep in his bosom, the realization dawning on him: Ah, so this is a truly compassionate heart of hearts.

He grabbed Kuro, who had clumsily spun on her heel and was about to leap into the passageway without delay, by the collar and held her in place, and as he did, the albino's running legs continued to wheel through the air; when he sat her down again, she stared down at her feet, finding it strange how she hadn't moved forwards at all, and while he gently stroked her head,
【Naomasa】 「Thank you kindly. I'll be sure to ask for your help when the time comes. But right now, I'm in the middle of figuring out what the right thing to do is.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……クロね。航海士のこと、おっかない思うけど、嫌いじゃない。ないですよ」
source.english: “…Kuro thinks the mates are scary. But doesn't hate them. Really doesn't.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Uhm, Kuro. Thinks the mates are scary, but doesn't dislike them. Really doesn't.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「シサムさん、キサラさん、ちょっとだけクロとおんなじ。クロは嵐が来ると、頭よい。航海士達は、離れると、ダメ、なる。
　だから、ええとおなじだから」
source.english:
“Sisam, Kisara, a little like Kuro. Kuro's clever when storms come. The mates, when they're apart, they're… no good.
So, um, the same.”

source.japanese: 一生懸命に考えに考えて、選んだ言葉でも伝えきれないもどかしさを眼差しに一杯に、訴えかけるクロ、舌足らずの船長クロ、案ずるなかれ、お前の心は朔屋に届いて彼の胸の扉の裡側で、想いを同じうさせた。
source.english: She thought and thought with all her might and chose her words, yet her eyes brimmed with the frustration of all they still failed to convey. Thus Kuro appealed to him—poor, tongue-tied Captain Kuro. Fear not: your heart reached Sakuya, and there, within the doors of his breast, made his feelings one with yours.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あるいは、俺らは、この船に乗ってるのは、みんなどっか同じなのかもな。
　だからか、俺がこうやってこの女の傍についてやってんのは」
source.english:
“…Maybe we're all alike in some way, everyone aboard this ship.
Maybe that's why I'm here beside this woman.”

source.japanese:
信天翁号───船乗りの中でも掃き溜め、無頼の奇人達の吹き溜まり、真っ当な船員達なら忌み嫌う最悪のオンボロ船。
　一癖も二癖もある乗り組み達は、皆それぞれに宿痾を抱えている。その病に傷、表立って舐め合うわけではないけれども。互いは互いに、あいつもくそったれだと。自分と同じ哀しきくそったれだと認め合っているのだろう。それ故に同じ船に寄り合っているだろう。
source.english:
The Albatross: the sailors' trash heap, a gathering place for outlaw eccentrics, the worst old wreck, loathed by decent sailors.
Its peculiar inhabitants each carried an old, abiding affliction. They did not openly lick one another's sicknesses and wounds. Yet perhaps each acknowledged: that one's a bastard too. A sad bastard, like me. Perhaps that was why they gathered on the same ship.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Shisamu-san, Kisara-san, just a little bit like Kuro. When a storm comes, Kuro becomes smart. When the mates are separated, they become useless. So, uhm, we're the same there, so.」

Thinking and thinking with all she had, her eyes brimming with the frustration of being unable to convey the feeling, even when so carefully choosing her words; pleading Kuro, lisping Captain Kuro, there was naught to be afeared of, for thine heart hath Sakuya reacheth, and beyond the door to his own, it stirred the self-same emotion.
【Naomasa】 「……Or perhaps, we, all of us who sail on this ship, are all the same in some way. And maybe that's why I'm here, staying by this woman's side.」

The Albatross───a garbage dump even amongst sailors, a hangout for knavish oddballs, a most despicable shabby ship that any respectable mariner would shun and abhor. The members of this eccentric crew each had their respective chronic condition they dragged with them. Although they certainly didn't make an open show of licking each other's wounds. Each of them thought the rest to be real pieces of shit. They had probably all come to recognize the same wretched piece of shit in each other. That was likely the reason they'd all gathered on the same ship.

source.japanese: 朔屋は合縁奇縁を想うた。自分の駄目さ加減など、この歳になれば百も千も承知している彼であるが、この船にいて刺激されるのはただ劣等感ばかりではない。奇妙な同類意識がある。朔屋は近頃、思えばこれまで脱走の機会は幾らでもあったのに、なぜそれを見逃してきたのだろうと考える事がある。
source.english: Sakuya thought of the strange affinities that fate contrived. By now he understood his own worthlessness a hundred, a thousand times over. Yet the Albatross stirred in him more than inferiority. It gave him an odd sense of kinship. Lately he sometimes wondered why, when he had enjoyed so many chances to escape, he had let every one pass.

source.japanese:
答えは単純だ。既に信天翁号は青年にとってわざわざ脱走を企てるような場では無くなっているからである。
　シサムもキサラも、こうして見舞いに来ているクロも、そして水夫長や機関長、下級水夫達。既に青年の景色の一つとなっているのである。
source.english:
The answer was simple. The Albatross was no longer a place he felt any need to plot an escape from.
Sisam and Kisara, Kuro here on her visit, the boatswain and chief engineer, the junior sailors: all had become part of the scenery of his life.

target.text: Sakuya thought it a strange relationship of incompatible personalities formed through quirks of fate. At his age, he knew a thousand times over just how much of a failure he was, but being on this ship stirred more within him than just his inferiority complex. There was a peculiar sense of kinship. Lately, Sakuya had found himself wondering. Thinking back, there had been plenty of chances for him to make his escape by now, so for what reason had he let them all pass him by?

The answer was simple. For the young man, the Albatross had long ceased to be a place worth plotting an escape from. There was Shisamu and Kisara, as well as Kuro, who had come to pay a visit out of concern like this, and then there was the Bosun and the Chief Engineer, and all the deck boys, too. They had already become part of the scenery that made up the young man's world.

source.japanese: 昏々と熱の眠りに眠り続けるキサラの額におずおず手を伸ばしては、青年にいいかどうか訊ねるような目を向けてくるのに頷[うなず]いてやると、ようやく額に小さな白い手をそろそろと被せて、熱さにたじろいだように手を引っ込めるクロ。またそろそろと伸ばして、額の汗に張り付く髪を指先で流してやったりしているクロ。同じ船に乗り合わせる者を案ずる心を見せるクロ。小さなクロ、愚かなクロ、けれど優しき、愛すべきクロ。
source.english: Kuro timidly reached for the brow of Kisara, sunk in fevered sleep, then looked to Sakuya as though asking permission. When he nodded, she laid one small white hand gingerly across Kisara's forehead, only to flinch from the heat and snatch it back.
