Then she ventured near again, brushing away with her fingertips the hair pasted there by sweat. Kuro, showing concern for another soul aboard the same ship. Little Kuro, foolish Kuro, and yet kind Kuro, lovable Kuro.

source.japanese:
朔屋は肩に圧迫感めいたものがのしかかっていた事に今更ながらに思い当たったのは、クロの仕草にその重みの幾分かが減じたからである。もちろん完全に消え去ったわけではない。それは朔屋と航海士達がこれまで経てきた時間がある以上消えるものではないし、消し去ると言う事は解放ではなく喪失なのだとも理解している。
　だから朔屋は、クロのやろうとしていた事は自分の役目なのだと信じた。
　双子を捜しに行くのは、自分なのだと。
source.english:
Only when Kuro's gesture lightened some part of it did Sakuya realize that a crushing weight had been bearing on his shoulders. It had not disappeared completely, of course. Nor could it: not after all the time he and the navigators had shared. And he understood that to erase it would be not liberation but loss.
And so Sakuya became certain that what Kuro had tried to do was his responsibility.
He was the one who must go in search of the missing twin.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───クロ。船は今、大変なんだ、知ってるだろ？　手はいくらあっても足りないって思う。みんなのところへ行ってくれ。手伝う事はいくらでもあるから」
source.english: “—Kuro. The ship's in trouble now, you know that, right? We need every hand we can get. Go to the others. Plenty you can do to help.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺はここで、キサラを見てるから」
source.english: “I'll stay here and look after Kisara.”

target.text: A trembling hand timidly reached for Kisara's forehead, the woman still in a deep, feverish slumber, and an inquiring look was turned towards the young man as if asking if it was okay; when he gave a nod of approval in return, finally, Kuro gently covered her brow with a small, white hand before pulling it back as if recoiling from the heat. Once more, Kuro gingerly reached out her hand, using her fingertips to comb through the hair sticking to her sweaty brow. Kuro, whose heart was full of concern for those she shared a ship with. Tiny Kuro, stupid Kuro, but kind, lovable Kuro.

Realization struck Sakuya, belated though it was, that there had been something like a heavy pressure weighing down on his shoulders, and it only did because Kuro's gesture had lightened part of that burden. Of course, it hadn't completely vanished. It was something that couldn't be erased, given everything Sakuya and the mates had been through together, and he understood that, were it to vanish, it would be a loss, not liberation. For that reason, Sakuya believed that what Kuro had been trying to do was his responsibility to see through. That setting off in search of the missing twin was his role to play.

【Naomasa】 「───Kuro. I'm sure you know that, right now, our ship is in big trouble, yeah? I don't think they can have too many hands. Go to where all the others are. There should be plenty of things that you can help with.」
【Naomasa】 「I'll stay here, keeping an eye on Kisara.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うん……」
source.english: “Okay…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Okay……」

source.japanese: 皆のところへ参じようとして、なおも不安げに振り返るクロへ、朔屋に不意にこみ上げてきたのはなんだったろう。愛しさか、共感か、物哀しさか、それらが混じり合ったものか。こらえきれずにクロの前に膝をつき、思いの限りを込めて抱きしめる───
source.english: As Kuro set off toward the others, still glancing anxiously back, what was it that suddenly welled up in Sakuya? Tenderness? Fellow feeling? Melancholy? Some mingling of all three? Unable to contain himself, he dropped to one knee before her and embraced her with all the feeling in him—

target.text: About to head over to join the others, when Kuro still couldn't help but anxiously glance back at him over her shoulder, what was it, exactly, that suddenly welled up inside Sakuya? Was it affection, empathy, melancholy, or perhaps a mixture of it all? Unable to keep it bottled up within him, he fell to his knees in front of Kuro, embracing her, pouring all his heart into squeezing her tight───

source.japanese:
どれだけそうしていたのか判らない。
　ただ、気づいた時にはクロは、白目を剥いてくったり弛緩の、ぷくぷく鳴っているのは唇の端から湧く小さな泡の。そう言えば寸前までもがいていたような、何事か呻[うめ]いていたようなだが、感無量の余り聞こえなかった朔屋である。
source.english:
He had no idea how long he stayed that way.
Only when at last he noticed did he see Kuro hanging limp, eyes rolled back, tiny bubbles burbling at the corner of her mouth. Come to think of it, she had been struggling until moments ago, perhaps trying to groan something; overcome with feeling, Sakuya had heard none of it.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……やっべやりすぎた……。
　てかやりづらいなあもう！」
source.english:
“…Shit. Overdid it…
God, you're hard to handle!”

source.japanese: 始末に困って朔屋は───
source.english: Not knowing what to do with her, Sakuya—

target.text: While holding her so, he lost track of time. However, by the time he snapped out of it, Kuro had gone entirely limp, eyes rolled back into her head, a soft bubbling sound coming from the tiny foam welling at the corner of her lips. Come to think of it, it did feel like she had been squirming and struggling just a moment ago, groaning or moaning about something or other, but Sakuya had been so overwhelmed with deep emotion that none of it had entered his ears.
【Naomasa】 「……Damn, I went too far……. Come on, this is such a pain to deal with!」
At a loss on how to handle this, Sakuya───

source.japanese:
担ぎ出して、戻ってきた肩に白子は無く、彼がクロを彼女の船室まで送り届けてやっていればいいのだが、それにしては帰りが早い。さすがにこの寒気に火の気のない船内通路に放置はしてきてはいないようだが───双子の部屋からは一番近い、日頃人が起居しているのは水夫長の部屋なのだが……。
　ともあれ、戻ってきて見れば、空けたのは僅かな間だったにもかかわらず、キサラは夜具を寝乱してひくりひくりと魘[うな]されてあった。
source.english:
He carried her out and returned without the albino on his shoulder. One would like to think he had delivered her to her own cabin, though he was back rather quickly for that. At least he did not seem to have abandoned her in one of the unheated passages—but the nearest regularly occupied cabin to the twins' was the boatswain's…
In any event, though he had been gone only a moment, Sakuya returned to find Kisara thrashing the bedding and twitching in the grip of a nightmare.

target.text: Slung her over his shoulder and carried her out, and when he returned, there was no albino to be seen; ideally, he would just have carried Kuro back to her own cabin, but for that to have been the case, he returned awfully quick. It seemed like he hadn't gone so far as to abandon her in the unheated passageways in this bitter cold, but───the cabin closest to the twins' that someone actually lived in day-to-day was the Bosun's, but……. In any case, when he returned, it was to find that, despite only having left the room for but a brief time, Kisara was tangled up in her bedding, twitching and jerking while she whimpered in her sleep.

source.english:
“…Uh… Mm…
Let me… out…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……U……nh……. Let……out.」

source.japanese: はい、と素直にズボンを脱ぎにかかって、何を出すつもりだったのか、朔屋は我に返って気まずくまた引き上げてから、なおも譫言が続くのに、キサラの枕元に跪[ひざま]いて耳を寄せる───熱に饐[す]えたような息遣いも苦しげなら、言葉も苦悶に満ちていた。
source.english: Yes, he obediently began lowering his trousers—what had he intended to let out? Recovering himself, Sakuya awkwardly pulled them up again. Her muttering continued. He knelt by the pillow and listened. Her breath seemed soured by fever, labored; the words, too, were full of torment.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたし達……違わない……。
　だから……閉じこめるの……いや……」
source.english:
“We're… not different…
So… hate… being shut away…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「キサラ……？
　閉じこめるってお前……お前も、その、なんか、クロと同じだったのか？」
source.english:
“Kisara…?
Shut you in? Were you, um, like Kuro too?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なんなんだろうなあ。この変な重なりは」
source.english: “…What is it with all these strange parallels?”

source.japanese: ……まるで何者かがどこかしら似たり寄ったりな者達を掻[か]き集めたようではないか。気の毒に思いながらもどうすることもできないと煩悶するうちに、朔屋もキサラの側に座り込んだまま、何時しか睡魔に捕まった。
source.english: …It was almost as though someone had scoured the world for people who, in one way or another, resembled one another. As he worried over her with pity, powerless to help, Sakuya too succumbed to drowsiness and fell asleep sitting beside Kisara.

target.text: With a "yes ma'am!", he obediently began to drop his pants; one could only wonder what exactly he could have been intending to let out here, but Sakuya came to his senses and awkwardly pulled them back up, and as her delirious mumbling continued, he knelt down by Kisara's pillow and leaned his ear close───if her breathing, laboured and stale with fever, seemed pained, her words were no less steeped in anguish.
【Kisara】 「We aren't……different……. So……don't want…… to be locked away……」
【Naomasa】 「Kisara……? When you say locked up, are you…… are you also, you know, kind of the same as Kuro?」
【Naomasa】 「……I wonder what it could mean. This strange overlap.」

……Wasn't it almost as if somebody had deliberately scraped together a group of people who, in some way, very closely resembled each other? While tormented by the fact that, though he felt very sorry for her, there was nothing he could do about it, Sakuya remained sitting by Kisara's side, and before he knew it, sleep overcame him.

source.japanese: ───そして朔屋がたまらない焦燥感にかられて飛び起きたのが深更、キサラの部屋まで来て何をやっているのだ自分は、迂闊に寝こけているなど下の下、もっとやるべき事があるはず、と焦りに焦って彼女たちが衣装を納めてある櫃[チェスト]に飛びつく。ただ一体双子の衣装櫃に朔屋が何をするつもりだったのかは明らかにならず、朔屋自身もはっきりとは判っていなかったであろう、寝ぼけて胡乱な目はキサラの寝台に激しく動揺して眠気を払い落とした。
source.english: —It was the dead of night when Sakuya sprang awake, seized by unbearable impatience. What was he doing in Kisara's room? Sleeping carelessly like this was beneath contempt; surely there was something more he ought to be doing. More and more frantic, he flung himself upon the chest that held the twins' clothes. What precisely Sakuya intended to do to their clothes chest was never revealed, and probably not clear even to him. Then his bleary, sleep-fogged eyes swung toward Kisara's bed. The sight jolted him fully awake.

source.japanese:
寝台にあるべき筈の姿がない───
　今度は寝台に、衣装櫃から猿のように飛びついては彼女の体なりにくぼんだ寝台を改めたが、息一杯に吸いこんだキサラの残り香があるだけ。それが目的だったのかも。夜具は既に棺桶並みに冷えてあり、キサラが一体どれくらい前に目覚めて床を離れたのか判らない。
source.english:
The figure that should have been there was gone.
He sprang like a monkey from chest to bed and searched the depression her body had left. Only her lingering scent, which he inhaled deeply. Perhaps that had been his purpose. The bedding was already cold as a coffin. No knowing how long ago Kisara had woken and risen.

source.japanese: とにかく朔屋は船室を飛び出した。今のキサラを放置しては置けない。目覚めた時の焦燥感よりまだひどい焦りにかられて部屋を出る。前にもう一度衣装櫃へ向けた視線のしつこく未練がましく、一体何を企んでいたのやら。
source.english: In any case, he rushed out. He could not leave Kisara alone in her present state. More frantic than even his waking impatience had made him, he left the room. But not before casting a lingering, regretful glance at the clothes chest once more. What on earth had he been planning?

target.text: ───Thus, when Sakuya once more leapt to his feet, driven by an unbearably gnawing restlessness, it was the dead of night; he wondered what the hell he thought he was doing, coming all the way to Kisara's cabin and then just letting himself carelessly fall asleep; he was the worst of the worst, there had to be something else he should be doing, so he thought as he burned up with frustration, then leapt at the chest where the girls kept their clothes.

While it wasn't clear what in the world it was Sakuya exactly intended to do with the twins' clothes chest, that probably wasn't entirely clear to the man himself either; his groggy, unfocused eyes landed on Kisara's bed, and the intense shock he received shook off any of his lingering drowsiness.

The figure that should have been in the bed was not there─── This time, he leapt onto the bed from the chest like a monkey, closely examining the indentation left by her body, but as he inhaled like his life depended on it, all that was left was the lingering fragrance of Kisara. That might have been his actual objective. The bedding was already cold as a casket, and he couldn't tell just how long it had been since Kisara had awoken and left her bed.

At any rate, Sakuya flew out of the cabin. He couldn't just leave Kisara unattended as she was right now. Spurred on by an even more restless anxiety than when he awoke, he left the room. Before he did so, he turned his eyes to the clothes chest one final time, his gaze thick with lingering attachment; truly, what could this man have been scheming?

source.japanese: また上甲板に上がってきたのは、何か考えがあったわけではなく、船内通路を走り回るうちに目についた昇降段を勢いのままに駆け上がってしまっただけの事、この朔屋、車を運転させれば、おそらく意味のない右折を繰り返して道に迷う型の人間である。さておき、このたびは偶然が味方したのか、キサラは上甲板に在った。
source.english: He returned to the upper deck not from any plan, but because, running about the passages, he saw a stairway and let his momentum carry him up. Given a car to drive, Sakuya would probably keep making meaningless right turns until lost. Let that pass. This time chance favored him: Kisara was on the upper deck.

source.japanese:
ああ、在ったとも。
　信天翁号にもう一艘[そう]残された、救命艇の傍らに。下級水夫君の一人に馬乗りになって。もしもし亀よ、の拍子で両の鉄槌（握拳の下側、小指の面）を代わる代わるリズミカルに振り下ろして。鉄槌が叩きつけられる度に哀れな下級水夫君の両足がびくんびくんと跳ね上がるのは、既に痙攣的な反射なのだった。
source.english:
Oh, she was there.
Beside the one lifeboat left aboard the Albatross. Astride a junior sailor. To the rhythm of the children's song ‘Hello, Mr. Turtle,’ she brought down her two hammer fists—the little-finger edge of each clenched hand—in steady alternation. With every blow the poor junior sailor's legs flew up in a jerk. By then it was nothing more than convulsive reflex.

target.text: That he'd gone up to the upper deck once again was not because he had any particular plan in mind, it was simply because he'd impulsively dashed up a ladder that he'd happened to catch sight of while running through the onboard passageways; this man, Sakuya, were he to drive a car, he'd in all likelihood be the type of person who would repeatedly take pointless right turns and end up getting lost. That digression aside, on this occasion, coincidence was on his side, for Kisara was on the upper deck.

Indeed, she certainly was. Right next to the only other lifeboat that still remained on the Albatross. Straddling a single deck boy. Swinging down alternating hammer fists (the bottom pinky side of her clenched fists) to the rhythm of "Moshi Moshi Kame Yo". Every time he was struck by her iron hammers, the pitiful deck boy's legs would twitch and jerk upwards, already nothing but a convulsive reflex. (TN: "Moshi Moshi Kame Yo" is from the lyrics of the children's song "うさぎとかめ", lit. "The Hare and the Tortoise", which consists almost entirely of dotted eighth-sixteenth note figures.)

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なにやってんだキサラっ」
source.english: “What are you doing, Kisara!”

source.japanese:
あまりの無残に怒鳴りつけた朔屋に肩越しにねじ向けた首などは、ぎりぎりと怖ろしく軋んだし、その挙動自体が、悪魔が憑依した身体を無理矢理に使っているようなおぞましさが満ちたし、横顔など闇より濃い陰が塗り潰しているにもかかわらず両眼が円く赤く昏い光が据わっているでないか。
　その横顔に裂け目が走ったかと見えたは、唇が開いたのだったが、そこからごはぁぁと噴出された白い蒸気の中に朔屋は、間違いなく炎が混じっていたと思った。
source.english:
Sakuya shouted at the brutality. Kisara's neck ground around over her shoulder with a dreadful creak. The movement had the horror of a devil forcing its borrowed body to obey. Darkness deeper than night obliterated her profile, yet within it both eyes shone round and red, fixed with a murky light.
A fissure seemed to split her face—her lips opening. From it burst a great gout of white vapor, and Sakuya could have sworn there was flame mixed in.

source.japanese: 朔屋は臆病者の当然の権利を行使して、腰を抜かしたわけだが、その恐怖に怯えた顔があまりにも醜く歪んでいたのか、キサラもやや正気を取り戻したようだ、顔から陰が去って目鼻立ちが戻って。
source.english: He exercised a coward's inalienable right: his legs gave way beneath him. Perhaps terror had twisted his face into such hideousness that even Kisara recovered some measure of sanity. The shadow withdrew; her features reappeared.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「What the hell are you doing, Kisara?!」

When she twisted her neck over her shoulder at Sakuya, who had yelled at her so pitifully, it produced a most terrifying grating, and the way it moved was brimming with the ghastliness of a devil possessing a human's body and forcing it to do his dark bidding, and despite how shadows denser than darkness itself had painted over her profile, was there not a round, red, murky glow fixed in both her eyes? What appeared to be a fissure splitting her profile open was actually her lips parting, yet within the plume of white steam that spewed forth with a wet, guttural "gwaaaaah", Sakuya was convinced he saw flames mixed inside.

Sakuya exercised the god-given right of the cowardly: his knees buckled under him, but perhaps the way his face twisted into a grimace of fear from witnessing this horror right before him was just that ugly a sight, for Kisara also seemed to regain some of her sanity, the shadows retreating from her face, her features returning to her.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋の言った通りのコトだよっ。
　誰かに頼んでもなんもしてくれない。
　頼んでる暇があったら、
　何をしてでもって！」
source.english:
“What you told me!
Ask people and nobody does a thing.
If I've got time to ask,
do whatever it takes!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I'm doing just as you told me to, Sakuya. Nobody will do anything for me if I beg them. So if I've got time to beg for help, then I should just use it to do whatever it damn well takes!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だからそうする、そうするだけっ。
　あんたも邪魔するってんならぁ……」
source.english:
“So I'll do that. That's all.
And if you're going to get in my way…”

source.japanese: また顔が陰にどんよりと隠れかかる、下級水夫からゆらりと立ち上がるも、その骨格がどこやら前時代の爬虫類じみて歪[いびつ]に見える、くらいにはキサラはまだ正気を失っていた。前身に持ち上げた手は構えもなにもなかったけれど、ぎゃんと反って鉤爪に、見ているだけで心が痛くなりそうに尖ってある。
source.english: Shadow began to thicken over her face again. She rose unsteadily from the junior sailor, her frame looking somehow warped, like that of a prehistoric reptile: such was the depth of Kisara's continuing delirium. The hand she raised before her assumed no proper guard; it merely bent back into a claw, so sharply pointed that the sight alone seemed to prick the heart.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわあ、さっきまで高熱だったのが完全復活してるよこの女」
source.english: “Whoa. This woman had a high fever a moment ago and now she's completely recovered.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「いや、まだ結構熱っぽい。
　だからさぁ、体が利かないからさあ、
　手加減とかできないと思うんだよね朔屋」
source.english:
“No, still pretty feverish.
Body won't do what I want.
Don't think I can hold back, Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「So that's what I'm doing, that's all this is. If you're also here to get in my way, then……」

Once again, her face began to obscure beneath a veil of gloomy shadow, and the way she swayed as she slowly rose to her feet from the deck boy made something in her skeletal frame look twisted in a manner reminiscent of prehistoric reptiles, such was the extent to which Kisara had lost her senses. The hand raised before her body was set in no particular stance or form, it arched violently into the shape of a talon, twisted into something so sharp that just looking at it made his heart ache.
【Naomasa】 「Woah, did you already fully recover from a fever that high, woman?」
【Kisara】 「No, I'm still pretty feverish. And that's why, because my body isn't mine to fully command, that I don't think I'll be able to pull my punches here, Sakuya.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「みんな熱のせいだから。あんたを叩きのめしてもそれは熱のせいなのよー。
　別にあの時怒鳴られた事、
　怨んでなんかいないのあたし」
source.english:
“It's all the fever. If I beat you flat, that's the fever too.
Not like I resent you
shouting at me earlier.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It's all this fever's fault. So even if I beat you into a pulp, that's also the fever to blame, see. It's not like you yelling at me earlier is something I bear a grudge against you for or anything!」

source.japanese:
じりじりと間合いを詰めるキサラの中で内圧が膨れあがりつつあって、これが解放された時には朔屋は、『朔屋だったモノ』になりはてる事だろう。いや、朔屋だったモノ、と見分けも付かないかも知れない。
　朔屋、腰を抜かしていたが、それでも必死に後ろ手に突いていた手を前に引き戻し、上半身を前に二つ折りにして、
source.english:
Pressure swelled inside Kisara as she closed the distance inch by inch. Once it broke loose, Sakuya would be reduced to ‘what had once been Sakuya’—if enough remained to identify as even that. His legs had given way,
but he desperately brought forward the hands braced behind him and folded his upper body down.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「偉そうに語ってすんませんっした！
　この朔屋、キサラさんにどこまでもついていくっす！」
source.english:
“Sorry I talked so big!
This humble Sakuya will follow Miss Kisara wherever she goes!”

source.japanese:
本日二度目の土下座だった。
　朔屋にとってはなにというほどもない行為である。頻繁な時などは、一日の間で、債鬼に、母方の伯父に、美人局の強面の破落戸に、路地裏の野良犬に、赤提灯のママに、と五度はやってのけた事がある。
source.english:
His second prostration of the day.
Nothing remarkable for Sakuya. On a busy day he had managed five: before a debt collector, his maternal uncle, the hard-faced thug behind a honey trap, a stray dog in an alley, and the proprietress of a red-lantern bar.

target.text: The internal pressure within Kisara continued to swell as she slowly but steadily closed the gap between them, and by the time that was unleashed, Sakuya would surely be reduced to 『The Thing That Once Was Sakuya』. Nay, perhaps what was left could not even amount to something that could be distinguished as The Thing That Once Was Sakuya. Though Sakuya's legs had given out beneath him, nevertheless, with desperate effort, he scrambled to bring forwards the hands he was using to prop himself up from behind, doubled his torso over at the waist,
【Naomasa】 「SORRY FOR ACTING SO HIGH AND MIGHTY! I, humble Sakuya, shall follow you to the end of the world, Kisara-san!」

The second dogeza of the day. For Sakuya, it was but a trivial act not even worth mentioning. When he frequently applied it, over the course of a single day, he would prostrate himself before the bill collector, his uncle on his mother's side, the thug with the intimidating face behind the badger game, the stray dog in the back alley, and the mama of the akachouchin; he would sometimes manage to pull it off five whole times. (TN: Akachouchin, written "赤提灯", lit. "red paper lantern", is a term that evolved from restaurants having red paper lanterns hanging outside, now slang for a cheap place to get some food and drink, like an izakaya. Mama is a term for the proprietress.)

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんた達がなに言おうとさ、生きてんの、シサムは。だってわかるんだからしょうがない。だったら捜しに行くだけ」
source.english: “Whatever you people say, Sisam's alive. I know it, that's all. So I'll go look.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はいっ、なんかシサムは、救命ボートと一緒に墜ちてったくさいです。だからもしかしたら、ほんとに生きてるかも」
source.english: “Yes! Sounds like Sisam went over with the lifeboat. So she really might be alive.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「No matter what you people say, Shisamu's still alive. I mean, I know she is, so what else can I do? All I can do is go look for her!」
【Naomasa】 「Right, it looks like Shisamu fell down together with the lifeboat or something. So maybe it's possible that she really is alive.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ていうかもう引っこみがつかないでしょこれ。わりと本気で水夫君達殴り倒しちゃったし、水夫長とはこの後すっげえきまずいだろうし」
source.english:
“Anyway, there's no backing out now, is there?
I beat up those junior sailors pretty badly, and things with the Boatswain are going to be incredibly awkward after this.”

source.japanese: と甲板に伏して、今なお全身をぴくんぴくんと痙攣させている下級水夫君に気の毒そうな視線を送ったが、下手人がそのような殊勝な顔したところで説得力にまるで欠ける。大体それで『わりと』の本気なら、本気の本気の場合は一体彼はどうなっていたというのだ。北海の夜に新たな妖怪出現の伝説でも付け加えていたかも知れないとでもいうのか。
source.english: She cast a pitying look at the junior sailor sprawled on the deck, his whole body still twitching. Such contrition was wholly unconvincing on the culprit's face. And if that was merely ‘pretty’ serious, what would have become of him had she been serious in earnest? Would the night over the northern seas have gained a new legend of some monster's appearance?

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Or more like, there's no backing down for me anymore now, right? I ended up knocking the sailors here out in a fairly serious way, and it'll be incredibly awkward to deal with the Bosun after this.」

Having said as much, she sent what seemed to be a look full of pity at the deck boy who was collapsed face-down on the deck, his body still twitching and convulsing even now, but when the perpetrator was the one who showed an expression full of such virtuous repentance, it was utterly unconvincing. To begin with, if that was her being "fairly" serious, then what the hell would have happened to the boy had she been dead serious? Could it be that she might have birthed another legend of a monster haunting the northern seas at night?

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「正直ね、今は気が張ってるから立ってられるけど、それが切れたらどうなるか判らない。
　でも、動けるから。今なら」
source.english:
“Honestly, I'm only on my feet because I'm so keyed up. I don't know what'll happen when that wears off.
But I can move. For now.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「To be honest with you, right now, I'm only still standing because I'm so on edge, but once that wears off, I have no idea what'll happen to me. But, I can still act. For now.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だから邪魔しないで、朔屋。
　あんたの事はわりと気に入ってるからさ、
　あたしもシサムも。
　そういう相手とは───」
source.english:
“So don't get in my way, Sakuya.
Sisam and I are pretty fond of you.
And someone we feel that way about—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「邪魔なんかしないし、
　ついていっちゃダメなのか？」
source.english:
“I'm not getting in your way.
Can't I come along?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「So please don't get in my way, Sakuya. I'm actually pretty fond of you, me and Shisamu both, so. I don't want to fight someone like───」
【Naomasa】 「I'm not getting in your way at all, can't I just come with you?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あれ？　なんか、あれ？」
source.english: “Huh? Wait, huh?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うん。なに言ってンのさっきから、キサラ。
　やっぱ熱、相当まずいんじゃないかそれ。
　俺が、ついていくって言ってたの、
　わかるか」
source.english:
“Yeah. What've you been talking about, Kisara?
That fever really is bad, isn't it?
I said I'd go with you.
Understand?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Huh? What are you───huh?」
【Naomasa】 「Yeah. What have you even been going on about, Kisara? Your fever must be pretty bad, huh. Like I said, I want to come with you, do you follow?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「───よし。行こう。
　あんたが役に立つかどうかの見せ所だよ」
source.english:
“—Right. Let's go.
Time to show whether you're any use.”

source.japanese:
ようやく戻ってきたキサラの顔だった。
　もちろん片割れと引き離された故の惑乱は抜けきってはいない。
　それでも朔屋が彼女にはかくあれかしと望んだ、荒海に昂然と挑む顔だった。
　夜の中で素敵に引き締まっていた。
source.english:
At last Kisara's own face had returned.
The frenzy born of separation from her other half had not entirely left her, of course.
Even so, this was the face Sakuya had wished to see upon her: the face that proudly challenged a raging sea. It looked magnificent, set firm against the night.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「何事もなかったように話を戻したよな」
source.english: “You just went straight back to talking as though none of that happened.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「───Alright. Let's go. Here's your chance to prove that you're actually good for something.」

At long last, Kisara's expression returned to her. Of course, the turmoil born from her other half missing hadn't fully left her. But even so, it was that very expression Sakuya had longed for her to bear, the face of a woman proud and unyielding as she challenged the raging seas. Strikingly sharp and resolute in the darkness of the night.
【Naomasa】 「Just changed the subject like nothing ever happened, huh?」

source.japanese:
夜気は夜更けてより強く、服の上から刺してくるようであったし、先行きなどはまるで見えない、なのに朔屋が腰を抜かした状態から自ら立ち直り、冗談めかした台詞さえ吐いたのは、豪く嬉しかったから。
　先ほど自分はこのキサラに、双子に何を言わせた？
source.english:
The night air sharpened as the hours wore on, piercing through his clothes, and he could see nothing at all of what lay ahead. Yet Sakuya rose under his own power from where his legs had failed him and even managed a joking remark, for he was overjoyed.
What had he just made Kisara—made the twins—say?

source.japanese:
【直正】
（うふふふふふ、この二人が、割と気に入ってるってさ、俺の事───）
source.english: (Hee hee hee hee… Those two said they like me pretty well—)

source.japanese: 朔屋を動かして、彼に諸々の縁とか柵[しがらみ]の類を捨てさせるにはそれで充分。後からえらく悔やむだろうが、この青年の、その時はそれで充分いやそれ以上。早速にキサラに手を貸す、救命艇を降ろす準備に取りかかる、と。
source.english: That was enough to move Sakuya, enough to make him cast off all manner of bonds and obligations. Later he would regret it bitterly, but for this young man, at this moment, it was enough—more than enough. He promptly lent Kisara a hand and began preparing to lower the lifeboat. And then—

target.text: The chill only grew stronger as the night advanced, like icy needles stabbed into their skin through even layers of clothing, and there was no telling what lay ahead of them; that Sakuya could nevertheless pull himself together all on his own after collapsing in terror, could even make a joking remark, was because he was incredibly happy. What had he made Kisara, the twins, admit to him just now?
【Naomasa】 （Uhuhuhuhuhu, these two, she said, they're pretty fond of me───）

To set Sakuya into motion, to make him cast off every bond and obligation that tied him down to this place, that was plenty. Later, he would probably come to regret it tremendously, but right now, it was enough for this young man, nay, it was more than just that. He quickly went to give Kisara a hand and began preparing to lower the lifeboat, and then.

source.japanese:
救命艇の舷側より、ひょこと出てきたのが、夜を集めて夜よりも艶[つや]やかに黒い髪の、寒気がその流れの中に宿る光の輪を更に清[さや]かに磨き上げていた。端麗な眼差しも同じ色合いの。
　と、このように、見た目だけなら、朔屋ですら脱がせたいかとか抱きたいと願うより先に凝然とその美に感銘して言葉に詰まるくらいの美少女なのだが。
source.english:
Up over the lifeboat’s gunwale popped a girl whose hair seemed to have gathered the night into itself, blacker and more lustrous than night; the cold had burnished still brighter the halo dwelling in its flowing strands. Her exquisite eyes shared the same darkness.
Thus, on looks alone, she was so beautiful that even Sakuya would be struck dumb by the sight before the desire to strip or bed her could so much as arise. But—

target.text: From the side of the lifeboat, peeking out over the gunwale, was hair like gathered night, a glossy and deeper black than the dark of night itself, and the crisp chill honed the halo of light nestled within those flowing strands to an even purer, crystal-clear brilliance. Her striking, refined gaze shared that very same shade. Like so, judging from but her appearance alone, she was a young woman so beautiful it would leave even Sakuya frozen in place before he could even think to beg for her to strip naked or make love to him, so deeply moved by her beauty that he would be left at a loss for words, but.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「その、なんていうか……今晩は。
　空気がとっても澄んで素敵な夜ね」
source.english:
“Well, um… Good evening.
Such a lovely night, the air so clear.”

source.japanese:
出てくる状況が状況の、そしてその見え透く白々しさが、見た目の麗質を残念に破壊する。名匠の精魂傾けた女神像でも、沢庵漬けの重しにしては台無しである。
　よっこらしょと支柱に索留されてあった救命艇から降りるにも黒蜜の流れがさんざめいて、星のない夜なのに、そこだけに銀河を切り取って、宿して、歩み去っていこうとする、肩にキサラの手がにゅういと伸びてがしりと食いこんだ。
source.english:
Given where and how she had appeared, the transparent effrontery of that pretense unfortunately demolished the beauty of her appearance. Even a goddess into whom a master sculptor had poured his soul would be wasted as a weight on a crock of pickled radish.
She clambered down from the lifeboat lashed to the davits, her black-honey hair rippling and glittering. Though the night was starless, in that flowing length alone a strip of the galaxy seemed to have been cut out and caught. She made to walk away. Kisara's hand snaked onto her shoulder and clamped down.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So, uhm, how do I put this…… good evening. The air is so clear, what a beautiful night, am I right?」

The nature of the situation, together with such transparent pretense, unfortunately spoiled her otherwise noble beauty. Even a goddess statue that a master artisan poured his heart and soul into crafting would be utterly wasted if used as a weight to press pickled radishes with. Even when she jumped down from the lifeboat still fastened to the arms with a "hup!", the flow of dark syrup cascaded in vibrantly shimmering ripples; though the night was starless, it alone had carved out a pocket of the galaxy and harboured it within its locks, and she made to walk away, but Kisara's hand slid out towards her shoulder in an eerily smooth motion, then dug in hard.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんたも聞いてたのかぁ…………」
source.english: “You heard us too…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「So you were also listening in……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「判った、あたしらを船の連中に売るつもりだな」
source.english: “Got it. Going to sell us out to the crew.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「や、こいつがそんな事したって意味がないだろう」
source.english: “No, what good would that do her?”

source.japanese: 朔屋が口を出したのは、庇うつもりもないではなかったけれど、それよりも時間が惜しかった、ここで時を空費していては、何時、誰が上がってくるか知れたものではない。
source.english: Sakuya spoke partly to defend her, but more because time was precious. Waste it here and anyone might come up, at any moment.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I get it. You plan on selling us out to the rest of the crew.」
【Naomasa】 「No, even should she do something like that, I don't really think she'll get anything out of it.」

Though it wasn't that he had no intention of protecting her at all, the reason Sakuya spoke up was, most of all, because time was precious, and if they wasted time here, it was possible that, soon enough, somebody might come up on deck.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そうよ、その通り。
　だからほら、私は引っこむから。
　なにも見たり聞いたりしなかった」
source.english:
“Exactly, that's right.
So I'll go away.
Never saw or heard anything.”

source.japanese: そして密航者の言葉にもこの際嘘偽りを含ませる余裕は無かったろうの、なにしろ今のキサラはこの黒髪の娘に増して余裕がなく、余裕がないこの手の女は何をしでかすか判らない、いや、ある意味ではわかりやすい。果断にして容赦なき挙しか選択肢が無くなるのだという。
source.english: Nor, surely, had the stowaway any room for deception just then. Kisara had even less composure than the dark-haired girl, and there was no telling what a woman of this sort might do when pressed. Or rather, in one sense she was utterly predictable: decisiveness and mercilessness became the only choices left to her.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「That's right, what he said. So, look, I'm staying out of all this. I didn't hear or see nothing.」

And then, while the stowaway probably didn't have the presence of mind to utter any lies or falsehoods at this juncture, right now, Kisara had even less composure to spare than this black-haired girl, and when this kind of woman lost her calm, it was impossible to say what she'd end up being guilty of; no, in a certain sense, it was actually quite easy. All options but decisive, merciless action would be swept off the table.

source.japanese:
果たして───今夜の信天翁号の上甲板は色々の音を聞いたろう。キサラとシサムの何かを期して語らう声や、朔屋が反吐する醜い音、土下座に額打ち付けられる音もあったろうし、いつも通り船体が軋む音もいったろう。
　そして次に軋んだ音に、久しぶりと苦笑したかも知れない。
source.english:
Indeed—the Albatross’s upper deck had heard all manner of sounds that night: the voices of Kisara and Sisam conferring with some purpose in mind; Sakuya’s hideous retching; the thump, too, of a forehead striking the planks in prostration; and, as ever, the groaning of the hull.
Perhaps, when the next creak came, the deck smiled wryly to itself: Ah, it’s been a while.

source.japanese:
キサラの手に出現していたのは、荒縄。
　最小限の手順しか取らなかったのは、キサラ自身この時は拙速を尊ぶべきを知っていたのだろう。密航者の影と航海士の影が重なって縺[もつ]れて離れるまで僅か数呼吸、朔屋には止めるも手伝うも割って入るも、隙がそもそも見つけられなかった。
source.english:
Rough rope had appeared in Kisara's hands.
She used only the bare minimum of steps; even Kisara understood that this was a time to prize speed over perfection. The stowaway's shadow and the navigator's overlapped, tangled, and parted within the space of a few breaths. Sakuya never found an opening in which to stop Kisara, help her, or come between them.

target.text: Indeed───the upper deck of the Albatross must have heard all manner of sounds tonight. The voices of Kisara and Shisamu plotting as they resolved to do something or other, the repulsive noise of Sakuya vomiting, there must also have been the sounds of a forehead being banged against something while performing a dogeza, and probably also the usual din of the hull creaking and grating. When next he heard this creaking, perhaps he would be smiling wryly, thinking it had been a while since last.

What emerged in Kisara's hand was straw rope. In taking only the bare minimum of steps, Kisara herself must also have realized speed ought to be favoured over polish on this occasion. The shadows of the stowaway and the mate overlapped, entangled, then separated, all in the span of but a few breaths, and even had Sakuya wanted to stop it, help out, or step in between them, he couldn't even find a chance to do so to begin with.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だから、ね？　私を縛ったり縛ったりぐるぐる巻きにしたりこんな寒い中に放置したりしないでぇぇぇ…………」
source.english: “So, please? Don't tie me up and tie me up and wrap me all round and leave me out in this coooold…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「You get me, right? Don't tie me up and down and spin me all around and leave me out in this cold pleeeease…………」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あそこまでやる必要って、全くなかったんじゃないのか？」
source.english: “Was there any need at all to go that far?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「I'm pretty sure there was absolutely no reason at all to go that far?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたし、あの子のせいで、後で苦労しそうな気がしてならなくってさ。後顧の憂いは断っておかないと」
source.english: “I can't shake the feeling she'll make trouble for me later. I had to make sure there was no trouble left behind us.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I just can't help feeling that girl there is gonna cause me a whole lot of headaches later. Had to nip any future problems in the bud.」

source.japanese:
───その前救命艇が繋留されていた支柱は、今や空[から]。側に残されていたのは、意識を断絶せられた下級水夫君と、黒髪の芋虫と成り果てた密航者。密航者の方はしばらくは必死で、塞がれた口で何事か訴えていたものの、舷側から救命艇が降ろされる水音と、やがて遠ざかっていく櫂[オール]の音を聞いて、絶望的に目の色濁らせたが、ふと思いついたようににじっていったの下級水夫君へ。
　もぞもぞと身を被せると、彼と体熱を共有する事でどうにか夜の冷たさを凌[しの]いで、誰かに発見される事を祈った。
source.english:
The davits that had held the lifeboat now stood empty. Beside them remained an unconscious junior sailor and the stowaway, reduced to a black-haired caterpillar. For a time she struggled desperately to plead something through her gag. Then she heard the splash of the lifeboat being lowered over the side and the fading beat of its oars, and her eyes clouded with despair. Suddenly struck by an idea, she began inching toward the junior sailor.
She wriggled over him and shared his body heat, managing thus to endure the night's cold while she prayed that someone would find them.

source.japanese:
これが、信天翁号は、珍しく支払われた前金によって、これまたこれまでにないくらい珍[めずら]かな事に、二艘も揃えた救命艇、結局一夜にして失った顛末だった。
　慣れない財は身につかない、の喩えである。
source.english:
Thus ended the Albatross's unprecedented possession of two lifeboats, purchased with that rarest of things, an advance payment: both were lost in the space of a single night.
Unaccustomed wealth never stays in one's hands, as the saying goes.

target.text: ───The arms that the lifeboat had been suspended from earlier were now empty. Left behind by their side was the deck boy who had been stripped of his consciousness, and the stowaway, reduced to a black-haired caterpillar. For a while, the stowaway desperately tried to make her appeals about something or other heard through her covered mouth, but as she listened to the splash of the lifeboat being lowered from the ship's side, followed by the fading creaking of oars as they rowed away into the distance, her eyes clouded over in despair, but then it seemed as though something suddenly struck her, and she headed for the deck boy.
She wriggled herself on top of his body, barely staving off the chill of the night by sharing body heat with him, and she prayed that they would be discovered by somebody.

Thus went the tale of how the Albatross, by means of a rare advance payment, had, in a turn of events so rare it was practically unheard of, managed to procure no fewer than two lifeboats, only to end up losing them both in a single night. An illustration of an old truth: Easy come, easy go.

source.japanese: ───その漁船の、潮に洗われ白く塩吹いて、木乃伊の肌に負けず劣らず荒れた上甲板や、なかば腐りかかった綱の巻き束なんぞを見る度に、朔屋の心に訪れる感情は、棘のついた鞭を伴って、臀を意地悪くつついて責め立てる、人はそれをいたたまれなさというのだが。
source.english: Whenever Sakuya looked upon the fishing boat's upper deck—scoured by the tides, blown white with salt, its surface every bit as ravaged as a mummy's skin—or upon its coils of half-rotten rope, a feeling visited his heart armed with a barbed whip, maliciously prodding and tormenting his backside. It was what people call being unable to live with oneself—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……とうとうやっちまったなぁ、俺……」
source.english: “…I've finally done it…”

source.japanese:
呟いて、船縁に凭[もた]れれば、潮気をじくじくと含んで船員服に染みてくる、その冷たさも朔屋の心をちくちく刺すようで。
　あの信天翁号が大きなお兄さんに思えるほどの、全長一五米程度の小型の漁船で、そこかしこに魚の鱗[うろこ]や生臭さが抜き去りがたく染み着いた、それらの手入れの悪さが朔屋の居心地を悪くするのではない。
source.english:
Muttering, he leaned against the side. Salt damp seeped into his sailor's clothes; its cold, too, seemed to prick at his heart.
The fishing boat was only about fifteen meters long, small enough to make even the Albatross look like a big brother. Fish scales and fish stink were ingrained everywhere. But it was not the neglect that made Sakuya uncomfortable.

source.japanese: たとえちっぽけな小舟であろうとも、たとえどれだけ草臥れていようとも、船乗りにとって船は自分の家であり恋人であり古女房であり、その中に抱かれている限りは、申し分のない衣装のように馴染む筈、ヤドカリならばそれ以上の宿替えを考えないようになる、見てくれはどうあれ居心地の良い巻き貝のようなもの。
source.english: However small, however worn out, to a sailor a ship was home, lover, old wife. Held within her, he ought to feel as comfortable as in perfectly fitting clothes. Whatever she looked like, she was the sort of comfortable shell a hermit crab would never think of exchanging.

target.text: ───Every time he saw that fishing boat's deck, washed by the tide and coated in white salt, so rough and coarse it could give the skin of a mummy a run for its money, or the coiled-up bundles of rope that had begun to partially rot, the emotion that arose within Sakuya's heart was accompanied by a thorned whip prodding maliciously at his rear, tormenting him with accusation; it was what man called insupportable unease.
【Naomasa】 「……I've gone and done it for good this time, I really have……」

Muttering to himself, as he leaned against the gunwale, the salty humidity of the ocean air slowly seeped into his sailor clothes, and the chill also pricked at his heart like icy needletips. It was a fishing boat small enough that the Albatross looked like its large elder brother, with a length overall of about fifteen metres, stained indelibly with a fishy stench and scales lying here and there and everywhere, but it was not the poor upkeep that was the source of Sakuya's discomfort.

Even if she were a tiny dinghy, and no matter how battered she may be, to a sailor, his ship was his home, his lover, his wife of many a good year, and as long as he was held in her rocking embrace, it would feel as natural as wearing a well-tailored outfit; were one a hermit crab, it would be like a spiral shell so comfortable and cozy that, regardless of appearance, one would find it unthinkable to seek better lodgings.

source.japanese:
ただし───その船へ正当に乗りこんだ場合に限り、という但し書きがつく。
　船主の名前を問われて、躊躇せずに答えられる限りに於いては、という条項がつく。
source.english:
Provided, however, he had boarded that vessel legitimately.
Provided he could answer without hesitation when asked the owner's name.

source.japanese:
……朔屋の胸中を覗いて、去来する情景を追ってみようか。
　見えてくる情景は───
source.english:
…Shall we peer into Sakuya's heart, follow the scenes passing through it?
What we see—

target.text: However───this came with a proviso: This only applied as long as the ship was boarded through legitimate means. It came with a clause: This only applied if when asked about the name of the shipowner, one could answer without hesitation.
……Why don't we peer into Sakuya's heart and follow the scenes of past deeds flitting through it? The scene coming into view was───

source.japanese:
───夜陰にまぎれて窺う波止場。
　
　───索留がいい加減な船を選り分ける、キサラと朔屋。
source.english:
—A quay watched under cover of darkness.

—Kisara and Sakuya selecting a carelessly moored boat.

target.text: ───Scoping out a wharf beneath the veil of night. ───Kisara and Sakuya, sorting through the boats sloppily moored.

source.japanese:
───辺境の鄙[ひな]びた漁港とて、管理も甘く、ろくな鍵もない、共同倉庫。
　
　───積み上げられた重油のドラム缶。
source.english:
—A communal warehouse in a remote, rustic fishing port. Lax supervision, scarcely a lock.

—Drums of heavy fuel oil stacked within.

target.text: ───A communal warehouse in a remote, rustic fishing port, poorly guarded and without so much as a proper lock on the door. ───Drums of fuel oil stacked high.

source.japanese: ───運び出す力は、片割れを追いかける事にただただ必死のキサラの方がよほど強く、どこか狂疾的な怖ささえ感じさせて。
source.english: —Kisara far stronger at carrying them out, desperate only to follow her other half. Something frightening, almost mad, in that strength.

target.text: ───When it came to carrying them out, Shisamu, who was simply desperate in her pursuit of her other half, proved stronger by far, even giving off a sense of manic fear.

source.japanese: ───ディーゼルエンジンは、しっかりとした手入れが施されておらず、一件廃物に見えない事もないが、信天翁号の機関よりはよほど綺麗で。
source.english: —A diesel engine, poorly maintained, looking at first glance almost like scrap. Yet much cleaner than the Albatross's machinery.

source.japanese:
───もちろん鍵がないと始動は出来ないはずだけれど。
　
　───裏をかくやり方は色々ある。
source.english:
—Of course it should not start without a key.

—There are ways around that.

target.text: ───The diesel engine had not been properly maintained, and it could easily be mistaken for a piece of junk at first glance, but it was still in better shape than the engine of the Albatross by far.
───Naturally, it shouldn't be possible for the engine to start without the key, but. ───There were plenty of methods to circumvent that issue.

source.japanese: ───引っぱり出した電線の、被膜を剥いて線を剥き出しにして。
source.english: —Wires drawn out, their coating stripped, the conductors bared.

target.text: ───Stripping the insulation from the pulled-out wire, exposing the bare conductor.

source.japanese: ───弾け飛ぶ火花、二度・三度・四度。
source.english: —Sparks leaping. Twice, three times, four.

target.text: ───Sparks flying, twice, thrice, four times.

source.japanese: ───遂に動き出す、エンジンの。
source.english: —At last, the engine coming to life.

target.text: ───The engine finally coming alive.

source.japanese: 今や朔屋の肩書きは、信天翁号の船員ではない。あの船から離れてしまって、キサラの片棒担いだ今は、『船泥棒の共犯』であった。
source.english: Sakuya's title was no longer sailor aboard the Albatross. Having left that ship and taken Kisara's part, he was now an ‘accomplice to boat theft.’

source.japanese: 頭を抱えて眺める海の向こうには、沿岸部の稜線が、波のうねりに合わせて上下して、今にもそこから追っ手の船の影が滑り出てくるのではないかと、朔屋はびくびくと、船縁の影に身を縮めた。
source.english: Clutching his head, he stared across the sea as the coastal ridgeline rose and fell with the swell. At any moment, it seemed, the dark shape of a pursuing boat might glide out from behind it. Trembling, Sakuya crouched below the gunwale.

source.japanese:
外洋に出られるような船ではなく、自然二人の航海は沿岸伝いとなる。
　キサラはかたわれが流されたとして、あの夜信天翁号が位置していた海域に程近い沿岸に流されているに違いないと言い張ったから、どちらにせよ沿岸沿いの航路になったわけだが、今のところそれらしい情報は、ない。
　絶対に生きている、との確信は、双子の感応力に根差したものか、ただの思いこみか、どちらにしても朔屋には彼女に替わって行き先を定めるような意志も決断力もなく、本当に、ただついてきただけ、の状態で。
source.english:
This was no vessel for the open ocean; naturally their voyage followed the coast.
Kisara insisted that if her sister had drifted away, she must have reached a shore near the waters where the Albatross had been that night. So their route would have been coastal anyway. Thus far there was no promising news.
Her certainty that Sisam lived might spring from the twins' shared perception, or mere conviction. Either way, Sakuya had neither the will nor the resolve to choose a destination in her stead. He had truly done nothing but tag along.

source.japanese:
シサムとキサラは二人とも、どこで習い覚えてきたものか、その超常的な知覚力を抜きにして、正統的かつ古典的な航海術を心得ており、船員学校に籍を置いていた、だけの朔屋よりよほど航海者としての格も上だった。
　ただ二人揃った時のあの超位置感覚は失われてしまうため、立ち寄ってきた漁村でなんとか手に入れた、どうにも版の古い海図と前時代的な航海具を頼りの航海となる。
source.english:
Both Sisam and Kisara knew proper, classical navigation, quite apart from their supernatural senses. Wherever they had learned it, they stood far above Sakuya as navigators; he had merely been enrolled at a maritime school.
But the extraordinary sense of position they possessed together was gone. They had to sail by antiquated instruments and an old-edition chart somehow acquired in a fishing village along the way.

target.text: Right now, Sakuya's official title was no longer that of a crew member of the Albatross. Now that he had ended up leaving that ship behind, and had also helped Kisara pull off her scheme, he was an 『Accomplice to Boat Theft』

Head buried in his hands, he looked out over the sea; on the far side, the silhouette of the coastal ridgeline fluctuated in tandem with the undulating of the waves, and nervously worrying if the shadow of a pursuing ship wouldn't emerge from there any moment now, Sakuya shivered, curling up behind the gunwale.

This wasn't the sort of vessel that one could brave the open seas with, so their voyage naturally ended up following the coastline. Kisara had asserted that under the assumption that her other half had been set adrift, she would undoubtedly have been swept away to the coast near the waters the Albatross had been located in that night, so one way or another, their course would have taken them along the coast, but currently, they had no information that would suggest any such thing to be true.

That confidence that allowed her to state she was definitely still alive, was it rooted in the twins' sympathetic connection, or was it just a subjective assumption? Regardless of which, Sakuya lacked both the determination and decisiveness to set their destination in place of her; truly, he was just along for the ride.

Even leaving out that ability both Shisamu and Kisara shared───and where had they even learnt such a skill, that supernatural perception of theirs───they were still well-versed in both orthodox as well as classical practices of seamanship and navigation, and as navigators, compared to Sakuya, who had merely been enrolled in a nautical school, they were superior by far.

However, as a consequence of having lost that transcendental spatial awareness she possessed when both were together, their voyage grew wholly reliant on an old, obsolete nautical chart, as well as some antiquated navigational instruments they had somehow managed to get their hands on in a fishing village they had stopped by.

source.japanese: ───ちなみに、これらの航海道具などの他、シサムの追跡行の間必要とされるだろう各種日用品に関しては、二人の持ち合わせで賄うしかなく、この際勿体ぶって隠している余裕もなく、お互い財布を底まで叩[はた]いて、そして当然綜麻繰りだって吐き出した。
source.english: Incidentally, those instruments and all the everyday necessities they would need in their pursuit of Sisam had to be paid for with what the two had on them. There was no room now for playing coy about their money. Both emptied their purses right to the bottom—and, of course, coughed up their secret savings too.

source.japanese: その段になって、喜ぶべきところをつい呆れ加減の乾いた笑みが転がったのは、お互い呆れるくらいの小金を身につけていた事である。信天翁号を出奔同然に飛び出してきた訳だから、二人ともろくな用意などなかったはずなのに、いざ服やその他の隠し所をさらってみると、出るわ出るわの打ち出の小槌、とまで景気よくはいかなかったけれど、ま、中くらいの目出度さ程度には。
source.english: What should have delighted them instead brought dry smiles of something like disbelief: both had a surprising little hoard on them. They had left the Albatross practically as fugitives, with hardly any preparation. Yet once they searched their clothes and other hiding places, out it came, and kept coming. Not quite a magic mallet showering riches, but, well, a medium-sized blessing.

source.japanese: 朔屋については、船員暮らしを始めてからちょろちょろと貯めてきた───陸では貯蓄の観念が零に等しかった彼にしてはその時点で驚天動地の事態なのだが───小金を、全て用心で身に帯びる習慣づいており、もし落としたりなくしたりしたら目も当てられないと思うのだが、この時は上手く転がった。
source.english: Since becoming a sailor, Sakuya had saved a little money here and there—an earth-shattering development in itself, given that ashore he had scarcely known what saving meant—and had got into the habit of carrying it all on him for safekeeping. Losing or dropping it would surely have been disastrous, but this time things worked out well.

source.japanese: キサラに関しては、朔屋より信天翁号での日々が長く───という事は、悪辣にかっ剥[ぱ]ぐ機会も多く、溜めこんできた金もより多い。それを持ち歩きに容易な貴金属類に換えていたのも利して、立ち寄った漁村の、まだ栄えている一つにて故買屋を探り当て、換金したところ、目減りはしたがかなりの金になった。普段のキサラなら片割れと二人がかりでその故買屋の尻の毛まで毟[むし]り取ったところであろうが。
source.english: Kisara had spent longer aboard the Albatross than Sakuya, which meant more opportunities to fleece people mercilessly and more money hoarded. It helped that she had converted her takings into portable precious metals. In one of the fishing villages that still prospered, they found a fence and cashed them in. The fence took his cut, but the sum remained considerable. Ordinarily Kisara and her other half would have plucked the fellow clean down to the hairs on his backside.

source.japanese: これによって、遊興気分を持たない限りは、それなりの期間持ちこたえられるだろうとの見通しが立った───ただ、二人とも帰りの事は口には出さなかったけれど。
source.english: Thus they could expect to manage for a reasonable time, provided neither felt like revelry. Neither, however, spoke of returning.

target.text: ───Incidentally, aside from these various navigational instruments, when it came to the matter of all the different types of daily necessities that would surely become indispensable while they tracked down Shisamu, they had no choice but to cover the costs with what they both had on hand, and at this point, they no longer had the luxury of acting coy about it and keeping things hidden; thus, both of them emptied their wallets down to the last coin, and naturally, even coughed up their secret savings as well.

When it actually came down to that, in what should have been a moment of rejoicing, a dry, disbelieving chuckle escaped them instead, for they both carried a staggering amount of small coin on their person.

They had as good as deserted when they ran away from the Albatross, so neither of them should have been able to make any proper arrangements, but when they actually tried to rummage through their clothes and any other hiding places, money poured out endlessly like they were swinging a magic wishing mallet; well, not quite to that extent, but it was still a moderately joyous occasion. (TN: The hammer referenced here is the "uchide no kozuchi", written "打ち出の小槌", a legendary hammer that grants wishes when swung. It frequently appears in Japanese tales (Issun-boshi and Momotaro, for example) and also in the hands of Daikokuten, a deity of wealth.)

In Sakuya's case, he'd been saving up money little by little since he began his new life as a sailor───though this was nothing short of an earth-shaking turn of events for a man like he who had no concept of saving while he was on land───and it had become a habit of his to vigilantly carry all his petty cash on his person; while it would have been too awful to bear had he dropped it somewhere or otherwise lost it, this time, it worked out well for him.

In Kisara's case, she'd put in more days aboard the Albatross than Sakuya─── that is to say, she'd had more opportunities to ruthlessly divest others of their money, and so she had also saved up more money as well. Capitalizing on the fact that she had exchanged it for easily portable precious metals, in the fishing village they'd stopped by, she'd tracked down a fence in one of the parts of town that still thrived, and when she cashed it in, though it had depreciated in value, it still yielded a respectable amount of cash. Had Kisara been her usual self, then she would probably have gone there together with her other half and plucked the fence clean, all the way to the hairs on his bum.

As a result, assuming they didn't find the desire to indulge in some merrymaking, prospects were reasonable that they could stay afloat for a while ───however, neither of the two ever uttered a word about returning home.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「アストロラーベ、コードラント、クロススタフ、他も色々あるけど、要は太陽との高度角を出す為の道具なんだね」
source.english: “Astrolabe, quadrant, cross-staff, plenty of others. Basically they're tools for measuring the sun's angle above the horizon.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「There are astrolabes, quadrants, cross-staves, and plenty of others, but at the end of the day, they're all instruments to calculate the sun's altitude angle, right?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ただこういった天測にはいくつか問題があって、まず晴れて太陽が出てないとお話にならない」
source.english: “But there are a few problems with observations like that. First, without clear weather and the sun out, you've got nothing.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「But there are several problems with this kind of celestial navigation, starting with the fact that the skies have to be clear and the sun out, otherwise there's no point in even trying.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それから、揺れる船の上では正確な観測が、ことのほか難しいって事。それでも人間はこんな道具立てでも航海してきたんだ」
source.english: “And making an accurate observation on a rocking ship is incredibly hard. Still, people sailed with equipment like this.”

source.japanese: 何日か引き続いた曇りの中で顔を出した太陽に、古めかしいコードラントを翳[かざ]して測定し終えてからキサラは、朔屋にふっと綻ばせた口元の、微妙な間を置いて、曇りゆく。朔屋は今時そんな前時代的な航海具が実際の用に供しているところなど見た事がなく、物珍しさについついそちらに気を取られていたのだが、
source.english: After several cloudy days, the sun appeared. Kisara raised an antiquated quadrant and took her measurement. She gave Sakuya a fleeting smile, then, after a curious pause, the smile faded. He had never seen such outmoded navigational instruments put to actual use. The novelty had caught his attention. But—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And then there's the issue of making precise measurements on a rocking boat, something exceptionally difficult to do. And yet, mankind has still navigated the seas using nothing more than these instruments.」

Pointing it at the sun, who had finally shown her face after several successive days of cloudy weather, Kisara raised the antique-looking quadrant up to her head, finished taking her measurements, then let her lips soften into a faint smile towards Sakuya, but after a delicate pause, her expression began to cloud over. Sakuya had never before seen such an antiquated navigational instrument put to actual use in this day and age, and he found his attention drawn to it from the sheer novelty, but.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ま、どうにかなる……なる……ならなかったらどうしよう」
source.english: “Well, we'll manage… Manage… What if we don't?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Well, one way or another, we'll make it work……work…… what do we do if it doesn't work?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたしのせいで流されて、二人とも飢え死にしたり転覆して溺死か心臓麻痺で死んじゃったらあわわわわわ」
source.english: “What if I get us swept away and we both starve, or capsize and drown or die of heart failure—awawawawa…”

source.japanese:
信天翁号を発って以来、気を張って気を張って、たとえよしそれが虚勢だとしても、キサラはまあ超越的な努力を常に尽くし続けた。朔屋から見れば、この女何時か近いうちに、目鼻耳口の七孔そして肛孔と尿道口と女の膣口の三竅[きょう]合わせて十穴から虹色の液を噴出させて悶死するのではと戦慄するほど、キサラはまあよく頑張った、と思っている。
　気鬱とキサラの狂疾とでは自ずと差異はあろうし一概には語り得ないが、鬱期に陥ると自助を恃[たの]みもせず、団子虫は丸まりたくて丸まっているのではない、これは世界の敵意がそうさせているのだと開き直って精神の薄暮へ好き勝手に閉塞する朔屋にしてみれば、信じがたい意識力である。
　しかし導師も得ずでは内観によって到達しうる境地にも限度があってあわわわわわわわわわわわわわわわわわわわわわわっ。
source.english:
Ever since leaving the Albatross, Kisara had held herself taut, tauter still, maintaining a superhuman effort even if it was all bravado. To Sakuya she had borne up so magnificently that he half expected her, in the near future, to spout rainbow fluid from all ten apertures—the seven of eyes, ears, nostrils, and mouth, plus anus, urethra, and vagina—and expire in agony.
Melancholia and Kisara's derangement were different conditions, of course, and no simple comparison could be made. But when Sakuya entered one of his black periods, he made no attempt to save himself. A pill bug did not curl up because it wished to; the hostility of the world forced it so. With this defiant excuse, he shut himself as deeply as he pleased into the twilight of the mind. To him, Kisara's force of will passed belief.
Yet without a spiritual guide there were limits to the enlightenment introspection alone could attain, and—awawawawawawawawawawawawawawawa—!

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It'll be my fault we're set adrift, and if we both starve to death or capsize and drown to death or have a heart attack and die then whatawawawawawa!」

Ever since they had departed from the Albatross, she had steeled herself, always been on edge, and even should we belittle that as false bravado, my, how Kisara still kept pushing herself to the limit with transcendent effort. From Sakuya's perspective, Kisara had certainly held on well, to the point he couldn't help but shudder in terror at the thought that, before long, the seven holes of this woman's face: her eyes, nose, ears, and mouth, as well as her three lower orifices: her anus, urethra, and vagina, all ten holes combined, would erupt with rainbow-coloured liquids.

While depression and Kisara's madness were different by nature, and it was not something that could be spoken of in such broad, general terms, when he suffered a depressive episode, he would not rely upon any sort of self-help, no, Sakuya instead would grow defiantly resigned, for a pillbug did not curl up in a ball because it desired to, but rather because the enmity of the world surrounding it compelled it to, and he would seal himself away in the fading twilight of his own mind, on his own terms, and so from his point of view, this was a strength of will that beggared belief.
However, in the absence of a guru, there are limits to the mental state one can attain even through introspection andawawawawawawawa awawawawawawawawawawawawawawawa!

source.japanese: とキサラが、見ているだけで妄気が感染しそうな程の惑乱の極みに自我が呑み込まれてしまう日はやはり到来して、朔屋はその時に至って、甲板の舳先先端でヨガの体位で言うところ『ライオン』の姿勢を取ってとんでもない白痴顔晒しているキサラに決断せざるを得なかった。
source.english: At last came the day when confusion swallowed Kisara's self so utterly that merely watching her seemed enough to catch her delusions. At the very tip of the bow, in the yoga pose called the Lion, she wore an outrageous idiot's face. Sakuya could no longer avoid a decision.

source.japanese: 確率としては五分五分、二分の一……いやもう少し下がるか。それでも試す他はなく、背後からキサラの胸元に腕[かいな]巻きつけ、顎をぐいと逸らせ、見ようによっては旅行者を襲う絞殺教集団サッグのメンバーが黄色いネッカチーフにて扼殺を試みているとも取れなくない勢いで、彼女の口と鼻に宛がったモノ其[そ]はなんぞ。
source.english: The odds were fifty-fifty, one in two… no, perhaps a little worse. Still, he had no choice but to try. He caught Kisara from behind, crooked an arm across her chest, wrenched her chin up, and clapped something over her mouth and nose with such vigor that, from a certain angle, he might have been a Thuggee strangler garroting a traveler with his yellow scarf. And what, pray, was it?

source.japanese:
それは布切れ。朔屋とキサラが信天翁号を出奔する直前、船室で人事不省に陥っていたクロがお見舞いに来た際、哀しみに啜[すす]り泣いていた白子の涙……と洟[はなみず]をぬぐってやったそれだ。
　朔屋はそれをキサラを寝台に寝かしつけてやった際に拾い上げたのである。ただその時はどちらがどちらの寝台か見分け得ず、キサラの持ち物という可能性もあり、だから五分で、そしてその後ついクロの体液も交えてしまったからもっと下がるかも、とはそういう計算であるがさて。
source.english:
A piece of cloth. Just before Sakuya and Kisara fled the Albatross, when Kuro came to visit Kisara as she lay unconscious in the cabin, Sakuya had used it to wipe the grief-stricken albino’s tears… and snot.
Sakuya had picked it up while putting Kisara to bed. At the time, he had been unable to tell which bed belonged to which twin, so it might have been Kisara’s: hence the fifty-fifty chance. And afterward he had gone and mixed Kuro’s bodily fluids into it, so perhaps the odds had fallen lower still. Such was his arithmetic; now, then—

source.japanese: 口と鼻を覆われて、その匂いを深く吸いこむしかなくて、短く吸ってもう一度短く吸って長く吐いてと、何か産時を思わせる呼吸を何度か繰り返した後キサラの眸[ひとみ]に渦巻く、渾沌の乱雲はどうにか鎮まっていって、とはいえ不安と懸念を完全には拭い去る事はできないのだが、薬効を現してはくれた、成功よ。
source.english: Her mouth and nose covered, she had no choice but to breathe its smell. A short breath, another short breath, a long exhalation, repeated several times like breathing in childbirth. Gradually the turbulent clouds of chaos in Kisara's eyes settled. Not all anxiety or concern was wiped away, but it had worked as a medicine. Success.

target.text: And so, the day did inevitably arrive when Kisara's self was consumed by such extreme delirium that just watching her made it feel as if the madness might infect him as well, and when that time finally came, when Kisara stood at the very tip of the deck's prow, assuming the posture known as the『Lion』asana in yoga, her expression one of profound mental retardation, Sakuya was left with no choice but to make a decision.

In terms of probability, it was as likely as not, a fifty-fifty……no, perhaps a little lower than that? Even so, he could do nothing but make the attempt, and so he wrapped his arm around Kisara's chest from behind, then sharply jerked her jaw to the side, and depending on how you looked at it, it was done with such force that he could be mistaken as a member of the Thuggee strangulation cult assaulting a traveller and trying to strangle her with his yellow neckerchief, but that object pressed against her mouth and nose, whatever could it be?

It was a rag. Just before Sakuya and Kisara took flight from the Albatross, when Kuro had paid a visit to the woman unconscious in her cabin, that which he had used to wipe away the tears the albino shed as she sobbed in sorrow……and her snot, that rag. It was something he'd picked up while he was putting Kisara to sleep in her bed. However, at that time, it had been impossible for him to discern which bed belonged to who, hence it was quite possible that it belonged to Kisara, hence the fifty-fifty, and then Kuro's body fluids had also been mixed in later by accident, so maybe it was even lower; thus went the logic of his calculations, but, let us move on.

With her mouth and nose covered, she had no choice but to deeply inhale that scent; a short inhalation, then another, after which came a long exhalation, and following several cycles of breathing that somewhat evoked the moment of birth, Kisara's eyes began to churn, the chaotic storm clouds just barely abating; be that as it may, her anxieties or worries had not been completely dispelled, yet the drug still took hold, its effect manifested: it was a success.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「すっはぁーー…………っっ」
source.english: “Hh—haaaah…………!”
“Hah… Ah…”

source.japanese: その時確かにキサラはとりあえずの落ち着きは得たから、どうやらシサムの持ち物だったようだが、朔屋にはそれがなにやらよく判らなかったから、キサラに訊ねてみたところ。
source.english: Kisara had certainly gained some immediate calm, so apparently it belonged to Sisam. But Sakuya had no clear idea what it was, and asked her.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Fhhhaaaaaーー…………」
【Kisara】 「Haah…………ah……」

At that moment, Kisara had indeed regained some temporary semblance of calm, so it seemed to have been one of Shisamu's belongings, but Sakuya still couldn't really tell what exactly it was supposed to be, and when he tried asking Kisara.

source.japanese: 彼女もその時ようやく確認してみたようだったが、その表情曰く言いがたいものに引きつる、というか笑う、というか納得と言うかに転変して、なおもしつこく訊いたら朔屋は拳固で殴られてとっても理不尽の。
source.english: She, too, seemed only then to examine it properly. Her expression went through a series of indescribable changes: a wince, or a laugh, or recognition. He persisted in asking and got punched. Most unjust.

target.text: It seemed that she, too, had finally tried to check what it was herself that second, and her expression twisted into something beyond description, then shifted into what was perhaps a smile, or rather, something like acceptance, but as Sakuya still continued to stubbornly pester her with his questions, he was struck in the face by a fist, which really was unreasonable.

source.japanese:
その時に取り上げられてしまって後はもう見せてもらえず、後々もキサラがそれを使用する姿を見せるのを頑なに拒[こば]んだからよっぽど大事なモノだったのだろう。
　ネル生地で、中には綿か何かが縫い詰めてあって、基本的にはやや幅広い短冊形で、中ほどには羽布がつき、そういえば布地の中央にはなにやら血の染みのような───と思い出すだけでも朔屋は殴られたり蹴られたり果ては噛み千切られそうになったので、しまいに思い出す事さえやめるようになった。

　となると───
source.english:
To conserve fuel, they followed the coast from fishing port to fishing port, leaving half their progress to the current. Sakuya could not entirely shed his unease, but he had no choice but to trust Kisara's knowledge of navigation.
Which meant—

source.english: Thus Sakuya had almost nothing to do. On the Albatross he had longed for a day without work, trying every secret art he knew to get out of his duties, failing, then trying again without learning a thing. Now such days had come, whatever their form. And what happened?

source.japanese: ……真の教養人というのは、いかに暇を潰すかの術を得る為にも心を砕く、という。教養などいうものは、歳一五の頃合いから三行半突きつけて縁切りした朔屋だからして、狭い船室の板材の木目を眺めて、あれは象さんの形、あっちは下駄の形、などと連想するくらいしかやる事がろくになくなり、退屈に腸[はらわた]弾けそうになったのだ、この怠け者が。
source.english: …The truly cultured, they say, take pains even to learn how to spend idle time. Sakuya had handed culture its divorce papers at around fifteen. source.english: Whenever he went on deck to relieve his boredom, the early-autumn northern sea offered only an unchanging gray expanse of water and sky. source.japanese:
船室は小振りの漁船だからして、キサラと二人起居するので一杯の手狭の小部屋、当然毎日顔をつきあわせる事になる。

source.japanese: そんなわけで二人は日がな一日語るともなく語らい、朔屋はそれまでの恥多き、という恥しかない人生を、キサラは彼女達双子の生い立ちなどを問わず語りに口にするようになった───

target.text: Their course taking them from fishing harbour to fishing harbour along the coastline was, for the sake of conserving precious fuel, partially left at the mercy of the ocean currents, and while it wasn't as if Sakuya didn't still have his concerns about the whole affair, all he could do was have faith in Kisara's seafaring knowledge. Beyond that, they had to maintain the ship and stand watch over the state of the sea, but even that didn't require much effort either.

Even when he tried going out on deck to stave off his boredom, all that unfolded before his eyes was the same old grey of the ocean and skies of early autumn, and while it was fortunate that they had yet to encounter any heavy storms at sea, glimpses of other ships were also few and far between, and though this, too, was a stroke of fortune for these two boat thieves, more than anything, the cold was severe, and he couldn't stay outside for long. Therefore, all he could do was go back inside the cabin once again.

The cabin belonged to a fishing boat on the smaller side, so living in there together with Kisara was enough to fill the cramped little room, and naturally, they came face to face with each other every single day.

……Indeed, even Sakuya had learnt a method to kill time, just one. Spending it with a woman. If Kisara hadn't been there for him to talk with when she was comparatively calm, Sakuya would have fallen into his usual depression in the blink of an eye, and after standing on the deck for a time, unable to decide whether or not he should throw himself into the grey waters, his body would have been ravaged by the cold, and he would probably have caught pneumonia, or something of the like.

Therefore, the two would talk from dawn to dusk without really talking about anything at all; Sakuya would speak of his life riddled with shame, or rather, his life that was nothing but shame itself, and Kisara, without being prompted, began to speak of the twins' childhood───

source.japanese: 以前に沿岸集落の呪術師から耳にした、北の邑[ムラ]での神聖双生児というのが、なんの事はない、まさに彼女達のこと。双子はその集落で、ほとんど監禁され、自由を奪われて育てられていたのだという。

source.english: That they hated it and fled was readily understandable. What twists and turns had brought them aboard the Albatross remained untold.

source.japanese: 北の邑[ムラ]で、生まれて物心つくまで双子と言うことで崇められ、また忌まれ、それが耐えられなくて逃げ出してきたのに、結局今だって双子ということに縛られたまま、と自嘲するキサラの横顔が、朔屋の胸に侘びしく迫る。
source.english: In the northern village, from birth until they were old enough to understand, they had been worshipped and shunned for being twins. They had escaped because they could not bear it, and yet, even now, being twins kept them bound. As Kisara spoke in self-mockery, the sight of her profile filled Sakuya with a bleak loneliness.

target.text: Those sacred twins from a village in the north, the ones he'd heard of earlier from that shaman in the coastal settlement, turned out to be none other than them. In that village, the twins had all but been kept in confinement, raised while deprived of their freedom, she said.

He could certainly understand that they had been fed up with such a lot in life and made their escape, but whatever manner of twists and turns that had served as the lead-up to them boarding the Albatross, that was all left untold.
Maybe the circumstances weren't really anything that important, or maybe Kisara just didn't want to speak of it. Sakuya also deliberately refrained from probing further and simply let things be.

In that northern village, from birth and until they grew conscious of the world around them, they had been worshipped, as well as shunned, simply for being twins, and for all that they had been unable to bear it and ran away, ultimately, they were still bound, even now, by the fact that they were twins; when Sakuya saw Kisara's profile as she said so in self-deprecation, mournful desolation weighed heavily on his chest.

source.japanese:

source.english: The stove burned. With Kisara's advice, Sakuya's clumsy handiwork had reduced the drafts to tolerable levels. Comfortable, on the whole. Though it was the peace of a thieving couple—a lean fox paired with a spear thistle—who had taken a badger's burrow while its owner was out.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……I'm really glad that I was born into this world with Shisamu as my twin. Even us falling apart when separated from each other, well, it's like an innate part of us, so I can live with it.」

……Almost entirely filled from just two beds and a seaman's chest used in place of a table, a cabin nestled at the bottom of the stern.
