source.japanese: そして、日誌の内容を要約すれば。
source.english: To summarize what the journal said—

source.japanese:
難破船の船長の妻メアリが双子だったようだ。しかも、シサム・キサラ同様の交感力が具わっていたらしい。
　ある日船が、洋上に浮かぶ一人の漂流者を発見したようだった。その漂流者は、何やら巡礼めいた衣装の奇妙な娘で、小舟の破片と思しき板切れにしがみついていた。意識を失っており、何処の国の人間なのかも不明で、切れ切れの譫言から、彼女がどうやら『ひとつにしてみっつのもの』の同胞を求める旅にあったらしいことが窺えるのみ。
source.english:
Mary, the wreck's captain's wife, had been a twin. She and her sister also possessed a sympathetic sense like that of Sisam and Kisara.
One day the ship found a solitary castaway at sea: a strange young woman dressed rather like a pilgrim, clinging to a board that appeared to have broken from a small boat. She was unconscious, and no one knew her country. From her fragmentary delirium they gathered only that she had been traveling in search of kindred who were ‘one and yet three.’

source.japanese:
そしてこの漂流者を拾い上げた時より、船長の妻とその妹の様子がおかしくなり始めたのである。心ここにあらずといった様相で、放心状態に陥ることが多くなる。
（朔屋はここで、難破船から戻ってからの双子の奇妙な振る舞いを思った）
source.english:
After they took this castaway aboard, the captain's wife and her younger sister began acting strangely. Minds elsewhere, frequently falling into vacant spells.
(Sakuya recalled the twins' strange behavior after returning from the wreck.)

target.text: So, to summarize the contents of the journal.

Maria, the wife of the captain of the wrecked ship, seemed to be a twin. Moreover, she also seemed possessed of a sympathetic resonance similar to Shisamu and Kisara's. A certain day, the ship seemed to have discovered a lone person adrift on the sea. And this castaway, she was a queer young woman dressed in something like a pilgrim's robes, clinging to some pieces of wood that were thought to be the remnants of a small boat. She had lost consciousness, whatever country she hailed from was unclear, and the girl incoherently mumbled in disconnected fragments, so all they could gather was that she seemed to be travelling in search of fellow kin that were『one that is also three』.

And so, ever since the moment they picked up this castaway, the behaviour of the captain's wife, as well as her younger twin sister, took a turn for the strange. With the air of someone whose mind had wandered elsewhere, they would frequently slip into a dazed state. （Here, Sakuya thought back on the strange behavior of the twins after they returned from that shipwreck.）

source.japanese:
どうやら船長の妻と妹の精神状態は、回復していく漂流者の意識状況に影響されていたらしい。
　そして完全に漂流者が目覚めたとき、その娘は船長の妻と双子の妹を見て、歓喜の声を上げた、という。
source.english:
Apparently the sisters' mental state was affected by the castaway's recovering consciousness.
When the young woman finally woke fully, she saw the captain's wife and her younger twin sister and cried out in joy, the journal said.

source.japanese: 『まさかこんなところで、はらからに出会えるなんて』
source.english: ‘To meet my own kin in a place like this!’

source.japanese: 『さあ、一緒に解き放たれましょう───』
source.english: ‘Come, let us be freed together—’

source.japanese:
結合、昇華、そうとしか言い様のない現象が発生した、と記されてあったが、朔屋は数度読み返しても、正確な意味を読みとれなかった。
　とにかく、『漂流者と船長の妻姉妹が一つに結合』され、『この世界から昇華』されていくといった現象が発生したようだ。
source.english:
Union, sublimation: the journal recorded a phenomenon describable only in those terms. Sakuya reread it several times without grasping the precise meaning.
In any case, apparently ‘the castaway and the captain's wife and her sister joined into one,’ then were ‘sublimated from this world.’

target.text: Somehow, it seemed that the mental state of the captain's wife and her younger sister were being influenced by the state of consciousness of the recuperating castaway. And when the castaway fully opened her eyes, when that girl saw the captain's wife and her younger sister, she then shouted in unbridled delight, or so it went.
『To think that I would meet fellow kin in a place like this!』
『Come then, let us be set free together───』

Joining, sublimation, a phenomenon that could only be described as such occurred, or so it was written, but no matter how many times Sakuya reread that passage, he couldn't glean a clear meaning from it. In any case, 『the castaway, the captain's wife, and her sister joined into one』, they were 『sublimated from this world』, such a phenomenon seemed to have taken place.

source.japanese:
その辺りから、日記の断片に残された筆致が、乱れに乱れた走り書きとなり、
『光が』
『たとえようもない感覚が』
『全てが溶け合うような』
『吸いこまれていくような』
　といった、麻薬常用者の絶筆めいた文言が、紙面の上で虫が這いずり回ったかの様相で乱舞しており、文字を追うだけで精神が汚染されるような不快感に襲われ、朔屋はそれ以上は見ずに終えようかと逡巡した、次の頁で筆致は比較的落ち着きを取り戻していた。
source.english:
Around there the writing grew wildly disordered, a scrawl.
‘The light—’
‘An indescribable sensation—’
‘As though all things melt together’
‘As though drawn in’
Words like a drug addict's last writings danced over the page as though insects had crawled all over it. Merely following the letters brought a discomfort like contamination of the mind. Sakuya hesitated, wondering whether to stop. On the next page the handwriting recovered some composure.

target.text: And from that point onwards, the brush strokes left in the fragmented diary grew more and more disorderly, degenerating into scribbles: 『The light』 『A sensation beyond compare』 『As if everything melts together』 『As if I am being absorbed into it』

So it went, words akin to the last writings of a drug addict, dancing wildly across the page like a scuttling swarm of insects, and he was struck with a discomfort, as if just tracing the letters with his eyes was contaminating his own mind; Sakuya hesitated, wondering if it was best to just end it here without seeing any further, but the brushstrokes on the next page had regained a relative peace of mind.

source.japanese:
漂流者の娘が、詫びるような言葉を述べたのだという。
　あなたがたを巻きこんでしまう、と。
　同胞と出会えた喜びと、そして自分の余命がもうあまり残されていないことの焦りから（船員達は気づかなかったのだが、娘は死病に犯されていたらしい）、この船の上で『昇華』を試みてしまったけれど。
　しかるべき場所ではない為、周囲に予想外の余波を及ぼしてしまうみたい、と。
　本当なら、自分達三者だけが『昇華』していくのに、その余波で、周囲に居合わせた者達まで巻きこんでしまう、と。
source.english:
The castaway had spoken apologetically, he read.
You will be drawn into it.
Delighted to meet her kin, impatient because little life remained to her—the sailors had not noticed, but apparently she suffered a fatal disease—she had attempted ‘sublimation’ aboard this ship.
Yet because this was not the proper place, it seemed to have unexpected repercussions on those around them.
Normally only the three would be ‘sublimated.’ Its repercussions would draw in others present too.

target.text: The castaway girl offered words that sounded apologetic, or so it went. An apology, for unintentionally involving them all, she said. The joy of meeting her fellow kin, as well as the impatient anxiety of knowing her life was nearing its end (though the crew hadn't noticed, the girl's body was apparently being ravaged by a fatal disease), had compelled her to attempt to『sublimate』 while still on board this ship.

As it was not done in its proper place, it appeared to have caused unexpected ripples in the surroundings, she said. When done properly, only their three selves would have『sublimated』, and yet those ripples had engulfed the rest of the people that happened to be present around them.

source.japanese:
有り得ざる事で、あなた方がどうなってしまうのか、判らないと漂流者の娘は詫びたという。
　その言葉が示す通りに、船員達は次々に『光の中に消えて』いき、船長自身は今のところはそこまでには至らずとも、奇妙で異様な感覚が心身から去らないことからして、程なくして自分も船員達の後を追うであろう、だが不思議と恐怖はない、そのように続いている。
source.english:
The castaway had apologized: this was something that should not have been possible, and she did not know what would become of them.
As her words suggested, the sailors began one after another to ‘vanish into the light.’ The captain himself had not yet done so, but an odd, strange sensation would not leave his mind and body. Soon he would follow them. Curiously, though, he felt no fear. So the journal continued.

source.japanese: 誰も彼もが幸福そうな顔をしており、何より船長の妻と妹が、それまで見た事のないくらい、浄福の境地に包まれた顔だった、と。
source.english: Everyone looked happy. Above all, his wife and her younger sister wore faces enveloped in a blessed peace such as he had never seen.

target.text: I know not what will end up happening to you as a result of this inconceivable event; thus did the castaway girl apologize. And just as those words promised, the crew began to『vanish into the light』, one by one, and though the captain had yet to reach that point himself, based on the odd, eerie sensation that refused to leave his mind and body, before long, he would surely be following the rest of his crew, and yet, strangely, he felt no fear; he continued in this vein.

Their faces seemed joyful, one and all, and above anything else, the captain's wife and her younger sister, their faces were enveloped in a state of supreme beatitude, an expression of a like he'd never seen before.

source.japanese:
最後の文章は───
　
『私にも理解された。
　これは哀しむべき事態ではない。
　むしろ喜ばしいことである。
　私も、解き放たれる───
　
　この無限の牢獄から』
source.english:
The final passage—

‘I, too, understand now.
This is not a thing to mourn.
Rather, it is cause for joy.
I, too, will be freed—

From this infinite prison.’

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……いや、さあ。最後だってのに随分余裕あったのねこのおっさん。こんな文章長々と書き残すくらいなら、逃げるとかすりゃよかったろうに……」
source.english: “…Look. Pretty relaxed at the end, weren't you, old man? Instead of writing all this down at length, you could've run away…”

source.japanese:
身も蓋もない指摘を吐きながら、それでも朔屋は身内に慄然たる感慨が忍び寄るを禁じえなかった。
　船長が最後まで筆を執る落ち着きを残していたという事は、船内を見舞った『昇華』とやらが、彼にとって進んで受け入れてもいいような心境にさせる現象であったと示していないか。
source.english:
A blunt observation. Yet Sakuya could not keep a chilling feeling from creeping through him.
If the captain retained the composure to write until the end, did that not suggest that this ‘sublimation’ had made him willing to accept it?

source.japanese:
【直正】
（なんだかよく判らんが、
　この世から消えちまうとか、
　そういうことなんだろ？）
source.english:
(Don't really get it,
but it means disappearing from this world or something,
right?)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（そんなのが『喜ばしい』って、
　宗教かなんかか、これは……）
source.english:
(And that's ‘cause for joy’?
Is this religion or what…?)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（とにかく、つまりこれが、アレか？
　あの難破船の中が無人になっていた理由）
source.english:
(Anyway, so this is it?
Why that wreck was deserted?)

source.japanese: 船内に生じたのは、殺戮でも集団自殺でもなく、『昇華』なる不可解な現象の、だから失踪の痕跡らしい痕跡も残されていなかったのか。ただそれがどういう感覚を伴った現象であろうとも、酒と女という極めて現世的な快楽を愛する朔屋には、この世から消失してしまうような末路などひどく忌まわしく陰惨なものとしか考えられず、己の身をかき抱いた。惻々と寒さが触手を伸ばしてくるかのようだった。
source.english: So what had happened aboard was neither slaughter nor mass suicide, but the inexplicable phenomenon called ‘sublimation’—was that why there had been no real traces of the disappearance? Whatever sensations accompanied it, Sakuya loved the thoroughly worldly pleasures of drink and women. An end that meant vanishing from this world could seem only hateful and grim to him. He hugged himself. Cold seemed to extend its tentacles, quietly, insistently.

target.text: His final words were─── 『Even I was made to understand. This is not a situation to be grieved. Rather, it is to be rejoiced. I, too, am being liberated─── From this eternal prison.』
【Naomasa】 「……No, come on. You're being way too relaxed in your final moments there, old man. If you had the time to write such a long-winded passage, you should have just run away instead……」

While uttering some very blunt commentary, Sakuya was still unable to suppress the biting chill that crept deep into his core. That the captain had remained in such a calm state of mind as he continued to pen his log until the very end, did that not indicate that this 『sublimation』or what-have-you that befell the ship was a phenomenon that brought him to a state of willing acceptance?
【Naomasa】 （I don't really understand it, but it's like disappearing from this world. That's what all this means, right?）
【Naomasa】 （And to say that should be『rejoiced』, is this a cult or something……）
【Naomasa】 （Anyways, in short, that's what this is, yeah? The reason why that shipwreck was completely deserted.）

What had occurred on board the ship was neither a massacre nor a mass suicide, it was the inexplicable phenomenon of『sublimation』, so was that why there were no traces left that hinted at any kind of disappearance? But no matter what sensation this phenomenon may be accompanied by, to Sakuya, a man who loved the exceedingly worldly pleasures of booze and women, a fate that involved disappearing from this world could only be seen as an affair both deeply abhorrent and grim, and he hugged himself tightly. It was as if the cold was reaching out with its tentacles, piercing him to the bone.

source.japanese: 一通り読み終えて、航海日誌の断片を下のように羽目板の裏に収め直した時だ、背後に物音を聞いたのは。
source.english: Having finished, he replaced the journal fragments behind the wallboards as before. That was when he heard a sound behind him.

target.text: After having read through more or less everything, while he was stuffing the fragments of the log back behind that wood panel, he heard a noise from behind.

source.japanese:
ぎくり、と振り返れば、戸口から覗きこんでいたキサラの顔。仕舞い終わった直後で、日誌を盗み見していたことを覚られたかどうかは判らない───いや。
　キサラは無言で、咎めはせず、ただ───
source.english:
He turned with a start. Kisara's face peered through the doorway. He had only just put it away. No knowing whether she had realized he was secretly reading the journal.
No—Kisara said nothing, did not reproach him. Only—

target.text: When he turned back around with a start, he saw Kisara's face peeking in from the doorway. It was right after he'd finished stowing it away, so he wasn't sure if she'd actually realized that he'd surreptitiously read through the log───no. Kisara remained mute, without any words of rebuke, she just───

source.japanese: 片頬を吊り上げて、朔屋に解いてみせた笑みの、静かな顔だったのに、どこか心を締めつけるような、何かを妖しく仄[ほの]めかしているようにも見えて、青年を凝[ぎょう]と硬直させた。
source.english: One cheek rose in the smile she gave him. A quiet face, yet somehow it seemed to squeeze his heart, to hint at something uncanny. The young man froze.

target.text: Despite the serenity beneath her expression, just one corner of her mouth curled into a faint smirk directed at Sakuya, there was something heart-wrenching about it, a subtle, bewitching hint of something otherworldly that petrified the young man where he stood.

source.japanese:
そのまま、戸口から身を引いて、また甲板に戻っていった気配だけれど、奇妙に跫音が聞こえない。
　もちろん、ただ単に忍ばせていただけだろう、けれど、朔屋にはどうしてか。
　彼女の首だけが身体を脱して、船室まで覗きに来たかの、『抜け首』の怪談のような怖さが、たまらなかった。
source.english:
She drew back from the door and apparently returned to the deck. Strangely, no footsteps sounded.
Of course, she must simply have muffled them.
Yet somehow Sakuya could not bear the fear that, like a ghost tale of a wandering head, her head alone had left her body to peer into the cabin.

source.japanese: だから朔屋は、その後も日誌の事を話題に上せようとはしなかったし、キサラも何事もなかったように振る舞って、二人の間に落ちるような影はない、何も、と信じこもうしていたのはさてどちらなのか、あるいは両方とも。
source.english: Thus Sakuya never raised the journal afterward. Kisara, too, acted as though nothing had happened. No shadow fell between them. None. Which of them was trying to believe that—or were they both?

target.text: Holding that expression, she pulled away from the door, and it felt as if she'd returned to the upper deck again, but strangely enough, he didn't hear any footsteps. Of course, she was probably just concealing them, but Sakuya wasn't fully convinced. The fear that struck him, as if the woman's neck alone had parted from her body and floated down to the cabin to spy on him like the ghost story of the『Nuke-kubi』, was unbearable. (TN: The nuke-kubi, written "抜け首", is an old variant of the rokuro-kubi. The nuke-kubi can detach its neck from its body and sucks the blood of its victims at night like a vampire.)

Therefore, Sakuya did not attempt to bring up that log after this, and Kisara also acted as if nothing had happened, so there was nothing to cast a shadow between the two, nothing at all, but which of the two was trying to convince themselves of that? Perhaps it was them both.

source.japanese:
それでも朔屋の心中に、根強い不安が残ったのは仕方なかったろう。
　船長の妻と、その妹と、漂流者と。
　三人が揃った時に生じた、昇華。
source.english:
Yet naturally a stubborn anxiety remained within Sakuya.
The captain's wife, her sister, the castaway.
Sublimation when the three came together.

source.japanese:
かつて呪術師の小屋を訪れた時、双子は何を老呪術師に問うていた？
　朔屋には、一にして三なるものとか、三位一体者とか、そのような言葉を口にしていたように記憶されていた。
source.english:
What had the twins asked the old sorcerer in his hut?
Sakuya remembered words like one and yet three, the Triune One.

target.text: Even so, it was surely inevitable that a deep-seated unease would linger in Sakuya's heart. The captain's wife, her younger twin sister, and the castaway. The sublimation that arose when all three were gathered together.
Back when they had visited that shaman's hut, what was it the twins had asked the old shaman again? Sakuya recalled hearing phrases like the three-in-one, or the Triune Being, leaving their lips.

source.japanese: 風の合間にロープを結索し直しながらキサラは、氷原の白へ記憶を投影させるように眼差しの焦点遠くして、語り出した口ぶりものんびりと。渺茫と広がる氷原のただ中で、吹き続けていた風は今、しばしその渡る足を緩めて、キサラの声は吹き散らされる事もなく朔屋に届いて、空模様も穏やかに陽が差した、旅程の合間の徒然話には似合いの頃合いなので。
source.english: In a lull in the wind, Kisara retied the ropes and began talking, unhurriedly. Her gaze had gone distant, as though she were projecting her memories onto the white ice. Across that immeasurable waste the wind had briefly slackened its pace; her words reached Sakuya without being torn away. Mild sunshine filled the sky. A good moment for an idle tale along the road.

target.text: While re-knotting the rope in a break from the wind, the focus of Kisara's gaze was distant, as if she was trying to project her memories upon the white of the ice field, and her manner of speech was also casual. Right in the heart of the vast, boundless ice field, the wind that had been blowing ceaselessly now eased its crossing stride for a brief time, Kisara's voice reached Sakuya without being blown away, and even the skies had turned tranquil, sunlight breaking through the clouds; it was a fitting moment for idle musings between stops on a journey.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ねえ朔屋、聞いた事ある？
　樺太の方かな？　露西亜の放蕩人のお遊び。海が凍りついている頃の話だって。まずね、博労で一番元気の良い雄馬買ってさ」
source.english:
“Hey, Sakuya. Ever heard this one?
Up around Sakhalin, maybe? A game Russian wastrels used to play, when the sea froze over. First you go to a horse dealer and buy the liveliest stallion he's got.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Hey, Sakuya, you ever heard of this? It comes from Karafuto, I think? A Russian libertine's idea of a good time. A tale from back when the oceans were frozen over. First, he buys the most spirited stallion he can find at a horse trader.」 (TN: Karafuto, written "樺太", is the Japanese name for Sakhalin, the Russian island just north of Hokkaido.)

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それから、持ってる金、一晩で使いきる勢いで、美味い酒と食い物、飲み放題して食いまくって、たぶんセックスだってしまくるんだきっと。精力剤とか媚薬とかもたっぷり入れんのかな」
source.english: “Then you get the best booze and food, and eat and drink like you're going to spend every last penny in one night. Probably fuck like mad too. I bet they did. Maybe took a load of stamina tonics and aphrodisiacs.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「またそいつは豪毅な話だなあ。
　外は寒いのに、がんがん火ぃ焚いて、
　暑いくらいの部屋の中で酒盛りか……。
　乙なもんだよな、そういうのも」
source.english:
“Now that's living large. Freezing outside,
and you build up a roaring fire,
get the room almost too hot, and drink yourselves silly…
That does have a certain appeal.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And after that, ready to burn through every last coin he has in the span of a single night, with ambrosian drink and mouth-watering food, the liquor would flow freely and he would devour all he could, hell, he probably even had sex, and a bunch of it to boot, no doubt. Maybe he even loaded up on stuff like stamina boosters and aphrodisiacs.」

【Naomasa】 「Now that's a tale of indulgent excess. Even with the cold outside, he's got a fire roaring, drinking up a storm in a sweltering room……. That kind of thing really has its own charm, doesn't it?」

source.japanese:
短艇の下に据えつけた、橇の緩みをがんがん打ちつけ締め直し、船底の下から這い出す朔屋は、細かな氷雪の粒一面に浴びたのを、身震いしながらはたき落とせば、粒が舞う、陽光に煌めいて、乱反射して、金剛石の粉を撒[ま]いたよう。
　薙いだ大気の中で氷の粒は宙に長く留まって、朔屋はその夢幻的な眺めについ見とれたけれど、背景の延々広がる氷原を透かし見ると白が目に染みる、遠近感が怪しくなるような気がして、軽く瞼[まぶた]を降ろす青年の、足下も白、周りも白、離れて彼とキサラを俯瞰してみても取り巻くのは白。雪と氷の。
source.english:
Sakuya hammered the loose sled fittings tight beneath the boat and crawled out from under its hull. Fine ice and snow coated him all over. He shivered and brushed them off; the grains whirled in the sunlight, scattering light like powdered diamond. They hung a long time in the still air.
For a moment he lost himself in that dreamlike sight. Then, looking through it to the endless ice beyond, he found the white soaking into his eyes, making depth and distance uncertain, and lowered his lids a little. White at his feet, white all around. Step back and look down upon him and Kisara, and still there was only white enclosing them. Snow and ice.

target.text: Having hammered away to re-tighten any slack in the sledge fastened beneath the small boat, Sakuya crawled out from below it, coated in a fine, powdery layer of ice and snow, and as he brushed it off while shaking his body, the particles whirled about, glittering in the sunlight, reflecting diffusely like scattering diamond dust.

Within the disturbed air, the particles of ice lingered, and Sakuya couldn't help but be captivated by that dreamlike sight, but the sheer white of the endlessly sprawling ice field in the background was permeating his vision; feeling his depth perception slip away from him, when the young man gently lowered his eyelids, below his feet was white, all around him was white, and even should he step back to look down on himself and Kisara from a distant vantage, all that enclosed them was white. Of snow and ice.

source.japanese: 果てなく続く大氷原のただ中に、二人はその身を置いていた。
source.english: The two stood in the midst of a boundless ice field.

source.japanese:
二人が北限氷土のとば口となる氷の沿岸に接舷してから数日が経つ。
　無論キサラの旅は岸についただけで終着になろう筈もなく、更に内陸深くに入りこまなければいけないようだったが、氷原を旅する為の足はどうするつもりなのか、の朔屋の問いにキサラが示したのが。
source.english:
Several days had passed since they made landfall on the frozen coast at the threshold of the Northern Ice Wastes.
Of course, reaching the shore could never have ended Kisara's journey. They apparently had to go much deeper inland. When Sakuya asked how she proposed to travel across the ice, she showed him—

source.japanese:
船に備えられていた短艇の、船底に橇を着け、船体中ほどに柱を立てて檣[マスト]と為した、即席の帆掛け橇[ぞり]だった。
　岸から内陸までは引いて運ぶしかなく、骨ではあったが、一度氷原に押し出してしまうと、帆は簡単な単帆ながらちゃんと風を捉えて短艇（というか橇というか）を思いのほか軽やかに運んだ。
source.english:
The ship's boat, fitted with runners beneath the hull and a post amidships to serve as a mast: an improvised sailing sled.
Dragging it from the coast to the inland ice was hard work. Once out on the ice field, however, its single, simple sail caught the wind properly and carried the boat—or sled—with a surprising lightness.

source.japanese: もちろん風任せは風任せ、氷原上は常に間断なく風が流れているわけでもなく、無風ともなれば二人は帆掛け橇[ぞり]を降りて、肩に食いこむ苦役、ロープで引いて歩かなければいけなかったわけだが、それでも一日の間にいずれかはまた吹き出す。完全に風が止まるという事はなかった。
source.english: That still left them at the mercy of the wind. It did not blow ceaselessly across the ice. In a calm they had to get out and haul their sailing sled on ropes that bit into their shoulders. Yet at some point during each day it would begin blowing again. It never deserted them altogether.

source.japanese: かといって、月に叢雲、花に大風ともいう、物事には好事魔つきものなのに、風に花弁のような雪片が混じる事はあっても、帆掛け橇[ぞり]を刻みつけ、転がす様な大吹雪には二人は未だ出会わず、好天も続いた、お陰で氷原上の旅はこれまでのところまずは上々、いや出来すぎなくらいに快調と言ってよく、時季も良かったのだろう。
source.english: Clouds hide the moon; high winds strip the blossoms. Something always comes along to spoil good fortune. Yet though snowflakes sometimes drifted through the wind like petals, they had encountered no blizzard savage enough to score and overturn their sailing sled. Fair weather held. So far their progress had been good—almost too good. They must have chosen the right season.

source.japanese: それでも日が落ちれば寒気は防寒具など薄布のように貫いて二人の肌を、血肉を噛み裂きにかかる豺狼の牙にと硬く鋭く尖る。夜空は透徹した大気に月魄も星影も凄いまでに燦々めいたが、冴えた光は寒気と呼応して薄い刃と化して二人に注がれるようで、それらの凍える夜夜を二人は、それぞれの肌の温もりを頼りにしのぐしかなかった。接舷してからの夜の数と同じくらい肌を重ねて今に至る（正確には二人の情交の回数はもっともっと多いのだが）、岸は既に遠く遠く後になった。
source.english: After sunset, though, the cold hardened into sharp jackal and wolf fangs, piercing their winter gear as if it were gauze, worrying at flesh and blood. In the utterly clear air, moon and stars shone with an almost terrible brilliance. Their keen light answered the cold, seeming to fall upon the travelers in thin blades. Through those freezing nights the two had only each other's bodily warmth to sustain them. They had lain skin to skin about as many times as nights had passed since landfall—strictly speaking, they had coupled many, many more times than that. The shore was far, far behind them now.

source.japanese: それだけの夜を過ごしていれば、二人が寄り添うのはもう当たり前となっており、橇の点検を終えて朔屋はキサラと肩を触れ合わせて腰を下ろす。
source.english: After so many nights, drawing close to each other had become a matter of course. His inspection of the sled finished, Sakuya sat down beside Kisara, shoulder to shoulder.

target.text: In the heart of a vast ice field that seemed to stretch on without end: that is where the two found themselves.

Several days had passed since they'd come alongside the icy shore that served as the threshold to the northernmost permafrost. Naturally, there was no way that Kisara's journey would have reached its final destination just from arriving at the shore, no, they would probably have to penetrate even deeper into the inland, and in response to Sakuya's question of what she intended to do about their means of travel across the ice field, Kisara revealed her answer.

It was attaching a sledge to the bottom of the small boat that the ship was equipped with, then erecting a post in the middle of that boat to serve as a mast, forming an improvised, sail-powered sledge. They were left with no choice but to transport it by hand, dragging it until they made it from the shore to the inland, and it certainly was laborious, but once pushed out onto the ice field, though the sail itself was but a lone, modest sail, it caught the wind perfectly fine, and it carried the boat (or perhaps that should be sledge) across the ice with surprising ease.

Of course, being dependent on the wind came with its own set of drawbacks: it wasn't as if wind was ever blowing across the ice field without interruption, so when it was windless, the two were given no choice but to alight from their now-becalmed sail-powered sledge and drag it along by rope on foot, drudgery that gnawed at their shoulders, but even so, at some point during the day, it would begin to blow once more. The wind never came to a complete standstill.

On the other hand, it is said that beauty draws disturbance just as clouds veil the moon and winds buffet the blooming flowers; wherever there is fortune, misfortune is never far behind, and yet, while they had encountered snowflakes drifting through the wind like scattered flower petals, the two had yet to run into any great blizzards that would send their sledge tumbling as it carved through the ice; the fine weather continued, and owing to that, their journey across the ice field had been excellent up to this point, why, one could say it was sailing so smoothly that it was almost too good to be true, and the season must have been favourable as well.

Nevertheless, as daylight faded, so did the chill also begin to pierce their winter clothing like it was made of diaphanous silk, hardening into the sharp fangs of a wolf sinking into their flesh and tearing it apart. In the limpid air, the night sky glittered brilliantly with the white soul-glow of the moon and radiant star-shade both, yet that crisp light, echoing the penetrating cold, seemed to morph into thin blades raining down upon the pair, and on such frigid nights, all the two could rely upon was the warmth of each other's skin.

Hitherto, they had spent as many nights in each other's arms as had passed since they first came ashore (more accurately, the actual amount of times they'd been intimate was much, much higher), and the shore was already far, far behind them.

And having spent so many nights of such a nature together, it had become natural for the two to cuddle close together, so after finishing his inspection of the sledge, Sakuya sat down with his shoulder leaning against Kisara's.

source.japanese: キサラが朔屋の髪に残っていた氷雪を払う、手は分厚い手袋の、これで簡単なロープワークくらいなら着けたままでこなすのだから大したものである。手袋だけでなく、彼女は全身分厚い防寒具に身を包み、あの偉大な乳房も中に押しこめてもこもこと、まるまる肥えた仔犬の様を髣髴とさせた。見慣れたリーファージャケットとミニスカートに比べれば女らしい曲線にはどうしたって隠されるが、こちらはこちらで雪国の童[わらし]のような可愛げがあると、朔屋はキサラの防寒具姿をそれなりに気に入っていた。
source.english: Kisara brushed the remaining ice and snow from his hair. Her hands were in thick mittens; it was impressive that she could even manage simple ropework without taking them off. Not just her hands but her whole body was bundled in heavy winter clothing, those magnificent breasts packed away inside it, making her look round and fluffy as a fat little puppy. Compared with her familiar reefer jacket and miniskirt, it inevitably hid her womanly curves. Still, it had a charm of its own, like a child of the snow country. Sakuya rather liked her in winter gear.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんでそれからどうすんの。
　馬買って、酒盛りして、それから」
source.english:
“So what happens next? Buy the horse,
have your drinking party, then what?”

target.text: Kisara brushed off the snow and ice that remained in his hair, and despite the thick mittens covering both her hands, she was still able to handle basic ropework without removing them, which really was quite impressive. She wasn't just wearing mittens, the girl's entire body was covered in thick winter gear, bulging as it managed to contain even her magnificent chest, making her resemble a round, plump puppy.

When compared to the familiar reefer jacket and miniskirt, her feminine curves were inevitably obscured, but this had its own endearing charm, reminiscent of a child from a snow country, Sakuya thought, quite fond of how Kisara looked in her winter outfit. (TN: Snow country, written “雪国”, is a Japanese term for regions that experience heavy snowfall during the winter months.)
【Naomasa】 「So then, what did he do after that? He buys a horse, makes merry with drink, and then what?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そんで、満腹して、酔いも回って腰もすっきり気怠くなったら、買った雄馬に、最上の朝鮮人参を囓らせる。で橇を着けると」
source.english: “Then, once you're stuffed and drunk and your hips are all loose and pleasantly tired, you give the stallion the best Korean ginseng to chew on. Hitch it to a sled.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And then, when his stomach is full, the alcohol is hitting, and his hips are pleasantly sore, he makes the horse he bought nibble on the finest ginseng. Then he hitches it to a sleigh.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そしたら、バスケットにウォトカだのウイスキイだのピロシキだのをたっぷり詰めて、それ持って馬橇に乗って海に乗りだすんだ。もちろんよく晴れた晩を選んで」
source.english: “Pack a basket full of vodka and whiskey and piroshki, climb aboard with it, and head out onto the sea. Pick a clear night, of course.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Once he's done that, he fills a basket with plenty of vodka, whisky, pirozhki and so on, and taking that with him, he rides out on the horse-drawn sleigh, out on the sea. Of course, he makes sure to pick an evening with clear skies.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「カンカンに凍ってるから、馬橇乗ったって、
　割れやしない」
source.english:
“It's frozen solid.
A horse and sled won't crack it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「海に乗りだすって、どこに行くつもりなんだ。いくら凍って割れないからって……」
source.english: “Head out onto the sea? Where are they going? Even if the ice won't break…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It's frozen solid, so even riding on a horse-drawn sleigh, it's not going to crack.」
【Naomasa】 「You say he rides out to sea, but where does he plan on going? Even if it won't crack from riding on it, that doesn't mean……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「どこに行くつもりもないんだよ、そんなの。
　ただただ、沖に向かって走らせる。
　海の氷はほら、
　緑がかった、深い深い色になるじゃん」
source.english:
“They're not going anywhere. That's not the point.
They just keep driving out toward the open sea.
You know how sea ice gets that greenish color?
That deep, deep green.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「He doesn't have anywhere he plans on going. He simply rides forth towards the open sea. See, the ice of a frozen ocean, it's tinged green, and it becomes this deep, deep colour.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そんな氷が、水平線の彼方まで広がって、月とか星の光を反射して、そりゃもうなんとも言えない凄い景色だって」
source.english: “It stretches past the horizon, reflecting the moon and stars. They say the view's just… beyond words.”

source.japanese:
短艇の横板に並んで腰を下ろすといって、朔屋もキサラと同様の防寒具を着けているから、布団でも挟んだように密着感に寂しい、キサラは朔屋の首に腕を回して引き寄せて、額と額を軽く合わせて瞑目して、小さく頷[うなず]く仕草の、己の頭の中の景色を朔屋へ移そうというかのように。
　キサラの額、始めは硬く冷たく、やがて温まって馴染み、濃く淡く、緑に凍てついた海の上を走り続ける馬橇の姿が、するりと解れるように、朔屋の脳裏にも映し出されていく。
source.english:
They sat side by side on the boat's thwart, but with Sakuya swaddled in winter clothes as thick as Kisara's, the closeness was disappointingly like an embrace through a quilt. Kisara put an arm around his neck and drew him close, touched her forehead lightly to his, and shut her eyes.
With each little nod, she seemed to be trying to transfer the view in her mind to his. Her forehead was firm against his and cold at first; then it warmed and settled there. Across a frozen sea, green in shades dark and pale, a horse sled ran on and on. The image softly unfolded in Sakuya's mind as well.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And that kind of ice, it stretches out beyond the horizon, reflecting the moonlight and the starlight, and that makes for an indescribably breathtaking sight, that's why.」

Though they were sitting side by side on the boat's thwart, both Sakuya and Kisara were wearing similar winter gear, so lacking a real sense of contact, like a futon had been squeezed between them, Kisara linked her arm around Sakuya's neck and pulled him closer, gently touching their foreheads together as she closed her eyes, then made a small nodding gesture as if attempting to transfer the mental landscape in her own head into Sakuya's. Kisara's brow, at first cold and hard, soon warmed and felt familiar, and a vision, both vivid and fleeting at once, of a horse-drawn sleigh gliding across a frozen sea of emerald ice was smoothly projected into Sakuya's mind as well.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「氷原のただ中を、いつまでもいつまでも走り続ける───
　運がよければ。方角があってれば。氷が途切れず続けば。馬の心臓が破れなければ。
　……北方諸島に辿り着けるかも知れない」
source.english:
“They go on and on across the ice forever. If they're lucky.
If they're heading the right way. If the ice doesn't end. If the horse's heart doesn't burst…
They might make it to the northern islands.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「運がなかったら。
　───どこにも行き着かないで、
　ただひたすら。
　───氷の上をどこまでも」
source.english:
“If they're unlucky…
they never reach anywhere.
They just keep going.
On and on across the ice.”

source.japanese: 緑氷に凍てつく海に駆け出した時、その蕩児も馬橇も、人の世の時間から飛翔するのだろう。たとえ春になって氷が溶けたとしても、かの疾走する姿は波間に沈むのではなく、氷と共に失せるだけ。季節が巡りまた海が閉ざされて、氷の上に大輪の月がかかれば、月影の中に馬橇はまた立ち現れて、走り続けるのだろう、何時までも。
source.english: Perhaps the moment the wastrel drove out upon that green-frozen sea, he and his horse sled took flight from human time. Even when spring came and the ice melted, that racing figure would not sink beneath the waves; it would simply vanish with the ice. Seasons would turn, the sea would close again, and when a great full moon hung over the frozen surface, the sled would reappear in its light and run on. Forever.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それはいくらなんでも、放蕩児の蕩尽にしたって破滅的に過ぎるだろ……。
　でもどうなのかな。
　酔っ払ってる間は凄え良い気分だろうし」
source.english:
“Even for a wastrel out to squander everything, that's a ruinous way to go…
Still, I don't know.
While you're drunk, it must feel incredible.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「その間は寒さなんか感じないんだろうな。
　いやはや、凍死が楽な死に方などと誰が言ったやら、だ。一回真冬の晩に、道端で寝かけた事があるけどさ」
source.english:
“Probably don't even feel the cold then. Honestly,
who said freezing to death was an easy way to go? Once, in the dead of winter, I nearly fell asleep by the roadside.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「酒が途中で切れて目を覚ましたっけ。
　ありゃひどかった。
　寒くて寒くて寝てなんかられねぇっつーの。
　でももっと酒が入ってたら、どうなったかわかんないな」
source.english:
“Woke up halfway through because the booze wore off.
God,
that was awful. So cold I couldn't possibly sleep.
If I'd drunk more, though, who knows?”

source.japanese: 合わせた額を離すのが少し勿体なくて、朔屋も目を閉じたまま、氷上の疾走に想起された記憶を低く物語る、が、朔屋にかかるとその凄絶な光景も、俗に塗れて酔漢の命拾いの話にと引きずり下ろされて、キサラはなんだかなと苦笑した。
source.english: Reluctant to break the contact of their foreheads, Sakuya kept his eyes closed and quietly told the memory that the race across the ice had brought to mind. In his hands, that magnificent, terrible vision was dragged down into the muck of everyday life: a drunkard's narrow escape. Kisara gave a wry smile. Well, really.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「In the middle of a field of ice, running and running, forever and ever─── If fortune favours him. If his heading stays true. If the ice stretches on unbroken. If the horse's heart doesn't burst. ……He might just make it to the Northern Islands.」
【Kisara】 「If fortune is not on his side. ───He will never arrive anywhere, just endlessly, single-mindedly. ───Drifting atop the ice, to wherever it ends.」

When he rode off across that ocean surface frozen in green, both the libertine and the horse-drawn sleigh alike must have soared beyond the bounds of human time. Even were it to become spring and the ice melt, that galloping figure would not sink beneath the waves, it would simply vanish with the ice. As the seasons turned and the sea was bound in frozen chains once more, when the moon stood in full bloom and struck the icy surface, that horse-drawn sleigh would once more manifest within the moonbeams, running ever onward, for all eternity.
【Naomasa】 「Surely that's going too far. Even for some libertine's reckless dissipation, that has to be too self-destructive……. But I do wonder. It must feel incredibly good while you're still drunk.」

【Naomasa】 「You probably wouldn't even feel the cold during that time. Honestly, whoever came up with this idea that freezing to death is an easy way to go? You know, once, on a midwinter night, I ended up sleeping by the roadside.」

【Naomasa】 「And if I remember right, I woke up after sobering up at some point. That was an absolute disaster. It was so unbearably cold, there was no damn way I could sleep through that, seriously. But if I had drunk some more, I'm not sure what would have happened to me.」

It felt like a shame to pull their foreheads apart; Sakuya's eyes were also still closed, quietly recounting the memories awakened by that dash across the frozen sea, but as soon as Sakuya got involved, even that stupendous spectacle was dragged down to the level of a tale smeared in the commonplace, of a drunkard barely escaping a dog's death, and so Kisara gave a slightly exasperated smile in return.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それに、その馬橇の道行きは、誰かとくっついてるじゃん。最期まで、寒くなんてないって」
source.english: “Besides, on that sled ride you've got someone close beside you. You wouldn't be cold. Not even at the end.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Besides, when you're travelling on your horse-drawn sleigh, you'd be snuggled up to someone, wouldn't you? You wouldn't feel cold until the very end.」

source.japanese: 朔屋から身を離したけれど、突き放すのではなく額を親しく擦り合わせてからで、それからキサラは短艇の艫[とも]の戸立板の下に積みこんである行糧から水と豆炭を取り出し、珈琲を沸かしにかかった。
source.english: She drew away, not pushing him off but first rubbing her forehead affectionately against his. Then she took water and briquettes from the provisions stowed beneath the boat's transom and began making coffee.

source.japanese: 離れてなおキサラの額の温度は朔屋の額に残って、次第に氷原の空気に冷えていったけれども彼女が示した親しさ、近しさについ頬が緩んだ。既に幾度となく肉の交わりを重ねた間なれど、こういう色事とは別の稠密な態度も朔屋には嬉しい。自分がなんだか人並みになったような気がして。
source.english: The warmth of her forehead lingered on Sakuya's, slowly cooling in the air above the ice. Her affection, her closeness, brought an involuntary smile to his face. They had coupled countless times already, but a gesture of intimacy this deep, quite apart from sex, made him happy too. It almost made him feel like an ordinary person.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───で、キサラよう。今いきなりそんな話を持ち出したのは、食い物がひもじいって言いたいのか」
source.english: “…So, Kisara. Did you bring that story up out of nowhere to say we're going hungry?”

target.text: She pulled away from Sakuya, but it wasn't to push him away in rejection, and only after intimately rubbing their foreheads together did Kisara then pull out some charcoal briquettes and water from their stash of provisions for the journey packed away under the todate-ita covering the bottom of the small boat's stern, getting ready to brew some coffee. (TN: A todate-ita, written "戸立板", is perhaps best compared to a transom board, but it is still different. It is essentially a board that covers a locker or storage space beneath the deck, sealing it off. These are a feature in traditional Japanese boatbuilding.)

Even after parting, the warmth of Kisara's brow still lingered on Sakuya's own, and though it was gradually cooled by the air of the ice field, at the intimacy the woman showed, the closeness, he couldn't help but let his cheeks soften into a smile. Though they had shared in physical intimacy many a time already, Sakuya was still glad for this sort of intimacy, an emotionally saturated behaviour distinct from the erotic. It made him feel like he was becoming somewhat normal.
【Naomasa】 「───So then, Kisara. Since you suddenly brought that up out of nowhere, are you trying to say that you're starving for food?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「や、決してそのような」
source.english: “No, certainly not.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Oh no, perish the thought.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「干し肉だって、鮭の日干しだって、海豹の皮の干したのだって、噛めば噛むほど味出るし」
source.english: “Dried meat, dried salmon, dried sealskin—the more you chew, the more flavor comes out.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I mean, the dried meat, the sun-dried fish, even the dried seal skin, the more you chew on it, the more flavourful it gets.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「干し林檎のチップスだって、干し葡萄だって、かみ続けてると甘甘だし」
source.english: “Dried apple chips and raisins too. Keep chewing and they're sweet as anything.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「There's the dried apple chips, the dried grapes, and if you keep biting down on those, they turn really sweet.」

source.japanese: ずらずら並べる食料は、いずれもこの短艇に積みこんだ物だが、どれもこれも『干し』の字が冠され聞いているだけで唾を吸い取っていきそうな、それくらいしか用意できなかったのである。
source.english: She reeled off the provisions they had aboard. Every last item began with ‘dried.’ Merely hearing the list seemed liable to suck the saliva from one's mouth. It was all they had been able to get.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……代わり顎ががくがくになるわ、えらい喉が渇くだけどな。
　水、保つかなあこれ……」

source.japanese: ……朔屋が帆の操作を放り出してキサラに、防寒具の留め具を外しながら突進していったのは、偏に彼女の惑乱を鎮めてやる為であり、自分の見ている前で女が銃弾で頭をぶち抜くなど真っ平ごめんだからであり、キサラから矢継ぎ早に浴びせられる指示の声を聞くうち、凛とした声音が何やら心の絃というか背筋の感じやすい部分と言うかに響いて、ぞくぞくとするような愉悦が上ってきて、知らず知らず逸物が硬くなり初[そ]めていたからではない、けして。

target.text: ……Sakuya abandoned handling the sail and headed for Kisara, charging forwards while unclasping the fasteners on his winter gear; this was something done solely to calm her turmoil, for the last thing he wanted to see was a woman blowing her brains out with a bullet right before his eyes.

The fact that, as he heard the woman's voice raining down upon him with one instruction right after the other, her dignified and valiant tone of voice had resonated with his heartstrings, or rather, that sensitive part of his spine, and that a delicious, shivering pleasure had crept upwards, and unconsciously, his penis had begun to harden, was certainly not the reason, no, woe betide any who would claim so.

source.japanese: キサラの不安を物哀しく案じたり、かと思えばどうしようもなく些細な事で欲情したり、朔屋の方がよほど不安定で、躁鬱の気が彼の知らない間に発動しているのかと危ぶまれるほどだが、帆から離れればこんなちっぽけな短艇などたちまち船体がぶれるのは当たり前。キサラから後ろ蹴りで弾き飛ばされる以前に、船体が風に揺らいだ弾みで船床の肋[ろく]に足を引っかけてばったりと、倒れてしたたかに鼻面を撲[う]ちつけて、声も無く蹲[うづくま]る、そんな朔屋に、
source.english: One moment sadly worrying over Kisara's distress, the next aroused by some utterly trivial thing: Sakuya was far the less stable of the two. One might wonder whether a manic-depressive streak had awakened without his knowledge. Leave the sail unattended, though, and naturally such a tiny boat would slew about at once. Before Kisara could kick him away, a gust rocked the hull. His foot caught on a rib in its floor, and he fell flat, smashing his nose. As he crouched there, speechless—

target.text: He showed a plaintive concern for Kisara's unease one moment, only to be helplessly aroused by the most trivial nonsense the next; Sakuya was also very unstable in his own right, to the point one might fear that one of Sakuya's episodes of manic depression had manifested without him realizing it, but having left the sail, it was only natural that a boat this tiny would immediately start drifting and shaking. Before he was sent flying backwards from a rear kick delivered by Kisara, as the hull rocked in the wind, he caught one of his feet on a rib running along the bottom, struck the tip of his nose as he collapsed with a loud crash, then crouched down without so much as a squeak.
The words sent this man's way were:

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だから、なんだかんだと今は、朔屋の下半身に救われてるのは、これはホント。あんたがついてきてくれて、よかったよ……」
source.english: “So, one way and another, your lower half really is saving me right now. That's true. I'm glad you came along…”

source.japanese: そんな朔屋の、どこまでも情けない有り様にも、キサラの眼差しは優しかった。
source.english: Even confronted with this utterly pathetic spectacle, Kisara's eyes were gentle.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「So in the end, when I say that, right now, it's your dick keeping me together, it's the truth, Sakuya. I'm really glad that you came with me……」

source.japanese:
吹雪が荒[すさ]ぶれるでもないが、向かいつけてくる凍風に、呼吸するだけで肺が凍りつくような氷原、大口を開けて声を出すだけでも体力は削られよう。
　なのにキサラは頬を上気させ、それどころか体内の不純物が冷気に濾過されていくような清冽な感覚に身を浸しているかのように、満悦の体だった。
source.english:
There was no raging blizzard, but the freezing headwind across the ice seemed enough to freeze their lungs with every breath. Even opening one's mouth wide to speak would sap one's strength.
Yet Kisara's cheeks were flushed. She looked positively content, as though luxuriating in a pure, clear sensation, the cold filtering impurities from her body.

target.text: It was hardly the case that a blizzard raged around them, but it was still an ice field battered by freezing winds, so cold that merely breathing made it feel as if your lungs would freeze over, and just opening your mouth wide and speaking was enough for your strength to be sapped. And yet, Kisara's cheeks weren't just flush with colour, it was as if every impurity in her body was being filtered out by the cold air, so cool and clear a sensation was she immersed in, basking in a state of pure bliss.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「げぇーふぅ。ああ……堪能したっ。生命って素っ晴らしいぃ……」
source.english: “Buuurp. Ah… That hit the spot! Life is absolutely wonderful…”

source.japanese:
キサラの血管で、血が燃えていた。
　新たな血を迎えて、生命の悦びに、躍動していた。
　それというのも───
source.english:
Blood burned in Kisara's veins.
Welcoming new blood, it pulsed with the joy of life.
For—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……俺かてびっくりだわ。こんな氷原に鳥がいるとも思わなければ、それを見事撃ち落としたはいいが、いきなり喉笛に食らいついて生き血を啜[すす]るたぁよ……」
source.english: “…Believe me, I was surprised too. Never thought there'd be birds in an ice field like this. Nice job shooting it down, but then you went straight for its throat and sucked the blood…”

source.japanese:
【直正】

They are usually fierce, bloodthirsty guardians or deities in the Japanese tradition, often depicted as devouring flesh and spirit.)

source.japanese:
【キサラ】

source.english: “I shared with you, didn't I?”

source.japanese:
あれから更に数日が経った。
　だが四方の景色は変化を全く欠いて、砂糖の盆のような白い氷雪が広がるばかり、近くに寄れば平原には瘤や窪みなどが散在しているのが判るのだが、ある程度離れると凹凸の感覚など距離の中に溶ける。
　変わり映えのしない景色は日数の感覚を削ぎ落とし、細やかな感情など鈍麻させて、後に残るものは根深い不安と苛立ちと。二人の暗い感情は物を言わずとも感じ取れるくらいに肩口から立ちのぼり、混ざり合って、より陰険な怪物と化して二人を上から押さえつけるよう。
　だから夜毎の交わりはただ快感の為というより、何か切実な、堰から溢れ出そうとする崩壊を食いとめる足掻きのように懸命なものとなり、その時は箍の外れたように睦言を交わし合うのだけれど。
source.english:
Several more days had passed.
The view in every direction remained unchanged: white snow and ice, like a tray of sugar. Close up, the plain revealed scattered bumps and hollows, but from any distance their unevenness dissolved.
The unvarying landscape stripped away the sense of days passing, dulled finer feelings, leaving only deep-rooted anxiety and irritation. Without a word spoken, their dark emotions seemed to rise visibly from their shoulders, mingle, and form a still more vicious monster that pressed down upon them.
Their nightly coupling thus became less a pursuit of pleasure than a desperate struggle to hold back a collapse about to overflow its dam. During it, they exchanged endearments with all restraint undone. But—

target.text: Several more days had passed since. But the view in every which direction remained utterly devoid of variation, and like a tray of sugar, all that unfolded was the white of snow and ice; when drawing closer, one could tell that there were bumps and hollows dotted across the plain, but were one to step back far enough, any sense of unevenness would dissolve into the distance.

The monotonous landscape gradually chipped away at any sense of the passage of time, any delicate emotions grew numb, and all that remained was a deep-rooted anxiety and frustration. The dark emotions of the two rose in billows so thick from their shoulders that they were easily felt even when left unspoken, intermixing, transforming into an even more sinister, black-hearted monster that seemed to press down upon them both from above.

Therefore, their nightly intimacy was not merely undertaken for pleasure, it became something earnest, something desperately fervent, like trying to stem a tide of ruin about to burst through a dam, and in those times, they would whisper sweet nothings to each other like they had lost any sense of self-restraint.

source.japanese: 今日ともなると、食事の時なのにお互いにめっきり口数が減ってしまって、味気なさは乾いた食物のせいばかりでもなかろう。内圧めいた物が二人の間に膨れあがっていって、どんな些細なきっかけで爆発するか知れたものではなく、我の強さに欠ける朔屋は、物言いが自然キサラの機嫌を窺うものになるのだが、それが気に触ったのか、干し肉を横ぐわえにして、やにわ立ち上がったその激しさ、とうとう逆上して喚き散らすかと身構えた朔屋の前で。
source.english: Today, even over a meal, both had grown markedly quiet. The dry food alone could hardly account for its tastelessness. Something like pressure built between them, ready to explode at the slightest provocation. Sakuya, lacking much force of will, naturally began speaking as though testing Kisara's mood. Perhaps it grated on her. With a strip of dried meat crosswise in her mouth, she suddenly stood so violently that he braced for the fit of rage he thought had finally come. Before his eyes—

target.text: And today, in spite of it being mealtime, they were both noticeably less talkative, and the insipid atmosphere could probably not be blamed entirely on the dried food. Something like an internal pressure was building, swelling up between the two; it was impossible to tell what trifle would trigger the explosion, and never one for assertiveness, Sakuya naturally began to walk on eggshells, speaking in a way that catered to Kisara's mood, and perhaps that rubbed her the wrong way, for with a piece of jerky clenched sideways between her teeth, she suddenly rose to her feet with such intensity in front of Sakuya that he was preparing himself for her to finally fly into a rage, rant and rave.

source.japanese: おもむろに拳銃を天に擬したかと思えば、二連の釣瓶撃ち、大気を劈[つんざ]く銃声をまともに受けて耳の中が残響でなかば麻痺して、呆然とキサラを見あげれば、蒼穹を睨[にら]みつけていた視線が下がりゆく、釣られて朔屋も視線を降ろした、先でどさり。
source.english: She calmly aimed her pistol at the sky and fired twice in quick succession. The shots split the air, striking his ears full on and leaving them half numb with echoes. Dazed, he looked up at Kisara. Her gaze, fixed upon the blue sky, descended. His followed it downward, and there came a heavy thud.

target.text: Just as she deliberately raised her revolver towards the sky, she fired two shots in rapid succession; catching the full brunt of the air-splitting gunfire, his ears were left ringing and numb from the reverberations, and as he looked up at Kisara in a daze, her gaze that had been fixed on the blue skies lowered, and Sakuya, drawn in by it, lowered his own gaze along with hers, and then a thud sounded ahead of them.

source.japanese: 落ちてきたのが純白の鳥だったわけで。
source.english: What fell was a pure-white bird.

target.text: What fell was a bird of pure white.

source.japanese:
単調の日々の中で、心を浮き立たせる出来事には相違なかったわけだが、朔屋の言った通り、生肉に囓りつくキサラは凄絶で。
　だが青年にも、生肉を喰らう事への抵抗感は始めこそ残っていたものの、でも邦では牛刺し、馬刺しを食えば、新鮮なレバーなら胡麻油と塩で食しもする民族である。ささみの佳いところは生を残しても食べられる、と勇を鼓して囓りついた朔屋の口の中で、肉は旨味に蕩[とろ]けるようで、血は甘みに染みこむようだった。幾日にも渡り、干物ばかり食っていた舌にはあまりにも鮮烈な食事だった───
source.english:
An event to lift their spirits amid those monotonous days, certainly. Yet, as Sakuya had said, Kisara gnawing at raw flesh was a fearsome sight.
At first he, too, had balked at eating raw meat. But back home his people ate raw beef and horse, and fresh liver with sesame oil and salt. Good chicken tenderloin could be eaten with some of it left raw. Taking courage from that thought, he bit in. The meat seemed to melt into savor upon his tongue; the blood seeped in as sweetness. After days of nothing but dried provisions, it was an almost unbearably vivid meal.

target.text: Amidst these days of monotony, this was certainly an event that enlivened the mind, and to be sure, just as Sakuya had said, the sight of Kisara sinking her teeth into raw flesh was a fiercely gruesome one to behold. However, even though the young man still harboured some resistance to the idea of eating raw meat, especially at first, back in his homeland, they were a people who would eat gyuusashi, or basashi, and if presented with a fresh liver, they would even eat that with some sesame oil and salt. (TN: Gyuusashi, written "牛刺し", is beef sashimi, thin slices of beef served raw. Basashi, written "馬刺し", is the same but horse meat.)

One of the virtues of fresh sasami is that it can still be eaten even when raw, Sakuya thought as he screwed up his courage, and when he sunk his teeth into it, the meat seemed to melt into umami in his mouth, as if a sweetness deeply permeated the blood. It was a meal too excessively vivid for his tongue that had been tasting nothing but dried foods for many a day─── (TN: Sasami, written "ささみ", is thin slices of chicken tenderloin. Since the meat has no fat, it dries very quickly when cooked, and so it is traditionally also eaten raw or medium-rare in Japan.)

source.japanese:
口中に残る濃厚な味わい、生命の要素といったものを舐め回してから、朔屋は大きく伸びをする、背骨や腰、首の節が、繋ぎが外れてばらばらになるのではないかと危ぶまれるほどに音高くなる。
　風に乗った帆掛け橇[ぞり]での帆走は、傍目に見れば飛ぶよう滑るようだが、乗りこむ者には震動がひどい。そもそもしっかりと専用に作られた橇[そり]でもない。これが横転せずに済んでいるのは、専らキサラの風読みによるところ大きい。ともかく、実のところ朔屋の身体は、帆走のうちに固く強ばって、解す事も億劫なまでに疲労を蓄積させていたのだが、久方ぶりの肉らしい肉を味わって幾らか細胞も賦活されたようだった。
source.english:
Sakuya licked the rich taste still coating his mouth, the very stuff of life, then stretched expansively. His spine, hips, and neck cracked so loudly that one feared the joints might come apart and scatter.
From outside, a sailing sled borne on the wind might appear to fly, to glide. For its passengers, it jolted terribly. It was hardly a properly built sled in the first place. That it had not overturned owed much to Kisara's reading of the wind. In truth, the voyage had left Sakuya's body so stiff and laden with fatigue that even working out the knots felt like too much trouble. His first taste in ages of meat worthy of the name seemed to have revived his very cells.

target.text: After swirling around the lingering richness with his tongue, what could well be said to be the essence of life itself, Sakuya stretched long and deep, the joints of his spine, lower back, and neck popping so loudly one might worry that all the connections keeping him together might disconnect and scatter to pieces.

When looking from the outside, sailing on the sail-powered sledge as it rode the wind might well look as if one was flying, gliding smoothly along, but the shaking was terrible for those who rode upon it. It wasn't even a properly made, purpose-built sledge to begin with. It was thanks almost entirely to Kisara's skill in reading the wind that it hadn't overturned yet. At any rate, the reality was that Sakuya's body tensed up hard while gliding, and he had built up so much fatigue that even the concept of loosening up his body felt burdensome, but after tasting meat that truly tasted like meat for the first time in ages, it felt as though even his very cells had been invigorated.

source.japanese: キサラも同じく伸びをしてから、短艇の底にへばりついていた、その鳥の胸羽を摘[つま]みあげ、ふっと風の中に吹き散らし、
source.english: Kisara stretched too, picked up a breast feather of the bird that had stuck to the boat's floor, and blew it out into the wind.

target.text: Kisara also stretched in the same way, then lay down flat on the bottom of the boat, plucked off the bird's breast feathers, and scattered them into the gently blowing wind.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でもこれでもうしばらくは保つよ」
source.english: “Still, this'll keep us going a while longer.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……だな。食ったすぐ後だが、なんとなく精もついた気分だ」
source.english: “…Yeah. Only just finished eating, but I feel like I've got some strength back.”

source.japanese:
しばらくは、保つ。確かに行糧もまだ残ってはいる。だがその『しばらくは保つ』という言葉は、目標と期間が明確に設定されていればこそで、後どれだけ氷原を往けばいいのか、果たしてシサムまで辿り着けるのか、それさえ定かならぬ状態では何も根拠がなく、声は明るいものの、朔屋の耳には虚ろに聞こえた。
　けれどそれを認めて受け入れてしまえば、二人の旅はたちどころに立ちゆかなくなる。
source.english:
A while longer. Certainly they still had provisions. But ‘a while longer’ meant something only when there was a definite goal and a definite length of time. They did not even know how much farther they had to travel across the ice, or whether they would ever reach Sisam. There was nothing to support those words. Bright though her voice was, they rang hollow to Sakuya.
Yet if they acknowledged and accepted that, their journey would fall apart at once.

source.japanese: 帆掛け橇[ぞり]を走らせる氷原は万年の凍土であろうに、二人が踏んでいるのは、何時ひび割れて呑みこんでしまうかの危機を常に孕んだ薄氷なのだった。
source.english: The ice beneath their sailing sled might have been frozen for ten thousand years, but what they were treading was thin ice, always liable to crack and swallow them.

source.japanese: どこまで保つか───
source.english: How long could it hold—

source.japanese: 先の事を思う賢明さなど耳貸す程度も持ち合わせない、はなはだしいほど暢気者の朔屋にして、この頃になるとそれを想わない日はなく、だからといってキサラを説得して引き返そうとも考えないのもまたこの青年なのだ。
source.english: Sakuya, prodigiously carefree, ordinarily would not spare so much as an ear for the wisdom of looking ahead. By now, however, not a day passed without his thinking of it. And yet it never occurred to this same young man to persuade Kisara to turn back.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Still, with this, we should be able to last a little while longer.」
【Naomasa】 「……Right. We only just finished eating, but I already feel like I've managed to get some life back in me again.」

Last a little while longer. Certainly, they still had provisions. But those words, "last a little while longer", they only mean anything if the goal and time frame is clearly defined; how much deeper into the ice field would they need to venture, would they ever reach Shisamu at all; in this situation where not even that was a certainty, there was no guarantee of anything, and though her voice was cheerful, it only sounded hollow in Sakuya's ears. But, if they were to admit as much and accept reality, their journey together would fall apart in the blink of an eye.

Though the icy field beneath their sail-powered sledge was surely eternal permafrost, the ground the two of them were threading on was thin ice, ever fraught with the danger of cracking open at any moment to swallow them whole.
For how long could they last───

Sakuya, a soul once so prodigiously careless that he lacked the capacity to even lend an ear to any wise words of foresight, found that, by now, there was not a day where he was not thinking about what lay ahead; that he still did not even entertain the thought of convincing Kisara that they should turn back in spite of that was also part of this young man's nature.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋───」
source.english: “Sakuya—”

source.japanese: 突如、血の愉悦に崩していた相好を引き締め、身を乗りだして、がっと肩を掴んできたキサラの剛力、防寒具越しなのに骨まで食いこんで、内心を見抜かれたかと狼狽えて、誤魔化そうとする言葉がまた朔屋ならでは、下に傾く。
source.english: Suddenly Kisara's face, relaxed in delight at the blood, drew taut. She leaned forward and seized his shoulders, her tremendous grip biting to the bone even through his winter clothes. Panicked that she had seen through him, he tried to talk his way out of it—and, Sakuya being Sakuya, his excuse promptly veered below the belt.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え、いや、純粋に体力としての精力というか、食ってすぐ交合うのは消化に悪いというか───」
source.english: “Huh? No, I meant strength in the ordinary sense. Not sexual stamina. Doing it right after eating's bad for the digestion—”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Sakuya───」

All of a sudden, she tightened her features that had gone slack from the delights of blood, leaned forwards, and as Kisara clamped down hard on his shoulder, the force of her unyielding strength dug all the way into his bones, even through the winter gear, and flustered at the thought that his inner thoughts might have been exposed, the words he came up with to deflect from it were also distinctively Sakuya; thus, they veered towards the loins.
【Naomasa】 「Oh, no, I'm talking life purely in terms of physical stamina, or rather, it would be bad for the digestion to have sex right after eating or, or, uhm───」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そうじゃねぇって！　望遠鏡！　〇度の方角！」
source.english: “Not that! Telescope! Bearing zero!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───おい、まさか」
source.english: “…Hey. Don't tell me—”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「That's NOT what I'm talking about! Telescope! Heading zero!」
【Naomasa】 「───Oi, there's no way!」

source.japanese: キサラの眼差しは、朔屋ではなく、彼の肩を越えて氷原遙かに据えられて、きりきりきりりと弓弦を引き絞る様な音さえ聞こえてくるほどに高まった緊張の中に、危うげだが期待も入り交じって───朔屋は防寒具の中からあの望遠鏡を取り出そうとするも、手袋や布地の厚さが邪魔して思うようにはいかず、格闘した数秒の長かった事、ようやく引き出した望遠鏡を、キサラ、奪うように引ったくり、
source.english: Her eyes were not on him but far across the ice beyond his shoulder. The tension drew so tight that one could almost hear a bowstring creaking; precarious hope mingled with it.
