source.japanese: 下腹に力をこめると、何かとんでもない量の流動物がどろりとあふれ出してきたのにキサラは幸せそうに微笑んだ。あっという間に内腿までが濡れていく量。自分の中で、朔屋が気持ちよくなった証。自分をこんなにも気持ちよくしてくれた証。
source.english: Kisara tightened her lower belly, and an astonishing quantity of fluid came spilling out of her in a thick rush. She smiled happily. Enough to wet her inner thighs almost at once. Proof that Sakuya had found pleasure inside her. Proof that he had given her so much pleasure in return.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「じゃあ、また、あたしに欲しいな……」
source.english: “Then I'd like some again…”

source.japanese:
今度は、シサムに、と朔屋を促す。
　朔屋はそれで、ふらふらと、それでも種をつけることに取り憑かれた眼差しで、シサムに挑んでいく。
source.english:
Sisam urged Sakuya toward her in turn.
Unsteady on his knees yet still possessed by the need to plant his seed, he took her invitation.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Phew……now that you've pulled out……it's so sticky…… and trickling out like crazy. You came a whole lot inside me too, huh……」

As she tensed up her abdomen, even though copious amounts of some kind of fluid began to stickily pour out from her, Kisara smiled joyfully. It came out in such quantities, it even made her inner thighs wet in the blink of an eye. This was proof, proof that Sakuya had felt good inside her. Proof that she herself was able to make someone feels so good.
【Shisamu】 「Well then, I think I'd like you to fill me up again……」

Now do it with me this time, Shisamu urged Sakuya. And so, even as he staggered and reeled, with the eyes of a man consumed by the urge to impregnate, Sakuya turned to face Shisamu as his next opponent.

source.japanese: ───三人の情交への飽くなき欲望は、夜が明けても続くのではないかというくらいに、果てしがなかった。
source.english: Their insatiable desire to couple seemed endless enough to outlast even the coming dawn.

source.japanese: 二人は打ち続く絶頂の間に、肌の裡[うち]から燐光、光の粒を零すようになる。初めは目の錯覚、汗の珠を見誤ったかと思われた朔屋だったけれど、何度見直しても以前として光の粒は零れ続ける。
source.english: Amid their continuing climaxes, the two began shedding phosphorescence, grains of light from within their skin. At first Sakuya thought it an illusion, beads of sweat mistaken for something else. Yet however often he looked again, the grains of light continued to fall.

source.japanese: その光の粒は清澄で、人界から隔絶した星の世界のもののように美しくて。ただその美しさが人間離れしているだけに、朔屋は不安を覚える。
source.english: They were clear and beautiful, as if belonging to a world of stars removed from the human realm. But precisely because that beauty was inhuman, Sakuya grew afraid.

source.japanese: 肉の身体ではこんなにも繋がっているのに、二人が何か遠い、手の届かない存在へと変わりゆくように想われてならなかったのだ。
source.english: Their bodies were joined so closely in the flesh, yet he could not shake the feeling that the women were changing into something distant, beyond his reach.

target.text: ───The unquenchable passion for intimacy shared between the three was so boundless, it felt as if it might continue even after dawn would break.

In the midst of their continuous climaxes, a faint phosphorescence began to radiate from beneath their skin, spilling forth like little motes of light. At first, Sakuya thought it but a trick of the eyes, just beads of sweat that he'd mistaken for something else, but no matter how many times he looked at it, glowing particles continued to scatter.

Those drops of light held a luminous serenity, beautiful like something born of the world of stars, far removed from the realm of man. And precisely because it was such an inhuman beauty, it made Sakuya uneasy.
Even though their flesh and blood was so intimately connected, he couldn't shake the feeling that the two were transforming into beings somewhere far-off, beyond his reach.

source.japanese:
夜半、目覚めた朔屋は、独り。
　情交の後で溶け崩れるようにして共に眠りに就いたはずの双子の姿、右にも左にもなく、ただ独り。
　狭苦しいはずの、天幕を張った短艇の内側に広がる空虚は、朔屋が独りであるという事を強調するかに、異様な圧迫感をもって押し寄せた。
source.english:
Sakuya woke in the middle of the night, alone.
The twins should have fallen asleep beside him after coupling, all three of them melting together into sleep. Neither lay to his right nor to his left. He was alone.
Emptiness filled the supposedly cramped interior of the tented boat, pressing upon him with a strange weight, as though to insist upon his solitude.

source.japanese:
この圧迫感にひしがれる朔屋に、自分がとても小さな生き物に逆戻りしたかの恐慌が波となって押し寄せる。
　───そう、母に手を引いてもらわないと怖くて外にも出られなかったあの頃に。
source.english:
Crushed by that pressure, he felt a wave of panic, as though he had become a very small creature again.
Yes—the days when he had been too frightened even to go outdoors unless his mother held his hand.

target.text: In the dead of night, Sakuya awoke. Alone. The twins, who had seemed to melt apart after their intimate evening, who should have fallen asleep together with him, were neither to his left nor his right; he was all by himself. The emptiness that filled the boat-turned-tent, which should have been uncomfortably cramped, as if to stress to Sakuya that he was by his lonesome, closed in on him with an abnormal feeling of oppression.

Being crushed beneath this pressure, the fear Sakuya felt of himself having regressed into but a tiny being formed waves that surged over him. ───Yes, just like back in those days, back when he was so scared that he couldn't even go outside if his mother wasn't there to pull him by the hand.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（キサラは、シサムは───!?）
source.english: (Kisara? Sisam—!?)

source.japanese:
短艇の中に自分以外の誰もいないという孤独がふいごとなって、朔屋の恐慌をことさらに猛らせるような風を送る。
　なんと恐ろしいのだろう。
　目覚めた時誰もいてくれないと言うのは。
　短艇を隙間なく埋めているとこの心細さ、一体誰に抗議すればいいのか判らなくなるほどの心細さに、朔屋の全身の細胞がてんで勝手に震え出す。
　その心細さは喩えるなら、昼とは全く異質の相に様変わりした夜の学校、それも見知らぬ校舎に迷子になった心細さを何倍にも拡大したのに近い。
　恐怖は抗[こう]しようもなく、朔屋にできることいったら、強硬症を起こした者がするように、背を丸め膝を抱き寄せるくらい。
source.english:
The solitude of being the only person in the boat worked like a bellows, blowing his panic to a fiercer heat.
How terrible it was to wake and find nobody there.
This helpless loneliness filled the boat to bursting.
He did not even know whom to complain to; every cell in his body began trembling on its own.
It was something like being lost at night in an unfamiliar school, the building transformed into something utterly unlike its daytime self—but that fear multiplied many times over.
He could not resist it. All he could do was hunch his back and draw his knees up, like someone seized by catalepsy.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （Where's Kisara, where's Shisamu───!?）

The loneliness of there being none but himself in the boat worked like a pair of bellows, sending out gusts of wind that only fanned the flames of Sakuya's terror. How dreadful a thing it must be. To have nobody there for you when you wake up. The isolation that filled every inch of the boat, so crushing he didn't even know who he should make his protests to, made every cell in Sakuya's body shiver.

If one were to offer a simile for this disheartening isolation, it would be something several times stronger than that experienced when one was at school late at night, a place transformed into something wholly unrecognizable from the face it bore in daylight, and one were to get lost in an unfamiliar schoolhouse. He could not even attempt to defy the fear running through him; at best, all Sakuya could do was react like someone struck by catalepsy, curling up his back and hugging his knees close to himself.

source.japanese:
震えて目を閉じようとした朔屋の耳に届いた声のある。
　短艇の外から、双子の声だった。
source.english:
As he trembled and tried to shut his eyes, voices reached him.
The twins, speaking outside the boat.

target.text: As Sakuya trembled and began to close his eyes, a voice reached his ears. It was the twins' voice, coming from outside the boat.

source.japanese:
弾かれるように這い出した朔屋が見たものは、短艇の檣[マスト]の上、帆桁に乗って佇む、双子の姿。
　不思議で、異様で、そして素晴らしく美しい眺めだった。
source.english:
Sakuya scrambled out as if flung from it. The twins stood upon the yard, high on the boat's mast.
A strange, uncanny, wonderfully beautiful sight.

source.japanese: ぱん、と一つ柏手を打てば、その衝撃で珠となって降り注ぎそうなほどに、密に夜空を充たした星々の下、帆桁に乗った二人は、不安定な足場なのに小揺るぎもせず、星の光に全身を浸して、金の髪を緩くたなびかせていた。
source.english: The stars packed the night sky so densely that one sharp clap might have shaken them down in beads. Beneath them the two stood upon the yard, motionless on that unsteady footing, their whole bodies steeped in starlight, golden hair streaming gently.

source.japanese:
短艇に立てた檣[マスト]はせいぜい五米[メートル]に足らないかという小振りなものなのに。
　双子が佇むは長大なる、まるで星々の間にも駕していこうかというほどの帆柱で。
　まるで朔屋が視界を上げた分だけ、すらすらと果てなく伸びあがり、遠ざかりゆくよう、そのくせ二人の姿だけは視界の中に何時までも留まって、道理が通じないこれは、夢の中なのか。
source.english:
The mast they had erected in the boat was a little thing, probably not even five meters high.
Yet the mast on whose yard the twins stood towered so high it seemed ready to bear them up among the stars.
As Sakuya raised his gaze, it seemed to extend smoothly and endlessly, receding—while their figures alone remained forever in view. This defied reason. Was he dreaming?

source.japanese:
あるいは本当にそうなのかも知れない。
　痛くて、ぎざぎざに尖って重い。爛れそうなほどの灼熱に、凍りついてしまいそうに冷たくて。
　それら全てを綯[な]い交ぜにした情動が、朔屋の身の裡にどろどろぐるぐると渦巻き、とぐろを巻き、おらび狂う。
　帆桁に乗った二人の姿が朔屋にもたらしたのは、身を薄く鋭い刃で切り刻まれるような、赤熱した金属を内臓に押し当てられるような、耐えがたい焦燥と喪失感、なのに───
source.english:
Perhaps he truly was. Painful, jagged, heavy.
Hot enough to blister, cold enough to freeze.
All those emotions twisted together within him, churning thickly, coiling and raging.
The pair upon the yard filled Sakuya with unbearable impatience and loss, as though fine, sharp blades were slicing his body, as though red-hot metal had been pressed against his organs. Yet—

source.japanese: それら暗く辛い、痛いほどの情動の渦に包まれるのが、どこか心地好く、身を委ねれば押し寄せるのは哀しみ、それも溶岩のように焦がし融[と]かすのではなく、清冽な流れの中に身を置いたかの、晴れやかな心地さえ伴って。
source.english: There was something pleasant in being enveloped by that dark, agonizing whirl of feeling. Yielding to it, he felt sorrow come over him, not scorching and melting like lava, but with something almost serene, as though he stood in a clear, pure stream.

source.japanese:
それは、死に別れてしまった人と夢の中で再会して、生ある時に語り残した事を全て語り終え、比世に残された者は彼の人の死を受け入れて、彼世に旅立った人は生者への未練なく、今度はお互いに全てを受け入れて、また別れを迎える時の心地だ。
　哀しい、悔しい、辛い、怖い。
　けれども。別れを受け入れよう。
source.english:
The feeling of meeting someone lost to death in a dream, and saying everything left unsaid in life. The one remaining in this world accepts the other's death; the one who has departed has no lingering attachment to the living. This time, both accept everything as they part again.
Sad. Bitter. Painful.
Frightening. Yet let us accept the parting.

target.text: Sakuya crawled out as if launched by something, and the sight that met his eyes was that of the twins standing on top of the mast of the boat, perched on the yard, motionless. A view that was mysterious, odd, as well as magnificently beautiful.

Atop the yard they stood, beneath a night sky so brimming with stars that were he to clap his hands together but once, it seemed as if that tiny impact alone would render them into pearls raining down upon him, and despite the uncertain footing, they didn't waver in the slightest, their entire bodies steeped in the celestial light of the stars, golden locks flowing softly in the wind.

The mast standing atop the boat was only a modest thing, at most reaching a height of five metres, and yet. What the twins stood atop seemed towering, a mast so grand it could well set sail for the very stars themselves. It was as if the higher Sakuya's gaze travelled, the longer it continued to smoothly stretch upwards, endlessly, growing ever more distant, and yet in spite of that, the twins always remained directly in the center of his vision; it just didn't make any sense, so perhaps he was dreaming?

Or perhaps it truly was real. It hurt, heavy and jagged. A heat so scorching he felt sore and inflamed, a cold so severe he was about to freeze over. All those emotions that had blended together continued to swirl around thickly within Sakuya, twisting into coils, shrieking with delirium. What the sight of the two standing atop that yard brought him was an almost unbearable feeling of burning frustration and loss, as if his body was being mangled by thin, sharp blades, like red-hot metal was being pushed against his heart, and yet───

The maelstrom of transitory emotion was so dark and painful it hurt him, and yet it somehow felt comfortable, and as he surrendered himself to the flow of melancholy rushing over him, it did not char or melt him like lava, no, it even brought to him a feeling of bracing clearness, as if he had immersed himself within a pure, refreshing stream

It was the feeling of a reunion within a dream with somebody taken from one by death, and after speaking of all the matters that were left unspoken during life, the one left behind in the world of the living accepted that other person's death, the one who had departed for the realm of the dead held no lingering regrets for the living; it was another final parting, this time shaped by mutual acceptance of everything. Miserable, frustrating, painful, scary. Nevertheless. They would accept the farewell.

source.japanese:
二人を振り仰ぐ朔屋が、夢中での別れを想うたのは、声なき声で囁き交わすその姿が、自らの裡よりおんもらとした光を放っているばかりか、その輪郭から燐光の粒を振り零し、まるでこの現界から遠く離れていこうかとする、霊質の存在であるかのようだったから。
　二人が振り零す光の粒、情交の極みに肌から湧き立たせた、あの不思議で精妙な光輝の粒子。高みから、星の粉のように朔屋へと降り注ぐ。
source.english:
Looking up at the pair, Sakuya thought of such a dream farewell because they seemed spiritual beings about to depart far from this world. Whispering together in voiceless voices, they not only gave off a soft light from within but spilled phosphorescent grains from their outlines.
Those grains—the strange, exquisite radiance that had welled from their skin at the height of coupling—fell from above upon him like powdered stars.

source.japanese:
ああ、双子の一方が、憧れに満ちて前[さき]を指し示す。
　ああ、かたわれが、感に堪[た]えかねたかのように強く頷[うなず]き返して、前を見つめる、眼差しを充たすのもやはり憧れの光で。
　満天下の星の下二人は、全身に星の光を浴びて、かつ自らもきらきら光の粒を振り零し、目にした者が我知らず涙してしまう程に綺麗で、幻想的で。
source.english:
Ah. One twin pointed ahead, full of longing. Ah.
Her other half nodded strongly, as if overwhelmed, and looked ahead with that same yearning light in her eyes. Beneath a sky full of stars,
bathed in their light and scattering bright grains of their own, the two were so beautiful, so dreamlike, that anyone seeing them might weep without knowing why.

source.japanese:
こうやって檣[マスト]の、帆桁の上に灯る火を、朔屋は知っている。
　それは、一つの現象にして、一つの伝説。
source.english:
Sakuya knew the fire that shone like this upon a mast's yard.
A phenomenon, and a legend.

target.text: As Sakuya looked up at the two, perhaps the reason his mind was drawn to thoughts of parting ways in a dream was because, from their figures exchanging wordless whispers, not only were they emitting a faintly shimmering radiance from within, phosphorescent motes of pale light were being shed from their silhouettes, as if they were slipping away from the realm of reality, like some manner of spiritual existence.

Ah, one of the twins, brimming with yearning, points to what lies ahead. Ah, the other half, as if unable to withstand the emotion within her, nods forcefully in return, gazing forwards, her eyes likewise filled with the light of longing. The two standing beneath the star-filled heavens that blanketed the world, entire bodies bathed in starlight, themselves scattering glittering beads of light besides, a beauty so pure and ethereal that it drew unbidden tears from any who beheld them.
A flame lit atop a mast, a yard, like this was one Sakuya knew of. It was at once a phenomenon, and a legend born from it.

source.japanese: その名も、セントエルモの火、名づく。
source.english: Its name: St. Elmo's fire.

target.text: And the name it was given was St. Elmo's fire.

source.japanese:
悪天候時に、静電気が尖った物体に発生させるコロナ放電、檣頭電光といってしまえばそれまで。
　けれども船乗り達は、そんな賢しげな原理を聞いたところで、セントエルモの火はセントエルモの火だと、自分達が泥[なず]んだ伝説に重きを置く。
source.english:
Corona discharge produced by static electricity on pointed objects in bad weather. Call it masthead electricity,
and that was that. Yet sailors, hearing such clever explanations, still insisted that St. Elmo's fire was St. Elmo's fire. They valued the legend to which they clung.

source.japanese:
海の一大難所である喜望峰を越える際、嵐に軋み苦しむ船の檣[マスト]上に、不思議の火が灯る事がある。暴風雨の中に掻[か]き消される事もなく灯り続けるその光を、船乗りは凶兆とも懼[おそ]れ、瑞兆とも喜ぶ。
　セント・エルモの灯───
　一つで現れた時は悪い兆しだという。
　二つで現れた時は、航海の安全を約束するという。
source.english:
Passing the Cape of Good Hope, one of the sea's great perils, sailors sometimes saw a mysterious fire light upon the mast of a ship creaking and suffering in a storm. Undimmed by wind and rain, it burned on. They feared it as an ill omen,
rejoiced in it as a good one.
St. Elmo's light.
One light, they said, meant evil. Two promised a safe voyage.

target.text: During inclement weather, a corona discharge would be induced around a tapered object by a field of static electricity, and if one were to dismiss it as a mere masthead electrical discharge, then that would be the end of it. However, no matter how clever-sounding the theory behind it might be, were sailors to hear that, they would simply respond with "St. Elmo's fire is just St. Elmo's fire", stubbornly holding dear the legends that they themselves had grown accustomed to.

When crossing the Cape of Good Hope, the most perilous pass at sea, atop the ship's mast creaking and groaning in the storm, a mysterious flame is lit. A light that is not drowned out in the raging rainstorm but continues to burn on, seen by sailors as both an omen of evil to be feared as well as a herald of good to be rejoiced. St. Elmo's fire─── Said to be an ill omen when appearing as one. Said to promise safe passage when appearing as two.

source.japanese:
朔屋は、双子が二人で揃っている時の、方位と位置に関する知覚力を想った。
　朔屋は、双子が一人に引き離された時の、彼女を狂わし苦しめる惑乱と不安感を想った。
source.english:
Sakuya thought of the twins' perception of direction and position when they were together.
He thought of the bewilderment and anxiety that tormented and maddened a twin left alone.

source.japanese: そして、シサムとキサラを、聖なる一対の存在として他から遠ざけ、自分達の守護として封じこめようとしていたいう北の邑[ムラ]の人々を想った。
source.english: And he thought of the people of that northern village, who had reportedly kept Sisam and Kisara apart from others as a sacred pair, seeking to confine them as their guardians.

source.japanese:
シサムとキサラ、双子の二人。
　彼女達は恐らく───
　北の邑[ムラ]の人々は、それを知っていて───
source.english:
Sisam and Kisara, the twin pair.
Perhaps they were—
And the northern villagers had known—

source.japanese:
双子の一人が、僅かに下界へと視線を降ろす。嵐に波濤逆巻く航路に難渋する航海者に、正しく安全な道を指し示すかのように。
　双子の一人が、星の位置を確かめて、かたわれに囁く。激浪の中、挫けずに怯まずに海を越えて新たな地を目指す、航海者達へ賛嘆の念を交えつつ。
　きらきらと、光の燐粉を撒きながら。
source.english:
One twin lowered her eyes a little toward the world below, as though showing a true, safe passage to voyagers struggling through storm-churned seas.
One checked the stars' positions and whispered to her other half, with admiration for voyagers who crossed the violent waves without faltering or flinching, seeking new land.
Scattering bright, phosphorescent dust.

source.japanese:
けれど朔屋は、二人の光輝に満ちた姿に、何故か切なくやりきれない嘆きを禁じえなかったのである。
　それは、確かに尊[とうと]く気高い務めではあろう。だが、ただ航海者達の航路を護る為だけに存在し続けなければならないとしたなら、それはあまりに孤独で、寂しい境涯ではないだろうか。
source.english:
Yet seeing their radiant forms, Sakuya could not suppress a strange, heartbreaking grief.
Certainly it must be a noble, exalted duty. But if they had to exist solely to guard the voyagers' passage, was that not too solitary, too lonely a fate?

source.japanese:
どれだけ航海者達を導こうとも、その火は人間に交わる事を知らず、ただ檣[マスト]の上に隔絶して灯り続けるだけだ。
　航海者達が方位のよすがとして見あげる星に、もし心あるとしたなら何を想うのだろうか。人間達の営みなど、星々はなんら関心を持たず、ただの宙空の己の位置で輝き続けるだけ。それならばまだよし。
　セントエルモの火が航海者を導くのは、それが定められた役割だからであり、人間に対して愛着を示しているからではない、のであるなら、まだよし。
source.english:
However many voyagers it guided, that fire knew nothing of mingling with humankind. It could only burn apart, high upon a mast.
If the stars sailors looked up to for their bearings had hearts, what would they think? If they cared nothing for human lives and simply went on shining in their appointed places in the sky, well and good.
If St. Elmo's fire guided voyagers because it was its ordained role, not because it felt affection for humankind—well and good.

source.japanese:
下界と交わった精霊は精霊ではない───
　北の邑[ムラ]の人々は、それを知って双子を他者から遠ざけ、封じこめようとしたのではないだろうか。
　この世に生を受けたその時より、人界より隔絶され、守護精霊としての定めを負わされた二人。それは、人界からの離脱を意味していないだろうか。
　人の世に生まれ落ちて、けれど人々の間に立ち混じる事は出来ない。人並みの幸せ、とは言うけれど、それを渇望しても得られないものには、どれだけ眩しく見えるだろう。
source.english:
A spirit that mingled with the lower world ceased to be a spirit.
Had the northern villagers known this? Was that why they tried to keep the twins apart from others, to shut them away?
Separated from the human realm from the moment of their birth, burdened with the destiny of guardian spirits: did that not amount to exile from humanity?
Born into the world of people, yet unable to stand among them. Ordinary happiness—how dazzling must it look to someone who longed for it and could never have it?

source.japanese:
信天翁号の船員達は、過去を語らない。
　だが、あの奇妙な襤褸船に至り、そしてそこで航海を続けるからには相応の理由があるのだろう。双子も、朔屋には想像できないような紆余曲折の果てにあの船にいるのではないか。
source.english:
The Albatross's crew did not speak of their pasts.
Yet each must have had some reason to come to that peculiar ragged ship, and another to continue voyaging aboard her. Perhaps the twins, too, had reached her only after twists and turns Sakuya could not imagine.

source.japanese:
そんな彼女達が、しばしば口にするようになった言葉。世界への居心地の悪さ。
　自分達を閉じこめてくるような、たまらない不快感があるのだという。
source.english:
The words they had lately begun saying so often: their discomfort in the world.
An unbearable, unpleasant feeling that it was shutting them in.

source.japanese: それは、本来の定めに従おうとしない双子への、この世界の摂理、根本の法則、そういった冠絶したものからの、圧力なのだとしたら？
source.english: What if that was pressure from the world's providence, its fundamental laws—something supreme—upon the twins who refused their original destiny?

source.japanese: セント・エルモの灯として存在し続ける事を否み続ける限り、世界は無間の牢獄と化して二人を鎖[くさり]し続ける。世界という牢獄に囚われた者が、何を望むのだろう───
source.english: So long as they kept refusing to exist as St. Elmo's light, the world would become an eternal prison, keeping them chained. What would someone imprisoned within the world itself desire—?

target.text: Sakuya thought: of when the twins were together, their sensory ability related to direction and location. Sakuya thought: of when one of the twins had been torn from the other, the delirium and anxiety that would drive her mad and torment her so.

And then, he thought of the people of that northern settlement, those who had treated Shisamu and Kisara as a sacred pair, kept them away from others, attempted to contain them as their own guardians.
Shisamu and Kisara, two twins. The girls were in all likelihood─── And the people of that northern settlement, they knew as much and───

One of the twins slightly lowered her gaze to the world below. As if showing the right and safe path forwards to a mariner struggling through a stormy sea of surging waves. One of the twins ascertained the position of the stars, then whispered to her other half. Offering quiet words of admiration for the sailors who, amidst raging waves, would press on undaunted, without losing heart, crossing the seas in pursuit of new lands. Sprinkling sparkling specks of scintillation all the while.

However, as Sakuya beheld their forms suffused with splendour, without knowing why, it struck him as unbearably heartrending, and he was unable to suppress his grief. It was certainly an exalted and noble duty. But if they could only live on as beings that merely existed to safeguard the passage of sailors, would that not be an existence far too solitary, too desolate?

No matter how many sailors it would show the way, that flame knew not how to dwell among humankind; it was simply isolated atop the mast, continuing to burn away by itself. If the stars that sailors look up to in search of a means of guidance had a heart, then what would they feel? The stars would hold no interest in human endeavours; they merely shine on from their place in the heavens. If that was all this was, it would be acceptable. If the act of guiding sailors was a role that St. Elmo's fire was destined to fulfill, if it wasn't a display of their affection for humanity, it would be tolerable.

A spirit that mingles with the mortal realm below is no spirit at all─── Did the people of that northern settlement know that, and so kept the twins away from others, attempted to confine them? Ever since they were born into this world, they had been secluded from the world of man, been made to carry the fate of being guardian spirits on their shoulders. Would that not imply leaving behind the world of man? Born into the world of man, yet unable to truly stand amongst them. Ordinary happiness, or so it might be called, but for someone unable to ever obtain it, no matter how desperately they craved it, how dazzlingly radiant a thing must it seem.

The crew of the Albatross speak not of their past. However, to have ended up aboard that strange, battered ship, and then choose to keep sailing with it, there must be a befitting reason. Could the twins not also have arrived at that ship after a long journey of twists and turns that Sakuya couldn't even begin to imagine?
And those girls, there were words that they had come to speak more and more frequently. Feeling ill at ease in this world. An unbearable discomfort, as if they were being imprisoned, they said.

If he supposed that it was a pressure, one that originated from the supreme laws of this world, its fundamental principles, bearing down on the twins who did not yield to their intrinsic destiny, then what?

For as long as they continue to deny their existence as St. Elmo's fire, the world becomes a perpetual prison, endlessly shackling them. What could those held captive in the prison that is this world possibly wish for───

source.japanese:
一なる、三者。三位一体者。
　一人一人は他と変わるところのない人間でも、その三人が揃い、ある条件を満たすと昇華していくという、一揃いの不思議な者達。
　二つの灯は、三つのものに。
source.english:
The Three Who Are One. The Triune One.
A mysterious set of beings, each individually a person no different from anyone else, who would undergo sublimation when all three came together and fulfilled certain conditions.
Two lights becoming three beings.

source.japanese:
シサムか、キサラか、かたわれがかたわれに前を指し示して、憧れに満ちて、語りかける。指し示す先に待ち受けているもの、二人が望むもの。
　それがなにかは朔屋に完全には理解し得ないだろうけれど。
　ただ、その求める先に行き着いてしまった時に双子は、自分は。
　もう二度と、この世の中では相会う事はないのであろうと。
　朔屋が抱いたのは、予感とか兆しとかそんなあやふやな感覚ではなく、はっきりとした確信だった。
source.english:
Sisam or Kisara—one half pointed ahead and spoke to the other, full of longing. What awaited where she pointed,
what the two desired, Sakuya could probably never understand completely.
He was sure of one thing.
If they reached that destination, the twins and he would never meet again in this world.
Not a vague foreboding or omen. A clear certainty.

source.japanese:
だから朔屋は、帆桁上の二人を呼び留めようと、この世界に留め置こうと、それが傲慢かどうかは判らない、ただただ行ってしまおうとしている二人が切なくて、狂おしくて、声を張り上げた。
　
　張り上げて、叫んで、喚いて、見苦しく騒いで足掻いた───のに。
　
　膠漬けにでもされたのか、一音も舌は言葉を発さず、手足は二人に向かって腕の一振り、踏み出す足の一歩もなく。
source.english:
So he tried to call the pair back from the yard, to keep them in this world. Whether that was arrogance, he did not know. He was simply heartbroken, maddened by their going, and raised his voice.
Raised it, shouted, screamed, struggled and made an ugly scene.
Yet—as though soaked in glue, his tongue uttered not one sound. Neither hand nor foot moved toward them, not a wave, not a step.

source.japanese:
それまでは朔屋に望見を許していたのも、それが最後の、別れの一時だったからと言わんばかりに、視界の中で二人の姿は遠ざかりゆき、何より悔しく情けなかったのが、遠ざかる二人を見送る事が、浄らかな門出を見送ってやれるような、哀しくも晴れやかな喜びさえ伴っていた事。
　置いていかれる者に、せめてもの慰めとして、流し続けても身を損なう事のない澄んだ涙と、嘆き続けても心を萎え腐らせる事のない、浄化された哀しみが贈り遺されていったかのように。
source.english:
Until then he had been allowed to gaze upon them, as though it had been a final moment of farewell. Now their figures receded within his sight. Most bitter and shameful of all, watching them go brought a sad yet serene joy, as if he were seeing them off upon a pure new beginning.
As a last comfort to the one left behind, they seemed to have bequeathed clear tears he could shed endlessly without harm, and a purified sorrow he could grieve forever without his heart withering and rotting.

source.japanese: 人生の、短い長いに関わらず、替え難い宝となるのは想い出だ。去りゆく双子が与えてくれる想い出は、繊細な酒のように、新しきうちは舌触りも生々しく朔屋を押し包もう。けれどそのきついくらいの味わいが、より記憶の中でこの想い出を特別な位置にと押し上げる。だから、やがて歳月のうちに古びても、別れの想い出は消して失われることなく、時間の経過と共に、流れに運ばれる石のように角を丸くして、まだ若かった頃の自分では受け入れきれなかった出来事の機微も見えてくるだろう。味わいも熟[な]れて凝縮されて、老いた舌には程良い酔いを染みこませてくれるだろう。
source.english: Whether a life was long or short, memories became its irreplaceable treasure. The memory the departing twins gave him would be like a delicate wine: while new, its rawness upon the tongue would envelop Sakuya. That almost harsh savor would secure it a special place in remembrance. Thus, though it aged with the years, the memory of parting would never be lost. Time would round its edges like a stone carried by a stream, and reveal subtleties in the event that his younger self could not accept. Its flavor would mature and concentrate, bringing an old tongue just the right intoxication.

target.text: One as three. The Triune Being. Though individually they are no different from any other person, when the three unite and fulfill a certain condition, they sublimate: a set of mysterious people. Though it would be two flames becoming three.

Was it Shisamu, or was it Kisara? One half pointed the way forward to the other, full of yearning, then began to speak. What awaited them in the direction she showed, it was something the two of them wished for. Whatever that was, it was probably something that Sakuya was completely incapable of understanding. However, by the time the twins reached the destination they so longed for, he would─── Likely never meet them again in this world. What Sakuya harboured within himself was nothing so vague a sensation as a premonition or an omen, it was a crystal clear conviction.

Even as Sakuya tried to call out to the two atop the yard and stop them, tried to keep them in this world, he knew not if he was being arrogant, it was just that the very notion of the two leaving him was suffocating, maddening, and so he raised his voice. He raised his voice, shouted, screamed, was a disgraceful mess as he floundered about───and yet. Had he been dipped in a vat of glue or something, for his tongue would not utter a single word, there was not a single wave of his arm, nor a single step taken towards the two.

Hitherto, Sakuya had been permitted to gaze upon them from afar, but as if to say that this was the final moment of parting, their figures receded from his view, and what stung the most, what was most pitiful of all, was that watching the two of them go brought with it a sorrowful yet bright joy, as if he was sending them off on a pure and noble journey. As the only consolation for the one left behind, even as crystalline tears continued to flow down his cheeks, they would not harm his body; even as his lamenting continued, his heart would not wither with despondency, as if he had been granted a parting gift of purified grief.

The most irreplaceable treasure of a life, be it short or long, is memories. The memory that the departing twins were giving him wholly enveloped Sakuya, like a delicate liquor that burns the tongue with a vivid bite while still fresh to the senses. But the very sharpness of that flavour uplifts the memory, enshrines it in a special place amidst his gallery of recollections.

Therefore, even should it grow old and faded with time, his memory of their parting would never be erased or lost, and in tandem with the passing of time, the edges would be rounded off like a rock carried down a stream, and even the subtle intricacies of what he was unable to accept in his younger days would eventually reveal themselves to him. The taste would mature and condense, bringing with it just the right degree of mellow intoxication to his aged tongue.

source.japanese:
───そんな───
　想い出など！
source.english:
—To hell—
with memories like that!

source.japanese: どれだけ甘美で懐かしくあろうとも、想い出は所詮想い出、触れない。抱く事も出来ない。想い出は想い出、たとえ失われる事がなくとも、それ以上の未来には進み得ない。共にあればこそ、泣き、笑い、怒りをぶつけ合い、喜びを共にする事も出来る。
source.english: However sweet and fond, memories were only memories. Untouchable. He could not hold them. Memories remained memories; even if never lost, they could not advance into any further future. Only together could they weep, laugh, rage at each other, share their joy.

source.japanese: だから───
source.english: So—

source.japanese: 朔屋は───
source.english: Sakuya—

source.japanese: 舌先も、指先も、微動だにさせる事すら出来ずとも、心はこうして震えている、だからひたすらに念じる、双子への想いだけで心を充たす、その内圧に耐えかねて、身体が裡から弾けてしまったとしても何を悔やもう。精神だけでも肉体の枠を超えて飛翔させ、去りゆく双子に追いすがろう。
source.english: Though he could not stir so much as the tip of his tongue or a finger, his heart still trembled. He willed it relentlessly, filling his heart with nothing but the twins. What would there be to regret if the pressure burst his body from within? Let his spirit alone fly beyond the confines of flesh and pursue them as they went.

source.japanese:
念じた、願った、また希[こいねが]った！
　これまでの生涯の中で、未だかつてないほどに全身全霊をこめて───
source.english:
He willed it, wished it, pleaded again!
With all his body and soul, more fiercely than ever in his life—

source.japanese: なのに。
source.english: And yet.

source.japanese:
所詮、心は肉体を脱ぎ捨て飛翔する事など叶わず。
　結局、双子は朔屋を置き去りに虚空へと去りゆきて。
source.english:
In the end, his heart could not cast off his body and fly.
In the end, the twins left Sakuya behind and departed into the void.

target.text: ───No─── As if mere memory could ever!

No matter how pleasantly sweet the nostalgia may taste, memories were but memories, untouchable. They could not be embraced. Memories would remain memories, and even if they may never be lost, they could never step into the future. It was precisely because they were together that their tears, their laughter, and their anger could clash, that they could share in their joy.
Therefore───
Sakuya───

Though neither the tip of his tongue nor his fingertips could so much as twitch, his heart trembled still, and so he poured his everything into a silent prayer, filled his heart with nothing but his feelings for the twins; he could barely endure the pressure building inside, but even should his body burst from within, what could he possibly have to regret? His soul alone would surely transcend the limits of his flesh and soar high in pursuit of the departing twins.
He prayed, he wished, and implored once more! With more than he had ever given in all his days, pouring all his heart and soul into it───
And yet.
Ultimately, the soul could not shed its mortal shell and take flight. In the end, the twins left Sakuya behind as they set off into the empty sky.

source.japanese: 絶叫が戻ったのは、満天の星空の彼方に、二人が消え去ってしまった後で───
source.english: His scream returned only after the two had vanished beyond the star-filled sky—

target.text: His screams returned to him only after the two had vanished beyond the starlit canopy───

source.japanese: 二人が振り零していた光の粒も失せ、短艇の檣[マスト]は急拵えのささやかな帆柱の姿を取り戻し、みすぼらしい帆を支える帆桁に乗った者の姿など見えない。
source.english: Their falling grains of light disappeared too. The boat's mast regained its modest, hastily fashioned shape. No one stood upon the yard holding up that shabby sail.

source.japanese:
見えるのは───
　帆桁の船縁に張り渡した天幕の裡から、きょとんと怪訝そうな貌[かお]を覗かせている双子の頭二つ。
　朔屋が騒ぎたてたによって眠りを破られたのか、同時に欠伸を漏らして、寒空の下立ち尽くす青年へ咎めるような視線をくれてから、船縁に顎を乗せてことんと傾げてみせた様は、巣穴から顔を出した海豹の仔のような、妙な愛嬌を湛えた眺めではあったけれど、朔屋は安堵のあまりその場にへたりこんだ。
source.english:
What he could see—
Two heads, the twins peering out from beneath the canvas stretched from yard to gunwale, looking puzzled and blank.
Apparently awakened by his uproar, they yawned together, gave the young man standing in the cold night a reproachful look, then rested their chins on the gunwale and tipped their heads. A curiously endearing sight, like seal pups peeking from a den. Sakuya sank down where he stood, overwhelmed by relief.

source.japanese:
夢か現かといえば、夢の方なのだろうが。
　氷原に手をつき、悪夢から覚めた時特有の荒い息に上下させる朔屋の肩から、零れ落ちたものがある。
　氷雪の上にころころと転がって、数度輝滅してから飛散して消えたそれは、帆桁の上から双子が振りまいていた光の粒。
　夢が現実に浸出してきたのだろうか。
　それでは、先ほどまでの光景が、夢か現なのかと問わば───朔屋には、もうその区別が怪しくなっていた。
source.english:
Dream or waking reality? Presumably a dream.
As Sakuya braced his hands upon the ice, his shoulders heaving with the ragged breath peculiar to waking from a nightmare, something fell from one of them.
It rolled across the snow and ice, flickered several times, then scattered and vanished.
One of the grains of light the twins had spilled from the yard. Had the dream seeped into reality?
Then, if asked whether that scene had been dream or waking—Sakuya could no longer trust the distinction.

target.text: The motes of light the twins had scattered also faded away, the boat's mast regained its humble, makeshift form, and no figures could be seen standing atop the yard supporting its tattered sail.
What could be seen was─── A pair of twin faces peeking out from beneath the tent of sailcloth rigged across the yard to the gunwale, staring at him with gazes that seemed both dazed and perplexed.

Perhaps their sleep had been disturbed by the racket Sakuya had made, for they both yawned in unison, and after sending a rebuking look at the young man standing stock-still under the freezing skies, the way they then rested their chins on the gunwale with a soft thud and tilted their heads was like little badger cubs sticking their heads out from their sett, a sight radiating a peculiar charm, but the overwhelming relief Sakuya felt made him sink to the floor right where he stood.

If asked whether it was dream or reality, it was probably a dream, but. As Sakuya put his hands to the frozen ground, from his shoulders heaving with the ragged breathing unique to waking from a nightmare, something fell. What rolled across the ice and snow, flickered with light several times, then scattered into nothing, was one of the motes of light the twins had strewn from atop the yard. Was the dream bleeding into reality? In that case, if he were asked whether the sight he had witnessed until just before was dream or reality, then───to Sakuya, the distinction between either had begun to blur.

source.japanese:
───明くる日の事。
　氷結した空気に乱反射する朝陽の中に、北限氷土の晩秋の風が氷原を吹き靡[なび]ける響きがその日は妙に寂しく胸に堪[こた]え朝。
　朔屋は双子にこれからの事をどうするべきか、どう切り出そうか、起きがけの尿意を帆掛け橇からちと離れたところで遣りながら考えても、いい案は出てこない。
　出てくるのは小便ばかり、氷原の白い面には、ナニを血迷ったモノか、
source.english:
The next day. Morning sunlight scattered through the frozen air.
That morning, the sound of the Northern Ice Wastes' late-autumn wind sweeping the ice struck his heart with a peculiar loneliness.
A short distance from the sailing sled, relieving his waking bladder, Sakuya considered what they should do next and how to raise it with the twins. No good ideas came out. Only piss.
In yellow upon the white ice, for some mad reason, he had written—

target.text: ───It happened on a bright day. Beneath the morning sun refracting diffusely through the freezing air, the rippling sound of the late autumn wind sweeping across the northernmost ice fields struck Sakuya's chest with a peculiar loneliness; it was that sort of morning. What was it Sakuya ought to do about these twins from now on, how should he break the ice; he stepped a little away from the sail-driven sledge to answer nature's call first thing in the morning, but no matter how hard he thought as he tended to his business, no good ideas surfaced. All that did surface was piss, together with some manner of lunacy on the white surface of the ice field,

source.japanese: 『いばり　いばり　おおいばり』
source.english: PISS, PISS, PISS WITH PRIDE.

source.japanese:
と黄色く記されてあって、よくまあ途中で途切れずにすんだものだし、この時季でよかっただろうの、これでもっと寒い時季だったら、逸物がえらい事になったはず。そもそも垂れる端から凍ったろう。
　多分ゆうべ、普段はいばっているシサムが、情事の最中とはいえ盛大にやらかしてくれたのが、青年のろくでもないインスピレーションを、更にどうしようもないベクトルに刺激したモノと見える。
source.english:
Quite a feat to manage it without interruption. Lucky it was this time of year. A colder season would have done something terrible to his cock; the stream would probably have frozen as it fell.
Last night's spectacular mishap, during lovemaking though it was, had apparently sent his worthless inspiration in a still more hopeless direction. Sisam, ordinarily so full of pride, had provided it.

target.text: 『urine liquid ego golden pride』 (TN: This is a repetition of the pun from the last chapter where Sakuya contemplated drinking piss. The word ibari can be read as "尿", meaning urine, and "威張り", meaning pride, boasting, arrogance, etc.)

So it was recorded in yellow; while it was impressive that he hadn't run empty partway through, it was probably a good thing it was this time of year, for had it been a colder season, his manhood would surely have found itself in serious trouble. It would like as not have frozen solid after the very first drop. It was probably last night, when Shisamu, usually all puffed up with pride, managed to make a spectacular mess of herself, even if it was in the midst of a passionate moment, which had provoked this young man's already misguided inspiration down an even more hopeless trajectory, or so it seemed.

source.japanese:
すっきりして帆掛け橇に戻ろうとしたら、双子はいかなる心変わりか、朔屋を置いて
帆掛けして、橇を帆走させようとしているところであり、朔屋は半泣きで追いかけて、ようやく艫の船縁に間に合ったの顛末、乗りこんでみると、シサムが氷原の冷たさを面に移したような厳しい顔で、キサラが片手拝みに頭を下げてくるところ。
　おまけにシサムは自ら、キサラはシサムに命令されてで、口をきかない令が布告されているらしく、朔屋にはちいとも訳が……いや、次第になんとなく察せられた。
source.english:
Feeling better, he turned back to the sled. Whatever had changed their minds, the twins were setting sail without him.
Half in tears, Sakuya chased it and only just reached the stern gunwale. Once aboard, he found Sisam with a severe face that seemed to reflect the ice field's cold, and Kisara bowing her head with one hand raised in apology.
Moreover, a ban on speaking appeared to have been declared: Sisam had imposed it on herself and ordered Kisara to obey. He had no idea why… No. Gradually, he began to suspect.

target.text: Feeling refreshed, as he returned to the sail-driven sledge, perhaps the twins had experienced some manner of change of heart, for they had put up the sail without Sakuya, and they were about to glide off on the sledge; thus began an episode of Sakuya chasing them down while half in tears until he finally caught up to the ship's gunwale, and as he tried climbing over, the look on Shisamu's face was so frigid, it was as if she had swapped her very face with the ice he stood on, while Kisara lowered her head with one hand raised in silent prayer.

On top of that, it seemed Shisamu herself refused to talk, and Kisara had apparently been directly ordered by Shisamu to stay her tongue, and with that order proclaimed, Sakuya had not the slightest clue what……no, gradually, it somehow began to come together in his head.

source.japanese:
短艇の荷袋の上に置かれていたのは、朔屋の望遠鏡。そしてキサラのジェスチュア。
　まずシサムを指して、彼女が望遠鏡を使っている仕草。
　ははあ、と朔屋は頷[うなず]いた。どうやらしまい忘れた望遠鏡を、シサムが悪戯したのであろう。それは、まあいい。
　次にキサラは、朔屋を指して、青年の立ち小便の仕草と字を書いている尻の振りを、氷原をがたがた揺れながら走る橇の上で実に器用に再現して見せた。
　それで朔屋は、短艇の中の、自分の発言が喪われたのを知ったという。朔屋はそれでかえって気が楽になった、これから先の事など、二人に好きにさせればいい、自分はついていくだけと、他人任せの怠惰にも程がある。
source.english:
Sakuya's telescope lay upon a baggage sack in the boat. Kisara began to gesture.
First she pointed to Sisam and mimed looking through it. Ah, Sakuya nodded. Apparently he had forgotten to put the telescope away, and Sisam had amused herself with it. Fine.
Next Kisara pointed at him and, with remarkable dexterity aboard a sled jolting over the ice, reproduced his stance as he pissed and the sway of his ass as he wrote.
Thus Sakuya learned that he had forfeited any voice in the boat's decisions. That actually came as a relief. Let the twins decide the road ahead; he would merely follow. There were limits to indolent dependence on others. He exceeded them.

target.text: Resting on top of the boat's seabag was Sakuya's telescope. And then there was Kisara's gesturing. First she pointed at Shisamu, then gestured as if she was using the telescope. A-ha, Sakuya nodded. It seemed that Shisamu must have been messing around with the telescope that he had forgotten to put away. Well, that was fine. Next, Kisara pointed to Sakuya, then imitated the mannerisms of the young man's outdoors urination and shook her ass as if writing letters with it; given this was done atop a sledge in motion, shaking and rattling as it slid across the ice field, it was a truly dextrous recreation.

And with that, Sakuya realized that he had lost any place to speak aboard this small boat, but contrary to his expectations, that actually made him feel a sense of ease, for whatever came next, he figured that he would just let the two do as they pleased, he'd simply tag along; it was a passing of the buck so indolent it beggared belief.

source.japanese: そして、双子が選んだ道は、前進、前進、前進。シサムが目指していた先なのだが、ほとんど平板な氷原に、そこだけ円錐を置いたような、妙に小綺麗な形した山が佇立している。
source.english: And the course the twins chose was forward, forward, forward. Toward Sisam's destination: a strangely neat mountain standing upon the almost level ice field as though someone had set a cone there.

source.japanese: どうやらその山、地図上の指標地点と関わりがあるらしいと言うのがシサムの弁で、なんの話だっけか？　と朔屋は本気で首を傾げて二人に後ろ頭を張り手でやられた。
source.english: According to Sisam, the mountain apparently had something to do with the reference point on the chart. What was that about again? Sakuya genuinely cocked his head and received a slap on the back of it from each twin.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ。今ので思い出したけどさ、その話、
　まだ引っ張んの？
　もう俺ら、信天翁号降りちゃってんのに？」
source.english:
“Oh. That reminded me.
But are we still keeping that business going?
We've already left the Albatross.”

source.japanese:
朔屋、二人に左右からじとりと睨[にら]まれる。これはこれでと思うあたりがこの男の唯一の不屈の美点。
　シサム、キサラの二人からすれば、信天翁号から片方は職務さえ放り出して来たとはいえ、地図渡され目指せと言われた場所ならそこに行きたくなるのが航海士の性というもの。この男、本当に航海士としての教育受けたのかしらと蔑まれ、受けてませんと情けなく答えたり。
source.english:
They stared at him sourly from both sides. That he could find even this enjoyable was the man's sole indomitable virtue.
To Sisam and Kisara, wanting to reach a destination marked upon a chart was simply a navigator's nature—even if one of them had abandoned her duties aboard the Albatross to do it. Had this man really received any training as a navigator? they asked with contempt. No, he answered pathetically, he had not.

source.japanese: 近づくにつれ、地形の厳しさはいや増し、ついには帆掛け橇でも進めぬほど、岩あちこちに突き出ては氷に覆われる悪路が続く。三人はそれでも、自らの脚を頼みに、歩みを進めていくのだった。
source.english: As they approached, the terrain grew harsher, until even the sailing sled could not advance. Rocks thrust out everywhere, sheathed in ice. Still the three went on, relying upon their own legs.

target.text: Thus, the path the twins had chosen went onward, onward, ever onward. The destination Shisamu was heading for turned out to be a nearly featureless ice field, but as if someone had placed a cone just there by hand, there stood a single mountain, oddly neat in shape.

That mountain apparently had something to do with the point of reference on the map, at least according to Shisamu, and when Sakuya asked them to remind him what exactly they were talking about again, the back of his head, still tilted in genuine puzzlement, was met with a slap from the both of them.
【Naomasa】 「Aah. I only just remembered it now, but you meant that thing. We're still taking that on? Even though we've already gotten off the Albatross?」

Sakuya was met with a cold, accusatory stare from both left and right. The fact that he could still think this had its own appeal was this man's one indomitable virtue. From the perspective of Shisamu and Kisara, even if one half had abandoned her professional duties on the Albatross to come all the way here, when handed a map and told to head for a place, then it was simply in a navigator's nature to want to go there. This man, when asked with a sneer if he actually had ever received an education to become a navigator, could only pitifully admit that no, he hadn't.

As they drew closer, the terrain grew increasingly harsh, and eventually, only a treacherous path lay before them, covered in ice and with jagged rocks jutting out everywhere, to the point that they could no longer advance on the sail-driven sledge. Nevertheless, the three of them relied on their own legs, continuing to advance on foot.

source.japanese: うまく迫り出た岩の影に帆布転用して雪風しのぎの壁がわりにし、その中で三人、岩を背もたれに腰をかけ、毛布にくるんだ体を寄せ合う。
source.english: In the lee of a conveniently jutting rock, they put the sailcloth to use as a wall against wind and snow. Inside, the three sat with the rock for a backrest, drawing their blanket-wrapped bodies close.

source.japanese: 互いの温もり伝わって、特に朔屋にとっては暖房いらずの温かさ。しかし、こうしてなんとかその日の寝床は確保できても、路はいよいよ厳しさを増し、そこを徒歩で進めば疲労も著しい。
source.english: Warmth passed between them; for Sakuya especially, no heater was needed. They had somehow secured that night's bed, yet the way grew ever more severe, and walking it left them terribly tired.

target.text: They had managed to cleverly put the canvas sail to use as a makeshift wall rigged up behind a protruding rock, shielding them against the snow-laden wind, and in there, the three sat down with their backs leaning against the rock, wrapped up in a blanket and huddling together.

They shared their respective body heat, and for Sakuya in particular, it was warm enough that he didn't need a heater. However, even though they had somehow managed to secure a shelter to sleep in for the night, the path forward was only growing harsher, and the fatigue from having to trek it on foot was considerable.

source.japanese: そして何より深刻な問題はと言えば。
source.english: Most serious of all—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「帰りの食糧と水……どうしようか……」
source.english: “Food and water for the way back… What are we going to do…?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「んー、まあどうにかなると思う」
source.english: “Mm. Think we'll manage somehow.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そうだよ。だってあたしは、ここまで徒歩歩きだったんだから」
source.english: “Yeah. I walked all the way here, didn't I?”

source.japanese: 水と食料の残りいよいよ心許なくなってきたことだった。シサムを無事に見つける前の時点で、すでに帰り路の計算に破綻が見えかけていたのだが、めでたく三人合流あいなれば、減る蓄えの量も五割り増しとなるのは当たり前。そこからさらに、三人は前へと進んでいるのだから。
source.english: Their remaining water and food had grown increasingly scant. Even before they found Sisam safe, their calculations for the return journey had begun to fall apart. Once the three were happily reunited, consumption naturally rose by half. And still they continued farther forward.

target.text: And as for the most grave issue of them all.
【Naomasa】 「Food and water for the trip back…… what are we gonna do……」
【Kisara】 「Hmm, well, I think we'll manage one way or another.」
【Shisamu】 「That's right. Look, I managed to trek all this way by myself, right?」

Their dwindling supplies of food and water were finally becoming worryingly scarce. Before they'd succeeded in finding Shisamu, the calculations of the logistics for the trip back home were already on the verge of falling apart, but once the three had realized their joyous reunion, it was only natural that the rate at which their supplies dwindled would also jump by fifty percent. And even after that, the three of them still kept moving forwards.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……そうかな？　ううん、そうだな。
　三人なら、どうにかなるよな、きっと」
source.english:
“…Think so? Yeah, you're right.
With three of us, we'll manage somehow. Surely.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そういうこと。まあ、あたしら二人が本気だしゃあ、朔屋一人ぐらいの食い扶持、また鳥でも撃って、氷でも溶かして、なんとかなるよ」
source.english: “Exactly. If the two of us really try, feeding one Sakuya should be easy enough. Shoot another bird, melt some ice. We'll work it out.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まだ鉄砲の弾も、いくらか残ってるしさ」
source.english: “Still got a few bullets too.”

source.japanese: 答える声は明るく言葉もしごく暢気の範疇にあったとしても、袋開ける度減っていく食料とこの先の行程慮れば、いずれ途上で尽きるのははっきりしている。まさに冷たい方程式、それは三人ともわかってはいたのだが、心まで曇り冷えては一歩も先に進めなくなる。どうせ力尽きるなら前に進むのが双子の精神方向だった。
source.english: Their voices were bright, their words perfectly carefree. Yet looking at the food dwindling each time they opened the bag, considering the journey ahead, it was obvious they would run out somewhere on the road. A cold equation indeed. All three knew it. But if they let their hearts grow dark and cold as well, they could not advance a single step. If they were going to exhaust themselves anyway, the twins' instinct was to keep moving forward.

source.japanese: しかし、この日の食糧問題検討会、いつものように明るい無計画で締めてはみたものの、なんのはずみか、双子の思索は翳[かげ]りを帯びたらしい。
source.english: That day's council on the food problem ended in their usual cheerful lack of a plan. Yet by some turn or other, the twins' thoughts afterward seemed to darken.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Are you sure? No, it has to be fine. With the three of us, we'll make it work somehow, no doubt.」

【Shisamu】 「That's the spirit. Well, if the two of us got serious about it, we could probably keep someone like you fed, Sakuya, by hunting some more birds, or melting some ice. We'll make do somehow.」
【Kisara】 「We've still got some bullets left.」

Even if the voices that spoke to him in return were bright and their words fell squarely within the category of the exceedingly nonchalant, when he carefully considered how every time the bag was opened, the stash of supplies within it shrunk, as well as the journey still ahead of them, it was evident that they would eventually run out somewhere along the way. A truly chilling equation, and they all three understood that well enough, but if even their hearts grew dim and chilled, they would be unable to take another step forwards. If they were going to use up all their strength one way or another, they might as well just keep moving; such was the mentality of the twins.

However, after the meeting held on this day reviewing the issue surrounding their provisions, although they had wrapped it up with the usual cheerful lack of an actual plan, whatever could have brought it on, for the twins' thoughts seemed tinged with gloomy shadow.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「シサム……こんな風にさ、狭いところに押しこめられてると、昔の事、思い出さない？」
source.english: “Sisam… Being packed into a tight place like this, doesn't it remind you of back then?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……ちょっとだけ。
　でもあの頃の事はやだ。
　あんま、考えたくない」
source.english:
“…A little.
But I hate that time.
Don't want to think about it much.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それは、あたしだってそうなんだけど。
　でもあたしが言いたかったのは、
　そうじゃなくて……」
source.english:
“Me too.
But that's not what
I meant…”

source.japanese: しかし、キサラもそこで一度、言葉を区切る。誰にでもあろう記憶の禁忌に触れようか、近づこうかという気配。そして朔屋、この手の沈黙にはことさら弱い。
source.english: Kisara broke off there. She seemed to be approaching one of those forbidden places in memory that everyone has. Sakuya was particularly weak against this kind of silence.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Shisamu……you know, when we're crammed into a tight space like this, doesn't it bring back old memories?」
【Shisamu】 「……Just a little bit. But I don't like the memories from back then. Don't like thinking about it.」
【Kisara】 「Well, I feel the same way too. But that wasn't really what I was trying to say……」

However, Kisara also cut her words short there. There was a sense that they were nearing a taboo, brushing up against the forbidden memories that dwell within any and all. And then there was Sakuya, who was particularly bad at dealing with this kind of silence.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「な……もっとくっついてよ。
　なんか冷えてきたような気ぃしないか？」
source.english:
“Hey… Get closer.
Doesn't it feel like it's getting colder?”

source.japanese: と、かけた声、本人明るく振る舞ったつもりだろうが、残念ながら軽薄に響いたものの、双子の失笑はどこか気抜けて怪我の功名か。
source.english: He had plainly meant to sound cheerful. Unfortunately, he sounded frivolous. Yet the twins' laughter held a certain release; perhaps the blunder had worked in his favor.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋さぁ。あんた女好きのわりには、やっぱり気配りとか下手くそだよね。
　そんな、無理矢理話替えようとしなくってもいいのに」
source.english:
“Sakuya. For someone so fond of women, you really suck at being considerate.
You don't have to force the conversation somewhere else like that.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ずばりと言いよる。
　でもいいもんねぇーだ。
　口が下手だろうとなんだろうと」
source.english:
“…Straight to the point.
Well, I don't care.
Bad with words or whatever…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Hey……huddle up a little closer, would you? Doesn't it kind of feel like it's gotten a little colder?」

He called out to them so, the man himself no doubt intending for it to sound upbeat, and yet it only rang hollow in its shallowness; regardless, the laughter escaping the twins took the edge off, so perhaps it ended up a fortunate misfire.
【Kisara】 「Come ooon, Sakuya. For being such a ladies' man, you really are terrible at being considerate. You don't have to try so hard to change the subject.」
【Naomasa】 「……Not mincing words, are you? But what's so wrong with that? So what if I'm bad with words?」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「こんな金髪の綺麗で可愛い姉ちゃん、
　両脇にはべらかしてさ。
　しかもその二人とも抱いちゃったもんな」
source.english:
“Here I am with a gorgeous,
sweet blonde on either side.
And I've slept with both of you.”

source.japanese: そう言って、毛布の下で双子の腰に手を回し、引き寄せられなくとも力を込めて抱き締めるの意志を示す。脳天気でお調子者、なるほど、それは時には美点になるものか。朔屋を挟んだ二人も、ふと笑いをこぼす。
source.english: Under the blanket he put a hand around each waist. There was no room to draw them any closer, but he squeezed them to show that he wanted to hold them. Airheaded and glib: yes, perhaps those could sometimes be virtues. On either side of Sakuya, the two let out a sudden little laugh.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「今の様子って、朔屋と初めて会ったあの晩、ほら、あたし達がドレス着て、間抜けな獲物捜してたときと同じだけど」
source.english: “This is like the night we first met you, Sakuya. Remember? We were wearing dresses, looking for some dumb mark.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ほら、あたしとキサラが両脇からくっついてて」
source.english: “Me and Kisara pressed up on either side of you.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「まさかあん時ゃあ、こうもなるとは考えなかった、ほんとに」
source.english: “Never imagined then that it'd end up like this. Really.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……間抜けな獲物だったよなあ。
　まんまと引っかかっちゃった。
　でもお陰で、あんたらと一緒になれたさ」
source.english:
“…I was a dumb mark, wasn't I?
Fell for it perfectly.
Still, that's how I got to be with you.”

source.japanese:
ああ、軽薄。
　しかし、双子は朔屋に両側から、その肩に頭預けてひたと体を寄せた。
source.english:
Ah, frivolity.
Yet from both sides the twins laid their heads upon his shoulders and pressed close.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「全く、運命なんてどう転がるんだかわからんね」
source.english: “Really, you never know which way fate's going to roll.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「同感同感。
　あたしたちもだ。あの頃は自分達がこんな風になるなんて、なれるなんて思えなかったから」
source.english:
“Couldn't agree more.
For us too. Back then we couldn't imagine ending up like this. Couldn't imagine it was possible.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「キサラ……そっか。さっきからやけにその話、持ちだしてくると思ったら。
　それが言いたかったわけか」
source.english:
“Kisara… Oh. Wondered why you kept bringing it up.
That's what you wanted to say.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Because I've got two blonde girls this pretty and adorable, one hanging off each arm. And on top of that, I've even slept with them both.」

With those words, he snaked his arms around the twins' waists beneath the blanket, and though he couldn't draw them closer, he held them tight to show his desire to embrace them. A lighthearted fool unable to read the room: indeed, perhaps that, too, could be a virtue at times. And the two flanking Sakuya also couldn't help but break into smiles.
【Shisamu】 「The way things are right now is just like that night when we first met Sakuya, you know, when we were wearing dresses and were out hunting for some clueless prey.」
【Shisamu】 「Look, you also had Kisara and I clinging to you from both sides then.」
【Shisamu】 「I never so much as dreamed we'd end up like this back then, seriously.」
【Naomasa】 「……I really was clueless prey, huh. I fell for it hook, line, and sinker. Still, thanks to that, I got to be with you.」
Aah, how flippant. However, the twins leaned in towards Sakuya from both sides, resting their heads on his shoulders while softly pressing their bodies close against him.
【Naomasa】 「Seriously, you never know what fate has in store for you.」
【Kisara】 「Yeah, couldn't agree more. It's the same for us. We couldn't even imagine we'd end up like this, and definitely not back then.」
【Shisamu】 「Kisara……I see. I was thinking you'd been bringing that up an awful lot lately. So that's what you wanted to talk about?」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───なあ。聞かせろよ。
　そこまで持ちだしたんならさ。
　ほら俺は、気遣いとかできないから、
　あんたらが話す気になるまで待ってるなんて、できない性分なんだ」
source.english:
“Hey. Tell me, then.
Now that you've brought it up.
You know I'm no good at being considerate.
Waiting until you're ready to talk isn't in my nature.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「それは、あたし達の昔話」
source.english: “It's the story of our past.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まだ毛も生えてないような、子供だった頃の話」
source.english: “When we were still kids. Hadn't even started growing hair.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「───Hey. Tell me then. Since you keep bringing it up. Look, I'm bad at being considerate, so it's just not in my nature to be able to wait patiently until you feel like talking about it.」
【Shisamu】 「It is a tale of our past.」
【Kisara】 「A tale from when we were but children, before we had so much as a hair on our bodies.」

source.japanese: ───それは、双子の昔語り───
source.english: —The twins' tale of long ago—

source.japanese:
あたしたちはね朔屋。
　木の股から産まれたんだってさ。
　
　え？　ネコマタじゃなくって？　って？
　　　…………はっはっは、おもしれえ事言
　　　　　　　いやがるじゃねえか、人の臀
　　　　　　　撫で回しながらさあ。
source.english:
We were born from the fork of a tree, Sakuya. That's what they said.
Huh? Don't I mean a fork-tailed cat?
…Ha-ha-ha. Pretty fucking funny, stroking someone's ass while you say it.

source.japanese:
のっけっから話の腰折るようなバカちんは、
　またケツの穴で、泣くまでいたぶったげよ
　うか、ねえシサム。
　　　　って、なにそんないい顔してるの？
　　もしかして、朔屋に……いたずら……。
　　　　こら。朔屋もシサムも。
　　　今、お互いの手でナニを
　　　触りッコしてたか、白状してみ？
　　　　　　　　怒んないから
　　　……てめえこのおんな、それにアホ正
　　今日はこの話、やめとくか、あ？
　もういい。あたしはすねた。
あとはシサム、あんたがやれ。
source.english:
An idiot who derails the story from the start—maybe we ought to torment his asshole till he cries again. Right, Sisam?
What's that happy look for? Is Sakuya… playing with you…? Hey. Sakuya, Sisam. Confess what you've just been touching with each other's hands. I won't get mad.
…You bitch. And you, you stupidly honest— You know what? Forget this story for today. Fine. I'm sulking. Sisam, you do the rest.

source.japanese:
あーあ、怒らせちゃった。
　朔屋、あんたホントバカだねえ。
　
　だからさ、
　あたしら孤児だったんだよ。
　　　お・や・な・し・ご。
　　なんかね、邑の卵塔場にぶ
　　ち転がってたらしいよ。
　だから木の股から産まれたって言われた方
　がまだまし───
　　卵塔場ってわかんない？
　モノを知らないヤツだね、
　墓場のコトだよ墓場。
　　まー狭くってしけてて
　　　しょっぼい邑[ムラ]だったからね。
　　　　そのまま埋めずに、
　　　　　　育ててくれた……だけでも……、
source.english:
Aw, now you've made her mad. Sakuya, you really are an idiot.
Anyway—we were orphans. No. Par. Ents.
Apparently we were found dumped in the village's rantōba. So being told we'd sprung from the fork of a tree would've been kinder—
What, you don't know what a rantōba is? Ignorant bastard. The graveyard. It means the graveyard.
It was a cramped, damp, pathetic little village. Still, they raised us instead of burying us then and there. For that alone, we ought to be…

source.japanese:
あり　がた　　い───
　……、……、
　　　……、……、
　
　　なんて、誰が思うかぁぁぁっっっ!!
　
　朔屋、どんな餓鬼だって、本気で怨むよ、
　　　　忘れないよ　　忘れないからね
　
　　あんな、犬のコの方がまだマシなんて扱
　　い、誰が忘れてやるもんか。
　　　朔屋、あんた、見たとこほんとはぼっ
　　　ちゃん育ちだな？
　いーないーなー。
　　　　……ま、もう良いんだ、そのことは。
　　　いや良くないけど、その辺りの精算は、
　　　きっちりつけたから。
source.english:
Grate… ful…
… …
… …
LIKE FUCK WE SHOULD!
Sakuya, any kid would seriously hate them. Wouldn't forget. Would never forget. Why should we forget being treated worse than puppies? You look like you were brought up a little gentleman, really. Lucky you, lucky you.

target.text: ───Thus, the twins began to speak of their past───

You know, Sakuya. They said we were born from the crotch of a tree. Huh? Not from a nekomata, you ask? What? ………Ha-ha-ha, you say the funniest things, don't you, and all while you're groping my ass. Wait, are you…… being naughty with Sakuya……? Come on, Sakuya, Shisamu, both of you. Why don't you try confessing to where exactly you're touching with your hands? I won't be mad. ……Damn you woman, and you too, Nao-moron. Maybe we just stop this story here for today, huh? Enough. I'm sulking now. You can do the rest, Shisamu.

Uh-oh, we made her mad. Sakuya, you really are an idiot, huh? So, back on topic, we were orphans. Children. With. No. Parents. Apparently, we were just dumped somewhere around the village's ancestral lichyard. So maybe being told we were born from the crotch of a tree wasn't really that bad after───

Wait, you don't know what I mean by lichyard? You really don't know anything, do you? It's a graveyard, a cemetary. Well, it was a small place, a shabby little village, right? They didn't just bury us right there in the ground, they raised us…… at least, but……, (TN: The term she uses is "rantoba", written "卵塔場", which is an archaic term for a cemetery. The kanji reads as "egg pagoda place", hence Sakuya's confusion. The name originates from the egg-shaped gravestones.)
Grate ful─── ……、……、 ……、……、 Who! The HELL! Would EVER feel that way!? Sakuya, even the worst brat would genuinely hold a grudge over that, they'd remember, never forget.

Being treated like I was worth less than any random mutt, how could anyone just let that go!?! Sakuya, far as I can tell, you were pretty much raised as a pampered little brat, right? Good for you, aren't you lucky. ……Well, it's fine, I'm over that now. Not that I've forgiven it or anything, no, but because I've already made sure to settle that score.

…………? What are you pulling away like that for? It's cold, let's snuggle closer together. What is it, Kisara? Sakuya's balls just crept up his crotch at an incredible speed? Huh, did I…… really make such a scary face? On that note, Kisara, you too, what exactly are you doing on the sly there? ……Well, guess we're even. …………?

Hmm……right, let's see. Take Kuro, for example. That girl. You know her, right, how whenever something dangerous happens, she's stuffed into the『Captain's Box』. The girl herself hates it, we know that much, but, when it gets dangerous on our ship, it gets really, really dangerous. So we have to put her away, for several reasons, right?

Hn? Bold words for someone about to sell her off, is what you're saying? Well that's why we made sure to send you with her, right? Anyway. We're, fundamentally, the opposite. This was our normal, okay? It was really cramped……alright? Mhm……about one or two tatami mats worth of space? That's how small the temple was. And they didn't let us out of there.
And it wasn't just cramped. It was cold. Scary……I kind of don't want to talk about it. But. But still. Willing or not. ……、……、 ……、……、

Alright, Shisamu. Tag. You go cuddle up with Sakuya for a bit. You really hated that place, right? I'll take over from here. Let's see, right, at the edge of that jutting cliff, right at the very tip, that place. Shisamu called it a temple, but, well, basically, it was a prison, just a prison.

She said they wouldn't let us out, but when the guys from the village, when they were heading out to sea to fish. Those were the only times we were dragged out. Right. Obviously, they were after the sense of orientation that Shisamu and I possess. That's where it came from, why they began to call us the "sacred twins", of all the things. Because as long as they brought us with them, almost no matter where they went, they'd be able to return home safely. But in the end, they didn't really treat us any better.

They wouldn't let us out of the temple. This time, it was not because we were treated like burdens, but because we were the communal property of the village. The food got a bit better, at least. But it was kind of like, becoming "sacred" meant that luxuries were off-limits to us. Something like a bath was completely out of the question. Shisamu and I, we were constantly picking lice and fleas off each other, like we were little monkeys. Seriously, what kind of backwater dump was that, and in this day and age?

……Remembering makes me more pissed off than scared. Kisara. There's also the story of St. Elmo's fire. Gets my blood boiling too, that one. Who even came up with that, I have no clue. Sakuya, they say that sometimes in this world, those born as children of man are mixed with something inhuman. Some mystic somewhere said that, apparently. It sounds completely crazy, but we also believe it. But, you know, it's like, umm…….

You can laugh at it if you want, but please don't, okay? If you do laugh, next time we fuck, I'll tie my hair around the base of your dick until you can't ejaculate, then make you cum all night, you got that? ……Thank goodness…… If you laughed, even we would feel hurt, you know?

St. Elmo's fire. It doesn't have to be that in particular. We just happen to have that nature, happen to be called by that name. On the ocean, no, in this world. There are sometimes those who take the shape of a human, but aren't. Personally, that Tomosato, for example. I've got my eye on him, something about that guy is real fishy.

So then─── In the end, we just couldn't endure it. Staying like that, not even being treated like we were human, right? No, it was really that bad. Hearing us talk about it now, it almost sounds like a joke, but superstitions and cults and that stuff, they really make people lose their minds.

Look, Kisara and I, our eyeballs, one each. They were about to carve them out. To become a true『Sacred Flame』, we had to be "different from others", or something. If we'd stayed in that temple for one more night, I really don't know what would have happened to us───

Who said even a single word about wanting to become some "Sacred Flame"? That village was already unbearable to live in. And we had to suffer for their sake? Even before that, we were alrea─── Hey. Sakuya. I'm sorry, okay? For making you stick with us, all this way here. This feeling, maybe that's what truly made them call us St. Elmo's fire, the real reason behind it.

The world itself is what drives us mad. No matter where we are, it always stands watch over us. So conversely, we can see through the eyes of the world and know where we are. It's not something to be grateful about. Really, in a lot of ways.

……Kind of feels like we got sidetracked there. Anyways. They were about to gouge out our eyeballs, so we escaped in a hurry. We were still children, and we had always been tiny, so if they chased us, we'd be caught for sure. And there was also this feeling in the air that, if they did, we'd probably be raped.
───So, we ended up setting it on fire. ───The village that raised us. ───It burned so beautifully, didn't it, Kisara───

【Kisara】 「Ah. Knew it, so he was doing it to you too, Shisamu. What a naughty, naughty way to touch us.」
【Naomasa】 「But I mean……the conversation, it got kind of heavy and……I just.」
【Kisara】 「Well, that's just who you are, I guess. So, hey, hey, Sakuya. How did it feel? Sinking your fangs into two twins who were once treated as gods?」
Naturally, there was not a shred of hesitation to be found in Sakuya's answer.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「すっげえ気持ち良かった！
　二人いっぺんにすると最高だ。たまらない。
　もっとしたい。ずっとしたい」
source.english:
“Fucking incredible!
Both at once is the best. Can't get enough. Want to do it more.
Want to keep doing it forever.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「即答がそれときた……。
　ねえ朔屋。それって、
　あたしらとずっと一緒にいたいって事だよね？」
source.english:
“That's your instant answer…
Hey, Sakuya.
That means you want to stay with us forever, right?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたしらを、連れ合いにしたいって、そう受け取るよ？　……で、どっちを？」
source.english: “We'll take it to mean you want us as your partners. …So, which one?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「It felt absolutely fucking fantastic! Doing it with you both at the same time is the best. I can't get enough. I want to do it more. I want to do it forever.」
【Shisamu】 「An instant answer, and that's what you come up with……. Hey, Sakuya. When you say that, it means you want to be with us forever, doesn't it?」
【Kisara】 「So you're saying you want to make us your wives, that's how it sound to us, you know? ……So then, which of us?」

source.japanese:
ちょっと待ってて、と二人は天幕を一旦出る。
　戻って再び毛布に潜[もぐ]り朔屋に寄り添い、また問いかける。右と左の両側から、耳元近くに口寄せて。
source.english:
Wait a second, they said, and briefly went out of the tent.
Returning, they slipped beneath the blanket again, nestled beside Sakuya and repeated the question, mouths close to his ears on either side.

target.text: Just a second, the two said as they left the tent for a brief while. They came back, crawled under the blanket again, leaned into Sakuya, then asked once more. From both left and right, their mouths right against his ears.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたし、キサラと」
source.english: “Between me, Kisara—”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたし、シサムを」
source.english: “And me, Sisam—”

source.japanese: ───どっちをとるの？
source.english: —Which will you choose?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あのさ。
　今、なんで入れ替わって見せたん？」
source.english:
“Hey.
Why'd you just switch places like that?”

source.japanese: と、此度も即答した朔屋の声に迷う気配は感じられず、むしろ素朴ささえ感じられた。
source.english: Again his answer was instant, without a hint of uncertainty. If anything, it sounded artless.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「今、キサラって言った方がほんとはシサムで、シサムの方がキサラだろ？」
source.english: “The one who just said Kisara is really Sisam, and the Sisam one's Kisara, right?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……あれ？　なんかあっさり……」
source.english: “…Huh? That was awfully easy…”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「運に頼るにしちゃ、迷いがなかったし……」
source.english: “Didn't hesitate enough for it to be luck…”

source.japanese: 二人としては必殺の、男の意気地（この男にそんなものはないのだが、惚れた相手に無い物ねだりも人の性である）見定める仕掛け、もちろん、当てて欲しい気持ちはあったのだが、こうもあっさりとは思いもよらず、しかも本人自覚がなさそう。二人揃って呆れていいやら意気込み空振ってくじけていいやら。素直に褒める気にもならない。続けて朔屋がこう言ったとあっては。
source.english: It had been their killer move, a test of a man's nerve—this man had none, but wanting what one's beloved lacked was human nature too. Of course they wanted him to guess correctly. But they had never expected it to be so easy, and he did not even seem aware of his feat. Both were left unsure whether to be astonished or disheartened at their wasted preparations. Neither felt like simply praising him. Especially when he went on to say—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Me, Kisara.」
【Kisara】 「Me, Shisamu.」
───Which of us will you pick?
【Naomasa】 「Come on now. Why did you just switch places in so blatant a way?」
There was not a trace of hesitation in Sakuya's voice as he answered immediately this time either; if anything, his answer even felt genuine in its artlessness.
【Naomasa】 「Just now, that was Shisamu who said Kisara, and Kisara who said Shisamu, right?」
【Shisamu】 「……Huh? That was kind of quick……」
【Kisara】 「For someone leaving it up to luck, you sure didn't hesitate……」

This was their secret killer technique, a trap to test a man's mettle (this man never had any such thing, but asking for the moon from those you love is but human nature), and of course, they did want him to guess correctly, but they never imagined he'd be able to do it so easily, and on top of that, the man himself didn't even seem aware of what he'd accomplished. Both were left wondering if they should just be exasperated or instead disheartened by the swing and a miss brought about by their own enthusiasm. They couldn't bring themselves to just praise him for it. And given what Sakuya said right after.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まあ、どういうつもりだか知らないが、どっちが欲しいかって聞かれたら、両方かなあ」
source.english: “Well, don't know what you're getting at, but if you ask which I want… Both, I guess.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺は、同じ物は二つもいらない派じゃなくって、同じ物が二つあると余計に嬉しい派だもの」
source.english: “I'm not in the camp that says you don't need two of the same thing. I'm in the camp that's even happier to have two.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それに、二人だって気分でずいぶんと変わるぜ。
　だってこないだなんか、キサラは最初シサムを凄いＳに責めてたし、シサムは後から積極的になった」
source.english:
“Besides, you both change a lot with your moods.
The other day Kisara started out tormenting Sisam like a real sadist, then Sisam got all eager afterward.”

source.japanese:
声音は無邪気といえるほどなのに、言うことときたらこの始末。
　二人揃って、は、と笑い、毛布の下で朔屋の両腕それぞれに抱き締める。
source.english:
His voice was almost innocent. What it said was another matter.
The two laughed together and, beneath the blanket, each hugged one of his arms.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「えっらいシモな話からたとえをどうもありがとね！　その上、二人とも選ぶと来たよ」
source.english: “Thanks so much for the filthy example! And on top of that, you choose both of us.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でもまあ実際、あたしらが二人離れて生きてく事は難しいしね」
source.english: “Still, it really would be hard for us to live apart.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「一緒にしておいてくれるなら、そのほうが嬉しいに決まってる」
source.english: “Of course we'd be happier if you kept us together.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……へっへっえ～……」
source.english: “…Heh-heh-heh…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Now, I'm not sure exactly what you were up to with all that, but if you want to know which of you I want, it's both, I guess?」
【Naomasa】 「I'm not the kind of guy who thinks having two of the same thing is pointless. I'm in the two makes me happier than one camp.」

【Naomasa】 「What's more, you two can also feel very different from each other, depending on your mood. You know, the other day, Kisara, when you went after Shisamu really hard like a total sadist, and Shisamu, you got really assertive afterwards.」

The tone of his voice could be called downright innocent, and yet the words he was uttering were a complete mess. The two let out a short bark of laughter, then each embraced one of Sakuya's arms tightly under the blanket.
【Shisamu】 「Really appreciate the absolutely filthy examples you brought up! And on top of that, you go and pick us both, of all the things.」
【Kisara】 「But the truth is, it would be difficult for the two of us to live apart, right?」
【Kisara】 「So if you're willing to keep us both together, then that'd obviously make me happier.」
【Kisara】 「……Heh heh heh～……」

source.japanese: そのだらしなく笑う顔すら愛おしく、まずはキサラがその頬に唇優しく押し当てる。
source.english: Even that slack grin was lovable. Kisara was the first to press her lips gently to his cheek.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんかおかしい関係だけど、納得できないでもないからこれでいいや」
source.english: “Strange sort of relationship, but I can't say it doesn't make sense. This'll do.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……ふふふっ……」
source.english: “…Heh-heh…”

target.text: Even that slack smile on her face made for an adorable sight; first, Kisara pressed her lips tenderly against his cheek.
【Shisamu】 「It's kind of a weird relationship, but I can't say it doesn't make some sense, so guess I'm fine with it.」
【Shisamu】 「……Huhuhuh……」

source.japanese: キサラ離れて続けてシサム。合いの手入らずの間髪に。
source.english: Kisara drew away and Sisam followed, without a beat between.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたしらがつかまえたのか」
source.english: “Did we catch him—”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたしらが捕まったのか」
source.english: “Or did we get caught—”

source.japanese: ───まあ、どっちでもいいか───
source.english: —Well, either way—

target.text: After Kisara pulled away, next came Shisamu. Taking over, without a moment's pause between.
【Shisamu】 「Did we make the catch?」
【Kisara】 「Or are we the ones who got caught?」
───Well, did it really matter either way?───

source.japanese:
そして、二人同時にキスを送る。受ける朔屋の顔、果てしなくだらしなく、でもそれが今の二人にはたまらなく愛おしく。
　零下の夜にも心と触れる肌だけは暖かく、片身欠けてはまともに生きられぬ双子と救いがたい駄目男、三人あわせて一つの影を仮の窟[いわや]の影に写すのだった。
source.english:
Then the two kissed him at once. Sakuya's face was infinitely foolish, yet to them now it was unbearably dear.
In the subzero night, only their hearts and the skin where they touched were warm: twins who could not live properly without their other half, and one irredeemable good-for-nothing of a man, the three together casting a single shadow upon the stone wall of their makeshift cave.

target.text: And when both of them then gave him a kiss at the same time, Sakuya's face melted into something utterly slack and sloppy, but to the two of them in this moment, it was an irresistibly precious response. Even on this sub-zero night, their hearts and touching skin alone remained warm; twins who couldn't lead a proper life without their other half and a hopeless man bordering on the irredeemable; the three of them together cast but a single flickering shadow on the wall of their temporary cave.

source.japanese:
影？
　そう、三人籠もる岩肌に、影が差す。それはつまり、天幕外より光差す。
　仄か茫洋たる、淡い光。
　語らいの中で時忘れていた三人は、いつの間にか外が明るくなっていたことに気付いた。もちろん、まだ朝日昇る時間ではない。
　では、これは何が光っているというのか。
　不審に顔合わせ、怯えるより前に体を起こす。
　天幕はねのけ外に出る。
　その眼前、見上げる天に広がっていたものは───
source.english:
A shadow?
Yes, a shadow fell upon the rock where the three sheltered.
That meant light was coming in from outside the tent.
A faint, hazy, pale light. Lost in their conversation, they had forgotten time, and now noticed that it had grown bright outside. Of course, it was not yet time for sunrise.
Then what was shining?
They exchanged puzzled looks and rose before fear could take hold.
Throwing back the canvas, they stepped outside.
Before their eyes, spread across the sky above—

target.text: A shadow? Right, a shadow fell upon the face of the rock the three were taking shelter behind. Which would mean light shone through from outside the tent. Dim and boundless, a pale light. Lost in their talking, the three had forgotten time, and they suddenly noticed that it had become bright outside. Of course, it was still much too early for the morning sun to rise.

Well now, what could it be that was emitting this light then? They exchanged wary glances, then decided to rise up rather than cower in fear. They pushed aside the canvas and stepped outside. And what unfolded in the heavens before their very eyes as they looked up was───
