source.japanese: うねり、揺らぎ、重なり、雅やかに緩やかに、たっぷりとした襞を取って展開される光の紗幕の、見上げれば、人の手でも掴み取れるのではないかというくらい間近に迫って夜空一面。
source.english: Undulating, wavering, overlapping, the gauze curtain of light unfolded in ample pleats, with a slow, elegant grace. Looking up, one felt it close enough to catch in a human hand. It filled the night sky.

source.japanese:
夜空一面に壮麗にたなびけるカーテン状の光の連なり、その色合いは、朔屋の邦[くに]の古い言葉では赤気と称するが、青年が振り仰いだところ、その形状、女の着物にたとえれば、身頃の辺りは緑がかり、裳裾の辺りは青みを帯びた、赤は紗幕の上の縁辺りを薄く縁取っている程度。
　けれど、いずれの幕も、刻一刻と階調変えて留まるところを知らぬ。
source.english:
The curtainlike bands streamed magnificently across the whole sky. An old word in Sakuya's country called such light ‘red vapor,’ but looking up, the young man saw—if its shape were compared to a woman's kimono—green around the body and blue toward the trailing hem. Red only faintly edged its upper border.
Yet every curtain changed its shades from moment to moment, never resting.

target.text: Undulating, fluctuating, layered, gracefully and gently, a diaphanous drape of light unfolding in generously flowing pleats: when he looked up, that was what covered the entire night sky, drawing so near to him it seemed as if he could reach up with his hands and grab hold of it.

A magnificent cascade of light taking the shape of fluttering veils unfurled across the night sky, and its colouration was what was once given the name "sekki" in ancient texts of Sakuya's homeland, a deep, dark red, but when the young man looked up, that form it took, were he to liken it to a woman's kimono, then the bodice of the garment would be tinged green, the trailing hem would deepen into shades of blue, and red but delicately fringed a faint border along the sheer curtain. (TN: Sekki, written "赤気", is an ancient Japanese word that refers to a low-latitude aurora.)
And yet, every layer shifted in hue with every passing moment, never knowing rest.

source.japanese:
色彩の。
　あでやかな。
　はなやかな。
　きらびやかな。
　今宵一面に垂れこめた光はカーテン状のオーロラの。
source.english:
Color.
Gorgeous.
Resplendent.
Glittering.
The light draped across the sky tonight: an aurora in curtains.

source.japanese:
光彩のカーテンの靡[なび]けるさまは、どこか貴婦人達の左右左を見るように、どこやら生物めいた質感さえ漂わせて。
　夜空一面がスクリーンとして投影されたる、オーロラの。壮麗、と一言で片付けるには、朔屋にとってはどこか不気味ですらあった。
source.english:
The flowing luminous curtains resembled, somehow, the ceremonial bows of noblewomen—left, right, left—even suggesting the texture of a living thing.
An aurora projected upon the whole night sky as its screen. To call it simply ‘magnificent’ would not do. To Sakuya it was almost uncanny.

target.text: Kaleidoscopic. Enchanting. Brilliant. Resplendent. The light blanketing the sky this evening was an aurora shaped like a flowing curtain.

The way in which the radiant veil fluttered resembled the sayusa of noblewomen in some ways, exuding a strangely animated quality, almost as if it were a living being. It was as if the entire night sky was a screen upon which the aurora was projected. Magnificent, but to reduce it merely to one such word even felt somewhat unpleasant to Sakuya. (TN: Sayusa, written "左右左", is a form of ceremonial dance combined with bowing. It involves turning the upper body from left to right to left while bowing deeply every time. This is a form of haibu, written "拝舞". It is done in traditional courtly or ceremonial contexts.)

source.japanese:
白がほとんどを占める世界の中での転変する色合いの鮮やかさをどう言おうか。
　けれど朔屋は。空の幻想色彩と地上の双子達を見比べて。
　やっぱりこっちの色がいいや、俺は、と頷[うなず]いたのだった。
source.english:
How could one describe the vividness of those changing colors in a world made almost entirely of white?
But Sakuya looked from the fantastic colors in the sky to the twins upon the ground and nodded.
Yeah. These were still the colors he preferred.

source.japanese: 一方地上では、シサムとキサラを迎えたのは一人の巡礼者ただ彼だけかと思いきや、氷原のそこかしこ、あちらの丘の陰やらそちらの雪の窪地やらから湧き出してくる同じような衣装の巡礼者が陸続と。常人というよりは、このオーロラの空の下でしかその形を保てないような、怪しき子実体が人の形を取りたるや。そんな風情で陸続と、朔屋達が苦難の旅路した氷原に、これほどの人数がどこから渡ってきたのかと、唖然となるほどの。
source.english: Meanwhile, on the ground, it seemed only one pilgrim had come to welcome Sisam and Kisara. Then more, similarly clothed, emerged in succession from here and there upon the ice, from behind that hill, from this hollow in the snow. Less ordinary people than strange fruiting bodies assuming human shapes, as though they could hold their forms only beneath an aurora's sky. On they came. Where had so many people come from to reach this ice field the three had struggled so hard to traverse? Sakuya could only gape.

source.japanese: 彼らが手に携える杖の先に点った灯りも、何らかの種が燃えているというのではなく、杖の先にてただ宿り、光る、あるいは本当に空の光紗を取ってきてそこに留め置いているのではないかと、さえ。
source.english: The lights at the tips of their staffs burned no apparent fuel. They simply inhabited the tips and shone. Perhaps the pilgrims really had plucked the luminous gauze from the sky and fastened it there.

source.japanese:
それまでは三人で一つの生き物のように寄り添っていた朔屋とシサムとキサラ。
　けれど、二人は。
　オーロラの下に参集した巡礼者達に迎えられ、他にも多くが集まっている事を認めると。
　朔屋の両脇から───
source.english:
Until then, Sakuya, Sisam and Kisara had nestled together like a single creature.
But when the two were welcomed by the pilgrims gathered beneath the aurora, when they saw how many others had assembled, they began to draw away—from either side of Sakuya—

target.text: Where should he even begin to describe this vivid alteration of colour amidst a world almost entirely occupied by white? However, Sakuya. He compared the fantastical hues of the sky to the twins standing on the ground. "Yeah, I prefer these colours after all", he thought, nodding to himself.

Meanwhile, on the ground, bidding Shisamu and Kisara welcome was but a single pilgrim, or so he had thought, but from here and there and everywhere on the ice field, they gushed forth from behind the snowdrifts and depressions in rapid succession, pilgrims all wearing similar outfits to one another. They seemed less like ordinary people than they did the fruiting bodies of fungi that had assumed the shape of humans, able to sustain their form only beneath this glowing aurora. Such was the manner in which they came, one after another, enough to leave him dumbstruck, wondering from where this many people had managed to cross the ice fields that Sakuya and the twins had endured such hardships to traverse.

The light that crowned the tips of the staves they carried in their hands, too; it was not that some manner of burning ember sustained the flame, it simply dwelt there, shining, or perhaps, one might even wonder if they had actually plucked a piece from the luminous veil in the skies and anchored it there.

Hitherto, Sakuya, Shisamu, and Kisara, as if a being that was three as one, had stood close together. However, the two. Welcomed by the pilgrims gathered beneath the aurora, they acknowledged that many others were also assembling there, and then. From either side of Sakuya───

source.japanese: 朔屋は、その時の喪失感をどう表せばいいのか、その言葉を知らない。
source.english: Sakuya knew no words to express the loss he felt then.

source.japanese: 双子は朔屋の両脇から、離れて、しまうと。
source.english: The twins left his sides.

source.japanese: 熱が消えていってしまう。
source.english: The warmth went away.

target.text: How could Sakuya even begin to express the feeling of loss in that moment? He didn't know the words.
Once the twins parted, from either side of Sakuya, and were gone.
The heat was fading.

source.japanese: 巡礼者達へ向かって。歩き出して。
source.english: They began walking toward the pilgrims.

source.japanese: 張りに満ちた、しなやかな肉の感触が、失せる。
source.english: The feel of supple, resilient flesh disappeared.

source.japanese: 朔屋を、振り返りもせず───否。
source.english: Without looking back at Sakuya—no.

target.text: They began to walk off. Towards the pilgrims.
The sensation of firm, supple flesh───lost.
Without even turning their heads to look back at Sakuya───nay.

source.japanese:
双子は、一度、朔屋に振り返った。
　その顔を見てしまったから、嘘や冗談などではないと。朔屋には、朔屋にさえ、判ってしまったのだ。
source.english:
Once, the twins turned to him.
Because he saw their faces, he knew—even Sakuya knew—it was neither a lie nor a joke.

target.text: But once, the twins looked back at Sakuya. And because he saw that look on their faces, he knew that this was no lie, no jest. Sakuya, yes, even Sakuya, understood.

source.japanese:
双子の全てが、朔屋の隣から、喪われる。
　オーロラに照らされて、氷原の色調も刻々と変わるのに、朔屋は二人が歩んでいるのが、黒い鏡のような氷の上のように思えてならず、そして二人はその上に影さえ落としていない、歩み出したその時にはもう、青年の手の届かない人達に列してしまったかのように。
　それとも───セントエルモの灯。
source.english:
The twins were gone from his side, utterly.
The aurora changed the ice field's colors moment by moment, yet to Sakuya they seemed to be walking over ice like a black mirror. They cast not even a shadow upon it, as though the moment they stepped away they had already joined those beyond his reach.
Or else—St. Elmo's light.

source.japanese:
一つの海の伝説。
　どちらにしても、朔屋とは異なる世界に歩み去ろうとしている。
　二人が振り向いた時、朔屋はきょとんと、彼にしては品の良い顔をしていた。地が出ると逆にこうなる朔屋の、それくらい、虚を憑かれていたのか。
source.english:
A legend of the sea.
Either way, they were walking away into a world apart from Sakuya's.
When they turned, Sakuya's face had gone blank and, for once, almost respectable. Perversely, this was how he looked when his true nature showed. Had he been caught so utterly off guard?

target.text: All that the twins were, mournfully vanishing, from Sakuya's side. Even as the ice field shifted in colour with every passing moment, illuminated by the aurora, Sakuya couldn't rid himself of the thought that it seemed as if the two leaving him walked atop a pitch-black mirror of ice; they seemed to not even cast shadows upon it, and by the time they had begun walking, it was as if the two had already joined the ranks of those beyond the reach of the young man's hands. Or perhaps───St. Elmo's fire.

A legend of the seas. One way or another, they were walking away, about to step into a world different from Sakuya's. When the two turned their heads back at him, Sakuya was wide-eyed and dazed, wearing an unusually graceful expression for the likes of him. For Sakuya to, conversely, look remarkably refined when truly taken by surprise, perhaps that meant the shock had simply taken root that deeply in him?

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ごめんね、朔屋」
source.english: “Sorry, Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Sorry, Sakuya.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「さようならだ、朔屋」
source.english: “Goodbye, Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「This is goodbye, Sakuya.」

source.japanese:
───せっかくあたし達を───
　
　
　───選んでくれたのにね───
source.english:
—And after you'd gone to all the trouble—
—Of choosing us, too—

target.text: ───And after you were so kind─── ───Kind enough to choose us───

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「よくぞ参られた。我ら『一なる三者』『三位一体者』『昇華三魂』の輪の中に」
source.english: “Welcome, indeed, to our circle of the ‘Three Who Are One,’ the ‘Triune One,’ the ‘Three Souls of Sublimation.’”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「此度の新たな同胞は、なんとめずらかなる者か。
　貴女達は『三位一体者』であり、そしてかの聖人の灯火である」
source.english:
“How rare our new fellows are this time.
You are the ‘Triune One,’ and also the light of that saint.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「一つに別れたる火は、旅人を惑わす陰火となり」
source.english: “A single flame, divided off alone, becomes a ghost-fire that leads travelers astray.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「二つに並べられた火は、旅人を導く灯火となり」
source.english: “Two flames burning side by side become a light that guides them.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「しこうして今一つは、我らの列に。
　三つと揃えられた火は、巴の炎となりて、
　この無間の牢獄よりの、
　昇華を果たさん───」
source.english:
“And when one more joins them, the three flames gathered together become a triple-whorled fire
and win sublimation
from this eternal prison.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あのさ……いきなり出てきてなんだいあんた達は。
　せっかく美人の双子の恋人できたってのに、なんだってそういう、拝み屋さんの縁起悪いご託宣めいた台詞ばっかり」
source.english:
“Hey… You turn up out of nowhere. Who are you people?
I've finally got beautiful twin girlfriends, and all you can do is spout ominous prophecies like some professional prayer merchant.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「間にあってんだよ、そういうのは。
　あんた達は一体なんなんだい」
source.english:
“I've had enough of that sort of thing already.
What the hell are you?”

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「We are honoured you have joined us. Joined the fold of we 『Three As One』 『Triune Beings』 『Sublimating Three Souls』」
【Pilgrim】 「And what rare souls that we welcome as new comrades on this occasion. You are『Triune Beings』, as well as the light of a well-known saint.」
【Pilgrim】 「When the fire is sundered into one, it becomes a phantom flame that beguiles the traveller and leads him astray.」
【Pilgrim】 「When two flames stand side by side, they become a light to guide the traveller on his path.」
【Pilgrim】 「And lo, another stands already in our fold. The three flames now gathered, together shall form a tomoe of flame, and from this ceaseless prison, shall achieve sublimation───」

【Naomasa】 「Now look……who do you guys think you are, popping up out of nowhere? I finally got two beautiful twins as my girlfriends, and here you are, spouting lines straight out of some ill-omened prophecy from a crackpot fortune-teller.」
【Naomasa】 「We've had more than enough of that stuff now, we're good, thanks. Who the hell are you people even?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「有難う、朔屋。
　あんたは良い男だったよ」
source.english:
“Thank you, Sakuya.
You were a good man.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Thank you, Sakuya. You were a good man.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんたといられて、幸せだったよ。
　半端な火酒より酔わせてくれたよ」
source.english:
“We were happy with you.
You got us drunker than any second-rate spirits.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Being with you was happiness itself. You left me more intoxicated than any half-decent hard liquor could ever hope to.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「だけど朔屋。さよなら朔屋」
source.english: “But, Sakuya. Goodbye, Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But Sakuya. This is goodbye, Sakuya.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたし達、行かなくっちゃいけないみたい」
source.english: “Looks like we've got to go.”

source.japanese:
古い古い歌謡曲の、歌詞のような言葉で。
　歌うような抑揚で。
　二人は一体何を告げようとしているのか、朔屋にはにわかに理解できかねた。
source.english:
Words like the lyrics of a very, very old popular song,
spoken with a singing cadence.
What were the two trying to tell him? Sakuya could not grasp it all at once.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It seems we're left no choice but to go.」
Words like the lyrics to an ancient, ancient Japanese ballad. Intonation as if they were singing. Whatever the two were trying to convey, Sakuya could scarcely comprehend any of it at first.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「いつか言ったよね。
　この世界は、居心地悪いって」
source.english:
“We told you once, didn't we?
This world makes us uncomfortable.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「We said it at some point, right? That this world makes us feel ill at ease.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「この世界は、どっかおかしいんだ。
　あたしたちはそいつに、我慢がならない」
source.english:
“Something's wrong with it.
We can't stand that.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「There's something wrong with this entire world. And we just can't stand it anymore.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「このまま在り続けたら、あたしたちはきっと」
source.english: “If we go on existing like this, we'll surely—”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If we continue to exist like this, there's no doubt that we'll───」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「永遠に彷徨い続ける『なにか』になっちまう」
source.english: “Become ‘something’ that wanders forever.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「End up turning into『something』 doomed ever to wander.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そうなったらそうなったで、
　かえって清々するのかも知れない」
source.english:
“Maybe once that happened,
we'd actually feel relieved.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And should it come to that, that might actually even be freeing in itself.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でもそれは───怖いんだ」
source.english: “But that… scares us.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「But that's───scary.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたし達が逃げ出してきた邑の言い伝え」
source.english: “The tradition of the village we escaped from.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「『セントエルモの灯』」
source.english: “‘St. Elmo's light.’”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「The tale passed down in the village we escaped from.」
【Shisamu】 「『St. Elmo's fire』」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「この閉じた世界にばらまかれた、伝説、言い伝えの数々」
source.english: “All the legends, all the tales scattered through this closed world.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたしたちは、そういうモノになっちまう」
source.english: “We'd turn into one of those things.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……訳がわかんねえってばっ」
source.english: “…I'm telling you, I don't understand!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺は、俺は───っ。
　あんた達に振られる為に、
　わざわざこんな北の果てまで、
　やって来たってのか？」
source.english:
“I—I came all the way
to the northern
end of the world just
so you could dump me?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いいや、振られるならそれでもいい。
　シサムよう、キサラなあ、あんたらは。
　いなくなっちまう気なんだ───！」
source.english:
“No. If you want to dump me,
fine. Sisam, Kisara.
You're going to disappear—!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「The numerous legends and old tales scattered throughout this sealed world.」
【Kisara】 「That's the kind of thing that we'll end up becoming.」
【Naomasa】 「……And I'm saying this makes no damn sense to me!」
【Naomasa】 「I'm-, did I───. Did I really come all this way, to the northern end of the world itself, all to be dumped by you?」
【Naomasa】 「No, if I was being dumped, then that would be fine. Come on, Shisamu, Kisara, hey, you two. It feels like you're going to disappear for good───!」

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「……あなたには、理解及ばぬ事であろうが。
　それこそが、幸いなる事なのだよ。
　いなくなる───のではない。
　解放、なのだ」
source.english:
“…It will be beyond your understanding.
But that is precisely the fortunate thing.
Not disappearing.
Liberation.”

source.japanese: 頭巾の裡[うち]よりの声なのに、聞き苦しいところの一切ない、澄んで耳に良く響く声。この氷原の、夾雑物を廃した空気を人の声にすれば彼の声となったろう。
source.english: Though it came from inside a hood, there was nothing harsh or unpleasant in the voice; it rang clear in his ears. If the ice field's air, purged of every impurity, had been given a human voice, this would have been it.

source.japanese: 美声、といって良いのだろうが、朔屋にはどうしてもこの声、好きになれそうにない。青年とて、なにも自身の無芸で無能だからと、世のあまねく美質というのに反感とか劣等感を抱くわけでもないのだ。それなのにこの巡礼者の声には、聞かされるだけでその場にいたたまれなくなるような、暗に表に、自分がこの世にある事を責められているような気にさえさせられる。
source.english: A beautiful voice, one could call it. Yet Sakuya could not like it. Even he did not resent every fine quality in the world, or feel inferior before it, merely because he himself had neither talent nor ability. Nevertheless, just hearing this pilgrim's voice made him unable to bear standing there. It almost seemed to rebuke him, openly or implicitly, for existing in this world.

source.japanese:
そんな朔屋の忌避感を知ってか知らずか、いや、覚っても無視しただろうの、万事に通じた長上がただ淡々と、動かしようのない事実を並べるように、告げた。無知を哀れむでもない、知識を誇るでもない、相手が知らぬと言うのなら、己の知る事実を伝えるだけ、その後でどう受け取ろうとも、それは相手に任せるほかない。そういった、突き放した声音でもあった。
　それ故に一層、朔屋はこの巡礼者とやら、胡散臭く思えてくる。
source.english:
Whether the pilgrim knew of Sakuya's aversion or not—no, even knowing, he would probably have ignored it—he spoke like an elder versed in all things, calmly setting out immovable facts. Neither pitying ignorance nor boasting of knowledge: if another did not know, he merely told him what he himself knew. What the listener made of it afterward was the listener's affair. His voice held that same remoteness.
For that very reason, Sakuya found this so-called pilgrim still more dubious.

source.japanese: オーロラの下、朔屋のわかりやすい表情に表れた不信は、顔に差し落ちる、転変する光の中でほとんど隠されていたけれど、それでも巡礼者は青年の佇まいから読み取ったのだろう。
source.english: Beneath the aurora, the shifting light falling upon Sakuya's face almost concealed the distrust plainly written there. The pilgrim must nevertheless have read it from his bearing.

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「……It may well be beyond your comprehension. Yet that, in truth, is a mercy. Disappearance───it is not. It is liberation.」

Though the voice came from the inside of his hood, it was not muffled at all, the clear voice resonating beautifully in his ear. If the air of this frozen field, purged of all impurities, were given human voice, then it would surely be his.

It could well be described as a beautiful voice, but Sakuya could by no means find it in himself to grow fond of it. It wasn't as if the young man's lack of accomplishments or competence had left him with a feeling of antipathy towards the universal qualities of beauty found throughout this world, nor had it made him harbour some manner of inferiority complex towards them. And yet, when it came to this pilgrim's voice, it was as though just listening to it made him feel ill at ease being there, as though it was both implicitly and explicitly condemning even his very existence in this world.

Was he aware of how repulsed Sakuya was or not, nay, even if he knew, he would most assuredly have disregarded it; this seasoned elder, well-versed in all things, simply spoke with calm detachment, declaring it as if enumerating immovable truths. He did not pity ignorance, nor did he boast of knowledge; should the other party claim to be unaware, then he would simply bequeath to them the truth, and whatever they made of it afterwards, that was left entirely in their hands. It was also a voice spoken in that sort of distant, cold tone. And consequently, these pilgrims, or whatever they called themselves, only began to look more dubious than ever to Sakuya's eyes.

Beneath the aurora, an unmistakable suspicion was written all over Sakuya's face, and although it was mostly obscured beneath the mutating light, the pilgrim could likely still read it from the young man's stance alone.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「……解放、なのだ。
　この牢獄のような世界からの。
　たとえば……そうだな、あなたはこの世界の真の形を理解しているか」
source.english:
“…Liberation.
From this prisonlike world.
For instance… Yes. Do you understand the world's true shape?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（うっわぁ……世界の真の形、と来たぜ。
　会ってすぐの人間に哲学問答、持ちかけるかぁ？）
source.english:
(Whoa… Now it's ‘the world's true shape.’
Who starts a philosophical debate with someone they've just met?)

source.japanese: 口にこそ出さなかっただけで、朔屋の眺める目つき、空の壮麗な舞台に対しても失礼なほどに胡散臭げに眉根にしわ寄せられたが、巡礼者は朔屋からの答えなくとも、淡々と続ける、これはよほどの辛抱強さ。それとも、事実を知る者としての揺るぎない自信によるものか。
source.english: He did not say it aloud, but his suspicious gaze, brows drawn together, was almost rude even to the magnificent stage overhead. Without an answer, the pilgrim went calmly on. Remarkable patience. Or was it unshakable confidence from one who knew the facts?

source.japanese:
いずれにしても巡礼者はなおも続けた。
　ただし今度は、携えた杖を軽く前に突き出して。
source.english:
Either way, the pilgrim continued.
This time he extended his staff a little in front of him.

source.japanese:
もちろん朔屋が身構えるまでもなく、それで青年の迷妄叩き散らそうと言うのではない、不遜な眼差しばかりを向けてくる眸[ひとみ]を突き潰そうしているのでもない。
　巡礼者は自分の前に、杖の石突きで楕円形を描き出して見せただけの事。だけの事、なのではあるが、うっすらと表を新雪が覆っているものの、すぐ下は万年氷土に硬質な氷の層だ。巡礼者の杖の石突きは、だというのに柔い砂浜に描くように容易に線を引いたのである。
source.english:
Sakuya need not have braced himself. The man did not propose to beat the delusions out of him, or gouge out the eyes that offered only insolent looks.
He merely drew an ellipse before himself with the staff's ferrule. Merely—but though a thin layer of fresh snow covered the surface, beneath it lay hard ice in ground frozen for ages. Yet the pilgrim traced his line as easily as on a soft, sandy beach.

source.japanese:
それも奇妙、そして描く際に長衣の袖[そで]の端からのぞいた腕は、声に相応しくすらりと美しい輪郭で、ただその肌が一面のしわに覆われているようにも、乙女のように滑らかに見えるのが、オーロラの光の下、朔屋にはひどく異様に。
　青年の戸惑いなど知らぬげに、巡礼者は楕円に色々の線を書き足して、できあがったのは朔屋にとってもなんの事もない、この世界の模造図だ。
source.english:
That was strange too. As he drew, an arm showed beneath the sleeve of his robe, its slender, beautiful outline worthy of the voice. Yet in the aurora's light its skin seemed at once covered with wrinkles and smooth as a maiden's. To Sakuya it was profoundly uncanny.
Apparently oblivious to his bewilderment, the pilgrim added various lines to the ellipse. The finished diagram was, even to Sakuya, nothing unusual: a model of this world.

source.japanese: 円盤状の地盤の表に、世界地図の略図が描かれ、なるほど手慣れて上手な絵であったが、朔屋には今更、の、いいやこの世界に住む者の大半にとっては同様の、何ほどもない、という思いを抱かせたろう。
source.english: A disk of ground with a sketch map of the world upon its surface. Certainly a practiced, skillful drawing. But to Sakuya—and surely to most inhabitants of this world—it was hardly a revelation worth making now.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「───およそ世界はこのように、円盤状の平面だ」
source.english: “Broadly speaking, the world is a disk-shaped plane, like this.”

source.japanese: とそこで一つ区切って、沈黙の音を朔屋に伝えたのは、次なる言葉の効果を高めるつもりだったのだろう。
source.english: He paused, conveying the sound of silence to Sakuya. Presumably to enhance the effect of his next words.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「───平面世界だ、というのがおそらくこの世界に住む、ほとんどの人間の理解であり見解なのだろうが、事実は異なる」
source.english: “A flat world: that is probably how most of its inhabitants understand it. The facts are otherwise.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「世界の本来の形は───球状である」
source.english: “The world's original shape is—spherical.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はぁん!?」
source.english: “Whaaat!?”

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「……It is liberation. From this prison of a world. For example……right, do you comprehend the true shape of this world?」
【Naomasa】 （Ugghh……and now he brings up the true shape of the world. Are you seriously gonna ask philosophical questions of some guy you just met?）

Though he said none of it aloud, the look in Sakuya's eyes was skeptical, his brows furrowed in distrust so deep it felt as if he was being openly irreverent even to the grandiose heavens setting the stage, yet the pilgrim needed no answer from Sakuya, for he continued on dispassionately, displaying a considerable patience. Or perhaps it arose from the unwavering confidence of someone who knows the truth.
In any case, the pilgrim continued on as before. This time, however, he lightly thrust forward the staff he carried.

Of course, there was really no need for the young man to be on guard, and it was hardly the case that he was going to physically beat the delusions out of the young man, nor try to crush the eyes that kept glaring at him with such insolence. The pilgrim did nothing more than trace an oval shape before him with the butt end of his staff. That was all, it was nothing more than that, but while there was a thin layer of fresh snow covering the surface, just below was the permafrost, a layer of solid ice. And yet, the butt end of the pilgrim's staff nevertheless carved a line with the ease of drawing on soft sand.

That was also strange, but as he drew, his arm peeked out from beneath the hem of his robe's sleeve; it was a slender and beautiful shape befitting of his voice, but even though its surface seemed covered in wrinkles, it also appeared as smooth as the skin of a maiden, and beneath the aurora's glow, it struck Sakuya as profoundly uncanny. As if entirely oblivious to the young man's bewilderment, the pilgrim added all manner of lines to the oval, and what emerged was something Sakuya found wholly devoid of significance: a replica of this world.

A rough sketch of the world map had been drawn atop the disk-shaped surface, and while it was undeniably skillfully done, certainly, a practiced illustration, it evoked in Sakuya, yea, likely in most who lived in this world, a feeling that, at this point, it was nothing of consequence at all.
【Pilgrim】 「───The world, broadly speaking, is a flat surface shaped like a disc.」
He deliberately paused there, letting the silence reach Sakuya, likely to lend weight to his next words.
【Pilgrim】 「───A flat world. That is, in all likelihood, both the understanding and opinion of the majority of those who live in this world, but the truth lies elsewhere.」
【Pilgrim】 「The true shape of this world───is spherical.」
【Naomasa】 「HUUH!?」

source.japanese: 朔屋の素っ頓狂な驚愕の声をよそに、巡礼者はまた、今度はいまし描いてみせた図の隣に並べて、真円の、ほとんど狂いのがないところをすらすらと。
source.english: Disregarding Sakuya's wildly startled cry, the pilgrim drew again. Beside his first diagram, he smoothly traced a circle almost perfectly true.

source.japanese: 真円の中には世界地図を描き出しはしなかったが、替わりに円周上に置いてみせたのが、簡略化した人の姿だった。これを見つめていたシサムとキサラは、いかにもやっぱり、という風情に目を伏せて吐息を漏らす。知らずともよかった知識をわざわざ晒して見せられたような。
source.english: He did not draw a world map within it. Instead, he placed a simplified human figure upon its circumference. Watching, Sisam and Kisara lowered their eyes and sighed as if to say: yes, just as we thought. As though someone had gone out of his way to expose them to knowledge they would rather never have possessed.

source.japanese: ……そういえばこの双子は、そもそもずっと以前より世界の形に疑問を抱いていたではないか。あの酒場での一夜の前、語っていたではないか。
source.english: …Come to think of it, had these twins not questioned the world's shape long before? Had they not spoken of it before that night in the tavern?

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「これが、本来の世界の形なのだ。閉ざされた平面の世界ではなく、球状の。この球の表面に人々達は存在し、住まいし生きている」
source.english: “This is the world's original shape. Not a closed, flat world, but a sphere. People exist, dwell and live upon its surface.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「ただ、それであるのなら、なぜ万物は地表から虚空に落下していかないのだ、とか、虚空には一体何があるのか、といった事柄に対する説明までは求めないでいただきたい」
source.english: “However, please do not ask me to explain why, in that case, all things do not fall from the surface into the void, or what precisely lies in that void.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「我らはただ『一なる三者』『三位一体者』、そして巡礼者であるだけだ。全知の存在などと驕るつもりもないのでな」
source.english: “We are merely the ‘Three Who Are One,’ the ‘Triune One,’ and pilgrims. We have no wish to arrogate omniscience to ourselves.”

source.japanese: 既にその声その物言いが驕っているのだ、とまでは言い得ず朔屋は、心の中で一番の疑問符を叩きつける。
source.english: That voice, that way of speaking, was already arrogant. Sakuya could not quite say so. Instead, he hurled forth the largest question in his mind.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃ、じゃあ、なにか！
　たとえばこの北限氷土をずっと歩いてったら、ええとそのなんだ、反対側に出て、そのうちもとのところに辿り着くって事かよ!?」
source.english:
“Then—then what?
Say we keep walking through the Northern Ice Wastes. We'd, uh, come out the other side and eventually get back to where we started!?”

source.japanese:
───朔屋の問いは、かつて平面状の世界観の中にあった人々が、自然科学の発達の途上、もたらされる様々な物証から、世界はもしや球状なのではないかという真実に辿り着きつつあった時と同様のものであったろう。
　
　───それであるのなら。
　
　───そもそも朔屋の住む世界は歪なのだ。
　
　───科学も何もかも、人々が球状の世界観を得た時より遙かに隔たっているのに、なぜその真実からは遠ざけられているのだろう。
source.english:
Sakuya's question must have resembled those asked by people once living with a flat-world view, when the growth of natural science and its various proofs brought them toward the truth that the world might be spherical.
If so—the world Sakuya lived in was distorted from the outset.
Science and everything else had advanced far beyond the time when people acquired a spherical view of the world.
Why, then, were they kept apart from that truth?

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「その通りである───ただしそれは、遙かな過去の事なれば」
source.english: “Precisely. Except that belongs to the distant past.”

source.japanese: ……朔屋の、日頃から不健康で柔弱な気の多い顔が、更に壊れたかの表情になった。
source.english: …Sakuya's face—sickly, weak and distractible at the best of times—seemed to break still further.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「かつて。遙かな過去。この世界は球状であった。海に果てなどなく、端は繋がっていた。あなたの言うとおり、航海者はこの北限氷土のみならず、どの方角に漕ぎ出でても、航路さえ過[あやま]たず、天然自然の脅威に耐え抜けば、球状の表面を一周する事も可能だった、という……」
source.english: “Once, in the distant past, this world was spherical. The seas had no end; their edges joined. As you say, a voyager setting out not only through these Northern Ice Wastes but in any direction could, if he kept a true course and survived nature's perils, complete a circuit of the globe. So we are told…”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「それなのに、何時しか世界は閉ざされた」
source.english: “Yet at some point the world was closed.”

source.japanese:
巡礼者は、己の描き出した球状世界の模造図を石突きでなぞると、それは氷原の表に線で上書きされたのではない、消しゴムをかけたように消えていったのだ。その不可思議な消し様も、一つ残った平面世界の模造図も、この世界の有り様をひどく不気味に突きつけているようで───それまでは氷原の、浄められて寒冷な空気が、無数の微細な針となって全身を覆っていくかのような、現実がそれまで秘されていた残酷な真実を牙として迫ってくるような恐怖が、朔屋をがんじがらめにした。
　今やオーロラの優雅な舞踏さえ、人の心を狂気に染めて、真実を見えなくさせるかの毒毒しい光の階調を露わにしたような。
source.english:
The pilgrim ran the ferrule over the diagram of the spherical world. Rather than being crossed by new lines upon the ice, it vanished as though erased. Between that uncanny disappearance and the one diagram left behind—the flat world—the hideous truth of this world's condition seemed thrust before Sakuya's eyes. The ice field's purified, frigid air hardened into countless fine needles against his skin. Terror bound him hand and foot, as though reality itself bore down upon him with the cruel truth hidden until now bared as fangs.
Now even the aurora's graceful dance seemed to reveal poisonous gradations of light, staining the human heart with madness and blinding it to the truth.

target.text: Ignoring the sound of Sakuya's hysterical shock, the pilgrim drew once more, and this time, next to the figure he'd just drawn, he fluidly traced a perfect circle with barely any inaccuracy.

He did not draw a world map within the perfect shape; in its place, he made a clear demonstration out of placing simplified figures of humans along the circumference. Shisamu and Kisara, who had been fixing their eyes upon it, lowered their gazes and let out a sigh, as if to all but say that it was exactly as they had expected. As if knowledge that was better left unknown had deliberately been laid bare before them.

……Now that he thought about it, had these twins not already been harbouring doubts about the shape of this world from the outset, since long ago? Right before that night they spent together in that bar, had they not spoken of it?
【Pilgrim】 「This is the natural shape of the world. The world is not a sealed plane, it is spherical. The people exist, dwell, and live atop the surface of this sphere.」
【Pilgrim】 「However, I must ask that you refrain from seeking any explanations for why nothing falls from the surface and into the void, or what that void truly is.」
【Pilgrim】 「We are but『Those Three As One』, 『Triune Beings』, as well as humble pilgrims. We are not so conceited as to presume ourselves omniscient beings.」

Your voice and the way you speak already reeks of arrogance; not that Sakuya went so far as to voice that thought, but he still struck back by flinging the sharpest question mark he had in his mind back at him.

【Naomasa】 「Th-, then-, so, what!? Are you saying if I, for example, were to keep walking through the northernmost permafrost up here, then, well, uhm, I'd come out on the opposite side, and in due time, I'd make it back to the place I started from!?」

───Sakuya's question was surely of a similar sort to those once asked by the people who lived within the confines of a flat-earth worldview, people who, through the gradual accumulation of material evidence produced by the progress of natural science, began to approach the truth and wonder: Might the world, in fact, be spherical?

───If that was the case, then. ───The world that Sakuya lived in was twisted from the outset. ───Even though science and everything else had advanced to a stage far removed from the age when mankind first embraced a spherical world, how could it be that they were still being kept away from that truth?
【Pilgrim】 「It is just as you say───however, it was only so in the distant past.」
……Sakuya's face, usually pale and frail, of fickle, shifting moods, twisted into an expression that seemed even more broken.

【Pilgrim】 「Long ago. In the distant past. This world was spherical. The seas were endless, connecting at their edges. Just as you say, and it was not limited to this northernmost permafrost, no matter the direction a sailor were to row forth in, if his course stayed true, if he could overcome the perils of nature, it was possible for him to make a full circuit of the spherical surface, it is said……」
【Pilgrim】 「And yet, at some point, the world was closed off.」

The pilgrim traced the imitation sketch that he himself had created of the spherical world with the butt end of his staff, but the lines already drawn were not overwritten, instead vanishing as though he was using an eraser. It was as if the inexplicable way of erasing and the single remaining sketch of the flat world both thrust the deeply uncanny state of this world right before his eyes───the air of the ice field, which had been a purified cold hitherto, now seemed to turn into innumerable minute needles covering his entire body, and a terror as if reality itself was lunging at him, fangs sharpened by the once-hidden horrible truth, bound Sakuya hand and foot.
Now even the graceful dance of the aurora seemed to stain the human heart with the colours of madness, as though it had unveiled odious gradations of light that seemed bent on obscuring the truth.

source.japanese: そして双子達。世界の真実に図らずも直面してしまった者を、痛ましい目で見やる、双子達。なのに、朔屋からは離れたままとはいえ数歩の間なのに、二者の距離は、氷原をそれこそ無限の海原に換えたように遠かった。
source.english: And the twins—the twins looking with pity upon a man who had stumbled unprepared into the truth of the world. They were still only a few steps from Sakuya. Yet the distance between them was as vast as though the ice field had become an infinite ocean.

target.text: And then there were the twins. With pity in their eyes, gazing upon the man who had unwittingly come face to face with the truth of this world, the twins. Although they were still standing apart from Sakuya, it was only a few steps, but they nevertheless seemed so far away, as if the icy wastes beneath their feet had been replaced with a boundless ocean.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「───人類が、人類に対して犯した罪の為、とそのように我々には伝えられている。
　そのために───」
source.english:
“Because of a sin humankind committed against humankind. That is what has been passed down to us.
Therefore—”

source.japanese: と巡礼者が翳[かざ]した杖は、先端に宿した光を、オーロラと同じ階調に揺らめかせながら、彼方、あの小高い山を、双子と朔屋が目指していたあの山を、指し示す。幻光の下でその山は、ただ静かに佇立するのみであったけれど、変移する光の中で───なぜかその影響を受けず、白々と、深海中に積み上げられた白石の金字塔のように異様な存在感を放つようにあった。
source.english: He raised his staff. The light at its tip flickered in the aurora's shades as it pointed far away, at the small mountain the twins and Sakuya had been seeking. Beneath that illusory light it stood silently. Yet amid all the shifting colors, it remained strangely unaffected: stark white, with the uncanny presence of a pyramid of white stones piled upon the deep-sea floor.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「あの山の根に、あの仕組み、機構が設けられたのだ。機械なのか、それとも別の何かなのか、どういう仕組みで作動しているのか、そしてそもそも、いかなる何者かが創造したのか。それも、訊ねられるだけ無駄だ。
　我々が知るのは───」
source.english:
“At the root of that mountain, that apparatus, that mechanism was installed. Whether it is a machine or something else, how it works, and indeed what manner of being created it—asking any of that will be equally futile.
What we know is—”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「その機構が、この世界を今のような形、巨大な平面状の牢獄に変えている、という事。同様の機構はこの北限氷土だけでなく、他にも点在していると言う事、そして……」
source.english: “That it makes this world into its present shape, a vast, flat prison. That similar mechanisms lie scattered elsewhere, not only in these Northern Ice Wastes. And…”

source.japanese: 周囲に参集し、澄んだ、ただし人の持つ、雑念に満ちた心とは隔たりすぎて異質の、澄んだ期待で夜空の幻灯舞踏を仰ぐ同胞達にやや振り返り、
source.english: He turned a little toward the fellows gathered around, who watched the night sky's luminous dance with a pure expectancy—pure, yet alien, impossibly remote from the clutter of a human heart.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「我々の『昇華』に際して発生する、エネルギーの余波……とでも言おうか。比喩的にはそれが適当だろうな。その余波が、かの機構を維持する為の燃料となるという事」
source.english: “The wake of energy released by our ‘sublimation,’ one might call it. The metaphor is apt enough. That residue becomes fuel for maintaining the mechanism.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「へぁ……て、え？」
source.english: “Huh… Wha—eh?”

source.japanese: いまだ真実の毒に、信天翁号の合成酒よりひどい悪酔いに落とし込まれたような心地の、朔屋の疑問の呻[うめ]きは間抜けていたけれど。
source.english: The truth still poisoned Sakuya, making him feel more sickeningly drunk than the Albatross's synthetic liquor ever could. His questioning groan sounded foolish. Yet—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、おい、旦那。
　それは少し、おかしくないか……？」
source.english:
“Hang on, mister.
Isn't that a little… wrong?”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「なにがだね？」
source.english: “What is?”

source.japanese: 問い返す、巡礼者の声も挙措も穏やかに、落ち着いたものであったけれど。
source.english: The pilgrim's answering voice and every gesture were calm and composed. But—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だって、その、なんだか知らないが、からくりが世界を平らにしてて、で、それが牢獄で、あのお……」
source.english: “Well, that thing, whatever it is, flattens the world, and that's the prison, and, uh…”

source.japanese: 自分の思考の道筋にすら狼狽えて、整理をつけようと深く息を吸いこんだ途端に冷え切った空気肺に刺さって咳こんで、まあこの異様な景色の下騒がしい事この上ない、しかしその朔屋の愚かさ弱さ、それがとても人間的で───
source.english: Confused even by the course of his own thinking, he drew a deep breath to collect himself. The freezing air stabbed his lungs; he coughed. What a commotion beneath this uncanny spectacle. Yet Sakuya's foolishness, his weakness, was so very human—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃああんたら、世界を牢獄にすんのに、手ぇ貸してるって事じゃないの！　そんな昇華とか、しなければいいじゃないか」
source.english: “Then aren't you helping turn the world into a prison? Just don't do this sublimation thing!”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「異な事を」
source.english: “What a curious thing to say.”

source.japanese: 引き替えこの巡礼者、そして周囲の同類の者達の、皆穏和で知的に思えるのに、どこか何かが、朔屋が代表する人の弱さ、人らしさを自ら切り離してなお、平然としているかに見えてならず───
source.english: In contrast, this pilgrim and the others around him all appeared gentle and intelligent. Yet they seemed to have calmly excised something from themselves: the human weakness, the very humanness, that Sakuya represented—

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「我々は巡礼者だ、と言ったろう。
　あるいは独覚であるかも知れん。三者が揃えば、だが。けれど菩薩ではない」
source.english:
“I told you we were pilgrims.
Perhaps self-awakened Buddhas, once three are gathered. But not bodhisattvas.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「我々は、我々をこの世界から解放し得たとしても、我々の輪に連ならない者達まではどうしようもないのだよ」
source.english: “Even if we can liberate ourselves from this world, we can do nothing for those outside our circle.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「かの機構を維持する事と引き替え、昇華が許されている。遺憾ではあるが、それ以上でも以下でもない」
source.english: “In return for maintaining that mechanism, we are permitted to undergo sublimation. Regrettably, it is no more and no less than that.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「それ故にこの夜、昼と夜との長さが同じになるこの夜、機構のあるこの地に集い、昇華する」
source.english: “Thus, on this night when day and night are equal, we gather here, where the mechanism lies, and undergo sublimation.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「時機を得ず、また場所を違えれば、昇華の余波は害となり、周囲に被害を及ぼすだろう。過去にはそういう事例もないではない」
source.english: “At the wrong time or in the wrong place, the aftereffects of sublimation become harmful and damage the surroundings. There have been such cases in the past.”

source.japanese:
───それが、朔屋達の出会ったあの難破船での真実なのだろう。
　けれども。朔屋は、巡礼者がもはやどのように整った言葉を連ねようとも、身の裡[うち]を満たす違和感、そして不快感をぬぐい去れず、この寒気の中に何時しか湧き出した額の脂汗を手袋の甲で拭い、足下の危うさを堪[こら]えようとする。
source.english:
That was probably what had happened on the wreck they had encountered.
Yet whatever well-ordered words the pilgrim might now string together, Sakuya could not shake the wrongness, the discomfort filling him. At some point oily sweat had sprung upon his forehead despite the cold. He wiped it with the back of his mitten and tried to steady himself on uncertain feet.

source.japanese: オーロラの遊舞はいよいよ幻妖怪奇の度合いひどくなりまさり、氷原と広がる地平線と、その手前の孤山という、単純で美しいと思えた風景は、全てが滅び去った後の荒廃しきった情景ともとれて青年は吐き気すら覚えたという。
source.english: The aurora's dance grew more and more uncanny. The ice field, the wide horizon, the lone mountain before it: a landscape he had thought simple and beautiful now looked just as readily like the desolation left after everything had perished. It made the young man feel sick.

source.japanese:
巡礼者の言葉は、声が美しく物言いが静かだからこそすらすらと耳に入っても、脳の中で奇怪な城郭を形成し、引き込んだ者を惑わせ出られなくさせるような、その癖その壁を、柱を強く一押しすれば全てがあっさり崩れ去りそう。
　すべて、どこかが妙な説明だった。なにかちぐはぐな、もっともらしいようでいて、自分たちに都合の良い事実だけを選び取っているような話ではないか。
source.english:
Because the voice was beautiful and the manner quiet, the pilgrim's words entered his ears smoothly. Yet in his brain they built a bizarre fortress, drawing people in, bewildering them, leaving no escape. And yet one firm push against its walls, its pillars, seemed enough to bring it all down.
Every explanation was somehow strange. Something did not fit. Plausible, apparently—but were they not simply selecting the facts most convenient to themselves?

source.japanese: 朔屋でさえその辺りの欠陥を指摘できるのに、巡礼者達に於いてはそれが絶対の真実であり、信じ切っている、それがなにより、気持ち悪い。
source.english: Even Sakuya could point out the defects. To the pilgrims, however, their account was absolute truth. They believed it utterly. That was the most repulsive thing of all.

source.japanese:
けれど、と朔屋は踏みとどまった、いや、すがりつこうとした。その事実は異様で不快であれ、彼らがここでひっそりその昇華やらに耽[ふけ]っている分には、実際のところ自分にはどうでもいい、関係のない事だと朔屋は思い込もうとした。
　世界がでかい玉羊羹みたいな形だろうが、それともお盆だろうが、それがそこまで自分に影響あるか？
　影響があるとすれば───
　朔屋は震えそうになる舌の根を懸命に鎮め、なおもしつこく問いかける。
source.english:
But Sakuya stopped himself—no, tried to cling to that thought. Strange and unpleasant though the facts might be, if these people quietly indulged in their sublimation here, it was really none of his business. He tried to persuade himself he did not care.
Did it affect him so much whether the world was shaped like a huge ball of bean jelly or a tray?
If it affected him at all—
Desperately stilling the tongue that threatened to tremble at its root, Sakuya kept asking.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃあもう、その辺りのおかしい点はどうでも良いよ。
　とにかくキサラとシサムも、そこの二人も、あんた達と同じ人種なんだな？」
source.english:
“Fine, forget what's wrong with all that. Anyway,
Kisara and Sisam, those two there, they're the same race as you?”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「人種が同じかどうかは、問題ではないよ。我らの中にはコーカソイドもニグロイドもモンゴロイドも、あるいは混血の者もある。重要とされるのは、『一なる三者』の遺伝的因子を持つかどうか───」
source.english: “Whether we are of the same race is immaterial. Among us are Caucasoids, Negroids, Mongoloids, and those of mixed descent. What matters is possessing the genetic factor of the ‘Three Who Are One’—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああもう！　だからとにかく、シサムとキサラもそうなのか？　あんた達と同じなのかって訊いてんだようっ」
source.english: “Oh, for—! I mean, are Sisam and Kisara like that too? Are they the same as you? That's what I'm asking!”

source.japanese: 然り。
source.english: Yes.

source.japanese:
それが巡礼者の答えで。
　その答えを聞いた時に、巡礼者達の列と朔屋の間の位置に留まっていた双子が、目を伏せて、一歩、踏み出して、巡礼者達に向かって。朔屋からは離れて。
source.english:
That was the pilgrim's answer.
Hearing it, the twins, who had lingered between Sakuya and the pilgrims' ranks, lowered their eyes and took a step. Toward the pilgrims. Away from him.

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「───A consequence of the grave sin that mankind committed against itself. Such is the manner in which it was passed down to us. For that reason───」

So the pilgrim said as he lifted up his staff, the light dwelling at the tip flickering with the same gradations as the aurora all the while, pointed into the distance, at that modest mountain, towards the mountain that the twins and Sakuya had been journeying towards. Underneath the phantasmal light, that mountain merely stood still in quietude, but bathed in the mutating rays───it alone, for some reason, remained utterly unaffected, a pale white, emitting a bizarre presence, like a pyramid of white stone erected in the depths of the ocean.

【Pilgrim】 「That mechanism, that structure, was established at the very roots of that mountain. Is it some manner of machine, or is it something entirely different, how does the contraption itself operate, and to begin with, by what manner of being was it created? Asking about that would also be futile. All that we know is───」

【Pilgrim】 「Ultimately, that machine is what is transforming the world into the shape it takes now: a colossal, flat prison. There are similar machines, not just here at the northernmost permafrost, but scattered about in other places, and finally……」

He turned slightly to look back at his brethren who had congregated around him, their eyes lifted to the illusory lights dancing across the night sky, not with the muddled hearts of men filled with worldly thoughts, but with a clarity of anticipation of an utterly foreign quality.

【Pilgrim】 「The residual ripples of the energy generated during our『Sublimation』 ……if I may call them that. I suppose that is fitting, in a figurative sense. Those ripples become the fuel needed to keep that structure running.」
【Naomasa】 「Bwah……wait, huh?」

Still reeling from the poison of the truth, feeling as if he'd been plunged into an even more nauseating stupor than what he'd suffer from after drinking the Albatross' synthetic sake, Sakuya's groans of doubt sounded rather idiotic, admittedly.
【Naomasa】 「No, hey, buddy. Don't you think that's a little strange……?」
【Pilgrim】 「And what do you mean by that?」
Asking a question in return, both the pilgrim's voice and mannerisms were gentle, relaxed, and yet.
【Naomasa】 「Well, that's because, uhm, I'm not sure what it is exactly, but that contraption makes the world flat, and then, that's a prison, and, uhhh……」

He was flustered even by his own train of thought, and when he took a deep breath to organize it, immediately after, the freezing air stabbed his lungs, sending him into a coughing fit; goodness, it was noisy beyond belief amidst this surreal scenery, but Sakuya's foolishness and weakness were only all too human───
【Naomasa】 「So then, you people are basically lending a hand with turning the world into a prison, aren't you!? Couldn't you just not do that-, that sublimation or whatever?」
【Pilgrim】 「What a peculiar thing to say.」

In contrast, though this pilgrim, as well as his kin surrounding them, all seemed pleasantly mild and intellectual, there was something off about them; he couldn't help but feel that they appeared so perfectly serene only because they had cut off that very human frailty, that humanity that Sakuya embodied.

【Pilgrim】 「As I am certain that I told you already, we are pilgrims. Or perhaps we are the solitary awakened. Should the three be gathered, that is. We are not, however, bodhisattva.」 (TN: The solitary awakened, written "独覚", is the Japanese term for a pratyekabuddha, one who reaches enlightenment independently, without the aid of teachers or guides and does not preach the path to others. Bodhisattva are those who vow to attain full buddhahood to liberate all living beings, remaining in the cycle of existence out of supreme compassion.)
【Pilgrim】 「Even should we achieve our own liberation from this world, there is nothing we can do for those who cannot join our fold.」
【Pilgrim】 「In exchange for maintaining that structure, we are permitted sublimation. Lamentable as it may be, it is nothing more, nothing less.」
【Pilgrim】 「Thus, on this night, this night upon which day and night share equal length, we assemble in this land where the structure rests, and we sublimate.」

【Pilgrim】 「If we fail to seize the right moment, or the place is mischosen, the ripples of the sublimation bring harm, and the damage will likely extend to the surroundings. It is not without precedent.」

───That was likely the truth of what had occurred on the wrecked ship that Sakuya and company had encountered. However. At this point, even should the pilgrim string together chains composed of the most elegantly refined of words, the feeling of discomfort and displeasure filling up Sakuya's entire body to the bursting point would not be erased; he wiped away the greasy sweat that had at some point begun to trickle down his brow, even in this freezing air, with his mitten, trying to stand firm against his unsteady feet.

By now, the swirling dance of the aurora was intensifying into a phantasmagoria, growing ever more grotesquely surreal; the frozen field and the horizon unfolding beyond it, as well as the solitary mountain that stood before them, all scenery that seemed plainly beautiful, now resembled a landscape of utter desolation, the aftermath wrought by total annihilation, and it was enough to even make the young man nauseous.

Though the pilgrim's words glided effortlessly into his ears precisely because his voice was beautiful and his cadence calm, they constructed a bizarre citadel within his mind, the sort that bewildered and mislead any it could draw inside its walls, keeping them trapped, and yet in spite of that, it also felt as if with but a single firm push against a wall or a pillar, the entire thing would quickly crumble into dust.

Every part of his explanation had something strangely off about it, somewhere. Something about it was incoherent and disjointed, and though it sounded perfectly reasonable on the surface, did it not seem like a narrative where they had selectively picked out only the truth that conveniently served their agenda?

Though even Sakuya of all people could identify the flaws in their narrative, to these pilgrims, it was the absolute truth, something they held unwavering faith in, and that was the most revolting thing of all.

However, Sakuya thought as he held his ground, no, attempted to cling to whatever he had left of it. No matter how bizarre and unpleasant that truth may be, as long as they were just quietly absorbed in their sublimation or whatever it was they did in this place, in actuality, it didn't really mean anything to him, it was something completely unrelated, or so Sakuya attempted to convince himself.

Whether the world was shaped like a giant ball of youkan or a platter, how much did that actually personally affect him? If it did truly affect him in any way, then it was only─── Sakuya did his utmost to wrest back control of the trembling root of his tongue, then stubbornly persisted with his questioning. (TN: Youkan, written "羊羹", is a jellied desert made from red bean paste, agar, and sugar.)
【Naomasa】 「All right then, I'm done caring about any of those inconsistencies. Anyways, Kisara and Shisamu, both of them, are they the same kind of people as you?」

【Pilgrim】 「Being of the same kind is not an issue. We count amongst our fold Caucasoids, Negroids, and Mongoloids, possibly some even of mixed blood. What is considered essential is whether or not one possesses the genetic factor of 『Those Three As One』───」 (TN: The word used here, "人種", can mean both race of people as well as kind/type of people.)
【Naomasa】 「Aargh, come on! That's what I'm asking about, are Shisamu and Kisara like that? I'm just asking if they're the same as you!」
Yea.

That was the pilgrim's answer. When they heard that answer, the twins, who had come to a halt between the group of pilgrims and Sakuya, cast their eyes downwards, then took one step forwards, towards the pilgrims. Away from Sakuya.

source.japanese:
片割れが朔屋へ少し、季節に残され散り残った一輪の花が、同じく季節外れの風に流されたように想いを遺して振り返ったけれどそれも僅かの、横顔をやや見せたのみ。一方の片割れが彼女の腕を取って進んでいく。呼びかけたいけれど、今の横顔だけでは、この位置からは見えない、それが朔屋をついに狂乱させた。
　両腕をがばと上げて頭を抱え込み、足はじたばたと氷原を踏んだがその場でばたつくのみで、前に進むどころか氷に滑って転倒し損ねる、必死で体を残して、巡礼者にすがりつこうとする───
source.english:
One of the pair looked back at Sakuya for a moment, leaving regret behind like a solitary flower carried off by a wind as untimely as the season that had spared it. But it lasted only an instant; she showed him no more than a sliver of profile. The other twin took her arm and led her on. He wanted to call out, but from where he stood that glimpse was not enough to tell him which twin had turned. That uncertainty finally drove Sakuya into a frenzy.
He flung both arms up and clutched his head. His feet scrabbled frantically at the ice but carried him nowhere; far from moving forward, he nearly slipped and fell. Fighting desperately to keep his balance, he tried to cling to the pilgrim—

target.text: One half turned her head slightly, a trace of emotion lingering, like a solitary flower left behind by the turning of the seasons, still clinging to its blossom, being swept away by a similarly unseasonable wind; it was only a faint movement, offering just a slight glimpse of her profile. The other half grabbed the woman's arm and moved onwards. He wanted to call out to her, but that glimpse alone revealed nothing from where he stood, and that was what ultimately sent Sakuya into a frenzy.

He suddenly raised both his arms and buried his head within them, he kicked and flailed against the ice, but he only thrashed in place; rather than moving towards them, he nearly slipped and fell over on the ice, and with frantic effort, he reached out to the pilgrim, attempting to cling to him───

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわ、うわあああっ。
　そりゃあねえようっ」
source.english:
“Oh, ohhh!
That's not fair!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「と、とりなしてくだせっ。
　とりなしてくだせっ。
　わしも連れていってくだせっ」
source.english:
“P-please put in a word for me, sir!
Put in a word for me!
Take me along too!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Wah, waaaaah! That's just wrong!」
【Naomasa】 「P-, please intervene for me! Smooth things over, please! Please take me with you too!」

source.japanese: 隠れた山村の隠れ切支丹の老人が、その宗派で尊崇される聖人に哀願するように、巡礼者に縋[すが]りつこうとする───も。
source.english: Like an old hidden Christian from a secluded mountain village pleading with a saint revered by his sect, he tried to cling to the pilgrim. But—

target.text: Like an elderly hidden Christian of a secluded mountain village entreating the saint venerated in his denomination, he tried to cling to the pilgrim─── but.

source.japanese:
眼前を燐光が塞いだ。目を灼く程の光量はなかったけれども、異様な色合いと階調が青年の意識を掻[か]き回し、もう耐えきれずにどすんとその場に尻もちの、脚だけがなおもばたばたやっているのが見苦しい。
　本当に、朔屋は何処でも何時でも、無様で見苦しい。
source.english:
Phosphorescence blocked his eyes. Not enough light to burn them, yet its strange colors and gradations churned his mind. Unable to bear any more, he landed heavily on his ass. Only his legs kept flailing, an ugly sight.
Truly, anywhere and always, Sakuya was pathetic and unsightly.

source.japanese: 腰を突いた青年に、杖はなおも擬されて矛先逸らさず、その先端でオーロラと同じ光が、夜天の拍子と同期して揺らめいて、やはり光は発光体も芯もなく、ただ光のみが灯っているのだった。
source.english: The staff remained aimed at the fallen young man. At its tip, the same light as the aurora wavered in time with the sky. Again, it had no luminous body, no wick. Only light burned there.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それなら、俺も連れて行ってくれようっ。俺も仲間にしてくれよっ。シサムとキサラと、一緒にさせろようっ」
source.english: “Then take me with you! Let me join! Let me stay with Sisam and Kisara!”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「お断りする。
　そもそもあなたには我らに列するべき因子がかけている」
source.english:
“We refuse.
In the first place, you lack the factor necessary to join us.”

source.japanese: 『お断りする』
source.english: ‘We refuse.’

source.japanese:
『お断りする』
『お断りする』
『お断りする』
source.english:
‘We refuse.’
‘We refuse.’
‘We refuse.’

source.japanese:
『おことわりする』
『おことわりする』
『おことわりする』
『おとこわりする』
『おことわりする』
source.english:
‘We refuse.’
‘We refuse.’
‘We refuse.’
‘We reufse.’
‘We refuse.’

source.japanese: 杖の光に視界がふさがれて、見えない姿からの声は、音源さえも狂ったかのように、朔屋に右から左から、前から後ろわんわんと襲いかかり、青年を翻弄し、いよいよ意識を、脳を掻[か]き回し、吐かせる寸前まで胃の腑を締め上げてから、ようやく解放した、で、脂汗で滲む視界に見れば。
source.english: With the staff's light blocking his sight, voices came from unseen figures. Their very sources seemed deranged; they roared at Sakuya from right and left, front and back, tossing him about, churning his consciousness, his brain, tightening his stomach almost to vomiting. At last they released him. Through a vision blurred with oily sweat he saw—

source.japanese: それまで朔屋に相対して者のみならず、幾人もの巡礼者達が青年を包囲して、幻光宿す杖を突きつけ、拒絶の言葉を口々に発して、呪詛のように投げつけているのだ。
source.english: Not only the man who had faced him before but many other pilgrims now surrounded Sakuya, thrusting their staffs of illusory light toward him and hurling words of rejection like curses.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「あなたを我らの輪の中に容れる事は、到底できかねる。あなたは、この世界の鬼子だ。
　一体いかなる存在が、あなたのような異物を産んだのだ」
source.english:
“We cannot possibly admit you into our circle. You are this world's monstrous child.
What manner of being could have given birth to such an alien thing as you?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え……なにそれ。なんで俺まであんた達と同類的に言われにゃならんの。俺なんかなんの変哲もないただの人間だって言うのに」
source.english: “Huh… What's that mean? Why do you get to talk as though I were one of your kind? I'm just a completely ordinary human being.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「というか今あんたら、人の事こんな風に意地悪に取り囲んでおいて、誰か一人、とちったろう？」
source.english: “Actually, while you were all surrounding me and being nasty like that, one of you messed it up, didn't you?”

source.japanese: いかに巡礼者達が暴力的手段からは遠いように見えても、力を行使する時は容赦ないのがこの手の人種の恐ろしさだし、状況としては朔屋になにも活路は見えない、にもかかわらず余計な事ばかりは聞き分け言ってのけるあたり、事態が見えているのかいないのか。
source.english: However far removed from violence these pilgrims might appear, the frightening thing about their kind was the merciless force they wielded once roused. Sakuya could see no way out. Yet he still picked out and voiced every irrelevant detail. Did he understand what was happening, or not?

source.japanese: この手の一件知的に見える人種というのは、それが綻びかけたところを指摘されたりすると取り上せる、朔屋がやってしまったのはまさにそういう蚋[ブヨ]の一刺し、刺す時にはぢくりと痛いのに加えて後を引く、鬱陶しく猛烈に痒くなる、人を怒らせて当たり前、もういけない。
source.english: People of this superficially intellectual sort grew heated whenever someone pointed to a tear in the facade. Sakuya had inflicted exactly such a gnat bite: a sharp pain at first, followed by a lingering, maddening itch. Naturally it angered them. Now he was done for.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「聖双生児と共に参った者であればこそ、話もしたものを、あなたは」
source.english: “We spoke to you only because you came with the Sacred Twins. Yet you—”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「あなたの時はもう尽きた。
　我らの列に迎えるは愚か、この場にもいてもらいたくはない。
　我々の時も迫りつつある」
source.english:
“Your time is up.
Far from welcoming you into our ranks, we no longer wish you even to remain here.
Our own time draws near.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「あのお二人に免じて、これ以上の実力行使は控えるが───去ね。この場から」
source.english: “For those two ladies' sake, we will refrain from further force. But—begone. Leave this place.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんな怒んなくったって……」
source.english: “No need to get so angry…”

source.japanese: もう何を言ったところで、朔屋の声と顔と言葉と振る舞いは、相手の神経を逆なでにした上に、やはり後に鬱陶しくしくしくさせる薊[アザミ]の棘、怒らせるばかりなのをいい加減に理解した方が良い。なにしろ彼は『世界の鬼子』とやらでもあるらしいのだし。
source.english: Whatever he said now, Sakuya's voice, face, words and behavior scraped their nerves, then continued to irritate like a lingering thistle prick. He ought at last to understand that he could only anger them. After all, he apparently was this ‘world's monstrous child.’

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「疾く疾[と]くと、この場から去りたまえ」
source.english: “Go. Go at once from this place.”

target.text: A phosphorescent light obstructed his eyes. It was not so bright as to burn them, but the bizarre hues and gradations churned the young man's consciousness around, and when he could no longer endure it, he fell right on his backside, his legs alone still flapping about in an unsightly spectacle. Truly, no matter the time or the place, Sakuya was disgraceful in his clumsiness.

The staff was still pointed at the young man after he landed on his behind, aim held steady, the light crowning the tip the very same as the aurora, flickering in synchronized flashes with the night sky; there really was no luminous body or burning core there, just light and nothing more.
【Naomasa】 「In that case, please take me with you too! Let me join your fold! Please, just let me stay with Shisamu and Kisara!」
【Pilgrim】 「We refuse. To begin with, you lack the factor one must possess to join our fold.」
『We refuse』
『We refuse』 『We refuse』 『We refuse』
『WE REFUSE』 『WE REFUSE』 『WE REFUSE』 『WE REFUSE』 『WE REFUSE』

The light from the staff obstructed his vision, and it felt as if even the source of the voice coming from the unseen figure was wrong; it loudly echoed from left and right, from his front and his back, as it assaulted him, the young man left entirely at its mercy, and as he was finally liberated from his consciousness being stirred around, his stomach constricting until he was on the verge of vomiting, there, what he saw through his eyes, vision blurry with greasy sweat.

It was no longer just the man who had hitherto faced Sakuya, several other pilgrims had surrounded the young man, thrusting their staves housing illusory light at him, uttering words of rejection in chorus, hurling them at him like maledictions.

【Pilgrim】 「It would be utterly unthinkable to let you into our fold. You are a changeling of this world. Whatever manner of entity could possibly have spawned an aberration such as you?」 (TN: The term used here is onigo, written "鬼子", a rare term used for unnatural offspring, like babies born with teeth or children who don't resemble their parents. It carries a lot of similarities with the concept of a changeling.)
【Naomasa】 「Huh……what's that supposed to mean? Why do I also have to be lumped in with your kind? I'm just a regular old human being, nothing out of the ordinary.」
【Naomasa】 「I mean, come on, after being so cruel and ganging on me like this, one of you just messed up there, right?」

No matter how far removed the pilgrims may have seemed from using violent means, the true terror of these kinds of people was how merciless they would be when finally resorting to exercising force; as things stood, there seemed to be no means of escape for Sakuya, and yet in spite of that, he kept blurting out nothing but uncalled-for remarks, so was he truly aware of the situation he was in?

This kind of person, one who seems intellectual at first glance, tends to flare up in anger when someone identifies the part of their logic that is fraying at the seams, and what Sakuya had done was exactly that; like the bite of a black fly, not only did it bring with it a throbbing pain at the time of the bite, it lingered with an obnoxiously fierce itch; anyone would be furious, unable to take it anymore.
【Pilgrim】 「It was only because you arrived together with the sacred twins that we chose to speak at all, and yet you!」
【Pilgrim】 「Your time is already spent. Not only would welcoming you into our fold be absurd, we do not even want you present in this place. Our time, too, is fast approaching.」
【Pilgrim】 「In deference to those two, we shall refrain from any further use of force, but───begone. From this place.」
【Naomasa】 「You don't have to get that mad……」

By now, no matter what he said, Sakuya's voice, face, words, and demeanour, on top of getting on their nerves, seemed all like the barbs of a thistle, leaving behind a persistently irritating, dull pain, and it really would be best if he just got it into his thick skull that he was only riling them up. After all, he was supposedly a so-called "changeling of this world".
【Pilgrim】 「Make haste, make haste, pray leave this place!」

source.japanese: 朔屋は右を見て、左を見て、前後に目をやって、後だけは僅かに巡礼者が、言葉を違えず退散の為に開けておいてくれたけれど。彼の求める者は後にはない。後にあるのは恥と失敗と怠慢と放蕩の日々ばかり、その中に見つけた、それだけは掴みたい光は二つ、こんな、変な奴らが居丈高に振り回して変な杖の芯のない光ではない、空にぶわぶわでぶっちょのベリーダンサーの裾[すそ]みたいに翻[ひるがえ]っている気色悪いのでもない、もっと鮮烈で、もっと気持ちよくて、もっともっと熱くて、胸を焦がす程で───!!
source.english: Sakuya looked right, left, ahead, behind. Only behind had the pilgrims left a narrow opening, true to their word, for his retreat. What he sought was not behind him. Behind lay only days of shame, failure, idleness, and debauchery. In the midst of those days he had found two lights, the one thing he wanted to seize. Not the wickless glow in the strange staffs these strange people brandished so pompously. Not that disgusting thing billowing overhead like the hem of a fat belly dancer. Something more vivid, more pleasurable, much, much hotter. Hot enough to scorch his heart—!

target.text: Sakuya looked to his right and left, his front and back, and there was only a slight gap between the pilgrims to his rear, a way left open for his retreat, true to their word, but. The ones he longed for were not behind him.

All that awaited him there were those days filled with nothing but shame and failure and sloth and debauchery, and amidst those, he had found two lights, and those alone, those were what he needed to hold on to; not the hollow light of these strange staves brandished with overbearing arrogance by freaks, not the sickening light flapping around in the skies like a blobby butterball of a belly dancer, they were more vivid, more euphoric, hotter still, so hot it set his heart aflame───!!

source.japanese: その二つの光も、朔屋の前に立ち並ぶ巡礼者に遮[さえぎ]られてもう見えない───いや、見える！　見えてそして、朔屋は慄然とした。
source.english: Those two lights were hidden now by the pilgrims standing before him. No—he could see them! And seeing, he shuddered.

source.japanese:
巡礼者達の肩越しに、夜気の中に光が散っている、光の珠が舞っている。オーロラのように妖しくも壮麗には広がっていないけれど、巡礼者達の杖の光のように不可思議な作用も示していないけれど、それらのどれよりも、痛切なくらいに綺麗に光り、舞い散り、宙に鮮烈で、けれど優しい光を軌跡と残し、そして儚く消えていく。
　それは、双子から零れる光。彼女たちの金の髪から、肩口の線から、背中の陰影から湧き出しては零れて流れ漂う光の粒。
　セント・エルモの灯火としての双子の。
source.english:
Over the pilgrims' shoulders, light scattered in the night air. Beads of light danced. They did not unfold as eerily and magnificently as the aurora, nor display the staffs' mysterious effects. Yet they were more beautiful than either, painfully beautiful, dancing and falling, leaving trails of vivid yet gentle light in the air before vanishing.
Light spilling from the twins. Grains welling from their golden hair, the lines of their shoulders, the shadows of their backs; spilling, flowing, drifting.
Light from the twins as St. Elmo's fire.

target.text: Even those two lights could no longer be seen, obstructed from view by the pilgrims forming a line before Sakuya───no, he could see them! And as they came into sight, a chilling dread washed over Sakuya.

Over the shoulders of the pilgrims, light was dispersing in the night air, pearls of light swirling about. It was not as bewitching as the aurora, nor did it unfold in as grandiose a manner, and it demonstrated no inexplicable effects like the light from the pilgrim's staves, but it shone more beautifully than either of them, so much so it made his heart ache; it scattered like a dance, blazing vividly through the air yet leaving behind gentle trails of light, then vanished, fading so fleetingly.

It was light spilling from the twins. From their golden hair, from the curves of their shoulders, from the shadows across their backs, it gushed out, shedding as flowing, drifting motes of light. From the twins, as the embodiments of St. Elmo's fire.

source.japanese:
往ってしまおうとしている。
　双子が。
　信天翁号の航海士としてではなく。
　シサムとキサラという、二人の女としてでもなく。朔屋が抱いた女としてではなく。
source.english:
They were about to go.
The twins.
Not as navigators of the Albatross.
Not as the two women Sisam and Kisara. Not as women Sakuya had held.

source.japanese:
海の伝説としての。
　セント・エルモの灯火が。
　一なる三者という別の伝説の中に入り交じり、消えていこうとしている。
source.english:
But as a legend of the sea.
As St. Elmo's light.
They were about to mingle with another legend—the Three Who Are One—and disappear.

source.japanese:
───朔屋の焦りに合わせたように、せせら笑うように。
　巡礼者達の、朔屋を包囲していない者達、朔屋の醜態を遠巻きにしていた者達が分かれて、三人一組にまとまって、その意味はさすがに察しの悪い朔屋にも怖ろしく迫った。
source.english:
As if keeping time with Sakuya's panic, as if mocking him,
the pilgrims who had been watching his disgrace from a distance began dividing into groups of three. Even slow-witted Sakuya understood what that meant, and the realization bore down upon him with terror.

source.japanese:
う、と朔屋は耳元へ手をやったのは、周囲に幽かな音が鳴り出したのを捉えたからの、それはかそけき音ではあったが、一度聞いてしまうと妙に青年の耳についた。衣擦れのような、あるいは別の、ぱちぱちと弾けるような。何か音源があるのではなく、周囲の空気それ自体が発しているかのような。
　強いて言えば、夜天のオーロラから垂れ落ちてきているような、だ。雨の日の送電線の鉄塔の下で聞く音に近いと言えば言えるかも知れない。
　朔屋がもしオーロラに関しての多少の知識があれば、『オーロラの音』という現象に心当たりがあったかも知れないしかし。
source.english:
Uh. Sakuya put a hand to his ear. A faint sound had begun around him. Quiet though it was, once heard, it caught strangely at his attention. Like rustling clothing, or something else: a crackle. It came from no particular source, as though the surrounding air itself made it.
If forced to place it, he would have said it dripped from the aurora overhead. It was perhaps a little like the sound beneath an electrical pylon on a rainy day.
Had Sakuya known anything of auroras, the phenomenon called ‘auroral sound’ might have occurred to him. But—

source.japanese:
その、衣擦れとも泡が立つ音とも別の、音が。鈴虫の音に近いが、その松風の響きは銀の羽が奏でだしているかのように、より清かで美しい。
　美しいが、朔屋の戦慄と焦りをより深める、それはそちらの音の出所は判るから。
　───その細かく響いて震える音は、三人一組に集った巡礼者達から響いてくるのであった。だから、今や氷原のあちこちで湧き立っていた。一つ一つはかそけき音なのに、幾つも重なると、異界異妖の重奏となり氷原に渡る。この調べが意味するところ。
source.english:
Then came another sound, neither that rustling nor the sound of bubbles. Something like the song of a bell cricket, but clearer and lovelier, its pine-wind sigh as though played by silver wings.
Beautiful—yet it deepened Sakuya's dread and urgency, because this time he knew the source.
Those fine, trembling notes rose from the pilgrims gathered in threes. Now they sprang up across the ice field. Each alone was faint; layered together, they became an uncanny ensemble of another world, sweeping over the ice. What this music meant—

source.japanese:
朔屋の推測はすぐに現実となった。
　始まりは、一組の三位一体者から。
　よく似た背丈の者達だったが、頭巾長衣の扮装では輪郭が判然としない、と見ると揃って長衣をするりと肩から抜いた。三人とも細身の体格の、似通った、美しい面差しの男女達、が、輪になって、見つめ合って。
　手と手、取り合って───
source.english:
Sakuya's guess soon became reality.
It began with one triune group.
They were similar in height, but their hoods and robes obscured their outlines. Then, as one, they slipped the robes from their shoulders. Three slender figures—men and women with similar, beautiful faces—formed a circle and looked at one another.
They took each other's hands—

target.text: They were about to leave for good. The twins. Not as mates of the Albatross. Not as the two women who went by Shisamu and Kisara. Not as the women who Sakuya had made love to.
As a legend of the seas. St. Elmo's fire. Was being weaved into the fabric of another legend, of those three as one, and fading away.

───As though sneering at him, as though keeping cadence with Sakuya's growing desperation. The pilgrims, those among them who were not enclosing Sakuya directly, those who surrounded him at a distance and observed his humiliating display, they split, then gathered into groups of three, and the significance of it weighed down on him with such terrifying imminence that even the slow-witted Sakuya grasped it.

With a groan, Sakuya brought a hand close to his ear, for he had perceived a faint sound ringing out from his surroundings, and while it was an elusive whisper of a sound, after hearing it once, it clung to his ear in a strange manner. Like the rustling of cloth, or perhaps it was something else, like a crackling or a popping. There wasn't any source of the sound, and it was as if it was being generated by the very air around him itself.

If he had to choose something, it was as though it dripped down from the aurora in the night sky. One might say it was similar to the sound one could hear when standing below a transmission tower on a rainy day. If Sakuya were a bit more knowledgeable about auroras, perhaps he might have guessed it to be the phenomenon known as 『The Sound of the Aurora Borealis』

That sound, it was different from both that of rustling cloth and bubbling water. Though it echoed the chirping of bell crickets, that rustling of wind through the pines sounded even clearer and more beautiful, like a melody played by wings of silver. It was beautiful, but it only intensified Sakuya's impatient dread, and that was because he realized where the sound originated from.

───This delicately resonating, trembling sound, it rang out from the pilgrims who had gathered in groups of three. And that was why it was suddenly surging forth from all over the ice field now. Individually, they were but fleeting notes quavering at the edge of silence, but when overlapping in many layers, it became an instrumental ensemble of otherworldly apparitions that spanned the entire ice field. The meaning carried by this melody was───

Sakuya's conjecture immediately became reality. It began with a single group of Triune Beings. They were people of a very similar stature, but he couldn't clearly discern the outlines of their bodies, disguised beneath hooded robes as they were, but just as he made that observation, they all smoothly slid the robes off their shoulders in unison. All three were of slender builds, they closely resembled each other, men and women with beautiful features, but, they formed a ring, locked eyes with each other. Joined hands───

source.japanese:
光が。
　
　輪の中に。
　オーロラと良く似通う光が、輪の中の空間に生じ、初めは拳大の燐光だったのが見る間に、脈打ちながら拡大し、輝滅しながら光度を増して三人を呑み込んで、最大限のその輝きは、カメラのストロボフラッシュの焚いた如きだが、不思議に目を灼かない。ただ眩ゆさの印象ばかりを置き遺して───爆ぜた。
source.english:
Light.
Within the circle.
A light much like the aurora appeared in the space between them, at first no more than a fist-sized phosphorescence. Before Sakuya's eyes it expanded, pulsing and flickering, growing brighter, swallowing all three. At its height it blazed like a camera flash, yet strangely did not sear his eyes. It left only the impression of dazzling brilliance—and burst.

target.text: Light. From within their circle. A light strikingly similar to the aurora emerged in the space at the center of the circle; at first, it was but a phosphorescent, fist-sized glow, but before his very eyes, it expanded while pulsating, flickering as it intensified in brightness, consuming the three within itself, and at the peak of its brilliance, it was like the flare of a camera's strobe flash, but strangely enough, it did not sear his eyes. It merely left behind the impression of a dazzling radiance───and exploded.

source.japanese:
数百の光球が爆発的に周囲に舞い散り、舞い踊る、舞い狂う、その光球達の群れの中心から───飛翔した。
　あの三人組だ。一糸まとわぬ裸形は光で組成され、異様なまでに美しい。その姿が光の箭[や]となって夜空に、光度を増すにつれ速度も増して、しまいに目で追い切れぬ程の疾[はや]さを得てオーロラに駕し、光紗貫いてそのまま見えなくなった、消えた、まさしく光の昇華で。
　飛翔し去った者達は、皆一様に至福の笑みを湛えていて、それが朔屋をこの上なく怯えさせた。ただ至福、と判じられるのは、そういう笑みの形であるからだけで、感情自体は一切感じられなかったから。
source.english:
Hundreds of luminous spheres exploded outward, dancing, whirling madly.
From the center of their swarm, the three took flight. Their naked forms were composed of light, beautiful to an uncanny degree. They became arrows of light in the night sky, gaining speed as they brightened, finally too fast for the eyes to follow. They mounted the aurora, pierced its luminous gauze and disappeared. Vanished.
Precisely a sublimation of light. Every departing figure wore the same blissful smile. That frightened Sakuya more than anything. He could judge them blissful only from the smiles' shape. No emotion itself could be felt in them.

source.japanese:
一方、地上には光の弾けた際に生じた光球がまだ残り、巨大な蛍の乱舞のように舞っていたが、するうち一つが宙に高く舞い上がったけれども、こちらはオーロラまで届かず、中点に暫[しばら]く飛び回っていたけれど、不意にある一方へ、彼方に佇立するあの孤山に。その頂きに───吸いこまれて消えた。
　その一つの珠を皮切りに、遺されていた珠も次々と後を追う。全て孤山の頂きに吸いこまれて消えていく。
　あれが、昇華のエネルギーの余波を機構の維持に回すと言う事なのだろうかと、そう考える朔屋の歯ががちがち鳴っていたのは、寒気が増してきた為ではない。むしろ寒さなどは気にしていなかった。
source.english:
On the ground, the spheres thrown off by the burst remained, whirling like giant fireflies. One rose high, though not as far as the aurora. It circled for a while midway, then suddenly flew in one direction: toward that solitary mountain.
Into its summit—drawn in, gone. After that first bead, the remaining ones followed in succession. Every one was sucked into the summit and disappeared.
Was this what the pilgrim meant by diverting the residual energy of sublimation to maintain the mechanism? Sakuya's teeth chattered as he thought it. Not because the cold had increased. He was no longer aware of the cold at all.

source.japanese:
朔屋は、孤山に吸いこまれた光球の中にも、顔を見ていたのである。それもまた、三人組の顔だった。幾つも幾つも別れていたけれど、全て三人の。表情だけが異なってあり、それが朔屋を恐怖させたのだ。
　光球内の顔が浮かべていた表情は───
source.english:
For Sakuya had seen faces within the luminous spheres drawn into the mountain: the faces of those same three people. Divided among sphere after sphere, yet every one belonged to the triad. Only their expressions differed, and that was what frightened him.
The faces within the spheres wore—

source.japanese:
恐怖。絶望。苦悶。無念。未練。失望。諦念。狂気。自棄。怨念。
　そしてそれらの表情の基幹を為していたのは、裏切られた、という怒りの。
　裏切られたと恐怖し、裏切られたと苦悶し、裏切られたと諦めてあったのだが一体何に裏切られたというのか。
　そして、天を抜けて飛翔していった三体にして一つの光体よりも、よほど人間の表情に見えたのが、朔屋を更なる恐怖の縁に追い込んだ。
source.english:
Fear. Despair. Agony. Bitterness. Lingering attachment. Disappointment. Resignation. Madness. Desperation. Rancor.
And at the root of all those expressions was the anger of betrayal.
Betrayed, they were afraid; betrayed, they agonized; betrayed, they gave up.
But betrayed by what? Those looked far more like human expressions than the three bodies fused into one luminous being that had flown through the heavens. That drove Sakuya to the brink of an even deeper terror.

source.japanese:
昇華。昇華。この檻のような平面世界からの解放、解脱、あんなものが？　とそれを云々している暇は、今の朔屋にはない。
　離れゆくシサムとキサラの前に、進み出た一人の巡礼者があった。見た限りでは、連れ添う者達がない一人きりの巡礼者。
　つまり、それはきっと。
　朔屋の恐れは現実化した。
source.english:
Sublimation. Sublimation. Liberation, deliverance from this cage of a flat world—that thing? Sakuya had no time to debate it now.
A pilgrim stepped forward before Sisam and Kisara as they departed. Apparently alone, without companions.
Which surely meant—
Sakuya's fear became real.

target.text: Hundreds of radiant orbs erupted into the surroundings, scattering, twirling, whirling in frenzy, and from the center of that cluster of light─── they soared. That group of three. Stark naked bodies composed of light, so beautiful it struck him as bizarre. Their forms became a ray of light streaking into the night sky; the brighter it grew, the faster it moved, and at last, it travelled with such blinding swiftness that it could no longer be followed by the naked eye, overtook the aurora itself, pierced the luminous veil, then faded from sight, vanished: indeed, a true sublimation into light.

Those left behind on the ground were all brimming with uniform smiles of beatitude, and that left Sakuya more frightened than ever. For they could only be judged as blissful from the shape of those smiles alone; not a trace of actual emotion could be felt.

Meanwhile, the spheres of light born from the earlier explosion of light yet lingered in this world, whirling about like the boisterous dancing of gigantic fireflies, and while this was taking place, a single ball soared high into the skies; this one did not reach the aurora, however, instead flitting about a central point for a time, until it then suddenly flew in a certain direction, towards that solitary mountain standing in the distance. It reached its peak and was─── swallowed within, then vanished.
