That one ball signalled the beginning, with the remaining orbs also following it in quick succession; every single one was drawn into the peak of that lone mountain and vanished. That must have been the energy from the aftermath of the sublimation being put to use in maintaining that mechanism like he had said, Sakuya thought, his teeth chattering, though not because of the cold. If anything, he didn't have even a thought to spare for that.

Even within those spheres of light drawn into the solitary mountain, Sakuya had seen faces. And those were the faces of that very same group of three. Though they had been sundered into countless fragments, they were all carrying the faces of those three. Only their expressions differed, and those were what struck Sakuya with such immense dread. The expressions worn on the faces within the balls of light were───

Terror. Despair. Anguish. Mortification. Chagrin. Regret. Disappointment. Resignation. Madness. Desperation. Malevolence. And at the core of those facial expressions lay the wroth of having been betrayed. Terrified from being betrayed, in anguish from being betrayed, resigned from being betrayed, but what in the world could possibly have betrayed them? What truly drove Sakuya to the brink of an even more profound terror was not the single radiant entity formed from three that pierced the heavens, but instead how those expressions seemed all too human to him.

Sublimation. Sublimation. Was that really supposed to be liberation from this cage of a flat world, a deliverance of the soul? But Sakuya had not the luxury to dwell on any such things by himself right now. Before the departing Shisamu and Kisara, a lone pilgrim stepped forth. As far as he could tell, he was a solitary pilgrim with none to call partner. In other words, this was surely. What Sakuya feared most taken form.

source.japanese: その者が、シサム・キサラの三位一体、昇華の為のもう一人、彼女たちの『適合者』にして、その巡礼者にとっては、双子こそが待ちかねていた『自分以外の二人』だったのだろう。
source.english: This was the third member needed for Sisam and Kisara's trinity, for their sublimation. Their ‘match.’ And to that pilgrim, the twins must be the ‘other two besides myself’ for whom he had long waited.

target.text: That person, he was the last person needed for Shisamu and Kisara to sublimate into a Triune Being, he was their『compatible candidate』, and from the pilgrim's perspective, the twins were surely 『the two besides himself』 whom he had been waiting for with an ever-growing anticipation.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「この人が……あたしたち、三つの中の一つ」
source.english: “This man… He's one of our three.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「This man is……is one of our three.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんでだろう……今まで一度もあったこと、ないのに。わかるよ、わかるんだ」
source.english: “Why…? We've never met him before. But I know. I know it.”

source.japanese:
頭巾を脱いで、歓迎するように腕を広げたのは、壮年の男性の、キサラ達よりは色の薄い金髪で、面差しは整っているのだが、奇妙に印象に乏しく、目を一度離すともうどういう顔をしていたのか思い出せなくなる。
　朔屋は、頭巾を外した巡礼者達は、皆似たような者達なのではないかと漠然と想った。美形だが、表情の印象に乏しく、それが鮮烈に強まるのは、あの地上に遺されて孤山に吸われていく光球の中でだけ。
　双子とは全く異なる。けれど、双子も昇華を果たしてしまったらああなるのか？　飛翔する、無表情な至福の顔、遺されて、裏切られたと吸われていく顔、顔、顔。
source.english:
He removed his hood and opened his arms in welcome. A man in his prime, his blond hair paler than the twins'. His features were regular, yet strangely left no impression. Look away once, and one could no longer recall his face.
Vaguely Sakuya thought all the pilgrims beneath their hoods might be like this: handsome, yet with expressions that left almost nothing behind. Only inside those spheres abandoned upon the ground and drawn into the mountain did their faces become vivid.
Utterly unlike the twins. Yet would sublimation make them the same? Blissful, expressionless faces in flight; faces left behind, drawn away in betrayal. Faces, faces, faces.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I wonder why……I've never met him before, and yet. I know, I can tell.」

Lowering his hood and spreading his arms wide as if to welcome them was a man in the prime of his life, with blond hair a shade paler than Kisara's and Shisamu's, and though his countenance was well-shaped and symmetrical, it strangely failed to leave any impression, the sort of face that would slip from memory the moment you were to take your eyes off it.

As Sakuya looked at the pilgrims who had removed their hoods, the hazy realization that they all seemed to look very alike settled in his mind. They were beautiful, but their visages left little impression; only within those orbs of light, left behind in this world and drawn into the lone mountain, did that absence transform into something searingly vivid. They were completely different from the twins. And yet, if the twins ended up realizing their sublimation, was that to be their fate as well? Soaring, blank faces of pure bliss, left behind, absorbed in betrayal, those faces, faces, faces.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「たぶん、この人はあたしらの……心とか、顔かたちとか、そんなモノはなんとも思ってない」
source.english: “Probably… This man doesn't care about our hearts, our faces, any of that.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「This man, he probably doesn't…… feel a thing for our hearts, our faces, none of it.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたしらだって、この人のこと、好きとか嫌いとか、そういう気持ちはこれっぽっちもないのに」
source.english: “And we don't feel the slightest thing about him either. Don't like him, don't dislike him.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It's not as though we feel any love or any hatred for this man either, there's not a shred of such emotions, and yet.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたしらが解放される為に、この人が必要なんだって、わかる───」
source.english: “But I know we need him if we're going to be freed—”

source.japanese:
朔屋にとって、とんでもなく怖ろしい事が始まろうとしていた。光の乱舞の中で、物凄まじい光景の中で。双子が、愛した女達が二人ともこのままでは、いなくなる、ただの別離どころではなく、この世から消滅して手の届かない者となる。
　だから朔屋は───
source.english:
For Sakuya, something unimaginably terrible was about to begin amid that fearsome dance of light. If this continued, the twins—the two women he loved—would disappear. This was no mere parting: they would vanish from the world and become beings forever beyond his reach.
So Sakuya—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「We need this man to be liberated, we just know that───」

To Sakuya, it felt as though something unimaginably terrifying was on the cusp of unfolding. Within the chaotic radiance of dancing lights, amidst a staggering spectacle. At this rate, the twins, the two women he loved so, would vanish; this was no mere parting of ways, they would disappear from this world entirely, become something forever beyond his reach. Therefore, Sakuya───

source.japanese: <01>泣き叫ぶ
source.english: Cry and scream.

target.text: <01>Wailed and screamed

source.japanese: <01>無理矢理この場から、連れ出そうとする。
source.english: Try to drag them away by force.

target.text: <01>Tried to drag them away by force

source.japanese:
朔屋は考えた。それはもう必死に、大して鋭くもない知能を酷使して考えに考えた。
　で、なにも思い浮かばなかった。人界から去りゆこうとしている二人を繋ぎとめる為の、冴えて尖った楔[くさび]の台詞、行動、何一つ閃かず、朔屋はもうなんだか自分とその生き様が厭[いや]になった。
　
　情けなくて情けなくて───
　
　悔しくて悔しくて───
　
　哀しくて、辛くて、腹立たしくて、様々に膨張し弾けてはまた湧き上がる、感情の奔流、もうどう抑えようもないほど朔屋の胸の裡[うち]で暴れ回って、遂に朔屋は思考を放棄して、それら感情の混沌が己が体をどう動かすのか、任せる事にした、ところ───
source.english:
Sakuya thought. Desperately, overworking his none-too-sharp intellect, he thought and thought.
Nothing came. Not one keen, pointed word or act to drive a wedge and hold the two back from leaving the human realm. He began to loathe himself and the way he had lived.
So pathetic,
so pathetic.
So bitter, so bitter. Sadness, pain, anger: swelling, bursting, rising anew, a torrent of emotions raged beyond restraint within his chest. At last he abandoned thought and let that chaos move his body as it pleased. Whereupon—

target.text: Sakuya thought. And desperately at that, wringing every last drop from his not-so-sharp mind, thinking and thinking. Alas, nothing came to mind. No clever, sharp lines or actions that could tie the two to the world of man that they were about to depart from, not a single flash of inspiration; Sakuya found himself sick and tired of both himself and his entire way of life. Pathetic and pitiable─── Bitter and frustrating───

He was miserable, in pain, infuriated; all manner of things swelled up, burst open, then welled up from within again, a violent torrent of emotion, rampaging within Sakuya's heart to the point he could no longer suppress them, and finally, Sakuya gave up thinking, he surrendered himself to that chaos of feeling, letting it steer his body, and at that moment───

source.japanese:
【直正】
「う、う、う、うあああんんんんんっっ!!」
source.english: “Uh, uh, uh, WAAAAAAAH!”

source.japanese:
涕泣であった。号泣であった。
　頭の片隅の奥深くに、ほんのちっぽけな、ひとかけだけ残った冷静さが、ああ、やっちまったと冷ややかな目でいたけれど、この涙と鼻水とおめき声と顔面痙攣の大噴出、内圧力と勢いだけは活火山の噴火にも秘されるほどであり、なんで止められるものであろう。
source.english:
He wept. He bawled.
Deep in a corner of his mind, one tiny remaining scrap of composure watched coldly: ah, you've done it now. Yet this great eruption of tears, snot, howls and facial spasms had the internal pressure and momentum of an active volcano. How could he stop it?

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「W-, W-, W- WAAAAAAAAHH!!」

He wept. He bawled. In the deepest recesses of his mind, there was a single fragment of his remaining reason, a truly tiny scrap, observing himself with a cold, detached gaze, thinking "ah, now I've really screwed things up" to itself, but this great eruption of tears, snot, wailing, and facial convulsions, the internal pressure and force of it was so immense that not even the fury of an active volcano could do it justice, so how could it possibly be contained?

source.japanese: 背を向ける女を引き留めんと、手を伸ばして、伸ばした、ら、爪先からつんのめって体が宙をあおいだ、氷原に倒れこむまいと足掻いて掴んだのが女の腰の、見上げればシサムである。
source.english: He reached after the woman turning away. Reached—and overbalanced, pitching forward from the toes. Flailing to keep from falling upon the ice, he caught a woman's waist. He looked up. Sisam.

target.text: Trying to hold back the women who had turned their backs to him, he reached out for them with his hand, stretched it out, further, then pitched forwards from the tip of his toes, his body flung upwards in midair, and in an effort to not collapse onto the ice field, he flailed about, managed to grab hold of a woman's waist, and when he looked up, he saw that it was Shisamu's.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やだあああああ、やああああーー、
　だめぇぇぇ、めーーーーなのぉぉーーーっ、
　あーんっ、うああああああんんんんっっっ、
　じざむ、じざむぅぅぅぅぅぅっ」
source.english:
“Nooooo, nooooo!
Don't, don't, you can't!
Waaaah, WAAAAAH!
Zizam, Zizaaaam!”

source.japanese:
とこれらのわめき声は、全ての文字に濁音がつくそれぐらい涙と鼻水と涎にくぐもって聞き苦しかった。
　なにしろ、これに度肝を抜かれたせいで、シサムとキサラが振り零し振り撒いていたあの燐光、美しい、あえかな、物哀しげなあの光の粒、しゅぱっと一気に飛び散って、出かけていた分は体の中に引っ込んで、怯えきったのか、あとはもう出てこなくなってしまったほどの。
source.english:
Every sound seemed clogged with tears, snot and drool, roughened and horrible to hear.
Indeed, it shocked Sisam and Kisara so thoroughly that the beautiful, fragile, sorrowful phosphorescent grains they had been spilling flew away at once. Those halfway out retreated into their bodies, and no more emerged. Apparently frightened out of their wits.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「えー…………。
　別れの場面だからさ、泣きの涙の一つもあって仕方ないけれど、朔屋あんたこれ、餓鬼の駄々とおんなじ……」
source.english:
“Uh… It's a farewell,
so a tear or two's understandable, Sakuya. But this is just a kid throwing a tantrum…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あば、あば、ずび、べしゃ、ごっぼ、
　ごぼごぼごぼごぼごぼごぼごぼごぼごぼっ、
　げへっ、おぶぇぇぇぇぇぇ……、
　ジザム、だぁだぁっ、ジザム、めーっっ」
source.english:
“Ab, ab, snrrk, splat,
glub, glubglubglubglubglub…
Geh, urrrgh…
Zizam, no-no! Zizam, don't!”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「うわー……さすがにここまでだと、幻滅するだろこれ……」
source.english: “Wow… This is enough to put anyone off you…”

source.japanese: ……慄然っ引[ひ]きにならない女の方がおかしい。昇華にまだ加わっていない巡礼者達、さすがに礼儀よろしく目を逸らしている、振りをして堪[こら]えかねた笑いの、頭巾の裡[うち]から。
source.english: …A woman who did not recoil in horror would be the odd one. The pilgrims not yet engaged in sublimation politely looked away—or pretended to, while laughter they could not contain escaped from within their hoods.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぎっ、ぎっ、ぐわばぁっ、ぎざ、らぁ、
　ぎざらもやらだあばばばっ、
　あーーーっっっ」
source.english:
“Gih, gih, gwaaah! Gizara…
Gizara can't go eith-abababa!
AAAAAH!”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……壊滅的だ……ちょっとは惚れたところがあったとしても、これじゃあ百年の恋だっても」
source.english: “…Catastrophic. Even if there was something about you I liked, this could kill a century-long romance…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ヴーッッ、ビェェェ、バビィィィィィっっ。
　ギザラァァァ。ギザラァァァゥゥウっ」
source.english:
“WUUUH! BEEEH! BAAAABEEE!
GIZARAAA! GIZARAAAA!”

source.japanese:
その迸[ほとばし]る、朔屋の声、涙。
　泣くという行為の哀しさ、美しさ、苦しさ、そういった崇高と言っていい要素どころか、嬉し泣き、悔し泣き、諸々の、時に矛盾する感情さえも乗せて、人という生き物の表情に精妙さと奥行きの深さを与えてくれる涙という現象の意味を、根本からして崩壊させかねない程の破壊力を有していた。馬鹿にしていた。ふざけていた。最悪だった。
　朔屋本人はどういうつもりであろうとも、この場に居合わせてこれを不幸にも見てしまった者、シサム・キサラに巡礼者達が抱いた印象を語るには───アリストテレスの「笑い」に関する論争中に、人が笑う事を『すると彼は顔からおならをした』という喩えを用いて非難した修道僧か哲学者があったが、この例を借りてあえてこう表現するしかないと思われる。
source.english:
His gushing voice, his tears.
Far from conveying the sadness, beauty and pain of weeping—those almost sublime qualities—they had enough destructive force to demolish the very meaning of tears: that phenomenon which lends subtlety and depth to the human face by carrying joy, frustration, and all the various, sometimes contradictory emotions. It mocked them. Made a farce of them. It was the worst.
Whatever Sakuya himself intended, one could describe the impression he made upon the unfortunate witnesses—Sisam, Kisara and the pilgrims—only by borrowing an example. In the debate over Aristotle's ‘laughter,’ some monk or philosopher condemned human laughter with the comparison, ‘Then he farted from his face.’ Borrowing his example, one can only venture—

source.japanese:
『すると彼は、顔から液便を漏らした。
　バビィィィブリョブリョバブゥゥンっ』
source.english:
‘Then he leaked liquid shit from his face.
BAAAA-BRRRR-BABOOOOM!’

source.japanese:
あの、物に怖じず、涙を見せず、信天翁号の赤い女悪魔と恐れられたキサラでさえ、これには哀しみを抑えきれなかったという。情けなすぎて。自分達が選んで、結局捨てる事になった男で、彼女達だとて苦しんでいる、悔やんでいる、それでも振りきっていこうとしている。
　むろん勝手な感傷だ。置いていかれる朔屋にとってはたまったものではなかろうが、シサムもキサラも───自分達が捨てていく男を惜しむ気持ちを持ちたい、と。そう願う。惜しむ程の男を捨てていくのだ、と。
　ところがその朔屋がこれである。
source.english:
Even Kisara, fearless and tearless, feared as the Albatross's red she-devil, could not contain her sadness at this. He was too pathetic. He was the man they had chosen and were now abandoning. They too suffered; they too regretted it; even so, they were trying to wrench themselves away.
Selfish sentiment, of course. Unbearable to Sakuya, the one being left behind. Still, Sisam and Kisara wanted to feel regret for the man they were leaving. They wanted to believe they were abandoning a man worth regretting.
And Sakuya gave them this.

source.japanese:
『すると彼は、顔から液（以下省略）　　』
　───である。
　キサラは、僅かに揺らいだ。
　朔屋と過ごした時間がシサムより多少長い分、彼女の鋼の土性骨も青年の成分に、ほんの僅かだが浸食されていたのだろう。
source.english:
‘Then he leaked liquid—[remainder omitted].’
So it was.
Kisara wavered slightly.
She had spent somewhat longer with Sakuya than Sisam had. Perhaps, in that extra time, some small part of the young man had seeped into even her steely constitution.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「さすがにわざとでしょ？　朔屋？　え。嘘。
　こいつ、本気だ……本気でこれだ」
source.english:
“Surely you're doing this on purpose, Sakuya? Huh? No.
He's serious… This is really him.”

source.japanese: 以下延々と朔屋の見苦しい聞き苦しい耐えがたい堪[こら]えがたい忍びがたい泣きが続くのだが、耐えろ、物語よ、耐えて今は己の糸を手繰れ……。
source.english: Sakuya's ugly, horrible, intolerable, unbearable, unendurable weeping continues at length below. Endure, story. Endure, and for now gather in your thread…

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「NOOOOOOO, NOOOOーー, SHTOOOOP, YOUーーーーCAAANDCHーーー, AAAH, WAAAAAAAHHHHH, SHISHAMUH, SHISHAMUUUUUUUH!」

So drenched in tears, snot, and drool were his screams, it sounded like every syllable was garbled and slurred with consonants. At any rate, as a result of their minds being so utterly boggled by this display, that phosphorescence Kisara and Shisamu were shedding and scattering all about, those beautiful, fleeting, melancholy drops of light, exploded outwards in a sharp burst, and then all the particles that had begun to make their departure retreated back into their bodies, perhaps out of fear, so terrified by what they'd seen that they would never dare venture outside again.
【Shisamu】 「Uhhー…………. Look, I know this is our moment of parting, so I had resigned myself to at least a bit of crying, but Sakuya, you're acting like some little brat throwing a tantrum……」
【Naomasa】 「Abuh, abuh, snrrk, splrch, guhbuh, glubglubglubglubgluhbgluhglubggluh, gehh, bluuggghhgeeehhhh……, Shishamuh, doh-doh-, Shishamuh, dondー」
【Shisamu】 「Whoa……at this point, I'm not sure if I can really look you in the eye anymore……」

……Any woman who didn't immediately shrink back in shuddering terror would have to be out of her mind. As one might expect, the pilgrims who had yet to participate in the sublimation were well-mannered enough to avert their eyes, though despite the display of politeness, they couldn't quite stifle the snickering slipping out from beneath their hoods.
【Naomasa】 「Ghi, Ghi, gwahgh, Ghisha, rah, you too, don't, Ghisharahababah, AAーーー!」
【Kisara】 「……This is just devastating…… I might have fallen just a little bit in love, but I don't think even a century's worth of love could survive this.」
【Naomasa】 「Bwaaah, bweeeeh, babeeeeeehhh. Ghisharaaah. GHISHARAAAAAAUUUH!」

That eruption, Sakuya's voice, tears. It was not just what one could well call the lofty components that constitute the act we define as crying: the melancholy, the beauty, the suffering, no, it was also the tears of joy, tears of bitter frustration, all manner of emotions that, at times, were contradictory; Sakuya's wailing contained within itself a destructive force so catastrophic, it could well crush the very significance of the phenomenon that is shedding tears, that which grants onto the expressions of the beings we call humans an exquisite excellence and deep profundity, at its very roots, annihilate its very essence. It made light of it. Mocked it. 'Twas appalling.

Whatever Sakuya himself may have intended, to describe the impression that Shisamu and Kisara had made on the pilgrims who had suffered the misfortune of witnessing the scene─── during a debate over Aristotle's theory of「laughter」, there was a certain monk or philosopher who used the metaphor of 『And then he farted from his face』 to condemn the act, and it seems we are left with no choice but to daringly borrow from his example and express it thus:
『And then he excreted liquid feces from his face. Babiiiihblblublblbluphloooot!』

Even Kisara, she who feared nothing, never shed a tear before others, and was dreaded far and wide as the Red She-Devil of the Albatross, was unable to contain her grief at the sight. It was far too pathetic. The man who had chosen them, he who had ultimately been dumped and abandoned: they were also suffering in anguish, lamenting it, but even so, they were still trying to push past it and keep going.

Needless to say, this was a very self-centered sentiment. It must have been completely intolerable for Sakuya, being left behind as he was, but Shisamu and Kisara also─── wanted to carry with them some feeling of lingering regret for the man they were going to abandon. That was their wish. To abandon a man whom the loss of was worth regretting. However, this was the state of that Sakuya:

『And then he excreted liquid fe(omitted below)』 ───So it was. Kisara was wavering, barely. She'd spent somewhat more time together with Sakuya than Shisamu had, and the woman's resolve, hard as steel, had likely also been corroded ever so slightly by the young man's essence
【Kisara】 「You have to be doing this on purpose, right, Sakuya? What. No way. This guy's serious…… he's genuinely doing this.」
What followed was an endless stream of Sakuya's unsightly, unpleasant, unbearable, intolerable, unendurable crying, but pray endure, O story, hold fast and retrace thine own threads…….

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「はぁ……駄目な奴情けない奴とは思っちゃいたが。最後の最後でも貫き通すとは、一周回ってまた行き越して、もうげんなりってしか言いようがない」
source.english: “Hah… I knew you were useless and pathetic. But carrying it through to the very end—it's gone full circle, then past it again. All I can say is, I'm exhausted.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「でもね、朔屋。あんた、さっきからあたしらのこと、完全に見分けて呼んでるね。それだけは凄いよ。できた奴は、男にも女にもいなかった」
source.english: “Still, Sakuya. You've called each of us by the right name every time. That alone is amazing. Nobody else has ever managed it, man or woman.”

source.japanese:
───空には赤気、地上には巡礼者達の杖の灯、そして地上から虚空には飛翔し、去っていく『三位一体者』の光。
　北の果ての凍てつく荒野に、幻夢到来したかの、美しくもあり、おぞましくもあり、謎秘めてあり、恐らくはこの世界の中でも秘奥に属する情景に違いあるまい、の、ただ中で、駄々漏らしの男を相手にシサムは奮戦していた。これほどまでの苦しい戦い、彼女も経験した事がないであろう。
source.english:
Aurora in the sky, pilgrims' staff lights on the ground, and from the ground into the void, the light of the ‘Triune One’ taking flight and departing.
In the frozen waste at the northern end of the world, it was as though a dream had arrived: beautiful, hideous, mysterious, surely a vision of this world's deepest secrets. Amid it all, Sisam fought bravely against a man leaking a tantrum from every pore. She could hardly have known a more painful battle.

source.japanese:
なにしろ、こんな朔屋の中からでさえも、どうにかして、納屋の藁の山から、いや浜の真砂の中から、と範囲拡大すべきか、いっそこうか、大海の潮の中からプランクトンの一匹を見つけ出すように、青年の美点を探し出して、別れをせめてもう少し哀しく美しいものに軌道修正せんとしていたのである。
　人間がいかに絶望的な戦いにあっても、闘い続ける事ができるか、魂の姿がここにある。
source.english:
Even within this Sakuya, somehow, she sought a virtue: like finding a needle in a barnful of straw—no, broaden the field to all the sand upon a beach. Or better yet, one speck of plankton in the ocean's tides. She was trying to steer their farewell toward something a little sadder and lovelier.
Here was the shape of the human soul: proof that people could go on fighting even the most hopeless battle.

source.japanese: ───とはいえ、確かに先刻も、朔屋は二人を見分けていたのであるが。
source.english: And yet Sakuya had, undeniably, told the pair apart only moments before.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それは、本当にそう。それができるくらい、あんたは女のことがよく見えてきた、ってことだ。
　ならさ、大丈夫だよ」
source.english:
“That's really true. If you can do that, it means you've learned to look closely at women.
So you'll be all right.”

source.japanese: やっとキサラも援軍に加わって、双子の力が合力に、これで綺麗な別離というのも見えてくるかと思ったが、シサム達が戦っていたのはアラモ砦であった。かの国の気高い精神の一つの発露だが、その結末はよく知られている。全滅である。
source.english: At last Kisara joined the battle as reinforcement, and the twins' strength became one. Perhaps a beautiful parting was finally within sight. But Sisam and company were defending the Alamo: one noble expression of that country's spirit, whose ending is well known. Total annihilation.

source.japanese:
キサラがどれだけ大丈夫と保証しようとも。
　この朔屋を見て真顔でそれを言えるものにはある種の才能がある。詐欺師か教祖か革命家か国家的指導者だ。皆いずれもどういう才能が要されるかは言うまでもあるまい。
source.english:
However often Kisara assured him he would be all right,
anyone who could look at this Sakuya and say it with a straight face possessed a certain talent. A swindler, a cult leader, a revolutionary, a national leader. No need to specify the talent each required.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そう、あたしらなんかより、もっと綺麗で気立ても優しい、いい女、きっと見つけられるって。だから、こんなくっそ汚ぇ未練なんぞ、いつまでも残してんじゃねえっ」
source.english: “Yes. You'll surely find someone prettier, kinder, better than us. So quit hanging on forever to this filthy fucking attachment!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Haaah……I already thought you were a hopeless and pathetic man. But you didn't just stick with it here at the very end, you lapped yourself, and all I can really say is that I'm just fed up by now.」
【Shisamu】 「But you know, Sakuya. When you called out to us just now, you told us apart perfectly. That alone is amazing. No man or woman has ever been able to do that.」

───In the sky was the aurora, on the surface the light of the pilgrims' staves, and finally, soaring from the ice into empty space, the departing light of the『Triune Beings』 In the frozen wilderness of the northernmost reaches, it was like the advent of a phantasmagoric dream; it was beautiful, repulsive, harbouring forgotten secrets, there could be no mistaking that this was, in all likelihood, a spectacle belonging to one of the most profound mysteries of this world, and right there, right in the heart of it, Shisamu struggled valiantly against an uncontrollably leaking man. Hitherto, the woman had likely never experienced a battle so painfully difficult.

For you see, even someone like Sakuya must have had something deep inside; thus, by whatever means she could think of, against all odds, she was rummaging through a mountain of straw in a barn, nay, through the sand of a beach, but perhaps the scope ought to be expanded; it was as though she was searching for but a single speck of plankton in the salty waters of the great ocean, trying to uncover the young man's virtues in an effort to, if nothing else, at least correct the trajectory of their parting down even just a slightly more poignant and beautiful path.
Whether one can keep fighting, no matter how hopeless the battle─── it is in this very question that the true shape of a human soul is revealed.
───Be that as it may, it certainly was true that, just a moment earlier, Sakuya had correctly distinguished between the two.
【Kisara】 「That really is true. If you can do that much, that means you've really come to have a good eye for women. In that case, you'll be fine.」

At long last, Kisara joined the battle as reinforcements, and with the power of the twins combined, she believed she could begin to see glimpses of a beautiful parting, however, the battle Shisamu was fighting in took place at the Alamo. While a manifestation of a certain country's noble spirit, the outcome is familiar to most. Annihilation.

No matter how steadfastly Kisara tried to assure him that it would be fine. To be able to look at Sakuya in his state and say that with a straight face took a certain kind of talent. That of a con artist, a religious founder, a revolutionary, or a national leader. It goes without saying exactly what talent is required to excel in each of these positions.
【Shisamu】 「Yeah, I'm sure you'll find a woman, one more beautiful, and with a kinder nature than the likes of us. So don't go clinging on to this filthy fucking regret forever!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あ、くそ、だめだ、釣られてなんか、こっちまで涙出てきそう。男も女もおいおい泣く愁嘆場なんか、コメディと変わんないのに……っ」
source.english: “Ah, shit. No, you're making me feel like crying too. A big farewell scene with men and women all bawling's no different from a comedy…”

source.japanese: とうとうキサラに次いでシサムまで、揺らぎつつあった。大体泣く泣かないを言うのなら、先だっての夜シサムは既にしてさんざん泣いている。
source.english: After Kisara, Sisam too began to waver. And if it came to who had or had not cried, Sisam had already done more than enough of it the other night.

source.japanese: ───既に、敗北している。
source.english: Already defeated.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「堪えて、シサム。あんたが泣いたら、あたしだって泣くよ、絶対にだ。結構本気で、涙腺にきてんだからあたしも……っ」
source.english: “Hold it in, Sisam. If you cry, I will too. Absolutely. I'm already fighting back tears myself…”

source.japanese: そう、二人は最初から戦術を見誤っていた。きっぱりとした別れ、哀しくも決然とした別れ、そんなものは朔屋が朔屋として発動した時点で成立の可能性は限りなく零[ゼロ]に近くなる。であるのならば、最初から三人しておいおい大泣きしていた方がよほど良い。少なくとも朔屋の『顔から液（以下略）』は二人の熱いか清いか哀しいか悔しいか、いずれにしても涙が少しは希釈してくれた筈だ。
source.english: Yes, their tactics had been wrong from the start. A clean break, a sad yet resolute farewell: once Sakuya went fully Sakuya, its chances approached zero. Better, then, to have bawled together from the outset. At least their tears—hot, pure, sad, bitter, whatever—would have diluted his ‘liquid from the face, etc.’ a little.

source.japanese:
男も女もおいおい泣く愁嘆場は、コメディと何ら変わりがない。確かに。なるほど。
　だが、コメディの何がいけない。
　コメディを演じる者達がどれだけ真剣であるのか───
source.english:
A farewell scene with men and women all bawling was no different from comedy.
True. Indeed. But what was wrong with comedy?
How earnestly its players performed—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ah, shit, this isn't working. I'm being drawn in, I'm about to start crying too. When men and women start bawling their eyes out in some melodramatic tearjerker of a goodbye, it's no different from a comedy, but I……」
Finally, following Shisamu, Kisara had also begun to waver. And if we're going to talk about crying and not crying, Shisamu was already crying her eyes out the night before.
───She was already defeated.
【Kisara】 「Keep it in, Shisamu. If you start crying, then I'll start crying too, guaranteed. It's actually hitting me real bad too, so I'm also about to tear up……」

Indeed, the two had misjudged their tactic from the very start. A resolute parting, a parting that was melancholy but decisive: the moment that Sakuya began acting like Sakuya, the possibility of that coming to fruition grew asymptotically close to zero. And given that was the case, it would have been much smarter if all three had been wailing and weeping instead. At the very least, whether it was passionate, pure, sorrowful, or regretful, between the two of them, their tears would surely have diluted some of Sakuya's 『liquid (omitted) from his face』

When men and women start bawling their eyes out in some melodramatic tearjerker of a goodbye, it's no different from a comedy. Certainly. Indeed. However, what is so wrong with a comedy? Do you realize just how dead serious the performers are while they act it out───

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うぅ、うぇ、ちが、ちがぅ……ぅ」
source.english: “Uh, weh, no, no… That's not…”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ああ、詰まったもの出すだけ出して、ようやく少しは口を聞けるようになってきたね。
　……ほら、ほんとに最後の言葉にしよう。
　───お互いに───」
source.english:
“Ah. You've finally let out everything stuck inside, so you can talk a little.
…Come on. Let's really make these our last words.
To each other.”

source.japanese: ぽんぽんと、すがる朔屋の肩を、赤ん坊のおくびを導いてやるように軽く叩いて、朔屋の鼻と喉に詰まった物を出してやろうとするシサムは、あるいはこんなのも、この青年との別れとしては相応しいのかも知れないと思い始めている───敗北、している。
source.english: Patting the clinging Sakuya's shoulder as though helping a baby burp, trying to dislodge whatever clogged his nose and throat, Sisam began to think that perhaps this, too, was a fitting farewell for the young man. Defeated.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「違う……んだ。違う。
　俺、見分けてなんか、ない」
source.english:
“That's… not it. Not it.
I'm not telling you apart.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なによ朔屋。
　偶然で当ててたって、
　それはあんたの運気の証拠。
　それでもいいじゃんか」
source.english:
“What, Sakuya?
Even if you guessed by chance,
that's proof of your luck.
That'd be fine too.”

source.japanese: 彼女たちは、朔屋の眼力や、そういった才や美質をどうにか見いだそうとして、自分達がいなくても大丈夫と、そう告げようとしている時点で、既に敗北している。
source.english: Trying to find in him some power of perception, some talent, some good quality, trying to tell him he would be all right without them: by that point they were already defeated.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だ、から、違うってぇ……言ってンだろ馬鹿女どもぁ！」
source.english: “I said that's not it, you stupid women!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Uuh, ueh, wrong, that's not……」
【Shisamu】 「Ah, now that you've gotten all that pent up stuff out, you can finally speak a little again? ……Come on, let's actually make these our final words. ───For all of us───」

With soft thuds, she gently tapped the clinging Sakuya's shoulder like she was burping a baby, and Shisamu, trying to clear the blockage from Sakuya's throat and nose, had begun to think that, maybe, this too might make for a suitable parting with this young man───she was defeated.
【Naomasa】 「That's……not it. You're wrong. I didn't tell you apart, or anything like that.」
【Kisara】 「What is it now, Sakuya? Even if you guessed it by chance, that's just proof you've got luck on your side. Isn't that good enough?」

By the time the girls were trying to uncover Sakuya's perceptiveness, or any other such talents or virtues he may have, by the time they were attempting to convey to him that he'd be fine, even without them, they had already lost.
【Naomasa】 「Like. I. Said……you're wrong, you stupid women!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ここ、逆上するタイミング？
　ならなんが違うよ。馬鹿が人を馬鹿女呼ばわりにするからには、よっぽどの事なんだろうなおい」
source.english:
“This is when you lose your temper?
Then what is it? An idiot calling us stupid women had better have one hell of a point to make.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「シサム、キサラの首筋見ろ、
　鰓の横辺りっ」
source.english:
“Sisam, look at Kisara's neck.
Beside her jaw!”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「───あっ。これ……って、あん時のっ」
source.english: “…Ah. This… From that time!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ほんでなキサラ、シサムの首にゃ、なんか残ってるかい」
source.english: “And Kisara, is there anything left on Sisam's neck?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ううんなにもついてなんか───あっ」
source.english: “No, there's nothing—ah.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やっと判ったのかよう。
　そうだよ、キスマークで目印着けてただけなんだよ、シサムの首筋に」
source.english:
“Finally figured it out?
Yeah. I was just using a hickey on Sisam's neck as a marker.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「この程度のことだ、今まで誰もやった奴、いなかったのなら逆にびっくりだ」
source.english: “That's all it takes. If nobody ever did that before, I'm surprised.”

source.japanese: あの、帆掛け橇[ぞり]の舷側に帆布掛け渡した狭苦しい中で、三人での交わりの中で。朔屋が我慢に我慢を重ねていたあの短かな時間。普段のセックスならキサラも気づいていただろう。肌に残るその痕に。けれどあの時キサラは、朔屋に焦らしに焦らされて、あまり正気ではなかった。シサムとの再会の喜びももちろんあったろう。
source.english: Inside that cramped space beneath the canvas stretched over the sailing sled's gunwales, during their coupling as three. In the brief interval when Sakuya held back and held back. During ordinary sex, Kisara would have noticed the mark left on her skin. But then, teased and teased by him, she had not been entirely sane. The joy of finding Sisam again must also have played its part.

source.japanese: 偶然が幾つか重なって、キサラもシサムも気づかなかった口づけの痕。まさに朔屋の言うその程度のもの。
source.english: Several coincidences had kept either twin from noticing the mark of that kiss. Exactly as Sakuya said: something so trivial.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でも逆に、その程度のことであんた達の区別なんて付くんだよ。なのになんだよ、三位一体とか、昇華だとかっ」
source.english: “But that's the point: something that small is enough to tell you apart. So what the hell is all this trinity and sublimation stuff?”

source.japanese: そんな、端的に言ってしまえば肌の鬱血一つで。
source.english: Something so slight. Simply put, one patch of bruised skin.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなんで見分けつくんなら、俺は何度だってマーク着けるよ、手を替え品を替えて。
　でもシサムとキサラがいなくなったら、俺は誰に一体マーキングすればいいの……。
　ぅ……っ、う……っ、うぇ、ふぇ、
　えーーーーんっ」
source.english:
“If that's enough to tell you apart, I'll mark you as often as it takes. I'll use every trick I know.
But if Sisam and Kisara disappear, who am I supposed to mark…?
Uh… Uh… Weh, feh…
WAAAAH!”

source.japanese:
そしてそれを捺[お]して、二人をこうまで誑[たぶら]かしたのは、何かというと言動行動シモに走る青年の。
　誑かす、という字は言葉で狂わす、と書くのである。朔屋の言葉を聞いた時点で、二人が何を考え何を想い、何を計画していたとしても、これで狂ってしまったのであろう。
source.english:
And the one who stamped that mark and so beguiled the pair was a young man whose every word and act went straight below the waist.
To beguile someone is to drive them mad with words—or so the written character tells us. Whatever they had been thinking, feeling, planning, hearing Sakuya's words must have deranged it all.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Is this really the right time to flip your lid? Then what's so wrong? If an idiot's calling us stupid women, then it has to be one hell of a mistake, huh?」
【Naomasa】 「Shisamu, look at the side of Kisara's neck, near the corner of her jaw!」
【Shisamu】 「───Ah. This is……wait, that's from back then!」
【Naomasa】 「And now, Kisara, can you tell us if there's anything remaining on Shisamu's neck?」
【Kisara】 「No, there's nothing on there at all───ah!」
【Naomasa】 「Seems you finally got it. That's right, I just left a love bite on Kisara's neck, as a mark.」
【Naomasa】 「If anything, I'd be more shocked if nobody's ever tried anything this simple before now.」

Back in that cramped space in the sail-driven sledge, with sailcloth stretched from gunwale to gunwale, during the intimacy shared between the three. In that fleeting moment, where Sakuya endured and endured many times over. Had it been regular sex, then Kisara would surely have noticed. A mark left on the skin. But at the time, Kisara was being driven mad with anticipation by Sakuya, teased again and again. The joy of her reunion with Shisamu must also have played its part.
Several coincidences overlapping, a kiss mark that neither Kisara nor Shisamu noticed. It truly was just as Sakuya said, a trifling thing.
【Naomasa】 「But on the other hand, this is all it takes to be able to tell you two apart. So what is all this about then? Triune Beings, sublimation!」
All it took was, spoken frankly, but a single congestion of blood under the skin.

【Naomasa】 「If that's enough to tell you apart, then I'll mark you as many times as I must, by hook or by crook. But, Shisamu, Kisara, if you're gone, then tell me, who am I even supposed to mark……. Uh……hrk, uh……, wah, fhh, waaーーーーh!」

Thus, placing that final stamp on their decision, the one who had so thoroughly seduced the two of them was none other than this young man whose every word and deed veered towards the loins. To seduce, or deceive, could also be elaborated on as the act of pushing someone down a different track with words. And from the moment they had heard Sakuya speak, whatever the two of them may have been thinking, feeling, or planning, it was all derailed and unravelling.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「また泣き出しよったこいつ」
source.english: “He's started crying again.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でも、さあ……シサム。
　こういう場面で、泣くしかできないこんな奴に、すっげぇ下らない手で一杯食わされる、
　間抜けな女がいるって事だよ、ここに、二人も」
source.english:
“But, Sisam…
There are two stupid women right here who've been taken in by a ridiculously cheap trick,
by someone who can only cry at a time like this.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……言葉もねえや」
source.english: “…Got nothing to say.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Now he's begun crying again, I swear, this guy.」

【Kisara】 「But, you know……Shisamu. It just goes to show that there's some real stupid women out there, who will let a guy like this, the kind who can do nothing but cry in these kinds of moments, pull the wool over their own eyes with some ridiculously stupid trick. And there's even two of them standing right here.」
【Shisamu】 「……What can I even say?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「馬鹿と間抜けで、底無しに駄目になるだけだろうが、なんかさ、もういいじゃんそれで」
source.english: “An idiot and two fools, and we'll just go hopelessly to the dogs. But, you know… Isn't that fine?”

source.japanese:
多分、キサラの言っている事は間違っている。馬鹿と間抜けで底無しに駄目になる、そちらの方ではない、そちらは今既に証明されている。
　彼女が間違っているのは、ここで朔屋に誑[たぶら]かされたから間抜けと土がついたのではなく。
　彼女達が朔屋と初対面の時あの夜あの酒場。
　あそこで朔屋を駄目で馬鹿な奴とほとんど見抜いておきながら。
　それでいて朔屋を信天翁号に連れこんでしまったその時点で、彼女達は間抜けと極まってしまったのである。
　───まこと、端倪すべからざる運命という奴は、どこに口を開けているやら知れたものでない。
source.english:
Kisara was probably wrong. Not about an idiot and two fools going hopelessly to the dogs; that was already proved.
Her mistake was thinking that being beguiled by Sakuya here was what first made fools of them.
That night, in that tavern, when they first met him, they had seen almost at once how useless and stupid he was. Yet they brought him aboard the Albatross anyway.
Their foolishness had been complete from that very moment.
Truly, who could tell where unfathomable fate lay in wait, its jaws agape?

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It's probably stupid, foolish, and absolutely doomed to fail, but you know what, I'm kind of fine with that.」

Most likely, what Kisara was saying was wrong. Not the part about being stupid, foolish, and absolutely doomed to fail; that was not where she erred, for that had already been proven at length. Where she made her mistake was in thinking that being seduced by Sakuya here, and consequently admitting defeat, was what branded them fools.

That night in that bar, where the girls had met Sakuya for the first time. While they had mostly seen through the fact that Sakuya was a worthless idiot. That they still brought Sakuya aboard the Albatross in spite of that, at that moment, that was exactly when their foolishness reached its apex. ───Truly, that rascal we call fate is ever impossible to predict, and who could ever know where she would next begin to speak her ironies.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「どんだけ居心地悪い世界だろうとも。
　馬鹿にできる相手がいるなら、憂さの一つくらいは晴らしていける、てことか」
source.english:
“However uncomfortable this world may be,
if there's someone to make fun of, we can work off a little steam. Is that it?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ひっでぇ話だ……」
source.english: “What a horrible story…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……うっうっうっ、でもあんた達もともとあんなひっでぇ船に乗ってるじゃないか。望んで乗ったッつってたじゃないか。
　だったら俺にももっと乗ってくれよ……」
source.english:
“…Uh, uh, uh. But you were on that horrible ship already. Said you wanted to be there.
Then ride me some more too…”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「はぁぁ……もうナニ言ってんだかわかんなくってきた。なんとなくわかるような気もするんだけど」
source.english: “Haaah… Can't tell what you're saying anymore. Feel like I sort of can, though.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「初めて寝た時がそれだったからね。
　なんかあそこで、こうなることが決まったんじゃなかろうか」
source.english:
“That's how we did it the first time we slept together.
Maybe it was settled then that we'd end up like this.”

source.japanese:
だからそう言う段階の話ではなく。
　きっと二人は。
　そもそも始まりのその時から。
　朔屋と出会ってしまった時点で。
　駄目になる事が、きっと───
source.english:
But it did not begin there.
Surely, the two of them—
from the very beginning,
from the moment they met Sakuya—
had been doomed to go to the dogs, surely—

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「もういいよこれで。
　はいはい朔屋。帰りまちょうね、
　あばばば」
source.english:
“Fine. This'll do. There,
there, Sakuya. Wet's go home, shall we?
Goo-goo-goo.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あやすなよう……でも聞いたからな。
　言い直しはさせないからな。一緒に帰るんだよな。当然シサムも」
source.english:
“Don't baby me… But I heard you.
No taking it back. We're going home together, right? Sisam too, obviously.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「えーえー。負けた負けた。ちぇー。綺麗なままにおさらばできたはずなのに。
　なんかもう、苦笑いしか出てこねえや」
source.english:
“Yeah, yeah. We lost, we lost. Damn. We could've parted beautifully.
Now all I can manage is a wry smile.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「───ってなわけよ、お歴々！
　やめたやめた、あたしらはやめた」
source.english:
“So that's how it is, your eminences!
We're out. We've quit.”

source.japanese:
二人とも、三位一体者とか昇華とか、あるいはセントエルモの灯が云々といった事柄から、憑きものが落ちたかのような顔で解放されてあり───
　あるいは、そう、朔屋というのが付いていた時点で、他の憑きものが入りこむ余地がなかったのかも知れない。
source.english:
Both wore faces freed from the Triune One, sublimation, St. Elmo's light and all the rest, as though an obsession had fallen away.
Or perhaps, yes, with Sakuya possessing them already, there had been no room for any other possessing thing.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「うちらはおさらば、
　後は皆様、ご自由に～～
　っときたもんだ」
source.english:
“We're off.
The rest of you,
do whatever you like!”

source.japanese:
笑っていた。この北の果てに集って、昇華という秘儀を行い、そして世界の秘密の一端を知る巡礼者達を、本人達は晴れ晴れと気持ちよく、見ている者は胸の扉と頭の鉢が同時に開いて怒りの魂が飛び出してきそうな、せせら笑いで、二人は───嗤っていた。
　偉そうな奴を、嗤っていた。
source.english:
They laughed. Laughed at the pilgrims gathered at the northern end of the world, performing the secret rite of sublimation and privy to one of the world's mysteries. The twins themselves felt gloriously refreshed; anyone watching that sneer might have felt the door of his chest and the crown of his skull fly open together, releasing the furious soul within. They laughed.
At pompous people, they laughed.

source.japanese: ───ああ、これだ。
source.english: Ah. This was it.

source.japanese:
シサムと再会し、やっと双子が揃ったはずなのに、朔屋がどこか足りないと感じていた何か。
　それが、これだ。
　この小憎らしい嘲笑。
source.english:
He had found Sisam again; the twins were finally together. Yet Sakuya had felt something missing.
This was it.
That infuriating mockery.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「No matter how unbearable a world it may be. As long as there's someone you can make a fool of, then I guess there's always a way to rid yourself of some of that bitterness, huh.」
【Kisara】 「What an awful thing……」

【Naomasa】 「……Ugh-ugh-uh, but you guys have been sailing with that awful ship right from the start, haven't you? You said you were only there because you wanted it, right? Then please, let me sail with you some more……」
【Kisara】 「Haaah……I can't even understand a word he's saying anymore. But I still kind of feel like I get it.」
【Shisamu】 「It's been like that since the first time we slept with him, right? It kind of feels like maybe this whole thing was set in stone ever since then?」
Like I said, you're barking up the wrong tree. These two were surely. From the very beginning, from that moment. When they ended up running into Sakuya. Becoming hopeless was surely───
【Kisara】 「That's enough of this already. Yeah, yeah, Sakuya. Let's go home now, okay? Ababababa.」
【Naomasa】 「Don't baby me……but I heard that. So I'm not letting you take that back. We're going home together. With Shisamu too, of course.」
【Shisamu】 「Fine, fine. I lost, I lost. Hmmph. We could've parted ways with some grace, but. At this point, all I've got left to give is a wry smile.」
【Shisamu】 「───So that's how it is, esteemed audience! We quit, we quit, we're done here!」

The two of them wore an expression as if they had been liberated from whatever had haunted them, be it the Triune Being or the sublimation, or perhaps even from St. Elmo's fire and all those kinds of things─── Or perhaps, yes, from the moment the man named Sakuya was attached to them, maybe there was no longer any room left for anything else to haunt them.
【Kisara】 「We're saying our goodbyes, and so, fine folks, the rest we leave up to you～～ That's the long and short of it.」

They smiled. At these pilgrims who had assembled at the northernmost reaches, who conducted a secret ceremony they called sublimation, who knew a fragment of this world's secrets; they were in high spirits and cheerful, while to the onlookers, it was as if the door to their hearts and the lids of their skulls had cracked open all at the same time, like the very soul of their anger was about to burst forth, and all because, while wearing that mocking smirk, the two of them───were laughing. They were laughing. At some self-important, conceited bastards.
───Aah, this was it.

Even though they had reunited with Shisamu, and the twins were finally gathered once more, there was a certain something Sakuya had felt was missing. And that, it was this. This endearingly impish sneer.

source.japanese: ───くそったれなこいつらの頭に酒を浴びせかけるような───
source.english: Like dousing these bastards' heads in liquor—

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「さ、もどろっか。シサム、朔屋」
source.english: “Come on, let's go back. Sisam, Sakuya.”

target.text: ───Like they were pouring booze over the heads of those fuckers───
【Kisara】 「Alright, let's head back? Shisamu, Sakuya.」

source.japanese: かくして双子は、一つの救いを捨て去った。一人の男の泣き落としと詐術に近い遣り口に、無敵の女二人がまんまと引っかかったその瞬間に、幻妖の光舞い踊る夜空の下、奇怪な昇華を遂げて光を撒き散らす一団の中を、さっと駆け抜けていった一筋の風を、その引っかけた当の男は、一生覚えているだろうと確信した。
source.english: Thus the twins cast aside one path to salvation. At the very instant two invincible women were neatly snared by one man's tears and near-fraudulent stratagem, a single gust went racing beneath the night sky where phantasmal lights danced, through the midst of a company achieving its grotesque sublimation and scattering radiance. The man who had snared them knew with certainty that he would remember that wind all his life.

source.japanese:
凍気に澄んだ風ではない。
　一体どこから吹ききたったものか、けれどそれは確かに。どこか生臭くさえある、精気に充ち満ちた、それは、潮風だった。
　シサムとキサラを祝福するように巻いて、吹き抜けて、二人の金の髪をなびかせて。
　帰ろう帰ろうと、背を向けた集団、かつては信天翁号に別れてまで追いかけた巡礼者達には、もう一瞥もくれずの切り替えの速さ。
　朔屋はこれでこそ、ただひたすらの歓喜のあまりに二人の腰にまた抱きつこうとしたら、今度は見事に躱[かわ]されて、氷原に顔から突っ込んで、嬉しいやら痛いやらの涙で顔を上げたところ、
source.english:
This was no wind purified by the cold.
Where could it have come from? Yet unmistakably it was a sea breeze, full of vitality, almost rank with life.
It curled around Sisam and Kisara as though blessing them, swept past, streamed their golden hair. Come home, come home.
They spared no further glance for the gathering they had turned their backs upon, the pilgrims they had once abandoned even the Albatross to pursue. Such a quick change of heart. That's more like it.
In sheer joy Sakuya tried to embrace their waists again. This time they evaded him neatly, and he plunged face-first into the ice. He raised his face through tears of happiness and pain—

target.text: Thus, the twins forsook one path to salvation. The instant these two peerless woman were completely suckered in by a single man's tears and something bordering on a swindle, beneath the sky where bewitchingly ethereal lights danced, amidst a group of people who scattered light as they carried out their mysterious sublimation, a single gust of wind swept by, and the man against whom it brushed was certain that it would stay with him forever.

It was not a wind carrying an icy clarity. He knew not where in the world it had blown in from, but there was no doubt, this was surely. Something about it smelled fishy, it was brimming with vitality, it was───the salty sea breeze. It enveloped Shisamu and Kisara as if giving them its blessing, then blew across the field, making their golden locks flutter in its wake.

Let's go back, let's go home, the group chanted as they turned their backs on the pilgrims whom they had once pursued, and so doggedly that they had even parted ways with the Albatross at that, shifting gears so fast they didn't so much as spare them a glance. The immense joy that this in particular brought Sakuya made him attempt to sling his arms around their waists once more, but this time, they evaded him flawlessly, leading him to land face first on the icy field, and right as he raised his head once more, both tears of happiness and pain flowing freely,

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「いやいやいやいや、ちょっと。
　そんなにあっさりと脱退を宣言されても、
　こっちとしては大いに困るのですよ」
source.english:
“No, no, no, no—wait.
You cannot simply announce your withdrawal so casually.
That leaves us in a very difficult position.”

source.japanese: 三人の針路に割って入ったのは、あの朔屋を否んだ巡礼者の、彼に対する威厳とか知性とか、は、なぜかあまり双子には効果を発揮しないようで、あっさりと斬り捨てられた。
source.english: The pilgrim who had refused Sakuya stepped across their course. His dignity and intellect, so effective upon the young man, somehow worked much less well upon the twins. They cut him short.

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「No no no no, a moment, please. Even should you proclaim your withdrawal so readily, you still leave us in a very difficult position.」

Wedging his way in front of their course was that one pilgrim who had refused Sakuya, but for whatever reason, that gravitas and intelligence he had displayed before Sakuya didn't seem to have much effect on the twins, and he was flatly cut down.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「んなこといわれたって、さぁ……。
　なるほど、昇華には未練があるよ。
　でもそれって、あたしらがそういう風に生まれついたってだけのことだろ」
source.english:
“You can say that, but… Sure,
I still want sublimation.
But isn't that just because we were born that way?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「You say that, but, you know……. Okay, sure, we do have some lingering attachment to the sublimation. But that's just the way we were born, isn't that all there is to it?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんたらが、この馬鹿よりもっとみっともねぇ泣きっ面見せてくれたら、考え直さないでもないさ」
source.english: “Show us a crying face uglier than this idiot's, and we might reconsider.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If you guys can show us a teary face even more pathetic than what this idiot managed, then we're not saying it's impossible for us to reconsider.」

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「いや、貴女たちの、
　不遜と剛毅こそ賞賛に値します。
　その心力たるや、昇華に際してはどれほどの過剰エネルギーを生み出すか知れず……」
source.english:
“No.
Your defiance and fortitude are precisely what deserve admiration.
Who knows how much excess energy such strength of spirit would generate upon sublimation…”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「是非とも、考え直していただきたい」
source.english: “I most earnestly ask you to reconsider.”

source.japanese: と、物腰丁重ながらも朔屋はそこに、なにやら膨れあがってぱんぱんになりつつある風船の印象を見たという。あの慇懃無礼に自分を拒絶した巡礼者が、そういう小物くさい反応を見せたのについほくそ笑む、朔屋もまた双子の威を借る痩せ狐。
source.english: Polite though his manner was, Sakuya saw something in him like a balloon swelling taut, on the verge of bursting. This pilgrim, who had rejected him with such insulting courtesy, was showing a decidedly petty reaction, and Sakuya could not help grinning inwardly. He too was a scrawny fox borrowing the twins' might.

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「Oh no, we believe that your insolence and unyielding resolve in particular are what truly merit admiration. It is impossible to predict just how much surplus energy will be generated from that force of will during your sublimation……」
【Pilgrim】 「By all means, we would be much obliged if you would reconsider.」

Saying so, though his demeanour was polite, to Sakuya, he only gave the impression of an inflating balloon gradually growing closer to the bursting point. He couldn't help but smirk smugly upon seeing that pilgrim, he who had rejected Sakuya so condescendingly beneath that thin veneer of politeness, react so pettily; Sakuya was also but a scrawny fox puffed up with authority borrowed from the twins.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ああもう鬱陶しいなぁ。
　朔屋とどっちがどっちだろ」
source.english:
“God, you're annoying.
Which is worse, you or Sakuya?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Argh, you're so annoying. Who should I go with then, Sakuya or that other guy?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋に決まっているさあ。
　だって朔屋は鬱陶しい上に馬鹿なんだよ」
source.english:
“Sakuya, obviously.
He's annoying and stupid.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はっはっは、もう涙も出ませんよ」
source.english: “Ha-ha-ha. No tears left now.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Sakuya, obviously. Because Sakuya isn't just annoying, he's also an idiot.」
【Naomasa】 「Ha-ha-ha, you will get no more tears out of me.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そりゃあんだけ泣けばね……」
source.english: “Not after crying that much…”

source.japanese: とうとう業を煮やして、巡礼者押しのけて場を離れようとする双子と、その後をひょこひょこへらへらの半笑いで追いかけていく朔屋の、どちらにむけと巡礼者達はついに溜めこんでいた怒りを爆発させたのだろう。
source.english: At last the twins lost patience and tried to shove past the pilgrims. Sakuya bobbed after them with his foolish half-smile. Which of the three finally set the pilgrims off? Whatever the answer, all the anger they had stored up now exploded.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「No shit, what with all that crying you already did……」

Having at last lost their patience, the twins shoved the pilgrim aside and made to leave, Sakuya trailing after them, a bounce in his step and a flippant half smirk on his face; now, who could it possibly be that the pilgrims finally decided to direct the explosion of their pent-up anger at?

source.japanese: キサラが一人巡礼者を押しのける、とその後にはまた巡礼者、それを今度はシサムが押しのけて、通れば次は朔屋の前にまた巡礼者だが、青年は内心ではなんだ浮かない金太郎飴みたいな、と毒づきながらも外では双子のように強引に出る気概もなくて、どーもどーもと半笑い、彼特有のあのにやけ笑いで脇を抜けた、ら。
source.english: Kisara pushed one pilgrim aside; another stood behind him. Sisam pushed that one aside. Once they passed, still another faced Sakuya. Like a stick of Kintaro candy: the same glum face on every slice. So he cursed them inwardly. Outwardly, he lacked the twins' nerve for forcing a passage. ‘Much obliged, much obliged,’ he simpered, and slipped around the pilgrim. Then—

source.japanese: 三人の前途にずらりと壁を造ったる巡礼者の列、皆杖を、敵に向けるかたちに構え筒。
source.english: Pilgrims formed a wall across their path. Every staff pointed at them as at an enemy.

target.text: Kisara pushed one pilgrim aside, then there was another right after, this time shoved aside by Shisamu, and as they passed him, a pilgrim stepped in front of Sakuya next; while the young man internally spoke bitterly of them, thinking them all cut from the same dour cloth, he didn't have the backbone to show it by acting overbearing like the twins did, so he instead sidled past them with his usual faint smirk, mumbling "thanks, see ya" while passing them by, but then.
The pilgrims had formed a long wall of a line cutting off the trio's path forward, all brandishing their staves like they were facing the enemy.

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「……我らの秘儀と世界の秘密、
　目の当たりにしておいてそのまま戻れるなど、思わないでいただきたい」
source.english:
“…Do not imagine
that, after witnessing our secret rite and a secret of the world, you may simply return.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「特にその男の無礼な態度は目に余る」
source.english: “That man's insolence, in particular, is intolerable.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「貴女たちお二人には、
　改悛の余地もまだありましょう……。
　しかしそ奴だけは許せませんな」
source.english:
“There may yet be room
for repentance for you two ladies.
But that fellow cannot be forgiven.”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「まずは先にそのふざけた男を引き渡して頂きたい。貴女たちの処遇はその後で」
source.english: “First hand over that ridiculous man. We shall decide your treatment afterward.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……参考までに聞くけど、俺、どうなっちゃう予定……？」
source.english: “…Just for reference, what's supposed to happen to me…?”

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「どうもせんよ。ただここに放置していくだけだ。だが聖双生児を誑[たぶら]かした愚か者には衣服などもったいない。腰のものだけは許してやるが」
source.english: “Nothing. We shall merely leave you here. But clothing is wasted on a fool who beguiled the Sacred Twins. We will permit you to keep what covers your loins.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「死ねって言ってんじゃないかそれ。
　なんで俺ばっか集中砲火でっ」
source.english:
“That's telling me to die.
Why am I the only one getting all the fire?”

source.japanese: 自分がそういう巡り合わせに産まれた事を、どうしても理解しきれないのが青年の不幸か、うんざりする彼を戒めようとたちまち迫る長衣の手、手、手、構えられたる杖、反射的に両手を挙げてホールドアップするより、速かった。銃声の方が。
source.english: Perhaps Sakuya's misfortune lay in never quite accepting that he had been born under a star that led to encounters like these. Robed hands swiftly closed in to chastise the exasperated young man. Hands, hands, hands. Raised staffs. Before he could reflexively throw up his own hands in surrender, something came faster: a gunshot.

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「……Now that you have witnessed our secret rite, as well as one of the world's great secrets, I would rather you not assume you can simply return as you are.」
【Pilgrim】 「That man's insolent attitude is particularly unpardonable.」
【Pilgrim】 「For the two of you, there is surely still room for a show of contrition……. But that one is beyond forgiveness.」
【Pilgrim】 「First, we would appreciate it if you would hand over that impertinent man to us. You two shall be dealt with afterwards.」
【Naomasa】 「……Just asking for reference, but, what's the plan for me exactly……?」
【Pilgrim】 「Nothing at all. You will simply be abandoned here. However, clothing is wasted on the fool who deceived the sacred twins. You shall be permitted what hangs from your waist alone.」
【Naomasa】 「Well that's just you telling me to die, isn't it? Why am I the only one in the line of fire here!?」

Perhaps the young man's true misfortune lies in his inability to reconcile with the unlucky star he was born under; in an effort to discipline the exasperated man, they flew out from beneath the robes: hands, hands, more hands, all brandishing staves, but it came faster than Sakuya could reflexively raise both his hands in surrender. The sound of gunfire.

source.japanese:
些か迫力を減じても相変わらず異妖にうねるオーロラの夜空、劈いて、走った閃光はあの三位一体者の飛翔よりよほど爽快と、青年の目を見張り、はしなかった。そもそもそちらを見ていなかったし、銃声の後に一拍遅れて頭を抱えて座り込んでいたから。
　ざっと包囲の輪を緩めた巡礼者達は、それでもまだ杖先を三人に向けてあり、その様を比べると、際立つ朔屋の姿の、情けなさ。
source.english:
Its flash cut across the night sky, where the aurora still undulated uncannily, though with a little less force. Far more bracing than the flight of the Triune One, it made the young man's eyes widen—no, it did not. He had not been looking that way. A beat after the shot, he had crouched down with his head in his hands.
The pilgrims drew back, loosening their circle, yet still held their staffs toward the three. Beside them, Sakuya's pathetic posture stood out.

target.text: Though its impact was somewhat dimmed, it yet writhed with uncanny grace; the auroral night sky was rent asunder, the flash of light streaking through it even more exhilarating to behold than those soaring Triune Beings; this, however, was not what Sakuya was thinking as he looked up at the night sky with eyes wide open. He wasn't even looking in the first place, actually, for he was cowering with his head in his hands as soon as the gunshot rang out. The pilgrims had loosened the ring they'd encircled them in with one swift motion, yet their staves remained pointed at the three, and compared to their poise, the pitifulness of Sakuya's form was only all the more striking.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「しつこい奴らだなぁ……。
　キサラ、やっぱシューキョーがらみはろくな目に遭わないよ」
source.english:
“Persistent bastards…
Kisara, nothing good ever comes of getting tangled up in religion.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「You people are damn persistent……. Kisara, there really is nothing good that comes from getting involved with religion.」

source.japanese: 銃口からの硝煙を吹き散らす唇の色、鮮やかに。
source.english: Her lips were vivid as she blew the smoke from the muzzle.

target.text: The colour of those lips, blowing away the gunpowder smoke rising from the muzzle, was vivid.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あの邑[ムラ]でさんざん学んだはずだったのに、うちらも朔屋のこと、馬鹿だと笑えないや。
　───とにかく橇船のほうまで！」
source.english:
“We should've learned that thoroughly in the village. Can't laugh at Sakuya for being stupid now.
Anyway, to the sled boat!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「That should have been hammered into our heads back in that village, so we're really in no position to laugh at Sakuya for being an idiot. ───Anyway, we gotta get to the sledge boat!」

source.japanese:
片割れのは威嚇、けれど次はまともに当てる、と総代格の巡礼者に照準合わせる眸[ひとみ]の、大胆不敵に。
　そして、蹲ったまま阿呆のように半開きの口で見とれる朔屋を、蹴ったぐって促す爪先は、かなり強い力で、容赦なく。
source.english:
Her twin's shot had been a warning. Her own next round would hit. Kisara fixed a bold, unflinching aim upon the pilgrim who seemed their spokesman.
Then her boot drove the still-crouching Sakuya into motion as he stared, mouth hanging open like an idiot. Hard. Without mercy.

source.japanese: 走り出す双子。逃げ出す朔屋。
source.english: The twins began to run. Sakuya began to flee.

target.text: One half's eyes were fixed on the pilgrim acting as the representative, telling him that while the first shot was a warning, the next would strike true, her gaze dauntless and daredevil. And finally, there sat Sakuya, still cowering with his mouth hanging open like a fool, mesmerized, until he was shoved with the tip of a boot, driven onwards with considerable force, mercilessly so.
The twins broke into a run. Sakuya took to his heels.

source.japanese:
執拗に追随してくる巡礼者達の、一体何がそこまで彼らを駆り立てるのか、双子への執着か朔屋への激甚か、知らず、引き離す為には双子は更に発砲を重ねなければならなかったが、撃つとなれば容赦がないのがこの二人である。
　夜の氷原は既に巡礼者の血を吸い黒々と濡れ、血潮は早くもシャーベット状に凝りつつあり、その骸に抱きついて軋り上げたその同胞の絶叫、悪夢にまで跨[また]ぎこしてきそうな、思えば斃[たお]された者は三位一体者であり、遺された者は永遠に昇華の機会を失った、という事なのだろう。
source.english:
What drove the pilgrims to such relentless pursuit? Fixation upon the twins, ferocious anger at Sakuya? They did not know. To shake them off, the twins had to fire again and again. Once shooting, neither showed mercy.
Blood had already soaked the night ice black and was beginning to congeal into slush. A fellow pilgrim embraced one of the bodies and loosed a grating scream that seemed capable of following them into their nightmares. The dead pilgrim had belonged to a triune group. Presumably those left behind had lost forever their chance at sublimation.

source.japanese:
その後の巡礼者達の追跡は、狂気じみていた。
　三人、どうにか帆掛け橇[ぞり]まで辿り着くも、キサラはやや息を荒くしている程度だが、シサムはそれよりも多少疲労が濃いが、それも当然か、右手には朔屋を引きずってあり、橇まで辿り着いてからペッと投げ出された青年は、別に追っ手の攻撃も受けてもいないのに、途中からはほとんどシサムの手で引きずってこられたというのに、息も絶え絶え、氷原に反吐などぶちまけていたり。
source.english:
After that, the pursuit became almost mad.
The three somehow reached the sailing sled. Kisara was breathing only a little harder; Sisam looked more plainly exhausted, and no wonder—she had spent the run dragging Sakuya with one hand. Once they arrived she spat him out onto the ice. Though none of the pursuers had so much as touched him, and Sisam had hauled him most of the way, the young man lay gasping and vomiting over the ice.

target.text: The pilgrims were doggedly gaining ground on them, but whatever could have possibly impelled them so; was it their fixation with the twins, or their vehement antipathy for Sakuya, they didn't know, and in order to keep their lead, the twins had to discharge their guns over and over again, but once they had decided to take that shot, these two were merciless.

The ice field beneath the night sky had already sucked up the blood of a pilgrim, drenched in jet black, the spurts of warm blood quickly beginning to freeze like sorbet, and the rasping wail of a comrade clinging to the corpse tore upwards, so harrowing it was as though he had crossed into the realm of nightmares, but come to think of it, the man killed had been a Triune Being, so it was likely because those of the trio left behind had forever lost their chance to sublimate.

After that, the pursuit by the pilgrims seemed almost frenzied in its intensity. Though the three of them somehow managed to make it back to the sail-driven sledge, while Kisara only seemed to breathe a little heavily, Shisamu's fatigue ran quite a bit deeper, but was that not only natural, for she was holding Sakuya with her right hand and dragging him along, and after reaching the sledge, the young man was flung off with a sharp flick; it wasn't even like he'd suffered a single blow from their pursuers, and yet partway through, Shisamu was practically hauling him along as he wheezed and gasped for breath, vomiting onto the ice.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「も、もそっとこう……優しく……っ」
source.english: “A little… gentler… if you could…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Be-, be more, you know…… gentle……」

source.japanese: 当然、朔屋のぼやきなど、帆掛け橇[ぞり]をあれこれしているキサラにもシサムにも黙殺されて、大体、今は朔屋を憂うより先に、懸念すべきは、とシサムは夜気に鼻を突き出して、匂いを嗅ぐようにしてから、思案顔に首を振った。
source.english: Naturally both twins, busy with the sailing sled, ignored his complaint. Before worrying about Sakuya, there was something more pressing. Sisam lifted her nose into the night air as if sniffing it, then shook her head thoughtfully.

target.text: Naturally, both Kisara and Shisamu turned a deaf ear to Sakuya's grumbling as they flitted about doing this and that on the sail-driven sledge, and to begin with, there was something they ought to be more concerned about than Sakuya; with that filling her mind, Shisamu stuck her nose into the night air, and after trying to sniff something out, she shook her head with a worried look.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「でも、風がないよ。
　曳いてくくらいなら、走ったほうが早いけど」
source.english:
“But there's no wind.
Faster to run than drag it.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But there's no wind. If we're gonna have to pull it, then it'd be faster to run.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それじゃあ何時までもは、続かない。
　……コルトの弾も、残り少ないしなあ」
source.english:
“Can't keep that up forever.
…Not many rounds left for the Colts either.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「But we can't keep that up forever. ……Don't have a lot of bullets left for my Colt either.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それはそれとして───
　その影で、なんか火ィ焚[た]いてるのは、なんだ？」
source.english:
“That aside—
what's that fire behind the sled?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Setting that aside for a moment─── Over in the shadows there, it kind of looks like a fire's burning, what's that?」

source.japanese:
ようやく立ち上がった朔屋の方が先に気づくのも妙な話だったが、帆掛け橇[ぞり]の影で、細い煙が上がっていた。
　回り込めば、三人の眸[ひとみ]が巡礼者などを相手にしていた時よりもよほど澱[よど]んで曇ったという。
source.english:
Oddly enough, Sakuya, only just back on his feet, noticed first. A thin thread of smoke rose in the sailing sled's lee.
When the three went around to look, their eyes grew far cloudier and duller than they had while facing the pilgrims.

target.text: It was odd that Sakuya, who had only just finally gotten back on his feet, was the first to notice, but from the shadow cast by the sail-driven sledge, a thin pillar of smoke was rising. Once they circled around, their eyes filled with a murkiness far duller than when they had been dealing with the pilgrims before.

source.japanese: 曇り濁る三者の眸[ひとみ]と裏腹に、緑を積層させて色深く艶[つや]やかに、氷原の寒夜に褪せるどころかむしろ透き通るように清[さや]かに、彼女が豆炭に火を点[とも]して、五徳で沸かし、優雅に啜[すす]っていた珈琲より黒い、もっと黒い。黒髪の密航者、氷原にて。
source.english: In contrast to their clouded, muddy gazes, her black hair gleamed richly, layer upon layer of green, so lustrous that rather than fading in the frozen night it seemed almost crystalline. Blacker than the coffee she had brewed over briquettes on a trivet and now sipped with elegant composure. Blacker still: the black-haired stowaway upon the ice.

target.text: In stark contrast to the clouded eyes of the trio, there was a variety of greens in laminate layers, saturated and glossy in hue, and a black that, far from fading in the cold night of the ice field, instead shone with such crystalline brilliance that it seemed almost translucent, blacker than what she was elegantly sipping, coffee boiled on a kettle stand heated by the fire she had lit using charcoal briquettes, blacker by far. It was the black-haired stowaway, on the ice field.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あっ。遅い。今頃来たって、珈琲は私が全部飲んでしまいましたー」
source.english: “Oh. You're late. I've drunk all the coffee already!”

source.japanese: なぜこうも得意気に言い放つのかの、三者三様の憮然の眼差しにも密航者、空のマグカップの底まで晒して、ついでにそこに残った豆の滓を五徳の火に翳[かざ]しての運勢占い、なにやら気に入らない卦が出たと見え、顔をしかめたが、朔屋達の方がよほど眉根は歪んでいた。
source.english: Why such a proud announcement? Under three differently disgruntled stares, the stowaway even held up the mug to display its empty bottom. For good measure she held the remaining coffee grounds over the trivet's flame to read her fortune. Apparently displeased by the omen, she frowned. Sakuya and the twins frowned far more deeply.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あの、なあ。お前、なんでいる」
source.english: “…Um. Hey. Why are you here?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Ah. You're late. You finally show up, but too bad, I already drank all the coffeeeeー」

Why was she saying that like she was proud of it? She even held up the cup before their eyes, each pair looking on with its own flavour of astonishment, showing off the empty bottom, and while she was at it, she also held the leftover coffee grounds over the fire on the kettle stand, divining their fortune, and it apparently showed her a fate that didn't suit her fancy, so she grimaced, but Sakuya and company's brows were furrowed into a far deeper frown.
【Naomasa】 「……Uhmm, listen. Why are you here?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あのね、私は密航者なんだから」
source.english: “Because I'm a stowaway.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Oh come on now, that's because I'm a stowaway.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「密航者が密航して、なにが悪い」
source.english: “What's wrong with a stowaway stowing away?”

source.japanese: 帆掛け橇[ぞり]をたんと叩いて大見得の、ちょっと見上げて何を想ったのか夜目にも頬を赤らめた、想った事はすぐに明らかになった。
source.english: She gave the sail-sled a resounding smack and struck a grand pose, then glanced upward and blushed visibly even in the dark. What she had been thinking soon became clear.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「What's so wrong with a stowaway stowing away?」

She struck a dramatic pose all while she gave the sail-driven sledge some hard taps with her knuckles, but then she looked a little upwards, and perhaps she remembered something, because her cheeks reddened noticeably even in the dark, and it quickly became clear exactly what she had recalled.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「人が密航して、それはもう健気に隠れているのに、君達と来たら毎日毎晩交尾交尾……。
　あれってそんなに気持ちいい？」
source.english:
“Someone stows away and hides ever so bravely, and what do you lot do? Mate, mate, every day and every night…
Does it really feel that good?”

source.japanese:
撃っちゃっていい？　と二人して銃口向けかけたが、思い直したのは大人げないとか哀れ思し召したからではなく、三人が越し方氷原の向こうに、光の列が鯨波伴って接近してくるのに、弾数が少ないのを思い出したからであろう。
　いかに双子が健脚韋駄天足だからとて、解囲しつつ朔屋を構いつつでは引き離すにも限度がある。向こうとて同胞を斃[たお]された、復讐の意地というのも手伝っていただろう。
source.english:
Both twins nearly trained their muzzles on her—Can we shoot her?—but thought better of it. Presumably not because they considered it childish or felt sorry for her, but because they remembered how few rounds they had left: beyond the ice field the three had crossed, a line of lights was bearing down on them amid battle cries.
No matter how fleet-footed the twins, there was a limit to how far they could pull ahead while breaking through the encirclement and looking after Sakuya besides. Their pursuers, for their part, had lost one of their own; the resolve born of vengeance must have helped drive them on.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Here I am, stowing away, doing my best to stay hidden like a saint, and you two are just going at it, day in and day out, mating and mating……. Does it really feel that good?」

"Can we just shoot her?" That was the question the two wordlessly asked as they began to raise their guns at her, but they didn't reconsider because they thought it immature or felt any pity for her; instead, they remembered that in the direction of the ice field they had just crossed, a rank of light accompanied by fierce battle cries was drawing ever nearer, but they were soon to be out of bullets.

Even should the twins have legs of steel and be as swift-footed as Idaten himself, there were limits to how much of a lead they could gain while also breaking the siege and having to worry over Sakuya. The opposing side was likely helped along by the desire to get revenge for their slain comrades as well. (TN: Idaten, written "韋駄天", is the Japanese name of the bodhisattva Skanda, known for his immense speed as he chased down demons that stole the Buddha's ashes, defeating them.)

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「それでどうするつもり、あれは。
　人格者めかした口ぶりだけど、あれ、えらい怒ってると思うよ」
source.english:
“So what are you going to do about those people?
They talk as if they're paragons, but I think they're awfully angry.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「言われるまでもなく、逃げるつもりだって。
　だがこいつを動かそうにも風が……」
source.english:
“You don't have to tell us. We're trying to run.
But to move this thing, we need wind…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So what do you plan on doing then, about those guys. They sure talked like they were paragons of virtue, but I think they're actually really mad.」
【Naomasa】 「We plan to run away, that goes without saying. But even if we try to get this thing gliding, there's no wind……」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「風なら───じきに吹くでしょう。
　船乗りというのなら、それくらい読めないの？」
source.english:
“Wind? It'll blow soon.
If you're sailors, can't you read that much?”

source.japanese:
さ、と片腕を体の脇に開いてまた、見得めいた姿勢の、芝居がかって鼻につく、事もなくこの娘の怜悧の秀貌と細身のしなやかな肢体がやると見事に箔をつける。
　それでも黒髪の、一筋もそよがず、
source.english:
She opened one arm out beside her, striking another pose. The theatricality did not even grate: her keen, fine features and slender, supple figure gave it a splendid distinction.
Yet not a single strand of black hair stirred.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「If you need wind, then───it should start blowing any moment now. If you call yourselves sailors, shouldn't you be able to read that much?」

Behold, she said as she swung one arm out to her side, once again striking a pose right out of kabuki, but with none of the gratingly pompous theatricality one might expect, for when this girl performed such gestures, the refined beauty of her sagacious visage and her slender, supple figure added a brilliant touch of dignity and prestige. And yet, not a single strand of her black hair rustled,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「適当なこと言ってンじゃないの。
　雲の様子も、空気の様子も、風が来る兆しなんてちっとも───」
source.english:
“Don't just make things up.
The clouds, the air—there's not the slightest sign of wind coming…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「You're just saying whatever pops into your head, aren't you? Far as I can tell from the clouds or the air, there's not even the slightest of signs that so much as a breeze───」

source.japanese:
黒髪の一筋もなびかせずと思いきや、そこに。一陣の風が、ひらひらと双子のミニスカートを捲[めく]りかけては果たせず、吹き抜けていった。
　ただ黒蜜の流れにはよく絡んで、一瞬間ではあれど、密航者の頭の回りに、たなびかせたのが、翼のように。
source.english:
Not a strand of black hair moving—or so it seemed. Then a gust swept through, made a play for the twins' miniskirts without quite lifting them, and passed on.
It caught beautifully in the stowaway's flowing black honey, however, spreading her hair about her head for an instant like wings.

target.text: Not a single strand of black hair rustled, or so they thought, but then. A gust of wind, one that tried to flip the twins' fluttering miniskirts but failed and blew past them. But it wrapped itself beautifully around the stream of dark molasses, and although it was just for an instant, it lingered around her head, making her hair flutter like a pair of wings.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「───あれぇ？」
source.english: “…Huh?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「───Huuuh?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ほら、吹いた」
source.english: “See? Wind.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「See, the wind blew.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「すげえしゃくに障[さわ]るが、有り難いは有り難い。朔屋、帆を上げて！」
source.english: “Pisses me off, but I am grateful. Sakuya, raise the sail!”

source.japanese:
そう、双子は航海士、素人どころかより小憎らしい密航者風情に味噌つけられた、しゃくに障[さわ]るも当たり前、ひどい八つ当たりの憎まれ口の一つもあって然るところを、前からキサラ、後からシサムが娘の首に上腕刀を同時に喰らわせて黙らせるだけに留めて、また口より手を使ったけれど、それは帆掛け橇[ぞり]を走らせる為に、別に密航者に噛みつく為ではない。
　あっさり昏倒した密航者の両足引っ張って短艇の中に引きずりこんでやったのは、朔屋としては温情と言うより、この娘と初顔合わせの時にたっぷりと鑑賞させてもらった臀への代金のつもりだった。
source.english:
Yes, the twins were navigators—and yet a mere amateur, worse still, an especially obnoxious stowaway, had shown them up. Naturally it rankled; no one could have blamed them for a spiteful word or two. Instead Kisara from the front and Sisam from behind clotheslined the girl's neck at the same instant and silenced her. Once again they acted first and talked later, but this was only to get the sail-sled moving, not to vent their anger on the stowaway.
Sakuya dragged the instantly unconscious girl into the boat by both ankles. Less an act of mercy, in his mind, than payment for the generous view of her backside she had given him when they first met.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「It is incredibly aggravating, but I have to admit, I appreciate it. Sakuya, hoist the sail!」

Yes, the twins were mates, so it was only natural that it would rub them the wrong way when made to look the fool by not just an amateur, but the likes of this smug little stowaway at that, and though it would only be expected for them to vent their frustrations with a bit of horribly abusive language, from the front came Kisara, from the back Shisamu, restraining themselves to just shutting her up by delivering a simultaneous lariat to the girl's neck with their upper arms, once more choosing action over words, but that was only because they needed to get the sail-driven sledge running, not because they were lashing out at the stowaway in particular.

Yanking the limp stowaway who had fainted readily into the boat by the legs wasn't exactly an act of compassion in Sakuya's book; he had intended it more as repayment for being given the pleasure of enjoying the sight of the girl's buttocks in full back during their first meeting.

source.japanese: 小癪なことに、それまで無風だったのが、降れば大雨吹けば嵐のたとえ通り、吹きも吹いたり、単帆の綱引きちぎらんばかり、吹いて吹いて吹き通しの。巡礼者風情など、たとえ犬橇繰り出してきたところで追いつけようもない、たちどころに引き離したそれは良い、それまでは彼方に見えていたオーロラが消えたのもほっとする。それも良い。微震がまだ続いているようなのも気にはなるが、これはどうしようもないので心の外に今は置く。
source.english: Infuriatingly, the absolute calm gave way to a wind worthy of the proverb: when it rains, it pours; when it blows, a storm. It blew hard enough almost to tear the single sail's ropes apart. Blew and blew and kept on blowing. Mere pilgrims could never catch them now, even on dog sleds. Leaving them instantly behind was good. The aurora vanished from the distance: a relief. Also good. The faint tremors seemed to be continuing, which was troubling, but nothing could be done about that, so for now they put it out of mind.

target.text: Cheekily enough, though it had been windless until then, as the old saying goes, if it rains, it pours, and when the wind blows, a storm is coming, and oh, how it blew and then some, as if trying to tear the single sail from the rope tethering it, it blew and blew and blew some more, right past them. The likes of those pilgrims didn't seem like they could ever hope to catch up to them, even had they sallied forth on dog sleds, and while swiftly gaining a lead over them was all well and good, it was also a relief that the aurora, which had lingered in the distance hitherto, was now gone. That, too, was good.
While the yet ongoing faint tremors running through the ice also weighed on his mind, there was nothing he could do about them, so for now, he decided to pay them no heed.

source.japanese: だが───
source.english: But—

source.japanese:
たとえ追跡者を引き離したところで、海岸線までは行き着くまでには、どうしても食糧と水が足らないのだ。口も一人増えた。
　……朔屋が、ぎょっと密航者を見やったのは、今更気づきもせいでいい事を、こういう時に気づいてしまったからの、間の悪さは危地にあろうが平時にあろうがこの青年、変わらない。
　氷原の滑走の震動に揺れる橇[そり]の、肋材にごんごん横頭を打ちつけたおかげで目覚めて半泣きになっている密航者に問いかける。
source.english:
Even with the pursuers left behind, there could not be enough food and water to reach the coast. They had another mouth now.
Sakuya looked at the stowaway in alarm. Now, of all times, he had noticed something he could have done without noticing. His timing remained bad, in peril or at peace.
As the sled jolted over the ice, the side of her head had knocked repeatedly against its ribs, waking her half in tears. Sakuya asked her—

target.text: However───

Even assuming they had managed to leave their pursuers behind, ultimately, there simply wasn't enough food or water left to last them until they reached the coast. And they also had another mouth to feed now. ……Sakuya's startled stare at the stowaway came from realizing something that really should have been obvious to him a long time ago, and it had to be at a time like this, of course, for whether in times of crisis or calm, the young man's terrible timing never changed.

And so he voiced his doubts to the stowaway, who was currently waking up half in tears thanks to her head slamming against the wooden ribs of the sledge, which was shaking violently from the shocks produced by its gliding across the icy field.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……そういえば、微妙に食糧の減りが早いと思っていたが、お前まさか」
source.english: “…Come to think of it, I thought the food was going a little fast. Don't tell me you…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……That reminds me, I was thinking that our food supply was dwindling at a strangely quick pace, but don't tell me that you───」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まさかってなに。
　食べ物なら自前で持ってきた私、なんて良心的な密航者。……けど途中で尽きてしまって、ちょっとだけ拝借したのはとっても秘密」
source.english:
“Don't tell you what?
