I brought my own food. What a conscientious stowaway I am. …But it ran out partway, and it's a very deep secret that I borrowed a little.”

source.japanese: ……密航者へ、舳先でじっとしとれと言い置いて、艫に集まって、朔屋達三人の、朔屋達三人による、朔屋達三人のための、緊急動議が開催された。
source.english: Telling the stowaway to stay still at the bow, the three gathered at the stern. An emergency meeting of Sakuya and the twins, by Sakuya and the twins, for Sakuya and the twins.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Don't tell you what? If you're talking about food, then I brought my own. What a conscientious stowaway I am, really. ……Though I did end up running out halfway through the trip, so the fact that I borrowed just a little bit has to stay super secret between you and me.」

……With a curt "you stay put at the bow" spat in the direction of the stowaway, he left her there, after which he called for an assembly at the stern; there, they convened for an emergency motion of the three, by the three, for the three.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……古い海洋冒険小説だとさ……飢えに負けて人肉食に手を出すって描写、時々あるらしいよ」
source.english: “…In old sea-adventure novels, apparently people sometimes give in to hunger and eat human flesh.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……So, you know how in old naval adventure fiction……sometimes, there's portrayals of people giving in to their hunger and trying their hands at cannibalism.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「密航者って人間なのかな。ほら、大陸で言う、両脚羊的な意味合いにおいて」
source.english: “Is a stowaway human? I mean in the mainland sense of a two-legged sheep.”

source.japanese: またこの二人、顎自体は先細形の美形なのだが、口自体は大きめで歯は尖ってえらく丈夫で噛む力も強い。その上大食らいだ。
source.english: Both had fine, tapered jaws, but rather large mouths, sharp, extraordinarily sturdy teeth and a powerful bite. They were also prodigious eaters.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I wonder if the stowaway's actually human. Look, like in the sense of what they call two-legged sheep in mainland China.」 (TN: These two-legged sheep she refers to is a euphemism for human meat, written "両脚羊", literally meaning "sheep with two legs", and it appears in many a Chinese historical record.)

Once more, though both had beautifully tapered jaws, their mouths were on the larger side, their teeth pointy and exceptionally sturdy, and their biting force was strong, too. On top of that, they were gluttons.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「その目はなぁに？
　ううん、見たことがある。
　精肉屋の軒先を覗いているお客さんのそれだ」
source.english:
“What's that look?
No, I've seen it before.
Customers looking into a butcher's shop.”

source.japanese:
いつの間にやら三人の輪の中にするりと潜[もぐ]りこんでいた密航者、言いつけ聞かず話を聞いてしまった密航者、そもそもそんな聞き分けいい玉なら密航者なんどになってなかったであろう密航者。
　世には聞かずに済ませたほうが幸せな事をあるものを、この時朔屋と双子は初めて彼女にしみじみ哀れな眸[ひとみ]を置いたという。
source.english:
At some point the stowaway had slipped into their circle. The stowaway who had ignored orders and overheard them. The stowaway who, had she been obedient enough to stay put, would never have become a stowaway at all.
There are things in this world one is happier never hearing. For the first time, Sakuya and the twins looked upon her with deep and heartfelt pity.

source.japanese: 密航者、朔屋をその、髪と同じで黒く、より澄んだ黒曜石の眸[ひとみ]で、真摯に見つめた。元が綺麗な貌立ちだけに、まっすぐに向き合うと朔屋の胸に要らぬ漣[さざなみ]に乱す。この娘はもう男って知ってるのかなぁ、などと。
source.english: The stowaway gazed earnestly at Sakuya with obsidian eyes, as black as her hair but clearer still. Her natural beauty meant that facing her directly sent an unwanted ripple through Sakuya's heart. Was she already acquainted with men, he wondered.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And whaaaat is that look in your eyes? No, I've seen that before. That right there's the look of a customer peeking into a butcher's shop.」

The stowaway, smoothly infiltrating their little circle before anyone realized it; the stowaway, not listening to his command and instead ending up hearing their conversation; the stowaway, had she been so compliant a character to begin with, then she surely wouldn't have been a stowaway in the first place. There are some things in this world that are better left unheard, and at that moment, for the very first time, Sakuya and the twins gazed upon her with an earnest look of pity in their eyes.

The stowaway, with those eyes, orbs of gleaming obsidian yet darker than even her hair, stared up at Sakuya with utmost sincerity. Though her visage was already beautiful enough as it was, when she stared right into his soul thus, it stirred needless ripples of turmoil in Sakuya's heart. Such as "I wonder if this woman has ever had a man before", and the like.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……直正。公平な評価をお願い。お肉の量的には、私と彼女達ではどっちが上？」
source.english: “…Naomasa. Give me a fair judgment. Who has more meat on her—me or those two?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「……Naomasa. I request your impartial assessment. Between me and these two girls, who's got more meat on their bones?」

source.japanese:
シサム、その碧の眸[ひとみ]で朔屋の心を強くしっかりと掴んだ。こんな綺麗な眸[ひとみ]が、先だっての晩では自分に乳房を掴まれただけで善[よ]がり啼[な]いたんだよなあ、などと想うと朔屋の股ぐらに要らぬ情火を掻[か]きたてる。
　抱いた事のある女とない女、今のところ分があるのはどちらか明白の。
source.english:
Sisam's blue eyes caught firm hold of Sakuya's heart. To think that a woman with such beautiful eyes had cried out in pleasure the other night at no more than his hand upon her breasts—that kindled a wholly unnecessary flame between his legs.
A woman he had known and a woman he had not: for the moment, there was no question which held the advantage.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「朔屋、冷静な判断をお願い。一等航海士と平船員、そして密航者の中で一番立場的に低いのはどれ？」
source.english: “Sakuya, use your head. Out of the chief mate, an ordinary sailor, and a stowaway, which one ranks lowest?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょっと待とうよ君達。短い時間になるかもしれないが、一つ船の仲間じゃないか。その中で別を着けるなんて俺にはできない」
source.english: “Hey, hold on. It might only be for a little while, but we're shipmates, aren't we? I can't play favorites among shipmates.”

source.japanese:
シサムとキサラ、密航者のどちらを立てるか朔屋には明白、だけれども。
　朔屋は密航者に二分と一両、の貸しは別段なけれども。先ほど橇[そり]に引きずり上げた時についうっかり触れてしまった彼女の臀と乳房と股ぐらの感触がまだ鮮やかに手に残っているからして、その辺りの名分は立てねばならんと考えた。
source.english:
For Sakuya, it was perfectly clear whether he ought to favor Sisam and Kisara or the stowaway.
And yet… It was not as though the stowaway owed him two bu and one ryō. But the feel of her buttocks, breasts and crotch, accidentally brushed when he hauled her onto the sled, still lingered vividly in his hands. Honor, he felt, demanded that he show her some consideration on that account.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ところで君達、カンビュセスの籤って知ってる？」
source.english: “By the way, have you heard of Cambyses' lottery?”

target.text: With those deep, aquamarine eyes, Shisamu seized Sakuya's heart in a firm, powerful grip. Just the other night, those eyes so beautiful had been moaning in satisfaction from her breasts being held in the hands of none other than himself, and as he thought such things, an entirely needless flame of passion was kindled in Sakuya's crotch. A woman he had made love to and one he had yet to: it was obvious who currently held the advantage.
【Shisamu】 「Sakuya, I request your calm judgment. Between a chief mate, a sailor, and a stowaway, who ranks the lowest?」
【Naomasa】 「Let's pause for a moment here, ladies. It might only be for a brief time, but are we not all in and from the same boat here? I couldn't possibly bring myself to choose between you.」

To Sakuya, the choice between Shisamu and Kisara or the stowaway was crystal clear, but still. While it wasn't as if Sakuya owed any particular debt to the stowaway, not even two bu and a ryo, still. The sensation of touching her butt, her chest, and her crotch by what could only be careless mistake when he had dragged her up into the sledge a little earlier still lingered vividly in his hands, and given that, he thought that some manner of justification had to be established first. (TN: A bu and a ryo, written "分" and "両" respectively, are obsolete currency units from pre-Meiji Japan.)

【Naomasa】 「Incidentally, have you ever heard of The Lottery of Cambyses?」 (TN: The Lottery of Cambyses is a short story by manga artist Fujiko F. Fujio, who is best known for the world-famous Doraemon among many other stories. It is from 1977 and inspired by Cambyses II's ill-fated expedition to Ethiopia as described by Herodotus, where the soldiers eventually resort to cannibalism. The lottery part is fiction, however.)

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「うわこいつえっげつねぇ……。あれってさ、運に任せるみたいなこと言ってるけどさ、絶対仕込みがあったよね」
source.english: “God, that's vicious… They say it's leaving it to luck, but there was definitely some rigging, wasn't there?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Wow, this guy's nasty……. That's you just telling us to leave it to fate, but you've definitely got some trick prepared, haven't you?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あー、確かに人が一〇人もいれば、一人くらい嫌われる奴って出てくるもんねえ」
source.english: “Ah, sure. Get ten people together, and one's bound to be disliked.”

source.japanese: これで話が通じる辺りは、やはり双子と朔屋の仲というところだし、いまいち飲みこめない様子の密航者は、このままだといざというとき本当に───
source.english: That they understood one another at this was a measure of Sakuya's intimacy with the twins. The stowaway seemed not quite to grasp it. At this rate, when the crisis really came—

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Ah, but it is true that with ten people in a group, there's always going to be that one guy who nobody likes, right?」

That they had a mutual understanding here just went to show exactly how close Sakuya and the twins had grown, and so at this rate, when push came to shove, the stowaway, who still hadn't caught on just yet, might actually end up being───

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「え、なに。どういうこと」
source.english: “Huh? What? What do you mean?”

source.japanese: 双子と朔屋が、彼女をどう料理するのか、それはその筋には高く売れるお話になったのかも知れないが、このお話には別の風が吹くのである。
source.english: How the twins and Sakuya might cook her up could perhaps have made a story that sold well to a certain clientele. But a different wind blows through this story.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Huh, what? What are you talking about?」
How would the twins and Sakuya cook her? That in itself might make for a story that could fetch a premium amongst certain circles, but a different wind blows through this tale.

source.japanese: キサラは密航者の最上等の絖[ぬめ]に優る肌理で、その上その白さの質、自分達より上等なのを東洋の神秘、と溜息で、ついつい指でなぞって突いて確かめていたけれど、視界の端に映ったものにぎょっと顔を上げた。
source.english: The stowaway's skin was finer-grained than the finest silk. Its whiteness, too, seemed somehow more exquisite even than the twins' own—some mystery of the East, Kisara thought with a sigh. She found herself tracing it with one finger, then giving it a little poke to make sure. Something at the edge of her vision made her look up with a start.

target.text: With a sigh, Kisara muttered that it must be one of the mysteries of the Orient how the texture of the stowaway's skin, which surpassed even the finest of silks, and boasted a whiteness of such rare quality on top of that, was of a finer grade than their own, and she had even unconsciously begun to trace it and poke at it with her finger to confirm its qualities, but startled by something at the edge of her vision, she jerked her head up.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……みんなちょっと向こうを見て。
　朔屋、望遠鏡───！」
source.english:
“…Everyone, look over there a second.
Sakuya, telescope!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……Everybody, have a quick look over here. Sakuya, the telescope───!」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだあれ、氷原が割れて……海？
　二人も見てみろ！」
source.english:
“What's that? The ice field's cracked…
Sea? You two look too!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「What is that, the ice is breaking…… the ocean? You two, come have a look too!」

source.japanese: 氷原に巨大な亀裂が走り、そして───
source.english: A vast fissure ran through the ice. And—

target.text: A colossal fissure ran through the icy field, and then───

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「それはだって、『北極圏』は氷が海を覆っているところだもの。その氷が割れたなら、海面が現れるのは、当たり前」
source.english: “Well, the ‘Arctic Circle’ is where ice covers the sea. If the ice cracks, obviously the surface of the sea appears.”

source.japanese: 密航者が呟くが、誰も相手にしない。
source.english: The stowaway muttered this, but nobody paid her any attention.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Well, that's just because ice covers the sea in the 『Arctic Circle』. So if that ice is sundered, the sea will become visible, obviously.」
Nobody paid any heed to the stowaway's muttering.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あっはっはっは！　朔屋、この望遠鏡壊れてるよ。さもなきゃあたしの目が壊れたか」
source.english: “Ha-ha-ha-ha! Sakuya, this telescope's broken. Or my eyes are.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「AH-HA-HA-HA! Sakuya, this telescope is broken. If not, then maybe my eyes are.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「貸して、キサラ！　一体なにが───
　あはははははっ、あたしの目もおかしくなったか雪盲か」
source.english:
“Give it here, Kisara!
What on earth—ha-ha-ha-ha! My eyes must've gone wrong too. Snow blindness?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだよ、確かに地形が変わったのは凄いと思うが、そんなにおかしいものが見えるのか？」
source.english: “What? Sure, a change in the terrain is amazing, but are you seeing something that strange?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Give that here, Kisara! What the hell is even─── Ahahahahaha, are my eyes also broken or is it snow blindness?」
【Naomasa】 「Come on, I do think the shift in terrain is incredible and all, but does it really look that bizarre to you?」

source.japanese:
───かつて、船があった。
　
　
　
　　　　船があった───
　
　
　
　　　　船の名は───
source.english:
—Once there was a ship.
There was a ship—
The ship's name—

target.text: ───Once upon a time, there was a ship. There was a ship─── And that ship's name was───

source.japanese:
【直正】
『見えたぁぁぁ！　おかしいものがぁ！
　なんであの船が　　こんな氷原に!?』
source.english:
‘I see it! Something strange!
Why's that ship in an ice field like this!?’

target.text: 【Naomasa】 『I SEE IIIIIIIT! SOMETHING BIZARRE! WHY IS THAT SHIP OUT HERE IN THE MIDDLE OF THE ICE!?』

source.japanese: 『信天翁号』！
source.english: ‘The Albatross!’

target.text: 『The Albatross』!

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あの信天翁号が、
　こんな頼もしく見えるなんて」
source.english:
“The Albatross—
I never thought she'd look so reassuring.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「To think the day would ever come where the Albatross, of all things, would be this reassuring a sight.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんか……複雑……」
source.english: “I have… mixed feelings…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それにしても……なんだってあの船が、こんなところまで……」
source.english: “Still… Why would she have come all the way here?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I kind of have……mixed feelings……」
【Naomasa】 「Even so……why is that ship all the way up here……」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「なんでって？　あの船は、もとよりこの周辺の調査を請け負っていたんじゃない。普通に仕事を、こなしているだけだと思うのだけど」
source.english: “Why? Didn't that ship take on a survey of this area in the first place? I think she's simply doing her job.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Why, you ask? Didn't that ship undertake a request to survey this area in the first place? I'm pretty sure that they're just actually doing their job.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「おいキサラ。この女、締めとこう。
　皆に通じるかどうかわからないけど、あたしらの脱走、こいつのせいにするっていうのはどう？」
source.english:
“Hey, Kisara. Let's tie her up.
Don't know if everyone will buy it, but how about blaming our desertion on her?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Oi, Kisara. Let's tie this woman up. I don't know if they're all going to buy it or not, but how about we pin our desertion on her?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「賛成。朔屋、綱を用意して。
　変な色気を出さないで、普通に縛ればいいから」
source.english:
“Agreed. Sakuya, get some rope.
Don't get any funny ideas. Just tie her up normally.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Agreed. Sakuya, prepare the rope. And please don't make it weirdly sexy, just tie her up like a normal person.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あれ？　私なんにもおかしな事言ってないのに、どうしてまたこう……ぐるぐる巻きに。
　痛いのよ、きついのよ、締まるのよ。
　やーめーてー……っっ」
source.english:
“Huh? I haven't said anything strange. Why am I being wrapped up again?
It hurts. It's tight.
It's squeezing. Stop…!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Huh? I haven't even said anything weird, so why am I being all…… wrapped up like this again? It hurts, it's tight, it's constricting. PLEASE STOOOOOPー……」

source.japanese: こうして三人は信天翁号に帰還を果たしたのだった───
source.english: Thus the three returned to the Albatross—

target.text: Thus, the three of them managed to return home to the Albatross───

source.japanese: ええおい、朝が爽やかで一日の始まりを祝福する、夏には涼やか、冬には清冽に身を引き締めて、春秋は清涼な、とにかく素敵な時間だと誰が言いやがった誰が決めた、と朔屋のぼやきは変に悪ずれして荒んであり、毒を吐き出した後も煙草を深々吸いこんで別の毒を肺に落としては溜息と共に色あせた紫煙を吐き捨てる。
source.english: Oh, come on. Who the hell had said—who had decided—that morning was a lovely hour, fresh and full of blessing at the day's beginning? Cool in summer, bracingly clear in winter, crisp in spring and autumn? Sakuya's complaints had grown peculiarly jaded and foul. After spewing one poison, he drew deep on his cigarette, dropped another into his lungs, and sighed out faded purple smoke.

source.japanese: 実際、朔屋の悪愚痴は故もない事ならず、波止場が迎えたこの朝の日は、重度のアルコール中毒患者の目のように濁って血走って、堤防に寄せくる波も濁って油が薄混じり、まだ潮も温んでいないから目立たないだけで、昼間ともなれば風には重油に臭気混じろう。
source.english: In truth, his venomous grumbling was not without cause. The morning sun over the quay was muddy and bloodshot as the eyes of a severe alcoholic. The waves lapping at the breakwater were turbid, thinly filmed with oil. Only the lingering chill of the sea kept it from being obvious; by midday the wind would carry the stench of fuel oil.

source.japanese: そして景色のみならず、時間もまた、朔屋にとっては新しい一日の始まりと言うより、夜のだらだらとした続きなのだった。それも腐れきって、酒と暴力となかば狂った哄笑が渦巻く最低の。
source.english: Nor was it only the view. To Sakuya, the hour seemed less the start of a new day than a dragging continuation of the night. A thoroughly rotten night, swirling with booze, violence and half-mad laughter. The worst.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「見えた見えた、短艇見えた～！
　おーーい、ウチらはここだーーーぃ！」
source.english:
“There, there! The boat!
Heeey! We're over here!”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「おー来たかぁ。
　今晩もどうにか逃げ切ったなあ。
　ねえ朔屋？」
source.english:
“Oh, here it comes.
Got away again tonight, somehow.
Right, Sakuya?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あーそうねぇー……」
source.english: “…Ah. Yeah…”

source.japanese:
そして双子達ばかりが、この濁り爛[ただ]れた朝日の中で生命力に満ちあふれて、喚く声は朔屋の耳を劈[つんざ]く、信天翁号からの迎えの短艇に喜ぶ跳ね回るのは良いとしても、そう晒しを巻いただけの上半身裸でやられては目の毒でたまらない。シサムに適当に受け答えしてやったつもりだけれど、やはり目が奪われる。
　こんなに疲れ切っているのに、そこだけは元気に主張を始めた逸物の位置をごそごそ整え、また一吸い、やろうとした煙草は横合いからねだられた。
source.english:
Only the twins brimmed with life in that murky, festering sunrise. Their shouts split Sakuya's ears. Fine for them to leap about at the sight of the boat sent from the Albatross, but to do it bare above the waist save for the cloth bound around their chests was more temptation than his eyes could bear. He thought he had given Sisam a suitably casual answer, but his gaze kept being drawn back.
Exhausted as he was, his cock alone began vigorously asserting itself. He fidgeted it back into place and went to take another drag, only for Kisara beside him to demand the cigarette.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「はーやーくーっ、
　朔屋、煙草、美味そうねえ。一本ちょうだい」
source.english:
“Hurry up!
Sakuya, that cigarette looks good. Give me one.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「悪いがこいつが最後の一本だ。
　回し呑みになるけど、それでもいいならね、
　そら、どうぞ」
source.english:
“Sorry, this is the last.
We'd have to share. If that's okay,
here you go.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「すはぁーー、あー、徹夜明けの煙草は脳にくらくらくるのう！　朔屋、今度は薄荷煙草のがいいな」
source.english: “Shaaah… Ah, a cigarette after an all-nighter goes right to the brain! Get menthols next time, Sakuya.”

source.japanese: 噴き出す紫煙の量、朔屋にも増して盛大に、朔屋もキサラもそしてシサムも、煙草は以前は遊び程度だったのだけど、近頃では常習化した。
source.english: She expelled even more purple smoke than he did. Once Sakuya, Kisara and Sisam had smoked only for amusement. Lately it had become a habit.

source.japanese: 首に巻き付く腕[かいな]の力は相変わらずに強い。が、傷だらけ包帯だらけで、今だって真新しい血がじくじく滲み、もう周りも血の赤、海も血の赤、双子も血の赤で、ついでにキサラから戻ったきた煙草をまた一口やれば、煙が血の匂い混じり、見れば吸い口は血に滲んでいた。唇も切れ、ばかりか片眼には眼帯のように包帯、片眼の女海賊の誉れここに有りとでも言いたげに、笑う。さも愉[たの]しそうに笑う、そして酒場からかっぱらってきた最上等の酒で口を濯[ゆす]いで吐き出せば、それにもまた血が混じった。
source.english: The arm around his neck was as strong as ever, though it was gashed and bandaged, fresh blood seeping through even now. Red blood around them; red blood upon the sea; the twins red with blood. Sakuya took another pull from the cigarette Kisara passed back, and even its smoke smelled of blood. He looked. The end he had put to his lips was stained red. Her lips were split, and one eye was bandaged like a patch. She laughed as though proudly claiming the rank of one-eyed woman pirate. Laughed so happily. Then she rinsed her mouth with the finest liquor, stolen from the tavern, and spat. Blood mingled with that too.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ほら朔屋、あんたも一口やりなよ。
　煙草の後はキスが燻くさくていけないや、酒で流しな」
source.english:
“Here, Sakuya. Have a sip too.
Kissing after cigarettes tastes smoky. Wash it away with booze.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あー、そいつはすまん」
source.english: “Ah, sorry about that.”

source.japanese:
煙草を回し、酒を回される、お互いに馴染みきって、あたしの男、俺の女と衒[てら]いもなく口に出るようになった仲なのに、受け取る朔屋の口ぶり些[いささ]かしょっぱい。
　まあ、無理もないのだ。
source.english:
Passing the cigarette, passing back the liquor. They had grown so utterly familiar that ‘my man’ and ‘my woman’ now came to their lips without embarrassment. Yet Sakuya sounded a little sour as he accepted the drink.
Well, naturally.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「朔屋、あんたなんか……怒ってたり拗[す]ねてたりする？　似合わないぞ、悩み顔で眉間に皺なんか」
source.english: “Sakuya, are you… angry or sulking or something? Worried frowns don't suit you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……別に拗[す]ねたりふて腐れたりじゃないよ。
　たださ、気になってね」
source.english:
“…Not sulking. Not in a bad mood.
It's just worrying me.”

source.japanese:
そう、べつに朔屋は双子に対して怒りを覚えているわけではない。抱いているのは懸念。双子を案ずる心の───自分の女の体を労[ねぎら]ってやって何が悪い。
　つい誰にともなくまた愚痴を垂れるのは、近頃本当に抵抗なくそうするりと言えるようになっている嬉しさの、裏返しなのかも知れなかった。
source.english:
No, Sakuya was not angry at the twins. What he felt was concern, worry for them. What was wrong with looking after his women?
Perhaps this latest complaint, muttered to no one in particular, was merely the other side of his happiness at how easily those words came to him now. Without resistance. Without embarrassment.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんたら二人、北方から帰ってきてから、
　まあはっきり言って無茶振りばっかだ。
　見れ、前の傷も癒えない前から、
　今夜のどんちゃかでまた傷だらけでないの」
source.english:
“Since you two came back from the north, frankly,
you've been doing nothing but reckless shit.
Look. The old wounds haven't healed,
and tonight's racket's left you covered in fresh ones.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それさあ……お互いがどっちか、分けるつもりでか？」
source.english: “Are you doing that… so I can tell the two of you apart?”

source.japanese:
先だってからずっと気になっていた事だ。
　朔屋は、まあ、よく言っても世故い小手先技で、この世界から飛翔しようとしていた二人をこちらの側に、ろくでもない世界に引き戻した。
　あの寒い氷原での出来事は、いまだ色あせずに記憶に残ってあるが、あんな心臓に悪い事はさっさと忘れてしまいたい、けれどあそこを通り抜けてきたおかげで双子達と結びついた、そちらの記憶は何時まででも大切にしておきたいので、痛し痒しというところ。
source.english:
It had been worrying him for a while.
By what could generously be called a shabby little piece of worldly cunning, he had drawn the pair—just as they were about to fly out of this world—back to his side.
Back to this worthless world. What happened upon that frozen field remained undimmed in his memory. He wanted to forget an ordeal so hard on the heart as quickly as possible. Yet it was by passing through that ordeal that he had bound himself to the twins, and he wanted to treasure that memory forever. A mixed blessing.

source.japanese: 問題は北海から戻ってきた後の二人だ、そして自分だ───
source.english: The problem was the twins after their return from the northern sea—and Sakuya himself—

source.japanese: もちろん、信天翁号に戻るにあたっても一悶着あった。最終的に宗右衛門猫が恩赦を下し、そして全ての罰を密航者が被ってくれなかったら、朔屋とシサムとキサラは何処の女衒と男娼窟に売り払われていたか知れたものではない。ちなみに行く先は、朔屋が女衒で双子が男娼窟である。信天翁号に伝ある女衒は男色家で男娼窟の女支配人は六〇絡みの白豚も真っ青の女傑だがそれはさておき、密航者は替わりに売られていって、その晩の皆の夕餐を贅沢にしてくれて、かついつの間にかその席に混じって人一倍喰らって呑んでいたというから、さしもの信天翁号の面子も天晴れ感じて刑は一等減じられ、いつものように吊されるだけで済んだ。
source.english:
Naturally, returning to the Albatross caused another commotion. Had Soemon the Cat not ultimately granted a pardon, and had the stowaway not shouldered the entire punishment, there was no telling to what procurer or den of male prostitutes Sakuya, Sisam, and Kisara might have been sold. Sakuya, incidentally, was for the procurer; the twins were for the brothel. The procurer known to the Albatross had a taste for men, while the brothel's female keeper was a sixtyish virago who would put a white sow to shame—but never mind that.
The stowaway was sold in their place. The sale paid for a luxurious dinner that evening; before anyone noticed, she had joined the feast and was eating and drinking more than anyone there. Even the crew of the Albatross were impressed enough to reduce her sentence by one degree. She escaped with merely being strung up, as usual.

source.japanese:
そしてそれから後の双子と来たら、朔屋が出会ってその傍若無人と命知らずに驚いていた頃よりまだひどい。とてもひどい。凄くひどい。
　戻ってきてから、二人がどれだけの数の鉄火場をくぐったのか、それに付き合って朔屋が何度死ぬような目に遭ってきたのか、数えるのも厭[いや]になってくる。
source.english:
Since then the twins had become worse even than when Sakuya first met them and marveled at their shamelessness and disregard for life. Worse. Much worse. Spectacularly worse.
He did not even want to count how many violent scrapes they had plunged through since returning, or how many times accompanying them had nearly killed him.

source.japanese: そして、それはもちろん厭[いや]で勘弁していただきたいとＮｏＴｈａｎｋＹｏｕ　の朔屋だが、双子との仲ある限りはこれは逃れられまいと、そちらはもう諦めの境地に達しつつあったのだけれど。
source.english: Naturally Sakuya hated that, wanted to be excused. No thank you. Yet he had begun resigning himself to the fact that, as long as he remained with the twins, there would be no escape.

source.japanese:
双子と港に寄るたびいかがわしげな盛り場に繰り出して、大騒ぎして、その都度乱闘騒ぎになるのも恒例の事になりつつあるけれど。
　シサムもキサラも、生傷負う事、以前よりずっと増えたような。
　むしろそういう乱闘の仕方を望んでいるような。
source.english:
At every port they visited some dubious pleasure quarter, made a racket, and ended in a brawl. It was becoming a ritual.
But Sisam and Kisara both seemed to be coming away with far more fresh wounds than before.
Almost as though this was precisely how they wanted to fight.

source.japanese: 近頃では、暴力沙汰の後の情事（双子は後で必ずそれを求めた。血を見た後は何時にも増して欲望激しく荒々しく燃やすのである）の時も、朔屋が変な小細工せずとも、このお腹の切り傷はシサム、この太腿の擦り傷はキサラと見分けられるようになってきており、とそこで朔屋は、もしや、と焦ったのである。
source.english: Lately, during the lovemaking that followed violence—the twins always demanded it afterward; seeing blood made their desire burn fiercer and wilder than ever—Sakuya had begun telling them apart without any little tricks. This cut across the belly belonged to Sisam; that scrape upon the thigh to Kisara. And there Sakuya suddenly panicked. Could it be—

source.japanese: 双子は、自分たちの区別をつける為に、あえて肌に傷を負うような真似を、と恐れたのである。
source.english: He was afraid the twins had begun deliberately taking wounds upon their skin so that he could tell them apart.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そうねえ、言われてみれば、それはそれであるかな？」
source.english: “Hmm. Now you mention it, maybe there's some of that too?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺はこれ、どう言うべきか……」
source.english: “How am I supposed to put this…”

source.japanese: 朔屋はなにやら、男女の情事の何も知らないよう初心な少女の処女を好き放題に破瓜したあげく、自分の欲望を好き勝手に押しつけてセックスを仕込み、気がついたら少女が目も当てられない色情狂に成り果てていた事に改めて気づいた時のように、いやそれよりもより深くひどく愕然となった、のだが。
source.english: Sakuya was horrified. As though, after deflowering an innocent woman who knew nothing of sex, taking his pleasure as he pleased, imposing every appetite and schooling her in the act, he had suddenly discovered that his pupil had become a nymphomaniac too dreadful to behold. No—he was more deeply, more terribly horrified even than that. And yet—

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんも言わんでいーって。
　結果的にそうなってる、ッてだけで」
source.english:
“Don't have to say anything.
That's just how it's worked out.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたしら、大いに愉[たの]しんでるんだこれはこれで」
source.english: “We're having a great time, in our own way.”

source.japanese:
双子は、何処までも屈託なかった。
　何処までも、底抜けに磊落ではあった。
　それが何か針が振り切れたような明るさではあっても、変に陰に籠もられるよりはずっと増しだと、朔屋はそう思い込もうとした。
　根が単純な彼だから、割と簡単だった。
　双子の陽性な笑い顔を大好きなのも、本当だったから。
source.english:
The twins were carefree to the end.
Boundlessly, incorrigibly free-spirited.
Even if their brightness seemed to have sent the needle off the scale, Sakuya told himself it was far better than watching them turn inward and dark.
Simple at heart, he found that fairly easy.
And it was true that he loved their sunny, laughing faces.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「今まではほれそのなんだ、わりと大人の対応で流してたとこあったじゃん、あたしらにゴロ撒いてくる奴にはさ」
source.english: “Up to now, you know, we sometimes took the grown-up approach and let things slide. With people who tried to start trouble with us.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……そーかぁー……？」
source.english: “…Did you…?”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そうだって。その場では堪[こら]えてたって大概は。でももうやめた、そんなんは」
source.english: “Sure. Most of the time we held back. But we've stopped that now.”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ただでさえくそったれな世の中なんだもん、
　そん中で毎日過ごすんだ、我慢は体に毒だってね」
source.english:
“It's a shitty enough world already.
We live in it every day. Bottling things up is bad for you.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ばーっと呑んで、がーっとぶん殴りあって、
　それがいいよ、なんも考えなくてすむ」
source.english:
“Drink like mad, beat the hell out of whoever's there.
That's better. Then we don't have to think.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「今までだって好き放題やってたじゃないかよう。
　なんやら大層なこと言ってるけど。
　本当は？」
source.english:
“You were doing whatever you wanted before too.

source.english:
A bargain—that was the only way to describe it. Sakuya sincerely believed so. Who cared how disgraceful he had looked? If tears could win a woman, he should have tried them much sooner.
Such were his thoughts. Yet whether he could have cried like that for any other woman—well. Well.

target.text: Ah, how invigorating the morning is as it blesses the beginning of the day; refreshingly cool in the summer, bracingly clear in the winter, crisp and fresh in the spring and autumn; anyways, who the hell ever said it was such a wonderful time, who made that call, Sakuya thought, his grumbling growing oddly jaded and rough, and after spewing his poison, he inhaled deeply on a cigarette, filling his lungs with yet another type of poison, then exhaled the dull, purple tobacco smoke with a sigh.

In reality, Sakuya's bitter complaints were not entirely without reason, for on this fine morning, as dawn fell upon the wharf, his eyes were turbid and bloodshot like those of someone suffering from severe alcoholism, and the waves crashing against the breakwater were also cloudy, lightly mixed with oil; it simply wasn't all that conspicuous since the sea water had yet to be warmed, but once it became noon, the stink of fuel oil would surely be carried on the wind.

And it was not just the scenery, it was also the time, for rather than it being the beginning of a new day, to Sakuya, it was just the night still dragging on. And that, too, had been completely rotten, the absolute worst kind of disgusting, jumbled swirl of booze, violence, and raucous laughter bordering on the insane.
【Kisara】 「I see it, I see it, I see the boat～! OOOーーI, WE'RE OVER HEREーーー!」
【Shisamu】 「Ooh, so it finally came? Got away by the skin of our teeth tonight too, huh. Right, Sakuya?」
【Naomasa】 「……Aah, riiight……」

And finally, the twins alone were brimming with vitality under the glow of this muddy, festering morning sun, their yells piercing Sakuya's ears, and while it was all well and good that they jumped around in joy at seeing the boat from the Albatross coming here to pick them up, when they did it while clad in nothing but a sarashi wrapped around their otherwise bare chests, it was far too great a temptation for him to resist. He'd intended to just give a noncommittal response to Shisamu, but he simply couldn't look away after all.

Although he was completely exhausted, that one most esteemed part of his body began to assert itself energetically, so he fidgeted to adjust its position, and just as he made to take another puff of the cigarette, he was pestered for it from the flank.
【Kisara】 「HUUーRRYYYーUUUPー, Sakuya, that smoke is looking mighty good. Gimme one please.」
【Naomasa】 「Sorry, but this here is the last stick I have. We'll have to pass it around, but if that's fine with you, here, go ahead.」
【Kisara】 「Fffhhhaaaaーー, aaーh, a smoke after pulling an all-nighter really gets the brain spinning! Sakuya, it sure would be great with some menthols next time.」

The volume of tobacco smoke she blew out was grand, greater even than what Sakuya had produced, and while Sakuya, Kisara, and Shisamu all had only dabbled in tobacco as but an amusement at first, it had grown into a habit lately.

The strength of the arm wrapping itself around his neck was as much of a force to be reckoned with as it ever was. But it was covered in wounds and bandages, and even now, fresh blood still oozed out from it; by now, all that surrounded him was blood-red, the sea was blood-red, the twins, too, were the red of blood, and as he tried taking another puff from the cigarette returned his way by Kisara, the smell of blood had mixed into the smoke, and as he looked, the filter tip was also stained with blood.

Not only was her lip split, she had a bandage wrapped over one eye like an eye patch, and she grinned, as though declaring that within here rests the honour of a one-eyed lady pirate. She smiled, as if truly enjoying herself, and as she spat out the top-shelf liquor, which she'd swiped from the bar, after rinsing her mouth with it, that, too, was mixed with blood.
【Shisamu】 「Come on, Sakuya, you take a mouthful too. Kisses after a cigarette taste way too smoky, so wash it down with some booze.」
【Naomasa】 「Aah, I'll pass on that.」

Passing the smoke, being passed the booze, although they had grown completely used to each other, close enough to call each other my man or my woman without a trace of pretense, there was a slightly bitter edge to Sakuya's tone as he took the bottle. Well, it was no great wonder.
【Kisara】 「Sakuya, are you a little…… mad or sulking or something? That worried look with the wrinkled brows, it just doesn't really suit you that well.」
【Naomasa】 「……It's not like I'm pouting or sulking or anything. It's just, it worries me, okay?」

Indeed, Sakuya wasn't feeling any anger towards the twins in particular. What he felt was worry. Concern for the twins───what was so wrong with wanting to tend to his woman's body? That he unconsciously ended up uttering complaints to nobody in particular might well have been the flip side of the joy he'd recently come to feel at being able to express himself so smoothly without any real hesitation.

【Naomasa】 「Ever since coming back from the north, you two have been, well, to put it bluntly, nothing but unreasonable. Look, your wounds from last time haven't even healed yet, and you're already covered in wounds again from tonight's commotion, aren't you?」
【Naomasa】 「So, about that……is this you attempting to distinguish yourselves from each other?」

It was something that was always weighing on his mind lately. Sakuya had, well, even when putting it generously, used a shrewd, cheap trick to keep these two, who had been on the verge of soaring away from this world, here on this side, had pulled them back to a worthless world.

What happened on that freezing plain of ice still remained fresh in his memory even now, but he really wanted to forget an experience that nerve-wracking as quickly as he could, but it was also only because he had made it through that situation that he was still connected with the twins, so he also wanted to treasure those memories forever; it was what one would call a double-edged sword, both a blessing and a curse.
The problem was these two after returning from the northern seas, as well as himself───

Of course, they ran into a minor spot of trouble upon returning to the Albatross. Ultimately, Souemon the cat granted them amnesty, and had the stowaway not taken all the punishment upon herself in their stead, who knows what manner of pimp and den of male prostitution that Sakuya, Shisamu, and Kisara would have been sold off to. Incidentally, Sakuya would be going to the pimp and the twins to the den of male prostitution. The pimp who the Albatross had a connection with was a sodomite, and the brothel madam in charge of the male brothel was such a formidable powerhouse of a woman, she could make even a white pig in his sixties turn pale.

Setting that aside, the stowaway was sold off in their place, and on that evening, they were all treated to a luxurious dinner; before they knew it, a certain somebody had joined them at the table, eating and drinking in unusual excess, and even the crew of the Albatross were won over to the point of expressing their admiration; thus, her punishment was commuted by one rank, and she got away with being strung up like usual.

And as for the twins after that, they were somehow even worse, managing to outdo even the outrageous insolence and recklessness that had shocked Sakuya so when first they met. Really awful. Absolutely terrible. After coming back, just how many deadly clashes of gunpowder and steel had the two made it through, and following their lead, just how many times had Sakuya come within an inch of death? He'd grown reluctant to even count.

And then, while Sakuya of course hated the idea, while he'd really rather be spared, No Thank You, as long as he was in a relationship with the twins, this could not be avoided, and so he had already reached a state of resignation on the matter, but.

It had gradually become established practice that every time the twins stopped by a port, they'd sally forth to some seedy-looking entertainment district, make a big ruckus, and every time that happened, it'd cause a scene and turn into an all-out brawl, but. Shisamu and Kisara both seemed to be receiving a lot more fresh wounds and bruises than before. Almost as if those brawls were actually what they hoped for.

Lately, even when they were enjoying their post-violence lovemaking (the twins would always ask for that after a fight; after seeing blood, their desire burned with a wilder intensity than usual), Sakuya didn't need to resort to any strange, petty tricks, for the one with this cut across the stomach was Shisamu, the one with that scratch on this thigh was Kisara; he'd become able to tell them apart in this way, and so, Sakuya thought, could it be, he worried.
He feared that the twins were acting in a way that would deliberately make them sustain wounds on their skin, all to make it possible to tell the difference between them.
【Kisara】 「Hmm, now that you mention it, I guess that might be it?」
【Naomasa】 「How do I even begin to say this……」

It was like the moment when it hit a man all over again that the utterly ignorant, naive little girl he was having a liaison with, who, after deflowering her in a bout of self-indulgence, he'd then proceeded to selfishly force his own desires upon, educating her in sex, had degenerated into a repulsive sex maniac; nay, Sakuya's astonishment grew far more profoundly intense than that, but.
【Shisamu】 「You don't have to say anything. It's just how things turned out, that's all it is.」
【Shisamu】 「We're really having a blast here, this has its own appeal.」

The twins were carefree to the bitter end. Come hell or high water, they were free spirits through and through. Even if it was a brightness akin to a needle swinging past the dial and breaking it, it was far better than secluding themselves in the shadows; that was what Sakuya had convinced himself of. He was a simple man at his core, so it was a relatively simple thing. Because it was true: he really did love the twins' radiant smiles.
【Kisara】 「Until now, we've been, you know, uhm, kind of letting it slide like relatively mature adults when people try to start shit with us.」
【Naomasa】 「……Reeeallyー……?」
【Shisamu】 「Yeah, it's true. I held it in at the time, most of the time. But I'm done doing that now.」
【Kisara】 「Because this world is a piece of shit even at the best of times. We have to live in that world every day, and they do say just bottling it up is bad for the body, right?」
【Shisamu】 「Chug it all down, start throwing some hands, that's good enough, don't have to think about anything.」
【Naomasa】 「Haven't you already been doing whatever the hell you wanted until now? Feels like you're saying some real grand stuff here, but. What's the truth?」
【Shisamu】 「He went and grabbed my ass, that's what.」
【Naomasa】 「Utterly unforgivable.」
Sakuya was furious. He reached his decision: that wicked, tyrannical drunkard most certainly had to be eradicated.
【Kisara】 「I had my ear licked.」
【Naomasa】 「Maybe I should have laced their drinks with a dash of tobacco broth.」
Sakuya seethed once again. "But then who the hell did I lick on the ear, thinking it was Kisara? It did reek an awful lot of pomade, but……", he thought.
【Shisamu】 「They really went and did that to someone injured, right?」
【Naomasa】 「Even if you're covered in wounds, you're still beautiful, and you've got great bodies. I guess it's only natural that someone would make a pass at you……」
【Kisara】 「Well, no matter how handsome a man approaches us. No matter what kind of rich men flock to us.」
【Kisara】 「As long as we've got Sakuya, that's all we need.」
Sakuya's face slowly turned red, and it could certainly not be entirely blamed on this inflamed morning sun.
【Shisamu】 「I mean, it was all thanks to you crying your eyes out that you kept us here, after all.」

A cheap price to pay: that was the only way it could be described. That's what Sakuya truly believed. Like he himself gave a shit about how pathetic he was, and if a tear or two were enough to seduce a woman, then he should have done it much earlier; that was the way he thought of it. However, as for whether he would have been able to cry like that for any other women, well now, let's just move on.

Well, at least this time their steps matched his.

fish for squid or octopus,

source.english:
Neither bothered saying it now, but whatever they did, they would certainly spend the rest of the night melting together, tangling and untangling until morning.
They were approaching a year together as lovers, yet neither twin showed the slightest sign of conceiving.
Perhaps, Sakuya thought vaguely,
that seed of cause and consequence would never bear fruit between him and these women.

source.japanese:
自分達の間に結ばれた縁の糸、三人一組ででぴったりと、他が収まる隙間はないのでないか。

source.english:
The threads of their bond fitted them exactly together as three. Perhaps there was no room for anyone else.
Such were his thoughts between their bodies, night after night, day after day.
That was fine. All he needed was these women. In this hopeless world, were they not far too good for a hopeless man like him?

source.english: The boat eventually drew alongside, carrying junior sailors sulking at being unnecessarily put to work so early in the morning. The ship they were returning to was the Albatross.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……Don't so much as think you're getting away for the rest of your life, got it?」
【Kisara】 「Should you start spouting some nonsense about being fed up, I don't give a damn. And if you're still gonna grumble on about it, well.」
【Kisara】 「Kisara is gonna rip it off.」
【Shisamu】 「Shisamu is gonna bite it off.」

As Sakuya cringed in fear, asking what part exactly, the twins grabbed one of his arms each and rose to their feet. The scene was just like back when the young man was being dragged aboard the Albatross for the very first time. Well, at the very least, this time, he was keeping pace with them as they walked.
【Kisara】 「You take that to heart, and once we're back home, let's go to bed together.」
【Shisamu】 「We'll sleep, wake up, and when the sun sets again. We'll head out once more. If there's a port nearby, we'll go drink at a bar.」
【Kisara】 「If we're out at sea, we'll put the boat out, and while we're fishing up some squid or octopuses, we'll make merry until it's bright outside again.」

The two of them, quite deliberately, did not put it into words anymore, but it was a given that whatever ended up happening, they would be entangled until dawn like they were melting in and out of one another's embrace. Though it already felt like ages since they first entered this sexual relationship, neither of the twins had ever showed any sign of conceiving whatsoever. Most likely─── Sakuya thought vacantly. The tree that was the relationship between himself and these women would never bear that sort of fruit.

Maybe it was just that the threads of fate tying them together made the perfect fit for the three of them, and so there just was no room for anything else? Night after night, day after day, pressed between their bodies, such thoughts ran through his mind. Well, that was still fine, he didn't need anything more than these women; in fact, were these women not much more than a hopeless man stuck in this hopeless world like himself deserved?
【Kisara】 「So what are you gonna do, Sakuya?」
All while fondling her own chest, soft and pliant.
【Shisamu】 「Maybe our fool of a man intends to seclude himself in his room, cowering?」
All while coquettishly pinching the hem of her skirt between her fingers, revealing little glimpses.
【Naomasa】 「Don't you underestimate me. ……Ah. I guess by this point, maybe there's really nothing left for you to underestimate about me.」

【Naomasa】 「Either way─── No need to do all that, for I've already decided. I'll follow you, wherever that leads, and I'll face whatever it is we meet together with you. That's what I decided back on that day.」
【Naomasa】 「If anything, you're the ones─── If you ever think of leaving me behind, then I'll cry again until you stay.」
【Naomasa】 「Ah, and also. If at all possible, and it only has to be once, I'd love to see a panty shot from you two, seriously.」
【Naomasa】 「It's sort of like, I haven't gotten a single glimpse so far, and it's just gnawing at me, I can't wrap my head around it.」
【Shisamu】 「A-ha-ha, iiidiot!」
【Kisara】 「Hu-hu-hu. You. Big. Dummy!」

Eventually, the rowboat came alongside, carrying a bunch of deck boys with frowns on their faces, clearly annoyed at being sent out on an undesirable errand this early in the morning. The ship they returned to: the Albatross.

意を決して、強引にシサム・キサラを連れ戻そうとて、朔屋は猛然と二人につかみかかった。男が、これだけの決意で女を連れて行こうとするのである。

source.english:
Steeling himself to drag Sisam and Kisara back by force, Sakuya flung himself ferociously upon the pair. Here was a man going to every length to carry away the women he loved.
Even if his strength failed him, surely his feelings would get through.

target.text: Determined, he attempted to forcibly drag Shisamu and Kisara back with him, and so Sakuya grasped ferociously at the two. It is with this unwavering resolve that a man seeks to bring a woman along with him. Even should his strength be wanting, his heart would surely reach them.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「行けないんだってば！」
source.english: “I told you we can't go!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I told you not to come!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ごめん朔屋、諦めて……！」
source.english: “Sorry, Sakuya. Give up…!”

source.japanese: なにがなんでも連れ戻す、との朔屋の力は愚か、心さえも。
source.english: Bring them back, no matter what. Yet not only Sakuya's strength but even his feelings—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Sorry Sakuya, give up……!」
Sakuya would bring them back no matter what it took, not just through strength, but even with his heart.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぎゃっ、ぶっ!!」
source.english: “Gyaah! Bff!”

source.japanese: 伝わるどころか、掴んだ手は乱暴に振り解かれ、ばかりか、勢いで流れた拳は、見事に朔屋の顎と横頬を直撃した。鼻血と口の中を切った血を撒き散らしながら、氷原を二転三転する朔屋。
source.english: Far from reaching them, his hands were violently shaken off. Worse, the twins' fists followed through with the motion and struck Sakuya squarely in jaw and cheek. Blood spraying from his nose and cut mouth, he rolled twice, three times across the ice.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「GYA, BHH!!」

Far from reaching them, not only were his grasping hands violently shaken free, the punches sent flying with force struck Sakuya squarely across the jaw and cheek. While scattering blood from his nose and cuts in his mouth all around him, Sakuya tumbled wildly around the ice field.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あら弱い。ちょっと朔屋、
　まさかそんなにあっさりと吹っ飛ぶなんて、
　思わなかったから」
source.english:
“Oh, you're weak.
Hey, Sakuya. Never thought you'd go flying
that easily…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Oh dear, how weak. Come on Sakuya, I never imagined you'd be blown away that easily, so I just.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「朔屋、朔屋、聞こえてる!?
　……でもこれでよかったのかも。
　これで朔屋もきっと諦め───」
source.english:
“Sakuya, Sakuya, can you hear me!?
…But maybe this is for the best.
Now he'll surely give—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Sakuya, Sakuya, can you hear me!? ……But maybe this is for the best. Even Sakuya has to give up now───」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「諦められっかぁーーーーっっ！」
source.english: “LIKE HELL I'LL GIVE UP!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Like hell I'd give upーーーー!」

source.japanese:
普段なら諦めてしまう朔屋も、今日だけは。
　またシサムとキサラの腕を掴もうとして。
source.english:
Ordinarily Sakuya might have given up. But not today.
He reached again for Sisam and Kisara's arms.

target.text: Ordinarily, even Sakuya would have given up, but today was the exception. He tried grabbing hold of Shisamu's and Kisara's arms again.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だから無理なの、もうあたしらは」
source.english: “I'm telling you, we can't. We've already—”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I'm telling you, it's not going to work, we already───」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「この人達と一緒に昇華するんだって、
　そう決めたから」
source.english:
“Decided to undergo sublimation
with these people.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「We're going to sublimate together with these people, that's what we decided.」

source.japanese: 二人が鮮やかに身を横にかわしたものだから、朔屋はたたらを踏み、よろめいた足下、双子の長靴に引っかかって、勢いのままに氷原に突っこんでしまう。顔面で滑って二米[メートル]ほど、首の辺りも厭[いや]な音を立てる。紅い筋も氷に伸びた。
source.english: The two slipped neatly aside. Sakuya staggered forward, tangled his feet in the twins' boots, and drove face-first into the ice with all his momentum. He slid nearly two meters on his face. His neck made an ugly sound as well. A red streak lengthened behind him across the ice.

target.text: The two of them dodged cleanly to the side, and so Sakuya stumbled a few steps too far; the twins' boots caught his staggering feet, and his momentum carried him as he plunged headlong onto the ice field. He slid around two meters on his face with an unpleasant noise coming from somewhere around his neck. A crimson streak also ran across the ice.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぎゃぼあああああっっ」
source.english: “GYABOAAAAH!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「GHWOAAAAH!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「さ、朔屋ッ!?　なんか珍妙な格好ですっころんでいる朔屋ぁ！　で、でもいい加減判ったよね？」
source.english: “S-Sakuya!? Sakuya! You took a really bizarre fall! B-but surely you understand by now?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「SA-, SAKUYA!? You're sprawled out in a kind of bizarre pose there, Sakuya! Bu-, but you have to finally get it now, right?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたしらの事は、もう構わないでさ……」
source.english: “Just leave us be…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「か、かみゃわずに、いられっふぁ……」
source.english: “C-can't… leab you be…”

source.japanese: 唇を切り、発音が変な擦過音に掠れて、それでも朔屋はまた立ち上がった。不屈だ、不屈である。よろよろと、蘇った亡者のように、双子の腰に縋りつこうとして、彼女達が反射的に繰り出してしまった膝頭に、したたかに、胸板と顎先を蹴り抜かれて描いた弧は半月の、朔屋はのけぞって後頭部まで打ちつけ、胸と顎と後頭部の痛みに氷原をもんどり打つ。
source.english: His lip split, his speech fraying into a strange, scraping rasp, and still Sakuya rose again. Indomitable. Indomitable indeed. He reeled toward the twins like one of the dead newly risen, reaching for their waists. Their knees flew up by reflex and drove hard into his chest and the point of his chin. Sakuya described a half-moon through the air, arched backward, smashed the back of his head, then writhed across the ice in a threefold agony of chest, chin and skull.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「You don't have to care about us anymore……」
【Naomasa】 「L-, like hell I'd shtop caring abwaah……」

Lip split, his pronunciation degraded into an odd fricative rasp, but even so, Sakuya rose to his feet once more. Unyielding, he was unyielding. Staggering like the risen dead, he attempted to cling to the twins' waists, but the girls lashed out with their knees reflexively, and with crushing force, they slammed into his chest and jaw; his body rose into the air, tracing an arc like a crescent moon, and he arched backwards and struck the back of his head, somersaulting across the ice field with pain blooming in his chest, his jaw, and the back of his head.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まずい、恐ろしいまでに正確なカウンターが入っちゃった」
source.english: “Oh shit. That counter landed with frightening accuracy.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「This is bad. I accidentally retaliated with a scarily precise counter.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あれ、下手すると再起不能かも……」
source.english: “That might've put him out of action for good…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Huh, if he's unlucky, he might be beyond recovery……」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おのれふぁ、これ、わふぁとふぁろ？
　もうおごっだ、本気でぇぇ」
source.english:
“You… did that… on purpoth, didn't you?
Now I'm… really angry…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「You bashtardsh, that wash on purposh, washn't it? Oh I'm pisshed now, I'm dead sherioussssh!」

source.japanese: 両手を翳[かざ]し、怪鳥のように、というより地上を不様に走るペンギンのようによちよちと向かってくる朔屋に、双子さすがにげんなりとなって、もう今度はリボルバーまで構える始末の、
source.english: Hands raised, he waddled toward them like a monstrous bird—or rather, like a penguin running clumsily over land. The twins, by now thoroughly fed up, went so far as to draw their revolvers.

target.text: With both hands raised, Sakuya ran at them like a monstrous bird, or rather, he tottered towards them like a penguin clumsily running on ground; even the twins were understandably exasperated by now, and this time, they actually drew their revolvers,

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「や、やめましょう、
　というかやめてあげてっ」
source.english:
“S-stop. Or rather,
please spare him!”

source.japanese: 双子を止めんとて、後から肩を掴んだのは彼女二人と三位を為す筈の、残り一要素の巡礼者だったのだが───
source.english: The pilgrim who seized their shoulders from behind to stop them was the third member meant to form a trinity with the twins. But—

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「Sto-, let us stop this. Actually, please stop for his sake!」
In an attempt to stop the twins, grabbing their shoulders from behind, was the pilgrim who had the final factor necessary for the two to become Triune, and yet───

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「うっせぇ！　朔屋がなあ、朔屋がなあ、あの駄目で屑で情けなくてだらしなくてちんぽだけ立派で頭が弱くて体力もなくて」
source.english: “Shut up! Sakuya—Sakuya, that useless, worthless, pathetic, slovenly man with nothing but a magnificent cock, no brains, no stamina—”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「SHADDUP! Sakuya, this guy Sakuya here, this useless piece of trash pathetic lazy loser with neither brains nor brawn who's only good for his dick!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「気が利かなくて女好きな癖に時々ヘタレで臆病者で騙されやすくて気が弱い朔屋がッ」
source.english: “Inconsiderate, woman-crazy, and yet sometimes a complete wimp—cowardly, gullible, weak-willed Sakuya—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Inconsiderate and tactless and for being a womanizer is sometimes a spineless wimp and a coward and gullible and timid, that Sakuya!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたしらに、こんなに真剣に───」
source.english: “He's so serious about—”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「He's being this earnest towards us and───」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……ゴロ撒いてきてるんだよぉ？
　これは徹底的に叩き潰してあげないとねえ。
　……邪魔するなっ」
source.english:
“…Picking a fight with us, you know?
We have to beat him completely into the ground.
…Don't interfere!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……He's throwing crap at us now, you know? We're gonna have to grind him into the dust, aren't we? ……Don't you get in my way!」

source.japanese: 後に繰り出した裏拳の、シサムとキサラの二人とも狙い過[あやま]たず巡礼者の顔面にめりこみ、鼻梁軟骨と右眼底骨を破壊した。あまりの苦痛に声も立てずに崩れ落ちた巡礼者に、双子達の追撃が入る。どかどかと踏み蹴りの、右と左で刻んだビートの景気よさだ。
source.english: Both twins flung a backfist behind them, neither missing: the blows buried themselves in the pilgrim’s face and shattered the cartilage of his nasal bridge and the floor of his right eye socket. He crumpled without a sound, the pain too great even for a cry; then came the twins’ follow-up, a great thudding fusillade of stamps and kicks, right and left beating out a positively jaunty rhythm.

target.text: The backhand blows that both Shisamu and Kisara launched right after did not err in their aim, sinking right into the pilgrim's face, destroying the cartilage of his nose and his right orbital floor bone. As the pilgrim collapsed from such overwhelming pain that it left him unable to even make a noise, the twins launched their follow-up strike. The pounding stomps and kicks hammered out an upbeat rhythm from both the right and the left.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ったくもう、朔屋ならこんな時にも情けねえ悲鳴を聞かせてくれんのに」
source.english: “God. Sakuya would give us a pathetic scream even now.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Good grief, if this was Sakuya, he'd at least let out some pathetic screams for us to enjoy.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あんたと来たら、なんだそれ、亀か？　ダンゴムシか？　ほらほら、ツノ出せヤリ出せチンコ出せ」
source.english: “What's this? A turtle? A pill bug? Come on, stick out your horns, your spear, your cock!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But when it comes to you, what are you supposed to be, a turtle? A pill bug? Come on, come on, show us your horn, bring out the spear, whip out your dick!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ほらほらどうしたの。あんた、あたしらと昇華するんでしょう？　そんなにヤワでどうするの」
source.english: “Come on, what's wrong? You're going to undergo sublimation with us, aren't you? How can you be so soft?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Come on, come on, what's wrong? You're going to sublimate with us, right? And how are you gonna do that while being this soft?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「朔屋みたいに、
　もっと仰々しく騒いでみてよ」
source.english:
“Make as huge a fuss
as Sakuya would.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Try being like Sakuya, make a more dramatic spectacle out of it.」

source.japanese: 一人の巡礼者、叩きのめされる巡礼者を中心に、氷原に花が咲く。赤い花紅い花、朱い花。人一人から飛び散る血の色の中々に多彩なのであった。
source.english: A flower bloomed upon the ice, centered on the lone pilgrim under the twins' assault. Red petals, crimson petals, scarlet petals. The blood scattered from one human body proved remarkably rich in shades.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「や、やめふぇあげふぇっ」
source.english: “S-stop… Pleathe…”

target.text: Centered on a single pilgrim, a pilgrim who was beaten into the ground, a flower bloomed on the ice field. A red flower, a crimson flower, a vermillion flower. The colour of the blood splattered from a single man is surprisingly varied in its hues.
【Naomasa】 「Sht-, shtop, let him go!」

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「わ、わかりました、もう結構ですからっ」
source.english: “W-we understand! That's quite enough!”

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「U-, understood, that is more than enough now, so please!」

source.japanese:
【巡礼者】
「あなた達の決意の固いこと、しかと確認させていただきましたからっ」
source.english: “We've thoroughly confirmed how firm your resolve is!”

source.japanese: と泡を食って双子を抑えにかかった朔屋と巡礼者達の一〇人がかりで止めるのがやっと、その時は双子の一要素であった者は、ひくりひくりと哀れに痙攣するのみ。
source.english: Sakuya and the pilgrims rushed in panic to restrain the twins. Even ten people together barely managed it. By then, the pilgrim intended to complete the twins' triad could do no more than twitch pitiably.

target.text: 【Pilgrim】 「We have confirmed the firmness of your resolve with the utmost certainty, so please!」

In a panic, Sakuya and ten pilgrims rushed to restrain the twins together, but even with all of them, it was a struggle, and at that moment, the man who had been the factor of the twins could only pitifully twitch and convulse.

source.japanese:
そして朔屋は。
　それまでは彼を排斥するに力で訴えるも止む無しとしていた巡礼者は、ころりと態度を変えて、願うは丁重なお引き取りの、雪原を渡る為の装備と食糧まで献上される有り様の、彼に迂闊な手を出したらと、巡礼者達はみな一様に戦慄していたという。
source.english:
And Sakuya—
the pilgrims who had previously considered force justified in expelling him now reversed themselves completely. They begged him with exquisite courtesy to depart and even presented him with food and equipment for crossing the snowfield. Every one of them shuddered at the thought of laying a careless hand upon him.

target.text: Thus, Sakuya. The pilgrims, who had not held any scruples in even resorting to force to reject Sakuya, changed their tune entirely; all they desired was for him to politely leave, going so far as to even offer him gear and provisions to ensure he could cross the snowy plains, and it was said that, should any one of them happen to carelessly brush even a finger against him, all the pilgrims would shudder in unison.

source.japanese:
そしてシサムとキサラの双子は。
　ややあって、我に返った時には、それまでの暴力衝動はすっぱり消費し尽くされ、とてもとても清冽な顔になっていたけれど。
　巡礼者達は、彼女達に対して、卑屈とか腫[は]れ物に触るようなとか、そんな態度に終始して。双子に叩きのめされた仲間を担架に担ぎ上げ、告げた言葉というのが、
source.english:
And the twins, Sisam and Kisara—
when they came to themselves a little later, their violent impulses were utterly spent and their faces looked very, very serene.
The pilgrims, meanwhile, remained servile and wary of them, as though any touch might provoke another explosion. Hoisting their battered companion onto a stretcher, they said—

source.japanese:
『彼が回復するまで、貴女方の昇華は順延されました。もちろんこれはあくまで延期であり、我々もすぐさま戻ります次第です』
『それまでお二人は、この極点にて御待機下さい、その為の設備と装備と食糧は残していきますし、我々も定期的にここに報告に参ります』
source.english:
‘Your sublimation has been postponed until he recovers. Naturally this is only a postponement; we shall return as soon as he has recovered.’
‘Until then, please remain here at the pole. We will leave facilities, equipment and food for that purpose, and we shall return regularly with reports.’

target.text: Thus, the twins, Shisamu and Kisara. A little while later, when they came to their senses, all the violent impulses they'd displayed hitherto were entirely exhausted, their faces the very picture of serene calm, but. The pilgrims treated the girls with constant deference, like they were walking on eggshells around a ticking time bomb the whole time. After lifting their comrade who had been beaten and bruised by the twins up on a stretcher, the words they spoke were:

『Your sublimation has been postponed until he recovers. Of course, this is but a postponement, and it is our intent to return here posthaste.』 『Until that time comes, you two are kindly requested to wait here at this pole. We have left behind facilities, equipment, and provisions to ensure that your stay is possible, and we shall also pay our visits to deliver periodic reports.』

source.japanese: であり、朔屋と自分達の魂の片割れを暴虐の嵐ですり潰して一時的な虚脱状態に陥った二人はぽかんぽかんと虚けた首肯を返すのみ。
source.english: Having ground Sakuya and the other half of their souls to pulp in a tempest of savagery, the two had fallen into a temporary daze of exhaustion and could only give vacant little nods.

target.text: So it went, and having fallen into a temporary state of mental numbness after pulverizing both Sakuya and a fragment of their own soul in a storm of appalling violence, the two could only vacantly nod their assent in return.

source.japanese: そして朔屋は、航海士の双子と極点にて別れたのであった。
source.english: Thus Sakuya parted from the twin navigators at the pole.

target.text: Thus, Sakuya parted ways with the twin mates on the pole.

source.japanese:
朔屋は、まあいつもの通りだ。信天翁号で。
　ただし双子がいない毎日。
　その事だけはどうやっても埋めようのない空虚となって、胸の中に広がっていた。
source.english:
Sakuya went on much as usual aboard the Albatross.
Except that every day passed without the twins.
That absence alone spread through his chest, an emptiness nothing could fill.

target.text: As for Sakuya, well, it was the usual. On the Albatross. Except it was an everyday without the twins. And that alone became a void he couldn't fill no matter how he tried, spreading its tendrils within his chest.

source.japanese: そして双子は、まだあの極点にいた。氷原中に、防寒だけはしっかり施した、退屈な住居を設営して。時折巡礼者達は訪れてくるものの、双子に対してはどこかよそよそしい。
source.english: The twins remained at the pole. They had set up a dreary dwelling upon the ice, at least thoroughly insulated against the cold. Pilgrims visited from time to time but always kept an awkward distance from them.

target.text: Thus, the twins yet remained on the pole to this day. In the heart of the ice field, they set up a dreary dwelling that was, if nothing else, thoroughly insulated against the cold. The pilgrims would periodically make a visit, but they were somewhat distant and reserved when dealing with the twins.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ねえシサム、ウチらなんかこれ……都合よくここに飼い殺しにされてない？」
source.english: “Hey, Sisam. Aren't we… being kept here, conveniently alive and out of the way?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Hey, Shisamu, aren't we kind of…… being kept here to just rot away at their convenience?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「言わないでキサラ。あたしもそんな気がしてならないんだけど、朔屋にああまで言って追い返しちゃったんだもの……」
source.english: “Don't say it, Kisara. I can't stop feeling that too. But we said all that to Sakuya and sent him away…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Don't say that, Kisara. I can't help but feel the same way, but we ended up saying all that stuff to Sakuya and drove him away, so……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……もう、引けないよねえ」
source.english: “…Can't back down now, can we?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……There's no more going back for us, is there?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……なんでこうなったかなあ……」
source.english: “…How did it end up like this…?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……I wonder why things turned out this way……」

source.japanese:
───一方その頃、密航者。
　何故か彼女もまた、この氷原中に在り、巡礼者達の会合点からやや離れた地点にある、雪丘の中腹に空いた洞穴に入りこんでいた。
　洞窟の奥の、一枚の巨大な氷板を見上げれば、氷中に埋まっている、一本の木柱がある。
source.english:
Meanwhile, the stowaway.
For some reason she too was upon the ice field, inside a cave in the flank of a snowy hill some distance from the pilgrims' meeting place.
Deep in the cave she looked up at a vast slab of ice. Embedded within it stood a single wooden pillar.

target.text: Elsewhere, around that time, the stowaway. For some reason, this girl was also still in the middle of this ice field, at a spot somewhat removed from the gathering point of the pilgrims, stepping into a cave opening halfway up a snowy hill. In the depths of the cave, as she looked up at a gigantic slab of ice, buried within it was a single wooden mast.

source.japanese: 彼女が木柱に手を差し延べると、氷から抜け出しながらそのサイズを縮めながら密航者の手の中に収まる。密航者は鉛筆大になった柱を、腰の革鞄の中にしまいこむ。
source.english: When she reached out to the wooden pillar, it pulled free of the ice and shrank as it came, until it nestled in the stowaway’s hand. She slipped the pillar, now no larger than a pencil, into the leather satchel at her waist.

target.text: As she reached out for the wooden mast with her hand, it shrunk in size as it broke free from the ice until it fit neatly within the stowaway's hand. The stowaway stuffed the mast, now the size of a pencil, into the leather bag around her waist.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「とうとう、取り返した、メインの」
source.english: “At last. I got it back. The main one.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I have finally recovered the main.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「さてこれからの……話だけど」
source.english: “Now, as for what happens next…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So……about what to do from here on.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まあしばらくは、また『密航』だ」
source.english: “Well, back to ‘stowing away’ for a while.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Well, for the time being, it's back to『stowing away』」

source.english: —A New Chapter—

target.text: ───Interlude───

source.japanese: 罐の火の一部が零れ落ちたかに一対の赤い光は床に溜まった影の中で灯る。しばし連星のように留まっていたが、ふっと消え失せた、としか思えないほどの速き起こりで、闇中を走ったのである。光の緒も引かない程の瞬速の、動きも小さな跫音も人間の感覚では追い切れない域にあったが、生き物を追う生き物として有史以前から完成された存在が船にはある。
source.english: A pair of red lights burned in the shadows pooled on the floor, as if a little of the furnace fire had spilled there. For a while they remained like binary stars, then moved so abruptly that they seemed simply to go out. They were racing through the dark. Too swift even to trail a thread of light, their movements and tiny footfalls exceeded human senses. But aboard this ship lived another creature, perfected since before recorded history for the pursuit of living prey.

source.japanese: 物陰から新たな影が生じて、しかしこちらは質量血肉を備えた影の、その身のこなしのしなやかな事流体の如く、疾き事弾丸の如く、先に消えた一対の光を追って影から出でて影にと沈む。一瞬、罐から漏れる明かりを弾いて、一対の光が爛[らん]と輝く。刹那の光輝───
source.english: A new shadow emerged from concealment. This one possessed mass, flesh, and blood. Fluid in its supple movements, swift as a bullet, it pursued the vanished pair of lights, emerging from shadow and sinking into shadow again. For an instant, another pair flared, reflecting the light escaping from the furnace. A moment's brilliance—

target.text: As if a part of the furnace fire had spilled over, a pair of red lights lit up the shadows that pooled on the floor. For a time, they held still like binary stars, and then they vanished: they ran through the dark so quickly that it could only seem that way, at least. With such blindingly quick speed that they did not even leave behind a trail of light, both their movements and tiny footsteps were now in the realm where human senses could no longer follow them, but there was an existence aboard this ship that had perfected the art of hunting its fellow life since prehistoric times.

A new shadow was born from the shade, however, this was a shadow endowed with mass, with flesh and blood; its carriage elegant as flowing liquid, speed like that of a bullet, it chased after the just-vanished twin lights, emerging from the shadow before sinking into it once more. For an instant, the light leaking from the furnace flared up, twin lights glittering brilliantly. A split second of radiance───

source.japanese: 影の溜まりの中ではどのような攻防が繰り広げられているのか定かではなかったけれど、長くは続かず、暗がりの奥で、「ヂッ！」と短く詰まった、生き物の断末魔が悲痛で、同時に生命が生命を奪う事の原初的な悦びを、耳にした者に思い出させた。
source.english: What attack and defense took place in those pools of darkness was uncertain, but it did not last long. From their depths came a short, strangled squeak. A creature's agonized death cry, which at the same time reminded anyone who heard it of the primal joy of one life taking another.

target.text: It was unclear what manner of offence and defence was unfolding within the pooling shadows, but it did not last long, and in the depths of the dark, there sounded a clipped, gasping chirp, what invoked for all who heard it the heartbreaking death throes of a living creature, and at the same time, the primeval joy of one life stealing the life of another.

source.japanese: やがて影からぬう、と出でても影がそのまま凝[こご]ったかに黒い、所々真夜中の流星のように白い毛筋を混ぜた毛並みの、信天翁号の番猫宗右衛門が、その逞[たくま]しき顎[あぎと]に丸々太って大なる鼠をぶら下げて。
source.english: Presently the Albatross's watch-cat Soemon emerged, still black as congealed shadow, a few white hairs streaking his coat like meteors in a midnight sky. From his powerful jaws hung an enormous, fat rat.

target.text: At long last, it smoothly emerged from the shadows, though it was black as if the shadows themselves had congealed, a coat of fur streaked in places with fine lines of white like comets soaring across the midnight sky: it was the watchcat of the Albatross, Souemon, with a great mouse so fat it was completely round dangling from his muscular jaws.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……お疲れ様、宗右衛門殿。
　申し訳ないのですが、食事は奥の方でお願いします」
source.english:
“…Well done, Mr. Soemon.
My apologies, but would you please take your meal farther back?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……Excellent work, Lord Souemon. My sincerest apologies, but I must request that you partake in your meal in the back.」

source.japanese: 機関長でさえ口調に敬意を表すこの黒猫は、ただ船の害獣をしかと仕留めた事を告げたかっただけと見え、大人しく影の中に戻って、貪り喰らう様こそ見せなかったものの、肉を割き骨を噛み砕く音が機関室の重低音の中で異様なまでに生々しかった。朔屋はこの咀嚼音に機関長振る舞いのウイスキイ垂らした紅茶に血の味さえ混じるような悪心地に見舞われたが、宗右衛門が相手では抗議も申し立てられない。彼以外の、機関室の卓に着いた男達には猫の食事の音など屁とも感じぬ豪毅の者ばかりで、水夫長はむしろ賞賛の頷[うなず]きを何度か繰り返してから、
source.english: Even the chief engineer addressed the black cat with respect. Apparently Soemon had only wanted to announce his successful disposal of a shipboard pest. He returned obediently to the shadows. They were spared the sight of him devouring it, but the tearing flesh and crunching bones sounded unnaturally vivid amid the engine room's deep rumble. Sakuya felt sick, as if the tea the engineer had served him, laced with whiskey, had acquired a taste of blood. But one could hardly lodge a complaint against Soemon. The other men at the engine-room table were a hardy lot who thought nothing of a cat's meal. The boatswain, in fact, nodded several times in approval before speaking.

target.text: This black cat, whom even the Chief Engineer spoke to with the utmost respect, appeared to just have wanted to report that he had dealt the killing blow to one of the pests aboard the ship without leaving room for doubt, for he quietly returned to the shadows once more, and though he did not show any outward signs of devouring his kill, the sounds of parting flesh and crushing bone were abnormally vivid even in the deep thrumming of the engine room. This sound of mastication left Sakuya with an uncomfortable feeling in his chest, like the black tea with whisky he had been treated to by the Chief Engineer was even beginning to taste a little of blood, but when it came to Souemon, he had no room to raise any objections.

Sakuya aside, all the men seated at this table in the engine room were of a hardy breed, men who cared less for the sound of a cat's meal than they would a fart in the wind; in fact, the Bosun nodded repeatedly in approval, and then,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「じゃあ、クソ鬱陶しいネズ公を宗右衛門が片づけてくれたところで、さっきの話の続きといこう」
source.english: “Now that Soemon's dealt with that damned nuisance of a rat, let's get back to what we were discussing.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Alright, now that Souemon has dealt with that obnoxious little shit of a mister mousey, let's get back to the talking.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ええと、どこまで話したっけか、王よ？」
source.english: “Where had we got to, Wang?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Uhm, where were we again, Wang?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「いや、私達はそもそも何故こんな会合を開いているのでしたか？」
source.english: “Well, why were we holding this meeting in the first place?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「No, why were we even holding this assembly here to begin with?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……。いや、すまん。
　あんたに聞いて悪かった。
　おい朔屋、なんだったか？」
source.english:
“…Sorry. My mistake, asking you.
Sakuya, what was it?”

source.japanese:
近々の事を記憶していられないという機関長の持病は水夫長も知るところであったし、折り合いは悪いとはいえ水夫の長と機関室の長、お互いを立てるところは心得ていて、軽く詫びてから朔屋に続きを促した。
　これでいつもの朔屋なら、他の男がする真面目な話なぞ聞き流していてまた水夫長の鉄拳を喰らうところであったが、この時に限っては話の再開を待ち侘びだったので、遅滞なく答えられた。
source.english:
The boatswain knew of the engineer's chronic inability to remember recent events. They might not get along, but the head of the sailors and the head of the engine room understood when to show each other respect. He apologized briefly, then prompted Sakuya.
Ordinarily Sakuya would have let other men's serious conversation flow past him, earning another blow from the boatswain's fist. This time, however, he had been eager for them to resume. He answered without delay.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺らがなんで集まってるのかは、正直俺もよく判りませんがね、話してたのはほらあの、ウミヒトの事だった」
source.english: “Honestly, I don't really know why we're all here either. But we were talking about that thing, you know. One of the Sea People.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……. No, my bad. Shouldn't have asked you. Oi, Sakuya, where were we again?」

It seemed like the Bosun was also aware of the Chief Engineer's chronic disease that left him unable to remember recent events, and for all that they got along like oil and water, the chief of the sailors and the chief of the engine room each had an understanding of where the other stood, so while offering a minor apology, he instead urged Sakuya to continue. Were this the usual Sakuya, he would once again suffer the iron fist of the Bosun for never paying attention to anything serious when spoken by another man, but this time alone, he was the one impatiently waiting for their conversation to continue, and he answered with no delay.
【Naomasa】 「Honestly, the reason why we're gathered here is not really something I understand myself, but we were talking about, you know, that Umihito thing.」

source.japanese:
───ウミヒト───
　
　深淵から浮上し来[きた]る、巨大な白いヒトガタ。嵐と追っ手から逃れ仰せたものの、今度は官憲に進路を阻まれた信天翁号の前に現れたる異形の存在。
　こうして朔屋達が機関室に集って話をしていられるという事は、官憲の巡視艦から逃れられたという事実を物語っており、あの異常事態からいかな流れを辿って今に至るのか、実に興味深く───
source.english:
The Sea People.
An enormous white human shape rising from the abyss. Having escaped the storm and their pursuers, the Albatross had found her course blocked by the authorities when this strange being appeared before her.
Sakuya and the others were now sitting in the engine room, so plainly they had escaped the patrol vessel. But how had that extraordinary situation led to this one? A most fascinating question—

target.text: ───Umihito─── Surfacing from the deepest abyss, a giant, white humanoid. Though they had just managed to make good their escape from their pursuers and the storm, their course forwards was now blocked by the authorities; it was then that it had suddenly emerged before the Albatross, a grotesque existence.

And so the fact that Sakuya and the rest were gathered here in the engine room and speaking thus was a testament to the fact that they had also managed to escape from the patrol boat helmed by the authorities, but just what course of events had brought them from that absurd situation to the present? In truth, it was an incredibly fascinating───

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう、そうだったそうだった。
　マアしかしあんなこたァどうでもいいんだ。
　それより下級水夫達が最近バラックで作ってるあれの事だが」
source.english:
“Right, right. That was it.
Well, none of that matters. What's more important is what the junior sailors have been making in their shack lately.”

source.japanese: 実に興味深く、深く───思っていたのは朔屋だけだったようで、水夫長には釣った魚がミノカサゴ、見た目は派手だが毒がある、喰って喰えない事はないが面倒くさいと実にあっさり投げ出して、さっさと次の話に入る、ウミヒトへの興味はまるで無し。
source.english: Most fascinating—fascinating—but apparently only to Sakuya. To the boatswain, it was like catching a lionfish. Showy, but venomous. You could eat it, perhaps, but too much trouble. He tossed it aside with perfect ease and went straight on to the next topic, utterly uninterested in the Sea People.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right, that's it, that's it. But come on, what does that thing even matter? More importantly, about that stuff the deck boys recently made in one of the shacks.」

It truly was fascinating, very much so ───and the only one who seemed to think so here was Sakuya, for to the Bosun, it was like the fish he'd caught had turned out to be a luna lionfish, and while it looked real flashy, it was also venomous, and so finding it too bothersome to weigh if he should eat it or not, he instead just nonchalantly tossed it back in the ocean, promptly moving on the next topic: he held basically no interest in the Umihito.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「あいつら、バラックの中に土盛って、野菜なんぞを育てているようだが……。
　うまくいくと思うか？」
source.english:
“They've piled up soil in the shack and seem to be growing vegetables…
Think they'll make it work?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Those guys have made a pile of dirt inside a shack, and it looks like they're growing vegetables or something in there, but……. You think it's gonna work out?」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「支那では、古代より船の道中、大豆を育ててモヤシにしていたという例もある。お陰で壊血病の害も抑えられたという。その辺りは西洋の船乗りより知恵深かったというところでしょう」
source.english: “There are accounts of soybeans being grown into sprouts aboard ships in China since ancient times. This is said to have reduced the harm done by scurvy. In that respect, they were wiser than Western sailors.”

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「だから、例がない事ではない。
　ただし、水夫君達が成功させられるかどうかはまた別だね」
source.english:
“So it is not without precedent.
Whether our sailors can succeed is another question.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「In China, there are examples from the ancient past of men growing soybeans on ships and eating the beansprouts as they sailed. As a result, they were able to limit the harmful effects of scurvy. It is said that, in this respect, they actually held a greater wealth of knowledge than Western sailors at the time.」 (TN: The Chief Engineer uses the old Japanese term for China here, "Shina", written "支那". After World War II, the Chinese claimed it was discriminatory, used derogatorily in the Sino-Japanese Wars, and so it is generally avoided now, replaced with "Chuukoku", written "中国", the same kanji as in Chinese.)
【Chief Engineer】 「As such, it is not unprecedented. However, whether the sailors will find success in their endeavours or not is a different story altogether.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だよなあ。しかもあいつらが植えてんのはモヤシなんぞよりむつかしい。トマトやニガウリあたりだ」
source.english: “Exactly. And what they've planted is harder to grow than sprouts. Tomatoes and bitter melons.”

source.japanese:
下級水夫達は細心の注意を払って育成に励んでいるようだが、なにしろ陸とは勝手が違う海の上、屋内とはいえバラックの造りはいい加減で、潮風が入れば時には大波に激しく揺すられる、先ほど宗右衛門が仕留めたとはいえ、鼠は後を絶たず、奴らは苗も囓る。なにより水夫君達は水夫であって農夫ではない。
　見込みはあまり高くはなかろうというのが座のおおよその意見だった。
source.english:
The junior sailors seemed to be tending their plants with the greatest care. But life at sea was not life on land. Indoors or not, the shack was poorly built. Salt wind found its way in; heavy waves sometimes shook it violently. Soemon had just dispatched a rat, but there were always more, and they gnawed seedlings too. Above all, these sailors were sailors, not farmers.
The general opinion around the table was that their chances were not particularly good.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right you are. Moreover, they've planted something a lot more complicated than some beansprouts. Stuff like tomatoes, bitter melons.」

The sailors seemed to have paid close attention to the finer details, making great efforts to nurture the plants, but they were out on the ocean, a place very different from land, and even if it was inside a building, the construction of the shacks was quite perfunctory; when the salty sea breeze came blowing, they would at times be made to violently shake and jolt by the surging waves, and even if Souemon had just put one down, there was also no end to the mice, and they would nibble on the saplings.
