And most pressing of all, the sailors were sailors, not farmers. It didn't seem like they should expect too much from it: that was the general opinion of those gathered here.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まあ、うまくいったらめっけもの、ってところだろ。飯にも幅が増える」
source.english: “Well, if it works, that'll be a bonus. Give us more variety at meals.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well, if things go well, it'll be a nice bonus, something like that. It'll add some variety to our meals.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「て訳で朔屋、手伝ってやれとは言わんが、邪魔したり生りかけの実をかっぱらったりするんじゃねえぞ。水夫共の機嫌を損ねるといろいろ面倒だからな」
source.english: “So, Sakuya. I'm not telling you to help, but don't get in their way or steal the fruit before it's ripe. Get on their bad side and you'll have no end of trouble.”

source.japanese: がっちり釘を刺されて朔屋、自分が信用されていない事はもちろん面白くなかったけれど、それよりウミヒトの話題が流されてしまったのが納得いかない。
source.english: A firm warning. Naturally, Sakuya disliked being so distrusted, but what bothered him more was having the subject of the Sea People brushed aside.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しませんてそんな事ぁ。
　てか、ウミヒトの方が気になるよ俺は。
　ありゃ一体なんだったのか───」
source.english:
“I wouldn't do anything like that. Anyway,
I'm more interested in that sea creature.
What the hell was it—?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So with that said, Sakuya, while I won't tell you to help them out, don't get in their way or pilfer whatever fruits they manage to grow. It's always a heap of trouble when the sailors get in a bad mood.」

Given an astute warning, it wasn't that Sakuya found it amusing to not be trusted in the slightest, of course, but the thing he was most displeased with was that the topic of the Umihito had been completely glossed over.
【Naomasa】 「I wouldn't do something like that. But hey, I'm more concerned about the Umihito. What in the world was that thing───」

source.japanese: あの時浮上したウミヒトは───
source.english: The being that had risen from the sea that day—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺達だけ行かせたけれど、巡視船だけ通せんぼして───」
source.english: “It let us through, but blocked the patrol vessel—”

source.japanese: まるで、信天翁号を助けるように───
source.english: As though it were helping the Albatross—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「この船が得体の知れないなぁもともとだが、
あんな化け物とも縁があるとはさすがにびっくりだ。どういう事なんですよ、水夫長」
source.english:
“This ship's always been mysterious,
but I never expected her to have ties to a monster like that. What was all that about, Boatswain?”

source.japanese: ───水夫達の菜園だ何だより、よほどそちらの方が重大事ではないかと食い下がるも水夫長ははんと鼻を鳴らして取りあわず、
source.english: Surely that was far more important than the sailors' vegetable garden? He persisted, but the boatswain merely snorted and refused to engage.

target.text: The Umihito that surfaced back then was───
【Naomasa】 「It only allowed us to leave, and it only denied the patrol boat passage───」
Almost as though it was…… coming to the Albatross' aid───
【Naomasa】 「I already knew this ship was one big enigma, but I'm certainly shocked to find she shares some kind of connection with a monster like that. What is all that about, Bosun?」
───But though he kept pressing that this was a matter far more important than the sailors' vegetable garden or whatever, the Bosun simply snorted with a "hmpf", not concerning himself with it at all,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「俺だってあれがなんなのかは知らねえし、
　べつにどうでもいいじゃねえか、
　だいたい二週間も前のコトだろうが」
source.english:
“I don't know what it was either.
And who cares?
It was two weeks ago, anyway.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「It's not like I know what that thing is either, and does it really even matter? It's already been two weeks since it happened.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おい殺し屋、
　てめえはなんぞ意見はあるか？」
source.english:
“Hey, assassin.
Got anything to say?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Oi, murderer, you have any opinion on this?」

source.japanese: 何故か彼までこの場に呼ばれていた、智里は、先程から懐手に腕組みで、黙然と卓に顔をうつむけ考えこんでいる様子、と見えたが、かくりと頭がのめった、船を漕いでいる。呼びかけに目を覚まして大欠伸、悪びれるところがない、実に悠然としたものである。
source.english: For some reason, Tomosato had been invited too. All this time he had sat with his arms folded inside his clothes, his head bowed toward the table, silently considering—or so it seemed, until his head dipped. He was nodding off. The question woke him, and he gave a great yawn without the slightest embarrassment. Perfectly at ease.

target.text: One could wonder why he'd even been called to this place, for Tomosato had been crossing his arms inside his kimono for some time now, looking down at the table in silence as if deep in thought, or so it seemed, but his head lurched forward: he was nodding off. He awoke as he was called upon with a great yawn, not a hint of shame to be seen; in fact, he was entirely composed.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……おお。この部屋ぁ陽気がよくって眠っちまったい。で、なんだって？」
source.english: “…Oh. Nice and warm in here. Fell asleep. What was that?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ウミヒトの事だよ。あんた、あれ見てなんか言ってたじゃないか。なんぞ心当たりとかは……」
source.english: “The Sea People. You said something when you saw that thing. Any idea what it was…?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Ooh. The climate down in this room makes me real sleepy. So, you were saying?」
【Naomasa】 「We're talking about the Umihito. Hey, didn't you say something when you saw it? Like you had some kind of idea about what it……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「『小学館入門百科シリーズ三二：妖怪なんでも入門』一四六ページ参照、だ」
source.english: “See page 146 of Everything You Need to Know About Monsters, volume thirty-two of Shogakukan's Beginner's Encyclopedia series.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はあ？」
source.english: “Huh?”

source.japanese: すらすらと諳んじた時、蒼い眸[ひとみ]が凛とした光を流して、機関室の赤い薄明かりの中で怜悧とあったが、台詞がなんとも手前勝手に垂れ流し、後は説明もない。本読みの水夫長や博学多識の機関長にも心当たりのない出版社と書名で、朔屋のみならず二人にも首を傾げさせる。この男の物言いと来たら何時でも此[こ]れ式[しき]の、彼自身にしか意味が判らない事ばかり。
source.english: As he rattled off the reference from memory, his blue eyes shone with a clear, keen light in the engine room's red gloom. Yet he had merely dropped the words before them for his own satisfaction and offered no explanation. Neither the bookish boatswain nor the immensely learned engineer had heard of the publisher or title. They cocked their heads along with Sakuya. This was how the man always spoke: in references meaningful to no one but himself.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Consult page 146 of 『The Shougakukan Encyclopediac Primer Series 32: Yokai for Dummies』」 (TN: Shougakukan is a real publisher of encyclopedias, among much else, in Japan. The "妖怪なんでも入門" is a real book, lit. "Introduction to all things yokai", published in 1974, written and illustrated by Mizuki Shigeru, who was a leading figure on the topic of yokai. He is also known, among many other things, for creating the manga "GeGeGe no Kitarou".)
【Naomasa】 「Haah?」

As he smoothly recited that from memory, a piercing, dignified light flowed from those azure eyes, a sagacious gleam within the dim red light of the engine room, but the line itself was a stream of awfully self-serving drivel with no explanation following it. Upon hearing a book title from a publishing company that neither the bibliophilic Bosun nor the extensively erudite Chief Engineer knew of, it was not just Sakuya who was left tilting his head quizzically, but the other two as well. The man's diction was ever thus: riddled with cryptic turns of phrase that only he himself could hope to fathom.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ともかく、海坊主かなんかの類だろ。
　俺が聞いたモノとはちと様子が違うようだが、まあ世界は広い。何があったっておかしかねえやな」
source.english:
“Anyway, some sort of sea monk, I suppose.
A little different from what I've heard of, but it's a big world. Nothing would surprise me.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Anyway, it's probably like some kind of Umibouzu. It's a bit different from the ones I've heard of, but the world's a big place. Anything can happen, really.」 (TN: An Umibouzu, written "海坊主", is a Japanese yokai. It takes the form of a giant, black, humanoid being, often encountered by ships at night, where a calm sea suddenly surges, only for a bald head to surface and destroy or damage the ship.)

source.japanese:
【智里】
「だいたい餅は餅屋で、海の事なら船乗りのあんた達だろうが」
source.english: “Every trade has its masters. When it comes to the sea, you sailors are the experts.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「To begin with, every man knows his business best, so matters of the sea are best left to sailors like you, right?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「抜かせよ、てめえだって殺し屋てぇ言いながら、標的のこれと仲良く酒呑んでんじゃねえか。殺るンならさっさと殺りやがれよ、俺はとめねえから」
source.english: “Spare me. You call yourself an assassin, but here you are having a friendly drink with your target. If you're going to kill him, get on with it. I won't stop you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ろくでもない事思い出させないでくれよ水夫長。ていうか、あんたも水夫の長なら止めてくれよな……」
source.english: “…Don't remind him of rotten ideas like that, Boatswain. And if you're the head of the sailors, you ought to stop him…”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「うるせえ、かえって良い厄介払いになるくれえだ。とにかく、こいつも知らねえようだし、ウミヒトの事はこれきりだ」
source.english: “Shut up. Be a good way to get rid of a nuisance. Anyway, he doesn't know either. That's the end of the Sea People.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Cut the crap. You keep calling yourself a murderer, but there you are, knocking 'em back like old chums with your mark. If you're gonna kill him, then get it over with already, I ain't stopping you.」
【Naomasa】 「……Please don't make me remember things best left forgotten, Bosun. Actually, you're the boss of us sailors, so you should stop him……」
【Bosun】 「Shaddup. If anything, he'd be ridding me of a lot of trouble. Anyway, he doesn't seem to know anything either, so that's it for the Umihito.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それで、次の話だが───」
source.english: “Now, next item—”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So then, onto the next topic───」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ところで、私達はそもそも何故こんな会合を開いているのでしたか？」
source.english: “By the way, why were we holding this meeting in the first place?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Incidentally, why are we even holding this assembly here to begin with?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……朔屋。説明してやれ」
source.english: “…Sakuya. Explain it to him.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺だってよくわかんないってば。
　なんで呼ばれたの、俺も智里も」
source.english:
“I told you, I don't know either.
Why did you call me and Tomosato here?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……言ってなかったか？　まあたまには、女子供ぬきでな、船のあれこれの事を確認しておきてえわけだ」
source.english: “…Didn't I say? Well, every now and then I want to go over the ship's affairs without the women or junior hands around.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それでこんな、色気もへったくれもない、むさ苦しい男所帯の寄り合いか……」
source.english: “So that's why it's a gathering of grubby men without a trace of charm…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Sakuya. Explain it to him.」
【Naomasa】 「I told you, it's not like I know that either. Why did you even call for us, Tomosato and me?」
【Bosun】 「……I never told you? Well, every now and then, I like to check in on what's happening around the ship. Without the women and kids around.」
【Naomasa】 「So that's why we're holding this sordid sausage fest with not a hint of sexiness to be found……?」

source.japanese:
朔屋としては、こんな薄暗い機関室で男だらけが額突き合わせてもそもそやっているくらいなら、シサムやキサラ、泪あたりも呼んだ方が見た目的に心が和らぐのにとつい不満を、口の端に上せた途端に水夫長の兇悪な一睨[にら]み。
　男尊女卑云々を賢しく言い出す以前の問題として、水夫長の単純な気分の問題なのだろう。それに付き合わされる朔屋としては色々言いたいところもないでもないが、ここで水夫長の機嫌損ねては後々厄介な事になろうと、卑屈に笑って口を噤んだ。
source.english:
If they were going to huddle together muttering in this gloomy engine room, Sakuya would have preferred to invite Sisam, Kisara, or Rui. The sight of them alone would have soothed his spirits. He let a little of this discontent reach his lips, and received a savage glare from the boatswain.
Before anyone clever started talking about male supremacy, this was probably just the boatswain's mood. Sakuya, obliged to accommodate it, had a thing or two he might have said. But annoying the boatswain now would make trouble later. He smiled cravenly and shut his mouth.

source.japanese: こうして信天翁号が、とにもかくにもあの窮地から逃れ出でてから数週間が経つ。そして過ぎてしまえば喉元の熱いのもなんとやらで、船の主だった面子はもう、あの巨大な白いヒトガタの事など思い煩[わずら]う事をやめていたのだった───
source.english: And so several weeks had passed since the Albatross somehow escaped that desperate situation. Danger past, terror was soon forgotten; the ship's principal figures no longer troubled themselves about the enormous white human shape—

target.text: In Sakuya's head, if he had to spend his time squirming in this gloomy engine room while huddled together with a bunch of men, his mind would be visually comforted if they had called Shisamu, Kisara, or maybe Rui for him to look at, but just as that complaint was about to escape his lips, he was met with a vicious glare from the Bosun.

Setting aside any clever talk of male chauvinism and so on, the issue here was likely more fundamental: a matter of the Bosun's temperament. As someone forced to keep him company here, Sakuya had plenty he wanted to say, but he also figured that it would just spell a bunch of trouble later if he upset the Bosun, so with a servile smile, he kept his mouth shut.

Thus, several weeks passed since the Albatross somehow or other managed to escape from its predicament. Just as it is oft said how vows made in storms are forgotten in calms or some such, the leading figures of the Albatross had already ceased to worry about anything regarding that giant, white, humanoid form───

source.japanese: 篩った胡粉よりもまだ細かな粒子は、湿って流れて渦を巻き、漕ぎ手の腕や腓を問わずむらむらとまとわりついて、水から揚がったばかりの蛙もかくやに肌をしとどに濡らす。粉糠と降る雨、というより雲が気まぐれに海上へ降り下ったかの狭霧で、短艇の舳先に掲げられた懐中電燈の、ほんのり暈掛かって潤んだ灯りは、天鵞絨の夜着をぬくぬくと羽織って窓硝子越しに味わうなら、接骨木の酒の柔らかな酔い心地で眠気を誘ったろう。しかしこう、ぽたぽたと、濡れてよじれた髪の先やら海兵襟[えり]の端やら鼻の先やらに雫結ばれ滴り落ちるとなると、洋燈のぼんやり曇った灯りを、夢に遠く覗いたようななど言うていられたものかで、意気を削ぐこと著しく、漕ぎ手は櫂を使いながらぼやく、その唇にも水滴が伝う。
source.english: Particles finer than sifted shell-white pigment flowed damply, swirled, and clung thickly to the rowers' arms and calves, drenching their skin like frogs freshly lifted from water. Less a fine rain than a mist: a cloud capriciously descended upon the sea. The lamp mounted at the boat's bow glowed wetly inside a faint halo. Seen through glass while one sat snug in a velvet nightgown, it might have induced the soft, sleepy intoxication of elderberry wine. But with drops beading and falling from sodden twists of hair, sailor collars and the tips of noses, who could call that dim, clouded light a far-off glimpse into dream? It crushed the spirits. One rower complained as he worked his oar, water tracing even his lips.

target.text: Particles finer than even sieved gofun, moist, flowing, and swirling, clung to the rower's arms and calves alike in uneven splotches, skin thoroughly soaked as though he were a frog freshly lifted from the water. (TN: Gofun, written "胡粉", is a traditional Japanese white pigment made from grinding and purifying weathered seashells.)

In the midst of this rain falling like rice bran, or more aptly, mist like the clouds themselves had descended upon the ocean surface in a stroke of whimsy, if one could bask in this light from the electrical torch hung upon the bow, glow faintly haloed and blurred with moisture, through a glass pane while snugly clad in warm, velvet nightclothes, then it would surely invite a drowsiness like the pleasant intoxication of a round, mellow elderberry wine.

But like this, with droplets joining to form trickling streams falling from the ends of his wet, tangled hair, the edge of his sailor collar, and the tip of his nose, how could he possibly speak of the lantern's dim, clouded light as though it were some dream glimpsed from afar; his spirit had been profoundly sapped, and the rower grumbled while he put his arms to work, the droplets even running down his lips.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ちぇー……。よりにもよってこんな夜に当番なんて……ついてないヨ」
source.english: “Damn… Of all nights to be on duty. No luck at all.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Dang……. Of all the nights to be on watch, it just had to be this one……what rotten luck.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ま、ま。そんなに愚痴らないの。
　ちゃんと追加のご褒美でるんだからさ」
source.english:
“Now, now. Don't complain so much.
We get a proper extra reward.”

source.japanese: 小型の短艇の、その小振りな櫂ながらしがみつく体はもっと小柄で、同僚を慰めながら漕ぐにも全身を一杯に、弓と伸ばしては黍粒のようにたわめてで、その度に水滴が零されては振り零されるのが、雨の中にもがくムク犬じみていた。
source.english: The boat was small and its oars undersized, yet the bodies clinging to them were smaller still. Even as he comforted his shipmate, rowing took every inch of him: now stretched taut as a drawn bow, now doubled small as a millet seed. With every stroke the droplets rolled and flew from him, until he looked like a shaggy dog struggling in the rain.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Now, now. Don't complain that much. There's definitely gonna be an extra treat for us.」

Though the small boat's oars were also on the smaller side, the body clinging to them was of an even smaller stature still, consoling his coworker even though he himself was already doing his utmost just to keep rowing; drawn taut like a bow, he warped like the seed head of a millet, and every time this motion was repeated, droplets of water were shed and shaken off, like a shaggy dog writhing in the rain.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「そればっかりが楽しみだね。
　こんな夜番なんだもの、いくら水夫長がけちんぼってったって、二つくらいはもらえるんじゃないかな、トマト」
source.english:
“That's the only thing to look forward to.
On a night watch like this—even if the boatswain's stingy, surely we'll get two tomatoes.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Guess that's all there is to look forward to, huh. Doesn't matter how much of a skinflint the Bosun is, after a night watch like this, maybe we'll even get two whole tomatoes.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「荷はこないだ積み込んだばっかだから、まだ萎びてないヤツだよ、きっと」
source.english: “Only loaded them the other day. Bet they won't be shriveled yet.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「The cargo was loaded just the other day, so they won't be all shrivelled up yet, surely.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「歯を立てると、ぱりんって弾けるよ。
　青臭くって、そして甘酸っぱいよ」
source.english:
“Bite in and the skin pops.
Green-smelling, then sweet and sour.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「And when you sink your teeth into one, it's gonna burst open. It'll have that grassy scent, and a tart sweetness too.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「なんか、唾わいてきちゃったぁ……」
source.english: “My mouth's watering…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「I've kind of ended up drooling……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ねーっ」
source.english: “Yeah…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Riiight?」

source.japanese:
待ちわびの御褒賞を思うだけでべとつく夜霧の憂さも薄らぐか、信天翁の水夫達が顔見合わせて交わす笑みのあどけない、その朗らかな仕草にあっては、彼らの輪郭や毛先に裏侘びしく結露した水滴さえも、一つ一つ洋燈の灯を、きらきら銀の珠粒と宿して燦々めく。
　老婦人の袱紗の裏地めいた、熟れて冷えた柔らかさで四囲に垂れこめる夜霧の中、水夫達の拍子に合わせ揺れる洋燈の光跡は緩やかで、幸いにして波ばかりは緩い、船腹に噛みつくような荒れたのも、底から突き上げるような乱暴なのもない。
source.english:
Merely thinking of the reward they awaited seemed to soften the misery of the sticky night mist. The smiles they exchanged were innocent; in those cheerful movements, even the dismal drops condensed along their outlines and hair tips glittered, each holding the lantern's light in a silver bead.
Night mist hung about them with the cool, worn softness of the lining in an old woman's silk wrapping cloth. The lantern traced gentle paths as it swayed in time with the sailors. Fortunately the waves alone were mild. None bit roughly at the hull or thrust violently from below.

source.japanese: 凪いだ夜海を往く小舟に載せた荷は、櫂を漕ぐ水夫達のやや後ろで、円やかな肩をやはりこちらも夜露に濡らして、生温いのが余計に気色悪い。まとうドレスは霧をしのぐにはいささか華美に過ぎ頼りなく、どちらかといえば肢体の線を艶[なま]めかしく強調する用の、それもそのはず、短艇の荷というのは酒場娘であった。信天翁号の立ち寄る港々に、まるで同じ場所のように立ち現れるあの。
source.english: The cargo in the little boat upon the calm night sea sat just behind the rowers. Her rounded shoulders were wet with night dew too, unpleasantly so because it was lukewarm. The dress was too ornamental, too flimsy to ward off mist. It was better suited to accentuating her body's sensuous lines. Naturally enough: the boat's cargo was a tavern woman. One of those who appeared at the ports the Albatross visited, making them seem almost the same place.

target.text: Perhaps merely thinking of their dearly desired reward was enough to make the clinging mists thin, for with the cherubic smiles they exchanged, those sunny gestures, it was as though even the forlorn beads formed by condensation along their contours and the tips of their hair seemed to brilliantly shine in the hazy lantern glow, each holding a drop of dazzling silver within.

Amidst the night mist that hung low all around them, with a mellow, chilled softness like the lining of an old woman's fukusa, the trails of light emitted from the lantern shaking in tandem with the deck boys' rhythm were gentle, and fortunately, so, too, were the waves; they were not the violent sort that raged as though snapping at the boat's belly, thrusting up from the bottom. (TN: Fukusa, written "袱紗", is a square piece of fine silk cloth traditionally used in Japan for covering or wrapping gifts, with the fabric itself being an important part of the gift. It is also used in tea ceremonies.)

The cargo carried on the small boat heading across the calm night sea was sitting a little behind the rowing deck boys, softly rounded shoulders likewise soaked with the night dew, the tepidness of which only made it all the more unpleasant. The dress enveloping the figure was a little too gaudy in its splendour to be of aid in warding off the mist, and if anything, it was made for the purpose of accentuating the captivating lines of its wearer's body; that was little wonder, however, for the cargo on the boat was a bar girl. At every port the Albatross made call at, there they would emerge, as though each and every one was the very same place: one of those.

source.japanese:
荒くれ男達の、酌を務めれば一夜の夢の伴連れもする彼女達。肌濡らす悪い温さに、肩掛けをかき寄せるしなやかな指に世慣れた身のこなしは、船は船でも放蕩者達が戯れの、クルーザーあたりでこそ造花のように映えようものを、このどこやら裏ぶれて、夜逃げの船路めく小舟にあっても案外似合うのは、客前でのみ夢見せて、店から退ければ冷えた脚温めてくれる情夫もない、酒場女の宿縁、と見るのはやや穿[うが]ちすぎで。
　酒場娘はこのしけた短艇に何故だか慣れて身の置きどころ心得た様子で、座板に据えたお尻も落ち着いた、下級水夫達に掛ける言葉も軽口で。
source.english:
Women who poured drinks for rough men and accompanied them through a single night's dream. Her supple fingers drew the shawl closer against the unpleasant damp warmth; her practiced movements belonged, if aboard any boat, upon some wastrel's pleasure cruiser, where she might bloom like an artificial flower. Yet she suited this shabby craft too, this passage through the night like a furtive escape. Was that the destiny of a tavern woman—permitted to sell dreams only before customers, then leaving work with no lover to warm her cold legs? Perhaps that read too much into it.
Whatever the reason, she was at home in this miserable skiff. She knew where to settle herself, sat comfortably upon the thwart, and traded easy banter with the junior sailors.

target.text: The girls who, after pouring drinks for rowdy fellows, would also serve as their companion for a fleeting dream that lasted but a night. In response to the clammy warmth that clung to her skin, she pulled her shawl close with supple fingers, the worldly sophistication in her movements only truly able to shine like an artificial flower not on a ship of toil but on a cruiser where libertines would amuse themselves with idle luxuries.

Yet even on this small boat, somewhat seedy as if bound for a vanishing act beneath the moonlight, it still suited her unexpectedly well, for was that not the tragic fate of a bar girl? Weaving dreams only for her customers, with no paramour waiting to warm her cold legs once off the clock, but perhaps interpreting it as such was reading a bit too far into things. For some reason, the bar girl had the demeanour of someone completely accustomed with where to place herself in this gloomy boat; planted on the boards, her behind was calmly fixed in place, and the words she spoke to the deck boys consisted of frivolous raillery as well.

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「徹夜仕事でもらえるのが、トマトのいくつかって。
　あたしの時と、待遇はそんなに変わってないのね」
source.english:
“All-night work, and a few tomatoes for your pay.
Not much has changed since my time.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「You receive a few tomatoes as compensation for working all night, you say? I suppose the working conditions aren't much different from my time, hmm.」

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「でもそんなので幸せになれるんだから、お手軽……っていえばお手軽か」
source.english: “Still, if that makes you happy, you're easy to please… Easy enough, I suppose.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「But if that's all it takes to make you happy, that makes life easy…… I suppose one could say?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「なにをー。姉さんだって、前は冷やしトマトにお塩少し振って食べるの大好きだったくせに」
source.english: “Hey! You used to love chilled tomatoes with a little salt too.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「You're one to talk. Before, you used to love chilled tomatoes with a little sprinkle of salt on top, big sis.」

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「『前は』、ね、確かにそうだったけれど」
source.english: “‘Used to.’ Yes, I certainly did.”

source.japanese:
……どこやら破落戸達の符丁めいた物言いで、舳先の洋燈では二者の間の闇を透かすまでは至らず、互いの顔色も窺えぬだろうに、やりとりに不都合は無さそうで、意は通い合っているらしい。
　酒場の娼妓と下級水夫という、安いマドロスパイプの紫煙とバンドネオンのダンス曲が漂うような取り合わせは、絵に描いたようにお似合いの組み合わせなのかも知れないが、この短艇に乗り合わせた両者は、釣り合うというより同類である。信天翁号の下級水夫達と港の酒場娘達、二つ共に知る者なら判るだろうが、何しろこいつら、一方は青い蕾の少年達、一方は咲き乱れ加減の女達と厳然たる際があるというのに、並べてみると貌立ちや雰囲気の要素というのが共通しているのである。
source.english:
…Their words had something of a ruffians' code. The lamp at the bow could not penetrate the darkness between them; they could scarcely have read one another's faces. Yet this caused no difficulty. Their meanings passed readily enough.
A tavern prostitute and junior sailors: a pairing redolent of cheap sailors' pipes and bandoneon dance music, picture-perfect in its way. But the passengers in this skiff were less a matched set than members of the same species. Anyone acquainted with both the Albatross's junior sailors and the port tavern women would understand. For all the obvious divide—male buds upon one side, women in riotous bloom upon the other—their faces and the cast of their whole presence shared the same elements.

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「"Before", right? I certainly used to be like that back then, but.」

……She spoke in a manner that echoed the coded cant of hoodlums, and with the light from the lamp hung at the bow proving insufficient to illuminate the dark between them, it was likely not possible for them to see the other's countenance, though that didn't seem like an inconvenience for them, for it appeared their minds were in accord. A prostitute from a bar and a sailor, a pairing akin to the violet haze wafting up from a cheap sailor's pipe and a dance tune played on the bandoneon drifting through the air together; it might well be a picture-perfect combination, but the pair who shared this boat were not so much a good match as they were of the same kind.

The deck boys of the Albatross and the bar girls of the ports: any who knows them both are likely aware of this, for you see, while a strict demarcation exists───on one hand are the young lads, green and unripe like unopened buds, and on the other hand are the women, in the midst of blooming profusely───when placed side by side, it becomes evident that the components of their visages and general atmosphere have several elements in common.

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「前はあなた達と同じだったけれど、
　んー……『今』はどちらかって言うと、
　サクランボ味のリコリスの方が好きなの」
source.english:
“I used to be just like you.
Mm… ‘Now,’ though,
I think I prefer cherry-flavored licorice.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Before, I used to be the same as you, but, mmhー……if I had to pick as I am "now", I prefer liquorice with the taste of cherry.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「なんか気取ったこと言ってらぁ」
source.english: “Listen to her getting fancy.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Listen to you, all pretentious.」

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「別に……陸に揚がると、食べ物飲み物の好みも変わってくるだけよ」
source.english: “Not really… Your taste in food and drink just changes when you come ashore.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Not really……it's just that, once you go ashore, you'll find that your preferences for food will change as well.」

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「なんにしても……毎回思うのだけど、どうしてあたしたちの物欲というのはこう、慎ましいのかしらね」
source.english: “Anyway… I think this every time. Why are our material desires so modest?”

source.japanese: リコリス、といえば聞き慣れず高級な嗜好品のようだが、スペインカンゾウの根の汁を煮出してアニスで香り付けしたチュウイングキャンディで、要は毛唐の駄菓子である。子供の食い物である。酒場の彼女の言う通りに、水夫がトマトに示す執着と大差はなく、慎ましやかな、練れた大人が胸を張って好物というにはどうにも浮かない稚気が利き過ぎの。
source.english: Licorice sounded unfamiliar, like some expensive indulgence, but it was chewy candy made by boiling the juice of Spanish licorice root and scenting it with anise. In short, foreign penny candy. Children's food. As she said, it differed little from the sailors' fixation upon tomatoes. Modest tastes, too steeped in childishness for seasoned adults to proclaim proudly as favorites without looking rather odd.

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Anyhow……I wonder about this every time, but why are our worldly desires so, you know, modest?」

Liquorice might sound like a high-class, luxury indulgence to the unfamiliar listener, but it is simply a chewing candy made from a decoction of Spanish liquorice root juice with anise added as flavouring: in short, a candy belonging to those scruffy Europeans. It is eaten by children. Just as the lady from the bar said, it was hardly different from the fixation the sailors held for tomatoes; it was modest, something far too childish for a mature adult to be able to puff out their chest with pride while declaring it their favourite food.

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「ま、それでいいんでしょうよ。
　あたし達、別に高いお酒や凄いご馳走がなくったって、それで毎日やってけるんだから」
source.english:
“Well, that's fine.
We don't need expensive booze or great feasts to get through each day.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Well, I suppose that's still fine. Even without expensive liquors or being treated to grand feasts, we still make it through the day.」

source.japanese: 霧を含んでしんねり重い前髪の陰となり、眼差しに浮かぶ想いは計れないが、胸中に通うのはやさぐれた船乗り相手に酌婦を務め、その夜限りの恋人として情交結ぶ、日々の暮らしの徒然草か。ふっと肩をすぼめたはずみに、ドレスの肩紐がずれてするりと、乳房の程良くふっくらしたのが夜闇に白々と優しく浮いた。櫂を使っていた水夫の一人が視界の端に捉えたが、同類への礼儀正しく見なかったふりをした。
source.english: Her gaze lay hidden beneath bangs made heavy with mist, and there was no measuring the thoughts afloat within it. Perhaps some idle chronicle of her days passed through her mind: pouring drinks for dissolute sailors, coupling with them as sweethearts for a single night. She gave a slight shrug; the shoulder strap of her dress slipped, and the pleasant fullness of one breast slid free, softly white in the darkness. One of the sailors at the oars caught it at the edge of his vision but, with the courtesy owed another of his kind, pretended not to see.

target.text: Her bangs, sodden and heavy with the mist, cast a deep shadow, the emotions surfacing in her eyes impossible to measure, but perhaps what coursed through her heart was the days of playing hostess for jaded sailors, joining them in intimacy for that night alone, the essays of idleness born from daily life. When she suddenly shrugged her shoulders, the shoulder strap of her dress slipped right off, her moderately swelling chest striking a pale and tender sight in the black of night. One of the sailors working the oars caught a glimpse in the corner of his vision, but out of politeness towards his fellow kind, he pretended not to see.

source.japanese: ───と、しばし会話が接ぎ穂を失って、狭霧が巻いて、櫂が軸受けに軋む音、湿った波音ばかりが惻々と迫る───と、夜闇の彼方から陰に籠もって鳴り渡ってきたのが、寝惚けた牛蛙の唸り声じみて、霧笛の響きだ。およそ二ケーブルほどと、音の深さで彼我の隔たりを測って、渡る最後の一息、漕ぐ手に力を籠める。と暫[しばら]くはただ流動する墨の中を進むばかりと見えたが、しまいにとうとう濃霧の奥、濃い闇の蟠りの果てに、貧弱だが確かに明かりの灯る、あれこそ下級水夫達が船尾近くのボロ小屋で腐りかかっていた棺桶の中から必死で探し出した航海灯に、不純物だらけの灯油を苦労して漉して注ぎこんでやっと点[とも]した母船への目標で、闇の中により黒々とうずくまるいい加減な形がようやく浮かび上がった。
source.english: Conversation lost its next thread for a while. Mist swirled. Only the oars' creaking in their locks and the damp sound of waves pressed mournfully close. Then from beyond the night darkness came a muffled bellow, like a sleepy bullfrog's groan: a foghorn. From the sound's depth they judged the distance at about two cable lengths and put strength into the last stretch of rowing. For a while it seemed they merely traveled through flowing ink. Finally, deep within the thick mist and gathered dark, a light shone. Feeble, but real. The navigation lamp the junior sailors had desperately found among rotting coffins in the ramshackle hut near the stern, and finally lit with dirty kerosene laboriously filtered, now marked their mother ship. At last her carelessly assembled shape emerged, crouching blacker within the black.

target.text: ───And so, for a while, the conversation lost its thread and faltered, the mist shrouded them, and the sound of the oars creaking against the oarlock and the dampened murmur of the waves was all that surrounded them, bearing down on them with poignant intensity───and so, clad in shadows, resounding far and wide from the distant dark of night, like the groaning of a half-asleep American bullfrog, came the sound of a foghorn. It was probably around two cables away, he thought, measuring the distance between himself and the other through the depth of the sound; this was the final bit of effort to overcome, and he mustered strength into his rowing arms.

For a while, it seemed as though they just glided through flowing ink, until finally, reaching the depths of the thick fog, there, at the furthest reaches beyond the coiled knots of dense darkness, though frail, was an undeniable light; that there was the very navigational light that the deck boys themselves had so strenuously dug out from those rotting coffins in the shabby shack near the stern, for which they had undergone such toils in order to strain the kerosene drowning in impure particulates before pouring it in and finally lighting up that mark of their mother ship, and out of the darkness, a shape an even deeper black, huddled and amorphous, finally emerged.

source.japanese: 闇が輪郭を曖昧にしてもなお、悪目立ちのする凸凹としたその船型、幸い今夜もどうにか浮いている、濃霧に航路を見失って座礁する船もあろうに、まさに憎まれっ子世に憚[はばか]るのなんとやら、信天翁号はあちこち軋ませぼろぼろと部品を振り零しながらも、今夜も洋上にその醜怪な姿をしぶとく晒していた。
source.english: Even with darkness blurring its outline, that lumpy hull stood out unpleasantly. Fortunately it was somehow still afloat tonight. Other ships might lose their course in the fog and run aground; the hated brat, as the saying went, thrived. Creaking everywhere, shedding parts, the Albatross stubbornly displayed her hideous form upon the sea again.

target.text: That vessel, whose unevenness was all the more conspicuous with her silhouette obscured in the dark, was fortunately still somehow managing to stay afloat tonight as well, and though there are surely ships that, losing their course in thick fog, run aground on hidden reefs, ill weeds truly do grow apace, or however that saying goes, for even as every which part of the Albatross creaked and jarred, even as she shed parts of herself into the sea, tonight was yet another night where that odiously grotesque shape was doggedly on display out on the open sea.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「はぁ～……やっと見えた。
　僕らが行ってる間に沈んでたらどうしようって思ってたけど」
source.english:
“Haaah…
Finally see her. I was wondering what we'd do if she'd sunk while we were gone.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Haaah～……I finally see her. I wasn't sure what to do if she had sunk while we were gone.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「後で航海のカミサマにお祈りしないと……」
source.english: “Have to pray to the god of sailing later…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「I'll have to offer up a prayer to the god of seafaring later……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「馬鹿だなあ君、カミサマなんかにこの船のことばれたら、逆にそのお怒りで沈められるって」
source.english: “You're stupid. If some god found out about this ship, he'd sink her in anger.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Are you an idiot? If something like a god ever catches wind of this ship, we'd just be sunk in a fit of his fury instead.」

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「そうねえ、どっちかっていうと、担当は悪魔さんの方だわあの船」
source.english: “Yes. That ship's more in a devil's jurisdiction.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Right. If you ask me, that ship's under the Devil's charge.」

source.japanese:
自分達が乗りこむ船に対して、なんとも麗しい信頼に満ち満ちた感想の眼差しで見上ぐる信天翁号は、確かにこうして霧とも雨ともつかぬ水気孕んだ闇に包まれて、地獄からうっかり彷徨いでてきたという形容がいかにもしっくりと当てはまって、バラック群のあちこちから悪魔どもが思い思いの見得でわらわら這いずりだしてきても一向に不思議はなかったのだが、しかし舷側からひょこりと顔を出し、呼ばわってきたのは同じ下級水夫であった。故郷では業火に馴染んだ悪魔どもにあっては、今夜の霧の、変に人肌めいた温さはさすがに閉口したのであろう。
　或いは信天翁号のバラックを眺めて、そのあまりにいい加減な有り様に地獄の荒野の方がまだ清潔と引き返したのかも知れない。
source.english:
Full of such lovely confidence in the ship they were boarding, they looked up at the Albatross. Enclosed in damp darkness neither mist nor rain, she did indeed look as though she had accidentally wandered out of hell. Nothing would have been strange about devils crawling in their various poses from the scattered shacks. Yet the face peeking over the side to call them belonged to another junior sailor. Devils accustomed to their homeland's inferno must have found tonight's mist, oddly lukewarm as human skin, too much.
Or perhaps they had taken one look at the Albatross's shacks, decided hell's wasteland was cleaner than this slapdash mess, and gone back.

target.text: The Albatross, beheld with a gaze brimming with such heartwarming trust as they looked up at the vessel they were about to board, certainly, while enveloped in this darkness laden with moisture that could not be pinned down as neither mist nor rain, describing her as something that had heedlessly strayed out from the depths of Hell suited her with an uncanny perfection, and it would not seem out of place in the slightest for demons to crawl and squirm forth from here and there, out from the clusters of shacks, each striking their own preferred poses, but the faces popping up over the ship's bulwark and calling out to them were identical deck boys.

For the demons long inured to the infernal hellfire of their homeland, tonight's fog, with its oddly human warmth, must surely have given them pause. Or perhaps, once they beheld the shacks of the Albatross, so slipshod was their state that even the desolate wastes of hell may have seemed sanitary by comparison, and so they turned back.

source.japanese:
【信天翁号の下級水夫】
「おおい……！　ボート……！」
source.english: “Heeey! Boat!”

target.text: 【Deck boy on the Albatross】 「OOOI……! BOAT……!」

source.japanese:
【短艇の下級水夫】
「おおい……！　信天翁号……！」
source.english: “Heeey! Albatross!”

target.text: 【Deck boy on the small boat】 「OOOI……! ALBATROSS……!」

source.japanese:
【信天翁号の下級水夫】
「お疲れぇ……！
　こっちの準備はできてるよ……っ」
source.english:
“Good work!
We're ready here!”

target.text: 【Deck boy on the Albatross】 「GOOD WORK……! EVERYTHING'S READY ON OUR END……!」

source.japanese:
【短艇の下級水夫】
「りょーかぁい（了解）……っ。
　じゃあ交替しよー……！」
source.english:
“Roger!
Let's switch!”

target.text: 【Deck boy on the small boat】 「ROOOーGER THAT……! THEN COME RELIEVE US……!」

source.japanese: 互いの合図は先ほどの霧笛と同じく滅々と霧に吸いこまれて、大声の割りには意気などちっとも上がらない、それでも用は通じて、船縁から放られた縄梯子は、信天翁号に残っていた交代要員にとっては炭坑掘りの重役に降りゆくかの昇降段に等しく、短艇を漕ぎ寄せてきた者には天上への架け橋と垂れ下がった。たとえ戻る先が乱雑の極みたる信天翁号の船内であったとしても、ぎしぎし軋む短艇を夜霧に巻かれて漕ぐよりはまし、と。
source.english: Like the foghorn, their signals faded into the mist. For all their shouting, no spirits rose. Still, the message got through. The rope ladder thrown over the gunwale was, to the relief crew left aboard, a gangway down to the heavy labor of a coal mine. To those who had rowed here, it hung as a bridge to heaven. Even if they were returning to the utter chaos of the Albatross's interior, it was better than rowing a creaking boat in the night mist.

target.text: Their mutual signals faded away as they were swallowed into the mist, just like the foghorn before, and for how loud their voices were, there was not a shred of spirit to be heard in them, but regardless, the message got through; to the relief personnel that had remained behind on the Albatross, taking the rope ladder flung over the gunwale was akin to going down the ladder leading down into the coal pit and the heavy duties within it, while for those rowing the boat up to it, it dangled down like a bridge leading to paradise.

Even if the place they were returning to was the interior of the Albatross, the epitome of disorder, it was still better than being enveloped in night mist while rowing some creaking boat, they thought.

source.japanese: 下級水夫達がぞろぞろ数珠繋ぎに縄梯子を昇り降りして交替する間、酒場女はただ一人残って波の拍子に揺られていたところを見るに、信天翁号の阿呆な誰か、たとえば朔屋あたりが、無鉄砲にも一夜の歓楽に彼女を陸から招き寄せた、というのでもないらしい。
source.english: While the junior sailors climbed the rope ladder in a long chain to change shifts, the tavern woman remained alone in the skiff, rocking with the waves. Plainly she was not some one-night guest whom an Albatross idiot—Sakuya, for instance—had recklessly summoned from shore.

target.text: While the deck boys clambered up and down in a long chain like beads on a string, though one might think, judging from the way the bar girl was left sitting all by herself, swaying to the rhythm of the waves, that perhaps someone on the Albatross, someone like Sakuya, for example, had recklessly invited her here from the shore for a night of merriment, it didn't seem like that was the case.

source.japanese: ───朔屋は、不意に鼻先に甘い白粉と酒の匂い聞いた気がして、ふんふんと鼻先を突き出しつつ調理室から、ふらふらと繰り出してきて、
source.english: Sakuya suddenly thought he smelled sweet face powder and liquor. Sniffing, nose extended, he drifted out of the galley—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あれ、なんか女の匂いしてないこれ？」
source.english: “Huh. Doesn't it smell like a woman here?”

source.japanese: 船内の澱[よど]んだ空気中にほんの僅か混じった匂いの微粒子の二・三粒だけで、過敏にも股ぐらが反応して既に腰が退け気味になっているあたり、この男はどこまでも行動が下半身に直結していると言わざるを得ず。手には菜切り包丁と剥きかけの馬鈴薯の、自分に言いつけられた仕事など嗅いだような気がするというだけの女の肌の香にすっかり頭から放逐されており、全神経は有るか無しかの匂いを追うことのみに傾注されてあった。
source.english: Two or three grains of scent in the ship's stagnant air were enough to rouse his crotch and make him hunch defensively around it. The man's every action ran straight from the waist down; there was no denying it. In his hands were a vegetable knife and a half-peeled potato. The merest possibility of a woman's skin upon the air had driven his assigned work clean out of his head. Every nerve bent upon pursuing that scent, whether it existed or not.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「最近日照り続きであんま体拭いてない、
　シサム・キサラの香ばしい匂いじゃなくって、泪姐さんの香水くさいのとも違って、
　クロのしっこ臭いのとは全然別の……」
source.english:
“Don’t smell like Sisam and Kisara’s toasty
funk—they haven’t wiped down much with this damn dry spell lately—not like Sister Rui’s perfume,
and sure as hell ain’t Kuro’s pee…”

target.text: ───Sakuya felt like he suddenly picked up the sweet scent of face powder and alcohol with the tip of his nose, and so he ventured forth from the galley on unsteady feet, nose-tip thrust forward, sniffing all the while,
【Naomasa】 「Huh, doesn't it sort of smell like woman here?」

With but two or three specks of minute particulates of smell faintly mixed into the stagnant air filling the ship, his sensitive crotch also began to react, his hips already starting to pull back, and one is compelled to mention once more that this man's actions were ever driven by his loins, come hell or high water.

In his hands were a vegetable knife and a potato in the midst of being peeled, but the likes of the work he'd been ordered to do was banished entirely from his mind the moment he felt as though he smelled the fragrance of a woman's skin, and his entire nervous system was now devoted to nothing but the pursuit of a scent that hovered somewhere between the boundary of presence and absence.

【Naomasa】 「It's not the heady aroma of Shisamu and Kisara, who haven't really been able to wipe down their bodies at all, what with the drought we've had lately, it's different from Rui-neesan's smell of perfume, and it's completely different from Kuro's smell of piss……」

source.japanese:
浅ましくもズボンの中で強張り始めた逸物のお陰で前屈み、飢えた犬のように鼻面翳して、手には刃物と馬鈴薯という、往来に置いたら要らぬ混乱を引き起こしそうな姿勢で上甲板を目指す朔屋に、調理室の戸口から二本の手が妖怪『小袖の手』はだしに五尺ばかりもにゅうるりと伸びて出て、一方は投げ輪のように朔屋の首にかかって締めあげ、一方は鉤縄のようにその肩に食いこんで、いずれもがっちりと、万力の剛さに青年を引き戻す、腕はいずれも赤茶のリーファージャケットの、船内でこの衣装を着けている者はといえば。
　朔屋が引きずり戻された、調理室からの戸口から漏れ伝わってきた声音は激昂に跳ね上がるでなくむしろ低いくらいの音だったけれど。
source.english:
Bent forward around the cock abjectly stiffening in his trousers, nose raised like a hungry dog's, knife and potato in hand—a posture likely to create needless alarm on any public street—Sakuya headed for the upper deck. Two arms slid from the galley doorway, stretching five feet or so, enough to put the yokai called Sleeved Hands to shame. One looped around his neck like a lasso and tightened; the other hooked into his shoulder. Both clamped him with the strength of a vise and hauled him back. Both emerged from reddish-brown reefer-jacket sleeves.
And who aboard wore those? The voices that followed Sakuya's retrieval did not rise in fury. If anything, they were low.

target.text: In a deplorable display, owing to the stiffening member concealed in his trousers, he was stooped over, muzzle held high like a starving dog, a knife and potato in his hands, and towards Sakuya, who was making his way to the upper deck with a posture that was bound to cause needless confusion were he placed in the middle of a public street, two hands emerged from the doorway of the galley, slithering as they stretched out about 150 centimetres in a way that put the yokai『Kosode no te』to shame. (TN: Kosode no te, written "小袖の手", is a yokai that manifests as a ghostly arm from the sleeves of a kosode, a type of kimono.)

One hand looped around Sakuya's neck like a lasso and tightened, the other dug into his shoulder like a grappling hook on the end of a rope, both of them with a solid grip, strong like a vice, pulling the young man back; both arms were clad in a reddish brown reefer jacket, and it didn't take a genius to figure out who wore an outfit like that on this ship. Sakuya was dragged back, and while the voices passing through the entrance to the galley did not rise sharply in indignation, on the contrary, they were on the lower side, still.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『たまに親切で、せっかくあんたの仕事に付き合ってやってるかと思えば』
source.english: ‘Once in a while we try being kind, take the trouble to help with your work—’

target.text: 【Shisamu】 『And here I was, thinking I'd go to the trouble of helping you out with your work in a rare display of consideration.』

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
『いきなりおっ放りだしてふらふらと、
　逃げ出したかと思えば』
source.english:
‘And you drop it all out of nowhere and wander off.
We thought you were running away—’

target.text: 【Kisara】 『But then you suddenly chucked it all aside and staggered out, and just as I thought you were about to run away or something.』

source.japanese:
【シサム】
『へえ朔屋……つまりお前はこう言いたいワケね？
　くっせぇ、この女、犬小屋の匂いがすんよ！
　───って』
source.english:
‘Oh, Sakuya… So this is what you mean?
This woman fucking stinks! Smells like a kennel!
That?’

target.text: 【Shisamu】 『Interesting, Sakuya……so this is what you really wanted to say, right? "Eww, this woman reeks like a damn kennel!" ───right?』

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
『ねえ朔屋、さあどっちにしようか？
　あたしの腋に挟まれるのと～』
source.english:
‘Hey, Sakuya.
Which will it be? Getting squeezed in my armpit—’

target.text: 【Kisara】 『Hey, Sakuya, what will it be then? Squeezed between our armpits～』

source.japanese:
【シサム】

So, Sakuya, the next time we meet, I know you’ll—”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Yeah……yeah……. I'll be waiting. Until that day comes, always. So, Sakuya-san, next time we meet, for sure.」

source.japanese: なんともはやちょっとした愁嘆場だが、別離の悲嘆に暮れる者、哀しみを慰める者、取り巻いて静かに見守る者と、どの間合いを見ても役者がみな顔が同じときては、名場面というより出来損ないの怪談めく。
source.english: A poignant little farewell, to be sure: one overcome by the pain of parting, another offering comfort, the rest gathered silently around. Yet when every actor wears the same face from every angle, the tableau resembles less a famous tragic scene than a botched ghost story.

target.text: Goodness gracious, it was a bit of a melodramatic scene, but the one overcome with the sorrow of parting, the one consoling that grief, and those who surrounded them, watching over it in silence: given that, no matter the angle one observed it from, every actor shared the same face, it seemed more like a misbegotten ghost story than a famous scene from a drama.

source.japanese:
ぞくぅぅと、朔屋が時を同じく非常な悪寒に襲われたのは偶然であり、この下級水夫の思慕が届いたせいと言うよりも、むしろ先ほどより立ち籠めたる異様な冷気のせいであったろう。
　おまけに冷気は下半身に集中しており、ぞくぞくと尿意を催させる、その切迫感と言ったら。冷たい空気は下方に溜まるなどの原理ではなく、単に朔屋が野菜屑の箱に頭から詰め込まれ、逆立ちの姿勢を強いられていたせいである。しかも下半身は裸に剥かれていた。ちなみに尻たぶの左右と真ん中の陰嚢の裏には左から順に、
『Ｒ．Ｉ．Ｐ』
　と木炭で書きつけられていた。
source.english:
It was mere coincidence that a prodigious chill seized Sakuya at that same moment—not, presumably, because the junior sailor's yearning had reached him, but because of the uncanny cold gathering for some time.
Worse, it concentrated around his lower parts, sending wave after wave of urgent need to piss through him. This had nothing to do with cold air settling downward. Sakuya had simply been stuffed headfirst into a crate of vegetable scraps and left standing on his head. His lower half, moreover, had been stripped bare. And upon his left buttock, the underside of his scrotum, and his right buttock, in order from left to right, someone had written in charcoal:
‘R.I.P.’

target.text: That Sakuya was struck with a long, most terrible creeping shudder at the very same time was a complete coincidence, for rather than laying the blame at the deck boy's yearning reaching his heart, if anything, it was surely due to this uncanny chill that hung in the air even more thickly than before.

To make matters worse, since the chill was concentrated on his lower half, sending through him shivers that stirred the urge to urinate, the sense of urgency he felt was beyond words. It was not because of the principle that cold air settles downward, but simply a result of Sakuya having been stuffed head-first into a box of vegetable scraps, forced into an upside-down posture. Furthermore, his lower half had been stripped bare. Incidentally, on his left and right buttocks, as well as on the bottom of his scrotum found between the two, reading from left to right, written with charcoal, were the letters: 『Ｒ．Ｉ．Ｐ』

source.japanese:
Ｒｅｓｔ Ｉｎ Ｐｅａｃｅ
　の略意であるが、こう実際に納骨堂もかくやの冷気に晒されては死者の憩いに休んでいるどころでなく、朔屋は尻の肌寒さに戦[おのの]きながら、裸の足のたうたせ反動に半身を野菜屑の中から引き抜く。髪にへばりつく芋やら玉葱の皮やら振り落とし、
source.english:
Short for Rest in Peace.
But in a chill fit for an actual ossuary, Sakuya could hardly be resting like a dead man. Shuddering at the cold upon his ass, he thrashed his bare legs, using the momentum to extract half his body from the vegetable scraps. He shook potato and onion peel from his hair.

target.text: Ｒｅｓｔ Ｉｎ Ｐｅａｃｅ. It was an abbreviation of the above, but since he was being exposed to a chill as if he were actually interred in some crypt, this was hardly the time to find repose in the peace of the dead, and while shuddering at the cold air stroking his buttocks, using the recoil from flexing his bare feet, he managed to wrench the upper half of his body free from the box of vegetable waste. He shook off the peels of potato and onion that stuck to his hair,

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ぷっは」
source.english: “…Phaaah.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Pwah!」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あの双子は男の下半身ひん剥くことにもう少し慎みというのを持っていただきたい。
　だって恥ずかしがる女に脱がしてもらった方が楽しいしなあ」
source.english:
“Those twins ought to show a bit more restraint about stripping a man's lower half.
It's more fun when the woman taking your clothes off is shy about it.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「I'd like for those twins to show just a tad more modesty or something when they pull off a man's pants. I mean, it's a lot more fun being stripped when it's a shy girl doing it.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ていうか、なに今のすっげえ悪寒!?」
source.english: “Actually, what was that terrible chill!?”

source.japanese: 辺りの様子に注意を傾け取ると、冷気は厨房の戸口から浸食性の粘菌のように床を這い、廊下から押し寄せきているらしかった……。
source.english: Taking stock of his surroundings, he saw that the cold was creeping from the passage through the galley doorway, crawling across the floor like an invasive slime mold.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「More importantly, what's up with this terrible chill right now!?」

As his attention turned to his surroundings, it seemed as though the chill was creeping in along the floor from the entrance to the galley like a corrosive slime mold, surging in from the passageway…….

source.japanese: 離れがたい未練と思慕に想われる朔屋の、なんとも果報者である事だが、それでも短艇は女になりつつある下級水夫を乗せて往く往く狭霧の波間。短艇と信天翁号は寄り添うては遊離する潮の泡沫と分かたれゆき、未練に後ろ髪引かれる下級水夫は切々とした哀惜の眼差しで、隔たっていくかつての母船の、子供の殴り書きじみた輪郭をまだ何度も振り返っていたけれど、だからそれに気づいたのだろう。
source.english: Fortunate indeed was Sakuya, to inspire such lingering attachment and longing. Yet the skiff carried the junior sailor—gradually becoming a woman—on and on through the misty waves. The boat and the Albatross drew apart amid the tidal foam, which gathered and drifted free. With his heart still tugged backward, the junior sailor kept turning a gaze of poignant sorrow upon the crude, childlike outline of his former mother ship as it receded. Perhaps that was why he noticed it.

source.japanese: 喫水線から船腹に、のろのろと重たげに身を起こしてはもたれかかる波の背は鈍く、別れの夜に催眠的な哀調を添えている。もちろん喫水線と波の境はほとんど夜闇にぼやけて暗さに慣れた目でもしかと見分けがたく、その下級水夫も一瞬は見逃したのだ。波の背が瘤と膨らんで、菌糸類が盛り上がるように頭をもたげ、粘い膠ともったり船腹に貼りついたを、下級水夫は波の気まぐれと見なして深くは考えず、物想いに戻ろうとした視界の端で───
source.english: Dull-backed waves lifted themselves slowly, heavily from the waterline and leaned upon the hull, adding a hypnotic sadness to the night of parting. Of course, the boundary between waves and waterline almost blurred into the dark; even night-adjusted eyes could not distinguish it clearly. For an instant the junior sailor missed it. A wave's back swelled into a lump, raised its head like burgeoning fungal growth and stuck thickly to the hull like viscous glue. He took it for a wave's caprice and was about to return to his thoughts. At the edge of his sight—

target.text: The target of a lingering attachment and yearning that made it difficult to let go, what an inordinately lucky fellow Sakuya was, but even so, the boat carrying the deck boy gradually becoming a woman drifted ever onward, cutting through the misty waves. Nestled together only to drift apart, the small boat and the Albatross parted ways like ephemeral flowers of tide-foam; the regret pulled at the deck boy's hair from behind, and with a look of passionate grief, he turned back to gaze at what was once his mother ship now growing ever more distant, at that silhouette reminiscent of a child's scrawlings, over and over again, and that was likely why he noticed that thing.

From the waterline and up the hull, the wave rose dully, heaving itself up with heavy lethargy only to recline its back against the ship, painting their nighttime parting in hypnotically plaintive tones. Naturally, the boundary between waterline and wave was almost entirely blurred in the black of night, and even with eyes accustomed to the dark, it would be difficult to distinguish with but a glance, and so the deck boy also failed to notice it for an instant.

The back of the wave swelled like a bump, it reared its head like mycelial threads bulging upwards, clinging to the ship's hull like gelatinous glue, and though the deck boy deemed it to be but the whimsy of the waves, not thinking too hard about it, just as he was about to lose himself in his thoughts once more, at the very edge of his vision───

source.japanese: 波が生み出した粘塊は、船腹に砕ける事もなく、重力から遊離したかの滑らかな動き、滴り落ちる樹脂をフィルムの逆回しに掛けたように、船腹を這い上がり、やがて開きっぱなしの船窓を抜けて船内に流れこんでいく、ぎくりと向き直った動揺の仕草に、酒場娘は不審げに、
source.english: The sticky mass born from the wave did not break against the hull. Moving smoothly as if freed from gravity, like dripping resin in a film run backward, it crawled up the ship's side and flowed through an open porthole. His startled turn made the tavern woman look at him curiously.

target.text: The sticky clump birthed from the wave was not smashed to pieces against the ship's hull, but with slippery movements, as though freed from the restraints of gravity, as though dripping resin was played back in reverse on film, it slithered up the hull, until it finally flowed into the ship's interior through a porthole that had been left open, and at his sudden, agitated turn, the bar girl fixed him with a doubtful look,

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「？　どうしたの？
　離れたくないのは判るけど、
　そんなにいつまでも未練を残してちゃ」
source.english:
“Hm? What's wrong?
I know you don't want to leave,
but you can't keep clinging forever…”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Hm? What's the matter? I can understand that you don't want to part, but you can't just keep clinging to that regret forever.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ううん、そういうのじゃなくって……。
　今、なにか海から船に……」
source.english:
“No, it's not that… Just now,
something came from the sea into the ship…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「No, that's not what this is……. Just now, something rose from the sea and went into the ship……」

source.japanese:
なおも続ける注視の先で波は夜に黒々と、凪に黒く、船腹に寄せては返すのみ、それだって夜闇に溶けて、下級水夫の心の中での補正が掛かった情景と指摘されたら反論ができぬ。結局先ほどの異様な物体は、船に遺した想いが見せた幻の類と諦めて、下級水夫はもう振り返らず、それでもなんとのう心細い、不気味な心地して酒場娘の横身に寄り添った。
　そして、離れていく短艇の背後で、船腹に寄せる波から黒い塊が分かたれては、一つ、二つ、三つ、丶丶丶。
source.english:
He kept watching, but saw only waves: black in the night, black upon the calm, advancing and withdrawing against the hull. Even those dissolved into the darkness. Had someone told him his feelings were correcting the scene inside his head, he could not have argued. At last he dismissed the uncanny object as an illusion born of everything he was leaving aboard. He did not look back again. Still vaguely lonely and afraid, he pressed close to the tavern woman.
Behind the departing skiff, black masses parted from the waves against the hull. One. Two. Three…

target.text: Where his gaze yet lingered, the waves stood dark against the night, dark in the calm, merely lapping against the hull before breaking and receding, and even that motion merely melted into the nocturnal gloom; if someone were to point out that this was just a scene shaped by the deck boy's mind filling in the blanks, he would be unable to refute it.

In the end, he resigned himself to the thought that the bizarre object had been but some manner of illusion shown to him by his yet lingering feelings for the ship, and the deck boy no longer turned his head, but even so, for reasons unclear to him, feeling forlorn and with an eerie unease in his heart, he snuggled up against the bar girl's side. Thus, behind the boat growing ever more distant, black lumps separated from the waves washing against the hull: one, two, three, and still many more.

source.japanese: で、朔屋は、冷気に怯えて恐る恐ると、頭を突き出して船内通路に右左、彼にしては勇を鼓して確かめてみたのに、通路は陽と影も見えず夜灯りに裏ぶれて、船の軋みに船腹越しの波の音が遠く物憂い、そればかり。馬鹿は常人とは季節を外して風邪を引く、だからこそ馬鹿というのだが、朔屋は双子に剥かれて下半身を夜気に当て、要らぬ悪気でも呼びこんだかと懸念して、無人の通路の嘘寒さにぶるるる、我が身を抱いた時、船窓が開きっぱなしになっていたのを認めた。
source.english: Meanwhile Sakuya, frightened by the chill, timidly poked his head into the passage and looked right and left. Brave of him to check, but not a soul showed in the corridor, only the drear of its night lamps. The ship creaked; waves beyond the hull sounded distant and melancholy. Nothing more. An idiot catches cold out of season, unlike ordinary people; that is why he is an idiot. Had the twins, by stripping him and exposing his lower half to the night air, invited some needless malign influence inside? Shivering and hugging himself in the deserted passage's dismal cold, he noticed that a porthole had been left open.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おいおい、今夜は波も静かだが、景気の悪い霧雨だ。窓をちゃんと閉めとかんと湿気っぽくていけない……」
source.english: “Hey, hey. Calm waves tonight, but miserable drizzle. Have to shut the portholes properly or it'll get damp…”

source.japanese: それでなくとも清潔とはお世辞にも言い難い船内、浸水や水気を放置しておいて寝網や畳みこんだサラシ、果ては食料の類が小人の寝床のような黴[カビ]に覆われたのも、朔屋が乗りこんでから一度や二度ではきかない。ずぼらな朔屋にしても、割り当てられた塩スープの薄切り薫製肉が元は黴たかりと知るのは閉口もので、船窓の丸いのを閉めようとして、
source.english: The ship's interior could not charitably be called clean in the first place. Since Sakuya came aboard, neglected leaks and damp had more than once covered hammocks, folded cotton wraps, even provisions in mold like bedding laid out for tiny folk. Slovenly though he was, Sakuya disliked discovering that the thin slice of smoked meat allotted to his salt soup had once been furred with mold. He reached to close the round porthole.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なんだあ、これぁ……？」
source.english: “…What's this…?”

source.japanese: 船窓の枠やその足下の床に、ちらちらと仄光るモノを見て拾い上げれば、指の先で気味悪くべとついた。通路灯の下に確かめれば、剥片、鱗である。落ちていたところを改めると、粘液が薄膜とへばりついてもいる。
source.english: He saw faintly gleaming things here and there on its frame and the floor below. Picking one up, he felt it stick unpleasantly to his fingers. Beneath the passage lamp he examined the flake. A scale. Looking again where it had lain, he found a thin film of slime too.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……誰ぞこんな船窓で夜釣りとしゃれこんだかね。また似非風流な……」
source.english: “…Someone decided to do a little night fishing from this porthole? Playing at refinement again…”

source.japanese: 信天翁号の下級水夫達は暇を持て余すとそういう手すさびに出る、また彼ら以外にもその手の消閑の遊を能[よ]くするのに心当たりはある。あの殺し屋だ。だから朔屋は、誰かが釣り上げた魚から零れ落ちたモノだと決めつけたのだけれども。先入観を取り払えば、その指先大の大きさからして、鱗の主は相当の大魚である事に気づいたはずである。
source.english: The Albatross's junior sailors indulged in that sort of pastime when bored. Besides them, he knew another who liked such idle amusements: the assassin. So Sakuya decided the scales had fallen from a fish someone caught. Without that preconception, their very size, each as big as a fingertip, would have told him the fish must have been very large.

target.text: And so, scared of the chill, Sakuya timidly stuck his head out into the passageway and looked from left to right, but for all that he screwed up his courage to confirm what was going on for himself for once, there were no shadows or lights to be seen in the passage; it only offered a dreary sight in the dim light of night, the ship's creaking and the sound of the waves lapping against the hull were faint and melancholy, and that was all there was.

Idiots catch colds out of season, hence why they are idiots in the first place, but when Sakuya's bottom, stripped bare by the twins, was hit by the night air, he feared that perhaps he had brought some avoidable malice upon himself; he shivered at the illusory chill of the deserted passageway, and when he began to hold himself tight, he realized that a porthole had been left wide open.
【Naomasa】 「Oi oi, the waves might be calm tonight, but there's a dreary drizzle out there. If you don't close the portholes right, it's going to get humid in here……」

Even if that weren't the case, even as flattery, it was hard to call the interior of this ship sanitary, and if flooding or moisture was neglected, then the hammocks, all the folded fabric, and finally, even the food, would be covered in mold that looked like tiny beds for little gnomes, and since Sakuya came aboard, that had happened more than just once or twice. Even for someone as sloppy as Sakuya, realizing that the thin slices of bacon in his allotted salt soup had once been mold-ridden still left him stewing in silent disgust, and so just as he went to close the round porthole,
【Naomasa】 「……What the hell is this……?」

Around the frame of the porthole and on the floor by his feet, he saw something glittering with a faint light, and as he picked it up, it stuck unpleasantly to his fingertip. When he confirmed what it was under the passageway light, it turned out to be a flake, a scale. Upon re-examining the place where it had fallen, he noticed there was a faint membrane of mucus still clinging to it.
【Naomasa】 「……Now who could possibly have decided to treat themselves to a spot of night fishing from a porthole. What sham sophistication……」

When the deck boys of the Albatross had more spare time than they knew what to do with, they would amuse themselves with such things, but he also happened to know of another who frequently killed time in that way. It was that murderer. Therefore, Sakuya arbitrarily decided that it must have been a scale shed from a fish that someone had reeled in there, however. If he had but rid himself of his preconceptions, he would surely have noticed that, given it was about the size of a fingertip, the owner of that scale was a fish of considerable size.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ってな事が昨夜にあってだな。
　あんた、夜釣りでもしたかい？」
source.english:
“…That's what happened last night.
Did you do some night fishing?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……And that's what happened last night. Did you maybe go night fishing or something?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「知らねえなあ。昨ン夜は船倉にひっ籠もって、この旦那相手にずっと将棋打ってたし」
source.english: “Don't know anything about it. Spent last night holed up in the hold, playing shogi with this gentleman.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Beats me. I was holed up in the hold last night, playing shogi against this good gentlecat the whole time.」

source.japanese: と智里が、大店の主でも呼びつけるように顎をしゃくった相手が宗右衛門で、この山猫ほども巨大な黒猫は索具函の上にでんと寝そべり、船の頭上を周回する水鳥にも目もくれず、毛皮の腹を波うたせてゆったりと。空は昨夜の鬱々とした霧雨とうってかわって好天で、船の名と同じ信天翁も先黒の翼を暢気に拡げ空に浮き文字「ｍ」のかたち。
source.english: Tomosato jerked his chin with the grand air of summoning the proprietor of some great establishment. The gentleman in question was Soemon. The black cat, huge as a wildcat, sprawled upon a rigging box. Ignoring even the seabirds circling above, he lay at ease, his furred belly rising and falling. After last night's gloomy drizzle, the sky was fair. An albatross, namesake of the ship, spread black-tipped wings lazily overhead, floating in the shape of an ‘m.’

source.japanese:
【直正】
「この猫は将棋の相手までするってかよう……いや、普通にやりかねないか、こいつなら。
　……おお、これだこれだ」
source.english:
“This cat even plays shogi…? No, he probably would. …Oh,
here it is.”

target.text: So Tomosato said, directing a jerk of his chin fit for summoning the wealthy master of a large store at none other than Souemon, the black cat colossal enough to rival even a wildcat, sprawled out with imposing dignity atop a chest of rigging gear, not sparing even a glance for the seabirds circling high in the skies over the ship either, the fur of his belly rippling in calm waves. The sky had changed completely from the gloomy drizzle of last night, the weather now fine, and the ship's namesakes, the albatrosses, spread their black-tipped wings and floated around the air in the shape of the letter "m".
【Naomasa】 「You telling me this cat can even play shogi……no, if it's this guy, he could actually pull it off. ……Oh, this is it, this is it.」

source.japanese: 払い落としたつもりがまだ残っていた、船員服の上着の裾[すそ]に貼りついた鱗[うろこ]を指先に掬[すく]い、猫なら魚の臭いは好物だろう程度のなんの気なしで、宗右衛門の鼻先に持っていったところ。一閃。前足の張り手で張り飛ばされて、後には不快そうに鼻面に皺寄せる宗右衛門猫と、指先に爪の傷で血を滲ませ呆気にとられる朔屋と。
source.english: He thought he had brushed them all away, but a scale still clung to his sailor jacket's hem. Scooping it onto a fingertip, he brought it to Soemon's nose, thinking idly that a cat would like a fish smell. A flash. A forepaw slapped it away. Left behind: Soemon wrinkling his muzzle in disgust, and Sakuya dumbfounded, claw marks bleeding on his fingertips.

target.text: What he thought he had already brushed off yet remained; he scooped up a scale that had stuck to the sleeve of the jacket of his sailor uniform with his fingertips, and without putting anymore thought behind it than the idle assumption that a cat would probably love the smell of fish, he brought it to the tip of Souemon's nose, and at that moment. A streak of light. It was sent flying with the smack of a forepaw, after which Souemon wrinkled his muzzle in what seemed to be displeasure, and Sakuya was left dumbfounded, blood oozing out from the scratch on the tip of his finger.

source.japanese: 更に朔屋を不安定な気分にさせたのは、離れたところで寝網を吊るし干しにしていた下級水夫の、仕事もせずにだべっていた朔屋を見咎めたか、先程からちらちらと横目を送ってきていたのだが、急ぎ足に寄ってきて、
source.english: What made Sakuya still more uneasy was a junior sailor hanging hammocks to dry some distance away. Perhaps noticing Sakuya chatting rather than working, he had been casting sidelong looks. Now he hurried over.

target.text: And what left Sakuya even more unsettled was how the deck boy who had been hanging up his hammock to dry a little ways away, and perhaps he had spotted Sakuya idly chatting instead of working, for he'd been sending sidelong glances at him for a while, was now making his way over to them in a hurry,

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「今の話、本当？　朔屋さん？」
source.english: “Is that story true, Mr. Sakuya?”

source.japanese: 真に迫った眼差しで、であり、口ぶりも懸念に硬い、上目遣いの（といっても眼差しは前髪の奥で窺えないのだが）下級水夫に、かえって鼻白む思いで朔屋、
source.english: The sailor's gaze was urgent and his voice rigid with concern. He looked up at Sakuya—though his eyes themselves remained hidden behind his bangs—with such intensity that Sakuya drew back, disconcerted.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「お、おお。本当だとも。でもそれがどうしたさ。
　誰かが魚釣りでもしたか、運んでいた魚を落とすかしたって事だろ？　なにをそんなぎょっとした顔で」
source.english:
“Y-yeah, it's true. What of it?
Someone was fishing, or dropped a fish they were carrying, right? Why look so shocked?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Is what you said just now, is that true? Sakuya-san?」

His eyes held a compellingly authentic intensity, indeed, his tone of voice was also stiff with concern; met with this deck boy giving him a pleading look from beneath his lashes (though with that said, his eyes were hidden behind his forelocks, and so they couldn't actually be seen) only made Sakuya feel all the more disconcerted instead,

【Naomasa】 「Ye-, yeah. It certainly is true. But so what if it is? Maybe somebody went out fishing, and then they probably just dropped the fish they were carrying, right? What's got you looking so startled?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ううん、そうじゃないの。
　あのね朔屋さん……」
source.english:
“No, it's not that. Listen,
Mr. Sakuya…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「No, that's not what I mean. You see, Sakuya-san……」

source.japanese: 憚るように辺りを見回して、語り出すのがひそひそと、それ立ち聞きを恐れたか、また恐れたとしても何者を遠ざけんとしたのか、朔屋達の周りを時ならぬ影が包んだ、いや影より濃い、暗闇だ。ぼ、と籠もった音で点ったと見れば丸くおぞましやかに据わる、百目蝋燭の炎なので。宗右衛門の黒い毛並みも闇に沈んで、双眸に宿した火灯りだけが炯々と物凄い。
source.english: He glanced about as though afraid to speak, then began in a whisper. Did he fear an eavesdropper? Even if so, whom was he trying to keep away? An untimely shadow enclosed them. No, something denser: darkness. A muffled puff, and the flame of a hefty thirteen-ounce candle sprang up, round and hideously steady. Soemon's black coat sank into the dark. Only the reflected fire in his eyes shone fiercely, terribly.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわわ、なんだいきなりこれ、暗くなったぞ」
source.english: “Whoa, what's this all of a sudden? It's gone dark!”

target.text: He looked around as if hesitant, and when he spoke, it was in hushed tones; was he that afraid of someone eavesdropping, but even supposing he was afraid, what was it he sought to keep at bay; unexpected shadows began to envelop Sakuya and his surroundings, nay, it was deeper than shadow, it was pure darkness. A muffled whoosh sounded, and as he looked around, there it was, fixed in place, circular and ghastly, the flame of a great candle. Souemon's dark coat also sunk into the gloom, and only the blaze in his twin orbs continued to burn with an eerie glare.
【Naomasa】 「Woah, what the hell is all this, it got dark of all a sudden.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「───東山三十六峰草木も眠る丑三つ時───」
source.english: “Across Higashiyama's thirty-six peaks, grass and trees sleep, deep in the hour of the ox…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「───It happened at the witching hour amidst the Thirty-Six Peaks of Higashiyama, when even the plants and trees slumber───」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「蝋燭顔の下から当てんなよ、薄鬼魅悪[わり]ぃなおい」
source.english: “Don't light your face from underneath. Creepy as hell.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Don't light your face from below with that candle, you're looking like some creepy ghost, oi.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「何処で鳴るのか夜陰の鐘が、陰に篭って物凄く───」
source.english: “Where sounds that bell of night, muffled and fearsome…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「From whence doth it toll? The bell of night's shadow, muffled by gloomy dark, groans eerily───」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「それは───とある可哀相な水夫の男の子が、船の通路の隅っこに隠しておいた、カステイラを誰かに盗られてしまった晩の事でございます」
source.english: “It happened on the night someone stole the castella a poor young sailor had hidden in a corner of the ship's passage.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……おい智里、あんたこの前、酒の肴にってちょろまかしてきたアレ……ホントの呑み助は甘味もつまみにするとか吹いてたアレ」
source.english: “…Hey, Tomosato. That thing you swiped to go with our drinks… When you were going on about real drinkers having sweets with booze…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「It all began───one evening, when a certain poor sailor boy, who had hidden his castella cake in a corner of the ship's passageway, had it stolen from him by someone.」

【Naomasa】 「……Oi, Tomosato, that thing you pilfered the other day as a snack to go with our booze……you know, when you started boasting about how a real drunkard can turn even sweets into drinking snacks, that thing.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おお、お前もぶつくさ垂れておきながら、『甘いのう甘いのう』とか俺が一切れ食う間に三切れも平らげたアレか。いやお前、持ってきた俺がいうのもなんだが、よう食えるぜアクアヴィット呑みながら」
source.english: “Ah, that? You complained, but kept saying, ‘So sweet, so sweet,’ and ate three slices while I ate one. Well, I brought it, but even so—how could you eat that while drinking aquavit?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Oh, you mean that thing, the one you chowed down three slices of while I was still on my first, going "so sweet, oh, it's so sweet" even after whining so damn much? Seriously man, maybe I'm not one to talk since I brought it and all, but I'm amazed you could shovel that down while chugging Akvavit.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「───そのカステイラは、男の子が朋輩と一緒に食べようと、ずっと楽しみにしていたとっておきで」
source.english: “That castella was a special treat the sailor had long been saving to share with his friend.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「───That castella was something the boy had cherished, that he was really looking forward to eating later together with his comrades.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「───なくしてしまったその子は、悔しくて哀しくて情けなくて、ずっとしくしく泣いていたそうでございます───朔屋さん、智里さん、僕、後でお話があります。ありますからね？」
source.english: “Losing it left him bitter, sad, miserable. He cried softly for a long time… Mr. Sakuya, Mr. Tomosato, I'll have a word with you later. I will.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「───And having lost it, that boy was so overcome with regret, sorrow, and misery that he wept softly for a long, long time, or so the story goes───Sakuya-san, Tomosato-san, I have something I need to talk with you two about after this. I really do, okay?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「───さておいて、その子は悔しさに夜も眠れない、だから当直を友達と替わって、ずっと物見櫓に立ってたけれど」
source.english: “In any case, the sailor was too upset to sleep. He traded watches with his friend and spent the whole night in the lookout tower.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「───Setting that aside, that boy was so disappointed that he couldn't even sleep at night, and so he swapped watch with a friend, simply standing atop the watchtower the whole time.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「真夜中、日も替わってから丑三つ時───ふっと身震いがして、辺りを見回した時の事でした。とっても静かな夜です。魘されて甲板を駆けずり回る酔っ払いもありません」
source.english: “After midnight, deep in the hour of the ox, he suddenly shivered and looked around. It was a very quiet night. Not even a drunkard racing over the deck in the grip of nightmares.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「When the clock struck midnight, in the dead of night after the date had changed───his body suddenly began to tremble, and he cast his eyes about his surroundings; that was when it happened. It was a very quiet night. There were no drunkards tormented by nightmares running madly across the deck.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「なんだかあまりの静かさにその子は、すこうし、そうほんの少しだけ怖くなって、身を縮めました。それに気のせいでない───」
source.english: “The silence made the sailor a little—yes, only a little—afraid, and he drew in upon himself. Nor was it his imagination…”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「潮も穏やか、風もないのに、真実空気が、二度三度冷えていたのです。なんだかおしっこにも行きたい感じです」
source.english: “Calm sea, no wind, but truly the air had grown two or three degrees colder. He rather felt he needed to pee too.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「And in that silence so overwhelmingly quiet, that boy began to feel a little, yes, just a tiny little bit afraid, and he shrank into himself. And it was no figment of his imagination───」
【Deck boy】 「Although the tide lay calm, no wind stirred, in truth, the air grew colder by two or three degrees. He began to get the urge to go pee for some reason.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「櫓から四方八方見渡しても、海は打ち出しの銀のお盆みたいに静かだし、船も岩陰も見えません。
　ちょっとくらいいなくなっても平気だと───」
source.english:
“Looking from the tower in every direction, he saw a sea quiet as a hammered silver tray. No ships, no rocks.
He'd be all right going away just a little while…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Although he looked out over it in all directions from atop the watchtower, the ocean was as quiet as a hammered-out silver tray, with not a shadow of a ship or rock to be seen. It would be fine if he left for just a little moment, he thought───」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「その子は急いで櫓[やぐら]を降りました。
　でもその時に気づくべきでした。さっきまでは水平線まで見渡せていたのに、いつの間にか霧が出ていた事に───」
source.english:
“He hurried down from the tower.
But he should have noticed then: a moment before he could see to the horizon. Without his knowing, mist had come…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「The boy hurried down from the watchtower. But he should have noticed it in that moment. For although the horizon had been clear to his eyes just moments before, before he knew it, a mist had rolled in───」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おいおい、聞かせるねぇ」
source.english: “Hey, you know how to tell it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それからそれから。おい、どうなったのよ」
source.english: “And then? And then? Hey, what happened?”

source.japanese: 男三人猫一匹、蝋燭の揺らぐ炎を語りの標に暗闇道中、猫の眸[ひとみ]が陰気に寄り来る人魂めいて怪の気配を、醸し出す。
source.english: Three men and one cat journeyed through darkness, the flickering candle their guide through the tale. In the cat's eyes, something uncanny gleamed like a gloomy approaching ghost-fire.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Damn, you really know how to spin a yarn.」
【Naomasa】 「What then, what then? Oi, what happened after that?」

Three men and a cat on a journey through the dark, narration guided by the flickering flame of a candle, the cat's eyes glimmering like sinister ghost-lights creeping nearer, exuding an eerie atmosphere.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「水夫のその子はもちろんすぐに戻るつもり、退屈な見張りだけど穴を開けてはいけません───でも本当は、いきなり冷えだした空気が奇妙で」
source.english: “Of course the sailor meant to come straight back. Lookout duty may be dull, but you must not leave the post empty… In truth, though, that sudden cold had unsettled him.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Naturally, that sailor boy meant to return to his station immediately, and though it was a boring watch, it couldn't just be left unattended───but in truth, he simply found the sudden chill in the air to be uncanny.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「だから小走りに、トイレに急いで、さっさと用を足して上に戻りたくって───不思議な事に、通路では物音一つしなかった」
source.english: “So he trotted to the toilet, wanting to finish quickly and get back above… Strangely, not a sound came from the passage.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「And so he jogged, hurrying to the toilet, wanting to get his business done with and return as quickly as he could───but curiously, the passageway was quiet as the grave.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「いつもなら、たいてい誰かが夜なべ仕事をしています。誰かとすれ違う事もある、なのにその晩は───」
source.english: “Normally someone is working late. You might pass someone. Yet that night…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Ordinarily, there was usually somebody up working late at night. He would even pass by somebody on the way sometimes, yet on that night───」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「誰もいないし、あたりはシンと静まり返っているし、その子は心細くなりました。足も段々にぶります。と通路の向こうで……！」
source.english: “No one there. Everything utterly still. The sailor grew uneasy. His steps slowed. And then, down the passage…!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「There was no one to be found, all around him had fallen deadly silent, and the boy grew disheartened. His legs gradually began to shake. And then, at the far end of the passageway……!」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ずる……っ、ぺた……。
　　　　　ずる……、ぺた……っ」
source.english:
“Drag… Slap…
Drag… Slap…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Shhrrllrrp……, squelch……. Shhrrllrrp……, squelch…….」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「声に直せばこのような、でも本当はもっと、なんとも言えない音で、
　ずる……っ、ぺた……。
　　　　　ずる……、ぺた……っ」
source.english:
“That's how I'd put it into words. In truth it was more indescribable than that.
Drag… Slap…
Drag… Slap…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ホントかそれ……
　おどかしっこなしだぜ……」
source.english:
“Is this really true…?
No scaring us just for fun…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「When rendered in the human voice, it would be something like this, but in reality, the sound was stranger by far, indescribable, shhrrllrrp……, squelch……. Shhrrllrrp……, squelch…….」
【Naomasa】 「Is that actually true…… Stop trying to spook me here……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「お前さん、なかなか巧い。で、どうなったよ」
source.english: “You're pretty good at this. What happened then?”

source.japanese: 実際下級水夫の声の上げ下げ間の取り方は絶妙で、男二人は他愛もなく語りに引きこまれ、一人は怖々と、一人は感興に先を促し、顎下からの火灯りが置く翳[かげ]も不気味を手伝った。
source.english: Indeed, the junior sailor's rising and falling voice, his timing, were exquisite. The two men were easily drawn into the tale. One urged him on fearfully, the other with delight. Shadows cast by the light beneath his chin helped the eeriness.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Buddy, you're pretty great at this. So, what happened then?」

In truth, the fluctuations of the deck boy's tone and the cadence of his pauses were exquisite; the two men had been completely hooked by the silly narration, one fearfully, the other urging him to continue out of interest, and the shadows cast by the firelight from beneath the boy's chin also added to the eerie atmosphere.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
