「冷気はいよいよ増すばかり、気づけば通路にも低く霧が渦巻いて、その向こう、通路の角の向こうから、
　ずる……っ、ぺた……。
　　　　　ずる……、ぺた……っ」
source.english:
“The cold kept growing. Then he noticed mist swirling low in the passage too. Beyond it,
beyond the corner… Drag…
Slap… Drag… Slap…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「The chill was only intensifying, and by the time he noticed it there, the passageway had already been fully enshrouded in a low-hanging fog, and over there, from around the corner of the passageway, shhrrllrrp……, squelch……. Shhrrllrrp……, squelch…….」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「もうその頃には水夫のその子は、おしっこだけじゃない、もっと別の寒気と震えで足が止まってしまって、またこの船の通路の灯りときたら、切れかかっているところもあちこちで」
source.english: “By then the sailor had stopped. Not only because he needed to piss: another chill, another trembling held his feet. And the lights in this ship's passageways—some are always on the verge of going out.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「His steps faltering, the sailor boy now shivered not just from the urge to pee, but also another kind of chill, and the lights in the ship's passageway were flickering here and there, on the verge of dying.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「そんなちらちらする灯りの向こうから、影が、音が、影が───大きくなって」
source.english: “From beyond those flickering lights came a shadow, a sound, a shadow… Growing…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「And from beyond those flickering lights they came, the shadows, the sounds, the shadows─── they grew larger.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「その子はもう動けない、影が大きく、跫音もいよいよ近く、そしてとうとう───
　ああとうとう───！」
source.english:
“He could no longer move. The shadow grew larger, the footsteps drew nearer, and at last—
Ah, at last—!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「The boy could no longer move, the shadows growing larger, the footsteps drawing ever closer, and then, at last─── aah, at last───!」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「───僕の話は、ここでお終いです───」
source.english: “My story ends here.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょ、なんだいそりゃあ！
　そこまで引っぱっといて」
source.english:
“Hey, what the hell!
You led us all that way…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「───This is where my tale ends───」
【Naomasa】 「Wha-, what the hell, man! You can't just string us along like that!」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「だって仕方ないんだものっ。
　覚えてるのは、ぬっと出てきたのもなんだか影ではっきりしなくって、ぬらぬらした感じくらいしかわからなくって……！」
source.english:
“Couldn't help it!
All I remember is something looming out, shadowy and indistinct. Only that it seemed wet and slippery…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But what am I supposed to do about that?! I only remember that thing suddenly looming out from the dark, but it wasn't really clear in the shadows, and all I could make out was that slimy, wet sensation……!」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あとはなんだか生臭かったのと、気づいてみれば『それ』が出てきたあたりに、ちらちら散らばっていた鱗[うろこ]とねばねばと」
source.english: “And a fishy smell. Then I noticed scales scattered about where ‘it’ had appeared, and slime.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「After that, I thought it smelled kind of fishy, and when I came to my senses, I noticed something gooey and those scales scattered around where『that thing』 had emerged from.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ほら、朔屋さんがさっき見せてたあの鱗[うろこ]と、ちょうど同じようなの」
source.english: “Just like that scale you showed us, Mr. Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あれか……」
source.english: “That…?”

source.japanese: 最後の最後で話の落としを透かされて、消化不良に下級水夫へ食ってかかった朔屋だったが、人伝えの怪談と聞いていたところに我が身と繋がって、なんとのう慄然とした心地を催す。朔屋が思い出すに、昨夜も確かに、唐突の冷気と狭霧にあってあの鱗[うろこ]を見出したのだから。
source.english: Denied the story's ending at the very last, Sakuya had snapped at the junior sailor in dissatisfaction. But what he had taken for someone else's ghost story now connected to himself, and a shudder crept through him. Last night, indeed, sudden cold and mist had accompanied his finding those scales.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Look, it was the exact same as that scale that Sakuya-san showed off just a moment ago.」
【Naomasa】 「That thing……?」

When the conclusion of the tale was ruined at the very last moment, Sakuya lashed out from a frustrated lack of understanding at the deck boy, but when what he had taken for a mere ghost tale passed from mouth to mouth turned out to be connected directly to himself, it stirred an inexplicable shuddering dread within him. For in Sakuya's recollection, certainly, there had, in fact, been a sudden chill and mist last night when he found that scale.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「まあこの、浮いてる方がおかしなくらいの襤褸船だ。幽的の一つや二つ寄ってきたって不思議はあんめえが」
source.english: “Well, it's a wreck of a ship. Stranger that it floats at all. Wouldn't be surprising if a ghost or two came round.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Well, this wreck of a ship is so ramshackle, it's a wonder it floats at all. Wouldn't be all that strange for a spirit or two to make their way here.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ともかく、うかうか話に聞き惚れたが、いい加減あっちいな」
source.english: “Anyway, got carried away listening. It's getting damn hot.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Anyways, I did end up letting myself be drawn into the tale, but I am just about fed up with this heat.」

source.japanese:
言うなり智里は、自分達を覆う暗闇に手を翳[かざ]して一ふるい、と、颯爽、闇の帷[とばり]はたちまち晴れ渡って、三人と一匹は眩い陽光の下に立ち戻る、陽差しは目に沁みて猫も瞳孔を細くした。
　なにも殺し屋の手練の業が闇を切り払ったのではない、他の生命を断って世過ぎとする手がそんな赫灼たる光輝をまとうはずもない、なんの事はないのである。
　朔屋達の周りに下級水夫達が四人五人、黒布で四囲を囲って天辺に蓋し、暗室造っていただけの事。なんぼなにが起こったとて不思議はない海の上でも、俄か怪談に合わせて陰々滅々と底冷えの闇夜が垂れこめたりはする筈もなく、蝋燭を吹き消した下級水夫はわざわざ火を傍にしていたせいで顔にはふつふつと汗、顎先から滴った。
source.english:
As he spoke, Tomosato raised one hand toward the darkness enclosing them and swept it aside. At once the black curtain cleared. Three men and one cat returned to dazzling sunlight. It stung their eyes; even the cat narrowed his pupils.
No assassin's art had cut away the dark. Hands that made their living severing lives could hardly be clothed in such radiant glory. Nothing of the kind.
Four or five junior sailors had simply enclosed the group in black cloth on every side and above, making a darkroom. However many strange things might happen at sea, a gloomy, bone-chilling night could hardly descend on cue for an impromptu ghost story. The narrator blew out his candle. Having kept it so close, he now wore beads of sweat across his face and dripping from his chin.

target.text: No sooner had Tomosato spoken than he raised his hand towards the dark that shrouded them and shook it once, gallantly, the veil of darkness instantly clearing up, the three men and one cat returning to the light of the sun, the rays stinging their eyes, even the cat's pupils constricting. The murderer had not cleaved through the darkness by means of some artful technique; those hands of his, making a living by cutting short the life of others, could never be enveloped in such brilliant radiance; it was nothing worth mentioning at all, really.

There were four, no, five deck boys surrounding Sakuya and company; they had simply created a darkroom by enclosing them on all sides with a black cloth, then covering the top. Even though they were out to sea where it wouldn't be strange for anything to happen, there was surely no way that the bone-chilling dark of night would descend in all its oppressive gloom merely to match an impromptu ghost story, and because the deck boy who had blown out the candle had also intentionally placed the candle right under himself, sweat flowed down his face, dripping down from the tip of his chin.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おう、演出ご苦労。
　ちいとばかり蒸し暑いのが玉に瑕[きず]だったがよ」
source.english:
“Yeah, thanks for the staging.
Bit too muggy. That was the only flaw.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なにしてんの君ら」
source.english: “…What are you doing?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Hey there, great work with the performance. Only fly in the ointment was the air being just a little too sultry.」
【Naomasa】 「……What are you guys doing?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「わあ、めっかったぁ～～」
source.english: “Ahh, caught us!”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Waah, they caught us～～」

source.japanese: ばれるばれないの問題ではないと思われるのだが、下級水夫達は四方に蜘蛛の子と散った、が一人はすぐにぶつかって弾き返され、鼻を押さえて仰ぎ見れば立ちはだかっていたのは壁ならぬ水夫長の、壁より始末が悪い。
source.english: Not really a question of being caught or not, one would think. The junior sailors scattered like baby spiders. One promptly collided with something and bounced back. Clutching his nose, he looked up. Not a wall: the boatswain. Far worse.

target.text: Being found out or not didn't really seem like the problem here to him, but the deck boys still scattered in all directions like baby spiders, however, one of them immediately ran into something and was repelled backwards, and as the boy looked up while holding his nose, what stood in his way was no wall; it was the Bosun, and that was far worse than any wall could ever hope to be.

source.japanese: 尻餅ついた水夫も弾かれたように起きあがって脱兎、の、水夫長は腕組みしてどっしり巌のよう、吊り上がった口の片端もこめかみに浮いた血の筋もひくひく引くと。
source.english: The fallen sailor sprang up and bolted like a rabbit. The boatswain stood with arms folded, solid as a boulder. One upturned corner of his mouth and the blood vessel at his temple twitched.

target.text: The sailor who had fallen on his backside jumped up as if propelled by a spring and fled like a startled hare, but the Bosun had his arms folded, his stance imposing like a massive boulder, and both the upturned corner of his mouth as well as the swollen veins at his temple twitched convulsively.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なにしてんだかなあお前はいつもいつも。
　てめえにゃ船倉の荷の点検を言いつけておいたと思ったが。さぼるにしても下にひっ籠もっていれば言い訳もついたろうが、のこのこ上甲板で日向ぼっこたぁ良い度胸だな、ええ？」
source.english:
“What the hell are you up to this time? It's always something with you.
I thought I told you to inspect the cargo in the hold. Even if you meant to slack off, you could've made excuses if you'd stayed below. But strolling up to the top deck to bask in the sun? You've got some nerve, don't you?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「って、なんで俺だけ怒られてんの？
　水夫君達は───」
source.english:
“Hey, why am I the only one getting yelled at?
The sailors—”

source.japanese: さっさと物陰に隠れて、にやにやしながら。
source.english: Already hidden behind things. Grinning.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ほんじゃ智里は───」
source.english: “Then Tomosato…”

source.japanese: 機敏に間合いから離れて、船縁に身を凭れて雲の形などを数えている風情で。
source.english: Nimbly out of reach, leaning against the gunwale, apparently counting cloud shapes.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「And just what the hell is this? It's always, always the same with you. Here I thought I'd already ordered you to go inspect the cargo in the hold. Even if you were just gonna slack off, had you hidden away somewhere below, then you could have at least come up with some excuse, but you have some balls to go shamelessly bask in the sun here on the upper deck, hmm?」
【Naomasa】 「Wait, why are you only getting mad at me? The sailors───」
Hurriedly hid in the shadows, smirking all the while.
【Naomasa】 「Well then, Tomosato───」
Had nimbly withdrawn from striking distance and was leaning against the gunwale with the air of someone idly counting the shapes of the clouds.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「てめえにゃ下っ端の心得手ぇ奴を、も一度叩っこんでやんねえと駄目なようだな……とはいえ」
source.english: “Looks like I have to beat the rules of being at the bottom into you again… Still…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Looks like I'm gonna need to beat the mindset of a low-ranking underling into your bones one more time……although.」

source.japanese:
めしりと節が軋むくらいに握りしめられた拳に朔屋は一瞬絶望したものの、すぐに緩められて禿頭の刺青をぼりぼり掻[か]いたのに、やや気が緩む。
　
　けれど。
source.english:
The boatswain's fist clenched so hard its joints creaked, and Sakuya despaired for a moment. Then the hand relaxed; the boatswain scratched at the tattoo across his bald scalp, and Sakuya relaxed a little too.
But—

target.text: For an instant, Sakuya despaired at the sight of his fists clenching so hard even the joints creaked and groaned, but he loosened them at once, and as he noisily scratched at the tattoo on his bald head, he eased up a little. However.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まあここんとこ、夜な夜な得体の知れねえヤツが船ン中ぁうろうろしてるのは、どうやら本当らしい」
source.english: “Seems it really is true. Something unknown's been wandering round the ship every night lately.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え……水夫長も？」
source.english: “Huh… You've heard about it too, Boatswain?”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ああ。っても俺は直で見た訳じゃあねえが、水夫達には何人も見たり聞いたりしたのがある」
source.english: “Yeah. Haven't seen it myself, but several sailors have seen or heard it.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well, seems like it's true after all. That lately, there's been some shady guy loitering around the ship night after night」
【Naomasa】 「Huh……you too, Bosun?」
【Bosun】 「Yeah. That said, I haven't seen it directly myself, but several sailors have seen or heard it.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ただどいつも、跫音を聞いたり影を見たりで終わっててな。正体を確かめた奴がいねえ」
source.english: “Only footsteps and shadows, though. Nobody's checked what it actually is.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「But no matter who it was, it always ended with hearing footsteps or seeing a shadow. There's nobody who has confirmed its true identity yet.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まあどうせ、ふざけた馬鹿が船のどっかに忍びこんでるとかってオチだろうが、なんにしたってそういう馬鹿にはちっとばかり『船内規約』て奴を教えて差し上げんとなあ……」
source.english: “Probably some fool sneaked aboard somewhere. Whatever it is, that sort of idiot needs a little instruction in the ‘shipboard regulations’…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はあ。密航者。この船に。はあ。
　心当たりが一人ないでもないが」
source.english:
“Ah. A stowaway. On this ship. Ah.
Can't say nobody comes to mind.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well, I'm sure the only punchline here is gonna be that some idiot who thinks he's funny is sneaking around somewhere on the ship, but one way or another, idiots like that need to be taught a little bit about what we call the『Shipboard Rules』……」
【Naomasa】 「Yes. A stowaway. On this ship. Yes. It's not like my mind's completely blanking on who it could be, but.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「奇遇だな。俺もだ。
　だが今回のは奴とはどうにも様子が違う」
source.english:
“Funny, me too.
But this one's nothing like her.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ですなあ」
source.english: “Indeed.”

source.japanese: 朔屋も水夫長もこの時額の先あたりに一人の娘の姿を思量していたのだが、そういえばここしばらくあの娘は絶えて船内に見えない。先だっての寄港の際にまたもしつこく船下層部をうろちょろしていたところを発見され、舳先の棒に蓑虫吊りの刑にされて行方不明になって以来それだ。たとえよし船内に舞い戻ってきていたとしても、密航、といって実際にはそう簡単事ではなく、船底の隔壁の鉄骨の隙間に引っかかって身動き取れないままに乾涸らびていたり、横揺れに崩れた積み荷の下敷きになって熨しイカじみた様に成り果てていたりというのもあり得る末路の、ただあの娘がそんな結末を従容と受け入れた玉か、といううんざりした思いが朔屋にも水夫長にもある。
source.english: Both had a certain young woman in mind. Come to think of it, she had not appeared aboard for some time. During their recent call at port, she had been caught stubbornly prowling the ship's lower levels again, wrapped up and hung from the bowsprit like a bagworm, and then disappeared. Even had she somehow returned, stowing away was not so easy. One might get caught between the iron frames of a partition in the bilge and shrivel there, unable to move, or wind up flat as pressed squid beneath cargo collapsing as the ship rolled. Yet neither Sakuya nor the boatswain could believe that woman would meekly accept such an ending.

source.japanese:
だが、この度夜の船内を徘徊している何者かは、あの娘とは違うような、というのが船の中で漠然と一致した見解だった。
　それでは別口の密航者があるのか？
source.english:
Nevertheless, the vague consensus aboard was that whatever prowled the ship at night was not her.
Another stowaway, then?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しかし密航たぁいえ、わざわざこの船を選んでですかい？　そんな脳腐れはあの娘以外にはそうそうありはしないと思うんですが」
source.english: “But stowing away on this ship, of all ships? I don't think anyone but her could have a brain that rotten.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What a coincidence. Me too. But whatever it is this time feels completely different from her.」
【Naomasa】 「So it does.」

At that moment, both Sakuya and the Bosun carefully contemplated the figure of a single girl as though picturing her somewhere right before their brows, but come to think of it, the girl had been nowhere to be seen aboard the ship for a while now. Just the other day, when she'd been discovered stubbornly loitering around the ship's lower deck as they made call at a port, she'd been made to undergo the bagworm hanging punishment from the bowsprit, and she'd been missing ever since.

Even if one were to assume that, alright, she'd made her return to the ship, stowing away might sound simple, but in reality, it wasn't quite that easy; you could get stuck in the gaps of the steel frame running through the bulkheads in the bilge, withering away without being able to so much as move your body, or you could be flattened below the cargo collapsing upon you as the ship rolled, reduced to something resembling noshiika. (TN: Noshiika, written "熨しイカ", is a Japanese snack consisting of seasoned, dried squid pressed into a thin, flat sheet.)

All this and more were possible ends, but was that girl really the sort of character who would calmly accept her fate? Such were the exasperated thoughts running through both Sakuya and the Bosun's minds.

However, that whoever it was who was roaming around the ship at night on this occasion seemed different from that girl, that was the vaguely agreed-upon view on the ship. In that case, did they have another stowaway?
【Naomasa】 「But even if you're stowing away, would you really go and choose this ship? That girl aside, I don't think there's a lot of people out there with brains that rotten.」

source.japanese: ───暫時後、余計な軽口が祟って、水夫長の鉄の指先で噛締機よろしく両のこめかみをぎりぎり締めあげられてのたうち回る朔屋があったが、そんな彼に、唾でも吐くように、
source.english: A little later, his unnecessary quip brought its curse: Sakuya writhed while the boatswain's iron fingers squeezed both temples like a clamp. As though spitting upon him, the boatswain said—

target.text: ───Soon thereafter, his needless quip came back to haunt him, for Sakuya writhed in pain as both his temples were squeezed tight between the Bosun's iron fingertips like they were a clamping machine, and to that man, like he was spitting it out at him:

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「まあなんだかわからんままじゃ寝覚めが悪いなあ本当だ。だからよ朔屋、てめえがそいつの正体、確かめてこいや」
source.english: “I won't sleep easy while we still don't know what it is. So, Sakuya—you go find out.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「痛い痛い頭の鉢が割れるぅぅ……って。
　今なんと水夫長」
source.english:
“Ow, ow, my skull's splitting… Wait.
What did you just say, Boatswain?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Now, it'll be hard to sleep at night without knowing exactly what that thing is, that much is true. So, Sakuya, you go and figure out what the hell that thing really is.」
【Naomasa】 「Ow ow my skull is crackiiing……wait. What was that just now, Bosun?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「阿呆面で訊き返すなクソが。てめえがそいつをとっ捕まえてこいっつってんだよ」
source.english: “Don't ask again with that stupid face. I said go catch it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやいやいや、なんで俺がッ。
　一人じゃ怖い……いやいや、もしそいつが乱暴な奴だったら俺だけじゃどうにもならんッス！」
source.english:
“No, no, no! Why me?
Alone, it's scary… No, no, if it's violent, I can't handle it myself!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Don't ask me to repeat myself with that stupid look on your face, damn it. I told you to go catch that thing.」
【Naomasa】 「Wait wait wait, why me!? It'll be scary all alone…… no no, I mean if that guy is violent, then I won't be able to do anything about him just by myself!」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「別に誰かに手伝ってもらったって構わんが」
source.english: “Don't mind if someone helps you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃあ君達……！」
source.english: “Then, you guys…!”

source.japanese: と求めた助け船、物陰の下級水夫達に頼ったけれど、目を逸らした者はまだ良い方で、中には舌打ちしたり敵意もあからさまに手の甲見せて二本指押っ立てている者もあるくらいで、
source.english: He appealed to the junior sailors behind their hiding places. Looking away was the kindest response. Some clicked their tongues, some openly raised two fingers at him, backs of their hands outward in hostility.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「I don't really care if you get somebody to help you out.」
【Naomasa】 「Alright then, you guys……!」

He sought aid, relying upon the deck boys hiding in the shadows, but those who averted their eyes from him were still the better response, for there were also some who clicked their tongues at him, and some even showed him the back of their hand with two fingers thrust up,

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「カステイラ……」
source.english: “Castella…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Castella……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「楽しみにしてたのに……」
source.english: “Was looking forward to it…”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「滅多に食べらんない甘々だったのに……っ」
source.english: “Such a rare sweet treat…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「I was really looking forward to it……」
【Deck boy】 「The sugary sweetness we almost never get to taste……」

source.japanese: いやはや、食い物の恨みは恐ろしい、巡り廻ってどこで砂中に埋まった骨の尖りと足裏を刺すものだか知れたものではない。なら共犯、という主犯の智里だと呑み友達を頼みの綱にすがれば、智里は船縁の上に凭[もた]れるのに退屈しただけならまだしも、その上に雪駄の足で立って傍目に危なっかしいという、相変わらずこの男の言行の脈絡の無さには恐れ入る。
source.english: Ah, resentment over food was terrible. Who knew where it might circle back and prick the sole like a sharp bone buried in sand? His accomplice, then—no, the chief culprit, Tomosato. Sakuya clung to his drinking friend as a lifeline. But the assassin had not merely tired of leaning against the gunwale. He stood upon it in his straw-soled sandals, looking precarious. As ever, the utter lack of connection between the man's words and actions was astonishing.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「智里、あんたなにやってんの!?」
source.english: “Tomosato, what are you doing!?”

target.text: Goodness gracious, a grudge held over food is a terrifying thing; you never know when it will come back around and bite you, like a sharp bone buried in sand piercing the sole of your foot. Then what of his accomplice, or rather, the principal offender? He tried to cling to his drinking buddy Tomosato as his last ray of hope, and it would have been one thing if Tomosato had merely leaned against the gunwale in boredom, but on top of that, he stood on the edge in his setta sandals, the whole thing looking downright dangerous to any outside observer, and as ever, the lack of coherence in this man's words and actions was an awesome thing to behold.
【Naomasa】 「Tomosato, what do you think you're doing!?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「朔屋よ、その夜の見回りとやらにゃ付き合えねえぜ。もちろん面倒くせえてのもあるが、俺ゃ少しこの船を離れんのよ。また戻ってはくるが」
source.english: “Sakuya, can't join you on that night patrol. Sure, partly because it's a pain, but I'm leaving the ship for a bit. I'll be back.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Hey Sakuya, can't join you on your nightly patrols or whatever. It's also because it would be a pain in the ass, sure, but I'll be taking my leave from this ship for a little while. I will be back again though.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「なんしろてめえを叩っ斬ってやんねえとならんしなあ……ても、しばらく後回しだ。
　じゃあな」
source.english:
“Have to cut you down, after all… But that'll wait a while.
See you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやお前、待てなにを───!?」
source.english: “Hey, you, wait! What are you—!?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「I still have to chop you down at some point, after all……but that'll have to be postponed for now. Later.」
【Naomasa】 「No, you-, wait, what are you───!?」

source.japanese: ひょいと敷居でも跨[また]ぐかに気易に踏み出して一歩、宙には当然踏む足下もなく、袴が靡[なび]いて袂[たもと]がはためいた、智里は実に平然と海に墜ちていなくなった。平然と落ち着き払っているのは、崖っぷちからおさらばする覚悟の自殺者だってそうである。朔屋とさすがに水夫長も泡を食って船縁に飛びついた、で見下ろせば白く泡の弾けて、けれどこれは船殻が切り裂く波濤で、人を呑みこんだものではない。
source.english: He stepped out as casually as crossing a threshold. Naturally there was nothing to stand on in the air. His hakama streamed, his sleeves flapped, and Tomosato calmly fell into the sea and disappeared. Someone resolved to commit suicide off a cliff could be just as calm. Sakuya and even the boatswain panicked and sprang to the gunwale. Below, white foam burst—but it belonged to waves cut by the hull, not to water that had swallowed a man.

target.text: He took a relaxed step forwards like he was nimbly striding over the threshold of a door, and naturally, his feet found no purchase in the air; his hakama swayed, his sleeves fluttered, and Tomosato fell into the ocean with absolute equanimity, then vanished. Even a determined suicide victim saying his goodbyes from the edge of a cliff remains calm and composed. Sakuya and even the Bosun leapt at the gunwale in a panic, and when they looked down, there was a burst of white foam, but it was from billowing waves rent asunder by the hull of a ship, not a person being swallowed by them.

source.japanese:
見れば───信天翁号の船腹にはいつの間にやら一層の屋形船───そう、胴の間に小間と屋根を備えたあれだ───が接舷し、智里はその舟の舳先辺りに身も軽く飛び移っていたのであった。
　起きあがって船を見上げて、手を上げてひらひらひら。呼びかけてきた声は波にも消されずよく透った。
source.english:
Only then did they see it: a roofed pleasure boat had somehow drawn alongside the Albatross—the sort with a little cabin and roof amidships. Tomosato had landed lightly near its bow.
Straightening, he looked up at the ship and waved. His voice carried clearly, undrowned by the waves.

target.text: As he looked closer───by the hull of the Albatross, without anyone having realized, a single-deck yakatabune─── indeed, the kind with a small roofed chamber built into the midship section ───had come alongside, and Tomosato had lithely jumped down and landed on that ship's bow. (TN: A yakatabune, written "屋形船", is a type of Japanese pleasure vessel with a tatami room resembling a pavilion built in the midship section, known as the dounoma, written "胴の間". It is used for sailing down rivers and was historically used by wealthy merchants or aristocrats for private banquets or other events.)
He got up, looked back up at the ship, raised a hand, then waved with it. The voice calling out to them was not drowned by the waves, piercing through the noise with crystalline clarity.

source.japanese:
【智里】
『……ってなわけでちょっと出かけてくるわ水夫長。また乗りこませてもらうが、出迎えなんぞは御免だぜ───』
source.english: ‘…So I'm off for a bit, Boatswain. I'll come aboard again. No welcoming party, though.’

target.text: 【Tomosato】 『……And so with that said, I'm heading out for a bit, Bosun. I'll be helping myself aboard the ship again at some point, but spare me any formal welcomes───』

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「誰がお出迎えなんぞ！
　戻ってこんでもええわぁ！」
source.english:
“Who'd throw you a welcoming party?
Don't bother coming back!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あいつ……逃げやがった……？」
source.english: “He… ran away…?”

source.japanese:
毒づく水夫長を傍らに、朔屋は安堵するべきか怒るべきか判別しがたい面持ちで屋形船が離れていくのを呆然と見送って、一体この時代にそしてこんな洋上に屋形船、いくら夕べのうちはまだ港の沖合に停泊していたとはいえ、今では相当に距離が開いている、そして停まってもいない信天翁号によくあれだけひたりと寄り添った、それにそれに、船頭は墨染めの僧衣の、どうやら女らしい、それも奇妙な面を被った。変な男には変物の同類が寄るものなのだろうと納得できるようでできないような。
　わざわざこんなところまできて別の船に乗り換える意味も判らない。疑問符は蜜蜂の群れのように朔屋の頭の中を唸り廻ったけれど、あの殺し屋の行動原理を問うだけ無駄なのだろう。さしもの水夫長も同じ心地だったようで、海に唾しながら吐き捨てた。
source.english:
With the boatswain cursing beside him, Sakuya watched the roofed boat depart, unable to decide whether to feel relieved or angry. Why a pleasure boat in this day and age, out here at sea? The Albatross had still been anchored off the port last night, yes, but by now they were a considerable distance away. And the Albatross had not even stopped; how had that smaller craft managed to come so precisely alongside? And, and—the boat operator wore black monk's robes, seemed to be a woman, and had a strange mask. Strange men drew strange company: an explanation he could almost accept, yet could not.
Nor did he understand the point of coming all this way to change boats. Questions buzzed round his head like a swarm of bees. There was plainly no point asking what made that assassin tick. Even the boatswain apparently felt the same, spitting into the sea as he spoke.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Who the hell would welcome you back! You don't need to come back at all!」
【Naomasa】 「Did that rat……just run away……?」

Standing next to the Bosun who was spitting his venom, Sakuya had the expression of a man who wasn't sure if he ought to feel relieved or angry as he watched the yashikibune drift further and further away in a daze, but how could a yashikibune, in this day and age, have made it so far out on the sea, for even if they had been anchored in the offing of that harbour last night, they'd made pretty good distance by now, and even with the Albatross not stopping, it still managed to stay right alongside them, and then, and then, also, the boatman clad in the monk's robe dyed all black, she seemed like a woman, and she wore some strange mask.

He could almost accept the idea that eccentrics would naturally gather around a similarly strange man, but not quite. He couldn't understand the purpose behind deliberately coming all the way out here to sea only to transfer to another ship. Question marks buzzed around Sakuya's head like a swarm of honeybees, but it was likely a waste of effort to even so much as attempt to question the principles governing the actions of that murderer. It seemed as though even the Bosun felt the same way, for he spat the following out towards the sea together with a lump of actual spittle.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……なんでこんな沖に屋形船だ。
　わからねえ……あいつだけはよくわからねえ」
source.english:
“…Why a pleasure boat this far offshore?
I don't understand… That man—I just don't understand him.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Why a yashikibune all this way out on the open sea? I don't get it……that guy alone I just cannot figure out.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「でもさー、陸に戻るんなら、昨夜のボートに便乗すれば済む話だよねえ」
source.english: “But if he's going back ashore, he could've just caught last night's boat.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But you know, if he's going back to shore, then he could have just hitched a ride on the boat last night, right?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「なのにわざわざあんな船
　呼び出すなんて、智里さんって
　もしかしてカッコつけたがり？」
source.english:
“Yet he went to the trouble of calling a boat like that…
Could Mr. Tomosato
be someone who likes to make an entrance?”

source.japanese: わらわらと、五月の燕のように舷側に並んで見下ろして首を傾げる下級水夫たちの方が、よほど冷静だったというもので───
source.english: Lined along the gunwale like swallows in May, the junior sailors looked down and cocked their heads. They were far the more composed.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But he still specifically went for a boat like that, summoning it all the way out here, so maybe Tomosato just wanted to look cool?」
The deck boys, flocking forth and crowding the gunwale like swallows in May, leaned over the edge and looked down with curious tilts of their heads; their calm was nothing short of remarkable───

source.japanese:
そしてその鉄鎖のじゃらつきは、鼻を刺す刺激臭も伴って、一層異様さをかきたてた。なんとなれば大蒜をずらずらと束ねた輪っかが上に掛かっていただけに。その大蒜の一つ一つに切れ目が入っているとなっては臭気は真新しく余計にひどい。
　こんな異形が、この夜船内を徘徊しており、もし出くわした者あれば、そいつは恐怖の余りに座尿するかシルバーバックのように胸板をぽこぽこ威嚇に叩いて突っ走りだし、舳先から船尾まで三往復はした挙げ句に泡を吹いてぶっ倒れること間違いなしの、それくらいに人の心に尖った釘でがりがり削る音と臭いは───朔屋から。
source.english:
The chains clattered, and a sharp smell stung the nose, making the apparition stranger still. For over them hung a wreath of garlic, bulb after bulb strung together. Each had been slit open; the smell was fresh, and all the worse for it.
Such a creature prowled the ship tonight that anyone meeting it would surely wet himself where he sat, or pound his chest like a silverback and take off running, making three round trips from bow to stern before collapsing in a froth. That was how savagely the noise and smell scraped at a person's mind, like a sharp nail. Both came from—Sakuya.

target.text: And so the rattling of that iron chain was also joined by an irritatingly pungent stench that stung the nostrils, further intensifying the bizarre nature of the scene. As for the reason, it was simply that a ring of garlic bulbs strung together on a long thread was hung on top of it. And a cut had been made in every single one of those bulbs, making the stink fresh as could be and all the more horrible for it.

Should any happen to encounter this grotesque sight as it prowled the ship at night, would they fall to their knees and piss themselves out of sheer terror, or would they rush forth while banging their chests in a display of intimidation like a silverback? With the sound and smells scraping so relentlessly against the heart like sharp nails, there was no doubt that after making three round trips from the bow to the stern, they'd collapse while foaming at the mouth, and it all───came from Sakuya.

source.japanese:
そして朔屋は。ついに。
　まず胸に掛かっていた鉄鎖、太さが虎を戒める引き鎖ほどもあり長さに至っては二米[メートル]余もある奴を、遂に重さに耐えかね床に叩きつければまた音高い。鎖には鉄材とリベットの不格好な混合体である十字架までも付属していた。次いで大蒜の首輪も打ち捨てる。沁み出した汁が船員服に着いてしまって、朔屋は自分が朝鮮人街の漬け物の樽にでもぶちこまれたかのみじめな気分一杯でまくしたてる。
source.english:
And Sakuya.
At last—at last—he could bear no more. First he hurled down the iron chain hanging from his chest, with another enormous clatter. It was thick enough to tether a tiger and more than two meters long, with a cross attached: a misshapen conglomeration of iron and rivets. Next went the garlic collar. Its juice had seeped onto his sailor suit, and Sakuya, feeling as miserable as if someone had shoved him into a pickle barrel in a Korean neighborhood, began to rant.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「重いわこんなん！
　重いし臭いし役にも立たない。
　くそうシサムにキサラ、
　クロだって悪気はないのかも知れないが」
source.english:
“This thing weighs a ton!
It's heavy, it stinks, and it's no damn use.
Damn Sisam and Kisara.
Kuro too, even if she didn't mean any harm.”

source.japanese: ぼやき、渋面に汗を拭っても独り、咳をしても独り。鉄鎖の騒音も止んで、森閑とした通路は音を寂しく吸いこんで、静かになったはなったがもの侘びしさは余計に際立った。
source.english: He grumbled, wiped sweat from his scowling face—alone. Even coughing—alone. The chains had fallen silent, and the still passage swallowed the little sounds forlornly. It was quieter now, certainly, but all the more desolate.

source.japanese:
鉄鎖も大蒜も、いずれも夜番の独りに耐えかねた朔屋に贈られた物である、贈られたのであるが。
　朔屋は生来の臆病者で、孤独な見回りに援軍を望んだのも当然であれば、すげなく断られたのもこの信天翁号においてはむべなるかな、というところ。
source.english:
The chains and the garlic had both been gifts to Sakuya when he could no longer bear the solitary watch.
Gifts, yes—but. He had always been a coward, so it was only natural that he should ask for reinforcements on his lonely rounds. On the Albatross, it was equally natural that he should be refused without ceremony.

target.text: And then, Sakuya. At long last. It began with the iron chain draped over his chest, as thick as the chains that would bind a tiger, stretching more than two metres long; he finally found himself unable to withstand its weight any longer, and when he slammed it down against the floor, the sound that rang out was also piercingly shrill. There was even an unshapely mixture of iron and rivets forming a clumsy cross attached to that chain. Following that, he also tossed away the necklace of garlic.

The garlic juices that had oozed out had completely stained his sailor clothes, and Sakuya started rattling on in an absolutely wretched mood, feeling like he'd been tossed into a barrel of pickles in a Korean town.
【Naomasa】 「This thing is so heavy! It's heavy, it stinks, and it's not even any help. Screw you, Shisamu and Kisara. Kuro probably didn't mean any harm, but still!」

Even as he grumbled, wiping the sweat off his sullen face, he was alone, and even as he coughed, he was still alone. The noise from the chain had also stopped, the desolation of the still passageway absorbing all sound; certainly, it had fallen silent, though that only made his loneliness all the more pronounced.

The chain and the garlic were both things gifted to Sakuya, who found the loneliness of the night watch hard to bear; they were a gift, yes, but. Sakuya was a natural-born coward, so while it was only natural that he would wish for reinforcements to join him on his solitary patrols, to be brusquely denied in turn was, indeed, only fitting aboard this Albatross; such was the way of things.

source.japanese:
航海士の双子に泣きついたところ、彼女達はその時自室で大きな金盥に水を張って行水中の、昨夜程度の霧雨でも、溜まり水をかき集めれば盥一杯くらいの真水にはなったらしい。
　かわるがわる背中の垢を擦り落としていた双子は、乳房と腰を手拭いで覆っただけの豪快な姿で、朔屋の訴えを一応気の毒そうには聞いていた、一応というのは上辺がたちまち剥がれて、嘲笑混じりに朔屋に押しつけてきたというのが例の鉄鎖である。
source.english:
When he went begging to the twin navigators, they were bathing in their cabin, in a large metal tub. Even last night's drizzle had apparently yielded a tubful of fresh water if they gathered every puddle.
Taking turns scrubbing the grime from each other's backs, they had only towels over their breasts and hips, a magnificent state of undress. They heard Sakuya out with apparent sympathy. Apparent, because the veneer soon peeled away: with barely concealed laughter, they pressed the aforementioned chain upon him.

target.text: When he went to cling to the twins in tears, the girls were in the middle of washing each other in a metal basin they had filled with water in their own cabin, and it seemed that enough water had pooled, even from a light drizzle like last night's, to fill a basin with fresh water when scrounged together. The twins were scrubbing the grime off each other's backs by turns, and with a stirringly glorious appearance, their breasts and hips covered by nothing more than a hand towel, they did ostensibly seem to listen to Sakuya's plea with a show of sympathy; that show, however, proved but a superficial facade instantly peeled away when, with mocking sneers, they pressed that aforementioned chain on Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「やあ気の毒だねえ。でもあたしらはほら、今晩は綺麗々々して、くっさいの落とさなくちゃいけないしさあ」
source.english: “Oh, poor you. But look, we've got to get ourselves nice and clean tonight. Wash off the stink.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Really pains my soul to hear that, it really does. But look, we're scrubbing ourselves sparkling clean tonight, we really need to get all that stink off, you know?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「なんしろ船のお仲間から、『こんなくっさい女と一緒にいて我慢できるのは、鼻が梅毒でもげた奴か、さもなくば』」
source.english: “After all, a certain shipmate told us, ‘The only man who could put up with a woman stinking like that is someone who's lost his nose to syphilis, or else—’”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「For you see, one of our comrades on this ship said 『You'd need nasal syphilis to handle being anywhere near women this stinky, or if not that.』」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「『纏足の包帯解いた足の裏に、鼻面突っこんで股ぐらおっ勃てる特殊変態性欲者くらいしかいない』───
　とかって言われちゃったしさあ」
source.english:
“‘Some kinky freak who sticks his face into the sole of a bound foot when the bandages come off and gets a hard-on.’
That's what he said.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……俺だって、なんぼなんでもそこまでは言ってないような……」
source.english: “Uh… Even I don't think I went quite that far…”

source.japanese: ……昨夜の些細な冗談（と思っているのは朔屋だけ）を、豪く根に持っていると見える。
source.english: They seemed to be nursing quite a grudge over last night's little joke. Little, that is, in Sakuya's estimation alone.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「『You'd need to be the sort of sexual deviant marked by unusual fetishes of the sort that'd leave you with a stiffy from stuffing your snout into the soles of a pair of lotus feet with the bandages undone.』─── We were told something like that.」
【Naomasa】 「……I don't feel like I ever said anything THAT extreme……」
……They still held one hell of a grudge for last night's trifling joke (Sakuya was the only person who thought of it that way), or so it seemed.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「てな訳で夜の見回りは独りで頑張ってちょーだいな。ま、お守りの十字架くらいはつけたげるからさ」
source.english: “So you'll just have to brave the night rounds on your own. We can at least give you a cross for protection.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「And so with that, you go do your best out there on your night patrol, please and thank you. Well, I'll at least give you a cross to wear as a charm.」

source.japanese: とかなんとか首に巻きつけてきた例の鉄鎖は、錆びついて身の丈に余ったし鉄材をぶっ違いに組んでリベットで留めた代物なぞ、十字という形こそ共通していたものの、聖印などと認めてしまうには、あまりに無骨で不細工で鉄塊に過ぎ、素直に鈍器と呼んだ方がよほど相応しい。不審者と遭遇した際には御庭番が用いた万力鎖はだしの威力を発揮するかも知れないが、こんな重荷は担ぎっぱなしでは、それこそ十字架を負わされたメサイアのように背中は曲がる腰は折れる。
source.english: And so forth, as they wound the chain around his neck. Rusted and longer than he was tall, with crossed iron bars riveted together, it shared the shape of a cross but was far too crude, ugly and brutally heavy to pass for a holy symbol. Blunt instrument was much nearer the mark. Faced with an intruder, it might outperform the weighted chains of the shogun's secret guards. But carry such a burden all night and his back would bow, his waist give way, like the Messiah beneath his cross.

target.text: After something to that effect, a contraption formed of lumps of iron held fast in the shape of a diagonal cross with rivets, rusted and far too large for his body, was attached to the chain, and though it shared its form with that of a crucifix, it was much too clumsy and unrefined to be recognized as a holy symbol; ait was far more appropriate to just be upfront about it and call it the blunt weapon that it was.

Perhaps it might demonstrate the might of the manriki-gusari used by the oniwaban when encountering a suspicious person, but being made to carry a load this heavy without respite, his back would warp, exactly like the Messiah made to bear the cross, and his spirit collapse. (TN: The manriki-gusari, written "万力鎖", also known as a kusari-fundo, is a weapon consisting of a chain with a weight attached at the end used in feudal Japan. The oniwaban, written "御庭番", was a special intelligence and spying corps formed by the 8th Shogun Tokugawa Yoshimune during the Edo period.)

source.japanese: かく抗議しようとした朔屋は、シサムとキサラの乳房の一揺すりで部屋から叩き出されて、頬にぶち当たった肉塊の感触はそれはそれで素晴らしかったが鞭打ちになりかけた。結局求めていた助けは得られず、しようことなしに朔屋が次に向かったのはクロの船室である。
source.english: Sakuya tried to protest, only for Sisam and Kisara to knock him out of the room with a swing of their breasts. The flesh striking his cheek felt splendid in its own way, but nearly gave him whiplash. He had obtained none of the help he sought. With little choice, he went looking for Kuro next.

target.text: Thus, Sakuya attempted to protest, but he was thrown out of the room by a single shake of Shisamu's and Kisara's breasts; the sensation of a lump of meat slamming into his cheek was a wonderful experience in its own right, but it was almost like being beaten with a whip. Ultimately, he did not obtain the help he was looking for, and so, with no other recourse, Sakuya's next destination was Kuro's cabin.

source.japanese: もとよりかかる事態の勃発する時、憤懣のはけ口として遣り玉に挙げられるのはいつも船長クロであり、今日はたまさか朔屋が上甲板に居合わせた為にその役を押しつけられた───そう信じているあたり朔屋もなかなかにクロを適当に扱っているが、ともかくあの白子の娘が役立たずであろうと舌足らずであろうと、独りで夜番を回るよりはずっと良い。
source.english: Whenever this sort of trouble arose, Captain Kuro usually served as the scapegoat upon whom everyone's resentment could be vented. Today, Sakuya happened to be on the upper deck and had the job thrust upon him instead—or so he believed, which showed how casually he too treated Kuro. Whatever else, useless and tongue-tied though the slight albino woman might be, she would be far better company than none on his rounds.

target.text: At the outbreak of situations such as these, it was ever Captain Kuro who was made the scapegoat, the punching bag of their resentment, but today, that role had been pushed onto Sakuya, all as a consequence of him just so happening to be present on the upper deck at the wrong time───the very fact that he believed something of this sort meant that Sakuya's treatment of Kuro was also pretty inconsiderate, but regardless, no matter how useless or inarticulately lisping that albino girl may be, it was much, much better than making the rounds at night by his lonesome.

source.japanese: と朔屋が捜し訪ね当てたクロは。食糧貯蔵庫でいつものように半泣きであった。クロの半べそ顔とやっている事を見て朔屋も泣きたくなった。
source.english: He found Kuro in the food store, half in tears as usual. The sight of her face, and of what she was doing, made Sakuya want to cry himself.

source.japanese: ───ハードタック、というのがある。堅焼きのビスケットないしはクラッカーの意で、いわゆる保存食料なのだが日保ちを利かせる為にそれはそれは堅く堅く焼成され、うっかりそのまま囓ると歯が欠けるわ顎関節症に罹るわの恐ろしい代物なのだが、この磁器紛いの焼き菓子にも挫けず食害する虫がある。蛆だ。人間様でもへこたれるこのハードタック、一名を『蛆の揺りかご』などと呼ぶように、腐敗こそ免れても長い航海の間に実によく蛆がたかった。こんな堅い代物にたかる辺り、蛆ではなくコクゾウムシの幼虫なのかも知れないが、ともかく、古強者の中には虫も良い蛋白源と、ものともせず茶や珈琲などに浸してふやかし諸共に食らった者もあるとはいえ、やはりたいがいの船乗りには忌避されて、さてそれではいかにしてこの蛆虫どもを取り除くか。
source.english: There is a thing called hardtack: a hard-baked biscuit or cracker made for long storage. To make it last, they baked it so very, very hard that anyone foolish enough to bite straight into it risked a broken tooth or a damaged jaw. Yet certain insects refused to be daunted by these porcelain imitations of baked goods. Maggots. Hardtack, formidable even to a human diner, was also known as the ‘maggot's cradle’: it might resist rot, but on a long voyage it attracted extraordinary quantities of larvae. Given what they were burrowing into, perhaps they were actually young grain weevils rather than maggots. In any event, some old hands regarded the bugs as good protein, soaked the lot in tea or coffee, and ate it without a qualm. Most sailors preferred not to. How, then, were the maggots to be removed?

source.japanese:
ハードタックの箱の上に生魚を置いて、蛆虫どもがより新鮮な餌に引っ越すのを待つのである。
　ひどい時には数度生魚を替えなければならなかったというから、堅焼き菓子にたかった虫の数というのは相当なものだったろう。たとえ取り除いたとはいえそんな代物を食わされる船員も気の毒だが、もっと可哀相なのは除去作業を押しつけられる係である事は言うまでもなく、この信天翁号においてはそういった役を振り分けられるのがクロである事も、これも言を俟たない事なのであった。
source.english:
Put a raw fish on the hardtack box, and wait for them to move to the fresher food.
In bad cases, the fish apparently had to be replaced several times; there must have been a prodigious number of bugs in those biscuits. Pity the sailors obliged to eat such things, even after the bugs had been removed. But spare still more pity for whoever was saddled with removing them. Needless to say, aboard the Albatross, such tasks fell to Kuro.

source.japanese: 貯蔵庫の広さはこの船の乗り組み達の胃袋を映してそこそこの奥行きを与えられ、林立する棚と所狭しの木箱と足場を塞ぐ麻袋で、床は辛うじて隙間が残されているくらい。棚と箱と袋は実に高低差に富んだ、玩具の兵隊なら格好の演習場となり得た地形を為し、かつ、そこかしこから干物や香辛料が混ざり合った際どい匂いが溢れ、食料市場の裏路地に迷いこんだかのよう、けして心地好い、とは言えないどぎつい臭いは信天翁号それ自体の船の臭気も加味されて、朔屋はここに入りこむ度（それは殆ど食い物を盗む為であったが）、曰く言い難い感慨に充たされたものだ。
source.english: The storeroom extended a respectable distance, in proportion to the stomachs it supplied. Shelves stood in ranks, wooden boxes crowded every space, and sacks obstructed the footing, leaving scarcely a patch of floor. Shelves, boxes and sacks made a landscape of remarkable elevations and hollows—a perfect training ground for toy soldiers. Everywhere, dried fish and spices mingled into an aggressive stench, as though one had wandered into a back alley of a food market. Hardly pleasant. The ship's own smell seasoned this overpowering mixture, and whenever Sakuya entered—usually to steal food—he was filled with feelings difficult to name.

source.japanese: それは船上暮らしにあっては、新鮮で豊潤な肉や瑞々しい野菜の香気など出港直後でもなければ到底望めないという過酷な現実を突きつけられるからでもあり、同時にこんな忌み嫌われる船にあればあるだけ、みずぼらしい食い物であっても、食べる事それだけで紛れもない快楽になってしまうと知らしめてくるからで。
source.english: Partly because it confronted him with the brutal truth of life at sea: unless they had only just left port, he could scarcely hope for the fragrance of rich fresh meat or succulent vegetables. And partly because it taught him that, aboard this hated ship, simply eating became an unmistakable pleasure, however shabby the food.

source.japanese: さてこの食糧と臭気の迷い森の中で朔屋が見出したクロは、前述したように半泣きでハードタックの箱に生魚を乗せては取り替えるという、文字通り鼻つまみものの仕事にそれは必死であった。
source.english: Within this bewildering forest of food and smells, Sakuya found Kuro, as already noted, half in tears. She was desperately setting raw fish on the hardtack boxes, then replacing them: a job that quite literally made one hold one's nose.

target.text: With that thought, Kuro, who Sakuya searched for and at last tracked down. Was half in tears like usual in the provisions store. And when he saw what had driven Kuro to the verge of crying, Sakuya also wanted to cry.

───It was hardtack. A word that covers anything from hard-baked biscuits to crackers, known around the world as a preserved food, but which is, in an effort to make it last as long as possible, baked to an extreme hardness; a terrifying thing that, if one were to bite into thoughtlessly, one might lose a tooth or come to suffer from a temporomandibular joint disorder, but there are bugs who will still ravage even these porcelain-like baked goods without losing heart. Maggots.

Even noble mankind would falter at the prospect of eating hardtack, but while it avoided spoilage, it would also frequently be swarmed by maggots on longer voyages, to the point it was given the nickname of "worm castles".

Given that they were swarming on something this hard, perhaps these weren't actually maggots but instead maize weevil larvae, but regardless, though some veterans will claim that insects are also a good source of protein, regardless of how some might be undaunted by the prospect of steeping them in tea or coffee or the like and eating it all together in one big slurry, all the same, most sailors are repulsed by the idea; well now, if that is the case, how should one go about getting rid of these maggots?

By placing a raw fish atop the box of hardtack, then waiting for the maggots to move to the fresher feed. It is said that when things were really bad, it was necessary to swap out several raw fish, one after the other, so there must have been a rather significant amount of bugs swarming all over those hard-baked biscuits. Even should they be removed, one would still have to pity the sailor being made to eat such food, but it went without saying that the most pitiful of all would be the one who had the role of removing these bugs foisted upon them, and it also went without saying that, on the Albatross, such roles were assigned to Kuro.

In a reflection of the stomachs of the crew of this ship, the store boasted a respectable amount of depth to its dimensions, it bristled with shelves, was crowded with wooden crates, and jute bags obstructed one's footing to the point there was barely any space left to stand on.

The shelves, crates, and bags were actually of very different elevations, so were one a toy soldier, it would transform into terrain well suited for use as a maneouvering ground, and in addition, when the peculiar smells of the dried seafood or spices wafted from here and there and everywhere and mixed into a heady blend, it was as though one had strayed into a food market in a backstreet, but the actual smell of the Albatross itself, which could not be called pleasant by any means, was added to that mix, so every time Sakuya came here (which was almost exclusively to pilfer something to eat), he was filled with a deep emotion that was difficult to articulate.

This was because his heart was being pierced by the cruel truth that, as long as he lived on a ship, the savoury smells of fresh, rich meat and crispy, juicy vegetables was a delight he could not possibly hope to experience unless it was in the scant days just after setting sail, yet at the same time, even if it was aboard a vessel he so loathed, whatever wretched provisions there may be, he was also forced to realize how undeniable a delight that the mere act of eating in itself had become to him.

Now then, amidst these lost woods of provisions and smells, Sakuya had found Kuro, who, as previously mentioned, was half in tears while replacing the fresh fish placed atop the box of hardtack, desperately fighting tooth and nail to finish a job that anyone would literally hold their nose at.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うっ、うぅぅ……臭いよう。
　お魚の腐った臭いがぷわぁんてくるの」
source.english:
“Ugh… Uuugh… It smells.
The rotten-fish smell comes whooshing up.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uh, uuuh……it stinks. The smell of rotten fish is everywhere.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「うぅ、うぷ、気持ち悪いよう。
　蛆ちゃんがにょろにょろ、ぞよぞよって、
　上がってくる……。
　見てるだけでクロは……っ」
source.english:
“Uuh… Urp… Kuro feels sick.
The maggots come squirming, all wriggly…
up here…
Just looking makes Kuro—”

source.japanese: 蛆で生魚が一杯になるまで、なにも付ききりで侍る事はない。頃合いを見計らって上げればいいので、その間離れていたとしても、それくらいは入口で張り番の下級水夫だって見逃すに吝かでない。臭い不快を除けばこの蛆除け仕事は、実はそれほどの重労働に非ずして、要領を得れば、ながらで居眠りもできれば雑誌を読んだっていい、がその要領を得るこそクロにもっとも欠けたる資質の一つである。おまけにクロは律儀にもずっと俯[うつむ]いて生魚と蛆の塩梅を見張っていたものだから、ただでさえ平衡神経の弱い彼女の事、下を向き続ければもう簡単に船酔いにかかる。傍らに古新聞を敷いたバケツの置いてあるはきっとその用意。
source.english: There was no need to stand over the fish until it was covered in maggots. She could leave and lift it away when the time seemed right; even the junior sailor guarding the entrance would gladly have overlooked an absence in the meantime. Apart from the horrible smell, removing maggots was not particularly strenuous work. Someone who knew how to manage it could nap on the job, or read a magazine. But that knack for getting by was among the qualities Kuro most conspicuously lacked. Worse, dutifully watching the fish and its maggots kept her head bowed the entire time. With her poor sense of balance, looking down for so long was enough to make her seasick. The bucket lined with old newspaper beside her was doubtless there in preparation.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uuh, ulp, it's so gross. The little maggies wriggling, squirming, crawling up……. Just watching makes Kuro feel……」

There was absolutely no reason to wait upon the raw fish with uninterrupted attendance until it was filled with maggots. One could simply make an estimate of the appropriate time and then return later to finish the deed, and even should one decide to leave the store entirely in the meantime, the deck boy standing watch at the entrance would be willing to overlook something so minor.

The smelly unpleasantness of it aside, this maggot removal job was not actually that hard a task, and once you got the knack for it, you could even take a nap while at it, or leaf through a magazine, yet it was precisely acquiring that knack that was one of the most sorely lacking qualities in Kuro. To make matters worse, Kuro had been vigilantly standing watch over the state of the fish and the maggots with utmost sincerity, and with the girl's vestibular nerves being deficient even at the best of times, just continuing to look downwards was enough to make her readily succumb to seasickness.
The old newspaper spread out near her and the bucket placed on top of it were surely preparations made for precisely that eventuality.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、さあ……お前、そんなべったりつきっきりでなくても良いんだぜ、こんなの」
source.english: “Look… You don't have to stick to it that closely, you know. Not for a job like this.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「No, look……you don't really have to hover around it all the time, not for this kind of thing.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「え……だって、もし魚から蛆ちゃん溢れる、するしたら、クロは、つまむの。
　一つ一つ手で」
source.english:
“But… if the maggots spill off the fish, Kuro has to pick them up. One by one.
By hand.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Huh……but then, if the maggies spill out of the fish, then Kuro has to pick them up. One by one, with fingers.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「くにくにって柔らかくて、すぐに潰りる。
　潰れる、すると、指でぐちゃあ……て。
　う、ふ……うぷぅ……っ」
source.english:
“They're all soft and squishy. They squash so easily.
When they squash, it's all mush…
on Kuro's fingers… Uuh… Urp…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「い、言うな、それ以上は判ってても言うな。食いモンあるところで反吐ぶちまけるなっ」
source.english: “D-don't tell me. Even if I know, don't tell me any more! And don't puke where there's food!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「というか、だなあ。なんだって今さらこんなハードタックなんだよこの船にしたって」
source.english: “More to the point, why the hell are we still keeping hardtack? Even on this ship?”

source.japanese:
───朔屋の指摘した通り。いくら前時代からの不埒なはぐれ者のような信天翁というて、さすがに食糧事情は多少の改善を見た。冷蔵施設など言う文明の利器こそ、油と電気と金を食うとて船に積まれる余裕もないが、それでも瓶詰め缶詰めで最低限の栄養は確保されており、壊血病を恐れて、ライム島の初潮前の少女から体液を無惨にも搾[しぼ]りとった、ライムジュースに頼った時代はもう遠い過去。そもそもハードタックなどを恒常的に用いたのは帆船時代だ。
　朔屋にしても、ハードタックを麦酒に浸して……などは古い海洋冒険小説中の一節でしかお目にかかった事もなく、信天翁号に乗りこんで来そこまでの食糧事情の悪化を見た事はない、まだ。
source.english:
—Just as Sakuya had pointed out. The Albatross might be a lawless relic washed up from another age, but even her provisions had improved somewhat. There was no room aboard for such fruits of civilization as refrigeration, gluttons for oil and electricity and money; still, bottles and tins ensured the bare minimum of nourishment. The days when fear of scurvy forced sailors to rely on lime juice—bodily fluids cruelly wrung from the women of Lime Island before their first monthly blood—were long past. Hardtack, after all, belonged to the age of sail.
Even Sakuya had encountered hardtack soaked in beer only in old sea-adventure novels. Since coming aboard the Albatross, he had never yet seen the food situation sink so low.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「All wiggly and soft, squeeze and pop. And when they go squash, fingers get all……slimy. Uh, fh……ulp……」
【Naomasa】 「Sto-, don't say it, I can guess the rest, so stop talking about it. Don't vomit all over the place where we keep the food!」
【Naomasa】 「Actually, you know. Why the hell would they have this kind of hardtack here, in this day and age, even on this ship?」

───It was exactly as Sakuya's critical remark would suggest. No matter how much the Albatross may have seemed like a lawless stray from ages past, as one would expect, the food situation had shown some improvement with the passage of time.

Refrigeration and the likes, the conveniences of modern, civilized life, all consume oil or electricity or money, and so there was no leeway to load something like that onto the ship, but even so, through bottled and tinned food, the minimum of nutritional needs could be covered, and the age where people lived in fear of scurvy, where they had to rely on lime juice, ruthlessly squeezing out the bodily fluids of the premenarchal little girls of Lime Island, was now a thing of the distant past. To begin with, hardtack only saw constant consumption during the Age of Sail.

Even for Sakuya, soaking hardtack in beer or the likes……was something he'd only ever laid eyes on in a single paragraph he'd read in some old nautical adventure novel, and since joining the Albatross, he had never witnessed their food situation deteriorate to such catastrophic levels. Not yet anyway.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ううう、だって、だって。水夫長が、もしもの時があったら、て。みんなに蛆たかりの、このビスケト食わせるか、て」
source.english: “Uuuh… Because the boatswain said, what if something happens? Are you going to make everyone eat these maggoty bis-kits?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「正論っちゃ正論なんだろうが、お前さんにとりあえず仕事を宛がっておこうてぇ方便にしか聞こえないやね、さすがに……」
source.english: “Fair enough, I suppose. But honestly, it sounds more like an excuse to give you something to do…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんな半端仕事なんざうっちゃってさ、クロよう、今晩俺に付き合って欲しいんだが」
source.english: “Chuck that stupid little job, Kuro. I want you to keep me company tonight.”

source.japanese: 生魚になけなしの集中力を注ぎ続けるあまり、腰のない白髪が肩から垂れて魚の腐れ加減の表皮に触れて、そこ伝いに蛆が這い上がってきているにもご存じないクロの、きょとんと顔を向けてきたクロにあらましを説明してやると。
source.english: She had poured her scant powers of concentration into the raw fish so completely that her limp white hair trailed from her shoulders onto its putrefying skin. Maggots were climbing the strands, unbeknownst to her. She turned a puzzled face toward him, and he explained the situation.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Uuuh, but, but. The Bosun said, if the worst happens. if the worst happens. Would you make them all eat these biscuits covered in maggots, he said.」
【Naomasa】 「That's probably sound reasoning, I suppose, but that really just sounds like a convenient excuse to saddle you with some busywork for the time being to me, being honest with you……」
【Naomasa】 「Now abandon this pointless odd job, dear Kuro, for tonight, I wish for you to join me.」

Pouring too much of what paltry concentration she had left into the fish, Kuro remained ignorant of the fact that her wispy, white hair had spilled down from her shoulders and was touching the outer skin of the fish marked by decay, maggots creeping up along it, and as Kuro turned her bewildered face towards him, he explained the gist of it to her.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「夜の見回り……するです、朔屋さん。
　クロも、たいてい空いてる、夜はひとり。
　船室で目をつぶって、
　寝るまでつぶってる」
source.english:
“You're doing the night rounds, Mr. Sakuya?
Kuro is usually free. At night. Alone.
In the cabin, Kuro closes her eyes.
Keeps them closed until she sleeps.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Patrolling……at night, Sakuya-san is. Kuro is also mostly free, alone at night. Closing eyes in cabin, closing them until asleep.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でも今日は。これ、クロ、しないと。
　水夫長に、上甲板のとりいに、お縛りのお仕置きです。されるです」
source.english:
“But today Kuro has to do this.
Otherwise the boatswain ties Kuro to the torii on the upper deck. For punishment.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But today. Kuro, has to do this. Or will be given binding punishment, at torii on upper deck. By the Bosun.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「こないだされたときは、一つしかないのに、鳥居、夜中に増えたり、色がむらさきに変わったりいて、怖くって───」
source.english: “Last time, there was only one torii, but during the night there were more, and they turned purple. It was scary—”

source.japanese: 沈黙。ひたひたと周囲から臭い以外の気配が忍び寄るかの沈黙。
source.english: Silence. A silence in which something besides the smell seemed to be stealing closer from all sides.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだそれ地味におっかねえよ……。
　ともかく、じゃあお前さん、今夜はここを離れる気はないと。一晩中くっせぇ魚と蛆と仲良くしてると」
source.english:
“That's quietly terrifying…
Anyway, you're not leaving here tonight, then. Spending the whole night making friends with stinking fish and maggots.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「When given the other day, there is only one, but the torii multiplied at night, colour changed to purple, was scary───」
Silence. A silence as though something other than just the smell was steadily creeping closer to them from their surroundings.

【Naomasa】 「What the hell, that's actually kind of scary……. Anyways, so you're saying you don't intend to leave this place at all tonight? That you want to hang out with smelly fish and maggots for the whole night?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「魚が臭い、も、蛆ちゃんもほんとは、や。
　前にコレした時、夢見たよ……」
source.english:
“Kuro doesn't like the fish smell, or the maggots.
Last time Kuro did this, she had a dream…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「The fish smells, and really, really don't like maggies. Last time Kuro did this, had a dream……」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロの寝床に、てんじょうから蛆ちゃんがぽた、ぽたって落ちてくる。一杯になって毛布に。その全部が水夫長の顔してて……、
　や、やだぁぁ」
source.english:
“The maggots came plop, plop, from the ceiling onto Kuro's bed. All over the blanket. And every one of them had the boatswain's face…
N-nooo!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だからそれは地味、どころか滅茶苦茶怖いからやめろってーのに……仕方ない。
　そこまで言うんなら、クロはここから離せねえなあ……」
source.english:
“That's not quietly terrifying, that's fucking horrifying! I told you to stop… Oh, well.
If you put it that way, I can't drag you out of here…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「On Kuro's bed, maggies fell down from the ceiling, plop plop. Into bedding full of them. And all of them had the Bosun's face……, no, nooooo!」
【Naomasa】 「Like I said, that's actually kind of-, no wait, that's really damn scary, so just stop……fine then. If you insist that much, then I can't exactly make you leave……」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……ごめん、あさい。
　でもそんなこわい見回り、怖いから。
　朔屋さんには、おまもり。これ」
source.english:
“…Kuro's sorry.
But a scary watch like that… it's scary.
So, Mr. Sakuya, for protection. Here.”

source.japanese: ───で、クロから差し出されたのが例の大蒜の首輪である。こういうのは臭いが魔除けになるのだとちゃんと知ってるクロは賢くて、朔屋が止めるにもかかわらずざくざくと、見ている前で切れ目を入れてよこした。大蒜臭がきつかったのもさりながら、果物ナイフ程度の刃物でもクロが使えば幼児が牛刀を振り回す危なっかしさ、案の定、刃が鈍っていたのが災いしてクロは指に切り傷こさえて大蒜にその不健康な血を吸わせた。いくら薄い血とはいうても、一応、もう一つ一応を重ねてクロは純潔の乙女と言って言えない事もなく、いや、どうなのだろう。腐れ魚と蛆と夜っぴて向き合うこの生き物を、乙女扱いしていいものやらどうやら深い思惟の余地がある。
source.english: What Kuro offered was the garlic collar already mentioned. Clever Kuro knew the smell would ward off evil. Despite Sakuya's protests, she hacked slits into the bulbs before his eyes. The garlic stank badly enough, but even a fruit knife in Kuro's hands was as alarming as a toddler waving a cleaver. Sure enough, the dull blade brought disaster: she cut a finger and let the garlic soak up her unhealthy blood. Thin as that blood might be, Kuro could at least—at least, with the qualification repeated—be called a pure maiden. Or could she? Whether a creature spending all night face-to-face with rotten fish and maggots deserved the designation of maiden was a matter for profound reflection.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Very sorry. But such a scary patrol, is scary, so. Amulet, for Sakuya-san. Here.」

───And so, what was presented to him by Kuro was the aforementioned garlic necklace. Kuro was a clever girl for actually knowing that this kind of thing worked as a charm against smells, and for all that Sakuya attempted to stop her, she still tried to carve cuts in the cloves right before his eyes. While the smell also grew harsher, once Kuro began to wield even a blade no bigger than a paring knife, it was as dangerous as a toddler swinging around a cleaver, and sure enough, the dullness of the blade became her downfall, causing Kuro to make a small cut in her finger, the garlic absorbing her sickly blood.

But no matter how watery and faint her blood may be, one could sort of, well, by layering yet another tentative caveat, it was not wholly impossible to call Kuro a pure maiden, no, I don't know about that. There is room for much deliberation on the subject of whether a creature who would spend the entire night face to face with rotting fish and maggots should ever be regarded as a maiden.

source.japanese: なんにしても朔屋はここでも援軍を諦めなければならず、彼にしてもがっくり肩を落として、保存食料の棚の谷間を退却したわけだが、貯蔵庫を出る前に見張り番の下級水夫が青年の身体検査を敢行したところ、ポケットからオリーブの実の瓶と薫製チーズの包みが発見されて、いつの間に紛れこんだやら、実に実に不思議な事もあったもの。
source.english: Whatever the case, Sakuya had to abandon hope of reinforcements here too. Shoulders sagging, he retreated through the valleys between the stored provisions. But before he left, the junior sailor on guard searched him, and discovered a jar of olives and a parcel of smoked cheese in his pockets. When could they possibly have got there? A very, very mysterious occurrence indeed.

target.text: At any rate, Sakuya also had to abandon his hopes for reinforcements even down here; his shoulder sunk deep in heartbreak, even for him, and so he made his retreat from the valley of the shelves loaded with preserved foods, but before he could leave the storeroom, when the deck boy on watch resolutely carried out a pat-down of his person, what should be discovered in his pockets but a jar of olives and a wrapped piece of smoked cheese, and just when exactly had those managed to slip in there without Sakuya noticing? It truly was a mystery for the ages.

source.japanese:
───およそこれらいくつかの前段が、結局朔屋が船内の独りの深夜番から免れそこなった顛末で、それでも始めのうちは彼女達からの鉄鎖やら大蒜やらを身に着けていたのは、彼にしても心細さに抗[あらが]いきれなかった故、にしても限界というもの、重いわ臭いわ煩[わずら]わしいわ、こんなもの魔は除けていくかもしれないが、それだって畏れて遠ざかるのではなく、相手にしては魔なりの沽券に関わると小馬鹿にして身を遠ざけるのである。
　馬鹿にされ、軽侮せらるるくらいで難事から逃れられるのなら、蔑みを受けるくらいさしたる労でもないと、まこと情けない向きに慣れきった朔屋にしても、わざわざこんな荷厄介を背負いこんでまで、とは至らない。
source.english:
Such, in brief, were the events that had failed to save Sakuya from patrolling the ship alone at midnight. He had initially worn the chain and garlic the twins gave him because he too could not entirely withstand his unease. But there were limits. Heavy, smelly, cumbersome—these things might drive evil away, but not by inspiring fear. Evil would simply sneer and keep its distance rather than compromise its own dignity by dealing with him.
Sakuya was already thoroughly accustomed to the pitiful principle that contempt was no great hardship if being mocked and despised got him out of trouble. Even he, however, saw no reason to shoulder all this extra baggage for the purpose.

source.japanese: こっ外[ぱず]せばなんとも清清とした、身も軽い、病から癒され目覚めた朝に雨戸を開けば外は清らかな一面の雪、その処女雪に足跡残さずに駆け回れそうに腰も軽やか、朔屋は勢いづいてとんとんと、これから一戦交える拳闘家を不遜にも真似て踵[かかと]で跳ねる、通路の前後を眺める。
source.english: Once he stripped it off, what relief! His body felt light. Like waking healed from an illness, opening the shutters onto a pure expanse of snow, and finding himself so buoyant he could run over it without leaving a footprint. Emboldened, Sakuya bounced on his heels, presumptuously imitating a boxer about to enter the ring, and looked both ways along the passage.

source.japanese:
で目にしたのが通路に細い灯りを落とす船室の扉、暖かそうなのにふと覚えたのがなんとも底意地悪いむかっ腹、自分がこんなに苦労しているのに平和そうな光が気に食わない。そっと跫音忍ばせ覗きこめば、下級水夫が二人ばかり古新聞から切り抜き帳を作っているところ。会話から窺うに、新聞内の世界各地の逸話やら珍しい記事やらを集めて、水夫長の活字中毒の餌を集めているのらしい、声は活発で、二人ともこの仕事にそれなりに熱中しているよう。
　で、またむらむらと、湧き上がったのが黒い、それも薄汚れた報復心というから埒が開かない。
source.english:
He saw a thin light spilling through a cabin door. It looked warm, which stirred an extraordinarily petty irritation: he was suffering, and resented that peaceful light. Creeping closer, he peered in. Two junior sailors were making a scrapbook from old newspapers. Their conversation suggested they were collecting anecdotes from around the world, unusual little articles—fodder for the boatswain's addiction to print. Their voices were lively; both seemed absorbed in their task.
Once again something dark welled up in Sakuya, and that something was a grubby desire for revenge. Hopeless.

target.text: ───These several preceding paragraphs described the general course of events that led to Sakuya's ultimate inability to escape from his lonesome late night patrols of the ship; that he had still initially been wearing the chain and the garlic he'd been given by the girls was because even he could not overcome the forlorn unease in his heart, but still, there were limits; it was heavy, it reeked, it was a nuisance, and perhaps one could ward off the demonic with these sorts of things, but that was not because they avoided him out of fear, but rather because just dealing with him would imperil the demon's own good name, and so they would rather scoff at him while keeping their distance.

If being mocked or scorned would be enough to let him escape trouble, then being on the receiving end of some contempt was hardly any trouble at all; so Sakuya thought, but even for him, long inured to such a truly wretched vector of thought, going to the trouble of actually carrying this sort of burden on his back? Now that was a step too far.

Once he threw it off, how remarkably refreshed he felt, his body light; it was like finding his illness suddenly cured after waking up one morning, and as he threw open the storm shutters, the outside was covered in a pure field of snow, and he could run around atop that virgin snow without leaving a single footprint behind, so nimble did his hips feel, and Sakuya, fired up, bounced on his heels with a light rhythm, impudently imitating a boxer about to fight a match, eyes sweeping up and down the passage.

And what caught his eye was a cabin door from which faint light leaked into the passageway, and though it seemed pleasantly warm, what spiteful anger he suddenly felt at that sight; he was out here suffering through such toils, and so he was utterly unable to stomach such a peaceful light.

As he tiptoed his way over and peeked inside, he saw just two deck boys by themselves, making a scrapbook from old newspapers. Based on what he could gather from their conversation, they were collecting interesting anecdotes or rare articles and the sort from all corners of the world found in those newspapers, apparently gathering fodder to sate the Bosun's addiction to the printed word, their voices animated, and both of them seemed quite engrossed in their work. And then, something suddenly welled up within him once more: a black, sullied urge for reprisal, and so this wasn't heading anywhere constructive.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（ほほうそうかいそうかい己ら。
　俺にこんな夜回り押しつけて、そっちゃ楽しそうに水夫長の暇潰し造りかい。
　そうかそうか、お前らも水夫長も───）
source.english:
(Oh, I see. I see how it is, you bastards.
Dump this night watch on me, then have a lovely time making things to amuse the boatswain.
Right. You lot and the boatswain—)

source.japanese:
ルサンチマン───それは虐げられし弱者の怨念、などといえば深い含みに聞こえようが、今の朔屋が燃やしているのはキュルケゴール師も地下で激怒しそうな、見当違いに腐りきった仕返しの一念であり、またこう言う時に限ってこの男、普段なら回らぬ工夫がよく働く。
　通路の隅にバラストと積まれていた土嚢の、死んだ豚の赤子の態を取りあげては逆さにして中の砂をぶちまけ空にして、中に詰めこむ例の鎖と大蒜の束、袋の上からぐりぐりと靴の踵[かかと]で踏みにじった、丁寧にしつこく。
　でそれを、切り抜き帳を制作中の船室の扉をやにわ開けるや、中に叩きこんだ、すぐにバタンと閉じて背を預けて外から封じた。
　中からは、扉に鍵していなかったのを不用心と責めるには酷な、中からは。
source.english:
Ressentiment. Call it the resentment of the oppressed, and it sounds suggestive, profound. What burned in Sakuya now was a thoroughly rotten, misdirected desire to get even, enough to enrage the late Master Kierkegaard in his grave. And at just such moments this man became ingenious, in ways that ordinarily escaped him.
In a corner of the passage lay sandbags used for ballast. He picked one up, shaped like a dead piglet, turned it over, and emptied the sand. In went the chain and the garlic wreath. Through the sack, he ground them beneath his heel, carefully, persistently.
Then he flung open the scrapbook-makers' cabin, hurled the sack inside, slammed the door, and braced his back against it.
Blaming the occupants for leaving it unlocked would have been cruel. From inside came—

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
『な、なにこれぇ……うわ、なんか鼻に刺さった、つんときたぁっ』
source.english: “Wh-what's this…? Ugh! Something stabbed me in the nose! It burns!”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
『ひいい、臭い、臭いよう。
　あ、開けて窓ぉ』
source.english:
“Eeee! It stinks! It stinks!
O-open the window!”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
『ダメこの部屋、窓ははめ殺し、
　う、かは、喉にもきた、
　こほ、こほこほこっ』
source.english:
“We can't, this room's windows don't open!
Urgh… It's in my throat too!
Cough… cough-cough-cough!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （Oh-ho, I see, so that's how it is, you people. You foist this night patrol on me, and then you're in there, seemingly having the time of your life making something for the Bosun to kill some time with. I see, so that's how it is, you people, and the Bosun, too───）

Ressentiment───the profoundly seething anger of the tormented and the weak, and perhaps when put that way, it might sound as if it has deeper implications, but what burned through Sakuya's soul was sure to make Kierkegaard roll in his grave with fury, for it was but a solitary fixation on revenge, one misguided and wholly corrupted both, and once more, in these situations alone, an otherwise unthinkable inventiveness would frequently begin to find purchase in this man's mind.

In the passageway corner lay sandbags piled up as ballast, and he picked one up, its shape like that of a dead piglet, then turned it upside down, dumping out the sand until it was empty, after which he stuffed the aforementioned chain and bundle of garlic inside it, then ground his heel into the bag, trampling it with meticulous tenacity. After that, he suddenly flung open the door to the cabin wherein the scrapbook was being worked on, tossed the bag inside, then immediately slammed the door shut, leaning his back against it, sealing it from the outside. From within───to call them negligent for not locking the door would be cruel───but from within.
【Deck boy】 『Wh-, what is this thing……wah, it kind of pricks at my nose, and it's reeeally sharp!』
【Deck boy】 『Hiiih, it stinks, it stinks so bad. O-, open the windooow!』
【Deck boy】 『I can't, the porthole in this cabin has fixed fittings, uh, khh, it's in my throat too, koh, cough cough khh!』

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
『出るんだ部屋から、すぐに───って、
　開かない、どうして、扉!?』
source.english:
“Out! Get out of the room, now—
It won't open! Why won't the door open!?”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
『こほこほこほ、僕喉が弱いのに、
　これ、ひど……開けて、あけてようっ、
　誰か助け……ご、ごほ、ごはぁぁっ』
source.english:
“Cough-cough-cough! My throat's bad enough already!
This is awful… Open it!
Please open it! Somebody help—Cough, gaaah!”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
『助けてぇ、誰か助けてぇ……』
source.english: “Help! Somebody help us…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 『We gotta get out of here, right now───wait, it won't open, the door won't, why!?』
【Deck boy】 『Cough cough cough, my throat is really sensitive too, this is awful……open, please open, somebody help……kh, cough, khaaaah!』
【Deck boy】 『Heeeelp, somebody help uuuus……』

source.japanese: 下級水夫の切ない苦鳴も、扉越しにどんどん叩きつけられる小さな拳の衝撃も、今の朔屋には御貴族お抱えの室内四重奏団の妙なる調べ、やがて叫びも細く解放を求めてもがく乱打も弱まるにつれ頬に浮かんだ笑みがなんとも卑しくどす黒い。錆にまみれた鉄鎖はそれだけで金属の異臭をまとっているのに加え、大蒜の潰し汁などをたっぷりまぶされて催涙瓦斯じみた威力を発揮したのだ、朔屋の企てた通りに。
source.english: The junior sailors' anguished cries, the little fists pounding on the other side of the door—to Sakuya just then, they were the exquisite music of a string quartet retained by some noble household. As the screams dwindled and the blows demanding release grew feeble, an ugly, black-hearted smile spread over his face. The rusty chain had a metallic stench of its own. Drenched in juice from the crushed garlic, it worked something like tear gas, exactly as Sakuya had intended.

source.japanese:
───復讐は足取り軽くする。たとえそれが、見当違いも良いところの唾棄されるべき所業であったとしても、この時の朔屋を諫める者はいなかった。
　朔屋がこの夜直後に異様な事態に巻きこまれ心胆氷水につけられる戦慄を味わう憂き目をみたとしても、だから彼を、この外道な手を下した後では彼を哀れむ必要など全くない、そうどこにも。
source.english:
Revenge lightens the step. Even when the deed is disgustingly, utterly misdirected, no one was there to admonish Sakuya that night.
Shortly afterward, he would find himself embroiled in strange events, chilled to the core as though his heart had been plunged into ice water. But after this vile trick, there was no need to pity him. None at all.

target.text: The miserable screams of the deck boys and the impacts of their thumping fists felt through the door: to Sakuya in this moment, both were as the exquisite melody of an indoor instrumental quartet kept on retainer by nobility, and as the screams finally grew faint and the frantic battering demanding liberation weakened at length, how despicably vulgar and dark a smile it was that bloomed on his cheeks. The rusted chain was by itself enveloped in the offensive smell of metal, but in addition to that, it had been smeared in plenty of juices from the crushed garlic, unleashing an effect akin to that of tear gas. All according to Sakuya's dastardly plot.

───Revenge lightens one's gait. Even should it, for example, be a most misguided of acts, a deed that ought to be abhorred and spat upon, in this moment, there were none present to expostulate with Sakuya. So even should Sakuya be dragged into some bizarre circumstances immediately following his actions this night, should icy water be thrown upon his heart, should he shudder and tremble in fear, should he suffer through misery and distress, after committing so fiendish a deed, there was absolutely no need to pity him at all, no, not in the slightest.

source.japanese:
的外れ、言いがかりも甚だしいところの仕返しに浮き立つ心は、しかし長保ちはせず、船内通路を廻って間もなく張力を失った。
　信天翁号のむさ苦しい船内通路は、夜闇に包まれるとただでさえ薄汚れが目立って侘びしく、あちこちの影の濃い辺りなどは、不気味というより老残の侘びしさを溜めて、なにやら人の被造物の空しささえ訴えてくる。
source.english:
The elation of so wildly misdirected, so wholly trumped-up a revenge did not last; scarcely had he resumed his circuit of the ship's passages before it went slack.
At night, the Albatross's squalid corridors only showed their grime more plainly and grew more forlorn. Wherever the shadows pooled thickly, they gathered not so much menace as the desolation of decrepit age, seeming almost to lament the futility of everything fashioned by human hands.

source.japanese: じじ、と薄れては光を取り戻す切れ加減の常夜灯も、ぱっと閃くでもなく、喘息患者の呼吸を思わせ照らされているだけで命が萎えてくるよう。用心に点された懐中電燈だって、この襤褸船の作法正しく心得て、電池が乏しく、点けているといつ切れるかもっと慎重に使って電力を保たせないととかえって神経を磨り減らす、でもって点さず歩けば暗がりの深さ増すばかり、通路の奥は影が意地悪く隠して見通しを鬱陶しく遮[さえぎ]る、あとはずるずると人が影に抱く退嬰的な連想を引き出す……。
source.english: A failing night light buzzed, dimmed, recovered. It never flashed sharply; its labored breathing recalled an asthmatic, and merely standing in its light seemed to sap one's life. Even the flashlight, switched on as a precaution, had learned the proper manners of this wreck. Its batteries were low. Keeping it lit meant worrying about when it would die, whether he should be more careful and conserve its power. Yet switching it off only deepened the dark. Shadows maliciously concealed the far end of the passage, blocked his view, and drew out all the dispiriting associations a mind could attach to darkness…

source.japanese: 船員学校で、試験の問題を漁りに悪友達と忍びこんだ夜の校舎とてここまでの裏ぶれた退廃感は覚えなかった、少なくともあの時は傍らには他人のあったし、夜回りの守衛がもたらした緊張感だって今にして思えば紛れもない実感だったと、朔屋は景気悪く追憶の尻尾に齧り付く。引き換えこの夜の船内通路ときたら。
source.english: Not even the night he had broken into the sailor school with his disreputable friends to steal the exam questions had felt this shabby, this decayed. At least he had company then. Even the tension brought by the night watchman now seemed something wonderfully real and solid. Glumly, Sakuya gnawed at the tail of that memory. Compared with this ship's passage tonight—

source.japanese:
ただただ退屈で影と奥行きが薄ら虚ろで、見ているだけでも目の力が弱まり視界が掠れていきそう、朔屋はごしごしと瞼を擦る。船内を何者がうろついているのか知らんが、好きなようにさせておけばいい、盗ったところで盗人好みの利鞘の甘い積み荷など有るはずも無し、あるならそもそもこの船、こんな誰からも嫌われる裏航路など進んではいない。はたまたなんらかの怨念に船の沈没を画策しているとしても、手間取る障害もあったものかは、船の弱点探すまでもなく、手頃な金床でも抱え上げて船床に叩きつければ、上下の隔壁ぶち抜いてたちまち船底まで貫いて、後は浸水に任せるだけで事は足りる。そもそもそれが目的なら、乗りこんで五分もあればこの信天翁号の脆さなど知れよう。
　船内の不審者の噂は数日前から囁かれており、それだけの期間があれはこんな船など三回は潰してお釣りが来る。
source.english:
Nothing but tedium. Its shadows and depths looked vaguely vacant; merely gazing into them seemed enough to weaken his eyes and blur his vision. Sakuya rubbed his eyelids hard. Whoever was roaming the ship could do as they pleased. There was no cargo here with the sweet profit margins a thief would want. If there were, the ship would not be taking these despised back routes in the first place. And if some grudge had inspired the intruder to sink her, what obstacle could possibly delay them? No need to hunt for a weakness. Pick up a convenient anvil, slam it onto the floor, and it would smash through partition after partition, straight to the bottom. Then leave the flooding to finish the job. Anyone boarding with that intention would discover the Albatross's fragility within five minutes. Rumors of an intruder had been circulating for days.
That was time enough to wreck a ship like this three times over, with change to spare.

target.text: His spirit was elated by a revenge completely off the mark, based on utterly groundless accusations, but it did not last long, and soon after he began patrolling the passageways, all that tension vanished.
