When shrouded in the dark of night, the usual foulness of the squalid passageways of the Albatross only grew more conspicuously dreary, the heavy pools of shadow here and there were not so much eerie as they were steeped in the desolation of decrepitude, and in some ways, it conveyed even the hollow futility of man's creation.

Those sputtering nightlights, too, dimming with a faint buzz before regaining their glow, never once flared up with sudden brilliance, and it felt as if life itself faded away just from being lit up by this light reminiscent of the breathing of an asthmatic.

Even the electric torch he had lit out of vigilance seemed to have learned well the etiquette of this ramshackle ship, for its battery was poor, it could run out at any moment if left on, and so he would need to use it with care to preserve its power, which in turn only frayed his nerves more; consequently, as he walked around without it turned on, the shadows only grew deeper and darker, the depths of the passage maliciously hidden from view by the shadows gloomily obstructing his sight, slowly dregding up the regressive associations that man harbours towards the dark…….

Back at the nautical school he once went to, he had sneaked into the schoolhouse at night with his partners-in-crime to rummage around for the exam questions, but he had not experienced a feeling of such dilapidated degeneracy even back then; at the very least, back then, he had other people next to him, and thinking back on it now, that feeling of tension that the security guard patrolling at night had brought him made it feel doubtlessly real; so Sakuya thought, gloomily clinging to the tail end of his reminiscence. In exchange, when it came to the ship passageways of tonight.

It was nothing but tedium, the shadows and depths faint and hollow, just looking at them was enough for his eyesight to weaken, his field of vision blurring, and Sakuya rubbed his eyelids vigorously. He wasn't sure if anyone was actually loitering around the ship at all, but surely they could just be left to their own devices; even were they trying to steal something, there should be no cargo with the kind of juicy profit margin that thieves prefer, and if there were, then this ship would not be sailing through these back routes despised by all in the first place.

Or even assuming they were scheming to sink this ship out of some manner of grudge, was there really any obstacle that could cause the execution of that plot to be delayed so long? There was not even really a need to seek out the ship's weaknesses, for if one lifted up even just an anvil of a reasonable size and slammed it against the deck, it would smash through both the upper and lower bulkheads, piercing all the way through to the ship's keel in an instant, and after that, it would be sufficient to simply leave the rest to the flooding. And if that was the objective from the beginning, then within just five minutes of boarding, one would surely become all too aware of just how fragile this Albatross was.

The rumour of this suspicious trespasser roaming around the ship had been whispered of for several days now, and with that much time, this ship could have already been wrecked three times over with change to spare.

source.japanese: だから盗むにしても壊すにしても、時間を無駄に掛けすぎだとたかをくくって朔屋、もうこの頃には侵入者への警戒など七分粥よりもっと薄くして、船内通路の侘びしげな様にそぞろ嘘寒くした背筋へ景気つけてやる為に、強い物を欲した。
source.english: Thieving or wrecking, whoever it was was taking far too long. Sakuya dismissed the danger; by now, his vigilance had grown thinner than watery rice gruel. The passage's desolation had sent a chilly unease down his spine, and he wanted something strong to put the life back into it.

source.japanese:
有り体に言えば、酒である。
　こんなしょぼくれた、心の浮かない、気分がくさくさしてくる夜回りなんぞは適当に、それこそこの通路の端まで進む程度に流すで申し訳も立とう。
source.english:
In plain language: a drink.
He could give this dreary, dispiriting, thoroughly miserable watch a cursory effort—say, as far as the end of this passage—and consider his duty done.

source.japanese:
そう思い切ってしまうと朔屋の心は、いかに貯蔵室の見張りの下級水夫を言いくるめるか、目当ての酒は残っているか、に集約されて、足取りも速まって現金な、懐中電燈の電池もあと少し保ってくれればいいとて点けッぱなしに、そうしない事には足下が頼りない。
　さもないと、青年の足は通路の段差や板の継ぎ目に蹴躓きそうだったので。
source.english:
Once he made that decision, his mind narrowed to two questions: how to sweet-talk the junior sailor guarding the store, and whether any of his preferred liquor remained. His steps quickened, opportunist that he was. He left the flashlight on; its batteries need only last a little longer. Otherwise he could not trust his footing.
His feet seemed ready to catch on every change of level, every joint between the boards.

source.japanese:
先程から、踏み出した足の底が、もしかしたら深淵に落ちこんでしまいそうに怪しく思われるくらい、通路の床は低く垂れこめた狭霧に覆い隠されていたからで。
　爪先で払うようにしても霧は、一時乱されて気流に巻くばかりでいっかな薄れず、朔屋の逸[はや]る足取りを邪魔して悪戯な事この上なく、しまいに青年は歩みを止めて四囲を見回して、そしてやっと───通路に渦巻く狭霧と冷気に気づいたという。足下の歩きづらさ、肌に続々と迫る冷気はこれは、夜回りに疲厭した心がもたらした影響ではなく、外部からのものだった。
source.english:
For some time, a low mist had concealed the floor, making each step feel disturbingly as though it might plunge into an abyss.
Sweeping a foot through it merely stirred the mist into temporary eddies. It would not thin, but kept mischievously impeding his impatient stride. At last he stopped and looked around. Only then did he notice the mist and cold filling the passage. His awkward footing, the successive waves of cold against his skin: these were not effects of a mind wearied by the watch. They came from outside him.

target.text: Therefore, even were they trying to steal or break something, they were wasting far too much time on it, Sakuya thought, making light of the intruder in his mind, and by this point, Sakuya's vigilance towards any intruder had grown thinner than rice gruel consisting of seven parts water to one part rice; to kick some warmth back into his spine chilled by the dreary gloom of the ship's passageway, he craved something strong.

To put it more frankly, he wanted booze. On a depressing, disheartening night patrol like this, one that only served to sour his mood, a perfunctory stroll down to the end of the passageway ought to be more than sufficient.

Having made up his mind thus, Sakuya's thoughts were all concentrated around a single topic: how he should try to cajole the deck boy on watch outside the storeroom, and was there any of that liquor he'd set his eyes on left? His stride hastened with mercenary resolve, electric torch left burning with the hope that its batteries would endure just a little longer, for without its glow, the footing was treacherous. If turned off, the young man's feet were like to stumble on the uneven steps of the passage or the gaps of its floorboards.

Because for some time now, the bottom of his advancing feet had been covered by a mist, a fog hanging low over the floor of the passage, thick enough to make him doubt if he hadn't fallen into an abyss at some point.

Even as he tried to sweep it aside with the toe of his shoe, the mist only dispersed briefly, whirling around with the air current, not thinning at all, obstructing Sakuya's impetuous stride in an act of mischief beyond compare until finally, the young man ceased walking and looked all around him, and only then, at last───did he notice the fog and chill swirling through the passageway. The awkwardness of his footing, the cold air pressing relentlessly against his skin, this was not a consequence of his heart having grown weary and embittered by the night patrol, no, it was something from the outside world.

source.japanese: 実際に通路には、それ自体が意志を持って蠢動するかに霧が澱[よど]んでいたし、空気だって二度・三度は低下していた。
source.english: Mist really lay stagnant in the passage, as though it stirred with a will of its own. The temperature had fallen two or three degrees.

target.text: In reality, a mist had settled in the passageway, writhing as if possessed by a will of its own, and the temperature of the air had even dropped by two or three degrees.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（あれ……この状況って……。
　冷気と……。
　霧と……）
source.english:
(Hang on… This is…
Cold…
And mist…)

source.japanese: ───冷気はいよいよ増すばかり───
source.english: —The cold kept growing—

source.japanese: ───気づけば通路にも低く霧が渦巻いて。
source.english: —Then he noticed mist swirling low in the passage too.

source.japanese:
耳に残響した下級水夫の言葉は、霧の粒子にざらつく通路の暗がりにはふさわしい、籠もった囁き声ではあったけれど───
　語られた時は、温気に蒸れる暗幕の内という舞台立て、端から怪談として安心に怖がっていられたけれど、いざ現実に同じ状況に放りこまれてみると、恐怖の実感は朔屋を瞬時に金縛りに掛けた。
　あの時下級水夫はなんと語っていた？
source.english:
The junior sailor's words echoed in his ears, in a muffled whisper well suited to the grainy, mist-filled darkness.
When he had heard them, he was safely sweating beneath a black cloth, a stage set where he could enjoy being frightened by a ghost story from the outset. Now, thrust into the same situation in reality, he felt fear seize and paralyze him in an instant.
What had the sailor said then?

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （Wait……this situation is……. A chill……. And mist……）
───The chill was only intensifying───
───And by the time he realized it, the passageway had already been fully enshrouded in a low-hanging fog.

The deck boy's words, the echoes of which lingered in his ears, were told in a hushed whisper, fitting for the darkness of this passage, grainy with drifting particles of mist, but─── When they had been narrated to him, the stage had been the sweltering, musty interior of a blackout curtain, he'd considered it a ghost story right from the outset, and so he could safely indulge in the fear, but now that he had been thrown into those same circumstances in reality, the very real feeling of terror instantly bound Sakuya on hand and foot. What was it that deck boy had spoken of back then again?

source.japanese:
───ずる……っ、ぺた……。
　　　　　ずる……、ぺた……っ。
source.english:
—Drag… Slap…
Drag… Slap…

source.japanese:
───声に直せばこのような───
　
　───でも本当はもっと───
source.english:
—Rendered in syllables, something like this—
—But in truth it was more—

source.japanese: ───なんとも言えない音で───
source.english: —Indescribable—

target.text: ───Shhrrllrrp……, squelch……. Shhrrllrrp……, squelch…….
───When rendered in the human voice─── ───But in reality, the sound was───
───Stranger by far, indescribable───

source.japanese:
ずる……っ、ぺた……。
　　　　　ずる……、ぺた……っ。
source.english:
Drag… Slap…
Drag… Slap…

source.japanese: 通常船内にはたとえ深更であろうとも、体内で鼓動や呼吸が止まないと同じく、機関の脈動や船体の軋みが響いているのに、この時それら信天翁号の生理音は絶えて、朔屋も歩度を止めているから跫音立てていないというのに───
source.english: Even at dead of night, a ship ordinarily had its engine's pulse, its hull's creaking, just as a body's heartbeat and breathing never ceased. But now the Albatross's bodily sounds had stopped. Sakuya, too, stood still, making no sound of his own—

source.japanese:
通路の奥。
　船体を横切る通路と交わっている、
　その影から───
source.english:
From farther down the passage.
Where it met another, running across the ship.
From that shadow—

target.text: Shhrrllrrp……, squelch……. Shhrrllrrp……, squelch…….

Normally, even should it, for example, be late at night, just as the palpitations and respiration within the human body do not stop, so would the pulsations of the engine and the creaking of the hull be resounding throughout the ship, but in this moment, all of those physiological sounds of the Albatross had ceased, and Sakuya had also come to a halt, so he was no longer producing any footfalls, and yet───
In the depths of the passageway. Where it intersected with another passageway that ran across the vessel, from those shadows───

source.japanese:
濡れた布を落として、引きずるような。
　秘やかで、かつ異様な拍子に則った。
　それは、漏れ伝わってくるそれは。
source.english:
Like a wet cloth dropped, then dragged.
Quiet, in a strange rhythm all its own.
That sound coming through—

source.japanese: 跫音、ではないのか───
source.english: Could it be footsteps—?

source.japanese: 通路の底を瓦斯立ち籠める夜の沼の面と見せている狭霧も、その角から湧いてきていないか───
source.english: And the mist, making the bottom of the passage look like the surface of a swamp fuming in the night—wasn't that pouring out of the same corner—?

source.japanese: 痙攣的な、握りしめた指の間から茘枝の実がぶるんと零れ出るような運動で、朔屋の眼球飛び出さんばかりに左右に走り、どれだけ彼を安堵せしめた事か、やや手前の船室の扉が細く開いていたのに気づいた時には。
source.english: His eyes jerked wildly from side to side, almost bursting from their sockets like a lychee squeezed between clenched fingers. Then he noticed a cabin door a little way back, standing slightly ajar. What relief.

target.text: Like someone had dropped a damp cloth and was dragging it along the floor. Conforming to a rhythm at once clandestine and bizarre. That thing, faintly leaking through to him, that thing was.
Footfalls, was it not───
This mist that had made the bottom of the passageway look like the surface of a nighttime swamp enveloped in dense fog, was it not also rolling in from around that corner───

Spasmodically, with motions like a lychee fruit bursting out from between tightly gripping fingers, Sakuya's eyeballs darted left and right as though about to pop out from their sockets, and what immense solace it must have brought him when he noticed that the door of the cabin just ahead had been left slightly ajar.

source.japanese:
もうその時には異妖なる跫音、通路の角を寸前にまで近づいて、あれは聞き間違えなどでない、迫り来る現実の驚異まざまざと、暗がりだというのに影は更に濃く通路に落ちて、その怪異な輪郭に朔屋は細く開いた扉を押し開けて内に飛びこんだ、幸い霧には雨夜に道行く人の脛にまとわりついて足取り縺れさせる猫の怪の様な拘束力はなく、転ぶような落ち度こそ無かったものの音まで殺せたかどうかは判らぬ。
　朔屋にできたのは、戸口の陰で息を潜[ひそ]め身を縮める事くらい、既に扉に錠する隙も失われた、ぎりぎりのタイミング。
source.english:
By then the uncanny footsteps had nearly reached the corner. No, he had not misheard them. Here was the approaching menace, vividly real: a shadow falling darker still upon the dark passage. At the sight of that monstrous outline, Sakuya pushed the door open and darted inside. Fortunately the mist had none of the binding power of those cat spirits that wind about a traveler's shins on rainy nights and tangle his steps. He did not trip. Whether he had made a sound, he could not say.
All he could do was shrink behind the doorway and hold his breath. There was no longer time to lock the door. Barely, barely in time.

source.japanese: そうやって耳から異妖の跫音締め出し、目も塞いでいればいい、人が正気を保ち続けるには、視界から追い出すべき事柄なぞこの世には幾らでもある、とそれくらいは朔屋にも会得せられている定理であったのに、何故彼は戸口の隙間から覗き見てしまったのか。
source.english: He should have shut the uncanny footsteps out of his ears, and closed his eyes as well. To remain sane, a person must keep any number of things in this world out of sight. Even Sakuya understood that much of the theorem. Why, then, did he peer through the crack in the door?

target.text: By now, those phantasmally queer footfalls had drawn so near that their source was on the very threshold of stepping around that corner; that was not just something he'd misheard, it was a looming marvel of reality laid bare before him.

Though it was already dark, an even deeper shadow fell upon the passage, and as he glimpsed that monstrous silhouette, Sakuya shoved open the slightly ajar door and leapt inside; fortunately, the mist did not posses binding powers akin to those of cat yokai, the sort that clings to a passerby's shins on a rainy night and makes them trip over their feet, but while he managed to avoid any missteps that could lead to a fall, it was unclear to him if he'd managed to suppress the noise he'd made.
The best Sakuya could do was hold his breath behind the door and curl into himself, for he had already missed his chance to lock the door behind him, having jumped in at the very last moment.

All he needed to do was stay like that and shut out the uncanny footsteps from his ears, and he should just close his eyes as well, for in order for a man to maintain his sanity, there are several things in this world one must needs banish from sight; even Sakuya had grasped that theorem, and yet for whatever possible reason could it then be that he still ended up peeking out from the gap in the doorway regardless?

source.japanese: しゃがみこんでいたところから見上ぐれば、扉の隙間を間切っていくそれは、氷河の谷間から垣間見る氷山の様にも巨大に映る、幸いなのは、それが総身に黒霧をまとい、輪郭が判然としなかった事、恐怖を呼んだのは、黒霧にも関わらず所々は見てとれてしまった事。
source.english: Seen from where he crouched, the thing crossing the crack looked as vast as an iceberg glimpsed through a glacial valley. Mercifully, black mist swathed its whole body and obscured its outline. Terrifyingly, despite that mist, certain parts remained visible.

source.japanese:
鱗、とか、青黒く滑[ぬめ]る肌、とか。
　おおよその形としては朔屋と同じく人だというのに、有りうべからざる鰭[ひれ]、だとか。
source.english:
Scales. Slippery, blue-black skin.
Its general shape was human, like Sakuya's, yet there were fins, which had no right to be there.

source.japanese:
夜毎通路に零れ貼りついていたあの鱗[うろこ]は、きっとこのモノ達の落としたものならん。
　夜毎徘徊していたのはこのモノ達、ヒトの形をした、魚類の異妖───
source.english:
The scales scattered and stuck along the passage each night must have fallen from these things.
These were the nightly wanderers. Fish-monsters shaped like humans—

target.text: He looked upwards from where he crouched, and what slipped past the crack of the door seemed immense, like glimpses of an iceberg from between glacial valleys, but fortunately, its entire body was clad in dark mist, its contours lay obscured, but what evoked terror in him was how, despite the shroud of black fog, he still ended up seeing parts of it.
Like scales, and such, bluish-black slimy skin, and the like. Its general shape was that of a human similar to Sakuya, and yet it had fins that ought not be, and so on.

Those shed scales stuck to the passageways night after night must surely have been dropped by this thing. What prowled night after night must have been this thing, this ichthyic monster taking human form───

source.japanese: ぎょろつく目だって魚と同じ、レンズのように丸く、かつある種の両生類のように横に平たい眸[ひとみ]をしてあり、それが朔屋に無意識裡に一つの観想もたらしたという。
source.english: Their staring eyes were fish eyes, round as lenses, but the pupils lay flat and horizontal, as in certain amphibians. Unbidden, a thought came to Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（……なんだ、あの目……。
　……え？　泪……さん……？）
source.english:
(…Those eyes…
What…? Ms. Rui…?)

source.japanese:
朔屋が脈絡無しにあの艶美な女を連想したのは、脈絡の無いように見えて故ない事ではなく、この魚怪の眸[ひとみ]は、泪のあの珍[めずら]かな水平器の形した瞳孔と似通っており───
　
　確かめようとした時には、魚怪は朔屋が隠形する船室の前を行き過ぎて、まず厄災蒙[こうむ]らずに済んだ事を喜ぶべきなのに、朔屋は見たばかりの魚怪と泪の相似に体が勝手に動いて、身を乗りだした、と見ればまた戸口の向こうに影だ。今と同じ、今に続く魚怪が、回り灯籠の絵のように後から。咄嗟に身を固くして扉の裏に貼りついて、やり過ごす、過ごしても、また後ろから魚怪の来たりて、陸続と。
source.english:
His apparently random association with that sensual woman was not without cause. The fish-monster's pupils resembled Rui's unusual, spirit-level-shaped pupils. By the time he tried to make sure, it had passed the cabin where he hid.
He ought first to have rejoiced at escaping unharmed. Instead, the resemblance between Rui and the monster sent him leaning out before he could think—and another shadow appeared beyond the door. Another fish-monster, following the first like successive pictures on a revolving lantern. He stiffened, flattened himself behind the door and let it pass. Then another came behind it. One after another.

source.japanese:
ここまで来ると深夜の徘徊者どころでない。
　百鬼、とはいかず単一種だが、夜行の群れであり、さすがの信天翁号と言えども化け物どもの寄り合い所にされていようとは朔屋にも予想外で、こっそり腿[もも]を捻ってみても確実に痛い、とあればこの情景は現実の、呪うべき事だが。
source.english:
This had gone far beyond a solitary midnight prowler.
Not a hundred varieties of demon, perhaps, but a nocturnal procession of a single species. Even aboard the Albatross, Sakuya had not expected the ship to serve as a meeting place for monsters. He secretly pinched his thigh. It certainly hurt. Then this scene was real. Damn it.

source.japanese: 古来こういう夜行は忌むべきモノ、身を、見るを慎むべきモノで、知恵在る先人達は戸口を閉ざして何が見えようが聞こえようが見ざる聞かざるそして言わざるを貫いたものだし、朔屋にもそれが正しき身の処し方と自ずと感得された、の、だけれど。
source.english: From ancient times, such night processions had been things to shun, to keep oneself from, to refrain from seeing. Wise forebears had shut their doors, and whatever might be heard or seen, resolutely seen nothing, heard nothing, said nothing. Sakuya instinctively understood that this was the proper course. But—

target.text: Its dull, bulging eyes were just like those of a fish, round like lenses, and moreover, its pupils were squashed flat and horizontal like a certain species of amphibian, and in the depths of the realms of his subconsciousness, that brought to Sakuya a single contemplative vision.
【Naomasa】 （……What is with those eyes……. ……Huh? Rui……san……?）

Though it may have appeared that Sakuya recalled that seductively beautiful woman without any coherence, it was not without cause, for the eyes of that fish monster bore an awfully close resemblance to those curious pupils that Rui possessed, shaped like a spirit level───

When he made an attempt to verify what he thought he had seen, the fish monster had already gone past the room Sakuya concealed himself within, and although he ought to first rejoice that he had made it through without catastrophe, the similitude of the fish monster he'd just seen and Rui made his body act automatically; he leaned forwards, and as he looked out, there came a shadow on the other side of the door once more. Same as the one before it, another fish monster following after the other, like pictures on a revolving lantern.
He tensed at once and clung to the inner side of the door, and he let it pass by him, but as he did, yet another fish monster came from behind this one, one after another.

At this point, this was no longer a simple issue of someone prowling around late at night. It was only a single species, and so it didn't quite reach the extent of a parade of one hundred demons, but it was still a horde of a night procession; even granted that this was the Albatross, and one could consider it the gathering place of all manner of monsters, this was well beyond even Sakuya's expectations, and when he stealthily tried pinching his thigh, it certainly hurt, which would mean this sight was reality, and what an accursed reality at that.

From time immemorial, these sorts of night parades have been regarded as abominable things, something one ought to refrain from looking upon; our wise ancestors would shut their doors tight, and no matter what was seen or heard, they would remain resolute to the end: see no evil, hear no evil, and speak no evil, and even Sakuya had awoken to the profound realization that this was the right action to take in this situation, but, still.

source.japanese:
緊張と恐怖の余りに蝋で塞がれたようになっていた耳が、この時聞き分けた音。
　老婆が数珠を繰りながら唱える念仏のように単調で、低い、泡立つような音。
　それは魚怪共の発声音であり、
source.english:
His ears, seemingly stopped with wax by tension and terror, now distinguished a sound.
Low, monotonous, bubbling, like an old woman chanting prayers while passing beads through her fingers.
The fish-monsters were uttering it.
“…Lady Rui…”

source.japanese:
音は言葉を造っており、呼んでいたのは船の女客の名であり。
　魚怪達は魚の吻に尖った鼻先で空気を嗅ぎ分けるように、のたのたと頭を打ち振りながら船内を進み往き、異様な行列もついには終わりとなって、朔屋の悪夢も尽きるかに見えたけれど。怪異が船内を嗅ぎ回りながら進んでいった或る方向というのは。
source.english:
The sounds made words, and the words named the ship's female passenger.
Wagging their heads clumsily, as though sniffing the air with the pointed tips of their fish snouts, the monsters proceeded through the ship. At last the strange procession ended, and it seemed Sakuya's nightmare might end as well. But the direction they had taken, sniffing through the ship—

target.text: 【Fish monster】 『……. ……. i』

The overwhelming fear and stress made it feels as if his ears were clogged with wax, but just now, there was a sound he could identify. It was monotone, like an old lady chanting the nembutsu while passing juzu beads through her fingers, low in tone, an almost bubbling sound. That was the sound of the fish monster vocalizing,
【Fish monster】 『……Rui-sama……』

The sounds formed words, and what they called out was the name of the ship's female passenger. The fish monsters pursed their fish snouts, swinging their heads around cumbersomely as though scenting something out with their nares while they advanced deeper into the ship, the bizarre parade finally reaching an end, and it might have seemed as though Sakuya's nightmare also came to a close, however. While the monsters sniffed around the ship, they were advancing in a certain direction.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（おい……あっちは泪さんの部屋がある方じゃねえか。まさかな……たまたまそっちの方に向かっていくってだけだよな……？）
source.english: (Hey… That's the way to Ms. Rui's cabin. No. Surely not… They just happen to be going that way, right…?)

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （Oi……isn't that the direction of Rui-san's stateroom? There's no way……that they just happen to be heading that way by chance, is there……?）

source.japanese:
怪異達が向かっていく先には、信天翁号の女客、泪の船室があることに気づいた朔屋の困惑と言ったら。
　他の誰ならともかく、あの女性だけはどうにも苦手な朔屋としては見なかったことにしたいが、もし泪に万が一の事あれば、今夜の見回りを命じられていた朔屋は、水夫長あたりから舷側から逆さ吊りにされ、鮫の寄せ餌に使われてしまうだろう。
　せっかく怪異と遭遇してなお、心に恐怖の跡が抉り残された以外は身を損なうことなく、狭霧と冷気は行列と共に遠ざかり、通路の奥に消えていったのに。
source.english:
Sakuya's consternation when he realized the monsters were heading toward Rui's cabin may be imagined. Had it been anyone else, he might have looked away. That particular woman so unnerved him that he wanted to pretend he had seen nothing. But should anything happen to her, Sakuya—the man assigned tonight's rounds—would doubtless be hung upside down over the side by the boatswain and used as shark bait.
He had met the monsters without bodily injury, however deeply terror had gouged its traces into his mind. The mist and cold had receded with the procession, disappearing into the depths of the passage. And now—

source.japanese: 朔屋には、仕方なくなく、泣く泣く怪異達の後を追いかける───しかなく。
source.english: There was nothing, nothing for Sakuya to do but follow the monsters, miserably, unwillingly—

target.text: When Sakuya realized that the monsters were heading towards the cabin belonging to Rui, the lady passenger of the Albatross, his bewilderment was beyond description. If wouldn't be so bad had it been anybody else, but from the perspective of Sakuya, who just could not cope with this woman in particular, while he would have loved to simply pretend to not have seen anything, if in the very unlikely case something were to happen to Rui, then Sakuya, being the one who had been ordered to patrol the ship tonight, would surely be hung upside down over the ship's side by, say, the Bosun, and end up being used as sharkbait.

Even after crossing paths with those monsters, he had suffered no harm aside from the lingering traces of fear carved deep into his heart; the mist and chill had receded together with the parade, vanishing into the far end of the passageway, and yet.
For Sakuya, left with no choice, there was nothing left to do─── but reluctantly purse the monsters.

source.japanese:
そこだけはいつも美しく飾られ、そしてどこかしら淫蕩な空気を秘めやかに湛えているは泪の船室。
　だがこの夜は、女の膏の匂いは魚臭に圧されて、部屋の主の艶冶な肢体をより蠱惑的に意味ありげに照らし出す卓上燈の熟れた明かりも、魚怪達の肌の上では汚怪に滑光る。
source.english:
Rui's cabin was always beautifully furnished, always held some secret suggestion of debauchery.
Tonight, however, the smell of fish overpowered the scent of the woman's flesh. The table lamp's mellow light, which ordinarily made its mistress's sensual figure more alluring, more suggestive, gleamed foully upon the fish-monsters' skin.

source.japanese:
豪奢と退廃と爛熟した快楽の香りに替わり、
信天翁号の中では格別に広いこの船室を充たしているのは、魚怪の、床と言わず寝台と言わずにひしめいて、室内はさながら幻視の画家が幻像、それも観じた者の正気を損ねる幻像を一つところに収斂させたかのよう。
source.english:
In place of luxury, decadence and the perfume of pleasure grown overripe,
fish-monsters filled this cabin, exceptionally spacious by the Albatross's standards, thronging floor and bed alike. The room looked as if some visionary painter had gathered all his phantasms into one place—and phantasms of the sort that cost the beholder his sanity.

source.japanese:
だというのに泪は。
　或いは、だからこそ泪は。
　奇怪な情景の中にあって、彼女の麗質は一層艶[あで]やかに鮮やかに、なにかしら美と醜の本質というものを会得させてしまうかに、際立っていたのである。
source.english:
And yet Rui.
Or perhaps because of it, Rui.
Amid that strange scene, her beauty shone more vividly, more richly. So starkly did it stand out that it seemed to impart some essential knowledge of beauty and ugliness.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（現実かよ、これは……）
source.english: (Is this actually happening…?)

source.japanese:
泪。
　どれだけ男どもの関心と情欲を浴びようと、怯む事も舞い上がる事もなく、常に雅やかな立ち居振る舞い、泰然とした身のこなしと目の置き方で、より一層に男達を狂わせる泪。
　
　泪───
　彼女の容貌は、魚怪達に取り囲まれても恐怖に歪むはおろか、大きな感慨もなく、何時もと同じ、倦怠にたゆたって。
　魚怪達の注視を浴びても、惰気は払われる事もなく座す、椅子が細部まで職人の感性に磨き上げられた工芸品なら、泪の美は天与の至宝であり、凭れた様は二つの美が相俟って、その姿を永遠の時に封じこめてしまいたくなるほどに端麗、魚怪の醜が更に浮き彫りに、泪の美質もくっきりと、ぶつかり合う、唱和する、高め合う。
source.english:
Rui.
However much male interest and desire rained upon her, she neither flinched nor became elated. Her graceful bearing, her composed movements, the repose of her gaze only drove men further out of their minds.
Rui—
Even surrounded by fish-monsters, her face did not twist with fear. No great emotion touched it at all; it drifted in its customary languor. Their watching eyes did nothing to dispel her indolence as she sat.
If the chair was a work of art, every detail polished by a craftsman's sensibility, Rui's beauty was a treasure bestowed by heaven. As she reclined there, the two beauties met in such elegance that one wanted to seal the sight within eternity. The monsters' ugliness stood out more starkly; Rui's beauty more distinctly. They clashed, sang together, heightened each other.

source.japanese: 朔屋の如き凡夫であっても、感嘆に失語し膠付けにされたように足が動かなくなってしまうのが当然と言えた。
source.english: Even an ordinary mortal like Sakuya could hardly fail to be struck dumb with wonder, his feet stuck fast as though glued to the floor.

source.japanese: そして魚怪達、深更に彼女一人の船室に蝟集した彼ら、筋書きとしては群がりあって　この美女に襲いかかり、その血肉の一片まで、血潮の一雫まで貪り喰らい、狂うて跳梁する辺りがありそうなところ、彼らもまた泪の美麗の前では猛るより奪魂されてしまったのか、驚くまいてや、みな等[ひと]し並[なみ]に跪き、礼賛の型を取っていたのだ。
source.english: And the fish-monsters gathered in her solitary cabin at dead of night—One might have expected them to fall upon this beautiful woman in a frenzy, devour every scrap of flesh, every drop of blood, and caper madly. But perhaps her beauty had stolen their souls rather than inflamed their savagery. Astonishingly, they all knelt, assuming postures of adoration.

target.text: It was the only place always decorated beautifully, as well as secretively suffused with an almost decadently debauched atmosphere wafting in from somewhere; that was Rui's stateroom. But on this night, the scents of a woman's perfumed ointments were dominated by a fishy stench, and the glow of the masterfully chosen desk lamp illuminating the lady of the stateroom's bewitchingly beautiful body into an even more alluring sight also made the skin of those fish monsters glisten with a grotesque, slimy sheen.

In place of the fragrance of extravagant, decadent, and overripe pleasure, this stateroom, exceptionally spacious for a cabin on the Albatross, was filled with the reek of fish monsters; whether it be the floor or the bed, they crowded it all, the interior as though a painter of hallucinations had concentrated a vision into a singular place, and a vision that would disturb the mind of any who beheld it at that.

And despite all this, Rui. Or perhaps that was exactly why. Amidst this mysteriously eerie spectacle, the woman's beauty was more lustrous and vibrant than ever, conspicuously striking, as though it somehow compelled the beholder to grasp the very essence of beauty and ugliness.
【Naomasa】 （Is this actually real……）

Rui. No matter how much of their interest and lust men showered her with, she neither faltered nor got carried away, her movements ever graceful, and with her self-possessed carriage and the deliberate way in which she cast her gaze, those men were driven into an even wilder frenzy; that was Rui. Rui─── The woman's countenance, far from twisting in terror at being surrounded by the fish monsters, was without a trace of profound feeling; instead, it was the same as it ever was, adrift upon the tides of hebetude.

Even when bathed in the unblinking stares of the fish monsters, she sat, the ennui left undispelled; if the chair was a work of art polished to perfection down to every detail by an artisan's sensibility, then Rui's beauty was a divine treasure bestowed by the heavens, and the way she reclined, where those two beauties combined, was so exquisitely beauteous that one longed to seal her figure away in eternal time; the ugliness of the fish monsters only threw it into even starker relief, Rui's beauty was bold and distinct, they clashed, they sung in chorus, elevated each other to greater aesthetic heights.

Even an ordinary, unenlightened man the likes of Sakuya found himself rendered speechless in admiration, and one could say it was only natural that he found himself unable to move his legs as though he'd been glued in place.

And so, the fish monsters, they who thronged a lone woman's room in the dead of night: as the narrative would have it, this was when they would swarm her, pounce upon this beautiful woman, ravenously devour her flesh to the last morsel and drink her hot blood to the last drop, then run rampant in madness, but perhaps even they were more enraptured than enraged by Rui's soul-snatching beauty, for in a yet more astonishing turn of events, they had all fallen to their knees as one, assuming a posture of reverent veneration.

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『……我らの…………に、
　ご拝謁の光栄に……浴したく……』
source.english:
“…Our… …We beg…
the honor… of an audience…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『我らが……海に戻ってこられたとの……報せ。まことであった事……なんと……。
　喜ばしき……』
source.english:
“Our… The report… that you had returned to the sea… It was true…
How… joyful…”

target.text: 【Fish monster】 『……our…………upon, wish to be bathed in……the honour of your gracious audience……』
【Fish monster】 『We……tidings……had returned to the sea. To know this to be the truth……what……. Joyous……』

source.japanese: 跪くばかりか、魚怪の中でももっとも泪に近い一体が、差し延べた、腕には鱗[うろこ]と鰭[ひれ]、指には水掻きの、怪にして妖の手が示したのは、恭しさ。鋭く角だった指先なのに、脆い雲母片のひとひら剥離させる事なき繊細な動きに泪の踝[くるぶし]をくるんで、おしいだきつ、冷たく湿った口吻を寄せて、足の甲に口づけの───最大限の恭順の仕儀だ。
source.english: More than kneeling: the creature nearest Rui extended a hand. Its arm had scales and fins, its fingers webbing; monstrous though it was, the hand expressed reverence. Angular, sharply pointed fingertips moved with a delicacy that would not flake a single layer from a fragile piece of mica. They cradled Rui's ankle, lifted her foot, and brought a cold, wet mouth to its instep. A kiss—the utmost expression of submission.

source.japanese: この屈従の形を他の魚怪達は当然のように受け入れて、低い喉鳴りと目つきに匂わせる不満は、ただ口づけを押した同類にのみ向けられて、泪への畏敬……もうはっきりと描写して良いだろう、畏敬の念は尽きる処なし。
source.english: The others accepted this act of abasement as entirely proper. Any discontent in their low throat sounds and glances was directed solely at the fellow who had kissed her. Their awe of Rui—yes, by now one could plainly call it awe—was boundless.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（得体が知れねえとは考えていたが、
　まさか化け物と懇ろたぁ……）
source.english:
(I always thought there was something strange about
her. But getting cozy with monsters…?)

source.japanese:
何に驚愕すればよいのか。
　魚怪達にこうまで傅かれる泪にか。
　それともここまで傅[かしづ]かれてなお、感慨らしい感慨一つも気取らせず、普段にも増した退屈の風に目を泳がせた泪にか、その驕慢にか。
　魚怪達の中にあって泪は、女王の相を顕していたのだった。
source.english:
What was he to be astonished by?
By Rui, to whom the fish-monsters paid such abject court?
Or by her arrogance: though waited upon with such devotion, she betrayed not a trace of feeling, but let her gaze drift with a boredom deeper than ever?
Among the fish-monsters, Rui bore the aspect of a queen.

target.text: They weren't just kneeling; what the fish monster closest to Rui reached out towards her with, arm covered in scales and fins, webbing between the fingers, was an eldritch hand that displayed reverence. Though his fingertips were like sharp horns, they wrapped around Rui's ankle with movements so delicate that they would not disturb even a single fragile flake of mica, clasping it tenderly, and bringing his cold, damp lips closer, he then planted a kiss on the instep of her foot───all conducted in the fullest spirit of humble submission.

The other fish monsters accepted this display of servile submission as though it was entirely natural, the low growls from their throats and the sharp looks in their eyes that hinted at dissatisfaction were all directed towards their kin who had pressed his lips onto her, and their reverence for Rui was……by now, it should be acceptable to describe it with clarity: their feelings of reverence were inexhaustible.
【Naomasa】 （I had been thinking something was suspicious about her, but to think she'd be this intimate with monsters……）

What should he even be astonished by? Rui, for being waited upon so by fish monsters? Or perhaps that Rui, who even after being waited upon so, without letting slip even so much as a semblance of sentiment that seemed like a sentiment, pointedly did not look them in the eyes, sitting with an air of even greater boredom than usual: that haughtiness of hers? In the midst of these fish monsters, Rui revealed the visage of a queen.

source.japanese:
【泪】
『……戻ってきたのじゃあ、ないのよ』
source.english: “…I haven't come back.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『今更そちらへ戻るつもりなんて、ないわ』
source.english: “I have no intention of returning to you now.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『わたくしが海に出たのは、なりゆき。
　そう、なりゆき。
　呼ばれたの、この船に。それだけ』
source.english:
“Circumstance brought me out to sea.
Yes, circumstance.
I was called to this ship. That is all.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『───どなたが呼んだのか、それはわからないけれど』
source.english: “Who called me, I don't know.”

source.japanese: 恭順の口づけを、令嬢なら相応しく労ったのかも知れないが、泪はあくまで超然と無視して、吐いた言葉もつれなくて、どこまでも冷たい。
source.english: A well-bred young lady might have graciously acknowledged the submissive kiss. Rui ignored it, utterly aloof. Her words were indifferent, cold through and through.

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『なれども主上は……殿下のご帰還を……』
source.english: “But His Majesty… awaits Your Highness's return…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『一夜を千の秋に過ごすお心にて……』
source.english: “Each night… is as a thousand autumns… to his heart…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『お待ちいたして候……』
source.english: “He waits… for you…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『そんなの、わたくしはぞんじません』
source.english: “That is no concern of mine.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『出戻りのこの身を抱えて？　おめおめと？
　そんなの、恥ずかしくって』
source.english:
“Go crawling back? Now that my marriage is over?
How humiliating.”

target.text: 【Rui】 『……Made my return, I have not.』
【Rui】 『I have no intention of returning there, not after all this time.』
【Rui】 『It was circumstance alone that brought me to the sea. Yes, circumstance. I was summoned, to this ship. That is all.』
【Rui】 『───Whoever it was that summoned me, however, I yet remain ignorant of.』

Perhaps the kiss of submission would be rewarded appropriately by a young lady of good breeding, but Rui remained aloof as she ignored it to the last, the words she uttered also unkind, cold in every respect.
【Fish monster】 『Howbeit, the Emperor…… longs for the return of Your Imperial Highness……』
【Fish monster】 『With every single night weighing upon his heart as though it were a thousand autumns long……』
【Fish monster】 『He humbly awaits……』
【Rui】 『I feel nothing for any such thing.』
【Rui】 『I should return in disgrace? And shamelessly so? To do so would be humiliating.』

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『なんの……恥辱など……。
　殿下は……欺かれたのです……』
source.english:
“There is… no disgrace…
Your Highness… was deceived…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『咎は……欺いた者にこそあれ……』
source.english: “The blame… belongs to the deceiver…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『かの不届き者を……誅した殿下を……。
　称揚する者こそあっても……』
source.english:
“Your Highness put… that insolent man to death…
There are those… who praise you…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『嘲る者など……我らのうちには……一つたりとも……』
source.english: “But not one… among us… would mock you…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『……昔の事をいつまで思い出させるおつもり？　あの方との事は、もうとっくに。
　そう、ずっと昔に終わってしまった事』
source.english:
“…How long do you intend to keep reminding me of the past? That man and I—it ended long ago.
Yes, a very long time ago.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『きっと父さまも、同じなのでしょうね。
　古い事をいつまでも、引きずって。
　お前たちだって同じ。
　───はあ。だから、厭なのよ』
source.english:
“Father must be just the same.
Forever dragging the past about.
And you are no different.
Ah… That's why I can't bear it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（こいつら、泪さんの事を……。
　一体この女はなんなんだ？
　この化け物達と───）
source.english:
(These things… Ms. Rui…
What on earth is this woman?
What is she to these monsters—?)

source.japanese: 殿下と呼ぶ、その尊称は貴き主上に捧げられるものにして、魚怪達にとっては泪こそ上にいただくべき存在であるらしく、どこまでも遜る、引き換え泪の言葉は俗といえたのに、魚怪を圧する威厳を具え、朔屋をいよいよ混乱させる。
source.english: Your Highness. A title of reverence reserved for exalted royalty. To the fish-monsters, Rui apparently belonged above them, to be honored and obeyed. They humbled themselves without end. By contrast, her words were almost commonplace, yet carried a majesty that overwhelmed the monsters and left Sakuya more confused than ever.

source.japanese:
常人としてはあるまじきほどの妖しい美しさを纏う女だとは感じていた知ってもいた。だがだからといって、人外の域に棲むモノだと言われては容易に首肯しかねる。
　けれども、魚怪達のこの振る舞いは。
　そして両者の眸[ひとみ]の相似は。
　やはり、泪は───
source.english:
He had felt—had known—that the woman's uncanny beauty exceeded anything an ordinary person should possess. But it was not easy to accept that she therefore belonged among things outside humanity.
And yet the monsters' behavior.
And the resemblance between their pupils.
Then Rui really was—

target.text: 【Fish monster】 『It is no disgrace……at all……. Your Imperial Highness…… was deceived……』
【Fish monster】 『The blame…… lies with the deceiver……』
【Fish monster】 『Your Imperial Highness…… put that blackguard to death……. Though there are those amongst us who extol that deed……』
【Fish monster】 『There exists not…… a single amongst us…… who would dare to scoff……』
【Rui】 『……How long do you intend to keep reminding me of the past? Whatever passed between that gentleman and I has long since ended. Yes, it all came to an end long, long ago.』
【Rui】 『I am certain my dear father is no different. Forever dragging with him matters of the distant past. All of you are the same. ───Haah. This is why I loathe you.』
【Naomasa】 （These guys are talking about Rui……. Just what the hell is this woman? She's just sitting here with all these monsters and───）

They called her Imperial Highness, but despite that honorific being something one would use to address an exalted emperor, it seemed that, to these fish monsters, Rui in particular ought to be treated with even greater reverence, for they were thoroughly debasing themselves, and even though by contrast, Rui's words could be called base, they possessed a majesty that dominated the fish monsters, and it all just made Sakuya more and more confused.

As a commoner, he knew and felt that she was a woman wrapped in such bewitching beauty that he was entirely unworthy of her. And yet, be that as it may, for her to be deemed a dweller of realms inhuman was not a claim he could so easily assent to. However, the behaviour of these fish monsters. And the resemblance of their pupils. In the end, Rui had to be───

source.japanese:
【泪】
『引きずっているのは、わたくしだって。
　それを想い出してしまうから。
　だから、戻りたくない。
　そんなつもりなんてない』
source.english:
“I drag it with me too.
Going back would make me remember.
That is why I don't want to return.
I have no intention of it.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『───おべっか、お追従。
　そんなもの、どれだけぶら下げてきたって。
　来るだけ、無駄というもの、お前たち』
source.english:
“Flattery. Blandishments.
Bring all you please dangling from your lips.
Your coming here was still a waste.”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『なんと仰有いましょうとも……。
　我らのこの体、この心……。
　全て殿下に捧げられたものにて……』
source.english:
“Whatever… you may say…
our bodies… our hearts…
All are dedicated… to Your Highness…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『久遠の忠義を仕るのみ……』
source.english: “We serve… in everlasting loyalty…”

source.japanese:
言葉を証すように、魚怪達はまた彼女の足下に跪き、足へ口づけしていく。まるで女王へ拝謁するかのよう、いや、まるでではない、まさにそれそのもの。
　泪自身はいつもの気怠げな風情のままで、化け物達を睥睨している。おぞましいくせに、それでいて淫靡な空気が漂う情景だった。
source.english:
As if to prove their words, the fish-monsters knelt again at her feet and kissed them, like subjects granted an audience with a queen. No—not like one. This was precisely that.
Rui looked down upon the monsters with her usual languor. Horrifying though the scene was, a lascivious air hung over it.

source.japanese:
【泪】
『退屈ね、お前たちは本当に。
　昔から、なにも変わっちゃいない』
source.english:
“You really are tedious.
Nothing has changed since the old days.”

target.text: 【Rui】 『And for that to be dragged up again and again. That means I will end up remembering it all, too. Therefore, I wish not to return. I have no intention of doing so at all.』
【Rui】 『───Flattery, sycophancy. No matter how you dangle such things before my eyes. Coming here at all is folly, you lot.』
【Fish monster】 『Whatever words may be spoken……. Our bodies, our souls……. All have been given unto Your Imperial highness……』
【Fish monster】 『We merely serve with eternal devotion……』

As if to prove their words true, the fish monsters once more knelt at the woman's feet, kissing them. It was almost like they were having an audience with a queen; no, not almost, it was exactly that. As ever, Rui herself remained in her usual languid state, looking down upon the monsters with contempt in her eyes. It was a ghastly scene, and yet still one pervaded by a lascivious air.
【Rui】 『How tiresome you are, truly. Not a single thing has changed from the past.』

source.japanese:
【泪】
『それは、なんのおつもり？
　そんな冷たい接吻なんて。
　寝惚けた殿方の、ふやけたキッスの方が、
　まだ、ずっとずっとまし』
source.english:
“What is that supposed to be?
Such cold kisses.
Even the soggy kiss of a half-asleep gentleman is far, far better.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『まだ温かいわ。熱い血潮が通っていらっしゃる。お前たちには、それさえない』
source.english: “At least it is warm. There is hot blood running through him. You don't even have that.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『……そうねえ。
　お前たち、わたくしを愉[たの]しませてみせなさい』
source.english:
“…Well,
then. Amuse me.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『どんな下らない喜劇だっていい。
　それでなければ、下手な悲劇でもいい。
　この退屈を、
　一時なりとも払ってごらんなさい』
source.english:
“Any foolish comedy will do.
Or, failing that, a badly acted tragedy.
Dispel this boredom, if only for a moment.”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『我ら……殿下の刃であり、具足であり……。
　なれども、舌先や虚言にて……、
　殿下をお慰めする術など……不調法にて』
source.english:
“We are… Your Highness's blades… and armor…
But with words… and falsehoods…
we lack the skill… to entertain you…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『それがお望みであるなら……。
　道化の一匹なり、連れて参ったものを』
source.english:
“Had we known… that was your wish…
we would have brought… a jester…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『女一人の興さえ、他人任せ？
　わたくしは、お前たちに求めているのよ。
　数ばかり揃えて、ご自分ではそんな事もできないと、そうおっしゃる』
source.english:
“You would leave even one woman's amusement to somebody else?
It is you I am asking.
You came in such numbers, yet claim you cannot manage even that yourselves?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『それくらいの機知もないのなら、そうねえ。
　お前……そちらのお前。向こうのお前。
　どなたでもいいわ』
source.english:
“If you haven't even that much wit, then…
You. You over there. You at the back.
Anyone will do.”

target.text: 【Rui】 『So then, what is the meaning of this? A buss so bereft of warmth. The indolent kiss of a gentleman half asleep would still be far, far preferable to this.』
【Rui】 『It would still be warm. Hot blood would course through his lips. And you lot, you can't even muster that little.』
【Rui】 『……That's right. See to it that you lot entertain me.』
【Rui】 『Any paltry comedy shall suffice. Failing that, a tactless tragedy will also serve. Even may it only be temporary, rid me of this boredom.』
【Fish monster】 『We……are Your Imperial Highness' blade, and armour……. Howbeit, by smooth words or falsehoods alike……, our means of consoling Your Imperial Highness……are inept.』
【Fish monster】 『Had we but known that to be your desire……. We would have brought a jester for your amusement.』

【Rui】 『You would leave even the entertainment of a single woman to others? This is something I demand of YOU. Having assembled in such a large flock, you are unable to achieve even such a trifle by yourselves; is that what you proclaim?』
【Rui】 『If you are so witless, then, yes. You……and you over there. And you on the other side. I care not who exactly it is.』

source.japanese:
【泪】
『わたくしを、抱いて下さいな。
　冷たい肌、滑る鱗[うろこ]。青臭いおとこのもので。
　わたくしの体、愉しませて？』
source.english:
“Take me, please.
Your cold skin, your slippery scales. That rank-smelling manhood of yours.
Give my body pleasure.”

source.japanese:
───嬉しげな、聞いた者の情火を心地良く高める媚声を立てるのだろうか。
　生々しいほどに艶やかな、耳にしただけで、最高の技前で雄の器官の快楽の帯を隈無く扱かれ舐められ揉まれ、ありとあらゆる愛撫の限りを尽くされたような絶後の快美に包まれて、精液を零してしまいそうな、そんな声だろうか。
source.english:
—Would she purr with pleasure, in a coaxing voice that sweetly fanned the listener's fire?
Would it be a voice so nakedly sensual that merely hearing it felt like having every sensitive part of a man's organ stroked, licked and kneaded with consummate skill—every conceivable caress lavished upon it—until an ecstasy beyond compare wrapped around him and threatened to spill his seed on the spot?

source.japanese: 貫かれてうねらせる、腰や胸の柔肉の有り様は、どれだけ淫らである事だろう。
source.english: How wanton the soft flesh of her hips and breasts must look, rippling as she was pierced.

source.japanese: それはきっと、まだ月のものを迎えていない少女でさえ、股間の裂け目が、排泄のためだけのモノではなく、もっと心地好い、愉悦の為にあるのだと知り始めたばかりの娘でさえ、声だけで未成熟の襞[ひだ]と包皮被った淫核にウットリする震動を送りこまれ、処女の膜に硬い膣口からさえも濃い愛蜜を溢れさせて達してしまいそうな。
source.english: Surely even a grown virgin whose monthly blood had never come, only beginning to understand that the cleft between her legs existed not merely for excretion but for a sweeter purpose—for pleasure—would feel that voice send rapturous tremors through her untouched folds and hooded clitoris, until rich honey overflowed the tight entrance sealed by her maidenhead and brought her almost to climax.
