source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『……なんと！
　……畏れ多き……ことに……ございます』
source.english:
“…What!
…Such… presumption…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『殿下の……玉体に……指の先なりとも……。
　触れて……しまっては……』
source.english:
“Were we… to lay so much as a fingertip…
upon Your Highness's sacred person…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『この身……千に引き裂かれましょう……。
　償いようのない……罪科と……。
　なりましょう』
source.english:
“Then this body… would be torn into a thousand pieces…
Such an offense…
could never be atoned for…”

target.text: 【Fish monster】 『……Preposterous! ……Such would be……far too…… great an honour.』
【Fish monster】 『Even should just……the tip of my finger……touch……. Your Imperial Highness'…… august person……』
【Fish monster】 『May this mortal flesh…… be rent into a thousand pieces……. It would surely stand…… as a transgression……. Beyond redemption.』

source.japanese:
【泪】
『……ふう。足には接吻できても、
　女一人、抱く気概もないというわけ……。
　だから駄目なのよ、お前たちでは』
source.english:
“…Ah. You can kiss a foot,
but you haven't the courage to take one woman to bed.
That's why you will never do.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（ああ全くだっ。
　なんでお前ら、この女を前にして、
　手の一つも出さない）
source.english:
(You're damn right.
With this woman in front of you,
why don't you even make a move?)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（やっぱりアレか。
　魚は発情期がこないと、
　交尾一つもできないってか？）
source.english:
(Is that it?
Fish can't even mate
unless it's breeding season?)

source.japanese: と魚怪達の不甲斐なさを罵ったのは室内の泪も朔屋も同じであったが、向こうはなかば予想していたように、失望と言うより皮肉の溜め息、一方朔屋は浅ましさも著けく、自分では泪に挑もうともしないくせに魚怪達を嘲罵する、どうにも情けない。
source.english: Rui and Sakuya both condemned the fish-monsters' inadequacy. But she seemed to have expected it; her sigh was more ironic than disappointed. Sakuya, on the other hand, was plainly contemptible. He mocked the monsters without daring to make a move on Rui himself. A sorry spectacle.

source.japanese:
【泪】
『口先でもできない。体でもいけないという。
　───お前たちには、わたくしがどういう気持ちで地上をぶらぶらしているのか……』
source.english:
“You cannot do it with words.
You cannot do it with your bodies. You have no idea what I feel, wandering about on land…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『まあ、他の方の胸の裡なんて、そもそも判りっこないものだけれど───それでも』
source.english: “Of course, no one can truly know what lies in another's heart. But even so—”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『ここで少しくらい奮い立ち、女一人愉しませようともしない』
source.english: “Even here, you cannot rouse yourselves enough to try pleasing one woman.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『そんなつまらない方々のところには。
　どうあっても戻るつもりなど、
　ありません』
source.english:
“To such tedious creatures as you,
I have no intention of returning.
None at all.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『退がりなさい、お前たち───
　この船の方々、お嘆きでしてよ。
　お前たちの跡で、お掃除が大変……って』
source.english:
“Leave, all of you.
The people of this ship are most distressed.
Cleaning up after you is such a burden, they say…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『このような穢[けが]れた船などに……、
　殿下が……お乗りあそばしている事のほうが』
source.english:
“That Your Highness… should be traveling…
upon so defiled a ship…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『由々しき……事態にて……』
source.english: “Is itself… a matter of grave concern…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（おーおー、言ってくれるじゃねえかよう。
　魚どもにも、穢れた船ときた。
　……はぁ……言い返せねぇわ……）
source.english:
(Oh, very nice. Very nice indeed.
Even the fish call it a filthy ship.
…Ah… Can't exactly argue…)

source.japanese:
【泪】
『……下らない舌で囀らないで。
　それでもこれくらいなら、
　伝えられるでしょう』
source.english:
“…Do not prattle with those worthless tongues.
Surely even they can carry this much of a message.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『伝えなさい、父上に───
　わたくし、まだ……いいえ、
　この先ずっと』
source.english:
“Tell my father:
I still… No.
From now on, forever—”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『そちらには戻りません、と』
source.english: “I will not return.”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『殿下……』
source.english: “Your Highness…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『───退がれ、と言ったわ。
　二度も言わせて、まだ言わせるおつもり？
　お前たち如きが？』
source.english:
“I told you to leave. You have made me say it twice.
Do you intend to make me say it again?
The likes of you?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『怒ること、とりのぼせること。
　それはそれで素敵な心の昂ぶりだけどね。
　お前たち相手では、
　どうにも甲斐がありません』
source.english:
“Anger. Losing one's head.
They are lovely stirrings of the heart, in their way.
But wasted upon you.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『けれども。
　これ以上退屈させるようなら───』
source.english:
“However.
If you persist in boring me—”

source.japanese:
泪は、傍にあるだけで男の心を狂おしく掻き乱し、しまいには破滅させる女ではあるけれど、その挙措、物言いは何時だって淑やかで、折に触れ意外な侠と茶目っ気を見せる事はあっても、ここまでの威と力を秘めた眼差しと言葉、部屋の外にある朔屋でさえ竦み上がって平伏しそうになるほどの、これは青年の知らない泪であった。
　ましてまともに真っ向から放りつけられた魚怪達にあってはひとたまりもなく、強風に吹かれた稲穂のようなもの、皆ばたばたと額を床に擦りつけ、贅を凝らした絨毯に粘液の筋残し、声を絞り出すのがやっとの様子、
source.english:
Rui might madden a man's heart merely by being near him, and eventually destroy him, but her bearing and speech were always gentle. At times she displayed surprising spirit or playfulness. Yet eyes and words containing this much authority, this much power—enough to make Sakuya, outside the room, nearly fall prostrate in terror—belonged to a Rui he did not know.
The fish-monsters facing her directly had no defense. Like ears of rice before a strong wind, they all bowed down at once, rubbing their foreheads against the floor, leaving trails of slime across the sumptuous carpet. Barely able to force out their voices—

target.text: 【Rui】 『……Hmph. So you can kiss feet, but you lack the backbone to lay with but a single woman……. That is why you are useless to me.』
【Naomasa】 （Yeah, you're damn right. How can you guys kneel in front of a woman like that, and then not even lay so much as a finger on her?）
【Naomasa】 （It's gotta be that, right? What was it again, unless it's breeding season, fish can't mate even once or something?）

And so both Rui within the room and Sakuya outside it similarly insulted the fecklessness of the fish monsters, but for her part, it was as though she had mostly anticipated the response, for her sigh was more cynical than disappointed; meanwhile, Sakuya's wretchedness was all too plain to see, for he was taunting the fish monsters in spite of his own inability to even make an attempt at courting Rui, how utterly pathetic.
【Rui】 『You can not accomplish it with lip service. Nor with your bodies. ───How could you possibly fathom what feelings I bear as I idly wander the surface……』
【Rui】 『Well, not that the heart of another has ever been something that could truly be understood, but───even so.』
【Rui】 『Here you are, unable to lift a lone woman's spirits even a little, unable to show her a good time.』
【Rui】 『No matter what may happen, returning to where such dull people dwell is something I have no intention of.』
【Rui】 『Withdraw at once, you lot─── The people aboard this ship lament your presence. Cleaning the mess left in your wake is hard work……they said.』
【Fish monster】 『For Your Imperial Highness…… to graciously sail……、 aboard this tainted a vessel.』
【Fish monster】 『Is the graver…… state of affairs……』
【Naomasa】 （Well, well, look who's talking big now. So even the fishmen think it's a tainted ship. ……Haah……I can't really argue with that……）
【Rui】 『……Spare me the babbling of your worthless tongue. Even so, a message of this clarity should still be within your abilities to convey.』
【Rui】 『You shall convey this to my father─── I am still……no, henceforth, and for all remaining time.』
【Rui】 『I shall never return to you.』
【Fish monster】 『Your Imperial Highness……』
【Rui】 『───I told you to withdraw, did I not? Do you dare to make me repeat once more what I have already declared twice? The likes of you?』
【Rui】 『Anger, and being carried away by it. That in itself is a wonderful stirring of the heart, yes? But when directed at you lot, there is precious little reward to be found in it.』
【Rui】 『Although. Should you attempt to bore me any further, then───』

Rui. A woman who stirred chaos and madness in the hearts of men merely from being by their side, a woman who ultimately led them to their ruin, yet her movements, her manner of speech, were all ever gracefully ladylike no matter the occasion, and though she would at times show a surprisingly pert playfulness should the chance arise, her words and gaze now contained such majesty and power within them, even Sakuya outside the room cowered with fear and almost prostrated himself; certainly, this was a Rui that the young man was wholly unfamiliar with.

And that was to say nothing of how it must have felt when you had them hurled directly at you; the fish monsters stood no chance, and like ears of rice buffeted by a gale, they all tumbled to the floor, foreheads scraping against it, leaving trails of slimy liquid on the carpet woven with opulent artistry, and they seemed barely able to wring out their voices,

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『殿下……。
　我らはただ、殿下の御心に……従うのみ。
　……退き……ましょう……いまは……』
source.english:
“Your Highness…
We obey… your wishes alone…
We shall… withdraw… for now…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『なれど……主上の御心は……。
　常に……いかなる時であろうとも……。
　殿下の……御許に向かっておられる事』
source.english:
“But His Majesty's heart…
always… at every moment…
turns toward… Your Highness…”

source.japanese:
───魚怪達の主上。
　───泪が父上と呼ぶ何者か。
　───両者が同じであるのなら。
source.english:
The fish-monsters' sovereign.
The being Rui called Father.
If they were one and the same—

source.japanese:
この泪は。
　人の形をしていても。
　やはり魚怪達と同じく。
　朔屋と同じ人間、ではないのか───
source.english:
Then Rui.
Though she had a human form.
Like the fish-monsters themselves.
Could she be something other than human, unlike Sakuya—?

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『それだけは……どうか……。
　御心に……留め置かれますよう……』
source.english:
“That alone… we beg you…
to keep… in your heart…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『されば……退出……仕る……』
source.english: “Then… we take… our leave…”

source.japanese: 泪の威に撃たれ、立ちどころも据わりどころもなく魚怪どもが身じろぎし、退出の気配を見せたのに朔屋、慌てて扉から身を起こし、泪の部屋から離れて通路の奥へ、魚怪達と同じ向きではないことをただ念じて遠ざかる。
source.english: Struck by Rui's authority, the fish-monsters shifted restlessly, unable to stand or sit still, and began to show signs of departing. Sakuya hurriedly straightened up from the doorway and fled down the passage, away from Rui's cabin, praying only that he had not chosen the same direction they would take.

target.text: 【Fish monster】 『Your Imperial Highness……. We serve only in accordance…… with the will of Your Imperial Highness. ……We shall……withdraw…… for now……』
【Fish monster】 『Howbeit……His Imperial Majesty's heart……. Will ever be…… whatever times may come……. Directed towards…… Your Imperial Highness.』
───The emperor of these fish monsters. ───Someone that Rui called father. ───And if they were both one and the same, then.
Then Rui was. Even if she took the form of a human. In the end, she was just like these fish monsters. So was she not human like Sakuya was───?
【Fish monster】 『Pray……may that sentiment alone……. Ever remain……within your heart……』
【Fish monster】 『Then……we humbly…… withdraw……』

Struck by Rui's majesty, the fish monsters were left with neither a place to stand nor sit as they stirred, and as they began to show signs of withdrawing, Sakuya quickly rose from the door in a panic, distancing himself from Rui's room by running further into the depths of the passage, just silently praying that he had not chosen the same direction as the fish monsters while he moved further away.

source.japanese: どうにかここでも偶然は朔屋に味方して、彼の背後で魚怪どもがぞろぞろと退散していく気配、跫音が伝わる───
source.english: Chance somehow favored him again. Behind him, the sounds, the footsteps of the monsters filing away—

source.japanese: ───この夜はこれ以上の怪異はなく、あったとしてももう耐えきれぬと自分の船室に駆け戻って毛布を被った朔屋には知りようもなかったけれど、もちろん彼に安らかな眠りの恩恵など与えられる筈もなかったのだった。
source.english: No further apparition troubled him that night—or if one did, Sakuya could not have known. Unable to endure any more, he ran back to his cabin and pulled a blanket over his head. Naturally, he was not granted the blessing of peaceful sleep.

target.text: Somehow, coincidence was on Sakuya's side this time as well, for behind him, he felt the stream of fish monsters shuffling off in retreat, the sound of their footsteps reaching him───

───There were no more mysterious happenings this night, and even if there were, Sakuya, who could no longer put up with it and so had rushed back to his cabin, then pulled a thick blanket over his head, would certainly know nothing about it, but of course, there was no chance that he would be granted the blessing of peaceful sleep tonight.

source.japanese:
───船内通路の窓から斜めなりに差しこむ朝の光は、この襤褸船の中にあっても爽快で、というより無駄に眩しくて、昨夜の妖異極まりない事象など吐き散らすかのようではあったが。光の線を一歩外れれば、他が鮮烈であるだけ影の部分のみずぼらしさ、荒れた気色は余計顕著で、影になっている箇所には、昨夜の魚怪達の持ちこんだ狭霧がいまだ蟠っているように錯覚させるほどに、暗い。
　同様に、朔屋の心中には泪への警戒心、それもこれまでの畏怖に上乗せされた恐怖が色濃く蟠り、女好きの青年をして、もう二度と泪に無警戒には近づくまいとの決意をより新たにさせた。
source.english:
Morning light slanted through the passage windows, refreshing even inside this wreck—or rather, dazzling to no purpose, as though it meant to spit out every uncanny event of the night. Step outside one of those shafts, however, and its brilliance only made the shabby, dilapidated shadows more conspicuous. They were so dark that one could imagine last night's fish-monsters had left their mist brooding there still.
Within Sakuya, too, suspicion of Rui lay thick: fear layered over his old awe, enough to renew even this inveterate woman-chaser's resolve never again to approach her unguarded.

source.japanese: 昨夜泪の船室から逃げ出した朔屋は、その足で水夫長に報せればいいものを（寝ているところを叩き起こす結果になったろうが、事態が事態だ、許してくれた筈）、自分の部屋に腰を抜かす寸前のほうほうの体で這うように戻り、結局朝までまんじりと過ごす事になった。船室の窓から室内を明るくする光と、鳴き交わす信天翁の声で朝を知ってから、ようやく水夫長の部屋まで足を運ぶ気になった朔屋の、無論臆病者は臆病者だが、この朝ばかりは強く責められまい。誰とて異界異妖の恐怖と遭遇して、心を凪に保っていられるものはいないのである。
source.english: After fleeing Rui's cabin, Sakuya ought to have gone straight to the boatswain. He would have had to wake him, but surely the circumstances would have earned forgiveness. Instead he had all but crawled back to his own room, on the verge of his legs giving out, and spent the rest of the night awake. Only when light brightened the cabin and albatrosses called to one another outside, announcing morning, did he feel able to visit the boatswain. A coward he certainly was, but one could hardly blame him too severely this morning. No one encounters the terrors of another world and keeps an untroubled heart.

source.japanese: こういう次第で、船内通路の朝の光と影の中に交互に現れ隠れしながら水夫長の部屋へと急ぐ朔屋、周囲に魚人共の痕跡が残されていないかどうか、目配せも抜かりなく、と思っているのは本人だけ。もう少し落ち着きのあれば、秘密警察長官へ報告に馳せ参ずる間諜、と下駄を履かせてやってもいいところを、こうもきょときょと、猫背で視線が定まらない姿は、兵隊さんならせいぜいがところ鬼教官に告げ口に行く三等兵の面構え、昇進には程遠い。
source.english: Thus Sakuya hurried toward the boatswain's cabin, now appearing, now vanishing amid the passageway's morning light and shadow, all the while casting what he alone supposed were vigilant glances about for traces of the fish-monsters. With a little more composure, one might generously have called him a spy racing to report to the chief of the secret police. But all that twitchy peering, that hunched back and wandering gaze gave him, in military terms, at best the look of a third-class private off to tattle to a demonic drill instructor. Promotion was a distant dream.

target.text: ───The rays of the morning sun streaming diagonally through the portholes and into the ship's passageways were, even on this ramshackle vessel, invigorating, or rather, needlessly dazzling, as though violently purging the utterly uncanny phenomena of yesternight, but. If one walked but a step away from those beams of light, the brilliance of the rest only rendered the shadowed parts into a sight all the more shabby, their dilapidated appearance all the more pronounced, with the portions cloaked in shadow clad in such darkness that it could induce a hallucination as though the mist those fish monster from last night had brought with them yet swirled around.

Similarly, in Sakuya's heart lingered a deep-seated wariness towards Rui, a fear only compounded by the daunting dread he had felt hitherto, festering intensely within him, renewing the resolve of this young man, womanizer though he may be, to never again approach Rui heedlessly.

After running away from Rui's cabin last night, Sakuya regretted not just heading straight to the Bosun to inform him like he should have (he would have needed to rouse him from his bed, but the situation being what it was, he would surely have been forgiven), but on the verge of his legs giving out under him, his scuttling body almost crawling back to his cabin on all fours, ultimately, he spent the night dozing off until morning arrived.

Once the bright glow lighting up his room from the porthole and the din of the albatrosses screeching at one another informed him it was morning, Sakuya finally felt inclined to make his way to the Bosun's room, and of course, while a coward remains a coward, on this morning alone, we shall not reproach him too sternly for it. Confronted with the terror of otherworldly monsters, no man can keep his heart calm as still waters.

Through these circumstances, Sakuya found himself rushing towards the Bosun's cabin, alternating between emerging in the light and vanishing back into the shadows of the ship's passageways, scanning for any traces of the fishmen that might have been left in his surroundings, though only he himself believed his actions to be meticulous. Had he only been a little more composed, he might have passed for a spy hastening along to deliver a report to the chief of the secret police, but when looking around so restlessly with his back hunched, at best, he had the look of a lowly private sneaking off to snitch to the demonic drill sergeant; promotion yet remained a distant dream.

source.japanese: 水夫長の船室のドアを叩くと、入れの許しがあって扉を開ければ、背筋を伸ばして船窓に向かい、一冊の書物を聖具のように朝日に掲げ立つ姿、朔屋とは違い流石に堂々としたものだが───
source.english: He knocked on the boatswain's door, received permission to enter, and opened it. There stood a man with his back straight, facing the porthole, holding a book up to the morning sun as though it were a sacred object. Unlike Sakuya, a thoroughly imposing figure—but—

target.text: As he knocked on the door to the Bosun's cabin, then opened the door after receiving permission to enter, there stood a figure facing the porthole, back straightened, holding up high a singular tome to the morning sun like it were a ritual implement, and in stark contrast to Sakuya, he certainly was as confidently imposing as one would expect of him, but───

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……うむう……。
　寝覚めの一冊は、詩集に限る。
　エドワード・フィッツジェラルド訳、
『ルバイヤート』───」
source.english:
“…Mmm…
For the first book of the day, nothing beats poetry.
The Rubaiyat,
translated by Edward FitzGerald—”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「昨夜の酒が綺麗に抜けた後だと、
　この酒を謳った詩文の韻の、
　なんと清しい事か」
source.english:
“Once last night's drink has cleared the system,
how refreshing the rhymes of these verses
in praise of wine!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「朝っぱらからシュールな光景見せつけんで下さいよ水夫長……」
source.english: “Please don't make me look at something this surreal first thing in the morning, Boatswain…”

source.japanese:
船の中では古参の先任軍曹格にあり、下士官、先輩としての水夫のありとあらゆる手本であり、降り注ぐ拳、怒鳴りつける口、それら全ての総代である水夫長が朝っぱらから詩だの韻だのほざいていては、地獄の羅卒の猿股がレースの刺繍入りで小さなハートのリボンがついているようなもので、全くしめしがつかない。
　おまけに、脱力しそうになって戸柱にすがった朔屋に、恥じ入る事もなく怒鳴りつけているから、今後も水夫長の習慣が改められる事はないだろう。
source.english:
Aboard ship, the boatswain ranked as a veteran sergeant: noncommissioned officer, senior hand, exemplar of all a sailor ought to be, the embodiment of every fist that rained down and every mouth that roared. To hear such a man spouting poetry and rhyme first thing in the morning was like discovering that the jailers of hell wore lace-embroidered drawers trimmed with tiny heart-shaped bows. It ruined all discipline.
Worse, he bellowed without the least shame at Sakuya, who had nearly gone limp and caught himself on the doorpost. Plainly the boatswain's habits were in no danger of reform.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Hummm……. Nothing beats a poetry collection as the first book of the morning. Translated by Edward FitzGerald, 『Rubaiyat』───」
【Bosun】 「After the drink of last night has worn off in full, from the rhyme of poetry extolling alcohol, how delightfully refreshing a purity that flows.」
【Naomasa】 「Bosun, please don't show me something this surreal so early in the morning……」

Aboard this ship he held the rank of a veteran senior sergeant, and as a petty officer and a senior sailor both, he was an exemplar in every conceivable way; fists falling like cascading rain, loud and furious shouting, the Bosun was a stellar representative of it all, and here he was, at this ungodly hour, prattling on about rhymes in poetry; it was like a demonic warden of Hell wearing underwear embroidered with lace and adorned with a little heart-shaped ribbon, what a truly terrible example it set.

And on top of all that, he did not feel deeply ashamed, no, he instead yelled angrily at Sakuya who clung to the side jamb of the door in exhaustion, and so it seemed unlikely that the Bosun's habits would be amended hereafter.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「やかましい。乗船して以来俺に活字の打たれた紙を一枚もよこさん貴様に、意見する資格など鼻糞ほどもないわ」
source.english: “Shut your mouth. Since coming aboard, you haven't given me so much as one sheet of printed paper. You haven't a booger's worth of right to criticize.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You're too noisy. You haven't handed me a single page with text printed on it since you boarded this ship, so you've got less right to have an opinion than the boogers in my nose.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そんなてめえがなにしにきやがった、それこそ朝っぱらから。
　お前の仕事なら、頼まれんでも山ほど用意してあるぜえ……」
source.english:
“What brings you here, then? At this hour, no less.
If it's work you want, I've got mountains ready, without being asked…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなあんた……当直明けの船員にちっとは加減ってものを……いやそうじゃなく、昨夜の事なんですが」
source.english: “Come on… Have a little mercy on a sailor just off watch… No, that's not it. About last night.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ほらあんた、俺に夜回り、言いつけたでしょうが」
source.english: “You told me to make the night rounds, remember?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「I should be asking you what the hell you came here for this early in the morning. If it's for work, I've already got a mountain of things prepared for you, so you don't have to come ask for more……」
【Naomasa】 「Come on, man……go a little easy on a sailor whose watch just ended…… no, forget that, this is about last night.」
【Naomasa】 「You know, you ordered me to do a night patrol, right?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう、それでどうだった……」
source.english: “Yeah. How'd it go…?”

source.japanese:
それなんですが、と言いかけて朔屋、言葉に詰まる。この部屋に来るまではただ、昨夜の怪異を水夫長に報告せねばの一念であったが、いざ彼の顔と向かい合うとなると逡巡してしまう。
　深夜の怪異に受けた衝撃は朔屋の心胆寒からせしめたけれど、水夫長の顔と向かい合うと悪い夢だったような気さえしてくるのに加え、それを告げたところで信用されるかどうにも怪しい。海の上ではなにが起こったところで不思議はない、というのが信天翁号に限らず船乗り達の不文律であるとはいえ、あんな、怪奇映画の特撮じみた異界異様の化け物の存在など、実際に舌に乗せてみればどれだけ陳腐化してしまうものか。
source.english:
Well, about that—Sakuya began, and stalled. Until he reached this room, he had thought of nothing but reporting last night's horrors. Now, face-to-face with the boatswain, he hesitated.
The midnight apparitions had chilled him to his core, yet looking at the boatswain made them seem almost like a bad dream. And would the man believe him anyway? Nothing that happened at sea was surprising: an unwritten law among sailors, not merely aboard the Albatross. Still, monsters from some other world, looking like effects from a horror movie—how tawdry they would become once he tried to put them into words.

source.japanese:
まして、泪の存在がある。
　あの艶麗な美女が魚怪どもと何やら誼[よしみ]を通じさせているらしい、などと言ってしまおうものなら、逆にこちらが讒訴と責め立ててられてしまうのではないかと、朔屋はそれを恐れた。自分の日頃の信用というものがどれだけ乏しいかをよくよく心得ているだけに。
source.english:
Then there was Rui.
Suggest that the exquisite beauty was somehow on intimate terms with fish-monsters, and perhaps he would find himself accused of slander instead. Sakuya feared that possibility, knowing all too well how little credibility he ordinarily possessed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ……その……それなんですが。
　実はですねえ」
source.english:
“Ah… Uh…
About that. Actually…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Sure did, what about it……」

"Yes, about that", Sakuya was on the verge of saying, but he found himself at a loss for words. Until he had made it to this cabin, the need to make a report to the Bosun about the monsters from last night was the only thing running through his mind, but now that he was face to face with him, he ended up hesitating.

The shock Sakuya had received from those monsters late at night had chilled him to the marrow of his bones, but now that he was looking the Bosun straight in the eyes, not only did it feel like he'd just had a bad dream, it was even looking doubtful that he'd actually be believed when he made the report. Anything could happen when out on the sea: even if that was an unwritten rule counting not just for the Albatross but any sailor, the existence of such otherworldly monsters that seemed like a product of special effects straight out of a horror movie, when he actually attempted to put that into words, how trite a cliche they tasted of upon his tongue.

Not to mention, there was the presence of Rui to consider. That dazzlingly beautiful women seemed on awfully friendly terms with those fish monsters for whatever reason, and if he were to say anything of that sort to another, was it not possible that he would conversely be accused of slander? That was what Sakuya feared. Precisely because he himself was all too painfully aware of just how little trust he normally commanded.
【Naomasa】 「Aaah……uhmm……so about that. The thing is, you see.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なんだよ、歯切れの悪い。
　あ。お前もしや。途中で寝ちまって、ろくに夜番もできなかったとか抜かすんじゃねえだろうなあ……」
source.english:
“Spit it out. Wait.
You didn't fall asleep halfway through, did you? Don't tell me you barely did the watch…”

source.japanese:
たやすく沸騰するのがこの水夫長、朔屋のはっきりしない口ぶりに業を煮やして、首筋に剣呑な血の管を浮かべていくのに、朔屋は慌てて思い切った。
　ままよ、誤解されたらされたでいい。見てしまった事をなにも告げないうちに鉄拳制裁される方がよほど精神衛生上よろしくない。
source.english:
The boatswain reached boiling point easily. As he lost patience with Sakuya's evasive mumbling, ominous veins began to rise along his neck. Sakuya hurriedly took the plunge.
To hell with it: let him misunderstand if he must. A beating before Sakuya had even reported what he saw would be far worse for his peace of mind.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや！　そんなことは！
　水夫長、これから俺が言う事は、酔っ払いの戯言でもなんでもない」
source.english:
“No! Nothing like that!
Boatswain, what I'm about to tell you isn't drunken rambling or anything of the sort.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「昨夜俺が酔っ払ってなかった事は、見回りの前にあったシサム・キサラにクロが証明してくれるはず」
source.english: “Sisam, Kisara, and Kuro saw me before my rounds. They can vouch for the fact that I wasn't drunk.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だから信じてくれなくたっていいが、今から言う事は嘘じゃない」
source.english: “So you don't have to believe me, but what I'm about to say isn't a lie.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What's wrong, get to the point. Ah. Could it be. Surely you're not here just to feed me some bullshit about how you fell asleep partway through and barely did any patrolling, are you……」

It was very like this bosun to reach his boiling point so quickly; he had lost his temper from Sakuya's vague way of speaking, and as ominous veins swelled prominently along his neck, Sakuya, in flustered haste, made a bold decision. To hell with it, if he was going to be misunderstood, then let it happen. Receiving a disciplinary beating by way of the Bosun's iron fists without even having reported what he ended up seeing would be far worse for his mental health.
【Naomasa】 「No! I would never! Bosun, what I'm about to tell you here now, it is absolutely not the rambling nonsense of a drunk, or anything like that.」
【Naomasa】 「I was not drunk last night, and that's something Shisamu, Kisara, and Kuro, who I met before patrolling, can attest to.」
【Naomasa】 「So while you're free to not believe it, what I'm about to tell you is not a lie.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……まわりくでぇな。だがてめえにしちゃいやに必死だ。いいよ、聞いてやるよ。
　とにかく言ってみろや。
　昨夜、一体何があった？　何を見た？」
source.english:
“…You're beating around the bush. But you're unusually desperate. Fine, I'll hear you out.
Just tell me.
What the hell happened last night? What did you see?”

source.japanese: 朔屋の懸命な口ぶりにほだされたか、珍しく物分かりのいいところを見せた水夫長に、息を整えさあ伝えようと身構えた、そこに。
source.english: Perhaps Sakuya's earnestness had moved him. The boatswain showed an unusual willingness to listen. Sakuya steadied his breathing and braced himself to speak. Just then—
“Last night—”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……You're being real roundabout. But you're also sounding unusually desperate. Fine, I'm all ears. Just try spitting it out. What the hell happened last night? You see something?」
Perhaps he was moved by how earnestly Sakuya spoke, for the Bosun displayed an unusually understanding side of himself, and Sakuya caught his breath, braced himself to tell him all, and just then.
【Naomasa】 「So, last night───」

source.japanese: 言葉を横からさらったのは。
source.english: The voice that stole his words from the side—

target.text: Brushing away his words from the side was.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「昨夜……？
　昨夜なんて、なにかありまして？」
source.english:
“Last night…?
Did something happen last night?”

source.japanese:
朝の光が一瞬にして薄氷のように薄く脆く砕け散っていくかの朔屋の気力は昨夜の怪の主役の登場にたちまち萎[な]えて、言葉は萎[しぼ]んだ。
　泪が、朔屋の背後の壁に泰然と背を預け、微笑んでいた。他の者に聞かれるを恐れてしかと閉めたはずの扉が開く気配も、跫音の軋みもたてずいつの間にか。
source.english:
As though the morning light had turned thin and brittle as skim ice, then shattered, Sakuya's courage crumbled at the arrival of last night's central figure. His words withered.
Rui was leaning serenely against the wall behind him, smiling. He had shut the door firmly, afraid of being overheard. Yet she had appeared without any sign of the door opening, without so much as the creak of a footstep. Somehow.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「る、泪さ……っ」
source.english: “M-Ms. Rui…!”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Last night……? Are you claiming anything of note happened last night?」

As the eerie leading actress of last night took to the stage, Sakuya's resolve, brittle and thin as ice shattering in an instant before the light of the morning sun, withered at once, and the well from which his words were drawn also turned bone-dry. Rui calmly leaned her back against the wall behind Sakuya, smiling. The door he had firmly shut lest others overhear never gave off any sign of being opened, nor had there been any creaking of footsteps to be heard, and yet, all of a sudden.
【Naomasa】 「Ru-, Rui-sa……!」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「泪女史……船員の私室には、みだりに立ち入らんでほしいですな」
source.english: “Madam Rui… I'd prefer you not to enter the crew's private cabins without permission.”

source.japanese: 苦りきる水夫長に構った風もなく、
source.english: She showed no concern for the boatswain's displeasure.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Madam Rui……I must ask you not to enter the private cabins of the crew without permission.」
Without showing any concern for the scowling Bosun,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「だって、ねえ……。気になりますもの。
　わたくし、昨夜もそれはそれは退屈で。
　眠れなくって、お船の中を、
　一回りしてみました」
source.english:
“But you see… I am curious.
Last night I was so very, very bored.
I couldn't sleep,
so I took a little turn about the ship.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Well, you see……. I simply thought it curious. Last night, I was so dreadfully bored. I couldn't sleep, and so I tried making a round of the ship.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「その時は、こちらの直さんとはお目に掛かれなかったみたいだけれど」
source.english: “I don't seem to have met Nao here while I was out.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「While I did so, however, it seems I never had the pleasure of running into Nao-san over here.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「しかたなくて、お部屋に戻った後でも、やっぱり、なぁんにもする事なくって」
source.english: “I had no choice but to return to my room. And still there was nothing, nothing to do.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It ended up being of no avail, and even after returning to my room, as expected, there was still nothing at all to occupy me.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そんなに退屈な夜でしたのに、直さんはなにかご覧になったご様子」
source.english: “Such a tedious night, and yet Nao appears to have seen something.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「なにかを見逃していたのなら、
　悔しいじゃないの。
　せっかく起きていたのに、
　もったいないわ」
source.english:
“If I missed something,
how disappointing.
I was awake, after all.
What a waste.”

source.japanese:
立てた人差し指を顎に当て、軽く口を尖らせる、蓮っ葉な娘がやれば軽薄で鼻につくが、この泪がそういった仕草を取ると、アンバランスに蠱惑的で、なればこそふらふらと寄っていく男が続出する、が、朔屋には、紅葉の幽谷に潜[ひそ]む鬼姫の美しい唇の内側の牙、蠱惑的であると同時に得体の知れない畏怖をもって迫ってくるのだ。
　じり、と何時でも水夫長の後ろに隠れられるように踵[かかと]を浮かせた。
source.english:
She touched a raised forefinger to her chin and pouted slightly. On a cheap, forward woman the gesture would have been irritatingly frivolous. On Rui, its incongruity was alluring; no wonder men drifted toward her in droves. To Sakuya, however, it was like the fangs behind the lovely lips of a demon princess concealed in an autumn-red ravine: alluring, yet bringing an unknowable dread close.
He lifted his heels a little, ready to slip behind the boatswain at any moment.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Yet despite it being such a boring night, Nao-san has the look of a man who witnessed something interesting.」
【Rui】 「If I happened to have overlooked something, wouldn't that be rather disappointing? Since I was awake and all, it would be such a shame.」

She placed her index finger on her chin, a delicate pout on her lips; if an impertinent girl were to do the same, the frivolity of it would grate on his nerves, but when Rui made such an expression, it was alluringly unbalanced, and that was exactly why so many men kept approaching her without thinking it through, but to Sakuya, like the fangs hiding behind the beautiful lips of the demoness who lurked within the secluded valley of crimson autumn leaves, it captivated him, yet at the same time loomed over him with an unfathomable dread. (TN: This is a reference to Momiji, a famous kijo, a female oni, slain in the Legend of Momiji.)
He shifted slightly, heels lifted off the floor so he could hide himself behind the Bosun whenever he should need to.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「泪女史、あんたはその時なにか不審な奴とか者とか見なかったか？」
source.english: “Madam Rui, did you see any suspicious people or things while you were out?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Madam Rui, did you happen to catch sight of any suspicious man or person at that time?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「さあ……。わたくしには、そのようなものには、なんにも、そうなんにも心当たり、ございません」
source.english: “Well… Of anything like that, I know nothing. No, nothing at all.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Well now……. I did not see anything of the sort, nothing at all. Indeed, I have no inkling as to who that could be.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……ってな事だが朔屋、おめえの方はなんか見たのかよ」
source.english: “…There you are, Sakuya. What about you? Did you see anything?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、俺は……その……」
source.english: “Well, I… Uh…”

source.japanese:
水夫長は泪の闖入に渋面を作ったもののそれ以上は咎めだてせず、泪は泪で実に落ち着き払って、昨夜の魚怪どもに傅[かしづ]かれていた様など毛ほども感じさせない小面憎さ。そして朔屋だけが、背筋に冷や汗伝うのを感じていた。
　泪がこんな朝から水夫長の部屋までやってきたのは、自分をつけ回しているからではないのか。昨夜の事を誰かに告げようものなら、どうなるか判っているのか。朔屋には泪が暗に脅迫してきているようにしか思えなかったのである。
　だから朔屋は───
source.english:
The boatswain had grimaced at Rui's intrusion but did not pursue the matter. Rui herself was infuriatingly composed, betraying not the faintest suggestion of the fish-monsters attending her last night.
Only Sakuya felt cold sweat trickling down his back. Had she come to the boatswain's room so early because she was following him? Was she there to warn him what would happen if he told anyone about last night? Sakuya could read her appearance only as an unspoken threat.
So—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「水夫君達はああ言っていたし、水夫長もこの船になにか入りこんでいるような事を言ってたけど、俺は何も見なかったス……」
source.english: “The sailors said all that, and you said something had got aboard too, Boatswain, but I didn't see anything, sir…”

source.japanese: 心とは裏腹な言葉で濁すしかなく───
source.english: He could only muddy the issue with words contrary to his heart—

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……So she says, but Sakuya, did you see anything?」
【Naomasa】 「No, I, uhh……well……」

While the Bosun made a surly face on account of Rui's sudden intrusion, he did not criticize her any further, and for her part, Rui remained thoroughly self-possessed, showing only a provocative pertness that betrayed not the slightest trace of having been waited upon by those fish monsters last night. And then there was Sakuya: he alone felt beads of cold sweat run down his back.

Was it not possible that Rui only came all the way to the Bosun's cabin this early in the morning because she had been shadowing him? "If you dare to so much as breathe a word about last night to anyone, do you know what will happen to you?" To Sakuya, it seemed only that Rui was implicitly threatening him. Therefore, Sakuya───
【Naomasa】 「I know the sailors said all that stuff, and you also said that it seemed like something had made its way onto the ship, Bosun, but I didn't see anything……」
He had no choice but to obscure the truth with words that ran contrary to his heart───

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ンだよ……。何もなかった事の報告かよ。
　まあこれでおめえだけがそう言ってンなら、
　まずさぼりを疑ったところだが───
　泪女史も同じ事を言っているもんな」
source.english:
“What…? You've come to report that nothing happened?
If you were the only one saying it,
I'd suspect you'd been slacking off.
But Madam Rui says the same.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ってことは、少なくともゆんべはなんもなかったって事か。わざわざンな事まで報告すんな、って言いたいところだが、まあおめえのゴクローサンには変わりねえ」
source.english: “Then at least nothing happened last night. I'd like to tell you not to bother reporting even that, but you still did your job.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What the hell……. So you're just here to report that nothing happened? Well, if you were the only one here saying that, then my first instinct would be to suspect you of having slacked off, but─── Madam Rui also said the same.」

【Bosun】 「Which means, at the very least, nothing happened at all last night? Don't even bother reporting something like that, is what I'd like to say, but it doesn't change the fact that I appreciate the effort.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ようしわかった。行ってええぞ朔屋。
　……あ、ちと待て」
source.english:
“All right, understood. Off you go,
Sakuya. …Ah, wait.”

source.japanese: 場の流れはすっかり泪と水夫長に主導権を握られている。そういう時に自分が何を言ったところで無駄と覚って朔屋、さっさと退散しようとしたところで呼びとめられた。もしや水夫長の中で何らかの不審が生じたのか？　自分が昨夜の怪異を告げる余地が生まれたのか？　気を取り直し立ち止まる朔屋に言いつけられたのは、
source.english: Rui and the boatswain had taken complete control of the situation. Realizing anything he said now would be useless, Sakuya was about to withdraw promptly when the man stopped him. Had something struck the boatswain as suspicious? Was there an opening to tell him about last night's horrors? His courage recovering, Sakuya halted. The order he received was—

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Alright, I got it. You can go now, Sakuya. ……Ah, just a second.」

Control over the flow of events here had been firmly grasped by Rui and the Bosun. Sakuya had learned that, in times like these, no matter what he said, it would be futile, and just as he made to leave right away, he was called back. Perhaps some manner of suspicion had arisen within the Bosun? Was there finally a chance for him to report on the monsters he'd seen last night? Sakuya pulled himself together and stopped in his tracks, and what he was told to do was:

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おめえの今日の仕事だよ。
　そうだな、操舵室の掃除してこいや」
source.english:
“Your work for today.
Let's see—go clean the wheelhouse.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……了解っす……」
source.english: “…Roger, sir…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Can't forget your work for today. Right, you go clean the wheelhouse.」
【Naomasa】 「……Roger that……」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なに鬱陶しい面してやがんだ、さっさと行けえ！　それとももっときっちい甲板掃除の方がええのか？　ああ！」
source.english: “What the hell's that miserable face for? Get going! Or would you rather have the harder job of scrubbing the deck? Eh!?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「朔屋直正、操舵室を全力で、
　掃除してきます！」
source.english:
“Naomasa Sakuya will clean the wheelhouse
with everything he's got!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What are you looking so damn glum for, move your ass! Or are you saying you'd like the much tougher task of cleaning the deck? HUH!?」
【Naomasa】 「I, Sakuya Naomasa, will go to the wheelhouse and clean it with all I have!」

source.japanese:
水夫長の胴間声に背中を叩かれて駆け出す。
　操舵室は日頃シサム・キサラが良く出入りするせいか、埃くらいは積もっても、船内の他の区画に比べて汚れは少ない。そして室内自体もさしたる広さはなく、掃除といっても片手間仕事のようなもの。目に着く汚れを落としておけば申し訳は立つし、後は今のところ何も言いつけられてはいない。
　となれば空いた時間を休息にあてるのは朔屋の自由であり、水夫長も当直明けの朔屋をそれくらいは慮ったのであろう。
　ただし、彼の温情とてその前でぐずぐずした様子を見せればいつまで続くか知れたものではない。
　だから朔屋は後は物も言わず上甲板に駆け出したし、泪とはもう言葉を交わす暇はなかった。
source.english:
The boatswain's bellow struck him in the back and sent him running.
Perhaps because Sisam and Kisara used it so often, the wheelhouse might collect dust, but was cleaner than the ship's other compartments. It was not particularly large, either. Cleaning it would be an easy little job. Remove the visible dirt, and he could consider the task done; he had no further orders yet.
Then he was free to spend the remaining time resting. The boatswain had probably shown that much consideration for a man just off watch.
His kindness, however, might not last if Sakuya dawdled in front of him.
So Sakuya ran up to the upper deck without another word. There was no time to speak with Rui.

target.text: With the Bosun's thick, booming voice battering against his back, he broke into a run. Perhaps it was because Shisamu and Kisara came and went on a daily basis, but while dust and the like did accumulate in the wheelhouse, compared to the other compartments on the ship, it was less dirty. And the room itself wasn't that spacious, so while it was still called cleaning, it was really more like a side job. If he just cleaned off the conspicuously visible grime, that would be excusable, and he hadn't been told to do anything else afterwards.

That being the case, it was left entirely up to Sakuya if he wanted to use the spare time to rest, so even the Bosun had likely been considerate enough to grant him at least that much after coming off his watch. However, there was no telling how long that kindness would last if he kept dawdling in front of him. So after that, without saying a word, Sakuya ran up to the upper deck; he didn't have the time to exchange words with Rui anymore.

source.japanese:
鉄板にじゅうじゅう脂が弾けて、分厚いヒレ肉はまさにミディアムレアの食べ頃の、これ以上熱を通しては程良い生加減の肉が失われる。
　朔屋はざくざくとナイフで切り分け、ぶすりとフォークで刺して、肉の香ばしさ湯気とまとう大きな一切れに齧り付く。
source.english:
Fat hissed and spat on the iron plate. The thick fillet was ready now, perfectly medium rare. Any more heat would destroy that ideal measure of rawness within.
Sakuya cut it briskly with his knife, stabbed in his fork, and bit into a great steaming piece, fragrant with meat.
“…kuya… Sakuya…”

target.text: The fat sizzled on the iron plate, the thick cut of filet mignon was a beautiful medium rare, and if it received any more heat, that perfect amount of rawness left in the meat would be lost. Sakuya cut it into large pieces with his knife, stabbed into the soft meat with his fork, then sunk his teeth into a big chunk, the savoury fragrance of the meat enveloping it like steam.
【Voice】 『ya……Sakuya……』

source.japanese: 塩胡椒を最良の加減で利かせ、大蒜の切片で香り付けして焼き締めた表面と裏腹に、肉の裡[うち]は豊潤な肉汁に満ちあふれ、噛み締める度に舌に沁みていくような……いくような……ような？
source.english: The salt and pepper were perfectly judged. Slices of garlic had scented the seared surface, while inside, rich meat juices brimmed, soaking into his tongue with each bite… soaking… into…?

source.japanese:
おかしい。こんなに良い焼き加減のフィレステーキなのに、素晴らしい肉質であるのに、舌には肉汁のいっかな通わず、歯はまるで帆布の鞄でも噛んでいるかの噛みごたえ。
　せっかくのステーキなのに裏切られた気分一杯で、朔屋は悔しさのあまりに力いっぱいに噛み締めて───
source.english:
Strange. A fillet steak this perfectly cooked, of such magnificent quality, yet not a drop of juice reached his tongue. To his teeth, it felt like chewing a canvas bag.
Betrayed by this precious steak, Sakuya bit down with all his strength in sheer frustration—

source.japanese:
【声】
『こら！　離せ朔屋』
source.english: “Hey! Let go, Sakuya!”

source.japanese:
【声】
『いい加減に口開けろってーのに！』
source.english: “Open your mouth already!”

target.text: Seasoned to perfection with salt and pepper, slices of garlic adding fragrance, top and bottom surfaces seared brown, the inside of the meat overflowing with rich juices, it was as though it sank deeper into his tongue with each bite…… as though it……as though?

Strange. Even though it was a tenderloin steak seared to such perfection, even though the meat was of such sublime quality, no juices ran across his tongue at all, and the texture was so chewy, it felt as if his teeth were sinking into a canvas bag. Filled with a feeling of being betrayed by such a precious steak, the overwhelmingly bitter frustration of promises broken made Sakuya bite down with all his might───
【Voice】 『HEY! Let go, Sakuya!』
【Voice】 『Can you just open your damn mouth like I told you to already!』

source.japanese:
がいんとこめかみにきた痛みにステーキは一遍に消えて、目の中に満ちたのは眩い光、あまりに眩しくて周囲の様子が見てとれない。
　徐々に光が収まり事物の輪郭が見分けられてくると。
source.english:
A crash of pain against his temple made the steak vanish all at once. Dazzling light filled his eyes, too bright to make out anything around him.
Gradually it subsided; the outlines of things became clear.

target.text: The pain that slammed into his temple made the steak poof out of existence, and the dazzling light that filled his eyes was so bright, he couldn't grasp the state of his surroundings. As the light gradually subsided, so did the contours of things begin to grow discernible from each other.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「おう。ようやく目ぇ覚ましたみたいね」
source.english: “Oh. Looks like you're finally awake.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あれえ？　シサム？　キサラ？
　お肉はあ？
　焼きたてで、にくじるたっぷりの」
source.english:
“…Huh? Sisam? Kisara?
Where's the meat?
Freshly cooked, all full of juice?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Hey, you. Seems like you're finally awake.」
【Naomasa】 「……Huuuh? Shisamu? Kisara? Where is the meat? That freshly seared steak, the one full of meat juices.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「いや、まだ寝てるよこいつ。
　そんな上等な肉なんざ、
　なんでこの船にあるもんかい」
source.english:
“No, he's still asleep.
Why would there be meat
that good on this ship?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うそん……あんた達のおっぱいみたいに馬鹿でっかくて、あんた達の尻みたいに脂の乗ったお肉はー……？」
source.english: “Nooo… The meat was stupidly huge, like your tits, and rich and fatty, like your asses. Where is it…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうか。隠したんだな。
　俺に食わせまいと。ひでえ、なんて意地悪な女だ。返せ、食わせてくりよう。どこだ、どこに隠した、ここかぁーっっ、
　───ぎゃあああっ」
source.english:
“I get it. You hid it.
So I couldn't eat it. Cruel! What horrible women. Give it back, let me eat it! Where? Where did you hide it?
In here—Gyaaaah!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Nope, this guy's still fast asleep. Like there's a damn chance such high-quality meat could ever be found anywhere on this ship.」
【Naomasa】 「You're lying……that slab of meat, as ridiculously big as your tits, as fatty as your asses, where did it……?」
【Naomasa】 「I see. You hid it. All so I can't eat it. Terrible, what wicked women you are. Give it back, please let me eat it. Where is it, where did you hide it, is it heeeereー, ───GYAAAAH」

source.japanese: 跳ね起きざまに、シサムのスカートの裡側に頭を潜[もぐ]りこませようとした朔屋の横っ腹にキサラの爪先が綺麗にめりこんで、それで朔屋は体をくの字に吹っ飛び操舵室の伝声管に肋[あばら]を強[したた]かに打ちつけて転がり回った。
source.english: Springing up, Sakuya tried to burrow his head beneath Sisam's skirt. Kisara's toe sank neatly into his flank. Bent double, he flew across the wheelhouse, struck his ribs hard against the speaking tube, and rolled about on the floor.

target.text: The instant he sprung up, Sakuya attempted to crawl under Shisamu's skirt head-first, and he was met with Kisara lodging her foot into his side; Sakuya's body folded into a chevron as he was sent flying, ribs slamming against the wheelhouse's voice pipes, and he rolled around on the floor.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「やめれってーのに！
　よく寝てると思って、
　情けかければこれだ……」
source.english:
“I told you to stop!
We thought you were sleeping so nicely,
showed you some kindness, and this is what we get…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「I told you to cut that shit out! Here I thought you were sleeping so soundly, but this is what I get for showing you some pity……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「まったく。こっちゃ上着の袖[そで]に歯形までつけられて、おまけにスカートの中を狙ってこようとはね……いくら寝惚けたにしたって」
source.english: “Honestly. First you leave teeth marks in my sleeve, then you go for the inside of my skirt… Even if you're half asleep.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Seriously. I've got teeth marks on the sleeve of my jacket, and on top of that, you tried going after the inside of my skirt…… that's too far, even for someone half asleep.」

source.japanese: ステーキと間違えて噛みついたと見え、シサムのリーファージャケットの袖[そで]に刻みこまれた弓なりの跡は、朔屋の歯形の。
source.english: Apparently he had mistaken it for the steak: the sleeve of Sisam's reefer jacket bore the curved impression of Sakuya's teeth.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやあ途中からは目を覚ましてたけれど、寝惚けたって事で誤魔化せるかなあとか思ってないよ、ホントだよ───ぐえ」
source.english: “Well, I woke up partway through, but I wasn't thinking I could get away with it by pretending to be half asleep. Honest—Guh!”

target.text: It seemed that he'd bit down on it after mistaking it for a steak, for the bow-shaped impressions embedded in the sleeve of Shisamu's reefer jacket were in the shape of Sakuya's teeth.
【Naomasa】 「Well, no, I woke up halfway through, but it's not like I thought I'd be able to get away with something by pretending to still be asleep, I promise───gweh!」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ……ちょ……ぎゅ……ぐ、けひ───」
source.english: “Ah… Wait… Ghh… Keh—”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Ah……wai……ghuh……ghh, kehh───」

source.japanese: ひゅん、と猫顔負けの素早さで背後に周り、朔屋の首に巻きついたキサラの腕は的確に気管と頸動脈を捉え、朔屋の気流と血流を封じこめる、絞め技は見事の一言ではあったが、軽口の罰というには、少々程度が過ぎたが女の怒りというのは時に男にとっては理不尽なもの、甘んじて受けよかし朔屋。
source.english: Kisara slipped behind him faster than a cat. Her arm wrapped expertly around his neck, finding windpipe and carotid artery, shutting off his air and blood. A magnificent chokehold, one had to say, though somewhat excessive as punishment for a smart remark. A woman's anger can sometimes seem unreasonable to a man. Accept it gracefully, Sakuya.

target.text: With a whoosh, she slipped around Sakuya, reaching his back with a speed that would put a cat to shame, and Kisara's arm twined around Sakuya's neck, seizing his windpipe and carotid artery with pin-point precision; her stranglehold technique was, put into simple words, magnificent, but as punishment for being too loose-lipped, it was a little bit excessive; the wrath of a woman is said to sometimes seem unreasonable to a man, however, so be content with your lot, Sakuya, and accept your fate.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひぬ……ひんじゃ……きゅふ……」
source.english: “Dying… Gonna… die… Ghh…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Diehh……gonh diehh……kff……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「どうしようかなあ。このまま締めたってかまわないけど、死体の始末もめんどくさい。キサラ、そのあたりにしとこ」
source.english: “What shall we do? I wouldn't mind letting you keep choking him, but getting rid of the corpse would be a nuisance. Kisara, let's leave it there.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「What to do, what to do. Now, I don't mind you just strangling him like this, but dealing with the corpse is going to be a real bother. Kisara, just leave it at that.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「シサムがそういうんなら、
　それで良いけどさ」
source.english:
“If you say so, Sisam.
Fine by me.”

source.japanese:
危ないところで解放されて、呼吸をどうにか整えるうち、朔屋は自分が操舵室にある事を思い出す。掃除をどうにか終えた後、睡魔に抵抗できずそのまま眠ってしまったようだ。操舵室に当直の下級水夫も、朔屋を思いやってか眠らせたままおいていったらしい。
　で、交替のシサム・キサラがやってきてみれば、朔屋は暢気に夢に舌鼓を打っていたところだったと、そういう次第の。
source.english:
Released at the dangerous last moment, Sakuya managed to steady his breathing and remembered that he was in the wheelhouse. After somehow finishing the cleaning, he had evidently succumbed to sleep on the spot. The junior sailor on watch had apparently left him there, perhaps out of consideration.
When Sisam and Kisara arrived to relieve the watch, Sakuya had been blissfully savoring his dream. So that explained it.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「仮眠のつもりが永遠に眠るところだったですとも……」
source.english: “A little nap nearly turned into eternal sleep…”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「If that's what you want me to do, then that's fine, Shisamu.」

He'd been released right when it was getting dangerous, and while he somehow managed to regain his breath, Sakuya recalled that he was in the wheelhouse. After he'd only just finished cleaning, he'd found himself powerless against the siren call of his drowsiness and fallen asleep right then and there. Perhaps the deck boy on watch in the wheelhouse had sympathized with Sakuya, for he had seemingly left him there to sleep. And so, when Shisamu and Kisara showed up to replace the deck boy, Sakuya was smacking his lips in dreamland with not a care in the world; that was apparently how it went.
【Naomasa】 「I was just going to take a nap, but I nearly went to sleep forever, my goodness……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「自業自得ってしか言いようが。
　寝ても覚めても女に悪戯する事しか考えてないのか、あんたは」
source.english:
“Only yourself to blame.
Awake or asleep, is groping women the only thing you think about?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「You can only call that getting your just deserts. Is molesting women all that goes through your head, awake or asleep?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こんなとこで居眠りこいてたみたいだけど、あんた昨夜は当直かなんかだったわけ？」
source.english: “Looks like you were having a nap here. Were you on watch last night or something?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「船内の夜回りを言いつけられてたんじゃないかよ……あんた達にも助っ人お願いしたしたろうが。すげなく断ったくせに」
source.english: “I was told to make the night rounds, remember? I asked you two to help. You turned me down cold.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Certainly looked like you were just dozing off here, but weren't you actually standing watch last night or something?」
【Naomasa】 「I was ordered to patrol the ship at night, wasn't I……I'm pretty sure I even went and asked you two for help. And then you turned me down so coldly.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ああ……そんなコトもあったような……」
source.english: “Oh… Something like that may have happened…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちぇ……自分達だけ、
　石鹸の佳い匂いさせやがってよ。
　よっぽど念入りに洗ったんだな」
source.english:
“Tch…
And now you're both smelling lovely and soapy.
You must have washed awfully thoroughly.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Aah……I do kind of feel like that might have happened……」
【Naomasa】 「Tch……there you two were, keeping the nice scent of soap all to yourselves. And you were being real thorough with the scrubbing.」

source.japanese: ふんふんとキサラの首筋を嗅ごうとするところを、またも拳骨で引き剥がされ。
source.english: He tried to sniff Kisara's neck, and another blow from her fist knocked him away.

target.text: Just as he leaned in to loudly sniff at Kisara's neck, he was yanked off once more by a set of knuckles.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんたなんぞにゃ嗅がせるもんかッ。
　吸うな、息するなっ」
source.english:
“You're not getting a sniff! Don't inhale!
Don't breathe!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はっはっは、無茶を言いよる」
source.english: “Ha ha ha. That's asking a bit much.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Like hell I'd ever let someone like you smell me. Stop inhaling, stop breathing!」
【Naomasa】 「Ha-ha-ha, now you're just talking nonsense.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「そんなに石鹸の匂いが好きなら、まるごと囓っとけば？　ともかく、そんな事はどうでもいいけど、結局なんかあった、昨夜は」
source.english: “If you like the smell of soap that much, why don't you eat a whole bar? Anyway, never mind that. Did anything happen last night?”

source.japanese: そのことだ、と朔屋も我に返る。水夫長には言い損ねたけれど、であればシサム・キサラには告げておいた方がいいのではないか？　先ほどは泪の横槍が入ったけれど、この今なら……。
source.english: Yes, that. Sakuya came back to himself. He had failed to tell the boatswain, but shouldn't he at least tell Sisam and Kisara? Rui had interrupted earlier; now, though—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうだ、その事だシサムにキサラ。
　昨夜なんだがな、
　やっぱりこの船にゃ───」
source.english:
“Right. That's it, Sisam, Kisara.
Last night.
This ship really does have—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「If you like the scent of soap that much, why don't you go gnaw on a bar of it instead? Anyways, who even cares about that, last night, did anything actually happen?」

"Yes, that's it", Sakuya thought as he came to his senses. He had missed his chance to tell the Bosun, so with that being the case, should he not make sure to tell Shisamu and Kisara while he could? Rui interfered earlier, but if he told them right now, then…….
【Naomasa】 「That's right, about that, Shisamu, Kisara. So, this happened last night, and as it turns out, this ship───」

source.japanese: こんこんと、操舵室の窓硝子を外から指の節で叩く小さな響き。
source.english: A little tapping sound: knuckles against the wheelhouse window, from outside.

target.text: Tap-tap, the soft sound of knuckles rapping against the wheelhouse window from the outside.

source.japanese:
【声】
『───お掃除、終わっていらしたのね』
source.english: “You've finished the cleaning, then.”

source.japanese:
窓から覗いてきた顔に、顔が、顔で、泪のその容、陽差しの下でもそこだけ退嬰的な、良く熟れた白葡萄酒の色を透かしたような黄昏の光を帯びているかに見えた。
　その麗質は陽差しにあっては陽の色に応じて映えるという質の物ではなく、どこであっても彼女が自分の空間に造りかえてしまう類のもの、それはそれで物凄い事なのだが、今の朔屋には目に重すぎる。何より夕べと朝の水夫長の船室の一幕があった後では余計に。
source.english:
