　まさか夜中まで本気でやる事になるなんて。
　でも、いやじゃなかったけどさ……」
source.english:
“No, no, you too.
I never thought we'd end up doing it in earnest, right into the night.
But I didn't mind…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「No no, you weren't any better. Never expected to seriously go at it until the middle of the night. But, it's not like it was unpleasant or anything, you know……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だよね。よく判るよ、
　あんたとあたしだもの」
source.english:
“Yeah. I know exactly what you mean.
It's you and me, after all.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Riight. I totally get it, I mean, it's you and me after all.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「さて───お許しもいただけた様子だし、行きましょ、直さん」
source.english: “Well. It appears we have permission. Shall we go, Nao?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ、いや……ええ判った、判りましたよ」
source.english: “Ah, no… Yes, all right. I understand.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Now then───it appears that we have received their blessings, so let us be off, Nao-san.」
【Naomasa】 「Ah, no……okay, fine, I understand.」

source.japanese: ……何やら、シサムとキサラの雰囲気がいかがわしきを帯びて、あるいは泪のまとう淫靡な空気に当てられたものか。なんとも微妙な目つきで目配せを交わし始めた二人を置いて、泪は朔屋の手を躊躇いもなく取って、甲板の上へ。女に手を握られたというのに、長手袋の掌は、布地の裡に柔らかな弾力を秘めた珍[めずら]かな心地好さなのに、朔屋には白蛇の腹に巻きつかれたようにも思えてたじろいでしまう、シサムとキサラにも妙な顔される。
source.english: Something rather indecent had entered the air between Sisam and Kisara. Perhaps Rui's own lascivious atmosphere had affected them. Leaving the two exchanging oddly delicate glances, Rui took Sakuya's hand without hesitation and led him onto the deck. A woman was holding his hand; beneath her long glove, the palm concealed a soft resilience, an unusually pleasant sensation. Yet Sakuya flinched, feeling almost as though the belly of a white snake had coiled around him. Sisam and Kisara gave him strange looks as well.

target.text: ……The air between Shisamu and Kisara seemed tinged with some manner of indecency, or perhaps he'd just been influenced by the lascivious air that ever hung heavy around Rui. Leaving behind the two, who had begun exchanging subtle, ambiguous looks, Rui did not hesitate in taking Sakuya by the hand, moving towards the deck. Even though his hand had been taken by a woman, even though the palm of her hand clad in that long glove concealed beneath the fabric a tender resilience, a novel and rare delight, it felt to him as though the belly of a white snake had coiled around him, and so he ended up recoiling, with even Shisamu and Kisara sending him a strange look.

source.japanese:
上甲板の中央船尾寄り、鳥居の傍の木陰にて。
　誰が用意したものか、日焼けに色褪せてはいるけれど、この船の持ち物としては清潔な円卓が据えられて、朔屋は泪と向かい合ってある。
　シサム・キサラと一緒にいた時は、会話の尾籠な流れに気を取られてあまり意識せなんだが、こうして向き合ってみると改めて蘇ってくるのは昨夜の戦慄。
source.english:
Near the stern, toward the middle of the upper deck, in the shade of a tree beside the torii. Someone had set out a round table, sun-faded but clean by this ship's standards, and Sakuya sat facing Rui.
With Sisam and Kisara, the conversation's bawdy course had distracted him enough to keep him from thinking too much. Face-to-face with her now, he felt last night's terror return.

source.japanese: 泪が胸に一つの含みもなく、朝から朔屋の行く先々に現れる筈もない───それを想えば心中穏やかではいられなかったけれど、かといってずばりと斬りこむには朔屋は怯懦に過ぎた。迂闊な事を口にしてしまえば、あの魚怪どもをけしかけられて海の底まで引き攫[さら]われてしまうのではないか。そんな危惧さえ朔屋は抱いていたが、まあこれはたしかに無理からぬところ。
source.english: Rui could hardly have appeared wherever he went all morning without some intention. That thought disturbed him, but Sakuya was too timid to address the matter outright. Say something careless, and perhaps she would set those fish-monsters on him, have him dragged to the bottom of the sea. He feared even that. Not unreasonably, one had to admit.

target.text: In the central area of the upper deck, a little towards the stern, in the shade of the tree standing next to the torii. Who had arranged this, one might wonder, for though faded by the sun, a round table, unusually clean for something belonging to this ship, was set in place, and there Sakuya sat, facing Rui. Back when he'd been with Shisamu and Kisara, he'd been preoccupied with the salacious flow of the conversation, and so he hadn't been too conscious of it, but now that he was sat face to face with her like so, it was the shivering dread from last night that was recalled anew.

Rui had not a single agenda hidden within her heart, nor could she possibly have shadowed Sakuya's every step since morning───as soon as those thoughts ran through his mind, it was impossibly for his heart to simply remain at peace, and yet he was also too cowardly to boldly cut straight to the matter. If he carelessly ran his mouth, could he not end up having those fishmen set after him and be dragged away to the bottom of the sea? Sakuya harboured even such fears, though admittedly, they were hardly unreasonable.

source.japanese: このように、女を前にした朔屋にしてはなんの天変地異の前ぶれか、珍しく警戒しており、泪が程よく冷えた白葡萄酒を奨めてきた時も、歯軋りしながらではあったが断ったし、普段なら隣に席を占めるところ、対面にできる限り距離をとって浅く腰を下ろした。そもそも葡萄酒だって、まともな冷蔵施設のないこの船で、どう用意したのか、それを想えば不気味だ。
source.english: Thus Sakuya, faced with a woman, was unusually wary—as though heralding some upheaval of heaven and earth. When Rui offered pleasantly chilled white wine, he declined, though it made him grind his teeth. Ordinarily he would have sat beside her. Instead he perched opposite, as far away as possible. Even the wine was unsettling: how had she obtained it chilled on a ship without proper refrigeration?

source.japanese:
ただ泪は、朔屋に断られてもさして気に病んだ様子もなく、淑やかに葡萄酒を味わうのみで、いっかな口火を切ろうとしない。
　その様子だけ見れば、なるほど彼女が言う通りに、梢を渡る潮風と信天翁の眠気を催すような声を優雅に愉[たの]しんでいるだけ、と見えなくもなかったが───朔屋が根負けして、問いかけた。
source.english:
Rui, however, seemed untroubled by his refusal. She merely savored her wine with quiet grace, making no attempt to open the conversation.
Watching her, one might indeed have believed she was doing only what she said: elegantly enjoying the sea breeze through the treetops and the drowsy calls of albatrosses. At last Sakuya gave in and asked—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あの二人、今二人きりにしておくとなんかヤバげな事になりそうな」
source.english: “…Leaving those two alone right now seems liable to lead to something a bit dangerous…”

source.japanese: 問いかけたと言っても、やはり本筋に進む勇気はなく、昨夜の出来事とはどうにも関係のよしなし事であるというのがなんともはや。
source.english: Asked, yes—but still without the courage to reach the main subject. Something incidental, having nothing to do with last night's events. Really.

target.text: For someone like Sakuya to act this way in front of a woman, was this some portent of an imminent cataclysm? He was unusually guarded, and even when Rui offered him a glass of perfectly chilled white wine, though he ground his teeth all the while, he refused; ordinarily, he'd be occupying the seat next to her, but he kept as much distance as was physically possible while still facing each other, and he only sat down lightly. Even this wine here, they were on a ship with no proper refrigeration facilities, so how had she managed to get her hands on it? Once he thought about it, it all felt uncanny.

However, Rui did not show any particular worry over being turned down by Sakuya, she just savoured her wine in a most ladylike manner, making no attempts at all to break the ice. Based on her mannerisms alone, it wasn't impossible that it could be just as she claimed, indeed, maybe she was simply elegantly enjoying the sea breeze passing through the treetops together with the soporific cries of the albatrosses, but─── Sakuya lost their game of patience, and so he asked her.
【Naomasa】 「……Leaving those two alone right now kind of seems like it's going to end badly, doesn't it?」

While he did ask her a question, as one might expect, he lacked the courage to venture into the heart of the matter, and to then ask about something so trivial with absolutely no relation to the happenings of last night, goodness, where do we even begin with this man?

source.japanese:
【泪】
「好きなようにさせてあげなさいな。
　お二人が気持ちいいと言っているんだから。
　それなら、素敵な事よ」
source.english:
“Let them do as they please.
They both say it feels good.
Then it is something lovely.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あなたは、いつもそれだ。
　いやさ、そりゃあ俺だって気持ちいい事は嫌いじゃない。むしろ積極的に好きだよ」
source.english:
“…That's always your answer.
Look, I don't dislike things that feel good myself. Quite the opposite. I'm actively in favor.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「自分が女にだらしないのもよく判っている。
　でも仕方ないだろう、女と抱き合うのはすげえ気持ちが良いんだからっ」
source.english:
“I know perfectly well I'm hopeless with women.
But what can I do? Holding a woman feels fucking wonderful!”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Let them do as they like. For the two of them did say it feels good. In that case, it is a lovely thing.」
【Naomasa】 「……You're always like that. No, listen, it's not like I'm against things that feel good. On the contrary, I'm actively all for them.」
【Naomasa】 「I'm more than well aware of how indulgent I am with women. But there's nothing I can do about that, right, because making love to a woman just feels so incredibly good!」

source.japanese: どん、と自信満々に拳で円卓を叩く朔屋。
source.english: Sakuya thumped his fist on the round table, full of conviction.

target.text: Sakuya slammed his fist down on the table, brimming with confidence.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「同感ね。そこまで言い切るのに、どうして直さんはわたくしを敬遠なさるの？」
source.english: “I agree. If you can say it so emphatically, why do you keep avoiding me, Nao?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I concur. But if you can declare that so assertively, how come you always keep me at arm's length then, Nao-san?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしは、ただ退屈を持て余しているだけの女よ。この船に乗りこんでみたのだって、とある誰かに呼ばれたからなのだけど───
　いいえ、その誰かの事は、わたくしも知らないの」
source.english:
“I'm only a woman with more boredom than she knows what to do with. I boarded this ship because someone called me—
No, I don't know who that someone was either.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I am but a woman with far more boredom than she knows what to do with. Even boarding this ship was merely something I did because I was summoned here by a certain someone─── no, I care not in the slightest about that certain someone or anything to do with them.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それでも、ちょっとは退屈しのぎになるかしら───そう思っただけ」
source.english: “Even so, I thought it might offer a little diversion. That was all.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Even so, perhaps it could alleviate me of some of my boredom─── that is all I thought of it.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「貴方が乗っていらしたのは嬉しかったわ。古いお知己と逢えるのは素敵な事ですもの」
source.english: “I was pleased to find you aboard. Meeting an old acquaintance is a lovely thing.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I was delighted to find that you were aboard the ship. Being reunited with old acquaintances is a most wonderful thing.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でも、なにも直さんにひどい事をしてやろうなんて、ちっとも考えてません。
　なのに直さんは……わたくしが、怖い？」
source.english:
“But I have no intention of doing anything dreadful to you, Nao. None at all.
And yet… Are you afraid of me?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「正直、それはある。でも泪さんのは、ただ怖いって言う前に、よく判らないんだな。
　あなたはたいそうな金持ちだ。
　おまけに前の旦那達の、遺族年金とかもあるんだろ？」
source.english:
“Honestly, yes. But with you, Ms. Rui, before it's even a matter of being afraid, I don't really understand.
You're tremendously rich.
You get survivors' pensions from your former husbands too, don't you?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「金や贅沢には不自由しない暮らしで、そういう人間がやることなくして暇を持て余すって言うのも聞かない話じゃない」
source.english: “You never lack money or luxury. It's not unheard of for someone living like that to have nothing to do, to be bored.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「However, try as I might, I simply cannot think of a single awful thing I might have done to you, Nao-san. And yet, Nao-san……are you, by any chance, afraid of me?」

【Naomasa】 「To be honest with you, yes, I am. But with you, it's not simply a question of fear, it's more that I don't really understand you. You're an immensely rich woman. And on top of that, you still have the survivor's pensions or whatever from your former husbands, right?」
【Naomasa】 「A life without want for money or lavish luxury, it's not like I haven't heard tales of how such people have nothing to do and end up with far too much idle time on their hands.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でも俺はさ、この通り金もなく、特技もある訳じゃない。だから、そういう金持ち達の退屈ってのがよく判らないんだ」
source.english: “But look at me. I've got no money, no special talent. So I don't really understand the boredom of people that rich.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「But, well, as you can see, I don't have any money, nor do I have any special skills. So, I just don't really understand that kind of boredom of the rich.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───まあね。
　直さんの仰有る事もわかります。
　貴方は貴方。わたくしはわたくし。
　わたくしの退屈は、
　直さんにはわからないのでしょうね」
source.english:
“Well.
I understand what you mean, Nao.
You are you.
I am I.
My boredom must be something you cannot understand.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でも逆に、わたくしには。
　お金に苦労する人というのはあるのでしょうし、わたくしにはそういった辛さは今のところ、わからない」
source.english:
“Conversely, for my part—
I suppose there are people who struggle for money. That is a kind of suffering I have never yet understood.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「───I suppose, yes. I do understand what you are saying, Nao-san. You are you. I am myself. I suppose that my boredom, Nao-san, is something you could never truly come to understand.」
【Rui】 「But conversely, I am no different. I suppose there are those who toil and worry for money, but as I am, I do not understand that hardship.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……ああ、そういう話じゃないの。
　とにかく退屈なのよ。長い事ずっと。
　それこそ───」
source.english:
“…Ah, that isn't what I mean.
I am simply bored. Have been, for a very long time.
Ever since—”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「最初の人と死に別れてから、ずっと。
　……あの人と死に別れてしまったからこそ、だからわたくしは、今こうして貴方と口を聞いていられるのだけれど」
source.english:
“Ever since death parted me from the first man I loved.
It is only because death parted us that I can speak with you like this now…”

source.japanese: 謎めいた一言を一瞥と共に朔屋に。
source.english: With a glance for Sakuya, she let fall that cryptic remark.

target.text: 【Rui】 「……Ah, that isn't what I mean to say. In any case, I am bored. And have been so for a very long time. In particular───」
【Rui】 「When death separated me from my first love, and ever since. ……It is precisely because death took that man from me that I am here now, sitting like this, able to talk with you thus.」
She sent those words veiled in mystery at Sakuya together with a glance.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「駄目ねえ。それから後は、人を好きになると言う事が、よく判らなくなってしまって」
source.english: “Hopeless, isn't it? Since then, I no longer quite understand what it means to love someone.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「だってあの人が死んだのに、わたくしはおめおめと生きながらえているのだもの」
source.english: “For he died, and I go on living, shamelessly.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It is hopeless, really. Ever since, the meaning of falling in love with another has eluded my grasp.」
【Rui】 「For even though that man passed away, I have continued to shamelessly live on for so many long years.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ともかく、それ以来、
　何人もの方と連れ添ったけれど。
　不思議ね、長続きしなくって」
source.english:
“At any rate,
since then I have lived with a number of gentlemen.
Strange, how it never lasts.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「In any case, ever since, I have been married to all manner of men. But strange as it is, it never lasts for long.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「確かなのは、肉体の快楽。
　後はちょっとだけ、ゲームの面白さ」
source.english:
“What is certain is the pleasure of the body.
Beyond that, a little enjoyment in games.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「だからわたくしは、
　誰かと肌を重ねるのだし、
　だからカードに夢中になる」
source.english:
“That is why I lie
with people.
That is why I lose myself in cards.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「The only certainty is the pleasure of the flesh. Beyond that, there is but a trace of the fun of playing games.」
【Rui】 「And that is why I sleep in the arms of another. That is why I lose myself in the cards.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「もしわたくしと、共に過ごして下さる方がいるなら、それは楽しい事でしょうね。そう願う事も、あったりするのよ───？」
source.english: “If someone would spend time with me, surely that would be pleasant. Sometimes I wish for it, you know…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや待って、ちょっと待って。
　そんな期待の眼差しで見られても。
　あなたの連れ合いは、
　例外なくくたばってるって話だ。
　俺はまだ命が惜しい」
source.english:
“No, wait. Just a second.
Don't look at me so expectantly. I hear that every partner you've had has died, without exception.
I'm still rather attached to being alive.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「And if there should happen to be someone who would so graciously be willing to spend their time together with me, that would make for an enjoyable time, I suppose. I do occasionally find myself wishing for such things───?」

【Naomasa】 「No, hold on, wait just a second. Look at me with those expectant eyes all you want. You just talked about how all of your husbands, without exception, have kicked the bucket. My life is still dear to me.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でも直さん、
　シサムさんが言っていたじゃない。
　直さんは、それが色仕掛けで、
　後から大変な事になるってわかっていても、
　進んで引っかかるって」
source.english:
“But Nao, didn't Ms. Sisam say it?
Even when you know someone is using her charms,
even when you know it will mean trouble afterward,
you willingly fall for it.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「But, Nao-san, didn't Shisamu just say it? That even though you know disaster awaits, whenever they pull some ruse of seduction, you voluntarily fall for it.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それなら、わたくしが相手でも、ね？
　なにもそんなに、敬遠なさらなくっても」
source.english:
“Then even with me, hmm?
There's no need to keep me quite so far away.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい、なんだか妙な話の流れになってきたな。だって泪さん、あなた別に俺の事が好きとか、そういう話でもないんだろう、これ」
source.english: “Hey, this conversation's taking a strange turn. Ms. Rui, it's not as though you've got feelings for me or anything, is it?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「That being the case, you would do the same even for me, no? You really don't have to shy away from me so.」
【Naomasa】 「Oi, this conversation is heading down a weird track. But Rui-san, it's not like you actually like me in particular or anything, that's not what this is about, right?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「さぁて……どうしようかな……」
source.english: “Well… What shall I do…?”

source.japanese: その時だけ泪は、日頃彼女が身を潜[ひそ]める、柔媚で秘やかで、そしてどこか淫靡な暗がりから陽差しの下に乗りだして、お菓子を選んで唇を舌で舐める子供のような、悪戯ッ気と稚気を見せて、朔屋のと胸を衝[つ]かせた事である。
source.english: For that moment alone, Rui leaned out into the sunshine from the soft, secretive, faintly lascivious darkness in which she ordinarily sheltered. She showed a mischievous childishness, like a child licking its lips as it chose a sweet. Sakuya's heart gave a startled beat.

source.japanese: 後は話は当たり障[さわ]りのない事柄に終始し、朔屋は別れた後で結局昨夜の事には触れずじまいで終わったに気づいた始末の、もしや泪は巧妙に、自分の身の上を俎上に載せる事ではぐらかしたのではないかと思い当たったけれど、今さら後の祭というもので。
source.english: After that, the conversation stayed with harmless subjects. Only once they parted did Sakuya realize that he had never mentioned last night at all. Perhaps Rui had cleverly diverted him by making her own life the subject. The possibility occurred to him, but by then it was much too late.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Well now……what to do, what to do……」

Only in that very moment did Rui emerge from the softly alluring, secretive, and somewhat licentious shadow she usually hid within, leaned into the sunlight, revealing both mischief and a childlike innocence, like a child licking their lips while deciding what candy to eat, and it hit Sakuya in the heart.

After this, the conversation revolved around nothing but harmless, inoffensive topics, and after parting ways with her, Sakuya noticed that, in the end, they never ended up touching on what had happened last night, and perhaps, he suddenly realized, that by placing some of her personal history on the chopping board, Rui had deftly managed to dodge the issue entirely, but by now, that realization was too belated to do him any good.

source.japanese:
泪と別れて雑仕事を終えて、自分の船室に戻ったその夜の事。
　朔屋はベッドに残されていた物を見て驚愕した。よろよろと、撃たれたように後退って踏みとどまる、足を支えるは怒りの念。
　それは鱗[うろこ]。
　あの夜朔屋が見出したものと同じ鱗[うろこ]。
　あの魚怪どもが這いずり回っていた後に残されていたものと同じ、あの鱗[うろこ]。
source.english:
That night, after parting with Rui and finishing his odd jobs, Sakuya returned to his cabin. What lay on his bed appalled him. He reeled backward as though shot, then held his ground; anger kept him standing.
A scale.
The same kind he had found that night. The same kind left behind wherever those fish-monsters crawled.

target.text: It happened at night, after he had parted ways with Rui, finished his chores, then returned to his own cabin. When Sakuya saw what had been left in his bed, he was horrified. He staggered as though shot, stumbled back, but held his ground, his wrath alone keeping him standing on his feet. Those were scales. The same scales as Sakuya had found that night. The same as what had been left behind in the wake of those fish monsters slithering around, those very scales.

source.japanese:
これを見て朔屋はたやすく、いともたやすく逆上した。昼間は葡萄酒など飲みながら、何やら思わしげな素振りを見せていた女であれど、あの魚怪どもと通じている事には間違いはなく、そしてその魚怪は朔屋の私室にまで侵入してきていると来る。どうして冷静でいられよう。
　このまま捨ておけば、いずれ自分にどんな厄が降ったものか知れない。
source.english:
At the sight, Sakuya flew into a rage—easily, all too easily. The woman might have sat drinking wine that afternoon with a look of something weighing on her mind, but there was no question she was in league with those fish-monsters; and now those same creatures had gone so far as to invade his private cabin. How could he possibly remain calm?
If he simply let matters lie, there was no telling what calamity might befall him in time.

source.japanese:
と、なれば───
　朔屋の眸[ひとみ]が、追いつめられた小心者特有の、危険なかぎろいを帯びた。
source.english:
In that case—
His eyes took on the dangerous flicker peculiar to a cornered coward.

target.text: Upon seeing them, Sakuya easily, all too easily, flew into a rage. Though she was a woman who presented an appearance of suggestive implications in the daytime as she sipped her wine, there was not a single doubt that she was clandestinely keeping in touch with those fish monsters, and now it had reached the point where those fish monsters had even intruded upon Sakuya's private room. How could he possibly remain calm? If he simply let this be, who could say what kind of danger would befall him, or when.
And that being the case─── Sakuya's eyes gleamed with a dangerous light, the kind unique to cowards driven into a corner.

source.japanese:
しどけなく寝乱れ姿でさえ、泪は美しい。
　普段はどういう衣装で眠るのかは知らず、今夜の泪はドレスを着けたままベッドに身を横たえて、その放恣にして艶[えん]なること、大なる花束を放った様かと見ゆる。乱れる髪の筋もしべが散ったような、息に香る葡萄酒の匂いも、花の芳しきのような。
　酒を喰らい酔い、挙げ句に潰れたと言ってしまえば剥きつけな、息だって寝息の酸いのが混じってはいる、けれど、この女の唇から零れると、その酒臭ささえ媚香めいて、無防備な肢体から立ち籠む肌の香と混じりあうともう、傍で吸うだけで股ぐらに芯が入ってくるほどの、生々しく官能をそそる空気となる。
source.english:
Even sprawled in disarray, Rui was beautiful.
What she ordinarily wore to bed, he did not know. Tonight she lay on her bed in her dress, wantonly graceful, like a great bouquet flung down. The loose strands of hair might have been scattered stamens; the wine on her breath, the flowers' fragrance.
To say she had drunk herself into a stupor would be crude. Her breathing did carry the sourness of sleep. Yet from this woman's lips even the smell of liquor became an aphrodisiac incense. Mingled with the scent rising from her defenseless limbs, it made the very air sensuous enough to stiffen a man's groin merely by standing near and breathing.

source.japanese:
泪の寝台の傍らに立ち、見下ろす朔屋はむらむらと、眠りを貪る女を自分勝手に弄[もてあそ]びたいとの劣悪極まりない衝動に流されかかる、なにしろ肌に張りつくドレスの布地は、隠す事によって、締めつける事によって、更に女の曲線を艶[なま]めかしく際立たせるばかりであったし、火照って朱を置いた肌は、性に喘[あえ]ぐ女の熱を直接に連想させるから。
　朔屋が荒い息遣いを懸命に抑えようとしているのも、獣欲に猛っているとしか見えず、息苦しげに襯衣の胸元を引いて風を通しているのだって、そのまま脱ぎ去って寝台に飛びこもうとする前準備としか思えない。
source.english:
Standing beside the bed, looking down, Sakuya nearly succumbed to the utterly vile impulse to do as he pleased with the sleeping woman. The dress clung to her skin; by concealing and constricting, it only made her curves more seductive. The flushed heat of her skin called directly to mind a woman panting in the throes of sex.
His desperate attempts to control his harsh breathing looked like nothing but bestial lust. Even tugging at his shirtfront for air seemed merely preparation to strip it off and leap into bed.

source.japanese:
だが朔屋は、眠りつづける泪に襲いかかりはせず、もっと不可解な行動を取った。泪の体の下に手を差し入れて、彼女を姫抱きに抱え上げたのである。
　見ようによっては女を介抱しようという献身とも取れなくもないが、やはり奇妙だ。そもそも泪は衣服を着けたままとはいえ自室の寝台で眠っている、抱き上げる必要など無い。
source.english:
But Sakuya did not fall upon the sleeping Rui. He did something stranger still: slid his hands beneath her and lifted her into his arms,
cradling her. One might, from a certain angle, have mistaken it for devoted care. Still, it was strange. Rui was asleep in her own bed, dressed though she might be. There was no need to pick her up.
“Ah… Uuh… Uuh…”

source.japanese: 目覚めた、というより肺の空気が押し出されての呻[うめ]き声に、朔屋の肩は大きく引き攣ったが、泪が目を覚ます兆しもないと見るや、運び出すが部屋の外へ。
source.english: Less a waking sound than a groan as air was pressed from her lungs. Sakuya's shoulders jerked violently. But seeing no sign that she would wake, he carried her out of the room.

target.text: Even when dishevelled and slovenly in the embrace of sleep, Rui was beautiful. He didn't know what clothes she normally slept in, but tonight, Rui had laid down in her bed while still wearing her dress, and the uninhibited, voluptuous beauty of it seemed like a great bouquet bursting into bloom. Her messy strands of hair were like the scattered stamens of a flower, and even the sweet scent of wine wafting off her breath was like the fragrance of that blossom.

To put it bluntly, she had guzzled liquor, succumbed to the intoxication, and passed out drunk; even her breath was laced with the acrid reek of a sleeping lush, however, when it spilt forth from this woman's lips, even that stench of booze seemed like an alluring perfume, and when it mixed with the heady aroma of her skin rising from her defenceless body, just standing next to her and inhaling it was enough to bring a stiffness to his crotch, so vividly tantalizing to his carnal senses did the air surrounding them become.

Sakuya stood next to Rui's bed and looked down at her, turned on, the utterly depraved impulse to selfishly toy with the body of this woman lost deep in sleep coursing through his body; after all, the way the fabric of her dress clung tightly to her skin, the way it hid her from him, the way it stretched taut, it only made her feminine curves stand out with all the more seductive a conspicuousness, and her skin, still warm with a vermillion flush, directly brought to mind the heat of a woman moaning in sexual arousal.

Even as Sakuya strenuously tried to suppress his wild breathing, he still only seemed to be at the mercy of his raging animal desire, and when, feeling stifled, he pulled at the front of his shirt to make some air pass through, even that only seemed to be the early preparations for stripping naked where he stood and jumping into her bed.

However, Sakuya did not pounce on the still-sleeping Rui; he did something even more incomprehensible. He put his hands below Rui's body, then lifted her up into a bridal carry. Depending on how you looked at it, it could be interpreted as the devoted self-sacrifice of a man looking after a woman, but it really was peculiar. To begin with, while Rui might still have been wearing her clothes, she was asleep in her own room, lying in her own bed, so there was no need at all to hold her in his arms.
【Rui】 「Ah……uh……nh.」

As he heard the groans of her stirring from sleep, or rather, the air in her lungs being pushed out, a large spasm ran through Sakuya's shoulders, but judging that it was not a sign of Rui awakening, he began to carry her out of the room.

source.japanese: 船内通路を抜け───途中、人目に遭うを憚[はばか]って、ひどく慎重で鈍[のろ]い歩みではあったが、それでもしまいには、夜の上甲板へ。
source.english: Through the ship's passages—fear of being seen made his steps exceedingly slow and careful. Even so, he eventually reached the upper deck at night.

target.text: He made his way through the ship's passageways───hesitant at being seen by others on the way, he walked with immense caution, his steps slow, but even so, he finally began moving up towards the upper deck under the night sky.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ん……ふぁぁ……だぁ……れ？」
source.english: “Mmm… Haa… Who…?”

source.japanese: 階段を上がる際の、膝に突き上げる足取りに眠りがやや浅くなったか、ぼんやりと問いかける泪を敢えて無視する、すると朧気な目覚めはたちまちに眠りの波に沈んで、またすぐにぐったりと。寝息が深くなるのを確かめてから上がり出す朔屋の顔は、この青年にしてはと目を背[そむ]けたくなるほど、狂おしい油光りを眸[ひとみ]に宿し、酷薄ですらあった。
source.english: Perhaps the jolting of his knees as he climbed the stairs had brought her toward the surface of sleep. Sakuya deliberately ignored the drowsy question. Her faint awakening sank beneath sleep's waves again; she soon went limp. Only once he was sure her breathing had deepened did he climb the rest of the way. His face was almost too cruel to look at, especially on a man like him. A mad, oily gleam burned in his eyes.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Nh……fwaah……who's……there?」
【Naomasa】 「…………」

Perhaps her sleep had grown somewhat lighter from the way he had raised his knees as he walked up the steps, but as he did his utmost to ignore the absentminded mutterings from Rui, her hazy awakening readily sunk back beneath the waves of sleep, and she quickly grew limp once more. After confirming that her breathing had deepened, Sakuya ascended the stairs once more, his eyes holding a frenzied, oily gleam within; so disturbing a look did it paint onto this young man's face that it was repellent to the eyes, it even looked inhumane.

source.japanese: 死の直後や、正体を失った人間の体は、中味が流動する革袋と同じでひどく持ち疲れがすると言う。もし泪を抱え上げるだけで朔屋が疲労困憊していれば、立ち止まったその時の、僅かな間だけで青年の思考に理性が入りこむ隙はきっとあった筈、それで正気を取り戻す隙もあっただろう。
source.english: A body just dead, or wholly insensible, is said to be exhausting to carry, like a leather sack with fluid shifting inside. Had merely lifting Rui worn Sakuya out, a pause might surely have given reason a small opening into his thoughts. He might have recovered his senses then.

source.japanese:
しかしこの時の泪の体は、確かに持ちごたえがあるとはいえ、どこまでも柔らかかつ肉感に満ちた、言わば情交の時の、女が上になる形の際に男の腹を艶[なま]めかしく圧すのと同じ重みであり、この女は正体なく眠っている時でさえ、淫らをまとって男を惑わせる。
　朔屋はその情火に流されまいと務めて思考を空にしていたから、ここまで正気づく事もなく泪を運んでこられた。
source.english:
But Rui's body, though substantial in his arms, was soft and sensuous throughout. Its weight was like a woman pressing voluptuously upon a man's belly when she rode him in bed. Even unconscious in sleep, this woman clothed herself in indecency and bewildered men.
To keep from being carried away by that heat, Sakuya had emptied his thoughts as best he could. Thus he had carried Rui this far without coming to his senses.

source.japanese:
そう、信天翁号の舷側まで。
　そして、そう、この時の朔屋は到底正気とは言い難い。なんとなれば泪を───いとけなく眠りつづける泪を───海に叩き落とそうとしていたのだから。
source.english:
Yes. To the Albatross's side.
And yes, at this moment Sakuya could hardly be called sane. For he intended to throw Rui—Rui, still innocently asleep—into the sea.

source.japanese: ……あの魚怪どもは泪を求めてこの船に這入りこんできた。あの魚怪どもは泪の帰還を求めている。泪がこの船にある限り、夜毎の魔群の跋扈はきっと止むことなく、そのままでは自分がどうなるか知れたものではない。一体如何なる意図で魚怪どもが朔屋の部屋に侵入したのか知る術もないが、理由がわかった時には手遅れ、という事も充分以上に有り得る。
source.english: Those fish-monsters had entered the ship seeking Rui. They wanted her return. As long as Rui remained aboard, the demonic throng would surely continue its nightly wandering. There was no knowing what might happen to him. Nor could he know why they had entered his room; by the time he learned, it might easily be too late.

target.text: Carrying the body of a human who has recently perished, or has lost consciousness, is said to be just as terribly tiring as carrying a leather bag whose contents flow freely around within. Should Sakuya suffer from total exhaustion just from carrying Rui, when he would come to a pause, that scant moment in time alone would be an opportunity for reason to wriggle its way into the young man's thinking, and that should surely provide an opportunity for him to come to his senses as well.

But at this time, while Rui's body certainly had a palpable weight to it, it was full of softness, a physical carnality filling every nook and cranny; it was a burden akin to the captivating pressure bearing down on a man's stomach when a woman rides him from above during intimacy, if pushed to describe it, and even when this woman was asleep, bereft of consciousness, she was clad in obscenity, leading men astray. In an effort to not let himself be swept away by such passions, Sakuya had emptied his head of thoughts, and so he had carried Rui all this way without ever having regained his sanity.

Indeed, all this way to the gunwale of the Albatross. And then, certainly, Sakuya could by no means be called sane in this moment. The reason being, he was holding Rui───Rui, sleeping so innocently───and about to throw her into the ocean.

……Those fish monsters had slithered aboard this ship because they wanted Rui. Those fish monsters wanted Rui to return home with them. For as long as Rui stayed aboard this ship, that swarm of monsters would surely never stop running rampant on this ship, and if that kept up, there was no telling what fate was in store for him. He had no means of finding out whatever it was that the fish monsters had been trying to accomplish by trespassing in his room, but by the time he figured that out, it was more than sufficiently possible that it would be too late for him.

source.japanese:
ならば───泪を帰してやればいい。
　奴らの住処へ、大海原の水底深くへ。
source.english:
Then—send Rui back. To their dwelling.
Deep beneath the waters of the open sea.

source.japanese: ……これだけならば、それなりに論理の道筋は通っているように見えるがしかし、泪が水中で生きていられるかの確証もないままに海に投げこもうという考えは、やはりどう控え目に見積もっても正気とは思われず。
source.english: Taken alone, the argument appeared to have a certain logical course. Yet throwing Rui into the sea without any assurance that she could live underwater was, even by the most charitable estimate, hardly a sane idea.

source.japanese:
持ち上げる。抱きかかえた泪を船縁で。
　朔屋の背にぶるると緊張が走り、首筋には血の管が脂汗を絡めて浮き上がる。
　泪の体が徐々に徐々に持ち上げられ、ついには舷側の高さを超える。事ここに至っても泪が目覚める兆しは見えず、海は黒々とうねり、獲物を待ち構えた獣の如く秘やかに静まり、ああ、次の瞬間には泪はこの船から姿を消すだろう───
source.english:
He lifted Rui in his arms, there at the rail.
Tension shuddered down his back; veins rose on his neck, tangled in greasy sweat.
Slowly, slowly, her body rose, until it cleared the ship's side. Even now she showed no sign of waking. The sea heaved blackly, secretive and hushed as a beast awaiting prey. Ah, in another moment Rui would disappear from this ship—

target.text: And so───he just had to send Rui home. To the place where they dwell, the bottom of the great deep.

……From this alone, it might have seemed to be following a somewhat coherent thread of logic, but when you considered how he was about to dump Rui in the ocean with no definite proof that she could survive underwater, in the end, even when given the most generously restrained assessment, he could not be considered sane.

Up Rui went. Held in his arms by the gunwale. A tense shiver ran up Sakuya's spine, blood vessels surfaced along his neck, entwined with a clammy sweat. Rui's body was gradually, little by little, lifted higher, until she finally rose above the gunwale. Even now, after things had escalated this far, Rui still showed no hint of rousing, the ocean swelled and surged in tones of pitch black, then abated furtively, like a beast lying in wait for its prey; aah, this very next moment, Rui would surely vanish from this ship, never to be seen───

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ふぅぅ……ふぅぅぅぅぅ……っ」
source.english: “Hhhh… Hhhhhhhh…!”

source.japanese:
全身の緊張に細められ、ナイフで刻んだ切れ目のようになっている目元でも、眼球の血走って濁っているのが見てとれたし、食いしばった歯の隙間からの吐息は、狂気で歯列に湧いた小泡を弾けさせ、朔屋を鬼畜の形相と化した。
　掲げた手を前に倒せばあとはしまいのそれなりけり、泪の体は遮[さえぎ]るものもなく海に呑みこまれるだろうの、まさに寸前で。
source.english:
Tension narrowed his eyes to knife-cut slits, but their bloodshot cloudiness remained visible. Breath hissed between clenched teeth, bursting the little bubbles madness had raised along them. Sakuya's face had become a brute's.
Tip his raised hands forward, and it was over. Nothing would prevent the sea from swallowing Rui. Just before that moment—

source.japanese:
【泪】
「けぷ……っ」
source.english: “Urp…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Fffhhh……ffhhhhhh……」

Even though his eyes had narrowed into slits the size of a knife's edge from the tension running through his entire body, one could still perceive how bloodshot and murky those eyes were, and the breath escaping from between his clenched teeth was so frenzied, it made foamy spittle spill out from his rows of teeth, transforming Sakuya's visage into that of a fiend. If he were to cast down his hands held aloft, that would be the end of the whole matter, that was all, the last thing keeping Rui's body from falling would be gone, and she would surely be swallowed by the sea; it was on the very brink of that happening.
【Rui】 「Erp……」

source.japanese:
乳を飲みすぎた赤子のような小さなおくびであったけれど、朔屋の動きがぎくりと停止した。吐き戻されてはと慌てたのがこの期に及んでのこと。
　凶暴な衝動は通りモノのように不意に来たりて、そして去っていくのも唐突で、呆気ない。泪の重みによろけて踏んばった時に、もう朔屋の顔からは先刻までの凶相は消え失せていた。
source.english:
A little burp, like a baby that had drunk too much milk. Sakuya froze. Even at this point, the prospect of being vomited on alarmed him.
A violent impulse comes suddenly, like a demon passing through, then departs just as abruptly, just as easily. When he staggered under Rui's weight and braced his feet, the savage expression had already vanished from his face.

target.text: It was just a small burp, like a babe who had drunk too much milk, but Sakuya's movement stopped with a jolt. He panicked at the idea of her vomiting back up what she'd had to drink, but only now, when it was far too late to matter. A savage impulse strikes man out of nowhere like a passing spirit, and its departure is just as abrupt, even anticlimactic. He staggered from Rui's weight, and when he braced his legs to stand firm, the evil countenance that had been drawn across Sakuya's face until but moments ago had vanished.

source.japanese: 泪をそろそろと脆い細工物を案じるように下ろす。
source.english: He lowered her slowly, as though she were a fragile ornament.
“…Mmm… Cool…”

source.japanese:
夜風が火照った肌を具合良く冷やしたのか、心地好さげな吐息を漏らす泪に朔屋は、胸迫る思いがして大きく息をついた。
　たとえいくら妖しどもと通じているように見えても、だからといって抵抗も出来ない女を海に投げ捨ててしまっていいものだろうか。船縁で迷ううちに、朔屋は結局思い留まる。やはりそこまで思い切った挙に出られる青年ではないのだ。
　泪もこのままにはしておかれず、部屋に戻してやらなければならないが、凶暴な衝動が去れば疲労が一気に襲いかかり、少し休まない事には動けそうにない。
　背中を船縁に預けて一息をつくのだが。
　さて───
source.english:
Perhaps the night breeze pleasantly cooled her flushed skin. Rui sighed contentedly, and Sakuya, overcome, let out a great breath.
However closely she seemed connected to uncanny things, did that give him the right to throw a defenseless woman into the sea? Hesitating by the rail, he finally stopped himself. He was not, after all, a man capable of carrying so drastic a deed through.
He could not leave Rui here, either; he had to take her back to her room. But with the violent impulse gone, exhaustion assailed him at once. He could scarcely move without a little rest.
He leaned back against the ship's side to catch his breath.
Now—

target.text: He gently lowered Rui like he was fretting over a fragile work of art.
【Rui】 「……Nh……so refreshing……」

Perhaps the night breeze brought just the right chill to cool her flushed skin, for Rui let slip a sigh of contentment, and upon hearing that, Sakuya was seized by a chest-tightening emotion, and he exhaled a long, heavy breath. No matter how in cahoots she may have seemed to be with those supernatural beings, was it really okay to just toss a woman, one powerless to even resist, into the ocean? As he hesitated by the gunwale, Sakuya ultimately gave up on the idea. When all was said and done, the young man was not the sort who could employ such drastic means.

Rui could not simply be left as is, she would have to be returned to her room, but now that the violent impulse had passed, the fatigue assailed him all at once, and until he took a little break, it didn't seem possible for him to move. He leaned his back against the gunwale and took a breather, but. Well then───

source.japanese: 朔屋の知らざる事だが、この日の午後、信天翁号船内には久方ぶりにアレが出現していた。アレ、黒くてつやつやしたアレ。というて油虫には非ずして、むしろそちらの方が、丸めた新聞紙で叩き潰したり、さもなくば薫蒸消毒でもしてやれば、普通にくたばってくれる分だけ大人しい。
source.english: Unknown to Sakuya, that afternoon something had reappeared aboard the Albatross after a considerable absence. That thing. Black and glossy. Not a cockroach, however. Cockroaches were better behaved: swat one with a rolled newspaper, or fumigate, and it would ordinarily oblige by dying.

source.japanese: だが久しぶりに出現したアレ、密航者は、海に叩き落としたり逆さに吊したりの、大人しい人間なら五六遍は死んでいる筈の目を見ているにも関わらず、いつの間にか船内に戻ってきていると来る。駆除した後にまた出現するゴキブリだとて、彼らは別の個体が発生しているだけであり、死んだそれが蘇ってくるわけではない。
source.english: The thing that had reappeared—the stowaway—had been dropped into the sea, hung upside down, subjected to enough ordeals to kill an ordinary person five or six times over, yet somehow always returned to the ship. Even cockroaches reappearing after extermination were different individuals. The dead ones did not come back to life.

source.japanese:
であれば、吊しても落としても戻ってくる密航者はゴキブリ以上にしぶといとしか言い様がなく、対処方法としては発見したその都度駆除するしかない。
　だからこの日も発見と同時に一個捜索小隊が直ちに編成せられ、追いたてて、捕縛して、海にと叩きこんだのであった。
source.english:
A stowaway who returned whether hung or dropped was therefore more tenacious than a cockroach. The only response was to exterminate on every sighting.
So that day, the moment the stowaway was found, a search squad was assembled, gave chase, captured the quarry, and threw it into the sea.

source.japanese: その際に、舷側を海にと開く為、固定ボルトが外されてあり、うっかり者の下級水夫が、板を宛がい戻してはおいたものの、ボルトをしっかりと固定する事を怠ってしまったのだった。
source.english: To open the ship's side onto the water, they had removed its fastening bolts. A careless junior sailor replaced the board afterward, but neglected to secure those bolts properly.

target.text: It was something that Sakuya could not possibly have known, but during that same day's afternoon, that thing had shown its face aboard the Albatross again for the first time in a while. That thing: the black, glossy one. Though such may make it sound like a cockroach, it was no such thing; if anything, a cockroach could simply be squashed with a rolled-up newspaper, or if not that, when fumigated, it would actually drop dead, and in that sense, it proved a well-behaved creature.

But what had shown itself once more after a long streak of quiet was that thing, the stowaway, who had been knocked down into the ocean and hung upside down, and even though she had suffered through what would have killed any well-behaved human being five or six times by now, she would always return to the ship without anyone noticing. When something like a cockroach resurfaces after being exterminated, that is because another of its kind has hatched or shown up, not because the dead cockroach itself has resurrected.

And with that being the case, this stowaway, who always returned even after being hung up or tossed overboard, could only be described as even more tenacious than a cockroach, and the only way to deal with the infestation was to exterminate her every time she was discovered. As a result, coincident with her being discovered today, a single reconnaissance platoon had immediately been formed, roused her from cover, apprehended her, then tossed her into the ocean.

On that occasion, in order to open the ship's side to the sea, a fastened bolt had been loosened, and when the board had been returned, a careless deck boy had been negligent in ensuring that bolt was fastened tightly once more.

source.japanese:
───それが、朔屋が舷側に寄り掛かった途端に、ぱん、と小気味よくボルトが弾けて板が外れ、朔屋諸共に暗い海へと投げ出した、その理由である。
　朔屋よ、粗忽者なは其[そ]も同じである。彼の下級水夫を、怨むなかれ。
source.english:
That was why, the instant Sakuya leaned against it, a bolt popped out with a crisp snap. The board came away and flung him with it into the dark sea.
Sakuya, you are just as careless. Bear that junior sailor no grudge.

target.text: ───And so, that became the reason that the moment Sakuya leaned against the gunwale, with a pleasing pop, the bolt sprang free and the board came loose, throwing Sakuya and Rui down into the dark sea together. O Sakuya, thou art a hapless fool all the same. Pray harbour no resentment towards that deck boy.

source.japanese:
背中で突き抜いてしまえば、支えてくれる筈の板は頼りない、予想だにしていなかった顛末だけに、朔屋は着水のその瞬間まで、いやその後も、自分を見舞った事態の正体判別し得ず、地中を掘り進んでいた螻蛄が水脈にぶち当たってしまったような突然の水の冷たさにたやすく恐慌を来[きた]した。
　しかし螻蛄の方がよほどましで、あの小さな虫は土竜と似通うなりをしていながらなかなかどうして、達者に泳ぐ。
source.english:
Once his back punched through it, the board that should have supported him proved frail indeed. The outcome was so unexpected that until he struck the water—no, even afterward—Sakuya could not recognize what had happened. Like a mole cricket tunneling into an underground stream, he panicked at the sudden cold of water.
Yet the mole cricket was considerably better off: little though it was, and mole-like in form, that insect could swim surprisingly well.

target.text: As his back went through it completely, the board that should have been there to support him offered no help, and because he never even entertained this outcome as a possibility, until he hit the water, no, even after, Sakuya remained unable to grasp the truth of what had befallen him, and like a mole cricket burying through the earth that struck a water vein, the sudden chill of the water swiftly threw him into a panic. But the mole cricket was in a much more enviable position, for while that little insect resembled a mole, for whatever reason, it had a good command of swimming.

source.japanese: 一方朔屋は、手足は恐慌に振り回されるのみで、出鱈目で、水をこれっぽっちも掴んでくれやしない。そう、水、水だそれも潮だ、と朔屋がやっと認識したのは、既に深く飲んでしまった後、鼻と喉の奥が潮気にひどく痛んだからで、こらえきれずに潮の中で激しく咳きこんだ、息の泡が立ち昇っていく向きと水面を通して差しこむ月明かりで、ようやく天地の上下を掴んだのである。
source.english: Sakuya, on the other hand, merely flailed his limbs in panic. Their random motions caught not the least purchase on the water. Water—yes, water, and salt water at that. By the time he recognized it, he had already swallowed deeply; the salt hurt fiercely behind his nose and in his throat. Unable to bear it, he coughed violently beneath the sea. Only the rising bubbles of his breath, and moonlight entering through the surface, finally told him which way was up.

source.japanese: だからといって冷静さが立ち戻ったかというとそうでもなく、青年を支配したのはとにかく水面に出る事、それのみで、身体手足は藻掻くばかり、着衣で足掻いたところで悪戯に体力と息を空費するだけで、着々と呼吸の限界が迫る。
source.english: That did not mean his composure returned. One thing alone governed him: reach the surface. He could only thrash; struggling in his clothes did nothing but waste his strength and breath. All the while, he was running out of breath.

source.japanese: それでも、まさに必死の足掻きとそして靱帯に具わった自然の浮力はどうにか彼を水面へと、押し上げていく───かに見えて、ぐんと足が引かれた。
source.english: Even so, his truly desperate flailing, together with the natural buoyancy resident in his very ligaments, seemed somehow to be pushing him toward the surface—when, with a wrench, his feet were dragged down.

source.japanese: ───凄まじいまでの恐怖が襲いかかった。
source.english: A tremendous terror struck him.

source.japanese:
溺死の恐怖に混乱する朔屋を、脇からぐんと押し流す水流がある。頭からぐい、と抑えつけるような流れがある、足下から引きずりこむ引力も変わらず、青年を翻弄する四方八方からの異様な水流！
　滝壺にでも放りこまれたのならともかく、海のただ中でのこの水流は異常で、信天翁号の船体が巻き起こす引き波があったとしても、ここまでの乱流は有り得ないのに───
source.english:
As Sakuya floundered in fear of drowning, a current drove him sharply sideways. Another pressed down upon his head. The pull beneath his feet remained. Strange currents from every direction tossed him about.
In the plunge pool of a waterfall, perhaps—but out in the open sea, this was abnormal. Even if the Albatross's hull created a wake, it could not produce turbulence like this—

source.japanese:
潮に濡れ、じんじん沁みる視界では捉えきれない。酸欠に眩む思考では推し量る事も出来ない。
　青年には追い切れなかったが、この時彼の周囲の海中を縦横無尽に、弾丸の如き速度で泳走していた影があった。水中にあっては、朔屋が昨夜目の当たりにした異様は力強さと変じ、その滑らかな肌と粘膜は水の抵抗をものともせぬ、泳走に格好の力学を得ている。
source.english:
His salt-soaked, smarting eyes could not make them out. His thoughts, dimming for want of air, could not fathom them.
Sakuya could not follow them, but shadows were coursing every which way through the water around him at the speed of bullets. Underwater, the grotesquerie he had witnessed the night before became a terrible strength: their smooth skin and mucous membranes made nothing of the water's resistance; here they possessed the perfect hydrodynamics for swimming.

source.japanese:
魚怪共。
　類の部屋に参集していた魚人達。
　朔屋の周囲を自由自在に泳ぎ渡り、その速度でもって巻き起こした水流で陸の生き物を弄[もてあそ]び、水底へと引きこもうとしている。
source.english:
The fish-monsters.
The creatures who had assembled in Rui's room.
They swam freely about Sakuya, using the currents raised by their speed to toy with a creature of the land and draw him to the bottom.

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『この者……殿下につきまとうて……』
source.english: “This one… follows Her Highness about…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『不埒な……不敬な……』
source.english: “Insolent… Irreverent…”

source.japanese: 水中なのに耳の際で響くように渡りきたる声に、朔屋の恐怖は倍増の、この声は、昨夜泪の部屋にひしめいていた魚怪達の声ではないかと、恐慌の中で聴き分けたのは、幸運でもなんでもなく、朔屋の恐怖をより残酷に煽り立てるだけ。
source.english: Though he was underwater, the voices sounded close against his ears, doubling Sakuya's terror. Amid his panic he recognized them: the voices of the fish-monsters crowding Rui's cabin last night. No good fortune in that recognition. It only fanned his fear more cruelly.

source.japanese: 泪には額[ぬか]ずいていたとしても、自分を同じように扱ってくれるわけではない事は、いまし聞いた言葉からも明らかで、それ以上に目にも止まらない速度の泳走が、朔屋を海面に逃す事許さず、海中に沈めようとしているではないか。
source.english: They might bow before Rui, but plainly, from the words he had just heard, they would not treat him the same. More plainly still, their movements, too fast to see, denied him escape to the surface and tried to sink him beneath the sea.

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『……この雄が……あるから……か』
source.english: “…Is it because… this male is here…?”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『殿下が……陸に……留まりて……。
　ご帰還……為されようとせぬのは……』
source.english:
“That Her Highness… remains on land…
and will not… return…?”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『されば……許せぬ』
source.english: “Then… he cannot be forgiven…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『ならば……戻せぬ』
source.english: “Then… he cannot be allowed back…”

source.japanese: それまでは、朔屋の周囲を旋回していた黒影が、この時びしりと見事に統率された挙動で停止して、青年を剣の林の如く包囲したによって、ようやくその姿を視界に捉えた。
source.english: The black shadows circling him stopped at once, in movements of perfect discipline. Only now, surrounded as though by a forest of swords, could he finally see them.

source.japanese: 人とも魚ともつかぬ姿は、暗い海中にあってはある種の均衡を誇り、鏡花の戯曲にある黒潮騎士というのは、あるいはこうもあらんと思わせる、武威さえ備えて青年を取り囲んでいたけれど。
source.english: Neither human nor fish, their forms possessed a certain balance within the dark water. Perhaps the Black Current Knights in Kyoka's play had looked like this. Martial authority itself seemed to surround Sakuya. But—

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『殿下に……無礼……働いた……』
source.english: “You have… shown disrespect… to Her Highness…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『己が軽挙……悔やむが……よいぞ』
source.english: “Regret… your rashness…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
（違う……そうじゃないだろっ。
　俺、泪さんには何も手ぇ出してないっ）
source.english:
(No… That's not it!
I haven't laid a finger on Ms. Rui!)

source.japanese: 必死に抗議する朔屋を無視し、睨めつける魚眼に、等し並に敵意と殺意を浮かべているとあっては、均衡も武威も脅威の素でしかなく、青年の心臓がその瞬間に停止しなかったのが奇跡的、だが酸欠と恐慌とで危険なまでに激しく動悸して、このままではすぐに張り裂ける。その前に、魚怪達が停止している隙にと、朔屋は海面を目指して水を蹴った、ら。
source.english: They ignored his desperate protest. Every staring fish eye held hostility and murderous intent; balance and martial authority became merely further sources of dread. It was miraculous that his heart did not stop at once. Instead, panic and lack of air drove it to a dangerous pounding. Soon it would burst. Before that, while the fish-monsters were motionless, Sakuya kicked toward the surface—and—

source.japanese: 魚怪達の姿が一斉に掻[か]き消えた。海水を抉る異常な速度で、彼らの軌跡を海中に歪んだ後として残すほどの冠絶の機動で、下に、渦を巻きながら海底へと。
source.english: The fish-monsters vanished together. At an extraordinary speed that gouged through the seawater, with unrivaled agility that left distorted wakes behind them, they spiraled down toward the seabed.

target.text: On the other hand, Sakuya could only flail around his limbs in panic, haphazardly, unable to grasp in the slightest that it was water. Right, water, this was water, and salty water at that, Sakuya finally realized, and that was only after he'd already swallowed it deeply, so because his throat and nose ached terribly from the brine, he was unable to keep himself from coughing violently into the sea, and as he looked in the direction the bubbles formed from his breath rose in, he saw the moonlight shining through the surface of the water, and so finally grasped what was up and down of heaven and earth.

Be that as it may, it was not as though his composure had returned just from that alone; all that dominated the young man's mind was just emerging from the water, that was all, his body and limbs merely struggled desperately, but floundering about in clothes only served to squander his stamina and remaining air in turn, and steadily, the limit of his breath drew near.

Nevertheless, through truly struggling to the death, and by means of the natural buoyancy that ligaments are possessed of, he somehow made it towards the surface, pushing himself upwards───or so it looked, until his legs were suddenly pulled back down.
───An immense terror assaulted him.

There was a water current sweeping away Sakuya, who was currently in a confused panic from the fear of drowning, from the side. There was a current pushing down on his head, as if to forcefully keep him down, and the suction that dragged him downwards from below his feet hadn't changed either; there was a bizarre combination of water currents tossing Sakuya about from every which direction! It would be a different story had he been flung into a waterfall basin, but even considering the undertow created by the hull of the Albatross, these strange water currents were impossibly turbulent to simply exist by themselves right in the middle of the ocean, and yet───

He couldn't grasp it with his vision, eyes still stinging from the salty water. He couldn't surmise it with his mind, judgment dizzied by oxygen deficiency. The young man was unable to keep up with them, but right now, there were shadows racing through the water around him, swimming with bullet-like speed, freely in every which direction. Within the water, that bizarre sight that Sakuya had witnessed first-hand last night had transformed into strength, the smooth skin and membranes defying the drag force of water with ease, endowing them with flawless dynamics for swift swimming.

The fish monsters. The fishmen who had assembled in Rui's room. Masterfully swimming around Sakuya's surroundings with total freedom, toying with this creature of the land by using that speed to generate water currents, drawing him further down into the watery depths.
【Fish monster】 『This man……clinging to the shadow of Her Imperial Highness……』
【Fish monster】 『Outrageous……profane……』

Though submerged, a voice still reached him, resonating as if spoken right beside his ear, and it only doubled Sakuya's terror, for was that not the voice of the fish monsters who had crowded Rui's room last night, but being able to discern as much in the midst of his panic was not a stroke of fortune in the least, it only mercilessly stirred the dread within him.

They might have prostrated themselves in the utmost reverence before Rui, but they were certainly not going to treat him with the same courtesy, that much was glaringly obvious from the words he just heard, and on top of that, were they not swimming around him with such speed he couldn't even keep them in his sight, not permitting Sakuya escape to the surface, attempting to submerge him into the depths of the sea?
【Fish monster】 『……Perhaps……this male's presence……begets it.』
【Fish monster】 『That Her Imperial Highness…… abides……upon the shore……. And does not seek……to return home……』
【Fish monster】 『Thus……he cannot be forgiven.』
【Fish monster】 『Thus……he cannot be returned.』

Until now, the dark shadows had been circling around Sakuya, yet in this moment, they froze, halting with a sharp, perfectly unified motion, encircling the young man like a thicket of swords, and so he finally managed to steady their figures within his field of vision.

Those figures, taking a form which could neither be classified as wholly human nor fish, boasted a certain kind of equilibrium when in the dark seas, calling to mind the Knights of the Black Current from Kyouka's play, and as though they might as well have been those very knights, were endowed even with martial might as they surrounded the young man.

(TN: This is a reference to Japanese writer and playwright Izumi Kyoutarou, known by his pen name Izumi Kyouka, and specifically to one of his more well-known plays, Kaijin Bessou, written "海神別荘", known in English as The Sea God's Villa, where a beautiful woman is sent as a human sacrifice to wed the heir of the Sea God. The Knights of the Black Current, written "黒潮騎士", being the knights serving said god.)
【Fish monster】 『Thou hast committed……affronts…… against Her Imperial Highness……』
【Fish monster】 『Thou ought repent…… for thine own……rashness.』
【Naomasa】 （You're wrong……there's no way that's right. I haven't even laid so much as a finger on Rui-san!）

They ignored Sakuya as he desperately protested, enmity and murderous desire smouldering within their glaring fish eyes in equal amounts, making any balance or martial dignity nothing but another source of menace directed his way; it was miraculous that the young man's heart didn't stop right then and there, though it was certainly violently palpitating from the dangerous level of panic and lack of oxygen, and if this kept up, it would burst any moment now. Before that could happen, he took his chances while the fish monsters were still, and so Sakuya kicked through the water, aiming for the surface, but.

The fish monsters vanished all at once, and with an abnormal speed that carved through the ocean, with agility so unparalleled they left warped traces in their path, down they went towards the bottom of the sea, leaving a whirlpool in their wake.

source.japanese: 巻き起こされる渦流、朔屋の身体が強く激しく、ぐん、と引かれ、ごぼり、と肺に残った最後の空気の一泡、泡は浮上し朔屋は沈降しゆく、上は生地で下は死地、朔屋の死骸は海の深みに捉えられ、二度と空気に触れる事叶わず、底流に流されて永劫、海底を彷徨い続けるのだろう。
source.english: The vortex caught Sakuya hard, violently, wrenching him downward. The last bubble of air left his lungs with a gurgle. The bubble rose; Sakuya sank. Above was life, below was death. His corpse would be caught in the sea's depths, never again to touch air, carried by deep currents to wander the seabed forever.

target.text: The swirling current they had produced pulled Sakuya with great, violent force, the final air left in his lungs spilled out from his mouth as a single bubble, and as that bubble rose upwards, so did Sakuya sink; above lay life, below awaited certain death, Sakuya's corpse was surely being taken by the depths of the sea, never again to touch the air, swept away by the undercurrents, doomed to forever wander around Davy Jones' locker.

source.japanese: 朔屋の最後の息が立ち上り───
source.english: Sakuya's last breath rose—

source.japanese: その息の泡を、指先でちょんとつついて細かな泡に弾けさせ、入れ替わりに降りてくるものは、何、誰───
source.english: A fingertip lightly touched the bubble, bursting it into smaller beads. In its place something descended. What—who—?

target.text: Sakuya's final breath rose up───
And that bubble of breath was poked with the tip of a finger, burst into smaller bubbles, and who could it be that descended in, their, place───

source.japanese: 魚怪達の泳走が直線的で男性的であるなら、この泳ぎは優美で緩慢ですらあり、軌跡も女の持ち合わせる曲線を思わせた。
source.english: If the fish-monsters swam in lines direct and masculine, this swimmer was graceful, almost languid, her path describing the curves of a woman's body.

source.japanese: だが、その速度は魚怪達にも勝って、穏やかに身をくねらせただけと見えたのに、水中を一息に渡って、朔屋の傍へと。
source.english: Yet it was faster even than the monsters. What looked like a gentle undulation carried her across the water in a single instant, to Sakuya's side.

source.japanese:
【泪】
『のんびり気持ち良く、夜風に当たっている事もできやしない───』
source.english: “One can't even peacefully enjoy the night breeze—”

source.japanese: 声はやはり、耳の中に直接に響いているかに届いて───
source.english: Again, the voice reached him as though sounding directly inside his ears—

source.japanese:
【泪】
『お前達。なにを心得違いを起こしているの。
　この人はね、お前達が連れていっていいような方じゃありません』
source.english:
“What have you got into your heads?
This gentleman is not someone you may carry away.”

source.japanese: か暗[ぐら]い潮の中にあって、肢体は、そして纏[まと]う紺青は、霊質が零れだしたかにあえかな光を帯び───
source.english: In the dark salt water, her limbs and the deep blue she wore held a delicate light, as though the substance of spirit were spilling out—

source.japanese:
【泪】
『それに、しつこいわ。
　わたくしは戻らない。そうしかと伝えたはず。なのに未練がましく、このお船の周りを、
　うようよと───』
source.english:
“And you are persistent.
I told you plainly that I would not return. Yet you linger about this ship, swarming,
unable to let go—”

source.japanese: 聞き分けのない子供のやんちゃを、始めは微笑ましいくらいと流していた声音も、度が過ぎればその威を思い起こさせるように険に尖る───
source.english: At first her tone indulged them like disobedient children whose mischief was almost amusing. As they went too far, it sharpened, reminding them of her authority—

source.japanese:
【泪】
『これ以上不作法が過ぎるようなら。
　お前達の筋など、全て引き抜いて。
　水母にも劣る、
　海の藻屑に変えて差し上げる───
　いかが？』
source.english:
“If you persist in such ill manners,
I shall pull out every sinew you possess
and turn you into mere flotsam, worth less than a jellyfish.
How would you like that?”

source.japanese: 身をうねらせて、朔屋の傍らに泳ぎ寄って、四囲に放った視線と声とが、鋭い刃のように波及して、魚怪達を圧倒する───
source.english: She undulated to Sakuya's side. The gaze and voice she cast about spread like sharp blades, overwhelming the fish-monsters—

target.text: If the swift swimming of the fish monsters was linear and masculine, then this swimming was graceful, even languid, the trail left behind also evoking the curves a woman possesses.

However, the speed surpassed even those fish monsters, and though it seemed as if she was just calmly wriggling her body back and forth, she crossed the water in one swift motion, drawing near to Sakuya's side.
【Rui】 『I cannot even be permitted to relax and enjoy the night breeze in peace───』
Her voice, just as earlier, seemed to reach him like it was resounding directly within his ear───
【Rui】 『You lot. What kind of misbegotten folly are you committing here? This man, you see, is not the sort you are allowed to take with you.』
In the faint darkness of the sea, her body, and the Prussian blue it was clad in, was tinged with a fleeting light as though an ethereal essence was spilling out from her───
【Rui】 『And you are stubborn on top of that. I will not return. I believe that I told you so in clear terms. And yet here you are, flocking about this ship, not knowing when to give up───』

At first, her voice let pass the mischief of these unruly children, almost as though finding it endearing, but when their actions went too far, even that sharpened into harsher tones, recalling its authority───

【Rui】 『Should this insolence go any further. I shall rip out every sinew from within your bodies. I will turn you into scraps of seaweed floating around the sea, inferior even to jellyfish─── How does that sound?』
Twisting her body, she swam closer to Sakuya's side, the gaze and voice she sent forth rippling through his surroundings like a sharp blade, overwhelming the fish monsters───

source.japanese: 泪。
source.english: Rui.

source.japanese: 男達のある種の夢想の結実にして、信天翁号の珍しき客にして、朔屋の畏怖の対象でもあり、そしてこの今は。
source.english: The embodiment of a certain male dream, the Albatross's unusual passenger, the object of Sakuya's awe. And now—

source.japanese: 魚怪達を従わせる、水界の妖姫として、その不思議な、水平器の形した眸[ひとみ]で屹然と睥睨する。
source.english: An uncanny princess of the watery realm, commanding the fish-monsters, looking down upon them sternly with those strange, spirit-level-shaped pupils.

target.text: Rui.
The realization of a certain kind of male fantasy, an unusual passenger aboard the Albatross, and also the object of Sakuya's dread, and finally, right now, she was.

An eerily beautiful princess of the subaqueous realms, making the fish monsters obey her commands, towering as she scowled contemptuously with those strange eyes of hers taking the shape of a spirit level.

source.japanese: 魚怪達に動揺と畏怖が広がり、暫時の躊躇の間を開けたが、さも不興げに、泪が水底へと顎を反らしたのを見てとって、磯巾着が針で突かれた蝕手を瞬時に引き戻すような瞬転の機動で、一気に海の深くの暗がりへ、消えていく、潜っていく、一体も残らずに。
source.english: Disquiet and awe spread among the fish-monsters. They hesitated briefly. Then Rui tipped her chin toward the depths with unmistakable displeasure. Like a sea anemone instantly withdrawing its tentacles at the touch of a needle, they turned in a flash and plunged into the deep darkness. Vanished into the depths. Not one remained.

target.text: Agitation and awe rippled through the fish monsters, and for a time, they hesitated, but when they saw Rui point her chin towards the depths in evident displeasure, with a rapid shift in movement, like a sea anemone instantly pulling back its tentacles after being punctured with a needle, they vanished all at once, down towards the darkness of the watery depths, diving deeper, not a single one remaining behind.

source.japanese:
戻ってくる気配のない事を見届けるように、しばし海の暗がりを睨[にら]んでいた泪だったけれど、ふっと肩の線を柔らげて、朔屋の状態を確かめるように彼の周囲をゆるりと、一周した動きもやはり、柔らかい。
　その動きの自在な事、水中に不自由な人間を遙かに越えて優雅で、ドレスの裾[すそ]も長く翻[ひるがえ]って古代魚の鰭[ひれ]のようだ。
　いや、実際に、肌とドレスの地が溶け合って鰭[ひれ]を為しているのか。息苦しさに霞む朔屋の目では、判別がつかない。
source.english:
Rui stared into the dark water for a while, as though making sure none would return. Then her shoulders softened. She swam one slow circle around Sakuya, apparently checking his condition, her movements supple still.
The freedom of those movements was exquisite, far beyond that of a human impeded by water. The long hem of her dress streamed like the fins of an ancient fish.
Or had skin and fabric truly melted together into fins? Sakuya's eyes, dimmed by suffocation, could not tell.

target.text: Rui continued to glare into the dark sea as if watching over it to ensure there was no sign of them returning, but suddenly, the curve of her shoulders softened, and as she relaxedly swam around Sakuya as if to ascertain his condition, that one revolution around him was likewise soft. Together with the remarkable freedom of that movement, far surpassing the clumsy, constrained motions of a human underwater with its grace, the long hem of her dress also fluttered like the fins of a living fossil. No, in actuality, perhaps her skin and the fabric of her dress had melded together and formed a fin. With Sakuya's eyes, blurring as he suffocated, it couldn't be clearly discerned.

source.japanese: ただ、この意識が途絶えてしまう前に、朔屋は泪に伝えておかなければならない言葉がある。
source.english: Before his consciousness failed, however, Sakuya had something he must tell Rui.

target.text: However, before his consciousness was cut short, there were some words Sakuya had to convey to Rui.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（泪さん───ごめん。
　───俺はあなたを───）
source.english:
(Ms. Rui—I'm sorry.
I was going to—)

source.japanese: 詫びておかなければならない言葉がある。
source.english: Something for which he must apologize.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（眠っているあなたを───
　海に投げ捨てようと───）
source.english:
(While you were asleep—I was going
to throw you into the sea—)

source.japanese:
【泪】
『なにを仰有っているのやら。
　わたくしが覚えているのは、酔い心地に、
　夜風がとうても気持ち良かった事ばかり』
source.english:
“Whatever are you talking about?
All I remember is how lovely the night breeze felt,
while I was pleasantly drunk.”

source.japanese: 怨みごと、嫉みごと、言い募る口は不粋と、泪が朔屋に語るは心地好さばかり、味わった夜風の快を胸の裡に蘇らせるように目を伏せて、撫で下ろした胸乳は水中にあって重みから解放されたように、ただ柔らかに揺れる。
source.english: As though grievances and resentments were vulgar, Rui spoke only of pleasant things. She lowered her eyes, seeming to revive within herself the delight of the night breeze. Her hand stroked down over her breasts; freed of their weight in the water, they merely swayed softly.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（苦しい───死ぬのか、俺は。
　息が───）
source.english:
(It hurts—Am I going to die?
I can't breathe—)

source.japanese:
【泪】
『なんの。今宵四海は波も穏やか。
　たとえ嵐の夜でも、海の下は静かなもの。
　それこそ───
　死ぬにも退屈なくらいにね』
source.english:
“Nonsense. Tonight the four seas are calm.
Even on a stormy night, it is quiet beneath the sea.
Indeed—so quiet
that even dying would be boring.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
『あの人と初めて会った時は、
　海はもっと荒れていたっけ───
　それでもわたくしは、
　あの人を死なせなかった』
source.english:
“The sea was rougher
when I first met that man.
Even then,
I did not let him die.”

source.japanese: 力を失い、沈みゆく朔屋の前で泪は、膝を曲げ、軽く流して、遠く想うように座る姿勢で、ふわりと留まる。髪が潮を吸って嵩を増したか、地上にある時より背中に長くたなびいて、その姿、青年に或る童話中の娘の姿を想起せしめたが、耳の中では血流ががんがん鳴る、肺は胸骨を弾けさせんばかりに膨れあがる、その姿に届く前に絶後の苦しみに掻き消される。
source.english: As Sakuya lost strength and sank, Rui bent her knees and let them drift lightly aside, hovering before him as though seated, her thoughts somewhere far away. Perhaps the seawater had lent her hair greater volume; it streamed farther down her back than it did on land. The sight put Sakuya in mind of a figure from a certain fairy tale—but blood was thundering in his ears, his lungs swelling fit to burst his breastbone, and before the likeness could resolve itself, an agony beyond all he had known blotted it away.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （Rui-san───I'm sorry. ───While you were asleep───）
There were words of apology he had to give.
【Naomasa】 （I was about to─── toss you into the ocean───）
【Rui】 『Whatever could you be speaking of? All that I remember is being intoxicated, and then how exquisitely pleasant the night breeze felt.』

Words of resentment, words of jealousy, as if to say such vehement speech would be uncouth, Rui spoke only of the pleasant to Sakuya; she closed her eyes as though to recall the delight of the night breeze she had tasted within her heart; her chest, as though released from its heft underwater, simply softly swayed as she stroked it.
【Naomasa】 （It hurts───am I going to die? I can't breathe───）
【Rui】 『Nonsense. Tonight, the waves of the Seven Seas are calm. Even should it be a stormy night, it would remain calm beneath the waves. Indeed─── So tediously calm, even death would be dull.』
【Rui】 『Back when I first met that man, the sea was much rougher, I believe─── and yet, I did not let that man perish.』

Floating before Sakuya, who was drained of his strength and sinking away, Rui bent her knees, flowing with light ease, and in a seated posture as though her thoughts were drifting to places far away, she came to a gentle rest. Perhaps her hair had absorbed the sea water and grown more voluminous, for it fluttered down her back with a length greater than when on land, and her figure evoked that of a maiden from a certain fairy tale within the young man's mind, but the flow of blood was pounding within his ears, his lungs were swollen to the point of almost splitting apart his sternum, and before he could reach that figure, he was being obliterated by suffering beyond compare.

source.english:
(Rui… Air… Water…
in my lungs…)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（冷たい───からだ───
　寒い───さむ、い───）
source.english:
(Cold—My body—Cold…
so… cold…)

source.japanese:
【泪】
『もう……そんなに暴れたりなさらないで。
　ほら、つかまえた』
source.english:
“Now… Don't struggle so. There.
I've got you.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （Rui……sa……breath……. Water……in lungs……）
【Naomasa】 （Cold───body─── cold───so cold───）
【Rui】 『Enough of that……no need to thrash about so much. Look, I caught you.』

source.japanese:
藻掻いた、といってももうそれこそ腹を上にして浮かぶ魚の鈍い鰭使いで、揺らがせつつも沈みゆく朔屋の手を取り、抱き寄せた、乳房には温度というものが通っていないかに感じられたが、すぐさま伝わって、朔屋にはその温もりが泣きそうなほどに恋しかった。
　見苦しく、焦ってすがる男を引き寄せる腕は優に優れて雅に、重ね合わせる、唇と、唇と、間から漏れる気泡がきらきら、珠のように立ち上る。
source.english:
He struggled, though his movements were scarcely more than the feeble fin-strokes of a fish floating belly-up. As he swayed and sank, she took his hand and drew him close. Her breasts seemed at first to hold no warmth, but it came through at once, and Sakuya longed for it almost to the point of tears.
With surpassing grace, her arms drew in the man clinging so desperately, so unbecomingly. Lips met lips. Bubbles escaped between them, rising like glittering pearls.

target.text: He struggled, if you could call it that, for it was more like the sluggish flicks of a fin made by a fish floating belly up, and she took Sakuya's hand, who was trembling as he sunk deeper, then drew him close to her breast, and though it felt almost as if there was no warmth running through her bosom, it reached him soon enough, and to Sakuya, that heat was so dearly missed it nearly made him cry. source.english: “Mmm… Hh…”

source.japanese:
青年の体を慈しむように抱きかかえ、唇を重ねて、吹きこむ息の、甘さ、香しさ。
　女の細い喉からもたらされてほんの一呼吸か二呼吸程度のものだったのにもかかわらず、朔屋の肺はたちまち空気に満たされて、したたかに呑みこんでいたはずの海水さえいつの間にか失せていた。
source.english:
She held Sakuya tenderly, joined their lips, and breathed into him. Sweetness. Fragrance.
Though her slender throat supplied only a breath or two, Sakuya's lungs immediately filled with air. Even the seawater he had swallowed so deeply had somehow vanished.

source.japanese:
【泪】
『久方ぶりの海の中。
　わたくしには馴染みの潮[うしお]だけど。
　直さんにはどうかしら。
　もう少しだけ、二人で水遊びというのも、
　ちょっと素敵じゃなくって？』
source.english:
“It's been a long time since I was beneath the sea.
These waters are familiar to me.
How are they for you, Nao?
Wouldn't it be rather lovely to play in the water together,
just a little longer?”

source.japanese:
ドレスの裾[すそ]なのか、鰭なのか、優雅にたなびかせ、地上にあっても豊麗な泪なのに、潮の中でそれまでは縮こめていた手足を初めて伸ばしたといわんばかりに、伸びやかで、華麗で。
　だがその美を鑑賞していられる余裕は、今の朔屋にはない。吹きこまれた息がいかに芳しかろうとも、人はそもそも水中で生きるようには創られておらず、では泪は何者かという問いはさておきに進んで忘れようとするくらい、朔屋はただただ戻りたかった。海の上へ、信天翁号へ。
source.english:
Whether dress hem or fins, they streamed gracefully. Rui was magnificent even on land, but here in the sea she was expansive, splendid, as though stretching limbs she had until now kept cramped.
Sakuya, however, had no leisure to admire her beauty. Fragrant though the breath she gave him might be, humans were not made to live underwater. He was so eager to return that he deliberately set aside—even tried to forget—the question of what Rui was. Above the sea. Back to the Albatross.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（ここは……ひどく冷たいよ……。
　凍えちまうよ……戻してくれ……）
source.english:
(It's… terribly cold here…
I'll freeze… Take me back…)

source.japanese:
【泪】
『あら。直さんは水練が不得手のよう。
　珍しく貴方を抱けたのに……仕方ありません。戻りましょうね、貴方のお船に』
source.english:
“Oh. You don't seem very good at swimming, Nao.
And here I had you in my arms for once… But it can't be helped. Let's return to your ship.”

source.japanese:
抱きとめられた、朔屋の腰に、ゆら、と下肢のうねりが伝わったかと思うと、視界が揺らいで、水の抵抗など知らぬかのように上昇する。朔屋は安堵と、そして寒さのあまりにほとんど喪神して、だから泪はどんな手管を使って船上に引き上げてくれたのか、それさえはっきり覚えていない。
　水中にあったのは、数えれば短い時間なのだろうが、身体は芯から冷えてしまっていた。
source.english:
Held at the waist, Sakuya felt a gentle undulation of her lower limbs. His vision swayed, and they rose as though the water offered no resistance. Relief and cold had nearly robbed Sakuya of consciousness. He could not even clearly remember how Rui brought him back aboard.
Measured out, his time underwater had probably been brief. Yet his body was chilled to its core.

target.text: 【Rui】 『Nh……fhh……』

Embracing the young man's body as though cherishing it, their lips met, and the sweetness of the breath she blew into him, the fragrance. Though what could be given from the slender throat of a woman amounted to but one or two breaths at most, Sakuya's lungs were quickly filled with air, and even the vast quantities of water he had surely swallowed also vanished before he knew it.

【Rui】 『It has been a long while since I last went into the sea. Though these briny waters are like a dear friend to me. I am not so sure the same can be said for you, Nao-san. Would it not be lovely if we were to frolic in the water, just the two of us, for a little while longer?』

Was it the hem of her dress, was it a fin, it flowed gracefully, and though Rui was so plump and beautiful even on land, here amidst the sea water, as though to say it was the first time she stretched out limbs that until then had been contracted, she moved with a comfortable ease and elegance.

But Sakuya had not the composure to appreciate that beauty right now. No matter how sweet-scented the breath blown into him may have been, man was never created to survive underwater, but setting aside the question of whatever Rui would then be, Sakuya longed only to return, to the point of willingly trying to forget about those doubts, so earnest was that desire. Return to the surface of the sea, to the Albatross.
【Naomasa】 （It is……so terribly cold here……. I'm frozen over……take me back……）
【Rui】 『Goodness. You don't seem to be much of a swimmer, Nao-san. And after being given such a rare opportunity to embrace you…… a shame, but needs must. Let us return then, to your ship.』

Caught in her arms, the moment he thought he sensed the twisting of legs below his waist, his vision wavered, and he ascended as though the drag of water was but a suggestion. Sakuya was almost entirely stupefied from the relief and excessive cold, and so he did not clearly remember what manner of artifice Rui used to pull him back on board the ship again. Had he counted the seconds, then he had likely only been underwater for a brief time, but his body was still chilled to the marrow.

source.japanese:
どのようにして泪の船室まで辿り着いたのか、朔屋には前後が判然とせぬ。ただあったのは、おぞましい寒さと温もりへの餓[かつ]えと。
　そんな朔屋に、泪は惜しげもなく己の温度を分け与えた。寝台に横たえた青年に上に身を屈め、凍えきった肌を温[ぬく]めるのも、また肌だ。常の畏怖も戸惑いも、この時には流石に働かず、朔屋はただただ女の温もりを欲したのに、四肢は感覚が失せて、抱き寄せようともできない、足を絡める事など大難事で。
source.english:
Sakuya could not clearly recall how he had reached Rui's cabin. There had been only the dreadful cold, and his hunger for warmth.
Rui gave him hers without reserve. Bending over Sakuya where he lay upon her bed, she warmed his frozen skin with her own. Even his usual awe and bewilderment had no hold on him now. He wanted only the woman's warmth, but sensation had left his limbs. He could not draw her close; even winding his legs about her was beyond him.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「寒い……寒いよ……。
　体に何も感じられないんだ……」
source.english:
“Cold… I'm so cold…
I can't feel anything in my body…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「安心なさいな。ここにいてよ、わたくしが。
　肌は確かに、氷のように、
　硬く冷たく冷えているけれど」
source.english:
“Don't worry. I am here.
Your skin is certainly hard and cold as ice,
but—”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「貴方の胸の裡側には───ほら。
　ちゃんと聞こえます。
　───とくん、とくんって」
source.english:
“Inside your chest—there.
I can hear it perfectly.
Thump, thump.”

target.text: By whatever means it was that he may have managed to arrive at Rui's stateroom, the before as well as after yet remained unclear to Sakuya. All he felt with certainty was a horrible chill and a starving hunger for warmth.

And Rui generously shared her own warmth with Sakuya. She was bending over the young man lying on the bed, and what warmed his chilled skin was yet more skin. His usual fear and bewilderment were, understandably, absent at this moment, Sakuya simply craved the warmth of a woman, and yet he had lost all sensation in his limbs, he couldn't even attempt to pull her closer, and the act of entwining his legs with hers was an undertaking of the greatest difficulty.
【Naomasa】 「Cold……it's so cold……. Can't feel anything in my body……」
【Rui】 「Rest assured. I am right here with you. Your skin is chilly, certainly, cold and hard as ice, but.」
【Rui】 「Within your bosom───listen. You can clearly hear it beating. ───Lub-dub, lub-dub.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「貴方のいのちの証。
　しっかりと脈を刻む」
source.english:
“The proof of your life.
Beating steadily.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしのも、貴方とおんなじ。
　どう……？　感じて……」
source.english:
“Mine is just the same.
How is it…? Feel it…”

source.japanese: 朔屋の冷えきった胸板に、押しつけられてたわむ乳房のなんと柔らかで、しっとりとした熱に満ちている事か。
source.english: How soft her breasts were, yielding against Sakuya's chilled chest. How full of moist heat.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「とくん……とくん……。
　貴方のも、わたくしのも。
　鼓動が運ぶわ。暖かな、いのちの血潮。
　なにより素敵な、生きていることの証」
source.english:
“Thump… thump… Yours,
and mine.
The heartbeat carries warm, living blood.
The loveliest proof that we are alive.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ん……ああ……。じんわり、沁みてくる。
　これ、もっと……泪さん……っ」
source.english:
“Mmm… Ah… It's soaking into me,
slowly. More… Ms. Rui…!”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どうぞ、好きなだけ。欲しいだけ。
　生きていたいと願うなら。
　わたくしの肌の温[ぬく]み、
　ご存分に味わっていいのよ」
source.english:
“As much as you like.
As much as you want.
If you wish to live,
you may savor all the warmth of my skin.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「血潮が巡って、あなたの手に、足に。
　でも焦らないで。慌てなくっても大丈夫。
　今はまだ、ゆるゆると感じているだけでいい」
source.english:
“The blood will circulate into your hands, your feet.
But don't hurry. There is no need to rush.
For now, only feel it, little by little.”

source.japanese:
乳房で解[と]き解[ほぐ]すように朔屋の胸を押しながら、青年の血の筋を指先でなぞり、血潮を運ぶように。肩から二の腕へ、腕から手首へ、そして指先へ。そうして泪は、朔屋の全身へ隈無く掌を這わせ、温もりを巡らせていく。
　そのしなやかで慈しみに満ちた手は、一方で官能を催させる愛撫でもあった。
source.english:
Pressing her breasts against his chest as though to loosen and thaw it, she traced the courses of his blood with her fingertips, seeming to carry it along. Shoulder to upper arm, arm to wrist, then to fingertips. Her palms traveled every part of him, sending warmth through his body.
Those supple, tender hands were also a caress that roused desire.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Proof of your life. Beating out a steady pulse.」
【Rui】 「And mine, too, is just like yours. How is it……? Feel it……」
