【Rui】 「Lub-dub……lub-dub……. Both yours, and mine. The heartbeats carry it forth. The warm, flowing blood of life. The most wonderful proof of all, that we live.」
【Naomasa】 「Nh……aah……. It's slowly soaking into me. More of this……Rui-san……nh.」
【Rui】 「By all means, as much as you want. As much as you desire. Should you wish to live. Then bask in the heat of my skin, savour it to your heart's content.」
【Rui】 「Warm blood circulates, to your hands, to your feet. But do not be impatient. There is no need to rush things. For now, all you need to do is relax in the sensation.」

While pushing her breasts against Sakuya's chest like she was trying to unravel the cold, she traced the young man's veins with the tip of a finger as though transporting the blood through them. From his shoulder to his upper arm, from his arm to his wrist, and then to his fingertip. Like so, Rui let her palms run over every nook and cranny of Sakuya's entire body, circulating warmth throughout it. Those supple hands, tender as could be, also caressed in a way that stirred carnal desire.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「じきに、手に力が戻る。

source.english:
“Soon the strength will return to your hands.
Enough to clasp me close
without the slightest trouble.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「足だってそう。わたくしを組み敷いて、強く抑える力なんて、すぐに戻ってくるから」
source.english: “Your legs too. Soon you will have all the strength you need to pin me down and hold me fast.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺が……泪さんを……抱く？」
source.english: “Me… Hold you, Ms. Rui…?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あら。女にここまでさせておいて、
　手も出さずに眠ってしまうおつもり？
　そんなの、ずいぶんとつれない仕打ち」

But good taste isn't
all there is to a drink.”

source.japanese: 場末の赤提灯の、偏屈親爺の繰り言めいた文句と、陸に揚がった魚怪の一派の水っぽく咳きこむ音、混ざり合って酒場の喧噪に呑みこまれる───
source.english: The remark, like the refrain of some crotchety old proprietor beneath a red lantern in a disreputable quarter, mingled with the watery coughing of the fish-monsters ashore and was swallowed up in the tavern’s din—

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Right. Gross, isn't it? Well, there's more to liquor than just being delicious, is all.」

The words that sounded like the grumblings of a stubborn old geezer at a cheap, back-alley izakaya, as well as the sound of the watery coughs coming from the party of fish monsters who had been hauled ashore, drifted together before being engulfed in the racket of the tavern───

source.japanese: ───信天翁空に舞い、真水樽の蛙[カワズ]（ネルソン提督二世。初代は宗右衛門に捕食された）はぷかりと浮いて、まだ樽の水は飲用可能、なべて海は事もなし。
source.english: Albatrosses wheeled in the sky. The frog in the fresh-water barrel—Admiral Nelson II; Soemon had eaten the first—floated at ease. The water was still drinkable. All was right with the sea.

source.japanese:
実際信じられない事ではあるが、信天翁号とて、己の尻尾を追いかけ回す痩せ犬と異なり、四六時中厄介事を追い求めているわけではない。
　朔屋がのんべんだらりと上甲板で、誰からも小突かれず怒鳴られもせず海を眺めていられる日があるのだから、本当である。
　たとえば。
source.english:
Incredible though it seemed, the Albatross was not always pursuing trouble, like a skinny dog chasing its own tail. It was true:
there were days when Sakuya could loaf upon the upper deck,
gazing at the sea without being shoved or shouted at. For example—

source.japanese: ある日ある時ある海で、日々の雑役に疲れた朔屋は、船縁にもたれて無数の銀鱗連ねて眩い波に不健康に隈がこずんだ目元を細め、海洋渡る豊潤な風に、汗ばんだ髪を涼しく覚ましながらこんな事を呟きました。
source.english: One day, at some hour, upon some sea, Sakuya, weary of his daily drudgery, leaned against the rail, narrowed his dark-ringed eyes at the dazzling waves arrayed in countless silver scales, and let the rich wind roaming the ocean cool his sweat-damp hair as he murmured the following.

target.text: ───In the skies, the albatrosses soared; in the barrel of freshwater, a kajika frog (Admiral Nelson the Second. The First had been preyed upon by Souemon) floated gently on the surface; the water in the barrel was still potable, and all was calm at sea.

It might sound truly preposterous, but the Albatross, unlike a scrawny dog chasing its own tail in circles, was not actually pursuing trouble every hour of the day. There were days where Sakuya could stand completely idle on the upper deck, gazing out over the sea with nobody shoving or yelling at him; therefore it was, indeed, truth. For example:

At a certain time on a certain day in a certain ocean, Sakuya, exhausted from his daily chores, leaned against the gunwale, then narrowed his eyes and pulled the skin covered in unhealthy, dark circles taut as he looked down upon the dazzling waves, countless silver scales in unbroken chains, and while the mellow breeze sweeping across the ocean cooled his hair that was damp with sweat, he muttered thus:

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なぁんで、海の水って、
　塩っ辛いだけなんだろ」
source.english:
“Why does seawater
have to be nothing but salty?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「この海この水、全部酒だったらなぁ……」
source.english: “If only this sea, all this water, were booze…”

source.japanese:
煌めく細波に新鮮な潮風、船全体が午睡にたゆたう、船の造作はやや傷としても、総体としては水晶玉のように澄んだ昼下がりに呟かれる願いとしては、溝泥なみに腐れた願いであり、もしもお天道様まで届いてしまったなら、たちどころに臍を曲げられお隠れ遊ばされ、替わりとばかりに乱雲の一個大隊を寄越されたとて文句は言えない
　もっとも嵐が来たら来たで真水の補給程度に考えている悪たれ者揃いだし、クロが発奮するだけのこと、幸いお天道様には聞かれた気配のなく、波も静かなままの、悪運下に生まれついてる朔屋にも、お目こぼしのある日もあるという事か。
source.english:
Glittering ripples, fresh salt wind, the whole ship drifting in an afternoon doze. The ship's looks marred the picture a little, admittedly, but otherwise the afternoon was clear as a crystal ball. As wishes murmured at such a time went, his was rotten as ditch mud. Had it reached the sun, he could hardly have complained if that luminary took offense, hid itself, and sent a battalion of turbulent clouds instead.
Of course, these scoundrels would merely regard a storm as a chance to replenish their fresh water, and Kuro would rise to the occasion. Fortunately, the sun showed no sign of having heard. The waves stayed calm. Perhaps even Sakuya, born under an unlucky star, had days when he was spared.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「But really, how come sea water is just salty and nothing more, I wonder?」
【Naomasa】 「I wish this ocean, and its water, was all alcohol. Ah, if only……」

Amidst shimmering ripples and a fresh sea breeze, the entire vessel swayed in her afternoon nap, and even though her workmanship had its flaws and blemishes, on the whole, this was an early afternoon clear as a crystal ball that he muttered his wish into, a wish as putrid as ditch mud, and should it reach all the way up to the great sun, she would at once take offence and withdraw from sight, and if a battalion of rain clouds were sent in her place, then he had no standing to complain.

Of course, even should a storm come, they were a band of rowdy rascals who merely though of it as an opportunity to replenish their supply of fresh water, and only Kuro would be roused to action, but fortunately, the great sun showed no sign of having heard his plea, the waves remained calm, so perhaps even Sakuya, born under an unlucky star, had days where fate would turn a blind eye to his antics.

source.japanese: それどころか、頬に口づけしてやりたくなるほど莞爾と可愛い笑顔で、キサラと秘密めかした目配せ交わし合いながら朔屋の背後に忍び寄っていたシサムが、例の呟きを聞くやげんなりと顔顰[しか]めて下がっていったのは幸運だった。何しろシサムは退屈しのぎに朔屋を海に蹴り落として遊んでやろうと跫音忍ばせていたので。
source.english: Better still, luck favored him when Sisam overheard. She had been creeping up behind him with a smile so sweet one wanted to kiss her cheek, exchanging secret glances with Kisara. At his murmur, she grimaced in disgust and retreated. For Sisam had been approaching silently to relieve her boredom by kicking him into the sea.

source.japanese: 蹴り落とす代わりに、双子は向き合って、猫足立ちになって、おもむろにジンガのステップを踏んだ。いくらかでも身体操作に紛らわせて気を鎮めない事には、聞いた自分達の方に朔屋の馬鹿さ加減が感染して海に飛びこんでしまいかねなかったからである。
source.english: Instead of kicking him overboard, the twins faced one another, settled into cat stances, and with grave deliberation began stepping a ginga. They had to work at least some of their agitation out through the discipline of movement, lest merely hearing Sakuya’s idiocy infect them with it and send them leaping into the sea themselves.

source.japanese: ひとしきりステップを繰り返して少しは落ち着いたのか、シサムは小粋にサウスポーに構えて、四番打者を制さんかの勢いでびしゅんと型も美事に朔屋へ人差し指を突きつけた。
source.english: After repeating the steps awhile, Sisam apparently recovered some composure. She took a jaunty southpaw stance and snapped her forefinger toward Sakuya with beautiful form, as though striking out a cleanup hitter.

target.text: And that was not all, for with a smile so adorably cheerful it made one want to plant a kiss on her cheek, Shisamu had been stealing up on Sakuya from behind while exchanging furtive glances with Kisara, so he was indeed fortunate when, upon hearing his muttering, she pulled a weary grimace, then backed away. For you see, Shisamu, in an effort to stave off her boredom, had muffled her footsteps with the intent to amuse herself by kicking Sakuya into the sea.

In place of kicking him off, the twins faced each other, stood cat-footed, then began moving with slow, deliberate ginga steps. For without soothing their minds through bodily motions, after hearing Sakuya's idiocy, the sheer extent of it could well have infected them and driven them to plunge headlong into the sea.

Perhaps she'd calmed down a little after repeating those steps for a while, for Shisamu took a southpaw stance with style, and with enough zest to dominate a cleanup hitter, she thrust her index finger at Sakuya, a motion crisp and beautiful in form.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「キサラ見て。こんなところに馬鹿がいる」
source.english: “Kisara, look. There's an idiot here.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Kisara, look. There's an idiot, and here of all places.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ほんとだ。この世界で最下等の生命体だ。
　両生動物の糞をかき集めたほどの値打ちしかない、馬鹿がいる」
source.english:
“There is. The lowest form of life in this world.
An idiot worth no more than a pile of amphibian shit.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだよう、そこまで言わなくってもさ。
　夢のある願い事じゃないか」
source.english:
“Come on, there's no need to go that far.
It's a wish with a little imagination.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Wow, you're right. It's the lowest life-form in this world of ours. There's an idiot whose only value is scraping together piles of amphibian shit, right here.」
【Naomasa】 「What the hell, no need to go that far. That was a wish packed full of dreams, wasn't it?」

source.japanese:
……朔屋が日頃から勤勉な質で、酒も百薬の長と嗜む程度であれば、真面目な奴がつまらない冗談を言った、と笑われたくらいで済んだのかも知れないが。
　何しろその船縁、つい一昨日前に酒に餓えた朔屋が船内の空き瓶の底に残った酒をかき集めて作った混合酒でえらい悪酔いに陥り、日がな一日お魚に撒き餌を撒いていたのと同じ船縁である。
　双子の反応はそれはそれで奇矯に過ぎたとしても、呆れかえるのも宜[むべ]なるところで。
source.english:
Had Sakuya ordinarily been diligent, drinking only a moderate amount as the best of medicines, they might simply have laughed at a serious man's feeble joke.
But only the day before yesterday, starving for a drink, he had gathered the remnants from the ship's empty bottles into a cocktail, made himself spectacularly sick, and spent the whole day scattering chum for the fish over this very rail.
Their response might be rather eccentric, but their disgust was understandable.

target.text: ……If Sakuya had been of a habitually hard-working sort, one who kept his intake of libations, the best of medicines, within the realm of moderation, perhaps this would have ended in some good-natured laughter at a serious chap making a silly joke.

But you see, just the day before yesterday, Sakuya, thirsty for booze, had gone about raking together all the alcohol still lingering in the bottom of the empty bottles around the ship, and he had then proceeded to fall terribly sick from drinking the ungodly mixture of liquors he'd created, leading him to spend all day scattering bait for the fish over the gunwale, that very same one he was currently standing at. Even if the reaction from the twins was excessively eccentric, being utterly astounded was only fitting.

source.japanese:
流石にあまりにも頭が悪い発言に、シサム・キサラばかりか再乗船を果たした智里までも渋面に、物事を見尽くして恬淡としたこの男にそのような顔をさせるとはある意味朔屋君の天晴れである。
　ちなみにこの殺し屋、今度信天翁号に乗りこむ際は、赤毛の山猫のような娘が操る謎のおちょろ船に乗ってきたと噂されるが真偽の程は定かではない。
source.english:
The remark was so astonishingly stupid that not only Sisam and Kisara but even Tomosato, back aboard, grimaced. To make this man, who had seen everything and remained so untroubled, grimace like that was an achievement of sorts for our Sakuya.
Incidentally, rumor had it that the killer returned on a mysterious courtesan boat piloted by a girl like a red-haired wildcat. Whether that was true remained uncertain.

target.text: Naturally, when faced with such an inordinately stupid remark, it was not only Shisamu and Kisara but even Tomosato, who had finished boarding the ship once more, who grimaced, and bringing this detached man, who seemed to have witnessed everything there was to see, to make a face like that was, in a certain sense, impressively done by Sakuya.

Incidentally, the veracity of the rumour that, when this murderer had boarded the Albatross, this time, he had arrived aboard a mysterious ochorobune helmed by a red-haired girl who resembled a wildcat, still remained unclear. (TN: The ochorobune, written "おちょろ船", were small, wooden shuttle boats used during the Edo and Meiji periods to ferry courtesans out to merchant ships anchored offshore in the Seto Inland Sea, a form of street prostitution directed at visiting sailors that took place in the port town of Mitarai on the island of Oosaki-shimojima.)

source.japanese:
【智里】
「お前ねえ。いくらなんでもいい歳こいた男がそれはないだろう……。
　俺かてよう言わんぜ、そこまではよ」
source.english:
“Look. A grown man saying that… Even I
wouldn't go that far.”

source.japanese: どうだか、と二人一緒に両掌を上に開掌で、双子がじとりと目を泳がせた。彼女達にとってこの殺し屋は、朔屋の呑み友達であるという時点で同類扱いなのである。
source.english: Really? Both twins turned their palms up and looked askance. To them, being Sakuya's drinking companion was enough to place the killer in the same category.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Come on, man. That's just not gonna fly for a guy your age……. Even I couldn't bring myself to go that far, no way.」

Both twins raised their hands with open palms facing upwards, letting their eyes sullenly wander anywhere but his, as if to say "I don't know about that". To these girls, just by virtue of being Sakuya's drinking buddy, he was tarred with the same brush and treated accordingly.

source.japanese: ともかく、三方から馬鹿にされ呆れられ、逃げるにも隠れるにも残された路は背後の海くらい、朔屋はなんの気なしの、一言を聞かれただけで何故ここまで糾弾されなければならないのか、と首を捻ったところに、横合いから。
source.english: Mocked and met with disgust from three directions, with nowhere left to flee or hide but the sea behind him, Sakuya wondered why a single idle remark deserved such condemnation. Then, from the side—

target.text: Regardless, he had been met with ridicule and exasperation from three sides now, and should he try to run or hide, the only place he could go was the ocean behind his back, and so, when Sakuya tilted his head, baffled as to why he must be denounced so severely for just one thoughtless remark, it came from his side.

source.japanese: 朔屋から幾らか離れた船縁に、頬杖、日傘で寄り掛かっていたのが泪、先ほどまでの朔屋と似通った姿勢ながら、彼の今にもバランスを崩して落ちるのではと危うい姿と比べて、天水の狭間で、日傘の縁から覗かせた鼻梁と唇が際立って、画にもしたいような女ぶり。
source.english: A little farther along the rail, Rui leaned beneath a parasol, her cheek resting on her hand. Much the same posture Sakuya had taken, yet where he looked ready to lose his balance and fall, the line of her nose and lips beneath the parasol's edge stood out between sky and water. A woman one wanted to paint.

source.japanese: 直に船室へ戻るつもりなのか、くるくると日傘を畳んで、
source.english: Perhaps about to return to her cabin, she twirled the parasol closed.

target.text: There, standing by the gunwale a little apart from Sakuya, Rui leaned against her parasol, chin in hand, and though she was in a posture that closely resembled Sakuya's until just before, compared to his form that, even now, was so poorly balanced that he seemed in imminent danger of falling, where she stood in the interstice between heaven and ocean, the glimpse of her lips and nasal bridge offered from beneath the rim of the parasol made a striking sight, radiating a womanly grace worthy even of a canvas.
Perhaps she intended to return to her cabin, for she folded her parasol shut with a twirl,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そお？　わたくしは素敵だと思うけれど。
　この水が全部お酒だったら、どれだけ呑んだって呑みつくせないものねえ」
source.english:
“Really? I think it sounds lovely.
If all this water were liquor, we could drink as much as we liked and never drink it dry.”

source.japanese: ようやく一人、心強い賛同者の御登場だが、泪は泪でかなり風変わりな感性にあり（少なくとも他の乗り組み達からはそう見なされている）、彼女が首肯すれば話は余計に現実味をふわふわと欠いた。
source.english: At last, a heartening ally appeared. But Rui herself had a decidedly unusual sensibility—or so the other inhabitants of the ship considered it. Her agreement only set the conversation floating farther from reality.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Truly? I, on the other hand, think it would be wonderful. Were all these waters wine, no matter how one tried, one could never drink them dry.」

Finally, a single reassuring supporter had taken the stage, however, Rui, for her part, was possessed of quite the eccentric sensibilities (at the very least, that was how she was regarded by all the other people aboard the ship), and so when she assented to something, the matter in question only drifted further away from reality.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「今日はお日柄もよろしいご様子。
　もしかしたら、直さんのお祈り、
　届くかもしれなくってよ」
source.english:
“It appears to be an auspicious day.
Perhaps your prayer will be heard,
Nao.”

source.japanese: やんわりと受け合われても、朔屋だって、まあ切なる願いではあったけれど、現実に叶うとまでは考えもしないよしなしごと、に泪は目を柔らかにして、朔屋に頷[うなず]いてからつと打ち仰ぐ。目を伏せて、気圏の蒼と陽を直に浴びて長く吸いこんだ、こんな時、どうかすると童女めいた無邪気な貌[かお]がその輪郭の中に浮かぶ時がある。
source.english: However gently Rui humored him, Sakuya himself had never imagined that this idle fancy—heartfelt wish though it might be—would actually come true. Her eyes softened; she nodded to him, then abruptly lifted her face. Lowering her eyes, she took the blue air and sunlight full upon her and drew a long breath. At such moments, the innocent face of a little girl would sometimes surface in her features.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Today also seems an auspicious day. So perhaps it is possible that maybe, just maybe, Nao-san's prayer might be answered.」

Though she assured him with gentle words, even Sakuya though that, well, while it was a heartfelt wish to him, it was still idle nonsense that he never even imagined would come true in reality; the look in Rui's eyes softened, she nodded to him, and then suddenly lifted her gaze to the skies. She lowered her eyes again, drank directly in the azure of the sky and the radiance of the sun, and in times like these, a look of girlish innocence was apt to flit across her features.

source.japanese: 襤褸船の中でどこか懐かしく、愛おしげな風景で、つい見とれた朔屋の脇を抜けて、中層甲板へ。
source.english: A sight somehow nostalgic, somehow dear, aboard this wreck. Sakuya found himself gazing at her as she passed him and went down to the middle deck.

target.text: While Sakuya found himself captivated by the sight that, upon this ramshackle ship, seemed somewhat nostalgic, even lovely, she made her way past his side, heading down towards the middle deck.

source.japanese:
シサムとキサラも朔屋をいじるのに飽きたか、別の暇潰しの種を探して散っていった。
　……客の泪はともかく、一等航海士からしてこうとあっては、今日は本当に信天翁号にとっては無為の空隙に落ちこんだような日なのだろう。
source.english:
Sisam and Kisara, too, seemed to have tired of tormenting Sakuya, and scattered in search of some other way to kill time.
Rui, being a passenger, was one thing; but if even the first mate was carrying on like this, today truly must have been one of those days when the Albatross had slipped into a pocket of pure idleness.

target.text: Perhaps Shisamu and Kisara also found themselves bored with making fun of Sakuya, for they went their separate ways, looking for some other means of killing time. ……Setting aside Rui the passenger, since even the first mates acted like this, then today was surely one of those days where the Albatross had slipped into a void of inaction.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……俺もたいがい人のこたぁ言えねえが、なんだってこう駄目な奴ばっかなんだろなこの船は」
source.english: “…I'm hardly one to criticize, but why is this ship full of such useless people?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……I know I'm not really one to talk here, but I really do wonder why this ship is full of nothing but the most hopeless people.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だよなあ。俺も事あるごとにびっくりだ」
source.english: “Right? I'm amazed every time.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「I know, right? I also find myself shocked at every turn.」

source.japanese: 自分を棚に上げての他人事、智里も苦笑で煙管を捻り出し、一服着ける───と、バラックの影から賑々しい音曲が鳴って、現れましたのは下級水夫君達二人。
source.english: With their own failings safely set upon the shelf and the whole matter made somebody else’s concern, Tomosato gave a wry smile, drew out his pipe, and lit it—whereupon a merry clatter of music burst from behind a shack, and who should appear but our two junior sailors.

target.text: Not seeing the beam in his own eye, Tomosato pulled out his kiseru with a wry smile, then took a puff─── as he did, a merry musical performance rang out from behind a shack, and who should emerge from there but two deck boys.

source.japanese: 一人は小器用にバンドネオンなどを鳴らしたて、一人は人形芝居に遣うような箱舞台をぶら下げて、朔屋と智里の前に進み出ると、
source.english: One skillfully played a bandoneon. The other carried a little box-stage of the kind used for puppet shows. They advanced before Sakuya and Tomosato.

target.text: One played on a bandoneon or something with modest skill, the other carried a little box stage like the sort used for puppet shows, and as they stepped forward before Sakuya and Tomosato,

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「何故なに海洋質問ばこ～～。
　今日の質問は、
『どうして海の水はしょっぱいのか』～～」
source.english:
“The Sea Question Box—Whys and Whats!
Today's question:
‘Why is seawater salty?’”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「It's the ocean question box of whys and whats～～. Today's question is: 『Why is sea water salty?』～～」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「どうしてだと思う水夫Ａ君」
source.english: “Why do you think it is, Sailor A?”

source.japanese: 散り紙で作った花と蝶をぱっぱっと撒くような、軽快な調子で口舌並べて、一人は楽器で節を付け、一人は箱舞台の中でちょいちょい指人形などを操って、随分と練習を積んだのか、舌も人形遣いもそれなりに練れていた。
source.english: Their patter was light as scattered paper flowers and butterflies. One supplied the tune, while the other busily worked finger puppets inside the box. They must have practiced considerably: speech and puppetry alike had acquired some polish.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Why do you think that is, sailor A?」

Stringing the words together in a lively cadence, as though scattering blossoms and butterflies cut from scrap paper, one setting the performance to music with his instrument, the other effortlessly controlling finger puppets inside the box stage, and perhaps they had practiced a significant amount, for both their tongues and puppetry alike were fairly polished.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「うん、それはね水夫Ｂ君。昔々、海の水がまだ真水だった頃、人間達が魚を捕りすぎていた事に怒った、妖怪塩辛入道が───」
source.english: “Well, Sailor B, long, long ago, when the sea was still fresh water, the Salty Monk monster grew angry because humans were catching too many fish—”

source.japanese:
二人の小芝居、それなりに練れていたのに。
　箱舞台では塩辛某が小さな海の底で、もっと小さな卓袱台を返していたのに。
source.english:
Their little performance was quite polished. Within the box,
that salty fellow was overturning a still smaller low table at the bottom of a miniature sea. And yet—

source.japanese: 二人の前からは、智里も朔屋も消えていて、こういう小芝居をわりと好む朔屋さえいなくなっていたのは、智里が隠してある酒でも出すべえと誘ったからだが、
source.english: Tomosato and Sakuya were gone. Even Sakuya, who rather liked this sort of play, was gone: Tomosato had invited him to sample some hidden liquor.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Yes, so about that, sailor B. Long, loooong ago, back when the ocean water was still freshwater, the yokai Shiokara-nyuudou, angered by the humans catching too many fish───」 (TN: 塩辛入道, or Shiokara-nyuudou as he is affectionately known here, is not a real yokai, but his name is composed of two parts. The former is shiokara, which is a paste made from fermented seafood, and the latter is nyuudou, which refers to a monk, and by extension, their bald heads, hence its frequent inclusion in the name of bald yokai all over Japan.)
Even though their play really was quite the refined production. Even though Mr. Shiokara was at the bottom of a small sea, flipping over an even smaller tea table.

Both Tomosato and Sakuya had vanished from their sight, and that even Sakuya, who was otherwise quite fond of these kinds of little performances, had disappeared, was because Tomosato had tempted him to leave by suggesting they break out some of the booze he'd stashed away, but……

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あれ？　誰もいない」
source.english: “Huh? Nobody's here.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Huh? There's nobody here.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「どうしてちゃんと最後まで聞かないかなあ」
source.english: “Why won't they listen all the way to the end?”

source.japanese: がっかりして、拗ね加減で口を尖らせた水夫達の耳に、この時。
source.english: Disappointed, the sailors pouted sulkily. Just then they heard—

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Why didn't they listen all the way to the end?」
At that moment, in the ears of the sailors pursing their lips, sulky and disappointed,

source.japanese:
ねがい　　は　
　　　　　かなえられた　　　！！
source.english:
THE WISH
HAS BEEN GRANTED!!

target.text: Your wish has been granted !!

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「……？　今なんか、聞こえてこなかった」
source.english: “…? Didn't you just hear something?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「……? Did you hear something just now?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ん、どうだろう」
source.english: “Hmm… Not sure.”

source.japanese:
海の底から響いてきたこんな声を、聞きとったのは水夫達だけであった。
　実はこの時その瞬間、星辰の運行が千年に一度の宿に入っていたのか、あるいは気まぐれな海の大神が聞き耳を立てていたのか。
　
　とにもかくにも───
source.english:
Only the sailors heard that voice resounding from the seabed. Perhaps,
at that very instant, the stars had entered a station they reached once in a thousand years. Or perhaps some capricious great sea god had been listening.
In any event—

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Hm, I'm not really sure.」

It was only these two sailors who had heard that voice resounding from the depths of the ocean. Could it be that, as a matter of fact, in this moment, this very instant, the course of the celestial bodies had entered an alignment that only occurs once in a millennium? Or perhaps it was simply that the capricious god of the seas had pricked up his ears and listened attentively? In all and any cases───

source.japanese:
愛すべき読書氏よ。
　少々困難な話かも知れないが───
　思い浮かべていただきたい。
　おんぼろで、継ぎ接[は]ぎだらけで、錆と虫食いが埋めつくし、半壊して、ぎいぎい軋んで、油断すると浸水が始まって、主機関などは重度の心臓病者のように何時停まっても不思議ではない、造船技術と物理法則への卑猥にして嘲笑的な挑戦の顕現であるこの船、信天翁号にも、造船所にてボルトの最後の一本を締められて間もなく、卸し立てで、晴れ晴れしい進水式を迎えた瞬間というのも、あるいはあった事だろう。
source.english:
Beloved reader.
This may be asking rather a lot—
but I ask you to imagine it.
Even this ship, the Albatross—decrepit, patched from stem to stern, riddled with rust and worm-eaten holes, half in ruins, creaking at every joint, ready to spring a leak at the least inattention, her main engine no less liable to stop at any moment than the heart of a gravely ill man; this obscene, jeering affront to shipbuilding and the laws of physics made manifest—even she, perhaps, once had her moment, not long after the shipyard tightened her final bolt, when, fresh-built and resplendent, she came to her launching.

source.japanese:
その時をば、想像していただきたい。
　……少々どころか、いや、非常に困難かも知れないが。
source.english:
Try to imagine that moment.
Perhaps ‘a little’ was not quite right. Perhaps it is exceedingly difficult.

source.japanese: 五色の紙テープが港の人々の手へと架け渡されて、舷側からは色絢な滝、ブラスバンドの奏でる音楽は人々の歓声に掻[か]き消されそう、弾ける花火は迸[ほとばし]る歓喜の現れか、きらきらと光の粒のように紙吹雪が舞う、音も光もなにもかも、嬉しさに大笑しているような情景の───
source.english: Streamers in five colors span the distance to the hands of people on the quay, a many-colored waterfall from her side. The brass band's music nearly vanishes beneath the cheers. Fireworks burst like joy made visible; confetti dances like glittering particles of light. Sound, light, everything seems to be laughing in delight—

source.japanese: 一番の焦点は酒の瓶を船首にぶつけるあの瞬間だろう。参集した者の注視の中では、支綱に繋いだ酒瓶が船首へと迫ってゆくのが期待の余りに緩慢に見える、そして激突して、ぱん、と酒と共に硝子の欠片がガス星の爆発のよう、砕け散る、そして船は初夜に臨む乙女のようにそろそろと進み往く。
source.english: The highlight would be that moment when the bottle strikes the bow. Under the eyes of everyone assembled, the bottle swings toward the bow on its rope, seeming slow in their eager anticipation. Then it strikes. Pop: liquor and glass scatter like an exploding gaseous star. The ship begins to move, cautiously as a maiden approaching her wedding night.

source.japanese: この晴れ晴れしい進水式に用いられる酒は今となってはシャンパンが用いられるのがほとんどだが、かつては専ら赤葡萄酒だったという。神に捧げる為の生き血の代用だったと言うが、その真偽の程はさておくとして、信天翁号も赤葡萄酒の瓶を受けて、破瓜の徴[しるし]のよう朱色を船首に垂らして、海に進み出た瞬間があったのかも……知れ……ない……が。
source.english: Nowadays champagne is generally used in such bright launching ceremonies, but once, it is said, red wine was the rule. A substitute for fresh blood offered to the gods—or so the story goes; its truth may be left aside. Perhaps the Albatross too once received a bottle of red wine, letting scarlet run down her bow like a sign of deflowering as she entered the sea. Perhaps… she… did… But—

source.japanese: 想像もつかないというのが、まあ大方の反応かと思われる。
source.english: Most people, one imagines, would find it impossible to picture.

source.japanese:
だが、少なくともこの今は、信天翁号は舳先を赤色で濡らしていた。
　船腹も赤で染まっていた。艫も赤に浸り、それどころか喫水下全体が赤に漬かっていた。染まりも漬かりもしよう。
　信天翁号の前も後ろも右も左も、全ての海が赤く変じているとあらば。
　赤いというより赤黒い。あたり一面の赤黒い海から立ち籠める、薄い赤紫の霞から漂ってきているのは、黒すぐりのような李[すもも]のような、木イチゴの様な───赤葡萄酒の香り。
source.english:
At least now, however, the Albatross's bow was wet with red.
Her belly was stained red. Her stern soaked in it; indeed, everything below the waterline lay steeped in red. Small wonder.
Before her, behind her, to either side, the entire sea had turned red.
Red-black, rather. A thin purplish-red haze rose from that dark red expanse, carrying scents of blackcurrant, plum, berries—the scent of red wine.

target.text: O beloved reader. Though this may prove to be of some difficulty─── Please try to picture the following in your mind:

Dilapidated, cobbled together with seams all over, riddled with rust, pitted as though worm-eaten, partially destroyed, heavily creaking, would begin to take water the moment you let your guard down, and a wretched main engine like a patient suffering from severe heart disease, liable to stop at any moment to the surprise of absolutely no one: even this ship, the very embodiment of an obscene and sneering challenge against shipbuilding technology and the laws of physics, even the Albatross surely experienced that moment when, fresh from the shipyard, just after the last bolt was tightened, she was celebrated with a splendid launching ceremony, probably.
Please try to envision that moment. ……A task not just a little difficult, yea, perhaps it might even be exceedingly so.

Five-coloured paper streamers bridge the gap to the hands of the crowd on the dock, forming a brilliantly cascading waterfall of colour down the ship's side, and the music performed by the brass band almost seems to be drowned out in the shouts of joy from the people; perhaps the bursting fireworks are an expression of the surging cheer, confetti soaring through the sky like glittering motes of light, the sounds and the lights and anything and everything, a scene where all seem to laugh heartily from the sheer happiness of it all───

And the highlight is sure to be the moment that bottle of alcohol is smashed against the bow. To the eyes of the assembled onlookers, the bottle of alcohol tied to that final ceremonial mooring line seems to approach the bow with an almost unsettling slowness, drawn out by the heavy weight of their anticipation, and then, it violently crashes against the ship with a bang, the liquor and shards of glass shattering into scattering fragments like a stellar explosion, and finally, the ship gingerly advances, as though a maiden on the threshold of her bridal night.

These days, it is mostly champagne that is used for these exuberant ceremonial ship launchings, but prior to that, it was supposedly mainly red wine. It is said to be with the purpose of offering to God a substitute for lifeblood, but setting aside the extent to which that is true or false, the Albatross is also struck by a bottle of red wine, the scarlet red trailing down the bow like the mark of a maiden deflowered, perhaps experiencing that moment of setting out to sea; she might have…… maybe……but.
I believe the prevailing reaction to this would be: "I can't even begin to imagine that."

However, right now, at the very least, the bow of the Albatross was wet with the colour of red. The ship's hull was also dyed red. The stern, too, was saturated in crimson, and indeed, the whole part of her that made up her draught was immersed in it. Stained and saturated alike, let us say. Should it be the case that the sea ahead of the Albatross, and behind her, and to her left and her right as well, had turned red. It was more of a dark red than just red. From the dark red sea covering all around them, a pale haze of purplish red billowed, carrying with it scents like cassis, plums, raspberries ───the aromas of red wine.

source.japanese: 信天翁号は───赤葡萄酒の海の中のただ中に浮かんでいたので。
source.english: For the Albatross floated in the midst of a sea of red wine.

source.japanese: 冗談などではない。酒も酒、本当に葡萄酒、赤ワインの海で、信天翁号の上甲板に集まって水夫長以下下級水夫達は皆、頬を自分で叩いて見るやらお互いに二の腕を抓[つね]り合うやらで夢に非ず現[うつつ]と確かめていたけれど、それでも愕然と口を半開きにするのが避けられず、
source.english: No joke. Liquor, actual wine, a sea of red wine. On the upper deck, the boatswain and junior sailors gathered, slapped their own cheeks, pinched one another's upper arms, and verified that this was waking reality, not a dream. Even so, they could not keep their mouths from hanging half open in astonishment.

target.text: And that was because the Albatross ───was floating in the heart of a sea of red wine.

And this was no mere jest. The wine was wine, it really was red wine, they were in a sea of red wine; gathered on the upper deck of the Albatross, the Bosun and all the deck boys slapped their own cheeks and pinched one another's arms to assure themselves that this was no dream but waking reality, yet they still could not help but stand aghast, mouths half agape in astonishment,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……おい、こりゃあなんの冗談だ……。
　海が赤くなるなぁ、
　見た事がないでもないが……」
source.english:
“…Hey.
What sort of joke is this…? I've seen the sea turn red before,
but…”

source.japanese:
そうそうある事ではないが、海が赤くなるのは有り得ない現象ではない。赤潮、というのがあるし、豪州南端の島嶼近辺のある海域では常に海水が赤く染まっているという。
　しかし、さしもの水夫長であっても、海水が赤葡萄酒に変ずるなど、これまで遭遇はおろか風聞にも覚えのない現象だった。
source.english:
Not common, but a red sea was not impossible. There were red tides; in a certain stretch near the islands off Australia's southern end, the seawater was said to be permanently red.
But even the boatswain had never encountered seawater becoming red wine, nor recalled hearing of such a thing.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Oi, what kind of joke is this……. It's not like I've never seen the sea turn red before, but……」

Though it doesn't happen often, the sea turning red is not an impossible phenomenon. There is the red tide, and it is also said that the waters near the islands of the southern tip of Australia are perpetually dyed red. However, for the ocean to change into red wine of all the things, now that was a phenomenon that even the Bosun had never encountered, let alone heard rumours of before.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「水夫長、これ、本当にお酒だよ！
　赤葡萄酒、
　それもブルゴーニュのフルボディ、
　瓶詰めしてから七・八年……？
　うん、それくらい経ってる奴とそっくり。
　良く熟れた葡萄酒だよ」
source.english:
“Boatswain, this really is liquor!
Red wine.
Full-bodied Burgundy, too.
Seven or eight years since bottling…?
Yes, it's just like one about that old.
A well-matured wine.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Bosun, this is actually wine! Red wine, and a full-bodied Burgundy at that, bottled for seven, maybe eight years……? Yeah, it's exactly like a bottle aged that long. This is well-aged wine.」

source.japanese: 早速桶を降ろして汲[く]み上げた下級水夫が、グラスに移して日に翳[かざ]し、色の深いところでは紅玉[ルビー]、光に透けるところでは紫水晶、グラスの縁では黄玉と変化する階調を賞翫し、香りを確かめて一口注意深く啜[すす]りと、いっぱしの評論家のような作法で味わって鑑定した後、はふぅんとドミノ板のようにぶっ倒れて上甲板に酒の残りと硝子片を撒き散らした。訓練された玄人はだしの舌を具[そな]えながら、酒精にはてんで弱いのがこの下級水夫である。
source.english: A junior sailor had promptly lowered a bucket and drawn some up. He poured it into a glass and held it to the sun, appreciating the shifting shades: ruby in the deeper color, amethyst where light passed through, topaz at the rim. He checked its bouquet and sipped cautiously, tasting and appraising it with the manners of a proper critic. Then, with a little sigh, he toppled like a domino, scattering the remaining wine and broken glass across the deck. This junior sailor's palate put a trained professional to shame. His tolerance for alcohol was nonexistent.

target.text: A deck boy had lowered a bucket and drawn some wine without delay, then transferred it to a glass and held it aloft to the sun; in its deepest tones, the colour was ruby, where the light shone through, it was amethyst, and by the rim of the glass, it was topaz, he noted as he admired the changing gradations, and after he then checked the fragrance, took an attentive sip, savoured the taste with the mannerisms of a fully-fledged sommelier, and finally gave his expert appraisal, he then collapsed with a thud like a domino tile, scattering the remaining wine and glass shards all over the upper deck.
While endowed with a tongue that could put a practiced connoisseur to shame, this deck boy had a very low tolerance for alcohol.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう、講釈ご苦労。
　だが今はそんなんどうでもええんだ。
　本気でこの海一面みんな酒か……」
source.english:
“Yeah, thanks for the lecture.
None of that matters now.
Is this whole damned sea really booze…?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right, appreciate the long-winded lecture. But who gives a shit about that right now. Is this entire damn sea really all wine……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ねえ水夫長、この葡萄酒、汲み上げて樽詰めにしたら、きっと良い値が付くと思う」
source.english: “Boatswain, if we draw this wine up and put it in barrels, I think it'll fetch a good price.”

source.japanese: ぶっ倒れた仲間の襟を緩め、ぱたぱたと風で醒ましてやりながらで看護婦にもしたいくらいのまめまめしさだが、そうやって送る風にも酒精の匂いたっぷりと密なのだから、さっさと船の中に担いでいってやるべきの。
source.english: He loosened his fallen companion's collar and fanned him, tending him so carefully that one might have made him a nurse. But the very air he fanned was dense with alcohol. He ought to have carried the patient below immediately.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Hey, Bosun, if we were to draw this wine and seal it in barrels, I think it'd definitely fetch a good price.」

While loosening the collar of his fallen brother and fanning him to sober him up was a show of such earnest diligence, it tempted one to make a nurse of him, even the air being fanned thus was packed dense with the reek of spirits, so he really ought to have carried him within the ship without delay.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おう、そりゃ良い考えだ。
　実は俺もそいつは考えた。だがな……」
source.english:
“Yeah, good idea.
Truth is, I thought of that too. But…”

source.japanese: 下級水夫へ賛意を示したもののお愛想で、水夫長にとってはそんな暢気な問題ではない。操舵室に飛びこみ、機関室へ繋がる伝声管に飛びついて胴間声張り上げる……。
source.english: He agreed with the junior sailor merely to be polite. To the boatswain, this was nothing to be so carefree about. He leaped into the wheelhouse, seized the speaking tube to the engine room, and bellowed.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Right, that's an excellent idea. Truth is, I had the very same. Thing is……」

Though he expressed agreement with the deck boy, it was but courtesy, for in the Bosun's eyes, this was not so lighthearted an issue. He barged into the wheelhouse, leapt at the voice pipe connecting to the engine room, then let loose a full-bodied shout with his booming voice…….

source.japanese: 熱っぽい暗闇に浮かぶ地獄の劫火めいた赤い輝きを背に、下級水夫の報告を受ける機関長は端正な貌立ちに黒眼鏡の、碩学を惑わす魔王じみた佇[たたず]まいだが、実際には相手が礼儀よろしきを守る限りは誰であろうと丁重に相対する男で、この時も蜜をたっぷり利かせた紅茶とスコーンを振る舞った。
source.english: Against a red glow like hellfire in the feverish darkness, the chief engineer received a junior sailor's report. Handsome features, dark glasses: he looked like a demon king tempting some great scholar. In fact, he treated anyone courteously, provided they observed good manners. Now too, he served tea sweetened generously with honey, and scones.

target.text: Back facing the red brilliance reminiscent of the apocalyptic conflagrations of Hell looming in the feverish darkness, the Chief Engineer's handsome features were framed by his dark glasses as he received a report from a deck boy, his presence like that of the Prince of Darkness confounding a great scholar, but in reality, this man would always treat any with courtesy, regardless of who they may be, provided they observed proper decorum in turn, and even right now, he was treating the deck boy before him to a cup of black tea flavoured with plenty of honey as well as a scone.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ご苦労様───そうか。酔っ払った朔屋君辺りの与太話かと思ったが。
　どうやら本当のようですね……」
source.english:
“Thank you. I see. I thought it might be some drunken nonsense from Sakuya.
But it appears to be true…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Thank you for the trouble───I see. I believed it to be balderdash from a drunken Sakuya or some such, but. Seems like it is true after all, yes……」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「船の喫水も具合が違う……。
　なによりこれは───」
source.english:
“The ship's draft has changed too.
Above all, this—”

source.japanese:
機関室備え付けの鉄椅子に足を組み、組んだ指の上に顎を乗せて機関に耳を澄ます風情の機関長は実に泰然としたものだったが、そんな彼でさえ声音には幾許かの懸念を浮かせていた。
　と、壁にのたうつ配管の中の、真鍮の伝声管の蓋が、裡からの怒鳴り声に押されてがぱんと独りでに開いて、吐き出したは水夫長の怒鳴り声、
source.english:
Seated in one of the engine room's iron chairs, legs crossed, chin resting on his interlaced fingers, the chief engineer listened to the machinery with perfect composure. Even his voice, however, carried a little concern.
Amid the pipes writhing along the wall, the brass speaking tube's cover sprang open of its own accord, forced by the shouting within. Out came the boatswain's roar.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『ロックフォール、
　おい、聞こえてるかっ？』
source.english:
“Roquefort!
Hey, can you hear me?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Even the ship's draught is different ……. But most important of all, this is───」

Crossing his legs in the iron chair that the engine room was furnished with, as the Chief Engineer placed his jaw atop his folded fingers and appeared to strain his ears for the sound of the engine, he truly was the picture of self-possession, but even he betrayed a trace of concern through the tone of his voice. And then, from amidst the squirming pipes littering the wall, the lid of the brass voice pipe was pushed out from the inside by an angry voice, opening by itself with a bang, and the yelling of the Bosun spewed out from within,
【Bosun】 『Roquefort, oi, can you hear me!?』

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ほら、ござった。
　ええ聞こえていますよ」
source.english:
“Ah, there he is. Yes,
I can hear you.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『信じられねえだろうが───』
source.english: “You won't believe it, but—”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「And behold, there he is. Yes, I can certainly hear you.」
【Bosun】 『You might not believe me when I tell you this, but───』

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「海の状態なら、把握しています。
　それよりこちらからも報告が」
source.english:
“I am aware of the sea's condition.
More importantly, I have a report of my own.”

source.japanese: 歩み寄って伝声管に応答する声は、静かで渋く落ち着いて、水夫長の破鐘とは好対照を成した。
source.english: He approached and answered the tube in a quiet, mellow, composed voice, in striking contrast to the boatswain's cracked-bell roar.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「───推進軸に障害を受けている。恐らくは藻かなにかでしょうが……。
　もともと信天翁の主罐には、こんな海を航海できるほどの推力はない」
source.english:
“Something is obstructing the propeller shaft. Probably weed of some kind.
The Albatross's main boiler never had enough power to drive through a sea like this.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『藻だぁ!?　そんなもんまで沈んでやがんのかこの辺りには』
source.english: “Weed!? There's even that crap down there?”

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「それに加えて、辺りの海が葡萄酒に変わっているとなると……液体の表面張力も異なってくる」
source.english: “And if the surrounding sea has become wine, the liquid's surface tension will be different too.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「If this is about the state of the sea, then I have already grasped it. More importantly, I also have a report I must give.」
He walked closer, his voice responding to the voice pipe subdued, mellow, and calm, forming a marked contrast with the great cracked bell resounding hoarsely from the Bosun.

【Chief Engineer】 「───The screw is experiencing a malfunction. Most likely caused by some manner of algae, although……. The main boiler of the Albatross could never provide enough propulsion to navigate a sea of this sort in the first place.」
【Bosun】 『SEAWEED!? We even have shit like that below the waters here?』
【Chief Engineer】 「Furthermore, now that the surrounding waters have turned into wine…… the surface tension of the liquid is changing as well.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『……まだるっこしいな、あんたはいつも。
　どういう事なのか、先に言えよっ』
source.english:
“You're always so long-winded!
Tell me what it means first!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 『……Same as always with you, tediously roundabout. Start by telling me what it means!』

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「そう怒鳴らずとも聞こえている。
　端的に言いますとね。このままではこの船は、航行不能という事ですよ」
source.english:
“I can hear without your shouting.
In short: under these conditions, this ship cannot proceed.”

source.japanese: 伝声管の向こうで急かし立てる水夫長の声にも悠揚と迫らぬ調子で、しかし告げた事実は空恐ろしい、この男は常に沈着でその言葉にも盤石の重みがあるだけに、虚飾のない事実が重苦しい。水夫長でさえ一瞬言葉を失ったようだった。
source.english: The boatswain's impatient voice at the other end did nothing to hurry his easy, measured delivery. Yet what he reported was frightening. This man was always calm; his words had the weight of bedrock, and the unadorned fact lay heavy. Even the boatswain seemed briefly at a loss for words.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『……。……。どうにか、なんねえのか？』
source.english: “… …Can't something be done?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「I can hear you just fine without all the yelling. Allow me to speak frankly then. As things stand, this ship will become unable to sail.」

Even in response to the urgency in the Bosun's pressing voice coming from the other end of the voice pipe, he answered in a calm and unhurried manner, however, what he announced was truly alarming; precisely by virtue of this man's ever-present composure, even his words carried the weight of solid rock, and the unvarnished truth coming from his lips was oppressive. Even the Bosun seemed at a loss for words for a brief moment.
【Bosun】 『……. ……. Is there anything that can be done?』

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「辺りの藻を除去してもらえれば。
　あるいは海の状態を、通常の海水に戻してもらえれば。その両方だって構わないが」
source.english:
“If you could remove the weed around us.
Or restore the sea to ordinary seawater. Both would be perfectly acceptable too.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『そんなんどうにかなるかよっ。
　こっちだって、なんだってこんな目に遭ってんだか、それさえわからねえんだから！』
source.english:
“How the hell are we
supposed to do that? We don't even know why this is happening!”

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……機関室の方から言える事は、全て言いました。主罐に無理を言わせれば、少しくらいは進めるかも知れない」
source.english: “…I have told you everything the engine room can say. If we force the main boiler, we might make a little headway.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「If you were to get rid of the algae in the vicinity. Or perhaps, if you were to restore the state of the sea to its usual saltwater. Either option would be acceptable.」
【Bosun】 『Like hell we can just do that. It's not like I even know why we're stuck in this mess to begin with!』
【Chief Engineer】 「……I have told you all there is to say from the engine room. Should we demand the unreasonable from the main boiler, perhaps we might be able to make a little headway.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「でも石炭が切れたら、そこでお終いだ。それでもいいなら、多少の無茶はやりますが」
source.english: “But when the coal runs out, that will be the end. If you accept that, I can overtax her somewhat.”

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
『……ああもう、七つの海の地獄蛸め！───』
source.english: “Oh, the fucking hell-octopuses of the seven seas!—”

source.japanese: その後も何事か古典的なの独創的なの取り混ぜて罵声は続いたようだが、そこまでは突き合う義理持たぬと機関長は伝声管の蓋を閉め、紅茶でスコーンを流しこんでいる下級水夫へ向き直る。
source.english: More curses followed, apparently, a mixture of the classical and the original. The chief engineer felt no obligation to hear him out. He closed the tube's cover and turned to the junior sailor, who was washing down a scone with tea.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「But the moment we run out of coal, that will be the end of things. If you say that is still acceptable, then I shall permit myself to act a little rashly.」
【Bosun】 『……Blast you, you infernal octopus of The Seven Seas!───』

After that, the stream of abuse formed from a mix of the classical and the original seemed to continue, but deciding that he had no obligation to deal with any further mutual jabbing, the Chief Engineer closed the lid of the voice pipe, then turned back around to face the deck boy washing down scones with black tea.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……ところで、いったい何故水夫長殿がああも慌てているのか、君、なにか心当たりがありますか」
source.english: “…By the way, have you any idea why the boatswain is so agitated?”

source.japanese: ……下級水夫も心得たもので、スコーンの最後の一口を呑み下すと、機関長へ再度の説明に取りかかる。……再度？　説明の度に出してくる、紅茶とスコーンにお行儀良く付き合う下級水夫君の腹具合からして、三回目という事すらありそうな。
source.english: The junior sailor knew the routine. Swallowing his last bite of scone, he began the explanation again. Again? Judging by how full he was after politely accepting the tea and scones served with every explanation, this might even have been the third time.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……Incidentally, whatever could have put the Bosun in a state of such flustered agitation? You there, do you have any idea?」

……The deck boy also understood perfectly well what was going on, and so, after washing down the final mouthful of scone, he set about explaining things to the Chief Engineer a second time. ……Second time? Based on the state of this deck boy's stomach, who always politely accepted the black tea and scone he was offered, it seemed very possible that this might even be the third.

source.japanese:
かくて、信天翁号に騒然とした気配が波及していった。二重の意味で。
　一つはもちろん海の水が酒になってしまったせいだが、もう一つは船が航行不能になっていたという事実。
　ややあって吹き始めた穏やかな風に薄い赤紫の霧が流され、濃赤の海面が露わになっていく様は、朝焼け夕暮れの空の奇観に匹敵する夢幻的な眺めではあったが、吹き流された後、露わになった海面に浮かんでいたものがある。
　葡萄だった。蔓付きの。しかも多量に。
　縺れ合い絡まり合い、波に寄せられ畝を為し、小さな丘の如く盛り上がっているところもある。
source.english:
Thus agitation spread through the Albatross, in two senses. One was, of course,
that the sea had become liquor. The other was that the ship could no longer sail.
Presently a gentle breeze began to carry off the thin purplish-red mist, revealing the deep red surface. It was a dreamlike spectacle to rival the marvels of a dawn or evening sky. But as the haze blew away, something appeared floating on the surface. Grapes.
Still on the vines. Vast quantities of them.
Entangled, interwoven, heaped by the waves into ridges, here and there rising like little hills.

source.japanese: 赤葡萄酒に葡萄を浮かべるとは、樺細工の盆に道明寺を重ねて飾る式の順当な取り合わせではあるが、そのただ中に取り囲まれた信天翁号にとっては一大災難、さながら多藻海の強靱な浮き藻の中に置かれたような危地で、一応スクリュー船ではあるがおんぼろの信天翁号、強引に浮遊物を突っ切っていったなら船が壊れる事も十分あり得る。
source.english: Grapes floating in red wine were as natural a pairing as domyoji rice cakes wrapped in cherry leaves and piled on a cherry-bark tray. For the Albatross, surrounded by them, it was a calamity: as though she had been trapped among the Sargasso Sea's tough floating weeds. She might technically be a screw steamer, but a wreck like this could easily break apart if forced through the floating mass.

source.japanese:
とはいえ、世界が終末を迎えるというその兆しに、川の水が苦蓬の毒汁に変じるというのはあっても、よもや世界の七つの海全てが葡萄酒に変じるというのはないだろう。この奇現象にも果てがある筈。とりあえずは低速で葡萄蔓を掻[か]き分けながら、可能な限り前進しようという事になったのだが、しかし───
　
　酒の海でもたもたなどしたりしたなら、信天翁号の中でなにが生ずるのか───気化した酒精だけでも酔いは回ってくるし、それでなくとても信天翁号の船員達は他の例に漏れず酒好きとくる。
source.english:
Among the signs of the world's end, rivers might turn to the poisonous juice of wormwood. Surely, however, all the seven seas would not become wine. This strange phenomenon must have an end. They decided to advance as far as possible, slowly parting the grapevines.
But—What would happen aboard the Albatross if they dawdled in a sea of liquor? The alcohol vapor alone was intoxicating. Besides, like sailors everywhere, the Albatross's crew loved a drink.

target.text: Thus, an uproarious atmosphere rippled through the Albatross. In two senses. The first was, of course, a result of the seawater turning into wine, but the other resulted from the reality that the ship had become unable to sail. A little while later, the gentle wind that had begun to blow carried away the pale purplish-red mist, and while the deep red surface of the sea being laid bare offered a phantasmagorical spectacle rivalling the wondrous sight of the glowing welkin at dawn or dusk, after the mist was blown away, something was emerging from the now-revealed surface of the sea.

It was grapes. With vines attached. And in flourishing abundance at that. They tangled together, wrapped around each other, and there were even places where, pressed together by the waves, they formed ridges, rising like little hills atop the sea.

While grapevines emerging from red wine was as proper a decorative pairing as doumyouji arranged in layers upon a kabazaiku tray, for the Albatross, encircled in the very heart of it, this was a calamity. (TN: Doumyouji, written "道明寺", is a type of Japanese sweet made from glutinous rice flour used in sakuramochi, traditionally eaten at cherry blossom viewings. Kabazaiku, written "樺細工", is a traditional Japanese craft using cherry bark, usually polished into trays, utensils, etc.)

They were in dire peril, like they'd been dropped right into the tough floating seaweed of the Sargasso Sea, and while she was a screw steamer, at least in name, if the ramshackle Albatross tried to forcibly cut across these floating things, then it was plenty plausible that she would break apart.

Be that as it may, even if it is said that the water of the rivers would turn to bitter and poisonous wormwood as a sign of the end times approaching, it is surely not said anywhere that the entirety of The Seven Seas of this world would turn into red wine. Surely there would be an end to this bizarre phenomenon. For now, they had decided to advance as far as possible while pushing through the grapevines at low speed, however───

Were they to dawdle around in a sea of wine, what would then happen aboard the Albatross───the vapourized alcohol alone was enough for intoxication to take hold, and even disregarding that, every crew member aboard the Albatross, without exception, had a love of drink.

source.japanese: たとえば、操舵室では。
source.english: In the wheelhouse, for example.

target.text: For example, in the wheelhouse:

source.japanese: ぱっ、とかたわれが顔を輝かせたのを目の当たりにしても、スキットルから匙に受けた赤いのを啜[すす]るキサラは、猿が木の股に溜めて発酵させるという木の実の汁を味見するような胡散臭げな顔つきであったが、匂いをかぎ一口嘗めて、シサムと同様に顔を明るくした。
source.english: Even after seeing her other half's face light up, Kisara wore a suspicious expression as she sipped a spoonful of red from the flask: as though sampling the fruit juice monkeys were said to ferment in tree forks. Then she smelled it, tasted a little, and brightened just as Sisam had.

target.text: Even though she had seen her other half's face light up in a flash before her eyes, when Kisara sipped the red stuff that had been poured from the skittle flask into the spoon, her face still showed a suspicion akin to that of a monkey tasting the juices of a fruit caught in a fork of a tree branch and left to ferment, but after sniffing the smell and tasting a mouthful, her face brightened just like Shisamu's.

source.japanese:
雲間から太陽が出でたような素敵な顔で、大きく煽った。スキットルではたちまち足らなくなって、バケツで汲[く]んできた。
　ワイングラスなどいう結構な品で味わう口ではない、馬鹿でかい陶製のジョッキに代わる代わる注ぎ合っているところにやってきて仰天したのは下級水夫である。
source.english:
Her lovely face was like the sun coming out from behind clouds. She took a long drink. The flask soon proved inadequate; they brought it up by the bucket.
No palates here for fine wineglasses. They were taking turns filling enormous ceramic tankards when a junior sailor arrived and stared in dismay.

target.text: With a lovely expression, like the sun was showing herself from behind the clouds, they knocked back large amounts. Drinking from a skittle flask quickly began to feel insufficient, and so they instead began to scoop it up by the bucketful. They weren't the sort to slowly savour things from something as elegant as a wine glass, and while they were taking turns pouring wine into a stupidly big ceramic stein, a deck boy arrived and was left dumbfounded at the sight.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あっ。一等航海士、駄目ですよ、
　勝手に呑んだりしたら。
　水夫長だっていけないって、
　みんなにお触れを」
source.english:
“Ah!
Mates, you can't drink it without permission!
The boatswain's sent an order to everyone,
saying not to!”

source.japanese: そのお触れを言触れに来たのだが遅かった、下級水夫君、慌てて双子のジョッキを取りあげようとしたのだけれど、
source.english: He had come to deliver that order, too late. Hastily, the junior sailor tried to take their tankards away.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Ah. Mates, you can't do that, no drinking without permission. Even the Bosun said it's forbidden, and that I had to make sure everyone hears it.」
He had come here to issue that announcement, but it was too late; though the young deck boy hurriedly tried to confiscate the twins' stein,

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「まあまあ、ちょびっとだけだって。
　こんなぷんぷん良い匂いしてるのに、
　我慢ばっかじゃかえって体に毒だ」
source.english:
“Now, now. Only a little.
With that lovely smell everywhere,
holding back too much would be worse for our health.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Now, now, it's just a little sip. With such a heady aroma in the air, abstinence would only be as poison to the body.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それに、しばらく雨も降ってなかったから、
　樽の水も臭くなってきてるし。
　そんなの呑んで腹下すのも、
　馬鹿馬鹿しいしね」
source.english:
“Besides, it hasn't rained for a while,
and the barrel water's beginning to smell.
Getting the runs from drinking
that would be stupid.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「On top of that, it hasn't rained for a good while now, so the water in the barrel has begun to stink. Drinking that and getting the trots, now that would just be ridiculous, wouldn't it?」

source.japanese:
にこやかに、しかし剛力で羽交い締めにされて下級水夫はそうだっけ？　と首を傾げて、真水樽のネルソン提督二世の様子を思い出す。
　まだ水の味も結構そうにのんびり浮かんでいたはずで───
source.english:
With a smile, one of the twins held the junior sailor in a full nelson of prodigious strength. Was it? he wondered. He recalled Admiral Nelson II in the fresh-water barrel.
The frog had still been floating contentedly, apparently quite satisfied with the water's flavor—

target.text: Though she was all smiles, the deck boy's arms were being held in a nelson with brute strength, and he tilted his head to ask "is that so?", recalling the state of Admiral Nelson the Second in the freshwater barrel. He was definitely floating around down there without a care, an indication that the taste of the water still seemed fine───

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「て、水みたいにそんなに、
　がばがば呑んだらっ」
source.english:
“But you can't gulp it
down like water!”

source.japanese: 抑えつけているキサラも、舵輪に就いている（あるいは就いたふりをしている）シサムも、大きく喉を鳴らしながらがぶがぶ飲み、水夫長も双子を止めさせるつもりなら、せめて下級水夫を一ダースは派遣するべきだったのだ。
source.english: Kisara, restraining him, and Sisam, at the wheel—or pretending to be—both drank in great noisy gulps. If the boatswain meant to stop the twins, he ought to have dispatched at least a dozen junior sailors.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Wait, if you just gulp that down like it's water, then!」

Kisara, who was restraining him, as well as Shisamu, who was at the helm (or perhaps she was just pretending to be), were both chugging down their drinks while loudly gulping, so if the Bosun had intended to put a stop to the twins, then he ought to have dispatched at least a dozen deck boys here.

source.japanese: あるいは、船下層部では。
source.english: Or on the lower decks.

target.text: Or perhaps, down in the ship's hold:

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あっ。密航者！　君、近頃見ないと思ったのに。
　やっぱり隠れてたなぁぁ……」
source.english:
“Ah! Stowaway! I thought we hadn't seen you lately.
You were hiding after all…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Ah. It's the stowaway! You, just when I though I hadn't seen you around recently. So you were hiding away down here after all……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「毎度毎度の事だから、いい加減判っているって思うけど。連れてくからね、水夫長のとこに。……いつまでもそんなところにへばりついてないで」
source.english: “This happens every time, so I assume you know the drill by now. I'm taking you to the boatswain. …Come away from there.”

source.japanese:
船底部の湾曲した肋[あばら]の曲線なりに身体を沿わせ、へばりついているは、疾走する馬の腹から滑り落ちまいとする這い虫の体の、なにやら必死の面持ちの密航者で。
　黒髪に艶、星雲のように煌めかせ、訴える風情だったが下級水夫君には彼女がなにを哀願しようと厳格に処するつもりだった、が。
source.english:
The stowaway clung along the curve of the hull's ribs, like a crawling insect desperate not to slip from the belly of a galloping horse. Her face was frantic.
Her glossy black hair glittered like a nebula as she seemed to plead. Whatever she begged, the junior sailor intended to deal with her strictly. But—

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「This happens every single time, so I think you should know better by now. I'm taking you with me, to the Bosun. ……Can you stop clinging to that rib already!」

Body pressed along the contour of the curved ribs of the ship's bottom, clinging to it, was the stowaway, her figure like a creeping insect desperately trying not to fall from the belly of a galloping horse, expression awfully desperate for some reason. Glossy black hair glittering like a nebula, she looked almost pleading, but no matter how she begged and entreated, the deck boy fully intended to deal with her strictly. However.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ま、待って。今はそれどころじゃない。
　穴空いてる。ここ、穴空いてるの。
　押さえてるんだってば、
　私、昨夜からずっと」
source.english:
“W-wait. This isn't the time.
There's a hole. A hole here.
I'm holding it shut.
I've been doing it all night.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「今手を離したら、浸水がどんどん広がってこの船が大変な事に！」
source.english: “If I let go now, the flooding will spread and the ship will be in terrible trouble!”

source.japanese:
千丈の堤[つつみ]も螻蟻の穴[けつ]を以[もっ]て潰[つい]ゆとかなんとやら。
　浸水と来たのには下級水夫君、些か面食らったけれど、相手は信天翁号の常連的密航者である、手強い。この彼はこれまでまだ一度しか密航者と遭遇した事はないが、その時の全く悪びれた様子なく、誰もが恐れる水夫長と平然とやりあっていたのを思い出し、哀訴してくるのも適当に流して引き剥がしにかかった。
source.english:
Even a towering embankment falls to an ant's hole, or some such saying.
The mention of flooding gave the junior sailor pause. But this was the Albatross's regular stowaway: a formidable opponent. He himself had met her only once before, but remembered her utter lack of shame, her composure when arguing with the boatswain everyone feared. He brushed aside her pleas and began to peel her off.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Wa-, wait. This isn't the time for any of that. There's a hole. Right here, a hole. I'm telling you, I've been covering it up since last night, without pause.」
【Stowaway】 「If I let go with my hand right now, then the flooding is going to spread fast, and the ship will be in huge trouble!」

Even the mightiest of embankments standing thousands of metres tall may collapse from a hole made by ants, or however that old saying goes. When she brought up flooding, the deck boy was a little taken aback, but he was dealing with the Albatross' habitual stowaway, a formidable foe. Hitherto, this lad had only encountered the stowaway but a single time, but he remembered how, back then, she showed not an ounce of shame, and she had calmly argued with the Bosun, a man feared by all, and so he brushed aside even her pleading and set about prying her off.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「はいはい、言い訳にしてももうちょっとマシなの考えようよ」
source.english: “Yes, yes. Think of a slightly better excuse, at least.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Yeah yeah, if you're going to make excuses, try to think up a slightly better one next time.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ほんとだとしても、君が押さえてられるような水漏れなんて大した事じゃない」
source.english: “Even if it's true, a leak you can hold shut can't be anything serious.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「And even should it be true, any leak that you can hold down can't be that big of a deal.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……ほんとうに？」
source.english: “…Really?”

source.japanese: 壁に体ごと掌を押しつけるにして、振り返る密航者の風情、陽差しの下よりも宵闇の刻に人知れず咲いて、朝にはまた閉じる花のような、儚い、物寂しい、優らしい、そんな白い肌と黒艶の髪の姿だった。
source.english: The stowaway turned, her palms and whole body pressed against the wall. With her white skin and glossy black hair, she seemed as fragile, lonely, and meek as a flower that bloomed unseen at dusk rather than in sunlight, only to close again by morning.

source.japanese: が、儚きも優[しお]らしきも信天翁号の鉄の規律には、豆の剥き殻を放りつけたほどにも堪[こた]えない、下級水夫は決然と頷[うなず]き、逃げようとしないだけは潔しと密航者の手を取る、並べばまだ娘の方が背が高い、けれど少年はたじろがず、
source.english: But neither fragility nor meekness made any more impression on the Albatross's iron discipline than a bean husk flung against it.
