source.english: “I came up with a way to drink like this—I guess I really am pretty smart after all. Hey, are you listening? All right, I’ll try it on you, too~”

source.japanese: とまあ、気絶している下級水夫の顎をぐいと反らして鼻孔に流しこみにかかるあたり、もう色々とお話にならない。
source.english: Then she tilted the unconscious junior sailor's chin sharply back and began pouring the wine into his nostrils. By now the whole business was beyond discussion.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Th-, this time it got in my nose……. Snn, snnrrk, it pricks, oooh, it really stings～」

【Stowaway】 「Ah. But this kind of hits my brain directly, feels good. Aah, this is a novel sensation. A new frontier. Onward, Prince Takaoka's Travels!」 (TN: "高岡親王航海記", known in English as Takaoka's Travels, is a Japanese novel by Shibusawa Tatsuhiko published in 1987, a fantastical travelogue based on the historical figure Prince Takaoka, who journeyed to India to seek Buddhist teachings after being unable to find a teacher in China and then vanished.)
【Stowaway】 「To come up with a way of drinking like this, I am really smart after all, aren't I? Hey, are you listening? Alright, I'll let you have a shot at it too～」
Anyway, given that she then took the unconscious deck boy's jaw and jerked it back, then poured wine into his nostrils, there was also no longer anything to be gained here, in many a sense.

source.japanese:
そして、乱痴気騒ぎとワインと来れば泪である。
　泪は船内の騒ぎにも超然として、自分の調子を崩さず船室に籠もりきり、あくまで優雅にかつ怠惰に、そして正気を保ったまま、下級水夫を愛おしげに、慈しみを充たして、柔和に唇に甘い息通わせ、それは大層な事可愛がっていた。
source.english:
And where there were wine and riotous revels, there was Rui.
Aloof from the uproar aboard, she had shut herself in her cabin without once losing her own rhythm. Elegant, indolent, perfectly sober, she lavished the junior sailor with tender affection, breathing sweetly from her lips to his and cherishing him with extraordinary care.

source.japanese: だがその慈しみ様は、愛玩動物を撫でさすりすぎてぐったりと疲れさせてしまう類のそれ、あるいは贅沢な餌を与えすぎて気分を悪くさせてしまう類のそれ。
source.english: But that sort of tenderness was the kind that leaves a pet limp with exhaustion from too much stroking, or makes it sick from too much rich food.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ごめんなさいごめんなさい。
　僕もう呑めません。お腹がぽこんぽこんいってるの。頭もくるくる回っているの……」
source.english:
“I’m sorry, I’m sorry.
I can’t drink anymore. My stomach’s making gurgling noises. My head’s spinning too…”

source.japanese:
ふぅらふぅらと、蛇遣いの笛の音[ね]に麻酔された子蛇のように、上体が揺れている。ゆるゆると、掻き回した珈琲に垂らした乳のように、頭も揺らいでいる。
　そんな下級水夫を腰を屈め気味に覗きこむ泪はどこまでも柔和な眼差しで、さらさらと産毛も柔い頬の感触を、楽しむように撫でながら、
source.english:
His upper body sways gently, like a young snake hypnotized by a snake charmer’s flute. His head sways slowly, too, like milk drizzled into stirred coffee.
Rui bends at the waist to look down at him, her expression soft. She strokes his smooth cheek and its soft down as if savoring the feel,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あら、そう。控え目なのね、貴方。
　ワインで舌が荒れたなら、
　こちらでお口をお濯[ゆす]ぎなさいな」
source.english:
“Oh, really? You’re quite the modest one, aren’t you?
If the wine has left your tongue feeling rough,
why don’t you rinse your mouth with this?”

source.japanese: 抱き寄せる、同じ年頃の女の子よりもややもすると繊細な下級水夫の肩がふかりと泪の乳房の中に埋まる。ことりと顎を上に傾かせ、桜桃を割ったような口に含ませる───
source.english: She drew him close. The junior sailor's shoulders, perhaps even more delicate than those of a woman his own age, sank softly into Rui's breasts. She tipped his chin up with a little touch and brought the glass to his split-cherry mouth—

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「有難うです……あ。これ、おいしい……。
　果物の香り……。すうっとする……。
　柑橘系……？　の、飲み物かな……」
source.english:
“Thank you… Oh. This is delicious…
It smells like fruit… It’s so refreshing…
Is it a citrus-based… drink…?”

source.japanese: 橙色の液体は、ショットグラスの内側をとろりと垂れ降って、濃密な旨味を秘めているようにこそ見えても、洗うような軽やかな舌触りを持ち合わせているとは考えられず、実際、
source.english: The orange liquid dripped thickly down the inside of the shot glass; even though it appeared to hold a rich, savory flavor, it was hard to imagine it having a light, refreshing mouthfeel—and in fact,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そうよ。マンダリンの匂いが素敵でしょう。
　ピストルっていうお名前の、ラム酒よ」
source.english:
“That’s right. The mandarin scent is lovely,
isn’t it? It’s a rum called ‘Pistol.’”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「ぷ、ぷはぁっ!?
　あ、後からキックがきたぁっ。
　ワインのチェーサーにラム酒なんて聞いたことないよぅ……っ」
source.english:
“P-phew!? Ah,
that kick hit me later.
I’ve never heard of rum as a chaser for wine…!”

source.japanese: 泪の腕の中で悶えたけれど、ばたつかせた手足も既にして酔いがさんざんに回って濃い粥を掻[か]き分けているかに頼りない。むしろ泪にはそれくらいの手足掻きは物足らないのではないか。
source.english: He squirmed in Rui’s arms, but he was already so thoroughly intoxicated that his flailing limbs were as feeble as if he were trying to push his way through thick porridge. In fact, perhaps such feeble struggles were not enough to satisfy Rui.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「なんか、もう、
　目もおかしくなってきて……。
　泪さんが……三人いるの。
　泪さんが三人もいたら、
　僕達なんてこの船全員、
　ぐにゃんぐにゃんにされちゃうよう……」
source.english:
“Somehow…
my eyes are playing tricks on me…
There are… three Ruis.
If there are three Ruis,
then all of us on this ship
are going to get all squishy and mushy…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そんなこと、いたしません。
　だって貴方達がいなくなってしまったら、
　ただでさえ退屈なお船の暮らしが、
　もっとつまらなくなってしまうもの」
source.english:
“I wouldn’t do that. If
you all disappeared,
life aboard this ship would get even more
boring than it already is.”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「それって僕らは泪さんのおもちゃって事だよね？　ねえそういう事だよね？」
source.english: “So that means we’re Ms. Rui’s toys, right? Hey, that’s what it means, isn’t it?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「貴方方みたいな可愛らしい男の子を、
　玩具……。
　それもいいわね、魅力的だこと。
　でも今は、ただお酒の相手、
　していただきたいだけ」
source.english:
“Sweet things like you as toys…
That has its charm. How tempting.
But for now, I only want you
to keep me company while I drink.”

source.japanese: ───かつてゾウアザラシと同じ名を持つ監督が撮った、とある古いモノクロのサアカスを題にした邦画があるのだが、劇中にヤクザの親分の囲い者、というか性欲の生贄にされている娘が登場する。親分はこの娘を『おもちゃ』『おもちゃ』と呼びつけ弄[もてあそ]び、以降もこの娘、劇中に名前が登場しない。そればかり終劇後のスタッフロールでも役名としてクレジットされていたのが『おもちゃ』。些かもやもやしたものを残した観客もいたのではないかと思われるが、泪が今舌に転がした『玩具』も仄昏い響きに鳴った。
source.english: There is an old Japanese black-and-white film about a circus, made by a director who shared his name with an elephant seal. A girl appears in it as the kept woman—or rather, the sexual sacrifice—of a yakuza boss. He calls her ‘toy,’ plays with his ‘toy,’ and nowhere in the film is she given a name. Even the closing credits list her role simply as ‘Toy.’ Some viewers may have left with a certain discomfort. The word Rui now rolled over her tongue had that same dim resonance.

target.text: And finally, where drunken revelry and wine is concerned, Rui cannot be ignored. Rui stood aloof from the commotion aboard the ship, keeping herself entirely cooped up within her cabin without changing her pace, elegant and indolent to the last; she had also kept her wits, and with tender affection, filled with compassion, her sweet breath landing softly over his lips, she doted upon the deck boy with great fondness.

But the shape of her affection was the sort where you pet a beloved animal so much it ends up limp from exhaustion, or perhaps the sort where the overly lavish feeding of luxurious food leaves it unwell.
【Deck boy】 「I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I can't drink any more. My stomach is gurgling. My head is spinning……」

Reeling like a neonate snake lulled by the notes from a snake charmer's flute, his upper body swayed. Slowly, like milk dripped into stirred coffee, his head also began to sway. How endlessly tender a gaze Rui beheld that deck boy with as she peered into him while stooped slightly forward, stroking him as if delighting in his silky peach fuzz and soft cheeks,
【Rui】 「Goodness, that so? You are a reserved one, dear. If the wine is too rough on your tongue, then rinse your mouth with this instead.」

She drew him closer, and the shoulders of the deck boy, which were more delicate than those of some girls his age, were buried deep inside Rui's bosom. His chin was gently tilted up, his lips like a split cherry as he was made to take it in his mouth.
【Deck boy】 「Thank you……ah. This is delicious……. A fruity aroma……. Refreshing……. Some kind of citrus……? In the drink, I guess……」

The orange liquid creamily oozed down the inside of the shot glass; it looked as if it concealed a dense, rich flavour, so it was hard to imagine that it could possess such a light, cleansing texture when meeting the tongue, but in reality,
【Rui】 「Correct. The scent of mandarin is wonderful, is it not? It is a rum, goes by the name "Pistol".
【Deck boy】 「P-, PWAAH!? Ah, the kick really hits you after. I've never ever heard of anyone having rum as a chaser after wine……」

He writhed and squirmed within Rui's arms, but the drink had already reached his flapping limbs in the meantime, making them as helpless as if he were trying to push through thick rice gruel. In fact, may Rui not have found this level of struggling wanting?
【Deck boy】 「It's already kind of like my eyes are acting funny……. There's……three Rui-sans. If there's three Rui-sans, then all of us, the whole crew, are gonna end up all floppy and limp……」
【Rui】 「I would never do such a thing. Why, if all of you dears were to disappear, life aboard this ship, already boring at the best of times, would end up even more unbearably dull.」
【Deck boy】 「Then that means we're just your toys, right, Rui-san? Hey, that's what that means, right?」
【Rui】 「To take boys as adorable as you dears and make playthings of them……. That has its charms, an attractive idea to be sure. But right now, all I want from you is to join me in drink.」

───Long ago, there was a certain old Japanese movie, one filmed in monochrome by a director who shared his name with the elephant seal, that was based on a circus theme, and during the movie, the mistress of a yakuza boss, or rather, a girl offered up as a sacrifice for his carnal desires, makes her appearance. (TN: This is a reference to the movie Nijisseiki Shounen Dokuhon, lit. "Twentieth Century Boys Manual", also known in English as Circus Boys, by director Hayashi Kaizou from 1989. The kanji in Hayashi Kaizou's given name, "海象", means elephant seal.)

The boss calls this woman "plaything", "plaything", toying and trifling with her, and henceforth, the girl's name would never appear for the rest of the movie's runtime. And that was not all, even during the credits at the end of the movie, she is credited only as 『plaything』. While it seemed some members of the audience were left a little unsettled by this, as the word "plaything" rolled of Rui's tongue now, it, too, held some gloomy undertones.

source.japanese: 下級水夫の言葉に何事を思いついたのか、泪が頬にあえかに刷いた笑みは、長い退屈に倦んでいた少女の、お人形遊びに誘われたような。もちろんそのお人形というのはちゃんと血肉具[そな]えて、いじれば声を出す他のモノも出すような、だが。
source.english: Something in the junior sailor's words had inspired Rui. A faint smile brushed her cheeks, like that of a woman wearied by long boredom who had just been invited to play with dolls. These dolls, of course, possessed proper flesh and blood, and when handled would produce voices—and other things besides.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ラムがお口に合わないなら、
　こちらはいかが」
source.english:
“If the rum’s not to your taste,
how about this instead?”

source.japanese: と下級水夫の口元に運んだのは、程良く実った大粒の葡萄の一粒。瑞々しさが航海の最中には得難い果実の、たしかに今現在船の周囲には幾らでも浮いているのだが、あちらは濃紫の種なのに対して、泪が今差し出したのは薄緑も爽やかな色合いのそれで、今しがた摘[つ]んできたように皮も張り詰めているが、なぜそんな新鮮な果実がこの船にあるのやら。
source.english: What Rui lifted to the junior sailor’s lips was a single, large, perfectly ripe grape. It was a fruit whose juiciness is hard to come by during a voyage—and while there were certainly plenty of them floating all around the ship right now, those were a dark purple variety, whereas the one Rui had just offered was a refreshing light green. Its skin was taut, as if it had just been picked, but why on earth was such a fresh fruit on this ship?

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あ、ブドウ。それなら食べます。
　いただきます」
source.english:
“Oh, grapes.
I’ll have some of those. I’ll dig in.”

target.text: Perhaps she was struck with an idea upon hearing the deck boy's words, for the smile faintly smeared across Rui's cheeks was like that of a little girl, one fed up with a long period of ennui, being invited to play with dollies. Of course, this doll, as it were, was endowed with real flesh and blood, and it was the sort of thing that would let out noises when fiddled with, however.
【Rui】 「If the rum should not suit your palate, then how about this?」

What she brought to the deck boy's mouth was a single large grape, ripened to perfection. Fruits were challenging to keep fresh during a voyage, but certainly, countless of them were floating around outside the ship at present; however, compared to the deep purple sort out there, what Rui was currently presenting was an invigorating colouration of light green, and in addition, its skin was so taut, it was as though it had just been plucked from the vine; it made one wonder how in the world such fresh fruit could be found aboard this ship.
【Deck boy】 「Ah, a grape. I'll eat that. Thanks.」

source.japanese: 弟を溺愛する姉がやるように、手ずから唇の中に差し入れてくるのを、今更気恥ずかしいとも思えないくらいこの下級水夫君は既に色々されてしまっている。素直に口を開いて、つるりと呑みこんで、けれど去り際唇をなぞっていった長手袋の指先には、背筋を撫で下ろされたような感触を残した。
source.english: Like an adoring older sister, she slipped it between his lips with her own hand. By then so many things had already been done to this junior sailor that bashfulness was beyond him. He obediently opened his mouth and let the grape slide in—but as she withdrew, the tip of one long-gloved finger traced his lips, leaving him with the sensation of a stroke run down his spine.

source.japanese: くすぐったさにもぞもぞ、しながら噛んだ果肉は素敵に甘く、程良く酸っぱく、それだけではない。舌を少し刺すような、じんわり広がるような、えも言われぬ風味を残した。
source.english: Wriggling with ticklishness, he bit into the fruit—the flesh was wonderfully sweet, with just the right amount of tartness, but that wasn’t all. It left an indescribable flavor that pricked his tongue slightly and spread gently throughout his mouth.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あれ……なにかこれ、不思議な味が……」
source.english: “Huh… this tastes kind of strange…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「良い舌をしていらっしゃるのね、貴方。
　よくお判りだこと。
　その葡萄にはね……」
source.english:
“You have a remarkably fine palate.
You understand it very well.
Now, that grape…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「『アルカゴーク・クラースヌイ』がお注射してあるの」
source.english: “It’s been injected with ‘Arkagork Krasnoy.’ ”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「うわああん、またなんか仕込んであるぅ。
　アルカゴ……ええとそれって、
『赤いお酒』って意味……。
　やっぱりお酒だぁ」
source.english:
“Waaah, there’s something hidden in there again.
Alkago… um, does that mean,
‘red liquor’…?
It really is liquor after all.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「よくご存じだこと。あなた、とっても賢いわ。そうよ。これはね、苔桃を醸して造ったお酒を、さらに紅天狗茸で色付けしてあるの」
source.english: “How very knowledgeable. Aren't you clever. Yes—this is liquor brewed from lingonberries and colored with fly agaric.”

source.japanese: ころころと、泪が無邪気に笑えばその無邪気という言葉に潜[ひそ]む、別の側面の怖さが引き立つ。取り出してみせる酒、手品の種明かし、けれどその手品というのは街から街を経巡って人に狂気をもたらす道化師が得意とするものだろうの、ラベルもない瓶の中に揺れている赤は船の外一面に満つる葡萄酒の赤より、妖しい。
source.english: Rui’s lilting, innocent laughter brought out the sinister side of the very word “innocent.” She pulled out a bottle of liquor and revealed the secret behind her magic trick—though such tricks are surely the specialty of a clown who travels from town to town, spreading madness among the people. The red liquid swaying inside the unlabeled bottle was more eerie than the red of the wine that filled the space outside the ship.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「……ってそれ毒キノコじゃないかぁーっ。
　うう、僕はもう駄目だ。泪さんのおふざけで毒を盛られて死んじゃうんだ」
source.english:
“…Wait, that’s a poison mushroom?!
Ugh, I’m done for. I’m going to die from being poisoned by Ms. Rui’s prank.”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「そういえばこのブドウ、みんなも食べてたけど、だからみんなしてぶっ倒れてる……。
　ただお酒で潰れたんだって思ってたけど。
　……ひどい」
source.english:
“Come to think of it, everyone was eating these grapes too—that’s why they’re all passed out…
I just thought they’d passed out from drinking.
…That’s awful.”

source.japanese: 見れば泪の船室には下級水夫達が正体なくして死屍累々、みなそれぞれに哀れなありさまでぶち転がっているという無惨図の。
source.english: Inside Rui’s cabin, junior sailors lay senseless, scattered like so many corpses, each sprawled in a pitiful state—a wretched sight.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「まさか。そんな事仰有ったらいけません。
　死んでしまっては、それでお終いですもの。
　気持ちいいことも、苦しいことも、
　生きていてこそ味わえる果実」
source.english:
“Don’t say that. If you died,
that would be the end. Pleasure,
pain—they’re fruits you can taste only
while you’re alive.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「だからわたくしは、誰にも死んでほしくないのよ、ほんとうに」
source.english: “That’s why I don’t want anyone to die—truly.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「その赤いお酒だって、
　たくさん飲みすぎなければ、
　体を元気に、心を素敵にしてくれます」
source.english:
“Even that red wine,
provided you do not drink too much,
will restore the body and brighten the heart.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ほら……利いてきたんじゃなくって？」
source.english: “See… isn’t it starting to work?”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「いわれて……見ると……苦しくはないけど。
　ううん……さっきまで気持ち悪かったのが、
　だんだんと、ほわほわしてきて……」
source.english:
“Now that you say it… I’m not… uncomfortable.
Mmm… I felt sick just now,
but I’m slowly starting to feel all floaty…”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「泪さんが……すごく綺麗に見える。
　違う、前から泪さんは綺麗だけど、
　そうじゃなくって、なんかこう……」
source.english:
“Ms. Rui… looks so beautiful. No, wait—
Ms. Rui has always been beautiful,
but that isn't what I mean. It's just… somehow…”

source.japanese: 彼にはそれまで意識されていなかったのだが、泪がひどく肉感的に、いやもっと直接に淫らに感じられてきていた。
source.english: Until that moment he hadn’t noticed, but Rui was beginning to seem incredibly sensual—no, lewd.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あれ……変だ僕、今までそんなコト、気にならなかったのに……」
source.english: “Huh… that’s weird. I’ve never really cared about stuff like that before…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ふふっ……どこを見ていらっしゃるの」
source.english: “Heh… what are you looking at?”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「違……っ、僕なんにも、
　見てない、見てませんっ」
source.english:
“No… wait, I’m not… looking at anything,
I’m not looking at a thing!”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───いいのよ。
　貴方のご覧になりたいように。
　なにもいけない事なんて、ないんだから」
source.english:
“───It’s fine.
Look however you like.
There’s nothing wrong with it at all.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしの体───見たいのでしょう？
　どこが気になるのかしら？
　───おっぱい？」
source.english:
“You want to see my body, don’t you?
I wonder which part interests you?
—My breasts?”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「そんな───」
source.english: “No way—”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それとも、お尻───？」
source.english: “Or maybe… my butt—?”

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「僕……見てない……。
　そんな、いやらしい……っ」
source.english:
“I…
didn’t see that… That’s so… lewd…”

source.japanese:
秘やかに、そして媚びをたっぷり含ませ囁[ささや]く、一つ一つの言葉の間に、ドレスを裡から押し上げる肉の果実を誇示しながら。

target.text: Tomosato sunk his fist into the nearby Bosun's stomach, silencing the snores gushing forth from him once more. A blow of that level apparently barely fazed the Bosun at all.
【Naomasa】 「And Rui-san……I didn't actually bother looking, but I can pretty much guess how that's going.」

【Naomasa】 「Making the boy sailors keep her company, making them drink booze spiked with aphrodisiac or something, drinking alone while feasting on their writhing in agony as a snack. The aphrodisiac is, in all likelihood, much too intense, and so the deck boys are probably all dead to the world.」

What profoundly discerning eyes he had, for Sakuya's prediction was spot on. This power of thought, unthinkable for his usual self, was brought about by Sakuya having a depressive episode. Last night, something unexpected had become the trigger, and he had once more fallen into a period of depression.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「お前にしちゃあえらい天眼通だな……。
　そうかてめえ、その賢しげなべしゃりといい、まぁた鬱になってやがるな？」
source.english:
“That's some clairvoyance, for you…
I see now. All that smart-sounding chatter—you're depressed again, aren't you?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうみたいだ……だから、みんなのように酒を呑む気にもなれない」
source.english: “Seems so… That's why I don't feel like drinking with everyone else.”

source.japanese:
なんとまぁ。
　しかし考えてみればこの船内の痴態狂態、平素の朔屋なら先頭切って参加していたことだろう。瓶詰めされた葡萄酒ちょろまかすのが早いか、密航者が必死に塞ぐ手はねのけ溢れる酒を浴びるのが早いか、いや、短艇降ろす手間も嫌って、赤く染まった海に飛び込むやもしれぬ。そうした朔屋が真っ先に酔っぱらって痴態晒し、そのひどさに一同醒め退いてもらった方が、むしろ事態の悪化は防げたかも知れぬ。
source.english:
Well, well.
Come to think of it, confronted with the ship’s present orgy of idiocy and depravity, the Sakuya of ordinary days would surely have charged in at the head of the pack. Would he have gone first for the bottled wine and filched it, or knocked away the stowaway’s hands as she desperately tried to plug the leak and bathed in the wine pouring through? No—he might have found even lowering a boat too much trouble and simply plunged into the wine-reddened sea. Perhaps matters would actually have gone no further if Sakuya had disgraced himself first and worst, appalling everyone else into sobriety and retreat.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「That's some impressive clairvoyance for someone like you……. So that's it. Buddy, with the clever way you're talking, did you get depressed again?」
【Naomasa】 「Seems like it……and that's why I just can't even bring myself to drink like the rest.」

Oh my goodness. But thinking about it, with all the disgraceful tomfoolery aboard the ship now, had this been the ordinary Sakuya, then he would surely have been leading the charge. Would he first have pilfered the bottled wine, would he first have bathed in the wine overflowing from the hole where the stowaway's desperately blocking hand had been pushed aside, nay, he might have found the effort of lowering a boat too tiresome, instead simply hurling himself headfirst into the sea dyed crimson.

Once he had done so, Sakuya would immediately get drunk and put on a humiliating display, and the awfulness of it would have all present sober up and withdraw, so if anything, the worsening of the situation might have been averted.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ああ呑むな呑むな。今のお前が酒なんぞ入れようものなら、漠然とした不安に取り憑かれて閃輝暗点、カルモチンをたらふく食らって玉川用水に入水と、こう遣りかねねえ」
source.english: “Yeah, don't drink, don't drink. If you start putting booze away in this state, I can see you getting possessed by vague unease, seeing shimmering blind spots, stuffing yourself with Calmotin, and drowning yourself in the Tamagawa Canal.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……だからさっきから、一体なんの話なのかそれは」
source.english: “…Again, what on earth are you talking about?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Aaah, no drinking, no drinking. If you were to get any drink in your system with the way you're behaving right now, you might well end up being possessed by a vague anxiety, struck with scintillating scotoma, stuffing yourself with Calmotin, then drowning yourself in the Tamagawa Aqueduct.」

(TN: This is a reference to Akutagawa Ryuunosuke and Dazai Osamu, famous Japanese authors. Akutagawa suffered from scintillating scotoma, a condition which causes strong anxiety, and committed suicide at age 35 by overdosing on barbital. Dazai Osamu tried to commit suicide by overdosing on Calmotin, a sedative. Several unsuccessful suicide attempts later, he finally succeeded the fifth time by jumping into the Tamagawa Aqueduct.)
【Naomasa】 「……Seriously, what the hell have you been talking about for the last good while now?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「気にするなって。こっちの話だ。
　まあ怪我の功名たぁこいつよ。
　今のお前は胃痛持ちの芋虫みてぇに鬱陶しいが、酔っ払ってないだけいくらかましだな」
source.english:
“Never mind. Just talking.
Anyway, a blessing in disguise.
You're as tiresome as a caterpillar with a stomachache, but at least you're not drunk.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ひどい言われようだな。鬱病持ちへの配慮というものがまるで足りていない。
　だが、君だって酔っ払ってないじゃないか」
source.english:
“What a horrible thing to say. You show absolutely no consideration for someone with depression.
But you aren't drunk either.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「I said don't worry about it. Just talking to myself. Well, this is a happy little accident. You might be as depressing as a caterpillar with a stomach ache right now, but you're still better just by virtue of not being drunk.」
【Naomasa】 「What a cruel thing to say. It's like you have no consideration at all for the man suffering from depression here. But it's not like you're drunk either, are you?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「莫迦だな直の字。このドぐされ船で酒てぇのは、見張りの目ぇ掠めて盗み呑むのが楽しいんだろ。
　こんないかにも呑んでちょうだいなと、海一杯にされたところでよ、有り難みちうもんに欠けるわな。そんなん一口二口で飽きるさね」
source.english:
“Idiot, Nao. On this rotten ship, the fun of a drink is sneaking it past the watch.
Fill the sea with the stuff, all ‘please drink me,’ and there's nothing to appreciate. One or two mouthfuls and I'm bored.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「欠けているのは酒の有り難み云々ではなく、君の論理性の方だろう……」
source.english: “What's lacking isn't appreciation of the liquor. It's logic on your part…”

source.japanese: そうぼやいて頭を抱えた様子がなんとも沈鬱だったが、その様はあまりに真に迫り、ただ鬱や智里の妄言のせいだけとは思われなかった。
source.english: He grumbled and held his head, looking profoundly gloomy. Yet the distress was so convincing that it seemed more than depression or Tomosato's nonsense alone could account for.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「とにかく……こんな野放図な、麻薬中毒者の幻覚じみた現状は……もしかして、僕のせいなのか？　ならどうにかしないと……」
source.english: “Anyway… This unrestrained state, like a drug addict's hallucination… Could it be my fault? If so, I have to do something…”

source.japanese:
朔屋青年は───
　自分が余計なことを願ったからこうなったのではないか、という罪悪感を抱えこんでいたのである。もしそれが真実なら、この現状をどうにかしないとと考えていたのである。
　だから、船内でどうにか残ったまともな頭の智里を食堂に連れこんで、相談していたのだった。
source.english:
Sakuya—
had taken upon himself the guilt of wondering whether his idle wish had caused the whole affair. If that were true, he believed he had to set matters right.
That was why he had brought Tomosato, somehow the only other sound mind left aboard, into the mess to ask his advice.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「What a silly thing to say, big Nao. On this rotten ship, the only fun in drinking comes from stealing it from right under the noses of those standing watch. When you're given a whole ocean of the stuff, practically being told to drink up and have all you want, it just lacks any sense of worth. I get fed up with that kind of swill after one or two mouthfuls, y'know?」
【Naomasa】 「Pretty sure it's your sense of logic that's lacking here, not the worth of the drink or whatever……」
The way he grumbled and held his head in his hands was awfully gloomy, and yet it seemed all too convincingly real, not merely a consequence of his depression or Tomosato's nonsense.

【Naomasa】 「Anyways……this unruly state of affairs we find ourselves in, almost like the hallucinations of a drug addict……maybe, just maybe, it might be my fault? In that case, I'll have to do something……」

The young man Sakuya was─── Saddled with a feeling of guilt, wondering if this could not all have been wrought from that needless wish he had uttered. If that really were true, he was thinking that he would have to be the one to do something about it. Therefore, he had taken Tomosato, whose head was somehow still straight on his shoulders, and dragged him to the mess room, consulting with him.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そういや水夫どもが、なんだか海の底から声が聞こえてきたとか抜かしてたな」
source.english: “Come to think of it, the sailors said they heard some voice coming from the bottom of the sea.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Oh yeah, now that you mention it, the deck boys did say something about hearing a voice coming from the bottom of the ocean.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おめえ、やっぱこりゃ、お前がろくでもないことほざいたのが悪いんでないの？」
source.english: “Maybe it is your fault, saying something that damned stupid?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やっぱり、僕の、せい……？」
source.english: “Then it really is… my fault…?”

source.japanese: この惨状、やはり己の軽率が引き起こした結果であったのかと朔屋、後悔罪悪感いや増して、顔を上げるもその目は鬱気に重く澱[よど]んでいる。
source.english: So this calamity had indeed been the fruit of his own rashness? Sakuya’s remorse and guilt mounted higher still. He raised his head, but his eyes lay heavy and stagnant beneath the pall of depression.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Buddy, in the end, isn't this all your fault for running your mouth and saying that nonsense?」
【Naomasa】 「So it really is my fault……?」

Thinking that this disastrous spectacle really was a result wrought by his own imprudence, Sakuya's feelings of regret and guilt only grew stronger and stronger, and when he raised his head, the look in his eyes was hazy with clouds of heavy gloom.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ああ。ちょっと潜[もぐ]って確かめてこいよ」
source.english: “Yeah. Dive down and check.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんな……事、言われても。
　この船には、まともな潜水道具なんて……」
source.english:
“Easy… to say.
This ship doesn't have any proper diving equipment…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Yeah. Go for a little dive and check it out.」
【Naomasa】 「Say that……all you want, but. There's no proper diving equipment anywhere on this ship……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「それなんだがよ」
source.english: “About that.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おめえ、泪の部屋にゃあまだ行ってねえと言ったな？」
source.english: “You said you haven't been to Rui's room yet?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ。この状況では近寄りたくないんだ」
source.english: “That's right. I don't want to go near it under these circumstances.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Yeah, about that.」
【Tomosato】 「You said you never went all the way to Rui's room, right?」
【Naomasa】 「Yeah. Don't wanna go anywhere near that place in this situation.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そうも言ってらんねえやな。
　いいか。あの女のな、宝石の中には、
　きっと真珠がある」
source.english:
“Can't afford that. Listen.
Among that woman's jewels,
there'll be pearls.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それは泪さんなら、真珠の一つや二つは蔵しているだろうよ。でもこの船に持ちこんでいるかどうか判らないぞ」
source.english: “I'm sure Ms. Rui owns a pearl or two. But we don't know whether she's brought them aboard.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「That's not gonna fly here. You listening? Somewhere in that woman's collection of stones, there's got to be a pearl.」
【Naomasa】 「If it's Rui-san we're talking about, I'm sure she's got a pearl or two somewhere. Can't say for sure if she's brought them with her aboard this ship though.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あるんだよ、間違いなくな。
　そんで、その一つや二つをさ、
　今からちょいと忍びこんできて、
　さくっと掠め取ってこいや」
source.english:
“She has. No doubt about it.
So go slip
in there now
and pinch one or two.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんで、僕が」
source.english: “Why me?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「She has, no doubt about it. And so, you go there right now, sneak in, swipe them real quick, just one or two of them, then come back here.」
【Naomasa】 「But why me?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おい直の字よう。
『自分のせいなら、どうにかしないと』
　と抜かした舌の根もまだ乾かぬうちだぜ？」
source.english:
“Nao.
‘If it's my fault,
I have to do something’—those words are barely out of your mouth!”

source.japanese: 智里が唆したのは、泪の持ち物から真珠を手に入れてこいとの、盗人仕事で───
source.english: What Tomosato urged him to do was a thief's errand: steal pearls from Rui's belongings—

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Oi, big Nao, buddy. 『If it's my fault, I'll have to do something about it.』 I don't think those words have even had time to leave your mouth yet?」
Procuring pearls from Rui's belongings, the work of a thief: that is what Tomosato was inciting him to do───

source.japanese: 御用聞きの小僧が勝手口から表へ抜ける小暗い廂間の、軒下の奥から酔いどれ達の放吟を聞くように、怖々と肩をすぼめていくのが今の朔屋である。船内のあちこち遠くではまだまだ大小の酔っぱらい達がそれぞれにそれぞれの放埒を、大道芸のようにぶちまけ続けてあり、捕まらないように脚を忍ばせつつ、泪の船室へ。
source.english: Sakuya crept with his shoulders drawn fearfully in, like an errand boy passing through a dim gap between houses from the back door to the street, hearing drunken singing deep beneath the eaves. Around the ship, distant drunkards great and small still flaunted their respective excesses like street performers. Keeping his steps quiet so none would catch him, he made for Rui's cabin.

source.japanese:
しかしまた、泪だ。
　先だっての魚怪騒ぎは渦の核、結局どこにあるのか定まらないまま流れていって沙汰止みに、ただ泪が深い繋がりがあったのは間違いないだろう。
　そして今回の騒ぎに関しても、なのか？　今のところ今回の騒ぎ、始まりが百歩譲って朔屋自身に帰する処のものだと認めるとして、泪が何かをやらかしたようにはみえないのだけれど。
source.english:
Rui again.
The recent fish-monster affair had drifted away without anyone establishing where its vortex began, and come to nothing.
But she had certainly been deeply involved. Was that true of this affair too? Even conceding, for argument's sake, that Sakuya himself had set it off, there was no sign so far that Rui had done anything.

source.japanese: とはいえあの殺し屋の言葉には、説得力は欠けるが実績はある、と朔屋は智里の物言いを思う。
source.english: Still, Sakuya thought of Tomosato’s pronouncement: whatever that assassin’s words lacked in persuasiveness, they made up for in their record of being right.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（なんだって彼の言う事は、
　ああなのだろう）
source.english:
(Why must everything he says
be like that?)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（普段の会話なら、まあ問題ないのだけれど、話が何かに噛みこむとなると、途端に意味が取りづらくなる）
source.english: (Ordinary conversation is fine. But once the talk gets its teeth into something, he suddenly becomes hard to understand.)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（しかも後々考えてみると、それが正解なのだから手に負えない……式を抜いて答えを寄越されているような）
source.english: (And later, when I think it through, he's right. Impossible to deal with… Like being given the answer without the calculations.)

source.japanese:
……確かに、確かにだ。
　天変地異、奇跡といって、たとえば今の信天翁号の状況のように、周囲の水が酒に変わるというのはいかにもわかりやすい例だろう。
　しかし、より隠微な顕れではあるが深刻の度合いとしては優るとも劣らぬものが他にもある。
source.english:
Certainly. Certainly.
Upheavals of nature, miracles: water becoming liquor all around them, as now happened to the Albatross, was an easily understood example.
But there were subtler manifestations, no less grave.
Behold—

source.japanese:
【直正】
（変な奴だよなあ。大体あいつ、何時もどこに刀隠している。気がつくと担いでいるが）
source.english: (Strange man. Where does he always hide that sword, anyway? Next thing you know, he's carrying it.)

source.japanese: ───鬱々と、朔屋がずっと『男』の事を考え続けている。
source.english: Gloomily, Sakuya had been thinking about a man all this time.

source.japanese: 気の弱い下級水夫君辺りなら、この一時を知っただけでしくしく泣き出すだろう。そのうちへらへら笑い出すかも知れない。そして鈴をば一つだけ携えて、自ら『船長の箱』に入り籠もって出てこなくなるだろう。鈴の音[ね]が途絶えたらそれが『その時』で、外蓋をこじ開けると中から出てくるのは新品の船長クロだ───
source.english: A timid junior sailor might begin to sob merely upon learning of this moment. In time he might start giggling instead. Then, taking only a single bell, he would shut himself inside the ‘Captain's Box’ and never emerge. When the bell fell silent, that would be ‘the moment.’ Pry open the lid, and out would come a brand-new Captain Kuro—

source.japanese:
このようにして信天翁号の船長というのはひっそり代替わりを重ねていくのである。
　……などというような事が本当にあったなら、下級水夫君と船長クロの生態を解剖しに、博物学者の集団が大挙して押し寄せて、船は今頃過重に沈没しているだろう。
source.english:
Thus the Albatross's captains would quietly succeed one another.
Had anything of that sort really happened, however, hordes of naturalists would have descended to dissect the junior sailors' and Kuro's peculiar lives. By now their weight would have sunk the ship.

source.japanese: ただ、朔屋は下級水夫の、しくしくと啜[すす]り泣くような、えへらへらと笑っているような、そして船長クロの緩んだような音質が混ざった声を泪の船室から伝え聞いて、はっと扉の影に身を潜[ひそ]めた事である。
source.english: However, Sakuya heard a junior sailor’s voice from Rui’s cabin—part soft sobbing, part giggling, with something of Captain Kuro’s slack tone—and he suddenly ducked behind the door.

target.text: Like a shop boy hearing the boisterous singing of drunkards from deep under the eaves of the alley leading from the kitchen door to the street, right now, Sakuya was timidly drawing his shoulders in. From distant places all over the ship, drunkards of every sort, each profligate in their own fashion, let their reckless abandon endlessly spill forth like a street performance, and while stealing forwards with furtive steps in an effort to not get caught, he headed for Rui's cabin.

But then again, this was Rui. Just the other day, he had been unable to determine the true heart of the turmoil with the fish monsters, it simply drifted away until it was dropped, but there seemed to be no doubt about the fact that Rui was deeply connected to them, at least. And to the uproar this time as well, perhaps? Even if, for the sake of argument, he admitted that the blame for the beginnings of this current uproar fell on Sakuya's own shoulders for now, and it might not look as though Rui had done anything wrong in particular, still.
With that said, while the words of that murderer weren't exactly persuasive, they still had a track record of being correct, Sakuya thought, reflecting on Tomosato's manner of speech.
【Naomasa】 （Really though, why must everything he says always be like that?）
【Naomasa】 （When we're having a normal conversation, well, it's not really a problem, but as soon as he starts digging deeper into something, it becomes very hard to follow.）
【Naomasa】 （What's more, when I try thinking it over later, he's always right, so what can I even do about it…… it's like being given a solution without the equation.）

……Certainly, that was indeed so. In terms of cataclysms and miracles, the present state of the Albatross, the sea around it turned into wine, was as clear an example as one could ask for. However, there were other more subtly abstruse manifestations of those that, in terms of gravity, rivalled or perhaps even surpassed it.
───Lo and behold───
【Naomasa】 （He really is a weird guy. To begin with, where does he always hide that blade of his? One moment it's nowhere to be seen, and the next he's carrying it over his shoulder.）
───Mood gloomy, Sakuya had a『man』on his mind the whole time.

A deck boy faint of heart would, merely upon learning of this situation, surely dissolve into soft weeping. And soon enough, he might burst into giddy laughter. Then, carrying but a single bell in his hand, he would probably shut himself in the 『Captain's Box』and refuse to leave. Once the sound of the bell had ceased, it would signify that『The Time』 had come, and when the outer lid was pried open, it would be a brand new Captain Kuro who emerged from within───

Thus, what was known as the Captain of the Albatross would inconspicuously be substituted, over and over again. ……If something of the sort were to be true, then groups of natural historians would descend upon the ship in droves with the purpose of conducting a detailed analysis of the ecology of the deck boys and Captain Kuro, and by now, the ship would surely have foundered from the excessive load.

However, Sakuya did hear a voice coming from Rui's cabin; one that seemed a mix of weeping, of foolish laughter, and of Captain Kuro's slack tone of voice, and with a start, he hid himself behind the door.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あ……う……もう、僕、ないよ……」
source.english: “Ah… uh… I… I don’t have any left…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Ah……uh……I can't anymore……」

source.japanese:
……なにやら聞いているだけで心が痛くなってくるような、弄ばれて悶える声を、しかし朔屋は鍵穴を耳で覗くように聞いたのではない。
　泪の部屋の扉[と]、誘っているつもりか、ただの風通しか、聞かれようと聞かれまいと構わないのか、そのいずれであろうか、とにかく細く開いていた。
source.english:
…It was that kind of sound—the kind that made his heart ache just to hear it—someone being toyed with and writhing; yet Sakuya did not listen as if peering through a keyhole.
The door to Rui’s room was ajar—whether by invitation, simply to let the air in, or because it didn’t matter whether anyone heard or not—whatever the reason, it was open just a crack.

source.japanese: 僅かな隙間からでも匂うてくるような濃密な艶事の気配、泪のなにやら下級水夫君を引きずりこんでお遊びの。お取り込み中のご様子、時を改めて後日と、こういう状況を既に予言しているのに今更逃げ腰な。
source.english: The atmosphere of lovemaking was so dense it seemed to seep through even that narrow crack: Rui had evidently dragged the junior sailor in for some sport. Clearly she was occupied. source.english: “But… Isn't fresh water precious under these circumstances?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Just have a drink. Don't panic, it's freshwater.」
【Naomasa】 「But……in our current situation, isn't freshwater really precious?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そういう話もないでもねえが、てめえの有り様見てるとよ」
source.english: “There's that, sure. But looking at you—”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「It's not like what you're saying isn't true, but just have a look at the state you're in, man.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「どうやらあの姐さんにさんざか搾[しぼ]りとられてきたらしいや。かっさかさだぁ。水気を入れとけ少しは」
source.english: “Seems that lady's wrung you dry. Parched as hell. Get some water in you, at least.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「It looks like you've had every last drop wrung out of you by that lady. You're bone-dry. Get some moisture in you, at least a little.」

source.japanese:
まるで泪の部屋での痴態一部始終を見透かされた覚えして、朔屋、差し出された水筒手に取り、蓋を外して口に運ぶ。喉を通る水は確かに若干饐[す]えた感じはしたものの、智里の推察通り、あの部屋での濃密な空気に晒された体は確かに水分欲しており、体中にしみ込んでいくよう。
　入っていた水の半分ばかりを流し込んで、ようやく朔屋、飲み口を離す。
source.english:
Feeling as though every indecency in Rui's room had been seen through, Sakuya took the offered canteen, removed the cap, and raised it to his mouth. The water did taste a little stale. But as Tomosato had guessed, his body, exposed to that room's thick atmosphere, craved moisture. It seemed to soak through him.
Only after drinking about half the contents did he lower the canteen.

target.text: Sakuya, feeling as though the whole debauched affair that took place in Rui's room had been seen through from start to finish, took the canteen that was offered, removed the lid, then raised it to his mouth. Though the water running down his throat certainly was somewhat spoiled, it was just as Tomosato had surmised; after having been exposed to the dense, saturated air of that room, his body did certainly desire moisture, and it was as though it soaked into his body. After pouring half the water within it down his throat, Sakuya finally removed his lips from the canteen.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……っ。その……なんというか、
　なりゆきで」
source.english:
“…Well… What can I say?
One thing led to another.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Hm. Well……how do I put it, it's just how things turned out.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「お前がどこで女を食おうが女郎を買おうが、そんなこたぁどうでもいいんだよ。
　だがよ───飲んだら、口、拭え」
source.english:
“I don't care where you bed women or buy whores.
But—wipe your mouth when you've finished drinking.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「You can go get laid or buy as many prostitutes as you want, wherever you want, that shit's no skin off my nose. But───now that you're done drinking, wipe your damn mouth.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「紅は魔除けになるたぁ言うが、そこまで口の回りべっとりさせてちゃあ、エロ気が利きすぎだぁ。こっちまで脂くさくなりそうだぜ。
　話をすんにも、その後にしようや、な？」
source.english:
“They say rouge wards off evil, but all that smeared around your mouth is laying the lewdness on a bit thick. I'll be smelling greasy myself next.
Wipe it off first, and then we can talk, yeah?”

source.japanese: 慌てて朔屋、口元を拭えば、その手の甲にはべっとりと、泪の唇を彩っていた紅が伸びた。
source.english: Sakuya hastily wiped his mouth. A thick smear of the rouge that had colored Rui's lips spread across the back of his hand.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「It is said red wards off evil spirits, but when you've got that much slathered around your mouth, it's too salacious to be tasteful. Feels like even I'll start smelling of greasy ointments just standing here. If we're going to talk, it'll be after you deal with that, got it?」
When Sakuya wiped his mouth in a fluster, the lipstick that adorned Rui's lips was smeared thickly across the back of his hand.

source.japanese: 上甲板に上がれば四囲は相変わらず酒の海、沸き立つ酒気が夥[おびただ]しい、立っているだけでも酒精体中の毛穴からしみ込んで足元に来そうな。船内にいればいくらかは酒気も避けられるというのに、なぜわざわざと朔屋が殺し屋に訝しげに目問いすれば、智里それは無視して逆に首尾を問う。
source.english: On the upper deck, the sea was still liquor all around them. So much alcohol rose into the air that merely standing there felt as though it might seep through every pore and make his knees unsteady. Below, they could avoid some of the fumes. Why come up deliberately? Sakuya asked the killer with a suspicious look. Tomosato ignored it and asked how his errand had gone instead.

target.text: When he ascended the ladder to the upper deck, the ocean was, as ever, wine in all directions, the air seethed with immense quantities of alcoholic vapour, and just standing there, it felt as though the alcohol seeped into his body through the skin pores on his body, reaching all the way to his feet. They could have avoided at least some of these vapours had they just stayed within the ship, so why did they have to go all the way up here, Sakuya asked the murderer with a puzzled look in his eyes; as he did, Tomosato ignored his question, instead asking him how things went.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そんで、どうだった、首尾は？
　あったんだろ、真珠」
source.english:
“So, how'd it go?
There were pearls, right?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ああ。あるにはあった、というか出てきたというか。ともかく───駄目だああ」
source.english: “…Yes. There were—or they appeared, perhaps. Anyway… It's no use!”

source.japanese: 朔屋、そもそもの目的の真珠の行方を思い出し、頭を抱える。確かに、智里の言う通りも真珠はあったとも、あったけれどもそれは今、己の腹の中だという事実。
source.english: Only then remembering the fate of the pearl he had come for in the first place, Sakuya clutched his head. Tomosato was right: there had indeed been a pearl. The trouble was, it was now in his belly.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「泪さんに飲まされてしまったんだ」
source.english: “Ms. Rui made me swallow it.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「So then, how did it go, did you succeed? She had one, right? A pearl.」
【Naomasa】 「……Yeah. Well, she had one, or rather, one showed up at least, or, well. Anyways───it's no gooood.」

Sakuya, remembering the whereabouts of the pearl, his objective from the start, was at his wits' end. Certainly, there was a pearl, to be sure, just like Tomosato had said, there was one, but the reality was that, right now, it was within his own stomach.
【Naomasa】 「Rui-san made me gulp it down.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「飲まされたぁ？　
　女ァ抱いてきたに飽きたらず、呑んできたとけつかる。どこの女王様だてめぇは」
source.english:
“Swallow it?
Bedding a woman wasn't enough, you had to drink it down too? What queen do you think you are?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……面目次第も……。
　あ。君もしかして、その長物で僕の腹を切開して取り出そうとか考えてないだろうな。
　そんな事したって、もうきっと消化液に浸食されてるぞ、故売屋だって買い取ってくれないぞ」
source.english:
“…I've no excuse… Wait.
You're not thinking of cutting my belly open with that long thing to take it out, are you?
It's probably being eaten away by digestive juices already. Even a secondhand dealer wouldn't buy it.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Made you gulp it down? So not content with just banging a woman, you even had the balls to swallow it? Who the hell do you think you are, some kind of queen?」

【Naomasa】 「……I am truly ashamed……. Ah. Hey, you're not by any chance maybe thinking about using that long stick of yours to make an incision in my stomach to retrieve it, are you? Even should you do that, it's got to be corroded by the digestive fluids now, not even a fence would take it.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「アホくさい。お前の腸[はらわた]かっ捌いたってなにが面白い。お前の酒まみれの肝[キモ]なんざ、それこそ薬種商だって買い取りゃしねえ」
source.english: “Stupid idea. What's so amusing about opening your guts? Even an apothecary wouldn't buy that booze-soaked liver of yours.”

source.japanese: 意地悪くせせら笑う智里だったが、この男、本格的に自分の仕事を忘れているのではないかと疑わしい。が、すぐさますとんと落ち着いて智里は、懐手に頷[うなず]いた。
source.english: Tomosato sneered maliciously. Had this man truly forgotten his own profession? Then he settled at once, tucked his hands inside his clothing, and nodded.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Ridiculous. What fun would there be in cutting open your guts? Your liver's so soaked in booze, not even an apothecary would touch it.」

Tomosato sneered cruelly, but it was up for debate whether or not this man had genuinely forgotten his own occupation. Still, Tomosato quickly settled into a complete calm, then nodded with his hands in his pockets.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「───ま、それでもいいんだ多分。
　腹ン中にあろうが身に着けていようがどっちでも。おらいっちょ試してみ？」
source.english:
“Well, probably fine either way.
In your belly, or worn on you. Come on, try it.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「───Well, that's still fine, probably. Doesn't matter if it's in your stomach or on your person. Hey, let's give it a crack?」

source.japanese: と無造作に、抜く手もみせずに舷側に一閃、その剣閃の速さもさりながら、朔屋にはそれまで智里が一体どこに刀を提げていたのかも見えず。無手だったのだ確かにそれまでは。分厚い舷側がたやすく断ち割られ、海へと開かれた時に朔屋が抱いた悪い予感は直後に証明された。
source.english: With no more ceremony than that, Tomosato slashed at the ship's side, too quickly even for the draw to be seen. Yet more astonishing than the speed of that flash was that Sakuya had never once noticed where on earth Tomosato was carrying a sword. He had quite definitely been empty-handed until then. The thick bulwark was cleft apart with ridiculous ease and the sea laid open beyond; the bad feeling that came over Sakuya at that moment was confirmed an instant later.

target.text: With a casual gesture, without even visibly unsheathing, a flash streaked towards the ship's side, but despite the speed of his glinting blade, Sakuya never even saw where in the world Tomosato had been wearing that sword before. He had most certainly been unarmed until just now. The bulky bulwark of the ship was cut apart, and the bad premonition Sakuya began to harbour the moment he saw the opening leading to the sea was proven right immediately after.

source.japanese: 智里が朔屋の腰を蹴ったぐり、叩き落としたのだ容赦なく。
source.english: Tomosato kicked him in the hips and knocked him overboard without mercy.

target.text: Tomosato gave Sakuya a solid kick in the rear, knocking him off mercilessly.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「待っ、莫っ」
source.english: “Wait, you id—”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「WAI-, YOU IDI-」

source.japanese: 待ても莫迦も言いきれず、落ちていくが酒の赤い水面へ、真っ逆様に悲鳴の緒も長く曳いて。
source.english: Before he could get out either wait or idiot, down he went headfirst toward the liquor's red surface, drawing a long thread of a scream behind him.

target.text: Unable to finish telling him to wait or calling him an idiot, he fell down towards the red surface of the wine, his scream stretching into a long trail behind him as he went down headlong.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（ごばっ！　ばばばば莫迦あの人殺し、
　斬る代わりに溺れ死なすつもり───
　ごぼごばごぼごぼぼ───っ）
source.english:
(Gub! Y-y-y-you idiot, you killer!
Drowning me instead of cutting
me down—Glub-glub-glub—!)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（死んだ、今度こそ死んだ、
　苦しい、息が、
　ボコボコボコボコボコボコ───）
source.english:
(Dead. I'm dead this time.
It hurts.
I can't breathe—Blub-blub-blub-blub-blub-blub—)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（ああ、なんだってこんな事に───）
source.english: (Ah… Why did it come to this—?)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（苦しい苦しい、がば、がぼぼぼっ、
　溺れ死ぬのなんて厭だ、ひどすぎる───）
source.english:
(It hurts, it hurts… Gah, glub…
I don't want to drown. Too horrible—)

source.japanese:
真に溺死の危機に直面した者には、そこまで悠長に恐怖していられる暇などあるまい。
　実際───
source.english:
Someone truly about to drown would scarcely have the leisure to indulge in so much terror.
In fact—

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （GLARGH! S-s-s-s-s-stupid damn murderer, does he intend to drown me in place of cutting me down─── GRBLBRLBRBLRBRLG───)
【Naomasa】 （I'm dead, this time I am absolutely dead, it hurts, can't breathe, ghrhrllrlrlrghlrhghlr───）
【Naomasa】 （Aah, how did I even end up in this situation───）
【Naomasa】 （It hurts it hurts, grah, grlrlrlr, I really don't want to drown to death, it's just awful───）
Those who were truly faced with the peril of death by drowning would not have the time to so leisurely dread their impending doom. In fact───

source.japanese: 温く体にまとわりつく葡萄酒の海の中、朔屋、必死に四肢振り回してもがきにもがく。もがけどしかし息は続かず水面は見えず、ついに堪[た]えかねて口を開けたところで流れ込む赤い液体、瞬く間に肺の中まで浸されて、遂に朔屋、呼吸もできずに、海の藻屑───
source.english: In the sea of wine, warm against him and clinging to his body, Sakuya thrashed all four limbs and struggled, struggled for his life. Yet struggle though he might, his breath would not last and the surface was nowhere in sight; at last he could bear no more and opened his mouth, whereupon the red liquid came flooding in, invaded even his lungs in the blink of an eye, and Sakuya, no longer able to breathe, was finally nothing but sea wrack—

source.japanese:
とはいかなかった。
　いかに人の肺は液体からでも酸素を得られるとはいっても、魚の鰓[えら]の様にはいかず、息続くわけないはずなのに、
　どういう奇跡なのか、朔屋は水中で呼吸が可能となっていたのだ。そればかりでなく、動くのも自在で、水の中の抵抗も上下感覚の混乱もなく、いともあっさりと水面に浮上する。
source.english:
But that was not to be.
Even if human lungs could extract oxygen from liquid, they were no fish's gills, and his breath ought never to have lasted.
Yet, by what miracle no one could say, Sakuya had become able to breathe underwater. Nor was that all: he could move as he pleased, untroubled by the water's resistance or any confusion as to up and down, and surfaced with absurd ease.

target.text: Within the ocean of red wine warmly enveloping his body, Sakuya had desperately been swinging around his limbs like his life depended on it, struggling and struggling. But no matter how he struggled, he was unable to breathe, the surface was nowhere to be seen, and when he finally could no longer endure it, when he opened his mouth, the red liquid flowed into him, filling him all the way to his lungs in an instant, and in the end, unable to breathe, Sakuya went to his winy grave───

Not that any such thing happened. No matter how people may claim that it is possible for the human lung to procure oxygen even from liquids, it could not do it in the same manner as the gills of a fish, and it should certainly not be able to continue breathing, and yet. What manner of miracle must it have been, for Sakuya had become able to breathe underwater. And that was not all, he could move as he pleased, there was no resistance in the water, nor did he experience any loss of vertical orientation, and he rose to the surface with remarkable ease.

source.english: “Huh—?”

source.japanese:
赤い水面に上がってみれば、肺より葡萄酒吐き出される感触はやや気分に障[さわ]るものの、もちろん、息も普通に続く。
　不思議に頭を捻りつつ周囲見渡せば、間近に信天翁号の船体があり、海面まで垂らされたのは縄梯子。手に取り上らんと見上げてみれば、こちらは見下ろしている殺し屋の顔。朔屋、全身酒に夥[おびただ]しく濡れて上甲板に戻るのだった。
source.english:
Once above the red surface, the sensation of wine leaving his lungs was a little unpleasant. Naturally, however, he could breathe normally too.
Puzzled, he looked about. The Albatross's hull was close by; a rope ladder hung down to the sea. Taking hold and looking up to climb, he found the killer's face gazing down. Drenched from head to foot in liquor, Sakuya returned to the upper deck.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「───Huh?」

When he tried to rise above the red surface, the sensation of expelling red wine from his lungs did spoil his mood a little, but of course, he could still breathe normally as well. As he surveyed his surroundings while twisting his head in wonder, there, on the hull of the nearby Albatross, was a ladder lowered all the way to the surface of the sea. As he took hold of it with his hands and attempted to lift himself out of the wine while looking up, there was the face of the murderer looking down his way. Sakuya, entire body drenched in vast quantities of wine, made his return to the upper deck.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「で、どうだったい、海水浴は」
source.english: “Well? How was your swim?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どうもなにも、いったいどうなっちまったんだ、僕の体は。海の中だというのに、息は続くし苦しくもならない。ああ、そうか、僕はいよいよ魚になっちまったんだなぁ」
source.english: “Never mind how it was. What on earth has happened to my body? Under the sea, I could breathe. No pain. Ah, I see. I've finally become a fish…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「So, how was your little dip in the ocean?」

【Naomasa】 「Who cares about that, what the hell is going on with my body? I was in the middle of the ocean, and I could just keep breathing without even feeling any pain. Aah, so that's it, I've finally turned into a fish for gooood!」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「いや、そういうのは他にまかせておけよ」
source.english: “No, leave that sort of thing to others.”

source.japanese: しかし、朔屋は己の変化に頭が回る。この際、このふざけた殺し屋でもかまわない、誰か僕にまっとうな説明をしてくれと縋[すが]らん気持ちで智里を見れば、平素のにやけた顔もどこへやら、顎に手当てて思案顔。
source.english: But Sakuya's thoughts turned to the change in his own body. Even this ridiculous killer would do: someone, give me a proper explanation. Almost ready to cling to him, he looked at Tomosato. The usual smirk had vanished. A hand at his chin, the man looked thoughtful.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Nah, leave that kind of stuff to other people.」

However, Sakuya was thinking hard about the change in himself. In these circumstances, it could even be this jesting murderer for all he cared, so clinging to the hope of there being anybody who could give him a proper explanation for all this, when he looked at Tomosato, his usual smirk was nowhere to be seen; he instead had his chin in hand with a pensive look on his face.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……水の中を酸素を取り出すだけでなく、人体を水中に適応させるような構造変換も行っているのか、あるいは単に体表面に力場を発生させて水の侵入を防いでいるのか」
source.english: “…Not merely extracting oxygen from the water, but restructuring the human body to adapt it to immersion? Or simply generating a force field at its surface to keep the water out?”

source.japanese: 朔屋には意味も通らぬことをぶつぶつと。さてはこの男、何か知ってると朔屋がその呟きに耳傾けようとしたところで、
source.english: He muttered things Sakuya could not understand. So this man knew something! Just as Sakuya tried to listen more closely—

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Maybe it's not just allowing you to extract oxygen while underwater, but also carrying out a structural transformation of the makeup of your body to make it adapt to being underwater, or perhaps it simply generates a force field on the body surface, preventing water from entering the body.」
He muttered things that made absolutely no sense to Sakuya. Thinking "well now, this man seems to know something", Sakuya attempted to listen carefully to those mutterings, and when he did,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ま、細かい仕組みなんぞ、俺だって知るかい」
source.english: “Well, hell if I know the details.”

source.japanese: と、あっさり己の思索、ぶん投げる。
source.english: And with that, he blithely tossed his own theories aside.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Well, not like I've got a clue about the detailed mechanics at play here either.」
He easily flung his own speculation aside.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「とにもかくにも、これでてめえがこの酒の海の中まで入っていけるってこった」
source.english: “Anyway, you can go down into this sea of liquor now.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもだって、息ができるのはいいとしても、
　僕は一体何処にどこに行って何をすればいいんだぁ……」
source.english:
“But… Fine, I can breathe.
Where—where on earth am I supposed to go, and what am I supposed to do…?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Anyway, this means you can now dive right into this sea of wine here.」
【Naomasa】 「But still, while being able to breathe is all well and good, just where am I supposed to go, and what exactly am I supposed to even do……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そこまで俺が知るかいよ。
　まあ行き先は、
　てめえの腹ン中の真珠に訊けや」
source.english:
“How would I know that much?
Ask the pearl
in your belly where to go.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「How should I know? Well, when it comes to your destination, just can always just ask that pearl in your stomach.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「後はまあ、なるようになんだろうぜ」
source.english: “After that, it'll work out however it works out.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「What comes after, hmm, let the chips fall where they may.」

source.japanese: ───小さな星雲が、踏み出した、朔屋の長靴の足底から。細かな雲母片を散らしたように砂が舞い上がる様は、あの、硝子玉の中にミニチュアの邸宅と雪に擬した粉末を封じこめた玩具を揺らしたてた時と似通う。硝子玉の中の密度の濃い液体に、巻き上げられた粉末がゆっくりと舞い、長い事かけて降り積もっていく、あの。
source.english: A little nebula rose beneath Sakuya's boot as he stepped forward. The sand swirled up like scattered flakes of mica, rather as powder did in those toys with a miniature house and imitation snow sealed inside a glass globe. Shake one, and the powder would drift slowly through the dense liquid, taking a long time to settle. Like that.

source.japanese: 朔屋は子供の頃、その輸入品の玩具にいたく気をそそられて、両親に強請りつけて買ってもらったのだけれど、いざ自分の物になってみると、硝子玉の中の雪景色への関心をそうそうに失い、お強請りした時の熱意も薄れ、玉は勉強机での文鎮、次は棚の隅の各地の土産物の中の一つ、そして押入の中のガラクタとどんどん転落していって、今朔屋が足下に舞い上がる砂に連想しなければ、思い出される事すらなかったろう。
source.english: As a child, Sakuya had been so taken with that imported toy that he begged his parents to buy it. Once it was his, however, he soon lost interest in the snowy scene inside the glass. His enthusiasm faded. The globe became a paperweight on his desk, then one among the souvenirs in a corner of the shelf, then junk in the closet: a steady decline. Had the sand rising at his feet not called it to mind, he would probably never have remembered it at all.

source.japanese:
そして、足下に舞い上がっては留まる砂を、珍しきと眺めたのも始めのうちだけで、硝子玉の玩具への関心と同じく、さっさと興味を無くして顧みる事はなくなっていた。
　……朔屋の歩んできた後を示して、巻き上げられた砂が渦巻きの形を留めて列を成しているというのは、興趣に富んだ眺めであるというのに───赤を重ねて闇に沈んだ海底を見渡す目を持ち合わせているのなら、だが。
source.english:
And he found the sand rising and hanging about his feet curious only at first. Just as with the toy globe, he quickly lost interest and ceased looking back.
A pity: the sand he had stirred up stood in a line of lingering whorls, tracing his passage. It was a fascinating sight—provided one had eyes capable of surveying a seabed sunk in layer upon layer of red darkness.

source.japanese:
左様、赤、なにもかも赤。いかなる奇跡にか赤葡萄酒と変じた海の中は、常よりも光が届かず、二・三米も潜[もぐ]れば無明の世界となる。たとえ灯りを持ったとしても、赤葡萄酒の濃度の前にはろくな視界が得られず難渋するだろう。
　なのに朔屋の目には、海底は黄昏程度の明るさに感じられ、さしあたって歩くに不自由はない。実に不思議な事ではあるが、なにから、どこからを不思議と区切ればいいのか。
source.english:
Yes, red. Everything red. Transformed by some miracle into red wine, the sea admitted less light than usual. Dive two or three meters and one entered utter darkness. Even with a lamp, the density of the wine would have made it hard to see.
Yet to Sakuya the seabed looked no darker than twilight. He could walk without difficulty. A marvel indeed—but where should one begin drawing the boundaries of the marvelous?

target.text: ───A small nebula emerged from beneath the soles of Sakuya's boot as he took a step forwards. Sand whirled up like a shower of delicate mica fragments, bearing a close resemblance to one of those glass globes, the toys containing a miniature mansion and fine powder mimicking snow, when vigorously shaken. In the thickened liquid of the glass globe, the stirred fine powder would slowly flutter about, then spend a long time falling and piling up below: one of those things.

In Sakuya's childhood, his interest had been greatly stimulated by that imported toy from foreign lands, and he had pestered and pleaded with his parents until they bought one for him, but once he actually got his very own, he quickly lost any interest in the snowy landscape within the glass globe.

The zeal from when he pleaded also faded away, and the globe became a paperweight sitting atop his writing desk before taking its place on the corner of his shelf amidst the other souvenirs from here and there; its rapid fall from grace finally saw it landing amongst all the other junk in his closet, and if the sand whirled up from beneath Sakuya's boots had not evoked memories of it, he would probably not even have remembered it at all.

Thus, he admired the novelty of the sand that swirled up from beneath his feet before landing again, but only at first, for just like his interest in the toy globe of glass, he quickly lost any interest in it and stopped paying it any attention. ……This very much in spite of the fact that, revealing the trail Sakuya had trod, the swept-up sand lingered in the shape of a vortex, forming a long line, making for a captivating view rich in charm───if one were endowed with eyes capable of looking out across the ocean floor, layered in reds and submerged in darkness, that is.

Verily, red, anything and everything was red. Within this ocean, transformed into red wine by what must have been some manner of miracle, the reach of the light was shorter than usual, and diving but two or three metres deep, one would enter an obscure world bereft of light. Even were one to carry a lamp, it would grant barely any visibility when faced with the density of the red wine, leaving one in a bog of misery.

Nevertheless, the ocean floor seemed to possess the brightness of twilight to Sakuya's eyes, and for the present, it made for no impairment to walking. It truly was a marvellous thing, but from what, and where, should he draw the boundary of what qualified as a marvel?

source.japanese: 葡萄酒に変じた海の中で、魚やその他海の生き物達も泥酔して乱舞を見せているかと思いきや、動く物は一個と見えぬ、精々が海草が躍っている程度の、大洪水が洗い流していった直後の箱庭もかくやの森閑とした眺めである事か？
source.english: With the silence, perhaps? One might have expected fish and other marine creatures to reel drunkenly through the wine. Instead, not a single thing moved, except for a little swaying seaweed. The scene was as still as a miniature garden just scoured by a great flood.

source.japanese: それともやはり、海面は頭上遙か、数百米はあろうかという深みなのに、朔屋はほとんど水圧の影響も受けず、ただ肌に圧されているような感触と、手足の屈伸に抵抗がある、程度にしか感じないでいる事か？
source.english: Or with the pressure? The surface lay far overhead, perhaps hundreds of meters above him, yet Sakuya felt scarcely any effect. A pressing sensation against his skin, a little resistance when he bent his limbs: no more than that.

source.japanese: そもそも、潜水器具もなにもなしに、形としては素潜りで海中にあるのに、呼吸に全く不自由していない事か？　ただ息をする分には、海中である事の違和感をほとんど意識する事もなく、強く息んだり溜息を漏らす時に小さな泡が列を連ねて立ち上っていくくらいで、液体の中にあるという事実さえ希薄になってくる。
source.english: Or, first of all, with the fact that he could breathe perfectly well? He had no diving equipment. By all appearances, it was an ordinary free dive. Yet breathing itself gave him almost no sense of being underwater. A hard grunt or a sigh sent a little string of bubbles upward; otherwise, even the fact of his immersion began to feel remote.

target.text: Within this ocean changed to wine, he would be greeted with the spectacle of fish and the other living creatures of the sea dancing boisterously in a drunken stupor, or so he thought, but he didn't see a single moving, living being; at best, he saw some marine grasses rustling, and a miniature garden moments after being scoured by a great flood would surely be a scene of equally profound silence as this, would it not?

Or perhaps, as he suspected, was the surface far above his head, and despite being likely hundreds of metres deep, Sakuya was barely impacted by the water pressure, he merely felt the sensation of something pressing on his skin, some resistance when he bent and stretched his limbs?

He didn't even have any diving gear in the first place, but despite the fact that he was functionally free-diving, was his breathing not completely unhindered? In terms of his breathing alone, he hardly even noticed the discomfort of being underwater; when he drew a strained breath or let out a sigh, there would at most be a line of small bubbles rising up, and even the reality of his being within a liquid was itself growing tenuous.

source.japanese: これで視界が赤く染まっていなかったなら、朔屋は高原を散歩しているのと大差ない心地だったろう。舌に葡萄酒の味を受ける事もなければ、鼻に匂いが届くわけでもない。それだって不可思議な作用であるが、やはりそもそもの不思議の始まりは、海が葡萄酒と変じてしまった事に始まっているだろう。
source.english: Had his view not been stained red, he might have felt little different from someone strolling across a highland. There was no taste of wine on his tongue, no smell in his nose. Those were mysterious effects too. But surely the beginning of all this mystery was the sea's transformation into wine.

source.japanese:
それまでは、さしもの信天翁号と言えども、無頼な日々の中朔屋の神経と生命を削り取るような事態は出来しても、まだ青年の理解の及ぶ、たとえば官憲に追われたり、あるいは変態外道な金持ちに仲間が売り払われ損なった現場に居合わせたりと、現実の範疇に収まっていた。
　それらに比べても今回の現象は───と、朔屋の脚が鈍る。
　あの夜の出来事はどうだ、と。
source.english:
Until then, even aboard the Albatross, the incidents that whittled away his nerves and threatened his life had remained within his understanding, however lawless the days. Fleeing the authorities, for instance. Being present when a shipmate narrowly escaped being sold to a rich, depraved pervert.
Still within the realm of reality. Compared with those, this phenomenon—Sakuya's steps slowed.
What about that night?

target.text: If his vision hadn't been steeped in red, Sakuya would likely hardly have felt any different than were he taking a stroll around a plateau. Had he not felt the taste of wine on his tongue either, then the smell would not have reached his nose. So inexplicable an effect did it have upon him, but ultimately, the origin of these mysteries must all lie in the very sea itself having turned into wine.

Hitherto, even the infamous Albatross, with its unruly everyday of villainy forcing trials upon Sakuya that would gnaw away at his nerves and very life, was still within the realm of this young man's understanding; even should he be pursued by the authorities, or even if he happened to be present at the scene of one of his comrades not quite managing to be sold off to a sexually degenerate, fiendish millionaire, it all fit neatly within the category of reality. Even compared to such things, this current phenomenon was─── and then, Sakuya's steps faltered. What about what happened that night then, he thought.

source.japanese:
あの夜、狭霧と冷気漂う船内通路で、魚怪共と出くわした、あれは確かに───常軌を逸していた。今回の現象とどこか似通った匂いが漂う。
　あの夜魚人達の群れ集う様を目撃して以来、朔屋の世界はどこかしらその運行の螺子が狂ってしまったような感がある、とは言えないだろうか。
source.english:
That night, in the ship's passageways filled with cold and thin mist, he had encountered the fish-monsters. That had certainly exceeded all ordinary bounds.
It carried something of the same scent as this. Since the night he witnessed those fish-people gathering, had not some screw in the workings of Sakuya's world been knocked awry?

source.japanese:
と、すれば泪だ。
　今こうして朔屋が海中を地上と変わらぬ呼吸、足取りで歩行する事可能ならしめる『真珠』も、あの泪からもたらされたもの。
source.english:
If so, there was Rui.
The pearl that now allowed him to walk beneath the sea, breathing and moving as freely as on land, had come from her too.

source.japanese:
それまでも朔屋にとっては畏怖の対象であった彼女だが、それを青年は、男を破滅させる魔性故にと思いみなしていたけれど、本能や肌感覚という、人間の根源に関わる感覚がもっと別の何事かを感じ取っていたからではないか。
　理性や知識といった、人間に後付けの知覚では感じ取れない、何かを。
source.english:
He had feared her even before that, but had put his dread down to the fatal allure with which she ruined men. Might his instincts, his skin—those senses rooted deepest in a human being—have perceived something else?
Something beyond reason and knowledge, those later additions to human perception?

source.japanese:
【直正】
（と、すれば泪さんは一体───）
source.english: (Then what on earth is Ms. Rui—?)

source.japanese: 常人ではなかろうと薄々覚りつつあるも、朔屋は彼女の正体に辿り着くに至ってはいない、今はまだ。
source.english: He was beginning to understand, dimly, that she could hardly be an ordinary woman. But he had not reached the truth of her identity. Not yet.

target.text: That night, when that mist and chill had rolled down the ship's passageways, when those fish monsters had made their appearance, certainly, that was─── when reality had gone completely off the rails. Something about it gave off a smell similar to this current phenomenon. Ever since he had witnessed the gathering of those fishmen that night, if felt as though the screws holding the inner workings of Sakuya's world together had come loose, could it not be said?

And if that were the case, it was Rui. That『Pearl』which allowed him to thus breathe underwater as though it were no different from breathing on land, which enabled him to walk on his feet: that, too, was brought to him by Rui.

Hitherto, the woman had been an object of fear to Sakuya, but the young man had believed that was something stemming from her devilishness, how she brought men to ruin, but could it not have been the result of something different he had sensed with his instincts, something crawling along his skin felt with one of these senses connected to the very essence of human existence? That which could not be sensed with reason or knowledge, post hoc perceptions based in hindsight, a certain something.
【Naomasa】 （But then, if that's true, what the hell is Rui───?）
While he had vaguely begun to realize that she was not an ordinary person by any means, Sakuya had not arrived at the truth of her identity. Not yet.

source.japanese: ───歩く、歩く、赤い酒の闇に閉ざされた海底を、朔屋は黙然と歩く。奇妙に静まりかえった海中を、ただ独り、生ある者として、海底の堆積物をひっそりと乱しながら、歩く。
source.english: On he walked, on he walked. Silently, Sakuya crossed the seabed enclosed in dark red wine. Alone, the only living presence in that strangely silent sea, he walked, quietly disturbing the sediment.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（羊水の中にあるというのは、
　こんな心地なんだろうか……）
source.english:
(Is this what it feels like
to be in amniotic fluid…?)

source.japanese:
朔屋はふとそんな風に物想いしたけれど、その喩えはしっくりと据わらず、それはやはり海の中が静寂に満ちているせいだからと気づく。胎児が宿る胎内は、母親の心臓の鼓動や血流で、常に音が満ちている。
　だとすればこの静けさに満ちた海底は、この世の外の風景といったほうが相応しい。
　現実とは思われない。と、すれば───さしずめ、物語の中か。
source.english:
The thought occurred to him, but the comparison would not quite settle. He realized why: the sea was filled with silence. A womb was always full of sound—the mother's heartbeat, the flow of blood.
This quiet seabed was better described as a landscape outside the world.
It did not feel real. In that case—inside a story, perhaps.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（そうか、これが───これは。
　物語の中に迷いこんでしまった……。
　そういう感覚なんじゃないだろうか）
source.english:
(That's it.
This is—this… Isn't this what it feels like
to have wandered into a story…?)

source.japanese: 物語に迷いこんでしまった朔屋青年、それは一体いかなる物語か。その答えは自分が歩み行く先にあるように思われてならず、ただひたすらに足を進める、その歩みは、ただ酒を買いに街に出る時も、注意が散漫で気が散りやすく、あちらこちらと寄り道ばかりする朔屋にしては、導かれるようにぶれがなかった。……実際、導かれていたのだろう。
source.english: Sakuya had wandered into a story. What sort of story? He could not shake the sense that the answer lay ahead, and kept walking. Even going into town to buy liquor, he was usually so distracted that he made detours everywhere. Now his steps never wavered, as though he were being guided. In fact, he probably was.

source.japanese:
智里が言った通りに、朔屋には己がどちらに進めば良いのか、ぼんやりと知覚されてある。身体の裡側の一点が、ある方向に引かれるような感覚がある。朔屋はそちらを目指して歩く、歩く、ひたすらに、歩く。
　体内に宿る泪の『真珠』が告げている。
source.english:
As Tomosato had said, he had a vague sense of which way to go. One point inside his body seemed to pull in a particular direction. He followed it, walking, walking, doing nothing but walking.
Rui's pearl, lodged inside him, was telling him the way.

source.japanese:
───どれくらい歩いたのだろうか。
　時間の感覚は希薄で、かつまた、身体の方も不思議と疲労を感じていない。依然として、体内の『真珠』が引かれるような感覚は残っているが、海中に降りて歩き出した時よりずっと弱くなっている。
source.english:
How long had he walked?
He had little sense of time. Stranger still, his body felt no fatigue. The pulling sensation remained, but it was much weaker than when he first began walking beneath the sea.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（おいおい……嘘だろう？
　ここで方角を見失ったりしたら……）
source.english:
(Come on… You're joking.
If I lose my bearings down here…)

source.japanese:
朔屋は危惧したけれど、前方遙かに見えてきたものに、ほっと胸を撫で下ろした。
　恐らくそここそが、今回の現象にまつわる何らかの鍵が潜[ひそ]んでいるところだ。その場所が見えてきたから、『真珠』の感応力も収まったのだろう。
　前方に望まれたのは、泥中に水晶の玉を沈めたように、そこだけ本来の海の色を保って、赤葡萄酒の色の中に浮かび上がった情景の、朔屋はまたも、あの硝子玉の玩具を思い浮かべた。
　なんとなればその球状の海水の中に見えていたのは、小さな建物の姿だったからで。
source.english:
He was alarmed, but the sight appearing far ahead brought relief.
That place probably held some key to the phenomenon. Perhaps the pearl's response was subsiding because the destination had come into view.
Like a crystal ball sunk in mud, one patch of water retained the sea's original color, standing out amid the red wine. Once again, Sakuya thought of the glass toy.
For inside that sphere of seawater stood a little building.

target.text: ───Walking, walking, along an ocean floor covered in the dark of red wine, Sakuya walked along in silence. Through an ocean strangely still as death, as the only being alive, all by himself, while quietly disturbing the sediment along the seabed, he walked.
【Naomasa】 （Wonder if this is how it feels to be inside amniotic fluid……）

Sakuya suddenly mused about such, but the metaphor was hardly a perfect fit, and he realized that it must have been because the ocean was laden with stillness. The womb carrying a foetus was always full of sound: the palpitations of the mother's heart, and the flow of her blood. With that being that case, this seabed steeped in silence was more aptly described as a landscape not of this world. It didn't appear real. And so, given that───when all was said and done, was he within a story?
【Naomasa】 （Is that it, this is───this must be. I've strayed into a story……. That's what this sensation is, isn't it?）

The young man Sakuya had strayed into a story, but whatever manner of story was it? He could not help but think the answer to that seemed to wait at the destination he was walking towards, and so he simply single-mindedly placed one foot in front of the other, and for someone like Sakuya, who even when merely walking to town to buy some booze would barely pay attention and easily be distracted, frequently making side trips and taking detours here and there, he walked as though guided, without wavering. ……In truth, he was most likely being guided.

Just as Tomosato had said, there lingered a vague awareness of which path he ought to take within Sakuya. He felt as though there was a point within his body that was being pulled in a certain direction. Sakuya walked towards that direction, walking, solely and devotedly walking. Rui's『Pearl』dwelling within his body was showing him the way.

───Just how long must he have walked? His grasp of the flow of time was tenuous, and at the same time, his body wasn't feeling any signs of fatigue either, strangely enough. As yet, the sensation of the『Pearl』 within his body still lingered, but it had grown much weaker compared to when he first dove into the ocean and began his walk.
【Naomasa】 （Oi oi……you're kidding me, right? If I lose my bearings here, then……）

Sakuya had grown uneasy, but he spotted something visible over yonder, and so relief washed over him. Most likely, some manner of clue relating to this phenomenon was lurking in that place. And since it was now visible to him, the responsiveness of the『Pearl』had likely abated in turn. What awaited ahead was like a crystal ball submerged into mire; only that place retained the natural colour of the ocean, a sight standing out vividly amidst the hues of red wine, and once again, Sakuya was reminded of that toy glass globe. If he were to give a reason, it would be because within that globe of seawater, he could see the shape of a small building.

source.japanese: ───ところが、傍まで寄って輪郭が判然となると、朔屋はどこかしら裏切られたような、期待外れの猥本でも掴まされたような、そんな肩透かしの心地に囚われる。
source.english: But as he approached and its outline grew clear, Sakuya felt somehow betrayed. The same deflated feeling as when one bought a dirty book that failed to deliver.

target.text: ───Nevertheless, when he came closer to it, and its outline grew distinct, Sakuya felt somehow betrayed, like he'd gotten his hands on a pornographic magazine only for it to not match his expectations; that was the feeling of disappointment that struck him.

source.japanese: 海を赤葡萄酒に替えたモノに関わる場所というて、漠然と西洋の城館とか、あるいはもっと直接に、葡萄農家、それもやはりあちらさんの、石造りの、質朴ながらも歳月に耐える頑丈な屋構え、そのあたりを勝手に想像していたところ、澄んだ海水の中に佇む、というより景気悪く這いつくばっていたのは、木造の平屋で。それも朔屋が下宿していたような、冴えない、ぱっとしない、家賃が安いだけが取り柄のような貧相な。
source.english: A place connected with whatever had turned the sea into red wine: he had vaguely imagined a Western château. Or, more directly, a winegrower's farmhouse, also Western, stone-built, plain but sturdy enough to withstand the years. What stood in the clear seawater—or rather crouched there forlornly—was a single-story wooden house. A shabby, unremarkable place like his old lodgings, with nothing to recommend it except the cheap rent.

target.text: When it comes to a place related to replacing the ocean with red wine, one would vaguely imagine the chateaus of the West, or perhaps more directly, a domaine, and it would have to be of the sort that those people preferred, built with stone, a building that, while rustic, presented a facade of sturdiness that would last through the ages; just when his imagination began to run away with him in tow, within the clear ocean water stood, or more accurately, slumped miserably as if crawling, a wooden, one-story house. And it was the dreary, unimpressive, seedy-looking sort where the only saving grace was the rent being cheap, the sort that Sakuya had lodged in before.

source.japanese: これならいっそ、巨大な蛤[ハマグリ]がでんと鎮座して、蓋をぱかぱか開閉させながら酒精の元素を吐いていた方がましだったと、身勝手な失望感に眉を顰[ひそ]めて玄関口に、回って戸を叩く時も、何やら貧乏教師に試験範囲を訊ねに来たかの、変に身近な感があって、どうにも怪異の解明とは程遠い、心が浮き立たない。
source.english: Better, he thought, if a giant clam had sat there grandly, opening and shutting its shell to exhale the elements of alcohol. Frowning at this entirely selfish disappointment, he went around to the entrance and knocked. It felt oddly familiar, as though he were visiting an impoverished teacher to ask what would be on the examination. Nothing like solving a supernatural mystery. Nothing to lift his spirits.

source.japanese: それでも、煙突から滾々と赤黒いの湧き出させ、海の中に溶けこませているところを見るに、ここが事態の核心である事に間違いはなく、さて、と応答を待ち受ける───が、返事がない。
source.english: Still, red-black liquid gushed from the chimney and dissolved into the surrounding sea. There could be no doubt that this place was at the heart of the affair. Well, then. He waited for an answer. None came.

target.text: If this was all he was getting, then he would strongly have preferred a giant clam imposingly enshrined there, upper valve clacking away as it snapped itself open and shut while spewing out the very elements of alcohol from within itself, he thought, wrinkling his brow in a self-absorbed feeling of disappointment, and when he walked around to the front door and knocked, there was a strange familiarity to it all, as if he was paying his penniless teacher a visit to ask about something related to exams; it was a far cry from shedding any light on this inexplicable mystery, and his heart remained in low spirits.

Even so, copious amounts of reddish-black gushed forth from the chimney, and seeing how it dissolved into the ocean waters, there was no doubt that this place was the heart of this situation; well then, he thought, waiting for a reply───but, none came.

source.japanese: もう一度叩いても、音が変にくぐもって、中まで伝わらないのか。仕方なく朔屋は、後家の夜這いにでも参るように、抜き足差し足で裏手に回れば縁側の、障子戸を立てた向こうから、聞こえてきた声がある。
source.english: He knocked again. The sound was strangely muffled; perhaps it did not carry inside. With no choice, Sakuya crept around the back, furtive as a man paying a widow a secret nighttime visit. Beyond the veranda's paper sliding doors, he heard a voice.

target.text: Even when he tried knocking again, the sound was weirdly muffled, so perhaps it simply hadn't travelled within? Reluctantly, but with nothing else for it, he tiptoed around to the back of the house like he was paying a nightly visit to the bedroom of a widow, and when he arrived at the engawa, from behind the shut shouji door, a voice was audible. (TN: The engawa, written "縁側", is the external corridor on the outer side of a traditional Japanese house.)

source.japanese:
