ここで、あの、岩壁に佇んで聞いた男の心を惑わし、船を難破させるという水妖の、白金の絃[いと]を震わすように妙なる声であったなら、朔屋はまだ納得しただろう。
　しかし、ぶつぶつと小言っぽく、小鼠のように甲高い、年寄りくさい声とあっては。
source.english:
Had it been the exquisite voice of a water-spirit perched upon a cliff, luring men to shipwreck—as though platinum strings were trembling—he might still have been satisfied.
But this voice muttered and grumbled. High and mouse-like. Old.

target.text: If the voice had been exquisitely melodious like vibrating strings of platinum, the mellifluous calls of the water spirits said to stand atop walls of stone, seducing the hearts of men and leading ships to ruin at sea, then Sakuya could probably still accept this. He was less impressed when the voice muttered and grumbled, was shrill and squeaky like a little mouse, and sounded rather elderly in tone.

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『……ええと、必要とされる要素は……と』
source.english: “…Now, the required elements… Let's see.”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「ブルゴーニュ地方の日照時間と、土壌の成分分析表と、それから、おお、当然葡萄の品種と、どこの醸造家が造っているか、もだ』
source.english: “Hours of sunshine in Burgundy, a table of soil analysis, and—oh, naturally—the grape varieties. Which winemaker produces it, too.”

source.japanese:
【老人】
『それから当地の歴史もシミュレイトしてやった方が良いな。
　過去の気候変動のデータと、文化風俗……仕事の時の歌なども重要だろう』
source.english:
“Better simulate the local history as well. Data on past changes in climate,
customs and culture… The songs they sing at work should be important too.”

source.japanese: そして、障子戸に浮かぶ影も、小柄で痩せて、年寄りくさい輪郭とあっては。
source.english: And the shadow on the paper door was small and thin, with an old man's outline.

target.text: 【Old man's voice】 『……Hmm, the components I'll need are……right.』
【Old man's voice】 「The daylight hours of the Bourgogne region, an analysis table of the soil composition, and after that, ah yes, the variety of grape, of course, and also which vigneron to use.』

【Old man's voice】 『After that, it would be best to simulate the history of the place too. The data of past climate change, the culture and customs…… they'll probably also need work songs and the like.』
And then, there was the shadow cast on the shouji door; for it to be of a small, skinny frame, a silhouette of the frail and aged.

source.japanese:
海を赤葡萄酒に替えるという、神話の奇跡にも匹敵する怪現象に関わる声としてはどうにも押し出しに欠けて、朔屋は内心の期待、そう期待だ、何も神話にあるような海底の大宮殿とか得体の知れない妖物までを望んでいたわけではないにしろ、もっとこうその、なんというか、外連味が欲しかったし予想していたのである朔屋にしても。
　強く目を閉じて、心中の予想と眼前の現実の折り合いが付くまで深呼吸、こぽこぽと気泡が立ち上がり、頭上に見えなくなるまで待って───
source.english:
For a voice concerned with a phenomenon fit to rival a mythic miracle—the sea transformed into red wine—it lacked presence. Sakuya had expectations. Yes, expectations. He had not necessarily hoped for a vast undersea palace out of myth, or an unidentifiable monster. Still, something a little more—well—showy. Even Sakuya had expected a touch of theater.
He shut his eyes hard and breathed deeply, waiting for his imagined scene to reconcile itself with the reality before him. Bubbles rose, burbling. He waited until they vanished overhead—

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『後はこの海域の地形と海流と、海水内の成分と、気候データと……ふう、まだまだ入力せにゃならん』
source.english: “Then the topography and currents of this stretch of sea, the constituents of the seawater, climate data… Phew. Still so much to enter.”

target.text: For a voice connected to changing the sea into red wine, this supernatural phenomenon that rivalled even the miracles found in myth, it was utterly lacking in presence, and the expectation, yes, the anticipation deep within Sakuya's heart, not that it was at all the case that he had been looking forward to some manner of incomprehensible monster lurking in a great temple at the bottom of the sea like in the legends, it was more of a, how to put it, Sakuya wanted something a bit more showy, he had expected something with a more pretentious affectation, and yet.

He clenched his eyes shut, drew several deep breaths until he could reach a compromise between the expectation in his heart and the reality before his eyes, air bubbles softly popping into existence and rising; he waited until they vanished above his head before───
【Old man's voice】 『After that, there's the topography of this area, of the ocean and its currents, and the composition of the water itself, and the climate data……phew, still so much left to type.』

source.japanese:
気泡が見えなくなるまで待って───
　ぱちぱちと算盤でも弾くような音。
　連動してばしゃばしゃばしゃと沢山の小さく硬いものが叩きつける音。
　ちーん、と、間を置きながら鳴る鈴の音[ね]。
　を、聞いた時、朔屋の鼻からまた気泡、今度は、ふは、と脱力に抜けた。
　その響きは字面として並べるなら正体不明でも、朔屋には聞き覚えがあったから。
source.english:
He waited until the bubbles vanished—A clicking like beads on an abacus.
In step with it,
a rapid clatter of many small, hard things striking.
A bell, dinging at intervals.
Hearing those sounds, he let bubbles escape from his nose again, this time in a deflated huff.
Written out, the noises might have seemed unidentifiable. But Sakuya had heard them before.

source.japanese:
算盤を弾くような音は、キーを叩く音。
　ばしゃばしゃ言うのは、ハンマーが紙に打ちつけられる音。
　鈴の音[ね]は、文字が紙の端まで来た時の、改行報せの合図だ。
　何かというと、タイプライターを動かしている時の音なので。
source.english:
The abacus-like clicking was the sound of keys.
The clatter was hammers striking paper.
The bell signaled the edge of the page: time for a new line.
In short, the sound of a typewriter at work.

source.japanese: 障子の向こうの何者かは、海を葡萄酒にの大奇跡をやってのけてみせたくせして、徹頭徹尾朔屋も覚えのある道具立てて攻めてくるらしいが、もう一々脱力するのも面倒だと、青年は意を決して呼びかけるが障子の向こうへ、さて。
source.english: Whoever was behind the door had performed the great miracle of turning the sea to wine, yet seemed determined to confront Sakuya with familiar trappings from first to last. Growing tired even of feeling deflated at each new discovery, Sakuya gathered his resolve and called through the paper door. Well, then.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あのぅ……お忙しいところ、お邪魔するのもなんなんですが……」
source.english: “Excuse me… I hate to interrupt when you're so busy…”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『なんじゃい。あんたの見た通り大忙しの最中じゃわい。黒潮騎士か悪魔の岩礁から迷い出てきた混血か知らんが、今は忙しい。後にしてくれ』
source.english: “What? As you can see, I'm extremely busy. Whether you're a Black Current Knight or some half-breed wandered out of Devil Reef, I don't know. I'm busy. Come back later.”

source.japanese:
と障子戸を、ちらとも開けないまま遮[さえぎ]った、にべもないので。
　だからといってここまで来て何もせず戻るわけにも行かず、縁側の前で手をこまねいて、
source.english:
He cut Sakuya off without opening the door so much as a crack. Utterly unaccommodating.
But Sakuya could hardly come all this way and return without doing anything. He stood helpless before the veranda.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、そうも言われても、こっちも都合があると言うか、難渋していると言うか……」
source.english: “Well, you may say that, but I have my own troubles, you might say. Or rather, I'm in a bit of a bind…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「せめて話だけでも……」
source.english: “At least hear me out…”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『ああもう、やかましいなあもう。
　忙しいと言っておろうが。
　近頃の若い者は、みぃんな、
　そちらの都合ばかり押しつけてきよる』
source.english:
“Oh, stop making such a racket.
I told you I'm busy.
Young people these days,
every last one of them—always expecting everyone else to work around them.”

target.text: He waited until the bubbles of air could no longer be seen─── A sound like somebody clacking away at an abacus or something. The sound of many small, hard things striking a surface in succession, a series of snaps and clicks. The sound of a bell going ding, marking a brief intermission. And the moment he heard this, bubbles left Sakuya's nose again, this time escaping with a limp exhale. For though the sounds might be unidentifiable if put into writing, they were familiar to Sakuya's ears.

The sound like that of somebody using an abacus: that was the sound of keys being struck. What produced the snapping clicks was the sound produced by hammers striking paper. The sound of the bell was the signal informing of a line break, that which would ring whenever the letters had reached the edge of the paper. Put simply, they were the sounds made by a typewriter in use.

For someone making it sound like he was the one who had managed to accomplish the great wonder that was changing the ocean into wine, whoever this was on the other side of the shouji was apparently wholeheartedly assailing a tool that even Sakuya knew from A to Z, and fed up with being exhausted at every little thing, the young man made up his mind, addressing the presence beyond the shouji.
【Naomasa】 「Errmm……I'm sorry for interrupting while you're so busy and all……」

【Old man's voice】 『What is it? Yes, as you surmise, I'm very busy and right in the middle of something. You could be a knight of the Black Current or some half-breed who stumbled out from Devil Reef for all I care, I'm busy right now. Come back later.』

So he said, holding the shouji door shut without even allowing him a peek inside, a flat refusal. But while that might all be true, he couldn't simply return with nothing to show for it after having come all this way, and so he remained before the engawa with his arms folded,
【Naomasa】 「No no, say that all you want, but I've also got my circumstances to consider, or rather, I'm in a real bind here……」
【Naomasa】 「Would you at least listen to……」

【Old man's voice】 『Aaagh, enough, you're a real noisy nuisance, seriously. I do believe I told you I'm busy. Young people these days, all cut of the same cloth, always foisting whatever suits their needs on others at their own convenience.』

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『近頃は陛下の近習も質が落ちたもんじゃ。
　───あ？』
source.english:
“The quality of His Majesty's attendants has fallen lately.
—Eh?”

source.japanese: そこで障子の向こうでようやく老人が向き直る気配のあったが、中途でびくりと声を爪弾きだし、そして固まった。
source.english: At last, behind the paper door, the old man seemed to turn toward him. Halfway through the movement, a startled note sprang from his voice. Then he froze.

source.japanese:
【老人】
『なんだとっ……人間……か？
　馬鹿なっ。なんで人間なんぞがここにおる。
　しかもお前、まだ生きとるじゃないか！』
source.english:
“What… A human?
Impossible! What's a human doing here?
And you're still alive!”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『おまけにろくなダイビングスーツも着けずタンクも背負わず、なんだって大人しく溺れ死にもしとらんのだ』
source.english: “Not even a proper diving suit, no tank on your back. Why haven't you quietly drowned?”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『水精の寵愛目出度き人間など近頃はとんと聞かぬし、オキシジェンカプセルは概念からして大戦前に滅び去っているはずだが……』
source.english: “One scarcely hears these days of a human favored by a water-spirit. And the oxygen capsule ought to have vanished even as a concept before the Great War…”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『いや、なんだっていいわい。
　ここはお前如き陸上の類人猿が気軽に踏みこんでいい場所と違う』
source.english:
“Never mind.
This is no place for a land-dwelling ape like you to stroll into.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『海精の怒りに触れんうちに、ほらとっとと去[い]んだ去[い]んだ』
source.english: “Before you incur the wrath of the sea-spirits—go on, be off with you.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『ここでのことを他言無用にするなら、まだ無傷で返してやるわい。命冥加と有り難く受け取って、さっさと消えろ猿もどきが』
source.english: “Keep what happened here to yourself and I'll let you leave unharmed. Count yourself lucky to be alive, and disappear, you imitation ape.”

source.japanese:
理解の及ばぬ言語でまくしたてられ、ただでさえ鬱期で他人との交流が苦痛な朔屋には身が縮む思いであったが、それでも彼をなお踏みとどまらせたものはなんだったのだろう。
　あるいは───信じがたいことに、そうまこと信じがたいことに、海上で停泊を余儀なくされている信天翁号と、その面子への義務感めいたものだったのかもしれない。
source.english:
Beset by a torrent of incomprehensible language, Sakuya felt himself shrinking. In his depressed state, dealings with others were painful enough already. Yet something kept him there.
What? Perhaps—unbelievable though it sounds, truly unbelievable—it was something like a sense of duty toward the Albatross, stranded above, and those aboard her.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しかしご老人、こっちもほとほと困っているんだ……。見ればこの辺りの海の潮水を葡萄酒にしているのは……あんたのご様子」
source.english: “But, sir, we're at our wits' end… From the look of things, the one turning the seawater around here into wine is… you.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「僕が乗りこんでいる……ああ、厭なことにそうなっている……船が、この葡萄酒のお陰で進めなくなっている」
source.english: “The ship I'm aboard—yes, unhappily, that is my situation—can't move because of this wine.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「この葡萄酒の海域が……どこまで広がっているのかは知らないが……せめて……そう、船がこの海域を離脱するまで……海を元通りにしてくれないか。その後はまたあなたの好きなようにしていいから」
source.english: “I don't know how far this sea of wine extends… But at least… Yes, until our ship leaves this area… Could you put the sea back the way it was? Afterward you can do as you please.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『はん。何を勝手な。これはな、儂の義務よ。
　伊達や酔狂、まして遊びで行っているわけではないんだ。そもそもこれは神聖不可侵の盟約』
source.english:
“Hah! What presumption. This is my duty.
I am not doing it for show or on a whim, much less for amusement. To begin with, this is a sacred and inviolable pact.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『かくかくしかじかの星辰整うた時、これこれの海上で願われた祈りは、この儂のデバイスを通じて速やかに主上へと転送されて決裁処理を待つ』
source.english: “When the stars align in such-and-such a configuration, a prayer offered upon such-and-such a sea is promptly forwarded through my device to our sovereign, to await the approval process.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『然るのちに主上からの受諾許可が通達され、それから適切な操作を行う。
　ま、今回の場合は、
【この海が酒だったらいい】
　などという巫山戯た請願だったわけだが』
source.english:
“Permission is then communicated from the sovereign,
and the appropriate operation is performed.
Well,
in this case the ridiculous petition was: [I wish this sea were booze].”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『全く勝手で陳腐な願いよな。
　それじゃとて周辺海域への影響は甚大で、
　生態系と海流がお陰で滅茶苦茶だわ。
　ひいてはお前、
　これは地上の気候にも影響するんだぞ』
source.english:
“A thoroughly selfish, banal wish.
Even so, its effects on the surrounding waters are enormous.
The ecosystem and currents are thrown into chaos.
Ultimately,
you realize, this affects the climate on land too.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『これらの悪影響を最小限に留め、かつ願いの効果範囲と抵触させないようにするにはどれだけの作業と計算と処理が必要なのか、お前判ってるのか？』
source.english: “Do you understand how much work, calculation, and processing it takes to minimize those adverse effects without infringing on the wish's effective range?”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『しかもそれを無効にしろと、キャンセルしろだと？　お断りじゃい。ようやく変換処理が落ち着いたばかりでな、これでも現在二二時間休憩なしで稼働中なんだ儂は』
source.english: “And now you tell me to nullify it? Cancel it? I refuse. The conversion process has only just stabilized. I've been operating for twenty-two hours without a break.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『そもそもこういう請願は、発心した本人だってキャンセルするには多大な処理が要求されるんだ。
　それをなんでお前のようなぽっと出の猿紛いが止められるもんかい』
source.english:
“Even the person who originated a petition like this requires considerable processing to cancel it.
How could an upstart imitation ape like you stop it?”

source.japanese: 一の言葉に一〇も撃ち返してくるのは、全くもってやかましいとしか言いようがないが、それでも案外親切なのか単に多弁なだけなのか。なんにせよ簡単にはとめられない事が判ったが、
source.english: For every word, he fired back ten. A racket, pure and simple. Still, perhaps he was surprisingly kind—or simply talkative. At any rate, Sakuya understood that stopping it would not be easy. But—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……それを願ったのは、どうやら僕であるらしい。昨日海を眺めながら、
『この海この水、全部酒だったらなぁ……』
　と。確かに言ってしまった記憶がある」
source.english:
“…It seems I may be the one who made that wish. Yesterday, looking at the sea, I said,
'If only this sea, all this water, were booze…'
I certainly remember saying it.”

source.japanese: 老人はしばし無言で何事か、作業している気配で、やがていかにも呆れたようにふんと鼻を鳴らした事である。
source.english: For a while the old man was silent, apparently doing something. At last he gave a snort of unmistakable disgust.

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『そうか。どこの阿呆かと思うたら、ここにいる阿呆か。
　……どれ声紋データ、オーラパターンチェック。なるほど確かにお前であるらしい』
source.english:
“So that's it. I'd wondered which fool it was, and here's the fool.
Let's see, voiceprint data, aura-pattern check… Yes. It does appear to be you.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『だがな、だからといって簡単にキャンセルできると思うなよ？　請願の取り消しは、発言した時と類似の星辰、位置情報、そして対応した発願文が必要じゃ』
source.english: “But don't think that makes cancellation easy. Revoking a petition requires a stellar configuration similar to the original one, location information, and a corresponding formulation of the wish.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『取り消しの言葉は、まあお前が発願人なら適当に考えられるじゃろ。ただし星辰と位置情報はそうもいかんぞ』
source.english: “If you're the petitioner, you can probably come up with suitable words to withdraw it. But the stars and location are another matter.”
“…Meaning…?”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『そういう星回りなど、滅多にやってこんと言う事よ。どれ……ふん、ざっと計算してみたところ、次の条件が揃うのは……おおなんだ、案外すぐじゃないか』
source.english: “Meaning those alignments seldom come around. Let's see… Hm. A rough calculation puts the next suitable combination at—oh, what do you know? Quite soon.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そりゃあ助かった……！
　いつだ、どこでどのくらい待てばいい？」
source.english:
“That's a relief…! When?
Where? How long do I have to wait?”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『訊きゃあ教えてもらえると思っとるのが、偽猿の都合良いところだな。ま、それくらい許してやろう』
source.english: “A sham ape always thinks he'll get an answer just by asking. Convenient, isn't it? Well, I'll grant you that much.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『位置はここより南南西三九マイル先、時期はただ今より二五年四ヶ月一五日五時間三四コンマ〇八秒先だ』
source.english: “Thirty-nine miles south-southwest of here. Twenty-five years, four months, fifteen days, five hours, and thirty-four point zero eight seconds from now.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「三九マイル先で、二五年て……。
　そ、そんなに待てやしない。
　それまでみんな急性アルコール中毒か、
　それでなくも餓死しちまうよ！」
source.english:
“Thirty-nine miles away, and twenty-five years…
I-I can't wait that long.
Everyone will die of acute alcohol poisoning before then—or starve,
if they don't!”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『だからそこまでは知ったことかい。
　その程度の時間も待てん陸猿の都合など、
　こっちには関係無いな』
source.english:
“As I said, what do I care?
Land apes unable to wait even that little
while are no concern of mine.”

target.text: 【Old man's voice】 『Lately, even His Imperial Majesty's attendants just aren't what they used to be. ───Wha?』
With that, it felt like the old man on the other side of the shouji finally turned around to face him, but mid-turn, he let out a startled yelp, then froze solid.
【Old man's voice】 『What in the Seven……a……human? Preposterous. Why would there be a human here? And what's more, you're still alive, aren't you!』
【Old man's voice】 『And on top of that, with no proper diving suit and no tank on your back, so why haven't you already drowned like any sensible human would?』

【Old man's voice】 『I haven't heard anything about any humans blessed with the favour of the water spirits recently, and the very concept of an oxygen capsule itself should have vanished long before the great war……』
【Old man's voice】 『No, none of that matters. This is not a place where some land-dwelling, anthropoid ape the likes of you may readily step foot in.』
【Old man's voice】 『Come now, hurry up and leave, go while you have yet to incur the wrath of the ocean spirits.』

【Old man's voice】 『If you promise not to speak a word of this to anyone, I can still send you home unharmed. Accept this providential protection with gratitude and begone from my sight, quickly now, monkey-man.』

Being bombarded with words he couldn't hope to comprehend made Sakuya, already in a depressive spell and finding interaction with others painful enough, want to curl in on himself, but then, what was it exactly that still made him stand his ground here? Perhaps it was───hard as it may be to believe, yes, even if it may truly beggar belief, perhaps it was something akin to a sense of obligation towards the crew of the Albatross, the ship currently forced to anchor at sea by forces beyond her control.
【Naomasa】 「But, good sir, I also find myself at my wits' end……. From what I can tell, the one who turned the seawater of this area into wine appears to be……you.」
【Naomasa】 「The ship that I'm sailing with…… aah, how I despise that things ended up like that……but that ship, as a result of this wine, can no longer make headway.」

【Naomasa】 「This sea of wine……I don't know how far it stretches exactly, but…… could you at least……right, until the ship clears this area of the sea……could you return the sea back to normal? After that, you can do whatever you want with it again.」

【Old man's voice】 『Humph. What selfish prattle. See, this here is my duty. I'm not doing this for show or on a whim, and certainly not for my own amusement. This originates from a sacred, inviolable covenant.』

【Old man's voice】 『When the celestial bodies of this-and-that are aligned, prayers born of someone's desire made on the such-and-such sea pass through this device of mine, where they are then swiftly forwarded to His Imperial Majesty, where they wait for the administrative procedures for acceptance to be completed.』

【Old man's voice】 『Thereafter, once I receive the directive that approval to accept the terms has been granted by His Imperial Majesty, I then proceed to execute the appropriate manipulations. Well, in this case, it was some ridiculous petition that went something like 【I sure wish this ocean was all alcohol.】』

【Old man's voice】 『Good grief, what a selfish and hackneyed wish. As a consequence, the effects on the surrounding waters are immense, and the ecosystems and ocean currents are a complete mess right now. And listen, you, what's more, this will also impact the climate on land.』

【Old man's voice】 『Do you know just how much work, calculating, and formal paperwork it takes to minimize the negative influences of all this, all while also ensuring that whatever happens doesn't conflict with the effective scope of the wish, do you have the first idea?』

【Old man's voice】 『And you're telling me to override that, insisting I cancel it? I refuse. The conversion procedures have only just reached a calm, and whatever it might look to you, I'll have you know that I've been going for twenty-two hours without a single break.』

【Old man's voice】 『And to begin with, when it comes to these kinds of petitions, even should the petitioner himself decide to cancel it, that would also require a lot of administrative processing. So why, exactly, would some upstart monkey-man fresh out of the jungle like you think you can put a stop to all of this?』

Having ten words fired back at you for every word spoken was, as a matter of fact, something that could only be described as carping, but perhaps he was unexpectedly considerate, or maybe just very voluble. Regardless of which it was, while he now understood that it was not something so readily stopped,

【Naomasa】 「……It seems that the one who made that wish, well, it was actually me. While looking out over the ocean, I said: 『I wish this ocean, and its water, was all alcohol. Ah, if only……』 I remember I definitely said that.」
The old man seemed to be working on something for a time, wordlessly, before finally letting out a snort of unmistakable exasperation.

【Old man's voice】 『Is that so? I was just wondering what idiot was to blame, and then it turns out to be the one standing right before me. ……Let's see, voiceprint data, aura pattern check. I see, it certainly does seem to be you.』

【Old man's voice】 『But still, don't go thinking that means it can just be easily cancelled. To withdraw a petition, you'd need a similar celestial body as when it was issued, the location information, as well as the appropriate words of prayer.』

【Old man's voice】 『As for the words of withdrawal themselves, well, you're the man who issued the prayer, so you just think up something suitable. However, I'm afraid that when it comes to the celestial body and the location information, the same can't be said.』
【Naomasa】 「……Which would mean……?」

【Old man's voice】 『Those kinds of fated stars rarely turn up, that's what I'm telling you. Let's see……hmm, based on some quick calculations here, the next time those conditions are all satisfied would be……oh, would you look at that, that's unexpectedly soon.』
【Naomasa】 「That's a huge relief……! So when is it, how long should I wait and where should I do it?」
【Old man's voice】 『Thinking you'll get an answer just because you asked, the kind of convenient little assumptions you monkey-men all take for granted. Well, I suppose I can allow for that much.』

【Old man's voice】 『The location is thirty-nine miles south-southwest from here, and the time is exactly twenty-five years, four months, fifteen days, five hours, and thirty-four-point-zero-eight seconds from now.』

【Naomasa】 「Thirty-nine miles, twenty-five years, you say……. B-, but I can't wait that long. They'll all end up suffering from acute alcohol poisoning before then, or if not that, then they'll all starve to death!」
【Old man's voice】 『Like I said, how should I know or care about any of that? The circumstances of some land-ape who can't even wait such a short time are completely irrelevant to me.』
【Naomasa】 「──────」

source.japanese:
絶句するしかない朔屋、打ちひしがれて項垂れると、背後から腕を軽くつついてくる者ものがあり───泪だった。
　周囲を赤黒く充たす葡萄酒も、彼女の周囲では和らいで色合い薄め、また彼女自身が裡[うち]から仄[ほの]かな光を発しているように、浮かび上がって。
source.english:
Sakuya could only fall silent. He hung his head, crushed. Then someone lightly nudged his arm from behind.
Rui. The red-black wine filling their surroundings grew paler about her. She stood out as though a faint light shone from within her own body.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「泪さん……!?
　あなたがなんでここに!?」
source.english:
“Ms. Rui…!?
What are you doing here!?”

target.text: Sakuya was left speechless, and when he hung his head in despondency, somebody poked his arm gently from behind───it was Rui. Even the wine filling the surroundings with a blackish red softened around her, the colouration thinning, and in addition, the woman herself seemed to release a faint light from within, standing out prominently against the dark backdrop.
【Naomasa】 「Rui-san……!? Why are you here!?」

source.japanese:
泪、そんな細かい事には一々答えず、障子戸を睨[にら]みつけた。
　優雅な怠惰を信条とする彼女は、いつものように微笑んでいたけれど、それは上辺だけ。眸には珍しいくらいに怒りを露わにしていた。
source.english:
Rui did not bother answering such trifling questions one by one.
She glared at the sliding door. Elegant indolence was her creed, and she wore her usual smile, but only on the surface. Anger showed in her eyes with a rare openness.

target.text: Rui, caring not in the slightest about something so trifling, glared at the shouji door. This woman had made a religion out of elegant indolence, and she wore a smile on her face as usual, but that was only plastered across the surface. The look in her eyes radiated an unusually intense anger.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「こちゃこちゃと。木っ端役人風情が。
　どこかで聞いた風な賢しら口を、
　よくもまあ垂れ流しにして下さること」
source.english:
“Such petty quibbling.
An insignificant little bureaucrat.
How very freely you regurgitate that borrowed cleverness.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『───なんと───
　そのお声、もしや、姫さま───？
　これは───
　二五六周期以来の───ご光臨』
source.english:
“What… That voice…
Can it be, Your Highness…?
This is… Your first visit
in two hundred and fifty-six cycles…”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『一体今まで何処におわされたのでしょうや……？　陛下にもただ一つの音信もないと伝え聞いております』
source.english: “Where in the world have you been all this time…? We hear that not even His Majesty has received a single word.”

source.japanese:
【老人の声】
『それがこのような草庵に……光栄極まりなき事でございまするがしかし、姫さまをお迎えするにはあまりにむさ苦しい住まい、せめて事前にお声を伝えて下されば花露の一樽なりご用意いたしましたものを』
source.english: “And to this humble retreat… An unparalleled honor, but alas, it is far too squalid a dwelling to receive Your Highness. Had you only sent word beforehand, I could at least have prepared a barrel of flower dew.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───もう少し黙ると言う事、学んだらいかが。本当に口ばかり回る」
source.english: “Might you learn to be a little quieter? Your mouth really never stops.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「So much pointless yammering. And from some petty, pathetic paper-pusher at that. The gall you have to spout such prattle, and all of it reeking of second-hand wisdom regurgitated from your betters.」
【Old man's voice】 『───What in the─── That voice, could it be, Princess───? Goodness─── It has been two hundred and fifty-six cycles since last─── I was graced with your presence.』
【Old man's voice】 『Where in the world might you have been all this time……? If the hearsay is to be believed, not a single communication has reached even His Imperial Majesty.』

【Old man's voice】 『And for you to arrive at such a tiny, thatched hut as mine own……it is an unparalleled privilege and honour, however, this is far too squalid a dwelling to receive a princess, and had you but sent word beforehand, I would have been able to prepare something appropriate, like a cask of flower dew and───!』
【Rui】 「───Perhaps you ought to learn how to hold your tongue for once? Truly, you do nothing but run your mouth.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしだってね、貴方の所になどお邪魔する気など、これっぽっちもなかったの。
　けれど───」
source.english:
“I had not the slightest intention of paying you a visit, you know.
But—”

target.text: 【Rui】 「You see, it is not as though I, personally, feel even the slightest inclination to pay a visit to the likes of your home. However───」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「直さんの事、少し気になりました。
　それで覗いてみれば───
　なんですか、貴方」
source.english:
“I grew a little concerned about Nao.
And when I looked in—what do you
think you are doing?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I grew a little concerned about Nao-san here. Lo and behold, when I went to take a peek─── What is all this supposed to be?」

source.japanese: かつかつと、下は柔い砂底なのにもかかわらず、踵の音高く鳴ったのは彼女の心中の程が音となって現れたか、紫紺のドレスの裾[すそ]も闘魚の鰭[ひれ]のようにはためかせ、縁側に上がるやいなや、ぱん、と高い音で開け放った、胸がすっとするような爽烈な。
source.english: Her heels rang sharply despite the soft sand underfoot, as though her feelings had found expression in sound. The hem of her deep violet dress fluttered like a fighting fish's fins. The moment she stepped onto the veranda, she flung the door open with a crisp crack. A fierce, exhilarating sound.

target.text: Despite the soft layer of sand below them, her heels loudly clicked as she stepped forth, so perhaps the woman's state of mind was being manifested as sound, and the hem of her indigo dress fluttered like fin of a ferocious fighting fish; no sooner than she had stepped up on the engawa did she fling open the entrance with a loud slam, one ringing out with the sort of intensity that vivified the heart.

source.japanese: 沓の留め輪を取るのさえもどかしげ、蹴るように脱ぎはなってから、中を横切るのも一足二足の大股、とすんと座って、また、ぱぁんと、横凪の腕の一閃で払ったのが、やはり小洒落たタイプライターだったが、打ち出し部分から無数の細いコードで繋がれているのが、なにやら妖しい光を湛えた玉だ。
source.english: Even undoing her shoe straps seemed too much delay. She kicked her shoes off, crossed the room in one or two long strides, and sat down with a thump. Then—crack! One horizontal sweep of her arm sent the object flying. A rather stylish typewriter, as expected. Countless fine cords ran from its printing mechanism to a sphere holding a strange light.

source.japanese: 泪のその、一連の所作が鮮やかで、目を奪って、だから朔屋は、タイプライターが海中をふわふわ漂って、ゆらゆらと降りた時になってようやく、室内の様子を見てとったのだった。
source.english: Rui's sequence of movements was so vivid, so arresting, that only when the typewriter drifted through the water and began settling did Sakuya take in the room.

source.japanese: 中は異様な岩戸───などではなく、外見と釣り合って、畳敷きの、朔屋にも馴染みやすいごくごくありふれた居間、丸い卓袱台にも生活臭が漂い、その前にちんまり正座していたのが、この屋の住人声の主、海を葡萄酒にした張本人（正確を期せば張本人できないようだが）の、人とは似ても似つかぬ妖物───これも、などではなく、禿頭で眼鏡、貧相な顔つきの痩せた、ワイシャツの袖[そで]には腕貫、に魚の形した繕[つくろ]いを当ててあるのがやや愛嬌ではあったが、田舎の役場の帳簿係でもやっていそうな年寄りで、さしずめ職場で片付けきれなかった仕事を持ち帰っての残業といった態で、なんともいえない裏ぶれた生活感が滲み出す。
source.english: The room was no uncanny cavern—or anything of the kind. In keeping with the exterior, it was the most ordinary of tatami sitting rooms, one in which even Sakuya could have felt at home; the round low table, too, breathed domestic life. Kneeling primly before it was the master of the house, owner of the voice, culprit behind the sea's transformation into wine (though, strictly speaking, he did not seem to qualify as the culprit): an inhuman apparition bearing no resemblance whatever to a man—or, again, nothing of the kind. He was a bald, bespectacled, scrawny old fellow with a pinched face, sleeve protectors over his shirtsleeves—the fish-shaped patches on them lent him a certain charm—who looked as though he kept the books at some rural town hall and had brought home the work he could not finish at the office; an indescribable air of shabby domesticity seeped from every inch of him.

target.text: Finding even unfastening the straps on her footwear too bothersome, she almost kicked the shoes off, crossed the room in only one, two big strides, plopped down with a heavy thump, and finally swept all away with a sweeping brandish of her arm; it was a chic typewriter after all, but connected to an output slot around the left carriage release lever were innumerable thin cords, all leading to some manner of ball brimming with mysterious light.

The chain of actions were performed so brilliantly by Rui that his gaze was captivated by it, and as a result, it was only after the typewriter had floated through the ocean water and begun its swaying descent that he grasped what the interior looked like.

A queer rock door leading to a cave───was not at all what greeted him; it was entirely harmonious with the exterior, an extraordinarily ordinary living room covered in tatami mats even Sakuya felt easily comfortable being within, the low, round dining table also feeling very lived-in, and sitting snugly before it was the owner of the voice belonging to the resident of the house, the mastermind (strictly speaking, he couldn't really be made out to be the culprit) responsible for turning the ocean into wine, a monster at once similar and foreign to man───

This, too, was not what greeted him, for he was bald and clad in glasses, with a gaunt-looking face, sleevelets at the end of his white shirt, but while the little patch in the shape of a fish sewn on them was rather charming, he was an old man who would look right at home as the bookkeeper of a rural town hall, and one who seemed to be in the middle of working overtime at that, having brought home the work he wasn't able to finish at his place of work: a man dripping with the feeling of an indescribably threadbare, exhausted daily life.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「なんですか、あの、賢しい言い草は。
　あんまりにも腹が立って、つい出てきてしまったじゃない。すべて貴方のせいよ」
source.english:
“What was all that clever talk?
You made me so angry I couldn't help coming out. Entirely your fault.”

source.japanese: 老人の顔には、予想外の貴人を迎えた呆然と驚愕と畏怖とが入り乱れ現れる、にも拘泥せず、卓袱台の向かいに腰を落として泪は、
source.english: Bewilderment, astonishment, and dread mingled on the old man's face at this unexpected noble visitor. Rui paid them no attention. Sitting down across the table, she said—

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしのこの気持ち、
　どう償って下さるおつもり───？」
source.english:
“How do you intend to compensate me
for what you've made me feel?”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「や、それは───姫さま」
source.english: “Well, that—Your Highness…”

source.japanese:
先程までは朔屋に居丈高に出ていた老人が、泪に対してはたじたじで、平伏せんばかりの勢いである。
　その姿、口ぶり、あの魚怪共とまったく同じで、ならばこの年寄りは姿は人間となんら変わりはないが、それでも眷属、一統のうちなのか。
　なんにせよ事態の急転に戸惑う朔屋は、
source.english:
The old man who had lorded it over Sakuya moments ago now faltered before Rui, almost prostrating himself.
His manner and speech were exactly like those fish-monsters'. Though he looked no different from a human being, was he nevertheless one of her kind, one of their company?
Bewildered by the sudden turn, Sakuya said—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あの……泪さん、さっきから訳がわからないんだが……一体どういう状況なんだ、これは───」
source.english: “Excuse me… Ms. Rui, I haven't understood any of this… What exactly is going on?”

source.japanese:
【老人】
「控えろ下郎が！
　貴様の如き毛も鱗[うろこ]もない猿が、口を聞いていい相手ではないわっ。
　こちらにおわしますお方こそ、誰あろう、四海全土を統治せらるる海皇陛下の───」
source.english:
“Silence, wretch!
An ape with neither fur nor scales, such as you, has no right to address her. His Majesty the Sea Emperor rules all the four seas,
and this exalted person is none other than his—”

source.japanese:
途端に朔屋には、また逆捩じに声をきんきん張り上げるのが、やはりどうにも小物臭い。
　海皇だのなんだのは朔屋に窺い知れぬ事であり、あまり心に響かない……ひびか、ない……海皇？　海の？　
　じわじわと、朔屋の胸中に、何事か途方もない驚きが迫りつつある。
　泪がその海皇の、なんだというのか。
source.english:
The way he instantly turned on Sakuya and shrilled at him again had the unmistakable reek of a petty man.
Sea Emperor, whatever that was: beyond Sakuya's knowledge, and it made little impression. Little… impression…
Sea Emperor? Of the sea? A vast astonishment was slowly overtaking Sakuya's heart.
What was Rui to this Sea Emperor?

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───黙るのは貴方。
　いいこと？　もう言いませんよ？
　これ以上煩[うるさ]くするなら───そんなにわたくしを怒らせたいのなら、お話は別だけど」
source.english:
“The one who will be silent is you.
Understand? I won't tell you again.
Unless you want to keep making a noise—unless you want to anger me that much. Then it will be a different conversation.”

source.japanese: 泪が睨[にら]みつけたに、青菜に、いやむしろ意気地のない蛞蝓に塩で、や、その、とかもごもごと身を反らして口ごもり、ただ朔屋へちらりと寄越した眼鏡越しの横目に、主筋の者が何故かくの如き下郎の肩を持つ、といわんばかり不満がありありと。
source.english: At Rui's glare he wilted as if salted—like a green, no, rather like a spineless slug. He drew back, mumbling, “Well… er…,” but the sidelong look he shot Sakuya through his spectacles plainly brimmed with grievance: why should one of his sovereign's own line take the part of such a wretch?

target.text: 【Rui】 「What is with that pretentiously impertinent tone? It was so inordinately offensive to my ears, I ended up making an entrance against my better judgment. The blame for that all lies at your feet.」

A jumble of astonishment, shock, and awe at welcoming the arrival of an unexpected member of royalty showed on the old man's face, but without paying that any particular mind, Rui sat down at the tea table opposite him,
【Rui】 「So having made me feel this way, how do you intend to atone───?」
【Old man】 「No, but that is───Princess.」

Until but a moment ago, the old man had been talking down at Sakuya from atop his high horse, but when faced with Rui, he was flustered, practically about to prostrate himself. His posture, his speech, they were the exact same as what those fish monsters had displayed, so even though this old man's physical shape was no different from that of any ordinary human, he must still have been some sort of retainer, or perhaps part of the same lineage? Regardless of which, Sakuya, left befuddled at the sudden change in the circumstances he found himself in,
【Naomasa】 「Uhmm……Rui-san, I've been completely lost for a while now, but…… what exactly is going on here───」

【Old man】 「Stand back, you lowborn cur! She is not someone that some monkey with neither fur nor scales like your wretched kin may speak to. She who graces us with her august presence is none other than the daughter of His Imperial Majesty the Emperor of the Seas, he who reigns supreme over all the realms of the Seven Seas───」

Just as Sakuya began to speak, he once again snapped back at him with a shrill, twisted screech, screaming out his petty, small-time character for all the world to hear. Sakuya couldn't even begin to guess at who this Emperor of the Seas or whatever he was supposed to be was, and it didn't really strike a chord in him……strike…a chord…… Emperor of the Seas? The seas? Some manner of extraordinary amazement began to slowly well up within Sakuya's bosom. What had he just said that Rui's relation was to this Emperor of the Seas again?

【Rui】 「───You are the one who shall stay their tongue here. Did you hear me? I will not repeat myself again, understood? If you intend to be any more importunately noisy───if you truly desire to anger me so, then it is a different story.」

Faced with Rui's glare, he wilted like leafy greens sprinkled with salt, nay, like a spineless slug shrivelling up, arching his body away and mumbling clipped objections, "no no, that's not what I-", but the sidelong glance sent Sakuya's way through his glasses was full of glaringly obvious dissatisfaction, all but asking why in the world one of the esteemed imperial bloodline would side with such a baseborn churl.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「直さん、これはね、塩辛入道とか、そんな風に呼ばれているモノ」
source.english: “Nao, this is a thing called the Salty Monk, or something of the sort.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「御主筋には火遠理命って言う高位の方もいらしているのだけれど、これはその眷属。古いは古いのだけれどね」
source.english: “Among his superiors is a high-ranking being called Hoori-no-Mikoto. This one belongs to his retinue. He is old, I'll grant him that.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「だからそっちの珠は、潮盈珠の下位のものなのだけど、まあそのあたりの事はどうでもいいわ」
source.english: “So that sphere over there is a lesser form of the Tide-Raising Jewel. But none of that really matters.”

source.japanese:
いかにも取るに足らぬ事、と泪が流したそのあたりの事情が今回の核心なのでは、と思わぬでもない朔屋ではあったけれど、問いの嘴迂闊に挟もうものなら、余計な勘気を蒙[こうむ]りそうな気がして、何度も大人しく頷[うなず]く、ちゃんと聞いていると訴える。
　何時しか朔屋も正座の、きちんと座るのが慣れていないのか、猫背気味で、それでも居ずまいを正させるような気迫が、泪から拡散されていた。
source.english:
Sakuya wondered if the matters Rui so lightly dismissed might not be the very heart of this affair. But sticking his beak in with a question seemed likely to earn him needless displeasure. He nodded obediently, again and again, to show he was listening.
At some point he too had knelt formally. Unaccustomed to the posture, he was a little hunched, yet something radiating from Rui compelled a proper bearing.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「これはね、もうご存じの通り、なにか言えば規則規則の、融通利かない喧[やかま]し屋。陰険で、鱗も剥げて、おまけに浮気性な癖して甲斐性無しだから、奥方にも逃げられて」
source.english: “As you already know, he's an inflexible, noisy creature. Rules, rules, every time you say anything. Sneaky, with his scales peeling off. And a philanderer with nothing to offer, so his wife left him.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「それは……あまりな、言われよう……」
source.english: “That is… an excessively harsh description…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「だって本当の事じゃありませんか。
　なんです、さっきの言い草は。
　意地が悪いったらない」
source.english:
“But it's true, isn't it?
And what was that way of talking just now?
Such extraordinary spite.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「姫さまともあろうお方が、その、盗み聞き……えへんっ、もとい、間諜めいた真似事をなさるとは……」
source.english: “For one such as Your Highness to indulge in eavesdropping—Ahem! Rather, in something resembling espionage…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Nao-san, this man here is what is known as a Shiokara-nyuudou, or something along those lines.」

【Rui】 「The main bloodline counts an esteemed man by the name of Hoori-no-mikoto amongst their number, and this here is one of his retainers. He is, if nothing else, very old.」 (TN: This references Japanese myth. In short, the god Hoori-no-mikoto, having lost his brother's symbol of happiness, a fishing hook, ventures to the palace of the sea god. There he is greeted by the sea god's daughter, Toyotama-hime, and while they eventually find it, the sea god makes Hoori-no-mikoto marry his daughter and stay in the sea. He later returns to shore.)

【Rui】 「Therefore, that ball over there is a low-ranking shiomichi-no-tama, but none of that really matters.」 (TN: The shiomichi-no-tama, written "潮盈珠", the tide-flowing jewel, is also part of the aforementioned myth, and is used by Hoori-no-mikoto in battle against his elder brother, Hoderi-no-mikoto, who had, to make a long story short, attacked Hoori-no-mikoto after being given back his fishing hook.)

Rui had brushed it away like it wasn't even worth talking about, but while there was a part of Sakuya that couldn't help but feel that whatever circumstances were at play there lay at the core of the current predicament, had he carelessly even attempted to voice a question, he felt like he'd only incur more disfavour than was strictly necessary, and so he just nodded meekly over and over, ensuring that she knew he was most certainly listening closely.

At some point, Sakuya had also ended up sitting in a seiza position, and perhaps he just wasn't used to sitting properly, for he had a bit of a hunchback, but even so, a commanding presence emanated from Rui, the sort that compelled him to straighten his posture.

【Rui】 「This man here, as I am sure you are already well aware, is the sort of inflexible, nitpicking caviler who never stops talking about rules this and regulations that. Insidious, his scales have also flaked off, a good-for-nothing scoundrel who also has a bad habit of cheating, and so even his wife abandoned him.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「Now that is……a rather…… harsh way to put it……」
【Rui】 「But it is all the truth, is it not? What was with the way you were talking just earlier? It was the epitome of spitefulness.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「That someone of your august eminence, Princess, would resort to, erm, eavesdropping……ahem, that is, engage in such spy-like conduct, is rather……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お黙りなさい。言葉なんて繕[つくろ]わなくっていいの。
　願った本人がもう要らないと言っているのだから、止めてあげればいいでしょうに」
source.english:
“Be quiet. You needn't dress up the words.
The man who made the wish says he no longer wants it. Why not stop it for him?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「なのにお前と来たら、ねちねちと。
　お前───なにか心得違いをしているのじゃなくて？」
source.english:
“But you go on and on.
Have you misunderstood something?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お前達海のモノと、その行いが、
　人間より尊い、偉いものだと、
　心得違いしているんじゃ───」
source.english:
“Have you begun to imagine that you creatures of the sea,
and what you do, are nobler
and greater than human beings?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Be silent. Do not attempt to cover this up with your words. The very man who made the wish himself claims it is no longer desired, so surely you could simply put a stop to it for him.」
【Rui】 「And then here you are, always so needling and nagging. You───are you not labouring under some fundamental misconception here?」
【Rui】 「The misconception that all of you, those of the ocean, and their conduct, are more noble, distinguished than the humans───」

source.japanese:
───泪の言葉に朔屋は、は、と顔を上げる。その舌鋒鋭きに感じ入ったのもあるが、それ以上に───この老人、見た目こそ小役人だが、こんな海の底で奇怪な機械を操っていた事、朔屋への物言いからして、人とは異なる存在なのだろう。そしてその老人は泪を姫と呼ぶ。泪もまた威をもって抑えつける。
　その泪の唇から述べられた『人間』という言葉の響きは、自分をその枠外に置いているようにしか朔屋に受け取れず、やはり、彼女もまた、人外の───？
source.english:
Sakuya lifted his face sharply at Rui's words. Their cutting force impressed him, but more than that—this old man looked like a petty official, yet operated strange machinery at the bottom of the sea. From his way of speaking to Sakuya, he was probably something other than human. And he called Rui a princess. Rui, in turn, suppressed him with her authority.
When the word 'human' left her lips, Sakuya could only hear it as placing herself outside that category. Then she too was something beyond humanity—?

target.text: ───Upon hearing Rui's words, Sakuya abruptly raised his head. As much as he admired her scathing tongue, there was something more pressing───while this old man's appearance was the spitting image of some petty official, given that he was controlling some mysterious machine here at the bottom of the ocean, together with the way he had spoken to Sakuya, he was surely a being distinct from humankind. And this old man called Rui "princess". And Rui was also keeping him in check through sheer authority.

The way that word "humans" rung as it was spoken through Rui's lips; Sakuya could only interpret it as her placing herself outside of that boundary, so in the end, she, too, was something non-human───?

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「……それのどこに間違いが。
　僭越なれど姫さま、発言させていただきましょう」
source.english:
“…Where is the misunderstanding
in that? Presumptuous though it may be, Your Highness, permit me to speak.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「海皇陛下以下、我ら擬人化概念体、この時空連続体の集合的無意識の為に尽力いたすもの。その義務、その責務」
source.english: “From His Majesty the Sea Emperor down, we personified conceptual entities labor on behalf of the collective unconscious of this spacetime continuum. That is our duty. Our responsibility.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「たとい少しばかり陸地が様変わりいたそうとも、我らの在り様、為すべき事は何も変わりませぬ」
source.english: “Even if the land has altered somewhat, neither what we are nor what we must do has changed.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「ただ時空連続体の集合無意識の法[のり]に従い、その発露するところを正しく、忠実に現象へ反映させる事」
source.english: “We follow only the laws of the spacetime continuum's collective unconscious, faithfully and correctly reflecting its expressions in phenomena.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「この不可侵の責務、なんで妨げる事、許させましょうや？」
source.english: “How can we permit interference with this inviolable responsibility?”

source.japanese: 神妙に、かつ丁重に並べ立てる言葉は、またしても朔屋にはこれっぽっちも理解できぬ言葉ばかり。異次元の原語を駆使されているのと同じである。
source.english: Solemnly and courteously, he laid out yet another array of words Sakuya could not understand in the slightest. He might as well have been wielding the original language of another dimension.

target.text: 【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「……What part of that is mistaken? Presumptuous of me as it may be, Princess, permit me a few words.」

【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「His Imperial Majesty the Emperor of the Seas, and we anthropomorphized conceptual beings, labour tirelessly for the sake of the collective unconsciousness of this space-time continuum. Those duties, and those obligations.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「Even supposing that the land were to undergo a minor metamorphosis, neither our mode of being, nor what we must do, will change in the slightest.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「We merely obey the principles of the collective unconsciousness of the space-time continuum, precisely and faithfully reflecting the expressions of its intent through phenomena.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「How could we then permit any to obstruct this inviolable obligation?」

A speech composed of words both solemn and courteous, and once again, words that Sakuya could not begin to comprehend, not even in the slightest. It was no different than were he spoken to by someone fluent in the language of another dimension.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「はぁ───筋金入りの愚か者。
　直さん、これの言う事、お判り？」
source.english:
“Ah… A fool through and through.
Nao, do you understand what this thing is saying?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いいえ。情けない事に、学生時代不勉強だったもので……」
source.english: “No. I'm ashamed to say I neglected my studies…”

source.japanese: ここで気の利いた受け答えの一つもできれば、この陰険な塩辛なんとかに意趣返しにもなろうし、泪にも株を上げる事ができるかもしれないのだが、生憎朔屋にとって、習わぬ経を読めといわれる方がまだ優しくて、身を縮め、不勉強を詫びるしかなく、この極まりの悪さは、居眠りしていたところ教師に当てられたよりまだひどかった。
source.english: Had he managed one clever answer, he might have paid back this sneaky Salty Something and risen in Rui's estimation too. Unfortunately, for Sakuya, reciting a sutra he had never learned would have been easier. He could only shrink into himself and apologize for his lack of study. It was even more mortifying than being called on by a teacher while asleep.

source.japanese: けれど泪も、始めから朔屋が理解しているなどと毛ほども期待していなかったようで、
source.english: But Rui seemed not to have expected, from the outset, that Sakuya would understand a word.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Haaah───an inveterate imbecile. Nao-san, do you understand what this man is saying?」
【Naomasa】 「No. Pathetic as it is, I did not apply myself much in my student days, and so……」

If only he could have given a clever response here; it would surely have served as a nice bit of revenge against this sly Shiokara-whatever, and perhaps it would also raise his standing in Rui's eyes, but unfortunately, to Sakuya, it would have been kinder had she asked him to recite a sutra he had never studied before; he shrunk into himself, all he could do was apologize for his lack of studying, and the deep mortification he currently felt was even worse than when he had been called upon by a teacher while nodding off in class.
However, Rui, as though she never held even the tiniest of expectations that Sakuya understood,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そうご自分を卑下なさらなくっていいの。
　漢字ばかりだからね、ご大層に聞こえるけれど、要するにこれが言っているのは」
source.english:
“You needn't put yourself down so.
All those ponderous kanji make it sound impressive. What he's saying amounts to this—”

target.text: 【Rui】 「There is no need for such self-deprecation, really. He used a lot of difficult words, so it might sound intimidatingly immense to your ears, but to put it simply, this is what he said.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「昔話。伝説。御伽話。伝承。
　その類の事柄を、この世にばらまいているのは自分達で、だから偉い。だから邪魔なんて許さないと、それだけのこと」
source.english:
“Old tales. Legends. Fairy tales.
Folklore. They are the ones scattering such things through the world, and therefore they are important. Therefore no one may interfere. That's all.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「昔話、御伽話って……」
source.english: “Old tales? Fairy tales…?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Stories of old. Legends. Fairy tales. Folklore. We are the ones who disseminated things of that nature around this world; therefore, we are very important people. That is why we will not permit interference, and that is all there is to it.」
【Naomasa】 「Stories of old, and fairy tales, you say……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「これとその一統の管轄は、
　まあ海なのだけど」
source.english:
“This one and his company have jurisdiction over the sea,
more or less.”

source.japanese: 姫さまもですぞ、という塩辛入道の呟きを無視し、
source.english: She ignored the Salty Monk's mutter of 'As does Your Highness.'

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あちこちにこういうのがいて、船乗り達の怪談やら法螺話やらに、一役買っている。
　ずうっと昔からね」
source.english:
“There are creatures like him here and there, playing their parts in sailors' ghost stories and tall tales.
They have been for a very long time.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「……必要なのです。それら原型が。人類の為に」
source.english: “…Those archetypes are necessary. For humanity.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「そういった原型の強固な守護によって、この時空連続体は存続しているのです。
　我らがなかったのなら、陸の人間風情の脆弱な精神など、なんで保たれましょうか」
source.english:
“This spacetime continuum endures through the steadfast protection of such archetypes.
Without us, how could the feeble minds of mere land-dwellers sustain themselves?”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「融通が利かぬと言うなら、それでいい。
　儂はただ自分の務めを果たしているだけなのです。原型は常にリロードされ、繰り返されなければならない」
source.english:
“Call me inflexible, then.
I am simply doing my duty. Archetypes must constantly be reloaded and repeated.”

source.japanese:
この世界はただ秘密によってのみ存続する。
　そう唱えた哲人は誰だったろう。
　そして、この海の眷属の一人が語る言葉、完全には理解及ばずとも、朔屋の知らざる世界の秘密を開陳しているようにも思われる。
　であれば、そんな秘密を不用意に耳にしては、朔屋の住む世界はこれより崩壊を始めるのではないだろうか。
source.english:
The world persists only through secrets.
Which philosopher had said that? Though Sakuya could not fully understand this member of the sea's retinue,
his words seemed to disclose secrets of a world Sakuya did not know.
If so, might overhearing such secrets carelessly cause the world he lived in to begin collapsing?

source.japanese:
ちぐはぐだった。なにもかも。
　伝説中の住人である筈の塩辛某は、贔屓目に見積もってもそこらの小役人が関の山。
　それが世界の裏面を物語る。
　海の底で潮を酒に替えた、物語の宝珠は、現代の技術に造られた機械に括[くく]られて、座敷の隅に空しく横転している。
source.english:
Everything was mismatched.
The Salty Something, supposedly a creature of legend, looked at best like a petty official one might find anywhere.
And he spoke of the world's hidden side.
A jewel from a story had turned the sea to liquor down here on the seabed, yet it was tethered to a machine made by modern technology, lying uselessly on its side in a corner of the room.

source.japanese: 少女の人形の手足に、熊のぬいぐるみのそれをとりつけたような、どこかちぐはぐで、そして不気味な雰囲気を、朔屋は聞いている。
source.english: Sakuya heard an unsettling incongruity in it all, as though the limbs of a girl's doll had been replaced with those of a stuffed bear.

source.japanese: それは多分、この世界が本来の姿からひどく歪められている事の示唆であり───
source.english: Perhaps it suggested how terribly this world had been twisted from its original form—

source.japanese: 伝説中の住人が操るにしては、ひどく時代を外れた言語である事を朔屋がもし理解したなら、その背後に潜[ひそ]む更なる秘密の深淵に到達し、彼は正気を失ったかも知れない。
source.english: Had Sakuya understood how far out of its proper time this language was for a creature of legend, he might have reached the deeper abyss of secrets behind it—and lost his mind.

source.japanese: 陸より遙かに広大な海[わたつみ]の、いかなる秘密潜[ひそ]ませたもうものか、全容を知るモノ、この世界に、果たしてありやなしや。
source.english: What secrets might the ocean, vaster by far than the land, harbor? Was there, in all this world, any being that knew them entire—or was there not?

source.japanese:
───影が。座敷の影が。朔屋の背後で深まって、蟠る不定形の粘塊となり、己が裡[うち]に取りこもうと、黒々とした触腕を伸ばして背筋にひたひたと触れてくるような。
　青年は知らずそんな戦慄に囚われて、つい肩越しに背後を覗きこんだが、擦り切れ加減の畳の目を見るばかり。
source.english:
Shadows. The room's shadows seemed to deepen behind Sakuya, coiling into a shapeless mass of slime, stretching black feelers to engulf him, softly touching his spine.
Caught unawares by that shudder, Sakuya glanced over his shoulder. He saw only the weave of the worn tatami.

source.japanese: それでも深淵を覗きこんだような不安は拭いきれず、泪に向かう目は救いを求める、迷える学僧の、朔屋にしてはひどく悩ましげな視線だ。
source.english: Yet he could not dispel the unease of having looked into an abyss. His eyes sought salvation in Rui. The gaze of a lost scholar-monk: unusually troubled for Sakuya.

source.japanese:
その視線を受けて泪は、昂然と美しかった。
　それが、朔屋の浮き上がって頼りなく流れそうだった腰をまたすとんと落ち着けた。
　女の美しさには、たとえ世界が揺らごうが明日滅びる事になろうが、そんな懼[おそ]れを癒すほどの、一つの真実が、ある。
source.english:
Meeting that gaze, Rui was proudly beautiful.
It settled Sakuya back onto the floor when he had seemed ready to float helplessly away.
In a woman's beauty there was one truth capable of soothing such fears, even if the world shook, even if it were to perish tomorrow.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Those, and all the rest of their kind are, well, under the jurisdiction of the seas.」
Ignoring Shiokara-nyuudou's muttered "so are you, Princess",
【Rui】 「You will find these things everywhere, taking on roles in the ghost stories and tall tales told by sailors. Ever since long, long ago.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「……They are indispensable. Those archetypes. For the sake of humanity.」

【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「It is through the firm safeguards of said archetypes that this space-time continuum persists. If we did not exist, how could the frail psyches of the likes of the land-dwelling humans possibly endure?」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「If you will call that inflexible, then so be it. I am simply fulfilling my duties. The archetypes must constantly be reloaded, repeated over and over again.」

This world is perpetuated only through secrecy. Now, who was the philosopher who advanced such a theory again? And then, even though he was utterly unable to comprehend the words spoken by one of these kin of the ocean, it still seemed to Sakuya that the secrets of a world he knew nothing of were being unravelled before him. And given that, now that he had carelessly come to hear such secrets, was it not all too possible that the world Sakuya lived in would now begin to crumble down around him?

It was an incoherent mess. Each and every part. This mister Shiokara, supposedly a denizen of legend, amounted to, if he was being charitable, nothing more than some two-bit functionary. And that alone spoke volumes about what lay beneath the surface of the world. At the bottom of the ocean, the precious jewel belonging to fable and myth that had changed seawater to wine was connected by cords to a machine built by modern technology, purposelessly rolling around in the corner of a tatami mat room.
It was disjointed and mismatched, like a little girl doll whose limbs had been replaced with those of a teddy bear; it all had an uncanny feel to it, that was how it sounded to Sakuya's ears.
It was, probably, something suggesting that this world had been horribly warped and twisted from the shape it ought to take───

If Sakuya ever were to grasp that, for language supposedly wielded by a creature of legend, it was terribly anachronistic, he would descend into the abyss of secrets that yet lurked ever deeper behind the scenes, and perhaps he would simply lose his mind.

What manner of secrets lurked in the fathomless sea, vast and boundless in ways no land-bound realms could rival, and were there truly any in this world who knew the full picture painted by their contents?

───The shadows. The shadows cast in this tatami room. They deepened behind Sakuya, forming viscous, amorphous pools that coiled and twined together, their jet-black tentacles steadily encroaching upon his back, as if brushing against him, trying to take him within themselves. Without realizing quite why, the young man was gripped by a shuddering dread thus, and when he couldn't help but peek over his shoulder, all he saw was the mesh of worn-out tatami mats.

Nevertheless, a feeling of anxiety as though he had gazed long into an abyss could not be entirely dispelled, and he turned to Rui, his eyes begging for salvation, like a novice monk lost and confused, an awfully apprehensive gaze for a man like Sakuya.

On the receiving end of this gaze, Rui was brimming with confidence and beauty. And that was what made Sakuya's behind, already floating in the air and about to be helplessly swept away, sink to the floor once more with a solid thump. Even should the world be shaken into instability or be brought to ruin on the morrow, within a woman's beauty lies a truth so profound it can soothe even the greatest dread.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ふぅん。だから、こんな海のただ中で、直さん達のお船を動けなくして？」
source.english: “I see. And that's why you've stranded Nao and his shipmates in the middle of the sea?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Hmmm. And so that is why you have made Nao-san and company's ship unable to sail forth, leaving it stuck in the middle of this ocean?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「はあ……馬鹿馬鹿しくって。
　お話にもならない。
　本末転倒の見本でしかないわ、こんなのは。
　このままなら、直さん達は全滅。
　誰も何が起こったのか、
　知る者とていなくなる」
source.english:
“Oh… How ridiculous.
It's beneath discussion.
A perfect example of mistaking means for ends.
Go on like this and Nao's entire company will die.
No one will remain
who knows what happened.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お前は得意がっているようね。
　でも。伝える者さえいないお話に、なんの意味があるというの？」
source.english:
“You seem so pleased with yourself.
But what meaning can a story have when no one remains to tell it?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「だいたいね、お話なんて、それこそ世に連れ人に連れ、よ。
　残るものは語り継がれるし、そうでないものは忘れ去られていくだけ」
source.english:
“Besides, stories change with the world and its people.
Those that endure are passed on. The others are simply forgotten.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Haah……what absurdity. That is completely out of the question. An exemplar of putting the cart before the horse and nothing more. As things stand, Nao-san and the rest will all perish. Whatever occurred by whose hands, not a soul will remain who knows.」
【Rui】 「You seem to still be puffed up with pride over it all, indeed. However. What possible significance can you claim there to be in a tale that does not even have any to tell it?」

【Rui】 「First and foremost, you understand, tales are shaped by the world and the people who live in it. Those that remain are handed down from generation to generation, and those that are not are merely forgotten and left behind by time.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「その証拠に、直さん、ごらんなさいこれを。
塩辛入道なんてしょぼくれた物の怪、直さん、貴方聞いたことがあって？」
source.english:
“For proof, Nao,
look at this. Had you ever heard of a shabby monster called the Salty Monk?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いえ……全然」
source.english: “No… Never.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「And as proof of my claims, Nao-san, take a good look at that thing. Dear, have you ever heard of this pathetic excuse for a yokai who goes by Shiokara-nyuudou?」
【Naomasa】 「No……not a word.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でしょう。なのにこれと来たら、自分の延命を図りたいばっかりに、こうして機会を捉えては、海の底で悪さしているの。
　小狡いって言ったらない」
source.english:
“Exactly. Yet this thing, solely to prolong his own existence, seizes every opportunity to make mischief at the bottom of the sea.
Cunning little wretch.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「……姫さまは、永の年月彷徨ううちに、陸地に、人間に染まりつつあるご様子だ……」
source.english: “…Your Highness seems to have grown tainted by the land, by humanity, through your long years of wandering…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Quite. And yet, all this creature wants to do is plot to extend his own life, and so he lurks thus at the bottom of the ocean, waiting until he can grasp an opportunity to set his wicked schemes into motion. As crafty as they come.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「……Princess, during these long months and years you have spent wandering, you appear to have been tainted by the land, by humanity……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「違うわね。いい加減に覚えなさい。
　お前達があって人の世があるのではないの。
　人の世があるから、貴方達があるの」
source.english:
“Wrong. Learn it at last.
The human world does not exist because you do. You exist
because the human world does.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「まったく、もう。いつからこんな風になってしまったのかしら。自分達が海を護っているなんて、とんだ恥さらしな勘違い」
source.english: “Honestly. When did you become like this? To imagine yourselves protectors of the sea—what a shameful delusion.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お前、少し省みなさい。
　いつからお前の持ち物は、そんな機械なんてつけるようになったのか。
　そしてそれは、
　誰から与えられたものなのか」
source.english:
“Reflect a little.
When did that possession of yours acquire such
a machine?
And who gave it to you?”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「それは───！
　否、違う、我らは初めに在りし時よりこうだった……！」
source.english:
“That—! No,
you're wrong. We have been this way from the beginning…!”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Incorrect. It is about time that you remember. The world of man does not exist by dint of your existence. Because the world of man exists, so do you.」
【Rui】 「Dear, oh dear. When did things end up this way, I wonder? That you are the ones who protect the ocean, of all the things, what an inconceivably disgraceful misconception.」

【Rui】 「Reflect a little upon your conduct, you. Since when was it, exactly, that your property there became connected to a machine like that? And then, think on who exactly it was that it was bestowed upon you by.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「That is───! No, that is wrong, we have ever been this way, since the very first moment of our existence……!」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「本当に？
　まあ、いいのよそれは、どうでも。
　いい加減に無駄話にも飽きちゃったわ」
source.english:
“Really?
Well, never mind that. It doesn't matter.
I'm tired of idle talk.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Truly? Well, that is fine then, it matters not a whit. I am fed up with even this idle chatter.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お前に命じます。
　さっさと元に戻しなさい。
　一切の曲解は許さないから」
source.english:
“I command you.
Put it back at once.
I will permit no distortion of what I mean.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「……儂の存在を懸けても……、
　それは……受諾しかねる……」
source.english:
“…Even at the cost of my existence…
I cannot… accept that…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I command you. Return things as they were this instant. I will not permit any misconstructions whatsoever.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「……Even if I must stake my very existence……, that would be…… difficult to approve……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ふぅん……お前の奥様、今は確か───
　ブルネイの沖に……、
　御住まいだったかしら？」
source.english:
“Hmm…
Your wife lives off Brunei now,
if I remember correctly?”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「ちょっ……何故それを。
　いや、今は話に関係無い───」
source.english:
“Wha—How do you know that? No,
it's irrelevant—”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Hmmmm……your wife, if I remember rightly─── she is currently residing……, in the coastal waters near Brunei, I believe?」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「Wai-……how do you know that? No, that has no relation to our current discu───」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お前の浮気のお相手、奥様の妹君だっていう事、奥様はご存知なのかしら……？」
source.english: “Does your wife know that your lover is her younger sister…?”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「ひ、ひひ、姫さまっ!?」
source.english: “Y-y-y-Your Highness!?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I do find myself wondering, would your wife happen to be aware that the person you're having a clandestine liaison with is none other than her younger sister……?」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「P-, P-P-, PRINCESS!?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「なんです、ひきつけでも起こしたみたいに、
　わたくしを呼ばないで」
source.english:
“What is it? Don't call me as though
you're having a seizure.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「よもやまさかああそんな、奥に密告されるおつもりでは……」
source.english: “Surely surely aaah you don't intend to inform my wife…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「What is it, and please do not call out for me as though you are having a seizure.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「Don't tell me, surely you don't intend to inform my wife……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしが言わなくっても、そんなのいつか知れるところになるでしょうね。
　速いか遅いかの違いはあっても」
source.english:
“Even if I say nothing, she'll learn eventually.
Sooner or later.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「泪さん、あなたって人は……」
source.english: “Ms. Rui, you really are…”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「お、仰せの通りに。
　この海域の状態、直ちに復元させていただきます。はい、それはもう可及的速やかに」
source.english:
“A-as you command.
I shall restore this region of sea at once. Yes, with all possible speed.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Even should I not be the one to tell her, she will surely come to know of it at some point. It is merely a question of how soon it will be.」
【Naomasa】 「Rui-san, you are unbelievable……」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「A-, as you command. The condition of these waters will be restored to normal right away. Yes, and it will be done as soon as possible!」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしたちがお船に戻るまでに、済ませるのよ？　そうでないとわたくし、奥様の妹君の方にも───貴方が、実は花柳病にお悩みだっていう事、うっかり口が滑ってしまうかも」
source.english: “Finish before we return to the ship, won't you? Otherwise I might let slip to your wife's younger sister, too, that you are in fact suffering from a venereal disease.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It will be done before we return to the ship, yes? If that is not the case, your wife's younger sister ───may perhaps discover that you are troubled by certain afflictions of the venereal variety through a careless slip of my tongue.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そのお年にして、ますます御盛んなご様子。
　大変結構ですこと」
source.english:
“Ever more vigorous at your age, it seems.
How very admirable.”

source.japanese:
【塩辛入道】
「ご猶予を！
　何卒しばしのご猶予ををを!!」
source.english:
“Give me time!
Please, just a little tiiime!!”

target.text: 【Rui】 「My, what vigour for one your age. How absolutely delightful.」
【Shiokara-nyuudou】 「A DEFERMENT! MERCY, I IMPLORE YOU FOR JUST A MOMENT'S GRACE!!」

source.japanese:
何やら必死の形相で珠を操作しだした塩辛入道の、長屋を後にしての道すがら。海上へと戻る海の中───葡萄酒の濃度は徐々に薄れつつあるようだった。
　ぽつりと、泪が呟いた。
source.english:
The Salty Monk was desperately operating his jewel as they left his shabby tenement. On the way back up through the sea, the wine seemed gradually to be thinning.
Rui murmured—

target.text: They were on their way back again, having left behind Shiokara-nyuudou's long, narrow house, the yokai in question operating his jewel with a rather desperate look on his face for whatever reason. While they travelled through the ocean back towards the surface─── the concentration of the wine also seemed to dilute little by little. Rui muttered a few words.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……さっきは、あのお爺ちゃんにああは言ったけれど。
　本当はどうなのかしらね」
source.english:
“…I said all that to the old fellow.
But I wonder what the truth is.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……Earlier, I spoke quite confidently to that old man. But I do wonder what truly happened.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「誰が、そうしむけたの？
　一体どなたが、物語の住人達を時代の向こうから引きずり出して、伝承、伝説の為に奉仕させるようにしたのかしら」
source.english:
“Who set things up that way?
Who dragged the inhabitants of stories out of their own time, and made them serve folklore and legend?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Who was it that pushed them into it? Whoever could it be that dragged out the denizens of stories from their ages past, then arranged matters so they would be put to use in service of ancient tales and legends?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「伝承、神話、そういったものが生きている世界。直さん、それはね。言い方を替えれば、檻のようなもの」
source.english: “A world where folklore and myth are alive. Nao, put another way, that is rather like a cage.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そういったものに縋[すが]ることによってしか、心の平穏を保てない世界」
source.english: “A world that can keep its peace of mind only by clinging to such things.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Tales, myth, a world wherein such things are living and breathing. Nao-san, a world like that, you see. Were I to rephrase that, it would be something akin to a cage.」
【Rui】 「A world that, only through depending on such things, can keep its peace of mind.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「この世界はきっと───そういう心の檻によって覆われているんでしょうよ」
source.english: “Surely this world is covered by cages of the mind like those.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「僕には、やっぱりよく判らない……。
　ただいずれにしても、泪さん、あなたも、
　あの老人と同じようなものなのか」
source.english:
“I still don't really understand…
But in any case, Ms. Rui,
are you something like that old man too?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「This world is surely─── confined within that sort of cage of the mind.」
【Naomasa】 「At the end of the day, I just don't really understand it……. But regardless of what or who it is, Rui-san, you are also something similar to that old man, I guess?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そういうことになるのでしょうよ」
source.english: “That would seem to be the case.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃあ、あなたの正体って言うのは……。
　いや、いい。泪さんが来てくれたお陰で助かったんだから、つまらない詮索は止めにしておきます」
source.english:
“Then your true identity is… No.
Never mind. You saved me by coming here, Ms. Rui. I'll stop my pointless prying.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I suppose that is how things stand, yes.」
【Naomasa】 「Then, your true identity would be……. No, it's fine. It's all thanks to you coming here for me that I live to see another day, so I'll put a lid on any tasteless prying here.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「女の正体をあれこれしない方って、好きよ。
　でも、そうね……わたくしの名前。
　お暇な時にでも、
　舌に転がしてごらんなさい」
source.english:
“I like a man who doesn't pry into a woman's identity.
But, yes… My name.
When you have a moment,
try rolling it around on your tongue.”

source.japanese:
泪───彩久津泪、いろくづ・るい。
　白状してしまえば朔屋は、『いろ』は『色気』の『いろ』と同じ音であるし、だし『くづ』は『屑』に通じているようで、彼女の多淫な事と相俟って、随分と露骨な名前だと折に触れそう感じていたのだけれど、もっと他の意味があるようで、探り当てようとするかに朔屋の見つめ直した泪は、復調しつつある海水の中で、どこか遠い眼差しを海の奥へ向けていた。
source.english:
Rui. Rui Irokuzu.
To confess the truth, Sakuya had sometimes thought it a remarkably blatant name. Iro sounded like the iro in iroke—sex appeal—and kuzu suggested trash. Together with her abundant lust, that seemed plain enough. But apparently it meant something else. Looking at her again, as though to discover that meaning, Sakuya found Rui gazing distantly into the depths of the recovering sea.

target.text: 【Rui】 「I do prefer men who do not poke around everywhere trying to figure a woman out. But, right……my name. When you have a spare moment, do try rolling it around atop your tongue.」

Rui───彩久津泪, Irokudzu Rui. If Sakuya were to make a confession, the『Iro』was pronounced the same as the『Iro』from『Sex appeal』, and the『Kudzu』seemed similar to the『Kuzu』from 『Trash』, and when coupled with the woman's lechery, he had, from time to time, caught himself thinking that it was an awfully unsubtle name, but surely there had to be another meaning hidden within; when Sakuya once more fixed his gaze upon Rui like he was trying to find it, there she stood amidst the waters gradually regaining their usual form, facing the depths of the ocean with a somewhat distant look in her eyes.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ただ、わたくしはもうずっとずっと昔に、
　あの方たちとは別れました。
　そして、もう戻るつもりも、ないの」
source.english:
“But I parted from those people a very,
very long time ago.
And I have no intention of returning.”

source.japanese:
朔屋には、人の心の機微に鈍[にぶ]い、気づきにくいというだけで、共感の情動というのが皆無なわけではけしてない。むしろどちらかといえばこの男、お人好しで感じ入りやすい方なのだ。
　気鬱の時はそれがなおさら。そして少しばかりは人の心の襞[ひだ]を覗く眼力も持ち合わせるようになる。
source.english:
Sakuya was slow to notice the subtleties of other people's hearts, but that did not mean he lacked empathy altogether. If anything, he was a softhearted man, easily moved. More so when depressed.
At such times he even acquired a little ability to peer into the folds of another's heart.

source.japanese:
今の朔屋に泪は。
　その、元の世界だったという、たとえこの海域ではないにせよ、繋がっている海の中、赤や紫が薄れ往く潮の中は、黄昏の天地の間と同じ色合い、渺漠とした平原に佇んで、経巡ってきたその上に思いを馳せる人の寂寥で、肉付き麗しい肩もその背も儚げに、古い昔と変わってしまった今の世の有様に哀しく戸惑う様の人に見えた。
　懐かしい過去を共に知るモノ達はあれど、その輪の中には帰れない、否、帰らない。
　自ら望んだ境涯であっても、遠ざかっていく過去を、懐かしい世界を、惜しむ心はどうしても倦まれ出ずる悩み。
source.english:
To Sakuya then, Rui seemed a woman standing in what had once been her world—not in this stretch of sea, perhaps, but in waters joined to it. As the reds and purples drained from the tide until it wore the color of the space between earth and sky at twilight, she stood as lonely as a traveler upon a boundless plain, looking back over all the country she had crossed: her beautifully rounded shoulders and back somehow frail, her figure sadly bewildered by the world of now, so altered from the world long ago.
There were beings still who shared her memories of that beloved past, yet she could not return to their circle. No—would not. Even when one's lot was freely chosen, the heart could not help grieving for the receding past, the familiar world; such sorrow would always rise anew.

source.japanese:
もちろん朔屋の思い込み、というのが一番ありそうなところだ。
　泪は性の快楽を一番の共連れに、札遊びの刺激を沓にして、華やかで退廃的な、男と女の破滅を眺め続けてきた貴婦人。
　記憶が勝手に美化する過去より、訪れる事が決まりきっている未来より、千変万化の現在のみをただ愛する。過去などは影の形なりに足を重くする、古い服のようなものなのかも知れない。
source.english:
Of course, the likeliest explanation was that Sakuya imagined it all.
Rui was a lady who had watched men and women destroy themselves in glittering decadence, with sexual pleasure as her closest companion and the excitement of cards for shoes.
Rather than a past beautified by memory, rather than a future certain to arrive, she loved only the endlessly changing present. Perhaps the past was merely old clothing, weighing down her steps in the guise of a shadow.

source.japanese:
それでも、と朔屋は、潮の流れに、またあの時のように流れを豊かに増して、その輪郭を縁飾りのように揺らぐ泪の髪を眺めつ、思う。彼女はあの老人の事をあそこまで怒したけれど、それはかつての姿を知るからこその失望なのではないだろうか。
　彼女が知っていたという、本来の、人間の心性から零れるように産まれて、人間によって名前を得てからは、彼ら自身がその受け皿になっていた、御伽話、伝説中の住人達。往時の姿を知って、現在の有様に我慢できないというのは、彼女は過去を愛していたと、そういう意味にならないか。
source.english:
Even so, Sakuya thought, watching Rui's hair grow flowing and abundant in the current again, rippling about her outline like ornamental trim. Had she been so angry with the old man precisely because she knew what he once had been? Disappointment in someone she remembered?
The inhabitants of fairy tales and legends as she had known them: born as though spilling from the human mind, then named by humans, and becoming vessels for them in turn. If she knew their former appearance and could not bear what they had become, did that not mean she loved the past?

source.japanese:
それ以上は、朔屋には判らない。
　判らないけれど、数歩先に進む泪が薄赤い潮の中のきらきらした小泡の中、なんだかひどく遠い人のように思えて、その背なへ伸ばした手で、朔屋は何をするつもりだったのだろう。
　かき抱くつもりだったのか。手を取るつもりだったのか。
　ただ手は伸びきらず、前に差し出された形で中途半端な形で留まって。
　一度・二度、と肌を重ねては、もう畏[おそ]れがどうのとは言ってもいられまい。その華やかな頽廃と、濃やかな情愛には惹かれるところない、といっては自分自身にも泪にも聞き苦しい嘘となる。
source.english:
Beyond that, Sakuya did not know.
Yet Rui, walking a few paces ahead among the sparkling bubbles in the pale red water, seemed terribly far away. What had he intended with the hand he reached toward her back?
To embrace her? To take her hand? It never extended fully,
but stopped in an awkward gesture before him.
Having lain with her once, twice, he could hardly go on speaking of fear. To claim that her glittering decadence and rich affection held no attraction would be an ugly lie, to himself as much as to Rui.

target.text: 【Rui】 「However, I have already parted from those people, and since long, long ago at that. And now, I no longer have any intention of returning.」

Sakuya was a man insensitive to the subtleties of the heart, but he was only poor at picking up on them, for it was certainly not at all the case that he was bereft of feelings of sympathy or empathy. Instead, if anything, this man was a credulous, sensitive soul who was easily moved by the circumstances of others. All the more so when he suffered from depression. And he had also begun to develop just a touch of the insight needed to peer into the creases of the human heart.

To Sakuya right now, Rui was. Within what must have been her former world, even if it were not these particular waters, she was in the great oceans connected to it, in brine of fading reds and purples, the very same hue as the boundary between the firmament and the earth at dusk, with the desolation of one who stands on an illimitable plain while letting their thoughts travel back across every road they have trod, her beautifully plump shoulders and back ephemeral; she looked to him like a woman miserably bewildered at the state of the world of today, so unrecognizably transformed from the distant past.

While there are those who shared in her experiences of those fondly-remembered halcyon days, she could never return to that world, nay, she refused to return. Though this lot in life is one she herself desired, the past drifting ever further away, that nostalgic world; the heart within her that yet clings to it all inevitably gives rise to an anguish born of weariness.

Of course, it seemed most likely of all that these were nothing but Sakuya's subjective assumptions. Rui and the worldly pleasures of the flesh were inseparable companions, with the thrill of playing cards serving as the stepping-stone, a noblewoman ever admiring the elegantly decadent downfall of man and woman from the sidelines. Rather than the past painted in rosy hues by memory unbidden, rather than the future whose arrival is but a foregone conclusion, she simply loved the ever-changing present alone. Perhaps the past was like an old garment to her, burdening her step and clinging to her as a shadow does to its shape.

Even so, Sakuya, gazing at Rui's hair playing in the tidal drift, richer and fuller within the current, just like back then, its contour wavering like the frills on a dress, thought. She grew so intensely angry with that old man, but was that not actually disappointment wrought precisely because she knew what he once had been?

The beings she knew, originally born as if spilling out from the overflowing nature of mankind itself, they who, once bestowed a name by humankind, themselves became receptacles for that very human nature, the inhabitants of fairy tales, of legend. If her inability to tolerate his present state arose from knowing what he used to be in bygone days, could that not also imply that she loves the past?

That was as far as Sakuya's understanding went. He wasn't really sure why, but as Rui moved a few steps ahead, gliding through the glittering bubbles in the pale-red tide, she seemed to him impossibly distant, and what was it exactly Sakuya intended to accomplish by stretching his hand out towards that back of hers?

Would he hug her tight? Would he take her by the hand? But his hand never fully reached out, simply lingering half-stretched before him, frozen in an unfinished gesture. Having shared in physical intimacy not once but twice, he could no longer rely on fear as an excuse. If he claimed to feel no attraction to her gorgeous degeneracy and tender passions, it would make for a lie so flimsy it would sound intolerable to Rui and himself alike.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そう……なんにしても、
　来てくれて有難う、泪さん」
