source.english:
“Yes… Whatever else,
thank you for coming, Ms. Rui.”

source.japanese: それでも、やはりどうしても、手を伸ばしきれなくって、言葉だけが、海の中で小泡とともに立ち上る。小泡、弾けて、感謝する気持ちに嘘はないのに、空々しく見せてしまうのが厭[いと]わしかった。
source.english: Still he could not quite reach out. Only his words rose through the sea with little bubbles. They burst. His gratitude was sincere, and he hated that the bubbles seemed to make it look empty.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Is that so……but all the same, I'm grateful that you came, Rui-san.」

And yet, no matter how he tried, he just could not reach out to her with that hand, and it was only mere words accompanied by bubbles that rose up through the ocean water. The little bubbles popped, and though his feelings of gratitude were no lie, he loathed how insincere they sounded to him.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どういたしまして───なんて。
　ふふっ。今日の直さんはずいぶんと御神妙で、それはそれで味だけど」
source.english:
“You're welcome—or something like that. Hehe.
You're so solemn today, Nao. It has its own charm, but…”

source.japanese:
やや振り向いて少し身をかがめ、足を止めて、朔屋が追いつくのを、赤色が褪せて解けいき、差し込み始めた日の光の中で待つ姿。
　古い絵葉書の、街角の写真の中で笑みかける穏やかな服の女。乳房や脚ばかりを強調する娼婦とばかり寝てきた船員が、何故か買ってしまって、夜ごとに取り出して、思春期の少年のような憧れをもって眺めるような、床しく親しい、優しい稠密さを教えてくれる女。
　今の泪はそんな柔らかな美しさを見せていて、それが、するりと。
source.english:
She turned a little, inclined her body, and stopped to wait for Sakuya in the sunlight beginning to enter as the red dissolved away.
A quietly dressed woman smiling from a street-corner photograph on an old postcard: a sailor accustomed only to whores flaunting breasts and legs might inexplicably buy that card, take it out each night, and gaze with tender, youthful longing at the woman who taught him something of intimate fullness. Rui wore that gentle beauty now.
Then, smoothly—

target.text: 【Rui】 「And you are very welcome─── but I jest. Huhu. You are awfully meek today, Nao-san, and while that does have its own appeal.」

Looking slightly over her shoulder, body slightly stooped over, she had stopped walking, waiting for Sakuya to catch up, bathing in the rays of the sun that had begun to shine through the fading, dissolving reds.

A woman on an old picture postcard, dressed in modest clothing and smiling at you from a street corner. A sailor, the sort who'd only ever sleep with prostitutes who flaunted their tits and legs, for some reason wound up buying that postcard, and he would take it out every night, staring at it with the yearning of a pubescent boy: a woman who taught him what a vaguely nostalgic affection, a gentle intimacy, truly felt like. That was the tender beauty that Rui showed in that moment, and then, it all slipped away effortlessly.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ちょっとつまらないから、ばらしちゃお。
　ほんとはね、あなたの様子が気になったからじゃあなかった」
source.english:
“It's a little dull, so I'll let the secret out.
I didn't actually come because I was concerned about you.”

source.japanese: 口ではそんな、つれない事を言いながら、なのに。朔屋の腕を取って、横に寄り添って、遅くもない、早過ぎもない、共歩きを幸せにする歩度に、歩き出す。
source.english: Unkind words. Yet she took Sakuya's arm, came close beside him, and began walking at a pace neither slow nor too quick: a pace that made walking together a joy.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「泪さん……」
source.english: “Ms. Rui…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It is getting a little boring, so I suppose I will spill the secret. You see, the truth is, it was not actually because I was concerned about you at all.」

She said such cold, unkind things with her mouth, and yet. She took Sakuya's arm in hers, and side by side, she began walking at a pace not slow, not too quick, but just right for the joy of walking together.
【Naomasa】 「Rui-san……」

source.japanese:
なあに、と迎える無言の笑みは、それは錯覚なのかも知れない、けれど、優しい恋人のように。
　腕に寄り添う乳房も、腹の柔味も、この時は官能よりも、朔屋の鬱を包む、穏やかな優しさを伝えてくるのである。
source.english:
What is it? Her silent smile welcomed him. Perhaps it was an illusion, yet she seemed a tender lover.
Even the breast against his arm, the softness of her belly, conveyed not so much sensuality now as a quiet kindness wrapping about his gloom.

source.japanese:
肉、肉の快楽と泪は言う。
　熔けてくずれて流れるようなが好き、と媚毒に爛[ただ]れるような喘[あえ]ぎで囁く。
　けれども、と朔屋は少しく意外な、いや、これもまた泪なのだと思うのだ。
　彼女は、こういった肌身と穏やかな優しさも知っているのだろうと。
　夜の娼婦ではない。黄昏の恋人としても在れる、そんな夢の女。
source.english:
Flesh, the pleasures of flesh:
that was what Rui spoke of. She liked it melting, crumbling, flowing, she whispered in gasps as though inflamed with an aphrodisiac poison.
Yet Sakuya found this a little unexpected.
No, this was Rui too. She must also know this kind of closeness, this gentle kindness.
Not a whore of the night. A dream woman who could also be a lover at twilight.

target.text: What is it, she asked wordlessly with a smile, and perhaps he was simply hallucinating, however, it looked like the gentle smile of a lover. The breast nestled against his arm, and the soft feeling of her stomach: in this moment, it was not carnal, but rather conveyed a gentle tenderness, one that enveloped Sakuya's depression within itself.

Flesh, the pleasure of the flesh, Rui had said. She loved how she melted and crumbled and drifted apart in its wake, so she had whispered in moans festering with seductive toxins. However, Sakuya thought to himself with a touch of surprise; no, this, too, was also part of who Rui was. She must also be acquainted with this kind of intimate, gentle warmth of bodily closeness, he thought. Not just as some harlot of the night. But as a woman right out of a dream, one who could also be as a lover at twilight.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あのお爺ちゃんが撒いたこの葡萄酒。
　ブルゴーニュの風味で、
　もちろんこれはこれで良いものよ。
　でもね。わたくしの好みは、
　南部はカオールで造ったワインなの」
source.english:
“This wine the old fellow spread about has the flavor of Burgundy.
Of course,
it's quite good in its way.
But my preference is for wine made in Cahors,
in the south.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「This wine, sprinkled about by that old man. It has the taste of Bourgogne, and of course, that is perfectly fine in its own right. But you see. When it comes to wines, my taste runs to those made in Cahors in the south.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そちらの味がしなかったから、
　ちょっとご注文をつけさせていただくつもりで、降りてみました───がっかりした？」
source.english:
“Since it didn't taste like
that, I came down to place a little order. Disappointed?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あなたって言う人は、
　やっぱり───綺麗な人だなあ」
source.english:
“…You really
are… a beautiful woman.”

source.japanese:
失望させるような言葉のくせに、腕に寄り添う泪がそれを口にすると、恋人同士の愛らしい、口の意地悪にしか聞こえない、それは恋の遊戯と変わりない。
　なにせ泪はこの時、信天翁号に上がるまで、こうして朔屋から身を離さず、なんとも穏やかなやり方で、肌の温みをずっと朔屋に置いていたのだ。たかだか数時間前の、あの退嬰的な交わりの後で、こんな柔かく優しい近しさを示されては───青年の胸が、ただの獣欲に根ざすものとは別のときめきを得たって仕方がない。
source.english:
The words ought to have disappointed him. Yet spoken by Rui as she nestled against his arm, they sounded only like a lover's sweet little cruelty, no more than the play of love.
Until they climbed aboard the Albatross, she never once drew away from Sakuya, but went on leaving the warmth of her flesh against him in that quiet, gentle fashion. Only hours after their decadent union, such soft and tender intimacy could hardly fail to make his heart thrill with something rooted in more than animal lust.

source.japanese: だから朔屋は、この泪との共歩きがあったから、いくらかは気分に張りをもって信天翁号に戻れた、行く時とは比べものにならない心の平穏をもって戻れた。
source.english: And so, because of this walk with Rui, Sakuya returned to the Albatross with a little renewed spirit, with a peace of mind incomparable to what he had known on the way down.

source.japanese: ───まあそれも、結局は上甲板に上がるまでなのだから、せいぜい潮に浸かっているうちに愉[たの]しんでおくがいいさ、っけ！───
source.english: —Well, that only lasts until you reach the upper deck anyway. Enjoy it while you're still soaking in the sea. Hah!—

source.japanese:
……今のは、朔屋の幻覚である。泪は気づきもしなかったから。
　信天翁号に上がる直前、空から落ちて海面を破り、もがいていた誰かが吐いた毒である。
　───上甲板に上がって朔屋は、毒づいた人物の正体を知る事になる。朔屋は海中にあって、未来の自分を幻視したのだった。
source.english:
That was Sakuya's hallucination. Rui had not noticed it at all.
Just before they climbed aboard the Albatross, someone had fallen out of the sky, broken the sea's surface, and thrashed about, spitting that venom.
On the upper deck, Sakuya would discover who had spoken. Down in the sea, he had glimpsed a vision of his future self.

target.text: 【Rui】 「And since it didn't taste of those, I decided to make my way down with the intent of placing a little order───have I disappointed you?」
【Naomasa】 「……Honestly, I don't know where to even begin with you, but─── you really are a beautiful woman.」

Despite being remarks that seemed apt to induce disappointment in him, when Rui put that into words while snuggling into his arm, it only sounded to him like the teasing cruelty of barbs shared between playful lovers, no different from any of love's other little games. At any rate, until they climbed back aboard the Albatross, Rui remained attached to Sakuya's body thus, leaving the warmth of her skin lingering on Sakuya's in such a gentle manner.

It had only been mere hours since they had finished that degenerate intercourse of theirs, and that he was now being shown such a soft, affectionate intimacy was───it was inevitable that, within the young man's bosom, a different throbbing of the heart, one that did not merely have its roots in animal desires, began to pound away.
Therefore, because Sakuya had thus shared that walk with Rui, he was able to return to the Albatross feeling more composed, with a peace of mind incomparable to when he'd set out.
───Well, that'll only last until you're back up on the deck anyway, so make sure you really savour that feeling while you're still soaking in the tide, got that!?───

……That just now was a hallucination of Sakuya's mind. Rui hadn't noticed it at all. Just before he began to climb aboard the Albatross, it fell from the skies and breached the ocean surface, poison spewed by someone frantically squirming and flailing. ───Having climbed back up to the upper deck, Sakuya came to realize the true identity of who had cursed so bitterly at him. For while he was in the sea, he had seen a vision of none other than his future self.

source.japanese:
そして潮の流れも色も通常に復しつつある波の間に間、信天翁号の上では。
　朔屋に対しての論功行賞の真っ最中であった───
　船に揚がって、『真珠』の効用か、深く染みこみはせず、船員服の上で細かな粒に弾かれる、赤葡萄酒の滴をぱんぱん払い落としている間にも、朔屋の為した事が船内に知れ渡っていたのである。
source.english:
Meanwhile, aboard the Albatross, amid waves whose currents and color were returning to normal—
they were in the very midst of dispensing rewards for Sakuya’s distinguished service.
Even as he climbed aboard and slapped the droplets of red wine from his sailor’s uniform—thanks, perhaps, to the “pearl,” they had not soaked in but stood in tiny beads upon the cloth—word of his deeds was spreading throughout the ship.

target.text: And so, atop the Albatross, floating between the waves gradually returning to normalcy in both hue as well as current. It was right in the middle of the conferral of honours upon Sakuya for his meritorious service─── After he had climbed back aboard the ship, even while he brushed off the droplets of wine rolling around atop his clothes, and perhaps it was a benefit of that『Pearl』, for it had not seeped deeply inside the fabric, the word of Sakuya's achievement was being spread all throughout the ship.

source.japanese:
すなわち。
　舳先の棒に立たされ、皆から罵声を浴びせかけられている最中であった。
　海賊時代を髣髴とさせた。
　青年を責め立てる文句も、古式よろしく伝統を踏まえていた。
source.english:
That is to say:
he had been made to stand on the bowsprit while everyone shouted abuse.
It recalled the age of piracy.
The cries with which they assailed him observed ancient tradition too.

target.text: In other words. He was made to stand atop the bowsprit, in the middle of being showered with jeers and abuse. It was a scene that evoked the age of pirates. The words of blame and reproach hurled at the young man also honoured tradition, carried out in the proper, classical manner.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「飛～～べっ！」
source.english: “Juuump!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「JUUU～～MP!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「飛～～べっ！」
source.english: “Juuump!”

source.japanese: 航海士の双子が、やいのやいのと責め、囃したてながら両手を振り上げ腿[もも]を跳ね上げ、朔屋の後ろで炎に昂奮した蛮族のようにしきりにぴょんぴょん跳びはねている。
source.english: The twin navigators clamored and taunted behind him, waving their arms, kicking up their legs, bouncing again and again like savages roused by fire.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「JUUU～～MP!」

The twin first mates noisily and repeatedly tormented him, throwing their hands up and kicking their legs high in the air while jeering, eagerly hopping around behind Sakuya like savage tribesmen agitated by the sight of fire.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「さっさとしやがれ、こっちゃまだ酒残ってふらふらしてんだからよ」
source.english: “Get on with it. I'm still swaying from all that booze.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Get it the hell over with already, I'm still groggy from all the wine.」

source.japanese:
【宗右衛門】
「ニャアアア」
source.english: “Mrrrrooow!”

source.japanese: 水夫長の渋面も、深酒の後でやや迫力に欠けるが、それら補いをつけるように宗右衛門猫が、でんと老水夫の隣に腰を据えて、朔屋に大口開けて火のような舌をそよがせている始末の。何故猫にまでこうも怒られなければならないのか、とんと見当もつかぬ朔屋に、
source.english: The boatswain's scowl had lost a little force after his heavy drinking. To make up for it, Soemon had planted himself beside the old sailor and was opening his mouth wide at Sakuya, his tongue flickering like fire. Why did even the cat have to be so angry with him? Sakuya had not the slightest idea. Then—

target.text: 【Souemon】 「MREEEOW!」

The Bosun's grimace was lacking a bit of its usual edge after the heavy drinking, but as though to compensate for that, the cat Souemon had settled down with an imposing dignity next to the old mariner, opening his mouth wide at Sakuya, his tongue swaying like a licking flame. And to Sakuya, who was completely clueless as to why even the cat had to become this upset with him,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ああそうだった直の字、お前ぇがな、泪の口紅べったり拭ったあれな、あの水な、宗右衛門の取り分だったんだわ」
source.english: “Oh, right, Nao. That water you used to wipe off all Rui's rouge? That was Soemon's share.”

source.japanese: なるほどそれでは黒猫がお怒りになっても仕方がない。宗右衛門、船の中で一等偉いご意見番、彼は常に一番良い水と一番良い食料を取る権利を行使する。
source.english: Well, then, the black cat had every right to be angry. Soemon, the ship's foremost elder statesman, always exercised his right to the best water and the best food.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Aah, that's right, big Nao, you know, when you wiped off Rui's lipstick, that water you used? Turns out that was Souemon's share.」

Certainly, in that case, it was no wonder that the black cat had grown rather offended. Souemon, most eminent of advisors aboard the ship, always exercised his right to imbibe only the finest of water and victuals.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
『人生は選択だよ、朔屋君。
　飛びこむ先が、海か主罐の中か。
　私としては、まあ海の方がこちらの手間にはならないかな』
source.english:
“Life is a matter of choices, Sakuya.
Will you jump into the sea or the main boiler?
Personally, I think the sea would mean less trouble on our end.”

source.japanese: 上甲板のど真ん中から唐突に突き出している伝声管からは、機関長も容赦なく督励している。朔屋は、さっきまでそんなところに伝声管など生えていなかった筈と首を捻った弾みに足を踏み外し、真っ逆様に海の中、といきかけて往生際の悪い事に辛うじて棒にしがみついたが、背中を下にぶら下がる様、棒に四肢を縛りつけられこれから丸焼きにされようという類人猿とよく似ていた。
source.english: The chief engineer, too, urged him on without mercy through a speaking tube that had abruptly sprouted from the very middle of the upper deck. Sakuya twisted around, wondering whether any such tube had been growing there a moment ago, lost his footing in the process, and all but plunged headfirst into the sea; with an unseemly refusal to accept his fate, however, he just managed to clutch the spar. Hanging beneath it belly-up, he looked remarkably like an ape with all four limbs lashed to a pole, about to be roasted whole.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 『Life is all about choices, Sakuya-kun. Make your choice───will you dive into the sea, or into the boiler? For my part, well, the sea would demand less effort.』

From the voice pipe that suddenly protruded from right in the middle of the upper deck, the Chief Engineer also mercilessly urged them on. Sakuya, certain that there had not been any voice pipe sticking out from there just a moment ago, cocked his head in confusion, and the momentum of the motion caused him to slip, plunging headfirst into the sea, but at the very last moment, not knowing when to give up, he just barely managed to cling on to the pole, dangling with his back facing down towards the water, all four limbs wrapped around the pole, closely resembling some anthropoid ape about to be roasted whole.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「余計な時に、ろくでもないコトばっか言うから、こんなコトになったじゃないか」
source.english: “This happened because you keep saying awful things when there's no call for it.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Isn't this only happening because you keep saying the stupidest things at all the wrong times?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「僕らの中には、まだ立てないのだっているんだヨ？」
source.english: “Some of us still can't stand, you know?”

source.japanese: 日頃温厚な下級水夫君達までもが、憤懣やるかたなしと言った相で舳先の上で震える朔屋を睨[にら]みつけ足踏みならしているとあっては、この船上裁判、朔屋に味方して弁護する者はいないようであった。
source.english: Even the usually mild junior sailors glared at Sakuya trembling over the bow, stamping their feet in unappeased indignation. Apparently no one would take his side in this shipboard trial.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「There are some among our number who still can't stand on their own two feet, you know?」

Given that even the usually mild-mannered deck boys were glaring at Sakuya as he trembled below the bow, with expressions of utter indignation, stamping their feet as they did, there seemed to be none left on this ship who would advocate on Sakuya's behalf during this shipboard trial.

source.japanese: そう、かくの如く───
source.english: Yes, thus—

source.japanese: 皆が朔屋に酬いようとしているのは、彼が海を元に戻してきた事を褒賞しようというのではない。朔屋が海底に降りていった事を知るのは泪と智里のみであり、智里はこれこの通り、
source.english: The reward everyone intended was not praise for restoring the sea. Only Rui and Tomosato knew that Sakuya had gone to the seabed. And Tomosato, as you can see—

target.text: Indeed, and thus───

Their wish to see Sakuya compensated so was not because they were trying to reward him for restoring the sea to its usual state. It was only Rui and Tomosato who knew that Sakuya had even gone to the bottom of the sea, and Tomosato, as one could plainly see, was acting like so:

source.japanese:
【智里】
「間違っちゃあいねえわな。
　諦めろや、朔屋よう。
　なぁに一瞬のことだ」
source.english:
“They're not wrong.
Give it up, Sakuya.
It's only a moment.”

source.japanese: 皆に説明する気など皆無のようだし、だいたい殺し屋の言動は意味不明瞭な事でも船内に知れ渡っている。口を聞いたところで余計の誤解を招きかねない。
source.english: He seemed to have no intention of explaining anything. Besides, the whole ship knew the killer's words and actions were incomprehensible. Speaking up might only create more misunderstanding.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「They're not wrong about that. Just give it up, Sakuya. Really, it'll be over in the blink of an eye.」

He seemed to have no desire to explain things to the rest, and to begin with, it was well-known around the ship that this murderer's words and actions were incomprehensibly cryptic. It was quite possible that him trying to put in a good word on Sakuya's behalf would only serve to invite more misunderstandings.

source.japanese:
では泪は、と言えば、朔屋を非難糾弾する輪にこそ入っていないものの、皆から離れて一人の下級水夫君と話しこんでいる最中で、青年をどういう扱いが待ち構えていようと、それには大した興味がないようだった。
　そもそも、朔屋など塩辛某にやりこめられて悄気ていたのが関の山で、今回の現象を収めたのは結局彼女なのであり、泪は泪はと頼るのにも限度があろう。
source.english:
And Rui? She had not joined the ring of accusers, but stood apart, engrossed in conversation with a junior sailor. Whatever treatment awaited Sakuya seemed to interest her little.
After all, he had done no more than let the Salty So-and-so browbeat him into despair. In the end she had settled the phenomenon. Rui, Rui—there had to be a limit to how heavily he leaned upon her.

target.text: So then, what of Rui? Although she was taking no part in the harsh public condemnation of Sakuya, she was standing a ways away from the rest, fully engrossed in conversation with a lone deck boy, and she didn't seem particularly curious about what manner of treatment was in store for this young man. The best that could ever have been expected from someone the likes of Sakuya was to be browbeaten into despondency by that Shiokara-what's-his-name, and ultimately, the one who had brought this phenomenon to a close was her, but with Rui being Rui, there were surely limits to how much he should depend on her.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……判った、判りましたようっ。
　僕のせいですよ、ええなんもかも……。
　飛びますよ、飛びゃあいいんでしょう」
source.english:
“…All right. All right!
It's my fault. Yes, everything… I'll jump.
That's what you want, isn't it?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……All right, I get it, I get it. It's all my fault, yep, each and every little thing……. I'm jumping, I just have to jump off, right?」

source.japanese: ぐすぐすと啜[すす]り泣く、鬱期の朔屋は、同じ能無しでもまだ普段のお調子者の方がましと十人が十人ともそう断ずるほど鬱陶しさに湿っぽく、不愉快な事極まりない。朔屋は棒に掴まったまま救いを求めるように頭を廻らせた、ところで誰も青年を擁護する者などおらず、どころか、べちゃんと、空から落ちてきて青年の両目を塞いだものがある。
source.english: In one of his low spells, sniffling and sobbing, Sakuya was a sodden misery. Ask ten people and all ten would have preferred his usual glib self, useless though that was too. Thoroughly unpleasant. Still clinging to the spar, he turned his head in search of salvation. No one came to his defense. Quite the contrary: something fell from the sky with a splat and covered both his eyes.

target.text: Sniffling and sobbing: when Sakuya was in one of his depressive moods, he was so gloomy and melancholy that out of ten people asked, all ten would decisively agree that they preferred the usual frivolous clown, for though both were equally useless, this was the epitome of unpleasantness. Still clasping the pole tightly, Sakuya whipped his head around in search of salvation, but there were none who would deign to be his champion, far from it, for with a wet squelch, something fell down from the skies and landed on the young man's face, covering both his eyes.

source.japanese: 彼の末路を見物するように最前より空をくるくる回っていた信天翁の糞である。鳥さえも痺[しび]れを切らしたのかも知れない。
source.english: Droppings from an albatross that had been circling overhead, seemingly to watch his end. Perhaps even the bird had run out of patience.

target.text: It was the guano of an albatross that had been circling in the sky above him for a little while now as though to watch his fate. Perhaps even the bird had grown impatient with his stalling.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うぎゃああ臭いようううっっっ！」
source.english: “Aaaagh, it stiiiinks!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Gwaaaah, that reeeeeeeks!」

source.japanese:
たまらず拭い落とそう、と手を離せば待ち受けている運命は判りきって、がくんと状態が垂れ下がって、腿で棒を挟んで持ちこたえていたのも僅かな間、朔屋は自決する意地さえ見せず、落ちていく、情けなく落ちていく。
　まあ、糞に塗れた顔も、海水で洗えば綺麗にもなろう。
source.english:
Unable to bear it, he released his hands to wipe it away. The fate awaiting him was obvious. His upper body dropped with a jerk. For a moment he held on with the spar between his thighs, but no longer. Without even the resolve to jump of his own accord, Sakuya fell.
Pathetically, he fell. Well, seawater would clean his shit-covered face.

target.text: Unable to endure it, he let go with his hands in an effort to wipe it off, and by then, it was all too obvious what fate awaited him; he dropped limply with a sudden jolt, thighs clenched around the pole, but that only lasted a scant few moments; unable to even muster the resolve to take his fate in his own hands, Sakuya fell, and how pitifully he fell. Well, smeared with shit as it was, he could at least wash his face clean with the sea water.

source.japanese:
先ほどは猿にも喩えたが、まだ水に映じた月に向かって飛びかかっては落ちる猿の方が勇ましく、朔屋の落ちゆく姿は皆の記憶に残った。不様の見本として。
　波間に呑まれて水音と飛沫が高い。
source.english:
He had been compared to an ape before, but even the ape that leaps for the moon reflected in the water and falls is the more gallant of the two. The sight of Sakuya dropping remained in everyone’s memory—as the very model of ignominy.
The waves swallowed him in a towering splash.

target.text: While Sakuya had been compared to a monkey just moments ago, a monkey that was falling after having pounced at the reflection of the moon in the water would still make a more gallant sight, and the image of Sakuya falling would remain in the memory of all present, as an exemplar of disgrace. Swallowed by the waves, both the sound and splash of water were flung high into the air.

source.japanese:
深く落ちこんだが、すぐさまぷかり浮いてきて、カツオノエボシのように頭を覗かせぱしゃぱしゃと水をかく、本人も忘れていたようだが、『真珠』の効果はまだ続いたらしい。
　しかしそれが幸いだったのかどうか。
　波間できょとんと浮かぶ朔屋の顔は、船員達の神経を鑢で逆撫でしたと見え、
source.english:
He sank deep, then promptly bobbed up again, his head showing like a Portuguese man-of-war as he paddled about. He seemed to have forgotten it himself, but the pearl's effect apparently continued.
Whether that was fortunate was another matter.
His bewildered face floating among the waves seemed to rake a file across the crew's nerves.

target.text: Though he sunk deep, he quickly bobbed back up to the surface again, head peeking up from below the water like a Portuguese man-of-war, splashing as he paddled through the water, and though even the man himself also seemed to have forgotten, the effects of the『Pearl』were apparently still active. But was that truly a stroke of fortune? The dazed look on Sakuya's face as he drifted amidst the waves appeared to have grated on the sailors' nerves with a rasp,

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なんじゃ、あいつ。
　平気の平左で浮かんできたぞ」
source.english:
“What's with him?
Came floating up without a care in the world.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「What's up with that guy? He's just floating along without a care in the world.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぺっぺ、なんかまだ微妙にワインの味が残ってて、潮と混ざって、これ、
　うえええ……あ、痛、痛いッ」
source.english:
“Ptui, ptui. There's still a faint taste of wine, mixed with salt,
and it's—bleeegh… Ow! Ow, that hurts!”

source.japanese: 朔屋、グルマン気取って潮の味など論評する暇もない。この男の溺れもがく様見れば少しは溜飲も下がるだろうという期待裏切られた船員達、特に双子が率先してあたりのガラクタ手当たり次第に水面の朔屋に向かって投げつけたのだ。
source.english: No time for Sakuya to play the gourmand and critique the seawater. The crew had hoped the sight of him struggling and drowning would ease their resentment. Disappointed, they began hurling whatever junk lay to hand at him in the water. The twins took the lead.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Ptoo, peh, there's still kind of a faint taste of wine lingering, and it's mixed with the salty water, this is, ueeeeggh……ah, ow, owww!」

Sakuya didn't even have the time to play at being some gourmand while giving his review of the taste of the brine. The sailors' expectations of feeling at least a little gratified at watching this man struggle in the water had been spectacularly betrayed, and the twins in particular took the initiative in hurling whatever junk they could get their hands on down at Sakuya on the surface of the water.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「全然堪えてないみたい」
source.english: “Doesn't seem to have bothered him at all.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Doesn't look like he's bothered in the least.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こりゃ、一回じゃあ懲[こ]りないかな」
source.english: “Maybe once isn't enough to teach him.”

source.japanese:
【機関長】
『そもそも彼は、物事に懲[こ]りるという性格でもないでしょうに』
source.english: “To begin with, he hardly has the sort of disposition that learns a lesson, does he?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Seems one round won't be enough to teach him his lesson.」
【Chief Engineer】 『I do believe he never was the sort to learn from experience either way.』

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「なら懲[こ]りるまで何度でもやってもらおうや。
　おら朔屋、もう一度だ。
　今度は竜骨潜りしてこい」
source.english:
“Then we'll make him do it as many times as it takes.
Come on, Sakuya. Again.
This time, it's a keelhauling.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Then we'll just need to have him do it again and again until he does. Hey, Sakuya, do it again. And this time, you'll be diving under the keel.」

source.japanese: 水夫長は投げ輪で朔屋を引きずり挙げたものの、当然温情からなどではなく、また舳先の棒に追いたてたし、
source.english: The boatswain hauled him up with a loop of rope, certainly not out of kindness, and drove him back onto the bowsprit.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「さすがに、それは……息が続いても、
　背中の皮と肉がずる剥けになっちまいますよう……」
source.english:
“Surely that's too much…
Even if I can keep breathing, it'll strip the skin and flesh off my back…”

target.text: The Bosun dragged Sakuya back up on deck with a thrown loop of rope, but of course, it was not done with any warm kindliness in mind, for he was quickly driven back to the bowsprit once more,
【Naomasa】 「Surely that's a little…… even if I can keep breathing, I feel like the skin and flesh on my back is going to be peeled off……」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「御託はいいから。いいから───
　飛～～べっ！」
source.english:
“Enough excuses.
Enough—Juuump!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Enough with the chatter. Come on─── JUUU～～MP!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そら飛～～べっ！」
source.english: “Come on, juuump!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「COME ON───JUUU～～MP!」

source.japanese: 双子は今度は回転式拳銃で狙いを着けて撃鉄を起こす始末の、躊躇っていては飛びこむよりひどい目に遭う事間違いなしの。
source.english: This time the twins went so far as to aim revolvers and cock the hammers. Hesitating would undoubtedly bring worse treatment than jumping.

target.text: This time, the twins went so far as to aim their revolvers at him and cock the hammers, so there was no doubt in his mind that he would be in for a much worse fate were he to hesitate instead of simply jumping.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーーーーーっっっ」
source.english: “Aaaaaaah!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「AAAーーーーーhhh!」

source.japanese:
かくして船上に信天翁は舞い、海中へと朔屋は落ちていく。
　何度でも。何度でも。
source.english:
Thus an albatross wheeled above the ship, and Sakuya fell into the sea.
Again. And again.

source.japanese: それでも、打ち身と擦り傷を全身にこさえただけですんだのは、さすがこの男、悪運の持ち主と言うべきか。
source.english: Still, he escaped with no more than bruises and scrapes all over. The devil's own luck, this man—what else could you call it?

target.text: Thus, the albatrosses soared above the ship, and Sakuya fell into the sea. Again. And again.
And yet, despite it all, he came out of it with nothing but bruises and scrapes across his whole body, just as one would expect of this man; perhaps he truly did have the luck of the devil.

source.japanese:
さて、この私刑の輪からやや離れて。
　時間は少し巻き戻り、舳先で泣き喚く朔屋が救い求めて見た泪の方。朔屋が怒りの形相下面々に舳先へ追い立てられる一方、共に船に戻った泪に、下級水夫君の一人がなにやら沈痛な面持ちで歩み寄る。
source.english:
Now, a little apart from this circle of summary justice.
Time winds back a little, to Rui—the Rui toward whom Sakuya, bawling on the bow, had cast his eyes in search of salvation. While the furious crew drove him out onto the bowsprit, one of the junior sailors approached Rui, who had returned aboard with him, wearing a deeply troubled expression.

target.text: Now then, a little ways away from this scene of vigilantism. Let us rewind time a little, this time focusing on Rui, who Sakuya, wailing at the bow, had been looking at in search of salvation. While Sakuya was being driven to the bow by a crowd of faces twisted into scowls, walking towards Rui, who Sakuya had returned to the ship together with, was a single deck boy with a rather sombre, heavy-hearted expression.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「泪さん、あのね……ごめんなさい」
source.english: “Ms. Rui, um… I'm sorry.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Rui-san, uhm, I……I'm sorry.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「なあに？　男の子が、いきなり謝ってくるなんて」
source.english: “What's this? A sailor coming up to apologize out of nowhere…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「What is this? Now why would a boy suddenly apologize to me?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「これ───」
source.english: “This—”

source.japanese: 彼が握った手開いて泪に差し出したのは、乳白色に虹を纏[まと]った白い粒。朔屋との口づけの後で床にこぼれた真珠。
source.english: He opened his fist and offered her a white bead, milky with a sheen of rainbow. The pearl that had fallen to the floor after her kiss with Sakuya.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「This───」
The boy opened his clenched fist, and what he presented to Rui was a milky-white drop clad in a rainbow. It was a pearl that had fallen to the floor after her kiss with Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「僕、あの後、
　泪さんの部屋から戻った後……。
　服の中にこれが入ってて……」
source.english:
“Afterward…
After I came back from your room…
This was inside my clothes…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「I-, after all that, after I returned from your cabin, Rui-san……. This was inside my clothes……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「でもあのっ。
　僕、盗んだりなんかしていない、です。
　本当に、知らないうちに───」
source.english:
“But, um!
I didn't steal it. Really.
I didn't know it was there—”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But, uhm. I-, I didn't steal it or anything, I didn't. I mean it, I didn't even realize that───」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「でもそんなのは、言い訳だ。
　だから、ごめんなさい。
　返します。罰だったら受けます」
source.english:
“But that's just an excuse.
So I'm sorry. I'll give it back.
If there's a punishment, I'll take it.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But, that's just an excuse. And so, I'm sorry. I'm returning it. I'll take whatever punishment you demand.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……謝る事なんて、なぁんにも。
　貴方が盗んだりなんてしてないこと、
　わかっているから」
source.english:
“…There's nothing at all
to apologize for. I know you
didn't steal it.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……There is nothing for you to apologize for, at all. You did not steal it or anything of the sort, that much I understand.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それは偶然に滑[すべ]りこんだのよ、きっと。
　そんなものを、返してなんて言わないし」
source.english:
“It must have slipped in by chance.
I'd never tell you to give something like that back.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It must have slipped in there by accident. I will not ask you to return something like that to me.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「でも……こんな綺麗な真珠……」
source.english: “But… It's such a beautiful pearl…”

source.japanese: 面伏せして、扱いあぐねたように手の中の白い珠へ、注ぐ眼差しは前髪の奥で見えないけれど、切なく涙を滲ませているのではないだろうかの、それくらい生真面目な面を持ち合わせているのが信天翁号の下級水夫達である。……この彼はやや行きすぎだとしても。
source.english: He lowered his face, uncertain what to do with the white sphere in his hand. His bangs hid his eyes, but perhaps they were filling with anguished tears. The Albatross's junior sailors possessed that much earnestness—though this particular one carried it rather far.

source.japanese:
そんな彼の前で。あの狂宴の一時に下級水夫を恣[ほしいまま]弄[もてあそ]んでいたのがこの泪なら、腰を落として目線を合わせて、穏やかに、男を惑わす魔性ではなく、清濁合わせて抱擁するかの観世音の相を綻ばせてみせるのも、また同じ泪なのだった。
　手を差し延べて、下級水夫の掌に掌重ねて白い珠を握らせてやりながら、気易に額を合わせてもう一度笑みかけた。
source.english:
Before him stood the same Rui who, during the hour of mad revelry, had toyed with a junior sailor to her heart's content. Now she lowered herself to meet his eyes and let her face blossom gently—not with the demonic allure that leads men astray, but with the countenance of Kannon embracing pure and impure alike.
She reached out and laid her palm over his, closing his fingers around the white bead; then, with easy familiarity, touched her forehead to his and smiled once more.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But……it's such a beautiful pearl……」

Face lowered out of shame, he seemed unsure of what to do with the white bead in his hand, and though the look in the eyes fixed upon it was hidden deep beneath his bangs, was it not all too possible that there were miserable tears welling up within them, so deeply earnest were the deck boys of the Albatross. ……Even if this particular lad was taking it a little too far.

Though she had self-indulgently toyed and trifled with them during that frenzied feast, this Rui here, she who bent down before this young lad, looked him straight in the eyes, and gently, with none of the devilishness that led men astray, let her expression blossom into something akin to that of Kannon's look of all-encompassing mercy that embraced the pure and impure alike, was still that very same Rui. She extended a hand towards his, put her palm atop the deck boy's own, and while closing his fist around the pearl, she leaned in with easy familiarity, touching her forehead to his, then smiled at him once more.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ふふ……っ。
　それはね、真珠とは少し違うのよ。
　貝の中で育ったものじゃない───
　それは」
source.english:
“Hehe…
It isn't quite a pearl, you know.
It didn't grow inside a shell.
It's—”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Huhu……. You see, this is a little different from a pearl. It is not something that grew within a shell─── This here.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「人魚の涙よ」
source.english: “A mermaid's tear.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Is a mermaid's tear.」

source.japanese:
先の『葡萄酒の海』事件以来、また信天翁号には凪が訪れ、航海も穏やかに。
　今宵、空には一面の星と、そして冴えた月魄、満ちる月齢には僅かに足りない月が清[さや]かな光を放っている。波のやや高し。それでも船腹を時折強く叩いて、居眠りを懲らすように揺らす程度、総体として今夜も穏やかな夜と言えた。
source.english:
Since the sea-of-wine affair, calm had returned to the Albatross, and the voyage proceeded peacefully.
Tonight, stars filled the sky. A clear moon, just short of full, shed its lucid light. The waves were a little high, but did no more than occasionally strike the hull hard and shake it, as though chastising anyone who nodded off. Taken all in all, another peaceful night.

target.text: Since the prior『Ocean of Wine』 incident, calm had arrived on the Albatross once more, and the voyage carried on peacefully. This evening, the sky was covered in a veil of stars, and the moon, a sliver away from being full, was emitting clear beams of moonlight that lit up the night. The waves ran a little high. And though they would at times slam powerfully against the hull, it only made the ship rock enough to snap someone out of their napping, so on the whole, tonight could also well be called a peaceful night.

source.japanese:
そんな信天翁号の上甲板は船尾に、一つの天幕がある。波間を越えて曲馬団が通って来るでもあるまいに、片づけもされず放置されてあるのは、ただの怠惰によるものか、あるいは船の知られざる事件の記念碑としてか。いずれにしても天幕の裡[うち]では丸盆が、客席の茣蓙が、歓声もなく、跳ねかつ跳び回る芸人もない。
　天幕の破れ目からは月影が差しこんで、幻影の格好の映写幕となっているというのに、この船では過去の幻も偏屈者なのか、いっかな立ち現れる気配のない。
source.english:
At the stern of the upper deck stood a tent. No circus was likely to come over the waves. Why had it been left there, never put away? Mere laziness, or a monument to some unknown incident aboard? In any case, there were no cheers inside, no performers leaping and bounding about the round tray and the audience mats.
Moonlight entered through tears in the canvas, making an ideal screen for phantoms. Yet perhaps even the ghosts of the past were contrary aboard this ship. Not one showed any sign of appearing.

source.japanese: それとももしかするとこの天幕は、信天翁号の数代前の乗組の中に一風変わった審美眼の主がいて、船尾にこういうオブジェがあれば面白かろうとの美的直感に従って設けたもので、実用などは一切考えていなかったのかも知れない。
source.english: Or perhaps, several generations of crew ago, someone with an unusual eye for beauty had decided an object like this at the stern would be interesting. Following that aesthetic intuition, he might have installed it without the slightest thought of practical use.

source.japanese:
とまれ、時折音高く飛沫く波の音をアクセントに、天幕の中はいよいよ寂寞と、この静謐をただ一つの口で呑み尽くす贅沢者一人、天幕の裡側の更に奥まった辺りに。
　天幕と続きの、楽屋裏めいた一画だが一方は海に開かれ、舷側の柵も低くして、寝椅子に寝そべりながらでも茫漠とした眺めを一望にできる。
source.english:
At any rate, punctuated by the occasional loud splash of a wave, the tent grew ever more deserted and still. Deep within it, one extravagant soul swallowed all that silence for himself.
An adjoining corner resembled a backstage area, but one side opened onto the sea. The rail there was low enough to afford a view of the whole immensity even from a reclining chair.

source.japanese:
寝椅子は元は何処ぞの海沿いの別荘にでも置かれていた物を、乗組の誰かが盗んできたのだろう、藤製の洒落た細工椅子で、およそ信天翁号にはそぐわぬ品かと思いきやその一角に放置されて潮風に哀しく放置されてきたと思しく、船の他の材と同じ風合いに朽ちている。これを実用に耐えるくらいにまで修理したのが、現在寝そべっている朔屋だ。
　藤椅子の傍にはマラスキーノ酒の瓶と、つまみのつもりか乾パンなどを置いて、王侯貴族の如き充足感で満腔の。
source.english:
The chair was a stylish piece of wickerwork, probably stolen by some crew member from a seaside villa. It might have seemed utterly unsuited to the Albatross, except that, sadly abandoned to the salt wind in that corner, it had decayed to match the rest of the ship's timbers. Sakuya, now reclining in it, had repaired it enough to make it usable.
A bottle of maraschino liqueur and some hardtack—presumably a snack—stood beside him. His breast brimmed with the satisfaction of a prince or nobleman.

source.japanese:
言うまでもなく酒も乾パンも食料庫からくすねてきた物で露見したならまた懲罰モノだが、とりあえず今宵ばれずにいたならそれでよいと、刹那的というより先を想う想像力に欠けているのも相変わらずである。
　自分の船室が与えられているにも関わらず、船の顧みられる事のない隙間を選んではこういう隠れ家めいた場所を作らずにいられないのは、男という生き物の習性か、単に朔屋の稚気が未だ抜けていないだけか、さて、さて。
source.english:
Needless to say, he had pilfered both liquor and hardtack from the stores. Discovery would mean punishment again. But so long as he escaped discovery tonight, that would do. Less a devotion to the moment than his usual inability to imagine the future.
Although he had a cabin of his own, he could not help selecting neglected spaces aboard and making little hideouts. Was that a habit of the male creature, or merely Sakuya's lingering childishness? Well, well.

target.text: And atop the upper deck of this Albatross, at the stern, stood a single tent. There was certainly no circus troupe that crossed the waves to make use of it, and yet it had simply been abandoned without any attempt at tidying up, perhaps simply out of laziness, or maybe left there as a commemorative monument to some incident that no one aboard the ship knew of. At any rate, within the tent were no round serving trays, no mats to serve as seating for the audience, no shouts of joy, and no performers jumping and flying through the air.

Moonbeams shone through a tear in the tent's fabric, and though it would have served as the ideal projection screen for the phantasmal, perhaps even the phantoms of the past aboard this ship were obstinate contrarians, for there was not a single sign of any manifesting into reality.

Or else, by some chance, there happened to be the owner of a rather eccentric eye for beauty amongst the crew of the Albatross of several generations past, a man who, in accordance with his aesthetic intuition, thought that having an objet d'art like this located on the stern would be amusing, then pitched this tent, thoughts of whatever practical use it may have never crossing his mind.

In any case, punctuated now and then by the sharp accent of the splashing of the waves, the tent's interior only felt all the more desolate in turn, and there was but a single mouth belonging to a single indulgent soul drinking dry that tranquility, around the part a little deeper inside the tent. Adjoining the tent was a section reminiscent of a backstage area, but one side was left open out to the sea, and with the railing along the ship's side being so low to the deck, one could take in the vast, sweeping view even while sprawled out on a reclining chair.

The reclining chair was the sort of thing that must have originally belonged to some seaside villa, and someone from the crew must have stolen it or something; it was a stylishly worked rattan chair, but contrary to the natural expectation that it was the sort of article that would make a poor match for the Albatross, it appeared to have been lamentably abandoned in that little corner, left at the mercy of the salty sea breeze, and so it was just as weathered and decayed in appearance as all the other wood on the ship. And the one who had repaired it to the extent it was fit for actual use, now that was none other than Sakuya who was currently lounging in it.

Placed by the rattan chair's side was a bottle of maraschino liqueur, along with some crackers and the like probably meant to serve as snacks for the drink, and his whole being was filled with a feeling of contentment fit for royalty.

It went without saying that both the liqueur and the crackers were pilfered from the food storage, and were that to be discovered, he would once again be disciplined, but regardless, he was satisfied as long as it would not be discovered for tonight at least; rather than living for the moment, it was more like he lacked the power of imagination required to think ahead, and that, too, was also the same as it ever was.

Why he invariably sought out these tiny, overlooked nooks and crannies of the ship and fashioned them into little hideaways, despite having been given his very own cabin, was perhaps simply a quirk of the nature of the creature known as man, or perhaps it was simply that Sakuya's childishness had yet to fully leave him, but, well, moving on.

source.japanese:
乾パンを噛み、口の中でもそもそするところにリキュールの瓶から直呑みに、流しこんでは芳烈な液体と混ぜ合わせて呑み下すという、少々品の悪い楽しみ方も一人なら許されよう。
　夜の小間物仕事は、下級水夫君の一人にとある贈り物で替わってもらってある。
source.english:
He chewed hardtack, then drank straight from the liqueur bottle, washing the dry mouthful down with the fragrant liquid. A somewhat ill-mannered pleasure, but permissible when alone.
A certain gift had persuaded one of the junior sailors to take over his little nighttime chores.

target.text: He bit into a cracker, downed the liqueur right from the bottle while slowly masticating, washed it down, the sharply aromatic liquid mixing with the cracker as he swallowed; it was a rather undignified way of enjoying oneself, but one that could surely be forgiven on account of him being by himself. Any minor nighttime chores had been handed off to one of the deck boys in exchange for a certain little gift.

source.japanese: そうやって乾パンと酒を片手で代わる代わるやりながら、もう片手でひねり回しているのがあの望遠鏡だ。折り畳み式で、小体ながらも性の佳い。
source.english: Alternating between hardtack and liquor with one hand, he turned that telescope about with the other. Collapsible, compact, but well made.

source.japanese: 朔屋の手に渡ってから随分になるが、このうっかり者の青年にしてはどこかに置き忘れたり落としたりする事も、壊したりもせず、航海を共にしてきてある。手沢の艶は今は青年の手膏に馴染んで、掌の中でひねくり回す様子、不思議と画に映えた。いずれの手で作られ、何処を経て朔屋の許に辿り着いたのかは知らず、歳月を経て狂いもない細工で、畳んだり伸ばしたりと悪戯に扱っても滑らかに収動する。
source.english: He had owned it for quite some time, yet, remarkably for someone so careless, had neither left it behind nor dropped nor broken it; it had voyaged with him all this way. Its old hand-worn gloss had by now blended with the grease of his own hands, and there was something curiously picturesque in the way he toyed with it in his palm. He did not know whose hands had made it or what places it had passed through before reaching him, but the years had put none of its workmanship out of true: however idly he pulled it open and folded it shut, it slid as smoothly as ever.

target.text: While alternating thus between grabbing crackers and the liqueur with one hand, he fiddled with that telescope using his other. A collapsible model, modest in scale yet of remarkable quality.

A considerable amount of time had passed since it had first fallen into Sakuya's hands, but despite how thoughtless a young man he was, he had not forgotten it somewhere or dropped it, nor broken it, and it had accompanied him throughout his voyages. The gloss of its patina had by now blended with the natural oils of the young man's hands, and the way he twirled it around in his hands made for an oddly picturesque scene.

Sakuya knew not by whose hands it had been wrought, nor by what paths it had travelled before finding its way into his possession, and its craftsmanship, unfaltering in its precision through the passage of many a moon, allowed it to slide with effortless smoothness, even when collapsed or extended in idle fancy.

source.japanese:
と、ことん、と甲板を踏む音に、盗み呑みが露呈したと慌てふためくのが朔屋の持ち芸だが、今日はどうした事かお大尽、跳ね上がる筈の腰は据わったままで跫音へ回され、目には望遠鏡をわざと宛がったままの茶目っ気まで見せた。
　灯りなど引いていない楽屋裏、望遠鏡の中は暗かったけれど、もう片方の目で紺青の色を見る。
source.english:
Clunk—a footfall sounded on deck. At such a sound Sakuya's stock turn was to fly into a panic, certain his stolen drink had been discovered. Yet tonight, for some reason, His Lordship remained firmly seated instead of jerking upright; he merely turned toward the footstep, even showing the impishness to keep the telescope ostentatiously to his eye.
No lamp burned in the backstage nook, so the telescope showed him darkness; with his other eye he saw indigo.

target.text: Upon hearing the clicking sounds of footsteps landing on the deck, he flew into a panic, convinced that his furtive drinking had been discovered, a performance that was practically a trademark of Sakuya's, but today, curiously enough, the great debauchee did not leap to his feet as he normally would; he remained seated, turning towards the footfalls, even purposely keeping the telescope pressed to his eye in a display of mischief. There were no lights or anything of the sort installed in the backstage, and so the view through the telescope was dark, but an indigo hue was already visible in the corner of one of his eyes.

source.japanese:
【声】
「お邪魔して、よろしい？」
source.english: “May I join you?”

source.japanese: 望遠鏡が、縁のある者を呼んだのか、物柔らかな声は、機関室の暗がりで朔屋に譲った女の。
source.english: Had the telescope summoned someone connected with it? The gentle voice belonged to the woman who had passed it to Sakuya in the engine room's darkness.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───泪さんか。どーぞどーぞ。
　まあむさ苦しいとこだけどさ」
source.english:
“Oh, Rui.
Come in, come in. It's a bit squalid, but…”

source.japanese: この愛想の良さ、気易く迎える様子、朔屋も随分と泪への接し様が様変わりしているが、それだけでない、泪の登場を予感、あるいは期待していたような節さえある。
source.english: This friendliness, this easy welcome: Sakuya's manner toward Rui had changed considerably. More than that, he seemed to have anticipated her arrival. Perhaps even hoped for it.

target.text: 【Voice】 「May I come in?」
Perhaps the telescope had summoned one it held a connection with, for it was a soft voice, one belonging to the woman who had once granted it to Sakuya in the darkness of the engine room.
【Naomasa】 「───So it's you, Rui-san. Come in, come in. Well, it is a little drab inside.」

From this air of affability, his friendly way of greeting her, it was clear that Sakuya had completely changed the way he interacted with Rui, but that was not all; it seemed that he had sensed, or perhaps even been expecting Rui's arrival.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「いいえ、とても素敵な眺めよ。
　ここは───きっと、他の方達は、あまり構わない場所なのじゃなくて」
source.english:
“No, it's a lovely view.
This must be a place the others don't pay much attention to.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「まあね。隠れ酒するにゃちょうどいいよ」
source.english: “More or less. Just right for a secret drink.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Not at all, it makes for a most wonderful view. This place───it must be somewhere that the other fine folk of this ship pay little attention.」
【Naomasa】 「I guess so, yeah. It does make a perfect place for drinking away from any prying eyes.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「直さんの、隠れ家？」
source.english: “Your hideaway, Nao?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなところかな」
source.english: “Something like that.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Is this your retreat, Nao-san?」
【Naomasa】 「Something along those lines, I guess.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あら……じゃあ、殿方の隠れ場所を覗くなんて、野暮だったかしら」
source.english: “Oh… Then perhaps it was tactless to peep into a gentleman's refuge.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやいや、途中泪さんに見られたのは判ってた。それでもここに入ってみせたのは、あなたには知られたって構わないからでさ」
source.english: “Not at all. I knew you'd seen me on the way. I made a point of coming in here anyway because I didn't mind you knowing.”

source.japanese: 朔屋の言葉に、一瞬空とぼけるように眼差しをたゆたわせたが、泪はすぐに微苦笑の、今宵先んじたの青年の、その余裕の分だけ、泪に対して構えずに済んでいる分だけ、彼女の表情の変化の優雅が普段よりよく見えた。
source.english: For an instant her gaze drifted, as though feigning ignorance. Then Rui gave a small, rueful smile. Tonight Sakuya had taken the lead. His ease, his freedom from being on guard against her, let him see the grace of her changing expression more clearly than usual.

source.japanese:
この楽屋裏に引っこむ前に、朔屋はバラックの隙間から、船縁に佇む泪の後ろ姿を目にしていたのである。背中から臀への線が月影に濡れて、その練れた麗しさといったらなく、つい立ち止まりかけたけれど、彼女の肩が。
　ふっと下がるのに、朔屋はいつもなら自分を見境なくさせる性欲が下がっていくのを感じ、そのまま行き過ぎたのだった。誰しも一人になりたい夜はあろうし、それに一人月影の下海に向かう後ろ姿に、朔屋は割りこむのも不粋な、風雅を覚えたのである。
source.english:
Before retiring backstage, Sakuya had glimpsed Rui's back through a gap between the shacks. She stood at the ship's side. Moonlight bathed the line from her back to her hips, a beauty refined beyond measure. He almost stopped.
Then her shoulders lowered a little. The lust that usually drove him beyond restraint subsided, and he walked on. Anyone might have a night when they wished to be alone. Besides, the sight of her back facing the sea beneath the moon had a quiet elegance he would have felt coarse interrupting.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Oh my……then I suppose it was rather uncouth of me to peek inside a gentleman's refuge.」
【Naomasa】 「Perish the thought, I already knew I'd been spotted by you while I was heading here. That I still made it obvious that I went in here, that's because I don't really mind you knowing.」

Upon hearing Sakuya's words, she did let her gaze wander for an instant as if feigning ignorance, but Rui's lips quickly quirked into a wry smile, and because the young man had taken the lead tonight, that gave him composure, allowed him to stay relaxed around Rui, which in turn made the elegance in her subtly shifting expressions seem all the more clearer to his eyes than usual.

Before retiring to this backstage, looking out from a gap between the shacks, Sakuya had seen Rui standing at the gunwale with her back facing him. The curve running from her back to her buttocks was bathed in moonbeams, her mature beauty ineffable, and it unintentionally brought the young man's step to a halt, but her shoulders.

When they suddenly dropped, Sakuya felt the lust that usually robbed him of any semblance of restraint subside, and he simply continued on his way past her. Surely everyone had nights where they wished to be alone, and Sakuya was struck by a refined grace, one that whispered to him that intruding upon this lone figure standing below the pale silver light of the moon while facing the ocean would be boorish.

source.japanese:
ただ、行きすぎる前に跫音を聞かれたか、こちらを振り向く様な仕草を見た。
　気取られていなければそれで良し、気づかれても構わない、くらいの心だったが、楽屋裏に潜[もぐ]りこむ時、ふと、彼女が追いかけてきたなら、それはそれで楽しそう、とも想った。
source.english:
But before he passed, he saw her make a movement as though turning toward him.
Had she heard his footsteps? If she hadn't noticed him, fine; if she had, he didn't mind. And entering the backstage nook, he thought that if she followed, that might be pleasant too.

source.japanese: 女の後を追いかけても、追いかけられた事といったら、悪友と共に軒先の吊し柿を盗んだ際、悪鬼の如き形相の老婆の追跡を二町ばかりも受けた時くらいの朔屋にしては、随分と思い上がったときめきではある。
source.english: For Sakuya, who chased women but had only been chased himself when he and his bad companions stole persimmons hanging under someone's eaves, and a demonic-looking old woman pursued them for a couple of hundred meters, this was a remarkably conceited flutter of hope.

source.japanese: まあ泪が気まぐれを起こしたならば、程度の期待で、今更航海士の双子あたりが不意に思い立ってこの楽屋裏の掃除に取りかかるといった可能性は低いし、訪れるとしても泪くらいであろうと、そのように考えていたのがたまさか当たっただけの事。
source.english: Only if Rui took it into her head, of course. It seemed unlikely that the twin navigators would suddenly decide, at this late hour, to clean the backstage area. If anyone came, it would probably be Rui. That thought merely happened to prove right.

target.text: However, perhaps his footsteps had been heard before he could make it past her, for she showed signs of being about to turn around towards him. If he hadn't been noticed, then all was well, and if he had, then he didn't mind that either; that was how he felt, and when he slipped into the backstage, he caught himself thinking that, if she came in pursuit of him, that in itself seemed like it would be good fun.

He might have been a frequent chaser of women, but when it came to being chased in return, there had only been that one time when, together with his partner-in-crime, he'd been stealing some dried persimmons hanging down from the eaves of a house, and some old lady with a visage that could put the devil to shame had chased them a good two hundred metres down the street, so to Sakuya, it set his heart aflutter with some remarkable conceit.

Well, it would only be the case if Rui happened to feel a little capricious, that was the extent of his expectations, and at this point, the likelihood of, say, those twin first mates suddenly getting the bright idea to start cleaning this backstage was low, so supposing that anybody were to visit, it would most likely only be Rui anyways; those were his assumptions, and it was nothing more than mere happenstance that proved them true.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「嬉しいこと。お招きをいただいたわけでもないのに、鷹揚なのね」
source.english: “How pleasing. So generous, although you hadn't invited me.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あなたには、色々と世話になってるからさ……まあ、座って」
source.english: “…You've done a great deal for me… Well, sit down.”

source.japanese:
それは正直なところで、かつて海に落ちた時も、海が酒になった時も、結局は泪によって朔屋は救われている。そればかりか、成り行きとはいえ一度・二度と寝る事にもなった。
　肌を交えた相手を何時までも憎しと思える朔屋ではない。
source.english:
That was honest. When he fell into the sea, when the sea became liquor, Rui had ultimately saved him. More than that, though circumstances had led them there, they had slept together once, twice.
Sakuya was not a man to go on hating someone he had slept with.

target.text: 【Rui】 「How delightful. I have not even been extended an invitation, and yet you're so open-handed about having me.」
【Naomasa】 「……Well, I do owe you a lot and all……anyways, have a seat.」

He was speaking in all honesty, for both when he had fallen into the ocean before, as well as when the ocean had turned to wine, in the end, Sakuya had been saved by Rui. And not only that, even if it had only come about by happenstance, he had even slept with her, and not once, but twice. Sakuya was not the sort who could forever go on resenting someone whom he had been intimate with.

source.japanese: 寝そべっていた籐椅子から身を起こし、泪へと場を譲る。楽屋裏には他に腰を下ろすような調度といったら酒を置いた台くらいだが、それで腰が落ち着かないなら、甲板に直に腰を下ろして憚るような上等の衣装でなし。その程度の腹づもりでいたのに、泪は寝椅子にちょん、と詰めて座って、隣の隙間を軽く叩いて、朔屋に促すような無言の仕草。
source.english: He sat up from the wicker chaise and yielded it to her. The only other furnishing one could sit on was the stand holding the liquor. If that proved uncomfortable, his clothes were not so fine that he need hesitate to sit on the deck itself. That was all he intended. But Rui sat neatly to one side of the chaise and lightly patted the space beside her. A silent invitation.

target.text: He got up from the rattan chair he had been lounging in, then conceded it to Rui. In terms of other furniture in the backstage that one could feasibly sit on, there was only really the table he'd placed his bottle of liqueur on, but one couldn't really settle down properly on top of that, and he wasn't exactly wearing any sort of high-quality clothing that would leave him hesitant to sit directly down on the deck. That was about the extent of his calculations, but Rui settled herself neatly into the lounge chair, then gently tapped the free part of the seat next to her, a wordless gesture meant to spur Sakuya to action.

source.japanese: 籐椅子は二人が横に並んで座れるくらいの大きさはあったけれど、それでも詰めないといけなくて、そうすると必然的に肩を触れ合わせ、横身がひたりと密着する事になって。
source.english: The wicker chair was large enough for two to sit side by side, though they had to squeeze in. Inevitably, shoulders touched and their sides rested close together.

source.japanese: ───しばしの沈黙の中で、体熱が……解け合う。
source.english: For a little while, in silence, their warmth… mingled.

target.text: The rattan chair was large enough for two people to sit next to each other, notwithstanding that they would have to squeeze in tightly together, and once they did that, their shoulders would inevitable brush against each other, and their sides would press firmly together.
───During a brief period of silence, the warmth of their bodies……merged into one.

source.japanese:
月下に波を聞きながら、というまこと情趣に富んだ状況に二人きりであること、泪という、ある意味男の夢想の結晶のような女が傍にあるのがにわかに意識されてくる。
　こうなると、先ほどはいったん収まりかかった性欲がまた立ち戻ってくる。いつものように、腹を減らした犬が肉を追いかけるような性急さに取り憑かれていないだけで、別に俄[にわか]聖者になったわけでもない朔屋だ。
　この想い、夜の満ちるまま波の寄せるままに膨らませ、泪を誘ってみるべきか、あるいは今夜は清い仲で通して穏当な会話だけを楽しむべきか。
　そんな迷いを曖昧に弄[もてあそ]ぶ事も、今夜は不思議と楽しかった。
source.english:
Alone together beneath the moon, listening to the waves: a scene rich in feeling. He suddenly became conscious of the woman beside him, Rui,
in some sense the crystallization of a man's dream. His lust, which had subsided earlier, returned. He was not possessed by the usual haste of a hungry dog chasing meat, but he had hardly become a saint overnight.
Should he let the feeling swell with the gathering night and the approaching waves, and invite her? Or keep things chaste tonight, enjoying only a peaceful conversation?
Even idly toying with that uncertainty was strangely pleasant.

source.japanese:
朔屋、曖昧な気分は曖昧なままとして、それよりかねてから気にかかっていた事がある。
　今夜は、泪に訊ねてみるのにいい機会だった。
source.english:
Sakuya left his uncertain feelings uncertain. There was something else he had long wondered about.
Tonight was a good opportunity to ask Rui.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「詮索するようで悪いんだが、
　泪さんはこの船になんで乗りこんだ？
　どこかに向かう途中なのか？」
source.english:
“Sorry to pry,
but why did you come aboard this ship, Rui?
Are you on your way somewhere?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あなたが乗ってきてもう随分と経つが、
　それでもまだ不思議に思うぜ。
　どう考えたってこのオンボロ船、
　泪さんに似合うような船じゃない」
source.english:
“You've been aboard quite a while now,
but it still puzzles me.
However I look at it,
this wreck of a ship isn't suited to you.”

source.japanese: 泪が信天翁号をわざわざ選んで乗船してきた、その理由。朔屋はあの日、魚怪どもが拝謁していた夜、盗み聞きしてはいたけれど、まだ泪本人に直接訊ねたわけではない。
source.english: Why had Rui deliberately selected the Albatross? He had overheard something that night, when the fish-monsters paid their respects, but had never asked her directly.

target.text: With just the two of them, alone in that richly evocative setting, listening to the waves beneath the moon, Sakuya suddenly grew keenly aware of the fact it was Rui next to him, this woman who was the embodiment of a particular kind of male fantasy. And once that happened, the lust that had begun to abate earlier now returned in full force. He had not been possessed by the usual impatience, like that of a starving dog chasing after a piece of meat, but Sakuya had certainly not suddenly become a saint either.

Those feelings swelled, growing as the night deepened and the waves drew closer; should he attempt to coax Rui into something, or should he instead let the night remain platonic, sharing only in amicable conversation? Even vaguely toying with such indecision was oddly enjoyable tonight.

Sakuya allowed his vague feelings to remain just that, and more importantly, there was something that had weighed on his mind for a while now. Tonight was an excellent opportunity to broach the subject with Rui.
【Naomasa】 「I apologize if it seems like I'm prying here, but why exactly did you board this ship, Rui-san? Are you in the middle of heading for somewhere?」
【Naomasa】 「It has been a good while since you first came aboard, but I still find it strange. No matter how you look at it, a ship this ramshackle is just not befitting of you, Rui-san.」

Rui had purposely chosen to board the Albatross, but what about the reason why? That day, that night, when the fish monsters had an audience with her, Sakuya had eavesdropped on them, but he had yet to directly ask Rui herself about it.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そお？　見た通り、あちこち汚れていたり壊れていたりするけれど、この信天翁号、わたくしなりに気に入っているのよ」
source.english: “You think so? As you see, it's dirty and broken here and there, but I'm rather fond of the Albatross, in my way.”

source.japanese: 泪はただ倦怠に満ちた、物憂げな笑みの方が印象に残るが、好悪の感情のはっきりした女でもある。確かに厭う心のあるなら、別の退屈しのぎの具を求めてとっくに降りていた事だろう。これまで港には幾度となく寄っているのだから。
source.english: Her languid smile, full of ennui, made the strongest impression, but Rui was also a woman of distinct likes and dislikes. Had she truly disliked it, she would long since have disembarked in search of some other amusement. They had called at ports often enough.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Really now? As is plain to see, it certainly is squalid and broken here and there, but I find myself quite fond of this Albatross, in my own way.」

The part of Rui that left a lasting impression was that listless smile radiating ennui, but she was a woman of unmistakably clear likes and dislikes. Certainly, if she balked at the prospect of staying, she would surely have disembarked long ago in the search of some new means to kill time with. For hitherto, they had made call at port many a time.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「とは申せ───確かに自分で選んだ訳じゃあない。どこか目的の処[ところ]があるのでもない」
source.english: “That said, I didn't actually choose it myself. Nor do I have a particular destination.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Or so I say───but admittedly, I did not choose it of my own accord. Nor do I have any particular destination in mind.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ご招待を受けたのよ。
　ある日ある時お手紙で」
source.english:
“I received an invitation.
One day, in a letter.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I was extended an invitation. On a certain day, at a certain time, by way of a letter.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「細かい中味は忘れてしまったし、
　乗りこむ時にこちらの水夫長に見せて、
　それから……どこかに失せてしまったわ」
source.english:
“I've forgotten the exact contents.
I showed it to the boatswain when I came aboard,
and then… It disappeared somewhere.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I have forgotten the finer details, but I showed it to your Bosun when I boarded, and then……it disappeared somewhere along the way.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でもこんな風なことが書いてあったっけ。
　───退屈しのぎが欲しいのなら、
『信天翁号』という名の船に乗れ───
　って」
source.english:
“But it said something like this: 'If
you wish to relieve your boredom,
board a ship called
the Albatross.'”

target.text: 【Rui】 「But something along these lines were written within: ───Should you desire a means to kill time, then board the vessel that goes by『The Albatross』───」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でもそれだけで乗船いたすには、
　さすがに酔狂が過ぎます」
source.english:
“Even for me, boarding on that alone
would have been too eccentric.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしはそんなお名前の船など知らなかったし、どの船舶名鑑の、どこの頁をひっくり返しても載っていなかったし」
source.english: “I'd never heard of a ship with that name. Nor was it listed on any page of any shipping register I looked through.”

source.japanese:
なんとのう指先で耳元の髪などをくるくるといじりながら、泪、船上暮らしでは調髪する機会などろくになかろうに、彼女の髪は何時でも綺麗に巻かれて整えられて、短めに見えても伸ばしてみれば意外に長い事を朔屋は知っている。
　ついついその柔らかなのに指先を潜[もぐ]りこませたくなるのを抑えつつ、
source.english:
As she spoke, Rui idly twirled the hair near her ear about a fingertip. Opportunities to have one's hair dressed aboard a ship could hardly be plentiful, yet hers was always beautifully curled and arranged. Sakuya knew that although it looked short, it proved surprisingly long when uncoiled.
Suppressing the urge to slip his fingers into that softness, he said—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……だろうなあ。
　むしろ本に載ってる方がびっくりだわ。
　犯罪記録とか事件簿以外のね」
source.english:
“…I imagine not.
I'd be more surprised to find it in a book.
Other than a criminal record or a case file.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「But boarding a ship based on that alone, why, that would be excessively whimsical, to be sure.」
【Rui】 「I knew of no ship that went by any such name, and no matter what register of ships I perused, what page I turned over to, it was not recorded anywhere.」

So she said while absentmindedly curling the hair by her ear around her fingertip. Rui's hair, despite the woman surely having hardly any opportunities to maintain it while living aboard a ship, was invariably neatly curled and kept impeccably styled, and despite how short it looked, Sakuya knew that, once straightened, it was surprisingly long. While quelling his sudden, ill-conceived desire to slide his fingers into that softness,
【Naomasa】 「……That figures. If anything, it being mentioned in a book would be shocking. Criminal records or case files aside, that is.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「けれども。
『朔屋直正という船員が、案内してくれるだろう』
　そのような事も書かれていてね」
source.english:
“But it also said:
'A sailor named Naomasa Sakuya
will show you around.'”

target.text: 【Rui】 「However. There was also written something along the lines of: 『A sailor by the name of Sakuya Naomasa will surely show you around.』」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「貴方のことは、覚えていたから。
　それで心が動きました。それ以外の事は書かれていなかったけれど」
source.english:
“I remembered you.
That moved me. There was nothing else written.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だからあの夜、俺の事を捜してた、ってのはそういうわけか。
　……しかし俺にはなんにも心当たり、ないけどな……」
source.english:
“So that's why you were looking for me that night.
But I have no idea what it's about…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「And I did remember you. And that tickled my fancy. There was nothing else written, however.」
【Naomasa】 「And so you went looking for me that night, so that's what that was? ……But I really don't have the faintest clue about any of that, none at all……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ええ、それにね。前の夫が身罷ってから、ちょっと経っていた頃だったの。夜会にもサロンにも、興味が薄れていた頃で」
source.english: “Yes. And it was a little while after my previous husband had died. I was losing interest in evening parties and salons.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Yes, and furthermore. It was shortly after my former husband had shuffled off this mortal coil. Right around the time when my interest in soirees and salons was waning.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「毎日が退屈なのに、かといってなにかしたいのでもなくって。本当に『渡りに船』っていうのはこのこと」
source.english: “Every day was dull, but there was nothing I wanted to do. And there was my boat, just when I needed to cross.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Every day was tedious boredom, but having said that, I had no desire to do anything in particular either. It truly was a ship to carry me across the sea of ennui I found myself drowning in.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「だから、乗ってみるつもりになった」
source.english: “So I decided to try going aboard.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「その、手紙の差出人は誰だったんだろう」
source.english: “Who sent the letter?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Therefore, I made up my mind to give boarding the ship a try.」
【Naomasa】 「But I do wonder who the sender of that letter was.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「さあ……お名前はありませんでした。
　起きたら、いつの間にかお部屋の机に置いてあってね」
source.english:
“Who knows… There was no name.
When I woke, it was on the desk in my room. Somehow.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんな得体の知れない手紙を信じたんだ、泪さんは……なんか少し不気味な話だな。俺も関わってきてるのに、手紙の主が知れないなんて」
source.english: “You trusted a letter like that, Rui… It's a little eerie. Especially when I'm involved too, and we don't know who wrote it.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Who can say……there was no name on it. When I woke up, it had simply been placed on my desk, suddenly there without me noticing when.」

【Naomasa】 「And you actually placed any faith in such a suspiciously mysterious letter, Rui-san……that's honestly kind of unsettling. I'm wrapped up in it too, and yet we still have no idea who the sender is.」

source.japanese: 会話の外で、泪の肩へ、少しずつ体重を預けてみる。自分の肉の重みに、言外の意味を潜[ひそ]ませて、相手との間境を測る。
source.english: Outside the conversation, he began letting his weight rest little by little against Rui's shoulder. He put an unspoken meaning into the weight of his flesh, testing the boundary between them.

source.japanese: これまで一度、二度と肌を重ねはしたけれど、その程度で女を自分のモノのように扱ってはいけない事は朔屋にして理解されてあり、こうして肩を並べる時であっても、簡単に押し倒してしまうわけにもいかない。
source.english: They had lain together once, twice, but even Sakuya understood that this did not entitle him to treat a woman as his possession. Sitting shoulder to shoulder like this, he could not simply push her down.

source.japanese:
肩と肩を触れ合わせて、肌の温もりを感じ合って、その先に進んで良いのか、間合いを探る。
　この手探りの間は、これはこれで朔屋は好きな時間であった。この境を越えて、一夜を共にしていいのか。期待を育て、互いの了解をとりつける為の大事な時間だからして。
source.english:
Their shoulders touched. They felt each other's warmth. He tested the distance: might he go further?
Sakuya liked this tentative interval in its own right. Could they cross the boundary and share a night? It was an important time for nurturing hope and reaching a mutual understanding.

source.japanese:
そして、泪もまた。
　朔屋の重みを円やかな肩で受けて、反らさず、押し返しもせず、ただ柔らかに受けとめて。そうなると、既に覚えていた彼女の肉の甘美が鮮やかに朔屋の胸中というかはっきりと股ぐらに立ち戻り、交わす言葉に取り立て艶はなくとも、二人を取り巻く空気は稠密なものになって、その胸苦しさ、なんとも甘やかな、心地好い。
source.english:
And Rui, too.
She received Sakuya's weight upon her rounded shoulder, neither shrinking away nor pushing back, only yielding softly beneath it. At that, the remembered lusciousness of her flesh rose vividly once more in Sakuya's heart—or rather, quite unmistakably in his crotch. Though nothing particularly amorous passed between them, the air around the pair grew dense, and the breathlessness of it was somehow sweet, delicious.

target.text: In between the lines of their conversation, he had tried to lean the weight of his body against Rui's shoulder, little by little. Concealing an unspoken subtext in the weight of his flesh, gauging the distance between them.

Hitherto, they had slept together once or twice, and even Sakuya, of all people, knew perfectly well that he had no right to treat a woman as if she belonged to him over just that, and even while sitting shoulder to shoulder like this, he could not simply pin her down with force.

Shoulder touching against shoulder, feeling the warmth of each other's skin: should they really take things any further, probing into the gap that lay between them. This period of blind fumbling had a charm in its own right, and it was a time Sakuya was fond of. Should they cross that boundary, spend the night together? It was an important time, crucial to nurturing their anticipation and securing mutual consent.

And then, there was also Rui. She took Sakuya's weight into her soft shoulders; she did not yield, nor did she push back, she just tenderly accepted him. And once she did, the luscious taste of the woman's flesh that he had already experienced vividly returned to his bosom, or rather, it distinctly returned to his crotch, and even though there was nothing particularly sensual in the words they exchanged, the air surrounding them thickened, and the tightness in his chest it wrought, how could one even express so sweet a comfort.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そうとも言えるわね。
　けれどわたくしにはちょうどよかったのよ。
　別に行き先が指定されていたのでもない。
　それでも構わなかった」
source.english:
“You could say
that. But it suited me perfectly.
No destination had been specified.
I didn't mind.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I suppose you could say that. But it suited my purposes just fine. No particular destination had been specified either. But that still didn't bother me.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「飽きたら降りればいいだけだったし」
source.english: “If I grew bored, I could simply get off.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そいつぁ不用心に過ぎるってもんだぜ泪さん。見ての通り無頼船だ。その手紙だって、なにかの罠ってコトもありうる」
source.english: “That's far too careless, Rui. As you can see, it's a lawless ship. That letter might have been a trap.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あなたを呼ぶだけ呼んで、身ぐるみ剥ぐなりどっかに売り飛ばすなり、そういう事だって有り得たろう」
source.english: “They might have lured you here just to strip you of everything or sell you somewhere.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「無事に戻れる降りられる、そういう保証なんてどこにもないじゃないかい。最悪、喉を耳元までかッ切られて、夜の海に投げ捨てられる……そんな憂き目だって見たかもしれんぜ、なあ」
source.english: “There was no guarantee you could leave safely, was there? At worst, they might have cut your throat from ear to ear and thrown you into the sea at night. You could have suffered that, you know.”

source.japanese:
信天翁号の船員達は、一度機嫌を損ねてしまったなら、不心得な客などどう扱うか知れたものではない。船内では刺すにも絞めるにも格好の暗がりなど幾らでもあるし、四方は海、投げこまれたとしてもその時文句の言える状態であるかは怪しい、その上機関長も言っている。主罐に入れてしまえば、人間など蒼い火ばかりで骨さえ残らない、と。
　想えばこの無頼の船員達の中で、泪のような一件無防備な富者が五体満足でいるのは希有な事だった。
source.english:
Once the Albatross's sailors took offense, there was no telling how they might treat an ill-advised passenger. The ship had any number of dark corners ideal for stabbing or strangling. Sea on every side: someone thrown overboard might not be in any condition to complain. Besides, the chief engineer said that a human put into the main boiler left nothing but blue flames, not even bones. Come to think of it,
that an apparently defenseless wealthy person like Rui remained intact among these lawless sailors was a rare thing indeed.

target.text: 【Rui】 「I could simply disembark whenever I should lose interest.」
【Naomasa】 「And that's what I'm saying is waaay too careless of you, Rui-san. This is a ship full of villains, as is plain to see. Even that letter itself could, very possibly, have been a trap.」

【Naomasa】 「Maybe they just wanted to lure you over, strip you of all your belongings, the clothes on your back included, then sell you off somewhere. Even something like that was only all too possible.」

【Naomasa】 「There's no guarantee at all that you'd just be allowed to return to land without incident. Worst case scenario, you could have been sliced open from throat to ear, then dumped into the sea at night……that's the kind of tragic fate that could have awaited you, alright?」

If the crew of the Albatross had found themselves offended but a single time, it was impossible to say what treatment awaited any imprudent passengers. Within the ship, there were more than enough dark corners perfectly suited for stabbing or strangling, there was nothing but ocean in all directions, and even should someone be moments from being tossed into the depths, it was doubtful they would be in any state to make their objections, and on top of all that, the Chief Engineer himself had said it. That if thrown inside the main boiler, a man would be reduced to naught but greenish-blue flames, with not even bones remaining.
Now that he thought about it, placed amidst this crew of scoundrels, the fact that a lone, vulnerable, wealthy lady like Rui was still sound in wind and limb was a miracle.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あれ、そういえば」
source.english: “Oh. Now that you mention it…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あれってあなた……。いつか言っていたじゃないか。自分は肉の快楽の為だけに生きる。けれどそれは生きていてこそ味わえるって」
source.english: “'Oh,' she says… You once told me you lived only for the pleasures of flesh. But that you could enjoy them only while alive.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そういうのこそ、なんて言うのか、命だけは大事にしないといけないんじゃないの？」
source.english: “Wouldn't that mean—how can I put it—you ought at least to value your life?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Oh my, now that you mention it.」

【Naomasa】 「"Oh my", she says……. Didn't you say it like this the other day? That you live solely for the purpose of carnal pleasure. But that it's only by virtue of being alive that you can still savour it.」
【Naomasa】 「Isn't that exactly the sort of attitude where, how do I put it, your life is the one thing that you really have to take good care of?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ふぅん……直さんはそういう女を許して下さるって？」
source.english: “Hmm… So you'd approve of a woman like that, Nao?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「許すもなにも───あなたはもう、ずっとそういう風に生きてきたんだろうしなあ」
source.english: “Approve? You've already lived that way all this time…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いったいどれだけ、そうやって過ごしてきたんですかね泪さんは」
source.english: “How long have you been living like that, anyway?”

source.japanese:
塩辛入道の住まいでの一幕が朔屋の脳裏に蘇る。あそこで出会った老人が、妖怪譚中の住人ならば、同類だという泪だって星霜の歳月を経てきたことも充分あり得る。
　ただ女性というものは年齢を知られることを厭うもの。偽り口を噤むもの。だから朔屋は訊いてしまった後で失言と、そしてどうせ答えてはくれないだろうと臍を噛んだのだけれど。
source.english:
The scene in the Salty Monk's dwelling returned to his mind. If that old man belonged in monster tales, then Rui, who said she was of his kind, could easily have lived through great stretches of time.
But women disliked their ages being known. They lied, or held their tongues. Having asked, Sakuya regretted his blunder—and thought she would never answer anyway.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Oh……so are you saying that you will condone a woman like that, Nao-san?」
【Naomasa】 「There is nothing to condone─── I'm sure you must have led a life like that for a long, long time by now.」
【Naomasa】 「I really do wonder just how long exactly you have been living life like that, Rui-san.」

Sakuya recalled the scene that played out in Shiokara-nyuudou's abode in his mind. The old man he'd met there, if he was a denizen of tales of the supernatural, then it was perfectly possible that Rui, supposedly of a similar sort, had lived through the passing of countless seasons. However, women were loath to let their age be known. They were the sort who would seal the lips of others with little white lies. Therefore, after asking, when Sakuya realized his slip of the tongue, he was certain that she'd most likely not answer him after all, and he could only bitterly regret his blunder, but.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……わたくしにもよく判らなくて。
　なにしろ途中から年を数えることが面倒になってしまったし……ええと……」
source.english:
“…I'm not very sure myself.
At some point, counting the years grew tiresome… Let's see…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、いい、
　無理に数えようとしなくても」
source.english:
“No, never mind.
You needn't force yourself to count.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……Even I am not entirely certain. For you see, it grew bothersome to count the years somewhere along the way……let me think……」
【Naomasa】 「No, it's fine, you don't have to go out of your way to count every single year.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ええと……それでも、直さんが生まれてくる前から、こんな風だったことは確か」
source.english: “Well… I was certainly like this before you were born, Nao.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Let's see……even so, it is certain that I have lived in this way since before you were born, Nao-san.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───貴方達の数え方で言うなら、もう随分とお婆ちゃんね、わたくし」
source.english: “By your way of counting, I'm quite an old woman now.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやあ、見た目が若ければそれで問題ないし、それにあなたの体ときたら婆さんどころか───あ。俺ってばなにを」
source.english: “Well, if you look young, there's no problem. And your body is hardly an old woman's—Ah. What am I saying?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「───Going by your way of counting age, I suppose I am already quite the granny.」
【Naomasa】 「Hey now, as long as you still look young, that's good enough for me, and when it comes to your body, forget grannies, it's more like ───ah. Come on, what am I even saying.」

source.japanese: 泪が人外のモノである事を、朔屋はこの期に及んでも半信半疑である。人外、というからには人の外にあってかけ離れているモノであるはずだが（例えばあの魚怪共のように）、泪はとてもそうとは見えず、手足目鼻立ち、朔屋と数は変わらず、洋装で覆われた肌に銀鱗でも生えていてくれればまだそれらしいものを、その肌はただただ艶[なま]めかしさを塗りこめて、そこらの人妻など及びもつかないほどに美しい、男なら誰しも唇を強く押し当て自分の痕を残したくなるような魔性を秘めて───自分の、痕？　と朔屋はふと思った。
source.english: Even now, Sakuya remained half doubtful that Rui was something other than human. Something inhuman ought to stand outside humanity, far removed from it—like those fish-monsters. Yet Rui looked nothing of the sort. Her limbs, her eyes and nose: the same number as his own. If silver scales grew on the skin beneath her dress, she might have looked the part.
