But that skin was only steeped in sensual beauty, far beyond any ordinary married woman's, with a fatal allure that would make any man want to press his lips hard against it and leave his mark—His mark? Sakuya suddenly wondered.

source.japanese: 泪との交わりの果ては、いずれも彼女の腹の中に深く差しこんで、何も遮[さえぎ]るものなく考えなしに流しこんだけれど、彼女はそれをむしろせがんで、悦の歔欷で迎えた。
source.english: At the end of each coupling with Rui, he had thrust deep inside her belly and heedlessly poured himself into her, with nothing between them. She had even begged for it, welcoming him with sobs of pleasure.

target.text: Even after all that had happened, Sakuya was still dubious about the idea of Rui being something inhuman. By definition, something deemed inhuman ought to be an existence far removed from us (to offer an example, like those fish monsters), but Rui certainly did not seem like that at all

In terms of limbs and facial features, she didn't differ in count from Sakuya, and had there been silvery scales growing over the skin concealed by her dress, then she would at least look the part, but her skin was plastered in nothing but a seductive sheen, possessed of a beauty that no ordinary married woman could ever hope to match, hiding a bewitching allure that would make any man want to press his lips hard against her skin and leave a mark of themselves on her───a mark, of themselves? The thought suddenly ran through Sakuya's mind.

At the end of his intercourse with Rui, he would invariably be thrust deep into her stomach, and with nothing to obstruct him, he would heedlessly pour his essence within her, and if anything, she would pester him for it, welcoming it with quivering sobs of delight.

source.japanese: それは、陸の者と海の者では実る実のないと言う事だからなのだろうか───
source.english: Was that because no fruit could ripen between one of the land and one of the sea?

source.japanese: と、少々生々しく思考は傾いたけれど、泪との情交を想い出して朔屋の鼻の下が盛大に伸びる。ただ惜しむらくはそのいずれの時も、凍えきった体を癒す為であったり、鬱期に陥っていたりで、朔屋としては本調子ではなくて、それが今となっては悔やまれる───が。
source.english: His thoughts took a somewhat graphic turn, and recalling their intimacy made Sakuya grin lecherously. The only pity was that neither time had he been at his best: recovering from the cold, or sunk in depression. Now he regretted it. But—

source.japanese:
朔屋としては珍しく真面目な話をしているつもりであったのに、ついつい色気を出してしまって、格好つけたのが台無しだ、という。
　しかし泪は、鈴の転[まろ]ぶに似た、華やかな音で笑って見せたものだった。
source.english:
He had meant to speak seriously, unusual though that was for him. Letting lust show had ruined his attempt to look impressive.
Rui, however, laughed with a bright sound like a rolling bell.

target.text: Was that perhaps because no fruit could be born between those of the land and those of the sea───

His thoughts drifted in a slightly graphic direction, but having remembered his intimacy with Rui, Sakuya's face broke into a grand, lecherous smile. The only thing he truly regretted was that, on every occasion so far, it had been to heal his frozen body, or he'd fallen into depression; Sakuya had yet to be in his regular form, and it was something he'd come to lament now───but.

It was one of those rare times where Sakuya meant to talk earnestly, yet he still could not help but be carried away by his sexual urges, completely ruining his attempts at affectations. However, Rui only laughed, a gorgeously sparkling sound reminiscent of a tinkling bell.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ふふ……っ、気に入ってもらえたのなら、
　わたくしだって満更じゃない。
　でも久しぶりよ、そういう殿方は」
source.english:
“Hehe… If you liked me, I can hardly complain.
It's been a long time
since I met a gentleman like that.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Huhu……, if it is to your liking, then I am not entirely opposed to the idea either. But still, it has been ages since I met a gentleman like yourself.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしの出自に気づかれた殿方というのは余りいなかったけれど、時々はそれでも平気と、構わないとおっしゃる方もいらしたっけ。直さんも、そう」
source.english: “Not many men noticed my origins. But now and then there was one who said he didn't mind, who was quite all right with it. You're like that too, Nao.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやだって、いつまでも若い嫁さんって、
　野郎にとっては一つの理想だもの」
source.english:
“Well, a wife who stays young forever
is one of a man's ideals.”

source.japanese:
それは自分の方が先に老いることに実感がない、若者特有の身勝手な理想なのかも知れないけれど。
　老いてなお、若き肉体に慰めを見出す男とていないわけでもない。閨の事だけでなく、晩境の話し相手として、同年代の乾いた鶴よりより若い花を喜ぶ者はいる。
source.english:
Perhaps it was a young man's selfish ideal, born of having no real sense that he would age first.
Yet there were men who found comfort in young flesh even in old age. Not merely in bed. For company in their declining years, some preferred a young flower to a dried-up crane of their own generation.

target.text: 【Rui】 「While there have never been many gentlemen who realized my origins at all, from time to time, there were those who would claim to still be fine with it, who would insist it didn't matter, I do believe. Like you, Nao-san.」
【Naomasa】 「Well, I mean, it's just that having a wife who stays young forever, that's one of those fantasies shared by every guy out there.」

Perhaps it was just an egotistical ideal peculiar to the young, to those who could not yet imagine themselves aging before she would. It was not as though there weren't any men who, having grown old, now discovered comfort in the flesh of the young. And there were also those who found greater joy in the company of youthful flowers over the withered cranes of their own generation, not just in the bedchambers, but also as someone to talk with in their twilight years.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「まあ、ね。そういう方と出会えるのなら、未練がましく世の中をぶらぶらしている甲斐もあるっていうこと」
source.english: “Well, yes. Meeting someone like that makes it worthwhile to linger in the world, unable to let it go.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I suppose. If I could encounter such a person, then perhaps that means clinging to this world and drifting through it did carry some worth after all.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「直さんもそうじゃないかしらと、ぼんやり想っていた───いいえ、願っていたのかな。
　ええ、悪くないわ、貴方」
source.english:
“I'd vaguely thought you might be like that. No—perhaps hoped.
Yes, you're not bad.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「気に入ってもらえたのならなにより。
　それなら早速、今晩この後どうだろう」
source.english:
“Glad you like me. In that case,
why don't we get straight to it tonight?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I used to idly wonder that, perhaps, you might be like that too, Nao-san───no, I suppose I was hoping for it. Yes, you are not bad at all, dear.」
【Naomasa】 「I'll count myself lucky if I suit your tastes. That being the case, how does later this evening sound?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あら。今夜は直さんにしては乗り気でいらっしゃる……でもどうしようかしら……」
source.english: “Oh. You're quite eager tonight, for you… But what shall I do…?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Goodness. You are unusually eager tonight, Nao-san……but what to do, I wonder……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「今夜の貴方、とってもお優しいんですもの。
　そういう時は、お話だけにしておいて、次の時まで気分を育てた方が、もっと愉[たの]しい事になる」
source.english:
“You're so kind tonight.
At such times, it's more enjoyable to keep to conversation and let the feeling grow until next time.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「You have been awfully kind tonight. And in times like these, leaving things at simple conversation, then letting that anticipation grow until next we meet, would make for a much more delightful experience.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「というのがわたくしの、
　長年の経験からの───あっ？」
source.english:
“That is the conclusion
of my many years of experience—Ah?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「That is what my many long years of experience tells me───ah?」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おっとっ、あ……っと！」
source.english: “Whoa—Ah!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Whoa, ah……hold on!」

source.japanese: 今までは誘う風だったのが、その気になれば遠ざかる、その小面憎い呼吸が男女の駆け引きなのかも知れないが、朔屋がやきもきとなりかかったところで、船の横揺れだ。
source.english: She had seemed to invite him, then drew away when he became willing. Perhaps that mildly infuriating rhythm was the game between men and women. Just as Sakuya began to fret, the ship rolled.

target.text: Hitherto, she had been doing the tempting, but as soon as he was so minded, she pulled away,; maybe these cheeky tricks were simply part of the dance between men and women, but just as Sakuya was beginning to grow impatient, the ship rolled.

source.japanese: 少し船が揺らいで、台の上に置いてあった望遠鏡が甲板に落ちて、海に転がり落ちかける。あっと二人揃って手を伸ばした、望遠鏡は掴んだけれど、慌ただしい動きに、緩慢に滞留していたせっかくの甘い空気が、吹き散らされてしまって、波の音もどこかよそよそしいし、バラックの隙間で眠る信天翁君の、眠りを乱された文句の夜鳴きが間抜けていた。
source.english: A slight sway sent the telescope from the stand onto the deck, where it nearly rolled into the sea. Both reached for it with a cry. They caught it, but the hurried movement scattered the sweet atmosphere that had so slowly gathered. Even the waves sounded distant now. An albatross sleeping in a gap between the shacks complained at the disturbance of its slumber. Its night cry sounded absurd.

target.text: The ship shook slightly, and the telescope he had placed atop the table fell down on the deck, about to roll down into the ocean. Letting out a surprised "ah", they both reached out for the telescope, and while they did manage to grab it, the abrupt, panicked movement scattered that enticingly sweet atmosphere that had lingered between them, that they had so painstakingly built; even the sound of the waves began to sound distant and cold, and the nocturnal squawks of Mr. Albatross who had been asleep somewhere between the shacks, a complaint at having his slumber disturbed, sounded comically silly.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「今、ちょっとかしゃんって鳴ったけれど、壊れた？」
source.english: “There was a little clink just now. Did it break?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、大丈夫みたいだ。少し焦ったけど」
source.english: “No, it seems all right. Gave me a fright, though.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It made a little clinking noise just then, but is it broken?」
【Naomasa】 「No, it seems to be fine. I got a little scared there.」

source.japanese:
気遣わしげに覗きこむ泪からは、寸前までの思わせぶりな媚色は綺麗に失せて、今夜の機会を逃してしまった事を覚り、朔屋はついへの字口になったが、すぐに緩んだ。
　青年の方から彼女に対してその気になった時に限って、水が差される事に諧謔を見た為ではない。
source.english:
Rui leaned in to look, concerned. The suggestive allure of a moment earlier had vanished completely. Realizing he had lost tonight's opportunity, Sakuya's mouth drooped, then soon relaxed.
Not because he saw humor in how something spoiled his chance whenever he was the one to desire her.

source.japanese: 今夜は泪もどこかしらその気で、触れなば落ちん風情ではあったけれど、日を替えて、全く前触れもなく、たとえば船内通路の暗がりに誘いこんで、その臀を掴んでやったら、性に慣れた彼女でも、驚かせてやれるのではないか、柳眉が逆立ったら、退屈しのぎにならないかと言い放ってやればいい。
source.english: Tonight Rui had seemed somewhat willing too, ready to fall at a touch. But another day, without any warning—say, drawing her into a dark passageway and grabbing her ass—might let him surprise even this sexually experienced woman. If her fine brows rose in anger, he could declare: doesn't it relieve your boredom?

source.japanese: そちらの方を選んでしまえば気が軽くなって、口調も暢気になる朔屋だった。
source.english: Choosing that prospect lightened his mood. His voice grew carefree too.

target.text: The suggestive, flirtatious look she'd worn just moments before was now completely gone from Rui's eyes as she anxiously looked into his, and realizing that he'd missed his chance tonight, Sakuya's mouth subconsciously slipped into a frown before it quickly slackened again. And it was not because he found some ironic amusement in the fact that, whenever he finally got in the mood to take things further with her, something would inevitably throw a damper on things.

Something about Rui tonight had felt that way: pliant, like she would give in when met with the softest of pushes, but if he waited for another day to arrive and, for example, without the slightest of warnings, lured her into a dim corner of the ship's passageways, then squeezed her buttocks tightly, surely even a woman as seasoned in the sensual as her would be shocked, and when her lissome brows rose in indignation, he could just make some quip about it being a way to stave off her boredom.
Once he decided on that course of action, Sakuya's heart felt lighter, and even his manner of speech turned carefree.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……思えばこれ、この望遠鏡は泪さんからもらったようなものだが、いやあん時も怖かった。なにしろ拳銃突きつけられるなんて、そうそうないぜ」
source.english: “…Come to think of it, I more or less got this telescope from you. That was frightening too. Having a pistol pointed at you isn't exactly an everyday event.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……もっとも、この船に乗ってからは、ちょくちょくそういう場面に出くわすよなあ。
　勘弁願いたいもんだ」
source.english:
“Though since coming aboard this ship, I do find myself in that situation rather often.
I'd like to be spared.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……Thinking back on it, this telescope was kind of something I got from you, Rui-san, but damn, that was so scary. I mean, I had a gun thrust right into my face, and that doesn't happen very often.」
【Naomasa】 「……Then again, ever since boarding this ship, I've run into situations like that pretty often, huh. I could really do without that.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしには、直さんの心がけのようにも思えるけれど」
source.english: “It seems to me it has something to do with your conduct.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It strikes me more as a reflection of your attitude, Nao-san.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしと違って、退屈はしないでしょうね、そういう毎日なら───そうか」
source.english: “Unlike me, you must never be bored with days like that—Oh.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Quite unlike me, I'm certain you aren't bored, living through days like those───I see.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そうなのねえ……貴方は」
source.english: “I see… So that's how you are.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「So that is what it is…… you are───」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「よしてくれ、なんだか死にたくなってくる。
　ところで泪さん、あなたにはこれ、なんて書いてあるか判ります？」
source.english:
“Stop it. You're making me want to die.
By the way, Rui, can you tell what this says?”

source.japanese: 望遠鏡は幸いどこも壊れた様子はなかったけれど、泪がここに来る前から気にかかっていたことを、あるいは彼女ならと訊ねてみる。左見右見してみると、この望遠鏡の飾り彫りの端の方には、なにごとかのアルファベットの一文が刻まれてある。英語であれば朔屋にもいくらかの見当が付くのだが、単語の結構からして異なっていては手が出ない。
source.english: Fortunately, the telescope seemed undamaged. Something had intrigued him even before Rui came. Perhaps she would know. Turning it this way and that revealed a sentence in Roman letters engraved at one edge of the decorative carving. English he could have made something of. But the very construction of the words was different, leaving him helpless.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Cut that out, please, it's making me want to die for some reason. By the way, Rui-san, can you understand what's written on it, the stuff down here?」

Fortunately, the telescope didn't seem to be broken anywhere, and he decided to try asking about something that had been weighing on his mind since before Rui came, thinking that, perhaps, if it was her, he could get an answer. If one gave it a proper look all around, one would see that, along the edge of the telescope's decorative engravings, there was a short line of letters carved into it. Had it been in English, then even Sakuya would have been able to make some guesses, but based on the construction of the words, it was something else, so it was well beyond his grasp.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「見せて───そうね、これは仏蘭西語。意味としては……」
source.english: “Let me see—Yes, this is French. It means…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Let me have a look───I see, this is French. And its meaning would be……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「『ルイ・エミール・ベルタン氏へ。
【ゆぬびぃし】？　を造りし記念に
　これを捧げる』
　そんな風なところ」
source.english:
“‘Presented to Mr. Louis Émile Bertin
in commemoration of the construction
of… Yunubishi?…’
Something like that.”

source.japanese: この時泪が発音した【ゆぬびぃし】のユ音はウ音との中間のような音だったが、どちらにしても朔屋には心当たりもない名前で、むしろ興味ひかれたのは、
source.english: The first vowel in Rui's Yunubishi sounded somewhere between “yoo” and “oo.” In any case, Sakuya did not recognize the name. What interested him more was—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ルイ……って。
　あなたのことじゃなかろうな」
source.english:
“Louis…
Doesn't mean you, does it?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「『To Mr. Louis-Emile Bertin. In commemoration of the construction of the【Unbish】? We grant this to you.』 Something along those lines.」 (TN: Louis-Emile Bertin was a French naval engineer, and he built many modern warships and naval facilities in Japan for the Imperial Japanese Navy as a special advisor from 1886-1890.)

When Rui pronounced the【Unbish】here, the "u" sound seemed to fall somewhere in between the Japanese "yu" and "u", but regardless of which it was, it was a name that didn't ring any bells with Sakuya; what actually caught his attention was:
【Naomasa】 「Louis……you say. I'm going to guess that's not you, right?」 (TN: In Japanese, Rui and Louis are both pronounced Rui (ルイ), hence Sakuya's confusion.)

source.japanese:
【泪】
「いいえ、たまさか同じなだけで、この方は男性でしょう」
source.english: “No, it is merely a coincidence. The gentleman must have been a man.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「No, we just happen to share a name by coincidence, for this person is a man.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「なにかを造った記念の品だったみたい。望遠鏡なんてものを記念にするのは───」
source.english: “It seems to have marked the construction of something. A telescope as a commemorative gift—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「天文学者とか？　ああ、船乗りって事もあるか。あの博打打ちがなんだってこんな代物を持っていたのかは知らないけど」
source.english: “An astronomer? Oh, or a sailor. I don't know why that gambler had a thing like this.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「巡り巡って船に戻ってきたと……よりにもよってこんなオンボロ船でなくっても良さそうなもんだが」
source.english: “So it's made its way back to a ship… You'd think it could have found something better than this wreck, of all vessels.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「It seems to be an article made in commemoration of the construction of something. And as for what a telescope of all things would commemorate───」
【Naomasa】 「An astronomer maybe? Ahh, could also be a sailor, right? Why that professional gambler was carrying something like this around is still a mystery to me, but.」
【Naomasa】 「To think it would come full circle and return to a ship……but of all the ships, it really didn't have to be this rust bucket.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「世の中の縁というのは、案外そういうものなんでしょうね」
source.english: “The ties between things in this world can be surprisingly like that.”

source.japanese: 身じろぎしかかった、情の獣を抑えつけたのはさて朔屋の方だけだったのか。青年は気づかずにいたのだが、望遠鏡をためつすがめつする彼に、泪は眼差し、情慾に潤ませて、身を乗りだしかかったのである。朔屋の額に口づけしようとでも言うように。泪が踏み越えて、唇が触れていたなら、月影の下、二つの影は一つに重なったろうが───
source.english: Was Sakuya the only one who had restrained the stirring beast of desire? He never noticed, but as he examined the telescope from every angle, Rui gazed at him with eyes moist with longing and almost leaned toward him. As though to kiss his forehead. Had she crossed the boundary, had her lips touched him, the two shadows would have joined as one beneath the moon. But—

source.japanese: この様にして、夜は燃え盛るような情事もなく、静かな語らいのうちに更けていった。
source.english: Thus the night deepened in quiet conversation, without a blazing affair.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Contrary to expectations, I suppose fate does tend to work out that way in this world of ours, no?」

Perhaps Sakuya was the only one who had managed to restrain the beast of passions that had begun to stir within? The young man himself never noticed, but as Sakuya took a closer look at the telescope from all sides, the gaze Rui sent his way was damp with desire, and she loomed over him. As if she were about to press her lips against Sakuya's forehead. Had Rui crossed that line, touched him with her lips, then their two shadows would surely have merged into one beneath the glow of the moon, but───
Thus, the night remained unlit by any brightly burning flames of passion, advancing as they peacefully chatted it away.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ようクロ。交替だよ」
source.english: “Hey, Kuro. Time to change over.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Hey, Kuro. Here to relieve you.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「クロ……交替だってば。
　あんたもしかして、
　居眠りしてたな……？」
source.english:
“Kuro… We said,
change over.
Have you been dozing…?”

source.japanese: 上甲板中央の物見櫓の上で、当直に就いていたクロと交替の為に上がってきた双子は、白子の娘が櫓台の柵に貼りついて身じろぎもしていないのに、やや気色を荒げる。
source.english: The twins had climbed to the lookout tower amidships to relieve Kuro on watch. She was pressed against the platform's rail, not moving at all. Their mood grew a little sharp.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Kuro……we said it's time to switch. You weren't, by any chance, dozing off, were you……?」

Atop the watchtower in the middle of the upper deck, the twins had climbed all the way up to relieve Kuro of her watch, but despite the albino girl plastering herself against the railing of the tower platform and not stirring in the slightest, she seemed a little agitated.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……あ。う、ううん。寝てない。
　クロ、寝てないよ。見てただけ」
source.english:
“…Ah. N-no. Not sleeping.
Kuro wasn't sleeping. Just looking.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Ah. N-, no. Not sleeping. Kuro, not sleeping. Just looking.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……あ。ううん、見てない、クロはなんにも、寝てない。ううん、見てない」
source.english: “…Ah. No, not looking. Kuro wasn't looking at anything, not sleeping. No, not looking.”

source.japanese: あわあわと両手を前で泳がせながら首を振るクロの、これほど判りやすい肯定のジェスチュアもあるまい。
source.english: Kuro shook her head, both hands flailing in front of her. There could hardly have been a clearer gesture of admission.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Ah. No, not looking, Kuro, slept nothing. No, wasn't looking.」
Seeing Kuro flapping her hands frantically and shaking her head in a panic, there could hardly be a more blatant gesture of affirmation.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「つまりなにか気になるものを覗いてたって訳だ。あんたがなにをそんなに気にしてたんだか」
source.english: “So you were peeping at something that caught your attention. What had you so interested?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「In other words, you were peeping on something that caught your interest. Now what could possibly get you so worked up?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「今さらこの船の上甲板なんか見慣れたもんだろうに……」
source.english: “Surely you're used to the upper deck by now…”

source.japanese:

source.japanese:
月満ちて───海は太陰に引かれて水平線をこんもり盛りあげて、月が白金の盆なら海は銀の盆、と凪渡った。
　しかし狂疾的（ｌｕｎａｔｉｃ）の語源でもあるように、あまりに清[さや]かで大盆の月は人の心を惑わせて狂気の淵に誘い、月面では兎が杵で搗[つ]くのも人肉饅頭に替えるとか。常人でさえ満月の夜には体の底にうずうずと狂騒の芽生え覚えるものを、この外道揃いの信天翁号に於いてはさぞかし目も当てられない騒ぎの勃発していよう、と思いきや。
　今宵もまた、信天翁号は不可思議な静けさに包まれてある。
source.english:
The moon was full. Drawn by it, the sea swelled at the horizon and lay calm: if the moon was a platinum tray, the sea was a silver one.
Yet, as the origin of lunatic suggests, so clear and broad a moon can bewilder the human mind and lure it to the brink of madness. Even the rabbit pounding with its pestle up there might switch to buns filled with human flesh. Ordinary people feel the seeds of frenzy stirring deep within them on a full-moon night. Surely aboard the Albatross, packed with such depraved souls, some appalling commotion must be breaking out.
Or so one might think. Tonight, too, the Albatross lay wrapped in an uncanny stillness.

source.japanese: マイナスとマイナスが乗算されるとプラスに転ずるように、外因的な狂気には信天翁号の面子、かえって心が薙ぐのかも知れないがその辺りの原因はどうあれ、船内には通路の端々、船室の隅々にまで、平穏が横溢し、それいっそ気怠いと言ってもいいほどの。
source.english: Perhaps, as multiplying a negative by a negative yields a positive, madness imposed from outside calmed this company instead. Whatever the cause, peace overflowed through every passageway and into every corner of every cabin. So much peace that one might almost call it languor.

target.text: It was a full moon───the ocean was pulled by the moon, lifting the horizon into a rounded swell, and if the moon was a tray of platinum, then the ocean was one of silver as it glided over the tranquil waters.

However, just as the etymology of the word "lunatic" would imply, a great full moon that casts too pure a radiant light will lead astray the hearts of men, tempting them deeper into the abyss of madness, where even the rabbit on the moon, pounding away with her mallet, trades her mochi for human flesh. Even ordinary people feel the restless seeds of mania throbbing deep within their bodies on a night of the full moon, so in this gathering of fiends that was the Albatross, there would surely be outbursts of disturbances so ghastly one couldn't bear to look, or so one would think. Tonight, the Albatross was once again enshrouded in an inexplicable stillness.

Just as two negative numbers shift to a positive number when multiplied, when met with madness wrought by outside forces, perhaps the crew of the Albatross instead found their hearts steadied by it, but regardless of the cause, tranquility seeped through the passageways, it inundated the cabins and reached into every little nook and cranny, to the point one might as well call it listlessness.

source.japanese:
垂れこめる静穏に、水夫長も航海士も、そして機関長辺りも、下級水夫の監督の手を休め、思い思いに夜の物憂さをやり過ごそうとしている。
　双子は上甲板で夜釣りと竿を二本並べ、ただ一々脈も中りも取らず、魚の引きを聴くのは竿先に着けた鈴に任せてやる気無さげだ。
　水夫長は今晩は下級水夫を読み聞かせの番から外してやり、秘蔵の大型四つ折り本、エリザベス朝戯曲集を独り黙読だが、目はどうしても活字を上滑りして、しまいには頁を閉じて皮紙の背を漫然と撫でているだけとなる。
source.english:
Beneath that pall of stillness, the boatswain, the navigator twins, and even the chief engineer relaxed their watch over the junior sailors, each seeking a private way to see the night's melancholy through.
On the upper deck, the twins had laid out two rods for a little night fishing, but could not be bothered to feel for every twitch or strike, leaving the bells fixed to the rod tips to heed the fishes' tug.
The boatswain had excused the juniors from reading aloud that evening and settled down alone with his prized great quarto of Elizabethan plays; but his eyes would only skate over the type, until at last he shut the book and sat absently stroking its vellum spine.

source.japanese:
機関長の姿は機関室に見えない───いや、いる。影の中に引き籠もって敢えて視覚を閉ざし（それとも見えているのか？）、脳内の『記憶の宮殿』の内部を逍遥中だ。大小取り混ぜて一千もの部屋がある大宮殿だが、訪れる度に間取りが変わっており、入りこんだが最後、機関長は一晩でも微動だにせず脳内を彷徨い続ける。
　船長クロは、今夜は端仕事からも解放され、はやばや寝台に入って、一日の間に縺[もつ]れてしまった白い髪の結び瘤を解こうと一生懸命だ。
source.english:
The chief engineer was nowhere to be seen in the engine room—no, there he was. Holed up in the shadows, he had deliberately closed off his sight (or could he see after all?) and was roaming the “memory palace” within his mind. It was a vast palace of a thousand rooms large and small, but its floor plan changed with every visit, and once he strayed inside, the chief engineer would wander its halls all night without so much as twitching a muscle.
Captain Kuro, freed even from her chores tonight, had gone early to her bunk and was hard at work untying the knots her white hair had tangled itself into over the course of the day.

source.japanese:
このようにこの船にしては、平和で穏やかな静けさ。全ての者を静かな眠りに引きこむような。
　朔屋もまた、この静けさに眠気がひどくて、厨房での洗い物の最中何度も船を漕ぎ、洗い水から皿を上げ損なって二枚割り、隠すのに右往左往していた。ようやく見つけた隠し場所、と思うた窪みに溜まっていた影は、影ではない。窪みは宗右衛門の寝場所の一つで、影と見えたのは毛並み豊かな腹の皮であり、皿の破片を押しこんでしまう寸前で朔屋が気づいたからいいものの、さもなくば顔一面に四筋の傷痕を刻まれてちょいとオツな面相に成り果てていただろう。
source.english:
Thus a peaceful, gentle stillness, unusual for this ship. A stillness that seemed to draw everyone into quiet sleep.
Sakuya too was dreadfully drowsy. Washing up in the galley, he nodded off repeatedly, failed to lift two plates from the wash water, broke them, and scurried about trying to hide the pieces. At last he found what seemed a suitable recess. But the shadow filling it was not a shadow. The recess was one of Soemon's sleeping places; the darkness was his luxuriantly furred belly. Fortunately Sakuya noticed just before pushing the broken crockery inside. Otherwise four stripes of scars across his face would have given him a rather striking new appearance.

target.text: As the serenity hung over them, the Bosun and the first mates alike, and the Chief Engineer too, had all paused their supervision of the deck boys, letting the languid air of this night pass them by in the way they each preferred. The twins were night fishing on the upper deck, two poles lined up next to each other, but they didn't even so much as bother checking the line or watching for a bite, they just let the little bell tied to the tip of the rod tell them if a fish was biting, all with an air of utter disinterest.

The Bosun had relieved the deck boys from their assigned watch of reading aloud for the night, instead pulling out the pearl of his collection, a large quarto volume that contained a collection of Elizabethan plays that he had been reading in solitary silence, his eyes only sliding superficially across the letters no matter how hard he tried, until finally, he folded the pages shut, contenting himself with absentmindedly stroking the vellum spine of the tome and nothing more.

In the engine room, the Chief Engineer was nowhere to be seen───no, he was in there. Confining himself to the shadows, purposely shutting out his sense of sight (or perhaps he could still see?), taking a stroll through the interior of the『Palace of Memories』 within his brain. It was a grand palace, one that boasted of a thousand rooms of all shapes and sizes jumbled together; whenever he would visit, the layout would change, and once he had stepped inside, the Chief Engineer would continue to wander around his mind all night without moving an inch.

Captain Kuro had also been relieved of her chores tonight, and so she climbed into bed early, fighting with all her might to unravel the knots in her hair that had formed as it tangled together all throughout the day.

Like so, considering the ship, it was a peaceful, gentle silence. One that seemed to lull all present into a serene slumber. Sakuya also found himself terribly drowsy from the hush, and he nodded off several times while in the middle of washing the dishes in the galley; he botched pulling the plates out of the wash water, ultimately breaking two, and was running about this way and that in an attempt to hide the evidence. He finally found a hiding place, or so he thought, but the shadows pooling in that hollow were no shadows at all.

The hollow was one of Souemon's places to sleep, and what he thought were shadows instead turned out to be the luxuriant fur growing from the skin of the cat's stomach, and while it was fortunate that Sakuya had noticed that while still only on the verge of shoving broken pieces of plates into him, else his entire face would have had four lines of scars carved into it, he probably ended up with a bit of a queer look on his face.

source.japanese: それでもどうにか今夜の仕事を片やっつけて、後は自室のベッドにぐん伸びるばかりと大欠伸生欠伸で通路を戻る途中に見かけたのは。
source.english: Still, he somehow dispatched the night's work, and now had only to return to his room and stretch himself out full-length on the bed. Yawning prodigiously, he was making his way back along the passage when he happened upon—

target.text: Nevertheless, he somehow managed to finish tonight's tasks, and all that was left to do now was to flop down onto the bed in his own cabin and stretch out his limbs, or so he thought with many a great yawn, but then, he spotted something while heading back through the passageway.

source.japanese: 上甲板からの昇降段の陰の暗がりで何事かを低く語らい合う、白の着物に灰黒の袴[はかま]、一方が和を着崩しているなら一方は紺青のドレスの、美々しく洋式に装って、片やこの戦後の世代にあっては時代遅れであり、片やこの長く打ち続く不景気の世の中にあっては華美に過ぎ、いずれも世相から外れてはいたのに、おんぼろ船の影に置いてみると奇妙な調和を見せた。
source.english: In the darkness beneath the companionway from the upper deck, two figures spoke together in low voices. One wore a white kimono and gray-black hakama, his Japanese dress hanging loose about him; the other was splendidly arrayed in Western fashion in a deep-blue gown. The one was antiquated for this postwar generation, the other too sumptuous for these long years of depression; both were out of step with the age, yet set in the shadow of the battered old ship, they made a strangely harmonious pair.

source.japanese: この信天翁号自体が、一体何時から海をよろよろ這いずり回っているのかも定かならぬ、時の輪から脱落したような老朽船だったからかも知れない。
source.english: Perhaps because the Albatross itself was an old wreck that seemed to have fallen out of time's wheel. No one knew how long it had been crawling unsteadily about the sea.

source.japanese: だから朔屋が足を留めたのは、およそ女の肉体以外には滅多に発動しない審美眼が作用して、二人の姿に興趣を見た為であり、下卑た出歯亀根性からではない、多分。
source.english: So Sakuya stopped because his eye for beauty, seldom activated by anything other than a woman's body, found something interesting in the two figures. Not from a vulgar urge to peep. Probably.

target.text: In the dark shadows cast by the ladder leading to the upper deck, a conversation was being held in hushed tones about something or other; one party was wearing a greyish-black hakama over his white kimono, his Japanese outfit worn in a relaxed, undone style, and the other wore an indigo dress, adorned in a beautiful, Western style; on the one hand, this was antiquated in this postwar age, and on the other, was overly extravagant for this prolonged chain of recessions, but despite being at odds with the zeitgeist of this age on both counts, it made for a curiously harmonic display when placed within this run-down ship.

It was uncertain exactly when this Albatross herself had first begun to falteringly creep across the seas, so perhaps it was simply that the ship was a decrepit relic that seemed to have somehow fallen out from the turning wheel of time.

Therefore, what made Sakuya stop in his tracks was his aesthetic sense, very seldom put to use on subjects that stretched beyond those related to the female body, stirring from its slumber, for he had perceived something intriguing in their appearance; it was most certainly not something born from his base, voyeuristic nature, probably.

source.english: Tomosato glanced around then, and turned back to Rui without any notable change of expression. But for an instant his blue eyes struck Sakuya like lightning. Sakuya hastily crouched behind a toolbox. Tomosato must already have known exactly where he was.

target.text: After saying that, he suddenly turned around; without betraying any particular reaction to anything, Tomosato turned back again to face Rui once more, but for an instant, those blue eyes pierced Sakuya as though they had emitted a flash of lightning. He crouched down behind a nearby toolbox in a panic, but Tomosato seemed to have already noticed Sakuya's presence there with certainty.

source.japanese: 夜更けを待って、陰に逢う男女二人。どうしても淫靡な意味合いがつきまとうし、泪は泪で多淫な女であること、朔屋も重々承知している。智里にしたところで膏気のないように見えて、あれだって立派な男だ。朔屋の与り知らぬところで、何人の娘を泣かせているのか知れたものではない。むしろ智里の方が朔屋よりもそれにかけては上手なのではあるまいか。
source.english: A man and a woman meeting in the shadows at dead of night: lewd implications inevitably clung to the thing, and Sakuya knew perfectly well what a wanton Rui was. Tomosato, for his part, might look as though he had not a drop of lust in him, but he was a grown man all the same. Who could say how many girls he had made weep beyond Sakuya's ken? Might not Tomosato, indeed, be the more accomplished of the two in such affairs?

source.japanese:
そこまで認識しているのにもかかわらず、朔屋は泪への妬心も智里への反感も覚えず、なにしろ彼自身女関係にてんでだらしないこと自覚しているのだからお話にもならない。
　それになにより、距離があって全てを聴き取れたわけではなかったけれど、二人が語らっていたのはあれは───朔屋の事としか思われなかった。
　そう、智里の請負仕事───朔屋を殺す事。
source.english:
Despite understanding all that, Sakuya felt neither jealousy toward Rui nor resentment toward Tomosato. He knew how hopelessly loose his own dealings with women were. He had no standing to speak.
Above all, though the distance kept him from hearing everything, what the two had been discussing could only have been Sakuya.
Yes: Tomosato's contracted work. Killing Sakuya.

source.japanese: だがこれも、そこまで認識しているのにもかかわらず、朔屋には脱兎でこの場を離れようとかどうにかして船から逃れようとか、そういった危機感をどうしても抱けないでいた。
source.english: Yet despite understanding even that, he could not summon the urgency to flee like a startled rabbit, or somehow escape the ship.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（だよなあ……あいつ『殺し屋』なんだよなあ。人を斬るところも見たし……）
source.english: (That's right… He's a killer. I've even seen him cut someone down…)

source.japanese:
【直正】
（なのにどうも、
　そんな風には感じられねえ……）
source.english:
(But somehow he
just doesn't feel like one…)

source.japanese:
確かに朔屋はまるごと警戒感が欠如しているものの、そればかりを嗤えまい。なにしろ智里は、その気になればこれまで朔屋を斬る機会など、それこそ一山幾らの大廉売で狙えた筈なのである。
　だのにその機会を悉[ことごと]く見送り、結果智里と朔屋の関係は、呑み友達というどうにも温いところに収まった。
source.english:
Sakuya certainly lacked all caution, but one could hardly laugh only at that. Had Tomosato wished, he could have found opportunities to cut Sakuya down by the bargain-priced bushel.
Yet he had passed up every one. Their relationship had settled into that thoroughly tepid thing: drinking companions.

target.text: Waiting until the small hours of the morning, a man and a woman meeting in secret. It would unavoidably carry with it licentious implications, and Sakuya was painfully aware of the fact that Rui was a wanton woman. As for Tomosato, while he didn't seem greasy, he was still a handsome man in his own right. It was impossible to know if he had made many a young girl cry in circumstances Sakuya knew naught of. If anything, was it not entirely possible that Tomosato was more proficient than Sakuya by far when it came to matters of that nature?

Despite being aware of as much, Sakuya felt no jealousy towards Rui, nor antipathy towards Tomosato, for you see, the man himself was self-aware of how utterly profligate he was where women were concerned, so there was really no place for him to say anything. And most of all, though he was some distance away and therefore couldn't pick out everything being said, what the two were speaking about had to be───it seemed to him that it could only be about Sakuya himself. Yes, the job Tomosato had been contracted for───murdering Sakuya.

However, in this, too, despite being so cognizant of it, Sakuya didn't flee from there like a scared rabbit, he didn't try to escape this ship by hook and by crook; he simply couldn't bring himself to feel any such sense of impending danger.
【Naomasa】 （Right……he is a『murderer』after all. I've even seen him cut other men down before……）
【Naomasa】 （But for some reason, try as I might, I just can't see him that way……）

Certainly, Sakuya was entirely deficient in wariness, but for that alone we cannot ridicule him. For you see, given that opportunities to kill Sakuya were so abundant they may as well have been sold in bulk for a bargain, had Tomosato ever felt the inclination to, he could easily have gone after him. And yet, he had let every such chance pass him by, and in the end, Tomosato and Sakuya's relationship had settled into something as comfortably tepid as drinking buddies.

source.japanese:
今夜泪がいかなる意図で智里に質したのかは知れずとも、少なくとも朔屋には殺し屋が殺し屋であるところを再認識はさせた筈である、のに、青年にはやはりこう……智里が、自分に刃を擬している情景というのが今ひとつ想像しづらく。
　それは対象に殺意を気づかせない、暗殺者としての業なのかも知れない。
source.english:
Whatever Rui intended by questioning him tonight, it ought at least to have reminded Sakuya that a killer was a killer. Yet Sakuya still found it somehow difficult to picture Tomosato directing a blade at him.
Perhaps that was an assassin's skill: preventing the target from sensing murderous intent.

source.japanese: けれどそれでもと、朔屋はどうにも真剣になりきれず、ぐるぐると思いは空転するばかり、するうちにもかくん、と。眠気がひどい。
source.english: Even so, Sakuya could not take it quite seriously. His thoughts merely turned in useless circles. And as they turned, his head nodded. He was terribly sleepy.

source.japanese: 部屋に戻る途中で足を止めてしまったのがまずかった。智里が朔屋に気づいている以上、気がついたら頭と体が泣き別れしていた、という事も十二分に有り得るのにもかかわらず、朔屋は通路の床にぐにゃぐにゃなりに崩れて眠りに落ちていく。
source.english: Stopping on the way to his room had been a mistake. Since Tomosato knew he was there, it was entirely possible that Sakuya might discover his head and body had parted company. Nevertheless, he folded limply onto the passage floor and sank into sleep.

target.text: Though he had no idea with whatever intention Rui had decided to question Tomosato tonight, at the very least, it should have made Sakuya realize anew that this murderer was, in fact, a murderer, and yet the young man still……he found it somewhat difficult to imagine the sight of Tomosato pressing his blade against him. Perhaps that was simply part of the assassin's craft, to keep the target from sensing his killing intent.

However, even were that so, Sakuya still could not bring himself to take it seriously; his thoughts just spun their wheels round and round, and while they did, his head suddenly drooped. He felt horribly drowsy.

Stopping here while on the way back to his room was where it all went wrong. Seeing that Tomosato had noticed Sakuya was there, soon enough, his head would be tearfully parting ways with his body before he even realized it had happened, or at least that was all too possible, and yet, in spite of that, Sakuya collapsed limply onto the floor of the passageway, sinking into sleep.

source.japanese:
異常なまでの睡魔だった。
　朔屋だけではない。この夜、主立った乗り組み以下、下級水夫達さえ全員眠ってしまっていたのだった。
source.english:
An abnormal compulsion to sleep.
Not Sakuya alone. That night, the principal crew and even every junior sailor had fallen asleep.

target.text: It was a sleepiness so intense it bordered on the bizarre. And it wasn't just Sakuya. This night, each and every prominent member of the crew, and even the deck boys too, ended up falling asleep, without exception.

source.japanese:
そして信天翁号の運行が───
　
　　　　　いつしか───
source.english:
And the Albatross's progress—

At some point—

source.japanese:
舵を取る手もなく
　
　　機関を監督する黒眼鏡もなく
source.english:
With no hand upon the helm,

No dark glasses watching over the engine,

source.japanese:
下級水夫達を走らせる胴間声も
　　　　　　黙りこくって
　
　
　　　　　　　　　　　　止まる───
source.english:
Even the booming voice that sent the junior sailors running
Had fallen silent.

Stopped—

target.text: Thus, the Albatross─── With none the wiser───
With no hands to take the helm With no dark glasses to supervise the engine
With even the booming voice sending the deck boys running now fallen silent she stopped───

source.japanese:
だから、船底が。
　柔らかながら、噛んだもの離さぬ。
　貪欲な口に。そのただ中に。
source.english:
And so the ship's bottom.
Into a greedy mouth. Soft, but never letting go of what it bit.
Into its very midst.

source.japanese:
嵌りこんでしまった、穏やかな軋みを。
　聞き取った耳は、紺青と。
　白と灰黒の衣の───二対。
source.english:
Had lodged there. The gentle creaking was heard by two pairs of ears:
those of the figures in deep blue,
and in white and gray-black—

source.japanese:
いや、今ひとつ。
　朔屋は完全に眠りに落ちる前、信天翁号に乗りこんでから、これまでに感じた事のないような、微妙ながら不気味に軋む、船底からの異様な振動が伝わってきたのを辛うじて聴き取っていた。
source.english:
No, one more pair.
Before falling entirely asleep, Sakuya just managed to hear an uncanny vibration coming through the ship's bottom. A faint but sinister creaking, unlike anything he had felt since boarding the Albatross.

source.japanese:
それは、どこかしら郷愁を誘う音ではあったけれど。
　暑い夏の午後、浜辺を駆けた時に聴いた音
だ。草履の底で。
　ざしゅぅ、と。
　踏みしめる音と似通ってはいたけれど。
source.english:
There was something nostalgic about the sound.
Something he had heard running along a beach on a hot summer afternoon.
Beneath his sandals.
Shushh.
Like the sound of a foot pressing down. And yet—

target.text: Therefore, at the ship's belly. Though gentle, once it bites, it never lets go. A ravenous maw. Drawn into its depths.
Lodged within. A gentle creak. Ears that caught it, of indigo. Of white and darkened ash─── two pairs.

No, there was one other just then. Before Sakuya had given himself completely to the embrace of sleep, he barely heard it, a subtle yet eerie creaking, of a sort that he had never heard even once since boarding the Albatross, an uncanny tremor rising from the bottom of the ship.

It was a sound that induced some manner of nostalgia in him. A sound he had heard on a warm summer afternoon, when running on the beach. Below the soles of his zouri sandals. A soft sshhff. It resembled closely the sound of him treading firmly on the sand.

source.english: “Hey—”

source.japanese:
【声】
『おいてばよ、直の字───』
source.english: “Hey, I said. Nao—”

source.japanese:
【声】
『智里さん、いっそ刀の先で突いてみてはいかが』
source.english: “Tomosato, why not try prodding him with your sword?”

source.japanese:
【声】
『やんねえっての。
　大根桂剥きにしたって魚[うお]の鱗を落としたって構わねえポン刀だが、なんだっていい歳こいた寝惚け野郎の目覚ましにせにゃならん』
source.english:
“I'm not doing
that. I don't mind using the blade to peel a radish in one long strip or scale a fish, but why make it an alarm clock for some grown-up sleepy bastard?”

source.japanese:
朔屋が目覚めたのは、何やら頭上で言い交わす声が響いたからではない。彼の体の裡側で、雲母の如きなにかが脆く崩れ去ると同時に、自分を押し包んでいた睡魔が晴れていくのを感じたからである。
　この時朔屋は、自分があの日泪に飲まされた『真珠』が力を使い果たした事を知った。
source.english:
Sakuya did not wake because of the voices sounding above him. Something inside his body crumbled, brittle as mica, and at that same moment he felt the sleep that had enveloped him clear away.
He knew then that the pearl Rui had made him swallow that day had exhausted its power.

source.japanese: のろのろと目覚めると、見守っていたのはやはり泪と智里の二人の、並んでしゃがみこみ見下ろす様子は、泪と再会し、智里と初めて遭うたあの晩とどこやら構図を共通にしていた。
source.english: Waking slowly, he found Rui and Tomosato watching over him, as expected. Crouching side by side and looking down, they formed something of the same composition as that night when he had met Rui again, and Tomosato for the first time.

target.text: 【Voice】 『Oi───』
【Voice】 『I said oi, big Nao───』
【Voice】 『Tomosato-san, have you considered just prodding him with the tip of your blade instead?』

【Voice】 『Told you I'm not doing that. This is a katana I don't mind using to peel a daikon katsuramuki-style, or to scrape the scales off a fish with, but why the hell should I have to use it to wake up some grown-ass, half-asleep moron?』 (TN: Katsuramuki, written "桂剥き", is a cutting technique where you make a long, uninterrupted, thin peel by slicing in a circular motion.)

When Sakuya woke up, it wasn't because of the remarks traded loudly above his head. It was because, just as he felt something frail and brittle like mica crumble away, the blanket of drowsiness enveloping him was also dispelled. In that moment, Sakuya realized that he had used up the power of that 『Pearl』he had been made to swallow by Rui on that day.

As he sluggishly opened his eyes, sure enough, it was Rui and Tomosato both who had been keeping watch over him, and the way they squatted down side by side while looking down at him made for a composition that somehow echoed that night, the night where he had reunited with Rui and ran into Tomosato for the very first time.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「おめざめ、貴方。でもまだ眠そう。
　ご自分の寝台に戻られる？
　それともこのままここで？」
source.english:
“Awake, dear? Still sleepy, though.
Will you return to your own bed?
Or stay here as you are?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Finally awake, dear. But you still seem sleepy. Will you be returning to your own bed? Or will you instead remain here?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「いいや、起きてもらうぜえ。
　おらしゃんとしろ朔屋」
source.english:
“No, you're getting up.
Come on, pull yourself together, Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Nope, we're gonna need you to get up. Come on, keep it together, Sakuya.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「どうにも妙な塩梅になってやがら」
source.english: “Things have taken a strange turn.”

source.japanese: 泪は朔屋がどこで眠ろうと放任の構えのようだったが、智里は面倒くさそうに、それでも朔屋を引き起こして、通路の丸い船窓に向けた横顔は、やはり面白くも無さそうに。
source.english: Rui seemed happy to let Sakuya sleep wherever he liked. Tomosato, looking put out, nevertheless hauled him upright. His profile as he faced the passage's round porthole looked equally displeased.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Seems the situation has taken a turn for the awfully strange.」

Rui seemed inclined to let Sakuya sleep wherever he wished, but though Tomosato seemed to find it annoying, he still pulled Sakuya up on his feet, and facing the round porthole in the passageway, his profile seemed just as unimpressed as ever.

source.japanese: 海は、潮を砂に替えていたのであった。広がる砂原に連なる砂丘、どこまでもどこまでも、薄い白霧に巻かれながら、視界が伸びる限り果てしなく。信天翁号の船足は確かに時に千鳥足、時に風任せの笹舟とふらふら定まらないけれど、といって己が船である分は弁えてあり、陸上にまで、まして内陸の沙漠にまで迷いこんだりするとは考えづらい。朔屋はまず己が覚醒しているのか、正気であるのかを疑った。それほどまでに砂原の眺めはどこか現実味を欠いていた。
source.english: The sea had exchanged its water for sand. A plain of sand, ranks of dunes, on and on, veiled in thin white mist: endless as far as sight extended. The Albatross's course was admittedly unsteady. Sometimes she staggered, sometimes she drifted like a leaf boat at the wind's mercy. But she ought to know at least that she was a ship. It was hard to imagine her wandering onto land, much less into an inland desert. First Sakuya doubted whether he was awake. Whether he was sane. The sandy vista felt that unreal.

target.text: The ocean had been transformed into sand. Series of sandy dunes were dotted across the vast expanse of sand, reaching from anywhere to everywhere, and though shrouded in a thin, white mist, it still stretched on boundlessly, extending as far as the eye could see. Certainly, the speed of the Albatross was like the staggering of a drunk at times, and at other times, she would drift unsteadily like a little toy boat made from a bamboo leaf riding the wind, but with that said, she was still mindful of her place as a ship, and it was very hard to imagine that she had somehow managed to run aground, to say nothing of making it all the way into an inland desert.
At first, Sakuya doubted if he was awake, if he was even sane. That was how strangely lacking in reality the view of the desert before him was.

source.japanese:
信天翁号は───
　
　
　
　海上ではなく砂上で。
　
　
　
　停止してあり───
　
　
　
　朔屋は仰天した。
source.english:
The Albatross—

Not upon the sea, but upon sand.

Stopped—

Sakuya was astounded.

target.text: The Albatross had─── Not atop the seas, but the sands. Come to a standstill─── Sakuya was flabbergasted.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだいこりゃあ……!?」
source.english: “What's all this…!?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「What the fuck is this……!?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「なんだって、そらお前、
　見ての通りだわな」
source.english:
“What's all this? Well,
as you can see.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「What do you mean what, buddy? It's exactly what it looks like.」

source.japanese:
砂浜に乗り上げてしまったなどというひらみっともない事態ではなく、ただ砂原ばかりが周囲に茫洋と広がっている。
　目覚めているの朔屋と泪と智里、その三人のみであるらしい。見たところ他は軒並み深い眠りに就いてあり、どれだけ揺すってもつついても一向に起きようとしない。
source.english:
This was no merely disgraceful business of running onto a beach. An indistinct expanse of sand spread all around.
Only Sakuya, Rui, and Tomosato seemed to be awake. Everyone else was apparently deep asleep; no amount of shaking or prodding would wake them.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「シサム、おいキサラ、おい、おいってば。
　ダメかこの二人も……」
source.english:
“Sisam. Hey, Kisara. Hey.
Come on! No use with these two either…”

source.japanese:
朔屋としては、上甲板で釣り竿の傍で、仰向けにひっくり返った蛙のような、相当に珍妙かつ大胆な寝姿を晒している航海士の双子をどうにか起こそうとして、あれこれ手を尽くした挙げ句通常の手段では通用しないと見てとると、非常手段に訴えた。
　だからそれは、純然たる、信天翁号の船員としての義務感から生じたもので、けしてそれ以外の不埒な意識が取らせた行動ではない、けして。
source.english:
Beside their fishing rods on the upper deck, the twin navigators lay in extraordinarily odd and uninhibited sleeping postures, like frogs flipped onto their backs. Sakuya tried everything to wake them. Seeing that ordinary methods failed, he resorted to an emergency measure.
Thus his action sprang purely from his sense of duty as a sailor aboard the Albatross. Certainly not from any other improper motive. Certainly not.

source.japanese: 朔屋は、双子のスカートの端を指先で摘[つま]み、そろそろと、極々慎重な手つきで───
source.english: He pinched the edge of a twin's skirt between his fingertips, and slowly, with the utmost care—

target.text: This was not some downright shameful situation like them having run aground on the beach, there was nothing but sand and more sand stretching out in every which direction around them. It seemed that it was only Sakuya, Rui, and Tomosato that were awake. Judging from appearances, the rest were deeply asleep one and all, and no matter how he shook or nudged them, they showed absolutely no sign of waking up.
【Naomasa】 「Shisamu, oi, Kisara, oi, can you hear me? These two aren't any good either……」

Sakuya, for his part, was doing his best to somehow wake up the twin first mates asleep next to their fishing rods on the upper deck, both sprawled out in a sleeping position resembling a frog lying belly-up, as bizarre as it was shameless, and after trying all possible means he could think of, it seemed to him that ordinary measures wouldn't be enough, and so he resorted to emergency measures instead. However, that was entirely born out of a pure sense of duty in his capacity as a sailor of the Albatross; it was most assuredly not an action driven by any other nefariously indecent impulses, not in the least.
Sakuya pinched the hems of the twins' skirts with his fingertips, and slowly, with extremely cautious movements───

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……直さん。起こすふりでね、
　お二人のスカートを捲[めく]ろうとなさるのは、
　いかがなものかしら」
source.english:
“…Nao.
Pretending to wake them while trying to lift their skirts—isn't
that rather questionable?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……Nao-san. Pretending to be waking them up, only to then attempt to lift up their skirts instead, does that not strike you as a little inappropriate?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……そういうのは、起きるかどうかの境で遊ぶのが愉[たの]しいんでしょうに」
source.english: “…The pleasure in such things is playing at the boundary where someone might wake.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……I believe that is surely the sort of game that is enjoyable when toying with the uncertainty of those right on the cusp of waking.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「本当に起きないような方になさって、
　面白い？」
source.english:
“Is it any fun when she really won't wake
at all?”

source.japanese: 極々慎重な手つきで捲[まく]り上げようとして、ぎりぎりの際で泪の呆れ加減の眼差しで見咎められ、同じくらいにそろそろ降ろしたが、それは慎重さからではなく未練に由来してあり───後もうちょっとだったのにと、歯噛みしながら。
source.english: He had been lifting with the utmost care when Rui caught him just at the brink, with a somewhat exasperated look. He lowered the skirt just as slowly. Not from caution, but reluctance. A little further, he thought, grinding his teeth. Just a little further.

target.text: 【Rui】 「If you play it with those who truly do not seem to be waking, is that really any fun?」

He had been rolling up their skirts with the utmost caution, and just at the very last moment, with an exasperated look, he was questioned by Rui, and he then lowered the skirts back down just as gingerly; this time, however, it was not done out of caution but regret───"and I was so close", he thought, grinding his teeth all the while.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「泪よ、あんたもたいがいだな……。
　まあ一理あるとは思うがよ」
source.english:
“Rui, you're something else yourself…
Though I suppose you have a point.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Rui, you're a piece of work in your own right……. Well, I do think you have a point here.」

source.japanese:
航海士の双子ばかりでなく、上甲板に上がってくるまで見かけたり覗きこんだりした下級水夫達や水夫長も同様で。
　そして智里と泪だが、この二人は自分と同じくいったん眠りに落ちた後で目覚めたのか、それとも始めから睡魔を寄せつけなかったのか、微妙に気になったものの、それを問うてしまえば、眠りに落ちる前に二人が対峙していた状況を覗き見していたのが露呈してしまいそうな気がして、結局言い出せなかった。
source.english:
It was not only the twin navigators. The junior sailors and boatswain they had passed or looked in on while coming up to the upper deck were the same.
As for Tomosato and Rui, had these two fallen asleep and awakened as Sakuya had, or never succumbed at all? He was mildly curious. But asking might reveal that he had spied on their confrontation before he fell asleep. In the end, he said nothing.

source.japanese:
ともかく、問題は一面の沙漠と化している周囲の状況だ。
　明礬水を引いたような、目の詰んだ砂原はあまりにも滑らかで、清らかに月の光に映えて、どこかの惑星上の眺めのよう。
　双子の脇に置かれていた水桶に詰まっていたのは砂、船の外に広がっている沙漠と同様の質感で、釣った魚を入れるつもりで組み上げた潮が、大海の変化と機を同じくして変成したものらしかった。
source.english:
In any case, the problem was their surroundings, transformed into desert.
The closely packed sand was so smooth it might have been brushed with alum sizing. Gleaming pure in the moonlight, it looked like a landscape on some other planet.
The twins' bucket was full of sand of the same texture as the desert outside the ship. Apparently the seawater they had drawn up for their catch had changed along with the great ocean.

source.japanese: その砂粒はあまりにも細かで、青白く柔らかに、粘着力を持って盛り上がっていて、手で掬[すく]い上げればそのまま水銀の珠と化して指の隙間から零れ落ちていくのではないかとさえ。丸い月さえも、舞台の背景に描かれた絵であるかのように、景色はあまりにも信天翁号が漂っていた海とは隔たってあり、この、海が充たすもの潮から砂に替えた現象に、朔屋はぞわりと悪寒を催した。
source.english: The grains were extraordinarily fine, rising in a pale, soft, clinging mound. Scoop some up, and one could almost imagine it turning into a bead of mercury and spilling between one's fingers. Even the round moon seemed like a painting on a stage backdrop. The scene was so far removed from the sea the Albatross had sailed that Sakuya shivered at this phenomenon: the sea replacing its water with sand.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや違う、してないぞ俺は。今度は違う。
　なにもお願いなんぞしたりしてない」
source.english:
“No, I didn't. Not me. Not this time.
I haven't made any wishes.”

source.japanese: 朔屋は、先だっての『赤葡萄酒の海』事件を思い出しては二人に言い咎められたわけでもないのにぶんぶんと首を振った。
source.english: Remembering the recent red-wine-sea affair, Sakuya shook his head vigorously, though neither of them had accused him.

target.text: It wasn't just the twin first mates, for all the deck boys, and the Bosun too, who he'd happened to catch sight of as he looked around on his way up to the upper deck, were all the same. And then there were Tomosato and Rui, but had those two awoken after falling asleep much like himself, or had they never allowed sleep to steal up on them in the first place? It niggled subtly at his mind, but if he were to ask them now, he felt like he'd be revealing to them the fact that he'd been peeking at their confrontation before falling asleep, and so in the end, he never broached the matter.

Regardless, the problem was the current situation of the entire surface surrounding them having been turned into a desert. The sand was so fine-grained and smooth, it was as though it had been coated with dousa, gleaming with a pure clarity in the light of the moon, as if he were looking out at a vista from atop the surface of another planet. (TN: Dousa, written "明礬水", is a traditional Japanese paper sizing solution made of alum and animal glue.)

The bucket of water that had been placed next to the twins was full of sand, the texture similar to that of the vast desert around the ship, and the seawater they had drawn from the ocean to put the fish they caught in must have undergone a similar metamorphosis at the same time the ocean underwent its own.

So fine were the grains of sand─── a pale, blueish white, soft and faintly adhesive as they rose in gentle mounds───that one might almost imagine scooping them up by hand only for them to turn into beads of mercury and slip through the fingers. Even the round moon was like a picture drawn on the backdrop of a stage, and the entire scenery was so utterly removed from the ocean the Albatross had been drifting upon that, confronted with this phenomenon of the sea transformed from brine to sand, Sakuya felt a shivering dread crawl up his spine.
【Naomasa】 「No no, I didn't do it. Not this time. I didn't make a single wish about anything.」
Sakuya thought back to the 『Ocean of Red Wine』incident from the other day, and despite the other two not blaming him in the slightest, he still shook his head rapidly back and forth in denial.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「まあ、確かに直さんなら、海をお酒にと願っても、砂にとは言わないでしょうし」
source.english: “Well, yes. You might wish for the sea to become liquor, Nao, but surely not sand.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Well, while it is certainly true that you might wish for the ocean to turn to wine, Nao-san, you would surely not ask for it to turn to sand.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それとも砂遊びでもなさる？」
source.english: “Or would you like to play in it?”

source.japanese: 泪は理解してくれている、疑っていないと疑心暗鬼から安堵した朔屋は、この小心者は、小心者故に泪の落ち着き払った様子にとりあえず同調する事にした。
source.english: Rui understood. She did not suspect him. Relieved of his fearful suspicions, Sakuya—that timid soul—decided for the moment to follow her composure, precisely because he was timid.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「泪さんに、首だけ出して埋めてもらったりとか、そういうのなら、いいかなあ……」
source.english: “Well, if you buried me with only my head showing, Rui, that might be nice…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もちろん泪さんは、ちらちら足や胸を見せたりでさ。裸になってくれたっていい。
　それでも俺は手も足も出せないの」
source.english:
“And of course you'd show me little glimpses of your legs and breasts. You could be naked if you liked.
But I couldn't move a hand or foot.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Or were you hoping to play in the sand?」

When he realized that Rui believed him, that she didn't suspect him, relief washed over Sakuya as his minor bout of paranoia passed, but this coward was only able to conform with Rui's composed behavior for now precisely because he was a coward.
【Naomasa】 「Maybe if I could be buried in the sand up to my neck by you, Rui-san, that could be nice……」
【Naomasa】 「Of course, you'd have to show me little glimpses of your feet and breasts. Would be nice if you'd get naked for me too, actually. But I'd still be unable to so much as lift a finger.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「直さんは、焦らされるのもお好きなの」
source.english: “You enjoy being teased too, Nao?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「So you are the type who likes being tantalized, Nao-san?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あっはっは。埋めてやるよ俺が、棺桶詰めにして、三尺ばかり深く、てめえら二人をまるごと全部」
source.english: “Ahahaha. I'll bury you myself. Both of you, all of you, packed into a coffin about three feet down.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「空気穴開けて、鈴だけは持たしてやろう」
source.english: “I'll make an air hole and let you have a bell.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Ah-ha-ha. Oh, I'd gladly bury you. In a coffin, about six feet under, then stuff the both of you in it.」
【Tomosato】 「I'll open a ventilation hole, and I'll let you have only a single bell.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「鈴の音[ね]が途絶えた頃に掘り出しゃあ、ちょいとおつな聖天さまのご本尊が出来上がっている事だろうぜ」
source.english: “Dig you up once the ringing stops, and there ought to be a rather fine two-bodied image of Shoten.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「すげえなあ智里、
　あんた、こういう異常な現象でも、
　なんだってそう落ち着いてられるんだ」
source.english:
“Amazing, Tomosato.
How can you stay so calm
through a phenomenon this strange?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Once the bell stops ringing, I'll dig you out, and by then, I'm sure I'll have myself a charmingly risque little Shouten figure waiting for me.」 (TN: Shouten, written "聖天", also known as Kangiten, is a Japanese Buddhist deity often depicted as a pair of figures locked in an intimate embrace. They are also associated with fertility and sexual energy.)
【Naomasa】 「I'm amazed, Tomosato. How do you manage to stay so calm, even when faced with this kind of bizarre phenomenon?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そりゃあこっちの台詞だこの莫迦。
　言いだしたなあてめえだろうが」
source.english:
“That's my line, you idiot.
You're the one who started it.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「That's my line, you idiot. You're the one who started this.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あいてっ」
source.english: “Ow!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Ouch!」

source.japanese:
益体もない軽口を泪と叩き合い続けていたのは、船の上にあってなお、潮の香りも波音も聴かないという異常な状況を務めて無視しようとした、一種の防衛本能なのだったが、流石に業を煮やした智里の拳槌で天骨をがんとやられてまで続ける芸ではない。
　痛みに目の中に飛び散った火花が去ってなお、依然として海は砂の海で、夢や幻覚ではない事を渋々受け入れて朔屋は、事態の原因を探ろうとした、と言って心当たりは一つくらいしかない。
source.english:
His continuing idle banter with Rui had been a kind of defensive instinct: a determined attempt to ignore the extraordinary situation of standing aboard a ship with neither the smell of salt nor the sound of waves. But even he could not keep it up after Tomosato lost patience and hammered him on the crown with his fist.
When the sparks of pain had cleared from his eyes, the sea remained a sea of sand. Reluctantly accepting that it was no dream or hallucination, Sakuya tried to find the cause. Though he had only one idea.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それはそれとして……泪さん、あなたに心当たりは？　またあなたのご一統方面の不思議なんじゃなかろうか、これは」
source.english: “That aside… Rui, does it suggest anything to you? Might it be another marvel from your side of things?”

target.text: The reason he continued to exchange this pointless banter with Rui was because he was trying, with all his might, to ignore this bizarre situation where, despite being on a ship, he couldn't hear the crashing of the waves or smell the salty sea breeze; it was a protective instinct of sorts, but it wasn't an act worth dragging out to the point of getting cracked on the top of the head by the hammer that was an exasperated Tomosato's fist. After the fireworks of pain were done exploding before his eyes, the ocean was as yet an ocean of sand, and Sakuya had to reluctantly accept it to be no dream or hallucination; he tried to fumble around for the cause, but with that said, he only had a single guess.
【Naomasa】 「Setting that aside for now…… Rui-san, do you have any guesses? Could this not be another strange miracle caused by your people?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───さあ？
　わたくしにもよくわかりません。
　そうかも知れないし、
　そうでないかも知れない」
source.english:
“Who knows?
I don't really understand
it myself.
It might be. It might not.”

source.japanese:
……沙漠の果てに目を凝らしてみたものの、どうやら泪にも判別のつかない事態のようで、瞼を下ろしてふるふると首を振る、その項に月が雫が滴って濡れたように光るのに、ついぼんやり見入ってから朔屋も目を醒ますように首を振った。
　こんな状況下にあるのに、どうにも泪にばかり目がいってしまうのは、朔屋の心が彼女に振れつつある証左なのかも知れない。
source.english:
She peered toward the desert's limit, but apparently could make no more sense of it. Lowering her eyelids, she shook her head gently. Moonlight shone upon her nape as though drops had fallen there and left it wet. Sakuya gazed absently for a moment, then shook his own head as though to wake himself.
That even in such circumstances his eyes kept turning to Rui might be evidence that his heart was inclining toward her.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうか……なんにしたって、
　どうしたもんかなこれは。
　みんな起きてくる気配もないし……」
source.english:
“I see…
Whatever it is, what should we do? No
one seems about to wake…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「部屋に戻って寝直そうかな……。
　起きたら元通りになってるかも知れないしなあ」
source.english:
“Maybe I'll go back to my room and sleep again…
It might be normal when I wake.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「───Who can say? I'm not quite sure myself either. It might be so, and it might not be so.」

……She strained her eyes towards the far edge of the desert, but it seemed they were in a situation not even Rui could make heads or tails of, for she lowered her eyelids and shook her head, the nape of her neck gleamed as though touched by droplets fallen from the moon itself, and Sakuya found himself staring at her blankly for a moment before shaking his head to snap himself awake. Despite being in a situation as dire as this, he couldn't keep his eyes from always wandering towards Rui, and it might well have been proof that Sakuya's heart was also beginning to sway towards her.
【Naomasa】 「Is that so……anyway, what can we even do about this? None of the others show any sign of waking……」
【Naomasa】 「Maybe I should just return to my cabin and go back to sleep……. This might all be back to normal once I wake up, right?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「けれども、船の蓄[たくわ]えが尽きる前に戻るとも、限らないわねえ」
source.english: “But it needn't return to normal before the ship's stores run out.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おっかねえコト言わないでくれよ……」
source.english: “Don't say frightening things like that…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「However, there is also no guarantee that things will return to normal before the ship's reserves run dry, no?」
【Naomasa】 「Please don't say scary things like that……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そういう事だって有り得ます。
　おお、やだやだ。
　飢え死に渇き死になんて」
source.english:
“It could happen. Oh,
how awful.
Dying of hunger or thirst.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「But that sort of thing could certainly happen. Oh, cruel fates. Death from starvation or thirst, alas.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「残った物にけちけち気を配りながら呑んだり食べたりなんて、わたくしは好きません」
source.english: “I have no taste for eating and drinking with one eye forever fixed on what little remains.”

source.japanese:
確かに、食材の残りを気にしつつ、爪に火を点[とも]すような日を送るのはどう考えてもこの女には似合わない。
　いっそ一晩にして尽きるような、そんな華やかな破滅の宴さえ催しかねない気色があって、朔屋は下手な籠城は有り得ないだろうと覚悟するしかなかった。
source.english:
Indeed, a miserly existence fretting over the remaining food could hardly suit this woman.
She looked capable of holding a splendid feast of ruin that exhausted everything in a single night. Sakuya had no choice but to accept that they couldn't simply hole up aboard.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……とりあえず、辺りがいったいどんな様子なのか、確かめておいた方がいいんだろうな、これは……でもなあ」
source.english: “…For now, we probably ought to see what the surroundings are like… But…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I care little for eating and drinking while fussing stingily over what scraps remain.」

Certainly, no matter how he looked at it, living life while fussing over every remaining scrap of food like she were squeezing blood from a stone certainly didn't suit this woman. On the contrary, there was a certain air to her, as if she might well stage a lavish banquet of ruin that would exhaust all their supplies in a single night, and so all Sakuya could do was accept the impossibility of any inadvertent attempt at holing up.
【Naomasa】 「……Anyways, it might be for the best to check just what exactly is going on around us here, sure, but……still, I mean.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お月様もとっても奇麗で、歩くのには不自由ないでしょうね」
source.english: “The moon is so beautiful. There should be no difficulty walking.”

source.japanese: 船でじっとしているべきなのかも知れないが、ずっとこのままなのかも知れない。となると周囲を調べてみるべきだが、他の者が起きてこない以上、
source.english: Perhaps they ought to remain aboard. But perhaps things would stay this way forever. In that case, they should investigate the surroundings. And since no one else would wake—

target.text: 【Rui】 「The moon is exceedingly beautiful today, so we are unlikely to find ourselves inconvenienced on that account while walking.」

Perhaps they ought to just remain stock still on the ship, but maybe things could also stay like this forever. And with that being the case, they ought to investigate their surroundings, but with nobody else waking up,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「俺たちが行くしかないやなあ」
source.english: “We'll have to go ourselves.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うえええ？　めんどくさいなあ」
source.english: “Whaaat? What a bother.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「We'll just have to go and take a look then, yeah?」
【Naomasa】 「Ehhhh? That sounds like such a pain though.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「いいから。行くから」
source.english: “Never mind. We're going.”

source.japanese: 渋る朔屋を無理矢理引っ張り出しにかかる智里だった。これに泪も、
source.english: Tomosato began dragging the reluctant Sakuya out by force. Rui added—

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Enough whining. We're going.」
Tomosata began to drag the hesitant Sakuya out by force. Seeing this, Rui, too,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「連れて行きなさい、退屈だから」
source.english: “Take me with you. I'm bored.”

source.japanese: と朔屋に命じ、なかば強制的に同行するつもりらしい。
source.english: She commanded Sakuya, apparently intending to accompany them whether they liked it or not.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「皆さんが気持ち良く眠っているところ、
　わたくし一人だけ起きているなんて、
　癪なのよ」
source.english:
“Everyone else sleeping so pleasantly,
and me alone awake?
It irritates me.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「You shall take me with you, for I am bored.」
Ordered Sakuya like so, apparently intending to make him accompany her whether he liked it or not.
【Rui】 「The thought of being the only woman awake while everyone else is sleeping so peacefully, it irks me.」

source.japanese:
───信天翁号を降りて沙漠に出てきたものの。三人にこれという当てがあったわけではなく───
　さくさくと、目の細かい砂に足跡を捺しつつ砂丘を越えてまた越えて、船影が遠くになりにける頃、朔屋は既に音を上げつつあった。
source.english:
They had left the Albatross and come out into the desert, but none of the three had any real lead. Crunch, crunch:
stamping footprints into the fine sand, they crossed dune after dune. By the time the ship's silhouette grew distant, Sakuya was already beginning to complain.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なー智里。
　俺ら、どこまで行きゃいいの？」
source.english:
“Hey, Tomosato.
How far are we supposed to go?”

target.text: ───They disembarked from the Albatross and set forth into the desert, however. The three of them had no particular aim in mind─── Feet sinking into the fine sand with a crunch, they left a trail of footprints as they crossed dunes of sand only to cross some more, and by the time the ship's silhouette had faded away into the distance, Sakuya was already whining and ready to throw in the towel.
【Naomasa】 「Heeey, Tomosato. Just how far do we have to go?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「んー、なにか変わったもんの一つでも見えてくるまで」
source.english: “Mm. Until we see something unusual, at least.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「泪さんは疲れないのか、
　こんな砂の上でさ」
source.english:
“Aren't you tired, Rui?
On sand like this?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Hmm, until we see at least one thing that looks different」
【Naomasa】 「Aren't you getting tired, Rui-san, walking on this sand?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ちいとも。
　さくさくと音も軽くて、
　かえって心地よいくらい」
source.english:
“Not a bit.
Such a light crunching sound.
Quite pleasant, actually.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Not in the slightest. On the contrary, the crunchy sound of stepping on the sand is light, almost pleasantly so.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「歩けないくらい、
　足の裏が柔らかい頃もあったっけ。
　ずっと昔だけど」
source.english:
“There was a time
when the soles of my feet were too tender for walking.
A very long time ago.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やっぱりお嬢様育ちだったか」
source.english: “So you were brought up a pampered young lady after all.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「There was a time when the soles of my feet were so soft, I couldn't even walk, if I'm not mistaken. Though that was long, long ago.」
【Naomasa】 「I knew it, so you were raised as a pampered little lady.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……お前ね、もちっとこう、教養てぇのを持とうな？　この女がそういうのなら、
『ならこんな水気もねえところで、体乾っ涸らびないの』と、こうだろう」
source.english:
“…You know, you ought to acquire a little culture.
When this woman says that, your reply should be: 'Then won't your body dry out somewhere with no moisture like this?'”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Buddy, have you ever considered being a little more of, how to put it, a man of culture and refinement? If this woman says something like that, you gotta say something like "Then wouldn't your body shrivel into a husk in a place this bone-dry?" in return, right?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そう言う貴方も、皮肉というならもう少し磨きなさい。つまらなくてよ」
source.english: “And if you mean to be ironic, polish it a little more yourself. You're dull.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「？　水筒なら三人分持ってきたし、
　まだ口をつけてもない。
　水ならしばらく保つだろ？」
source.english:
“Huh? I've brought water for three,
and we haven't touched it yet.
We should have enough for a while, shouldn't we?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Go polish your own sarcastic wit, if that is the best you can come up with. It is dull.」
【Naomasa】 「Huh? But we brought canteens with water enough for three, and we haven't even touched it yet. Our water should still last us a while yet, right?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「言ってもわからぬ馬鹿がまた一人……」
source.english: “Another fool who won't understand even when you tell him…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「And here we have yet another idiot who doesn't understand things, even when they're spelled out to his face……」

source.japanese: ───沙漠の夜は冷えるとは、子供でも知るような常識であり、朔屋と智里は着た切り雀で普段の和服と船員服姿のままだが、泪はドレスの上にケープを重ね、頭にはボンネットを着けた。
source.english: Even children knew that a desert grew cold at night. Sakuya and Tomosato had come in their usual sailor's clothes and Japanese dress, with nothing more to wear. Rui had added a cape over her dress and a bonnet on her head.

source.japanese:
実際にはそこまで冷えこんでいるわけではないが、ケープの端やドレスの裳裾を砂上に軽やかに捌[さば]けば、むくつけき男二人の中にあって水魚の鰭[ひれ]のように優雅がな軽やかに翻[ひるがえ]るのに、型くずれもなくすぐに泪の身体なりに落ち着く様は、よほど高級で目の詰んだ生地と見えた。
　肩口の肌が隠れてしまうのは傷としても、その娘のようなラインが不思議と泪に似合っていたし、今だってボンネットの裡から智里をやりこめた口元が、沙漠にあって華やいでいた。
source.english:
It was not actually so cold, but when she handled the cape's edge and her dress's hem lightly above the sand, their grace fluttered like a fish's fins between the two ungainly men. Then they settled at once to her body's shape, without losing their own. The cloth must have been exceptionally fine and closely woven.
Hiding the skin about her shoulders was a drawback, but those maidenly lines suited Rui strangely well. Even now, the mouth that had put Tomosato in his place shone brightly within the bonnet, here in the desert.

target.text: ───It was common knowledge even for children that deserts grow cold at night, and while Sakuya and Tomosato, who owned no other clothes than the ones currently on their backs, had respectively left the ship still wearing their regular sailor outfit and Japanese clothes, Rui had draped a cape over her dress, and she wore a bonnet over her head.

It was not actually all that cold, and as the trailing sweep of her cape and the train of her dress brushed over the surface of sand, despite lightly flapping in a way that evoked the graceful fin of a fish gliding through the water when next to these two coarse, uncultured men, the garments always kept their shape, settling around the lines of Rui's body, and it seemed they must both have been made with remarkably fine-gauge material of the highest quality.

Even if the way the skin at her collar ended up hidden from view was a fly in the ointment, the demure, maidenly silhouette made for a curiously perfect match with Rui, and even her lips, which were peeking out from within her bonnet and currently rendering Tomosato silent through power of argument, made for a vividly brilliant sight in the desert.

source.japanese: その智里、何かを当てこすったつもりらしいが、泪は取りあわず、朔屋は何を当てこすっているのかも理解できず、少々むかっ腹で言い返す。
source.english: Tomosato apparently meant some pointed allusion. Rui ignored it. Sakuya, unable even to understand what the allusion was, answered in mild irritation.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「馬鹿って言う方が馬鹿なんだぞぅ。
　でもなー智里よぅ。
　あるにはあるが、この水だけじゃ、
　そうそう何時までも続かないよ」
source.english:
“Whoever calls someone a fool is the fool.
But, Tomosato…
We have water, sure,
but this much won't last forever.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ホントにどこまで行けばいいんだこの沙漠。
　地平線の向こうまでか？
　一応シサム達から、
　コンパス（勝手に）借りてきたけどさ。
　それだって方角見失ったら、
　船にも戻れなくなるぜ」
source.english:
“How far do we really have to go through this desert?
Beyond the horizon?
I did borrow a compass
from Sisam and the others—without asking—but if
we lose our bearings,
we won't even get back to the ship.”

target.text: And that Tomosato, he seemed to have intended to make some satirical dig at her, but Rui didn't pay it any heed, and Sakuya couldn't comprehend just what exactly he was making that dig at either; with a small ember of anger burning within him, he retorted.
【Naomasa】 「Only idiots call other people idiots. But Tomosato, come on. We do have some water, sure, but what we have isn't going to last us that long.」

【Naomasa】 「Seriously, how far out into this desert do we have to go? Until we reach the horizon? Just in case, I did borrow a compass from Shisamu (without asking), but really. Even so, if we lose our bearings, we're never making it back to the ship again.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしはてっきり、貴方がたお二人が、なにかあてがあるのかと」
source.english: “I'd rather assumed the two of you had some idea.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺はこういう海での不思議は、泪さんがどうにかしてくれるかと」
source.english: “I thought you'd handle a sea marvel like this, Rui.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Well, I was fully convinced that the two of you had some sort of goal in mind.」
【Naomasa】 「And I was certain that you'd be able to handle any of these kinds of mysteries at sea, Rui-san.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ちなみに俺は、朔屋はここぞという時には、凄ぇ馬力を発揮して、事を解決してくれる奴だと信じてる」
source.english: “For my part, I believe Sakuya's the sort who finds tremendous power when it really counts and solves the problem.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「For the record, I have absolute faith that when the chips are down at the eleventh hour, Sakuya's the kind of guy who's gonna use his incredible horsepower to step up and fix everything.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ほんとうに？」
source.english: “Really?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「本当に？」
source.english: “Really?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Truly?」
【Naomasa】 「Really?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「奇麗サッパリ嘘だよ言わせんな、
　恥ずかしい」
source.english:
“A complete and utter lie. Don't make me say it.
It's embarrassing.”

source.japanese: 漫才道中である。
source.english: A comedy act on the road.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「That was obviously a complete load of shit, don't make me spell it out for you. It's embarrassing.」
An en route comedy act.

source.japanese: 歩み止めれば、沙漠の無音がかえって耳に耐えがたく響いた、などいうのは字面からして矛盾した事態なれども、船乗り暮らしに馴染んだ耳にはままあること、なにしろ船内には常に様々な音が満ち満ちている。機関の低い轟き、船殻の軋み、そもそも四方に広がる海からして、波の音は絶え間ないし、信天翁は鳴いて羽ばたき風は索具を揺らして吹き抜けて、これに泥[なず]んだ者は陸に揚がると昼下がりの音の谷間に落ち着きなくし、夜明け前の静けさには聴覚を奪われた蝙蝠のように眠りを乱されるとかなんだとか。
source.english: When their steps stopped, the desert's silence rang unbearably in their ears. A contradiction even on the page, yet common enough to ears accustomed to a sailor's life. A ship was always full of sounds: the engine's low roar, the hull's creaking. And the sea on every side, to begin with, never ceased sounding its waves. Albatrosses cried and beat their wings; wind swept through and shook the rigging. One heard that men steeped in such sounds, once ashore, grew restless in the afternoon's quiet trough and had their sleep disturbed by the stillness before dawn, like bats robbed of hearing. Something like that.

target.text: When they came to a halt, the endless silence enveloping the desert only resounded all the louder in his ears by virtue of its quiet, and though such words may literally have described a contradictory state of affairs, it was a common occurrence in the ears of those accustomed to life on a ship, for a ship was always filled to the gills with noises of various shapes and sizes.

The deep roaring of the engine, the creaking of the hull, and before any of that, the sound of the waves coming from the ocean unfolding in every which direction was ceaseless; the albatrosses would screech and flap their wings, the wind would blow across the deck and send the rigging rattling, and when those who had grown accustomed to this din were to go ashore, they would be left restless in the hush of the early afternoon, their sleep would be as disturbed as bats robbed of their sense of hearing when met with the pervasive stillness just before daybreak, or so the stories go.

source.japanese:
引き換えこの沙漠、もっと冷えていれば砂が寒気に軋む音が響いたかも知れないし、風があればその音も聞こえたろうが、風もなく空気はやや冷える程度で、そして砂が音を吸うのか、三人が黙りこくれば空気に『しーん』という、あの無音の擬音さえ満ちるよう。
　生み出された沈黙に耐えきれなくなったか、朔屋はわざと智里めかした伝法な口調で、
source.english:
