Here in this desert, by contrast, a deeper cold might have made the sand creak. Had there been wind, they would have heard it. But there was none, and the air was only a little cool. Perhaps the sand absorbed sound. When the three fell silent, the air seemed filled even with that hush that gives silence itself a sound.
Unable to endure the silence they had created, Sakuya deliberately adopted Tomosato's rough manner.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……そんなん自分かてこれっぽっちも思っちゃいねえわい」
source.english: “…Wouldn't believe a word of it myself, neither.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「って事はなにか？
　いい歳晒した男女三人が、なにも考えもなく沙漠におん出てきたと……」
source.english:
“So what does that mean?
Three grown men and women came out into the desert without a thought in their heads…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい智里よう、
　言い出しっぺはあんただろう」
source.english:
“Hey, Tomosato.
It was your idea.”

target.text: In turn, had this desert been colder, perhaps the sand may have creaked in the cold air, and had there been wind, he could surely have listened to its murmuring voice at least, but with no wind and the desert being on the slightly colder side of things, and perhaps the sand was absorbing all sound, once all three of them fell quiet, the air seemed to be filled even with the soundless hissing of the sound effect of silence. Perhaps he found himself unable to stand the silence that had been created, for Sakuya spoke in a manner deliberately aping the mannerisms of Tomosato,
【Naomasa】 「……Ain't nobody who would believe any of that garbage for a damn second, myself least of all.」
【Naomasa】 「So what are you trying to say here? Three grown-ass men and women, all just deciding to wander into the desert without a thought in their heads……」
【Naomasa】 「Oi, Tomosato, buddy. You're the one who suggested this in the first place, right?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「気にするな細けぇ事をよ」
source.english: “Don't fret over little things.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんたなあ……。あっ。判った。
　智里、あんたこういう邪魔の入らんところに俺を連れ出して、それでばっさり殺るつもりだな！」
source.english:
“You… Ah! I see.
You've brought me somewhere no one can interfere, and now you're going to cut me down!”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Don't sweat the small stuff.」
【Naomasa】 「Come on maaan……. Ah. I get it. Tomosato, this whole time, you were luring me out here where there's nobody to interfere, and now, now you're gonna cut me down where I stand!」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「てめえを叩っ斬るのに場所なぞ選ぶかい。
　だいたい刀も持ってきてねえぞ、ほーら」
source.english:
“Would I bother choosing a place to cut you down?
I didn't even bring my sword. Look.”

source.japanese:
懐手から袖[そで]を通して、掌を開掌にぶらぶらして見せたのが馬鹿馬鹿しいほどとわざとらしい、けれど確かに殺し屋の獲物はどこにも見えず、あの定寸を越えて長い刀を全く気取らせずに隠し持てるとは考えづらい。
　ともかく、全員がなにかの解決策も持たず沙漠に出てきた事がはっきりして、朔屋の意志はたちまち沮喪していった。
source.english:
He drew his hands from his clothing, passed them through the sleeves, and dangled his open palms in a ridiculously exaggerated display. Yet the killer's weapon was indeed nowhere to be seen. It was difficult to imagine him concealing that unusually long sword without any sign.
In any case, it was clear that everyone had come into the desert without a solution. Sakuya's will promptly collapsed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃあ戻ろうよ。
　手ぶらで帰るのも仕方ないって」
source.english:
“Then let's go back.
Can't help it if we return empty-handed.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だいたいなにかを探すにしても、船のみんなをどうにか起こしてさ、手分けしてやった方が効率が良いだろう」
source.english: “Besides, if we're going to look for something, it'd be more efficient to wake everyone aboard somehow and split the work.”

source.japanese: 効率云々を考えたわけではなく、ただもう面倒くさくなっていただけの朔屋だったが、口振りだけはもっともらしい。
source.english: Sakuya had not considered efficiency at all. He was merely tired of the bother. But he sounded plausible.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「I don't need to be picky about the scenery to chop a punk like you into pieces. I didn't even bring my sword with me, look.」

He slid his hands, which were tucked inside the front folds of his kimono, sideways into and through the sleeves, lazily displaying his open palms with such contrived innocence it reached the ludicrous, but it was certainly true, the murderer's weapon of choice was nowhere to be seen, and it was hard to imagine that he was carrying that long blade far exceeding the standard measure of a katana somewhere hidden on his person without betraying a hint of it in his mannerisms. Regardless, now that it was clear that each and every one of them alike had walked out into the desert without any sort of solution for the problem in mind, any semblance of Sakuya's will that still remained quickly deflated.
【Naomasa】 「Then I'm going back. Nothing for it but to go back home empty-handed.」
【Naomasa】 「And to begin with, even if we're out here looking for something, we'll still have to wake everybody back on the ship up, so surely it would be more efficient to split up.」

He wasn't thinking of anything concerning efficiency or its like, Sakuya had simply grown fed up of walking through the desert by now, but at least the way he spoke sounded believable, if nothing else.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……あんなに色々起こそうとしたのに、ぴくりともしなかった皆さんを、本当にどうにかできるおつもり？」
source.english: “…We tried so many things, and none of them so much as twitched. Do you really mean to do something about it?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「シサムさんなんて、直さんがスカートをいじっても全然だったのに。ああいう女性はね、その手の気配に聡いものよ」
source.english: “Sisam didn't react even when you meddled with her skirt, Nao. A woman like that is sensitive to such signs.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……After trying so many methods of rousing them, none of them so much as twitched, and you truly still believe that you will somehow be able to do something about it?」
【Rui】 「Even when you were groping around Shisamu-san's skirt, Nao-san, there was no reaction at all. Girls like her, you know, they are very sensitive to even the slightest hint of such a nature.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「起きられる眠りならば、今頃直さんはこうやって歩いていることもできないはず」
source.english: “If she could wake from that sleep, you wouldn't be walking around here now.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ごもっとも」
source.english: “…Very true.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Had it been a slumber she could be roused from, I do not believe you would still be able to walk about on your own two feet right now.」
【Naomasa】 「……Can't argue there.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「たぁいえ確かにこれじゃあ埒もあかんやな。
　よし朔屋、お前な、望遠鏡持ってたろ。
　ご自慢の逸物で辺りを見回してみろや。
　肉眼よりは遠くが見えンだろ」
source.english:
“Still, we're certainly getting nowhere like this. Right, Sakuya.
You've got a telescope, haven't you?
Take that fine instrument you're so proud of and look around.
See farther than with the naked eye, won't it?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……残念でした。船室に置いてきちゃった。
　いやだっていつもいつも持ち歩いてるわけじゃないし」
source.english:
“…Bad luck. Left it in my cabin.
I mean, I don't carry it everywhere.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「That said, it's true we ain't getting anywhere like this. Alright, Sakuya, buddy, you've got a telescope, yeah? Go have a look in your pants, down near your pride and joy. Should let us see further than with the naked eye.」
【Naomasa】 「……I regret to say this. But I must have left it behind in my cabin. No, I mean, it's not like I'm always walking around with it on me to begin with.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そお？　ならその、後のポケットのは？
　上着の上からでも判るけれど」
source.english:
“Really? Then what's that in your back pocket?
I can see it even through your coat.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あれぇ……何時の間に？」
source.english: “Huh… When did that get there?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Really now? Then what is that in your back pocket? It is visible even through your jacket.」
【Naomasa】 「Uhhhh……when did that get there?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「てめえの持ち物さえ忘れてるたぁ、耄碌極まったもんだな、朔屋。よかったじゃねえか。
　早速一つ頼むわ」
source.english:
“Forgetting even your own possessions: senility's really taken hold, Sakuya. Lucky for us.
Go on, have a look.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……いいけどさ、こんな見晴らしのいいところだぞ、望遠鏡使ったって、大差ないと思うけどな……」
source.english: “…All right, but the view's so open here. I doubt a telescope will make much difference…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「When you start even forgetting your own stuff, that's the height of senility, Sakuya. But that's a lucky break for us, isn't it. Go have a look already then, please and thank you.」
【Naomasa】 「……Alright, but we're already standing on such a great vantage point, I don't think there will be that big of a difference when using the telescope……」

source.japanese:
ところが、朔屋が望遠鏡越しに覗くと、有る筈のないものが、その視界に。
　何度も目を凝らす、何度そうしてみても、見間違いや幻のよう大人しくは消えてくれない。朔屋にはそれが、船のように見えてならなかったのだ。
source.english:
Yet when Sakuya looked through it, something that ought not to exist appeared in his view.
Again and again he strained his eyes. However often he looked, it would not obligingly vanish like an illusion or a mistake. He could only see it as a ship.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……信じられない。が、やってみるもんだ。
　右手の方に、なにかがある……」
source.english:
“…Unbelievable. But it's worth trying things.
There's something to the right…”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「右の方角……？　どこになにが」
source.english: “To the right…? Where? What?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ありゃあ……船……か？
　幾つもある……」
source.english:
“Those are… ships…?
Several of them…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「え？　……え？　なぁに？
　なんのこと？」
source.english:
“Eh? …Eh? What?
What do you mean?”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あっちは砂丘も途切れた、地平線まで拓けたとこだが……芥子粒ほども、なんも見えねえが」
source.english: “The dunes end over there. It's open right to the horizon… But I can't see anything, not a speck.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなに離れてるか？　廃船っぽいな、望遠鏡でもそれくらいは判る距離だよ……？」
source.english: “Are they that far away? Look like abandoned ships. Close enough for me to tell that through the telescope…?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……直さん。ちょっと望遠鏡を除けて、自分の目で見てごらんなさい」
source.english: “…Nao. Take the telescope away a moment and look with your own eyes.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺、視力は人並み程度しか無いんだけどな。
　どれどれ───あれ？」
source.english:
“My eyesight's only ordinary, though.
Let's see—Huh?”

target.text: On the contrary, when Sakuya peered into the distance through the telescope, something that shouldn't exist found its way into his field of vision. He strained his eyes at it again and again, but no matter how many times he squinted, it wouldn't behave and vanish like a trick of the eyes or some Fata Morgana. Sakuya couldn't help but feel that it looked very much like a ship to him.
【Naomasa】 「……Unbelievable. But, I guess it pays to give things a shot. There's something over there, on the right……」
【Tomosato】 「On the right……? Where and what?」
【Naomasa】 「That's……a ship……I think? And several at that……」
【Rui】 「Hn? ……Huh? What? Whatever are you talking about?」
【Tomosato】 「There's a gap in the dunes there, and you can see all the way to the horizon, but……I can't even see anything the size of an ant.」
【Naomasa】 「Is it really that far away? They look like hulks, and they're at a distance where I can tell that much detail, even if it is through the telescope, so……?」
【Rui】 「……Nao-san. Put away that telescope for a moment, then take a look with your own two eyes.」
【Naomasa】 「My eyesight is only as good as the average guy, but sure. Let's see───huh?」

source.japanese: あるいは、信天翁号のように、航行中に沙漠の中に囚われた船が他にもあったのかしらん、ともかく、泪に促されるままに望遠鏡を目から外し、瞼を擦る。
source.english: Perhaps other ships had been trapped in the desert while under way, like the Albatross. At any rate, as Rui suggested, he took the telescope from his eye and rubbed his eyelids.

source.japanese:
───と、砂上には、何も見えず、ただ月影に白々輝いているばかり。
　納得できずに朔屋がもう一度望遠鏡を目に宛がうと、レンズ越しの視界の中には、また確かに浮かび上がる廃れた船影達がある。
source.english:
Nothing could be seen on the sand. It merely shone pale beneath the moon.
Unable to accept that, he raised the telescope again. Through its lenses, the silhouettes of abandoned ships rose unmistakably into view once more.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、見えてるって。
　って事は、よっぽど距離があるんだよ。
　そうだとしか考えられない」
source.english:
“No, I can see them.
That means they're very far away.
It's the only explanation.”

target.text: Perhaps they were other ships who, just like the Albatross, had also been trapped in this desert while on their own voyages, but regardless, he removed his eye from the telescope as urged by Rui, then rubbed his eyelids.

───But, atop the sands, he saw nothing, just the pale radiance of glimmering moonbeams. Unable to accept what he saw, when Sakuya raised the telescope to his eye once more, there, in his field of vision as seen through the lens, the silhouettes of shipwrecks emerged once more with certainty.
【Naomasa】 「No, I see them, I'm telling you. Which would mean, they've got to be very far away. That's all I can imagine it to be.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……ああ、そうか。
　判ってきたぜ……
　俺の『目』より視えるたぁ、
　その望遠鏡───面白い」
source.english:
“…Ah. I see.
I'm beginning to understand…
Seeing more than my eyes can? That's
an interesting telescope.”

source.japanese: 智里の蒼い目が、月影の中で炯々と、自ずから光を放っていた。───一名、浄眼、あるいは水晶眼。大陸の伝承に言う見鬼の眼、見えざるモノを見透かす目が、朔屋の望遠鏡にやや遅れ、沙漠に秘められたモノを見出していた。
source.english: Tomosato's blue eyes shone fiercely in the moonlight, giving off a light of their own. Known as pure eyes, or crystal eyes: the spirit-seeing eyes of continental tradition, eyes that saw through invisible things. A little after Sakuya's telescope, they discovered what the desert concealed.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Aah, so that's it? I get it now…… To be able to descry even more than my『Eyes』, that telescope of yours─── how interesting.」

Within the moonlight, Tomosato's eyes of azure were emitting a piercing light of their own. ───By another name, the Jougan, the Dharma eye, or perhaps the crystal eye. Known in the old legends of the mainland as the Eyes of Jian Gui. (TN: Jougan, written "浄眼", lit. eyes of purity, refer to the fourth eye of the five eyes of Buddhism. Crystal eyes, written "水晶眼", likely refers to the eyes of crystal set within the eyes of statues of Buddhas. The Eyes of Jian Gui, written "見鬼の眼", lit. spirit-seeing eyes, are seen in Japanese and Chinese folklore, Daoist sorcery, Feng Shui, etc.)
The Eyes of Discernment, those eyes that could see through the nature of the unseeable, fell slightly short of Sakuya's telescope, which had discovered that which lay hidden in the desert.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ちょっとそれ、泪にも貸してやれ。
　そんで泪もその望遠鏡で見てみるといい。
　俺が指差す方だ……」
source.english:
“Lend it to Rui a moment.
Rui, try looking through it too.
Where I'm pointing…”

source.japanese: 泪もやや訝しげにしながらも、言われた通りに試みると、
source.english: Still a little doubtful, Rui tried as he said.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Let Rui borrow that thing for a bit. And then you have a look through the telescope too, Rui. In the direction I'm pointing……」
Though Rui was also a bit puzzled, when she tried doing as he told her,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───あ。本当……に。
　見える。
　壊れた船、錆びついた船、一杯……」
source.english:
“Ah… It's true.
I can see them.
Broken ships, rusted ships, so many…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「───Ah. It's really……true. I see them. Broken ships, rusted ships, all over……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───蜃気楼？　でも遠眼鏡の中にしか見えない蜃気楼なんて───不思議」
source.english: “A mirage? But one visible only inside a telescope… How strange.”

source.japanese: どこかうっとりした声音で囁く泪は、この現象に感興さえ催しているような。
source.english: She whispered with something of a rapt voice. The phenomenon seemed even to stir her interest.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「この望遠鏡、こないだちょっと落としちまったが、そのせいでおかしくなったんじゃなかろうな……」
source.english: “I dropped this telescope the other day. Didn't make it go strange, did I…?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「でもなぁ……どういう仕組みが知らないが、望遠鏡の中だけに見えたってどうしようもないだろう？」
source.english: “But… Whatever the mechanism, what good is it if they're visible only through the telescope?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「───A mirage? But a mirage that can only be seen from within a telescope is simply───how mystifying.」
Rui murmured with an almost spellbound tone of voice, as though this phenomenon was stirring even a form of fascination within her.
【Naomasa】 「I accidentally dropped this telescope on the deck the other day, so it must have broke a little as a result or something……」
【Naomasa】 「But still……I don't know what kind of mechanism is at work here, but it's not going to be of any use if we can only see it through the telescope, right?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……そうでも、ないらしいな……」
source.english: “…Seems that isn't quite so…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……That's not the case, apparently……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……ええ。蜃気楼、
　わたくしたちの先にも」
source.english:
“…Yes.
The mirage is ahead of us too.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なにを訳のわからんことを……って。え？
　……なんで？　どうして？」
source.english:
“What incomprehensible—Huh?
Why…? How?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……Quite. For this mirage, lies right before us too.」
【Naomasa】 「What kind of nonsense are you even……wait. Huh? ……Why? How?」

source.japanese: 望遠鏡で覗いて、肉眼で確かめて、を何度か繰り返すうちに、現実の砂上に廃船群が出現してくる。
source.english: As he repeated the process—looking through the telescope, checking with the naked eye—the abandoned ships began appearing upon the actual sand.

target.text: While he had been engaged in repeatedly peering through the telescope and then attempting to confirm if what he saw was true with his own eyes, the cluster of hulks had manifested atop the sands of reality.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「不思議な望遠鏡だこと。
　大事にするといいわ、直さん」
source.english:
“What a curious telescope.
Take good care of it, Nao.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「What a mysterious telescope. You would do well to treasure it, Nao-san.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そら、さっき言ったよな。
　変わったもんの一つくらい見えるまでって。
　出てきたじゃねえか。
　行ってみようぜ」
source.english:
“See, I said it earlier.
Until we see something unusual.
Here it is. Let's
go look.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Well then, just like I said before. Until we see at least one thing that looks different. And what do you know. Let's go get a closer look.」

source.japanese:
船、というのは人類の叡智の一つの極致である。ただの丸木を刳り抜いて浮かべた時から、人類の挑戦は始まって、言い知れぬ試行錯誤が費やされ、犠牲者も出し、それでも繰り返し挑み続けてきた。
　丸木に始まった木材の船から、鉄を得てそして鋼鉄に至り、更には樹脂や様々の新素材。
　手漕ぎの、人力から、帆を張って風の力を利し、やがては原動機、機関の発明を見て、様々な動力を用いるように。
　もちろん全てがこの流れのように順に変遷していったわけではなく、人力と風力が前後した時代もあったし、時代を降っても木造の船は依然として存在している。
source.english:
A ship is one of the culminating achievements of human wisdom. The challenge began when humanity hollowed out a log and set it afloat. Incalculable trial and error followed. Lives were sacrificed. Still, the attempts continued.
From wooden vessels, beginning with the log, to iron, then steel, then resins and all manner of new materials.
From human strength at the oars to sails that harnessed the wind, and eventually the invention of motors and engines, employing various sources of power.
Naturally, not everything changed neatly in that sequence. Human power and wind power had exchanged precedence at times. Wooden vessels still existed in later ages.

target.text: Ships, one of the pinnacles of human intellect. Starting from when we first hollowed out a mere round log and floated atop it, the dauntless human spirit rose to the challenge, and though it took indescribable amounts of trial and error, and many lost their lives in the process, we still continued to undertake the arduous task, time and time again. What began as round logs became vessels of timber, and after mastering iron, we ultimately attained steel, and in addition to that came resin and many other new types of materials.

From paddling by hand, through human strength, we then raised sails and exploited the power of wind before finally arriving at the motor, and having witnessed the invention of the motor, began to make use of all manner of motive powers. Naturally, not everything changed so perfectly in order by following this transitory flow; there were ages where both the power of man and the power of wind co-occurred, and even though their age may have long past, wooden vessels continued to exist as of old.

source.japanese: なんにせよ、その時代もちうる限りの技術と知識を結集させて新しい船が建造されてきた事には変わりなく、人は遂に見あげるほどに高く、舳先から艫[とも]まで街の区画一つを収めて余るまでに巨船を造り上げるまでに至った。
source.english: At any rate, people had always built new ships by bringing together as much technology and knowledge as their age possessed. Finally they made great vessels one had to look up at, large enough to hold an entire city block between bow and stern, and more.

source.japanese:
船───偉大なる構造物よ。
　大なるものから小なるものまで、水を往くその姿には一種の完成された美に充たされる。
　たとえあの信天翁号であろうとも、あのような姿に至ってなお浮かび続けている事それ自体に、しぶとい生命美が見受けられはしないか。
source.english:
Ships—great structures.
Large or small, their passage through water possesses a kind of perfected beauty.
Even the Albatross: does not the mere fact that she keeps floating, despite what she has become, display a stubborn beauty of life?

source.japanese: それだけに、船が偉大であればあるほど、美しければ美しいその分だけ、この情景は凄惨だった。無惨だった。悲惨だった。陰惨だった。残酷だった。醜怪であった。荒涼としていた。悲哀の極みだった。惨めで、惨たらしく、哀しく、哀れで、醜く、切なく、ありとあらゆる哀と悲と惨の形容を連ねてまだ足りなかった。
source.english: All the more, then, for every measure of a ship's greatness, for every measure of its beauty, this scene was ghastly. Pitiless. Tragic. Grim. Cruel. Monstrous. Desolate. The utmost sorrow. Miserable, brutal, sad, pitiable, ugly, heartbreaking. Every adjective for grief and sorrow and ruin, strung together, would still have fallen short.

source.japanese:
沙漠のただ中に忽然として出現していたのは、船の墓場。
　狭霧を崩れた屍衣の様にまとわりつかせ佇立する船の残骸の、小型の物の傍を歩む時は近しき死者達の声なき声を聴くように、大なる艦の影に入る時は、滅びし巨神の慟哭に包まれるように、朔屋達は皆一様に、黙して砂を踏みしめ、葬列に連なるように廃船群の奥へと進んでいく。
source.english:
What had appeared without warning in the midst of the desert was a graveyard of ships.
Their wrecks stood with thin mist clinging about them like unraveling shrouds. Passing a small vessel, one seemed to hear the voiceless voices of familiar dead. Entering the shadow of a great warship, one seemed enveloped in a fallen giant god's lament. All three walked silently over the sand, deeper into the abandoned fleet, as though joining a funeral procession.

target.text: At any rate, it did not change the fact that new ships were constructed by concentrating all the knowledge and technology utilized in their ages, and man finally built them so tall, he had to look up at them, reaching gigantic vessels so vast that an entire city block could fit from bow to stern with room to spare.

Ships───O magnificent structures. From the grand to the tiny, as your form floats atop the water, it realizes a particular sort of perfected beauty. Even should we consider that damnable Albatross, that she manages to stay afloat even looking the way she does, could that itself not be interpreted as the aesthetic beauty of the unyielding tenacity of life?

And it was precisely for that reason, for as grand and majestic as the ship is, for every ounce of beauty within it, that this scene was all the more ghastly. It was tragic. Pitiful. Gloomy. Brutal. Hideous. It made a desolate sight. The pinnacle of sorrow. Wretched, atrocious, lamentable, miserable, unsightly, heartrending: one could string together expressions of every possible form of pity, sorrow, and misery, and it would still be lacking.

Suddenly emerging, right in the middle of the desert, was a ship graveyard. Mist clung to the still remains of ships like an untidy, shapeless funeral shroud; when they walked next to a smaller boat, it was as though they could hear the voiceless voices of the dear departed, and when they entered the shadow of a grand warship, it was as though they were engulfed by the wailing of a once-great god of eld, perished and forgotten, and Sakuya and company, all as one, kept silent as they tread firmly upon the sand, venturing ever deeper into the cluster of wrecked ships as though they were attending a funeral procession.

source.japanese: 廃船群は三人が近づいても幻影と消えることはなく、その密な事、規模といい、沙中の廃都に三人を迷いこんだ心地にさせる。
source.english: The ships did not vanish into illusion as they approached. So dense, so vast was the assembly that the three felt they had strayed into an abandoned city in the sand.

source.japanese: これなるは船の墓場。巨人達と死せる文明の凄絶な記念碑。
source.english: This was a graveyard of ships. A terrible monument to giants and dead civilizations.

source.japanese: 毀たれ、錆びつき、腐朽した船体のあちこちからさらさらと振り零れゆく砂の粒、風に撒かれる骨の灰のよう。ここに至るまでの沙漠は清[さや]かな晴夜であったのに、船の墓場の陰鬱な気配は大気さえ歪ませて、上空を薄暗く閉ざして、月貌隠す、暗雲の隙間から辛うじて届く月光も死体の顔のように青ざめて。
source.english: Grains of sand trickled from every part of the broken, rusted, rotting hulls, like bone ash scattered by wind. Until they reached this place, the desert had enjoyed a clear night. But the ship graveyard's gloomy presence seemed to warp even the air, darkening the sky and hiding the moon's face. What moonlight barely reached them through gaps in the clouds was pale as a corpse's face.

source.japanese: どれだけ進んだのか、廃船から立ち込む凄惨な死の気配に遂に耐えきれなくなったのは朔屋で、
source.english: How far had they gone? Sakuya was the first unable to endure any longer the dreadful sense of death rising from the wrecks.

target.text: Even as the three of them approached, the cluster of hulks did not vanish like a mirage, the sheer density and scale alike invoking within the trio a feeling of having strayed into a ruined city left buried and forgotten in the sands.
Here be a graveyard of ships. A haunting monument to titans and a fallen civilization.

Powdery grains of sand spilt down from all over the damaged, rusted, deteriorated hulls like bone ash scattering in the wind. Hitherto, it had been such a pure, clear night in this desert, yet the sepulchral aura of this ship graveyard distorted even the atmosphere itself, covering the skies above in a dim darkness, and the moonlight barely reaching them through a rift in the dark skies was pallid as the faces of the dead.
Just how far had they advanced already; it was Sakuya who found himself unable to bear the feeling of gruesome death pervading the air from every hulk around them,

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああもう歩けないよ、せめて一息入れない事には。長靴ん中、足がぱんぱんに張っちまってるわ……」
source.english: “Oh, I can't walk any farther. Not without a breather. My feet are swollen solid inside these boots…”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Aaargh, I can't walk any further, I've got to at least have a little breather. My feet are so swollen in my boots, they're about to burst at the seams……」

source.japanese: 他の二人の応えも待たず、廃船から零れ落ちた部品のなるべく少ない砂地を選んで腰を落とし、長靴を引き抜くと、朔屋がぼやいたほどには脹[ふく]ら脛[はぎ]は張ってはいなかったけれど、長靴の口を逆さに振ると、ざぁ、と夥[おびただ]しく流れ出して、ころんと最後に句点の様に転がり出でたのは、何時入りこんだものやら、鼠の頭蓋骨で。長靴からの砂の小山の天辺にちょんと据わったのは、朔屋が期せずして廃船の群に塚をこしらえてしまったような、気まずいとも皮肉めくともつかぬ、食傷しそうに悪趣味な空気が漂った。
source.english: Without waiting for the others to answer, he chose a patch of sand with as few fallen ship parts as possible and sat down. When he pulled off a boot, his calf was not as swollen as his complaints suggested. But turning the boot over and shaking it sent an immense quantity of sand pouring out. At last, like a period, a mouse's skull tumbled from it. When had that got in? It settled neatly atop the little mound. Sakuya had inadvertently built a burial mound amid the fleet. Neither quite embarrassing nor quite ironic: a tasteless atmosphere, almost cloying, hung about it.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あのさ、これ……。
　わざとなんかじゃないからな」
source.english:
“Listen,
this… I didn't do it on purpose.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ああ判ってンよ。お前にしちゃあ上出来すぎる冗談だったもの」
source.english: “Yeah, I know. Too good a joke for you.”

source.japanese: 朔屋の、全く意図していないとはいえ、芸術点をくれてやりたくなるほどに浮かない洒落が効かされた一発芸が、智里のこれまた品のよろしくない琴線に引っかかったのか、歩みを留めさせた。
source.english: Though entirely unintended, Sakuya's little performance carried a gloomy wit almost worthy of marks for artistry. Perhaps it had struck one of Tomosato's equally ill-bred chords, for it made him stop.

target.text: He didn't even wait for a response from the other two; he chose some sandy soil where as few parts had fallen down from the abandoned ships as he could possibly find, then sat down on his behind, and when he pulled off one of his boots, though his calf wasn't as swollen as he'd complained about, when he then turned the boot upside down and gave it a good shake, an immense amount of sand poured out with a hiss, and at the very end, like a period at the end of a sentence, and when exactly had that gotten in there, came the skull of a mouse, tumbling out with a little crack.

It remained atop the peak of the little hill of sand from Sakuya's boot, and it looked as though Sakuya had inadvertently made a little burial mound amidst the cluster of wrecked ships; an air of tastelessness, an indefinable mix of awkwardness and irony that left them nauseatingly surfeit, hung heavy around them.
【Naomasa】 「Uhmm, listen, this……. This wasn't on purpose, just to be clear.」
【Tomosato】 「Oh yeah, I know. That was way too good a joke for you to have made it.」

Perhaps Sakuya's dismal one-man gag, notwithstanding that it really wasn't intentional at all, featuring wit so leaden that one felt compelled to grant it points for artistic merit, had struck a decidedly low-brow chord with Tomosato, for he came to a halt.

source.japanese: 腰を下ろして、休むとなったら朔屋より徹底しており、砂地の上に横たわって肘をつき、早速懐から取り出して、煙管に点けた一服の、紫煙を鎮魂の香に、替えるなどの殊勝げな志など持ち合わせるはずもなく、三回ばかり立て続けに煙を輪にして吐く。
source.english: When he sat down to rest, he did so more thoroughly than Sakuya. Lying on the sand with an elbow propped beneath him, he promptly took out his pipe and lit it. Naturally he harbored no pious intention of turning the violet smoke into incense for the dead. He simply blew three smoke rings in succession.

source.japanese:
痩せぎすに見えて、一つの刃であるかに強靱な筋骨具[そな]えた智里はまだともかくとして、女の足、まして姫さま育ちであろう泪にはこの遠歩き、口では暢気に言っても、随分と堪[こた]えているのではないか。
　朔屋が様子を窺えば、泪は先程から黙りこくって、廃船のあちこちへ視線を配って、何事かをしきりに気にしている表情の。ぱちり、ぱちりと留め輪外して沓[くつ]を脱いでいくのだって、どこか上の空だ。
source.english:
Tomosato might look thin, but his sinews were tough as a blade. Rui, by contrast, was a woman, and probably a princess by upbringing. Might this long walk have been hard on her legs, however casually she spoke?
Looking over, Sakuya found her silent, casting glances about the wrecks, apparently much troubled by something. Even as she unfastened her shoe straps, click by click, and took her shoes off, she seemed distracted.

source.japanese:
朔屋は彼女が何故そこまで周囲の廃船を気にかけるのか訝しくあったが、彼自身これら廃船群を目の当たりにして抱いた疑念がある。
　もう片方の長靴も脱いで砂を抜きながら、
source.english:
He wondered why she was so concerned with the surrounding vessels. But seeing the wrecks himself had raised a question of his own.
Taking off his other boot and emptying the sand, he said—

target.text: He sat down, and if they were resting, then he was doing it far more thoroughly than Sakuya, for he then laid down atop the sand, propped himself up on his elbow, promptly pulled his kiseru out of his pocket, lit it up, then took a puff, the purple smoke serving in place of the incense used in ceremonial rites to grant repose to the dead, or so one might think, not that this man possessed any such laudable intentions, and he breathed out rings of smoke, three times in succession.

Setting aside Tomosato who, though he looked skinny, was endowed with a tough physique as though he himself were a blade, Rui, who had the delicate feet of a woman, to say nothing of likely having been raised as a princess, had also walked this far, and while she seemed nonchalant judging by her words, was it not possible that this was taking a heavy toll on her?

While Sakuya tried to covertly gauge how she was holding up, Rui had been keeping silent for a while now, directing her gaze at the various wrecks around them with the expression of someone intently concerned about something. Though she unfastened the straps of her boots with loud clicks, she seemed to still have her head somewhere up in the clouds.

Part of Sakuya was suspicious of why exactly the hulks surrounding them seemed to weigh so heavily on her mind, but he himself also harboured some misgivings about the cluster of abandoned ships that he'd caught sight of on the way here. While removing his other boot and getting rid of the sand within,

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……妙だな。いくつかは知っている船型もある。あっちのドでかいのは、その通りドレッドノート級だし、さっきはシャルンホルスト級か？」
source.english: “…Strange. I know some of these designs. That enormous one over there is a Dreadnought-class, just as it looks. And earlier—was that a Scharnhorst-class?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もう少し小型の、アリシューザ級とかカヴェンディッシュ級なんかのもあったし……」
source.english: “There were some smaller ones too, Arethusa-class and Cavendish-class…”

source.japanese: 過ぎ来し方、そしてまだ足を踏み入れぬ方へと廻らせる視線は、この青年にしては真摯な不審に満ちていた。
source.english: His gaze traveled back along the way they had come, then forward into the unknown. For Sakuya, the doubt in it was unusually earnest.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……It's strange. There are several types of vessels here that I'm familiar with. That big one over there, name true to its size, belongs to the Dreadnought class, and that one before was a Scharnhorst class?」
【Naomasa】 「And the slightly smaller ones there, those are Arethusa-class or Cavendish-class vessels……」
His gaze moved to the path they had already trod, then towards where they had yet to tread, full of an earnest doubt quite rare for this young man.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「三本マスト、帆船時代のフリゲートなんかもあったみたいだぞ」
source.english: “I think there were three-masted frigates from the age of sail too.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……まあ俺だって聞きかじりの知識だから詳しい事は判らないが、それより昔の船もあるみたいだ───が」
source.english: “…My knowledge's only scraps I've heard, so I don't know much. But there seem to be ships older than those as well. Still—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ありゃ一体なんだ？　あそこら辺一帯のは、船型も構造も見たことがない。
　Ｕボートに見えなくもないが、それとも全然違う奴さえある」
source.english:
“What on earth are those? That whole stretch over there. I've never seen designs or structures like them.
Some look something like U-boats, but others are completely different even from those.”

source.japanese:
指差した方には、朔屋がそれまで書物にも口伝えにも見た事聞いた事すらない規模、構造の船舶も累々と屍を晒していた。
　それらに目をやって、口を開いたは怠惰に砂上に寝そべっていた智里の、
source.english:
Where he pointed, the corpses of ships lay heaped in sizes and constructions he had never encountered in books or heard described.
Looking toward them, Tomosato spoke from his lazy sprawl upon the sand.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……Ｕボートに似たのは、シーウルフ級攻撃型原子力潜水艦だ。お前が言った、全然違うてぇ奴は、オービノバノス級の空母だな。原潜よりもっと後の時代の……ま、要するにみんな軍艦さね」
source.english: “…The ones like U-boats are Seawolf-class nuclear attack submarines. The completely different ones you mean are Obinobanos-class carriers. From a period later still than the nuclear subs… Well, in short, they're all warships.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「智里……？　その原子力やらオービノなんとかってのは……なんだ？」
source.english: “Tomosato…? What's this nuclear power and Obino-whatever…?”

source.japanese:
煙とともに吐き出された殺し屋の言葉は、煙よりも希薄な感触しか与えず、聞いても耳の右から左へ抜け落ちていくような。
　無理もない話であった。それらの船式は朔屋達の時代には有り得ず、ほとんど狂的なまでに野放図な科学者が、辛うじて理論の着想を得た段階だったからで、更に言うならオービノ某に至っては、『未だ地球上には存在すらしていない』。より細かく重ねるなら、『地球の史実的には、朔屋が述べた艦達が一つの戦争で同時期に就航した事もない』
source.english:
The killer's words, exhaled with his smoke, felt less substantial than the smoke itself. They passed in one ear and out the other.
Naturally enough. Such ship designs could not exist in Sakuya's time. Scientists of almost crazily unrestrained imagination had barely begun to conceive the theories. As for the Obino-something, it did not yet even exist on Earth. To be more precise still: in Earth's recorded history, the vessels Sakuya had named had never all served in a single war at the same time.

source.japanese: 眸の裡に溜めていた、流動する煙のような蒼い光にすっと瞼を下ろし閉ざして智里は、
source.english: Tomosato smoothly lowered his lids over the blue light pooled inside his eyes, fluid as smoke.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Seems like there are even three-masted frigates from the Age of Sail.」
【Naomasa】 「……Now, this is something I only have a smattering knowledge of, so I don't exactly know the details, but there also seems to be even older ships than those───however.」

【Naomasa】 「What in the world are those? That whole area over there, it's full of designs and frames I've never seen before. Some look a bit like U-boats, but then there are others still that look completely different.」

In the direction he pointed, there were vessels of scales and construction that Sakuya had never read of, been told of, seen, or even so much as heard whispers of before, their corpses lying in heaps. And opening his mouth in response after taking a look in their direction was none other than Tomosato, lazily relaxing on his side atop the sand,

【Tomosato】 「……The one that looks like a U-boat there, that's a Seawolf-class nuclear-powered fast attack submarine. And the one you mentioned, the completely different thing, that's an Orbinovanos-class aircraft carrier. It comes from an age far beyond the nuclear submarine and…… well, to make a long story short, they're all warships.」 (TN: The Orbinovanos class is a reference to Seirei Densetsu Hudie, written "精霊伝説ヒューディー", a manga by Oono Yasuyuki that was briefly serialized starting in 1988. It was never released in the West.)
【Naomasa】 「Tomosato……? This nuclear-powered and Orbi-what-have-you thing…… what are those?」

The words of the murderer gave him an even more tenuous impression than the smoke that accompanied them, and though he certainly heard them, it felt as if they passed in one ear only to come out the other.

It was no wonder, really. These classes of ship were inconceivable in Sakuya's age; it began at the level where only a scientist so lacking in limits it bordered on the insane could just barely conceive of the theories behind them, and going even further, when it came to matters concerning the Orbino-something, 『It had yet to even exist on Earth.』 And if we were to repeat ourselves in even greater detail, 『In actual Earth history, the ships Sakuya mentioned had never even been in service at the same time during a single war.』
Tomosato suddenly lowered his eyelids, cutting off the azure light swirling like smoke contained within his eyes,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……まあ、この世界にゃ、どうやらむかぁし、でっけえ戦争があったってこった」
source.english: “…Well, it seems there was a great big war in this world, long ago.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「それは俺らだって聞いてるけどさ。でもその当時にこんなばかでかい艦が就航してたなんて聞いた事ないぞ」
source.english: “We've heard about that ourselves. But I've never heard of such enormous ships being in service then.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Well, supposedly, there was a huuuge war in this world, back in the day.」
【Naomasa】 「We already know about that part. But I've never heard anything suggesting that ships this ridiculously gargantuan were in service at the time.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「智里さん、それはいったい───
　どの戦争のお話？」
source.english:
“Tomosato,
which war are you speaking of?”

source.japanese: 一体、余り物事に深くこだわらず、自分の興味の赴く肉の快楽と遊戯以外にはたださらさらと水のように流れゆく泪でさえ、周囲の廃船の様子に深い疑念を覚えたようで、それというのも、廃船の腐朽の度合いは様々なのだが、中には『時の順序を違えたように』、朔屋達に近しい年代の船が、彼らから遠いはずの木造の帆船以上に、ほとんど化石のように風化しているのもあったから。朔屋がその船式さえ知らず、智里がさらりと一度告げたきりの巨大空母などは、自然物のように沙漠と一体化しかけていて───
source.english: Even Rui, who otherwise flowed past things like water unless they concerned her own interests in fleshly pleasure and games, seemed to harbor grave doubts about the surrounding wrecks. Their decay varied, but some seemed to violate the order of time. Ships from ages nearer to their own had weathered almost into fossils, worse than wooden sailing ships that ought to have been much older. The enormous carrier whose design Sakuya did not know, named only once in passing by Tomosato, was almost merging with the desert like a natural formation.

source.japanese: ボンネットの目庇のうちから、朔屋と無言に目を交わす、陸と海とで異なる世界、年月を送ってきた二人の方がまだ意が通い合って、智里の方がよほど異物に二人には感じられた瞬間だった。
source.english: From beneath her bonnet's brim, she and Sakuya exchanged a silent look. For an instant these two, who had lived their years in different worlds, land and sea, understood one another better. Tomosato felt far more alien to them both.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「『第三次世界大戦』が一応終戦したのだって、もう四〇年は前のはず。景気はなかなか回復してこないし、あんな艦を造ったなんて聞いた事もない……」
source.english: “Even the Third World War supposedly ended forty years ago. The economy still won't recover. I've never heard of ships like those being built…”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「悪いが、俺だって『聞き囓りに聞いた』事でな。ま、いくつかはてめえの眼で見たモノもあるが」
source.english: “Sorry, but that's only something I've heard in passing myself. Well, a few I've seen with my own eyes.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「この世界はどうやら───
　お前らが知っているよりずっと、何度も何度も。戦争を繰り返してるらしいな。
　ま、所詮は余所者の半可通よ」
source.english:
“Seems this world's repeated its wars far more often than you know.
Over and over and over.
But I'm only an outsider with a smattering of knowledge.”

source.japanese:
朔屋達の口ぶりからして、彼らが言う先の大戦とやらは『第二次世界大戦』を指しているべき筈なのに、呼び方からして異なる。
　ならば、朔屋達の世代、あるいはその前の世代が経てきた戦争とは、一体、なにか。
　智里が語りかけて口を濁した歴史は、一体なんなのだろう───
source.english:
Judging by the way Sakuya and Rui spoke, what they called the last great war ought to have meant the Second World War. Yet even their name for it was different.
Then what war had their generation, or the generation before them, lived through?
What was the history Tomosato had begun to describe, then left obscure?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あんた───殺し屋なんかじゃないだろ、本当は」
source.english: “You're not really a killer, are you?”

source.japanese: 朔屋の疑問も、むべなるかな。
source.english: Sakuya's question was understandable.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「いんや、殺し屋は殺し屋だよ。
　それで飯食ったこともあるし。
　ま、どこの話で、とは言わないがね」
source.english:
“No, a killer's a killer.
I've earned my meals that way too.
Won't say where, though.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Tomosato-san, just what war─── is it that you speak of, exactly?」

Just what indeed. Even Rui, who was never overly bothered with things, who let everything that didn't concern the games and carnal pleasures that were the targets of her own interest smoothly pass her by like a stream of water, seemed to hold some profound misgivings about the hulks surrounding them.

This was because, although these wrecked ships came in various degrees of rot and decrepitude, amongst them were those for which it was 『As if the flow of time had been altered』, for there were ships that, despite being from an age close to theirs, were weathered almost to the point of petrifaction, far more so than the sailing ships of wooden make that should have been far-removed in time from them. Sakuya didn't even know what class of ship it belonged to, that gigantic aircraft carrier, as Tomosato had unflinchingly called it but once; it was becoming one with the desert like it was an object of the natural world───

From within the deep brim of her bonnet, she wordlessly exchanged glances with Sakuya; there was still a mutual understanding to be found between these two who had lived many years in their differing worlds of the land and the sea, and there was an instant where the two of them felt that Tomosato was far more foreign to them both.

【Naomasa】 「It's already been forty years since the『Third World War』came to an end, for the time being at least. The economy has by no means recovered since, and I've never even heard of warships like those being built……」
【Tomosato】 「Sorry, but even I "only have a smattering knowledge" of this. Well, you have seen several of these with your own eyes at least, but.」

【Tomosato】 「It seems that this world─── For far longer than any of you people know, time and time again. Has repeatedly gone to war. Well, ultimately, this is just the superficial knowledge of a complete outsider.」

From the way in which Sakuya spoke, this previous great war he mentioned ought to have been referring to the 『Second World War』, but based on how he called it, it differed from that. Given that, this war that Sakuya's generation, or perhaps the generation before his, went through: just what in the world was it? This history that Tomosato had begun to address in vague, evasive tones: just what could it be───
【Naomasa】 「You───are actually not a murderer at all, are you?」
Sakuya's suspicion was also all too reasonable.
【Tomosato】 「Nah, a murderer is but a murderer. I've even made a living out of it. Well, not gonna tell you where I did it.」

source.japanese: 不可解な言い様に、朔屋がなおも食い下がろうとした時、辺りを見回していた泪が、不意に立ち上がって駆け出して、一直線に。
source.english: As Sakuya tried to pursue that inscrutable answer, Rui, who had been looking around, suddenly rose and ran straight ahead.

target.text: Just when Sakuya grew even more persistent in the face of his incomprehensible manner of speaking, Rui, who had been quietly surveying their surroundings, suddenly rose to her feet and bolted away, heading straight for something.

source.japanese: 彼女が走り出す前に朔屋は、短く息を呑んだのを聞いた。何事か、最前より彼女を悩ませていた不審の素をついに探り当てたような、唐突の走り出し、沓も履かないまま。
source.english: Before she ran, he heard her briefly catch her breath. As though she had finally found the source of the doubt that had troubled her all this time. She took off abruptly, without even putting her shoes on.

target.text: Just before she broke into a run, Sakuya had heard a short gasp of surprise coming from her. It was a run so sudden, shoes still left behind on the sand, that it was as though she'd finally figured out the source of what had been troubling her so for a time, whatever it was.

source.japanese: 突然の行動に朔屋は泡を食う、今まで自分達以外の何者とも遭遇してはいないが、どんな危険が潜[ひそ]んでいるものか知れたものではない未知の沙漠、ただの岩くれだって尖っていれば、柔らかな泪の身体には充分身を損なう害となる。
source.english: Sakuya panicked at the sudden action. They had encountered no one but themselves, yet this was an unknown desert. Who knew what dangers lurked? Even an ordinary rock, if sharp, could hurt Rui's soft body badly enough.

target.text: Sakuya lost his head at the sudden action, for though they may not have encountered any others until now, this was a wholly unfamiliar desert where all manner of dangers may lurk behind every corner, and even just a regular rock, if sharp enough, could bring plenty of harm to Rui's soft body.

source.japanese: 慌てて後を追うと、泪は一隻の廃船の元で、呆然と見上げていた。朽ちかけて、辛うじて帆船と言う事が見てとれる、木造船だった。そしてひどく破損していた。
source.english: Hurrying after her, he found her staring upward, dazed, beside one of the wrecks. Wooden, rotting, barely recognizable as a sailing ship. And terribly damaged.

target.text: As he chased after her in a panic, he found Rui standing before a single ruined vessel, looking up at it in a daze. It was of wooden make and had already begun to rot, what one could just barely perceive to be a sailing ship. And it was terribly damaged too.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「これ───あの人の───」
source.english: “This… His…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「泪さん、いきなり駆け出さないでくれ。
　なにかあったかとびっくりするだろう。
　で、今、なにか言ったか？」
source.english:
“Don't suddenly run off like that, Rui.
You'll make me think something's happened.
What did you just say?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「This───is his───」
【Naomasa】 「Rui-san, please don't start running all of a sudden. You gave me a real shock, I was afraid something might have happened to you. Wait, hold on, what was that just now?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「このお船……わたくしが、
　初めて愛した人の」
source.english:
“This ship…
My first love's—”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あの方が乗っていらした……」
source.english: “He sailed aboard her…”

source.japanese:
見あげる泪の眼差しに、遠き日々が去来して、彼女の初めての男に嫉妬するよりも、泪がこんな、恋に焦がれる処女のような表情を見せた事が、何故か嬉しかったのである。
　だが、その表情は表情としても、さすがにその木造船の状況はひどすぎた。歳月の中で石のように硬くなり損ね、大火事の後に焼け残った柱や土台のような、竜骨や肋材がかろうじて輪郭を残している物の、風にもぐさぐさ欠片が腐れ、零されていくような。
source.english:
Distant days passed through Rui's upturned gaze. Rather than jealousy of her first man, Sakuya felt an inexplicable pleasure that she could show an expression like a maiden yearning for love.
Yet whatever her expression, the wooden ship's condition was dreadful. It had failed to harden like stone through the years. Like pillars and foundations left after a great fire, its keel and ribs barely retained an outline. The wind seemed capable of crumbling them into rotten fragments.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「このボロッボロのが……？」
source.english: “This wrecked old thing…?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「This ship……it is the one that my very first love.」
【Rui】 「It is the ship that he sailed……」

Halcyon days of yore flitted by in Rui's raised gaze, but for some reason, rather than feeling jealous of the woman's first man, he rejoiced at seeing Rui make an expression so similar to that of a maiden in deep, yearning love. However, as wonderful an expression as it may have been, the state of this wooden ship was surely far too appalling. It had not managed to harden like stone as time passed it by; it was more akin to a pillar or a foundation that had survived a fierce fire, with only the silhouette of a keel and ribs barely surviving, as though fragments of it were rotting off and being scattered in the wind.
【Naomasa】 「This old piece of junk……?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でも、そうなのよ。
　わたくしが見誤るわけがありません」
source.english:
“But it is. I
could not mistake it.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「難破するこの船から、
　あの方をお救いいたしました───」
source.english:
“I saved him
from this ship when she was wrecked.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「But it is the truth. I could never mistake it.」
【Rui】 「As this ship foundered, I saved him from it───」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「この船がこんなところにあるなんて───
　やっぱりこの沙漠は、
　父上の仕業───？」
source.english:
“For this ship to be here…
Is this desert my father's
doing after all?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「For this ship to be in a place like this is simply─── I knew it, this desert, is this all father's doing───?」

source.japanese:
泪、物語を諳[そら]んじるように、遠い声音で呟いて、───それとももしかして、本当に一つの物語だったのかも知れない───頷くと、夢遊病者じみた仕草で傍[そば]に落ちていた二枚の貝を拾い上げた。
　二つを合わせてそっと息を吹きこめば、女の息というより、風が通うように蕭々と、美しい、そして物哀しい、音色が廃船群の間に鳴り響いていく。
source.english:
Rui murmured distantly, as though reciting a story from memory. Perhaps it really had been a story. She nodded, then, with a sleepwalker's movements, picked up two shells lying nearby.
Bringing them together, she gently breathed into them. Not so much a woman's breath as wind passing through: a beautiful, mournful sound sighed among the wrecks.

source.japanese:
鎮魂歌のようだった。
　海の姫が奏でたる鎮魂の、
　けれど泪は誰に、なんの魂に捧げようというのだろう。
source.english:
Like a requiem.
A requiem played by the princess of the sea.
Yet to whom, to what soul, was Rui offering it?

target.text: Rui murmured in a distant tone of voice, as though reciting a tale from memory ───or perhaps, who could say if this truly was but a tale─── and with a nod, she picked up two shells that were lying nearby on the ground, her mannerisms reminiscent of a somnambulist. When she pressed the two together and gently sent her breath through them, a lonely, beautiful, as well as melancholy timbre, more akin to the soughing of the wind than any woman's breath, resounded between the cluster of abandoned ships.
It was like a requiem, A repose for the souls of the dead performed by a princess of the seas, but to whom, and just what kind of soul, did Rui dedicate it?

source.japanese:
───すると、残骸と化した船の合間に浮かび上がり始めたのが、幾つもの幻影だ。
　大きな戦争の様子だった。
source.english:
Then visions began to rise between the ruined ships.
Scenes of a great war.

source.japanese:
人々が沢山沢山、夥しく死んでいった。
　都市は破壊され、海も沸き立つ。
source.english:
People died in vast, vast numbers.
Cities were destroyed. The sea boiled.

source.japanese:
いくつかは朔屋と泪にも見当がつく情景があったし、またいくつかは、二人には想像もつかない兵器を用いた戦場もあった。
　なにやら智里だけが、なにかを悟っている風情に目を逸らしたけれど、結局は何も語らずに幻景を受け流すまま。
source.english:
Some scenes Sakuya and Rui could make sense of. Others showed battlefields with weapons neither could imagine.
Only Tomosato looked away as though understanding something. But in the end he said nothing, letting the phantom scenes pass.

source.japanese: 不思議で、異様で、そして哀しい風景ではあったけれど、朔屋は沙漠の蜃気楼のようなものとして、受け入れられる心境にあったのだ。そしてそれを台無しに男が一人。
source.english: Strange, uncanny, and sad, yet Sakuya found himself able to accept them as something like a desert mirage. Then one man spoiled it all.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「なあ泪よ。
　あんた、淑やかに吹いてござるが、
　その貝二枚。
　……あんたの昔の乳隠しじゃねえの」
source.english:
“Hey, Rui.
You're blowing so demurely
into those two shells…
Aren't they your old breast covers?”

target.text: ───When she did, they emerged from between the ships that had turned to wreckage, countless phantoms. It formed the scene of a great war.
Innumerable people, all fallen dead in staggering amounts. Cities were destroyed, and the oceans boiled.

Several scenes were vaguely familiar to Sakuya and Rui, but then there were several more battlefields where weapons the two could not even begin to imagine were utilized. For some reason, Tomosato alone, having discerned something, turned his eyes from the spectacle and ultimately brushed off the phantoms without speaking a word.

It was an incredible, bizarre, and miserable scene, but Sakuya treated it like something akin to a mirage of the desert, with a feeling of solemn acceptance. And then, there was a single man who completely ruined that.
【Tomosato】 「Hey, Rui. A profoundly graceful performance, my lady, but those two shells there. ……You ever use those to cover up your tits back in the day?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……また適当なことをへらへらと。
　最低の男だわ、貴方って。
　わたくし、海にいた頃は『着けない派』でした」
source.english:
“…More idle nonsense and grinning.
What a dreadful man you are. When I lived in the sea,
I belonged to the wear-nothing school.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え、なに？　なんなん？」
source.english: “Huh? What? What's this?”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「直の字は、どっちが似合うと思うね？
　貝殻か、それとも海星か」
source.english:
“Which do you think suits her better,
Nao? Shells or starfish?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だから何の話だよ。智里、あんたは意味不明の発言が多すぎ───」
source.english: “What are you talking about? Tomosato, you make far too many incomprehensible—”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……Once again, more thoughtless prattle. You are a most despicable man. Back when I lived in the seas, I counted myself part of the『au naturel』faction.」
【Naomasa】 「Huh, what? Hold on, what?」
【Tomosato】 「Big Nao, which do you think looks best? Seashells? Or starfish?」
【Naomasa】 「Again, what are you talking about? Tomosato, you make way too many incomprehensible statements───」

source.japanese: 朔屋の口を閉ざしたのは、やにわ身を起こして遮[さえぎ]った智里の片手の、泪もなにごとか察したのか貝を吹くをやめて、耳を澄ますように眼を閉じ意識を凝らす。
source.english: Tomosato suddenly sat up and cut Sakuya off with a raised hand. Rui too seemed to sense something. She stopped blowing into the shells, closed her eyes as though listening closely, and concentrated.

target.text: What made Sakuya shut his mouth was Tomosato, who had suddenly sprung to his feet, covering it with one of his hands, and Rui also stopped blowing into the shells after sensing something; she closed her eyes like she was straining her ears, concentrating her entire being into them.

source.japanese:
初めは、遠い砂鳴りかと思えた。
　しかしそれは次第に高まって、はっきりと聴き取れるようになる。
　砂、などではない。海鳴りの音だ───！
source.english:
At first, it seemed to be the distant sound of sand.
But it grew louder, until they heard it clearly.
Not sand. The roar of the sea—!

target.text: At first, it seemed like the distant rustling of sand. But it gradually grew in intensity, until it became clearly audible. That was no mere sand. It was the rumbling of the sea───!

source.japanese: 地平線を浸食するように、沙漠の向こうから大津波の押し寄せたる、圧倒的な広がりを持って。
source.english: From beyond the desert a vast wave approached, with an overwhelming breadth, as though eating away the horizon.

source.japanese: 沙漠に海が戻ろうとしている───！
source.english: The sea was returning to the desert—!

target.text: As if eroding away the horizon, a great tsunami surged towards them from the other side of the desert, possessing an overwhelming span.
The sea was trying to return to the desert───!

source.japanese: しかしそれは、三人にとって必ずしも望ましい出来事に非ず、少なくとも今は。
source.english: For the three, however, this was not necessarily a welcome event. At least not now.

target.text: However, for the three of them, this was not an entirely welcome state of affairs, at least not right now.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ありゃ」
source.english: “Oh.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ありゃじゃねえだろ智里、んな軽く驚ける事態かこれ！　どうするんだあんな海、こんな沙漠のど真ん中で」
source.english: “Not 'oh,' Tomosato! Is this something to be so mildly surprised at? What are we going to do about that sea, out here in the middle of the desert?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「I'll be darned.」
【Naomasa】 「Tomosato, this isn't a situation where "I'll be darned" is going to cut it! What the hell do we do about the sea, we're right in the middle of the desert!」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ごめんなさいね、直さん。
　これやっぱり、わたくし絡みの事みたい」
source.english:
“I'm sorry, Nao.
It seems this really does concern me.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はへ？」
source.english: “Huh?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I am very sorry, Nao-san. As I feared, this does appear to be something related to my affairs.」
【Naomasa】 「Awhah?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「父上は、どうあってもわたくしを連れ戻すおつもりのよう。あの方の船がこんなところに、見せつけるみたいに置いてあるから、まさかとは思ったんだけど」
source.english: “Father appears determined to bring me back, whatever it takes. When I found the ship my first love sailed on here, as though put on display for me, I wondered if it could be…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ってことは、泪さんならどうにかできないのかあれ。
　お父さんとやらにお願いするとかで」
source.english:
“Then can't you do something about it, Rui?
Ask this father of yours?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Father dearest, it seems, intends to bring me back no matter the cost. With his ship left in a place like this, in a way that seemed to almost be flaunting it, the unlikely thought did strike me.」
【Naomasa】 「So then, Rui-san, surely you can do something about this, right? Go ask your father or whoever to stop this or something.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「昔から、娘の言う事には聞く耳持たない方でね。ましてや貴方がた陸の者には関心が薄いの。この場合は、悪い意味で」
source.english: “He's never listened to his daughter's wishes. And he has little interest in you people of the land. In this case, in the worst sense.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「じゃああの真珠！　こないだ酒の海に潜[もぐ]る時に呑んじゃったあれ！　あれなら水の中でも息が……」
source.english: “Then that pearl! The one I swallowed when I went into the sea of liquor! With that, I could breathe underwater…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「The man has never had an ear to lend to the words of his daughter. To say nothing of how little he concerns himself with the plight of you land dwellers. In this case, that is not to your benefit.」
【Naomasa】 「Theeen, that pearl! The one I swallowed when I dove into the sea of wine the other day! If I had that, I could breathe underwater……」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「今は持ち合わせてません。
　今すぐに、わたくしを本気で泣かせるか、
　悦ばせるかして下さるのなら、
　差し上げられるけれど」
source.english:
“I haven't one with me now.
If you could make me truly cry,
or give me pleasure right this instant,
I could give you one.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I do not have any on hand right now. If you can genuinely make me cry, or delight me, right this moment, then you may be offered one.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「なにか厭ねえ、そういうのは。野暮よ」
source.english: “But I dislike that sort of thing. So graceless.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「野暮とかなんか言ってる場合ですか……。
　いいや、なら智里───」
source.english:
“Is this the time to talk about gracelessness…?
Fine, then, Tomosato—”

target.text: 【Rui】 「But something about that sort of thing strikes me as disagreeable. Lacking in taste.」
【Naomasa】 「Is this really the time to be talking about taste……. Whatever, then, Tomosato───」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「お前ね、他力本願が悪いとは言わんが、そんな暢気な状況でも無さそうだ」
source.english: “I won't say relying on others is wrong, but things don't seem quite so leisurely.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Buddy, I'm not going to say that relying on others for salvation is wrong, but this doesn't look like a situation where we can afford to be that carefree.」

source.japanese:
迫り来る海の勢い物凄く、信天翁号まで戻ろうにも間に合いそうにない。
　周囲に散在する艦は、どれもこれも朽ち果て、破損しているものばかり。このままでは泪以外はどうなってしまうことか───
source.english:
The approaching sea was tremendously swift. They would never reach the Albatross in time.
Every ship scattered about them was decayed and damaged. If this continued, what would become of them—except Rui?

target.text: The looming sea approached with an awesome force, and even should they try to make it back to the Albatross, it didn't seem like they would reach her in time. The warships scattered around their surroundings were each and all rusted and decayed, all defect and broken. As things stood, Rui aside, what would become of them───

source.japanese: 進むもならず退がるには時既に遅く、立ち往生余儀なくされる三人から、かなり離れた窪地だ、明かりが灯ったのは。廃船を間にいくつか置いて隔てて、光ばかりが廃れた船体の連なりを通して漏れてくるから、やや近づいてみるまでその輪郭が判別されなかったが。
source.english: Unable to advance, too late to retreat, the three stood stranded. Then a light came on in a hollow some distance away. Several wrecks lay between them and it; only light leaked through the line of ruined hulls. Until they drew a little nearer, they could not distinguish its shape.

target.text: They had nowhere to advance, and it was already too late to retreat, but from a depression, quite the distance away from the three who had been left stumped through no will of their own, there shone a light. Several hulks separated them from it, with only light leaking through as it travelled through the series of abandoned hulls, so until they got a little closer, they were unable to distinguish the exact contour of the thing.

source.japanese:
船体全殻が鋼鉄で鎧われた艦だ。他の廃船に紛れて判らなかったが、その艦はほぼ無傷に留まっている。先ほど智里が原子力潜水艦と告げたものと似たような形と朔屋には見えたが、その詳細までは当然判別し得ぬ。
　ただ、彼らを招くように船殻のハッチが開き、艦全体に息を吹き返すような起動音が轟いたのが、離れた三人まで伝わった。
source.english:
A vessel armored in steel over its entire hull. Hidden among the wrecks, it had escaped notice, but remained almost undamaged. To Sakuya it resembled the nuclear submarine Tomosato had identified earlier. Naturally, he could not distinguish the details.
A hatch in the hull opened as though inviting them aboard. The sound of the whole vessel starting up, returning to life, reached the three from afar.

target.text: It was a warship whose entire hull was clad in steel. It had disappeared into the cluster of broken ships before, so they hadn't realized it, but this warship had remained in almost perfect condition. To Sakuya, it looked similar in form to that vessel Tomosato had just earlier informed him was a nuclear-powered fast attack submarine, but naturally, it was impossible for him to discern that in such detail. However, the hatch in the hull was opened as if inviting them inside, and as though entire vessel had come back to life, the roar of machinery starting up reverberated through the vessel, reaching even the three standing some distance away.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おっ。捨てる神あれば拾うなんとやらだ。
　あの艦なら、いい目が出れば持ちこたえられるかも知れねえ」
source.english:
“Oh! One god casts you off, another picks you up,
or however it goes. With that vessel, a lucky roll might let us hold out.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ピンゾロが出たら親の総取りだぞっ。
　言いたかないけど、
　俺は博才はからっきしだ」
source.english:
“If the ones come up, the banker takes everything!
Hate to say it,
but I've no talent for gambling.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Ooh. When one door closes, another door opens, or something like that. In a ship like that, if we get a lucky roll of the dice, we might just be able to make it through this.」
【Naomasa】 「And if we get snake eyes, the dealer takes all. I really don't like admitting it, but I am completely hopeless when it comes to gambling.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「カードゲームも弱いものねえ……」
source.english: “You're weak at cards too…”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Card games too……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そんなら朔屋一人置いてきゃ、俺と泪には運が向くか。朔屋、てめえはここでだだってろい。
　俺は乗っかってみるからよ」
source.english:
“Then leaving Sakuya behind might improve the odds for Rui and me. Sakuya, stand there and sulk.
I'm taking the chance.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あっ。そんな。
　俺も行くって、友達だろう？」
source.english:
“Ah! No! I'm coming too.
We're friends, aren't we?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「In that case, should we just leave Sakuya here and hope Rui and I are in luck's way? Sakuya, you keep throwing your little tantrum. I'm gonna give climbing in this thing a shot.」
【Naomasa】 「Ah. No way. I'm coming too, we're friends, right?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「けっ、都合のイイこった。
　なんにしても、急ぐぞ！」
source.english:
“Hah. Convenient,
that. Anyway, hurry!”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Bah, it's always about what suits you. Anyhow, just make it quick!」

source.japanese: 朽ちた船の一部、部品が混じる砂を蹴立てれば、弱い月影の中骨片のように舞う、走る脚は智里なら袴[はかま]の、疾走には本来向かないのだが裾[すそ]の捌きに無駄の無く一番早い、脚にまとわりつくような洋装の泪、さすがに褄[つま]を摘[つま]んで脹[ふく]ら脛[はぎ]を露わに、少々はしたないのも彼女なら佳景となる、なにより走る歩度に合わせてその尻が、縦にみっしり布地を張り詰めさせて、と見入る朔屋は列の最後の訳だが、なにも泪の臀を観賞する為でも、二人の為に殿[しんがり]を買って出たわけでもなく、この男、三人の中では一番走りやすいなりをしていながら、一番足が遅いのである。
source.english: They kicked up sand mingled with fragments and fittings of rotted ships, which wheeled like splinters of bone in the feeble moonlight. Tomosato led: his hakama were never made for sprinting, yet not a motion of the hems was wasted. Rui's Western dress clung about her legs; obliged at last to gather her skirts, she bared her calves—a trifle indecorous, though on her even that became a pleasing prospect—and, better yet, with every stride her buttocks drew the fabric taut from top to bottom. Sakuya, watching, came last in line. Not, mind you, because he had elected to admire Rui's backside, nor because he had nobly volunteered for the rear guard. Though dressed more suitably for running than either of them, the man was simply the slowest of the three.

source.japanese:
走る姿勢も眼を背[そむ]けたくなる。朔屋はどうしてか必死に走る時ほど、いや必死だからか、無様さが際だつのだ。それも、戦国の塗炭に苦しみ逃散する百姓、大火に焼け出される町民、大風に吹き飛ばされつつ逃げ惑う村民、と前近代的な悲惨さがつくのは、なぜかこの男、必死で走る時つい両手を挙げる癖[ヘキ]があるからで、恐らくその辺りから、側対歩時代の人間を思わせるのだろう。
　ともかく、二人にやや遅れて朔屋も、どうにか潜水艦まで辿り着き、船殻の昇降梯子を這い上がり───
source.english:
Even his running posture made one want to look away. Somehow, the more desperately Sakuya ran—or precisely because he was desperate—the more conspicuous his ineptitude became. It carried a premodern misery: peasants fleeing the torments of the age of warring states, townspeople driven out by a great fire, villagers running as a gale blew them off their feet. For some reason, whenever he ran desperately, he raised both hands. Perhaps that was what recalled an earlier age, when people moved arm and leg together on the same side.
At any rate, a little behind the other two, he somehow reached the submarine and crawled up the hull's ladder.

target.text: As they kicked off against the sand mixed with parts fallen from some of the decrepit ships, it soared into the air like spicules of bone in the faint moonlight; to describe the running of the three, Tomosato was the fastest, and despite being clad in a hakama, a garment that was never suited for sprinting, he wasted not a single moment in dealing with the hem.

Rui, clad in a dress that seemed to almost cling to her legs, had, as one might expect, pinched the skirt of her dress between her fingers, exposing her calves, but while slightly immodest, it made for a beautiful sight when she was the culprit, and more than anything, the way her behind moved in unison with her running steps, how the fabric was pulled taut across it, made a spectacle that entranced Sakuya, who had formed the end of the line, but this was certainly not because he wanted to admire Rui's buttocks, nor because he had volunteered to form the rear guard for the sake of the other two.
It was simply because this man, while the best dressed for running, also happened to be the most leaden-footed of the three.

His running posture also made one want to avert one's eyes. For whatever reason, the harder Sakuya tries to run in desperation, or rather, perhaps it is simply by virtue of the fact Sakuya is trying desperately at all, the more conspicuous his disgracefulness becomes. In addition, why was it that this man, like the farmers suffering under the distress of the Warring States period who fled their fields, the townspeople burned out of their homes by great conflagrations, or the villagers being blown away by typhoons, what one might call victims of the tragic misery of pre-modern life, had a habit of raising both his hands high in the air whenever he ran for his life?

It was likely this way of running that made him resemble a relic from the era of the lateral gait. Regardless, while somewhat slower than the other two, Sakuya also somehow managed to make his way to the submarine, and he scrambled up the climbing ladder leading up the hull─── (TN: Sokutaiho, written "側対歩", refers to a way of walking that was common in Edo-period Japan and earlier. It is theorized that before the introduction of Western marching, Japanese people didn't walk or run with diagonal movements, instead moving laterally with, for example, the right leg and right arm at the same time without twisting their torso.)

source.japanese: 迎えたのは分厚い鋼のハッチ、泪も既に降りていく頭が暗がりに浮いている程度なのが今沈んだ、どこかの防空壕にでも潜[もぐ]りこむような息苦しさを覚えて、朔屋はまだ逡巡してたものの、他にどうしようもなく、かといって溺れ死にたくもないので、狭い昇降口を不器用に降りていったところ、
source.english: A thick steel hatch awaited him. Rui was already descending. Only her head floated in the darkness, and now it sank. The entrance gave him the stifling feeling of crawling into an air-raid shelter. He still hesitated, but there was no other choice, and he did not want to drown. Awkwardly, he climbed down through the narrow opening.

target.text: What greeted him was a thick steel hatch, and Rui was already climbing down, her head floating in the darkness as it descended before his eyes; struck by a suffocating feeling as though he were about to conceal himself in some air-raid shelter, Sakuya hesitated once more, but left with no other choice───it wasn't as though he particularly desired to drown to death───right when he began to clumsily clamber down the narrow hatchway,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「締めてこいよハッチをよ。
　逃げてきた意味がねえだろうが」
source.english:
“Close the hatch.
What's the point of escaping in here otherwise?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Close it, the hatch. Or there'll be no point having fled in here, right?」

source.japanese: 智里に怒鳴られて、慌てて締めに戻った時には津波は朔屋には泣きたくなるほど間近に迫って、がたがた震える手を必死に宥[なだ]めてハッチを封する、間に合った、さあ下へ、皆と一緒なら少しは恐怖も紛らわせる、と、足を踏み外してがんがんがん。肘やら脛[すね]やら打ちつけて落ちてきた朔屋に智里は腹を抱え、泪は行儀よく見てみないふり、そこに───
source.english: Tomosato's shout sent him hastily back to close it. By then the wave was so near he could have wept. Desperately calming his trembling hands, he sealed the hatch. In time. Now down. With everyone together, some of his fear would ease—He missed a step. Bang, bang, bang. Sakuya fell, striking elbow and shin. Tomosato clutched his belly with laughter. Rui politely pretended not to see. Then—

target.text: Yelled at by Tomosato, when he made it back up to the hatch in a panic to close it, the tsunami had drawn so imminent, it made Sakuya want to cry; he desperately tried to calm his trembling hand, then sealed the hatch: he made it; now then, back down, and with all of them together, surely his fear would be soothed and───he missed a rung on the ladder, falling down with loud clanging and banging; upon seeing Sakuya fall down, hitting his elbows and his shins and so forth, Tomosato was clutching his stomach with laughter, Rui was pretending not to see anything, as was only polite, and then───

source.japanese: 船殻を叩く、凄まじい衝撃の、水がぶつかったと言うよりその轟音、朔屋には一度だけ見た事のあるトラックと乗り合いバスの衝突事故を想い出させた。断じて流体がぶつかるような生やさしい音ではない。
source.english: A tremendous impact struck the hull. Rather than water hitting it, the roar reminded Sakuya of a collision between a truck and a bus he had once witnessed. Nothing so gentle as the sound of fluid striking.

source.japanese: 更に被さる、金属が甲高く擦れるような不快な響きに朔屋はつい両手で耳を覆ったが、途端、浮遊感に足許がさらわれる、実際に床を離れてふわりと、舞ったまではいいが、また強かに内部の隔壁に叩きつけられの、これで鋭角の船内の機構や配管の類があれば、津波から逃れても自身の血の海に沈んだ事だろう。艦は、津波に引きもぎられて、沙漠の砂の褥[しとね]から奔流の中に呑み込まれていた。幸い泪は、配管の一本に腕絡めて足場を確保した、智里に腕掴まれて無事のよう。
source.english: Over it came an unpleasant, high scraping of metal. Sakuya instinctively covered his ears. At once a floating sensation swept away his footing. He actually left the floor, rose lightly—and was slammed hard into an internal bulkhead. Had there been sharp-edged machinery or piping there, he would have escaped the wave only to sink into a sea of his own blood. The vessel had been torn loose by the wave and swallowed into the torrent from its sandy bed. Fortunately, Rui seemed safe. Tomosato had secured his footing with an arm hooked about a pipe and caught her by the arm.

source.japanese:
内臓を直で絞られるような、天地の別も不明になるような揺れ、というより回転が何度か見舞い、その都度朔屋を猫に弄[もてあそ]ばれる蛙のように無様にあちこちにと転がしたが、青年は途中で襟元をバルブに引っかけて固定された為、それ以上翻弄される事はなくなった、首が些[いささ]か危険に締まりはしたが。
　それでも揺れは徐々に減じ、最後に船殻をなにやら硬い物が叩いたこぉーんという音を、お終いの合図にしたように鎮まりゆく。
　どうにか三人も、この鋼の艦も、沙漠の中の津波という、どうにも冴えない洒落の効いた事態の中、持ちこたえたようだった。
source.english:
Several times, a shaking—or rather a rolling—seemed to wring their innards directly, obliterating all distinction between up and down. Each time it tumbled Sakuya about as pitifully as a frog toyed with by a cat. But midway through, his collar caught on a valve and held him. He was tossed no farther, though his neck was constricted rather dangerously. The shaking gradually diminished.
At last, a hard object struck the hull with a hollow clang, as though signaling the end,
and it subsided. Somehow the three and their steel vessel had endured that lamentable joke of a situation: a great wave in the desert.

target.text: Something struck the hull, a terrific impact, and to Sakuya, the thunderous boom sounded not like the sound of colliding with water, instead making him recall something he'd witnessed but a single time: the traffic collision of a truck and a transit bus. It was decidedly not a sound simple and light enough to seem like it originated from being struck with a liquid.

On top of that, the unpleasant sound of what seemed like a shrill scraping coming from the metal covering them made Sakuya unconsciously block his ears with both hands, but the moment he did, his footing was swept away like he was floating, and in fact, he had left the floor, which was fine for as long as he remained gently floating, but when he was once more violently slammed into the internal bulkhead, had there been some kind of piping or the sharp corner of some onboard machinery in his path, even had he managed to escape the tsunami, he would surely have drowned in a sea of his own blood.

The vessel of war was tossed about in the tsunami, taken from its cushion of sand in the desert and swallowed by the torrent. Fortunately, Rui had managed to secure her footing by hooking an arm around a pipe, and with Tomosato holding on to the other, it seemed she was safe.

It was like his viscera were being squeezed directly, a shaking so intense he could no longer discern between heaven and earth, or rather, the vessel actually rolled over several times, and each time, Sakuya would be rolling around here and there in an unseemly display akin to a frog being toyed with by a cat, but thanks to his collar getting stuck on a valve partway through, he was spared the suffering of being tossed about any further, although it was getting a little dangerously tight around his neck.

Still, the shaking gradually abated, and finally, as if the hull struck something hard, a resonant metallic gong rang out, and as though that were the closing bell, the vessel returned to quiet. Somehow or other, these three, and this vessel of steel, too, had managed to withstand this tsunami in the middle of a desert, a situation dull and wryly amusing both.

source.japanese: ……朔屋はそこを、司令所と見た。三方に円い小さな窓のある、堅牢な区画だ。こういう時でもなかったら、その秘密めかした狭苦しさは、信天翁号のあの、天幕の楽屋裏に巣を作った朔屋に好ましく感じられたろう。
source.english: Sakuya took this to be the command station. A sturdy compartment with small round windows on three sides. In other circumstances, its secretive confinement would probably have appealed to the man who had made himself a nest backstage in the Albatross's tent.

target.text: ……Sakuya noticed they were in a control room. Small round windows in three directions, a sturdy compartment. Had it not been in a situation like this one, the cramped, secretive nature of the place would surely have been thought of fondly by Sakuya, the man who created his little hidey-hole in the backstage of that tent on the Albatross.

source.japanese: 窓に身を乗り出しても、暗くて良くは見えない、と汗ばんだ鼻先を押し当てると、不意に明かりが灯ったのに驚いて、肩が跳ねて頭をぶつけたが、何ほどの事はない、というよりむしろ望ましい兆候の、艦内に明かりが灯っていた。内部は駆動系はどうなっているのか不明だが、電装系はまだどうにか生きているようだ。
source.english: Leaning toward a window, he could see little in the darkness. He pressed his sweaty nose against it. Suddenly a light came on. Startled, he jerked his shoulders and struck his head. Nothing serious—indeed, rather a welcome sign. The interior had lit up. Whatever the condition of its propulsion, the vessel's electrical equipment still seemed somehow alive.

source.japanese: どうやら、艦の周囲はすっかり元の海に戻っていると三人には思われた。がくん、と体が一方に押しつけられるような感覚が朔屋達を包む。
source.english: Around the vessel, it seemed to all three, everything had returned to sea. Then a jolt, a sensation of being pressed toward one side, enveloped them.

source.japanese:
黒髪を一揺すり、可変する黒翼のように艦内部の宙に舞わして、胸を誇らかに反らす。
密航者とは密航する者だからして、ここに密航しているのは当然なのだ、とそう言いたいのだろうが───密航者は、右の胸に蛞蝓が這ったような悪心地に突如襲われて、困惑して見れば、朔屋の眼が爛々と、南米の沼地に出現する妖怪のような光に滑っていた。それだけでない。左の胸にもなにやら視線の圧力が、こちらは泪の、密航者の美質をいかにも好もしく愛でていたけれど、泪の愛しようというのは肉に直接結びつく。
　密航者は、慌てて腕で覆い隠して暗がりに引っ込んだけれど、弱った事には、泪が眺めていた方は柔らかい羽のような感触が、朔屋の方は生ぬるい葛の汁で覆われたような心地が何時までも続いて、大いに彼女を戸惑わせた。
source.english:
She tossed her black hair, sending it aloft inside the vessel like a shifting black wing, and proudly threw out her chest.
A stowaway was one who stowed away, so naturally she was here stowing away—that, presumably, was what she meant. Then a sensation as vile as a slug crawling over her right breast came upon her. Bewildered, she looked and found Sakuya's eyes blazing, their gleam slick as some bogey rising from a South American swamp. Nor was that all. Her left breast, too, felt the pressure of a gaze: Rui's. Rui was admiring the stowaway's charms with the fondest appreciation; unfortunately, whatever Rui loved tended to connect directly to the flesh.
The stowaway hastily covered herself with an arm and retreated into the dark. Worse, the side Rui had admired went on tingling as though brushed by a soft feather, while Sakuya's felt coated in lukewarm kudzu slime. The sensations lingered and lingered, to her profound discomfiture.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Why are you asking the obvious? I mean, I'm a stowaway.」

She gave a shake of her black hair, and as though it had transformed into a pair of black wings, it fluttered about in the air within the warship, and she puffed out her chest with pride. Given that a stowaway was someone who stowed away, it was only natural for her to be stowing away here: that was probably what she was trying to say, but───the stowaway was suddenly seized by a most wicked sensation, like a slug were crawling across her right breast, and as she looked around in perplexity, Sakuya's eyes were ablaze, dissolving into a shimmering light akin to the apparitions that manifest in the swamps of South America. And that was not all.

She felt the heavy weight of some manner of stare upon her left breast, and this one was from Rui, who was very fondly appreciating the excellent qualities of this stowaway, however, whenever Rui felt admiration for something, it was inevitably directly related to the carnal. The stowaway covered her chest in a panic, drawing back into the darkness, but what had her at such a loss was how, no matter how much time passed, the sensation of Rui's staring, like the touch of a soft feather, and Sakuya's, which left her feeling like she was being covered in lukewarm kudzu, never ceased, leaving her greatly confused.

source.japanese: 潜水艦は何者かに誘導されたように、海の底まで潜行し、やがて海底の山腹の腹に黒々と口を開ける虚ろを、投影される光の中に見た、潜った。
source.english: As though guided by someone, the submarine descended to the seabed. In its projected light, they saw a hollow gaping black in the flank of an undersea mountain. The vessel entered.

source.japanese:
どうやら海底洞窟と思しく、それもかなりの広がりを有しているようで、艦は航行に不自由なく闇淵の中を進んでいく。
　やがて行き着いた果て。
　洞窟奥に佇立したるは、異形異様の、遙かな歳月を閲[けみ]し、人間とは隔絶した神気をおんもらと放つ、其は神殿か。
　潜水艦を迎えるように、群れ集う魚人達がある。それは朔屋がいつか見た、泪の船室に押しかけていたモノ達だ。
　やがて潜水艦が停止したのは、海底洞窟内の広間。空気があって比較的乾いている。潜水艦の中に留まっていても仕方ないので、朔屋達は洞窟内に進んでいく事となったのだが、あの密航者が、いつの間にか姿を消していた。
source.english:
Apparently an undersea cave, and a vast one. The vessel proceeded without difficulty through its dark depths.
At the end of its journey stood something strange,
something alien, steeped in far-reaching ages and quietly giving off a divinity utterly removed from humanity. A temple?
Fish-people gathered as though to receive the submarine. They were the beings Sakuya had seen crowding into Rui's cabin.
At last the vessel stopped in a hall within the undersea cave. There was air, and it was comparatively dry. Nothing would be gained by remaining aboard, so Sakuya and the others went farther inside. The stowaway, however, had vanished unnoticed.

target.text: As though being guided by someone's hand, the submarine dove all the way to the bottom of the sea, until finally, within the light being projected, they saw a hollow, a dark maw leading into the belly of the seamounts rising from the seabed, and it dove within.

It seemed to be some manner of underwater cave, and one boasting of quite the breadth, for the warship continued onward into the dark, abyssal depths without the slightest inconvenience. Eventually, they reached the end of their journey. Standing in the depths of the cavern, equal parts grotesque and bizarre, something that had seen countless aeons pass, emitting a fierce flood of a divine aura utterly removed from humanity, was a temple?

Fishmen crowded together as if to welcome their submarine. They were the ones Sakuya had seen in the past, the ones who had barged into Rui's cabin. When the submarine finally came to a halt, it was in a grand, spacious hall within the underwater cavern. There was breathable air, and it was relatively dry.
