Nothing would come from holing up in the submarine, and so Sakuya and company decided to venture further into the cavern, but that stowaway had managed to vanish without any of them noticing exactly when.

source.japanese:
暗がりの中に一つ点じられた懐中電燈の灯りがおずおずと照らし出した、滑やかに濡れた質感は、生き物の内臓の粘膜のそれであり、ならば三人は旧約聖書のヨナなる預言者の如く、巨獣の腹に呑みこまれてしまったとでもいうのか。
　が、跫音は隧道の中を歩むように硬く響いて石か岩、つまりここは鍾乳洞なのだった。それも海底の。
source.english:
A single flashlight shone timidly through the darkness. The smooth, wet texture it revealed was that of the mucous lining of living organs. Had the three been swallowed into a great beast's belly, like Jonah, the prophet of the Old Testament?
Yet their footsteps rang hard, as in a tunnel. Stone or rock. In other words, this was a limestone cave. Beneath the sea.

source.japanese:
……歳月というのは不思議なものだ。地中に埋もれた生き物の体を石にするかと思えば、こうして岩壁に生き物めいた肌合いを与えたりもする。
　三人の歩度と共に移動する光源の中に展開されていく内壁は、無機質の岩塊というより、指先で軽く突いただけで生命の息遣いを取り戻し、秘やかにうねりだしそうな、そんな危うさを秘めた均衡の中に停止した、生き物の胎内と言った方がよほど適当だろう。
source.english:
Time is a curious thing. It turns the bodies of creatures buried underground to stone, yet here it gave rock walls the texture of life.
Unfolding in the light that moved with the three, the inner walls seemed less like inert masses of rock than a living interior, arrested in a precarious balance. A light prod from a fingertip might restore their breath and set them secretly undulating.

source.japanese: 時の停止したような鍾乳洞は、より地下深くへと傾斜していき、地軸まで通じているのではないかと疑わしいほどの規模であり、洞内を構成する岩塊の質量は、閉所に弱い者なら一歩踏みこんだだけでも気死せしめてしまいそうに圧倒的な。
source.english: The cave, where time seemed stopped, sloped deeper underground. So vast was it that one might wonder whether it reached the world's axis. The sheer mass of rock around them was so overwhelming that a claustrophobic person might have died of shock on taking a single step inside.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うひゃあ……っ!?」
source.english: “Eeeah…!?”

source.japanese: 岩肌には染み出した海水の伝い、足元で小流れとなって降り行く、首筋に降った雫はどこやら生温かったが、朔屋にとっては獅子の涎を受けるよりまだ肝を冷やして、それでも悲鳴は懸命に抑えて、なのに音はたちまち殷々と反響して、岩塊や岩襞のあちこちに拡散していった。
source.english: Seawater seeped over the rock, gathering into little streams that descended at their feet. A drop fell upon Sakuya's neck. Somehow lukewarm, it chilled him worse than a lion's drool would have. He struggled to suppress his scream, yet the sound instantly echoed thunderously, scattering through the masses and folds of stone.

target.text: The single light shining in the dark coming from the flashlight trembled fearfully as it illuminated a wet, slippery texture, what might well have been the membrane covering the viscera of some living creature, so given that, had the trio perhaps been swallowed within the stomach of a great beast, just like the prophet Jonah of the Old Testament? However, their footsteps rang out with a sharp hardness, like they were walking through a tunnel of stone or rock, which meant this had to be a limestone cavern. And one at the bottom of the sea at that.

……The passage of time truly was a marvellous thing. Not only did it transform the bodies of living creatures entombed in the earth into stone, it also granted walls of rock like these a texture reminiscent of those living creatures.

The inner walls, unveiled before them within the cone of light moving in tandem with their step, rather than an inorganic mass of rock, seemed to secretively undulate, as if they would regain the breath of life were they to but lightly poke them with the tip of a finger, and it was surely far more apt to describe it as the womb of a living being, hiding within it such worrying danger, its state of standstill but a temporary matter kept in a precarious balance.

The limestone cavern, in which the passage of time itself seemed to have come to a halt, sloped downwards and took them even deeper underground, its scale so vast it was enough to make one question if one had passed through even the earth's axis, and the sheer mass of rock that formed the inner cavern was so overwhelming in its presence that, were one a claustrophobic soul, merely taking one step inside might lead one to die from shock.
【Naomasa】 「Uhyaah……!?」

Seawater seeped out from the rock surface and formed a small, descending stream by their feet, and the drops landing on his neck were somewhat lukewarm, striking even greater fear into Sakuya's heart than were he to be slathered in the saliva of a lion, and yet he still desperately quelled his scream, for the sound quickly returned as a booming echo, bouncing off the lumps of rock and folds of stone as it scattered everywhere throughout the tunnel.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「やかましいよ、この阿呆」
source.english: “Keep quiet, you fool.”

source.japanese: 朔屋としては声を押さえたつもりなのに、邪険に叱りつけられたのが物哀しい。
source.english: Sakuya had meant to keep his voice down. The harsh rebuke left him feeling forlorn.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なあここって……もしや……、
　まさかして……その……」
source.english:
“…Hey, this place… Could it be… Surely not…
You know…”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「You're too loud, idiot.」
Sakuya really had tried to keep his voice down, so it was rather disheartening to be snapped at so harshly.
【Naomasa】 「……Hey, could this be……maybe……, it's unlikely, but……you know……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「思いつかねえなら、わざわざ喋んな」
source.english: “If you can't think of anything, don't bother talking.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「If you can't think of anything, don't bother talking.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……馬鹿馬鹿しい。
　馬鹿馬鹿しいくらい、変わり映えのない」
source.english:
“…Ridiculous.
So unchanged it's ridiculous.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……Ridiculous. It looks just as dull as before, to the point of absurdity.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「直さん、女がね、自分の郷を殿方に見られて思うのは、逃げ出したい、さもなければ、厭わしい、どちらかしかないわ」
source.english: “Nao, when a man sees the home a woman came from, she feels only one of two things. She wants to run away, or she finds it hateful.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんでそんなに穏やかじゃないんだよ、両方とも」
source.english: “Why do both options have to sound so alarming?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Nao-san, see, when a woman realizes her hometown is being seen by a gentleman, she wants to run away, or if not that, feels disgusted; those are the only two outcomes.」
【Naomasa】 「Why are you so on edge, both of you?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あら、だって。一度家を出た女にとってはね、郷など、昔のつまらない、恥ずかしい姿を知るところか、さもなくば今の男から連れ戻そうとする、厭わしい追っ手か、どちらかしかないの」
source.english: “Well, once a woman has left home, it is either a place that knows her old, dull, embarrassing self, or a hateful pursuer trying to reclaim her from her present man. Nothing else.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「貴方の恥ずかしい姿とか、今の旦那とか、両方関係無いじゃないか……」
source.english: “Your embarrassing self, your present husband—neither has anything to do with this…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だいたいここが、泪さんの郷って。
　こんな海底大洞窟が……？　下手な宮殿よりでかいぜ、ここ」
source.english:
“Besides, this is your home?
An enormous undersea cave? It's bigger than a second-rate palace.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Goodness, it is quite simple. To a woman who has already eloped once before, all that home will bring is the insignificant disgraces of the past coming to light, or else, repugnant pursuers who will attempt to take her back, away from her current man; those are the only two outcomes.」
【Naomasa】 「I'm pretty sure that whatever embarrassing things happened in the past and your current husband are completely unrelated……」
【Naomasa】 「And before any of that, you say this is your home, Rui-san? A huge underwater cave like this……? This is bigger than any shabby old palace I've seen.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「いいえ。下手な宮殿よ。ああ厭になる」
source.english: “No. It is a second-rate palace. Oh, how tiresome.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「No. This is a shabby old palace. Ah, how I loathe it so.」

source.japanese: 空気が流動して渦を巻く、というよりその場それ自体が歪んで、洞窟奥の暗がりへと引きずられていくような。洞内の薄光もまた空気ごと奥の暗がりに吸われいき、明るさが減じていくと共に洞窟奥の暗さがいや増して、気圧が変じているのか、それとも重低音の圧力が増したせいか、耳の中に高山に登った時のような違和感を覚え、朔屋は何度も唾を呑み下した。
source.english: Air moved and whirled—or rather, the place itself seemed to distort, being dragged into the darkness at the back of the cave. Its faint light was drawn there with the air. As brightness diminished, the darkness deepened. Had the air pressure changed, or was it the pressure of some deep bass rumble? His ears felt strange, as though he had climbed a high mountain. Sakuya swallowed repeatedly.

target.text: The air flowed and formed a maelstrom, or rather, the place itself warped as though it were being pulled deeper towards the darkness in the depths of the cavern. The pale light in the cavern was also being sucked into the shadowy depths, the dark within them growing thicker as the light abated, and perhaps the atmospheric pressure was changing, or perhaps it was because of the increasing pressure coming from that low-frequency sound, for Sakuya felt a discomfort akin to that which one feels within the ears when climbing tall mountains, and he swallowed his saliva again and again.

source.japanese:
彼らを引き連れてきた魚怪達は洞内の大気の変調が始まると共に、海流に撫でつけられる藻のようにばたばたと平伏していって、朔屋はつい場の流れに乗せられて同じように平伏そうとしたが、泪も智里も倒れゆく葦の中でしなやかに風に向かう若柳と佇んだまま。
　平伏すも抗[こう]するも、己の心のままにすれば良かろうに、そんな事さえ決めかねて、及び腰で魚怪から自分の連れ、そしていや増しに濃くなり増さる海底洞の奥の闇に視線が廻った時に、墨を練り固めて育てていくような闇の密度に、朔屋は平衡感覚に異常を来[きた]してよろめいた。
source.english:
As the cavern's air began to change, the fish-monsters who had led them here fell prostrate, one after another, like weed pressed flat by a current. Swept along by the mood, Sakuya nearly bowed down too. But Rui and Tomosato remained standing, supple young willows facing the wind amid fallen reeds.
Bow or resist: he ought to have followed his own heart. Unable to decide even that, he hovered uncertainly. His gaze moved from the fish-monsters to his companions, then to the dark growing ever denser in the cave's depths. As though ink were being kneaded solid and made to swell, its density disturbed his sense of balance. He staggered.

source.japanese: 溜まりゆく闇の密度、深さはただ事でなく、暗さに視界が通らないどころではない。視線を向けたそれだけでその闇の中へ墜落していきそうに、感覚の危うきに襲われるほど。眼球には構造上、盲点という、見えない一点が存在する。たとえば紙の上に小さな黒点なり×印なりを記して、その一点に焦点を当てないようにして視界の中紙の位置をあれこれ変えてみると、印付けたその一点が視界からすぱりと消失する位置がある。そこが視界内の盲点だ。
source.english: The gathering darkness had an extraordinary density and depth. It was not merely too dark to see through. Simply directing his gaze toward it gave him the precarious sensation that he might fall into it. By their structure, human eyes have a blind spot: one point they cannot see. Make a small black dot or cross on paper, for instance. Without focusing on that point, move the paper about in your field of vision. There is a position where the mark abruptly vanishes. That is the blind spot.

source.japanese:
生理的にどうしても発現してしまう盲点だが、そうと判っていても自分の視界内に見えない点があると知るのは愉快な事ではない。
　今洞内の奥に凝集しつつある闇は、その盲点を幾層倍も拡大してそこに置いた様なもので、船の揺れには慣れたつもりの朔屋でも、見つめるだけで嘔吐しそうになったくらいだ。それも見やるうちにどんどんとその嵩を増していき、しまいには洞窟の天井近くにまで至った。
source.english:
A blind spot is physiologically inevitable. Even knowing that, it is unpleasant to discover an invisible point in one's own sight.
The darkness concentrating at the back of the cavern was like that blind spot enlarged many times and placed before him. Sakuya, who thought himself accustomed to a ship's rolling, nearly vomited merely looking at it. And as he watched, it kept increasing in bulk until it reached almost to the cavern's roof.

source.japanese: 魚怪共は見慣れた、とまではいかずともまだ見た目が異様とか奇怪といった言葉で片づけられる。しかし今洞内の奥に顕現しつつある、人間の知覚を拒[こば]むようなその闇は。朔屋はおろおろと智里に助けを求めるように目を向けると、
source.english: He could not quite say he was accustomed to the fish-monsters. Still, words such as strange or grotesque could account for their appearance. But this darkness manifesting in the cave's depths seemed to reject human perception itself. Flustered, Sakuya looked toward Tomosato as though seeking help.

target.text: As that anomaly of the atmosphere began, the fishmen who had brought them here all noisily prostrated themselves flatly against the ground like seaweed combed down by the ocean current, and Sakuya subconsciously found himself going with the flow and began to prostrate himself similarly, but Rui and Tomosato both remained standing like youthful willows gracefully facing the wind amidst a field of collapsing reeds.

Regardless of whether he should prostrate himself or remain defiant, as long as it was what his heart desired, surely that would be good enough, but he found even that difficult to determine, and in addition, with bent back, as his gaze swung from the fishmen to his own companions before finally settling on the darkness in the depths of the undersea cave, which only seemed to grow ever darker and thicker, when faced with that Stygian dark deepening like ink kneaded and hardened, it induced disorder in Sakuya's sense of balance, and he stumbled.

The density of the pooling dark wasn't merely profoundly deep, nor was it simply that his vision didn't pierce through it. Just gazing at it alone was enough to make it feel as though he were about to fall into it, to make him doubt the veracity of his senses.

As a consequence of the way the eyeball is structured, there is a point where nothing can be seen, a place known as the blind spot. If, for example, you were to write a small black "x" mark upon a piece of paper, were you to then shuffle the paper around within your field of vision so as not to allow yourself to focus upon it, there is a particular position where that singular marked spot would completely vanish from your field of view. That is the blind spot in the visual field.

It is a blind spot that will inevitably manifest for physiological reasons, but even knowing that, it still does not make the reality of a particular point within your field of view where you can see nothing a very pleasant realization. That darkness, continuing to coalesce even now, was like having a blind spot several magnitudes larger placed within his vision, and even Sakuya, who liked to think he had gotten used to the shaking of a ship by now, felt nauseous just from looking at it. And in addition to that, as he gazed upon it, it grew taller and taller until, finally, it reached all the way up to the ceiling of the cavern.

While calling the fish monsters a familiar sight would be going too far, their appearance could still be expressed through words like grotesque or bizarre. But that which was currently emerging from the depths of the cave, that darkness that seemed to refuse human perception, on the other hand. When Sakuya helplessly turned his gaze to Tomosato in search of salvation,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……なんかこりゃあれみたいだな。
　ほら、あれよ、映画館。
　映画掛かかる寸前で、灯りが落とされる。
　あん時と同じ塩梅じゃねえか」
source.english:
“…Feels a bit like that thing, doesn't it?
You know, a cinema.
Just before the picture starts, they lower the lights.
Same sort of business.”

source.japanese:
言うに事かいてこれで、双眸が暗がりの中でまた自ずと燐を発して光を透かした蒼水晶、朔屋はそれまで己を揺るがしていた恐怖を、そこまであっさりと言い換えられてはと馬鹿馬鹿しくなってしまった由で、そう軽んじては悪いのではないかと、むしろ申し訳なさを感じたくらい。
　泪はどうしているかと見やれば、こちらはこちらで、自分の郷だというくらいだもの、やはり恐怖は気振りにも覗かせていなかったけれども、唇を引き結んでのむくれ顔、智里の軽口が癇に触ったと言うより、彼女はこの海底洞窟に連れてこられてからずっとご不興のご様子だ。
source.english:
Of all things to say. His eyes shone again within the dark, blue crystal emitting its own phosphorescence. To have the fear that had shaken him put so casually into other words made Sakuya feel ridiculous. Indeed, he almost felt apologetic: surely it was wrong to make so light of it.
Looking at Rui, he found no trace of fear there either, as one might expect since she called this her home. But her lips were pressed into a sulk. Less irritation at Tomosato's joke than the displeasure she had shown ever since being brought into this undersea cave.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……This is kind of like that thing. Look, you know, in a cinema. Just before the movie starts, all the lights are turned off. Isn't this just like that?」

Of all the things he could have said, his twin orbs once again azure crystals emitting a phosphorescent light from within themselves; upon hearing that terror that had shaken him to the core so casually rephrased into something that ridiculous, Sakuya almost felt it to be wrong, in fact, he even felt somewhat guilty, so absurd was it.

When he looked over at Rui to see how she was handling things, as expected, she never betrayed even a hint of fear───this was her own home after all───but her lips were tightly pursed, her expression displeased, but rather than Tomosato's flippant words rubbing her the wrong way, she seemed to have been in a state of ill humour ever since first being brought along into this cave at the bottom of the sea.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ほらよ───ござったぜ」
source.english: “Here we go. He's arrived.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Look───he has arrived.」

source.japanese: 視線を置いてしまうとどうしても失墜感に見舞われるから、できる限り焦点を合わせないように洞内の奥を目探れば、見あげんばかりに膨れあがった影塊の、頂き辺りに二つ灯った陰火の双眸と思しき。
source.english: Letting his gaze rest there inevitably brought a sense of falling. He searched the depths without focusing as best he could. Near the top of the looming mass of shadow, two dark flames kindled. Eyes, apparently.

target.text: He was struck by a sinking feeling no matter where he placed his gaze, and so as he tried his utmost to never focus anywhere specific while surveying the depths of the cave, just as he looked up, right around the top of that swelling mass of shadows, there were what looked like two eyes shaped by blazing ignes fatui.

source.japanese: 陰火の双眸の下方に、火で焼き切ったような線が走るのと、声が。
source.english: Below those eyes, a line ran as though burned through by fire. And a voice.

target.text: Below the twin orbs of ghostflame, a line split shade like a mark seared by a flame, and a voice boomed.

source.english:
“At last—You
have returned—Youngest
princess—My
daughter—”

source.japanese: 声というより震動が、その溶岩の裂け目のような口から大音量で響くのではなく、大気を伝わり、居合わせた者の耳元で発現して、耳の間近で殷々と緒を引いた。
source.english: More vibration than voice. It did not thunder directly from that mouth like a fissure in lava. It traveled through the air and manifested beside each listener's ear, trailing reverberations close at hand.

source.japanese:
聳立する巨影、輪郭定かならぬのに、押し寄せる存在の圧迫感に底無しに深まり渡る声、震動、対峙しているだけで、朔屋は身体が、四肢の先端から肉の一粒一粒が弾けていきそうな圧倒的な恐怖、畏怖、に重囲される。
　朔屋は先ほどの智里の軽口に乗ってしまっていて、魚怪達の長上を甘く見すぎていた事を覚った。
source.english:
A towering, vast shadow, its outline uncertain. The pressing weight of its presence, the voice—the vibration—deepening without limit. Merely standing before it surrounded Sakuya with such overwhelming fear, such awe, that every grain of his flesh seemed about to burst from the ends of his limbs inward.
He realized he had followed Tomosato's earlier joke and underestimated the fish-monsters' lord terribly.

source.japanese: なぜ周りの魚怪達に入り交じって、岩肌に額を擦りつけ赦しを願わない？　平伏してしまえば、自分の卑小なると過[あやま]ちを認めて赦しを願うべきなのではないか。その結果、哀願届かず、無情なる手に斬首されたとしても、少なくとも迫り来る刃を目の当たりにするという恐怖からは逃れられる。平伏すというのは、相手に自分の首を差し出すのと同じ行為であるという事。
source.english: Why not mingle with the fish-monsters around him, press his forehead against the rock, and beg forgiveness? Prostrate himself, acknowledge his insignificance and his error, and plead for pardon. Even if the plea failed and a merciless hand beheaded him, he would at least escape the fear of watching the blade approach. Prostration was the same act as offering one's neck.

source.japanese: 自ら死を望む姿勢を取らせてしまうほどに人間という存在の根源に、本能に根差した古い古い恐怖であった。海は全生命の故郷ではあろうが、そこが優しい揺籃だとは限らない。海はまた、畏怖の対象なのでもあった。
source.english: An old, old fear, rooted in humanity's very foundations, in instinct. Strong enough to make a person assume a posture that invited death. The sea might be the home of all life, but that did not make it a gentle cradle. The sea was also an object of dread.

source.japanese: 朔屋は懼れの余り砕けそうな膝を必死に支えつつ、果たして泪はこの原初の恐怖に持ちこたえているのかと危ぶんで見遣ったが、恐怖の圧に面伏せ強いられる青年とは裏腹に、麗貌皓然と顎先を反らして、
source.english: Desperately bracing knees that seemed ready to shatter with fear, Sakuya looked toward Rui. Could she withstand this primordial terror? Where Sakuya was forced to bow beneath its pressure, Rui raised her chin, her beautiful features luminous.

target.text: 【Voice】 『───At long last─── ───You have returned─── ───Youngest Princess─── ───O daughter of Ours───』

It was more a tremor than a voice, and it was no mere loud noise echoing forth from that chasm of lava that formed his mouth; it travelled through the air, manifesting itself within the ears of all present, leaving a long, resonant trail of sound.

Despite its indefinite contour, the very existence of that towering titan of shadow was so inundating it oppressed all, and its voice, its tremors deepened and spread endlessly; merely being confronted with that besieged Sakuya's entire body from the tips of his limbs with an overwhelming fear, a dread as though every little particle of meat within him were about to burst. Sakuya had let himself be swept along by Tomosato's earlier banter, and he came to realize that he had taken the leader of these fish monsters far too lightly.

Why did he not join the fish monsters in rubbing his brow against the bare rock, begging for forgiveness? Were he to prostrate himself against the stone, ought he not to simply implore mercy and forgiveness for the mistake that was his own insignificant pettiness? Should the result be that his supplication was met with deaf ears, even if he were decapitated by a cruel hand, at the very least, he'd be spared the terror of seeing the impending blade as it drew closer to his neck. The act of prostration itself was no different than presenting your own neck to the other party.

It was an ancient, primeval fear found at the core of human existence, rooted in our instincts, one so profound that it could drive man to adopt a posture desiring of his own death. The sea may be the birthplace of all life, but that was no guarantee that she was a gentle cradle. For the ocean was also an object of awe and dread alike.

Sakuya desperately braced his knees against the overwhelming fear threatening to make them buckle any second, and he looked over at Rui, anxious if she could truly endure in the face of this primordial terror, but in stark contrast to this young man forced to keep his face down from the sheer pressure of the horror, her elegant visage faced it with radiant clarity in all its classical beauty, chin jutting upwards in defiance,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お父様───
　まさか、またお会いするとはね」
source.english:
“Father—I never
expected to see you again.”

source.japanese:
声にも、光閉ざす影塊を凝視する眼差しにも、一切の揺らぎなく、どころか挑むように背筋伸ばして、それはこの巨魁が娘と呼ぶ、眷属である故の強気なのか、それとも泪の、彼女自身が放蕩の歳月の間に自ら、それこそ貝母の裡[うち]の真珠のように育ててきたしなやかな倨傲の故か。
　朔屋は───後者であればいいと、竦み上がり、縮こまりそうになる背を泪に倣[なら]って起こしながら。
source.english:
Not a tremor in her voice or in the gaze fixed upon that lightless mass. Instead, she straightened her back as though challenging it. Was this confidence because she belonged to him, because the great being called her daughter? Or was it Rui's own supple pride, cultivated through her years of dissipation as a pearl grew within its shell?
Sakuya hoped it was the latter. Following her example, he straightened the back that threatened to cower and shrink.

source.japanese: 広大な岩の間に、平伏せる無数の魚怪達の中で立つ人間達はただの三人、けれどその少数の中に一応自分も含まれているのだと朔屋は、恐怖と戦う、友は、恐らくは悪の字がつく友はどうなのだ。先ほどは自分の恐れを幾分か払ってくれた男は、魚怪の王がもたらす重圧にも平然としていられるのだろうか。
source.english: In the vast rock hall, amid countless prostrate fish-monsters, only three human figures stood. Sakuya fought his fear with the thought that he counted among that small number, at least. What of his friend—his bad influence, more likely? Could the man who had eased his fear earlier remain unmoved beneath the weight the fish-monsters' king imposed?

target.text: 【Rui】 「Father─── To think that we would meet again.」

In her voice, as well as her gaze fixated on the mass of shadow shutting out all light, she betrayed not a single hint of wavering; on the contrary, she straightened her back in challenge; perhaps this was a confidence born from being what this leader of monsters called daughter, his kin, or perhaps it came from Rui herself, a graceful haughtiness fostered during her years of debauchery just like the pearl within the mother-shell. Sakuya───hoped it was the latter as he stood back up, imitating Rui's example by attempting to straighten out his cowering, curling back.

In the vast rock hall, amidst innumerable prostrating fish monsters, stood but three humans, but figuring that he was at least nominally included in that small number, Sakuya fought his fears, and his friend, though he was more of a trouble-making partner in crime, how was he doing? That man had brushed away Sakuya's own fear just earlier to some extent, so surely he would remain composed even in the face of the heavy pressure produced by the lord of the fish monsters?

source.japanese:
智里は───
　智里は智里で、朔屋の脇を小突いて。
source.english:
Tomosato—Tomosato
nudged Sakuya's side.

target.text: Tomosato was─── Tomosato was acting very much like himself, poking Sakuya in the side.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……炭団の塊みたいじゃねえ？　あれ？」
source.english: “…Doesn't that look like a heap of charcoal briquettes?”

source.japanese:
これであった。
　魚怪達の王を指して、泪が父と呼ぶ巨影を指して、この世界の海の伝説の主を指して、言いだした事がこれである。朔屋は慌てて殺し屋の口を塞ごうとしたのだが、するりと躱[かわ]されて、
source.english:
That was what he said.
Of the fish-monsters' king. Of the vast shadow Rui called Father. Of the lord of this world's sea legends. Sakuya hastily tried to cover the killer's mouth, but he slipped away.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……He's like a big old lump of charcoal briquettes, right? Huh?」

This was what he was doing. Pointing at the lord of the fish monsters, pointing at the colossal shadow Rui called father, pointing at the legendary lord of this world's seas, and this was what he was saying. Sakuya panicked and tried to physically shut the murderer's mouth, but his attempt was smoothly dodged,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「よせやい、男に唇べったり触られる趣味はねえやなあ」
source.english: “Stop that. I don't care for a man's hands plastered over my lips.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやその、あんたの莫迦……。
　軽口にも場と状況ってのがだな……。
　あの……馬鹿でかいのと向かい合って、
　よくもまああんたって奴は」
source.english:
“No, you idiot…
There's a time and place for jokes…
Facing that… enormous thing…
How can you…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「怖くはねえのかよう、ちょっとはさ」
source.english: “Aren't you frightened at all?”

source.japanese: 何故朔屋が恨み節になるのか、だが、それはこの面子の中で自分だけが恐れ、心折りひしがれる思いしているのが何やら悔しくさえ感じられてきたからである。
source.english: Why did Sakuya sound resentful? Because being the only one among them afraid, the only one with his heart crushed, had begun to feel somehow galling.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Stop that, I'm not into having my lips fondled by dudes.」
【Naomasa】 「No, that's not, you idiot……. Even your stupid jokes have a time and place where……. Uhmm……you have some serious balls, saying that right to this stupidly big thing's face.」
【Naomasa】 「Are you just not scared, not even a little?」

For some reason, Sakuya's complaints began to grow resentful, however, that was because, when he thought of how he was the only one amongst this group who was afraid, whose spirit was on the verge of being crushed, he came to feel bitterly frustrated with himself.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あー、人間てのは、おっかないおっかないで、たやすく気ぃ狂ったりもするが、同時に案外図太ぇもんでな。
　初めは発狂するくらいおっかなくても、そのうち慣れちまうもんだ」
source.english:
“Ah, people can go mad easily enough from fear. But they're surprisingly thick-skinned too.
Something may be frightening enough to drive you mad at first, yet eventually you get used to it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「う……む……言われてみりゃあそうかなあ。
　お化け屋敷だって何回か入ると、
　もうネタが割れて笑けてくるもんな」
source.english:
“Mm… Now you mention it, maybe.
Go into a haunted house a few times, and you know all its tricks.
Starts making you laugh.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Aaah, so you see, human beings, while they easily lose their minds because it's so scary, ooh so scary, at the same time, they're surprisingly bold. While you might think you're about to go insane from the fear at first, you get used to it soon enough.」
【Naomasa】 「Hmm……mmh……now that you mention it, I guess, yeah. Like how when you go into a haunted house enough times, you already know all the tricks and end up laughing instead.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「だろう？　だから、ここの親分は、前におン出てくるより、姿を影に引っこめておく事を選んでんだな。
　見えない方が大物っぽいから」
source.english:
“Right? That's why the boss here chooses to stay hidden in shadow instead of coming out front.
Looks more important when you can't see him.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Right? That's exactly why the big boss-man up there chooses to hide in the shadows instead of stepping out into the light. Because he looks bigger when you can't see him.」

source.japanese: 智里も幾分か声は潜[ひそ]めてはいるものの、それとて泪と魚怪の王に憚って、というより、この岩洞で下手に声張り上げれば、谺が騒ぎ回ってやかましいから、なのであった。どこまでもこの蒼い眸[ひとみ]の殺し屋は自分の調子崩さず、この手の奇人の磁場に逆らう術もたぬ朔屋などは簡単に影響されて、また同調してしまっている。
source.english: Tomosato did lower his voice a little, but less out of deference to Rui and the fish-monsters' king than because raising it carelessly in this rock cavern would set the echoes running noisily about. The blue-eyed killer never lost his own rhythm. Sakuya, with no way to resist the magnetic field of such an eccentric, was easily influenced. Once again, he fell into step.

source.japanese: 周囲の魚怪もいい加減腹に据えかねたのか、やや顔を上げ二人を睨[にら]めつけて、取り押さえようとの気勢に背をたわめたが、王がまた声を轟かせたによって、たちまち這いつくばる、潰れた蛙とよくよく似た姿に。
source.english: Perhaps the surrounding fish-monsters had finally had enough. They lifted their faces slightly, glared at the two, and arched their backs as though preparing to seize them. But the king's voice sounded again. Instantly they flattened themselves to the floor, remarkably like crushed frogs.

target.text: Tomosato was also keeping his voice somewhat hushed, but even so, that was less because he was hesitant to interrupt Rui or the lord of the fish monsters and more because, were he to thoughtlessly raise his voice in this rock cave, the resulting echo would be obnoxiously loud. Come hell or high water, this murderer with eyes of azure never lost his rhythm, and the likes of Sakuya, who possessed no means of resisting the magnetic field of this sort of eccentric, was easily swayed, adjusting to his wavelength once more.

The fish monsters surrounding them must finally have grown unable to stomach it anymore, for they raised their heads a little and glared at the two, their backs bending as if ready to jump up and seize them, but when the emperor once more let his voice resound through the hall, they immediately grovelled, their posture closely resembling that of a squashed frog.

source.japanese:
【父王】
『───これなる人間共と、
　───交わった故か。
　───お前の不遜は』
source.english:
“Is it because you
have mingled—with these humans—that you
are insolent?”

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 『───Does it stem from your consorting. ───With these humans who stand before Us? ───Your insolence.』

source.japanese:
【父王】
『───人間。お前を。
　───ただ遊ばせるために。
　───雇ったわけでは。
　───ないのだぞ』
source.english:
“Human.
I did not hire you—merely
to amuse
yourself.”

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 『───Human. Thy services. ───Were not engaged. ───Simply for thee. ───To fool around.』

source.japanese:
魚怪の長上の声は、今度は智里の耳の傍[そば]でだけ響いて、朔屋に、は、と目を瞠[みはら]らせた。智里は殺し屋だと言う、朔屋を狙う殺し屋なのだと言い張る、他からどう見られていようとも。なら殺し屋であるのなら、依頼人がある筈なのだ。
　ようやくその辺りの背後が朔屋にも透けてきてあった。
source.english:
This time the fish-monsters' lord's voice sounded only beside Tomosato's ear, making Sakuya open his eyes wide. Tomosato said he was a killer, insisted he was a killer targeting Sakuya, whatever others thought of him. A killer must have a client.
At last, Sakuya was beginning to glimpse what lay behind it all.

target.text: This time, the elder fish monster's words only echoed from next to Tomosato's ears, and Sakuya's eyes opened wide in shock. Tomosato claimed to be a murderer, and he insisted that he was a murderer after Sakuya's life, no matter how it may have looked to any other. In that case, if he was a contracted murderer, then surely there must also be a client. At long last, even Sakuya was finally seeing the forces at work behind it all.

source.japanese:
泪の再会と同時にやってきた殺し屋。
　その泪、差出人不明の手紙で、信天翁号に誘われた泪。海に戻ってきた泪。
　───手紙に書かれていた名前は、誰であったか？
source.english:
The killer who had arrived when he met Rui again.
Rui, invited to the Albatross by an unsigned letter. Rui, returned to the sea.
Whose name had been written in the letter?

source.japanese: つまり───魚怪達は、その長上は、泪を誘い出し、誑かした者を、朔屋だと睨[にら]んでいるのではないだろうか。それ故に智里を、殺し屋を───
source.english: In other words, did the fish-monsters and their lord suspect Sakuya of having enticed and deceived Rui? Was that why they had employed Tomosato, the killer—?

target.text: A murderer whose appearance just so happened to coincide with his reunion with Rui. And Rui, she who had been lured onto the Albatross through a letter penned by an unidentified hand. Rui, who had then returned to the ocean. ───Whose name was it again that had been written in that letter?

In other words───was it not possible that the fish monsters, and their leader, judged that Sakuya was the one who had tempted Rui to leave them, who had seduced and deceived her? And as a result, they had hired Tomosato, the murderer, to───

source.japanese:
【泪】
「不遜……などと言わないで下さいましね。
　わたくしの敬意は、
　一族にはもう向いておりませんの」
source.english:
“Please don't call it insolence.
My respect no
longer belongs to the family.”

source.japanese: 泪は、とっく一族とはとうに訣別しているのだと、魚怪達にも、海の底で器械と珠を操っていた妖にも、何度も何度も告げていて、それ故にまた同じ事を繰り返す煩雑と、髪の先を指でくるくると弄[もてあそ]びながら、
source.english: Rui had told the fish-monsters, and the creature operating machinery and a jewel beneath the sea, again and again that she had long since parted from her family. Irritated by having to repeat the same thing yet again, she twirled the ends of her hair about a finger.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Insolence……would you kindly refrain from calling it such? It is simply that my respect no longer belongs to my kin.」

Rui had already parted from her kin long ago, and she had made that clear time after time again, be it to the fish monsters or the spirit controlling pearls and machinery at the bottom of the sea, and as a result, finding it vexatious to once more be made to repeat the same thing, while curling the tips of her hair around her finger and fiddling with it,

source.japanese:
【泪】
「姉様達は皆縁づいて落ち着いたのに、わたくしだけがふらふらと、地上を彷彷徨っていることに焦慮して」
source.english: “All my sisters have married and settled, while I alone wander aimlessly over the land. That worries you.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「手元に呼び戻して適当な処[ところ]に縁づかせてしまおうという、そういう魂胆でしょうね」
source.english: “So you intend to call me back into your keeping and marry me off somewhere suitable.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「My elder sisters have all married and settled down, and yet I alone continue to wander the surface aimlessly, something that must bring you great worry.」
【Rui】 「Calling me back home to your side only to cavalierly marry me off to somewhere must be your ulterior motive then, I suppose.」

source.japanese:
【父王】
『娘を想わぬ親が、どこに在る───
　そして身に負うた定めに───
　まつろわぬ王がどこにある───』
source.english:
“Where is a parent who does not care
for his daughter—And where is a king
who does not submit—to the destiny he bears—”

source.japanese:
【父王】
『末姫よ───
　それに、お前とて───
　我が一族なる───
　その身に流れる血潮に───
　抗い続けるわけにはいかぬぞ───』
source.english:
“Youngest
princess—You,
too—belong to our family—You
cannot forever
resist—the blood flowing through you—”

source.japanese:
王の声。この世界の海の伝説の主の声。
　洞内に膨れあがる、影に包まれた巨身が膨張する、今やその火口の如き顎[あぎと]から直に撃ち放たれ、轟き、岩の宮殿、悠久の歳月の中に臓腑めいた質感を有するに至った謁見の間を蠕動させて、魚怪達はいよいよ畏まり、朔屋は遂に耳を塞ぎ、そして泪は。
source.english:
The king's voice. The voice of the lord of this world's sea legends.
The enormous body cloaked in shadow swelled within the cavern. Now the sound fired directly from its crater-like jaws, roaring, setting the rock palace's audience hall in peristaltic motion: a hall that had acquired the texture of organs through immeasurable ages. The fish-monsters cowered further. At last Sakuya covered his ears. And Rui—

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 『There is no father who worries not for his daughter─── Just as there is no emperor─── who can defy the burden of his destiny───』
【Father Emperor】 『O youngest princess─── You are one─── of Our kin withal─── You cannot continue to deny─── the blood flowing through your veins───』

The voice of the emperor. The voice of the lord of the legends of this world's seas. It expanded within the cave, the titanic body enveloped in shadow swelled in size, and it erupted directly from his flaming crater of a maw, thundering; the audience chamber in the palace of rock, which had taken on a visceral texture as strange aeons passed, pulsated peristaltically, the fish monsters retreated into even humbler awe, Sakuya blocked his ears at last, and then Rui.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「やだやだ。
　娘一人に、いつまでも構いつけて」
source.english:
“Oh, how tiresome.
Fussing over one daughter forever.”

source.japanese:
泪の腕を第二の肌のように覆う、長手袋の手を表に裏に返し、指の股からありもしない塵などにふうと息で吹き散らして、また被り直し、お行儀よく座っている事に飽いた猫が、前足の手入れや身繕いを始めたよう。と始めた猫なら後は寝るか歩き出すかで、ところが泪は眠るには熱い血潮と肌を欲する。事に一日の中で無聊やご不興高じた後などは特に。
　お陰で信天翁号の下級水夫君は時々泪に船室に引っぱりこまれ、出ないモノを出るまでいじくり回されたりしないでもない。
source.english:
Rui turned her gloved hands—the long gloves covering her arms like a second skin—palm up, palm down, puffed imaginary dust from between the fingers, then drew the gloves snug again: a cat, tired of sitting so primly, beginning to wash its forepaws and groom itself. Once a cat begins, it will next either sleep or walk away; Rui, however, requires warm blood and warm skin if she is to sleep, especially after boredom or ill humor has mounted over the course of a day.
And so the Albatross's junior sailor does sometimes find himself dragged into Rui's cabin and toyed with until she has coaxed out what refuses to come.

source.japanese:
ともかく、どれだけこの海底洞窟、いやさ宮殿が広大で雄壮であろうと、泪が望む者だけは蔵してはおるまい、なにしろ君臨するモノも伺候するモノも皆人外、冷たい血の。
　それが望めないここに、長居する理由はないと泪は、泪の身繕いは、はやばやと帰り支度なのであった。
source.english:
However vast and magnificent this undersea cavern—no, palace—might be, it could not contain the beings Rui desired. Its ruler and all his attendants were inhuman, cold-blooded.
Unable to obtain what she wanted here, she had no reason to remain. Rui's grooming was already preparation to leave.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Good grief. Still fussing over a single daughter for all eternity.」

Rui turned over her hand from front to back, clad in a long glove that covered her arm like a second skin, sent any non-existent dust between her fingers scattering in the air with a breath, then re-affixed the glove, like a cat that had begun to groom its front paws after growing bored of sitting politely. Were she a cat, however, then she'd either take a nap or start walking away, but when it came to Rui, she desired warm blood and skin to keep her company in bed. This was especially true after a long day filled with boredom and displeasure.

Owing to that, a young deck boy of the Albatross would occasionally be dragged inside Rui's cabin, and it was not unheard of for said boy to be fiddled and toyed with until he had let out even the things he didn't have.

Regardless, no matter how grand and soul-stirringly majestic an underwater cavern, or rather, a temple, it housed not those whom Rui desired, for you see, both they who reigned and they who waited upon were all inhuman, coldblooded. Given all that awaited her here was something she desired not, there was no reason to overstay her welcome, Rui thought, and so this grooming of hers was simply her making her preparations for returning home early.

source.japanese:
【父王】
『───どこまでも、聞かぬ子よな。
　───だが、お前は昔からそうであった。
　───一度言いだしたら。
　───後には、引かぬ』
source.english:
“Disobedient to the last—But you
have always been so—Once
you speak—you
never retreat—”

source.japanese:
【父王】
『───あの時も。
　───吾も、魔女めも。
　───説き伏せて。
　───なれどそれ故に、吾は。
　───お前を愛すのだ』
source.english:
“That time
too—you persuaded
both
me—and the witch—Yet
that is why—I love you—”

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 『───A stubborn child to the bitter end. ───And yet, you have ever been so. ───Should you proclaim something but once. ───You never retract it.』
【Father Emperor】 『───Back then, too. ───We, and that damnable witch. ───Utterly confuted by you. ───Howbeit, that is precisely why We. ───Love you so.』

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……出るぜ、懐柔策」
source.english: “…Here comes the soft approach.”
“…Huh?”

source.japanese: 魚怪達の王が僅かに覗かせた泪の昔に気を取られ、朔屋は智里が呟いた声を聞き流したのだが、王が何を目論んでいるのか、すぐさま目の当たりにする事となった。それは実に、泪の好みに───
source.english: Distracted by the glimpse of Rui's past the king had offered, Sakuya let Tomosato's mutter pass. But he would soon see what the king intended. Something truly suited to Rui's tastes—

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Here it comes, the grand plan to win her over.」
【Naomasa】 「……Huh?」

Distracted by the brief reveal of Rui's past that the Emperor of the fish monsters had let him glimpse, Sakuya let Tomosato's muttering voice in one ear and out the other, but whatever the emperor was scheming, he would get to witness it firsthand right away. It was, in fact, perfectly in accordance with Rui's preferences───

source.japanese:
【父王】
『吾はなにもお前を───
　今更、意に添わぬ男に───
　娶せようとは、思っておらぬよ───」
source.english:
“I have no wish—at this late
hour—to marry
you to a man—against your will—”

source.japanese:
【父王】
『───お前の後に、人間に。
　───嫁いだ子もあった。
　───ならばお前が今一度』
source.english:
“After you—another daughter
married—a human—Then
if you should once again—”

source.japanese:
【父王】
『───人の子に嫁[とつ]いでも。
　───吾は、許そう
　───そら』
source.english:
“Marry a human—I
shall permit
it—Look—”

source.japanese:
【父王】
『───お前の望みが、ここに───』
source.english: “What you desire—is here—”

source.japanese: 物分かりのよい父親を今更演じようとてか、声を幾分か柔らかにして、語る言葉も泪を許すようなと朔屋には聞こえたが、王というのは身内でさえもその地位の為に道具と為すのが習性で、泪の望みと謳[うた]っていながら、ルビには『吾が望み』と振られて、偽善臭も芬々と漂わせて、朔屋でさえ嗅ぎとった。
source.english: Was he trying, at this late hour, to play the understanding father? His voice had softened somewhat, and to Sakuya his words sounded almost like permission granted to Rui. But kings are creatures accustomed to making tools even of their own blood for the sake of the throne. He called it her desire, yet the gloss above it read my desire; the stench of hypocrisy rose so richly that even Sakuya caught it.

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 『We have no intent, no longer─── To marry you off to a man─── who suits not your wishes───」
【Father Emperor】 『───Following your example. ───There were other girls who married humans. ───This being the case, should you once more.』
【Father Emperor】 『───Marry a child of man. ───We shall permit it. ───Behold.』
【Father Emperor】 『───Your desire lies here with us───』

Was this a rather belated attempt at playing the understanding father, for his voice softened to some extent, and it sounded to Sakuya like the words he uttered were approving of Rui, but it was in the nature of a ruler to treat even their relatives as tools in service of their position, and while he declared it to be Rui's desire, "Our desire" might as well have been assigned as the ruby text above it, for it emanated a pungent stench of hypocrisy, so strong that even Sakuya sniffed it out.

source.japanese: だから泪などは父王の何か目論むなど、当然感じ取っていたはずなのに。肩やその背なに格別の構えはなかったけれど、それはいかなる事態にも即座対応しうる自然の位だったはずなのに。
source.english: Rui must naturally have sensed her father's designs. There had been no particular tension in her shoulders or back, but that should have been an effortless readiness to answer any eventuality at once.

target.text: Therefore, whatever her Father Emperor may have been scheming, Rui would naturally grasp it as well, and yet. While her shoulders or her back were not readied in any particular stance, she should still have been in a position of natural readiness, one allowing for an immediate response to any turn of events, and yet.

source.japanese:
───強張らせたのだ。
　魚怪の群をざっと左右に割れたのに。
　泪の優美な物腰、艶めかしい肢体の線は、鎧の曲面と同じで、なまじの悪意などは意にも介せず矛先を逸らし得るけれど、強張れば失う、防ぐ力が弱まる。
source.english:
Yet she stiffened.
When the fish-monsters' ranks swept apart to left and right.
Rui's graceful bearing, the sensual lines of her body, were like the curved surfaces of armor. Ordinary malice could slide from them without troubling her. Stiffen, however, and that protection was lost. Its strength diminished.

target.text: ───She had gone completely rigid. The swarm of fish monsters roughly split in two, shuffling to the left and right before her, and yet. Rui's graceful demeanor, the bewitching curves of her body, just like the curved surfaces of armour,let her deflect any desultory spearheads of malice without the slightest care, but once she stiffened, that was lost, her defence weakening.

source.japanese: 岩の広間の床に這いつくばっていた魚怪達が一斉に、ざっと左右に開いたは、月夜に陸に揚がって番[つが]うという小蟹達が、絨毯ほどにも分厚く群れてざわめくのと同じ、量による不気味さを持ち合わせていたが、泪が動揺したのはそれにではない。
source.english: All at once the fish-monsters prostrate on the rock floor opened to either side. Like little crabs said to come ashore and mate on moonlit nights, swarming and rustling in a carpet-thick mass: an eeriness of sheer numbers. But that was not what unsettled Rui.

target.text: The way the fish monsters, who had been grovelling against the floor of the hall of rock, suddenly parted to the left and right in unison, opening the path for her, was just like those small crabs that go ashore on moonlit nights to mate, rustling and stirring in great swarms as thick as a carpet, unsettling just by virtue of their sheer numbers alone, but that was not what shook Rui.

source.japanese:
青黒い魚怪達とただ中、岩床を歩む姿に。
　美々しく装った、その姿に。
　金髪白皙の、その容貌に。
source.english:
It was the figure walking over the rock amid the blue-black fish-monsters.
Splendidly dressed.
Fair-skinned, golden-haired.

target.text: It was the figure in the middle of the bluish black of the fish monsters, walking atop the floor of rock. That figure, dressed in ornate beauty. Those features, adorned with golden locks and fair skin.

source.japanese:
歩み寄ってくる姿は、手足すらり整って、姿勢の悪い朔屋と比したりすると、百日紅の若木とひねこびた灌木程も差があった。
　姿形良く、近寄ってくるにつれその容貌の秀でたる事も明らかに、金の髪も白皙の額も、全く申し分のない美男子、その見本。
　ありとあらゆる恋愛物語中で、時に颯爽と暴漢から救い、あるいは貧者に身をやつし、時には初め悪辣を装って（もちろん後から偽悪であった事が明らかになる）、真実の愛に焦がれる女性達の心を射止める、王子さまだ───
source.english:
He approached with elegantly proportioned limbs. Compared with Sakuya and his poor posture, he was a young crape myrtle beside a stunted shrub. His form was fine.
As he drew nearer, the excellence of his face became clear. Golden hair, fair brow: nothing to fault. A model of male beauty.
A prince, such as appeared in every manner of romance—sometimes gallantly rescuing the heroine from ruffians, sometimes disguising himself in poverty, sometimes seeming wicked at first, though naturally his apparent villainy was later revealed as a pose. Winning the hearts of heroines who longed for true love.

source.japanese: 一目見ただけで、連綿と続く青い血の、その精髄として生を受け、祝福と歓呼と光輝に満ちた半生を辿ってきた事が伝わってくるほどの、完全無欠の公子、物語を飛び出してこういうのが存在していたりするのだから、現実というのは恐ろしい。
source.english: At a glance, one knew he had been born as the distilled essence of a long line of blue blood, and had lived his life amid blessings, acclaim, and radiance. A flawless prince. That such a being could step out of a story and actually exist was one of reality's terrors.

source.japanese:
けれど泪の心掻[か]き乱したのは、公子に出くわした、乙女らしい驚きなどではない。
　魚怪達の王の、聳え立つ麓から天孫降臨と歩んでくる、その歩度が奇妙にぎこちなかった。どれだけ人形を精巧に作って内部に精妙巧緻な絡繰りを仕込もうと、それを欠いては人体の動きを模倣しようとしてもしきれない核心がある。重心だ。歩み寄ってくる姿は重心を欠いて、その動作、ぎくしゃくと、姿形が美々しいだけに、動きの不様が全てを台無しにしていた。
source.english:
But what disturbed Rui was no maiden's surprise at encountering a prince.
He came from the foot of the towering king as though he were heaven's grandson descending to earth, yet his steps were strangely awkward. However finely a doll was made, however exquisite the mechanism installed within it, something essential remained without which human movement could not be imitated. A center of gravity. The approaching figure lacked one. Its movements jerked. The more beautiful its form, the more that inept motion ruined everything.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お父様。その方は───！」
source.english: “Father. That man—!”

target.text: The limbs of the approaching figure were slender and well-proportioned, and compared to Sakuya with his poor posture, it was like the difference between a young crape myrtle and an old shrub. He cut a fine figure, and the nearer he came, the more evident his excellent facial features became in turn: with his golden locks and fair-skinned brow, he made an absolutely flawlessly handsome man, the very exemplar of one.

He was the sort you'd find in every conceivable tale of romance, who at times would gallantly rescue her from ruffians, or perhaps disguise himself in pauper's clothes, and who at yet other times would at first be feigning villainy (naturally, it would later become obvious that this was but a pretence of evil), he who would pierce the hearts of all the heroines yearning for true love: the prince───

Just from a single glance, one could tell that he was born as the crystallized essence of a continuous line of blue blood, one could feel how he had spent half a lifetime filled with blessings, jubilation, and radiant splendour, so utterly flawless a prince was he, a man who had leapt straight out of a story stood amongst them; truly, reality was terrifying.

However, what had disturbed Rui's heart so was no maidenly shock at the sudden appearance of her prince. From the foot of the towering mountain that was the emperor of the fish monsters, he walked towards them like Ninigi-no-Mikoto descending to earth, but his gait was oddly stiff. (TN: The term used is here is "天孫降臨", which describes the event where Ninigi-no-Mikoto, grandson of the sun goddess Amaterasu-Oomikami, descends to earth.)

No matter how elaborately one constructs a puppet, how many exquisite and delicate mechanisms one fits within it, there will always be a core lacking inside it, never allowing it to perfectly imitate human movements, however hard it tries. And that is balance. The approaching figure lacked the right center of gravity to balance itself around, and so its movements were awkward and stilted, and for all the beauty of its figure, those ungraceful movements spoiled it all.
【Rui】 「Father. That man is───!」

source.japanese:
【父王】
「おおさ───
　お前が愛して、結局その愛を───
　得られなんだ、人間よ───』
source.english:
“Yes—The human
you loved—and whose love—in the end
you could not gain—”

source.japanese:
───それは、泪の心。　
　
　
　───彼女が初めて捧げた、愛。
　
　
　
　───報われなかった、愛。
source.english:
It was Rui's heart.

The love she had offered for the first time.

The love that had not been returned.

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 「Verily─── He whom you loved, who, in the end─── won that love, that very human───』
───It was Rui's heart. ───Love, the first she ever gave. ───Love, ill-fated and unfulfilled.

source.japanese:
【父王】
『───お前はこれを。
　───殺めたと。
　───そう、思っていたようだが』
source.english:
“You seem
to have thought—you
killed him—”

source.japanese:
【父王】
「───あの短剣で殺めたとあれば。
　───その命、我らに捧げたも同じ事。
　───なればこそ、ほれ、このように』
source.english:
“But to kill
with that dagger—is the same as offering his life to us—Thus,
look—as you see—”

source.japanese: 王子は半ば傀儡のようになってしまっていた。死せるモノなのが、ありありとしていた。
source.english: The prince had become half a puppet. It was unmistakably clear that he was dead.

source.japanese:
【父王】
『比世に、留めおくこともできるのだ』
source.english: “We can keep him—in this world—”

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 『───You. ───Murdered this one. ───Indeed, it seems you believed so, howbeit.』
【Father Emperor】 「───A murder committed with that dagger. ───Is no different to sacrificing that life to Us. ───That is precisely why, behold, as you see before you.』
The prince had become something almost entirely like a puppet. He was dead, that much was clear to see.
【Father Emperor】 『We can keep him here, anchored to this world.』

source.japanese:
───人魚の王の六人の娘たちの内、末の姫は一五歳の、その誕生日。
　気まぐれに昇っていった海の上は嵐。
　人魚達には波の下に潜[もぐ]れば、暖かな暖炉の部屋の硝子越しに眺める五月雨のような雨と風だが、船で海往く人間には悪魔の爪と虎狼の牙となる。
source.english:
Of the mermaid king's six daughters, the youngest princess reached her fifteenth birthday.
On a whim, she rose to the surface. Above the sea was a storm.
To mermaids, once they dived beneath the waves, the rain and wind were like summer rain viewed through glass from a room with a warm hearth. To humans crossing the sea in ships, they became a devil's claws and the fangs of wolves and tigers.

source.japanese:
船の上には美しい人の、嵐に敢然と立ち向かい、その気高き容貌、破滅を前に怯まず仲間を庇[かば]う高邁な心立て───一目で高鳴る胸の、居ても立ってもいられぬときめき、焦り、切なさ、苦しさ。
　人魚の姫が、初めて知った心だった。
　初めて知った恋だった。
　───だから、失いたくなかった。
　───だから、難破する船から、海に住まうモノの禁を破って救い出した。
source.english:
A beautiful man stood aboard the ship, courageously facing the storm. His noble face, his lofty heart: shielding his companions without flinching before destruction. One look, and her heart raced. Restless excitement, impatience, longing, suffering.
A feeling the mermaid princess knew for the first time.
Love, known for the first time.
Therefore she did not want to lose him.
Therefore, breaking the prohibition laid upon beings of the sea, she saved him from the wreck.

source.japanese:
恋が姫を衝[つ]き動かす。海の魔女の家を訪れ、声と引き換えに、下半身の魚の尾を人間の足に変える飲み薬を譲り受ける。
「もし王子が他の娘と結婚するような事になれば、姫は海の泡となって消えてしまうよ」
　との、警句とともに。
　───何かを得る為には何かを喪わなければならない。全ての物語に通ずる大原則だ。
source.english:
Love drove the princess on. She went to the sea witch's house and, in exchange for her voice, obtained a potion that would turn the fishtail below her waist into human legs.
“If the prince should marry another girl, you will vanish into sea foam.”
So came the warning.
To gain one thing, another must be lost. The great law that governs every story.

source.japanese:
泪は、何時かこう語っていなかったか？
『……あの人と死に別れてしまったからこそ、だからわたくしは、今こうして貴方と口を聞いていられるのだけれど』───と。
source.english:
Had Rui not once said something
like this? '…It is precisely because death parted me from him that I can speak to you like this now.'

target.text: ───When the youngest of the emperor of the merfolk's six daughters turned fifteen, on that birthday of hers. When the youngest princess surfaced on a whim, a storm was raging atop the sea. To the merfolk, were they to simply dive beneath the waves, the rain and wind were no different than looking out at the rain of early summer through the window of a room warmed by the heat of a fireplace, but to the humans crossing the seas by ship, they quickly became the cruel claws of the devil and the ferocious fangs of wolves and tigers.

On that ship stood a beautiful man bravely facing the storm, and the proud look on his face, his noble disposition as he attempted to protect his comrades without faltering even in the face of imminent ruin───her heart throbbed so loudly from but a single glance; the pounding, the burning impatience, the suffocating misery, the agony, it wouldn't let her remain still. It was the first time the mermaid princess had ever felt anything like it. The first time she had ever been in love. ───And so, she did not want to lose that. ───And so, she violated the taboo of they who live in the seas and rescued him from the sinking ship.

Love spurred the princess on. She visited the den of the Sea Witch, and in exchange for her voice, was offered a potion that would change the fishy tail of her bottom half to human legs. Together with the warning that: "Should the prince come to marry another girl, you will dissolve into sea foam upon the waves and vanish." ───In order to gain something, you must lose something. A grand principle that applies to all stories.
Did Rui not, at some point, say something like this? 『……It is precisely because death took that man from me that I am here now, sitting like this, able to talk with you thus.』───

source.japanese:
魔女は更に続ける───
　これまで地を踏んだ事のない海のモノ、人間の足を得たとて、歩む度に短刀で抉られるような痛みを感じる事になろうよ……。
source.english:
The witch continued.
A creature of the sea who had never trodden land, even with human feet, would feel as though knives gouged her at every step…

source.japanese:
泪は、沙漠でこうも語っていなかったか？
『歩けないくらい、
　足の裏が柔らかい頃もあったっけ』
source.english:
Had Rui not also said this in the desert?
'There was a time when the soles
of my feet were too tender for walking.'

source.japanese:
その後人魚姫は。
　王子と一緒に御殿で暮らせるようにはなったけれど。声を失っては、王子を救った事実も語れない。だから、王子は人魚姫が命の恩人である事に気付かない。
　───筆談、を云々するのは物語の作法に反する。そう、これは、物語だ。
source.english:
Afterward,
the mermaid princess came to live in the palace with the prince. But having lost her voice, she could not tell him that she had saved him. So the prince never recognized his rescuer.
Bringing up written communication would violate the rules of the story. Yes, this was a story.

target.text: And the witch still continued─── You of the sea, who has hitherto never walked on land, when you obtain human legs, with your every step, you will feel the pain of walking on sharp knives…….
Had Rui not said something like so in the desert? 『There was a time when the soles of my feet were so soft, I couldn't even walk, if I'm not mistaken.』

Later, this is what happened to the mermaid princess. She managed to live together with the prince in his palace, however. She had lost her voice, and so she could not even tell the prince of the truth that she had saved him. Consequently, the prince never realized that he owed his life to the mermaid princess. ───Communicating about this in writing and so forth would violate the rules of storytelling. Yes, indeed, for this was a story.

source.japanese:
そのうち事実は捻じ曲がる。
　王子は偶然浜を通りかかった娘が命の恩人と勘違いしてしまう。
　後は話は水のように流れる。
　やがて王子と娘との結婚が決まる。悲嘆に暮れる人魚姫の前に現れた姫の姉たちが、髪と引き換えに海の魔女に貰った短剣を差し出し、王子の流した血で人魚の姿に戻れる事を教える───
source.english:
In time, the truth was twisted.
The prince mistook a girl who happened to pass along the shore for the one who had saved his life.
After that, the tale flowed like water.
Eventually the prince and the girl were to marry. The princess's sisters appeared before her in her grief. They offered a dagger obtained from the sea witch in exchange for their hair, telling her that the prince's spilled blood could restore her mermaid form.

source.japanese:
もちろん、当然、言うまでもなく。
　心優しい、人を殺める事など知らぬ可憐な姫だもの。
　愛する王子を殺すなど、なんでできよう。
　愛する王子を殺す事の出来ない人魚姫は死を選び、海に身を投げて泡に姿を変え、空気の精となって天国へ昇っていった───
source.english:
Of course. Naturally. Needless to say.
She was a tenderhearted, lovely princess who knew nothing of killing.
How could she kill the prince she loved?
Unable to kill him, the mermaid princess chose death, threw herself into the sea, became foam, then rose to heaven as a spirit of the air.

source.japanese:
……この結末に、絵本の頁に幼い拳を叩きこんだ嬢やに坊やは必ずいるはずだ。
　そんな哀しいお終いなんて厭[いや]だ、と。
　実際、この御伽話で、物語の結末は必ずしも幸せな形を迎えるとは限らない、哀しい結末というものがある事を教えられた子供達は多いだろう。
source.english:
Surely some little girl or boy had struck the picture-book page with a small fist at that ending.
No, not such a sad end.
Indeed, many children must have learned from this fairy tale that a story need not end happily. That there was such a thing as an unhappy ending.

source.japanese:
けれども。
　では、だからといって人魚姫が最後の最後で禁断の一線を踏み越えて、王子の心臓を刺し貫き、使い物にもならなかったその足を生き血に浸して本来の尾鰭を取り戻していたなら子供達はどう思ったろう。声を取り戻して人魚の姫が、その時何を叫んだのか、切ない慟哭だったのか、哀しい歓喜だったのか、華やかな絶望だったのか、子供達に告げてしまっていいものだろうか。
source.english:
But then—what if,
at the very last, the mermaid princess had crossed the forbidden line? Pierced the prince's heart, bathed those useless feet in his living blood, and recovered her own tail fin? What would the children have thought? What had she cried out when her voice returned? A heartbroken lament? Sorrowful rejoicing? Glittering despair? Was it something one ought to tell children?

target.text: Soon enough, truth was twisted into falsehood. The prince mistook a young woman he coincidentally happened to pass by on the beach as the one who saved his life. After that, the tale flowed as smoothly as water. In the end, it was decided that the prince and that young woman were to be married. Before the mermaid princess, overcome with sorrow, her elder sister-princesses appeared, presenting her with a dagger they had received from the Sea Witch in exchange for their own beautiful hair, imparting onto her how she would return to her mermaid form should the blood coursing through the prince reach her feet───

Of course, naturally, needless to say. This was a gentle, sweet little princess who knew nothing of deeds as wicked as the murder of another. How could she possibly kill her beloved prince? The mermaid princess, unable to kill her beloved prince, chose death; she threw herself into the ocean and dissolved into foam, becoming a spirit, a daughter of the air, and ascended into the Kingdom of Heaven───

……Upon hearing this ending, there must have been little girls and boys who slammed their tiny fists against the pages of their picture books. Refusing such a sad ending. In reality, there is no guarantee that the story reaches a happy ending in this fairy tale, and there are surely many children who have been told the unhappy ending.

However. Now then, while that may be the case, if the mermaid princess had crossed that most final of final forbidden lines, had pierced the prince's heart, steeped those useless legs of hers in his warm blood and regained her former tail and fins, what would the children have thought then? Having regained her voice, would the mermaid princess have screamed, and would it have been a scream of heart-rending wailing, melancholy delight, gorgeous despair? Would it truly even be something that was right to tell children of?

source.japanese: ───だから、これは、大人の為の御伽話。　愛を喪って、その後の長きにわたる生に倦んで、肉の快楽と遊戯の感興だけを信じ、追い求めるようになった人魚の姫の、生と性の遍歴の物語。愛欲と哀訴の、業と情の。
source.english: Thus, this is a fairy tale for adults: the tale of a mermaid princess who lost love, wearied of the long life that followed, and came to believe in and pursue nothing but the pleasures of the flesh and the exhilaration of play—her wanderings through life and sex; a tale of lust and lamentation, of karma and passion.

source.japanese: 今や朔屋の中では、漠然とした目鼻立ちしか持たなかった人魚姫が、くっきりと泪の輪郭を具[そな]えるに至っていた───ただどうしても一五の時の泪というのが想像できなくって、現在朔屋が知る彼女の貌[かお]で、人魚の姿。
source.english: In Sakuya's mind, the mermaid princess—until then little more than a blur—now wore Rui's clear contours. He could not imagine the Rui of that distant youth, however; instead he saw a mermaid with the face he knew today.

source.japanese: 上半身は……確か『海にあった時は着けない派』と言っていたから乳房は円[まろ]やかに零れていたし、そんなのが、思いを告げられぬ苦しみに呻吟しているのは、これはなかなか朔屋にとって───そそる姿で。
source.english: As for her upper body… if he remembered correctly, she had once said she was “the type who went without a top when she lived in the sea,” so her breasts spilled out in a rounded, supple curve—and seeing her groaning in agony at being unable to confess her feelings was, for Sakuya, quite an alluring sight.

target.text: ───Therefore, this is a fairy tale told by and for adults. Bereaved of love, losing interest in the long life still ahead of her, believing only in the excitement of games and carnal pleasure: the tale of a mermaid princess turned pursuer, of her travels through life and lust. Of desire and supplication, of karmic fate and passion.

Currently, within Sakuya, there was a mermaid princess who had only possessed hazy facial features before, but she was now endowed with the very distinct features of Rui───yet no matter how he tried, he could not imagine Rui at age fifteen, and so it became a mermaid body with the face of the woman as he knew her in the present.

Her upper half was……certainly, she had said she counted herself part of the "au naturel" faction when she lived in the seas, or something like that, so her breasts would have to be spilling out from her chest with a soft roundness, and when that woman groaned and moaned with the anguish of being unable to confess any of her emotions, to Sakuya, that made for a rather───stimulating sight.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「……たいがい良い趣味してんな、
　てめえもよ」
source.english:
“……You’ve got some pretty good taste yourself,
don’t you?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「……Real interesting tastes you've got there. And that goes for you too, buddy.」

source.japanese: 声をどうにか絞り出したいその煩悶に、喉に戦慄く指這わせ、乳房を揉みしだき、それでもなお唇に通う音のなく、ああその時滴らせた涙もきっと真珠になったろう、などと妄想力ばかりは人一倍の朔屋が、視界の中に幻視までしていた泪の苦境に、智里の貌[かお]がぬうと被さって、蒼い眸[ひとみ]にいかがわしげな影像はたちまち掻[か]き消され、青年は思わずぎゃあとのけぞった。
source.english: As she writhed to force out a voice, trembling fingers crawling over her throat and kneading her breasts while still no sound passed her lips—ah, surely the tears she shed then would have turned to pearls—Sakuya, whose powers of fantasy surpassed all men's, had conjured Rui's anguish before his very eyes. Then Tomosato's face loomed into the vision; beneath that blue stare, the salacious apparition vanished at once, and Sakuya shrieked and recoiled.

target.text: The agony within her, of her desire to wring out her voice no matter how, even if just a faint murmur, her throat trembling as his finger trailed across it, and when he would grope her chest so hard its shape deformed, there would still be not a single sound passing through her lips, aah, the tears dripping from her eyes in that moment would surely turn to pearls as well.

Such were the delusions of Sakuya, a man whose power of imagination was twice as grand as the average man's only in these situations, but the visual hallucination of Rui in distress within his sight suddenly overlapped with Tomosato's face, the azure eyes instantly erasing the indecent silhouette from his mind, and the young man reflexively let out a scream as he bent away.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「大方あの女が、乳放り出して、
『声が出せない、苦しい切ない』
　とか悶えてるあたり、
　思い浮かべてたんだろ」
source.english:
“You were probably picturing that woman
baring her breasts and writhing,
‘I can’t speak—it’s so painful
and heartbreaking,’ weren’t you?”

source.japanese:
───元はそれなりに歴史在る旧家の、次男坊だったと言う事を物語るような、小首をかしげて、優しくきょとんとした顔だった。智里の言葉に朔屋がまず浮かべてみせたのは。
　次に唇をちょっと開いて、目も少し瞠[みは]って、鼻梁や眉間のあたりに疑問符を漂わせて、こちらもまた育ちの良い者が穏やかに戸惑う顔だった。
　そして朔屋は、次の瞬間それまでの平和で上品な相を一気に崩してぶーと噴き出した。
source.english:
He tilted his head with a gentle, puzzled look—the expression of someone who had once been the second son of a long-established family. That was Sakuya’s first reaction to Tomosato’s words. Then he parted his lips a hair, widened his eyes a fraction, and let a question mark hang over the bridge of his nose and between his eyebrows—more polite bewilderment.
 Then, in the very next instant, Sakuya’s previously peaceful and refined expression crumbled completely, and he burst out laughing.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「You were imagining that woman, her tits on full display, writhing and moaning, thinking "I can't speak, it hurts, the misery", the whole thing clear as day in your head, yeah?」

───In a manner that attested to his origins as the second son of a family quite storied in its own right, he tilted his head slightly to one side, face covered in graceful puzzlement. That was the first thing that showed on Sakuya's face in reaction to Tomosato's words. Next, his lips faintly opened, his eyes slightly widened, a question mark floated in the air somewhere between the bridge of his nose and his brow, and this, too, was a gentle expression of bewilderment of a man of good upbringing. And then, the next moment, ruining his hitherto harmoniously refined look in a single breath, Sakuya erupted.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだってあんたはそう目聡いんだ」
source.english: “How come you’re always so perceptive?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「How the hell are your eyes that sharp?!」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「てめえの面が判りやしいだけだあ。
　で、いいのかよ、妄想じゃねえ、
　こっちの泪の方はよ？」
source.english:
“It’s just that your face is so easy to read.
So, you okay with what’s happening to Rui over there—the real one,
outside your fantasies?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Your mug is just easy to read, is all. So, you good with this, and I don't mean your delusions, but Rui here, yeah?」

source.japanese: 智里が親指で指せば、泪と父王の対峙は未だ続いており、両者の隔たりを繋ごうと死せる王子はのろのろと、それでもついには彼女の眼前に立って、両腕広げて見せた、姿勢は止めの間は美事ではあったがやはり動きがどうしても、しなやかな肉と筋に織り成される生の動きには程遠い。
source.english: Tomosato pointed with his thumb. Rui still faced her father. The dead prince moved slowly to bridge the distance between them, eventually standing before her and spreading both arms. At rest, the pose was beautiful. In motion, however, he remained far from the living movement woven of supple flesh and sinew.

source.japanese: そんな彼女達のやや後ろに立つ朔屋には、泪の貌[かお]は見えなかったけれど、後退る足下の危うさ、欹てた肩の硬さで、泪の戦[おのの]きは明らかで、なにも妄想する必要もなかったのである。
source.english: Standing a little behind them, Sakuya could not see Rui's face. But the unsteadiness of her retreating steps, the stiffness of her raised shoulders, made her trembling plain. There was no need to imagine anything.

target.text: As Tomosato jabbed his thumb in her direction, the confrontation of Rui and her Father Emperor was still ongoing; the perished prince, who seemed to be trying to connect the gap between the two, was moving sluggishly, and yet he finally stood before her very eyes, both arms held wide open,; while his form was beautiful to behold when still, in the end, his movements were hopelessly removed from the natural motions born from the interweaving of supple flesh and tendons.

Standing a little behind the woman and her former man, Sakuya could not see Rui's expression, but from the uncertainty in her retreating step, the tension in her raised shoulders, the shivering of Rui's body was plain to see, and so there was never a need for any of his wild fancies to begin with.

source.japanese:
【父王】
「───の。
　───こうやってお前が愛した男も。
　───そら、ここにあるぞう……』
source.english:
“You
see—The man you loved—is here
as well—Look…”

source.japanese:
【父王】
『───我が元に戻ってこよ。
　───よもや厭とは。
　───申すまいな」
source.english:
“Return to me—Surely
you
will not—refuse—”

source.japanese: 父王はかく泪を低く黒々と誘惑したし、朔屋にも泪の困惑手にとるように判ったが、それで敢えて駆け寄って、前に立ちし死王子を遮[さえぎ]ったり、泪の顔を覗きこんで力づけたりしなかったのは、結局泪がどういう答えを選ぶのか、それもまた掌を指すように判りきっていたのである。
source.english: Thus her father tempted Rui, low and dark. Her distress was plain as day to Sakuya. Yet he did not rush over to stand between her and the dead prince, or look into her face to encourage her. In the end, the answer she would choose was just as plain to him.

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 「───So? ───Thus, the man you once loved, too. ───Remains here with Us……』
【Father Emperor】 『───Return to Our side. ───Surely you will no longer claim. ───To be reluctant.」

With a base temptation as dark as shadow, the Father Emperor thus tempted Rui, and even Sakuya understood her bewilderment perfectly well, but that he still did not daringly run to her side to stand before her, obstructing the prince of death, peering into Rui's face and granting her the strength to face another day, was because, ultimately, Rui's answer was also as plain as a pikestaff to him.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あの『懐柔策』とやら。
　あんなの泪さんに、
　なんの効き目があるもんかい」
source.english:
“…That soft approach,
or whatever.
What effect could it possibly have on Rui?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「……This "grand plan to win her over" or whatever. There's no way that's going to have any effect on Rui whatsoever.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「だよなあ」
source.english: “Right?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「I know, right?」

source.japanese:
男二人が女の背中で、出来の悪い党派の拙[まず]い答弁に失笑堪[こら]えかね、互いに肘で小突き合う宰相と腹心のように、二人互いににやにやしながらつつき合う。
　脅しつけてくる人魚の王に、泪、やや動揺するも、最後には言い放った。
source.english:
Behind the woman's back, the two men grinned and nudged each other, like a chancellor and his trusted aide struggling not to laugh at some inept faction's fumbling reply.
Threatened by the mermaid king, Rui faltered a little, but at last declared—

target.text: Behind the woman, like a prime minister and his closest confidante poking each other in the side with their elbows, barely able to contain their sniggering at the ham-fisted answers of a flailing political party of incompetents, the two men prodded each other with a smirk on their faces. Faced with the intimidating emperor of the mermen, while somewhat discomposed, in the end, Rui declared thus:

source.japanese:
【泪】
「いりません、なんですか、そんな冷たい半分死人。お父様、わたくしはね、長くさすらっているうちに、愛だの、恋だの、そんなのはどうでもよくなってしまったんです」
source.english: “I don't want him. What is that cold, half-dead thing? Father, in my long wandering, love and romance have ceased to matter to me.”

source.japanese: きっぱり、と───
source.english: Firmly—

target.text: 【Rui】 「I have no need of whatever this is supposed to be, this cold cadaver already half in the grave. Father dearest, you see, during my longstanding wandering, love, romance, all things of that ilk have come to utterly lose any value in my eyes.」
Flatly───

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしが求めるのは、ただ温かい血潮、肉の快楽。そんな冷たい体なんて、誰が愛しますか」
source.english: “All I seek is warm blood, the pleasures of flesh. Who would love a cold body like that?”

source.japanese: 決然と───
source.english: Resolutely—

target.text: 【Rui】 「What I desire is simply warm blood, the carnal pleasures. Who could possibly love a cold body like the one that stands before me?」
Resolutely───

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そんな蝋人形みたいな体より、今はこの方をわたくし、愛しておりますの」
source.english: “Rather than that wax-doll body, it is this gentleman I love now.”

source.japanese: 潔い刃で斬り落とすように言い切って、そして、するりと身を寄せたが、朔屋の許へ。
source.english: She said it as though severing something with a clean blade. Then she slipped close—to Sakuya.
“Huh? Me!?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Right now, I love this gentleman far more than that wax effigy of a body.」
She finished her declaration like she were cutting him down with a pure blade's edge, and then, she smoothly drew closer, to Sakuya.
【Naomasa】 「Wait, ME!?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お慕い申しておりますわ。
　我が君、愛しの貴方」
source.english:
“I adore you.
My lord, my beloved.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「今さっき愛とか恋とかどうでもいいって言ったくせにーっ。
　泪さんあなた、適当なコト言ってその場逃れしようとしてないか？」
source.english:
“You just said love and romance don't matter!
Rui, aren't you saying whatever comes to mind to get out of this?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I yearn for you with all my being. My heart's sovereign, my beloved.」
【Naomasa】 「But you JUST finished saying how love and romance means nothing to you. Rui-san, are you sure you're not just making up some nonsense so you have an excuse to get out of here?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「女にこれ以上、
　好いたの惚れたのと言わせないで。
　貴方がおっしゃって。泣けと。狂えと」
source.english:
“Do not make a woman
speak of love and longing any further.
You must say it. Tell me to weep. Tell me to go mad.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Please, do not make a woman proclaim her affections or explain what lies in her heart any further. You must be the one to command me. Bid me cry. Go mad.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「さすれば、泣きましょう狂いましょう。
　嬉し涙に泣きましょう。
　恋の炎に狂いましょう。
　貴方───直正様」
source.english:
“Then I shall weep, I shall go mad.
I shall weep with tears of joy.
I shall go mad in love's flame.
For you—my lord Naomasa.”

source.japanese: 芝居のように囀[さえず]る泪の、なにかしら茶番のような、舞台劇のような。あるいはそうなのかも知れない。これは、海の底の物語、朔屋が何時しか迷いこんでしまっていた。
source.english: Rui trilled as though in a play. Something of a farce, a stage performance. Perhaps that was what it was. This was a story beneath the sea, into which Sakuya had wandered unnoticed.

target.text: 【Rui】 「And when you do, I shall weep and lose my mind. I shall weep tears of joy. I shall lose my mind in the flames of love. My dearest───Naomasa-sama.」

Rui sung and warbled like she were performing in a drama, like some manner of charade, a stage play. Or perhaps, that was what this really was. This was a tale set at the bottom of the sea, and Sakuya had managed to stray into it without ever noticing.

source.japanese:
【父王】
「───許さぬぞ、末姫。
　───我らの責務は。
　───この海に物語を撒き続ける事。
　───それあるのみ」
source.english:
“I shall not permit it,
youngest princess—Our duty—is to go
on scattering stories
through this sea—That, and nothing else—”

source.japanese: 泪の流麗な、歌うようなとは対照を成して、岩の広間をどよもす波動は魚怪達の王を核にして、それは怒りの表出か、王の巨大な陰の麓[ふもと]を炎に染めた───とそこに浮かび上がる奇妙な物体がある。
source.english: In contrast to Rui's flowing, almost sung words, a vibration filled the rock hall from the fish-monsters' king. Was it an expression of anger? It stained the foot of his vast shadow with flame. There a strange object became visible.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（なんだあれ……世界の……模型？）
source.english: (What's that… A model… of the world?)

source.japanese:
朔屋が珍しく本質を衝[つ]いたような言を吐いたのは、その物体がまさしくそうとしか見えないものであったから。
　宏大な岩の間の中で、そして巨大な王の足許に安置せられていたから、盆程度の大きさにしか見えなかったが、実際には一つの大きな部屋ほどもあったろう。
source.english:
Sakuya had spoken with unusual insight because the object could look like nothing else.
Within the vast rock hall, placed at the immense king's feet, it seemed only tray-sized. In fact it was probably as large as a spacious room.

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 「───We do not approve, youngest princess. ───Our duty. ───Is to scatter tales throughout these seas. ───That is all.」

In stark contrast to Rui's elegant, song-like speech, the roaring waves surging through the hall of rock were all centered around the Emperor of the fish monsters; perhaps it was an expression of wrath, for the gigantic base of the Emperor's shadow was dyed in hues of flame───and then, a strange object emerged.
【Naomasa】 （What is that……a model…… of the world?）

The reason Sakuya was able to express something that actually seemed to hit the nail on the head, something rather unusual for him, was because that truly was the only way to interpret that object. In the center of the vast hall of stone, its size only looked like that of a serving tray, but that was only because it had been installed directly by the feet of the titanic Emperor, for in reality, it was likely the size of a big room in its own right.

source.japanese:
それは、朔屋もよく知る、世界地図の半立体模型とよく似通っていた。
　円盤状の土台の面に、海と陸との地図を、陸の盛り上がりや海水面の起伏などを精細に写し取り、その上部には、ドーム状に細い鋼材を何条にも、天球儀とよく似た式に張り巡らせている。
source.english:
It closely resembled a relief model of the world map Sakuya knew well.
Upon a disk-shaped base, a map of sea and land reproduced elevations and the undulations of the sea's surface in fine detail. Above it, many thin steel strips formed a dome, in an arrangement much like a celestial globe.

source.japanese: ……もし朔屋に、智里のような闇を見透かす鋭い眼が在ったなら、その表面上の海の一角に、砂が敷き詰めてあり、更にその上にわざと襤褸に造った模型の船が転がしてあるのを見ただろう。その襤褸の模型が、信天翁号をそのまま縮小した輪郭を持ち合わせていた事も。
source.english: Had Sakuya possessed sharp eyes that penetrated darkness as Tomosato's did, he would have seen sand covering one part of the model's sea. Upon it lay a ship model deliberately made shabby. That shabby miniature had the exact outline of a reduced Albatross.

target.text: It bore a close resemblance to a raised-relief map of the whole world, the sort which even Sakuya knew well. Atop a disk-shaped foundation was a map of the oceans and the land, the bulges of the landmasses and the fluctuating highs and lows of the surface of the sea reproduced meticulously, and above it, several sections of thin steel forming a dome, stretching around in a manner closely resembling an armillary sphere.

……If Sakuya had been possessed of sharp eyes like Tomosato's that could see through the darkness, he would surely have noticed that atop that surface, a corner of the ocean had been blanketed in sand, and in addition, there was a model of a ship deliberately made to look ramshackle sitting atop it. As well as the fact that this ramshackle model held the exact contour of a scaled-down version of the Albatross.

source.japanese:
【智里】
（見た通りさあ。ありゃ『世界模型』てぇいうんだな）
source.english: (Just as it looks. That's called a world model.)

source.japanese: そして泪も、その『世界模型』に、隔てたこちらから送った視線には、憂愁と嘆きを揺曳させる、その想いの色合い、葡萄酒の海の底であの入道と対峙した時と同じ。
source.english: Rui's gaze toward that world model, from where she stood apart, trailed melancholy and lament. The shade of feeling was the same as when she had faced the monk beneath the sea of wine.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 （It's exactly what it looks like. That's a『model of the world』.）

And Rui's gaze, directed at that 『model of the world』from their far side of the hall, shimmered with a lingering melancholy and grief, the hues of those emotions the very same as when she had confronted that Nyuudou at the bottom of the sea of wine.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「まだそのような事を……。
　いい加減におかしいと、お気づき遊ばせ。
　伝説とは産まれ出ずるものであっても、
　造り出されるものではないでしょうに」
source.english:
“Still doing such things…
Please realize at last
how wrong it is. Legends are born.
Surely they are not manufactured.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「This again……. It is past time that you realize how strange this all is. Born from legend we may be, but surely we are not beings of creation.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「我らの在り様はそんなものではなかった筈。
　わたくし達は人に縛られるものであっても。
　そのようなものに縛られるなどと───
　情けなや」
source.english:
“We were not meant to be like this. We
may be bound by humans,
but to be bound by something like that—how
pitiful.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「That is not what our way of being ought to be. We may be fettered by humanity. But to allow ourselves to be chained down by such a thing─── is pathetic.」

source.japanese:
【父王】
「───やむなし。
　───おのが卑しき片手業、
　───今こそ振るえやよかし、殺し屋。
　───その男を、斬れ」
source.english:
“So be it—Now
ply your lowly trade,
killer—Cut
that man down—”

source.japanese: 泪が今、執着しているといえるのは朔屋だった。なればこそ、と王は智里に命じた言葉こそ智里が受けていた使命だった。
source.english: The one Rui could now be said to cling to was Sakuya. Thus the king's command to Tomosato was the very mission he had accepted.

target.text: 【Father Emperor】 「───It is inexorable. ───The time has come, murderer. ───For thee to exhibit thine ignoble skill. ───Cut that man down.」
