Rui was currently fixated on Sakuya. It was for that exact reason that the very words the Emperor just ordered Tomosato with were also the mission he had accepted.

source.japanese:
泪を連れ戻すこと、そのために朔屋を殺[あや]めること。智里はどこに隠し持っていたのか、日本刀を取り出して抜き放ち、朔屋につきつけた、その佇まい微塵も隙が無く、普段の飄々とした様子が嘘のよう。
　この智里の業前は以前にも見たことがあるが、それにも増して凄まじい殺気が刀身に展開されていた。
　それに智里、今まで朔屋とじゃれ合っていた事など知らぬげに、そして雇い主の命には逆らえぬとばかり、斬る気満々の様子であった───
source.english:
Bring Rui back. To that end, kill Sakuya. From wherever he had concealed it, Tomosato produced his Japanese sword, drew it, and leveled it at Sakuya. His stance held not the slightest opening. His usual airy manner seemed a lie.
Sakuya had seen his skill before, but now an even more terrible murderous intent unfolded along the blade.
As though he knew nothing of their earlier banter, as though unable to oppose his employer's command, Tomosato seemed entirely ready to cut him down.

target.text: To bring back Rui, and to kill Sakuya to accomplish this. Where exactly had Tomosato been hiding it? He pulled out his Japanese sword and unsheathed it, thrusting it at Sakuya, his stance betraying not the slightest of flaws, as though his usual easygoing detachment was but a lie. He had seen this Tomosato's abilities at work before, but a greater, more awesome thirst for blood than even then was emanating from the blade. Moreover, as if to say that Tomosato thought nothing of all the silly antics he'd gotten up to with Sakuya until now, that he was unable to defy an order from his employer, he seemed ready and raring to strike him down───

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あー、うん。
　という事で朔屋、まあこういうこった」
source.english:
“Ah, yes.
So, Sakuya. That's the situation.”

source.japanese: 刃を長く擬されて人が思うのは、こいつ、何故さっさと斬らないかという焦燥の念であり、朔屋もたまりかねて叫んだ。
source.english: When someone keeps a blade leveled at you, impatience sets in: why doesn't he just strike? Unable to bear it, Sakuya cried out.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やめてくれよ、友達だろう！」
source.english: “Stop it! We're friends, aren't we?”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「まあそうなんだが、友達だからって喧嘩しないという事もあんめえよ」
source.english: “Well, yes. But being friends doesn't mean we never fight.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「喧嘩とかって段階じゃないだろ、これ」
source.english: “This is a bit beyond a fight!”

source.japanese:
朔屋は窮地に追い込まれ───
　逃れる手段を───
source.english:
Sakuya had been driven into a corner—

A means of escape—

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Aah, yeah. So, uh, Sakuya, that's just how it is.」

What a man feels when a blade this long is pressed against him is the burning impatience of "why hasn't this guy just cut me down already", and Sakuya, also unable to put up with it any longer, shouted:
【Naomasa】 「STOP THAT, PLEASE, AREN'T WE FRIENDS!?」
【Tomosato】 「Well, sure we are, but just because we're friends, that doesn't mean we can't have a fight.」
【Naomasa】 「This is a few rungs up the ladder from fighting!」
Sakuya had been driven into a corner─── There was a way out of this, but did it───

source.japanese: <01>思いつく
source.english: Think of a way out

target.text: <01>Come to mind

source.japanese: <01>思いつかない
source.english: Can't think of a way out

target.text: <01>Not come to mind

source.japanese:
───などて。
　
　そうそう都合のよい機に都合のよろしい手段を思いつくようなら、恐らく朔屋はそもそもこんな海の下の、こんな常識外れの海底洞窟の、こんな絵空事のような状況に迷いこんではいないのである。
source.english:
Why, indeed?
If Sakuya could think of a convenient escape at such a convenient moment, he would probably never have strayed beneath the sea, into this undersea cave beyond all common sense, into this scene of pure fantasy.

source.japanese: いや、正確にはこの時朔屋が痛切に願うた事というのがあるにはあったのだが。なにしろ今日は一日もそもそ冴えない（とこれはいつもの事なのだが）働き振りを示し、その後多少は眠ったというか眠らされたけれど、沙漠や船の墓場をちんたらと歩いて慣れない鋼鉄殻の艦に乗り、こんな潮臭い海の底まで潜[もぐ]りこむ羽目になって、そして青臭い魚怪どもやその長上に取り囲まれたという、ちゃんぽん酒を呑むより悪酔いしそうな流れの果てに、突き出されたのが温[ぬる]い番茶や支那ソバならまだともかく、刃鋼の匂いも凍みるような刀の眸子とあっては締めにもならない、いやならなくてもいい締めになったら斬り殺される、と狼狽えるうちに、背筋がぬるぬるしてきた朔屋がまず思いついたというか願ったのは、
source.english: Strictly speaking, there was something he wished for desperately. He had spent the day doing dull, fumbling work—though that was usual—then slept a little, or been made to sleep. Afterward he had trudged through a desert and a graveyard of ships, boarded an unfamiliar steel-hulled vessel, descended to this briny seabed, and found himself surrounded by fish-stinking monsters and their lord. A sequence more likely to make one sick than mixing one's drinks. If lukewarm tea or a bowl of ramen had been offered at the end, that would have been one thing. A sword point whose very steel smelled cold was hardly a fitting finish. No, better not finish anything; if it finished him, he'd be cut dead. Amid that fluster, his back growing clammy, the first thing Sakuya thought of—or wished for—was—

source.japanese:
【直正】
（熱い風呂に入りてぇなあ、もう！）
source.english: (I want a hot bath. A really hot bath!)

source.japanese:
であり、この時風呂というイメエジから天啓のように湧き出でた単語があった！
　それすなわち、
source.english:
And from the image of a bath, a word sprang up as though in divine revelation!
Namely—

source.japanese: 『ヘウレーカ！』
source.english: Eureka!

source.japanese: であり、この場に於いては完全無欠に極めてリアルにシリアスに、役に立たなかった。困じ果てて朔屋は、ついうっかりにも程がある、眸子から視線を外してしまい流したのが運の尽き、先ほどからどうにも、芝居めかしてると詰[なじ]るべきなのか、柳腰至妙と詠嘆するべきなのか、撓垂れかかったままの泪にであり、朔屋は彼女の肌の火照りを聞いて、自分の胸に添うていた掌が梔子の花弁滑ると流れて、襟元へ留まるを見た。見て、見て、目が逸らせなくなった。
source.english: Which, here, was utterly, perfectly, realistically, seriously useless. At his wits' end, Sakuya committed an oversight beyond the limits of oversight: he took his eyes from the sword point. His gaze drifted to Rui, still leaning against him. Should he complain that she was acting, or marvel at the perfection of her supple waist? He heard the heat of her skin. The palm resting at his chest slid like a gardenia petal and came to rest at her collar. He saw it. Saw it. Could no longer look away.

target.text: ───As if. If he could come up with such a convenient means of escape suited so perfectly for the occasion, Sakuya would most likely never have stumbled into this outlandish underwater cave at the bottom of the sea, into this situation that seemed a product of formless wool-gathering, in the first place.

No, strictly speaking, there was something one could call a heartfelt desire within Sakuya in this moment. For you see, he'd already spent the entire day creeping about, dreary and depressed (not that this was anything out of the ordinary) while pretending to work, and after that, he'd gotten a bit of sleep, but then he had dilatorily walked through a desert and a cemetery of ships, climbed within an unfamiliar steel pod of a warship, then been forced to suffer through diving all the way down to the bottom of this salty sea, and after that, he'd been surrounded by these smelly, ichthyic monsters and their leader.

Finally, at the end of this course of events that left him even sicker than a night of mixing drinks, it'd be one thing if he was having a serving of lukewarm barley tea and Chinese soba thrust in his face, but given he was being stared down by the glinting tip of a blade that the smell of edged steel seemed to almost congeal around, it made for a poor finisher, no, he was finished, but if he gave up here, he'd be cut down, and while he was losing his head, realizing what a horrible situation he found himself in here, his spine clammy and cold, what he wished for was:
【Naomasa】 （Damn, I could really use a hot bath right now!）
So it was: in that very moment, a word formed from that image of a bath, gushing forth like a divine revelation! It was, in other words:
『EUREKA!』

So it was: utterly, completely, exceedingly useless in any real and serious sense in his present position. At his wits' end, realizing there had to be a limit to just how careless one could be, Sakuya let his gaze stray from the sword's point because he was at the end of his rope, for ought he to continue as he had just now, rebuking Tomosato like he was acting a part in some play, or ought he to instead exclaim his admiration for this waist as he marvelled at it, slender and lissome as a willow, extolling it as the pinnacle of grace, for Rui was still leaning against him.

Sakuya could hear the glowing heat of her skin; the palm of her hand that had been resting atop his chest slid across him, flowing like the petals of a gardenia, and he saw as it came to a stop by his collar. He saw, oh how he saw, he couldn't tear his eyes from it.

source.japanese: 凝脂の艶[つや]、薄い貝母重ねたような白、なぜ洋装の襟元高く締めて隠されているはずなのに青年の目を釘付けにする、のは泪が自ら緩めていたからの、なるほどそれで、その首筋のくぼみに光が溜まっていたりも一々よく見える───智里の差料も見ておいたほうが良かろうと思われるが、この時朔屋、泪の首筋に、その首筋に。
source.english: A rich gloss, white as layers of thin mother-of-pearl. Why did it arrest his eyes when the high collar of her dress should have concealed it? Because Rui had loosened the collar herself. Ah, naturally. Now he could see every detail, even the light gathered in the hollow of her neck. It might have been wise to keep an eye on Tomosato's sword too. But at that moment, Sakuya saw only Rui's neck. Her neck.

source.japanese:
だから朔屋は気づかない。殺し屋の据[す]えた眸子が妙な動きを見せていた。棒切れでくいくいと、何事かを指す軌道だ。
　そして朔屋は気づいていない。泪が巧妙に、智里と、二者に他には気取られぬ目配せで何事か示しあっていた事を。
source.english:
Thus he did not notice the killer's leveled sword point making a peculiar movement. Little nudges, as though indicating something with a stick.
Nor did he notice Rui and Tomosato exchanging deft signals with their eyes, unseen by anyone else.

target.text: Smooth and glossy like solidified oil, a white like layers of thin whorled fritillaria: how come his eyes were glued to her skin that should be hidden beneath the tall, closed neckline of her dress, why, that was because Rui herself had loosened it; indeed, in that case, he could certainly see how the light pooled in the hollow below her throat in every little detail─── it did seem like it would be smartest to be keeping an eye on the steel Tomosato carried on his hip, but in this moment, Sakuya was focused on Rui's neck, and oh, that neck.

Therefore, Sakuya did not notice. How the tip of the murderer's blade set against him betrayed a strange movement. How he nudged the twig ever so slightly, tracing a path pointing at something or other. And Sakuya still did not notice. How Rui and Tomosato deftly exchanged glances with none other than the two of them noticing, notifying of something or other.

source.japanese:
智里が指したの朔屋の、泪が添う腕へ。
　
　泪が返したのは、万事承知の目礼。
　
　朔屋が泪の麗しい首筋に目を奪われている間に───と、するりと。泪の体が朔屋の体から滑った。あまりに自然で滑らかな流れだったから、日頃は不調法な青年をして、自然に応じさせ、泪の体を支える形に。この時朔屋が、それまで一番目を奪われていた部分をつい支えてしまったのも当然だったろう。
　
　つまり、自分の腕で、体を斜交いにするように滑ってきた、泪の首筋だ。
source.english:
Tomosato indicated Sakuya's arm, against which Rui leaned.
Rui answered with a nod: understood.
While Sakuya's gaze was captured by her beautiful neck, her body slipped from his. So natural, so smooth was the movement that even ordinarily clumsy Sakuya responded instinctively, supporting her. Naturally enough, he supported the part that had most held his attention.
Her neck, as she slid diagonally across him into his arm.

target.text: What Tomosato pointed to was Sakuya's arm, the one Rui was clinging to. What Rui returned was an ocular nod of complete understanding. While Sakuya was captivated by Rui's beautiful neck───whoosh. Rui's body slipped away from Sakuya's, moving in a manner so natural and smooth that even this habitually clumsy young man responded automatically, ending up in a position where he was supporting Rui's body. It was, of course, only natural that, in this moment, Sakuya came to support the part of Rui that he had been the most captivated by hitherto.
In other words, it was the nape of Rui's neck, which had slid into his arms as if to leave her body oblique against his.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（まずいな、ちょっと熱っぽいし、この女[ひと]だって疲れるよな）
source.english: (This isn't good. She's a little feverish. Of course she gets tired too.)

source.japanese:
と、どこまで筋が悪いのかこの男、力なくもたれて来たはずの泪が、もう一度体を入れ替えた時には、青年の前身に背中を押しつける形になって、ばかりか、支えたと思った腕は、彼女の首筋にきちんと巻きついたと認識するまでに数瞬かかった。朔屋と、智里が擬[ぎ]する眸子の間に丁度泪が挟まる形になっていたと理解するには、もっとかかったけれど、それが何を意味するのかを完全に覚るには、次の殺し屋の声を俟[ま]たなければならなかった。
　智里はこう声を張ったのである。
source.english:
How hopelessly off course could this man be? Rui, who ought to have leaned against him weakly, shifted once more, putting her back against his front. Several moments passed before he realized that the arm he thought was supporting her had wrapped neatly around her neck. Longer still before he understood that she stood exactly between him and Tomosato's sword point. To grasp what that meant fully, he had to wait for the killer's next words.
Tomosato raised his voice.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 （This isn't good, she's a bit feverish. I guess even this woman gets tired.）

So he thought; truly, was there no end to how clueless and incompetent this man could be, and Rui, who was supposedly leaning against him, feeble and weak, once again shifted her body, this time into a stance where she was pushing her back against the young man's front, and that was not all; it took several moments before he realized that his arms, which he thought were supporting her weight, were now wrapped tightly around her neck.

It took even longer before Sakuya realized that they were now in a stance where Rui was perfectly positioned between Sakuya and the tip of Tomosato's sword, but it took even until the murderer next raised his voice for him to understand exactly what that signified. Tomosato raised his voice thus:

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あっ。野郎。ここの姫さん、人質にとりゃあがった！」
source.english: “Ah! The bastard's taken the princess hostage!”

source.japanese: そして朔屋はこう返したのである。
source.english: And Sakuya answered—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「えっ!?　誰が誰を人質にって！」
source.english: “What!? Who's taken whom hostage!?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Ah. You bastard. You took their princess hostage, how dare you!」
And then Sakuya replied thus:
【Naomasa】 「HUH!? Who are you saying took who hostage!?」

source.japanese: これに応じたのは魚怪どもである。
source.english: The fish-monsters responded.

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『……やはり……あやつ……』
source.english: “…As we thought… That man…”

source.japanese:
【魚怪】
『もとより……殿下を……！』
source.english: “From the beginning… Her Highness…!”

target.text: The fish monsters responded thus:
【Fish monster】 『……Knew it……that man……』
【Fish monster】 『From the very outset…… he meant to take……!』

source.japanese: 激甚に巨体を震撼させたは、魚怪達の王である。
source.english: The fish-monsters' king shook his great bulk violently.

source.japanese:
【父王】
「───どこまでも。
　───無能か。
　───お前など雇うて。
　───無駄だったわ」
source.english:
“Useless—to
the
last—Hiring
you—was a waste—”

target.text: The body of the emperor of the fish monsters shook violently.
【Father Emperor】 「───Incompetent. ───To the very end? ───Employing the likes of thee. ───Was effort wasted.」

source.japanese: 更に泪はこう付け加えたのである。
source.english: Rui added—

source.japanese:
【泪】
「いやあああっ、殺されるーっ。
　たすけてえええ。
　だめよ怒らせないでこの人を。
　少しでも手出ししようモノなら───」
source.english:
“Aaaah, he'll kill me!
Heeelp!
No, don't anger him.
If you so much as try to interfere—”

target.text: Furthermore, Rui added to the proceedings thus:
【Rui】 「Noooo, I will be killed. Save meeee. You cannot, do not anger this man. Should you interfere even in the slightest, then───」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくし、二目と見られない体に、されてしまうにちがいなくってよ。
　だからおねがい、助けて、でも手出しは、いけないわ」
source.english:
“He'll surely leave me a sight no one could bear to look at twice.
So please, help me—but you mustn't act.”

source.japanese:
それから泪が挙げた悲鳴は、明らかに作った声、それどころか楽しそうな声だった。
　それとも彼女の艶麗な背中に、濡れた落ち葉の如くべったり密着する羽目になっている朔屋にしか、その声の色合い感じ取れなかったのか？　まさか、とは思うた。
　大体にして朔屋が感じているのは、人質というならそれらしく体を強張らせていればいいものを、強張るどころか柔らかな、かといって弛[たる]みなど全く感じられぬ、青年の体の凹凸に合うて包みこんでくるかの、触れなば落ちん寸前まで円熟した泪の臀。
　……ああ、強張る、というかそのようになりつつあるモノならあった。
source.english:
Her ensuing scream was plainly fabricated. Indeed, it sounded delighted.
Or could only Sakuya hear that shade in her voice, plastered to her exquisite back like a wet fallen leaf? Surely not, he thought.
After all, what he felt was Rui's bottom. A hostage ought to stiffen her body. Yet she was soft, without a trace of slackness, almost wrapping herself to fit the contours of his own. Ripened to the brink of yielding at a touch.
Ah, something was stiffening, or becoming so.

source.japanese: 二人の背丈の差は泪の脚の長さと沓[くつ]の踵[かかと]がほどよく埋めて、朔屋の股ぐらと泪の臀の割れ目の高さがぴたり合う。密着してしかも、緩やかに、押しつけられて、鼠蹊部に心地好い柔味が応えて、逸物は臀の割れ目の奥へと挟みこまれるかたち、おまけに泪はこの状況を見てそれをやっているのか、軽いペッティングのように微妙に蠢かせていて、青年の逸物はたちまち甘勃ちとなり、意識が持って行かれる、気持ちよさ。
source.english: Rui’s long legs and the heels of her shoes made up the difference in their heights just so, bringing Sakuya’s crotch into perfect alignment with the cleft of her buttocks. They were pressed close—gently, gradually closer—and a delicious softness yielded against his groin, nestling his member deep between her cheeks. What was more, perhaps because she knew exactly what she was doing, Rui kept up the faintest motion, a delicate petting; in no time his member had risen sweetly half-hard, and the pleasure carried his wits away.

target.text: 【Rui】 「This body of mine will be rendered into a state that none will wish to look upon ever again, of that there is no doubt. So please, I beg of you, save me, but you cannot interfere.」

The scream that Rui let out was clearly made in an affected tone of voice, or rather, she even seemed to be enjoying herself. But even so, was Sakuya, stuck with Rui's strikingly beautiful back pressed tightly against him like wet fallen leaves sticking together, simply incapable of picking up the emotion tinging the timbre of her voice? Surely not, one should think.

The world was fun, full of wonder, becoming spellbound by it after beginning to realize just how magnificently vast it truly was; it was as though the childhood experienced by the boys and girls of all manner of living beings were returning to Rui───

逃げる最中に、小休止の為に入りこんだ、小さな一角で。岩肌の影に沈んで、入口は容易に見つかりそうになく、二人が暫[しばら]く息を整える暇くらいは作れそうだった。
　どうやらこの隠れ家のような岩間、泪がかつてこの海底洞にいた際の彼女の秘密の小部屋らしかった。
source.english:
While fleeing, they slipped into a little recess for a pause. Sunk in the rock's shadow, its entrance seemed unlikely to be found easily. It would give them time to catch their breath.
Apparently this hideout-like gap had been Rui's secret little room when she lived in the undersea cave.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ひどい汗ね、直さん。ほら……」
source.english: “You're terribly sweaty, Nao. Here…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ってなあ、泪さん。
　完全に巻きこんだな、俺を」
source.english:
“Listen, Rui.
You've dragged me into this completely.”

source.japanese: 泪は殊勝げに押し当ててきた手巾に汗を吸わせつつ、朔屋はどうにも微妙な面持ちの、事のあらましがいい加減見えてきた彼に、ぬけぬけと、浮かべた笑みがまあ素敵だった事。
source.english: As the handkerchief she pressed to him so dutifully absorbed his sweat, Sakuya wore an uncertain expression. He was finally beginning to see what had happened. The smile she offered him with utter shamelessness was nevertheless splendid.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そういうことになるかしら。
　でも女のすることに巻きこまれる、というのも、素敵な殿方の素養の一つよ」
source.english:
“Perhaps it amounts to that. But being caught up
in a woman's doings is one of an attractive gentleman's accomplishments.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……ねえ、直さん」
source.english: “…Nao.”

source.japanese: 朔屋の膝に手を置いて、胸元を指でなぞりながら、寄せる顔の静かな、先ほどまでの疾走の間中の汗の名残で僅かに艶[つや]帯びたが、深い風情に翳[かげ]りを帯びた。
source.english: Resting a hand on his knee and tracing his chest with a finger, she brought her face close. It still gleamed faintly with the sweat of their flight, but was quiet now, with a shadowed gravity to it.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくし、途中まではね、お別れを言おうって思っていたのよ」
source.english: “Until a certain point, I meant to say goodbye.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「どんなにその時は燃え上がっても、いずれ冷えてしまうのが、海と陸の定め。
　二人を退屈の水が冷やしてしまって」
source.english:
“However fiercely they burn at first, sea and land are fated to cool in time.
The waters of boredom cool them both.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え……本当は、そんなつもりで……？
　だって、俺、ようやくあなたと、なんというか、馴染み始めた感じなのに……」
source.english:
“Huh…
You really meant that…? But I've only just begun to feel… comfortable with you…”

source.japanese:
と朔屋が抱いた危惧は。
　この小さな岩屋の壁が迫り来るような、胸が締め付けられるように痛く、重苦しいものであったのに、同じ岩肌に響いてころころと転がったのは、別離を悼む女の思わしげと言うより、男をからかう事を覚え始めた娘の侠[きゃん]の声。
source.english:
The fear Sakuya felt was heavy and painful,
as though the little chamber's walls were closing upon him, tightening his chest. Yet the voice that rolled lightly against those same walls sounded less like a woman mourning a parting than a pert woman only just discovering how to tease a man.

target.text: In order to take a short breather during their escape, they went into a little nook. The entrance was covered in shadow by the rock surrounding them and would not so easily be found, and it seemed they would be able to find some time to regain their breath for a little while. Apparently, this small gap between the rocks reminiscent of a hideaway had been Rui's secret little room when the woman had lived in this underwater cave long ago.
【Rui】 「You're sweating terribly, Nao-san. Look……」
【Naomasa】 「Seriously, Rui-san. You've really gone and dragged me fully into this mess, haven't you?」

While Rui wiped off his sweat with the handkerchief she so laudably pressed against him, Sakuya had a very complicated expression on his face, and the shameless smile that bloomed across her face as she looked at the man who had finally realized the gist of what had happened was a wonderful sight to behold.
【Rui】 「I suppose that is what ended up happening here, yes. But being dragged into a woman's affairs and doings is a crucial part of the cultivation of a most lovely gentleman.」
【Rui】 「……Listen, Nao-san.」

Placing a hand on Sakuya's knee, tracing a finger across his chest, her face was calm as she drew closer to him, still slightly glossy with the remnants of sweat from their earlier sprinting, but it was also tinged with a grave shadow.
【Rui】 「On the way here, I was thinking that I should say my goodbyes to you.」

【Rui】 「No matter how brightly it may flare up in the moment, sooner or later, it will cool off: such is the fate of the sea and the land. Both of us will end up drenched in the icy waters of boredom.」
【Naomasa】 「Wha……are you…… really planning to do that……? But, it feels like I've only just, how do I put it, finally begun to get close to you, and……」

That was Sakuya's fear. It was suffocating, painful like his heart was being squeezed tight, like the walls of their little grotto were closing in around him, and yet, what tumbled around as it bounced from those rocks walls were not the musings of a woman lamenting a parting, but the pert laughter of a girl who had only just learned of how it felt to tease a man.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───とかなんとか、思いこんでいたのだけれど」
source.english: “Or something along those lines. That's what I'd convinced myself of.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「───Or something to that effect. That is what I had set my heart on, however.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……考えを改めました、今日。
　ありがとうね、直さん。
　こんなに愉[たの]しんだのなんて、
　もう思い出せないくらい遠くのこと」
source.english:
“…Today I changed my mind.
Thank you, Nao.
It's been so long since I enjoyed myself
this much that I can't remember.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ねえ泪さん……あなたさ、もしかして、その、なにか切なげな顔はさ、哀しいとかそういうことではなく、なにかをこらえていらっしゃる？」
source.english: “Rui… That rather heartbroken expression… Is it not sadness, but you holding something back?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わかったの。貴方。ただ二人だけでは、
　冷えてしまうのかも知れないけれど」
source.english:
“I understand now, dear.
Alone, the two of us might cool.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「炎は、風が熾します。直さん。
　わたくし、貴方を守って差し上げますね」
source.english:
“Wind stokes a flame.
Nao, I shall protect you.”

source.japanese:
見ようによっては、哀しげ、運命の無情と愛情という感情の性質を嘆く風情は確かに見えたが、最後の一言。
　一体、何から何を守る、と？
　朔屋の胸中に来したのは、傘も持たないのに、前方にわき起こる黒雲を見た時の不安に等しい。
source.english:
Looked at one way, she certainly appeared sad, lamenting fate's mercilessness and the nature of love.
But that last remark. Protect what from what?
Sakuya felt the unease of seeing black clouds gathering ahead when one had no umbrella.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「頼もしい言葉なのに、
　何やら、不穏な……」
source.english:
“Such reassuring words.
Yet somehow ominous…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「いつまでもわたくしを追いかけて、嫌い、鬱陶しいと思っていたけれど。
　あの者達を出し抜いた時の、心地好さ」
source.english:
“I hated their endless pursuit. Found it tiresome.
But the pleasure when we outwitted them…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……これねえ。
　直さんが私の傍にいて下さる限り、
　いつでも楽しめるのじゃなくって？」
source.english:
“…Couldn't I enjoy
that whenever I liked,
as long as you stay beside me?”

source.japanese:
つまり泪は。
　要するに、適度な危険があった方が燃えるじゃない、スリルという、吹く風が強くてあなたが吹き飛ばされそうでも、自分が一緒にいるから、と。
source.english:
In other words,
Rui meant: a little danger made things burn brighter. Even if the wind of that thrill blew hard enough to sweep him away, she would be with him.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょ……泪さん、それは、俺に───
　的になれと───？
　あいつらを引き寄せる為の？」
source.english:
“Wait… Rui,
are you telling me to be a target?
To draw them in?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしの傍に、
　いてくださりませんの？」
source.english:
“Won't you
stay beside me?”

source.japanese: 朔屋の膝に、胸元に、泪の爪の先が軽く、弱く、時に少しだけ強く食いこむのは、ねだるというのもあったし、朔屋を今更逃しはしないと、自分の刻印を刻んでいるようでもあったし、青年の頬に浮かんだ笑いも、女の深情けにはにかむ色と同時に、落ちるべき処に落ちてしまってもう抜けられない、そんな自分を見いだした、乾いた笑いの。
source.english: The tips of Rui's nails pressed into Sakuya's knee, into his chest: lightly, faintly, now and then a little harder. There was pleading in it, and also something of carving her seal into him—a declaration that she had no intention of letting him escape now. The smile that rose to Sakuya's face held both the bashfulness of a man receiving a woman's ardent devotion and the dry laughter of one who found himself fallen precisely where he had been bound to fall, with no getting out again.

source.japanese: 二つの意味を互いに秘めて、寄り添う男と女は、まあそれなりに───愉しそうで、幸せそうで。
source.english: Each concealing two meanings, the man and woman nestled together looked, well, reasonably happy. Reasonably pleased.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そんなに切なげな顔で迫られたって、
　迫られたって……。
　もっと、見せてくれます？」
source.english:
“Even if you press me with such a sorrowful face…
Even if you
do… Could you show me more of it?”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お側において下さるのなら、
　わたくしは、直さんの為にどんな顔でも。
　どんなことでも」
source.english:
“If you'll keep me beside you,
any face for you, Nao.
Anything at all.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「……I changed my mind. Today. Thank you very much, Nao-san. Last I had this much fun was so long ago, I can no longer even remember it.」
【Naomasa】 「Hey, Rui-san……are you, could it be, you know, that sort of pained, wistful look on your face, are you saying that's not because you're sad, but because you're holding something in?」
【Rui】 「I am all too aware. Dear. With just the two of us, perhaps the flames of passion will cool and fade.」
【Rui】 「But flames are kindled by the wind. Nao-san. I promise that I shall protect you.」

Depending on the way one looked at it, it certainly did seem sad, like she was lamenting the cruelty of fate and the nature of love, but that final sentence. Protect who from what, exactly? What formed within Sakuya's chest was just like that apprehension one would feel upon seeing black clouds emerge from the distant horizon when one did not have an umbrella at hand.
【Naomasa】 「Those are reassuring words, and yet, I still kind of feel very disturbed……」
【Rui】 「Being forever chased is something I despised, an annoyance ever hanging over me, but. Oh, that pleasant sensation of getting the better of them.」
【Rui】 「……And now, well. For as long as you are by my side, Nao-san, will I not always be able to enjoy myself like this?」

That is to say, Rui. In essence, she was saying that just the right amount of danger lit a fire in her, that certain thrill of it all, and even when the wind would blow so fiercely it might sweep her off her feet, it was enjoyable because he was there with her.
【Naomasa】 「Wai-……Rui-san, you're saying I'm─── going to be a target───? To lure those guys in?」
【Rui】 「Will you not stay by my side?」

When the tip of Rui's nails dug lightly, softly, and at times ever so slightly forcefully into Sakuya's knee, and his chest, it was a form of pleading, but also a way to carve her own mark into him, to proclaim that she wasn't going to allow Sakuya to get away from her any longer, and the smile that surfaced on the young man's cheeks was at once tinged with a bashfulness from being met with a woman's deep affection, as well as a smirk of dry laughter, bitterly resigned after seeing himself fall into the pit of ruin he deserved, no longer able to get out.
There they were, a man and a woman both hiding the unspoken implications, nestling together, and, well─── they seemed to be enjoying themselves. Seemed happy, in their own way.
【Naomasa】 「When you compel me with such a sad look on your face, urge me on…… Will you show me more of that?」
【Rui】 「If you will stay by my side, I will make any expression for you, Nao-san. I will do anything.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でも勘違いなさっちゃいやよ。
　貴方、だからなの。
　貴方以外の殿方と逃避行なんて」
source.english:
“But don't misunderstand.
It is because it's you.
Fleeing with some other gentleman…”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でも、もし、直さんがわたくしから逃げてしまわれたなら───これほど哀しいことは、在りません」
source.english: “But if you were to run away from me—nothing could be sadder.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「哀しくて、哀しくて、きっとどこまでも追いかけてしまうことでしょう。わたくしをここまでその気にさせたのだもの」
source.english: “So sad, so sad, I'd surely pursue you everywhere. You've got me this eager, after all.”

source.japanese:
どこやら郭の誠めかした言葉を、そのような口ぶりでわざと言う。
　けれど朔屋は、それが泪の深情けだと信じた。長の歳月彷徨った、人魚の姫の誠の心、那辺にあろうとも。それでもこの綺麗な女にここまで言われるのは、心地いい。
　安い偽り？　騙される幸せ？
　ああ、そういうのもどうでもいいのだ。
　寄り添う泪は間違いなく美しく、きっと何時までも変わらずに美しく、そしてこの美しい女を───
source.english:
Words somewhat like a courtesan's vows, spoken deliberately in just that manner.
Yet Sakuya believed them to be Rui's deep affection. Wherever the true heart of a mermaid princess who had wandered for so many years might lie, it felt good to have this beautiful woman speak to him so.
A cheap lie?
The happiness of being deceived?
Ah, none of that mattered either. Rui beside him was unquestionably beautiful, surely beautiful forever. And this beautiful woman—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そうときたか。はっはっはっ。もう駄目だ俺。だってさあ、だってさあ、泪さん、あんたそんなでも、綺麗なんだもの、抱きたいって思わせるんだもの」
source.english: “So that's how it is. Hahaha. I'm finished. Because, because, Rui—even like that, you're beautiful. You make me want to take you in my arms.”

source.japanese:
この美しい女を抱く事は、抱かれる事は、なによりも素晴らしい、底無しの麻薬のような体だ、溺れて飽きる事はないが、これ以外はなにも満足できなくなってしまうほどの。
　女の手練手管？　男の悲哀？
　ああ、そういうのもどうでもいいのだ。
　なにしろ、泪は始めから言っていたではないか。
source.english:
To embrace this beautiful woman, to be embraced by her, was more wonderful than anything. A body like a bottomless narcotic. One could drown in it and never tire, until nothing else could satisfy.
A woman's wiles?
A man's sorrow? Ah, none of that mattered either.
Had Rui not said it from the beginning?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───優しく、してね。これから先」
source.english: “Be gentle with me. From now on.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「But do not misunderstand me here. It is because it is with you. I would never dream of eloping with any other gentleman in this world.」
【Rui】 「But if, and only if, you should attempt to run away from me, Nao-san───there could be no greater heartbreak.」
【Rui】 「The sorrow, the grief, I am certain I would end up chasing you down to the end of the world. For you are the man who made me feel something this intense.」

She spoke with the feigned sincerity, the poisoned honey of a courtesan of the red-light districts, adopting that tone quite intentionally as she did so. However, Sakuya believed this to merely be Rui's excessive love for him. Regardless of where the sincere heart of the mermaid princess who had drifted through the ages below countless moons truly resided, if it still was anywhere to be found. Nevertheless, it felt good when this beautiful woman was willing to go so far with her words.

A cheap falsehood? Or the happiness found in deception? Ah, none of that mattered. Rui, leaning against him, was undeniably beautiful; she would surely retain that beauty no matter how much time passed, and finally, he took this beautiful woman and───

【Naomasa】 「So that's how it is? Ha-ha-ha. It's over, I'm a lost cause. Because, I mean, it's just, Rui-san, you may be like that, but you're still so beautiful, and that just makes me want to hold you tight.」

To embrace this beautiful woman, to be embraced by her, was wonderful beyond compare, for not only was her body like a bottomless narcotic, one he could drown in forever and never have his fill of, it was to the point that he could never be satisfied by any other ever again. The wiles of a woman? The sorrows of a man? Ah, none of that mattered. For you see, had Rui not been saying it from the very beginning?
【Naomasa】 「───Be gentle with me, okay? From now on and always.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ええ、もちろん。
　直さんが望むように。優しく、じわじわと。
　お互いの首を、真綿で絞めるように。
　愉しみましょうねえ……」
source.english:
“Yes, of course.
As you wish, Nao. Gently, little by little.
As though strangling each other with soft silk.
Let us enjoy ourselves…”

source.japanese: そう、泪が言っていたとおりに、愉しむだけでいい。肉の快楽の素晴らしさ、堪能し、そして自分達を追い来たる危難が、味の彩りとなって快楽をより高めてくれよう。
source.english: Yes, as Rui had said, they need only enjoy themselves. Savor the marvel of fleshly pleasure. The dangers pursuing them would lend color to its flavor and heighten it further.

source.japanese:
───この時、朔屋が、泪のいう、肉の快楽、ただ一つの確かなもの、彼自身がその一つになったのだろう。泪の快楽として。
　そして泪もまた、朔屋の為の唯一最高の快楽として、人魚の肉を差し出して。朔屋はあるいはもしかしたらこの先、どれだけの生を生きる事になるのか、それはわからない、この時は、まだ。
source.english:
At this moment, perhaps Sakuya himself became one of those pleasures of flesh Rui called the only certain things. A pleasure for Rui.
And Rui, too, offered her mermaid flesh as his single greatest pleasure. And Sakuya—how long might he live from this point on? There was no knowing. Not yet, at that moment.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Yes, but of course. Just the way you desire it. Gently, little by little. Like we are strangling each other with threads of silk floss. Let us enjoy ourselves, shall we……」

Indeed, just as Rui had said, as long as they enjoyed it, that was all that mattered. They would have their fill of the wonders of the pleasures of flesh, and may the danger always nipping at their heels become a spice driving that pleasure to ever greater heights.

───In this moment, Sakuya had become what Rui had spoken of: the pleasure of the flesh, the one and only certainty in life. As Rui's pleasure. And Rui, too, offered up her mermaid flesh, as a unique and greatest of pleasures, all for Sakuya's sake. In this moment, it was still unclear to Sakuya just how many lives he would maybe, perhaps, go on to live.

source.japanese: 何か自分がとんでもない間違いをやらかしたような気がしてならない朔屋だが、岩屋を出でて逃げるうちに潜水艦を留めてあったところまで辿り着く。
source.english: Unable to shake the feeling that he had made some tremendous mistake, Sakuya left the rock chamber. In their flight, they reached the place where the submarine had stopped.

target.text: Sakuya couldn't help but feel like he'd just made one of the greatest mistakes of his entire life, but they left the grotto, and as they ran away, they arrived at the place where the submarine was kept.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「よう、二人とも、逃げおおせたようだの」
source.english: “Hey, you two. Looks like you got away.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うーん、どうなんだろうなぁ……。
　だってあれ」
source.english:
“Mm. I wonder… Because,
look…”

source.japanese:
智里とも合流を果たしたのだけれど、海底洞窟の奥からは、洞窟自体が震動しているのではないかと言うくらいの魚怪たちの雄叫びと、らんらんと光る魚眼がそれこそ津波のように迫り来たる。
　この潜水艦まで逃げ延びてきたけれど、朔屋も泪もこんな巨大な鋼の塊、どう動かすのか見当も付かない。
source.english:
They had rejoined Tomosato, but cries from the cave's depths were so tremendous that the cave itself seemed to shake. Gleaming fish eyes approached like a great wave.
They had escaped as far as this submarine, yet neither Sakuya nor Rui had any idea how to move such a great lump of steel.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「まあいいから。ぐずってねえでハッチ開けて入っていろよ」
source.english: “Never mind. Stop dawdling, open the hatch, and get in.”

source.japanese: 重い鋼の蓋の中に二人を押し込め、締め直す前に智里は内部の暗がりに声を張り上げた。
source.english: He pushed them beneath the heavy steel lid. Before closing it again, he called into the interior darkness.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Hey there, looks like you two also managed to make your escape.」
【Naomasa】 「Yeah, I don't know about that……. I mean, look over there.」

They had managed to reunite with Tomosato as well, but from the depths of the underwater cave came the roaring war cries of the fish monsters, so intense it could make one wonder if the very cave itself was not trembling, and their glinting fish eyes surged towards them as though a tsunami. They had successfully escaped all the way to this submarine, however, neither Sakuya nor Rui had the first idea of how to make that massive lump of steel move.
【Tomosato】 「Meh, doesn't really matter. Stop your whining, get that hatch open, then jump inside.
He stuffed the two of them down past the heavy steel lid, and before refastening it, Tomosato yelled down into the darkness within.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「やい。いるんだろう！？　どこに潜[もぐ]り込んでいるやら知らねえが、お前、いるな？」
source.english: “Hey! You're there, aren't you? Don't know where you've crawled off to, but you're in there, right?”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「だったらこの船、どうにか動かして信天翁まで持って行け」
source.english: “Then get this ship moving somehow and take it to the Albatross.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Oi, you. You're in there, right!? I don't really care to know exactly what kind of hole you've slunk into, but you're in there, yeah?」
【Tomosato】 「Then get this vessel running somehow, and bring it back to the Albatross.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「つべこべ言わねえでやれよ、そんくらいできるんだろ、本当は？」
source.english: “No arguing. Do it. You can manage that much, can't you? Really?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Stop your whining, you can do that much. What's the real reason?」

source.japanese:
この期に及んで意味不明の物言いだが、もう朔屋たちにその意味を問いただしている暇はない、ハッチを閉じる、ギリギリと締める。
　朔屋が最後に見たモノは、押し寄せる魚怪の大群に、弧剣一振りで対峙する智里の姿。
source.english:
Incomprehensible words even now, but Sakuya and Rui had no time to ask what they meant. The hatch closed, tightened down.
What Sakuya saw last was Tomosato facing the approaching mass of fish-monsters with a single sword.

target.text: Even here, at the very end, his manner of speaking was nonsensical, but neither Sakuya nor Rui had the luxury to ask him what he actually meant, and so they closed the hatch, fastening it as tight as possible. The very last thing Sakuya saw was Tomosato confronting the great horde of fish monsters, giving an arced swing of his blade as they descended upon him.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「いやあ……最低だと言ってくれる女は多いんだが、殺し屋を友達と呼ぶ阿呆は滅多にいなくってさあ」
source.english: “Well… Plenty of women call me the worst. But not many fools call a killer their friend.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「But really, now……plenty of women that have called me the lowest cur they've ever met, but there are very few idiots out there who will call a murderer friend.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あとお前、こう後顧の憂いなく大量殺戮の機会なんてそうそうねえぜえ。
　まあそういうこった。
　その人魚姫と達者でな。
　───あばえ！」
source.english:
“Besides, you don't often get a chance for wholesale slaughter without having to watch your back.
So that's that. Stay well
with your mermaid princess.
Be seeing you!”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Not to mention, you don't get a lot of chances to slaughter this many people without a care for the future woes it might bring. Well, that's just how it goes. Stay safe out there with your mermaid princess. ───See ya!」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「ああ後こいつを持ってけ、忘れんな」
source.english: “Oh, take this too. Don't forget it.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Oh yeah, and take this with you; don't forget it!」

source.japanese: ハッチが閉まる寸前に、隙間から投げ込んできた短剣こそが、泪が王子を刺し貫いたものであったのだが、何故智里がそんなモノを持ち出してきたのか、朔屋に渡したのか、それはまだ判らない、今はまだ。
source.english: Just before the hatch closed, he threw a dagger through the gap. It was the one with which Rui had pierced the prince. Why Tomosato had brought such a thing away, why he gave it to Sakuya, remained unknown. Not yet.

target.text: Just before the hatch closed, a dagger was tossed through the gap, the very same one that Rui had pierced the prince with, but why exactly had Tomosato brought that with him, and why had he given it to Sakuya? That much he still didn't understand. Not yet.

source.japanese:
……智里はああ叫んだけれど、二人は艦内のどこにも密航者の姿を見つけられず、それにやはりこんな鋼の船の動かしたかたなど判るはずもなく。
　朔屋は、別れる寸前の魚怪たちの圧倒的な数と、智里の姿を想い、やはり耐えきれず、自分などなんの助けにもならないと知りつつも、もう一度ハッチから彼に、一体何を言おうしたのだろう。一体何をしてやろうとしたのだろう。
source.english:
Tomosato had shouted all that, but the two could find the stowaway nowhere aboard. Nor, naturally, did they know how to operate such a steel vessel.
Thinking of the overwhelming number of fish-monsters at their parting, and Tomosato facing them, Sakuya could not bear it. Knowing he could offer no help, he nevertheless made for the hatch again. What had he intended to say? What had he hoped to do for him?

source.japanese:
なんにせよその機会は失われた。
　潜水艦が突如また息を吹き返したのである。一体どのような原理で作動しているのか相変わらず判らないが、動いてしまえば泪と朔屋にはもうできる事はない。
　二人で暗がりの中にしゃがみこみ、浮上するまで───言うまでもない。存分に愉[たの]しみ合った。危地を逃れた安堵が、朔屋を異様に昂奮させていたし、泪もまた長きの伴侶得たといたく喜んでいたから。
　───暗がりのどこかから、聞き覚えのある舌打ちが聞こえたような気がしたけれど、二人は気にせず、いや、その気があったら混ざるといいと手招きしたけれど反応がなかったので、そのまま二人で交合[まぐわ]り続けたのだった。
source.english:
In any case, the chance was lost.
The submarine abruptly came to life again. They still had no notion what principle made the thing run, but once it was under way there was nothing more Rui or Sakuya could do.
They crouched together in the darkness and, until they surfaced—needless to say—took their fill of one another. The relief of escaping danger had excited Sakuya beyond reason, while Rui was overjoyed to have acquired a lasting companion.
They thought they heard a familiar click of the tongue somewhere in the darkness, but paid it no mind—no, they beckoned, inviting whoever it was to join them if so inclined. No answer came, and so the two went on coupling.

target.text: ……Despite Tomosato's yelling earlier, the two of them couldn't find that stowaway no matter where they looked, and moreover, they certainly had no way of knowing how to operate this vessel of steel. Sakuya, remembering that moment just before their parting, of Tomosato and the overwhelming number of fish monsters, ultimately couldn't bear it, and though he was well aware that someone like himself would be of absolutely no help, what exactly could he have been intending to say after opening the hatch again? What exactly could he have been intending to do?

Regardless of what, the chance slipped away from him. For the breath of life suddenly returned to the submarine. As always, it was completely unclear to him exactly by what mechanism it operated, but now that it was moving, there was no longer anything Rui or Sakuya could do about it.

The two of them crouched down in the darkness, and until they surfaced once more───well, it went without saying. They made sure to enjoy themselves to their heart's content. The relief of escaping peril had left Sakuya bizarrely aroused, and Rui was also pleased as punch to have found a long-term partner in life. ───From somewhere in the dark, they felt like they could hear a familiar clicking of the tongue, but the two of them paid it no mind, or rather, they actually invited her to join them, should she be so inclined, but they received no response, and so they continued their intercourse with just the two of them.

source.japanese:
そうしてその後の二人は、結局、信天翁号から降りてしまった。
　無頼者どもたちとの別れは実にあっさりしたもので、惜しむ愁嘆場も再会の約もなくオンボロ船は港を離れ、彼らたちの流離いに還っていく。
　ただ。信天翁号を降りた二人を待ち受けているのも、結局は。
　似通った日々なのだった。
source.english:
Afterward, in the end, the two left the Albatross.
Their parting from its lawless company was remarkably brief. No sorrowful scene, no promise to meet again. The dilapidated ship left port and returned to its wandering.
Yet what awaited the pair who had disembarked was, after all,
a similar life.

source.japanese: ───乗りこんだ車両の、予約していたコンパートメントとは異なる個室だ。先客には幾許かの金で言い含め、しばらく席を外してもらっている。
source.english: A private compartment in the train they had boarded, not the one they had reserved. A little money had persuaded its previous occupants to step out for a while.

source.japanese:
個室の椅子に落ち着く、ではなく二人は車窓の窓の下、窓枠からはみ出さないように身を屈めて、共に息を潜[ひそ]める。
　───追っ手は、今日も二人の辿る道を後から、迫ってきている、さて躱[かわ]せるかどうか。
　躱せる。躱せますとも。
　二人ともそれは知っている。
　知っていたとしても、もしや、の想いは何時もつきまとい、それが二人を緊張させる。
　ただその緊張は、二人には必要なものだった。これがないと、日々が引き締まらない。
source.english:
Rather than settling into the seats, they crouched beneath the window, careful not to show above its frame, holding their breath together.
Their pursuers were following their path again today.
Would they evade them?
They would. Of course they would. Both knew it.
Yet even knowing, the thought of what if always clung to them, keeping them tense.
That tension, however, was something they needed. Without it, their days lacked definition.

source.japanese:
その後二人は───
　旅から旅の浮き草生活を続けている。魚怪たちの王、泪の父王は諦めた様子はなく、二人に寄せられる追っ手や搦[から]め手も相変わらずで、朔屋は心が安まる暇がない。おそらくはこの女と一緒にいる限り、ずっとこうなのだ。
　だがそのような暮らしでいい、と朔屋は口ではどうであれ、心では受け入れている。
source.english:
Afterward,
the two continued their drifting life, journey after journey. The fish-monsters' king, Rui's father, showed no sign of giving up. Pursuers and indirect schemes kept coming. Sakuya had no time for peace of mind. Probably it would always be this way,
so long as he stayed with this woman. Yet whatever he said aloud, his heart accepted such a life.

target.text: Thus, after this, the two of them ultimately ended up disembarking from the Albatross. Their parting with those scoundrels was, in fact, a very quick affair; with no pathetic scenes of reluctant parting or promises of future reunions, that ramshackle ship left port, and her crew all went back to their drifting about. However. What awaited the two who had disembarked from the Albatross was, in the end. Very similar days.

───They were sitting in a different private compartment from they one they had reserved on the train they had boarded. The preceding passengers had been asked to leave their seats for a time, easily convinced with a bit of money.

Sitting in the chairs of the private compartment and relaxing they were not; both of them were bent over to make sure they didn't jut out above the window frame, their breath bated. ───Today, their pursuers were, yet again, closing in on them by tracing the path the duo had taken; now then, would they be able to evade them or not? They would. Of course they could. They both knew that.

But even though they knew it, that feeling of perhaps, of what if, always stuck with them, and it made them both tense. But that tension was something indispensable for the two of them. Without this, there would be no excitement in their days.

After all that, the two of them─── The two of them continued their unstable life of travelling from one place to the next. The emperor of the fish monsters, Rui's father, showed no signs of giving up, pursuers came after them one after the other as ever, and Sakuya never had the time to feel at ease. In all likelihood, for as long as he was together with this woman, he never would. But living like this was fine, and no matter what Sakuya might say, he had accepted it in his heart.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ようやく行ったみたいね。
　しつこいったらありません」
source.english:
“They seem to have gone at last.
So persistent.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「泪さんよう。今年に入って何度目だ。
　住まいを替えて、こんな風に冷や汗モノで逃げ出すのは」
source.english:
“Rui, how many times this year?
Changing where we live, then fleeing like this in a cold sweat?”

source.japanese: 車窓の下に身を屈める朔屋は、彼と向かい合い同じく身を屈める泪へぼやいた。汽車の車窓の向こうには、行き交う黒服の男達、一見しただのマフィアの手下辺りに見えたが、泪の父王の息が掛かっていること、恐らく間違いはない。
source.english: Crouched beneath the train window, Sakuya complained to Rui, crouched opposite. Beyond the glass, men in black passed to and fro. At first glance they might have been ordinary Mafia henchmen, but they were almost certainly under Rui's father's influence.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Seems they have finally left. They really are beyond persistent.」
【Naomaso】 「Rui-san, please. How many times has it been this year alone? Changing residences, running away like this, drenched in cold sweat.」

Sakuya, stooped low beneath the window frame, grumbled to Rui, who was facing him in a similar posture. On the other side of the window of their steam train were men in black clothes running to and fro, and while they might have looked like underlings from some mafia at first glance, there was most likely no doubt that they were under the patronage of Rui's Father Emperor.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしが、そういう勘定などしないって、もうご存じの筈よ」
source.english: “You ought to know by now that I don't count such things.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「いいじゃない。退屈とは無縁なのだもの」
source.english: “Isn't it fine? We never have to be bored.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺、なんか、どこかで女性というものの事を考え違いしていたかも……」
source.english: “Maybe… Somewhere along the way… I misunderstood something about women…”

source.japanese:
やれやれ、と身を起こしたのも、充分に時間を空けてのつもりだったけれど、ホームの端に運悪く追っ手の一人が残っていて、朔屋へと振り向いてくる───寸前で。
　
　泪に手を引かれ、また慌てて車窓の下に潜[もぐ]りこむ。
source.english:
He rose with a weary sigh, thinking he had allowed enough time. Unfortunately, one pursuer remained at the platform's edge and began turning toward him. Just before he did, Rui pulled Sakuya's hand.
He hastily ducked beneath the window again.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「貴方、わたくしから離れてはいけなくってよ。もし離れたら───あっという間に捕まって、よくって八つ裂きにされるわね」
source.english: “Dear, you mustn't leave me. If you do, you'll be caught at once. Torn into eight pieces, at best.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「貴方がわたくしを人質にしている限りは、お父様も貴方には手出しできないでしょう」
source.english: “So long as you hold me hostage, Father probably can't lay hands on you.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「だからね、わたくしをずっと人質にしていてね、きっとよ、貴方───」
source.english: “So keep me your hostage forever. Promise, dear…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やれやれ……」
source.english: “Good grief…”

source.japanese:
船員服を質のいい背広に換えた朔屋、服に着られる口かと思いきやなかなかに嵌る。馬子には衣装で、泪と並べれば似合いの二人、と言って言えなくない。
　そんな連れ合いの、景気悪いぼやきを封じるように、片手の人差し指、朔屋の唇に軽く押し当てて「しぃー……」の泪の仕草、向けられる目線の、軽く細め、唇は内緒話を持ちかけるように軽くすぼめられて、悪戯っぽい、人魚の蠱惑の魅力、汲めど尽きる事のない。
source.english:
Sakuya had exchanged his sailor's clothes for a good suit. One might have expected it to wear him, but it suited him surprisingly well. Clothes make the man.
With Rui beside him, the two could almost pass for a well-matched couple. As though sealing off her companion's gloomy complaint, she lightly pressed an index finger to his lips. Shh… Her eyes narrowed a little. Her lips pursed as though proposing a secret. Mischievous, the mermaid's beguiling charm could never be exhausted.

target.text: 【Rui】 「You should know by now that I no longer keep count of such things.」
【Rui】 「It is fine, is it not? It is certainly a far cry from boredom.」
【Naomasa】 「I, uh, kind of feel like I might have completely misunderstood something about women……」

He stood up while muttering a "good grief", believing himself to have hidden for more than enough time, but unluckily, near the very edge of the platform, there remained a single pursuer, and he turned towards Sakuya───but just before that. He was pulled down by Rui's hand, ducking beneath the train window once more in a panic.
【Rui】 「Dear, you are not allowed to leave me. Should you try─── you will be caught in the blink of an eye, and then you will be torn limb from limb, if you are lucky.」
【Rui】 「For as long as you hold me hostage, my father will surely be unable to lay a finger on you.」
【Rui】 「And so, you will hold me hostage forever, I am sure, dear───」
【Naomasa】 「Good grief……」

Sakuya had changed out of his sailor uniform and into a good-quality business suit, and while he might seem the sort who would be worn by his clothes, contrary to expectations, it actually suited him quite well. Fine feathers make fine birds, and when he stood next to Rui, one could even say that they made a well-matched couple.

And as though to seal away her partner's dreary grumbling, she gently pushed one forefinger against Sakuya's lips, and that gesture of shushing, the softly narrowed gaze sent his way, how her lips slightly pursed as though about to tell a secret: it was impish, the seductive charm of a mermaid princess, a well that would never run dry.

source.japanese:
朔屋は思う。連中は自分をこの女を人質に取ったと思っているようだが、本当はそうではない。
　この女が始めから、自分を自由のための旅券としてとらえたのではないか、と───
　いつからそうするつもりだったのか、そのうち泪に訊ねてみよう。時間は幾らでもある。
　快楽と頽廃の、二人の旅。
　また始まったばかり。
　求める限り、何時までも。
source.english:
Sakuya thought. They seemed to believe he had taken this woman hostage, but in truth it was nothing of the kind.
Was it not she who, from the very beginning, had marked him down as her passport to freedom?
One day he would ask Rui just when she had begun planning it. They had time enough and more.
Their journey together, of pleasure and decadence.
Only just begun again.
For as long as they desired.
Forever.

target.text: Sakuya thought to himself. They believed he was the one who had taken her hostage, but the truth was different. Had this woman not, from the very beginning, captured him to use as her own ticket to freedom─── Just when had she first planned to do that? He'd try asking Rui one of these days. They had plenty of time. Their journey of two, of pleasure and decadence. Had only just begun. And as long as they desired it, would go on forever and ever.

source.japanese:
───一方その頃。
　一人、潜水艦内の隠れ処から出でて、海底洞窟の奥を目指す、密航者がある。
　やがて行き着いたのは、洞内の大きな吹き抜け。
　見あげても視界は闇に呑まれ、届かない、そんな広大な吹き抜けの中央に一本の巨大な鍾乳石、石筍が聳え立っていた。
source.english:
Meanwhile, alone,
the stowaway emerged from her hiding place aboard the submarine and headed deeper into the undersea cave.
Eventually she reached a great open shaft.
Looking up, her sight was swallowed by darkness before it reached the top. In the center of that vast space stood an enormous limestone formation: a stalagmite.

target.text: ───Elsewhere, around that time. Having left her hiding place by herself, heading for the depths of the underwater cave, was the stowaway. Eventually, she arrived in a great vault within the cave. Even when looking up, one's vision was swallowed by the darkness, never to reach the top, and at the center of that vast vault there hung a single massive stalactite, or rather, a towering stalagmite rose into the air.

source.japanese:
彼女が石筍に手を差し延べると、その鉱物質の表面が、不思議───まるでこれが予定されていた事であるかのようにさらさらと砂に崩れ、現れ出たものは如何。
　
　それは───一本の木柱だ。
　なんの変哲もない……と見るのは船乗りの、知らざる人間にはそれがマストだと判らないだろう。
source.english:
She reached toward it. The mineral surface crumbled softly into sand, strangely, as though this had been planned. What appeared? A wooden pillar.
Nothing remarkable,
a sailor might think. A person ignorant of such things would not know it was a mast.

source.japanese: 木柱は、なんの支えもなくしばし佇立していたけれど、やがて均衡を逸して密航者へと倒れかかる、その途中で、木柱はそのサイズを縮めながら、遂に鉛筆大にまでなって、その手の中に収まった。密航者は鉛筆大になった柱を、腰の革鞄の中にしまいこむ。
source.english: For a while the pillar stood without support. Then it lost its balance and fell toward the stowaway. As it fell, it shrank, until it lay pencil-sized in her hand. She put the little pillar into the leather bag at her waist.

target.text: When the woman reached out for that stalagmite with her hand, the mineral surface, strangely───almost as if it were scheduled to happen, crumbled into sand, and what, then, should appear from within. It was───a single wooden mast. Nothing out of the ordinary…… is what a sailor would say, but those not in the know would most likely not recognize it as a mast.

For a time, the wooden mast stood still without any support, but before long, it lost its balance and fell towards the stowaway, but during its descent, the wooden mast shrunk in size, finally becoming the size of a pencil, landing directly in that outstretched hand. The stowaway stuffed the pencil-sized mast into the leather bag at her waist.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「取り返せた……これは、フォア」
source.english: “Got it back… This one's the foremast.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I recovered it……this is the fore.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「さてこれからの……話だけど」
source.english: “Now, as for what happens next…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So……about what to do from here on.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まあしばらくは、また『密航』だ」
source.english: “Well, back to ‘stowing away’ for a while.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Well, for the time being, it's back to『stowing away』」

source.japanese:
───思いつかない。
　朔屋、この期に及んで何も思いつかない。もとより危地に当たって輝くような、朔屋タイプでもなんでもない。
　泪は魚怪達に取り抑えられて引き離され、智里は気を抜いた次の瞬間には真っ向唐竹割にしてこんばかりの剣気だ。
source.english:
—Nothing came to him.
Even now, at this late hour, Sakuya could think of nothing. Then again, he had never been the sort to shine when cornered. Rui had been seized and dragged away by the fish-monsters, while Tomosato bristled with the sword-spirit of a man ready to split Sakuya clean down the middle the instant he let his guard slip.

source.japanese:
一つ一つ数えて、どれもこれも手詰まりに突き当たった状況が、朔屋の感覚をどこか他人の物のように替えて、彼自身の実感を乏しくした。
　そもそもここは───どこなのだ、と青年は自答する。海の底と単純に納得してはいたが、信天翁号が忽然と沙漠に捕まってしまっていた段階から、朔屋が知る世界からどう考えても異なる道筋に踏みこんでしまったかの感が強い。といって、本当は自分がいまだ目覚めず夢の中に埋没してある、などと逃避に走ろうにも、この遠近感を狂わせるような広さの岩の間も、自分達を囲繞する魚怪どもも、そして智里が眼前に据えてきている日本刀の眸子も、匂いや空気感、質感、環境音、といった細々とした要素が一々明瞭に過ぎた。
source.english:
Count the circumstances one by one: every one a dead end. The situation made Sakuya's senses seem someone else's, diminished his own feeling of reality.
Where was this place, to begin with? He asked himself. He had simply accepted that it was beneath the sea. Yet from the moment the Albatross had suddenly been caught in a desert, he felt strongly that he had stepped onto a path different from the world he knew. He might try escaping into the thought that he had never truly awakened, remained buried in a dream. But the rock hall, so vast it distorted perspective, the fish-monsters surrounding them, and Tomosato's Japanese sword point before his eyes were all too vivid in their smallest details: smells, the feel of the air, textures, the sounds around him.

target.text: ───He couldn't think of anything. Sakuya, when it mattered the most, couldn't think of anything. To begin with, Sakuya was never the heroic type who shone brilliantly in times of danger. Rui was about to be seized by the fish monsters and taken away from him, and the moment he let down his guard, Tomosato was ready to cut him clean in half where he stood.

As he counted every possibility one by one, the situation invariably ended in a deadlock, and Sakuya's sensations began to feel like they belonged to another, his reality growing tenuous. To begin with, where───was this place even, the young man asked himself. He had naively accepted that it was at the bottom of the ocean, but ever since the Albatross had abruptly found itself captured by a desert, no matter how he looked at it, there was a very strong feeling like everything had gone down a path completely different from the world Sakuya knew.

With that said, no matter how he tried to sprint into the escapism of this actually all just being him still immersed in a dream he had yet to wake from, the vastness of this hall of stone that seemed to disturb his sense of distance, the fish monsters encircling them, the gleaming tip of the Japanese sword Tomosato was holding right before his eyes, the smell and the atmosphere, the feel, the environmental sounds: every one of these assorted elements were simply far too vivid.

source.japanese: 海底洞窟だの、魚と人の合成のような化け物だのその王だの、凄腕の殺し屋だのどれもこれも尖鋭的なのにも関わらず、馬鹿馬鹿しいほどに、いじましいほど「本当の事」で。なにやらなし崩しに連れて来られてしまった、どこか知らないところ。朔屋が知る者は二人だけ。
source.english: An undersea cave, monsters compounded of fish and human, their king, a terribly skilled killer: every detail extreme, yet ridiculously, oppressively real. He had somehow been brought here, without a clear moment of assent, to a place he did not know. Only two people were familiar to him.

source.japanese:
その一人、泪は───向こうで行動を封じられてはいるけれど、魚怪達の接し様自体は青年に対するものより丁重にどこまでも恭[うやうや]しく、それも当たり前、彼女はここの長上の末の姫なのだというのだから。
　泪はならば、この、朔屋が知らない現実の住人だ。
source.english:
One, Rui, was being held over there, unable to move. Yet the fish-monsters treated her far more courteously than they treated him, with unfailing reverence. Naturally: she was their lord's youngest princess. Rui,
then, belonged to this reality Sakuya did not know.

source.japanese:
それでは、智里はどうだろう。飄然、恬淡として、朔屋ではそうなりきれない、通人の果てになりすぎてしまった、変梃な殺し屋、けれど朔屋の死の標[しるべ]。この男だけは本当によく判らない。様々な人種が居合わせる信天翁号の中で、船員でもなんでもないのに、朔屋にとって友達と言えるのはこの男しかいない。
　元から殺し屋だと、朔屋の殺し屋だと言っていたのだから、むしろこの状況を迎えるのは遅すぎた、というくらいなのだけれど。
source.english:
What of Tomosato? Airy and detached, beyond any worldly ease Sakuya could hope to achieve: an eccentric killer, yet the signpost to Sakuya's death. This man alone was truly incomprehensible. Amid all the kinds of people aboard the Albatross, he was not a sailor or anything of the sort. Yet he was the only man Sakuya could call a friend.
Since he had declared himself a killer from the beginning, Sakuya's killer, this situation had if anything taken too long to arrive.

source.japanese: それでも朔屋には解せない事がありすぎた。
source.english: Still, far too much remained beyond Sakuya's understanding.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（そもそもこいつ、
　俺を本当に殺したいのだろうか）
source.english:
(To begin
with, does he really want to kill me?)

source.japanese: これまでに朔屋を斬る機会が幾らでもあったのにそれを見逃していた、というからだけではなく、智里にそれを命じたモノが明らかになり、その本人に斬れを命じられて、こうして対峙してどのくらいが過ぎた。もちろん、一時間二時間の単位は過ごしていないだろうか、それでも数分間は経って、朔屋が知る限りの智里の業前であれば、それこそ雲燿の間で青年など両断されているはず。
source.english: Not only because Tomosato had overlooked countless earlier opportunities. Now the being who commissioned him had revealed himself and personally ordered Sakuya cut down. How long had the two faced one another like this? Not an hour or two, certainly, but several minutes. With the skill Sakuya knew Tomosato possessed, Sakuya ought to have been divided in a flash.

source.japanese: 常なら刃を擬[ぎ]されなどしたら泣き叫んで命乞いするのが当然の青年にしては、いかさま奇妙な事を気にするものだが、この時はその疑念、つい口にのぼせてしまうを止められず、
source.english: For a man ordinarily given to crying and begging for his life when faced with a blade, it was a peculiar concern. Yet Sakuya could not stop the question from rising to his lips.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なあ……あのさ、
　なんでこんな……時間かけんの？
　こう、じりじりと剣先向けられてるの、
　すごく厭[いや]なんだが……」
source.english:
“Hey…
Why take so long…?
I really hate having your sword pointed
at me like this…”

target.text: The underwater cave, the monsters that seemed a hybrid of man and fish as well as their emperor, the masterful murderer, each and every one so acutely sharp, to the point of absurdity, almost naggingly「real」. One thing had lead to another, and he'd suddenly found himself being taken here, to somewhere he didn't know. The only thing Sakuya knew here was but two people.

One of those, Rui───was being prevented from moving, but the fish monsters' treatment of her was far more courteous than what he was given; it was as reverent as could be, though that was only natural if she was the youngest princess of their liege. Rui, then, was a resident of this reality so unfamiliar to Sakuya.

In that case, what about Tomosato? Aloof, detached, Sakuya could never imitate him in that respect, a man who had reached and gone past the end of the path trod by the jaded worldly, an oddball of a murderer, but he was the very mark of Sakuya's death. This man alone he truly did not understand. Even on the Albatross, where all manner of races and types cohabited, despite not even being a sailor himself, this man was the only one whom Sakuya could call friend. He had said it right from the beginning: he was a murderer, he was going to be Sakuya's murderer; if anything, the situation reaching this point was very much belated, so often had he said it, but.
Even with that said, there were far too many inconsistencies that were incomprehensible to Sakuya.
【Naomasa】 （Actually, does this guy really even want to kill me?）

It wasn't just because he'd let so many opportunities to cut Sakuya down pass him by hitherto, it had become obvious who Tomosato had been ordered to do it by, but for just how long had they stared each other down like this since the order was given by the client himself? Of course, it wasn't something in the realm of an hour or two, but several minutes must have passed, and as far as Sakuya knew, with Tomosato's ability, the young man should have been cut down in a brief flash of lightning.

Ordinarily, it would only be all too natural for this young man to break into screams while begging for his life when a blade was pressed to his throat, so this certainly was something rather strange for him to worry about, but in this moment, he was unable to keep those doubts from spilling out from his lips.
【Naomasa】 「Hey……listen, uh, why are you……taking so long? It's really, really unpleasant, having a sword pointed at me like this, so……」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あん？
　ああ、そりゃあ時間稼ぎだからな」
source.english:
“Huh?
Oh, because I'm buying time.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Huh? Oh, that's because I'm buying time.」

source.japanese: 含みとか、勿体とか、そういった仄[ほの]めかしからは、鳥と小石が縁の無いように遠い男である。智里自身は常に明瞭な物言いをするだけれど、それを耳にするモノには間の説明が省かれすぎていてまるで足りない、それなのにこの場に居合わせたモノは、魚怪の一統も朔屋も、背景が、一枚の硝子板に描かれていたのが、一瞬で壊れてそのひびの中に緊迫感、殺し、殺される、生命の遣り取りに伴う殺伐とした気配が吸われていって台無しになったのを覚った。不快そうに眉をひそめて眼を細ませていたのは、泪。それまでは智里に対して、それでも品の佳い、当たらず障[さわ]らずの距離感で接していたのか、ここでとうとうこらえきれなくなったと見える。
source.english: A man as far from insinuation, portentousness, and hints as a bird from a pebble. Tomosato always spoke plainly, but omitted so much connecting explanation that his listeners had far too little to work with. Even so, everyone present, fish-monsters and Sakuya alike, felt the scene—as though painted on a pane of glass—break in an instant. Its tension, the harsh air of killing and being killed, of lives at stake, was sucked into the cracks. Ruined. Rui narrowed her eyes and frowned unhappily. Until then she had maintained a courteous, unobtrusive distance toward Tomosato. Now she seemed finally unable to endure it.

target.text: A man as distant from implications and putting on airs, any of those sorts of suggestive hints, as a bird is from a pebble. Tomosato himself always spoke in a clear, articulate way, but to any who heard him, it was ever so lacking in explanation that it felt almost insufficient, and yet all present here felt it, every fish monster and Sakuya included: how the background, drawn across a single pane of glass, shattered in an instant, and through those cracks, the tension, kill or be killed, the brutally bloodthirsty atmosphere that accompanied life's give-and-take, was sucked out, utterly ruined.

The one who furrowed their brows in displeasure and narrowed their eyes was Rui. Until now, when it came to Tomosato, while always graceful, she had interacted with him from a non-committal distance, but here, it seemed like she finally could no longer tolerate it.

source.japanese:
智里、朔屋の問いに、酒の瓶でも置くように、刀を下ろして応えた。
　無論そうやって脇に自然に垂らした形から、どのような機だろうが先んじて刃を撃ちこむ剣腕である。全く安心はできないのだが、それでも鼻先に向けられているよりは精神的によほど気が楽だ。
　朔屋は自分の肩が下がったのを知る、やはり体の方は相当以上に緊張していたようで、背中にどっと汗も浮いているでないか。
source.english:
Answering Sakuya, Tomosato lowered the sword as casually as setting down a bottle.
Naturally, from that relaxed position at his side he could strike first at any opening. There was no safety to be found. Yet it was far easier on the mind than having the point directed at his nose.
Sakuya felt his shoulders drop. His body had apparently been under considerable tension. Sweat sprang over his back too.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「俺は今回、三方から依頼を受けてなあ。
　一つは殺しだ、ここの親分からな。
　二つは守ってくれと。朔屋、お前をな。
　……モテてんじゃねえかよう、直の字」
source.english:
“This time I've taken commissions from three sides.
One to kill,
from the boss here. Two to protect you, Sakuya.
Popular fellow, aren't you, Nao?”

source.japanese: 刀を下げたとて、全く油断はできない男だとはいえ、さすがに片手を懐手に納めたとあっては、おまけに懐の中でごそごそ煙管も探す様子とあっては。
source.english: He was not a man one could trust merely because he lowered his sword. Yet now he tucked one hand inside his clothes, and apparently rummaged for his pipe as well.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「守ってくれって、俺を？
　誰がそれを……いや。
　一つは見当が付くが……」
source.english:
“Protect me?
Who asked that…? No.
I can guess one…”

source.japanese: 朔屋は、魚怪の一統によって隔てられた泪を眺めやる、それで彼女の表情が、すっと消えたのに答えを見たと思った、思って、
source.english: Sakuya looked toward Rui, kept apart by the fish-monsters. Her expression vanished smoothly. He thought he saw his answer in that. Thought so—

target.text: In response to Sakuya's question, Tomosato lowered his sword like he were setting down a bottle of booze. Of course, he was the sort of master swordsman who could strike first no matter the occasion, even with his blade hanging naturally at his side like that. He felt no relief in the slightest, and yet he still felt far more at ease mentally without a sword pointed at the tip of his nose. Sakuya realized his own shoulders had slumped; his body really must have been substantially tense, and was that not also a veritable flood of sweat he felt rolling down his back?

【Tomosato】 「This time around, I received a request from three people. One was to kill, from the boss here. The other two was to protect. Protect you, Sakuya. ……You're a real popular guy, aren't you, big Nao?」

He might have been the sort of man one could never be careless around, even with his blade lowered, but when he placed one hand in his pocket, and on top of that, also seemed to be rummaging around within it for his kiseru, then it was another story.
【Naomasa】 「To protect? Protect me? Who would ask……wait. I can imagine at least one……」

Sakuya looked over at Rui, who was separated from them by the entire swarm of fish monsters, and despite how whatever expression was on her face suddenly vanished, he thought he'd found his answer, so he thought, but,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「一人はほれ、あの密航女。
　ここに来る時なんかいたろ、潜水艦中に」
source.english:
“One was that stowaway woman.
Saw her aboard the submarine coming here, didn't you?”

source.japanese: 朔屋にとっては無論それはそれで意外ではあったけれど、智里が続けた言葉には、茶請けに食うた大福が、店先に飾る用の模造のものであったような、歯ごたえの異様な悪さが堪[こた]えて後じさった。
source.english: Naturally that surprised Sakuya in its own right. But Tomosato's next words made him recoil as though he had bitten into a sweet rice cake with his tea, only to discover it was a fake made for a shop-window display. That horrible feel between his teeth.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「One is that, you know, that stowaway girl. She was somewhere in that submarine on the way here, right?」

Needless to say, that was kind of not what Sakuya had really expected to hear, but when he heard Tomosato's next words, with a nausea welling up within him similar to the strange chewiness of biting into a daifuku one had ordered as a snack to go with tea only to discover that it was one of those fakes used to decorate storefronts, he backed away. (TN: A daifuku, written "大福", is a piece of round mochi usually stuffed with sweetened red bean paste, often served with green tea.)

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あと一つは俺だあな、朔屋。
　てめえは斬れねえよ。
　となると二対一の多数決だな」
source.english:
“The other is me, Sakuya.
Can't cut you down.
That makes it a two-to-one majority.”

source.japanese: 泪もまた、魚怪達の腕の中では、と前髪震わせ顔を上げ、表情を取り戻したというのに、智里は煙管は出したが今度は刻みはどこだともそもそやりと、いっこうに場を意に介さぬ様子で、
source.english: In the fish-monsters' arms, Rui too lifted her face with a tremor of her fringe, recovering her expression. Tomosato had produced his pipe, but now fumbled about for the shredded tobacco, apparently unconcerned with the scene.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え、な、なんで、あんたは殺し屋って」
source.english: “Huh? Why? You said you were a killer…”

source.japanese:
ようやくだった。朔屋の身裡を、冷たい棘だらけの危機感が転がり回って喉を締め付けたのは。殺し屋を名乗っておきながら自分を生かしておいたのはもしや、まさか。
　───口は悪く伝法に聞くけれど、実のところなにくれと朔屋に手を貸す事も多い。
　
　───ただ着崩している、を通りこして、妙に色気にはだけすぎているその前身頃。
　───蒼い眸[ひとみ]に癖がありすぎるが、細身の優男でいかにも女殺しの造作があるのに、浮いた噂というのが聞こえてこない、女郎を買いに行っている姿を見た事もない。
source.english:
At last a sense of danger, cold and bristling with thorns, rolled through Sakuya and gripped his throat. Calling himself a killer, yet keeping Sakuya alive: could it be—surely not?
His tongue was harsh and rough, but he often helped Sakuya in one way or another.
His clothes were not merely worn loosely; their front was opened with an oddly excessive allure.
Those blue eyes were peculiar, but he was a slender, handsome man with features fit to break women's hearts. Yet there were no romantic rumors. Sakuya had never seen him go to buy a woman.

source.japanese: それらが物語るある一つの結論に、朔屋は思わず泪の前に飛び出して身を投げ出して額を撃ちつけつ何度も頭を下げて許しをこいねがいたくなった。
source.english: At the single conclusion those things suggested, Sakuya suddenly wanted to throw himself before Rui, strike his forehead down, bow again and again, and plead for forgiveness.

source.japanese:
───ごめんなさいごめんなさい
　
　───あなたが誘った事だとはいえ
　
　───あなたのお尻をほじってしまって
　
　───ごめんなさい!!
　
　
　
　───だからホ、あいや智里君。
　
　───僕のお尻を狙わないで───！
　
　朔屋は、更に後じさったという。
source.english:
—I'm sorry, I'm sorry.

—Even if it was at your invitation.

—For poking around in your bottom.

—I'm sorry!!

—So, Ho—no, Tomosato.

—Please don't come after my bottom—!

Sakuya, it is said, backed still farther away.

source.japanese: そんな朔屋に何事か思うところはあるようはあるが、無視して、燐火の蒼い眸[ひとみ]を撓[たわ]めつ智里の、
source.english: Tomosato seemed to have some thought about this behavior, but ignored it. His phosphorescent blue eyes curved.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「And the other one is me, Sakuya. I'm not gonna cut you down. And with that, it becomes two against one, and majority rules.」

From within the arms of the fish monters, Rui's bangs shook, and she raised her head, but despite having regained the expression on her face, this time, though Tomosato had found his pipe and was fiddling around looking for his tobacco, seemingly completely uncaring of what was going on around him,
【Naomasa】 「Huh, b-, but why? You're a murderer, so!」

Finally. Within Sakuya, a feeling of danger covered in chilling thorns began to roll around, constricting his throat. For he called himself a murderer and yet let him live, which perhaps meant, but surely not, but could it be? ───Though his tone was rough and rude, in reality, he would very frequently lend a hand to Sakuya in all kinds of ways.

───He wasn't simply wearing his clothes casually, no, it went beyond that; the front of his outfit was far too exposed in a weirdly sexy way. ───While his azure eyes were a bit too peculiar for most, he was still a slender, elegant man with the facial features of a ladykiller, and yet he had never heard any romantic rumours about the man, nor had he ever so much as seen him head out to pick up a prostitute.

All this spoke of only one conclusion, and upon drawing it, Sakuya instinctively wanted to leap in front of Rui, throw himself on the floor, bang his brow against the rock again and again while desperately beseeching her for mercy.

───I'm sorry, I'm sorry. ───You might have been the one who asked for it. ───But I am so very sorry. ───For fucking you in the ass!! ───So please, Homo-, I mean, Tomosato-kun. ───Leave my asshole alone───！ Sakuya retreated even further.
He seemed to have his own ideas about what Sakuya was doing, but Tomosato ignored it, the phosphorous blaze in his azure eyes warping,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「知ってるか朔屋、お前なあ、お前どうやら、自分で思ってるよりよほど、あの襤褸船の重要人物だぜ。俺はそういうのは、基本的に殺らねぇの」
source.english: “Know something, Sakuya? Seems you're a far more important figure aboard that wreck than you think. As a rule, I don't kill those.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「So did you know, Sakuya? Turns out that you, for whatever reason, is someone far, far more important to that piece of junk ship than you yourself realize. I don't kill things like that, on principle.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「流儀てぇのが俺にあるとすれば、そいつだ。
　お話への、礼儀だぁね。
　……『あんた、一体なにものだ……？』
　とか浮かねえ返しを、してくれるなよ？」
source.english:
“If I've a principle, that's it.
Courtesy toward a story.
And don't give me some gloomy reply like,
'Who on earth are you…?'”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……よかったぁ……俺、隠れホモ、ホモ里に見込まれた訳じゃなかったんだ……っ」
source.english: “…Thank goodness… I wasn't singled out by some closet homo, Homosato…!”

source.japanese: 朔屋がほとんど身を二つ折りに、吐いた息はもし足下に小蟹でも這っていたなら吹き飛ばしていただろうと言うほどの肺活量、生命を狙われるより尻を狙われた方が青年にとっては脅威の、安堵のあまりへたりこみかけた程だった。
source.english: Sakuya almost folded double as he exhaled. Had a small crab been crawling at his feet, that lungful would have blown it away. Having his bottom targeted was more threatening to him than having his life targeted. He nearly collapsed with relief.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「If there's anything you could call my "style", it would be that. Good manners when dealing with a story, yeah? ……And don't you dare give me some lame-ass response like 『You-, just who on earth are you……?』」
【Naomasa】 「……Thank God……Homosato the closet gay hasn't marked me as his next victim……」

Sakuya was almost bent in two, and had there been any small crabs crawling around his feet, his breath would surely have blown them away, so immense was the lung capacity of it; for this young man, having his ass targeted was a greater threat than his life being targeted, to the point the overwhelming relief made him sink down to the floor.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あー、そっちかあ。
　そっちできやがったかあ。
　まー、そういう馬鹿しか、
　言わねえ口だもんなあ」
source.english:
“Ah, that way.
That's where you went.
Well,
nonsense is all that mouth of yours ever produces.”

source.japanese: いかにも愉快そうにくつくつ笑い、
source.english: He chuckled, plainly delighted.

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Aah, so that was the problem? You really went there, did you? Well, that is the kind of brainless shit only an idiot would say.」
With stifled laughter, like he truly was enjoying himself,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「いいぜ、馬鹿にここまで付き合ったんだ、ついでに逃がしてやるよ。お前が逃げの一手でも思いつきゃあ、そいつに乗っかったんだが、ま、無理だんべお前じゃよ」
source.english: “Fine. I've gone along with the fool this far. I'll let you escape too. If you'd thought of a move, I'd have played along. But that's beyond you, isn't it?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Sure thing, I've already come this far with your stupid ass, so I'll let you escape while I'm at it. If you had come up with some way to escape on your own, I would have gone along with it, but, guess that's not happening with you.」

source.japanese:
そんな事を言っておきながら、朔屋へとくるりと背中を向けてにべもなく、すたすた歩み去っていくのはついてこいと言っているつもりか知らねど、歩を進めていくのが泪を押さえている魚怪共一統へ。
　佳いところへ連れて行ってやるからと誘った先がイカサマ賭場だったというようなもので、逃げるも蜂の頭もあったものではない。
　大体にして朔屋と智里の遣り取りを耳にしていた魚怪共も、殺し屋のあまりのいい加減さ節操の無さに皆開いた口が塞がらないので、中には怒気を浮かせた真面目ものもいる。
source.english:
Having said that, he turned his back on Sakuya without ceremony and strode away. Perhaps he meant follow me. But he was walking toward the fish-monsters holding Rui.
Like someone promising to take you somewhere nice, then leading you to a crooked gambling den. Escape, my foot.
The fish-monsters who had heard the conversation were equally open-mouthed at the killer's extraordinary lack of consistency or principle. A few earnest ones showed anger.

source.japanese:
呆れるモノ嘲笑うモノ怒るモノあり。
　けれど。
　魚怪共もここに集ったモノは人に当てはめられば兵士達だったろうに、けれど。
　その中の一体たりとも、朔屋も泪も。
　どの眼も恐れ、危機感、まして絶望など、智里の歩みに認めたものなど一つもなかった。一つたりとも。故にそうなった。泪を奪われ、朔屋も共に逸する事になった。
source.english:
Some were astonished, some mocked,
some grew angry.
Yet—these assembled fish-monsters would have been soldiers,
in human terms.
Yet not one of them, nor Sakuya or Rui, saw fear, urgency, much less despair in Tomosato's steps. Not one eye. That was why it happened. Rui was taken from them, and Sakuya escaped too.

target.text: While saying that, he curtly turned his back to Sakuya, then briskly walked off, and perhaps he was trying to tell him to follow, but the direction he was advancing in was straight towards the crowd of fish monsters restraining Rui. It was like having been invited out to a nice establishment only to find yourself in a rigged gambling joint; there was not even the ghost of a chance to escape there.

Most of the fish monsters who had overheard the exchange between Sakuya and Tomosato were left with their jaws dropped at the murderer's sheer carelessness and lack of faithfulness, but there were also some of the more grave among them who let their anger show.

There were the dumbfounded, the sneering, and the seething. However. Had the fish monsters gathered here been human, they would have been soldiers of some kind, however. Not a single amongst them, not even Rui or Sakuya. None of them recognized terror, impending danger, and certainly not despair and its like within Tomosato's stride. Not a single one. Hence it happened. Rui was stolen, and Sakuya was forgotten along with her.

source.japanese: すたすたと泪を戒めた魚人達の前に出て、三振りで斬り伏せ、泪の手を取り朔屋の元まで連れ戻してくると、とんと彼女の背中を押して青年に預けた。
source.english: He walked straight before the fish-people restraining Rui and cut them down with three swings. Taking her hand, he brought her back to Sakuya, then gave her a light push between the shoulders and entrusted her to him.

target.text: He briskly walked in front of the fish monsters holding Rui, cut them down with three slashes, took Rui's hand, brought her back to where Sakuya stood, gave the woman a push on the back, then left her in Sakuya's hands.

source.japanese:
歩いて、斬って、それだけだ。
　智里がやったのはそれだけだ。
　泪を引っ張ってきたのは付け足しのようなものだろう。
　足許は裏鉄も打たず革だけ張った雪駄だから跫音だって派手を着ず、刀運びだって歩きながらの無造作というのも馬鹿馬鹿しい、傘で道端の枝を叩くのとそっくり、剣の術理の至妙や足法の極致とはかくの如きと、無理矢理当てはめるより、飯を食って屁を放[ひ]るような、と表すしかない。
