　目の当たりにしていた魚怪達、それどころか長上でさえ、朔屋が智里に押しやられ、泪の肩を抱いてよろよろと出口の方へと歩み出すを、何処へ行くつもりならんか、と見守って、二人が巨大な横穴奥の暗がりへ消えていくまで、誰も手出しをせず暢気に見送ってから、物事のどういう流れを経てそうなったのか、やっと頭の中で順序がついた有様の。
source.english:
Walk. Cut.
That was all Tomosato did. Pulling Rui away might have been an afterthought.
His sandals had only leather soles, no iron fittings,
so even his footsteps were unobtrusive. To call his sword work casual as he walked would itself be ridiculous. It was like knocking a roadside branch with an umbrella. Rather than force it into descriptions of exquisite sword theory or ultimate footwork, one could only compare it to eating a meal and farting.
Even the fish-monsters watching, even their lord, looked on as Sakuya was pushed onward, put an arm about Rui's shoulders, and staggered toward the exit. Where were they going? No one interfered. Everyone watched them disappear into the great side tunnel's darkness, quite at ease. Only afterward did the sequence of events arrange itself in their heads.

target.text: He walked, he slashed; that was all. That was all Tomosato did. Pulling Rui away must have been like a little addendum. Below his feet were setta sandals clad entirely in leather, no thin iron plates underneath, and so his footsteps were subdued; even the ease with which he handled his sword as he walked was ludicrous, exactly like swatting away a roadside branch with an umbrella, and rather than trying to force some high-minded concepts like "the sublime principles of sword technique" or "the pinnacle of footwork" onto it, the only proper way to describe it was that it was as artless as eating a meal and passing wind.

It was not just the fish monsters who had witnessed it, but even their liege too; they all simply watched as Sakuya was pushed by Tomosato, flung an arm around Rui's shoulder, then staggered towards the exit, and wondering just where they were going, none of them moved a finger until they had carelessly watched the two vanish into the darkness of the depths of a giant tunnel; only then did it seem like the order of what exactly just happened and how fell into place in their heads.

source.japanese:
歩いて、斬って、泪を引っ張って朔屋と二人で逃して。
　この状況下でそれをやってのけられても、魚怪達が、海の伝説達がまず感じたのは戸惑いと困惑、怒りや逸失感は後から押し寄せて、その時にはもう───手遅れなのだった。
　その激甚大津波に比し、その暴威、嵐にも引き合う、一つ一つの魚怪の集合というより、大なる奔流と化した海のモノ達が怒りもて殺到していく、広間の出入りの横穴に、末姫を追って、不届き者を誅する為に。
　けれど。時は既に逸した。
　二人が逃れていった横穴の前に位置を移して立ちはだかるは殺し屋とはいえたかだか一人の人の子、持てるは剣の一振り、と押し寄せていく魚怪達は、二人をこの群集から逃したのもその同じ人間である事に、今ひとつ理解が至っていない。
source.english:
Walk, cut, drag Rui free, send her fleeing with Sakuya.
Even after seeing all that accomplished, the fish-monsters—the legends of the sea—felt bewilderment and confusion first. Anger and the shock of loss came surging afterward. By then it was already too late.
The creatures of the sea ceased to be a gathering of individual fish-monsters and became a single great torrent, fierce as a cataclysmic wave, violent as a storm. They rushed for the side tunnel, to pursue the youngest princess and punish the insolent offender.
But the moment was gone.
The man who moved to bar the tunnel through which the pair had fled was, killer though he might be, only one human armed with one sword. The charging fish-monsters had not yet quite grasped that this was the same man who had spirited the pair out of their midst.

source.japanese: 血風が、吹き荒れた───青黒い血の霧だけが。
source.english:
A bloody wind blew wild.

Only a mist of blue-black blood.

target.text: He had walked, slashed, pulled away Rui, then let her get away together with Sakuya. Even having managed that impressive feat under these conditions, the first thing the fish monsters, these legends of the sea felt, was confusion; the anger and feeling of loss only descended upon them later, but by then ───it was already too late. Its intensity was like a great tsunami, the violence rivalling a storm; it was less a gathering of singular fish monsters and more of a grand, unified torrent as a deluge of fish monsters rushed forth in anger towards that tunnel that served as the entrance to the hall, in pursuit of the princess, to put that blackguard to death.

However, the time to do so had already passed. Having moved to the front of the tunnel the two had escaped through was the murderer, standing imposingly in the way, but murderer he may be, he was but a single child of man, he had but a single sword to swing, so the surging fish monsters thought, but not a single one had grasped that it was this very same human who had only just allowed the two to get away from them.
A blood-wind swept through the tunnels───a mist of darkened blue blood alone.

source.japanese: 朔屋と智里の別れは、押し寄せる魚怪達の群れを間近にして。だから、交わせる言葉も、もう幾つも残されていなかった。その一つを朔屋は、
source.english: Sakuya and Tomosato parted with the approaching fish-monsters close at hand. Few words remained that they could exchange. One of them Sakuya spent—

target.text: When Sakuya and Tomosato parted, the advancing swarm of fish monsters were close by. As a result, there were precious few words left to exchange. One of those exchanges was:

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おう、な、朔屋。
　こっちは俺がやっておくから、
　お前、泪と二人で、な？」
source.english:
“Hey, Sakuya.
I'll handle this end. You and Rui,
the two of you, right?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ああ、ええと。
　あんたが船に隠してある酒の残り、
　呑んじゃっていい？」
source.english:
“…Ah, um.
Can I drink the rest of the liquor
you've hidden aboard?”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Yo, hey, Sakuya. I'll take care of these guys here, so you go with Rui, yeah?」
【Naomasa】 「……Yeah, uhmm. All the booze you still have hidden around the ship, can I have what's left?」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「馬鹿、そんなんとっておくかよ。
　出てくる前に皆干してきたわ」
source.english:
“Idiot. Why would I leave any?
Drained it all before coming out.”

source.japanese: で費やしてしまったし、智里は智里で、突出し、撃ちかかってきた魚怪を振り向き様の拝み撃ちで両断すると、
source.english: —and squandered it on that. Tomosato, for his part, turned and split in two a fish-monster that broke from the pack and came at him, bringing his sword down in a two-handed overhead stroke—

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Idiot, you think I'd leave something like that just lying around? I drank every last drop before we left.」
They were spent thus, and Tomosato, being himself, suddenly thrust his sword out, bisecting an attacking fish monster with a two-handed overhead vertical prayer-slash while pivoting,

source.japanese:
【智里】
「あの親分の積んだ金が一番高かったんだがな。考えてみりゃあこれ、親馬鹿の片棒担ぎじゃねえか。やだよそんなの、間抜け臭い。やっぱやめた」
source.english: “That boss offered the most money. But thinking about it, I'd just be helping a doting father. Don't want that. Makes me look stupid. Changed my mind.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「But the boss back there did pay the best. Now that I think about it though, wasn't that me being the accomplice of an overly doting father? No thanks, sounds retarded. Yep, I'm not doing that.」

source.japanese: ぴっぴっといささか滑稽に見えるほどの暢気さで血振りする智里に、魚怪達は一瞬ひるんだものの、すぐさま二重三重に包囲して、押し寄せてくるその圧力、一人の人間にはどう抗しようもないはずなのに、智里は微塵も気負いも見せず、朔屋へ、さっさと行けと、犬の子でも追うように手を振った。
source.english: He flicked the blood from his sword with an ease almost comical. The fish-monsters flinched for an instant, then promptly surrounded him in two, three ranks. One human ought never to have resisted that pressure. Yet Tomosato showed not the slightest strain. He waved Sakuya away as though shooing a puppy. Go on, quickly.

target.text: As Tomosato flicked off the blood covering his sword with an almost comical ease, the fish monsters flinched for a moment, but soon enough, they encircled him in two, three rows; the pressure bearing down upon him should have been impossible for a single human to defy, and yet Tomosato betrayed not a single shread of nervousness, waving his hand at Sakuya, telling him to get going like he were chasing off a puppy.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「智里さん、貴方、直さんを助けるようでご立派に見えますけれど」
source.english: “Tomosato, you look admirable, appearing to save Nao.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Tomosato-san, you certainly look splendidly handsome as you attempt to save Nao-san, however.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「それは果てしなく───見苦しい真似だと言う事、ご承知でしょうね」
source.english: “But surely you know how endlessly disgraceful this behavior is.”

source.japanese:
泪にしては角の立つ言葉は、朔屋にはどうにも、智里の真の依頼人というのが誰なのかに関わっているように思えてならず、泪は、泪でさえこの殺し屋に面目立てられたのがどうにも気に入らない風情らしい、とそこまで見て朔屋はそれ以上ほじくり返さない事にした。幾つか腑に落ちて、幾つか腑に落ちない事はある。
　たとえば、泪が結局のところ、智里に朔屋の護衛を依頼していたのなら、なぜそれを隠していたのか、とか。
source.english:
For Rui, those were sharp words. Sakuya could not help thinking they concerned the identity of Tomosato's true client. Even Rui seemed to resent having this killer preserve her dignity. Having seen that much, Sakuya decided not to dig any further. Some things made sense; others did not.
For instance: if Rui had, after all, commissioned Tomosato to guard Sakuya, why had she concealed it?

target.text: 【Rui】 「You are surely aware─── that your conduct is endlessly deplorable, yes?」

Rather prickly words coming from Rui, and Sakuya couldn't help but feel that this had something to do with whoever Tomosato's true client was, and since he noticed that Rui, even Rui, seemed displeased at having her honour salvaged by this murderer, Sakuya decided not to dig any further. He'd come to understand several things, but there were also several things he still did not. For example, if Rui ultimately turned out to have requested Tomosato to protect Sakuya, then why exactly was she hiding that, and so on.

source.japanese:
【智里】
「おおともよ。いつ後から刺されんじゃねえかと、びくびくものだぁ！」
source.english: “Of course. Trembling at the thought of being stabbed in the back later!”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「それからな、朔屋、
　最後にあの潜水艦動かすやり方教えてやる。
　船に入ってハッチ締めたらな、
『びねうびねうびねう』
　と逆立ちして唱えろ」
source.english:
“And Sakuya,
I'll tell you how to move that submarine before you go.
Get aboard and close the hatch.
Then stand on your head and chant:
'Bineu, bineu, bineu.'”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「そうすりゃあ、浮くだけは浮くから」
source.english: “That'll make it float, at least.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Damn right. Never know when I'll get stabbed in the back for it, leaves a man shivering!」
【Tomosato】 「And lastly, Sakuya, as a parting gift, I'll teach you how to operate that submarine. You get in the vessel, close the hatch, then do a handstand and chant 『ibenUibenUibenU』」
【Tomosato】 「You do that, it'll float, at least.」

source.japanese:
最後の最後で智里はまた朔屋の眉の根と下顎をかたんと落とす言葉を置いて、背を向けてそれっきり。
　朔屋が最後に目にした光景は、押し寄せる魚怪の大群に、弧剣一振りで対峙する智里の姿だった。
source.english:
At the very last, Tomosato left words that dropped Sakuya's brow and jaw with a clunk, then turned his back.
That was all. What Sakuya saw last was Tomosato facing the approaching mass of fish-monsters with a single sword.

target.text: At the very end, Tomosato once again left Sakuya with words that made him lift his brows and drop his jaw; he then turned his back, and that was that. The very last thing Sakuya saw was Tomosato confronting the great horde of fish monsters, giving an arced swing of his blade as they descended upon him.

source.japanese:
友達との別れというのがこう言うのでいいのか、何か自分がとんでもない間違いをやらかしたような気がしてならない朔屋だが、岩屋を出でて泪と連れ立ち、逃げるうち、鍾乳洞の暗さは長さを果てなく見せたが、それでもしまいには、岩床の端、潮の寄せくる岸辺に潜水艦の輪郭を見た。それまで二人、無言。お互い何を言うべきなのか、男と女の駆け引きに練れた筈の泪でさえ、虚脱したかのように口を閉ざしたまま。
　それでもこの潜水艦まで逃げ延びてきたけれど、朔屋も泪もこんな巨大な鋼の塊、どう動かすのか見当も付かない。
source.english:
Was this any way to part from a friend? Unable to shake the feeling that he had made some tremendous mistake, Sakuya left the chamber with Rui. In their flight, the limestone cave's darkness made its length seem endless. Yet at last, at the edge of the rock floor where seawater lapped the shore, they saw the submarine's outline. Until then, neither had spoken. What should they say to one another? Even Rui, supposedly so practiced in the dealings between men and women, kept her mouth closed as though drained.
They had reached this submarine, but neither knew how to move such a great lump of steel.

target.text: Was this really a proper way to say goodbye to a friend; Sakuya couldn't help but feel that he had made a tremendous mistake somewhere along the way, but after leaving the little rock chamber together with Rui, as they made their escape, while the darkness of the limestone cavern seemed to stretch on endlessly, even that finally ended, and at the far end of the bedrock, he saw the outline of that submarine by the bank where the tide came surging in. Until that point, the two of them had kept silent.

What ought they even say to one another; even Rui, experienced in the art of diplomacy between men and woman, refused to talk as if despondent. Even so, while they had managed to make good their getaway to this submarine, neither Sakuya nor Rui had the faintest idea how to operate the gigantic mass of steel.

source.japanese:
とにかく、重い鋼の蓋を二人がかりで開いて、身を押し込めて、梯子段を降りる時も、二人は言葉をお互いにかけあぐねたまま。
　そんな空気の中、朔屋は智里の言葉を思い出したけれど、実行するには大変な開き直りが要求され、やった後も泪との間に立ち籠めた微妙な空気は鈍感な朔屋をして羞恥に顔を染めさせた。
　───これで潜水艦が突如また息を吹き返さなんだら、朔屋はハッチを開けて智里に文句を垂れに戻ったかも───いや、そんな面倒な事を朔屋がするはずもないか。
source.english:
At any rate, it took both of them to heave open the heavy steel hatch, squeeze themselves inside, and climb down the ladder—all without managing to find a word for one another.
In that atmosphere, Sakuya remembered Tomosato's instructions; but carrying them out demanded a magnificent degree of brazen shamelessness, and the peculiar air that settled between him and Rui afterward was enough to bring a blush even to insensitive Sakuya's face.
—Had the submarine not abruptly come back to life at that, Sakuya might have opened the hatch and gone back to give Tomosato a piece of his mind—no, as if Sakuya would ever go to so much trouble.

source.japanese:
ともかく、一体どのような原理で作動しているのか相変わらず判らないが、動いてしまえば泪と朔屋にはもうできる事はない。
　二人で暗がりの中にしゃがみこみ、浮上するまで───ひっそりと、交わった。肉の交わりを無上の愉悦とする泪にしては、どこか物哀しさを帯びた、涙を共にするような交わりで。
source.english:
At any rate, how it worked remained unknown, but once it moved, Rui and Sakuya could do no more. Crouched together in the darkness,
until they surfaced, they quietly coupled. For Rui, who found supreme delight in fleshly union, it was a strangely sorrowful joining, as though sharing tears.

source.japanese: ───暗がりのどこかから、聞き覚えのある舌打ちが聞こえたような気がしたけれど、二人は気にせず、行為に没頭した。時を惜しむかのように。洋上に出でて、沙漠もなにも満月のもたらした幻夢と言わんばかりに平然と揺れる、信天翁号の前でハッチを開けるまで、二人はお互いの身に寄り添うてあったが、その後は───
source.english: —It seemed as though a familiar click of the tongue had sounded from somewhere in the darkness, but the two of them paid it no mind and remained absorbed in their actions, as if they were racing against time. They had been clinging to one another until they reached the open sea and opened the hatch in front of the Albatross—which swayed calmly, as if to suggest that the desert and everything else were merely an illusion brought on by the full moon—but after that—

target.text: Regardless, even when they both lifted the heavy steel lid together, climbed inside, then descended the ladder, neither managed to find a single word to speak to the other. Within that atmosphere, Sakuya remembered Tomosato's words, but it required a great deal of brazenness to perform, and even after doing it, the awkward air hanging between himself and Rui left even someone as dull as Sakuya red in the face from shame. ───Had this not suddenly made the submarine spring back to life, Sakuya might have opened the hatch and gone back to complain to Tomosato ───no, could Sakuya really bring himself to go to all that trouble?

At any rate, while they still remained just as ignorant of what exact principles the submarine operated on as before, once it began to move, there was no longer anything that Rui or Sakuya could do about it. The two crouched in the dark, and until they surfaced─── they copulated, quietly. For someone like Rui, who considered carnal coupling to be the greatest bliss, it was somewhat tinged in melancholy, as if sharing in both flesh and tears alike.

───Somewhere from within the dark, it felt like they heard a familiar sound of tongue-clicking, but the two paid it no mind, immersing themselves in the act. As if time was precious. When they arrived back at the surface of the sea, it calmly swayed as if the desert and everything within it had been nothing but an illusion produced by the moon, and until they opened the hatch next to the Albatross, the two of them were nestled close together, but after that───

source.japanese: その後───とある港の波止場で、別れの時を迎える泪と朔屋の姿があった。
source.english: Afterward—At the wharf of a certain port, Rui and Sakuya came to their parting.

target.text: After that───on the wharf of a certain port, there stood Rui and Sakuya, facing the moment of their final parting.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「この船での暮らしは、
　なかなか愉快だったけれど」
source.english:
“Life aboard this ship
was quite amusing.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Life aboard this ship was quite enjoyable.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしが乗っていると、
　どうしてもお父様からの追っ手が掛かって騒々しいでしょう」
source.english:
“But while I'm here,
Father's pursuers inevitably come after us. Such a commotion.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「But for as long as I remain aboard, pursuers sent by my father will inevitably show up and make a commotion.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしのせいで船を沈めるのは、
　少し後味が悪いから」
source.english:
“Sinking the ship because of me would leave
a slightly unpleasant aftertaste.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Were this ship to sink on account of me, it would leave a slightly bitter aftertaste.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「降りるわね、わたくし」
source.english: “I'll disembark.”

source.japanese:
【泪】
「後はこの命、適当に使い切る事にするわ」
source.english: “After that, I'll use up this life as I please.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「And so I am disembarking.」
【Rui】 「As for what is left of this life, I shall simply spend it all aimlessly, however it comes.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「まあ今までもそうしてきたのだし、これからもそうするだけよ」
source.english: “Well, that's what I've always done. I'll simply go on doing it.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Well, I have spent it thus hitherto, and I shall simply also be spending it thus henceforth.」

source.japanese: 色々と泪に想いは残るが、朔屋は結局引き留めきれない……なんで引き留める事ができたろう。
source.english: Many feelings for Rui remained, but in the end Sakuya could not keep her. How could he have kept her?

target.text: Although many feelings for Rui yet remained within him, ultimately, Sakuya was unable to make her stay…… how could he even have done so?

source.japanese:
泪に背を向けた、朔屋の後ろで、水飛沫の響く音。
　振り返れば泪の紺青のドレスばかりが桟橋に残り、波止場の海から外海に向けて、泳ぎ去っていく泪の姿があった。
source.english:
Sakuya turned his back on Rui. Behind him came the sound of splashing water.
When he looked around, only her deep blue dress remained upon the pier. From the harbor toward the open sea, Rui was swimming away.

source.japanese: 人魚の姿で───
source.english: In a mermaid's form.

target.text: He turned his back to Rui, and from behind Sakuya came the sound of splashing water. When he looked back, only Rui's indigo dress remained on the wharf, and he could see Rui's figure swimming away, away from the waters of the wharf and into the distant open sea.
As a mermaid───

source.japanese:
───それは、シサムの、キサラの航海。
　
　
　───あるいは、クロの航海。
　
　
　───もしくは、泪の航海。
source.english:
It is Sisam's voyage. Kisara's.

Or Kuro's voyage.

Or Rui's.

source.japanese:
そして───私の、航海。　
　
　そして───あなたの、航海。
source.english:
And—my voyage.

And—yours.

target.text: ───It was Shisamu's voyage, Kisara's voyage. ───Or else it was Kuro's voyage. ───Or perhaps it was Rui's voyage.
And───it was my voyage. And───it was your voyage.

source.japanese:
信天翁航海録
　
　　　　　その、最後の
　
　　　　　　　これは
　
　　　　　　　　　　最後の物語。
source.english:
The Albatross Logbook

At its very end—

This is

The final story.

target.text: The Albatross log. The very last of its kind. This is the final story.

source.japanese: この世界のどこか、どこかの港、夜闇と霧の二重の帳[とばり]がおおう埠頭の一つに。
source.english: Somewhere in this world, at some port, upon a wharf covered by the double curtain of night and mist.

target.text: Somewhere in this world, in some port somewhere, on a wharf covered by the twin-layered veils of night and mist.

source.japanese: 一目見れば信じがたいほどの、浮かんでいるのが奇跡であるほどの、これが海を往くなど物理法則に反すると言えるほどの、襤褸船が停泊している。もちろん、その船を知っている。名乗るも憚[はばか]られる船乗り達の鼻つまみ者、信天翁号である。
source.english: A wreck so unbelievable at a glance, so miraculous merely in remaining afloat, so plainly in defiance of physical law were she ever to sail the seas, lies moored there. Of course, we know that ship: the Albatross, pariah of sailors everywhere, whose very name they shrink from uttering.

source.japanese:
しかし、今はもう、誰もこの船を見て顔をしかめたり目を背[そむ]けたり忌々しげに唾を吐き捨てたりする者もいない。いるとすれば、何故、こんなガラクタが浮かんでいるのだろうと首を傾げるばかり。それほどに。
　それほどに、この信天翁号は失っていた。その悪名を、その存在感を。
source.english:
Yet now no one looks at her and grimaces, averts their eyes, or spits in disgust. Anyone who notices merely tilts their head, wondering why such junk remains afloat. So much.
So much has the Albatross lost: her notoriety, her presence.

source.japanese: あの後。かの神域で、かの異海での冒険の後。航海士が、船長が、女客が船を離れたのをきっかけとするかのように、信天翁号からは一人、二人と乗り組みがいなくなり、下級水夫達も段々に減っていき、ついには誰もいなくなってしまったのだ。その後信天翁号は沈没したとも亡失したとも噂されていたが、今この港にひっそり停泊してあった。
source.english: Afterward. After the adventures in that divine realm, that alien sea. As though the departure of the navigators, the captain, and the lady passenger had set it off, crew members vanished one by one. The junior sailors gradually dwindled too, until no one remained. Later, the Albatross was rumored sunk, or lost. Yet now she lay quietly in this port.

target.text: There she lay moored, a ship that, at first glance, was so unbelievably ramshackle and shabby that it was a miracle she even floated, that it could even be called a violation of the laws of physics for this thing to sail across the seas. You know that ship, of course. She was the outcast shunned by all sailors, they feared even mentioning her by name: the Albatross.

However, by now, none were left to twist their faces into a grimace, avert their gazes, or spit in resentment upon seeing that ship. Were there any here, they would simply tilt their heads in confusion as they wondered just how that heap of rubbish managed to stay afloat. So far had she fallen. So much had the Albatross lost. Of her infamy, of her presence.

After that happened. After the adventure in a certain sacred realm, in a certain foreign sea. As though the first mates, the captain, and the female passenger leaving the ship had kicked it into motion, the rest of the crew had vanished one after the other from the Albatross; even the deck boys grew fewer in number, bit by bit, until finally, there was no longer anyone left. It was rumoured that the Albatross had later foundered or even vanished, but she was currently moored in this silent, deserted port.

source.japanese: そんな静まり返った信天翁号の舷側にただ一人、佇むは───密航者。
source.english: One figure alone stood by the silent Albatross's side. The stowaway.

source.japanese: 船を操る者とてなく、潮風と夜霧が侘びしく吹き抜けていくのみ。だがそれでも密航者は一人立ち続ける。港より伸びる道の彼方へ目を注いだままで。あるいは誰かを待っているのか？　だとしたら一体誰を？　潮風に髪を遊ばせながら密航者が視線を埠頭へ注ぎ続けるうちに、船着き場を駆けてくるしなやかな影がある。
source.english: No one to handle the ship. Only salt wind and night mist blew through her forlornly. Still the stowaway remained standing, eyes upon the distant road from the harbor. Was she waiting for someone? If so, whom? As the salt wind played in her hair and her gaze rested on the wharf, a supple shadow came running along the landing.

target.text: Standing by the ship's broadside, now still as death, was but a lone figure───the stowaway.

With none to steer the ship, only the salty breeze and night fog blew drearily across. And yet, the stowaway remained standing by her lonesome. Eyes remaining fixed on the road stretching out from the port and into the distant beyond. Or perhaps she was waiting for someone? If that were the case, who in the world could it be? Sea breeze playing in her hair, the stowaway continued to focus her gaze on the wharf, and soon enough, there came a graceful shadow dashing across the port.

source.japanese: 黒く柔らかな鞠が跳ねるが如き、それでいて力強い生き物、宗右衛門猫だ。そのがっしりと逞[たくま]しき顎[あぎと]にくわえこんでいるのは一冊の文庫本。剛力の猫である彼にとっては造作も無き荷物にて、霧をまいて駆け抜け、舷側に垂らされた縄梯子を危うげなく駆け上がり、黒猫は密航者のもとへ。
source.english: Black and soft as a bouncing ball, yet a powerful creature: Soemon the cat. In his strong, sturdy jaws he carried a paperback. No difficult burden for a cat of his strength. Running through the mist, he climbed the rope ladder hanging from the ship's side without a hint of danger and reached the stowaway.

target.text: A creature that resembled a soft, black ball bouncing, yet possessed of great strength: it was Souemon the cat. Carried within his sturdy and powerful jaws was a single paperback. A light burden for a cat of such herculean strength as he, and clad in fog, he sprang across the wharf, effortlessly flew up the rope ladder hanging down the side of the ship, after which the black cat made his way to the stowaway's side.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……お疲れ様、宗右衛門。
　───それで、あの人は見つかった？」
source.english:
“…Good work, Soemon.
Did you find him?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「……Appreciate the effort, Souemon. ───So then, did you find him?」

source.japanese: 黒猫は文庫本を落として毛繕いしながら一声だけ面倒くさそうに鳴いて答える。どうやら問題はないらしい。
source.english: The black cat dropped the paperback and, grooming himself, answered with a single put-upon meow. Apparently there was no problem.

target.text: The black cat dropped the paperback, and while grooming his fur, he answered with a single annoyed cry. It seemed there hadn't been any issues.

source.japanese: 了解し、密航者が頷[うなず]くと、猫の声を肯[うけが]うように、桟橋をどたどたと駆けてくる逞[たく]しい体躯がある。やがて霧の中から現れたのは、信天翁号の水夫長だ。なにやらひどく乱れ、泣き喚いては黒猫に対して悪態を撒き散らしている。
source.english: Understanding, the stowaway nodded. As though confirming the cat's reply, a stout body came pounding down the pier. At last the Albatross's boatswain emerged from the mist. Terribly distraught, he wailed and showered the black cat with abuse.

target.text: When the stowaway gave a nod of understanding, as if in affirmation of the cat's meow, there came a burly body noisily trampling its way down the wharf. Soon enough, who should emerge from the mist but the Bosun of the Albatross. He seemed awfully dishevelled, crying and yelling abuse at a black cat all the while.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「うおおおおんんっ、待てよう、
　この悪魔猫めぇ、ひどいいいい。
　返ちてえええ。
　儂のご本を、取るなああああ……っ」
source.english:
“Waaaaah, wait!
You devil cat, you're cruel!
Give it baaaack!
Don't take my boooook…!”

source.japanese: あの悪魔も退く傲岸と暴戻に部下達を睥睨してきた水夫長がなんの冗談だと唖然とさせるほど、不様にみっともなく泣き崩れ、足下も怪しくつんのめっては転びかけては手を振り回してわあわあと。して水夫長は涙の向こう、桟橋の果てに待ち構えていた船を見て、そしてそれが信天翁号であることを認めて、呆然となる涙と洟[はなみず]まみれ。この筋骨、巌と鉄塊にも勝る男がそれだと滑稽を通り越し哀れですら。
source.english: The boatswain, who had always glared down his subordinates with an arrogance and brutality to make even the Devil recoil, now collapsed into tears so abject, so hideous, that one could only stare and wonder what joke this was—reeling on uncertain feet, pitching forward, nearly falling, flinging his arms about and bawling. Then, through his tears, the boatswain saw the ship waiting at the end of the pier, recognized her as the Albatross, and stood dumbstruck, his face awash in tears and snot. This mass of sinew, this man harder than boulders and iron ingots—reduced to such a state, he passed beyond comedy and became almost pitiable.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「えうううううっ、ア、アルバトロス？
　まさかぁ、で、でも……」
source.english:
“Euuuh… A-Albatross?
Can't be… B-but…”

source.japanese: 予想外であり、同時に半ば予感していたような顔つきだった。
source.english: He looked astonished, yet as though he had half expected it.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……やっぱりだぁ。宗右衛門、見た時から、
　いやァな感じしてたし、ううう」
source.english:
“…Knew it. Had a nasty feeling from the moment I saw Soemon.
Uuuh…”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「WAAAAAAH, WAIT, YOU DAMN DEVIL CAT, HOW COULD YOUUU! GIVE IT BAAAACK! DON'T TAKE MY PRECIOUS BOOOOOK……」

It was a sight that would leave any flabbergasted; that arrogant, tyrannical Bosun, the man who could drive away even the Devil with the scowls he levelled at his subordinates, broke down in tears in a display so pathetically disgraceful it almost seemed like a joke, and with unsteady steps, he pitched forwards, arms flailing around on the verge of falling over. And then, when the Bosun saw the ship that lay in wait for him beyond his tears, and when he then recognized that it was the Albatross, he was left aghast, face drenched in tears and snot.
Coming from a man with muscles and bones stronger than even boulders or lumps of iron, it transcended the comical and became pitiful.
【Bosun】 「EUUUGGH, Al-, Albatross? Impossible, b-, but……」
Judging from his expression, it was unexpected, and yet it was as though he had also half expected it at the same time.
【Bosun】 「……I knew iiiit. Souemon. When I first saw you, I had a really bad feeling, uuuuh!」

source.japanese:
【声】
「いたぞ！　あっちだ！　あそこだぁ！」
source.english: “There he is! That way! Over there!”

target.text: 【Voice】 「There he is! There! Right over there!」

source.japanese: 今にも膝から崩れ落ちそうな水夫長。その背中にまっすぐ向けて、彼が今し方現れ出でた方角、そこには港に連なる町がある、当たり前のように汚くて猥雑で乱暴な船乗り達のための町だ、そこから怒号が漏れ聞こえてくる。
source.english: The boatswain looked ready to crumple at the knees at any moment. And now, aimed squarely at his back, angry shouts came leaking from the direction he had just appeared—from the town adjoining the harbor, a town for sailors and thus, quite naturally, filthy, bawdy, and violent.

target.text: The Bosun's knees could well have given way under him at any moment. From the direction he himself had appeared from just earlier, there was a town connecting to the port, a town built for the sort of sailors who were rowdy, vulgar, and dirty like it came naturally to them, and from there, he could hear angry yelling directed right at his back.

source.japanese: その声を分厚い背中で受け止めた水夫長、顔をしかめて舌打ち一つ。先ほど、黒猫が放り捨てた文庫本を拾い上げる。
source.english: Receiving them against his broad back, the boatswain grimaced and clicked his tongue. He picked up the paperback the black cat had discarded.

target.text: Catching those voices with his bulky back, the Bosun's face twisted into a scowl, and he clicked his tongue. He picked up the paperback the cat had thrown away just earlier.

source.japanese: がくがくと震えながら頁を繰り開いては二・三行読み下し、鼻先を擦りつけて深々と深呼吸、全身を蝕[むしば]む震えがたちどころに弱まっていった様、麻薬中毒者と同じである。しばし恍惚と喘[あえ]いでいたが、再び怒号が、今度は先ほどよりはやや大きく聞こえてきた段に、しっかと文庫本を握りしめ、昇降段に足をかける。
source.english: Trembling violently, he thumbed the book open, read two or three lines, pressed his nose against it, and drew a deep, deep breath; at once, the shaking that gnawed through his entire body began to subside. Exactly like a drug addict. For a while he panted in ecstasy, but when the angry shouts came again, somewhat louder than before, he clutched the paperback tight and planted one foot on the gangway.

target.text: Bones rattling as he trembled, he unfolded the pages and read a few lines of text, rubbed his nose, let out an immensely deep sigh, and the way the shivers racking his entire body instantly subsided was profoundly similar to a junkie. He remained enraptured for a brief time, but when the yelling began again, and this time sounded a little louder than before, he ran up the gangway, paperback clutched tightly in his hand.

source.japanese: 一段、また一段と昇る度、跫音は重みを増していき、丸まっていた背は伸びていく。気のせいだろうか？　体に纏[まと]う肉の量さえ増えていく。すべての段[ステップ]を昇り終え甲板に踏み入ってみれば、そこに佇むのは黒髪の。幾度となく彼がこの甲板から放り出しては現れる、そしてついには水夫長自身がこの船から離れても目の前にまた現れる密航者。たちどころに威圧感を取り戻したはずの顔はげんなりと曇る。
source.english: With each step, his footfalls grew heavier. His rounded back straightened. Was it imagination? Even the flesh upon his body seemed to increase. At the top, he stepped onto the deck, and there stood the black-haired stowaway. The stowaway he had thrown from this deck time and again, only for her to reappear. Now she had reappeared before him even after he himself left the ship. The face that had just recovered its menace clouded with weary dismay.

target.text: Every time he ascended one step and then another, his footsteps grew heavier and his hunched back straightened out. He must have been imagining things, right? Even the amount of meat clinging to his body was increasing. When he had finally ascended the last step and reached the deck, there stood a figure with black hair. She who would appear before him no matter how many times he had tossed her off this deck, and now, here at the end, when even he himself had left the ship, the stowaway appeared before him yet again. His face, which should by all rights have regained its intimidating air, immediately clouded over with weariness.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そして、お前さんか───
　いってえなんのつもりだよ。
　俺もこの呪われた船から、
　ようやくおさらばできたと思ったんだが」
source.english:
“And it's you.
What the hell are you playing
at? Thought I'd finally
said goodbye to this cursed ship.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「And then there's you─── just what the hell are you planning? I thought I had finally, finally seen the last of this accursed ship.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「陸で安泰に暮らすつもりだったんだ。
　それがおめえ、
　いきなりその黒いのが出てきて、
　俺の大ぇ事な本をとっていきくさった！」
source.english:
“Meant to live safely ashore.
Then that black
thing of yours turns up all of a sudden
and steals my precious book!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「I was going to live in peace and quiet ashore. And then, suddenly that black cat appeared, and he was bastard enough to take my precious book with him!」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「……まさかおめえが、
　けしかけたんじゃねえだろうな……？」
source.english:
“…Don't tell
me you set her on me…?”

source.japanese: 凄味をきかせて睨[にら]みつける水夫長に、密航者は平然と答える。
source.english: Under the boatswain's threatening glare, the stowaway answered calmly.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「……Now, surely you didn't set this whole thing in motion, right……?」
Faced with the Bosun's menacing glare, the stowaway answered coolly and without compunction.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だとしたら、どうする？」
source.english: “And if I did?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And if I did, what will you do?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だとしたらっておめえ、
　なにをいけしゃあしゃあと……っ」
source.english:
“If you did? How can you
stand there so brazenly…!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「"If I did", she says. Girlie, how shameless can you……」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だいたい水夫長、あなただって、陸に揚がったって、ろくろく馴染めもしなかった癖に」
source.english: “Besides, Bosun, you barely managed to settle in ashore yourself.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「寝ても覚めても思うのは、この船での暮らし。
　それどころかなにをやっても長続きしない」
source.english:
“Awake or asleep, all you thought of was life aboard this ship.
You couldn't stick with anything you tried.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「But you're one to talk, Bosun, 'cause even after going ashore, you've had a real rough time settling in.」
【Stowaway】 「Awake or asleep, you're always thinking of life on this ship. In fact, no matter what you do with yourself, it won't last long.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「身を持ち崩すばかりで、お大事の本も手放していくしかなくて、それが最後の一冊だったじゃない」
source.english: “You only went to ruin, giving up your treasured books one after another. That was the last one.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「All you do is bring ruin upon yourself, left with no choice but to let go of your precious books. Why, isn't that one the very last volume you own?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そうよ、そうなのあなた達。
　どのみち陸[おか]になんか、
　ううん、この世界のどこにも居場所はないの。
　───この、信天翁号以外には」
source.english:
“Yes.
That's how you all are. In any case, there's no place for you ashore.
No, nowhere in this world.
Except this Albatross.”

source.japanese: きっぱり言い切られて、水夫長は憮然となるも、やがて苦笑した。
source.english: The boatswain looked displeased at her flat declaration. Eventually he gave a rueful smile.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Indeed, that's right, for all of you. In the end, there is no place for you on land. No, anywhere in this whole world. ───Apart from this Albatross.」
Stated so flatly to his face, the Bosun did grow indignant, but in the end, he gave a bitter smile.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「知った風な口をききやがる。
　まあしょうがねえや。
　この港にいられなくなったのは、確かだ」
source.english:
“Talk as if you know everything.
Well, can't help it.
It's true I can't stay in this port now.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You sure yap on like you know everything. But what can you do. I can't stay in this port, that's for damn sure.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「にしたってどうすんだよ。見たところ、この船にゃあ、もう誰もいないみてぇじゃねえか」
source.english: “But what are you going to do? Looks like there's no one left aboard.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「But even if we go with that, what are we supposed to do? Far as I can see, it doesn't look like there's anybody else around on this ship anymore.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「航海士も。船長も。水夫どももなけりゃ。
　乗りこむ客だっていやしねえ。
　船を動かすにゃあ、あのいけ好かない機関長がいるわ。どうすんだよ」
source.english:
“No navigators, no captain, no sailors.
No passengers boarding either.
Need that obnoxious chief engineer to move the ship. What now?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「No first mates. No captain. Not even any sailors. We don't even have any passengers. Only reason the ship could even sail was because that freak of a chief engineer was around. So what are we supposed to do?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そうね。誰もいないわ、今は。
　でもあんたが戻ってきたから、船は少しずつ目覚め始めた───ほら」
source.english:
“Yes. No one's here, for now.
But since you've returned, the ship has begun waking little by little. Look.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「That's true. There's nobody around, for now. But now that you've come back, the ship is beginning to stir from her slumber, little by little ───look.」

source.japanese: 密航者が指差すと、バラックから───それまでは単に廃屋としか思えなかった、信天翁号の上甲板のバラックから、ばらばらとあの下級水夫達が歩み出してくる。皆一様に、今目覚めたばかりと言った感じで、眠たげに目をこすっている。ただその数は、前に比べてずっと少ない。
source.english: Where she pointed, junior sailors came straggling out of the shacks. Until then, the shacks on the Albatross's upper deck had looked like nothing but abandoned houses. Everyone seemed just awakened, rubbing sleepy eyes. But their number was much smaller than before.

target.text: When the stowaway pointed at it, from the shack───from what he'd thought had been but deserted shacks until then, from the shacks on the upper deck of the Albatross, out came those deck boys, one by one from here and there. All as one rubbing at their eyes sleepily, as if to say they had only just awoken. However, compared to before, they were fewer in number by far.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あれ？　また僕らの出番？」
source.english: “Huh? Our turn again?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Huh? We have a part to play again?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「でもみんな、全然揃わないから、僕らもちょっとしかいないよ」
source.english: “But hardly anyone's here. So there are only a few of us too.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「But we're not even close to having everyone here, so there's only a few of us, too.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「という事だけど。
　どうするの？　確かにまだ機関長もいない」
source.english:
“There you have it.
What will you do? The chief engineer certainly isn't here yet.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And there you go. So what do we do? True, we still don't have even the Chief Engineer here either.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「それともこれっぽっちじゃ、流石の龍[ロン]の親爺もお手上げ？」
source.english: “Or is that not enough for even Old Long to work with?”

source.japanese: 挑発するが如く言い放つ密航者をもう一度睨[にら]み据えてから、水夫長は鼻を鳴らす。
source.english: She spoke as though provoking him. The boatswain fixed her with another glare, then snorted.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Or is it that even the great old man Long will strike the colours with only this paltry an amount of men at his disposal?」
After fixing the stowaway, who was practically taunting him to his face, with another mean glare, the Bosun snorted.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ま、これくらいでも船を漕ぎ出すくらいはどうにかなる。でもそれだっていつまでも続かない。
　せめて機関長がいないと駄目だぜ？」
source.english:
“Well, with this many I can at least get the ship out. But it won't last forever.
Need the chief engineer, at a minimum.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Well, even setting out to sea with this number, we'll somehow manage. But that's not going to last forever. We'll need at least the Chief Engineer or this ain't going to work, got it?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「大丈夫。彼の居場所なら把握している。
　ううん、彼だけじゃない。他のみんなも。
　信天翁号のみんなの居場所は、私には判ってる」
source.english:
“No problem. I know where he is. Not only him.
Everyone else too.
I know where everyone from the Albatross is.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「It's okay. I know where he's located. No, it's not just him. It's all the rest too. I know the whereabouts of everybody from the Albatross.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「そうかよ。
　……けっ。薄々感じちゃあいたんだ。
　お前がなんだって、叩き出しても叩き出しても、いつの間にかこの船にまぎれてるのか」
source.english:
“Do you?
Hah. Had a vague feeling.
Why you always turn up somewhere aboard, no matter how many times I throw you out.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「That so? ……Bah. I had a vague suspicion. Just how is it that no matter how many times I kicked you off, again and again, there you'd be, having slipped right back onto this ship without anyone realizing?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「お前はきっと───いや。
　今はそんな事も言ってられねえな」
source.english:
“You must be—No.
Can't talk about that now.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「You must be───nah. Not the time for that.」

source.japanese: 港の向こうの怒声はいよいよ騒がしくなり、どうやらこの信天翁号のことに気づいた御様子だ。水夫長の野太い集合の声に、寝起きの下級水夫達が動き出す。目の前に集まる、まだちと少し気合いの入らぬ寝呆け顔。欠伸をしたり背伸びをしたりする同じ顔の群れに、水夫長の顔にも自然と笑みが浮かぶ。まぁ、ちぃとばかり数が足りん分だけ手間はかかるが、この港から逃げ出すだけなら十分だ。これなら。
source.english: The shouts beyond the harbor grew louder and louder. Apparently their owners had noticed the Albatross. At the boatswain's deep summons, the newly awakened juniors began moving. Sleepy faces gathered before him, still a little short on spirit. A crowd of identical faces, yawning and stretching. Naturally, a smile came to his own face too. Well, the shortage of numbers would mean a little more work. But there were enough to escape this port. With these—

target.text: The angry voices coming from the port were finally growing boisterous, and it appeared they must have noticed this Albatross. Upon hearing the rough, deep voice of the Bosun calling for assembly, the deck boys still getting up were set in motion. They gathered before him, faces still a little drowsy and lacking in spirit. When met with a crowd of similar faces yawning and stretching their backs, a smile naturally formed on even the Bosun's face. Well, given how short-staffed they were, it would take some extra effort, but it was more than enough to get the hell out of this port. This would do.

source.japanese:
眠気覚ましの怒声が響き、下級水夫君達の背が一斉に伸びる。続けざまに飛ぶ出航のための下知に一人二人と散っていく。まるで、そうまるで、体中を駆け回って酸素を届ける赤血球のように。人数が少ないから、かなりの無理を利かせるしかないがそこは長くこの船の水夫長をやっていた彼のこと、どうにかやりくりをつけるだろう。
　信天翁号、再び出港させるために。
source.english:
An angry shout banished sleepiness. Every junior sailor straightened at once. Orders for departure followed in rapid succession, scattering them one by one. Like—yes, like red blood cells racing through a body to deliver oxygen. With so few men, he'd have to push them hard. But after so long as this ship's boatswain, he would manage somehow.
To put the Albatross out to sea again.

target.text: An angry voice rang out to shake off the drowsiness, and the back of every single deck boy stiffened in unison. They rushed away one after another, scattering into groups of one or two to prepare for setting sail as ordered. Almost, yes, almost exactly like red blood cells running about the body transporting oxygen. They were short on hands, and so his only choice was to push things to the limit, but he'd served as the Bosun of this ship for many long years, so he'd surely manage to get by somehow. To ensure that the Albatross would set sail yet again.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それで、行き先はどこだよ」
source.english: “So where are we going?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「So then, where are we heading?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まずは桑港へ。そこに機関長がいる。
　それからは───ま、おいおいにね」
source.english:
“Frisco first. The chief engineer's there.
After that—well, we'll get to that.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「First, we head for San Francisco. That's where the Chief Engineer is. And after that───well, one thing at a time, okay?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ち、仕切ってんじゃねえよただ乗り風情が。
　そのうちきっと、袋叩きにしてやらあ」
source.english:
“Tch. Don't go taking charge, you freeloader.
One day I'll have you beaten black and blue.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Tch, for someone hitching a free ride, you sure talk like you're in charge. One of these days, we're giving you the thrashing of a lifetime.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まあ、その時はその時で、ね」
source.english: “Well, when that day comes, we'll see.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「We'll cross that bridge when we get to it, yeah?」

source.japanese:
……夜風に黒髪を靡[なび]かせる密航者に、水夫長は思い出す。何時かの日。遠い昔。自分がこの船に乗りこむことになったあの夜。目にしていたのだ。
　翼ひるがえす海鳥とも、飛翔する飛び魚ともつかないシルエットを。
　すなわちこの、密航者の後ろ姿を───
source.english:
As the stowaway’s black hair streamed in the night wind, the boatswain remembered. A day once upon a time. Long ago. The night he first came aboard this ship. He had seen it then:
a silhouette impossible to tell whether it belonged to a seabird wheeling on its wings or a flying fish in flight.
That is to say, this very stowaway, seen from behind—

target.text: ……As he looked at the stowaway, her black hair dancing in the night wind, the Bosun remembered. It was some day. In the distant past. That night, when he had ended up boarding this ship. He had seen it. A silhouette, one that he could not pin down as neither a seabird flapping its wings nor a soaring flying fish. In other words, it had been the sight of this very stowaway's figure from behind───

source.japanese: そしてこれより、信天翁号はかつての乗組員達を取り戻す航海に出る事になる。
source.english: And so the Albatross would now set out on a voyage to recover her former crew.

target.text: Thus, thenceforth, the Albatross set out to sea on a voyage to recover her former crew.

source.japanese:
そして一方、朔屋直正。
　一体何故、この異様な船と奇怪な船乗り達の物語の中で主人公にあるのかわからないほどの駄目人間。
source.english:
And meanwhile, Naomasa Sakuya.

A man so thoroughly useless that his place as protagonist in this story of a bizarre ship and her outlandish sailors defies explanation.

source.japanese: 彼はずっと後悔していた。自分の選択が彼女達を哀しい目に遭わせる事になってしまったのではないか、と。それがために朔屋の鬱はいよいよひどくなり勝り、遂にある日、鬱心のままに身投げ、あるいは嵐に巻きこまれるなどして、いなくなってしまった。その後の消息は杳[よう]として知れず───
source.english: He had been regretting it all along. Had his choices brought sorrow upon those women? His depression deepened until, one day, he disappeared—throwing himself overboard in despair, perhaps, or getting caught in a storm. Nothing more was heard of him—

source.japanese:
いや。
　そんな朔屋だったが、彼は死んではいなかった。どっこい生きていた。で、今彼はどこにいるかというと。
source.english:
No.

For all that, Sakuya was not dead. Very much alive, in fact. And where might he be now?

target.text: And then, meanwhile, there was Sakuya Naomasa. Such a hopelessly pathetic excuse of a human being that one is left to wonder just why in the world he was ever chosen to serve as the protagonist of the tale of this bizarre ship and her stranger crew.

He had regretted it ever since. Had it not been his own choices that were to blame for those girls meeting with their miserable fates? And that had served as the catalyst driving Sakuya into an ever deeper depression, until finally, a certain day, caught in the throes of his spiralling depression, he had thrown himself overboard, or he'd been caught up in some storm at some point, then vanished. There had been no news of his whereabouts ever since───
No. That was the sort of man Sakuya was, but dead he was not. He was still alive, somewhere. So then, the question becomes: just where was he?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あはははははははははっ」
source.english: “Ahahahahahahahahaha!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーははっはゎっ、はっはっはっはっゎっは」
source.english: “Aahahaha—hah, hahahahaha—haha!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あーはは、あーは、あー、はー、
　うー、うぅ」
source.english:
“Aahaha, aaha, aah, haa…
Uuh, uuuh.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……死にたい。もう死んでしまいたい」
source.english: “…I want to die. I just want to die.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「AHAHAHAHAHAHAHA!」
【Naomasa】 「AAAH-HA-HA HAWAH, HA HA HA HA WAH-HAH!」
【Naomasa】 「AAAH-HAHA, aaahah, aah, haah, uuh, uuugh.」
【Naomasa】 「……I want to die. I wish I were just in a grave already.」

source.japanese: 一見するや、どこまで鬱陶しいことこの上ない、蛞蝓かいやさ草履虫、そのくらいまで己を沈み込ませた手前勝手な鬱状態、かに思えたが。
source.english: At first glance, this looked like an exceptionally tiresome bout of self-indulgent depression. He had sunk to the level of a slug—no, a paramecium. Or so one might have thought.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「バーで一番たけえ酒の海に溺れて死にたい。女の腹の中に出し尽くして死にたい」
source.english: “I want to drown in an ocean of the most expensive booze in the bar. I want to empty myself into a woman and die.”

source.japanese: なんてことはない、いつもながらの朔屋である。
source.english: Nothing of the sort. This was merely Sakuya being Sakuya.

target.text: At first glance, there seemed not a sight more depressing in the whole world; was he a slug, or rather, a paramecium? So deeply had he sunk into his egocentric depressive state; so it seemed, at least, however.
【Naomasa】 「I want to drown to death in an ocean of the most expensive liquor in a bar. I want to shoot every last drop I have inside a woman's stomach and perish.」
It was nothing, really; it was just the regular old Sakuya.

source.japanese:
ふと見渡せば、ここは信天翁号の船倉である。
　相も変わらず雑多に物が詰め込まれというより、次から次に放り込まれてできあがった迷宮。固定も疎[おろそ]かに、船が波を越える度にあちらこちらで床と木箱がこすれ合い、数寸単位で模様替え。おかげで船賃払わぬただ乗り客と船につきものの鼠しかして人間大というよりそのものの二人が身を潜[ひそ]めることもできようというわけだが。
source.english:
A glance around showed that they were in the Albatross's hold.

As ever, a labyrinth of miscellaneous cargo—crammed in, or rather built up by throwing one thing after another into it. Little was properly secured. Each time the ship crossed a wave, wooden crates scraped along the floor, rearranging the place a few inches at a time. Which did make it possible for a pair of fare-dodgers to hide: the ship's resident rats, though human-sized—or, to be precise, human.

source.japanese:
しかして朔屋は、なぜここにいるのか、この船にいるのか。
　それは、朔屋自身すらはっきりと憶えていない。どのようにして自分が再び信天翁号に辿り着いたのか、定かではない。海上を漂流していたように思う。けして沈むことのない、一本の望遠鏡に支えられて。漂流した果てに、死にきることもできず、拾い上げられたのがまた信天翁号だったというのは、どんな呪われた運命なのか。朔屋は己の不甲斐なさを嘆き、掬いあげられた時のままに、この密航者の隠れ家に引き籠もっている。
source.english:
But why was Sakuya here? Why aboard this ship?

Even he could not clearly remember. How he had found his way back to the Albatross was uncertain. He thought he had been adrift at sea, supported by a telescope that would never sink. After all that drifting, unable even to die, he had been picked up by the Albatross again. What kind of accursed destiny was that? Lamenting his own worthlessness, Sakuya had stayed holed up in the stowaway's hideout ever since his rescue.

source.japanese: そして隣の密航者。下らぬことをほたえつつゴロゴロと場所を食う居候、まぁそもそも彼女自身がこの船の居候なのだがそれはそれとして、をうち眺めて息をつく。
source.english: And beside him, the stowaway. She watched her lodger rolling about, making a fuss over nonsense and taking up space, and sighed. She was herself a lodger aboard this ship, of course, but that was beside the point.

target.text: Were one to take another look around the scene, where should this turn out to be but the hold of the Albatross. As ever, it was less a miscellaneous assortment of goods crammed inside and instead more like a labyrinth that had formed as things were tossed inside one after the other. They had also been remiss in securing the cargo, so whenever the ship crossed a wave, the boxes would slide across the floor and scrape against each other, resulting in a redecoration that could be measured in several inches.

Thanks to this, it would appear that these two───one a stowaway who pays no fare, the other a rat of the sort that inevitably accompanies a ship─── would also be able to hide themselves here, and yet not just as their human-sized selves, but rather as even the very embodiment of those concepts, or so things stood.
And now, why was Sakuya here? Why was he on this ship?

That was something even Sakuya himself couldn't recall clearly. How exactly had he made his way back aboard the Albatross once more? It remained uncertain. He had been adrift atop the sea or something of the sort, he thought. He never went down below the waves, sustained by a single telescope. At the end of his drifting, unable to even die, he had been picked up by some vessel, and which vessel should that turn out to be but the Albatross yet again; just how cursed a fate was he doomed to live? Sakuya lamented his own pathetic spinelessness, and ever since he'd been scooped up, he'd confined himself within this little hideaway belonging to the stowaway.

And then there was the stowaway by his side. As she gazed upon this sponger lazily clowning around with his worthless nonsense while encroaching upon her space, well, setting aside whether the woman herself was a sponger on this ship for now, she took a deep breath.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「よかった。それでもいつもの直正だ。
　お酒の高い安いなら、ここには安いのしかないけれど、女だったら滅多にないのがいるわ」
source.english:
“That’s good. You’re still the Naomasa I know.
As for whether the sake is expensive or cheap, there’s nothing but cheap stuff here, but when it comes to women, there’s one you don’t find every day.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どこに？」
source.english: “Where?”

source.japanese: どんよりとした目を向けられて、胸を張る。
source.english: She stood there, chest puffed out, those gloomy eyes fixed on her.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Thank goodness. Despite it all, you're still the same old Naomasa. When it comes to alcohol, there's only cheap swill around here, but when it comes to women, there's a real one-of-a-kind.」
【Naomasa】 「Where?」
Leaden-eyed, when he looked at her, she puffed out her chest.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ここに。この私。
　いえ、本当に余りいないタイプだと思う。
　なんでって？」
source.english:
“Here. Me.
No, I really think I’m a rare type.
Why, you ask?”

source.japanese: 我が胸指し示し、聞かれもせずに答える。
source.english: She pointed at her chest and blurted out the answer before anyone even asked.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Right here. None other than me myself. No, really, I think women like myself are very few and far between. And as for why?」
Pointing a finger at her own chest, she gave an answer without being asked.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だって私───地球の出身だから」
source.english: “Because I'm—from Earth.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……なに言ってんだかさっぱりわからん」
source.english: “…I haven't got a clue what you're talking about.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ？　ちきゅう？　それはどこの国だ？　どこの港だ？　そもそも今、どこにいるんだ、この船は。海の上だってことはわかってるけどさ。そんな状況で……あんたの郷里のことなど知ったことか」
source.english: “Huh? Earth? What country is that? What port? Where is this ship, anyway? I know we're at sea. Under the circumstances…why should I give a damn about where you're from?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Because I─── am from the planet Earth.」
【Naomasa】 「……I have absolutely no clue what you're talking about.」

【Naomasa】 「Huh? Earth? Is that a country somewhere? A port somewhere? To begin with, where are we even, on this ship? I know we're at sea somewhere, but, you know. In the situation I'm in…… do you really think I give a shit about your hometown?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そっかな……結構勇気を出して、正体明かしたつもりだったのに」
source.english: “Really…? I thought I'd worked up quite a bit of courage to reveal who I really am.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Is that so……and here I was, really trying to muster up my courage to reveal my true identity.」

source.japanese: ぞんざいな朔屋の反応に、憮然と口を尖らせる密航者。彼女の言う勇気がどれほどのものかはわからないが、朔屋にとっては前言通りにどうでもよく、
source.english: The stowaway pouted at Sakuya's offhand response. How much courage she meant was anyone's guess, but Sakuya, as he had just said, could not care less.

target.text: Met with Sakuya's dismissive response, the stowaway pursed her lips in dejection. While he wasn't sure just exactly what kind of bravery it had taken, just as he'd said before, it really didn't matter to Sakuya,

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あー、はー、うー、うぅ」
source.english: “Aah, haa, uuh, uuuh.”

source.japanese: と、また床と戯れ出す。
source.english: And he went back to making friends with the floor.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Aah, haaah, uuuh, uuh.」
And with that, he began messing around on the floor again.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「今どこだ、ここはどこの海の上だ。そもそもなんで俺はまたこの船にいるんだよう……」
source.english: “Where are we? What sea is this? Why am I even on this ship again…?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Where am I right now, what ocean are we in. Actually, before any of that, why am I even on this ship again……」

source.japanese: この男が今少し、頭の回る状況だったら、いや、回る人間だったら、すでに動き出した信天翁号において、下っ端もいいとこの朔屋が水夫長にもどやされず、下級水夫達にも捜し回られずにここで芋虫の真似事をしていられる矛盾に気付いただろう。洋上漂う朔屋をこの船に引き揚げたのは誰か？　他の誰にも知られずにここまで連れてきたのは誰か？　他に誰もいるまい、隣にいる密航者以外には。
source.english: Had the man been in a state to use his head a little—or been capable of using it—he would have noticed something odd. The Albatross was already under way. How could Sakuya, the lowest of the low, lie here impersonating a caterpillar without the boatswain bawling him out or the junior sailors hunting him down? Who had hauled him aboard from the open sea? Who had brought him here without anyone else knowing? There was only one possibility: the stowaway beside him.

source.japanese: しかし、朔屋はどうにもそのことには思い至らず、今度は膝抱えて座り直し、ぼんやりと視線は斜め上、さまよう思いは変転流転で自業自得な身の上だ。
source.english: But none of this occurred to Sakuya. Now he sat up and hugged his knees, staring vaguely upward, his thoughts wandering through the twists and turns of a life whose troubles were entirely his own doing.

target.text: Had this man been in a state where his head was working well, even just a little, no, had he been a man whose head had ever worked well, he would surely have noticed the contradiction of how, despite the Albatross already being at sea, Sakuya, a lowly grunt at the best of times, had yet to be scolded by the Bosun, and no deck boys had been sent out to search for him, instead allowing him to lay here and imitate a caterpillar. Just who was it that had dragged Sakuya up on this ship as he drifted across the sea? Just who had then dragged him all the way down here without anyone the wiser? It couldn't have been anyone else, none but the stowaway currently by his side.

However, Sakuya simply wasn't able to realize that, and this time, he corrected his sitting posture and hugged his knees, his gaze absentmindedly directed diagonally upwards, his wandering thoughts fickle and ever-changing, a destiny wrought by reaping what he himself had sowed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はああ～、なんだってまた、俺はこの船に関わっちまったんだよう……」
source.english: “Haaah…why did I ever get mixed up with this ship again…?”

source.japanese:
なんだって？　なんだってまた？
　自堕落のままに生家から学校から追い出された。それでも船乗りなんぞになる気はなかった。ではいったい、どこで、この身は誤ったのか。
　そうだ、あの夜だ。港町の酒場で同じ顔した双子の美女に酔い潰されて、拉致同然に港に泊まったこの船に───
　いや、ちがう、そこではない。
　あの日、いつとは言えぬあの日。
　そこで、どことは言えぬその町で。
　宵闇が溶け出し、喧噪が溢れ出す雑踏の中で。
source.english:
Why? Why again?

His dissolute ways had got him kicked out of his family home and his school. Even so, he had never meant to become a sailor. Where, then, had he gone wrong?

That was it. That night. In a bar in a port town, two identical beauties had drunk him under the table and all but abducted him to this ship, moored in the harbor—

No. Not there.

That day. No saying when.

There, in that town. No saying where.

In a crowd where dusk was beginning to melt and the clamor was spilling out.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Haaa～, why, just why did I have to end up getting involved with this ship again……」

Ah, not this time. There are no choices. There is only one thing left to choose.

source.japanese:
さぁ、朔屋よ、その手を取るのだ。そして、ここから出よう。船底の穴蔵から。甲板に出よう。
　航海を始めるのだ！
source.english:
Come, Sakuya. Take her hand. Let's get out of here. Out of this hole in the bottom of the ship. Onto the deck.

Begin the voyage!

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Now, let us go meet them. For I am also still in need of them. To see through my own voyage.」

He looked at the palm before his eyes, then at the face belonging to its owner. He couldn't grasp the intentions of the girl who had said those words. Why had she said that, and why had she invited him along? Sakuya couldn't understand.
However. They all overlapped, layered atop one another. The hands held out towards him. Those questions.

Back then. And back then. And back then, too. Had they not desired an answer from Sakuya, had hands not been held out towards him? Sakuya had simply never taken those hands in his, that was all, but they certainly had been held out towards him, had they not?

Now, Sakuya. What will you do this time? Will you once more lose your nerve, turn your back on them? Or else? Yes, this time you will not. There is no alternative. Right now, there is but one thing you can choose.
Now, O Sakuya, take that hand in yours. And then leave this place. Step out of this cave in the ship's hold. Step out on the deck. Set out on your voyage!

source.japanese:
そこは、氷雪吹き荒ぶ極北の平原。
　極点と呼び慣わされたそこに、絶えず氷点下の風が吹き見上げれば見えるのは空覆い尽くす雲と舞う雪の白い斑点ばかりのその平原の真ん中に、木造小屋といえば聞こえばかりはいい掘っ立て小屋、どこか懐かしいと思うのは、かつて乗り組んだ船の甲板一杯狭しと立ち並んでいたあのバラックどもを思い出すからか。
source.english:
That was the far-northern plain, scourged by ice and snow.

There, in the place customarily known as the Pole, where a wind below freezing blew without cease and, looking up, one saw nothing but clouds swallowing the whole sky and the white flecks of dancing snow—there, in the middle of that plain, stood what one might flatteringly call a wooden cabin, though it was no more than a shack; and if the thing felt somehow familiar, perhaps it was because it recalled those barracks that had once stood packed tight across every inch of the deck of the ship they had served aboard.

target.text: It was a vast tundra of the northernmost reaches where fierce blizzards raged. There, in the place commonly known as the North Pole, where the freezing winds never cease to blow, where if one were to look up, all one would see was the heavens covered in clouds and dancing, white specks of snow, right in the middle of that field stood what, if one was being generous, could be called a log house, but in reality was but a dreary shack, and something about it was familiar, nostalgic, perhaps because it evoked images of those cramped clusters of shacks that had filled the deck of that ship whose crew they'd formerly been part of?

source.japanese: そこに、シサムとキサラ、双子の航海士はただ漫然と時を過ごしていた。住んでいた暮らしていたとは言えまい。彼女達二人は日々の糧を得るための努力を何一つしていないのだから。食料はある。贅沢はできなくとも、不足はない。ただしそれは、二人にここに留まるよう伝えたあの者どもが運んでくるからだ。彼らはただ、彼女達に時が来るまで待てとしか言わない。それに従って双子はここに留まっているのだ。そう決めたのだから。縋るあの男を振り払った時に。
source.english: Here Sisam and Kisara, the twin navigators, idled their time away. One could hardly call it living, making a life. Neither lifted a finger to earn her daily bread. There was food. No luxury, but no shortage. It was brought by those who had told them to remain here. Wait until the time comes: that was all those people said. And the twins obeyed, staying here. They had decided to. When they shook off the man who clung to them.

source.japanese: だから二人は留まり続ける。今日も今日とて顔突き合わせて。
source.english: So they stayed. Today, as ever, facing one another.

target.text: And there, Shisamu and Kisara, the twin first mates, spent their days in an entirely desultory fashion. What they did could not be described as inhabiting the place or living there. For the two women did not spend a single shred of their own effort to earn their daily bread. They had food. Though they could not lavishly indulge, it wasn't lacking. However, it was only here because it had been brought by those people who had instructed them to remain in this place. All they had told the women was to wait here until the right time comes. And in accordance with that, the twins had remained here. Because that is what they had decided. Back when they had shaken off that man clinging to them.
Therefore, the two of them continued to stay. Today, the same as ever, they stood face to face.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「……そんな辛気くさい顔、しないでよ」
source.english: “…Don't look so miserable.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「……Get that grim look off your face, please.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「まあ、鏡を見ているようなもんだと思って、諦めて」
source.english: “Well, think of it as looking in a mirror. You'll just have to live with it.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Just give it up, think of it like looking into a mirror or something.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ちぇー。やっぱ失敗だったかなあ」
source.english: “Tch. Maybe we made a mistake after all.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Tsk. Guess this really was a big mistake after all, huh.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「でも仕方ないよ。
　どっちにしろ、もう取り返しの付かないことだし」
source.english:
“But what can we do?
Either way, it's too late to take it back.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「But there's nothing we can do. Whatever we choose, we can't ever hope to make up for what happened anymore.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「まあ、ね」
source.english: “Well, yeah.”

source.japanese:
揃って溜息をつくタイミングは刹那も乱れず、双子の形ばかりは豊かで、でも今は空虚な胸に去来するのは、あの航海の日々。この世で一番の襤褸船に乗り組んで海を渡っていた日々。そう、何をさせても駄目で駄目だったあの男もいた日々。何度ブン殴られても罵られてものろのろと立ち上がり、二人の前でへらへら笑ってぐずぐずと泣いていた男。
　それがついには、二人揃って肌も重ねて離れがたく、この氷原まで連れ回し運命の前に涙の別れ？　そしてこうして今もふとした弾みにもぽつねんと思い起こされるとあっては、情絆されるにもほどがある。
source.english:
Their sighs coincided to the instant. Through hearts now empty, for all the fullness of their breasts, passed the days of their voyage. Days crossing the sea aboard the most decrepit ship in the world. Yes, days with that man who was useless at everything. However often they hit him or cursed him, he would slowly get up again, grinning foolishly or sniveling before them.

And in the end they had both slept with him, grown inseparable from him, dragged him all the way across these ice fields, then parted in tears before their destiny? And now he came back to them in stray, lonely moments. There were limits to how badly one ought to be ensnared by affection.

source.japanese: そうして、双子は今日もここに留まり続けているのだった。また顔見合わせて、溜息をつきながら。
source.english: And so the twins remained here today too, looking at one another and sighing again.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Yeah, I guess.」

The timing of their joint sighs wasn't off by even a fraction of a split second; in their capacity as twins alone, they were still ample, but what now came and went through their hollow bosoms were the recurring thoughts of those days at sea. The days they had spent crossing the seas as members of the crew of the most ramshackle ship in this world. Yes, the days where that man, useless and hopeless no matter what one put him to, was also there with them. That man, he who would always get back on his feet no matter how many times he'd been socked in the face or verbally abused, who would flippantly laugh and snivel and weep before them.

And finally, they had both become intimate with him, skin held against warm skin, reluctant to part; they had dragged him all the way to this field of ice, then held a tearful parting in the face of destiny. And even now, standing by their lonesome, they would be reminded of him even by the most unexpected of impulses; there had to be a limit to how bound by affection one could be.
Thus, today was yet another day where the twins elected to continue to stay here. They looked each other in the eyes again, sighing deeply all the while.

source.japanese: 目の前の光景に、息呑むタイミングはぴたりと合っていたという。
source.english: They are said to have gasped at the sight before them in perfect unison.

source.japanese:
シサムとキサラ、今二人は尋常ならざる光景の前にいた。
　事の始まりは退屈だった。退屈に過ぎたのだ、氷原に留まる事は二人にとって。
　だから二人は紛らわせに氷原を彷徨った。良く言い換えれば探検に赴いたのだ。いいではないか、逃げ出すのでなければ散歩くらい。
　そして、二人はここに踏み込んだ。ここ、とは。氷原に裂く亀裂、クレバスだ。それもただのものではない。岩山のようにせり上がった巨大な氷の塊が、真っ二つに裂けている。氷の谷底が二人の前に顔を出していたのだ。
　それまで二人は、そこにクレバスがあることなど知らなかった。いや、気付かなかった。『散歩』は今日が初めてではない。小屋の周囲は何度となく歩き回っている。しかし、ここにこんなものがあるとは知らなかった！
source.english:
Sisam and Kisara now stood before something extraordinary.

It had begun with boredom. Staying on the ice fields was far too dull for them.

To relieve it, they had wandered out—or, to put it more favorably, gone exploring. Surely a walk was allowed, so long as they were not running away.

And they had entered this place. What place? A rift in the ice: a crevasse. No ordinary one, either. A vast mass of ice, thrust up like a rocky mountain, had split clean in two. The bottom of an icy valley lay exposed before them.

Until then they had not known the crevasse was there. No, had not noticed it. This was hardly their first ‘walk.’ They had roamed around the shack time and again. Yet they had never known anything like this was here!

target.text: Even the timing of their breath being taken from them at the sight unfolding before their eyes was perfect.

Shisamu and Kisara were currently faced with an anomalous sight. It all began with boredom. It was much too boring. Remaining still in this frozen waste, that is, for the two of them. And so they wandered out onto the icy field to divert their minds from that boredom. Expressed in nicer words, they sallied forth on an adventure. It was fine, was it not? It wasn't as though they were running away, they were simply heading for a walk.

And then the two ventured into this place. This place. A crack that rendered the ice asunder, a crevice. And it was no ordinary crevice at that. A gargantuan mass of ice jutting up from below like a rocky mountain had been split clean in two. The bottom of the icy chasm was revealing itself right before their eyes. Until now, the two had never know there to be a crevice in this place. No, they simply hadn't noticed. For was today not the very first time they had gone for a "walk"? They'd wandered around their dwelling countless times over. Still, they never knew that anything like this existed here!

source.japanese: 当然、二人はその中へと踏み込んだ。氷原に口を開けたものなら避けるしかないが、裂け目が天で底が目の前にあるのなら苦労はない。なにしろ退屈だったのだから。ロクな装備も持たずに。暇つぶしの散歩にそんなものを持ち歩くはずもない、そもそもそんな物は小屋にない。だが双子はそんなことは意に介さず、進んでいった、奥へ奥へと。そして───
source.english: Naturally, they ventured in. Had it been a hole yawning open in the ice field, there would have been nothing for it but to keep away; but with the opening to the sky and the floor laid out before them, there was no trouble at all. Besides, they were bored out of their minds. In they went without a scrap of decent equipment. Who brought such things on a stroll undertaken to kill time? For that matter, the shack contained no such things to bring. The twins paid none of this the slightest mind, but pressed on, deeper and deeper. And then—

source.japanese:
それを見たのだ。
　それは氷の中にいた。壁一面を覆う氷、氷壁の中に。
　初めは気付かなかった。二人とも。何故か、それがあまりにも巨大だったため。そこにいることすら気付けなかったのだ。しかし、気付いてしまった、二人同時に、右と左の氷壁にいるものに。
　氷の中、佇む白面茫洋たる巨大な姿───
source.english:
They saw it.

It was there inside the ice. Inside the wall of ice—the ice sheathing the entire face of the wall.

At first neither of them noticed. Why? Because it was too enormous. So enormous they had failed to perceive that anything was there at all. But now they saw them, both at the same instant: the things within the walls of ice to right and left.

Standing in the ice, those vast, white, vacant figures—

target.text: Naturally, the two stepped into the depths. If a gap opens in an ice field, you are left with no choice but to avoid it, but with the opening of the rift itself being near the heavens and the bottom right before their eyes, it was no hassle. And most of all, they were bored. And they had no decent equipment. And there was no way they'd bring something like that with them on a leisurely stroll, and there was nothing of the sort in their shack to begin with. Therefore, the twins paid such things no heed and advanced, deeper and deeper. And then───

They saw it. It was inside the ice. Covered in a wall of ice, inside that wall of ice. At first, they didn't notice what it was. Neither of them. The reason being, it was simply too titanic in size. They didn't even notice it was there at all. However, they did end up realizing it, both of them at the same time, what was within the wall of ice to both their right and left. Within the ice stood a boundlessly vast titan of purest white───

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんで……ウミヒトがこんなところに……」
source.english: “Why…are there Sea People here…?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Why……is there an Umihito in a place like this……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「知るもんかい。でもシサム、
　これ、なんか厭[いや]だ。
　こいつら、厭だ。
　出ようよ早く、こんなとこ」
source.english:
“How should I know? But Sisam,
I don't like this.
I don't like these things.
Let's get out of here. Now.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「How should I know? But, Shisamu, I don't really like this. I don't like these things. Let's get out of here, quick, hurry!」

source.japanese:
二人の頬を汗が伝う。
　異様な光景の前に、二人の鼓動は増すばかり。血の巡りが速まれば自然と体温も上がる。想像の及びもつかない光景を前にした息苦しさも手伝って、二人は知らず上着を脱ぐ。重く分厚い防寒着。たちまち冷気がリーファージャケットとすり抜けて来るが、今の二人にはかえってありがたかった。
source.english:
Sweat ran down their cheeks.

Before that unearthly sight their hearts beat faster and faster. As the blood raced, so, naturally, their body heat rose. The impossible spectacle left them short of breath as well, and before they knew it they had stripped off their outer layers—their heavy, ponderous winter gear. The cold at once slipped through their reefer jackets, but just then it came as a blessing.

target.text: Sweat rolled down their cheeks. Faced with this bizarre sight, the pace of their throbbing hearts accelerated. As the circulation of their blood quickened, so did their body temperature naturally rise. The oppressive, suffocating feeling of standing before this incomprehensible view also contributed, and they both unconsciously removed their jackets. Their heavy, thick winter clothes. The chill in the air instantly pierced their reefer jackets, but in this moment, the two were only grateful for its arrival.

source.japanese:
呆然とする二人、その眼前に立つヒトガタと呼ばれるモノ。
　白く、巨大な、目も鼻もない、のっぺりとした顔と肌───そう、ないのだ。目と認識できるものは。頭のようだとかろうじて認められるもの以外は。
　しかし、そこが。まるで。
　自分達が安住するねぐらに踏み入ってきた者を。
　一瞥するかの様に。わずかに。
　視線を向けたように見えた。
source.english:
The stunned pair faced the things called Hitogata.

White, enormous, with featureless faces and skin—no eyes, no noses. Yes: nothing one could recognize as eyes. Only something that could just barely be recognized as a head.

And yet that part—

As though glancing at the intruders who had entered their peaceful lair—

Seemed, ever so slightly,

To turn its gaze toward them.

target.text: The two stood in blank amazement, and before their eyes stood that which was known as the "Hitogata". White, titanic, with no nose or eyes, a flat, featureless face, and smooth skin───indeed, there was nothing. Nothing that could be identified as eyes. Only something that could barely be recognized as a head. (TN: The "南極のニンゲン", lit. "Antarctic human", is an urban legend about cryptids originating from the occult board on 2chan. The type that appears in the Arctic is known as "Hitogata", while the type that appears near Antarctica is the "Ningen".)
However, it was. Almost as though. It seemed to throw a glance. Only a fleeting one. At those who had dared enter the lair wherein it found repose. It was as though it were looking right at them.

source.japanese: 二人は瞬時に我に返った。
source.english: Both came to their senses instantly.

target.text: The two came to their senses in an instant.

source.japanese: ───地が、揺れたのだ。
source.english: —The ground had shaken.

source.japanese:
地が揺れる？　そんな馬鹿な。この世に大地が揺れることなどありはしない！
　しかし、揺れた。気のせいかとも思えた、ヒトガタのわずかな身じろぎで。立つのも困難なほどに地が揺れたのだ。双子の立つ足下が。
source.english:
The ground, shake? Absurd. In this world, the earth never shook!

But it had. At a movement of the Hitogata so slight they might have imagined it, the ground had shaken hard enough to make standing difficult. The ground beneath the twins.

source.japanese: これが海の上、船の甲板でなら、どんな波にも揺らぐことなく仁王立ちできる二人だが、今ばかりは違った。跳ね上がらんばかりの揺れに、体投げ出され転がるのを防ぐのが精一杯、生まれたばかりの牛か馬が力入らぬ足を必死に突っ張って震えているよう、いや震えているのは足下なのだが。
source.english: At sea, on a ship's deck, they could stand firm against any wave. Now it was different. The ground jolted as though it would leap upward. Keeping themselves from being flung down and rolling away was all they could do. Like newborn calves or foals, they strained to brace their powerless, trembling legs—though it was the ground beneath them that trembled.

target.text: ───For the earth shook.

The earth shook? What nonsense. The earth had never quaked in this world before! However, it still shook. It seemed almost like a trick of the mind, how the Hitogata faintly stirred. Oh, how the earth shook, just remaining on their feet was a struggle. How the ice beneath their feet trembled.

Had they stood upon the seas, upon the deck of a ship, they would strike a dauntless pose, unflinching in the face of whatever waves may come, but it was a very different story in this moment. The ground heaved and shook as though every tremor would send them flying into the air, and keeping themselves from being thrown around or to the ground took everything they had; they trembled like the feeble legs of a newborn calf or foal desperately braced against the ground, or rather, it was the ice beneath their feet that shook.

source.japanese: そして、このヒトガタの身じろぎは二人にさらなる驚愕を打ちつける。
source.english: And that movement of the Hitogata dealt them another shock.

target.text: And then, the stirring of the Hitogata drove yet more spikes of shock into their minds.

source.japanese:
裂けたのだ、この谷底が。
　谷底の底にさらなる谷底が口を開けたのだ。そう、ちょうど二人の真ん中で。
　見る間に新たに生まれた亀裂はその口を大きく開けていく。深く、そして何より広く。そう、二人の真ん中で。この亀裂に悪意があるのか、いやきっとあるに違いない、双子は同時に悲鳴を上げる。二人の距離がどんどんと離れていく。二人の頭の中で、恐怖と狂気が迫り上がる。
source.english:
The bottom of the valley split.

Beneath its bottom, another valley opened its mouth. Right between them.

Before their eyes, the newborn crack gaped wider. Deep, and above all wide. Right between them. Did this crack bear them malice? Surely it must. The twins screamed together. The distance between them kept growing. Terror and madness rose within their heads.

target.text: It was splitting: this ravine floor. In the bottom of its bottom, a mouth leading to a yet deeper valley was opening. Yes, exactly between the two of them. Before their eyes, the newly formed rift expanded into a great opening. Deep, and above all, vast. Yes, right between where the two of them stood. Was there malicious intent behind this crack, no, there had to be, it was beyond a shadow of a doubt, and the twins both let out a scream in unison. The distance between them grew larger and larger, and within their heads, terror and madness surged forth.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ちょっとやだシサムッ!?
　どうにかして飛んでよ、
　じゃないとあたしら、離れ離れに……っ」
source.english:
“No, no, Sisam!?
You've got to jump somehow!
Otherwise we'll be split up…!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「This isn't good, Shisamu!? Jump over to me, somehow, because if you don't, we'll be torn apart……!」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「わかってるけど……
　なにかロープとかない!?」
source.english:
“I know, but…
Isn't there a rope or something!?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Yeah, I know that, but…… do we have a rope or something!?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「そんな都合の良いものがそうそう……っ」
source.english: “We can't just expect something that convenient…!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Life's never that convenient……」

source.japanese: 慌てふためき辺りを見回す二人。しかし、何も持たずにここまで来たのだ。先ほど脱ぎ捨てた防寒具すら、もう呑みこまれている。ロープだと？　そんな都合の良いものなど───
source.english: Frantic, they looked around. But they had come here empty-handed. Even the winter coats they had just discarded had been swallowed up. A rope? Something that convenient—

target.text: Falling into a panic, the two surveyed their surroundings. However, they had come here with nothing on their persons. Even the winter gear they'd discarded just earlier had already been swallowed up. A rope? There was no way they'd have something that convenient just lying───

source.japanese:
【？？？】
「あるんだなそれが、ここに、あるよ！」
source.english: “As it happens, there is! Right here!”

target.text: 【???】 「We've got one! There's a rope right here!」

source.japanese: 揺れる地をものともせずに一人、黒髪を翼のようにはためかせ、なるほどこの羽ならここまで飛んできたのもうなずけると思えるほど軽快に現れた。続いて転びまろびつしながらも必死についてきたもう一人。密航者と朔屋直正だった。
source.english: One figure appeared, utterly untroubled by the shaking ground, black hair streaming like wings. So lightly did she move that one could believe such wings had carried her all the way here. Another followed, stumbling and tumbling but struggling desperately to keep up. The stowaway and Naomasa Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「シサムー！　今投げるから、ロープ！」
source.english: “Sisam! I'm throwing you a rope!”

source.japanese: なんとかへっぴり腰で足踏みしめ、朔屋は担いできた物を一度地に投げ落とし、その先端を掴んでぐるぐると振り回す。そう、ロープだった。結んでよし牽いてよし、船乗りの第二の腕、船上の万能索具、いかな万年不良三等航海士の朔屋といえど、この場だけは外さずに、ロープは広がりつつある亀裂の上空を飛び、違わずシサムの足下に落ちて滑る。
source.english: Sakuya managed to plant his feet, his backside sticking out awkwardly. He dumped his burden on the ground, caught its end, and swung it round and round. Yes, a rope. For tying, for pulling: a sailor's second arm, the all-purpose rigging of a ship. Even Sakuya, that eternally delinquent third mate, did not miss this time. The rope flew over the widening crack and landed squarely at Sisam's feet, sliding over the ground.

target.text: Unfazed by the shaking earth, black hair fluttering in the wind like a pair of wings, so nimble and light did that lone figure appear that one could almost be convinced she had simply flown here, carried upon those wings. In her wake came another, stumbling and tumbling all the while as he desperately attempted to catch up to her. It was the stowaway and Sakuya Naomasa.
【Naomasa】 「SHISAMUUU! I'M THROWING THE ROPE DOWN NOW!」

Planting his feet firmly while still looking kind of weak in the knees, Sakuya dropped what he was carrying on his shoulders onto the ground, then grabbed the end and swung it around. Indeed, it was a rope.
