Good for tying knots, good for hauling and pulling, the sailor's second arm, the all-purpose rigging on sea, and for all that Sakuya may have been a perennially poor third mate, this time alone he did not miss, and the rope unfurled as it flew high over the fissure, landing and sliding across the ice right next to Shisamu's feet.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「嘘言わないでよ、なんで朔屋なの！」
source.english: “You've got to be kidding! Why is it Sakuya!?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Tell me this isn't a lie! Why are you here, Sakuya?!」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「深く考えるな、使え！」
source.english: “Don't think about it! Use it!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Don't think too hard about it, just use it!」

source.japanese: 確かに、深く考えている場合ではないと、シサム、足下のロープ拾い上げ、輪になったその中に自分の頭を通し肩通し豊かな胸でひとつかえ、腰になんとか回してぐいと結び目を引き締める。もはや眼前にまで迫り来た亀裂を前に、二歩三歩と後退り。
source.english: Indeed, this was no time to think. Sisam picked up the rope at her feet and passed her head and shoulders through its loop. It caught for a moment on her ample breasts, but she managed to get it round her waist and tugged the knot tight. The crack was almost upon her. She backed away two or three steps.

target.text: Certainly, this was hardly the time to think too hard about things, Shisamu thought, and she picked up the rope by her feet, made a loop, put her head and shoulders through it, and though it did hitch on her voluptuous chest, she somehow managed to get it around her waist before fastening the knot with a big, hard tug. By now, the fissure loomed right before her very eyes, and she retreated two, three steps from it.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「なんかもう、いやな考えしか浮かんでこないけど、これ、飛ぶしかないか───ええい、ままよ」
source.english: “I've got nothing but horrible thoughts about this, but I suppose I have to jump—oh, to hell with it!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I kind of have nothing but bad feelings about this, but this is jump or die, isn't it─── argh, here goes nothing!」

source.japanese: しかし、そこは元一等航海士、すかさず覚悟を決め、下がった分だけ助走距離に換えて、凍てつく地面蹴りつけ、一二の三で宙に舞う。
source.english: But she was a former first mate. Making up her mind at once, she used the distance she had retreated for a run-up, kicked off the frozen ground, and on one, two, three flew into the air.

target.text: However, she was a former first mate; she found her resolve without a moment's delay, and changing the distance she'd retreated into a run-up, she kicked off against the frozen surface, and with a one, two, three, she soared lightly through the air.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「っと、わ、とっ、あっ、あ～～～っっ！」
source.english: “Hup—whoa—oh—ah—aaaah!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Wait, wah, uh, ah, AA～～～HH!」

source.japanese: しかし、やはり船上とは勝手が違ったか、あるいは単にシサムの跳躍力をしても亀裂の幅を飛び越えるには至らなかったか、泳ぐ手伸ばす手必死に宙を漕ぐ脚の足掻きも空しく、哀れシサム、亀裂の底へと飲み込まれ───
source.english: Perhaps it was not like being aboard ship after all. Or perhaps even Sisam could not jump the width of the crack. Her flailing hands, outstretched arms and legs desperately paddling the air availed her nothing. Poor Sisam was swallowed by the rift—

target.text: However, perhaps it was too different from being on a ship, or perhaps it was simply that Shisamu's jumping power was insufficient to clear the breadth of the fissure, for no matter how her hands clawed, her arms reached, or her legs frantically paddled through the air, her thrashing was all in vain, and Shisamu, pitiful Shisamu, was swallowed by the dark as she fell down into the depths of the fissure───

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「大丈夫！　ここであなたをなくすわけにはいかないんだ私は！　───っても───！」
source.english: “It's all right! I can't afford to lose you here!—Except—!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「It's okay! I can't afford to lose you here! ───That said───!」

source.japanese:
しかし、シサムに結わえ付けられたロープのもう片端は、しっかと密航者の手に握られていた。
　そして、しっかりと握られていただけに、地の底に吸い込まれるシサムの体重、落ちる加速も積み上げられて、密航者の体をぐいと亀裂へ引き寄せる。足下必死に踏みしめるも、ここは凍土。
source.english:
The other end of the rope tied to Sisam was held fast in the stowaway's hands.

And precisely because she held it fast, Sisam's weight, compounded by her accelerating fall into the depths, hauled the stowaway toward the rift. She desperately braced her feet, but this was frozen ground.

target.text: However, the other end of the rope tied around Shisamu was tightly gripped by the stowaway's hand. And as it was only being held tightly, as she fell towards the bottom of the earth, Shisamu's body weight, and the increasing force from it as the speed of her fall accelerated, suddenly pulled the stowaway's body towards the fissure with a powerful jerk. She desperately tried to brace against the pull by planting her feet, but this was frozen soil.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「足下がこれじゃ、私も引かれて！　ちょっとわわわ！」
source.english: “With this footing, I'm getting dragged in too! Wait—whoa, whoa, whoa!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「With what's under my feet, I'm being pulled in too! Hold ooowoWOW!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「嘘、私までこんなところで───わぅ！」
source.english: “No way! Not me too, not here—wah!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「No way, not me too, not somewhere like this───WAAH!」

source.japanese: ずるずるずると見る間に今度は密航者が亀裂に向かって一直線。あやうく二人もろともというところで。
source.english: Now the stowaway was sliding straight toward the crack. Just as both were about to go over—

target.text: As she slid away before their eyes, this time, it was the stowaway who was heading for the fissure in a straight line. Just when the both of them were moments from falling in together.

source.japanese:
引きずり込まれる寸前で、密航者の体は引き止められる。朔屋だ、朔屋の手が密航者のポーチをしっかりと掴んでいたのだ。
　まぁ当然、革鞄はベルトに付いており、ベルトはズボンを共連れに。谷底にて宙吊りになったシサムに引っ張られ、密航者の上半身は伸びきり、下半身は革鞄頼みに朔屋に引っ張られているとあっては、朔屋の眼前にはいつぞどこかで見た光景、まろび出る尻の白さよ。さすがに、この時ばかりはその絶景を楽しむ余裕などないのだが。
source.english:
Just before she could be dragged in, the stowaway’s body was brought up short. Sakuya—it was Sakuya, his hand clamped firmly around her pouch.

The leather pouch, naturally enough, was fixed to her belt, and the belt had taken her pants along for the ride. Sisam, dangling down in the chasm, hauled the stowaway’s upper body out to full stretch; Sakuya, with nothing but the leather pouch to rely on, hauled her lower half the other way. The result, directly before Sakuya’s eyes, was a sight he had seen somewhere once before: behold the white splendor of her butt spilling forth. Though this once, even he had no leisure to enjoy so magnificent a view.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「っく、は……っ、うーーーーっ！
　お腹、お腹が、あーっ！　あーっ！」
source.english:
“Guh, ha…! Uuuuuugh!
My stomach, my stomach—aaah! Aaah!”

target.text: On the brink of being dragged within, the stowaway's body was held in place. It was Sakuya, Sakuya's hand was holding firmly on to the stowaway's bag. Well, naturally, with the leather bag attached to the belt, so did the belt take the pants with them. Pulled by Shisamu, who was suspended in mid-air at the bottom of the ravine, the stowaway's upper half was stretched to the breaking point, and when her lower half was pulled on by Sakuya by way of her leather bag, a sight that he'd seen somewhere before unfolded before Sakuya's eyes: the white of a pair of buttocks suddenly popped into view. All the same, this time alone he certainly did not have the luxury to enjoy the splendid sight.
【Stowaway】 「Kkhh, ha……nh, uーーーー! Stomach, my stomach is, AAー! Aー!」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「シサム、そして君も！　
　絶対に離すなよ、離したら怒るよ俺ぁ！
　あんた達相手でも！」
source.english:
“Sisam! And you too!
Don't you dare let go! I'll be mad if you do!
Even at you two!”

source.japanese: 朔屋の必死の声に、谷の底からシサムの言葉にならないこちらも必死の返事が返ってくる。
source.english: At Sakuya's desperate shout, an equally desperate, wordless reply came from Sisam in the depths.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Shisamu, and you too! Absolutely do not let go! If you do, I'll get angry! Even with you two!」
In response to the desperation in Sakuya's voice, he received Shisamu's wordless groans from the bottom of the ravine and a frantic reply from close to him.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「でも───これで、どうにか……シサム、変に身動きしないでね。今、引き上げる、から……」
source.english: “But—now we can somehow…Sisam, hold still. We're pulling you up…now…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「キサラも手伝え、俺を引っぱってくれっ。
　三人がかりならどうにか……っ」
source.english:
“Kisara, help! Pull me!
The three of us should manage somehow…!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「But───like this, we'll somehow…… Shisamu, don't make any sudden movements, okay? I'm pulling you up……right now……」
【Naomasa】 「Kisara, you help too, pull on me. With the three of us together, we can do it……!」

source.japanese: 慌ててキサラが二人にとりつく。ロープをしっかと掴み、力の限りに引き揚げる。何しろその先にいるのは片時も離れることのできぬ自分の半身なのだ。少しまた少したぐり寄せるたび、涙鼻水混じりの悲鳴は近くなり、キサラは安堵とともに引く手も強く、ようやくのことでシサムを引き上げることができたのだった。
source.english: Kisara hastily joined them. She seized the rope and hauled with all her strength. At its other end was her own other half, from whom she could not be parted even for a moment. Inch by inch they reeled her in. Screams thick with tears and snot grew closer; relief lent strength to Kisara's hands. At last they managed to pull Sisam up.

target.text: Panicked, Kisara hurriedly grabbed on. With the rope clutched tightly in her hands, she pulled up with all the strength she could muster. After all, it was none other than own other half on the other end, someone she couldn't be apart from for even an instant. As they reeled the rope in by hand, little by little, the screams drowning in tears and snot came closer, and as the relief in Kisara grew stronger, so too did her arms, until finally, they succeeded in pulling Shisamu up.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あぁぁ……っ、やばかったぁ……。
　まぁだ胸がばくばく言ってンよ……。
　でも助かった……あんがと、朔屋、
　そしてなんだかわかんないが、あんたも」
source.english:
“Aaaah…that was close…
My heart's still pounding…
But I'm safe…thanks, Sakuya.
And I don't know what to make of this, but you too.”

source.japanese: 死地から脱したシサムがへたり込むその横で、密航者はぶつくさとくさりながら、ずれたズボンとパンツを直していた。
source.english: Beside Sisam, who had escaped death and was slumped on the ground, the stowaway grumbled under her breath, tugging up her slipped pants and underwear.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Aaaah……, that was craaazy……. My heart is still about to explode……. But you saved me……thanks, Sakuya, and I don't really know why, but thank you too.」
Next to Shisamu, who had limply fallen to the ground after narrowly escaping the clutches of death, stood the stowaway, fixing her sagging trousers and underwear while grumbling.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あー、また尻出しかぁ……」
source.english: “Ugh, showing my butt again…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Aah, my butt was in full view again……」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「でも言ってる場合じゃないし」
source.english: “But we don’t have time for this.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「But this isn't the time for that.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「いいもの、ちゃんと綺麗だもの、
　下着もお尻も───うん？
　なに？　お礼なんて。
　私があなた達を助けるのは当たり前なのだし」
source.english:
“It’s nice—it’s really pretty,
both the underwear and my butt—huh?
What? Thanks?
It’s only natural that I’d help you guys.”

source.japanese: 言葉だけではなく態度からも、さも当然と胸を張り密航者はシサムに言う。そして、自身、荒い息を深呼吸で整えながら、
source.english: In word and manner alike, the stowaway told Sisam this as though nothing could be more obvious, drawing herself up proudly. Then, getting her own ragged breathing under control with deep breaths:

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「It's fine, really, they're nice and clean, my underwear and my butt both───hmm? What? Oh, no need for thanks. It's only natural that I'd come help you out.」

It wasn't just her words but her mannerisms too, and while saying so to Shisamu, the stowaway puffed out her chest with pride as though it truly was only natural. And then, while calming her heavy breathing with some deep breaths of her own,

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「さあ、呼吸が整ったら走ろう。
　さっさと出よう、気分が悪くなるだけだ」
source.english:
“Come on. Once you've caught your breath, let's run.
Let's get out of here. This place will only make us sick.”

source.japanese: そう言って、振り仰ぐ。睨めつける視線の先には、ウミヒト。今はただ氷壁の中で、まるで眠っているかのよう。
source.english: As she spoke, she looked up. Her glare fell upon the Sea People. Now they stood within the ice walls as though asleep.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Now, once we've caught our breath, let's run. Let's get out of here right away, we'll just end up feeling sick.」
Saying that, she looked up. In the direction she glared stood the Umihito. Right now, it simply remained dormant within the wall of ice as though it was fast asleep.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「お前達なんて───出来れば壊してやりたいけど、今はかまってもいられない」
source.english: “You things—I'd destroy you if I could, but I haven't got time for you now.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「If at all possible───I would love to smash the likes of you to bits, but I can't afford to bother with you right now.」

source.japanese:
憎々しげに吐き捨ててから、密航者は朔屋達に視線を戻す。
　まだ地は揺れているのだ、音を立てながら。一同は立ち上がり、足早に歩き出す。向かうはシサムとキサラが踏み込んできたのとは逆の方向。居並ぶウミヒトの列の間を揺れる大地に脚をとられながらも進み続ける。やがて、切り立った氷壁の隘路を抜けたその先には。
source.english:
Spitting out the words with hatred, the stowaway turned back to Sakuya and the twins.

The ground still shook, rumbling. They got up and set off at a brisk pace, in the opposite direction from the one the twins had entered by. Through the ranks of Sea People they went, the shaking earth tripping their feet. Eventually they passed through a narrow way between sheer ice walls, and beyond it—

target.text: After spitting out that venom, the stowaway turned back to Sakuya and company. The earth was still quaking, and growling loudly all the while. The party got back on their feet, then began to walk at a brisk pace. Their direction was the opposite of where Shisamu and Kisara had entered from. Even as they stumbled over the shaking earth, they continued to advance through the rows of Umihito. At last, they passed through the narrow path of precipitous ice walls, and what awaited them there was:

source.japanese: 海が広がっていた。
source.english: The sea spread before them.

target.text: The vast ocean unfolding before their eyes.

source.japanese:
シサムとキサラ、二人同時に目をまん丸と瞠り、しばたたかせてから、頭を抱える。
　何がどうなっているのか、これは。海上では目印無くとも自分の位置を過[あやま]たぬ二人が、思いも寄らぬ場所に海を見つけて混乱する。歪んでいるのはこの世の地理か己の頭か。もし無線があるならどこぞの国の地理院まで青筋立てて怒鳴り込んでやろうかと真剣に考え込んだところで、またもあり得ぬ光景に双子は目を瞠[みは]る。
source.english:
Sisam and Kisara widened their eyes together, blinked, then clutched their heads.

What was going on? At sea, even without landmarks, they never mistook their position. Now they had found the sea somewhere wholly unexpected, and were bewildered. Was it the geography of this world that had warped, or their own heads? They were seriously contemplating whether, with a radio, they might call some country's geographical institute and shout themselves purple. Then another impossible sight made their eyes widen.

target.text: Shisamu and Kisara both goggled in unison, eyes like saucers, and after blinking rapidly, they clutched their heads. What in the world was going on here? The two of them, able to determine their own position on sea without err, even without any landmarks, were left befuddled at discovering the ocean in a place as unexpected as this. Was it the world or their own minds that were warped here? Just as they seriously considered beaming a flurry of angry yelling, veins bulging on their foreheads, to the Geospatial Information Authority of a certain country if they but had a radio, the twins' eyes shot wide open yet again at yet another impossible sight.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「信天翁号まで！」
source.english: “Even the Albatross!”

source.japanese:
そうそこには。
　この極北の海にあってはひどく頼りない姿の襤褸船が。しかし、今この場の二人にとっては百万頓[トン]の巨船よりも頼もしい信天翁号の姿があった。
source.english:
Yes, there she was.

A ragged ship, pitifully frail for this northernmost sea. Yet to those two, here and now, the Albatross was more reassuring than a million-ton vessel.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Even the Albatross!」

Indeed, there she was. In the seas of the northernmost reaches, the ramshackle ship made for a terribly unimpressive sight. However, in this moment, in this place, to these two, the Albatross cut a figure far more dependable than any ocean liner weighing a million tons.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「それはありますとも当然！」
source.english: “Of course she's here! Naturally!”

source.japanese:
得意気に胸を張る密航者に、シサムとキサラ、何かを言いたげに口を開く。
　そう、聞きたい事は山とある。何故ここに信天翁号がいるのか、それを何故お前が知っていたのか、そもそもなんであんたはまたぞろ信天翁号にひっついて出てくるのか、そして、朔屋がどうしてここに来たのか───
source.english:
The stowaway drew herself up proudly. Sisam and Kisara opened their mouths as though to say something.

Yes, they had mountains of questions. Why was the Albatross here? How had she known? Why did this woman keep appearing with the Albatross anyway? And how had Sakuya come here—?

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「She certainly is, of course!」

Shisamu and Kisara both opened their mouths as though they wanted to say something to the stowaway puffing out her chest with pride. Yes, there were a million things they wanted to ask. Why and how was the Albatross here, and how did you know that it was here at all, and to begin with, why was she doggedly sticking with the Albatross yet again, and then, why had Sakuya come here and───

source.japanese:
しかし、シサムとキサラは顔見合わせて肩竦め、揃って溜息軽く一つあわせて二つ、ついただけだった。
　逡巡の全てをぶつけてしまいたくはあるのだが、それよりなにより、今は目の前にある信天翁号への気持ちが勝った。
source.english:
But Sisam and Kisara merely looked at each other, shrugged, and sighed lightly together. One each; two in all.

They wanted to fling every doubt at her. But stronger than any of that, now, was what they felt for the Albatross before them.

target.text: However, Shisamu and Kisara just looked each other in the eyes, shrugged their shoulders, sighed lightly in unison, then sighed twice more for good measure. They wanted to unleash every last bit of their vacillation, but more importantly, most importantly, right now, the feelings they harboured towards the Albatross floating right before their eyes took precedence.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「…………いいや。
　色々訊きたいこととかあるけど。
　たぶんあたしらには、この船が」
source.english:
“…Never mind.
There's a lot we want to ask.
But I suppose this ship is—”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「…………Never mind. There are a whole lot of things I want to ask you, but. I think, to us, this ship here is, probably.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「本来あるべき場所、ってことなんだろね」
source.english: “Where we really belong.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「The place we truly ought to be, or something, right?」

source.japanese:
そう言って、シサムとキサラは海べり目指して駆け出す。信天翁号からこちらに向けて、ライトが灯る一度二度。そして短艇が舷側から降ろされ、こちらに向かってくるではないか。そう、彼女達を迎えに。
　ここに留まり時を待てと言われ、双子はそれを受け入れた。そんな時もあったが今はそんなの昔の話ということだ。二人は千切れんばかりに、短艇に向かって両手を振り続ける。帰ろうじゃないか、再び乗り込もうじゃないか、あの襤褸船に。
source.english:
With that, Sisam and Kisara ran toward the sea. A light flashed toward them from the Albatross, once, twice. A boat was lowered over her side and began coming toward them. Yes, to fetch them.

Stay here and wait for the time to come: the twins had been told that, and accepted it. Such a time had existed. Now it was ancient history. They waved both arms at the boat as though they would tear them off. Let's go home. Let's board that ragged ship again.

target.text: After saying that, Shisamu and Kisara broke into a run towards the shore. From the Albatross, a light shone in their direction, once and then twice. Then a boat was lowered down the side, and why, if it wasn't also coming their way, too. Indeed, to pick them up. They had been told to remain here and wait for the right time, and the twins had accepted that. There had been a time like that, but now, it was but a thing of the past. The two of them raised both their hands and kept waving them at the boat so vigorously they seemed liable to tear off any moment. Let us return home, let us board our shabby ship once more, why don't we?

source.japanese: そんな二人の背中を見て、朔屋もまた海べりへと近づくために歩き出す。密航者もまた。足踏み出して、しかし、踏鞴を踏む。
source.english: Watching their backs, Sakuya started walking toward the shore too. So did the stowaway. She took a step—and staggered.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい、大丈夫か？」
source.english: “Hey, are you all right?”

source.japanese: 隣で急に蹌踉けた女に、朔屋は声かけ、その顔覗き込む。
source.english: Sakuya spoke to the woman who had suddenly stumbled beside him, peering into her face.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい、君、
　なんだかえらく消耗してないか？」
source.english:
“Hey, you.
You're looking awfully worn out, aren't you?”

target.text: Watching the two acting like that from behind, Sakuya also began to walk closer to the shore. So too did the stowaway. She stepped forwards, but, she stumbled.
【Naomasa】 「Oi, are you okay?」
Sakuya called out to the woman suddenly stumbling by his side and peered into her face.
【Naomasa】 「Oi, you, you're looking awfully drained, no?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そう見える？
　でもそれは余り、気にしないで」
source.english:
“Do I look it?
But don't worry too much about that.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Do I look that way? But don't worry too much about that.」

source.japanese: そう言って手さえ振ってみせて、密航者は双子の方へと歩いていく。短艇はもう間近、シサムとキサラは海に飛び込まんばかりに足踏みならして大声を上げている。
source.english: She even waved a hand to dismiss it, then walked toward the twins. The boat was already close. Sisam and Kisara were stamping their feet and shouting, all but leaping into the sea.

target.text: Saying so, even waving a hand at him, the stowaway walked towards the twins. The boat was already drawing near, and Shisamu and Kisara were yelling loudly and stomping their feet like they were just about ready to leap into the ocean.

source.japanese: ───かくして信天翁号に、航海士が戻ってきたのだった。
source.english: —And thus the navigators returned to the Albatross.

target.text: ───Thus, the first mates returned to the Albatross.

source.japanese:
場面は移る。
　───そこは、何時だって嵐の中に在った島だ、かつては。
source.english:
The scene shifts.

—To an island that was always in a storm. Once.

source.japanese:
今は嵐は晴れ、島は木造の廃屋に埋めつくされ、というよりもこの島全体が古い木材を継ぎ接ぎして出来あがっているのだろう。かつてはこの島は、遙かな過去の亡霊が住まう島だった。神の怒りに触れた人類の、方舟の成れの果てだった。けれど今やその亡霊さえも島からいなくなり、木造の廃屋はまさに無人の静寂に静まり返っている。
　その廃屋の中で、一人だけ、生きて動いている者があった。小さな人影だった。痩せて哀れな、白い小柄な影。それは、かつて信天翁の船長と呼ばれていた、クロという名の少女だった。
source.english:
Now the storm has cleared. The island is buried beneath derelict wooden houses—or perhaps the whole island is pieced together from old timber. Once, ghosts of a distant past inhabited it. It was what remained of an ark belonging to a humanity that had incurred God's wrath. But now even those ghosts have left. The wooden ruins stand in the silence of utter vacancy.

Among them, one living thing still moved. A small human figure. A thin, pitiable, small white shadow. Kuro, once called captain of the Albatross.

source.japanese:
そしてクロは、今日もまた廃墟の中で目を覚ます。たった一人で。目覚めの度に一人きりだというその事を思い知り、涙を流すクロ。何時からこうなってしまったのだろう。自分が失敗したのは判っている。それでも自分は、前は一人ではなかったはず。もう一人、その一人だけ、けれどその人が彼女にとってどれだけ大きな存在であったか。
　でも、その人は、何時しかいなくなってしまった。だからクロは一人、孤独に目を覚まし、泣きながら今日も彼を捜しに出かける。もうこの島内にはいないのは判りきっていたけれど、島から漕ぎ出す船もなく、どのみち一人ではどうしようない。
source.english:
Today, again, Kuro wakes among the ruins. Alone. Every awakening teaches her anew that she is alone, and she cries. When did it come to this? She knows she failed. Even so, she was not alone before. There had been someone else. Only one person—but how much that one person had meant to her.

Yet at some point he had vanished. So Kuro wakes alone, lonely, and goes out crying to look for him again. She knows perfectly well he is no longer on this island. But she has no boat to row away in; alone, she can do nothing anyway.

target.text: The scene shifts. ───It was an island that existed within an ever-raging storm, once upon a time.

Now the storm had cleared, the island was buried beneath wooden ruins, or rather, the island itself was most likely cobbled together from ancient timber. Once upon a time, a ghost of a distant past resided on this island. The mere shadow of the ark built by humanity after incurring God's wrath. However, now, even that ghost had disappeared from this island, and the wooden ruins had truly fallen still as deserted death.

Within these ruins there was a single, yes, but a single being that yet lived and stirred. It was a small figure. Scrawny and pitiful, a petite, white shadow. It was she who had once been known as the Captain of the Albatross, a little girl by the name Kuro.

And so, as always, Kuro woke up inside the ruins. All by her lonesome. Whenever she awoke, Kuro would realize just how alone she was, and tears would roll down her cheeks. How long had it been since things turned out like this? She knew she had failed. But still, she hadn't been alone before, to be sure. There had been another, just that one other, but just how grand an existence had he been to this girl.

However, that man had vanished at some point. And so Kuro was alone, she woke up in solitude, and as the tears flowed, as always, she set out to search for him. She was well aware that he was nowhere to be found on this island anymore, but she had no boat to row out from the island with, and even should she have, that was hopeless to try by herself.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「だぁれも……いないんだね」
source.english: “There's…nobody here.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「There's nooobody…… here at all, huh.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「誰かといっしょのときは、いつも大変で、大変がいやだったけど」
source.english: “When Kuro was with someone, it was always hard. Kuro didn't like it being hard.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Being with someone was always very hard, didn't like hard, but.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「一人なのも───いや、みたいだ、クロは」
source.english: “But being alone—Kuro doesn't seem to like that either.”

source.japanese:
目が覚めてまた疲れ果てて眠るまで泣きながら島を捜し巡る。その繰り返しを幾度となく幾度となく、数えきれぬほど、いつしか数えることも止めるほど。
　そうしてクロは、ある日気がつくと船もなくただ海へ突き出るだけの桟橋に立っていた。
source.english:
From waking until she falls asleep exhausted, she searches the island, crying. Again and again and again. Too often to count, until at some point she stops counting.

And one day Kuro finds herself standing on a pier with no ship alongside, merely jutting into the sea.

source.japanese:
あるいは考えたのかもしれない。ここで待っていれば、あの人が帰ってきてくれるのかもしれないと。
　けれどクロの赤い眼に映るのは、島を取り巻く海原だけ。水平線と空は取り巻く嵐に覆われてどこまでも鈍色の、もう見慣れた景色、彼女の悲哀と絶望を映した景色。それのみ。
source.english:
Perhaps she thought: if she waited here, that person might come back.

But all her red eyes see is the sea surrounding the island. Horizon and sky are covered by the encircling storm, a familiar landscape of dull gray stretching on and on, reflecting her sorrow and despair. Nothing else.

source.japanese:
そう、ついに。
　ちっぽけな白子は絶望した。
　誰も帰ってこない。あの船は帰ってこない。あの人は帰ってこない。そのことを受け入れてしまった。
source.english:
Yes, at last.

The little albino despaired.

No one was coming back. That ship was not coming back. That person was not coming back. She had accepted it.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro also doesn't─── like being alone, it seems.」

She would wake up, and until she was utterly exhausted and went to bed, she would search around the island in tears. She had repeated this many, many times, until it had reached the countless, until she had suddenly stopped counting along the way. And so, a certain day, Kuro realized that she was standing on the pier that simply jutted out into the sea with no boat to its name.

Or perhaps the thought had crossed her mind. That if she waited here, maybe that man would come back to her. However, all that was shown to Kuro's red eyes was the vast ocean surrounding the island. The horizon and the sky was covered in an all-enclosing storm, a veil of dull, dark grey, a scenery she was already familiar with, a scenery that reflected the girl's sorrow and despair. That alone.
And then, at last. The tiny albino despaired. Nobody was coming back. That ship wasn't coming back. He wasn't coming back. She came to accept that.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「一人って。さみしいって。
　わかりたく、ない。でした」
source.english:
“Being alone. Being lonely.
Kuro…didn't want to understand.”

source.japanese:
ぽつりとクロは呟く。それは荒れる波が桟橋を洗う音に掻[か]き消され、彼女以外に聞く者はいない。
　それでもクロは呟く。
source.english:
Kuro murmurs it, a few words at a time. The sound of rough waves washing the pier drowns her out. No one but she hears.

Still she murmurs.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Being alone. Being lonely. Didn't want. To understand that.」
Kuro muttered in fragments. It was drowned out in the sound of rough waves laving the pier, and there were none to hear it but the girl herself. And yet, Kuro still muttered.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ばいばい。
　航海士。水夫長。機関長。泪さん。
　水夫のみんな。宗右衛門さん。
　───朔屋、さん」
source.english:
“Bye-bye.
Mates. Bosun. Chief Engineer. Rui.
All the sailors. Mr. Soemon.
—Mr. Sakuya.”

source.japanese: そして最後に呟く。最後に自分を受け入れてくれるであろう、その海に。
source.english: And she murmurs one last word to the sea, which will, in the end, accept her.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Bye bye. Mates. Bosun. Chief Engineer. Rui-san. All the sailors. Souemon-san. ───Sakuya……san.」
A final murmur. To the ocean, the one place that might finally take her in.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「───さいなら」
source.english: “—Goodbye.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「───G'bye.」

source.japanese: ああ、哀れ、どこまでも哀れでちっぽけな白子は、ついに海へと踏み出すのだ。あと一歩、その一歩で、海はクロを抱き止めて、そのまま底深くまで招き入れるだろう。さらばクロ。
source.english: Ah, the pitiable, utterly pitiable little albino finally steps toward the sea. One step more, and the sea will catch Kuro and invite her down into its depths. Farewell, Kuro.

target.text: Alas, the pitiful, ever pitiful, tiny albino finally stepped forth towards the sea. Just one more step: with that one last step, the ocean would surely catch Kuro in her arms and guide her down to her welcoming depths. Farewell, Kuro.

source.japanese: ───しかしその寸前で。
source.english: —But just before that.

target.text: ───However, on the verge of stepping in.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……ウミヒトだ……」
source.english: “…A Sea Person…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……An Umihito……」

source.japanese:
島の内湾の向こうに、見たのだった。海上に立ちはだかる、白く巨大な影───ヒトガタを。
　クロにとって、あれを見るのは初めてのことではなかったが、しかし滅多に見ることのないモノではある。
　そして、その天をも衝かん巨大な影は、見る者の心を嫌でも不安という爪で掻[か]き毟[むし]る。今のクロもその爪に精神抉[えぐ]られ、体はピンと張り詰めて強張ったまま、湧きたつ瘧[おこり]に震えるばかり。
source.english:
She had seen it across the island's inlet. A huge white figure barring the sea—a Hitogata.

Kuro had seen one before, but they were rarely seen.

And that towering shadow, vast enough to pierce the sky, raked at the beholder's heart with claws of unease. Those claws gouged at Kuro's mind now. Her body stiffened, taut as a string. She could only tremble in a rising ague.

source.japanese:
そのクロの瞬きすらできぬほど見開かれた目、見渡す視界の隅に。
　そびえ立つ白い巨体の麓すり抜けて。
　水平線より、縋りつく嵐を振り切って。
　まっすぐに向かってくるものがあった。
source.english:
At the edge of Kuro's vision, her eyes so wide she could not even blink—

Past the foot of that towering white body—

From the horizon, shaking off the storm that clung to it—

Something came straight toward her.

target.text: She saw it, on the other side of the island's inner bay. Obstructing the path out to sea, a gargantuan white shadow───the Hitogata. This was not the first time Kuro saw it, but it was a rare sight all the same. And how this titanic shadow that pierced even the heavens tore at the hearts of any who witnessed it, willing or not, with the claws of anxiety. Those claws also gouged Kuro's soul, her body tensed and grew stiff as a board, and she simply shivered from the ague suddenly welling up within her.

And there, in the corner of Kuro's vision, of her eyes opened so wide that she couldn't even blink. It slipped by the base of that towering, white shadow. It came from the horizon, cutting through the storm clinging to it. There was something heading straight her way.

source.japanese:
クロの体は今度は驚きに強張る。
　そう、それは。まぎれもなく。
source.english:
Now surprise stiffened Kuro's body.

Yes. That was unmistakably—

target.text: This time, it was astonishment that made Kuro stiffen. Yes, for that was. Unmistakably.

source.japanese: 浮かんでいることすら信じがたい、襤褸船。すなわち信天翁号───
source.english: A ragged ship whose very ability to float defied belief. The Albatross—

target.text: A ramshackle ship, so shabby even the notion of it floating beggared belief. In other words, the Albatross───

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロって、ほんとは、もう死んじゃったのかな。
　だから、ほんとに見たかった。見れる。
　クロ───見てる！」
source.english:
“Has Kuro…actually died already?
That's why what Kuro really wanted to see…Kuro can see it.
Kuro—is seeing it!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Maybe, Kuro is actually already dead? Because, really wanted to see it. Can see it now. Kuro───sees it!」

source.japanese:
ああ、確かにクロの視界の中で、信天翁号はどんどんその姿を大きくしてくる。
　甲板を埋め尽くしたバラックの隙間を縫って走り回るのは下級水夫。追い立てるように怒号を飛ばすのは水夫長。ブリッジに翻[ひるがえ]る赤いリーファージャケットは双子の航海士のものだ。煙突の半ばの穴より吐き出される黒煙は速度に牽かれてたなびいている。あの速度が出ているなら、機関室には当然、その主がいるのだろう。
　そして。
source.english:
Ah, yes. Within Kuro's sight, the Albatross grew steadily larger.

Junior sailors ran through the gaps between the shanties covering her deck. The boatswain roared, driving them on. The red reefer jackets fluttering on the bridge belonged to the twin navigators. Black smoke, spewing from a hole halfway up the funnel, streamed behind her with her speed. If she was making that speed, surely the master of the engine room was there too.

And—

target.text: Yes, there was no mistaking it; as Kuro watched, the Albatross gradually grew bigger and bigger. Darting about the little passages stitched between the patchwork of shacks covering the deck were the deck boys. Sending angry bellows flying through the air as if to urge them forwards was the Bosun. Standing atop the bridge with red reefer jackets flapping about in the wind were the twin first mates. The trails of black smoke expelled from the holes of half the funnels swayed from the speed. And if the Albatross was going that fast, then naturally, the master of the engine room was surely in his rightful place. And then.

source.japanese: まるで船の針路を示すかのように甲板最前に立ってクロを見ているのは、黒髪を羽ばたかせるように風に広げているのは。
source.english: Standing at the very front of the deck, as though indicating the ship's course, looking at Kuro, black hair spread in the wind like beating wings—

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「そんな。アルバトロスだけじゃないよ。
　いるよ。あの人。密航の人」
source.english:
“No. It isn't just the Albatross.
She's there. That person. The stowaway.”

source.japanese:
そして───
　その横で舷側から身を乗り出してクロに手を振っているのは。身を乗り出しすぎて海へと落ちかけ、慌てた下級水夫達に引き上げられ呆れられているのは。
source.english:
And—

Beside her, leaning over the side and waving at Kuro—leaning out too far, nearly falling into the sea, dragged back aboard by alarmed junior sailors who then looked at him in disgust—

target.text: Who Kuro saw standing at the fore of the deck, almost as though she herself were indicating the course of the ship, black hair fluttering in the wind, was.
【Kuro】 「No way. It's not just the Albatross. She's there. That lady. The stowaway lady.」

And finally─── Leaning over the side of the ship, waving his arms at Kuro, was. Leaning too far over the ship, about to fall into the ocean, pulled back up in a panic by deck boys who were none too impressed by him, was.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「それに、なんで、なんでぇ!?
　───朔屋さん、なんでぇ!?」
source.english:
“And why—why!?
—Mr. Sakuya, why!?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「And then, why, WHY!? ───Sakuya-san, WHY!?」

source.japanese: 呆然と立ち尽くすクロの目前に、信天翁号はいよいよ迫り、するすると桟橋に接岸する。クラッカーから爆ぜ飛んだ紙テープのように勢いまかせに放り投げられた縄梯子が少女の目の前でたわんで跳ねる。クロは、驚きのあまり気が遠くなりかけた。見上げた縄梯子の先で早く上がってこいと手を伸ばしているのは、少女が探し求めていた男だったのだから。
source.english: Before the dumbstruck Kuro, the Albatross drew closer and closer, then slid alongside the pier. A rope ladder flung out with reckless force, like a streamer bursting from a party popper, bounced and sagged before her. Surprise nearly made her faint. For at the top of the ladder, holding out his hand and urging her to come up, was the man she had searched for.

target.text: The Albatross drew closer and closer before Kuro's eyes as she stood there dumbfounded, and she smoothly came alongside the pier. A rope ladder was thrown with such force that it bent and bounced off the ground right in front of her, like a paper streamer exploding out from a party cracker. Kuro was about to lose consciousness from the overwhelming shock of it all. For when she looked up, there, at the top of the ladder, reaching down a hand towards her and telling her to hurry up and climb it, there was the man she had been searching for all this time.

source.japanese: クロ、涙で滲み出る眼[まなこ]をきゅっと閉じる。そして、なお桟橋に立ち尽くしたまま、
source.english: Kuro squeezed shut her tear-blurred eyes. Still standing motionless on the pier:

target.text: Wet with tears, Kuro clenched her eyes shut. And then, she simply remained motionless on the pier,

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ウソじゃない。でも怖くって。
　目。開ける。消えてたら───でも」
source.english:
“It isn't a lie. But Kuro's scared.
Open…Kuro's eyes. If it's gone—
But…”

source.japanese:
勇気を出すのだ、クロ。
　上を見上げ、瞼を開く───
source.english:
Find your courage, Kuro.

Look up. Open your eyes—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あばばばばばぁ！」
source.english: “Abababababa!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「It's not a lie. But Kuro's scared. If eyes. Open. He could vanish───but.」
Muster the courage, Kuro. Look up, open your eyes───
【Naomasa】 「ABABABABAA!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ヒィ!?　───あうん」
source.english: “Eek!?—Auhn.”

source.japanese: そして、縄梯子つたってこっそり間近まで降りてきていた朔屋の阿呆象った面[ツラ]が目の前一杯に広がって、今度こそクロ、目玉ひっくり返して気絶する。
source.english: And then Sakuya's idiot mug—he had crept quietly down the rope ladder until he was inches away—loomed across her entire field of vision, and this time Kuro's eyes rolled back in her head and out she went.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「HIIH!? ───Auwhn!」

And then, Sakuya had stealthily climbed down the ladder next to her, and his face, created in the image of man's stupidity, suddenly filled her entire vision, and this time, Kuro did faint, her eyes rolling into the back of her head.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「調子出てきたみたいね、直正。
　でも余計なことはしないで。
　ほら起きて、クロ」
source.english:
“Looks like you're getting back to normal, Naomasa.
But don't get carried away.
Come on, wake up, Kuro.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Looks like you're really getting into things here, Naomasa. But please, spare us the unnecessary trouble. Come on, wake up, Kuro.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……ぅぁ……あ？
　あー……。やっぱり、夢……。
　やっぱり、会えない……。
　ふ、ふくっ、ぅぇー」
source.english:
“…Uah…ah?
Ahh…it was a dream after all…
Kuro can't see him after all…
H-hic…waah…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いるっつーの！
　ほらもっかい目ぇ開けろ！」
source.english:
“I'm here, I said!
Come on, open your eyes again!”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Uah……ah? Ah……. Knew it was a dream……. Couldn't meet him after all……. Fh, hic, waaーh!」
【Naomasa】 「Oh for-, I'm right here! Come on, just open your damn eyes one more time!」

source.japanese: 頬はたかれて目を覚まし、密航者と朔屋に囲まれてなお、夢と現、取り違えて泣き出すクロの頭を朔屋がやさしく小突く。
source.english: A slap on the cheek woke her. Surrounded by the stowaway and Sakuya, Kuro still confused dream and reality and began to cry. Sakuya gave her head a gentle knock.

target.text: She opened her eyes after being slapped on the cheek, but being surrounded by both the stowaway and Sakuya only made her confuse reality for a dream all the more, and as Kuro burst into tears, Sakuya gently poked her head.

source.japanese: そしてようやく、クロの顔に涙はまだ残っているものの、あのしまりのない笑顔が浮かんだのであった。
source.english: And at last, though tears still lingered on Kuro's face, that slack smile appeared.

target.text: Thus, at last, though tears still stained her face, that slack smile graced Kuro's cheeks once more.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「えへへへ。ほんとにいるね。
　クロの夢じゃ、ない朔屋さんだ」
source.english:
“Ehehehe. You're really here.
It's Mr. Sakuya. Not Kuro's dream.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おうとも、俺だ。
　クロよう、久しぶりだなぁ」
source.english:
“That's right. It's me.
Kuro, it's been a while.”

source.japanese: 朔屋にわしゃわしゃと白い髪掻[か]き回されるクロに、縄梯子の上から密航者が声をかける。
source.english: As Sakuya ruffled Kuro's white hair vigorously, the stowaway called down from the rope ladder.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Ehehehe. You're really here. Sakuya-san is here, not the one from Kuro's dreams.」
【Naomasa】 「Damn right it's me. Oh Kuro, it's been so looong!」
As Sakuya tousled around Kuro's white hair, the stowaway called out to her from the top of the ladder.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あなたが今また、必要になったの。
　これまで充分休養したでしょう。
　さあ、来てよ───来て！」
source.english:
“We need you again now.
You've had plenty of rest, haven't you?
Come on—come!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I have need of you once more. You must have had enough rest by now, I'm sure. Now, come───come!」

source.japanese: 朔屋に手を牽[ひ]かれ、クロは信天翁号への縄梯子を昇る。よたよたと舷側を乗り越え、着地にはやや失敗して尻餅の。ついた先には彼女を迎える顔、顔、顔。シサム、キサラ、水夫長、わらわらわらと下級水夫達。
source.english: Led by Sakuya's hand, Kuro climbed the rope ladder to the Albatross. She clambered unsteadily over the side, made a poor landing, and fell on her backside. Waiting there to greet her were faces, faces, faces. Sisam, Kisara, the boatswain, a swarming crowd of junior sailors.

target.text: Pulled along by Sakuya's hand, Kuro climbed up the rope ladder leading to the Albatross. After unsteadily clambering over the gunwale, she failed at sticking the landing and ended up falling on her butt. In front of where she landed, the sight that greeted her was one of faces, faces, so many faces. Shisamu, Kisara, the Bosun, and deck boys shuffling and bustling about.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「や！　クロ。あんたも再乗船か」
source.english: “Hey, Kuro! You're back aboard too?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Hey! Kuro. So you're back on board too?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「航海士さん！
　クロ、もどってきちゃった」
source.english:
“Mate!
Kuro's come back.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Mate! Kuro has returned!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「結局戻ってくるのはこの船なんだよなー。
　しかも今回はなにがアレだって、
　あの密航女の仕込みってことなんだよなー」
source.english:
“In the end, we come back to this ship, don't we?
And what's odd this time is—
That stowaway woman set it all up.”

source.japanese: シサムとキサラ、二人揃って視線を向けるその先に。
source.english: Where Sisam and Kisara both turned their eyes—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「In the end, it's more like this ship returned for us, riiight. And what's more, this time, the crazy thing is, this whole thing was that stowaway lady's handiwork, riiight.」
Where Shisamu and Kisara, both as one, directed their gaze.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……あの人。なにか、違う、ます。
　前と。なんか今のが、ほんとみたい」
source.english:
“…That person. Something's different.
From before. Somehow…this seems more like her real self.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Her. Something different, is. From before. Like she seems, serious now.」

source.japanese: 密航者が立っていた。その視線はまっすぐに、敵意さえ含んで海の向こうに立つ白い影を見つめていた。
source.english: The stowaway stood. Her gaze fixed straight ahead, even hostile, upon the white shadow standing across the sea.

target.text: Stood the stowaway. Her gaze, on the other hand, was directed straight ahead, filled with what could even be called hostility as she stared daggers at the white figure standing before them in the ocean.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「よぉ、クロ、帰ってきやがったか。
　よぉし、これで荷物は無事回収だ！
　とっととこんな島はずらかろうぜ！」
source.english:
“Hey, Kuro! So you're back!
Right! Cargo safely collected!
Let's get the hell off this island!”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hey there, Kuro. So you made your way back? Alright, with that, we've retrieved the goods without incident! About time we make a quick getaway from this island!」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「でも、どうやって？
　入江の出口には、あれが───」
source.english:
“But how?
At the mouth of the inlet, that thing—”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「But, how? At the way out of the inlet, that thing is───」

source.japanese: そう、この島の唯一の港が望む内湾から外洋に向かう出口には、いつの間にかそこまで近づいていたウミヒトが立ちはだかっていた。まるで、まるで？　そうではない。明らかな意図を含んで立ちはだかっていた。ここよりお前達を出すわけにはいかないと。
source.english: Yes. Between the inlet overlooked by the island's only harbor and the open sea, the Sea Person stood in their way. Unnoticed, it had come that close. As though—as though? No. It barred the way with unmistakable intent. You will not leave this place.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だよなぁ。行きはなんとか脇すり抜けて来れたんだが、こうまでびっちりと塞がれちまうとなぁ」
source.english: “Yeah. We managed to slip past it on the way in, but when it's blocking the whole way like that…”

source.japanese: 頭を掻[か]く朔屋にはもとより名案浮かぶはずもないが、航海士も水夫長も考えあぐねて思案顔。しかし、それを打ち破る一言をあっさり投げ放ったのは以前なら真っ先に投げ出され、今ならそのままウミヒトへの供物に捧げられてた扱いの女だった。
source.english: Sakuya scratched his head, with no prospect of a brilliant idea. The navigators and boatswain looked troubled, unable to think what to do. But a few casually flung words broke through their deliberations. They came from the woman who, before, would have been the first thrown overboard—and now would have been offered straight up to the Sea Person.

target.text: Indeed, at the only exit visible from the island's harbour leading from the inlet and out to open sea, and just when had it drawn so close, stood the Umihito, blocking the way. Almost as if───almost? It wasn't almost. It was standing in their way in a manner that was clearly intentional. All but telling them it would not permit them to leave this place.
【Naomasa】 「Yeeeah. We managed to somehow slip past it when coming here, but with the exit blocked this thoroughly, I don't know……」

Sakuya, scratching his head, would never have been able to come up with a good idea to begin with, but the mates as well as the Bosun also had pensive looks on their faces as they racked their brains to no avail. However, the one who casually flung out the words needed to break through this deadlock was the woman who, previously, would herself have been flung off the boat first thing, and had they been in this situation back then, she'd have been presented as an offering to the Umihito.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あっちから出られないのなら、別の水路を使えば良いだけ」
source.english: “If we can't get out that way, we only have to use another channel.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「If we can't get out from there, all we need to do is use another waterway.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだって君が、この島のこんな廻廊まで知ってるのか……。
　ま、聞いたところで意味が通るような答えは返ってこないんだろうが……」
source.english:
“How do you even know about passages like this on the island…?
Well, I doubt I'd get an answer that made sense if I asked…”

source.japanese: ぼやく朔屋の声には、微かな残響がまとわりついていた。
source.english: A faint echo clung to Sakuya's grumbling voice.

source.japanese: 信天翁号は、暗闇の中、流れのない水をかき分け進んでいた。か細い角燈の灯りはすぐに闇へと溶け飲み込まれ、天井はとても見渡せない。両岸もわずかに浮かび上がるほど。天井？　両岸？　そう、信天翁号は水路引かれた隘道を進んでいるのだった。
source.english: In the darkness, the Albatross plowed through dead-still water. The frail lantern-light dissolved at once, swallowed by the dark: the ceiling lay entirely out of sight, and even the banks showed only faintly. Ceiling? Banks? Yes—the Albatross was making her way down a narrow passage threaded by a waterway.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「伊達に信天翁号の航路に付き合っていないって言う事。
　───本当に色々なところを航海したのよ、
　この船はね」
source.english:
“I haven't followed the Albatross's voyages for nothing.
—This ship really has sailed to all sorts of places.”

source.japanese:
そう言って、密航者は微笑む。
　信天翁号の上甲板、薄気味悪げに朔屋は右に左に視線を振り分ける。そしてその横で暗闇を必死に見透そうと目を凝らすクロ。密航者たる彼女だけが平然と言葉を続ける。
source.english:
The stowaway smiled as she said it.

On the Albatross's upper deck, Sakuya glanced uneasily from side to side. Beside him, Kuro strained to see through the darkness. Only the stowaway went on speaking without concern.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あなた達が考える以上に、長い事、そう、とっても長い事、この世界の海を彷徨ってきたっけ」
source.english: “She's wandered the seas of this world for longer than you think. Yes, a very, very long time.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……だって閉じこめられてるから、そうするしかなかったわけだけど」
source.english: “…Being shut in, she didn't have much choice.”

source.japanese:
その言葉が真ならば。
　今、信天翁号が進むこの水路も、かつて通った航跡だと言うのだろうか。
source.english:
If those words were true—

Did that mean this waterway, along which the Albatross now traveled, was a course she had sailed before?

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Just how is it that you know even about these kinds of passages on this island……. Well, even if I ask, I'm pretty sure I'm not getting an answer that makes any sense……」
A faint echo followed in the wake of Sakuya's grumbling.

The Albatross, surrounded by darkness, was pushing her way forwards through still water. The feeble light of their lanterns quickly melted into the dark, engulfed by it, and the ceiling was practically impossible to see. Both banks only offered fleeting glimpses. Ceiling? Banks? Indeed, the Albatross was proceeding down a narrow path through a waterway.

【Stowaway】 「Just goes to show that I haven't been sticking around with the Albatross all this time for nothing. ───But she really has been to all kinds of places on her voyages, this ship here, hasn't she?」

Saying so, the stowaway smiled. Atop the upper deck of the Albatross, feeling ill at ease from the eeriness of this place, Sakuya's gaze swung from left to right. And standing by his side, desperately straining her eyes to see through the darkness, was Kuro. The stowaway woman alone continued to speak with an air of self-possession.
【Stowaway】 「For long, longer than you people imagine, yeah, for a very, very long time, I've been roaming the seas of this world.」
【Stowaway】 「……I mean, I'm imprisoned here, so there wasn't really anything else for me to do.」
If those words were true, then. This waterway the Albatross was proceeding down right now, perhaps she must have been saying that they were simply following in the wake she had left here long ago?

source.japanese: 暗闇の中、両岸を見通すのは難しい。だがしかし、仄かには見えるのだ、灯りは届いているのだ。現に朔屋は落ち着かなさげに、左右をへと忙しく視線を移す。しかしそれは、その実、見たくない物から視線を逸らす素振りにも似ている。そう、見たくはないのだ、誰も。この水路の両岸に打ち棄てられた物達を、はっきりとは。
source.english: In the darkness, it was hard to see the banks. But they were faintly visible; the light did reach them. Sakuya was, in fact, glancing busily left and right, looking restless. Yet it resembled the way someone averts his gaze from what he does not want to see. Yes, no one wanted a clear view of what lay abandoned on either bank of this waterway.

source.japanese:
ここはクロが取り残されていた島の地下。
　ウミヒトに外洋への出口塞がれた信天翁号は、密航者の指し示すまま舵を切った。その示された先は、建て増しされて海へとせり出し溢れ出た木造小屋どもの作りだしたわずかな隙間。シサムもキサラも水夫長も、そして朔屋すらも、そこは無いと思った。確かにせり出した小屋の床下はぎりぎりで信天翁号を通してくれるだろう。だが、その先は？　海埋め尽くす木造の島にぶち当たるだけなのでは？
source.english:
They were beneath the island where Kuro had been left behind.

With the Sea Person blocking her way out to the open ocean, the Albatross had put her helm over at the stowaway's direction. The woman had pointed toward a meager gap made by wooden shacks that successive additions had sent jutting and spilling out over the sea. Sisam, Kisara, the boatswain—even Sakuya—had all thought: there could be no way through. True, there might just be room beneath those overhanging floors for the Albatross to squeeze past. But after that? Wouldn't they simply smash into the wooden island choking the sea?

source.japanese: しかし、密航者は有無を言わせず航海士に舵を切らせた。水夫長に命じて下級水夫を走らせ、船幅ぎりぎりの隙間に信天翁号をねじ込ませた。誰もが島にぶち当たって海の藻屑になることを覚悟したが、ウミヒトに突っ込むのも御免、なにより、この島まで嵐をついて辿り着けたのは確かに、この密航者の功であったのだし。そして。
source.english: But the stowaway had allowed no argument. She made the navigators turn the helm, ordered the boatswain to send the junior sailors running, and had the Albatross forced into a gap barely as wide as her hull. Everyone braced for a collision with the island and a watery end. But no one wanted to charge into the Sea Person either. Above all, it was certainly thanks to this stowaway that they had made it through the storm to the island. And—

source.japanese:
信天翁号は進んでいるのだ。
　その先にあったこの地下水路を進んで。
source.english:
The Albatross was moving.

Along this underground waterway, which had lain beyond.

target.text: In the dark, getting a proper view of the banks proved a challenge. And yet, nevertheless, however faintly, one could still see, for the light did reach. At present, Sakuya was busying himself by looking around from left to right, unable to settle down. However, that was, in fact, done in a manner like he was averting his gaze from something he didn't want to see. Yes, something he didn't want to see, something nobody wanted to. Clearly see that which had been abandoned by the banks of this waterway, that is.

This was below the surface of the island where Kuro had been left behind, the underground. With the exit to the open sea obstructed by the Umihito, the Albatross had turned the rudder on the stowaway's instructions. The place she had shown them was a little gap found between some of the extra annexes built onto the wooden buildings that spilled out from the island and jutted into the sea. Shisamu, Kisara, the Bosun, and even Sakuya all thought that it wasn't going to work. True, the Albatross could probably barely pass under the floors of the houses jutting out. However, what about in front of them? Would they not only crash into the wooden island that filled the sea?

However, the stowaway peremptorily made the mates turn the rudder. She barked orders at the Bosun and sent the deck boys running, then squeezed the Albatross through a gap barely wide enough to fit her. Everyone on board had resigned themselves to slamming into the island and meeting their watery grave, but they would also rather pass on ramming into the Umihito, and most importantly, it was certainly also only thanks to this stowaway that they had even been able to brave the storm and arrive at this island. Thus.
The Albatross advanced. She advanced down the underground waterway that awaited them there.

source.japanese:
そこは、白骨散らばる木造家屋が堆[うずたか]く積み上がる島の上とは正反対の世界だった。
　島の上には、今は白骨になり果ててはいるものの、ありとあらゆる動物達が集められた生命の世界だとしたら。
　ここは、血も通わぬ息吹感じられぬ冷たい金属どもの世界だった。
　信天翁号が放つわずかな灯りに浮かび上がるものは、およそ人が、木の枝に草の蔓もて石を括りつけたか、あるいはその石同士を叩きつけ合って望む形に拵[こしら]えたか、それとも食べ終えた後の獣の骨を削ったか……道具というものを使い始めてからこの方、産み出してきたものが打ち棄てられていたのだった。
　道具はやがて、より高度に複雑に、道具同士が組み合わさり、器械、機械と名を変えて文明とともに発達していく。その様が残骸となって今、信天翁号が進む水路の両岸に積み上げられているのだ。
source.english:
This was the opposite of the island above, where wooden houses piled high amid scattered bones.

If the surface was a world of life, where animals of every kind had been gathered—though now reduced to bare bones—

Then here was a world of cold metal, with no blood, no breath.

What emerged in the Albatross's scant light was everything people had produced since first they began to use tools. Whether tying stones to branches with vines, striking stones together to make the shapes they wanted, or carving the bones of animals they had eaten…all of it lay abandoned here.

Tools grew ever more advanced, more complex. Combined with one another, they became apparatus, machinery, developing alongside civilization. The remains of that progress now stood heaped along both banks of the Albatross's course.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……機械っつーにしても、これはなんかがおかしいな」
source.english: “…Even for machinery, there's something wrong with this.”

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「うん。なにかね。あたしらの知っているものもあるけど。これ、時代順に並んでいるのだとしたら？」
source.english: “Yes. Something. There are things we know, but—if they're arranged in chronological order?”

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あたしらの時代よりあとの方が、
　長い───
　どういうこと？」
source.english:
“There's a longer stretch after our time—
What does that mean?”

source.japanese: そう、双子の推察裏付けるように、初めは本で見ただけの骨董品の骸がそのうち、懐かしくそして見慣れたものへと変わり、やがて、そして今は見た事もなければ何がどう動くのかもわからない物となっている。そして……見慣れ見覚えのある物共の山は遙か後方へと過ぎ去っていたのだ。
source.english: Yes. As though confirming the twins' conjecture, the carcasses of antiques known only from books had given way to things nostalgic and familiar. Then—and now—to things they had never seen, whose workings they could not imagine. The piles they recognized had passed far behind.

target.text: It was a world utterly antithetical to the surface of the island, covered as it was in wooden buildings filled with scattered bones. The island's surface was a world of life, where every conceivable animal had been gathered, even if they were now reduced to pale bone. This was a world of cold metal, where no blood circulated, where no vital breath could be felt.

What surfaced in their vision, lit up by the dim light emitted from the Albatross, was rocks tied to branches with vines, most likely by human hands, or else stones smashed together to manufacture the desired shape, or bones of beasts sharpened after they were done eating them……ever since they had begun to use tools, like so, they had abandoned that which they had formerly created.

Before long, the tools grew more sophisticated and complex: tools combined with other tools, changing name to instrument, to machine, developing in tandem with civilization. They were now broken remains, piled up on either side of the waterway through which the Albatross was travelling.
【Kisara】 「……Even for machines, something about this isn't right.」
【Shisamu】 「Yeah. There's something off, right? There's stuff here that we do recognize. But suppose these are arranged in chronological order?」
【Kisara】 「There's stuff from beyond our age, and there's way more ahead of us than behind us─── What is going on here?」

Indeed, as if to substantiate their conjecture, at first, it was musty relics they'd only ever seen in books, but soon enough, it changed into the nostalgic, then the familiar, and finally, it turned into things they'd never seen before, that they had no idea how functioned. And then……the mountain of the familiar and the recognizable passed them by, fading far into the distance.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……私のもともといたところでもね。
　珍説、奇説の類がいくらでもあって」
source.english:
“…Where I originally came from, too,
there were all sorts of strange theories.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「人類の文明というものは、少なくとも既知のレベルに達するまで、二度は崩壊している」
source.english: “Before reaching the level we know, human civilization has collapsed at least twice.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「その名残が、アトランティス、あるいはムー……その伝説として残っている、とかさ」
source.english: “And traces of it remain in the legends of Atlantis, or Mu…that sort of thing.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「少なくとも、こっちでは本当に起こっている。
　文明の崩壊と───再生？」
source.english:
“Here, at least, it's really happened.
The collapse of civilization—and its rebirth?”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「再生は……しているのかな、これで。
　直正、これが」
source.english:
“Reborn…can we really call this rebirth?
Naomasa, these are—”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「君達の知らない。誰かが封じこめた。
　過去からの───
　未来というものが、過去になるくらい、
　遙かな歳月の」
source.english:
“Things you don't know. That someone sealed away.
From a past—
So unimaginably long ago
that the future itself has become the past—”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「……So, back where I originally hail from, too. There were also any number of strange, bizarre theories.」
【Stowaway】 「What we call human civilization has, at least before reaching the level it is at today, collapsed twice.」
【Stowaway】 「The remnants of that, they remain as legends……like Atlantis, or Mu, that kind of thing.」
【Stowaway】 「At the very least, here, it truly did happen. The collapse of civilization and ───its rebirth?」
【Stowaway】 「But I wonder…… is it truly being reborn, like this. Naomasa, this here.」
【Stowaway】 「Was sealed away. By someone unknown to you. From a past so distant─── Of such staggering aeons that even the future may as well be the past.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「亡骸ってわけなのか……」
source.english: “The remains, you mean…?”

source.japanese: 朔屋、ごくりと生唾飲み込む。正直、朔屋には彼女の言葉の中にあったアトなんとかやらたる名詞はちともピンと来ない。この女、いったい何を言ってやがる？　文明の崩壊と再生だと？　つまりここに捨てられた物は……かつて実際に使われていたのだと？　その、かつて、は崩壊したのだと？　今より進んだ物を産み出した文明が、いったい何故、どうやって。
source.english: Sakuya swallowed hard. Frankly, that At-something-or-other she'd mentioned meant not a thing to him. What the hell was this woman talking about? The collapse and rebirth of civilization? So the things dumped here…had actually been used once? And that once—that whole age—had collapsed? A civilization capable of producing things more advanced than anything today: why? How?

source.japanese: その場にいた誰もが言いようのない薄気味悪さに囚われる。背筋にひっそりと汗が伝い落ちるような。その中で、ただ一人、まったく違う方向に思考を辿っていた少女が声をあげた。
source.english: An inexpressible unease gripped everyone there. As though sweat were silently trickling down their spines. Amid it all, Kuro alone had been following an entirely different train of thought. She spoke.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「みらい……かこ？　クロ知ってる。
　それはれきしの言葉。クロれきしっていえた」
source.english:
“Future…past? Kuro knows.
They're words from history. Kuro said ‘history.’”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おうおう、クロは相変わらず賢いなー」
source.english: “Yes, yes. Clever as ever, Kuro.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「So you're saying that these are corpses……」

Sakuya swallowed his saliva with an audible gulp. Truth be told, Sakuya didn't have the first clue what the proper nouns like Atlanto-something meant in relation to whatever she was talking about. Just what the hell was this woman trying to say? The collapse and rebirth of civilization? That is to say, all the stuff that had been abandoned here……had formerly seen actual use? And it had, some time in the past, collapsed? A civilization producing things more advanced than what they presently used was gone, but why, and how?

All present were seized by an ineffable eeriness. Like a bead of sweat silently rolling down along their spines. Amidst that, but a single girl, one whose thoughts had travelled down an entirely different lane, raised her voice.

【Kuro】 「Future……past? Kuro knows. Those are words about history. It's called a dark past.」 (TN: There is some wordplay here based on Kuro's speech patterns that can't be translated. While what she said could mean "Kuro said (the word) history", it could also be read as Kuro-rekishi, a "dark past/history". In modern slang use, it refers to something one would rather have erased because it is embarrassing. It originates from Turn A Gundam where it refers to a forgotten, sealed-away era of war, rather apropos.)
【Naomasa】 「That's right, that's right. You're always such a smart cookie, Kuro.」

source.japanese:
やがて、この陰鬱なだけの水路を抜けた信天翁号は、島を囲う嵐のただ中に放り出される。
　もちろん、襤褸船など木っ端微塵にしてくれようという波と風の中、クロの眠れる才気は叩き起こされ、この島での孤独な月日など感じさせぬ指示に双子の航海士が抜群の操船でもって応え、信天翁号は嵐を抜けるのだった。
source.english:
Eventually the Albatross emerged from that unrelievedly gloomy channel and was flung into the storm surrounding the island.

Naturally, in wind and waves intent upon reducing a ragged ship to splinters, Kuro's dormant brilliance was jolted awake. Nothing in her orders suggested her time alone on the island. The twin navigators answered with superb seamanship, and the Albatross passed through the storm.

target.text: Eventually, the Albatross made it out of that gloomy waterway, only for her to be thrust right into the storm encircling the island. Of course, now that they were sailing through winds and waves that were apt to smash their ramshackle ship into splinters any moment, Kuro's sleeping wit was roused out of bed, and through her instructions, so precise one could scarcely feel the lonely life she had led on this island, the twin mates responded with exceptional steering, and the Albatross escaped the storm.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「全く、本当に、憎々しい……。
　どこまでつきまとうんだ、お前達は。
　そうやってぷかぷか浮かんでるだけでも鬱陶しいのに、よくもまあ影でこそこそと」
source.english:
“Honestly. Truly loathsome…
How long are you going to follow us?
It's irritating enough just having you bobbing there, but creeping about behind the scenes as well—”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「You really, truly, are so very loathsome……. How far will you go, how long will you continue to haunt me? Just having you floating around like that is irritating enough, but you still have the temerity to skulk around in the shadows too.」

source.japanese: 遙か遠くに佇む白い影を尻目に。
source.english: With a dismissive glance at the white shadow standing far in the distance.

target.text: With a sidelong glance at the white shade standing still in the far distance.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「アウ、アウッ、アァアッ……ハーッッ」
source.english: “Au, auh, aaah…haaah!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Auh, ARGH, AAaAAA……HAー!」

source.japanese: そして、密航者は荒い息とともに、膝頽れて甲板に手を突く。
source.english: Then the stowaway's knees gave way. Breathing harshly, she planted her hands on the deck.

target.text: And then, with ragged breath, the stowaway fell to her knees and slammed her fists onto the deck.

source.japanese: 一度、朔屋は似たような光景を見ていた。極点で双子の航海士を拾い上げた時。あの時は今この時ほどではなかったものの、確かにこの娘は疲れていなかったか？　そう、今回のように素晴らしい活躍とともに、仲間を再び迎え入れたその後に。
source.english: Sakuya had seen something like this before. When they picked up the twin navigators at the pole. It had not been as bad then, but hadn't she been exhausted? Yes: just as now, after a splendid performance and the return of their companions.

target.text: Once before, Sakuya had seen a similar sight. When they had picked up the twin mates from the extreme north. Back then, it had not been as intense as it was now, but hadn't this girl been tired back then as well? Yes, after making an effort just as great as she had this time, and after welcoming back their companions.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「君、やっぱりおかしいだろ。どう考えても。
　なんでそんなに疲労しちまってるんだ!?」
source.english:
“There's something wrong with you, isn't there? Any way you look at it.
Why are you so exhausted!?”

source.japanese: 駆け寄る朔屋にのろのろと顔を上げた密航者の言うことには。
source.english: Sakuya ran over. The stowaway slowly raised her face and said:

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Hey, you, there really is something strange about you. No matter how I look at this. Why are you getting so exhausted!?」
Slowly raising her head at Sakuya rushing to her side, this is what the stowaway said.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……なんで覗くかなあ、一応、人目を忍んでいるつもりなのに」
source.english: “…Why do you have to look? I am trying to keep out of sight, you know.”

source.japanese:
減らず口を吐く言葉は擦[す]り切れた響きが強いものの、その視線は朔屋に振り向けられてから、船の進む先へと。
　信天翁号は再び、外洋に戻る。
　相変わらずスクラップ寸前の船体、しかしその血肉たる乗り組み達は再び集い来る。そう、あと少し。その時、信天翁号はどこへ旅立とうというのか。
source.english:
The words were as impudent as ever, though her voice sounded badly frayed; her gaze left Sakuya and went to the waters ahead.

The Albatross returned once more to the open sea.

Her hull was as close to scrap as ever, yet her crew—her flesh and blood—were gathering to her again. Yes, only a little more. When that time came, where would the Albatross set sail for?

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「……Why did you have to come peek? I was kind of hoping to do this away from any prying eyes.」

The tone of her cheeky response was awfully worn-out, but she diverted her gaze from Sakuya to the direction the ship was heading. The Albatross returned to the open sea once more. The ship's hull was, as ever, on the verge of being scrap, but the crew that made up her flesh and blood was gathering together once more. Yes, just a little more. And when that time came, just where would the Albatross be setting out for?

source.japanese: ───かくして信天翁号に、船長が戻ってきたのだった。
source.english: —And thus the captain returned to the Albatross.

target.text: ───Thus, the captain returned to the Albatross.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もう君が、何をやらかしたって驚いたりはしない、しないがよぉ……」
source.english: “Nothing you do is going to surprise me anymore. Nothing. But still…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「さすがにこれは
　無茶苦茶なんじゃないかっ？」
source.english:
“Isn't this a bit much,
even for you?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「At this point, nothing you can pull is ever going to surprise me, it really won't, but still……」
【Naomasa】 「Surely this has to be way too reckless, no?」

source.japanese:
目も丸く開いた口から言葉絞り出す朔屋の体は、彼の立つ信天翁号上甲板の船縁、その眼前の海に浮かび上がってきた物を見て驚愕に打たれ硬直していた。
　その浮かび上がってきた物とは。鉄の外殻で全身を覆った船。いや、水上を走る物を船と言うのだから水中より現れたこれは船ではないと言える。水の中を走るもの、潜水艦。
source.english:
At the rail of the Albatross's upper deck, Sakuya stood rigid with shock, eyes round, squeezing words from his open mouth at the thing that had surfaced in the sea before him.

What had surfaced? A vessel covered entirely in an iron shell. No: a ship travels over water, so this thing emerging from beneath it might be said not to be a ship. Something that travels underwater. A submarine.

source.japanese: 果たして、この潜水艦という物を初めて考えついた者はいったい何を考えていたのだろう。人の生息域ではない水中を旅するための物を作ろうなどと。いや、人とはそういうものなのかもしれない。これもまた、未知の世界への欲求が創りあげた物の末裔なのだ。
source.english: What, indeed, had the first person to conceive of a submarine been thinking? To make something for traveling underwater, where humans do not live. No, perhaps that is what humans are like. This too was a descendant of things born from a longing for an unknown world.

target.text: Eyes like saucers, wringing the words out from his throat, Sakuya stood by the gunwale of the upper deck of the Albatross, and when he saw that thing surfacing in the ocean right before his very eyes, the shock struck him so hard his body went completely stiff. The thing that emerged. Turned out to be that ship whose entire hull was covered in an iron shell. No, a ship is something that travels on water, so this thing appearing from below that water couldn't be called a ship. It travelled through the water, a submarine.

Really, just what exactly was the man who first came up with the concept of the submarine thinking, one could wonder. Let me create something for the express purpose of travelling underwater, a place far removed from the realm of human habitation, or something of the sort. No, perhaps that is simply how humanity is. This, too, was but another descendant of the things built to satisfy the desire to explore unknown worlds.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「確かに、泪さんを迎えに行くには、これに乗るしかないわけなんだが……」
source.english: “Sure, if we're going to fetch Rui, we have to get aboard this thing…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「だからといって、犬や馬や執事じゃないんだ。呼んだってほいほい来るもんじゃないだろうに」
source.english: “But it's not a dog, or a horse, or a butler. It shouldn't just come running when you call.”

source.japanese:
しかし事実、泪を捜しに行くためにこれを呼び出したのだ、密航者は。船縁で手を叩いたわけではない。形はある程度似ているが、潜水艦は鯉ではない。密航者は、よりタチの悪い事に、
『じゃぁ、行こうか』
　そんな気軽な一言で。
　朔屋がそんな簡単なものでもなかろうと言い返す間もなく、まるで密航者の言葉を待っていたかのように目の前にこれを浮上させたのだ。
source.english:
Yet that was exactly what the stowaway had done: called it up to go and find Rui. She had not clapped her hands at the rail. Similar though their shapes might be, a submarine was no carp. Worse, the stowaway had merely said,

‘Well, shall we go?’

That casually.

Before Sakuya could protest that it surely wasn't that simple, she had brought it to the surface before them, as though it had been waiting for her words.

source.japanese:
すでに朔屋は疑わなくなっていた。密航者のこの尋常ではない能力を。
　シサム、キサラを迎えに行くために、信天翁号に氷の海を渡らせ───
　クロを迎えに行くために、現れ立ちはだかったウミヒトを躱[かわ]してみせた。
source.english:
By now Sakuya no longer doubted the stowaway's extraordinary power.

To fetch Sisam and Kisara, she had made the Albatross cross a sea of ice—

To fetch Kuro, she had evaded the Sea Person that appeared to bar their way.

source.japanese:
そう、信じざるを得ない。
　彼女は自在に操るのだ、船を。
　もはや信天翁号だけではなく、この潜水艦をも。どうやって？　そんなこと説明がつくわけがない。しかし、とにかくやってしまうのだ。
source.english:
Yes, he had to believe it.

She could control vessels at will.

Not just the Albatross anymore, but this submarine too. How? There could be no explanation for such a thing. Yet she did it anyway.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はぁ、もう十分驚いたからいいや。
　じゃ、さっさと泪さんのとこに行こうか」
source.english:
“Hah. All right, I've had enough surprises.
Let's hurry over to Rui.”

source.japanese: 呆れの溜息ついて、朔屋は密航者へと振り向く。しかし、そこには誰もおらず。
source.english: With an exasperated sigh, Sakuya turned to the stowaway. But no one was there.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Sure, if we're going to pick up Rui-san, then we'll have to ride this thing, but……」
【Naomasa】 「While that may be true, it's not a dog, a horse, or a butler. It's not going to just show up here because you call for it, surely.」

However, in reality, the stowaway, who had summoned this so they could go search for Rui. Had not clapped her hands by the gunwale. Though it bore some resemblance, the submarine was not a carp. Instead, the stowaway, in a display far more galling, said: 『Alright, let's go then?』 (TN: The act of clapping to summon something is deeply rooted in Japanese culture, from myth to religion to carp ponds.)

And with that casual line. Sakuya wasn't even given the time to retort that surely it wouldn't be so simple, for this thing emerged right before his eyes as though it had only been waiting for the stowaway to give the command.

Sakuya had already stopped doubting it. This extraordinary ability the stowaway was possessed of. When they went to pick up Shisamu and Kisara, she made the Albatross cross a sea of ice─── When they went to pick up Kuro, she evaded the Umihito that had emerged before them to block their path.

Indeed, he was left no choice but to believe in it. The woman could control it at will, the ship. And it was no longer just the Albatross, but this submarine as well. How? There was simply no way to explain it. Yet she still went ahead and did it.
【Naomasa】 「Haaah, I'm more than surprised enough by now, so whatever. Alright then, let's just hurry up and get down to Rui-san, shall we?」
Heaving a sigh of exasperation, Sakuya turned towards the stowaway. However, there was nobody there.

source.english: “Hm?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Hm?」

source.japanese: 首を傾げた瞬間、予感めいたものが朔屋の頭を駆ける。首筋が冷えたかのような類の予感だ。朔屋、ばばっと素早く左右に視線を振り分けると、勘だけで手近なバラックの一つを回り込む。果たしてそこには。
source.english: As he tilted his head, something like a premonition shot through him. The kind that chills the back of your neck. Sakuya glanced quickly left and right, then, following his instincts alone, rounded a nearby shanty. Sure enough—

target.text: The instant he tilted his head, something akin to a premonition rushed through Sakuya's head. A premonition of the sort that made him feel like a chill was running down his neck. After quickly looking left and right, he circled around a nearby shack on pure instinct. Sure enough, there she was.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ！　やっぱり！」
source.english: “Ah! I knew it!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Aah! I knew it!」

source.japanese: そこには、倒れんとする我が身をこらえるためだったのか、はたまたこれから起き上がろうとしていたのか、壁に力無く手をついて座り込む密航者の姿だった。
source.english: There sat the stowaway, one hand resting weakly against the wall. Had she been trying to keep herself from collapsing? Or was she about to get up?

target.text: There, perhaps on the verge of collapse and trying to endure it, or else attempting to get back on her feet, the stowaway was sitting feebly with both hands braced against the wall.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あなたって───最低の男ね」
source.english: “You—are the absolute worst.”

source.japanese: 朔屋が自分の背後に現れたのを感じ取り、密航者は恨めしげに振り向いたものの、発した言葉は平素と変わらず。
source.english: Sensing Sakuya behind her, the stowaway turned resentfully. Yet her words were no different from usual.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、自覚はあるが。いやそうじゃないだろう。君、また無茶したんじゃないのか？　いや、無茶だよな、どう考えたって。あんな物を呼び出したんだから！」
source.english: “Well, I know that. No, that's not the point. Haven't you pushed yourself too hard again? No, of course you have. Any way you look at it. You summoned that thing!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「You are just───a horrible man, you know that?」
Sensing Sakuya appearing behind her, the stowaway looked over her shoulder reproachfully, but the words she spoke were the same as ever.

【Naomasa】 「Oh, I'm well aware of that myself. No, that's not the point here. You're being reckless again, aren't you? No, you definitely are, no matter how you look at this. This is because you summoned that thing!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「気にしないで」
source.english: “Don't worry about it.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Don't worry about it.」

source.japanese: そう言って、密航者、立ち上がる。朔屋が潜水艦見て呆然としている間に回復したのか、服についた埃払いながら、朔屋の前まで歩いてくる様も軽快。
source.english: Saying that, the stowaway got up. Had she recovered while Sakuya gaped at the submarine? She brushed the dust from her clothes and walked lightly toward him.

target.text: Saying that, the stowaway rose to her feet. She must have recovered while Sakuya was looking at the submarine in dumb amazement, for the way she walked up to Sakuya, brushing the dust off her clothes all the while, was even light.

source.japanese: かに見えた。
source.english: Or so it seemed.

target.text: Or so it seemed.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おい！　大丈夫か？」
source.english: “Hey! Are you all right?”

source.japanese: 目の前まで来てよろめいた密航者の体を朔屋は支える。朔屋の腕の中に収まるかのように、胸に手を当て頬を当てる、まるでその様抱き合う恋人同士のよう。
source.english: Sakuya caught the stowaway, who had staggered right up to him. As if nestling into Sakuya’s arms, the stowaway placed a hand on his chest and rested her cheek against him—just like a pair of lovers embracing.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Oi! Are you okay?」

Sakuya supported the stowaway's body, who had stumbled after walking right up to him. One hand on her chest, the other on her cheek, like he was holding her within his arms, almost exactly like embracing lovers.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「頼んでいい？　ちょっと縋[すが]らせて。
　いやらしい事してもいいけど、途中で気絶するかも知れないから、手加減してね」
source.english:
“Can I ask you a favor? Let me cling to you for a bit.
You can do naughty things to me, but I might pass out partway through, so please go easy on me.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……どいつもこいつも、俺はみんなの中でどういう扱いをされているんだおっとっと。リクエストにお答えしてみました」
source.english: “……Every single one of you—how am I being treated by all of you? Oops. I tried to fulfill your request.”

source.japanese: 体密着されてそう囁かれれば、朔屋もうっかり勘違いのふりして調子に乗って、その尻と胸に手を回してみたものの。
source.english: With her body pressed against his and her whisper in his ear, Sakuya pretended to misunderstand, let himself get carried away, and put his hands on her butt and breasts—but.

source.japanese: 冷えた肌に鼓動も息も弱く震える様子伝われば、慌てて手を不純な位置より引き上げて密航者の肩つかみその体を支える。
source.english: When he felt her chilled skin, faint heartbeat, weak breath, and trembling, he hurriedly withdrew his hands from their inappropriate positions, grabbed the stowaway’s shoulders, and steadied her.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「って君、マジで消耗してるじゃないかッ」
source.english: “You're seriously worn out!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Can I ask you a favour? Just let me hold on to you for a bit. You can do some naughty stuff with me if you want, but I might faint halfway through, so be gentle, okay?」
【Naomasa】 「……This goes for each and every one of you, but just what kind of horrible treatment am I receiving inside your hea───woah there. I tried answering your request.」

When he had that whispered to him while she pressed her body firmly against him, Sakuya got a little carried away and unconsciously acted like she'd gotten the wrong idea, all while moving his hands to her butt and chest, but.

When the state of her cold skin, her feeble pulse and breath, as well as her shivering body was felt by him, he pulled his hands back from their impure positions in a hurry, instead grabbing the stowaway by the shoulders and supporting her body.
【Naomasa】 「Hey, you, come on, you are seriously fatigued!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「使えば使い減りする。それが全ての大法則。
　私だってそう。でもまだしばらくは保つ、
　走れる」
source.english:
“Use something, and it wears away. That's the great law of everything.
It applies to me too. But I can last a while longer.
I can still run.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「What you use will be spent. That is the fundamental law of all. I'm no different. But I'll still endure a little while longer. I can still sail.」

source.japanese:
そう言って、密航者は体の重み朔屋にいくばくか預けて目を閉じる。
　朔屋としては、その体支えてしばらくの間、そう密航者が再び目を開き突き飛ばすように彼を潜水艦へと共に乗り込むように促すまでの間、じっとしている他ないのだった。
source.english:
With that, the stowaway rested some of her weight on Sakuya and closed her eyes.

Sakuya could only support her and stay still for a while. Until she opened her eyes again and urged him, almost pushing him, to board the submarine with her.

target.text: Having said that, the stowaway leaned some of her body weight against Sakuya and closed her eyes. As for Sakuya, in the brief while he supported her, yes, that brief while until the stowaway once more opened her eyes and almost pushed him inside as she urged him to board the submarine together with her, all he could do was remain entirely still.

source.japanese:
朔屋と密航者が乗り込んだのと同時に潜水艦は水音立てて海中へと沈みゆく。
　初めは清[さや]かな月光吸い込んで仄[ほの]かに青をなしていた海の色も、またたくまに明度下がり闇と変わらぬ様で潜水艦の窓を塗り込める。
source.english:
The moment Sakuya and the stowaway boarded, the submarine sank into the sea with a splash.

At first, the water was faintly blue, drinking in the clear moonlight. In moments it darkened until it painted the submarine's windows with something indistinguishable from night.

target.text: Right as Sakuya boarded it, the submarine dove into the sea with the sound of splashing water. The colour of the ocean, at first a faint blue from the pure moonlight it was absorbing, lost its brightness in the blink of an eye, forming a veil of unchanging dark that painted over the submarine's windows.

source.japanese: 一米、また一米[メートル]と鉄でできた船体が沈むたび、不気味な音が艦内には響き渡り、どうにも朔屋を落ち着かない気分にさせる。なにしろそれは潜水艦が周囲からの水の圧力に耐えるために歯食いしばる音、鉄の船体が軋む音。もし、この潜水艦が握り潰さんとする力に耐えかねたその時は、朔屋の体は周囲より圧壊する艦の鉄板に挽き潰されるか、ぼきりと折れたそこから海中に放り出されて水の力にひしゃげるか。
source.english: Meter by meter, as the iron hull sank, uncanny sounds resounded inside, making Sakuya uneasy. They were the submarine gritting its teeth against the pressure of the surrounding water: the creaking of its iron hull. If it failed to withstand that crushing force, Sakuya would be ground to pulp between the plates collapsing around him—or flung into the sea through a break in the hull and flattened by the water.

source.japanese: そう水の底とは、人間にとっては死の世界なのだ。圧力なくとも空気はない。こんなところで生きていける者は人魚か魚人の類だけ。その人魚の一人を朔屋達は捜しに出たのだが。
source.english: Yes, beneath the water lay a world of death for humans. Even without the pressure, there was no air. Only mermaids, fish-men and their like could live here. Sakuya and the stowaway had set out to find one such mermaid.

target.text: Whenever the hull wrought of iron descended one metre after another, an eerie noise resounded through the vessel that made it impossible for Sakuya to feel at ease. After all, that noise was the sound of the submarine clenching its teeth to withstand the pressure of the surrounding water, the sound of the iron hull creaking and jarring.
