Maybe, just maybe, when the time came that this submarine was unable to endure that pressure, that crushing force clenching down upon it, would Sakuya's body be ground into a paste by the iron plates of the vessel mangled by the pressure bearing down from outside, or would it snap in two, expelling him into the ocean to be squashed flat by the force of the water?

Yes, the watery depths are a world of death in the eyes of mankind. Even disregarding the pressure, there is no air to breathe. Only mermen and mermaids could live in a place like this. It was, however, one of those very mermaids that Sakuya and the stowaway had set out to find.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……私のもといたところでも、
　いずれこんな『兵器』を造り出すようになるのかしらね……」
source.english:
“…I wonder if, where I came from,
we'll eventually make ‘weapons’ like this too…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「……I wonder if, even in the place I originally hail from, they'd also have made a『weapon』 like this at some point……」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「海の中を往く船───か。驚異の、夢の創造物なのに……まあ人の性[さが]を、今はどうこう言う気はないけれど」
source.english: “A ship that travels through the sea. Such a wondrous creation, a thing of dreams…and yet. Well, I don't intend to argue about human nature now.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「A ship sailing through the ocean───is it? A creation from the realm of wonder, of dreams, and yet……well, I don't really feel like commenting on the nature of man right now.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「一つ不満があるとすれば、せっかくの海の中なのに、外の様子が見られないこと、か」
source.english: “If I have one complaint, it's that we can't see outside, despite being here in the sea.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……それは同感だけどさ、なんかこの船、軋んで、いまはそれがおっかない……」
source.english: “…I agree, but this ship keeps creaking, and right now that's scaring me…”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「If I had to make one complaint, it would be that, despite heading all the way down into the ocean, we can't see what it looks like outside, I guess?」
【Naomasa】 「……I agree with you there, but, this ship is kind of creaking, and that's got me really scared……」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「怖い？　それならもっとそばに寄って。
　ふふっ……役得だ」
source.english:
“Scared? Then come a little closer. Hehe…
This is a perk of the job.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Scared? Then come sit down closer to me. Huhu……now that's a nice perk.」

source.japanese: 言われるままに朔屋、密航者の隣に腰を下ろし、身を寄せる。今ひとつ実感はないものの、確かにここは海の底。軋みは響き、窓の外を覗いても深海の闇。空気はあれど風はなく、それを求めて外に出る事もかなわない。もし、たった一人でこんなとこに閉じこめられていたとしたら……朔屋などは一日で夢の世界へ旅立つだろう。それだけに、今は密航者の体から伝わる温もりがありがたかった。
source.english: Sakuya sat beside the stowaway and leaned in. It still didn’t feel real, but this was the bottom of the ocean. Creaking echoed; he peered out the window and saw only the dark deep. There was air, no wind, and going outside to find it was out of the question. If he’d been locked away in a place like this all by himself… Sakuya would likely have drifted off into the world of dreams within a day. For that very reason, he was grateful for the warmth radiating from the stowaway’s body.

target.text: Doing as he was told, Sakuya sat down next to the stowaway, leaning into her. It didn't feel real in the slightest right now, but this was, undoubtedly, the bottom of the sea. The creaking echoed, and all he could see from peeking out the windows was the black of the abyssal dark of the deep sea. They had air, but there was no wind, and should one go outside in search of it, that desire would not be granted.

If, hypothetically, he had been locked away in a place like this all by himself……the likes of Sakuya would surely have left for a better place in the land of dreams on the first day. That was precisely why he was so grateful for the warmth he could feel reaching him from the stowaway's body right now.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「番が、何かというと寄り添いたがる気持ち、なんとなく、判ってきたかな。直正、君の身体を、もっとくっつけて」
source.english: “I think I’m starting to understand that feeling couples have—how they always want to be close to each other. Naomasa, press your body closer to mine.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いいけど……これ、なんか変な気分になりそうだ……」
source.english: “Fine… but this might make me feel kind of weird…”

source.japanese: いつの間にか、寄り添うだけでなく膝の上にまで上ってきた密航者の体に、朔屋の腕は自然と回る。柔らかな胸の膨らみが押しつけられ、たまらず朔屋の手が伸びる。
source.english: Before he knew it, Sakuya’s arm had wrapped around the stowaway, who had not only snuggled up to him but had even climbed onto his lap. The soft curve of her breast pressed against him, and unable to resist, Sakuya reached out his hand.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I guess I've kind of come to understand that, how do you put it, feeling of wanting to nestle close together that mated pairs have. Naomasa, press your body closer.」
【Naomasa】 「Sure, but……I'm probably going to get in a kind of weird mood sitting like this……」

Sakuya automatically wrapped his arms around the stowaway's body that, without him really noticing when, was no longer just leaning against him but now also on top of his knees. The soft mounds of her chest pressed against him, and unable to bear it, Sakuya reached out with his hand.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あン……今は、触るだけで、ね？
　いずれ落ち着いたら、その時に、
　続き……ね？」
source.english:
“Ahh… For now, just touching, okay?
Once things settle down, then…
we’ll continue, okay?”

source.japanese: 触るだけならと許しを得れば、朔屋の手は密航者の乳房を掴む。その刺激に密航者が身じろぎすれば、尻は揺すられ朔屋の股間も落ち着きをなくす。
source.english: Once granted permission on the condition that he merely touch, Sakuya closed a hand around the stowaway’s breast. She squirmed at the sensation, rocking her backside against him, and his groin, too, grew restless.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Anh……only touching for now, okay? Things will calm down soon, and when that time comes, we'll continue……alright?」

Now that he had been granted permission if he restrained himself to only touching, Sakuya's hand grabbed the stowaway's breasts. When the stowaway wriggled and stirred from that stimulation, her behind shook, making Sakuya's crotch lose its calm as well.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ん……はぁー……。あ……。
　あぁ……君の……もうこんな、硬くなって。
　ふぁ……後で……後でだよ……繋がるのは、
　私も、君も、あ……と……で……ちゅ」
source.english:
“Mm… Haa… Ah… Ah… Yours…
it’s already so… hard. Ah… Later…
later, okay… coming together…
for both of us… la… ter… mwah.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Nh……haah……. Ah……. Aah……you're……already so hard. Fwah……later……wait until later…… we'll be bound together, you and I. I……said……later……chu」

source.japanese: 目を閉じ迫る密航者の唇に自分のものを重ね合わせ、舌を絡めて唾液を交わす。薄灯りの下ゆっくりと、響く軋みを遠くに追いやり、朔屋と密航者は水底での愛撫に耽[ふけ]りもしたのだった。
source.english: He pressed his lips against those of the stowaway, who closed her eyes and drew near, and entwined his tongue with hers, exchanging saliva. Slowly, beneath the dim light, pushing the echoing creak far away, Sakuya and the stowaway lost themselves in caresses at the bottom of the sea.

target.text: Closing his eyes and drawing closer, he placed his lips atop the stowaway's, coiling tongue around tongue while swapping saliva. Taking their time beneath the dim light, driving that resounding creaking far, far away, Sakuya and the stowaway engrossed themselves in their caressing at the bottom of the sea.

source.japanese: そんな気の紛らわしもできるからこそ陰気な潜水音楽にも幾分慣れるというものの、この広い海のどこかにいる尋ね人の元へ向かわなくてはならないのだ。朔屋の心も陰気に染まり、この海底の旅はいつまで続くのか、もし二万海里かけて世界中の海（の底）を旅する奴がいたとしたら、そいつはきっと気違いだ、そうも思って溜息つくも、泪への思慕は拭いがたくそれだけを支えにまぁ何日かは耐えてもみようと、この男にしては珍しく殊勝な覚悟を決めたのだが。
source.english: It was precisely because he could distract himself like this that he had grown somewhat accustomed to the gloomy underwater music—but he still had to make his way to the person he was searching for, somewhere out there in this vast ocean. Sakuya’s spirit, too, had grown gloomy. He wondered how long this journey across the ocean floor would last. He sighed, thinking that if there were anyone who would travel twenty thousand nautical miles across the ocean floors of the entire world, that person would surely be mad. Yet his longing for Rui was impossible to shake off, and with that as his sole support, he resolved—in a rare display of fortitude for a man like him—to endure it for a few days, but…

target.text: It was precisely through being able to beguile the time in such a way that they had managed to grow somewhat accustomed to even the gloomy music of submersion, but there was still a missing person somewhere in this vast sea they needed to head for.

Sakuya's heart was also tainted by the gloom; how long would this journey along the seabed take, and if there were any who decided to travel all twenty-thousand nautical miles from one side of the (bottom of the) sea to the other, they were certainly touched in the head, but even as Sakuya thought so while sighing, he couldn't fully rid himself of his yearning for Rui, and, well, he'd probably last a few days or so with that as his only source of strength, an unusually laudable resolve for this man, but.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ちょっと詐欺じゃあないのか、泪さん。まさかこんな簡単に会えるなんてさぁ」
source.english: “Isn't this cheating a little, Rui? I never thought we'd find you this easily.”

source.japanese:
そう、あっさりと尋ね人は見つかったのだ。潜水艦が海の底を進み始めてから、そうも経たぬうちに。
　海の底の暗闇しか映さぬとはいえ間近を通る魚くらいは眺める事はできる、無聊かこってそれを眺めるために潜水艦の窓を覗き込む目の前に、泪が不意に現れた時には、朔屋、心底たまげた。
　鉄の塊に穿[うが]たれた窓の裡[うち]に朔屋を認めた泪は、にっこり笑ってコンコンと窓さえ叩いてみせたのだ。
source.english:
Yes, they had found her with astonishing ease, not long after the submarine began its journey along the seabed.

The windows showed only the dark depths, but one could at least watch fish passing close by. Sakuya was peering through a window to relieve his boredom when Rui suddenly appeared before him. He was utterly astonished.

Recognizing Sakuya within the window pierced through that mass of iron, Rui smiled sweetly and even tapped on the glass.

source.japanese:
そのまま、海を優雅に泳ぐ泪に導かれて辿り着いたのが、ここ。
　泪の故郷というか実家というか、あの海底の洞窟だった。あの時と同じ場所に潜水艦は浮上し、めでたく朔屋と泪は邂逅を果たす。
　しかし、開口一番、朔屋の口から出たのは先述の、旧懐の欠片もなければ道理も通らぬ恨み言だった。
source.english:
And here was where they had arrived, guided by Rui as she swam gracefully through the sea.

That cave beneath the sea: Rui's homeland, or family home. The submarine surfaced in the same place as before, and Sakuya and Rui were happily reunited.

Yet the first words from Sakuya's mouth were the complaint already quoted, devoid of either fond reminiscence or sense.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Aren't you kind of cheating us here, Rui-san? I never thought we'd be able to meet again so easily, seriously.」

Indeed, they had easily found the woman they were looking for. And not even that long after the submarine first began to glide along the seabed. Even if all it reflected was the abyssal dark of the bottom of the sea, they could at least gaze out on the fish swimming close by them, and when, right before his eyes, as he gazed into the dark while lamenting his ennui, Rui suddenly appeared, Sakuya was shocked from the bottom of his heart. When Rui caught sight of Sakuya through the window cut into the mass of iron, she even knocked softly against the glass with a cheerful smile.

And just like that, they were led to this place by Rui as she elegantly swam through the ocean, but this place was. It was Rui's home, or at least her parents' home, whatever one would call it: that cave at the bottom of the sea. The submarine surfaced in the very same place as it had back then, and Sakuya and Rui carried out their auspicious chance reunion. However, before anything else, the very first words that came out of Sakuya's mouth were, as mentioned above, words of reproach without a shred of nostalgic fondness or even sense.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「大体、なんだってここの近くにいたんだい？　あんまり来たいとこでもないでしょうに」
source.english: “Anyway, why were you near here? It's not exactly somewhere you'd want to come, is it?”

source.japanese:
泪にしてみれば、退屈紛らわしに海の中を当てもなく泳ぎ回っているのだ、図らずもこの近くを通る事もあるという。
　朔屋にももし、事態の流れを見る目があれな気付きもしたろう。何故、潜水艦はそうもかからずに泪に会えたのか、何故泪はそうもかからずにこの洞窟まで朔屋達を誘えたのか。答えは朔屋、お前の隣にある。最初からここに信天翁号を向かわせ、潜水艦を呼んだ者が。潜水艦という密閉された空間から解放されて背伸びなぞしている女が。
source.english:
For Rui, swimming aimlessly through the sea to kill her boredom, happening to pass nearby was nothing unusual.

Had Sakuya possessed any eye for the course of events, he might have noticed. Why had the submarine found Rui so quickly? Why had Rui been able to guide them to this cave so quickly? The answer, Sakuya, stands beside you. The one who brought the Albatross here and called the submarine in the first place. The woman stretching now that she was free of the submarine's sealed confines.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「To begin with, why are you even staying so close to this place? I'm pretty sure this isn't somewhere you'd really want to come.」

According to Rui, she had been swimming aimlessly around the seas to relieve herself from boredom, and she had also passed by this place by chance. If Sakuya had the ability to see through and understand the flow of events, then even he would surely have noticed. Why exactly was the submarine able to meet up with Rui so quickly, and why had Rui led Sakuya and the stowaway to this cave so quickly? The answer, dear Sakuya, is right by your side. The one who had, from the very beginning, steered the Albatross in this direction and summoned forth the submarine. The woman currently stretching her back after being released from the hermetically sealed space that was the submarine.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「───退屈の、無聊の果てに見たのが、直さんだけならまだしもの。こちらは？」
source.english: “—After all that boredom and idleness, seeing Nao would have been one thing. But who might this be?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「───If what I saw at the end of my boredom, my ennui, was Nao-san and Nao-san alone, that would have been preferable. You would be?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「見た通りの、密航者。
　泪さんはあちらから逃げて。
　私たちは、あなたの持ち物を取り返すから」
source.english:
“A stowaway, as you can see.
Rui, get out that way.
We'll recover what belongs to you.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Exactly what I look like, a stowaway. You go make your escape from here. We are here to retrieve one of your belongings.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、かくして泪さんも信天翁号に戻る事になったのだった、めでたしめでたし。
　───ん？　なんだって？」
source.english:
“Ah, and thus Rui returned to the Albatross too. Happily ever after.
—Hm? What was that?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Right, and thus, Rui-san also returned to the Albatross, and they all lived happily ever after. ───Hm? Wait, what was that?」

source.japanese:
朔屋よ、まだ海底の旅は終わっていない。
　こちらに顔を向けて、にぃっと笑う密航者の姿に、朔屋、嫌な予感を覚えたのだった。
source.english:
Sakuya, the voyage beneath the sea is not over yet.

The stowaway turned toward him and grinned. A bad feeling came over him.

target.text: O Sakuya, your journey at the bottom of the sea is yet to come to a close. When he saw the stowaway looking his way with a broad grin on her face, Sakuya felt a sense of foreboding deep in his bones.

source.japanese: それは、朔屋にも見覚えのあるものだった。
source.english: It was something Sakuya recognized too.

target.text: It was something even Sakuya recalled seeing before.

source.japanese: 泪の父親である海の長上おわす座といえばよいか、その父親たるや、泪とは似ても似つかぬ容貌にてその巨躯威容まさに海は深淵をはらむを体現したかのよう。幸いにして、その父御も眷属たる魚怪どもも不思議と今はこの場におらず、またもこの密航者が何か細工をしたのかと朔屋は訝るものの、確信も持てずにそのうち深く考えるのをやめた。
source.english: This, one might say, was the seat of the lord of the sea—Rui’s father. And the father himself could scarcely have looked less like Rui: vast and imposing, he seemed the very embodiment of the abyss the sea held in its depths. Fortunately, neither that august father nor his retinue of fish-monsters was presently there. Sakuya wondered whether the stowaway had contrived this too; unable to be sure, he soon gave up thinking deeply about it.

source.japanese: そう、主も従者も今は不在のこの場に、それは設えられていた。『世界模型』とあの飄々としてつかみ所のなさすぎた殺し屋兼悪友は言っていた。それはまさに、体を表す名だと朔屋も思う。
source.english: Yes. Here, with master and attendants absent, it stood. The airy, impossibly elusive assassin who was also his disreputable friend had called it a ‘world model.’ Sakuya too thought the name suited what it was.

source.japanese: 一つの大きな部屋ほどもある巨大な円盤状の土台の面に、海と陸との地図が模されている。その精緻、陸の盛り上がりや海水面の起伏などをも再現し、その天蓋は、ドーム状に細い鋼材を何条にも、天球儀とよく似た式に張り巡らせている。
source.english: The surface of a huge circular base, as large as a room, reproduced a map of sea and land. So precise was it that even the rise of the land and the undulations of the water were modeled. Above it, slender lengths of steel formed a dome, arranged much like a celestial globe.

source.japanese:
以前に遠目にちらと見た時には、なにしろあの時は泪父娘の再会の場であったし、その後には魚怪どもに追い立てられて這々の体でこの場を逃げ出したのだから。
　なので、改めてその世界模型に近づき、その全容を視界に収めて朔屋は思わず言葉こぼして後、絶句する。
source.english:
Before, he had only glimpsed it from a distance. That had been the occasion of Rui's reunion with her father, after all. Then the fish-monsters had chased them, and they had fled this place in utter disarray.

Now, approaching the world model anew and taking in its entirety, Sakuya let a few words slip out—and was speechless.

target.text: It was the throne occupied by Rui's father, the ruler of the seas, a father with features that did not remotely resemble Rui's own and a gargantuan body that seemed the embodiment of the abyss contained deep in the sea. Fortunately, this father and the fish monsters who made up his kin were not present, curiously, and though Sakuya suspected that the stowaway had once more tampered with things behind the scenes, without any confidence, he gave up on thinking any deeper on the subject soon enough.

Indeed, in this place currently lacking both a regent and subjects, that thing had been installed. A『model of the world』, as that overly elusive and aloof murderer-cum-buddy of his had called it. It was a name that quite literally represented its form, Sakuya thought.

On the surface of a massive, disc-shaped base, one as large as an entire room, a map of the land and seas was depicted. The very minute details, like the bulging of the land and the undulations of the surface of the sea, had also been recreated, and several thin strips of steel stretched across it, coming together to form a dome-shaped covering in a manner bearing a close resemblance to a celestial globe.

When he had previously seen it from a distance, it had been during Rui's father-daughter reunion, and after that, he'd been chased away by the fish monsters, scrambling to get out of there. Therefore, when he once again drew closer to that model of the world, the full scope of it within his vision, after unconsciously letting a few words spill from his lips, he was left speechless.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだぁ、こりゃぁ……」
source.english: “What the hell…is this…?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「What in the world is this……」

source.japanese: 答えを求めて、隣に立つ密航者を見れば、彼女の視線は真っ直ぐに模型の一部に注がれている。朔屋もその視線を追って目を向ければ。
source.english: Seeking an answer, he looked at the stowaway beside him. Her eyes were fixed straight upon one part of the model. Sakuya followed her gaze.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ん？　なんだ、あれは」
source.english: “Hm? What's that?”

target.text: When he looked to the stowaway standing by his side for answers, the girl's gaze was already aimed directly at a particular part of the model. And when Sakuya followed her gaze with his own.
【Naomasa】 「Hm? What's that thing?」

source.japanese: 世界模型は単にこの世界の地理を模しただけではなかった。そのあちこちに、つまりこの世界のあちこちに、様々な物が置かれている。例えば、東の果ての海の上には、漆塗りの箱が。他にも独鈷や鏃[やじり]、竪琴などがあちこちに、よくよく見ればどこかで見たような襤褸船の模型まで置いてある。怖れ知らずにこの海の底、魚怪どもの巣であるこの場に忍び込んだ盗賊が見れば、この模型はまさしく宝物庫と歓喜に小躍りもしようが、あの時の泪の言葉を聞いた身としては、これはまさに、伝説寓話の見本市。
source.english: The world model did not merely reproduce the geography of this world. Here and there upon it—and therefore here and there in the world—various objects were placed. A lacquered box, for example, rested on the sea at the eastern edge. Elsewhere lay a single-pronged vajra, an arrowhead, a harp. Looking closely, one could even spot the model of a suspiciously familiar ragged ship. A fearless thief who slipped down into this nest of fish-monsters might dance for joy at this treasure house of a model. But having heard Rui's words back then, Sakuya saw a veritable trade fair of legends and fables.

source.japanese: その中で、密航者の向ける視線の先は。世界模型の中央より、朔屋達の側から見ればやや離れた方向に偏った、小さく突き出たものと大きく弓なりにせり出すものの二つの半島に挟まれた小さな島、その島の上に造られた町のその上に。
source.english:
And among them, where the stowaway looked—

A little island lay between two peninsulas, one jutting out a short way, the other extending far in a bow. It was offset from the model's center, farther away as seen from where they stood. Upon that island was a town, and upon that town—

target.text: The model of the world was not merely a model of this world's geography. Various things were placed here and there, in other words, here and there in this world. For example, atop the ocean in the far east was a lacquer box. In addition, there were single-pronged vajras or arrowheads, harps, and so on dotted here and there, and if he looked really close, there was even a model of a ship that really resembled something he'd seen elsewhere before.

From the perspective of some bandits who had intrepidly sneaked into this den of fish monsters at the bottom of the sea, this model was the sort of veritable treasure house that would send them jumping and dancing in delight, but as someone who had heard the words Rui spoke back then, it truly was a trade fair of legends and fables.

Amidst that, in the spot the stowaway was directing her gaze at. It was slightly off from the center of the model of the world from their perspective, on a small island surrounded by two peninsulas, one protruding only slightly and the other jutting out like a curved bow, on top of the town built on that island.

source.japanese: 幾つもの宝石を彩りに拵[こしら]えられた短剣が安置されていたのだ。
source.english: Rested a dagger adorned with many jewels.

source.japanese:
その短剣に朔屋、見覚えはあっただろうか。あるいはなかっただろうか。
　しかし、彼の記憶の中にあるいくつかの知識と出来事が脳野から芽吹き蔦伸ばして絡み合う。
　幼い頃に読み聞かされた、世に敷衍する御伽噺の一節が。彼が信天翁号で旅するうちに知った泪の正体が。そして、おそらくここからそう遠からぬ場所に鎮座するあの巨大な存在が彼の目の前で泪に告げた言葉の内容が。
　今、朔屋が視線を向けている短剣へと伸びていく。
　そう、あれこそが、人魚の姫に手渡され、誰かの胸に突き立てられた物なのだろう。
source.english:
Had Sakuya seen that dagger before? Or had he not?

But scraps of knowledge and events in his memory sprouted from the field of his mind, stretched out vines, intertwined.

A passage from the fairy tale told throughout the world, which he had heard as a child. Rui's true identity, learned during his travels on the Albatross. The words that immense being, probably enthroned not far from here, had spoken to Rui before his eyes.

They reached toward the dagger he now regarded.

Yes. Surely that was the thing handed to the mermaid princess, then plunged into someone's breast.

source.japanese:
朔屋、ごくりと唾を飲み込む。
　傍らの密航者は、ここに来る前、なんと言った？
『私たちは、あなたの持ち物を取り返すから』
　と、こう言ったか？
　ということは、つまり。
source.english:
Sakuya swallowed.

What had the stowaway beside him said before they came here?

‘We'll recover what belongs to you.’

Was that it?

Which meant—

target.text: There, a dagger wrought with an array of jewels serving as ornamentation was enshrined.

Sakuya had seen that dagger somewhere before, hadn't he? Or perhaps he didn't recognize it? However, certain pieces of knowledge and events from his memory sprouted from his cerebral cortex, stretching out as vines and tangling together. A passage from a fairy tale that permeates the world, one that was read aloud for him in his childhood. The true identity of Rui, which he had come to know during his time travelling aboard the Albatross. And then, the contents of the words Rui had spoken while that titanic existence had been there right before his very eyes, most likely sitting in a place not that far from where he currently stood.
Those tendrils reached out for the dagger Sakuya was now staring at. Indeed, that right there was probably what the mermaid princess had once been handed, what had been stabbed into someone's heart.
【Naomasa】 「………………」

Sakuya audibly gulped. What was it the stowaway by his side had said again, just before coming here? 『We are here to retrieve one of your belongings.』 That was what she had said, wasn't it? Which would then mean, in other words.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おいおい、あれを取りに行こうってのか？」
source.english: “Hey, hey. You're saying we're going to get that?”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Oi oi, are you saying you're going to go and grab that?」

source.japanese: 密航者は、小さく頷[うなず]く。
source.english: The stowaway nodded slightly.

target.text: The stowaway gave a small nod in return.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……その前に、
　一応保険をかけておこうか……。
　頼る羽目にはなりたくないけれど」
source.english:
“…Before that,
let's take out a little insurance…
I don't want to have to rely on it, though.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「……But before that, maybe I should prepare a backup, just in case……. I don't really want to end up having to rely on it though.」

source.japanese: そう言って、彼女は自分のポーチを漁る。中から取りだしたのは、どこにでもあるありふれた包帯だった。その端を握ると、密航者はえいとそれを放り投げる。しゅるしゅるとロール解きながら白い放物線を描きながら飛ぶ包帯は、模型の中、狙う短剣の側へと落ちる。
source.english: She rummaged in her pouch. What she took out was a perfectly ordinary bandage. Holding its end, the stowaway flung it out. The roll unwound with a rustle as the bandage traced a white arc and fell into the model near the dagger they wanted.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「おいおい、まさかあれに掴まるってんじゃなかろうな」
source.english: “Hey, don't tell me we're going to hold on to that.”

target.text: Saying that, the girl began to rummage through her own bag. What she pulled out was a completely ordinary bandage of the sort you could find anywhere else in the world. After gripping hold of the end of it, the stowaway flung it with a little "ei!". With a whizz, the roll unfurled as the bandage flew, trailing a white parabola through the air, landing next to the dagger she was aiming for inside the model.
【Naomasa】 「Oi oi, surely you're not trying to catch it with that, right?」

source.japanese:
何があってもおかしくないと、すでにその境地に達してしまった朔屋がそう言うと、密航者から帰ってきたのは鼻を軽く鳴らした笑い。朔屋の微妙な期待を裏切り、そんなことあるわけないでしょうと、密航者は天蓋のドームを構成する鋼材の一つにとりつき、よじ登り始める。
　ぽかんとそれを見つめていた朔屋も、密航者の一睨[にら]みに促されて、後に続く。
source.english:
Sakuya had reached the point where nothing could be ruled out. At his words, the stowaway gave a little snort of laughter. Dashing his faint expectations—of course not—she caught hold of one of the steel struts forming the dome and began to climb.

Sakuya stared blankly. One glare from the stowaway prompted him to follow.

target.text: When Sakuya, having already reached the point where he expected anything could happen, said that, the only thing he got in return from the stowaway was a light snort. Betraying Sakuya's odd expectations, all but telling him there was no way that would be the case, the stowaway grabbed hold of one of the steel strips forming the dome canopy, then began to scramble her way up. Sakuya, simply staring at her with his mouth wide open, was urged along by a glare from the stowaway, and so he followed after her.

source.japanese: 鉄骨の道をよじ登り、目指す短剣の真上まで辿り着いた二人、密航者は今度はロープを取り出し、その先に磁石を括[くく]りつける。そして、括りつけた磁石を下にロープを下ろし、なるほどこれで短剣を吸い付け引き上げる算段かと朔屋は得心したものの、垂らされた磁石は短刀まであと一米[メートル]とわずかというところで宙に止まる、所在なく。情けなく表情の密航者と朔屋は顔を見合わせる。
source.english: Climbing the iron framework, they reached a point directly over the dagger. Now the stowaway took out a rope and tied a magnet to its end. She lowered it, magnet first. Ah, Sakuya understood: they would attract the dagger and haul it up. But the dangling magnet stopped uselessly in midair, a little over a meter short. With dismal faces, the two looked at one another.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「俺、肉体労働には不向きなのに……この体勢はかなりしんどい」
source.english: “I'm not cut out for physical labor…and this position is pretty hard on me.”

source.japanese:
尺足りぬものは仕方なく、密航者は手を伸ばし、鉄骨の足場よりいっぱいに身を乗り出す。そのままでは数米[メートル]下まで真っ逆さまというわけで、朔屋が密航者の体を支えることになったわけだが。
　密航者の体はほとんど足場に残っておらず、朔屋は自分の体も落ちぬように踏ん張りながら、彼女の体重のほとんども支えているというわけだ。鍛えの足らぬ朔屋の足腰なかなか踏ん張ることもできず、二人の体はゆらゆらと、その振れもロープに伝わり、磁石は短剣の側で孤を描く。
source.english:
The rope was too short; nothing could be done about that. The stowaway extended her arm and leaned as far out as possible from the iron foothold. Left alone, she would fall headfirst several meters, so Sakuya had to support her.

Almost none of her body remained on the foothold. Sakuya had to brace himself against falling while supporting nearly all her weight. His untrained legs and back could scarcely hold firm. Both their bodies swayed, the movement passing down the rope, and the magnet swung in arcs beside the dagger.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「またお尻でも見えてくれれば、もうちょっとがんばれるのになぁ」
source.english: “If I could just catch another glimpse of her butt, I bet I could push a little harder.”

target.text: Having clambered up the steel frame, the two arrived directly above the dagger they were aiming for, and this time, the stowaway pulled out a rope, then secured a magnet to the end of it. She then lowered the rope with the fastened magnet at the bottom, and certainly, Sakuya convinced himself, with this, she'd be able to attract the blade to the magnet and pull it up with the rope, but the suspended magnet stopped in the air just barely above the dagger, no more than a metre away, and there was nothing left to give. The stowaway and Sakuya looked at each other with a pitiful expression on their faces.
【Naomasa】 「I'm not even really suited for manual labour……and this position is pretty damn draining.」

With no other way to compensate for the missing length, the stowaway stretched out her arms, leaning even further down from the steel frame she stood on. If left to her devices, she would have fallen several metres head-first, and so Sakuya ended up supporting the stowaway's body, but. The stowaway's body had almost no footing left to speak of, and while standing firm to ensure his own body didn't fall too, Sakuya ended up supporting almost her entire body weight. Sakuya's legs and loins, thoroughly lacking in training, could barely hold, and their bodies swayed and swung, the motion travelling through the rope and making the magnet swing in large arcs around the dagger.
【Naomasa】 「If you'd just let me see your ass again, I might be able to try a little harder.」

source.japanese: 不純なことをぼやく朔屋に、密航者は振り仰いで冷たい視線。
source.english: At Sakuya’s lewd grumbling, the stowaway turned to look up at him and gave him a cold stare.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「これ……降りて下から回った方が早いんじゃないのか？」
source.english: “Wouldn't it be quicker to get down and go round from below…?”

target.text: Upon hearing his impure grumblings, the stowaway looked up at Sakuya with an icy glare.
【Naomasa】 「I'm thinking……wouldn't it be faster to climb down and come at it from below?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ん……ん、もうちょっと……。
　だめ、それは。余計な手間になる。
　もっとちゃんと支えて、君も」
source.english:
“Mm…mm, just a little more…
No. That would make extra work.
You need to hold me properly.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Nh……nh, just a little more……. That won't work. Will take too much extra time. Could you also support me a little better here.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……お手伝い、差し上げた方がいいんじゃなくて？」
source.english: “…Shouldn't I lend you a hand?”

source.japanese: 必死な二人に投げかけられる、高貴さ故にどこか緊張感を削ぐ声。世界模型の設えられたこの間に現れたのは泪だった。
source.english: A voice reached the struggling pair, its very nobility somehow draining away the tension. Rui had entered the chamber housing the world model.

target.text: 【Rui】 「……Would it not be better if I were to offer some assistance?」
A voice bearing a nobility that somehow diffused the tension was directed at the desperately struggling duo. Who should have emerged in this hall where the model of the world was installed but Rui.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「泪さんはこの下らない道具には近づかないほうがいい。取りこまれてしまうから───って、逃げてって言ったのに、もう」
source.english: “Rui, you'd better stay away from this stupid contraption. It'll take you in—honestly, I told you to escape.”

source.japanese: ロープと悪戦苦闘を続ける密航者の心配に不満も混ざった声も、泪はさして意に介さず、出てくる言葉はドームの上で踏ん張る二人の必死さからどこかずれていて、
source.english: The stowaway went on wrestling with the rope, concern and complaint mingling in her voice. Rui took little notice. Her words were somehow out of step with the desperate efforts of the pair braced atop the dome.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「It'd be best for all of us if you didn't get too close to this good-for-nothing tool. It'll end up taking you within itself, so─── wait, I told you to run away, come on!」

Rui paid no particular heed to the mixture of worry and dissatisfaction bleeding into the stowaway's tone of voice while she continued her valiant struggle with the rope, and the words she said seemed on a somewhat different wavelength from the franticness of the two bracing themselves atop the dome.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「あなた達がなにをなさるつもりなのか、興味を催して、ね。直さん、貴方、そちらとずいぶん親しくなられたご様子───あーあ、取られちゃった」
source.english: “I grew curious about what you meant to do. Nao, you seem to have become quite close to her—ah, she's stolen you away.”

source.japanese: そして直正を直撃した。
source.english: And the words struck Naomasa directly.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Why, I found myself curious about whatever it is you two are up to in here. Nao-san, dear, you seem awfully intimate with that girl─── alas, my man has been taken from me.」
And then she scored a direct hit on Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「い、いやその、
　別に浮気とかそういうんじゃ！」
source.english:
“N-no, well,
it's not like I'm cheating or anything!”

source.japanese: 泪ほどの女性にそう言われて、動じもせずに笑って気の利いた言葉を返す真似など朔屋にはできようはずもなく。そして、この男、よりにもよって狼狽えた。泪にしてみれば他愛のない冗談でも、泪に関わって様々な目に遭ってきた朔屋にすれば、思わずいらぬ力があらぬ方にかかったりもするもの。その結果。
source.english: When a woman like Rui said such a thing to him, there was no chance Sakuya could laugh it off with an unruffled air and offer some witty reply. And this man—of all possible responses—panicked. To Rui it was no more than an idle joke; but Sakuya had been through so much on her account that his panic made him put strength in entirely the wrong direction. The result—

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Wah-, no, I mean, it's not like I'm cheating on you here or anything!」

When told that by a women of Rui's caliber, laughing like he was unperturbed and offering some tastefully clever words in return was conduct unthinkable for Sakuya to manage. And then, this man, of all the things he could have done, panicked. To Rui, it had been naught but a trifling joke, but when it came to Sakuya, who'd suffered through all manner of things ever since becoming involved with Rui, he unintentionally applied some needless force in an unexpected direction. The result of that being.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「こら直正っ、気を逸らさないで───え？
　滑……っ、ぅあーっ」
source.english:
“Naomasa, stop getting distracted—huh?
Slipping…uah!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「え、あ、まず……った、ぁぁーーっ」
source.english: “Huh—ah—I've messed…up—aaah!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Hey, Naomasa, don't get distracted───eh? I'm slip……, uWAAー!」
【Naomasa】 「Oh, ah, that's bad……wah, AAーー!」

source.japanese:
バランスは崩れるというわけだ。
　朔屋と密航者、二人合わせて足場の上で、詩的に表現すれば躍[おど]るように、しかし実態無様に手足ばたつかせ、一瞬の後には宙へと放り出された。
source.english:
They lost their balance, in other words.

Together upon their foothold, Sakuya and the stowaway danced—if one wished to put it poetically. In reality, they flailed their limbs disgracefully. A moment later they were flung into the air.

target.text: That they lost their balance. Sakuya and the stowaway, together on their shared foothold: if described poetically, they took a great leap, but in reality, they ungracefully thrashed around with their arms and legs only to be flung through the air the next instant.

source.japanese: 救いがあるとするなら、二人揃って落ちる瞬間、その動きがどう伝わったのかロープは翻[ひるがえ]り、その先に括りつけられた磁石はカチリと音を鳴らして、見事に目指す短剣を捕まえたことなのだが。
source.english: One mercy: at the instant they both fell, somehow their movement flicked the rope, and the magnet tied to its end gave a click, neatly catching the dagger they sought.

target.text: If there was any saving grace to be found, then it was that the moment the two of them fell together, that motion must have travelled through the rope, for it flapped around, and the magnet fastened to its end made a clicking sound, meaning it had managed to catch hold of the dagger they were after, however.

source.japanese:
二人が足場踏み外して転がり落ちた鋼材から世界模型の大地、あるいは海面かも知れぬ、までは運が悪ければ首なり頭なり打ちつけ骨砕かれて御陀仏と相成ってもおかしくはない高さ。
　しかし、朔屋の体に伝わってきたのは、柔らかく弾んで彼を受け止める感触だった。
　恐怖から閉じていた目を開いてみれば、朔屋の落ちたのは幅一米[メートル]ほどの布の道だった。
source.english:
From the steel strut off which they had slipped to the earth of the world model—or perhaps its sea—was a height quite sufficient to kill them. An unlucky blow to neck or head, shattered bone, and that would be that.

But what Sakuya felt was something soft and springy catching him.

He opened the eyes he had shut in fear. He had fallen upon a road of cloth, about a meter wide.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「痛てて……って、なに、ここ……？」
source.english: “Ow…wait, what is this place…?”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「言った端から手を離して……何もなにも。
　これが世界模型の中。見た通りの品じゃないって訳よ……泪さんの短剣は拾えたけど」
source.english:
“You let go the moment I told you not to…what do you mean, what?
We're inside the world model. It isn't what it looks like…I did get Rui's dagger, though.”

source.japanese: 見れば、いつの間にロープをたぐり寄せたものか、密航者の手には短剣が握られている。かつて泪の運命を決した短剣が。
source.english: At some point she must have reeled in the rope. The dagger lay in the stowaway's hand. The dagger that had once decided Rui's fate.

source.japanese:
そして見渡せば。朔屋は確かに世界模型の中に落ちたはずなのに。
　朔屋の立つ布の下に広がるのは、水面、いや、この色の濁りはよく知っている、海ではないか？　布の道は橋のように水面より浮いている。そして四方は。どういうことだ、霧がかかって端さえ見えぬ。巨大であったとはいえ、模型の中にいるはずなのに。霧の中、彼方に見える影は世界模型の端を囲う盆の淵ではなく、信天翁号の見張り台から眺めた陸地の影にそっくりではないか。
source.english:
And looking around—Sakuya had certainly fallen into the world model, yet—

Beneath the cloth on which he stood lay water. No: he knew that murky color well. Wasn't it the sea? The cloth road hung above the surface like a bridge. And all around—what was this? Mist hid even the edges. Vast though the model had been, they were supposed to be inside it. The shadows beyond the mist did not resemble the rim of the tray enclosing the world model. They looked exactly like land seen from the Albatross's lookout.

target.text: The two slipped, tumbled, and fell down from the steel frame towards the ground of the model of the world, or perhaps it was the surface of its oceans, but it was from such a height that, if luck wasn't on their side, it wouldn't be strange at all if they hit their neck or head, their bones shattered as they shuffled off this mortal coil. However, what Sakuya felt in his body was the sensation of something soft and bouncy catching him. When he opened his eyes clenched shut from fear, Sakuya saw that he had fallen onto a path of fabric about a metre wide.
【Naomasa】 「Owowow……wait, what is this……?」

【Stowaway】 「And the moment I say something, he just lets go……no, it's nothing. This is inside the model of the world. It's not just what it appears to be on the surface……we did manage to get Rui-san's dagger though.」
As he took a closer look, and just when had she coiled up the rope, there, clasped tightly in the stowaway's hand, was the dagger. The dagger that had determined Rui's fate once upon a time.

And when he then took a look around. Certainly, Sakuya must have fallen into that model of the world, and yet. What unfolded below the fabric Sakuya stood upon was a surface of water, no, he knew the murkiness of this hue well; was it not the ocean?

The road of fabric floated above the water's surface like a bridge. And then, in all directions. Just what was going on, for it was shrouded in so much fog he couldn't even see the edges. Even if it was enormous, he had to be within that model, and yet. The distant shadows he could discern from within the fog were not the edge of the disk that surrounded the model, no, did it not fit the distant shapes of land he had seen from atop the watchtower on the Albatross to a T?

source.japanese:
【直正】
「どういうことだい、こいつぁ……」
source.english: “What the hell's going on…?”

source.japanese:
思い出すのなら、こんな物語もあったはず。
　嵐に巻き込まれて巨人の国に迷い込んだとある船乗りは、箱庭の池に船を浮かべて遊んだとか遊ばれたとか。
　ここまで来たのなら、もはやどんな不思議も不可思議ではない。世界象った模型の中に落ちたのなら、この身がその縮尺に合わせて縮むくらい、むしろ道理の範疇ではないか。
source.english:
There was a story like this, if one remembered.

A sailor caught in a storm strayed into a land of giants. There, he floated a boat on a garden pond to play—or to be played with.

Having come this far, no marvel was inexplicable anymore. If one fell into a model of the world, shrinking to match its scale was almost within the bounds of reason.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「面倒なことになってきたかな、これは」
source.english: “This may be getting troublesome.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「What in the world is going on with this thing……」

If he could recall, there was a story like this as well. A certain sailor was caught in a storm, blown into the Land of Giants, sailing his boat around the pond of a miniature garden, a lusus naturae playing and being played with. After having come this far, there was no mystery so inexplicable as to be unfathomable. If he had fallen into a model made to represent the world, then if his body had shrunk to fit its scale, was that not, on the contrary, well within the realm of reason?
【Stowaway】 「This may have taken a turn for the troublesome.」

source.japanese:
言うなり、密航者は走り出した。
　いつの間に腕取られていたのか、朔屋もそれに手を牽かれ、走り出す。
　一体何事と駆け出しながらも周囲を見渡せば───
source.english:
As she said it, the stowaway began to run.

At some point she had taken Sakuya's arm. Pulled by her hand, he ran too.

Wondering what was happening, he looked around as he ran—

target.text: With that, the stowaway broke into a run. He didn't even notice when she'd grabbed him by the arm, but Sakuya found himself led by the hand and also began to run. While running, wondering just what the meaning of all this was, he took a look around, and lo───

source.japanese:
周囲を包む霧に不吉としかいいようのない影が浮かび上がる。朔屋、冷や汗感じて思い出す。ここまでの自分の災難の中、こんな現れ方をするのは、自分に敵意を向けてくる者ばかり。
　それは見事に的中し、彼方にようやくはっきりと見えてきたその姿は。
source.english:
Shapes emerged from the surrounding mist, shapes that could only be called ominous. Sakuya felt a cold sweat and remembered: in all his misfortunes thus far, anyone who appeared like that had been hostile.

He was perfectly right. At last, in the distance, their forms became clear.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ななな、なんだぁありゃぁ！」
source.english: “Wh-wh-what the hell are those!?”

source.japanese: それは、骨、人の骨。人間の体から綺麗に腐敗する肉だけを落としてできた白骨の骸。それが群れなし、カシャカシャ不気味な軋み響かせて二人めがけて来るではないか。この模型の世界に落ちてきた客人を歓待しようというにはとても見えない。いやむしろ、人様の墓に勝手に忍び込み、まさにお宝の一つを手にした盗人に制裁加えるべく古の王[ファラオ]に殉じて共に葬られた戦士がその使命だけを存念に己が骸に取り憑いた骸骨兵、そう考えた方が納得がいく。
source.english: Bones. Human bones. White skeletons, made by stripping human bodies clean of only their rotting flesh. In a swarm they came toward the pair, rattling and creaking eerily. They scarcely seemed intent on welcoming guests who had fallen into this model world. Rather, one might imagine skeletal soldiers: warriors buried with an ancient pharaoh, their bones haunted solely by the duty for which they had died, come to punish thieves who had intruded upon another's tomb and laid hands on its treasure. That made more sense.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「とにかく走って、絶対私の手を離さないように。
　迷ったら最後、出られなくなる」
source.english:
“Just run, and don't let go of my hand.
If you get lost, you'll never get out.”

target.text: From the mist enveloping their surroundings rose shadowy figures that could only be described as sinister. A cold sweat beginning to form, Sakuya remembered. In every misfortune that had befallen him hitherto, anything and everything that had manifested like this was always hostile towards him. That proved to be right on the mark as soon as the figures in the distance finally came clearly into view.
【Naomasa】 「W-W-W-, WHAT THE HELL ARE THOSE!」

It was bones, human bones. The white, bleached remains of human bodies, the flesh alone cleanly rotted off. And if he was not mistaken, were they not forming a horde, bones eerily clacking and creaking, heading right for the two of them? It certainly did not look in the slightest like they were about to provide a warm welcome for the two guests who had fallen into this model of the world.

No, quite to the contrary, these were skeleton soldiers possessed by the warriors who had once sacrificed themselves as martyrs to be buried with their ancient Pharaoh as they followed him into the afterlife, binding themselves to their own remains through sheer indelible duty, here to punish they who had violated the grave of another through unsanctioned trespass, and not only that, also thieves who had taken a treasure for themselves; it made a good deal more sense to him when he thought of it that way.
【Stowaway】 「Anyway, just run, and make sure you don't let go of my hand. If you get lost in here, you will never be able to get out again.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「やっぱり使うことになっちゃった、あーあ」
source.english: “We ended up needing it after all. Oh dear.”

source.japanese: 密航者が駆け足緩めず嘆息するのを聞けば、今二人が必死の逃走に使っているこの布の道は、なるほど、最初に投げ入れた包帯なのだろう。今はその用心に頭を下げて、二人は迫り来る骸に背を向け走る走る。走れどしかし。
source.english: Hearing the stowaway sigh without slowing, Sakuya understood: this cloth road along which they desperately fled must be the bandage she had thrown in at the start. Grateful now for that precaution, they turned their backs on the approaching remains and ran and ran. Yet however they ran—

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So I did end up having to use it after all, ugh.」

When he heard the stowaway heave that deep, frustrated sigh without relaxing her pace, he realized that this path of cloth the two were currently using for their desperate escape must have been that bandage she tossed down at the very beginning. Right now, he could only admire her prudence, and the two turned their backs to the encroaching horde of skeletons and ran. They ran and they ran, but.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだこの玩具の舞台の癖して、
　走っても走っても……！」
source.english:
“It's just a toy stage!
We run and run, and still…!”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「黙って走る！　さすがに本当の世界ほどではないから。せいぜい二・三キロ───」
source.english:
“Shut up and run! It's not as big as the real world.
Two or three kilometers at most—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「無理だぁ！　ただ走るだけならまだしも、　
その距離、こいつらから逃げきんのは！」
source.english:
“I can't! Just running would be one thing,
but escaping these things for that distance!”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「どうしてそんなに軟弱かなもう。
　でも確かにこれは───」
source.english:
“Why do you have to be so feeble?
Still, this is—”

source.japanese: どう見ても、こちらは生身、対して向こうは骨のみである。構造がどうなっているのかはわからねど、疲れてくれるとはとても思えぬ。逃げる方はすでに一名、ぜいぜいと息をついているというのに。
source.english: Plainly, they were flesh and blood; their pursuers were nothing but bone. Whatever their structure, they scarcely seemed likely to tire. One of the fugitives was already wheezing.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「What's going on? It's nothing more than some stupid toy stage, but I run and I run and I still……!」
【Stowaway】 「Shut up and run! It's not as big as the real word. At worst, it's another two or three kilome───」
【Naomasa】 「Not happening! If we just had to run, that'd be one thing, but we're not going to be able to stay ahead of these freaks for that long!」
【Stowaway】 「Why are you so weak, come on. But you're right, the way things stand───」

No matter how one looked at this, they were of flesh and blood, and in contrast, the other party was nothing but bones. It wasn't clear just exactly how they'd been constructed, but it was very hard to imagine they'd grow tired. And one of the people fleeing was already panting, out of breath.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「荒事の手の二・三手、用意しておくべきだったかぁ……」
source.english: “I should've had a few ways to handle a fight ready…”

source.japanese: なおも走れど、出口も世界の果ても見えぬ。追っ手はじりじりと迫り来る。
source.english: They kept running. Neither exit nor world's end came into view. The pursuers drew steadily closer.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「一手だけなら、もしかしてあるかも知れないけれど」
source.english: “Though I may have one move.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Guess I really should have prepared a couple of ways to handle some fighting……」
They ran as ever, but neither an exit nor the end of the world were anywhere to be seen. Little by little, their pursuers drew closer.
【Stowaway】 「But if one way is enough, there might be something here.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ならその一手、さっさと使ってくれよう！」
source.english: “Then hurry up and use it!”

source.japanese:
朔屋の縋[すが]る泣き言響き渡る。
　その声がどう天に届いたのか、二人が逃げる道の先に影が一つ現れる。すわ、通せんぼか、ついに二人は前後を敵に挟まれて、ここで一巻の終わりとなり果てるのか。
　が、しかし、豈図らんや、その影の正体は。
source.english:
Sakuya's pleading whine resounded.

However that voice reached heaven, a figure appeared farther along their escape route. A roadblock? At last enemies hemmed them in before and behind: was this where their story ended?

But contrary to all expectation, the figure was—

source.japanese:
【智里】
「てなわけで、俺か。
　もう出番はねえものと、安心してたんだが」
source.english:
“And so, it's me.
I'd relaxed, thinking I wouldn't have another scene.”

source.japanese: 白い着物に灰黒の地に細縞の袴[はかま]、黒い髪に蒼い瞳、おどけた声に笑いを浮かべ、すでに白刃抜き放った智里だった。
source.english: Tomosato. White kimono, fine-striped hakama on a gray-black ground, black hair, blue eyes. A smile in his joking voice, and his sword already drawn.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「貴方の気配が残っていたから、声を掛けておいたんだけど……奏効したか。ま、出てきたなら出てきたで、さっさと叩き斬って」
source.english: “I sensed you lingering here, so I called to you…looks like it worked. Well, since you've appeared, hurry up and cut them down.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そのくらいしか使い道がないんだから」
source.english: “That's about all you're useful for.”

source.japanese:
【智里】
「へーへー」
source.english: “Yeah, yeah.”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Then please just hurry up and use that way!」

Sakuya's tearful plea resounded far and wide. His voice must have reached the heavens somehow, for before them, on the path the two were escaping down, a lone figure emerged. Goodness gracious, it was blocking the way; in the end, the duo had been caught between enemies from the front and the back; was this the end of the line? But, however, in a twist impossible for any to predict, the true identity of that figure was none other than.
【Tomosato】 「So that means me? Here I was, at ease, certain there was no part left for me to play.」
There, clad in a pinstriped, grey hakama over a white kimono, with black hair, azure eyes, a jesting tone of voice, and a smile on his face, naked blade already unsheathed, was Tomosato.
【Stowaway】 「Your presence still lingered, so I called out to you in advance, but……looks like it worked? Well, if you're gonna show up, then just do it. Go chop them down already.」
【Stowaway】 「Because that's about the only thing that you're good for.」
【Tomosato】 「Yeah, yeah.」

source.japanese:
聞こえる返事も軽かれど、その脇駆け抜け一拍おけば、空裂く刃[やいば]が骸の骨を、断ち割る音の響きも高く。
　智里健在を示すその音を背に、朔屋と密航者はようやく、模型世界の果てへと辿り着いたのであった。
source.english:
His answer was light. They ran past him; a beat later, a blade split the air, and the sound of cleaving bones rang out.

With that sound assuring them that Tomosato was still going strong at their backs, Sakuya and the stowaway at last reached the end of the model world.

target.text: His response was also flippant, but a heartbeat after he dashed past their flanks, the sound of his heaven-splitting blade cleaving the bony remains resounded sonorously. With sounds signifying that Tomosato was still going strong coming from behind them, Sakuya and the stowaway finally reached the end of this model of the world.

source.japanese: そこより抜け出して振り返ってみれば、世界模型の大きさはもとより変わらず、いや初見の衝撃が消えた分、あの中に落ちた後走りに走った分、以前より小さく見えるほど。
source.english: Emerging and looking back, they found the world model no larger than before. No: with the initial shock gone, and after all that running within it, it seemed smaller still.

source.japanese: 朔屋は息も整えず、まずは心配していた素振りもない泪の元へ向かう辺り、妙に律儀と言えば律儀で。
source.english: Before even catching his breath, Sakuya first made for Rui, who showed no sign of having worried about them. Oddly dutiful, if dutiful was the word.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ぜえはぁ、ぜぇはああーー……る、泪さん、これ……」
source.english: “Hah, haa—hah, haaa…R-Rui, this…”

source.japanese: そう言って差し出すのは、苦労して得た、ことここにいたっては言葉も飾る必要もない、盗み出した短剣。
source.english: What he held out was the dagger they had labored to obtain—or, at this point, with no need to dress up the words, stolen.

target.text: When he looked over his shoulder after making his way out, the model of the world was the same size as it had been from the very start, no, for with the shock of seeing it for the first time having faded, and having had to run so hard after falling into it, it actually looked smaller than before.

Sakuya didn't even stop to catch his breath; the first thing he did was head for Rui, who didn't seem worried in the slightest, and in a manner that could be called dutiful, even if expressed in a rather strange way.
【Naomasa】 「Fhhhhhaaah, Fffhhhhhaaaaーーh…… Ru-, Rui-san, take this……」
Saying that, he presented what he had obtained through great hardships, what no longer needed to be embellished with pretty words at this point: the dagger he had stolen.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お疲れ様。なんだかばたばたしていたご様子だったけれど」
source.english: “Well done. It looked as though you were rather busy.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Thank you for your hard work. It appears things took a turn for the hectic.」

source.japanese: あまり実感の込められてないねぎらいの言葉の後、泪は朔屋の手から短剣を受け取る。
source.english: After those words of appreciation, with little feeling in them, Rui took the dagger from Sakuya's hand.

target.text: After bestowing upon him some words of appreciation that didn't feel terribly sincere, Rui accepted the dagger from Sakuya's hands.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「これは、わたくしにはあまりいい想い出、ないけれど。それでも、有難う存じますね」
source.english: “This holds no very pleasant memories for me. Even so, you have my thanks.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「This is not something I have very fond memories of. Even so, I shall accept it with gratitude.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「立ち話は後、後。こうしてる間にも、泪さんのご一統がご登場、って事にもなりかねない」
source.english: “Chat later, later. While we're standing here, Rui's whole family might put in an appearance.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Leave the talking for later, later. While we're standing here, there's a good chance that Rui-san's entire lineage is going to make its entry on stage.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「だな。俺もあいつらを斬るのはもう飽いたわ」
source.english: “Right. I've had enough of cutting them down too.”

source.japanese: いつの間にあそこより抜け出したのか、智里もひょっこりと顔を出す。
source.english: At some point Tomosato had emerged as well. Now he popped into view.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あ、もう戻ってきたんだ。結構早かったんだな」
source.english: “Oh, you're back already. That was pretty quick.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Right. I've also had my fill of cutting those guys down.」
Tomosato also suddenly showed up, and just when had he made his way out from there?
【Naomasa】 「Oh, you're already back. That was surprisingly quick.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「当たり前だ。
　あんたらが逃げ切る分だけ時間を稼げりゃそれでよかろう。何もあんなのを最後の一つ叩き斬るまで付き合う道理もあるまい。なにより刀が傷んぢまう。
　とっととずらかってきたわ」
source.english:
“Of course.
I only had to buy enough time for you to escape. No reason to stick around till I'd chopped up every last one. Besides, it'd damage my sword.
I got the hell out.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Yeah, obviously. All I needed to do was buy enough time for you guys to make good your escape. There was not a single good reason why I should stay there and cut them down to the last bone. Most importantly, it'd just nick my blade. I beat it from there in a hurry.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「さて、もう荒事は御免だろう？
　こっちの抜け道を使おうぜ」
source.english:
“Now, you've had enough trouble, haven't you?
Let's use this way out.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Alright then, you guys have had enough of the fighting by now, yeah? Let's use the shortcut back here.」

source.japanese:
そう智里が指し示すのは、朔屋と密航者がここへと入り込んだのとは別の道。それがどこへ続くと知れる保証もないが、朔屋にしてもこれ以上の災難は懲り懲りであり、なによりこの智里、ここで伴連れを欺いて魚怪どもの巣に導くような詐術をしてくるとも思えぬとあって、一行、素直にその道を進む。
　果たして。
source.english:
Tomosato indicated a different path from the one by which Sakuya and the stowaway had entered. There was no guarantee where it led, but Sakuya had suffered quite enough disaster. More importantly, he could not imagine Tomosato deceiving his companions here and leading them into another nest of fish-monsters. The party took the path without protest.
And indeed—

target.text: The path Tomosato indicated was different from the one that Sakuya and the stowaway had made their way through here. There was no guarantee just where it would lead them, but Sakuya had also had enough misfortune for today, and most of all, it was hard to imagine Tomosato pulling a trick on them by pretending to accompany them only to lead them deeper into the lair of the fish monsters, and so the whole group obediently went down that path. And sure enough.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……なんて都合のいいこと」
source.english: “…How convenient.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「……How very convenient.」

source.japanese:
【智里】
「てめぇにゃ言われたかねえなあ」
source.english: “You're one to talk.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「I do not want to hear that coming from you.」

source.japanese:
無事に潜水艦の待つ海底洞窟の入り江に到着できたのであった。
　長居は無用と、一行はそそくさと潜水艦へと乗り込む。行きよりは客の増えた分だけ手狭に感じるものの、朔屋は遥かに心安く潜行の様を感じられたという。
source.english:
They arrived safely at the inlet in the underwater cave, where the submarine waited.

There was no reason to linger. They hurried aboard. With more passengers than on the way out it felt cramped, but Sakuya is said to have found the dive far more comforting.

target.text: They managed to arrive at the inlet pool within the underwater cave where the submarine waited without incident. With no reason to overstay their welcome, the entire party hurriedly boarded the submarine. With more passengers, it made for a more cramped experience than when they first came, but it also made for a far more lighthearted underwater trip for Sakuya.

source.japanese: 朔屋と密航者、そして新たに泪と智里を乗せた潜水艦、その帰り路でも密航者の神通力はあらたかで、音と共に水面を割って浮上したその目の前には、今ややけっぱちな懐かしささえ感じられる信天翁号の姿があった。
source.english: The submarine carried Sakuya and the stowaway, now joined by Rui and Tomosato. The stowaway's miraculous power remained effective on the return journey: before them as they broke the surface with a splash stood the Albatross, by now an almost desperately familiar sight.

target.text: The submarine, carrying Sakuya and the stowaway, and now Rui and Tomosato too, was clearly affected by the stowaway's supernatural powers on the trip back home as well, for when the submarine emerged together with the sound of the water's surface breaking, there, right before his eyes, was the Albatross, a sight that even made him feel a desperate nostalgia right now.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「そして、またこちらのお船、というわけ。
　いいけれどね、別に。
　他よりは退屈しないし」
source.english:
“And it's this ship again, then.
Well, I don't mind.
She's less boring than anywhere else.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「Thus, I am back on your ship once more, it would seem. That is fine, I have no particular issue with that. I shall be less bored than anywhere else.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「直さんだってまた、
　乗りこんでいらしてるし」
source.english:
“And Nao is
aboard again too.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「After all, you are also sailing aboard her once more, Nao-san.」

source.japanese: 役目を終え、今度はその重みに任せただけのように再び海に沈んでいく潜水艦を背に、上甲板にあがった四人を迎えたのは、船長以下航海士と水夫長、そしてわらわらわらと数を揃えて集まってきた下級水夫達。
source.english: Her work done, the submarine sank once more into the sea, this time as though simply yielding to her weight. On the upper deck the four were greeted by the captain, the navigators and boatswain, and junior sailors gathering in swarming numbers.

source.japanese: そう、やっと信天翁号にすべての面子が戻ってきたのだ。一度はこの世界のあらゆる場所に散りながら、再び爪弾きされてきた者どもが。
source.english: Yes. At last the whole company had returned to the Albatross. Those who had once scattered to every corner of this world, only to be cast out again.

source.japanese: 満足げに密航者は彼らを見渡す。
source.english: The stowaway surveyed them with satisfaction.

target.text: With the submarine behind them, this time sinking back into the ocean as though relying on its mass alone, its role now finished, as the four of them went up to the upper deck, they were greeted by the captain, the first mates, and the Bosun, as well as a swarm of deck boys bustling and shuffling about as they gathered in full number.
Indeed, the full crew of the Albatross had finally returned to her. They who had once been scattered across this world only to be shunned and spurned once more.
With a satisfied look, the stowaway looked out over them all.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「っていうことで───
　言っておかなくちゃいけない言葉があります」
source.english:
“And so—
There's something I have to say.”

source.japanese: そして、高らかにこう言ったのだ。
source.english: Then she proclaimed it loudly.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So then─── There is something I need to say.」
And so, she proclaimed thus in a sonorous voice:

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「なんだ、結局みんな、この船しか行き場がないのじゃあないか！」
source.english: “Well, in the end, none of you has anywhere to go but this ship!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Well, would you look at that? Turns out none of us have anywhere else to go but this ship after all!」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「うるせぇっ！　わかっちゃいるが、あんたに言われるとなんか腹が立ってくる！」
source.english: “Shut up! We know that, but hearing it from you pisses me off!”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Shut UP! I know it's true, but hearing it from you just kind of pisses me off!」

source.japanese: ───かくして信天翁号に、女客が戻ってきたのだった。
source.english: —And thus the lady passenger returned to the Albatross.

target.text: ───Thus, the female passenger returned to the Albatross.

source.japanese:
誰もが共感していたわけではなかろうが、少なくとも密航者である彼女だけは満喫していた再会の交歓は、見張り台に立っていた下級水夫の声によって終わりを告げる。すなわち、こちらに向かってくる船影有り、彼方の船足速く、警戒を要す。
　世界中を旅して怨みを買ってきた信天翁号だ、この船に目指して進んでくる船が友好的であった試しはない。平たく言えば『敵襲ーッ！』と叫んだのだ。
　降りかかる声はさらに続く。ほぼ同じ報告が立て続け、違っているのは方角で、三時、六時、九時、そして十二時と。瞬く間に信天翁号は敵意ある船団に取り囲まれたということだ。
　そして。この船がどうしようもない者どもの集まりだということに。次々と上がる報告に、水夫長以下下級水夫達は一斉に力漲[みなぎ]り、甲板上は活気づく。
source.english:
Not everyone could have shared the feeling, but the stowaway, at least, had been thoroughly enjoying the reunion. A junior sailor's voice from the lookout brought it to an end: a vessel was approaching, fast, and caution was required.

The Albatross had earned grudges all over the world. No ship that came straight for her had ever been friendly. In plain language, he shouted, ‘Enemy attack!’

The calls kept coming down. Almost the same report, again and again; only the direction differed. Three o'clock, six, nine, then twelve. In moments the Albatross was surrounded by a hostile fleet.

And here was proof that this ship was a collection of hopeless cases. At each new report, the boatswain and junior sailors filled with vigor. The deck came alive.

target.text: It was surely not the case that everyone felt the same way, but at the very least, the woman who stowed away enjoyed the fraternization of their reunion to the fullest, right until the voice of a deck boy standing atop the watchtower marked the end of it. In other words, there was the outline of a ship coming this way, and at a swift pace at that, which demanded caution. This was the Albatross, a ship that had incurred the enmity of many as she sailed around the world, and there had never before been an instance where a ship heading directly for her was friendly. In plain terms, he had yelled: 『ENEMY ATTACK!』

The voice pouring over them from above continued. Practically identical warnings were issued in succession, all from different directions, 3 o'clock, 6 o'clock, 9 o'clock, as well as 12 o'clock. In the blink of an eye, the Albatross had been encircled by a fleet of hostile ships. And then. Despite this ship being one big gathering of hopeless good-for-nothings. As the warnings came flying one after the other, the Bosun and all his deck boys brimmed with vigour, livening up all around the upper deck.

source.japanese:
しかし。
　囲み作って寄り来たる船影はっきりと浮かび上がるにつれ。
　一部の者の顔が曇る。
source.english:
But—

As the ships closing their ring came clearly into view,

Some faces clouded.

target.text: However. As the outlines of the approaching ships forming the encirclement began to stand out clearly against the sea. The expressions of some of those present clouded over.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「せ、船尾のほうからも、くる！
　どうして、ノアがなんで、まだクロのことを」
source.english:
“Th-they're coming from the stern too!
Why? Why is Noah still after Kuro—”

source.japanese: 逃げ出した烏を未だ妄執もて追いかけてきた巨大な船影が。
source.english: The hulking ship that had pursued the runaway crow this far, its obsession undiminished.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Th-, they're coming from the stern, too! Why, why would Noah come for Kuro again?」
There was the silhouette of a titanic ship driven by deep-rooted delusion, still pursuing the bird who escaped.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あっちはあたしらがらみの追っ手か……。
　なんだって無駄にしつこい……」
source.english:
“Over there, they're after us…
Why do they have to be so pointlessly persistent…?”

source.japanese: 『一なる三者』のうちの三分の二を求める巡礼者を満載した船団が。
source.english: A fleet packed with pilgrims seeking two-thirds of the Three Who Are One.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「And those over there would be the pursuers after us……. Why are they so pointlessly persistent……」
A fleet packed to the gills with pilgrims in search of two parts of the three that make up the 『Triune Being』

source.japanese:
【泪】
「……娘一人から、いつまで子離れできないの、まったく……」
source.english: “…Will he never learn to let go of his daughter? Honestly…”

source.japanese: 家おん出た愛娘を連れ戻さんと差し向けられた魚怪の群れが。
source.english: A swarm of fish-monsters sent to bring home the beloved daughter who had left.

target.text: 【Rui】 「……How long will you remain unable to let go of but a single of your daughters, my word……」
A swarm of fish monsters dispatched to bring home a beloved daughter who had left home of her own accord.

source.japanese:
信天翁号を囲んでいるとわかったのだ。
　もちろん、意趣返しを図った、いや筋の通った復讐の念も混ざっておろうが、海賊どももいる。四方八方この時ばかりと一斉に、敵意が信天翁号を囲んでいるのだ。
source.english:
These, they realized, surrounded the Albatross.

Of course, there were pirates too, bent on getting their own back—some, indeed, with quite legitimate grounds for revenge. From every direction, as though this were their moment, hostility surrounded the Albatross.

target.text: It had become clear that they were surrounding the Albatross. Of course, they were planning revenge; well, while there were probably some amongst them with a rational lust for vengeance, those pirates were also there. Animosity from every direction was closing in on the Albatross all at once, as if to say this was the time to strike.

source.japanese:
彼らの恨みはどれほどだろう。
　彼我の距離が縮まるにつれ、彼らの積もりに積もった呪詛の声が聞こえてくるようだった。
source.english:
How deep did their grudges run?

As the distance closed, one seemed to hear all their accumulated curses.
“Give it back—”
“Return it—”

source.japanese:
聞こえてくるよう？
　朔屋は我が耳を疑った。
　そして、もう一度、聴覚に集中する。
source.english:
Seemed to hear?

Sakuya doubted his ears.

Then he concentrated on listening again.
“That—”
“Hand it over—”

source.japanese: 違う、空耳などではない、実際に聞こえてくるのだ、尋常ではない声が。
source.english: No. He was not imagining it. He could actually hear those extraordinary voices.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「な、な、な。
　なんだぁ、こりゃぁ!?」
source.english:
“Wh-wh-what—
What the hell is this!?”

source.japanese: 取り囲む船に乗る者どものすべてが、信天翁号に向かって放っているのだ、その声を。
source.english: Everyone aboard the surrounding ships was directing those words at the Albatross.
“That thing—”
“Of yours—”
“Hand it over—”

source.japanese:
ノアが、
　巡礼者達が、
　魚怪の群が、
　海賊どもが、
　口そろえ一様に、正気の欠片も乗らぬ声を。
source.english:
Noah,
The pilgrims,
The swarms of fish-monsters,
The pirates—

All speaking in unison, in voices without a trace of sanity.
“That thing—”
“Of yours—”
“Hand it over—”

source.japanese: ただ一点を見つめて。
source.english: Staring at a single point.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なな、なんなんだぁ、こいつらぁ！」
source.english: “Wh-what the hell is wrong with these people!?”

source.japanese: 朔屋、狂気困惑に憑かれて駆られ、彼らの声、視線の向かう先を直感的に捉えて振り返る。
source.english: Driven by maddening bewilderment, Sakuya sensed instinctively where their voices and eyes were directed, and turned.

source.japanese: そこには───
source.english: There stood—

target.text: How bitterly malicious a grudge must they have held. As the distance between both sides grew smaller and smaller, it was as though he could hear the sound of their accumulated malisons.
『Give back───』
『Return───』
As though he could hear? Sakuya could scarcely believe his own ears. And then, once more, he tried to concentrate his sense of hearing.
『That thing───』
『Hand it over───』
No, he wasn't mishearing things at all, he could actually hear it, an abnormal voice.
【Naomasa】 「Wh-, wh-, wha-. WHAT IS THAT!?」
All of those aboard the ships surrounding them were emitting that thing at the Albatross, that voice.
『Your───』
『That thing───』
『Hand it over───』
Noah, the pilgrims, the horde of fish monsters, the pirates, all in unison, in a voice holding not a shred of sanity.
『Your───』
『That thing───』
『Hand it over───』
Staring fixedly at but a single point.
【Naomasa】 「Wha-wha-, what is going on with them!?」
Sakuya, possessed by madness and impelled by perplexity, intuitively grasped where their voices and gazes were directed, and he turned around towards it.
And there was───

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「寄越せ寄越せと騒がしい。　
でもね、これはそもそもあいつらのモノじゃない」
source.english:
“Give us this, give us that. What a racket.
But you know, it never belonged to them in the first place.”

source.japanese:
周囲に群がる敵船睨[にら]みつけ、決意秘めて不敵に笑う密航者が立っていた。
　そこは上甲板、船首の近く。取り囲む不穏に当てられたのかやや波高しの海原で揺れる船体ものともせず、しっかと甲板踏みしめて立っていた。
　気がつけば、その左手には細く縒られた縄の束、そして右手には風に煽られ炎揺らめく燐寸があった。
source.english:
The stowaway stood glaring at the enemy ships around them, a fearless smile concealing determination.

Near the bow of the upper deck. Untroubled by the ship's rocking upon a sea whose waves had risen a little, perhaps infected by the surrounding unrest, she planted her feet firmly on the deck.

And now, in her left hand, there was a bundle of thinly twisted cords. In her right, a match, its flame trembling in the wind.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So noisy with all your hand it over, hand it over talk. But you know, this was never yours in the first place.」

Glaring at the enemy vessels gathering around them, there stood the stowaway with a dauntless smile hiding within it a bold determination. It was on the upper deck, close to the bow. The hull shook atop the tall waves of the rocky sea as though it were struck by the menace hanging in the air around it, but she paid it no heed, her feet firmly planted on the deck. By the time he noticed her there, she was holding a coil of slender, plied rope in the left hand and a lit match, flame swaying as it was fanned by the wind, in her right.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「お、おい君何を!?
　なんかいやぁな予感しかしないぞ、おい！」
source.english:
“H-hey, what are you doing!?
I've got nothing but a bad feeling about this!”

source.japanese: 朔屋、言葉にしてしまった予感に駆られて、縄の一筋が伸びているバラックに視線を向ける。外れかけた戸板の隙間から見えたそれは。
source.english: Driven by the premonition he had put into words, Sakuya looked toward the shanty into which one of the cords ran. Through a gap beside its half-detached door, he saw—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだこりゃぁ！」
source.english: “What the hell is this!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「O-, oi, you, what are you!? I've got a baaad feeling about this, HEY!」
Sakuya, driven by the hunch he had just put into words, looked towards the shack with a single line of rope leading out from it. And there he saw it, through the gap where a shutter had once been.
【Naomasa】 「What is THAT thing!」

source.japanese: 驚愕は重ねて二つ、一つは、十把一絡げに襤褸船をよりそれたらしめるだけの存在と思っていた、時には彼もその一棟を許可無く借りて隠れ家代わりにくすねた酒を隠し当直のサボって憩いの場としていたバラックの中に、なんてぇもんが隠されていたことか、その衝撃に朔屋、凍り付く。
source.english: Two shocks came one atop the other. The first froze Sakuya where he stood: a thing like this had been hidden inside one of the shanties he had always lumped together as mere appendages making a ragged ship raggedder still—one of the same shanties he would sometimes commandeer without permission for a hideout, stashing his pilfered liquor there and lounging away the watches he ought to have stood.

source.japanese:
そこにあったものは。
　台座を城と鎮座し、分厚い鉄板を楯と構えた砲台から、伸びるは二四糎[サンチ]三五口径の単装砲。込められた砲弾を炸薬の爆発力もて撃ち放つ兵器だった。
source.english:
There stood—

A gun emplacement enthroned upon a fortress of a base, thick iron plate raised as its shield, and projecting from it a single 24-centimeter gun, its barrel thirty-five calibers long: a weapon built to hurl its loaded shell with the explosive force of a powder charge.

source.japanese: もう一つは───
source.english: The other shock—

target.text: The shock came in twos: the first was what was hidden inside that shack, which merely by virtue of its existence seemed to worsen the already generally ramshackle impression given by everything else on this ship, the very same building he had once borrowed without permission, using it in place of a proper hideaway, hiding the sake he'd swiped, slacking off when on watch, and used as a general place of repose, and the impact of it left Sakuya frozen where he stood.

The thing that was in there. Presiding over its pedestal as if it were a fortress stood a gun battery, thick iron plates as shields held at the ready, a 24cm/35 single-mounted turret protruding from within. A weapon that unleashed its loaded shells through the raw power of an explosive charge.
The other was───

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「集めたのも私なら、
　そのそもそもの持ち主もこの私だと。
　どうせ言ってもわからぬ馬鹿ばかり、か」
source.english:
“I gathered them.
And they were mine in the first place.
But you're all too stupid to understand, even if I tell you.”

source.japanese: 燐寸の炎に浮かび上がって、より凶悪に映えた密航者の笑みだった。
source.english: Was the stowaway's smile, lit by the match flame and all the more vicious for it.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だったら───
　こうするしか、なかろうなぁ」
source.english:
“Then—
There's nothing for it but this.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「わあよせ馬鹿やめろうっ」
source.english: “Aah, stop, you idiot! Don't!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I'm the one who gathered them, and I'm also their original owner. But you're all idiots who'll never get it no matter what I say, right?」
Lit up by the flame of the match, the stowaway's smile shone with an even more fiendish sheen.
【Stowaway】 「In that case─── There's only one thing left to do, isn't there?」
【Naomasa】 「WAAH, CUT THAT OUT YOU IDIOT, STOP!」

source.japanese: 制止求める朔屋の叫び、ちとも耳に届いた風も無く、密航者の右手は軽やかにひらめき、燐寸の炎はいまやはっきりとわかった火縄へと接触する。
source.english: Sakuya's shouted plea for restraint did not seem to reach her ears at all. Her right hand flicked lightly. The match flame touched what was now plainly a fuse.

target.text: Showing no sign of Sakuya's screaming demands for restraint reaching her ears in the slightest, the stowaway's hand lightly flashed, and the flame of the match came into contact with what was now clearly distinguishable as a fuse.

source.japanese: かすかな音と植物質が焼ける臭いを風が運んだかと思うと、
source.english: The wind brought a faint sound and the smell of burning plant fiber—

target.text: No sooner than a faint noise and the smell of vegetable matter burning was carried towards him on the wind,

source.japanese: まさしく与えられたのは朱色の命、炎は歓喜の声をあげて火縄を端から燃やして走る。後に残ったわずかな炭は風にまかれて霧散する。
source.english: Granted scarlet life, the flame cried out in joy and ran along the fuse, devouring it from the end. The little char it left behind scattered into the wind.

source.japanese: 朔屋、火縄を食む炎がすぐ側のバラックの中に駆け込んでいくのを見て、この次に起こるであろう事態を想像する。想像して一瞬で、自分の取る行動を決めた。この時ばかりは速かった。
source.english: Sakuya watched the flame eating the fuse dash into the shanty beside him, and imagined what would happen next. In an instant he decided what to do. For once, he was quick.

target.text: Verily, a spark of vermilion life was born into the world, and the flame raised its voice in delight, burning the fuse as it ran from its outset. The faint, charred traces it left behind were whirled up by the wind, dispersing.

Sakuya, seeing the flame feeding on the fuse run into the shack right next to him, imagined the situation that would probably occur right after it was done partaking. And the instant he did, he decided on his course of action. In this moment alone, he was fleet of both foot and mind.

source.japanese:
轟音が
　　　　大気震わせて
　　　　響き渡る
source.english:
A roar
Shook the air
And rang out.

target.text: A thunderous roar Set the air ashake And resounded

source.japanese:
音の衝撃波と同時に、粉微塵に吹き飛んだバラックの破片が朔屋の体に叩きつけられる。砲身より火弾吐き出す震撃は信天翁号すら大きく揺らす。
　事態の恐怖に耳塞ぎ甲板に這いずるように伏せ叫んでいた朔屋だが、破片の雨が体を打つ痛みも感じられぬ。ただひたすら、意味のない言葉を叫ぶばかり。
　そのうちにも。
source.english:
With the sonic shock came fragments of the shanty, blown to atoms, battering Sakuya’s body. The convulsion that vomited a ball of fire from the gun barrel sent even the Albatross reeling.

Terrified by the unfolding catastrophe, Sakuya clapped his hands over his ears and cowered flat against the deck, screaming. He could not even feel the pain of the debris raining against him. He could do nothing but shriek senseless words.

And all the while—

target.text: When the shock wave of sound hit Sakuya's body, so too did the fragments of the shack that had been blown to splinters. The concussive blasts of the flaming shells as they were belched from the gun barrel were so violent it rocked even the Albatross to her core. Covering his ears out of sheer terror at the situation, Sakuya was face-down on the deck and screaming, almost crawling along it, but he didn't even feel the pain of the hail of splinters striking him. All he did was desperately scream words without meaning. And even as this went on.

source.japanese:
砲撃の轟音は続けざまに響き渡る。朔屋の隣で今、高らかに笑う女が持っていた火縄は一条のみではなかったのだから。左右の舷側より、後部甲板より、次々と、地の底にて鎖持て呪縛されていた獣が解き放たれた歓喜の雄叫び然様に砲声轟く。
　そのたびに砲座を抱えていたバラックは粉々に砕かれて空に巻き上げられる。その周囲にひしめく同輩を道連れにして。
source.english:
Gunfire roared again and again. The woman now laughing loudly beside Sakuya had held more than one fuse. From port and starboard, from the afterdeck, one after another the guns thundered, like beasts chained and cursed in the depths of the earth bellowing with joy at their release.

Each time, the shanty containing the gun emplacement shattered and flew into the sky, taking its crowded neighbors with it.

target.text: The roaring booms of the shelling continued to resound around him. For the woman by his side, now laughing sonorously, was not holding just a single fuse in her hand. From the broadside on port and starboard, from the deck at the stern, one after another, the peals of cannon-fire rumbled forth like the euphoric war cries of a foul beast chained at the bottom of the earth now liberated from its binding spell. Every time it rang out, so was the shack sheltering the gun platform within smashed to pieces and blown into the air. Taking its jostling peers in its surroundings down with it.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「おおぅ……
　我が砲なれど、なかなかの威力……。
　一斉射だけでも、よく保ったもんだけど」
source.english:
“Ooh…
Even if they are my guns, that's quite a punch…
I'm impressed she held together even for a single salvo.”

source.japanese: 体震わす衝撃、ようやく途絶えたかと窺って、恐る恐ると耳を塞いでいた手を離す。硝煙の臭いが鼻衝く中、そこに聞こえてきたのは、悪魔の哄笑、いやさ、密航者の満足げな声だった。
source.english: When the shocks shaking his body seemed at last to have ceased, Sakuya listened warily, then fearfully took his hands from his ears. Powder smoke stabbed at his nose. What reached him was a devil’s peal of laughter—or rather, the stowaway’s satisfied voice.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Oooh…… Not to brag about my own ordnance, but that was quite the firepower……. I'm surprised at how well you were able to hold out, even if it was but a single shelling.」

After surmising that the impacts making his entire body tremble had finally ceased, he timidly removed the hands covering his ears. As the stench of gunpowder smoke slammed into his nose, what he heard was the loud laughter of the Devil himself, or rather, the satisfied voice of the stowaway.

source.japanese: 思いも寄らぬ砲撃に魂消たのか、信天翁号を囲んでいた船どもは、散り散りに進路を百八十度、反転させてまっしぐらに逃げていく。
source.english: Stunned by the utterly unexpected gunfire, the ships surrounding the Albatross scattered, turned their courses a full hundred and eighty degrees, and fled straight away.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あっはっは、逃げろ逃げろ」
source.english: “Ahahaha! Run, run!”

source.japanese: 船影が水平線の彼方に消える頃、洋上に残ったのは不幸にも砲弾の直撃を受けた船の残骸と、信天翁号自身が纏[まと]っていた襤褸の破片だった。
source.english: By the time their silhouettes disappeared beyond the horizon, all that remained upon the sea was the wreckage of vessels unlucky enough to take direct hits—and scraps of the Albatross's own rags.

source.japanese: ようやく静穏が戻ってくれば、どううまく要領得ていたのか、信天翁号の乗り組み達がわらわらと姿を現す。砲撃の振動に巻き込まれて海に放り出された間抜けなど見当たらないのが、さすがと言うべきか。
source.english: At last calm returned, and the Albatross's crew emerged in a swarm. Somehow they had known how to handle themselves. Not one fool seemed to have been shaken overboard by the gunfire. Impressive, one might say.

target.text: They must have been thunderstruck by the truly unexpected shelling, for the ships encircling the Albatross were scattering, changing course by 180 degrees, reversing and fleeing at full tilt.
【Stowaway】 「A-HA-HA, RUN, RUN AWAY!」

By the time the ships had vanished beyond the horizon, all that remained on the surface of the sea were the broken remains of any ships unfortunate enough to have been on the receiving end of a direct hit from a shell, as well as the fragments of the shabby scraps the Albatross had clad herself in.

When tranquility finally returned, though it was not clear how well they had grasped the situation, the crew of the Albatross appeared in droves.
