There were no signs of any fools having been caught up in the shaking caused by the shelling and then being thrown overboard, although perhaps that was only to be expected?

source.japanese: しかし、信天翁号の上甲板はすっかり様変わりしていた。
source.english: But the Albatross's upper deck had changed completely.

target.text: However, the upper deck of the Albatross had been thoroughly transformed.

source.japanese: 所狭し、原木栽培された平茸のように密集していたバラックはきれいさっぱり一掃され、今はその残骸が散らばるばかり。見張り台すら吹き飛ばされている。なんとも見通しのよくなったことだ。
source.english: The shanties that had crowded it like oyster mushrooms grown thick upon logs had been swept clean away. Only their wreckage lay scattered now. Even the lookout had been blown off. What an unobstructed view.

target.text: The shacks, which had been clumped together like log-grown oyster mushrooms, had been completely swept away, only their wreckage scattered about. Even the watchtower had been blown away. How wonderfully clear the view was now.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「嘘、あれって、穴が空いてたのを継ぎ当ててたんじゃなかったんだ……？」
source.english: “No way. Those weren't patches over holes…?”

source.japanese: あまりの変容に、呆然と呟く者あり。なにより一番の変化は、襤褸の下から現れた砲門達だ。まだ余韻たる硝煙うっすらたなびかせ、砲身触れれば火傷する王者の威容。
source.english: At the transformation, some murmured in disbelief. Above all, the greatest change was the guns revealed beneath the rags. Faint powder smoke still trailed from them. Their barrels would burn anyone who touched them; they stood in regal majesty.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「No way, isn't that where I patched up that hole……?」

There were those muttering in blank amazement at the overwhelming change in appearance. The greatest change of all was all the muzzles that had emerged from beneath the junk. With the imposing majesty of a king, faint trails of gunpowder smoke still wafted from them: touch and you shall be burnt.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「ど、どこの馬鹿だ、甲板上の物ごと、大砲ぶっ放したやつぁ……。
　……そもそも、この船にあんな砲なんぞ、
　一体いつ置いた……？」
source.english:
“Wh-what idiot fired cannons right through everything on deck…?
…And in the first place, when the hell were guns like that put aboard this ship…?”

source.japanese: そこにいた誰もが、初めて目にする信天翁号の主砲であった。古株の水夫長もだ。船の全てを把握しているはずのこの大男ですら、厳つく構えたこの砲塔を知らなかったのだ。
source.english: Everyone there was seeing the Albatross's main guns for the first time. Even the boatswain, an old hand. Even this huge man, who ought to know everything about the ship, had known nothing of those grimly poised turrets.

source.japanese: そこにいた誰もが？　いいや、違った。一人を除いて。彼女を除いて。
source.english: Everyone there? No. Except one. Except her.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Wh-, which idiot did this, who blew everything on the upper deck to pieces with a cannon……? ……Actually, first things first, since when exactly did this ship ever have guns like those……?」

It was the first time that all present had seen the main battery of the Albatross. Even the Bosun, a veteran of the ship. Even this giant of a man, who should know all there was to know about the ship, assumed a grim air, having been completely in the dark about this turret.
All present? No, that wasn't right. There was a single exception. She was the exception.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まあ、もともとあそこら辺は綺麗にしないと、って思ってたからね」
source.english: “Well, I'd been thinking that area needed cleaning up anyway.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Well, I was originally thinking that I really should clean this place up, you know?」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あんたかぁ！
　……そろそろ吐いてもらおうか」
source.english:
“You!
…It's about time you talked.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「So it was you! ……Isn't it about damn time you come clean?」

source.japanese:
皆がもう耐えかねていたのだ。
　問い糾したくて仕方なくなっていたのだ。
source.english:
None of them could stand it any longer.

They were desperate to question her.

target.text: None of them could put up with it anymore. They were dying to get some answers out of her.

source.japanese:
この少女。
　何度海に放り出しても舞い戻る。
　いつの間にか船倉に潜[ひそ]んでいる。
　この新しく始まった航海において、クロも双子もいない中で進む針路を指し示す。
　そして、
　今また、誰も知らなかった信天翁号の姿を晒して見せた。
　この密航者に。
source.english:
This woman.

However often they threw her into the sea, she returned.

Unnoticed, she hid in the hold.

On this newly begun voyage, without Kuro or the twins, she pointed out their course.

And now—

She had revealed an Albatross no one knew.

This stowaway.

source.japanese: 一体お前は───何者だ。
source.english: Who in the world—are you?

target.text: This girl. No matter how many times she is tossed into the ocean, she always comes back. Before you know it, she's hiding down in the hold of the ship. And when it came to this newly launched voyage, she showed the course forward even without Kuro or the twins present. And finally, just now, she revealed a side of the Albatross that none other knew. This stowaway.
Just───who in the world are you?

source.japanese: さて、皆の疑念も危険な水位をとうに越え、あとは表面張力にかろうじて引き留められて、雫のひと垂らしで溢れんばかりであったのだが。最後の一滴となる誰ぞの声が上がる寸前に、ここまで胸さえ張って昂然と構えてさあ来いの態、示していた密航者がいきなりばたりと倒れたとあっては、さしもの一同も慌てたのことであった。
source.english: By now everyone's suspicion had long since risen above the danger line. Surface tension alone held it back; one drop would make it overflow. Yet just before someone's voice could supply that last drop, the stowaway—who had stood proudly, chest out, all but saying ‘Come on, then’—suddenly fell flat. Even this company was alarmed.

source.japanese: 気を失った女の頬張って目を覚まさせんというのもあんまりかということで、代わりに皆の標的になったのは朔屋であった。なにしろここのところ、この謎の女の行動、ことあるごとについて回っていたのが朔屋だったのだから。皆の剣幕に晒されてしどろもどろに朔屋が答えるには、この密航者、ここまでかなり無理していた様子、ぶっ倒れるのも仕方ないんじゃないとの今ひとつ、要領の得ないものではあったが、今気絶して甲板に大の字になった密航者以上のことを朔屋が知るわけもなしと皆不承不承。ひとまず針路はそのままに、破片残骸散らばる甲板の掃除もあるのだしと一時、解散となったのだが。
source.english: Slapping an unconscious woman's cheek to wake her seemed a little much, so they turned instead upon Sakuya. Lately, after all, he had followed this mysterious woman through everything she did. Faced with their fury, Sakuya stammered out an answer: she seemed to have pushed herself rather hard all this time, so wasn't collapsing only natural? Not much of an explanation. But Sakuya could scarcely know more than the stowaway now sprawled unconscious on deck. Reluctantly they accepted it. The course would remain unchanged for now; besides, there was a deck full of wreckage to clean. They dispersed for the moment.

target.text: Well then, the water level of the doubts felt by all present had long since crossed the threshold of the perilous, now only just barely kept in place by surface tension, about to spill from but a single drop more. Just before someone's clamouring voice became the proverbial drop that made the glass overflow, the stowaway, who until now had even been puffing out her chest in triumphant pride, her bearing defiant, suddenly collapsed onto the deck with a thud, sending even all here into a panic.

Deciding that slapping the unconscious woman's cheeks to wake her up was going a bit too far, in exchange, it was Sakuya who became their target. That was because, of late, it was Sakuya whom this enigmatic woman's actions had all revolved around. Faced with the menacing glares of all present, Sakuya's only answer was that she seemed to have been overworking herself up to this point, so maybe it was inevitable that she'd collapse, an answer that didn't really get to the point, but they all reluctantly accepted that Sakuya wouldn't know anything more about this stowaway currently lying spread-eagle on the deck while unconscious.
For now, they decided to stay the course and spend some time cleaning up the debris littering the deck, and so they dispersed.

source.japanese: いつまでもこの宙ぶらりんな気持ちは誰とも良しとしないわけで、気絶したまま船倉の彼の女の隠れ家───朔屋からこの存在を明かされた水夫長はよくもご立派にこんなものいつの間にこさえやがったんだと言ったものだが───に放り込まれた密航者が、再びひょいと上甲板に現れた時、たちまち見つけた下級水夫の一人の声に、皆わらわらと集まり寄ったのだった。
source.english: No one was content to remain indefinitely in this uncertain state. Still unconscious, the stowaway was dumped into her hideout in the hold—when Sakuya revealed its existence, the boatswain had demanded when the hell she'd built such a fine establishment. When she popped up on the upper deck again, a junior sailor spotted her and called out. Everyone promptly swarmed around.

target.text: No one was content to be left with these feelings of uncertainty forever, and so the still-unconscious stowaway was carried down to her hideaway in the ship's hold───when Sakuya revealed its existence to the Bosun, he even exclaimed his amazement at just when she'd found the time to make something that impressive───and then hurled inside; when a deck boy happened to catch sight of her as she suddenly appeared once more on the upper deck, he raised his voice, and everyone rushed to gather around her at the sound.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……あの。密航者さん。
　ええと。その、みんな、集まったね。
　もどって、この船、もとどおり？」
source.english:
“…Um. Stowaway.
Well. Everyone's here now.
They've come back. Is this ship…back to normal?”

source.japanese: まずはクロ、これも船長の勤めと思ったか、はたまた何も考えずこの少女なりに考えまとめて二三段、言葉に出すのはすっ飛ばして声をかける。
source.english: Kuro spoke first. Perhaps she thought it a captain's duty. Or perhaps, without much thought, she put her ideas together in her own way, skipped two or three steps in saying them aloud, and addressed her.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Uhm. Miss stowaway. Uuhmm. So, all gathered now, right? Returned, so this ship, also as before?」
First up was Kuro, who, whether she felt it was her duty as captain or simply wasn't thinking at all, jumped a few steps ahead in her own logic, skipped the verbal preamble, and just spoke.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「って言えるかこれぇ？
　おーおー、すっかり、見晴らしよくなっちまってさ」
source.english:
“Can we really call it that?
Well, well. Look at the view we've got now.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Can you really call it that though? Ooh, wow, just look at how much better the view's gotten.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「だいたい、あたしらだってこの信天翁に乗ってそれなりになってたつもりだけど」
source.english: “Anyway, we'd thought we'd been aboard the Albatross for quite a while ourselves.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「First and foremost, we'd also like to think that we've been aboard the Albatross for long enough to feel like we belong here, but.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「それでもこの船に、あんな大砲が積んであるたぁ考えてもみなかった」
source.english: “Even so, we never dreamed this ship was carrying cannons like that.”

source.japanese: シサムとキサラ、双子同じく見つめる先は、先日、あっと驚く登場と同時の轟音響かす大活躍した単装砲だった。
source.english: Sisam and Kisara alike were looking at the single-barreled gun that had burst so spectacularly upon the scene the other day, announcing itself with a thunderous roar.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Even so, the thought that this ship could have a cannon like that stowed away on her never so much as crossed my mind.」

The thing Shisamu and Kisara, both twins together, stared at was that single-mounted gun that had knocked the breath out of them the other day, where it had suddenly made its presence known with resounding peals of thunder during its spectacular showing.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「当たり前でしょう、隠してたんだから」
source.english: “Of course not. I was hiding them.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Well yeah, obviously? Because I was hiding it.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「隠してたっておめえよ……。
　なんぼバラックの中に押しこまれたって、
　俺らはちょくちょく
　バラックも使ってたぜ？」
source.english:
“Hiding them, you say…
However much you crammed them into shanties,
we used those shanties
pretty often, you know?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「"Hiding it", you little……. No matter how damn hard you crammed that thing inside a shack, we also use those shacks every now and then, yeah?」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「それでも、
　ちいとも気づかないってのは……」
source.english:
“And we never
noticed a thing…”

source.japanese: 誰よりもこの船を知っているはず、その自尊心もいたく傷つけられたのか、声にもどこか凄みの欠けた水夫長に、言葉をかけたのはもう一方の船の主[ヌシ]、ただしこちらの担当は船の下層の釜の方。
source.english: He ought to know this ship better than anyone. Perhaps his pride had been badly wounded; even the boatswain's voice lacked something of its menace. Another master of the ship spoke to him—though this one's domain was the boilers below.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「And the fact that we still didn't notice even in the slightest……」

The Bosun, he who should know this ship better than any other, whose self-esteem must have been gravely wounded judging from the lack of menace in his tone of voice, was spoken to by the other head of the ship, this one instead in charge of the boiling pot near her bottom.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「……目の当たりにしていたとしても、『見た事を覚えていなかった』なら、わからない、と。
　そういうことですか？」
source.english:
“…Even if we saw them with our own eyes, we wouldn't know if we ‘didn't remember having seen them.’
Is that what you mean?”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「……Supposing that even were you to catch sight of it, you would 『not remember seeing it』, then you would never know. Is it something to that effect?」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「うわあ！　機関長！
　何年ぶりですか、明るいうちに上甲板に出てくるのなんて」
source.english:
“Whoa! Chief!
How many years has it been since you came onto the upper deck in daylight?”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Waah! Nanban! How many years has it been since you've showed up on the upper deck while the sun's still out?」 (TN: In Japan, nanban, written "南蛮", is a dated term that literally means southern barbarian, often used to refer to Western Europeans and their colonies like Hong Kong historically. It can be derogatory, depending on intent.)

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「僕初めて見た……機関長が上甲板に出てくるのなんて……」
source.english: “I've never seen it before…the chief engineer coming onto the upper deck…”

source.japanese: 中層甲板より続く昇降段を跫音響かせ影の中から現れたのは、機関長。その姿を見て驚いた下級水夫君達からひそひそざわめく声あがるのだが、それには構わず密航者は彼に向かってにっこり微笑む。
source.english: Footsteps rang upon the ladder from the middle deck. The chief engineer emerged from the shadows. The startled junior sailors whispered and murmured at the sight, but the stowaway ignored them and smiled at him.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「I've never seen this before…… to think that the Chief Engineer would show himself on the upper deck……」

With clacking footsteps, the Chief Engineer emerged from within the shadows of the ladder leading to the middle deck. The deck boys who saw him stirred with shocked whispering, but the stowaway paid it no mind, turning to face him with a broad grin.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あなたはなかなか筋が良い、機関長。
　あなたの脳の構造が、かえって理解を深めるのかな……興味深い……開けてみていい？　だめ？
　ともかく、おおよそはそういうこと」
source.english:
“You have a knack for this, Chief Engineer.
Perhaps the structure of your brain actually helps you understand…interesting…may I open it up? No?
Anyway, that's more or less it.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「You've got a good head on your shoulders, Chief Engineer. Maybe the structure of your brain actually deepens your understanding instead……fascinating……may I open it up and have a look? No? Anyway, that's pretty much the long and short of it.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そしてそのあたりも、大筋には余り関係がなかったりするけどね」
source.english: “Though that doesn't have much to do with the main point.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And, well, that's not really all that relevant to the important bits of this story, alright?」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「でしたら、その大筋というものを、
　お話になってはいかが？
　みなさん、やきもきしていらっしゃるようだわ」
source.english:
“Then why not
explain that main point?
Everyone seems rather impatient.”

source.japanese: そう言ったこの人自身は、果たしてそのやきもきとやらをどれほど共有してるのやら、微塵もそんなものを感じさせぬ泪の言葉にすかさず被さる、
source.english: How much of that so-called impatience the lady herself shared was anybody’s guess; not a trace of it entered Rui’s voice. Promptly speaking over her came—

target.text: 【Rui】 「If so, why don't you speak of these "important bits" then? It seems we are all getting rather impatient here.」

Did the woman who said those words herself actually ever share in any of that impatience or whatever one could call it? There was not a trace of any such thing to be found in Rui's words, and more immediately followed them,

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ああ。手短に頼むわ。
　さっきみたいな、まわりくどいうえに、
　わかりづらいなんてのはごめんだからね」
source.english:
“Yeah. Keep it short.
None of that roundabout,
impossible-to-follow stuff from before.”

source.japanese: こちらはしごく直截な、航海士の声。
source.english: The navigator's exceedingly direct voice.

source.japanese: そう、もうもはや皆は焦らされ待ちきれなくなっているのだ。砲が見えたの見えないだのはどうでもよろしい。さぁ、いざいざ皆の衆どうぞこちらへ拝聴あれ。密航者はその場にいる皆すべてに視線を向けて、自分の正体を明かすのだった！
source.english: Yes, by now they had all been kept waiting too long. Whether the guns had been visible or invisible no longer mattered. Come, come, ladies and gentlemen, gather round and lend an ear. The stowaway looked at everyone present and revealed who she was!

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Yeah. And keep it short, please. If you start getting roundabout like just now, it'll be too hard to understand, and I'll pass on that.」
It was the first mate speaking in an exceedingly blunt tone.

Indeed, by now, they had all been tantalized to the point they couldn't bear to wait a second longer. Who cared about being able to see some cannon or not? Now come, come, all present, listen with great care and respect. The stowaway sent a look to all here, then revealed her true identity!

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「船には船霊というものがあるの。
　あなた達が信天翁号と呼ぶ、
　この船にもね。
　そしてその船霊が私」
source.english:
“Ships have what we call a ship's spirit.
This ship you call the Albatross has one too.
And that ship's spirit is me.”

source.japanese: ご要望通り、至極手短に、微塵ももったいぶることなく。
source.english: As requested: exceedingly brief, without the least show of mystery.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Ship's have these things called Funadama. And this ship you call the Albatross, she has one too, okay? And that Funadama is me.」 (TN: A Funadama, written "船霊", is a Shinto goddess enshrined in the main mast of a specific ship to serve as her guardian deity.)
As requested, it was kept exceedingly concise, without even the slightest bit of pretense.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「マジで手短にまとめやがったよこいつ。
　……なんだか気配が変わったな、あんた。
　この船に忍びこんでは、簀巻きにされてた頃と比べると」
source.english:
“She really did keep it short.
…You feel different somehow.
From when you used to sneak aboard and get rolled up in a mat.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Damn, she really did keep it short. ……There's something that's changed about the way you feel. Compared to when you'd sneak aboard this ship, get tied up in bamboo mats, then be tossed into the sea.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「手短は手短だろうけどさ。
　今のは説明？　今のでなにかわかった人いる？　今ので納得した人は？」
source.english:
“Brief, sure.
But was that an explanation? Did anyone understand anything? Is anyone satisfied?”

source.japanese: 皆一様に、首を左右に振る。
source.english: Everyone shook their head.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……もうちょっとさ、噛み砕いた説明ってのをしてやったほうがいいんじゃないか？
　俺もいい加減、なにがどうなっているのか知りたいんだよ」
source.english:
“…Shouldn't you explain it a little more simply?
I'd like to know what's going on too, by now.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「You did keep it short, yeah, but. Was that right now supposed to be an explanation? Is there anybody here who understood anything from that? Anybody here who is satisfied?」
They all shook their heads from side to side in unison.
【Naomasa】 「……Don't you think it would be better if you explain it in a way that is a little, you know, easier to digest? I'd also really just like to know what in the world is going on already.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だって私、『あんたはなにもんだ』って訊かれたから、その通りに答えただけで」
source.english: “But you asked, ‘Who are you?’ I only answered the question.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「But, I mean, I was asked "Who are you?", so I just answered accordingly, that's all.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「その答えが答えだっつぅの！
　船霊だぁ？　まああたしらもこれでも船乗りだからね、知ってることは知ってるさ」
source.english:
“It's that answer we're talking about!
A ship's spirit? Well, we're sailors, after all. We do know about them.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「So you're saying that answer is the truth! A Funadamaaa? Well, while it might not always look like it, we are proper sailors, so we know of the concept.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あれでしょ、読んで字の如し、船の魂みたいなもんで、航海の安全とか豊漁とか授けてくれるっていう、カミサマみたいなもん」
source.english: “What the name says, right? Something like the soul of a ship. A sort of god who grants safe voyages and good catches.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「I guess it is literally what the kanji sound like, something like the spirit of a ship, one that you offer things to for a safe voyage or a good haul of fish, a bit like a god or something.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「するってーと最近のカミサマは、女の子の姿でベストにズボンでリボンタイか。また見やすい格好を選んでくれたもんだ」
source.english: “So these days the gods take the form of girls in vests, pants and ribbon ties? How considerate of them to choose a look that's easy on the eyes.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「So then, the gods these days run around as girls dressed in a vest, a pair of pants, and a ribbon tie? Wow, you really picked an outfit that makes it easy to tell.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「でもこの海には、リーファージャケットでミニスカートの『セント・エルモの灯』もいるのだし」
source.english: “But these seas also have St. Elmo's fire in reefer jackets and miniskirts.”

source.japanese: 呆れに嫌味重ねたシサムの声に、変わらず飄とした態で答える密航者、双子に始まり一人ずつ視線を向けて自分の時と同じようにその正体を確認していく。
source.english: The stowaway answered Sisam's exasperated sarcasm with her usual airy manner. Beginning with the twins, she looked at them one by one, confirming their true identities just as she had her own.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「But we've also got『St. Elmo's fire』 dressed in reefer jackets and miniskirts sailing around these seas.」

Faced with the mixture of exasperation and snide sarcasm in Shisamu's tone, the stowaway answered with her usual nonchalant attitude, and starting from the twins, she looked at them all one by one, confirming their true identities like she had her own.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ノアが放ったという烏は白いし。
　人魚姫は遊蕩尽くし果たして退屈してるし」
source.english:
“The crow Noah released is white.
And the mermaid princess has exhausted every pleasure and grown bored.”

source.japanese: そしてさて、といった風に皆に向き直る。
source.english: Then she turned to the company again, as though to say: well, then.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「The bird Noah sent forth is white. Having exhausted every dissolute pleasure in life, the mermaid princess tires of it all.」
And then, with an unspoken "well then", she turned about to face all of them once more.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「私が船霊と今さらいったところで───
　って思う人、はい手を上げて」
source.english:
“Anyone thinking, ‘Why make a fuss about her being a ship's spirit at this point?’—
Raise your hand.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Me being a Funadama isn't really that outlandish at this point─── All who agree, raise your hands.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「はい」
source.english: “Here.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Yep.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「はい」
source.english: “Here.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Yep.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あい」
source.english: “Here.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Aye.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「こちらに同じ」
source.english: “Likewise.”

source.japanese: ぱらぱらぱらと揃いはせずとも、手を下げっぱなしの者はなし。キサラも今度は心底呆れるだけ。
source.english: Hands went up here and there, not in unison, but no one left theirs down. This time Kisara could only be utterly exasperated.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Same here.」
Though they didn't go up all at once, there wasn't a single person who kept their hand down. This time, Kisara could also only be exasperated from the bottom of her heart.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……なにこのノリ。
　だけどごめん。なんかもうごめん。
　言われてみればそうだった」
source.english:
“…What's with this?
But sorry. No, really—sorry.
Now you mention it, that's true.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……What's with everybody playing along here? But I'm sorry. I'm really so sorry. Now that you mention it, yeah, you're right.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「で、その船霊様は一体なにをしようとしているわけよ」
source.english: “So what, exactly, is our ship's spirit trying to do?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「So then, what exactly is our great guardian spirit trying to accomplish here?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「私は海に帰りたい」
source.english: “I want to return to the sea.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I want to go home to the sea.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「私は今さら帰りたくない」
source.english: “I have no wish to return now.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I am not very inclined to return home anymore.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「この場合の対立はパラダイムが違うので、大してお話に差し支えはないよ。私が帰りたい海というのは、この船が浮かんでいるここじゃないから」
source.english: “We're working in different paradigms, so that disagreement doesn't really interfere with the discussion. The sea I want to return to isn't this one, where the ship is floating.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「This conflict here stems from a difference in paradigms, so it won't make much of an impediment for what I'm talking about. The sea I'd like to go home to is not the one this ship is currently floating on.」

source.japanese: 舷側に寄りかかり、一度だけ密航者は広がる海を振り返る。その見つめる目に一瞬、翳ったのは郷愁の色だろうか、しかしその視線は水平線の果てさらにその果てへと向けられて、実は海には焦点してないと一体誰が気付いたろう。
source.english: Leaning against the rail, the stowaway looked back once at the sea. Was it homesickness that briefly shadowed her eyes? But her gaze extended to the horizon and farther beyond. Who could have noticed that it was not actually focused on the sea?

target.text: Leaning against the side of the ship, the stowaway looked over her shoulder to gaze out upon the vast sea but a single time. A shadow, surely tinged with the warm hues of nostalgia, flitted across those intently staring orbs for a brief instant, but did anyone ever notice how that gaze was directed at an end beyond the end of the horizon, never actually finding a focal point on the ocean?

source.japanese:
再び密航者は皆へと向かう。
　そしてその口から語られ始めたのは、この少女の船の旅の物語だった。
source.english:
She turned to them again.

And from her lips began the story of this woman's voyage, this ship's voyage.

target.text: The stowaway once more faced everyone else. And then her lips began to narrate, to weave together the tale of the voyage of this girl's ship.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「───かつて、船がありました。
『地球』という名の惑星の、とある国で。
　その国が『明治』という元号を使っていた時代」
source.english:
“—Once, there was a ship.
In a certain country on a planet called ‘Earth.’
In the days when that country used the era name ‘Meiji.’”

source.japanese: その国は、大雑把に頼まれもせぬのに東洋と一括りされた地域、その星で一番広い大洋に浮かんだひとかたまりの島々にあったその国は、大きな歴史の区切りをうんとこしょと漸[ようや]く乗り越えやっとのことで近代国家の態、繕い始めたばかり、そう、親鳥はおらず、羽根はようやく生えそろったばかり、それでも、すでに先に空へと飛び立ち、我が物顔で旋回する猛禽どもの姿を見て、羽ばたこうと決意した雛鳥だった。足らないところは多かったけれど、開化の機運に満ちて、他の国にたくさん学び、様々なモノを作り出そうとしていた。
source.english: That country lay among a cluster of islands in the planet's widest ocean, in a region lumped, broadly and without being asked, under the name ‘the Orient.’ Heaving itself at last over a great divide in history, it had only just begun to put together the semblance of a modern nation. Yes: a fledgling without a parent bird, its feathers barely grown. Yet watching the birds of prey that had already taken wing and circled as though the sky were theirs, it had resolved to flap its own wings. Much was lacking, but it brimmed with the impulse toward enlightenment, learned a great deal from other countries, and tried to produce all manner of things.

source.japanese: その中の一つに、蒸気機関船があった。異国に設計と建造を任され、作り上げられたその軍艦───巡洋艦は、けれども確かにその新しい国家のための艦だった。名前だってその新しい国の言葉で名付けられた。
source.english: Among them were steamships. Design and construction were entrusted to a foreign country. Yet the warship—the cruiser—built there was certainly a vessel for that new nation. Even her name came from its language.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「───Once upon a time there was a ship. On a planet, a great globe known as 『Earth』, in a certain country. In the age when that country used the name『Meiji』as the designation of its Imperial era.」

That country was located in an area that had been loosely lumped together as the Orient, unsolicited as that may have been, and that country, a cluster of islands floating atop the vastest ocean on that planet, had through strenuous efforts finally overcome a major historical turning point and turned into a modern state, barely in the infant stages of stitching things together, yes, with feathers that had only just fledged, with no mother bird to turn to, and yet, it was already taking off, diving into the air, like a bird of prey circling the skies and acting like it owned the place, a baby bird that had resolved to spread its wings and fly.
It was still lacking in many places, but it was brimming with the momentum of enlightenment, learning much from other countries, attempting to manufacture all manner of things on its own.

Amongst those many things was a steamship. A warship───a cruiser, whose design and building had been entrusted to a foreign country, but even so, it was certainly a warship built expressly for that new nation. It was even christened in the language of that new country.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そう、かつて、船があったの。
　船の名は───畝傍。
　フランスから日本へ、届けられるはずだった、その船」
source.english:
“Yes, once there was a ship.
Her name was—Unebi.
She was supposed to be delivered from France to Japan.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Indeed, once upon a time there was a ship. That ship's name was─── the Unebi. That ship, the one that was supposed to have been delivered from France to Japan.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「けれどその船は。
　回航航海の途上であろう事か行方不明となり、そのまま消失と判断されて───」
source.english:
“But that ship—
Of all things, she went missing on her delivery voyage. In the end she was declared lost—”

source.japanese: そう、その船は期待に胸膨らませて待つその国には辿り着かなかった。連絡途絶え、待てども現れず、探せど見つからなかった船を、その国は消失艦として諦めた。では、その船はどこへ行ったのか。どうなったのか。それは、彼女の口から語られる。
source.english: Yes. She never reached the country waiting for her with eager anticipation. Contact ceased. She did not appear, however long they waited; she could not be found, however they searched. The country gave up on her as a lost ship. Then where had she gone? What had become of her? That would be told in the woman's own words.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「However, that ship. It was surely lost in the middle of its voyage there, and it was simply deemed to have vanished───」

Indeed, that ship never arrived in that country, which was waiting for it with its chest swelling with anticipation. All contact had been lost, and just as it never came while they waited, they also never found it when they searched, and so that country gave up on it as a missing ship. So, where did that ship go then? What happened to it? That, too, was narrated by her lips.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「───あの航海の途中、とてつもない大時化に巻き込まれ、もう沈むしかないと諦めかかったっけ。けれどもけして沈むわけにはいかないと、頑張って頑張って、それはもう頑張った」
source.english: “—During that voyage, we were caught in a tremendous storm. I nearly gave up, thinking we could only sink. But I couldn't sink. I struggled and struggled—oh, how I struggled.”

source.japanese: その嵐の風はどれほど強かったのだろう、波はどれほど高かったのだろう。雨は雷はどれほど降り注いだのだろう。艦橋にて指示飛ばし必死に舵握る艦長、航海士達。甲板船倉駆け回る水夫達。頑張った、彼らは頑張った。彼らの故郷に帰るために、この船を待つ彼らの国に帰るために。引っ繰り返らんばかりの揺れに海に投げ出された者もいたのだろう。高波を被り甲板洗われた時に流された者もいたのだろう。それでも彼らは、最後の一人になってもなお、頑張ったのだろう。
source.english: How strong had the wind been in that storm? How high the waves? How much rain and lightning had poured down? The captain and navigators, giving orders on the bridge, desperately holding the helm. Sailors running through the decks and holds. They struggled. They struggled to return to their homes, to the country waiting for this ship. Perhaps some had been flung into the sea as she rocked, almost overturning. Perhaps some had been swept away when high waves washed the deck. Even down to the last man, surely they had struggled.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「───During that voyage, we were caught in a tremendous storm, and I was on the verge of resigning myself to foundering. But I was determined to never let myself sink, and so I persevered, we persevered, we kept at it when all seemed lost.」

How biting must the howling gales of that storm have been, how tall must the waves have surged. How the rain must have fallen in great torrents upon them, the lightning struck them. On the bridge, the captain and the first mate desperately clutching the helm as the orders they barked flew through the air. The sailors bustling about the hold and the deck. They tried, oh, how they fought. So they could return to their homeland, so they could bring this ship with them, back home to the country so eagerly awaiting it.

There must surely have been some unfortunate souls tossed overboard when the ship lurched as if about to capsize. Even so, they must have continued their valiant struggle, even when they were brought down to the last man.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そうしてどうにか嵐を乗り越えたにはもう───私はこの海にいたのでした」
source.english: “And when at last I'd somehow weathered the storm—I was already in these seas.”

source.japanese: 今は晴天穏やかなこの海に。そう密航者は語りを締めてみせたのだった。
source.english: In these seas, now calm beneath a clear sky. With that, the stowaway brought her story to an end.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And after struggling so, when we managed to ride out the storm─── I found myself in this sea.」
And now, she was in this clear, calm sea. The stowaway concluded her tale thus.

source.japanese:
誰もが、声を失っていた。しばしの間。
　やがてあがった声はしどろもどろな朔屋のもの。
source.english:
Everyone had lost their voice. For a while.

Eventually Sakuya spoke, stumbling over his words.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「途中で船と君の視点が混じってるんだが、
　ええとつまり……君が船霊だっていうと、
　それはそれでいいわけで、ああ、なんだ、
　この信天翁号って言うのはもともとは───」
source.english:
“You and the ship got mixed together halfway through the story,
but, um…if you're the ship's spirit,
I suppose that's fine. Ah, so,
this Albatross was originally—”

target.text: All were left at a loss for words. For a time. It was Sakuya who eventually raised his faltering voice, stumbling over his words.

【Naomasa】 「Your perspective and that of the ship got kinda mixed up along the way, but, uhh, to summarize…… if you say you're a Funadama, that's fine, no problem there, uhmm, what was it, so the Albatross here was originally the───」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「その、畝傍が前身、という事ですか。
　妙だ妙だとは思っていた」
source.english:
“That Unebi was her former identity, you mean.
I'd thought it strange. Very strange.”

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「この船の、いや、艦の、と言い直しますか。
　ともかく、二軸レシプロ蒸気機関、円罐九基、などという形式は、これまでどんな記録にもない」
source.english:
“This ship—no, perhaps I should say warship.
In any case, I've never found a record of a configuration like this: twin-shaft reciprocating steam engines, nine cylindrical boilers…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「This "Unebi" would be her predecessor of sorts, is that correct? I did always find it curious, very curious indeed.」

【Chief Engineer】 「This ship's, or rather, warship's, as I should instead restate it? Regardless, the two-shaft compound reciprocal steam engine, the nine cylindrical boilers: this manner of design has never been found in any records hitherto.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「つまりその『地球』製の機関だと。
　だから異なっているのだと」
source.english:
“In other words, machinery made on ‘Earth.’
And that is why it differs.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「That is to say, it is a machine of『Earth』make. So you claim that is why it differs so.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「だいたいよ、その『地球』ていうのはなんなんだ、どこなんだ。それがまずわかんねえ。字面からすると、地面の球？　丸い地面？」
source.english: “First off, what is this ‘Earth’? Where is it? I don't even understand that. The name means ‘earth’ and ‘globe’? A ball of ground? Round ground?”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「First of all, what is this globe you call『Earth』supposed to be, where is it? That's the first thing I don't get. From the literal meaning, a globe made of earth? A round piece of land?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……地球とこの世界はとてもよく似ている。景色や海の様子、住んでいる者たち。あなた達の姿を思い浮かべれば、それが地球の似姿になる」
source.english: “…Earth and this world are very much alike. Their landscapes, their seas, their inhabitants. Picture yourselves, and you have a likeness of Earth.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「……Earth and this world very closely resemble each other. The landscapes and the seas, as well as the peoples who live there. If you try to imagine how it looks to you in your head, that will share a close likeness with Earth.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ただ決定的に異なる点は、さっき水夫長が言ったこと。私が居た地球は。その名前の通りに。文字通り、球形の世界だったよ───」
source.english: “But the decisive difference is what the boatswain just said. The Earth I came from. As its name says. Literally a spherical world—”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「But the crucial, defining difference lies in what the Bosun just said. The Earth I lived on. As the word globe would suggest. Was, literally, a globe, a spherical world───」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「嘘だろおい。そんな世界なんて想像もつかないぜ？　じゃあなにか？　野球の球をなぞるように、たとえばこの海域からどこからどこまでも北上していくと───」
source.english: “You're kidding. I can't imagine a world like that. So what? Following the surface of a baseball, say—if you kept sailing north from these waters, on and on—”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Oi, now that's gotta be a lie. I can't even imagine a world like that, yeah? So, is this what you're saying? If, for example, you kept heading north from this part of the sea, as far as you could, it would be like tracing a finger across a baseball and───」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「しまいには、同じ海域に戻ってくるって事か？
　ありえねえ」
source.english:
“You'd end up back in the same waters?
Impossible.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「In the end, you'd come back to the same part of the sea you left? Unthinkable.」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「世界は平べったい皿みてえなもんで、世界の果ては暗黒の未踏破海域であって、そっから先を越えるとどこかに落っこちちまう。
　これが世界の有り様だろうが」
source.english:
“The world's like a flat plate. At its edge lies a dark, unexplored sea, and if you go beyond that, you fall somewhere.
That's how the world is.”

source.japanese:
きっぱりと水夫長、密航者の言葉をはねのける。密航者にとっては道理の常識当たり前であっても、この世界に生まれてきた者にとっては無理が通って非常識なのだ。
　だが、それでも。ここに集まった者には多かれ少なかれ、無理と非常識がついて回っていたのだ。
source.english:
The boatswain firmly rejected the stowaway's words. What was perfectly sensible common knowledge to her was impossible nonsense to those born in this world.

And yet. More or less, impossibility and nonsense had dogged everyone gathered here.

target.text: 【Bosun】 「The world's flat like a plate, there is an uncharted, dark sea at the end of the world, and if you cross that sea, you'll end up falling down to who-knows-where. That's the way the world is, no doubt about it.」

The Bosun flatly rejected the stowaway's words. No matter how obvious, how common sense it was to the stowaway, it was an unreasonably absurdity to those born in this world. However, even so. The unreasonable and the absurd clung to those gathered here, to a greater or lesser extent.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……水夫長。それなんだけどさ、あたしらはそれ、なんとなく受け入れられるような気がするんだ」
source.english: “…Bosun. About that—we think we might be able to accept it, somehow.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……Bosun. So, about that. For some reason, we kind of feel like we can accept that as being true.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたしらは、北方氷土で見てきた、聞いてきたことがある。どうやらこの世界は歪められた物だって話も聞いた」
source.english: “In the northern ice fields, we saw and heard things. We also heard that this world's apparently been distorted.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Up there in the frozen northern wastes, we saw some things, heard some things. And we were told about how this world is twisted and distorted, apparently.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「ねえ水夫長、ちょっと考えてみて」
source.english: “Bosun, think about it a little.”

source.japanese:
あたしらは海にいる。海流が流れ、風が吹く。それは当たり前だ、海なのだから。
　しかし、その風は何処から吹いているのだろう、何故、最初の空気の流れは生まれたのだろう。海流は？　何処から流れて何処へ行くのか。世界の果てでそれらが消えるなら、消えた流れは何処に行ってしまうのだろう。
source.english:
We're at sea. Currents flow, winds blow. Naturally: it's the sea.

But where does that wind come from? Why did the first movement of air arise? And the currents? Where do they flow from, where do they go? If they vanish at the world's edge, where does the vanished flow go?

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Come on, Bosun, just try to think on it for a little bit.」

We are on the ocean. The ocean currents flow, the wind blows. That much is obvious, because it is the ocean. However, just where does that wind blow in from, and why, exactly, was that very first flow of air formed? The ocean currents? Where do they flow in from, and to where do they flow? If they disappear at the end of the world, just where does that vanished flow go?

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ううむぅ……」
source.english: “Hmmm…”

source.japanese: 誰もそれを考えなかった。それを考え、疑問に思い、究明しようとする者はいなかったのか。何故、そんな者が現れなかったのか。
source.english: No one had thought about it. Had no one thought, wondered, tried to find out? Why had no such person appeared?

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Hummm……」
Nobody had ever thought of that. Was there simply nobody who had ever thought of it, doubted it, and then attempted to investigate it? Why had no such person ever materialized?

source.japanese: そこでおそらく、先ほどの筋がよいとの言に寄れば、一番そこに近い者が声をあげる。惜しむらくは彼生来の奇癖が行く手に立ちはだかっているだろうが。
source.english: Then someone spoke who, perhaps, judging by the earlier remark about his knack for this, had come closest. Unfortunately, his peculiar lifelong habit probably stood in his way.

target.text: Then, the man who was, in all likelihood, the best candidate for what the stowaway mentioned earlier, having a good head on your shoulders, spoke up. Unfortunately, his congenital quirk was likely getting in his way.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ああ、なるほど。つまり君の『地球』というのは、私たちのこの世界とは異なる世界だと」
source.english: “Ah, I see. In other words, your ‘Earth’ is a different world from ours.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Aah, I see. So to summarize, you claim this『Earth』of yours is a world that differs from our own.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「あー、お姉さん、里帰りしたいんだ」
source.english: “Oh—you want to go home, miss.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Aah, so you just want to go back home, lady.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そういう事よ、水夫君。ちなみに君のことはよく覚えているからね」
source.english: “That's it, sailor. Incidentally, I remember you very well.”

source.japanese: 同じ顔した群の中から、密航者、迷いもせずに声をあげた下級水夫君を特定する。
source.english: Without hesitation, the stowaway picked out the junior sailor who had spoken from the crowd of identical faces.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「That's right, young sailor. Incidentally, I remember you very well, you know.」
Without any hesitation, the stowaway identified one particular deck boy from the crowd of identical faces.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「……奇遇だなあ、僕もだよ」
source.english: “…What a coincidence. So do I.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「……What a coincidence, I also remember you.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「なにしろ私を二回簀巻きにして海に放りこみ、一回舷側から逆さ吊りにして、二回袋に詰めて港のゴミ捨て場に放置してくれた子だもんね」
source.english: “After all, you're the man who rolled me in a mat and threw me into the sea twice, hung me upside down over the side once, and stuffed me into a sack and left me at a harbor dump twice.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「For you see, you're the boy who tied me up in a bamboo mat and tossed me overboard twice, you hung me upside down from the side of the ship once, and you stuffed me in a sack and left me in the garbage dump in some port twice.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「よかったよね。私が船霊でなかったら、五回は死んでたところよ、この殺人未遂者」
source.english: “Lucky for you. If I weren't a ship's spirit, you'd have killed me five times over, you would-be murderer.”

source.japanese: どうやら浅からぬ因縁あったようだ。
source.english: Apparently they had quite a history.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Aren't you lucky? If I hadn't been a Funadama, I would have died five times over, you attempted murderer!」
It seems they shared a deep connection.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「僕だけがやったんじゃないよう」
source.english: “It wasn't just me!”

source.japanese: 許してやれ、密航者よ。その時のお前はただの密航者。仕方がないとはいえ、何度も戻ってきたお前が悪い。
source.english: Forgive him, stowaway. At the time, you were merely a stowaway. Unavoidable though it was, you were to blame for coming back so often.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「It's not like I was the only one doing it.」
Forgive him, O stowaway. At the time, you were but a mere stowaway. Even if it was an inevitability of your being, you are still to blame for coming back again and again.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まあそんな事は大した問題じゃないのよ」
source.english: “Well, none of that's very important.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Well, that stuff isn't really a big deal.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「とにかく、私は、厭。平面的で四方が封鎖された世界なんて、厭」
source.english: “Anyway, I hate it. I hate a flat world sealed off on all sides.”

source.japanese: きっぱりと言い放つ声の強さは彼女の矜恃によるものか。それもあろう、地球という世界の半周を旅して、己が身を待ち望み、乗り組み達の故郷たる国へと向かっていた船なのだ。
source.english: Was it her pride that lent such force to the flat declaration? That must have been part of it. She was a ship that had traveled halfway round Earth, bound for the country eagerly awaiting her, the homeland of her crew.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Anyway, I just can't stand it. I can't stand the thought of this flat world sealed off in every which direction.」

Perhaps the strength in her tone of voice as she made that blunt assertion was a product of her pride? That, and because she was a ship that had travelled halfway round the world she called Earth, bound for the country eagerly awaiting her very own self, the birthplace of her crew.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だから私は、帰りたい」
source.english: “So I want to go home.”

source.japanese: それは望郷と、彼の国の力にならんという気概入り交じった宣言だった。
source.english: The declaration mingled homesickness with the resolve to serve that country.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「That's why I want to return home.」
It was a declaration formed of a mixture of homesickness and the determination to be of aid to that country.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「お好きなように。誰も止めはしなくってよ」
source.english: “As you please. No one will stop you.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「By all means, as you please. None here will stop you.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「よかった。なら協力してね、泪さんも」
source.english: “Good. Then help me, Rui.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「That's a relief. Then help me out here, and that goes for you too, Rui-san.」

source.english: “—With what?”

target.text: 【Rui】 「───With what?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「長い事この世界を航海してきて、ようやく見つけたの」
source.english: “After sailing this world for a long time, I finally found it.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「After sailing around this world for a long time, I finally found it.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「南の海の彼方に、この世界が綻んでいる場所が、一つあるらしい」
source.english: “Far out in the southern seas, there seems to be one place where this world is coming apart at the seams.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そこからなら、元居た地球に帰れるかもしれない。でもその航海に必要なのは、世界の枠組みからはみ出した乗り組み達じゃないと」
source.english: “From there, perhaps I can get back to the Earth I came from. But for that voyage, I need a crew who don't fit within this world's framework.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「It seems that, down beyond the southern seas, there is a single place where this world is coming apart at the seams.」

【Stowaway】 「And if I head through there, I might be able to go back to the Earth I came from. But in order to make that voyage happen, I needed a crew that couldn't be contained in the framework of this world.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「たとえば、三位一体者になり損ねた双子とか、全ての生き物の運び手であったはずの、ノアからも呪われた烏とか、王子さまを刺し殺して生きのびている人魚姫とか」
source.english: “Twins who failed to become a Triune One, for instance. A crow cursed even by Noah, who was supposed to carry all living things. A mermaid princess still alive after stabbing her prince to death.”

source.japanese: さらりと面々の古傷暴いて晒す密航者。悪意微塵も感じられないのがいっそ質悪い。不意の名指しに呆気にとられた彼女達に代わり、朔屋も声も憮然としたもの。
source.english: The stowaway blithely laid bare one old wound after another. Her utter lack of malice only made it worse. While the women stood dumbstruck at being singled out without warning, Sakuya spoke for them, his voice no less sullen.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……やめろって。君は物言いに、歯に衣を着せなさすぎ。ほらみなよ」
source.english: “…Stop that. You're far too blunt. Look.”

source.japanese: 一瞬呆けてそれが過ぎれば、後には当然、怒りが湧く。
source.english: A moment's blankness passed. After it, naturally, anger arose.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「For example, twins who failed to become a Triune Being, or a crow cursed even by Noah, the man who should have brought all life with him, or a mermaid princess who stabbed the prince to death and lived long.」

The stowaway dug out and exposed their old wounds for all to see without hesitation. That not the slightest trace of malice could be felt from it only made it in even poorer taste. In place of the girls, left astonished at unexpectedly being called out, it was Sakuya, the man and his tone of voice dejected both, who spoke.
【Naomasa】 「……Stop that. The way you speak, it's way too direct. Come on, look at them.」
For an instant, they were all struck dumb, but once that passed, naturally, anger welled up.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「じゃあなにか。あたしらは、あんたの里帰りのためにかき集められた、航海具みたいなもんか？」
source.english: “So what? We're like navigation equipment you collected for your trip home?”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「So, what are you saying? That we're all like navigational instruments scraped together here all just so you can go back home?」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロ、密航者さんの、言うことよくわからない、けど。なんかひどいことされてる気がする……」
source.english: “Kuro doesn't really understand what the stowaway's saying. But it feels like something cruel is being done…”

source.japanese: シサムとキサラは気色ばみ、クロも薄ぼんやりとしおれてみせる。泪でさえ、退屈の二文字以外を前に珍しくも憮然顔。しかし、彼女達の言葉も声も顔色も、密航者に心情伝える術となってはいなかった。
source.english: Sisam and Kisara bristled. Kuro wilted vaguely. Even Rui, rarely troubled by anything but the word boredom, looked displeased. Yet neither their words, their voices, nor their faces conveyed their feelings to the stowaway.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro doesn't really……understand what the stowaway says too well, but. Kind of feels like, Kuro is being treated really poorly……」

Shisamu's and Kisara's anger was on open display, and Kuro also appeared to be slightly crestfallen. Even Rui had an indignant look on her face, something rarely shown when not faced with the dreaded word of boredom. However, neither their words, their voices, nor their expressions managed to serve as a means to convey their feelings to the stowaway.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「でもその何がいけないの？」
source.english: “But what's wrong with that?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「But what's wrong with that?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「私は大好きだよ。愛している。あなたたちを。私の船の大事な船具として、航海道具として」
source.english: “I'm very fond of you. I love you. As precious equipment for my ship, as instruments of navigation.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「船のために欠かせない、
　他にはない部品として」
source.english:
“As indispensable,
irreplaceable parts of the ship.”

source.japanese: そして一同、はっきりとではなくうっすらと、理解したのではなくなんとなく、それが何がとは言えずも腑に落ちた。
source.english: Then, not clearly but faintly, not understanding but somehow sensing it, something settled within them. They could not say what.

source.japanese:
そう、先ほども密航者自身が明かした事、彼女はこの船が化身したものなのだ。人の姿を取り同じ言葉を話していても、仕草や表情は人の体使って見せてはいても。
　
　船であるが故に。
　
　愛するのだ。
　
　己が心臓たる蒸気機関に石炭くべ、船底破れれば慌てて塞ぐ乗り組み達が。
　
　短艇にロープ、羅針盤、大きなものも小さなものも、海往くために必要な船具、航海道具、艤装達が。
　
　すべてが彼女にとって必要なものなのだから。愛さずにはいられない。あの国へ帰るための大切なもの達。
source.english:
Yes. As the stowaway herself had just revealed, she was this ship made flesh. Though she took human form and spoke their language, though she made a human body gesture and smile—

Because she was a ship—

She loved them.

The crew who fed coal to the steam engine that was her heart, who rushed to patch her whenever her hull was breached.

The boats, the ropes, the compass; the great things and the small; every fitting and instrument of navigation she needed to voyage the sea.

All were necessary to her. How could she not love them? Her precious things, by which she would return to that country.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I really like you. I love you. All of you. As my ship's precious rigging, as her navigational instruments.」
【Stowaway】 「As those indispensable for this ship, components that can't be found anywhere else.」
And so, all concerned, though it wasn't clear, only faint, though it wasn't an understanding, somehow, without being able to put it into words, were able to understand.

Indeed, as the stowaway herself had revealed just earlier, she was an incarnation of this ship. However human a form she had taken, however similar the words they used, no matter how the mannerisms and expressions she showed were made using a human body. It was precisely by virtue of being a ship. That she loved.

Loved the crew that threw coal into the steam engine that was her beating heart, who, as soon as a hole was torn in the ship's bottom, rushed to plug her up. Loved the dinghy, the ropes, the compasses, things large and small, all the equipment, navigational instruments, and rigging necessary to sail out to sea. All of it was essential to her. And so she could not help but love them. Those all-important people, whom she needed to return home to that country.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「後は、君」
source.english: “And then, you.”

source.japanese: そして、皆を見る愛おしげな眼差しをそのまま、朔屋へ向ける。
source.english: Still with the loving gaze she had turned upon them all, she looked at Sakuya.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And then, there's you.」
And finally, still retaining the same affectionate look in her eyes she'd given everybody else, she turned to Sakuya.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「君が絡むと、事態はもう目も当てられない事になる。それは君が、世界に愛想を尽かされているから」
source.english: “Whenever you get involved, things become unbearable to watch. That's because the world has lost patience with you.”

source.japanese: そして、変わらぬ調子でひどいことを言う。
source.english: And in the very same tone, she said something dreadful.

source.japanese:
そう、そして朔屋、この男。
　全ての選択肢を駄目にする男。
　だからこそ、この航海を始められた男。
　君の事だよ、朔屋。
　この世界から、決定的に見放されている単一存在よ。
source.english:
Yes. And Sakuya, this man.

The man who ruins every choice.

The very reason this voyage could begin.

That's you, Sakuya.

You singular being, decisively abandoned by this world.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……ひでぇ」
source.english: “…That's cruel.”

source.japanese: そう一言、ぼやいてみるのがせいぜいな。
source.english: One muttered word was the best he could manage.

source.japanese: しかし、一番駄目でひどい道具が自分ではないとわかったのが幸いしたか、はたまたもうこれ以上何を言っても無駄と悟ったか、乗り組み達はおのおの溜息ついて瓦斯を抜き、むしろ精々とした表情に常の不敵を取り戻す。
source.english: Perhaps discovering that they were not the worst and most useless tool helped. Or perhaps they realized there was no point in saying anything more. The crew each sighed to let off the pressure. Looking almost relieved, they recovered their usual fearlessness.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「As soon as you get involved, things become so awful one can hardly bear to look on. And that is because this world is absolutely disgusted with you.」
And then, without changing pace, she said something terribly mean.

Yes, and then there is Sakuya, this man. The man who messes up every single choice he is given. That is exactly why he was the man to start this voyage. I speak of you, Sakuya. The sole existence that has been decisively abandoned by this world.
【Naomasa】 「……Harsh.」
Whose best showing was muttering that one word in return.

However, perhaps they felt fortunate in knowing that they themselves were not the most useless, terrible implements around, or perhaps they had realized that even should they say anything more, it would only prove to be a waste, for the members of the crew each sighed, any fuel left in the tank spent; if anything, with an unburdened countenance, they recovered their usual dauntlessness.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「言われてみりゃそうかも。朔屋って」
source.english: “Now she says it, maybe that's true. About Sakuya.”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Now that you mention it, I guess that might be true. About Sakuya, I mean.」

source.japanese:
【智正】
「まぁ、それも今さらだぁなぁ」
source.english: “Well, that's nothing new either.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……だからひでぇって」
source.english: “…I said, that's cruel.”

target.text: 【Tomosato】 「Well, little late for that revelation, if anything.」
【Naomasa】 「……Again, that's really harsh.」

source.japanese:
【宗右衛門】
「ニャアアア」
source.english: “Miaaaoow!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「何言ってるか、うっすらわかるぞ、
　こんちくしょう……」
source.english:
“I've got a vague idea what you're saying,
damn you…”

target.text: 【Souemon】 「Nyaaa.」
【Naomasa】 「I kind of get what you're telling me there, you little shit……」

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「おい、生意気な口きいてんじゃねぇぞ、
　この愚図が」
source.english:
“Hey, don't get mouthy,
you useless fool.”

target.text: 【Bosun】 「Oi, watch your damn mouth, you dunderhead.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「なるほど、君は人間の屑だったんですね」
source.english: “I see. So you're human garbage.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うぅ……」
source.english: “Uuh…”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「I see, so you were the dregs of humanity.」
【Naomasa】 「Uugh……」

source.japanese: 密航者、もう今日は何度目か、再び彼ら全員を見渡す。
source.english: For the umpteenth time that day, the stowaway surveyed them all again.

target.text: The stowaway, and just how many times had it already been today by now, looked out over all present once more.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そういう者達を、まあ長い事捜したのよ、　
そしてやっと見つけたあなた達」
source.english:
“I spent a long time looking for people like that.
And at last I found you.”

source.japanese: 長い密航の果てに、ようやく集まった、再び航海始めるためのもの達。何度見渡しても嬉しいのだろう。そして、腰の革鞄に手を添える。
source.english: At the end of her long stowing away, she had finally gathered what she needed to begin sailing again. However often she looked over them, she must have been happy. Then she rested a hand upon the leather bag at her waist.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I've been looking for people like that for a rather long time, and then, I finally found all of you.」

At the end of a long stowaway, finally had they gathered, those she needed to begin her voyage once more. No matter how many times she looked out over them, she would surely always be delighted. And then, she placed her hand on the leather bag at her waist.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「無くしていたモノも、ようやく揃ったし」
source.english: “And I've finally got everything I lost back together too.”

source.japanese:
そして、号令がかかる。
　針路は定まった。乗り組み達は揃い、船具も万端整った。もう待つべき理由は何もない。
source.english:
Then came the command.

Their course was set. The crew were assembled, the equipment ready. There was no reason to wait any longer.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And I've also finally gathered that which I had once lost.」
And then the command was given. The course was decided. The crew was assembled, and the ship's fittings were also all in good condition. There was no longer any reason to wait.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「というわけで、この畝傍───いいか、別に信天翁号でも」
source.english: “And so, this Unebi—oh, never mind. Albatross will do.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「信天翁号は、これからこの世界で最後の航海に出発するから」
source.english: “The Albatross is now setting out on her final voyage in this world.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So with that said, the Unebi ───whatever, I don't really mind calling her the Albatross.」
【Stowaway】 「The Albatross will henceforth set out on her final voyage in this world.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「各員の奮起を求む。以上」
source.english: “I expect every one of you to rise to the occasion. That is all.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I request a rousing performance from all of you. That is all.」

source.japanese: さぁ、船出だ、信天翁。
source.english: Come. Set sail, Albatross.

source.japanese:
鳴らす汽笛はないものの、代わりに頭上舞う小さな同型艦から鳴き声があがる。
　揃った乗り組み達も、気合いを乗せて、あがるはエイエイオウの鬨の声───
source.english:
There was no whistle to blow. In its place, a little sister ship wheeling overhead cried out.

The assembled crew, fired with determination, raised their rousing cheers—

target.text: Now then, set sail, Albatross.

There was no steam whistle that blew the signal, but in exchange, screeching cries rang out from the small warships of the same model soaring through the air above their heads. With great enthusiasm, the assembled crew also let out a deafening war cry: EI-EI-OH─── (TN: Ei-Ei-Oh is an ancient war cry originally used by military commanders in the Sengoku era to raise morale. In modern use, you can think of it like "let's go team" or something similar with the cadence of a "hip-hip-hooray".)

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「物が言えないとは、このことか……」
source.english: “So this is what it means to be speechless…”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「So this is what it really means to be left speechless……」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「確かに氷原にいたってやることなかったけどさぁ……どうにも解せない。けど……この船にはそういうのがお似合いか」
source.english: “Sure, we had nothing to do on the ice fields…but I can't make sense of it. Still…maybe that suits this ship.”

source.japanese:
とはいかないのが、どうしようもない阿呆鳥。
　お似合い同士が寄せ集まって、信天翁号は南へ向けて舵を切ったのだった。
source.english:
But no such triumphant cheer was forthcoming from this incorrigible fool-bird.

And so, with her well-matched lot all thrown together aboard her, the Albatross set her course south.

target.text: 【Kisara】 「There definitely was absolutely nothing to do back up on that ice field, but still……this whole thing is just so incomprehensible to me. Then again……maybe that kind of thing actually suits this ship?」

Trying to make sense of this hopeless fool of an Albatross was itself but a fool's errand. The misfit birds of a feather had now flocked together, and so the Albatross turned the rudder, heading south.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「またか……、君は……」
source.english: “Again…? You…”

source.japanese:
夜半。どうにも心落ち着かず、眠りに落ちること難しく感じていた朔屋は、上甲板へとあがり月でも星でも見て一杯との心づもりでふらりとここまで上がってきたのだが。
　月明かり照らす甲板には当直の下級水夫の姿も不思議と見えず、そこにいたのは、いや、寝そべっていたのはかの密航者だった。
source.english:
It was the middle of the night. Restless and finding sleep elusive, Sakuya had wandered up to the upper deck, intending to have a drink while looking at the moon or stars.

Strangely, no junior sailors on watch were visible on the moonlit deck. There was only—or rather, lying there was—the stowaway.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「This again……, you're……」

It was the dead of night. Unable to calm his heart, and so finding it difficult to fall asleep, Sakuya had climbed to the upper deck, heading up there with the intention of just having a drink while looking up at the moon and stars, however. Curiously, not even the deck boy on watch was anywhere to be seen on the moonlit deck, and the person there, or rather, the person lying down there, was a certain stowaway.

source.japanese: 密航者は朔屋を見つけ、寝そべった姿勢からわずかに肘立て首を回してにっこりと、手さえ振ってみせており笑いながらも口を動かしているようなのだが。
source.english: Spotting Sakuya, the stowaway raised herself a little on one elbow, turned her head and smiled. She even waved. Her mouth seemed to move as she smiled, but—

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ええぃ、いらっしゃいとでも言ったつもりか、声になっとらんわい！　そんなになるまで消耗しおってからに！」
source.english: “Bah! Did you mean to say welcome or something? You're not making a sound! You've worn yourself out that badly!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「はあぁ……」
source.english: “Haaah…”

source.japanese:
どやしつけてみたものの、続けて出たのは溜息だった。
　朔屋、密航者の側まで歩み寄り、どっかと腰を下ろす。
source.english:
He had tried scolding her, but a sigh followed.

Sakuya walked over and sat down heavily beside her.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「しかし、君なぁ。
　なんだってそんなになるまで無茶をするんだ。
　まぁ、気持ちはわからんでないんだが」
source.english:
“But honestly.
Why push yourself that far?
Well, I can understand the feeling, but…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もう少しやりようなかったのか？」
source.english: “Wasn't there a better way?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、そもそもだ。
　なんだってそんな疲れるまでして、彼女達を捜さなきゃならなかったんだ。
　よく考えりゃ、捜しに行く前、みんながそろってる時に、昼間みたいに事情ぶちまけちまえばよかったじゃぁないか」
source.english:
“No, in the first place—
Why did you have to wear yourself out looking for those women?
Now I think about it, before you went looking, when everyone was together, couldn't you just have told us what was going on, like you did today?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なのに君ときたら、ひょいひょいといらんところ、思わぬところに現れては、叩き出されていたじゃぁないか。船霊とかっていうなら、最初からもっと堂々とこの船にいればよかったじゃないか」
source.english: “Instead you kept popping up where you weren't wanted, where nobody expected you, and getting thrown out. If you're a ship's spirit, why didn't you just stay openly aboard from the start?”

source.japanese: 月夜の霊験とでも言うべきか、珍しく朔屋にしては頭の回ったことを言う。しかし、朔屋の疑念ももっともで、この船霊の少女が先ほど、皆に明かしたような正体と目的持っていたのなら、彼女の望むものはすべて揃っていたはずだ。
source.english: Perhaps it was the miraculous influence of the moonlit night: for once, Sakuya said something remarkably perceptive. And his doubts were reasonable. If this woman—the ship's spirit—possessed the identity and purpose she had just revealed to them all, everything she desired ought already to have been assembled here.

target.text: The stowaway noticed Sakuya, pushed herself slightly up from the deck, resting on her elbows, and turned her neck with a grin; she even made a show of waving her hand, attempting to say something with a smile still on her face, but.
【Naomasa】 「Grahh, maybe you're trying to bid me welcome here or something, but I can't even hear your voice! And all because you've gone and worked yourself to the bone, just look at you!」
【Naomasa】 「Haaaah……」
He tried to loudly scold her, but all that came out after it was a sigh. Sakuya walked up to the stowaway's side, then plopped down with a heavy thud.
【Naomasa】 「But still, look, you. Why are you acting so rash, to the point you end up like this? It's not like I don't get how you feel here, but still.」
【Naomasa】 「Was there really not a slightly better way to do this?」

【Naomasa】 「No, actually, to begin with. Why did you have to find those girls so desperately that you'd run yourself so ragged for it? Thinking about it, before we went looking for them, back when everybody was all gathered here, couldn't you just have blurted out everything like you did earlier at noon today?」

【Naomasa】 「And yet, every damn time with you, you'd always just casually appear somewhere both unexpected and unwanted, then get kicked out, right? If you're this Funadama or something, couldn't you just have been more open about being on this ship right from the start?」

Perhaps it should be considered a manifestation of the miraculous powers of a moonlit night, for Sakuya was saying some unusually clever things. However, Sakuya's doubts were only reasonable, for if this Funadama girl had both the true identity and objective she had divulged before the others a short while ago, then she should have already had everything she wanted.

source.japanese: 朔屋の問いに、密航者は細い声で答える。
source.english: The stowaway answered Sakuya's questions in a faint voice.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あれは、彼女達の航海だったから。
　そして、私は密航者だから」
source.english:
“Because those were their voyages.
And because I'm a stowaway.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「密航者が密航するのは、当然のことでしょう？
　……まあ、その理屈で今は納得しなさいね」
source.english:
“Stowaways stow away. Naturally.
…Well, accept that reasoning for now.”

source.japanese: 当然、それは納得のいく答えではなかったのだが、もとより朔屋、くるくる回って他人の言に自分の重ねて打ち負かすような上等なおつむは持ち合わせていない。なにより、言論などに興じる質でもないのだ。
source.english: Naturally, it was no satisfactory answer. But Sakuya's mind had never been nimble enough to answer every argument with one of his own and win. Above all, he was not the sort to enjoy a debate.

source.japanese: しかし、この時はもう少し、朔屋の頭の中で自分の疑念と密航者の言葉が渦を巻く。信天翁号に連れ去られてからの航海の記憶。その途中途中でこの少女は現れた。あの時も、あの時も。クロとあの薄気味悪い島に上がった時、キサラと共にシサムを追おうとした時、泪と一緒に潜水艦に乗った時もだ。
source.english: Yet this time his doubts and the stowaway's words swirled a little longer in his head. Memories of his voyages since the Albatross carried him away. At point after point along the way, this woman had appeared. That time. That time too. When he landed with Kuro on that eerie island. When he tried to follow Sisam with Kisara. When he boarded the submarine with Rui.

target.text: The stowaway answered Sakuya's question in a thin voice.
【Stowaway】 「That was because those were their voyages. And because I am the stowaway.」
【Stowaway】 「A stowaway stowing away is only natural, right? ……Well, just be satisfied with that logic for now, okay?」

Of course, that was not at all a satisfactory answer, but Sakuya had never been possessed of the sort of fancy intellect that would let him participate in the mental gymnastics of word games to crush others verbally. Most of all, it wasn't in his nature to find discussion itself amusing.

However, in this moment, within Sakuya's head, his own doubts and the stowaway's words swirled around a little longer than usual. His memories of the voyage he had undertaken ever since being shanghaied onto the Albatross. This girl had appeared along the way, here and there. Back then, and back then too. When he had gone ashore on that eerie island with Kuro, when he had been pursuing Shisamu together with Kisara, and when he had boarded that submarine together with Rui as well.

source.english: —No.

source.japanese: 待て、それはいつだ？
source.english: Wait. When was that?

source.japanese: 朔屋の記憶たぐる小船が、その頭の渦の中で、見えぬ岩礁にぶち当たる。朔屋、そこでピタリと思考を止める。止めようとしたのだが。
source.english: The little boat nosing back through Sakuya’s memories struck an unseen reef in the whirlpool of his mind. There his thoughts stopped dead. Or tried to.

source.japanese: 朔屋の顔見つめる密航者の言葉はそれを許さなかった。
source.english: The stowaway's words, as she watched his face, would not let him.

target.text: Hold on, just when had that been?
Within that swirl in his head, the small boat retracing Sakuya's memories crashed against a hidden reef. Sakuya completely stopped thinking at that point. He tried to stop thinking, but.
Staring intently into Sakuya's face, the stowaway's words did not permit that.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「君は、今、余り深く考えないようにしている。
　どうして自分が、あの女性達の想い出を、全部保っているのか」
source.english:
“Right now, you're trying not to think too deeply.
About why you still have all your memories of those women.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「航海の双子との想い出。船長クロとの想い出。女客泪との想い出。それぞれはそれぞれの想い出の筈。共有することは、できない」
source.english: “Memories of the twin navigators. Memories of Captain Kuro. Memories of Rui, the lady passenger. Each ought to be separate. They can't be shared.”

source.japanese:
そうだった。
　止まない嵐の中心にあるあの島にクロを閉じこめてきたのなら。
　極北の表現でシサムキサラに殴られ突き放されていたのなら。
　海底洞窟の奥で為すすべなく逃げ出してそのまま泪に去られてしまっていたのなら。
　それらはいつ、起きたのだ？　朔屋の航海のどこに置くことができるのだ、それぞれは。
source.english:
That was true.

If he had left Kuro imprisoned on the island at the heart of the ceaseless storm—

If Sisam and Kisara had beaten him and cast him off on the ice fields of the far north—

If he had fled helplessly from the depths of the underwater cave, and Rui had then left him—

When had all those things happened? Where could he place each one within his voyages?

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「普通ならね、そうの筈」
source.english: “Normally, that would be how it worked.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「でも直正は違う。ここに君がいるというのは、現状、取り得る限りの結末を見たから」
source.english: “But you're different, Naomasa. You're here because you've seen every ending available under the circumstances.”

source.japanese: そんな結末を見てきたのか、朔屋よ。どうやって、いやもうすでにそれを論じる段ではない。いや増す不安が朔屋の背を汗となって伝う。
source.english: Had you seen such endings, Sakuya? How? No, that was no longer the question. His growing unease ran down his back as sweat.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「その結果、なにが起こったかっていうと。
　比喩的表現を使うわね」
source.english:
“And as a result, what happened was—
I'll use a metaphor.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「君は、辿りうる先々の世界から、弾き出されたのです」
source.english: “You were cast out of every world you could reach.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「世界が、君の存在を拒否した、そういうこと」
source.english: “The world rejected your existence. That's what it means.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Right now, you're trying not to think too hard about it. Just why it is that you retain all of the memories of those girls.」
【Stowaway】 「Memories of the seafaring twins. Memories of Captain Kuro. Memories of Rui, the female passenger. Each should have their respective memories. They couldn't possibly be shared.」
【Naomasa】 「───!」

That was right. If Kuro had been imprisoned on that island in the eye of the ceaseless storm, then. If he had been punched and pushed away by Shisamu and Kisara in that ice field on the North Pole, then. If he had escaped from the depths of that cave at the bottom of the sea without being able to devise a means himself, with Rui leaving him just like that, then. Just when had all those things happened? Just where could each of those events be placed in the timeline of Sakuya's voyage?
【Stowaway】 「It shouldn't be possible, under normal circumstances.」
【Stowaway】 「But you're different, Naomasa. That you're here means that, at present, you've seen every conclusion possible to attain.」
【Naomasa】 「………………」
Have you seen such outcomes, O Sakuya. But how, no, it was long past the need to dispute that. The ever-intensifying unease took shape as a bead of cold sweat rolling down Sakuya's back.
【Stowaway】 「So then, what happened as a result? I'll use a figurative expression here, alright?」
【Stowaway】 「You have been cast out from every future world you could possibly have arrived at.」
【Stowaway】 「The world rejected your very existence, that sort of thing.」

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うわあああああ、まただぁ！」
source.english: “Aaaaah! Again!”

source.japanese: あっさりきっぱり言い切られ、朔屋頭を掻き毟[むし]る。密航者の宣告、その表情声音に重み暗さはないけれど、ここまで付き合ってきた朔屋にとってはそれこそが真実実感を伝える術になる。
source.english: She said it plainly, decisively. Sakuya clawed at his head. Neither the stowaway's face nor her voice gave her verdict any gravity or gloom. Yet after accompanying her this far, Sakuya found that very absence made it feel real and true.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「またひどいこと言ったよ、君はッ！
　ああそうだ、俺は駄目な存在なんだそうなんだ。
　ああもういっそ、誰か俺をひと───」
source.english:
“You've said something cruel again!
Yes, that's right. I'm a useless being. That's right.
Ah, someone should just finish—”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「何故一思いに殺すなりしない？　それは浅はかな、素人の、考えなしの、まるで直正、君のように愚かでろくでもない馬鹿まるだし」
source.english: “Why not simply kill you? That's shallow, amateurish, thoughtless—just like you, Naomasa. Foolish, worthless, sheer idiocy.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あああああああああ。
　そうさ、そうさ、俺は浅はかで素人で考えなしで他なんだ？
　世界中から嫌われてるんだあああ」
source.english:
“Aaaaaaah!
Yes, yes, I'm shallow and amateurish and thoughtless—what else?
The whole world hates me!”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「……嫌いなはずないじゃない。大好きよ。むしろ自分のものだって言い張るわ。ある意味でその通りなんだけど」
source.english: “…Of course I don't hate you. I'm very fond of you. I'd even insist you're mine. In a sense, you are.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ふぇ？」
source.english: “Huh?”

source.japanese: 頭掻き毟[むし]り泣き言垂れるのに注力していて、朔屋、何か言葉を聞き逃す。うっかり右から左に耳を通って抜け出てしまってはいけないような言葉を。ふと、手と声止めてみたものの、密航者の言葉はすでに次の話に移っていた。
source.english: Concentrating on clawing his head and whining, Sakuya missed something she said. Something that ought not to have slipped in one ear and out the other. He suddenly stopped his hands and his voice, but the stowaway had already moved on.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「とにかく───人一人を殺すって言うのは、沢山沢山影響がある事だから」
source.english: “Anyway—killing a single person has a great many consequences.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そして今度は仮定法。世界、というのを、ある遊園地のオーナーと考えてみて。そして、朔屋少年はこのオーナーから嫌われている」
source.english: “Now let's use a hypothetical. Think of ‘the world’ as the owner of an amusement park. And the owner dislikes young Sakuya.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「とにかく嫌われていて、その遊園地の中でやることなすこと許されていない。だから追い出されてしまう。どんな乗り物に乗ろうとしても」
source.english: “Dislikes him so much that nothing he does in the park is allowed. So he gets thrown out. Whatever ride he tries to go on.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「うう、わかるぞ、
　そのたとえ話の結末が……」
source.english:
“Uuh, I know
how that story ends…”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「直正、君はそういう人。すごい！　そういう人ってなかなかいない。というか、造るのがとてもとても大変だった」
source.english: “Naomasa, that's the kind of person you are. Amazing! There aren't many people like that. Or rather, making one was very, very difficult.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「やあっぱりぃ……！
　……いや、今なんと？
　なんだって？　大変？　造るの、が……？」
source.english:
“I knew it…!
…No, what did you say?
What? Difficult? To make…?”

source.japanese:
しかし、今度は見事受け止めた。受け止めてみたものの、言葉の意味量りかねて、朔屋は鸚鵡の様に問い返す。
　言葉はそのまま返ってきた。一度の疑念は、二度目の肯定で返されたのだ。
source.english:
This time, though, he caught it perfectly. Caught it, but could not gauge what the words meant. Sakuya repeated the question like a parrot.

The same words came back. His first doubt was answered by a second affirmation.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そう。君は、私が造った。だから私のものと言ったのは、そういうこと」
source.english: “Yes. I made you. That's what I meant by calling you mine.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「なんだって……？」
source.english: “What…?”

source.japanese:
いい加減、何を聞いても驚かないと思っていた。
　しかし、朔屋は混乱した。誰が自分を造ったと？
　朔屋、必死に記憶をたぐる。もう家を出てからどれほど経ったか定かではなくとも、まだ父と母の顔くらいは思い出せる。今は当時より年も重ねて皺も増えたかも知れぬ、髪にも白い筋が通っているかも知れぬ。しかし、ここにいる朔屋を有り体な言い方で製造した両親は、少なくとも母は、今目の前にいるような美しいと言ってよい少女ではなかったはずだ。ああ、母の若い頃は知らないが想像して見るも顔立ちの異なりもあって繋がらぬ。
source.english:
He had thought by now that nothing he heard could surprise him.

But Sakuya was bewildered. Who, she said, had made him?

Desperately he reeled in his memories. He no longer knew how much time had passed since he left home, but he could still remember his parents' faces. They might have aged since then, gathered wrinkles, acquired white strands in their hair. Yet the parents who had—to put it plainly—manufactured the Sakuya standing here, his mother at least, could surely not have been the beautiful woman before him. True, he had never seen his mother in her younger days; but however he tried to imagine her, the features would not connect.

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「AaaaAAARGH, THIS AGAIN!」

Easily and resolutely declared to his face, Sakuya tore at his head. As the stowaway delivered her verdict, there was no gravitas or darkness to be found in her expression or tone of voice, but to Sakuya, after having known her for this long, that in particular made it even better at conveying a sense of reality and truth.
【Naomasa】 「You're saying some really awful things again here! Yeah, of course, I'm a worthless existence, that's all I am. Aah, someone might as well just end me alre───」

【Stowaway】 「Why wouldn't it just kill you in an instant and get it over with? Because that would be shallow, amateurish, thoughtless, the act of some stupid, worthless idiot, someone just like you, Naomasa.」
【Naomasa】 「Aaaaaaaaaaaaaah. That's right, you're right, I'm shallow, amateurish, thoughtless, and what more? I'm hated by the entire woooorld!」
【Stowaway】 「……I certainly don't hate you. I love you. If anything, I'll claim you as mine. Well, in a certain sense, you literally are, but still.」
【Naomasa】 「Bwuh?」

Too concentrated on clutching at his head and whining, Sakuya failed to hear something. Words that he should not by any means have allowed to go in his right ear only to carelessly let pass through his left. Suddenly, both his hands and mouth came to a stop, but the stowaway had already moved on to the next topic.
【Stowaway】 「In any case───the act of killing one man comes with a whole lot of repercussions.」

【Stowaway】 「And now I'll speak in the subjunctive mood. I want you to think of the world as if it were, say, the owner of a certain amusement park. And then, the young boy Sakuya is despised by this owner.」
【Stowaway】 「He is thoroughly loathed, to the point that nothing he does within that amusement park is tolerated. And so he ends up being driven out. No matter the attraction he tries to ride.」
【Naomasa】 「Uuugh, I get it, I know how your simile ends……」
【Stowaway】 「Naomasa, that's the kind of man you are. Amazing! People like you are a rare breed. Or rather, it was actually really hard work to create someone like that.」
【Naomasa】 「I knew iiit……! ……No, wait, what was that? What did you just say? Hard work? To create……?」

However, this time, he caught the whole thing. He caught the whole thing, but struggling to conjecture the meaning of the words, Sakuya just asked in return like a parrot. Those words came back his way without change. The first doubt was answered with the second affirmation.
【Stowaway】 「That's right. I created you. So when I say you're mine, that's what I mean.」
【Naomasa】 「What are you saying……?」

He was certain that, by now, no matter what he heard, it wouldn't surprise him anymore. However, Sakuya was confused. Who did she say had created him? Sakuya desperately trawled through his memories. By now, it was no longer entirely clear to him just how long it had been since he'd left home, but he could still remember the faces of his mother and father, at least. Perhaps they would look older now and have more wrinkles than back then, and maybe there would even be streaks of white running through their hair.

However, when it came to his parents, who, when phrased bluntly, had produced the Sakuya right here, his mother, at least, could certainly not be the sort of young girl one could well call beautiful lying right before his eyes. Well, he didn't know what his mother had looked like in her youth, but even when he tried to imagine it, their facial features were so patently different that he could find no relation.

source.japanese: 必死に郷里におる両親の顔試行錯誤する朔屋に、密航者はなおも言葉を続ける。
source.english: As Sakuya desperately tried to reconstruct his parents' faces back home, the stowaway continued.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「始まりは、とある一族の選定からだった。神隠しに合いやすい人達だったっけ。当然、世界に嫌われやすい要素を持った人達で」
source.english: “It began with choosing a certain family. They were prone to being spirited away. Naturally, they had traits that made the world likely to dislike them.”

source.japanese: 混乱しつつも朔屋、彼女の言葉に疑念は浮かぶ。選定、要素、確かにそれは、子を為す連れ合い見つけるのに必要なことかも知れぬ。しかし、世界に嫌われやすいとは。そんなもの───
source.english: Confused though he was, her words raised doubts in Sakuya. Selection, traits—yes, those might be necessary in finding a partner with whom to have children. But likely to be disliked by the world? Such a thing—

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「なんでわかるかっていうのは、私もほら、この世界でははみ出しものだから、そういうのを見分けられるの」
source.english: “How can I tell? Well, I'm an outsider in this world too. I can recognize that sort of thing.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「とにかく、その一族にいろんな血を取り入れて、いろんな事をやらせて、いろんな習慣、気性、家風、その他諸々一切合切。そうして産まれて最高に『世界からの嫌われ者』が君」
