source.english: “Anyway, I brought all kinds of blood into that family, made them do all kinds of things. Habits, temperaments, family traditions, everything under the sun. And born from all that, the ultimate ‘person hated by the world’—was you.”

source.japanese: 密航者は朔屋に人差し指向ける。そう、密航者が語るのは朔屋の話だった。
source.english: The stowaway pointed her forefinger at Sakuya. Yes, it was his story she was telling.

source.japanese: 造られた？
source.english: Made?

target.text: While Sakuya underwent the desperate process of trial and error that was imagining the faces of his parents back in his hometown, the stowaway continued to speak to him.

【Stowaway】 「It all began with the selection of a particular clan. They were people who were easy to spirit away, if I recall. Of course, they were also people who carried a component that made them easily despised by the world.」

Even while in the throes of his confusion, Sakuya still felt doubt surface as he heard her words. Selection, component, that could be important for finding a companion in life to rear children with for all he knew. However, when it came to being easily despised by the world. Just what could that possibly───
【Stowaway】 「And if you're wondering how I could tell, look, I'm also an outcast who sticks out from this world, so I can recognize those kinds of things.」

【Stowaway】 「Anyway, I introduced all kinds of blood to that clan, made them do all kinds of things, various customs, temperaments, family traditions, all the rest, any and every thing. And the『Anathema to the World』 born thus, that's you.」
The stowaway pointed her index finger at Sakuya. Indeed, it was Sakuya whom the stowaway had spoken of.
【Naomasa】 「Me……?」
Created?

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「もう名前とか、顔とか、その行動とか、言動とか、考え方とか、君のありとあらゆるものがこの世界の神経を逆撫でしちゃう。それはもう、造った私でも気が引けちゃうくらいに」
source.english: “Your name, your face, your behavior, what you say, how you think—everything about you rubs this world the wrong way. So much that even I, who made you, feel a little bad about it.”

source.japanese: そう造った？
source.english: Made that way?

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Your name, your face, your conduct, your words and deeds, the way you think, every conceivable part of you really ends up grating on this world's nerves. It's so bad, even I, your creator, can't help feeling ashamed of you.」
【Naomasa】 「I……?」
Was created like that?

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「我ながらやり過ぎたかも。だからね、直正、数百年も待ち続けた君を、私が必要とするのは当然でしょうが」
source.english: “I may have overdone it. So, Naomasa, after waiting hundreds of years for you, isn't it obvious that I need you?”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「───なんで？　なんで、俺を？」
source.english: “—Why? Why me?”

source.japanese:
そんな風に造った？
　数えきれぬ失敗を繰り返さなければならぬほど。
　行き着く先々で必ず最後は爪弾きされねばならぬほど。
　どれほどの善意も好意も機会もすべて無駄にしてしまう人間に。
　あらゆる期待に裏切られ望まぬ結果だけを掴んでしまう人間に。
source.english:
Made him that way?

So that he had to fail over and over, too many times to count.

So that wherever he arrived, he had to be cast out in the end.

A person who wasted every kindness, every affection, every opportunity.

A person whose every expectation was betrayed, who got only the outcomes he did not want.

source.japanese: ───世界から拒否される存在に。
source.english: —An existence rejected by the world.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「なんでもなにも。この船に必要だったから。最後の一つのパーツとして。それ以外の何者でもないに決まってるじゃない」
source.english: “What do you mean, why? Because this ship needed you. As its final part. What else could it possibly have been?”

source.japanese:
何故、造った。
　そんな、道具として。
source.english:
Why make him?

As a tool like that.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I might have gone too far in a few places, if I may say so myself. So, you know, Naomasa, I guess it would only be natural that I need you, someone I've waited hundreds of years to finally meet.」
【Naomasa】 「───Why? Why me, why would you?」

Create me like that? So he would have to repeat countless failures, again and again. So he would inevitably be cast out from any future he reached. As a man who would bring any good will, kindness, and opportunity to naught, no matter how great. As a man who would betray every expectation laid upon him, clutching nothing but outcomes desired by none.
───As an existence rejected by the world.
【Stowaway】 「What do you mean "why"? Because it was essential for this ship. As her final component. It's nothing more than that, isn't that obvious?」
Why was he created. As a tool like that.

source.japanese:
朔屋の視界の中で───
　彼の腕は伸び、その手は目の前の女の白く細い首へと向かっていった。
　自分がその時、何を言ったか朔屋は知らぬ。
　しかし、指は密航者の首に回り、そのままくっと掴んでいた。
source.english:
Within Sakuya’s field of vision—
his arm reached out, his hand advancing toward the white, slender throat of the woman before him.
Sakuya did not know what he said then.
But his fingers closed around the stowaway’s neck and gripped it hard.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ええー……そんなに私の事が憎い？
　私はこんなにこんなに君が大切なのに。
　じゃあね、こうしよう」
source.english:
“Really…? Do you hate me that much?
I care about you so, so much.
Well then, let’s do this.”

source.japanese: その指にどれほどの力が込められているのか、朔屋は自覚できなかった。ただ、自分の手は密航者の首に回されている。しかし、彼女の口から出る言葉は、先ほどまでと変わらない。
source.english: He had no idea how much force he was putting into those fingers. All he knew was that his hand was around the stowaway’s neck. Yet the words coming out of her mouth were no different from before.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「もう、君だから許しちゃおう───
　一回。一回だけ君の好きなようにするといい」
source.english:
“Fine, since it’s you, I’ll let it slide—just this once.
Just this once, you can do as you please.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「その一回で私をどうしようとも、それは君の自由だ」
source.english: “Whatever you do to me that one time, it’s entirely up to you.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「私をボロボロにしようとどうしようとも」
source.english: “Do what you like, rip me to shreds—”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「まあ、船の方は、もう先にボロボロになっているけどさ」
source.english: “The ship’s already falling apart, though.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「でもこっちの世界に壊されるんじゃなく。
　こっちの世界で、私が造りあげた君に殺されるのなら。ま、いっかー」
source.english:
“But if, instead of being torn apart by this world,
I’m gonna get killed by the you I made here… Well, whatever.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「さあどうしてくれるのかしら。
　やだ、そんなに焦らさないで」
source.english:
“Well, what are you going to do to me?
Oh, come on, don’t keep me in suspense like that.”

target.text: In Sakuya's field of vision─── His arms stretched forwards, the hands reaching for the pale, slender neck of the girl right in front of him. Sakuya didn't know what it was that he himself said in that moment. However, his fingers curled around the stowaway's neck, seizing it tightly without pause.
【Stowaway】 「Aawww……do you really hate me that much? Even though you're so, so dear to me? Alright then, let's do it like this.」

Just how much force must have been put into those fingers, Sakuya himself had no idea. His own hands were wrapped around the stowaway's neck. However, the words coming from her lips were no different from just before.
【Stowaway】 「Guess I'll let it slide, since it's you and all─── Once. Just once, you can do whatever you please.」
【Stowaway】 「This one time, whatever you want to do to me, that is entirely up to you.」
【Stowaway】 「Whatever kind of miserable mess you try to leave me in, whatever you do.」
【Stowaway】 「Well, the ship's already battered and falling to pieces, but, you know.」
【Stowaway】 「Still, I won't be destroyed by this world. I'll be killed by you, the man I created in this world, and if that's the case? Eh, whatever.」
【Stowaway】 「Now then, whatever shall be done to me. Come on, don't keep me hanging like this.」

source.japanese: そう言葉かけ続ける密航者の姿を、朔屋その目を通しているものの、まるで朔屋自身が頭の中の奥深くに引っ込んで、眼というスクリーン通して眺めているかのよう。
source.english: Sakuya watched the stowaway keep talking with his own eyes, yet it felt as if he had retreated deep inside his head and was observing the scene through his eyes as though they were a screen.

source.japanese: その光景の中で、朔屋の手は、密航者の首から離れてしまった。離れてなお、戸惑ってその手の向ける先探すよう。密航者、ついと視線をわずかに逸らし、なお言葉を続ける。どこまでも、朔屋のことをわかっているのかいないのか。朔屋も己と目の前の女がわかっているのかいないのか。
source.english: In that vision, Sakuya's hand slipped from her neck. Even after letting go, it hovered in bewilderment, as though searching for somewhere to be. The stowaway glanced aside, then continued. How much did she understand of Sakuya, and how much did she not? How much did Sakuya understand of himself—or of the woman before him?

target.text: Although Sakuya's eyes roved over the stowaway's form as she spoke those words to him, it was like Sakuya himself had retreated deep inside his own head, observing through the screen that was his eyes.

Within that scene, Sakuya's hands withdrew from the stowaway's neck. Even after pulling them away, he seemed bewildered, as if searching for where to put his hands. The stowaway, quickly averting her gaze ever so slightly, continued to speak. Just how thoroughly did she understand Sakuya? And how well did Sakuya understand both himself and the girl before him?

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あ、なんだか今さらになって───」
source.english: “Ah, somehow, only now, after all this time—”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「恥ずかしくなってきちゃった、みたい。
　だっていま私、とても磨り減ってるから」
source.english:
“I guess I’m starting to feel a little embarrassed.
After all, I’m really worn down right now.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「君の気持ちを煽り立てるようなポーズとか、取れない。こうやってだらしなく伸びてるくらいしか。お化粧とかも、しておけばよかったな」
source.english: “I can’t strike a pose that would stir up your emotions. All I can do is lie here slumped like this. I wish I’d put on some makeup.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「女の子のこと、色々と覚えてみたのよ。
　君ができてくるのを、待つ間にさ」
source.english:
“I tried to learn all sorts of things about girls.
While I was waiting for you to come into being.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「待つ時間は長くて、長くて、でも君を待つようになってからは、嬉しくて、楽しみで」
source.english: “The wait was long, so very long, but ever since I started waiting for you, I’ve been happy and full of anticipation.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Ah, it does kind of feel a little late for this───」
【Stowaway】 「Seems like I've ended up getting a little embarrassed here. I mean, I'm just really worn down right now, that's all.」
【Stowaway】 「I can't strike any poses that would stir up your emotions. All I can do is lay here like this, all slack and feeble. Really should have found the time to put on some makeup or something.」
【Stowaway】 「I tried learning a lot of stuff about girls. You know, while I was waiting until I could do it with you.」
【Stowaway】 「The wait was long, so very long, but once I started waiting for you, I was happy, excited for it.」

source.japanese: その言葉は、深く情を交わした女が愛しい男に、胸ときめかせてのねだり言。肌重ね合わせた事のあるこの二人なら、こんな言葉も交わされて不思議はないはずなのに、なぜ先ほどまで、男は相手の首に手をかけ、女はそれを怖れもせずに受け入れたのだろうか。
source.english: Those words were the pleading of a woman who had shared a deep affection with the man she adored, her heart fluttering as she spoke to him. For these two, who had lain together, it wouldn’t be strange at all for such words to be exchanged—so why, just moments ago, did the man place his hand around her neck, and why did she accept it without a hint of fear?

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「君にはこの気持ち、わからないだろうな。
　そうよ。これだけは、たとえ君にもあげられない。私の他のなにをあげたっていいけど、この気持ちだけはね、抱いたままで、壊される」
source.english:
“You probably don’t understand this feeling, do you?
That’s right. This is the one thing I can’t give you—not even you. You can have anything else about me, but this feeling—I’ll still be holding onto it when I’m destroyed.”

source.japanese:
この女は今、何を望んでいるのだろう。何かをしかと抱いているのは朔屋にも理解できた、言葉聞いてもそれが何かとわからぬまま。そして、この女は今、何を朔屋に望んでいるのだろう。自分は何を望まれているのだろう。自分を造ったと言ったこの女は、今、朔屋がどうするように造ったのだろう。自分は、どうするように造られたのだろう。
　朔屋の手は逡巡する。逡巡する朔屋とその手を見つめ、女は言った。
source.english:
What is she hoping for right now? He could tell she was clinging to something, but even after hearing her words, he still didn’t know what. And what does she want from him right now? What is she expecting? This woman who said she made him—what did she make him to do now? What was he made to do?
Sakuya’s hand hesitated. Watching Sakuya and his hesitant hand, the woman said,

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「さあ、ひと思いに？　じわじわと？」
source.english: “So, all at once? Or slowly, bit by bit?”

source.japanese: その言葉と同時に、朔屋の目には、先ほどまで自分の掌が、指が、女の肌にわずかに穿[うが]った痕に映った。それは白い肌に条なした、その薄皮の下で血通う管が潰されてできた───
source.english: At that instant he saw, etched into her white skin, the faint traces his palm and fingers had left behind—streaks where the blood vessels just under the surface had been crushed—

target.text: Those were the words of a woman who had exchanged profound passions, pleading words that would set the heart of her darling man aflutter. Since these two had already shared in physical intimacy, there should be nothing strange about such words being shared between them, but why, then, had the man had his hands wrapped around her neck until just now, and why had the woman accepted it without a trace of fear?

【Stowaway】 「I suppose you could not understand these feelings. That's right. These alone I will not give to any other, even to you. I will give anything else, but these feelings alone, I will carry with me as I am destroyed.」

Just what could it be that this woman desired right now? Sakuya could tell that she was holding onto something with an iron grip, but even as he heard her words, he still remained none the wiser as to what it was. And then, just what could it be this woman desired of Sakuya? What was it Sakuya himself desired? This woman, the one who claimed to have created him, just what had she created Sakuya to do right now? Just what had he himself been created to do? Sakuya's hands hesitated. Staring at those hesitating hands of his, the woman said thus:
【Stowaway】 「Now then, will it be instant? Or slow and steady?」

At the same time as those words hit him, the faint traces of the mark on the woman's skin that his own fists, his own fingers had left as they dug into her skin just earlier reflected in Sakuya's eyes. It formed a streak against her white skin, the blood vessels beneath the thin skin crushed───

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ああ絞殺……一番憎しみの籠もる殺し方」
source.english: “Ah, strangulation… the killing method that holds the most hatred.”

source.japanese: 今度こそ、女の声はかすれる。
source.english: This time, the woman’s voice really did grow hoarse.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Aah, strangulation……the method of killing most laden with hatred of them all.」
This time, her voice grew hoarse.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「自分……のっ、指……で、息の根……とめる」
source.english: “You’ll… use your… fingers… to… take my life.”

source.japanese: かすれた声漏らしながらも、女はそっと朔屋の腕に手を添える。もっと、もっと力を込めろと促すように。
source.english: Even as she spoke in a hoarse voice, the woman gently placed her hand on his arm—as if urging him to put more, more strength into it.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Snuffing out……the breath of life with……your……own……fingers.」
While letting her hoarse voice spill from between her lips, the woman gently placed her hands on Sakuya's arms. As though urging him to squeeze harder, to put more strength into it.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「げ……ぅ……っ」
source.english: “Guh… uhh…”

source.japanese: そして、女の喘ぐように口を開き、しかしそこから漏れるのは潰されつつある気管から吹き出た音無くした、ただの息。
source.english: Then she opened her mouth as if gasping, but all that came out was soundless breath—just breath—pushing through her windpipe as it was being crushed.
“Ku… kyu…”

source.japanese: さぁ、朔屋よ。
source.english: Now then, Sakuya.

source.japanese: お前は何を望んだのだ。
source.english: What did you want?

source.japanese: この女の最後に零れるかすれた息か。まだなお、お前を見つめる瞳が、眼球ごと裏返り光を無くす瞬間か。鬱と凝った血が貯まり肌赤黒く変色し、最後は舌さえ伸ばして涎垂れ流すその様か。さぁ、あと少し、望むがいい。あとわずか、その手に力込めれば───
source.english: Is it the ragged breath that slips out of her at the very end? The instant her eyes—still on you—roll back and go dark? The way her skin turns reddish-black as the blood pools underneath, till she sticks out her tongue and drools? Come on, just a little longer—wish for it. If you put just a little more strength in that hand—

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Gehh……uh……」
And then, she opened her mouth as if struggling to breathe, but what escaped her throat was just the air being squeezed out of her trachea as it was crushed, just soundless breath.
【Stowaway】 「Khh…………kyuh……」
Now, O Sakuya.
What did you desire?

Was it the final, guttural breath wrenched from this woman's throat? Or did you want still more, desiring the moment those eyeballs fixed upon you rolled up in their sockets and lost their light? Was it how her stagnant and congealed blood would accumulate, causing the skin to discolour into dark, reddish-black hues, even her tongue ultimately hanging out her mouth, a river of drool discharged from her lips? Come now, just a little more, whatever your heart's desire. If you were to put just the slightest bit more strength into those hands───

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「かはっ……」
source.english: “Gah…”

source.japanese: 絶息する寸前だった密航者の口から肺に貯まっていたかつての吸気が、不意に解放された気管を駆け抜け爆ぜた。
source.english: From the mouth of the stowaway, who had been an instant from suffocation, the breath trapped in her lungs suddenly tore through her released throat and burst free.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「けはっ、かはっ、かはっっ」
source.english: “Keh, ka, ka!”

source.japanese: 二度三度とえずいて、密航者は喉押し広げ、途絶えさせられていた呼吸を再開する。
source.english: After retching twice or three times, the stowaway opened her throat wide and resumed the breath that had been cut off.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ひぅぅー……、ひぅー……」
source.english: “Hiiuuu… hiiuuu…”

source.japanese: そう、朔屋は手を離したのだ。最後の最後の瞬間に。そして今は、離した手を宙に浮かせ、ぐじぐじと涙を流していた。
source.english: Yes, Sakuya had let go. At the very, very last moment. And now, with his released hand hanging in midair, he was weeping uncontrollably.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あれ、まだ私は、この身この身体には息が通っているよ？」
source.english: “Hey, I’m still breathing in this body, right?”

source.japanese:
ぜいぜいと荒い息を混ぜながら、密航者は己の状態を声に出して確認する。
　そして、苦しい呼吸を押して笑い放つ。朔屋をまだ幾分、霞んだ目で見つめながら。
source.english:
Gasping between words, the stowaway confirmed her own condition aloud.

Then, forcing the laughter through her labored breath, she laughed out loud—still watching Sakuya through eyes not quite clear.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ぷ。はは。あははは。そう。結局君にはそれは出来ないんだ」
source.english: “Pfft. Haha. Ahahaha. Yeah. In the end, you just can’t do it.”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ……」
source.english: “Ah…”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「女一人絞め殺す事も」
source.english: “Even strangling a woman to death…”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そう、だ……。
　そうだよ……！
　できなかったよ！　できねぇよ！
　でも、でもさぁ！　君がそういうふうに俺を造ったんだろうが……っ！」
source.english:
“That’s right…
That’s exactly it…!

source.english: The place lay on the ship’s lowest deck, in the great common room allotted to the lower-ranking sailors—in other words, their nest; though put it like that and one was liable to picture the junior sailors forever swarming busily in and out, food over here, drink over there, mushrooms cultivated here, eggs laid there, the hatchlings spending their first two weeks in this corner and the next three in that one, until, behold, a fully-fledged sailor!—a picture so alarmingly specific it ceased to be any sort of joke.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「……あれ？　なんだってあんた達がこんなとこに巣ぅ作ってんだ？」
source.english: “…Huh? Why have you lot made a nest down here?”

source.japanese:
だから巣と例えるのはやめよ、朔屋。さておき。
　その大部屋の一画に、集まり寄り添い、服下着干したり広げたりしているのは、顔立ちだけはこの部屋の住人どもとまるで変わらぬ酒場女達だった。
source.english:
That's why you must stop calling it a nest, Sakuya. Anyway.

Gathered close together in one part of the room, hanging up or spreading out clothes and underwear, were the barmaids. In face alone, they were indistinguishable from the room's residents.

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Kyaah, he found us!」
The moment he happened to set foot in that place, Sakuya was met with shrill, cheerful voices.

It was the lowest deck of the ship, the large room that had been assigned to the deck boys, their nest so to speak, and following that simile, this would be where the deck boys would constantly come and go in a big bustle, this is where they would eat, this is where they would drink, here they grew mushrooms, and last but not least, here they would lay their eggs, and after incubation, they would be placed here, another two weeks later over there, and in three weeks over yonder, and there they'd hatch into fully-fledged sailors; in fact, it almost didn't feel like a joke at all, and he couldn't help but imagine the whole process in concrete detail.
【Naomasa】 「……Huh? Why are you girls building a nest in a place like this?」

Naomasa, please, would you stop likening this to a nest already? But I digress. Gathering in one particular area of that large room, huddling close together and spreading their clothes and underwear out to dry, were the bar girls whose faces alone were practically identical to those of the residents of this room.

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「実は私たちも、こっそり乗船していたのでしたぁ！」
source.english: “Actually, we've secretly come aboard too!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いやこっそりって……結構な数がまぎれこんでんじゃんかよう……」
source.english: “Secretly…? There's quite a crowd of you in here…”

source.japanese:
ざっとその数、数えてみれば、今すぐにでも店を開くに不足はないほど。
　同じ顔を並べて、次から次へと朔屋に向かって述べ立てるのは、些か筋の通らぬ乗船理由。
source.english:
A quick count showed enough of them to open a bar at once.

Lining up their identical faces, they offered Sakuya, one after another, reasons for boarding that made rather little sense.

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Truth is, we also sneakily slipped aboard the ship!」
【Naomasa】 「I don't know about sneakily…… there's quite a lot of you girls who have slipped in here……」

When he tried to eyeball the number, he'd have enough girls on hand to open a shop right here and now. All wearing the same face, turning to face Sakuya one after another, excitedly telling him about their somewhat illogical reasons for boarding the ship.

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「そりゃあ、私ら世界のあっちこっちに散らばっていたからねえ」
source.english: “Well, we were scattered all over the world, you know.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Well, see, that's because we've been scattered all across the world.」

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「まーいいじゃないいいじゃない。
　私たちとこのお船、
　切っても切れない仲なんだし」
source.english:
“Oh, what's the harm?
We and this ship
have ties you couldn't cut if you tried.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Come on, it's fine, it's fine. We share an inseparable bond with this ship.」

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「あたし等が混ざったって、信天翁号にはまだまだ余裕あるしね」
source.english: “There's plenty of room left on the Albatross, even with us aboard.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Even with us joining in, the Albatross still has plenty of room to spare, right?」

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「それに───私達だけが置いていかれるのなんて、寂しいじゃないさ」
source.english: “Besides—it'd be lonely if we were the only ones left behind.”

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Besides───if we were the only ones left behind, just think of how lonely we'd be.」

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「そうそう。それに道中、あたしらお相手差し上げてよ、色々と、ね？」
source.english: “Exactly. And along the way, we'll keep you company. In all sorts of ways, hm?”

source.japanese:
最後にそう言って朔屋にしなだれかかる彼女から聴いてきたのは、どこか憶えのある香で、さてはこの娘、いつぞやどこぞの港の酒場の二階で一夜限りとはいえ濃密に情交わし合った女ではなかろうかと、推し量ってみても断言はできぬ何しろ並ぶ同じ顔。
　しかしその触れる体の柔らかかさは心地よく、朔屋は早速鼻の下を伸ばしにかかったことである。そこはこの手の機微には長けたものであって、娘もそっと朔屋の耳元に唇寄せて、吐息を混ぜて囁いた。
source.english:
The woman who said this last and melted against Sakuya gave off a scent he seemed to remember, and he wondered whether this might not be the very woman with whom, once upon a time, somewhere upstairs over some harbor tavern, he had shared a single night of exceedingly intimate congress—though conjecture was as far as he could go, what with that row of identical faces.

Still, the softness of the body pressed against him was delightful, and Sakuya promptly began letting his face go slack with lust. The woman, being well versed in such delicate signs, softly brought her lips to his ear and whispered, her breath mingling with the words.

source.japanese:
【酒場のお姉さん】
「寂しくなったり色々溜まったりしたら、何時でもおいでなさいな」
source.english: “Whenever you're lonely, or you've got things building up, come and see us.”

source.japanese:
それなら早速と娘の肩を抱こうとした時、現れたのは朔屋と同じように船内をうろついていた密航者。肩に回さんとした手をピタリと止めた朔屋、しかし一度伸びた鼻の下は容易にもとには戻らず、そのだらしない顔に冷たい視線投げかけて、鼻で笑いさえして立ち去った。
　仕方なく朔屋もすごすごとその部屋を出たのだが。
source.english:
He was about to put an arm around her shoulders and accept at once when the stowaway appeared, wandering through the ship as he had been. Sakuya's hand stopped dead. But wiping that leer off his face wasn't so easy. She cast a cold glance at that slack expression, even snorted, and left.

Sakuya had no choice but to slink out of the room too.

target.text: 【Lady from the bar】 「Yeah, yeah. And also, en route, we'd be pleased to keep you company, and in several ways, okay?」

As the girl who had said that last line leaned her body coquettishly against him, he picked up a vaguely familiar fragrance, so could it not be that she was the very same girl with whom he had, even if just for a single night, shared in a deep, passionate exchange of intimacy on the second floor of a bar in some port somewhere, but no matter how he conjectured, it was impossible to say for certain, for you see, they all shared the same face.

However, the softness of her body as it touched his was pleasant, and Sakuya immediately began to blatantly ogle her body. The girl also excelled in the delicate inner workings of these things, and she softly drew her lips close to Sakuya's ear, hitting him with a breathy whisper.
【Lady from the bar】 「If you're ever lonely or start feeling pent up, you can pay me a visit any time.」

Thinking that in that case, he might as well get right to it, the moment Sakuya made to embrace the girl by the shoulders, who should appear but the stowaway, roaming around the ship just like Sakuya had been. About to make its way around her shoulder, Sakuya's hand came to a complete stop, however, once leering, a man's eyes do not so easily soften again, and so she threw a cold glare at his slovenly expression, even snorting in displeasure as she took her leave. Reluctant but left with no other option, a dejected Sakuya also left the room.

source.japanese: こうして、信天翁号はあますとこなく、この世のあぶれ者を回収して南へと向かっているのだった。
source.english: Thus the Albatross gathered up this world's outcasts without leaving any behind, and headed south.

target.text: Thus, with none left behind, the Albatross had now retrieved all the lepers of this world and was heading south.

source.japanese: 窓に映し出される光景は、常に千転して万変していた。
source.english: The scene displayed in the window was forever shifting through a thousand, ten thousand transformations.

source.japanese:
ここは信天翁号の船倉の片隅、今や船の皆に黙認された密航者の隠れ家だった。
　もちろん、船倉は船の最下層にある。外を眺められる窓などあるはずもない。
　しかし、二人は確かに、窓から外の光景を眺めていた。二人、朔屋と密航者。頼みもしないのにすり寄ってきた密航者を膝に乗せ、朔屋はその光景を眺めていた。窓、この隠れ家を船員の目から隠すために密航者が板きれ立てて作った壁にくり抜かれた窓。船の外になど続いているわけもない。しかし、密航者に促されて覗いてみれば、たしかにその窓に映るのは信天翁号の船外に広がる空と海だったのだ。
　今さら何をか言わん、朔屋、仕組みと道理を考えるのをやめて、密航者の呟きを聞きながら、その光景を見続ける。
source.english:
This was the stowaway's hideout in a corner of the Albatross's hold, now tacitly accepted by everyone aboard.

The hold, of course, was at the ship's lowest level. There could be no window looking outside.

Yet two people were certainly looking out of a window at the view. Sakuya and the stowaway. She had sidled up unasked, and he sat with her on his lap, watching. The window was cut into the wall of boards she had erected to hide this retreat from the sailors. It could not possibly open onto the outside of the ship. Yet when he looked through it at her prompting, it certainly showed the sky and sea surrounding the Albatross.

What was left to say at this point? Sakuya stopped thinking about mechanisms and logic. He kept watching, listening to the stowaway's murmurs.

source.japanese: 信天翁号は遂に世界の南の果てへと踏み込んだ。幻想と現実の狭間の、この世の彼方の海の航海。船の周囲は予兆もなく、ある時急に様変わりし、風の向き、潮の向きが引っ繰り返る。そして、現れるのだ、あらゆる海の光景が。人が、海の上で為してきたことが。
source.english: At last the Albatross entered the southernmost reaches of the world. A voyage through seas beyond this world, between fantasy and reality. Without warning, her surroundings suddenly changed; wind and current reversed. Then every scene of the sea appeared. All that humans had done upon it.

target.text: The spectacle unfolding through the glass was a perpetual cycle of flickering mutations and alterations.

It was in a corner of the hold of the Albatross, the place that everyone had now tacitly acquiesced to being the stowaway's hideout. Of course, the hold was in the ship's lowest deck. There should be no windows that allowed one to admire the outside. However, two people were, without question, looking out over the outside from a window. Those two being Sakuya and the stowaway. Though the stowaway snuggling up to him had not asked for it, Sakuya had placed her on his lap, looking out on that view.

The window, one carved into the wall mainly made of scrap lumber that the stowaway had erected to keep this refuge hidden from the prying eyes of the crew. There was no way it could possibly have connected to the outside of the ship. However, when he peeked through it after being urged to do so by the stowaway, it certainly was the vast sky and ocean unfolding outside the Albatross that was projected onto it. What was there even to say anymore? Sakuya gave up on even trying to rationalize the logic or the workings of it, and while lending an ear to the stowaway's mutterings, he gazed long at that view.

At long last, the Albatross was approaching the southernmost end of the world. A voyage into the sea beyond this world, through the threshold of illusion and reality. The area around the ship would, without any prior signs, suddenly change drastically, the direction of the wind and the tide reversing on a whim. And then, they came into sight, scenes of all manner of seas. Of all what man had achieved at sea.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「この情景は、きっと海に溶かしこまれた、人間達の記憶の投影なのでしょうね」
source.english: “These scenes must be projections of human memories dissolved into the sea.”

source.japanese: まだ超古代の戦争が続いている海域もある───命からがら行き過ぎる。
source.english: In some waters, wars of the remotest antiquity still raged—they passed through, barely escaping alive.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「This spectacle has to be a projection of the memories of mankind dissolved into the sea, right?」
There were also waters still locked in primordial conflict───they passed them by, but only by the skin of their teeth.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「この情景を見て、あああーやだな～。
　やっぱりそうだって再確認しちゃった。
　この世界ってば、私の地球のずっと後の時代なんだって」
source.english:
“Seeing this—aaah, I hate it.
It confirms what I thought.
This world is far in my Earth's future.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「何度も何度も滅びかかって、しぶといかと思えば、こりゃもういけない」
source.english: “So close to destruction, over and over. You might think it resilient—but no, this won't do.”

source.japanese: 停滞しきったあげく、ゆるやかな滅びを迎えた海域もある───怖気を振り払いながら行き過ぎる。
source.english: In some waters, utter stagnation had given way to a slow extinction—they passed through, shaking off their dread.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「When I see these scenes, aaaah, it just sucks～. I end up reaffirming that it really is the case. That this world here is an era long after my Earth.」
【Stowaway】 「On the brink of ruin again and again, but you can't go thinking it's tenacious or anything.」
There were also waters that, after having fully stagnated, began a gentle descent towards extinction───while shaking off the dread, they passed them by.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「私がなによりおぞましく思って、嫌いなのはね。
　この世界がこんな風に、戦争に次ぐ戦争を続けて、疲弊していったから、そうではないの」
source.english:
“What I find most horrible, what I hate above all—
It isn't that this world went on fighting war after war like this, wearing itself out.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「You know, what I find the most odious, the most loathsome. It's not that the world, as you've seen, keeps going from one war to the next, exhausting itself in the process.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「疲れきって、やめるのならそれでいい。
　それでなければ、戦争の果てに滅び去ったって、それならそれで一つの結末だもの、ありでしょうよ」
source.english:
“If it grew exhausted and stopped, that would be fine.
Or if it perished in the end from war, that too would be an ending. Fair enough.”

source.japanese: 轟音と共に尻より炎吹いて空を切り裂く丸太よりも巨大な金属柱が飛び交うこともあれば。
source.english: Sometimes metal pillars larger than logs tore through the sky, roaring, spitting flame from their rear ends.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「If, completely worn out, it gives up, then that's fine. Otherwise, should it fall into ruin at the end of a war, that is still a conclusion in its own right, so that's probably also fine.」
There were also gigantic metallic pillars flying past one another, thicker than even a log, rendering the heavens asunder as flames spouted from their rears with thunderous roars.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そうではないの。こうやって戦争を続けた挙げ句に、自分達を騙す事を覚えた、という事」
source.english: “No. After continuing these wars, they learned to deceive themselves.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「戦争を、やめることもせず、続けて滅び去ることも厭[いや]だっていう。挙げ句どうしたかと思えば」
source.english: “They wouldn't stop fighting. And they didn't want to go on and perish either. So what did they do in the end?”

source.japanese: 天より真っ直ぐな稲光が海面を打ったかと思うと、すさまじい水蒸気噴き上げ海面が爆発したこともある。
source.english: Sometimes a straight flash of lightning struck the sea from above; tremendous vapor burst upward, and the surface exploded.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「But that's not what this is. After continuing to war with one another like this, they learned how to deceive themselves.」
【Stowaway】 「They did not wish to stop the war, nor did they want it to continue and be destroyed as a result. So in the end, what did they do?」
There were also times when, no sooner than he thought he saw lightning descending directly from the heavens and striking the sea, the surface exploded in an immense eruption of steam.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「世界を囲いこんで、閉じたのよ。
　私が見てきた限りでは、この世界、実はなかなか大したものだった。そうなの。信じられないことに」
source.english:
“They enclosed the world. Shut it in.
From what I've seen, this world had actually been quite remarkable. Yes. Incredible as it seems.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「They fully enclosed this world, then shut it away. From what I've been able to glean, this world is actually quite the amazing feat. That's right. To the point it beggars belief.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「科学の力は、ある点では絶頂を極めていてね。
　信じられる？　彼らはこの空の上、星々にまで届こうとしていたっけ」
source.english:
“In some respects, science had reached its height.
Can you believe it? They were trying to reach beyond this sky, to the stars.”

source.japanese:
それを朔屋は眺めていた。ぼんやりと。この胸に頭預けて語り続ける密航者を優しく抱きながら。
　耳をじっと澄ませれば、この外の状況に必死に船を操る乗り組み達の喧噪がかすかに聞こえてもきただろう。しかし、今は誰も二人を呼び立てて猫の手にしようとは考えなかった。密航者はこの船そのものであり、健在であればそれでよい。うっかり甲板走らせて海に落ちでもしたら心臓に悪い。朔屋は……朔屋なのだ。この船の一員ではあるが、もはや誰もが役に立たないと認めていた。だからこそ、この船にいるのだと。
source.english:
Sakuya gazed upon it all in a haze, gently holding the stowaway as she rested her head against his chest and went on talking.

Had he strained his ears, he might have faintly heard the clamor of the crew fighting desperately to handle the ship amid the turmoil outside. Yet it occurred to no one now to call the two of them up and press them into service, however desperate they might be for hands. The stowaway was the ship itself; so long as she remained in good health, that was enough. To send her scurrying over the deck only to let her tumble into the sea would be murder on everyone’s nerves. As for Sakuya… Sakuya was Sakuya. He belonged to the ship, true, but by now everyone agreed he was no earthly use. And that, precisely, was why he was aboard.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「In certain respects, the power of science has reached its peak. Can you believe it? They were trying to travel into the skies, reaching even for the stars glittering above, I think.」

Sakuya beheld that. In a daze. While tenderly embracing the stowaway continuing her narration as she leaned her head into his chest. Had he concentrated on straining his ears, he would surely have been able to hear the faint sound of the noisy bustling of the crew as they desperately tried to steer the ship through the situation unfolding outside.

However, right now, there was no one who thought of calling for the two, frantically busy as they might have been. The stowaway was this very ship herself, and as long as she stayed in good health, all was well. Were she to heedlessly run across the deck and tumble into the sea, it would be bad for the heart. And Sakuya……well, he was Sakuya. He was a member of the crew, but by now, everyone had deemed him useless. That was, after all, exactly why he was on this ship.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そっちに進めばいいのにね……力を全部戦争で使い果たして、星への道まで閉ざしちゃった」
source.english: “They should have gone that way…instead they used up all their strength on war, and closed the road to the stars too.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「If only we could have proceeded down that path……but they squandered all their strength in the war, and even the path leading to the stars was cut off.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「それでなにをやっているかと思えば、世界を閉じきって、伝説だの神話だのをばらまいて。疲れきった精神を、それら原型のぬるま湯に浸して」
source.english: “And what do they do now? Seal the world completely, scatter legends and myths about. Soak their exhausted minds in the lukewarm bath of those archetypes.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「自分達の自由にできる世界。
　自分達の揺りかごになってくれる物語」
source.english:
“A world they can control.
Stories to cradle them.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そんなものに浸って、自分を騙して。
　それで時々は、昔みたいに戦争をしたりする。
　でも温い戦争。自分達がまだ戦えるって事を言い張るような、じじばばの繰り言みたいな、ね」
source.english:
“They soak in those things and deceive themselves.
And sometimes they fight wars, as in the old days.
But lukewarm wars. Like old men and women droning on about how they can still fight.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And just when you think they might do something useful, it turns out they just closed off the world, busying themselves with peddling around legends and myths. Soaking their exhausted souls in the comfortably tepid waters of those archetypes.」
【Stowaway】 「A world where they can do exactly as they like. Stories that become their cradles.」

【Stowaway】 「Immersed in such things, they deceive themselves. And then, at times, they war as they did in the past. But it is a tepid war. Like the repetitive ramblings of geriatrics obstinately insisting that they're still waging war against one another, you know?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あなた達の世代が知る戦争というのは、みんなそのようなもの。老爺の、萎びきった性器のような。老媼の、弛んだ乳房のような。おお、いやだいやだ」
source.english: “Every war your generation knows is like that. Like an old man's shriveled genitals. Like an old woman's sagging breasts. Oh, how I hate it.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「The wars that your generation, that your world knows, they're all like that. Like an old man's shrivelled dick. Like an old woman's saggy tits. Oooh, I just can't stand it.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あのね、戦争をするにあたって一番大切なのは、わかっているかも知れないけれど、落としどころ」
source.english: “You know, perhaps you already understand this, but the most important thing when you go to war is knowing what settlement you'll accept.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「どこで手を打ってやめるか、その条件を設定すること。それがない戦争ほど、見苦しいものはないわ」
source.english: “Setting the terms on which you'll strike a bargain and stop. Nothing is uglier than a war without that.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Look, the most important thing when you're fighting in a war, and maybe you already know this, is finding common ground.」
【Stowaway】 「Exactly where can you come to an agreement and reach a ceasefire, establishing those terms. There's nothing more deplorable than a war without that.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「中にはね、闘争の為の闘争、なんて言い出す者もいるのは知っている。───言葉に酔いしれただけの阿呆という。
　そういう人間にとっては、この世界はあるいはありなのかもね」
source.english:
“I know some people talk of ‘struggle for struggle's sake.’—Fools drunk on words.
For such people, perhaps this world is acceptable.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「There are some people who speak of conflict for the sake of conflict, I'm aware of that. ───Fools, I say, infatuated with their own rhetoric. To people like that, maybe this world could be acceptable, yeah.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「戦争が許されているのだから。
　箱庭の、戦争が。
　ああなんて、だらだら続く、
　お祭りのようなくだらなさ」
source.english:
“War is permitted, after all.
War in a miniature garden.
Ah, what endless,
pointless nonsense. Like a festival.”

source.japanese: こうして密航者は語り終える。最後に、朔屋の頬にその手を当てて、その顔じっと見て予言を残し。
source.english: Thus the stowaway came to the end of her discourse. Then, laying a hand against Sakuya’s cheek and gazing steadily into his face, she left him with this prophecy:

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Because war is permitted here. War, in a miniature walled garden. Aah, what worthlessness, like a never-ending festival that just drags on and on.」
Thus, the stowaway's narration came to an end. At its close, she put her hand on Sakuya's cheek, looked intently into his face, and left him with a prophecy.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「でもね直正教えてあげる。
　君……この航海の最後に、滅茶苦茶に、それこそ脳溢血あたり起こしかねないくらいに、怒ることになるよ」
source.english:
“But Naomasa, let me tell you.
At the end of this voyage, you'll be furious. So furious you might well have a brain hemorrhage.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「But, you know, I will tell you this, Naomasa. You will……at the very end of this voyage, you will become incredibly upset, so angry that you might well suffer a cerebral apoplexy.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「じゃあ鑑賞はこれくらいにして、お酒呑もうか。
　それともほかのことする？　私としては、抱いてくれるのが嬉しいかな」
source.english:
“Well, enough watching—let’s grab a drink.
Or do something else? Honestly, I’d be happy if you made love to me.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Alright then, let's leave appreciating the scenery at that. Want to have a drink? Or perhaps you'd like to do something else? Personally, I was just thinking that I might like for you to make some love to me.」

source.japanese: 朔屋と密航者が二人の隠れ家しけ込んで、ややもすれば睦み合いの休憩時間に窓打ち眺めているその時も。
source.english: Even at that moment, while Sakuya and the stowaway had holed up in their hideaway and were gazing out the window during a break in their lovemaking…

source.japanese:
信天翁号はただひたすらに、南を目指して進んでいた。
　すでに先人達の航跡の洗礼受けた海域はとうに過ぎ、ここより先は未知の海域、誰も踏み込んだことのない、あるいは踏み込んだ者は帰らなかった海を進む。
　船倉で二人が見る光景は洋上の事実で、船外一望が変わる度に、信天翁号は新たな危機に見舞われる。
source.english:
The Albatross pressed steadily south.

The waters where she had been baptized by her predecessors' wakes lay far behind. Beyond was uncharted sea, where no one had ventured—or no one who ventured had returned.

What the pair saw in the hold was the truth of the open sea. Each change of scenery outside brought the Albatross a new crisis.

target.text: Sakuya and the stowaway slipped into their hideout, and while they gazed out the window during their intermissions, which were apt to take a turn for the intimate.

The Albatross only continued heading south, advancing with a single-minded focus. They had long since passed the waters baptized by the wakes of their predecessors; what awaited ahead were waters yet unknown, and so they advanced into the seas where none had dared tread, or perhaps those who had dared had never returned to tell the tale. The scenes the two saw play out from the hold were what was actually happening out at sea, and whenever the sweeping view outside the ship changed, so did the Albatross also face a new crisis.

source.japanese: それでも、シサムとキサラ、双子の航海士の冴えは抜群で、海図も存在しないこの海域でも針路見失うことなく舵を捌いて船進ませる。
source.english: Even so, Sisam and Kisara, the twin navigators, were brilliantly sure. In waters for which no chart existed, they never lost their course, working the helm and driving the ship onward.

source.japanese: 船長クロも、百万遍でもしりとり続けられそうなほど覚醒し、双子と伝声管を相手に指示を飛ばし、襲いかかる脅威から信天翁号を守る。
source.english: Captain Kuro too was so thoroughly awake that she might have kept a word chain going a million rounds. Through the speaking tube she fired orders at the twins, protecting the Albatross from the threats that assailed her.

source.japanese: 水夫長は下級水夫達を怒鳴り飛ばしてクロの指示を完遂させ、機関長は船の心臓蒸気機関に細心のタイミングで炭を放り込み速度を保つ。
source.english: The boatswain roared at the junior sailors to carry out Kuro's orders. The chief engineer fed coal into the ship's heart, her steam engines, with exacting timing, maintaining her speed.

source.japanese: そして智里は盃になみなみ満たした安酒を、おっとっと口から迎えに行って一息に、乾した吐息が満悦の。皆が小鳥廻[まわ]しに忙しい時に、しけこんでいるのが酒場のお姉さん達の一角で、酒の相伴は宗右衛門猫さ。お姉さん達は船が大揺れ、船体が軋む度、不安そうな顔見せるものの。ホッケの燻製などを泰然と囓[かじ]る宗右衛門猫の泰然と動ぜぬ佇[たたず]まいに心強いもの覚えて、客あしらいの艶笑取り戻す。
source.english: And Tomosato, with a cup brimful of cheap liquor—whoops, lips down to meet it—drained it in one breath and sighed contentedly. While everyone else bustled nimbly about, he had holed up in the barmaids' corner. His drinking companion was Soemon the cat. The women looked anxious whenever the ship lurched violently or her hull creaked. But the serene composure of Soemon, calmly gnawing smoked greenling and the like, reassured them, and they recovered the alluring smiles with which they entertained guests.

target.text: Nevertheless, Shisamu and Kisara, the twin mates, displayed an exceptional clarity of mind, deftly handling the helm without losing track of the ship's course, even through these waters for which no nautical charts had ever been drawn, letting the ship sail onward.

Likewise, Captain Kuro had been roused into a state so clearheaded she could well have continued a game of shiritori a million times over, rapidly dispatching orders to the twins and through the voice pipes, protecting the Albatross from any encroaching threats.

The Bosun was barking loudly at the deck boys, carrying Kuro's orders through, and the Chief Engineer was meticulously throwing coal into the steam engine, the ship's beating heart, adding more with just the right timing to maintain their speed.

And then there was Tomosato who, with a "whoops, that's enough", filled his cup to the brim with cheap sake, slowly raised it to his lips, then drank it all in one gulp, letting out a sigh of great satisfaction.

While everyone else flitted around busily like little hummingbirds, he had slipped into the corner where the bar girls gathered, sharing a drink with none other than Souemon the cat. Whenever the ship rolled and the hull creaked, a look of worry would show on the ladies' faces. But the presence of Souemon, imposingly unmoving and self-possessed as he chewed on some smoked Arabesque greenling, made for a reassuring sight, and they regained the usual coquettish smiles they treated their customers to.

source.japanese: およそ海の暴虐を並べ尽くした海域を、信天翁号は逃げ惑いながらもまっすぐ南へと突き抜けた。
source.english: Through waters displaying every conceivable outrage of the sea, the Albatross fled and dodged, yet pushed straight through to the south.

target.text: Desperate escape that it was, the Albatross still managed to break through these waters where the entire repertoire of the ocean's treacherous cruelty had been put on full display, advancing south.

source.japanese:
突き抜けた、
　その先に、
　待っていたものは。
source.english:
And beyond—

After she had pushed through—

What awaited her?

target.text: She broke through, and before them, in the place they arrived, what awaited them was none other than.

source.japanese: その姿、目にするのは何度目か。
source.english: How many times had they seen that form?

target.text: How many times had they seen that figure by now?

source.japanese: それは、白く、巨大な、目も鼻もない、のっぺりとした顔と肌で───総体としては人間型に見えなくもなかったけれど。
source.english: White and immense, with smooth skin and a blank face, neither eyes nor nose—taken as a whole, it might have been called human in shape.

target.text: It was white, titanic, with no eyes or nose, with a flat, featureless face and smooth skin───on the whole, it was possible to interpret its shape as humanoid, but.

source.japanese: そう、───ウミヒト。
source.english: Yes—a Sea Person.

target.text: Indeed, ───the Umihito.

source.japanese:
極圏にて、世界の果て目指す者を摘[つ]み取ってきた守人がその巨体、まるで一つの森の主の如く、海に根を下ろし天に向かってそびえ立つ。そのウミヒトが、今、信天翁号の前に。一つ、二つ、三つ───
　
　そう、このような存在がどこに隠れていたのか、群なして南の果ての海に集うていた。もし、彼らがまともに餌を食う存在であったのなら、この世界の海から一晩きりですべての生命、藻類、微虫類の類をたゆたう水もろとも吸い込み、海底近くでは蟹海老の甲殻類、蛸烏賊の頭足類を砂ごと掬[すく]って飲み込み、魚類、爬虫類、果ては鯨の哺乳類まで、大小すべての生けるものを喰らい尽くしてしまうだろう。そして残るは死の海のみ。
source.english:
The guardians that plucked away those who sought the world's edge in the polar regions rooted their vast bodies in the sea and towered skyward, like the lord of a forest. Now such Sea People stood before the Albatross. One, two, three—

Yes, where had beings like these been hiding? They gathered in a swarm at the southernmost sea. Had they fed as ordinary creatures did, in one night they might have consumed every living thing in this world's waters: algae and tiny organisms swallowed with the water in which they drifted; crabs and shrimp, octopuses and squid scooped up with the sand near the seabed; fish, reptiles, even the mammalian whales. Great and small, all life devoured. Only a dead sea would remain.

source.japanese:
そのウミヒトの群が、立ちはだかっていた、信天翁号の前に。ここから先は通さぬと言うように、ここより誰も逃がさぬと言うように。貴様らは逃げられぬのだと言うように。
　
　おぞましく蠢く様は、舗装路の上、水蒸気が灼熱の太陽光に暖められて立ち上り、それをレンズに遠景歪ませる陽炎に似た揺らめきよう、ゆらゆらと無貌を揺らめかせ、彼ら、信天翁号目指して集い来る。信天翁号目指して？
　
　いや、違う。彼らは集うのだ。一所に。
source.english:
The Sea People barred the Albatross's way. As though saying: you will not pass. No one will escape from here. You cannot get away.

They writhed horribly, their faceless forms wavering like a heat haze above a paved road, where vapor warmed by the blazing sun rises and lenses the distant view into distortion. They gathered toward the Albatross. Toward the Albatross?

No. They gathered together. In one place.

source.japanese:
よく磨かれた硝子の上に、零れて玉となった水に息吹きかければ、それはそよいで硝子を滑る。
　
　そよぐ雫が別の雫に近づき、その二つが触れあう瞬間、玉の表面、微少極まる水の粒が織りなす皮膜が触れ合い破れる瞬間に、二つの水はひと息に解けて一つとなる。
　
　ウミヒトはその様をおぞましいほどのスケールで、極北の洋上にて再現したのだ。触れ合い融[と]け合い膨れ上がる、ウミヒトの群は、数減らし嵩[かさ]増やし、そして一つが残る───
source.english:
Blow upon beads of spilled water on well-polished glass, and they stir and slide.

A stirring drop approaches another. At the instant the two touch, at the instant their surfaces—the films woven by minuscule particles of water—meet and break, the two dissolve at once into one.

On the seas of the far north, the Sea People reproduced that sight upon a horrifying scale. Touching, melting together, swelling. Their numbers dwindled, their bulk increased, until one remained—

target.text: Those titans, the guardians of the Antarctic, they who would nip any buds who dared set their sights on the end of the world: like the lord of a great forest, they took root in the ocean, faced the heavens, towering over all. Those Umihito now stood before the Albatross. One, two, three───

Indeed, just where had such beings hidden themselves, congregating together in a great flock in the ocean by the southernmost end. Perhaps, had these been beings that needed to eat food like any other, then all lifeforms, algae, and any micro-arthropods drifting about in the oceans of the whole world would be inhaled into their maws overnight; the crustaceans like the crabs and shrimp and the cephalopods like the octopuses and squids near the ocean floor would be scooped up with the sand and swallowed whole; the fish, the reptiles, and in the end, even the mammalian whales, all life, large and small alike, would surely be devoured whole. And all that would remain was an ocean of death.

A flock of those Umihito stood in the way before the Albatross, obstructing her. As if to say she would not pass, to say they would let none escape from here. That you cannot escape from here. The way in which they loathsomely wriggled was like steam rising from a paved road warmed by the scorching heat of the sunlight, flickering like the shimmering haze of hot air warped through the view of a distant lens, faceless forms swaying back and forth, flocking together, heading for the Albatross. Heading for the Albatross? No, that was not quite right. They were gathering. At a certain spot.

Were you to breathe on a droplet of water set atop a sheet of finely-polished glass, it would stir and slide along that glass. When the swaying drop nears another, the instant they touch, the moment the infinitesimally small molecules of water that bond in a web across its surface come into contact with the surface of another and breaks, the two drops dissolve into one in an instant.

The Umihito recreated this phenomenon on a horrifying scale atop the ocean of the distant south. Connecting, melting together, swelling in size, and as the swarm of Umihito diminished in number, so did they increase in mass in turn, and finally, when only one of their kind remained───

source.japanese:
それは、遥かに遥かに遥かに巨大だったのだ。
　天まで伸びる壁のようであり、裾は一面の海を埋め尽くすようであり。まるでこのあたり海そのものが白くあり、それがたまたま空へと伸びているのだと思えるほど。巨大である故に、もし幸運であったなら、それを個のウミヒトとは認識できずなんの疑問も抱かずにその体の中に船進ませていただろう。そしてどうなるかは知らないが。そして不幸な事にその存在に気付いてしまったのなら。忘れようとするだろう、その記憶を消したいと願うだろう。それには脳の襞[ひだ]すべてこそぎ落として白痴となるのが一番手っ取り早く、それでいいと己の人格捨て去ろうとする者、後を絶たぬに違いない。
source.english:
It was far, far, far more enormous.

Like a wall extending to heaven, its base covering the whole sea. One might almost think the sea here was itself white and had happened to stretch up into the sky. So vast was it that, if one were fortunate, one might fail to recognize a single Sea Person and sail into its body without a question. What happened then, who knew? And if one were unfortunate enough to notice its existence, one would try to forget. Wish to erase the memory. The quickest way would be to scrape every fold from one's brain and become an idiot. Surely there would be no end to those willing to surrender their selves on those terms.

target.text: It was far, far, far more enormous. Like a wall stretching all the way to the heavens, the foot of it seeming to blanket the entire surface of the sea. It was as though the entire sea itself had turned white, and the waters themselves reached into the sky, so titanic was it. By virtue of its enormity, were one amongst the fortunate ignorant, one could well sail through its body without a single doubt surfacing, never realizing it was a singular Umihito. Though it was unclear what would happen.

If one were unfortunate enough to become aware of its existence. One would surely try to forget, one would surely pray and wish for those memories to be erased. The quickest way to accomplish that would be to shave off every fold of one's brain and become profoundly retarded, and there would surely be no end to the long line of those who would find this preferable, willingly forsaking their own personhood.

source.japanese:
今、信天翁号の眼前に立ちはだかったのは、それだった。
　もちろん、今さらこの船には幸も不幸も選ぶ輩など一人もおらぬのだが。
source.english:
That was what now stood before the Albatross.

Of course, by this point no one aboard cared to choose between fortune and misfortune.

target.text: In this moment, that is what stood right before the Albatross, obstructing her passage. Of course, there was not a single soul on this ship who was given the choice between luck and misfortune.

source.japanese: 船倉の隠れ家からいつの間に飛び出してきたのか、ブーツの底で昇降段蹴りつける跫音高く響かせて、密航者は甲板へと飛び出した。
source.english: At some point the stowaway had sprung out of the hideout in the hold. Her boots hammered the ladder, footsteps ringing loudly, and she burst onto the deck.

target.text: It wasn't clear just when she'd leapt out from their refuge in the hold, but with resounding footfalls as she kicked off against the steps of the ladder with the soles of her boots, the stowaway rushed out on deck.

source.japanese: そこには視界の半ばを埋め尽くす白、極点の果てに鎮座して今、無貌のまま信天翁号を睥睨する。しかし航海者、その威容意に介さず逆に仰ぎ見、睨めつけ、吠える。
source.english: White filled half their sight. Enthroned at the end of the pole, it looked down facelessly upon the Albatross. But the voyager paid no heed to its majesty. She looked up, glared back, and roared.

target.text: There she was greeted with a white that covered most of her vision, dominating the polar end of the world, glaring at the Albatross with its featureless face. However, the stowaway was undaunted by its imposing form; in fact, she looked up at it, scowled at it, howled at it.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「さて、来たか、来たな、来やがったなぁぁ！
　シサム。キサラ。泪さん。クロ」
source.english:
“Well, here you are! Here you are! Here you damn well are!
Sisam. Kisara. Rui. Kuro.”

source.japanese: 彼女のたてた昇降段昇る跫音はそのまま皆呼ぶ半鐘となったのか、いつしか甲板には船に乗る面々が顔を揃えていた。密航者、彼らに振り返る。
source.english: Had the footsteps she made climbing the ladder served as an alarm bell? At some point the whole ship's company had assembled on deck. The stowaway turned to them.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「他のみんなも、聞いて。
　この白いはんぺんもどき、ふやけた白饅頭、
　パン生地の出来損ない、みたいなこいつら、
　あなた達はウミヒトとか呼んでいたね」
source.english:
“Everyone else, listen too.
These things, like white fish cakes, soggy white buns,
a botched batch of bread dough—
You call them Sea People, don't you?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Well, well, you're here, you've come, you fiiiinally show your ugly mug! Shisamu. Kisara. Rui-san. Kuro.」

Perhaps the sound of her steps as she leapt up the ladder must have functioned as a fire alarm summoning everyone else, for all those aboard this ship had gathered on the deck. The stowaway turned around to look at them.
【Stowaway】 「The rest of you listen too. These white fish cake freaks, these soggy, white, steamed buns, these defective lumps of dough, you called them the Umihito or something, right?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「私の航海を、最後に邪魔しにかかるはこいつら、憎い、憎い、憎いいいい！」
source.english: “They're the ones making one last attempt to stop my voyage. I hate them. Hate them. Haaate them!”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ついでに言うと気持ち悪いし、おぞましいし、呪わしいし、ええいもう、死んじゃえ死んじゃえ死にくされ、死んで、ねえ死んで、そんなになってもなんで生きてるわけよ己ら」
source.english: “They're disgusting, too. Horrible, accursed—oh, just die, die, die and rot! Die, won't you die? Why the hell are you still alive in that state?”

source.japanese: 隠そうともしない怨嗟をそのまま言葉に乗せて、密航者は吐き捨てる。確かに彼女の恨み辛みの程は皆に伝わりはしたものの。
source.english: The stowaway spat out the words, putting her rancor into them without any attempt to hide it. Certainly she conveyed the extent of her bitterness to everyone, but—

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「These things, just dying to interfere with my voyage at the very end, oh how I hate, hate, HAAAATE them!」
【Stowaway】 「While I'm at it, they're revolting, repulsive, accursed, arghh, enough, die, die, die and rot, die, come on, just die, look at you, why are you even alive after being reduced to that!?」

Without even attempting to hide it, the stowaway let her deeply held resentment express itself through words unadorned, all but spitting them out. Yes, the extent of the girl's rancour was certainly conveyed to all present, but.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「……いやあのね。今さらあんた一人がぶち切れたって」
source.english: “…Well, look. Losing your temper all by yourself now—”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「……No, well, I mean. You're really not getting anything out of flying off the handle by yourself here.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「あたしらにとっちゃ、ああ邪魔なんだな、
　ってくらいで」
source.english:
“To us, it's just—oh,
they're in the way.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「To us, at least, all we really feel is "argh, these guys are in the way", and that's about it.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「クロも、気持ち悪いなって思うけど、でも、なんだかよく、わかり、よくないから」
source.english: “Kuro thinks they're nasty too. But Kuro doesn't really…understand very well…”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Kuro also think they're gross, but, but, Kuro doesn't really, get it, isn't good, so.」

source.japanese:
【泪】
「わたくしも、あの方たちのご一統とは、関わりが薄くって。お互い無関心なのね」
source.english: “I too have little to do with their company. We are mutually indifferent.”

target.text: 【Rui】 「I do not have much to do with that group of theirs either. We're mutually indifferent, you see.」

source.japanese: 共感までは得られなかったようで。しかし、それを気にする密航者ではない。皆の一歩退いた感想も右から左とやり過ごし、言葉の爆弾、投げ続ける。
source.english: She seemed not to have won their sympathy. But the stowaway was not one to mind that. Their cautious impressions went in one ear and out the other as she kept flinging verbal bombs.

target.text: It seems she didn't quite manage to get them to share in her sentiment. However, the stowaway was not the sort to let that bother her. She let their above-mentioned reactions of taking an emotional step backwards pass right by her, then continued to hurl her verbal bombs.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「なあにが、無関心どころか。泪さん、あなた達、伝説の生き残りに機械装置を与えて。慢心と驕慢の徒にしたのは、あいつら」
source.english: “Indifferent, are you? Rui, they're the ones who gave mechanical devices to you survivors of legends. Who made you creatures of complacency and arrogance.”

source.japanese: 腕を振り上げ巨体の頭と思しき辺りを指し示す。そして彼女は暴くのだ、彼の存在の悪業を、犯した罪を、この船に乗る者達に降りかかる災厄の因果はどこから回り来たのかを、あいつだと指し示し。
source.english: She flung up her arm and pointed toward what seemed to be the vast body's head. Then she laid bare its evil deeds, its sins, and showed everyone aboard where the chain of calamities that had befallen them all began: with that thing.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「What do you mean indifferent, you're anything but. Rui-san, you and your kind were given those mechanisms by the extant remnants of legend. They are the ones who turned you and yours into beings of pride and arrogance.」

Raising her arm overhead, she pointed to what seemed to be somewhere near the titan's head. And then she exposed it, the evil of their existence, the sins they had committed, from where exactly the calamities befalling those aboard this ship originated, pointing out how that thing was to blame for it all.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あいつらが、今のあなた達を作りあげた。
　シサムにキサラ。北方氷土の果てにこいつらを見たでしょう、あの氷の壁の中」
source.english:
“They made you what you are now.
Sisam and Kisara. You saw them at the far end of the northern ice fields, didn't you? In that wall of ice.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Those things are who created you as you are now. Shisamu and Kisara. You must have seen them at the ends of the northern permafrost, inside that wall of ice.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あそこで、そして残りの東西それにこの南冥で、世界を閉ざしているのがこいつらだっていったらどう思う」
source.english: “What if I told you they're the ones sealing off the world there, and in the east and west, and here in the southern seas?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「If I were to tell you that those guys up there, as well as in the east and the west, and also here in the Southern Ocean, are the ones keeping this world sealed shut, then what?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「選ばれしモノ三位一体者。ちなみに選んだのはこいつらだけど？　雌雄ともう一要素の巌合体。それらの霊的結合ああもう言葉はいいわ」
source.english: “The chosen Triune One. Incidentally, they're the ones who chose you. A fusion of male, female and a third element. Their spiritual union—oh, enough of the words.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「The chosen ones, the Triune Beings. By the way, those guys are the ones who chose you, just so you know? A rock-solid combination of a male, a female, and one extra component. And their spiritual union-, argh, that's enough about that already.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「三位一体者ってのはね、要するにこいつらの餌よ餌。昇華って言われているけれど、なんのことはない、あれは一回で燃え尽きる交尾みたいなもので」
source.english: “The Triune One is their food. Food, in short. It's called sublimation, but really it's a sort of mating that burns itself out in a single act.”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「その時に産まれる、快楽のエネルギーを食ってこいつらは、時空を閉ざすエネルギーに変換する」
source.english: “They eat the energy of pleasure produced then, and turn it into the energy that seals off space and time.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「These Triune Beings are, in essence, their dinner, their feed. They call it sublimation, but it's really no big deal, more like a form of mating where you burn out completely after a single round.」
【Stowaway】 「They feed on the pleasure energy that's created at that time, and then they convert it into energy that closes off space-time.」

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「あ……？　するってぇとなにか？　あたしら、最っ高にイく時の、最っ高に気持ちいい瞬間を横取りされるとこだった!?」
source.english: “Huh…? So what? They were going to steal the most incredible moment, when we came as hard as we possibly could!?”

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Hah……? What's that supposed to mean? So when we cum our brains out, right in that instant we feel on top of the world, you say they just snatch that from us!?」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「───ふふ、ふふっ、ウフフッ、うふふフフわっハァあああっっ！　さあ殺すか！」
source.english: “—Hehe. Heheh. Ufufu, ufufufuwaaahahaha! Right, let's kill them!”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「───Huhu, huhu, uhuhu, uhuhuhuhu waa-hahahAAAH! Alright, let's go kill it!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「それから、世界が滅びかけた時に……それだって戦争のせいだけど、生物相の保存と称して、再三箱船を造ったのもこいつら」
source.english: “And they're the ones who built ark after ark when the world nearly perished…because of war, again. In the name of preserving its living creatures.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And then, when the world was on the brink of extinction……war was also to blame for that one, but the ones who built those arks over and over again, purporting to preserve the biota of all the world, were also none other than those guys.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「人類の戦争に巻きこまれて滅びるを肯[がえ]んじずとかなんとか、それはどういうカミサマ根性だ、そんなの私だって言えないわよ烏滸がましい、ましてこいつら、元は同じ生き物なくせに」
source.english: “They wouldn't accept dying in humanity's wars, or some such thing. What sort of divine conceit is that? Even I couldn't say it. The presumption! And these things were originally living creatures like the rest.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「What kind of divine disposition is that supposed to be, refusing to be dragged into the wars of man and be brought to ruin or some such, even I wouldn't say something like that, it's absurdly presumptuous, and especially galling given those guys were originally the very same creatures they lord it over.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「じゃあ、ノアのおじいがあんな事になったのも、クロがこんななのも、みんな……？」
source.english: “Then Noah turning out like that, and Kuro turning out like this, all of it…?”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「So then, that's why grandpa Noah ended up like that, why Kuro is like this, all of it……?」

source.japanese: そう、そう、そうと、ぶちまけた彼女の見てきた、この世界での長い長い航海の中で見てきた、この己が移し身信天翁号に乗り込んだ者達が辿った経緯末路の裡[うち]に見てきた、憎いあいつらのしてきたことを、一つ一つ晒す中、皆からあがる声に力強く頷[うなず]く。
source.english: Yes, yes, yes. She nodded vigorously at their voices as she laid it all bare, one thing after another. What she had seen during her long, long voyages through this world. What she had seen in the lives and ends of those who boarded the Albatross, her embodied self. What those hateful things had done.

target.text: Yeah, yeah, that's right, the girl said as she revealed all; she'd seen it, she'd seen it all during her long, long voyage around this world, she'd witnessed every little detail of the roads travelled by those who had boarded her alter ego, the Albatross, from humble beginnings to tragic ends, and as every single sin those abominable things had perpetrated was exposed, one after one, she nodded vigorously in response to the loud voices rising from the crowd.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ここまで人を舐めくさった人も珍しい。
　物事は多角的な視点を持たないと、観念は硬直化するっていう」
source.english:
“Rarely do you find people with such contempt for others.
They say your ideas grow rigid unless you look at things from several angles.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「It's rare to find men bastard enough to look down their nonexistent nose on others to this extent. They say that if you don't consider things from multifarious perspectives, your conceptions will grow rigid.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だからこいつらウミヒトだって、視点によってはこれなりの道理を持っているかもしれないでもね！」
source.english: “So from some angle, these Sea People might have a logic of their own. But!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So, depending on your perspective on things, even these Umihito might operate under their own form of reason, however!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「このふやけはんぺんどもが私たちを阻むのは、私たちを必要ってしているから！」
source.english: “These soggy fish cakes are stopping us because they need us!”

source.japanese: あいつらにどんな道理があろうと、それは認めてはならないのだ、彼女としては。彼女はすでに使命を持ったまま、この世界に来た。それを捨て、勝手な道理を押し付けられるわけにはいかないのだ。だから密航者は目指すのだ、断固として、このウミヒトが立ち塞ぐその先を。
source.english: Whatever logic those things might have, she could not accept it. She had come to this world with a mission already. She could not abandon it and submit to whatever reasoning they chose to impose. So the stowaway aimed resolutely beyond the Sea Person barring her way.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「The reason these soggy fish cakes are obstructing us, why, that's because they need us!」

Whatever logic they operated on, it was unacceptable, at least to her. When she came into this world, she already had a mission. She could not simply abandon that and allow others to impose on her whatever logic suited their convenience. That was why the stowaway was heading there, with a will as firm as steel, towards what lay beyond this Umihito standing in her way.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「あのー」
source.english: “Um—”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「Uhmm.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「何。たとえ君でも今水差したら、みんなの前で犯すから」
source.english: “What? Even you—if you try to ruin this now, I’ll rape you right in front of everyone.”

source.japanese:
わあ、と震え上がる朔屋の、背筋に走ったざわめきと、股ぐらに走ったときめき、どう表すべきか。背筋を冷やしたものは、清冽でそして苛烈に燃える瞋恚の炎。逸物を震わせたものは、皆の前でこれに搾り取られる情景の嗜虐の魅惑。
　朔屋はそれで、問いを慌てて替えた。
　朔屋はこう問おうとしたのである。
　密航者の言葉から、こう感じ取って。
source.english:
Sakuya shuddered with a gasp—how to describe the chill that ran down his spine and the flutter he felt between his legs? What chilled his spine was the pure, fiercely burning flame of wrath. What made his cock quiver was the sadistic allure of imagining her wringing him dry in front of everyone.
That’s why Sakuya hurriedly changed his question.
He had been about to ask about something he’d gathered from the stowaway’s words:

source.japanese:
元は同じ生き物って。
　人を舐めくさった『人』って。
　つまりはこの巨大浮きはんぺん───
　元は、自分達と同じ───
source.english:
Originally living creatures like the rest.

‘People’ with contempt for others.

In other words, this huge floating fish cake—

Originally, the same as them—

source.japanese:
それを口にしようとした時の、密航者の眸[ひとみ]で白炎と化した激甚に朔屋は竦み上がった。
　彼女はそれだけは言わせまいとするかの如く、朔屋を視殺した。あるいはこの密航者にして、それは絶対に認めてはならない最後の事実だったのかも知れない。
source.english:
As he tried to voice it, the fury that became white flame in the stowaway's eyes made Sakuya shrink back.

She looked murderously at him, as though determined not to let him say that much. Perhaps, even for this stowaway, it was the final fact she absolutely could not acknowledge.

source.japanese:
だから朔屋は、この青年にしては目覚ましい勘働きで、慌てて質問を替えたので。
　まあそれだって、密航者にとっては怒りの種の一つだったのだけれど。
source.english:
So Sakuya, with a flash of intuition remarkable for him, hastily changed his question.

Though that, too, was one of the sources of the stowaway's anger.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「そういうのはそういうので。
　でもな、こいつらが俺を必要としているっていうのはそれ、怒るところなら、なにを怒ればいいのかわからない───」
source.english:
“All right, leave that aside.
But these things needing me—if that's something to be angry about, I don't understand what I should be angry at—”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「What. Even should it be you, if you try to put a damper on things now, I WILL rape you in front of everyone here.」

With a "woah!", a shudder ran through Sakuya, and how ought one express the tingling through his spine, and the throbbing through his crotch? What sent a chill down his spine were the flames of fury burning with a fierce, clear coolness. What set his crotch aquiver was the sadistic allure of the image of him being squeezed dry in front of everyone here. Sakuya then hastily changed his question. This is what Sakuya had been trying to ask. What he had sensed from the stowaway's words.
You said they were originally the very same creatures. You mentioned『men』looking down on others. In other words, these titanic, floating fish cakes─── Were, originally, just like all of us───

When he tried to put that into words, he was met with the vehemence burning white-hot in the stowaway's eyes, and so Sakuya cowered in fear. She glared daggers at Sakuya, almost as if to strangle the words before they could leave his lips. Or perhaps, from this stowaway's perspective, that was the final truth that should never, ever be acknowledged.
Therefore, Sakuya, in a striking display of intuition quite rare for this young man, changed his question in a hurry. Well, even that itself was a source of anger for the stowaway, but regardless.
【Naomasa】 「Don't threaten me with a good time. Still, you tell me that they need me, and that's something that should anger me, but I don't even know what I'm supposed to be angry about here───」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「こいつらが信天翁号を逃がしたくないのは、この世界の、あぶれ者達の受け皿がいるから、だから」
source.english: “They don't want to let the Albatross escape because they need somewhere to put this world's outcasts. That's why.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「The reason they don't want to let go of the Albatross is because she serves as the saucer picking up all the misfits of this world, that's why you should be angry.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「こんな停滞しきった世界を良しとしないで、はみ出てしまうモノがある。あなたとあなた、それにあなたや君もそう」
source.english: “Some things can't accept a world this stagnant. They don't fit. You, and you, and you—and you too.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「There are those who don't consider this stagnant world a good thing, and they end up sticking out from the crowd. You and you, and also you, and you over there too, you are all like that.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そんなのを放置していって増えるに任せたら、そのうち世界に影響を与え出す。だから締め出さなきゃならなかった、陸から海から、その住む社会から」
source.english: “If they're left alone to multiply, eventually they'll begin affecting the world. So they had to be shut out. From the land, from the sea, from the societies they live in.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「If they just left such people to their own devices, to spread and multiply, soon enough, it would have an impact on the world. So they have to exclude you from the rest, from the land and from the sea, and from all the societies that live there.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「そういうあぶれ者達を詰めこむ豚箱として、この船。くさいモノにはなんとやら」
source.english: “This ship is a jail to cram those outcasts into. Put a lid on anything that stinks, as they say.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「This ship serves as the holding pen for all those misfits. Better to sweep the whole mess under the rug, or however you say it.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だから、こいつらにとっては必要とはそういう意味合いに於[お]いて。ねえ怒らないの、怒れないの？　そんなにこいつらに去勢されちゃったの直正」
source.english: “That's the sense in which they need us. Doesn't it make you angry? Can't you be angry? Have they castrated you that thoroughly, Naomasa?”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So when I say that they need you, that's the kind of necessity I'm getting at. Hey, aren't you mad, doesn't that just make you seethe? Just think of how they've castrated and broken you in, Naomasa.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あなたが見てきたこと。排斥される信天翁号。
　あなたがまだ見ていないこと。排斥された人達は、信天翁号に乗りこんでは人知れずいなくなる」
source.english:
“What you've seen: the Albatross driven out.
What you haven't seen yet: the people driven out board the Albatross, then disappear without anyone knowing.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「What you have seen: the Albatross being shunned and ostracized. What you have not seen: how those men and women who were shunned and ostracized, how those who board the Albatross vanish unnoticed.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「その為だけに、存在を許されて、そしてどこにも逃げ出すことは許されない地獄の船だ、信天翁号は」
source.english: “A ship of hell, allowed to exist for that alone, and permitted no escape anywhere. That's the Albatross.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「For that reason alone, this hellish ship is permitted existence, and yet not permitted to escape anywhere else: that is the Albatross.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「私、なのに。この船！　私、なのに。
　みんなを好きなのは。私、私、あいつらじゃない。なのに必要としている？　巫山戯ないで！」
source.english:
“But she's me. This ship! She's me.
I'm the one who loves everyone. Me, me, not those things! Yet they need us? Don't make me laugh!”

source.japanese:
密航者の叫び、上甲板に響き渡る。やがてそれは洋上に散り、誰もが声を出すことなく、音もなく。
　密航者は朔屋を見つめている。期待して。朔屋の中に、何かが起こるのを期待して。
source.english:
The stowaway's cry rang over the upper deck. Eventually it scattered upon the sea. No one spoke. No sound.

She watched Sakuya, expectantly. Expecting something to happen within him.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「And yet, it is I. This ship! It's me, and for all that! I'm the one who loves all of you! It's me, me, not them. And still they need you? Preposterous!」

The stowaway's cry reverberated across the entire upper deck. Before long, it scattered across the seas, and none could say a word, make a sound. The stowaway stared intently at Sakuya. Expecting. Hoping that something was stirring inside Sakuya.

source.japanese:
そして、朔屋。
　密航者の視線を受け、さらにここにいる皆からの注視を受け。
source.english:
And Sakuya—

With the stowaway's gaze upon him, and everyone else's too—

target.text: Thus, Sakuya. Was met with the stowaway's eyes, as well as the steady gazes of all present.

source.japanese: そして、途方に暮れていた。
source.english: Was at a loss.

source.japanese: どうしていいのか、わからなかったのだ。何をしていいかわからなかったのだ。その胸の裡[うち]には今靄立ちこめている。何かを形作ろうとのろのろと渦を巻いてはいるのだが、まだそれははっきりとしてこない。まだ、どう吐き出していいのか、わからなかったのだ。この男は。
source.english: He did not know what to do. Did not know what he could do. Mist lay within his chest. Slowly it swirled, trying to take some shape, but nothing was clear yet. He still did not know how to let it out. This man.

target.text: And then, he was at a loss.

He had not the faintest idea what the right thing to do here was. He didn't know what to do. His heart was shrouded in fog. There was something trying to take shape in there, a whirlpool sluggishly churning along, but its form had yet to become clear. What's more, he didn't know how to let it out. This man didn't know how.

source.japanese: それでも。
source.english: Even so.

target.text: Even so.

source.japanese: 密航者がもう一度だけ、その名前を呼ぼうとわずかに口を開きかけた時。
source.english: Just as the stowaway parted her lips to call his name one more time—

source.japanese: 朔屋は一つだけ思いついたことをやってみた、とりあえず。
source.english: Sakuya tried the one thing that occurred to him. For now.

target.text: When the stowaway's lips narrowly parted, about to call his name one final time.
Sakuya tried doing the only thing that came to his mind, for the time being.

source.japanese: 足を上げ、その靴底を、甲板に打ちつけたのだ。
source.english: He raised a foot and struck its sole against the deck.

source.japanese: たった、それだけ。音が鳴る。
source.english: Only that. A sound.

target.text: He raised his foot, then slammed the sole of his shoe down on the deck.
That was all. A sound echoed.

source.japanese: しかし、もう一度、同じことを繰り返した。そして、もう一度、繰り返した。さらにもう一度。さらに、さらに。
source.english: But he did it again. Then again. Once more. Again, again.

source.japanese:
【直正】
（そうか、君は帰りたいんだな、こんなにも、元いた場所へと）
source.english: (I see. You want to go home. This badly. Back where you came from.)

target.text: However, he repeated the same thing, one more time. And then, he repeated it again. Then yet another time. And again, and again.
【Naomasa】 （I see, you want to go back, you want it this much, to return from whence you came.）

source.japanese: 君は、この船は、与えられた使命を果たすために、乗り組み達と必死に頑張って、その結果、この世界に来てしまった。この、閉じてしまった世界に。帰りたいのに、出口を閉ざした世界に。
source.english: You—this ship—had struggled desperately with your crew to fulfill your assigned mission. And as a result, you came to this world. This shut-in world. A world that had sealed its exits, though you wanted to go home.

source.japanese: そして、勝手な都合を押し付けられた。はずれ者、この世界の不都合の辻褄合わせ、汚穢押し付けられ追われるためだけの航海を強いられた。それでも、船は乗り組み達を愛した。自分を動かしてくれる者達を愛した。愛さずにはいられない。動かしてくれるのだから。航海を続けさせてくれるのだから。いつか故郷に帰るために、航海を続けなければいけないのだから。しかし、乗り組み達は役目終えれば取り上げられ、打ち棄てられる。
source.english: Then you had their selfish purposes forced upon you. They loaded you with outcasts—with everything used to paper over this world's inconvenient contradictions, with all its filth—and condemned you to a voyage whose only purpose was to be hounded from place to place. Even so, the ship loved her crew. Loved those who made her move. Could not help loving them. Because they moved her. Because they let her voyage on. Because she had to voyage on, if someday she was to return home. And yet, when the crew had served their purpose, they were taken from her and cast away.

target.text: You, this ship, struggled so desperately together with your crew so you could all accomplish the mission you had been given, and as a result, you ended up in this world. In this world sealed shut. You want to return home, but you ended up in a world where the way out was closed.

And then, you had the circumstances of others selfishly foisted upon you. An outcast, forced into a voyage only to be chased down and saddled with the filth of whatever inconveniences of this world needed accommodating. Nevertheless, the ship loved her crew. She loved they who set her into motion. How could she possibly not? They were the ones who made her sail. They were the ones who let her continue her voyage. For the voyage had to continue, so that she could one day return to the land she called home. However, when the roles of the crew members came to an end, they were taken away from her, then discarded.

source.japanese:
朔屋も見たのだ。
　嵐の中に放たれた烏は、役目を忘れて船に乗った。そして再び方舟に戻った時、そこに再び囚われ絶望した。
　三位一体になり損ねた双子はこの船に乗った。そして極北の地に戻ってみれば永遠にそこに野ざらしだ。
　王子を刺し殺してまで結末に逆らった人魚姫はこの船に乗った。そして退屈だけを抱えて海に戻った。
source.english:
Sakuya had seen it too.

The crow released into the storm forgot her role and boarded the ship. When she returned to the ark, she was imprisoned there again and despaired.

The twins who failed to become a trinity boarded this ship. When they returned to the far north, they were left exposed there forever.
