The mermaid princess who defied her ending even by stabbing her prince to death boarded this ship. And returned to the sea with nothing but boredom.

source.japanese: それでも船は航海を続けた。帰るために、使命を果たすために。お前達の都合じゃない。自分には自分の使命があるのだと叫んだのだ。
source.english: Still the ship kept sailing. To go home. To fulfill her mission. Not for your convenience. I have a mission of my own: that was what she cried.

target.text: Sakuya had also witnessed it. The bird, the one sent forth into the storm, had forgotten its duty and boarded the ship. And then, when it once more returned to the ark, it was once more imprisoned there and despaired. The twins, they who had failed to form a Triune Being, had boarded this ship. And then, when they tried to return to the North Pole, they were abandoned there, left exposed to the elements for all eternity. The mermaid princess, she who had gone so far as to stab the prince to death to defy the conclusion of her tale, had boarded this ship. And then, with nothing to her name but boredom, she had returned to the sea.
Nevertheless, the ship continued her voyage. So she could return home, so she could fulfill her mission. It was not for your benefit. I have my own mission, she yelled.

source.japanese:
朔屋はただ、足を打ち鳴らしていただけだった。
　そこにシサムとキサラ、二人が同時にブーツの踵を甲板へと叩きつける。その音に、また一つまた一つと重なっていく。クロさえも、踵鳴らそうとして要領を得ないものの、ぴょこぴょこと飛び跳ねる。お愛想だけといった素振りで手拍子するだけの者もいたが、誰もがなにか音を鳴らした。
source.english:
Sakuya merely kept stamping his foot.

Then Sisam and Kisara struck their boot heels against the deck together. One sound after another joined theirs. Even Kuro, unable to get the knack of stamping her heels, hopped up and down. Some merely clapped, looking as though they were being polite. But everyone made some sound.

target.text: All Sakuya did was stomp his feet; that was all. Then Shisamu and Kisara joined in, clacking the heels of their boots against the deck in unison. That sound continued to grow in layers, one after the other. Even Kuro tried her best to stomp with her heels, although she didn't quite get the point and just hopped up and down. There were some who clapped in a way clearly meant as nothing more than courtesy, but everyone made some kind of noise.

source.japanese:
表す態度、その心情、多少のズレは出ようとも。
　そうなのだ、ここにいる者どもは、この船は。
　道踏み外した愚か者、迷い込んだ船に集え、そしてあちこち追われて逃げまどえばよい。それがお前達の運命なのだ、相応しい役割なのだ。この世界の中で定まった港も持てぬまま、ただ洋上をあちこちと、出会う者から皆、石投げつけられておればよい、などと。
　勝手な不都合押し付けられて、ただ大人しく、へらへら笑ってそうですねと、背を丸めて従うわけがないのであった。道踏み外したのは自分の勝手と百も承知、だが、そこから進む針路は自分で決めるのだ。
source.english:
Their gestures, their feelings, might differ a little.

Yes. Those here, this ship—

You fools who strayed from your path, gather aboard a ship that lost its way. Be driven here and there, flee in confusion. That is your fate, your fitting role. Have no settled harbor in this world. Merely wander its seas, while everyone you meet throws stones at you—

They were not going to accept that inconvenience thrust upon them, hunch their backs, grin and say, ‘Yes, of course.’ They knew perfectly well they had strayed by their own choice. But the course they took from there was theirs to decide.

target.text: Even if there were some discrepancies in the attitudes expressed and the feelings behind them. That's right, all the people here, this whole ship. All ye fools who have strayed from the right path, gather upon this ship you have stumbled aboard, and when pursued wherever you go, scurry about frantically as you try to escape. That is your fate, the role fitting for you. You will have no fixed port which you can call home, but will simply wander about the ocean, having stones thrown your way by all you encounter, and so on.

Having unreasonable inconveniences foisted upon them, they would surely not simply meekly smile like fools, stooping over in obedience. They knew only all too well that it was entirely for their own benefit that they had strayed from the right path, however, they themselves were the ones who now decided the course to take.

source.japanese:
そう、今、たった今。
　最後の一人、朔屋直正だって、そうなったのだ。
source.english:
Yes. Now. This very moment.

Even the last of them, Naomasa Sakuya, had become that too.

target.text: Indeed. Now, in this very moment. Even Sakuya, the very final one, was no exception.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「直正、みんな───わあ凄い！」
source.english: “Naomasa, everyone—wow!”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「いや、正直、君が言ったように自分が怒ってるかどうかはわからないんだ。脳溢血にもほど遠いしさ。でも───」
source.english: “Honestly, I don't know whether I'm angry, like you said. I'm nowhere near a brain hemorrhage. But—”

source.japanese:
【直正】
「ああ、なにか、ようやく、わかった。
　そうだな。俺はたった一言、
　こう言えばいいんだ」
source.english:
“Ah, somehow, at last, I understand.
Yes. There's just one thing
I have to say.”

source.japanese:
朔屋、わかった。
　
　ようやくわかった。
　
　君が何故、こんな俺を望んだのか。世界の全てから拒否されるような存在を望んだのか。
　
　故郷に帰ることを願って造った最後の道具、それが朔屋だ。ならば、叫ぶがよい。叫んで己の存在、示すがよい。ああ、そうか、怒っているわけではないらしい、いっそ清々しいと言うべきか。駄目で駄目な存在がこんな役に立つとは知らなかった。なかなか君の拵[こしら]いようは上等だ。いっそすっきりする。
　朔屋、息を吸え、そして大声叫んで見せろ。
　
　そして───
source.english:
Sakuya understood.

At last he understood.

Why you wanted someone like me. Wanted an existence that the whole world would reject.

The last tool made in hope of returning home: that was Sakuya. Then shout. Shout and make your existence known. Ah, perhaps he was not angry. Refreshed might be the word. He had never known that someone so utterly useless could be useful like this. You did quite a fine job making me. It was downright refreshing.

Sakuya, draw breath. Show them how loudly you can shout.

And—

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Naomasa, all of you───wow, this is amazing!」
【Naomasa】 「Well, honestly, I'm still not sure if I'm really as mad as you said I'd be. I'm nowhere near having a stroke here. But───」
【Naomasa】 「Yeah, I kind of feel like I finally get it. Right. That's really all, that's all I need to say.」
Sakuya understood. He finally understood. Why it was that you wanted him like this. Why you wanted an existence that seemed to be rejected by all of the world.

The final tool created with the hope of returning home: that was Sakuya. Then scream. Cry out your own existence, show it to the world. Ah, I see, apparently he isn't angry, so perhaps he feels more refreshed than anything? He never knew that a hopelessly useless existence like himself could be this useful. Your craftsmanship really is quite excellent. Might as well feel relieved. Sakuya sucked in a deep breath, then yelled out loudly. And then───

source.japanese:
この世界からも。
　弾かれてしまえ。
　この船と一緒に。
source.english:
Be cast out—

From this world too.

Together with this ship.

target.text: Just be rid of me already. From this world. Together with this ship.

source.japanese:
【直正】
「もう信天翁号が航海できる海なんて、
　この世界にはどこにもないんだ───！」
source.english:
“There's no sea left in this world
where the Albatross can sail!”

target.text: 【Naomasa】 「There aren't even any waters left in this world where the Albatross can still sail───!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「ああ───待ってた。
　その言葉。君が広げてくれた。
　この船の航路を」
source.english:
“Ah—I've been waiting.
For those words. You've opened up
this ship's course.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Aah───how I've waited. For those words. For you to use them. To clear the course for this ship to take.」

source.japanese: 朔屋の声が響いた瞬間、巨大なウミヒトは一瞬、身じろいだだろうか。もしこれに目があれば、汚物見るように朔屋を見ただろうか。貌があるなら、嫌悪にしかめて見せただろうか。
source.english: At the instant Sakuya's voice rang out, did the vast Sea Person stir for a moment? Had it eyes, would it have looked at Sakuya as at filth? Had it a face, would it have contorted it in disgust?

source.japanese: ゆっくりとウミヒトは海へと倒れる。ご丁寧に信天翁号が浮かぶ海に。
source.english: Slowly the Sea Person fell into the sea. Considerately, into the very sea where the Albatross floated.

source.japanese: ウミヒトの体はもとよりさらに海へと広がり、一面を埋め尽くしたかと見ると。
source.english: Its body spread still farther across the water. Just as it seemed to cover the whole expanse—

target.text: The moment that Sakuya's voice resounded, the gigantic Umihito stirred for just an instant, did it not? If it had eyes, surely it would have looked at Sakuya like he was filth. If it had a face, surely it would have twisted into a grimace in repugnance.
Slowly, the Umihito began to fall into the sea. And it was courteous enough to be certain to fall into the very part in which the Albatross was floating.
Not only did the Umihito's body spread further into the sea, it seemed as though it covered the entire surface.

source.japanese: 巨大な渦を巻き始めたのだ。
source.english: It began to form a vast whirlpool.

target.text: And began to form an enormous maelstrom.

source.japanese:
この、とてつもなく、心ひしぐほど奇怪である光景。けれどそのスケールだけは比類なく壮大な見物。
　海は魔性だった。空も魔性だった。
　ここまでの異界異妖の眺望を前に。
　クロは。
source.english:
An utterly, crushingly uncanny sight. Yet in scale alone, an incomparably magnificent spectacle.

The sea was demonic. The sky was demonic.

Before this view of another world, of monstrous strangeness—

Kuro—

target.text: This tremendous scene, one so outrageously bizarre it could crush the heart. But the sheer scale of it alone made it a spectacle of unparalleled and magnificent proportion. The sea was bewitching. The sky, too, was bewitching. Faced with a view this phantasmically unearthly. Kuro.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「ふわぁぁ……。
　どうして、あんなんなるの？
　どうしたら、海に穴があくの？」
source.english:
“Waaah…
Why does it turn into that?
How do you make a hole in the sea?”

source.japanese:
呪われて、取るに足りない存在に成り下がった、クロ。
　呪った者、その大本を辿ればウミヒトに行き着くのだろう。
　けれどもクロは。
source.english:
Kuro, cursed and reduced to a worthless existence.

Trace the one who cursed her back to the beginning, and one would probably reach the Sea People.

Yet Kuro—

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「あんな大きいうず……海の水、
　あそこから全部ながれてっちゃいそう」
source.english:
“A whirlpool that big…the seawater
looks like it'll all drain away through it.”

source.japanese: その呪ったモノと人の心の枠をたやすく踏み越える展望を前にしてなおクロは。
source.english: Even faced with the thing that had cursed her, and a prospect that so easily overstepped the bounds of the human mind, Kuro—

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Waaaow……. Why did it become like that? How did a hole open in the ocean?」
Kuro, cursed and degraded into a feeble, worthless existence. Are we to trace the origins of the man who cursed her, we will probably arrive at these Umihito. And yet, Kuro still.
【Kuro】 「A whirlpool that big……the water, looks like all the water in the sea would just flow down there.」
Even when faced with a spectacle that could so effortlessly breach the boundaries between that cursed being and the human heart, Kuro.

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「……なんか、見てるだけで、
　あたまがぽーってなってくるよ」
source.english:
“…Just looking at it
makes Kuro's head go all floaty.”

target.text: 【Kuro】 「……Feels like just looking at it makes Kuro's head start spinning.」

source.japanese:
【クロ】
「渦巻き、ぐるぐる……。
　怖い、怖いし、でもそれだけじゃない。
　なんか、すごい───」
source.english:
“Whirlpool, round and round…
It's scary. Scary, but not just that.
Somehow…it's amazing—”

source.japanese:
恐れては、いなかった。怯えてさえもいなかった。僅かな心の震えはあったかも知れない。けれどそれさえも、未知なるものへ飛びゆこうと逸る心を後押ししていた。
　
　この未曾有の大渦巻きを前にしてクロは。
クロの胸の中には。
　
　かつて空を翔[か]けていたその座から転落して以来、同時に萎[な]え饐[す]えていたもう一つの翼、未知なる地へ求めて飛ぼうとする飽くなき好奇心。
　それが今、クロの中に再来していた。
source.english:
Was not afraid. Not even frightened. There might have been a slight trembling in her heart, but even that urged on her eagerness to fly into the unknown.

Before this unprecedented maelstrom—

Within Kuro's heart—

Since falling from the place where she once soared through the sky, another wing too had withered and soured: her insatiable curiosity, her desire to fly in search of unknown lands.

Now it had returned.

target.text: 【Kuro】 「Swirling around, round and round……. Scary, it's scary, but that's not all it is. It's kind of amazing───」

Terrified she was not. Not even frightened was she. Perhaps her heart trembled ever so slightly. But even that only encouraged her excited heart to leap into the great unknown. Confronted with this maelstrom of unprecedented scale, Kuro. Inside Kuro's bosom. Ever since she had fallen from grace, from the sky she once soared through, there was another pair of wings that had also withered and rotted away: the insatiable curiosity that once made her want to fly off in pursuit of unknown lands. Right now, those wings were resurfacing within Kuro.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「───言葉もねえ。こりゃあ───」
source.english: “—No words. This is—”

source.japanese:
それから、シサムとキサラ。
　この二つにして一つの、大胆不敵の魂。
　───けれども、恐れる魂。
　それが今。
source.english:
And then, Sisam and Kisara.

This fearless soul, two and yet one.

—Yet a soul that feared.

Now—

target.text: 【Kisara】 「───Words fail me. This is───」
And then, there were Shisamu and Kisara. These two souls as one, bold and dauntless. ───Yet souls that knew fear. And right now.

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「確かにこの大渦巻き、これの底がどこか別の場所に繋がっているって言うの、信じちまいそうになるわ」
source.english: “Seeing this maelstrom, I could really believe its bottom connects to somewhere else.”

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「Sure, if you told me the bottom of this massive maelstrom connected to some other place, I might just come to believe you.」

source.japanese:
【シサム】
「保つのか、この船……なんて、今さら考えんのも馬鹿馬鹿しいや。もう笑えてきたさ」
source.english: “Will this ship hold together…? It's ridiculous even thinking about that now. I'm starting to laugh.”

source.japanese:
世界を牢獄だと。
　自分達をセント・エルモの灯りの伝説として縛り付けようとする世界を恐れて、抜け出さんと三位一体者という伝説を求めた彼女達。
source.english:
They had feared the world as a prison.
A world that sought to bind them to the legend of St. Elmo's fire. To escape, they had sought the legend of the Triune One.

source.japanese:
けれど、双子は今、そんな腑抜け逃げを打とうとした、あの時の自分達の心を拳と蹴りで形変わるまで叩き直したい気分に一杯だ。
　それは凶暴なまでの、冒険心。
source.english:
But now the twins wanted to beat and kick their former selves into a different shape for trying such a spineless escape.

It was a spirit of adventure fierce enough to be violent.

target.text: 【Shisamu】 「But is this ship going to last…… nah, what a silly thing to worry about at this point. I'm already laughing.」

The world is a prison, they said. The women who fear the world that is trying to confine them as the legend of St. Elmo's fire, who in an attempt to break free of it pursued the legend of the Triune Being.

However, right now, those twins were filled with the desire to beat their spirit, their nature that had made them try to run away from it all in such a cowardly manner back then, back into shape with fists and kicks. It was a spirit so adventurous it became barbarous.

source.japanese:
【キサラ】
「こんなんに飛びこんでみようてえ気違いは、あたしらくらい……いいね、いいよ、こういうの。
　こいつは素敵だ、素敵すぎて踊り出したくなる」
source.english:
“We're about the only lunatics who'd jump into something like this…yes, I like it. This sort of thing.
It's wonderful. So wonderful I want to dance.”

source.japanese:
双子の心は、今更ながらに想い出してある。
　あの閉塞した邑[ムラ]を燃やし尽くして後にしたあの日。胸に灯った炎の種。セント・エルモの灯火なる、押しつけの灯ではない自分達だけの炎。
　その炎は先から教えていたではないか。
　前に、前に、前に！
　求めるものは前にこそ。
　後を向いて何が得られる。
source.english:
At last the twins' hearts remembered.

The day they burned that stifling village and left it behind. The seed of flame kindled in their breasts. Not a light imposed upon them as St. Elmo's fire, but their own flame.

Hadn't that flame been telling them all along?

Forward, forward, forward!

What you seek lies ahead.

What will looking back gain you?

source.japanese:
今だって、見よ。
　セント・エルモの火だの三位一体者だの、しょぼくれた伝説は後にしようとする世界のもの。
　新たな世界に通ずる大渦巻きは船の前に、進む針路に。
source.english:
Look, even now.

St. Elmo's fire, the Triune One: those dreary legends belonged to the world they were leaving behind.

The maelstrom leading to a new world lay before the ship, upon her course.

source.japanese:
燃える、燃え立つ、心が。
　腕を脚をどうしようもなく震わせる。
　こんな素敵な事に、なんでじっとしていられよう。
source.english:
Their hearts burned, blazed.

Arms and legs trembled beyond control.

How could they stay still before something this wonderful?

target.text: 【Kisara】 「Guess we're the only ones mad enough to dare plunge into something like that……that's good, I like this kind of thing. This is fantastic, it's so incredibly great it makes me want to break into dance.」

The twins remembered that spirit anew. That day, after they had burned that closed-off village to ash and left it all behind. The seed of flame that lit in their bosom. Not what would become St. Elmo's fire, the fire that was imposed upon them, but a flame of their very own. Had this flame not been telling them this all along? Forwards, forwards, forwards! What you seek lies before you. What is there to gain from looking back?

Even now. Behold. St. Elmo's fire and the Triune Being, those miserable legends are all of the world that you are leaving behind. The great maelstrom that leads to a new world lies before this ship, on the course she is taking.
Their burning, blazing hearts. Made their arms and legs tremble helplessly. How could they simply sit still when faced with something so wonderful?

source.japanese:
かつ、信天翁号のあちこちで。
　上甲板であったり、船内通路であったり、機関室であったり、船底倉庫であったり、船の至る所で。
source.english:
And throughout the Albatross—

On the upper deck, in the passages, in the engine room, in the hold. Everywhere aboard her.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「……凄いねえ。僕らもいろんなところ、航海してきたけど」
source.english: “…It's amazing. We've sailed all sorts of places, but—”

source.japanese: 畝傍と命名された船が、この海にやってきて、信天翁号という名前が何時しか被さって、そして同じように何時しか船内に現れるようになった下級水夫達。
source.english: The ship named Unebi came to these seas. At some point the name Albatross was laid over hers. And likewise, at some point, the junior sailors began appearing aboard.

source.japanese: 彼らは、畝傍の船霊の霊威に引かれて出てきたのだろうか。いずれにしても彼らなくしては、信天翁が立ちゆかない縁の下の（あるいは、甲板下の）力持ちである彼ら。
source.english: Had they emerged, drawn by the spiritual power of Unebi's ship's spirit? Whatever the case, without them the Albatross could not function. Her unsung pillars of support—beneath the floor, or beneath the deck.

target.text: Meanwhile, all over the Albatross. On the upper deck, in the ship's passageways, in the engine room, in the hold at the bottom, all throughout the ship.
【Deck boy】 「……Incredible, isn't it? We've sailed to all kinds of places, but.」
The ship christened as the Unebi had come to this sea, been given the name of the Albatross at some point, and then the deck boys had begun to appear within the ship at a similarly uncertain point.

They must have emerged after being drawn to the mysterious power of the Unebi's Funadama. Regardless, without their presence, the Albatross would not be able to maintain her voyage, and the unsung heroes behind the scenes (or perhaps below decks) were none other than them.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「こんな景色は、さすがに初めてだ……」
source.english: “We've never seen anything like this…”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Yeah, this is definitely the first time I've seen a sight like this……」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「この船、保つのかなぁ……？」
source.english: “Will this ship hold together…?”

source.japanese:
彼らもまた、この景色に驚嘆し、中には恐れる者もいたけれど。
　けれど彼らは揺るがない。
source.english:
They too marveled at this scene; some were afraid.

Yet they did not waver.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「I don't know, can this ship reeeally withstand this……?」
They, too, were awestruck by this scenery, and there were some amongst them who feared it. Yet none of them wavered.

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「まあどうにかなるよ。今までだってそうだったし、これからだってきっとそうさ」
source.english: “We'll manage somehow. We always have. I'm sure we will from now on too.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Well, it'll all work out somehow. That's how it's always been until now, and I'm sure it'll keep being that way.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「だね。どっちにしたって、僕達は自分のお仕事、するだけだ」
source.english: “Right. Either way, we just have to do our jobs.”

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Right? Whatever happens, we just do our jobs.」

source.japanese:
【下級水夫】
「うん、さ、みんな、持ち場についてようよ」
source.english: “Yes. Come on, everyone. Let's get to our posts.”

source.japanese:
自分達の家である信天翁号の為に、揺るがない。揺るがないけれど。
　皆それぞれ持ち場に走る前に。
　上甲板の舷側から。船内の丸い船窓から。
　大渦巻きを覗きこんで、皆一様に浮かべた笑みは、少年らしい感動に満ち満ちて。
　なにしろ彼らだって、この不敵な阿呆船、信天翁号の一部である事には、変わりないのだから。
source.english:
For the Albatross, their home, they would not waver. They would not waver, but—

Before they each ran to their posts—

From the rail of the upper deck, from round portholes within the ship—

They looked into the maelstrom. Every smile was brimming with boyish wonder.

For they, too, remained part of this fearless ship of folly, the Albatross.

target.text: 【Deck boy】 「Yeah. Alright everybody, let's head to our stations.」

On behalf of the Albatross, the ship that was their very own home, they would not waver. They did not waver, but. Before they all raced to their respective stations. Over the ship's side on the upper deck. Through the round portholes inside the ship. They peered into the great maelstrom, the smiles that surfaced on all of their faces brimming with boyish excitement. After all, they were still a part of this intrepid ship of fools, the Albatross.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「素晴らしいわ───なんて、壮麗。
　これを見られただけでも、乗り合わせた甲斐があったというもの」
source.english:
“Wonderful—how magnificent.
Seeing this alone has made it worthwhile to be aboard.”

source.japanese:
更に、泪。
　己の愛を、己が長らえる為に殺してしまった人魚姫。
source.english:
And Rui.

The mermaid princess who killed her love to preserve her own life.

source.japanese:
その手を血に濡らしてしまった事に、今更許しを求めようとは思わない。
　生も死も、抱えて世界を巡るうちに鈍磨してしまって。
　そしてまたこの世界は、彼女が知る限り海も陸も閉ざされていて。
　人々はそれと気づいていないのだろうが、実に様々な物語に取り囲まれて、あやされ続けていた。世界を閉ざしているのは、平面上の世界観だけでない。
source.english:
She had no thought of seeking forgiveness now for having stained her hands with blood.

As she wandered the world bearing life and death alike, she had grown numb.

And as far as she knew, this world was sealed shut on sea and land alike.

Its people likely never noticed, but they lived ringed about by stories of every kind, forever rocked and soothed by them. Nor was it only a flat conception of the world that kept it sealed.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Wonderful───what magnificence. Even just being given the chance to see this has made sailing with you worthwhile.」
Furthermore, Rui. The mermaid princess who killed her own love in order to ensure her own survival.

By now, even the thought of desiring forgiveness for having stained those hands with blood was long gone. While she roamed the world with life and death cradled in her arms, the feeling faded and dulled. Furthermore, as far as she knew, the sea and the land alike of this world are kept under lock and key. The people at large surely do not realize it, but they are surrounded by a wide variety of tales, ever dandled. It is not just the view that the world is flat that is closing off the world.

source.japanese:
なにかというと繰り返される伝説と、物語とが、人々の心をぬるま湯の揺籃に沈めてしまっている。
　そこに新たな物語が産まれる余地はない。
　愛を失った人魚姫。悲哀が胸を蝕んだのも、遠い昔。うち続く遊歴の日々が、泪に与えたものは、果てしない退屈と、鈍磨していく心と。そんな生の軌跡は、人魚の乙女を肉の快楽だけを信ずる退嬰の貴婦人となした。
source.english:
Legends and stories, repeated at every turn, sank people's hearts into a lukewarm cradle.

There was no room for a new story to be born.

The mermaid princess who lost her love. It was long ago that sorrow had eaten at her heart. Endless days of travel had given Rui boundless boredom and a heart growing numb. Such a course of life turned the mermaid maiden into a noblewoman in retreat from life, who believed only in the pleasures of the flesh.

source.japanese:
けれどもそんな人魚姫が、今この時は、ただ眼前に広がる景色に、心を湧き立たせている。無邪気だった遠い娘時代のように、単純な感動に手を打ち鳴らしている。
　まだまだ世の中には、こんな不思議で妖しい景色が残っている。
source.english:
Yet now this mermaid princess's heart leaped at nothing more than the view before her. As in her distant, innocent girlhood, she clapped her hands in simple wonder.

The world still had strange and uncanny sights like this.

source.japanese: 長年の退屈でさえ、一息で吹き飛ばしてしまうほどのこの眺め。
source.english: A view that could sweep away even years of boredom in a breath.

target.text: Legends and stories repeated again and again at every opportunity, lowering the hearts of the people into a cradle of complacent, uneventful comfort. There is no room for new stories to be born there. The mermaid princess bereaved of her love. Even the grief gnawing at her heart was a thing of the distant past. All that those endless days of touring the world had given Rui was endless boredom and a dulling heart. A trajectory through life that had turned a mermaid maiden into an unadventurous lady of high society who only believed in the carnal pleasures.

But even that mermaid princess, in this moment, from watching the scenery unfolding before her eyes alone, felt something welling up in her heart. Like in those distant days of girlhood spent in innocence, she was clapping her hands out of pure excitement. There yet remain sights this mysteriously bewitching out there in the world.
It was a view so spectacular, it could blow away her long years of boredom with a single breath.

source.japanese:
【泪】
「ふふっ、うふふっ、
　よくってよ、よくってよ貴女。
　少しだけ貴女を好きになれそうよ」
source.english:
“Hehe, ufufu.
Very good. Very good, my dear.
I might begin to like you just a little.”

source.japanese: 悪くない、どころかとてもとても素敵だ、こんな素敵な事を隠していたなんてずるい、と泪の心は娘時代の感動と侠[きゃん]に沸き立って、密航者に抱擁さえ送りたい、華やいだ気分で一杯になっている、満たされている。
source.english: Not merely acceptable—very, very wonderful. It was unfair to have hidden something so wonderful. Rui's heart bubbled with the wonder and spirit of her girlhood. She even wanted to embrace the stowaway. Bright delight filled her, filled her utterly.

target.text: 【Rui】 「Huhu, uhuhu, well done, my dear, very well done. I think I might just grow a little fond of you.」

Not bad, or rather, it was absolutely wonderful, why, hiding something this spectacular simply wasn't fair, Rui thought, her heart boiling excitedly with the emotions and pert tomboyishness of her girlhood, even wanting to embrace the stowaway in her arms, filled with bright cheer, fulfilled by it.

source.japanese: あるいは、船に乗り合わせる男達。
source.english: Or the men aboard the ship.

source.japanese:
どすんどすんとプレス機はだしの分厚く重い足で船内通路を駆け巡っている水夫長は、下級水夫にあれこれ怒鳴りつけながらも、その目が船窓に向かってしまうのが止まらない、止められない。
　しまいには観念して、ええいと一呻[うめ]き。
source.english:
The boatswain pounded through the passages on thick, heavy feet that put a press to shame. While roaring this and that at the junior sailors, he could not stop his eyes turning toward the portholes.

At last he surrendered, with a growl.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「ええい！　待っていてくれろお前ら。
　ちょっとだけ俺に時間をよこせ、
　そのちょっとだけ、お前たちだけで、
　船を保たせい！」
source.english:
“Damn it! Wait, you lot.
Give me just a moment.
For that little moment, keep the ship going
by yourselves!”

source.japanese:
自分達の長がなにを考えているかなぞ、それこそ以心伝心なのが下級水夫君達、だからこそ彼らは大いにぶうたれてみせる。
　本当は少しくらいだったら全然平気と笑顔で送り出したいところ、水夫長には恥も外聞もあるを知っているから、その面目を保たせる為に、あえて不満顔で送り出す。
　水夫長は水夫長で、少年達がそうと知って文句を零しているのを覚っている。奇妙な交感がここにある。
source.english:
The junior sailors knew their leader's thoughts without a word. Precisely because they knew, they grumbled loudly.

Really, they wanted to send him off smiling: a little while would be quite fine. But they knew the boatswain had his pride and appearances to consider, so they deliberately looked dissatisfied as they let him go, preserving his dignity.

The boatswain, in turn, knew that the boys complained because they understood. A strange communion existed here.

source.japanese:
とにかく大急ぎで、自分の船室から取ってきたのが古い単行本、表題には、
　
『Ｔｈｅ　Ｎａｒｒａｔｉｖｅ　ｏｆ　
　Ａｒｔｈｕｒ　Ｇｏｒｄｏｎ　Ｐｙｍ
　ｏｆ　Ｎａｎｔｕｃｋｅｔ』
　
　とずらずら長い文字の列、を、指先でなぞって上甲板へ、見晴らしの良いところへ。
source.english:
At any rate, he hurried to his cabin and fetched an old book. Upon its cover, the title:

The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket.

Tracing that long line of letters with a fingertip, he went up to the upper deck, to a place with a good view.

target.text: Or perhaps, the menfolk aboard the ship.

Running about the ship's passageways with weighty thuds, feet thick and heavy enough to put a pressing machine to shame, was the Bosun, who, while shouting orders about this and that at the deck boys, could not stop his eyes from drifting towards the portholes; he just couldn't stop them. At last, he resigned himself, and with a loud groan.
【Bosun】 「Aargh! Wait for me, lads. Just give me a little bit of time. For just a little while, you boys will have to keep this ship running by yourselves!」

The deck boys in particular had a tacit understanding of what exactly their boss was thinking here, which is also precisely why they made a deliberate showing of their displeasure. In truth, they wanted to tell him that if it really was just a bit of time, then they'd be completely fine, a smile on their lips, but the Bosun had both a reputation and an appearance to uphold, and so to let him save face, they deliberately let him go with a discontent look. For the Bosun's part, he also knew that the boys were only complaining because they knew that. There was a peculiar rapport between them.

In any case, in a great hurry, he retrieved an old volume from his own cabin, the title reading: 『The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket』 After tracing that long stream of letters with a fingertip, he went to the upper deck, to somewhere with a good view.

source.japanese:
そうして水夫長は、龍の親爺は、女達と同じように、この幻妖にして瑰麗な光景に向かって、顔の半分を牙だらけの口にして、半面の龍も跳びださんばかりにうねらせて、叫ぶのだ。
　本の頁をざっと捲[めく]って風にばたつかせて、それでもお気に入りの場面だからすぐにそこに落ち着いて、眺めと頁に半々目を遣りながら、叫ぶのだ。
source.english:
And then the boatswain, Old Long, shouted at that phantasmal, jewel-bright spectacle just as the women had. His fang-filled mouth took up half his face; the dragon on the other half writhed as though it might leap free.

He rifled through the book, its pages flapping in the wind. But this was his favorite passage, and the book soon fell open to it. His gaze darting between spectacle and page, he shouted.

target.text: And like that, the Bosun, old man Long, just like the women, turning to face this sight both bewilderingly magical and exceptionally gorgeous, half his face forming a mouth full of fangs, the dragon covering one side of it undulating as if about to fly out from the skin, screamed. He quickly flipped through the book, the wind rustling the pages, but still, it was his favourite scene, and so he landed on it right away; with his eyes half on the view and half on the pages, he screamed.

source.japanese:
【水夫長】
「凄ぇ！　大渦巻きってな、本当にあったんだなあ！」
source.english: “Amazing! Maelstroms really do exist!”

source.japanese:
けれど、茹だった禿頭を風になぶらせていたのはしばし、ほんの数呼吸、それで景色を飲みつくして、船内に駆け戻っていく。
　こんな光景にぶち当たるのだから、やっぱりこの船の船員はやめられない、と。
source.english:
But he let the wind play upon his heated bald head only briefly. A few breaths, enough to drink in the whole view, and he ran back inside.

When sights like this awaited them, how could he ever stop being a sailor aboard this ship?

target.text: 【Bosun】 「AMAZING! The maelstrom is ACTUALLY REAL!」

However, after letting the wind blow over his boiling bald head for just a short while, only for a moment or two, he had finished drinking in the scenery, and so he ran back down below decks. All while thinking that it was precisely because he would run into spectacles like this one that he couldn't quite quit being a member of this ship's crew.

source.japanese:
水夫長とくれば機関長の事も忘れてはならない。
　ただこの機関室の長は、状況がどうであれ、船の底の熱い暗がりからは離れず、下級水夫達を物静かに督励している。
　ふと立ち上がって物音に耳を澄ますような仕草を見せたりするけれど、それでも主罐の前からは離れず、いつものように紅茶を入れたりの、なにも気に留めてもいないよう。
source.english:
Having mentioned the boatswain, one must not forget the chief engineer.

But whatever the circumstances, this master of the engine room did not leave the hot darkness at the ship's bottom. He quietly urged the junior sailors on.

Sometimes he stood, appearing to listen closely to some sound. Even then he never left the main boilers. He made tea as usual, seemingly concerned by nothing.

source.japanese: ただ───今し淹れたばかりの熱い紅茶の面が───ずずずず、と渦巻いて、規模こそ極微なれど、それは船の針路に口を開ける大渦巻きと同期している。
source.english: Only—the surface of the hot tea he had just brewed—swirled and swirled. Tiny though its scale was, it moved in synchrony with the maelstrom gaping in the ship's course.

target.text: And if we speak of the Bosun, then we must also not forget the Chief Engineer. However, the master of this engine room, no matter what the situation may be, never leaves the warm darkness of the bottom of the ship, calmly supervising the deck boys. He would suddenly stand up, his mannerisms suggesting he was straining his ears at some sound, but even so, he did not move from where he stood in front of the boiler, brewing his black tea as usual, not seeming to pay any heed to anything.

However───the surface of the warm black tea he had just finished brewing ───was swirling around, and while the scale was microscopic in comparison, it was perfectly synchronized with the gaping maelstrom that had opened on the ship's course.

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「ほう……どうやら海は、大渦巻きか。しかし些[いささ]かその……困る」
source.english: “Oh…apparently, a maelstrom at sea. But this is somewhat…troublesome.”

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「Humm……it would seem a maelstrom has formed in the ocean? However, that is slightly, well……troubling.」

source.japanese:
【機関長】
「どういう作用の故かは判らないが、
　これではお茶が飲めない」
source.english:
“I don't know what causes it,
but I can't drink my tea like this.”

source.japanese:
機関長、ロックフォール・王。
　陽があるうちに上甲板に揚がったのは割と先日の事。また暫くはその必要もないと考える機関の魔術師。何処にあろうと、彼は己のなすべき事を知っているから、今はただ、主罐の火ばかりを、眺めている。
source.english:
The chief engineer, Roquefort Wang.

It was only the other day that this magician of machinery had come up to the upper deck in daylight. He thought he would have no need to do so again for a while. Wherever he was, he knew what he ought to do. For now, he merely watched the fire in the main boilers.

target.text: 【Chief Engineer】 「I know not what forces are to blame, but I cannot drink my tea like this.」

The Chief Engineer, Roquefort Wan. It was relatively recent that he had gone up on the upper deck while the sun was still out. That would not be necessary for some time to come, thought the wizard of engines. Wherever he may find himself, he knows exactly what he himself must do, and right now, it is to observe the fire in the main boiler and nothing else.

source.japanese: 智里と宗右衛門猫は、良い感じに安酒も廻り腹もくちくなっているので、一人と一匹で、酒場のお姉さん達の区画でぐうぴい眠っている。この超然とした一人と一匹は、数多の物語知るもの故に、今は酒と女にたっぷり囲まれた豪勢な眠りを貪り、次の物語の巡りに、備えている。
source.english: Tomosato and Soemon the cat, pleasantly warmed by cheap liquor and with full bellies, lay snoring in the barmaids' quarter. Aloof, this man and this cat knew many stories. Now they feasted upon a lavish sleep, surrounded by plenty of liquor and women, preparing for the next story's turn.

target.text: Tomosato and Souemon the cat were enjoying the pleasant buzz of cheap drink and full stomachs, man and animal snoring away in the section occupied by the bar girls. These two, transcendental man and animal, aloof from the world, knew a great number of stories themselves, and consequently, they were now indulging in luxurious sleep while surrounded by plentiful women and booze, preparing for the next story that would come their way.

source.japanese:
そして───密航者。
　かつて畝傍と呼ばれた、船の魂。
　彷徨い続けた孤高の魂。
　けれども、今は。
source.english:
And—the stowaway.

The soul of the ship once called Unebi.

The solitary soul that had wandered endlessly.

But now—

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あれが、あそこが。この航海の目的の！
　大渦巻き───メイルシュトローム！」
source.english:
“There! That's where this voyage leads!
The great whirlpool—the maelstrom!”

target.text: And finally───the stowaway. The soul of the ship once known as the Unebi. A proudly independent soul doomed ever to wander. However, right now.
【Stowaway】 「There, right over there. That's the goal of this voyage! The great whirlpool─── the Maelstrom!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あの大渦の中に、私は行くんだ。
　あれが地球へ続く、ただ一つの道。
　海の底まで続いているような大渦だけど」
source.english:
“I'm going into that great vortex.
The only way to Earth.
It looks like it goes all the way to the bottom of the sea.”

source.japanese:
そう、彼女は往く。
　けれども往くのは、彼女だけではない。
　ここに、航海を共にする者達あるからこそ。
source.english:
Yes, she would go.

But she was not going alone.

Because here were those who shared her voyage.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「I am going into that great whirlpool. That is the one and only path that leads to Earth. It is a maelstrom so vast it seems to lead to the very bottom of the sea, but.」
Indeed, she was going. But she was not the only one. For there were others here who shared this voyage with her.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「心配しないで。みんながいる。
　それなら私は、この船を往[ゆ]かせてみせる！　だって私はこの船の───魂なんだから」
source.english:
“Don't worry. Everyone's here.
Then I'll make this ship go! Because I am this ship's—soul.”

source.japanese:
大渦巻きの彼方から、ほんの僅かに、匂いの粒子にして、数えられるくらいの数なのに。
　それを感じた瞬間に。
　体を構成する要素、心を織り上げる想いの数々、全てが───
　打ち震えた。
　恐いくらいの。
　目を覆って泣き叫びたいくらいの。
　それは、喜び、歓喜、狂喜。
　その迸[ほとばし]り。
source.english:
From beyond the maelstrom, so little: a countable handful of particles of scent.

Yet the instant she sensed it—

Every element of her body, every feeling that wove her heart—

Trembled.

Almost frighteningly.

Enough to make her want to cover her eyes and cry out.

Joy, delight, ecstasy.

Its surge.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Do not be concerned. We are all here. Then I shall make this ship sail forth! For I am this ship ───her very soul.」

From beyond the maelstrom came particles of scent, ever so faint, so few they could be counted with her fingers, and yet. The instant she sensed that. The components that formed her body, the numerous emotions that weaved together her heart, all of it─── Trembled. So intensely it was frightening. It made her want to cover her eyes from it, to wail and scream. It was joy, delight, ecstasy. A bursting flood of it.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だからみんな、恐れないで、目を逸らさないで」
source.english: “So everyone, don't be afraid. Don't look away.”

source.japanese:
自分に言い聞かせる。
　皆にも呼びかける。
　けれど、船霊である彼女。
　人間の、判っていない事がまだあって。
source.english:
She told herself.

She called to them all.

Yet she, a ship's spirit,

Still had things to learn about humans.

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「So all of you, be not afraid, do not avert your eyes.」
She was convincing herself. And summoning all the others. However, the girl is a Funadama. There is still much of mankind she does not comprehend.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「みんなで航海の果てを、見よう───！」
source.english: “Let's all see the end of this voyage—!”

source.japanese:
そんな事など言わずとも。
　皆は、見るのだ、味わうのだ、飲み干し尽くすのだ。全身に受けとめるのだ。
source.english:
Without any need to say so—

They would see it. Taste it. Drink it dry. Receive it with their whole bodies.

source.japanese: この航海の果てを───！
source.english: The end of this voyage—!

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「Let us all together bear witness to the end of this voyage───!」
You didn't need to say all that. They are all looking, tasting it, drinking it in to the last drop. Accepting it with body and soul.
The end of this voyage───!

source.japanese: 「さあ、大見得を切ろう───」
source.english: “Come. Let's strike a grand pose—”

target.text: 「Now, let us strike a grand pose and declare it───」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「───マスト展開───！」
source.english: “—Deploy masts—!”

source.japanese: 密航者が腰の革鞄を開け放つと、信天翁号の甲板に縦に並んで三つのマストが天に向かって高々と現れる。
source.english: The stowaway threw open the leather bag at her waist. Three masts appeared in a line along the Albatross's deck, towering high toward heaven.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「フォア！
　メイン！
　ミズン！」
source.english:
“Fore!
Main!
Mizzen!”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「畝傍に立っていた、
　そしてこっちに来て失われていた、
　三本の帆柱───取り戻したぞ」
source.english:
“The three masts that stood aboard Unebi,
that were lost when I came here—
I've got them back!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「───Step the masts───!」
When the stowaway flung open the leather bag at her waist, three masts lined up from bow to stern on the deck of the Albatross materialized, reaching high into the heavens.
【Stowaway】 「Fore! Main! Mizzen!」
【Stowaway】 「What once stood tall on the Unebi, and was then lost when I came to this world, the three masts─── I took them back.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「風よし、帆、全展開！」
source.english: “Good wind! Set every sail!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「The wind is good, unfurl all the sails!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「私が選んだあなた達、そして君」
source.english: “All of you I chose. And you.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「All of you chosen by me, and you as well.」

source.japanese:
振り仰ぐ。
　
　ついに、この世界に来る前の姿を取り戻した信天翁号、真っ直ぐにそそり立つ三本の帆柱に差し渡される帆桁より下ろされた帆は、はち切れんほどの風をはらむ。
　
　
　振り返る。
　
　己が裡[うち]に集った者どもを。方舟より飛び立って戻らなかった烏、船乗り達の聖火にして完全への昇華を拒[こば]んだ双子、愛する王子の胸突いた人魚姫、道より外れてこの船に流れ着いた者達。
source.english:
She looked up.

At last the Albatross had regained the form she had before coming to this world. Sails lowered from the yards spanning her three straight, towering masts filled with wind almost to bursting.

She looked back.

At those gathered within her. The crow that flew from the ark and did not return. The twins, sailors' sacred fire, who refused sublimation into perfection. The mermaid princess who pierced her beloved prince's breast. Those who strayed from the path and drifted to this ship.

target.text: She looked up. At long last, the Albatross had regained the shape she held before coming to this world, her sails, lowered from the yards spanning the three towering masts, so filled with wind they seemed about to be torn off.

She looked back. At those who had gathered within her. The crow who had flown away from the ark to never return; the twins who rejected sublimation into perfection as the sacred fire of sailors around the world; the mermaid princess who pierced her beloved prince's heart; all those who had strayed from their path and ended up on this ship.

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「セントエルモの双子の灯は航海を守り、
　ノアの烏は嵐を飛んで、
　人魚姫は快楽を言祝ぐ───そして」
source.english:
“The twin flames of St. Elmo guard the voyage.
Noah's crow flies through the storm.
The mermaid princess blesses pleasure—and—”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「St. Elmo's twin fires protect our voyage, Noah's crow flies through the storm, the mermaid princess celebrates pleasure─── and finally.」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「君。見ているね、君。
　私が翼を広げた姿を、見ていたね」
source.english:
“You. You're watching, aren't you?
You saw me with my wings spread.”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「You. You're looking, aren't you? You saw me spread my wings, right?」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「あの夜、あんなふやけきった夜の中でも、見つけてくれたね、ねえ私の君───！」
source.english: “That night, even in a night so sodden, you found me. Didn't you, my own—!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「That night, even in that limp, bloated night, you found me, didn't you, my beloved───!」

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「君が見つけてくれたから。
　つばさだ、と認めてくれたから」
source.english:
“With a woman at her prow like a figurehead, black hair streaming like the wings of an albatross. A pair of St.
Elmo's fires upon her masts, the eyes of the crow that endured the Great Flood in her wheelhouse, and the mermaid princess held within her—”

source.japanese:
【密航者】
「だったら飛ぼう、海を離れて、この世界を離れて、飛んでみせるよ、船だって飛ぶさ！」
source.english: “Then let's fly. Away from the sea, away from this world. I'll show you. Even a ship can fly!”

target.text: 【Stowaway】 「It is all because you found me there. Because you recognized me as a pair of wings.」
【Stowaway】 「So let us fly off then, leave this sea, leave this world, show them we can fly, that even a ship can fly!」

source.japanese: 巨影をかわし、信天翁号は荒れ狂い渦を巻く海面から、遂に舞い上がるは、宙空へ。
source.english: Evading the vast shadow, the Albatross at last rose from the raging, swirling sea—into the air.

target.text: Evading the titanic figure, the Albatross finally flew high from the violently churning surface of the sea, taking into the empty skies.

source.japanese: 飛べ───信天翁号
source.english: Fly—Albatross.

source.japanese: 黒髪をまさしく信天翁の翼のごとくたなびかせた少女を、フイギュアヘッドのように舳先に置き、マストには一対のセントエルモの火、操舵室には大洪水を耐えたカラスの目、そして人魚の姫君を懐に抱き───
source.english: With a girl at her prow like a figurehead, black hair streaming like the wings of an albatross. A pair of St. Elmo's fires upon her masts, the eyes of the crow that endured the Great Flood in her wheelhouse, and the mermaid princess held within her—

source.japanese:
同胞達も共に翔ぼう。
　黒に縁取られた白い翼で。
　風に怯むことなく、乗りこなして。
source.english:
Let our fellows soar with us too.

On white wings edged in black.

Uncowed by the wind, riding it.

target.text: Fly───Albatross.

The girl whose black hair flowed in the wind like it truly were the wings of the Albatross stood on the bow like a figurehead, the pair of St. Elmo's fires on the masts, the eyes of a crow who had braved the Great Flood in the wheelhouse, and the imperial princess of the mermaids held to her bosom───
Come fly with me, brothers and sisters. On wings of white fringed with black. Not afeared of the wind, but riding on it.

source.japanese: 跳べ───信天翁号。
source.english: Leap—Albatross.

source.japanese: この停滞し、緩みきった海と陸地に居場所を持たぬ、奇矯不屈の魂宿した者たちを乗せて。
source.english: Bearing those with eccentric, indomitable souls, with no place amid these stagnant, slackened seas and lands.

target.text: Leap───Albatross.
Take on board they who harbour souls both eccentric and indomitable, they with no place to call their own in this stagnant, flaccid land and sea.

source.japanese: 翔べ───信天翁号！
source.english: Soar—Albatross!

source.japanese: かつて、何時からか、そしてこれからも何時までも、閉ざされたるこの牢獄、平面世界から、お前が本来在るべき世界へ───！
source.english: From this prison, this flat world—sealed at some forgotten hour and to remain so forevermore—into the world where you truly belong—!

target.text: Soar───Albatross!
From this flat world, sealed off long ago from time immemorial and forever more hitherto, into the world where you rightfully belong───!

source.japanese: 「───体がどれだけ壊れても───」
source.english: “—However broken my body becomes—”

source.japanese: 「───またマストが失われても───」
source.english: “—Even if my masts are lost again—”

source.japanese: 「───くそったれな奴らに───」
source.english: “—For you damned creatures—”

source.japanese: 「───くそったれで最高な───」
source.english: “—Damned and wonderful—”

source.japanese: 「───最高で、大好きな───」
source.english: “—Wonderful, and dearly loved—”
“—Dearly loved—”

target.text: 「───No matter how my body may break───」
「───Even should my masts be lost to me once more───」
「───To these shitheads───」
「───The greatest shitheads───」
「───The greatest, my beloved───」
「───My beloved───」

source.japanese: 「あなた達に、君に」
source.english: “All of you. And you.”

source.japanese: 「とっておきの」
source.english: “Our treasured stores—”

source.japanese: 「酒と煙草と火薬の一切合切を」
source.english: “Liquor, tobacco, gunpowder—every last bit.”

source.japanese: 「ぶちまけよう。祝福のために」
source.english: “Let's let it all fly. In celebration.”

target.text: 「To all of you, and you」
「Let's take all that we've saved up」
「All the booze, tobacco, and gunpowder, lock, stock, and barrel」
「And dump it all out. To celebrate.」

source.japanese: 「信天翁！」
source.english: “Albatross!”

target.text: 「Albatross!」

source.japanese:
信天翁号は飛び立った。
　
　海流渦巻いて流れ落ちるその中心へ。
　要らぬものどもを突き落とす、この世界の排泄口の中を、飛ぶ。
　この世界に必要だった、悪意の受け皿として望まれた信天翁号が。
　くそったれと叫んで、自ら望んで飛び込んだのだ。
source.english:
The Albatross took flight.

Into the center, where the currents swirled and fell.

Through this world's drain, where it cast down whatever it did not want.

The Albatross, needed by this world, wanted as a vessel for its malice.

She had shouted, ‘Fuck you,’ and plunged in of her own will.

source.japanese:
古来、世界に果てを造った者はみな、そこに嵐と、落ちれば二度と上がってはこれない深い穴を置く。
　切り立つ断崖絶壁では、人は希望を込めてよじ登ろうとしてしまうから、永遠に落ち続ける果てを造るのだ。
source.english:
Since ancient times, everyone who made an edge to the world placed storms there, and a deep hole from which the fallen could never climb back.

Give people sheer cliffs and they will try to scale them with hope. So the makers made an edge where one fell forever.

target.text: The Albatross took off. Right into the middle of where the ocean currents swirled and flowed down. She flew, into the drain hole of this world, where all things deemed unnecessary are thrust down. The Albatross, indispensable to this world in her capacity as the saucer of malice. Screaming "shithead!" at the top of her lungs, she plunged in of her own accord.

From time immemorial, all those who have created an end of the world have placed a storm there, or else a deep hole from which any who fall in can never climb out from again. Faced with a precipitous cliff towering sharply over all, man has ever attempted to claw his way up with hope held in his chest, creating for himself a fate that results in him falling down for all eternity.

source.japanese:
しかし、今、信天翁号は飛ぶ。
　三本のマストに張られたその帆に風をはらみ。
　陸地の見えぬ海原をいつまででも飛び続ける信天翁。
source.english:
But now the Albatross flew.

Wind filled the sails upon her three masts.

An albatross flying endlessly over seas where no land could be seen.

source.japanese:
そう、飛び続けるのだ、飛び続けていられるのだ。
　どこまで落ちようとも。
　いつか必ず、羽根休められる場所を見つけるまでは。
source.english:
Yes. She would keep flying. She could keep flying.

However far she fell.

Until she found a place to rest her wings—as she surely would, someday.

source.japanese:
嵐にまかれて羽根は折れ、その体傷つけられても。
　帆は破れ、マストは折れ、ついにその船体すら粉々に。
　乗り組みどもをぶちまけながらも。
source.english:
Even if the storm caught her, broke her wings and wounded her body.

Her sails torn, her masts broken, even her hull finally shattered.

Even as she spilled her crew—

source.japanese:
ああ、信天翁。
　
　
　お前はきっと見つけられる。
　お前はきっと辿り着ける。
　
　
　そこに───
　その場所に───
source.english:
Ah, Albatross.

Surely you will find it.

Surely you will arrive.

There—

At that place—

target.text: However, right now, the Albatross flies. The sails stretching out across her three masts filled with wind. An Albatross flying forever above an ocean with no land in sight.
Indeed, she continues to fly, she can fly on forever. No matter how far you fall. Until the day comes, and it will come, when you find the place where your wings can rest.

Even should the storm take you and break your wings, your body damaged. Your sails ripped, your masts snapped, and finally, even your hull smashed to pieces. Even as your entire crew is tossed overboard.
Aah, Albatross. You will surely find it. You will surely reach it. And there─── In that place───

source.japanese: それは、彼が知る祖国と、同じようでいてどこか異なる景色だった。
source.english: The view resembled the homeland he knew, yet was somehow different.

source.japanese: その国はついこの間、敗北を受け入れたばかりだった。世界中を巻き込んだ大戦の最後の敗者となることを。
source.english: That country had only just accepted defeat. Accepted being the last defeated nation in a war that had drawn in the whole world.

source.japanese: 空から街を焼かれ、海外に持つ領土をすべて失い、因業の炎の二柱、たくさんの民が死に、兵は殺し殺され、そしてやっと敗北の宣言読み上げて、戦争を終わらせたばかりだった。
source.english: Its cities burned from the sky, every overseas territory lost, two pillars of accursed flame, multitudes of its people dead, its soldiers killing and being killed—and then, at last, the declaration of defeat read aloud: only now had the country brought its war to an end.

source.japanese: その時、この国民はなにを思っただろう。悔しさか、悲しみか、あるいは安堵か。ともかく張り詰めていたものが切れ、誰もが一度膝をついたのだった。
source.english: What had the people of this country thought then? Frustration, grief—or relief? Whatever it was, something stretched taut had snapped. Everyone had dropped to their knees once.

target.text: It was the motherland he knew well, a scenery at once familiar and yet somehow different.
That country had only just accepted its defeat. That it was the final loser of the great world war that had engulfed the entire world.

Cities burnt to the ground from the skies, all overseas territory lost, two pillars of wicked hellfire, countless citizens dead, soldiers had slaughtered and been slaughtered in turn; finally, having read aloud the declaration of defeat, they had only just brought the war to its end.
What must the people have felt at the time? Bitterness, sorrow, or perhaps relief? Regardless, what had been swollen with tension was cut open, and all fell to their knees at least once.

source.japanese: しかし、彼らは次の日には立ち上がる。残されたのは焼き払われ荒廃した国土であっても、生きてゆかねばならぬのだから。立ち上がり廃材集めて家を作り、土くれを鋤で打ち、生きる術を探し出す。混乱はまだしばらく続こうとも、彼らは足を踏み出した。皆が前を向いて進むのなら、その息吹はこの国に、復興という風を吹かせる。そんな時代だった。
source.english: Yet by the next morning they were on their feet. Burned bare and ruined though the land left to them might be, live they must: up they rose, gathering salvage to build houses, breaking clods with their hoes, searching out the means to survive. Confusion might reign a while yet, but they had taken their first step. If everyone faced forward and pressed on, their breath would blow through this country as a wind called reconstruction. Such were the times.

source.japanese:
そこに彼は辿り着いた。
　どこからとは言わぬ。
　どうやってとも言わぬ。
source.english:
There he arrived.

From where, we will not say.

Nor how.

source.japanese: ただ、遥か遠い異国の地で海に投げ入れられた空き瓶が海流に乗って砂浜に流れ着いたように襤褸屑同然の格好で、ここに辿り着いたのだ。
source.english: Only: like an empty bottle thrown into the sea in some far-off foreign land, borne by currents to a beach, he arrived here looking little better than a heap of rags.

target.text: However, they rose to their feet once more the next day. Even if all that remained was a devastated country reduced to ashes, they had to live on. They rose to their feet, gathered the scrap materials, built houses from it, stuck their spades in the soil, found a way to survive. Even if the chaos seemed poised to linger for a while yet, they took a step forwards. If everyone kept moving forwards, their breath of life would surely become the winds of recovery blowing through this land. That was the era.
That is where he arrived. Unwilling to explain from where. Unwilling to explain even how.

He had simply arrived here in what amounted to little more than rags, like an empty bottle thrown into the sea in a faraway foreign land travelling along the ocean currents before washing ashore on a beach.

source.japanese: 放っておけばそこでそのまま死体となっていたかもしれぬほど、疲れ果て動けずにいた彼は幸いな事に拾われる。
source.english: Exhausted, unable to move, he might have become a corpse where he lay if left alone. Fortunately, someone picked him up.

source.japanese: 彼を拾ったのは、街の片隅で身を寄せ合って巣を作り、街駆け巡って日々の糧をあらゆる手使って稼ぐ、浮浪児達だった。戦争の中、あるいはその後の混乱の中、死に別れたかはぐれたか或いは故あって放り出されたか、親も失く庇護者もいない子供達だった。
source.english: Those who found him were street children. Huddled together, they had made a nest in a corner of town, and ran through its streets earning their daily bread by every means. Children without parents or protectors: bereaved, separated, or cast out for some reason during the war or the confusion afterward.

source.japanese: 倒れた彼を見つけた浮浪児達は、野垂れ死にの体から金目のものでも毟[むし]って埋めてやろうと近づいてみれば、まだ息のあることに驚いた。彼らは顔突き合わせ、何を相談しどうまとまったのかはわからぬが、その行き倒れを自分達の住み処まで、彼の手持ち足持ちやや扱いは雑ながら、引きずっていった。そして、多くはないが、幸運な事に仲間の一人が今日は大当たり引き当てたのが幸いした、食べ物と水を分け与えた。
source.english: Finding him fallen, they approached to strip anything valuable from a body dead by the roadside and then bury it. They were surprised to find him still breathing. They put their heads together. What they discussed, how they agreed, we do not know. But they dragged the fallen man to their dwelling, handling his arms and legs rather roughly. And they shared food and water with him. Not much, but fortunately one of their number had struck it lucky that day.

source.japanese: 浮浪児達にしてみれば、大人の一人も仲間にいれば、いろいろと便利もあるだろうと考えたのかもしれぬ。気まぐれが入り込んでいたことは大いに否定できぬ。なぁに、厄介となれば追い出してしまえばいいとはやや浅慮ともいえるが。しかし、自分達の身の上多少は顧みれば捨て置く事が出来なかったのだとすれば、小狡く生き抜く彼らの中にも、純心は汚れず残っているのだろう。それは拾われた男にとっても、浮浪児達にとっても、この国の行く末にとっても幸いであるに違いない。
source.english: Perhaps the street children reckoned that having even one grown-up among them might come in handy. Nor can we altogether deny that caprice had wormed its way into the decision. Well, if he proved a nuisance, they could always throw him out—though that, one might say, was rather shortsighted of them. Yet if some small recollection of their own lot had left them unable to abandon him, then even in these sly little survivors a pure heart must have remained unsullied. A blessing, surely, for the man they picked up, for the street children, and for the future of this country alike.

source.japanese:
明けて翌朝まだ早く。
　ものすごい勢いで与えた食べ物平らげたかと思ったら、また倒れて眠り込んだ昨日からの居候を、浮浪児達、その頭蹴り飛ばして手荒く起こす。せっかく拾ったからには、働いてもらわねば困るのだ。動ける者に無駄飯食わせる余裕はなし、稼ぎが悪けりゃ飯抜きだ、それでも悪けりゃ追い出すぞと脅して彼を住み処から引っ張り出す。
source.english:
Early the next morning—

Their lodger since yesterday had devoured the food with tremendous speed, then collapsed and slept again. The street children woke him roughly, kicking his head. Having gone to the trouble of picking him up, they needed him to work. They could not afford to feed an able-bodied man for nothing. Earn poorly and you get no food; keep doing badly and you're out. With those threats, they hauled him from their dwelling.

source.japanese:
向かう先は荒廃の混乱から自然発生した物流の集積地、闇市だった。
　前年の挑発から隠し通した米の余り、庭先の土掘り起こしてようやく実った野菜、配給切り詰めて貯めた小麦粉などの食料品から、それを焼いたり捌[さば]いたり欠けた椀に鍋の中味よそって出すもあり、焼失免れた家屋の箪笥から引っ張り出した衣類、同様になんとか守り通した本雑誌しかしこちらはやや人気薄か、そして出所問えぬ品々等々、ある者は金に困り、ある者は物に困り、ある者は目聡く金儲けの機会狙って集い来る。
source.english:
Their destination was the black market, a great depot of goods sprung spontaneously from the chaos of devastation.
Here were foodstuffs—rice left over from stores concealed from the previous year's requisitions, vegetables at last coaxed from soil dug up in front gardens, flour saved by stinting one's rations—while others grilled or carved such fare, or ladled what was in the pot into chipped bowls and served it; clothes hauled from wardrobes in houses spared the fires; books and magazines likewise preserved, though these proved somewhat less popular; and all manner of articles whose provenance did not bear asking. And here they gathered: some for want of money, some for want of goods, and some sharp-eyed for a chance to turn a profit.

source.japanese: 商品抱えた者どもが思い思いに店を広げて連なり通りの左右を埋め尽くす。そこに品求めて人が集まるのだから、そこは常にごった返して喧噪もやかましい。そして、こんな場所だから糧を稼ぐ、まぁどのようにかは聞かぬとして、機会も多かろうと浮浪児達は男を連れてきたのだ。お前はでかいんだから、自分達とは別のやりようもあるんだろうと言いながら。
source.english: People with goods set up stalls wherever they pleased, lining both sides of the street. People seeking goods gathered too; it was always crowded, always noisy. In a place like this there must be plenty of chances to earn one's bread—let us not ask how. That was why the street children had brought the man here. You're big, they told him. There must be ways for you that aren't open to us.

source.japanese: 男への案内もそこそこに、浮浪児達は稼ぎ求めて散っていく。
source.english: After only a brief introduction, the children scattered in search of earnings.

source.japanese:
残された男と言えば……、まぁ、人混みの中で立ち尽くし、呆然としていたわけだ。
　右も左もわからぬ彼にとっては異国の地。稼げと言われてもどうしたものやら。この手には技も何もありはしないのだ。一宿一飯の恩はありがたいが、さてどう報いたものか、いや待て、このままとんずらこいてもかまわんのじゃないかなぁ、などと。
source.english:
As for the man left behind…well, he stood dumbstruck in the crowd.

A foreign country to him; he knew nothing of the place. Told to earn, what was he to do? His hands had no skills. He was grateful for a night's lodging and a meal, but how to repay them? No, wait. Couldn't he just make himself scarce…?

source.japanese: ぼんやりと休んだがましの考え巡らせながら、眺めていた人混みの中に。
source.english:
As he idly turned over thoughts he'd have been better off without, he watched the crowd.

And in it—

target.text: So exhausted he couldn't move, had he been left as he was, he might well have perished right then and there, but fortunately, he was picked up.

The ones who found him were a group of street urchins who had huddled together in a corner of the city and built their haunt there, running about the city as they used every trick in the book to earn their daily bread. Whether they were separated by death, had lost sight of each other, or had been abandoned due to unavoidable circumstances in the middle of the war, or perhaps the post-war chaos, they were all children who had lost their parents and were also without a guardian.

When the children who had discovered him tried to approach him with the intent of filching any valuables and then burying this man who had died by the roadside, they were shocked to find he still breathed. They huddled together, and though it wasn't clear just what kind of discussion they had or what agreement they came to, they brought that man collapsed on the road to their den, and while the way they handled him was a bit rough, they still dragged him there by hand and foot. And then, although it wasn't much, fortunately, one of their comrades had been lucky enough to hit the jackpot that day, and he shared with the rest both food and water.

Perhaps from the perspective of these street urchins, they had thought that having an adult in their number would be convenient in many ways. Although it could not be denied that caprice had been a considerable factor. Why, if he became a burden, they could just drive him out, a thought that was, perhaps, a bit injudicious. However, if we assume that, after reflecting upon their own lot in life, they found they could not simply ignore him, then even in these urchins, surviving on the streets through cunning, there was surely a purity of heart yet to be stained. That was undoubtedly a blessing for the man who had been picked up, for the street urchins themselves, and for the future of this country.

It was still early the next morning. No sooner than he had inhaled every scrap of food he had been given with great gusto did he once more collapse, falling into a deep slumber, and the waifs leapt at this man who had been freeloading since yesterday, kicking him in the head and rousing him violently. They'd gone out of their way to pick him up, so they needed him to put in some work. They didn't have the luxury to let those who could work eat for free, and if earnings were bad, they'd go without dinner; while threatening to kick him out if he still wouldn't do it, they dragged him out of their dwelling.
Their destination was a place that had naturally formed from the chaos of the devastation, a gathering place for the flow of goods: a black market.

Surplus rice kept hidden after the provocations of the previous years; vegetables finally ripened after digging up the soil in one's garden; dishes made from food supplies such as flour, which had been saved by scrimping on rations, or perhaps ladling the contents of a pot into a chipped wooden bowl; clothing taken from the dressers of homes that survived the fires, and similarly surviving books and magazines painstakingly protected, but perhaps those weren't quite as popular, and then there were all the goods of unknown origin: it was a gathering of people short on money, people short on things, and people with a keen sense for opportunities to make some money.

Those carrying goods set up their shops in whatever way they preferred, forming a long chain that filled up the street from left to right. Those looking for goods all gathered there, so it was a constant commotion, a clamorous hustle and bustle. Hence they would earn their daily bread here; well, let us not get bogged down asking how, but there would surely be many a chance here, or so the urchins thought, and they brought the man there. And while telling him that since he was big, there was surely some way of doing it that differed from theirs.
After barely showing the man around, the street urchins scattered in pursuit of money.

As for the man who had been left behind……, well, he stood stock still in the middle of the crowd, dumbfounded. To he, a man who knew neither right from left, this was foreign land. He had been told to earn money, but how was he meant to do it? He had no skills that were of any use for this sort of thing. He did feel a debt of gratitude for the night's lodging and the meal he'd been given, but, well then, how should he repay it, no, hold on, maybe they wouldn't care if he just ran away right now, and so on.
As thoughts, ones as idle as if he were absentmindedly taking a break, drifted through his brain, there, in the crowd he had been gazing out upon.

男、思わず駆け出す。
　こちらは、人にぶつかり物にぶつかり、舌打ちとまれに怒号をかけられながら、近づいていく。
　その背があとわずかまでとよろめき出たところで、男は何かを叫んだだろうか。あるいは何も言わずに立ち尽くしただろうか。どちらを選んだのだとしても。
source.english:
The man broke into a run before he knew it.

He, by contrast, kept bumping into people and things. Tongues clicked; now and then someone shouted at him.

When he stumbled out just a little way behind her, did he shout something? Or stand without a word? Whichever he chose—

source.japanese: 少女は振り返る。ごく自然に。すぐ後ろに男がいて、自分を見つめているのが当たり前であるというように。
source.english: The woman turned. Quite naturally. As though it were only to be expected that the man stood just behind her, looking at her.

target.text: There she was.
Just like she had been back then.

Black hair that let glimpses of deep green slip through depending on the light that fell upon it, toyed with by the wind like fluttering wings, gliding through the busy street, freely weaving her way through the streams of people as if they were but flows of air.

Instinctively, the man broke into a run. He, on the other hand, ran into men and things alike, and while showered in yells and tutting tongues, he drew closer. When that back was so close that he needed just one final, staggering step, did the man perhaps shout something? Or perhaps he said nothing, just standing there motionlessly? Regardless of which option he chose.
The girl turned around. Entirely effortlessly. As if to say that it was only natural for there to be a man right behind her, staring at her.
